translation: In the name of Allah, the Entirely Merciful, the Especially Merciful.
interpretation: This verse, known as the Basmala, is an invocation of God's name at the beginning of each chapter (surah) of the Qur'an (except for Surah 9). It emphasizes two key attributes of God: His all-encompassing mercy and His special mercy that He bestows upon the believers. Starting with this phrase is a reminder for the reader to approach the Qur'an with reverence and to seek God's guidance and mercy in understanding and applying its teachings. It sets the tone for the reader's mindset and establishes a connection between the reader and the divine source of the message.
orig: بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم

translation: All praise is due to Allah, Lord of the worlds.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that all praise, gratitude, and worship belong exclusively to Allah, the Creator and Sustainer of the entire universe. It acknowledges His sovereignty over all creation and His role as the ultimate Provider and Cherisher of all beings. By recognizing Allah as the "Lord of the worlds," the verse highlights His absolute authority and the fact that everything in existence is dependent upon Him. This opening verse sets the tone for the entire Qur'an, reminding believers to direct their praise and devotion towards Allah alone.
orig: الحمد لله رب العالمين

translation: The Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.
interpretation: This verse refers to two of the most important attributes of Allah: His infinite grace and mercy. It emphasizes that Allah's mercy encompasses all things and that His grace is bestowed upon all of His creation. The repetition of these two attributes at the beginning of every surah (except one) in the Qur'an highlights their significance in the Islamic concept of God. This verse serves as a constant reminder to humans of Allah's compassion and love, encouraging them to seek His forgiveness and strive to emulate these qualities in their own lives.
orig: الرحمن الرحيم

translation: Master of the Day of Judgment.
interpretation: This verse affirms that Allah alone is the Master and Ruler of the Day of Judgment, when all of humanity will be held accountable for their deeds. It emphasizes His absolute authority and sovereignty over the ultimate fate of every soul. On that day, no one else will have any power or influence, and Allah's judgment will be final and just. This verse serves as a reminder for believers to be mindful of their actions in this life, as they will have consequences in the Hereafter, and to submit to Allah's will and guidance.
orig: مالك يوم الدين

translation: It is You we worship and You we ask for help.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of directing all acts of worship and seeking assistance solely from Allah. It serves as a reminder for believers to maintain sincerity in their faith and to rely on Allah's guidance and support in all their endeavors. By acknowledging Allah as the only One worthy of worship and the ultimate source of help, Muslims reaffirm their submission to His will and their trust in His wisdom and mercy. This verse encapsulates the essence of the relationship between the believer and Allah, highlighting the significance of unwavering devotion and complete reliance on Him.
orig: إياك نعبد وإياك نستعين

translation: Guide us to the straight path.
interpretation: This verse is a prayer for God's guidance to the right path in life. It is a plea for God to show us the way that leads to righteousness, truth, and ultimately, salvation. The straight path refers to the path of Islam, which is characterized by submission to God's will and adherence to His commandments. It is a path of moderation, balance, and justice, avoiding the extremes of excess and deficiency. By seeking God's guidance to the straight path, the believer acknowledges their need for divine support and direction in navigating the challenges and choices of life. This prayer reflects the believer's desire to stay true to their faith and to live a life that is pleasing to God.
orig: اهدنا الصراط المستقيم

translation: The path of those upon whom You have bestowed favor, not of those who have evoked [Your] anger or of those who are astray.
interpretation: This verse is a prayer for guidance to follow the straight path of those whom Allah has blessed, which includes the prophets, the truthful, the martyrs, and the righteous. It also seeks protection from following the path of those who have earned Allah's anger, such as the willfully disobedient, and those who have gone astray from the truth out of ignorance or negligence. The verse emphasizes the importance of seeking Allah's guidance to stay on the right path and avoid the pitfalls of misguidance and disobedience.
orig: صراط الذين أنعمت عليهم غير المغضوب عليهم ولا الضالين

translation: Alif, Lam, Meem.
interpretation: These disjointed letters are one of the miracles of the Qur'an, and none but Allah (Alone) knows their meanings. They indicate that this book, the Qur'an, is composed of letters of the Arabic alphabet, which the Arabs knew well, yet they were unable to produce anything similar to it in terms of its eloquence, perfect style, and profound impact. This highlights that the Qur'an is a divine revelation and not the words of a human being.
orig: الم

translation: This is the Book about which there is no doubt, a guidance for those conscious of Allah.
interpretation: This verse affirms that the Qur'an is a divine revelation from Allah, free from any doubt or uncertainty. It serves as a clear guidance for those who are mindful of Allah and seek to follow His path. The Qur'an provides a comprehensive framework for living a righteous life, offering wisdom, moral teachings, and spiritual enlightenment to those who sincerely believe in its message and strive to implement its principles in their lives. It is a source of guidance that leads believers towards the path of righteousness, helping them navigate the challenges of this world and attain success in the hereafter.
orig: ذلك الكتاب لا ريب فيه هدى للمتقين

translation: Who believe in the unseen, establish prayer, and spend out of what We have provided for them,
interpretation: This verse describes the qualities of the righteous believers. They have faith in the unseen aspects of reality, such as Allah, the angels, and the afterlife, without demanding physical evidence. They are steadfast in establishing the five daily prayers, which demonstrates their dedication to worshipping Allah and maintaining a connection with Him. Moreover, they are generous in spending from the wealth and provisions that Allah has granted them, whether through obligatory alms (zakat) or voluntary charity. This spending purifies their souls and shows their gratitude to Allah. These qualities of faith, prayer, and charity are essential foundations of righteousness in Islam.
orig: الذين يؤمنون بالغيب ويقيمون الصلاة ومما رزقناهم ينفقون

translation: And those who believe in what has been revealed to you, [O Muhammad], and what was revealed before you, and of the Hereafter they are certain [in faith].
interpretation: This verse refers to the true believers who have complete faith not only in the Qur'an revealed to Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him), but also in the divine scriptures revealed before him to other prophets. They firmly believe in the Hereafter, the Day of Judgment, and the life after death. This unwavering faith in God's revelations and the afterlife is a key characteristic that distinguishes the true believers. It shows their conviction in the continuity of God's message throughout time and their understanding that this worldly life is not the end, but rather a transient phase before the eternal life in the hereafter, where they will be held accountable for their deeds. This faith is the driving force behind their righteous actions and their striving to follow the straight path ordained by God.
orig: والذين يؤمنون بما أنزل إليك وما أنزل من قبلك وبالآخرة هم يوقنون

translation: Those are upon [right] guidance from their Lord, and it is those who are the successful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that true guidance comes only from Allah. Those who follow the guidance provided by their Lord are the ones who will ultimately attain success and prosperity, both in this world and in the Hereafter. The verse implies that success is not measured by worldly gains or status, but rather by one's adherence to divine guidance and righteousness. It also suggests that while individuals may strive for success through their own efforts, ultimate success is a blessing from Allah bestowed upon those who sincerely follow His guidance.
orig: أولئك على هدى من ربهم وأولئك هم المفلحون

translation: Indeed, those who disbelieve - it is all the same for them whether you warn them or do not warn them - they will not believe.
interpretation: This verse highlights the stubborn nature of those who reject faith in Allah. It suggests that no matter how much the Prophet (peace be upon him) tries to warn them of the consequences of their disbelief, they will remain unmoved and persist in their rejection of the truth. Their hearts are sealed, and they have chosen to deny the signs and guidance of Allah, making it impossible for them to embrace faith unless Allah wills otherwise. The verse emphasizes the importance of the Prophet's mission to convey the message, while acknowledging that the ultimate outcome rests with Allah alone.
orig: إن الذين كفروا سواء عليهم أأنذرتهم أم لم تنذرهم لا يؤمنون

translation: Allah has set a seal upon their hearts and upon their hearing, and over their vision is a veil. And for them is a great punishment.
interpretation: This verse refers to those who have persistently denied the truth and rejected the guidance of Allah. As a result of their obstinacy and arrogance, Allah has sealed their hearts, making them unable to comprehend or accept the truth. Their hearing and sight are also veiled, preventing them from perceiving the signs of Allah's existence and power. Due to their continuous disbelief and transgression, they will face a severe punishment in the Hereafter. This verse serves as a warning to those who knowingly reject the message of Islam and persist in their disbelief, highlighting the consequences of their actions in the afterlife.
orig: ختم الله على قلوبهم وعلى سمعهم وعلى أبصارهم غشاوة ولهم عذاب عظيم

translation: And of the people are some who say, "We believe in Allah and the Last Day," but they are not believers.
interpretation: This verse is referring to the hypocrites who outwardly profess their belief in Islam, but inwardly they harbor doubt and disbelief. They say with their tongues that they believe in Allah and the Last Day, but their hearts are not in conformity with their words. They are not sincere in their faith and their actions do not reflect true belief. The verse exposes the reality of their hypocrisy and the emptiness of their claims. It serves as a warning to Muslims to be wary of such people who may try to undermine the community from within by pretending to be believers while secretly working against the interests of Islam.
orig: ومن الناس من يقول آمنا بالله وباليوم الآخر وما هم بمؤمنين

translation: They [think to] deceive Allah and those who believe, but they deceive not except themselves and perceive [it] not.
interpretation: This verse is referring to the hypocrites who outwardly pretend to be believers but inwardly harbor disbelief and ill intentions towards Islam and the Muslims. They think that by putting on a false front, they can deceive Allah and the believers. However, in reality, they are only deceiving themselves because Allah knows what is in their hearts and will hold them accountable for their hypocrisy. They are heedless of the spiritual consequences of their actions and the ultimate futility of trying to deceive the All-Knowing.
orig: يخادعون الله والذين آمنوا وما يخدعون إلا أنفسهم وما يشعرون

translation: In their hearts is disease, so Allah has increased their disease; and for them is a painful punishment because they [habitually] used to lie.
interpretation: This verse refers to the hypocrites who outwardly professed belief but inwardly harbored doubts and ill intentions. Because of their insincerity, Allah allowed their spiritual disease of hypocrisy and doubt to increase. Their dishonesty and deception, born out of the sickness in their hearts, will lead them to a severe punishment in the Hereafter. It serves as a warning that inner intentions and purity of faith are crucial, and that Allah is aware of what lies within people's hearts. Deceptive speech and conduct will only lead one further away from the truth and result in painful consequences.
orig: في قلوبهم مرض فزادهم الله مرضا ولهم عذاب أليم بما كانوا يكذبون

translation: And when it is said to them, "Do not cause corruption on the earth," they say, "We are but reformers."
interpretation: This verse is highlighting the hypocrisy and self-delusion of those who spread corruption and evil while believing that they are actually doing good. They justify their misdeeds by claiming to be reformers or people of righteousness, failing to recognize the harm they are causing. It serves as a warning against self-deception and emphasizes the importance of being honest with oneself about one's actions and intentions. True reform and righteousness come from sincere devotion to God and adhering to His guidance, not from hollow claims or self-serving justifications.
orig: وإذا قيل لهم لا تفسدوا في الأرض قالوا إنما نحن مصلحون

translation: Unquestionably, it is they who are the corrupters, but they perceive [it] not.
interpretation: This verse is pointing out the irony and lack of self-awareness of those who spread corruption on earth. They engage in actions that cause harm and damage to society, yet they are oblivious to the fact that they themselves are the source of the very corruption they may blame on others. Their hearts are blind to the truth of their own misdeeds. It is a reminder for people to engage in introspection and recognize how their own actions can sow seeds of corruption, even if unintentionally. True righteousness requires vigilance over one's own heart and conduct.
orig: ألا إنهم هم المفسدون ولكن لا يشعرون

translation: And when it is said to them, "Believe as the people have believed," they say, "Should we believe as the foolish have believed?" Unquestionably, it is they who are the foolish, but they know [it] not.
interpretation: This verse is criticizing the hypocrites who refuse to sincerely believe like the true believers. When they are told to have faith like the believers, they arrogantly reply wondering how they could believe like those they consider to be fools. However, Allah makes it clear that in reality, it is the hypocrites who are the true fools, but they are too ignorant and arrogant to realize their own foolishness in rejecting sincere faith.
orig: وإذا قيل لهم آمنوا كما آمن الناس قالوا أنؤمن كما آمن السفهاء ألا إنهم هم السفهاء ولكن لا يعلمون

translation: And when they meet those who believe, they say, "We believe"; but when they are alone with their evil ones, they say, "Indeed, we are with you; we were only mockers."
interpretation: This verse is referring to the hypocrites who outwardly pretend to be believers, but inwardly they are disbelievers. When they meet the true believers, they claim to have faith, but when they are alone with their fellow disbelievers, they reveal their true colors and admit that they were only mocking the believers and the faith. This verse highlights the deceptive nature of the hypocrites and their lack of sincerity in their claims of belief.
orig: وإذا لقوا الذين آمنوا قالوا آمنا وإذا خلوا إلى شياطينهم قالوا إنا معكم إنما نحن مستهزئون

translation: Allah mocks them and prolongs them in their transgression [while] they wander blindly.
interpretation: This verse speaks to the fate of those who reject Allah's guidance and persist in their disbelief and wrongdoing. Allah allows them to continue in their misguidance, seemingly giving them free rein, but in reality, He is mocking their foolishness and allowing them to become more entrenched in their sinful ways. This divine response is a form of punishment, as the more they wander blindly in their transgression, the further they distance themselves from Allah's mercy and the more severe their ultimate punishment will be. It serves as a warning to those who might follow a similar path and a reminder that Allah's justice will prevail, even if it appears that the wicked are prospering in the short term.
orig: الله يستهزئ بهم ويمدهم في طغيانهم يعمهون

translation: Those are the ones who have purchased error [in exchange] for guidance, so their transaction has brought no profit, nor were they guided.
interpretation: This verse is a metaphor comparing those who choose misguidance over the truth to someone who makes a bad trade, exchanging something valuable for something worthless. It emphasizes that rejecting divine guidance and choosing falsehood instead leads to loss and failure, both in this world and the hereafter. Those who make this choice are not guided and cannot find the right path. The verse implies that true guidance comes from Allah, and to reject it in favor of misguidance is a grave error with serious consequences.
orig: أولئك الذين اشتروا الضلالة بالهدى فما ربحت تجارتهم وما كانوا مهتدين

translation: Their example is that of one who kindled a fire, but when it illuminated what was around him, Allah took away their light and left them in darkness [so] they could not see.
interpretation: This verse is a metaphor for the hypocrites who outwardly show faith but inwardly harbor disbelief. The fire represents the guidance of Islam, which illuminates the truth for those around it. However, due to the hypocrites' insincerity, Allah removes this light of guidance from them, leaving them in a state of spiritual darkness and inability to perceive the truth. It highlights the consequence of hypocrisy - being deprived of divine guidance and remaining in a state of confusion and misguidance, unable to see the right path.
orig: مثلهم كمثل الذي استوقد نارا فلما أضاءت ما حوله ذهب الله بنورهم وتركهم في ظلمات لا يبصرون

translation: Deaf, dumb and blind - so they will not return [to the right path].
interpretation: This verse is describing those who have turned away from the truth and guidance of Allah. They are compared to people who are deaf, unable to hear the truth; dumb, unable to speak the truth; and blind, unable to see the signs of Allah all around them. As a result of their spiritual state, they are unable to find their way back to the straight path and to the mercy and forgiveness of Allah. The verse serves as a warning to all of mankind not to allow ourselves to become so hardened and misguided, as doing so will lead to our own spiritual destruction if we don't sincerely seek Allah's guidance.
orig: صم بكم عمي فهم لا يرجعون

translation: Or [it is] like a rainstorm from the sky within which is darkness, thunder and lightning. They put their fingers in their ears against the thunderclaps in dread of death. But Allah is encompassing of the disbelievers.
interpretation: This verse draws a vivid analogy between the state of the disbelievers and a person caught in a severe rainstorm, surrounded by darkness, thunder, and lightning. The disbelievers are likened to those who, in fear of death, try to block out the sound of the thunder by putting their fingers in their ears. However, this action is futile, as it cannot protect them from the all-encompassing power of Allah. The verse emphasizes that no matter how much the disbelievers try to ignore or deny the truth, they cannot escape the reality of Allah's presence and His ultimate judgment. It serves as a powerful reminder that Allah's knowledge and power surround everyone, and that the disbelievers' denial of faith will not protect them from the consequences of their actions in the end.
orig: أو كصيب من السماء فيه ظلمات ورعد وبرق يجعلون أصابعهم في آذانهم من الصواعق حذر الموت والله محيط بالكافرين

translation: The lightning almost snatches away their sight. Whenever it lights [the way] for them, they walk therein; but when darkness comes over them, they stand [still]. And if Allah had willed, He could have taken away their hearing and their sight. Indeed, Allah is over all things competent.
interpretation: This verse is a metaphor for the hypocrites who only follow the truth when it is convenient for them. The lightning represents the truth, which they can see clearly at times, allowing them to walk the right path. However, when the darkness of doubt or difficulty comes, they stop and falter. The verse emphasizes that Allah has the power to take away their senses, symbolizing His control over their guidance. It serves as a warning that one should sincerely follow the truth regardless of the circumstances, as Allah is aware of all things and has power over all.
orig: يكاد البرق يخطف أبصارهم كلما أضاء لهم مشوا فيه وإذا أظلم عليهم قاموا ولو شاء الله لذهب بسمعهم وأبصارهم إن الله على كل شيء قدير

translation: O mankind, worship your Lord, who created you and those before you, that you may become righteous.
interpretation: This verse is a call to all of humanity to worship Allah alone, as He is the One who created them and all those who came before them. The purpose of this worship is so that people may become righteous and God-fearing, living their lives in accordance with Allah's guidance and attaining success in this world and the Hereafter. It emphasizes the importance of acknowledging Allah as the sole Creator and Sustainer, and directs mankind to express their gratitude and submission to Him through sincere worship and obedience to His commands. This verse serves as a reminder that the ultimate goal of human existence is to develop a strong connection with Allah and lead a righteous life.
orig: يا أيها الناس اعبدوا ربكم الذي خلقكم والذين من قبلكم لعلكم تتقون

translation: [He] who made for you the earth a bed [spread out] and the sky a ceiling and sent down from the sky, rain and brought forth thereby fruits as provision for you. So do not attribute to Allah equals while you know [that there is nothing similar to Him].
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the oneness and uniqueness of Allah, reminding us of His countless blessings and provisions. It highlights that Allah has created the earth as a comfortable abode for humans and the sky as a protective ceiling. He sends down rain from the sky, which allows fruits and vegetation to grow, providing sustenance for mankind. The verse warns against attributing partners or equals to Allah, as it is an act of ingratitude and goes against the fundamental belief in His unity. It encourages people to acknowledge Allah's favors and worship Him alone, without associating any partners with Him, especially when they have the knowledge and understanding of His omnipotence and singularity.
orig: الذي جعل لكم الأرض فراشا والسماء بناء وأنزل من السماء ماء فأخرج به من الثمرات رزقا لكم فلا تجعلوا لله أندادا وأنتم تعلمون

translation: And if you are in doubt about what We have sent down upon Our Servant [Muhammad], then produce a surah the like thereof and call upon your witnesses other than Allah, if you should be truthful.
interpretation: This verse challenges those who doubt the divine origin of the Qur'an to produce a chapter like it, calling upon their witnesses or helpers besides Allah to assist them in this task. It implies that the Qur'an is inimitable and cannot be replicated by human beings, serving as a proof of its divine source. The verse also emphasizes the importance of being truthful and sincere in one's claims and beliefs, as the challenge is addressed to those who are honest in their doubts about the Qur'an's authenticity.
orig: وإن كنتم في ريب مما نزلنا على عبدنا فأتوا بسورة من مثله وادعوا شهداءكم من دون الله إن كنتم صادقين

translation: And if you do not and you will never be able to then fear the Fire whose fuel is people and stones, prepared for the disbelievers.
interpretation: This verse serves as a stern warning to those who reject the message of Islam and the prophethood of Muhammad (peace be upon him). It emphasizes the severe consequences of disbelief, stating that those who persist in their rejection of faith will face the torment of Hell, where they will be consumed by a fire fueled by people and stones. The mention of stones alongside people as fuel for the Fire may allude to the idols and false deities that the disbelievers worshipped. The verse underscores the gravity of rejecting God's message and the ultimate fate that awaits those who choose disbelief over faith. It is a powerful reminder of the importance of heeding the call to righteousness and submitting to the will of the Almighty before it is too late.
orig: فإن لم تفعلوا ولن تفعلوا فاتقوا النار التي وقودها الناس والحجارة أعدت للكافرين

translation: And give good tidings to those who believe and do righteous deeds that they will have gardens [in Paradise] beneath which rivers flow. Whenever they are provided with a provision of fruit therefrom, they will say, "This is what we were provided with before." And it is given to them in likeness. And they will have therein purified spouses, and they will abide therein eternally.
interpretation: This verse is a promise from Allah to the believers who do good deeds. It describes the eternal reward of Paradise that awaits them in the Hereafter. In Paradise, they will have gardens with rivers flowing beneath them, and whenever they are provided with fruits, they will recognize them as similar to what they were given in the worldly life, but of a superior quality. The believers will also have spouses who are pure and free from any imperfections or impurities. This verse emphasizes the eternal nature of Paradise, as the believers will reside there forever, enjoying its endless blessings and delights. It serves as an encouragement and motivation for the believers to continue doing good deeds and remain steadfast in their faith.
orig: وبشر الذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات أن لهم جنات تجري من تحتها الأنهار كلما رزقوا منها من ثمرة رزقا قالوا هذا الذي رزقنا من قبل وأتوا به متشابها ولهم فيها أزواج مطهرة وهم فيها خالدون

translation: Indeed, Allah is not timid to present an example - that of a mosquito or what is smaller than it. And those who have believed know that it is the truth from their Lord. But as for those who disbelieve, they say, "What did Allah intend by this as an example?" He misleads many thereby and guides many thereby. And He misleads not except the defiantly disobedient,
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah, in His infinite wisdom, can use any example or parable to convey His message, even if it seems insignificant like a mosquito. The believers understand and accept these examples as the truth from their Lord, recognizing the deeper meaning and lessons behind them. However, the disbelievers question the purpose of such examples and find them perplexing. Allah clarifies that these parables serve to guide those who are open to His guidance, while those who are disobedient and reject the truth will only find themselves further misled by their own arrogance and lack of faith. The verse highlights the divide between the believers and the disbelievers in their reception and understanding of Allah's wisdom.
orig: إن الله لا يستحيي أن يضرب مثلا ما بعوضة فما فوقها فأما الذين آمنوا فيعلمون أنه الحق من ربهم وأما الذين كفروا فيقولون ماذا أراد الله بهذا مثلا يضل به كثيرا ويهدي به كثيرا وما يضل به إلا الفاسقين

translation: Those who break the covenant of Allah after contracting it and sever that which Allah has ordered to be joined and cause corruption on earth. It is those who are the losers.
interpretation: This verse is referring to those who violate their covenant with Allah and disobey His commands. They break the ties of kinship and spread mischief and corruption in the land. These people are ultimately the losers in both this world and the Hereafter. They have lost Allah's favor and blessings by going against His teachings and spreading evil. The verse emphasizes the importance of fulfilling one's commitments, especially the covenant made with Allah, and maintaining the ties of kinship and righteousness that Allah has ordained. Those who fail in these duties and instead spread corruption are in manifest loss and will face the consequences of their actions in the Hereafter.
orig: الذين ينقضون عهد الله من بعد ميثاقه ويقطعون ما أمر الله به أن يوصل ويفسدون في الأرض أولئك هم الخاسرون

translation: How can you disbelieve in Allah when you were lifeless and He brought you to life; then He will cause you to die, then He will bring you [back] to life, and then to Him you will be returned.
interpretation: This verse is a powerful reminder of Allah's power over life and death, and the inevitability of our return to Him. It questions how one can deny the existence of Allah when it is He who has given us life, and will take it away, only to resurrect us again for the final judgment. The verse emphasizes the cyclical nature of our existence - from a state of lifelessness, to being brought to life, to death, and then resurrection. It serves as a wake-up call for those who disbelieve, urging them to recognize Allah's omnipotence and the ultimate reality that we will all be held accountable before Him in the Hereafter. The verse aims to inspire gratitude for the gift of life and encourages believers to live their lives in accordance with Allah's guidance, knowing that our ultimate destination is back to Him.
orig: كيف تكفرون بالله وكنتم أمواتا فأحياكم ثم يميتكم ثم يحييكم ثم إليه ترجعون

translation: It is He who created for you all of that which is on the earth. Then He directed Himself to the heaven, [His being above all creation], and made them seven heavens, and He is Knowing of all things.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's power, creativity, and omniscience. It reminds us that everything on Earth has been created by Allah for the benefit of humanity. The verse also highlights the vastness and complexity of the universe, with the mention of seven heavens, indicating that there is much beyond our world that we do not know or understand. Despite the grandeur of His creation, Allah has complete knowledge of all things, down to the smallest detail. This should inspire humility, gratitude, and awe in the believer, knowing that we are a small part of a much larger, divinely-ordained system.
orig: هو الذي خلق لكم ما في الأرض جميعا ثم استوى إلى السماء فسواهن سبع سماوات وهو بكل شيء عليم

translation: And [mention, O Muhammad], when your Lord said to the angels, "Indeed, I will make upon the earth a successive authority." They said, "Will You place upon it one who causes corruption therein and sheds blood, while we declare Your praise and sanctify You?" Allah said, "Indeed, I know that which you do not know."
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine wisdom and knowledge of Allah, who decided to create human beings as His representatives on earth, despite the angels' concerns about their potential for causing corruption and bloodshed. The interpretation is that Allah, in His infinite wisdom, knew the potential for goodness and righteousness within humanity, even though the angels could only foresee their negative aspects. This verse emphasizes the importance of trusting in Allah's plan and acknowledging that His knowledge and understanding far surpass that of His creation.
orig: وإذ قال ربك للملائكة إني جاعل في الأرض خليفة قالوا أتجعل فيها من يفسد فيها ويسفك الدماء ونحن نسبح بحمدك ونقدس لك قال إني أعلم ما لا تعلمون

translation: And He taught Adam all the names, then presented them to the angels and said, "Inform Me of the names of these, if you are truthful."
interpretation: This verse highlights the special status and knowledge bestowed upon Adam by Allah. It indicates that Allah granted Adam the unique ability to know and comprehend the names and attributes of all things, setting him apart from the angels. By presenting this knowledge to the angels and challenging them to name what Adam knew, Allah demonstrates the superiority of human potential and the wisdom behind appointing Adam as His representative on Earth. This event also signifies the importance of knowledge and learning in Islam, as it was the very first thing Allah taught Adam, emphasizing the value of education and understanding in the life of a believer.
orig: وعلم آدم الأسماء كلها ثم عرضهم على الملائكة فقال أنبئوني بأسماء هؤلاء إن كنتم صادقين

translation: They said, "Exalted are You; we have no knowledge except what You have taught us. Indeed, it is You who is the Knowing, the Wise."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the limitedness of human knowledge and the vastness of God's knowledge. The angels acknowledge that their knowledge is only what God has taught them, and they affirm two of God's attributes: Al-'Aleem (the All-Knowing) and Al-Hakeem (the All-Wise). It is a reminder for humans to be humble, recognize the limitations of their own knowledge, and seek knowledge from the ultimate source of wisdom, God Himself. The verse also underscores the importance of attributing all knowledge and wisdom to God and not being arrogant about one's own intellectual capabilities.
orig: قالوا سبحانك لا علم لنا إلا ما علمتنا إنك أنت العليم الحكيم

translation: He said, "O Adam, inform them of their names." And when he had informed them of their names, He said, "Did I not tell you that I know the unseen [aspects] of the heavens and the earth? And I know what you reveal and what you have concealed."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's omniscience and superiority over the angels. By commanding Adam to name the objects, Allah demonstrates that human beings have the capacity for knowledge that even the angels do not possess. The verse also highlights that Allah is aware of what is apparent and what is hidden, including the inner thoughts and intentions of His creation. This serves as a reminder for humankind to be mindful of their actions and intentions, as nothing is concealed from Allah's knowledge.
orig: قال يا آدم أنبئهم بأسمائهم فلما أنبأهم بأسمائهم قال ألم أقل لكم إني أعلم غيب السماوات والأرض وأعلم ما تبدون وما كنتم تكتمون

translation: And [mention] when We said to the angels, "Prostrate before Adam"; so they prostrated, except for Iblees. He refused and was arrogant and became of the disbelievers.
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of obedience to Allah's commands and the consequences of disobedience and arrogance. Iblees' refusal to prostrate before Adam, despite Allah's direct order, demonstrates his pride and sense of superiority over Allah's creation. This act of defiance led to Iblees' expulsion from Allah's grace and his categorization as a disbeliever. The verse serves as a reminder to all believers to submit to Allah's will, avoid arrogance, and not to consider oneself superior to others based on personal judgments or preferences, as doing so may lead to one's spiritual downfall.
orig: وإذ قلنا للملائكة اسجدوا لآدم فسجدوا إلا إبليس أبى واستكبر وكان من الكافرين

translation: And We said, "O Adam, dwell, you and your wife, in Paradise and eat therefrom in [ease and] abundance from wherever you will. But do not approach this tree, lest you be among the wrongdoers."
interpretation: This verse is a reminder of God's command to Adam and Eve to enjoy the blessings of Paradise, but also a warning not to disobey His order by approaching the forbidden tree. The interpretation is that God tests humans by giving them free will to make moral choices. Obeying God's commands leads to righteousness, while disobeying them out of arrogance or temptation leads one astray and makes one a wrongdoer against their own soul. The verse emphasizes the importance of heeding God's guidance and boundaries to live a life pleasing to Him.
orig: وقلنا يا آدم اسكن أنت وزوجك الجنة وكلا منها رغدا حيث شئتما ولا تقربا هذه الشجرة فتكونا من الظالمين

translation: But Satan caused them to slip out of it and removed them from that [condition] in which they had been. And We said, "Go down, [all of you], as enemies to one another, and you will have upon the earth a place of settlement and provision for a time."
interpretation: This verse refers to the story of Adam and Eve's expulsion from Paradise. Satan tempted them to eat from the forbidden tree, causing them to disobey Allah's command. As a result, they were sent down to Earth, where they and their descendants would live as enemies to one another, struggling and competing for resources until the end of time. This verse highlights the consequences of giving in to temptation and disobeying Allah, but also points to His mercy in providing humanity with a place to live and means of sustenance on Earth, despite their original sin.
orig: فأزلهما الشيطان عنها فأخرجهما مما كانا فيه وقلنا اهبطوا بعضكم لبعض عدو ولكم في الأرض مستقر ومتاع إلى حين

translation: Then Adam received from his Lord [some] words, and He accepted his repentance. Indeed, it is He who is the Accepting of repentance, the Merciful.
interpretation: This verse highlights the mercy and forgiveness of Allah towards His creation. Despite Adam's disobedience in the Garden of Eden, Allah did not abandon him. Instead, He taught Adam words of repentance, which Adam accepted and recited sincerely. As a result, Allah forgave him, demonstrating His infinite mercy and willingness to accept the repentance of His servants, no matter how great their sins may be. This verse serves as a reminder to all believers that the door of repentance is always open, and that Allah is ever ready to forgive those who turn to Him with sincerity and humility.
orig: فتلقى آدم من ربه كلمات فتاب عليه إنه هو التواب الرحيم

translation: We said, "Go down from it, all of you. And when guidance comes to you from Me, whoever follows My guidance - there will be no fear concerning them, nor will they grieve."
interpretation: This verse is a reminder of God's mercy and guidance to humanity. It emphasizes that those who follow the guidance sent by God will be free from fear and grief in this world and the hereafter. The verse implies that God's guidance is available to all people, regardless of their background or circumstances. It also suggests that following God's guidance is a choice that individuals must make for themselves. The promise of being free from fear and grief is a powerful incentive for people to follow the path laid out by God. Ultimately, this verse highlights the importance of faith and submission to God's will as a means of attaining inner peace and spiritual fulfillment.
orig: قلنا اهبطوا منها جميعا فإما يأتينكم مني هدى فمن تبع هداي فلا خوف عليهم ولا هم يحزنون

translation: But those who disbelieved and denied Our signs - those are the companions of the Fire; they will abide therein eternally.
interpretation: This verse serves as a stark warning to those who reject faith in God and deny His revelations. It emphasizes the grave consequences of disbelief, stating that those who choose this path will be condemned to the eternal punishment of Hell. The verse highlights the importance of faith and the acceptance of God's messages, as it is the key to avoiding the fate of the deniers. It also underscores the finality and permanence of the punishment for those who persist in their disbelief, as they will abide in the Fire forever, with no hope of escape or redemption.
orig: والذين كفروا وكذبوا بآياتنا أولئك أصحاب النار هم فيها خالدون

translation: O Children of Israel! Remember My Favour which I bestowed upon you, and fulfill (your obligations to) My Covenant (with you) so that I fulfill (My Obligations to) your covenant (with Me), and fear none but Me.
interpretation: This verse is a reminder to the Children of Israel of the favors and blessings that Allah has bestowed upon them, and a call for them to fulfill their covenant with Him. The interpretation is that the Children of Israel should be grateful for the blessings and guidance that Allah has given them, and in return, they should fulfill their obligations and worship Him alone, without associating partners with Him. They should fear Allah and be mindful of their actions, knowing that He is aware of all that they do. This verse emphasizes the importance of remembering Allah's favors, being grateful to Him, and fulfilling one's obligations towards Him.
orig: يا بني إسرائيل اذكروا نعمتي التي أنعمت عليكم وأوفوا بعهدي أوف بعهدكم وإياي فارهبون

translation: And believe in what I have sent down confirming that which is [already] with you, and be not the first to disbelieve in it. And do not exchange My signs for a small price, and fear [only] Me.
interpretation: This verse is a call to the People of the Book (Jews and Christians) to believe in the message revealed to Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him), as it confirms the truth they already possess in their scriptures. It warns them against being the first to reject this message and encourages them to embrace it wholeheartedly. The verse also cautions against selling out one's faith for worldly gains or temporal benefits, emphasizing that true believers should fear Allah alone and prioritize their loyalty to Him above all else. It highlights the importance of recognizing and accepting the continuity of Allah's message through all prophets and the unity of the divine message throughout history.
orig: وآمنوا بما أنزلت مصدقا لما معكم ولا تكونوا أول كافر به ولا تشتروا بآياتي ثمنا قليلا وإياي فاتقون

translation: And do not mix the truth with falsehood or conceal the truth while you know [it].
interpretation: This verse is a warning against distorting or hiding the truth, especially when one knows it. It cautions against confusing truth with falsehood or presenting them as indistinguishable. The Qur'an emphasizes the importance of upholding truth and not deceiving others by mixing it with lies or concealing it. Doing so is a grave sin, as it misleads people and corrupts the purity of the truth. The verse reminds us of the responsibility to be honest and truthful, and to courageously stand up for what is right, even if it may be difficult or unpopular. Ultimately, the truth will prevail, and those who manipulate or hide it will be held accountable by Allah.
orig: ولا تلبسوا الحق بالباطل وتكتموا الحق وأنتم تعلمون

translation: And establish prayer and give zakah and bow with those who bow [in worship and obedience].
interpretation: This verse is commanding the believers to uphold the ritual prayer (salah), pay the obligatory alms (zakah), and join the community of worshippers in congregation. It emphasizes the importance of both the individual and communal aspects of worship in Islam. Establishing regular prayer and giving charity are two of the core pillars of the Islamic faith. By participating in congregational prayers, one demonstrates unity, humility and devotion to Allah alongside fellow believers. This verse highlights how ritual acts of worship, when performed sincerely, serve to bind the Muslim community together and strengthen each individual's connection with God.
orig: وأقيموا الصلاة وآتوا الزكاة واركعوا مع الراكعين

translation: Do you order righteousness of the people and forget yourselves while you recite the Scripture? Then will you not reason?
interpretation: This verse is a strong condemnation of hypocrisy. It criticizes those who preach righteousness and virtues to others, yet fail to practice those same teachings themselves, even though they read and recite scripture which contains those teachings. The rhetorical question at the end is a rebuke, implying that such behavior demonstrates a lack of understanding, reasoning and self-awareness. The message is clear - one must internalize and sincerely apply the moral and ethical principles they advocate to others. Scholars consider this an important reminder for religious teachers and scholars in particular to hold themselves to the high standards they preach.
orig: أتأمرون الناس بالبر وتنسون أنفسكم وأنتم تتلون الكتاب أفلا تعقلون

translation: And seek help through patience and prayer. Indeed, it is difficult except for the humbly submissive [to Allah]
interpretation: This verse encourages seeking assistance through two powerful means: patience and prayer. Patience helps in enduring life's trials, while prayer connects one to Allah, seeking His aid and guidance. The verse acknowledges that being steadfast in prayer and patience is challenging, except for those who humble themselves before Allah with complete submission and sincerity. It emphasizes the importance of developing humility and reverence to make the practice of patience and prayer easier, thereby facilitating the path to self-improvement and gaining Allah's help in overcoming hardships.
orig: واستعينوا بالصبر والصلاة وإنها لكبيرة إلا على الخاشعين

translation: Who are certain that they will meet their Lord and that they will return to Him.
interpretation: This verse speaks about the believers who have firm faith and conviction that they will ultimately meet their Lord after death and that they will return to Him for judgment. This belief in the afterlife and accountability instills in them a sense of responsibility and motivates them to lead righteous lives in accordance with God's commandments. They strive to do good deeds and avoid sins, knowing that they will be held answerable for their actions when they stand before their Lord. This unwavering faith gives them hope and inner peace even amidst the trials and challenges of worldly life.
orig: الذين يظنون أنهم ملاقو ربهم وأنهم إليه راجعون

translation: O Children of Israel! Remember My Favour which I bestowed upon you and that I preferred you over the worlds.
interpretation: This verse is a reminder from Allah to the Children of Israel, the descendants of Prophet Jacob, of the numerous blessings and favors He had bestowed upon them. These favors included being chosen as the recipients of divine revelation, being granted prophets and messengers from among them, and being given a special status above all other nations during their time. The verse emphasizes the importance of gratitude and remembrance of Allah's blessings, as it is through acknowledging and appreciating these favors that one can truly submit to Allah and follow His guidance. It also serves as a warning against arrogance and a reminder that the special status granted to the Children of Israel was not due to their own superiority, but rather a result of Allah's grace and mercy.
orig: يا بني إسرائيل اذكروا نعمتي التي أنعمت عليكم وأني فضلتكم على العالمين

translation: And fear a Day when no soul will suffice for another soul at all, nor will intercession be accepted from it, nor will compensation be taken from it, nor will they be aided.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of individual accountability on the Day of Judgment. It reminds believers that on that day, no one will be able to help or benefit another person, regardless of their closeness or relationship in this world. Intercession, which is the act of pleading on behalf of someone else, will not be accepted unless Allah permits it. Additionally, no compensation or ransom can be paid to save oneself from the consequences of their actions. This highlights the significance of leading a righteous life and being mindful of one's deeds, as ultimately, everyone will be held responsible for their own actions and will face the consequences alone, without any external aid or support.
orig: واتقوا يوما لا تجزي نفس عن نفس شيئا ولا يقبل منها شفاعة ولا يؤخذ منها عدل ولا هم ينصرون

translation: And [recall] when We saved you from the people of Pharaoh, who afflicted you with the worst torment, slaughtering your [newborn] sons and keeping your females alive. And in that was a great trial from your Lord.
interpretation: This verse is a reminder to the Children of Israel of the great favor that Allah bestowed upon them by saving them from the tyranny and oppression of Pharaoh and his people. Pharaoh had subjected the Israelites to the worst kind of torture and humiliation, killing their male children and sparing their females, possibly to use them as slaves. This verse emphasizes that their deliverance from such a great affliction was a tremendous blessing and a test from Allah, requiring gratitude and faithfulness to Him. It also serves as a lesson for all believers, reminding them of Allah's power to save His servants from even the most dire of circumstances and the importance of remaining steadfast in faith during times of hardship and oppression.
orig: وإذ نجيناكم من آل فرعون يسومونكم سوء العذاب يذبحون أبناءكم ويستحيون نساءكم وفي ذلكم بلاء من ربكم عظيم

translation: And [recall] when We parted the sea for you and saved you and drowned the people of Pharaoh while you were looking on.
interpretation: This verse is a reminder to the Children of Israel of the great miracle that Allah performed for them when He saved them from the tyranny of Pharaoh. It highlights Allah's power and His ability to protect and save His believing servants even in the most dire of circumstances. The verse also serves as a warning to those who oppose Allah and His messengers, as the fate of Pharaoh and his people demonstrates the consequences of such defiance. Moreover, it emphasizes the importance of gratitude and remembrance of Allah's favors, as the Children of Israel witnessed this incredible event firsthand, yet they still strayed and disobeyed Allah later on. Thus, the verse encourages believers to remain steadfast in their faith and to always remember and appreciate the blessings and miracles that Allah bestows upon them.
orig: وإذ فرقنا بكم البحر فأنجيناكم وأغرقنا آل فرعون وأنتم تنظرون

translation: And [recall] when We made an appointment with Moses for forty nights. Then you took [for worship] the calf after him, while you were wrongdoers.
interpretation: This verse is a reminder of the incident when Allah appointed Moses for forty nights to receive the Torah, but in his absence, the Israelites turned to worshipping the golden calf. This act of idolatry is condemned as a grave sin and a clear act of wrongdoing. It highlights the importance of remaining steadfast in faith and avoiding the worship of false deities, even in the absence of a prophet or leader. The verse also emphasizes the gravity of the Israelites' actions, as they had just been saved from Pharaoh's oppression and had witnessed numerous miracles, yet they still strayed from the path of monotheism.
orig: وإذ واعدنا موسى أربعين ليلة ثم اتخذتم العجل من بعده وأنتم ظالمون

translation: Then We forgave you after that so perhaps you would be grateful.
interpretation: This verse highlights the immense mercy and forgiveness of Allah towards His servants, even after they have committed grave errors or sins. It suggests that Allah's forgiveness is a means for people to reflect upon their actions, turn back to Him in repentance, and express gratitude for His blessings and mercy. The verse implies that through Allah's forgiveness, people are given another chance to mend their ways and to live a life of righteousness and thankfulness to their Lord. It serves as a reminder that no matter how far one may stray, the door of repentance and forgiveness is always open, and that Allah's mercy encompasses all things. The verse encourages believers to constantly seek Allah's forgiveness and to be grateful for His countless blessings and favors upon them.
orig: ثم عفونا عنكم من بعد ذلك لعلكم تشكرون

translation: And [recall] when We gave Moses the Scripture and criterion that perhaps you would be guided.
interpretation: This verse reminds us of the great favor that Allah bestowed upon Prophet Moses and his people by giving them the Torah, which contained divine teachings and commandments. The "criterion" mentioned here likely refers to the ability to distinguish between truth and falsehood, right and wrong, that comes with the guidance of revelation. By mentioning this favor, Allah encourages the believers to seek guidance through the Qur'an, just as the followers of Moses were expected to be guided by the Torah. It emphasizes the importance and necessity of divine revelation in leading people to the straight path and attaining success in this life and the Hereafter.
orig: وإذ آتينا موسى الكتاب والفرقان لعلكم تهتدون

translation: And [recall] when Moses said to his people, "O my people, indeed you have wronged yourselves by your taking of the calf [for worship]. So repent to your Creator and kill yourselves. That is best for [all of] you in the sight of your Creator." Then He accepted your repentance; indeed, He is the Accepting of repentance, the Merciful.
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of sincere repentance and the severity of worshipping false idols. Moses admonishes his people for worshipping the golden calf, urging them to seek forgiveness from Allah by purifying themselves through self-reflection and renouncing their wrongdoings. The act of "killing yourselves" metaphorically represents the need to suppress one's ego and desires that lead to sin. The verse emphasizes that true repentance involves a genuine change of heart and actions, and that Allah, in His infinite mercy, accepts the repentance of those who sincerely turn to Him.
orig: وإذ قال موسى لقومه يا قوم إنكم ظلمتم أنفسكم باتخاذكم العجل فتوبوا إلى بارئكم فاقتلوا أنفسكم ذلكم خير لكم عند بارئكم فتاب عليكم إنه هو التواب الرحيم

translation: And [recall] when you said, "O Moses, we will never believe you until we see Allah outright"; so the thunderbolt took you while you were looking on.
interpretation: This verse is a reminder to the Children of Israel of their arrogance and lack of faith. Despite witnessing the miracles and signs of Allah through Moses, they demanded to see Allah directly, refusing to believe until their demand was met. This audacious request demonstrated their lack of true faith and submission to Allah. As a consequence of their insolence, Allah caused a thunderbolt to seize them while they were watching, serving as a severe punishment for their rebellious attitude. The verse emphasizes the importance of having complete faith in Allah and His messengers without making unreasonable demands or setting conditions for belief.
orig: وإذ قلتم يا موسى لن نؤمن لك حتى نرى الله جهرة فأخذتكم الصاعقة وأنتم تنظرون

translation: Then We revived you after your death that perhaps you would be grateful.
interpretation: This verse is a reminder of Allah's power and mercy. It refers to an incident where Allah caused a group of people to die and then brought them back to life. This was done to demonstrate His ability to resurrect the dead and to give people a second chance at life. The verse encourages gratitude towards Allah for His blessings and for the opportunity to live again. It also serves as a reminder that death is not the end, and that there will be a Day of Judgment when all will be resurrected and held accountable for their deeds in this life.
orig: ثم بعثناكم من بعد موتكم لعلكم تشكرون

translation: And We shaded you with clouds and sent down to you manna and quails [saying], "Eat from the good things with which We have provided you." And they wronged Us not - but they were [only] wronging themselves.
interpretation: This verse is a reminder of Allah's favors upon the Children of Israel during their journey in the wilderness. The "clouds" provided shade and comfort from the harsh desert sun. "Manna and quails" were sent as sustenance, a miraculous provision from Allah. Despite these blessings, the people were ungrateful and disobeyed Allah's commands. Their actions did not harm Allah in any way, but rather they were only harming themselves spiritually by their disobedience and ingratitude. It emphasizes that sinning and wrongdoing ultimately harms one's own soul, and that Allah's favors should be met with gratitude and obedience.
orig: وظللنا عليكم الغمام وأنزلنا عليكم المن والسلوى كلوا من طيبات ما رزقناكم وما ظلمونا ولكن كانوا أنفسهم يظلمون

translation: And [recall] when We said, "Enter this city and eat from it wherever you will in [ease and] abundance, and enter the gate bowing humbly and say, '[O Allah], relieve us of our burdens. ' We will [then] forgive your sins for you, and We will increase the doers of good [in goodness and reward]."
interpretation: This verse is a reminder of Allah's favor upon the Children of Israel. He commanded them to enter the holy land He had granted them, freely enjoy its bounties, and enter its gate with humility and repentance, seeking forgiveness for their sins. In return, Allah promises to forgive their wrongdoings and increase His rewards for those who do good deeds. It emphasizes the importance of obedience to Allah's commands, humility, seeking forgiveness, and striving for righteousness in order to attain Allah's mercy and blessings.
orig: وإذ قلنا ادخلوا هذه القرية فكلوا منها حيث شئتم رغدا وادخلوا الباب سجدا وقولوا حطة نغفر لكم خطاياكم وسنزيد المحسنين

translation: But those who wronged changed [those words] to a statement other than that which had been said to them, so We sent down upon those who wronged a punishment from the sky because they were defiantly disobeying.
interpretation: This verse highlights the consequences of disobedience and altering the divine message. When people deliberately change the words and commandments given to them by Allah, they invite His wrath upon themselves. The verse emphasizes that those who engage in such wrongdoing and corruption will face severe punishment from the heavens, as a result of their persistent disobedience and defiance of Allah's laws. It serves as a warning to all believers to adhere to the authentic teachings of Islam and not to distort or manipulate the divine message for their own interests or desires.
orig: فبدل الذين ظلموا قولا غير الذي قيل لهم فأنزلنا على الذين ظلموا رجزا من السماء بما كانوا يفسقون

translation: And [recall] when Moses prayed for water for his people, so We said, "Strike with your staff the stone." And there gushed forth from it twelve springs, and every people knew its watering place. "Eat and drink from the provision of Allah, and do not commit abuse on the earth, spreading corruption."
interpretation: This verse is a reminder of Allah's mercy and provision for the Children of Israel during their time in the wilderness. When they were in need of water, Allah instructed Moses to strike a rock with his staff, miraculously causing twelve springs to gush forth, providing each tribe with its own water source. This demonstrates Allah's power over His creation and His ability to provide for His servants, even in the most difficult of circumstances. The verse also serves as a warning against spreading corruption on the earth by reminding the Children of Israel to be grateful for Allah's blessings and to use them responsibly, without committing abuse or causing harm to others or the environment.
orig: وإذ استسقى موسى لقومه فقلنا اضرب بعصاك الحجر فانفجرت منه اثنتا عشرة عينا قد علم كل أناس مشربهم كلوا واشربوا من رزق الله ولا تعثوا في الأرض مفسدين

translation: And [recall] when you said, "O Moses, we can never endure one [kind of] food. So call upon your Lord to bring forth for us from the earth its green herbs and its cucumbers and its garlic and its lentils and its onions." [Moses] said, "Would you exchange what is better for what is less? Go into [any] settlement and indeed, you will have what you have asked." And they were covered with humiliation and poverty and returned with anger from Allah [upon them]. That was because they [repeatedly] disbelieved in the signs of Allah and killed the prophets without right. That was because they disobeyed and were [habitually] transgressing.
interpretation: This verse highlights the ingratitude and disobedience of the Children of Israel during their time in the wilderness. Despite being provided with manna and quails by Allah, they complained to Moses about the monotony of their food and demanded a variety of vegetables. This request demonstrated their lack of appreciation for Allah's blessings and their preference for worldly desires over spiritual sustenance. As a consequence of their ungrateful behavior and their repeated rejection of Allah's signs and prophets, they were subjected to humiliation, poverty, and divine anger. The verse emphasizes the importance of gratitude, obedience to Allah, and the consequences of persistent disbelief and transgression.
orig: وإذ قلتم يا موسى لن نصبر على طعام واحد فادع لنا ربك يخرج لنا مما تنبت الأرض من بقلها وقثائها وفومها وعدسها وبصلها قال أتستبدلون الذي هو أدنى بالذي هو خير اهبطوا مصرا فإن لكم ما سألتم وضربت عليهم الذلة والمسكنة وباءوا بغضب من الله ذلك بأنهم كانوا يكفرون بآيات الله ويقتلون النبيين بغير الحق ذلك بما عصوا وكانوا يعتدون

translation: Indeed, those who believed and those who were Jews or Christians or Sabeans [before Prophet Muhammad] - those [among them] who believed in Allah and the Last Day and did righteousness - will have their reward with their Lord, and no fear will there be concerning them, nor will they grieve.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the universality of God's message and the equality of all people in His sight, regardless of their religious affiliation. It suggests that what matters most is one's faith in God, belief in the Day of Judgment, and good deeds, rather than the specific religion one follows. Those who sincerely believe and do good will be rewarded by God and have nothing to fear in the afterlife. This interpretation promotes religious tolerance and the idea that righteousness is not limited to a particular faith tradition.
orig: إن الذين آمنوا والذين هادوا والنصارى والصابئين من آمن بالله واليوم الآخر وعمل صالحا فلهم أجرهم عند ربهم ولا خوف عليهم ولا هم يحزنون

translation: And [recall] when We took your covenant and raised over you the mount, [saying], "Take what We have given you with determination and remember what is in it that perhaps you may become righteous."
interpretation: This verse is a reminder to the Children of Israel of the covenant they made with Allah. It emphasizes the importance of fulfilling one's commitments and obligations to Allah. The raising of the mount above them symbolizes the gravity and significance of this covenant. The verse also stresses the need to hold fast to the teachings and commandments given by Allah with strength and determination. Additionally, it encourages the remembrance and contemplation of these divine injunctions, as this can lead to righteousness and the development of a God-conscious mindset, which is essential for spiritual growth and attaining piety.
orig: وإذ أخذنا ميثاقكم ورفعنا فوقكم الطور خذوا ما آتيناكم بقوة واذكروا ما فيه لعلكم تتقون

translation: Then you turned away after that. And if it was not for the Grace of Allah upon you and His Mercy, you would have been among the losers.
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of Allah's grace and mercy in guiding and protecting the believers. It suggests that even when people turn away from the right path after being guided to it, Allah's favor and compassion can still save them from being among the losers in this world and the hereafter. The verse emphasizes the idea that without divine assistance and forgiveness, humans are prone to going astray and suffering loss. It serves as a reminder for believers to constantly seek Allah's grace, remain grateful for His blessings, and strive to stay on the straight path to avoid being among the losers.
orig: ثم توليتم من بعد ذلك فلولا فضل الله عليكم ورحمته لكنتم من الخاسرين

translation: And you had already known about those who transgressed among you concerning the sabbath, and We said to them, "Be apes, despised."
interpretation: This verse is a reminder of a past incident where a group of people, despite knowing the commandment to keep the Sabbath holy, violated it. As a consequence of their disobedience, Allah transformed them into apes as a form of humiliation and punishment. This serves as a warning to all believers that transgressing the limits set by Allah and disregarding His commands can lead to severe consequences in this world and the hereafter. It emphasizes the importance of obedience, reverence for divine laws, and the need to learn from the mistakes of the past.
orig: ولقد علمتم الذين اعتدوا منكم في السبت فقلنا لهم كونوا قردة خاسئين

translation: And We made it a deterrent punishment for those who were present and those who succeeded [them] and a lesson for those who fear Allah.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah's punishment serves as a severe warning and a lesson for all, both for those who witnessed it and for the generations to come. It is a reminder for the righteous to remain steadfast in their faith and to fear Allah, as they should be mindful of the consequences of disobedience. The verse highlights the importance of learning from the past and being aware that Allah's punishment can befall anyone who transgresses His boundaries. It encourages believers to lead a life of piety and righteousness, seeking to avoid the fate of those who were punished for their sins.
orig: فجعلناها نكالا لما بين يديها وما خلفها وموعظة للمتقين

translation: And [recall] when Moses said to his people, "Indeed, Allah commands you to slaughter a cow." They said, "Do you take us in ridicule?" He said, "I seek refuge in Allah from being among the ignorant."
interpretation: This verse is a reminder of the story of Moses and the cow, where Allah commanded the Children of Israel to slaughter a cow as a means of revealing the identity of a murderer. The people's initial response was one of disbelief and mockery, thinking that Moses was joking with them. However, Moses sought refuge in Allah from being among the ignorant, emphasizing the seriousness of the divine command. This story highlights the importance of obedience to Allah's commands, even when they may seem unusual or difficult to understand. It also demonstrates the need for faith and trust in Allah's wisdom, as the slaughtering of the cow ultimately served a greater purpose in revealing the truth and administering justice.
orig: وإذ قال موسى لقومه إن الله يأمركم أن تذبحوا بقرة قالوا أتتخذنا هزوا قال أعوذ بالله أن أكون من الجاهلين

translation: They said, "Call upon your Lord to make clear to us what it is." [Moses] said, "[Allah] says, 'It is a cow which is neither old nor virgin, but median between that,' so do what you are commanded."
interpretation: This verse is about the story of the cow that the Children of Israel were commanded to slaughter. When they asked Moses for more details about the cow, Allah revealed to him that it should be neither too old nor too young, but of middle age. This specific description was a test for the Children of Israel to see if they would obey Allah's command without question or hesitation. The verse emphasizes the importance of following divine instructions precisely and without doubt or delay, as a demonstration of true faith and submission to Allah's will.
orig: قالوا ادع لنا ربك يبين لنا ما هي قال إنه يقول إنها بقرة لا فارض ولا بكر عوان بين ذلك فافعلوا ما تؤمرون

translation: They said, "Call upon your Lord to make clear to us what is her color." He said, "He says, 'It is a yellow cow, bright in color - pleasing to the observers.' "
interpretation: This verse is emphasizing the importance of following God's commands precisely, even if they may seem arbitrary or unnecessary. The people's repeated questioning of Moses regarding the specifics of the cow they were to slaughter demonstrates their reluctance and lack of faith. God's detailed response, specifying the exact color of the cow, highlights the need for obedience and submission to His will, without questioning the wisdom behind His commands. It also shows that God is aware of every detail and that nothing is too insignificant for His attention. The vibrant yellow color of the cow, pleasing to the eye, could symbolize the beauty and perfection of following God's path, even when we don't fully understand it.
orig: قالوا ادع لنا ربك يبين لنا ما لونها قال إنه يقول إنها بقرة صفراء فاقع لونها تسر الناظرين

translation: They said, "Call upon your Lord to make clear to us what it is. Indeed, [all] cows look alike to us. And indeed we, if Allah wills, will be guided."
interpretation: This verse is a continuation of the story of the cow that the Children of Israel were commanded to slaughter. They kept asking Moses for more and more details about the cow, rather than simply obeying the command. Their excessive questioning is seen as a sign of their reluctance and lack of faith. The repeated questioning also shows how people can sometimes complicate matters unnecessarily when God's commands are clear. The verse ends with them saying "if Allah wills, we will be guided," indicating that guidance ultimately comes from Allah, but also that they will only follow the command if they feel like it, making their obedience conditional. This is seen as a flawed attitude in the Quranic discourse.
orig: قالوا ادع لنا ربك يبين لنا ما هي إن البقر تشابه علينا وإنا إن شاء الله لمهتدون

translation: He said, "He says it is a cow neither trained to plow the earth nor to irrigate the field, one free from fault with no spot upon her." They said, "Now you have come with the truth." So they slaughtered her, but they could hardly do it.
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of following divine guidance precisely. The Israelites were instructed to sacrifice a specific type of cow, but they kept asking for more details, making the task increasingly difficult. This shows that when we receive clear guidance from God, we should act upon it without hesitation or excessive questioning. The verse also emphasizes the need for obedience and submission to God's commands, even when they may seem challenging or inconvenient. Ultimately, the Israelites did slaughter the cow as instructed, but their initial reluctance and near failure to do so serves as a reminder for believers to trust in God's wisdom and follow His guidance wholeheartedly.
orig: قال إنه يقول إنها بقرة لا ذلول تثير الأرض ولا تسقي الحرث مسلمة لا شية فيها قالوا الآن جئت بالحق فذبحوها وما كادوا يفعلون

translation: And [recall] when you slew a man and disputed over it, but Allah was to bring out that which you were concealing.
interpretation: This verse refers to a murder that took place among the Children of Israel, where they argued and blamed each other for the crime, trying to conceal the truth. However, Allah reveals that He will expose what they tried to hide, emphasizing that no secret can be kept from Him. It serves as a reminder that Allah is All-Knowing and that the truth will always prevail, no matter how much one tries to conceal it. The verse encourages people to be truthful and to seek justice, as Allah will ultimately bring the truth to light and hold the guilty accountable for their actions.
orig: وإذ قتلتم نفسا فادارأتم فيها والله مخرج ما كنتم تكتمون

translation: So We said: "Strike him with a part of it." Thus Allah brings the dead to life, and He shows you His signs that you may understand.
interpretation: This verse demonstrates Allah's power to resurrect the dead, just as He brought the murdered man back to life when he was struck with a part of the sacrificed cow. It is a reminder for mankind to reflect upon the signs of Allah's omnipotence and to use their intellect to recognize the truth of His message. The verse emphasizes that Allah has the ability to give life to the dead, both physically and spiritually, and that this should serve as a powerful reminder for people to be mindful of their actions and to live according to His guidance.
orig: فقلنا اضربوه ببعضها كذلك يحيي الله الموتى ويريكم آياته لعلكم تعقلون

translation: Then your hearts hardened after that, being like stones or even harder. For indeed, there are stones from which rivers burst forth, and there are some of them that split open and water comes out, and there are some of them that fall down for fear of Allah. And Allah is not unaware of what you do.
interpretation: This verse is a reminder of how the hearts of people can become hardened and unresponsive to the message of Allah, even after witnessing clear signs and miracles. It compares such hearts to stones, which are known for their hardness and lack of emotion. However, the verse also points out that even among stones, there are those that have the capacity to bring forth water and sustain life, and there are those that are so moved by the fear of Allah that they crumble and fall. This serves as a powerful metaphor for the potential of the human heart to either remain unmoved and lifeless, or to be softened and humbled by the remembrance of Allah. The verse ends with a warning that Allah is fully aware of all our deeds, emphasizing the importance of striving to keep our hearts alive and responsive to His message.
orig: ثم قست قلوبكم من بعد ذلك فهي كالحجارة أو أشد قسوة وإن من الحجارة لما يتفجر منه الأنهار وإن منها لما يشقق فيخرج منه الماء وإن منها لما يهبط من خشية الله وما الله بغافل عما تعملون

translation: Do you covet [the hope, O believers], that they would believe for you while a party of them used to hear the words of Allah and then distort the Torah after they had understood it while they were knowing?
interpretation: This verse is addressing the believers, expressing surprise that they would expect the Jews to believe in Islam, when some of them had heard the words of Allah in the Torah, understood them, and then deliberately distorted their meaning. It suggests that the Jews who engaged in such distortion knew full well that they were misrepresenting the truth, but did so anyway out of stubborn opposition. The implication is that people who would act in such a deceptive manner with their own scriptures cannot be trusted to embrace the message of Islam with sincerity and honesty.
orig: أفتطمعون أن يؤمنوا لكم وقد كان فريق منهم يسمعون كلام الله ثم يحرفونه من بعد ما عقلوه وهم يعلمون

translation: And when they meet those who believe, they say, "We believe"; but when they are alone with one another, they say, "Do you talk to them about what Allah has revealed to you so they can argue with you about it before your Lord?" Then will you not reason?
interpretation: This verse is referring to the hypocrites who outwardly pretend to be believers, but when they are alone with each other, they reveal their true disbelief and mock the believers. They question why the believers would share the knowledge that Allah has given them, as it could be used against them in the Hereafter. The verse is criticizing the hypocrites for their lack of understanding and reasoning, as they fail to realize that Allah is aware of their true intentions and that they will be held accountable for their actions in the Hereafter.
orig: وإذا لقوا الذين آمنوا قالوا آمنا وإذا خلا بعضهم إلى بعض قالوا أتحدثونهم بما فتح الله عليكم ليحاجوكم به عند ربكم أفلا تعقلون

translation: Do they not know that Allah knows what they conceal and what they declare?
interpretation: This verse is a reminder that Allah is all-knowing and aware of everything, both what people hide in their hearts and what they openly express. It serves as a warning that one cannot keep secrets from Allah or deceive Him, as He has knowledge of all things, including people's innermost thoughts and intentions. This understanding should motivate believers to be sincere in their faith and actions, knowing that Allah is always watching and will hold them accountable for their deeds, whether done in private or in public.
orig: أولا يعلمون أن الله يعلم ما يسرون وما يعلنون

translation: And among them are unlettered ones who do not know the Scripture except in wishful thinking, but they are only assuming.
interpretation: This verse is referring to a group of people who are illiterate and have no real knowledge of the scriptures. They rely only on hearsay, wishful thinking, and assumptions about what the scriptures contain, rather than having any actual understanding or direct knowledge of them. It suggests that their beliefs about the scriptures are baseless and misguided, as they are not grounded in true comprehension of the texts. The verse implies the importance of seeking authentic knowledge and understanding, rather than blindly following conjecture or unsubstantiated opinions about religious matters.
orig: ومنهم أميون لا يعلمون الكتاب إلا أماني وإن هم إلا يظنون

translation: So woe to those who write the "scripture" with their own hands, then say, "This is from Allah," in order to exchange it for a small price. Woe to them for what their hands have written and woe to them for what they earn.
interpretation: This verse condemns those who falsely attribute their own writings to Allah for worldly gain. It warns of severe punishment for those who engage in such deceptive practices, emphasizing the gravity of fabricating religious scriptures for personal benefit. The repetition of "woe" underscores the seriousness of the offense and the inevitable consequences that await those who knowingly mislead others by claiming divine authorship of their own words, seeking to profit from their deception. The verse highlights the importance of honesty, integrity, and the preservation of authentic religious teachings.
orig: فويل للذين يكتبون الكتاب بأيديهم ثم يقولون هذا من عند الله ليشتروا به ثمنا قليلا فويل لهم مما كتبت أيديهم وويل لهم مما يكسبون

translation: And they say, "Never will the Fire touch us, except for a few days." Say, "Have you taken a covenant with Allah? For Allah will never break His covenant. Or do you say about Allah that which you do not know?"
interpretation: This verse is addressing the false belief held by some people that even if they were to face the punishment of Hell, it would only be for a short period of time. It challenges this notion by asking if they have made a special agreement with Allah that would limit their time in Hell. The rhetorical question implies that no such agreement exists, and that Allah's justice cannot be compromised. The verse also suggests that those who make such claims are speaking without knowledge, attributing to Allah something that they cannot be certain of. It emphasizes the gravity of making unfounded assertions about Allah and His judgment, and warns against the consequences of doing so.
orig: وقالوا لن تمسنا النار إلا أياما معدودة قل أتخذتم عند الله عهدا فلن يخلف الله عهده أم تقولون على الله ما لا تعلمون

translation: Yes, whoever earns evil and his sin has encompassed him - those are the companions of the Fire; they will abide therein eternally.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the consequences of persistently engaging in sinful actions. It suggests that those who continuously commit evil deeds, to the point where their sins completely surround and define them, will be the inhabitants of Hell, condemned to remain there forever. The interpretation highlights the gravity of allowing oneself to be consumed by wrongdoing, as it leads to an eternal punishment in the afterlife. It serves as a warning to individuals to be mindful of their actions and to strive for righteousness, lest they face the severe repercussions of their misdeeds.
orig: بلى من كسب سيئة وأحاطت به خطيئته فأولئك أصحاب النار هم فيها خالدون

translation: And those who believe and do righteous deeds - they are the companions of Paradise, they will abide therein eternally.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of both faith and good deeds in attaining eternal salvation in Paradise. It suggests that merely believing in God is not enough; one must also actively strive to do what is right and virtuous in accordance with God's commands.
