Those who combine sincere faith with righteous actions will be rewarded with the everlasting bliss of Paradise, where they will remain forever as its honored companions. This interpretation highlights the significance of aligning one's beliefs with their actions and living a life dedicated to pleasing God in order to achieve the ultimate goal of eternal happiness in the Hereafter.
orig: والذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات أولئك أصحاب الجنة هم فيها خالدون

translation: And [recall] when We took the covenant from the Children of Israel, [enjoining upon them], "Do not worship except Allah; and to parents do good and to relatives, orphans, and the needy. And speak to people good [words] and establish prayer and give zakah." Then you turned away, except a few of you, and you were refusing.
interpretation: This verse reminds the Children of Israel of the covenant they made with Allah, which included worshipping none but Him, treating parents, relatives, orphans, and the needy with kindness, speaking gently to people, establishing prayer, and giving zakah (obligatory charity). However, most of them turned away from this covenant and became heedless of their obligations. The verse emphasizes the importance of fulfilling one's commitments to Allah and maintaining good relations with fellow human beings, especially those who are vulnerable or in need. It also highlights the significance of prayer and charity as essential acts of worship and social responsibility.
orig: وإذ أخذنا ميثاق بني إسرائيل لا تعبدون إلا الله وبالوالدين إحسانا وذي القربى واليتامى والمساكين وقولوا للناس حسنا وأقيموا الصلاة وآتوا الزكاة ثم توليتم إلا قليلا منكم وأنتم معرضون

translation: And [recall] when We took your covenant, [saying], "Do not shed each other's blood or evict one another from your homes." Then you acknowledged [this] while you were witnessing.
interpretation: This verse is a reminder of the covenant that Allah took from the Children of Israel, prohibiting them from killing each other or expelling one another from their homes. The verse emphasizes the sanctity of human life and the importance of maintaining a peaceful and harmonious society. It also highlights the significance of keeping one's promises and commitments, as the Children of Israel acknowledged this covenant while witnessing it. The verse serves as a lesson for all believers to respect the rights of others, refrain from violence and oppression, and fulfill their obligations towards Allah and their fellow human beings.
orig: وإذ أخذنا ميثاقكم لا تسفكون دماءكم ولا تخرجون أنفسكم من دياركم ثم أقررتم وأنتم تشهدون

translation: Then, you are those [same ones who are] killing one another and evicting a party of your people from their homes, cooperating against them in sin and aggression. And if they come to you as captives, you ransom them, although their eviction was forbidden to you. So do you believe in part of the Scripture and disbelieve in part? Then what is the recompense for those who do that among you except disgrace in worldly life; and on the Day of Resurrection they will be sent back to the severest of punishment. And Allah is not unaware of what you do.
interpretation: This verse criticizes the hypocrisy and inconsistency of some people who claim to follow the Scripture. They engaged in infighting, oppression and the unjust expulsion of their own people, which was prohibited. Yet, they would then ransom captives, showing selective application of Scriptural teachings. Believing in only parts of the revelation that suit them while rejecting what does not align with their desires and actions is strongly condemned. Such people are warned of humiliation in this life and severe punishment in the Hereafter, for Allah is fully aware of their deeds and intentions. It emphasizes the importance of upholding justice, avoiding oppression, and following the Scripture in totality with sincerity.
orig: ثم أنتم هؤلاء تقتلون أنفسكم وتخرجون فريقا منكم من ديارهم تظاهرون عليهم بالإثم والعدوان وإن يأتوكم أسارى تفادوهم وهو محرم عليكم إخراجهم أفتؤمنون ببعض الكتاب وتكفرون ببعض فما جزاء من يفعل ذلك منكم إلا خزي في الحياة الدنيا ويوم القيامة يردون إلى أشد العذاب وما الله بغافل عما تعملون

translation: Those are the ones who have bought the life of this world [in exchange] for the Hereafter, so the punishment will not be lightened for them, nor will they be aided.
interpretation: This verse is referring to those who prioritize the temporary pleasures and desires of this worldly life over the eternal rewards of the Hereafter. They have essentially "sold" their chance at Paradise for the fleeting enjoyments of this world. As a result, they will face the full consequences of their actions in the Hereafter, where their punishment will not be reduced, and they will have no one to help or support them. It serves as a reminder for believers to focus on the life to come and not be distracted by the temptations of this world, as the ultimate goal is success in the Hereafter.
orig: أولئك الذين اشتروا الحياة الدنيا بالآخرة فلا يخفف عنهم العذاب ولا هم ينصرون

translation: And We gave Moses the Scripture and followed up after him with messengers. And We gave Jesus, the son of Mary, clear proofs and supported him with the Pure Spirit. But is it [not] that every time a messenger came to you, [O Children of Israel], with what your souls did not desire, you were arrogant? And a party [of messengers] you denied and another party you killed.
interpretation: This verse highlights the rebellious nature of the Children of Israel towards the messengers sent by Allah. Despite being given clear signs and miracles, such as those given to Moses and Jesus, they consistently rejected the messengers whose message did not align with their desires. Their arrogance led them to deny some of the messengers and even kill others. This serves as a warning to all people to humble themselves before the truth and not let their ego or desires cloud their judgment when receiving divine guidance through the prophets.
orig: ولقد آتينا موسى الكتاب وقفينا من بعده بالرسل وآتينا عيسى ابن مريم البينات وأيدناه بروح القدس أفكلما جاءكم رسول بما لا تهوى أنفسكم استكبرتم ففريقا كذبتم وفريقا تقتلون

translation: And they say, "Our hearts are wrapped." But, [in fact], Allah has cursed them for their disbelief, so little is it that they believe.
interpretation: This verse is a response to those who claim that their hearts are sealed or covered, making them unable to understand or accept the message of Islam. However, the Qur'an states that it is not their hearts that are sealed, but rather it is Allah who has cursed them due to their disbelief and rejection of the truth. The verse implies that their lack of faith is a result of their own choices and actions, not because of any inherent inability to comprehend or believe. As a consequence of their disbelief, they have little faith, and their hearts remain closed to the guidance and mercy of Allah.
orig: وقالوا قلوبنا غلف بل لعنهم الله بكفرهم فقليلا ما يؤمنون

translation: And when there came to them a Book from Allah confirming what was with them - although before they used to pray for victory against those who disbelieved - but [then] when there came to them that which they recognized, they disbelieved in it; so the curse of Allah will be upon the disbelievers.
interpretation: This verse highlights the hypocrisy and stubbornness of those who rejected the message of Islam despite recognizing its truth. It suggests that before the advent of Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him), the Jews and Christians used to pray for victory against the pagans, hoping for a new prophet to come and support their faith. However, when the Qur'an was revealed, confirming the teachings of their own scriptures and the arrival of the prophet they had been waiting for, they chose to disbelieve out of pride, envy, or fear of losing their authority. As a result, they incurred the curse of Allah for their deliberate rejection of the truth.
orig: ولما جاءهم كتاب من عند الله مصدق لما معهم وكانوا من قبل يستفتحون على الذين كفروا فلما جاءهم ما عرفوا كفروا به فلعنة الله على الكافرين

translation: How wretched is that for which they sold themselves - that they would disbelieve in what Allah has revealed through [their] outrage that Allah would send down His favor upon whom He wills from among His servants. So they returned having [earned] wrath upon wrath. And for the disbelievers is a humiliating punishment.
interpretation: This verse is criticizing those who reject faith out of jealousy and resentment that Allah would choose to bless some of His servants with revelation and prophethood over others. By doing so, they have earned Allah's anger in this life and a humiliating punishment in the next. It shows the folly of turning away from truth and faith due to pride, envy or tribal prejudices. True believers accept Allah's wisdom in selecting prophets and sending down revelation according to His will, without questioning or begrudging it.
orig: بئسما اشتروا به أنفسهم أن يكفروا بما أنزل الله بغيا أن ينزل الله من فضله على من يشاء من عباده فباءوا بغضب على غضب وللكافرين عذاب مهين

translation: And when it is said to them, "Believe in what Allah has revealed," they say, "We believe in what was revealed to us," and they disbelieve in what is beyond it, while it is the truth confirming that which is with them. Say, "Then why did you kill the prophets of Allah before, if you are believers?"
interpretation: This verse highlights the hypocrisy and selective belief of those who claim to follow divine revelation. They accept only what aligns with their own traditions and reject the truth that comes after, even though it confirms and validates their own scriptures. The rhetorical question exposes their inconsistency, as true believers would not have killed the prophets sent by God. It suggests that their faith is not genuine, and they are merely following their own desires and prejudices rather than submitting to the complete message of Allah.
orig: وإذا قيل لهم آمنوا بما أنزل الله قالوا نؤمن بما أنزل علينا ويكفرون بما وراءه وهو الحق مصدقا لما معهم قل فلم تقتلون أنبياء الله من قبل إن كنتم مؤمنين

translation: And Moses had certainly brought you clear proofs. Then you took the calf [in worship] after that, while you were wrongdoers.
interpretation: This verse is a reminder to the Children of Israel of their past transgression when they worshipped the golden calf, despite the clear signs and miracles that Moses had brought them from Allah. It emphasizes the gravity of their sin and their wrongdoing in turning away from the truth after it had been made evident to them. The verse serves as a warning against forsaking the guidance of Allah and falling into idolatry or the worship of false deities, even after receiving clear proofs and signs. It highlights the importance of remaining steadfast in faith and avoiding the mistakes of previous nations who were led astray by their desires and inclinations.
orig: ولقد جاءكم موسى بالبينات ثم اتخذتم العجل من بعده وأنتم ظالمون

translation: And [recall] when We took your covenant and raised over you the mount, [saying], "Take what We have given you with determination and listen." They said [instead], "We hear and disobey." And their hearts absorbed [the worship of] the calf because of their disbelief. Say, "How wretched is that which your faith enjoins upon you, if you should be believers."
interpretation: This verse is a reminder of the covenant that God took from the Children of Israel, and how they broke it by worshipping the golden calf. Despite God's clear commands and the miraculous signs He showed them, such as raising Mount Sinai above them, they still disobeyed and allowed the love of the calf to penetrate their hearts due to their disbelief. The verse criticizes their faith, suggesting that if this is what their faith commands them to do, then it is a miserable and wretched faith. The message is that true faith should lead to obedience to God, not disobedience.
orig: وإذ أخذنا ميثاقكم ورفعنا فوقكم الطور خذوا ما آتيناكم بقوة واسمعوا قالوا سمعنا وعصينا وأشربوا في قلوبهم العجل بكفرهم قل بئسما يأمركم به إيمانكم إن كنتم مؤمنين

translation: Say, "If the home of the Hereafter with Allah is for you alone and not the [other] people, then wish for death, if you should be truthful."
interpretation: This verse challenges those who claim that Paradise is exclusively reserved for them, and not for others. It tells the Prophet Muhammad to say to them that if they are truthful in their claim, then they should wish for death, as it would hasten their journey to the Hereafter and the exclusive Paradise they claim. However, they will not wish for death because deep down they know that their claim is false and that the Hereafter is not exclusively for them. This verse exposes their hypocrisy and arrogance in making such a claim.
orig: قل إن كانت لكم الدار الآخرة عند الله خالصة من دون الناس فتمنوا الموت إن كنتم صادقين

translation: And they will never wish for it, because of what their hands have put forth. And Allah is Knowing of the wrongdoers.
interpretation: This verse highlights the fact that the wrongdoers and sinners will never wish for death or the Hereafter due to their guilty conscience and the fear of facing the consequences of their evil deeds. They are aware that Allah knows all their wrongdoings, and they will be held accountable for their actions in the afterlife. This serves as a reminder for believers to refrain from committing sins and to always be mindful of Allah's presence and knowledge of their deeds.
orig: ولن يتمنوه أبدا بما قدمت أيديهم والله عليم بالظالمين

translation: And you will surely find them the most greedy of people for life - [even] more than those who associate others with Allah. One of them wishes that he could be granted life a thousand years, but it would not remove him in the least from the [coming] punishment that he should be granted life. And Allah is Seeing of what they do.
interpretation: This verse highlights the intense desire of the disbelievers and polytheists for worldly life, even to the extent of wishing to live for a thousand years. However, their longevity would not save them from the punishment of the Hereafter. It emphasizes that no matter how long one lives in this world, it cannot serve as a substitute for faith and good deeds. The verse also affirms that Allah is fully aware of their actions and intentions, and will hold them accountable accordingly in the afterlife.
orig: ولتجدنهم أحرص الناس على حياة ومن الذين أشركوا يود أحدهم لو يعمر ألف سنة وما هو بمزحزحه من العذاب أن يعمر والله بصير بما يعملون

translation: Say, "Whoever is an enemy to Gabriel - it is [none but] he who has brought the Qur'an down upon your heart, [O Muhammad], by permission of Allah, confirming that which was before it and as guidance and good tidings for the believers."
interpretation: This verse affirms that the Qur'an was revealed to Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) through the angel Gabriel, by Allah's permission. It also emphasizes that the Qur'an confirms the divine messages that came before it, such as the Torah and the Gospel, and serves as a guide and glad tidings for those who believe in its message. The verse implies that being an enemy to Gabriel is equivalent to being an enemy to Allah, as Gabriel is a faithful servant of Allah who carries out His commands. It also suggests that rejecting the Qur'an is tantamount to rejecting the previous scriptures, as the Qur'an confirms and safeguards their original teachings.
orig: قل من كان عدوا لجبريل فإنه نزله على قلبك بإذن الله مصدقا لما بين يديه وهدى وبشرى للمؤمنين

translation: Whoever is an enemy to Allah and His angels and His messengers and Gabriel and Michael - then indeed, Allah is an enemy to the disbelievers.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the severity of being an enemy to Allah, His angels, and His messengers, particularly singling out Gabriel and Michael. It serves as a strong warning to those who reject faith and oppose the divine message. The interpretation is that enmity towards Allah and those close to Him, such as the prominent angels Gabriel and Michael, will result in Allah's enmity towards the disbelievers. This highlights the grave spiritual consequences of rejecting faith and actively opposing the truth revealed by Allah through His messengers and angels.
orig: من كان عدوا لله وملائكته ورسله وجبريل وميكال فإن الله عدو للكافرين

translation: And We have certainly revealed to you verses [which are] clear proofs, and no one would deny them except the defiantly disobedient.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the Qur'an contains clear and unambiguous signs and proofs of its divine origin. These signs are so evident that only those who are obstinate and rebellious would reject them. The "defiantly disobedient" mentioned here refers to those who knowingly and willfully reject the truth, not out of ignorance but out of arrogance and a refusal to submit to God's guidance. The verse implies that the Qur'an's message is accessible and understandable to those who approach it with sincerity and an open heart, and that denying its truth is a sign of moral corruption rather than intellectual disagreement.
orig: ولقد أنزلنا إليك آيات بينات وما يكفر بها إلا الفاسقون

translation: Is it not [true] that every time they took a covenant a party of them threw it away? But, [in fact], most of them do not believe.
interpretation: This verse highlights the repeated betrayal and breaking of covenants by some groups, likely referring to certain Jewish tribes during the time of Prophet Muhammad. It suggests that this behavior was a recurring pattern, with a significant portion of these people consistently failing to uphold their agreements. The verse implies that this lack of commitment to their pledges stems from a fundamental absence of true faith and belief in God. It underscores the importance of honesty, trustworthiness, and adherence to one's promises as essential aspects of genuine faith and righteousness.
orig: أوكلما عاهدوا عهدا نبذه فريق منهم بل أكثرهم لا يؤمنون

translation: And when a messenger from Allah came to them confirming that which was with them, a party of those who had been given the Scripture threw the Scripture of Allah behind their backs as if they did not know.
interpretation: This verse is criticizing the behavior of some of the People of the Book (Jews and Christians) who rejected the message of Prophet Muhammad despite it confirming the teachings they already had in their scriptures. By ignoring or "throwing behind their backs" the book of Allah, i.e. the Qur'an, when it came to them, they are acting as if they have no knowledge of the truth it contains that is consistent with their own revelations. It suggests they are rejecting it out of ignorance or stubbornness rather than based on a sincere disagreement or lack of conviction in its divine origin.
orig: ولما جاءهم رسول من عند الله مصدق لما معهم نبذ فريق من الذين أوتوا الكتاب كتاب الله وراء ظهورهم كأنهم لا يعلمون

translation: And they followed [instead] what the devils had recited during the reign of Solomon. It was not Solomon who disbelieved, but the devils disbelieved, teaching people magic and that which was revealed to the two angels at Babylon, Harut and Marut. But the two angels do not teach anyone unless they say, "We are a trial, so do not disbelieve [by practicing magic]." And [yet] they learn from them that by which they cause separation between a man and his wife. But they do not harm anyone through it except by permission of Allah. And the people learn what harms them and does not benefit them. But the Children of Israel certainly knew that whoever purchased the magic would not have in the Hereafter any share. And wretched is that for which they sold themselves, if they only knew.
interpretation: This verse warns against the practice of magic and sorcery, which was taught by the devils during the time of Prophet Solomon. The devils deceived people into believing that Solomon himself practiced magic, but in reality, it was the devils who disbelieved and taught people magic. The verse also mentions two angels, Harut and Marut, who were sent down to test people by teaching them magic. However, they always warned people not to misuse this knowledge and fall into disbelief. The verse emphasizes that magic can cause harm and separation between spouses, and that it is only by Allah's permission that it can have any effect. It also states that those who engage in magic will have no share in the rewards of the Hereafter, and that they have sold their souls for a miserable price, if only they knew the consequences of their actions.
orig: واتبعوا ما تتلو الشياطين على ملك سليمان وما كفر سليمان ولكن الشياطين كفروا يعلمون الناس السحر وما أنزل على الملكين ببابل هاروت وماروت وما يعلمان من أحد حتى يقولا إنما نحن فتنة فلا تكفر فيتعلمون منهما ما يفرقون به بين المرء وزوجه وما هم بضارين به من أحد إلا بإذن الله ويتعلمون ما يضرهم ولا ينفعهم ولقد علموا لمن اشتراه ما له في الآخرة من خلاق ولبئس ما شروا به أنفسهم لو كانوا يعلمون

translation: And if they had believed and feared Allah, then the reward from Allah would have been better, if they only knew.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of having faith in Allah and being mindful of Him. It suggests that if people truly believed in Allah and lived their lives in accordance with His teachings, they would be rewarded with something far greater than any worldly gain or pleasure. The reward from Allah, whether in this life or in the hereafter, is always better than anything one could acquire through other means. However, the verse also implies that many people are unaware of this truth and fail to recognize the immense value of faith and righteousness. They prioritize worldly pursuits over their relationship with Allah, not realizing that ultimately, the path of faith and obedience leads to the greatest happiness and fulfillment.
orig: ولو أنهم آمنوا واتقوا لمثوبة من عند الله خير لو كانوا يعلمون

translation: O you who have believed, do not say [to Allah's Messenger], "Ra'ina" but say, "Unthurna" and listen. And for the disbelievers is a painful punishment.
interpretation: This verse is addressing the believers and instructing them on the proper etiquette when speaking to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him). The word "Ra'ina" was used by the Jews in a derogatory manner, twisting its meaning to insult the Prophet. Therefore, Allah commands the believers to use the word "Unthurna" instead, which means "look upon us," "pay attention to us," or "give us time." This change in wording serves to prevent any disrespect or mockery towards the Prophet. Additionally, the verse emphasizes the importance of listening attentively to the Prophet's teachings. It concludes with a warning to the disbelievers, stating that they will face a painful punishment for their disbelief and antagonistic behavior towards the Prophet and the believers.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا لا تقولوا راعنا وقولوا انظرنا واسمعوا وللكافرين عذاب أليم

translation: Those who disbelieve from the People of the Book and the polytheists do not like that any good should be sent down to you from your Lord. But Allah selects for His mercy whom He wills, and Allah is the possessor of great bounty.
interpretation: This verse highlights the animosity and jealousy that the disbelievers, both from the People of the Book (Jews and Christians) and the polytheists, harbor towards the believers. They do not wish for any good or blessings to be bestowed upon the believers from Allah. However, Allah reminds the believers that He chooses whom He wills for His mercy and blessings, regardless of the feelings and desires of the disbelievers. This emphasizes Allah's sovereignty and His exclusive right to grant His favor and grace to whomever He chooses. The verse concludes by affirming that Allah is the possessor of immense bounty, indicating His limitless generosity and the abundance of His blessings, which He grants to His faithful servants despite the envy and resentment of the disbelievers.
orig: ما يود الذين كفروا من أهل الكتاب ولا المشركين أن ينزل عليكم من خير من ربكم والله يختص برحمته من يشاء والله ذو الفضل العظيم

translation: We do not abrogate a verse or cause it to be forgotten except that We bring forth [one] better than it or similar to it. Do you not know that Allah is over all things competent?
interpretation: This verse affirms Allah's sovereignty and omnipotence in revealing His message. It asserts that if Allah chooses to abrogate or cause to be forgotten any verse of the Qur'an, He replaces it with something equal or better. This points to the divine wisdom behind the revelation of the Qur'an in stages, adapting the message to the needs and circumstances of the Muslim community over time. The verse emphasizes that Allah has the power and knowledge to guide His revelation in the most suitable way, and that believers should trust in His wisdom, as He is competent over all things. It is a reminder that the revelation of the Qur'an is a manifestation of Allah's will and power, not a product of human intervention or limitation.
orig: ما ننسخ من آية أو ننسها نأت بخير منها أو مثلها ألم تعلم أن الله على كل شيء قدير

translation: Do you not know that to Allah belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth and [that] you have not besides Allah any protector or any helper?
interpretation: This verse reminds us of Allah's ultimate power and authority over all of creation. It emphasizes that everything in the heavens and the earth belongs to Him alone, and that no one else can provide true protection or help. This should inspire humility and reliance on Allah, recognizing that He is the only source of strength and support in our lives. It also warns against placing our trust or seeking assistance from anyone or anything other than Allah, as they are ultimately powerless and unable to benefit us without His permission.
orig: ألم تعلم أن الله له ملك السماوات والأرض وما لكم من دون الله من ولي ولا نصير

translation: Or do you intend to ask your Messenger as Moses was asked before? And whoever exchanges faith for disbelief has certainly strayed from the soundness of the way.
interpretation: This verse warns the believers against demanding miracles or proofs from their Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) as the Children of Israel did with Moses. It emphasizes that faith should be based on the clear signs and guidance already provided by Allah, and that seeking to test or challenge the Prophet is a form of disbelief. Those who choose to reject faith in favor of disbelief, despite the clear proofs, have strayed from the straight path and are in manifest error. The verse reminds the believers to trust in Allah's wisdom and accept the guidance brought by His Messenger without demanding additional signs or miracles.
orig: أم تريدون أن تسألوا رسولكم كما سئل موسى من قبل ومن يتبدل الكفر بالإيمان فقد ضل سواء السبيل

translation: Many of the People of the Book wish they could turn you back to disbelief after you have believed, out of envy from themselves [even] after the truth has become clear to them. So pardon and overlook until Allah delivers His command. Indeed, Allah is over all things competent.
interpretation: This verse highlights the attitude of some of the People of the Book (Jews and Christians) towards the believers. Despite the truth of Islam being evident to them, they are driven by their envy and wish to see the believers revert to disbelief. However, Allah instructs the believers to respond with forgiveness and forbearance, and to await Allah's decree. It emphasizes that Allah is All-Powerful and His will shall ultimately prevail. The verse teaches Muslims to face hostility and ill-will from others with patience, mercy and trust in Allah's plan.
orig: ود كثير من أهل الكتاب لو يردونكم من بعد إيمانكم كفارا حسدا من عند أنفسهم من بعد ما تبين لهم الحق فاعفوا واصفحوا حتى يأتي الله بأمره إن الله على كل شيء قدير

translation: And establish prayer and give zakah, and whatever good you put forward for yourselves - you will find it with Allah. Indeed, Allah of what you do, is Seeing.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of establishing regular prayer and giving charity (zakah). It reminds believers that any good deeds they do in this world, even if seemingly small or unnoticed by others, are known to Allah and will be rewarded by Him in the Hereafter. The verse encourages Muslims to prioritize their spiritual obligations and to be sincere in their worship and good deeds, knowing that Allah is always aware of their actions and intentions. It highlights the concept of divine accountability and the belief that one's ultimate reward lies with Allah in the afterlife.
orig: وأقيموا الصلاة وآتوا الزكاة وما تقدموا لأنفسكم من خير تجدوه عند الله إن الله بما تعملون بصير

translation: And they say, "None will enter Paradise except one who is a Jew or a Christian." That is [merely] their wishful thinking. Say, "Produce your proof, if you should be truthful."
interpretation: This verse is addressing the false belief held by some Jews and Christians that only they will enter Paradise, to the exclusion of all others. Allah refutes this notion as baseless and challenges them to bring forth evidence to support their claim if they are indeed truthful. The Qur'an emphasizes that salvation is not determined by mere affiliation with a particular religious group but rather by one's faith, righteousness, and submission to the will of Allah. This verse serves as a reminder that entry into Paradise is not the exclusive right of any one community; it is open to all who sincerely believe in Allah and follow His guidance.
orig: وقالوا لن يدخل الجنة إلا من كان هودا أو نصارى تلك أمانيهم قل هاتوا برهانكم إن كنتم صادقين

translation: Yes, whoever submits his face to Allah while being a doer of good will have his reward with his Lord. And no fear will there be concerning them, nor will they grieve.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that those who sincerely submit to Allah and do good deeds will be rewarded by Him. They will have nothing to fear in the Hereafter and will not grieve over what they may have lost in this worldly life. It highlights the importance of complete submission to Allah, coupled with righteous actions, as the path to attaining peace and contentment in both this life and the next. The verse serves as a reassurance to the believers that their efforts will not go unnoticed or unrewarded by their Lord.
orig: بلى من أسلم وجهه لله وهو محسن فله أجره عند ربه ولا خوف عليهم ولا هم يحزنون

translation: The Jews say, "The Christians have nothing [true] to stand on," and the Christians say, "The Jews have nothing to stand on," although they [both] recite the Scripture. Thus the polytheists speak the same as their words. But Allah will judge between them on the Day of Resurrection concerning that over which they used to differ.
interpretation: This verse highlights the religious disputes and mutual rejection between Jews and Christians, despite both groups claiming to follow divine scriptures. It suggests that their disagreements stem from ignorance and resemble the baseless arguments of polytheists. The verse emphasizes that ultimately, Allah will judge between them on the Day of Judgment regarding their differences, implying the importance of seeking truth and unity based on genuine understanding of scriptures rather than sectarian biases.
orig: وقالت اليهود ليست النصارى على شيء وقالت النصارى ليست اليهود على شيء وهم يتلون الكتاب كذلك قال الذين لا يعلمون مثل قولهم فالله يحكم بينهم يوم القيامة فيما كانوا فيه يختلفون

translation: And who are more unjust than those who prevent the name of Allah from being mentioned in His mosques and strive toward their destruction. It is not for them to enter them except in fear. For them in this world is disgrace, and they will have in the Hereafter a great punishment.
interpretation: This verse strongly condemns those who prevent people from worshipping Allah in mosques and try to destroy these sacred places. Such individuals are considered among the most unjust and oppressive. Due to their evil actions, they will live in a state of fear and disgrace in this world. Moreover, in the afterlife, they will face a severe punishment from Allah for their attempts to hinder His worship and damage His houses of prayer. This highlights the gravity of their sins and the consequences they will face for their sacrilegious behavior.
orig: ومن أظلم ممن منع مساجد الله أن يذكر فيها اسمه وسعى في خرابها أولئك ما كان لهم أن يدخلوها إلا خائفين لهم في الدنيا خزي ولهم في الآخرة عذاب عظيم

translation: And to Allah belongs the east and the west. So wherever you [might] turn, there is the Face of Allah. Indeed, Allah is all-Encompassing and Knowing.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the omnipresence and omniscience of Allah. It suggests that Allah's presence is not confined to any particular direction or place. Wherever one turns, they will find Allah's presence and guidance. The verse also highlights the vastness of Allah's knowledge and the fact that He is aware of all things. It serves as a reminder to the believers that they should always be mindful of Allah and seek His guidance in all aspects of their lives, knowing that He is always with them and aware of their actions and intentions.
orig: ولله المشرق والمغرب فأينما تولوا فثم وجه الله إن الله واسع عليم

translation: And they say, "Allah has taken a son." Exalted is He! Rather, to Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and the earth. All are devoutly obedient to Him.
interpretation: This verse refutes the false claim made by some people that Allah has taken a son. It emphasizes the absolute transcendence and oneness of Allah, stating that He is far above such assertions. Instead, everything in the heavens and the earth belongs to Him alone, and all of creation is subservient and obedient to His will. The verse affirms that Allah is self-sufficient and does not need any offspring or partners, as He is the sole creator, sustainer, and owner of the universe. It also highlights the importance of maintaining a pure monotheistic belief in Allah, free from any form of association or attribution of divine qualities to anyone or anything else.
orig: وقالوا اتخذ الله ولدا سبحانه بل له ما في السماوات والأرض كل له قانتون

translation: The Originator of the heavens and the earth. When He decrees a matter, He only says to it, "Be," and it is.
interpretation: This verse highlights Allah's attribute as the Creator and Originator of the entire universe. It emphasizes His omnipotence and supreme authority over all creation. When Allah wills something to happen, He merely commands it to "Be," and it comes into existence. This demonstrates the ease with which Allah creates and the immediacy of His command. It also serves as a reminder for humans to submit to Allah's will and recognize His power and control over all aspects of life.
orig: بديع السماوات والأرض وإذا قضى أمرا فإنما يقول له كن فيكون

translation: The ignorant people say, "Why does Allah not speak to us or send us a sign?" The same was said by those who came before them. Their hearts are all alike. Indeed, We have made the signs clear for people of sure faith.
interpretation: This verse highlights the skepticism and disbelief of those who lack knowledge and understanding of Allah's wisdom. They demand direct communication from Allah or tangible signs to prove His existence, similar to the doubts expressed by previous generations. However, their hearts are all alike in their inability to comprehend the truth. Allah emphasizes that He has already provided ample signs and evidence for those who possess certainty and faith, making it clear that the problem lies within the doubters' own hearts and minds, not in the absence of proof from Allah.
orig: وقال الذين لا يعلمون لولا يكلمنا الله أو تأتينا آية كذلك قال الذين من قبلهم مثل قولهم تشابهت قلوبهم قد بينا الآيات لقوم يوقنون

translation: Indeed, We have sent you with the truth as a bringer of good tidings and a warner. And you will not be asked about the companions of Hellfire.
interpretation: This verse affirms that Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) was sent by Allah with the true message of Islam, to give glad tidings of Paradise to those who believe and do righteous deeds, and to warn those who disbelieve and sin of the punishment of Hellfire. The Prophet's duty is only to convey the message, and he is not responsible for the fate of those who choose to reject it and become the dwellers of Hell. It is a reminder that guidance is ultimately in Allah's hands, and the Prophet's role is to deliver the message faithfully without being accountable for people's individual choices and destinations in the Hereafter.
orig: إنا أرسلناك بالحق بشيرا ونذيرا ولا تسأل عن أصحاب الجحيم

translation: And never will the Jews or the Christians approve of you until you follow their religion. Say, "Indeed, the guidance of Allah is the [only] guidance." If you were to follow their desires after what has come to you of knowledge, you would have against Allah no protector or helper.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the fundamental differences between Islam and the beliefs of Jews and Christians. It suggests that seeking the approval or validation of these groups is futile unless one abandons Islamic principles and adopts their religious practices. The verse asserts that the only true guidance comes from Allah and that following the desires or beliefs of others, after having received divine knowledge, would leave one without Allah's protection and support. It highlights the importance of remaining steadfast in one's faith and not compromising religious principles for the sake of pleasing others or gaining their acceptance.
orig: ولن ترضى عنك اليهود ولا النصارى حتى تتبع ملتهم قل إن هدى الله هو الهدى ولئن اتبعت أهواءهم بعد الذي جاءك من العلم ما لك من الله من ولي ولا نصير

translation: Those to whom We have given the Book recite it with its true recital. They [are the ones who] believe in it. And whoever disbelieves in it - it is they who are the losers.
interpretation: This verse is referring to the true believers who have been given the divine scripture, such as the Qur'an. They recite it as it should be recited, with sincerity, understanding, and reflection. They have complete faith in its message and teachings. In contrast, those who reject the divine book and its guidance are the ultimate losers, as they have failed to recognize and accept the truth from their Lord. They will face the consequences of their disbelief and will be deprived of Allah's mercy and blessings in this world and the Hereafter.
orig: الذين آتيناهم الكتاب يتلونه حق تلاوته أولئك يؤمنون به ومن يكفر به فأولئك هم الخاسرون

translation: O Children of Israel, remember My favor which I have bestowed upon you and that I preferred you over the worlds.
interpretation: This verse is a reminder to the Children of Israel of the special favors and blessings that Allah had bestowed upon them, such as the revelation of the Torah, the sending of many prophets among them, and granting them superiority over other nations of their time. It emphasizes the importance of gratitude and the need to fulfill their covenant with Allah by following His guidance and commandments. The verse also implies that the Children of Israel's privileged status is not unconditional and that they must uphold their end of the covenant to maintain Allah's favor and avoid His displeasure.
orig: يا بني إسرائيل اذكروا نعمتي التي أنعمت عليكم وأني فضلتكم على العالمين

translation: And fear a Day when no soul will suffice for another soul at all, nor will intercession be accepted from it, nor will compensation be taken from it, nor will they be aided.
interpretation: This verse is a stark reminder of the Day of Judgment, when each individual will be held accountable for their own deeds. On that day, no one will be able to help another, regardless of how close they were in this worldly life. Neither intercession on behalf of others nor any form of compensation will be accepted. The verse emphasizes the ultimate justice of Allah, where each soul will be judged solely on its own merits and actions. It serves as a powerful warning for mankind to be mindful of their deeds and to live righteously, as on the Day of Judgment, they will have no one to turn to for help except Allah's mercy.
orig: واتقوا يوما لا تجزي نفس عن نفس شيئا ولا يقبل منها عدل ولا تنفعها شفاعة ولا هم ينصرون

translation: And [mention, O Muhammad], when Abraham was tried by his Lord with commands and he fulfilled them. [Allah] said, "Indeed, I will make you a leader for the people." [Abraham] said, "And of my descendants?" [Allah] said, "My covenant does not include the wrongdoers."
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of obedience to Allah and the consequences of righteousness. Abraham's unwavering faith and fulfillment of Allah's commands elevated his status, making him a leader for mankind. However, Allah clarifies that this honored position is not automatically inherited by Abraham's descendants; rather, it is contingent upon their own righteousness. The covenant of leadership and guidance is not attainable by those who engage in wrongdoing and deviate from the path of Allah. This emphasizes the individual responsibility of each person to uphold justice and righteousness to be worthy of Allah's favor and leadership roles in society.
orig: وإذ ابتلى إبراهيم ربه بكلمات فأتمهن قال إني جاعلك للناس إماما قال ومن ذريتي قال لا ينال عهدي الظالمين

translation: And [mention] when We made the House a place of return for the people and [a place of] security. And take, [O believers], from the standing place of Abraham a place of prayer. And We charged Abraham and Ishmael, [saying], "Purify My House for those who perform Tawaf and those who are staying [there] for worship and those who bow and prostrate [in prayer]."
interpretation: This verse highlights the sanctity and importance of the Ka'bah, the sacred House of Allah in Makkah. It was established as a place of spiritual retreat, security, and worship for all people. The standing place of Abraham, where he stood while building the Ka'bah, is singled out as a spot for prayer, emphasizing the connection between the worship practices of Abraham and the rituals performed by Muslims. The verse also underscores the duty entrusted to Abraham and his son Ishmael to keep the Ka'bah pure and dedicated to the worship of Allah alone, catering to the needs of those who engage in the rituals of Tawaf (circumambulation around the Ka'bah), I'tikaf (staying in the mosque for worship), and prayer in the form of bowing and prostration. This signifies the continuity of the monotheistic message and the centrality of the Ka'bah in the lives of the believers.
orig: وإذ جعلنا البيت مثابة للناس وأمنا واتخذوا من مقام إبراهيم مصلى وعهدنا إلى إبراهيم وإسماعيل أن طهرا بيتي للطائفين والعاكفين والركع السجود

translation: And [mention] when Abraham said, "My Lord, make this a secure city and provide its people with fruits - whoever of them believes in Allah and the Last Day." [Allah] said. "And whoever disbelieves - I will grant him enjoyment for a little; then I will force him to the punishment of the Fire, and wretched is the destination."
interpretation: This verse highlights Abraham's prayer for Makkah to be a city of security and prosperity for the believers. It also emphasizes that while the disbelievers may enjoy the temporary pleasures of this world, their ultimate fate will be the painful punishment of Hell. The verse serves as a reminder for the believers to stay steadfast in their faith and for the disbelievers to heed the warning and embrace the path of righteousness before it is too late.
orig: وإذ قال إبراهيم رب اجعل هذا بلدا آمنا وارزق أهله من الثمرات من آمن منهم بالله واليوم الآخر قال ومن كفر فأمتعه قليلا ثم أضطره إلى عذاب النار وبئس المصير

translation: And [mention] when Abraham was raising the foundations of the House and [with him] Ishmael, [saying], "Our Lord, accept [this] from us. Indeed, You are the Hearing, the Knowing."
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of sincerity and devotion in one's actions, especially when it comes to acts of worship. Abraham and Ishmael's supplication to Allah while building the Ka'bah demonstrates their humility and recognition of Allah's omnipotence. It serves as a reminder for believers to always seek Allah's acceptance and guidance in their endeavors, acknowledging that He is the All-Hearing and All-Knowing. The verse also emphasizes the significance of the Ka'bah as a sacred house of worship, which was built by two of the most prominent prophets in Islamic history.
orig: وإذ يرفع إبراهيم القواعد من البيت وإسماعيل ربنا تقبل منا إنك أنت السميع العليم

translation: Our Lord, and make us Muslims [in submission] to You and from our descendants a Muslim nation [in submission] to You. And show us our rites and accept our repentance. Indeed, You are the Accepting of repentance, the Merciful.
interpretation: This verse is a prayer and supplication to Allah, asking Him to make the supplicants and their descendants submissive and obedient to Him, following the teachings of Islam. It is a plea for guidance in performing the religious rites and a request for Allah's forgiveness and mercy. This highlights the importance of seeking Allah's help in remaining steadfast in faith and passing on the Islamic teachings and way of life to future generations. The verse emphasizes the significance of repentance and the assurance that Allah is the One who accepts repentance and grants mercy to those who sincerely turn to Him.
orig: ربنا واجعلنا مسلمين لك ومن ذريتنا أمة مسلمة لك وأرنا مناسكنا وتب علينا إنك أنت التواب الرحيم

translation: Our Lord! Send amongst them a Messenger of their own, who shall recite unto them Your Verses and instruct them in the Book and Wisdom, and sanctify them. Verily, You are the All-Mighty, the All-Wise.
interpretation: This verse is a prayer asking Allah to send a messenger from among the people, who would recite Allah's verses to them, teach them the Qur'an and wisdom, and purify their souls. The interpretation is that the coming of a messenger from among themselves would make it easier for the people to understand and follow the message, as he would be familiar with their language, customs and way of thinking. The messenger's role would be to convey Allah's message, educate people about Islam, and guide them to righteousness, helping to purify their hearts and souls. The verse ends by affirming that Allah is All-Mighty and All-Wise, implying that sending a messenger is a manifestation of His power and wisdom in guiding humanity to the right path.
orig: ربنا وابعث فيهم رسولا منهم يتلو عليهم آياتك ويعلمهم الكتاب والحكمة ويزكيهم إنك أنت العزيز الحكيم

translation: And who turns away from the religion of Abraham except he who makes a fool of himself. And We had chosen him in this world, and indeed he, in the Hereafter, will be among the righteous.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance and superiority of the monotheistic faith of Prophet Abraham. It implies that only those who are foolish and unwise would reject the pure monotheism that Abraham preached and practiced. The verse also affirms that Allah had chosen Abraham in this worldly life due to his righteousness and devotion, and that he will be among the righteous in the Hereafter as well. This interpretation highlights the significance of following the path of Abraham, which is the path of pure monotheism and submission to the One True God.
orig: ومن يرغب عن ملة إبراهيم إلا من سفه نفسه ولقد اصطفيناه في الدنيا وإنه في الآخرة لمن الصالحين

translation: When his Lord said to him, "Submit", he said "I have submitted [in Islam] to the Lord of the worlds."
interpretation: This verse highlights the complete submission and obedience of Prophet Ibrahim (Abraham) to Allah. When Allah commanded him to submit, he immediately responded by declaring his total surrender to the will of the Lord of all the worlds. This demonstrates Ibrahim's unwavering faith, sincerity, and readiness to obey Allah's commands without any hesitation or reservation. It sets an example for all believers to strive for such a level of devotion and submission to the One True God.
orig: إذ قال له ربه أسلم قال أسلمت لرب العالمين

translation: And Abraham instructed his sons [to do the same] and [so did] Jacob, [saying], "O my sons, indeed Allah has chosen for you this religion, so do not die except while you are Muslims."
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of remaining steadfast in faith until death. Abraham and Jacob, both revered prophets, emphasized to their children the significance of adhering to the religion chosen by Allah. They urged their descendants to live and die as Muslims, submitting themselves wholly to the will of Allah. This instruction underscores the paramount importance of faith and the necessity of passing on this message from generation to generation. It serves as a reminder for believers to hold fast to their religion, remaining committed to Islam throughout their lives, until their final breath.
orig: ووصى بها إبراهيم بنيه ويعقوب يا بني إن الله اصطفى لكم الدين فلا تموتن إلا وأنتم مسلمون

translation: Or were you witnesses when death approached Jacob, when he said to his sons, "What will you worship after me?" They said, "We will worship your God and the God of your fathers, Abraham and Ishmael and Isaac - one God. And we are Muslims [in submission] to Him."
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of monotheism and the continuity of the message of worshipping the One True God across generations. Jacob, on his deathbed, seeks assurance from his sons that they will remain steadfast in their worship of Allah alone, following the religion of their forefathers Abraham, Ishmael, and Isaac. The sons' response affirms their commitment to Islam, emphasizing the oneness of God and their submission to Him. This passage demonstrates the significance of passing down the true faith to one's children and the value of remaining devoted to the worship of the One God throughout one's life.
orig: أم كنتم شهداء إذ حضر يعقوب الموت إذ قال لبنيه ما تعبدون من بعدي قالوا نعبد إلهك وإله آبائك إبراهيم وإسماعيل وإسحاق إلها واحدا ونحن له مسلمون

translation: That is a nation which has passed on. It will have [the consequence of] what it earned, and you will have what you have earned. And you will not be asked about what they used to do.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the individual responsibility of each person and each generation. The deeds of the past generations will not affect the recompense of the present generation, and vice versa. Each individual is accountable for their own actions and will be judged accordingly by Allah. One cannot rely on the good deeds of their ancestors nor be punished for their misdeeds. This encourages each person to focus on rectifying their own conduct and strive in good works, rather than feeling a false sense of security or despair due to the actions of those who came before them.
orig: تلك أمة قد خلت لها ما كسبت ولكم ما كسبتم ولا تسألون عما كانوا يعملون

translation: And they say, "Be Jews or Christians [so] you will be guided." Say, "Rather, [we follow] the religion of Abraham, inclining toward truth, and he was not of the polytheists."
interpretation: This verse is addressing the claim made by some Jews and Christians that the only way to attain guidance is to follow their respective religions. In response, Allah instructs Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) to declare that the true path to guidance is through following the pure monotheistic faith of Prophet Abraham, who was neither a Jew nor a Christian, but a devout believer in the oneness of Allah. The verse emphasizes that Abraham was not among those who associated partners with Allah (polytheists), and thus, the path of true guidance lies in following his example of sincere devotion to the one true God, rather than adhering to the specific religious traditions that emerged later in history.
orig: وقالوا كونوا هودا أو نصارى تهتدوا قل بل ملة إبراهيم حنيفا وما كان من المشركين

translation: Say, "We have believed in Allah and what has been revealed to us and what has been revealed to Abraham and Ishmael and Isaac and Jacob and the Descendants and what was given to Moses and Jesus and what was given to the prophets from their Lord. We make no distinction between any of them, and we are Muslims [in submission] to Him."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the unity of the divine message across different prophets and generations. It calls upon the believers to affirm their faith in Allah and all His revelations, without making any distinction between the prophets. This highlights the continuity and universality of the core message of submission to the One God. The verse also underscores the importance of embracing Islam as a complete way of life, in total submission to Allah's will, as exemplified by the prophets mentioned. It promotes religious tolerance, recognizing the common thread of monotheism that binds all the prophets and their followers.
orig: قولوا آمنا بالله وما أنزل إلينا وما أنزل إلى إبراهيم وإسماعيل وإسحاق ويعقوب والأسباط وما أوتي موسى وعيسى وما أوتي النبيون من ربهم لا نفرق بين أحد منهم ونحن له مسلمون

translation: And if they believe in the same as you believe in, then they have been [rightly] guided; but if they turn away, they are only in dissension, and Allah will be sufficient for you against them. And He is the Hearing, the Knowing.
interpretation: This verse conveys the message that if people come to believe in the same truth that the believers follow, then they are rightly guided. However, if they turn away from this truth, then they are only creating discord and division. In such a case, Allah assures the believers that He will suffice them against those who oppose the truth, as He is All-Hearing and All-Knowing. This interpretation highlights the importance of unity in faith and the consequences of turning away from the right path. It also emphasizes the believer's trust in Allah's support and protection in the face of adversity.
orig: فإن آمنوا بمثل ما آمنتم به فقد اهتدوا وإن تولوا فإنما هم في شقاق فسيكفيكهم الله وهو السميع العليم

translation: The color of Allah. And who can be better than Allah in coloring? And we are His worshippers.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the way of life prescribed by Allah is the best way, just as the color Allah gives is the best color. It affirms complete devotion and submission to Allah alone. The "color" here metaphorically refers to the religion, nature and characteristics that Allah has chosen for His true servants and worshippers. Nothing can be better than what Allah ordains and prescribes. As His devoted servants, the believers wholeheartedly embrace the path Allah has decreed for them.
orig: صبغة الله ومن أحسن من الله صبغة ونحن له عابدون

translation: Say, "Do you argue with us about Allah while He is our Lord and your Lord? For us are our deeds, and for you are your deeds. And we are sincere [in deed and intention] to Him."
interpretation: This verse is a response to those who argue with the believers about Allah. It emphasizes that Allah is the Lord of all, both the believers and the disbelievers, and that each group is responsible for their own deeds. The believers declare their sincerity and devotion to Allah alone, making it clear that they do not associate partners with Him or seek the approval of others. This verse highlights the importance of focusing on one's own relationship with Allah and being sincere in worship and obedience to Him, rather than engaging in fruitless arguments or seeking to please others.
orig: قل أتحاجوننا في الله وهو ربنا وربكم ولنا أعمالنا ولكم أعمالكم ونحن له مخلصون

translation: Or do you say that Abraham, Ishmael, Isaac, Jacob, and the Descendants were Jews or Christians? Say, "Are you more knowing or is Allah?" And who is more unjust than one who conceals a testimony he has from Allah? And Allah is not unaware of what you do.
interpretation: This verse challenges the claim that the early Prophets followed Judaism or Christianity, which did not exist during their time. It emphasizes that Allah knows best about their true religion, which was submission to Him alone (Islam). It condemns those who hide the truth revealed to them by Allah, as it is a great injustice. The verse also serves as a warning that Allah is fully aware of all our actions and intentions, and we will be held accountable for them.
orig: أم تقولون إن إبراهيم وإسماعيل وإسحاق ويعقوب والأسباط كانوا هودا أو نصارى قل أأنتم أعلم أم الله ومن أظلم ممن كتم شهادة عنده من الله وما الله بغافل عما تعملون

translation: That was a nation which has passed on. It will have [the consequence of] what it earned, and you will have what you have earned. And you will not be asked about what they used to do.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the individual responsibility of each person and nation. The deeds and actions of previous nations will not affect the ultimate judgment of the present one. Each nation will be held accountable for their own actions and choices, and will face the consequences accordingly in the Hereafter. Muslims should focus on their own moral conduct and righteousness, striving to earn good deeds, rather than concerning themselves with or feeling accountable for the actions of those who came before them. Ultimately, each soul bears the burden of its own spiritual destiny.
orig: تلك أمة قد خلت لها ما كسبت ولكم ما كسبتم ولا تسألون عما كانوا يعملون

translation: The foolish among the people will say, "What has turned them away from their qiblah, which they used to face?" Say, "To Allah belongs the east and the west. He guides whom He wills to a straight path."
interpretation: This verse addresses the change of the qiblah, or direction of prayer, from Jerusalem to the Ka'bah in Mecca. It anticipates the reaction of the foolish and ignorant people who would question this change. The response is that the direction of prayer is not as important as the fact that all directions belong to Allah, and He guides whom He wills to the straight path. This emphasizes the sovereignty of Allah and His authority to guide people according to His wisdom, regardless of their expectations or preferences. It also implies that the change of qiblah is a test of faith and obedience for the believers, to distinguish those who follow the Prophet's guidance from those who oppose it.
orig: سيقول السفهاء من الناس ما ولاهم عن قبلتهم التي كانوا عليها قل لله المشرق والمغرب يهدي من يشاء إلى صراط مستقيم

translation: And thus we have made you a just community that you will be witnesses over the people and the Messenger will be a witness over you. And We did not make the qiblah which you used to face except that We might make evident who would follow the Messenger from who would turn back on his heels. And indeed, it is difficult except for those whom Allah has guided. And never would Allah have caused you to lose your faith. Indeed Allah is, to the people, Kind and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah has chosen the Muslim community to be a moderate and just nation, serving as an example and witness to the rest of humanity. The change in the direction of prayer (qiblah) from Jerusalem to Mecca was a test of faith, distinguishing the true believers who followed the Prophet Muhammad from those who turned away. Although this change was challenging, Allah assures the believers that their past prayers towards Jerusalem were not in vain and that He would not let their faith go to waste. The verse concludes by emphasizing Allah's kindness and mercy towards all people, even as He tests their faith and commitment to His path.
orig: وكذلك جعلناكم أمة وسطا لتكونوا شهداء على الناس ويكون الرسول عليكم شهيدا وما جعلنا القبلة التي كنت عليها إلا لنعلم من يتبع الرسول ممن ينقلب على عقبيه وإن كانت لكبيرة إلا على الذين هدى الله وما كان الله ليضيع إيمانكم إن الله بالناس لرءوف رحيم

translation: We have certainly seen the turning of your face, [O Muhammad], toward the heaven, and We will surely turn you to a qiblah with which you will be pleased. So turn your face toward al-Masjid al-Haram. And wherever you [believers] are, turn your faces toward it [in prayer]. Indeed, those who have been given the Scripture well know that it is the truth from their Lord. And Allah is not unaware of what they do.
interpretation: This verse signifies a major event in the history of Islam - the change of the qiblah (direction of prayer) from Jerusalem to the Ka'bah in Mecca. It underscores God's omniscience, as He was aware of the Prophet's desire for this change. The command to face the Sacred Mosque (al-Masjid al-Haram) applies universally to all Muslims, emphasizing unity in worship. The verse also affirms that the People of the Book (Jews and Christians) recognize the truth of this revelation, highlighting the continuity in the Abrahamic faiths. Ultimately, it reminds us that God is fully aware of all actions and intentions, encouraging sincerity and mindfulness in worship.
orig: قد نرى تقلب وجهك في السماء فلنولينك قبلة ترضاها فول وجهك شطر المسجد الحرام وحيث ما كنتم فولوا وجوهكم شطره وإن الذين أوتوا الكتاب ليعلمون أنه الحق من ربهم وما الله بغافل عما يعملون

translation: And even if you brought to those who were given the Scripture every sign, they would not follow your qiblah. Nor will you be a follower of their qiblah. Nor would they be followers of one another's qiblah. So if you were to follow their desires after what has come to you of knowledge, indeed, you would then be among the wrongdoers.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the stubborn resistance of the People of the Book (Jews and Christians) to the message of Islam, even if presented with clear proofs. It also warns Muslims not to compromise their faith by following the whims and desires of others, as this would lead them astray from the path of righteousness. The verse underscores the importance of adhering firmly to the truth that has been revealed by God, regardless of the opposition or pressure one may face from those who reject it. Ultimately, the Qiblah represents a symbol of unity and submission to the will of Allah, and Muslims must remain steadfast in their commitment to it.
orig: ولئن أتيت الذين أوتوا الكتاب بكل آية ما تبعوا قبلتك وما أنت بتابع قبلتهم وما بعضهم بتابع قبلة بعض ولئن اتبعت أهواءهم من بعد ما جاءك من العلم إنك إذا لمن الظالمين

translation: Those to whom We have given the Book recognize it as they recognize their [own] sons. But indeed, a party of them conceal the truth while they know [it].
interpretation: This verse is referring to the People of the Book, namely the Jews and Christians, who were given divine scriptures before the revelation of the Qur'an. The verse states that they recognize the truth of the Qur'an and the prophethood of Muhammad (peace be upon him) just as clearly as they recognize their own children. However, some of them deliberately hide this truth, despite knowing it in their hearts, out of envy, pride, or fear of losing their authority. They reject the message of Islam, even though deep down they know it to be true. This highlights the importance of sincerity and honesty in faith, and the consequences of allowing worldly desires to overpower one's recognition of the truth.
orig: الذين آتيناهم الكتاب يعرفونه كما يعرفون أبناءهم وإن فريقا منهم ليكتمون الحق وهم يعلمون

translation: The truth is from your Lord, so do not be among the doubters.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute truth and certainty of the message that comes from Allah. It serves as a reminder to the believers to have unwavering faith in the divine revelation and not to be swayed by doubts or skepticism. The Qur'an is the ultimate truth, and it is the duty of every Muslim to accept it wholeheartedly without any reservations. This verse encourages the believers to strengthen their faith, trust in Allah's guidance, and remain steadfast on the path of Islam, even in the face of challenges or doubts that may arise from within or from external sources.
orig: الحق من ربك فلا تكونن من الممترين

translation: For each [religious following] is a direction toward which it faces. So race to [all that is] good. Wherever you may be, Allah will bring you forth [for judgement] all together. Indeed, Allah is over all things competent.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that while different religious communities may have different practices or orientations, what ultimately matters is that they strive to do good deeds. It encourages people to focus on righteousness rather than differences. The verse also affirms Allah's power to gather all people together for judgment regardless of where they may be, highlighting His omnipotence and the inevitability of being held accountable for one's actions in the Hereafter. It serves as a reminder to Muslims to concentrate on leading an ethical life.
orig: ولكل وجهة هو موليها فاستبقوا الخيرات أين ما تكونوا يأت بكم الله جميعا إن الله على كل شيء قدير

translation: And from wherever you go out [for prayer], turn your face toward the Sacred Mosque. Indeed, it is the truth from your Lord. And Allah is not unaware of what you do.
interpretation: This verse instructs the believers to face the direction of the Sacred Mosque (the Ka'bah in Mecca) when performing their prayers, no matter where they are. It emphasizes that this command is the truth from Allah and that He is fully aware of all actions and intentions of His servants. This verse establishes the importance of unity and consistency in the direction of prayer for Muslims worldwide, symbolizing their unified devotion to the One true God. It also serves as a reminder that Allah is always watching and knows the deeds and intentions of every individual, encouraging sincerity and mindfulness in worship.
orig: ومن حيث خرجت فول وجهك شطر المسجد الحرام وإنه للحق من ربك وما الله بغافل عما تعملون

translation: So from wherever you go out [for prayer, O Muhammad], turn your face toward al-Masjid al-Haram, and wherever you [believers] may be, turn your faces toward it in order that the people will not have any argument against you, except for those of them who commit wrong; so do not fear them but fear Me. And [it is] so I may complete My favor upon you and that you may be guided.
interpretation: This verse instructs the Prophet Muhammad and the believers to face the direction of the Sacred Mosque in Mecca (al-Masjid al-Haram) during their prayers, no matter where they are. This commandment serves to unify the Muslim community and prevent others from criticizing or arguing against their religious practices. The verse emphasizes that the believers should not fear those who oppose or wrong them, but rather fear Allah alone. By following this command, Muslims will receive Allah's favor and guidance, allowing them to stay on the right path.
orig: ومن حيث خرجت فول وجهك شطر المسجد الحرام وحيث ما كنتم فولوا وجوهكم شطره لئلا يكون للناس عليكم حجة إلا الذين ظلموا منهم فلا تخشوهم واخشوني ولأتم نعمتي عليكم ولعلكم تهتدون

translation: Just as We have sent among you a messenger from yourselves reciting to you Our verses and purifying you and teaching you the Book and wisdom and teaching you that which you did not know.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance and role of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) as a messenger sent by Allah to guide and teach the people. The interpretation is that Allah has blessed the believers by sending them a prophet from among themselves who recites Allah's revelations, purifies their souls, and imparts knowledge and wisdom that they did not possess before. This highlights the significance of prophetic teachings in the spiritual and intellectual growth of individuals and society. The verse also implies that the Prophet's mission is not merely to convey the message but also to purify and educate, indicating the transformative nature of his teachings.
orig: كما أرسلنا فيكم رسولا منكم يتلو عليكم آياتنا ويزكيكم ويعلمكم الكتاب والحكمة ويعلمكم ما لم تكونوا تعلمون

translation: So remember Me; I will remember you. And be grateful to Me and do not deny Me.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of remembering Allah and being grateful to Him. It reminds us that if we remember Allah and are thankful for His blessings, He will remember us and bestow His mercy and grace upon us. On the other hand, if we forget Allah and are ungrateful, we will be denying His favors and inviting His displeasure. The verse encourages us to maintain a strong connection with Allah through constant remembrance (dhikr) and gratitude, which will lead to a deeper spiritual relationship with Him and protect us from falling into disbelief or ingratitude.
orig: فاذكروني أذكركم واشكروا لي ولا تكفرون

translation: O you who have believed, seek help through patience and prayer. Indeed, Allah is with the patient.
interpretation: This verse encourages believers to turn to patience and prayer during times of hardship or difficulty. It reminds us that by remaining steadfast and turning to Allah in sincere supplication, we can find the strength and guidance needed to overcome life's challenges. The verse also emphasizes that Allah is with those who are patient, offering His support, comfort, and aid to those who persevere in faith. This highlights the importance of maintaining a strong spiritual connection with Allah and trusting in His plan, even during trying times.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا استعينوا بالصبر والصلاة إن الله مع الصابرين

translation: And do not say about those who are killed in the way of Allah, "They are dead." Rather, they are alive, but you perceive [it] not.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the concept of martyrdom in Islam. Those who are killed while fighting for the cause of Allah are not considered dead in the conventional sense. Instead, they are believed to be alive in the spiritual realm, enjoying the blessings and rewards of Allah. However, this spiritual life is beyond the perception of ordinary human beings. The verse encourages Muslims to view martyrdom not as a loss of life, but as a transition to a higher state of existence in the presence of Allah. It also serves as a consolation to the families and friends of martyrs, reminding them that their loved ones are not gone forever but are alive and well in the eyes of Allah.
orig: ولا تقولوا لمن يقتل في سبيل الله أموات بل أحياء ولكن لا تشعرون

translation: And We will surely test you with something of fear and hunger and a loss of wealth and lives and fruits, but give good tidings to the patient.
interpretation: This verse is a reminder that God tests human beings with various trials and tribulations, such as fear, hunger, loss of wealth, lives, and crops. These tests are a means of purifying and strengthening the believers, as they require patience, perseverance, and unwavering faith in God's plan. The verse also emphasizes the importance of remaining steadfast and patient during times of hardship, as those who endure these trials with grace and trust in God will be rewarded with good tidings and ultimately, God's pleasure and paradise in the afterlife. It encourages believers to view challenges as opportunities for spiritual growth and to maintain a positive outlook, knowing that God is with them every step of the way.
orig: ولنبلونكم بشيء من الخوف والجوع ونقص من الأموال والأنفس والثمرات وبشر الصابرين

translation: Who, when disaster strikes them, say, "Indeed we belong to Allah, and indeed to Him we will return."
interpretation: This verse highlights the patience and steadfastness of the believers in the face of adversity. When faced with trials and tribulations, they acknowledge that everything belongs to Allah and that they will ultimately return to Him. This attitude reflects their deep faith and trust in Allah's wisdom and plan. It also shows their acceptance of divine decree and their willingness to submit to Allah's will, even during difficult times. By adopting this mindset, the believers find solace and strength, knowing that their hardships are temporary and that their ultimate destination is with Allah in the Hereafter.
orig: الذين إذا أصابتهم مصيبة قالوا إنا لله وإنا إليه راجعون

translation: Those are the ones upon whom are blessings from their Lord and mercy. And it is those who are the [rightly] guided.
interpretation: This verse indicates that those who receive blessings and mercy from Allah are the ones who are truly guided. They have earned Allah's favor through their faith, righteousness, and adherence to the straight path. The blessings and mercy mentioned in this verse are not mere worldly comforts, but spiritual gifts that bring inner peace, contentment, and success in both this life and the hereafter. Being rightly guided is the ultimate achievement, as it leads to salvation and eternal bliss in Paradise. The verse emphasizes that divine guidance is a special gift from Allah, bestowed upon those who sincerely seek it and strive to live according to His commands.
orig: أولئك عليهم صلوات من ربهم ورحمة وأولئك هم المهتدون

translation: Indeed, as-Safa and al-Marwah are among the symbols of Allah. So whoever makes Hajj to the House or performs 'umrah - there is no blame upon him for walking between them. And whoever volunteers good - then indeed, Allah is Appreciative and Knowing.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the hills of Safa and Marwah are sacred sites decreed by Allah. It establishes that walking or running between them during Hajj or Umrah is a virtuous act and an integral part of these pilgrimages. There is no sin on the pilgrim for performing this rite. In fact, doing extra circuits voluntarily between Safa and Marwah is encouraged, as Allah recognizes and appreciates those who do good deeds beyond what is obligatory. Allah's knowledge encompasses the intentions and actions of those who perform these additional acts of worship.
orig: إن الصفا والمروة من شعائر الله فمن حج البيت أو اعتمر فلا جناح عليه أن يطوف بهما ومن تطوع خيرا فإن الله شاكر عليم

translation: Indeed, those who conceal what We sent down of clear proofs and guidance after We made it clear for the people in the Scripture - those are cursed by Allah and cursed by those who curse,
interpretation: This verse warns against those who deliberately hide or conceal the truth and guidance that Allah has revealed in His scriptures, even after it has been made clear to them. Such people incur the curse and condemnation of Allah, as well as the curses of those who are aware of their wrongdoing. It emphasizes the severity of knowingly suppressing divine guidance and denying others access to it. The verse implies that it is a grave sin to withhold or obscure religious knowledge that can benefit and enlighten people, and those who engage in such behavior will face serious consequences in this world and the hereafter.
orig: إن الذين يكتمون ما أنزلنا من البينات والهدى من بعد ما بيناه للناس في الكتاب أولئك يلعنهم الله ويلعنهم اللاعنون

translation: Except for those who repent, reform, and make evident [what they concealed]. Those - I will accept their repentance, and I am the Accepting of repentance, the Merciful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of sincere repentance and making amends for one's mistakes. It shows that Allah, in His infinite mercy, is always ready to forgive those who turn back to Him with a genuine intention to reform themselves and rectify their wrongdoings. The verse also highlights the significance of being transparent and making evident what one might have previously concealed, as a sign of true repentance. It serves as a reminder that Allah is the Most Forgiving and the Most Merciful, and He will accept the repentance of those who sincerely seek His forgiveness and strive to become better individuals.
orig: إلا الذين تابوا وأصلحوا وبينوا فأولئك أتوب عليهم وأنا التواب الرحيم

translation: Indeed, those who disbelieved and died while they were disbelievers - upon them will be the curse of Allah and of the angels and the people, all together,
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the severe consequences that await those who reject faith in Allah and die in a state of disbelief. The interpretation is that such individuals will face the wrath and condemnation not only of Allah but also of the angels and all of humanity. This underscores the gravity of their choice to deny the truth and the unanimous disapproval they will face in the afterlife from all quarters. The verse serves as a strong warning against disbelief and highlights the importance of embracing faith before it is too late.
orig: إن الذين كفروا وماتوا وهم كفار أولئك عليهم لعنة الله والملائكة والناس أجمعين

translation: Abiding eternally therein. The punishment will not be lightened for them, nor will they be reprieved.
interpretation: This verse speaks about the fate of those who reject faith and do evil deeds. It emphasizes that they will abide in Hell eternally, without any hope of the punishment being lightened or being given a temporary reprieve. This highlights the severity and permanence of the consequences of rejecting God's message and choosing to follow the path of sin and disobedience. It serves as a strong warning to mankind to be mindful of their actions and to strive for righteousness and faith in order to avoid such a terrible fate in the Hereafter.
orig: خالدين فيها لا يخفف عنهم العذاب ولا هم ينظرون

translation: And your God is one God. There is no deity [worthy of worship] except Him, the Entirely Merciful, the Especially Merciful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the oneness and uniqueness of Allah, the only true God worthy of worship. It highlights two of His divine attributes: "Ar-Rahman" (the Entirely Merciful) and "Ar-Rahim" (the Especially Merciful). These attributes underscore Allah's infinite compassion, grace, and mercy that He extends to all His creation. The verse serves as a powerful reminder for believers to direct their worship, devotion, and submission solely to Allah, as He alone is the source of all mercy and blessings. It also reinforces the fundamental Islamic belief in monotheism (Tawheed) and the rejection of any form of polytheism or association of partners with Allah.
orig: وإلهكم إله واحد لا إله إلا هو الرحمن الرحيم

translation: Indeed, in the creation of the heavens and the earth, and the alternation of the night and the day, and the ships which sail through the sea with that which benefits people, and what Allah has sent down from the heavens of rain, giving life thereby to the earth after its lifelessness and dispersing therein every [kind of] moving creature, and [His] directing of the winds and the clouds controlled between the heaven and the earth are signs for a people who use reason.
interpretation: This verse draws our attention to the signs of Allah's existence, power, and wisdom that are evident in the natural world around us. It invites us to ponder upon the marvels of creation, such as the perfect harmony in the heavens and the earth, the alternation of day and night, the ships that sail the seas for the benefit of mankind, the life-giving rain that revives the dead earth, the countless creatures that Allah has scattered throughout the world, and the winds and clouds that are controlled by His command. These are all indications of a higher power and a greater purpose behind our existence. The verse emphasizes that these signs are apparent to those who use their intellect and reflect deeply, encouraging us to engage in critical thinking and to appreciate the wonders of Allah's creation. Ultimately, it reminds us of our responsibility to acknowledge and worship the One who has created and sustains everything around us.
