The verse emphasizes that Allah is fully aware of the intentions and actions of people, and that everyone will ultimately return to Him for judgment. It serves as a reminder for Muslims to prioritize their loyalty to Allah and the community of believers over any temporal alliances with those who reject faith.
orig: لا يتخذ المؤمنون الكافرين أولياء من دون المؤمنين ومن يفعل ذلك فليس من الله في شيء إلا أن تتقوا منهم تقاة ويحذركم الله نفسه وإلى الله المصير

translation: Say, "Whether you conceal what is in your breasts or reveal it, Allah knows it. And He knows that which is in the heavens and that which is on the earth. And Allah is over all things competent."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the all-encompassing knowledge and power of Allah. It reminds us that nothing can be hidden from Him, whether it is the innermost thoughts and feelings in our hearts or the actions we manifest outwardly. Allah's knowledge extends beyond the realm of human perception, encompassing the vastness of the heavens and the earth. The verse also highlights Allah's omnipotence, affirming that He has the ability to do all things and that His power is limitless. This understanding should instill a sense of consciousness and mindfulness in believers, encouraging them to align their intentions and actions with what pleases Allah, as He is fully aware of all that we do and will hold us accountable for it.
orig: قل إن تخفوا ما في صدوركم أو تبدوه يعلمه الله ويعلم ما في السماوات وما في الأرض والله على كل شيء قدير

translation: The Day every soul will find what it has done of good present [before it] and what it has done of evil, it will wish that between itself and that [evil] was a great distance. And Allah warns you of Himself, and Allah is Kind and Merciful to [His] servants.
interpretation: This verse is a reminder of the Day of Judgment, when every person will face the consequences of their actions in this world. The good deeds will be presented before them, bringing joy and satisfaction, while the evil deeds will cause immense regret and the wish for a great distance between themselves and their wrongdoings. This verse also emphasizes Allah's attribute of warning mankind against His punishment, while simultaneously highlighting His kindness and mercy towards His servants who seek His forgiveness and strive to do good. It serves as an encouragement for people to be mindful of their actions and to turn to Allah in repentance and obedience.
orig: يوم تجد كل نفس ما عملت من خير محضرا وما عملت من سوء تود لو أن بينها وبينه أمدا بعيدا ويحذركم الله نفسه والله رءوف بالعباد

translation: Say, [O Muhammad], "If you should love Allah, then follow me, [so] Allah will love you and forgive you your sins. And Allah is Forgiving and Merciful."
interpretation: This verse is a call to those who claim to love Allah to prove their love by following the teachings and example of Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him). It emphasizes that true love for Allah is demonstrated through obedience to His messenger. The verse also promises that by sincerely following the Prophet, one will earn Allah's love and forgiveness, highlighting the mercy and forgiving nature of Allah towards His servants who strive to please Him. It serves as a reminder that actions speak louder than words when it comes to expressing devotion to Allah.
orig: قل إن كنتم تحبون الله فاتبعوني يحببكم الله ويغفر لكم ذنوبكم والله غفور رحيم

translation: Say, "Obey Allah and the Messenger." But if they turn away - then indeed, Allah does not like the disbelievers.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of obedience to Allah and His Messenger, Muhammad (peace be upon him). It is a clear command to follow their guidance and submit to their authority. The verse also serves as a warning to those who reject faith and refuse to obey, stating that Allah does not love or approve of those who disbelieve in Him and His messages. It highlights the consequences of turning away from the path of Islam and the necessity of complete submission to the will of Allah to attain His love and pleasure.
orig: قل أطيعوا الله والرسول فإن تولوا فإن الله لا يحب الكافرين

translation: Indeed, Allah chose Adam and Noah and the family of Abraham and the family of 'Imran over the worlds.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the special status and favor that Allah has bestowed upon certain individuals and families throughout history. The selection of Adam, Noah, the family of Abraham, and the family of 'Imran demonstrates Allah's wisdom in choosing those who are most worthy and capable of carrying out His message and guiding humanity. This divine choice also highlights the continuity of the prophetic mission and the importance of following the examples set by these chosen individuals and families in terms of faith, righteousness, and submission to Allah's will. The mention of these figures serves as a reminder for believers to strive for excellence in their spiritual lives and to seek inspiration from the lives of the prophets and their families.
orig: إن الله اصطفى آدم ونوحا وآل إبراهيم وآل عمران على العالمين

translation: Offspring, some of them from others. And Allah is All-Hearing, All-Knowing.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the continuity and interconnectedness of human generations. It suggests that all humans are part of a single lineage, descended from one another in a continuous chain. The mention of Allah's attributes of being All-Hearing and All-Knowing at the end of the verse implies that He is fully aware of this human connection and the relationships between individuals and generations. It also indicates that Allah hears the prayers and supplications of all people, regardless of their place in the generational chain, and has knowledge of their actions and intentions.
orig: ذرية بعضها من بعض والله سميع عليم

translation: When a woman of 'Imran said, "My Lord, indeed I have pledged to You what is in my womb, consecrated [for Your service], so accept this from me. Indeed, You are the Hearing, the Knowing."
interpretation: This verse is referring to the mother of Mary, the mother of Jesus. She dedicated her unborn child to the service of God, even before knowing whether the child would be male or female. This shows her deep faith and trust in God's plan. It also highlights the importance of making sincere intentions and following through on our commitments to God. The verse emphasizes that God is all-hearing and all-knowing, indicating that He is aware of our innermost thoughts and intentions, and will accept our devotion when it is genuine and pure.
orig: إذ قالت امرأت عمران رب إني نذرت لك ما في بطني محررا فتقبل مني إنك أنت السميع العليم

translation: But when she delivered her, she said, "My Lord, I have delivered a female." And Allah was most knowing of what she delivered, and the male is not like the female. "And I have named her Mary, and I seek refuge for her in You and [for] her descendants from Satan, the expelled [from the mercy of Allah]."
interpretation: This verse highlights the trust and faith of Mary's mother in Allah. Despite giving birth to a girl when she hoped for a boy to serve in the temple, she accepts Allah's will and seeks His protection for Mary and her offspring from the influence of Satan. This demonstrates the importance of submitting to Allah's plan and seeking refuge in Him, even when faced with unexpected or seemingly disappointing outcomes.
orig: فلما وضعتها قالت رب إني وضعتها أنثى والله أعلم بما وضعت وليس الذكر كالأنثى وإني سميتها مريم وإني أعيذها بك وذريتها من الشيطان الرجيم

translation: So her Lord accepted her with good acceptance and caused her to grow in a good manner and put her in the care of Zechariah. Every time Zechariah entered upon her in the prayer chamber, he found with her provision. He said, "O Mary, from where is this [coming] to you?" She said, "It is from Allah. Indeed, Allah provides for whom He wills without account."
interpretation: This verse highlights the special status and miraculous nature of Mary, the mother of Jesus. Despite her young age and the absence of a husband, God provided for her needs in miraculous ways, as evidenced by the provisions that Zechariah found in her prayer chamber. This demonstrates God's power to provide sustenance to whomever He wills, without limit or measure. The verse also emphasizes the importance of trusting in God's providence and recognizing that all blessings come from Him alone.
orig: فتقبلها ربها بقبول حسن وأنبتها نباتا حسنا وكفلها زكريا كلما دخل عليها زكريا المحراب وجد عندها رزقا قال يا مريم أنى لك هذا قالت هو من عند الله إن الله يرزق من يشاء بغير حساب

translation: At that time Zechariah called upon his Lord, saying, "My Lord, grant me from Yourself a good offspring. Indeed, You are the Hearer of supplication."
interpretation: This verse shows the importance and power of sincere supplication to Allah. Zechariah, despite his old age and his wife's barrenness, turns to Allah with humility and faith, asking for a righteous child. This demonstrates that no matter how impossible our desires may seem, we should never lose hope in Allah's power to grant them. The verse also emphasizes Allah's attribute as the "Hearer of supplication", reminding us that He always listens to the prayers of His servants. When we call upon Him with sincerity and trust, He will respond in the way that is best for us, even if it may be different than what we expect.
orig: هنالك دعا زكريا ربه قال رب هب لي من لدنك ذرية طيبة إنك سميع الدعاء

translation: Then the angels called him while he was standing in prayer in the chamber, "Indeed, Allah gives you good tidings of John, confirming a word from Allah and [who will be] honorable, abstaining [from women], and a prophet from among the righteous."
interpretation: This verse signifies the miraculous birth of Prophet John (Yahya) to the Prophet Zachariah and his wife, who was barren. The angels give Zachariah the good news of a son who will be a righteous prophet, confirming the truth of God's message. John is described as being "honorable" and "abstaining", indicating his piety and devotion to God. This verse highlights the power of God to grant a child to an elderly couple and the importance of faith and righteousness in God's chosen prophets.
orig: فنادته الملائكة وهو قائم يصلي في المحراب أن الله يبشرك بيحيى مصدقا بكلمة من الله وسيدا وحصورا ونبيا من الصالحين

translation: He said, "My Lord, how will I have a boy when I have reached old age and my wife is barren?" [The angel] said, "Such is Allah; He does what He wills."
interpretation: This verse highlights the power and omnipotence of Allah. Even in seemingly impossible situations, such as an elderly couple having a child despite the wife being barren, Allah can make it happen if He wills it. It emphasizes that nothing is beyond Allah's capabilities and that His decree supersedes the natural order of things. The verse also demonstrates the importance of having faith and trust in Allah's plan, even when it may seem unlikely or impossible from a human perspective. It encourages believers to submit to Allah's will and have confidence in His wisdom and mercy.
orig: قال رب أنى يكون لي غلام وقد بلغني الكبر وامرأتي عاقر قال كذلك الله يفعل ما يشاء

translation: He said, "My Lord, make for me a sign." He Said, "Your sign is that you will not [be able to] speak to the people for three days except by gesture. And remember your Lord much and exalt [Him with praise] in the evening and the morning."
interpretation: This verse is a reminder of the importance of patience and trust in Allah's plan. Zechariah, upon being told that he would have a son despite his old age, asked for a sign to confirm this miracle. Allah's response was to make him unable to speak for three days, except through gestures. This was a test of Zechariah's faith and a reminder to him to remember and praise Allah abundantly, particularly in the evening and morning. The verse emphasizes the significance of constant remembrance and gratitude towards Allah, even in times of difficulty or when facing seemingly impossible circumstances. It encourages believers to maintain a strong connection with their Lord through dhikr (remembrance) and to trust in His wisdom and timing.
orig: قال رب اجعل لي آية قال آيتك ألا تكلم الناس ثلاثة أيام إلا رمزا واذكر ربك كثيرا وسبح بالعشي والإبكار

translation: And [mention] when the angels said, "O Mary, indeed Allah has chosen you and purified you and chosen you above the women of the worlds."
interpretation: This verse highlights the special status and honor bestowed upon Mary, the mother of Jesus, by Allah. The angels convey to her that she has been chosen and purified by Allah, and elevated in status above all other women of the worlds. This indicates her piety, righteousness, and the unique role she would play in the divine plan as the mother of one of Allah's greatest prophets. It is a testament to her faith and submission to Allah's will, and a reminder of the high regard in which she is held in Islam.
orig: وإذ قالت الملائكة يا مريم إن الله اصطفاك وطهرك واصطفاك على نساء العالمين

translation: O Mary, be devoutly obedient to your Lord and prostrate and bow with those who bow [in prayer].
interpretation: This verse is calling upon Mary, the mother of Jesus, to be fully devoted and obedient to God. It instructs her to engage in acts of worship and submission such as prostration (sujud) and bowing (ruku') in prayer along with the community of believers. The command to Mary serves as an example for all believers to be sincere and humble in their worship and to join together in congregation rather than remaining isolated. It highlights the importance of prayer and the spiritual connection with God and with fellow worshippers.
orig: يا مريم اقنتي لربك واسجدي واركعي مع الراكعين

translation: That is from the news of the unseen which We reveal to you, [O Muhammad]. And you were not with them when they cast their pens as to which of them should be responsible for Mary. Nor were you with them when they disputed.
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine nature of the Qur'an and the knowledge it contains. It emphasizes that the information about Mary and the casting of lots to determine who would be her guardian was not known to Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) through any human means, but rather it was revealed to him by Allah. This serves as a proof of the Prophet's truthfulness and the authenticity of the Qur'an, as it contains knowledge of the unseen that could not have been known to him otherwise. The verse also alludes to the fact that even the most righteous people, such as the guardians of Mary, were not immune to disagreements and disputes, emphasizing the human nature of all individuals except the prophets.
orig: ذلك من أنباء الغيب نوحيه إليك وما كنت لديهم إذ يلقون أقلامهم أيهم يكفل مريم وما كنت لديهم إذ يختصمون

translation: When the angels said, "O Mary, indeed Allah gives you good tidings of a word from Him, whose name will be the Messiah, Jesus, the son of Mary - distinguished in this world and the Hereafter and among those brought near [to Allah].
interpretation: This verse signifies the great honor bestowed upon Mary, the mother of Jesus. The angels brought her the good news that she would miraculously give birth to a son, Jesus, who would be the Messiah. This news highlights Jesus' special status and his closeness to God. The verse emphasizes that Jesus will be highly respected and distinguished both in this worldly life and in the Hereafter, indicating his important role as a prophet and messenger of God. It also suggests that Jesus will be among those closest to God in Paradise, a position of great honor and blessing.
orig: إذ قالت الملائكة يا مريم إن الله يبشرك بكلمة منه اسمه المسيح عيسى ابن مريم وجيها في الدنيا والآخرة ومن المقربين

translation: And he will speak to the people in the cradle and in maturity and will be of the righteous.
interpretation: This verse refers to Jesus, who was blessed with the miracle of speaking as an infant in the cradle. This was a sign of his prophethood and a testament to the power of God. The verse also mentions that Jesus will speak to people in his adulthood, indicating his role as a messenger of God throughout his life. The final part of the verse describes Jesus as being among the righteous, affirming his status as a pious and virtuous individual chosen by God to guide humanity. This verse highlights the unique qualities and divine nature of Jesus as a prophet in Islam.
orig: ويكلم الناس في المهد وكهلا ومن الصالحين

translation: She said, "My Lord, how will I have a child when no man has touched me?" [The angel] said, "Such is Allah; He creates what He wills. When He decrees a matter, He only says to it, 'Be,' and it is."
interpretation: This verse highlights the miraculous nature of Jesus' birth and the power of Allah's decree. Mary questions how she can conceive without having been touched by a man, but the angel reassures her that Allah's power transcends the natural order. The phrase "He only says to it, 'Be,' and it is" emphasizes the effortless nature of Allah's creation and His ability to bring about anything He wills, even if it seems impossible from a human perspective. This verse also serves as a reminder to have faith in Allah's plan and to trust in His wisdom, even when faced with seemingly insurmountable challenges or situations that defy our understanding.
orig: قالت رب أنى يكون لي ولد ولم يمسسني بشر قال كذلك الله يخلق ما يشاء إذا قضى أمرا فإنما يقول له كن فيكون

translation: And He will teach him the Book and wisdom and the Torah and the Gospel.
interpretation: This verse refers to the knowledge and wisdom that Allah will bestow upon Jesus, the son of Mary. It indicates that Jesus will be taught the divine scriptures, including the Torah revealed to Moses and the Gospel revealed to him. This knowledge and wisdom will enable Jesus to fulfill his role as a prophet and messenger of Allah, guiding people to the straight path. The verse highlights the special status and divine favor granted to Jesus, as he will be blessed with a comprehensive understanding of the sacred texts and the ability to convey their teachings to humanity.
orig: ويعلمه الكتاب والحكمة والتوراة والإنجيل

translation: And [make him] a messenger to the Children of Israel, [who will say], "Indeed I have come to you with a sign from your Lord in that I design for you from clay [that which is] like the form of a bird, then I breathe into it and it becomes a bird by permission of Allah. And I cure the blind and the leper, and I give life to the dead - by permission of Allah. And I inform you of what you eat and what you store in your houses. Indeed in that is a sign for you, if you are believers.
interpretation: This verse is highlighting the miracles that Allah bestowed upon Jesus, peace be upon him, as a sign of his prophethood and a means to invite the Children of Israel to believe in the message he brought. These miracles, such as breathing life into a clay bird, healing the blind and the leper, and bringing the dead back to life, were performed only by Allah's permission. They serve as a testament to Allah's power and Jesus' role as His messenger. Additionally, Jesus' knowledge of what people ate and stored in their homes, without being present, further proves his divine connection. The verse emphasizes that these miracles should be sufficient proof for those who truly believe in Allah and His messengers.
orig: ورسولا إلى بني إسرائيل أني قد جئتكم بآية من ربكم أني أخلق لكم من الطين كهيئة الطير فأنفخ فيه فيكون طيرا بإذن الله وأبرئ الأكمه والأبرص وأحيي الموتى بإذن الله وأنبئكم بما تأكلون وما تدخرون في بيوتكم إن في ذلك لآية لكم إن كنتم مؤمنين

translation: And [I have come] confirming what was before me of the Torah and to make lawful for you some of what was forbidden to you. And I have come to you with a sign from your Lord, so fear Allah and obey me.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the continuity and consistency of the divine message brought by Prophet Jesus (peace be upon him) with the previous revelations, particularly the Torah. It also highlights his role in providing guidance and making lawful some of the things that were previously forbidden to the Children of Israel. This points to the evolving nature of divine law, which is adapted to the needs and circumstances of different times and communities. The verse also underscores the importance of fearing Allah and obeying His messenger, as Jesus came with clear signs and proofs from God to support his message. This interpretation suggests that following the guidance of the prophets and messengers is essential for attaining righteousness and earning Allah's pleasure.
orig: ومصدقا لما بين يدي من التوراة ولأحل لكم بعض الذي حرم عليكم وجئتكم بآية من ربكم فاتقوا الله وأطيعون

translation: Indeed, Allah is my Lord and your Lord, so worship Him. This is a straight path.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the oneness of Allah and His sovereignty over all creation. It calls upon humanity to submit to Allah alone and worship Him exclusively, as that is the only path that leads to success and salvation. The straight path mentioned here refers to the way of life prescribed by Allah, which involves following His guidance, obeying His commands, and abstaining from what He has prohibited. By adhering to this straight path, one can attain inner peace, contentment, and ultimately, eternal bliss in the Hereafter.
orig: إن الله ربي وربكم فاعبدوه هذا صراط مستقيم

translation: But when Jesus felt [persistence in] disbelief from them, he said, "Who are my supporters for [the cause of] Allah?" The disciples said, "We are supporters for Allah. We have believed in Allah and testify that we are Muslims [submitting to Him].
interpretation: This verse highlights the unwavering faith and commitment of the disciples of Jesus (peace be upon him) in the face of disbelief and opposition. When Jesus sensed the persistent disbelief of some people, he sought out those who would stand by him in support of Allah's cause. The disciples, without hesitation, declared their belief in Allah and their submission to Him as Muslims. This verse emphasizes the importance of remaining steadfast in one's faith, even in the face of adversity, and the value of having a strong support system of fellow believers who will stand together in the cause of righteousness and truth.
orig: فلما أحس عيسى منهم الكفر قال من أنصاري إلى الله قال الحواريون نحن أنصار الله آمنا بالله واشهد بأنا مسلمون

translation: Our Lord, we have believed in what You revealed and have followed the messenger Jesus, so register us among the witnesses [to truth].
interpretation: This verse is a prayer and declaration of faith by the disciples of Jesus. They affirm their belief in the revelation sent down by God and their following of Jesus as God's messenger. They ask God to count them among those who bear witness to the truth of His message. This points to the importance of both faith and good deeds - inward belief must be coupled with outward obedience to God's commandments and following the example of His prophets. The disciples also recognize that it is only by God's grace that they can be counted among the righteous witnesses in the end.
orig: ربنا آمنا بما أنزلت واتبعنا الرسول فاكتبنا مع الشاهدين

translation: And the disbelievers planned, but Allah planned. And Allah is the best of planners.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the supremacy of Allah's plan over the schemes of the disbelievers. It asserts that no matter how cleverly the enemies of Islam may plot against the believers, Allah's plan will always prevail. The use of the word "makr" (planning or plotting) for both the disbelievers and Allah highlights the contrast between the two - while the disbelievers' plotting is motivated by evil intentions, Allah's planning is inherently good and wise. The verse serves as a reassurance to the believers that they should not be disheartened by the plots of their enemies, as Allah is always in control and will ultimately ensure the victory of truth over falsehood.
orig: ومكروا ومكر الله والله خير الماكرين

translation: When Allah said, "O Jesus, indeed I will take you and raise you to Myself and purify you from those who disbelieve and make those who follow you [in submission to Allah alone] superior to those who disbelieve until the Day of Resurrection. Then to Me is your return, and I will judge between you concerning that in which you used to differ."
interpretation: This verse speaks about Allah's promise to Jesus (peace be upon him). It affirms that Allah will protect Jesus from the plots of the disbelievers, raise him alive to the heavens, and purify him from the false accusations made against him. Furthermore, Allah promises that the true followers of Jesus, i.e., the Muslims, will be made superior to the disbelievers until the Day of Judgment. On that day, all will return to Allah, and He will judge between them regarding their differences and disputes in this worldly life. This verse highlights Allah's support for His prophets and believers, and the ultimate triumph of truth over falsehood.
orig: إذ قال الله يا عيسى إني متوفيك ورافعك إلي ومطهرك من الذين كفروا وجاعل الذين اتبعوك فوق الذين كفروا إلى يوم القيامة ثم إلي مرجعكم فأحكم بينكم فيما كنتم فيه تختلفون

translation: And as for those who disbelieved, I will punish them with a severe punishment in this world and the Hereafter, and they will have no helpers.
interpretation: This verse serves as a stern warning to those who reject faith in Allah and His message. It emphasizes that disbelievers will face severe consequences for their actions, not only in this worldly life but also in the Hereafter. The punishment mentioned here is a result of their conscious choice to deny the truth and persist in disbelief. Moreover, the verse highlights the helplessness of the disbelievers, stating that they will have no one to support or protect them from Allah's judgment and punishment. This interpretation underscores the gravity of rejecting faith and the ultimate consequences that await those who choose this path.
orig: فأما الذين كفروا فأعذبهم عذابا شديدا في الدنيا والآخرة وما لهم من ناصرين

translation: And as for those who believed and did righteous deeds, He will give them in full their rewards. And Allah does not like the wrongdoers.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the justice and fairness of Allah. Those who have faith and do good deeds will be fully rewarded for their actions in the Hereafter. On the other hand, Allah does not love those who are unjust and engage in wrongdoing. The verse serves as a reminder that our actions in this life have consequences, and that ultimately, it is Allah who will judge us based on our faith and deeds. It encourages believers to strive for righteousness and to avoid transgressing the limits set by Allah.
orig: وأما الذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات فيوفيهم أجورهم والله لا يحب الظالمين

translation: These are the verses of the Qur'an and a clear Book that We recite to you
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the divine nature and wisdom of the Qur'an. It is a reminder that the verses being recited to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) are not mere words, but a profound revelation from Allah. The Qur'an is described as "clear" (mubin), indicating that its message and guidance are evident and accessible to those who sincerely seek to understand it. By reciting these verses to the Prophet, Allah is affirming the authenticity and significance of the Qur'anic revelation, which serves as a source of guidance and enlightenment for all of humanity.
orig: ذلك نتلوه عليك من الآيات والذكر الحكيم

translation: Indeed, the example of Jesus to Allah is like that of Adam. He created Him from dust; then He said to him, "Be," and he was.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the power and authority of Allah in creating and giving life. Just as Adam was created from dust by Allah's command, without a father or mother, so too was Jesus created by Allah's command, without a father. The verse highlights the similarity between the two prophets in terms of their miraculous creation and serves as a reminder that all creation comes into being through Allah's will and power alone. It also refutes the notion of Jesus being the literal son of God, as he was created by divine command, just like Adam.
orig: إن مثل عيسى عند الله كمثل آدم خلقه من تراب ثم قال له كن فيكون

translation: The truth is from your Lord, so do not be among the doubters.
interpretation: This verse is a reminder from Allah to the believers to have firm faith and conviction in the message of Islam. It emphasizes that the Qur'an and the teachings of Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) are the ultimate truth that comes directly from Allah. Therefore, one should not have any doubts or uncertainties about their faith. The verse encourages the believers to stay steadfast in their belief and not be swayed by the doubts or criticisms of others who may try to undermine their faith. It is a call to trust in Allah's guidance and to have confidence in the path of Islam, knowing that it is the truth that leads to success in this life and the hereafter.
orig: الحق من ربك فلا تكن من الممترين

translation: So whoever argues with you about it after the knowledge that has come to you, say: "Come, let us call our sons and your sons, our women and your women, ourselves and yourselves, then let us humbly pray and invoke the curse of Allah upon the liars."
interpretation: This verse is inviting those who dispute the truth of Islam, after clear proofs have come, to a Mubahala (invocation of God's curse). It's a challenge to the disputers to come together with the Prophet, bringing their families, and to pray humbly to God to curse the side that is lying. This highlights the Prophet's confidence in his message, as he's willing to put himself and his loved ones on the line. It also shows that when faced with stubborn denial of clear truths, sometimes a dramatic, spiritually-weighted challenge is warranted to shake the disputers and make them face the gravity of their rejection. The verse emphasizes the seriousness of rejecting the truth of Islam after it has been made clear through undeniable proofs.
orig: فمن حاجك فيه من بعد ما جاءك من العلم فقل تعالوا ندع أبناءنا وأبناءكم ونساءنا ونساءكم وأنفسنا وأنفسكم ثم نبتهل فنجعل لعنت الله على الكاذبين

translation: Indeed, this is the true narration. And there is no deity except Allah. And indeed, Allah is the Exalted in Might, the Wise.
interpretation: This verse affirms that the stories and accounts mentioned in the Qur'an are true and factual, not mere legends or myths. It emphasizes the absolute oneness and uniqueness of Allah, negating the existence of any other deity worthy of worship. The verse also highlights two of Allah's attributes: Al-'Azeez (the Almighty, the All-Powerful) and Al-Hakeem (the All-Wise). It conveys that Allah's power and wisdom are unparalleled, and that He alone deserves to be worshipped and obeyed. This verse serves as a reminder for believers to put their trust in Allah and to seek guidance from the Qur'an, as it contains the ultimate truth.
orig: إن هذا لهو القصص الحق وما من إله إلا الله وإن الله لهو العزيز الحكيم

translation: And if they turn away, then indeed Allah is Knowing of the corrupters.
interpretation: This verse warns that if people turn away from the message of Islam and the guidance of Allah, then Allah is fully aware of those who spread corruption and cause mischief in the land. It implies that Allah will hold them accountable for their actions and will deal with them accordingly in this world and the Hereafter. The verse serves as a reminder that one cannot escape the knowledge and justice of Allah, and that it is in one's own best interest to follow the straight path and avoid corruption.
orig: فإن تولوا فإن الله عليم بالمفسدين

translation: Say, "O People of the Scripture, come to a word that is equitable between us and you - that we will not worship except Allah and not associate anything with Him and not take one another as lords instead of Allah." But if they turn away, then say, "Bear witness that we are Muslims [submitting to Him]."
interpretation: This verse is an invitation to the People of the Book (Jews and Christians) to come to a common ground and mutual understanding with Muslims. It emphasizes the fundamental principle of worshipping Allah alone and not associating any partners with Him. The verse also rejects the idea of taking religious leaders or figures as lords besides Allah, which means not to blindly follow them or elevate them to a divine status. If the People of the Book refuse this invitation, Muslims are instructed to declare their submission to Allah and bear witness to their faith.
orig: قل يا أهل الكتاب تعالوا إلى كلمة سواء بيننا وبينكم ألا نعبد إلا الله ولا نشرك به شيئا ولا يتخذ بعضنا بعضا أربابا من دون الله فإن تولوا فقولوا اشهدوا بأنا مسلمون

translation: O People of the Book! Why do you argue about Abraham while the Torah and the Gospel were not revealed until after him? Then will you not reason?
interpretation: This verse is addressing the People of the Book, which refers to the Jews and Christians, questioning why they dispute about the religion of Prophet Abraham. It points out that both the Torah and the Gospel were revealed after the time of Abraham, so their arguments about his faith are baseless. The verse ends with a rhetorical question, challenging them to use their intellect and reason to realize the flaw in their disputations. It implies that if they were to reflect rationally, they would come to the understanding that Abraham preceded their scriptures, and thus their claims about his beliefs are unfounded.
orig: يا أهل الكتاب لم تحاجون في إبراهيم وما أنزلت التوراة والإنجيل إلا من بعده أفلا تعقلون

translation: Here you are - those who argue about that of which you have [some] knowledge, but why do you argue about that of which you have no knowledge? And Allah knows, while you know not.
interpretation: This verse is a rebuke to those who engage in arguments and debates about matters of religion without having proper knowledge or understanding. It highlights the importance of seeking knowledge before engaging in such discussions. The verse also emphasizes the vast difference between God's knowledge and human knowledge, reminding us that God is the All-Knowing, while human beings have limited knowledge. It encourages humility and cautions against arguing about matters that one has no expertise in, as it may lead to misguidance and spreading of misinformation about religion.
orig: ها أنتم هؤلاء حاججتم فيما لكم به علم فلم تحاجون فيما ليس لكم به علم والله يعلم وأنتم لا تعلمون

translation: Abraham was neither a Jew nor a Christian, but he was one inclining toward truth, a Muslim [submitting to Allah]. And he was not of the polytheists.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the prophet Abraham, who is revered by Jews, Christians, and Muslims, was not affiliated with any particular religious group that exists today. Rather, he was a monotheist who submitted himself wholly to the one true God (Allah). Abraham's faith was pure and uncorrupted by the idolatry and polytheism that was prevalent in his time. The verse implies that the essence of Abraham's faith, which is submission to the one God, is the same as the message of Islam. It also suggests that the divisions and differences between religious groups are a later development, and that the original message of all prophets, including Abraham, was the worship of one God alone.
orig: ما كان إبراهيم يهوديا ولا نصرانيا ولكن كان حنيفا مسلما وما كان من المشركين

translation: Indeed, the most worthy of Abraham among the people are those who followed him [in submission to Allah] and this prophet, and those who believe [in his message]. And Allah is the ally of the believers.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of following the example of Prophet Abraham and the teachings of Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him). It suggests that those who are truly deserving of being associated with Abraham are the ones who emulate his faith, submission to God, and righteous deeds. The verse also highlights the significance of believing in and supporting the message of Prophet Muhammad. Moreover, it reassures the believers that Allah is their protector and ally, guiding and supporting them in their spiritual journey. This interpretation underscores the value of aligning oneself with the prophetic tradition and the community of believers, while trusting in Allah's guidance and support.
orig: إن أولى الناس بإبراهيم للذين اتبعوه وهذا النبي والذين آمنوا والله ولي المؤمنين

translation: A group of the People of the Book wish they could mislead you. But they mislead not except themselves, and they perceive [it] not.
interpretation: This verse is referring to the fact that there were some among the People of the Book (Jews and Christians) who wished to lead the Muslims astray from the right path. However, Allah makes it clear that their attempts to mislead others will only lead themselves astray, even though they may not realize it. It highlights the fact that those who try to deceive others or lead them away from the truth are ultimately only harming themselves spiritually, even if they are unaware of the consequences of their actions.
orig: ودت طائفة من أهل الكتاب لو يضلونكم وما يضلون إلا أنفسهم وما يشعرون

translation: O People of the Scripture, why do you disbelieve in the verses of Allah while you witness [to their truth]?
interpretation: This verse is addressing the People of the Book, specifically the Jews and Christians, questioning their disbelief in the revelations and signs of Allah despite their knowledge and recognition of the truth. It suggests that they are rejecting the message of Islam and the prophethood of Muhammad (peace be upon him) even though deep down, they know it to be true. The verse implies that their disbelief stems from their stubbornness, prejudice, or worldly desires rather than a lack of evidence or conviction. It is a call for them to reflect on their actions and embrace the truth that they already witness and know in their hearts.
orig: يا أهل الكتاب لم تكفرون بآيات الله وأنتم تشهدون

translation: O People of the Scripture, why do you mix the truth with falsehood and conceal the truth while you know [it]?
interpretation: This verse is a rebuke to the People of the Scripture (Jews and Christians) for their practice of mixing truth with falsehood in their religious teachings and scriptures. They are accused of concealing the truth about the message of Islam and the prophethood of Muhammad, despite knowing it to be true from their own scriptures. The Qur'an calls them out for their dishonesty and challenges them to embrace the truth of Islam, rather than hiding or distorting it for their own purposes.
orig: يا أهل الكتاب لم تلبسون الحق بالباطل وتكتمون الحق وأنتم تعلمون

translation: And a faction of the People of the Scripture say [to each other], "Believe in that which was revealed to the believers at the beginning of the day and reject it at its end that perhaps they will abandon their religion,
interpretation: This verse is referring to a deceptive tactic employed by some of the People of the Book (i.e., Jews and Christians) in an attempt to create doubt and confusion among the Muslims. They would pretend to believe in the revelation sent down to the Muslims at the beginning of the day, but then reject it later on, hoping that this would cause the Muslims to question their own faith and abandon Islam. It highlights the insincere and manipulative behavior of those who opposed the message of Islam and sought to undermine it through various means.
orig: وقالت طائفة من أهل الكتاب آمنوا بالذي أنزل على الذين آمنوا وجه النهار واكفروا آخره لعلهم يرجعون

translation: And do not believe except those who follow your religion. Say, "Indeed, the [true] guidance is the guidance of Allah. [Do you fear] lest someone be given [knowledge] like you were given or that they would [thereby] argue with you before your Lord?" Say, "Indeed, [all] bounty is in the hand of Allah - He grants it to whom He wills. And Allah is all-Encompassing and Wise."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that true guidance comes only from Allah, and that believers should not put their trust in anyone except those who follow the same religion. It also reminds us that all blessings and knowledge come from Allah alone, who bestows them upon whomever He chooses according to His infinite wisdom. The verse warns against the fear of others being given similar or greater knowledge, as this could lead to them arguing against the believers before Allah. Ultimately, it affirms that Allah's favor and bounty are in His hands alone, and He grants them to whom He wills, for He is All-Encompassing in His knowledge and Wise in His decisions.
orig: ولا تؤمنوا إلا لمن تبع دينكم قل إن الهدى هدى الله أن يؤتى أحد مثل ما أوتيتم أو يحاجوكم عند ربكم قل إن الفضل بيد الله يؤتيه من يشاء والله واسع عليم

translation: He selects for His mercy whom He wills. And Allah is the possessor of great bounty.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's absolute sovereignty and discretion in bestowing His mercy and blessings upon whomever He chooses. It highlights that Allah's grace and generosity are immense and that He alone decides who will receive His special favor and guidance. The verse also implies that humans should strive to be among those whom Allah selects for His mercy through faith, righteousness, and sincere devotion. Ultimately, it is a reminder that all bounties and blessings come from Allah, and one should always be grateful and humble in seeking His mercy and grace.
orig: يختص برحمته من يشاء والله ذو الفضل العظيم

translation: Among the People of the Scripture is he who, if you entrust him with a great amount [of wealth], he will return it to you. And among them is he who, if you entrust him with a [single] silver coin, he will not return it to you unless you are constantly standing over him [demanding it]. That is because they say, "There is no blame upon us concerning the unlearned." And they speak untruth about Allah while they know [it].
interpretation: This verse highlights the varying degrees of trustworthiness and integrity among the People of the Book (Jews and Christians). Some of them are so trustworthy that they would return a large sum of entrusted wealth, while others would not even return a single silver coin unless constantly pressured. The verse attributes this behavior to their belief that they are not accountable for their actions towards the gentiles or the unlearned. They falsely claim that God has allowed them to act dishonestly with non-Jews and non-Christians, which is a lie against Allah. This interpretation emphasizes the importance of individual integrity and the consequences of falsely attributing lies to God, regardless of one's religious affiliation.
orig: ومن أهل الكتاب من إن تأمنه بقنطار يؤده إليك ومنهم من إن تأمنه بدينار لا يؤده إليك إلا ما دمت عليه قائما ذلك بأنهم قالوا ليس علينا في الأميين سبيل ويقولون على الله الكذب وهم يعلمون

translation: But whoever fulfills his commitment and fears Allah - then indeed, Allah loves those who fear Him.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of fulfilling one's promises and obligations, especially those made with Allah. It also highlights the virtue of taqwa, which is the consciousness and fear of Allah that leads one to obey His commands and avoid His prohibitions. Allah's love is reserved for those who embody these qualities, as they demonstrate sincerity, loyalty, and devotion to Him. The verse serves as a reminder for believers to be truthful and steadfast in their commitments and to maintain a strong connection with Allah through righteous conduct and mindfulness of Him in all aspects of life.
orig: بلى من أوفى بعهده واتقى فإن الله يحب المتقين

translation: Indeed, those who exchange the covenant of Allah and their [own] oaths for a small price will have no share in the Hereafter, and Allah will not speak to them or look at them on the Day of Resurrection, nor will He purify them; and they will have a painful punishment.
interpretation: This verse is a stern warning to those who break their promises and oaths to Allah for worldly gains. It emphasizes that such people will face severe consequences in the afterlife, including being deprived of Allah's mercy, communication, and purification. They will be subjected to a painful punishment for their betrayal and lack of integrity. The verse highlights the importance of staying true to one's commitments and the gravity of breaking a covenant with Allah, as it not only affects one's spiritual well-being but also has serious repercussions in the Hereafter.
orig: إن الذين يشترون بعهد الله وأيمانهم ثمنا قليلا أولئك لا خلاق لهم في الآخرة ولا يكلمهم الله ولا ينظر إليهم يوم القيامة ولا يزكيهم ولهم عذاب أليم

translation: And indeed, there is among them a party who alter the Scripture with their tongues so you may think it is from the Scripture, but it is not from the Scripture. And they say, "This is from Allah," but it is not from Allah. And they speak untruth about Allah while they know.
interpretation: This verse is a warning against those who deliberately misinterpret or distort the teachings of the Qur'an for their own benefit. It suggests that there are individuals who twist the meaning of the scripture with their tongues, making it appear as if their false interpretations are part of the divine message. They attribute their own fabrications to Allah, knowingly speaking lies about Him. This act of deception is strongly condemned, as it misleads people and corrupts the true message of the Qur'an. The verse emphasizes the importance of upholding the integrity of the scripture and not allowing personal agendas or biases to influence its interpretation.
orig: وإن منهم لفريقا يلوون ألسنتهم بالكتاب لتحسبوه من الكتاب وما هو من الكتاب ويقولون هو من عند الله وما هو من عند الله ويقولون على الله الكذب وهم يعلمون

translation: It is not for a human [prophet] that Allah should give him the Scripture and authority and prophethood and then he would say to the people, "Be servants to me rather than Allah," but [instead, he would say], "Be pious scholars of the Lord because of what you have taught of the Scripture and because of what you have studied."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that no prophet, despite being given divine revelation, wisdom, and prophethood by Allah, would ever call people to worship him instead of Allah. Rather, a true prophet would guide people to be devoted servants and scholars of Allah, who study, teach, and live by the divine scriptures. It highlights the importance of humility and submission to Allah alone, even for those chosen as prophets, and encourages the pursuit of religious knowledge and piety.
orig: ما كان لبشر أن يؤتيه الله الكتاب والحكم والنبوة ثم يقول للناس كونوا عبادا لي من دون الله ولكن كونوا ربانيين بما كنتم تعلمون الكتاب وبما كنتم تدرسون

translation: Nor would He order you to take the angels and prophets as lords. Would He order you to disbelieve after you had been Muslims?
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah would never command people to worship anyone other than Him, including angels and prophets. It is a reminder that once a person has accepted Islam and submitted to Allah, it would be contradictory and illogical for Allah to then order them to commit shirk (associating partners with Allah) by worshipping others alongside Him. The verse affirms the fundamental principle of Islamic monotheism, which is the worship of Allah alone and the rejection of all forms of idolatry and polytheism. It also highlights the consistency and coherence of the divine message, as Allah's commands remain steadfast in guiding people towards true faith and submission to Him alone.
orig: ولا يأمركم أن تتخذوا الملائكة والنبيين أربابا أيأمركم بالكفر بعد إذ أنتم مسلمون

translation: And [recall, O People of the Scripture], when Allah took the covenant of the prophets, [saying], "Whatever I give you of the Scripture and wisdom and then there comes to you a messenger confirming what is with you, you [must] believe in him and support him." [Allah] said, "Have you acknowledged and taken upon that My commitment?" They said, "We have acknowledged it." He said, "Then bear witness, and I am with you among the witnesses."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the continuity and unity of the divine message throughout history. All prophets were given the same essential message and were bound by a covenant with Allah to support and confirm the truth of subsequent messengers who would come after them. This highlights the importance of believing in all the prophets and their messages, as they all come from the same divine source and are interconnected. The verse also serves as a reminder to the People of the Scripture (Jews and Christians) that they should accept and support the final messenger, Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him), as his message confirms and completes the previous revelations.
orig: وإذ أخذ الله ميثاق النبيين لما آتيتكم من كتاب وحكمة ثم جاءكم رسول مصدق لما معكم لتؤمنن به ولتنصرنه قال أأقررتم وأخذتم على ذلكم إصري قالوا أقررنا قال فاشهدوا وأنا معكم من الشاهدين

translation: And whoever turns away after that - then those are the defiantly disobedient.
interpretation: This verse warns that those who turn away from the truth and guidance of Allah after it has been made clear to them are considered "fasiqun" or defiantly disobedient. It implies that once a person has been exposed to the message of Islam and understands it, they have an obligation to follow it. Rejecting faith at that point is a serious sin that puts one in the category of the rebellious who intentionally disobey Allah's commands. The verse emphasizes the severity and consequences of knowingly turning one's back on divine guidance.
orig: فمن تولى بعد ذلك فأولئك هم الفاسقون

translation: Do they seek other than the religion of Allah, while to Him have submitted all those within the heavens and earth, willingly or by compulsion, and to Him they will be returned?
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the universality and inevitability of submission to Allah. It questions those who seek a religion other than Islam, pointing out that all beings in the heavens and earth, whether willingly or unwillingly, are subject to Allah's will and laws. The verse also reminds us that ultimately, all will return to Allah for judgment. It underscores the idea that Islam is the natural and true religion, in harmony with the inherent nature of the universe and all creation, and that submitting to Allah is the only path to salvation and eternal success.
orig: أفغير دين الله يبغون وله أسلم من في السماوات والأرض طوعا وكرها وإليه يرجعون

translation: Say, "We have believed in Allah and what has been revealed to us and what has been revealed to Abraham and Ishmael and Isaac and Jacob and the Descendants and what was given to Moses and Jesus and what was given to the prophets from their Lord. We make no distinction between any of them, and we are Muslims [in submission] to Him."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the unity of the divine message sent through various prophets. It calls upon the believers to affirm their faith in Allah and all His revelations without making any distinction between the prophets. This highlights the continuity of the core message brought by all the prophets, which is the belief in one God and submission to His will. The verse also stresses the importance of not discriminating between the prophets, as they all came with the same fundamental teachings. By declaring themselves as Muslims, the believers express their willingness to surrender to Allah's commandments and follow the guidance provided by all His messengers.
orig: قل آمنا بالله وما أنزل علينا وما أنزل على إبراهيم وإسماعيل وإسحاق ويعقوب والأسباط وما أوتي موسى وعيسى والنبيون من ربهم لا نفرق بين أحد منهم ونحن له مسلمون

translation: And whoever seeks a religion other than Islam, it will never be accepted from him, and in the Hereafter he will be one of the losers.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Islam is the only religion accepted by Allah. It warns that those who follow other religions or ideologies will ultimately face loss and disappointment in the afterlife, as their deeds and beliefs will not be accepted. The verse stresses the importance of sincerely submitting to Allah and following the teachings of Islam as the sole path to salvation and success in the eternal life to come. It serves as a reminder for Muslims to remain steadfast in their faith and for non-Muslims to embrace Islam before it is too late.
orig: ومن يبتغ غير الإسلام دينا فلن يقبل منه وهو في الآخرة من الخاسرين

translation: How shall Allah guide a people who disbelieved after their belief and had witnessed that the Messenger is true and clear proofs had come to them? And Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that those who reject faith after having believed and witnessed the truth of the Prophet's message are not deserving of God's guidance. It suggests that once a person has been exposed to clear proofs and signs of the truth, turning away from belief is a form of wrongdoing and injustice that merits being deprived of divine guidance. The implication is that God's guidance is a mercy that He bestows upon those who are sincere and receptive to the truth, not those who willfully reject it after recognizing it.
orig: كيف يهدي الله قوما كفروا بعد إيمانهم وشهدوا أن الرسول حق وجاءهم البينات والله لا يهدي القوم الظالمين

translation: Those - their recompense is that upon them is the curse of Allah and the angels and the people, all together,
interpretation: This verse speaks about the severe punishment that awaits those who reject faith and oppose the truth. The interpretation is that those who persistently deny the message of Islam and work against it will face the wrath and condemnation of Allah, His angels, and all of humanity on the Day of Judgment. This is the ultimate disgrace and humiliation, as they will be completely cut off from Allah's mercy and forever doomed, with no one to support or defend them. It emphasizes the gravity of disbelief and the importance of embracing faith and righteousness to avoid such a dreadful fate in the Hereafter.
orig: أولئك جزاؤهم أن عليهم لعنة الله والملائكة والناس أجمعين

translation: Abiding eternally therein. The punishment will not be lightened for them, nor will they be reprieved.
interpretation: This verse speaks about the fate of those who reject faith and do evil deeds. It emphasizes that they will abide in Hell forever, without any hope of the punishment being reduced or postponed. The use of the word "khālidīna" (abiding eternally) stresses the permanent nature of their suffering. The verse also highlights the severity and inevitability of divine justice, as the wrongdoers will not be given any respite or mercy once they are condemned to Hell. This serves as a strong warning for people to avoid evil and to embrace faith and righteousness in order to escape such a terrible fate in the Hereafter.
orig: خالدين فيها لا يخفف عنهم العذاب ولا هم ينظرون

translation: Except for those who repent after that and correct themselves. For indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of sincere repentance and making amends for one's wrongdoings. It highlights the merciful nature of Allah, reassuring believers that if they turn back to Him with genuine remorse and strive to rectify their mistakes, Allah will forgive them and shower His mercy upon them. This verse serves as a reminder that the door to repentance is always open, encouraging individuals to seek Allah's forgiveness and guidance, no matter how far they may have strayed from the righteous path. It also underscores the significance of not only seeking forgiveness but also actively working to improve oneself and make positive changes in one's life.
orig: إلا الذين تابوا من بعد ذلك وأصلحوا فإن الله غفور رحيم

translation: Indeed, those who have disbelieved after their belief and then increase in disbelief - never will their [claimed] repentance be accepted, and they are the ones astray.
interpretation: This verse speaks about those who once believed in Islam but later turned away from it and became disbelievers. It states that if such people continue to increase in their disbelief and rejection of faith, their repentance will not be accepted by Allah. They are considered to be truly astray and misguided because they had known the truth of Islam but still chose to abandon it for disbelief. The verse emphasizes the severity of apostasy in Islam and that those who persist in disbelief after having believed are far from Allah's mercy and guidance.
orig: إن الذين كفروا بعد إيمانهم ثم ازدادوا كفرا لن تقبل توبتهم وأولئك هم الضالون

translation: Indeed, those who disbelieve and die while they are disbelievers - never would the [whole] capacity of the earth in gold be accepted from one of them if he would [seek to] ransom himself with it. For those there will be a painful punishment, and they will have no helpers.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the severity and permanence of the consequences of disbelief. It states that even if a disbeliever were to offer an enormous amount of wealth, as much as the earth can contain of gold, it would not be accepted as a ransom to save them from the painful punishment in the Hereafter. This indicates that once a person dies in a state of disbelief, there is no way to escape the eternal consequences of their choice. The verse also highlights the fact that the disbelievers will have no helpers or supporters in the Hereafter, emphasizing their complete isolation and helplessness in the face of God's judgment.
orig: إن الذين كفروا وماتوا وهم كفار فلن يقبل من أحدهم ملء الأرض ذهبا ولو افتدى به أولئك لهم عذاب أليم وما لهم من ناصرين

translation: Never will you attain the good [reward] until you spend [in the way of Allah] from that which you love. And whatever you spend - indeed, Allah is Knowing of it.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of sacrificing what one loves for the sake of Allah. It suggests that true righteousness and piety can only be achieved when a person is willing to give up something dear to them in order to please Allah and seek His reward. The verse also reminds us that Allah is fully aware of whatever we spend in His cause, whether it is from our wealth, time, or effort. This encourages believers to be sincere and generous in their giving, knowing that their sacrifices are not in vain and that Allah will reward them accordingly in this life and the hereafter.
orig: لن تنالوا البر حتى تنفقوا مما تحبون وما تنفقوا من شيء فإن الله به عليم

translation: All food was lawful to the Children of Israel except what Israel had made unlawful to himself before the Torah was revealed. Say, [O Muhammad], "So bring the Torah and recite it, if you should be truthful."
interpretation: This verse addresses the Jews who claimed that certain foods were forbidden to them before the revelation of the Torah. It challenges them to bring forth the Torah and recite the relevant passages to support their claim. The verse implies that the prohibition of certain foods was not from Allah, but rather a personal choice made by Prophet Jacob (Israel) upon himself. It emphasizes the importance of referring to the divine scripture for guidance and not relying on personal preferences or traditions. The verse also serves as a reminder to the Jews that Muhammad is the true messenger of Allah, and they should accept his message if they are sincere in their faith.
orig: كل الطعام كان حلا لبني إسرائيل إلا ما حرم إسرائيل على نفسه من قبل أن تنزل التوراة قل فأتوا بالتوراة فاتلوها إن كنتم صادقين

translation: And whoever invents a lie about Allah after that - then those are [truly] the wrongdoers.
interpretation: This verse is a stern warning against those who attribute false statements or lies to Allah, especially after clear evidence has been presented to them. It emphasizes that such people are not just misguided but are actively engaging in wrongdoing and injustice. By fabricating lies about Allah, they are crossing a serious boundary and committing a grave sin. The verse implies that once the truth has been made clear through revelation and prophetic teachings, there is no excuse for inventing falsehoods about Allah or His message. Those who persist in doing so are condemned as "the wrongdoers" - a term that highlights the severity and sinfulness of their actions in the sight of Allah.
orig: فمن افترى على الله الكذب من بعد ذلك فأولئك هم الظالمون

translation: Say, "Allah has told the truth. So follow the religion of Abraham, inclining to truth. And he was not of the polytheists."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of following the true monotheistic religion of Abraham, which is Islam. It calls upon the believers to accept the truth revealed by Allah and to abandon all forms of polytheism and idolatry. The verse highlights that Abraham was a sincere monotheist who submitted himself completely to the will of Allah and did not associate any partners with Him. By following Abraham's example, Muslims can attain the true path of righteousness and avoid the misguidance of polytheism. The verse also serves as a reminder that the message of Islam is not a new invention but rather a continuation and restoration of the original monotheistic faith preached by all the prophets, including Abraham.
orig: قل صدق الله فاتبعوا ملة إبراهيم حنيفا وما كان من المشركين

translation: Indeed, the first House [of worship] established for mankind was that at Bakkah [i.e., Makkah] - blessed and a guidance for the worlds.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the significance and sanctity of the Ka'bah, the first house of worship built for humanity. It highlights that the Ka'bah, located in Makkah, is a source of blessings and guidance for all people, regardless of their nationality or background. The verse suggests that the Ka'bah serves as a symbol of unity and a focal point for worship, inviting people to recognize the oneness of Allah and to submit to His will. Moreover, it implies that the message of Islam, which is closely tied to the Ka'bah, is universal and applicable to all of mankind, providing them with spiritual guidance and direction.
orig: إن أول بيت وضع للناس للذي ببكة مباركا وهدى للعالمين

translation: In it are clear signs [such as] the standing place of Abraham. And whoever enters it shall be safe. And [due] to Allah from the people is a pilgrimage to the House - for whoever is able to find thereto a way. But whoever disbelieves - then indeed, Allah is free from need of the worlds.
interpretation: This verse highlights the sanctity and significance of the Ka'bah, the sacred House of Allah in Makkah. It mentions that there are clear signs and evidence within the Ka'bah, such as the standing place of Prophet Abraham, which testifies to its divine origin and importance. The verse also emphasizes the safety and security that Allah has granted to those who enter the sacred precincts of the Ka'bah. Furthermore, it underscores the obligation of pilgrimage (Hajj) to the House of Allah for those who have the means and ability to undertake this sacred journey. However, the verse also warns that those who reject faith and disbelieve in the importance of the Ka'bah and the pilgrimage, Allah is not in need of them or their worship, as He is self-sufficient and independent of all His creation.
orig: فيه آيات بينات مقام إبراهيم ومن دخله كان آمنا ولله على الناس حج البيت من استطاع إليه سبيلا ومن كفر فإن الله غني عن العالمين

translation: Say, "O People of the Scripture, why do you disbelieve in the verses of Allah while Allah is Witness over what you do?"
interpretation: This verse is addressing the People of the Scripture, which refers to the Jews and Christians, questioning their disbelief in the revelations and signs of Allah. It emphasizes that Allah is fully aware and witnesses their actions and deeds. The verse implies that their rejection of the truth is unjustifiable, as they have received clear proofs and evidences from Allah through their own scriptures. It serves as a reminder that they will be held accountable for their choices and that they cannot hide anything from the All-Knowing Creator.
orig: قل يا أهل الكتاب لم تكفرون بآيات الله والله شهيد على ما تعملون

translation: Say, "O People of the Scripture, why do you avert from the way of Allah those who believe, seeking to make it [seem] deviant, while you are witnesses [to the truth]? And Allah is not unaware of what you do."
interpretation: This verse is addressing the People of the Scripture, which refers to the Jews and Christians, who had received divine revelations before the advent of Islam. The verse questions their actions of trying to mislead the believers from the straight path of Allah, even though they themselves are witnesses to the truth of Islam. They are being warned that Allah is fully aware of their deeds and intentions, and that they cannot hide anything from Him. The verse highlights the importance of being truthful and sincere in one's faith, and not letting prejudice or personal interests come in the way of accepting the truth.
orig: قل يا أهل الكتاب لم تصدون عن سبيل الله من آمن تبغونها عوجا وأنتم شهداء وما الله بغافل عما تعملون

translation: O you who have believed, if you obey a party of those who were given the Scripture, they would turn you back, after your belief, [to being] unbelievers.
interpretation: This verse is a warning to the believers not to follow the teachings or the ways of the People of the Book (Jews and Christians) who may try to lead them astray from the path of Islam. It emphasizes that even after having faith, one can still be misguided by those who wish to create doubts and confusion. The Qur'an reminds the believers to stay steadfast in their faith and to rely on the guidance provided by Allah and His Messenger, rather than being swayed by the opinions or influences of others who do not share the same beliefs. It underscores the importance of guarding one's faith and being cautious of those who may try to undermine it, even if they are from the People of the Book.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا إن تطيعوا فريقا من الذين أوتوا الكتاب يردوكم بعد إيمانكم كافرين

translation: And how can you disbelieve while to you are being recited the verses of Allah and among you is His Messenger? And whoever holds firmly to Allah has [indeed] been guided to a straight path.
interpretation: This verse is questioning how one can reject faith when the clear signs and guidance of Allah are being conveyed to them directly through the recitation of the Qur'an, and while the Messenger of Allah is present among them as a living example of righteousness. It emphasizes that holding fast to Allah and His guidance is the sure path to being rightly guided in life. Rejecting faith in this circumstance would be an act of great ingratitude and heedlessness to the manifest signs and proofs that Allah has provided. The straight path mentioned alludes to the way of Islam - submission to the will of Allah, which leads to success and salvation.
orig: وكيف تكفرون وأنتم تتلى عليكم آيات الله وفيكم رسوله ومن يعتصم بالله فقد هدي إلى صراط مستقيم

translation: O you who have believed, fear Allah as He should be feared and do not die except as Muslims [in submission to Him].
interpretation: This verse is a powerful reminder to the believers to maintain a constant state of God-consciousness (taqwa) throughout their lives. It emphasizes the importance of fearing Allah in the most appropriate manner, which involves obeying His commands, refraining from His prohibitions, and striving to please Him in all aspects of life. The verse also stresses the significance of dying as a Muslim, in a state of complete submission to Allah. This implies that one should live their life in accordance with Islamic teachings and principles, so that when death approaches, they are in a state of obedience and submission to their Creator. The verse serves as a call to the believers to prioritize their relationship with Allah above all else and to strive for His pleasure until their last breath.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا اتقوا الله حق تقاته ولا تموتن إلا وأنتم مسلمون

translation: And hold firmly to the rope of Allah all together and do not become divided. And remember the favor of Allah upon you - when you were enemies and He brought your hearts together and you became, by His favor, brothers. And you were on the edge of a pit of the Fire, and He saved you from it. Thus does Allah make clear to you His verses that you may be guided.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of unity and brotherhood among believers. It reminds us of Allah's favor in bringing together the hearts of those who were once enemies, making them brothers in faith. The "rope of Allah" symbolizes the Qur'an and the teachings of Islam, which serve as a unifying force for the believers. Holding firmly to this rope and avoiding division is essential for the spiritual well-being and success of the Muslim community. The verse also highlights the fact that it is Allah who guides people to the right path and saves them from the dangers of disbelief and sin, just as He saved the believers from the edge of the pit of Fire. By reflecting on these clear signs and favors of Allah, believers are encouraged to stay united, grateful, and steadfast in their faith.
orig: واعتصموا بحبل الله جميعا ولا تفرقوا واذكروا نعمت الله عليكم إذ كنتم أعداء فألف بين قلوبكم فأصبحتم بنعمته إخوانا وكنتم على شفا حفرة من النار فأنقذكم منها كذلك يبين الله لكم آياته لعلكم تهتدون

translation: And let there be [arising] from you a nation inviting to [all that is] good, enjoining what is right and forbidding what is wrong, and those will be the successful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of having a group of people within the Muslim community who actively promote righteousness and discourage evil. It suggests that it is not enough for individuals to simply practice their faith privately, but that there must be a collective effort to establish and maintain a moral society. The verse implies that those who take on this responsibility of enjoining good and forbidding wrong will be the ones who ultimately attain success in both this world and the hereafter. It highlights the concept of "amr bil ma'ruf wa nahi anil munkar" (commanding what is right and forbidding what is wrong) as a fundamental duty of the Muslim community.
orig: ولتكن منكم أمة يدعون إلى الخير ويأمرون بالمعروف وينهون عن المنكر وأولئك هم المفلحون

translation: And do not be like those who became divided and differed after the clear proofs had come to them. And those will have a great punishment.
interpretation: This verse warns Muslims against falling into the same trap as earlier nations who, despite receiving clear guidance from Allah, allowed themselves to become divided by petty differences and sectarianism. Such behavior earns the severe punishment of Allah in the Hereafter. The verse emphasizes the critical importance of unity among the Muslim community and avoiding disputes, especially after the truth has been made evident through revelation. It is an exhortation to hold firmly to the Qur'an and prophetic teachings, and not let internal disagreements and divisions weaken the faith or divert Muslims from the straight path, as happened with some previous religious communities. Remaining united upon the truth is essential for the strength and success of the ummah.
orig: ولا تكونوا كالذين تفرقوا واختلفوا من بعد ما جاءهم البينات وأولئك لهم عذاب عظيم

translation: On the Day [some] faces will turn white and [some] faces will turn black. As for those whose faces turn black, [to them it will be said], "Did you disbelieve after your belief? Then taste the punishment for what you used to reject."
interpretation: This verse is referring to the Day of Judgment, when people will be divided into two groups based on their faith and deeds. Those whose faces turn white will be the believers who will be blessed with the mercy and pleasure of Allah. In contrast, those whose faces turn black will be the disbelievers who rejected the truth after having believed in it. They will be rebuked for their disbelief and will taste the severe punishment of Hell as a consequence of their actions. This verse serves as a powerful reminder of the importance of remaining steadfast in faith and the grave consequences of turning away from the truth after having acknowledged it.
orig: يوم تبيض وجوه وتسود وجوه فأما الذين اسودت وجوههم أكفرتم بعد إيمانكم فذوقوا العذاب بما كنتم تكفرون

translation: And as for those whose faces will turn white, they will be in the mercy of Allah. They will abide therein eternally.
interpretation: This verse speaks about the reward that awaits the righteous believers on the Day of Judgment. Those whose faces are radiant and shining with light on that day will be enveloped in Allah's infinite mercy and grace. They will enter Paradise, where they will remain forever, enjoying the countless blessings and delights that Allah has prepared for them. This eternal life in Paradise is a testament to Allah's immense love and generosity towards His faithful servants who strived to please Him in this worldly life. It is the ultimate goal and aspiration of every believer to be among those blessed with this great reward of everlasting peace, happiness, and closeness to their Lord.
orig: وأما الذين ابيضت وجوههم ففي رحمة الله هم فيها خالدون

translation: These are the verses of Allah which We recite to you, [O Muhammad], in truth. And Allah does not intend [any] injustice to the worlds.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the Qur'an is the truth from Allah, and it is being revealed to Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) without any alteration or distortion. The interpretation highlights that Allah, in His infinite wisdom and justice, does not intend to wrong or oppress any of His creation. Rather, the revelation of the Qur'an is a manifestation of His mercy and guidance for all of mankind, so that they may follow the right path and attain success in this world and the hereafter. The verse serves as a reminder that the Qur'an is a divine message, and its teachings should be followed and adhered to for the betterment of oneself and society as a whole.
orig: تلك آيات الله نتلوها عليك بالحق وما الله يريد ظلما للعالمين

translation: And to Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth. And to Allah will [all] matters be returned.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute sovereignty and ownership of Allah over all things in the universe. It reminds us that everything in existence belongs to Him alone, and that all affairs and matters will ultimately return to Him for judgment and final decision. This reinforces the concept of Allah's omnipotence and the idea that we should submit to His will and seek His pleasure in all our endeavors, knowing that we will be accountable to Him in the end.
orig: ولله ما في السماوات وما في الأرض وإلى الله ترجع الأمور

translation: You are the best nation produced [as an example] for mankind. You enjoin what is right and forbid what is wrong and believe in Allah. If only the People of the Scripture had believed, it would have been better for them. Among them are believers, but most of them are defiantly disobedient.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the Muslim community is the best nation because of their moral qualities - they encourage good, forbid evil, and have true faith in God. It suggests that if the People of the Book (Jews and Christians) had similar sincere belief, it would be very beneficial for them. The verse acknowledges that there are some true believers among them, but states that the majority are disobedient to God's commands. It highlights the importance of not just having faith, but putting it into practice by actively promoting virtue and opposing wrongdoing in society.
orig: كنتم خير أمة أخرجت للناس تأمرون بالمعروف وتنهون عن المنكر وتؤمنون بالله ولو آمن أهل الكتاب لكان خيرا لهم منهم المؤمنون وأكثرهم الفاسقون

translation: They will not harm you except for [some] annoyance. And if they fight you, they will show you their backs; then they will not be aided.
interpretation: This verse assures the believers that their enemies can do them no real harm, only some minor annoyance. If the disbelievers were to engage in battle against the Muslims, Allah promises that they would be defeated and would turn their backs in retreat. Moreover, the disbelievers would receive no help or support from anyone in their fight against the believers. This highlights the weakness and ultimate failure of those who oppose Islam and the Muslims, and emphasizes that the believers can rely on Allah's support and protection in the face of their enemies.
orig: لن يضروكم إلا أذى وإن يقاتلوكم يولوكم الأدبار ثم لا ينصرون

translation: Ignominy shall be their portion wheresoever they are found save (where they grasp) a rope from Allah and a rope from men. They have incurred anger from their Lord, and wretchedness is laid upon them. That is because they used to disbelieve the revelations of Allah, and slew the prophets wrongfully. That is because they were rebellious and used to transgress.
interpretation: This verse speaks about the punishment that befell the Children of Israel due to their repeated transgressions and disobedience to Allah's commands. They were subjected to humiliation and disgrace wherever they went, except when they held onto their covenant with Allah and their treaties with other people. They earned Allah's anger and were stricken with misery and poverty because of their disbelief in Allah's signs, wrongful killing of the prophets, and their persistent rebellion and transgression against the divine laws. This interpretation highlights the consequences of defying Allah and emphasizes the importance of faith, obedience, and upholding one's commitments to Allah and fellow human beings.
orig: ضربت عليهم الذلة أين ما ثقفوا إلا بحبل من الله وحبل من الناس وباءوا بغضب من الله وضربت عليهم المسكنة ذلك بأنهم كانوا يكفرون بآيات الله ويقتلون الأنبياء بغير حق ذلك بما عصوا وكانوا يعتدون

translation: They are not [all] the same; among the People of the Scripture is a community standing [in obedience], reciting the verses of Allah during periods of the night and prostrating [in prayer].
interpretation: This verse highlights that not all the People of the Book (Jews and Christians) are alike. Among them, there exists a righteous community that remains steadfast in their faith and devotion to Allah. They spend their nights reciting the verses of the Qur'an and engage in sincere worship, particularly through prostration in prayer. This interpretation emphasizes the importance of recognizing the diversity within religious communities and acknowledging the existence of pious individuals who adhere to the true essence of their faith, even among those who may have deviated from the right path.
orig: ليسوا سواء من أهل الكتاب أمة قائمة يتلون آيات الله آناء الليل وهم يسجدون

translation: They believe in Allah and the Last Day, and they enjoin what is right and forbid what is wrong and hasten to good deeds. And those are among the righteous.
interpretation: This verse highlights the qualities of the righteous believers. They have firm faith in Allah and the Day of Judgment, which motivates them to lead a virtuous life. They actively promote goodness and discourage evil in their communities, striving to establish a moral and just society.
