Moreover, they are always eager to perform good deeds and acts of kindness, seeking Allah's pleasure and reward. These characteristics distinguish them as being among the righteous, who are beloved to Allah and will be granted His mercy and blessings in this world and the hereafter.
orig: يؤمنون بالله واليوم الآخر ويأمرون بالمعروف وينهون عن المنكر ويسارعون في الخيرات وأولئك من الصالحين

translation: And whatever good they do - never will it be removed from them. And Allah is Knowing of the righteous.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah recognizes and rewards the good deeds of the righteous. It assures believers that their efforts in doing good will not go unnoticed or unrewarded by Allah. The verse highlights the importance of sincerity and consistency in performing righteous actions, as Allah is fully aware of those who are truly righteous and God-fearing. It serves as an encouragement for people to persist in doing good, knowing that their deeds will be acknowledged and recompensed by Allah, and that the reward for their righteousness will never be lost or taken away from them.
orig: وما يفعلوا من خير فلن يكفروه والله عليم بالمتقين

translation: Indeed, those who disbelieve - never will their wealth or their children avail them against Allah at all, and those are the companions of the Fire; they will abide therein eternally.
interpretation: This verse warns that for those who reject faith in God, their worldly possessions and offspring will be of no benefit to them in the Hereafter when they face God's judgment. Wealth and children, which are often a source of pride and attachment in this life, will have no power to protect them from God's punishment. Their eternal fate will be the Fire of Hell, where they will remain forever as a consequence of their disbelief. It highlights the severity of denying God, showing that nothing in this temporary world can save a person if they turn away from their Creator.
orig: إن الذين كفروا لن تغني عنهم أموالهم ولا أولادهم من الله شيئا وأولئك أصحاب النار هم فيها خالدون

translation: The example of what they spend in this worldly life is like that of a wind containing frost which strikes the harvest of a people who have wronged themselves and destroys it. And Allah has not wronged them, but they wrong themselves.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the fleeting and ultimately destructive nature of worldly pursuits and spending when done without regard for Allah's guidance. It compares such actions to a frigid wind that decimates a people's harvest, ruining what they have worked for. The people have brought this loss upon themselves through their own misdeeds and disregard for Allah's commands. Allah is not unjust to them, but they are unjust to themselves by focusing on temporary worldly gains rather than seeking Allah's pleasure and reward in the Hereafter. The verse serves as a warning to prioritize one's relationship with Allah and adhere to His guidance to avoid spiritual loss and destruction.
orig: مثل ما ينفقون في هذه الحياة الدنيا كمثل ريح فيها صر أصابت حرث قوم ظلموا أنفسهم فأهلكته وما ظلمهم الله ولكن أنفسهم يظلمون

translation: O you who have believed, do not take as intimates those other than yourselves, for they will not spare you [any] ruin. They wish you would have hardship. Hatred has already appeared from their mouths, and what their breasts conceal is greater. We have certainly made clear to you the signs, if you will use reason.
interpretation: This verse warns the believers against taking non-believers as close friends or confidants. It suggests that such people, despite their outward show of friendship, actually harbor hatred and ill-will towards the believers and would like to see them suffer. Their true feelings may be concealed, but are ultimately known to Allah. The verse urges the believers to use their reason and not be deceived by false displays of friendship from those who do not share their faith. It implies that the believers should be cautious and discerning in their social relationships, and should prioritize their bonds with fellow believers.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا لا تتخذوا بطانة من دونكم لا يألونكم خبالا ودوا ما عنتم قد بدت البغضاء من أفواههم وما تخفي صدورهم أكبر قد بينا لكم الآيات إن كنتم تعقلون

translation: Lo! You are the ones who love them, but they love you not, and you believe in all the Scripture. When they meet you, they say, "We believe". But when they are alone, they bite their fingertips at you in rage. Say, "Perish in your rage. Indeed, Allah is Knowing of that within the breasts."
interpretation: This verse highlights the hypocrisy and insincerity of those who pretend to be friends with the believers while harboring hatred and enmity towards them in their hearts. Despite the believers showing them love and accepting the entire scripture, these hypocrites display false amity when they meet the believers but secretly curse them and wish for their destruction. Allah exposes their true feelings and intentions, commanding the Prophet to tell them to die in their rage, for Allah is fully aware of what lies within their hearts and will hold them accountable for their malice and deception.
orig: ها أنتم أولاء تحبونهم ولا يحبونكم وتؤمنون بالكتاب كله وإذا لقوكم قالوا آمنا وإذا خلوا عضوا عليكم الأنامل من الغيظ قل موتوا بغيظكم إن الله عليم بذات الصدور

translation: If good touches you, it distresses them; but if harm strikes you, they rejoice at it. And if you are patient and fear Allah, their plot will not harm you at all. Indeed, Allah is encompassing of what they do.
interpretation: This verse highlights the attitude of the enemies of Islam towards the believers. They are distressed when something good happens to the believers, and they rejoice when the believers face hardships or difficulties. However, the verse also provides a solution for the believers: to remain patient and have consciousness of Allah (taqwa). By doing so, the plots and schemes of the enemies will not be able to harm the believers in any way. The verse concludes with a reminder that Allah is fully aware of everything that the enemies do, and He will hold them accountable for their actions. This interpretation emphasizes the importance of patience, faith, and reliance on Allah in the face of adversity and opposition.
orig: إن تمسسكم حسنة تسؤهم وإن تصبكم سيئة يفرحوا بها وإن تصبروا وتتقوا لا يضركم كيدهم شيئا إن الله بما يعملون محيط

translation: And [remember] when you, [O Muhammad], left your family in the morning to post the believers at their stations for the battle [of Uhud] - and Allah is Hearing and Knowing -
interpretation: This verse is addressing Prophet Muhammad, reminding him of the time when he left his family in the morning to assign the believers their positions for the battle of Uhud. It emphasizes that Allah is All-Hearing and All-Knowing, which means that He is aware of everything that happens, including the strategies and intentions of the believers and their enemies. The verse implies that the believers should trust in Allah's plan and have faith that He will guide them to victory, even in the face of adversity. It also serves as a reminder that Allah is always watching over His servants and that they should strive to please Him in all their actions, including during times of war.
orig: وإذ غدوت من أهلك تبوئ المؤمنين مقاعد للقتال والله سميع عليم

translation: When two parties among you were about to lose courage, but Allah was their ally; and upon Allah the believers should rely.
interpretation: This verse is referring to the Battle of Uhud, where some of the Muslims were close to losing heart and fleeing the battlefield. However, Allah supported them and gave them courage. The key message is that believers should always put their trust in Allah, even in the most difficult of circumstances. When faced with hardship or challenges, Muslims should not despair or lose faith, but rather should turn to Allah and rely on His support and guidance. This unwavering trust in Allah is a fundamental aspect of faith and a source of strength for believers.
orig: إذ همت طائفتان منكم أن تفشلا والله وليهما وعلى الله فليتوكل المؤمنون

translation: And already had Allah given you victory at [the battle of] Badr while you were few in number. Then fear Allah; perhaps you will be grateful.
interpretation: This verse reminds the believers of Allah's favor upon them when He granted them victory at the Battle of Badr, despite their small numbers and weakness compared to the enemy. It encourages them to be mindful of Allah and to fear Him, so that they may be grateful for His blessings and continue to receive His support and guidance. The verse emphasizes the importance of taqwa (God-consciousness) and gratitude as key factors in attaining success and divine assistance, both in times of hardship and ease. It also highlights the fact that victory comes from Allah alone, and not from one's own strength or numbers, which should instill humility and reliance on Him.
orig: ولقد نصركم الله ببدر وأنتم أذلة فاتقوا الله لعلكم تشكرون

translation: When you said to the believers, "Is it not sufficient for you that your Lord should reinforce you with three thousand angels sent down?"
interpretation: This verse is a reminder to the believers that Allah's support and help is always sufficient for them, no matter how difficult the circumstances may seem. It highlights the fact that Allah can send down His angels to assist the believers in times of need, which should serve as a source of comfort and strength for them. The verse also emphasizes the importance of having faith and trust in Allah's plan and His ability to provide support and guidance, even in the most challenging of situations. It encourages the believers to rely on Allah and to have confidence in His power and wisdom, knowing that He is always there to help and support them.
orig: إذ تقول للمؤمنين ألن يكفيكم أن يمدكم ربكم بثلاثة آلاف من الملائكة منزلين

translation: Yes, if you remain patient and conscious of Allah and the enemy come upon you [attacking] in rage, your Lord will reinforce you with five thousand angels having marks [of distinction]
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of patience and God-consciousness (taqwa) in the face of adversity. It promises that if the believers remain steadfast and mindful of Allah, even when the enemy attacks them in a state of rage, Allah will support them by sending down five thousand angels bearing distinctive marks. This divine assistance is a reward for their perseverance and faith, showing that Allah is always with those who are patient and righteous. The verse encourages believers to trust in Allah's help and remain committed to their faith, even in the most challenging circumstances.
orig: بلى إن تصبروا وتتقوا ويأتوكم من فورهم هذا يمددكم ربكم بخمسة آلاف من الملائكة مسومين

translation: And Allah made it not except as [a sign of] good tidings for you and to reassure your hearts thereby. And victory is not except from Allah, the Exalted in Might, the Wise.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that all victory and success ultimately come from Allah alone. Whatever means or forces are employed, they are merely instruments in His hands. The believers should take comfort in this and not place their trust or reliance in worldly means of success. They should have faith that Allah will grant them victory in accordance with His wisdom and at the appropriate time, as long as they sincerely strive in His cause. Knowing that Allah is the source of victory should boost the believers' morale and determination.
orig: وما جعله الله إلا بشرى لكم ولتطمئن قلوبكم به وما النصر إلا من عند الله العزيز الحكيم

translation: That He may cut off a part of those who disbelieved or suppress them so that they turn back disappointed.
interpretation: This verse refers to the ultimate fate of the disbelievers who oppose Allah and His messenger. It suggests that Allah will either destroy a portion of them or crush their power and strength, causing them to retreat in despair and frustration. The verse implies that the disbelievers' efforts against Islam will be futile and that they will face a humiliating defeat and disappointment in the end. It emphasizes Allah's power over His enemies and serves as a warning to those who reject faith and fight against the truth.
orig: ليقطع طرفا من الذين كفروا أو يكبتهم فينقلبوا خائبين

translation: Not for you, [O Muhammad, but for Allah], is the decision whether He should [cut them down] or forgive them or punish them, for indeed, they are wrongdoers.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the ultimate judgment and decision regarding the fate of the wrongdoers lies with Allah alone. It is not the responsibility or the right of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) to decide whether these individuals should be forgiven or punished. The verse highlights the sovereignty of Allah in matters of judgment and the importance of leaving the final decision to Him. It also serves as a reminder that even though people may commit wrongs and injustices, it is Allah who will determine their ultimate consequences based on His infinite wisdom and justice.
orig: ليس لك من الأمر شيء أو يتوب عليهم أو يعذبهم فإنهم ظالمون

translation: And to Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth. He forgives whom He wills, and punishes whom He wills. And Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's absolute sovereignty and authority over the entire universe. It affirms that Allah alone has the power to forgive sins or punish individuals according to His divine wisdom and justice. The mention of Allah's attributes of forgiveness and mercy at the end of the verse underscores the fact that while Allah may punish some, His mercy encompasses all things and He is ever ready to forgive those who sincerely repent and seek His forgiveness. This verse serves as a reminder for believers to constantly strive for Allah's pleasure, as their ultimate fate rests in His hands.
orig: ولله ما في السماوات وما في الأرض يغفر لمن يشاء ويعذب من يشاء والله غفور رحيم

translation: O you who have believed, do not consume usury, doubled and multiplied, but fear Allah that you may be successful.
interpretation: This verse is a clear prohibition of usury or interest (riba) in financial transactions. It emphasizes that engaging in such practices, where the amount of interest compounds and multiplies over time, is a grave sin. Instead, the verse encourages believers to be mindful of Allah and to conduct their financial dealings in a manner that is pleasing to Him. The implication is that by refraining from usury and adopting a God-conscious approach in economic activities, one can attain true success and prosperity, both in this world and in the Hereafter. The verse underscores the importance of fairness, justice, and compassion in financial dealings, as opposed to exploitative practices that can lead to oppression and social inequality.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا لا تأكلوا الربا أضعافا مضاعفة واتقوا الله لعلكم تفلحون

translation: And fear the Fire, which has been prepared for the disbelievers.
interpretation: This verse serves as a stern warning to those who reject faith in Allah and His message. It emphasizes the severe consequence of disbelief: the eternal punishment of the Fire (Hell). The verse aims to instill a sense of taqwa (God-consciousness and fear of His punishment) in the hearts of the believers, urging them to stay on the right path and avoid actions that could lead them to the same fate as the disbelievers. It also highlights the justice of Allah, as He has prepared the Fire specifically for those who choose to deny Him and His guidance, despite the clear signs and warnings sent through His messengers.
orig: واتقوا النار التي أعدت للكافرين

translation: And obey Allah and the Messenger so that you may receive mercy.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of obedience to Allah and His Messenger, Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him), as a means of attaining Allah's mercy and compassion. It suggests that by following the commandments of Allah and the teachings of the Prophet, believers can hope to receive Allah's blessings, forgiveness, and ultimately, His mercy in this world and the hereafter. The verse also implies that disobedience to Allah and His Messenger may lead to being deprived of Allah's mercy and facing the consequences of one's actions.
orig: وأطيعوا الله والرسول لعلكم ترحمون

translation: And hasten to forgiveness from your Lord and a garden as wide as the heavens and earth, prepared for the righteous.
interpretation: This verse encourages believers to race towards seeking Allah's forgiveness and striving to enter Paradise, which is described as being as vast as the heavens and the earth. This metaphor emphasizes the immense size and beauty of Paradise. The verse also states that this reward is prepared specifically for the righteous, those who are mindful of Allah and follow His guidance. It motivates individuals to prioritize their spiritual growth and good deeds, as they lead to the ultimate goal of attaining forgiveness and entering Paradise in the Hereafter.
orig: وسارعوا إلى مغفرة من ربكم وجنة عرضها السماوات والأرض أعدت للمتقين

translation: Those who spend [in the cause of Allah] during ease and hardship and who restrain anger and who pardon the people - and Allah loves the doers of good;
interpretation: This verse highlights the virtuous qualities of true believers. They are those who spend in charity for the sake of Allah, both in times of prosperity and adversity. This demonstrates their sincerity and consistency in faith. Moreover, they exercise self-control when faced with anger, choosing to restrain their rage rather than lashing out. They also forgive others who have wronged them, showing mercy and compassion. These actions of generosity, patience, and forgiveness are beloved by Allah, as they reflect the highest standards of moral conduct and righteousness. The verse emphasizes that such individuals who embody these noble traits are the ones whom Allah loves and is pleased with, due to their excellence in character and devotion to goodness.
orig: الذين ينفقون في السراء والضراء والكاظمين الغيظ والعافين عن الناس والله يحب المحسنين

translation: And those who, when they commit an immorality or wrong themselves [by transgression], remember Allah and seek forgiveness for their sins - and who can forgive sins except Allah? - and [who] do not persist in what they have done while they know.
interpretation: This verse highlights the qualities of the righteous believers. When they commit a sin or wrong themselves, they immediately remember Allah and seek His forgiveness. They acknowledge that only Allah can forgive sins, and they do not persist in their wrongdoings knowingly. This demonstrates their consciousness of Allah, their humility in recognizing their mistakes, and their sincere repentance. The verse emphasizes the importance of seeking Allah's forgiveness and not continuing in sinful behavior once a person becomes aware of it. It encourages believers to turn back to Allah, seek His mercy, and strive to rectify their actions.
orig: والذين إذا فعلوا فاحشة أو ظلموا أنفسهم ذكروا الله فاستغفروا لذنوبهم ومن يغفر الذنوب إلا الله ولم يصروا على ما فعلوا وهم يعلمون

translation: Those - their reward is forgiveness from their Lord and gardens beneath which rivers flow [in Paradise], wherein they will abide eternally; and excellent is the reward of the [righteous] workers.
interpretation: This verse highlights the immense rewards that await the righteous believers in the Hereafter. It emphasizes that those who sincerely believe in Allah and perform good deeds will be granted forgiveness for their sins and will be admitted into Paradise, where they will enjoy eternal bliss in gardens with flowing rivers. The verse also underscores the excellence of this reward, which is the ultimate goal and aspiration of every righteous person who strives to please Allah through their actions and devotion. It serves as a powerful motivation for believers to persist in their faith and good works, knowing that their efforts will be richly rewarded in the afterlife.
orig: أولئك جزاؤهم مغفرة من ربهم وجنات تجري من تحتها الأنهار خالدين فيها ونعم أجر العاملين

translation: Similar situations have passed before you, so travel through the earth and observe how was the end of those who denied.
interpretation: This verse is a reminder and a warning to mankind. It encourages people to study history and learn from the fate of past nations who rejected the truth and the messages of their prophets. The verse implies that the consequences of denying the truth are severe and destructive, as evidenced by the ruins and remains of those past civilizations. It is an invitation to reflect on the universal laws and patterns that govern the rise and fall of nations, and to realize that the ultimate fate of those who persist in falsehood and corruption is one of loss and regret. The verse urges people to open their eyes, minds and hearts to the signs of Allah in the world around them, and to heed the lessons of history in order to make wise choices and avoid the pitfalls of those who came before them.
orig: قد خلت من قبلكم سنن فسيروا في الأرض فانظروا كيف كان عاقبة المكذبين

translation: This [Qur'an] is a clear statement to [all] the people and a guidance and instruction for those conscious of Allah.
interpretation: The Qur'an serves as a clear message and declaration to all of humanity. It provides guidance to the straight path and serves as a reminder and admonition to those who are mindful of Allah and seek to live righteously. The Qur'an is not just a book, but a living guide that instructs people on how to conduct themselves morally and ethically in order to attain success in this life and the Hereafter. Those who heed its teachings and sincerely apply them will find illumination for their souls and clarity in their lives.
orig: هذا بيان للناس وهدى وموعظة للمتقين

translation: Do not weaken and do not grieve, and you will be superior if you are [true] believers.
interpretation: This verse is a reminder to the believers to stay strong and steadfast in the face of adversity. It encourages them not to lose heart or feel saddened, as they have the support and guidance of Allah. The verse emphasizes that true believers will ultimately prevail and be successful, both in this world and in the hereafter, as long as they maintain their faith and trust in Allah. It is a message of hope and reassurance, urging the believers to persevere through hardships and challenges, knowing that their unwavering belief will lead them to victory and spiritual elevation.
orig: ولا تهنوا ولا تحزنوا وأنتم الأعلون إن كنتم مؤمنين

translation: If a wound has touched you, be sure a similar wound has touched the others. And so are the days (good and not so good), We give to men by turns, that Allah may test those who believe, and that He may take martyrs from among you. And Allah likes not the Zalimun (polytheists and wrongdoers).
interpretation: This verse is reminding the believers that they should not be disheartened by the setbacks or losses they face in the path of Allah, as the enemy also faces similar losses. It emphasizes that both victory and defeat are in the hands of Allah, and He alternates them among people as a test of their faith and steadfastness. Through these trials, Allah distinguishes the true believers and chooses martyrs from among them. The verse also underscores Allah's dislike for the wrongdoers and oppressors who reject faith and spread corruption.
orig: إن يمسسكم قرح فقد مس القوم قرح مثله وتلك الأيام نداولها بين الناس وليعلم الله الذين آمنوا ويتخذ منكم شهداء والله لا يحب الظالمين

translation: And that Allah may purify the believers [through trials] and destroy the disbelievers.
interpretation: This verse suggests that Allah tests the faith of believers through various trials and challenges, which serve to purify and strengthen their belief. On the other hand, these same trials expose the disbelievers and ultimately lead to their destruction. It highlights the idea that hardships and difficulties are a means for Allah to distinguish the true believers from those who reject faith, and that the ultimate fate of the disbelievers is destruction, while the believers emerge stronger in their faith.
orig: وليمحص الله الذين آمنوا ويمحق الكافرين

translation: Or do you think that you will enter Paradise while Allah has not yet made evident those of you who fight in His cause and made evident those who are steadfast?
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that entering Paradise is not a matter of mere belief or wishful thinking. Allah tests the believers to distinguish those who strive in His cause with sincerity and patience from those who are not willing to sacrifice for His sake. The path to Paradise involves trials, hardships and perseverance. Only those who prove their faith through their actions, by patiently enduring difficulties and remaining steadfast in obeying Allah and struggling in His way, will be granted the reward of Paradise. This verse encourages believers to actively live out their faith and be ready to face challenges with determination and fortitude.
orig: أم حسبتم أن تدخلوا الجنة ولما يعلم الله الذين جاهدوا منكم ويعلم الصابرين

translation: And you had certainly wished for death [i.e., martyrdom] before you encountered it, and [now] you have [indeed] seen it [before you] while you were looking on.
interpretation: This verse is addressing the believers who had previously expressed their desire for martyrdom in the cause of Allah. It reminds them that they had wished for this great honor before actually facing the reality of battle. The verse then states that they have indeed witnessed the opportunity for martyrdom that they had longed for, emphasizing the importance of remaining steadfast and true to their convictions when confronted with the challenges and hardships of upholding their faith. It encourages the believers to embrace the path they had chosen and to face the difficulties that come with it, having already made the commitment in their hearts to sacrifice for the sake of Allah.
orig: ولقد كنتم تمنون الموت من قبل أن تلقوه فقد رأيتموه وأنتم تنظرون

translation: Muhammad is no more than a messenger, and indeed (many) messengers have passed away before him. If he dies or is killed, will you then turn back on your heels (as disbelievers)? And he who turns back on his heels, not the least harm will he do to Allah, and Allah will give reward to those who are grateful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Prophet Muhammad, despite his exalted status, is still a mortal messenger like those before him. It serves as a reminder to the believers that their faith should not be contingent upon the Prophet's life, as even in the event of his death, Allah's message endures. The verse also warns against apostasy and highlights the importance of remaining steadfast in faith, as turning away from Islam after the Prophet's passing would not harm Allah in the least. Instead, Allah promises to reward those who are grateful and unwavering in their belief, emphasizing the significance of resilience and faith in the face of adversity.
orig: وما محمد إلا رسول قد خلت من قبله الرسل أفإن مات أو قتل انقلبتم على أعقابكم ومن ينقلب على عقبيه فلن يضر الله شيئا وسيجزي الله الشاكرين

translation: And it is not [possible] for one to die except by permission of Allah at a decree determined. And whoever desires the reward of this world - We will give him thereof; and whoever desires the reward of the Hereafter - We will give him thereof. And we will reward the grateful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that death only occurs by the will and decree of Allah, at a predetermined time. It also highlights the contrast between those who seek worldly gains and those who strive for the rewards of the Hereafter. Allah promises to grant both groups what they desire, but the implication is that seeking the eternal rewards of the Hereafter is more virtuous. The verse concludes by affirming that Allah will reward those who are grateful to Him, suggesting that gratitude and seeking the Hereafter are closely linked. This encourages believers to focus on their ultimate spiritual goal and to be grateful for Allah's blessings and decree in this life.
orig: وما كان لنفس أن تموت إلا بإذن الله كتابا مؤجلا ومن يرد ثواب الدنيا نؤته منها ومن يرد ثواب الآخرة نؤته منها وسنجزي الشاكرين

translation: And how many a prophet [fought and] with him fought many religious scholars. But they never lost assurance due to what afflicted them in the cause of Allah, nor did they weaken or submit. And Allah loves the steadfast.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of perseverance and steadfastness in the face of adversity, especially when fighting for the cause of Allah. It highlights the example of the prophets and their devoted followers who remained firm in their faith despite the hardships and challenges they faced. They did not lose heart, weaken in their resolve, or submit to their enemies. The verse concludes by affirming that Allah loves those who exhibit patience and remain steadfast, indicating that such qualities are highly valued and rewarded by Him. It serves as an encouragement to believers to emulate the unwavering commitment and resilience of the prophets and their companions in their own struggles and trials.
orig: وكأين من نبي قاتل معه ربيون كثير فما وهنوا لما أصابهم في سبيل الله وما ضعفوا وما استكانوا والله يحب الصابرين

translation: And their words were not but that they said, "Our Lord, forgive us our sins and the excess [committed] in our affairs and plant firmly our feet and give us victory over the disbelieving people."
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of seeking forgiveness from Allah and acknowledging one's shortcomings and mistakes. It emphasizes the need for humility and reliance on Allah's mercy and guidance. The believers are asking Allah to forgive their sins, keep them steadfast on the right path, and grant them victory over those who reject faith. This demonstrates that success and triumph come from Allah alone, and that the believers should constantly turn to Him in repentance and supplication.
orig: وما كان قولهم إلا أن قالوا ربنا اغفر لنا ذنوبنا وإسرافنا في أمرنا وثبت أقدامنا وانصرنا على القوم الكافرين

translation: So Allah gave them the reward of this world and the good reward of the Hereafter. And Allah loves the doers of good.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah rewards those who do good deeds and live righteously in both this world and the Hereafter. It suggests that the ultimate reward for one's good actions lies with Allah in the afterlife, but that Allah may also grant blessings and success in this worldly life to those who strive to do good. The verse also highlights one of Allah's attributes - His love for those who excel in doing good, which serves as an encouragement for believers to constantly engage in virtuous deeds and seek Allah's pleasure.
orig: فآتاهم الله ثواب الدنيا وحسن ثواب الآخرة والله يحب المحسنين

translation: O you who have believed, if you obey those who disbelieve, they will turn you back on your heels, and you will [then] become losers.
interpretation: This verse serves as a warning to the believers that if they were to obey and follow the disbelievers, it would lead them astray from the right path. They would be turned back from Islam and revert to their old ways of ignorance and disbelief, resulting in a state of spiritual loss and failure. The verse emphasizes the importance of staying firm in one's faith, resisting the influence of those who reject the truth, and not compromising one's beliefs for the sake of pleasing others or giving in to external pressures. Ultimately, the path of obedience to Allah is the only way to attain success and salvation, while following the disbelievers leads to loss and regret in this life and the hereafter.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا إن تطيعوا الذين كفروا يردوكم على أعقابكم فتنقلبوا خاسرين

translation: But Allah is your protector, and He is the best of helpers.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah is the ultimate protector and supporter of the believers. It reminds us that no matter what challenges or difficulties we face in life, we can always turn to Allah for help and guidance. He is the one who will never abandon us and will always be there to support us. The verse also implies that seeking help from anyone or anything other than Allah is futile, as He is the only one who can truly assist us in our times of need. It encourages us to put our trust in Allah and rely on Him alone, knowing that He is the best of all helpers.
orig: بل الله مولاكم وهو خير الناصرين

translation: We will cast terror into the hearts of those who disbelieve for what they have associated with Allah of which He had not sent down [any] authority. And their refuge will be the Fire, and wretched is the residence of the wrongdoers.
interpretation: This verse is a warning to those who associate partners with Allah and reject His message. Allah will instill fear and terror in their hearts as a consequence of their disbelief and polytheistic practices, for which they have no divine authority or justification. Their ultimate abode will be the Hellfire, which is the worst possible destination for those who wrong themselves by rejecting the truth and engaging in idolatry. This verse emphasizes the severity of the punishment that awaits those who persist in their disbelief and the importance of submitting to Allah alone, without attributing partners to Him.
orig: سنلقي في قلوب الذين كفروا الرعب بما أشركوا بالله ما لم ينزل به سلطانا ومأواهم النار وبئس مثوى الظالمين

translation: And Allah had certainly fulfilled His promise to you when you were killing the enemy by His permission until [the time] when you lost courage and fell to disputing about the order [given by the Prophet] and disobeyed after He had shown you that which you love. Among you are some who desire this world, and among you are some who desire the Hereafter. Then he turned you back from them [defeated] that He might test you. And He has already forgiven you, and Allah is the possessor of bounty for the believers.
interpretation: This verse is a reminder that victory and defeat are in the hands of Allah. Even when the Muslims were on the verge of victory, their own shortcomings, such as disagreements, disobedience, and worldly desires, led to their defeat. However, this defeat served as a test and a lesson for the believers. Despite their mistakes, Allah forgave them, emphasizing His grace and favor upon the believers. This highlights the importance of unity, obedience to the Prophet, and focusing on the Hereafter rather than worldly gains. It also underscores the mercy and forgiveness of Allah towards His believing servants, even when they falter or make mistakes.
orig: ولقد صدقكم الله وعده إذ تحسونهم بإذنه حتى إذا فشلتم وتنازعتم في الأمر وعصيتم من بعد ما أراكم ما تحبون منكم من يريد الدنيا ومنكم من يريد الآخرة ثم صرفكم عنهم ليبتليكم ولقد عفا عنكم والله ذو فضل على المؤمنين

translation: When you were climbing [the mountain] and did not look aside at anyone while the Messenger was calling you from behind. So Allah repaid you with distress upon distress that you might not grieve for that which had escaped you [of victory and spoils of war] or [for] that which had befallen you [of injury and death]. And Allah is [fully] Aware of what you do.
interpretation: This verse refers to the Battle of Uhud, where some Muslims disobeyed the Prophet's orders and left their positions to pursue the fleeing enemy, hoping to collect spoils of war. As a result, the tide of the battle turned against the Muslims, causing them distress and grief. The verse emphasizes that this distress was a consequence of their actions and a lesson from Allah, reminding them not to be overly concerned with worldly gains or losses, but to focus on obeying Allah and His Messenger. It also highlights Allah's awareness of all human actions and their consequences.
orig: إذ تصعدون ولا تلوون على أحد والرسول يدعوكم في أخراكم فأثابكم غما بغم لكيلا تحزنوا على ما فاتكم ولا ما أصابكم والله خبير بما تعملون

translation: Then after distress, He sent down upon you security [in the form of] drowsiness, overcoming a faction of you, while another faction worried about themselves, thinking of Allah other than the truth - the thought of ignorance, saying, "Is there anything for us [to have done] in this matter?" Say, "Indeed, the matter belongs completely to Allah." They conceal within themselves what they will not reveal to you. They say, "If there was anything we could have done in the matter, some of us would not have been killed right here." Say, "Even if you had been inside your houses, those decreed to be killed would have come out to their death beds." [It was] so that Allah might test what is in your breasts and purify what is in your hearts. And Allah is Knowing of that within the breasts.
interpretation: This verse highlights the different reactions of the believers during a time of distress and hardship. Some found peace and security in their faith, while others were overcome with worry and doubt. The verse emphasizes that everything happens by Allah's decree, and even if the believers had tried to avoid the calamity, those destined to die would have met their fate regardless. The purpose behind such trials is for Allah to test the sincerity of faith in the hearts of the believers and to purify them. It underscores Allah's omniscience and that He is fully aware of the innermost thoughts and feelings hidden in the hearts of people.
orig: ثم أنزل عليكم من بعد الغم أمنة نعاسا يغشى طائفة منكم وطائفة قد أهمتهم أنفسهم يظنون بالله غير الحق ظن الجاهلية يقولون هل لنا من الأمر من شيء قل إن الأمر كله لله يخفون في أنفسهم ما لا يبدون لك يقولون لو كان لنا من الأمر شيء ما قتلنا هاهنا قل لو كنتم في بيوتكم لبرز الذين كتب عليهم القتل إلى مضاجعهم وليبتلي الله ما في صدوركم وليمحص ما في قلوبكم والله عليم بذات الصدور

translation: Indeed, those of you who turned back on the day the two armies met, it was Satan who caused them to slip because of some [blame] they had earned. But Allah has already forgiven them. Indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Forbearing.
interpretation: This verse is addressing those Muslims who fled from the battlefield of Uhud due to the influence of Satan, who took advantage of some of their past misdeeds. However, the verse emphasizes that Allah has forgiven them for this mistake, highlighting His attributes of forgiveness and forbearance. The interpretation is that even if believers falter or make mistakes due to the temptations of Satan, sincere repentance and seeking Allah's forgiveness can lead to their sins being pardoned by the All-Forgiving and All-Merciful Allah. It serves as a reminder of Allah's infinite mercy and encourages believers to always turn back to Him in repentance.
orig: إن الذين تولوا منكم يوم التقى الجمعان إنما استزلهم الشيطان ببعض ما كسبوا ولقد عفا الله عنهم إن الله غفور حليم

translation: O you who have believed, do not be like those who disbelieved and said about their brothers when they traveled through the land or went out to fight, "If they had been with us, they would not have died or have been killed," so Allah makes that [misconception] a regret within their hearts. And it is Allah who gives life and causes death, and Allah is Seeing of what you do.
interpretation: This verse is a reminder to the believers not to think or behave like the disbelievers who, when their fellow disbelievers died or were killed in battle, would say that if they had stayed behind, they would have remained alive. Allah points out that this thinking is a misconception and a source of regret for them. It emphasizes that life and death are in the hands of Allah alone, and He is fully aware of all our actions and intentions. The verse encourages believers to have faith in Allah's decree and to strive in His cause without fear of death, knowing that their ultimate fate lies with Him.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا لا تكونوا كالذين كفروا وقالوا لإخوانهم إذا ضربوا في الأرض أو كانوا غزى لو كانوا عندنا ما ماتوا وما قتلوا ليجعل الله ذلك حسرة في قلوبهم والله يحيي ويميت والله بما تعملون بصير

translation: And if you are killed in the cause of Allah or die - then forgiveness from Allah and mercy are better than whatever they accumulate [in this world].
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the ultimate reward for those who sacrifice their lives or die in the path of Allah is far greater than any worldly possessions or achievements. It highlights the importance of seeking Allah's forgiveness and mercy, which are infinitely more valuable than the temporary and fleeting gains of this world. The verse encourages believers to prioritize their spiritual goals and to be willing to make sacrifices for the sake of Allah, with the assurance that their reward in the Hereafter will be far superior to anything they might accumulate in this life.
orig: ولئن قتلتم في سبيل الله أو متم لمغفرة من الله ورحمة خير مما يجمعون

translation: And whether you die or are killed, verily, unto Allah you shall be gathered.
interpretation: This verse reminds us that death is inevitable, whether it comes naturally or through being killed, and that our ultimate destination is to return to Allah. It emphasizes the belief in the afterlife and the Day of Judgment, where all individuals will be held accountable for their deeds in this world. The verse encourages believers to live their lives with the consciousness that they will eventually face Allah and that their actions in this world will have consequences in the hereafter. It also offers comfort to those who may face persecution or death for their beliefs, reminding them that their ultimate reward lies with Allah in the afterlife.
orig: ولئن متم أو قتلتم لإلى الله تحشرون

translation: So by mercy from Allah, [O Muhammad], you were lenient with them. And if you had been rude [in speech] and harsh in heart, they would have disbanded from about you. So pardon them and ask forgiveness for them and consult them in the matter. And when you have decided, then rely upon Allah. Indeed, Allah loves those who rely [upon Him].
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of kindness, forgiveness, and consultation in leadership. The Prophet Muhammad's (peace be upon him) gentle and forgiving nature, which was a result of Allah's mercy, attracted people to him and kept them united. Had he been harsh and unforgiving, people would have abandoned him. The verse instructs leaders to pardon their followers, seek forgiveness for them, and consult with them in matters of importance. However, once a decision is made after consultation, the leader should put their trust in Allah and remain steadfast. The verse concludes by stating that Allah loves those who rely upon Him, emphasizing the importance of faith and trust in God in all matters, especially in leadership and decision-making.
orig: فبما رحمة من الله لنت لهم ولو كنت فظا غليظ القلب لانفضوا من حولك فاعف عنهم واستغفر لهم وشاورهم في الأمر فإذا عزمت فتوكل على الله إن الله يحب المتوكلين

translation: If Allah helps you, none can overcome you; and if He forsakes you, who is there after Him that can help you? And in Allah (Alone) let believers put their trust.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of relying on Allah's support and trusting in His plan. It reminds believers that with Allah's help, they are invincible, and without it, they are helpless. The verse encourages Muslims to put their complete trust in Allah, knowing that He is the only true source of strength and support. It also highlights the concept of tawakkul, which is the complete reliance on Allah in all matters of life, with the understanding that He is the ultimate controller of all affairs. The verse serves as a reminder to believers to always turn to Allah for help and guidance, and to have faith in His wisdom and mercy, even in the face of adversity or challenges.
orig: إن ينصركم الله فلا غالب لكم وإن يخذلكم فمن ذا الذي ينصركم من بعده وعلى الله فليتوكل المؤمنون

translation: It is not [attributable] to any prophet that he would act unfaithfully [in regard to war booty]. And whoever betrays, [taking unlawfully], will come with what he took on the Day of Resurrection. Then will every soul be [fully] compensated for what it earned, and they will not be wronged.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of honesty and integrity, especially for those in positions of leadership and authority, such as prophets. It warns against the act of "ghulul", which refers to the misappropriation of war booty or public property. The verse states that anyone who engages in such dishonest practices will be held accountable on the Day of Judgment, where they will face the consequences of their actions. The verse also highlights the concept of divine justice, asserting that every soul will be fairly compensated for what it has earned, without any injustice or oppression. This serves as a reminder for all believers to maintain honesty and trustworthiness in all their dealings, knowing that they will be held responsible for their deeds in the Hereafter.
orig: وما كان لنبي أن يغل ومن يغلل يأت بما غل يوم القيامة ثم توفى كل نفس ما كسبت وهم لا يظلمون

translation: Is the one who follows the pleasure of Allah like the one who brings upon himself the wrath of Allah and his abode is Hell? And wretched is the destination.
interpretation: This verse highlights the stark contrast between those who strive to please Allah and those who incur His wrath. It emphasizes that seeking Allah's pleasure is the ultimate goal, leading to a blessed outcome, while those who disobey Him and earn His anger will face the terrible consequences of Hell. The verse serves as a reminder for believers to align their actions with what pleases Allah, as that is the path to success and salvation, and to avoid what displeases Him at all costs, as it leads to a dreadful fate in the Hereafter.
orig: أفمن اتبع رضوان الله كمن باء بسخط من الله ومأواه جهنم وبئس المصير

translation: They are of varying degrees in the sight of Allah. And Allah is All-Seeing of what they do.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that people have different ranks and statuses in the eyes of Allah, based on their deeds and righteousness. It highlights the concept of divine justice, where individuals are judged according to their actions and intentions. The verse also underscores Allah's omniscience, affirming that He is fully aware of all that people do, whether good or bad. This serves as a reminder for believers to strive for good deeds and sincerity, knowing that Allah witnesses their actions and will hold them accountable accordingly in the Hereafter.
orig: هم درجات عند الله والله بصير بما يعملون

translation: Certainly did Allah confer [great] favor upon the believers when He sent among them a Messenger from themselves, reciting to them His verses and purifying them and teaching them the Book and wisdom, although they had been before in manifest error.
interpretation: This verse highlights the immense favor and blessing that Allah bestowed upon the believers by sending them a messenger from among themselves. The messenger's role was to recite Allah's verses to the people, purify their hearts and souls, and teach them the Qur'an and wisdom. This emphasizes the importance of prophetic guidance in leading people out of ignorance and error, and towards the path of righteousness and truth. It also underscores the significance of spiritual purification and the acquisition of knowledge in the life of a believer.
orig: لقد من الله على المؤمنين إذ بعث فيهم رسولا من أنفسهم يتلو عليهم آياته ويزكيهم ويعلمهم الكتاب والحكمة وإن كانوا من قبل لفي ضلال مبين

translation: And why [is it that] when a disaster struck you, although you had struck [the enemy] with one twice as great, you said, "From where is this?" Say, "It is from yourselves." Indeed, Allah is over all things competent.
interpretation: This verse is addressing the believers who suffered a defeat in battle, reminding them that their loss was a result of their own shortcomings and mistakes. It emphasizes that even though they had previously achieved a greater victory, their current defeat was due to their own actions and decisions. The verse also highlights Allah's power and control over all matters, implying that the outcome of any situation is ultimately in His hands. It serves as a reminder for the believers to introspect, learn from their mistakes, and trust in Allah's wisdom and decree.
orig: أولما أصابتكم مصيبة قد أصبتم مثليها قلتم أنى هذا قل هو من عند أنفسكم إن الله على كل شيء قدير

translation: And what befell you on the day the two armies met was with the permission of Allah, and that He might make evident the [true] believers.
interpretation: This verse refers to the Battle of Uhud, where the Muslims faced a setback despite initial victory. The interpretation is that whatever befalls the believers, whether good or bad, happens by Allah's will and decree. The events of Uhud were a test to distinguish the true believers, who remained steadfast in their faith despite hardship, from the hypocrites and weak in faith. It highlights that trials and tribulations are part of the divine plan to purify and strengthen the believers' faith and commitment to Allah's cause.
orig: وما أصابكم يوم التقى الجمعان فبإذن الله وليعلم المؤمنين

translation: And that those who are hypocrites may be made evident, and that it may be said to them, "Come, fight in the way of Allah or [at least] defend." They said, "If we had known [there would be] fighting, we would have followed you." They were nearer to disbelief that day than to faith, saying with their mouths what was not in their hearts. And Allah is most Knowing of what they conceal.
interpretation: This verse reveals the true nature of the hypocrites who, when called upon to fight for the cause of Allah or at least defend the Muslim community, made excuses and claimed that they would have joined the fight if they had known there would be actual combat. Their words betrayed their insincerity and lack of faith, as they were closer to disbelief than belief at that moment. The verse emphasizes that Allah is fully aware of the hidden intentions and secrets within their hearts, even if they try to conceal them with false statements. It serves as a warning against hypocrisy and highlights the importance of having a sincere and unwavering faith in Allah.
orig: وليعلم الذين نافقوا وقيل لهم تعالوا قاتلوا في سبيل الله أو ادفعوا قالوا لو نعلم قتالا لاتبعناكم هم للكفر يومئذ أقرب منهم للإيمان يقولون بأفواههم ما ليس في قلوبهم والله أعلم بما يكتمون

translation: Those who said about their brothers while sitting [at home], "If they had obeyed us, they would not have been killed." Say, "Then prevent death from yourselves, if you should be truthful."
interpretation: This verse is addressing those who did not participate in the battle and blamed the death of their fellow believers on their disobedience. It challenges them to prevent their own deaths if they are truthful in their claim that they could have prevented the deaths of others. The interpretation is that no one can escape death, and it is not in the hands of humans to prevent it when it is decreed by Allah. It also emphasizes the importance of obeying Allah and His Messenger, as those who obey will be rewarded, while those who disobey will face the consequences of their actions in this life and the hereafter.
orig: الذين قالوا لإخوانهم وقعدوا لو أطاعونا ما قتلوا قل فادرءوا عن أنفسكم الموت إن كنتم صادقين

translation: And do not think of those who have been killed in the cause of Allah as dead. Rather, they are alive with their Lord, receiving provision,
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the concept of martyrdom in Islam. Those who are killed while fighting for the cause of Allah are not to be considered dead in the conventional sense. Instead, they are believed to be alive in the presence of Allah, receiving divine blessings and provisions. This interpretation highlights the spiritual reward and honor bestowed upon those who sacrifice their lives for the sake of their faith, and it serves as a source of comfort and inspiration for the believers, encouraging them to remain steadfast in their devotion to Allah, even in the face of adversity and death.
orig: ولا تحسبن الذين قتلوا في سبيل الله أمواتا بل أحياء عند ربهم يرزقون

translation: They rejoice in what Allah has bestowed upon them of His bounty, and they receive good tidings about those [to be martyred] after them who have not yet joined them - that there will be no fear concerning them, nor will they grieve.
interpretation: This verse refers to the martyrs who have died in the path of Allah. They are happy and content with the blessings and rewards that Allah has granted them in Paradise. Moreover, they receive the good news that those believers who will be martyred after them will also have nothing to fear or grieve about in the Hereafter. This verse highlights the honor, joy, and peace that the martyrs experience in the afterlife, and it serves as an encouragement and consolation for the believers, assuring them that death in the cause of Allah leads to a blessed and rewarding outcome.
orig: فرحين بما آتاهم الله من فضله ويستبشرون بالذين لم يلحقوا بهم من خلفهم ألا خوف عليهم ولا هم يحزنون

translation: They rejoice in grace from Allah and bounty and [in] that Allah does not allow the reward of believers to be lost.
interpretation: This verse highlights the joy and contentment that believers feel when they receive Allah's blessings and favor. They are assured that their good deeds and faith will not go unrewarded, as Allah never allows the efforts of the faithful to be in vain. The verse emphasizes the importance of maintaining a strong belief in Allah's justice and mercy, knowing that He will always recognize and reward those who strive to please Him. This understanding brings a sense of peace and happiness to the hearts of the believers, even in the face of challenges and difficulties.
orig: يستبشرون بنعمة من الله وفضل وأن الله لا يضيع أجر المؤمنين

translation: Those [believers] who responded to Allah and the Messenger after injury had struck them. For those who did good among them and feared Allah is a great reward -
interpretation: This verse praises the steadfast believers who remained committed to Allah and His Messenger even after facing hardships and injuries. It emphasizes that those who persevere in faith and righteousness, despite challenges, will be rewarded greatly by Allah. The verse encourages believers to stay strong, do good deeds, and maintain their consciousness of Allah, with the promise of a magnificent reward in the Hereafter for their unwavering devotion and obedience.
orig: الذين استجابوا لله والرسول من بعد ما أصابهم القرح للذين أحسنوا منهم واتقوا أجر عظيم

translation: Those to whom hypocrites said, "Indeed, the people have gathered against you, so fear them." But it [merely] increased them in faith, and they said, "Sufficient for us is Allah, and [He is] the best Disposer of affairs."
interpretation: This verse is referring to the unwavering faith and trust in Allah that the believers have, even in the face of threats and intimidation from the enemies of Islam. When the hypocrites tried to instill fear in the hearts of the believers by telling them that a great army had gathered against them, it only served to increase their faith and their reliance on Allah's help and protection. They reaffirmed their belief that Allah alone is sufficient for them, and that He is the best guardian and protector. This demonstrates the power of true faith in Allah, which remains strong and unshakeable even in the most difficult of circumstances.
orig: الذين قال لهم الناس إن الناس قد جمعوا لكم فاخشوهم فزادهم إيمانا وقالوا حسبنا الله ونعم الوكيل

translation: So they returned with favor from Allah and bounty, no harm having touched them, and they pursued the pleasure of Allah, and Allah is the possessor of great bounty.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the blessings and rewards that Allah bestows upon those who strive in His cause and seek His pleasure. It suggests that when believers remain steadfast in their faith and pursue the path of righteousness, they will be protected from harm and will be granted abundant favors and blessings from Allah. The verse also highlights the immense generosity and grace of Allah, reminding believers that He is the possessor of infinite bounty and that His rewards for those who follow His path are beyond measure. This interpretation underscores the importance of remaining committed to one's faith and actively seeking to please Allah in order to attain His blessings and protection in this life and the hereafter.
orig: فانقلبوا بنعمة من الله وفضل لم يمسسهم سوء واتبعوا رضوان الله والله ذو فضل عظيم

translation: It is only Satan who suggests to you the fear of his supporters. So fear them not, but fear Me, if you are [indeed] believers.
interpretation: This verse is a reminder to the believers that they should not fear the allies of Satan, but rather fear Allah alone. It emphasizes that the fear of Allah is a fundamental aspect of faith, and that true believers should not be intimidated by the threats or actions of those who oppose them. The verse also implies that the fear of Allah is a source of strength and courage for the believers, enabling them to stand firm in the face of adversity and to resist the temptations and deceptions of Satan and his followers. Ultimately, the verse encourages the believers to put their trust in Allah and to rely on Him for protection and guidance, rather than succumbing to fear or doubt.
orig: إنما ذلكم الشيطان يخوف أولياءه فلا تخافوهم وخافون إن كنتم مؤمنين

translation: And do not be grieved, [O Muhammad], by those who hasten into disbelief. Indeed, they will never harm Allah at all. Allah intends that He should give them no share in the Hereafter, and for them is a great punishment.
interpretation: This verse is a reassurance to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) not to be saddened or disheartened by those who rush towards disbelief and reject the message of Islam. It emphasizes that their actions will not harm Allah in any way, as He is far above being affected by the disbelief of His creation. The verse also highlights the consequence of their choice to disbelieve: Allah intends to deprive them of any share or portion in the rewards and blessings of the Hereafter. Instead, they will face a severe punishment for their rejection of faith and their haste in embracing disbelief. This interpretation underscores the importance of remaining steadfast in faith and not being discouraged by those who oppose or reject the truth, as their actions will ultimately lead to their own detriment in the afterlife.
orig: ولا يحزنك الذين يسارعون في الكفر إنهم لن يضروا الله شيئا يريد الله ألا يجعل لهم حظا في الآخرة ولهم عذاب عظيم

translation: Indeed, those who purchase disbelief [in exchange] for faith - never will they harm Allah at all, and for them is a painful punishment.
interpretation: This verse warns those who reject faith in favor of disbelief that their actions will not harm or affect Allah in any way. They may think that by choosing disbelief over faith, they are somehow causing harm to Allah or His religion, but in reality, they are only harming themselves. Their choice to disbelieve will lead them to a painful punishment in the Hereafter, while Allah remains unaffected by their actions. This highlights the severity of choosing disbelief and the consequences one will face for making such a choice.
orig: إن الذين اشتروا الكفر بالإيمان لن يضروا الله شيئا ولهم عذاب أليم

translation: And let not those who disbelieve ever think that [because] We extend their time [of enjoyment] it is better for them. We only extend it for them so that they may increase in sin, and for them is a humiliating punishment.
interpretation: This verse serves as a stern warning to the disbelievers who may be deluded by the temporary respite and worldly pleasures that Allah grants them. They should not mistakenly assume that this is a sign of Allah's favor or approval of their actions. In reality, this extension of time and resources is only given to them so that they may further indulge in their sinful ways and accumulate more transgressions, ultimately leading to a severe and humiliating punishment in the Hereafter. It emphasizes that the apparent success or ease in the life of a disbeliever is not a blessing, but rather a test and a means for them to incur more sins, sealing their fate in the afterlife if they do not repent and change their ways.
orig: ولا يحسبن الذين كفروا أنما نملي لهم خير لأنفسهم إنما نملي لهم ليزدادوا إثما ولهم عذاب مهين

translation: Allah would not leave the believers in that [state] you are in [presently] until He separates the evil from the good. Nor would Allah reveal to you the unseen. But [instead], Allah chooses of His messengers whom He wills, so believe in Allah and His messengers. And if you believe and fear Him, then for you is a great reward.
interpretation: This verse indicates that Allah tests the believers to distinguish the sincere from the insincere. He does not inform people about the unseen, as that knowledge belongs only to Him. However, He selects certain messengers to receive divine revelation. The believers are instructed to have faith in Allah and His messengers, and if they do so while being mindful of Allah, they will be granted a tremendous reward in the Hereafter. This emphasizes the importance of genuine faith, obedience to the messengers, and righteousness in attaining salvation and Allah's pleasure.
orig: ما كان الله ليذر المؤمنين على ما أنتم عليه حتى يميز الخبيث من الطيب وما كان الله ليطلعكم على الغيب ولكن الله يجتبي من رسله من يشاء فآمنوا بالله ورسله وإن تؤمنوا وتتقوا فلكم أجر عظيم

translation: And let not those who [greedily] withhold what Allah has given them of His bounty ever think that it is better for them. Rather, it is worse for them. Their necks will be encircled by what they withheld on the Day of Resurrection. And to Allah belongs the heritage of the heavens and the earth. And Allah, with what you do, is [fully] Acquainted.
interpretation: This verse warns those who are miserly and withhold the wealth and blessings that Allah has bestowed upon them, thinking that hoarding their wealth will benefit them. In reality, their greed and stinginess will only harm them in the Hereafter. The wealth they selfishly withheld will become a source of torment for them on the Day of Judgment, like a chain around their necks. This verse reminds us that everything in the heavens and the earth belongs to Allah, and He is fully aware of our deeds and intentions. It encourages believers to be generous and spend their wealth in the cause of Allah, seeking His pleasure and reward in the Hereafter.
orig: ولا يحسبن الذين يبخلون بما آتاهم الله من فضله هو خيرا لهم بل هو شر لهم سيطوقون ما بخلوا به يوم القيامة ولله ميراث السماوات والأرض والله بما تعملون خبير

translation: Allah has certainly heard the statement of those [Jews] who said, "Indeed, Allah is poor while we are rich." We will record what they said and their killing of the prophets without right and will say, "Taste the punishment of the Burning Fire."
interpretation: This verse is a stern warning to those who mocked Allah and claimed to be self-sufficient, while belittling the message of Islam. It highlights their arrogance and disbelief in rejecting the prophets sent by Allah. The verse emphasizes that their statements and actions are recorded, and they will face severe consequences in the form of a painful punishment in the Hereafter, described as the "Burning Fire". This interpretation underscores the gravity of their offense against Allah and the divine message, and the justice that will be served in the afterlife.
orig: لقد سمع الله قول الذين قالوا إن الله فقير ونحن أغنياء سنكتب ما قالوا وقتلهم الأنبياء بغير حق ونقول ذوقوا عذاب الحريق

translation: That is because of what your hands have put forth and because Allah is not ever unjust to [His] servants.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the concept of personal responsibility in Islam. It states that whatever misfortune or difficulty a person faces is a result of their own actions and choices. At the same time, it affirms that Allah is never unjust to His servants. He does not punish them without reason or cause them undue hardship. Rather, people's own deeds and decisions lead to the consequences they face in life. This encourages individuals to be mindful of their actions, as they will be held accountable for them. It also highlights Allah's perfect justice and fairness in dealing with His creation.
orig: ذلك بما قدمت أيديكم وأن الله ليس بظلام للعبيد

translation: Those who said, "Indeed, Allah has taken our promise not to believe any messenger until he brings us an offering which fire [from heaven] will consume." Say, "There have already come to you messengers before me with clear proofs and [even] that of which you speak. So why did you kill them, if you should be truthful?"
interpretation: This verse is addressing the Jews who rejected the prophethood of Muhammad (peace be upon him) by claiming that they had a covenant with Allah not to believe in any messenger unless he brings a specific miracle - an offering consumed by fire from heaven. Allah refutes their claim by reminding them that previous prophets came to them with clear signs and even the very miracle they demanded, yet they still rejected and killed those prophets. This exposes their insincerity and the falseness of their excuse for not believing in Muhammad. The verse emphasizes that their rejection is not due to lack of proof, but rather due to their own stubbornness and disbelief.
orig: الذين قالوا إن الله عهد إلينا ألا نؤمن لرسول حتى يأتينا بقربان تأكله النار قل قد جاءكم رسل من قبلي بالبينات وبالذي قلتم فلم قتلتموهم إن كنتم صادقين

translation: Then if they deny you, [O Muhammad] - so were messengers denied before you, who brought clear proofs and written ordinances and the enlightening Scripture.
interpretation: This verse is a consolation to Prophet Muhammad, reminding him that if his people reject his message, he is not alone in this experience. Many prophets before him, such as Noah, Abraham, Moses, and Jesus, were also rejected by their people, despite bringing clear signs, scriptures, and enlightenment from Allah. The verse encourages the Prophet to remain steadfast in his faith and mission, knowing that the rejection he faces is not a reflection of the truth he brings, but rather a pattern of human behavior that has been repeated throughout history. It also serves as a warning to those who reject the message, reminding them that they are not only denying the Prophet but also the long line of messengers before him who brought similar guidance from Allah.
orig: فإن كذبوك فقد كذب رسل من قبلك جاءوا بالبينات والزبر والكتاب المنير

translation: Every soul will taste death, and you will only be given your [full] compensation on the Day of Resurrection. So he who is drawn away from the Fire and admitted to Paradise has attained [his desire]. And what is the life of this world except the enjoyment of delusion.
interpretation: This verse reminds us of the fleeting nature of this worldly life and that death is an inevitable reality for every soul. It emphasizes that the ultimate reward or punishment will only be given on the Day of Judgment. Those who are saved from the Fire and admitted into Paradise are the successful ones, having achieved the true purpose of life. The verse also highlights that the life of this world is merely a deceptive enjoyment, and we should not be distracted by its temporary pleasures, but rather focus on striving for the eternal rewards of the Hereafter.
orig: كل نفس ذائقة الموت وإنما توفون أجوركم يوم القيامة فمن زحزح عن النار وأدخل الجنة فقد فاز وما الحياة الدنيا إلا متاع الغرور

translation: You will surely be tested in your possessions and in yourselves. And you will surely hear from those who were given the Scripture before you and from those who associate others with Allah much abuse. But if you are patient and fear Allah - indeed, that is of the matters [worthy] of determination.
interpretation: This verse indicates that the believers will face various trials and tribulations, both in terms of their wealth and their personal lives. They will also face verbal abuse and harassment from those who were given revealed scriptures before them, such as the Jews and Christians, as well as from the polytheists who associate partners with Allah. However, the verse encourages the believers to remain patient and steadfast in their faith, and to have consciousness of Allah (taqwa) in the face of these challenges. It emphasizes that persevering through such difficulties with patience and piety is a matter of great resolve and determination, and is highly commendable in the sight of Allah.
orig: لتبلون في أموالكم وأنفسكم ولتسمعن من الذين أوتوا الكتاب من قبلكم ومن الذين أشركوا أذى كثيرا وإن تصبروا وتتقوا فإن ذلك من عزم الأمور

translation: And [mention, O Muhammad], when Allah took a covenant from those who were given the Scripture, [saying], "You must make it clear [i.e., explain it] to the people and not conceal it." But they threw it away behind their backs and exchanged it for a small price. And wretched is that which they purchased.
interpretation: This verse is a reminder of the covenant that Allah took from the People of the Book (Jews and Christians) to explain the truth of their scriptures to the people and not to hide it. However, they broke this covenant by concealing the truth and exchanging it for worldly gains and status. They chose to follow their own desires and the ways of their forefathers instead of the guidance sent by Allah. As a result, they earned the wrath of Allah and a miserable fate in the Hereafter. This serves as a warning to all believers to fulfill their covenant with Allah, to follow His guidance, and to avoid the temptations of this world that lead to misguidance and loss in the Hereafter.
orig: وإذ أخذ الله ميثاق الذين أوتوا الكتاب لتبيننه للناس ولا تكتمونه فنبذوه وراء ظهورهم واشتروا به ثمنا قليلا فبئس ما يشترون

translation: Let not those who exult in what they have brought about and love to be praised for what they have not done - never think, [O Muhammad], that they are in safety from the punishment, and for them is a painful punishment.
interpretation: This verse warns against those who are proud of their accomplishments and seek praise for things they have not done. It emphasizes that such people should not feel secure from Allah's punishment, as they will face a severe penalty in the Hereafter for their arrogance and deception. The verse reminds believers to be humble, honest, and sincere in their actions, seeking praise and reward only from Allah, rather than from people.
orig: لا تحسبن الذين يفرحون بما أتوا ويحبون أن يحمدوا بما لم يفعلوا فلا تحسبنهم بمفازة من العذاب ولهم عذاب أليم

translation: And to Allah belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth, and Allah is over all things competent.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute sovereignty and power of Allah over all of His creation. It reminds us that everything in the heavens and the earth belongs to Him alone, and that He has the ability to do all things. This should instill in believers a sense of humility, submission, and reliance upon Allah, knowing that He is the ultimate authority and that nothing happens without His permission. It also serves as a warning to those who may oppose or disobey Him, as they will ultimately have to answer to the One who has complete control over all things.
orig: ولله ملك السماوات والأرض والله على كل شيء قدير

translation: Indeed, in the creation of the heavens and the earth and the alternation of the night and the day are signs for those of understanding.
interpretation: This verse draws our attention to the wonders of Allah's creation as a means for reflection and deepening faith. The perfect design, balance and precision in the universe, from the vast galaxies down to the alternation of night and day, are presented as signs for people of insight and intellect to ponder over. It invites us to use our minds and reflect on these marvels as a way to appreciate the power, wisdom and supremacy of the Creator. Contemplating on the universe and its workings can strengthen belief, inspire humility and remind us of the temporary nature of the worldly life in contrast to the eternal hereafter. The verse emphasizes that these signs are specifically for "Ulul-Albaab" - people of sound reasoning and pure understanding, encouraging the use of intellect in the path of faith.
orig: إن في خلق السماوات والأرض واختلاف الليل والنهار لآيات لأولي الألباب

translation: Who remember Allah while standing or sitting or [lying] on their sides and give thought to the creation of the heavens and the earth, [saying], "Our Lord, You did not create this aimlessly; exalted are You [above such a thing]; then protect us from the punishment of the Fire."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of remembering Allah and reflecting on His creation. Those who constantly remember Allah in all positions and ponder over the marvels of the universe recognize that everything has a purpose and is not created in vain. They acknowledge Allah's wisdom and perfection, and seek His protection from the punishment of Hell. This verse encourages believers to maintain a strong connection with their Lord through remembrance and contemplation, which will lead them to appreciate the purposeful creation and seek refuge in Allah's mercy.
orig: الذين يذكرون الله قياما وقعودا وعلى جنوبهم ويتفكرون في خلق السماوات والأرض ربنا ما خلقت هذا باطلا سبحانك فقنا عذاب النار

translation: Our Lord, indeed whoever You admit to the Fire - You have disgraced him, and for the wrongdoers there are no helpers.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the severity of being condemned to the Hellfire by Allah. It suggests that those who are sent to Hell have been utterly humiliated and disgraced by Allah due to their wrongdoings and sins. The verse also points out that the wrongdoers and sinners will have no one to help or support them in the Hereafter, as they have earned Allah's punishment through their own actions. It serves as a warning to mankind to avoid sin and to strive for righteousness, as the consequences of being admitted to the Fire are severe and eternal.
orig: ربنا إنك من تدخل النار فقد أخزيته وما للظالمين من أنصار

translation: Our Lord, indeed we have heard a caller calling to faith, [saying], 'Believe in your Lord,' and we have believed. Our Lord, so forgive us our sins and remove from us our misdeeds and cause us to die with the righteous.
interpretation: This verse is a heartfelt plea and prayer to Allah from the believers. It expresses their sincere faith and trust in Allah, acknowledging that they have heard and responded to the call of the messenger inviting them to believe. They beseech Allah for forgiveness of their sins, asking Him to erase their misdeeds and ultimately allow them to die as righteous individuals in a state of His favor and grace. This prayer encapsulates the essence of a believer's journey - hearing the truth, accepting it wholeheartedly, seeking Allah's mercy and forgiveness, striving to do good, and hoping to die as a righteous person with the ultimate aim of attaining Allah's pleasure and closeness in the Hereafter.
orig: ربنا إننا سمعنا مناديا ينادي للإيمان أن آمنوا بربكم فآمنا ربنا فاغفر لنا ذنوبنا وكفر عنا سيئاتنا وتوفنا مع الأبرار

translation: Our Lord! Grant us what You promised unto us through Your messengers and disgrace us not on the Day of Resurrection, for You never break promise.
interpretation: This verse is a humble and earnest supplication to Allah. The believers are beseeching Allah to fulfill the promises He has made to them through His messengers, which include His forgiveness, mercy, and the ultimate reward of Paradise. They are also pleading to Allah to spare them from humiliation and disgrace on the Day of Judgment. The verse emphasizes the believers' complete trust in Allah's promises, affirming that He never fails to keep His word. It underscores the importance of faith, righteous deeds, and turning to Allah with sincere prayers and supplications, especially in seeking His grace and favor in the Hereafter.
orig: ربنا وآتنا ما وعدتنا على رسلك ولا تخزنا يوم القيامة إنك لا تخلف الميعاد

translation: And their Lord responded to them, "Never will I allow to be lost the work of [any] worker among you, whether male or female; you are of one another. So those who emigrated or were evicted from their homes or were harmed in My cause or fought or were killed - I will surely remove from them their misdeeds, and I will surely admit them to gardens beneath which rivers flow as reward from Allah, and Allah has with Him the best reward."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the equality of men and women in the eyes of Allah. It assures that Allah will reward all those who strive in His cause, regardless of their gender. It specifically mentions those who faced hardships, such as emigration, eviction from their homes, being harmed, fighting, or even getting killed for the sake of Allah. Allah promises to erase their misdeeds and grant them entry into Paradise as a reward from Him. This highlights the importance of sacrifice, perseverance and dedication to Allah's cause, and shows His appreciation and acknowledgement of the struggles of the believers.
orig: فاستجاب لهم ربهم أني لا أضيع عمل عامل منكم من ذكر أو أنثى بعضكم من بعض فالذين هاجروا وأخرجوا من ديارهم وأوذوا في سبيلي وقاتلوا وقتلوا لأكفرن عنهم سيئاتهم ولأدخلنهم جنات تجري من تحتها الأنهار ثوابا من عند الله والله عنده حسن الثواب

translation: Let not the free disposal (and affluence) of the disbelievers throughout the land deceive you.
interpretation: This verse warns believers not to be deceived by the apparent prosperity and freedom enjoyed by disbelievers in this worldly life. Their affluence and ability to travel freely for trade and other purposes may give the impression that they are successful and blessed. However, this is a temporary and illusory state that should not make believers doubt the truth of Islam or envy the position of the disbelievers. Rather, believers should remain steadfast, knowing that the true success and eternal reward lies with those who have faith and do righteous deeds, regardless of their worldly circumstances. The fleeting nature of the disbelievers' prosperity will become apparent in the Hereafter.
orig: لا يغرنك تقلب الذين كفروا في البلاد

translation: A little enjoyment, then their abode is Hell, and wretched is the resting place.
interpretation: This verse warns that the pleasures and enjoyments of this worldly life are fleeting and short-lived. Those who indulge in them excessively while neglecting their spiritual duties will ultimately face the consequences in the Hereafter. Their final abode will be Hell, which is described as a terrible resting place of suffering and misery. It emphasizes the importance of prioritizing one's relationship with God and the pursuit of righteousness over temporary worldly gains, as the latter will be of no benefit in the eternal life to come.
orig: متاع قليل ثم مأواهم جهنم وبئس المهاد

translation: But those who feared their Lord will have gardens beneath which rivers flow, abiding eternally therein, as accommodation from Allah. And that which is with Allah is best for the righteous.
