interpretation: This verse emphasizes the great reward that awaits the righteous believers who fear Allah and obey His commands. It describes Paradise as a place of eternal bliss, with gardens underneath which rivers flow. This is the ultimate gift and accommodation from Allah Himself to those who lived a life of righteousness. The verse also points out that whatever rewards or pleasures Allah has in store for His faithful servants in the Hereafter are far superior to anything in this worldly life, highlighting the importance of striving for the eternal rather than the temporary.
orig: لكن الذين اتقوا ربهم لهم جنات تجري من تحتها الأنهار خالدين فيها نزلا من عند الله وما عند الله خير للأبرار

translation: And indeed, among the People of the Scripture are those who believe in Allah and what was revealed to you and what was revealed to them, [being] humbly submissive to Allah. They do not exchange the verses of Allah for a small price. Those will have their reward with their Lord. Indeed, Allah is swift in account.
interpretation: This verse highlights that there are righteous individuals among the People of the Book (Jews and Christians) who sincerely believe in Allah, the Qur'an, and the previous revelations. They are humble and submissive to Allah, and they do not compromise their faith for worldly gains or benefits. Allah acknowledges their sincerity and affirms that they will be rewarded by Him for their faith and good deeds. The verse emphasizes that Allah is swift in reckoning, indicating that He will promptly reward those who are faithful to Him and adhere to His teachings.
orig: وإن من أهل الكتاب لمن يؤمن بالله وما أنزل إليكم وما أنزل إليهم خاشعين لله لا يشترون بآيات الله ثمنا قليلا أولئك لهم أجرهم عند ربهم إن الله سريع الحساب

translation: O you who have believed, persevere and endure and remain stationed and fear Allah that you may be successful.
interpretation: This verse is a call to the believers to remain steadfast in the face of adversity and to persevere through hardships. It encourages them to be patient, to endure the difficulties they face, and to remain vigilant in their faith. The verse also reminds the believers to have taqwa, which is the fear of Allah and the consciousness of Him in all their actions. By doing so, they may attain success and felicity, both in this world and in the Hereafter. This verse highlights the importance of patience, perseverance, and God-consciousness as key qualities that every believer should strive to embody in their lives.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا اصبروا وصابروا ورابطوا واتقوا الله لعلكم تفلحون

translation: O mankind, fear your Lord, who created you from one soul and created from it its mate and dispersed from both of them many men and women. And fear Allah, through whom you ask one another, and the wombs. Indeed Allah is ever, over you, an Observer.
interpretation: This verse is a reminder for all of humanity to be conscious of Allah, who created them all from a single soul (Adam) and created from that soul its mate (Eve), and then spread from these two many men and women. It emphasizes the importance of fearing Allah, in whose name people swear and make requests, and also highlights the significance of family ties, particularly the wombs that bore us. The verse concludes by stating that Allah is always watching over us, aware of our actions and intentions. This interpretation suggests that we should live our lives with a sense of responsibility, mindful of our Creator and maintaining the bonds of kinship.
orig: يا أيها الناس اتقوا ربكم الذي خلقكم من نفس واحدة وخلق منها زوجها وبث منهما رجالا كثيرا ونساء واتقوا الله الذي تساءلون به والأرحام إن الله كان عليكم رقيبا

translation: And give the orphans their properties and do not substitute the bad for the good, and do not consume their properties into your own. Indeed, that is a great sin.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of protecting the rights and property of orphans. As their guardians, we have a responsibility to manage their wealth with integrity and not exploit their vulnerability for personal gain. Misappropriating an orphan's property or mixing it with one's own is considered a major sin in Islam. The verse calls for honesty, trustworthiness, and selflessness in dealing with those who are weak and unable to defend their own interests. It reflects the Qur'an's strong emphasis on social justice and its particular concern for safeguarding the rights of the most vulnerable members of society.
orig: وآتوا اليتامى أموالهم ولا تتبدلوا الخبيث بالطيب ولا تأكلوا أموالهم إلى أموالكم إنه كان حوبا كبيرا

translation: And if you fear that you will not deal justly with the orphan girls, then marry those that please you of [other] women, two or three or four. But if you fear that you will not be just, then [marry only] one or those your right hand possesses. That is more suitable that you may not incline [to injustice].
interpretation: This verse addresses the just treatment of orphan girls and the number of wives a man can marry. If a man fears he cannot deal fairly with orphan girls under his care, he should marry other women, up to four, provided he can treat them equally. However, if he fears he cannot maintain justice between multiple wives, he should only marry one, or marry from among his slave women. The purpose is to avoid injustice or sin by taking on more than one can handle fairly. Ultimately, the verse guides towards justice, self-control and avoiding transgression of limits, especially regarding vulnerable groups like orphans and women.
orig: وإن خفتم ألا تقسطوا في اليتامى فانكحوا ما طاب لكم من النساء مثنى وثلاث ورباع فإن خفتم ألا تعدلوا فواحدة أو ما ملكت أيمانكم ذلك أدنى ألا تعولوا

translation: And give the women [upon marriage] their [bridal] gifts graciously. But if they give up willingly to you anything of it, then take it in satisfaction and ease.
interpretation: This verse instructs men to give women their bridal gifts or dowry (mahr) willingly and graciously at the time of marriage. It is an obligation upon the husband and a right of the wife. However, if after receiving the dowry, the wife voluntarily chooses to give up a portion of it to the husband, then he may accept it without any blame or guilt. This shows the importance of mutual understanding, consent, and goodwill between spouses regarding their financial matters. The verse promotes generosity and willingness in marital transactions, while allowing flexibility and accommodation based on the couple's mutual agreement.
orig: وآتوا النساء صدقاتهن نحلة فإن طبن لكم عن شيء منه نفسا فكلوه هنيئا مريئا

translation: And do not give the foolish your wealth which Allah has made a means of sustenance for you, but provide for them with it and clothe them and speak to them words of appropriate kindness.
interpretation: This verse instructs believers not to entrust their wealth to those who are incompetent or unable to handle it responsibly, as this wealth is a means of livelihood that Allah has provided. Instead, they should maintain control over their assets while using a portion to provide for the basic needs of those dependent on them, such as food and clothing. When dealing with these dependents, they should communicate with kindness and understanding, offering words of support and encouragement rather than harshness or condescension. This guidance promotes responsible financial management, compassion, and positive relationships within the community.
orig: ولا تؤتوا السفهاء أموالكم التي جعل الله لكم قياما وارزقوهم فيها واكسوهم وقولوا لهم قولا معروفا

translation: And test the orphans [in their abilities] until they reach marriageable age. Then if you perceive in them sound judgement, release their property to them. And do not consume it excessively and quickly, [anticipating] that they will grow up. And whoever, [when acting as guardian], is self-sufficient should refrain [from taking a fee]; and whoever is poor - let him take according to what is acceptable. Then when you release their property to them, bring witnesses upon them. And sufficient is Allah as Accountant.
interpretation: This verse provides guidance on dealing with the property of orphans. It instructs guardians to test the orphans' maturity and ability to handle their own affairs before handing over their property. If the orphans demonstrate sound judgment upon reaching marriageable age, their property should be released to them. The verse warns against misusing or hastily consuming the orphans' wealth out of fear that they will grow up and claim it. Guardians who are wealthy should refrain from taking any compensation, while those in need may take a reasonable amount. When returning the property to the orphans, the process should be witnessed to ensure transparency and accountability. Ultimately, Allah is sufficient as a watchful Accountant over all affairs.
orig: وابتلوا اليتامى حتى إذا بلغوا النكاح فإن آنستم منهم رشدا فادفعوا إليهم أموالهم ولا تأكلوها إسرافا وبدارا أن يكبروا ومن كان غنيا فليستعفف ومن كان فقيرا فليأكل بالمعروف فإذا دفعتم إليهم أموالهم فأشهدوا عليهم وكفى بالله حسيبا

translation: For men is a share of what the parents and close relatives leave, and for women is a share of what the parents and close relatives leave, be it little or much - a determined share.
interpretation: This verse establishes the principle of inheritance in Islam, affirming that both men and women have a rightful share in the property left behind by their parents and close relatives. The share is determined by Islamic law and is not dependent on the amount of wealth left behind, whether it be little or much. This verse emphasizes the importance of fairness and justice in the distribution of inheritance, ensuring that both male and female heirs receive their due rights. It also highlights the significance of family ties and the responsibility of caring for one's relatives, even after their passing.
orig: للرجال نصيب مما ترك الوالدان والأقربون وللنساء نصيب مما ترك الوالدان والأقربون مما قل منه أو كثر نصيبا مفروضا

translation: And when [other] relatives and orphans and the needy are present at the [time of] division, then provide for them [something] out of it [i.e., the estate] and speak to them words of appropriate kindness.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of showing kindness and generosity towards relatives, orphans, and the needy, especially during the distribution of inheritance. It encourages Muslims to set aside a portion of the estate for these individuals, even if they are not entitled to a legal share, as a gesture of goodwill and compassion. The verse also stresses the significance of speaking to them with kindness and respect, recognizing their dignity and ensuring that they feel included and cared for during this sensitive time. This act of generosity and considerate speech is a reflection of the Islamic values of social responsibility, empathy, and maintaining strong family ties.
orig: وإذا حضر القسمة أولو القربى واليتامى والمساكين فارزقوهم منه وقولوا لهم قولا معروفا

translation: And let those [executors and guardians] fear [injustice] as if they [themselves] had left weak offspring behind and feared for them. So let them fear Allah and speak words of appropriate justice.
interpretation: This verse is a reminder for those who are responsible for the care of others, particularly those who are vulnerable such as orphans or the elderly. It encourages them to treat those under their care with the same concern and compassion they would show to their own children if they were to pass away and leave them behind. The verse emphasizes the importance of fearing Allah and speaking justly, as one will be accountable for their actions in the Hereafter. It serves as a warning against taking advantage of the weak or using their wealth or property unjustly. Instead, guardians should fulfill their duties with integrity, ensuring the rights and well-being of those entrusted to them.
orig: وليخش الذين لو تركوا من خلفهم ذرية ضعافا خافوا عليهم فليتقوا الله وليقولوا قولا سديدا

translation: Indeed, those who unjustly consume orphans' wealth [in fact] consume into their bellies only fire. And they will be burned in a Blaze.
interpretation: This verse is a stern warning against those who wrongfully take the property of orphans and use it for their own benefit. It emphasizes that such an act is a grave sin, comparable to consuming fire itself. The verse makes it clear that those who commit this injustice will face severe consequences in the Hereafter, where they will be subjected to the blazing fire of Hell as a punishment for their actions. This interpretation highlights the importance of protecting the rights of the vulnerable, especially orphans, and the gravity of violating their trust and misappropriating their wealth.
orig: إن الذين يأكلون أموال اليتامى ظلما إنما يأكلون في بطونهم نارا وسيصلون سعيرا

translation: Allah instructs you concerning your children: for the male, what is equal to the share of two females. But if there are [only] daughters, two or more, for them is two thirds of one's estate. And if there is only one, for her is half. And for one's parents, to each one of them is a sixth of his estate if he left children. But if he had no children and the parents [alone] inherit from him, then for his mother is one third. And if he had brothers [or sisters], for his mother is a sixth, after any bequest he [may have] made or debt. Your parents or your children - you know not which of them are nearest to you in benefit. [These shares are] an obligation [imposed] by Allah. Indeed, Allah is ever Knowing and Wise.
interpretation: This verse provides guidance on the Islamic rules of inheritance. It specifies the shares that should be allocated to children, parents, and siblings from the estate of the deceased. The shares vary depending on the number and gender of the heirs. The verse emphasizes that these rules are decreed by Allah, who is All-Knowing and Wise. The rules aim to ensure fair distribution of the estate among the heirs based on their relationship to the deceased and their level of financial responsibility within the family.
orig: يوصيكم الله في أولادكم للذكر مثل حظ الأنثيين فإن كن نساء فوق اثنتين فلهن ثلثا ما ترك وإن كانت واحدة فلها النصف ولأبويه لكل واحد منهما السدس مما ترك إن كان له ولد فإن لم يكن له ولد وورثه أبواه فلأمه الثلث فإن كان له إخوة فلأمه السدس من بعد وصية يوصي بها أو دين آباؤكم وأبناؤكم لا تدرون أيهم أقرب لكم نفعا فريضة من الله إن الله كان عليما حكيما

translation: And for you is half of what your wives leave if they have no child. But if they have a child, for you is one fourth of what they leave, after any bequest they [may have] made or debt. And for the wives is one fourth if you leave no child. But if you leave a child, then for them is an eighth of what you leave, after any bequest you [may have] made or debt. And if a man or woman leaves neither ascendants nor descendants but has a brother or a sister, then for each one of them is a sixth. But if they are more than two, they share a third, after any bequest which was made or debt, as long as there is no detriment [caused]. [This is] an ordinance from Allah, and Allah is Knowing and Forbearing.
interpretation: This verse outlines the inheritance rights of spouses and siblings in Islam. It establishes that a husband receives half of his deceased wife's estate if they had no children, and a quarter if they had children. Conversely, a wife receives a quarter of her deceased husband's estate if they had no children, and an eighth if they had children. If the deceased had no children or parents, but had siblings, each sibling receives a sixth of the estate. If there are more than two siblings, they collectively receive a third. The verse emphasizes that these distributions should take place after fulfilling any bequests or debts, and without causing any detriment. This ordinance is attributed to Allah's knowledge and forbearance, underlining the wisdom and fairness behind these rules of inheritance in Islam.
orig: ولكم نصف ما ترك أزواجكم إن لم يكن لهن ولد فإن كان لهن ولد فلكم الربع مما تركن من بعد وصية يوصين بها أو دين ولهن الربع مما تركتم إن لم يكن لكم ولد فإن كان لكم ولد فلهن الثمن مما تركتم من بعد وصية توصون بها أو دين وإن كان رجل يورث كلالة أو امرأة وله أخ أو أخت فلكل واحد منهما السدس فإن كانوا أكثر من ذلك فهم شركاء في الثلث من بعد وصية يوصى بها أو دين غير مضار وصية من الله والله عليم حليم

translation: These are the limits [set by] Allah, and whoever obeys Allah and His Messenger will be admitted by Him to gardens [in Paradise] under which rivers flow, abiding eternally therein; and that is the great attainment.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of obeying Allah and His Messenger, Muhammad (peace be upon him). It promises that those who adhere to the limits set by Allah and follow the teachings of Islam will be rewarded with eternal Paradise, where they will enjoy gardens with flowing rivers. This reward is described as the "great attainment" or the ultimate success, highlighting the significance of living a life in accordance with Allah's commandments. The verse encourages believers to stay within the boundaries of what is permissible and to avoid transgressing against Allah's laws, as this obedience will lead to the greatest reward in the Hereafter.
orig: تلك حدود الله ومن يطع الله ورسوله يدخله جنات تجري من تحتها الأنهار خالدين فيها وذلك الفوز العظيم

translation: And whoever disobeys Allah and His Messenger and transgresses His limits - He will put him into the Fire to abide eternally therein, and he will have a humiliating punishment.
interpretation: This verse serves as a stern warning to those who willfully disobey Allah and His Messenger (ﷺ) and transgress the limits set by Allah. It emphasizes the severity of such a sin by stating that the punishment for this is eternal hellfire and humiliation. The verse underscores the importance of obedience to Allah and His Messenger (ﷺ) and staying within the bounds of what has been decreed as permissible. It is a reminder to the believers to be ever mindful of Allah's commands and prohibitions, lest they fall into grave sin and suffer the painful consequences in the hereafter.
orig: ومن يعص الله ورسوله ويتعد حدوده يدخله نارا خالدا فيها وله عذاب مهين

translation: And those who commit unlawful sexual intercourse of your women - bring against them four [witnesses] from among you. And if they testify, confine the guilty women to houses until death takes them or Allah ordains for them [another] way.
interpretation: This verse prescribes the punishment for women who engage in unlawful sexual relations (zina). It requires four witnesses to establish the crime. If guilt is proven, the women are to be confined to their homes until they die or until God provides another way out for them. This could refer to the possibility of repentance, marriage, or a divine decree replacing this ruling. The verse aims to strongly discourage and punish zina to protect chastity, honor, and moral purity in society. It reflects the gravity of the sin of zina in Islam.
orig: واللاتي يأتين الفاحشة من نسائكم فاستشهدوا عليهن أربعة منكم فإن شهدوا فأمسكوهن في البيوت حتى يتوفاهن الموت أو يجعل الله لهن سبيلا

translation: And the two who commit it among you, dishonor them both. But if they repent and correct themselves, leave them alone. Indeed, Allah is ever Accepting of repentance and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse is addressing the issue of homosexuality. It instructs that if two people engage in this sinful act, they should be reprimanded and dishonored in society as a form of punishment and deterrent. However, if they sincerely repent, mend their ways, and refrain from repeating the sin, then the believers should forgive them and not continue to shame or punish them. The verse emphasizes that Allah is All-Forgiving and Merciful, so He will accept the repentance of those who turn back to Him sincerely after committing sins. It highlights the Islamic principle of balancing justice with compassion and offering a path to redemption for sinners.
orig: واللذان يأتيانها منكم فآذوهما فإن تابا وأصلحا فأعرضوا عنهما إن الله كان توابا رحيما

translation: Allah accepts only the repentance of those who do evil in ignorance and foolishness and repent soon afterwards; it is they to whom Allah will forgive and Allah is Ever All-Knower, All-Wise.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's mercy and forgiveness towards those who commit sins out of ignorance or foolishness, but sincerely repent and turn back to Him soon after realizing their mistakes. It highlights that Allah, in His infinite wisdom and knowledge, accepts the repentance of such individuals, understanding the human nature and its weaknesses. The verse also implies that one should not delay repentance, as the acceptance of repentance is tied to it being done "soon afterwards" the commission of the sin. This encourages believers to constantly self-reflect, recognize their errors, and seek Allah's forgiveness without delay, trusting in His mercy and wisdom.
orig: إنما التوبة على الله للذين يعملون السوء بجهالة ثم يتوبون من قريب فأولئك يتوب الله عليهم وكان الله عليما حكيما

translation: But repentance is not [accepted] of those who [continue to] do evil deeds up until, when death comes to one of them, he says, "Indeed, I have repented now," or of those who die while they are disbelievers. For them We have prepared a painful punishment.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that repentance and seeking forgiveness from Allah is not accepted from those who persistently commit sins and only turn to Allah when they are on the verge of death. It also states that those who die as disbelievers will face a severe punishment in the Hereafter. The verse underscores the importance of sincere and timely repentance, as well as the consequences of rejecting faith and dying in a state of disbelief. It serves as a reminder for individuals to mend their ways and turn to Allah in earnest repentance before it is too late.
orig: وليست التوبة للذين يعملون السيئات حتى إذا حضر أحدهم الموت قال إني تبت الآن ولا الذين يموتون وهم كفار أولئك أعتدنا لهم عذابا أليما

translation: O you who have believed, it is not lawful for you to inherit women by compulsion. And do not make difficulties for them in order to take [back] part of what you gave them unless they commit a clear immorality. And live with them in kindness. For if you dislike them - perhaps you dislike a thing and Allah makes therein much good.
interpretation: This verse establishes the rights and dignity of women in Islam. It prohibits the pre-Islamic practice of inheriting women against their will and oppressing them to take back dowry. It commands husbands to treat their wives with kindness and respect, even if they dislike certain aspects about them. The verse emphasizes that what one may dislike could actually hold much good, by the will of Allah. This underscores the importance of patience, wisdom and trust in Allah in marital relationships.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا لا يحل لكم أن ترثوا النساء كرها ولا تعضلوهن لتذهبوا ببعض ما آتيتموهن إلا أن يأتين بفاحشة مبينة وعاشروهن بالمعروف فإن كرهتموهن فعسى أن تكرهوا شيئا ويجعل الله فيه خيرا كثيرا

translation: And if you want to replace one wife with another and you have given one of them a great amount [in gifts], do not take [back] from it anything. Would you take it in injustice and manifest sin?
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of fairness and justice in marital relationships. If a man wishes to divorce his wife and marry another, he should not take back the gifts or dowry he has given to his first wife, as this would be an act of injustice and a clear sin. The verse highlights the sanctity of marriage and the rights of women in Islam, discouraging men from treating their wives unfairly or taking advantage of them financially. It promotes the principles of equity, respect, and compassion within the context of marriage and divorce.
orig: وإن أردتم استبدال زوج مكان زوج وآتيتم إحداهن قنطارا فلا تأخذوا منه شيئا أتأخذونه بهتانا وإثما مبينا

translation: And how could you take it while you have gone in unto each other and they have taken from you a solemn covenant?
interpretation: This verse is addressing the issue of divorce and the return of the dowry. It is emphasizing the seriousness and sanctity of the marriage covenant by reminding the spouses that they have been intimate with each other and have made a solemn promise before Allah to honor and fulfill the rights and responsibilities of marriage. The rhetorical question "And how could you take it" is expressing disapproval and censure towards the idea of a husband taking back the dowry from his wife in the event of a divorce, given the weightiness of the marital bond that had been consummated between them. It underscores the gravity of the marriage commitment and how it should not be easily dissolved or treated lightly.
orig: وكيف تأخذونه وقد أفضى بعضكم إلى بعض وأخذن منكم ميثاقا غليظا

translation: And do not marry those [women] whom your fathers married, except what has already occurred. Indeed, it was an immorality and hateful [to Allah] and was evil as a way.
interpretation: This verse prohibits Muslim men from marrying women who were previously married to their fathers, considering such marriages as immoral, hateful, and an evil practice. However, it makes an exception for cases that occurred before the revelation of this verse, implying that those pre-existing marriages are not subject to this prohibition. The verse emphasizes the importance of maintaining proper and moral relationships within the family structure and avoiding practices that were common in pre-Islamic Arabia but were deemed unethical in Islam.
orig: ولا تنكحوا ما نكح آباؤكم من النساء إلا ما قد سلف إنه كان فاحشة ومقتا وساء سبيلا

translation: Prohibited to you [for marriage] are your mothers, your daughters, your sisters, your father's sisters, your mother's sisters, your brother's daughters, your sister's daughters, your [milk] mothers who nursed you, your sisters through nursing, your wives' mothers, and your step-daughters under your guardianship [born] of your wives unto whom you have gone in. But if you have not gone in unto them, there is no sin upon you. And [also prohibited are] the wives of your sons who are from your [own] loins, and that you take [in marriage] two sisters simultaneously, except for what has already occurred. Indeed, Allah is ever Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse specifies the categories of women that a Muslim man is forbidden to marry due to blood relations, milk relations or marital relations. It prohibits marriage to one's mother, daughter, sister, paternal aunt, maternal aunt, brother's daughter, sister's daughter, milk mother, milk sister, wife's mother, step-daughter born to a wife one has consummated marriage with, son's wife, and being married to two sisters at the same time. The prohibitions are based on the close familial ties and the need to maintain the purity and sanctity of such relationships. However, the verse ends by emphasizing Allah's forgiveness for any such relations that may have occurred before one's acceptance of Islam.
orig: حرمت عليكم أمهاتكم وبناتكم وأخواتكم وعماتكم وخالاتكم وبنات الأخ وبنات الأخت وأمهاتكم اللاتي أرضعنكم وأخواتكم من الرضاعة وأمهات نسائكم وربائبكم اللاتي في حجوركم من نسائكم اللاتي دخلتم بهن فإن لم تكونوا دخلتم بهن فلا جناح عليكم وحلائل أبنائكم الذين من أصلابكم وأن تجمعوا بين الأختين إلا ما قد سلف إن الله كان غفورا رحيما

translation: And [also prohibited to you are all] married women except those your right hands possess. [This is] the decree of Allah upon you. And lawful to you are [all others] beyond these, [provided] that you seek them [in marriage] with [gifts from] your property, desiring chastity, not unlawful sexual intercourse. So for whatever you enjoy [of marriage] from them, give them their due compensation as an obligation. And there is no blame upon you for what you mutually agree to beyond the obligation. Indeed, Allah is ever Knowing and Wise.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the sanctity of marriage and the prohibition of adultery. It allows Muslim men to marry women who are not already married, as long as they do so with pure intentions and not just for sexual gratification. If a man marries a woman, he must give her the agreed upon mahr (dowry) as her right. The verse ends by stating that any further agreements made between the husband and wife are permissible, as long as they are mutually agreed upon, and that Allah is All-Knowing and All-Wise, emphasizing that He knows the intentions behind people's actions and has legislated these rulings with perfect wisdom.
orig: والمحصنات من النساء إلا ما ملكت أيمانكم كتاب الله عليكم وأحل لكم ما وراء ذلكم أن تبتغوا بأموالكم محصنين غير مسافحين فما استمتعتم به منهن فآتوهن أجورهن فريضة ولا جناح عليكم فيما تراضيتم به من بعد الفريضة إن الله كان عليما حكيما

translation: And whoever among you cannot [find] the means to marry free, believing women, then [he may marry] from those whom your right hands possess of believing slave girls. And Allah is most knowing about your faith. You [believers] are of one another. So marry them with the permission of their people and give them their due compensation according to what is acceptable. [They should be] chaste, neither [of] those who commit unlawful intercourse randomly nor those who take [secret] lovers. But once they are sheltered in marriage, if they should commit adultery, then for them is half the punishment for free [unmarried] women. This [allowance] is for him among you who fears sin, but to be patient is better for you. And Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse provides guidance for Muslim men who cannot afford to marry free believing women. It allows them to marry believing slave women instead, with the permission of the slave women's guardians and giving them fair dowry. The verse emphasizes that all believers are equal in faith, regardless of social status. It commands the believing men to marry the slave women in a chaste and proper manner, not using them for mere sexual gratification or taking them as secret lovers. If the married slave women then commit adultery, their punishment is half of that prescribed for free unmarried women. The concession of marrying slave women is for those men who fear falling into sin. However, the verse concludes that it is better to remain patient and avoid this if possible, and that Allah is Forgiving and Merciful, emphasizing the preference for freeing and marrying slave women rather than keeping them in bondage.
orig: ومن لم يستطع منكم طولا أن ينكح المحصنات المؤمنات فمن ما ملكت أيمانكم من فتياتكم المؤمنات والله أعلم بإيمانكم بعضكم من بعض فانكحوهن بإذن أهلهن وآتوهن أجورهن بالمعروف محصنات غير مسافحات ولا متخذات أخدان فإذا أحصن فإن أتين بفاحشة فعليهن نصف ما على المحصنات من العذاب ذلك لمن خشي العنت منكم وأن تصبروا خير لكم والله غفور رحيم

translation: Allah wants to make clear to you [the lawful from the unlawful] and guide you to the [good] practices of those before you and to accept your repentance. And Allah is Knowing and Wise.
interpretation: In this verse, Allah expresses His desire to guide humanity and make the right path clear to them. He wants to show people the way of the righteous individuals who came before, as their example is one to be emulated. The mention of Allah's acceptance of repentance emphasizes His infinite mercy and forgiveness. He is willing to pardon those who sincerely turn back to Him in remorse and strive to follow His guidance. The verse ends by affirming two of Allah's key attributes - His vast knowledge and perfect wisdom. This conveys that Allah's guidance and commandments stem from His all-encompassing understanding and insight, and that following His directives is the wisest course of action for mankind.
orig: يريد الله ليبين لكم ويهديكم سنن الذين من قبلكم ويتوب عليكم والله عليم حكيم

translation: Allah wants to accept your repentance, but those who follow [their] passions want you to digress [into] a great deviation.
interpretation: This verse highlights the contrast between Allah's desire for humanity and the desires of those who are misguided by their passions. Allah, in His infinite mercy, wants to forgive and accept the repentance of His servants, guiding them towards the right path. On the other hand, those who are driven by their worldly desires and lusts seek to lead others astray, encouraging them to deviate significantly from the path of righteousness. This verse serves as a reminder for believers to be cautious of the influences that may lead them away from Allah's guidance and to always seek His forgiveness and mercy.
orig: والله يريد أن يتوب عليكم ويريد الذين يتبعون الشهوات أن تميلوا ميلا عظيما

translation: Allah intends to lighten for you [your difficulties]; and mankind was created weak.
interpretation: This verse highlights Allah's mercy and compassion towards His creation. He acknowledges the inherent weakness and limitations of human beings and thus, intends to ease their burdens and provide them with guidance and support. It serves as a reminder that Allah does not expect perfection from us, but rather, He is aware of our frailties and wants to help us navigate through life's challenges. The verse encourages us to turn to Allah for strength and guidance, recognizing that our own abilities are limited and that we are in constant need of His mercy and assistance.
orig: يريد الله أن يخفف عنكم وخلق الإنسان ضعيفا

translation: O you who have believed, do not consume one another's wealth unjustly but only [in lawful] business by mutual consent. And do not kill yourselves [or one another]. Indeed, Allah is to you ever Merciful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of fair and just economic transactions between individuals. It prohibits Muslims from wrongfully taking the wealth or property of others through unlawful means such as fraud, cheating, or coercion. The only permissible way to exchange wealth is through mutually agreed upon trade or business. The verse also forbids suicide and murder, as taking one's own life or the life of another is a grave sin. It reminds believers that Allah is merciful and compassionate, so they should treat each other with kindness and respect in all dealings.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا لا تأكلوا أموالكم بينكم بالباطل إلا أن تكون تجارة عن تراض منكم ولا تقتلوا أنفسكم إن الله كان بكم رحيما

translation: But whoever does that in aggression and injustice - then We will drive him into a Fire. And that, for Allah, is [always] easy.
interpretation: This verse serves as a stern warning to those who transgress the limits set by Allah and commit acts of aggression and injustice. It emphasizes that such individuals will face severe consequences for their actions in the form of being cast into the Fire of Hell. The verse also highlights the absolute power and authority of Allah, stating that punishing the wrongdoers is an easy matter for Him. This interpretation underscores the importance of adhering to the principles of justice and refraining from oppressing others, as doing so will incur the wrath of Allah and lead to a painful punishment in the Hereafter.
orig: ومن يفعل ذلك عدوانا وظلما فسوف نصليه نارا وكان ذلك على الله يسيرا

translation: If you avoid the major sins which you are forbidden, We will remove from you your lesser sins and admit you to a noble entrance [into Paradise].
interpretation: This verse conveys a powerful message of hope and encouragement for believers. It promises that if they abstain from the major sins that Allah has prohibited, He will forgive their minor sins and grant them entry into Paradise through a noble gate. This highlights the immense mercy and forgiveness of Allah, as well as the importance of striving to avoid the grave sins. It also shows that while all sins are displeasing to Allah, some are more severe than others. By staying away from the major transgressions, one can attain forgiveness and the great reward of Paradise. This should motivate the believers to be conscious of their actions and strive for righteousness.
orig: إن تجتنبوا كبائر ما تنهون عنه نكفر عنكم سيئاتكم وندخلكم مدخلا كريما

translation: And do not wish for that by which Allah has made some of you exceed others. For men is a share of what they have earned, and for women is a share of what they have earned. And ask Allah of his bounty. Indeed Allah is ever, of all things, Knowing.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of being content with what Allah has decreed for each individual, rather than envying others for what they have been given. It affirms that both men and women will be rewarded according to their own efforts and deeds, and that Allah's bounty is vast and He can grant it to whomever He wills. The verse encourages believers to turn to Allah in supplication and ask of His favor, acknowledging that He has perfect knowledge of all things and knows what is best for each person.
orig: ولا تتمنوا ما فضل الله به بعضكم على بعض للرجال نصيب مما اكتسبوا وللنساء نصيب مما اكتسبن واسألوا الله من فضله إن الله كان بكل شيء عليما

translation: And for all, We have made heirs to what is left by parents and relatives. And to those whom your oaths have bound [to you] - give them their share. Indeed Allah is ever, over all things, a Witness.
interpretation: This verse establishes the Islamic law of inheritance. It states that Allah has predetermined the rightful heirs of a deceased person's wealth, which includes their parents, relatives, and those with whom they had made a covenant or agreement. It emphasizes the importance of fulfilling these covenants and giving each heir their designated share of the inheritance. The verse also reminds us that Allah is always watching and is a witness to everything, including the distribution of inheritance and the fulfillment of oaths and covenants. This encourages Muslims to be just and fair in such matters, knowing that they will be held accountable by Allah for their actions.
orig: ولكل جعلنا موالي مما ترك الوالدان والأقربون والذين عقدت أيمانكم فآتوهم نصيبهم إن الله كان على كل شيء شهيدا

translation: Men are in charge of women by [right of] what Allah has given one over the other and what they spend [for maintenance] from their wealth. So righteous women are devoutly obedient, guarding in [the husband's] absence what Allah would have them guard. But those [wives] from whom you fear arrogance - [first] advise them; [then if they persist], forsake them in bed; and [finally], strike them. But if they obey you [once more], seek no means against them. Indeed, Allah is ever Exalted and Grand.
interpretation: This verse establishes the roles and responsibilities within a marriage in Islam. Men are given authority over women due to the qualities Allah has given them and their duty to financially support their wives. Righteous wives are described as obedient and faithful, protecting their honor and their husbands' interests in their absence. For wives who show egregious disobedience or disloyalty, a stepwise process is prescribed to the husband to discipline her - first through verbal counsel, then by suspending intimacy, and finally by striking in a manner not severe or injurious if the prior steps are ineffective. However, if she returns to obedience, the husband is commanded not to seek further action against her. The verse concludes by emphasizing Allah's supreme status, perhaps as a reminder to husbands not to abuse their authority, knowing Allah is above them.
orig: الرجال قوامون على النساء بما فضل الله بعضهم على بعض وبما أنفقوا من أموالهم فالصالحات قانتات حافظات للغيب بما حفظ الله واللاتي تخافون نشوزهن فعظوهن واهجروهن في المضاجع واضربوهن فإن أطعنكم فلا تبغوا عليهن سبيلا إن الله كان عليا كبيرا

translation: And if you fear dissension between the two, send an arbitrator from his people and an arbitrator from her people. If they both desire reconciliation, Allah will cause it between them. Indeed, Allah is ever Knowing and Acquainted [with all things].
interpretation: This verse provides guidance for resolving marital disputes. If there is a serious conflict between a husband and wife, and there is fear that it may lead to the breakdown of the marriage, then it is recommended to appoint arbitrators or mediators from both sides of the family. These arbitrators should be wise, trustworthy, and sincere in their efforts to reconcile the couple. If the husband and wife truly desire to resolve their differences and restore harmony in their relationship, then Allah will facilitate this reconciliation through the efforts of the arbitrators. This is because Allah is All-Knowing and fully aware of the intentions and actions of His servants. The verse emphasizes the importance of making every effort to save a marriage before resorting to divorce.
orig: وإن خفتم شقاق بينهما فابعثوا حكما من أهله وحكما من أهلها إن يريدا إصلاحا يوفق الله بينهما إن الله كان عليما خبيرا

translation: Worship Allah and associate nothing with Him, and to parents do good, and to relatives, orphans, the needy, the near neighbor, the neighbor farther away, the companion at your side, the traveler, and those whom your right hands possess. Indeed, Allah does not like those who are self-deluding and boastful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of worshipping Allah alone and avoiding shirk (associating partners with Him). It also highlights the significance of treating parents, relatives, orphans, the needy, neighbors, companions, and travelers with kindness and generosity. Additionally, it reminds Muslims to treat their servants or slaves ("those whom your right hands possess") with fairness and compassion. The verse concludes by stating that Allah dislikes those who are arrogant, boastful, and self-absorbed, as these traits are incompatible with true faith and righteousness.
orig: واعبدوا الله ولا تشركوا به شيئا وبالوالدين إحسانا وبذي القربى واليتامى والمساكين والجار ذي القربى والجار الجنب والصاحب بالجنب وابن السبيل وما ملكت أيمانكم إن الله لا يحب من كان مختالا فخورا

translation: Those who are stingy and enjoin upon [other] people stinginess and conceal what Allah has given them of His bounty - and We have prepared for the disbelievers a humiliating punishment.
interpretation: This verse is a strong condemnation of those who are miserly and encourage others to be miserly as well. It suggests that whatever wealth and blessings Allah has bestowed upon a person should be acknowledged and shared with others, not hoarded and concealed out of greed or selfishness. Doing so is tantamount to ingratitude and disbelief. The verse warns that those who are ungrateful and withhold Allah's blessings will face a degrading punishment in the Hereafter. It emphasizes the importance of generosity, charity and acknowledging the true source of our sustenance and blessings - Allah's favor and grace. Concealing and withholding these blessings is a form of denying Allah's bounty.
orig: الذين يبخلون ويأمرون الناس بالبخل ويكتمون ما آتاهم الله من فضله وأعتدنا للكافرين عذابا مهينا

translation: And [also] those who spend their wealth to be seen by people and believe not in Allah nor in the Last Day. And he to whom Satan is a companion - then evil is he as a companion.
interpretation: This verse is criticizing those who spend their wealth ostentatiously, only to gain praise and admiration from others, rather than out of sincere faith in Allah and belief in the Day of Judgment. It suggests that such people have taken Satan as their close companion, leading them astray from the righteous path. The verse implies that having Satan as a close associate is the worst kind of companionship one can have, as it will lead to evil and misguidance. It serves as a warning against hypocrisy, insincerity, and letting worldly desires dictate one's actions, instead of having genuine faith and seeking Allah's pleasure.
orig: والذين ينفقون أموالهم رئاء الناس ولا يؤمنون بالله ولا باليوم الآخر ومن يكن الشيطان له قرينا فساء قرينا

translation: And what [harm would come] upon them if they believed in Allah and the Last Day and spent out of what Allah provided for them? And Allah is ever, about them, Knowing.
interpretation: This verse is questioning why people do not believe in Allah and the Day of Judgment, and spend in charity from what Allah has provided them. It suggests that there would be no harm in doing so, and in fact it would be beneficial for them. The verse emphasizes that Allah is fully aware of their actions and intentions. It serves as an invitation and encouragement for people to have faith, and to be generous with their wealth in the way of Allah, reminding them that Allah knows what is in their hearts and will reward them accordingly.
orig: وماذا عليهم لو آمنوا بالله واليوم الآخر وأنفقوا مما رزقهم الله وكان الله بهم عليما

translation: Indeed, Allah does not do injustice, [even] as much as an atom's weight; while if there is a good deed, He multiplies it and gives from Himself a great reward.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's perfect justice and immense generosity. It assures us that Allah never wrongs anyone, not even by an atom's weight. He is absolutely just and fair in His judgment. Moreover, it highlights Allah's boundless mercy and grace. When someone does a good deed, even if it is small, Allah multiplies its reward many times over. He gives from Himself a tremendous reward, far greater than what the deed merits. This motivates the believer to do righteous deeds, even if they seem insignificant, with the knowledge that Allah will appreciate and reward their efforts abundantly. It instills hope and optimism, knowing that Allah's generosity knows no limits for those who seek to please Him.
orig: إن الله لا يظلم مثقال ذرة وإن تك حسنة يضاعفها ويؤت من لدنه أجرا عظيما

translation: And how [will it be] when We bring from every nation a witness and We bring you, [O Muhammad] against these [people] as a witness?
interpretation: This verse is describing the Day of Judgment, when Allah will bring forth a witness from every nation to testify about the deeds of their people. The witness will likely be a prophet or messenger sent to that nation. Additionally, Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) will be a witness over his nation, the Muslims. He will testify regarding their faith and deeds. This emphasizes the great responsibility the Prophet has, as well as the importance of following his teachings and example, since he will be a witness for or against us on that momentous Day. It also highlights the justice of Allah in judging people, as He will call forth witnesses to establish the truth of what nations and individuals did in this world.
orig: فكيف إذا جئنا من كل أمة بشهيد وجئنا بك على هؤلاء شهيدا

translation: On that Day, those who disbelieved and disobeyed the Messenger will wish that the earth were leveled with them. And they will not conceal from Allah a [single] statement.
interpretation: This verse is referring to the Day of Judgment, when the disbelievers and those who disobeyed the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) will face the consequences of their actions. They will be in such a state of despair and regret that they will wish the earth would swallow them up to escape the punishment. However, they will not be able to hide anything from Allah, as He is All-Knowing and All-Aware of their deeds and intentions. This verse serves as a warning to those who reject faith and encourages believers to stay steadfast in their obedience to Allah and His Messenger.
orig: يومئذ يود الذين كفروا وعصوا الرسول لو تسوى بهم الأرض ولا يكتمون الله حديثا

translation: O you who have believed, do not approach prayer while you are intoxicated until you know what you are saying or in a state of janabah, except those passing through [a place of prayer], until you have washed [your whole body]. And if you are ill or on a journey or one of you comes from the place of relieving himself or you have contacted women and find no water, then seek clean earth and wipe over your faces and your hands [with it]. Indeed, Allah is ever Pardoning and Forgiving.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of maintaining a state of purity and clear-mindedness when approaching prayer. It forbids Muslims from praying while intoxicated or in a state of ritual impurity (janabah) until they have regained sobriety or performed the necessary purification. The verse also provides alternatives for purification when water is unavailable, such as using clean earth for dry ablution (tayammum). This demonstrates Islam's practicality and flexibility in accommodating various circumstances while upholding the sanctity of prayer. The verse concludes by highlighting Allah's forgiving nature, emphasizing that He understands the challenges faced by believers and offers them mercy and forgiveness when they strive to follow His guidance.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا لا تقربوا الصلاة وأنتم سكارى حتى تعلموا ما تقولون ولا جنبا إلا عابري سبيل حتى تغتسلوا وإن كنتم مرضى أو على سفر أو جاء أحد منكم من الغائط أو لامستم النساء فلم تجدوا ماء فتيمموا صعيدا طيبا فامسحوا بوجوهكم وأيديكم إن الله كان عفوا غفورا

translation: Have you not seen those who were given a portion of the Scripture, purchasing error [in exchange for it] and wishing you would lose the way?
interpretation: This verse is criticizing those who, despite having received divine revelation, choose to deviate from the truth and lead others astray. They have been given knowledge and guidance through the scriptures, yet they "purchase error" by deliberately adopting misguided beliefs and practices. Not only do they go astray themselves, but they also desire to mislead others from the straight path of God's guidance. The verse is a warning against religious leaders and scholars who misuse their knowledge and influence to spread misguidance and corruption, rather than guiding people to the truth.
orig: ألم تر إلى الذين أوتوا نصيبا من الكتاب يشترون الضلالة ويريدون أن تضلوا السبيل

translation: And Allah is most knowing of your enemies; and sufficient is Allah as an ally, and sufficient is Allah as a helper.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah has complete knowledge of who our enemies are, both external and internal. We need not fear them or obsess over them, because Allah alone is sufficient as our protector and supporter. Trusting in Allah's knowledge, power and aid gives the believer peace of mind and confidence in the face of adversity. Allah is the best of allies and the most reliable of helpers. Relying on Him should be the believer's primary recourse in any difficulty.
orig: والله أعلم بأعدائكم وكفى بالله وليا وكفى بالله نصيرا

translation: Among the Jews are those who distort words from their [proper] usages and say, "We hear and disobey" and "Hear but be not heard" and "Ra'ina," twisting their tongues and defaming the religion. And if they had said [instead], "We hear and obey" and "Wait for us [to understand]," it would have been better for them and more suitable. But Allah has cursed them for their disbelief, so they believe not, except for a few.
interpretation: This verse highlights the dishonesty and disbelief of some Jews during the time of Prophet Muhammad. They would deliberately twist the meaning of words and use derogatory language to mock and insult the Prophet and the religion of Islam. The verse points out that if they had been sincere and respectful, saying "We hear and obey" and "Please wait for us to understand," it would have been better for them. However, due to their persistent disbelief and hostility towards the message of Islam, they have been cursed by Allah, and only a few among them truly believe.
orig: من الذين هادوا يحرفون الكلم عن مواضعه ويقولون سمعنا وعصينا واسمع غير مسمع وراعنا ليا بألسنتهم وطعنا في الدين ولو أنهم قالوا سمعنا وأطعنا واسمع وانظرنا لكان خيرا لهم وأقوم ولكن لعنهم الله بكفرهم فلا يؤمنون إلا قليلا

translation: O you who were given the Scripture, believe in what We have sent down [to Muhammad], confirming that which is with you, before We obliterate faces and turn them toward their backs or curse them as We cursed the sabbath-breakers. And ever is the decree of Allah accomplished.
interpretation: This verse is a call to the People of the Book (Jews and Christians) to believe in the message revealed to Prophet Muhammad, which confirms the truth they already possess in their scriptures. It warns them of severe consequences if they refuse to accept the truth, such as facing humiliation and being cursed by Allah, similar to the punishment faced by the sabbath-breakers among the Children of Israel. The verse emphasizes the certainty of Allah's decree and that His will shall always come to pass, reminding the People of the Book to heed this warning and embrace the final revelation sent to mankind.
orig: يا أيها الذين أوتوا الكتاب آمنوا بما نزلنا مصدقا لما معكم من قبل أن نطمس وجوها فنردها على أدبارها أو نلعنهم كما لعنا أصحاب السبت وكان أمر الله مفعولا

translation: Indeed, Allah does not forgive association with Him, but He forgives what is less than that for whom He wills. And he who associates others with Allah has certainly fabricated a tremendous sin.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the gravity of shirk, or associating partners with Allah, which is considered the greatest sin in Islam. It states that Allah will never forgive those who commit shirk, as it goes against the fundamental principle of tawhid (the oneness of Allah). However, Allah, in His infinite mercy, may forgive any other sin for whomever He wills. The verse also highlights the severity of shirk by describing it as a "tremendous sin," underscoring the importance of maintaining a pure monotheistic belief in Islam.
orig: إن الله لا يغفر أن يشرك به ويغفر ما دون ذلك لمن يشاء ومن يشرك بالله فقد افترى إثما عظيما

translation: Have you not seen those who claim purity for themselves? Rather, Allah purifies whom He wills, and injustice is not done to them, [even] as much as a thread [inside a date seed].
interpretation: This verse is a reminder that true purity and righteousness come from Allah alone, not from one's own claims or self-praise. It warns against the sin of self-righteousness and highlights the importance of humility before Allah. The verse emphasizes that Allah is the ultimate judge of who is truly pure and that He does not wrong anyone in the slightest. It encourages believers to seek Allah's purification and to avoid the arrogance of claiming purity for themselves.
orig: ألم تر إلى الذين يزكون أنفسهم بل الله يزكي من يشاء ولا يظلمون فتيلا

translation: See how they invent lies about Allah. And that is sufficient as a manifest sin.
interpretation: This verse is a strong condemnation of those who fabricate falsehoods and attribute them to Allah. It emphasizes that inventing lies about God is a grave and obvious sin. Falsely claiming something is from Allah, when it is not, is considered an act of disbelief and a major transgression. The verse warns that this sin alone is sufficient to warrant severe punishment, as it is an affront to Allah's truth and a corruption of His message. It cautions believers to be truthful about religious matters and not to engage in or spread religious disinformation, as doing so incurs Allah's wrath.
orig: انظر كيف يفترون على الله الكذب وكفى به إثما مبينا

translation: Have you not seen those who were given a portion of the Scripture, believing in Jibt and Taghut and saying to the disbelievers, "These are better guided than the believers as regards the way"?
interpretation: This verse is criticizing the hypocrisy and disbelief of some of the People of the Book (Jews and Christians) who, despite having knowledge of the truth from their scriptures, chose to believe in false gods and idols (Jibt and Taghut). Even worse, they proclaimed that the polytheist disbelievers were better guided than the Muslims who believed in the One True God. This shows how far they had strayed from the right path and aligned themselves with the enemies of faith and truth. It is a warning to Muslims not to follow their example but to hold fast to pure monotheism.
orig: ألم تر إلى الذين أوتوا نصيبا من الكتاب يؤمنون بالجبت والطاغوت ويقولون للذين كفروا هؤلاء أهدى من الذين آمنوا سبيلا

translation: Those are the ones whom Allah has cursed, and he whom Allah curses - never will you find for him a helper.
interpretation: This verse speaks to the fate of those who have earned Allah's condemnation through their actions and beliefs. When someone incurs the curse of Allah, it means they are cut off from His mercy and blessings. The verse emphasizes that for such individuals, there will be no one to help or support them. They will face the consequences of their misdeeds alone, without any aid or intercession. It serves as a warning that going against Allah's guidance leads to a state of loss and helplessness in this life and the next.
orig: أولئك الذين لعنهم الله ومن يلعن الله فلن تجد له نصيرا

translation: Or have they a share of dominion? Then [if that were so], they would not give the people [even as much as] the speck on a date seed.
interpretation: This verse is questioning whether the disbelievers have any share in the dominion or power that belongs to Allah alone. It suggests that if they did have such power, they would be miserly and not even give people the tiniest thing, described as the speck on a date seed. The interpretation is that complete authority and power belong to Allah, and those who reject His signs have no share in it whatsoever. It also highlights the stinginess and greed of those who ascribe partners to Allah, showing that even if they hypothetically had power, they would not be generous towards others.
orig: أم لهم نصيب من الملك فإذا لا يؤتون الناس نقيرا

translation: Or do they envy people for what Allah has given them of His bounty? But we had already given the family of Abraham the Scripture and wisdom and conferred upon them a great kingdom.
interpretation: This verse is addressing the envy and resentment that some people harbor towards others who have been blessed by Allah with certain favors or bounties. It reminds us that Allah bestows His blessings and gifts upon whomever He chooses, and it is not for us to question or envy those whom He has favored. The verse gives the example of the family of Prophet Abraham, who were granted the great blessings of divine scripture, wisdom, and a mighty kingdom. This suggests that the blessings and favors that Allah grants to some people are a part of His divine wisdom and plan, and we should accept and appreciate them rather than resenting or envying those who have received them. The verse encourages us to focus on our own spiritual growth and relationship with Allah, rather than comparing ourselves to others or coveting what they have been given.
orig: أم يحسدون الناس على ما آتاهم الله من فضله فقد آتينا آل إبراهيم الكتاب والحكمة وآتيناهم ملكا عظيما

translation: And among them are those who believed in it, and among them are those who turned away from it. And sufficient is Hell as a blaze.
interpretation: This verse highlights the divergent responses of people to the message of Islam. Some people embraced faith and believed in the divine message, while others rejected it and turned away from the truth. The mention of Hell as a "blaze" serves as a stern warning to those who consciously choose to reject faith, emphasizing that their ultimate destination will be the torment of Hellfire. It underscores the gravity of the consequences of denying the truth and the importance of making the right choice in accepting the guidance provided by Allah.
orig: فمنهم من آمن به ومنهم من صد عنه وكفى بجهنم سعيرا

translation: Indeed, those who disbelieve in Our verses - We will drive them into a Fire. Every time their skins are roasted through We will replace them with other skins so they may taste the punishment. Indeed, Allah is ever Exalted in Might and Wise.
interpretation: This verse is a stern warning to those who reject Allah's signs and revelations. It highlights the severe and everlasting nature of the punishment in Hell, where the disbelievers will be burned in a blazing Fire. The verse emphasizes the intensity of the torment by mentioning that every time their skins are burnt off, Allah will replace them with new skins so that they can continue to feel the pain and agony. This replacement of skins underscores the eternal nature of the punishment. The verse concludes by affirming two of Allah's attributes - His Might and Wisdom. It implies that Allah is capable of inflicting such punishment and that it is a manifestation of His wisdom and justice, as the disbelievers chose to reject His guidance and signs despite the clear proofs and warnings sent to them.
orig: إن الذين كفروا بآياتنا سوف نصليهم نارا كلما نضجت جلودهم بدلناهم جلودا غيرها ليذوقوا العذاب إن الله كان عزيزا حكيما

translation: And those who believe and do righteous deeds, We will admit them to gardens beneath which rivers flow, wherein they abide forever. For them therein are purified spouses, and We will admit them to deepening shade.
interpretation: This verse promises the believers who do good deeds that they will be admitted to Paradise, where they will live eternally. In Paradise, they will have pure spouses, untouched by any impurity or indecency. They will also enjoy "deepening shade" which represents the complete comfort, peace, and protection they will experience, free from any discomfort or hardship. This shade is a metaphor for Allah's mercy, grace and favor upon the believers in the life to come, providing them with an abode of ultimate tranquility and satisfaction as a reward for their faith and righteousness.
orig: والذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات سندخلهم جنات تجري من تحتها الأنهار خالدين فيها أبدا لهم فيها أزواج مطهرة وندخلهم ظلا ظليلا

translation: Indeed, Allah commands you to render trusts to whom they are due and when you judge between people to judge with justice. Excellent is that which Allah instructs you. Indeed, Allah is ever Hearing and Seeing.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of fulfilling trusts and being just in one's judgments. It reminds believers that Allah is always watching and listening, and that they should strive to act in a way that pleases Him. The verse encourages people to be trustworthy and fair in their dealings with others, as this is what Allah commands. It also highlights the idea that Allah's instructions are always good and beneficial for humanity, and that following them will lead to the best outcomes in this life and the next.
orig: إن الله يأمركم أن تؤدوا الأمانات إلى أهلها وإذا حكمتم بين الناس أن تحكموا بالعدل إن الله نعما يعظكم به إن الله كان سميعا بصيرا

translation: O you who have believed, obey Allah and obey the Messenger and those in authority among you. And if you disagree over anything, refer it to Allah and the Messenger, if you should believe in Allah and the Last Day. That is the best [way] and best in result.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of obedience to Allah, His Messenger, and those in authority among the believers. It establishes a hierarchy of authority and a means for resolving disputes within the Muslim community. When disagreements arise, Muslims are instructed to refer the matter back to the Qur'an and the teachings of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) for guidance. This demonstrates that the ultimate authority lies with Allah and His Messenger, not with any individual or group. The verse also highlights the importance of belief in Allah and the Day of Judgment as the basis for this obedience and system of conflict resolution. Following this divinely ordained process is described as the best way and the one that leads to the best outcome, both in this world and the Hereafter.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا أطيعوا الله وأطيعوا الرسول وأولي الأمر منكم فإن تنازعتم في شيء فردوه إلى الله والرسول إن كنتم تؤمنون بالله واليوم الآخر ذلك خير وأحسن تأويلا

translation: Have you not seen those who claim to have believed in what was revealed to you, [O Muhammad], and what was revealed before you? They wish to refer legislation to Taghut, while they were commanded to reject it; and Satan wishes to lead them far astray.
interpretation: This verse is criticizing the hypocrites who outwardly professed belief in the revelation sent to Muhammad and the earlier prophets, yet they still sought judgment from false authorities and idols (taghut) instead of the divine law. Despite being commanded to reject such false sources of authority, they were tempted by Satan to gravely deviate from the straight path of true faith and obedience to God alone. It highlights the importance of fully submitting to God's law and revelation, and the dangers of partial faith mixed with the following of misguided desires and illegitimate authorities that oppose divine guidance.
orig: ألم تر إلى الذين يزعمون أنهم آمنوا بما أنزل إليك وما أنزل من قبلك يريدون أن يتحاكموا إلى الطاغوت وقد أمروا أن يكفروا به ويريد الشيطان أن يضلهم ضلالا بعيدا

translation: And when it is said to them, "Come to what Allah has revealed and to the Messenger," you see the hypocrites turning away from you in aversion.
interpretation: This verse highlights the attitude of the hypocrites towards the divine message and the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him). When they are invited to follow the teachings of the Qur'an and the guidance of the Prophet, they turn away in aversion and rejection. This behavior reveals their true nature as hypocrites, as they outwardly claim to be believers but inwardly harbor doubt, disbelief, and a lack of commitment to the Islamic faith. The verse emphasizes the importance of sincere faith and obedience to Allah and His Messenger, exposing the hypocrisy of those who refuse to embrace the truth when it is presented to them.
orig: وإذا قيل لهم تعالوا إلى ما أنزل الله وإلى الرسول رأيت المنافقين يصدون عنك صدودا

translation: How [will it be] when disaster strikes them because of what their hands have put forth and then they come to you swearing by Allah, "We intended nothing but good conduct and accommodation."
interpretation: This verse is referring to the hypocrites who, when faced with the consequences of their own misdeeds and wrongdoings, come to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) swearing by Allah that their intentions were pure and good. However, their actions belie their words. The interpretation is that mere words and oaths are not sufficient if one's actions are contrary to them. It is a reminder that ultimately, people will be held accountable for their deeds, and insincere words or excuses will not avail them in front of Allah. The verse emphasizes the importance of aligning one's actions with their claimed intentions and beliefs.
orig: فكيف إذا أصابتهم مصيبة بما قدمت أيديهم ثم جاءوك يحلفون بالله إن أردنا إلا إحسانا وتوفيقا

translation: Those are the ones of whom Allah knows what is in their hearts, so turn away from them but admonish them and speak to them a far-reaching word.
interpretation: This verse is directing the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) on how to deal with the hypocrites who outwardly profess Islam but inwardly harbor doubts and ill intentions. Allah knows the secrets within their hearts, so the Prophet is instructed to turn away from them, meaning not to trust or rely on them. However, he is still to admonish them, advising them to be sincere in their faith and mend their ways. When speaking to them, he should use impactful and eloquent words that will reach into their souls and stir their conscience. The "far-reaching word" refers to meaningful and wise speech that will leave a lasting effect on the listener. This guidance applies to anyone in a position of leadership or authority - to be aware of those who are insincere, not to be taken in by outward appearances, yet still try to council and reform them with words of wisdom.
orig: أولئك الذين يعلم الله ما في قلوبهم فأعرض عنهم وعظهم وقل لهم في أنفسهم قولا بليغا

translation: We sent no messenger but to be obeyed by Allah's leave. If, when they wronged themselves, they had come to you and asked forgiveness of Allah and the Messenger had asked forgiveness for them, they would have found Allah Forgiving, Merciful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of obedience to the messengers sent by Allah and seeking forgiveness through them. It suggests that if people who have wronged themselves sincerely turn to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and seek Allah's forgiveness, and if the Prophet also prays for their forgiveness, they will find Allah to be Forgiving and Merciful. This highlights the role of the Prophet as an intercessor and the significance of repentance and seeking forgiveness directly from Allah through the guidance of His messengers.
orig: وما أرسلنا من رسول إلا ليطاع بإذن الله ولو أنهم إذ ظلموا أنفسهم جاءوك فاستغفروا الله واستغفر لهم الرسول لوجدوا الله توابا رحيما

translation: But no, by your Lord, they will not [truly] believe until they make you, [O Muhammad], judge concerning that over which they dispute among themselves and then find within themselves no discomfort from what you have judged and submit in [full, willing] submission.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of accepting the Prophet Muhammad's judgement and authority in all matters. It suggests that true faith is not merely a verbal declaration, but a state of complete submission to God's messenger. Believers are expected to wholeheartedly accept the Prophet's decisions without any reservations or doubts, even if it goes against their personal inclinations or desires. This unconditional obedience and willingness to submit to the Prophet's judgement is presented as a necessary condition for genuine faith in Islam.
orig: فلا وربك لا يؤمنون حتى يحكموك فيما شجر بينهم ثم لا يجدوا في أنفسهم حرجا مما قضيت ويسلموا تسليما

translation: And if We had decreed upon them, "Kill yourselves" or "Leave your homes," they would not have done it, except for a few of them. But if they had done what they were instructed, it would have been better for them and a firmer position [for them in faith].
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of obedience to Allah's commands, even if they seem difficult or against one's desires. It suggests that if Allah had commanded the people to do something as extreme as taking their own lives or abandoning their homes, most would not have complied. However, if they had obeyed the teachings and instructions given to them, it would have strengthened their faith and been ultimately better for them in this life and the hereafter. The verse emphasizes the value of submission to Allah's will and following the guidance provided through divine revelation and prophetic teachings, as this leads to spiritual growth, stability, and success.
orig: ولو أنا كتبنا عليهم أن اقتلوا أنفسكم أو اخرجوا من دياركم ما فعلوه إلا قليل منهم ولو أنهم فعلوا ما يوعظون به لكان خيرا لهم وأشد تثبيتا

translation: And then We would have given them from Us a great reward.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the immense generosity and mercy of Allah towards His servants. Had the disbelievers followed the guidance sent by Allah and obeyed His commands, He would have bestowed upon them a magnificent reward from His infinite treasures. This reward could be in the form of both worldly blessings and the ultimate bliss of Paradise in the Hereafter. The verse encourages believers to stay steadfast in their faith and obedience to Allah, knowing that their sincere efforts will be greatly compensated by their Lord. It also serves as an invitation to those who have gone astray, showing them the path to attain Allah's pleasure and the great bounties that await the righteous.
orig: وإذا لآتيناهم من لدنا أجرا عظيما

translation: And We would have guided them to a straight path.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's willingness to guide mankind to the straight path - the path of righteousness and truth that leads to success in this world and the Hereafter. It implies that guidance is a divine gift and blessing from Allah, and He is ever ready to bestow it upon those who sincerely seek it. The straight path refers to the way of life prescribed by Islam, which is based on the teachings of the Qur'an and the Sunnah of Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him). Following this path with sincerity and devotion ensures one's well-being, spiritual growth, and attainment of Allah's pleasure and Paradise.
orig: ولهديناهم صراطا مستقيما

translation: And whoever obeys Allah and the Messenger - those will be with the ones upon whom Allah has bestowed favor of the prophets, the steadfast affirmers of truth, the martyrs and the righteous. And excellent are those as companions.
interpretation: This verse promises a great reward for those who obey Allah and His Messenger (ﷺ). It indicates that such obedient servants will be in the company of the most exalted people in Paradise - the prophets, the most truthful and sincere, those who witnessed for the truth and were martyred in Allah's cause, and the pious and righteous believers. This signifies the lofty status and honor that Allah grants to His obedient servants in the Hereafter. Being in the company of these illustrious personalities and sharing in their blessings is indeed a tremendous blessing and favor from Allah. The verse emphasizes that these are the best companions one could ever hope for in eternal life.
orig: ومن يطع الله والرسول فأولئك مع الذين أنعم الله عليهم من النبيين والصديقين والشهداء والصالحين وحسن أولئك رفيقا

translation: That is the bounty from Allah, and sufficient is Allah as Knower.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that all blessings, favors, and bounties come from Allah alone. It is His grace and generosity that bestows upon His servants whatever they have. The verse also highlights Allah's attribute of being All-Knowing, implying that He knows what is best for His creation and grants them accordingly. It serves as a reminder for believers to be grateful to Allah for His endless favors and to seek His pleasure in all their endeavors, acknowledging that He is the source of all goodness in their lives.
orig: ذلك الفضل من الله وكفى بالله عليما

translation: O you who have believed, take your precaution and [either] go forth in companies or go forth all together.
interpretation: This verse is calling upon the believers to be vigilant and prepared in the face of their enemies. It instructs them to take necessary precautions and to mobilize themselves, either in smaller groups or as a united force, to defend themselves and their faith. The underlying message is one of readiness, unity, and willingness to fight for the cause of Islam when necessary. It emphasizes the importance of being proactive in the face of threats and challenges, rather than being caught off guard or divided. The verse also implies a sense of collective responsibility among the believers to protect and support one another in times of need.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا خذوا حذركم فانفروا ثبات أو انفروا جميعا

translation: And indeed, there is among you he who lingers behind; and if disaster strikes you, he says, "Allah has favored me in that I was not present with them."
interpretation: This verse is referring to the hypocrites who lag behind when called to fight in the way of Allah. They are reluctant to join the believers in their struggle and make excuses to avoid participating. If the believers face any hardship or defeat, these hypocrites express their relief and satisfaction at not being present with them, considering it a favor from Allah. This attitude reveals their true nature and lack of commitment to the cause of Islam. The verse exposes their insincerity and the weakness of their faith.
orig: وإن منكم لمن ليبطئن فإن أصابتكم مصيبة قال قد أنعم الله علي إذ لم أكن معهم شهيدا

translation: And if bounty comes to you from Allah, he would surely say, as if there had never been between you and him any affection, "Oh, I wish I had been with them so I could have attained a great attainment."
interpretation: This verse is referring to the hypocrites who, when they see the believers blessed with bounty from Allah, such as victory or spoils of war, wish that they had been with the believers so that they too could have shared in the rewards. They say this even though previously there had been no real bond of affection or loyalty between them and the believers. Their statement exposes their opportunistic attitude and lack of sincere faith. They are only interested in worldly gains rather than true devotion to Allah's cause. The verse highlights the insincerity and self-interest of those who claim to be believers but lack true commitment.
orig: ولئن أصابكم فضل من الله ليقولن كأن لم تكن بينكم وبينه مودة يا ليتني كنت معهم فأفوز فوزا عظيما

translation: So let those fight in the cause of Allah who sell the life of this world for the Hereafter. And he who fights in the cause of Allah and is killed or achieves victory - We will bestow upon him a great reward.
interpretation: This verse encourages believers to fight in the way of Allah, sacrificing the temporary pleasures of this worldly life for the eternal rewards of the Hereafter. It promises that those who fight for Allah's cause, whether they are martyred or achieve victory, will be granted a magnificent reward by Allah. This interpretation highlights the importance of selflessness, devotion, and willingness to make sacrifices for the sake of one's faith and the promise of divine recompense for those who do so.
orig: فليقاتل في سبيل الله الذين يشرون الحياة الدنيا بالآخرة ومن يقاتل في سبيل الله فيقتل أو يغلب فسوف نؤتيه أجرا عظيما

translation: And what is [the matter] with you that you fight not in the cause of Allah and [for] the oppressed among men, women, and children who say, "Our Lord, take us out of this city of oppressive people and appoint for us from Yourself a protector and appoint for us from Yourself a helper?"
interpretation: This verse is encouraging the believers to fight in the way of Allah and to defend the oppressed, including men, women, and children who are suffering under tyrannical rule. They are crying out to Allah to save them from their oppressors and to provide them with a protector and helper. The verse emphasizes the importance of standing up against injustice and oppression, and seeking Allah's help and support in doing so. It also highlights the responsibility of the believers towards the vulnerable and oppressed members of society.
orig: وما لكم لا تقاتلون في سبيل الله والمستضعفين من الرجال والنساء والولدان الذين يقولون ربنا أخرجنا من هذه القرية الظالم أهلها واجعل لنا من لدنك وليا واجعل لنا من لدنك نصيرا

translation: Those who have believed fight in the cause of Allah, and those who disbelieve fight in the cause of Taghut. So fight against the allies of Satan. Indeed, the plot of Satan has ever been weak.
interpretation: This verse draws a clear distinction between the believers and disbelievers in terms of what they fight for. The believers fight for the sake of Allah and in His cause, which is truth and justice, while the disbelievers fight for the sake of false deities and powers (taghut), which are in essence the allies of Satan. The verse encourages the believers to fight against these allies of Satan, reassuring them that Satan's plots and schemes are ultimately weak and destined to fail in the face of unwavering faith and righteousness. It highlights the eternal struggle between good and evil, with the believers standing firm on the side of truth against the deceptive forces of falsehood.
orig: الذين آمنوا يقاتلون في سبيل الله والذين كفروا يقاتلون في سبيل الطاغوت فقاتلوا أولياء الشيطان إن كيد الشيطان كان ضعيفا
