translation: Have you not seen those who were told, "Restrain your hands [from fighting] and establish prayer and give zakah"? But then when fighting was ordained for them, at once a party of them feared men as they fear Allah or with [even] greater fear. They said, "Our Lord, why have You decreed upon us fighting? If only You had postponed [it for] us for a short time." Say, "The enjoyment of this world is little, and the Hereafter is better for he who fears Allah. And injustice will not be done to you, [even] as much as a thread [inside a date seed].
interpretation: This verse is addressing those who were initially reluctant to fight in the cause of Allah, preferring to focus on prayer and charity. However, when fighting was made obligatory upon them, some of them became fearful of the enemy, even more than they feared Allah. They questioned Allah's decree and wished for the fighting to be postponed. The verse reminds them that the pleasures of this worldly life are fleeting and that the rewards of the Hereafter are far superior for those who are righteous and obedient to Allah. It also assures them that Allah will not allow any injustice to be done to them, even in the slightest amount.
orig: ألم تر إلى الذين قيل لهم كفوا أيديكم وأقيموا الصلاة وآتوا الزكاة فلما كتب عليهم القتال إذا فريق منهم يخشون الناس كخشية الله أو أشد خشية وقالوا ربنا لم كتبت علينا القتال لولا أخرتنا إلى أجل قريب قل متاع الدنيا قليل والآخرة خير لمن اتقى ولا تظلمون فتيلا

translation: Wherever you may be, death will overtake you, even if you should be within towers of lofty construction. But if good comes to them, they say, "This is from Allah"; and if evil befalls them, they say, "This is from you." Say, "All [things] are from Allah." So what is [the matter] with those people that they can hardly understand any statement?
interpretation: This verse reminds us of the inevitability of death, regardless of our circumstances or perceived safety. It also highlights how people often attribute good fortune to Allah, while blaming misfortune on others, such as the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him). However, the verse emphasizes that all things, both good and bad, ultimately come from Allah. It suggests that some people lack the understanding to grasp this concept fully, and may struggle to comprehend the true nature of divine will and decree.
orig: أينما تكونوا يدرككم الموت ولو كنتم في بروج مشيدة وإن تصبهم حسنة يقولوا هذه من عند الله وإن تصبهم سيئة يقولوا هذه من عندك قل كل من عند الله فمال هؤلاء القوم لا يكادون يفقهون حديثا

translation: What comes to you of good is from Allah, but what comes to you of evil, [O man], is from yourself. And We have sent you, [O Muhammad], to the people as a messenger, and sufficient is Allah as Witness.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that all the good and blessings in one's life come from Allah's grace and mercy, while the evil and misfortunes are a result of one's own actions and choices. It also affirms Prophet Muhammad's role as a messenger to humanity, sent by Allah to guide them towards the right path. The verse concludes by stating that Allah is sufficient as a witness to the truth of Muhammad's prophethood and the divine message he conveyed.
orig: ما أصابك من حسنة فمن الله وما أصابك من سيئة فمن نفسك وأرسلناك للناس رسولا وكفى بالله شهيدا

translation: Whoever obeys the Messenger has obeyed Allah; but those who turn away - We have not sent you over them as a guardian.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of obeying the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) as it is equivalent to obeying Allah. It also clarifies that the Prophet's role is not to force people to follow the message, but rather to convey it clearly. The responsibility of accepting or rejecting the message lies with each individual, and the Prophet is not accountable for their choices. This highlights the concept of free will in Islam and the absence of compulsion in accepting the faith.
orig: من يطع الرسول فقد أطاع الله ومن تولى فما أرسلناك عليهم حفيظا

translation: They say, "[We pledge] obedience." But when they leave you, a group of them spend the night determining [to do] other than what you say. But Allah records what they plan by night. So leave them alone and rely upon Allah. And sufficient is Allah as Disposer of affairs.
interpretation: This verse reveals the hypocrisy of some people who outwardly pledge obedience to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him), but secretly plot against him and his teachings. It emphasizes that Allah is fully aware of their schemes, even those hatched in the darkness of night. The Prophet is advised to disregard their treachery, put his trust completely in Allah, and rely on Him alone. It highlights the sufficiency of Allah as the One who manages all affairs and protects those who sincerely believe in Him, rendering the plots of the hypocrites ultimately futile.
orig: ويقولون طاعة فإذا برزوا من عندك بيت طائفة منهم غير الذي تقول والله يكتب ما يبيتون فأعرض عنهم وتوكل على الله وكفى بالله وكيلا

translation: Then do they not reflect upon the Qur'an? If it had been from [any] other than Allah, they would have found within it much contradiction.
interpretation: This verse is a challenge to those who doubt the divine origin of the Qur'an. It asks them to deeply ponder and reflect upon the Qur'an, for if it had been authored by anyone other than Allah, they would have surely found within it many inconsistencies and contradictions. The fact that the Qur'an is free from any discrepancies, despite being revealed over a period of 23 years and discussing a wide range of subjects, is a testament to its divine authorship. The coherence and consistency of the Qur'anic message is a proof that it could not have been the product of human imagination, but rather a revelation from the All-Wise Creator.
orig: أفلا يتدبرون القرآن ولو كان من عند غير الله لوجدوا فيه اختلافا كثيرا

translation: And when there comes to them information about [public] security or fear, they spread it around. But if they had referred it back to the Messenger or to those of authority among them, then the ones who [can] draw correct conclusions from it would have known about it. And if not for the favor of Allah upon you and His mercy, you would have followed Satan, except for a few.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of verifying information before spreading it, especially in matters concerning public security or fear. It suggests that spreading unverified information can lead to unnecessary panic and chaos. Instead, one should refer such matters to the appropriate authorities, such as the Prophet (in the context of the verse) or those in positions of leadership, who have the wisdom and ability to properly assess the situation and draw correct conclusions. The verse also highlights the role of Allah's favor and mercy in guiding believers towards the right path and protecting them from the influence of Satan, except for a few who may still follow his temptations.
orig: وإذا جاءهم أمر من الأمن أو الخوف أذاعوا به ولو ردوه إلى الرسول وإلى أولي الأمر منهم لعلمه الذين يستنبطونه منهم ولولا فضل الله عليكم ورحمته لاتبعتم الشيطان إلا قليلا

translation: So fight in the cause of Allah; you are not held responsible except for yourself. And encourage the believers [to join you] that perhaps Allah will restrain the [military] might of those who disbelieve. And Allah is greater in might and stronger in [exemplary] punishment.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of individual responsibility in fighting for the cause of Allah. Each person is accountable for their own actions and should not be burdened by the actions or inactions of others. The verse also encourages the believers to join in the fight, with the hope that Allah will help them overcome the military might of the disbelievers. It reminds us that Allah is the most powerful and can inflict the strongest punishment on those who oppose Him and His cause. This highlights the significance of having faith and trust in Allah's support and victory, even in the face of seemingly overwhelming odds.
orig: فقاتل في سبيل الله لا تكلف إلا نفسك وحرض المؤمنين عسى الله أن يكف بأس الذين كفروا والله أشد بأسا وأشد تنكيلا

translation: Whoever intercedes for a good cause will have a share in its reward, and whoever intercedes for an evil cause will have a share in its burden. And ever is Allah, over all things, a Keeper.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the concept of individual responsibility and the far-reaching consequences of one's actions. It encourages people to actively promote good and righteousness, as they will be rewarded for their efforts in supporting virtuous causes. Conversely, it warns against advocating for or facilitating evil deeds, as those who do so will bear a portion of the blame and punishment. The verse also highlights Allah's omnipotence and His role as the ultimate overseer and judge of all matters, ensuring that justice will prevail and that everyone will be held accountable for their actions and intentions.
orig: من يشفع شفاعة حسنة يكن له نصيب منها ومن يشفع شفاعة سيئة يكن له كفل منها وكان الله على كل شيء مقيتا

translation: And when you are greeted with a greeting, greet [in return] with one better than it or [at least] return it [in a like manner]. Indeed, Allah is ever, over all things, an Accountant.
interpretation: This verse encourages Muslims to respond to greetings in a better manner or at least return the same greeting. It promotes kindness, respect, and good manners in social interactions. The verse also reminds believers that Allah is always watching and keeping account of their actions, emphasizing the importance of treating others well and being mindful of one's behavior. This teaching fosters a positive and harmonious society where people treat each other with courtesy and respect.
orig: وإذا حييتم بتحية فحيوا بأحسن منها أو ردوها إن الله كان على كل شيء حسيبا

translation: Allah - there is no deity except Him. He will surely assemble you for [account on] the Day of Resurrection, about which there is no doubt. And who is more truthful than Allah in statement.
interpretation: This verse affirms the fundamental Islamic belief in the oneness of Allah and that there is no god worthy of worship except Him alone. It also asserts with certainty that Allah will resurrect all of humanity to hold them accountable for their deeds on the Day of Judgment. This is an unequivocal promise from Allah, and there can be no statement more truthful than Allah's word, as He is the ultimate source of all truth. The verse emphasizes having complete trust in Allah's promise of resurrection and the importance of living this life in preparation for that inevitable event.
orig: الله لا إله إلا هو ليجمعنكم إلى يوم القيامة لا ريب فيه ومن أصدق من الله حديثا

translation: What is [the matter] with you [that you are] two groups concerning the hypocrites, while Allah has made them fall back [into error and disbelief] for what they earned. Do you wish to guide those whom Allah has sent astray? And he whom Allah sends astray - never will you find for him a way [of guidance].
interpretation: This verse is addressing the believers who were divided in their opinion about the hypocrites who outwardly professed Islam but inwardly harbored disbelief. It rebukes those who were inclined to excuse the hypocrites or defend them, reminding that Allah Himself has turned the hypocrites back to disbelief because of their evil deeds and inner doubts. It emphasizes that once Allah has decreed someone to be astray due to their own choices and actions, no one can guide them back to the right path. The believers should not be confused or conflicted about the status of the hypocrites, but rather trust Allah's judgment about them.
orig: فما لكم في المنافقين فئتين والله أركسهم بما كسبوا أتريدون أن تهدوا من أضل الله ومن يضلل الله فلن تجد له سبيلا

translation: They wish you would disbelieve as they disbelieved so you would be alike. So do not take from among them allies until they emigrate for the cause of Allah. But if they turn away, then seize them and kill them wherever you find them and take not from among them any ally or helper.
interpretation: This verse is warning the believers not to take the disbelievers as allies or protectors, unless they sincerely repent and emigrate for the sake of Allah. If they turn away from this and remain in a state of disbelief and enmity, then the believers are commanded to seize them and kill them wherever they are found, and to completely disavow any alliance or support for them. The verse emphasizes the severity of allying with the disbelievers and the importance of cutting ties with those who are hostile to Islam, while leaving the door open for them to repent and join the believers. It establishes a clear distinction between the camp of faith and the camp of disbelief.
orig: ودوا لو تكفرون كما كفروا فتكونون سواء فلا تتخذوا منهم أولياء حتى يهاجروا في سبيل الله فإن تولوا فخذوهم واقتلوهم حيث وجدتموهم ولا تتخذوا منهم وليا ولا نصيرا

translation: Except those who join a group between whom and you there is a treaty (of peace), or those who approach you with hearts restraining them from fighting you as well as fighting their own people. If Allah had pleased, He could have given them power over you, and they would have fought you: Therefore if they withdraw from you but fight you not, and (instead) send you (Guarantees of) peace, then Allah Hath opened no way for you (to war against them).
interpretation: This verse provides an exception to the general command to fight the disbelievers. It states that Muslims should not fight those who have a peace treaty with them, or those who come to them with no intention of fighting, either against the Muslims or their own people. If Allah had willed, He could have given these people power over the Muslims, but He did not. So if they refrain from fighting and offer peace, the Muslims have no justification to fight them, as Allah has not given them permission to do so in this case. The verse emphasizes the importance of honoring treaties and maintaining peaceful relations with those who seek peace, even if they are not Muslims.
orig: إلا الذين يصلون إلى قوم بينكم وبينهم ميثاق أو جاءوكم حصرت صدورهم أن يقاتلوكم أو يقاتلوا قومهم ولو شاء الله لسلطهم عليكم فلقاتلوكم فإن اعتزلوكم فلم يقاتلوكم وألقوا إليكم السلم فما جعل الله لكم عليهم سبيلا

translation: You will find others who wish to obtain security from you and [to] obtain security from their people. Every time they are returned to [the influence of] disbelief, they fall back into it. So if they do not withdraw from you or offer you peace or restrain their hands, then seize them and kill them wherever you overtake them. And those - We have made for you against them a clear authorization.
interpretation: This verse refers to the hypocrites who pretend to be Muslims but secretly support the enemies of Islam. They seek security from both sides, the Muslims and their own people, but whenever they have the opportunity, they revert back to their disbelief and hostility towards Islam. The verse instructs Muslims to deal firmly with such people if they do not cease their hostility, refuse to make peace, and continue to pose a threat. In such cases, Muslims are permitted to seize and kill them wherever they are found, as a clear divine sanction against their treachery and aggression.
orig: ستجدون آخرين يريدون أن يأمنوكم ويأمنوا قومهم كل ما ردوا إلى الفتنة أركسوا فيها فإن لم يعتزلوكم ويلقوا إليكم السلم ويكفوا أيديهم فخذوهم واقتلوهم حيث ثقفتموهم وأولئكم جعلنا لكم عليهم سلطانا مبينا

translation: And never is it for a believer to kill a believer except by mistake. And whoever kills a believer by mistake - then the freeing of a believing slave and a compensation payment presented to the deceased's family [is required] unless they give [up their right as] charity. But if the deceased was from a people at war with you and he was a believer - then [only] the freeing of a believing slave; and if he was from a people with whom you have a treaty - then a compensation payment presented to his family and the freeing of a believing slave. And whoever does not find [one or cannot afford to buy one] - then [instead], a fast for two months consecutively, [seeking] acceptance of repentance from Allah. And Allah is ever Knowing and Wise.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the sanctity of a believer's life and the gravity of taking it unjustly, even by mistake. It prescribes the expiation and compensation required if a believer accidentally kills another believer. The offender must free a believing slave and pay blood money to the victim's family, unless they charitably forgo it. If the victim was from an enemy people, then only freeing a believing slave is necessary. If from a people with a treaty, then blood money is paid to the family in addition to freeing a slave. If the offender cannot afford a slave, they must fast two consecutive months sincerely repenting to Allah. This highlights the value of a believer's life, encourages careful and peaceful conduct, and provides a means to compensate the victim's family and expiate the sin in the sight of Allah, the All-Knowing and All-Wise.
orig: وما كان لمؤمن أن يقتل مؤمنا إلا خطأ ومن قتل مؤمنا خطأ فتحرير رقبة مؤمنة ودية مسلمة إلى أهله إلا أن يصدقوا فإن كان من قوم عدو لكم وهو مؤمن فتحرير رقبة مؤمنة وإن كان من قوم بينكم وبينهم ميثاق فدية مسلمة إلى أهله وتحرير رقبة مؤمنة فمن لم يجد فصيام شهرين متتابعين توبة من الله وكان الله عليما حكيما

translation: But whoever kills a believer intentionally - his recompense is Hell, wherein he will abide eternally, and Allah has become angry with him and has cursed him and has prepared for him a great punishment.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the severity and gravity of intentionally killing a believer. It states that the punishment for such a heinous act is eternal damnation in Hell, incurring the wrath, curse, and severe punishment from Allah. This highlights the sanctity of human life, particularly that of a believer, and serves as a powerful deterrent against murder. The verse underscores the idea that taking a life unjustly is one of the gravest sins in Islam, warranting the harshest punishment in the Hereafter.
orig: ومن يقتل مؤمنا متعمدا فجزاؤه جهنم خالدا فيها وغضب الله عليه ولعنه وأعد له عذابا عظيما

translation: O you who have believed, when you go forth [to fight] in the cause of Allah, investigate; and do not say to one who gives you [a greeting of] peace "You are not a believer," aspiring for the goods of worldly life; for with Allah are many acquisitions. You [yourselves] were like that before; then Allah conferred His favor upon you, so investigate. Indeed Allah is ever, with what you do, Acquainted.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of thoroughly investigating and verifying information before making judgments, especially in matters of faith and warfare. It cautions against hastily assuming someone is a disbeliever based on superficial factors or worldly motives. The verse reminds believers that they too were once in a similar position before Allah guided them, so they should be careful and just in their assessments. It underscores the idea that Allah is fully aware of all actions and intentions, encouraging believers to act with sincerity and thoughtfulness.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا إذا ضربتم في سبيل الله فتبينوا ولا تقولوا لمن ألقى إليكم السلام لست مؤمنا تبتغون عرض الحياة الدنيا فعند الله مغانم كثيرة كذلك كنتم من قبل فمن الله عليكم فتبينوا إن الله كان بما تعملون خبيرا

translation: Not equal are those believers remaining [at home] - other than the disabled - and the mujahideen, [who strive and fight] in the cause of Allah with their wealth and their lives. Allah has preferred the mujahideen through their wealth and their lives over those who remain [behind], by degrees. And to both Allah has promised the best [reward]. But Allah has preferred the mujahideen over those who remain [behind] with a great reward -
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the superiority and virtue of those who strive and make sacrifices in the path of Allah, both with their wealth and their lives, compared to those believers who remain behind and do not participate in jihad, except for those who have valid excuses like disabilities. Allah promises good rewards for both groups, but He has distinguished the mujahideen with higher degrees of reward and honor due to their sacrifices and efforts in His cause. This encourages believers to be active participants in striving for Allah's religion and not to hold back from it, seeking the great rewards and blessings that Allah has prepared for the mujahideen.
orig: لا يستوي القاعدون من المؤمنين غير أولي الضرر والمجاهدون في سبيل الله بأموالهم وأنفسهم فضل الله المجاهدين بأموالهم وأنفسهم على القاعدين درجة وكلا وعد الله الحسنى وفضل الله المجاهدين على القاعدين أجرا عظيما

translation: Degrees [of high position] from Him and forgiveness and mercy. And Allah is ever Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse highlights the immense rewards that Allah bestows upon those who strive in His cause and seek His pleasure. It indicates that Allah grants the believers elevated ranks and degrees of honor in Paradise as a recompense for their good deeds and sacrifices. Moreover, Allah forgives their sins, shortcomings, and faults out of His infinite mercy and compassion. The repetition of Allah's attributes of forgiveness and mercy emphasizes that no matter how much people fall short or err, the door to Allah's forgiveness is always open when they sincerely repent and turn back to Him. It is a reminder of Allah's immeasurable grace and love towards His servants.
orig: درجات منه ومغفرة ورحمة وكان الله غفورا رحيما

translation: Indeed, those whom the angels take [in death] while wronging themselves - [the angels] will say, "In what [condition] were you?" They will say, "We were oppressed in the land." The angels will say, "Was not the earth of Allah spacious [enough] for you to emigrate therein?" For those, their refuge is Hell - and evil it is as a destination.
interpretation: This verse is a warning to those who fail to fulfill their religious obligations and emigrate from places where they face oppression and persecution. It emphasizes that Muslims have a duty to strive in the cause of Allah and not remain passive in the face of injustice. The verse also highlights the consequences of such inaction - those who do not emigrate to more favorable environments, despite having the means to do so, will face the punishment of Hell in the afterlife. It serves as a reminder that Muslims must actively work to create conditions conducive to practicing their faith and living righteously, even if it means leaving their homeland.
orig: إن الذين توفاهم الملائكة ظالمي أنفسهم قالوا فيم كنتم قالوا كنا مستضعفين في الأرض قالوا ألم تكن أرض الله واسعة فتهاجروا فيها فأولئك مأواهم جهنم وساءت مصيرا

translation: Except the oppressed among men, women and children who cannot devise a plan nor are they able to direct their way.
interpretation: This verse is making an exception for those who are truly oppressed and helpless, unable to escape their situation or find a way out. It recognizes that there are some individuals - men, women, and children - who are genuinely powerless and cannot be held fully accountable for their circumstances or actions. God's mercy and justice takes into account their weakness and inability. The verse encourages showing compassion and not judging such oppressed people who are deprived of means and options to change their difficult state.
orig: إلا المستضعفين من الرجال والنساء والولدان لا يستطيعون حيلة ولا يهتدون سبيلا

translation: Those are the ones from whom Allah will accept repentance, and Allah is ever Pardoning and Forgiving.
interpretation: This verse highlights the immense mercy and forgiveness of Allah. It indicates that even those who have committed sins or wrongdoings have the opportunity to sincerely repent and turn back to Allah. Allah, in His infinite grace, is willing to accept their repentance and forgive their past misdeeds. The verse emphasizes that Allah is "Afu" (Pardoning) and "Ghafur" (Forgiving), which means that He not only forgives but also removes the burden of sin from the repentant person. This verse offers hope and encouragement to those who seek Allah's forgiveness, assuring them that the door of repentance is always open, and Allah's mercy encompasses all who sincerely turn to Him.
orig: فأولئك عسى الله أن يعفو عنهم وكان الله عفوا غفورا

translation: And whoever emigrates for the cause of Allah will find on the earth many [alternative] locations and abundance. And whoever leaves his home as an emigrant to Allah and His Messenger and then death overtakes him - his reward has already become incumbent upon Allah. And Allah is ever Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse encourages Muslims to make sacrifices and emigrate for the sake of Allah, with the promise that they will find ample opportunities and provisions in other lands. It also assures that even if death befalls someone during this righteous migration, their reward is guaranteed with Allah, emphasizing His forgiveness and mercy. The verse highlights the importance of prioritizing one's faith and being willing to leave behind worldly comforts in devotion to Allah and His messenger.
orig: ومن يهاجر في سبيل الله يجد في الأرض مراغما كثيرا وسعة ومن يخرج من بيته مهاجرا إلى الله ورسوله ثم يدركه الموت فقد وقع أجره على الله وكان الله غفورا رحيما

translation: And when you travel in the land, there is no blame upon you for shortening the prayer, if you fear that those who disbelieve may disrupt [or attack] you. Indeed, the disbelievers are ever to you a clear enemy.
interpretation: This verse provides a concession for Muslims who are traveling to shorten their prayers if they fear that the disbelievers might take advantage of their vulnerability during prayer to attack or harm them. It highlights the hostility that existed between the Muslims and the disbelievers at the time. The verse emphasizes the importance of being cautious and taking necessary measures to protect oneself, even if it means modifying religious practices temporarily. It also serves as a reminder that the disbelievers are a clear enemy to the Muslims, and that one should always be on guard against their potential aggression or plots.
orig: وإذا ضربتم في الأرض فليس عليكم جناح أن تقصروا من الصلاة إن خفتم أن يفتنكم الذين كفروا إن الكافرين كانوا لكم عدوا مبينا

translation: And when you are among them and lead them in prayer, let a group of them stand [in prayer] with you and let them carry their arms. And when they have prostrated, let them be [in position] behind you and have the other group come forward which has not [yet] prayed and let them pray with you, taking precaution and carrying their arms. Those who disbelieve wish that you would neglect your weapons and your baggage so they could come down upon you in one [single] attack. But there is no blame upon you, if you are troubled by rain or are ill, for putting down your arms, but take precaution. Indeed, Allah has prepared for the disbelievers a humiliating punishment.
interpretation: This verse provides guidance on how to perform prayers during times of fear or war. It instructs the believers to divide themselves into two groups, with one group praying while the other stands guard with their weapons. After the first group completes their prayer, they switch positions with the second group, allowing them to pray while the first group stands guard. This precautionary measure is taken to prevent the enemy from launching a surprise attack while the believers are vulnerable during prayer. However, the verse also states that if the believers are troubled by rain or illness, they are permitted to put down their weapons, but should still remain vigilant. The verse concludes by warning that Allah has prepared a humiliating punishment for those who disbelieve.
orig: وإذا كنت فيهم فأقمت لهم الصلاة فلتقم طائفة منهم معك وليأخذوا أسلحتهم فإذا سجدوا فليكونوا من ورائكم ولتأت طائفة أخرى لم يصلوا فليصلوا معك وليأخذوا حذرهم وأسلحتهم ود الذين كفروا لو تغفلون عن أسلحتكم وأمتعتكم فيميلون عليكم ميلة واحدة ولا جناح عليكم إن كان بكم أذى من مطر أو كنتم مرضى أن تضعوا أسلحتكم وخذوا حذركم إن الله أعد للكافرين عذابا مهينا

translation: And when you have completed the prayer, remember Allah standing, sitting, or [lying] on your sides. But when you become secure, re-establish [regular] prayer. Indeed, prayer has been decreed upon the believers a decree of specified times.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of remembering Allah and being mindful of Him at all times, even after completing the obligatory prayers. It encourages believers to engage in dhikr (remembrance of Allah) in various postures - standing, sitting, or lying down. However, when the situation becomes safe and secure, Muslims are instructed to perform the prayers in their prescribed manner and timings, as it is a fundamental obligation ordained upon them by Allah. This highlights the significance of maintaining a consistent and disciplined prayer life, as it serves as a means of connecting with Allah and seeking His guidance and blessings.
orig: فإذا قضيتم الصلاة فاذكروا الله قياما وقعودا وعلى جنوبكم فإذا اطمأننتم فأقيموا الصلاة إن الصلاة كانت على المؤمنين كتابا موقوتا

translation: And do not weaken in pursuit of the enemy. If you are suffering, then surely they too are suffering as you are suffering, but you expect from Allah that which they expect not. And Allah is ever Knowing and Wise.
interpretation: This verse encourages the believers to remain steadfast and persevere in their struggle against the enemy, even in the face of hardships and suffering. It reminds them that their enemies are also experiencing similar pain and difficulties. However, the believers have an advantage over their enemies: they have hope and faith in Allah's support and ultimate victory, while their enemies do not. The verse also emphasizes that Allah is all-knowing and wise, implying that He is fully aware of the believers' struggles and will guide them according to His wisdom and plan.
orig: ولا تهنوا في ابتغاء القوم إن تكونوا تألمون فإنهم يألمون كما تألمون وترجون من الله ما لا يرجون وكان الله عليما حكيما

translation: Indeed, We have revealed to you, [O Muhammad], the Book in truth so you may judge between the people by that which Allah has shown you. And do not be for the deceitful an advocate.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the responsibility placed upon Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) as a recipient of divine revelation. The Qur'an has been revealed to him with the truth, so that he may judge between people fairly and justly, based on the guidance provided to him by Allah. It also serves as a warning to the Prophet not to side with those who are deceitful or who try to undermine justice, even if they are close to him. As a leader and a judge, his ultimate loyalty must be to Allah and to upholding the truth, not to protecting those who engage in dishonest behavior.
orig: إنا أنزلنا إليك الكتاب بالحق لتحكم بين الناس بما أراك الله ولا تكن للخائنين خصيما

translation: And seek forgiveness from Allah. Indeed, Allah is ever Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of seeking forgiveness from Allah. It reminds us that Allah is always ready to forgive those who sincerely repent and seek His mercy. The verse encourages believers to turn to Allah in repentance whenever they commit sins or make mistakes, with the assurance that Allah is Forgiving and Merciful. It highlights the boundless nature of Allah's forgiveness and mercy, which are available to all who seek them with sincerity and humility. The verse also implies that seeking forgiveness should be a continuous process in a believer's life, as it helps maintain a strong connection with Allah and purifies the soul from the burden of sins.
orig: واستغفر الله إن الله كان غفورا رحيما

translation: And do not argue on behalf of those who deceive themselves. Indeed, Allah loves not one who is a habitually sinful deceiver.
interpretation: This verse is a warning against defending or making excuses for those who engage in dishonest and sinful behavior. It emphasizes that Allah does not love those who habitually deceive others and commit sins. The interpretation is that believers should not support or argue in favor of those who are known to be untrustworthy and engage in immoral actions, as doing so would be displeasing to Allah. Instead, one should stand for justice and righteousness, even if it means going against those who are close to them but are in the wrong.
orig: ولا تجادل عن الذين يختانون أنفسهم إن الله لا يحب من كان خوانا أثيما

translation: They conceal [their evil intentions and deeds] from the people, but they cannot conceal [them] from Allah, and He is with them [in His knowledge] when they spend the night in such as He does not accept of speech. And ever is Allah, of what they do, encompassing.
interpretation: This verse highlights the futility of attempting to hide one's misdeeds from Allah. Even if people try to conceal their evil intentions and actions from others, they cannot hide them from the All-Knowing Creator. Allah is fully aware of what they plot and plan, even in the depths of the night when they think no one is watching. This serves as a reminder that one should always be mindful of Allah and strive to do what pleases Him, for He encompasses all our actions and will hold us accountable for them.
orig: يستخفون من الناس ولا يستخفون من الله وهو معهم إذ يبيتون ما لا يرضى من القول وكان الله بما يعملون محيطا

translation: Here you are - those for whom you used to argue in the worldly life. But who will argue with Allah for them on the Day of Resurrection, or who will be their representative?
interpretation: This verse is a rebuke to those who argue in defense of the disbelievers and wrongdoers in this worldly life. It reminds them that on the Day of Judgment, no one will be able to argue on their behalf before Allah or represent them. They will have to face the consequences of their actions alone, without any intercession or support. It emphasizes the importance of standing up for truth and justice in this life, rather than defending the wrongdoers, as ultimately everyone will be held accountable for their deeds by Allah.
orig: ها أنتم هؤلاء جادلتم عنهم في الحياة الدنيا فمن يجادل الله عنهم يوم القيامة أم من يكون عليهم وكيلا

translation: And whoever does a wrong or wrongs himself but then seeks forgiveness of Allah will find Allah Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the immense mercy and forgiveness of Allah. It reassures us that no matter how much we have sinned or wronged ourselves, the door to repentance is always open. If we sincerely turn back to Allah, seek His forgiveness, and strive to reform ourselves, He will surely forgive us. Allah's infinite mercy and compassion transcend the sins of His servants. This verse encourages us to never despair of Allah's mercy, to hasten to repent when we falter, and to have faith that Allah is Ever-Forgiving and Most Merciful to those who sincerely turn to Him in repentance and seek His pardon.
orig: ومن يعمل سوءا أو يظلم نفسه ثم يستغفر الله يجد الله غفورا رحيما

translation: And whoever earns sin, only earns it against himself. And Allah is ever Knowing and Wise.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the concept of individual responsibility in Islam. It states that whoever commits a sin or wrongdoing, the consequences of that action will be borne by the individual alone. They cannot shift the blame onto others or expect to escape the repercussions of their misdeeds. The verse also highlights two important attributes of Allah - He is All-Knowing, fully aware of all our actions, and He is Wise, always acting with perfect wisdom and justice. This serves as a reminder for people to be mindful of their deeds, knowing that Allah sees and knows everything, and to strive towards righteousness and away from sin.
orig: ومن يكسب إثما فإنما يكسبه على نفسه وكان الله عليما حكيما

translation: But whoever earns an offense or a sin and then blames it on an innocent [person] has taken upon himself a slander and manifest sin.
interpretation: This verse warns against falsely accusing an innocent person of wrongdoing. It emphasizes the gravity of such an act, equating it to both slander and a clear sin. By blaming someone else for one's own misdeeds, the offender compounds their initial transgression with an even greater evil. This highlights the importance of personal accountability and the need to take responsibility for one's own actions, rather than seeking to shift blame onto the blameless. The verse serves as a strong deterrent against bearing false witness and ruining the reputation of the innocent.
orig: ومن يكسب خطيئة أو إثما ثم يرم به بريئا فقد احتمل بهتانا وإثما مبينا

translation: And if it was not for the favor of Allah upon you and His mercy, a group of them would have determined to lead you astray. But they do not lead astray except themselves, and they will not harm you at all. And Allah has revealed to you the Book and wisdom and has taught you that which you did not know. And ever has the favor of Allah upon you been great.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the protection and guidance that Allah provides to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him). It suggests that there were people who tried to mislead the Prophet, but Allah's favor and mercy prevented them from succeeding. The verse also highlights the importance of divine revelation and wisdom that Allah bestowed upon the Prophet, teaching him what he did not know before. It underscores the immense favor and blessings that Allah has granted to the Prophet, which can be seen as a testament to his status and the truth of his message.
orig: ولولا فضل الله عليك ورحمته لهمت طائفة منهم أن يضلوك وما يضلون إلا أنفسهم وما يضرونك من شيء وأنزل الله عليك الكتاب والحكمة وعلمك ما لم تكن تعلم وكان فضل الله عليك عظيما

translation: There is no good in most of their secret conversations except for those who enjoin charity or that which is right or conciliation between people. And whoever does that seeking means to the approval of Allah - then We are going to give him a great reward.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of having conversations and interactions that are beneficial and righteous. It states that most private conversations between people are devoid of goodness, except for those that encourage acts of charity, good deeds, or resolving conflicts and making peace between people. Those who engage in such virtuous conversations and actions, seeking the pleasure and approval of Allah, will be granted a tremendous reward by Him. This highlights the value Islam places on using our speech and interactions to spread goodness, help others, and create harmony in society.
orig: لا خير في كثير من نجواهم إلا من أمر بصدقة أو معروف أو إصلاح بين الناس ومن يفعل ذلك ابتغاء مرضات الله فسوف نؤتيه أجرا عظيما

translation: And whoever opposes the Messenger after guidance has become clear to him and follows other than the way of the believers - We will give him what he has taken and drive him into Hell, and evil it is as a destination.
interpretation: This verse serves as a stern warning to those who knowingly reject the guidance brought by Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and choose to follow a path contrary to that of the believers. It emphasizes that once the truth has been made evident, opposing the Prophet and the way of the faithful will lead to grave consequences in the Hereafter. The verse highlights the importance of submitting to divine guidance, unity among believers, and the severity of punishment for those who deliberately deviate from the straight path after it has been made clear to them. It serves as a reminder for Muslims to stay steadfast in their faith and to avoid falling into the traps of disbelief and disobedience.
orig: ومن يشاقق الرسول من بعد ما تبين له الهدى ويتبع غير سبيل المؤمنين نوله ما تولى ونصله جهنم وساءت مصيرا

translation: Indeed, Allah does not forgive association with Him, but He forgives what is less than that for whom He wills. And he who associates others with Allah has certainly gone far astray.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the gravity of shirk (associating partners with Allah), stating that it is an unforgivable sin if one dies without repenting from it. Allah, in His infinite mercy, may forgive all other sins as He wills, but the sin of shirk severs the person's connection with Allah and leads them far astray from the path of guidance. This highlights the importance of maintaining a pure monotheistic belief in Islam and avoiding any form of idolatry or polytheism. It also serves as a reminder for believers to constantly seek Allah's forgiveness for their shortcomings and to strive towards sincere repentance.
orig: إن الله لا يغفر أن يشرك به ويغفر ما دون ذلك لمن يشاء ومن يشرك بالله فقد ضل ضلالا بعيدا

translation: They invoke not besides Him except female [deities], and they [actually] invoke not except a rebellious Satan.
interpretation: This verse is criticizing the pagan Arabs who used to worship female deities besides Allah. It states that in reality, by worshipping these false goddesses, they are actually invoking and following Satan, who has rebelled against God. The verse implies that Satan has deluded them into this false worship of female deities, which are powerless and have no divinity. It emphasizes that Allah alone is worthy of worship, and invoking anyone else is equivalent to following the path of misguidance laid by Satan to lead people astray from the truth.
orig: إن يدعون من دونه إلا إناثا وإن يدعون إلا شيطانا مريدا

translation: Allah cursed him and he said, "I will surely take from among Your servants a specific portion."
interpretation: This verse refers to Satan's arrogance and defiance against Allah. After being cursed by Allah for his disobedience, Satan vowed to mislead a portion of mankind away from the straight path. It highlights the rebellious nature of Satan and his determination to lead humans astray. The "specific portion" mentioned alludes to those who will follow Satan's temptations and fall into misguidance. This verse serves as a warning to believers about the ever-present threat of Satan's influence and the importance of seeking refuge in Allah and adhering firmly to His guidance to avoid being among those led astray by Satan's deceptions.
orig: لعنه الله وقال لأتخذن من عبادك نصيبا مفروضا

translation: And I will surely mislead them, and I will surely arouse in them [sinful] desires, and I will surely command them so they will slit the ears of cattle, and I will surely command them so they will change the creation of Allah. And whoever takes Satan as an ally instead of Allah has certainly sustained a clear loss.
interpretation: This verse is a warning about the deceptive tactics of Satan, who seeks to lead people astray from the path of Allah. Satan's methods include instilling false hopes and desires, encouraging superstitious practices like slitting the ears of cattle, and tempting people to alter Allah's creation. Those who follow Satan instead of Allah are ultimately doomed to suffer great loss in this life and the hereafter. The verse emphasizes the importance of remaining steadfast in faith and resisting the temptations of Satan, as succumbing to his influence leads to clear ruin and deprivation of Allah's grace and guidance.
orig: ولأضلنهم ولأمنينهم ولآمرنهم فليبتكن آذان الأنعام ولآمرنهم فليغيرن خلق الله ومن يتخذ الشيطان وليا من دون الله فقد خسر خسرانا مبينا

translation: Satan promises them and arouses desire in them. But Satan does not promise them except delusion.
interpretation: This verse warns against the deceptive nature of Satan, who makes false promises and creates vain desires in people to lead them astray from the path of righteousness. It emphasizes that Satan's promises are nothing but delusions and that believers should be cautious not to fall into his traps. The verse reminds us to rely on Allah's guidance and promises, which are true and everlasting, rather than being swayed by the temporary and deceptive allures of Satan.
orig: يعدهم ويمنيهم وما يعدهم الشيطان إلا غرورا

translation: Those - their refuge is Hell, and they will not find from it an escape.
interpretation: This verse warns that those who reject faith and persist in wrongdoing will find their ultimate abode in Hell, with no possibility of escape or reprieve. It emphasizes the severity and permanence of the punishment that awaits the unrighteous in the Hereafter. The verse serves as a stern admonition for people to mend their ways, seek forgiveness, and follow the path of righteousness to avoid this terrible fate. It highlights the concept of divine justice, where every soul will face the consequences of their actions and choices in this world.
orig: أولئك مأواهم جهنم ولا يجدون عنها محيصا

translation: And those who believe and do righteous deeds - We will admit them to gardens beneath which rivers flow, wherein they abide forever. [It is] the promise of Allah, [which is] truth, and who is more truthful than Allah in statement.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of faith and good deeds in attaining Paradise. It assures the believers that if they have faith and do righteous actions, Allah will reward them with eternal residence in gardens with flowing rivers. The verse also affirms the absolute truthfulness of Allah's promise, indicating that there is none more truthful than Him. This serves as a strong motivation for the believers to persist in their faith and good deeds, knowing that Allah's promise of Paradise is certain and will be fulfilled.
orig: والذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات سندخلهم جنات تجري من تحتها الأنهار خالدين فيها أبدا وعد الله حقا ومن أصدق من الله قيلا

translation: It will not be in accordance with your desires, nor those of the People of the Book. Whoever does evil will be recompensed for it, and they will not find for themselves any protector or helper besides Allah.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the concept of individual responsibility and divine justice. It states that the ultimate fate of each person, whether Muslim or from the People of the Book (Jews and Christians), will be determined by their actions and deeds, not by their wishes, desires, or religious affiliation. Those who commit evil acts will face the consequences of their actions and will not find any protector or helper besides Allah to save them from His judgment. This highlights the importance of leading a righteous life and being accountable for one's actions, as Allah's justice will prevail, and no one can escape the consequences of their deeds.
orig: ليس بأمانيكم ولا أماني أهل الكتاب من يعمل سوءا يجز به ولا يجد له من دون الله وليا ولا نصيرا

translation: And whoever does righteous deeds, whether male or female, while being a believer - those will enter Paradise and will not be wronged, [even as much as] the speck on a date seed.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of faith and good deeds in attaining salvation and entering Paradise. It highlights the equality between men and women in terms of their spiritual potential and rewards. Allah promises that those who believe and do righteous deeds, regardless of their gender, will be admitted into Paradise without any injustice or decrease in their rewards. The mention of "the speck on a date seed" indicates that even the smallest injustice will not be done to them, and they will be given their full rewards for their faith and good deeds. This verse encourages believers to strive for righteousness and assures them of Allah's justice and generosity in the Hereafter.
orig: ومن يعمل من الصالحات من ذكر أو أنثى وهو مؤمن فأولئك يدخلون الجنة ولا يظلمون نقيرا

translation: And who is better in religion than one who submits himself to Allah while being a doer of good and follows the religion of Abraham, inclining toward truth? And Allah took Abraham as an intimate friend.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the best way of practicing religion is to completely submit oneself to Allah, do good deeds, and follow the pure monotheistic teachings of Prophet Abraham. It highlights that Abraham was chosen by Allah as His close friend (Khalil) due to his unwavering faith, sincerity, and righteousness. The verse encourages believers to emulate Abraham's example by dedicating themselves wholly to Allah, striving to be righteous, and adhering to the true religion of Islam, which is based on the pure monotheism that Abraham preached. It also underscores the importance of having a direct, intimate relationship with Allah through sincere worship and obedience.
orig: ومن أحسن دينا ممن أسلم وجهه لله وهو محسن واتبع ملة إبراهيم حنيفا واتخذ الله إبراهيم خليلا

translation: And to Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth. And ever is Allah, of all things, encompassing.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute sovereignty and omnipresence of Allah. It reminds us that everything in the universe, whether in the heavens or on earth, belongs to Him alone. It also highlights His all-encompassing knowledge and power, suggesting that nothing escapes His awareness or control. This understanding should instill humility, reverence, and trust in Allah, as we recognize that our existence and everything around us is ultimately under His dominion and care.
orig: ولله ما في السماوات وما في الأرض وكان الله بكل شيء محيطا

translation: They request from you a [legal] ruling concerning women. Say, "Allah gives you a ruling about them and [about] what has been recited to you in the Book concerning the orphan girls to whom you do not give what is decreed for them - and [yet] you desire to marry them - and concerning the oppressed among children and that you maintain for orphans [their rights] in justice." And whatever you do of good - indeed, Allah is ever Knowing of it.
interpretation: This verse addresses the rights of women and orphans in society. It emphasizes the importance of treating them fairly and justly, especially in matters of inheritance and marriage. The verse also highlights the responsibility of the community to protect and support the vulnerable, particularly orphaned children. It serves as a reminder that Allah is aware of all our actions, both good and bad, and that we will be held accountable for how we treat others, especially those who are weak and in need of our help.
orig: ويستفتونك في النساء قل الله يفتيكم فيهن وما يتلى عليكم في الكتاب في يتامى النساء اللاتي لا تؤتونهن ما كتب لهن وترغبون أن تنكحوهن والمستضعفين من الولدان وأن تقوموا لليتامى بالقسط وما تفعلوا من خير فإن الله كان به عليما

translation: And if a woman fears from her husband contempt or evasion, there is no sin upon them if they make terms of settlement between them - and settlement is best. And present in [human] souls is stinginess. But if you do good and fear Allah - then indeed Allah is ever, with what you do, Acquainted.
interpretation: This verse provides guidance for resolving marital conflicts. If a wife fears that her husband is turning away from her or mistreating her, the couple is encouraged to try to reconcile and reach a settlement that is agreeable to both. Making peace is better than letting the situation worsen. However, human souls are prone to selfishness and greed. The verse reminds that if the couple makes a sincere effort to do the right thing and be mindful of Allah in resolving their issues, then Allah is fully aware of their good intentions and efforts, even if they fall short. Ultimately, Allah knows best about all that we do.
orig: وإن امرأة خافت من بعلها نشوزا أو إعراضا فلا جناح عليهما أن يصلحا بينهما صلحا والصلح خير وأحضرت الأنفس الشح وإن تحسنوا وتتقوا فإن الله كان بما تعملون خبيرا

translation: And you will never be able to be equal [in feeling] between wives, even if you should strive [to do so]. So do not incline completely [toward one] and leave another hanging. And if you amend [your affairs] and fear Allah - then indeed, Allah is ever Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse acknowledges the difficulty of treating multiple wives with complete equality and fairness, despite one's best efforts. It advises against showing excessive favor to one wife while neglecting the others, leaving them in a state of uncertainty and emotional limbo. The verse emphasizes the importance of striving for justice, reconciliation, and righteousness in marital relationships. It concludes by reassuring believers that Allah is Forgiving and Merciful, recognizing the challenges and imperfections inherent in human relationships, and encouraging them to seek His forgiveness and guidance in navigating these complexities.
orig: ولن تستطيعوا أن تعدلوا بين النساء ولو حرصتم فلا تميلوا كل الميل فتذروها كالمعلقة وإن تصلحوا وتتقوا فإن الله كان غفورا رحيما

translation: But if they separate [by divorce], Allah will enrich each [of them] from His abundance. And ever is Allah Encompassing and Wise.
interpretation: This verse highlights Allah's infinite wisdom and generosity. It reassures that even if a married couple decides to part ways through divorce, Allah will provide for each of them from His boundless resources. It emphasizes that Allah's provisions are not limited, and He is capable of granting sustenance and blessings to individuals, regardless of their marital status. The verse also underscores Allah's all-encompassing knowledge and wisdom in decreeing such situations, reminding believers to trust in His plans and have faith that He will take care of their needs, even during challenging times like divorce.
orig: وإن يتفرقا يغن الله كلا من سعته وكان الله واسعا حكيما

translation: And to Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth. And We have instructed those who were given the Scripture before you and yourselves to fear Allah. But if you disbelieve - then to Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth. And ever is Allah Free of need and Praiseworthy.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute ownership and sovereignty of Allah over all that exists in the heavens and the earth. It also highlights the importance of righteousness and God-consciousness (taqwa) which was enjoined upon the previous recipients of divine scriptures as well as the followers of Islam. The verse warns that if one chooses to disbelieve, it does not affect Allah in the least, as He is self-sufficient and not in need of anyone's belief or worship. Allah's praiseworthy attributes remain evident regardless of the actions of His creation.
orig: ولله ما في السماوات وما في الأرض ولقد وصينا الذين أوتوا الكتاب من قبلكم وإياكم أن اتقوا الله وإن تكفروا فإن لله ما في السماوات وما في الأرض وكان الله غنيا حميدا

translation: And to Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth. And sufficient is Allah as Disposer of affairs.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute sovereignty and control of Allah over everything in the universe. It affirms that Allah is the ultimate owner and master of all that exists in the heavens and the earth. The verse also highlights the sufficiency of Allah as the disposer of all affairs, implying that He is the one who manages, regulates, and determines the course of all matters in the universe. Believers should put their trust in Allah, knowing that He is sufficient as a guardian and protector, and that He has the power to handle all their concerns and needs.
orig: ولله ما في السماوات وما في الأرض وكفى بالله وكيلا

translation: If He wills, He can do away with you, O people, and bring others [in your place]. And ever is Allah competent to do that.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute power and sovereignty of Allah over His creation. It reminds us that our existence is entirely dependent on Allah's will, and that He has the ability to replace us with others if He so desires. This serves as a powerful reminder of our ultimate insignificance in the grand scheme of things, and encourages us to remain humble and submissive to Allah's will. It also highlights the importance of striving to be among those whom Allah is pleased with, as our ultimate fate rests in His hands.
orig: إن يشأ يذهبكم أيها الناس ويأت بآخرين وكان الله على ذلك قديرا

translation: Whoever desires the reward of this world - then with Allah is the reward of this world and the Hereafter. And ever is Allah Hearing and Seeing.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah is the ultimate source of all rewards, both in this worldly life and in the eternal Hereafter. It reminds us that while we may strive for success and happiness in this world, we should never lose sight of the greater reward that awaits the righteous in the afterlife. The verse also highlights two of Allah's essential attributes: His all-encompassing hearing and sight. This serves as a reminder that Allah is always aware of our actions and intentions, and that we should strive to live in a manner pleasing to Him, seeking His rewards in both this life and the next.
orig: من كان يريد ثواب الدنيا فعند الله ثواب الدنيا والآخرة وكان الله سميعا بصيرا

translation: O you who have believed, be persistently standing firm in justice, witnesses for Allah, even if it be against yourselves or parents and relatives. Whether one is rich or poor, Allah is more worthy of both. So follow not [personal] inclination, lest you not be just. And if you distort [your testimony] or refuse [to give it], then indeed Allah is ever, with what you do, Acquainted.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of upholding justice and fairness in all circumstances, even if it means testifying against oneself or loved ones. It reminds believers that Allah is aware of their actions and that they should not let personal biases or inclinations sway them from the path of righteousness. The verse also highlights the equality of all individuals before Allah, regardless of their wealth or social status, and encourages believers to prioritize their duty to Allah above all else.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا كونوا قوامين بالقسط شهداء لله ولو على أنفسكم أو الوالدين والأقربين إن يكن غنيا أو فقيرا فالله أولى بهما فلا تتبعوا الهوى أن تعدلوا وإن تلووا أو تعرضوا فإن الله كان بما تعملون خبيرا

translation: O you who have believed, believe in Allah and His Messenger and the Book that He sent down upon His Messenger and the Scripture which He sent down before. And whoever disbelieves in Allah, His angels, His books, His messengers, and the Last Day has certainly gone far astray.
interpretation: This verse is a call to the believers to have complete faith in Allah, His Messenger Muhammad (peace be upon him), the Qur'an that was revealed to him, and the divine scriptures that came before it. It emphasizes the importance of believing in all the fundamental aspects of faith, which include Allah, His angels, His revealed books, His messengers, and the Day of Judgment. The verse warns that those who reject any of these essential components of faith have indeed strayed far away from the right path and are in manifest error. It highlights the significance of having a comprehensive and unwavering belief in the Islamic creed.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا آمنوا بالله ورسوله والكتاب الذي نزل على رسوله والكتاب الذي أنزل من قبل ومن يكفر بالله وملائكته وكتبه ورسله واليوم الآخر فقد ضل ضلالا بعيدا

translation: Indeed, those who have believed then disbelieved, then believed, then disbelieved, and then increased in disbelief - never will Allah forgive them, nor will He guide them to a way.
interpretation: This verse is referring to those who vacillate in their faith, going back and forth between belief and disbelief. It indicates that there is a point of no return, where if someone keeps reverting to disbelief after having believed, and increases in their disbelief, Allah will not forgive them or guide them to the right path. It serves as a warning against being fickle in one's faith and a reminder of the severity of repeatedly rejecting faith after having accepted it. The repeated opportunities to repent and believe are not infinite, and one risks sealing their fate if they continue to choose disbelief over faith.
orig: إن الذين آمنوا ثم كفروا ثم آمنوا ثم كفروا ثم ازدادوا كفرا لم يكن الله ليغفر لهم ولا ليهديهم سبيلا

translation: Give glad tidings to the hypocrites that there is for them a painful punishment.
interpretation: This verse serves as a stern warning to those who outwardly profess belief in Islam while harboring disbelief and ill intentions in their hearts. It emphasizes that such hypocrisy is a grave sin that will be met with severe consequences in the Hereafter. The "painful punishment" mentioned here alludes to the intense suffering that awaits the hypocrites in Hell as a result of their deception and betrayal of faith. This interpretation highlights the importance of sincerity and consistency between one's inner beliefs and outward actions in the Islamic faith.
orig: بشر المنافقين بأن لهم عذابا أليما

translation: Those who take disbelievers as allies instead of the believers. Do they seek with them honor [through power]? But indeed, honor belongs to Allah entirely.
interpretation: This verse is criticizing those who align themselves with disbelievers over their fellow believers, perhaps seeking worldly power, prestige or protection from them. However, it reminds that true honor and might belongs only to Allah. Seeking it from any other source is futile. The implication is that believers should put their trust in Allah alone and not compromise their faith or loyalties in pursuit of worldly gain from those who reject faith. All power and glory is ultimately in Allah's hands alone.
orig: الذين يتخذون الكافرين أولياء من دون المؤمنين أيبتغون عندهم العزة فإن العزة لله جميعا

translation: And it has already come down to you in the Book that when you hear the verses of Allah [recited], they are denied [by them] and ridiculed; so do not sit with them until they enter into another conversation. Indeed, you would then be like them. Indeed Allah will gather the hypocrites and disbelievers in Hell all together.
interpretation: This verse is a warning to the believers not to associate with those who mock and reject the verses of Allah. If they find themselves in the company of such people, they should leave and not participate in their blasphemous conversations. Remaining in their presence and listening to their ridicule would be akin to approving of their behavior and sharing in their sin. The verse emphasizes that Allah will punish both the hypocrites and the disbelievers together in Hell for their actions, as they are equally guilty of rejecting faith and ridiculing the truth.
orig: وقد نزل عليكم في الكتاب أن إذا سمعتم آيات الله يكفر بها ويستهزأ بها فلا تقعدوا معهم حتى يخوضوا في حديث غيره إنكم إذا مثلهم إن الله جامع المنافقين والكافرين في جهنم جميعا

translation: Those who wait in watch for you. Then if you gain a victory from Allah, they say, "Were we not with you?" But if the disbelievers have a success, they say [to them], "Did we not gain the advantage over you, and we protected you from the believers?" Allah will judge between [all of] you on the Day of Resurrection, and never will Allah give the disbelievers over the believers a way [to overcome them].
interpretation: This verse is referring to the hypocrites who change their stance and loyalty depending on the circumstances. When the Muslims are victorious, they claim to have been on their side all along. But when the disbelievers have some success, the hypocrites side with them and boast about protecting them from the believers. However, Allah makes it clear that He will judge between them on the Day of Judgment, and He will never allow the disbelievers to have a lasting upper hand over the true believers.
orig: الذين يتربصون بكم فإن كان لكم فتح من الله قالوا ألم نكن معكم وإن كان للكافرين نصيب قالوا ألم نستحوذ عليكم ونمنعكم من المؤمنين فالله يحكم بينكم يوم القيامة ولن يجعل الله للكافرين على المؤمنين سبيلا

translation: Indeed, the hypocrites [think to] deceive Allah, but He is deceiving them. And when they stand for prayer, they stand lazily, showing [themselves to] the people and not remembering Allah except a little.
interpretation: This verse reveals the true nature of the hypocrites who outwardly profess faith but inwardly harbor disbelief and evil intentions. Their attempts to deceive Allah are futile, as He is fully aware of their deception and will ultimately expose and punish them for their hypocrisy. The verse also highlights the hypocrites' lack of sincerity in their religious practices, such as prayer, which they perform only to be seen by others and not out of genuine devotion to Allah. This emphasizes the importance of sincerity and true faith in one's actions, as opposed to mere outward displays of piety.
orig: إن المنافقين يخادعون الله وهو خادعهم وإذا قاموا إلى الصلاة قاموا كسالى يراءون الناس ولا يذكرون الله إلا قليلا

translation: Wavering between them, [belonging] neither to these [i.e., the believers] nor to those [i.e., the disbelievers]. And whoever Allah leaves astray - never will you find for him a way.
interpretation: This verse is referring to the hypocrites who outwardly claim to be believers but inwardly harbor doubt and disbelief. They are not fully committed to either the believers or the disbelievers, but rather waver between the two groups depending on what suits their interests. As a result of their insincerity and lack of commitment to the truth, Allah has left them to stray, and they will not find guidance or a clear path to follow. The verse emphasizes the importance of having a firm faith and commitment to Allah, as those who are wishy-washy and insincere will be lost and misguided.
orig: مذبذبين بين ذلك لا إلى هؤلاء ولا إلى هؤلاء ومن يضلل الله فلن تجد له سبيلا

translation: O you who have believed, do not take the disbelievers as allies instead of the believers. Do you wish to give Allah against yourselves a clear case?
interpretation: This verse is a warning to the believers not to form alliances with the disbelievers at the expense of their fellow believers. It emphasizes the importance of loyalty and solidarity within the Muslim community. By aligning with the disbelievers, the believers would be providing Allah with a clear proof against themselves on the Day of Judgment, as this action demonstrates a lack of faith and trust in Allah and His guidance. The verse implicitly encourages the believers to prioritize their religious identity and the bonds of faith over any worldly alliances or interests that may compromise their commitment to Islam.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا لا تتخذوا الكافرين أولياء من دون المؤمنين أتريدون أن تجعلوا لله عليكم سلطانا مبينا

translation: Indeed, the hypocrites will be in the lowest depths of the Fire - and never will you find for them a helper.
interpretation: This verse is a stern warning to those who outwardly profess faith in Islam while inwardly harboring disbelief and doubt. Such hypocrisy is considered among the gravest of sins, warranting the most severe punishment in the depths of Hell. The verse emphasizes that on the Day of Judgment, these hypocrites will find themselves utterly alone and abandoned, with no one to support, defend or intercede on their behalf before Allah. It serves as a reminder for believers to be sincere in their faith and to shun any form of hypocrisy or double-dealing in their religious and worldly affairs.
orig: إن المنافقين في الدرك الأسفل من النار ولن تجد لهم نصيرا

translation: Except for those who repent, correct themselves, hold fast to Allah, and are sincere in their religion for Allah, for those will be with the believers. And Allah is going to give the believers a great reward.
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of sincere repentance, self-improvement, and devotion to Allah. It suggests that even those who have strayed from the right path can attain forgiveness and be counted among the believers if they genuinely turn back to Allah, rectify their actions, and remain steadfast in their faith. The verse also emphasizes the significance of purifying one's intentions and dedicating one's religious practices solely for the sake of Allah, without any form of hypocrisy or insincerity. As a reward for their repentance, righteousness, and sincere devotion, Allah promises the believers a great reward in the afterlife, underscoring the immense value placed on faith and good deeds in Islam.
orig: إلا الذين تابوا وأصلحوا واعتصموا بالله وأخلصوا دينهم لله فأولئك مع المؤمنين وسوف يؤت الله المؤمنين أجرا عظيما

translation: What would Allah do with your punishment if you are grateful and believe? And ever is Allah Appreciative and Knowing.
interpretation: This verse conveys the idea that Allah, in His infinite mercy and wisdom, does not seek to punish those who are grateful to Him and have faith in Him. It suggests that if people sincerely express their gratitude to Allah and believe in His message, He will not subject them to punishment. The verse also emphasizes two important attributes of Allah: He is "Shakir" (Appreciative), meaning that He recognizes and rewards those who are thankful to Him, and He is "Alim" (All-Knowing), indicating that He has complete knowledge of people's intentions, actions, and the sincerity of their faith. This interpretation highlights the compassionate and forgiving nature of Allah towards those who strive to follow His path with gratitude and belief.
orig: ما يفعل الله بعذابكم إن شكرتم وآمنتم وكان الله شاكرا عليما

translation: Allah does not like the public mention of evil except by one who has been wronged. And ever is Allah Hearing and Knowing.
interpretation: This verse indicates that Allah dislikes when people speak openly about evil things or sins, except in cases where someone has been wronged or oppressed. In such situations, the wronged person is permitted to speak out about the injustice they have faced, as this can help bring about justice and prevent further wrongdoing. The verse also emphasizes that Allah is All-Hearing and All-Knowing, which means that He is aware of all that happens, including any evil that is spoken or committed, and He will hold people accountable for their actions in the Hereafter. This serves as a reminder for believers to be mindful of their speech and actions, and to strive for justice and righteousness in all aspects of life.
orig: لا يحب الله الجهر بالسوء من القول إلا من ظلم وكان الله سميعا عليما

translation: If you do good openly or secretly or pardon an evil, then indeed Allah is Ever-Pardoning, All-Powerful.
interpretation: This verse highlights the immense mercy and forgiveness of Allah. It encourages people to do good deeds, whether openly or in private, and to forgive those who have wronged them. The verse emphasizes that such acts of goodness and pardoning are pleasing to Allah, who Himself is Ever-Pardoning and All-Powerful. It serves as a reminder that believers should strive to emulate Allah's attributes of forgiveness and mercy in their dealings with others. By doing so, they can earn Allah's pleasure and forgiveness for their own shortcomings.
orig: إن تبدوا خيرا أو تخفوه أو تعفوا عن سوء فإن الله كان عفوا قديرا

translation: Indeed, those who disbelieve in Allah and His messengers and wish to discriminate between Allah and His messengers and say, "We believe in some and disbelieve in others," and wish to adopt a way in between -
interpretation: This verse is criticizing those who claim to believe in God but reject some of His messengers. It asserts that true faith requires believing in all of God's messengers without distinction. One cannot selectively believe in some prophets while rejecting others, as this amounts to disbelief. The desire to take a middle path between belief and disbelief is condemned as an unacceptable position. The verse emphasizes the importance of complete submission to God's message as conveyed through all of His chosen messengers.
orig: إن الذين يكفرون بالله ورسله ويريدون أن يفرقوا بين الله ورسله ويقولون نؤمن ببعض ونكفر ببعض ويريدون أن يتخذوا بين ذلك سبيلا

translation: Those are the true disbelievers, and We have prepared for the disbelievers a humiliating punishment.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the severity of disbelief and its consequences in the Hereafter. Those who persistently reject faith in Allah and His messages are considered the "true disbelievers" because they have chosen to deny the truth despite clear signs and guidance. As a result of their conscious choice to disbelieve, Allah has prepared a "humiliating punishment" for them in the afterlife. This punishment is described as humiliating because it reflects the disgrace and shame that the disbelievers will face as a consequence of their arrogance and rejection of Allah's mercy and guidance in this world. The verse serves as a strong warning to those who persist in disbelief and a reminder of the importance of faith and submission to Allah.
orig: أولئك هم الكافرون حقا وأعتدنا للكافرين عذابا مهينا

translation: And those who believe in Allah and His messengers and do not discriminate between any of them - to those He is going to give their rewards. And ever is Allah Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of having complete faith in Allah and all His messengers without making any distinction between them. It assures that those who believe in the oneness of Allah and accept all the prophets and messengers sent by Him, without discriminating or preferring one over the others, will be rewarded abundantly by Allah. The verse also highlights two of Allah's essential attributes: His forgiveness and His mercy. This interpretation suggests that Allah, in His infinite grace, forgives the shortcomings of His faithful servants and showers them with mercy, granting them the rewards they deserve for their unwavering belief and righteousness.
orig: والذين آمنوا بالله ورسله ولم يفرقوا بين أحد منهم أولئك سوف يؤتيهم أجورهم وكان الله غفورا رحيما

translation: The People of the Scripture ask you to bring down to them a book from the heaven. But they had asked of Moses [even] greater than that and said, "Show us Allah outright," so the thunderbolt struck them for their wrongdoing. Then they took the calf [for worship] after clear evidences had come to them, and We pardoned that. And We gave Moses a clear authority.
interpretation: This verse highlights the audacity and stubbornness of the People of the Book (Jews) in their demands from the prophets. Despite witnessing clear signs and miracles, they were not satisfied and demanded even greater proofs, such as asking Moses to show them Allah directly. This arrogance led to their punishment through a thunderbolt. However, even after this incident and receiving clear evidence, they still worshipped the golden calf, showcasing their persistent disobedience. Yet, Allah's mercy and forgiveness are emphasized, as He pardoned them and continued to support Moses with clear authority and miracles. The verse serves as a reminder for believers to be humble, grateful, and steadfast in their faith, avoiding the mistakes of past nations who were given clear signs but still strayed from the right path.
orig: يسألك أهل الكتاب أن تنزل عليهم كتابا من السماء فقد سألوا موسى أكبر من ذلك فقالوا أرنا الله جهرة فأخذتهم الصاعقة بظلمهم ثم اتخذوا العجل من بعد ما جاءتهم البينات فعفونا عن ذلك وآتينا موسى سلطانا مبينا

translation: And We raised the Mount over them at [the taking of] their covenant and said to them, "Enter the gate bowing humbly", and We said to them, "Do not transgress on the sabbath", and We took from them a solemn covenant.
interpretation: This verse refers to the covenant that Allah took from the Children of Israel. The raising of the Mount over them symbolizes the gravity and importance of this covenant. They were commanded to enter the gate of the city humbly and not to violate the sanctity of the Sabbath. The solemn covenant emphasizes the binding nature of these commandments upon them. The verse serves as a reminder that the Children of Israel were given clear guidance and commandments, which they were obligated to follow as part of their covenant with Allah. Violating these commandments would be a breach of this sacred covenant.
orig: ورفعنا فوقهم الطور بميثاقهم وقلنا لهم ادخلوا الباب سجدا وقلنا لهم لا تعدوا في السبت وأخذنا منهم ميثاقا غليظا

translation: And because of their breaking their covenant and their disbelief in the signs of Allah and their killing the prophets without right and their saying, "Our hearts are wrapped". Rather, Allah has sealed them because of their disbelief, so they believe not, except for a few.
interpretation: This verse highlights the consequences of the actions of the Children of Israel, who broke their covenant with Allah, rejected His signs, and even killed His prophets unjustly. They arrogantly claimed that their hearts were sealed from understanding the truth. However, it was not that their hearts were sealed by nature, but rather it was a result of their persistent disbelief that Allah sealed their hearts as a punishment. Due to this seal, only a few of them would come to believe in the truth. This emphasizes the gravity of rejecting faith and the signs of Allah, as it can lead to spiritual insensitivity and distance from divine guidance.
orig: فبما نقضهم ميثاقهم وكفرهم بآيات الله وقتلهم الأنبياء بغير حق وقولهم قلوبنا غلف بل طبع الله عليها بكفرهم فلا يؤمنون إلا قليلا

translation: And for their disbelief and their saying against Mary a great slander.
interpretation: This verse refers to the grave sin committed by those who rejected faith and slandered Mary, the mother of Jesus, by falsely accusing her of unchastity. It highlights the severity of their transgression in spreading lies and false allegations against a pure and righteous woman chosen by Allah. The verse condemns their disbelief and their audacity in making such a tremendous accusation, emphasizing the magnitude of their slander against Mary, which is considered a major sin in Islam.
orig: وبكفرهم وقولهم على مريم بهتانا عظيما

translation: And their saying, "Indeed, we have killed the Messiah, Jesus, the son of Mary, the messenger of Allah." And they did not kill him, nor did they crucify him; but [another] was made to resemble him to them. And indeed, those who differ over it are in doubt about it. They have no knowledge of it except the following of assumption. And they did not kill him, for certain.
interpretation: This verse refutes the claim of the Jews that they killed Jesus, the Messiah. It clarifies that they did not actually kill or crucify him, but rather, someone else was made to resemble him to them. This caused confusion and doubt among those who differed concerning this matter. The verse emphasizes that they have no certain knowledge about it and are merely following assumptions and conjectures. It firmly establishes that Jesus was not killed by the Jews with certainty.
orig: وقولهم إنا قتلنا المسيح عيسى ابن مريم رسول الله وما قتلوه وما صلبوه ولكن شبه لهم وإن الذين اختلفوا فيه لفي شك منه ما لهم به من علم إلا اتباع الظن وما قتلوه يقينا

translation: But Allah raised him to Himself. And Allah is Ever Mighty, Ever Wise.
interpretation: This verse affirms that Allah raised Jesus to Himself, refuting the claim that he was crucified. It emphasizes Allah's power and wisdom in doing so.
