The raising of Jesus to Allah is understood by most Muslims to mean that he was taken up alive to heaven, body and soul, and that he will return near the end of time to defeat the Antichrist, establish justice on earth, and spread the message of Islam before his eventual death.
orig: بل رفعه الله إليه وكان الله عزيزا حكيما

translation: And there is none from the People of the Scripture but that he will surely believe in Jesus before his death. And on the Day of Resurrection he will be against them a witness.
interpretation: This verse indicates that before Jesus' death, all the People of the Book (i.e., Jews and Christians) will come to believe in him as a prophet and messenger of Allah. This suggests that near the end times, the truth about Jesus will become clear to everyone. On the Day of Judgment, Jesus himself will testify against those who rejected him or ascribed false teachings to him. It emphasizes the inevitability of all people recognizing Jesus' true status and message, even if they fail to do so during their worldly lives.
orig: وإن من أهل الكتاب إلا ليؤمنن به قبل موته ويوم القيامة يكون عليهم شهيدا

translation: For wrongdoing on the part of the Jews, We made unlawful for them [certain] good foods which had been lawful to them, and for their averting from the way of Allah many [people]
interpretation: This verse suggests that due to the transgressions and misdeeds committed by some Jews, Allah prohibited them from consuming certain foods that were previously permissible. Their actions, which included hindering others from the path of Allah, led to this punishment. It implies that disobedience to Allah's commands and causing corruption can result in the loss of blessings and privileges that were once granted. The verse also highlights the concept of divine justice, where wrongdoings are met with appropriate consequences as decreed by Allah.
orig: فبظلم من الذين هادوا حرمنا عليهم طيبات أحلت لهم وبصدهم عن سبيل الله كثيرا

translation: And [for] their taking of usury while they had been forbidden from it, and their consuming of the people's wealth unjustly. And we have prepared for the disbelievers among them a painful punishment.
interpretation: This verse is a strong condemnation of those who engage in usury (lending money at exorbitant interest rates) and those who unjustly consume other people's wealth. It makes clear that such practices are strictly forbidden in Islam. The mention of a "painful punishment" for the disbelievers who commit these sins underscores the severity with which Islam views financial exploitation and economic injustice. The verse implies that fair economic dealings and respect for others' property rights are essential values in Islamic ethics.
orig: وأخذهم الربا وقد نهوا عنه وأكلهم أموال الناس بالباطل وأعتدنا للكافرين منهم عذابا أليما

translation: But those firm in knowledge among them and the believers believe in what has been revealed to you, [O Muhammad], and what was revealed before you. And the establishers of prayer [especially] and the givers of zakah and the believers in Allah and the Last Day - those We will give a great reward.
interpretation: This verse highlights the qualities of the true believers who are steadfast in their faith. They not only believe in the revelation sent to Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) but also in the revelations sent before him to other prophets. They are those who establish prayer, give zakah (obligatory charity), and have unwavering belief in Allah and the Day of Judgment. Allah promises these believers a tremendous reward for their sincerity and adherence to the pillars of faith. It emphasizes that true belief is not merely a verbal attestation but is accompanied by righteous deeds and a commitment to the fundamental principles of Islam.
orig: لكن الراسخون في العلم منهم والمؤمنون يؤمنون بما أنزل إليك وما أنزل من قبلك والمقيمين الصلاة والمؤتون الزكاة والمؤمنون بالله واليوم الآخر أولئك سنؤتيهم أجرا عظيما

translation: Indeed, We have revealed to you, [O Muhammad], as We revealed to Noah and the prophets after him. And we revealed to Abraham, Ishmael, Isaac, Jacob, the Descendants, Jesus, Job, Jonah, Aaron, and Solomon, and to David We gave the book [of Psalms].
interpretation: This verse highlights the continuity of divine revelation across different prophets and messengers throughout history. It affirms that Muhammad (peace be upon him) received revelation from God, just as earlier prophets like Noah, Abraham, Moses, Jesus and others did. This establishes Muhammad's prophethood as being in the same tradition and lineage as previous prophets, while also emphasizing that all these prophets received their message from the same single source, Allah. The specific mention of some prophets and the scripture given to David underscores their significance and the commonality of the core message brought by all of Allah's messengers.
orig: إنا أوحينا إليك كما أوحينا إلى نوح والنبيين من بعده وأوحينا إلى إبراهيم وإسماعيل وإسحاق ويعقوب والأسباط وعيسى وأيوب ويونس وهارون وسليمان وآتينا داوود زبورا

translation: And [We sent] messengers about whom We have related [their stories] to you before and messengers about whom We have not related to you. And Allah spoke to Moses with [direct] speech.
interpretation: This verse highlights the fact that Allah has sent many messengers throughout history, some of whose stories have been narrated in the Qur'an, while others have not been mentioned. This emphasizes the universality of Allah's message and the continuous nature of prophethood. The verse also underscores the unique status of Prophet Moses, who was granted the privilege of direct communication with Allah. This direct speech between Allah and Moses serves as a testament to Moses' elevated rank among the prophets and the special relationship he had with Allah. The verse reminds believers that the message of Islam is not an isolated event but rather a continuation of the divine guidance that has been sent to humanity through numerous prophets across time.
orig: ورسلا قد قصصناهم عليك من قبل ورسلا لم نقصصهم عليك وكلم الله موسى تكليما

translation: Messengers as bearers of good news and warners so that mankind will have no argument against Allah after the Messengers. And Allah is Ever All-Powerful, All-Wise.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the divine wisdom behind sending Messengers to humanity. They were sent as both bearers of good tidings for those who believe and follow the straight path, and as warners for those who disbelieve and stray from the truth. The primary purpose of sending Messengers is to establish proof against mankind, so that no one can claim ignorance or lack of guidance on the Day of Judgment. After the Messengers have conveyed the message clearly, people will have no excuse or argument against Allah for their actions. The verse also highlights two of Allah's attributes: His power (Al-'Azeez) to execute His will and His wisdom (Al-Hakeem) in decreeing the sending of Messengers for the benefit and guidance of humanity.
orig: رسلا مبشرين ومنذرين لئلا يكون للناس على الله حجة بعد الرسل وكان الله عزيزا حكيما

translation: But Allah bears witness to that which He has revealed to you. He has sent it down with His knowledge, and the angels bear witness [as well]. And sufficient is Allah as Witness.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the authenticity and divine origin of the Qur'an. It asserts that Allah Himself bears witness to the truth of the revelation that He has sent down to Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) through the angel Gabriel. The verse also mentions that the angels, who are pure and trustworthy beings, bear witness to the truth of the Qur'an. This serves as a powerful testimony to the Qur'an's divine source and its absolute truthfulness. The verse concludes by stating that Allah's witness alone is sufficient, emphasizing His ultimate authority and the unquestionable nature of the Qur'anic revelation.
orig: لكن الله يشهد بما أنزل إليك أنزله بعلمه والملائكة يشهدون وكفى بالله شهيدا

translation: Indeed, those who disbelieve and avert [people] from the way of Allah have certainly gone far astray.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the gravity of disbelief and hindering others from the path of Allah. Those who engage in such actions are described as having strayed far from the truth and guidance. It implies that their deviation is not a minor one, but rather a profound and severe misguidance that leads them far away from the straight path. The verse serves as a warning against disbelief and obstructing others from following the way of Allah, highlighting the serious consequences of such actions in terms of one's spiritual state and ultimate destiny.
orig: إن الذين كفروا وصدوا عن سبيل الله قد ضلوا ضلالا بعيدا

translation: Indeed, those who disbelieve and commit wrong [or injustice] - never will Allah forgive them, nor will He guide them to a path.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the severity of disbelief and wrongdoing in the sight of Allah. Those who persistently reject faith and engage in oppression or injustice have strayed so far from the right path that Allah will not forgive them or guide them to the way of righteousness. It serves as a warning to those who deliberately choose to deny the truth and commit evil deeds, highlighting the consequences of their actions in the afterlife. The verse also implies that forgiveness and guidance are available to those who sincerely repent and seek Allah's mercy, but those who remain defiant until the end will face the ultimate punishment for their choices.
orig: إن الذين كفروا وظلموا لم يكن الله ليغفر لهم ولا ليهديهم طريقا

translation: Except the way to Hell, they will abide in it forever, and that is easy for Allah.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the severity and permanence of the punishment in Hell for those who reject Allah's guidance. It asserts that the path to Hell is the only destination for the disbelievers, and they will remain there for eternity. The verse also highlights Allah's power and control over all things, stating that condemning the disbelievers to an eternal punishment in Hell is easy for Him. This serves as a warning to those who refuse to follow the right path and a reminder of Allah's ultimate authority and ability to mete out justice in the afterlife.
orig: إلا طريق جهنم خالدين فيها أبدا وكان ذلك على الله يسيرا

translation: O mankind, the Messenger has come to you with the truth from your Lord, so believe; it is better for you. But if you disbelieve - then indeed, to Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and earth. And ever is Allah Knowing and Wise.
interpretation: This verse is a call to all of humanity to believe in the message brought by the Prophet Muhammad, which is the truth from Allah. It emphasizes that believing in this message is in the best interest of every individual, as it will lead to their ultimate success and salvation. On the other hand, the verse warns that disbelief will not harm Allah in any way, as He is the Owner and Controller of everything in the heavens and the earth. The verse also highlights two of Allah's attributes: His Knowledge and Wisdom. This implies that Allah knows what is best for His creation and has sent His message with wisdom and purpose. Believing in Allah's message is, therefore, the wise choice for every human being.
orig: يا أيها الناس قد جاءكم الرسول بالحق من ربكم فآمنوا خيرا لكم وإن تكفروا فإن لله ما في السماوات والأرض وكان الله عليما حكيما

translation: O People of the Scripture, do not exaggerate in your religion or say about Allah except the truth. The Messiah, Jesus, the son of Mary, was but a messenger of Allah and His word which He directed to Mary and a soul [created at a command] from Him. So believe in Allah and His messengers. And do not say, "Three"; desist - it is better for you. Indeed, Allah is but one God. Exalted is He above having a son. To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth. And sufficient is Allah as Disposer of affairs.
interpretation: This verse warns Christians against exaggerating the status of Jesus and believing in the Trinity. It emphasizes that Jesus was a prophet and servant of God, not divine himself or the literal son of God. God is absolutely one and singular, without any partners or offspring. Belief in the Oneness of God (Tawheed) is paramount, while attributing divine qualities to Jesus or believing in the Trinity is prohibited. The verse calls Christians to correct their beliefs and accept pure monotheism.
orig: يا أهل الكتاب لا تغلوا في دينكم ولا تقولوا على الله إلا الحق إنما المسيح عيسى ابن مريم رسول الله وكلمته ألقاها إلى مريم وروح منه فآمنوا بالله ورسله ولا تقولوا ثلاثة انتهوا خيرا لكم إنما الله إله واحد سبحانه أن يكون له ولد له ما في السماوات وما في الأرض وكفى بالله وكيلا

translation: Never would the Messiah disdain to be a servant of Allah, nor would the angels near [to Him]. And whoever disdains His worship and is arrogant - He will gather them to Himself all together.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of humility and submission to Allah, even for those held in high regard such as the Messiah (Jesus) and the angels. It suggests that no one is above serving Allah and that those who reject His worship out of pride or arrogance will ultimately be gathered before Him for judgment. The verse highlights the fundamental principle in Islam that all beings, regardless of their status, are servants of Allah and should devote themselves to His worship and obedience.
orig: لن يستنكف المسيح أن يكون عبدا لله ولا الملائكة المقربون ومن يستنكف عن عبادته ويستكبر فسيحشرهم إليه جميعا

translation: As for those who believed and did righteous deeds, He will give them in full their rewards and grant them extra from His bounty. But as for those who disdained and were arrogant, He will punish them with a painful punishment, and they will not find for themselves besides Allah any protector or helper.
interpretation: This verse highlights the consequences of belief and disbelief in Allah. Those who have faith and do good deeds will be rewarded generously by Allah, both in this world and the Hereafter. He will grant them even more than what they deserve out of His infinite grace and mercy. On the other hand, those who are too proud to submit to Allah and reject His message will face a severe and painful punishment. They will have no one to protect them or come to their aid besides Allah, emphasizing the importance of humbling oneself before the Almighty and following the path of righteousness.
orig: فأما الذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات فيوفيهم أجورهم ويزيدهم من فضله وأما الذين استنكفوا واستكبروا فيعذبهم عذابا أليما ولا يجدون لهم من دون الله وليا ولا نصيرا

translation: O mankind, there has come to you a conclusive proof from your Lord, and We have sent down to you a clear light.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of the divine message that has been sent to humanity. The "conclusive proof" refers to the clear signs and evidences that demonstrate the truth of the message, leaving no room for doubt. The "clear light" symbolizes the guidance and enlightenment that the Qur'an provides, illuminating the path to righteousness and dispelling the darkness of ignorance and disbelief. It is an invitation for all people to recognize and accept the truth that has been revealed, and to follow the guidance that will lead them to success in this life and the hereafter.
orig: يا أيها الناس قد جاءكم برهان من ربكم وأنزلنا إليكم نورا مبينا

translation: So as for those who believed in Allah and held fast to Him - He will admit them to His mercy and bounty and guide them to Himself on a straight path.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of having strong faith in Allah and staying steadfast on His path. Those who sincerely believe in Allah and hold tight to their faith will be rewarded with Allah's mercy, grace, and guidance. Allah will lead them on the straight path, which is the path of righteousness and success in this world and the hereafter. This verse serves as a reminder for believers to remain committed to their faith, as it is the key to attaining Allah's pleasure and entering Paradise.
orig: فأما الذين آمنوا بالله واعتصموا به فسيدخلهم في رحمة منه وفضل ويهديهم إليه صراطا مستقيما

translation: They request from you a [legal] ruling. Say, "Allah gives you a ruling concerning one having neither descendants nor ascendants [as heirs]." If a man dies, leaving no child but [only] a sister, she will have half of what he left. And he inherits from her if she [dies and] has no child. But if there are two sisters [or more], they will have two-thirds of what he left. If there are both brothers and sisters, the male will have the share of two females. Allah makes clear to you [His law], lest you go astray. And Allah is Knowing of all things.
interpretation: This verse provides guidance on the Islamic rules of inheritance, specifically in the case where a person dies without leaving any descendants or ascendants. It clarifies that if a man dies leaving only a sister, she is entitled to half of his inheritance. If the deceased woman has no children, her brother would inherit from her. In the case of two or more sisters, they collectively receive two-thirds of the inheritance. When there are both brothers and sisters, the male's share is twice that of the female. This verse emphasizes that Allah clarifies these laws to prevent people from straying, and it highlights Allah's all-encompassing knowledge.
orig: يستفتونك قل الله يفتيكم في الكلالة إن امرؤ هلك ليس له ولد وله أخت فلها نصف ما ترك وهو يرثها إن لم يكن لها ولد فإن كانتا اثنتين فلهما الثلثان مما ترك وإن كانوا إخوة رجالا ونساء فللذكر مثل حظ الأنثيين يبين الله لكم أن تضلوا والله بكل شيء عليم

translation: O you who have believed, fulfill [all] contracts. Lawful for you are the animals of grazing livestock except for that which is recited to you [in this Qur'an] - hunting not being permitted while you are in the state of ihram. Indeed, Allah ordains what He intends.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of fulfilling contracts and agreements, which is a fundamental principle in Islam. It also highlights the permissibility of consuming certain animals, except for those that are specifically prohibited. The verse further stresses that hunting is not allowed during the state of ihram (ritual purity) while performing Hajj or Umrah. Ultimately, the verse affirms Allah's absolute authority in determining what is lawful and unlawful, emphasizing the importance of submitting to His will and following His commandments.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا أوفوا بالعقود أحلت لكم بهيمة الأنعام إلا ما يتلى عليكم غير محلي الصيد وأنتم حرم إن الله يحكم ما يريد

translation: O you who have believed, do not violate the rites of Allah or [the sanctity of] the sacred month or [neglect the marking of] the sacrificial animals and garlanding [them] or [violate the safety of] those coming to the Sacred House seeking bounty from their Lord and [His] approval. But when you come out of ihram, then [you may] hunt. And do not let the hatred of a people for having obstructed you from al-Masjid al-Haram lead you to transgress. And cooperate in righteousness and piety, but do not cooperate in sin and aggression. And fear Allah; indeed, Allah is severe in penalty.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the sanctity of the religious rites and symbols ordained by Allah, particularly during the sacred months and at sacred places like the Ka'bah. Muslims are prohibited from violating these sanctities or transgressing against others, even if there is hostility or enmity between them. The verse promotes righteousness, piety and cooperation in matters of goodness, while warning against sin, aggression and transgression of limits set by Allah. It reminds believers to be always conscious of Allah and mindful of the severe punishment for those who violate His commands and prohibitions.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا لا تحلوا شعائر الله ولا الشهر الحرام ولا الهدي ولا القلائد ولا آمين البيت الحرام يبتغون فضلا من ربهم ورضوانا وإذا حللتم فاصطادوا ولا يجرمنكم شنآن قوم أن صدوكم عن المسجد الحرام أن تعتدوا وتعاونوا على البر والتقوى ولا تعاونوا على الإثم والعدوان واتقوا الله إن الله شديد العقاب

translation: Prohibited to you are dead animals, blood, the flesh of swine, and that which has been dedicated to other than Allah, and [those animals] killed by strangling or by a violent blow or by a head-long fall or by the goring of horns, and those from which a wild animal has eaten, except what you [are able to] slaughter [before its death], and those which are sacrificed on stone altars, and [prohibited is] that you seek decision through divining arrows. That is grave disobedience. This day those who disbelieve have despaired of [defeating] your religion; so fear them not, but fear Me. This day I have perfected for you your religion and completed My favor upon you and have approved for you Islam as religion. But whoever is forced by severe hunger with no inclination to sin - then indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of following the dietary laws prescribed by Allah. It serves as a reminder that Muslims should only consume what is permissible (halal) and avoid what is prohibited (haram). The verse also highlights the significance of the day when this revelation was received, as it marks the completion of the Islamic religion and Allah's favor upon the believers. It provides reassurance that even in times of extreme hardship or hunger, if one is forced to consume something forbidden without the intention of sinning, Allah's forgiveness and mercy will encompass them.
orig: حرمت عليكم الميتة والدم ولحم الخنزير وما أهل لغير الله به والمنخنقة والموقوذة والمتردية والنطيحة وما أكل السبع إلا ما ذكيتم وما ذبح على النصب وأن تستقسموا بالأزلام ذلكم فسق اليوم يئس الذين كفروا من دينكم فلا تخشوهم واخشون اليوم أكملت لكم دينكم وأتممت عليكم نعمتي ورضيت لكم الإسلام دينا فمن اضطر في مخمصة غير متجانف لإثم فإن الله غفور رحيم

translation: They ask you, [O Muhammad], what has been made lawful for them. Say, "Lawful for you are [all] good foods and [game caught by] what you have trained of hunting animals which you train as Allah has taught you. So eat of what they catch for you, and mention the name of Allah upon it, and fear Allah." Indeed, Allah is swift in account.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the permissibility of consuming wholesome and pure foods, including the meat of animals caught by trained hunting animals. It highlights the importance of mentioning Allah's name over the caught game and being mindful of Allah in all actions. The verse serves as a reminder that Allah is swift in reckoning and that believers should maintain consciousness of Him in their dietary choices and daily lives.
orig: يسألونك ماذا أحل لهم قل أحل لكم الطيبات وما علمتم من الجوارح مكلبين تعلمونهن مما علمكم الله فكلوا مما أمسكن عليكم واذكروا اسم الله عليه واتقوا الله إن الله سريع الحساب

translation: This day [all] good foods have been made lawful, and the food of those who were given the Scripture is lawful for you and your food is lawful for them. And [lawful in marriage are] chaste women from among the believers and chaste women from among those who were given the Scripture before you, when you have given them their due compensation, desiring chastity, not unlawful sexual intercourse or taking [secret] lovers. And whoever denies the faith - his work has become worthless, and he, in the Hereafter, will be among the losers.
interpretation: This verse highlights the permissibility of consuming good and lawful food, including the food of the People of the Book (Jews and Christians). It also establishes the allowance of marrying chaste believing women and chaste women from the People of the Book, provided that they are given their dowries and the marriage is based on chastity and not mere sexual desires or secret affairs. The verse emphasizes that those who reject faith will find their deeds rendered worthless in the Hereafter, and they will be among the losers. This underscores the importance of faith and adherence to Islamic principles in all aspects of life, including dietary choices and marital relationships.
orig: اليوم أحل لكم الطيبات وطعام الذين أوتوا الكتاب حل لكم وطعامكم حل لهم والمحصنات من المؤمنات والمحصنات من الذين أوتوا الكتاب من قبلكم إذا آتيتموهن أجورهن محصنين غير مسافحين ولا متخذي أخدان ومن يكفر بالإيمان فقد حبط عمله وهو في الآخرة من الخاسرين

translation: O you who have believed, when you rise to [perform] prayer, wash your faces and your forearms to the elbows and wipe over your heads and wash your feet to the ankles. And if you are in a state of janabah, then purify yourselves. But if you are ill or on a journey or one of you comes from the place of relieving himself or you have contacted women and do not find water, then seek clean earth and wipe over your faces and hands with it. Allah does not intend to make difficulty for you, but He intends to purify you and complete His favor upon you that you may be grateful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of physical and spiritual purification before prayer. It outlines the steps of ablution (wudu) which involve washing the face, arms, head, and feet. In cases where water is unavailable or one is physically unable, tayammum (dry ablution) with clean earth is permitted as a substitute. The verse underscores that these rituals are not meant to burden believers, but rather to purify them both physically and spiritually. Ultimately, these acts of purification and prayer are meant to evoke a sense of gratitude towards Allah for His favors and blessings upon the believers.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا إذا قمتم إلى الصلاة فاغسلوا وجوهكم وأيديكم إلى المرافق وامسحوا برءوسكم وأرجلكم إلى الكعبين وإن كنتم جنبا فاطهروا وإن كنتم مرضى أو على سفر أو جاء أحد منكم من الغائط أو لامستم النساء فلم تجدوا ماء فتيمموا صعيدا طيبا فامسحوا بوجوهكم وأيديكم منه ما يريد الله ليجعل عليكم من حرج ولكن يريد ليطهركم وليتم نعمته عليكم لعلكم تشكرون

translation: And remember the favor of Allah upon you and His covenant with which He bound you when you said, "We hear and we obey"; and fear Allah. Indeed, Allah is Knowing of that within the breasts.
interpretation: This verse reminds believers of the great favor and blessing that Allah has bestowed upon them by guiding them to Islam and making a covenant with them. The covenant refers to the pledge of allegiance and obedience that the believers made to Allah and His Messenger. By saying "We hear and we obey", the believers affirmed their commitment to submit to Allah's commands and prohibitions. The verse then enjoins taqwa (consciousness and fear of Allah), emphasizing that Allah knows the secrets within people's hearts. This underscores the importance of having sincere faith and devotion, as Allah is fully aware of one's innermost thoughts and intentions, not just outward actions and words. Upholding the covenant with Allah and being mindful of Him will lead to His pleasure and rewards in this life and the Hereafter.
orig: واذكروا نعمة الله عليكم وميثاقه الذي واثقكم به إذ قلتم سمعنا وأطعنا واتقوا الله إن الله عليم بذات الصدور

translation: O you who have believed, be persistently standing firm for Allah, witnesses in justice, and do not let the hatred of a people prevent you from being just. Be just; that is nearer to righteousness. And fear Allah; indeed, Allah is Acquainted with what you do.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of upholding justice and fairness, even in the face of personal animosity or hatred. It calls upon believers to stand firm in their faith and to act as witnesses for the sake of Allah, not allowing their emotions or biases to sway their judgment. The verse reminds us that being just is a fundamental aspect of righteousness and that we should always strive to act with integrity and impartiality. It also serves as a warning that Allah is aware of our actions and intentions, encouraging us to be mindful of our behavior and to fear His judgment.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا كونوا قوامين لله شهداء بالقسط ولا يجرمنكم شنآن قوم على ألا تعدلوا اعدلوا هو أقرب للتقوى واتقوا الله إن الله خبير بما تعملون

translation: Allah has promised those who believe and do righteous deeds [that] for them there is forgiveness and great reward.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of faith and good deeds in attaining God's forgiveness and reward in the Hereafter. It serves as an encouragement and motivation for believers to stay steadfast in their faith and to actively engage in righteous actions throughout their lives. The promise of forgiveness provides hope and solace to those who may have faltered or sinned, assuring them of God's mercy if they sincerely repent and strive to reform themselves. The mention of a "great reward" highlights the immense value and significance of the afterlife, indicating that the ultimate goal of a believer should be to secure their place in Paradise through their belief and virtuous conduct in this worldly life.
orig: وعد الله الذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات لهم مغفرة وأجر عظيم

translation: But those who disbelieved and denied Our signs - those are the companions of Hellfire.
interpretation: This verse serves as a stern warning to those who reject faith in Allah and deny the truth of His revelations. It emphasizes that those who choose to disbelieve and persistently refuse to acknowledge the signs and messages sent by Allah will face severe consequences in the afterlife. Their ultimate abode will be the Hellfire, where they will suffer eternal punishment for their ingratitude and rebellion against their Creator. The verse highlights the gravity of disbelief and the importance of accepting and following the guidance provided by Allah through His signs and revelations.
orig: والذين كفروا وكذبوا بآياتنا أولئك أصحاب الجحيم

translation: O you who have believed, remember the favor of Allah upon you when a people determined to extend their hands [in aggression] against you, but He withheld their hands from you; and fear Allah. And upon Allah let the believers rely.
interpretation: This verse is a reminder to the believers of Allah's protection and favor upon them. It refers to a specific incident where an enemy had planned to attack the Muslims, but Allah intervened and prevented them from carrying out their evil intentions. The verse encourages the believers to always be mindful of Allah's blessings, to fear Him, and to put their trust in Him alone. It emphasizes that the believers should rely on Allah's support and protection, rather than their own strength or resources. This reliance on Allah is a fundamental aspect of faith and a source of inner peace and security for the believers.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا اذكروا نعمت الله عليكم إذ هم قوم أن يبسطوا إليكم أيديهم فكف أيديهم عنكم واتقوا الله وعلى الله فليتوكل المؤمنون

translation: And indeed Allah took the covenant of the Children of Israel and We appointed twelve leaders among them. And Allah said: "I am with you if you perform As-Salat (Iqamat-as-Salat) and give Zakat and believe in My Messengers; honor and assist them, and lend to Allah a good loan. Verily, I will remit your sins and admit you to Gardens under which rivers flow (in Paradise). But if any of you after this, disbelieved, he has indeed gone astray from the Straight Path."
interpretation: This verse highlights the covenant that Allah took from the Children of Israel, appointing twelve leaders among them. Allah promises to be with them if they fulfill certain conditions: establishing prayer, giving charity, believing in and supporting His messengers, and lending to Allah a goodly loan. In return, Allah assures them that He will forgive their sins and admit them into Paradise with its flowing rivers. However, the verse also warns that if any of them disbelieve after this covenant, they have strayed from the right path. This emphasizes the importance of faith, obedience to Allah's commands, and fulfilling one's commitments to attain Allah's pleasure and eternal reward.
orig: ولقد أخذ الله ميثاق بني إسرائيل وبعثنا منهم اثني عشر نقيبا وقال الله إني معكم لئن أقمتم الصلاة وآتيتم الزكاة وآمنتم برسلي وعزرتموهم وأقرضتم الله قرضا حسنا لأكفرن عنكم سيئاتكم ولأدخلنكم جنات تجري من تحتها الأنهار فمن كفر بعد ذلك منكم فقد ضل سواء السبيل

translation: So for their breaking of the covenant We cursed them and made their hearts hard. They distort words from their [proper] usages and have forgotten a portion of that of which they were reminded. And you will still observe deceit among them, except a few of them. But pardon them and overlook [their misdeeds]. Indeed, Allah loves the doers of good.
interpretation: This verse refers to the Jewish people who broke their covenant with Allah. As a result, Allah cursed them and hardened their hearts, making them stubborn and unrepentant. They began to distort the meaning of the scriptures and forgot much of what they had been taught. The verse points out that dishonesty and betrayal are common traits among them, with only a few exceptions. However, Muslims are instructed to pardon and overlook their misdeeds, as Allah loves those who do good and show mercy, even in the face of hostility and enmity from others. This exemplifies the Islamic principle of responding to evil with good and showing forgiveness and compassion.
orig: فبما نقضهم ميثاقهم لعناهم وجعلنا قلوبهم قاسية يحرفون الكلم عن مواضعه ونسوا حظا مما ذكروا به ولا تزال تطلع على خائنة منهم إلا قليلا منهم فاعف عنهم واصفح إن الله يحب المحسنين

translation: And from those who said, "We are Christians" We took their covenant; but they forgot a portion of that of which they were reminded. So We caused among them animosity and hatred until the Day of Resurrection. And Allah is going to inform them about what they used to do.
interpretation: This verse highlights the consequences faced by those Christians who failed to uphold their covenant with God. They neglected and forgot a significant part of the teachings and reminders given to them. As a result, God allowed animosity and hatred to arise among them, which will persist until the Day of Judgment. This discord and enmity among them is a direct consequence of their negligence and disregard for the divine message. The verse also serves as a warning that God is fully aware of their actions and will inform them of the repercussions of their deeds in the Hereafter.
orig: ومن الذين قالوا إنا نصارى أخذنا ميثاقهم فنسوا حظا مما ذكروا به فأغرينا بينهم العداوة والبغضاء إلى يوم القيامة وسوف ينبئهم الله بما كانوا يصنعون

translation: O People of the Scripture, there has come to you Our Messenger to make clear to you much of what you used to conceal of the Scripture and to pardon much. There has come to you from Allah a light and a clear Book.
interpretation: This verse is addressing the People of the Book, namely the Jews and Christians, informing them that a Messenger (Prophet Muhammad) has come to them to clarify many of the truths they used to hide from their scriptures. The Messenger also pardons much of their wrongdoings. The verse emphasizes that this Messenger has come with a light (guidance) and a clear Book (the Qur'an) from Allah. It implies that the People of the Book should accept this message and follow the guidance brought by the Prophet, as it will lead them to the truth and the right path, correcting the distortions and concealments that have occurred in their religious traditions over time.
orig: يا أهل الكتاب قد جاءكم رسولنا يبين لكم كثيرا مما كنتم تخفون من الكتاب ويعفو عن كثير قد جاءكم من الله نور وكتاب مبين

translation: By which Allah guides those who pursue His pleasure to the ways of peace and brings them out from darknesses into the light, by His permission, and guides them to a straight path.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah guides those who sincerely seek His pleasure and follow His commands. He leads them out of the darkness of ignorance, disbelief, and sin, and brings them into the light of knowledge, faith, and righteousness. This guidance is achieved through Allah's permission and mercy, as He directs His sincere servants to the straight path that leads to success in this world and the hereafter. The verse highlights the importance of seeking Allah's pleasure and submitting to His will in order to attain true peace, enlightenment, and guidance in life.
orig: يهدي به الله من اتبع رضوانه سبل السلام ويخرجهم من الظلمات إلى النور بإذنه ويهديهم إلى صراط مستقيم

translation: They have certainly disbelieved who say, "Allah is the Messiah, the son of Mary" Say, "Then who could prevent Allah at all if He had intended to destroy the Messiah, the son of Mary, or his mother or everyone on the earth?" And to Allah belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth and whatever is between them. He creates what He wills, and Allah is over all things competent.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute oneness and sovereignty of Allah. It refutes the Christian belief that Jesus is divine or the son of God. The Qur'an asserts that Jesus and his mother Mary were merely human beings, subject to Allah's will and power. If Allah willed, He could destroy them like any other creature. This highlights Allah's omnipotence and the fact that everything in the heavens and earth belongs to Him alone as the sole creator and sustainer. The verse aims to correct the grave error of attributing divinity to anyone besides Allah, which is considered disbelief in Islam.
orig: لقد كفر الذين قالوا إن الله هو المسيح ابن مريم قل فمن يملك من الله شيئا إن أراد أن يهلك المسيح ابن مريم وأمه ومن في الأرض جميعا ولله ملك السماوات والأرض وما بينهما يخلق ما يشاء والله على كل شيء قدير

translation: The Jews and the Christians say, "We are the children of Allah and His beloved." Say, "Then why does He punish you for your sins?" Rather, you are human beings from among those He has created. He forgives whom He wills, and He punishes whom He wills. And to Allah belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth and whatever is between them, and to Him is the [final] destination.
interpretation: This verse addresses the claims of some Jews and Christians who considered themselves to be the chosen people of God and immune from His punishment due to their special status. The Quran refutes this notion, emphasizing that all humans are accountable before God for their deeds. God's forgiveness and punishment are based on His divine will and justice, not on the false assumptions of any particular group. The verse also affirms God's absolute sovereignty over the entire universe and the ultimate return of all creation to Him. This serves as a reminder for humility and the necessity of seeking God's mercy and forgiveness through sincere faith and righteous actions.
orig: وقالت اليهود والنصارى نحن أبناء الله وأحباؤه قل فلم يعذبكم بذنوبكم بل أنتم بشر ممن خلق يغفر لمن يشاء ويعذب من يشاء ولله ملك السماوات والأرض وما بينهما وإليه المصير

translation: O People of the Scripture, there has come to you Our Messenger to make clear to you [the religion] after a period [of suspension] from the messengers, lest you say, "There came not to us any bringer of good tidings or a warner." But there has come to you a bringer of good tidings and a warner. And Allah is over all things competent.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of the Prophet Muhammad's mission to the People of the Book (Jews and Christians). It suggests that after a long period without prophets, they might have claimed that no one had come to guide them or warn them. However, with the arrival of Muhammad, they have received both a bearer of good news and a warner. The verse also affirms Allah's power and ability to send messengers as He wills, highlighting His control over all affairs. This serves as a reminder to the People of the Book to acknowledge and accept the message of Islam, as it is a continuation of the divine guidance they had previously received.
orig: يا أهل الكتاب قد جاءكم رسولنا يبين لكم على فترة من الرسل أن تقولوا ما جاءنا من بشير ولا نذير فقد جاءكم بشير ونذير والله على كل شيء قدير

translation: And [mention, O Muhammad], when Moses said to his people, "O my people, remember the favor of Allah upon you when He appointed among you prophets and made you possessors and gave you that which He had not given anyone among the worlds.
interpretation: This verse reminds the Children of Israel of the great blessings and favors that Allah bestowed upon them. These favors include appointing prophets from among them to guide them, granting them kingship and authority, and providing them with blessings and provisions that were not given to any other nation in their time. It emphasizes the importance of acknowledging and appreciating Allah's favors and using them in a way that pleases Him, rather than being ungrateful or arrogant. The verse also serves as a reminder for all believers to reflect upon the blessings in their own lives and to use them in a way that is pleasing to Allah.
orig: وإذ قال موسى لقومه يا قوم اذكروا نعمة الله عليكم إذ جعل فيكم أنبياء وجعلكم ملوكا وآتاكم ما لم يؤت أحدا من العالمين

translation: O my people, enter the Holy Land which Allah has assigned to you and do not turn back [from fighting in Allah 's cause] and [thus] become losers.
interpretation: This verse is a call to the Israelites to enter the Holy Land that God had promised them. It warns them against turning away from this divine command out of fear or doubt, as doing so would be an act of disobedience that would lead to loss and failure. The verse emphasizes the importance of faith, trust in God's plan, and willingness to strive in His cause, even when faced with challenges or hardships. It teaches that ultimate success lies in following the path that God has ordained, while turning away from it leads to spiritual ruin.
orig: يا قوم ادخلوا الأرض المقدسة التي كتب الله لكم ولا ترتدوا على أدباركم فتنقلبوا خاسرين

translation: They said, "O Moses, indeed within it is a people of tyrannical strength, and indeed, we will not enter it until they leave it; but if they leave it, then we will enter."
interpretation: This verse highlights the fear and hesitation of the Israelites when they were commanded to enter the Promised Land. Despite Moses' encouragement, they were intimidated by the strength and might of the inhabitants of the land, the Canaanites. The Israelites expressed their reluctance to confront these people, stating that they would not enter the land unless the current inhabitants departed. This response demonstrates a lack of faith and trust in God's promise and plan for them. It serves as a reminder for believers to have faith in God's guidance and to face challenges with courage and reliance on divine support, rather than being overcome by fear or doubt.
orig: قالوا يا موسى إن فيها قوما جبارين وإنا لن ندخلها حتى يخرجوا منها فإن يخرجوا منها فإنا داخلون

translation: Said two men from those who feared [to disobey] upon whom Allah had bestowed favor, "Enter upon them through the gate, for when you have entered it, you will be predominant. And upon Allah rely, if you should be believers."
interpretation: This verse is encouraging the believers to have faith in Allah's plan and to take action with courage and reliance on Him. The two men mentioned were likely among the twelve scouts sent by Moses to explore Canaan. Despite the strength of the enemy, they trusted in Allah's promise of victory to the believers. They advised their people to enter the city boldly, putting their trust in Allah's support. It conveys the message that with faith and reliance on Allah, believers can overcome daunting challenges and achieve success in their righteous endeavors. Steadfast trust in Allah's aid is a hallmark of true faith.
orig: قال رجلان من الذين يخافون أنعم الله عليهما ادخلوا عليهم الباب فإذا دخلتموه فإنكم غالبون وعلى الله فتوكلوا إن كنتم مؤمنين

translation: They said, "O Moses, indeed we will not enter it, ever, as long as they are within it; so go, you and your Lord, and fight. Indeed, we are remaining right here."
interpretation: This verse reflects the fear and lack of trust that the Israelites had in God's promise to grant them victory over the people of Palestine. Despite witnessing God's miracles and favors upon them, they refused to fight and conquer the Holy Land as commanded by God. Instead, they told Moses to go with his Lord and fight, while they would remain sitting there. This shows their weakness in faith and their disobedience to God and His messenger. It is a lesson for believers to trust in God's promise, obey His commands, and strive in His cause with courage and determination, no matter how difficult the challenges may seem.
orig: قالوا يا موسى إنا لن ندخلها أبدا ما داموا فيها فاذهب أنت وربك فقاتلا إنا هاهنا قاعدون

translation: He said, "My Lord, I have control only over myself and my brother, so separate us from the defiantly disobedient people."
interpretation: This verse reflects the prophet Moses' plea to Allah to separate him and his brother Aaron from the disobedient and rebellious people among the Children of Israel. It shows Moses' acknowledgment of his limited power and control, which extends only to himself and his brother. He beseeches Allah to make a distinction between them and the transgressors, indicating his desire to disassociate from their sinful actions and to be counted among the righteous. This verse emphasizes the importance of taking responsibility for one's own actions, seeking Allah's help in the face of adversity, and distancing oneself from those who persistently engage in defiant disobedience to Allah's commands.
orig: قال رب إني لا أملك إلا نفسي وأخي فافرق بيننا وبين القوم الفاسقين

translation: [Allah] said, "Then indeed, it is forbidden to them for forty years [in which] they will wander throughout the land. So do not grieve over the defiantly disobedient people."
interpretation: This verse refers to the punishment that Allah decreed upon the Children of Israel for their disobedience and lack of faith. Despite witnessing the clear signs and miracles of Allah, they refused to enter the holy land as commanded. As a consequence, Allah prohibited them from entering the land for forty years, leaving them to wander in the wilderness. The verse also serves as a consolation to Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ), instructing him not to feel sorrow or regret over those who persist in transgression and defiance against Allah's commands. It emphasizes that the fate of the disobedient is a result of their own actions and that the Prophet's duty is only to convey the message, while the ultimate judgment rests with Allah.
orig: قال فإنها محرمة عليهم أربعين سنة يتيهون في الأرض فلا تأس على القوم الفاسقين

translation: And recite to them the story of Adam's two sons, in truth, when they both offered a sacrifice [to Allah], and it was accepted from one of them but was not accepted from the other. Said [the latter], "I will surely kill you." Said [the former], "Indeed, Allah only accepts from the righteous [who fear Him].
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of sincerity and righteousness in acts of worship. The story of Adam's two sons teaches us that Allah does not accept deeds based on their outward appearance or quantity, but rather on the purity of intention and the righteousness of the individual. It also emphasizes the gravity of envy and jealousy, as it can lead to terrible consequences, such as the threat of murder. The verse reminds us to focus on our own spiritual growth and to strive for righteousness, rather than comparing ourselves to others or harboring negative feelings towards them.
orig: واتل عليهم نبأ ابني آدم بالحق إذ قربا قربانا فتقبل من أحدهما ولم يتقبل من الآخر قال لأقتلنك قال إنما يتقبل الله من المتقين

translation: If you should raise your hand against me to kill me - I shall not raise my hand against you to kill you. Indeed, I fear Allah, Lord of the worlds.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of fearing Allah and refraining from violence, even in self-defense. It teaches that a true believer should prioritize their faith and obedience to Allah over their own life. The verse also highlights the concept of forgiveness and not retaliating with violence, even when faced with aggression. It serves as a reminder that ultimately, one should fear Allah and seek His pleasure, rather than succumbing to worldly desires or emotions such as anger or revenge.
orig: لئن بسطت إلي يدك لتقتلني ما أنا بباسط يدي إليك لأقتلك إني أخاف الله رب العالمين

translation: Indeed, I want you to be burdened with my sin and your sin so you will be among the companions of the Fire. And that is the recompense of the wrongdoers.
interpretation: This verse is a warning against leading others astray or taking on the sins of others. It emphasizes that each person is ultimately responsible for their own actions and will face the consequences in the Hereafter. Those who misguide others and carry the burden of their sins, in addition to their own, will be among the people of Hellfire. This is the just recompense for those who choose to wrong themselves and others by straying from the right path and encouraging others to do the same. The verse serves as a reminder to be mindful of one's actions and to avoid bearing the sins of others.
orig: إني أريد أن تبوء بإثمي وإثمك فتكون من أصحاب النار وذلك جزاء الظالمين

translation: And his soul permitted to him the murder of his brother, so he killed him and became among the losers.
interpretation: This verse is a reminder of the grave consequences of letting one's ego and anger take control. It refers to the story of Cain and Abel, the sons of Adam. Cain's jealousy and anger towards his brother Abel led him to commit the ultimate sin of murder. By giving in to his lower self and committing this heinous act, Cain became one of the losers in the sight of Allah. The verse emphasizes the importance of controlling one's ego, emotions and desires. Succumbing to negative impulses can lead one to transgress the limits set by Allah and bring about one's own spiritual downfall. It is a warning for mankind to be vigilant against the whisperings of the ego and to strive for righteousness.
orig: فطوعت له نفسه قتل أخيه فقتله فأصبح من الخاسرين

translation: Then Allah sent a crow searching in the ground to show him how to hide the disgrace of his brother. He said, "O woe to me! Have I failed to be like this crow and hide the body of my brother?" And he became of the regretful.
interpretation: This verse teaches us the importance of seeking knowledge and guidance, even from unlikely sources. The crow, often seen as a lowly creature, becomes a teacher for the son of Adam, showing him how to properly bury his brother's body. It also highlights the value of humility and the danger of arrogance. The man realizes his own shortcomings and regrets his actions, understanding that he should have sought wisdom instead of acting out of anger and jealousy. This story encourages us to be open to learning from all of Allah's creation and to turn to Him in repentance when we make mistakes.
orig: فبعث الله غرابا يبحث في الأرض ليريه كيف يواري سوءة أخيه قال يا ويلتا أعجزت أن أكون مثل هذا الغراب فأواري سوءة أخي فأصبح من النادمين

translation: Because of that, We decreed upon the Children of Israel that whoever kills a soul unless for a soul or for corruption [done] in the land - it is as if he had slain mankind entirely. And whoever saves one - it is as if he had saved mankind entirely. And our messengers had certainly come to them with clear proofs. Then indeed many of them, [even] after that, throughout the land, were transgressors.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the sanctity of human life and the gravity of taking it unjustly. It declares that killing an innocent person is akin to killing all of humanity, while saving a life is like saving all of humanity. This highlights the immense value Islam places on each individual life. The verse also serves as a reminder to the Children of Israel, who were given clear signs by the prophets, yet many of them still transgressed and committed sins. It underscores the importance of adhering to divine guidance and the consequences of straying from the righteous path.
orig: من أجل ذلك كتبنا على بني إسرائيل أنه من قتل نفسا بغير نفس أو فساد في الأرض فكأنما قتل الناس جميعا ومن أحياها فكأنما أحيا الناس جميعا ولقد جاءتهم رسلنا بالبينات ثم إن كثيرا منهم بعد ذلك في الأرض لمسرفون

translation: Indeed, the penalty for those who wage war against Allah and His Messenger and strive upon earth [to cause] corruption is none but that they be killed or crucified or that their hands and feet be cut off from opposite sides or that they be exiled from the land. That is for them a disgrace in this world; and for them in the Hereafter is a great punishment.
interpretation: This verse outlines the severe punishments prescribed for those who actively oppose Allah and His Messenger and spread corruption and mischief in the land. The punishments mentioned - execution, crucifixion, cutting off hands and feet from opposite sides, or exile - signify the gravity of the crime and serve as a deterrent. These harsh penalties reflect the seriousness of waging war against the divine order and causing disorder in society. The verse also emphasizes that such transgressors will face humiliation in this world and a severe punishment in the Hereafter, underlining the consequences of their actions both in the present life and the afterlife.
orig: إنما جزاء الذين يحاربون الله ورسوله ويسعون في الأرض فسادا أن يقتلوا أو يصلبوا أو تقطع أيديهم وأرجلهم من خلاف أو ينفوا من الأرض ذلك لهم خزي في الدنيا ولهم في الآخرة عذاب عظيم

translation: Except for those who repent before you apprehend them. And know that Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the mercy and forgiveness of Allah towards those who sincerely repent for their wrongdoings before facing the consequences of their actions. It encourages people to turn back to Allah and seek His forgiveness, assuring them that Allah is ever ready to forgive and show mercy to those who genuinely seek it. The verse also serves as a reminder for believers to be forgiving and merciful towards others who repent and seek forgiveness, just as they would want Allah's forgiveness and mercy for themselves.
orig: إلا الذين تابوا من قبل أن تقدروا عليهم فاعلموا أن الله غفور رحيم

translation: O you who have believed, fear Allah and seek the means [of nearness] to Him and strive in His cause that you may succeed.
interpretation: This verse is a call to the believers to be mindful of Allah and to seek ways to draw closer to Him. It emphasizes the importance of striving in the path of Allah, which includes not only physical struggle but also the inner struggle against one's own desires and temptations. The verse suggests that by doing so, one may attain success and salvation in this world and the hereafter. It highlights the significance of having a strong relationship with Allah and making efforts to please Him through righteous deeds and sincere devotion.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا اتقوا الله وابتغوا إليه الوسيلة وجاهدوا في سبيله لعلكم تفلحون

translation: Indeed, those who disbelieve - if they should have all that is in the earth and the like of it with it by which to ransom themselves from the punishment of the Day of Resurrection, it will not be accepted from them, and for them is a painful punishment.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the severity and inevitability of the punishment that awaits those who reject faith in Allah. It states that even if the disbelievers were to offer all the wealth and treasures of the earth, and even double that amount, as a ransom to save themselves from the torment of the Day of Judgment, it would not be accepted from them. This highlights the gravity of their sin of disbelief and the justice of Allah in punishing them. The verse also serves as a warning to those who have not yet believed, urging them to embrace faith before it is too late, as no amount of worldly riches can save one from the consequences of rejecting Allah's message.
orig: إن الذين كفروا لو أن لهم ما في الأرض جميعا ومثله معه ليفتدوا به من عذاب يوم القيامة ما تقبل منهم ولهم عذاب أليم

translation: They will wish to get out of the Fire, but they will not [be able to] emerge from it, and for them is an enduring punishment.
interpretation: This verse speaks about the fate of those who reject God's message and persist in disbelief. It emphasizes that once they are condemned to the Fire of Hell, they will desperately desire to escape from it, but will be unable to do so. The punishment they face is not temporary, but rather an everlasting one. This serves as a severe warning for those who refuse to acknowledge the truth and a reminder of the grave consequences of leading a life without faith and righteous deeds.
orig: يريدون أن يخرجوا من النار وما هم بخارجين منها ولهم عذاب مقيم

translation: As for the thief, both male and female, amputate their hands in recompense for what they committed as a deterrent [punishment] from Allah. And Allah is Exalted in Might and Wise.
interpretation: This verse prescribes the punishment for theft in Islam. The cutting off of the hand serves as a severe deterrent and a just retribution for the crime committed, showing the seriousness of violating others' property rights in Islam. It reflects the wisdom of Allah in legislating laws that protect society and individual rights. However, this punishment is not applied automatically and has specific conditions that must be met, such as the stolen item meeting a minimum value, the theft not being driven by hunger, and the stolen goods being taken from a secured place. The verse ultimately aims to establish justice, security, and respect for ownership in society.
orig: والسارق والسارقة فاقطعوا أيديهما جزاء بما كسبا نكالا من الله والله عزيز حكيم

translation: But whoever repents after his wrongdoing and reforms, indeed, Allah will turn to him in forgiveness. Indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the boundless mercy and forgiveness of Allah. It assures us that no matter how grave our sins may be, if we sincerely repent, mend our ways, and strive to do good, Allah will forgive us. It highlights the importance of tawbah (repentance) in Islam. Tawbah involves acknowledging one's wrongdoings, feeling remorse, seeking Allah's forgiveness, and resolving not to repeat the sin. The verse also underscores two of Allah's beautiful names - Al-Ghafoor (The Most Forgiving) and Ar-Raheem (The Most Merciful), reminding us that His door of forgiveness is always open for those who turn back to Him with a sincere heart. It encourages us to never lose hope in Allah's mercy, and to constantly strive to better ourselves.
orig: فمن تاب من بعد ظلمه وأصلح فإن الله يتوب عليه إن الله غفور رحيم

translation: Do you not know that to Allah belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth? He punishes whom He wills and forgives whom He wills, and Allah is over all things competent.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute sovereignty and power of Allah over all creation. It reminds us that Allah alone has the ultimate authority to judge and either punish or forgive individuals as He sees fit, based on His infinite wisdom and justice. The verse underscores the importance of recognizing Allah's omnipotence and submitting to His will, as He has the ability to determine the fate of every soul. It also serves as a warning to those who may disbelieve or disobey Allah, while offering hope and comfort to those who seek His mercy and forgiveness. Ultimately, this verse encourages believers to live their lives with consciousness of Allah's power and to strive for His pleasure, knowing that He is the All-Mighty and the Most Merciful.
orig: ألم تعلم أن الله له ملك السماوات والأرض يعذب من يشاء ويغفر لمن يشاء والله على كل شيء قدير

translation: O Messenger, let them not grieve you who hasten into disbelief of those who say, "We believe" with their mouths, but their hearts believe not, and from among the Jews. [They are] avid listeners to falsehood, listening to another people who have not come to you. They distort words beyond their [proper] usages, saying "If you are given this, take it; but if you are not given it, then beware." But he for whom Allah intends fitnah - never will you possess [power to do] for him a thing against Allah. Those are the ones for whom Allah does not intend to purify their hearts. For them in this world is disgrace, and for them in the Hereafter is a great punishment.
interpretation: This verse is a warning to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) not to be saddened by those who rush to disbelieve, whether they are those who claim to believe with their tongues but not their hearts, or those among the Jews who eagerly listen to lies and distortions of the truth. These people twist the meanings of words to suit their own purposes, and follow the dictates of others who have not even come to the Prophet directly. The verse also notes that for those whose hearts Allah does not wish to purify, the Prophet will have no power to help them against Allah's will. Such people will face humiliation in this world and a severe punishment in the next.
orig: يا أيها الرسول لا يحزنك الذين يسارعون في الكفر من الذين قالوا آمنا بأفواههم ولم تؤمن قلوبهم ومن الذين هادوا سماعون للكذب سماعون لقوم آخرين لم يأتوك يحرفون الكلم من بعد مواضعه يقولون إن أوتيتم هذا فخذوه وإن لم تؤتوه فاحذروا ومن يرد الله فتنته فلن تملك له من الله شيئا أولئك الذين لم يرد الله أن يطهر قلوبهم لهم في الدنيا خزي ولهم في الآخرة عذاب عظيم

translation: [They are] avid listeners to falsehood, devourers of [what is] unlawful. So if they come to you, [O Muhammad], judge between them or turn away from them. And if you turn away from them - never will they harm you at all. And if you judge, judge between them with justice. Indeed, Allah loves those who act justly.
interpretation: This verse is addressing the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) regarding a group of people who are described as eager listeners to lies and consumers of unlawful gains. If they come to the Prophet seeking judgment, he has the choice to either judge between them or turn away from them. If he chooses to turn away, they will not be able to harm him in any way. However, if he decides to judge, he must do so with justice and fairness, as Allah loves those who uphold justice. The verse emphasizes the importance of maintaining integrity and impartiality when dealing with people, even if they are known for their wrongdoings.
orig: سماعون للكذب أكالون للسحت فإن جاءوك فاحكم بينهم أو أعرض عنهم وإن تعرض عنهم فلن يضروك شيئا وإن حكمت فاحكم بينهم بالقسط إن الله يحب المقسطين

translation: But how is it that they come to you for judgement while they have the Torah, in which is the judgement of Allah? Then they turn away, [even] after that; but those are not [in fact] believers.
interpretation: This verse questions the sincerity and faith of those who seek the Prophet's judgement despite having the Torah, which contains Allah's laws and commandments. It suggests that their act of turning away from the Prophet's decision, after seeking his judgement, is a sign of their lack of true belief. The verse implies that if they were genuine believers, they would have accepted the divine judgement found in the Torah and would not have needed to seek the Prophet's decision, only to later reject it. This highlights the importance of following Allah's commandments and the inconsistency of those who claim to believe but do not adhere to the divine laws.
orig: وكيف يحكمونك وعندهم التوراة فيها حكم الله ثم يتولون من بعد ذلك وما أولئك بالمؤمنين

translation: Indeed, We sent down the Torah, in which was guidance and light. The prophets who submitted [to Allah] judged by it for the Jews, as did the rabbis and scholars by that with which they were entrusted of the Scripture of Allah, and they were witnesses thereto. So do not fear the people but fear Me, and do not exchange My verses for a small price. And whoever does not judge by what Allah has revealed - then it is those who are the disbelievers.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the divine origin of the Torah and its role as a source of guidance and light for the Jewish people. The prophets, rabbis, and scholars who followed Allah's teachings were entrusted with upholding and judging by the Torah. The verse warns against fearing people more than Allah and trading His revelations for worldly gain. It also declares that those who do not judge according to Allah's revelations are considered disbelievers. This highlights the importance of adhering to divine law and the consequences of deviating from it.
orig: إنا أنزلنا التوراة فيها هدى ونور يحكم بها النبيون الذين أسلموا للذين هادوا والربانيون والأحبار بما استحفظوا من كتاب الله وكانوا عليه شهداء فلا تخشوا الناس واخشون ولا تشتروا بآياتي ثمنا قليلا ومن لم يحكم بما أنزل الله فأولئك هم الكافرون

translation: And We ordained for them therein a life for a life, an eye for an eye, a nose for a nose, an ear for an ear, a tooth for a tooth, and for wounds is legal retribution. But whoever gives [up his right as] charity, it is an expiation for him. And whoever does not judge by what Allah has revealed - then it is those who are the wrongdoers.
interpretation: This verse establishes the principle of justice and equality in punishment, known as "qisas" or legal retribution. It means that the punishment should fit the crime - a life for a life, an eye for an eye, and so on. However, the verse also encourages forgiveness and charity by stating that if one forgoes their right to retribution and pardons the offender, it will serve as expiation for their own sins. The final part of the verse warns that those who do not judge according to the laws revealed by Allah are wrongdoers, emphasizing the importance of adhering to divine justice.
orig: وكتبنا عليهم فيها أن النفس بالنفس والعين بالعين والأنف بالأنف والأذن بالأذن والسن بالسن والجروح قصاص فمن تصدق به فهو كفارة له ومن لم يحكم بما أنزل الله فأولئك هم الظالمون

translation: And We sent, following in their footsteps, Jesus, the son of Mary, confirming that which came before him in the Torah; and We gave him the Gospel, in which was guidance and light and confirming that which preceded it of the Torah as guidance and instruction for the righteous.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the continuity and consistency of God's message through the prophets. Jesus, as a messenger of God, came to confirm the teachings of the Torah that preceded him. The Gospel given to Jesus contained guidance, light, and served as a confirmation of the Torah's message. It also provided guidance and admonition for those who are mindful of God and seek to live righteously. This highlights the interconnectedness of the divine messages and the importance of following the guidance provided by God through His prophets.
orig: وقفينا على آثارهم بعيسى ابن مريم مصدقا لما بين يديه من التوراة وآتيناه الإنجيل فيه هدى ونور ومصدقا لما بين يديه من التوراة وهدى وموعظة للمتقين

translation: And let the People of the Gospel judge by what Allah has revealed therein. And whoever does not judge by what Allah has revealed - then it is those who are the defiantly disobedient.
interpretation: This verse calls upon the Christians to judge and rule according to the revelation that Allah has sent down in the Gospel. Those who fail to do so and do not uphold the laws and commandments revealed by Allah are considered to be disobedient and rebellious against Him. It emphasizes the importance of adhering to divine revelation as the basis for judgment and way of life.
orig: وليحكم أهل الإنجيل بما أنزل الله فيه ومن لم يحكم بما أنزل الله فأولئك هم الفاسقون

translation: And We have revealed to you, [O Muhammad], the Book in truth, confirming that which preceded it of the Scripture and as a criterion over it. So judge between them by what Allah has revealed and do not follow their inclinations away from what has come to you of the truth. To each of you We prescribed a law and a method. Had Allah willed, He would have made you one nation [united in religion], but [He intended] to test you in what He has given you; so race to [all that is] good. To Allah is your return all together, and He will [then] inform you concerning that over which you used to differ.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the divine origin and truth of the Qur'an, which serves as a criterion to judge and confirm the teachings of the previous scriptures. It instructs the Prophet Muhammad to judge among people according to God's revelations and not to follow their desires or deviate from the truth. The verse acknowledges the diversity of laws and paths prescribed for different communities, suggesting that this is part of God's plan to test people in what He has given them. It encourages all people to strive for righteousness and good deeds, reminding them that ultimately everyone will return to God, who will then inform them about the matters over which they differed in this world.
orig: وأنزلنا إليك الكتاب بالحق مصدقا لما بين يديه من الكتاب ومهيمنا عليه فاحكم بينهم بما أنزل الله ولا تتبع أهواءهم عما جاءك من الحق لكل جعلنا منكم شرعة ومنهاجا ولو شاء الله لجعلكم أمة واحدة ولكن ليبلوكم في ما آتاكم فاستبقوا الخيرات إلى الله مرجعكم جميعا فينبئكم بما كنتم فيه تختلفون

translation: And judge between them by what Allah has revealed, and do not follow their inclinations, and beware of them lest they tempt you away from some of what Allah has revealed to you. And if they turn away - then know that Allah only intends to afflict them with some of their [own] sins. And indeed, many among the people are defiantly disobedient.
interpretation: This verse instructs the Prophet Muhammad to judge disputes between people according to the divine revelation from Allah, not according to people's whims and desires. It warns the Prophet to be on guard against those who may try to sway him from Allah's laws. If they reject the Prophet's judgment, it is because Allah wills to punish them for some of their sins due to their disobedience. The verse suggests that many people are rebellious and do not follow the straight path ordained by Allah.
orig: وأن احكم بينهم بما أنزل الله ولا تتبع أهواءهم واحذرهم أن يفتنوك عن بعض ما أنزل الله إليك فإن تولوا فاعلم أنما يريد الله أن يصيبهم ببعض ذنوبهم وإن كثيرا من الناس لفاسقون

translation: Then is it the judgement of [the time of] ignorance they desire? But who is better than Allah in judgement for a people who are certain [in faith].
interpretation: This verse is a rhetorical question that criticizes those who prefer to follow the misguided ways and customs of the pre-Islamic era, known as the "time of ignorance" (jahiliyyah), over the divine law revealed by Allah. It emphasizes that Allah's judgement and guidance is far superior and more perfect than the flawed human traditions and opinions of the past. The verse implies that those who have strong faith and conviction in Allah should willingly submit to His laws and commandments, as they are the best source of guidance for leading a righteous life and attaining success in this world and the hereafter.
orig: أفحكم الجاهلية يبغون ومن أحسن من الله حكما لقوم يوقنون

translation: O you who have believed, do not take the Jews and the Christians as allies. They are [in fact] allies of one another. And whoever is an ally to them among you - then indeed, he is [one] of them. Indeed, Allah guides not the wrongdoing people.
interpretation: This verse warns the believers against forming alliances with Jews and Christians, stating that they are allies of each other. It emphasizes that those who align themselves with them will be considered as one of them, suggesting a loss of faith and identity. The verse asserts that Allah does not guide those who engage in wrongdoing by allying with the Jews and Christians, implying that such an act is a form of injustice and a deviation from the right path. The underlying message is to maintain loyalty to the Muslim community and to avoid compromising one's faith by forming close ties with those who do not share the same beliefs.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا لا تتخذوا اليهود والنصارى أولياء بعضهم أولياء بعض ومن يتولهم منكم فإنه منهم إن الله لا يهدي القوم الظالمين

translation: So you see those in whose hearts is disease hastening into [association with] them, saying, "We are afraid a misfortune may strike us." But perhaps Allah will bring conquest or a decision from Him, and they will become, over what they have been concealing within themselves, regretful.
interpretation: This verse is a warning to the hypocrites who secretly align themselves with the enemies of Islam out of fear of being persecuted or suffering misfortune. They lack true faith and trust in Allah's plan. However, Allah may grant the believers victory or bring about events that expose the hypocrites' true intentions. When that happens, the hypocrites will regret their concealed doubts and disloyalty, realizing that they were on the wrong side all along. The verse emphasizes the importance of remaining steadfast in faith and trusting in Allah's wisdom, even in the face of adversity or uncertainty.
orig: فترى الذين في قلوبهم مرض يسارعون فيهم يقولون نخشى أن تصيبنا دائرة فعسى الله أن يأتي بالفتح أو أمر من عنده فيصبحوا على ما أسروا في أنفسهم نادمين

translation: And those who believe will say, "Are these the ones who swore by Allah their strongest oaths that indeed they were with you?" Their deeds have become worthless, and they have become losers.
interpretation: This verse is referring to the hypocrites who outwardly claimed to be believers and swore their allegiance to the Muslims, but inwardly harbored doubt and disbelief. On the Day of Judgment, the true believers will express their astonishment at the fate of these hypocrites, whose insincere deeds and false oaths will be exposed. The verse emphasizes that the actions and words of the hypocrites will be rendered worthless due to their lack of genuine faith, and they will ultimately face the consequences of their deception by becoming the losers in both this world and the Hereafter.
orig: ويقول الذين آمنوا أهؤلاء الذين أقسموا بالله جهد أيمانهم إنهم لمعكم حبطت أعمالهم فأصبحوا خاسرين

translation: O you who have believed, whoever of you should revert from his religion - Allah will bring forth [in place of them] a people He will love and who will love Him [who are] humble toward the believers, powerful against the disbelievers; they strive in the cause of Allah and do not fear the blame of a critic. That is the favor of Allah; He bestows it upon whom He wills. And Allah is all-Encompassing and Knowing.
interpretation: This verse is a warning to those who may consider leaving Islam, that Allah will replace them with others who are more devoted and sincere in their faith. The characteristics of these believers are that they are humble and kind towards other believers, while being strong and firm against the disbelievers. They are not afraid to strive in Allah's cause and do not fear criticism or blame from anyone for their actions. This verse emphasizes that faith and devotion to Allah is a favor and blessing that He grants to whomever He wills, and that He has infinite knowledge and wisdom in all affairs. It encourages believers to be steadfast in their faith and to embody these praiseworthy qualities.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا من يرتد منكم عن دينه فسوف يأتي الله بقوم يحبهم ويحبونه أذلة على المؤمنين أعزة على الكافرين يجاهدون في سبيل الله ولا يخافون لومة لائم ذلك فضل الله يؤتيه من يشاء والله واسع عليم

translation: Your ally is none but Allah and [therefore] His Messenger and those who have believed - those who establish prayer and give zakah, and they bow [in worship].
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the true allies and protectors of the believers are Allah, His Messenger (Muhammad), and the righteous believers who establish prayer, give zakah (obligatory charity), and humble themselves before Allah in worship. It highlights the importance of faith, prayer, charity, and humility as the defining characteristics of the true believers who deserve the alliance and support of other believers. The verse also implies that seeking the alliance or protection of non-believers or those who do not uphold these righteous qualities is not permissible for Muslims.
orig: إنما وليكم الله ورسوله والذين آمنوا الذين يقيمون الصلاة ويؤتون الزكاة وهم راكعون

translation: And whoever is an ally of Allah and His Messenger and those who have believed - indeed, the party of Allah - they will be the predominant.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that those who align themselves with Allah, His Messenger, and the believers are part of the "party of Allah". It suggests that this group will ultimately be victorious and prevail over others. The interpretation is that by staying loyal to Allah and following the guidance of the Prophet and the community of believers, one will be on the winning side in both this world and the hereafter. It encourages Muslims to stay united and steadfast in their faith, as that is the path to success and predominance over those who oppose them.
orig: ومن يتول الله ورسوله والذين آمنوا فإن حزب الله هم الغالبون

translation: O you who have believed, do not take those who have taken your religion in ridicule and amusement among the ones who were given the Scripture before you nor the disbelievers as allies. And fear Allah, if you should [truly] be believers.
interpretation: This verse warns the believers against taking those who mock and make fun of their religion, whether from the People of the Book or the disbelievers, as close friends and allies. It reminds them to be mindful of Allah and to have consciousness (taqwa) of Him if they are true in their faith. The underlying message is to be cautious of those who disrespect or belittle one's religious beliefs, as they are not suitable to be taken as intimate companions or trusted allies. Instead, the believers should foster closer ties with fellow believers who share their reverence for the religion.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا لا تتخذوا الذين اتخذوا دينكم هزوا ولعبا من الذين أوتوا الكتاب من قبلكم والكفار أولياء واتقوا الله إن كنتم مؤمنين

translation: And when you call to prayer, they take it in ridicule and amusement. That is because they are a people who do not reason.
interpretation: This verse is criticizing the disbelievers who mock and make fun of the Muslim call to prayer (adhaan). It suggests that their ridicule stems from a lack of understanding and reasoning. They are portrayed as foolish people who do not grasp the significance and sacredness of the prayer and the call to it. The verse implies that if they had sound intellect, they would recognize the importance of prayer and not resort to such immature behavior as mockery. It highlights the contrast between the believers who take prayer seriously and the disbelievers who treat it frivolously.
orig: وإذا ناديتم إلى الصلاة اتخذوها هزوا ولعبا ذلك بأنهم قوم لا يعقلون

translation: Say, "O People of the Scripture, do you resent us except [for the fact] that we have believed in Allah and what was revealed to us and what was revealed before and because most of you are defiantly disobedient?"
interpretation: This verse is addressing the People of the Book (Jews and Christians) and questioning the reason behind their resentment and hostility towards the Muslims. The interpretation is that their animosity is not based on any genuine grievance, but rather stems from the fact that the Muslims have faith in Allah, believe in the revelation sent down to Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him), and also believe in the previous revelations sent to earlier prophets.
