Furthermore, the verse suggests that the majority of the People of the Book are defiantly disobedient, meaning they knowingly reject the truth and act contrary to the teachings of their own scriptures. This highlights the irrational nature of their opposition to Islam and the Muslims.
orig: قل يا أهل الكتاب هل تنقمون منا إلا أن آمنا بالله وما أنزل إلينا وما أنزل من قبل وأن أكثركم فاسقون

translation: Say, "Shall I inform you of something worse than that as penalty from Allah? [It is that of] those whom Allah has cursed and with whom He became angry and made of them apes and pigs and slaves of Taghut. Those are worse in position and further astray from the sound way."
interpretation: This verse is a stern warning to those who reject faith and incur the wrath of Allah. It suggests that the punishment for such people is worse than any worldly suffering - they will be cursed by Allah, transformed into lowly creatures like apes and pigs, and become servants of false gods or evil forces (Taghut). This metaphorical degradation signifies how they have lost their way and sunk to the lowest of ranks spiritually. The verse emphasizes that nothing is worse than earning Allah's anger and being led far astray from the straight path of guidance and righteousness.
orig: قل هل أنبئكم بشر من ذلك مثوبة عند الله من لعنه الله وغضب عليه وجعل منهم القردة والخنازير وعبد الطاغوت أولئك شر مكانا وأضل عن سواء السبيل

translation: And when they come to you, they say, "We believe." But they had entered with disbelief [in their hearts], and they had certainly left with it. And Allah is most knowing of what they were concealing.
interpretation: This verse refers to the hypocrites who outwardly professed belief in Islam, but inwardly harbored disbelief. They would come to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and the Muslims, claiming to have faith, but their intentions were insincere. Allah exposes their true nature, stating that they entered the fold of Islam with disbelief in their hearts and left with that same disbelief, never having truly embraced the faith. The verse emphasizes that Allah is fully aware of what they conceal in their hearts, despite their outward pretenses. It serves as a warning to the believers not to be deceived by those who feign belief while harboring ill intentions towards Islam and the Muslim community.
orig: وإذا جاءوكم قالوا آمنا وقد دخلوا بالكفر وهم قد خرجوا به والله أعلم بما كانوا يكتمون

translation: And you see many of them hastening into sin and aggression and the devouring of [what is] unlawful. How wretched is what they have been doing.
interpretation: This verse is a strong condemnation of those who engage in sinful and aggressive behavior, and consume what is forbidden. It suggests that such actions are not only wrong, but are done eagerly and without hesitation by many people. The verse emphasizes the severity and deplorability of these deeds by describing them as "wretched". It serves as a warning and reminder to believers to avoid such conduct and to adhere to righteousness and permissible means of living. The verse also implies that there will be consequences for those who persistently engage in sin and transgression.
orig: وترى كثيرا منهم يسارعون في الإثم والعدوان وأكلهم السحت لبئس ما كانوا يعملون

translation: Why do the rabbis and religious scholars not forbid them from saying what is sinful and devouring what is unlawful? How wretched is what they have been practicing.
interpretation: This verse criticizes the religious leaders, the rabbis and scholars, for failing to prevent their followers from engaging in sinful speech and consuming what is forbidden. It suggests that these leaders have a responsibility to guide their people and prevent them from wrongdoing, and that by neglecting this duty, they are complicit in the sins of their followers. The verse implies that the actions of these leaders are wretched and condemnable in the sight of God.
orig: لولا ينهاهم الربانيون والأحبار عن قولهم الإثم وأكلهم السحت لبئس ما كانوا يصنعون

translation: And the Jews say, "The hand of Allah is chained." Chained are their hands, and cursed are they for what they say. Rather, both His hands are extended; He spends however He wills. And that which has been revealed to you from your Lord will surely increase many of them in transgression and disbelief. And We have cast among them animosity and hatred until the Day of Resurrection. Every time they kindled the fire of war [against you], Allah extinguished it. And they strive throughout the land [causing] corruption, and Allah does not like corrupters.
interpretation: This verse condemns the Jews for their blasphemous statement that Allah's hand is "chained" or constrained, implying that He is stingy or unable to provide. Allah refutes this notion, affirming that both His hands are extended freely and that He spends and provides as He wills, without any limitation. The revelation of the Quran and the truth it contains will only increase many of the Jews in their arrogance, transgression and disbelief, as they reject it out of stubbornness and pride. As a consequence of their spiritual corruption, Allah has caused enmity and hatred to arise between them until the Day of Judgment. Whenever they try to ignite the flames of war against the Muslims, Allah extinguishes their efforts. The Jews are actively engaged in spreading mischief and corruption in the land, but Allah dislikes those who cause corruption and will hold them accountable for their misdeeds.
orig: وقالت اليهود يد الله مغلولة غلت أيديهم ولعنوا بما قالوا بل يداه مبسوطتان ينفق كيف يشاء وليزيدن كثيرا منهم ما أنزل إليك من ربك طغيانا وكفرا وألقينا بينهم العداوة والبغضاء إلى يوم القيامة كلما أوقدوا نارا للحرب أطفأها الله ويسعون في الأرض فسادا والله لا يحب المفسدين

translation: And if only the People of the Scripture had believed and feared Allah, We would have removed from them their misdeeds and admitted them to Gardens of Pleasure.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of faith and righteousness. It suggests that if the People of the Book, referring to Jews and Christians, had sincerely believed in Allah and followed His commandments, Allah would have forgiven their past sins and granted them entry into Paradise. This highlights the mercy and forgiveness of Allah towards those who turn to Him in repentance and strive to live according to His teachings. It also implies that the path to salvation is open to all people, regardless of their previous religious affiliation, if they embrace the message of Islam and lead a righteous life.
orig: ولو أن أهل الكتاب آمنوا واتقوا لكفرنا عنهم سيئاتهم ولأدخلناهم جنات النعيم

translation: And if only they upheld [the law of] the Torah, the Gospel, and what has been revealed to them from their Lord, they would have consumed [provision] from above them and from beneath their feet. Among them are a moderate community, but many of them - evil is that which they do.
interpretation: This verse suggests that if the People of the Book (Jews and Christians) had truly followed the teachings of their scriptures and what God had revealed to them, they would have been blessed with abundance and prosperity from all directions. However, only a moderate group among them adheres to the right path, while many of them engage in evil deeds and actions that are displeasing to God. This highlights the importance of not only believing in the divine scriptures but also putting their teachings into practice and leading a righteous life in accordance with God's commandments.
orig: ولو أنهم أقاموا التوراة والإنجيل وما أنزل إليهم من ربهم لأكلوا من فوقهم ومن تحت أرجلهم منهم أمة مقتصدة وكثير منهم ساء ما يعملون

translation: O Messenger, announce that which has been revealed to you from your Lord, and if you do not, then you have not conveyed His message. And Allah will protect you from the people. Indeed, Allah does not guide the disbelieving people.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of the Prophet's role in conveying the message of Islam without fear or hesitation. It reassures the Prophet that Allah will protect him from any harm or opposition he may face while carrying out his duty. The verse also highlights the fact that those who reject the message of Islam are not guided by Allah, and it is not the Prophet's responsibility to make them believe. The Prophet's only duty is to deliver the message clearly and completely, and the rest is up to Allah's will and the individual's choice to accept or reject the message.
orig: يا أيها الرسول بلغ ما أنزل إليك من ربك وإن لم تفعل فما بلغت رسالته والله يعصمك من الناس إن الله لا يهدي القوم الكافرين

translation: Say, "O People of the Scripture, you are [standing] on nothing until you uphold [the law of] the Torah, the Gospel, and what has been revealed to you from your Lord." And that which has been revealed to you from your Lord will surely increase many of them in transgression and disbelief. So do not grieve over the disbelieving people.
interpretation: This verse is a call to the People of the Book (Jews and Christians) to fully adhere to the original teachings revealed in their scriptures, as well as what was revealed to Prophet Muhammad in the Qur'an. It suggests that without complete adherence to divine revelations, their religious practices are baseless. The verse also acknowledges that many among the People of the Book will reject the Qur'anic message out of arrogance and disbelief, leading them further astray. However, Prophet Muhammad is instructed not to feel disheartened by their rejection, as it is the consequence of their own choice to deny the truth.
orig: قل يا أهل الكتاب لستم على شيء حتى تقيموا التوراة والإنجيل وما أنزل إليكم من ربكم وليزيدن كثيرا منهم ما أنزل إليك من ربك طغيانا وكفرا فلا تأس على القوم الكافرين

translation: Indeed, those who believed and those who were Jews or Sabeans or Christians - those who believed in Allah and the Last Day and did righteousness - no fear will there be concerning them, nor will they grieve.
interpretation: This verse conveys a message of religious tolerance and inclusivity. It states that those who sincerely believe in God and the Day of Judgment, and do good deeds, will have nothing to fear and will not grieve, regardless of their specific religious affiliation. This suggests that in Islam, what ultimately matters is one's faith, righteousness and good conduct, rather than the label of one's religion. The verse promotes the idea of pluralism and peaceful coexistence among people of different faiths who share core ethical values and belief in the Divine.
orig: إن الذين آمنوا والذين هادوا والصابئون والنصارى من آمن بالله واليوم الآخر وعمل صالحا فلا خوف عليهم ولا هم يحزنون

translation: We had already taken the covenant of the Children of Israel and had sent to them messengers. Whenever there came to them a messenger with what their souls did not desire, a party [of messengers] they denied, and another party they killed.
interpretation: This verse highlights the disobedience and rebelliousness of the Children of Israel towards the messengers sent by Allah. Despite making a covenant with Allah to follow His guidance, they repeatedly rejected and even killed the messengers who came to them with teachings that conflicted with their desires and worldly inclinations. This behavior demonstrates their arrogance, stubbornness, and lack of faith in Allah's revelations. It serves as a warning to all believers to submit humbly to Allah's will and accept the guidance brought by His messengers, rather than following their own whims and desires.
orig: لقد أخذنا ميثاق بني إسرائيل وأرسلنا إليهم رسلا كلما جاءهم رسول بما لا تهوى أنفسهم فريقا كذبوا وفريقا يقتلون

translation: They thought there would be no trial, so they became blind and deaf; then Allah turned to them in mercy; then many of them again became blind and deaf. And Allah is All-Seer of what they do.
interpretation: This verse highlights the tendency of people to become heedless and turn away from the truth when they face no immediate consequences for their actions. They become "blind and deaf" to the signs and warnings from Allah. However, Allah, in His infinite mercy, gives them another chance by turning to them and guiding them back to the right path. Despite this, many of them revert to their old ways, becoming "blind and deaf" once again to the truth. The verse emphasizes that Allah is fully aware of their deeds and will hold them accountable for their actions, as He is the All-Seer, witnessing everything they do.
orig: وحسبوا ألا تكون فتنة فعموا وصموا ثم تاب الله عليهم ثم عموا وصموا كثير منهم والله بصير بما يعملون

translation: They have certainly disbelieved who say, "Allah is the Messiah, the son of Mary" while the Messiah has said, "O Children of Israel, worship Allah, my Lord and your Lord." Indeed, he who associates others with Allah - Allah has forbidden him Paradise, and his refuge is the Fire. And there are not for the wrongdoers any helpers.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the fundamental Islamic belief in the oneness of God (tawheed) and rejection of the Christian doctrine of the divinity of Jesus. It clearly states that those who believe that Jesus is God have committed disbelief. The Messiah himself commanded the Children of Israel to worship Allah alone, affirming that Allah is his Lord and their Lord. Associating partners with Allah is an unforgivable sin that leads to being barred from Paradise and consigned to the Fire of Hell. Those who commit this grave wrong will have no helpers or saviors to protect them from Allah's punishment in the Hereafter.
orig: لقد كفر الذين قالوا إن الله هو المسيح ابن مريم وقال المسيح يا بني إسرائيل اعبدوا الله ربي وربكم إنه من يشرك بالله فقد حرم الله عليه الجنة ومأواه النار وما للظالمين من أنصار

translation: They have certainly disbelieved who say, "Allah is the third of three." And there is no god except one God. And if they do not desist from what they are saying, there will surely afflict the disbelievers among them a painful punishment.
interpretation: This verse is a strong condemnation of the Christian belief in the Trinity, which holds that God is three persons in one divine being. The Qur'an emphatically rejects this notion, asserting that Allah is absolutely one and singular, without any partners or equals. Those who ascribe divinity to anyone or anything besides Allah are considered disbelievers. The verse warns that if they persist in this belief and do not repent, they will face a severe punishment in the Hereafter for their polytheism and deviation from the pure monotheism that Islam teaches.
orig: لقد كفر الذين قالوا إن الله ثالث ثلاثة وما من إله إلا إله واحد وإن لم ينتهوا عما يقولون ليمسن الذين كفروا منهم عذاب أليم

translation: So will they not repent to Allah and seek His forgiveness? And Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse is a call to sinners and wrongdoers to turn back to Allah in sincere repentance and seek His forgiveness. It emphasizes the vastness of Allah's mercy and forgiveness, reminding us that no matter how great our sins may be, Allah is always ready to forgive those who turn to Him with a contrite heart. The verse encourages us to never despair of Allah's mercy, but to always have hope in His forgiveness and to continuously strive to mend our ways and seek His pleasure through repentance and righteous deeds. It highlights the importance of tawbah (repentance) in the life of a believer as a means of spiritual purification and a way to attain Allah's love and mercy.
orig: أفلا يتوبون إلى الله ويستغفرونه والله غفور رحيم

translation: The Messiah, son of Mary, was not but a messenger; [other] messengers have passed on before him. And his mother was a supporter of truth. They both used to eat food. Look how We make clear to them the signs; then look how they are deluded.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the humanity of Jesus and his mother Mary, rejecting the idea of their divinity. It asserts that Jesus was a prophet like the prophets before him, and that he and his mother were both human beings who ate food, a basic human need. The verse then draws attention to the clear signs and evidence that God provides to people, yet they still turn away from the truth and are deluded. This highlights the importance of recognizing the true nature of Jesus and Mary as human beings and servants of God, rather than elevating them to divine status.
orig: ما المسيح ابن مريم إلا رسول قد خلت من قبله الرسل وأمه صديقة كانا يأكلان الطعام انظر كيف نبين لهم الآيات ثم انظر أنى يؤفكون

translation: Say, "Do you worship besides Allah that which holds for you no [power of] harm or benefit while it is Allah who is the Hearing, the Knowing?"
interpretation: This verse is a rhetorical question that highlights the futility and irrationality of worshipping anyone or anything besides Allah. It emphasizes that only Allah has the power to benefit or harm, and that He alone is All-Hearing and All-Knowing. The verse implies that worshipping false deities is not only misguided but also illogical, as these entities are powerless and cannot respond to the needs of their worshippers. It serves as a reminder to direct one's worship and devotion solely to Allah, who possesses all knowledge and power.
orig: قل أتعبدون من دون الله ما لا يملك لكم ضرا ولا نفعا والله هو السميع العليم

translation: Say, "O People of the Scripture, do not exaggerate in your religion beyond the truth and do not follow the inclinations of a people who had gone astray before and misled many and have strayed from the soundness of the way."
interpretation: This verse is a warning against religious extremism and blindly following misguided people. It urges the People of the Scripture, referring to Jews and Christians, not to exceed the boundaries of truth in practicing their faith. They should not elevate religious figures to divine status or attribute to God what does not befit Him. The verse also cautions against imitating those who have strayed from the right path in the past, as their misguidance led many others astray. Instead, one should adhere to the straight path based on divine guidance and reason, avoiding the pitfalls of exaggeration and deviance that lead people away from the true essence of religion.
orig: قل يا أهل الكتاب لا تغلوا في دينكم غير الحق ولا تتبعوا أهواء قوم قد ضلوا من قبل وأضلوا كثيرا وضلوا عن سواء السبيل

translation: Cursed were those who disbelieved among the Children of Israel by the tongue of David and of Jesus, the son of Mary. That was because they disobeyed and [habitually] transgressed.
interpretation: This verse indicates that some of the Children of Israel, due to their persistent disobedience and transgression against God's commands, were cursed by two of their own prophets, David and Jesus. This underscores the severity of their actions and the consequences of consistently defying God's message and guidance, even to the point of being rebuked and cursed by the very prophets sent to guide them. It serves as a warning to all believers not to follow in their footsteps, but to strive for obedience and righteousness.
orig: لعن الذين كفروا من بني إسرائيل على لسان داوود وعيسى ابن مريم ذلك بما عصوا وكانوا يعتدون

translation: They used not to prevent one another from wrongdoing that they did. How wretched was that which they were doing.
interpretation: This verse is a strong condemnation of those who fail to prevent or discourage others from committing sins and wrongdoings. It suggests that it is a collective responsibility of believers to promote virtue and prevent vice in their communities. Remaining silent or passive in the face of evil is itself blameworthy. The verse implies that those who allow misconduct to continue unchecked are themselves guilty of a serious moral failing. It is an exhortation for people to stand up against wrongdoing, enjoin what is right, and create a society of mutual accountability and righteousness.
orig: كانوا لا يتناهون عن منكر فعلوه لبئس ما كانوا يفعلون

translation: You see many of them taking those who disbelieved as allies. How wretched is that which they have put forth for themselves in that Allah has become angry with them, and in the punishment they will abide eternally.
interpretation: This verse is a warning against taking disbelievers as close allies and protectors instead of the believers. It suggests that doing so will incur the anger of Allah and lead to eternal punishment in the Hereafter. The interpretation is that Muslims should be cautious about forming deep alliances and friendships with those who reject faith in Allah, as it can lead one astray from the straight path and result in severe consequences in this life and the next. The verse emphasizes the importance of keeping good company with fellow believers and not compromising one's faith and principles for worldly gains or relationships.
orig: ترى كثيرا منهم يتولون الذين كفروا لبئس ما قدمت لهم أنفسهم أن سخط الله عليهم وفي العذاب هم خالدون

translation: And if they had believed in Allah and the Prophet and in what was revealed to him, they would not have taken them as allies; but many of them are defiantly disobedient.
interpretation: This verse is addressing the believers and criticizing those who take the disbelievers as allies or protectors instead of relying on Allah and following the teachings of the Prophet Muhammad. It implies that true faith in Allah and His messenger is incompatible with forming alliances with those who oppose Islam. The verse suggests that such people, despite their claims to belief, are in fact transgressors and disobedient to Allah due to their choice of allies. It highlights the importance of complete trust and reliance on Allah and adhering to the path of the Prophet, rather than compromising one's faith by aligning with those who reject the truth.
orig: ولو كانوا يؤمنون بالله والنبي وما أنزل إليه ما اتخذوهم أولياء ولكن كثيرا منهم فاسقون

translation: You will surely find the most intense of the people in animosity toward the believers [to be] the Jews and those who associate others with Allah; and you will find the nearest of them in affection to the believers those who say, "We are Christians." That is because among them are priests and monks and because they are not arrogant.
interpretation: This verse highlights the contrast between the attitudes of Jews and Christians towards Muslims. It suggests that Jews and polytheists (those who associate others with Allah) are the most hostile towards believers in Islam, while Christians are the closest in affection to Muslims. The verse attributes this difference to the presence of priests and monks among Christians, who are known for their devotion and humility. It also implies that the Christians' lack of arrogance contributes to their more positive stance towards Muslims compared to other groups.
orig: لتجدن أشد الناس عداوة للذين آمنوا اليهود والذين أشركوا ولتجدن أقربهم مودة للذين آمنوا الذين قالوا إنا نصارى ذلك بأن منهم قسيسين ورهبانا وأنهم لا يستكبرون

translation: And when they hear what has been revealed to the Messenger, you see their eyes overflowing with tears because of what they have recognized of the truth. They say, "Our Lord, we have believed, so register us among the witnesses."
interpretation: This verse speaks about the sincere believers who, upon hearing the Qur'an, are deeply moved and touched by its truth. Their eyes overflow with tears as they recognize the undeniable truth in the divine message. Overwhelmed with conviction and sincerity, they declare their faith, saying, "Our Lord, we have believed in what You have revealed, so count us among those who bear witness to the truth." This emotional response demonstrates their genuine submission to Allah and their readiness to embrace Islam wholeheartedly. The verse highlights the profound impact of the Qur'an on the hearts of true believers and their eagerness to be counted among the faithful witnesses to Allah's message.
orig: وإذا سمعوا ما أنزل إلى الرسول ترى أعينهم تفيض من الدمع مما عرفوا من الحق يقولون ربنا آمنا فاكتبنا مع الشاهدين

translation: And why should we not believe in Allah and what has come to us of the truth? And we aspire that our Lord will admit us [to Paradise] with the righteous people.
interpretation: This verse is a rhetorical question that emphasizes the importance and logic of believing in Allah and the truth that has been revealed. It suggests that there is no valid reason or excuse for not having faith, especially when one desires to be among the righteous people whom Allah will admit into Paradise. The verse implies that belief in Allah and following the truth is the path to righteousness and salvation in the Hereafter.
orig: وما لنا لا نؤمن بالله وما جاءنا من الحق ونطمع أن يدخلنا ربنا مع القوم الصالحين

translation: So Allah rewarded them for what they said with gardens [in Paradise] beneath which rivers flow, wherein they abide eternally. And that is the reward of doers of good.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the immense reward that Allah has prepared for those who remain steadfast in their faith and do good deeds. It highlights that their ultimate reward will be the eternal gardens of Paradise, where they will find everlasting peace, comfort, and joy. The flowing rivers beneath the gardens symbolize the abundance of blessings and the absence of any form of hardship or discomfort. This reward is not merely a result of their actions but a manifestation of Allah's grace and generosity towards those who strive to please Him. The verse also implies that the key to attaining this reward is through a combination of faith and righteous deeds, as it is the distinguishing characteristic of the "doers of good" or "Al-Muhsineen." This serves as an encouragement for believers to persevere in their devotion to Allah and to continuously engage in acts of goodness, knowing that their ultimate reward will be far greater than any temporary hardship they may face in this world.
orig: فأثابهم الله بما قالوا جنات تجري من تحتها الأنهار خالدين فيها وذلك جزاء المحسنين

translation: But those who disbelieved and denied Our signs - those are the companions of Hellfire.
interpretation: This verse serves as a stern warning to those who reject faith in Allah and deny the truth of His revelations. It emphasizes that disbelief and denial of Allah's signs lead to severe consequences in the afterlife. Those who persist in their disbelief and refuse to acknowledge the divine messages will be condemned to the eternal punishment of Hellfire. The verse highlights the gravity of rejecting faith and the ultimate fate that awaits those who choose to disbelieve, reminding believers of the importance of staying steadfast in their faith and heeding the signs and guidance provided by Allah.
orig: والذين كفروا وكذبوا بآياتنا أولئك أصحاب الجحيم

translation: O you who have believed, do not prohibit the good things which Allah has made lawful to you and do not transgress. Indeed, Allah does not like transgressors.
interpretation: This verse reminds believers that they should not forbid themselves from enjoying the lawful and good things that Allah has permitted them to enjoy. It emphasizes the importance of balance and moderation in life, and warns against going to extremes or becoming overly restrictive in one's religious practices. The verse also highlights the fact that Allah disapproves of those who transgress the boundaries He has set and engage in excessive behavior. It encourages Muslims to live a balanced life, enjoying the blessings that Allah has bestowed upon them while staying within the limits of what is permissible.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا لا تحرموا طيبات ما أحل الله لكم ولا تعتدوا إن الله لا يحب المعتدين

translation: And eat of what Allah has provided for you [which is] lawful and good. And fear Allah, in whom you are believers.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of consuming only what is permissible (halal) and good, as provided by Allah. It reminds believers to be mindful of their sustenance and to show gratitude for the blessings bestowed upon them. The verse also encourages Muslims to maintain their consciousness of Allah (taqwa) in all aspects of life, including their dietary choices. By eating what is lawful and wholesome, one demonstrates obedience to Allah and strengthens their faith. The verse ultimately highlights the connection between physical nourishment and spiritual well-being, urging believers to make choices that align with their belief in Allah.
orig: وكلوا مما رزقكم الله حلالا طيبا واتقوا الله الذي أنتم به مؤمنون

translation: Allah will not impose blame upon you for what is meaningless in your oaths, but He will impose blame upon you for [breaking] what you intended of oaths. So its expiation is the feeding of ten needy people from the average of that which you feed your [own] families or clothing them or the freeing of a slave. But whoever cannot find [or afford it] - then a fast of three days [is required]. That is the expiation for oaths when you have sworn. But guard your oaths. Thus does Allah make clear to you His verses that you may be grateful.
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of being mindful and sincere in one's oaths. It teaches that while Allah forgives unintentional or meaningless oaths, breaking an oath deliberately is a serious matter that requires expiation. The prescribed expiation involves feeding or clothing the needy, freeing a slave, or fasting for three days if one cannot afford the other options. This encourages believers to be cautious and truthful in their oaths and to fulfill their commitments. The verse also emphasizes Allah's mercy in providing guidance and the opportunity for redemption, which should inspire gratitude in the believers.
orig: لا يؤاخذكم الله باللغو في أيمانكم ولكن يؤاخذكم بما عقدتم الأيمان فكفارته إطعام عشرة مساكين من أوسط ما تطعمون أهليكم أو كسوتهم أو تحرير رقبة فمن لم يجد فصيام ثلاثة أيام ذلك كفارة أيمانكم إذا حلفتم واحفظوا أيمانكم كذلك يبين الله لكم آياته لعلكم تشكرون

translation: O you who have believed, indeed, intoxicants, gambling, [sacrificing on] stone alters [to other than Allah], and divining arrows are but defilement from the work of Satan, so avoid it that you may be successful.
interpretation: This verse is a clear prohibition of intoxicants (like alcohol), gambling, idolatry, and fortune-telling in Islam. It declares these practices as impure and satanic, and instructs believers to abstain from them completely in order to attain success and felicity. The underlying wisdom is that these activities are spiritually and socially harmful, leading people away from remembrance of God and corrupting both the individual and society. By shunning them, Muslims can maintain their spiritual purity and focus on good deeds that please Allah and benefit humanity. The verse emphasizes that true success lies in obedience to divine guidance and resisting the temptations of Satan.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا إنما الخمر والميسر والأنصاب والأزلام رجس من عمل الشيطان فاجتنبوه لعلكم تفلحون

translation: Satan only wants to cause between you animosity and hatred through intoxicants and gambling and to avert you from the remembrance of Allah and from prayer. So will you not desist?
interpretation: This verse is a warning from Allah against the evil plots of Satan, who seeks to sow discord and enmity between people through the means of intoxicants (like alcohol) and gambling. These vices not only harm individuals, but also create conflicts and hostility within society. Moreover, indulgence in such activities distracts one from remembering Allah and fulfilling religious obligations like prayer. The verse ends with a question, urging the believers to reflect and abstain from these destructive practices, and to choose the path of righteousness and obedience to Allah.
orig: إنما يريد الشيطان أن يوقع بينكم العداوة والبغضاء في الخمر والميسر ويصدكم عن ذكر الله وعن الصلاة فهل أنتم منتهون

translation: And obey Allah and obey the Messenger and beware. And if you turn away - then know that upon Our Messenger is only [the responsibility for] clear notification.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of obeying Allah and His Messenger, Muhammad (peace be upon him). It warns believers to be mindful of their actions and to avoid turning away from the path of Islam. The verse makes it clear that the Prophet's duty is only to convey the message of Islam clearly and that he is not responsible for people's ultimate choice to accept or reject it. It places the responsibility on each individual to heed the warning and to follow the guidance that has been provided through the Qur'an and the teachings of the Prophet. Ultimately, each person will be accountable for their own decisions and actions.
orig: وأطيعوا الله وأطيعوا الرسول واحذروا فإن توليتم فاعلموا أنما على رسولنا البلاغ المبين

translation: There is no blame upon those who have believed and done righteous deeds for what they have eaten [in the past] if they [now] fear Allah and believe and do righteous deeds, and then fear Allah and believe, and then fear Allah and do good; and Allah loves the doers of good.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that those who have sincerely believed in Allah and performed good deeds will not be held accountable for their past actions, as long as they continue to be mindful of Allah, maintain their faith, and persist in doing what is right. It underscores the importance of having a consistent and steadfast approach in one's faith and actions. The repetition of "fear Allah" highlights the significance of being constantly conscious of Allah and striving to please Him. The verse concludes by stating that Allah loves those who excel in doing good, which serves as an encouragement for believers to always strive for excellence in their righteous conduct.
orig: ليس على الذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات جناح فيما طعموا إذا ما اتقوا وآمنوا وعملوا الصالحات ثم اتقوا وآمنوا ثم اتقوا وأحسنوا والله يحب المحسنين

translation: O you who have believed, Allah will surely test you through something of the game that your hands and spears [can] reach, that Allah may make evident those who fear Him unseen. And whoever transgresses after that - for him is a painful punishment.
interpretation: This verse is a reminder to the believers that Allah will test their faith and obedience through certain prohibitions, such as the prohibition of hunting while in the sacred state of Ihram during Hajj or Umrah. The test is designed to distinguish between those who sincerely fear Allah, even when no one is watching, and those who do not. It emphasizes the importance of obeying Allah's commands and refraining from what He has forbidden, even when it may be tempting or seemingly harmless. The verse also serves as a warning that transgressing Allah's limits after being reminded of them will result in a severe punishment in the Hereafter, highlighting the gravity of disobedience to Allah.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا ليبلونكم الله بشيء من الصيد تناله أيديكم ورماحكم ليعلم الله من يخافه بالغيب فمن اعتدى بعد ذلك فله عذاب أليم

translation: O you who have believed, do not kill game while you are in the state of ihram. And whoever of you kills it intentionally - the penalty is an equivalent from sacrificial animals to what he killed, as judged by two just men among you as an offering [to Allah] delivered to the Ka'bah, or an expiation: the feeding of needy people or the equivalent of that in fasting, that he may taste the consequence of his deed. Allah has pardoned what is past; but whoever returns [to violation], then Allah will take retribution from him. And Allah is Exalted in Might and Owner of Retribution.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the sanctity of the state of ihram during Hajj or Umrah, where hunting is prohibited. It lays out the consequences for violating this prohibition, which include offering a sacrificial animal equivalent to the game killed, as determined by two just members of the community. Alternatively, one can expiate by feeding the needy or fasting for an equivalent period. This is to make the violator mindful of their actions. While Allah forgives past transgressions, repeat offenders will face His retribution, for He is Mighty and capable of punishment. The verse underscores the importance of respect for the sacred rites and the consequences of transgressing the boundaries set by Allah.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا لا تقتلوا الصيد وأنتم حرم ومن قتله منكم متعمدا فجزاء مثل ما قتل من النعم يحكم به ذوا عدل منكم هديا بالغ الكعبة أو كفارة طعام مساكين أو عدل ذلك صياما ليذوق وبال أمره عفا الله عما سلف ومن عاد فينتقم الله منه والله عزيز ذو انتقام

translation: Lawful to you is game from the sea and its food as provision for you and the travelers, but forbidden to you is game from the land as long as you are in the state of ihram. And fear Allah to whom you will be gathered.
interpretation: This verse indicates that Allah has made it permissible for Muslims to catch and eat seafood, whether they are in a state of ihram (ritual purity for pilgrimage) or not. This provision is extended to travelers as well. However, hunting land animals is prohibited during ihram. The verse ends with an exhortation to be mindful of Allah, to whom all will return on the Day of Judgment. This reminder serves to encourage Muslims to obey Allah's commands and refrain from what He has forbidden, as they will be accountable for their deeds in the Hereafter.
orig: أحل لكم صيد البحر وطعامه متاعا لكم وللسيارة وحرم عليكم صيد البر ما دمتم حرما واتقوا الله الذي إليه تحشرون

translation: Allah has made the Ka'bah, the Sacred House, standing for the people and [has sanctified] the sacred months and the sacrificial animals and the garlands [by which they are identified]. That is so you may know that Allah knows what is in the heavens and what is in the earth and that Allah is Knowing of all things.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the sanctity and importance of the Ka'bah, the Sacred House of worship, as a means of spiritual upliftment and unity for all people. It also highlights the significance of the sacred months, sacrificial animals, and garlands, which serve as symbols of devotion and obedience to Allah. The deeper message is that Allah's knowledge encompasses everything in the heavens and the earth, and that humans should strive to recognize and appreciate His omniscience. By honoring these sacred institutions, believers demonstrate their acknowledgment of Allah's wisdom and submit to His divine will, which ultimately leads to a stronger connection with the Creator.
orig: جعل الله الكعبة البيت الحرام قياما للناس والشهر الحرام والهدي والقلائد ذلك لتعلموا أن الله يعلم ما في السماوات وما في الأرض وأن الله بكل شيء عليم

translation: Know that Allah is severe in punishment and that Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse reminds us of the dual nature of Allah's attributes. On one hand, Allah is severe in punishing those who transgress His limits and disobey His commands, emphasizing the importance of fearing Him and avoiding sinful acts. On the other hand, Allah is also Forgiving and Merciful to those who sincerely repent and seek His forgiveness, highlighting His infinite compassion and love for His creation. This verse encourages believers to strike a balance between fear and hope in their relationship with Allah, striving to obey Him while also seeking His mercy and forgiveness when they falter.
orig: اعلموا أن الله شديد العقاب وأن الله غفور رحيم

translation: The Messenger's duty is only to convey the Message. And Allah knows all that you reveal and all that you conceal.
interpretation: The role of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) is to faithfully deliver the message of Islam as revealed to him by Allah. It is not his responsibility to force people to accept it or to ensure that they follow its teachings. Ultimately, Allah is aware of what people openly express as well as what they keep hidden in their hearts, including their true intentions and beliefs. He will hold them accountable for their actions and decisions in response to the message conveyed by the Prophet. This verse emphasizes the limited scope of the Prophet's mission and highlights Allah's omniscience and the individual accountability of each person in matters of faith.
orig: ما على الرسول إلا البلاغ والله يعلم ما تبدون وما تكتمون

translation: Say, "The evil and the good are not equal, even though the abundance of evil might impress you." So fear Allah, O people of understanding, that you may be successful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of distinguishing between good and evil, and choosing the path of righteousness even if the evil seems more appealing or abundant. It reminds us that the ultimate success lies in being mindful of Allah and making choices based on wisdom and understanding, rather than being swayed by temporary attractions or worldly gains. The verse encourages believers to develop a strong moral compass and to make decisions that align with the teachings of Islam, as this is the key to attaining true success and happiness in this life and the hereafter.
orig: قل لا يستوي الخبيث والطيب ولو أعجبك كثرة الخبيث فاتقوا الله يا أولي الألباب لعلكم تفلحون

translation: O you who have believed, do not ask about things which, if they are shown to you, will distress you. But if you ask about them while the Qur'an is being revealed, they will be shown to you. Allah has pardoned that which is past; and Allah is Forgiving and Forbearing.
interpretation: This verse cautions believers against asking unnecessary questions that may cause them distress or discomfort if the answers were to be revealed. It suggests that some matters are better left unquestioned, as the knowledge of them might be a source of anxiety or unease. The verse also implies that Allah, in His wisdom and mercy, has chosen to keep certain things hidden from us for our own benefit. We should trust in Allah's judgment and not be overly curious about matters that do not concern us directly. The verse emphasizes Allah's forgiving and forbearing nature, indicating that He overlooks our past mistakes and shortcomings when we sincerely repent and seek His guidance.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا لا تسألوا عن أشياء إن تبد لكم تسؤكم وإن تسألوا عنها حين ينزل القرآن تبد لكم عفا الله عنها والله غفور حليم

translation: A people before you asked [the same questions] and then they became thereby disbelievers.
interpretation: This verse warns against asking unnecessary or inappropriate questions about matters of faith. It suggests that some people in the past had asked similar questions, perhaps challenging or doubting the teachings of Islam, and as a result, they lost their faith and became disbelievers. The implication is that one should be cautious and respectful when inquiring about religious matters, and not let curiosity or skepticism lead them astray from the path of belief. The verse emphasizes the importance of maintaining a strong and unwavering faith, even in the face of questions or doubts.
orig: قد سألها قوم من قبلكم ثم أصبحوا بها كافرين

translation: Allah has not appointed [such innovations as] bahirah or sa'ibah or wasilah or ham. But those who disbelieve invent falsehood about Allah, and most of them do not reason.
interpretation: This verse is criticizing the pre-Islamic Arabian practice of dedicating certain cattle to idols and superstitions. The bahirah was a she-camel whose milk was spared for the idols and nobody was allowed to milk it. The sa'ibah was a she-camel let loose for free pasture for the idols. The wasilah was a she-camel set free for idols because it had given birth to a she-camel at its first delivery and then again gave birth to a she-camel at its second delivery. The ham was a stallion-camel freed from work for the idols, after it had finished a number of copulations assigned for it. The verse is stating that Allah did not ordain these superstitious practices, but rather it is the disbelievers who invent these lies and attribute them falsely to Allah. Most of them lack understanding to see the irrationality of such practices. Overall, it condemns following baseless customs not sanctioned by Allah.
orig: ما جعل الله من بحيرة ولا سائبة ولا وصيلة ولا حام ولكن الذين كفروا يفترون على الله الكذب وأكثرهم لا يعقلون

translation: And when it is said to them, "Come to what Allah has revealed and to the Messenger," they say, "Sufficient for us is that upon which we found our fathers." Even though their fathers knew nothing, nor were they guided?
interpretation: This verse criticizes those who blindly follow the traditions and beliefs of their ancestors, even if those beliefs are misguided or based on ignorance. It emphasizes the importance of seeking guidance from Allah's revelations and the teachings of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him), rather than relying solely on inherited customs. The verse implies that one should use reason and critical thinking to evaluate the validity of their beliefs, and not simply accept them because they have been passed down through generations. It encourages individuals to take responsibility for their own spiritual growth and to actively seek the truth, rather than remaining complacent in their inherited ways.
orig: وإذا قيل لهم تعالوا إلى ما أنزل الله وإلى الرسول قالوا حسبنا ما وجدنا عليه آباءنا أولو كان آباؤهم لا يعلمون شيئا ولا يهتدون

translation: O you who have believed, upon you is [responsibility for] yourselves. Those who have gone astray will not harm you when you have been guided. To Allah is your return all together; then He will inform you of what you used to do.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of personal responsibility in faith and actions. It reassures the believers that as long as they remain steadfast in their guidance, the misguidance of others will not harm them. Ultimately, everyone will return to Allah and be held accountable for their deeds. This encourages the believers to focus on their own spiritual growth and righteousness, without being overly concerned about the actions of others. It also highlights the concept of individual accountability on the Day of Judgment, where each person will face the consequences of their own choices and actions.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا عليكم أنفسكم لا يضركم من ضل إذا اهتديتم إلى الله مرجعكم جميعا فينبئكم بما كنتم تعملون

translation: O you who have believed, testimony [should be taken] among you when death approaches one of you at the time of bequest - [that of] two just men from among you or two others from outside if you are traveling through the land and the disaster of death should strike you. Detain them after the prayer and let them both swear by Allah if you doubt [their testimony, saying], "We will not exchange it for a price, even if he should be a near relative, and we will not withhold the testimony of Allah. Indeed, we would then be of the sinful."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of having two reliable witnesses present when a person is making their will, especially when death is imminent. These witnesses should be trustworthy individuals, either from within the Muslim community or from outside if the person is traveling. If there is any doubt about the witnesses' reliability, they should be asked to swear an oath after the prayer, affirming that they will not falsify their testimony for any worldly gain, even if it involves a close relative, and that they will not conceal the truth, as doing so would be a grave sin in the sight of Allah. This practice ensures that the rights of the deceased and their beneficiaries are protected, and that the distribution of wealth and assets is carried out according to the will of the deceased, in a just and transparent manner.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا شهادة بينكم إذا حضر أحدكم الموت حين الوصية اثنان ذوا عدل منكم أو آخران من غيركم إن أنتم ضربتم في الأرض فأصابتكم مصيبة الموت تحبسونهما من بعد الصلاة فيقسمان بالله إن ارتبتم لا نشتري به ثمنا ولو كان ذا قربى ولا نكتم شهادة الله إنا إذا لمن الآثمين

translation: But if it is found that those two were guilty of sin, let two others stand in their place from those against whom the former have been guilty, and let them swear by Allah, "Our testimony is truer than their testimony, and we have not transgressed. Indeed, we would then be of the wrongdoers."
interpretation: This verse provides a mechanism for resolving disputes in testimony. If it is discovered that two witnesses have given false testimony, then two other witnesses from those who were wronged by the false testimony should come forward to replace them. These new witnesses should swear by Allah that their testimony is more truthful and that they have not transgressed in their testimony. If they were to lie in this oath, they would be counted among the wrongdoers and sinners. This process helps ensure the integrity of testimony and the establishment of justice.
orig: فإن عثر على أنهما استحقا إثما فآخران يقومان مقامهما من الذين استحق عليهم الأوليان فيقسمان بالله لشهادتنا أحق من شهادتهما وما اعتدينا إنا إذا لمن الظالمين

translation: That is more likely that they will give testimony according to its [true] face or they would fear that [other] oaths might be taken after their oaths. And fear Allah and listen; and Allah does not guide the defiantly disobedient people.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of giving truthful testimony and the consequences of false oaths. It suggests that people are more likely to provide honest testimony if they fear that their false oaths may be exposed by subsequent oaths taken by others. The verse also reminds believers to have taqwa (fear and consciousness) of Allah and to listen to His guidance. It concludes with a warning that Allah does not guide those who are defiantly disobedient and persist in their wrongdoing, highlighting the gravity of giving false testimony and the need for uprightness in one's conduct.
orig: ذلك أدنى أن يأتوا بالشهادة على وجهها أو يخافوا أن ترد أيمان بعد أيمانهم واتقوا الله واسمعوا والله لا يهدي القوم الفاسقين

translation: On the Day when Allah will gather the messengers and say, "What was the response you received?" They will say, "We have no knowledge. Indeed, it is You who is Knower of the unseen."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the ultimate knowledge and wisdom of Allah. Even the messengers, who were chosen by Allah to convey His message to humanity, will acknowledge on the Day of Judgment that they have no knowledge of the unseen and that Allah alone possesses this knowledge. It highlights the importance of humility and the recognition that human knowledge, even that of the prophets, is limited compared to the all-encompassing knowledge of Allah. This verse also serves as a reminder that we should trust in Allah's wisdom and submit to His will, as He is the ultimate source of all knowledge and understanding.
orig: يوم يجمع الله الرسل فيقول ماذا أجبتم قالوا لا علم لنا إنك أنت علام الغيوب

translation: [The Day] when Allah will say, "O Jesus, Son of Mary, remember My favor upon you and upon your mother when I supported you with the Pure Spirit and you spoke to the people in the cradle and in maturity; and [remember] when I taught you writing and wisdom and the Torah and the Gospel; and when you designed from clay [what was] like the form of a bird with My permission, then you breathed into it, and it became a bird with My permission; and you healed the blind and the leper with My permission; and when you brought forth the dead with My permission; and when I restrained the Children of Israel from [killing] you when you came to them with clear proofs and those who disbelieved among them said, "This is not but obvious magic.""
interpretation: This verse highlights the special favors and miracles that Allah granted to Jesus, son of Mary. It emphasizes that these miracles were performed by Jesus only with the permission and support of Allah, not of his own power. This serves to affirm the Islamic belief that Jesus was a highly respected prophet, but not divine himself. The verse also notes how some still rejected Jesus' message and accused him of magic, underlining a recurring Quranic theme of the stubbornness of the disbelievers in the face of clear signs. Overall, the verse upholds Jesus' status as a great prophet while putting his miracles in the context of being manifested through Allah's power, thus maintaining the core monotheistic message of Islam.
orig: إذ قال الله يا عيسى ابن مريم اذكر نعمتي عليك وعلى والدتك إذ أيدتك بروح القدس تكلم الناس في المهد وكهلا وإذ علمتك الكتاب والحكمة والتوراة والإنجيل وإذ تخلق من الطين كهيئة الطير بإذني فتنفخ فيها فتكون طيرا بإذني وتبرئ الأكمه والأبرص بإذني وإذ تخرج الموتى بإذني وإذ كففت بني إسرائيل عنك إذ جئتهم بالبينات فقال الذين كفروا منهم إن هذا إلا سحر مبين

translation: And [remember] when I inspired to the disciples, "Believe in Me and in My messenger Jesus." They said, "We have believed, and bear witness that we are Muslims [in submission to Allah]."
interpretation: This verse highlights the continuity of the divine message and the unity of faith among all the prophets and their followers. The disciples of Jesus, upon receiving divine inspiration, affirmed their belief in Allah and His messenger, Jesus. They declared themselves as Muslims, submitting to the will of Allah. This emphasizes that the core message of all prophets was the same: to believe in the One true God and to submit to His will. It also suggests that the true followers of Jesus were those who embraced Islam and followed the teachings of Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him), as they recognized the unity of the divine message and the continuity of prophethood.
orig: وإذ أوحيت إلى الحواريين أن آمنوا بي وبرسولي قالوا آمنا واشهد بأننا مسلمون

translation: [And remember] when the disciples said, "O Jesus, Son of Mary, can your Lord send down to us a table [spread with food] from the heaven?" [Jesus] said, "Fear Allah, if you should be believers."
interpretation: This verse is a reminder of the importance of having faith and trust in Allah. The disciples of Jesus asked him if Allah could send down a table of food from heaven, which shows a lack of faith on their part. Jesus responded by telling them to fear Allah and have true belief in Him. This highlights the significance of having a strong and unwavering faith in Allah's power and ability to provide for His servants. It also emphasizes the need for believers to rely on Allah and trust in His wisdom, rather than making demands or questioning His capabilities.
orig: إذ قال الحواريون يا عيسى ابن مريم هل يستطيع ربك أن ينزل علينا مائدة من السماء قال اتقوا الله إن كنتم مؤمنين

translation: They said, "We wish to eat from it and let our hearts be reassured and know that you have been truthful to us and be among the witnesses to it."
interpretation: This verse shows the desire of the disciples of Jesus to have a tangible proof of his prophethood and the truth of his message. They wanted to witness a miracle that would strengthen their faith and remove any doubts from their hearts. By asking for a divine table spread with food to descend from heaven, they sought reassurance and certainty in their belief. This highlights the human need for both spiritual and physical nourishment, as well as the role of miracles in solidifying faith. The disciples also wished to bear witness to this event for future generations, recognizing the importance of preserving and conveying the truth to others.
orig: قالوا نريد أن نأكل منها وتطمئن قلوبنا ونعلم أن قد صدقتنا ونكون عليها من الشاهدين

translation: Jesus, son of Mary, said, "O Allah, our Lord, send down to us a table [spread with food] from the heaven to be for us a festival for the first of us and the last of us and a sign from You. And provide for us, and You are the best of providers."
interpretation: This verse demonstrates the faith and trust that Jesus had in Allah. By asking for a miraculous table of food from the heavens, Jesus shows his belief in Allah's power and ability to provide for His servants. The request for the table to serve as a festival and a sign further emphasizes the significance of this miracle as a means of strengthening faith and bringing people together in worship. Additionally, by acknowledging Allah as the best of providers, Jesus highlights the importance of relying on Allah for sustenance, both physical and spiritual.
orig: قال عيسى ابن مريم اللهم ربنا أنزل علينا مائدة من السماء تكون لنا عيدا لأولنا وآخرنا وآية منك وارزقنا وأنت خير الرازقين

translation: Allah said, "I will send it down unto you, but whosoever of you disbelieves afterwards, I will surely punish him with a punishment such as I have not inflicted on anyone among (all) the worlds."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the severity of disbelieving in Allah's signs and revelations after they have been clearly sent down and made apparent. It serves as a stern warning that rejecting faith in God, after His message has been conveyed, is one of the gravest sins that will incur a uniquely terrible punishment in the Hereafter, more severe than any other punishment. This highlights the paramount importance of faith and submission to God's will, and the consequences of arrogantly denying the truth after it has been made manifest through divine revelation.
orig: قال الله إني منزلها عليكم فمن يكفر بعد منكم فإني أعذبه عذابا لا أعذبه أحدا من العالمين

translation: And [beware the Day] when Allah will say, "O Jesus, Son of Mary, did you say to the people, 'Take me and my mother as deities besides Allah?'" He will say, "Exalted are You! It was not for me to say that to which I have no right. If I had said it, You would have known it. You know what is within myself, and I do not know what is within Yourself. Indeed, it is You who is Knower of the unseen.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the pure monotheism of Islam and rejects the Christian concept of the Trinity. It depicts a conversation between Allah and Jesus on the Day of Judgment, where Allah questions Jesus if he ever instructed people to worship him and his mother Mary as divine beings besides Allah. Jesus emphatically denies this, affirming that he would never claim divinity or ask others to worship him, as that would be contrary to the fundamental Islamic belief in the Oneness of Allah. Jesus acknowledges Allah's omniscience, stating that Allah knows what is in his inner self, while he has no knowledge of what is in Allah's essence. This verse serves as a powerful reminder for Muslims to worship Allah alone and avoid ascribing divine attributes to anyone else, including revered prophets like Jesus.
orig: وإذ قال الله يا عيسى ابن مريم أأنت قلت للناس اتخذوني وأمي إلهين من دون الله قال سبحانك ما يكون لي أن أقول ما ليس لي بحق إن كنت قلته فقد علمته تعلم ما في نفسي ولا أعلم ما في نفسك إنك أنت علام الغيوب

translation: I said not to them except what You commanded me - to worship Allah, my Lord and your Lord. And I was a witness over them as long as I was among them; but when You took me up, You were the Observer over them, and You are, over all things, Witness.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Jesus' role as a prophet and messenger of God, who called people to worship the one true God alone. It also highlights God's omniscience and omnipresence, as He is the ultimate witness and observer over all His creation, even after Jesus' ascension. The verse underscores the importance of submitting to God's will and worshipping Him alone, as this was the core message of all prophets, including Jesus.
orig: ما قلت لهم إلا ما أمرتني به أن اعبدوا الله ربي وربكم وكنت عليهم شهيدا ما دمت فيهم فلما توفيتني كنت أنت الرقيب عليهم وأنت على كل شيء شهيد

translation: If You punish them, then indeed they are Your servants, but if You forgive them, then indeed You are the All-Mighty, All-Wise.
interpretation: This verse highlights two key attributes of Allah: His power and His wisdom. It conveys that all humans are ultimately servants of Allah, and their fate rests in His hands alone. If He chooses to punish, it is within His right as the Almighty. However, the verse also emphasizes that if Allah decides to forgive, it is due to His infinite wisdom. The use of the word "Al-Hakeem" (the All-Wise) suggests that Allah's decisions, whether to punish or forgive, are not arbitrary but based on divine wisdom and knowledge that humans may not always comprehend. It serves as a reminder for believers to humble themselves before Allah and trust in His judgment.
orig: إن تعذبهم فإنهم عبادك وإن تغفر لهم فإنك أنت العزيز الحكيم

translation: Allah has said, "This is the Day when the truthful will benefit from their truthfulness. For them are gardens [in Paradise] beneath which rivers flow, wherein they will abide forever, Allah being pleased with them, and they with Him. That is the great attainment."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance and value of truthfulness and honesty. On the Day of Judgment, those who were truthful and sincere in their faith and actions will be rewarded with Paradise, where they will enjoy eternal bliss and contentment. The verse also highlights the reciprocal nature of the relationship between Allah and His faithful servants. Allah is pleased with their devotion and obedience, and they are pleased with the rewards and blessings bestowed upon them by their Lord. This mutual pleasure and satisfaction is described as the ultimate success and triumph, surpassing all worldly gains and achievements.
orig: قال الله هذا يوم ينفع الصادقين صدقهم لهم جنات تجري من تحتها الأنهار خالدين فيها أبدا رضي الله عنهم ورضوا عنه ذلك الفوز العظيم

translation: To Allah belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth and whatever is within them, and He is over all things competent.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute sovereignty and power of Allah over all of creation. It affirms that everything in the heavens and the earth belongs to Him alone, and that He has the ability to do all things. This serves as a reminder to humans that ultimately, it is Allah who is in control of the universe and all that happens within it. It encourages believers to put their trust in Allah and submit to His will, knowing that He is the All-Powerful and All-Capable One who can fulfill their needs and guide them towards what is best.
orig: لله ملك السماوات والأرض وما فيهن وهو على كل شيء قدير

translation: All praise is due to Allah, who created the heavens and the earth and made darkness and light. Yet those who disbelieve equate [others] with their Lord.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah alone deserves all praise and gratitude, for He is the Creator of the entire universe, including the heavens, the earth, darkness, and light. Despite these clear signs of Allah's power and authority, there are still those who disbelieve and associate partners with Him, equating others with their Lord. This interpretation highlights the importance of recognizing Allah's unique status as the sole Creator and the gravity of the sin of shirk (associating partners with Allah), which is in direct contradiction to the fundamental Islamic belief in the oneness of Allah (tawhid).
orig: الحمد لله الذي خلق السماوات والأرض وجعل الظلمات والنور ثم الذين كفروا بربهم يعدلون

translation: It is He who created you from clay and then decreed a term and a specified time [known] to Him; then [still] you are in dispute.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah is the One who created human beings from clay, and that He has decreed a lifespan for each individual, as well as a specific time for the Day of Judgment. Despite this clear knowledge, people still engage in disputes and doubts about the truth of Allah's message and the inevitability of the Hereafter. The verse serves as a reminder of our humble origins, the fleeting nature of worldly life, and the importance of having faith in Allah's plan and purpose for humanity.
orig: هو الذي خلقكم من طين ثم قضى أجلا وأجل مسمى عنده ثم أنتم تمترون

translation: And He is Allah in the heavens and on the earth. He knows what you conceal and what you declare, and He knows what you earn.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the omnipresence and omniscience of Allah. It reminds us that Allah is present everywhere, both in the heavens and on the earth. He has complete knowledge of all our actions, whether they are hidden or apparent. Moreover, Allah is aware of what we earn through our deeds, both good and bad. This verse encourages believers to be mindful of their actions and intentions, as nothing escapes Allah's knowledge. It also highlights the importance of sincerity in our worship and the need to strive for righteousness in all aspects of life, as Allah will hold us accountable for what we earn in this world.
orig: وهو الله في السماوات وفي الأرض يعلم سركم وجهركم ويعلم ما تكسبون

translation: And no sign comes to them from the signs of their Lord except that they are from it turning away.
interpretation: This verse highlights the stubbornness and arrogance of those who reject the truth. Despite being presented with numerous clear signs and proofs from Allah, they persistently turn away and refuse to acknowledge or accept them. They are so deeply entrenched in their disbelief that no matter how many miracles or revelations are shown to them, they remain unmoved and continue in their ways of denial and aversion. It demonstrates the hardness of their hearts and their unwillingness to embrace the guidance that Allah provides through His signs and messengers.
orig: وما تأتيهم من آية من آيات ربهم إلا كانوا عنها معرضين

translation: For they have denied the truth when it came to them, but there will come to them the news of what they used to ridicule.
interpretation: This verse is a warning to those who reject the truth of Islam when it is presented to them. It suggests that these deniers will eventually face the consequences of their mockery and disbelief. They will receive news or tidings of the very thing they used to ridicule, possibly referring to the punishment or reality of the afterlife that they had dismissed. The verse implies that divine justice will ultimately prevail, and those who arrogantly deny the truth will face the repercussions of their choices and actions.
orig: فقد كذبوا بالحق لما جاءهم فسوف يأتيهم أنباء ما كانوا به يستهزئون

translation: Have they not seen how many generations We destroyed before them which We had established upon the earth as We have not established you? And We sent [rain from] the sky upon them in showers and made rivers flow beneath them; then We destroyed them for their sins and brought forth after them a generation of others.
interpretation: This verse is a reminder of the power and might of Allah. It points out that many civilizations before were destroyed by Allah due to their sins and disobedience, even though they were well-established and prosperous. It emphasizes that worldly power and stability is no guarantee of safety from Allah's punishment if one turns away from His path. The verse also underscores the continuous cycle of rise and fall of nations as per Allah's will - new generations replace the ones destroyed. Ultimately, it serves as a warning for people to be mindful of Allah's commands and avoid the fate of those before them.
orig: ألم يروا كم أهلكنا من قبلهم من قرن مكناهم في الأرض ما لم نمكن لكم وأرسلنا السماء عليهم مدرارا وجعلنا الأنهار تجري من تحتهم فأهلكناهم بذنوبهم وأنشأنا من بعدهم قرنا آخرين

translation: And even if We had sent down to you, [O Muhammad], a written scripture on a page and they touched it with their hands, the disbelievers would say, "This is not but obvious magic."
interpretation: This verse highlights the stubborn nature of the disbelievers who refuse to accept the truth of the Qur'an and the prophethood of Muhammad (peace be upon him), even if they were to witness tangible evidence. It suggests that their rejection stems from their arrogance and closed-mindedness, rather than a lack of proof. The verse implies that no matter how clear and convincing the signs of Allah may be, those who have already decided to disbelieve will find ways to dismiss them as mere magic or trickery. It serves as a reminder to the believers to remain steadfast in their faith and not be disheartened by the opposition they face from the disbelievers.
orig: ولو نزلنا عليك كتابا في قرطاس فلمسوه بأيديهم لقال الذين كفروا إن هذا إلا سحر مبين

translation: And they say, "Why was there not sent down to him an angel?" And if We had sent down an angel, the matter would have been decided; then they would not be reprieved.
interpretation: This verse addresses the disbelievers' demand for a physical angel to be sent down as proof of Muhammad's prophethood. However, Allah explains that if He were to send an angel as they requested, it would mark the end of their respite. The appearance of an angel would be a sign of the commencement of divine judgment, leaving no further opportunity for the disbelievers to repent and believe. Allah, in His wisdom and mercy, grants them time to reflect and mend their ways, rather than hastening their punishment by fulfilling their misguided demand for an angel.
orig: وقالوا لولا أنزل عليه ملك ولو أنزلنا ملكا لقضي الأمر ثم لا ينظرون

translation: And if We had made him an angel, We would have made him [appear as] a man, and We would have covered them with that in which they cover themselves.
interpretation: This verse suggests that if God had sent an angel as a messenger instead of a human, He would have given that angel the appearance of a man. This is because humans can only relate to and understand other humans. If the messenger had come in a non-human form, it would have caused confusion and doubt among the people, obscuring the message. By sending human messengers, God ensures that His guidance is accessible and relatable to mankind. The verse also implies that those who reject the human messengers are simply looking for excuses, as they would likely have found reason to doubt even if the messenger had come in another form.
orig: ولو جعلناه ملكا لجعلناه رجلا وللبسنا عليهم ما يلبسون

translation: And indeed, [many] messengers were mocked before you, but those who ridiculed them were enveloped by what they used to ridicule.
interpretation: This verse serves as a reminder and consolation to Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) that he is not the first prophet to face ridicule and mockery from his people. Many prophets before him were also mocked and ridiculed by their communities for conveying the message of Allah. However, the verse also warns that those who mocked the prophets were eventually afflicted by the very punishment they used to ridicule and dismiss. This interpretation highlights the consequences of rejecting the truth and mocking the messengers of Allah, emphasizing that divine retribution will ultimately befall those who persist in their disbelief and ridicule.
orig: ولقد استهزئ برسل من قبلك فحاق بالذين سخروا منهم ما كانوا به يستهزئون

translation: Say, "Travel through the land; then observe how was the end of the deniers."
interpretation: This verse is a reminder for people to reflect on the consequences of denying the truth. It encourages them to travel and observe the ruins of past civilizations that rejected the messages of their prophets. By witnessing the destruction that befell those who denied the truth, one can learn valuable lessons about the importance of faith and the consequences of disbelief. The verse emphasizes that the ultimate fate of those who reject the signs and guidance of Allah is destruction and loss, both in this world and in the hereafter. It serves as a warning for people to heed the message of Islam and to follow the path of righteousness.
orig: قل سيروا في الأرض ثم انظروا كيف كان عاقبة المكذبين

translation: Say, "To whom belongs whatever is in the heavens and earth?" Say, "To Allah." He has decreed upon Himself mercy. He will surely assemble you for the Day of Resurrection, about which there is no doubt. Those who will lose themselves [that Day] do not believe.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's absolute ownership and control over everything in the universe. It highlights His infinite mercy, which He has made incumbent upon Himself. This mercy is evident in His promise to gather all of humanity on the Day of Resurrection, a day that is certain to come. However, those who reject faith in Allah and His message will ultimately lose themselves, both in this world and in the Hereafter, as they fail to recognize and embrace the truth.
orig: قل لمن ما في السماوات والأرض قل لله كتب على نفسه الرحمة ليجمعنكم إلى يوم القيامة لا ريب فيه الذين خسروا أنفسهم فهم لا يؤمنون

translation: And to Him belongs whatsoever exists in the night and the day, and He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that everything in existence, whether it is during the night or day, belongs to Allah alone. It affirms His absolute ownership and control over all things. The mention of "night and day" encompasses all of time, symbolizing the entirety of creation. The verse ends by highlighting two of Allah's essential attributes: He is All-Hearing, meaning He hears every sound and knows every spoken word, and He is All-Knowing, indicating His complete knowledge of all things, whether apparent or hidden, past, present, or future. This verse instills in believers a sense of humility, servitude, and reliance upon Allah, as they recognize His supreme authority and omniscience.
orig: وله ما سكن في الليل والنهار وهو السميع العليم

translation: Say, "Is it other than Allah I should take as a protector, Creator of the heavens and the earth, while it is He who feeds and is not fed?" Say, "Indeed, I have been commanded to be the first [among you] who submit [to Allah] and [was commanded], 'Do not ever be of the polytheists.'"
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of taking Allah as the only protector and guardian, as He is the Creator of the heavens and the earth, and the One who sustains all creation while being self-sufficient. It also highlights the significance of submitting to Allah and shunning polytheism. The verse serves as a reminder that one should rely solely on Allah for guidance, protection, and sustenance, rather than turning to anyone or anything else. It underscores the fundamental Islamic principle of Tawhid (monotheism) and the rejection of shirk (associating partners with Allah).
orig: قل أغير الله أتخذ وليا فاطر السماوات والأرض وهو يطعم ولا يطعم قل إني أمرت أن أكون أول من أسلم ولا تكونن من المشركين

translation: Say, "Indeed I fear, if I should disobey my Lord, the punishment of a tremendous Day."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of obedience to Allah and the fear of His punishment on the Day of Judgment. It serves as a reminder for the believer to stay on the right path and to avoid disobedience, as the consequences of going against Allah's commands are severe. The verse also highlights the magnitude and gravity of the Day of Judgment, describing it as a "tremendous Day," indicating the immense significance and impact it will have on every soul. This instills a sense of awe and reverence for Allah's power and justice, encouraging the believer to lead a life of righteousness and submission to His will.
orig: قل إني أخاف إن عصيت ربي عذاب يوم عظيم

translation: Whoever is spared from it on that Day, He has certainly granted him mercy. And that is the clear attainment.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the ultimate success and salvation on the Day of Judgment. It indicates that whoever is saved from the punishment of Hell on that momentous day has indeed received God's infinite mercy and forgiveness. Attaining this salvation is described as the "clear attainment" or the greatest triumph one can achieve, surpassing all worldly accomplishments. It highlights the significance of striving for God's mercy and forgiveness in this life to be among those spared from the torment of Hell and granted eternal bliss in Paradise.
orig: من يصرف عنه يومئذ فقد رحمه وذلك الفوز المبين

translation: And if Allah should touch you with adversity, there is no remover of it except Him. And if He touches you with good - then He is over all things competent.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute power and control of Allah over all aspects of human life. It conveys the message that if Allah decides to afflict someone with hardship or adversity, no one else has the power to remove it except Him. Conversely, if Allah blesses someone with goodness and prosperity, it is a testament to His omnipotence and ability to do all things. The verse encourages believers to put their trust in Allah, knowing that He alone has the ultimate authority to determine the course of their lives, and to seek His help and guidance in both times of ease and difficulty.
orig: وإن يمسسك الله بضر فلا كاشف له إلا هو وإن يمسسك بخير فهو على كل شيء قدير

translation: And He is the Omnipotent over His servants, and He is the Wise, the Aware.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's absolute power and control over His creation. He is Al-Qahir, the Omnipotent and Irresistible, whose will prevails over all things. Nothing happens except by His decree. At the same time, He is Al-Hakeem, the Wise, whose every command and action is full of wisdom and purpose. He is also Al-Khabeer, the All-Aware, who knows the secrets of the hearts and the hidden realities of all things. This reminds us to submit to Allah's will, trust in His wisdom, and be ever conscious that He is fully aware of us at all times.
orig: وهو القاهر فوق عباده وهو الحكيم الخبير

translation: Say, "What thing is greatest in testimony?" Say, "Allah is witness between me and you. And this Qur'an was revealed to me that I may warn you thereby and whomever it reaches. Do you [truly] testify that with Allah there are other deities?" Say, "I will not testify [with you]." Say, "Indeed, He is but one God, and indeed, I am free of what you associate [with Him]."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the fundamental Islamic belief in the oneness of God (tawhid). It challenges the polytheistic beliefs of the Meccans by asking them to consider what the greatest testimony is. The answer is that Allah Himself is the greatest witness, and He has revealed the Qur'an to Muhammad as a warning to all who hear its message. The Prophet is instructed to firmly reject the idea of other deities besides Allah and to affirm His uniqueness. This verse serves as a powerful reminder for Muslims to maintain their belief in the absolute oneness of God and to reject any form of idolatry or polytheism.
orig: قل أي شيء أكبر شهادة قل الله شهيد بيني وبينكم وأوحي إلي هذا القرآن لأنذركم به ومن بلغ أئنكم لتشهدون أن مع الله آلهة أخرى قل لا أشهد قل إنما هو إله واحد وإنني بريء مما تشركون

translation: Those to whom We have given the Book recognize it as they recognize their [own] sons. Those who will lose themselves [in the Hereafter] do not believe.
interpretation: This verse is referring to the People of the Book, namely the Jews and Christians, who were given previous scriptures by Allah. They recognize the truth of the Qur'an and the prophethood of Muhammad (peace be upon him) as clearly as they recognize their own children. However, some of them still refuse to believe despite this recognition, and as a result, they will lose themselves in the Hereafter by incurring Allah's punishment for their disbelief. The verse highlights the tragedy of those who reject faith despite having clear signs and knowledge, and the consequences they will face in the afterlife for their choice.
orig: الذين آتيناهم الكتاب يعرفونه كما يعرفون أبناءهم الذين خسروا أنفسهم فهم لا يؤمنون

translation: And who is more unjust than one who invents about Allah a lie or denies His verses? Indeed, the wrongdoers will not succeed.
