interpretation: This verse strongly condemns those who fabricate lies against Allah or reject His clear signs and revelations. It emphasizes that such people are the most unjust and wrongful of all, as they not only deceive themselves but also mislead others. The verse asserts that those who engage in such grave injustice and wrongdoing will never attain success or salvation, neither in this world nor in the Hereafter. It serves as a stern warning to all believers to refrain from such heinous sins and to hold fast to the truth revealed by Allah.
orig: ومن أظلم ممن افترى على الله كذبا أو كذب بآياته إنه لا يفلح الظالمون

translation: And [mention] the Day when We will gather them all together; then We will say to those who associated others with Allah, "Where are your 'partners' that you used to claim [with Him]?"
interpretation: This verse is a stern warning to those who associate partners with Allah in worship. On the Day of Judgment, Allah will gather all of mankind and then question the polytheists about the false gods they used to worship alongside Him. This question is rhetorical, as it will expose the falsehood of their beliefs and the powerlessness of their so-called "partners". It emphasizes that ultimately, everyone will stand alone before Allah and be held accountable for their deeds and beliefs. The verse also serves as a reminder to the believers to shun all forms of polytheism and to worship Allah alone, as that is the only path to salvation in the Hereafter.
orig: ويوم نحشرهم جميعا ثم نقول للذين أشركوا أين شركاؤكم الذين كنتم تزعمون

translation: Then their excuse was no other than that they said, "By Allah, our Lord, we were not idolaters."
interpretation: This verse refers to the excuses the idolaters will make on the Day of Judgment when they will be questioned about their idolatry. They will swear by Allah that they were not idolaters, lying to avoid punishment. However, their false oaths will not benefit them, as Allah knows the truth of their actions and intentions. This highlights the human tendency to deny wrongdoing and make excuses, even before God. It also emphasizes that no one can deceive Allah and escape the consequences of their deeds, as He is All-Knowing and All-Wise.
orig: ثم لم تكن فتنتهم إلا أن قالوا والله ربنا ما كنا مشركين

translation: Look how they lied to themselves and lost what they used to invent.
interpretation: This verse is a reminder of the consequences of self-deception and falsehood. When people engage in lies and fabrications, they ultimately harm themselves. The very false beliefs and inventions they cling to will eventually be lost and fail them. It is a warning that dishonesty and living in a false reality will lead to one's own detriment and loss. The verse emphasizes the importance of being truthful with oneself and others, as lies and deceptions are unsustainable and will ultimately collapse, leaving the person with nothing.
orig: انظر كيف كذبوا على أنفسهم وضل عنهم ما كانوا يفترون

translation: And among them are those who listen to you, but We have placed over their hearts coverings, lest they understand it, and in their ears deafness. And if they should see every sign, they will not believe in it. Even when they come to you arguing with you, those who disbelieve say, "This is not but legends of the former peoples."
interpretation: This verse highlights the stubborn attitude of the disbelievers who, despite hearing the Prophet's message and witnessing clear signs, refuse to believe due to the veils of ignorance and arrogance covering their hearts. They dismiss the divine revelation as mere legends of the past, engaging in futile arguments with the Prophet. This emphasizes the importance of having an open heart and mind to recognize and accept the truth, as mere exposure to the message does not guarantee faith without sincere reflection and divine guidance.
orig: ومنهم من يستمع إليك وجعلنا على قلوبهم أكنة أن يفقهوه وفي آذانهم وقرا وإن يروا كل آية لا يؤمنوا بها حتى إذا جاءوك يجادلونك يقول الذين كفروا إن هذا إلا أساطير الأولين

translation: And they forbid [people] from it and are [themselves] remote from it. And they do not destroy except themselves, but they perceive [it] not.
interpretation: This verse highlights the hypocrisy of those who preach against something but secretly engage in it themselves. They warn others to stay away from what they consider sinful, yet they indulge in the same behavior when no one is looking. In doing so, they only bring about their own spiritual destruction, corrupting their souls and distancing themselves from God's mercy. However, they are often oblivious to the damage they inflict upon themselves, failing to recognize the consequences of their actions both in this world and the hereafter.
orig: وهم ينهون عنه وينأون عنه وإن يهلكون إلا أنفسهم وما يشعرون

translation: If you could but see when they are made to stand before the Fire and will say, "Oh, would that we could be returned [to life on earth] and not deny the signs of our Lord and be among the believers."
interpretation: This verse is a reminder of the regret and remorse that the disbelievers will feel on the Day of Judgment when they are confronted with the consequences of their actions. They will wish to be sent back to the world to correct their mistakes and believe in the signs of Allah, but it will be too late. This highlights the importance of believing in Allah and following His guidance in this life, as there will be no second chances in the Hereafter. It also emphasizes the reality of the Hellfire and the severe punishment that awaits those who reject faith.
orig: ولو ترى إذ وقفوا على النار فقالوا يا ليتنا نرد ولا نكذب بآيات ربنا ونكون من المؤمنين

translation: Rather, what they concealed before has [now] appeared to them. And even if they were returned, they would return to that which they were forbidden; and indeed, they are liars.
interpretation: This verse suggests that the hypocrites' true nature and intentions have been exposed, despite their previous attempts to conceal them. It also implies that even if they were given another chance, they would revert to their forbidden and sinful behavior, as they are inherently dishonest and insincere in their faith. This interpretation highlights the deep-rooted hypocrisy and lack of genuine commitment to Islamic principles among those who outwardly profess faith but inwardly harbor disbelief and malicious intentions.
orig: بل بدا لهم ما كانوا يخفون من قبل ولو ردوا لعادوا لما نهوا عنه وإنهم لكاذبون

translation: And they say, "There is not but our worldly life, and we will not be resurrected."
interpretation: This verse refers to the disbelievers who deny the existence of an afterlife and the Day of Resurrection. They believe that their worldly life is the only reality and that there is nothing beyond death. This interpretation highlights the narrow-mindedness and short-sightedness of those who reject the concept of accountability and the ultimate purpose of human existence, which is to worship Allah and prepare for the eternal life in the Hereafter. The verse serves as a reminder for believers to maintain their faith in the Day of Judgment and to live their lives in accordance with Islamic teachings, as opposed to falling into the trap of disbelief and denying the inevitable reality of resurrection and divine justice.
orig: وقالوا إن هي إلا حياتنا الدنيا وما نحن بمبعوثين

translation: And if you could but see when they will be made to stand before their Lord. He will say, "Is this [resurrection] not the truth?" They will say, "Yes, by our Lord." He will [then] say, "So taste the punishment because you used to disbelieve."
interpretation: This verse is a stark reminder of the consequences of disbelief in the Hereafter. It depicts a scene from the Day of Judgment when the disbelievers will be made to stand before Allah, and He will question them about their denial of the truth. They will admit that the resurrection and the judgment are indeed true, acknowledging Allah's Lordship. However, it will be too late for them, and they will be condemned to taste the punishment of Hell as a result of their disbelief and rejection of the truth in their worldly life. This verse emphasizes the importance of faith and the gravity of denying the Hereafter, as it will lead to severe and eternal consequences in the afterlife.
orig: ولو ترى إذ وقفوا على ربهم قال أليس هذا بالحق قالوا بلى وربنا قال فذوقوا العذاب بما كنتم تكفرون

translation: Those who deny the Meeting with Allah have certainly lost, until when the Hour comes upon them unexpectedly, they will say, "Oh, [how great is] our regret over what we neglected concerning it," while they bear their burdens on their backs. Unquestionably, evil is that which they bear.
interpretation: This verse is a stark warning to those who reject the concept of being held accountable before Allah on the Day of Judgment. Their realization of the truth will come too late, when the Day of Resurrection arrives suddenly, and they will be full of regret for not heeding the message and preparing for that Meeting in their worldly lives. The burdens on their backs symbolize the weight of their sins and misdeeds, which they will carry with them as a consequence of their denial and heedlessness. The verse emphasizes the severity of their fate and the evil nature of the metaphorical burdens they will bear as a result of their disbelief.
orig: قد خسر الذين كذبوا بلقاء الله حتى إذا جاءتهم الساعة بغتة قالوا يا حسرتنا على ما فرطنا فيها وهم يحملون أوزارهم على ظهورهم ألا ساء ما يزرون

translation: And the worldly life is not but amusement and diversion; but the home of the Hereafter is best for those who fear Allah, so will you not reason?
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the fleeting and ultimately meaningless nature of worldly pursuits and pleasures compared to the eternal rewards of the Hereafter. It serves as a reminder for believers to prioritize their actions and decisions based on what is pleasing to Allah and beneficial for their souls in the life to come, rather than being distracted by temporary entertainments in this world. The verse also urges people to use their intellect and reason to recognize the superiority of the Hereafter over the worldly life, and to live accordingly with righteousness and mindfulness of Allah.
orig: وما الحياة الدنيا إلا لعب ولهو وللدار الآخرة خير للذين يتقون أفلا تعقلون

translation: We know that you, [O Muhammad], are saddened by what they say. And indeed, they do not call you untruthful, but it is the verses of Allah that the wrongdoers reject.
interpretation: This verse is consoling the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and reassuring him that the disbelievers are not rejecting him personally, but rather they are rejecting the message and verses of Allah that he is conveying. It is a reminder that the Prophet should not be disheartened by their rejection and should continue his mission of spreading the truth, for it is not a personal attack against him but a rejection of the divine message due to the wrongdoers' own ignorance and stubbornness.
orig: قد نعلم إنه ليحزنك الذي يقولون فإنهم لا يكذبونك ولكن الظالمين بآيات الله يجحدون

translation: And certainly were messengers denied before you, but they were patient over [the effects of] denial, and they were harmed until Our victory came to them. And none can alter the words of Allah. And there has certainly come to you some information about the [previous] messengers.
interpretation: This verse is a reminder to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) that he is not the first prophet to face rejection and persecution. Many prophets before him were also denied and harmed by their people, but they remained patient and steadfast in their faith until Allah's help and victory came to them. The verse also emphasizes that no one can change or alter the words and decrees of Allah. The stories of the previous prophets serve as a source of comfort and encouragement for the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and the believers, reminding them that the ultimate victory belongs to those who remain patient and steadfast in the face of adversity and persecution.
orig: ولقد كذبت رسل من قبلك فصبروا على ما كذبوا وأوذوا حتى أتاهم نصرنا ولا مبدل لكلمات الله ولقد جاءك من نبإ المرسلين

translation: And if their evasion is difficult for you, then if you are able to seek a tunnel into the earth or a stairway into the sky to bring them a sign, [then do so]. But if Allah had willed, He would have united them upon guidance. So never be of the ignorant.
interpretation: This verse is addressing the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him), telling him that if he finds it difficult to bear the disbelief and rejection of his message by his people, he should not go to extreme lengths to convince them, such as seeking a tunnel into the earth or a stairway into the sky to bring them a miraculous sign. It emphasizes that guidance is ultimately in the hands of Allah, and He could have united all people upon the right path if He so willed. The Prophet is advised not to be among the ignorant who fail to recognize this reality and exert themselves in vain. The verse highlights the importance of recognizing the limitations of human efforts in the face of Allah's divine will and wisdom.
orig: وإن كان كبر عليك إعراضهم فإن استطعت أن تبتغي نفقا في الأرض أو سلما في السماء فتأتيهم بآية ولو شاء الله لجمعهم على الهدى فلا تكونن من الجاهلين

translation: Only those who listen will respond. But the dead - Allah will resurrect them; then to Him they will be returned.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that only those who are spiritually alive and attentive to God's message will respond to it and benefit from it. Those who are spiritually dead, i.e., those who have closed their hearts to faith, are like lifeless corpses. However, Allah has the power to resurrect even the dead and bring them back to Him for judgment. This serves as a reminder that everyone will ultimately face the consequences of their actions and beliefs in the Hereafter, and that it is never too late for one to turn to Allah and embrace His message.
orig: إنما يستجيب الذين يسمعون والموتى يبعثهم الله ثم إليه يرجعون

translation: And they say, "Why is a sign not sent down to him from his Lord?" Say, "Indeed, Allah is Able to send down a sign, but most of them do not know."
interpretation: This verse addresses the disbelievers who demand a miraculous sign from the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) as proof of his prophethood. Allah responds by affirming His power and ability to send down any sign He wills, but also points out that most of the disbelievers lack true knowledge and understanding. The interpretation is that even if a clear sign were sent, many would still not believe due to their obstinacy and ignorance of Allah's wisdom and power. It emphasizes the importance of faith and submission to Allah's will, rather than relying solely on tangible proofs or miracles.
orig: وقالوا لولا نزل عليه آية من ربه قل إن الله قادر على أن ينزل آية ولكن أكثرهم لا يعلمون

translation: There is no creature that crawls on the earth, nor a bird that flies with its wings, but are communities like yourselves. We have neglected nothing in the Book. Then to their Lord they shall be gathered.
interpretation: This verse highlights the unity and interconnectedness of all living beings in God's creation. It suggests that animals, like humans, form their own communities and have their own ways of life. The verse also emphasizes the completeness and comprehensiveness of the Qur'an, stating that nothing has been left out of this divine book. Finally, it reminds us that all creatures will ultimately return to their Lord, indicating the inevitability of the Day of Judgment and the accountability of all beings before God. This verse encourages us to view all of God's creation with respect and to recognize the common destiny shared by all living things.
orig: وما من دابة في الأرض ولا طائر يطير بجناحيه إلا أمم أمثالكم ما فرطنا في الكتاب من شيء ثم إلى ربهم يحشرون

translation: But those who deny Our signs are deaf and dumb within darknesses. Whomever Allah wills - He leaves astray; and whomever He wills - He puts him on a straight path.
interpretation: This verse speaks to the spiritual condition of those who reject the signs and guidance of Allah. They are described as being "deaf and dumb", meaning they are unable or unwilling to hear and understand the truth. They exist in a state of darkness, lost without the light of faith. The verse also affirms that Allah is in ultimate control - He allows some to stray, by their own choices and actions, while He guides others to the straight path. It is a reminder that guidance and misguidance are in the hands of Allah, but we have the free will to make choices that impact our spiritual destiny. Ultimately, it is up to Allah whether someone remains astray or is guided aright.
orig: والذين كذبوا بآياتنا صم وبكم في الظلمات من يشإ الله يضلله ومن يشأ يجعله على صراط مستقيم

translation: Say, "Have you considered: if there came to you the punishment of Allah or there came to you the Hour - is it other than Allah you would invoke, if you should be truthful?"
interpretation: This verse is a challenge to those who worship other than Allah, asking them to consider what they would do if faced with Allah's punishment or the coming of the Day of Judgment. It implies that in such dire circumstances, they would inevitably call upon Allah alone for help, recognizing His supreme power and authority. This highlights the futility and inconsistency of worshipping others besides Him, as they would be of no avail in the face of Allah's judgment. The verse emphasizes that true faith and devotion should be directed towards Allah alone, as He is the only one who can provide ultimate salvation and protection.
orig: قل أرأيتكم إن أتاكم عذاب الله أو أتتكم الساعة أغير الله تدعون إن كنتم صادقين

translation: Rather, it is Him [alone] you call, and He removes that for which you called upon Him if He wills, and you forget what you associate [with Him].
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute power and sovereignty of Allah. When people are in distress, they instinctively call upon Allah alone for help, forgetting the false gods they associate with Him. This shows that deep down, they recognize Allah as the only true God who can answer their prayers and remove their afflictions. It also highlights the folly of shirk (associating partners with Allah), as these false deities are powerless and forgotten in times of crisis. The verse reminds us to turn to Allah alone and to abandon any form of idolatry or polytheism, as only He has the ability to respond to our supplications and alleviate our hardships, if He so wills.
orig: بل إياه تدعون فيكشف ما تدعون إليه إن شاء وتنسون ما تشركون

translation: And indeed We sent [messengers] to nations before you, [O Muhammad], and We seized them with poverty and hardship that perhaps they might humble themselves [to Us].
interpretation: This verse is a reminder that Allah has sent messengers to previous nations, just as He has sent Prophet Muhammad to his people. When these past nations rejected the message and turned away from the truth, Allah afflicted them with various difficulties such as poverty, illness, and other hardships. The purpose of these trials was to humble them and make them turn back to Allah in repentance and supplication. It is a warning that if the people of Prophet Muhammad also reject the message, they may face similar consequences. The verse emphasizes the importance of humility, gratitude, and turning to Allah during times of ease and hardship alike.
orig: ولقد أرسلنا إلى أمم من قبلك فأخذناهم بالبأساء والضراء لعلهم يتضرعون

translation: Then why, when Our punishment came to them, did they not humble themselves? But their hearts became hardened, and Satan made attractive to them that which they were doing.
interpretation: This verse is a rebuke to those who persist in their wrongdoing and disobedience to Allah, even when faced with His punishment. It suggests that instead of being humbled and turning to Allah in repentance when afflicted with difficulties, their hearts grew harder and they continued in their sinful ways, being further misled by the whisperings and temptations of Satan. The verse emphasizes the danger of allowing one's heart to be hardened and being enticed by the temporary allure of sin, as this leads one further away from Allah's guidance and mercy.
orig: فلولا إذ جاءهم بأسنا تضرعوا ولكن قست قلوبهم وزين لهم الشيطان ما كانوا يعملون

translation: So when they forgot that by which they had been reminded, We opened to them the doors of every [good] thing until, when they rejoiced in that which they were given, We seized them suddenly, and they were [then] in despair.
interpretation: This verse is a warning to those who forget Allah's blessings and become arrogant. It suggests that when people are ungrateful and turn away from divine guidance, Allah may initially grant them worldly pleasures and success as a test. They become engrossed in these material blessings, thinking they have achieved it all by themselves. However, at the height of their exultation and self-delusion, Allah seizes them suddenly with punishment, leaving them in utter despair and hopelessness. It highlights the fleeting nature of worldly joys and the importance of remaining humble and grateful to Allah at all times, knowing that both blessings and trials come from Him.
orig: فلما نسوا ما ذكروا به فتحنا عليهم أبواب كل شيء حتى إذا فرحوا بما أوتوا أخذناهم بغتة فإذا هم مبلسون

translation: So the root of the people who did wrong was cut off. And all praise is due to Allah, Lord of the worlds.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the ultimate fate of those who engage in wrongdoing and oppression. It suggests that their power and influence will eventually be destroyed or "cut off" by Allah, as a consequence of their unjust actions. The phrase "root of the people" implies that not only the individuals, but their entire power structure and legacy will be eradicated. The verse ends with praising Allah as the "Lord of the worlds," affirming His supreme authority and control over all creation, and His ability to bring about justice and retribution against the wrongdoers in due time. It serves as a warning to those who oppress others and a reassurance to the oppressed that Allah will ultimately support and deliver justice to them.
orig: فقطع دابر القوم الذين ظلموا والحمد لله رب العالمين

translation: Say, "Have you considered: if Allah should take away your hearing and your sight and set a seal upon your hearts, which deity other than Allah could bring them [back] to you?" Look how We diversify the verses; then they [still] turn away.
interpretation: This verse is a powerful reminder of Allah's absolute control over our faculties and the need to acknowledge His supremacy. It challenges the disbelievers to consider that if Allah were to take away their hearing, sight, and seal their hearts, no other deity could restore them. The verse emphasizes the complete dependence of human beings on Allah's mercy and the futility of turning to anyone else for help. It also highlights the Quran's use of diverse examples and arguments to convey its message, yet the disbelievers persist in their rejection. This interpretation underscores the importance of recognizing Allah's omnipotence and the consequences of denying His signs and guidance.
orig: قل أرأيتم إن أخذ الله سمعكم وأبصاركم وختم على قلوبكم من إله غير الله يأتيكم به انظر كيف نصرف الآيات ثم هم يصدفون

translation: Say, "Have you considered: if the punishment of Allah should come to you unexpectedly or manifestly, will any be destroyed but the wrongdoing people?"
interpretation: This verse is a warning to those who persist in wrongdoing and disbelief. It reminds us that Allah's punishment can come suddenly or openly, and when it does, only the wrongdoers will be destroyed. The righteous believers who follow Allah's guidance will be saved. It is a call to reflect on our actions and the consequences we may face if we do not change our ways and turn to Allah in repentance. The verse emphasizes the justice of Allah, as He does not punish indiscriminately, but rather those who have earned it through their own misdeeds.
orig: قل أرأيتكم إن أتاكم عذاب الله بغتة أو جهرة هل يهلك إلا القوم الظالمون

translation: And We send not the messengers except as bringers of good tidings and warners. So whoever believes and reforms - there will be no fear concerning them, nor will they grieve.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the role of the messengers sent by Allah. They serve two primary functions: to bring good news to those who believe and do righteous deeds, assuring them of Allah's pleasure and reward, and to warn those who disbelieve and engage in wrongdoing of the consequences of their actions. The verse then states that those who accept the message, believe in Allah, and reform their conduct will have nothing to fear in this world or the Hereafter, nor will they grieve over what they may have lost or missed in worldly affairs. This interpretation highlights the importance of faith and righteous action in attaining inner peace and tranquility, knowing that Allah's mercy and protection will be with those who follow the guidance brought by His messengers.
orig: وما نرسل المرسلين إلا مبشرين ومنذرين فمن آمن وأصلح فلا خوف عليهم ولا هم يحزنون

translation: But those who deny Our signs are touched by the punishment because they used to defiantly disobey.
interpretation: This verse warns that those who reject the signs and revelations of Allah will face severe consequences in the form of divine punishment. Their denial and disobedience stem from their persistent sinfulness and rebellion against Allah's commands. The verse emphasizes that the punishment is a direct result of their own evil actions and defiance. It serves as a reminder that faith and obedience to Allah's message are essential to avoid His wrath and attain His mercy in this world and the Hereafter.
orig: والذين كذبوا بآياتنا يمسهم العذاب بما كانوا يفسقون

translation: Say, "I do not tell you that I have the depositories of Allah or that I know the unseen, nor do I tell you that I am an angel. I only follow what is revealed to me." Say, "Is the blind equivalent to the seeing? Then will you not give thought?"
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the human limitations of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him). He is instructed to clarify that he does not possess God's treasures, nor does he have knowledge of the unseen, and he is not an angel. Rather, he is a human being who follows the divine revelation given to him. The verse then poses a rhetorical question, comparing the blind and the seeing, to encourage people to reflect and understand the difference between those who are guided by revelation and those who are not.
orig: قل لا أقول لكم عندي خزائن الله ولا أعلم الغيب ولا أقول لكم إني ملك إن أتبع إلا ما يوحى إلي قل هل يستوي الأعمى والبصير أفلا تتفكرون

translation: And warn with it those who fear that they will be gathered before their Lord - for them besides Him will be no protector and no intercessor - that they might become righteous.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of fearing Allah and being mindful of the Day of Judgment. The Qur'an serves as a warning to those who believe in the Hereafter, reminding them that on that day, they will have no one to protect or intercede for them except Allah. This realization should motivate believers to lead righteous lives, following the guidance of the Qur'an and striving to please their Lord. The verse highlights the individual responsibility of each person and the necessity of developing a direct connection with Allah through piety and good deeds.
orig: وأنذر به الذين يخافون أن يحشروا إلى ربهم ليس لهم من دونه ولي ولا شفيع لعلهم يتقون

translation: And do not send away those who call upon their Lord morning and evening, seeking His countenance. Not upon you is anything of their account and not upon them is anything of your account. So were you to send them away, you would [then] be of the wrongdoers.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of not discriminating against or turning away those who sincerely worship and call upon Allah, regardless of their social status or appearance. It reminds the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and the believers that they are not accountable for the actions or intentions of others, and that each person is responsible for their own deeds. The verse also warns against the sin of wrongfully sending away the sincere worshippers of Allah, as this would be an act of oppression and injustice.
orig: ولا تطرد الذين يدعون ربهم بالغداة والعشي يريدون وجهه ما عليك من حسابهم من شيء وما من حسابك عليهم من شيء فتطردهم فتكون من الظالمين

translation: And thus We have tried some of them through others that they might say, "Is it these whom Allah has favored among us?" Is not Allah most knowing of those who are grateful?
interpretation: This verse highlights the fact that God tests people through one another, by giving some more wealth, status or blessings than others. This is done to see how they react - whether those given less will question God's wisdom and feel envy, or whether they will remain grateful and content with their portion. It also tests those given more, to see if they will be arrogant or humble, grateful or ungrateful for their blessings. Ultimately, God knows best who is truly grateful to Him regardless of their worldly status, and He will reward people accordingly in the Hereafter based on their faith, actions and inner state, not their outward circumstances in this temporary world.
orig: وكذلك فتنا بعضهم ببعض ليقولوا أهؤلاء من الله عليهم من بيننا أليس الله بأعلم بالشاكرين

translation: When those come to you who believe in Our verses, say, "Peace be upon you. Your Lord has decreed upon Himself mercy: that any of you who does wrong out of ignorance and then repents after that and corrects himself - indeed, He is Forgiving and Merciful."
interpretation: This verse highlights the immense mercy and forgiveness of Allah. It instructs the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) to greet the believers with "Peace be upon you" when they come to him, reassuring them that Allah has decreed mercy upon Himself. This means that Allah's mercy is an inherent part of His divine attributes. The verse then emphasizes that if anyone commits a wrong out of ignorance, but later repents sincerely and mends their ways, Allah will forgive them and show mercy. This interpretation underscores the importance of repentance and self-correction in the path of spiritual growth, and the boundless mercy of Allah towards those who turn to Him in sincere repentance.
orig: وإذا جاءك الذين يؤمنون بآياتنا فقل سلام عليكم كتب ربكم على نفسه الرحمة أنه من عمل منكم سوءا بجهالة ثم تاب من بعده وأصلح فأنه غفور رحيم

translation: And thus do We detail the verses, and [thus] the way of the criminals will become evident.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah explains His verses and signs in detail so that the path of the wrongdoers and criminals becomes clear and evident. By making the truth plain and apparent through His revelations, Allah exposes the falsehood of those who reject His guidance and persist in sin and disbelief. The detailed verses serve as a means of distinguishing between the righteous and the criminal, making the consequences of one's choices clear for all to see.
orig: وكذلك نفصل الآيات ولتستبين سبيل المجرمين

translation: Say, "Indeed, I have been forbidden to worship those you invoke besides Allah." Say, "I will not follow your desires, for I would then have gone astray, and I would not be of the [rightly] guided."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of worshipping Allah alone and not following the desires or false beliefs of others. The Prophet Muhammad is instructed to declare that he has been forbidden to worship anyone or anything besides Allah, and that he will not give in to the pressure or temptations of those who invite him to do so. Following one's own desires or the misguided beliefs of others leads to misguidance and straying from the straight path. The verse highlights the significance of remaining steadfast in the worship of Allah alone and seeking guidance from Him, rather than succumbing to the whims and desires of those who are misguided.
orig: قل إني نهيت أن أعبد الذين تدعون من دون الله قل لا أتبع أهواءكم قد ضللت إذا وما أنا من المهتدين

translation: Say, "Indeed, I am on clear evidence from my Lord, and you have denied it. I do not have that for which you are impatient. The decision is only for Allah. He relates the truth, and He is the best of deciders."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the Prophet's unwavering faith in the message he has received from Allah, despite the disbelief and impatience of his opponents. It highlights that the ultimate judgment and decision belong to Allah alone, who is the source of all truth and the best of judges. The Prophet is instructed to convey this message with confidence and to remind his detractors that their hastiness for punishment will not change the fact that Allah's judgment will prevail, and His truth will be made manifest in due time.
orig: قل إني على بينة من ربي وكذبتم به ما عندي ما تستعجلون به إن الحكم إلا لله يقص الحق وهو خير الفاصلين

translation: Say, "If I had that for which you are impatient, the matter would have been decided between me and you, but Allah is most knowing of the wrongdoers."
interpretation: This verse is a reminder that the ultimate judgment and decision belongs to Allah alone. If the Prophet Muhammad had the power to bring about the punishment that the disbelievers were hastily demanding, the matter would have been settled decisively between them. However, Allah is the Most Wise and the Most Knowing of those who commit injustice and wrongdoing. He alone will determine the appropriate time and manner of judgment, and His decision will be just and fair. The verse emphasizes the importance of patience, trust in Allah's wisdom, and the realization that the ultimate outcome rests with Him alone.
orig: قل لو أن عندي ما تستعجلون به لقضي الأمر بيني وبينكم والله أعلم بالظالمين

translation: And with Him are the keys of the unseen; none knows them except Him. And He knows what is on the land and in the sea. Not a leaf falls but that He knows it. And no grain is there within the darknesses of the earth and no moist or dry [thing] but that it is [written] in a clear record.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the all-encompassing knowledge and omniscience of Allah. It states that Allah alone possesses the keys to the unseen, which includes knowledge of the future and all that is hidden from human perception. Furthermore, Allah's knowledge extends to every detail in the universe, from the vastness of the land and sea to the smallest falling leaf or grain buried deep within the earth. The verse also asserts that everything, whether moist or dry, is recorded in a clear book, which can be understood as a reference to the divine decree or the preserved tablet (al-Lawh al-Mahfūz). This interpretation highlights the absolute sovereignty and infinite wisdom of Allah, as well as the idea that nothing escapes His knowledge or control.
orig: وعنده مفاتح الغيب لا يعلمها إلا هو ويعلم ما في البر والبحر وما تسقط من ورقة إلا يعلمها ولا حبة في ظلمات الأرض ولا رطب ولا يابس إلا في كتاب مبين

translation: And it is He who takes your souls by night and knows what you have committed by day. Then He revives you therein that a specified term may be fulfilled. Then to Him will be your return; then He will inform you about what you used to do.
interpretation: This verse highlights Allah's power and knowledge over His creation. It reminds us that Allah is the one who takes our souls during sleep and is fully aware of all our deeds, both good and bad, during the day. He then resurrects us each morning to continue living until the appointed time of our death. The verse emphasizes that ultimately, we will all return to Allah and face the consequences of our actions in this world. It serves as a reminder for us to be mindful of our deeds and to strive for righteousness, knowing that we will be held accountable for everything we do.
orig: وهو الذي يتوفاكم بالليل ويعلم ما جرحتم بالنهار ثم يبعثكم فيه ليقضى أجل مسمى ثم إليه مرجعكم ثم ينبئكم بما كنتم تعملون

translation: And He is the subjugator over His servants. He sends over you guardian-angels until, when death comes to one of you, Our messengers take him, and they do not fail [in their duties].
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's absolute power and control over His creation. He has assigned guardian angels to watch over each individual, recording their deeds until the moment of death. When a person's time comes, Allah's messengers, the angels of death, take the soul without fail, demonstrating the inevitability of death and the precision with which Allah's will is carried out. This verse serves as a reminder for humans to be mindful of their actions, as nothing escapes Allah's knowledge and everything will be accounted for in the Hereafter.
orig: وهو القاهر فوق عباده ويرسل عليكم حفظة حتى إذا جاء أحدكم الموت توفته رسلنا وهم لا يفرطون

translation: Then they are returned to Allah, their true Lord. Unquestionably, His is the judgement, and He is the swiftest of accountants.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that ultimately, all beings will return to Allah, who is their true Master and Protector. It highlights Allah's absolute authority in passing judgment and His swift reckoning of deeds. The verse serves as a reminder for believers to be mindful of their actions, as they will be held accountable by Allah, who is the swiftest in settling accounts. It encourages individuals to lead righteous lives and to remember that their ultimate destination is back to their Creator, who will judge them based on their deeds in this world.
orig: ثم ردوا إلى الله مولاهم الحق ألا له الحكم وهو أسرع الحاسبين

translation: Say, "Who rescues you from the darknesses of the land and sea [when] you call upon Him imploring [aloud] and privately, 'If He should save us from this [crisis], we will surely be among the thankful.'"
interpretation: This verse highlights the innate human tendency to turn to God in times of hardship and danger, even if one is not ordinarily devout or mindful of God. It suggests that deep down, humans recognize God as the ultimate source of help and salvation. The verse also emphasizes the importance of gratitude - that if God rescues us from calamity, we should not forget Him afterwards but should remain thankful. It is a reminder to be consistently mindful of God, in good times and bad, and to express our gratitude for His blessings and mercy.
orig: قل من ينجيكم من ظلمات البر والبحر تدعونه تضرعا وخفية لئن أنجانا من هذه لنكونن من الشاكرين

translation: Say, "It is Allah who saves you from it and from every distress; then you [still] associate others with Him."
interpretation: This verse highlights the ingratitude of those who associate partners with Allah despite acknowledging that it is He who delivers them from hardships and calamities. It emphasizes that even after recognizing Allah's power to save them from distress, they still commit the grave sin of shirk (associating others with Allah in worship). This serves as a reminder for believers to be grateful to Allah alone and to avoid falling into the trap of polytheism, as it is a severe violation of the fundamental principle of Islam - the oneness of Allah (tawheed).
orig: قل الله ينجيكم منها ومن كل كرب ثم أنتم تشركون

translation: Say, "He is the [one] Able to send upon you affliction from above you or from beneath your feet or to confuse you [so you become] sects and make you taste the violence of one another." Look how We diversify the signs that they might understand.
interpretation: This verse is a reminder of Allah's power and control over all things. It emphasizes that Allah is capable of sending punishment or affliction upon people from any direction, whether it be from above or below. Additionally, it highlights the potential consequences of disunity and division among people, as Allah can cause them to split into factions and experience the violence and harm that comes from internal conflict. The verse also points to the importance of paying attention to the diverse signs and messages that Allah sends, as they serve as a means for people to understand and reflect upon His wisdom and authority.
orig: قل هو القادر على أن يبعث عليكم عذابا من فوقكم أو من تحت أرجلكم أو يلبسكم شيعا ويذيق بعضكم بأس بعض انظر كيف نصرف الآيات لعلهم يفقهون

translation: And your people have denied it, while it is the truth. Say, "I am not over you a manager."
interpretation: This verse is addressing the Prophet Muhammad, telling him that even though his people have rejected the message of Islam, it is still the ultimate truth. Allah is instructing the Prophet to declare that he is not a guardian or disposer of their affairs, meaning that he is not responsible for their actions and cannot force them to believe. It emphasizes the concept of free will in Islam, where individuals are accountable for their own choices and beliefs, and that the role of the Prophet is only to convey the message, not to impose it on others.
orig: وكذب به قومك وهو الحق قل لست عليكم بوكيل

translation: For every news there is a reality, and soon you will know.
interpretation: This verse reminds us that every piece of information or news has a reality behind it, and that the truth will eventually become clear. It is a warning against spreading or believing in false rumors or unverified information, and encourages seeking the truth. The verse also implies that those who spread false news will eventually face the consequences of their actions when the truth is revealed. It emphasizes the importance of patience, as the truth may not always be immediately apparent, but will come to light in due time.
orig: لكل نبإ مستقر وسوف تعلمون

translation: And when you see those who engage in [offensive] discourse concerning Our verses, then turn away from them until they enter into another conversation. And if Satan should cause you to forget, then do not remain after the reminder with the wrongdoing people.
interpretation: This verse instructs the believers on how to deal with those who mock or ridicule the verses of the Qur'an. It commands them to turn away and not engage with such people until they change the subject of their conversation. If a believer forgets this instruction and sits with those who are mocking the Qur'an, they should leave their company as soon as they remember, so as not to be counted among the wrongdoers. This verse emphasizes the importance of respecting the sanctity of the Qur'an and not allowing its verses to be ridiculed or belittled, even passively by one's presence in such gatherings.
orig: وإذا رأيت الذين يخوضون في آياتنا فأعرض عنهم حتى يخوضوا في حديث غيره وإما ينسينك الشيطان فلا تقعد بعد الذكرى مع القوم الظالمين

translation: And those who fear Allah are not accountable for them [i.e., the disbelievers] at all, but [only for] a reminder - that perhaps they will fear Him.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the righteous believers who are mindful of Allah and follow His guidance are not responsible for the actions and sins of the disbelievers. The role of the believers is to convey the message of Islam and remind others of the importance of righteousness and piety. However, it is ultimately up to each individual to choose whether to accept the reminder and adopt a God-conscious lifestyle. The believers should focus on their own spiritual growth and not be overly concerned with the choices of others, as everyone will be accountable for their own deeds on the Day of Judgment.
orig: وما على الذين يتقون من حسابهم من شيء ولكن ذكرى لعلهم يتقون

translation: And leave alone those who take their religion as play and amusement, and whom the worldly life has deceived. But remind with the Qur'an, lest a soul be given up to destruction for what it earned; it will have other than Allah no protector and no intercessor. And if it should offer every compensation, it would not be taken from it. Those are the ones who are given to destruction for what they have earned. For them will be a drink of scalding water and a painful punishment because they used to disbelieve.
interpretation: This verse is a warning to those who have taken their religion lightly, as a mere pastime or amusement, and have been deceived by the temporary pleasures of this worldly life. It urges the believers to remind such people with the Qur'an, lest they destroy themselves spiritually due to their misdeeds. It emphasizes that on the Day of Judgment, no soul will have any protector or intercessor besides Allah, and no compensation or ransom will be accepted from those who have earned their own destruction. As a consequence of their disbelief and heedlessness, they will face a severe punishment in the form of scalding drink and painful torment in the Hereafter.
orig: وذر الذين اتخذوا دينهم لعبا ولهوا وغرتهم الحياة الدنيا وذكر به أن تبسل نفس بما كسبت ليس لها من دون الله ولي ولا شفيع وإن تعدل كل عدل لا يؤخذ منها أولئك الذين أبسلوا بما كسبوا لهم شراب من حميم وعذاب أليم بما كانوا يكفرون

translation: Say, "Shall we invoke instead of Allah that which neither benefits us nor harms us and be turned back on our heels after Allah has guided us? [We would then be] like one whom the devils enticed [to wander] upon the earth confused, [while] he has companions inviting him to guidance, [calling], 'Come to us.'" Say, "Indeed, the guidance of Allah is the [only] guidance; and we have been commanded to submit to the Lord of the worlds."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of staying true to Allah's guidance and not reverting to the worship of false deities or idols that can neither benefit nor harm us. It compares the person who turns away from Allah's guidance to someone who is lost and confused, being tempted by the devils to stray from the right path, even though they have companions calling them back to the truth. The verse affirms that the only true guidance is that which comes from Allah and that we must submit ourselves completely to Him as the Lord of all the worlds.
orig: قل أندعو من دون الله ما لا ينفعنا ولا يضرنا ونرد على أعقابنا بعد إذ هدانا الله كالذي استهوته الشياطين في الأرض حيران له أصحاب يدعونه إلى الهدى ائتنا قل إن هدى الله هو الهدى وأمرنا لنسلم لرب العالمين

translation: And to establish prayer and fear Him. And it is He to whom you will be gathered.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of establishing regular prayer and having consciousness of Allah (taqwa). It reminds believers that ultimately, they will be gathered before Allah on the Day of Judgment to account for their deeds. The command to establish prayer and fear Allah is a central theme in the Qur'an, as prayer is a means of maintaining a connection with Allah and taqwa helps guide one's actions in life. The verse also underscores the inevitability of the afterlife and the accountability that each individual will face before Allah, encouraging believers to lead a righteous life in preparation for that ultimate gathering.
orig: وأن أقيموا الصلاة واتقوه وهو الذي إليه تحشرون

translation: And it is He who created the heavens and the earth in truth. And the Day He will say, "Be," and it is, His word is the truth. And His is the dominion [on] the Day the Horn is blown. [He is] Knower of the unseen and the witnessed; and He is the Wise, the Acquainted.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's power and sovereignty over all creation. He created the heavens and the earth with a divine purpose and ultimate truth. When the Day of Judgment arrives, Allah will command the resurrection to occur, and it will happen by His mere word. This highlights that His word is the absolute truth. The verse also affirms that on the Day of Judgment, when the Horn is blown to signal the resurrection, Allah alone will have dominion over all things. Furthermore, it underscores Allah's omniscience, as He has perfect knowledge of both the unseen realms and the witnessed world. The verse concludes by describing Allah as the Wise, indicating that His creation and judgment are based on divine wisdom, and the Acquainted, affirming His intimate knowledge of all things.
orig: وهو الذي خلق السماوات والأرض بالحق ويوم يقول كن فيكون قوله الحق وله الملك يوم ينفخ في الصور عالم الغيب والشهادة وهو الحكيم الخبير

translation: And [mention] when Abraham said to his father Azar, "Do you take idols as deities? Indeed, I see you and your people to be in clear error."
interpretation: In this verse, Abraham confronts his father Azar about his idolatrous practices. Abraham expresses his strong disapproval of worshipping idols instead of the One True God. He boldly states that he sees Azar and his people as being in manifest error by engaging in this practice. This verse highlights Abraham's unwavering monotheism and his willingness to stand up against the polytheistic beliefs of his family and community, even at a young age. It demonstrates his strong faith and commitment to guiding others towards the truth of worshipping Allah alone.
orig: وإذ قال إبراهيم لأبيه آزر أتتخذ أصناما آلهة إني أراك وقومك في ضلال مبين

translation: And thus We showed Abraham the realm of the heavens and the earth that he would be among the certain [in faith].
interpretation: This verse highlights how Allah granted Prophet Abraham a profound insight into the vastness and magnificence of His creation, encompassing both the heavens and the earth. By witnessing the marvels of the universe, Abraham's faith in the oneness and omnipotence of Allah was strengthened and solidified. This divine revelation served as a means to remove any lingering doubts and firmly establish Abraham as one of those who possess unwavering certainty in Allah's existence and supreme authority over all of creation. The verse emphasizes the importance of contemplating and reflecting upon the signs of Allah in the universe as a way to reinforce one's faith and attain a higher level of spiritual conviction.
orig: وكذلك نري إبراهيم ملكوت السماوات والأرض وليكون من الموقنين

translation: When the night covered him [with darkness], he saw a star. He said, "This is my lord." But when it set, he said, "I like not those that disappear."
interpretation: This verse is part of the story of Prophet Abraham's search for the true God. When he saw a star at night, he initially thought it might be his lord, but when it set and disappeared, he realized that anything that fades away cannot be the eternal, all-powerful God. This realization led him to reject the worship of celestial bodies and continue his quest for the one true God. The verse emphasizes the importance of critical thinking, logical reasoning, and the rejection of false deities in the pursuit of divine truth.
orig: فلما جن عليه الليل رأى كوكبا قال هذا ربي فلما أفل قال لا أحب الآفلين

translation: And when he saw the moon rising, he said, "This is my lord." But when it set, he said, "Unless my Lord guides me, I will surely be among the people gone astray."
interpretation: This verse is part of the story of Prophet Abraham's search for the true God. When he saw the moon rising, he initially thought it might be his lord due to its beauty and radiance. However, when the moon set, he realized that it could not be the true God, as God is eternal and does not set or change. This realization led him to understand that unless God guides him to the truth, he would be among those who are misguided and lost. The verse emphasizes the importance of seeking divine guidance to find the right path and avoid going astray.
orig: فلما رأى القمر بازغا قال هذا ربي فلما أفل قال لئن لم يهدني ربي لأكونن من القوم الضالين

translation: And when he saw the sun rising, he said, "This is my lord; this is greater." But when it set, he said, "O my people, indeed I am free from what you associate with Allah."
interpretation: This verse is part of the story of Prophet Ibrahim (Abraham) in the Qur'an. In his search for the true God, Ibrahim first considers the sun as his lord due to its apparent greatness and power. However, when the sun sets, he realizes that it cannot be the true God because it is subject to change and disappearance. This realization leads him to declare his disassociation from the false gods that his people worship and his devotion to the one true God, Allah. The verse highlights the importance of using reason and observation to arrive at the truth and reject false beliefs, even if they are widely accepted by society.
orig: فلما رأى الشمس بازغة قال هذا ربي هذا أكبر فلما أفلت قال يا قوم إني بريء مما تشركون

translation: Indeed, I have turned my face toward He who created the heavens and the earth, inclining toward truth, and I am not of those who associate others with Allah.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of pure monotheism and the rejection of polytheism or the association of partners with Allah. It highlights the act of turning one's face, which symbolizes the complete devotion and submission of one's entire being, towards the Creator of the heavens and the earth. The term "ḥanīf" denotes inclining towards the truth, emphasizing the innate human disposition towards monotheism. The verse also serves as a declaration of the speaker's disassociation from those who engage in shirk (polytheism) and a firm affirmation of their belief in the oneness of Allah.
orig: إني وجهت وجهي للذي فطر السماوات والأرض حنيفا وما أنا من المشركين

translation: And his people argued with him. He said, "Do you argue with me concerning Allah while He has guided me? And I fear not what you associate with Him [and will not be harmed] unless my Lord should will something. My Lord encompasses all things in knowledge; then will you not remember?
interpretation: This verse highlights the unwavering faith and trust in Allah that believers should have, even in the face of opposition and arguments from disbelievers. The prophet mentioned in this verse, likely Abraham, remains steadfast in his belief and is not afraid of the false gods that his people worship. He recognizes that Allah's knowledge and power encompass all things, and that nothing can harm him unless Allah wills it. The verse serves as a reminder for believers to put their trust in Allah's guidance and not be swayed by the arguments or threats of those who reject faith in Him.
orig: وحاجه قومه قال أتحاجوني في الله وقد هدان ولا أخاف ما تشركون به إلا أن يشاء ربي شيئا وسع ربي كل شيء علما أفلا تتذكرون

translation: And how should I fear what you associate while you do not fear that you have associated with Allah that for which He has not sent down to you any authority? So which of the two parties has more right to security, if you should know?
interpretation: This verse questions the logic of fearing false deities that the polytheists have associated with Allah without any authority or proof from Him. It emphasizes that it is Allah alone who deserves to be feared and worshipped. The believers who worship Allah alone have more right to feel secure and protected, as they are not committing the grave sin of associating partners with Him. The verse challenges the disbelievers to consider which group is more deserving of security - those who worship Allah alone or those who associate false gods with Him.
orig: وكيف أخاف ما أشركتم ولا تخافون أنكم أشركتم بالله ما لم ينزل به عليكم سلطانا فأي الفريقين أحق بالأمن إن كنتم تعلمون

translation: Those who have believed and have not obscured their faith with wrongdoing - for them is security, and they are [rightly] guided.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of sincere faith and righteous deeds. Those who believe in Allah and His messengers, and do not mix their faith with wrongdoing or injustice, will be granted security in this world and the hereafter. They will be guided to the straight path and will be protected from the punishment of Allah. The verse implies that true faith must be accompanied by good deeds and the avoidance of sin and oppression. It also suggests that those who commit wrongdoing, even if they claim to have faith, may not be considered among the truly faithful and may not receive the same security and guidance as those who combine sincere belief with righteous actions.
orig: الذين آمنوا ولم يلبسوا إيمانهم بظلم أولئك لهم الأمن وهم مهتدون

translation: And that was Our [conclusive] argument which We gave Abraham against his people. We raise by degrees whom We will. Indeed, your Lord is Wise and Knowing.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah bestowed upon Prophet Abraham (peace be upon him) convincing arguments and clear proofs to establish the truth of monotheism and refute the false beliefs of his people who worshipped idols. It also highlights Allah's wisdom in guiding and elevating the status of those He chooses, based on His infinite knowledge and wisdom. The verse serves as a reminder that the prophets were given divine knowledge and support to guide their nations, and that Allah's will and wisdom are supreme in determining the spiritual ranks of individuals.
orig: وتلك حجتنا آتيناها إبراهيم على قومه نرفع درجات من نشاء إن ربك حكيم عليم

translation: And We bestowed upon him Isaac and Jacob, and We guided each of them. And Noah, We guided before; and among his descendants, David and Solomon and Job and Joseph and Moses and Aaron. Thus do We reward the doers of good.
interpretation: This verse highlights the continuity of God's guidance and blessings upon His chosen prophets and their descendants. It emphasizes that God's favor is not limited to a single generation or lineage, but rather extends to those who follow the path of righteousness and do good deeds. The mention of various prophets from different times and places underscores the universality of God's message and the importance of following the guidance provided by His messengers. The verse also serves as a reminder that God rewards those who strive to do good and live according to His teachings, encouraging believers to emulate the examples set by these righteous individuals.
orig: ووهبنا له إسحاق ويعقوب كلا هدينا ونوحا هدينا من قبل ومن ذريته داوود وسليمان وأيوب ويوسف وموسى وهارون وكذلك نجزي المحسنين

translation: And Zechariah and John and Jesus and Elias; each one was of the righteous.
interpretation: This verse highlights the righteousness and virtue of four important prophets: Zechariah, John (Yahya), Jesus, and Elias (Ilyas). It emphasizes that they were all among the righteous servants of Allah, chosen for their devotion, piety, and steadfastness in conveying the divine message to their respective nations. Their inclusion together in this verse signifies the continuity of the prophetic tradition and the unity of the core message they delivered, which is the worship of the One true God and adherence to His commandments. The verse serves as a reminder for believers to emulate the qualities of these noble prophets in their own lives.
orig: وزكريا ويحيى وعيسى وإلياس كل من الصالحين

translation: And Ishmael and Elisha and Jonah and Lot, and all [of them] We preferred over the worlds.
interpretation: This verse highlights the special status and honor that Allah bestowed upon His chosen prophets, namely Ishmael, Elisha, Jonah, and Lot. By mentioning that He preferred them over the worlds, it emphasizes their elevated rank, righteousness, and the significance of their roles in conveying the divine message to humanity. This preference also serves as a reminder for believers to hold these prophets in high regard, follow their teachings, and strive to emulate their virtuous qualities in order to seek Allah's pleasure and attain success in this world and the hereafter.
orig: وإسماعيل واليسع ويونس ولوطا وكلا فضلنا على العالمين

translation: And [some] among their fathers and their descendants and their brothers - and We chose them and We guided them to a straight path.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah has chosen and guided certain individuals from among the ancestors, descendants, and siblings of the believers to the straight path of Islam. It highlights the concept of divine selection and guidance, indicating that Allah bestows His favor upon whom He wills, regardless of their familial connections. The "straight path" refers to the path of righteousness, submission to Allah, and adherence to His commandments. It is a reminder that being rightly guided is a blessing from Allah and that one should strive to stay on this path throughout their life.
orig: ومن آبائهم وذرياتهم وإخوانهم واجتبيناهم وهديناهم إلى صراط مستقيم

translation: That is the guidance of Allah by which He guides whomever He wills of His servants. But if they had associated others with Allah, then worthless for them would be whatever they were doing.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that guidance comes solely from Allah, and He bestows it upon whomever He chooses among His servants. It also warns that if people commit shirk (associating partners with Allah), all their good deeds and actions would become void and worthless. This highlights the importance of pure monotheism (tawheed) in Islam and that associating partners with Allah nullifies one's good deeds, rendering them meaningless in the sight of Allah.
orig: ذلك هدى الله يهدي به من يشاء من عباده ولو أشركوا لحبط عنهم ما كانوا يعملون

translation: Those to whom We have given the Book, Wisdom and Prophethood, even if these [people] disbelieve in it, We have certainly entrusted it to a people who are not ungrateful for it.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that even if some people reject the divine message after it has been conveyed to them through revelation, wisdom and prophethood, Allah has entrusted this message to another group of people who will appreciate it and remain grateful for this guidance. It shows that the truth and guidance of Allah's message is not dependent on any particular person or group accepting it - Allah will ensure that there will always be believers who cherish and uphold the divine revelation and its teachings.
orig: أولئك الذين آتيناهم الكتاب والحكم والنبوة فإن يكفر بها هؤلاء فقد وكلنا بها قوما ليسوا بها بكافرين

translation: Those are the ones whom Allah has guided, so from their guidance take an example. Say, "I do not ask you for this message any payment [but] it is not except a reminder for the worlds."
interpretation: This verse instructs Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and, by extension, all believers to follow the guidance of the righteous individuals whom Allah has guided, such as the prophets and messengers mentioned in the Qur'an. It emphasizes that the message of Islam is not a means for personal gain or worldly benefit, but rather a reminder and a guidance for all of humanity. The Prophet's role is to convey this message without expecting any reward from the people, as his ultimate reward lies with Allah. This highlights the sincerity and selflessness that should characterize the actions of those who call others to the path of Allah.
orig: أولئك الذين هدى الله فبهداهم اقتده قل لا أسألكم عليه أجرا إن هو إلا ذكرى للعالمين

translation: And they did not appraise Allah with true appraisal when they said, "Allah did not reveal to a human being anything." Say, "Who revealed the Scripture that Moses brought as light and guidance to the people? You [Jews] make it into pages, disclosing [some of] it and concealing much. And you were taught that which you knew not - neither you nor your fathers." Say, "Allah [revealed it]." Then leave them in their [empty] discourse, amusing themselves.
interpretation: This verse criticizes those who deny Allah's revelation to His prophets and messengers. It points out the inconsistency in the beliefs of those who accept the Torah revealed to Moses but reject the revelation to Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him). The verse emphasizes that it is Allah who reveals the scriptures and grants knowledge to mankind. It instructs the Prophet to affirm Allah's revelation and to leave those who engage in baseless discussions and reject the truth, as they are merely amusing themselves with falsehood.
orig: وما قدروا الله حق قدره إذ قالوا ما أنزل الله على بشر من شيء قل من أنزل الكتاب الذي جاء به موسى نورا وهدى للناس تجعلونه قراطيس تبدونها وتخفون كثيرا وعلمتم ما لم تعلموا أنتم ولا آباؤكم قل الله ثم ذرهم في خوضهم يلعبون

translation: And this is a Book which We have sent down, blessed and confirming what was before it, that you may warn the Mother of Cities and those around it. Those who believe in the Hereafter believe in it, and they are maintaining their prayers.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the divine nature of the Qur'an and its role in confirming the previous revelations. It also highlights the Prophet Muhammad's mission to warn the people of Mecca ("Mother of Cities") and its surroundings about the consequences of their actions and the importance of believing in the Hereafter. The verse suggests that true believers are those who have faith in the Qur'an and the Hereafter, and who are diligent in maintaining their prayers. This interpretation underscores the significance of the Qur'an as a guiding light for humanity and the centrality of faith and prayer in the life of a believer.
orig: وهذا كتاب أنزلناه مبارك مصدق الذي بين يديه ولتنذر أم القرى ومن حولها والذين يؤمنون بالآخرة يؤمنون به وهم على صلاتهم يحافظون

translation: And who is more unjust than one who invents a lie about Allah or says, "It has been inspired to me," while nothing has been inspired to him, and one who says, "I will reveal [something] like what Allah revealed." And if you could but see when the wrongdoers are in the overwhelming pangs of death while the angels extend their hands, [saying], "Discharge your souls! Today you will be awarded the punishment of [extreme] humiliation for what you used to say against Allah other than the truth and [that] you were, toward His verses, being arrogant."
interpretation: This verse condemns those who invent lies about Allah, falsely claim divine inspiration, or arrogantly assert that they can reveal something similar to what Allah has revealed. It depicts the terrible fate that awaits such wrongdoers in the throes of death, when the angels will demand that they surrender their souls and face the consequences of their actions. The punishment for their arrogance and false claims against Allah will be extreme humiliation on the Day of Judgment. This verse serves as a severe warning against attributing falsehood to Allah or belittling His revelations, emphasizing the gravity of such sins and the severe retribution that awaits those who commit them.
orig: ومن أظلم ممن افترى على الله كذبا أو قال أوحي إلي ولم يوح إليه شيء ومن قال سأنزل مثل ما أنزل الله ولو ترى إذ الظالمون في غمرات الموت والملائكة باسطو أيديهم أخرجوا أنفسكم اليوم تجزون عذاب الهون بما كنتم تقولون على الله غير الحق وكنتم عن آياته تستكبرون

translation: And you have come to Us alone as We created you the first time, and you have left whatever We bestowed upon you behind your backs. And We do not see with you your intercessors whom you claimed that they were partners with Allah in your affairs. Now all relations between you have been cut off, and lost from you is what you used to claim.
interpretation: This verse is referring to the Day of Judgment, when all individuals will stand alone before Allah, without any worldly possessions or claimed intercessors. It emphasizes that the relationships, material goods, and false beliefs that one held in the worldly life will be of no benefit on that day. The individual will be held accountable solely for their own deeds and faith. This serves as a reminder to focus on one's relationship with Allah and to live righteously, rather than being distracted by temporary worldly attachments or misguided beliefs.
orig: ولقد جئتمونا فرادى كما خلقناكم أول مرة وتركتم ما خولناكم وراء ظهوركم وما نرى معكم شفعاءكم الذين زعمتم أنهم فيكم شركاء لقد تقطع بينكم وضل عنكم ما كنتم تزعمون

translation: Indeed, Allah is the cleaver of grain and date seeds. He brings the living out of the dead and brings the dead out of the living. That is Allah; so how are you deluded?
interpretation: This verse highlights Allah's power and control over life and death. It emphasizes that Allah is the one who initiates and sustains all life, and has the ability to bring forth the living from the dead and the dead from the living. The metaphor of cleaving the grain and date seeds illustrates Allah's ability to create and originate life. The verse ends with a rhetorical question, challenging those who are "deluded" and turn away from the truth of Allah's power and existence, despite the clear signs and evidence in the natural world around them.
orig: إن الله فالق الحب والنوى يخرج الحي من الميت ومخرج الميت من الحي ذلكم الله فأنى تؤفكون

translation: He is the Cleaver of the daybreak and has made the night for rest and the sun and the moon for calculation. That is the determination of the Exalted in Might, the Knowing.
interpretation: This verse points to Allah's power and wisdom in creating and regulating the universe. He causes the daybreak to emerge, providing light and starting a new day. He has ordained the night as a time for rest and tranquility, allowing humans and creatures to rejuvenate. The sun and moon move in precisely calculated orbits, which is a sign of Allah's magnificent design and knowledge. The regular cycles of day and night, and the predictable patterns of the sun and moon, demonstrate that this universe has been meticulously arranged by the Almighty, the All-Knowing Creator. It encourages humans to reflect on these signs and appreciate the perfection behind Allah's creation.
orig: فالق الإصباح وجعل الليل سكنا والشمس والقمر حسبانا ذلك تقدير العزيز العليم

translation: And it is He who placed for you the stars that you may be guided by them through the darknesses of the land and sea. We have detailed the signs for a people who know.
interpretation: This verse highlights Allah's guidance and mercy towards mankind. He has created the stars as a means of navigation, especially in the darkness of the night, whether on land or at sea. The stars serve as a natural compass, helping people find their way and reach their destinations safely. This is a sign of Allah's wisdom and care for His creation. The verse also emphasizes that Allah has explained His signs in detail for those who seek knowledge and understanding. It invites people to reflect upon the wonders of the universe and recognize the power and benevolence of the Creator.
orig: وهو الذي جعل لكم النجوم لتهتدوا بها في ظلمات البر والبحر قد فصلنا الآيات لقوم يعلمون

translation: And it is He who has produced you from one soul and [gave you] a place of dwelling and of storage. We have detailed the signs for a people who understand.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the unity of humanity, as all humans originate from a single soul, referring to Adam. It also alludes to the different stages of human life, with "a place of dwelling" representing the womb where the fetus develops, and "a place of storage" signifying the grave after death. The verse suggests that God has provided clear signs and evidence of His creation and power, which can be understood by those who reflect deeply and seek to comprehend the truth.
orig: وهو الذي أنشأكم من نفس واحدة فمستقر ومستودع قد فصلنا الآيات لقوم يفقهون

translation: It is He who sends down rain from the sky; from it is drink and from it is foliage in which you pasture [animals]. He causes to grow for you thereby the crops, olives, palm trees, grapevines, and from all the fruits. Indeed in that is a sign for a people who give thought.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the power and benevolence of Allah in providing sustenance for His creation. The rain that falls from the sky is a vital source of life, enabling the growth of vegetation which serves as food for both humans and animals. The diversity of crops, fruits, and plants mentioned in the verse, such as olives, palm trees, grapevines, and others, showcases the abundance and variety of Allah's provisions. This is presented as a sign for those who reflect and ponder upon the wonders of creation, leading them to acknowledge and appreciate the existence and generosity of the Creator. The verse encourages people to observe and contemplate the natural world around them, as it serves as a testament to Allah's power, wisdom, and mercy.
orig: وهو الذي أنزل من السماء ماء فأخرجنا به نبات كل شيء فأخرجنا منه خضرا نخرج منه حبا متراكبا ومن النخل من طلعها قنوان دانية وجنات من أعناب والزيتون والرمان مشتبها وغير متشابه انظروا إلى ثمره إذا أثمر وينعه إن في ذلكم لآيات لقوم يؤمنون

translation: And they have made the jinn partners with Allah, though He created them. And they falsely attribute to Him sons and daughters without knowledge. Exalted is He and high above what they describe.
interpretation: This verse is criticizing the polytheistic beliefs of those who associate partners with Allah, such as the jinn, and those who falsely attribute offspring to Him. The interpretation is that Allah is far above and exalted beyond such false descriptions and associations. He alone is the Creator of all things, including the jinn, and He does not have any offspring or partners. Attributing such things to Allah without knowledge is a grave error and goes against the fundamental Islamic belief in His Oneness and Uniqueness.
orig: وجعلوا لله شركاء الجن وخلقهم وخرقوا له بنين وبنات بغير علم سبحانه وتعالى عما يصفون

translation: He is the Originator of the heavens and the earth. How could He have a son when He does not have a companion and He created all things? And He is, of all things, Knowing.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the fundamental Islamic belief in the oneness and uniqueness of Allah. It asserts that Allah is the sole creator and originator of the entire universe, including the heavens and the earth. The rhetorical question "How could He have a son when He does not have a companion" refutes the notion held by some religions that God has a son or offspring. In Islam, attributing a son to Allah is considered a form of shirk (associating partners with Allah). The verse also highlights Allah's omniscience, stating that He has complete knowledge of all things, as He is the one who created everything. This interpretation underscores the Islamic principles of tawheed (monotheism) and Allah's divine attributes of being the Creator and All-Knowing.
orig: بديع السماوات والأرض أنى يكون له ولد ولم تكن له صاحبة وخلق كل شيء وهو بكل شيء عليم

translation: That is Allah, your Lord; there is no deity except Him, the Creator of all things, so worship Him. And He is Disposer of all things.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the oneness and uniqueness of Allah as the sole Creator and Sustainer of all things in existence. It calls upon humanity to direct their worship and devotion exclusively to Him, as He alone is worthy of it. The verse also highlights Allah's complete control and authority over all affairs, affirming that He is the ultimate Disposer and Manager of everything in the universe. This interpretation underscores the fundamental Islamic belief in the unity of God (tawheed) and the necessity of submitting to His will and guidance in all aspects of life.
orig: ذلكم الله ربكم لا إله إلا هو خالق كل شيء فاعبدوه وهو على كل شيء وكيل

translation: Vision perceives Him not, but He perceives [all] vision; and He is the Subtle, the Acquainted.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the transcendence and omniscience of Allah. Human perception and understanding are limited, and we cannot fully comprehend or visualize Allah. However, Allah is all-seeing and all-knowing, aware of everything that happens in the universe. He is subtle in His actions and dispositions, yet He is fully acquainted with all things, even the most minute details of His creation. The verse highlights the importance of recognizing the limitations of human understanding and submitting to the infinite wisdom and knowledge of Allah.
orig: لا تدركه الأبصار وهو يدرك الأبصار وهو اللطيف الخبير

translation: There has come to you enlightenment from your Lord. So whoever will see does so for [the benefit of] his soul, and whoever is blind [does harm] against it. And [say], "I am not a guardian over you."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the individual responsibility of each person in accepting or rejecting the truth that has been revealed by Allah. The "enlightenment" refers to the clear signs and guidance that have come through the Quran and the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him). It is up to each individual to either open their heart to this guidance and benefit their own soul, or turn away from it and suffer the consequences of remaining in spiritual blindness. The Prophet is reminded that he is not a "guardian" over the people in the sense of forcing them to believe or being held accountable for their choices and actions. Rather, his duty is to convey the message, while the ultimate fate of each soul rests with Allah and the consequences of their own decisions.
orig: قد جاءكم بصائر من ربكم فمن أبصر فلنفسه ومن عمي فعليها وما أنا عليكم بحفيظ

translation: And thus We diversify the verses so that they [i.e., the disbelievers] will say, "You have studied," and so We may make it [i.e., the Qur'an] clear for a people who know.
interpretation: This verse indicates that Allah reveals the Qur'an in various ways and with different examples and parables so that the disbelievers may accuse the Prophet (ﷺ) of having learned it from someone else. However, the true purpose of this diversification is to make the message of the Qur'an clear and understandable for those who have knowledge and are willing to learn and reflect upon its teachings. It emphasizes that the Qur'an is not a product of human learning, but a divine revelation meant to guide those who sincerely seek guidance.
orig: وكذلك نصرف الآيات وليقولوا درست ولنبينه لقوم يعلمون

translation: Follow what has been revealed to you from your Lord; there is no deity except Him. And turn away from the polytheists.
interpretation: This verse instructs the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) to remain steadfast in following the divine revelation from Allah, emphasizing the core Islamic belief in the oneness of God (tawheed). It also directs the Prophet to disregard and turn away from the polytheists who associate partners with Allah, as their beliefs and practices are contrary to the fundamental teachings of Islam. The verse serves as a reminder for the Prophet and the believers to remain committed to the path of monotheism and not be swayed by the misguided beliefs of those who ascribe partners to Allah.
orig: اتبع ما أوحي إليك من ربك لا إله إلا هو وأعرض عن المشركين

translation: And if Allah had willed, they would not have associated. And We have not appointed you over them as a guardian, nor are you a manager over them.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the concept of free will in Islam. Although Allah is all-powerful and could have prevented people from committing shirk (associating partners with Him), He chose to grant humans the freedom to believe or disbelieve. The role of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) is also clarified - he is not responsible for forcing people to believe or for controlling their actions. His duty is only to convey the message of Islam, while the ultimate fate of individuals depends on their own choices and Allah's judgment. This highlights the importance of personal responsibility and the absence of compulsion in matters of faith.
