orig: ولو شاء الله ما أشركوا وما جعلناك عليهم حفيظا وما أنت عليهم بوكيل

translation: And do not insult those they invoke other than Allah, lest they insult Allah in enmity without knowledge. Thus We have made pleasing to every community their deeds. Then to their Lord is their return, and He will inform them about what they used to do.
interpretation: This verse instructs Muslims not to verbally abuse or insult the false gods or idols worshipped by the polytheists, because this would cause them to retaliate and speak ill of Allah out of ignorance and enmity. It emphasizes that Allah has made the deeds and beliefs of each community seem fair and attractive to them. However, everyone will ultimately return to their Lord, who will inform them about the truth regarding their actions and hold them accountable accordingly. The verse promotes wisdom, respect, and avoiding unnecessary provocation in dealing with those who hold different beliefs.
orig: ولا تسبوا الذين يدعون من دون الله فيسبوا الله عدوا بغير علم كذلك زينا لكل أمة عملهم ثم إلى ربهم مرجعهم فينبئهم بما كانوا يعملون

translation: And they swear by Allah their strongest oaths that if a sign came to them, they would surely believe in it. Say, "The signs are only with Allah." And what will make you perceive that even if a sign came, they would not believe?
interpretation: This verse highlights the stubbornness and disbelief of those who oppose the message of Islam. Despite their claims that they would believe if they were given a miraculous sign, Allah knows that even if such a sign were provided, they would likely continue in their disbelief. It emphasizes that true faith is not dependent on witnessing miracles, but rather on sincerity and openness of the heart to Allah's guidance. The verse also serves as a reminder to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and the believers not to be discouraged by the opposition they face, as the ultimate judgment and authority belong to Allah alone.
orig: وأقسموا بالله جهد أيمانهم لئن جاءتهم آية ليؤمنن بها قل إنما الآيات عند الله وما يشعركم أنها إذا جاءت لا يؤمنون

translation: And We will turn their hearts and their eyes away [from guidance], as they refused to believe in it the first time, and We will leave them in their transgression, wandering blindly.
interpretation: This verse speaks about those who have persistently rejected the truth and refused to believe in the message of Islam, despite clear signs and warnings. As a consequence of their stubborn disbelief, Allah will seal their hearts and eyes, leaving them to wander astray in their transgression and defiance. They will be deprived of the ability to see the truth or to be guided to the right path. This is a severe punishment for those who consciously choose to reject faith and remain in a state of rebellion against Allah. It serves as a warning to all people to open their hearts to the message of Islam and to embrace faith before it is too late, as there may come a time when Allah leaves the disbelievers in their misguidance as a result of their own choices.
orig: ونقلب أفئدتهم وأبصارهم كما لم يؤمنوا به أول مرة ونذرهم في طغيانهم يعمهون

translation: And even if We had sent down to them the angels [with the message] and the dead spoke to them [of it] and We gathered together every [created] thing in front of them, they would not believe unless Allah should will. But most of them, [of that], are ignorant.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the stubbornness and ignorance of those who reject faith in Allah. It suggests that even if they were presented with overwhelming evidence, such as angels descending from the heavens, the dead speaking to them, and all of creation gathered before them as proof, they would still not believe unless Allah willed it. The verse implies that their disbelief is not due to a lack of evidence but rather stems from their own ignorance and obstinacy. It highlights the fact that faith is ultimately a matter of divine will and guidance, and that no amount of external proof can force someone to believe if their heart is not open to it.
orig: ولو أننا نزلنا إليهم الملائكة وكلمهم الموتى وحشرنا عليهم كل شيء قبلا ما كانوا ليؤمنوا إلا أن يشاء الله ولكن أكثرهم يجهلون

translation: And thus We have made for every prophet an enemy - devils from mankind and jinn, inspiring to one another decorative speech in delusion. But if your Lord had willed, they would not have done it, so leave them and that which they invent.
interpretation: This verse highlights the universal struggle between good and evil, and how the forces of evil, both among humans and jinn, work to deceive and lead people astray through alluring words and false promises. However, it also emphasizes that this happens only by God's will, and that ultimately, people have the choice to either be misled or to turn away from falsehood. The verse serves as a reminder to be cautious of those who speak with deceptive eloquence and to put one's trust in God's guidance rather than falling for the deceptions of the devil's allies.
orig: وكذلك جعلنا لكل نبي عدوا شياطين الإنس والجن يوحي بعضهم إلى بعض زخرف القول غرورا ولو شاء ربك ما فعلوه فذرهم وما يفترون

translation: And let the hearts of those who do not believe in the Hereafter incline to it, and let them be pleased with it, and let them commit what they are committing.
interpretation: This verse suggests that those who do not believe in the Hereafter are more easily swayed by worldly pleasures and desires. Their hearts are inclined towards the temporary attractions of this life, leading them to be pleased with and pursue those things, even if it means committing sins or acts that are ultimately harmful. It highlights the contrast between believers who are mindful of the consequences in the afterlife and those who are only focused on immediate gratification in this world.
orig: ولتصغى إليه أفئدة الذين لا يؤمنون بالآخرة وليرضوه وليقترفوا ما هم مقترفون

translation: "Shall I seek other than Allah as judge while it is He who has revealed to you the Book explained in detail?" Those to whom We [previously] gave the Scripture know that it is sent down from your Lord in truth, so never be among the doubters.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah is the ultimate judge and lawgiver. It questions the believer, asking why they would seek judgment from anyone other than Allah when He has revealed the Qur'an, which provides detailed guidance. The verse also serves as a reminder to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and the believers that the people who received earlier scriptures, such as the Jews and Christians, recognize that the Qur'an is revealed by Allah in truth. Therefore, the believers should have no doubt about the divine origin and authority of the Qur'an and should submit to Allah's judgment alone.
orig: أفغير الله أبتغي حكما وهو الذي أنزل إليكم الكتاب مفصلا والذين آتيناهم الكتاب يعلمون أنه منزل من ربك بالحق فلا تكونن من الممترين

translation: The word of your Lord has been fulfilled in truth and justice. None can change His words, and He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the immutability and perfection of Allah's words and decrees. His promises and judgments are always true, just, and unchangeable. No one can alter or override what He has ordained. The verse also highlights two of Allah's attributes: He is the All-Hearing, meaning He hears all supplications and utterances, and the All-Knowing, meaning He has complete knowledge of everything, including the intentions behind people's actions and words. This verse serves as a reminder for believers to trust in Allah's wisdom, submit to His will, and find comfort in the fact that His words and decrees are perfect and unchangeable.
orig: وتمت كلمت ربك صدقا وعدلا لا مبدل لكلماته وهو السميع العليم

translation: And if you obey most of those on earth, they will mislead you far away from Allah's Path. They follow nothing but conjectures, and they do nothing but lie.
interpretation: This verse warns against blindly following the majority of people, as they may lead one astray from the righteous path of Allah. It emphasizes that most people rely on mere speculation and guesswork rather than divine guidance. The verse implies that true believers should not be swayed by popular opinion but should instead adhere to the teachings of Allah and His messenger, even if it means going against the majority. It highlights the importance of using one's intellect and discernment to distinguish between truth and falsehood, rather than simply conforming to the crowd.
orig: وإن تطع أكثر من في الأرض يضلوك عن سبيل الله إن يتبعون إلا الظن وإن هم إلا يخرصون

translation: Indeed, your Lord is most knowing of who has gone astray from His way, and He is most knowing of the [rightly] guided.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's omniscience and His perfect knowledge of the spiritual state of every individual. He alone knows who has strayed from the straight path and who is rightly guided. It serves as a reminder that we cannot judge others based on outward appearances, as only Allah truly knows what is in people's hearts. The verse also implies that guidance comes from Allah alone, and that we should turn to Him for direction and support in staying on the right path. Ultimately, it is a call to humility and recognition of our own limitations in contrast to Allah's all-encompassing knowledge.
orig: إن ربك هو أعلم من يضل عن سبيله وهو أعلم بالمهتدين

translation: So eat of that [meat] upon which the name of Allah has been mentioned, if you are believers in His verses.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of consuming only what is permissible according to Islamic law. It instructs believers to eat the meat of animals that have been slaughtered in the name of Allah, as a sign of their faith and obedience to His commandments. This practice serves as a reminder to be mindful of Allah's blessings and to express gratitude for the sustenance He provides. By following this guidance, believers demonstrate their submission to Allah and their adherence to the principles laid out in the Qur'an.
orig: فكلوا مما ذكر اسم الله عليه إن كنتم بآياته مؤمنين

translation: And why should you not eat of that upon which the name of Allah has been mentioned while He has explained in detail to you what He has forbidden you, excepting that to which you are compelled. And indeed do many lead [others] astray through their [own] inclinations without knowledge. Indeed, your Lord - He is most knowing of the transgressors.
interpretation: This verse is emphasizing the permissibility of eating meat that has been slaughtered in the name of Allah, as long as it is not from the categories that Allah has clearly forbidden, such as carrion or animals dedicated to other than Allah. The verse also acknowledges that many people are misled by their desires and ignorance into forbidding what Allah has made lawful. It affirms that Allah alone knows best who the true transgressors are - those who violate His laws and prohibitions out of willful disobedience, not those who follow His guidance regarding what is permissible to consume.
orig: وما لكم ألا تأكلوا مما ذكر اسم الله عليه وقد فصل لكم ما حرم عليكم إلا ما اضطررتم إليه وإن كثيرا ليضلون بأهوائهم بغير علم إن ربك هو أعلم بالمعتدين

translation: And leave what is apparent of sin and what is concealed thereof. Indeed, those who earn [blame for] sin will be recompensed for that which they used to commit.
interpretation: This verse is a strong warning and reminder for us to avoid all forms of sin, whether they are committed openly or secretly. It emphasizes that no sin is hidden from Allah, and that those who engage in sinful acts will face the consequences of their deeds in the Hereafter. The message is clear - as believers, we must strive to purify ourselves both externally and internally, guarding against sins in our actions as well as in our hearts. By heeding this warning and living righteously, we can hope to earn Allah's pleasure and be saved from the punishment that awaits the sinful.
orig: وذروا ظاهر الإثم وباطنه إن الذين يكسبون الإثم سيجزون بما كانوا يقترفون

translation: And do not eat of that upon which the name of Allah has not been mentioned, for indeed, it is grave disobedience. And indeed do the devils inspire their allies [among men] to dispute with you. And if you were to obey them, indeed, you would be associators [of others with Him].
interpretation: This verse warns against consuming food over which Allah's name has not been pronounced, deeming it an act of disobedience. It also cautions that the devils whisper to their human allies, encouraging them to argue with the believers about such matters. Obeying these devilish incitements and engaging in the prohibited practices would amount to associating partners with Allah (shirk), which is among the gravest of sins in Islam. The verse emphasizes the importance of adhering to divine guidelines and resisting the temptations and arguments posed by those who oppose the truth.
orig: ولا تأكلوا مما لم يذكر اسم الله عليه وإنه لفسق وإن الشياطين ليوحون إلى أوليائهم ليجادلوكم وإن أطعتموهم إنكم لمشركون

translation: And is one who was dead and We gave him life and made for him light by which to walk among the people like one who is in darkness, never to emerge therefrom? Thus it has been made pleasing to the disbelievers that which they were doing.
interpretation: This verse draws a powerful comparison between the believer and the disbeliever. The believer, who was once spiritually dead, has been given new life and guidance by Allah, allowing them to walk through life with clarity and purpose. In contrast, the disbeliever remains in a state of darkness, unable to find their way or see the truth. The verse suggests that the disbelievers are content with their state because their misdeeds and false beliefs have been made attractive to them. It highlights the stark difference between the enlightenment of faith and the blindness of disbelief, and serves as a reminder of the importance of seeking guidance from Allah.
orig: أومن كان ميتا فأحييناه وجعلنا له نورا يمشي به في الناس كمن مثله في الظلمات ليس بخارج منها كذلك زين للكافرين ما كانوا يعملون

translation: And thus We have made in every city the greatest of its criminals to conspire therein. But they conspire not except against themselves, and they perceive [it] not.
interpretation: This verse suggests that in every society, there are influential wrongdoers who plot and scheme, ultimately bringing about their own downfall. They are oblivious to the fact that their evil plans will backfire on them. It is a divine principle that the consequences of one's actions will eventually catch up with them, even if they are unaware of it. The verse implies that the corrupt elite may hold power and influence, but their own misdeeds will lead to their undoing, often in ways they cannot foresee. It serves as a warning against engaging in sinful behavior and a reminder of the inescapable justice of God.
orig: وكذلك جعلنا في كل قرية أكابر مجرميها ليمكروا فيها وما يمكرون إلا بأنفسهم وما يشعرون

translation: And when a sign comes to them, they say, "We will not believe until we are given like that which was given to the messengers of Allah." Allah is most knowing of where He places His message. There will afflict those who committed crimes debasement before Allah and severe punishment for what they used to conspire.
interpretation: This verse is criticizing the attitude of those who reject the signs and messages brought by the Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him. They arrogantly demand to receive direct revelation like the prophets did, instead of accepting the truth of Muhammad's prophethood. Allah rebukes them, affirming that He alone chooses whom to entrust with His message. As a consequence for their criminal disbelief and scheming against the Prophet, they will be humiliated before Allah and will face a severe punishment in the Hereafter. The verse warns against the sin of arrogantly rejecting Allah's signs and messengers.
orig: وإذا جاءتهم آية قالوا لن نؤمن حتى نؤتى مثل ما أوتي رسل الله الله أعلم حيث يجعل رسالته سيصيب الذين أجرموا صغار عند الله وعذاب شديد بما كانوا يمكرون

translation: So whoever Allah wants to guide - He expands his breast to [contain] Islam; and whoever He wants to misguide - He makes his breast tight and constricted as though he were climbing into the sky. Thus does Allah place defilement upon those who do not believe.
interpretation: This verse highlights the concept of divine guidance and misguidance in Islam. It suggests that those whom Allah chooses to guide will find their hearts and minds open and receptive to the teachings of Islam, while those whom He leaves to stray will find the path of faith difficult and constricting, as if they were struggling to climb an impossible height. The metaphor of a constricted chest symbolizes the spiritual and psychological state of those who reject faith, while an expanded breast represents the ease and contentment found by those who embrace Islam. Ultimately, the verse affirms that it is Allah who places these spiritual conditions upon people in accordance with His divine will and wisdom.
orig: فمن يرد الله أن يهديه يشرح صدره للإسلام ومن يرد أن يضله يجعل صدره ضيقا حرجا كأنما يصعد في السماء كذلك يجعل الله الرجس على الذين لا يؤمنون

translation: And this is the Path of your Lord, straight. We have detailed the verses for a people who remember.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the path laid out by Allah is the straight and correct one. The Qur'an provides clear guidance and detailed explanations of its verses for those who are mindful of Allah and reflect upon His signs. It suggests that by following the Qur'anic teachings and remembering Allah's guidance, one can stay on the right path that leads to His pleasure and to success in this life and the Hereafter. The verse also implies that the Qur'an is not meant for those who are heedless and do not ponder over its meanings.
orig: وهذا صراط ربك مستقيما قد فصلنا الآيات لقوم يذكرون

translation: For them will be the Home of Peace with their Lord, and He will be their protecting Friend because of what they used to do.
interpretation: This verse speaks about the ultimate reward for the righteous believers in the Hereafter. "The Home of Peace" refers to Paradise, where they will find everlasting peace, tranquility, and security. This reward is granted to them by their Lord as a result of their good deeds and righteous actions in this worldly life. Allah, their Lord, will be their protecting Friend, guiding and supporting them in Paradise, just as He did in the world. This emphasizes the importance of doing good deeds consistently throughout one's life, as it is the key to attaining this blessed state in the Hereafter under the care and protection of Allah.
orig: لهم دار السلام عند ربهم وهو وليهم بما كانوا يعملون

translation: And [mention] the Day when He will gather them together [and say], "O company of jinn, you have [misled] many of mankind." And their allies among mankind will say, "Our Lord, some of us made use of others, and we have [now] reached our term, which you appointed for us." He will say, "The Fire is your residence, wherein you will abide eternally, except for what Allah wills. Indeed, your Lord is Wise and Knowing."
interpretation: This verse highlights the accountability and consequences on the Day of Judgment for both the jinn and humans who misled others. The jinn are addressed, emphasizing their role in misguiding many humans. The humans who followed them will acknowledge that they benefited from each other in worldly life, but now face the repercussions of their actions. Allah declares that their abode will be the Fire, where they will remain eternally, subject to His will. This interpretation underscores the gravity of leading others astray and the importance of taking responsibility for one's actions, as everyone will face the ultimate justice on the Day of Reckoning according to Allah's wisdom and knowledge.
orig: ويوم يحشرهم جميعا يا معشر الجن قد استكثرتم من الإنس وقال أولياؤهم من الإنس ربنا استمتع بعضنا ببعض وبلغنا أجلنا الذي أجلت لنا قال النار مثواكم خالدين فيها إلا ما شاء الله إن ربك حكيم عليم

translation: And thus do We make some of the wrongdoers allies of others for what they used to earn.
interpretation: This verse points to the fact that Allah allows the wrongdoers and oppressors to become allies and supporters of one another due to their evil actions and the sins they commit. It is a form of punishment from Allah, as their alliance in wrongdoing will only lead them further astray and increase their burden of sin. This also serves as a test and a trial for the believers, who must remain steadfast in the face of the apparent strength of the wrongdoers' alliances. Ultimately, the wrongdoers' mutual support will not avail them anything before Allah's judgment, and they will face the consequences of their deeds.
orig: وكذلك نولي بعض الظالمين بعضا بما كانوا يكسبون

translation: O company of jinn and men! Did there not come to you messengers from among you, relating to you My verses and warning you of the meeting of this Day of yours? They will say, "We bear witness against ourselves"; and the worldly life had deluded them, and they will bear witness against themselves that they were disbelievers.
interpretation: This verse is a reminder from Allah to both jinn and humans that He sent messengers to them from among their own kind, to convey His message and warn them about the Day of Judgment. On that day, they will admit that they received the message but were deluded by the attractions of worldly life, and will testify against themselves that they knowingly rejected the truth and were disbelievers. This highlights the importance of heeding the message brought by the prophets and not being distracted by temporary worldly pleasures at the expense of one's eternal fate.
orig: يا معشر الجن والإنس ألم يأتكم رسل منكم يقصون عليكم آياتي وينذرونكم لقاء يومكم هذا قالوا شهدنا على أنفسنا وغرتهم الحياة الدنيا وشهدوا على أنفسهم أنهم كانوا كافرين

translation: That is because your Lord would not destroy the cities for wrongdoing while their people were unaware.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's justice and mercy. He does not punish people for their wrongdoings without first sending them warnings and giving them a chance to repent. Allah does not destroy communities unjustly while they are unaware of their mistakes. Rather, He sends messengers and signs to remind them, so they have no excuse. This highlights Allah's perfect justice - He only punishes those who knowingly persist in wrongdoing after being warned, not those who are ignorant or unaware.
orig: ذلك أن لم يكن ربك مهلك القرى بظلم وأهلها غافلون

translation: And for all there are degrees [of reward and punishment] for what they have done, and your Lord is not unaware of what they do.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the concept of divine justice in Islam. It suggests that every individual will be held accountable for their deeds and will be rewarded or punished accordingly in the afterlife. The varying degrees of reward and punishment indicate that the judgment will be proportionate to one's actions. Moreover, the verse affirms that God is fully aware of all that people do, implying that nothing escapes His knowledge and that the ultimate judgment will be based on perfect and complete information. This interpretation highlights the importance of individual responsibility and the belief in the inevitability of divine justice in Islamic thought.
orig: ولكل درجات مما عملوا وما ربك بغافل عما يعملون

translation: And your Lord is the Free of need, the possessor of mercy. If He wills, He can do away with you and give succession after you to whomever He wills, just as He produced you from the descendants of another people.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's absolute sovereignty and independence. He is not in need of His creation, and His mercy is vast. If He so wills, He has the power to replace humanity with others, just as He created the present generation from the descendants of previous nations. This serves as a reminder for humankind to be humble and recognize their dependence on Allah's mercy and will, and to strive to be obedient and grateful servants.
orig: وربك الغني ذو الرحمة إن يشأ يذهبكم ويستخلف من بعدكم ما يشاء كما أنشأكم من ذرية قوم آخرين

translation: Indeed, what you are promised is coming, and you will not cause failure [to Allah].
interpretation: This verse is a reminder and warning to humanity that the Day of Judgment, as promised by Allah, is inevitable and will surely come to pass. No one can escape or prevent it from happening, regardless of their power or status in this world. It emphasizes the absolute authority and power of Allah over His creation and the certainty of His promise. The verse also implies that those who deny or disbelieve in the Day of Judgment will face the consequences of their actions and will not be able to escape Allah's justice.
orig: إن ما توعدون لآت وما أنتم بمعجزين

translation: Say, "O my people, work according to your position; [for] indeed, I am working. And you are going to know who will have succession in the home. Indeed, the wrongdoers will not succeed."
interpretation: This verse is a reminder that everyone will be judged according to their deeds and actions in this world. The Prophet is instructed to tell his people to do whatever they want, while he will continue to do what he believes is right. Ultimately, it is those who follow the righteous path and refrain from wrongdoing who will be successful in the Hereafter, inheriting Paradise. The wrongdoers and oppressors, on the other hand, will not attain salvation or success, despite their worldly power or influence. It emphasizes the importance of staying true to one's faith and principles, regardless of the opposition or challenges faced.
orig: قل يا قوم اعملوا على مكانتكم إني عامل فسوف تعلمون من تكون له عاقبة الدار إنه لا يفلح الظالمون

translation: And they assign to Allah a share of the crops and cattle which He has created, and they say, "This is for Allah," by their claim, "and this is for our partners." But what is for their partners does not reach Allah, while what is for Allah - this reaches their partners. Evil is that which they rule.
interpretation: This verse is criticizing the polytheistic practice of dedicating a portion of one's crops and livestock to Allah, while also dedicating a portion to other deities or idols that they worship alongside Allah. The verse points out the flawed logic in this practice, as the portion dedicated to the false deities does not benefit or reach Allah in any way, while the portion dedicated to Allah ends up benefiting the false deities. This is because the polytheists would actually use the portion dedicated to Allah for their own personal benefit or for the benefit of their idols. The verse concludes by condemning this practice as an evil way of assigning portions and making judgments.
orig: وجعلوا لله مما ذرأ من الحرث والأنعام نصيبا فقالوا هذا لله بزعمهم وهذا لشركائنا فما كان لشركائهم فلا يصل إلى الله وما كان لله فهو يصل إلى شركائهم ساء ما يحكمون

translation: And likewise, their "partners" have made fair-seeming to most of the polytheists the killing of their children in order to lead them to their own destruction and cause confusion in their religion. And if Allah had willed, they would not have done so. So leave them and that which they invent.
interpretation: This verse highlights the deceptive influence of the polytheists' false deities or "partners" that they associated with Allah. These false deities made the abhorrent act of infanticide seem acceptable and even desirable to the polytheists. The verse suggests that this was done to lead the polytheists astray and create confusion in their understanding of religion. However, it also emphasizes that this happened only by Allah's will, as nothing occurs without His permission. The verse concludes by instructing the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) to leave the polytheists and their false inventions, as they will ultimately face the consequences of their actions in the Hereafter.
orig: وكذلك زين لكثير من المشركين قتل أولادهم شركاؤهم ليردوهم وليلبسوا عليهم دينهم ولو شاء الله ما فعلوه فذرهم وما يفترون

translation: And they say, "These animals and crops are forbidden; no one may eat from them except whom we will," by their claim. And there are those [camels] whose backs are forbidden [by them] and those upon which the name of Allah is not mentioned - [all of this] an invention of untruth about Him. He will punish them for what they were inventing.
interpretation: This verse is a condemnation of the pagan Arabs who used to falsely attribute certain prohibitions and restrictions to Allah regarding their cattle and crops. They would arbitrarily declare some animals and agricultural produce as sacred, claiming that only certain people could consume them. They would also prohibit the use of some camels for riding and refrain from mentioning Allah's name upon them, wrongfully ascribing these practices to divine command. The verse makes it clear that these were baseless innovations and fabrications attributed to Allah. It asserts that Allah will punish them for their false inventions and for distorting the true religion with their self-imposed restrictions that had no basis in divine revelation.
orig: وقالوا هذه أنعام وحرث حجر لا يطعمها إلا من نشاء بزعمهم وأنعام حرمت ظهورها وأنعام لا يذكرون اسم الله عليها افتراء عليه سيجزيهم بما كانوا يفترون

translation: And they say, "What is in the bellies of these animals is exclusively for our males and forbidden to our females. But if it is [born] dead, then all of them have shares therein." He will punish them for their description. Indeed, He is Wise and Knowing.
interpretation: This verse is referring to the pre-Islamic Arab practice of dedicating certain animals or their offspring to their idols, and prohibiting women from consuming them. They would claim that if the offspring died in the womb, both men and women could partake of it. The verse condemns this baseless practice and the attribution of such false rulings to Allah. It emphasizes that Allah, in His wisdom and knowledge, will hold them accountable for their false claims and for inventing such prohibitions without any divine authority.
orig: وقالوا ما في بطون هذه الأنعام خالصة لذكورنا ومحرم على أزواجنا وإن يكن ميتة فهم فيه شركاء سيجزيهم وصفهم إنه حكيم عليم

translation: Indeed, lost are those who have killed their children in foolishness without knowledge and have forbidden what Allah has provided for them, inventing falsehood about Allah. They have gone astray and were not [rightly] guided.
interpretation: This verse condemns the pre-Islamic practice of infanticide, particularly of female children, and the prohibition of certain foods due to baseless superstitions. It emphasizes that such actions stem from ignorance and foolishness, leading people astray from the right path. The verse also highlights the gravity of attributing false rulings to Allah, as it is a form of inventing lies against Him. This interpretation underscores the importance of relying on divine guidance and knowledge rather than misguided cultural practices or personal whims, as they can lead to severe consequences both in this world and the hereafter.
orig: قد خسر الذين قتلوا أولادهم سفها بغير علم وحرموا ما رزقهم الله افتراء على الله قد ضلوا وما كانوا مهتدين

translation: And it is He who causes gardens to grow, [both] trellised and untrellised, and palm trees and crops of different [kinds of] food and olives and pomegranates, similar and dissimilar. Eat of [each of] its fruit when it yields and give its due [zakah] on the day of its harvest. And be not excessive. Indeed, He does not like those who commit excess.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the power and generosity of Allah in creating a diverse array of plants and fruits for human sustenance. It encourages gratitude and moderation in the consumption of these provisions, reminding believers to give the obligatory charity (zakah) from their harvest. The verse also warns against wastefulness and excessive consumption, as Allah does not approve of those who are extravagant or ungrateful for His blessings. This highlights the Islamic principles of balance, mindfulness, and social responsibility in relation to the bounties provided by Allah.
orig: وهو الذي أنشأ جنات معروشات وغير معروشات والنخل والزرع مختلفا أكله والزيتون والرمان متشابها وغير متشابه كلوا من ثمره إذا أثمر وآتوا حقه يوم حصاده ولا تسرفوا إنه لا يحب المسرفين

translation: And the cattle, He has created them for you; in them is warmth and [numerous] benefits, and from them you eat. And for you in them is [the enjoyment of] beauty when you bring them in [for the evening] and when you send them out [to pasture]. And they carry your loads to a land you could not have reached except with difficulty to yourselves. Indeed, your Lord is Kind and Merciful. And [He created] the horses, mules and donkeys for you to ride and [as] adornment. And He creates that which you do not know.
interpretation: This verse highlights the blessings that Allah has bestowed upon humanity through the creation of cattle. It emphasizes the numerous benefits we derive from them, such as warmth from their skins, food from their meat, and the beauty and pleasure we find in watching them graze or return home in the evening. Moreover, these animals serve as a means of transportation, carrying heavy loads to distant lands that would otherwise be difficult for humans to reach. This showcases Allah's kindness and mercy towards His creation. The verse also mentions horses, mules, and donkeys as creatures provided for riding and adornment, further emphasizing the diverse ways in which Allah has facilitated our lives through the creation of these animals. Lastly, it reminds us that there are still many things that Allah creates which are beyond our knowledge and understanding, encouraging us to remain humble and grateful for His blessings.
orig: ومن الأنعام حمولة وفرشا كلوا مما رزقكم الله ولا تتبعوا خطوات الشيطان إنه لكم عدو مبين

translation: Eight pairs: of the sheep two and of the goats two. Say, "Is it the two males He has forbidden or the two females or that which the wombs of the two females contain? Inform me with knowledge, if you should be truthful."
interpretation: This verse questions the arbitrary prohibitions that the polytheists had invented regarding certain animals. It challenges them to provide evidence for their claims, as these prohibitions have no basis in divine revelation or sound reasoning. The verse emphasizes the importance of basing one's beliefs and practices on authentic knowledge rather than mere conjecture or tradition.
orig: ثمانية أزواج من الضأن اثنين ومن المعز اثنين قل آلذكرين حرم أم الأنثيين أما اشتملت عليه أرحام الأنثيين نبئوني بعلم إن كنتم صادقين

translation: And of the camels two and of the cattle two. Say, "Is it the two males He has forbidden or the two females or that which the wombs of the two females contain? Or were you witnesses when Allah charged you with this? Then who is more unjust than one who invents a lie about Allah to mislead the people by [something] other than knowledge? Indeed, Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people."
interpretation: This verse questions the arbitrary prohibitions that the pagans of Mecca had placed on certain animals, without any divine authority. It challenges them to provide evidence for their claims, either through rational argument or divine revelation. The rhetorical questioning emphasizes the absurdity of their stance. The verse asserts that inventing lies about God's laws to mislead people is a grave injustice, and that Allah does not guide those who engage in such wrongdoing. It underscores the importance of basing religious practices and prohibitions on authentic divine guidance rather than human whims or cultural traditions.
orig: ومن الإبل اثنين ومن البقر اثنين قل آلذكرين حرم أم الأنثيين أما اشتملت عليه أرحام الأنثيين أم كنتم شهداء إذ وصاكم الله بهذا فمن أظلم ممن افترى على الله كذبا ليضل الناس بغير علم إن الله لا يهدي القوم الظالمين

translation: Say, "I do not find within that which was revealed to me [anything] forbidden to one who would eat it unless it be a dead animal or blood spilled out or the flesh of swine - for indeed, it is impure - or it be [that slaughtered in] disobedience, dedicated to other than Allah. But whoever is forced [by necessity], neither desiring [it] nor transgressing [its limit], then indeed, your Lord is Forgiving and Merciful."
interpretation: This verse is addressing the dietary restrictions in Islam. It states that the only foods that are prohibited are carrion (animals that died without being slaughtered), flowing blood, pork, and animals dedicated to other than Allah (such as those offered to idols). However, if one is in a situation of necessity and is forced to consume these prohibited items without desire or transgression, then Allah is Forgiving and Merciful. This highlights the principle that the preservation of life takes precedence over dietary restrictions in extreme circumstances. The verse also emphasizes that these restrictions come from divine revelation to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him).
orig: قل لا أجد في ما أوحي إلي محرما على طاعم يطعمه إلا أن يكون ميتة أو دما مسفوحا أو لحم خنزير فإنه رجس أو فسقا أهل لغير الله به فمن اضطر غير باغ ولا عاد فإن ربك غفور رحيم

translation: And to those who are Jews We prohibited every animal of uncloven hoof; and of the cattle and the sheep We prohibited to them their fat, except what adheres to their backs or the entrails or what is joined with bone. [By] that We repaid them for their injustice. And indeed, We are truthful.
interpretation: This verse indicates that God imposed certain dietary restrictions specifically on the Jews as a punishment for their transgressions and injustice. The prohibited foods included animals with uncloven hooves and the fat of cattle and sheep, except what is attached to their backs, entrails, or mixed with bone. These restrictions serve as a reminder of the consequences of deviating from God's path and the importance of obedience and righteousness. The verse also emphasizes God's truthfulness in His words and actions, affirming that these prohibitions are just and warranted.
orig: وعلى الذين هادوا حرمنا كل ذي ظفر ومن البقر والغنم حرمنا عليهم شحومهما إلا ما حملت ظهورهما أو الحوايا أو ما اختلط بعظم ذلك جزيناهم ببغيهم وإنا لصادقون

translation: But if they deny you, [O Muhammad], say, "Your Lord is the possessor of vast mercy; but His punishment cannot be repelled from the people who are criminals."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the vastness of Allah's mercy, which encompasses all of His creation. However, it also serves as a warning to those who persistently deny the truth and commit crimes, reminding them that they cannot escape Allah's punishment if they continue on their wrongful path. The verse encourages the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) to remain steadfast in conveying the message, even in the face of rejection, knowing that the ultimate fate of the deniers rests with Allah, who is both merciful and just.
orig: فإن كذبوك فقل ربكم ذو رحمة واسعة ولا يرد بأسه عن القوم المجرمين

translation: Those who associated [others with Allah] will say, "If Allah had willed, we would not have associated [anything] and neither would our fathers, nor would we have prohibited anything." Likewise did those before deny until they tasted Our punishment. Say, "Do you have any knowledge that you can produce for us? You follow not except assumption, and you are not but falsifying."
interpretation: This verse points out the flawed logic of those who ascribe partners to Allah. They claim that their idolatry and prohibitions are in accordance with Allah's will. However, this is just an excuse to justify their wrongdoings. The same argument was used by previous generations until they faced the consequences of their disbelief. The Prophet is instructed to challenge them to bring forth any proof for their claims. In reality, they merely follow conjecture and lies, having no solid evidence to support their practices. The verse emphasizes that attributing false things to Allah and following baseless assumptions lead to misguidance and punishment.
orig: سيقول الذين أشركوا لو شاء الله ما أشركنا ولا آباؤنا ولا حرمنا من شيء كذلك كذب الذين من قبلهم حتى ذاقوا بأسنا قل هل عندكم من علم فتخرجوه لنا إن تتبعون إلا الظن وإن أنتم إلا تخرصون

translation: Say, "With Allah is the far-reaching argument. If He had willed, He would have guided you all."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the ultimate power and wisdom of Allah. It suggests that Allah possesses the most compelling and conclusive arguments or proofs. If He had so willed, He could have easily guided all of humanity to the right path. However, Allah has given humans free will to choose their own way, whether to follow His guidance or not. The verse also implies that the responsibility for not being guided falls upon the individuals themselves, as Allah has provided sufficient evidence and arguments for the truth, but it is up to each person to accept or reject it based on their own choice.
orig: قل فلله الحجة البالغة فلو شاء لهداكم أجمعين

translation: Say, "Bring forward your witnesses who can testify that Allah has forbidden this." And if they testify, do not testify with them. And do not follow the desires of those who deny Our verses and those who do not believe in the Hereafter, and they equate [others] with their Lord.
interpretation: This verse challenges the polytheists who claimed that Allah had forbidden certain animals or practices without any evidence. It asks them to bring forward witnesses to support their claims, but even if they do, the believers are instructed not to follow their testimony. The verse also highlights the characteristics of the disbelievers: they reject Allah's signs, do not believe in the Hereafter, and associate others with Allah in worship. The message conveyed is that the believers should not follow the whims and desires of those who lack faith and engage in polytheistic practices, as their claims are baseless and contradict the teachings of Islam.
orig: قل هلم شهداءكم الذين يشهدون أن الله حرم هذا فإن شهدوا فلا تشهد معهم ولا تتبع أهواء الذين كذبوا بآياتنا والذين لا يؤمنون بالآخرة وهم بربهم يعدلون

translation: Say, "Come, I will recite what your Lord has prohibited to you. [He commands] that you not associate anything with Him, and to parents, good treatment, and do not kill your children out of poverty; We will provide for you and them. And do not approach immoralities - what is apparent of them and what is concealed. And do not kill the soul which Allah has forbidden [to be killed] except by [legal] right. This has He instructed you that you may use reason."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of monotheism and the prohibition of associating partners with Allah. It also stresses the significance of treating one's parents with kindness and respect. The verse forbids the killing of children due to fear of poverty, assuring that Allah will provide sustenance for both the parents and the children. It also prohibits engaging in any form of immorality, whether openly or secretly. Furthermore, the verse emphasizes the sanctity of human life and forbids taking it unjustly, except in cases where it is legally permissible. These commandments are given to mankind so that they may use their intellect and reason to understand and follow the right path.
orig: قل تعالوا أتل ما حرم ربكم عليكم ألا تشركوا به شيئا وبالوالدين إحسانا ولا تقتلوا أولادكم من إملاق نحن نرزقكم وإياهم ولا تقربوا الفواحش ما ظهر منها وما بطن ولا تقتلوا النفس التي حرم الله إلا بالحق ذلكم وصاكم به لعلكم تعقلون

translation: And do not approach the property of the orphan except in the best manner until he reaches maturity. And give full measure and weight in justice. We do not charge any soul except [with that within] its capacity. And when you speak [i.e., testify], be just, even if [it concerns] a near relative. And the covenant of Allah fulfill. This has He instructed you that you may remember.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of dealing justly and fairly with others, especially those who are vulnerable such as orphans. It instructs believers to safeguard the wealth of orphans and to deal with it in a manner that is best for the orphan until they reach the age of maturity. It also commands giving full measure and weight in transactions and not burdening anyone beyond their capacity. The verse stresses the importance of speaking the truth and being just in testimony, even if it goes against one's own relatives. Finally, it reminds believers to fulfill their covenants with Allah. These instructions are meant to guide believers to righteousness and to be mindful of Allah in all their dealings.
orig: ولا تقربوا مال اليتيم إلا بالتي هي أحسن حتى يبلغ أشده وأوفوا الكيل والميزان بالقسط لا نكلف نفسا إلا وسعها وإذا قلتم فاعدلوا ولو كان ذا قربى وبعهد الله أوفوا ذلكم وصاكم به لعلكم تذكرون

translation: And, [moreover], this is My path, which is straight, so follow it; and do not follow [other] ways, for you will be separated from His way. This has He instructed you that you may become righteous.
interpretation: In this verse, Allah is emphasizing the importance of following the straight path that He has ordained, which is the path of Islam. He warns against following other paths or ways, as they will only lead astray from His path. The straight path is the way of the Quran and the Sunnah of Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him). Following this path is the key to righteousness and success in this life and the Hereafter. The verse also highlights the fact that there is only one straight path, and all other ways are crooked and lead to deviation. It is a reminder for the believers to stay steadfast on the path of Islam and not be swayed by other ideologies or temptations that may lead them away from the truth.
orig: وأن هذا صراطي مستقيما فاتبعوه ولا تتبعوا السبل فتفرق بكم عن سبيله ذلكم وصاكم به لعلكم تتقون

translation: Then We gave Moses the Scripture, making complete [Our favor] upon the one who did good and as a detailed explanation of all things and as guidance and mercy that perhaps in [the matter of] the meeting with their Lord they would believe.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance and significance of the scripture given to Moses (peace be upon him). It was a complete and comprehensive guide, detailing everything that the people needed for their spiritual and worldly well-being. The scripture was a manifestation of Allah's favor upon Moses and a reward for his righteousness. It served as a guidance and mercy, directing people towards the path of faith and belief in the eventual meeting with their Lord in the Hereafter. The verse suggests that by following the teachings of the scripture and believing in the Divine encounter, people may attain salvation and success in both this world and the next.
orig: ثم آتينا موسى الكتاب تماما على الذي أحسن وتفصيلا لكل شيء وهدى ورحمة لعلهم بلقاء ربهم يؤمنون

translation: And this is a blessed Book which We have revealed, so follow it and fear Allah that you may receive mercy.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the divine origin and the blessed nature of the Qur'an. It commands the believers to follow its teachings and to be mindful of Allah in order to attain His mercy. The interpretation is that the Qur'an is not an ordinary book, but a sacred scripture revealed by Allah as a guide for humanity. By adhering to its teachings and leading a righteous life, one can hope to receive Allah's mercy, forgiveness, and ultimate salvation in the Hereafter. The verse also implies that the Qur'an is a source of blessings and that following it will bring about positive changes in one's life, both in this world and the next.
orig: وهذا كتاب أنزلناه مبارك فاتبعوه واتقوا لعلكم ترحمون

translation: That you say, "The Scripture was only revealed to two groups before us, but we were of their study unaware."
interpretation: This verse is addressing the excuses made by those who rejected the message of Islam. They claimed that divine revelation had only been sent to two groups before them, likely referring to the Jews and Christians, and that they were unaware of the teachings of those scriptures. This excuse is being dismissed as invalid, implying that the truth of Islam is evident and that ignorance of previous revelations is not a justification for rejecting it. The verse suggests that the message of Islam is universal and applicable to all people, regardless of their previous exposure to divine scriptures.
orig: أن تقولوا إنما أنزل الكتاب على طائفتين من قبلنا وإن كنا عن دراستهم لغافلين

translation: Or lest you say, "If only the Scripture had been revealed to us, we would have been better guided than they." Now there has come to you a clear evidence from your Lord and a guidance and mercy. Then who is more unjust than one who denies the verses of Allah and turns away from them? We will recompense those who turn away from Our verses with the worst of punishment for their having turned away.
interpretation: This verse warns against the attitude of rejecting divine guidance when it comes, thinking that one would have been better guided if the revelation had come directly to them. It emphasizes that clear evidence, guidance, and mercy have indeed come from God, and that to deny or turn away from it is a great injustice that will be met with severe punishment. The verse stresses the importance of accepting and following divine guidance when it is presented, rather than making excuses or thinking oneself superior to it.
orig: أو تقولوا لو أنا أنزل علينا الكتاب لكنا أهدى منهم فقد جاءكم بينة من ربكم وهدى ورحمة فمن أظلم ممن كذب بآيات الله وصدف عنها سنجزي الذين يصدفون عن آياتنا سوء العذاب بما كانوا يصدفون

translation: Do they await but that the angels should come to them or your Lord should come or that there come some of the signs of your Lord? On the day when some of the signs of your Lord shall come, faith shall not profit a soul which did not believe before, or earn good through its faith. Say: Wait; we too are waiting.
interpretation: This verse warns that there will come a time when it will be too late for people to repent and believe. Some signs of the Day of Judgment will appear, such as the coming of the angels or other signs from God, at which point having faith will no longer benefit those who did not believe beforehand or do good deeds while they had faith. The believers are told to wait patiently for that day, while the disbelievers are also waiting, heedless of the consequences. It emphasizes the importance of having faith and doing righteousness in the present, before it's too late, as each soul will be held accountable for its beliefs and actions in this life.
orig: هل ينظرون إلا أن تأتيهم الملائكة أو يأتي ربك أو يأتي بعض آيات ربك يوم يأتي بعض آيات ربك لا ينفع نفسا إيمانها لم تكن آمنت من قبل أو كسبت في إيمانها خيرا قل انتظروا إنا منتظرون

translation: Indeed, those who have divided their religion and become sects - you, [O Muhammad], are not [associated] with them in anything. Their affair is only [left] to Allah; then He will inform them about what they used to do.
interpretation: This verse warns against the dangers of sectarianism and division within religion. It emphasizes that the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) is not associated with those who have divided their religion into sects and factions. The matter of these people is left to Allah, who will judge them based on their deeds and actions. The verse implies that unity and cohesion within the religious community is important, and that splintering into competing sects is not condoned. Ultimately, Allah will hold people accountable for their choices and actions, including any religious divisions they may have caused or participated in.
orig: إن الذين فرقوا دينهم وكانوا شيعا لست منهم في شيء إنما أمرهم إلى الله ثم ينبئهم بما كانوا يفعلون

translation: Whoever comes [on the Day of Judgement] with a good deed will have ten times the like thereof [to his credit], and whoever comes with an evil deed will not be recompensed except the like thereof; and they will not be wronged.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the immense mercy and justice of Allah. It shows that Allah, in His infinite grace, multiplies the reward for good deeds by ten, while the recompense for evil deeds is only equal to the deed itself, with no multiplication of punishment. This highlights the fact that Allah's mercy far outweighs His wrath. Moreover, the verse assures that no one will be wronged on the Day of Judgment; everyone will receive precisely what they deserve, based on their deeds in this worldly life. This should encourage believers to strive for righteousness and discourage them from committing sins, knowing that their deeds will be weighed with perfect justice and fairness by Allah.
orig: من جاء بالحسنة فله عشر أمثالها ومن جاء بالسيئة فلا يجزى إلا مثلها وهم لا يظلمون

translation: Say, "Indeed, my Lord has guided me to a straight path - a correct religion - the way of Abraham, inclining toward truth, and he was not among those who associated others with Allah."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of following the straight path of Islam, which is the true religion of Abraham. It highlights the significance of monotheism and rejecting the association of partners with Allah. The verse also affirms that the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) was guided by Allah to this straight path, and it serves as a reminder for all believers to adhere to the correct religion and avoid polytheism. It underscores the continuity of the divine message from Abraham to Muhammad, and the need to remain steadfast in faith and submission to the One True God.
orig: قل إنني هداني ربي إلى صراط مستقيم دينا قيما ملة إبراهيم حنيفا وما كان من المشركين

translation: Say, "Indeed, my prayer, my rites of sacrifice, my living and my dying are for Allah, Lord of the worlds."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the complete submission and devotion of the believer to Allah in all aspects of life. It means that every act of worship, from prayer to sacrifice, and every moment of one's life and death, should be dedicated to Allah alone, the Lord of all creation. This is the essence of pure monotheism (Tawheed) in Islam, where a person directs all their actions and intentions towards pleasing their Creator and Sustainer, without associating partners with Him or seeking the approval of others. It is a powerful declaration of faith and a reminder to live a life centered around the worship and obedience of Allah.
orig: قل إن صلاتي ونسكي ومحياي ومماتي لله رب العالمين

translation: He has no partner, and this I have been commanded, and I am the first of those who submit.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the fundamental Islamic belief in the oneness and uniqueness of Allah, known as Tawheed. It states that Allah has no partners or equals, and that this is a commandment that must be followed. The speaker, likely Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him), declares that he is the first among those who submit to Allah's will and embrace Islam. This sets an example for all believers to follow, highlighting the importance of submitting to Allah alone and rejecting any form of polytheism or idolatry.
orig: لا شريك له وبذلك أمرت وأنا أول المسلمين

translation: Say, "Is it other than Allah I should desire as a lord while He is the Lord of all things? And every soul earns not [blame] except against itself, and no bearer of burdens will bear the burden of another. Then to your Lord is your return, and He will inform you concerning that over which you used to differ."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the oneness and supremacy of Allah as the only true Lord worthy of worship. It highlights the concept of individual responsibility, stating that each person is accountable for their own deeds and will not bear the burden of others' sins. The verse also points to the ultimate return to Allah, who will judge and inform people about the matters in which they differed, emphasizing the importance of following the right path and resolving disputes based on divine guidance.
orig: قل أغير الله أبغي ربا وهو رب كل شيء ولا تكسب كل نفس إلا عليها ولا تزر وازرة وزر أخرى ثم إلى ربكم مرجعكم فينبئكم بما كنتم فيه تختلفون

translation: And it is He who has made you successors upon the earth and has raised some of you above others in degrees [of rank] that He may try you through what He has given you. Indeed, your Lord is swift in penalty; but indeed, He is Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that it is Allah who has appointed human beings as His representatives on earth and has given them different ranks and abilities in order to test them. The varying degrees of wealth, power, and skills that people possess are a means for Allah to see how they utilize His blessings. The verse also highlights two contrasting attributes of Allah - His swiftness in punishing those who misuse His favors and disobey Him, and His forgiveness and mercy towards those who seek His pardon and strive to please Him. It serves as a reminder for humans to be grateful for Allah's blessings, use them responsibly, and turn to Him in repentance.
orig: وهو الذي جعلكم خلائف الأرض ورفع بعضكم فوق بعض درجات ليبلوكم في ما آتاكم إن ربك سريع العقاب وإنه لغفور رحيم

translation: Alif, Lam, Meem, Sad.
interpretation: This verse consists of disjoined letters, the meaning of which is known only to Allah. Some scholars suggest that these letters serve as a way to grab the attention of the listener or reader, indicating that an important message is about to be conveyed. Others propose that these letters may have a deeper, symbolic meaning that is not readily apparent to us. Ultimately, the true meaning and purpose of these letters remains a mystery known only to Allah, and we are encouraged to reflect upon them as we ponder the profound wisdom contained within the Qur'an.
orig: المص

translation: A Book has been revealed to you, so let there not be in your breast distress therefrom, that you may warn thereby and as a reminder to the believers.
interpretation: This verse is addressing the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him), reassuring him that he should not feel any hesitation or unease in conveying the message of the Qur'an, which has been revealed to him by Allah. The purpose of this revelation is to serve as a warning to mankind and a reminder to the believers of their duties and obligations towards their Creator. The Prophet is being instructed to deliver the message with clarity and conviction, without letting any doubts or concerns hinder him from fulfilling his mission. This highlights the importance of the Qur'an as a source of guidance and enlightenment for all of humanity.
orig: كتاب أنزل إليك فلا يكن في صدرك حرج منه لتنذر به وذكرى للمؤمنين

translation: Follow, [O mankind], what has been revealed to you from your Lord and do not follow other than Him any allies. Little do you remember.
interpretation: This verse is a clear command to humanity to follow the guidance and revelation sent down by Allah, and to avoid taking anyone else as a protector or guardian besides Him. It emphasizes that most people do not reflect on this message or take heed of this important directive. The verse implies that following allies other than Allah will lead people astray, as they do not have the wisdom and guidance that comes from the divine revelation. It is a reminder to be mindful of Allah's message and to make Him alone the source of guidance and authority in one's life.
orig: اتبعوا ما أنزل إليكم من ربكم ولا تتبعوا من دونه أولياء قليلا ما تذكرون

translation: And how many a city did We destroy, and Our punishment came to it at night or while they were sleeping at noon.
interpretation: This verse is a reminder of Allah's power and a warning to those who disobey Him. It emphasizes that Allah has destroyed many cities and civilizations in the past due to their wrongdoings and that His punishment can come at any time, whether it be at night or during the day when people are resting. This serves as a cautionary tale for people to be mindful of their actions and to always be in a state of obedience to Allah, for they do not know when His punishment may come. It also highlights the idea that no matter how powerful or secure a city or civilization may seem, it is ultimately at the mercy of Allah's will.
orig: وكم من قرية أهلكناها فجاءها بأسنا بياتا أو هم قائلون

translation: And their cry, when Our punishment came to them, was only that they said, "Indeed, we were wrongdoers!"
interpretation: This verse highlights the realization and confession of the wrongdoers when faced with the consequences of their actions. It suggests that when God's punishment befalls them, they finally acknowledge their transgressions and admit to their wrongdoing. This interpretation emphasizes the idea that often, people only recognize their mistakes and sins when they are confronted with the dire results of their choices. It also implies that this admission of guilt may come too late, as the punishment has already been unleashed upon them. The verse serves as a reminder for individuals to be mindful of their actions and to seek forgiveness before it is too late.
orig: فما كان دعواهم إذ جاءهم بأسنا إلا أن قالوا إنا كنا ظالمين

translation: Then We will surely question those to whom [a message] was sent, and We will surely question the messengers.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the accountability of both the messengers and the people to whom they were sent. On the Day of Judgment, Allah will question the messengers about how they conveyed His message and fulfilled their duties. He will also question the people who received the message about how they responded to it and whether they followed the guidance provided by the messengers. This verse serves as a reminder that everyone will be held responsible for their actions and decisions, and that no one can escape the ultimate judgment of Allah.
orig: فلنسألن الذين أرسل إليهم ولنسألن المرسلين

translation: Then We will surely relate [their deeds] to them with knowledge, and We were not [at all] absent.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah has complete knowledge of all the deeds and actions of His creation, and that nothing escapes His attention. On the Day of Judgment, Allah will recount to each individual their deeds with precise knowledge, highlighting His omniscience and the fact that He is always present, witnessing everything. This serves as a reminder for humans to be mindful of their actions, as they will be held accountable for them in the Hereafter, and that Allah's judgment will be based on His perfect knowledge and justice.
orig: فلنقصن عليهم بعلم وما كنا غائبين

translation: And the weighing [of deeds] that Day will be the truth. So those whose scales are heavy - it is they who will be the successful.
interpretation: This verse refers to the Day of Judgment when people's deeds will be weighed on a scale. Those whose good deeds outweigh their bad deeds will be the successful ones who will attain salvation and enter Paradise. The "weighing" on that Day will be absolutely just and fair, as it will be done by Allah Himself. This serves as a reminder for people to focus on doing righteous deeds in this world, as they will determine one's fate in the eternal life of the Hereafter. The verse emphasizes the importance of living a life pleasing to Allah and the ultimate justice that will be established on the Day of Judgment.
orig: والوزن يومئذ الحق فمن ثقلت موازينه فأولئك هم المفلحون

translation: And those whose scales are light - it is they who will lose themselves for what injustice they were doing toward Our verses.
interpretation: This verse warns that those whose good deeds are outweighed by their bad deeds on the Day of Judgment will be the ultimate losers. They will have forfeited their own souls and condemned themselves to punishment in the Hereafter because of their persistent wrongdoing and rejection of God's messages and signs during their worldly lives. Injustice towards God's revelations, whether disbelief, mockery, or disobedience, will lead to devastating consequences in the next life. The scales of deeds symbolize perfect divine justice.
orig: ومن خفت موازينه فأولئك الذين خسروا أنفسهم بما كانوا بآياتنا يظلمون

translation: And We have certainly established you upon the earth and made for you therein ways of livelihood. Little are you grateful.
interpretation: This verse is a reminder from Allah to humanity of the blessings and favors He has bestowed upon them. He has established humans on the earth, giving them authority and the means to live and thrive through various ways of earning a livelihood. However, despite these abundant blessings, humans often fail to show proper gratitude to their Lord. The verse serves as an admonition, urging people to recognize and appreciate the countless bounties provided by Allah, and to express their thankfulness through obedience and worship. It highlights the tendency of human beings to take God's blessings for granted and not acknowledge them with sufficient gratitude and praise.
orig: ولقد مكناكم في الأرض وجعلنا لكم فيها معايش قليلا ما تشكرون

translation: And indeed, We created you, then We fashioned you, then We said to the angels: Prostrate yourselves unto Adam! So they fell prostrate, all save Iblis; he was not of those who make prostration.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the special status of human beings in God's creation. It indicates that God not only created human beings, but also fashioned them into their final form, giving them a unique status above other creatures. The command to the angels to prostrate before Adam symbolizes the elevated position of humans. However, Iblis (Satan) refused to bow down out of pride and disobedience. This serves as a warning that even those close to God can fall into sin by rejecting His commands and succumbing to arrogance. The verse reminds humans to be humble, obedient, and grateful for their God-given status, while being vigilant against the temptations of pride and rebellion exemplified by Iblis.
orig: ولقد خلقناكم ثم صورناكم ثم قلنا للملائكة اسجدوا لآدم فسجدوا إلا إبليس لم يكن من الساجدين

translation: [ Allah ] said, "What prevented you from prostrating when I commanded you?" [Satan] said, "I am better than him. You created me from fire and created him from clay."
interpretation: This verse highlights the arrogance and disobedience of Satan (Iblis). When commanded by Allah to prostrate before Adam, Satan refused, claiming superiority due to being created from fire while Adam was created from clay. This demonstrates how pride and feelings of self-importance can lead one to rebel against the commandments of Allah. It serves as a reminder for humans to remain humble and obedient to Allah, regardless of their perceived status or origins, and to avoid falling into the same trap of arrogance that led to Satan's downfall.
orig: قال ما منعك ألا تسجد إذ أمرتك قال أنا خير منه خلقتني من نار وخلقته من طين

translation: He said, "Then get down from it (Paradise), for it is not for you to be arrogant therein. Get out, indeed you are of the debased."
interpretation: This verse is a rebuke from Allah to Iblis (Satan) for his arrogance and disobedience. Allah is commanding Iblis to descend from Paradise as a punishment for refusing to prostrate to Adam out of pride and arrogance. The command "get down from it" signifies expulsion and disgrace. Allah makes it clear that Paradise is not a place for arrogance and that Iblis' behavior has rendered him among the humiliated and debased. This verse serves as a lesson for all of humanity that arrogance and pride are despised by Allah, and that obedience and humility are the path to His pleasure and Paradise.
orig: قال فاهبط منها فما يكون لك أن تتكبر فيها فاخرج إنك من الصاغرين

translation: He said, "Reprieve me until the Day they are resurrected."
interpretation: This verse is a plea from Iblis (Satan) to Allah, asking for a reprieve from death until the Day of Resurrection. Iblis seeks to use this time to misguide and tempt humanity away from the straight path. It highlights the respite given to Iblis by Allah to test mankind, emphasizing the importance of resisting temptations and remaining steadfast in faith until the Day of Judgment. The verse also underscores Iblis's arrogance and defiance, as he plots to lead mankind astray despite acknowledging Allah's supremacy.
orig: قال أنظرني إلى يوم يبعثون

translation: He said: "Indeed, you are of those reprieved."
interpretation: This verse is from Surah Al-A'raf, where Allah is addressing Iblis (Satan) after he refused to prostrate to Adam. Iblis requested Allah to grant him respite until the Day of Resurrection. Allah's response, as mentioned in this verse, indicates that He granted Iblis' request, allowing him to live until the appointed time. This verse highlights the concept of divine will and predestination, as even Iblis' disobedience and subsequent reprieve until the Day of Judgment are part of Allah's greater plan. It also serves as a reminder that while evil forces may be allowed to exist and operate in this world, their ultimate fate is sealed, and they will face the consequences of their actions in the Hereafter.
orig: قال إنك من المنظرين

translation: [Iblees] said, "Because You have put me in error, I will surely sit in wait for them on Your straight path."
interpretation: This verse reflects the arrogance and defiance of Iblees (Satan) after being condemned by Allah for refusing to prostrate before Adam. Iblees blames Allah for his own disobedience and vows to mislead humanity from the straight path of guidance and righteousness out of spite and revenge. It highlights the danger of pride, the importance of taking responsibility for one's actions, and the constant presence of Satan's temptations and deceptions that believers must be vigilant against throughout their lives in order to stay on the straight path leading to Allah's pleasure and Paradise.
orig: قال فبما أغويتني لأقعدن لهم صراطك المستقيم

translation: Then I will come to them from before them and from behind them and on their right and on their left, and You will not find most of them grateful [to You].
interpretation: This verse can be interpreted as referring to the pervasive influence of Satan and his attempts to mislead humans from all directions and aspects of their lives. He approaches them from the front, symbolizing the allure of worldly temptations; from behind, representing the tendency to dwell on past sins and regrets; from the right, signifying the corruption of good deeds through insincerity or pride; and from the left, alluding to the invitation towards sinful actions. Despite God's blessings and guidance, most people fail to be truly grateful and instead succumb to Satan's persuasions in various forms. The verse emphasizes the importance of being vigilant against these spiritual attacks and striving to maintain sincere gratitude and obedience to God.
orig: ثم لآتينهم من بين أيديهم ومن خلفهم وعن أيمانهم وعن شمائلهم ولا تجد أكثرهم شاكرين

translation: [ Allah ] said, "Get out of Paradise, reproached and expelled. Whoever follows you among them - I will surely fill Hell with you, all together."
interpretation: This verse is a stern warning from Allah to Satan, expelling him from Paradise for his disobedience and arrogance. It also serves as a warning to humanity that those who follow Satan's path and turn away from Allah's guidance will face the same fate as Satan - being cast into Hell. The verse emphasizes the gravity of following Satan and the ultimate consequence of rejecting faith in Allah. It is a reminder for believers to stay steadfast in their faith and resist the temptations and whispers of Satan.
orig: قال اخرج منها مذءوما مدحورا لمن تبعك منهم لأملأن جهنم منكم أجمعين

translation: And O Adam, dwell you and your wife in Paradise and eat from wherever you will but do not approach this tree, lest you be among the wrongdoers.
interpretation: This verse is a command from Allah to Adam and his wife, Eve, to live in Paradise and enjoy its blessings. They are allowed to eat from any part of Paradise they desire, symbolizing the abundance and lack of restrictions in Paradise. However, Allah also warns them not to approach a specific tree, which is not identified in the Quran. Approaching it would be an act of disobedience to Allah, and doing so would place them among the wrongdoers, those who transgress against Allah's commands. This verse sets up the story of Adam and Eve's temptation by Satan and their eventual disobedience, leading to their expulsion from Paradise. It demonstrates that Allah gives humans free will, but also sets limits and consequences for transgressions.
orig: ويا آدم اسكن أنت وزوجك الجنة فكلا من حيث شئتما ولا تقربا هذه الشجرة فتكونا من الظالمين

translation: Then Satan whispered to them to make apparent to them that which was concealed from them of their private parts. He said, "Your Lord did not forbid you this tree except that you become angels or become of the immortal."
interpretation: This verse refers to the story of Adam and Eve in Paradise. Satan, out of his jealousy and evil nature, whispers to them and deceives them into disobeying Allah's command not to eat from a certain tree. He tries to tempt them by suggesting that the reason for Allah's prohibition was to prevent them from attaining a higher status, either as angels or immortal beings. Satan's whispering and deception led to Adam and Eve's fall from Paradise. The verse highlights the cunning and persistent nature of Satan in leading humans astray, and the importance of being vigilant against his whispers and temptations.
orig: فوسوس لهما الشيطان ليبدي لهما ما ووري عنهما من سوآتهما وقال ما نهاكما ربكما عن هذه الشجرة إلا أن تكونا ملكين أو تكونا من الخالدين

translation: And he swore to them, "Indeed, I am to you from among the sincere advisors."
interpretation: This verse is referring to Satan, who deceived Adam and Eve in the Garden of Eden. Satan swore to them that he was a sincere advisor, trying to convince them that he had their best interests at heart. However, his true intention was to lead them astray and cause them to disobey Allah. The verse highlights the deceptive nature of Satan and serves as a warning to humans to be cautious of those who claim to be sincere advisors but may have hidden malicious intentions. It emphasizes the importance of trusting in Allah's guidance and not being swayed by the false promises and deceptions of others.
orig: وقاسمهما إني لكما لمن الناصحين

translation: So he made them fall, through deception. And when they tasted of the tree, their private parts became apparent to them, and they began to fasten together over themselves from the leaves of Paradise. And their Lord called to them, "Did I not forbid you from that tree and tell you that Satan is to you a clear enemy?"
interpretation: This verse is referring to the story of Adam and Eve in Paradise. Satan deceived them into eating from the forbidden tree, causing them to become aware of their nakedness and leading them to cover themselves with leaves. The key message is that disobeying Allah's commands, even when tempted or deceived, has consequences. It also highlights how Satan is an open enemy to mankind, always trying to lead people astray. The verse serves as a reminder for believers to be mindful of Allah's boundaries and to be wary of Satan's tricks and temptations in this life.
orig: فدلاهما بغرور فلما ذاقا الشجرة بدت لهما سوآتهما وطفقا يخصفان عليهما من ورق الجنة وناداهما ربهما ألم أنهكما عن تلكما الشجرة وأقل لكما إن الشيطان لكما عدو مبين

translation: They said, "Our Lord, we have wronged ourselves, and if You do not forgive us and have mercy upon us, we will surely be among the losers."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of seeking forgiveness from Allah and acknowledging one's mistakes. It teaches us that even great figures like Adam and Eve, who were created directly by Allah and lived in Paradise, were capable of committing errors. However, the key is to recognize one's faults, sincerely repent, and turn back to Allah with humility, pleading for His forgiveness and mercy. The verse also highlights the consequences of not seeking Allah's forgiveness - being among the losers in both this world and the Hereafter. It serves as a reminder for all believers to constantly engage in self-reflection, seek Allah's forgiveness, and strive to be among those who earn His mercy and ultimate success.
orig: قالا ربنا ظلمنا أنفسنا وإن لم تغفر لنا وترحمنا لنكونن من الخاسرين

translation: He said, "Descend, being to one another enemies. And for you on the earth is a place of settlement and enjoyment for a time."
interpretation: This verse is referring to the descent of Adam and Eve from Paradise to Earth after they disobeyed Allah by eating from the forbidden tree. Allah is telling them that they will descend to Earth as enemies to one another, meaning that there will be enmity and conflict among human beings. However, Allah also provides hope by mentioning that the Earth will be a place of temporary settlement and enjoyment for humans until an appointed time, which is the Day of Judgment. This verse highlights the temporary nature of the life of this world and reminds humans of their ultimate return to Allah.
orig: قال اهبطوا بعضكم لبعض عدو ولكم في الأرض مستقر ومتاع إلى حين

translation: He said, "Therein you will live, and therein you will die, and from it you will be brought forth."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the temporary nature of life on earth. It reminds us that our entire existence - from birth to death - takes place on this earth. However, it also points to the inevitability of resurrection, as we will be brought forth from the earth in the Hereafter. This highlights the importance of living righteously and preparing for the eternal life to come, rather than being overly attached to the fleeting nature of this worldly existence.
orig: قال فيها تحيون وفيها تموتون ومنها تخرجون

translation: O children of Adam, We have bestowed upon you clothing to conceal your private parts and as adornment. But the clothing of righteousness - that is best. That is from the signs of Allah that perhaps they will remember.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of inner purity and righteousness over physical appearance and worldly adornments. While Allah has provided humans with clothing to cover their bodies and for beautification, the true essence of being clothed lies in adorning oneself with virtues, morality, and God-consciousness. The clothing of piety and righteousness is considered the best attire in the sight of Allah. This verse serves as a reminder for people to prioritize their spiritual well-being and to constantly remember the signs and blessings of Allah in their lives.
orig: يا بني آدم قد أنزلنا عليكم لباسا يواري سوآتكم وريشا ولباس التقوى ذلك خير ذلك من آيات الله لعلهم يذكرون

translation: O children of Adam! Let not Satan deceive you as he got your parents [Adam and Hawwa] out of Paradise, stripping them of their garments to show them their private parts. Surely, he and his tribe watch you from where you cannot see them. Surely, We have made the devils allies to those who do not believe.
interpretation: This verse serves as a warning to humanity against the deceptions and temptations of Satan.
