Just as Satan deceived Adam and Eve, causing them to be expelled from Paradise, he continues to mislead mankind. Satan and his followers are constantly observing humans from the unseen realm, seeking to exploit their weaknesses and lead them astray. The verse emphasizes that those who lack faith are particularly vulnerable to the influence of the devils, who become their allies and supporters. It is a reminder for believers to remain vigilant, strengthen their faith, and seek protection from God against the schemes of Satan and his tribe.
orig: يا بني آدم لا يفتننكم الشيطان كما أخرج أبويكم من الجنة ينزع عنهما لباسهما ليريهما سوآتهما إنه يراكم هو وقبيله من حيث لا ترونهم إنا جعلنا الشياطين أولياء للذين لا يؤمنون

translation: And when they commit an immorality, they say, "We found our fathers doing it, and Allah has ordered us to do it." Say, "Indeed, Allah does not order immorality. Do you say about Allah that which you do not know?"
interpretation: This verse is a strong condemnation of those who justify their immoral actions by claiming that it is what their ancestors did and what Allah has commanded. The Qur'an firmly rejects this notion, emphasizing that Allah never orders people to commit sins or acts of indecency. It suggests that those who make such claims are speaking about Allah without knowledge, essentially attributing false rulings to Him. The message is clear: take responsibility for your own actions and do not falsely invoke Allah or tradition to excuse wrongdoing. The verse upholds the perfect justice and wisdom of Allah's commandments.
orig: وإذا فعلوا فاحشة قالوا وجدنا عليها آباءنا والله أمرنا بها قل إن الله لا يأمر بالفحشاء أتقولون على الله ما لا تعلمون

translation: Say, "My Lord has ordered justice and that you maintain yourselves [in worship of Him] at every place [or time] of prostration, and invoke Him, sincere to Him in religion." Just as He originated you, you will return [to life].
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of worshipping Allah with sincerity and devotion. It commands believers to establish justice, maintain proper conduct during prayer, and invoke Allah with pure intentions. The verse reminds us that just as Allah originated our creation, we will ultimately return to Him in the Hereafter. This encourages believers to live righteously and remain mindful of their actions, as they will be held accountable before Allah on the Day of Judgment. The verse also highlights the concept of resurrection, affirming that just as Allah brought us into existence, He has the power to resurrect us after death for the final reckoning.
orig: قل أمر ربي بالقسط وأقيموا وجوهكم عند كل مسجد وادعوه مخلصين له الدين كما بدأكم تعودون

translation: A group [of you] He guided, and a group deserved [to be in] error. Indeed, they had taken the devils as allies instead of Allah while they thought that they were guided.
interpretation: This verse highlights the contrast between those whom Allah has guided to the straight path and those who have gone astray by following the footsteps of the devils. It emphasizes that some people, despite their belief that they are on the right path, have actually taken the devils as their allies and protectors instead of Allah. This misguided alliance leads them further away from the truth and deeper into error. The verse serves as a warning for believers to be cautious of the deceptions of the devils and to seek guidance and protection only from Allah.
orig: فريقا هدى وفريقا حق عليهم الضلالة إنهم اتخذوا الشياطين أولياء من دون الله ويحسبون أنهم مهتدون

translation: O children of Adam! Take your adornment at every mosque, and eat and drink, but be not excessive. Indeed, He likes not those who commit excess.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of maintaining modesty and humility in worship, while also encouraging believers to enjoy the lawful pleasures that Allah has provided. It reminds us to dress appropriately when attending the mosque, as a sign of respect and reverence for the sacred space. At the same time, it instructs us to partake in eating and drinking, but to do so in moderation and avoid extravagance or wastefulness. This verse highlights the Islamic principle of balance - that we should neither be ascetic nor indulgent, but rather strive for a middle path of gratitude, contentment, and self-restraint. It also underscores Allah's dislike for those who are excessive or wasteful, as this reflects a lack of appreciation for His blessings and provisions.
orig: يا بني آدم خذوا زينتكم عند كل مسجد وكلوا واشربوا ولا تسرفوا إنه لا يحب المسرفين

translation: Say, "Who has forbidden the adornment of Allah which He has produced for His servants and the good [lawful] things of provision?" Say, "They are for those who believe during the life of this world [but] exclusively for them on the Day of Resurrection." Thus do We detail the verses for a people who know.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the beautiful and lawful things in this world are meant to be enjoyed by the believers, as they are blessings from Allah. However, in the Hereafter, these blessings will be exclusively for those who had faith in this world. The verse also points out that Allah provides detailed explanations in the Qur'an for those who seek knowledge and understanding, so that they may comprehend the wisdom behind His commands and prohibitions.
orig: قل من حرم زينة الله التي أخرج لعباده والطيبات من الرزق قل هي للذين آمنوا في الحياة الدنيا خالصة يوم القيامة كذلك نفصل الآيات لقوم يعلمون

translation: Say, "My Lord has only forbidden immoralities - what is apparent of them and what is concealed - and sin, and oppression without right, and that you associate with Allah that for which He has not sent down authority, and that you say about Allah that which you do not know."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the prohibition of major sins and immorality, whether they are committed openly or secretly. It also condemns oppression, polytheism (associating partners with Allah), and making false claims about Allah without knowledge. The verse serves as a reminder for believers to adhere to the moral and ethical principles laid out by Allah and to refrain from transgressing the boundaries set by Him.
orig: قل إنما حرم ربي الفواحش ما ظهر منها وما بطن والإثم والبغي بغير الحق وأن تشركوا بالله ما لم ينزل به سلطانا وأن تقولوا على الله ما لا تعلمون

translation: And for every nation is a [specified] term. So when their time has come, they will not remain behind an hour, nor will they precede [it].
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the concept of divine destiny and the predetermined lifespan of nations. It suggests that every nation has a fixed time period in which to exist and function, and when that time comes to an end, the nation will neither be able to delay its demise nor advance it by even an hour. This interpretation highlights the idea that the rise and fall of civilizations is part of God's greater plan and that humans have limited control over the ultimate fate of their societies. It serves as a reminder of the fleeting nature of worldly power and the importance of striving for righteousness within the time allotted to each individual and nation.
orig: ولكل أمة أجل فإذا جاء أجلهم لا يستأخرون ساعة ولا يستقدمون

translation: O children of Adam, if there come to you messengers from among you relating to you My verses, then whoever fears Allah and reforms - there will be no fear concerning them, nor will they grieve.
interpretation: This verse is a reminder from Allah to humanity that He will send messengers from among them to convey His messages and guide them to the right path. Those who heed the warnings of the messengers, fear Allah, and mend their ways will have nothing to fear in this world or the Hereafter, nor will they grieve over what they may have lost in worldly pursuits. It emphasizes the importance of following the guidance of the prophets and messengers sent by Allah and the rewards that await those who do so - peace and contentment in this life and the next.
orig: يا بني آدم إما يأتينكم رسل منكم يقصون عليكم آياتي فمن اتقى وأصلح فلا خوف عليهم ولا هم يحزنون

translation: But those who deny Our signs and are arrogant toward them - those are the companions of the Fire; they will abide therein eternally.
interpretation: This verse warns that those who reject the clear signs and revelations of Allah, and who arrogantly turn away from them, will be the inhabitants of Hell, where they will remain forever. It emphasizes the severe consequence of denying the truth and being too proud to accept and follow the guidance sent by Allah. The verse serves as a strong reminder for people to humble themselves, acknowledge the signs of Allah, and follow His path to avoid the eternal punishment of the Hellfire.
orig: والذين كذبوا بآياتنا واستكبروا عنها أولئك أصحاب النار هم فيها خالدون

translation: So who is more unjust than one who invents a lie about Allah or denies His verses? Those will attain their portion of the decree until when Our messengers come to them to take them in death, they will say, "Where are those you used to invoke besides Allah?" They will say, "They have departed from us," and will bear witness against themselves that they were disbelievers.
interpretation: This verse highlights the severity of inventing lies about Allah or rejecting His revelations. It emphasizes that those who engage in such actions are the most unjust and will face the consequences of their deeds. When the time of their death arrives and the angels come to take their souls, they will realize the futility of their false beliefs and the deities they used to invoke besides Allah. In that moment, they will confess their disbelief and bear witness against themselves, acknowledging that they were indeed disbelievers. This interpretation underscores the importance of faith, sincerity, and accepting the truth revealed by Allah to avoid being among the unjust and facing the ultimate loss in the Hereafter.
orig: فمن أظلم ممن افترى على الله كذبا أو كذب بآياته أولئك ينالهم نصيبهم من الكتاب حتى إذا جاءتهم رسلنا يتوفونهم قالوا أين ما كنتم تدعون من دون الله قالوا ضلوا عنا وشهدوا على أنفسهم أنهم كانوا كافرين

translation: [Allah] will say, "Enter among nations which had passed on before you of jinn and mankind into the Fire." Every time a nation enters, it will curse its sister until, when they have all overtaken one another therein, the last of them will say about the first of them "Our Lord, these had misled us, so give them a double punishment of the Fire." He will say, "For each is double, but you do not know."
interpretation: This verse speaks about the fate of those who reject faith and follow falsehood. On the Day of Judgment, they will be commanded to enter Hell along with the past nations of jinn and men who were also disbelievers. As each group enters, they will curse the group that came before them for misleading them, until all are gathered together in Hell. The later generations will plead to Allah to give double punishment to the earlier ones for misguiding them, but Allah will respond that each will receive the punishment they deserve, although they may not comprehend the full extent of it. The verse highlights the severity of the consequences for rejecting the truth and following misguidance, and emphasizes Allah's ultimate justice in recompensing each soul according to their deeds.
orig: قال ادخلوا في أمم قد خلت من قبلكم من الجن والإنس في النار كلما دخلت أمة لعنت أختها حتى إذا اداركوا فيها جميعا قالت أخراهم لأولاهم ربنا هؤلاء أضلونا فآتهم عذابا ضعفا من النار قال لكل ضعف ولكن لا تعلمون

translation: And the first of them will say to the last of them, "Then you had no superiority over us, so taste the punishment for what you used to earn."
interpretation: This verse is referring to the conversations that will take place between the leaders and their followers on the Day of Judgment. The leaders, who were once followed and obeyed, will disassociate themselves from their followers and declare that they had no real power or superiority over them. The leaders will tell their followers to taste the punishment for their own deeds and earnings, emphasizing that each soul is responsible for what it has earned. This highlights the justice of Allah, as no soul will bear the burden of another, and everyone will be recompensed for their own actions.
orig: وقالت أولاهم لأخراهم فما كان لكم علينا من فضل فذوقوا العذاب بما كنتم تكسبون

translation: Indeed, those who deny Our verses and are arrogant toward them - the gates of Heaven will not be opened for them, nor will they enter Paradise until a camel enters into the eye of a needle. And thus do We recompense the criminals.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the severe consequences for those who reject and are arrogant towards Allah's signs and revelations. It states that the gates of Heaven will be closed to them and they will be denied entry into Paradise, comparing this impossibility to a camel passing through the eye of a needle. This metaphor illustrates the gravity of their disbelief and the resulting punishment. The verse also affirms that this is how Allah recompenses those who are guilty of such criminal behavior, highlighting the justice in Allah's judgment and the importance of faith and humility before His signs.
orig: إن الذين كذبوا بآياتنا واستكبروا عنها لا تفتح لهم أبواب السماء ولا يدخلون الجنة حتى يلج الجمل في سم الخياط وكذلك نجزي المجرمين

translation: They will have from Hell a bed [of fire] and from above them coverings [of fire]. And thus do We recompense the wrongdoers.
interpretation: This verse describes the terrible fate that awaits the wrongdoers and evildoers in the Hereafter. Their punishment in Hell will be all-encompassing, with the flames of the Fire surrounding them from beneath and above. The "bed" and "coverings" of Fire symbolize the inescapable nature of their torment. This imagery conveys the severity and totality of divine justice against those who have transgressed and oppressed others in this world. It serves as a powerful warning for humans to be mindful of their deeds and to strive for righteousness, as God will ultimately requite everyone according to what they have earned.
orig: لهم من جهنم مهاد ومن فوقهم غواش وكذلك نجزي الظالمين

translation: But those who believe and do righteous deeds - We charge no soul except [within] its capacity. Those are the companions of Paradise; they will abide therein eternally.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah does not burden any soul beyond its capacity. Those who have faith and do good deeds will be rewarded with Paradise, where they will reside forever. It highlights the mercy and justice of Allah, as He only expects from individuals what they are capable of doing. The verse also serves as a reminder that one's ultimate goal should be to attain Paradise through belief and righteous actions, and that this is within reach for every person, as long as they strive within their own capabilities.
orig: والذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات لا نكلف نفسا إلا وسعها أولئك أصحاب الجنة هم فيها خالدون

translation: And We will remove whatever is in their breasts of resentment, [while] flowing beneath them are rivers. And they will say, "Praise to Allah, who has guided us to this; and we would never have been guided if Allah had not guided us. Certainly the messengers of our Lord had come with the truth." And they will be called, "This is Paradise, which you have been made to inherit for what you used to do."
interpretation: This verse speaks about the state of the believers in Paradise. It indicates that Allah will remove all negative feelings, such as resentment or ill-will, from their hearts. They will experience a state of pure bliss and contentment, with rivers flowing beneath them in their eternal abode. The believers will acknowledge and praise Allah for guiding them to this blessed state, recognizing that it is only through His guidance that they were able to attain it. They will also affirm that the messengers of Allah had indeed come with the truth, guiding them to the straight path. Finally, they will be welcomed into Paradise as an inheritance, a reward for their good deeds and righteousness during their worldly life.
orig: ونزعنا ما في صدورهم من غل تجري من تحتهم الأنهار وقالوا الحمد لله الذي هدانا لهذا وما كنا لنهتدي لولا أن هدانا الله لقد جاءت رسل ربنا بالحق ونودوا أن تلكم الجنة أورثتموها بما كنتم تعملون

translation: And the companions of Paradise will call out to the companions of the Fire, "We have already found what our Lord promised us to be true. Have you found what your Lord promised to be true?" They will say, "Yes." Then an announcer will announce among them, "The curse of Allah shall be upon the wrongdoers."
interpretation: This verse highlights the stark contrast between the fate of the believers and the disbelievers in the Hereafter. The people of Paradise will affirm that Allah's promise of reward was true, while the people of Hell will admit that His warning of punishment was also true. This serves as a reminder that the choices we make in this life have eternal consequences. The verse also emphasizes Allah's justice, as the wrongdoers who rejected faith and transgressed against His laws will be condemned and cursed for their actions.
orig: ونادى أصحاب الجنة أصحاب النار أن قد وجدنا ما وعدنا ربنا حقا فهل وجدتم ما وعد ربكم حقا قالوا نعم فأذن مؤذن بينهم أن لعنة الله على الظالمين

translation: Those who hinder [people] from the way of Allah and seek to make it [seem] deviant while they are, concerning the Hereafter, disbelievers.
interpretation: This verse refers to those who actively work against the path of Allah and try to mislead others from following it. They reject the concept of the Hereafter and the accountability that comes with it. Their disbelief in the afterlife is tied to their actions in hindering others from the straight path. They not only disbelieve themselves but also seek to create doubts and confusion in others, attempting to make the way of Allah seem crooked or deviant. This highlights the severity of their actions and the consequences they will face in the Hereafter for their disbelief and for leading others astray.
orig: الذين يصدون عن سبيل الله ويبغونها عوجا وهم بالآخرة كافرون

translation: And between them will be a partition, and on [its] elevations are men who recognize all by their mark. And they call out to the companions of Paradise, "Peace be upon you." They have not [yet] entered it, but they long intensely.
interpretation: This verse refers to the people of Al-A'raf, a place between Paradise and Hell. They are the people whose good deeds and bad deeds are equal, so they are neither admitted to Paradise nor cast into Hell. They recognize the people of Paradise by their faces that are bright with the light of faith and good deeds. They will call out to the people of Paradise, greeting them with peace, even though they themselves have not yet entered it. However, they hope and long to enter Paradise by the mercy of Allah.
orig: وبينهما حجاب وعلى الأعراف رجال يعرفون كلا بسيماهم ونادوا أصحاب الجنة أن سلام عليكم لم يدخلوها وهم يطمعون

translation: And when their eyes are turned towards the companions of the Fire, they say: "Our Lord! Place us not with the people who are Zalimun (polytheists and wrong-doers).
interpretation: This verse speaks to the fear and desperation of those who, upon seeing the people condemned to Hell, plead with Allah not to be counted among the wrongdoers and placed in the Fire alongside them. It highlights the recognition, in that moment, of the severity of punishment that awaits the evildoers, and the urgent desire to be spared such a fate by Allah's mercy. The verse also emphasizes the importance of living righteously and avoiding the company and deeds of the unjust, so as not to share in their ultimate condemnation.
orig: وإذا صرفت أبصارهم تلقاء أصحاب النار قالوا ربنا لا تجعلنا مع القوم الظالمين

translation: And the companions of the heights will call to men [within Hell] whom they recognize by their mark, saying, "Of no avail to you was your gathering and [the fact] that you were arrogant."
interpretation: This verse is referring to the people of Al-A'raf, a place between Paradise and Hell. They will call out to the people of Hell, whom they recognize by their appearance, rebuking them that neither their large numbers nor their arrogance benefited them in the end. It emphasizes that worldly power, wealth, and pride are ultimately meaningless in the face of God's judgment. The people of Al-A'raf are giving a lesson that righteousness, humility, and faith are what truly matter for one's ultimate fate in the Hereafter.
orig: ونادى أصحاب الأعراف رجالا يعرفونهم بسيماهم قالوا ما أغنى عنكم جمعكم وما كنتم تستكبرون

translation: Are these the ones whom you swore that Allah would never show them mercy? [To them it will be said], "Enter Paradise, no fear will there be concerning you, nor will you grieve."
interpretation: This verse is a rebuke to those who arrogantly assumed that certain individuals would never receive Allah's mercy and be admitted into Paradise. It emphasizes that Allah's mercy and forgiveness are boundless, and that He alone decides who will enter Paradise. The verse also serves as a comfort to the believers, assuring them that they need not fear or grieve if they have faith and do righteous deeds, for Allah's mercy will encompass them. It highlights the importance of humility, and cautions against passing judgment on others or assuming that anyone is beyond the reach of Allah's grace.
orig: أهؤلاء الذين أقسمتم لا ينالهم الله برحمة ادخلوا الجنة لا خوف عليكم ولا أنتم تحزنون

translation: And the companions of the Fire will call to the companions of Paradise, "Pour upon us some water or from whatever Allah has provided you." They will say, "Indeed, Allah has forbidden them both to the disbelievers."
interpretation: This verse highlights the stark contrast between the fate of the believers and the disbelievers in the afterlife. The people of Hell, in their desperation and anguish, will plead with the people of Paradise to share with them some water or other provisions that Allah has bestowed upon them. However, the people of Paradise will respond by stating that Allah has prohibited the blessings of Paradise from the disbelievers. This serves as a reminder that the choices we make in this life have eternal consequences, and that the ultimate reward or punishment lies with Allah alone.
orig: ونادى أصحاب النار أصحاب الجنة أن أفيضوا علينا من الماء أو مما رزقكم الله قالوا إن الله حرمهما على الكافرين

translation: Those who took their religion as distraction and amusement and whom the worldly life deluded - so today We will forget them just as they forgot the meeting of this Day of theirs and for having rejected Our verses.
interpretation: This verse is a warning to those who treat religion as a mere pastime or entertainment, allowing themselves to be deceived by the temporary pleasures and distractions of this worldly life. As a consequence of their negligence and rejection of God's signs, they will be forgotten by God on the Day of Judgment, just as they had forgotten and failed to prepare for that inevitable encounter. It emphasizes the importance of taking one's faith seriously, living conscientiously, and not being misled by the fleeting nature of this world at the expense of one's eternal well-being in the Hereafter.
orig: الذين اتخذوا دينهم لهوا ولعبا وغرتهم الحياة الدنيا فاليوم ننساهم كما نسوا لقاء يومهم هذا وما كانوا بآياتنا يجحدون

translation: And indeed, We have brought them a Book which We have explained in detail with knowledge, as a guidance and a mercy for a people who believe.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the Qur'an is a divine revelation that has been sent down by Allah as a guidance and mercy for those who believe. The Book, referring to the Qur'an, has been explained in detail with the knowledge and wisdom of Allah, making it clear and easy to understand for those who seek guidance. The Qur'an serves as a comprehensive guide for believers, providing them with the knowledge and instructions they need to lead a righteous life and attain success in both this world and the hereafter. It is a mercy from Allah, as it offers hope, comfort, and salvation to those who follow its teachings sincerely.
orig: ولقد جئناهم بكتاب فصلناه على علم هدى ورحمة لقوم يؤمنون

translation: Do they await but its interpretation? The Day its interpretation comes those who had ignored it before will say, "The messengers of our Lord had come with the truth, so are there now any intercessors to intercede for us or could we be sent back to do other than we used to do?" They will have lost themselves, and lost from them is what they used to invent.
interpretation: This verse warns that those who reject the truth of the Quran in this life will realize their error on the Day of Judgment, but it will be too late. They will wish for another chance or for someone to intercede on their behalf, but they will have squandered their opportunity. The false beliefs they invented and clung to in the world will be of no avail. It conveys that faith and good deeds must be acted upon in this life, before the coming of death and judgment, after which there is no return or repentance.
orig: هل ينظرون إلا تأويله يوم يأتي تأويله يقول الذين نسوه من قبل قد جاءت رسل ربنا بالحق فهل لنا من شفعاء فيشفعوا لنا أو نرد فنعمل غير الذي كنا نعمل قد خسروا أنفسهم وضل عنهم ما كانوا يفترون

translation: Indeed, your Lord is Allah, who created the heavens and the earth in six days and then established Himself above the Throne. He covers the night with the day, [another night] chasing it rapidly; and [He created] the sun, the moon, and the stars, subjected by His command. Unquestionably, His is the creation and the command; blessed is Allah, Lord of the worlds.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's power and sovereignty as the Creator and Sustainer of the universe. It highlights that Allah created the heavens and the earth in six days, demonstrating His ability to bring into existence such a vast and complex creation. The verse then mentions that Allah established Himself above the Throne, which symbolizes His authority and control over all creation. The alternation of night and day, the movement of the celestial bodies, and their subjugation to Allah's command further underscore His omnipotence and the perfection of His design. The verse concludes by affirming that both the creation and the command belong to Allah alone, and He is blessed as the Lord of all the worlds, deserving of all praise and worship.
orig: إن ربكم الله الذي خلق السماوات والأرض في ستة أيام ثم استوى على العرش يغشي الليل النهار يطلبه حثيثا والشمس والقمر والنجوم مسخرات بأمره ألا له الخلق والأمر تبارك الله رب العالمين

translation: Call upon your Lord humbly and privately. Indeed, He does not like the transgressors.
interpretation: This verse encourages believers to supplicate to Allah with humility and sincerity, both in public and private. It emphasizes the importance of maintaining a balance in supplication, without transgressing the limits set by Allah. The verse suggests that one should approach Allah with a sense of humility, recognizing His greatness and our own weakness. It also implies that our supplications should be made with sincerity and not for show or to impress others. Allah does not like those who transgress the boundaries of what is acceptable in supplication, such as asking for something sinful or being arrogant in one's approach. The verse serves as a reminder to cultivate a deep, personal relationship with Allah through humble and sincere prayer.
orig: ادعوا ربكم تضرعا وخفية إنه لا يحب المعتدين

translation: And cause not corruption upon the earth after its reformation. And invoke Him in fear and aspiration. Indeed, the mercy of Allah is near to the doers of good.
interpretation: This verse is a reminder from Allah to mankind not to spread corruption and mischief on earth after He has set it in order and made it suitable for life. It encourages people to call upon Allah with both fear of His punishment and hope in His mercy and reward. The verse emphasizes that Allah's mercy is always close to those who do good deeds and live righteously, following His commands and avoiding what He has prohibited. It motivates believers to strive for excellence in their conduct and dealings, knowing that Allah's acceptance and blessings are within reach for those who sincerely seek to please Him through their actions.
orig: ولا تفسدوا في الأرض بعد إصلاحها وادعوه خوفا وطمعا إن رحمت الله قريب من المحسنين

translation: And it is He who sends the winds as good tidings before His mercy until, when they have carried heavy rainclouds, We drive them to a dead land and We send down rain therein and bring forth thereby [some] of all the fruits. Thus will We bring forth the dead; perhaps you may be reminded.
interpretation: This verse is a reminder of Allah's power and mercy. The winds are sent as a sign of His mercy, carrying the heavy rainclouds to bring life-giving water to dead lands. This is a metaphor for the resurrection of the dead on the Day of Judgment. Just as Allah brings forth fruits and vegetation from the dead earth after the rain, He will bring forth the dead from their graves. This verse encourages reflection on the signs of Allah's power and the inevitability of the resurrection and judgment, urging people to be mindful of their actions in this life.
orig: وهو الذي يرسل الرياح بشرا بين يدي رحمته حتى إذا أقلت سحابا ثقالا سقناه لبلد ميت فأنزلنا به الماء فأخرجنا به من كل الثمرات كذلك نخرج الموتى لعلكم تذكرون

translation: The good land - its vegetation emerges by permission of its Lord; but that which is bad - nothing emerges except sparsely. Thus do We diversify the signs for a people who are grateful.
interpretation: This verse draws a comparison between two types of land - the fertile land which by Allah's grace brings forth abundant vegetation, and the barren land which produces little even with effort. The "good land" symbolizes the heart of the believer which, illuminated by faith, produces an abundance of good deeds. The barren land represents the heart of the disbeliever which is unreceptive to faith and therefore produces little good, if any. Allah presents such parables and signs in diverse ways so that those who are grateful may reflect and understand His message.
orig: والبلد الطيب يخرج نباته بإذن ربه والذي خبث لا يخرج إلا نكدا كذلك نصرف الآيات لقوم يشكرون

translation: Indeed, We sent Noah to his people, and he said, "O my people, worship Allah; you have no deity other than Him. Indeed, I fear for you the punishment of a tremendous Day."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of worshipping Allah alone and avoiding idolatry. It serves as a reminder that those who fail to worship Allah and instead turn to false deities will face severe consequences on the Day of Judgment. The verse also highlights the role of prophets, such as Noah, who were sent to guide their people to the straight path and warn them of the dangers of polytheism. It underscores the gravity of the message that prophets conveyed to their communities and the urgent need for people to heed their warnings and embrace monotheism before it is too late.
orig: لقد أرسلنا نوحا إلى قومه فقال يا قوم اعبدوا الله ما لكم من إله غيره إني أخاف عليكم عذاب يوم عظيم

translation: The eminent among his people said, "Indeed, we see you in clear error."
interpretation: This verse illustrates the common reaction of those in power towards the prophets and messengers of Allah. They accused the prophet of being misguided and in clear error, as his message challenged their traditional beliefs, customs, and way of life. This accusation stems from their arrogance, ignorance, and attachment to the status quo. They failed to recognize the truth and wisdom in the prophet's teachings, as they were blinded by their own desires and interests. The verse highlights the challenges faced by the prophets in conveying the divine message to their people, and the resistance they encountered from those in authority who sought to maintain their power and influence.
orig: قال الملأ من قومه إنا لنراك في ضلال مبين

translation: He said, "O my people, there is no error in me, but I am a messenger from the Lord of the worlds."
interpretation: In this verse, the prophet is asserting his truthfulness and sincerity to his people. He is declaring that he is not misguided or deluded, but rather he is a messenger sent by Allah, the Lord of all creation. This emphasizes the divine source of his message and his role as a prophet chosen by God to guide humanity. It is a powerful statement of his conviction and his commitment to conveying the revelation he has received, even in the face of opposition or disbelief from his community.
orig: قال يا قوم ليس بي ضلالة ولكني رسول من رب العالمين

translation: I convey to you the messages of my Lord and advise you, and I know from Allah what you do not know.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the role of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) as a messenger of Allah. He is not only conveying the divine message, but also sincerely advising and guiding people based on the knowledge and wisdom bestowed upon him by Allah. The Prophet has access to divine knowledge that ordinary people do not possess. This special knowledge allows him to guide people in the best possible way and provide them with teachings and insights that they could not attain on their own. The verse underscores the importance of following the Prophet's teachings and trusting his advice, as it is divinely inspired and comes from a source of supreme knowledge and wisdom.
orig: أبلغكم رسالات ربي وأنصح لكم وأعلم من الله ما لا تعلمون

translation: Or do you wonder that there has come to you a reminder from your Lord through a man from among you, that he may warn you and that you may fear Allah so you might receive mercy?
interpretation: This verse is addressing the disbelievers who are surprised and skeptical that Allah has sent a messenger from among them to deliver His message. It emphasizes that the purpose of sending a prophet is to warn people, guide them to righteousness, and encourage them to be mindful of Allah so that they may attain His mercy. The verse implies that there should be no astonishment in a man being chosen for this task, as Allah selects prophets from among the people to whom they are sent, so they can effectively convey the message in a relatable manner.
orig: أوعجبتم أن جاءكم ذكر من ربكم على رجل منكم لينذركم ولتتقوا ولعلكم ترحمون

translation: But they denied him, so We saved him and those with him in the ship and drowned those who denied Our signs. Indeed, they were a blind people.
interpretation: This verse highlights the consequences of denying God's messages and His prophets. Those who reject the truth and persist in their disbelief will face divine retribution, while the believers who follow the guidance will be saved from destruction. The verse also emphasizes that spiritual blindness, the inability to perceive and accept the truth, leads to one's downfall. It serves as a reminder for people to open their hearts to the signs of God and embrace the guidance provided by His messengers to attain salvation and avoid the fate of those who are "blind" to the truth.
orig: فكذبوه فأنجيناه والذين معه في الفلك وأغرقنا الذين كذبوا بآياتنا إنهم كانوا قوما عمين

translation: And to the 'Aad [We sent] their brother Hud. He said, "O my people, worship Allah; you have no deity other than Him. Then will you not fear Him?"
interpretation: This verse is a call to the people of 'Aad to worship Allah alone and abandon the worship of false deities. Hud, as their brother and prophet, reminds them that Allah is the only true God worthy of worship, and that they should fear Him and be mindful of their actions. The verse emphasizes the importance of monotheism and the consequences of polytheism or idolatry. It also highlights the role of prophets in guiding their communities to the right path and warning them against disobedience to Allah.
orig: وإلى عاد أخاهم هودا قال يا قوم اعبدوا الله ما لكم من إله غيره أفلا تتقون

translation: The eminent ones who disbelieved among his people said, "Indeed, we see you in foolishness, and indeed, we think you are of the liars."
interpretation: This verse shows the arrogance and stubbornness of the disbelievers who reject the message brought by the prophet despite its clear truth. They accuse the prophet of foolishness and lying, reflecting their own ignorance and refusal to acknowledge the truth. It highlights the challenges and opposition that prophets face from the elite and powerful members of their society who feel threatened by the message of monotheism and righteousness. The verse also serves as a consolation to the Prophet Muhammad, letting him know that other prophets faced similar accusations and hostility from their people.
orig: قال الملأ الذين كفروا من قومه إنا لنراك في سفاهة وإنا لنظنك من الكاذبين

translation: He said, "O my people, there is no foolishness in me, but I am a messenger from the Lord of the worlds."
interpretation: In this verse, the prophet is asserting his status as a messenger of God to his people, who may have doubted or rejected his message. He denies any foolishness or unsoundness of mind on his part, making it clear that his role as a prophet comes from divine appointment by the Lord of all creation. This emphasizes the gravity and truth of the message he brings, as it is not from his own whims but from the highest authority. The prophet urges his people to recognize his legitimacy and the importance of heeding the revelation he conveys to them from their Creator.
orig: قال يا قوم ليس بي سفاهة ولكني رسول من رب العالمين

translation: I convey to you the messages of my Lord, and I am to you a trustworthy adviser.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the role of the prophets as messengers of God, whose duty is to faithfully convey His message to their people. The prophets are described as being sincere and trustworthy in their advice and guidance, having the best interests of their followers at heart. They do not alter or conceal any part of the divine revelation, but deliver it as it was revealed to them. This highlights the importance of the prophets as reliable sources of spiritual knowledge and moral guidance for mankind.
orig: أبلغكم رسالات ربي وأنا لكم ناصح أمين

translation: Or do you wonder that there has come to you a reminder from your Lord through a man from among you, that he may warn you? And remember when He made you successors after the people of Noah and increased you in stature extensively. So remember the favors of Allah that you might succeed.
interpretation: This verse is a reminder to the people to be grateful for the blessings and favors bestowed upon them by Allah. It emphasizes that Allah has sent a messenger from among them to warn and guide them towards the right path. The verse also highlights how Allah made them successors after the people of Noah, granting them power and authority on earth, and blessed them with physical strength and stature. By remembering and appreciating these favors, and following the guidance of the messenger, they may attain success in this world and the hereafter.
orig: أوعجبتم أن جاءكم ذكر من ربكم على رجل منكم لينذركم واذكروا إذ جعلكم خلفاء من بعد قوم نوح وزادكم في الخلق بسطة فاذكروا آلاء الله لعلكم تفلحون

translation: They said, "Have you come to us that we should worship Allah alone and leave what our fathers have worshipped? Then bring us what you promise us, if you should be of the truthful."
interpretation: This verse reflects the stubborn attitude of the disbelievers towards the message of worshipping Allah alone. They challenge the Prophet or messenger to bring the punishment that he warns them of for rejecting the message, as they are not willing to abandon the false gods and idols that their forefathers used to worship. It shows their blind following of ancestral traditions and their arrogant demand for proof or signs, doubting the truthfulness of the messenger. The verse highlights the typical response of those who are deeply entrenched in polytheism and unwilling to change their ways despite the clear call to worship the One True God.
orig: قالوا أجئتنا لنعبد الله وحده ونذر ما كان يعبد آباؤنا فأتنا بما تعدنا إن كنت من الصادقين

translation: He said, "There has already fallen upon you anger and wrath from your Lord. Do you dispute with me concerning mere names you and your forefathers have made up for which Allah has not sent down any authority? So wait; I am waiting with you."
interpretation: This verse is a rebuke to those who argue about matters of faith based on man-made names and labels, rather than on the truth revealed by Allah. It emphasizes that such arguments are futile and baseless, as they are not supported by any divine authority. The verse also conveys a warning that those who engage in such disputes have already earned Allah's anger and should expect His punishment. It calls on them to desist from their wrongful ways and instead wait for the ultimate judgment, just as the Prophet and the believers wait patiently for Allah's decree.
orig: قال قد وقع عليكم من ربكم رجس وغضب أتجادلونني في أسماء سميتموها أنتم وآباؤكم ما نزل الله بها من سلطان فانتظروا إني معكم من المنتظرين

translation: So We saved him and those with him by mercy from Us. And We eliminated those who denied Our signs, and they were not [at all] believers.
interpretation: This verse speaks to the ultimate fate of those who reject God's signs and messages. While God saves the believers through His mercy, those who persist in disbelief and denial of the truth will face destruction. The verse emphasizes that their disbelief was a choice they made, as "they were not [at all] believers" to begin with. It serves as a warning that rejecting faith has severe consequences, while also highlighting God's mercy towards the faithful who are saved from such a fate.
orig: فأنجيناه والذين معه برحمة منا وقطعنا دابر الذين كذبوا بآياتنا وما كانوا مؤمنين

translation: And to Thamud [We sent] their brother Salih. He said, "O my people, worship Allah; you have no deity other than Him. There has come to you clear evidence from your Lord. This is the she-camel of Allah [sent] to you as a sign. So leave her to eat within Allah's land and do not touch her with harm, lest there seize you a painful punishment.
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of worshipping Allah alone and heeding the warnings of His prophets. The people of Thamud were sent a clear sign in the form of a miraculous she-camel, which was meant to be a reminder of Allah's power and a test of their obedience. By harming the camel or refusing to let it graze freely, they would be inviting Allah's punishment upon themselves. The verse emphasizes that there is no deity worthy of worship except Allah and that ignoring His signs and disobeying His prophets will lead to severe consequences in this life and the hereafter.
orig: وإلى ثمود أخاهم صالحا قال يا قوم اعبدوا الله ما لكم من إله غيره قد جاءتكم بينة من ربكم هذه ناقة الله لكم آية فذروها تأكل في أرض الله ولا تمسوها بسوء فيأخذكم عذاب أليم

translation: And remember how He made you successors after 'Aad and settled you in the land, [and] you take for yourselves palaces from its plains and carve from the mountains, homes. Then remember the favors of Allah and do not commit abuse on the earth, spreading corruption.
interpretation: This verse reminds us of Allah's favor upon the people, making them successors on earth after the destruction of the previous nation of 'Aad. It highlights how Allah granted them the ability to build palaces in the plains and carve homes in the mountains, displaying their power and capabilities. However, it also serves as a warning not to become arrogant and spread corruption on earth due to these blessings. Rather, we should remember Allah's favors with gratitude and humility, using our abilities for good and righteousness, not oppression and transgression.
orig: واذكروا إذ جعلكم خلفاء من بعد عاد وبوأكم في الأرض تتخذون من سهولها قصورا وتنحتون الجبال بيوتا فاذكروا آلاء الله ولا تعثوا في الأرض مفسدين

translation: The eminent ones who were arrogant among his people said to those who were oppressed - to those who believed among them, "Do you [actually] know that Saleh is sent from his Lord?" They said, "Indeed we, in that with which he was sent, are believers."
interpretation: This verse highlights the arrogance and disbelief of the elite among the people of Prophet Saleh (peace be upon him). They tried to create doubt in the minds of the oppressed believers by questioning the authenticity of Saleh's prophethood. However, the believers remained steadfast in their faith and affirmed their belief in the message with which Saleh was sent. This demonstrates the unwavering conviction of true believers, even in the face of opposition and skepticism from those in positions of power and influence.
orig: قال الملأ الذين استكبروا من قومه للذين استضعفوا لمن آمن منهم أتعلمون أن صالحا مرسل من ربه قالوا إنا بما أرسل به مؤمنون

translation: Those who were arrogant said, "Indeed we, in that which you have believed, are disbelievers."
interpretation: This verse highlights the arrogance and disbelief of those who reject the message of Islam despite clear signs and evidence. It shows their stubbornness in clinging to their false beliefs and their refusal to humble themselves before the truth. The verse also implies that those who have believed in the message have done so based on clear proofs and conviction, while the disbelievers' rejection stems from their arrogance and pride. This attitude ultimately leads to their spiritual downfall and loss in both this world and the hereafter.
orig: قال الذين استكبروا إنا بالذي آمنتم به كافرون

translation: But they hamstrung the she-camel and were insolent toward the command of their Lord and said, "O Salih, bring us what you promise us, if you should be of the messengers."
interpretation: This verse is a stark warning against defying the commands of Allah and His messengers. The people of Thamud, to whom Prophet Salih was sent, arrogantly demanded that he bring upon them the punishment he had warned them about if they did not believe, as a challenge to his prophethood. Their act of hamstringing the she-camel, a miracle sent by Allah as a sign, demonstrated their utter disregard and contempt for the divine message. It reflects the depths of insolence and rebellion the human soul can descend to when it is devoid of faith and humility before the Almighty Creator. The consequence for their defiance was a severe punishment that decimated their civilization. The verse thus serves as a reminder for believers to always submit obediently to Allah's commands and honor His signs and messengers, lest they incur His wrath.
orig: فعقروا الناقة وعتوا عن أمر ربهم وقالوا يا صالح ائتنا بما تعدنا إن كنت من المرسلين

translation: So the earthquake seized them, and they became within their home [corpses] fallen prone.
interpretation: This verse refers to the punishment that befell the people of Thamud, who rejected the message of their prophet, Salih. They were seized by a powerful earthquake that destroyed their dwellings and left them lifeless, lying face down in their homes. It serves as a reminder of the consequences of disobedience to Allah and rejection of His messengers. The verse emphasizes the suddenness and severity of the divine retribution, as the people were caught off guard and perished in an instant, becoming a cautionary tale for future generations.
orig: فأخذتهم الرجفة فأصبحوا في دارهم جاثمين

translation: Then he turned away from them and said, "O my people, I have certainly conveyed to you the message of my Lord and advised you, but you do not like advisors."
interpretation: In this verse, the prophet is expressing his disappointment and frustration with his people who have refused to listen to his message and advice. Despite his sincere efforts to guide them to the right path, they have turned away from him and rejected his wisdom. The prophet is reminding them that he has fulfilled his duty of conveying the message of Allah and offering them sincere advice, but they have chosen to ignore it. This verse highlights the importance of being open to good advice and the consequences of rejecting it. It also emphasizes the role of prophets as messengers and advisors to their people, even in the face of rejection and opposition.
orig: فتولى عنهم وقال يا قوم لقد أبلغتكم رسالة ربي ونصحت لكم ولكن لا تحبون الناصحين

translation: And [mention] Lot, when he said to his people, "Do you commit immorality such as no one has preceded you with from among the worlds?
interpretation: This verse is a strong condemnation of the homosexual behavior practiced by the people of Lot. It emphasizes the gravity and unnaturalness of their actions by stating that no one in the world had committed such immorality before them. The verse implies that homosexuality is a severe transgression against the natural order established by Allah. It serves as a warning to all people to avoid this major sin and deviance which brings about the wrath and punishment of Allah, as was ultimately faced by the people of Lot who were destroyed for their persistence in this vice.
orig: ولوطا إذ قال لقومه أتأتون الفاحشة ما سبقكم بها من أحد من العالمين

translation: Indeed, you approach men with desire, instead of women. Rather, you are a transgressing people.
interpretation: This verse is condemning homosexual behavior among men. It suggests that engaging in sexual acts with other men instead of women is a transgression and an overstepping of the natural bounds set by God. The use of the word "musrifun" (translated as transgressing) implies excessiveness and going beyond what is permissible. This verse makes clear that in Islam, homosexual relations are considered sinful and a serious violation of God's law and the natural order He has established.
orig: إنكم لتأتون الرجال شهوة من دون النساء بل أنتم قوم مسرفون

translation: And the answer of his people was not but that they said, "Evict them from your city! Indeed, they are men who keep themselves pure."
interpretation: This verse is referring to the people of Lut (Lot) and their response to his preaching against their immoral practices. Instead of heeding his warnings and reforming their ways, they mocked and threatened Lut and the believers, accusing them of being self-righteous and "too pure" for their society. The people's reaction demonstrates their arrogance, stubbornness, and refusal to abandon their sinful lifestyle, even when confronted with divine guidance. It also highlights the challenges faced by prophets and believers when calling people to righteousness in a corrupt environment. The verse serves as a reminder that those who stand firm in their faith and morality may face rejection, ridicule, and even persecution from those who are deeply entrenched in their wrongdoing.
orig: وما كان جواب قومه إلا أن قالوا أخرجوهم من قريتكم إنهم أناس يتطهرون

translation: So We saved him and his family, except for his wife; she was of those who remained [with the evildoers].
interpretation: This verse highlights the mercy and justice of Allah. He saved the Prophet Lut (Lot) and his believing family members from the punishment that befell his people due to their immoral actions and rejection of Allah's message. However, Lut's wife was not saved as she aligned herself with the wrongdoers and did not believe in Allah's warnings. This demonstrates that each individual is responsible for their own faith and actions, and that ultimately, Allah's judgment is based on one's choices and deeds, not on familial ties or relationships.
orig: فأنجيناه وأهله إلا امرأته كانت من الغابرين

translation: And We rained upon them a rain [of stones], so see how was the end of the criminals.
interpretation: This verse serves as a warning and reminder of the consequences that befall those who engage in criminal and sinful behavior. It emphasizes that God's punishment is severe and that those who transgress against His laws and commit evil deeds will ultimately face a terrible fate. The verse encourages people to reflect on the past nations that were destroyed due to their wrongdoings and to take heed of their example. It also highlights the power and authority of God, who is capable of inflicting such punishment upon those who deserve it. The verse ultimately serves to deter people from engaging in criminal behavior and encourages them to follow the path of righteousness.
orig: وأمطرنا عليهم مطرا فانظر كيف كان عاقبة المجرمين

translation: And to [the people of] Madyan [We sent] their brother Shu'ayb. He said, "O my people, worship Allah; you have no deity other than Him. There has come to you clear evidence from your Lord. So fulfill the measure and weight and do not deprive people of their due and cause not corruption upon the earth after its reformation. That is better for you, if you should be believers."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of worshipping Allah alone and following the guidance sent through His prophets. It calls for honesty and fairness in business dealings, particularly in matters of weights and measures. The verse also warns against causing corruption and mischief on earth after it has been set in order by Allah's guidance. This is a reminder that as believers, it is our responsibility to maintain justice and righteousness in society, as this is what pleases Allah and benefits us in both this world and the hereafter.
orig: وإلى مدين أخاهم شعيبا قال يا قوم اعبدوا الله ما لكم من إله غيره قد جاءتكم بينة من ربكم فأوفوا الكيل والميزان ولا تبخسوا الناس أشياءهم ولا تفسدوا في الأرض بعد إصلاحها ذلكم خير لكم إن كنتم مؤمنين

translation: And do not sit on every path, threatening and averting from the way of Allah those who believe in Him, seeking to make it [seem] deviant. And remember when you were few and He increased you. And see how was the end of the corrupters.
interpretation: This verse is a warning against those who actively try to prevent others from following the path of Allah. It reminds us that such people, who threaten and mislead believers seeking to make the way of Allah seem crooked or wrong, will face consequences for their actions. The verse also encourages believers to remember how Allah has supported and increased them in number, even when they were few. This serves as a reminder of Allah's favor and a warning to those who seek to corrupt and lead others astray from His path. Ultimately, the verse urges us to consider the fate of those who spread corruption and mischief, suggesting that their end will be one of loss and regret.
orig: ولا تقعدوا بكل صراط توعدون وتصدون عن سبيل الله من آمن به وتبغونها عوجا واذكروا إذ كنتم قليلا فكثركم وانظروا كيف كان عاقبة المفسدين

translation: And if a group among you believes in that with which I have been sent and a group does not believe, then be patient until Allah judges between us, and He is the best of judges.
interpretation: This verse is addressing the Prophet Muhammad and his followers, acknowledging that there will be some people who believe in his message and others who do not. It advises the believers to remain patient and steadfast in the face of this disbelief, trusting that Allah will ultimately judge between the two groups and that His judgment is the best and most just. This highlights the importance of patience, faith, and trust in Allah's plan, even in the face of opposition or adversity.
orig: وإن كان طائفة منكم آمنوا بالذي أرسلت به وطائفة لم يؤمنوا فاصبروا حتى يحكم الله بيننا وهو خير الحاكمين

translation: The eminent ones who were arrogant among his people said, "We will surely evict you, O Shu'ayb, and those who have believed with you from our city, or you must return to our religion." He said, "Even if we were unwilling?"
interpretation: This verse highlights the arrogance and oppression of the elite in Shu'ayb's community. They threaten to exile Shu'ayb and his followers unless they conform to the prevailing religious practices, even against their will. Shu'ayb's response, "Even if we were unwilling?", emphasizes his steadfastness and unwillingness to compromise his faith and principles under duress. This passage illustrates the challenges faced by prophets and believers in the face of societal pressure and persecution, and the importance of remaining committed to one's beliefs despite opposition.
orig: قال الملأ الذين استكبروا من قومه لنخرجنك يا شعيب والذين آمنوا معك من قريتنا أو لتعودن في ملتنا قال أولو كنا كارهين

translation: We would have certainly fabricated a lie against Allah if we returned to your religion after Allah has saved us from it. And it is not for us to return to it except that Allah, our Lord, should will. Our Lord has encompassed all things in knowledge. Upon Allah we have relied. Our Lord, decide between us and our people in truth, and You are the best of those who give decision.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the firm resolve of the believers in staying true to their faith, even in the face of pressure or temptation to revert to their previous beliefs. It highlights their complete trust in Allah's will and their reliance on Him to guide them through any challenges or conflicts they may face with their people. The believers recognize that it is only by Allah's grace that they have been saved from their previous ways, and they cannot return to those ways unless Allah wills it. They seek Allah's judgment and decision in their affairs, acknowledging Him as the ultimate authority and the best of judges.
orig: قد افترينا على الله كذبا إن عدنا في ملتكم بعد إذ نجانا الله منها وما يكون لنا أن نعود فيها إلا أن يشاء الله ربنا وسع ربنا كل شيء علما على الله توكلنا ربنا افتح بيننا وبين قومنا بالحق وأنت خير الفاتحين

translation: The chiefs of his people who disbelieved said: "If you follow Shu'aib, you shall then most surely be losers"
interpretation: This verse highlights the opposition and disbelief of the leaders of Prophet Shu'aib's community towards his message. They tried to discourage the people from following Shu'aib by claiming that doing so would lead to loss and ruin. This reflects a common pattern where those in power resist change and reforms brought by prophets, as it threatens their authority and privileges. They use fear-mongering and false warnings to maintain their grip on the masses. However, the Qur'an makes it clear that the real loss is in rejecting divine guidance and adhering to corrupt leadership. Following the truth, even if it goes against the majority, is ultimately the path to success and salvation.
orig: وقال الملأ الذين كفروا من قومه لئن اتبعتم شعيبا إنكم إذا لخاسرون

translation: So the earthquake seized them, and they became within their home [corpses] fallen prone.
interpretation: This verse refers to a punishment that befell a group of people who rejected the message of their prophet. The "earthquake" mentioned here could be a literal earthquake or a metaphorical one, representing a severe punishment or calamity that struck them suddenly. As a result, they perished and their bodies were left lifeless in their very homes, in a state of submission and helplessness. This verse serves as a warning to those who oppose God's message and persist in wrongdoing, reminding them that divine retribution can be swift and devastating, leaving the evildoers humbled and destroyed, even within the confines of their own homes where they thought they were safe and secure.
orig: فأخذتهم الرجفة فأصبحوا في دارهم جاثمين

translation: Those who denied Shu'ayb became as if they had never resided there. Those who denied Shu'ayb - it was they who were the losers.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the consequences of rejecting the message of Prophet Shu'ayb. Those who denied his teachings and warnings were ultimately the ones who suffered the greatest loss. They were destroyed and their dwelling places were left in ruins, as if they had never existed there. This serves as a reminder that denying the truth and the guidance of Allah's messengers leads to destruction and eternal loss in the Hereafter. The fate of the deniers of Shu'ayb is a lesson for all people to heed the call of the prophets and follow the straight path to attain success and salvation.
orig: الذين كذبوا شعيبا كأن لم يغنوا فيها الذين كذبوا شعيبا كانوا هم الخاسرين

translation: Then he turned away from them and said, "O my people, I have certainly conveyed to you the messages of my Lord and advised you, so how could I grieve for a disbelieving people?"
interpretation: In this verse, the prophet is expressing his disappointment and sadness over his people's rejection of his message despite his sincere efforts to guide them. He is essentially saying that he has done his duty by conveying God's message and offering them sincere advice, so he should not feel any sorrow or regret over their choice to persist in disbelief. The verse highlights the prophet's deep concern for his people's spiritual welfare, but also his recognition that he cannot force them to believe and that ultimately, they are responsible for their own choices and the consequences that follow.
orig: فتولى عنهم وقال يا قوم لقد أبلغتكم رسالات ربي ونصحت لكم فكيف آسى على قوم كافرين

translation: And We did not send a prophet to a town but We seized its people with misery and adversity that they might humble themselves [to Allah].
interpretation: This verse highlights a pattern in the way Allah deals with nations to whom He sends prophets. When a prophet is sent to a town or a nation, Allah often tests the people with hardships, such as poverty, illness, or other difficulties. The purpose of these trials is to encourage the people to turn to Allah in humility and submission, recognizing their weakness and need for His mercy and guidance. Through these challenges, people have the opportunity to grow in faith, patience, and reliance upon Allah. This verse serves as a reminder that hardships in life can be a means of spiritual purification and growth, and that turning to Allah in times of difficulty is essential for believers.
orig: وما أرسلنا في قرية من نبي إلا أخذنا أهلها بالبأساء والضراء لعلهم يضرعون

translation: Then We changed the evil for the good, until they increased [in number] and said, "Our fathers [also] were touched with hardship and ease." Then We seized them suddenly while they did not perceive.
interpretation: This verse highlights the human tendency to forget Allah's blessings and take them for granted. When people are faced with difficulties, they turn to Allah for help, but when the hardships are replaced with ease and prosperity, they often attribute it to their own efforts or mere chance. They fail to recognize that both hardship and ease are from Allah, and that they should remain grateful and obedient to Him in all circumstances. As a result of their ingratitude and heedlessness, Allah may seize them with a sudden punishment when they least expect it. This serves as a reminder for believers to constantly acknowledge Allah's favors and remain steadfast in their faith, even during times of prosperity and comfort.
orig: ثم بدلنا مكان السيئة الحسنة حتى عفوا وقالوا قد مس آباءنا الضراء والسراء فأخذناهم بغتة وهم لا يشعرون

translation: And if only the people of the cities had believed and feared Allah, We would have opened upon them blessings from the heaven and the earth; but they denied [the messengers], so We seized them for what they were earning.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of faith and righteousness. It suggests that if the people of past nations had believed in Allah and followed His guidance, they would have been blessed with abundance and prosperity from the heavens and the earth. However, because they rejected the messengers and continued in their wrongdoing, Allah punished them for their misdeeds. The verse serves as a reminder that obedience to Allah leads to blessings and disobedience leads to negative consequences in this world and the hereafter.
orig: ولو أن أهل القرى آمنوا واتقوا لفتحنا عليهم بركات من السماء والأرض ولكن كذبوا فأخذناهم بما كانوا يكسبون

translation: Then, did the people of the cities feel secure from Our punishment coming to them at night while they were asleep?
interpretation: This verse is a warning to those who feel secure in their disobedience to Allah, thinking that His punishment will not come upon them unexpectedly. It reminds us that Allah's punishment can come at any time, even when people are asleep and feeling safe. The verse encourages believers to always be mindful of Allah and to strive for righteousness, never becoming complacent or assuming they are beyond His reproach. It emphasizes Allah's power and ability to send His punishment whenever He wills, so people should live in a state of cautiousness and reverence for Him.
orig: أفأمن أهل القرى أن يأتيهم بأسنا بياتا وهم نائمون

translation: Did the people of the cities feel secure from Our punishment coming to them in the morning while they were at play?
interpretation: This verse is a warning to those who are heedless and engrossed in worldly pleasures, thinking that they are safe from Allah's punishment. It reminds us that divine retribution can come at any time, even when people are distracted by amusements and feel secure in their daily lives. The verse implies that one should never become complacent or feel immune from the consequences of their actions, as Allah's judgment can be swift and unexpected. It is a call to be always mindful of our deeds and to live in a state of consciousness and submission to Allah, rather than being lost in heedlessness and play.
orig: أوأمن أهل القرى أن يأتيهم بأسنا ضحى وهم يلعبون

translation: Then did they feel secure from the plan of Allah? But no one feels secure from the plan of Allah except the losing people.
interpretation: This verse serves as a warning to those who think they can outsmart or escape the will of Allah. It emphasizes that no one should feel safe from Allah's plan or decree, as He is All-Knowing and All-Powerful. Only those who are ultimately doomed and have lost their way would foolishly believe that they can avoid the consequences of their actions or evade Allah's judgment. The verse reminds believers to remain humble, cautious, and mindful of Allah's power and wisdom at all times.
orig: أفأمنوا مكر الله فلا يأمن مكر الله إلا القوم الخاسرون

translation: Is it not a guidance for those who inherit the earth from its [previous] inhabitants that if We willed, We could afflict them for their sins? But We seal over their hearts so they do not hear.
interpretation: This verse serves as a reminder and a warning to those who come after previous generations and inherit the earth. It points out that if Allah had willed, He could have punished them for their sins just as He did with the previous inhabitants. However, because of their heedlessness and lack of faith, Allah has sealed their hearts, making them unable to comprehend and hear the truth. This emphasizes the importance of learning from the fate of past nations, being mindful of one's actions, and turning to Allah in repentance and obedience before it is too late.
orig: أولم يهد للذين يرثون الأرض من بعد أهلها أن لو نشاء أصبناهم بذنوبهم ونطبع على قلوبهم فهم لا يسمعون

translation: Those cities - We relate to you, [O Muhammad], some of their news. And certainly did their messengers come to them with clear proofs, but they were not to believe in that which they had denied before. Thus does Allah seal over the hearts of the disbelievers.
interpretation: This verse highlights the stubborn nature of the disbelievers who, despite receiving clear signs and proofs from their messengers, refused to believe in the truth due to their prior rejection. It emphasizes that their persistent denial and disbelief led to Allah sealing their hearts, making it difficult for them to accept the truth and guidance. This interpretation suggests that the disbelievers' own actions and choices played a significant role in their spiritual state, as their continuous rejection of the truth resulted in a hardening of their hearts decreed by Allah.
orig: تلك القرى نقص عليك من أنبائها ولقد جاءتهم رسلهم بالبينات فما كانوا ليؤمنوا بما كذبوا من قبل كذلك يطبع الله على قلوب الكافرين

translation: And We did not find for most of them any covenant; but indeed, We found most of them defiantly disobedient.
interpretation: This verse suggests that most people do not keep their promises or covenants with Allah. They are characterized as "fasiqeen" which means those who rebel against Allah's commands and exceed the limits set by Him. It implies that the majority of mankind is disobedient to Allah and does not fulfill the obligations and responsibilities towards Him. The verse highlights the widespread corruption and lack of integrity among people when it comes to honoring their commitments to Allah.
orig: وما وجدنا لأكثرهم من عهد وإن وجدنا أكثرهم لفاسقين

translation: Then We sent after them Moses with Our signs to Pharaoh and his establishment, but they were unjust toward them. So see how was the end of the corrupters.
interpretation: This verse highlights the story of Prophet Moses, who was sent by Allah to Pharaoh and his people with clear signs and miracles as evidence of his prophethood. However, Pharaoh and his followers responded with injustice, arrogance, and rejection of the divine message. The verse directs our attention to the fate of those who engage in corruption and wrongdoing, emphasizing that their end will be one of destruction and loss. It serves as a warning to those who oppose the truth and persist in their wrongdoing, reminding us that the consequences of such actions will ultimately lead to their downfall.
orig: ثم بعثنا من بعدهم موسى بآياتنا إلى فرعون وملئه فظلموا بها فانظر كيف كان عاقبة المفسدين

translation: And Moses said, "O Pharaoh, I am a messenger from the Lord of the worlds."
interpretation: In this verse, Moses declares his prophethood and divine mission to Pharaoh, the ruler of Egypt. It emphasizes that Moses was sent by Allah, the Lord of all creation, to convey His message and to challenge Pharaoh's claim of divinity. This declaration serves as a powerful testament to the unity and sovereignty of Allah, as well as the role of prophets in guiding humanity towards the truth. It also sets the stage for the confrontation between Moses and Pharaoh, which ultimately demonstrates the triumph of faith over tyranny and oppression.
orig: وقال موسى يا فرعون إني رسول من رب العالمين

translation: It is right for me not to say about Allah except the truth. I have come to you with clear evidence from your Lord, so send with me the Children of Israel.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of speaking the truth about God and relying on clear evidence from Him. It also highlights the role of prophets in guiding their people to the right path and delivering them from oppression. The verse suggests that the prophet, likely Moses, has come with a divine mandate to lead the Israelites out of bondage in Egypt, and he urges Pharaoh to allow them to leave with him. This interpretation underscores the themes of divine revelation, prophetic mission, and the struggle against tyranny and injustice in the Qur'anic narrative.
orig: حقيق على أن لا أقول على الله إلا الحق قد جئتكم ببينة من ربكم فأرسل معي بني إسرائيل

translation: He said, "If you have come with a sign, then bring it, if you are truthful."
interpretation: This verse is challenging the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) to produce a miracle or sign to prove his claim of prophethood, if he is truthful in his claim. It reflects the skepticism and disbelief of those who opposed the Prophet's message, demanding tangible evidence of his divine appointment. The verse implies that the burden of proof lies with the one making the claim, and that extraordinary claims require extraordinary evidence. It also highlights the importance of truthfulness and honesty in one's claims and actions, especially when it comes to matters of faith and religion.
orig: قال إن كنت جئت بآية فأت بها إن كنت من الصادقين

translation: Then he threw down his staff, and behold, it was a serpent, manifest.
interpretation: This verse is referring to the miracle of Moses, where he threw down his staff and it transformed into a clear, visible serpent. This was a sign of his prophethood and a demonstration of God's power. The transformation of the staff into a serpent was meant to convince Pharaoh and his people of the truth of Moses' message, as it was a supernatural event that could not be explained by ordinary means. The clarity and visibility of the serpent also highlights the undeniable nature of this miracle, leaving no room for doubt.
orig: فألقى عصاه فإذا هي ثعبان مبين

translation: And he drew out his hand, and thereupon it was white for the beholders.
interpretation: This verse refers to one of the miracles given to Prophet Moses (peace be upon him) as a sign of his prophethood. When Moses put his hand into his cloak and drew it out, it appeared shining white, without any disease or abnormality. This was a supernatural sign to help establish his credibility as a messenger of Allah to the people and to Pharaoh. It symbolizes divine power, purity, and the truth of Moses' message and mission. The miracle served as a compelling proof for those witnessing it, demonstrating that Moses was indeed sent by Allah and supported by divine miracles to affirm his prophethood.
orig: ونزع يده فإذا هي بيضاء للناظرين

translation: The eminent among the people of Pharaoh said, "Indeed, this is a learned magician."
interpretation: This verse shows the arrogance and disbelief of Pharaoh's elite when confronted with the clear signs and miracles of Moses. Instead of acknowledging the truth, they accused Moses of being a skilled magician, attempting to discredit him and maintain their own power and influence over the people. This highlights the tendency of those in positions of authority to reject divine guidance when it threatens their worldly interests, and the importance of humility and openness to the truth in one's spiritual journey.
orig: قال الملأ من قوم فرعون إن هذا لساحر عليم

translation: He wants to expel you from your land, so what do you order?
interpretation: This verse is likely addressing a situation where an enemy or oppressor is seeking to drive the believers out of their homeland. The question "so what do you order?" suggests that the verse is asking the believers how they will respond to this threat. The implication is that they should remain steadfast, united, and seek Allah's help in defending their land and way of life against those who wish to uproot them. It emphasizes the importance of standing firm in the face of oppression and not allowing oneself to be unjustly driven from one's rightful place.
orig: يريد أن يخرجكم من أرضكم فماذا تأمرون

translation: They said, "Postpone [the matter of] him and his brother and send among the cities gatherers
interpretation: The chiefs of Pharaoh's people, upon hearing Moses' message, suggested to Pharaoh to delay taking action against Moses and his brother Aaron. They advised him to send messengers to various cities to gather magicians who could challenge Moses and invalidate his miracles, in an attempt to discredit him and maintain their own authority and beliefs. This highlights the lengths to which those in power will go to suppress the truth and maintain their hold on power when faced with a message that challenges their way of life.
orig: قالوا أرجه وأخاه وأرسل في المدائن حاشرين

translation: They will bring you every learned magician.
interpretation: This verse refers to the story of Moses and Pharaoh, where Pharaoh summons the most skilled magicians in the land to challenge Moses and discredit his miracles. It highlights the arrogance and defiance of those in power who refuse to acknowledge the truth, instead relying on their own worldly means to oppose the message of God. The verse also emphasizes the futility of such efforts, as no matter how skilled or knowledgeable the magicians may be, they cannot match the power and wisdom of God that is manifested through His prophets.
orig: يأتوك بكل ساحر عليم

translation: And the magicians came to Pharaoh. They said, "Indeed for us is a reward if we are the predominant."
interpretation: This verse highlights the materialistic and worldly motivations of the magicians who came to challenge Moses. They were primarily interested in the reward they would receive from Pharaoh if they could outperform Moses and prove their superiority in magic. This shows that their hearts were not sincere in seeking the truth, but rather they were driven by their desire for worldly gain and status. It is a reminder that one should always be mindful of their intentions and seek to please Allah above all else, rather than being motivated by temporary worldly benefits.
orig: وجاء السحرة فرعون قالوا إن لنا لأجرا إن كنا نحن الغالبين

translation: He said, "Yes, and indeed you are of those brought near [to Allah]."
interpretation: This verse is a continuation of the dialogue between Allah and the angels regarding the creation of Adam. Allah is affirming to the angels that they are among His closest servants, and that they have a special status of nearness to Him. This highlights the honor and distinction that Allah has bestowed upon the angels, while also emphasizing their subservience to His commands, as they are ultimately His creation and servants. The verse underscores the importance of obedience and submission to Allah's will, even for those held in high regard.
orig: قال نعم وإنكم لمن المقربين

translation: They said, "O Moses, either you throw [your staff], or we will be the ones to throw [first]."
interpretation: This verse is from the story of Moses and the magicians of Pharaoh. The magicians challenge Moses to either throw his staff first or let them begin the contest. They are confident in their magic and believe that they can defeat Moses. However, this verse also demonstrates the courage and faith of Moses, as he is willing to face the challenge despite the apparent power of the magicians. The verse sets the stage for the miraculous event where Moses' staff, by Allah's power, overcomes the magic of Pharaoh's sorcerers, proving the truth of Moses' prophethood and the supremacy of Allah over all false powers.
orig: قالوا يا موسى إما أن تلقي وإما أن نكون نحن الملقين

translation: He said, "Throw," and when they threw, they bewitched the eyes of the people and struck terror into them, and they presented a great [feat of] magic.
interpretation: This verse refers to the confrontation between Moses and the magicians of Pharaoh's court. When the magicians threw their staffs and ropes, they created an illusion that deceived the eyes of the onlookers, making them believe that the objects had turned into real snakes. This display of magic was intended to strike fear into the hearts of the people and demonstrate the power of the magicians. However, the verse implies that their magic, while impressive, was ultimately inferior to the genuine miracle that Moses would perform with the help of Allah. The verse highlights the difference between mere illusion and true divine power.
orig: قال ألقوا فلما ألقوا سحروا أعين الناس واسترهبوهم وجاءوا بسحر عظيم

translation: And We inspired to Moses, "Throw your staff," and at once it devoured what they were falsifying.
interpretation: This verse is referring to the confrontation between Moses and the magicians of Pharaoh's court.
