God commanded Moses to throw his staff, which then transformed into a serpent and swallowed up the illusory snakes created by Pharaoh's magicians. This miracle served as a powerful demonstration of God's power and the truth of Moses' message, exposing the falsehood and trickery of the magicians. It symbolizes the ultimate triumph of truth over falsehood and the power of genuine faith over deception and illusion.
orig: وأوحينا إلى موسى أن ألق عصاك فإذا هي تلقف ما يأفكون

translation: So the truth was established, and abolished was what they were doing.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the ultimate triumph of truth over falsehood. It suggests that the efforts of those who oppose the truth will eventually prove futile and be rendered void. The verse implies that the truth, being from God, has an inherent power and permanence that will always prevail in the end, no matter how much the wrongdoers may strive against it. It is a reminder to the believers to remain steadfast in their faith and to trust in the inevitable victory of the divine truth, even in the face of adversity and opposition from those who reject it.
orig: فوقع الحق وبطل ما كانوا يعملون

translation: So they were defeated there and returned disgraced.
interpretation: This verse refers to the defeat and humiliation of the disbelievers who opposed the Prophet Muhammad and the message of Islam. It indicates that those who reject the truth and fight against it will ultimately face defeat and disgrace, both in this world and in the Hereafter. The verse emphasizes the power and victory of Allah's cause, and serves as a warning to those who might consider challenging or opposing it. It also provides reassurance and encouragement to the believers, reminding them that their faith and steadfastness will be rewarded with divine support and ultimate triumph over their adversaries.
orig: فغلبوا هنالك وانقلبوا صاغرين

translation: And the magicians fell down prostrate.
interpretation: This verse refers to the story of Moses and the magicians of Pharaoh's court. When Moses threw down his staff and it turned into a serpent, the magicians realized that this was not mere magic, but a true miracle from God. They immediately fell into prostration, acknowledging the power and authority of the One True God, despite knowing that this would anger Pharaoh. This demonstrates the overwhelming effect of witnessing a genuine miracle and the magicians' readiness to submit to the truth when it was made clear to them, even at the cost of defying the ruler they served.
orig: وألقي السحرة ساجدين

translation: They said, "We have believed in the Lord of the worlds."
interpretation: This verse reflects the sincere declaration of faith by the believers in Allah, the Lord and Sustainer of all creation. It demonstrates their unwavering commitment to monotheism and their acknowledgment of Allah's supreme authority over the entire universe. By proclaiming their belief in the "Lord of the worlds," they affirm that Allah is the sole creator, owner, and ruler of everything that exists, transcending all boundaries and encompassing all realms. This statement serves as a powerful testament to their submission to the one true God and their rejection of all false deities or objects of worship.
orig: قالوا آمنا برب العالمين

translation: The Lord of Moses and Aaron.
interpretation: This verse affirms that Allah is the Lord and Sustainer of the Prophets Moses and Aaron. It emphasizes the continuity of the divine message and Allah's support for His chosen messengers throughout history. By mentioning these two prominent prophets together, the Qur'an highlights the shared essence of their teachings and the unity of the source of their revelations, which is Allah Himself. This verse serves as a reminder to the believers to trust in Allah's guidance and follow the path of the righteous messengers who came before Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him).
orig: رب موسى وهارون

translation: Pharaoh said, "You believed Moses before I gave you permission. Indeed, this is a conspiracy which you conspired in the city to expel therefrom its people. But you are going to know."
interpretation: This verse shows Pharaoh's arrogance and his belief that he had absolute authority over his subjects. He accused Moses and his followers of conspiring against him and the state, and threatened them with severe punishment. It reflects the tyrannical nature of Pharaoh's rule and his opposition to the message of Moses. The verse also highlights the courage and faith of those who believed in Moses despite Pharaoh's threats, and their willingness to stand up to oppression and injustice for the sake of their beliefs.
orig: قال فرعون آمنتم به قبل أن آذن لكم إن هذا لمكر مكرتموه في المدينة لتخرجوا منها أهلها فسوف تعلمون

translation: I will surely cut off your hands and your feet on opposite sides; then I will surely crucify you all.
interpretation: This verse is a warning of severe punishment for those who reject God's message and oppose His messengers. The cutting off of hands and feet on opposite sides and crucifixion were severe corporal punishments used in ancient times. The verse emphasizes the gravity of denying the truth and actively working against it when it has been made clear through God's signs and revelations. It is meant to strike fear in the hearts of those who persistently and defiantly disbelieve, signaling that there are serious, terrible consequences for such a stance in the Hereafter if they do not repent and correct their ways. However, it is important to note that this punishment is not to be carried out by individuals, but is reserved for God to apply in the afterlife as He deems just.
orig: لأقطعن أيديكم وأرجلكم من خلاف ثم لأصلبنكم أجمعين

translation: They said, "Indeed we, to our Lord, will return."
interpretation: This verse reflects the strong faith and belief of the believers in the Hereafter and their ultimate return to Allah. It shows their acceptance of whatever befalls them in this worldly life, whether good or bad, knowing that their final destination is back to their Lord. This unwavering faith in the return to Allah provides them with comfort, patience, and steadfastness in the face of trials and tribulations.
orig: قالوا إنا إلى ربنا منقلبون

translation: And you resent us only because we have believed in the signs of our Lord when they came to us. Our Lord, pour upon us patience and let us die as Muslims [in submission to You].
interpretation: This verse can be interpreted as a reminder to remain steadfast in faith despite facing opposition or resentment from others. It emphasizes the importance of patience and perseverance in the face of adversity, and the ultimate goal of dying in a state of submission to God (Allah). The believers are asking God to grant them the strength and patience to endure any hardships they may face due to their belief, and to allow them to remain faithful until the end of their lives. This highlights the concept of remaining committed to one's principles and beliefs, even if it brings about challenges or difficulties from those who oppose them.
orig: وما تنقم منا إلا أن آمنا بآيات ربنا لما جاءتنا ربنا أفرغ علينا صبرا وتوفنا مسلمين

translation: The chiefs of Pharaoh's people said, "Will you leave Moses and his people to cause corruption in the land and abandon you and your gods?" [Pharaoh] said, "We will kill their sons and keep their women alive; and indeed, we are subjugators over them."
interpretation: This verse highlights the arrogance and tyranny of Pharaoh and his chiefs. They view Moses and his followers as a threat to their power and their polytheistic beliefs. Pharaoh's response is one of brutal oppression, threatening to kill the male children and enslave the women of the Israelites. This demonstrates the depths of cruelty and injustice that those in power can resort to when they feel their authority is challenged. It also shows the unwavering faith and resilience of Moses and his people in the face of such oppression, as they continue to follow the path of monotheism despite the grave dangers they face.
orig: وقال الملأ من قوم فرعون أتذر موسى وقومه ليفسدوا في الأرض ويذرك وآلهتك قال سنقتل أبناءهم ونستحيي نساءهم وإنا فوقهم قاهرون

translation: Moses said to his people, "Seek help through Allah and be patient. Indeed, the earth belongs to Allah. He causes to inherit it whom He wills of His servants. And the [best] outcome is for the righteous."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of seeking help from Allah and remaining patient in the face of adversity. It reminds believers that ultimately, the earth and everything in it belongs to Allah, and He grants it to whomever He chooses among His servants. The verse also highlights that the best outcome and ultimate success is reserved for those who are righteous and God-fearing. It encourages the followers of Moses to put their trust in Allah, persevere through hardships, and maintain their faith, knowing that the reward for their righteousness will be a favorable outcome in this world and the hereafter.
orig: قال موسى لقومه استعينوا بالله واصبروا إن الأرض لله يورثها من يشاء من عباده والعاقبة للمتقين

translation: They said, "We have been harmed before you came to us and after you have come to us." He said, "Perhaps your Lord will destroy your enemy and grant you succession in the land and see how you will do."
interpretation: This verse reflects the trials and tribulations faced by the believers, both before and after the coming of the Prophet. Despite the difficulties, there is hope that Allah will ultimately destroy their enemies and grant the believers authority and succession in the land. This is a test to see how they will act and conduct themselves when given this power and responsibility. Will they be just and righteous leaders, or will they succumb to corruption and oppression? The verse serves as a reminder to remain steadfast in faith during hardships and to strive for righteousness in all circumstances.
orig: قالوا أوذينا من قبل أن تأتينا ومن بعد ما جئتنا قال عسى ربكم أن يهلك عدوكم ويستخلفكم في الأرض فينظر كيف تعملون

translation: And We certainly seized the people of Pharaoh with years of famine and a deficiency in fruits that perhaps they would be reminded.
interpretation: This verse is a reminder that Allah has the power to inflict punishment and hardship on those who reject His messages and persist in wrongdoing. The people of Pharaoh, despite witnessing the miracles of Moses, continued in their arrogance and disbelief. As a result, Allah sent upon them years of drought and famine, causing a shortage in their crops and fruits. This was meant to serve as a wake-up call, a chance for them to reflect on their actions and turn back to Allah in repentance. It highlights the fact that Allah's punishment is not arbitrary but rather a means of reminding people of their purpose and guiding them back to the right path. The verse also implies that even in times of hardship, there is an opportunity for introspection and spiritual growth if one is willing to heed the signs and messages from Allah.
orig: ولقد أخذنا آل فرعون بالسنين ونقص من الثمرات لعلهم يذكرون

translation: But when good came to them, they said, "This is ours [by right]." And if a bad [condition] struck them, they saw an evil omen in Moses and those with him. Unquestionably, their fortune is with Allah, but most of them do not know.
interpretation: This verse highlights the fickle nature of the people who opposed Moses. When good things happened to them, they attributed it to their own merits, refusing to acknowledge God's blessings. However, when faced with difficulties, they blamed Moses and his followers, considering them as bad omens. The verse emphasizes that their fate and fortune are determined by Allah alone, but most of them fail to recognize this truth due to their ignorance and lack of faith.
orig: فإذا جاءتهم الحسنة قالوا لنا هذه وإن تصبهم سيئة يطيروا بموسى ومن معه ألا إنما طائرهم عند الله ولكن أكثرهم لا يعلمون

translation: And they said, "No matter what sign you bring us with which to bewitch us, we will not be believers in you."
interpretation: This verse is referring to the stubborn disbelief of those who reject the message of the prophets, even when presented with clear signs and miracles. They are so entrenched in their disbelief that they attribute these signs to magic or sorcery, rather than accepting them as proof of the prophet's truthfulness. It highlights the depth of their denial and their unwillingness to open their hearts to the truth, no matter how compelling the evidence may be. The verse suggests that for some people, no amount of proof or persuasion will change their minds if they have already decided to reject faith.
orig: وقالوا مهما تأتنا به من آية لتسحرنا بها فما نحن لك بمؤمنين

translation: So We sent upon them the flood and locusts and lice and frogs and blood as distinct signs, but they were arrogant and were a criminal people.
interpretation: This verse is a warning to those who reject the signs and messages of Allah. It refers to the plagues that Allah sent upon the people of Pharaoh as a punishment for their arrogance and defiance. The plagues mentioned - the flood, locusts, lice, frogs, and blood - were clear signs of Allah's power and a test for Pharaoh and his people. However, despite witnessing these miracles, they remained arrogant and continued in their criminal ways, refusing to believe in Allah and submit to His will. The verse emphasizes that those who persist in disbelief and transgression, even after being shown clear proofs, will face severe consequences for their actions. It serves as a reminder for all of mankind to heed the signs of Allah and to humble themselves before His might and wisdom.
orig: فأرسلنا عليهم الطوفان والجراد والقمل والضفادع والدم آيات مفصلات فاستكبروا وكانوا قوما مجرمين

translation: And when the punishment fell upon them, they said, "O Moses, invoke for us your Lord by what He has promised you. If you [can] remove the punishment from us, we will surely believe you, and we will send with you the Children of Israel."
interpretation: This verse is referring to the story of Prophet Moses and the Israelites. When the punishment of God fell upon the Egyptians in the form of plagues, they turned to Moses, pleading with him to pray to his Lord to remove the affliction from them. They promised that if the punishment was lifted, they would believe in Moses and allow the Children of Israel to leave with him. This highlights the human tendency to turn to God and make promises in times of hardship, but often forget or break those promises when the difficulty passes. It also shows the power of prayer and the mercy of God in responding to sincere supplication.
orig: ولما وقع عليهم الرجز قالوا يا موسى ادع لنا ربك بما عهد عندك لئن كشفت عنا الرجز لنؤمنن لك ولنرسلن معك بني إسرائيل

translation: But when We removed the punishment from them until a term which they were to reach, then at once they broke their word.
interpretation: This verse highlights the fickleness and ingratitude of some people. Even when God relieves them of their afflictions and grants them respite until an appointed time, they quickly forget His mercy and revert to their old ways of disobedience and breaking their promises. It shows how short-lived human gratitude can be and how easily people can fall back into transgression once the immediate danger or hardship is lifted. The verse serves as a reminder for people to remain steadfast in faith and gratitude towards God, even during times of ease and comfort.
orig: فلما كشفنا عنهم الرجز إلى أجل هم بالغوه إذا هم ينكثون

translation: So We took retribution from them and drowned them in the sea because they denied Our signs and were heedless of them.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the consequences of denying and ignoring the signs and messages sent by Allah. Those who persistently reject the truth and remain heedless of the divine guidance will face the wrath of Allah. The verse refers to a past nation that was punished by drowning in the sea due to their disbelief and inattention to Allah's signs. It serves as a reminder that Allah's retribution is severe for those who choose to disbelieve and that one should always be mindful and attentive to the signs and guidance provided by Him.
orig: فانتقمنا منهم فأغرقناهم في اليم بأنهم كذبوا بآياتنا وكانوا عنها غافلين

translation: And We made the people who were oppressed inherit the eastern and western parts of the land which We had blessed. And the good word of your Lord was fulfilled for the Children of Israel because of what they had patiently endured. And We destroyed [all] that Pharaoh and his people were producing and what they had been building.
interpretation: This verse highlights the ultimate triumph of the oppressed and steadfast believers over their oppressors. The Children of Israel, who were subjugated and persecuted by Pharaoh and his people, were eventually granted inheritance of the blessed lands as a reward for their patience and faith in God's promise. The verse also emphasizes the transient nature of worldly power and the futility of the oppressors' efforts, as all that Pharaoh and his people had built and produced was ultimately destroyed by God's will. This serves as a reminder that those who remain steadfast in their faith and endure hardships will be rewarded, while those who oppress others and rely on their worldly might will ultimately face destruction and loss.
orig: وأورثنا القوم الذين كانوا يستضعفون مشارق الأرض ومغاربها التي باركنا فيها وتمت كلمت ربك الحسنى على بني إسرائيل بما صبروا ودمرنا ما كان يصنع فرعون وقومه وما كانوا يعرشون

translation: And We took the Children of Israel across the sea; then they came upon a people intent in devotion to [some] idols of theirs. They said, "O Moses, make for us a god just as they have gods." He said, "Indeed, you are a people behaving ignorantly."
interpretation: This verse highlights the ignorance and lack of faith among the Children of Israel, despite witnessing the miracles of Allah. When they encountered a polytheistic nation worshipping idols, they demanded that Moses create a similar idol for them to worship. Moses admonished them, pointing out their foolishness in desiring to worship false gods after experiencing the true power and guidance of Allah. This incident serves as a reminder for believers to remain steadfast in their faith and not be swayed by the misguided practices of others, even in the face of adversity or temptation.
orig: وجاوزنا ببني إسرائيل البحر فأتوا على قوم يعكفون على أصنام لهم قالوا يا موسى اجعل لنا إلها كما لهم آلهة قال إنكم قوم تجهلون

translation: Indeed, those [worshippers], destroyed is that in which they are [engaged], and worthless is whatever they were doing.
interpretation: This verse is a strong condemnation of those who engage in false worship or follow misguided beliefs and practices. It suggests that their actions are futile and ultimately lead to their own destruction. The verse implies that anything done without sincerity and not in accordance with God's guidance is worthless and will not bring any benefit in this life or the hereafter. It serves as a warning to be mindful of our beliefs and deeds, and to strive to follow the straight path of divine guidance.
orig: إن هؤلاء متبر ما هم فيه وباطل ما كانوا يعملون

translation: He said, "Is it other than Allah I should desire for you as a god while He has preferred you over the worlds?"
interpretation: In this verse, Moses is reminding the Children of Israel of Allah's favors upon them, specifically that He chose them above all other nations at that time. Moses is rebuking them for their ingratitude and their desire to worship other gods besides Allah, who has bestowed upon them such blessings and favors. It is a reminder that they should be devoted to Allah alone and not seek any other object of worship, as that would be the height of ingratitude to the One who has preferred them and given them a special status among all peoples.
orig: قال أغير الله أبغيكم إلها وهو فضلكم على العالمين

translation: And [recall] when We saved you from the people of Pharaoh, who afflicted you with the worst torment, slaughtering your [newborn] sons and keeping your females alive. And in that was a great trial from your Lord.
interpretation: This verse is a reminder to the Children of Israel of Allah's favor upon them, when He saved them from the oppression and persecution of Pharaoh and his people. Pharaoh had ordered the killing of all male newborns among the Israelites, while allowing the females to live, in an attempt to prevent the emergence of a leader who could challenge his rule. This was a severe trial and affliction for the Israelites, but it also served as a test of their faith and resilience. The verse emphasizes the magnitude of Allah's blessing in delivering them from such oppression and highlights the importance of remembering and being grateful for His favors.
orig: وإذ أنجيناكم من آل فرعون يسومونكم سوء العذاب يقتلون أبناءكم ويستحيون نساءكم وفي ذلكم بلاء من ربكم عظيم

translation: And We made an appointment with Moses for thirty nights and perfected them by [the addition of] ten; so the term of his Lord was completed as forty nights. And Moses said to his brother Aaron, "Take my place among my people, do right [by them], and do not follow the way of the corrupters."
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of leadership and responsibility. Moses, being chosen by Allah, was called to the mount for forty nights to receive the Torah. Before leaving, he entrusted his brother Aaron with the leadership of the Israelites in his absence, urging him to lead them righteously and not follow the path of those who cause corruption. This emphasizes the significance of having trustworthy and righteous leaders who can guide the community in the right direction, especially during the absence of the main leader. It also stresses the duty of those in positions of authority to act with justice and integrity, and to steer clear of anything that may lead to corruption or wrongdoing.
orig: وواعدنا موسى ثلاثين ليلة وأتممناها بعشر فتم ميقات ربه أربعين ليلة وقال موسى لأخيه هارون اخلفني في قومي وأصلح ولا تتبع سبيل المفسدين

translation: And when Moses came at Our appointed time and his Lord spoke to him, he said, "My Lord, show me [Yourself] that I may look at You." [Allah] said, "You will not see Me, but look at the mountain; if it should remain in place, then you will see Me." But when his Lord appeared to the mountain, He rendered it level, and Moses fell unconscious. And when he awoke, he said, "Exalted are You! I have repented to You, and I am the first of the believers."
interpretation: This verse highlights the profound spiritual experience of Prophet Moses when he sought to see Allah directly. It emphasizes the transcendent nature of Allah, who cannot be perceived by human eyes. The verse also underscores the importance of humility and repentance in one's relationship with Allah. Moses' request to see Allah was not out of arrogance but a deep longing for closeness. Allah's response and the subsequent events serve as a powerful reminder that even the greatest of prophets cannot comprehend the full majesty of Allah. The verse teaches us to approach Allah with reverence, to seek His forgiveness, and to submit to His will, as Moses did when he declared himself as the first of the believers.
orig: ولما جاء موسى لميقاتنا وكلمه ربه قال رب أرني أنظر إليك قال لن تراني ولكن انظر إلى الجبل فإن استقر مكانه فسوف تراني فلما تجلى ربه للجبل جعله دكا وخر موسى صعقا فلما أفاق قال سبحانك تبت إليك وأنا أول المؤمنين

translation: He said, "O Moses, I have chosen you over the people with My messages and My words [to you]. So take what I have given you and be among the grateful."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the special status of Prophet Moses, who was chosen by Allah to receive His messages and to communicate directly with Him. It is a reminder of the great honor and responsibility bestowed upon Moses. The verse also instructs Moses to accept the divine revelation and teachings with gratitude, highlighting the importance of being thankful for the guidance and blessings provided by Allah. It serves as a lesson for all believers to appreciate and follow the guidance given to them through the prophets and the divine scriptures.
orig: قال يا موسى إني اصطفيتك على الناس برسالاتي وبكلامي فخذ ما آتيتك وكن من الشاكرين

translation: And We wrote for him on the tablets [something] of all things - instruction and explanation for all things, [saying], "Take them with determination and order your people to take the best of it. I will show you the home of the defiantly disobedient."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance and comprehensiveness of the divine message given to Moses. The "tablets" likely refer to the Torah, which contained detailed instructions and guidance covering all aspects of life. God commands Moses to adhere to these teachings with strength and conviction, and to instruct his people to uphold the best and most virtuous aspects of the law. The verse serves as a warning that those who defiantly disobey God's commandments will face severe consequences in the afterlife, with God showing them the ultimate fate and "home" of the sinners. It highlights the significance of following divine guidance and the ramifications of straying from the righteous path.
orig: وكتبنا له في الألواح من كل شيء موعظة وتفصيلا لكل شيء فخذها بقوة وأمر قومك يأخذوا بأحسنها سأريكم دار الفاسقين

translation: I will turn away from My signs those who are arrogant upon the earth without right; and if they should see every sign, they will not believe in it. And if they see the way of consciousness, they will not adopt it as a way; but if they see the way of error, they will adopt it as a way. That is because they have denied Our signs and they were heedless of them.
interpretation: This verse speaks about those who are arrogant and reject the signs of Allah despite their clarity. Their arrogance and pride prevent them from believing in the truth even if they are presented with every possible evidence. They deliberately choose the path of misguidance over the path of righteousness. This is because they have denied Allah's revelations and were heedless of them, not reflecting upon them or taking them seriously. As a result, Allah will turn them away from His signs as a consequence of their arrogance and disbelief.
orig: سأصرف عن آياتي الذين يتكبرون في الأرض بغير الحق وإن يروا كل آية لا يؤمنوا بها وإن يروا سبيل الرشد لا يتخذوه سبيلا وإن يروا سبيل الغي يتخذوه سبيلا ذلك بأنهم كذبوا بآياتنا وكانوا عنها غافلين

translation: But as for those who denied Our signs and the meeting of the Hereafter, their deeds have become worthless. Are they recompensed except for what they used to do?
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that those who reject God's messages and signs, and deny the reality of the Day of Judgment, will find that all their good deeds and efforts in this world will be rendered null and void in the Hereafter. They will not receive any reward for them, because they lacked true faith and did not perform those deeds for the sake of God. Instead, they will only be punished for their bad deeds and their disbelief. This highlights the importance of faith and sincere intention behind our actions, as ultimately only those deeds that are done for the pleasure of God will be accepted and rewarded in the Hereafter.
orig: والذين كذبوا بآياتنا ولقاء الآخرة حبطت أعمالهم هل يجزون إلا ما كانوا يعملون

translation: And the people of Moses made, after [his departure], from their ornaments a calf - an image having a lowing sound. Did they not see that it could neither speak to them nor guide them to a way? They took it [for worship], and they were wrongdoers.
interpretation: This verse highlights the grave error committed by the Israelites in the absence of Moses. Despite witnessing God's miracles and receiving His guidance, they strayed by crafting a golden calf to worship. The verse emphasizes their folly by pointing out that the inanimate calf could neither communicate with them nor provide any guidance. By worshipping a mere creation instead of the Creator, they became transgressors, falling into idolatry and disobedience to God. This incident serves as a reminder for believers to remain steadfast in their faith and not be swayed by worldly temptations or false deities.
orig: واتخذ قوم موسى من بعده من حليهم عجلا جسدا له خوار ألم يروا أنه لا يكلمهم ولا يهديهم سبيلا اتخذوه وكانوا ظالمين

translation: And when they regretted and saw that they had gone astray, they said, "If our Lord does not have mercy upon us and forgive us, we will surely be among the losers."
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of seeking Allah's mercy and forgiveness when one realizes their mistakes and shortcomings. It emphasizes the human tendency to go astray and the need for divine intervention to guide us back to the right path. The verse also implies that without Allah's mercy and forgiveness, one risks being among the losers in both this world and the hereafter. It serves as a reminder for believers to constantly turn to Allah in repentance and seek His grace, acknowledging that ultimate success lies in His hands.
orig: ولما سقط في أيديهم ورأوا أنهم قد ضلوا قالوا لئن لم يرحمنا ربنا ويغفر لنا لنكونن من الخاسرين

translation: And when Moses returned to his people, angry and grieved, he said, "How wretched is that by which you have replaced me after [my departure]. Were you impatient over the matter of your Lord?" And he threw down the tablets and seized his brother by [the hair of] his head, pulling him toward him. [Aaron] said, "O son of my mother, indeed the people oppressed me and were about to kill me, so let not the enemies rejoice over me and do not place me among the wrongdoing people."
interpretation: This verse highlights Moses' anger and disappointment upon returning to his people and finding that they had strayed from the right path in his absence. It demonstrates the importance of patience and trust in God's plan, as well as the consequences of succumbing to temptation and disobedience. The interaction between Moses and Aaron also emphasizes the significance of brotherhood and the need for understanding and forgiveness, even in the face of wrongdoing. Ultimately, this verse serves as a reminder for believers to remain steadfast in their faith and to seek God's guidance in all matters.
orig: ولما رجع موسى إلى قومه غضبان أسفا قال بئسما خلفتموني من بعدي أعجلتم أمر ربكم وألقى الألواح وأخذ برأس أخيه يجره إليه قال ابن أم إن القوم استضعفوني وكادوا يقتلونني فلا تشمت بي الأعداء ولا تجعلني مع القوم الظالمين

translation: He said, "My Lord, forgive me and my brother and admit us into Your mercy, for You are the most merciful of the merciful."
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of seeking forgiveness from Allah and supplicating for His mercy. It demonstrates humility and acknowledgment of one's shortcomings before Allah. The speaker, believed to be Prophet Moses, is asking for forgiveness not only for himself but also for his brother, showing a sense of care and concern for others' spiritual well-being. By asking to be admitted into Allah's mercy, it emphasizes the believer's ultimate goal of attaining Allah's pleasure and being enveloped in His infinite mercy and compassion. The supplication ends with the acknowledgment that Allah is the most merciful of those who show mercy, indicating that no matter how much mercy and compassion one may receive from others, it pales in comparison to the boundless mercy of Allah.
orig: قال رب اغفر لي ولأخي وأدخلنا في رحمتك وأنت أرحم الراحمين

translation: Indeed, those who took the calf [for worship] will obtain anger from their Lord and humiliation in the life of this world, and thus do We recompense the inventors [of falsehood].
interpretation: This verse warns that those who worshipped the golden calf instead of Allah will face His wrath and be disgraced in this worldly life. It shows that Allah punishes those who fabricate lies and false gods to worship besides Him. Worshipping anything other than Allah is among the gravest of sins. This humiliating punishment in the world is in addition to the punishment that awaits them in the Hereafter for their idolatry and disbelief, unless they sincerely repent to Allah.
orig: إن الذين اتخذوا العجل سينالهم غضب من ربهم وذلة في الحياة الدنيا وكذلك نجزي المفترين

translation: But those who committed misdeeds and then repented after them and believed - indeed, your Lord, thereafter, is Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse conveys the immense mercy and forgiveness of Allah. It reassures us that even if we have committed sins or wrongdoings in the past, the door to repentance is always open. If we sincerely turn back to Allah, seek His forgiveness, and embrace faith, He will surely forgive us and shower us with His mercy. This highlights the compassionate nature of our Lord, who is ever ready to accept the repentance of His servants, no matter how far they may have strayed. It encourages us to never despair of Allah's mercy and to always seek His forgiveness, for He is the Most Forgiving and the Most Merciful.
orig: والذين عملوا السيئات ثم تابوا من بعدها وآمنوا إن ربك من بعدها لغفور رحيم

translation: And when the anger subsided in Moses, he took up the tablets; and in their inscription was guidance and mercy for those who are fearful of their Lord.
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of controlling one's anger and the rewards that come with it. When Moses was able to subdue his anger, he found guidance and mercy inscribed on the tablets for those who fear Allah. This suggests that by managing our emotions and turning to Allah's guidance with reverence, we can attain divine mercy and direction in our lives. It emphasizes the spiritual benefits of emotional restraint and the significance of seeking Allah's guidance with a heart full of awe and respect.
orig: ولما سكت عن موسى الغضب أخذ الألواح وفي نسختها هدى ورحمة للذين هم لربهم يرهبون

translation: And Moses chose from his people seventy men for Our appointment. And when the earthquake seized them, he said, "My Lord, if You had willed, You could have destroyed them before and me [as well]. Would You destroy us for what the foolish among us have done? This is not but Your trial by which You send astray whom You will and guide whom You will. You are our Protector, so forgive us and have mercy upon us; and You are the best of forgivers."
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of leadership and responsibility. Moses, as a leader, chose seventy men to represent his people before God. However, when they were struck by an earthquake, Moses turned to God in humility, acknowledging that the actions of a few foolish individuals could have consequences for the entire community. He recognized that ultimately, guidance and misguidance are in God's hands, and sought forgiveness and mercy on behalf of his people. The verse emphasizes the role of a leader in interceding for their community, while also acknowledging God's supreme authority and the importance of seeking His protection and forgiveness.
orig: واختار موسى قومه سبعين رجلا لميقاتنا فلما أخذتهم الرجفة قال رب لو شئت أهلكتهم من قبل وإياي أتهلكنا بما فعل السفهاء منا إن هي إلا فتنتك تضل بها من تشاء وتهدي من تشاء أنت ولينا فاغفر لنا وارحمنا وأنت خير الغافرين

translation: And ordain for us good in this world, and in the Hereafter. Certainly, we have turned unto You. He said: "(As to) My Punishment I afflict therewith whom I will and My Mercy embraces all things. That (Mercy) I shall ordain for those who do right, and practice regular charity, and those who believe in Our Signs."
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of seeking Allah's mercy and blessings in both this world and the Hereafter. It emphasizes that while Allah's punishment is reserved for those He wills, His mercy encompasses all things. The verse also outlines the qualities of those who will be granted Allah's mercy: those who are righteous, give in charity, and believe in Allah's signs. This serves as a reminder for believers to strive towards these qualities in order to attain Allah's mercy and favor.
orig: واكتب لنا في هذه الدنيا حسنة وفي الآخرة إنا هدنا إليك قال عذابي أصيب به من أشاء ورحمتي وسعت كل شيء فسأكتبها للذين يتقون ويؤتون الزكاة والذين هم بآياتنا يؤمنون

translation: Those who follow the Messenger, the unlettered prophet, whom they find written in what they have of the Torah and the Gospel, who enjoins upon them what is right and forbids them what is wrong and makes lawful for them the good things and prohibits for them the evil and relieves them of their burden and the shackles which were upon them. So they who have believed in him, honored him, supported him and followed the light which was sent down with him - it is those who will be the successful.
interpretation: This verse highlights the characteristics of Prophet Muhammad and his followers. It emphasizes that he was foretold in the earlier scriptures, and that his message is one of righteousness, forbidding evil, and making life easier by making good things lawful and bad things unlawful. Those who sincerely believe in him, honor him, support his cause, and follow the divine light that was revealed to him are promised success in this world and the next. It signifies that following the Prophet's teachings is the path to spiritual fulfillment and salvation.
orig: الذين يتبعون الرسول النبي الأمي الذي يجدونه مكتوبا عندهم في التوراة والإنجيل يأمرهم بالمعروف وينهاهم عن المنكر ويحل لهم الطيبات ويحرم عليهم الخبائث ويضع عنهم إصرهم والأغلال التي كانت عليهم فالذين آمنوا به وعزروه ونصروه واتبعوا النور الذي أنزل معه أولئك هم المفلحون

translation: Say, "O mankind, indeed I am the Messenger of Allah to you all, [from Him] to whom belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth. There is no deity except Him; He gives life and causes death." So believe in Allah and His Messenger, the unlettered prophet, who believes in Allah and His words, and follow him that you may be guided.
interpretation: This verse is a universal declaration of Prophet Muhammad's mission as the final messenger of Allah to all of humanity. It emphasizes the oneness and sovereignty of Allah over the entire universe and His exclusive right to be worshipped. The verse calls upon people to have faith in Allah and His messenger, who, despite being unlettered, believed in Allah and His revelations. Following the guidance brought by Prophet Muhammad is presented as the path to attain divine guidance and success in this life and the hereafter. The verse underscores the universality of Islam and its message, which transcends all boundaries of race, ethnicity, and nationality.
orig: قل يا أيها الناس إني رسول الله إليكم جميعا الذي له ملك السماوات والأرض لا إله إلا هو يحيي ويميت فآمنوا بالله ورسوله النبي الأمي الذي يؤمن بالله وكلماته واتبعوه لعلكم تهتدون

translation: And among the people of Moses is a community which guides by truth and by it establishes justice.
interpretation: This verse highlights that even among the people of Moses, there existed a righteous community that adhered to the truth and acted with justice. It suggests that within every nation or religious group, there are those who remain steadfast in their faith and uphold the principles of righteousness and fairness. This community serves as an example for others to follow, guiding them towards the path of truth and encouraging them to establish justice in all their affairs. The verse emphasizes the importance of having role models within a community who can inspire others to lead a virtuous life.
orig: ومن قوم موسى أمة يهدون بالحق وبه يعدلون

translation: And We divided them into twelve tribes [as distinct] nations. And We inspired to Moses when his people implored him for water, "Strike with your staff the stone," and there gushed forth from it twelve springs. Every people knew its watering place. And We shaded them with clouds and sent down upon them manna and quails, [saying], "Eat from the good things with which We have provided you." And they wronged Us not, but they were [only] wronging themselves.
interpretation: This verse highlights God's favor upon the Children of Israel, whom He divided into twelve tribes and provided with miraculous sustenance and guidance. When they were in need of water, God instructed Moses to strike a rock with his staff, causing twelve springs to gush forth, one for each tribe. God also shaded them with clouds and sent down manna and quails as food. Despite these blessings, the verse points out that they did not wrong God through their disobedience, but rather they wronged themselves by not being grateful and following the guidance provided to them. It emphasizes the importance of recognizing and appreciating God's favors and the consequences of ingratitude and disobedience.
orig: وقطعناهم اثنتي عشرة أسباطا أمما وأوحينا إلى موسى إذ استسقاه قومه أن اضرب بعصاك الحجر فانبجست منه اثنتا عشرة عينا قد علم كل أناس مشربهم وظللنا عليهم الغمام وأنزلنا عليهم المن والسلوى كلوا من طيبات ما رزقناكم وما ظلمونا ولكن كانوا أنفسهم يظلمون

translation: And [mention] when it was said to them, "Settle this city and eat from wherever you will, and say, '[We seek] forgiveness,' and enter the gate bowing humbly; We will [then] forgive you your sins. We will increase the doers of good [in goodness and reward]."
interpretation: This verse is a reminder of the blessings and favors bestowed upon the Children of Israel by Allah. They were commanded to settle in a particular city, where they would find abundance and could eat freely from its provisions. They were also instructed to seek forgiveness for their sins and enter the city gate with humility and submission to Allah. In return, Allah promised to forgive their sins and increase the rewards of those who do good deeds. This verse emphasizes the importance of obedience to Allah's commands, seeking His forgiveness, and approaching Him with humility and gratitude for His blessings. It also highlights the fact that Allah rewards those who perform good deeds and live righteously.
orig: وإذ قيل لهم اسكنوا هذه القرية وكلوا منها حيث شئتم وقولوا حطة وادخلوا الباب سجدا نغفر لكم خطيئاتكم سنزيد المحسنين

translation: But those who wronged among them changed [the words] to a statement other than that which had been said to them. So We sent upon them a punishment from the sky for the wrong that they were doing.
interpretation: This verse highlights the consequences of disobeying Allah's commands and changing His words. When a group of people deliberately alter the divine message and persist in their wrongdoing, they invite Allah's punishment upon themselves. The verse implies that defying Allah's instructions and manipulating His words is a grave sin that can lead to severe repercussions, such as a punishment from the sky. It serves as a warning to those who might consider distorting or disregarding the divine revelation for their own interests or desires, emphasizing the importance of adhering to Allah's guidance faithfully.
orig: فبدل الذين ظلموا منهم قولا غير الذي قيل لهم فأرسلنا عليهم رجزا من السماء بما كانوا يظلمون

translation: And ask them about the town that was by the sea - when they transgressed in [the matter of] the sabbath - when their fish came to them openly on their sabbath day, and the day they had no sabbath they did not come to them. Thus did We give them trial because they were defiantly disobedient.
interpretation: This verse is a reminder of the consequences of disobeying Allah's commands. The people of the town were tested by Allah when the fish would come to them abundantly on the day of Sabbath, which was the day they were commanded to dedicate solely to worship. However, they gave in to their greed and violated the sanctity of the Sabbath by catching the fish. As a result, Allah punished them for their transgression and defiant disobedience. This serves as a lesson for all believers to prioritize obedience to Allah over worldly temptations and to fear the consequences of sin.
orig: واسألهم عن القرية التي كانت حاضرة البحر إذ يعدون في السبت إذ تأتيهم حيتانهم يوم سبتهم شرعا ويوم لا يسبتون لا تأتيهم كذلك نبلوهم بما كانوا يفسقون

translation: And when a community among them said, "Why do you advise [or warn] a people whom Allah is [about] to destroy or to punish with a severe punishment?" They [the advisors] said, "To be absolved before your Lord and perhaps they may fear Him."
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of enjoining good and forbidding evil, even in the face of seemingly insurmountable odds. The advisors in the verse continue to warn and admonish the wrongdoers, despite knowing that Allah has decreed their destruction or severe punishment. They do so to fulfill their moral obligation and to be absolved of any blame before Allah. This demonstrates the significance of standing up for what is right and speaking truth to power, regardless of the consequences. Additionally, the verse suggests that there is always hope for repentance and reform, as the advisors mention the possibility that the wrongdoers may become mindful of Allah and change their ways.
orig: وإذ قالت أمة منهم لم تعظون قوما الله مهلكهم أو معذبهم عذابا شديدا قالوا معذرة إلى ربكم ولعلهم يتقون

translation: So when they forgot that by which they had been reminded, We saved those who had forbidden evil and seized those who wronged, with a wretched punishment, because they were defiantly disobeying.
interpretation: This verse highlights the consequences of heedlessness and the importance of forbidding evil. When people forget the reminders and warnings sent to them by God and persist in their wrongdoings, a distinction is made between two groups: those who actively forbid evil and those who engage in it. God saves and protects the former group, while the latter faces a severe punishment for their defiant disobedience. This interpretation emphasizes the significance of standing up against evil, as it can lead to salvation, while turning a blind eye to it or engaging in it can result in severe consequences decreed by God.
orig: فلما نسوا ما ذكروا به أنجينا الذين ينهون عن السوء وأخذنا الذين ظلموا بعذاب بئيس بما كانوا يفسقون

translation: So when they were insolent about that which they had been forbidden, We said to them, "Be apes, despised."
interpretation: This verse is a warning to those who persistently and arrogantly disobey God's commands. It refers to a group of people who were told not to violate the Sabbath but did so anyway out of defiance. As punishment for their disobedience, God transformed them into apes, a lowly and despised form. The verse emphasizes the severity of deliberately going against divine orders and showcases God's power to disgrace the disobedient in this life before the ultimate punishment in the Hereafter. It serves as a reminder for believers to humble themselves before God and to obey His commands, lest they face a similar fate of humiliation and debasement.
orig: فلما عتوا عن ما نهوا عنه قلنا لهم كونوا قردة خاسئين

translation: And [mention] when your Lord declared that He would surely [continue to] send upon them until the Day of Resurrection those who would afflict them with the worst torment. Indeed, your Lord is swift in penalty; but indeed, He is Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse is a reminder of Allah's promise to punish the wrongdoers until the Day of Judgment. It emphasizes that Allah's punishment is severe and swift for those who persist in their wrongdoings. However, the verse also highlights Allah's attributes of forgiveness and mercy, indicating that even though He punishes the sinners, He is always ready to forgive those who sincerely repent and seek His mercy. This verse serves as a warning for the disbelievers and a source of hope for the believers, encouraging them to turn to Allah and seek His forgiveness.
orig: وإذ تأذن ربك ليبعثن عليهم إلى يوم القيامة من يسومهم سوء العذاب إن ربك لسريع العقاب وإنه لغفور رحيم

translation: And We divided them throughout the earth into nations. Of them some were righteous, and of them some were otherwise. And We tested them with good [times] and bad that perhaps they would return [to obedience].
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine wisdom behind the dispersion of people into different nations and communities across the earth. It suggests that this division serves as a test for humanity, with some being righteous and others deviating from the right path. God tests people with both good times and hardships to see who will remain faithful and return to obedience. The trials and tribulations faced by individuals and communities are meant to encourage introspection, repentance, and a return to God's path. The verse emphasizes the importance of remaining steadfast in faith and righteousness, regardless of the circumstances one faces in life.
orig: وقطعناهم في الأرض أمما منهم الصالحون ومنهم دون ذلك وبلوناهم بالحسنات والسيئات لعلهم يرجعون

translation: But there followed them successors who inherited the Scripture [while] taking the commodities of this lower life and saying, "It will be forgiven for us." And if an offer like it comes to them, they will [again] take it. Was not the covenant of the Scripture taken from them that they would not say about Allah except the truth, and they studied what was in it? And the home of the Hereafter is better for those who fear Allah, so will you not use reason?
interpretation: This verse is criticizing those who inherited the divine scriptures but became preoccupied with worldly gains and pleasures, assuming they will be forgiven for such negligence. They broke the covenant that they would follow the truth in the scriptures. The verse reminds that the rewards of the Hereafter are far better for the righteous and pious, and encourages using reason to realize this and follow the straight path rather than being distracted by fleeting worldly temptations. It's a warning against religious hypocrisy and emphasizes sincerity and commitment to divine teachings.
orig: فخلف من بعدهم خلف ورثوا الكتاب يأخذون عرض هذا الأدنى ويقولون سيغفر لنا وإن يأتهم عرض مثله يأخذوه ألم يؤخذ عليهم ميثاق الكتاب أن لا يقولوا على الله إلا الحق ودرسوا ما فيه والدار الآخرة خير للذين يتقون أفلا تعقلون

translation: And those who hold fast to the Book and establish prayer - indeed, We will not allow to be lost the reward of the reformers.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of adhering to the teachings of the Qur'an and establishing regular prayer. It assures those who do so that Allah will not let their efforts and good deeds go to waste. The "reformers" mentioned here are those who strive to improve themselves and their society by following the guidance of the Qur'an and living righteously. The verse serves as an encouragement and promise of reward for those who remain steadfast in their faith and good works, even in the face of challenges or difficulties.
orig: والذين يمسكون بالكتاب وأقاموا الصلاة إنا لا نضيع أجر المصلحين

translation: And [recall] when We raised the mountain above them as if it was a dark cloud and they were certain that it would fall upon them, [and Allah said], "Take what We have given you with determination and remember what is in it that you might fear Allah."
interpretation: This verse is a reminder of the covenant that Allah made with the Children of Israel. The raising of the mountain above them symbolizes the gravity and importance of the covenant, and the fear they felt at the time. The verse emphasizes the need for the believers to hold firmly to the teachings and commandments of Allah, and to remember them constantly in order to attain righteousness and piety. It is a call to take the divine message seriously and to strive to live by it with sincerity and devotion.
orig: وإذ نتقنا الجبل فوقهم كأنه ظلة وظنوا أنه واقع بهم خذوا ما آتيناكم بقوة واذكروا ما فيه لعلكم تتقون

translation: And [mention] when your Lord took from the children of Adam - from their loins - their descendants and made them testify of themselves, [saying to them], "Am I not your Lord?" They said, "Yes, we have testified." [This] - lest you should say on the day of Resurrection, "Indeed, we were of this unaware."
interpretation: This verse refers to the concept of the primordial covenant, where Allah took a covenant from all of humanity before their existence in this world, acknowledging Him as their Lord. This event is said to have taken place when Allah extracted all of the future progeny of Adam from his loins and made them bear witness that He is their Lord. The purpose of this covenant is to remind humans of their inherent recognition of Allah's lordship and to leave them no excuse for disbelief or polytheism on the Day of Judgment. It emphasizes the innate human nature to believe in the oneness of Allah and serves as a reminder of the consequences of forgetting this covenant.
orig: وإذ أخذ ربك من بني آدم من ظهورهم ذريتهم وأشهدهم على أنفسهم ألست بربكم قالوا بلى شهدنا أن تقولوا يوم القيامة إنا كنا عن هذا غافلين

translation: Or lest you say, "It was only that our fathers associated [others in worship] with Allah before, and we were but descendants after them. Then would You destroy us for what the falsifiers have done?"
interpretation: This verse warns against the excuse of blindly following the misguided practices of one's ancestors. It suggests that people should not use the argument that they are merely continuing the polytheistic ways of their forefathers as a justification for their own wrongdoing. The verse implies that each individual is responsible for their own beliefs and actions, and cannot blame their fate on the mistakes of previous generations. It emphasizes that Allah's judgment and punishment is based on one's own deeds, not those of their ancestors. The verse encourages breaking free from the cycle of inherited misguidance and embracing the truth of Islam.
orig: أو تقولوا إنما أشرك آباؤنا من قبل وكنا ذرية من بعدهم أفتهلكنا بما فعل المبطلون

translation: And thus We explain in detail the signs, and perhaps they may return.
interpretation: In this verse, Allah is emphasizing the importance and purpose of providing detailed explanations of His signs and revelations in the Qur'an. The detailed explanations serve as a means of guidance and a reminder for people, with the hope that they may recognize the truth, reflect upon their actions, and return to the righteous path. This verse highlights the Qur'an's role as a source of guidance and its potential to inspire people to turn back to Allah in repentance and obedience.
orig: وكذلك نفصل الآيات ولعلهم يرجعون

translation: And recite to them, [O Muhammad], the news of him to whom we gave [knowledge of] Our signs, but he detached himself from them; so Satan pursued him, and he became of the deviators.
interpretation: This verse is a warning against turning away from the guidance of Allah after having received it. It refers to a man who was given knowledge of Allah's signs, but he chose to abandon them and follow the path of Satan instead. As a result, he became misguided and lost. The verse emphasizes the importance of holding fast to the truth and the guidance of Allah, and the dangers of allowing oneself to be led astray by the temptations and deceptions of Satan. It serves as a reminder to the believers to remain steadfast in their faith and to seek Allah's protection from the whispers and influence of Satan.
orig: واتل عليهم نبأ الذي آتيناه آياتنا فانسلخ منها فأتبعه الشيطان فكان من الغاوين

translation: And if We had willed, We could have elevated him thereby, but he adhered [instead] to the earth and followed his own desire. So his example is like that of the dog: if you chase him, he pants, or if you leave him, he [still] pants. That is the example of the people who denied Our signs. So relate the stories that perhaps they will give thought.
interpretation: This verse is a reminder that worldly desires and attachments can lead us astray from the path of righteousness. The person mentioned in the verse was given the opportunity to elevate himself spiritually, but instead chose to remain attached to the material world and follow his own whims and desires. The analogy of the dog panting, whether it is chased or left alone, illustrates how those who are consumed by their desires will never find true contentment or peace. They will always be in a state of restlessness and agitation, just like the panting dog. The verse encourages us to reflect on the stories and examples in the Qur'an, so that we may learn from them and avoid falling into the same traps of worldly temptations and distractions from our higher purpose.
orig: ولو شئنا لرفعناه بها ولكنه أخلد إلى الأرض واتبع هواه فمثله كمثل الكلب إن تحمل عليه يلهث أو تتركه يلهث ذلك مثل القوم الذين كذبوا بآياتنا فاقصص القصص لعلهم يتفكرون

translation: How evil an example [is that of] the people who denied Our signs and used to wrong themselves.
interpretation: This verse is a strong condemnation of those who reject God's messages and signs, and instead choose to oppress and wrong themselves through their disbelief and misdeeds. It suggests that such people set a terrible example for others to follow. By denying the truth and acting unjustly, they bring harm upon their own souls. The verse implies that faith in God's signs and living righteously are essential for one's own spiritual well-being and for setting a positive example in society.
orig: ساء مثلا القوم الذين كذبوا بآياتنا وأنفسهم كانوا يظلمون

translation: Whoever Allah guides - it is he who is the [rightly] guided. And whoever He sends astray - it is those who are the losers.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that true guidance comes only from Allah. Those whom Allah guides are the ones who are truly guided and will attain success, while those whom Allah leaves to stray due to their own actions and choices are the ultimate losers in this world and the Hereafter. It highlights the importance of seeking Allah's guidance and the consequences of turning away from it. The verse also affirms Allah's absolute control and wisdom over the guidance or misguidance of individuals based on His divine knowledge and justice.
orig: من يهد الله فهو المهتدي ومن يضلل فأولئك هم الخاسرون

translation: And We have certainly created for Hell many of the jinn and mankind. They have hearts with which they do not understand, they have eyes with which they do not see, and they have ears with which they do not hear. Those are like livestock; rather, they are more astray. It is they who are the heedless.
interpretation: This verse is a stern warning to those who are heedless and do not use their God-given faculties of understanding, sight, and hearing to recognize the truth and follow the right path. Despite having the means to perceive and comprehend, they choose to remain blind and deaf to the signs and guidance of Allah. As a result, they are likened to animals or even considered worse, because animals follow their instincts while these people deliberately reject the truth. Their hearts are sealed, their eyes are blind, and their ears are deaf to the message of Islam. They are heedless of their purpose in life and their ultimate fate in the Hereafter, and thus they are condemned to Hell for their willful ignorance and disobedience.
orig: ولقد ذرأنا لجهنم كثيرا من الجن والإنس لهم قلوب لا يفقهون بها ولهم أعين لا يبصرون بها ولهم آذان لا يسمعون بها أولئك كالأنعام بل هم أضل أولئك هم الغافلون

translation: And to Allah belong the best names, so invoke Him by them. And leave [the company of] those who practice deviation concerning His names. They will be recompensed for what they have been doing.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of using the beautiful names of Allah when invoking Him in prayer or supplication. It suggests that these names represent His divine attributes and qualities, and that by calling upon Him using these names, one can establish a closer connection with Him. The verse also warns against those who deviate from the proper use of Allah's names, either by denying them, distorting their meanings, or associating them with false deities. It asserts that such people will face consequences for their actions, implying that the misuse of Allah's names is a serious transgression. The interpretation highlights the significance of respecting and properly utilizing the divine names as a means of worship and spiritual connection with Allah.
orig: ولله الأسماء الحسنى فادعوه بها وذروا الذين يلحدون في أسمائه سيجزون ما كانوا يعملون

translation: And among those We created is a community which guides by truth and thereby establishes justice.
interpretation: This verse highlights the existence of a righteous community among the people created by Allah. This community is characterized by their adherence to the truth and their commitment to establishing justice. They guide others to the right path through their actions and words, setting an example of righteousness and fairness. The verse implies that this community serves as a beacon of guidance and a model for others to follow in terms of upholding the truth and maintaining justice in society. It emphasizes the importance of having a group of people who actively promote and embody these virtuous qualities, as they play a crucial role in leading others towards goodness and creating a just and harmonious society.
orig: وممن خلقنا أمة يهدون بالحق وبه يعدلون

translation: Those who deny Our signs, We will progressively lead them [to destruction] from where they do not know.
interpretation: This verse is a warning to those who reject the signs and messages of Allah. It means that Allah will gradually lead such people astray, drawing them further into their disbelief and wrongdoing. They will be unaware of the ultimate consequences of their actions, thinking that they are doing well or that there is no accountability. However, this is a form of divine punishment, as they are being led down a path of self-destruction without realizing it. The verse emphasizes the importance of heeding the signs and guidance of Allah to avoid such a fate.
orig: والذين كذبوا بآياتنا سنستدرجهم من حيث لا يعلمون

translation: And I will give them time. Indeed, my plan is firm.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the patience and planning of Allah. He gives the wrongdoers time and respite, letting them enjoy temporary pleasures, but this is all part of His wise plan. They should not be deceived by this seeming reprieve, because in reality, Allah's plan against them is firm and will come to pass at the appointed time. It is a warning not to be misled by the apparent success of evil, as the ultimate victory belongs to Allah and those who are righteous. The verse underscores Allah's wisdom, power and control over all affairs.
orig: وأملي لهم إن كيدي متين

translation: And have they not reflected? There is no madness in their companion [Muhammad]. He is not but a clear warner.
interpretation: This verse is a reminder for people to reflect upon the character and mission of Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him). It asserts that he is not a man afflicted with madness or insanity, but rather a messenger of Allah whose duty is to warn people and deliver the clear message of Islam. The verse encourages people to ponder and recognize the truth of his prophethood, as his teachings and actions demonstrate clarity of mind and purpose, not the ramblings of a madman. It is an invitation to approach his message with an open heart and mind, and to acknowledge him as the final prophet sent by Allah to guide humanity.
orig: أولم يتفكروا ما بصاحبهم من جنة إن هو إلا نذير مبين

translation: Do they not look into the realm of the heavens and the earth and everything that Allah has created and [think] that perhaps their appointed time has come near? So in what statement hereafter will they believe?
interpretation: This verse is a call for people to reflect deeply on the signs of Allah's creation in the heavens and the earth, and to recognize that their time on this earth is limited. It suggests that if people truly contemplated the wonders of the universe and the inevitability of death, they would be more likely to believe in the truth of Allah's message and the Hereafter. The verse implies that those who fail to heed this call and do not believe in the Qur'an will have no excuse on the Day of Judgment, as they had ample opportunity to reflect on the signs and embrace faith.
orig: أولم ينظروا في ملكوت السماوات والأرض وما خلق الله من شيء وأن عسى أن يكون قد اقترب أجلهم فبأي حديث بعده يؤمنون

translation: Whoever Allah leaves astray - there is no guide for him. And He leaves them in their transgression, wandering blindly.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that guidance and misguidance are ultimately in the hands of Allah. When Allah chooses to let someone go astray due to their own actions and choices, no one can guide them back to the right path. Allah will leave such people in their state of rebellion and disobedience, allowing them to continue in their wrongdoing and confusion. They will wander aimlessly, spiritually blind and lost, as a consequence of their own decisions to turn away from Allah's guidance. This highlights the importance of sincerely seeking Allah's guidance and striving to stay on the straight path, as well as the grave danger of persisting in transgression and earning Allah's displeasure.
orig: من يضلل الله فلا هادي له ويذرهم في طغيانهم يعمهون

translation: They ask you, [O Muhammad], about the Hour: when is its arrival? Say, "Its knowledge is only with my Lord. None will reveal its time except Him. It lays heavily upon the heavens and the earth. It will not come upon you except unexpectedly." They ask you as if you are familiar with it. Say, "Its knowledge is only with Allah, but most of the people do not know."
interpretation: This verse speaks to the fact that knowledge of the exact timing of the Day of Judgment (the Hour) is known only to Allah. Even the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) did not have this knowledge. It emphasizes that the coming of the Hour will be sudden and unexpected. The heaviness in the heavens and earth could refer to the momentous nature of that event and its impact on all of creation. The repeated questioning by the people shows their curiosity and concern about it. However, the verse makes it clear that such knowledge is exclusively with Allah, and most people, despite their questions and speculations, do not truly comprehend this reality.
orig: يسألونك عن الساعة أيان مرساها قل إنما علمها عند ربي لا يجليها لوقتها إلا هو ثقلت في السماوات والأرض لا تأتيكم إلا بغتة يسألونك كأنك حفي عنها قل إنما علمها عند الله ولكن أكثر الناس لا يعلمون

translation: Say, "I hold not for myself [the power of] benefit or harm, except what Allah has willed. And if I knew the unseen, I could have acquired much wealth, and no harm would have touched me. I am not except a warner and a bringer of good tidings to a people who believe."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the limitations of human knowledge and power, even for a prophet like Muhammad (peace be upon him). It highlights that only Allah has the power to bring about benefit or harm, and that knowledge of the unseen belongs to Him alone. If the Prophet had access to such knowledge, he could have used it for his own advantage, avoiding harm and acquiring wealth. However, his role is not to predict the future or control events, but to serve as a warner to those who disbelieve and a bearer of good news for those who have faith. This interpretation underscores the importance of humility, submission to Allah's will, and the recognition that true power and knowledge belong to Him alone.
orig: قل لا أملك لنفسي نفعا ولا ضرا إلا ما شاء الله ولو كنت أعلم الغيب لاستكثرت من الخير وما مسني السوء إن أنا إلا نذير وبشير لقوم يؤمنون

translation: It is He who created you from one soul and created from it its mate that he might dwell in security with her. And when he covers her, she carries a light burden and continues therein. And when it becomes heavy, they both invoke Allah, their Lord, "If You should give us a good [child], we will surely be among the grateful."
interpretation: This verse highlights the deep connection and intimacy between a husband and wife. It reminds us that men and women were created from a single soul, and that marriage is a means for them to find comfort and security in one another. The verse also emphasizes the importance of gratitude and supplication during pregnancy, as the couple turns to Allah in hope and prayer for a righteous child. This serves as a lesson for all couples to approach pregnancy with a sense of spiritual responsibility and to recognize children as a blessing from Allah.
orig: هو الذي خلقكم من نفس واحدة وجعل منها زوجها ليسكن إليها فلما تغشاها حملت حملا خفيفا فمرت به فلما أثقلت دعوا الله ربهما لئن آتيتنا صالحا لنكونن من الشاكرين

translation: But when He gave them a good [child], they attributed to Him partners in that which He had given them. But Allah is exalted above what they associate with Him.
interpretation: This verse is criticizing the attitude of some people who, after being blessed by Allah with a righteous child, start associating partners with Allah in that blessing. They may attribute their child's good qualities or achievements to other factors rather than acknowledging them as a favor from Allah alone. The verse emphasizes that Allah is far above and free from any partners that people may wrongly attribute to Him. It highlights the importance of maintaining pure monotheism and gratitude to Allah, recognizing that all blessings come solely from Him without any partners or associates.
orig: فلما آتاهما صالحا جعلا له شركاء فيما آتاهما فتعالى الله عما يشركون

translation: Do they associate with Him those who create nothing and they are [themselves] created?
interpretation: This verse is criticizing the polytheists who worship idols and false gods alongside Allah. It points out the absurdity of their belief by highlighting that these idols and false gods are themselves created beings, incapable of creating anything, yet the polytheists ascribe to them a share of divinity with Allah. The rhetorical question emphasizes the irrationality of their idolatry and encourages reflection on the exclusive right of Allah, as the sole Creator, to be worshipped without any partners associated with Him.
orig: أيشركون ما لا يخلق شيئا وهم يخلقون

translation: And they are unable to [give] them help, nor can they help themselves.
interpretation: This verse highlights the powerlessness and helplessness of false deities or idols that people worship besides Allah. These false gods are not only incapable of providing any assistance or support to their worshippers, but they are also unable to defend or protect themselves. This emphasizes the futility of worshipping anything or anyone other than Allah, as He is the only One who possesses the power to help, protect, and guide His creation. The verse serves as a reminder to humans that relying on false deities is a fruitless endeavor and that they should direct their worship and seek help only from Allah, the Almighty.
orig: ولا يستطيعون لهم نصرا ولا أنفسهم ينصرون

translation: And if you invite them to guidance, they will not follow you. It is all the same for you whether you invite them or you remain silent.
interpretation: This verse highlights the stubbornness and resistance of those who reject the message of Islam, even when they are invited to the truth. It suggests that the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and the believers should not be disheartened by the disbelievers' lack of response to their call, as it is ultimately their choice to accept or reject guidance. The verse implies that the duty of the believers is to convey the message, while the outcome is in the hands of Allah. It also emphasizes the importance of remaining steadfast in one's faith, regardless of the reaction of others.
orig: وإن تدعوهم إلى الهدى لا يتبعوكم سواء عليكم أدعوتموهم أم أنتم صامتون

translation: Indeed, those you call upon besides Allah are servants like you. So call upon them and let them respond to you, if you should be truthful.
interpretation: This verse challenges the polytheists who worship idols and other deities besides Allah. It asserts that these objects of worship are merely created beings, just like the worshippers themselves, and have no power or ability to respond to their calls or provide them with any benefit or harm. The verse demands that the polytheists call upon their false gods and see if they answer their prayers, exposing the futility and falsehood of their beliefs. It emphasizes that only Allah, the One True God, is worthy of worship and that all other objects of worship are powerless and false.
orig: إن الذين تدعون من دون الله عباد أمثالكم فادعوهم فليستجيبوا لكم إن كنتم صادقين

translation: Do they have feet by which they walk? Or do they have hands by which they strike? Or do they have eyes by which they see? Or do they have ears by which they hear? Say, "Invoke your 'partners' and then conspire against me and give me no respite.
interpretation: This verse challenges the idolaters who associate partners with Allah. It questions whether their false gods possess any physical attributes or abilities that would make them worthy of worship. The rhetorical questions highlight the absurdity of their beliefs, as their idols are merely inanimate objects without any power or perception. The verse then challenges the idolaters to call upon their supposed partners and plot against the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him), emphasizing the futility of their actions and the ultimate power and protection of Allah over His messenger.
orig: ألهم أرجل يمشون بها أم لهم أيد يبطشون بها أم لهم أعين يبصرون بها أم لهم آذان يسمعون بها قل ادعوا شركاءكم ثم كيدون فلا تنظرون

translation: Indeed, my protector is Allah, who has sent down the Book; and He is an ally to the righteous.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah is the ultimate protector and guardian of the believers. It affirms that Allah has revealed the Qur'an as a guide for humanity and that He supports and takes care of those who are righteous and follow His guidance. The verse encourages the believers to put their trust in Allah and seek His protection, knowing that He will always be there for them and will never abandon them as long as they strive to live a righteous life according to the teachings of the Qur'an.
orig: إن وليي الله الذي نزل الكتاب وهو يتولى الصالحين

translation: And those whom you invoke other than Him are unable to help you, nor can they help themselves.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the powerlessness and inability of false gods and idols that people worship besides Allah. It points out that these false deities are incapable of providing any assistance or benefit to their worshippers, and they cannot even help or defend themselves. This highlights the futility and irrationality of worshipping anyone or anything other than Allah, as He alone possesses the power and ability to help and support His creation. The verse encourages people to direct their worship, supplication, and reliance solely towards Allah, as He is the only One worthy of worship and the only One capable of responding to the needs of His servants.
orig: والذين تدعون من دونه لا يستطيعون نصركم ولا أنفسهم ينصرون

translation: And if you invite them to guidance, they do not hear; and you see them looking at you while they do not see.
interpretation: This verse highlights the spiritual blindness and deafness of those who reject divine guidance. Despite the clear signs and invitations to the truth, they remain unmoved and unresponsive. They may appear to be looking at the messenger, but in reality, they lack true perception and understanding. Their hearts are sealed, preventing them from recognizing and accepting the truth. This state of spiritual insensitivity is a result of their choice to turn away from God's guidance and persist in their disbelief. The verse emphasizes the importance of open-heartedness and willingness to receive guidance, without which one remains in a state of spiritual darkness.
orig: وإن تدعوهم إلى الهدى لا يسمعوا وتراهم ينظرون إليك وهم لا يبصرون

translation: Show forgiveness, enjoin what is good, and turn away from the ignorant.
interpretation: This verse encourages Muslims to adopt a gentle and forgiving attitude in their dealings with others, even in the face of provocation or ignorance. It advises them to actively promote what is right and good, and to avoid engaging with those who are foolish or ignorant. The verse emphasizes the importance of taking the moral high ground, focusing on positive actions, and not being drawn into fruitless arguments or conflicts with those who lack understanding. It promotes the virtues of patience, wisdom, and leading by example in one's conduct and interactions with others.
orig: خذ العفو وأمر بالعرف وأعرض عن الجاهلين

translation: And if an evil suggestion comes to you from Satan, then seek refuge in Allah. Indeed, He is Hearing and Knowing.
interpretation: This verse advises Muslims to seek protection in Allah whenever they are tempted by the whisperings of Satan. It reminds us that Allah is all-hearing and all-knowing, and He is aware of the struggles and temptations we face. By turning to Him and seeking His protection, we can overcome the evil suggestions of Satan and stay on the right path. This highlights the importance of maintaining a strong connection with Allah and relying on Him for guidance and support in the face of temptation and sin.
orig: وإما ينزغنك من الشيطان نزغ فاستعذ بالله إنه سميع عليم

translation: Indeed, those who fear Allah - when an impulse touches them from Satan, they remember [Him] and at once they have insight.
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of taqwa (God-consciousness) in protecting believers from the whisperings and temptations of Satan. When the righteous are faced with evil thoughts or desires inspired by the devil, they immediately remember Allah and seek His protection. This remembrance of God grants them clarity of mind and heart, allowing them to see through the deceptions of Satan and remain steadfast on the right path. The verse emphasizes that the key to resisting temptation lies in maintaining a strong connection with Allah and turning to Him in times of spiritual struggle.
orig: إن الذين اتقوا إذا مسهم طائف من الشيطان تذكروا فإذا هم مبصرون

translation: And their brothers extend them in error; then they do not stop short.
interpretation: This verse refers to the disbelievers who are led further astray by their fellow disbelievers. The "brothers" here are those who share in disbelief, and they encourage and support each other in their misguidance and deviation from the truth. They continue to persist in their false beliefs and sinful actions without relenting or desisting. It highlights the dangerous influence of bad company and how it can lead one to remain entrenched in wrongdoing, making it more difficult to find the right path.
orig: وإخوانهم يمدونهم في الغي ثم لا يقصرون

translation: And when you do not bring them a sign, they say, "Why have you not contrived it?" Say, "I only follow what is revealed to me from my Lord. This [Qur'an] is enlightenment from your Lord and guidance and mercy for a people who believe."
interpretation: This verse is addressing the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and the disbelievers who demanded that he produce miracles or signs to prove his prophethood.
