The verse emphasizes that such actions are truly evil and blameworthy in the sight of Allah. It serves as a warning against prioritizing material gains over faith and righteousness, and highlights the severity of leading others astray from the truth.
orig: اشتروا بآيات الله ثمنا قليلا فصدوا عن سبيله إنهم ساء ما كانوا يعملون

translation: They do not observe toward a believer any pact of kinship or covenant of protection. And it is they who are the transgressors.
interpretation: This verse is referring to the disbelievers who do not respect any ties of kinship or agreements of protection with the believers. They are willing to violate their oaths and commitments without any regard for the consequences. Such people are considered transgressors and wrongdoers in the sight of Allah because they fail to uphold their end of covenants and treat the believers unjustly despite their pledges. It highlights the treacherous nature of those who oppose the believers and their lack of trustworthiness in honoring their obligations.
orig: لا يرقبون في مؤمن إلا ولا ذمة وأولئك هم المعتدون

translation: But if they repent, establish prayer, and give zakah, then they are your brothers in religion; and We detail the verses for a people who know.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of forgiveness and unity among believers. If those who have strayed from the right path sincerely repent, fulfill their religious obligations such as prayer and giving charity, then they should be accepted back into the fold of the Muslim community as brothers and sisters in faith. The Qur'an provides clear guidance and detailed verses to those who seek knowledge and understanding, so that they may discern the right course of action and live in harmony with their fellow believers.
orig: فإن تابوا وأقاموا الصلاة وآتوا الزكاة فإخوانكم في الدين ونفصل الآيات لقوم يعلمون

translation: And if they break their oaths after their treaty and defame your religion, then fight the leaders of disbelief, for indeed, there are no oaths [sacred] to them; [fight them that] they might cease.
interpretation: This verse is instructing the Muslims to fight against those who break their treaties and mock or insult Islam, specifically the leaders of disbelief. It suggests that such people cannot be trusted to uphold their oaths and agreements. The purpose of fighting them is to make them desist from their hostility and attacks against the religion. The verse implies that when the other party breaks a treaty, the Muslims are no longer bound by it either and are justified in fighting to defend their faith and community.
orig: وإن نكثوا أيمانهم من بعد عهدهم وطعنوا في دينكم فقاتلوا أئمة الكفر إنهم لا أيمان لهم لعلهم ينتهون

translation: Would you not fight a people who broke their oaths and determined to expel the Messenger, and they had begun [the attack upon] you the first time? Do you fear them? But Allah has more right that you should fear Him, if you are [truly] believers.
interpretation: This verse is encouraging the believers to fight against those who have broken their treaties, plotted to expel the Prophet (peace be upon him), and initiated hostilities against the Muslims. It reminds the believers that they should fear Allah above all else, as He is more deserving of their reverence and obedience. The verse emphasizes that true faith requires standing up against oppression and defending the cause of Islam, even if it means confronting formidable enemies. It also highlights the importance of fulfilling one's commitments and the gravity of breaking oaths, especially when they pertain to matters of faith and community.
orig: ألا تقاتلون قوما نكثوا أيمانهم وهموا بإخراج الرسول وهم بدءوكم أول مرة أتخشونهم فالله أحق أن تخشوه إن كنتم مؤمنين

translation: Fight them; Allah will punish them by your hands and will disgrace them and give you victory over them and satisfy the breasts of a believing people.
interpretation: This verse encourages the believers to fight against the disbelievers, with the promise that Allah will support them and grant them victory. It suggests that through this fight, the believers will be able to alleviate the pain and anguish in their hearts caused by the disbelievers' actions. The verse implies that fighting against the enemies of Islam is a means to attain spiritual satisfaction and inner peace, as it is a way of fulfilling one's duty towards Allah and defending the faith. It also emphasizes the idea that the ultimate victory belongs to Allah and that He will punish the disbelievers through the hands of the believers, bringing disgrace upon them.
orig: قاتلوهم يعذبهم الله بأيديكم ويخزهم وينصركم عليهم ويشف صدور قوم مؤمنين

translation: And He removes the anger of their hearts. And Allah turns in forgiveness to whom He wills; and Allah is Knowing and Wise.
interpretation: This verse highlights Allah's infinite mercy and wisdom. It conveys that Allah has the power to remove anger, resentment, and ill feelings from people's hearts. He forgives whomever He chooses, granting them peace and tranquility. The mention of Allah's attributes of being "Knowing and Wise" emphasizes that His decisions are based on His perfect knowledge and understanding of His creation. It serves as a reminder for believers to seek Allah's forgiveness, strive to purify their hearts, and trust in His wisdom, as He knows what is best for each individual.
orig: ويذهب غيظ قلوبهم ويتوب الله على من يشاء والله عليم حكيم

translation: Or do you think that you will be left [as you are] while Allah has not yet made evident those among you who strive [for His cause] and do not take other than Allah, His Messenger and the believers as intimates? And Allah is Acquainted with what you do.
interpretation: This verse is a reminder to the believers that Allah will test them to distinguish the sincere and steadfast among them from those who are weak in faith. It emphasizes that true believers should have loyalty only to Allah, His Messenger, and the community of believers, and not form close alliances with those outside this circle. The verse also affirms that Allah is fully aware of all actions and intentions, implying that He will judge people based on their deeds and the sincerity of their faith.
orig: أم حسبتم أن تتركوا ولما يعلم الله الذين جاهدوا منكم ولم يتخذوا من دون الله ولا رسوله ولا المؤمنين وليجة والله خبير بما تعملون

translation: It is not for the polytheists to maintain the mosques of Allah [while] witnessing against themselves with disbelief. [For] those, their deeds have become worthless, and in the Fire they will abide eternally.
interpretation: This verse conveys that those who associate partners with Allah (polytheists) have no right to maintain or frequent the mosques of Allah while openly acknowledging their disbelief. Their insincere acts of worship and good deeds are rendered void and meaningless due to their polytheism. As a consequence of their disbelief, they will be condemned to the eternal punishment of the Hellfire in the Hereafter. This highlights the severity of the sin of polytheism (shirk) and its incompatibility with the maintenance of Allah's places of worship.
orig: ما كان للمشركين أن يعمروا مساجد الله شاهدين على أنفسهم بالكفر أولئك حبطت أعمالهم وفي النار هم خالدون

translation: The mosques of Allah are only to be maintained by those who believe in Allah and the Last Day and establish prayer and give zakah and do not fear except Allah, for it is expected that those will be of the [rightly] guided.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the true caretakers and frequenters of Allah's mosques are those who have sincere faith in Allah and the Day of Judgment. They are steadfast in establishing prayer, giving obligatory charity (zakah), and fearing none but Allah. These qualities demonstrate their righteousness and devotion, making them worthy of being considered among the rightly guided individuals who maintain and worship in the mosques. It suggests that mere physical presence in the mosque is not enough; rather, it must be accompanied by sincere faith, righteous deeds, and a heart that is focused on pleasing Allah alone.
orig: إنما يعمر مساجد الله من آمن بالله واليوم الآخر وأقام الصلاة وآتى الزكاة ولم يخش إلا الله فعسى أولئك أن يكونوا من المهتدين

translation: Do you consider the providing of water for the pilgrims and the maintenance of al-Masjid al-Haram as equal to [the deeds of] one who believes in Allah and the Last Day and strives in the cause of Allah? They are not equal in the sight of Allah. And Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that mere outward acts of worship like providing water to pilgrims or maintaining the Sacred Mosque are not equal in merit to true faith, belief in the Hereafter, and striving in God's cause. It suggests that what matters most is the sincerity of faith and struggling for the sake of God, not just outward religious acts. Those who equate superficial good deeds with genuine faith and sacrifice are considered "wrongdoers" who are not rightly guided by God. The verse establishes a hierarchy of deeds, placing the highest value on inner conviction, preparing for the afterlife, and exerting efforts in God's way.
orig: أجعلتم سقاية الحاج وعمارة المسجد الحرام كمن آمن بالله واليوم الآخر وجاهد في سبيل الله لا يستوون عند الله والله لا يهدي القوم الظالمين

translation: Those who have believed and emigrated and striven in the cause of Allah with their wealth and their lives are greater in rank in the sight of Allah. And it is those who are the attainers [of success].
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the elevated status and ultimate success of those who demonstrate true faith through their actions. Those who sincerely believe in Allah, leave their homes and families for the sake of their faith, and strive with their possessions and their own selves to support and spread the cause of Islam are held in the highest regard by Allah. They have made immense sacrifices, prioritizing their devotion to Allah above all else. As a result of their unwavering commitment and selflessness, they will be the ones to attain the supreme triumph of earning Allah's pleasure and being granted entry into Paradise in the Hereafter. Their sacrifices will not go unnoticed or unrewarded by Allah.
orig: الذين آمنوا وهاجروا وجاهدوا في سبيل الله بأموالهم وأنفسهم أعظم درجة عند الله وأولئك هم الفائزون

translation: Their Lord gives them good tidings of mercy from Him, and acceptance, and gardens wherein lasting pleasure will be theirs;
interpretation: This verse conveys the joyous news that the righteous believers will receive from their Lord on the Day of Judgment. Allah will grant them His mercy, which encompasses His forgiveness, protection, and blessings. They will also earn His pleasure and acceptance, indicating that He is satisfied with their faith, good deeds, and obedience during their worldly life. As a reward, they will be admitted into the gardens of Paradise, where they will experience everlasting delights, comforts, and pleasures that will never end or diminish. This verse instills hope, encourages believers to strive for righteousness, and reminds them of the immense rewards that await those who remain faithful to Allah and follow His path.
orig: يبشرهم ربهم برحمة منه ورضوان وجنات لهم فيها نعيم مقيم

translation: Abiding therein forever. Indeed, Allah has with Him a great reward.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the eternal nature of the reward that Allah has prepared for the righteous believers in Paradise. It assures them that they will remain in this state of bliss and contentment forever, without any fear of it coming to an end or being taken away from them. The verse also highlights the magnanimity and generosity of Allah, as it describes the reward He has in store as being "great" or "tremendous". This serves to motivate the believers to strive harder in their faith and good deeds, knowing that their ultimate goal is to attain this everlasting reward from their Lord. It also instills a sense of hope and optimism in the hearts of the believers, knowing that whatever hardships or challenges they may face in this temporary worldly life, they have the promise of an infinitely greater reward awaiting them in the Hereafter, by the grace and mercy of Allah.
orig: خالدين فيها أبدا إن الله عنده أجر عظيم

translation: O you who have believed, do not take your fathers or your brothers as allies if they have preferred disbelief over belief. And whoever does so among you - then it is those who are the wrongdoers.
interpretation: This verse warns the believers against taking their disbelieving family members as close allies or protectors, especially if they prefer disbelief over faith. It emphasizes that the bond of faith should take precedence over family ties when there is a conflict between the two. Those who prioritize their family relationships over their loyalty to Allah and His religion are considered wrongdoers, as they have failed to uphold the true values and principles of Islam. The verse reminds Muslims to maintain a balance between their love for family and their devotion to Allah, ensuring that their faith remains the guiding force in their lives.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا لا تتخذوا آباءكم وإخوانكم أولياء إن استحبوا الكفر على الإيمان ومن يتولهم منكم فأولئك هم الظالمون

translation: Say, [O Muhammad], "If your fathers, your sons, your brothers, your wives, your relatives, wealth which you have obtained, commerce wherein you fear decline, and dwellings with which you are pleased are more beloved to you than Allah and His Messenger and jihad in His cause, then wait until Allah executes His command. And Allah does not guide the defiantly disobedient people."
interpretation: This verse is a stark warning to those who prioritize worldly attachments and desires over their devotion to Allah and His cause. It highlights that even the most cherished relationships and possessions, such as one's family, wealth, and homes, can become a source of spiritual downfall if they are held in higher regard than one's commitment to Allah and His Messenger. The verse urges believers to examine their priorities and to be willing to sacrifice everything for the sake of Allah. It also serves as a reminder that those who choose to be disobedient to Allah will not be guided to the right path and will ultimately face the consequences of their actions.
orig: قل إن كان آباؤكم وأبناؤكم وإخوانكم وأزواجكم وعشيرتكم وأموال اقترفتموها وتجارة تخشون كسادها ومساكن ترضونها أحب إليكم من الله ورسوله وجهاد في سبيله فتربصوا حتى يأتي الله بأمره والله لا يهدي القوم الفاسقين

translation: Allah has already given you victory in many regions and [even] on the day of Hunayn, when your great number pleased you, but it did not avail you at all, and the earth was confining for you with its vastness; then you turned back, fleeing.
interpretation: This verse reminds the believers of Allah's favor upon them in granting them victory in many battles, even when they were outnumbered. It specifically mentions the Battle of Hunayn, where the Muslims were initially pleased with their large numbers but were then tested by Allah when they faced difficulties and some of them fled the battlefield. The verse emphasizes that victory comes from Allah alone, not from numerical superiority or any other worldly factor. It also implies that the believers should remain humble and reliant upon Allah, recognizing that their strength and success are ultimately from Him.
orig: لقد نصركم الله في مواطن كثيرة ويوم حنين إذ أعجبتكم كثرتكم فلم تغن عنكم شيئا وضاقت عليكم الأرض بما رحبت ثم وليتم مدبرين

translation: Then Allah sent down His tranquillity upon His Messenger and upon the believers and sent down soldiers angels whom you did not see and punished those who disbelieved. And that is the recompense of the disbelievers.
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine support and intervention that Allah provides to the believers and His Messenger in times of difficulty. The "tranquillity" mentioned refers to the inner peace, confidence, and spiritual strength that Allah bestows upon the hearts of the faithful. The unseen "soldiers" can be interpreted as angels or other forces that Allah sends to assist the believers in their struggles against the disbelievers. The verse also emphasizes that those who reject faith and oppose the message of Islam will face punishment and recompense for their actions, both in this world and in the Hereafter. It serves as a reminder that the ultimate victory belongs to Allah and those who believe in Him, even if the odds seem against them.
orig: ثم أنزل الله سكينته على رسوله وعلى المؤمنين وأنزل جنودا لم تروها وعذب الذين كفروا وذلك جزاء الكافرين

translation: Then Allah will forgive whom He wills after that. And Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's infinite mercy and forgiveness. Even after people have committed sins or wrongdoings, Allah is willing to forgive those who sincerely repent and seek His forgiveness. It shows that the door to repentance is always open, and Allah's mercy encompasses all things. The verse encourages believers to turn back to Allah and seek His forgiveness, knowing that He is the Most Forgiving and the Most Merciful. It instills hope in the hearts of those who may feel burdened by their sins, reassuring them that Allah's forgiveness knows no bounds for those who sincerely turn to Him in repentance.
orig: ثم يتوب الله من بعد ذلك على من يشاء والله غفور رحيم

translation: O you who have believed, indeed the polytheists are unclean, so let them not approach al-Masjid al-Haram after this, their [final] year. And if you fear privation, Allah will enrich you from His bounty if He wills. Indeed, Allah is Knowing and Wise.
interpretation: This verse establishes a clear distinction between the believers and the polytheists, declaring the latter as spiritually "unclean" due to their association of partners with Allah. As a result, they are prohibited from entering the sacred mosque (al-Masjid al-Haram) in Mecca after the revelation of this verse. The believers are assured that if they fear economic hardship due to the loss of trade with the polytheists, Allah will provide for them from His bounty, as He is All-Knowing and All-Wise. This verse demonstrates the importance of maintaining the purity and sanctity of Islam's holiest site and the believers' trust in Allah's provision and wisdom.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا إنما المشركون نجس فلا يقربوا المسجد الحرام بعد عامهم هذا وإن خفتم عيلة فسوف يغنيكم الله من فضله إن شاء إن الله عليم حكيم

translation: Fight those who do not believe in Allah or in the Last Day and who do not consider unlawful what Allah and His Messenger have made unlawful and who do not adopt the religion of truth from those who were given the Scripture - [fight] until they give the jizyah willingly while they are humbled.
interpretation: This verse is instructing Muslims to fight against those from the People of the Book (Jews and Christians) who do not believe in the core tenets of Islam, do not forbid what Allah and His Messenger have forbidden, and do not follow Islam as the true religion. The fighting is to continue until they agree to pay the jizyah tax while in a state of submission to Muslim rule. The jizyah was a per capita yearly tax historically levied by Islamic states on certain non-Muslim subjects as a form of tribute and state protection in exchange for exemption from military service and certain other privileges.
orig: قاتلوا الذين لا يؤمنون بالله ولا باليوم الآخر ولا يحرمون ما حرم الله ورسوله ولا يدينون دين الحق من الذين أوتوا الكتاب حتى يعطوا الجزية عن يد وهم صاغرون

translation: The Jews say, "Ezra is the son of Allah"; and the Christians say, "The Messiah is the son of Allah." That is their statement from their mouths; they imitate the saying of those who disbelieved [before them]. May Allah destroy them; how are they deluded?
interpretation: This verse criticizes the beliefs of Jews and Christians who ascribe divine sonship to Ezra and Jesus respectively. It suggests that these claims are mere utterances without basis, similar to the claims of previous disbelievers. The verse expresses a strong condemnation of these beliefs, invoking Allah's destruction upon those who hold them and expressing astonishment at how they can be so deluded in their thinking.
orig: وقالت اليهود عزير ابن الله وقالت النصارى المسيح ابن الله ذلك قولهم بأفواههم يضاهئون قول الذين كفروا من قبل قاتلهم الله أنى يؤفكون

translation: They have taken their scholars and monks as lords besides Allah, and [also] the Messiah, the son of Mary. And they were not commanded except to worship one God; there is no deity except Him. Exalted is He above whatever they associate with Him.
interpretation: This verse criticizes those who elevate religious figures to a divine status, treating them as authorities equal to or above God. It asserts that no matter how revered or influential these scholars, monks, or even the Messiah may be, they are not to be worshipped or regarded as lords alongside Allah. The verse emphasizes that all worship and obedience should be directed to the one true God alone, and that attributing divine characteristics to anyone else is a form of polytheism (shirk) which Allah is exalted above. It serves as a reminder to focus worship and submission on Allah alone.
orig: اتخذوا أحبارهم ورهبانهم أربابا من دون الله والمسيح ابن مريم وما أمروا إلا ليعبدوا إلها واحدا لا إله إلا هو سبحانه عما يشركون

translation: They want to extinguish the light of Allah with their mouths, but Allah refuses except to perfect His light, although the disbelievers dislike it.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the futility of the disbelievers' attempts to suppress or extinguish the message and truth of Islam, which is metaphorically referred to as the "light of Allah." Despite their efforts to undermine and reject the faith through their words and actions ("with their mouths"), Allah asserts His power and control over the situation, ensuring that His light will be perfected and will prevail. This highlights the supremacy of Allah's will and plan over the schemes and desires of those who oppose Him and His message. The verse also implies that the disbelievers' aversion to the completion of Allah's light will not affect the outcome, as their disapproval is insignificant in comparison to Allah's ultimate decree.
orig: يريدون أن يطفئوا نور الله بأفواههم ويأبى الله إلا أن يتم نوره ولو كره الكافرون

translation: It is He who sent His Messenger with guidance and the religion of truth to manifest it over all religion, although those who associate others with Allah dislike it.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the divine mandate given to Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) to spread the message of Islam. The "religion of truth" refers to the teachings and principles of Islam, which are meant to supersede all other belief systems. The verse also acknowledges the opposition and dislike that the Prophet and his followers faced from those who associated partners with Allah (the polytheists of Mecca). Despite this resistance, the verse asserts that the ultimate victory and dominance of Islam over all other religions is inevitable, as it is the will of Allah.
orig: هو الذي أرسل رسوله بالهدى ودين الحق ليظهره على الدين كله ولو كره المشركون

translation: O you who have believed, indeed many of the scholars and the monks devour the wealth of people unjustly and avert [them] from the way of Allah. And those who hoard gold and silver and do not spend it in the way of Allah - give them tidings of a painful punishment.
interpretation: This verse is a warning to those who exploit religion for worldly gain and hoard wealth without spending it in the way of Allah. It specifically calls out some religious leaders who mislead people for their own benefit. The verse emphasizes that those who accumulate wealth without using it for good will face severe consequences in the Hereafter. It serves as a reminder to be mindful of how we acquire and utilize the blessings Allah has bestowed upon us, ensuring that we prioritize faith and good deeds over material pursuits.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا إن كثيرا من الأحبار والرهبان ليأكلون أموال الناس بالباطل ويصدون عن سبيل الله والذين يكنزون الذهب والفضة ولا ينفقونها في سبيل الله فبشرهم بعذاب أليم

translation: The Day when it will be heated in the fire of Hell and seared therewith will be their foreheads, their flanks, and their backs, [it will be said], "This is what you hoarded for yourselves, so taste what you used to hoard."
interpretation: This verse is a stern warning against hoarding wealth and not spending it in the way of Allah. It describes the severe punishment that awaits those who accumulate wealth selfishly in this world. On the Day of Judgment, the wealth they hoarded will be heated in the fires of Hell and used to brand their foreheads, sides, and backs. They will be painfully reminded that this is the consequence of their greed and stinginess. The verse emphasizes that the wealth we accumulate is ultimately for our own benefit in the Hereafter, so we should spend it generously for good causes in this life. It highlights the importance of using wealth responsibly and not being miserly, as it will only lead to suffering in the afterlife.
orig: يوم يحمى عليها في نار جهنم فتكوى بها جباههم وجنوبهم وظهورهم هذا ما كنزتم لأنفسكم فذوقوا ما كنتم تكنزون

translation: Indeed, the number of months with Allah is twelve [lunar] months in the register of Allah [from] the day He created the heavens and the earth; of these, four are sacred. That is the correct religion, so do not wrong yourselves during them. And fight against the disbelievers collectively as they fight against you collectively. And know that Allah is with the righteous [who fear Him].
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of the Islamic lunar calendar, which consists of 12 months, with four of them being sacred months (Dhul-Qa'dah, Dhul-Hijjah, Muharram, and Rajab) during which fighting is prohibited. It reminds Muslims to be mindful of their actions during these sacred months and to avoid wrongdoing. The verse also encourages Muslims to stand united against those who oppose Islam and to fight against them collectively, just as the disbelievers fight against Muslims collectively. It concludes by reassuring the believers that Allah is with those who are righteous and mindful of Him, supporting and guiding them in their struggles.
orig: إن عدة الشهور عند الله اثنا عشر شهرا في كتاب الله يوم خلق السماوات والأرض منها أربعة حرم ذلك الدين القيم فلا تظلموا فيهن أنفسكم وقاتلوا المشركين كافة كما يقاتلونكم كافة واعلموا أن الله مع المتقين

translation: Indeed, the postponing [of restriction within sacred months] is an increase in disbelief by which those who have disbelieved are led [further] astray. They make it lawful one year and unlawful another year to correspond to the number made unlawful by Allah and [thus] make lawful what Allah has made unlawful. Made pleasing to them is the evil of their deeds; and Allah does not guide the disbelieving people.
interpretation: This verse refers to the practice of some pagan Arabs who would arbitrarily change the timing of the sacred months to suit their worldly interests. They would declare a sacred month to be ordinary if they wished to fight or conduct business as usual, thus violating its sanctity. Conversely, they might declare an ordinary month to be sacred to make up for a month whose sanctity they had previously violated. The Qur'an condemns this self-serving manipulation of the sacred months as a manifestation of disbelief and misguidance. It emphasizes that such distortion of divine law to accommodate human desires is a grave sin, and that those who engage in it have been deceived by the superficial appeal of their evil deeds. The verse ends with the assertion that Allah does not guide those who choose to persist in disbelief and reject His guidance.
orig: إنما النسيء زيادة في الكفر يضل به الذين كفروا يحلونه عاما ويحرمونه عاما ليواطئوا عدة ما حرم الله فيحلوا ما حرم الله زين لهم سوء أعمالهم والله لا يهدي القوم الكافرين

translation: O you who have believed, what is [the matter] with you that, when you are told to go forth in the cause of Allah, you adhere heavily to the earth? Are you satisfied with the life of this world rather than the Hereafter? But what is the enjoyment of worldly life compared to the Hereafter except a [very] little.
interpretation: This verse is a call to the believers to be ready and willing to strive and make sacrifices in the path of Allah, rather than being attached to the temporary pleasures and comforts of this worldly life. It reminds us that the life of this world is fleeting and insignificant compared to the eternal life of the Hereafter. The verse encourages the believers to prioritize the pleasure of Allah and the rewards of the afterlife over the material pursuits and temptations of this world. It is a powerful reminder to keep our focus on our ultimate goal and not get distracted or held back by our worldly desires and attachments.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا ما لكم إذا قيل لكم انفروا في سبيل الله اثاقلتم إلى الأرض أرضيتم بالحياة الدنيا من الآخرة فما متاع الحياة الدنيا في الآخرة إلا قليل

translation: If you do not go forth, He will punish you with a painful punishment and will replace you with another people, and you will not harm Him at all. And Allah is over all things competent.
interpretation: This verse is a warning to the believers that if they do not go forth in the cause of Allah, He will punish them severely and replace them with another people who will obey Him. It emphasizes the importance of striving in the way of Allah and that no one is indispensable. The believers should not think that by refusing to fight, they will harm Allah in any way. Allah is All-Powerful and does not need anyone. The verse also highlights the consequences of disobedience to Allah and the importance of fulfilling one's duties towards Him.
orig: إلا تنفروا يعذبكم عذابا أليما ويستبدل قوما غيركم ولا تضروه شيئا والله على كل شيء قدير

translation: If you do not aid him [i.e., the Prophet] - Allah has already aided him when those who disbelieved had driven him out [of Makkah] as one of two, when they were in the cave and he said to his companion, "Do not grieve; indeed Allah is with us." And Allah sent down his tranquillity upon him and supported him with soldiers [i.e., angels] you did not see and made the word of those who disbelieved the lowest, while the word of Allah - that is the highest. And Allah is Exalted in Might and Wise.
interpretation: This verse highlights the unwavering support and protection that Allah provides to His messengers and believers, even in the face of severe adversity. It refers to the incident when Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and his companion Abu Bakr were forced to flee Makkah due to persecution from the disbelievers. They sought refuge in a cave, and despite the dire circumstances, the Prophet reassured Abu Bakr that Allah was with them. The verse emphasizes the divine intervention that followed, with Allah sending down tranquillity upon the Prophet and supporting him with unseen forces (angels). This incident serves as a powerful reminder that true victory and the highest word belong to Allah, and that He is always there to support and guide those who have faith in Him, no matter how difficult the challenges may seem.
orig: إلا تنصروه فقد نصره الله إذ أخرجه الذين كفروا ثاني اثنين إذ هما في الغار إذ يقول لصاحبه لا تحزن إن الله معنا فأنزل الله سكينته عليه وأيده بجنود لم تروها وجعل كلمة الذين كفروا السفلى وكلمة الله هي العليا والله عزيز حكيم

translation: Go forth, whether light or heavy, and strive with your wealth and your lives in the cause of Allah. That is better for you, if you only knew.
interpretation: This verse is a call to action for the believers, urging them to participate in jihad, or striving in the path of Allah, regardless of their circumstances. "Light or heavy" refers to whether they are young or old, healthy or ill, rich or poor. It emphasizes that no excuse is acceptable for not taking part in this noble cause. The verse also highlights the importance of sacrificing one's wealth and life for the sake of Allah, stating that this is the best course of action for believers, even if they may not fully comprehend its significance in this world. It implies that the rewards for such sacrifices will be great in the hereafter and that this should be the ultimate motivation for the believers.
orig: انفروا خفافا وثقالا وجاهدوا بأموالكم وأنفسكم في سبيل الله ذلكم خير لكم إن كنتم تعلمون

translation: Had it been a near gain and an easy journey, they would have followed you, but the distance was long for them. And they will swear by Allah, "If we were able, we would have gone forth with you," destroying themselves [through false oaths], and Allah knows that indeed they are liars.
interpretation: This verse is addressing those who made excuses and did not join the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) in a expedition or battle, claiming that the journey was too long and difficult for them. However, Allah exposes their true intentions and states that if the gain had been near and the journey easy, they would have readily joined. These hypocrites will even swear by Allah that they would have gone forth if they were able, but Allah knows that they are lying and their oaths are false. Their excuses are merely a cover for their lack of faith and willingness to make sacrifices for the cause of Islam. This verse serves as a warning to those who make false excuses and emphasizes the importance of sincerity and devotion in one's faith.
orig: لو كان عرضا قريبا وسفرا قاصدا لاتبعوك ولكن بعدت عليهم الشقة وسيحلفون بالله لو استطعنا لخرجنا معكم يهلكون أنفسهم والله يعلم إنهم لكاذبون

translation: May Allah pardon you [O Muhammad]! Why did you give them permission [to remain behind] until it was evident to you who were truthful and you knew [who were] the liars?
interpretation: This verse is addressing the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) after he had given permission to some people to stay behind from a battle. The interpretation is that Allah is gently admonishing the Prophet for granting this permission without first ascertaining who had a valid excuse and who was merely making false excuses to avoid participating. It emphasizes the importance of verifying people's claims and intentions, especially in matters of religious obligation, before making allowances or exceptions for them. The verse also implies that the Prophet's eagerness to accommodate people should be balanced with wisdom and discernment.
orig: عفا الله عنك لم أذنت لهم حتى يتبين لك الذين صدقوا وتعلم الكاذبين

translation: Those who believe in Allah and the Last Day would not ask permission of you to be exempted from striving with their wealth and their lives. And Allah is Knowing of the righteous.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the devotion and commitment of true believers in Allah and the Day of Judgment. It suggests that those with strong faith will not seek exemption from contributing their wealth and risking their lives in the cause of Allah. They are willing to make sacrifices without hesitation because of their unwavering belief. The verse also affirms that Allah knows who among His servants are truly righteous and sincere in their faith, indicating that one cannot hide their true intentions from Allah.
orig: لا يستأذنك الذين يؤمنون بالله واليوم الآخر أن يجاهدوا بأموالهم وأنفسهم والله عليم بالمتقين

translation: Only those who do not believe in Allah and the Last Day ask your permission [to be excused from fighting], and whose hearts have doubted, and so they waver in their doubt.
interpretation: This verse is addressing those who are hesitant to join the Muslims in their struggle for the cause of Islam. It suggests that those who seek to be excused from participating in the fight do so because they lack true faith in Allah and the Day of Judgment. Their hearts are filled with doubt, causing them to waver and be indecisive. The verse implies that true believers would not hesitate to stand up for their faith and would be willing to make sacrifices for the sake of Allah. It highlights the importance of having strong conviction and unwavering faith in the face of challenges and difficulties.
orig: إنما يستأذنك الذين لا يؤمنون بالله واليوم الآخر وارتابت قلوبهم فهم في ريبهم يترددون

translation: And if they had intended to go forth, they would have prepared for it [some] preparation. But Allah disliked their being sent, so He kept them back, and they were told, "Remain [behind] with those who remain."
interpretation: This verse suggests that the hypocrites who stayed behind from the battle had no real intention of joining in the first place. If they had truly wanted to participate, they would have made the necessary preparations. However, Allah knew their true intentions and disliked their participation, so He kept them from going and commanded them to stay behind with the other non-participants. This highlights the idea that Allah knows what is in people's hearts and that He may prevent insincere people from engaging in important matters or struggles for the sake of the believers.
orig: ولو أرادوا الخروج لأعدوا له عدة ولكن كره الله انبعاثهم فثبطهم وقيل اقعدوا مع القاعدين

translation: Had they gone forth with you, they would not have increased you except in confusion, and they would have been active among you, seeking [to cause] you fitnah. And among you are avid listeners to them. And Allah is Knowing of the wrongdoers.
interpretation: This verse warns the believers that the hypocrites, had they joined them in battle, would only have caused harm and discord. They would have actively spread rumors and false information to create doubt, dissension and "fitnah" (trials, tribulations) among the ranks of the believers. The verse also points out that there were some among the Muslims who were inclined to listen to and believe the words of the hypocrites. However, Allah knows best the true nature and intentions of the wrongdoers and hypocrites, even if some believers are deceived by them. It serves as a reminder to be cautious of those who may outwardly claim to be allies but secretly harbor ill intentions towards the Muslim community.
orig: لو خرجوا فيكم ما زادوكم إلا خبالا ولأوضعوا خلالكم يبغونكم الفتنة وفيكم سماعون لهم والله عليم بالظالمين

translation: They had already desired discord before and had upset matters for you, until the truth came and the ordinance of Allah became manifest, though they were averse.
interpretation: This verse refers to the hypocrites who sought to create discord and confusion among the Muslims, even before the truth of Islam became clear. They tried to undermine the Prophet's mission by spreading false rumors and creating doubts. However, despite their efforts, the truth of Islam prevailed and Allah's decree became manifest, much to their dismay. The verse highlights the persistence of those who oppose the truth, but also emphasizes the ultimate triumph of Allah's will, regardless of the machinations of the disbelievers.
orig: لقد ابتغوا الفتنة من قبل وقلبوا لك الأمور حتى جاء الحق وظهر أمر الله وهم كارهون

translation: And among them is he who says, "Permit me [to remain at home] and do not put me to trial." Unquestionably, into trial they have fallen. And indeed, Hell will encompass the disbelievers.
interpretation: This verse is a warning to those who make excuses to avoid fulfilling their religious duties and participating in the struggle for God's cause. They fear the trials and hardships that come with standing up for their faith, but in reality, by avoiding these trials, they have already fallen into a greater trial - that of disobedience to God. The verse emphasizes that there is no escape from God's judgment, and those who disbelieve and fail to fulfill their obligations will be encompassed by Hell in the Hereafter. It serves as a reminder to the believers to remain steadfast in their faith and not let worldly concerns or fears deter them from the path of righteousness.
orig: ومنهم من يقول ائذن لي ولا تفتني ألا في الفتنة سقطوا وإن جهنم لمحيطة بالكافرين

translation: If good touches you, it distresses them; but if disaster strikes you, they say, "We took our matter [in hand] before," and turn away while they are rejoicing.
interpretation: This verse highlights the hypocrisy and ill-will of some people towards the believers. When good fortune or blessings come to the believers, these hypocrites feel distressed and unhappy, as they do not wish to see the believers succeed. However, when the believers face difficulties or calamities, the same hypocrites rejoice and turn away, claiming that they had already taken precautions to avoid such misfortunes. This attitude reveals their true nature and lack of genuine support for the believers, as they derive pleasure from seeing them suffer while feeling resentment towards their success and well-being. The verse serves as a reminder for the believers to be cautious of such individuals and to place their trust in Allah, who is the true source of support and guidance.
orig: إن تصبك حسنة تسؤهم وإن تصبك مصيبة يقولوا قد أخذنا أمرنا من قبل ويتولوا وهم فرحون

translation: Say, "Never will we be struck except by what Allah has decreed for us; He is our protector." And upon Allah let the believers rely.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of complete trust and reliance on Allah. As believers, we should have faith that everything happens according to Allah's divine plan and decree. No harm or benefit can come to us except what Allah has written for us. This understanding brings inner peace, knowing that Allah is our protector and guardian. It encourages us to put our full trust in Him and rely on His wisdom and mercy in all aspects of our lives. By doing so, we can face the challenges and uncertainties of life with strength, resilience, and unwavering faith in Allah's support and guidance.
orig: قل لن يصيبنا إلا ما كتب الله لنا هو مولانا وعلى الله فليتوكل المؤمنون

translation: Say, "Do you await for us except one of the two best things while we await for you that Allah will afflict you with punishment from Himself or at our hands? So wait; indeed we, along with you, are waiting."
interpretation: This verse is a challenge to the disbelievers who were waiting for the Muslims to be defeated or destroyed. It asserts that the Muslims are in a win-win situation: either they will be victorious in this world or attain martyrdom and paradise in the Hereafter. On the other hand, the disbelievers face a lose-lose situation: either they will be defeated and punished by the Muslims in this world, or they will face Allah's punishment in the Hereafter for their disbelief and opposition to the truth. The verse concludes by telling the disbelievers to keep waiting for the Muslims' defeat, while the Muslims are also waiting for Allah's judgment to befall them. It emphasizes the unwavering faith and confidence of the believers in Allah's support and victory, despite the odds stacked against them.
orig: قل هل تربصون بنا إلا إحدى الحسنيين ونحن نتربص بكم أن يصيبكم الله بعذاب من عنده أو بأيدينا فتربصوا إنا معكم متربصون

translation: Say, "Spend willingly or unwillingly; never will it be accepted from you. Indeed, you have been a defiantly disobedient people."
interpretation: This verse is addressing the hypocrites who spend in charity only to show off or out of reluctance, not out of sincere faith and desire to please Allah. It emphasizes that such insincere spending will not be accepted by Allah, because these people are characterized by persistent disobedience and corruption. The message is that the intention and spiritual state of the giver is more important than the mere act of giving. Spending should be done willingly and with a pure heart for it to be acknowledged and rewarded by Allah. Insincere and hypocritical acts, even if they are outwardly good, are worthless if the underlying faith and submission to Allah is absent.
orig: قل أنفقوا طوعا أو كرها لن يتقبل منكم إنكم كنتم قوما فاسقين

translation: And what prevented their expenditures from being accepted from them except that they have disbelieved in Allah and in His Messenger and that they come not to prayer except while they are lazy and that they do not spend except while they are unwilling.
interpretation: This verse is pointing out that the disbelievers' good deeds, such as spending in charity, are not accepted by Allah because of their disbelief in Him and His Messenger. Their prayers are also not accepted because they pray reluctantly and lazily, without sincerity or devotion. Similarly, when they do spend in Allah's cause, they do so unwillingly and begrudgingly. As such, their actions lack the essential element of faith and sincerity that is necessary for deeds to be accepted by Allah. This highlights the importance of having true faith and performing good deeds with the right intentions for them to be of benefit in the Hereafter.
orig: وما منعهم أن تقبل منهم نفقاتهم إلا أنهم كفروا بالله وبرسوله ولا يأتون الصلاة إلا وهم كسالى ولا ينفقون إلا وهم كارهون

translation: So let not their wealth or their children impress you. Allah only intends to punish them through them in worldly life and that their souls should depart [at death] while they are disbelievers.
interpretation: This verse warns the believers not to be dazzled or impressed by the wealth and offspring of the disbelievers. It emphasizes that these worldly possessions and blessings are temporary, and Allah has granted them to the disbelievers as a means of punishment in this life. Their attachment to these temporary things will lead to their suffering and ultimate loss in the Hereafter. The verse also points out that the disbelievers will die in a state of disbelief, which will result in their eternal doom. It serves as a reminder for the believers to focus on their faith and not be distracted by the fleeting pleasures and riches of this world, as they may lead to one's destruction in the Hereafter if one does not use them in accordance with Allah's guidance.
orig: فلا تعجبك أموالهم ولا أولادهم إنما يريد الله ليعذبهم بها في الحياة الدنيا وتزهق أنفسهم وهم كافرون

translation: And they swear by Allah that they are from you while they are not from you; but they are a people who are afraid.
interpretation: This verse refers to the hypocrites who outwardly pretend to be part of the Muslim community, swearing by Allah that they belong to the believers. However, in reality, they are not true believers. They only feign belief out of fear and cowardice, as they are afraid of the consequences of openly showing their disbelief and hypocrisy. They lack the courage to stand up for what they truly believe in and instead resort to deception to protect themselves. This highlights the importance of sincerity and genuineness in faith, as opposed to mere outward appearances and false oaths.
orig: ويحلفون بالله إنهم لمنكم وما هم منكم ولكنهم قوم يفرقون

translation: If they could find a refuge or some caves or a place of concealment, they would turn straightaway thereto, with an obstinate rush.
interpretation: This verse is referring to the hypocrites who, when faced with difficulty or danger, would seek to flee and find a place to hide rather than standing firm in their faith and facing the challenges with the believers. It highlights their cowardice, lack of conviction, and desire for self-preservation at the expense of their supposed beliefs. The verse suggests that these individuals are not true believers, as they prioritize their own safety and comfort over their commitment to Allah and His cause. It serves as a warning to the believers to be cautious of such individuals who may appear to be part of the community but will quickly abandon it in times of hardship.
orig: لو يجدون ملجأ أو مغارات أو مدخلا لولوا إليه وهم يجمحون

translation: And among them are some who criticize you concerning the [distribution of] charities. If they are given from them, they approve; but if they are not given from them, at once they become angry.
interpretation: This verse highlights the hypocritical nature of some individuals who find fault with the Prophet Muhammad's distribution of charity. Their contentment is conditional upon receiving a share of the donations, revealing their true intentions and lack of sincerity. They are quick to express anger and dissatisfaction when they do not receive what they desire, exposing their selfish motives and disregard for the true spirit of charity. The verse serves as a reminder that one's intentions and attitude towards giving should be pure, selfless, and not driven by personal gain or recognition.
orig: ومنهم من يلمزك في الصدقات فإن أعطوا منها رضوا وإن لم يعطوا منها إذا هم يسخطون

translation: And if they had been satisfied with what Allah and His Messenger gave them and said, "Sufficient for us is Allah; Allah will give us of His bounty, and [so will] His Messenger; indeed, we are desirous toward Allah," [it would have been better for them].
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of being content with what Allah and His Messenger have provided. It suggests that if people were to put their trust in Allah and His Messenger, believing that Allah will grant them from His bounty, it would be better for them. The verse highlights the virtues of reliance on Allah, contentment, and seeking Allah's pleasure above worldly gains. It encourages believers to turn to Allah with hope and desire, rather than relying on material possessions or other people for fulfillment and satisfaction in life.
orig: ولو أنهم رضوا ما آتاهم الله ورسوله وقالوا حسبنا الله سيؤتينا الله من فضله ورسوله إنا إلى الله راغبون

translation: Zakah expenditures are only for the poor and for the needy and for those employed to collect [zakah] and for bringing hearts together [for Islam] and for freeing captives [or slaves] and for those in debt and for the cause of Allah and for the [stranded] traveler - an obligation [imposed] by Allah. And Allah is Knowing and Wise.
interpretation: This verse specifies the eight categories of people who are entitled to receive Zakah (obligatory charity). It is a divine injunction that Zakah funds should be distributed among these groups, which include the poor, the needy, those employed to administer the funds, those whose hearts need to be reconciled to Islam, those in bondage, those in debt, those struggling in the cause of Allah, and the wayfarer. The verse emphasizes that this is an obligation decreed by Allah, who is All-Knowing and All-Wise. It highlights the importance of Zakah in supporting the vulnerable members of society and promoting social welfare and justice.
orig: إنما الصدقات للفقراء والمساكين والعاملين عليها والمؤلفة قلوبهم وفي الرقاب والغارمين وفي سبيل الله وابن السبيل فريضة من الله والله عليم حكيم

translation: And among them are those who abuse the Prophet and say, "He is an ear." Say, "[It is] an ear of goodness for you that believes in Allah and believes the believers and [is] a mercy to those who believe among you." And those who abuse the Messenger of Allah - for them is a painful punishment.
interpretation: This verse is addressing the hypocrites who would insult and abuse the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) by calling him "an ear", implying that he listens to and believes everything he hears. Allah responds by telling the Prophet to say that he is indeed an ear, but an ear of goodness that listens to and believes in Allah and the believers. The Prophet's attentiveness and trust in the believers is a mercy for those among them who are truly faithful. As for those who persist in abusing and insulting the Messenger of Allah, they will face a severe and painful punishment from Allah for their actions.
orig: ومنهم الذين يؤذون النبي ويقولون هو أذن قل أذن خير لكم يؤمن بالله ويؤمن للمؤمنين ورحمة للذين آمنوا منكم والذين يؤذون رسول الله لهم عذاب أليم

translation: They swear by Allah to you [Muslims] to satisfy you. But Allah and His Messenger are more worthy for them to satisfy, if they should be believers.
interpretation: This verse is addressing the hypocrites who would swear oaths by Allah in front of the Muslims in order to please them and gain their trust. However, Allah is making it clear that if these people were true believers, they should be more concerned with pleasing Allah and His Messenger rather than trying to appease other people. Seeking the pleasure of Allah should be the utmost priority for a believer, over and above seeking the approval or satisfaction of any human being. This highlights the importance of sincerity in faith and actions, and that one's primary focus should be on earning the pleasure of Allah, even if it may sometimes be at odds with pleasing other people.
orig: يحلفون بالله لكم ليرضوكم والله ورسوله أحق أن يرضوه إن كانوا مؤمنين

translation: Do they not know that whoever opposes Allah and His Messenger - that for him is the fire of Hell, wherein he will abide eternally? That is the great disgrace.
interpretation: This verse serves as a stern warning to those who oppose or work against Allah and His Messenger (Muhammad). It emphasizes that such individuals will face severe consequences for their actions, namely, being condemned to the eternal fire of Hell. This punishment is described as the ultimate disgrace, highlighting the gravity of their offense. The verse aims to deter people from defying or challenging the authority of Allah and His Messenger, reminding them of the dire spiritual repercussions they will face in the afterlife for their disobedience and hostility towards the divine message.
orig: ألم يعلموا أنه من يحادد الله ورسوله فأن له نار جهنم خالدا فيها ذلك الخزي العظيم

translation: The hypocrites are apprehensive lest a surah be revealed about them, informing them of what is in their hearts. Say, "Mock [as you wish]; indeed, Allah will expose that which you fear."
interpretation: This verse is a warning to the hypocrites who outwardly profess Islam but inwardly harbor disbelief and ill intentions towards the Prophet and the Muslim community. They fear that a Qur'anic revelation will expose their true feelings and intentions, which they try to keep hidden. However, Allah reassures the Prophet that their mockery and hypocrisy will be of no avail, as He will bring to light what they are trying to conceal. This verse emphasizes the all-encompassing knowledge of Allah and serves as a reminder that one's true intentions and inner thoughts are known to Him, even if they are hidden from others.
orig: يحذر المنافقون أن تنزل عليهم سورة تنبئهم بما في قلوبهم قل استهزئوا إن الله مخرج ما تحذرون

translation: If you ask them, they will surely say, "We were only conversing and playing." Say, "Is it Allah and His verses and His Messenger that you were mocking?"
interpretation: This verse is a stern warning against those who mock or make light of Allah, His revelations, and His Messenger. It suggests that some people, when confronted about their disrespectful behavior, will try to brush it off as mere joking or playful conversation. However, Allah makes it clear that such an excuse is unacceptable, and that ridiculing or belittling the sacred aspects of Islam is a severe offense. The rhetorical question at the end of the verse emphasizes the gravity of their actions, implying that mocking Allah, His verses, and His Messenger is a form of disbelief and a serious sin that warrants divine retribution.
orig: ولئن سألتهم ليقولن إنما كنا نخوض ونلعب قل أبالله وآياته ورسوله كنتم تستهزئون

translation: Make no excuse; you have disbelieved after your belief. If We pardon one faction of you - We will punish another faction because they were criminals.
interpretation: This verse is addressing a group of people who have turned away from their faith after previously believing. It states that no excuses will be accepted for their disbelief. However, it also indicates that while one group may be forgiven, another group will face punishment due to their criminal actions. This highlights the concept of divine justice in Islam, where individuals are held accountable for their deeds and intentions. It also emphasizes the severity of abandoning one's faith and the consequences that may follow such a decision.
orig: لا تعتذروا قد كفرتم بعد إيمانكم إن نعف عن طائفة منكم نعذب طائفة بأنهم كانوا مجرمين

translation: The hypocrite men and hypocrite women are of one another. They enjoin what is wrong and forbid what is right and close their hands. They have forgotten Allah, so He has forgotten them [accordingly]. Indeed, the hypocrites - it is they who are the defiantly disobedient.
interpretation: This verse highlights the characteristics and fate of the hypocrites. It states that the hypocrites, both men and women, are all alike in their actions and attitudes. They encourage evil deeds, forbid good actions, and are stingy in spending for the sake of Allah. Due to their negligence in remembering Allah and obeying His commands, Allah has abandoned them. The verse emphasizes that the hypocrites are the ones who are truly disobedient and rebellious against Allah's guidance, as their outward appearance of faith is not matched by their inner reality and actions.
orig: المنافقون والمنافقات بعضهم من بعض يأمرون بالمنكر وينهون عن المعروف ويقبضون أيديهم نسوا الله فنسيهم إن المنافقين هم الفاسقون

translation: Allah has promised the hypocrite men and hypocrite women and the disbelievers the fire of Hell, wherein they will abide eternally. It is sufficient for them. And Allah has cursed them, and for them is an enduring punishment.
interpretation: This verse serves as a stern warning to those who outwardly profess faith in Islam while harboring disbelief and hypocrisy in their hearts, as well as to those who openly reject the message of Islam. It emphasizes that their ultimate fate is the eternal punishment of Hell, which is a sufficient recompense for their actions. The verse also highlights that they are distant from Allah's mercy, as indicated by Him cursing them. This interpretation underscores the gravity of hypocrisy and disbelief, and the severe consequences awaiting those who choose this path, serving as a reminder for believers to be sincere in their faith and actions.
orig: وعد الله المنافقين والمنافقات والكفار نار جهنم خالدين فيها هي حسبهم ولعنهم الله ولهم عذاب مقيم

translation: [You disbelievers are] like those before you; they were stronger than you in power and more abundant in wealth and children. They enjoyed their portion [of worldly enjoyment], and you have enjoyed your portion as those before you enjoyed their portion, and you have engaged [in vanities] like that in which they engaged. [It is] those whose deeds have become worthless in this world and in the Hereafter, and it is they who are the losers.
interpretation: This verse is a warning and admonition to the disbelievers, reminding them of the fate of previous nations who were mightier and wealthier than them, yet ultimately faced destruction due to their disbelief and indulgence in worldly pleasures. It emphasizes that the temporal enjoyments of this world are fleeting and that those who prioritize them over faith and righteousness will ultimately face loss and disappointment in both this world and the Hereafter. The verse serves as a call to reflect on the transient nature of worldly life and to focus on deeds that hold value in the eternal life to come.
orig: كالذين من قبلكم كانوا أشد منكم قوة وأكثر أموالا وأولادا فاستمتعوا بخلاقهم فاستمتعتم بخلاقكم كما استمتع الذين من قبلكم بخلاقهم وخضتم كالذي خاضوا أولئك حبطت أعمالهم في الدنيا والآخرة وأولئك هم الخاسرون

translation: Has there not reached them the news of those before them - the people of Noah and 'Aad and Thamud and the people of Abraham and the companions of Madyan and the overturned cities? Their messengers came to them with clear proofs. And Allah would never have wronged them, but they were wronging themselves.
interpretation: This verse is a reminder to the disbelievers that they are not the first to reject the message of Allah. Many nations before them, such as the people of Noah, 'Aad, Thamud, Abraham, and the companions of Madyan, were also visited by messengers with clear proofs and evidence of the truth. However, they chose to deny and reject the message, wronging themselves by their disbelief and disobedience. Allah did not wrong them by punishing them; rather, they brought the punishment upon themselves through their own actions. This serves as a warning to the disbelievers that they too will face the consequences of their rejection if they do not heed the message and believe in Allah and His messengers.
orig: ألم يأتهم نبأ الذين من قبلهم قوم نوح وعاد وثمود وقوم إبراهيم وأصحاب مدين والمؤتفكات أتتهم رسلهم بالبينات فما كان الله ليظلمهم ولكن كانوا أنفسهم يظلمون

translation: The believing men and believing women are allies of one another. They enjoin what is right and forbid what is wrong and establish prayer and give zakah and obey Allah and His Messenger. Those - Allah will have mercy upon them. Indeed, Allah is Exalted in Might and Wise.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the strong bond of faith and solidarity that exists between believing men and women in Islam. As allies, they support each other in righteousness, encouraging good deeds and discouraging evil. They are committed to the fundamental pillars of faith, like prayer and charity. By obeying Allah and His Messenger, they hope to attain Allah's mercy. The verse concludes by affirming Allah's power and wisdom, suggesting that the believers' unity and obedience stem from, and are rewarded by, Allah's might and wise judgment. It underscores the importance of the community of believers standing together in faith and good works.
orig: والمؤمنون والمؤمنات بعضهم أولياء بعض يأمرون بالمعروف وينهون عن المنكر ويقيمون الصلاة ويؤتون الزكاة ويطيعون الله ورسوله أولئك سيرحمهم الله إن الله عزيز حكيم

translation: Allah has promised the believing men and believing women gardens beneath which rivers flow, wherein they abide eternally, and pleasant dwellings in gardens of perpetual residence; but approval from Allah is greater. It is that which is the great attainment.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the immense reward that awaits the faithful believers in the afterlife. The promise of eternal gardens with flowing rivers and pleasant dwellings signifies the ultimate bliss and comfort that they will experience. However, the verse highlights that the greatest reward of all is attaining Allah's approval and pleasure. This divine acceptance and satisfaction surpass all the material delights of Paradise and represent the true success and triumph for a believer. Striving to earn Allah's approval should be the primary goal and motivation in a believer's life, as it guarantees the supreme achievement in the Hereafter.
orig: وعد الله المؤمنين والمؤمنات جنات تجري من تحتها الأنهار خالدين فيها ومساكن طيبة في جنات عدن ورضوان من الله أكبر ذلك هو الفوز العظيم

translation: O Prophet! Strive against the disbelievers and the hypocrites, and be stern with them. Hell will be their home, a hapless journey's end.
interpretation: This verse instructs the Prophet Muhammad to firmly resist and oppose those who reject faith in God (the disbelievers) as well as those who outwardly profess Islam while concealing disbelief in their hearts (the hypocrites). The Prophet is told to be harsh and uncompromising with them in upholding the truth of Islam. It warns that such people are destined for Hell in the afterlife as a consequence of their deliberate choice to deny or hide from the truth of God's message. The verse emphasizes the importance of the Prophet's duty to stand firmly against forces hostile to Islam and convey God's warning of the ultimate fate that awaits those who persistently reject faith.
orig: يا أيها النبي جاهد الكفار والمنافقين واغلظ عليهم ومأواهم جهنم وبئس المصير

translation: They swear by Allah that they did not say [anything against the Prophet] while they had said the word of disbelief and disbelieved after their [pretense of] Islam and planned that which they were not to attain. And they were not resentful except [for the fact] that Allah and His Messenger had enriched them of His bounty. So if they repent, it is better for them; but if they turn away, Allah will punish them with a painful punishment in this world and the Hereafter. And there will not be for them on earth any protector or helper.
interpretation: This verse highlights the hypocrisy and treachery of those who outwardly professed Islam but harbored disbelief and enmity towards the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and the Muslim community. Despite their oaths and claims of innocence, they had uttered words of disbelief and plotted against the Prophet, ungrateful for the blessings and prosperity that Allah had bestowed upon them through the Prophet's leadership. The verse warns them of severe consequences in this world and the next if they do not sincerely repent and mend their ways, emphasizing that they will find no protector or helper besides Allah if they persist in their hypocrisy and opposition to the truth.
orig: يحلفون بالله ما قالوا ولقد قالوا كلمة الكفر وكفروا بعد إسلامهم وهموا بما لم ينالوا وما نقموا إلا أن أغناهم الله ورسوله من فضله فإن يتوبوا يك خيرا لهم وإن يتولوا يعذبهم الله عذابا أليما في الدنيا والآخرة وما لهم في الأرض من ولي ولا نصير

translation: And among them are those who made a covenant with Allah, [saying], "If He should give us from His bounty, we will surely spend in charity, and we will surely be among the righteous."
interpretation: This verse is referring to the hypocrites who made false promises to Allah. They claimed that if Allah blessed them with wealth, they would spend it in charity and be among the righteous. However, their intentions were insincere, and they failed to fulfill their promises when they were given wealth. This verse highlights the importance of sincerity in one's intentions and actions, and the danger of making false promises to Allah. It serves as a warning to believers to be truthful in their commitments and to fulfill their obligations to Allah and to others.
orig: ومنهم من عاهد الله لئن آتانا من فضله لنصدقن ولنكونن من الصالحين

translation: But when He gave them from His bounty, they were stingy with it and turned away, and they were averse.
interpretation: This verse is referring to the ungrateful nature of some people. When Allah bestows His blessings and bounties upon them, instead of being grateful and using those blessings in a way that pleases Him, they become stingy and miserly. They turn away from the path of righteousness and are averse to spending in the way of Allah or helping others. This behavior is a sign of ingratitude and a lack of faith. The verse serves as a reminder for believers to always be grateful for Allah's blessings and to use them in a way that benefits others and pleases Him.
orig: فلما آتاهم من فضله بخلوا به وتولوا وهم معرضون

translation: So He penalized them with hypocrisy in their hearts until the Day they will meet Him - because they failed Allah in what they promised Him and because they [habitually] used to lie.
interpretation: This verse highlights the consequence of breaking promises made to Allah and being dishonest. Those who engage in such behavior are afflicted with hypocrisy in their hearts, which will remain with them until the Day of Judgment when they meet Allah. This hypocrisy is a form of punishment for their insincerity and lack of commitment to their word. It serves as a reminder that one's actions and intentions have lasting spiritual consequences, and that being truthful and fulfilling one's promises to Allah are essential for maintaining a pure and sincere heart.
orig: فأعقبهم نفاقا في قلوبهم إلى يوم يلقونه بما أخلفوا الله ما وعدوه وبما كانوا يكذبون

translation: Do they not know that Allah knows their secrets and their private conversations and that Allah is the Knower of the unseen?
interpretation: This verse is a reminder that Allah is all-knowing and aware of everything, including people's innermost thoughts, secrets, and private conversations. It emphasizes that nothing can be hidden from Allah, even if people try to conceal their actions or intentions from others. The verse also highlights one of Allah's attributes, "Knower of the unseen," which means that He has knowledge of what is hidden from human perception, including the future and the unseen realms. This understanding should motivate believers to be mindful of their actions and intentions, as they will be accountable to Allah, Who is fully aware of everything they do, say, or think, whether in public or in private.
orig: ألم يعلموا أن الله يعلم سرهم ونجواهم وأن الله علام الغيوب

translation: Those who criticize the contributors among the believers concerning [their] charities and [criticize] the ones who find nothing [to spend] except their effort, so they ridicule them - Allah will ridicule them, and they will have a painful punishment.
interpretation: This verse condemns those who mock and criticize the believers who give in charity, whether they give much or little according to their means. It emphasizes that Allah will punish these mockers with ridicule in the Hereafter and subject them to a severe torment for their arrogant and ungrateful behavior. The verse highlights the importance of sincerity in giving charity and not belittling any amount of good that one does for the sake of Allah, as He rewards all deeds based on the intention behind them.
orig: الذين يلمزون المطوعين من المؤمنين في الصدقات والذين لا يجدون إلا جهدهم فيسخرون منهم سخر الله منهم ولهم عذاب أليم

translation: Ask forgiveness for them, [O Muhammad], or do not ask forgiveness for them. If you should ask forgiveness for them seventy times - never will Allah forgive them. That is because they disbelieved in Allah and His Messenger, and Allah does not guide the defiantly disobedient people.
interpretation: This verse indicates that the hypocrites who outwardly embraced Islam but inwardly rejected it are not eligible for Allah's forgiveness, even if the Prophet (ﷺ) were to seek forgiveness for them repeatedly. Their disbelief in Allah and His Messenger has sealed their fate, and Allah does not guide those who persistently and defiantly disobey Him. The number seventy here is not meant to be taken literally; rather, it signifies a large number or an indefinite repetition, emphasizing that even persistent intercession on their behalf will not change the consequence of their disbelief and hypocrisy.
orig: استغفر لهم أو لا تستغفر لهم إن تستغفر لهم سبعين مرة فلن يغفر الله لهم ذلك بأنهم كفروا بالله ورسوله والله لا يهدي القوم الفاسقين

translation: Those who remained behind rejoiced in their staying [at home] after [the departure of] the Messenger of Allah and disliked to strive with their wealth and their lives in the cause of Allah and said, "Do not go forth in the heat." Say, "The fire of Hell is more intense in heat" - if they would but understand.
interpretation: This verse is criticizing those who chose to stay behind and not join the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) in the expedition to Tabuk. They were happy to avoid the hardship of the journey and the battle, and to keep their wealth and lives for themselves instead of sacrificing them for the sake of Allah. They tried to discourage others from going by pointing out the extreme heat. However, Allah reminds them that the heat of Hell is far more severe, if only they had the understanding to realize the consequences of their actions and choices. It highlights the importance of striving in the path of Allah and not letting worldly comforts or difficulties deter one from fulfilling their religious duties and obligations.
orig: فرح المخلفون بمقعدهم خلاف رسول الله وكرهوا أن يجاهدوا بأموالهم وأنفسهم في سبيل الله وقالوا لا تنفروا في الحر قل نار جهنم أشد حرا لو كانوا يفقهون

translation: So let them laugh a little and [then] weep much as recompense for what they used to earn.
interpretation: This verse is a warning to those who mock and ridicule the teachings of Islam and the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him). It suggests that while they may find amusement and laughter in their disbelief and rejection of the truth, they will ultimately face the consequences of their actions in the form of weeping and sorrow in the Hereafter. The verse emphasizes the gravity of their misdeeds and the justice of Allah in recompensing them accordingly. It serves as a reminder that the temporary pleasures and amusements of this world are fleeting, and that one should be mindful of their actions and their implications for the life to come.
orig: فليضحكوا قليلا وليبكوا كثيرا جزاء بما كانوا يكسبون

translation: If Allah returns you to a group of them, and they ask your permission to go out [to battle], say, "You will never go out with me, ever, and you will never fight with me an enemy. Indeed, you were satisfied with sitting [at home] the first time, so sit [now] with those who stay behind."
interpretation: This verse is addressing the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and his companions who stayed behind from the Battle of Tabuk. It warns them that if they seek permission to join future battles, they will be denied because they chose to stay behind the first time. The verse emphasizes the importance of commitment and consistency in faith and actions. It also highlights the consequences of choosing comfort and ease over fulfilling one's duty and obligation towards Allah and His cause.
orig: فإن رجعك الله إلى طائفة منهم فاستأذنوك للخروج فقل لن تخرجوا معي أبدا ولن تقاتلوا معي عدوا إنكم رضيتم بالقعود أول مرة فاقعدوا مع الخالفين

translation: And do not pray [the funeral prayer, O Muhammad], over any of them who has died - ever - or stand at his grave. Indeed, they disbelieved in Allah and His Messenger and died while they were defiantly disobedient.
interpretation: This verse is instructing the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and the believers not to offer the funeral prayer for those who died as disbelievers and hypocrites, or to stand at their graves seeking forgiveness for them. This is because they rejected faith in Allah and His Messenger during their lives and died in a state of persistent disobedience and defiance against the truth. Their actions and beliefs have consequently placed them beyond the mercy and forgiveness of Allah in the Hereafter. The verse emphasizes the gravity of disbelief and the consequences it entails in the afterlife.
orig: ولا تصل على أحد منهم مات أبدا ولا تقم على قبره إنهم كفروا بالله ورسوله وماتوا وهم فاسقون

translation: And let not their wealth and their children impress you. Allah only intends to punish them through them in this world and that their souls should depart [at death] while they are disbelievers.
interpretation: This verse warns not to be dazzled or impressed by the worldly possessions and progeny of the disbelievers. It states that Allah has granted them these bounties not out of His favor, but rather as a means of punishment in this worldly life. Their wealth and children keep them preoccupied and heedless of the Hereafter. Ultimately, the greatest punishment is that they will die as disbelievers, without faith, resulting in a grievous eternal fate in the Afterlife. So Muslims should not be deceived by outward appearances of prosperity, but should focus on cultivating sincere faith and good deeds.
orig: ولا تعجبك أموالهم وأولادهم إنما يريد الله أن يعذبهم بها في الدنيا وتزهق أنفسهم وهم كافرون

translation: And when a surah was revealed [enjoining them] to believe in Allah and to fight with His Messenger, those of wealth among them asked your permission [to stay back] and said, "Leave us to be with them who sit [at home]."
interpretation: This verse is criticizing the hypocrites who, when called upon to fight in the way of Allah alongside the Prophet (ﷺ), made excuses to stay behind with those who remained at home, like women, children, and the infirm. They preferred the comfort and ease of staying behind over the hardship and sacrifice of fighting for the cause of Islam. It exposes their weak faith and reluctance to make sacrifices for Allah's sake, and their similarity to those who are legitimately excused from fighting. The verse implies that true believers should eagerly respond to the call of jihad and not seek excuses to avoid it.
orig: وإذا أنزلت سورة أن آمنوا بالله وجاهدوا مع رسوله استأذنك أولو الطول منهم وقالوا ذرنا نكن مع القاعدين

translation: They were satisfied to be with the women who remain behind, and their hearts were sealed; thus they do not understand.
interpretation: This verse is referring to a group of people who chose to stay behind with the women instead of joining the battle, indicating a lack of courage and commitment to the cause of Islam. As a result, Allah has sealed their hearts, meaning that they have lost the ability to understand and appreciate the truth of the religion. This sealing of the heart is a punishment for their choice to prioritize their own comfort and desires over their duty to Allah and His messenger. It serves as a warning to all believers to remain steadfast in their faith and to be willing to make sacrifices for the sake of Allah, lest they too suffer the consequences of a sealed heart and a lack of understanding.
orig: رضوا بأن يكونوا مع الخوالف وطبع على قلوبهم فهم لا يفقهون

translation: But the Messenger and those who believed with him strove [in the cause of Allah] with their wealth and their lives. Those will have [all that is] good, and it is those who are the successful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of striving in the cause of Allah with one's wealth and life. It distinguishes the Prophet Muhammad and his true followers from those who were hesitant or hypocritical in their commitment to Islam. Those who sincerely strive and make sacrifices for the sake of Allah will be granted the best of rewards in this world and the Hereafter, and they will be among the successful ones who attain salvation and the pleasure of Allah. This verse encourages believers to prioritize their faith and to be willing to dedicate their resources and efforts to upholding and spreading the message of Islam.
orig: لكن الرسول والذين آمنوا معه جاهدوا بأموالهم وأنفسهم وأولئك لهم الخيرات وأولئك هم المفلحون

translation: Allah has prepared for them gardens beneath which rivers flow, wherein they will abide eternally. That is the great attainment.
interpretation: This verse speaks of the ultimate reward that Allah has prepared for the righteous believers in Paradise. The mention of "gardens beneath which rivers flow" paints a vivid image of the serenity, beauty, and abundance that awaits them. The eternal nature of this reward is emphasized, indicating that it is not a fleeting pleasure but an everlasting state of bliss. The verse concludes by describing this as "the great attainment", underscoring the immense value and significance of attaining Allah's pleasure and being granted entry into Paradise. It motivates the believers to strive for this noble goal and remain steadfast on the path of righteousness.
orig: أعد الله لهم جنات تجري من تحتها الأنهار خالدين فيها ذلك الفوز العظيم

translation: And those with excuses among the bedouins came to be permitted [to remain], and they who had lied to Allah and His Messenger sat [at home]. There will strike those who disbelieved among them a painful punishment.
interpretation: This verse speaks about the hypocrites among the Bedouins who made excuses to avoid joining the Muslims in their expeditions and campaigns.
