They fabricated lies to Allah and His Messenger to justify their staying behind. The verse then warns that a painful punishment awaits those who disbelieved and stayed behind without a valid excuse. It emphasizes the gravity of lying to Allah and His Messenger and the consequences of hypocrisy and lack of commitment to the cause of Islam.
orig: وجاء المعذرون من الأعراب ليؤذن لهم وقعد الذين كذبوا الله ورسوله سيصيب الذين كفروا منهم عذاب أليم

translation: There is no blame upon the weak or ill or those who do not find anything to spend [for the cause of Allah], if they are sincere to Allah and His Messenger. There is not upon the doers of good any cause [for blame]. And Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that those who are unable to participate in jihad or spend in the way of Allah due to genuine reasons such as weakness, illness or poverty are not blameworthy as long as their intentions are sincere towards Allah and His Messenger. It highlights that Allah does not burden a soul beyond its capacity. The verse also points out that those who do good and are sincere will not have any reason to be blamed. It ends by affirming Allah's attributes of forgiveness and mercy, indicating that He excuses those who have legitimate reasons for not being able to contribute or participate in His cause.
orig: ليس على الضعفاء ولا على المرضى ولا على الذين لا يجدون ما ينفقون حرج إذا نصحوا لله ورسوله ما على المحسنين من سبيل والله غفور رحيم

translation: Nor [is there blame] upon those who, when they came to you that you might give them mounts, you said, "I can find nothing for you to ride upon." They turned back while their eyes overflowed with tears out of grief that they could not find something to spend [for the cause of Allah].
interpretation: This verse is highlighting the sincerity and devotion of certain companions of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) who were so eager to participate in expeditions and battles for the cause of Islam that they became deeply saddened and cried when the Prophet was unable to provide them with mounts or provisions due to lack of resources. Despite their disappointment, they are not blamed or criticized because their intentions were pure and they genuinely wished to contribute and make sacrifices for their faith. The verse praises their earnestness and dedication, indicating that their sincere desire to serve Allah's cause is appreciated even if circumstances did not allow them to participate as they had hoped.
orig: ولا على الذين إذا ما أتوك لتحملهم قلت لا أجد ما أحملكم عليه تولوا وأعينهم تفيض من الدمع حزنا ألا يجدوا ما ينفقون

translation: The cause is only against the ones who ask your permission while they are rich. They are satisfied to be with those who stay behind, and Allah has sealed over their hearts, so they do not know.
interpretation: This verse is criticizing those who are wealthy and able-bodied, yet they seek permission to stay behind from joining the fight in the cause of Allah. They prefer to remain with those who are exempt from fighting, such as women and children. As a result of their choice, Allah has sealed their hearts, causing them to lack understanding of the importance of sacrificing for His sake. They are content with weakness and cowardice, not realizing the spiritual consequences of their decision.
orig: إنما السبيل على الذين يستأذنونك وهم أغنياء رضوا بأن يكونوا مع الخوالف وطبع الله على قلوبهم فهم لا يعلمون

translation: They will make excuses to you when you return to them. Say, "Do not make excuses; we will never believe you. Allah has already informed us of your news. And Allah will observe your deeds, and [so will] His Messenger; then you will be taken back to the Knower of the unseen and the witnessed, and He will inform you of what you used to do."
interpretation: This verse is addressing the hypocrites who make false excuses for their actions and behavior. It emphasizes that their excuses will not be accepted, as Allah has already exposed their true intentions and deeds. The verse also serves as a warning that Allah and His Messenger are fully aware of their actions, and they will be held accountable for them in the Hereafter, where they will face the consequences of their deeds before the All-Knowing, Allah.
orig: يعتذرون إليكم إذا رجعتم إليهم قل لا تعتذروا لن نؤمن لكم قد نبأنا الله من أخباركم وسيرى الله عملكم ورسوله ثم تردون إلى عالم الغيب والشهادة فينبئكم بما كنتم تعملون

translation: They will swear by Allah to you when you return to them that you would leave them alone. So leave them alone; indeed they are evil; and their refuge is Hell as recompense for what they had been earning.
interpretation: This verse is referring to the hypocrites who outwardly profess Islam but inwardly harbor disbelief and animosity towards the Muslims. When the Muslims return to them after a battle or expedition, they will swear by Allah that they are believers and ask to be left alone. However, Allah instructs the Muslims to turn away from them and leave them alone, as they are spiritually impure and their ultimate abode is Hell, as a consequence of their evil deeds and hypocrisy. This highlights the importance of sincerity in faith and the gravity of religious hypocrisy in Islam.
orig: سيحلفون بالله لكم إذا انقلبتم إليهم لتعرضوا عنهم فأعرضوا عنهم إنهم رجس ومأواهم جهنم جزاء بما كانوا يكسبون

translation: They swear to you [Muslims] to please you. But if you should be pleased with them - indeed, Allah is not pleased with the defiantly disobedient people.
interpretation: This verse is referring to the hypocrites who outwardly pretend to be Muslims in order to gain favor and approval from the believers. However, their insincere oaths and attempts to please the Muslims are futile, because Allah knows the truth of their inner disbelief and defiant disobedience. The lesson is that the pleasure and approval of Allah is what ultimately matters, not the fleeting approval of people. Muslims should not be deceived by empty words and flattery from those who inwardly reject faith, and should instead seek to please Allah alone through sincere devotion and righteousness.
orig: يحلفون لكم لترضوا عنهم فإن ترضوا عنهم فإن الله لا يرضى عن القوم الفاسقين

translation: The bedouins are stronger in disbelief and hypocrisy and more likely not to know the limits of what Allah has revealed to His Messenger. And Allah is Knowing and Wise.
interpretation: This verse suggests that the nomadic Arabs (bedouins) were more prone to rejecting faith and displaying hypocrisy compared to the settled folks. They were also more likely to be ignorant of the divine injunctions revealed to the Prophet Muhammad. The verse ends by affirming that Allah is All-Knowing of people's inner states and All-Wise in His decrees and judgments. It cautions against the insincerity and religious shallowness found among some of the desert Arabs during the Prophet's time.
orig: الأعراب أشد كفرا ونفاقا وأجدر ألا يعلموا حدود ما أنزل الله على رسوله والله عليم حكيم

translation: And among the Bedouins are some who consider what they spend as a loss and await for you turns of misfortune. Upon them will be a misfortune of evil. And Allah is Hearing and Knowing.
interpretation: This verse refers to the hypocrites among the Bedouins who grudgingly spend in the way of Allah, considering it a burden and a loss. They wish for misfortune to befall the Muslims, hoping that it would weaken their cause. However, Allah affirms that the evil consequences of their ill intentions and actions will rebound upon them. The verse emphasizes that Allah is fully aware of their hypocritical attitudes and insincerity, and He will hold them accountable for their deeds. It serves as a warning to those who harbor ill will towards the believers and reminds us that Allah's knowledge encompasses all things, including the innermost thoughts and intentions of people.
orig: ومن الأعراب من يتخذ ما ينفق مغرما ويتربص بكم الدوائر عليهم دائرة السوء والله سميع عليم

translation: And among the Bedouins are some who believe in Allah and the Last Day and consider what they spend as means of nearness to Allah and of [obtaining] invocations of the Messenger. Unquestionably, it is a means of nearness for them. Allah will admit them to His mercy. Indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse highlights that among the Bedouins, there are sincere believers who spend their wealth seeking closeness to Allah and the prayers of the Prophet (ﷺ). Their charitable deeds are a means of drawing nearer to Allah, and He will reward them by admitting them into His mercy. This emphasizes the importance of sincerity in faith and good deeds, and that Allah's forgiveness and mercy encompass all those who strive to please Him, regardless of their background or societal status.
orig: ومن الأعراب من يؤمن بالله واليوم الآخر ويتخذ ما ينفق قربات عند الله وصلوات الرسول ألا إنها قربة لهم سيدخلهم الله في رحمته إن الله غفور رحيم

translation: And the first forerunners [in the faith] among the Muhajireen and the Ansar and those who followed them with good conduct - Allah is pleased with them and they are pleased with Him, and He has prepared for them gardens beneath which rivers flow, wherein they will abide forever. That is the great attainment.
interpretation: This verse highlights the special status and reward for the early believers who made great sacrifices for Islam. The "first forerunners" refers to the Muhajireen, who were the early converts to Islam who emigrated from Mecca to Medina, and the Ansar, the residents of Medina who welcomed and supported the Prophet Muhammad and the Muhajireen. Those who followed the example of these pioneering Muslims with sincerity and good conduct are also included in Allah's pleasure and reward. Allah's pleasure upon them and their pleasure with Him signifies the reciprocal nature of the relationship between the sincere believers and their Lord. As a reward for their sacrifices, sincerity and good deeds, Allah has prepared for them the eternal bliss of paradise with its never-ending delights. Attaining this eternal reward of paradise is described as the supreme success and triumph, the greatest achievement one can aspire for, in contrast to the fleeting pleasures of this worldly life.
orig: والسابقون الأولون من المهاجرين والأنصار والذين اتبعوهم بإحسان رضي الله عنهم ورضوا عنه وأعد لهم جنات تجري تحتها الأنهار خالدين فيها أبدا ذلك الفوز العظيم

translation: And among those around you of the bedouins are hypocrites, and [also] from the people of Madinah. They have become accustomed to hypocrisy. You, [O Muhammad], do not know them, [but] We know them. We will punish them twice [in this world]; then they will be returned to a great punishment [in the Hereafter].
interpretation: This verse warns about the presence of hypocrites among the Bedouins around Madinah and even within the city itself. These hypocrites have grown bold and persistent in their hypocrisy. The Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) may not know their true nature, but Allah is fully aware of them. Allah promises that these hypocrites will face punishment twice - once in this world and then again in the Hereafter, where they will face a severe punishment for their deceit and disloyalty to the Islamic faith and community. This verse serves as a reminder for Muslims to be cautious of those who may outwardly profess faith but harbor ill intentions, and to trust in Allah's knowledge and justice in dealing with such individuals.
orig: وممن حولكم من الأعراب منافقون ومن أهل المدينة مردوا على النفاق لا تعلمهم نحن نعلمهم سنعذبهم مرتين ثم يردون إلى عذاب عظيم

translation: And [there are] others who have acknowledged their sins. They had mixed a righteous deed with another that was bad. Perhaps Allah will turn to them in forgiveness. Indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse speaks about those who recognize their wrongdoings and feel remorse for their sins. They have done both good and bad deeds in their lives. The verse indicates that Allah, in His infinite mercy, may forgive them for their sins if they sincerely repent and seek His forgiveness. It emphasizes Allah's attributes of being All-Forgiving (Ghafoor) and All-Merciful (Raheem), giving hope to those who have made mistakes but wish to turn back to the right path. The verse encourages people to acknowledge their faults, repent sincerely, and have faith in Allah's mercy and forgiveness.
orig: وآخرون اعترفوا بذنوبهم خلطوا عملا صالحا وآخر سيئا عسى الله أن يتوب عليهم إن الله غفور رحيم

translation: Take, [O, Muhammad], from their wealth a charity by which you purify them and cause them increase, and invoke [Allah's blessings] upon them. Indeed, your invocations are reassurance for them. And Allah is Hearing and Knowing.
interpretation: This verse instructs the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) to collect obligatory charity (Zakah) from the wealth of the believers. The act of giving charity purifies the giver from greed and attachment to worldly possessions, while also spiritually uplifting them and causing their wealth to increase through Allah's blessings. The Prophet is also directed to pray for those who give charity, as his prayers bring them comfort and reassurance. This verse emphasizes the importance of Zakah in Islam, not only as a means of redistributing wealth and helping the needy but also as a spiritual purification for the giver. It also highlights the role of the Prophet as an intercessor and spiritual guide for the believers.
orig: خذ من أموالهم صدقة تطهرهم وتزكيهم بها وصل عليهم إن صلاتك سكن لهم والله سميع عليم

translation: Do they not know that it is Allah who accepts repentance from His servants and receives charities and that it is Allah who is the Accepting of repentance, the Merciful?
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's infinite mercy and forgiveness. It reminds us that Allah is always ready to accept sincere repentance from His servants, no matter how grave their sins may be. It also highlights the importance of giving charity, as it is a means of purifying one's wealth and drawing closer to Allah. The repetition of Allah's attributes "the Accepting of repentance" and "the Merciful" reinforces the message that Allah's door of forgiveness is always open for those who turn to Him with sincere hearts and seek His mercy. This verse offers hope and encouragement to believers, urging them to constantly seek Allah's forgiveness and engage in acts of charity to attain His pleasure and mercy.
orig: ألم يعلموا أن الله هو يقبل التوبة عن عباده ويأخذ الصدقات وأن الله هو التواب الرحيم

translation: And say, "Do as you will, for Allah will see your deeds, and [so, will] His Messenger and the believers. And you will be returned to the Knower of the unseen and the witnessed, and He will inform you of what you used to do."
interpretation: This verse is a reminder that all our actions, whether good or bad, are witnessed by Allah, His Messenger, and the believers. It emphasizes the importance of being mindful of our deeds, as we will be held accountable for them in the Hereafter. The verse encourages us to strive for righteousness and to refrain from wrongdoing, knowing that nothing escapes Allah's knowledge and that we will face the consequences of our actions in the afterlife. It also highlights the concept of divine justice, as Allah, the Knower of the unseen and the witnessed, will inform us of what we used to do and judge us accordingly.
orig: وقل اعملوا فسيرى الله عملكم ورسوله والمؤمنون وستردون إلى عالم الغيب والشهادة فينبئكم بما كنتم تعملون

translation: And [there are] others deferred for the decree of Allah. Either He will punish them or He will turn to them in forgiveness. And Allah is Knowing and Wise.
interpretation: This verse refers to a group of people whose fate is yet to be decided by Allah. It suggests that Allah, in His infinite wisdom and knowledge, will either punish them for their wrongdoings or forgive them if He wills. This highlights the concept of divine justice and mercy in Islam, where the ultimate decision of one's fate rests with Allah. It also emphasizes the importance of repentance and seeking forgiveness from Allah, as He is the one who can grant it to whomever He chooses. The verse serves as a reminder that all human beings are accountable for their actions and that the consequences of their deeds are determined by Allah's judgment.
orig: وآخرون مرجون لأمر الله إما يعذبهم وإما يتوب عليهم والله عليم حكيم

translation: And [there are] those [hypocrites] who took for themselves a mosque for causing harm and disbelief and division among the believers and as a station for whoever had warred against Allah and His Messenger before. And they will surely swear, "We intended only the best." And Allah testifies that indeed they are liars.
interpretation: This verse is referring to the hypocrites who built a mosque with the intention of causing harm to the Muslim community, promoting disbelief, and creating division among the believers. They also intended to use it as a base for those who had previously fought against Allah and His Messenger. When confronted, they would swear that their intentions were good, but Allah bears witness to their lies. The interpretation is that the hypocrites' actions were driven by malice and ill intentions, and their false oaths cannot conceal the truth that Allah knows. It serves as a warning against those who seek to undermine the unity of the believers and act against the teachings of Islam while claiming to be Muslims themselves.
orig: والذين اتخذوا مسجدا ضرارا وكفرا وتفريقا بين المؤمنين وإرصادا لمن حارب الله ورسوله من قبل وليحلفن إن أردنا إلا الحسنى والله يشهد إنهم لكاذبون

translation: Do not stand [for prayer] within it - a mosque founded on righteousness from the first day is more worthy for you to stand in. Within it are men who love to purify themselves; and Allah loves those who purify themselves.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of praying in a mosque that is built upon the foundation of righteousness and piety from the very beginning. It suggests that such a mosque is more deserving of being a place of worship than others. The verse also highlights the significance of spiritual and physical cleanliness, as it mentions that within this mosque are men who love to purify themselves, both inwardly and outwardly. This love for purification is praised by Allah, who loves those who constantly strive to maintain their purity. The interpretation underscores the value of sincerity, righteousness, and cleanliness in the life of a believer, especially when it comes to places of worship and religious devotion.
orig: لا تقم فيه أبدا لمسجد أسس على التقوى من أول يوم أحق أن تقوم فيه فيه رجال يحبون أن يتطهروا والله يحب المطهرين

translation: Is it then he who laid the foundation of his building on piety to Allah and His Good Pleasure better, or he who laid the foundation of his building on the brink of an undetermined precipice ready to crumble down, so that it crumbled to pieces with him into the Fire of Hell. And Allah guides not the people who are the Zalimun (cruel, violent, proud, polytheist and wrong-doer).
interpretation: This verse is drawing a contrast between two types of people - those who build their lives on the foundation of piety and seeking Allah's pleasure, versus those who build on the edge of destruction without any firm footing. Building one's life on taqwa - consciousness and fear of Allah - and seeking His pleasure is the path of stability and ultimate success. On the other hand, those who live recklessly without regard for Allah are setting themselves up for ruin, like someone building a house on the edge of a cliff that will inevitably collapse and lead them to the Hellfire. Allah does not guide those who choose to wrong themselves by rejecting faith and wisdom. The wise person builds their life on the solid foundation of faith and obedience to Allah.
orig: أفمن أسس بنيانه على تقوى من الله ورضوان خير أم من أسس بنيانه على شفا جرف هار فانهار به في نار جهنم والله لا يهدي القوم الظالمين

translation: Their building which they built will not cease to be a [cause of] skepticism in their hearts until their hearts are cut [i.e., stopped]. And Allah is Knowing and Wise.
interpretation: The hypocrites built a mosque with the intention of causing harm and promoting disbelief. This evil plot will continue to create doubt and unease in their hearts, making them question their actions and motives. This feeling of uncertainty will persist within them until their hearts stop beating at the time of their death. Allah, in His infinite wisdom and knowledge, is well aware of their malicious intentions and the consequences they will face as a result of their actions.
orig: لا يزال بنيانهم الذي بنوا ريبة في قلوبهم إلا أن تقطع قلوبهم والله عليم حكيم

translation: Indeed, Allah has purchased from the believers their lives and their properties [in exchange] for that they will have Paradise. They fight in the cause of Allah, so they kill and are killed. [It is] a true promise [binding] upon Him in the Torah and the Gospel and the Qur'an. And who is truer to his covenant than Allah? So rejoice in your transaction which you have contracted. And it is that which is the great attainment.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the ultimate sacrifice that believers make in the path of Allah - giving up their lives and wealth in exchange for the promise of Paradise. It highlights the unwavering commitment and devotion required of true believers, who are willing to fight and die for the cause of Allah. The promise of reward is affirmed as a binding covenant mentioned in all the sacred scriptures. The verse encourages believers to rejoice in this transaction, considering it the greatest achievement and success one can attain in this life and the hereafter. It underscores the importance of fulfilling one's covenant with Allah and remaining steadfast in faith and struggle.
orig: إن الله اشترى من المؤمنين أنفسهم وأموالهم بأن لهم الجنة يقاتلون في سبيل الله فيقتلون ويقتلون وعدا عليه حقا في التوراة والإنجيل والقرآن ومن أوفى بعهده من الله فاستبشروا ببيعكم الذي بايعتم به وذلك هو الفوز العظيم

translation: Those who repent, those who worship, those who praise, those who journey, those who bow down, those who prostrate themselves, those who enjoin what is right and forbid what is wrong, and those who observe the limits set by Allah. And give glad tidings to the believers.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the qualities and actions of the true believers. They constantly turn to Allah in repentance, engage in worship and praise of Him, and strive in His cause. They humble themselves before Allah through prayer and prostration. The believers actively promote righteousness and forbid evil, acting as a positive force in society. They adhere to the boundaries and guidelines set by Allah in all aspects of life. The verse ends with a glad tiding to the believers, indicating that those who possess these qualities will be rewarded by Allah. It serves as an encouragement for Muslims to adopt these righteous traits and actions in their lives.
orig: التائبون العابدون الحامدون السائحون الراكعون الساجدون الآمرون بالمعروف والناهون عن المنكر والحافظون لحدود الله وبشر المؤمنين

translation: It is not for the Prophet and those who have believed to ask forgiveness for the polytheists, even if they were relatives, after it has become clear to them that they are companions of Hellfire.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that once it becomes evident that someone has died as a polytheist, it is prohibited for the Prophet and the believers to seek forgiveness for them, even if they were close relatives. This is because seeking forgiveness for those who died as polytheists implies approving of their disbelief, which contradicts the fundamental principles of Islam. The verse highlights the importance of adhering to the boundaries set by Allah and prioritizing one's faith over personal relationships when they come into conflict.
orig: ما كان للنبي والذين آمنوا أن يستغفروا للمشركين ولو كانوا أولي قربى من بعد ما تبين لهم أنهم أصحاب الجحيم

translation: And the request of forgiveness of Abraham for his father was only because of a promise he had made to him. But when it became apparent to him [Abraham] that he [his father] was an enemy to Allah, he disassociated himself from him. Indeed was Abraham compassionate and patient.
interpretation: This verse shows the importance of keeping one's promise, even if it was made to a disbeliever. Abraham had promised his father to pray for his forgiveness, and he kept his word until it became clear to him that his father was an enemy of Allah and would not believe. At that point, Abraham disassociated himself from his father. The verse also highlights the noble character of Abraham, describing him as compassionate and patient. Even in the face of his father's disbelief, Abraham still treated him with kindness and prayed for his guidance, until all hope was lost. This teaches us to honor our commitments and to treat others with compassion, while staying true to our principles and our faith in Allah.
orig: وما كان استغفار إبراهيم لأبيه إلا عن موعدة وعدها إياه فلما تبين له أنه عدو لله تبرأ منه إن إبراهيم لأواه حليم

translation: And Allah would not let a people stray after He has guided them until He makes clear to them what they should avoid. Indeed, Allah is Knowing of all things.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's justice and mercy. Allah does not misguide people arbitrarily after having guided them. Instead, He first makes it clear to them what they should avoid and what the consequences of their actions will be. This shows that people have the free will to choose their path, but also the responsibility to follow Allah's guidance once it has been made clear to them. The verse also highlights Allah's omniscience - He has perfect knowledge of all things, including people's intentions and actions, and therefore His judgment is always just and fair.
orig: وما كان الله ليضل قوما بعد إذ هداهم حتى يبين لهم ما يتقون إن الله بكل شيء عليم

translation: Indeed, to Allah belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth; He gives life and causes death. And you have not besides Allah any protector or any helper.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute sovereignty and power of Allah over all creation. It affirms that Allah alone is the true owner and controller of the heavens and the earth, and that He alone has the power to give life and cause death. The verse also reminds us that we have no protector or helper besides Allah, and that we should rely solely on Him for guidance, support, and salvation. It encourages us to submit to Allah's will and to seek His pleasure in all aspects of our lives, knowing that He is the only true source of strength and guidance.
orig: إن الله له ملك السماوات والأرض يحيي ويميت وما لكم من دون الله من ولي ولا نصير

translation: Allah has already forgiven the Prophet and the Muhajirun and the Ansar who followed him in the hour of difficulty after the hearts of a party of them had almost inclined [to doubt], and then He forgave them. Indeed, He was to them Kind and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the mercy and forgiveness of Allah towards the Prophet Muhammad and his companions, particularly the Muhajirun (those who migrated from Mecca to Medina) and the Ansar (the helpers in Medina). It refers to a specific incident, likely the Battle of Tabuk, where some of the believers faced hardships and doubts. However, Allah's forgiveness and mercy encompassed them, as He is always Kind and Merciful to His servants who strive in His cause and follow the Prophet's guidance, even if they face moments of weakness or difficulty along the way. This verse serves as a reminder of Allah's infinite grace and the importance of staying steadfast in faith.
orig: لقد تاب الله على النبي والمهاجرين والأنصار الذين اتبعوه في ساعة العسرة من بعد ما كاد يزيغ قلوب فريق منهم ثم تاب عليهم إنه بهم رءوف رحيم

translation: And [He also forgave] the three who were left behind [and regretted their error] to the point that the earth closed in on them in spite of its vastness and their souls confined them and they were certain that there is no refuge from Allah except in Him. Then He turned to them so they could repent. Indeed, Allah is the Accepting of repentance, the Merciful.
interpretation: This verse is referring to the three companions of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) who did not join him in the battle of Tabuk without a valid excuse. As a result, they were boycotted by the community until Allah accepted their repentance. The key lesson is that no matter how great one's sin, the door to sincere repentance is always open. Allah's mercy encompasses all things, and He is ever ready to forgive those who turn back to Him remorsefully, seeking His pardon. The verse emphasizes Allah's infinite mercy and His readiness to accept the repentance of those who sincerely turn to Him in contrition.
orig: وعلى الثلاثة الذين خلفوا حتى إذا ضاقت عليهم الأرض بما رحبت وضاقت عليهم أنفسهم وظنوا أن لا ملجأ من الله إلا إليه ثم تاب عليهم ليتوبوا إن الله هو التواب الرحيم

translation: O you who have believed, fear Allah and be with those who are true.
interpretation: This verse is a reminder for the believers to have consciousness of Allah (taqwa) in all their affairs, and to always strive to be among the truthful and sincere people. It emphasizes the importance of honesty and integrity in one's dealings with others and in one's relationship with Allah. Being truthful is a key characteristic of the righteous believers, as opposed to hypocrisy and deception. The verse encourages the believers to keep the company of those who are known for their truthfulness, as this will help them stay on the right path and avoid falsehood. It also implies that being truthful and sincere is a means of attaining closeness to Allah and earning His pleasure.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا اتقوا الله وكونوا مع الصادقين

translation: It was not [proper] for the people of Madinah and those surrounding them of the bedouins that they remain behind after [the departure of] the Messenger of Allah or that they prefer themselves over his self. That is because they are not afflicted by thirst or fatigue or hunger in the cause of Allah, nor do they tread on any ground that enrages the disbelievers, nor do they inflict upon an enemy any infliction but that is registered for them as a righteous deed. Indeed, Allah does not allow to be lost the reward of the doers of good.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of supporting and following the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) in his efforts to spread Islam, even if it means enduring hardships and making sacrifices. It suggests that those who remain behind and prioritize their own comfort over the Prophet's mission are not acting properly. The verse also highlights that any difficulty or challenge faced in the path of Allah, whether it is physical discomfort, confronting the enemies of Islam, or any other struggle, will be rewarded by Allah as a righteous deed. It underscores the idea that Allah appreciates and never allows the efforts and good deeds of the believers to go to waste.
orig: ما كان لأهل المدينة ومن حولهم من الأعراب أن يتخلفوا عن رسول الله ولا يرغبوا بأنفسهم عن نفسه ذلك بأنهم لا يصيبهم ظمأ ولا نصب ولا مخمصة في سبيل الله ولا يطئون موطئا يغيظ الكفار ولا ينالون من عدو نيلا إلا كتب لهم به عمل صالح إن الله لا يضيع أجر المحسنين

translation: Nor do they spend an expenditure, small or large, or cross a valley but that it is registered for them that Allah may reward them for the best of what they were doing.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah takes into account every good deed that a person does, no matter how small or insignificant it may seem. Whether it is spending in charity, even if the amount is little, or undertaking a difficult journey for a righteous cause, Allah records it and will reward the person in the best possible manner for their sincerity and good intentions. It encourages the believers to strive in doing good, with the assurance that no act of goodness will go unnoticed or unrewarded by Allah.
orig: ولا ينفقون نفقة صغيرة ولا كبيرة ولا يقطعون واديا إلا كتب لهم ليجزيهم الله أحسن ما كانوا يعملون

translation: And it is not for the believers to go forth [to battle] all at once. For there should separate from every division of them a group [remaining] to obtain understanding in the religion and warn their people when they return to them that they might be cautious.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of religious education and the role of scholars in the Muslim community. It suggests that not all believers should go out to fight in battles, but rather a group from each section of the community should remain behind to study and gain a deeper understanding of the religion. This group then has the responsibility to teach and warn their people when they return, so that the community may be mindful of their religious duties and cautious of straying from the right path. The verse highlights the significance of seeking knowledge and sharing it with others for the spiritual well-being and growth of the Muslim society.
orig: وما كان المؤمنون لينفروا كافة فلولا نفر من كل فرقة منهم طائفة ليتفقهوا في الدين ولينذروا قومهم إذا رجعوا إليهم لعلهم يحذرون

translation: O you who have believed, fight those adjacent to you of the disbelievers and let them find in you harshness. And know that Allah is with the righteous.
interpretation: This verse calls upon the believers to fight against the disbelievers who are in close proximity to them, both physically and ideologically. It encourages the Muslims to be firm and uncompromising in their stance against the enemies of Islam, letting them experience the strength and determination of the believers. The verse also reminds the Muslims that Allah is with those who are righteous and mindful of Him, supporting and aiding them in their struggle against the forces of disbelief. It emphasizes the importance of remaining steadfast in faith and not showing any weakness or hesitation when confronting the adversaries of Islam.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا قاتلوا الذين يلونكم من الكفار وليجدوا فيكم غلظة واعلموا أن الله مع المتقين

translation: And whenever a surah is revealed, there are among them those who say, "Which of you has this increased in faith?" As for those who believed, it has increased them in faith, and they are rejoicing.
interpretation: This verse highlights the contrasting reactions of believers and disbelievers when a new surah of the Qur'an is revealed. While the disbelievers question the impact of the revelation on people's faith, the true believers find their faith strengthened and rejoice in the new guidance from Allah. This interpretation emphasizes the power of the Qur'an to fortify the faith of those who sincerely believe and accept its message, while also exposing the skepticism and disbelief of those who reject it.
orig: وإذا ما أنزلت سورة فمنهم من يقول أيكم زادته هذه إيمانا فأما الذين آمنوا فزادتهم إيمانا وهم يستبشرون

translation: But as for those in whose hearts is disease, it has [only] increased them in evil [in addition] to their evil. And they died while they were disbelievers.
interpretation: This verse refers to the hypocrites and those with weak faith. When they hear the revelations of Allah, instead of benefiting from them and increasing in faith, it only increases them in doubt, disbelief, and hypocrisy due to the sickness of their hearts. They reject the truth until they die as disbelievers, having gained no guidance from Allah's signs and revelations. It highlights the spiritual consequences of allowing doubts and desires to overpower one's faith, leading to a state of increased corruption and disbelief.
orig: وأما الذين في قلوبهم مرض فزادتهم رجسا إلى رجسهم وماتوا وهم كافرون

translation: Do they not see that they are tried every year once or twice but then they do not repent nor do they remember?
interpretation: This verse is pointing out the heedlessness and ingratitude of those who face trials and tribulations repeatedly, yet fail to turn back to Allah in repentance and remembrance. It suggests that when people are tested with hardships, it should serve as a reminder for them to reflect on their actions, seek forgiveness, and mend their ways. However, many persist in their negligence and do not take heed of the lessons and warnings that these trials bring. The verse emphasizes the importance of introspection, repentance, and being mindful of Allah's messages and signs in our lives.
orig: أولا يرون أنهم يفتنون في كل عام مرة أو مرتين ثم لا يتوبون ولا هم يذكرون

translation: And whenever a surah is revealed, they look at each other, [saying], "Does anyone see you?" and then they dismiss themselves. Allah has dismissed their hearts because they are a people who do not understand.
interpretation: This verse is referring to the hypocrites who, when a new surah was revealed, would look around to see if anyone was watching them before leaving the gathering of the Prophet (peace be upon him). Their behavior showed their lack of sincerity and commitment to Islam. Allah has turned their hearts away from the truth because they refuse to understand and accept the message of the Qur'an. They are more concerned with appearances and the opinions of others than with truly comprehending and embracing the guidance of Allah.
orig: وإذا ما أنزلت سورة نظر بعضهم إلى بعض هل يراكم من أحد ثم انصرفوا صرف الله قلوبهم بأنهم قوم لا يفقهون

translation: There has certainly come to you a Messenger from among yourselves. Grievous to him is what you suffer; [he is] concerned over you and to the believers is kind and merciful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the compassionate and empathetic nature of Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) towards his followers. As a messenger chosen from among the people, he deeply cares about their well-being and is distressed by the hardships they face. The Prophet's (peace be upon him) concern for the believers is characterized by his kindness and mercy towards them. This verse highlights the special bond between the Prophet (peace be upon him) and the believers, showing that he is not a distant or indifferent figure, but rather a caring and involved leader who has the best interests of his followers at heart.
orig: لقد جاءكم رسول من أنفسكم عزيز عليه ما عنتم حريص عليكم بالمؤمنين رءوف رحيم

translation: But if they turn away, [O Muhammad], say, "Sufficient for me is Allah; there is no deity except Him. On Him I have relied, and He is the Lord of the Great Throne."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of relying on Allah alone and seeking His support and guidance, especially in the face of rejection or opposition from others. It reminds the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and the believers to remain steadfast in their faith and to trust in Allah's plan, knowing that He is the ultimate authority and the Lord of the mighty Throne. This interpretation highlights the concept of tawakkul (reliance on Allah) as a key aspect of Islamic faith, encouraging believers to find strength and comfort in their connection with Allah, even during challenging times.
orig: فإن تولوا فقل حسبي الله لا إله إلا هو عليه توكلت وهو رب العرش العظيم

translation: Alif, Lam, Ra. These are the verses of the wise Book.
interpretation: The letters Alif, Lam, Ra at the beginning of this verse are among the mysterious letters that appear at the beginning of some surahs in the Qur'an. Their exact meaning is known only to Allah. The mention of these letters serves to draw the attention of the listener or reader to the divine nature and wisdom of the Qur'an. The verse then proclaims that the verses that follow are part of a wise book, indicating that the Qur'an is full of wisdom, guidance and enlightenment for those who reflect upon its meanings. This sets the stage for the profound and insightful verses that are to follow in this surah.
orig: الر تلك آيات الكتاب الحكيم

translation: Was it a wonder for the people that We revealed [Our message] to a man from among them, [saying], "Warn mankind and give good tidings to those who believe that they will have a [firm] precedence of honor with their Lord"? [But] the disbelievers say, "Indeed, this is an obvious magician."
interpretation: The verse highlights the disbelief and astonishment of the people when Allah chose a man from among them to be His messenger. It emphasizes that the role of the prophet is to warn people of the consequences of their actions and to give good news to the believers about their honored status with Allah. However, the disbelievers reject the prophet's message and accuse him of being a magician, denying the divine nature of his revelation. This interpretation underscores the challenges faced by prophets in conveying the message of Islam and the resistance they encounter from those who refuse to believe in the truth of their mission.
orig: أكان للناس عجبا أن أوحينا إلى رجل منهم أن أنذر الناس وبشر الذين آمنوا أن لهم قدم صدق عند ربهم قال الكافرون إن هذا لساحر مبين

translation: Indeed, your Lord is Allah, who created the heavens and the earth in six days and then established Himself above the Throne, arranging the matter [of His creation]. There is no intercessor except after His permission. That is Allah, your Lord, so worship Him. Then will you not remember?
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the supreme power and authority of Allah as the Creator and Sustainer of the universe. It highlights that Allah alone is worthy of worship and that no one can intercede with Him except by His permission. The verse serves as a reminder for humans to acknowledge Allah's lordship, worship Him alone, and reflect upon His signs and blessings. It also underscores the importance of seeking Allah's guidance and mercy directly, without relying on intermediaries or intercessors, as ultimately, it is only Allah who has the power to grant or withhold permission for intercession.
orig: إن ربكم الله الذي خلق السماوات والأرض في ستة أيام ثم استوى على العرش يدبر الأمر ما من شفيع إلا من بعد إذنه ذلكم الله ربكم فاعبدوه أفلا تذكرون

translation: To Him is your return all together. [It is] the promise of Allah [which is] truth. Indeed, He begins the [process of] creation and then repeats it that He may reward those who have believed and done righteous deeds, in justice. But those who disbelieved will have a drink of scalding water and a painful punishment for what they used to deny.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the ultimate return of all humans to Allah, and the fulfillment of His promise of resurrection and judgment. It highlights the justice of Allah in rewarding the believers who did good deeds, while punishing the disbelievers who denied the truth with scalding water and painful torment. The repetition of the creation process affirms Allah's power and ability to resurrect the dead for judgment. The verse serves as a reminder of the consequences of faith and disbelief, encouraging humans to live righteously in preparation for the Day of Judgment.
orig: إليه مرجعكم جميعا وعد الله حقا إنه يبدأ الخلق ثم يعيده ليجزي الذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات بالقسط والذين كفروا لهم شراب من حميم وعذاب أليم بما كانوا يكفرون

translation: It is He who made the sun a shining light and the moon a derived light and determined for it phases - that you may know the number of years and account [of time]. Allah has not created this except in truth. He details the signs for a people who know.
interpretation: This verse highlights Allah's wisdom and power in creating the sun and moon, which serve as a means for humans to keep track of time and organize their lives. The sun's brightness and the moon's phases are not random or coincidental, but rather a deliberate sign of Allah's design and purpose. The verse emphasizes that everything in the universe has been created with truth and for a reason, and encourages people to reflect upon these signs to gain a deeper understanding and appreciation of Allah's creation. It also suggests that those who have knowledge and insight will be able to recognize and comprehend the significance behind these celestial phenomena.
orig: هو الذي جعل الشمس ضياء والقمر نورا وقدره منازل لتعلموا عدد السنين والحساب ما خلق الله ذلك إلا بالحق يفصل الآيات لقوم يعلمون

translation: Indeed, in the alternation of the night and the day and [in] what Allah has created in the heavens and the earth are signs for a people who fear Allah.
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of reflecting upon the natural phenomena around us, such as the cycle of day and night, and the wonders of Allah's creation in the heavens and the earth. These signs serve as reminders for those who are mindful of Allah and seek to live righteously. By contemplating these signs, believers can strengthen their faith, recognizing the power, wisdom, and mercy of the Creator. The verse encourages people to be among those who are God-conscious and use the signs in nature as a means to draw closer to Allah and increase their reverence for Him.
orig: إن في اختلاف الليل والنهار وما خلق الله في السماوات والأرض لآيات لقوم يتقون

translation: Indeed, those who do not expect the meeting with Us and are satisfied with the life of this world and feel secure therein and those who are heedless of Our signs -
interpretation: This verse is referring to those who are content with the material world and do not believe in or anticipate the afterlife. They are satisfied with the temporary pleasures and comforts of this worldly existence, feeling secure and at ease in it. As a result, they become heedless and neglectful of the signs and revelations of Allah, failing to reflect upon them and take heed. Their focus remains solely on the present life, without any concern for the eternal consequences of their actions or the ultimate meeting with their Lord. This attitude is condemned as it reflects a lack of faith, spirituality, and mindfulness of one's true purpose and final destination.
orig: إن الذين لا يرجون لقاءنا ورضوا بالحياة الدنيا واطمأنوا بها والذين هم عن آياتنا غافلون

translation: Those - their refuge is the Fire because of what they used to earn.
interpretation: This verse warns that those who persistently engage in evil deeds and reject faith will face the consequences of their actions in the Hereafter. Their ultimate abode will be the Fire of Hell, as a direct result of the sins they committed and the good they neglected during their worldly life. It emphasizes the principle of individual responsibility and divine justice, reminding humans that their choices and actions in this life have a profound impact on their eternal fate.
orig: أولئك مأواهم النار بما كانوا يكسبون

translation: Indeed, those who believe and do righteous deeds - their Lord will guide them because of their faith. Beneath them rivers will flow in the Gardens of Pleasure.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of faith and good deeds in attaining guidance from Allah and the ultimate reward of Paradise. Those who sincerely believe in Allah and His message, and couple their faith with righteous actions, will be guided by Allah on the straight path. Their unwavering faith will be the key to their guidance. As a result of their faith and good deeds, they will be granted the blissful abode of Paradise, where rivers flow beneath them, signifying the abundance of blessings and delights they will experience eternally. This interpretation highlights the direct correlation between one's faith, actions, and the consequent reward in the Hereafter.
orig: إن الذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات يهديهم ربهم بإيمانهم تجري من تحتهم الأنهار في جنات النعيم

translation: Their call therein will be, "Exalted are You, O Allah," and their greeting therein will be, "Peace." And the last of their call will be, "Praise to Allah, Lord of the worlds!"
interpretation: This verse describes the state of the believers in Paradise. They will glorify Allah and greet each other with peace. Their final call will be to praise Allah, the Lord of all creation. This interpretation suggests that in Paradise, the believers will be in a state of constant remembrance, gratitude, and peace, acknowledging Allah's greatness and their submission to Him as the Lord of the worlds.
orig: دعواهم فيها سبحانك اللهم وتحيتهم فيها سلام وآخر دعواهم أن الحمد لله رب العالمين

translation: And if Allah were to hasten for the people the evil [they invoke] as He hastens for them the good, their term would have been ended for them. But We leave the ones who do not expect the meeting with Us, in their transgression, wandering blindly.
interpretation: This verse highlights the mercy and wisdom of Allah. If He were to respond to people's invocations for evil and punishment as swiftly as He responds to their prayers for good, they would have been destroyed due to their own impatience and short-sightedness. However, Allah gives people time and opportunity to repent and mend their ways. Those who do not believe in the Hereafter and the meeting with Allah are left to continue in their transgression and misguidance, as a result of their own choice and actions. The verse serves as a reminder for people to be careful about what they invoke and to have faith in Allah's wisdom and timing.
orig: ولو يعجل الله للناس الشر استعجالهم بالخير لقضي إليهم أجلهم فنذر الذين لا يرجون لقاءنا في طغيانهم يعمهون

translation: And when affliction touches man, he calls upon Us, whether lying on his side or sitting or standing; but when We remove from him his affliction, he continues [in disobedience] as if he had never called upon Us to [remove] an affliction that touched him. Thus is made pleasing to the transgressors that which they have been doing.
interpretation: This verse highlights the fickle nature of human beings. When faced with hardship or suffering, they turn to Allah in supplication, desperately seeking relief in whatever state they find themselves. However, once Allah removes their affliction and grants them ease, they often forget their previous state of humility and revert to their old ways of disobedience and ingratitude. They carry on as if they had never experienced any difficulty or called upon Allah for help. This behavior is common among those who transgress the boundaries set by Allah, as their misdeeds and extravagance are made appealing to them, blinding them to the reality of their actions and the consequences they will face in the Hereafter. The verse serves as a reminder for people to remain consistent in their faith and gratitude towards Allah, both in times of hardship and ease.
orig: وإذا مس الإنسان الضر دعانا لجنبه أو قاعدا أو قائما فلما كشفنا عنه ضره مر كأن لم يدعنا إلى ضر مسه كذلك زين للمسرفين ما كانوا يعملون

translation: And We had already destroyed generations before you when they wronged, and their messengers had come to them with clear proofs, but they were not to believe. Thus do We recompense the criminal people.
interpretation: This verse serves as a warning to those who reject the truth and persist in wrongdoing. It reminds us that throughout history, God has destroyed entire generations who refused to believe in the clear signs brought to them by their messengers. Despite the evidence presented to them, they chose to remain in disbelief and continued their unjust practices. As a result, they faced the consequences of their actions, and God punished them for their transgressions. This verse emphasizes the importance of heeding the warnings of the messengers and believing in the truth, as those who persist in their criminal behavior will ultimately face the repercussions of their choices.
orig: ولقد أهلكنا القرون من قبلكم لما ظلموا وجاءتهم رسلهم بالبينات وما كانوا ليؤمنوا كذلك نجزي القوم المجرمين

translation: Then We made you successors in the land after them, to see how you would act.
interpretation: This verse speaks to the concept of human beings as successors or vicegerents on Earth. It implies that God has entrusted humanity with the responsibility of managing and taking care of the world, and that He is observing how we fulfill this duty. The verse suggests that our actions and decisions in this life will be judged, and that we will be held accountable for how we use the trust and authority given to us as God's representatives on Earth. It is a reminder of the great responsibility that comes with the gift of free will, and the importance of striving to act in a way that is pleasing to God.
orig: ثم جعلناكم خلائف في الأرض من بعدهم لننظر كيف تعملون

translation: And when Our clear verses are recited to them, those who do not expect the meeting with Us say, "Bring us a Qur'an other than this or change it." Say, [O Muhammad], "It is not for me to change it on my own accord. I only follow what is revealed to me. Indeed I fear, if I should disobey my Lord, the punishment of a tremendous Day."
interpretation: This verse is a response to the disbelievers who, upon hearing the clear verses of the Qur'an, demanded that the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) bring a different revelation or alter the existing one. The verse emphasizes that the Prophet had no authority to change the divine message according to his own whims or the desires of others. He was bound to follow only what was revealed to him by God. The Prophet is further instructed to convey to the disbelievers that he fears the punishment of a tremendous Day (i.e., the Day of Judgment) if he were to disobey his Lord by altering the revelation. This highlights the importance of conveying the message of Islam in its pristine form, without any alterations or modifications, and the grave consequences of disobeying God's commands.
orig: وإذا تتلى عليهم آياتنا بينات قال الذين لا يرجون لقاءنا ائت بقرآن غير هذا أو بدله قل ما يكون لي أن أبدله من تلقاء نفسي إن أتبع إلا ما يوحى إلي إني أخاف إن عصيت ربي عذاب يوم عظيم

translation: Say, "If Allah had willed, I would not have recited it to you, nor would He have made it known to you. I had remained among you for a lifetime before it. Then will you not reason?"
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) did not bring the Qur'an of his own accord, but rather it was revealed to him by Allah's will. The Prophet is instructed to remind the people that he had lived among them for a considerable time before the revelation of the Qur'an, and during that period, he was not known to have composed anything similar to the divine revelation. This fact should serve as a proof that the Qur'an is not the Prophet's own creation, but a message from Allah. The verse encourages people to use their reason and understand that the Qur'an's origin is divine, and not from the Prophet himself.
orig: قل لو شاء الله ما تلوته عليكم ولا أدراكم به فقد لبثت فيكم عمرا من قبله أفلا تعقلون

translation: So who is more unjust than one who invents a lie about Allah or denies His verses? Indeed, the criminals will not succeed.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the severity of the sin of fabricating lies against Allah or rejecting His revelations. It suggests that there is no greater injustice than attributing false statements to Allah or denying the truth of His messages. Those who engage in such criminal behavior are condemned as the most unjust of people. The verse affirms that success will never be attained by those who commit these grave transgressions against Allah. It serves as a strong warning against the consequences of dishonesty and disbelief in relation to Allah and His verses.
orig: فمن أظلم ممن افترى على الله كذبا أو كذب بآياته إنه لا يفلح المجرمون

translation: And they worship other than Allah that which neither harms them nor benefits them, and they say, "These are our intercessors with Allah." Say, "Do you inform Allah of something He does not know in the heavens or on the earth?" Exalted is He and high above what they associate with Him.
interpretation: This verse criticizes the polytheistic practice of worshipping idols and false deities, believing that they can intercede with Allah on their behalf. It emphasizes that these idols have no power to benefit or harm and that Allah is aware of all things in the heavens and earth. The verse asserts Allah's oneness and transcendence above any partners people may associate with Him, highlighting the gravity of the sin of shirk (associating others with Allah in worship).
orig: ويعبدون من دون الله ما لا يضرهم ولا ينفعهم ويقولون هؤلاء شفعاؤنا عند الله قل أتنبئون الله بما لا يعلم في السماوات ولا في الأرض سبحانه وتعالى عما يشركون

translation: And mankind was not but one community [united in religion], but [then] they differed. And if not for a word that preceded from your Lord, it would have been judged between them [immediately] concerning that over which they differ.
interpretation: This verse suggests that originally, all of humanity was united as a single community, presumably following the same religious path. However, over time, people began to differ in their beliefs and practices. The verse implies that this divergence was not part of God's original plan for humanity. It also suggests that God had already decreed or predetermined how these differences would ultimately be resolved or judged. If not for this divine decree, God would have passed immediate judgment to settle these disputes and differences that arose among people. The verse points to an underlying divine wisdom in allowing differences to exist, while affirming that God will indeed judge between differing factions in the end according to His plan.
orig: وما كان الناس إلا أمة واحدة فاختلفوا ولولا كلمة سبقت من ربك لقضي بينهم فيما فيه يختلفون

translation: And they say, "Why is a sign not sent down to him from his Lord?" So say, "The unseen is only for Allah [to administer], so wait; indeed, I am with you among those who wait."
interpretation: This verse is a response to the disbelievers who demand a miraculous sign from the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) as proof of his prophethood. Allah instructs the Prophet to inform them that the knowledge of the unseen, including the timing and nature of such signs, belongs exclusively to Allah. The Prophet and the believers are urged to be patient and await Allah's decree, trusting in His wisdom and plan. This highlights the importance of faith and submission to Allah, even in the face of challenges and doubts from others. It also emphasizes that the ultimate proof of the Prophet's message lies in the Qur'an itself, rather than in external miracles.
orig: ويقولون لولا أنزل عليه آية من ربه فقل إنما الغيب لله فانتظروا إني معكم من المنتظرين

translation: And when We let the people taste mercy after adversity has touched them, at once they conspire against Our verses. Say, "Allah is swifter in strategy." Indeed, Our messengers record that which you conspire.
interpretation: This verse highlights the fickle nature of human beings. When they are blessed with ease and comfort after facing hardships, they often forget the lessons learned during difficult times and start plotting against the signs of Allah. However, Allah reminds us that He is always aware of their schemes and can easily outmaneuver them. The verse also emphasizes the importance of being grateful and steadfast in faith, even during times of prosperity, as Allah's messengers are constantly recording our actions and intentions.
orig: وإذا أذقنا الناس رحمة من بعد ضراء مستهم إذا لهم مكر في آياتنا قل الله أسرع مكرا إن رسلنا يكتبون ما تمكرون

translation: It is He who enables you to travel on land and sea until, when you are in ships and they sail with them by a good wind and they rejoice therein, there comes a storm wind and the waves come upon them from everywhere and they assume that they are surrounded, supplicating Allah, sincere to Him in religion, "If You should save us from this, we will surely be among the thankful."
interpretation: This verse reminds us of Allah's power and control over all things, including the forces of nature. It describes a situation where people are enjoying a pleasant journey by ship, feeling safe and secure. However, when a sudden storm arises and the waves engulf them from all sides, they realize their helplessness and turn to Allah in sincere prayer and supplication. They promise that if Allah saves them from this calamity, they will be grateful to Him. This highlights the human tendency to forget Allah during times of ease and prosperity, only remembering Him during hardships and trials. It emphasizes the importance of maintaining a constant connection with Allah and being grateful for His blessings at all times, not just in moments of distress.
orig: هو الذي يسيركم في البر والبحر حتى إذا كنتم في الفلك وجرين بهم بريح طيبة وفرحوا بها جاءتها ريح عاصف وجاءهم الموج من كل مكان وظنوا أنهم أحيط بهم دعوا الله مخلصين له الدين لئن أنجيتنا من هذه لنكونن من الشاكرين

translation: But when He saves them, at once they commit oppression upon the earth without right. O mankind, your oppression is only against yourselves, [being merely] the enjoyment of worldly life. Then to Us is your return, and We will inform you of what you used to do.
interpretation: This verse highlights the ungrateful nature of some people who, after being saved by Allah from hardships, return to their wrongdoings and oppression on earth. It serves as a reminder that such actions only harm one's own soul, as the pleasures gained from worldly life are temporary. Ultimately, everyone will return to Allah and face the consequences of their deeds. The verse emphasizes the importance of being grateful to Allah and refraining from oppression, as one will be held accountable for their actions in the Hereafter.
orig: فلما أنجاهم إذا هم يبغون في الأرض بغير الحق يا أيها الناس إنما بغيكم على أنفسكم متاع الحياة الدنيا ثم إلينا مرجعكم فننبئكم بما كنتم تعملون

translation: The example of [this] worldly life is but like rain which We have sent down from the sky that the plants of the earth absorb - [those] from which men and livestock eat - until, when the earth has taken on its adornment and is beautified and its people suppose that they have capability over it, there comes to it Our command by night or by day, and We make it as a harvest, as if it had not flourished yesterday. Thus do We explain in detail the signs for a people who give thought.
interpretation: This verse is a reminder of the fleeting nature of worldly life. It compares the life of this world to rain that causes plants to grow and flourish, making the earth beautiful and bountiful. People may then assume they have control over their lives and their environment. However, Allah's decree can come at any time, night or day, and suddenly take away all that seemed established, leaving the earth barren as if the abundance never existed. This analogy is meant to encourage reflection on the temporary nature of worldly existence and to turn people's attention towards the eternal life of the Hereafter, which is of far greater significance. It highlights the importance of using our limited time in this life wisely and not being deceived by worldly adornments or a false sense of control.
orig: إنما مثل الحياة الدنيا كماء أنزلناه من السماء فاختلط به نبات الأرض مما يأكل الناس والأنعام حتى إذا أخذت الأرض زخرفها وازينت وظن أهلها أنهم قادرون عليها أتاها أمرنا ليلا أو نهارا فجعلناها حصيدا كأن لم تغن بالأمس كذلك نفصل الآيات لقوم يتفكرون

translation: And Allah invites to the Home of Peace and guides whom He wills to a straight path.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah, in His infinite wisdom and mercy, guides those whom He chooses to the path of righteousness and peace. The "Home of Peace" refers to Paradise, the ultimate abode of tranquility and eternal bliss. The verse also implies that while Allah invites all to this blessed state, He grants His special guidance to those who sincerely seek Him and strive to follow His commandments. It is through Divine guidance that one can stay on the "straight path" - the path of truth, virtue, and submission to Allah's will. This interpretation highlights the importance of seeking Allah's guidance and striving to be among those whom He guides to the eternal home of peace and happiness.
orig: والله يدعو إلى دار السلام ويهدي من يشاء إلى صراط مستقيم

translation: For those who have done good is the best [reward] and extra. No darkness will cover their faces, nor humiliation. Those are companions of Paradise; they will abide therein eternally.
interpretation: This verse promises the ultimate reward for those who do good deeds in this world - Paradise. Allah will grant them the best of rewards and even more. Their faces will be radiant, without any trace of darkness, shame or humiliation. They will be the inhabitants of Paradise, enjoying its blessings forever. This interpretation highlights that doing good in this life leads to the eternal bliss of the Hereafter, which is the greatest success one can attain.
orig: للذين أحسنوا الحسنى وزيادة ولا يرهق وجوههم قتر ولا ذلة أولئك أصحاب الجنة هم فيها خالدون

translation: And those who have earned evil deeds, the recompense of an evil deed is its equivalent, and humiliation will cover them. They will have from Allah no protector. It will be as if their faces are covered with pieces of the night - so dark [are they]. Those are the companions of the Fire; they will abide therein eternally.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the concept of divine justice in Islam. Those who commit evil deeds will face a punishment that is proportional to their actions. They will be humiliated and will find no protection from Allah. The darkness covering their faces symbolizes the severity and hopelessness of their situation. The verse also affirms the existence of Hell, where the evildoers will remain forever as a consequence of their choices and actions in this life. It serves as a warning to humans to be mindful of their deeds and to strive for righteousness.
orig: والذين كسبوا السيئات جزاء سيئة بمثلها وترهقهم ذلة ما لهم من الله من عاصم كأنما أغشيت وجوههم قطعا من الليل مظلما أولئك أصحاب النار هم فيها خالدون

translation: And the Day We will gather them all together, then We will say to those who associated others with Allah, "[Remain in] your place, you and your 'partners.'" Then We will separate them, and their 'partners' will say, "You did not used to worship us,"
interpretation: This verse speaks about the Day of Judgment when Allah will gather all of mankind together. He will then address those who associated partners with Him in worship, telling them to stay in their place along with their alleged partners. Allah will then separate them from their false gods, making it clear that these 'partners' had no power or divinity. The false gods will even testify against their worshippers, declaring that they were not truly worshipped by them. This highlights the futility of polytheism and the grave error of those who ascribe partners to Allah, as their false gods will disown them on the Day of Reckoning.
orig: ويوم نحشرهم جميعا ثم نقول للذين أشركوا مكانكم أنتم وشركاؤكم فزيلنا بينهم وقال شركاؤهم ما كنتم إيانا تعبدون

translation: But sufficient is Allah as a witness between us and you that we were of your worship unaware.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah is the ultimate witness between the believers and the disbelievers. It affirms that the believers were completely unaware and disassociated from the false worship and idolatry practiced by the disbelievers. The believers' focus was solely on worshipping Allah alone, and they had no involvement in or knowledge of the misguided practices of the disbelievers. Allah's testimony is sufficient to establish the truth and distinguish between the two groups, making it clear that the believers were on the right path of monotheism, while the disbelievers were astray in their polytheistic practices.
orig: فكفى بالله شهيدا بيننا وبينكم إن كنا عن عبادتكم لغافلين

translation: There, [on that Day], every soul will be put to trial for what it did previously, and they will be returned to Allah, their master, the Truth, and lost from them is [all] that they used to invent.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the ultimate accountability of every soul before Allah on the Day of Judgment. Each individual will face the consequences of their actions and deeds performed in this worldly life. They will be brought back to Allah, their true Master, and all the false beliefs, idols, or powers they used to associate with Him or invent will be lost and of no avail to them. It serves as a reminder that one should be mindful of their actions and focus on submitting to Allah alone, as He is the only true authority and everything else is merely a deception or distraction from the truth.
orig: هنالك تبلو كل نفس ما أسلفت وردوا إلى الله مولاهم الحق وضل عنهم ما كانوا يفترون

translation: Say, "Who provides for you from the heaven and the earth? Or who controls hearing and sight and who brings the living out of the dead and brings the dead out of the living and who arranges [every] matter?" They will say, "Allah," so say, "Then will you not fear Him?"
interpretation: This verse is a powerful reminder of Allah's sovereignty and control over all aspects of life. It challenges us to reflect on the fact that Allah alone sustains us, grants us our faculties, and governs the cycles of life and death. The verse compels us to acknowledge Allah's supreme authority, as even the disbelievers will admit that it is Allah who does all these things. In light of this realization, we are asked, "Then will you not fear Him?" This question urges us to be mindful of Allah, to revere Him, and to align our actions with His commands, knowing that He alone holds ultimate power and control over our lives and the universe itself.
orig: قل من يرزقكم من السماء والأرض أمن يملك السمع والأبصار ومن يخرج الحي من الميت ويخرج الميت من الحي ومن يدبر الأمر فسيقولون الله فقل أفلا تتقون

translation: Such is Allah, your Lord in truth. So after the truth, what else can there be, save error? How then are you turned away?
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute truth of Allah's existence and His lordship over all creation. It implies that once one recognizes this ultimate truth, anything else that contradicts it or leads away from it can only be misguidance and falsehood. The rhetorical question "How then are you turned away?" is a reminder for people not to be misled by worldly distractions or false beliefs, as doing so would mean turning away from the clear truth of Allah's sovereignty. It encourages believers to stay firmly grounded in their faith and to constantly orient themselves towards Allah, as He is the only source of truth and guidance.
orig: فذلكم الله ربكم الحق فماذا بعد الحق إلا الضلال فأنى تصرفون

translation: Thus the word of your Lord has come into effect upon those who defiantly disobeyed - that they will not believe.
interpretation: This verse indicates that Allah's decree has been established against those who persistently rebel and disobey Him. Due to their continuous transgression and refusal to accept the truth, Allah has sealed their fate, and they will not attain faith. It is a consequence of their own actions and choices that they have been deprived of the opportunity to believe and guided. This verse serves as a warning to those who deliberately persist in their wrongdoings, highlighting the severity of the consequences of their actions in the sight of Allah.
orig: كذلك حقت كلمت ربك على الذين فسقوا أنهم لا يؤمنون

translation: Say, "Is there of your 'partners' any who begins creation and then repeats it?" Say, "Allah begins creation and then repeats it, so how are you deluded?"
interpretation: This verse challenges the idolaters who associate partners with Allah. It asks them if any of their false gods can initiate creation and then bring it back to life after death, emphasizing that this power belongs to Allah alone. The repetition of creation refers to Allah's ability to resurrect the dead on the Day of Judgment. The verse concludes by questioning how the idolaters can be so misled and deluded to attribute such powers to their false deities when it is clear that only Allah possesses the power to create, give life, cause death, and resurrect.
orig: قل هل من شركائكم من يبدأ الخلق ثم يعيده قل الله يبدأ الخلق ثم يعيده فأنى تؤفكون

translation: Say, "Is there of your 'partners' any who guides to the truth?" Say, "Allah guides to the truth. So is He who guides to the truth more worthy to be followed or he who guides not unless he is guided? Then what is [wrong] with you - how do you judge?"
interpretation: This verse challenges the idolaters who ascribe partners to Allah by asking them if any of their false gods can guide to the ultimate truth. It asserts that only Allah is the true guide to the right path. The verse then questions the logic of following those who cannot guide themselves unless they are guided by Allah. It criticizes the flawed judgment of those who choose to follow misguided leaders instead of Allah's guidance. The rhetorical question at the end emphasizes the irrationality of their choice, as if to say, "What is wrong with your reasoning that you would make such a flawed decision?" This verse highlights the importance of following divine guidance over the misguided leadership of those who are themselves astray.
orig: قل هل من شركائكم من يهدي إلى الحق قل الله يهدي للحق أفمن يهدي إلى الحق أحق أن يتبع أمن لا يهدي إلا أن يهدى فما لكم كيف تحكمون

translation: And most of them follow nothing but assumption. Indeed, assumption avails not against the truth at all. Indeed, Allah is Knowing of what they do.
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of seeking truth and knowledge, rather than relying on mere assumptions or conjecture. It emphasizes that assumptions, no matter how widely held, cannot replace or override the truth. The verse also reminds us that Allah is fully aware of all actions and intentions, implying that one should strive to act in accordance with the truth and with sincerity, as nothing escapes His knowledge. It is a call to base one's beliefs, decisions, and actions on sound knowledge and divine guidance, rather than on unfounded speculations or the opinions of the majority.
orig: وما يتبع أكثرهم إلا ظنا إن الظن لا يغني من الحق شيئا إن الله عليم بما يفعلون

translation: And it was not [possible] for this Qur'an to be produced by other than Allah, but [it is] a confirmation of what was before it and a detailed explanation of the [former] Scripture, about which there is no doubt, from the Lord of the worlds.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the divine origin of the Qur'an, asserting that it could not have been fabricated by anyone other than Allah. It serves as a confirmation and detailed explanation of the previous revelations, leaving no room for doubt about its authenticity and its status as a revelation from the Lord of all creation. The Qur'an, therefore, is the ultimate truth and guidance for humanity, as it comes directly from the Creator himself.
orig: وما كان هذا القرآن أن يفترى من دون الله ولكن تصديق الذي بين يديه وتفصيل الكتاب لا ريب فيه من رب العالمين

translation: Or do they say, "He invented it"? Say, "Then bring forth a surah like it and call upon [for assistance] whomever you can besides Allah, if you should be truthful."
interpretation: This verse challenges those who claim that the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) invented the Qur'an himself. It asks them to produce a single chapter like it, seeking help from anyone they wish, besides Allah. This challenge serves to prove the divine origin of the Qur'an, as no one can produce something of its caliber. It also emphasizes the truthfulness of the Prophet and the authenticity of his message, as he could not have created such a masterpiece on his own, without divine inspiration.
orig: أم يقولون افتراه قل فأتوا بسورة مثله وادعوا من استطعتم من دون الله إن كنتم صادقين

translation: But they have denied that which they encompass not in knowledge and whose interpretation has not yet come to them. Thus did those before them deny. Then observe how was the end of the wrongdoers.
interpretation: This verse points to the arrogance and ignorance of those who reject divine revelation without fully understanding it or witnessing its ultimate fulfillment. They are hasty in their denial, similar to past generations who also rejected the truth brought by the prophets. The verse warns that those who wrongfully reject the truth will face severe consequences in the end, just as previous deniers were punished for their arrogance and disbelief. It emphasizes the importance of seeking knowledge, being open-minded, and not rushing to judgment about matters of faith without proper understanding.
orig: بل كذبوا بما لم يحيطوا بعلمه ولما يأتهم تأويله كذلك كذب الذين من قبلهم فانظر كيف كان عاقبة الظالمين

translation: And among them are those who believe in it, and among them are those who do not believe in it. And your Lord is most knowing of the corrupters.
interpretation: This verse highlights the fact that people have different attitudes towards the divine message. Some people readily accept it and believe in it, while others reject it and refuse to believe. Allah is fully aware of those who spread corruption and mischief, and He will hold them accountable for their actions. The verse serves as a reminder that faith is a personal choice, but one that has consequences in the sight of Allah.
orig: ومنهم من يؤمن به ومنهم من لا يؤمن به وربك أعلم بالمفسدين

translation: And if they deny you, say, "For me are my deeds, and for you are your deeds. You are disassociated from what I do, and I am disassociated from what you do."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes individual responsibility and accountability before God. It instructs the Prophet Muhammad, and by extension all believers, to focus on their own actions and not be overly concerned with how others respond to the message of Islam. Each person will be judged according to their own deeds, and no one will bear the burden of another's actions. This verse promotes a mindset of staying true to one's own faith and convictions, while respecting the free will of others to accept or reject the message. It discourages becoming emotionally invested in trying to control or change others, and instead encourages focusing on one's own spiritual growth and righteous conduct.
orig: وإن كذبوك فقل لي عملي ولكم عملكم أنتم بريئون مما أعمل وأنا بريء مما تعملون

translation: And among them are those who listen to you. But can you cause the deaf to hear, even though they will not use reason?
interpretation: This verse is addressing the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him), reminding him that even though there are some people who appear to listen to his message, they are spiritually "deaf" and unable to truly understand or accept it. The rhetorical question highlights the idea that no matter how clear or compelling the message may be, it is ultimately up to the individual to open their heart and mind to the truth. The verse emphasizes the importance of using reason and intellect in matters of faith, suggesting that those who refuse to do so are choosing to remain in a state of spiritual deafness, unable to benefit from the guidance being offered to them.
orig: ومنهم من يستمعون إليك أفأنت تسمع الصم ولو كانوا لا يعقلون

translation: And among them are those who look at you. But can you guide the blind although they will not [attempt to] see?
interpretation: This verse is addressing the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him), reminding him that even though some people may look at him and observe his actions, it is not within his power to guide those who are spiritually blind and unwilling to see the truth.
