The verse emphasizes that true guidance comes from Allah, and that the Prophet's role is to convey the message, not to force people to accept it. It also implies that some people may be so deeply entrenched in their disbelief that they will not accept the truth, even if it is presented to them clearly. Ultimately, it is up to each individual to open their heart and mind to the guidance of Allah.
orig: ومنهم من ينظر إليك أفأنت تهدي العمي ولو كانوا لا يبصرون

translation: Indeed, Allah does not wrong the people at all, but it is the people who are wronging themselves.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the justice and fairness of Allah. It asserts that Allah never wrongs or oppresses people in any way. If people face difficulties, hardships, or suffering in their lives, it is not because Allah is unjust towards them. Rather, it is a result of their own actions, choices, and misdeeds. People wrong themselves by disobeying Allah's commands, indulging in sins, and not following the righteous path. Thus, any misfortune or punishment they face is a consequence of their own doings, not because Allah is ever unjust or unfair in His dealings with His creation.
orig: إن الله لا يظلم الناس شيئا ولكن الناس أنفسهم يظلمون

translation: And the Day when He will gather them, [it will be] as if they had not remained [in the world] but an hour of the day, [and] they will know each other. Those will have lost who denied the meeting with Allah and were not guided.
interpretation: This verse speaks about the Day of Judgment, emphasizing the brevity of worldly life in comparison to the eternal afterlife. It suggests that on that day, people will recognize each other as if they had only been apart for a short while, despite the actual passage of time. The verse also highlights the loss and misfortune of those who denied the inevitability of meeting Allah and failed to follow the right path during their earthly lives. It serves as a reminder for believers to prioritize their spiritual growth and connection with Allah over temporary worldly pursuits, as the ultimate reality will be faced in the hereafter.
orig: ويوم يحشرهم كأن لم يلبثوا إلا ساعة من النهار يتعارفون بينهم قد خسر الذين كذبوا بلقاء الله وما كانوا مهتدين

translation: And whether We show you some of what We promise them, [O Muhammad], or We take you in death, to Us is their return; then, [either way], Allah is a witness concerning what they are doing.
interpretation: This verse serves as a reminder to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and the believers that regardless of whether they witness the punishment of the disbelievers in this world or not, ultimately, all will return to Allah for judgment. It emphasizes that Allah is fully aware of the actions and deeds of every individual, and He will hold them accountable for their choices in the Hereafter. The verse also implies that the Prophet's role is to convey the message, while the ultimate outcome and judgment rest with Allah alone.
orig: وإما نرينك بعض الذي نعدهم أو نتوفينك فإلينا مرجعهم ثم الله شهيد على ما يفعلون

translation: And for every nation is a messenger. So when their messenger comes, it will be judged between them in justice, and they will not be wronged.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the justice and fairness of Allah's judgment. Every nation was sent a messenger to guide them, and on the Day of Judgment, each nation will be judged according to how they responded to their messenger's teachings. The judgment will be entirely just, and no one will be treated unfairly or wronged in any way. This highlights the importance of following the guidance of the messengers sent by Allah and the consequences of rejecting their message. It also serves as a reminder that ultimately, all will be held accountable before Allah for their deeds in this life.
orig: ولكل أمة رسول فإذا جاء رسولهم قضي بينهم بالقسط وهم لا يظلمون

translation: And they say, "When is this promise, if you should be truthful?"
interpretation: This verse is addressing the disbelievers who mockingly ask the Prophet Muhammad and the believers about when the Day of Judgment will come, challenging the truthfulness of their claims. It reflects the skepticism and disbelief of those who reject the concept of resurrection and accountability in the Hereafter. The tone of their question implies doubt and ridicule, as they demand a specific time for the fulfillment of God's promise. This verse highlights the importance of having faith and trust in God's plan, even in the face of skepticism and opposition from non-believers.
orig: ويقولون متى هذا الوعد إن كنتم صادقين

translation: Say, "I hold not for myself [the power of] benefit or harm, except what Allah has willed. For every nation is a [specified] term. When their time has come, then they will not remain behind an hour, nor will they precede [it]."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the complete submission and powerlessness of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) before Allah. It highlights that the Prophet, despite his elevated status, has no control over his own benefit or harm, and that everything happens according to Allah's will. The verse also underscores the concept of divine destiny, stating that every nation has a predetermined lifespan, and when the appointed time arrives, it cannot be delayed or hastened even by a single moment. This serves as a reminder for humans to recognize Allah's supreme power and to submit to His will, understanding that everything in this world is transient and bound by His divine decree.
orig: قل لا أملك لنفسي ضرا ولا نفعا إلا ما شاء الله لكل أمة أجل إذا جاء أجلهم فلا يستأخرون ساعة ولا يستقدمون

translation: Say, "Have you considered: if His punishment should come to you by night or by day, for which [aspect] of it would the criminals be impatient?"
interpretation: This verse is a warning to the disbelievers who mock and challenge the Prophet (ﷺ) to bring Allah's punishment upon them. It asks them to consider whether they would be in such a hurry for the punishment if it were to come upon them suddenly, either by night or by day. The verse implies that the disbelievers are foolish and arrogant to challenge Allah's punishment, as they do not realize the severity and swiftness with which it can befall them. It also highlights their criminal nature, as they are referred to as "the criminals" (al-mujrimoon). The verse serves as a reminder to all people to be mindful of Allah's power and to turn to Him in repentance before it is too late.
orig: قل أرأيتم إن أتاكم عذابه بياتا أو نهارا ماذا يستعجل منه المجرمون

translation: Then, when it occurs, you believe in it? Now? And you were [already] for it impatient?
interpretation: This verse is admonishing those who disbelieved in the Day of Judgment and were impatient for its coming. It points out the irony that when the Day actually arrives, they will then believe in it, but it will be too late. The verse emphasizes the importance of having faith and patience in this life, before facing the realities of the Hereafter when it will be of no benefit to believe. It is a warning against the foolishness of denying the truth until it is too late to benefit from believing in it.
orig: أثم إذا ما وقع آمنتم به آلآن وقد كنتم به تستعجلون

translation: Then it will be said to those who wronged, "Taste the punishment of eternity; are you being recompensed except for what you used to earn?"
interpretation: This verse is a stern warning to the wrongdoers and disbelievers. On the Day of Judgment, they will be addressed and told to taste the everlasting punishment of Hell. This punishment is a direct consequence of their evil deeds and disbelief in the worldly life. The rhetorical question "are you being recompensed except for what you used to earn?" emphasizes the fact that this punishment is a just and fair recompense for their actions. It highlights the principle of individual accountability, as each person will be held responsible for their own deeds. The verse also implies that the punishment is inescapable and eternal, as indicated by the term "the punishment of eternity". This serves as a powerful reminder for people to be mindful of their actions and to strive for righteousness in this life.
orig: ثم قيل للذين ظلموا ذوقوا عذاب الخلد هل تجزون إلا بما كنتم تكسبون

translation: And they ask you, [O Muhammad], "Is it true?" Say, "Yes, by my Lord. Indeed, it is truth; and you will not cause failure [to Allah]."
interpretation: This verse affirms the truthfulness of the Prophet Muhammad's message and the inevitability of Allah's plan. It emphasizes that despite the doubts and questions of the disbelievers, the Prophet's message is undeniably true, as he swears by his Lord. The verse also asserts that no one can escape or prevent the fulfillment of Allah's will and decree. It serves as a reminder to the believers to have unwavering faith in the truth of Islam and to the disbelievers that their rejection will not hinder the realization of Allah's promise.
orig: ويستنبئونك أحق هو قل إي وربي إنه لحق وما أنتم بمعجزين

translation: And if every soul that wronged had everything on earth, it would offer it in ransom. And they will confide regret when they see the punishment; and they will be judged in justice, and they will not be wronged.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the severity and inevitability of God's justice on the Day of Judgment. It suggests that even if the wrongdoers were to offer everything on earth as a ransom to save themselves from the punishment, it would not be accepted. They will feel intense regret upon witnessing the consequences of their actions, but it will be too late. The verse also underscores the fairness of God's judgment, as every soul will be judged equitably and none will be treated unjustly. This serves as a reminder for people to be mindful of their deeds in this world, as they will be held accountable in the Hereafter.
orig: ولو أن لكل نفس ظلمت ما في الأرض لافتدت به وأسروا الندامة لما رأوا العذاب وقضي بينهم بالقسط وهم لا يظلمون

translation: Unquestionably, to Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and the earth. Unquestionably, the promise of Allah is truth, but most of them do not know.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that everything in the universe belongs to Allah alone. It affirms the absolute ownership and authority of Allah over all creation. The verse also asserts that Allah's promise is true and will certainly come to pass, even though most people do not recognize or acknowledge this reality. It suggests that many are heedless of Allah's sovereignty and the inevitability of His decree, failing to grasp the deeper spiritual truths. The verse serves as a reminder for believers to have faith in Allah's words and to trust in His promise, even if others remain ignorant or doubtful.
orig: ألا إن لله ما في السماوات والأرض ألا إن وعد الله حق ولكن أكثرهم لا يعلمون

translation: It is He who gives life and causes death, and to Him you will be returned.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute power and authority of Allah over life and death. It reminds us that Allah is the One who grants life and takes it away, and that all of humanity will ultimately return to Him for judgment in the Hereafter. This realization should inspire us to live our lives in accordance with Allah's guidance, seeking His pleasure and preparing for our inevitable return to Him. It also serves as a comfort in times of loss, knowing that death is not the end, but rather a transition to the eternal life that awaits the believers in Paradise.
orig: هو يحيي ويميت وإليه ترجعون

translation: O mankind, there has come to you instruction from your Lord and healing for what is in the breasts and guidance and mercy for the believers.
interpretation: This verse is a reminder that the Qur'an serves as a source of guidance, healing, and mercy for those who believe in its message. The "instruction" refers to the teachings and wisdom contained within the Qur'an, which provide a framework for living a righteous life. The "healing for what is in the breasts" suggests that the Qur'an offers spiritual and emotional comfort, helping to alleviate the doubts, fears, and anxieties that reside within the hearts of individuals. Moreover, the Qur'an is described as a source of "guidance" and "mercy," indicating that it directs believers towards the path of truth and compassion. This verse emphasizes the all-encompassing nature of the Qur'an and its ability to address the various needs of the human soul, ultimately leading to a more fulfilling and purposeful existence for those who embrace its teachings.
orig: يا أيها الناس قد جاءتكم موعظة من ربكم وشفاء لما في الصدور وهدى ورحمة للمؤمنين

translation: Say, "In the bounty of Allah and in His mercy - in that let them rejoice; it is better than what they accumulate."
interpretation: This verse reminds us that true happiness and contentment come from recognizing and appreciating the blessings and mercy that Allah has bestowed upon us. The bounties and mercy of Allah are far superior to any worldly possessions or wealth that people may accumulate. It encourages believers to find joy and satisfaction in their faith and in the favors that Allah has granted them, rather than being preoccupied with material gains. This mindset helps us maintain a healthy perspective on life and prioritize our spiritual well-being over temporary worldly pursuits.
orig: قل بفضل الله وبرحمته فبذلك فليفرحوا هو خير مما يجمعون

translation: Say, "Have you seen what Allah has sent down to you of provision of which you have made [some] lawful and [some] unlawful?" Say, "Has Allah permitted you [to do so], or do you invent [something] about Allah?"
interpretation: This verse is questioning the authority of those who declare certain provisions as lawful or unlawful without the permission of Allah. It emphasizes that it is Allah alone who has the right to determine what is permissible and what is prohibited. The verse implies that those who make such declarations without divine authority are essentially attributing false rulings to Allah and inventing lies about Him. It serves as a reminder that humans should not overstep their boundaries and should submit to the laws and guidance provided by Allah.
orig: قل أرأيتم ما أنزل الله لكم من رزق فجعلتم منه حراما وحلالا قل آلله أذن لكم أم على الله تفترون

translation: And what will be the supposition of those who invent falsehood against Allah on the Day of Resurrection? Indeed, Allah is full of bounty to the people, but most of them are not grateful.
interpretation: This verse warns of the severe consequences that await those who attribute lies to Allah and make false claims about Him. On the Day of Judgment, they will face the reality of their actions and the gravity of their sin. Despite Allah's abundant blessings and favors upon mankind, many people are ungrateful and fail to acknowledge His generosity. Instead of being thankful, they fabricate lies against Him. This verse emphasizes the importance of being truthful about Allah and appreciating His countless bounties, while also serving as a stern warning against inventing falsehoods about Him.
orig: وما ظن الذين يفترون على الله الكذب يوم القيامة إن الله لذو فضل على الناس ولكن أكثرهم لا يشكرون

translation: And, [O Muhammad], you are not [engaged] in any matter or recite any of the Qur'an and you [people] do not do any deed except that We are witness over you when you are involved in it. And not absent from your Lord is any [part] of an atom's weight within the earth or within the heaven or [anything] smaller than that or greater but that it is in a clear register.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the omniscience and omnipresence of Allah. It states that Allah is aware of every action and deed performed by human beings, no matter how small or insignificant it may seem. The verse also highlights the concept of divine record-keeping, suggesting that all deeds are meticulously noted in a "clear register." This interpretation underscores the importance of being mindful of one's actions, as nothing escapes Allah's knowledge and every deed will be accounted for. It serves as a reminder for believers to strive for righteousness and refrain from wrongdoing, knowing that Allah is always watching and will hold them accountable for their actions.
orig: وما تكون في شأن وما تتلو منه من قرآن ولا تعملون من عمل إلا كنا عليكم شهودا إذ تفيضون فيه وما يعزب عن ربك من مثقال ذرة في الأرض ولا في السماء ولا أصغر من ذلك ولا أكبر إلا في كتاب مبين

translation: Behold! Verily, on the friends of Allah there is no fear, nor shall they grieve.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that those who are close to Allah and have earned His favor and protection need not fear anything in this world or the Hereafter. They will be protected from harm and will not experience the sorrow or grief that afflicts others. This is because they have put their trust in Allah and have lived their lives according to His guidance. The verse serves as a reassurance to the believers that if they strive to be among the "friends of Allah", they will be granted a special status of peace, security, and contentment in both this life and the next.
orig: ألا إن أولياء الله لا خوف عليهم ولا هم يحزنون

translation: Those who have believed and were fearing Allah
interpretation: This verse refers to the righteous believers who have faith in Allah and strive to obey His commands and avoid His prohibitions. "Taqwa" or "fearing Allah" means being conscious of Allah, having reverence for Him, and being mindful of one's actions and their consequences in the Hereafter. These individuals prioritize their relationship with Allah and adhere to the teachings of Islam in their daily lives. As a result of their faith and righteousness, they will be rewarded with Paradise in the afterlife. The verse emphasizes the importance of having a strong belief in Allah coupled with righteous deeds and God-consciousness.
orig: الذين آمنوا وكانوا يتقون

translation: For them are good tidings in the worldly life and in the Hereafter. No change is there in the words of Allah. That is what is the great attainment.
interpretation: This verse conveys a message of hope and reassurance to the believers. It promises them glad tidings not only in this worldly life but also in the life to come. The "good tidings" could refer to various blessings, such as inner peace, contentment, and the promise of Paradise. The verse emphasizes that Allah's words and promises are unchangeable and certain. This immutability of divine decree is a source of comfort for the faithful, as they can rely on Allah's promises with complete certainty. The verse concludes by stating that attaining these glad tidings and the fulfillment of Allah's unchanging words is the supreme triumph and success. It suggests that true victory lies in earning Allah's pleasure and being recipients of His eternal blessings, rather than in any temporary worldly gains.
orig: لهم البشرى في الحياة الدنيا وفي الآخرة لا تبديل لكلمات الله ذلك هو الفوز العظيم

translation: And let not their speech grieve you. Indeed, honor [due to power] belongs to Allah entirely. He is the Hearing, the Knowing.
interpretation: This verse is a reminder that true power and honor belong to Allah alone. The Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) should not be saddened or affected by the hurtful words or actions of the disbelievers, as their opinions hold no real weight. Allah is All-Hearing and All-Knowing, aware of everything that is said and done. The believers should find comfort and strength in the fact that Allah is the ultimate authority and that He will support and honor those who are steadfast in their faith.
orig: ولا يحزنك قولهم إن العزة لله جميعا هو السميع العليم

translation: Unquestionably, to Allah belongs whoever is in the heavens and whoever is on the earth. And those who invoke other than Allah do not [actually] follow [His] "partners." They follow not except assumption, and they are not but falsifying.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute sovereignty and ownership of Allah over all of His creation. It also points out the folly of those who associate partners with Allah or worship others besides Him. These people are not following any real entities, but rather their own baseless assumptions and conjecture. They are merely engaging in falsehood by attributing divinity to anything other than Allah. The verse affirms the pure monotheistic message of Islam and rejects all forms of polytheism or idolatry.
orig: ألا إن لله من في السماوات ومن في الأرض وما يتبع الذين يدعون من دون الله شركاء إن يتبعون إلا الظن وإن هم إلا يخرصون

translation: It is He who made for you the night to rest therein and the day giving sight. Indeed in that are signs for a people who listen.
interpretation: This verse highlights Allah's wisdom and power in creating the alternation of night and day. The night is a time for rest and tranquility, allowing humans and other creatures to recharge and find peace. The day, with its light, enables people to see clearly and go about their daily activities. These natural phenomena are not mere coincidences but rather signs of Allah's existence, creativity, and mercy. The verse emphasizes that these signs are apparent to those who listen attentively and reflect upon the world around them, using their senses and intellect to recognize the truth of Allah's message and the perfection of His creation.
orig: هو الذي جعل لكم الليل لتسكنوا فيه والنهار مبصرا إن في ذلك لآيات لقوم يسمعون

translation: They say, "Allah has taken a son." Exalted is He! He is the [one] Free of need. To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is in the earth. You have no authority for this [claim]. Do you say about Allah that which you do not know?
interpretation: This verse refutes the false claim that Allah has taken a son. It emphasizes Allah's self-sufficiency and absolute ownership of everything in the heavens and earth. The verse challenges those who make this baseless assertion, pointing out that they have no evidence or authority to support their claim. It admonishes them for attributing something to Allah without knowledge, which is a grave sin. The verse affirms the fundamental Islamic belief in the oneness and uniqueness of Allah, rejecting any notion of Him having offspring or partners.
orig: قالوا اتخذ الله ولدا سبحانه هو الغني له ما في السماوات وما في الأرض إن عندكم من سلطان بهذا أتقولون على الله ما لا تعلمون

translation: Say, "Indeed, those who invent falsehood about Allah will not succeed."
interpretation: This verse serves as a stern warning to those who attribute lies to Allah or fabricate falsehoods about His religion. It emphasizes that such individuals will never attain true success or prosperity, neither in this world nor in the Hereafter. Inventing lies about Allah is a grave sin that leads to misguidance and ultimately, failure and loss. The verse encourages believers to always speak the truth about Allah and His teachings, and to refrain from spreading misinformation or false beliefs, as doing so will only lead to their own detriment and deprive them of Allah's blessings and mercy.
orig: قل إن الذين يفترون على الله الكذب لا يفلحون

translation: Enjoyment in this world, then to Us will be their return, then We will make them taste the severe punishment because they used to disbelieve.
interpretation: This verse warns that the pleasures and enjoyments of this worldly life are temporary and fleeting. Eventually, all people will return to Allah (God) after their death. Those who disbelieved in Allah and rejected His messages will taste the severe punishment of Hell in the Hereafter as a consequence of their disbelief. It emphasizes that the ultimate return is to Allah and that people will be held accountable for their faith and actions in this world.
orig: متاع في الدنيا ثم إلينا مرجعهم ثم نذيقهم العذاب الشديد بما كانوا يكفرون

translation: And recite to them the news of Noah, when he said to his people, "O my people, if my residence and my reminding of the signs of Allah has become burdensome upon you - then I have relied upon Allah. So resolve upon your plan and [call upon] your associates. Then let not your plan be obscure to you. Then carry it out upon me and do not give me respite.
interpretation: This verse is a reminder to the believers to stay steadfast in their faith and trust in Allah, even in the face of opposition and difficulty. Noah faced great challenges and hardships in conveying the message of Allah to his people, who were stubborn and resistant. Despite this, he remained patient and put his trust completely in Allah, knowing that ultimately, the truth would prevail. The verse encourages us to do the same - to have faith in Allah's plan and to persevere in doing what is right, even when it is difficult or unpopular. It also serves as a warning to those who oppose the message of Islam, that their plans and plots will ultimately fail, and they will have to face the consequences of their actions in this life and the next.
orig: واتل عليهم نبأ نوح إذ قال لقومه يا قوم إن كان كبر عليكم مقامي وتذكيري بآيات الله فعلى الله توكلت فأجمعوا أمركم وشركاءكم ثم لا يكن أمركم عليكم غمة ثم اقضوا إلي ولا تنظرون

translation: But if you turn away, then I have not asked you for any reward. My reward is only from Allah, and I am commanded to be of the Muslims.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) did not seek any worldly gain or reward for conveying the message of Islam. His sole purpose was to fulfill the command of Allah and submit to His will. It also implies that even if people reject the message, it does not affect the Prophet's mission or reward, as he is content with whatever Allah has decreed for him. The verse encourages the Prophet to remain steadfast in his faith and continue to be among those who submit to Allah, regardless of people's response to his message.
orig: فإن توليتم فما سألتكم من أجر إن أجري إلا على الله وأمرت أن أكون من المسلمين

translation: But they denied him, so We saved him and those with him in the ship and made them successors, and We drowned those who denied Our signs. Then see how was the end of those who were warned.
interpretation: This verse highlights the consequences of denying Allah's messages and His prophets. Those who reject the truth will face destruction, while the believers who follow the guidance will be saved and granted power and authority in the land. It serves as a warning to those who oppose the divine message, emphasizing that their end will be one of loss and regret. The verse also reassures the believers that Allah will support and protect them, even in the face of adversity and opposition.
orig: فكذبوه فنجيناه ومن معه في الفلك وجعلناهم خلائف وأغرقنا الذين كذبوا بآياتنا فانظر كيف كان عاقبة المنذرين

translation: Then We sent after him messengers to their peoples, and they came to them with clear proofs. But they were not to believe in that which they had denied before. Thus We seal the hearts of the transgressors.
interpretation: This verse highlights the pattern of people rejecting the clear signs and messages brought by the prophets sent to them, due to their arrogance and transgression. It suggests that once someone has chosen to deny the truth, it becomes increasingly difficult for them to accept it later, as their hearts become sealed and hardened against it. This is a consequence of their own actions and choices, and a manifestation of Allah's justice in dealing with those who persistently reject His guidance despite receiving clear proofs and warnings.
orig: ثم بعثنا من بعده رسلا إلى قومهم فجاءوهم بالبينات فما كانوا ليؤمنوا بما كذبوا به من قبل كذلك نطبع على قلوب المعتدين

translation: Then We sent after them Moses and Aaron to Pharaoh and his establishment with Our signs, but they behaved arrogantly and were a criminal people.
interpretation: This verse highlights the arrogance and criminal nature of Pharaoh and his people, who rejected the clear signs and miracles brought to them by Moses and Aaron. Despite being shown undeniable proofs of God's power and the truth of the prophets' message, they persisted in their disbelief and oppression. This demonstrates the depths of their corruption and the justness of the divine punishment that would befall them for their actions. The verse serves as a warning to those who would similarly reject God's messages and prophets out of pride and wickedness.
orig: ثم بعثنا من بعدهم موسى وهارون إلى فرعون وملئه بآياتنا فاستكبروا وكانوا قوما مجرمين

translation: But when the truth came to them from Us, they said, "Indeed, this is obvious magic."
interpretation: This verse highlights the stubborn nature of those who reject the truth even when it is presented to them clearly. Despite the Qur'an being a revelation from Allah, containing guidance and wisdom, the disbelievers dismiss it as mere magic. They refuse to acknowledge its divine origin and the profound message it conveys. This interpretation emphasizes the arrogance and close-mindedness of those who are confronted with the truth but choose to deny it, attributing it to something as baseless as magic rather than accepting it as a sign of Allah's guidance and mercy.
orig: فلما جاءهم الحق من عندنا قالوا إن هذا لسحر مبين

translation: Moses said, "Do you say [what you say] about the truth when it has come to you? Is this magic? But magicians will not succeed."
interpretation: This verse is a response from Moses to those who accused him of practicing magic when he presented them with the truth and clear signs from God. Moses is questioning their denial of the truth, asking how they can attribute it to magic when it is clearly not so. He asserts that what he has brought is indeed the truth from God, not mere magic or trickery. Furthermore, he states a fundamental principle - that magicians and practitioners of falsehood will never attain true success, implying that the truth will ultimately prevail. The verse highlights the importance of recognizing and accepting the truth when it is presented, rather than stubbornly denying it due to preconceived notions or prejudices.
orig: قال موسى أتقولون للحق لما جاءكم أسحر هذا ولا يفلح الساحرون

translation: They said, "Have you come to us to turn us away from that upon which we found our fathers and so that you two may have grandeur in the land? And we are not believers in you."
interpretation: This verse reflects the stubborn attitude of those who reject the message of Allah's prophets. They accuse the prophets of trying to lead them astray from the traditions and beliefs of their ancestors, suggesting that the prophets are motivated by a desire for power and status. They make it clear that they have no intention of believing in the prophets or their message, as they are content with following the ways of their forefathers, even if those ways are misguided. This highlights the importance of using reason and revelation to determine truth, rather than blindly adhering to inherited traditions.
orig: قالوا أجئتنا لتلفتنا عما وجدنا عليه آباءنا وتكون لكما الكبرياء في الأرض وما نحن لكما بمؤمنين

translation: And Pharaoh said, "Bring to me every learned magician."
interpretation: This verse shows the arrogance and disbelief of Pharaoh. When confronted with the miracles of Moses, instead of acknowledging the power of God, Pharaoh sought to challenge Moses by summoning the best magicians in the land. He believed that human magic could match or surpass divine miracles. This highlights Pharaoh's complete lack of faith and his reliance on worldly power and knowledge rather than submitting to the signs and guidance of God. It is a reminder for us to humble ourselves before the might of the Creator and not be deluded by our own abilities or status.
orig: وقال فرعون ائتوني بكل ساحر عليم

translation: So when the magicians came, Moses said to them, "Throw down whatever you will throw."
interpretation: This verse is part of the story of Moses and his encounter with the magicians of Pharaoh's court. When the magicians arrived to challenge Moses, he confidently told them to present whatever tricks or illusions they had prepared. This shows Moses' unwavering faith in God and his mission, as he was not intimidated by the magicians' skills or reputation. It also demonstrates his trust that the truth and power of God would prevail over any deception or false display of power. The verse highlights the contrast between genuine divine miracles and mere illusions created by human trickery.
orig: فلما جاء السحرة قال لهم موسى ألقوا ما أنتم ملقون

translation: So when they had cast, Moses said, "What you have brought is [only] magic. Indeed, Allah will expose its worthlessness. Indeed, Allah does not amend the work of corrupters."
interpretation: This verse highlights the confrontation between Moses and the magicians of Pharaoh's court. When the magicians cast their spells, Moses recognized it as mere magic and expressed his faith that Allah would reveal the truth and nullify their deception. The verse emphasizes that Allah does not support or improve the actions of those who spread corruption and falsehood. It serves as a reminder that ultimately, truth will prevail over illusions and deceptions, and that those who engage in such practices will face the consequences of their actions in the eyes of Allah.
orig: فلما ألقوا قال موسى ما جئتم به السحر إن الله سيبطله إن الله لا يصلح عمل المفسدين

translation: And Allah will establish the truth by His words, even if the criminals dislike it.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the ultimate triumph of truth and justice, as decreed by Allah, regardless of the opposition or disapproval of those who commit wrongdoings. It serves as a reminder that the will of Allah shall prevail, and that the truth will always come to light, no matter how much the wrongdoers attempt to suppress or deny it. This verse encourages believers to remain steadfast in their faith and trust in Allah's plan, knowing that His words and decrees will ultimately establish the truth, even in the face of adversity or resistance from those who oppose it.
orig: ويحق الله الحق بكلماته ولو كره المجرمون

translation: But none believed in Moses except [some] youths among his people, for fear of Pharaoh and his establishment that they would persecute them. And indeed, Pharaoh was haughty within the land, and indeed, he was of the transgressors.
interpretation: This verse highlights the immense pressure and intimidation that Pharaoh and his elite exerted over the people, to the extent that only a small group of young people from among the Israelites had the courage to believe in Moses and his message, despite the risk of persecution. It also emphasizes Pharaoh's arrogance, tyranny and transgression, as he considered himself superior to others and acted oppressively towards his subjects. The verse serves as a reminder that true faith often requires courage and perseverance in the face of oppression and adversity, and that those who transgress the bounds set by Allah will ultimately face the consequences of their actions.
orig: فما آمن لموسى إلا ذرية من قومه على خوف من فرعون وملئهم أن يفتنهم وإن فرعون لعال في الأرض وإنه لمن المسرفين

translation: And Moses said, "O my people, if you have believed in Allah, then rely upon Him, if you should be Muslims."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of complete trust and reliance on Allah for those who truly believe. Moses is urging his people, if they sincerely believe in Allah, to place their full trust in Him and surrender their affairs to His will. This is a key aspect of being a true Muslim - having unwavering faith and confidence in Allah's plan, wisdom, and support, especially during times of hardship or uncertainty. By putting one's trust in Allah, a believer demonstrates submission, humility, and faith, acknowledging that Allah is the ultimate source of strength, guidance, and success in all matters of life.
orig: وقال موسى يا قوم إن كنتم آمنتم بالله فعليه توكلوا إن كنتم مسلمين

translation: They said, "Upon Allah we rely. Our Lord, make us not [objects of] trial for the wrongdoing people."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of placing one's trust in Allah and seeking His protection from being subjected to the trials and temptations caused by the wrongdoers. It highlights the believers' reliance on Allah's guidance and support in the face of adversity and oppression. By supplicating to Allah, they seek to remain steadfast in their faith and avoid falling into the traps set by those who engage in wrongdoing and injustice. This verse encourages the believers to turn to Allah for strength and to have faith in His divine plan, even in the midst of difficult circumstances.
orig: فقالوا على الله توكلنا ربنا لا تجعلنا فتنة للقوم الظالمين

translation: And save us by Your mercy from the disbelieving people.
interpretation: This verse is a prayer and supplication to Allah, seeking His mercy and protection from those who reject faith and disbelieve in Him. It acknowledges that only through Allah's mercy and grace can one be saved from the ways and influence of the disbelievers. The verse implies that the believers should seek refuge in Allah and pray for His guidance to stay on the right path, away from the company and actions of those who deny the truth of Islam. It is a reminder to the faithful to always turn to Allah for help and salvation, especially in the face of opposition or challenges from those who do not believe.
orig: ونجنا برحمتك من القوم الكافرين

translation: And We inspired to Moses and his brother, "Settle your people in Egypt in houses and make your houses [facing the] qiblah and establish prayer and give good tidings to the believers."
interpretation: This verse is a divine command to Moses and his brother Aaron to settle the Children of Israel in Egypt and to establish places of worship facing towards the qiblah (the direction of prayer). It also instructs them to be steadfast in prayer and to give glad tidings to the believers. This verse highlights the importance of having a designated place of worship, maintaining regular prayer, and keeping faith in God's plan and promises, even in the face of hardship and opposition. It serves as a reminder to the believers to remain hopeful and to trust in God's guidance and support.
orig: وأوحينا إلى موسى وأخيه أن تبوآ لقومكما بمصر بيوتا واجعلوا بيوتكم قبلة وأقيموا الصلاة وبشر المؤمنين

translation: And Moses said, "Our Lord, indeed You have given Pharaoh and his establishment splendor and wealth in the worldly life, our Lord, that they may lead [men] astray from Your way. Our Lord, obliterate their wealth and harden their hearts so that they will not believe until they see the painful punishment."
interpretation: This verse highlights Moses' prayer to Allah regarding Pharaoh and his people. Moses acknowledges that Allah has bestowed upon Pharaoh and his elite wealth and adornments in this worldly life. However, he fears that they may use these blessings to mislead others from the path of Allah. Moses then beseeches Allah to destroy their wealth and harden their hearts so that they may not believe until they face the severe punishment in the Hereafter. This interpretation emphasizes the potential misuse of worldly blessings and the consequences of leading others astray from the truth.
orig: وقال موسى ربنا إنك آتيت فرعون وملأه زينة وأموالا في الحياة الدنيا ربنا ليضلوا عن سبيلك ربنا اطمس على أموالهم واشدد على قلوبهم فلا يؤمنوا حتى يروا العذاب الأليم

translation: He said, "Your invocation has been answered; so remain on a right course and do not follow the way of those who do not know [the truth]."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of staying steadfast on the right path after receiving guidance from Allah. It warns against following those who are ignorant or misguided, as their way leads to misguidance and straying from the truth. The verse encourages the believers to remain committed to their faith, to act upon the knowledge they have been given, and to trust in Allah's guidance. It also highlights the significance of seeking knowledge and understanding, as opposed to blindly following others without discernment.
orig: قال قد أجيبت دعوتكما فاستقيما ولا تتبعان سبيل الذين لا يعلمون

translation: And We took the Children of Israel across the sea, and Pharaoh and his soldiers pursued them in tyranny and enmity until, when drowning overtook him, he said, "I believe that there is no deity except that in whom the Children of Israel believe, and I am of the Muslims."
interpretation: This verse highlights the arrogance and stubbornness of Pharaoh, who refused to believe in Allah despite witnessing numerous miracles. It was only when he was on the brink of death, drowning in the sea, that he finally declared his belief in the God of the Children of Israel. However, his belated declaration of faith was not accepted, as it was driven by the fear of imminent death rather than a sincere change of heart. The verse emphasizes that true faith and submission to Allah should be embraced wholeheartedly during one's lifetime, not merely as a last resort when faced with the consequences of one's actions.
orig: وجاوزنا ببني إسرائيل البحر فأتبعهم فرعون وجنوده بغيا وعدوا حتى إذا أدركه الغرق قال آمنت أنه لا إله إلا الذي آمنت به بنو إسرائيل وأنا من المسلمين

translation: "But you had disobeyed [Him] before and were of the corrupters."
interpretation: This verse is addressing someone who had previously disobeyed Allah and was among those who spread corruption on earth. It implies that this person's current situation or punishment is a consequence of their past disobedience and misdeeds. The verse serves as a reminder that our actions have consequences and that we will be held accountable for the choices we make in this life. It also highlights the importance of seeking forgiveness, repenting, and striving to be among the righteous rather than the corrupters.
orig: آلآن وقد عصيت قبل وكنت من المفسدين

translation: So today We will save you in body that you may be to those who succeed you a sign. And indeed, many among the people, of Our signs, are heedless.
interpretation: This verse is referring to the story of Pharaoh, who was drowned in the sea as a punishment for his arrogance and defiance of Allah's message. Allah is telling Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) that He saved Pharaoh's body as a sign and a lesson for future generations, so that they may reflect upon the consequences of rejecting faith and opposing the truth. However, the verse also points out that despite such clear signs, many people remain heedless and fail to recognize the truth of Allah's message. It serves as a reminder for believers to be mindful of Allah's signs and to learn from the lessons of history.
orig: فاليوم ننجيك ببدنك لتكون لمن خلفك آية وإن كثيرا من الناس عن آياتنا لغافلون

translation: And We had certainly settled the Children of Israel in an agreeable settlement and provided them with good things. And they did not differ until [after] knowledge had come to them. Indeed, your Lord will judge between them on the Day of Resurrection concerning that over which they used to differ.
interpretation: This verse highlights the favors bestowed upon the Children of Israel by Allah. They were given a good and secure place to live and were provided with lawful and pure provisions. However, despite these blessings, they fell into disputes and differences after receiving divine knowledge. The interpretation emphasizes that on the Day of Judgment, Allah will judge between them regarding the matters they differed over, indicating that differences arising after attaining knowledge are not justified and will be accounted for in the Hereafter. It serves as a reminder for people to strive for unity and avoid disputes, especially when guided by divine knowledge.
orig: ولقد بوأنا بني إسرائيل مبوأ صدق ورزقناهم من الطيبات فما اختلفوا حتى جاءهم العلم إن ربك يقضي بينهم يوم القيامة فيما كانوا فيه يختلفون

translation: So if you are in doubt, [O Muhammad], about that which We have revealed to you, then ask those who have been reading the Scripture before you. The truth has certainly come to you from your Lord, so never be among the doubters.
interpretation: This verse is addressing Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him), telling him that if he has any doubts about the revelation he has received, he should ask the people who have been reading the scriptures before him, such as the Jews and Christians. This is because the message that Muhammad received confirms the previous revelations. The verse emphasizes that the truth has indeed come to him from Allah, and he should never be among those who doubt it. This highlights the continuity and consistency of the divine message across different prophets and scriptures.
orig: فإن كنت في شك مما أنزلنا إليك فاسأل الذين يقرءون الكتاب من قبلك لقد جاءك الحق من ربك فلا تكونن من الممترين

translation: And be not of those who reject the signs of Allah, lest you be among the losers.
interpretation: This verse is a stern warning against rejecting the signs and revelations of Allah. Those who deny the truth of Allah's messages and persist in disbelief are ultimately doomed to loss and failure, both in this world and the Hereafter. The verse emphasizes the grave consequences of such rejection and urges the believers to steer clear of this path. It serves as a reminder to have faith, accept the divine guidance, and follow the right way to avoid being among the losers who will face the wrath of Allah and be deprived of His mercy and blessings.
orig: ولا تكونن من الذين كذبوا بآيات الله فتكون من الخاسرين

translation: Indeed, those upon whom the word of your Lord has come into effect will not believe.
interpretation: This verse suggests that there are some individuals who are so deeply entrenched in their disbelief and rejection of faith that even clear signs and guidance from Allah will not lead them to believe. It implies that Allah, in His infinite wisdom and knowledge, knows that the hearts of these people are sealed and that no amount of preaching or proofs will sway them. Their fate of remaining in disbelief has already been decreed. This highlights the concept of divine predestination - that Allah knows the ultimate outcome and destination of each soul even if humans have free will to choose their path. The verse serves as a reminder that while we should strive to guide others to faith, ultimately hidayah (guidance) comes from Allah alone, and some hearts will remain closed to belief.
orig: إن الذين حقت عليهم كلمت ربك لا يؤمنون

translation: Even if every sign should come to them, until they see the painful punishment.
interpretation: This verse suggests that even if the disbelievers were presented with every possible sign or evidence of the truth of Islam, they would still not believe until they face the severe punishment of Allah in the Hereafter. It implies that their hearts have become so hardened and their minds so closed that no amount of proof or warning would convince them to accept faith. They are stubborn in their disbelief and will only realize the gravity of their error when it is too late and they are faced with the painful consequences of their rejection of God's message. The verse highlights the depth of their denial and the inevitability of divine justice.
orig: ولو جاءتهم كل آية حتى يروا العذاب الأليم

translation: Then has there not been a [single] city that believed so its faith benefited it except the people of Jonah? When they believed, We removed from them the punishment of disgrace in worldly life and gave them enjoyment for a time.
interpretation: This verse highlights the exceptional case of the people of Jonah (Yunus) who, unlike other nations, believed in God's message when it was conveyed to them by their prophet. As a result, God spared them from the punishment that befell other disbelieving nations in this worldly life. This serves as an example of God's mercy towards those who sincerely repent and embrace faith, showing that it is never too late to turn to God and that His forgiveness is always accessible to those who seek it. The verse also implies that the ultimate judgment and eternal punishment or reward will be in the Hereafter, while in this life, God may grant respite and enjoyment even to those who disbelieve, until a predetermined time.
orig: فلولا كانت قرية آمنت فنفعها إيمانها إلا قوم يونس لما آمنوا كشفنا عنهم عذاب الخزي في الحياة الدنيا ومتعناهم إلى حين

translation: And if your Lord had willed, all those on earth would have believed entirely. Would you then compel the people to become believers?
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the concept of free will in Islam. It states that if Allah had willed, He could have made everyone on earth believe in Him. However, He has given humans the choice to believe or not to believe. The verse also questions the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him), asking if he would compel people to become believers against their will. This implies that forced conversion is not acceptable in Islam, and that people must come to faith through their own free choice and conviction. The verse highlights the importance of respecting individual autonomy and the right to choose one's beliefs, while also acknowledging Allah's ultimate power and control over all things.
orig: ولو شاء ربك لآمن من في الأرض كلهم جميعا أفأنت تكره الناس حتى يكونوا مؤمنين

translation: And no soul can believe except by permission of Allah, and He will place defilement upon those who will not use reason.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that true faith and belief in Allah can only come about through His divine permission and guidance. It is not something that a person can attain solely through their own efforts or will. At the same time, Allah places "defilement" or impurity upon those who refuse to use their intellect and reasoning to recognize the truth of His message. They choose to remain ignorant and reject faith, so Allah leaves them in their state of spiritual uncleanliness. The verse implies that Allah guides to faith those who sincerely seek Him and strive to use the intelligence He has blessed them with to understand His signs. But those who arrogantly turn away, Allah abandons to their own impurity and lack of guidance.
orig: وما كان لنفس أن تؤمن إلا بإذن الله ويجعل الرجس على الذين لا يعقلون

translation: Say, "Observe what is in the heavens and earth." But of no avail will be signs or warners to a people who do not believe.
interpretation: This verse is a call to reflect upon the signs of Allah's creation in the universe. It encourages people to ponder over the wonders of the heavens and the earth, which serve as clear evidence of Allah's existence, power, and wisdom. However, it also acknowledges that no matter how many signs or warnings are given, they will not benefit those who have chosen to disbelieve. The verse implies that true faith comes from within, and that those who have closed their hearts to the truth will not be swayed by external evidence alone. It is a reminder that guidance ultimately comes from Allah, and that the role of the Prophet is to convey the message, while the choice to believe or not rests with each individual.
orig: قل انظروا ماذا في السماوات والأرض وما تغني الآيات والنذر عن قوم لا يؤمنون

translation: Then do they wait except for like the days of those who passed away before them? Say, "Then wait; indeed I am with you among those who wait."
interpretation: This verse is a warning to the disbelievers who reject the message of Islam. It reminds them of the fate of previous nations who also rejected the truth and were subsequently destroyed by Allah's punishment. The Prophet Muhammad is instructed to tell them to wait and see, for he too is waiting along with the believers for Allah's judgment to come to pass. The verse implies that the disbelievers will face a similar destruction as those before them if they do not heed the warning and embrace the truth of Islam. It is a call to reflect on the lessons of history and to submit to Allah before it is too late.
orig: فهل ينتظرون إلا مثل أيام الذين خلوا من قبلهم قل فانتظروا إني معكم من المنتظرين

translation: Then We will save Our messengers and those who have believed. Thus, it is an obligation upon Us that We save the believers.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's promise to protect and save His messengers and the believers who follow them. It highlights the divine responsibility and commitment to ensure the ultimate success and salvation of those who have faith in Him and His messengers. The verse serves as a reassurance to the believers that, despite the challenges and trials they may face in this world, Allah will ultimately grant them victory and deliver them from harm in the Hereafter. It also underscores the importance of having faith and remaining steadfast in one's belief, as it is through this that one attains Allah's protection and mercy.
orig: ثم ننجي رسلنا والذين آمنوا كذلك حقا علينا ننج المؤمنين

translation: Say, "O people, if you are in doubt as to my religion, then [know that] I do not worship what you worship besides Allah, but I worship Allah who causes your death. And I have been commanded to be of the believers."
interpretation: This verse is a clear declaration of the Prophet's unwavering faith in Allah alone and his rejection of the false deities worshipped by the polytheists. It serves as a reminder to all people that if they have doubts about the truth of Islam, they should know that the Prophet does not worship anyone besides Allah, the One who has the power over life and death. The verse also emphasizes the importance of being among the believers, those who submit to Allah and follow His guidance. It is a powerful message of Tawheed (monotheism) and a call to abandon the worship of false gods and embrace the worship of the One True God, Allah.
orig: قل يا أيها الناس إن كنتم في شك من ديني فلا أعبد الذين تعبدون من دون الله ولكن أعبد الله الذي يتوفاكم وأمرت أن أكون من المؤمنين

translation: So direct your face toward the religion, inclining to truth, and never be of those who associate others with Allah.
interpretation: This verse is a command to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and, by extension, to all believers to remain steadfast in their devotion to the true religion of Islam. It emphasizes the importance of monotheism and the rejection of polytheism or the association of partners with Allah. The phrase "direct your face" is a metaphor for setting one's intention, devotion, and focus towards the worship of the One true God. It also implies that one should turn away from all false beliefs and practices. The verse reminds believers to always maintain their faith in the oneness of Allah and to never fall into the grave sin of shirk (associating partners with Allah), which is considered the greatest violation of the principle of monotheism in Islam.
orig: وأن أقم وجهك للدين حنيفا ولا تكونن من المشركين

translation: And do not invoke besides Allah that which neither benefits you nor harms you, for if you did, then indeed you would be of the wrongdoers.
interpretation: This verse is a clear warning against invoking or worshipping anyone or anything besides Allah. It emphasizes that such false deities or objects of worship have no power to benefit or harm us in any way. By engaging in this kind of polytheistic behavior, one would be committing a grave sin and would be counted among the wrongdoers and oppressors. The verse reminds us to direct all our worship, supplications, and devotion solely to Allah, as He alone has the power to grant us benefit or cause us harm. It is a call to maintain pure monotheism (Tawheed) and avoid the pitfalls of shirk (associating partners with Allah).
orig: ولا تدع من دون الله ما لا ينفعك ولا يضرك فإن فعلت فإنك إذا من الظالمين

translation: And if Allah should touch you with adversity, there is no remover of it except Him. And if He intends for you good, then there is no repeller of His bounty. He causes it to reach whom He wills of His servants. And He is the Forgiving, the Merciful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's absolute power and control over all affairs. It conveys that if Allah decides to afflict someone with hardship, no one can remove it except Him. Likewise, if Allah intends to bless someone with goodness, no one can prevent or repel His bounty. It is solely Allah's will and decision to bestow His mercy and blessings upon whomever He chooses among His servants. The verse also highlights two of Allah's beautiful names and attributes: Al-Ghafoor (the All-Forgiving) and Ar-Raheem (the Most Merciful), indicating that Allah forgives the sins of His servants and showers them with His mercy and grace.
orig: وإن يمسسك الله بضر فلا كاشف له إلا هو وإن يردك بخير فلا راد لفضله يصيب به من يشاء من عباده وهو الغفور الرحيم

translation: Say, "O mankind, the truth has come to you from your Lord, so whoever is guided is only guided for [the benefit of] his soul, and whoever goes astray only goes astray [in violation] against it. And I am not over you a manager."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the individual responsibility of each person in accepting or rejecting the truth that has come from God. The Prophet Muhammad is instructed to declare that he is merely a messenger and not a guardian or manager over the people, meaning that he cannot force anyone to believe or be held accountable for their choices. Ultimately, each soul will bear the consequences of its own decisions, whether it is guided by the truth or goes astray. This highlights the importance of free will and the accountability of every individual before God.
orig: قل يا أيها الناس قد جاءكم الحق من ربكم فمن اهتدى فإنما يهتدي لنفسه ومن ضل فإنما يضل عليها وما أنا عليكم بوكيل

translation: And follow what is revealed to you, [O Muhammad], and be patient until Allah will judge. And He is the best of judges.
interpretation: This verse instructs Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) to adhere to the divine revelation given to him by Allah and to remain steadfast in the face of adversity and opposition until Allah delivers His judgment. It emphasizes the importance of patience and trust in Allah's wisdom and justice, as He is the ultimate judge and the best of all judges. The verse encourages the Prophet and, by extension, all believers to stay committed to the path of righteousness and to have faith in Allah's plan, even during difficult times.
orig: واتبع ما يوحى إليك واصبر حتى يحكم الله وهو خير الحاكمين

translation: Alif, Lam, Ra. [This is] a Book whose verses are perfected and then presented in detail from [one who is] Wise and Acquainted.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the divine nature and perfection of the Qur'an. The letters "Alif, Lam, Ra" are among the mysterious letters that open some chapters of the Qur'an, the meaning of which is known only to Allah. The verse then describes the Qur'an as a book whose verses are flawless, well-constructed, and free from any contradictions or inconsistencies. The Qur'an is revealed by Allah, who is described as "Wise" and "Acquainted," indicating that the verses are full of wisdom and knowledge, and that Allah is fully aware of the needs and conditions of His creation. This verse sets the stage for the rest of the chapter, affirming the authenticity and authority of the Qur'an as a divine revelation.
orig: الر كتاب أحكمت آياته ثم فصلت من لدن حكيم خبير

translation: Worship none but Allah. Verily, I (Muhammad) am unto you from Him a warner and a bringer of glad tidings.
interpretation: This verse is a clear command to worship Allah alone and not to associate any partners with Him. It emphasizes the role of Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) as a messenger of Allah, whose duty is to warn people of the consequences of disobeying Allah and to give glad tidings to those who follow the right path. The verse highlights the importance of Tawheed (monotheism) and the rejection of shirk (associating partners with Allah). It serves as a reminder for believers to direct all forms of worship, such as prayer, supplication, and seeking help, towards Allah alone.
orig: ألا تعبدوا إلا الله إنني لكم منه نذير وبشير

translation: And seek forgiveness of your Lord and repent to Him, [and] He will let you enjoy a good provision for a specified term and give every doer of favor his favor. But if you turn away, then indeed, I fear for you the punishment of a great Day.
interpretation: This verse encourages people to seek forgiveness from Allah and turn to Him in repentance. If they do so, Allah promises to grant them a good life until a predetermined time, and to reward those who do good deeds according to their merit. However, the verse also serves as a warning to those who turn away from Allah's guidance, stating that they may face a severe punishment on the Day of Judgment. This highlights the importance of seeking Allah's forgiveness, repenting sincerely, and adhering to His commands to attain success in this life and the hereafter.
orig: وأن استغفروا ربكم ثم توبوا إليه يمتعكم متاعا حسنا إلى أجل مسمى ويؤت كل ذي فضل فضله وإن تولوا فإني أخاف عليكم عذاب يوم كبير

translation: To Allah is your return, and He is over all things competent.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the ultimate power and authority of Allah. It reminds us that regardless of our actions or beliefs in this worldly life, we will all eventually return to Allah for judgment. He has the ability to do all things and His power extends over everything in existence. This verse serves as a reminder for humans to be mindful of their actions and to strive to live in accordance with Allah's guidance, knowing that we will be held accountable for our deeds in the Hereafter. It also provides comfort and reassurance to believers, knowing that Allah is in control and has the power to help and support them through all of life's challenges.
orig: إلى الله مرجعكم وهو على كل شيء قدير

translation: Unquestionably, they the disbelievers turn away their breasts to hide themselves from Him. Unquestionably, [even] when they cover themselves in their clothing, Allah knows what they conceal and what they declare. Indeed, He is Knowing of that within the breasts.
interpretation: This verse points to the futility of the disbelievers trying to hide their inner thoughts and intentions from Allah. Even if they turn away or try to conceal themselves outwardly, Allah is fully aware of what is in their hearts, both what they keep secret and what they reveal. It emphasizes Allah's omniscience and that nothing whatsoever is hidden from Him, since He knows the very depths of what lies within the hearts of His creation. The message is that it is pointless to try to deceive Allah or imagine one can escape His knowledge, as He is aware of a person's innermost thoughts and feelings.
orig: ألا إنهم يثنون صدورهم ليستخفوا منه ألا حين يستغشون ثيابهم يعلم ما يسرون وما يعلنون إنه عليم بذات الصدور

translation: And there is no creature on earth but that upon Allah is its provision, and He knows its place of dwelling and place of storage. All is in a clear register.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's omniscience and His role as the ultimate provider for all living beings. It asserts that every creature on Earth, no matter how small or insignificant, is under the care and supervision of Allah. He not only provides for their sustenance but also has knowledge of their dwelling places and where they will ultimately be stored (in death). The verse concludes by stating that all of this information is contained within a clear register, which can be interpreted as the divine records or the Preserved Tablet (al-Lawh al-Mahfūẓ). This verse serves as a reminder for believers to trust in Allah's providence and to recognize His power and knowledge over all aspects of creation.
orig: وما من دابة في الأرض إلا على الله رزقها ويعلم مستقرها ومستودعها كل في كتاب مبين

translation: And it is He who created the heavens and the earth in six days - and His Throne had been upon water - that He might test you as to which of you is best in deed. But if you say, "Indeed, you are resurrected after death," those who disbelieve will surely say, "This is not but obvious magic."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the power and wisdom of Allah, who created the universe in six days and established His throne upon water before the creation of the heavens and the earth. The purpose of creation is to test mankind and see who among them will perform the best deeds. The verse also highlights the skepticism of disbelievers, who, when faced with the concept of resurrection after death, dismiss it as mere magic or trickery. This disbelief stems from their inability to comprehend the immense power of Allah and the reality of the afterlife, which is a central tenet of Islamic faith.
orig: وهو الذي خلق السماوات والأرض في ستة أيام وكان عرشه على الماء ليبلوكم أيكم أحسن عملا ولئن قلت إنكم مبعوثون من بعد الموت ليقولن الذين كفروا إن هذا إلا سحر مبين

translation: And if We hold back from them the punishment for a limited time, they will surely say, "What detains it?" Unquestionably, on the Day it comes to them, it will not be averted from them, and they will be enveloped by what they used to ridicule.
interpretation: This verse is a warning to those who mock and disbelieve in Allah's punishment. It suggests that even if the punishment is delayed for a while, it will inevitably come and cannot be avoided. The disbelievers will be surrounded by the very thing they used to ridicule, indicating the severity and inescapability of Allah's judgment. This verse emphasizes the importance of belief and the consequences of denying the truth, urging people to reflect on their actions and their ultimate fate in the Hereafter.
orig: ولئن أخرنا عنهم العذاب إلى أمة معدودة ليقولن ما يحبسه ألا يوم يأتيهم ليس مصروفا عنهم وحاق بهم ما كانوا به يستهزئون

translation: And if We give man a taste of mercy from Us and then We withdraw it from him, indeed, he is despairing and ungrateful.
interpretation: This verse highlights the fickle nature of human beings. When God bestows His mercy and blessings upon a person, they are content and happy. However, if those blessings are taken away, even for a short while, the person becomes desperate and ungrateful, forgetting all the previous favors they enjoyed. This shows the weakness of human faith and the tendency to focus on the present hardships rather than remembering God's past kindness. The verse serves as a reminder for people to remain steadfast in their faith and gratitude towards God, even in times of difficulty or when blessings seem to have been withdrawn, trusting that God's mercy and wisdom are ever-present.
orig: ولئن أذقنا الإنسان منا رحمة ثم نزعناها منه إنه ليئوس كفور

translation: And if We give him a taste of favor after hardship has touched him, he will surely say, "Bad times have left me." Indeed, he is exultant and boastful -
interpretation: This verse is commenting on the nature of the human being, who often becomes arrogant and boastful when blessed with ease and comfort after experiencing difficulty. Rather than being grateful to Allah for the blessings and acknowledging that both hardship and ease come from Him, he attributes the good to himself and believes the bad times are over for good. This attitude reflects the human tendency towards pride and ingratitude, forgetting that all circumstances are in Allah's control and that both good and bad are tests from Him. The verse warns against such a mindset and emphasizes the importance of remaining humble and grateful to Allah in all situations.
orig: ولئن أذقناه نعماء بعد ضراء مسته ليقولن ذهب السيئات عني إنه لفرح فخور

translation: Except for those who are patient and do righteous deeds, for them is forgiveness and great reward.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of patience and righteous deeds in attaining Allah's forgiveness and great reward in the Hereafter. It suggests that those who persevere through hardships and consistently perform good actions will be granted forgiveness for their sins and will be generously rewarded by Allah. The verse implies that patience and righteousness are key qualities of true believers, and that these virtues will ultimately lead to success and salvation in the afterlife.
orig: إلا الذين صبروا وعملوا الصالحات أولئك لهم مغفرة وأجر كبير

translation: Then perhaps you would leave some of what is revealed to you, and your breast would become straitened by it because they say, "Why has not a treasure been sent down to him, or an angel come with him?" But you are only a warner. And Allah is Disposer of all things.
interpretation: This verse is addressing the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him), acknowledging the difficulty he faced in conveying the message of Islam. It suggests that he might be tempted to omit some parts of the revelation due to the pressure and criticism from the disbelievers who demanded material proof of his prophethood, such as a treasure or an accompanying angel. However, the verse reminds the Prophet that his role is to serve as a warner, delivering the message as it was revealed to him, and that Allah is the one who has control over all things. This highlights the importance of the Prophet's trust in Allah and his steadfastness in fulfilling his mission, regardless of the challenges he encountered.
orig: فلعلك تارك بعض ما يوحى إليك وضائق به صدرك أن يقولوا لولا أنزل عليه كنز أو جاء معه ملك إنما أنت نذير والله على كل شيء وكيل

translation: Or do they say, "He invented it"? Say, "Then bring ten surahs like it that have been invented and call upon [for assistance] whomever you can besides Allah, if you should be truthful."
interpretation: This verse challenges those who claim that the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) invented the Qur'an himself. It asks them to produce ten chapters like those of the Qur'an, and to seek help from anyone they wish, besides Allah, in doing so. The implication is that if the Qur'an were the work of a mere human being, others would be able to produce something similar. The fact that no one has been able to do so is proof that the Qur'an is of divine origin and that Muhammad (peace be upon him) was indeed a prophet receiving revelation from Allah.
orig: أم يقولون افتراه قل فأتوا بعشر سور مثله مفتريات وادعوا من استطعتم من دون الله إن كنتم صادقين

translation: But if they do not respond to you, then know that it was revealed with the knowledge of Allah and that there is no deity except Him. Then, would you [not] be Muslims?
interpretation: This verse is a call to the believers to have faith in the divine origin of the Qur'an and to submit to Allah's will. It emphasizes that if the disbelievers do not accept the message of Islam despite clear evidence, it is because the Qur'an has been revealed with Allah's knowledge and wisdom. The verse also affirms the fundamental principle of Islam, which is the oneness of Allah and the absence of any other deity worthy of worship. It concludes with a question that encourages the believers to embrace Islam wholeheartedly and submit to Allah's guidance, as it is the path to ultimate success and salvation.
orig: فإلم يستجيبوا لكم فاعلموا أنما أنزل بعلم الله وأن لا إله إلا هو فهل أنتم مسلمون

translation: Whoever desires the life of this world and its adornments - We fully repay them for their deeds therein, and they therein will not be deprived.
interpretation: This verse is a reminder that those who are solely focused on the material pleasures and superficial adornments of this worldly life will be recompensed in full for their deeds in this world. They will receive the rewards of their actions in this life and will not be wronged or deprived of anything they deserve. However, the verse subtly implies that such people may have neglected the more important and everlasting rewards of the Hereafter by being preoccupied with worldly gains. It serves as a caution against becoming distracted by temporary pleasures at the expense of one's eternal well-being in the afterlife.
orig: من كان يريد الحياة الدنيا وزينتها نوف إليهم أعمالهم فيها وهم فيها لا يبخسون

translation: Those are the ones for whom there is nothing in the Hereafter but the Fire, and whatever they had done in it has failed, and worthless is whatever they used to do.
interpretation: This verse warns that those who reject faith and do evil deeds will have nothing but the punishment of Hellfire in the Hereafter. All their worldly efforts and accomplishments will be rendered worthless and futile because they did not believe in Allah and follow His guidance. It emphasizes that success in the Hereafter depends on one's faith and righteous deeds in this world, and that the ultimate loss is to be deprived of Allah's mercy and face His wrath in the Afterlife due to one's disbelief and disobedience.
orig: أولئك الذين ليس لهم في الآخرة إلا النار وحبط ما صنعوا فيها وباطل ما كانوا يعملون

translation: So is he who is on clear evidence from his Lord, and a witness from Him follows it, and before it was the Scripture of Moses to lead and as mercy. Those [believers in the former revelations] believe in it [the Qur'an]. But whoever disbelieves in it from the [various] factions - the Fire is his promised destination. So be not in doubt about it. Indeed, it is the truth from your Lord, but most of the people do not believe.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that those who believe in the Qur'an and follow its teachings are guided by clear evidence from Allah. They also have the testimony of a witness, which could refer to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) or the inherent truth and wisdom within the Qur'an itself. The verse also mentions that the Torah, revealed to Moses, served as a guide and mercy before the Qur'an. True believers of the previous scriptures will recognize the truth of the Qur'an and believe in it. However, those who reject the Qur'an from among the various groups are promised the punishment of the Fire. The verse asserts that there should be no doubt about the Qur'an being the truth from Allah, even though most people do not believe in it. This highlights the importance of faith and the consequences of disbelief, despite the clear evidence provided by Allah.
orig: أفمن كان على بينة من ربه ويتلوه شاهد منه ومن قبله كتاب موسى إماما ورحمة أولئك يؤمنون به ومن يكفر به من الأحزاب فالنار موعده فلا تك في مرية منه إنه الحق من ربك ولكن أكثر الناس لا يؤمنون

translation: And who is more unjust than one who invents a lie about Allah? Those will be presented before their Lord, and the witnesses will say, "These are the ones who lied against their Lord." Unquestionably, the curse of Allah is upon the wrongdoers.
interpretation: This verse strongly condemns those who attribute falsehood to Allah, considering it one of the gravest forms of injustice. On the Day of Judgment, these liars will be brought before Allah and the witnesses, likely the angels or prophets, will testify against them, exposing their lies. The verse emphasizes that such people, who deliberately lie about Allah, are undoubtedly under His curse. It serves as a severe warning against inventing lies about Allah or His religion, and affirms that those who engage in this egregious sin will face the consequences of Allah's anger and punishment in the Hereafter.
orig: ومن أظلم ممن افترى على الله كذبا أولئك يعرضون على ربهم ويقول الأشهاد هؤلاء الذين كذبوا على ربهم ألا لعنة الله على الظالمين

translation: Those who hinder [people] from the way of Allah and seek to make it [seem] deviant while they, concerning the Hereafter, are disbelievers.
interpretation: This verse is referring to those who actively work against the path of Allah and try to mislead others from following it. They reject the concept of the Hereafter and the accountability that comes with it. Their disbelief in the afterlife is tied to their actions in hindering others from the straight path. The verse emphasizes that these people are not just passively disbelieving, but are actively trying to undermine the message of Islam and create obstacles for those who would follow Allah's way.
orig: الذين يصدون عن سبيل الله ويبغونها عوجا وهم بالآخرة هم كافرون

translation: Those were not causing failure [to Allah] on the earth, nor did they have besides Allah any protectors. For them the punishment will be multiplied. They were not able to hear, nor did they see.
interpretation: This verse speaks about the fate of those who reject Allah's message and oppose His prophets. It emphasizes their ultimate powerlessness and inability to escape Allah's punishment, despite their apparent might or influence in this world. The verse highlights that they will have no protectors or allies besides Allah to help them on the Day of Judgment. As a consequence of their disbelief and transgressions, their punishment in the Hereafter will be multiplied manifold. The verse also points out their spiritual deficiencies - they were unable to hear the truth or see the signs of Allah's existence and unity, which led to their deviance and downfall.
orig: أولئك لم يكونوا معجزين في الأرض وما كان لهم من دون الله من أولياء يضاعف لهم العذاب ما كانوا يستطيعون السمع وما كانوا يبصرون

translation: Those are the ones who have lost their souls, and lost from them is what they used to invent.
interpretation: This verse refers to those who have strayed far from the path of God and have lost their way in life. They have forfeited their own souls by rejecting the truth and following their own desires and false beliefs. All the false idols, philosophies, and ideas that they invented and followed instead of God's guidance will be of no benefit to them. They will realize the emptiness and futility of their misguided ways, but it will be too late. Their loss is complete and irreversible, encompassing both this world and the hereafter. It is a stark warning about the consequences of turning away from divine guidance and inventing one's own misguided beliefs.
orig: أولئك الذين خسروا أنفسهم وضل عنهم ما كانوا يفترون

translation: Without doubt, in the Hereafter they will be the greatest losers.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that those who reject faith and do evil deeds will be the ultimate losers in the eternal life of the Hereafter. They may seem to gain worldly benefits in this temporary life, but they will face the severe consequences of their disbelief and wrongdoings in the eternal abode. The verse serves as a strong warning to humanity that the real success lies in having faith and leading a righteous life, as that is what will determine one's fate in the everlasting life to come.
orig: لا جرم أنهم في الآخرة هم الأخسرون

translation: Indeed, those who have believed and done righteous deeds and humbled themselves to their Lord - those are the companions of Paradise; they will abide eternally therein.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that those who have true faith, perform good deeds, and humble themselves before Allah will be granted the ultimate reward of eternal Paradise. It highlights the importance of not only believing but also acting upon that belief with sincerity and humility. The verse serves as a promise and reassurance to the believers that their efforts will not go in vain, and they will be blessed with the everlasting bliss of Paradise as a result of their devotion to Allah.
orig: إن الذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات وأخبتوا إلى ربهم أولئك أصحاب الجنة هم فيها خالدون

translation: The example of the two parties is like the blind and deaf, and the seeing and hearing. Are they equal in comparison? Then will you not remember?
interpretation: This verse draws a stark contrast between those who reject faith and those who accept it.
