The disbelievers are likened to the blind and deaf, unable to perceive truth or guidance, while the believers are like those with sight and hearing, receptive to God's message. The rhetorical question highlights how vastly different these two groups are, prompting the listener to reflect and remember the importance of faith and heeding the truth.
orig: مثل الفريقين كالأعمى والأصم والبصير والسميع هل يستويان مثلا أفلا تذكرون

translation: And We had certainly sent Noah to his people, [saying], "Indeed, I am to you a clear warner"
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the role of Prophet Noah as a warner to his people. He was sent by Allah to warn them of the consequences of their wrongdoings and to call them towards the path of righteousness. The use of the word "clear" suggests that his message was unambiguous and easily understandable, leaving no room for doubt or confusion. It also implies that Noah delivered his message with sincerity and clarity, fulfilling his duty as a prophet and messenger of Allah.
orig: ولقد أرسلنا نوحا إلى قومه إني لكم نذير مبين

translation: That you not worship except Allah. Indeed, I fear for you the punishment of a painful day.
interpretation: This verse is a clear warning and reminder to humanity that they should worship none other than Allah alone. The speaker, who is likely a prophet or messenger of Allah, expresses deep concern and fear that if people do not heed this message and instead worship false idols or other entities besides Allah, they will face severe punishment on a "painful day" - likely referring to the Day of Judgment. This interpretation highlights the gravity of shirk (polytheism) and the importance of Tawheed (the Oneness of Allah) in Islam. It also underscores the role of prophets and messengers in conveying Allah's message and warning to mankind out of sincere care and concern for their ultimate fate in the Hereafter.
orig: أن لا تعبدوا إلا الله إني أخاف عليكم عذاب يوم أليم

translation: But the eminent ones who disbelieved among his people said, "We do not see you but as a man like ourselves, and we do not see you followed except by those who are the lowest of us [and] at first suggestion. And we do not see in you over us any merit; rather, we think you are liars."
interpretation: This verse reflects the arrogance and pride of the elite disbelievers who rejected the message of the prophet despite clear signs. They viewed the prophet as just an ordinary man and saw his followers as the lowest members of society, judging by outward appearances. They were blind to the truth and spiritual merit of the prophet and his followers. The disbelievers' worldly status and wealth deluded them into denying the message and falsely accusing the prophet of lying, as their materialistic outlook prevented them from recognizing the truth.
orig: فقال الملأ الذين كفروا من قومه ما نراك إلا بشرا مثلنا وما نراك اتبعك إلا الذين هم أراذلنا بادي الرأي وما نرى لكم علينا من فضل بل نظنكم كاذبين

translation: He said, "O my people, have you considered if I am upon clear evidence from my Lord and He has given me mercy from Himself, but it has been made unapparent to you? Should we force it upon you while you are averse to it?"
interpretation: In this verse, the prophet is questioning his people, asking them to consider his position. He asserts that he is acting based on clear guidance and mercy from God, even if the people cannot perceive or appreciate it. He then rhetorically asks if it would be right to impose this divine message on them against their will, while they are averse to it. The implication is that true faith cannot be forced; it is an individual choice that people must make based on their own understanding and inclination. The prophet's role is to deliver the message clearly, but not to compel anyone to follow it unwillingly.
orig: قال يا قوم أرأيتم إن كنت على بينة من ربي وآتاني رحمة من عنده فعميت عليكم أنلزمكموها وأنتم لها كارهون

translation: And O my people, I ask not of you for it any wealth. My reward is not but from Allah. And I am not one to drive away those who have believed. Indeed, they will meet their Lord, but I see that you are a people behaving ignorantly.
interpretation: In this verse, the prophet is addressing his people, making it clear that he is not seeking any material gain or reward from them for his message. He emphasizes that his reward comes only from Allah. Furthermore, he refuses to turn away the believers, even if they are from the lower classes of society, because he recognizes that they will ultimately meet their Lord. The prophet sees that his people are acting ignorantly by judging others based on their social status rather than their faith and righteousness. This highlights the importance of treating all believers equally and not discriminating based on worldly factors.
orig: ويا قوم لا أسألكم عليه مالا إن أجري إلا على الله وما أنا بطارد الذين آمنوا إنهم ملاقو ربهم ولكني أراكم قوما تجهلون

translation: And O my people, who would protect me from Allah if I drove them away? Then will you not be reminded?
interpretation: This verse is a reminder that one should not mistreat or expel believers, even if they are poor or weak, out of fear of the disapproval of others. The speaker is emphasizing that Allah is the ultimate authority and protector, and that one should fear Him above all else. Driving away the believers would be a grave sin that would incur Allah's wrath. The rhetorical question at the end is meant to make the audience reflect on this reality and be mindful of their actions, lest they face the consequences in this life and the hereafter for wronging the believers.
orig: ويا قوم من ينصرني من الله إن طردتهم أفلا تذكرون

translation: And I do not say to you that I have the depositories of Allah or that I know the unseen, nor do I say that I am an angel, and I do not say of those upon whom your eyes look down that Allah will never grant them any good. Allah is most knowing of what is within their souls. Indeed, I would then be among the wrongdoers.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the humility and honesty of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him). He acknowledges that he does not possess the treasures of Allah, nor does he have knowledge of the unseen future. He also affirms that he is not an angel, but a human being chosen by Allah to deliver His message. Furthermore, the Prophet is instructed not to look down upon or despise those who may appear lowly or disadvantaged in society, as Allah alone knows what goodness lies within their hearts. The verse serves as a reminder to judge people not by their outward appearance or status, but by their inner character and faith.
orig: ولا أقول لكم عندي خزائن الله ولا أعلم الغيب ولا أقول إني ملك ولا أقول للذين تزدري أعينكم لن يؤتيهم الله خيرا الله أعلم بما في أنفسهم إني إذا لمن الظالمين

translation: They said, "O Noah, you have disputed us and been frequent in dispute of us. So bring us what you threaten us with, if you should be of the truthful."
interpretation: This verse reflects the stubbornness and disbelief of Prophet Noah's people. Despite Noah's repeated attempts to guide them to the right path and warn them of God's punishment, they remained defiant and challenged him to bring about the divine retribution he had been warning them about. Their words indicate their lack of faith and their arrogant attitude towards the prophet's message. It also shows their failure to recognize the signs and warnings sent by God through His messenger. The verse emphasizes the importance of heeding the call of the prophets and the consequences of rejecting divine guidance.
orig: قالوا يا نوح قد جادلتنا فأكثرت جدالنا فأتنا بما تعدنا إن كنت من الصادقين

translation: He said, "Allah will only bring it to you if He wills, and you will not cause failure [to Him]."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute power and control of Allah over all things. It conveys that whatever happens or is brought about is solely by the will of Allah, and that human beings are ultimately powerless in comparison to Him. They cannot escape His decree or prevent what He has willed to occur. The verse also implies that one should submit to Allah's will and trust in His wisdom, recognizing that He knows what is best for His creation.
orig: قال إنما يأتيكم به الله إن شاء وما أنتم بمعجزين

translation: And my advice will not benefit you - although I wished to advise you - if Allah should intend to put you in error. He is your Lord, and to Him you will be returned.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the ultimate power and will of Allah over His creation. Even if someone sincerely wishes to guide others to the right path, their efforts will be futile if Allah has decreed that those individuals should remain misguided. It serves as a reminder that guidance comes from Allah alone, and that all matters ultimately return to Him. The verse also highlights the importance of recognizing Allah's sovereignty and submitting to His will, as He is the Lord and Master of all.
orig: ولا ينفعكم نصحي إن أردت أن أنصح لكم إن كان الله يريد أن يغويكم هو ربكم وإليه ترجعون

translation: Or do they say, "He has invented it"? Say, "If I have invented it, then upon me is [the consequence of] my crime; but I am innocent of what [crimes] you commit."
interpretation: This verse is addressing the accusations made by the disbelievers that the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) had fabricated the Qur'an himself. Allah instructs the Prophet to respond by saying that if he had indeed invented it, then he alone would bear the consequences of that great sin. However, the Prophet affirms his innocence of their false accusations and states that he is free of the crimes and sins they commit by rejecting the truth of the Qur'an and its message. The verse highlights the Prophet's sincerity and the divine origin of the Qur'an, while also pointing out the disbelievers' stubborn refusal to accept the truth despite clear evidence.
orig: أم يقولون افتراه قل إن افتريته فعلي إجرامي وأنا بريء مما تجرمون

translation: And it was revealed to Noah that none of your people will believe except those who have already believed, so do not be distressed by what they have been doing.
interpretation: This verse is a message of consolation to Prophet Noah, who had been preaching to his people for a long time with little success. Allah reveals to him that no one else from his nation will believe in his message except those who have already accepted faith. Allah instructs Noah not to feel saddened or disheartened by the actions and disbelief of his people, as he has already fulfilled his duty of conveying the message. This verse emphasizes the concept of divine decree and that guidance is ultimately in the hands of Allah. It also highlights the importance of patience and perseverance for prophets and believers in the face of adversity and rejection.
orig: وأوحي إلى نوح أنه لن يؤمن من قومك إلا من قد آمن فلا تبتئس بما كانوا يفعلون

translation: And construct the ship under Our Eyes and with Our Revelation, and do not address Me concerning those who have wronged; indeed, they are [to be] drowned.
interpretation: This verse is a command from Allah to Prophet Noah to build the Ark according to Allah's guidance and revelation. It also contains a warning not to plead on behalf of the wrongdoers who rejected the message, as their fate of drowning in the flood has already been decreed. This highlights the importance of following divine instructions and the consequences of rejecting the truth. It also shows that there comes a point when the decision of punishment is final, and no intercession can be made for those who persist in wrongdoing.
orig: واصنع الفلك بأعيننا ووحينا ولا تخاطبني في الذين ظلموا إنهم مغرقون

translation: And he constructed the ship, and whenever an assembly of the eminent of his people passed by him, they ridiculed him. He said, "If you ridicule us, then we will ridicule you just as you ridicule."
interpretation: This verse is referring to the story of Prophet Noah (peace be upon him) and his people. The interpretation is that despite facing ridicule and mockery from his people while building the ark, Prophet Noah remained steadfast in his faith and continued his mission. He responded to their ridicule by saying that just as they mock him now, there will come a time when the believers will have the last laugh and the mockers will be the ones facing humiliation and regret for their disbelief. This highlights the importance of patience, perseverance, and complete trust in Allah's plan in the face of adversity and opposition when striving to fulfill divine commandments.
orig: ويصنع الفلك وكلما مر عليه ملأ من قومه سخروا منه قال إن تسخروا منا فإنا نسخر منكم كما تسخرون

translation: And you will come to know who it is upon whom will come a punishment that will disgrace him and upon whom will fall an enduring punishment.
interpretation: This verse serves as a warning to those who reject the message of Islam and the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him). It emphasizes that those who persist in their disbelief and wrongdoing will face a humiliating punishment in this world, and an even more severe and lasting punishment in the Hereafter. The interpretation highlights the consequences of rejecting divine guidance and encourages individuals to reflect upon their actions and beliefs, as they will be held accountable for their choices in the afterlife.
orig: فسوف تعلمون من يأتيه عذاب يخزيه ويحل عليه عذاب مقيم

translation: Until, when Our command came and the oven overflowed, We said, "Load upon the ship of each [creature] two mates and your family, except those about whom the word has preceded, and [include] whoever has believed." But none had believed with him, except a few.
interpretation: This verse is referring to the story of Prophet Noah (peace be upon him) and the great flood. When Allah's command came and the oven overflowed, which was a sign for Noah to begin loading the ark, Allah instructed him to take on board a pair of each animal species, his family members (except those who were destined to be drowned), and the believers who had faith in his message. However, the verse points out that only a few people believed in Noah and joined him on the ark, highlighting the fact that the majority of his people rejected his warnings and faced the consequences of the flood. This story emphasizes the importance of faith, obedience to Allah's messengers, and the consequences of disbelief.
orig: حتى إذا جاء أمرنا وفار التنور قلنا احمل فيها من كل زوجين اثنين وأهلك إلا من سبق عليه القول ومن آمن وما آمن معه إلا قليل

translation: And he said, "Embark therein; in the name of Allah is its course and its anchorage. Indeed, my Lord is Forgiving and Merciful."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of seeking Allah's protection and blessings when embarking on any journey or undertaking. It reminds believers to put their trust in Allah, acknowledging that He is the One who guides and controls the course of their lives. The mention of Allah's forgiveness and mercy also highlights the fact that even when humans make mistakes or face difficulties, they can always turn to Allah for forgiveness and support. This verse encourages individuals to approach their endeavors with faith, humility, and reliance on Allah's grace.
orig: وقال اركبوا فيها بسم الله مجراها ومرساها إن ربي لغفور رحيم

translation: And it sailed with them through waves like mountains, and Noah called to his son who was apart [from them], "O my son, come aboard with us and be not with the disbelievers."
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of faith and obedience to Allah, even in the face of great adversity. Noah's son, despite being called by his father to join the believers on the Ark, chose to remain with the disbelievers. This decision ultimately led to his demise, as he was not saved from the flood. The verse serves as a reminder that one's faith and actions have consequences, and that following the guidance of the prophets and remaining steadfast in belief is essential for salvation. It also emphasizes the strength of family ties, as Noah still called out to his son with concern and love, despite his disobedience.
orig: وهي تجري بهم في موج كالجبال ونادى نوح ابنه وكان في معزل يا بني اركب معنا ولا تكن مع الكافرين

translation: He said, "I will take refuge on a mountain to protect me from the water." [Noah] said, "There is no protector today from the decree of Allah, except for whom He gives mercy." And the waves came between them, and he was among the drowned.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the futility of seeking protection from Allah's punishment through worldly means. The son of Prophet Noah believed that he could escape the flood by taking shelter on a mountain, but Noah warned him that nothing can save a person from Allah's decree except His mercy. The son's refusal to believe in Allah and enter the ark led to his drowning. This emphasizes the importance of complete reliance on Allah and seeking His mercy and protection, rather than depending on one's own strength or worldly resources in the face of divine retribution.
orig: قال سآوي إلى جبل يعصمني من الماء قال لا عاصم اليوم من أمر الله إلا من رحم وحال بينهما الموج فكان من المغرقين

translation: And it was said, "O earth, swallow your water, and O sky, withhold [your rain]." And the water subsided, and the matter was accomplished, and the ship came to rest on the [mountain of] Judiyy. And it was said, "Away with the wrongdoing people."
interpretation: This verse signifies the end of the great flood that was sent as a punishment to the people of Noah who rejected his message. It demonstrates God's ultimate power and control over all elements of nature. The earth and sky obey His command, causing the floodwaters to recede. The ark carrying Noah and the believers comes to rest on Mount Judi, symbolizing their salvation and the triumph of faith. The final statement "Away with the wrongdoing people" emphasizes the fate of those who oppose God's will and the consequences of their actions, serving as a warning to future generations.
orig: وقيل يا أرض ابلعي ماءك ويا سماء أقلعي وغيض الماء وقضي الأمر واستوت على الجودي وقيل بعدا للقوم الظالمين

translation: And Noah called to his Lord and said, "My Lord, indeed my son is of my family; and indeed, Your promise is true, and You are the most just of judges!"
interpretation: In this verse, Prophet Noah is pleading with Allah regarding his son, who refused to believe in Allah's message and did not board the Ark. Noah reminds Allah that his son is a part of his family, and Allah had promised to save his family. He acknowledges that Allah's promise is true and that Allah is the most just of all judges. This verse highlights Noah's deep concern for his son's fate and his unwavering faith in Allah's justice and wisdom, even in the face of a difficult situation involving his own family.
orig: ونادى نوح ربه فقال رب إن ابني من أهلي وإن وعدك الحق وأنت أحكم الحاكمين

translation: He said, "O Noah, indeed he is not of your family; indeed, he is [one whose] work was other than righteous, so ask Me not for that about which you have no knowledge. Indeed, I advise you, lest you be among the ignorant."
interpretation: This verse is a reminder that even the closest of family ties cannot save a person from the consequences of their actions if they persist in wrongdoing and disbelief. Allah is advising Prophet Noah (peace be upon him) not to plead on behalf of his disbelieving son, as the latter's actions have placed him outside the fold of the righteous. The verse emphasizes the importance of individual accountability and the supremacy of one's deeds over familial connections in determining their ultimate fate. It also serves as a warning against advocating for something without proper knowledge, as doing so may lead to ignorance and misguidance.
orig: قال يا نوح إنه ليس من أهلك إنه عمل غير صالح فلا تسألن ما ليس لك به علم إني أعظك أن تكون من الجاهلين

translation: He said, "My Lord, I seek refuge in You from asking that of which I have no knowledge. And unless You forgive me and have mercy upon me, I will be among the losers."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of seeking knowledge and understanding before making judgments or requests. It teaches humility and the recognition of one's own limitations, encouraging individuals to seek refuge in God's forgiveness and mercy when they have erred or acted without proper knowledge. The verse also highlights the consequences of failing to seek forgiveness and mercy, which may lead to being among the losers in both this world and the hereafter. It serves as a reminder to approach God with sincerity, humility, and a desire for guidance and understanding.
orig: قال رب إني أعوذ بك أن أسألك ما ليس لي به علم وإلا تغفر لي وترحمني أكن من الخاسرين

translation: It was said, "O Noah, disembark in security from Us and blessings upon you and upon nations [descending] from those with you. But other nations [of them] We will grant enjoyment; then there will touch them from Us a painful punishment."
interpretation: This verse is a divine command to Prophet Noah (peace be upon him) after the great flood, instructing him to disembark from the Ark with peace and blessings from Allah. It also conveys that while some nations descending from those saved on the Ark will be blessed, others will enjoy the temporary pleasures of this world, but will ultimately face a severe punishment from Allah in the Hereafter. This interpretation highlights the idea that the ultimate fate of nations depends on their faith, actions, and adherence to the divine message, and that worldly enjoyment does not necessarily equate to success in the eyes of Allah.
orig: قيل يا نوح اهبط بسلام منا وبركات عليك وعلى أمم ممن معك وأمم سنمتعهم ثم يمسهم منا عذاب أليم

translation: That is from the news of the unseen which We reveal to you, [O Muhammad]. You knew it not, neither you nor your people, before this. So be patient; indeed, the [best] outcome is for the righteous.
interpretation: This verse highlights that the stories and information revealed in the Qur'an, such as the story of Prophet Joseph, were previously unknown to Prophet Muhammad and his people. It emphasizes that this knowledge comes from divine revelation, not from any human source. The verse also encourages patience and righteousness, as the ultimate success and the best outcome belong to those who are mindful of Allah and follow His guidance. It serves as a reminder that the Prophet's role is to convey the divine message and that the ultimate wisdom and knowledge belong to Allah alone.
orig: تلك من أنباء الغيب نوحيها إليك ما كنت تعلمها أنت ولا قومك من قبل هذا فاصبر إن العاقبة للمتقين

translation: And to the 'Aad [We sent] their brother Hud. He said, "O my people, worship Allah; you have no deity other than Him. You are not but inventors [of falsehood].
interpretation: This verse conveys a message to the people of 'Aad through their prophet Hud, who was sent to guide them. Hud's message emphasizes the importance of worshipping Allah alone and rejecting all false deities. He accuses the people of 'Aad of inventing false gods and attributes, which is a form of deception and falsehood. The verse highlights the concept of Tawhid (monotheism) and the rejection of shirk (associating partners with Allah). It serves as a reminder for all people to worship Allah alone and to avoid the sin of attributing divine characteristics to anyone or anything other than Him.
orig: وإلى عاد أخاهم هودا قال يا قوم اعبدوا الله ما لكم من إله غيره إن أنتم إلا مفترون

translation: O my people, I do not ask you for any reward for it. My reward is only from the One who created me. Will you not then understand?
interpretation: The verse emphasizes that the prophet is not seeking any worldly gain or reward from his people for conveying the message of God. His sole purpose is to fulfill the duty assigned to him by his Creator, and his reward is with God alone. The rhetorical question at the end is a call for the people to use their reason and understand the sincerity of the prophet's intentions, as he has no ulterior motive in preaching to them other than concern for their spiritual well-being and salvation.
orig: يا قوم لا أسألكم عليه أجرا إن أجري إلا على الذي فطرني أفلا تعقلون

translation: And O my people, ask forgiveness of your Lord and then repent to Him. He will send [rain from] the sky upon you in showers and increase you in strength [added] to your strength. And do not turn away, [being] criminals.
interpretation: This verse is a call to the people to seek forgiveness from Allah and turn to Him in repentance. It promises that if they do so, Allah will bless them with abundant rain and increase their strength. The verse also warns against turning away from this message and becoming sinners. It emphasizes the importance of seeking Allah's forgiveness and the benefits that come with it, both in this world and the hereafter. The verse encourages people to establish a strong connection with their Lord through repentance and seeking His forgiveness.
orig: ويا قوم استغفروا ربكم ثم توبوا إليه يرسل السماء عليكم مدرارا ويزدكم قوة إلى قوتكم ولا تتولوا مجرمين

translation: They said, "O Hud, you have not brought us clear evidence, and we are not ones to leave our gods on your say-so. Nor are we believers in you."
interpretation: This verse reflects the stubborn disbelief of Prophet Hud's people when he called them to worship Allah alone and leave their idols. They demanded clear proof of his prophethood, refusing to abandon their false gods merely on the basis of his words. They also declared their lack of faith in Hud himself. This highlights the challenges faced by prophets in conveying the message to obstinate unbelievers who cling to their traditional beliefs and resist the truth, even when it comes from a messenger of Allah. It shows the importance of clear evidence and persuasion in the face of skepticism and the difficulty of overcoming deeply entrenched polytheistic beliefs.
orig: قالوا يا هود ما جئتنا ببينة وما نحن بتاركي آلهتنا عن قولك وما نحن لك بمؤمنين

translation: "We only say that some of our gods have possessed you with evil [thoughts]." He said, "Indeed, I call Allah to witness, and witness [yourselves] that I am free from whatever you associate with Allah"
interpretation: In this verse, the disbelievers accuse the Prophet (peace be upon him) of being possessed by their gods with evil thoughts, causing him to speak against their idols. In response, the Prophet strongly affirms his belief in the oneness of Allah and his complete disassociation from the false gods and idols that they worship. He calls upon Allah as his witness and asks the disbelievers themselves to bear witness to his unwavering stance against polytheism and his devotion to the one true God. This verse highlights the Prophet's firm conviction in Islamic monotheism (tawheed) and his rejection of all forms of idolatry and associating partners with Allah.
orig: إن نقول إلا اعتراك بعض آلهتنا بسوء قال إني أشهد الله واشهدوا أني بريء مما تشركون

translation: So plot against me all together; then give me no respite.
interpretation: This verse is a bold challenge from the Prophet Muhammad to his enemies, daring them to conspire against him without delay. It reflects his unwavering faith in Allah's protection and his fearlessness in the face of opposition. The verse implies that no matter what schemes or plots the disbelievers may devise, they will ultimately be futile because the Prophet is under the care and support of Allah. It is a powerful statement of courage and conviction in the face of adversity.
orig: من دونه فكيدوني جميعا ثم لا تنظرون

translation: Indeed, I have relied upon Allah, my Lord and your Lord. There is no creature but that He holds its forelock. Indeed, my Lord is on a path [that is] straight.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of complete reliance and trust in Allah. It reminds us that Allah has control over all living beings, as symbolized by holding their forelocks. This metaphor signifies Allah's power, authority, and the fact that nothing happens without His knowledge and permission. The straight path mentioned in the verse represents the path of truth, guidance, and righteousness that Allah has ordained for His creation. By putting our trust in Allah and following His guidance, we can stay on this straight path and attain success in both this world and the hereafter.
orig: إني توكلت على الله ربي وربكم ما من دابة إلا هو آخذ بناصيتها إن ربي على صراط مستقيم

translation: But if you turn away, then I have conveyed to you that with which I was sent to you, and my Lord will replace you with another people, and you will not harm Him at all. Indeed, my Lord is Guardian over all things.
interpretation: This verse is a warning to those who reject the message of Islam. It emphasizes that the Prophet's duty is only to convey the message, and if people choose to turn away from it, they will not harm Allah in any way. Instead, Allah will replace them with others who will be obedient to Him. The verse also highlights Allah's power and control over all things, as He is the Guardian and Protector of everything in existence. This interpretation underscores the importance of heeding the message of Islam and the consequences of rejecting it, while also reminding believers of Allah's omnipotence and sovereignty.
orig: فإن تولوا فقد أبلغتكم ما أرسلت به إليكم ويستخلف ربي قوما غيركم ولا تضرونه شيئا إن ربي على كل شيء حفيظ

translation: And when Our command came, We saved Hud and those who believed with him, by mercy from Us, and We saved them from a harsh punishment.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's mercy and protection towards His believing servants. When the time for the punishment of the disbelievers came, Allah saved Prophet Hud and the believers who followed him from the impending destruction. This highlights the importance of faith and obedience to Allah, as it is the key to attaining His mercy and being saved from His punishment. The verse also implies that the punishment inflicted upon the disbelievers was severe and harsh, underscoring the gravity of rejecting Allah's message and the consequences that follow.
orig: ولما جاء أمرنا نجينا هودا والذين آمنوا معه برحمة منا ونجيناهم من عذاب غليظ

translation: And that was 'Aad, who denied the signs of their Lord and disobeyed His messengers and followed the order of every obstinate tyrant.
interpretation: This verse is referring to the people of 'Aad, an ancient Arabian tribe. They rejected the clear signs and warnings sent to them by God through His messengers. Instead of heeding the guidance, they arrogantly chose to follow the oppressive commands of their stubborn and tyrannical leaders. The verse highlights the consequences of denying divine revelation and submitting to corrupt human authorities instead of the will of God. It serves as a warning for people to carefully consider what they choose to believe in and obey, as the people of 'Aad faced destruction for their rebellion against God's messages.
orig: وتلك عاد جحدوا بآيات ربهم وعصوا رسله واتبعوا أمر كل جبار عنيد

translation: And they were followed in this world with a curse and [as well] on the Day of Resurrection. Unquestionably, 'Aad denied their Lord; then away with 'Aad, the people of Hud.
interpretation: This verse highlights the consequences faced by the people of 'Aad, who were the tribe of Prophet Hud, for their disbelief and rejection of Allah's message. They were cursed in this world, meaning they faced divine punishment and humiliation, and they will also be cursed on the Day of Judgment. The repetition of the phrase "then away with 'Aad" emphasizes their distance from Allah's mercy due to their persistent denial of the truth, serving as a warning to others who might follow in their footsteps.
orig: وأتبعوا في هذه الدنيا لعنة ويوم القيامة ألا إن عادا كفروا ربهم ألا بعدا لعاد قوم هود

translation: And to Thamud [We sent] their brother Salih. He said, "O my people, worship Allah; you have no deity other than Him. He has produced you from the earth and settled you in it, so ask forgiveness of Him and then repent to Him. Indeed, my Lord is near and responsive."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of worshipping Allah alone and seeking His forgiveness. It reminds us that Allah is the One who created us from the earth and established us on it, providing us with all the means of life. Therefore, we should turn to Him in repentance and seek His forgiveness, knowing that He is always near and responsive to our prayers. This highlights the direct connection between the Creator and His creation, and the significance of sincerely worshipping Him alone.
orig: وإلى ثمود أخاهم صالحا قال يا قوم اعبدوا الله ما لكم من إله غيره هو أنشأكم من الأرض واستعمركم فيها فاستغفروه ثم توبوا إليه إن ربي قريب مجيب

translation: They said, "O Salih, you were among us a man of promise before this. Do you forbid us to worship what our fathers worshipped? And indeed we are, about that to which you invite us, in disquieting doubt."
interpretation: This verse reflects the resistance and skepticism of Salih's people towards his message of monotheism. They question his authority to forbid them from worshipping the idols that their ancestors had worshipped, and express their doubts about the truth of his teachings. This highlights the challenges faced by prophets in conveying the message of Islam to people who are deeply entrenched in their traditional beliefs and practices. It also emphasizes the importance of faith and conviction in the face of doubt and opposition.
orig: قالوا يا صالح قد كنت فينا مرجوا قبل هذا أتنهانا أن نعبد ما يعبد آباؤنا وإننا لفي شك مما تدعونا إليه مريب

translation: He said, "O my people, have you considered if I am upon clear evidence from my Lord and He has given me mercy from Himself, who would protect me from Allah if I disobeyed Him? So you would not increase me except in loss."
interpretation: In this verse, the prophet is appealing to his people to consider his position carefully. He asserts that he is acting on clear guidance and mercy from Allah. As such, if he were to disobey Allah by abandoning his mission, no one could protect him from Allah's punishment. He argues that by asking him to go against Allah, they are only inviting loss upon him. The verse highlights the prophet's firm conviction, his sense of duty towards Allah above all else, and serves as an attempt to make his people reflect on the ramifications of rejecting the divine message. It underscores that the prophet has no choice but to obey Allah, and cannot yield to any pressure to the contrary.
orig: قال يا قوم أرأيتم إن كنت على بينة من ربي وآتاني منه رحمة فمن ينصرني من الله إن عصيته فما تزيدونني غير تخسير

translation: O my people, this is the she-camel of Allah, a sign for you. Let her graze in Allah's land and do not touch her with harm, lest a near punishment seizes you.
interpretation: This verse is a warning from the prophet Salih to his people, the Thamud, who were demanding a miracle as proof of his prophethood. Allah sent a miraculous she-camel as a sign for them. Salih instructed his people to allow the camel to graze freely on Allah's land and not to harm her in any way. This was a test of their faith and obedience to Allah. Salih warned them that if they were to harm the camel, a severe punishment from Allah would befall them very soon. The verse emphasizes the consequences of rejecting Allah's signs and disobeying His messengers. It also highlights the importance of treating Allah's creatures with respect and compassion.
orig: ويا قوم هذه ناقة الله لكم آية فذروها تأكل في أرض الله ولا تمسوها بسوء فيأخذكم عذاب قريب

translation: So they hamstrung her. Then he said, "Enjoy yourselves in your homes for three days. That is a promise not to be denied."
interpretation: This verse is a warning to the people of Thamud, who were given a miraculous she-camel as a sign from God. However, they disobeyed and killed the camel. As a consequence, the prophet Salih told them that they would have only three more days to enjoy their lives before the divine punishment would befall them. This interpretation highlights the importance of obeying God's signs and the severe consequences of disobedience. It also emphasizes the certainty of God's promise, whether it is a promise of reward for the righteous or punishment for the wrongdoers.
orig: فعقروها فقال تمتعوا في داركم ثلاثة أيام ذلك وعد غير مكذوب

translation: So when Our command came, We saved Salih and those who believed with him, by mercy from Us, and [saved them] from the disgrace of that day. Indeed, it is your Lord who is the Powerful, the Exalted in Might.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the power and might of Allah in saving the believers from destruction and disgrace. It shows that when Allah's decree comes to pass, He has the ability to protect and rescue those who have faith and follow His guidance, even in the face of great adversity or punishment. The verse also highlights the mercy and compassion of Allah towards His faithful servants, as He saves them from humiliation and grants them honor and dignity. Ultimately, it reinforces the idea that true strength and power belong to Allah alone, and those who align themselves with His will shall be saved and successful, both in this life and the Hereafter.
orig: فلما جاء أمرنا نجينا صالحا والذين آمنوا معه برحمة منا ومن خزي يومئذ إن ربك هو القوي العزيز

translation: But the shriek seized those who had wronged, and they became within their homes [corpses] fallen prone.
interpretation: This verse refers to the fate of those who rejected the message of Allah and His prophets. They were seized by a sudden, overwhelming punishment that left them lying dead in their homes. It serves as a warning to those who persist in wrongdoing and disbelief, reminding them that the consequences of their actions will catch up with them when they least expect it. The verse also highlights the power and justice of Allah, who will not allow the evildoers to escape the consequences of their deeds.
orig: وأخذ الذين ظلموا الصيحة فأصبحوا في ديارهم جاثمين

translation: As if they had never prospered therein. Unquestionably, Thamud denied their Lord; then, away with Thamud.
interpretation: This verse is a reminder of the fate that befell the people of Thamud, an ancient Arab tribe, due to their disbelief and disobedience to Allah. Despite the blessings and prosperity they enjoyed, they rejected the message of their prophet, Salih, and continued in their wrongdoing. As a result, Allah destroyed them, leaving no trace of their existence, as if they had never lived there at all. The verse emphasizes that their denial of Allah led to their ultimate doom and serves as a warning to others who might follow in their footsteps. The phrase "away with Thamud" is a declaration of their distance from Allah's mercy and a condemnation of their actions.
orig: كأن لم يغنوا فيها ألا إن ثمود كفروا ربهم ألا بعدا لثمود

translation: And certainly did Our messengers come to Abraham with good tidings; they said, "Peace." He said, "Peace," and did not delay in bringing [them] a roasted calf.
interpretation: This verse highlights Abraham's hospitality and generosity towards his guests, who were actually angels sent by God. Despite not knowing their true identity, Abraham welcomed them warmly and immediately prepared a roasted calf for them. This act of kindness demonstrates the importance of treating guests with respect and providing for their needs, even if they are strangers. It also shows Abraham's readiness to serve others and his willingness to share his blessings with those around him. The verse emphasizes the virtues of hospitality, generosity, and kindness, which are highly regarded in Islam.
orig: ولقد جاءت رسلنا إبراهيم بالبشرى قالوا سلاما قال سلام فما لبث أن جاء بعجل حنيذ

translation: And when he saw their hands not reaching for it, he distrusted them and felt from them apprehension. They said, "Fear not. We have been sent to the people of Lot."
interpretation: This verse is referring to the angels who visited Prophet Abraham in the form of men. When they did not eat the food he offered them, which was a sign of goodwill and hospitality, Abraham became suspicious and afraid of them. The angels then reassured him that he should not fear, as they were sent as messengers to Prophet Lot's people to warn them of the impending punishment for their sins and transgressions. This highlights the importance of hospitality in the Islamic tradition, as well as the role of angels as messengers and agents of divine will.
orig: فلما رأى أيديهم لا تصل إليه نكرهم وأوجس منهم خيفة قالوا لا تخف إنا أرسلنا إلى قوم لوط

translation: And his wife was standing, and she smiled. Then We gave her good tidings of Isaac and after Isaac, Jacob.
interpretation: This verse highlights the power and mercy of Allah in granting the gift of children to Abraham and Sarah despite their old age. Sarah's laughter upon hearing the news is interpreted as a sign of joy and amazement at the miraculous nature of the announcement. The mention of Isaac and Jacob in the glad tidings emphasizes the continuation of prophethood and the establishment of a righteous lineage. This verse demonstrates that nothing is impossible for Allah and that His blessings can come in the most unexpected ways. It also serves as a reminder to have faith in Allah's plan and to trust in His wisdom, even in the face of seemingly impossible circumstances.
orig: وامرأته قائمة فضحكت فبشرناها بإسحاق ومن وراء إسحاق يعقوب

translation: She said, "Woe to me! Shall I bear a child while I am an old woman and this, my husband, is an old man? Indeed this is an amazing thing!"
interpretation: This verse expresses the astonishment and disbelief of Sarah, the wife of Prophet Abraham, upon receiving the news from the angels that she would bear a child in her old age. It highlights the miraculous nature of the event, as it is beyond the natural course of life for an elderly couple to have a child. The verse also emphasizes the power and will of Allah, who can make anything happen, even that which seems impossible to human beings. It is a reminder that Allah's plans and decrees supersede the limitations of human understanding and expectations.
orig: قالت يا ويلتى أألد وأنا عجوز وهذا بعلي شيخا إن هذا لشيء عجيب

translation: They said, "Are you amazed at the decree of Allah? May the mercy of Allah and His blessings be upon you, people of the house. Indeed, He is Praiseworthy and Honorable."
interpretation: This verse highlights the idea that one should not be surprised or amazed by the decree or will of Allah. It emphasizes that Allah's mercy and blessings are upon the righteous people, particularly the family of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him), referred to as the "people of the house". The verse also affirms two important attributes of Allah: that He is Praiseworthy, meaning He is deserving of all praise and gratitude, and that He is Honorable, indicating His majesty, glory, and nobility. It serves as a reminder to have faith in Allah's wisdom and to trust in His plans, even if they may sometimes be unexpected or difficult to understand.
orig: قالوا أتعجبين من أمر الله رحمت الله وبركاته عليكم أهل البيت إنه حميد مجيد

translation: And when the fright had left Abraham and the good tidings had reached him, he began to argue with Us concerning the people of Lot.
interpretation: This verse shows the compassion and concern that Prophet Abraham (peace be upon him) had for the people, even those who were engaged in grave sins like the people of Lot. Despite receiving the good news about being granted a son, Abraham did not forget the plight of Lot's people. He tried to plead and argue with Allah to give them more respite and chance to repent, hoping that the punishment may be averted from them if they mend their ways. This highlights Abraham's immense compassion, his caring attitude even towards the sinners, and his role as an active intercessor for humanity. It's an example for believers to have concern for fellow humans and make efforts for their guidance and reformation.
orig: فلما ذهب عن إبراهيم الروع وجاءته البشرى يجادلنا في قوم لوط

translation: Indeed, Abraham was forbearing, tenderly penitent [to Allah], and devoutly turning [to Him].
interpretation: This verse highlights the exemplary qualities of Prophet Abraham (peace be upon him). He was patient and forbearing in the face of adversities and challenges. He was also tenderly penitent, constantly seeking Allah's forgiveness and turning to Him in repentance. Abraham's devotion and submission to Allah were evident in his unwavering commitment to monotheism and his readiness to sacrifice his son in obedience to Allah's command. These characteristics made him a role model for believers, emphasizing the importance of patience, repentance, and complete submission to Allah's will in the life of a believer.
orig: إن إبراهيم لحليم أواه منيب

translation: O Ibrahim, give up this [plea]. Indeed, the command of your Lord has come, and indeed, there will reach them a punishment that cannot be repelled.
interpretation: This verse is addressing Prophet Ibrahim (Abraham) and asking him to abandon his plea to save the people of Lut (Lot) from the impending punishment. It emphasizes that Allah's decree has already been issued, and the sinful people will face an inevitable punishment that cannot be averted. The interpretation suggests that once Allah's command is given, it will come to pass, and no intercession or plea can change the fate of those who have persistently disobeyed and transgressed the boundaries set by Allah. It also highlights the finality and certainty of Allah's judgment upon those who have earned His wrath through their actions.
orig: يا إبراهيم أعرض عن هذا إنه قد جاء أمر ربك وإنهم آتيهم عذاب غير مردود

translation: And when Our messengers came to Lot, he was distressed for them and felt for them great discomfort. He said, "This is a distressful day."
interpretation: This verse shows the great concern and care that the prophet Lot (peace be upon him) had for his guests, who were actually angels sent by Allah. Despite the difficult situation he was in with his people, Lot prioritized the safety and well-being of his guests. He felt a sense of responsibility towards them and was deeply distressed by the potential harm that could befall them from his own people. This highlights the importance of hospitality, protection of guests, and standing up for what is right, even in the face of adversity. It also demonstrates the compassionate nature of the prophets and their willingness to put others before themselves.
orig: ولما جاءت رسلنا لوطا سيء بهم وضاق بهم ذرعا وقال هذا يوم عصيب

translation: And his people came hastening to him, and before this they had been doing evil deeds. He said: O my people! Here are my daughters! They are purer for you. So guard against (the punishment of) Allah and do not disgrace me about my guests. Is there not among you one right-minded man?
interpretation: This verse is a reminder that even in the face of societal pressure and the temptation to engage in immoral acts, one must remain steadfast in their faith and adhere to the teachings of Allah. The people of Lot were known for their evil deeds, yet when Lot offered them a pure alternative in marriage to his daughters, they refused and continued in their ways. This serves as a lesson that we must always strive to choose the path of righteousness, even when it may be unpopular or difficult. Additionally, the verse highlights the importance of treating guests with respect and not bringing shame upon them, as this is a fundamental aspect of Islamic hospitality and etiquette.
orig: وجاءه قومه يهرعون إليه ومن قبل كانوا يعملون السيئات قال يا قوم هؤلاء بناتي هن أطهر لكم فاتقوا الله ولا تخزون في ضيفي أليس منكم رجل رشيد

translation: They said, "You have already known that we have not concerning your daughters any claim, and indeed, you know what we want."
interpretation: The people of Lut (Lot) responded to his pleas by saying that he knew full well they had no interest or desire for his daughters, and that he was also aware of their true evil intentions towards the male guests he was hosting. This verse highlights the depths of their depravity and their open defiance of Lut's attempts to dissuade them from their sinful ways. It shows that they were fully conscious of the immorality of their actions but persisted in them anyway, ignoring Lut's warnings and the opportunity he provided them to turn away from their transgression.
orig: قالوا لقد علمت ما لنا في بناتك من حق وإنك لتعلم ما نريد

translation: He said, "If only I had strength against you, or could take refuge in a strong support."
interpretation: This verse is expressing the sentiment of someone who feels powerless against a stronger force or group. They wish that they had the strength to stand up to this opposition, or at least a strong support or ally to turn to for protection and help. It conveys a sense of vulnerability and a desire for empowerment or aid in the face of a threat or challenge that seems beyond one's own capacities to confront alone. The "strong support" could be interpreted as a powerful backer, a fortified place of safety, or even one's faith and trust in God's help and protection when feeling weak and exposed to danger.
orig: قال لو أن لي بكم قوة أو آوي إلى ركن شديد

translation: They said, "O Lot, indeed we are messengers of your Lord; [therefore], they will never reach you. So set out with your family during a portion of the night and let not any among you look back - except your wife; indeed, she will be struck by that which strikes them. Indeed, their appointment is [for] the morning. Is not the morning near?"
interpretation: This verse is a divine assurance to Prophet Lot (peace be upon him) that he and his believing family members will be saved from the impending punishment that will befall his people due to their sinful actions. The angels, who were sent as messengers, instruct Lot to leave the city with his family during the night without looking back. However, his wife, who was among the disbelievers, would face the same fate as the rest of the sinful people. The verse emphasizes the nearness of the appointed time for the punishment, which was to take place in the morning, indicating that the disbelievers' judgment was imminent and inescapable.
orig: قالوا يا لوط إنا رسل ربك لن يصلوا إليك فأسر بأهلك بقطع من الليل ولا يلتفت منكم أحد إلا امرأتك إنه مصيبها ما أصابهم إن موعدهم الصبح أليس الصبح بقريب

translation: So when Our command came, We made the highest part [of the city] its lowest and rained upon them stones of layered hard clay, [which were]
interpretation: This verse refers to the destruction of the people of Lut (Lot) due to their persistence in immoral and sinful behavior. When Allah's command came to destroy them, He caused a great upheaval in their city, turning it upside down and raining upon them stones of baked clay. This interpretation highlights the severe consequences of disobeying Allah and engaging in wickedness, serving as a reminder for people to abstain from such actions and to follow the righteous path to avoid a similar fate.
orig: فلما جاء أمرنا جعلنا عاليها سافلها وأمطرنا عليها حجارة من سجيل منضود

translation: Marked in the presence of your Lord, and not far from the wrongdoers.
interpretation: This verse refers to the punishment that awaits the wrongdoers in the Hereafter. The phrase "marked in the presence of your Lord" indicates that their deeds are recorded and known to Allah, and they will be held accountable for them. The verse also emphasizes the proximity of the punishment, suggesting that it is not far off or unlikely to happen. It serves as a warning to those who engage in wrongdoing and oppression, reminding them that their actions will have consequences and that divine justice will ultimately prevail.
orig: مسومة عند ربك وما هي من الظالمين ببعيد

translation: And to [the people of] Madyan [We sent] their brother Shu'ayb. He said, "O my people, worship Allah; you have no deity other than Him. And do not decrease from the measure and the scale. Indeed, I see you in prosperity, but indeed, I fear for you the punishment of an all-encompassing Day.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of worshipping Allah alone and being honest in business dealings. Shu'ayb, as a prophet sent to the people of Madyan, reminds them that their prosperity is a blessing from Allah and that they should not engage in fraudulent practices such as giving short measures or weights. He warns them of the consequences of their actions, fearing that they may face a severe punishment on the Day of Judgment that will encompass them entirely. This interpretation highlights the Islamic principles of Tawheed (oneness of Allah) and the importance of ethical conduct in commerce and everyday life.
orig: وإلى مدين أخاهم شعيبا قال يا قوم اعبدوا الله ما لكم من إله غيره ولا تنقصوا المكيال والميزان إني أراكم بخير وإني أخاف عليكم عذاب يوم محيط

translation: And O my people, give full measure and weight in justice and do not deprive the people of their due and do not commit abuse on the earth, spreading corruption.
interpretation: This verse is a call to uphold justice and fairness in all dealings, especially in matters of trade and commerce. It emphasizes the importance of giving people their full due, without shortchanging them or engaging in fraudulent practices. The verse also warns against spreading corruption and causing harm on earth through unjust and unethical conduct. It highlights the Islamic principles of honesty, integrity, and social responsibility, urging believers to establish a society based on justice and righteousness. The message is clear: as individuals and as a community, we must strive to maintain the highest moral standards and treat others with fairness and respect, in order to prevent corruption and create a harmonious, God-conscious society.
orig: ويا قوم أوفوا المكيال والميزان بالقسط ولا تبخسوا الناس أشياءهم ولا تعثوا في الأرض مفسدين

translation: What remains [lawful] from Allah is best for you, if you would be believers. But I am not a guardian over you.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that what Allah has made lawful and permissible is ultimately better for the believers than what they may desire or deem beneficial according to their own understanding. It serves as a reminder to trust in Allah's wisdom and guidance, even if it may not align with personal inclinations or societal norms. The verse also clarifies that the Prophet's role is to convey the message and not to force people to follow it or be held accountable for their actions, as that is a matter between each individual and Allah.
orig: بقيت الله خير لكم إن كنتم مؤمنين وما أنا عليكم بحفيظ

translation: They said, "O Shu'ayb, does your prayer command you that we should leave what our fathers worship or not do with our wealth what we please? Indeed, you are the forbearing, the discerning!"
interpretation: This verse reflects the attitude of Shu'ayb's people towards his message. They sarcastically question whether his prayers have commanded him to ask them to abandon their ancestral idols and traditions, and to dictate how they should spend their wealth. They mock him by calling him "forbearing" and "discerning", implying that his teachings are foolish and unreasonable. This highlights their arrogance, attachment to their old ways, and resistance to the truth that Shu'ayb brings. It shows how people can be blinded by their desires and traditions, rejecting divine guidance in favor of their own whims and interests.
orig: قالوا يا شعيب أصلاتك تأمرك أن نترك ما يعبد آباؤنا أو أن نفعل في أموالنا ما نشاء إنك لأنت الحليم الرشيد

translation: He said, "O my people, have you considered if I am upon clear evidence from my Lord and He has provided me with a good provision from Him? And I do not intend to differ from you in that which I have forbidden you; I only intend reform as much as I am able. And my success is not but through Allah. Upon Him I have relied, and to Him I return."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of following divine guidance and the Prophet's role in conveying it. The Prophet is not seeking personal gain or power, but rather desires to guide his people to what is best for them, even if it means forbidding them from certain practices. He recognizes that true success and guidance can only come from reliance upon Allah. The verse underscores the sincerity and humility that should characterize a leader who is calling people to righteousness.
orig: قال يا قوم أرأيتم إن كنت على بينة من ربي ورزقني منه رزقا حسنا وما أريد أن أخالفكم إلى ما أنهاكم عنه إن أريد إلا الإصلاح ما استطعت وما توفيقي إلا بالله عليه توكلت وإليه أنيب

translation: And O my people, let not [your] dissension from me cause you to be struck by that similar to what struck the people of Noah or the people of Hud or the people of Salih. And the people of Lot are not from you far away.
interpretation: This verse is a warning from the Prophet to his people, urging them not to let their opposition and enmity towards him lead them to a fate similar to that of previous nations who rejected their prophets. He reminds them of the consequences faced by the people of Noah, Hud, Salih, and Lot, who were punished for their disobedience and rejection of divine message. The Prophet emphasizes that the people of Lot, in particular, were not far removed from them in time and location, serving as a stark reminder of the nearness of God's punishment for those who persist in disbelief and opposition to His messengers. The verse underscores the importance of heeding the Prophet's warning and avoiding the mistakes of past nations.
orig: ويا قوم لا يجرمنكم شقاقي أن يصيبكم مثل ما أصاب قوم نوح أو قوم هود أو قوم صالح وما قوم لوط منكم ببعيد

translation: And ask forgiveness of your Lord and then repent to Him. Indeed, my Lord is Merciful and Affectionate.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of seeking forgiveness from Allah and turning to Him in sincere repentance. It highlights two of Allah's beautiful names: Ar-Raheem (the Most Merciful) and Al-Wadud (the Most Loving). The interpretation is that Allah, in His infinite mercy and love, is always ready to forgive those who sincerely repent and seek His forgiveness. It encourages believers to recognize their shortcomings, feel remorse for their sins, and turn back to Allah with a resolute intention to obey Him and refrain from wrongdoing. The verse also implies that repentance is a continuous process, as humans are prone to making mistakes, and that Allah's door of forgiveness is always open for those who sincerely turn to Him.
orig: واستغفروا ربكم ثم توبوا إليه إن ربي رحيم ودود

translation: They said, "O Shu'ayb, we do not understand much of what you say, and indeed, we consider you among us as weak. And if not for your family, we would have stoned you [to death]; and you are not to us one respected."
interpretation: This verse reflects the arrogance and stubbornness of the people of Madyan towards their prophet Shu'ayb. They belittled his message, considering it incomprehensible, and viewed Shu'ayb himself as weak and powerless. They even threatened to stone him to death if it were not for the protection of his clan. This shows their complete disregard for Shu'ayb's prophethood and their attachment to their own misguided ways. It highlights the challenges faced by prophets in conveying the divine message to obstinate communities who are deeply entrenched in their wrongdoings and resist any call for change or reform.
orig: قالوا يا شعيب ما نفقه كثيرا مما تقول وإنا لنراك فينا ضعيفا ولولا رهطك لرجمناك وما أنت علينا بعزيز

translation: He said, "O my people, is my family more respected for you than Allah? But you put Him behind your backs. Indeed, my Lord is encompassing of what you do."
interpretation: In this verse, the prophet Shu'ayb is addressing his people, who were more concerned with maintaining their worldly ties and relationships than obeying Allah's commands. He reminds them that Allah should be given the utmost importance and priority in their lives, and that nothing should be held in higher regard than Him. Shu'ayb also warns his people that Allah is fully aware of their actions and will hold them accountable for their deeds. This verse emphasizes the importance of putting one's faith and obedience to Allah above all else, and serves as a reminder that Allah is always watching and will judge us based on our actions.
orig: قال يا قوم أرهطي أعز عليكم من الله واتخذتموه وراءكم ظهريا إن ربي بما تعملون محيط

translation: And O my people, work according to your position; indeed, I am working. You are going to know to whom will come a punishment that will disgrace him and who is a liar. So watch; indeed, I am with you a watcher [over you].
interpretation: This verse is a warning from the Prophet to his people, telling them to continue in their ways while he continues in his. He warns them that a punishment will come to the disbelievers that will disgrace them, exposing their lies. He tells them to wait and watch for this punishment, just as he too is waiting and watching. It conveys a sense of confidence on the part of the Prophet that he is on the right path and that the disbelievers will be proven wrong in time with the coming of God's judgment. It also contains an element of a threat or challenge to the disbelievers.
orig: ويا قوم اعملوا على مكانتكم إني عامل سوف تعلمون من يأتيه عذاب يخزيه ومن هو كاذب وارتقبوا إني معكم رقيب

translation: And when Our command came, We saved Shu'ayb and those who believed with him, by mercy from Us. And the shriek seized those who had wronged, and they became within their homes [corpses] fallen prone.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the fate of those who reject the message of Allah and His prophets. When the divine decree comes to pass, Allah saves the believers through His mercy, while the wrongdoers face a terrible punishment. The "shriek" mentioned here could refer to a mighty blast or a deafening noise that strikes the evildoers, causing their destruction. It also emphasizes that no one can escape Allah's judgment and that the ultimate abode of the disbelievers is a state of humiliation and lifelessness, represented by their lying dead in their very homes. The verse serves as a reminder for people to heed the warnings of the prophets and to follow the path of righteousness before it is too late.
orig: ولما جاء أمرنا نجينا شعيبا والذين آمنوا معه برحمة منا وأخذت الذين ظلموا الصيحة فأصبحوا في ديارهم جاثمين

translation: As if they had never prospered therein. Then, away with Madyan, just as Thamud had perished.
interpretation: This verse is a warning to the people of Madyan, who were destroyed by Allah due to their persistent wrongdoing and rejection of His messages. It emphasizes the complete destruction of their civilization, to the point that it seemed as if they had never existed or prospered in their land. The verse also draws a parallel to the fate of the people of Thamud, another nation that was destroyed for their disobedience to Allah. This serves as a reminder that no matter how powerful or prosperous a nation may be, if they turn away from the path of righteousness and reject the guidance of Allah, they will face a similar fate of destruction and oblivion.
orig: كأن لم يغنوا فيها ألا بعدا لمدين كما بعدت ثمود

translation: And indeed, We sent Moses with Our signs and a clear authority
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the divine mission of Prophet Moses, who was sent by Allah with clear signs and undeniable proofs of his prophethood. The "clear authority" mentioned in the verse refers to the compelling evidence and miracles that Moses was granted to support his message and convince his people of the truth. This interpretation highlights the importance of prophets being supported by divine signs and authority to establish the legitimacy of their mission and to guide their communities towards the path of righteousness.
orig: ولقد أرسلنا موسى بآياتنا وسلطان مبين

translation: To Pharaoh and his establishment, but they followed the command of Pharaoh, and the command of Pharaoh was not [at all] discerning.
interpretation: This verse highlights the blind following of Pharaoh's commands by his people, despite the fact that his orders were misguided and lacked wisdom. It emphasizes the importance of using one's own discernment and not simply following authority figures blindly, especially when their actions go against divine guidance. The verse also implies that leaders have a responsibility to guide their followers righteously, and that there will be consequences for those who lead others astray.
orig: إلى فرعون وملئه فاتبعوا أمر فرعون وما أمر فرعون برشيد

translation: He will lead his people on the Day of Resurrection and lead them into the Fire. And wretched is the place to which they are led.
interpretation: This verse warns about misleading leaders who will lead their followers astray on Judgment Day, ultimately causing them to enter Hell. It emphasizes the grave responsibility of leadership and the severe consequences for those who misguide others away from the straight path. The verse also highlights the terrible nature of Hell, describing it as a "wretched" destination. It serves as a reminder for people to be cautious about whom they follow and to strive to be righteous leaders themselves.
orig: يقدم قومه يوم القيامة فأوردهم النار وبئس الورد المورود

translation: And they were pursued by a curse in this [life] and on the Day of Resurrection. How wretched is the gift which is given.
interpretation: This verse refers to the punishment that befalls those who reject faith and oppose the messengers of Allah. They are not only cursed in this worldly life, but this curse extends to the Day of Judgment as well. The "gift" here ironically refers to the curse and punishment - it is a terrible gift indeed that they have earned through their misdeeds. The verse emphasizes the severity and permanence of the consequences that the deniers of truth bring upon themselves by their actions in this world.
orig: وأتبعوا في هذه لعنة ويوم القيامة بئس الرفد المرفود

translation: That is from the news of the cities, We relate it to you. Among them are those that stand and those mowed down.
interpretation: This verse speaks to the idea that Allah conveys to Prophet Muhammad the stories and histories of past nations and civilizations. Some of these places still stand, with their ruins bearing witness to their existence, while others have been completely destroyed and "mowed down" due to their transgressions and defiance of Allah's messages. It's a reminder that the ultimate fate of any community lies with Allah based on their deeds and that the Quran contains valuable lessons from the past for our guidance.
orig: ذلك من أنباء القرى نقصه عليك منها قائم وحصيد

translation: And We did not wrong them, but they wronged themselves. And their gods on whom they called besides Allah did not avail them in the least when there came the command of your Lord, nor did they add to them other than ruin.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah does not wrong people, but rather they wrong themselves through their own actions and choices. It also highlights the futility of worshipping false gods or idols, as they are powerless and cannot help or benefit their worshippers in any way, especially when faced with Allah's decree. Instead of providing aid or support, these false objects of worship only lead to further loss and destruction for those who rely on them. The verse serves as a reminder to focus on worshipping Allah alone and to avoid ascribing partners to Him, as doing so will ultimately lead to ruin and regret.
orig: وما ظلمناهم ولكن ظلموا أنفسهم فما أغنت عنهم آلهتهم التي يدعون من دون الله من شيء لما جاء أمر ربك وما زادوهم غير تتبيب

translation: And thus is the seizure of your Lord when He seizes the cities while they are committing wrong. Indeed, His seizure is painful and severe.
interpretation: This verse is a warning to those who commit injustice and wrongdoing. It emphasizes that when Allah decides to punish a community for their transgressions, His punishment is severe and painful. The verse implies that Allah's justice will catch up with the wrongdoers, even if they are living in cities and think they are secure. It serves as a reminder that no one can escape Allah's judgment and that the consequences of oppression and injustice will be faced in this world or in the Hereafter. The verse encourages people to be mindful of their actions and to strive for justice and righteousness to avoid incurring Allah's wrath.
orig: وكذلك أخذ ربك إذا أخذ القرى وهي ظالمة إن أخذه أليم شديد

translation: Indeed in that is a sign for those who fear the punishment of the Hereafter. That is a Day for which the people will be collected, and that is a Day [which will be] witnessed.
interpretation: This verse is a reminder and a warning to those who believe in the Day of Judgment and fear Allah's punishment in the Hereafter. It emphasizes the significance and inevitability of that Day, when all of humanity will be gathered together to face the consequences of their deeds in this world. The verse also highlights the fact that the Day of Judgment will be witnessed by all, and there will be no escape or hiding from the ultimate truth and justice of Allah. This should serve as a motivation for believers to lead righteous lives and strive for Allah's mercy and forgiveness.
orig: إن في ذلك لآية لمن خاف عذاب الآخرة ذلك يوم مجموع له الناس وذلك يوم مشهود

translation: And We do not delay it except for a limited term.
interpretation: This verse suggests that everything happens according to God's predetermined plan and timeline. The events in this world, whether good or bad, are not delayed except until the appointed time that God has set. It emphasizes the idea of divine destiny and that ultimately, God is in control of everything and His wisdom and knowledge encompass all things. Believers should trust in His timing and plan, knowing that He is the best disposer of affairs.
orig: وما نؤخره إلا لأجل معدود

translation: The Day it comes, no soul will speak except by His permission, and among them will be the wretched and the prosperous.
interpretation: This verse refers to the Day of Judgment when all souls will stand before Allah. On that day, no one will be able to speak or intercede on behalf of another except with the permission of Allah. The people will be divided into two groups: the wretched ones who will face the consequences of their evil deeds and the prosperous ones who will be rewarded for their righteousness and faith. This verse emphasizes the absolute authority of Allah on the Day of Judgment and the ultimate fate of every individual based on their deeds in this world.
orig: يوم يأت لا تكلم نفس إلا بإذنه فمنهم شقي وسعيد

translation: As for those who are wretched, they will be in the Fire. For them therein is [violent] exhaling and inhaling.
interpretation: This verse speaks about the fate of those who are miserable and wretched in the Hereafter. They will be condemned to the Fire of Hell, where they will experience extreme suffering and anguish. The "violent exhaling and inhaling" mentioned in the verse refers to the sounds of their painful sighs and cries as they are tormented in the flames. This interpretation emphasizes the severity of the punishment that awaits those who have earned God's wrath through their disbelief and evil deeds in this world. It serves as a warning to humanity to strive for righteousness and avoid the path that leads to such a dreadful outcome in the afterlife.
orig: فأما الذين شقوا ففي النار لهم فيها زفير وشهيق

translation: They will abide therein as long as the heavens and the earth endure, except what your Lord wills. Indeed, your Lord is the doer of what He intends.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the eternal nature of the afterlife, indicating that those who enter Paradise or Hell will remain there permanently, as long as the heavens and earth exist. However, it also acknowledges the ultimate authority of Allah, who has the power to change this if He so wills. The verse highlights the idea that Allah's will is absolute and that He can do whatever He intends, emphasizing His omnipotence and sovereignty over all creation.
orig: خالدين فيها ما دامت السماوات والأرض إلا ما شاء ربك إن ربك فعال لما يريد

translation: And as for those who were blessed, they will be in Paradise, abiding therein as long as the heavens and the earth endure, except what your Lord wills - a bestowal uninterrupted.
interpretation: This verse speaks about the eternal reward for the righteous believers in Paradise. They will dwell there forever, as long as the heavens and earth exist, except for what Allah wills. This indicates that their stay in Paradise is not limited by time and will last for eternity. The phrase "except what your Lord wills" denotes that the eternal stay in Paradise is subject to Allah's will and power, emphasizing His absolute authority over all matters. The verse also describes the blessings in Paradise as "a bestowal uninterrupted," meaning that the rewards will be continuous, abundant, and never-ending, highlighting the immense generosity and mercy of Allah towards His righteous servants.
orig: وأما الذين سعدوا ففي الجنة خالدين فيها ما دامت السماوات والأرض إلا ما شاء ربك عطاء غير مجذوذ

translation: So do not be in doubt, [O Muhammad], as to what these [polytheists] are worshipping. They worship not except as their fathers worshipped before. And indeed, We will give them their share undiminished.
interpretation: This verse is addressing the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him), telling him not to have any doubts about the nature of the worship of the polytheists. They are not worshipping anything new or unique, but rather following the misguided practices of their forefathers before them in blindly worshipping false idols and deities other than Allah. The verse affirms that Allah will requite these polytheists fully for their deeds and actions without any reduction in the recompense they have earned, emphasizing divine justice. It warns against being misled by ancestral traditions that go against the pure monotheism of Islam.
orig: فلا تك في مرية مما يعبد هؤلاء ما يعبدون إلا كما يعبد آباؤهم من قبل وإنا لموفوهم نصيبهم غير منقوص

translation: And We had certainly given Moses the Scripture, but it came under disagreement. And if not for a word that preceded from your Lord, it would have been concluded between them. And indeed they are, concerning the Qur'an, in disquieting doubt.
interpretation: This verse highlights the fact that even though God sent down revelation and scripture to Moses, people still differed and disagreed about it. This shows the tendency of human beings to dispute and doubt even in matters of divine revelation. The verse implies that had God not already decreed to delay judgment until the appointed time, He could have settled these disputes and removed all doubts immediately. However, God in His wisdom allows people to exercise free will and lets matters run their course until the time He has predetermined for final judgment. So the disagreements and doubts will persist until that time. The verse subtly warns that those who doubt the Qur'an are in a similarly precarious position of disquieting doubt, because the Qur'an is also divine revelation, and opposing it or doubting it is risky as judgment is inevitable.
orig: ولقد آتينا موسى الكتاب فاختلف فيه ولولا كلمة سبقت من ربك لقضي بينهم وإنهم لفي شك منه مريب

translation: And indeed, each [of them] - your Lord will fully compensate them for their deeds. Indeed, He is Acquainted with what they do.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the concept of divine justice and accountability. It assures that every individual will be fully compensated by Allah for their deeds, whether good or bad. The use of the word "ليوفينهم" (will fully compensate them) indicates the completeness and perfection of Allah's justice. The verse also highlights Allah's omniscience, as He is fully aware of all actions performed by His servants. This serves as a reminder for believers to be mindful of their deeds, knowing that nothing escapes Allah's knowledge and that they will be held accountable for their actions in the Hereafter.
orig: وإن كلا لما ليوفينهم ربك أعمالهم إنه بما يعملون خبير

translation: So remain on a right course as you have been commanded, [you] and those who have turned back with you [to Allah], and do not transgress. Indeed, He is Seeing of what you do.
interpretation: This verse is a command from Allah to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and the believers to remain steadfast in their faith and to follow the straight path that Allah has ordained for them. It emphasizes the importance of staying true to the teachings of Islam and not deviating from them, even in the face of challenges or temptations. The verse also serves as a reminder that Allah is always watching over us and is aware of all our actions, both good and bad. It encourages us to be mindful of our deeds and to strive to do what is right and pleasing to Allah.
orig: فاستقم كما أمرت ومن تاب معك ولا تطغوا إنه بما تعملون بصير

translation: And do not incline toward those who do wrong, lest you be touched by the Fire, and you would not have other than Allah any protectors; then you would not be helped.
interpretation: This verse warns believers against forming close alliances or relationships with wrongdoers and oppressors. Inclining towards them or supporting them may lead to facing the consequences of their actions, symbolized by being touched by the Fire. It emphasizes that if one falls into such a situation due to their inclination towards the wrongdoers, they will have no protectors or helpers besides Allah. This highlights the importance of being cautious about the company one keeps and the potential spiritual and worldly repercussions of associating with those who engage in injustice and wrongdoing.
orig: ولا تركنوا إلى الذين ظلموا فتمسكم النار وما لكم من دون الله من أولياء ثم لا تنصرون

translation: And establish prayer at the two ends of the day and at the approach of the night. Indeed, good deeds do away with misdeeds. That is a reminder for those who remember.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of establishing regular prayers throughout the day and night. The "two ends of the day" refer to the morning (Fajr) and evening (Maghrib and Isha) prayers, while the "approach of the night" refers to the afternoon (Dhuhr and Asr) prayers. The verse also highlights the power of good deeds in erasing one's sins and misdeeds. Performing righteous acts, such as prayer, charity, and kindness, can help counterbalance and even erase the negative effects of one's past wrongdoings. This serves as a reminder and encouragement for the believers to constantly engage in remembrance of Allah and strive to perform good deeds consistently.
orig: وأقم الصلاة طرفي النهار وزلفا من الليل إن الحسنات يذهبن السيئات ذلك ذكرى للذاكرين

translation: And be patient, for indeed, Allah does not allow to be lost the reward of those who do good.
interpretation: This verse encourages believers to remain patient and steadfast in the face of difficulties and challenges, with the assurance that Allah will not let the efforts and good deeds of those who strive for righteousness go to waste.
