It emphasizes the importance of perseverance and trust in Allah's plan, knowing that He will ultimately reward those who consistently do good and remain patient in adversity. The verse serves as a reminder that the path of righteousness may not always be easy, but the reward for those who stay the course will be immense in the sight of Allah.
orig: واصبر فإن الله لا يضيع أجر المحسنين

translation: So why were there not among the generations before you those of enduring discrimination forbidding corruption on earth - except a few of those We saved from among them? But those who wronged pursued what luxury they were given therein, and they were criminals.
interpretation: This verse is a reminder that throughout history, there have been very few people who have stood up against corruption and wrongdoing in society. Most people, especially those who are privileged and enjoy luxury, tend to ignore or even participate in the corruption. They pursue their own pleasures and comforts even if it means committing crimes and harming others. Only a small minority have the moral conviction to forbid evil and call for righteousness. These are the ones that God saves and delivers from among the sinful masses. The verse is a call to be among those few who have the courage to stand against the moral decay of society, even if it means going against the tide of the majority. It's a reminder to not be complacent or complicit in wrongdoing, but to actively forbid it and work for positive change.
orig: فلولا كان من القرون من قبلكم أولو بقية ينهون عن الفساد في الأرض إلا قليلا ممن أنجينا منهم واتبع الذين ظلموا ما أترفوا فيه وكانوا مجرمين

translation: And your Lord would not destroy the cities unjustly while their people were reformers.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's justice and mercy. It assures that Allah does not punish or destroy a community arbitrarily or unjustly, especially when its people are righteous, striving to reform themselves and their society. The verse implies that the destruction of a city or a nation is a consequence of the widespread corruption, evil, and injustice that prevails among its people, despite warnings and reminders. It also serves as a reminder for people to constantly engage in self-reflection, reform, and righteous deeds to avert divine punishment.
orig: وما كان ربك ليهلك القرى بظلم وأهلها مصلحون

translation: And if your Lord had willed, He could have made mankind one community; but they will not cease to differ.
interpretation: This verse highlights the concept of free will that Allah has granted to humans. It suggests that if Allah had wanted, He could have created all of humanity as a single nation, united in their beliefs and ways of life. However, He has instead chosen to allow people to have different opinions, perspectives, and paths in life. The verse implies that this diversity and difference among humans is a natural consequence of the free will that Allah has bestowed upon them. It is a part of His divine wisdom and plan. The interpretation is that Allah acknowledges and allows the differences that exist among people, and that it is not His intention to force everyone to believe or act in a single, uniform manner. Rather, He has given humans the ability to choose their own way, even if that leads to them differing from one another.
orig: ولو شاء ربك لجعل الناس أمة واحدة ولا يزالون مختلفين

translation: Except whom your Lord has given mercy, and for that He created them. But the word of your Lord is to be fulfilled that, "I will surely fill Hell with jinn and men all together."
interpretation: This verse highlights the concept of divine predestination in Islam. It suggests that Allah has created humanity with a predetermined fate, and that only those whom He has chosen to grant His mercy will be saved from Hell. The rest, both jinn and men, are destined to fill Hell as decreed by Allah's word, which is absolute and unchangeable. This emphasizes the supreme power and authority of Allah over His creation, and the importance of seeking His mercy and guidance to be among those spared from eternal punishment.
orig: إلا من رحم ربك ولذلك خلقهم وتمت كلمة ربك لأملأن جهنم من الجنة والناس أجمعين

translation: And each [story] We relate to you from the news of the messengers is that by which We make firm your heart. And there has come to you, in this, the truth and an instruction and a reminder for the believers.
interpretation: This verse highlights the purpose behind relating the stories of the previous prophets to Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ). These stories serve to strengthen his heart and resolve in the face of adversities and challenges. Moreover, these stories bring the truth, guidance, and a reminder to the believers. They offer lessons, wisdom, and inspiration that believers can apply to their own lives. The Qur'an's narratives are not mere historical accounts; rather, they are a source of spiritual nourishment, moral instruction, and a means of increasing faith and steadfastness for those who believe in Allah and His messengers.
orig: وكلا نقص عليك من أنباء الرسل ما نثبت به فؤادك وجاءك في هذه الحق وموعظة وذكرى للمؤمنين

translation: And say to those who do not believe, "Work according to your position; indeed, we are working."
interpretation: This verse is a warning to the disbelievers that they should continue in their ways and face the consequences of their actions, while the believers will continue to do good deeds according to their faith. It implies that both groups will be recompensed according to their deeds and that the ultimate outcome will be in favor of the believers who are working righteousness. The verse also conveys a sense of confidence and steadfastness on the part of the believers, who are not swayed or intimidated by the actions or attitudes of the disbelievers.
orig: وقل للذين لا يؤمنون اعملوا على مكانتكم إنا عاملون

translation: And wait; indeed, we are waiting.
interpretation: This verse is a warning and a challenge to the disbelievers. It tells them to wait and see the consequences of their disbelief and rejection of the truth, while the believers wait patiently for Allah's help and victory. It implies that the ultimate outcome will be in favor of the believers, and the disbelievers will face the consequences of their choices. The verse also reflects the confidence and trust of the believers in Allah's plan and promise, despite the challenges and opposition they face.
orig: وانتظروا إنا منتظرون

translation: And to Allah belongs the unseen [aspects] of the heavens and the earth. And to Him will be returned the matter, all of it, so worship Him and rely upon Him. And your Lord is not unaware of that which you do.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah has complete knowledge and control over all that is hidden and unseen in the heavens and the earth. It reminds us that ultimately, all affairs will be returned to Him for judgment. Therefore, we should devote our worship exclusively to Allah and put our trust in Him alone. The verse also serves as a warning that Allah is fully aware of all our actions, both good and bad, and we will be held accountable for them in the Hereafter. It encourages us to be mindful of our deeds and strive for righteousness, knowing that nothing escapes Allah's knowledge and justice.
orig: ولله غيب السماوات والأرض وإليه يرجع الأمر كله فاعبده وتوكل عليه وما ربك بغافل عما تعملون

translation: Alif, Lam, Ra. These are the verses of the clear Book.
interpretation: This verse is the opening of a chapter in the Qur'an. The letters "Alif, Lam, Ra" are among the "Muqatta'at" or "disjoined" letters that appear at the beginning of some chapters. Their exact meaning is unknown, but they are believed to hold a profound significance known only to Allah. The verse then proclaims that the verses that follow are part of a divine book that is clear, unambiguous, and full of guidance for those who seek the truth. It emphasizes the Qur'an's clarity and its role as a source of guidance for mankind.
orig: الر تلك آيات الكتاب المبين

translation: Indeed, We have sent it down as an Arabic Qur'an that you might understand.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the Qur'an has been revealed in the Arabic language so that the people, particularly the Arabs to whom it was first revealed, may comprehend its message, reflect upon its meanings, and apply its teachings in their lives. The use of the Arabic language, with its rich vocabulary, eloquent expression, and profound literary style, facilitates the understanding and appreciation of the divine message. Moreover, this verse implies that the Qur'an is not merely a book to be recited but a guide to be understood and acted upon, encouraging the believers to engage their intellect and reason in the pursuit of spiritual enlightenment.
orig: إنا أنزلناه قرآنا عربيا لعلكم تعقلون

translation: We relate to you, [O Muhammad], the best of stories in what We have revealed to you of this Qur'an although you were, before it, among the unaware.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the stories in the Qur'an are the best and most beneficial stories because they come from divine revelation. It also points out that before receiving this revelation, Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) was unaware of these stories and their details. This highlights the fact that the Qur'an is a divine revelation and not something that the Prophet (peace be upon him) could have composed himself based on prior knowledge. The verse serves as a reminder of the authenticity and divine origin of the Qur'anic narratives.
orig: نحن نقص عليك أحسن القصص بما أوحينا إليك هذا القرآن وإن كنت من قبله لمن الغافلين

translation: When Joseph said to his father, "O my father, indeed I have seen [in a dream] eleven stars and the sun and the moon; I saw them prostrating to me."
interpretation: This verse is interpreted as a prophetic dream that Joseph had, indicating his future status and the blessings that would be bestowed upon him. The eleven stars represent his eleven brothers, while the sun and the moon represent his parents. Their prostration to him in the dream symbolizes their future submission and recognition of his high rank and status, which would come to pass when Joseph becomes a prominent figure in Egypt. This dream also foreshadows the trials and tribulations that Joseph would face from his brothers due to their jealousy, as well as his eventual triumph and reunification with his family.
orig: إذ قال يوسف لأبيه يا أبت إني رأيت أحد عشر كوكبا والشمس والقمر رأيتهم لي ساجدين

translation: He said, "O my son, do not relate your vision to your brothers or they will contrive against you a plan. Indeed Satan, to man, is a manifest enemy."
interpretation: In this verse, Prophet Jacob advises his son Joseph not to share his dream with his brothers, fearing that they may become jealous and plot against him. This highlights the importance of being cautious about sharing personal matters, even with close family members, as it may lead to unintended consequences. The verse also emphasizes the role of Satan as an open enemy to mankind, always seeking to create discord and enmity among people, especially through envy and jealousy. It serves as a reminder for believers to be vigilant against the whisperings and temptations of Satan, and to trust in the wisdom and guidance of righteous individuals, such as prophets and pious parents.
orig: قال يا بني لا تقصص رؤياك على إخوتك فيكيدوا لك كيدا إن الشيطان للإنسان عدو مبين

translation: And thus will your Lord choose you and teach you the interpretation of narratives and complete His favor upon you and upon the family of Jacob, as He completed it upon your fathers before, Abraham and Isaac. Indeed, your Lord is Knowing and Wise.
interpretation: This verse indicates that Allah has chosen Prophet Joseph and blessed him with the gift of interpreting dreams and events. It also emphasizes the continuation of Allah's favor upon Joseph and his family, just as He had favored his forefathers, Abraham and Isaac. The verse highlights the wisdom and knowledge of Allah in His choices and blessings upon His servants. It shows that Allah's favors are not random but are based on His infinite wisdom and knowledge.
orig: وكذلك يجتبيك ربك ويعلمك من تأويل الأحاديث ويتم نعمته عليك وعلى آل يعقوب كما أتمها على أبويك من قبل إبراهيم وإسحاق إن ربك عليم حكيم

translation: Certainly were there in Joseph and his brothers signs for those who ask.
interpretation: This verse highlights that the story of Prophet Joseph and his brothers, as narrated in the Qur'an, contains many important lessons, signs, and wisdom for those who seek knowledge and reflect upon it. The story serves as a reminder of God's power, the importance of faith, patience in the face of adversity, and the ultimate triumph of good over evil. It encourages believers to ponder upon the Qur'anic narratives and extract valuable insights that can be applied in their own lives.
orig: لقد كان في يوسف وإخوته آيات للسائلين

translation: When they said, "Joseph and his brother are dearer to our father than we, while we are a clan. Indeed, our father is in clear error."
interpretation: This verse reflects the jealousy and resentment felt by Joseph's brothers towards him and his younger brother Benjamin. They believed that their father, Jacob, favored Joseph and Benjamin over them, despite the fact that they were a strong and united group. The brothers' statement suggests that they viewed their father's love for Joseph and Benjamin as a form of misguidance or error in judgment. This jealousy ultimately led them to conspire against Joseph, demonstrating the destructive nature of envy and the importance of treating all children with fairness and equity.
orig: إذ قالوا ليوسف وأخوه أحب إلى أبينا منا ونحن عصبة إن أبانا لفي ضلال مبين

translation: Kill Joseph or cast him out to [another] land; the countenance of your father will [then] be only for you, and you will be after that a righteous people.
interpretation: This verse is showing the jealousy and resentment of Joseph's brothers towards him. They are plotting to get rid of him, either by killing him or abandoning him in a faraway land, so that they can have their father's full attention and favor. The verse also hints at their guilt, as they say that after getting rid of Joseph, they will become "righteous people", implying that they know that what they are planning is wrong. It demonstrates how jealousy and envy can lead people to contemplate terrible acts, even against their own family members.
orig: اقتلوا يوسف أو اطرحوه أرضا يخل لكم وجه أبيكم وتكونوا من بعده قوما صالحين

translation: Said a speaker among them, "Do not kill Joseph but throw him into the bottom of the well; some travelers will pick him up - if you would do [something]."
interpretation: This verse is referring to the story of Prophet Joseph (Yusuf) and his brothers. One of the brothers, who had some compassion towards Joseph, suggested an alternative to killing him outright. He proposed that instead of murder, they should throw Joseph into a well, with the hope that some passing caravan would find him and take him away. This suggestion was made as a compromise between getting rid of Joseph, which is what the brothers wanted due to their jealousy, and avoiding the grave sin of fratricide. It shows that even in the midst of evil intent, there can be a voice of relative reason and mercy. However, this act was still a great wrong against Joseph and caused much grief to their father Jacob. The story of Joseph in the Qur'an conveys many lessons about patience in the face of adversity, the need to resist temptation and evil, and maintaining faith in God's plan despite hardships.
orig: قال قائل منهم لا تقتلوا يوسف وألقوه في غيابت الجب يلتقطه بعض السيارة إن كنتم فاعلين

translation: They said, "O our father, why do you not entrust us with Joseph while indeed, we are to him sincere counselors?"
interpretation: In this verse, the brothers of Joseph are trying to convince their father, Jacob, to let them take Joseph with them on a trip. They are assuring their father that they have Joseph's best interests at heart and will take good care of him. However, this is a deception on their part, as they are actually planning to get rid of Joseph out of jealousy. The verse highlights the manipulative nature of the brothers and their willingness to deceive even their own father to achieve their goals. It also shows the deep love and concern Jacob has for his son Joseph, as he is reluctant to let him go with his brothers whom he does not fully trust.
orig: قالوا يا أبانا ما لك لا تأمنا على يوسف وإنا له لناصحون

translation: Send him with us tomorrow to enjoy himself and play, and indeed, we will be his guardians.
interpretation: This verse is likely about a group of people, perhaps siblings or friends, requesting someone's permission to take a young boy out with them to play and enjoy leisure activities. They are assuring the boy's guardian that they will look after him and keep him safe. The interpretation is that the verse reflects the importance of play, leisure, and social bonding for children. It also shows the value of having responsible guardians to supervise and protect children during such activities to ensure their wellbeing and safety.
orig: أرسله معنا غدا يرتع ويلعب وإنا له لحافظون

translation: He said, "Indeed, it saddens me that you should take him, and I fear that a wolf would eat him while you are of him unaware."
interpretation: This verse reflects a father's deep concern and love for his son. He is hesitant to let his son go with his brothers, fearing that harm may come to him in their absence, such as being attacked by a wolf. The father's words express his emotional attachment and his desire to protect his child from any potential danger, even if it means keeping him close by. It highlights the natural instinct of a parent to safeguard their children and the worry that comes with entrusting their care to others.
orig: قال إني ليحزنني أن تذهبوا به وأخاف أن يأكله الذئب وأنتم عنه غافلون

translation: They said, "If a wolf should eat him while we are a [strong] clan, indeed, we would then be losers."
interpretation: This verse is expressing the arrogance and overconfidence of Prophet Joseph's brothers. They are essentially saying that it would be a great shame and loss for them if a wolf were to eat Joseph while they, being a strong and capable group, were present. It highlights their pride and their perceived sense of control over the situation, while also foreshadowing the very event they are dismissing - that Joseph would indeed face danger and be lost to them, though not in the way they imagined. The verse sets the stage for the unfolding of Allah's plan and the lessons that the brothers would learn about humility, faith, and the limits of their own power in the face of divine will.
orig: قالوا لئن أكله الذئب ونحن عصبة إنا إذا لخاسرون

translation: So when they took him [out] and agreed to put him into the bottom of the well... But We inspired to him, "You will surely inform them [someday] about this affair of theirs while they do not perceive [your identity]."
interpretation: This verse is referring to the story of Prophet Yusuf (Joseph) and his brothers. The interpretation is that even though Yusuf's brothers plotted against him out of jealousy and threw him into a well, Allah gave Yusuf a revelation that a day would come when he would have power over them and inform them of what they did, while they would not recognize him. It shows that Allah's plan and protection is always at work, even in the face of hardships and evil plots of others. It also foreshadows how the story will unfold, with Yusuf eventually rising to a high position and his brothers coming to him for help, unaware that it is the brother they wronged.
orig: فلما ذهبوا به وأجمعوا أن يجعلوه في غيابت الجب وأوحينا إليه لتنبئنهم بأمرهم هذا وهم لا يشعرون

translation: And they came to their father at night, weeping.
interpretation: This verse is referring to the story of Prophet Yusuf (Joseph) and his brothers. The brothers, out of jealousy, had plotted against Yusuf and sold him into slavery. They then returned to their father, Prophet Yaqub (Jacob), at night, pretending to weep and claiming that a wolf had eaten Yusuf while they were busy in their play. The verse highlights the deceptive nature of the brothers and the depth of their betrayal towards both their younger brother and their father. It also sets the stage for the unfolding of the story, which ultimately demonstrates God's plan and wisdom in the face of human schemes and wrongdoing.
orig: وجاءوا أباهم عشاء يبكون

translation: They said, "O our father, indeed we went racing each other and left Joseph with our possessions, and a wolf ate him. But you would not believe us, even if we were truthful."
interpretation: This verse is from the story of Prophet Joseph (peace be upon him) in the Qur'an. It shows the deceit of Joseph's brothers, who, out of jealousy, plotted against him and threw him into a well. They then came to their father, Jacob, with a false story that a wolf had eaten Joseph while they were engaged in a race, knowing that their father would have difficulty believing them. This highlights the depth of their betrayal and the pain it caused their father. It also demonstrates the importance of honesty and the consequences of lying and jealousy within a family.
orig: قالوا يا أبانا إنا ذهبنا نستبق وتركنا يوسف عند متاعنا فأكله الذئب وما أنت بمؤمن لنا ولو كنا صادقين

translation: And they brought upon his shirt false blood. [Jacob] said, "Rather, your souls have enticed you to something, so patience is most fitting. And Allah is the one sought for help against that which you describe."
interpretation: This verse is referring to the story of Joseph and his brothers. The brothers had plotted against Joseph and sold him into slavery, then brought his shirt stained with false blood to their father Jacob as evidence of Joseph's supposed death. Jacob, however, saw through their deception. His response demonstrates his wisdom, patience and trust in Allah. Despite the great hardship of losing his beloved son, Jacob turned to Allah for comfort and strength, remaining steadfast. He refused to despair or lash out at his other sons, instead exercising beautiful patience (sabr jamil). This highlights the importance of trusting Allah's plan, maintaining faith and responding with patience and dignity in the face of life's trials. Ultimately, Allah is the one who can help us through difficult times when we turn to Him sincerely.
orig: وجاءوا على قميصه بدم كذب قال بل سولت لكم أنفسكم أمرا فصبر جميل والله المستعان على ما تصفون

translation: And there came a caravan, and they sent their water-drawer. So he let down his bucket. He said, "Good news! Here is a boy." And they concealed him as merchandise, and Allah was Knowing of what they did.
interpretation: This verse refers to the story of Prophet Yusuf (Joseph) when he was thrown into a well by his brothers out of jealousy. A caravan passing by sent their water-drawer to fetch water from the well, and he discovered Yusuf inside. The caravan people decided to take Yusuf with them and sell him as a slave in Egypt, concealing his true identity. However, Allah was fully aware of their actions and intentions. This highlights that no matter how much people try to hide their deeds, Allah is All-Knowing and sees what they do in secret.
orig: وجاءت سيارة فأرسلوا واردهم فأدلى دلوه قال يا بشرى هذا غلام وأسروه بضاعة والله عليم بما يعملون

translation: And they sold him for a reduced price - a few silver coins - and they were, concerning him, of those content with little.
interpretation: This verse is referring to the story of Prophet Yusuf (Joseph) when his brothers sold him into slavery. The interpretation is that his brothers traded him for a very low price, just a handful of silver coins, showing how little they valued him. They were willing to give him away for such a small amount because they had no regard for him and wanted to get rid of him. This demonstrates their jealousy, cruelty and lack of compassion towards their own brother. It also highlights the severe trials and hardships that Prophet Yusuf had to endure, even at the hands of his own family.
orig: وشروه بثمن بخس دراهم معدودة وكانوا فيه من الزاهدين

translation: And the one from Egypt who bought him said to his wife, "Make his residence comfortable. Perhaps he will benefit us, or we will adopt him as a son." And thus, We established Joseph in the land that We might teach him the interpretation of events. And Allah is predominant over His affair, but most of the people do not know.
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine plan and wisdom behind Joseph's journey to Egypt. Despite being sold as a slave, God had a greater purpose for him. The Egyptian official's kindness towards Joseph, motivated by a desire for worldly gain, was part of God's plan to establish Joseph in a position of influence and authority. This would later enable Joseph to play a crucial role in the affairs of Egypt and his own family. The verse also emphasizes that God teaches Joseph the interpretation of dreams, which would be a key factor in his rise to prominence. Ultimately, the verse reminds us that God's plan always prevails, even if most people are unaware of it.
orig: وقال الذي اشتراه من مصر لامرأته أكرمي مثواه عسى أن ينفعنا أو نتخذه ولدا وكذلك مكنا ليوسف في الأرض ولنعلمه من تأويل الأحاديث والله غالب على أمره ولكن أكثر الناس لا يعلمون

translation: And when he reached his maturity, We gave him wisdom and knowledge. And thus do We reward the doers of good.
interpretation: This verse highlights that when a person reaches the age of maturity and responsibility, Allah grants them wisdom and knowledge as a reward for their good deeds and righteousness. It emphasizes the importance of doing good and living a virtuous life, as it will lead to Allah's blessings and favors in the form of wisdom and knowledge. The verse also implies that the acquisition of wisdom and knowledge is not merely a result of age or experience, but rather a divine gift bestowed upon those who strive to be among the "doers of good" (al-muhsineen).
orig: ولما بلغ أشده آتيناه حكما وعلما وكذلك نجزي المحسنين

translation: And she, in whose house he was, sought to seduce him. She closed the doors and said, "Come, you." He said, "[I seek] the refuge of Allah. Indeed, he is my master, who has made good my residence. Indeed, wrongdoers will not succeed."
interpretation: This verse is a stark reminder that even those in positions of power and authority can be tempted towards sin and immorality. The woman, despite her status and influence, sought to seduce Joseph and lead him astray. However, Joseph's unwavering faith and righteousness allowed him to resist temptation and seek refuge in Allah. This highlights the importance of maintaining one's integrity and moral compass, even in the face of pressure or enticement from others. It also underscores the idea that those who engage in wrongdoing and transgression will ultimately not succeed, as Allah's justice will prevail.
orig: وراودته التي هو في بيتها عن نفسه وغلقت الأبواب وقالت هيت لك قال معاذ الله إنه ربي أحسن مثواي إنه لا يفلح الظالمون

translation: And she certainly determined [to seduce] him, and he would have inclined to her had he not seen the proof of his Lord. And thus [it was] that We should avert from him evil and immorality. Indeed, he was of Our chosen servants.
interpretation: This verse is referring to the story of Prophet Yusuf (Joseph) and the wife of Al-Aziz, who tried to seduce him. The interpretation is that even though she had a strong desire for him and he himself felt inclined towards her, he resisted the temptation because of his faith in Allah and the proof he saw from his Lord. This incident demonstrated Yusuf's righteousness and his status as one of Allah's chosen servants. It also shows that with strong faith and conviction, one can overcome temptations and avoid falling into sin and immorality.
orig: ولقد همت به وهم بها لولا أن رأى برهان ربه كذلك لنصرف عنه السوء والفحشاء إنه من عبادنا المخلصين

translation: And they both raced to the door, and she tore his shirt from the back, and they found her husband at the door. She said, "What is the recompense of one who intended evil for your wife but that he be imprisoned or a painful punishment?"
interpretation: This verse is interpreted as a lesson in the importance of maintaining one's integrity and resisting temptation. The woman's false accusation against Joseph, despite his innocence, demonstrates the lengths that some may go to protect their own reputation at the expense of others. It also highlights the need for justice and the consequences of making false allegations. The verse emphasizes the value of honesty, trustworthiness, and the protection of one's honor, even in the face of pressure or temptation to do otherwise.
orig: واستبقا الباب وقدت قميصه من دبر وألفيا سيدها لدى الباب قالت ما جزاء من أراد بأهلك سوءا إلا أن يسجن أو عذاب أليم

translation: He said, "It was she who sought to seduce me." And a witness from her family testified, "If his shirt is torn from the front, then she has told the truth, and he is of the liars."
interpretation: This verse is referring to the story of Prophet Yusuf (Joseph) and the wife of Al-Aziz who tried to seduce him. When her husband found them, she accused Yusuf of trying to rape her. A wise person from her household suggested that Yusuf's shirt should be examined. If it was torn from the front, it would mean that she was telling the truth and he was trying to escape from her grip. This shows the wisdom of looking at evidence and using reasoning to arrive at the truth, rather than just taking accusations at face value. It also demonstrates the virtue of Yusuf in resisting temptation and maintaining his chastity and integrity, despite being in a vulnerable position as a servant in the household.
orig: قال هي راودتني عن نفسي وشهد شاهد من أهلها إن كان قميصه قد من قبل فصدقت وهو من الكاذبين

translation: But if his shirt is torn from the back, then she has lied and he is of the truthful.
interpretation: This verse is referring to the story of Prophet Yusuf (Joseph) and the wife of the Aziz of Egypt, who tried to seduce him. When Yusuf refused her advances, she accused him of attempting to assault her. As evidence, Yusuf's shirt was torn from the back, indicating that he was running away from her, not towards her. This proves that the wife of the Aziz was lying and that Yusuf was telling the truth. The verse emphasizes the importance of seeking and relying on evidence to determine the truth in a situation and not simply accepting accusations at face value. It also highlights the virtue of honesty and integrity, as exemplified by Prophet Yusuf, even in the face of false accusations and temptation.
orig: وإن كان قميصه قد من دبر فكذبت وهو من الصادقين

translation: So when he saw his shirt torn from the back, he said, "Indeed, it is of your [i.e., women's] plan. Indeed, your plan is great [i.e., vehement]."
interpretation: This verse is interpreted as a commentary on the deceptive nature of women. When the Prophet Joseph's master saw that his shirt was torn from the back, he realized that Joseph was innocent and that his wife had tried to seduce him. The master's statement "Indeed, it is of your [i.e., women's] plan" suggests that women are capable of devising clever schemes to achieve their desires. The additional comment "Indeed, your plan is great [i.e., vehement]" emphasizes the potential intensity and effectiveness of women's plots. This interpretation reflects a traditional patriarchal perspective that views women as inherently cunning and untrustworthy.
orig: فلما رأى قميصه قد من دبر قال إنه من كيدكن إن كيدكن عظيم

translation: Joseph, ignore this. And, [my wife], ask forgiveness for your sin. Indeed, you were of the sinful.
interpretation: This verse is addressed to the Prophet Joseph and the wife of his master who tried to seduce him. It instructs Joseph to turn away from and disregard her advances and immoral proposal. At the same time, it commands the woman to seek forgiveness from Allah for her sinful conduct and wrongdoing in attempting to lure Joseph and falsely accusing him when he refused her. The verse emphasizes that she was certainly among the sinners for her actions. It highlights the importance of resisting temptations, maintaining chastity and morality, and sincerely repenting to Allah for any transgressions.
orig: يوسف أعرض عن هذا واستغفري لذنبك إنك كنت من الخاطئين

translation: And women in the city said, "The wife of al-'Azeez is seeking to seduce her slave boy; he has impassioned her with love. Indeed, we see her [to be] in clear error."
interpretation: This verse is commenting on the scandalous nature of the actions of the wife of al-'Azeez (referred to as Zulaikha in Islamic tradition), who attempted to seduce her slave Joseph (referred to as Yusuf). The women of the city are gossiping about her behavior, noting that she has been overcome with love and passion for him to the point that they see her actions as a clear misguidance and error in judgment. It highlights how her desires led her to cross ethical and social boundaries in an inappropriate way that became the subject of public discussion and disapproval.
orig: وقال نسوة في المدينة امرأت العزيز تراود فتاها عن نفسه قد شغفها حبا إنا لنراها في ضلال مبين

translation: So when she heard of their scheming, she sent for them and prepared for them a banquet and gave each one of them a knife and said [to Joseph], "Come out before them." And when they saw him, they greatly admired him and cut their hands and said, "Perfect is Allah! This is not a man; this is none but a noble angel."
interpretation: This verse is a part of the story of Prophet Yusuf (Joseph) and the wife of the Aziz of Egypt. When the women of the city heard about her love for Yusuf and how she tried to seduce him, they started blaming her. In response, she invited them to her palace and arranged a banquet. She gave each of them a knife to cut the fruit, and then asked Yusuf to come out. When they saw his beauty, they were so stunned that they cut their own hands with the knives, exclaiming that he could not be a human being, but rather a noble angel. This incident showed that the wife of Aziz was not the only one infatuated by Yusuf's beauty, and that it was a test from Allah for Yusuf, who remained steadfast and did not give in to temptation, thus proving his chastity and righteousness.
orig: فلما سمعت بمكرهن أرسلت إليهن وأعتدت لهن متكأ وآتت كل واحدة منهن سكينا وقالت اخرج عليهن فلما رأينه أكبرنه وقطعن أيديهن وقلن حاش لله ما هذا بشرا إن هذا إلا ملك كريم

translation: She said, "That is the one about whom you blamed me. And I certainly sought to seduce him, but he firmly refused; and if he will not do what I order him, he will surely be imprisoned and will be of those debased."
interpretation: This verse sheds light on the power dynamics and gender roles in the story of Prophet Yusuf (Joseph) and the wife of Al-Aziz. Despite her high status and influence, the wife of Al-Aziz admits to her wrongdoing in attempting to seduce Yusuf, acknowledging his innocence and moral uprightness in resisting her advances. The verse also highlights the unjust nature of the threat she makes against Yusuf, warning that if he does not submit to her desires, he will face imprisonment and humiliation. This demonstrates how those in positions of power can abuse their authority to coerce and manipulate others, especially those who are morally righteous and unwilling to compromise their principles.
orig: قالت فذلكن الذي لمتنني فيه ولقد راودته عن نفسه فاستعصم ولئن لم يفعل ما آمره ليسجنن وليكونا من الصاغرين

translation: He said, "My Lord, prison is more to my liking than that to which they invite me. And if You do not avert from me their plan, I might incline toward them and [thus] be of the ignorant."
interpretation: This verse shows the strong faith and moral character of Prophet Yusuf (Joseph). Despite the temptations and pressures from the women in the palace, he preferred to face imprisonment rather than succumb to their advances and commit sin. He recognized his own human weakness and sought Allah's help to protect him from falling into wrongdoing. This demonstrates the importance of turning to Allah in times of difficulty and seeking His guidance to overcome temptations and remain steadfast in faith. It also highlights the virtue of preserving one's chastity and integrity, even in the face of hardship or persecution.
orig: قال رب السجن أحب إلي مما يدعونني إليه وإلا تصرف عني كيدهن أصب إليهن وأكن من الجاهلين

translation: So his Lord responded to him and averted from him their plan. Indeed, He is the Hearing, the Knowing.
interpretation: This verse highlights the power of sincere supplication and Allah's response to those who turn to Him in times of hardship. When Prophet Yusuf (Joseph) was faced with the temptations and plots of the women in the house of the Aziz, he sought refuge in Allah and made a sincere supplication. Allah, in His infinite mercy, responded to Yusuf's prayer and protected him from falling into sin, averting the evil plans of the women. This demonstrates that Allah is All-Hearing, fully aware of the supplications of His servants, and All-Knowing, fully cognizant of their situations and the intents of others. The verse emphasizes the importance of turning to Allah with sincerity and trust, seeking His protection and guidance in the face of trials and temptations.
orig: فاستجاب له ربه فصرف عنه كيدهن إنه هو السميع العليم

translation: Then it occurred to them after they had seen the signs that al-'Azeez should surely imprison him for a time.
interpretation: This verse refers to the story of Prophet Yusuf (Joseph) when he was falsely accused by the wife of al-'Azeez (the minister of Egypt). Despite the clear signs of his innocence, those in power decided to imprison Prophet Yusuf for a period of time. This decision may have been influenced by societal pressure, personal interests, or a lack of complete trust in his innocence. It highlights the challenges and trials faced by the righteous, even when the truth is apparent. The verse also alludes to the patience and perseverance required to endure such hardships, trusting in Allah's plan and ultimate justice.
orig: ثم بدا لهم من بعد ما رأوا الآيات ليسجننه حتى حين

translation: And there entered the prison with him two young men. One of them said, "Indeed, I have seen myself [in a dream] pressing wine." The other said, "Indeed, I have seen myself carrying upon my head [some] bread, from which the birds were eating. Inform us of its interpretation; indeed, we see you to be of those who do good."
interpretation: This verse is about two young men who were imprisoned with Prophet Yusuf (Joseph). They both had dreams and sought Yusuf's interpretation, recognizing him as a righteous person with knowledge. The interpretation shows that even in difficult circumstances, such as imprisonment, believers should use their God-given abilities to help and benefit others. It also highlights the importance of seeking knowledge and understanding, especially from those who are known for their righteousness and wisdom.
orig: ودخل معه السجن فتيان قال أحدهما إني أراني أعصر خمرا وقال الآخر إني أراني أحمل فوق رأسي خبزا تأكل الطير منه نبئنا بتأويله إنا نراك من المحسنين

translation: He said, "No food will come to you as provision, but I will inform you of its interpretation before it comes to you. This is from what my Lord has taught me. Indeed, I have abandoned the way of a people who do not believe in Allah, and they, in the Hereafter, are disbelievers."
interpretation: This verse shows the deep knowledge and wisdom that Allah bestowed upon Prophet Yusuf (Joseph). He was able to interpret dreams and signs by Allah's permission, even before they came to pass. Yusuf emphasizes that this ability is not from himself, but a gift from Allah. He also distances himself from the way of the disbelievers, who reject faith in Allah and the Hereafter. This highlights Yusuf's strong belief and trust in Allah, even in the midst of hardship, and serves as an example for believers to remain steadfast in their faith.
orig: قال لا يأتيكما طعام ترزقانه إلا نبأتكما بتأويله قبل أن يأتيكما ذلكما مما علمني ربي إني تركت ملة قوم لا يؤمنون بالله وهم بالآخرة هم كافرون

translation: And I have followed the religion of my fathers, Abraham, Isaac and Jacob. And it was not for us to associate anything with Allah. This is from the favor of Allah upon us and upon the people, but most of the people are not grateful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of following the monotheistic faith of the prophets Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, who were the ancestors of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him). It stresses the need to avoid associating partners with Allah in worship, which is considered the gravest sin in Islam. The verse also highlights that the guidance to the true faith is a favor and blessing from Allah upon the prophets and their followers. However, it points out that despite this great blessing, most people fail to be grateful to Allah and instead follow false beliefs and practices.
orig: واتبعت ملة آبائي إبراهيم وإسحاق ويعقوب ما كان لنا أن نشرك بالله من شيء ذلك من فضل الله علينا وعلى الناس ولكن أكثر الناس لا يشكرون

translation: O my two companions of the prison, are separate lords better or Allah, the One, the Irresistible?
interpretation: This verse is addressing the fundamental question of monotheism versus polytheism. It challenges the notion that worshipping multiple deities is superior to worshipping the One True God, Allah, who is unique and all-powerful. The verse implies that the concept of multiple gods is inherently flawed and that ultimate authority and power belong to Allah alone. It invites the listeners to reflect on the nature of divinity and to recognize the supremacy of the One God over any other objects of worship. The mention of Allah's attributes, "the One, the Irresistible," emphasizes His singular nature and His absolute dominion over all creation, further underscoring the futility of polytheism.
orig: يا صاحبي السجن أأرباب متفرقون خير أم الله الواحد القهار

translation: You worship not besides Him except [mere] names you have named them, you and your fathers, for which Allah has sent down no authority. Legislation is not but for Allah. He has commanded that you worship not except Him. That is the correct religion, but most of the people do not know.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the false gods and idols worshipped by the polytheists are mere names without any reality or authority from Allah. It asserts that the right to legislate and command worship belongs to Allah alone. Worshipping anything else besides Allah is contrary to the true religion, which most people are ignorant of. The verse establishes the concept of Tawheed (Islamic monotheism) and rejects the validity of worshipping any entity besides Allah, as it has no basis or sanction from Him.
orig: ما تعبدون من دونه إلا أسماء سميتموها أنتم وآباؤكم ما أنزل الله بها من سلطان إن الحكم إلا لله أمر ألا تعبدوا إلا إياه ذلك الدين القيم ولكن أكثر الناس لا يعلمون

translation: O two companions of prison, as for one of you, he will give drink to his master of wine; but as for the other, he will be crucified, and the birds will eat from his head. The matter has been decreed about which you both inquire.
interpretation: This verse is interpreted as a demonstration of Joseph's prophetic abilities, as he was able to accurately predict the fate of his two fellow prisoners based on the dreams they had described to him. It also highlights the concept of divine decree in Islam, as Joseph attributes the ultimate outcome to the will of God, stating that "the matter has been decreed". The verse emphasizes the idea that all events, even those that may seem uncertain or subject to human influence, are ultimately predetermined by God's will and knowledge.
orig: يا صاحبي السجن أما أحدكما فيسقي ربه خمرا وأما الآخر فيصلب فتأكل الطير من رأسه قضي الأمر الذي فيه تستفتيان

translation: And he said to the one whom he knew would be saved, "Mention me to your master." But Satan made him forget the mention [to] his master, so he remained in prison several years.
interpretation: This verse highlights the deceptive nature of Satan, who can make people forget even the most important things. The man who was saved from prison forgot to mention Joseph to the king, despite Joseph's request, due to the influence of Satan. As a result, Joseph remained in prison for several more years. This serves as a reminder to always be mindful of Allah and not let worldly distractions or the whispers of Satan cause us to forget our duties and responsibilities towards Him.
orig: وقال للذي ظن أنه ناج منهما اذكرني عند ربك فأنساه الشيطان ذكر ربه فلبث في السجن بضع سنين

translation: And [subsequently] the king said, "Indeed, I have seen [in a dream] seven fat cows being eaten by seven [that were] lean, and seven green spikes [of grain] and others [that were] dry. O eminent ones, explain to me my vision, if you should interpret visions."
interpretation: This verse is referring to the dream of the king, which was interpreted by Prophet Yusuf (Joseph). The interpretation is that the seven fat cows represent seven years of prosperity and abundance, while the seven lean cows represent seven years of famine and hardship that will follow. The seven green spikes of grain represent the years of prosperity, and the dry spikes represent the years of famine. This dream was a warning from Allah to the king and his people to prepare for the upcoming hardship by storing food and resources during the years of abundance. It also highlights the wisdom and knowledge that Allah bestowed upon Prophet Yusuf, who was able to interpret the dream accurately and provide guidance to the king and his people.
orig: وقال الملك إني أرى سبع بقرات سمان يأكلهن سبع عجاف وسبع سنبلات خضر وأخر يابسات يا أيها الملأ أفتوني في رؤياي إن كنتم للرؤيا تعبرون

translation: They said, "[These are but] confused dreams, and we are not learned in the interpretation of dreams."
interpretation: This verse suggests that some people, when presented with divine revelation or prophetic visions, may dismiss them as mere confused dreams or nonsensical ramblings. They claim ignorance about the interpretation of dreams, indicating a skepticism or lack of spiritual understanding. It implies that the deeper meanings and wisdom within such revelations are lost on those who lack the knowledge, insight, or openness to comprehend them. The verse highlights the importance of having the right spiritual and intellectual capacity to grasp the significance of divine messages and prophetic dreams, rather than dismissing them outright.
orig: قالوا أضغاث أحلام وما نحن بتأويل الأحلام بعالمين

translation: But the one who was freed and remembered after a time said, "I will inform you of its interpretation, so send me forth."
interpretation: This verse is referring to one of the two men who were imprisoned with Prophet Yusuf (Joseph). After being released from prison and remembering Yusuf's ability to interpret dreams, he offers to provide the interpretation of the king's dream, which Yusuf had previously interpreted for the two men while in prison. The man's remembrance and willingness to speak about Yusuf's abilities, even after a long time had passed, demonstrates the lasting impact of Yusuf's righteousness and the importance of remembering and acknowledging the gifts and good deeds of others, even in their absence. It also highlights the power of divine wisdom and how it can manifest through individuals to help others in times of need.
orig: وقال الذي نجا منهما وادكر بعد أمة أنا أنبئكم بتأويله فأرسلون

translation: Joseph, O man of truth, explain to us about seven fat cows eaten by seven [that were] lean, and seven green spikes [of grain] and others [that were] dry - that I may return to the people; perhaps they will know [about you].
interpretation: This verse is an interpretation of the dream of the king of Egypt, who sought Joseph's help in understanding its meaning. The interpretation is that the seven fat cows represent seven years of prosperity and abundance, while the seven lean cows represent seven years of famine and hardship that will follow. The seven green spikes of grain represent the crops that will grow during the years of prosperity, while the dry spikes represent the lack of crops during the famine. Joseph's ability to interpret dreams and his wisdom in advising the king to store surplus grain during the prosperous years, in order to prepare for the famine, is a sign of his prophethood and his trust in Allah's plan. The verse also emphasizes the importance of seeking knowledge and understanding from those who are knowledgeable and truthful.
orig: يوسف أيها الصديق أفتنا في سبع بقرات سمان يأكلهن سبع عجاف وسبع سنبلات خضر وأخر يابسات لعلي أرجع إلى الناس لعلهم يعلمون

translation: He said, "You will plant for seven years consecutively; and what you harvest leave in its spikes, except a little from which you will eat."
interpretation: This verse is advising to plan ahead and save resources for the future. It suggests that for seven years, most of the harvest should be stored and left untouched, with only a small portion used for immediate consumption. This is a wise strategy to build up reserves and ensure food security during times of hardship or famine that may lie ahead. It highlights the importance of forward-thinking, discipline, and efficient resource management for the long-term well-being of individuals and society.
orig: قال تزرعون سبع سنين دأبا فما حصدتم فذروه في سنبله إلا قليلا مما تأكلون

translation: Then, after that, seven difficult [years] will come that will consume what you saved for them, except a little from which you will store.
interpretation: This verse is referring to the interpretation of the dream of the king of Egypt by Prophet Yusuf (Joseph). It foretells that after seven years of abundance, there will come seven years of severe drought and famine that will consume most of what was saved during the previous seven years of plenty, except a little that was stored away safely. This interpretation highlights the wisdom and foresight of Prophet Yusuf in advising the king to store away a portion of the harvest during the years of abundance as a contingency for the upcoming difficult years. It also emphasizes the importance of planning and preparing for the future, both materially and spiritually.
orig: ثم يأتي من بعد ذلك سبع شداد يأكلن ما قدمتم لهن إلا قليلا مما تحصنون

translation: Then, there will come a year in which the people will be given rain and in which they will press [olives and grapes].
interpretation: This verse is referring to a future time of prosperity and abundance, after a period of hardship. The people will be blessed with ample rainfall, allowing them to cultivate their crops and produce olive oil and grape juice in abundance. This verse serves as a reminder that even in the face of adversity, there is always hope for a better future, and that God's mercy and blessings are ever-present. It encourages believers to remain patient and steadfast during times of difficulty, knowing that relief and prosperity will come in due time, by the grace of God.
orig: ثم يأتي من بعد ذلك عام فيه يغاث الناس وفيه يعصرون

translation: And the king said, "Bring him to me." But when the messenger came to him, [Joseph] said, "Return to your master and ask him what is the case of the women who cut their hands. Indeed, my Lord is Knowing of their plan."
interpretation: This verse highlights Joseph's wisdom and trust in Allah. Despite the king's summons, which could have been an opportunity for Joseph to be freed from prison, he instead chose to clear his name and reputation first. He asked the messenger to inquire about the women who had cut their hands upon seeing his beauty, knowing that their testimony would prove his innocence. Joseph's faith in Allah's knowledge and justice guided his decision, emphasizing the importance of patience, integrity, and reliance on Allah's plan in the face of adversity.
orig: وقال الملك ائتوني به فلما جاءه الرسول قال ارجع إلى ربك فاسأله ما بال النسوة اللاتي قطعن أيديهن إن ربي بكيدهن عليم

translation: He said, "What was your affair when you sought to seduce Joseph?" They said, "Perfect is Allah! We know about him no evil." The wife of al-'Azeez said, "Now the truth has become evident. It was I who sought to seduce him, and indeed, he is of the truthful."
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of honesty and truthfulness. The wife of al-'Azeez, who had previously tried to seduce Joseph and then falsely accused him when he resisted, finally admits the truth when confronted by the king. Her confession demonstrates that the truth will always come to light, no matter how much one tries to conceal it. Joseph's integrity and honesty are also emphasized, as he remained steadfast in his righteousness despite the temptations and false accusations he faced. This verse teaches us to always be truthful and to trust in Allah's justice, even in the face of adversity.
orig: قال ما خطبكن إذ راودتن يوسف عن نفسه قلن حاش لله ما علمنا عليه من سوء قالت امرأت العزيز الآن حصحص الحق أنا راودته عن نفسه وإنه لمن الصادقين

translation: That [was] so he would know that I did not betray him in [his] absence and that Allah does not guide the plan of betrayers.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of honesty and loyalty, even when no one is watching. It suggests that betrayal and deception are not condoned by Allah, and that those who engage in such behavior will ultimately face consequences for their actions. The verse also highlights the idea that Allah is aware of all that happens, even in secret, and that He will not support or guide those who act dishonestly or betray the trust of others.
orig: ذلك ليعلم أني لم أخنه بالغيب وأن الله لا يهدي كيد الخائنين

translation: And I do not acquit myself. Indeed, the soul is a persistent enjoiner of evil, except those upon which my Lord has mercy. Indeed, my Lord is Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the inherent weakness of the human soul and its inclination towards evil desires and temptations. It serves as a reminder that no one is perfect or free from sin, and that we should constantly seek Allah's mercy and forgiveness. The verse also highlights the importance of humility and avoiding self-righteousness, as even the most pious individuals are not immune to the whisperings of their own souls. Ultimately, it is only through Allah's mercy and grace that one can hope to overcome their base desires and attain righteousness.
orig: وما أبرئ نفسي إن النفس لأمارة بالسوء إلا ما رحم ربي إن ربي غفور رحيم

translation: And the king said, "Bring him to me; I will appoint him exclusively for myself." And when he spoke to him, he said, "Indeed, you are today established [in position] and trusted."
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of trust and reliability in attaining high positions. The king recognized Joseph's virtues and abilities through his conversation with him, and thus appointed him to an exclusive and trusted position in his court. It shows that one's character, wisdom, and integrity can open doors to great opportunities and responsibilities, even in the face of previous hardships or challenges. The verse emphasizes the value of proving oneself through actions and words, which can lead to earning the trust and favor of those in authority.
orig: وقال الملك ائتوني به أستخلصه لنفسي فلما كلمه قال إنك اليوم لدينا مكين أمين

translation: He said, "Appoint me over the storehouses of the land. Indeed, I will be a knowing guardian."
interpretation: This verse shows the importance of entrusting responsibilities to those who are qualified and capable. The speaker, believed to be Prophet Yusuf (Joseph), offers his services to manage the storehouses of the land, asserting that he is trustworthy ("hafeez") and knowledgeable ("aleem"). This highlights the Islamic principle of putting the right person in the right position based on their merits, skills, and character. It also emphasizes the value of integrity and competence in leadership and administration.
orig: قال اجعلني على خزائن الأرض إني حفيظ عليم

translation: And thus We established Joseph in the land to settle therein wherever he willed. We touch with Our mercy whom We will, and We do not allow to be lost the reward of those who do good.
interpretation: This verse highlights the power and wisdom of Allah in establishing Prophet Joseph in a position of authority and influence in Egypt, despite the challenges and difficulties he faced. It emphasizes that Allah grants His mercy and blessings to whomever He wills, especially those who consistently do good deeds and remain steadfast in their faith. The verse also serves as a reminder that the ultimate reward for one's good deeds and righteousness lies with Allah, and He never allows the efforts of those who strive for His sake to go to waste. This encourages believers to persevere in their faith and good deeds, trusting in Allah's plan and mercy.
orig: وكذلك مكنا ليوسف في الأرض يتبوأ منها حيث يشاء نصيب برحمتنا من نشاء ولا نضيع أجر المحسنين

translation: But the reward of the Hereafter is better for those who believed and were fearing Allah.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that while worldly gains and pleasures may seem attractive, the ultimate reward in the afterlife is far superior for those who have faith and live righteously. It encourages believers to prioritize their spiritual well-being over material pursuits, as the eternal bliss of Paradise awaits those who remain steadfast in their belief and piety. The verse serves as a reminder that the temporary nature of this world pales in comparison to the everlasting joy and peace that God has prepared for His devout servants in the Hereafter.
orig: ولأجر الآخرة خير للذين آمنوا وكانوا يتقون

translation: And Joseph's brothers came and entered upon him, and he recognized them, but they did not recognize him.
interpretation: This verse highlights the dramatic irony of the situation where Joseph recognizes his brothers who have come to Egypt seeking aid, but they do not recognize him as the brother they had wronged years ago. It sets the stage for the unfolding of Joseph's plan to test his brothers and ultimately forgive them, demonstrating the power of forgiveness and the hand of God in shaping destinies. The verse also underscores the contrast between Joseph's elevated status and his brothers' humbled position, showing how God can elevate those who remain faithful and patient in the face of adversity.
orig: وجاء إخوة يوسف فدخلوا عليه فعرفهم وهم له منكرون

translation: And when he had furnished them with their supplies, he said: "Bring unto me a brother of yours from your father. See ye not that I fill up the measure and I am the best of hosts?"
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of honesty and fairness in business dealings. The speaker, likely Joseph, is demonstrating his integrity by giving full measure and being a gracious host, even to those who had previously wronged him. It also highlights the value of family bonds, as Joseph requests to see his brother as a condition for further assistance. The verse suggests that even in difficult circumstances, one should strive to act with kindness and righteousness, trusting in God's plan and the power of forgiveness.
orig: ولما جهزهم بجهازهم قال ائتوني بأخ لكم من أبيكم ألا ترون أني أوفي الكيل وأنا خير المنزلين

translation: But if you do not bring him to me, then there will be no measure for you from me, nor will you approach me.
interpretation: This verse is a stern warning from a figure of authority, likely Prophet Yusuf (Joseph), to his brothers. He is telling them that if they do not bring their youngest brother to him as proof of their honesty, then he will not provide them with any more provisions and they will not be allowed to come near him or seek his help in the future. It demonstrates the seriousness of the demand being made and the consequences of failing to comply. The verse highlights themes of trust, integrity, and the importance of keeping one's word in dealings with others.
orig: فإن لم تأتوني به فلا كيل لكم عندي ولا تقربون

translation: They said, "We will try to get him from his father, and indeed, we will do it."
interpretation: This verse is referring to the brothers of Prophet Yusuf (Joseph) who were plotting to separate him from his father, Prophet Yaqub (Jacob). They were jealous of the love and affection their father had for Yusuf, so they devised a plan to get rid of him. The interpretation is that people can be driven by negative emotions like jealousy and envy to commit wrong actions, even against their own family members. It also highlights the importance of being aware of such feelings and striving to overcome them with good deeds and righteousness.
orig: قالوا سنراود عنه أباه وإنا لفاعلون

translation: And he said to his servants, "Put their merchandise back into their saddlebags so that they may recognize it when they return to their people, so that they may come back."
interpretation: This verse shows the wisdom and foresight of Prophet Yusuf (Joseph). By secretly returning the goods that his brothers had brought to trade, he hoped to give them a reason to come back to Egypt. This would allow him to keep his younger brother with him and to ultimately reunite with his family. It demonstrates Yusuf's strategic thinking and his desire to bring his family back together, despite the wrongs his brothers had committed against him in the past. The verse highlights the importance of forgiveness, wisdom, and planning in difficult situations.
orig: وقال لفتيانه اجعلوا بضاعتهم في رحالهم لعلهم يعرفونها إذا انقلبوا إلى أهلهم لعلهم يرجعون

translation: So when they returned to their father, they said, "O our father, [further] measure has been denied to us, so send with us our brother [that] we will be given measure. And indeed, we will be his guardians."
interpretation: In this verse, the brothers of Joseph return to their father Jacob after their second trip to Egypt, where they were denied further rations of grain unless they brought their youngest brother Benjamin with them. They plead with their father to send Benjamin, promising to protect him at all costs. This verse highlights the desperation of the brothers due to the famine and their willingness to risk taking Benjamin to Egypt in order to secure more food for their family. It also shows their attempt to convince Jacob to trust them with Benjamin's safety, despite their past betrayal of Joseph.
orig: فلما رجعوا إلى أبيهم قالوا يا أبانا منع منا الكيل فأرسل معنا أخانا نكتل وإنا له لحافظون

translation: He said, "Should I entrust him to you except [under coercion] as I entrusted his brother to you before? But Allah is the best guardian, and He is the most merciful of the merciful."
interpretation: This verse is interpreted as Jacob expressing his reluctance to send his youngest son Benjamin with his other sons to Egypt, as he had lost trust in them after they failed to protect Joseph before. Jacob acknowledges that only Allah can truly protect his son, and that He is the most merciful. It highlights the importance of putting one's trust in Allah and seeking His protection, rather than relying solely on human assurances. The verse also emphasizes Allah's attributes of being the best guardian and the most merciful.
orig: قال هل آمنكم عليه إلا كما أمنتكم على أخيه من قبل فالله خير حافظا وهو أرحم الراحمين

translation: And when they opened their baggage, they found their merchandise returned to them. They said, "O our father, what [more] could we desire? This is our merchandise returned to us. And we will obtain supplies for our family and protect our brother and obtain an increase of a camel's load; that is an easy measurement."
interpretation: This verse highlights the honesty and integrity of Prophet Joseph's brothers. Despite their past wrongdoings, they demonstrate a sense of responsibility towards their family by wanting to secure provisions, protect their younger brother, and fulfill their promise to their father. The returned merchandise is seen as a divine blessing and a sign of hope for their future sustenance. It also shows that God rewards those who seek forgiveness and strive to make amends for their past mistakes.
orig: ولما فتحوا متاعهم وجدوا بضاعتهم ردت إليهم قالوا يا أبانا ما نبغي هذه بضاعتنا ردت إلينا ونمير أهلنا ونحفظ أخانا ونزداد كيل بعير ذلك كيل يسير

translation: He said, "Never will I send him with you until you give me a promise by Allah that you will bring him [back] to me, unless you should be surrounded [i.e., overcome by enemies]." And when they had given him their promise, he said, "Allah, over what we say, is Witness."
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of trust and keeping promises. Jacob (peace be upon him) was reluctant to send his son Benjamin with his other sons to Egypt, fearing that harm might befall him as it did with Joseph. He demanded a solemn oath from them, invoking Allah's name, that they would bring Benjamin back safely unless they were completely overpowered by circumstances beyond their control. Once they gave their promise, Jacob entrusted the matter to Allah, emphasizing that Allah is the ultimate witness over their agreement and intentions. This demonstrates the significance of making sincere commitments, keeping promises, and relying on Allah's protection and guidance in all affairs.
orig: قال لن أرسله معكم حتى تؤتون موثقا من الله لتأتنني به إلا أن يحاط بكم فلما آتوه موثقهم قال الله على ما نقول وكيل

translation: And he said, "O my sons, do not enter from one gate but enter from different gates; and I cannot avail you against [the decree of] Allah at all. The decision is only for Allah; upon Him I have relied, and upon Him let those who would rely [indeed] rely."
interpretation: This verse is interpreted as a lesson in wisdom and reliance on Allah. Jacob advised his sons to enter the city through different gates as a precaution against drawing attention and potential harm. However, he acknowledged that ultimately, no one can protect against Allah's decree. The verse emphasizes the importance of taking practical measures while simultaneously having complete trust and reliance on Allah's will and divine plan. It highlights the balance between making an effort and recognizing that the final outcome is in Allah's hands alone.
orig: وقال يا بني لا تدخلوا من باب واحد وادخلوا من أبواب متفرقة وما أغني عنكم من الله من شيء إن الحكم إلا لله عليه توكلت وعليه فليتوكل المتوكلون

translation: And when they entered from where their father had ordered them, it did not avail them against Allah at all except [it was] a need within the soul of Jacob, which he satisfied. And indeed, he was a possessor of knowledge because of what We had taught him, but most of the people do not know.
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of trusting in Allah's plan and decree, regardless of the precautions one may take. Despite Jacob's sons following their father's advice to enter the city from different gates, it did not change what Allah had destined for them. The verse also emphasizes that Jacob's advice stemmed from his own personal concern and the knowledge Allah had granted him. However, most people fail to recognize that ultimately, it is Allah's will that prevails, and no human actions can alter His decree.
orig: ولما دخلوا من حيث أمرهم أبوهم ما كان يغني عنهم من الله من شيء إلا حاجة في نفس يعقوب قضاها وإنه لذو علم لما علمناه ولكن أكثر الناس لا يعلمون

translation: And when they entered upon Joseph, he took his brother to himself; he said, "Indeed, I am your brother, so do not despair over what they used to do [to me]."
interpretation: This verse is referring to the reunion between Prophet Joseph and his younger brother Benjamin. Joseph, who had been separated from his family for many years, finally reveals his true identity to Benjamin and comforts him, telling him not to feel saddened or guilty about what their other brothers had done to Joseph in the past. This moment represents the power of forgiveness, the unbreakable bond of brotherhood, and the relief that comes with reconciling after a long period of estrangement. It also showcases Joseph's maturity, wisdom, and ability to move past the wrongs committed against him, focusing instead on the joy of reuniting with his beloved brother.
orig: ولما دخلوا على يوسف آوى إليه أخاه قال إني أنا أخوك فلا تبتئس بما كانوا يعملون

translation: And when he had furnished them with their supplies, he put the [gold measuring] bowl into the bag of his brother. Then an announcer called out, "O caravan, indeed you are thieves."
interpretation: This verse is interpreted as a test of faith and honesty for Joseph's brothers. By placing the golden bowl in Benjamin's bag, Joseph creates a situation where his brothers are accused of theft. This tests their loyalty to Benjamin and their willingness to stand by him in the face of adversity. It also serves as a way for Joseph to keep Benjamin with him in Egypt while sending the others back to their father. The deeper meaning is that sometimes God tests our faith and integrity through difficult situations, and we must remain steadfast and trust in His plan even when things seem to be going against us.
orig: فلما جهزهم بجهازهم جعل السقاية في رحل أخيه ثم أذن مؤذن أيتها العير إنكم لسارقون

translation: They said, while approaching them, "What is it that you are missing?"
interpretation: This verse is likely referring to a group of people who have lost something and are being approached by others who are inquiring about what they have misplaced. The phrase "while approaching them" suggests that the questioners are coming closer to the group in order to engage with them and find out more about their situation. The direct and simple nature of the question "What is it that you are missing?" implies a sense of concern and willingness to help on the part of those asking. It is an opening to a conversation aimed at understanding the problem and potentially offering assistance in finding what has been lost.
orig: قالوا وأقبلوا عليهم ماذا تفقدون

translation: They said, "We are missing the measure of the king. And for he who produces it is [the reward of] a camel's load, and I am responsible for it."
interpretation: This verse is referring to the story of Prophet Joseph (Yusuf) and his brothers. The "measure of the king" is interpreted by many scholars to be a drinking cup belonging to the king that was secretly placed in the bag of Joseph's youngest brother Benjamin by Joseph's men as part of a plan to keep Benjamin with him in Egypt. When the caravan departed, it was announced that the king's cup was missing, and whoever returned it would be rewarded with a camel-load of provisions. The person making this announcement, likely one of Joseph's men, took personal responsibility ("and I am responsible for it") for delivering the reward, showing the gravity of the matter and perhaps to dispel any doubts about the reward being given. This announcement was part of Joseph's plan to create a situation where Benjamin would have to stay back, so that Joseph could ultimately reveal his identity to his brothers and test their character to see if they had changed since the time they had plotted against Joseph himself.
orig: قالوا نفقد صواع الملك ولمن جاء به حمل بعير وأنا به زعيم

translation: They said, "By Allah, you have certainly known that we did not come to cause corruption in the land, and we have not been thieves."
interpretation: In this verse, the brothers of Joseph are defending themselves against the accusation of theft. They invoke Allah's name to emphasize their innocence, asserting that their intentions were not to spread corruption or commit theft in the land. This highlights the importance of honesty and integrity in Islamic teachings, and the need to avoid false accusations. The brothers' response also demonstrates their faith in Allah and their willingness to rely on Him as a witness to their innocence.
orig: قالوا تالله لقد علمتم ما جئنا لنفسد في الأرض وما كنا سارقين

translation: They said, "Then what would be its recompense if you should be liars?"
interpretation: This verse is part of the story of Prophet Joseph (peace be upon him) in the Qur'an. When his brothers falsely accused him of theft, they were asked what punishment should be given to the thief. The question "Then what would be its recompense if you should be liars?" suggests that if the accusers are found to be lying about the theft, then they should face the same punishment that they propose for the alleged thief. It highlights the principle of justice in Islam, where false accusations and bearing false witness are considered grave sins and are subject to punishment. The verse also implies that one should be cautious and truthful when making accusations against others, as the consequences of lying can be severe.
orig: قالوا فما جزاؤه إن كنتم كاذبين

translation: They said, "The penalty for the one in whose bag it is found is [that] he [himself] will be its penalty. Thus do we recompense the wrongdoers."
interpretation: This verse reveals the brothers' suggestion of punishment for the alleged theft of the king's cup. They propose that whoever is found with the cup in his bag should himself become a slave as compensation. This shows their willingness to mete out a severe penalty without due process, indicating their own moral failings and readiness to wrong others. It reflects the principle that wrongdoers often suffer consequences similar to the wrongs they commit. The verse subtly critiques the brothers' hypocrisy and injustice, while affirming that God will ultimately ensure that the unjust face fitting repercussions for their misdeeds.
orig: قالوا جزاؤه من وجد في رحله فهو جزاؤه كذلك نجزي الظالمين

translation: So he began [the search] with their bags before the bag of his brother; then he extracted it from the bag of his brother. Thus did We plan for Joseph. He could not have taken his brother within the religion of the king except that Allah willed. We raise in degrees whom We will, but over every possessor of knowledge is one [more] knowing.
interpretation: This verse shows the wisdom and planning of Allah in helping Joseph retrieve his brother. Despite the laws of the land, Allah's will supersedes all and He can elevate whoever He wills with knowledge and status. It also highlights that there is always someone with more knowledge than anyone else, and ultimately all knowledge and wisdom belongs to Allah.
orig: فبدأ بأوعيتهم قبل وعاء أخيه ثم استخرجها من وعاء أخيه كذلك كدنا ليوسف ما كان ليأخذ أخاه في دين الملك إلا أن يشاء الله نرفع درجات من نشاء وفوق كل ذي علم عليم

translation: They said, "If he has stolen, a brother of his has stolen before." But Joseph kept it within himself and did not reveal it to them. He said, "You are in a worse position, and Allah is most knowing of what you describe."
interpretation: This verse sheds light on the wisdom and patience of Prophet Yusuf (Joseph) in the face of false accusations. When Yusuf's brothers accuse his younger brother Binyamin of theft, they try to justify their claim by saying that Yusuf had also stolen in the past. However, Yusuf keeps his composure and does not reveal his identity or the truth of the matter to them. Instead, he reminds them that their own actions and intentions are far worse in the sight of Allah. This demonstrates Yusuf's faith, maturity, and ability to handle difficult situations with grace and wisdom, trusting in Allah's knowledge and justice.
orig: قالوا إن يسرق فقد سرق أخ له من قبل فأسرها يوسف في نفسه ولم يبدها لهم قال أنتم شر مكانا والله أعلم بما تصفون

translation: They said, "O 'Azeez, indeed he has a father [who is] an old man, so take one of us in his place. Indeed, we see you as one of the doers of good."
interpretation: In this verse, the brothers of Joseph are pleading with the Egyptian minister (referred to as Al-'Azeez) to take one of them as a slave instead of Benjamin, who was caught with the king's cup in his bag. They appeal to the minister's sense of compassion, mentioning that Benjamin has an elderly father who would be devastated by the loss of his youngest son. The brothers hope that the minister, being a righteous man, would show mercy and accept their offer to substitute one of them for Benjamin. This verse highlights the brothers' concern for their father's well-being and their willingness to sacrifice their own freedom for the sake of their younger brother and father.
orig: قالوا يا أيها العزيز إن له أبا شيخا كبيرا فخذ أحدنا مكانه إنا نراك من المحسنين

translation: He said, "Allah forbid that we take except him with whom we found our possession. Indeed, we would then be wrongdoers."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of justice and fairness in Islam. The speaker, likely one of the brothers of Joseph, is saying that they would be committing a great wrong if they were to take anyone other than the person with whom their stolen goods were found. This highlights the Islamic principle of presumption of innocence and the need for evidence before accusing or punishing someone. It also shows the value placed on honesty and integrity, even in difficult situations where one may be tempted to act unjustly for personal gain or to protect oneself or loved ones.
orig: قال معاذ الله أن نأخذ إلا من وجدنا متاعنا عنده إنا إذا لظالمون

translation: So when they despaired of him, they secluded themselves in private consultation. The eldest of them said, "Do you not know that your father has taken upon you an oath by Allah and [that] before you failed in [your duty to] Joseph? So I will never leave [this] land until my father permits me or Allah decides for me, and He is the best of judges."
interpretation: The eldest brother's statement reflects his strong sense of responsibility and commitment to fulfilling the oath they made to their father. He recognizes the gravity of their past failure with Joseph and refuses to repeat the same mistake. His resolve to stay in Egypt until his father allows him to return or until Allah decrees otherwise demonstrates his submission to both parental authority and divine will. This highlights the importance of keeping promises, being accountable for one's actions, and trusting in Allah's wisdom and judgment.
orig: فلما استيأسوا منه خلصوا نجيا قال كبيرهم ألم تعلموا أن أباكم قد أخذ عليكم موثقا من الله ومن قبل ما فرطتم في يوسف فلن أبرح الأرض حتى يأذن لي أبي أو يحكم الله لي وهو خير الحاكمين

translation: Return to your father and say, "O our father, indeed your son has stolen, and we did not testify except to what we knew. And we were not guardians of the unseen."
interpretation: This verse is addressing the brothers of Joseph, instructing them to return to their father Jacob and inform him that Benjamin, Joseph's younger brother, has been accused of theft. The brothers are told to admit that they can only testify to what they have witnessed and that they had no knowledge of the unseen or future events. This highlights the concept of honesty and the importance of bearing witness only to the truth, even if it may be difficult or unpleasant. It also emphasizes the idea that human beings have limited knowledge and cannot predict or control the future, which is known only to God.
orig: ارجعوا إلى أبيكم فقولوا يا أبانا إن ابنك سرق وما شهدنا إلا بما علمنا وما كنا للغيب حافظين
