translation: And ask the town in which we were and the caravan in which we came; and indeed, we are truthful.
interpretation: This verse is emphasizing the importance of seeking verification and evidence to establish the truth. It suggests that if there is any doubt about the truthfulness of a claim or statement, one should seek corroboration from reliable sources or witnesses who can attest to the facts. The mention of the town and the caravan implies that there were people who could vouch for the truth of what was being said. The verse also underscores the value of honesty and integrity in speech and conduct, asserting that the speaker is being truthful in what they are saying.
orig: واسأل القرية التي كنا فيها والعير التي أقبلنا فيها وإنا لصادقون

translation: He said, "Rather, your souls have enticed you to something, so patience is most fitting. Perhaps Allah will bring them to me all together. Indeed, it is He who is the Knowing, the Wise."
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of patience and trust in Allah's plan during difficult times. Jacob (peace be upon him) demonstrates remarkable composure and faith, even after losing his beloved son Joseph and being presented with the supposed evidence of his death. He refuses to believe the worst and instead chooses to have hope and trust in Allah's wisdom. This teaches us that when faced with trials and tribulations, we should remain patient, keep faith in Allah's plan, and pray for His guidance and mercy. Ultimately, Allah is the All-Knowing and the All-Wise, and He has the power to restore what was lost and bring about the best outcome in any situation.
orig: قال بل سولت لكم أنفسكم أمرا فصبر جميل عسى الله أن يأتيني بهم جميعا إنه هو العليم الحكيم

translation: And he turned away from them and said, "Oh, my sorrow over Joseph," and his eyes became white from grief, for he was [of that] a suppressor.
interpretation: This verse shows the immense grief and sorrow that Prophet Jacob felt over the loss of his beloved son, Joseph. Despite the passage of many years, his pain remained raw and all-consuming, causing him to weep until he lost his eyesight. Yet, he bore this suffering with patience and did not openly express the depth of his anguish, choosing instead to suppress his emotions and turn to Allah for comfort and strength. This demonstrates the nobility of Jacob's character and his unwavering faith, even in the face of unimaginable hardship and heartbreak.
orig: وتولى عنهم وقال يا أسفى على يوسف وابيضت عيناه من الحزن فهو كظيم

translation: They said, "By Allah, you will not cease remembering Joseph until you become fatally ill or become of those who perish."
interpretation: This verse is a rebuke from Joseph's brothers to their father, Jacob, who continued to grieve and remember his beloved son Joseph long after he had been lost. The brothers express their frustration and concern, saying that Jacob's persistent mourning for Joseph would either cause him to become severely ill or lead to his death. It highlights the depth of Jacob's love and sorrow for his son, as well as the brothers' lack of empathy and understanding towards their father's emotional state. The verse also serves as a reminder of the profound impact that losing a loved one can have on an individual and the importance of dealing with grief in a healthy manner.
orig: قالوا تالله تفتأ تذكر يوسف حتى تكون حرضا أو تكون من الهالكين

translation: He said, "I only complain of my suffering and my grief to Allah, and I know from Allah that which you do not know."
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of turning to Allah in times of distress and hardship. The speaker, Prophet Yaqub (Jacob), expresses his deep faith and trust in Allah, acknowledging that he finds solace in pouring out his grief and sorrow to Him alone. It emphasizes the belief that Allah possesses knowledge and wisdom beyond human comprehension, and that believers should seek comfort and guidance from Him during difficult times. The verse encourages individuals to maintain a strong connection with Allah and to rely on Him for support and understanding, even when faced with challenges that others may not fully grasp.
orig: قال إنما أشكو بثي وحزني إلى الله وأعلم من الله ما لا تعلمون

translation: O my sons, go and find out about Joseph and his brother and despair not of relief from Allah. Indeed, no one despairs of relief from Allah except the disbelieving people.
interpretation: This verse encourages people to maintain hope and trust in Allah's mercy and support, even in the face of adversity or seemingly hopeless situations. It emphasizes that despair is a characteristic of disbelief, as true believers should always have faith in Allah's plan and the possibility of relief from hardship. The verse also highlights the importance of taking action and actively seeking solutions to problems, rather than passively accepting defeat or giving in to despair.
orig: يا بني اذهبوا فتحسسوا من يوسف وأخيه ولا تيأسوا من روح الله إنه لا ييأس من روح الله إلا القوم الكافرون

translation: And when they entered upon him, they said, "O 'Azeez, adversity has touched us and our family, and we have come with goods poor in quality, but give us full measure and be charitable to us. Indeed, Allah rewards the charitable."
interpretation: This verse highlights the humility and desperation of Prophet Yusuf's brothers when they came to him seeking food during the famine. Despite their past wrongdoings towards Yusuf, they acknowledged their difficult situation and appealed to the 'Azeez's (Yusuf's) generosity and kindness. They brought whatever goods they had, even if they were of poor quality, hoping that he would show mercy and provide them with the necessary provisions. The brothers also recognized that being charitable is a noble act that Allah rewards, thus encouraging the 'Azeez to be generous towards them in their time of need. This verse demonstrates the power of humility, seeking help, and relying on the kindness of others during hardships.
orig: فلما دخلوا عليه قالوا يا أيها العزيز مسنا وأهلنا الضر وجئنا ببضاعة مزجاة فأوف لنا الكيل وتصدق علينا إن الله يجزي المتصدقين

translation: He said, "Do you know what you did with Joseph and his brother when you were ignorant?"
interpretation: This verse is a powerful reminder of the importance of forgiveness and the consequences of our actions. It speaks to the moment when Joseph, who had been wronged by his brothers, reveals his true identity to them. Instead of seeking revenge, he asks them if they realize the gravity of what they had done to him and his brother out of ignorance and jealousy. This question is not meant to condemn them, but rather to encourage them to reflect on their past mistakes and seek forgiveness. It is a lesson for all of us to be mindful of how our actions, even those committed in ignorance, can have lasting impacts on others. At the same time, it emphasizes the power of forgiveness and the opportunity for redemption, as Joseph ultimately forgives his brothers and reconciles with them. This verse encourages us to approach others with compassion, understanding, and a willingness to forgive, just as we would hope to be forgiven for our own shortcomings.
orig: قال هل علمتم ما فعلتم بيوسف وأخيه إذ أنتم جاهلون

translation: They said, "Are you indeed Joseph?" He said, "I am Joseph, and this is my brother. Allah has certainly favored us. Indeed, he who fears Allah and is patient, then indeed, Allah does not allow to be lost the reward of those who do good."
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of piety, patience, and doing good deeds. Joseph, despite the hardships he faced, remained steadfast in his faith and was ultimately rewarded by Allah. It teaches us that even in the face of adversity, we should trust in Allah's plan and continue to do good, for Allah will never let the efforts of the righteous go to waste. The verse also emphasizes the value of recognizing and acknowledging Allah's favors and blessings upon us.
orig: قالوا أإنك لأنت يوسف قال أنا يوسف وهذا أخي قد من الله علينا إنه من يتق ويصبر فإن الله لا يضيع أجر المحسنين

translation: They said, "By Allah, certainly has Allah preferred you over us, and indeed, we have been sinners."
interpretation: This verse reflects the brothers of Joseph acknowledging their wrongdoing and recognizing the favored status that Allah has bestowed upon Joseph. It is an admission of their past sins and transgressions against their brother, coupled with a realization that despite their actions, Allah has elevated Joseph's rank and position above them. This interpretation highlights the theme of repentance and the acknowledgment of divine wisdom in the face of human shortcomings.
orig: قالوا تالله لقد آثرك الله علينا وإن كنا لخاطئين

translation: He said, "No blame will there be upon you today. Allah will forgive you, and He is the most merciful of the merciful."
interpretation: This verse demonstrates the immense mercy and forgiveness of Allah. Even when someone has committed a grave wrong, if they sincerely repent, Allah is willing to forgive them completely. The verse also shows the noble character of Prophet Yusuf (Joseph), who forgave his brothers despite the great harm they had done to him. It teaches us to let go of grudges and to be forgiving towards others, knowing that Allah is the Most Merciful and will forgive us for our own shortcomings if we turn to Him in repentance.
orig: قال لا تثريب عليكم اليوم يغفر الله لكم وهو أرحم الراحمين

translation: Go with this shirt of mine and cast it over the face of my father; he will become seeing. And bring me your family, all together.
interpretation: This verse is interpreted as a demonstration of the power of faith and the mercy of Allah. The shirt of Yusuf (Joseph) is seen as a symbol of his righteousness and closeness to Allah. By casting the shirt over his father's face, Yusuf is able to restore his father's sight, both physically and spiritually. This miraculous event is a sign of Allah's favor upon Yusuf and his family. The verse also emphasizes the importance of family unity, as Yusuf instructs his brothers to bring their entire family to him. This reunion is seen as a blessing from Allah and a reward for Yusuf's patience and perseverance through his trials.
orig: اذهبوا بقميصي هذا فألقوه على وجه أبي يأت بصيرا وأتوني بأهلكم أجمعين

translation: And when the caravan departed, their father said, "Indeed, I find the smell of Joseph [and would say that he was alive] if you did not think me weakened in mind."
interpretation: This verse speaks to the deep connection and love between a father and his son. Even though Joseph had been separated from his father Jacob for many years, Jacob could still sense his presence and smell his scent when the caravan carrying Joseph's shirt passed by. It demonstrates the powerful bond of family and the unwavering hope and faith that Jacob had in being reunited with his beloved son, despite the doubts and skepticism of those around him who thought his mind was failing in old age. The verse highlights the strength of a parent's love and the spiritual connection that can transcend physical distance and time.
orig: ولما فصلت العير قال أبوهم إني لأجد ريح يوسف لولا أن تفندون

translation: They said, "By Allah, indeed you are in your [same] old error."
interpretation: This verse is referring to the response of Prophet Joseph's brothers when he revealed his true identity to them. They realized that they had been wrong about him all along, and that he was not the evil person they had assumed him to be. The verse highlights their amazement and shock at the realization of their past misjudgment. It also emphasizes the fact that often, our preconceived notions and biases can lead us astray and cause us to misjudge others. The verse serves as a reminder to be open-minded and not to jump to conclusions about others based on limited information or past misconceptions.
orig: قالوا تالله إنك لفي ضلالك القديم

translation: And when the bearer of good tidings arrived, he cast it upon his face, and he returned [once again] seeing. He said, "Did I not tell you that I know from Allah that which you do not know?"
interpretation: This verse is a powerful reminder of the importance of trusting in Allah's plan and having faith in His wisdom. The arrival of the bearer of good tidings, who cast the shirt upon Jacob's face and restored his vision, symbolizes the relief and joy that comes from remaining steadfast in the face of adversity. Jacob's words to his sons serve as a gentle admonishment, emphasizing that his unwavering trust in Allah's knowledge and guidance sustained him through the darkest of times. This verse encourages believers to cultivate a deep connection with Allah, seeking solace and strength in His infinite wisdom, even when faced with trials and tribulations that may seem insurmountable.
orig: فلما أن جاء البشير ألقاه على وجهه فارتد بصيرا قال ألم أقل لكم إني أعلم من الله ما لا تعلمون

translation: They said, "O our father, ask for us forgiveness of our sins; indeed, we have been sinners."
interpretation: In this verse, the brothers of Joseph acknowledge their wrongdoing and seek forgiveness from their father, Jacob. This demonstrates the importance of repentance and seeking forgiveness in Islam. It also highlights the role of parents in guiding their children and the respect that children should have for their parents. The verse emphasizes the significance of admitting one's mistakes, expressing remorse, and turning to Allah for forgiveness, as it is only through His mercy that one can attain salvation and spiritual growth.
orig: قالوا يا أبانا استغفر لنا ذنوبنا إنا كنا خاطئين

translation: He said, "I will ask forgiveness for you from my Lord. Indeed, it is He who is the Forgiving, the Merciful."
interpretation: This verse shows the importance of seeking forgiveness from Allah through the intercession of righteous people. It demonstrates the mercy and forgiveness of Allah towards those who sincerely repent and seek His pardon. The verse also highlights the role of prophets and righteous individuals in guiding people towards repentance and seeking Allah's forgiveness. It emphasizes the importance of having faith in Allah's mercy and forgiveness, and the need to constantly seek His pardon for one's shortcomings and sins.
orig: قال سوف أستغفر لكم ربي إنه هو الغفور الرحيم

translation: Then, when they entered upon Joseph, he took his parents to himself and said, "Enter Egypt, Allah willing, safe [and secure]."
interpretation: This verse shows the great respect and love that Prophet Yusuf (Joseph) had for his parents. After being separated from them for many years due to the plotting of his brothers, he was finally reunited with them in Egypt. He warmly welcomed them, giving them an honorable reception and reassuring them of their safety and security in the land by the will of Allah. This demonstrates the importance of honoring one's parents and treating them with utmost kindness, even after attaining a high position of power and authority. It also reflects Yusuf's continued faith and reliance on Allah, acknowledging that their well-being and future in Egypt was ultimately in Allah's hands.
orig: فلما دخلوا على يوسف آوى إليه أبويه وقال ادخلوا مصر إن شاء الله آمنين

translation: And he raised his parents upon the throne, and they bowed to him in prostration. And he said, "O my father, this is the interpretation of my vision of before. My Lord has made it reality. And He was certainly good to me when He took me out of prison and brought you [here] from bedouin life after Satan had induced [estrangement] between me and my brothers. Indeed, my Lord is Subtle in what He wills. Indeed, it is He who is the Knowing, the Wise."
interpretation: This verse shows the fulfillment of Joseph's dream and the power of Allah in making it come true. It highlights the importance of patience, faith, and forgiveness. Despite the hardships Joseph faced, he remained steadfast in his belief, and Allah rewarded him by reuniting him with his family and elevating his status. The verse also emphasizes the subtle ways in which Allah works and His ultimate wisdom and knowledge in all affairs. It teaches us to trust in Allah's plan and to forgive those who have wronged us, as Joseph forgave his brothers for their past misdeeds.
orig: ورفع أبويه على العرش وخروا له سجدا وقال يا أبت هذا تأويل رؤياي من قبل قد جعلها ربي حقا وقد أحسن بي إذ أخرجني من السجن وجاء بكم من البدو من بعد أن نزغ الشيطان بيني وبين إخوتي إن ربي لطيف لما يشاء إنه هو العليم الحكيم

translation: My Lord, You have given me [something] of sovereignty and taught me of the interpretation of dreams. Creator of the heavens and earth, You are my protector in this world and in the Hereafter. Cause me to die a Muslim and join me with the righteous.
interpretation: This verse can be interpreted as a heartfelt supplication to Allah, acknowledging His blessings and seeking His guidance. The speaker, Prophet Yusuf (Joseph), recognizes that Allah has bestowed upon him a position of authority and the gift of interpreting dreams. He attributes these blessings to Allah alone, addressing Him as the Creator of the heavens and earth, and affirming His protection in both this world and the Hereafter. The Prophet humbly prays to Allah to allow him to die as a Muslim, in a state of complete submission to His will, and to join him with the righteous in the afterlife. This interpretation highlights the importance of recognizing Allah's favors, seeking His guidance, and striving to live and die as a faithful Muslim.
orig: رب قد آتيتني من الملك وعلمتني من تأويل الأحاديث فاطر السماوات والأرض أنت وليي في الدنيا والآخرة توفني مسلما وألحقني بالصالحين

translation: That is from the news of the unseen which We reveal to you, [O Muhammad]. And you were not with them when they put together their plan while they conspired.
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine source of the Qur'an and the knowledge it contains. It emphasizes that the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) had no way of knowing the details of the past events mentioned in the Qur'an, as he was not present when the people of the past conspired and plotted against the messengers of Allah. The verse serves as a proof of the Qur'an's authenticity and the Prophet's truthfulness, as the information revealed to him could have only come from Allah, the All-Knowing, Who is aware of the unseen and the secrets of the past and future. It also implies that the disbelievers' plots against the Prophet will ultimately fail, just as the plots of the past nations against their prophets failed, and that Allah's will and support will always prevail.
orig: ذلك من أنباء الغيب نوحيه إليك وما كنت لديهم إذ أجمعوا أمرهم وهم يمكرون

translation: And most of the people, although you strive [for it], are not believers.
interpretation: This verse suggests that no matter how much effort the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) puts into conveying the message of Islam and calling people to faith, the majority of people will still choose not to believe. It highlights the reality that faith is a matter of individual choice and that guidance ultimately comes from Allah. The Prophet's role is to deliver the message clearly, but he cannot force anyone to accept it. This verse also serves as a consolation to the Prophet, letting him know that he should not be disheartened by the rejection of his message by many people, as this is the nature of human free will.
orig: وما أكثر الناس ولو حرصت بمؤمنين

translation: And you do not ask them for any reward for it; it is not but a reminder to the worlds.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) did not seek any worldly gain or reward for conveying the message of Islam. His sole purpose was to remind and guide all of humanity to the path of righteousness, as the Qur'an is a universal message meant for all people, regardless of their background or status. The Prophet's selfless dedication to his mission demonstrates the sincerity and purity of his intentions, as well as the divine nature of the Qur'an itself.
orig: وما تسألهم عليه من أجر إن هو إلا ذكر للعالمين

translation: And how many a sign within the heavens and earth do they pass over while they, therefrom, are turning away.
interpretation: This verse is a reminder that there are countless signs of Allah's existence and power all around us in the heavens and the earth, yet many people pass by them without paying attention or reflecting on their significance. They are so caught up in their worldly lives and pursuits that they fail to recognize and appreciate these signs. The verse is a call to open our eyes and hearts to the wonders of Allah's creation, and to turn towards Him in gratitude and worship. It encourages us to be mindful and contemplative, rather than heedless and distracted, as we journey through life.
orig: وكأين من آية في السماوات والأرض يمرون عليها وهم عنها معرضون

translation: And most of them believe not in Allah except while they associate others with Him.
interpretation: This verse suggests that even though many people claim to believe in Allah, their belief is not pure or complete because they still associate partners with Him. They may worship other beings or forces alongside Allah, or attribute some of His divine attributes to others. True belief in Allah requires dedicating one's worship and devotion exclusively to Him alone, without setting up any rivals or equals. Ascribing partners to Allah nullifies one's faith, as it goes against the fundamental principle of Islam, which is the oneness and uniqueness of Allah.
orig: وما يؤمن أكثرهم بالله إلا وهم مشركون

translation: Then do they feel secure that there will not come to them an overwhelming [aspect] of the punishment of Allah or that the Hour will not come upon them suddenly while they do not perceive?
interpretation: This verse is a warning to those who are heedless of Allah's signs and do not fear His punishment. It reminds us that the punishment of Allah can come upon us at any time, without warning, and that the Day of Judgment will also come suddenly, catching many people unaware. The verse implies that we should always be mindful of our actions and strive to obey Allah, so that we may be prepared for what is to come. It also suggests that feeling secure and complacent in this world is a dangerous attitude, as it can lead to neglecting our spiritual duties and being caught off guard when faced with the realities of the Hereafter.
orig: أفأمنوا أن تأتيهم غاشية من عذاب الله أو تأتيهم الساعة بغتة وهم لا يشعرون

translation: Say, "This is my way; I invite to Allah with insight, I and those who follow me. And exalted is Allah; and I am not of those who associate others with Him."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of inviting others to the path of Allah with clear knowledge and insight. The Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) is instructed to declare that this is his way, and that he and his followers call people to the worship of Allah alone, based on clear evidence and understanding. The verse also includes the proclamation of Allah's perfection and the Prophet's disavowal of shirk (associating partners with Allah). It highlights the significance of having a strong foundation in knowledge when spreading the message of Islam and the necessity of doing so with sincerity and humility, acknowledging Allah's greatness and oneness.
orig: قل هذه سبيلي أدعو إلى الله على بصيرة أنا ومن اتبعني وسبحان الله وما أنا من المشركين

translation: And We sent not before you except men to whom We revealed [Our message] from among the people of the towns. So have they not traveled through the earth and observed how was the end of those before them? And the home of the Hereafter is best for those who fear Allah; then will you not reason?
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that all the prophets and messengers sent by Allah were human beings, chosen from among the people of various towns and cities. They were not supernatural beings, but rather ordinary men inspired with divine revelation. The verse encourages people to travel, explore the world, and learn from the history of past nations. It reminds them to consider the fate of those who rejected the message of Allah and to realize that the ultimate reward in the eternal life of the Hereafter is reserved for those who are righteous and mindful of Allah. The verse concludes with a powerful rhetorical question, challenging humankind to use their intellect, reason, and reflect upon the lessons of history and the wisdom behind Allah's message.
orig: وما أرسلنا من قبلك إلا رجالا نوحي إليهم من أهل القرى أفلم يسيروا في الأرض فينظروا كيف كان عاقبة الذين من قبلهم ولدار الآخرة خير للذين اتقوا أفلا تعقلون

translation: Until, when the messengers despaired and were certain that they had been denied, there came to them Our victory, and whoever We willed was saved. And Our punishment cannot be repelled from the people who are criminals.
interpretation: This verse highlights the unwavering faith and perseverance of the messengers of Allah, even in the face of adversity and rejection. Despite facing immense challenges and feeling despair, they remained steadfast in their belief and mission. The verse emphasizes that Allah's help and victory will ultimately come to those who remain patient and true to their faith, while the wrongdoers and criminals will face the consequences of their actions, unable to escape divine retribution. It serves as a reminder to believers to trust in Allah's plan and remain hopeful, even during difficult times, as His support will always be there for those who strive in His cause.
orig: حتى إذا استيأس الرسل وظنوا أنهم قد كذبوا جاءهم نصرنا فنجي من نشاء ولا يرد بأسنا عن القوم المجرمين

translation: There was certainly in their stories a lesson for those of understanding. Never was the Qur'an a narration invented, but a confirmation of what was before it and a detailed explanation of all things and guidance and mercy for a people who believe.
interpretation: The stories of the past prophets and nations in the Qur'an contain profound wisdom and lessons for those who reflect and ponder. These Quranic narratives are not mere tales or legends invented by Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ), but rather a divine revelation that confirms the core message of previous scriptures while providing a comprehensive elucidation of all aspects of faith and life. The Qur'an serves as a guide and a mercy for those who sincerely believe in Allah, steering them towards righteousness and the path of salvation.
orig: لقد كان في قصصهم عبرة لأولي الألباب ما كان حديثا يفترى ولكن تصديق الذي بين يديه وتفصيل كل شيء وهدى ورحمة لقوم يؤمنون

translation: Alif, Lam, Meem, Ra. These are the verses of the Book and what has been revealed to you from your Lord is the truth, but most of the people do not believe.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the divine origin and truthfulness of the Qur'an, which was revealed to Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) by Allah. Despite the clear evidence and the truth contained within the Qur'an, the majority of people still do not believe in its message. This highlights the stubborn nature of human beings who often reject the truth even when it is presented to them clearly. The verse also serves as a reminder for the believers to remain steadfast in their faith, knowing that the Qur'an is the ultimate truth from their Lord, regardless of the disbelief of others around them.
orig: المر تلك آيات الكتاب والذي أنزل إليك من ربك الحق ولكن أكثر الناس لا يؤمنون

translation: It is Allah who erected the heavens without pillars that you [can] see; then He established Himself above the Throne and made subject the sun and the moon, each running [its course] for a specified term. He arranges [each] matter; He details the signs that you may, of the meeting with your Lord, be certain.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's omnipotence and sovereignty over the universe. The fact that He raised the heavens without visible pillars is a testament to His immense power. His establishment on the Throne signifies His supreme authority and control over all creation. The subjugation of the sun and moon, which follow precise orbits for a designated time, further highlights Allah's absolute command over the cosmos. By meticulously arranging every affair and providing clear signs, Allah enables humans to attain certainty in the inevitability of meeting their Lord on the Day of Judgment. This verse serves as a powerful reminder for mankind to recognize Allah's greatness and to live in preparation for the ultimate encounter with Him.
orig: الله الذي رفع السماوات بغير عمد ترونها ثم استوى على العرش وسخر الشمس والقمر كل يجري لأجل مسمى يدبر الأمر يفصل الآيات لعلكم بلقاء ربكم توقنون

translation: And it is He who spread the earth and placed therein firmly set mountains and rivers; and from all of the fruits He made therein two mates; He causes the night to cover the day. Indeed in that are signs for a people who give thought.
interpretation: This verse highlights Allah's power and wisdom in creating the earth and everything in it. The mountains and rivers serve important purposes, providing stability and nourishment for life. The creation of fruits in pairs demonstrates the perfect balance and design in nature. The alternation of night and day is a sign of Allah's control over the universe. These are all indications for people who reflect deeply and recognize the existence and greatness of the Creator behind the intricate systems and beauty of the world around us.
orig: وهو الذي مد الأرض وجعل فيها رواسي وأنهارا ومن كل الثمرات جعل فيها زوجين اثنين يغشي الليل النهار إن في ذلك لآيات لقوم يتفكرون

translation: And within the land are neighboring plots and gardens of grapevines and crops and palm trees, [growing] several from a root or otherwise, watered with one water; but We make some of them exceed others in [quality of] fruit. Indeed in that are signs for a people who reason.
interpretation: This verse highlights the diversity and variety in Allah's creation, even within the same species of plants and fruits that grow side by side and share the same water source. Yet, Allah causes some of them to be superior in quality and taste over others. This is a sign for people who use their intellect to reflect on the wisdom, power and precise measure with which Allah creates things in His universe. It invites us to ponder and appreciate the beauty and bounty that Allah has placed in the world as a blessing for mankind.
orig: وفي الأرض قطع متجاورات وجنات من أعناب وزرع ونخيل صنوان وغير صنوان يسقى بماء واحد ونفضل بعضها على بعض في الأكل إن في ذلك لآيات لقوم يعقلون

translation: And if you are astonished, [O Muhammad], astonishing is their saying, "When we are dust, will we indeed be [brought] into a new creation?" Those are the ones who have disbelieved in their Lord, and those will have shackles upon their necks, and those are the companions of the Fire; they will abide therein eternally.
interpretation: This verse expresses amazement at the disbelievers' denial of resurrection and their incredulity towards the idea of being brought back to life after death when their bodies have decomposed into dust. It suggests that such denial stems from a fundamental lack of faith in God's power and ability to create anew. As a consequence of their disbelief, they are described as being shackled and doomed to eternal punishment in the Fire of Hell. The imagery of shackles around their necks symbolizes their enslavement to their own disbelief and their inability to free themselves from its consequences. Overall, the verse warns of the severe repercussions of rejecting faith in God and the Day of Resurrection.
orig: وإن تعجب فعجب قولهم أإذا كنا ترابا أإنا لفي خلق جديد أولئك الذين كفروا بربهم وأولئك الأغلال في أعناقهم وأولئك أصحاب النار هم فيها خالدون

translation: And they ask you to hasten the evil before the good, while there has already occurred before them similar punishments [to what they demand]. And indeed, your Lord is full of forgiveness for the people despite their wrongdoing, and indeed, your Lord is severe in penalty.
interpretation: This verse highlights the impatience and shortsightedness of some people who mockingly ask the Prophet to bring about the divine punishment they have been warned about, rather than praying for God's mercy and forgiveness. It emphasizes that although God is forgiving towards those who have wronged themselves through their misdeeds, He has also punished past nations for their transgressions as a lesson for humanity. The verse serves as a reminder that while God's mercy is vast, one should not take it for granted or test His limits, for His punishment, when it comes, is severe for those who persistently reject the truth and act with arrogance.
orig: ويستعجلونك بالسيئة قبل الحسنة وقد خلت من قبلهم المثلات وإن ربك لذو مغفرة للناس على ظلمهم وإن ربك لشديد العقاب

translation: And those who disbelieve say, "Why has a sign not been sent down to him from his Lord?" You are only a warner, and for every people is a guide.
interpretation: This verse addresses the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and the disbelievers who demand a miraculous sign from God as proof of his prophethood. It asserts that Muhammad's role is to serve as a warner, reminding people of the consequences of their actions and the importance of faith. The verse also emphasizes that for every community, God has appointed a guide to lead them to the right path. This suggests that divine guidance is available to all people, regardless of their background or circumstances, and that the ultimate responsibility lies with each individual to heed the warning and follow the guidance provided to them.
orig: ويقول الذين كفروا لولا أنزل عليه آية من ربه إنما أنت منذر ولكل قوم هاد

translation: Allah knows what every female carries and what the wombs lose [prematurely] or exceed. And everything with Him is by due measure.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the omniscience of Allah, particularly in relation to the mysteries of human reproduction. It underscores that Allah has complete knowledge of what happens in the womb during pregnancy, including miscarriages, premature births, and prolonged pregnancies. The verse also highlights that everything in the universe, including these aspects of human life, is precisely measured and ordained by Allah. This interpretation suggests that believers should trust in Allah's wisdom and knowledge, even in matters that may seem uncertain or beyond human understanding, such as the outcomes of pregnancy and childbirth.
orig: الله يعلم ما تحمل كل أنثى وما تغيض الأرحام وما تزداد وكل شيء عنده بمقدار

translation: Knower of the unseen and the witnessed, the Grand, the Exalted.
interpretation: This verse refers to two of the beautiful names and attributes of Allah: Al-Aleem (The All-Knowing) and Al-Mutaal (The Exalted One). It emphasizes that Allah has complete knowledge of all things, whether they are unseen by human beings (like the matters of the unseen realm) or visible and apparent (the physical world). Nothing is hidden from His knowledge. The verse also highlights Allah's grandeur and sublimity, that He is exalted above all of His creation. It is a reminder for us to be in awe of Allah's infinite knowledge and majesty, and to humble ourselves before Him, as He alone is truly great and deserving of all praise and glorification.
orig: عالم الغيب والشهادة الكبير المتعال

translation: It is the same [to Him] concerning you whether one conceals [his] speech or publicizes it and whether one is hidden by night or conspicuous [among others] by day.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the all-encompassing knowledge and awareness of Allah. It conveys that Allah knows everything about His creatures, whether they express themselves secretly or openly, and whether they hide under the cover of the night or go about their business during the day. It highlights that nothing is hidden from Allah, and He is fully aware of all our actions, intentions, and even our innermost thoughts. This verse serves as a reminder for believers to be mindful of Allah at all times and to strive for sincerity and righteousness in their deeds, knowing that Allah is always watching over them.
orig: سواء منكم من أسر القول ومن جهر به ومن هو مستخف بالليل وسارب بالنهار

translation: For each one are successive [angels] before and behind him who protect him by the decree of Allah. Indeed, Allah will not change the condition of a people until they change what is in themselves. And when Allah intends for a people ill, there is no repelling it. And there is not for them besides Him any patron.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the concept of divine protection and the role of personal responsibility in one's fate. It suggests that God assigns angels to protect each person, but this protection is contingent upon the person's own actions and inner state. The verse implies that God will not change the condition of a people for the better unless they first change themselves for the better. Conversely, if a people's actions and inner state warrant misfortune, nothing can prevent God's will from being carried out, and they will have no protector other than Him. The interpretation is that while God's protection and decree play a role, each person and community is ultimately responsible for their own destiny through their actions and spiritual state.
orig: له معقبات من بين يديه ومن خلفه يحفظونه من أمر الله إن الله لا يغير ما بقوم حتى يغيروا ما بأنفسهم وإذا أراد الله بقوم سوءا فلا مرد له وما لهم من دونه من وال

translation: It is He who shows you the lightning, [causing] fear and aspiration, and generates the heavy clouds.
interpretation: This verse highlights Allah's power and control over natural phenomena. The lightning that we witness is a manifestation of His might, instilling both fear and hope in our hearts. Fear, because it reminds us of our vulnerability and His supreme authority; and hope, because lightning is often followed by rain-bearing clouds that bring life and sustenance to the earth. The formation of heavy clouds, too, is an act of Allah's creation and a sign of His mercy towards His creatures. This verse invites us to reflect on these marvels of nature and appreciate the greatness of our Creator.
orig: هو الذي يريكم البرق خوفا وطمعا وينشئ السحاب الثقال

translation: And the thunder exalts [Allah] with praise of Him - and the angels [as well] from fear of Him - and He sends thunderbolts and strikes therewith whom He wills while they dispute about Allah; and He is severe in assault.
interpretation: This verse highlights the immense power and majesty of Allah. The thunder and the angels glorify Him out of reverence and awe, acknowledging His supremacy over all creation. Allah's ability to send thunderbolts and strike whomever He wills serves as a reminder of His ultimate control and authority, even as some people dare to dispute about Him. The verse emphasizes that Allah is mighty in His punishment, capable of severely penalizing those who reject or challenge Him. It serves as a warning to humankind to recognize Allah's sovereignty and submit to Him, rather than engaging in futile arguments against Him.
orig: ويسبح الرعد بحمده والملائكة من خيفته ويرسل الصواعق فيصيب بها من يشاء وهم يجادلون في الله وهو شديد المحال

translation: For Him [alone] is the supplication of truth. And those they call upon besides Him do not respond to them with a thing, except as one who stretches his hands toward water [from afar, calling it] to reach his mouth, but it will not reach it. And the supplication of the disbelievers is not but in error [i.e. futility].
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that only Allah has the power to answer prayers and fulfill supplications. Those who invoke others besides Him, such as idols or false deities, will not receive any response, just like a thirsty person desperately reaching out for water from a distance, but unable to quench their thirst. It highlights the futility and misguidance of the disbelievers who direct their prayers and worship to anyone other than Allah, as their supplications are ultimately in vain and will lead them astray.
orig: له دعوة الحق والذين يدعون من دونه لا يستجيبون لهم بشيء إلا كباسط كفيه إلى الماء ليبلغ فاه وما هو ببالغه وما دعاء الكافرين إلا في ضلال

translation: And to Allah prostrates whoever is within the heavens and the earth, willingly or by compulsion, and their shadows [as well] in the mornings and the afternoons.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute sovereignty and power of Allah over all of His creation. It states that every being in the heavens and the earth, whether living or inanimate, submits to Allah's will and prostrates before Him. This prostration is either voluntary, out of love and obedience, or involuntary, as a manifestation of Allah's supreme control over all things. Even the shadows cast by these beings prostrate, acknowledging Allah's might and authority at all times of the day. This verse serves as a powerful reminder for humans to humble themselves before their Creator and submit to His will, recognizing that everything in existence is subservient to Him.
orig: ولله يسجد من في السماوات والأرض طوعا وكرها وظلالهم بالغدو والآصال

translation: Say, "Who is Lord of the heavens and earth?" Say, "Allah." Say, "Have you then taken besides Him allies not possessing [even] for themselves any benefit or any harm?" Say, "Is the blind equivalent to the seeing? Or is darkness equivalent to light? Or have they attributed to Allah partners who created like His creation so that the creation [of each] seemed similar to them?" Say, "Allah is the Creator of all things, and He is the One, the Prevailing."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute power and authority of Allah as the sole Creator and Sustainer of the universe. It challenges the idea of taking any other beings or entities as allies or partners alongside Allah, as they possess no power to benefit or harm themselves, let alone others. The verse also highlights the vast difference between the truth and falsehood, comparing the blind to the seeing and darkness to light. It asserts that attributing partners to Allah who claim to have created like His creation is a false notion, as Allah alone is the Creator of all things and the One who prevails over all.
orig: قل من رب السماوات والأرض قل الله قل أفاتخذتم من دونه أولياء لا يملكون لأنفسهم نفعا ولا ضرا قل هل يستوي الأعمى والبصير أم هل تستوي الظلمات والنور أم جعلوا لله شركاء خلقوا كخلقه فتشابه الخلق عليهم قل الله خالق كل شيء وهو الواحد القهار

translation: He sends down water from the sky, and the valleys flow according to their capacity, and the flood carries a rising foam. And from that [ore] which they heat in the fire, desiring adornments and utensils, is a foam like it. Thus Allah presents [the example of] truth and falsehood. As for the foam, it vanishes, [being] cast off; but as for that which benefits the people, it remains on the earth. Thus does Allah present examples.
interpretation: This verse draws a powerful analogy between the ephemeral nature of falsehood and the enduring quality of truth. Just as the foam that rises to the surface during a flood is quickly swept away, leaving behind the life-giving water that sustains the earth, falsehood may appear alluring and substantial in the moment but ultimately dissipates and leaves no lasting value. In contrast, truth, represented by the water that nourishes the land and benefits humanity, endures and provides ongoing sustenance and guidance. The verse also suggests that people's hearts and minds, like valleys, have varying capacities to absorb and retain divine wisdom. The choice of this metaphor encourages introspection about one's own receptiveness to truth and the importance of seeking out and holding fast to what is authentic and beneficial, while letting go of fleeting distractions and deceptions.
orig: أنزل من السماء ماء فسالت أودية بقدرها فاحتمل السيل زبدا رابيا ومما يوقدون عليه في النار ابتغاء حلية أو متاع زبد مثله كذلك يضرب الله الحق والباطل فأما الزبد فيذهب جفاء وأما ما ينفع الناس فيمكث في الأرض كذلك يضرب الله الأمثال

translation: For those who have responded to their Lord is the best [reward], but those who did not respond to Him - if they had all that is in the earth entirely and the like of it with it, they would [attempt to] ransom themselves thereby. Those will have the worst account, and their refuge is Hell, and wretched is the resting place.
interpretation: This verse highlights the stark contrast between those who obey and respond to Allah versus those who turn away from Him. Those who heed Allah's call and follow His guidance will be rewarded with the very best in the Hereafter. On the other hand, those who reject Allah's message would be willing to give up everything they possess in this world and more to save themselves from the severe punishment that awaits them on the Day of Judgment. However, no amount of ransom or worldly wealth will be accepted from them. They will face a terrible reckoning and will be consigned to the Hellfire, which is the worst possible abode. This verse serves as a strong reminder for mankind to respond to Allah's call and follow the righteous path to avoid a grievous fate in the Hereafter.
orig: للذين استجابوا لربهم الحسنى والذين لم يستجيبوا له لو أن لهم ما في الأرض جميعا ومثله معه لافتدوا به أولئك لهم سوء الحساب ومأواهم جهنم وبئس المهاد

translation: Then is he who knows that what has been revealed to you from your Lord is the truth like one who is blind? They will only be reminded who are people of understanding.
interpretation: This verse highlights the stark contrast between those who recognize and accept the truth of Allah's revelations and those who are spiritually blind to it. Those endowed with understanding and wisdom will reflect upon the Qur'an and take heed of its teachings, while the ignorant will remain unmindful. It emphasizes that true insight and guidance come from acknowledging the divine truth and applying the lessons of the Qur'an in one's life. The "people of understanding" mentioned here are those who use their intellect to discern right from wrong and make choices that align with Allah's guidance.
orig: أفمن يعلم أنما أنزل إليك من ربك الحق كمن هو أعمى إنما يتذكر أولو الألباب

translation: Those who fulfill the covenant of Allah and do not break the contract.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of being true to one's commitments and promises, especially those made with Allah. It highlights the virtuous character of those who consistently honor their pledges, agreements, and covenants, considering them sacred and binding. Such individuals are praised for their trustworthiness, reliability, and unwavering loyalty in fulfilling their obligations, both in their relationship with Allah and with fellow human beings. The verse implies that breaking promises and violating contracts is a grave sin that goes against the teachings of Islam and the character of a true believer.
orig: الذين يوفون بعهد الله ولا ينقضون الميثاق

translation: And those who join that which Allah has ordered to be joined and fear their Lord and are afraid of the evil of [their] account.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of maintaining the ties of kinship and other relationships that Allah has commanded us to uphold. It also highlights the significance of having consciousness and fear of Allah, especially when it comes to our deeds and actions, as we will be held accountable for them on the Day of Judgment. Those who are mindful of this reality strive to maintain good relations with others, fulfill their obligations, and refrain from severing the bonds that Allah has ordered us to keep intact, such as family ties and social contracts. They do so out of obedience to Allah and fear of the consequences of their actions in the Hereafter.
orig: والذين يصلون ما أمر الله به أن يوصل ويخشون ربهم ويخافون سوء الحساب

translation: And those who are patient, seeking the countenance of their Lord, and establish prayer and spend from what We have provided for them secretly and publicly and prevent evil with good - those will have the good consequence of [this] home.
interpretation: This verse highlights the qualities of the righteous believers who will be rewarded with Paradise in the Hereafter. They are those who remain steadfast in their faith and obedience to Allah, seeking His pleasure above all else. They establish prayer regularly, fulfilling this important pillar of Islam. They also spend from their wealth in charity, both in private and in public, seeking Allah's reward and helping those in need. Moreover, they respond to evil and harm with good deeds and kindness, not allowing the wrongdoings of others to sway them from the path of righteousness. Because of these noble qualities, they will ultimately be granted the blessed abode of Paradise as a reward for their faith and perseverance.
orig: والذين صبروا ابتغاء وجه ربهم وأقاموا الصلاة وأنفقوا مما رزقناهم سرا وعلانية ويدرءون بالحسنة السيئة أولئك لهم عقبى الدار

translation: Gardens of perpetual residence; they will enter them with whoever were righteous among their fathers, their spouses and their descendants. And the angels will enter upon them from every gate,
interpretation: This verse speaks about the eternal reward in Paradise for those who were righteous in this worldly life. They will be admitted to the Gardens of Eden along with their family members who were also righteous - their parents, spouses, and children. The angels will come to them from every door, greeting them and congratulating them on their great achievement of attaining Paradise through their faith and good deeds. It emphasizes the importance of righteousness and how it leads to the ultimate success and happiness in the eternal life of the Hereafter, where the believers will be reunited with their loved ones in a perfect and blissful existence.
orig: جنات عدن يدخلونها ومن صلح من آبائهم وأزواجهم وذرياتهم والملائكة يدخلون عليهم من كل باب

translation: Peace be upon you for what you patiently endured. And excellent is the final home.
interpretation: This verse is a greeting and congratulations to those who have been patient and steadfast in the face of difficulties and trials in this worldly life. It conveys that their ultimate reward will be peace and an excellent final abode in the Hereafter, in Paradise. This interpretation highlights the importance of patience and perseverance in the face of adversity, and the promise of a great reward for those who remain firm in their faith and good deeds. It encourages believers to stay strong and focused on the ultimate goal of attaining Allah's pleasure and entering Paradise, no matter what challenges they may face in this temporary world.
orig: سلام عليكم بما صبرتم فنعم عقبى الدار

translation: And those who break the covenant of Allah after contracting it and sever that which Allah has ordered to be joined and cause corruption on earth - for them is the curse, and they will have the worst home.
interpretation: This verse warns of the severe consequences for those who break their promises and covenants with Allah, cut off ties of kinship and relationships that Allah has commanded to maintain, and spread corruption and evil in the world. It emphasizes that such people will be cursed by Allah and will have a terrible abode in the Hereafter as a result of their disobedience and transgression. The verse highlights the importance of fulfilling one's commitments, preserving the bonds of family and community, and working towards righteousness and goodness on earth.
orig: والذين ينقضون عهد الله من بعد ميثاقه ويقطعون ما أمر الله به أن يوصل ويفسدون في الأرض أولئك لهم اللعنة ولهم سوء الدار

translation: Allah extends provision for whom He wills and restricts [it]. And they rejoice in the worldly life, while the worldly life is not, compared to the Hereafter, except [brief] enjoyment.
interpretation: This verse reminds us that it is Allah who ultimately controls the provisions and sustenance that we receive in this worldly life. Some may be granted abundance, while others may face limitations, but it is all according to His divine wisdom and plan. The verse also points out the fleeting nature of the joys and pleasures of this world, emphasizing that they are insignificant compared to the eternal bliss of the Hereafter. It serves as a reminder for believers to keep their focus on the ultimate goal of attaining success in the afterlife, rather than being distracted by temporary worldly gains.
orig: الله يبسط الرزق لمن يشاء ويقدر وفرحوا بالحياة الدنيا وما الحياة الدنيا في الآخرة إلا متاع

translation: And those who disbelieve say, "Why has a sign not been sent down to him from his Lord?" Say, "Indeed, Allah leaves astray whom He wills and guides to Himself whoever turns back [to Him]"
interpretation: This verse highlights the contrast between the disbelievers who demand a miraculous sign from the Prophet Muhammad to prove his prophethood, and Allah's response that guidance is not dependent on such signs. Rather, it is Allah who guides or leaves astray whoever He wills based on their own intentions and actions. The verse emphasizes that true guidance comes from turning back to Allah in repentance and submission, not from demanding or expecting miraculous signs. It also affirms Allah's absolute control over the guidance and misguidance of individuals, as He alone knows what is in their hearts and what they deserve based on their choices and deeds.
orig: ويقول الذين كفروا لولا أنزل عليه آية من ربه قل إن الله يضل من يشاء ويهدي إليه من أناب

translation: Those who have believed and whose hearts find rest in the remembrance of Allah, Verily, in the remembrance of Allah do hearts find rest.
interpretation: This verse highlights the profound spiritual impact of remembering Allah. It suggests that true inner peace and contentment can only be attained through a strong connection with the Divine. By engaging in the remembrance of Allah, through prayer, supplication, and reflection upon His names and attributes, the hearts of the believers find solace and tranquility. This verse emphasizes the importance of maintaining a constant spiritual relationship with Allah, as it is the key to achieving a state of emotional and psychological well-being. It serves as a reminder that amidst the chaos and challenges of worldly life, the remembrance of Allah is the ultimate source of comfort and serenity for the believers.
orig: الذين آمنوا وتطمئن قلوبهم بذكر الله ألا بذكر الله تطمئن القلوب

translation: Those who have believed and done righteous deeds - a good state is theirs and a good return.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of faith and good deeds in attaining a blessed and happy state in this life and the hereafter. Those who sincerely believe in Allah and His message, and couple that belief with righteous actions, will be rewarded with inner peace, contentment, and a sense of purpose in this world. Moreover, they will be granted the ultimate reward of Paradise in the afterlife, where they will enjoy eternal bliss and proximity to their Lord. The verse serves as a reminder and encouragement for believers to strive for excellence in both faith and action, knowing that their efforts will be duly rewarded by Allah in the best possible way.
orig: الذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات طوبى لهم وحسن مآب

translation: Thus have We sent you to a community before which [other] communities have passed on so you might recite to them that which We revealed to you, while they disbelieve in the Most Merciful. Say, "He is my Lord; there is no deity except Him. Upon Him I rely, and to Him is my return."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the role of Prophet Muhammad as a messenger of God, sent to convey the divine message to his community, just as previous prophets were sent to their respective communities. Despite the fact that some people reject faith in God, the Most Merciful, the Prophet is instructed to declare his unwavering belief in the oneness of God and his complete reliance and trust in Him. This highlights the importance of remaining steadfast in one's faith and relying on God's guidance, even in the face of opposition or disbelief from others.
orig: كذلك أرسلناك في أمة قد خلت من قبلها أمم لتتلو عليهم الذي أوحينا إليك وهم يكفرون بالرحمن قل هو ربي لا إله إلا هو عليه توكلت وإليه متاب

translation: And if there was a Qur'an by which the mountains could be moved or the earth could be broken apart or the dead could be made to speak, [it would be this Qur'an], but to Allah belongs the affair entirely. Then have those who believed not accepted that had Allah willed, He would have guided the people, all of them? And those who disbelieve do not cease to be struck, for what they have done, by calamity - or it will descend near their home - until there comes the promise of Allah. Indeed, Allah does not fail in [His] promise.
interpretation: This verse highlights the power and authority of Allah over all things. It suggests that even if the Qur'an had the ability to move mountains, split the earth, or make the dead speak, it is ultimately Allah who has control over all affairs. The verse also addresses the disbelievers, stating that they will continue to face calamities and disasters due to their actions until the promise of Allah (likely referring to the Day of Judgment) comes to pass. It emphasizes that Allah's promise is true and that He never fails to fulfill it. The verse serves as a reminder to believers to have faith in Allah's will and to the disbelievers that they will face the consequences of their actions.
orig: ولو أن قرآنا سيرت به الجبال أو قطعت به الأرض أو كلم به الموتى بل لله الأمر جميعا أفلم ييأس الذين آمنوا أن لو يشاء الله لهدى الناس جميعا ولا يزال الذين كفروا تصيبهم بما صنعوا قارعة أو تحل قريبا من دارهم حتى يأتي وعد الله إن الله لا يخلف الميعاد

translation: And indeed, [many] messengers were mocked before you, but I granted respite to those who disbelieved; then I seized them, and how [terrible] was My penalty.
interpretation: This verse serves as a reminder and a warning to those who mock and disbelieve in Allah's messengers. It emphasizes that while the disbelievers may be given time and respite in this world, ultimately they will face the severe consequences of their actions in the form of Allah's punishment. The verse also consoles the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) by letting him know that he is not alone in facing ridicule and opposition, as many prophets before him had similar experiences. It underscores the gravity of rejecting faith and the importance of believing in and following the guidance brought by Allah's messengers.
orig: ولقد استهزئ برسل من قبلك فأمليت للذين كفروا ثم أخذتهم فكيف كان عقاب

translation: Is He [not best] who is a maintainer of every soul, [knowing] what it has earned? But they have attributed to Allah partners. Say, "Name them. Or do you inform Him of that which He knows not upon the earth or of what is apparent of speech?" Rather, their [own] plan has been made attractive to those who disbelieve, and they have been averted from the way. And whomever Allah leaves astray - there will be for him no guide.
interpretation: This verse highlights the omniscience and omnipotence of Allah, who is aware of every soul's deeds and is the ultimate maintainer of all creation. It criticizes those who associate partners with Allah, challenging them to name these alleged partners or prove their existence. The verse suggests that such claims are baseless and stem from the disbelievers' own delusions and misguided plans, which have been made attractive to them. As a result, they have strayed from the righteous path. The verse emphasizes that those whom Allah leaves astray will have no guide to lead them back to the truth, underscoring the importance of seeking Allah's guidance and avoiding the pitfalls of polytheism and disbelief.
orig: أفمن هو قائم على كل نفس بما كسبت وجعلوا لله شركاء قل سموهم أم تنبئونه بما لا يعلم في الأرض أم بظاهر من القول بل زين للذين كفروا مكرهم وصدوا عن السبيل ومن يضلل الله فما له من هاد

translation: For them is punishment in the life of this world, and the punishment of the Hereafter is more severe. And they have not from Allah any protector.
interpretation: This verse warns that those who reject Allah's message and oppose His messengers will face punishment both in this worldly life and in the Hereafter. The punishment of the Hereafter is emphasized as being even more severe and painful than any suffering in this world. It also affirms that no one can protect them from Allah's punishment or save them from His justice. This serves as a strong warning and reminder of the serious consequences of denying faith and encourages people to follow the right path to avoid such a fate.
orig: لهم عذاب في الحياة الدنيا ولعذاب الآخرة أشق وما لهم من الله من واق

translation: The example of Paradise, which the righteous have been promised, is [that] beneath it rivers flow. Its fruit is lasting, and its shade. That is the consequence for the righteous, and the consequence for the disbelievers is the Fire.
interpretation: This verse describes the eternal bliss that awaits the righteous in Paradise. It emphasizes that Paradise is not a temporary reward, but an everlasting abode of peace and comfort. The flowing rivers beneath the gardens of Paradise symbolize the abundance of blessings and the tranquility that the righteous will experience. The lasting fruit and the shade represent the continuous provision and protection that Allah will bestow upon His faithful servants. In contrast, the verse warns that the ultimate fate of the disbelievers is the Fire of Hell. This stark difference in the consequences of faith and disbelief serves as a powerful motivation for mankind to lead a righteous life and strive for the eternal rewards of Paradise.
orig: مثل الجنة التي وعد المتقون تجري من تحتها الأنهار أكلها دائم وظلها تلك عقبى الذين اتقوا وعقبى الكافرين النار

translation: And those to whom We have given the Book rejoice at what has been revealed to you, but among the factions are those who deny part of it. Say, "I have only been commanded to worship Allah and not associate [anything] with Him. To Him I invite, and to Him is my return."
interpretation: This verse highlights the varied reactions to the Qur'anic revelation among the People of the Book (Jews and Christians). Some of them rejoice in the truth and message of the Qur'an, recognizing its consistency with their own scriptures. However, there are factions among them who reject parts of the Qur'an that do not align with their beliefs or desires. In response, Allah instructs Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) to remain steadfast in his worship of Allah alone, without associating any partners with Him. The Prophet's mission is to invite people to the pure monotheism of Islam, emphasizing that his ultimate return and the return of all creation is to Allah, the One True God.
orig: والذين آتيناهم الكتاب يفرحون بما أنزل إليك ومن الأحزاب من ينكر بعضه قل إنما أمرت أن أعبد الله ولا أشرك به إليه أدعو وإليه مآب

translation: And thus We have revealed it as an Arabic legislation. And if you should follow their inclinations after what has come to you of knowledge, you would not have against Allah any ally or any protector.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the divine nature of the Qur'an as a revelation from Allah in the Arabic language. It serves as a warning to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and, by extension, to all believers not to deviate from the teachings of the Qur'an by following the desires and whims of those who oppose its message. The verse reminds us that if one were to abandon the knowledge and guidance provided by the Qur'an in favor of misguided inclinations, they would have no protector or ally against the consequences of disobeying Allah. This highlights the importance of staying steadfast in adhering to the Qur'an and its teachings, as it is the ultimate source of guidance and protection for believers.
orig: وكذلك أنزلناه حكما عربيا ولئن اتبعت أهواءهم بعدما جاءك من العلم ما لك من الله من ولي ولا واق

translation: And indeed, We sent Messengers before you (O Muhammad), and made for them wives and offspring. And it was not for a Messenger to bring a sign except by Allah's Leave. For every matter there is a Decree (from Allah).
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that all the prophets and messengers before Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) were human beings, not divine or supernatural entities. They had normal human lives, which included marriage and having children. This highlights the fact that the role of the prophets was not to showcase miracles at will, but rather to convey the divine message and guide people to the right path. The verse also underscores the concept of divine decree, suggesting that everything happens according to Allah's will and predetermined plan. Miracles, therefore, only occur by Allah's permission and in accordance with His divine wisdom and timing, not at the whim or desire of the prophets themselves.
orig: ولقد أرسلنا رسلا من قبلك وجعلنا لهم أزواجا وذرية وما كان لرسول أن يأتي بآية إلا بإذن الله لكل أجل كتاب

translation: Allah eliminates what He wills or confirms, and with Him is the Mother of the Book.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute power and authority of Allah over all things. He has the ability to erase or confirm whatever He wills, whether it pertains to the destinies of individuals or the laws governing the universe. The "Mother of the Book" refers to the preserved tablet (al-Lawh al-Mahfūẓ) which contains the original, unchangeable divine decrees. This verse reminds believers that ultimately, everything is subject to Allah's will and that He has complete control over the creation and the events that unfold within it. It encourages Muslims to submit to Allah's will and trust in His wisdom, knowing that He is the source of all knowledge and the final authority on all matters.
orig: يمحو الله ما يشاء ويثبت وعنده أم الكتاب

translation: And whether We show you some of what We promise them, [O Muhammad], or We take you in death, it is only upon you to convey [the message], and upon Us is the account.
interpretation: This verse is a reminder to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) that his role is to convey the message of Islam, and it is not his responsibility whether people accept it or not. Allah is telling the Prophet that regardless of whether he lives to see the fulfillment of Allah's promises or passes away before that, his duty is only to deliver the message. It is Allah who will hold people accountable for their actions and decisions in response to the message. This highlights the importance of conveying the message of Islam with clarity and wisdom, without being overly concerned about the outcome, as that is in the hands of Allah.
orig: وإن ما نرينك بعض الذي نعدهم أو نتوفينك فإنما عليك البلاغ وعلينا الحساب

translation: Have they not seen that We set upon the land, reducing it from its borders? And Allah decides; there is no adjuster of His decision. And He is swift in account.
interpretation: This verse is a reminder of Allah's power and control over the earth. It points out that Allah can cause the land to shrink or expand as He wills, and that no one can overrule His decisions. It also emphasizes that Allah is swift in His reckoning, meaning that He will hold people accountable for their deeds without delay on the Day of Judgment. The verse encourages people to be mindful of Allah's power and to live righteously, knowing that they will face the consequences of their actions in the Hereafter.
orig: أولم يروا أنا نأتي الأرض ننقصها من أطرافها والله يحكم لا معقب لحكمه وهو سريع الحساب

translation: And the people before them had plotted, but to Allah belongs all plotting. He knows what every soul earns, and the disbelievers will know for whom is the final home.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the ultimate power and knowledge of Allah. It suggests that while people may scheme and plot, Allah is aware of all their machinations and in the end, He is the best of planners. The verse also serves as a warning to the disbelievers that their actions will have consequences, and they will eventually come to realize in the Hereafter that the ultimate reward of Paradise belongs to the righteous believers, not to them. It is a reminder that no matter how much people may try to outwit Allah, He is always in control and will ensure justice prevails in the end.
orig: وقد مكر الذين من قبلهم فلله المكر جميعا يعلم ما تكسب كل نفس وسيعلم الكفار لمن عقبى الدار

translation: And those who disbelieve say, "You are not a messenger." Say, "Sufficient is Allah as Witness between me and you, and [the witness of] whoever has knowledge of the Scripture."
interpretation: This verse is a response to those who rejected Prophet Muhammad's claim of prophethood. Allah instructs the Prophet to tell the disbelievers that Allah Himself is sufficient as a witness between him and them, affirming his truthfulness. Additionally, those who have knowledge of previous scriptures, such as learned Jews and Christians, can also testify to the truth of Muhammad's prophethood, as his coming was foretold in their books. This verse emphasizes that the Prophet's message is not baseless, but rather supported by divine testimony and the evidence found in earlier religious texts.
orig: ويقول الذين كفروا لست مرسلا قل كفى بالله شهيدا بيني وبينكم ومن عنده علم الكتاب

translation: Alif, Lam, Ra. [This is] a Book which We have revealed to you, [O Muhammad], that you might bring mankind out of darknesses into the light by permission of their Lord - to the path of the Exalted in Might, the Praiseworthy.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the role of the Qur'an as a guide for humanity, bringing them from the darkness of ignorance, disbelief, and sin into the light of knowledge, faith, and righteousness. This guidance is achieved through the permission and will of Allah, who is described as the Exalted in Might and the Praiseworthy. The verse also highlights the importance of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) as the messenger chosen by Allah to convey this divine message to mankind, leading them to the straight path of Islam.
orig: الر كتاب أنزلناه إليك لتخرج الناس من الظلمات إلى النور بإذن ربهم إلى صراط العزيز الحميد

translation: It is Allah to whom belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is in the earth. And woe to the disbelievers from a severe punishment.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that everything in existence belongs to Allah alone, as He is the Creator and Sustainer of all things. It serves as a powerful reminder of His absolute sovereignty and ownership over the entire universe. The verse also contains a stern warning for those who reject faith in Allah, making it clear that they will face severe consequences in the form of a painful punishment in the Hereafter. This highlights the gravity of disbelief and the importance of acknowledging Allah's supreme authority and submitting to His will.
orig: الله الذي له ما في السماوات وما في الأرض وويل للكافرين من عذاب شديد

translation: Those who prefer the life of this world over the Hereafter and avert [people] from the way of Allah, seeking to make it (seem) deviant. Those are in extreme error.
interpretation: This verse is referring to those individuals who prioritize the temporary pleasures and desires of this worldly life over the eternal rewards of the Hereafter. They actively try to prevent others from following the path of Allah and His guidance, attempting to distort and misrepresent the truth of Islam. They seek to make the straight path of Allah appear crooked or deviant, in order to lead people astray. As a result of their actions and misguided priorities, these individuals are described as being in a state of extreme misguidance and error, far removed from the truth and the mercy of Allah. This interpretation highlights the importance of keeping our focus on the Hereafter and staying steadfast on the straight path, while also warning against those who seek to lead others astray from the way of Allah.
orig: الذين يستحبون الحياة الدنيا على الآخرة ويصدون عن سبيل الله ويبغونها عوجا أولئك في ضلال بعيد

translation: And We did not send any messenger except [speaking] in the language of his people to state clearly for them, and Allah sends astray [thereby] whom He wills and guides whom He wills. And He is the Exalted in Might, the Wise.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the wisdom and mercy of Allah in sending prophets who spoke the language of their own people, so that they could clearly convey the divine message. The verse also affirms that guidance and misguidance are ultimately in the hands of Allah, who is Almighty and All-Wise. The interpretation is that effective communication is essential for the success of the prophetic mission, and that the ultimate fate of individuals depends on Allah's will and wisdom, not solely on the efforts of the prophets.
orig: وما أرسلنا من رسول إلا بلسان قومه ليبين لهم فيضل الله من يشاء ويهدي من يشاء وهو العزيز الحكيم

translation: And indeed, We sent Moses with Our signs, [saying], "Bring out your people from darknesses into the light and remind them of the days of Allah." Indeed in that are signs for everyone patient and grateful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the role of prophets, particularly Moses, in guiding people from the darkness of ignorance and disbelief to the light of faith and knowledge. The "days of Allah" refer to the significant events in history where God's power, mercy, and justice were manifested, such as the parting of the Red Sea for Moses and his followers. These events serve as reminders and lessons for those who are patient in the face of adversity and grateful for God's blessings. The verse encourages believers to reflect upon these signs and to draw strength and guidance from them in their own lives.
orig: ولقد أرسلنا موسى بآياتنا أن أخرج قومك من الظلمات إلى النور وذكرهم بأيام الله إن في ذلك لآيات لكل صبار شكور

translation: And [recall] when Moses said to his people, "Remember the favor of Allah upon you when He saved you from the people of Pharaoh, who were afflicting you with the worst torment and were slaughtering your [newborn] sons and keeping your females alive. And in that was a great trial from your Lord."
interpretation: This verse is a reminder to the Children of Israel of the immense favor that Allah bestowed upon them by saving them from the tyranny and oppression of Pharaoh and his people. Pharaoh had subjected the Israelites to the worst kind of torture and humiliation, killing their male children and sparing their females, possibly to use them as slaves. Moses reminds his people that this deliverance from such a great affliction was a tremendous blessing and a test from Allah, one that required gratitude and obedience. The verse emphasizes the importance of remembering Allah's favors and blessings, especially in times of hardship and difficulty, and of remaining steadfast in faith and thankfulness to Him.
orig: وإذ قال موسى لقومه اذكروا نعمة الله عليكم إذ أنجاكم من آل فرعون يسومونكم سوء العذاب ويذبحون أبناءكم ويستحيون نساءكم وفي ذلكم بلاء من ربكم عظيم

translation: And [remember] when your Lord proclaimed, 'If you are grateful, I will surely increase you [in favor]; but if you deny, indeed, My punishment is severe.'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of gratitude in Islam. Allah promises to increase His blessings and favors upon those who are grateful for what they have been given. On the other hand, those who are ungrateful and deny Allah's blessings will face severe punishment. This interpretation highlights the direct correlation between a believer's gratitude and the abundance of blessings they receive from Allah, as well as the consequences of ingratitude and denial of His favors.
orig: وإذ تأذن ربكم لئن شكرتم لأزيدنكم ولئن كفرتم إن عذابي لشديد

translation: And Moses said, "If you disbelieve, you and whoever is on the earth entirely, indeed, Allah is Free of need and Praiseworthy."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute independence and self-sufficiency of Allah. It conveys that even if all of humanity and every creature on Earth were to disbelieve and reject faith in Allah, it would not diminish His greatness or affect Him in any way. Allah is above any need for His creation, and He is worthy of all praise regardless of whether people acknowledge Him or not. This verse serves as a reminder that one's faith and obedience to Allah should stem from sincere devotion and recognition of His inherent worthiness, rather than from a misguided notion that Allah needs or benefits from human worship.
orig: وقال موسى إن تكفروا أنتم ومن في الأرض جميعا فإن الله لغني حميد

translation: Has there not reached you the news of those before you - the people of Noah and 'Aad and Thamud and those after them? No one knows them but Allah. Their messengers came to them with clear proofs, but they returned their hands to their mouths and said, "Indeed, we disbelieve in that with which you have been sent, and indeed we are, about that to which you invite us, in disquieting doubt."
interpretation: This verse serves as a reminder to the disbelievers that they are not the first to reject the message of Allah. Many nations before them, such as the people of Noah, 'Aad, and Thamud, were also sent messengers with clear proofs and miracles, but they stubbornly refused to believe. They put their hands over their mouths, symbolizing their refusal to listen and their rejection of the truth. They expressed their disbelief and doubts about the message, finding it disturbing and unsettling. This verse highlights the recurring pattern of human resistance to divine guidance throughout history and the consequences that befell those who persisted in their disbelief.
orig: ألم يأتكم نبأ الذين من قبلكم قوم نوح وعاد وثمود والذين من بعدهم لا يعلمهم إلا الله جاءتهم رسلهم بالبينات فردوا أيديهم في أفواههم وقالوا إنا كفرنا بما أرسلتم به وإنا لفي شك مما تدعوننا إليه مريب

translation: Their messengers said, "Can there be doubt about Allah, the Originator of the heavens and the earth? He invites you that He may forgive you of your sins, and He delays your death for a specified term." They said, "You are not but men like us who wish to avert us from what our fathers were worshipping. So bring us a clear authority."
interpretation: This verse highlights the role of the prophets in conveying the message of monotheism and the invitation to worship Allah alone. Despite the clear signs and evidence presented by the messengers, the disbelievers remained skeptical and accused the prophets of being mere humans trying to divert them from the worship of their ancestral idols. The verse emphasizes the importance of faith in Allah as the Creator and Sustainer of the universe, and the need for clear divine authority to support the claims of the prophets. It also shows the stubborn nature of the disbelievers who, despite being reminded of Allah's forgiveness and the temporary nature of worldly life, chose to adhere to their misguided beliefs.
orig: قالت رسلهم أفي الله شك فاطر السماوات والأرض يدعوكم ليغفر لكم من ذنوبكم ويؤخركم إلى أجل مسمى قالوا إن أنتم إلا بشر مثلنا تريدون أن تصدونا عما كان يعبد آباؤنا فأتونا بسلطان مبين

translation: Their messengers said to them, "We are only men like you, but Allah confers favor upon whom He wills of His servants. It has never been for us to bring you evidence except by permission of Allah. And upon Allah let the believers rely."
