interpretation: This verse emphasizes the humanity of the prophets and messengers, indicating that they are not divine beings, but rather mortal men chosen by Allah to convey His message. It also highlights the fact that the miracles and signs brought by the messengers are not of their own doing, but are only possible through the permission and power of Allah. Furthermore, the verse encourages believers to put their trust and reliance solely in Allah, recognizing that ultimate authority and control belong to Him alone.
orig: قالت لهم رسلهم إن نحن إلا بشر مثلكم ولكن الله يمن على من يشاء من عباده وما كان لنا أن نأتيكم بسلطان إلا بإذن الله وعلى الله فليتوكل المؤمنون

translation: And why should we not rely upon Allah while He has guided us to our [good] ways. And we will surely be patient against whatever harm you should cause us. And upon Allah let those who would rely [indeed] rely.
interpretation: This verse encourages the believers to put their complete trust in Allah, knowing that He has guided them to the right path. It also urges them to remain patient in the face of any harm or persecution they may face from the disbelievers. The verse emphasizes that those who truly rely on Allah will find strength and support through their faith in Him, and that ultimately, all matters should be entrusted to Allah.
orig: وما لنا ألا نتوكل على الله وقد هدانا سبلنا ولنصبرن على ما آذيتمونا وعلى الله فليتوكل المتوكلون

translation: And those who disbelieved said to their messengers, "We will surely drive you out of our land, or you must return to our religion." So their Lord inspired to them, "We will surely destroy the wrongdoers."
interpretation: This verse highlights the arrogance and stubbornness of the disbelievers who, instead of accepting the truth brought by the messengers, threaten to exile them or force them to revert to their old religion. However, Allah reassures His messengers that He will destroy these wrongdoers who persist in their disbelief and oppression. This interpretation emphasizes the ultimate fate of those who reject the divine message and the protection and support that Allah grants to His messengers in the face of adversity.
orig: وقال الذين كفروا لرسلهم لنخرجنكم من أرضنا أو لتعودن في ملتنا فأوحى إليهم ربهم لنهلكن الظالمين

translation: And We will surely cause you to dwell in the land after them. This is for he who fears My position and fears My threat.
interpretation: This verse is a promise from Allah to the believers that they will inherit the land and be established in it after the disbelievers have been destroyed or removed from power. However, this promise is conditional upon the believers having true fear and consciousness of Allah, both in terms of fearing His lofty position and majesty, and fearing His threat of punishment for disobedience. It reminds us that the success and empowerment of the believers is tied to their level of taqwa (God-consciousness) and that the higher their taqwa, the more they will be aided to achieve victory and establish themselves in the land to uphold Allah's rule.
orig: ولنسكننكم الأرض من بعدهم ذلك لمن خاف مقامي وخاف وعيد

translation: And they sought judgement and every obstinate tyrant failed.
interpretation: This verse refers to the ultimate fate of those who are arrogant and tyrannical in their worldly life. They seek victory and dominance, but in the end, they will face failure and disappointment. It serves as a reminder that no matter how powerful or influential one may seem, if they are unjust and oppose the truth, their end will be one of loss and humiliation. The verse emphasizes the importance of humility, justice, and submitting to the will of Allah, as those who are obstinate and tyrannical will ultimately face the consequences of their actions in this life and the hereafter.
orig: واستفتحوا وخاب كل جبار عنيد

translation: In front of him is Hell, and he will be given a drink of purulent water.
interpretation: This verse warns of the terrible fate that awaits the disbelievers in the Hereafter. "In front of him" refers to the disbeliever who rejected God's message. "Hell" emphasizes the severity of the punishment - the blazing Fire of Hell lies ahead for those who turn away from the truth. The "drink of purulent water" highlights the disgusting and agonizing nature of the torment. Instead of pure, refreshing water, they will be forced to drink festering, putrid fluids as a consequence of their disbelief. This interpretation serves as a stark warning to mankind about the ultimate result of rejecting faith and a reminder to stay on the straight path to avoid such a dreadful outcome in the eternal life to come.
orig: من ورائه جهنم ويسقى من ماء صديد

translation: He will sip it but will hardly be able to swallow it. Death will come to him from everywhere, but he will not die. And beyond him is a massive punishment.
interpretation: This verse speaks to the severity and unrelenting nature of the punishment that awaits the disbelievers in the Hereafter. The person being punished will be made to drink something extremely bitter and unpleasant, which he can barely get down his throat. He will be surrounded by death and suffering from all directions, yet death will not come to end his misery. Instead, he will continue to suffer incessantly. Beyond this already terrible state, there awaits an even greater and more severe punishment. This conveys the gravity of the consequences of rejecting faith and the sheer hopelessness and despair that will befall those condemned to Hell.
orig: يتجرعه ولا يكاد يسيغه ويأتيه الموت من كل مكان وما هو بميت ومن ورائه عذاب غليظ

translation: The example of those who disbelieve in their Lord is [that] their deeds are like ashes which the wind blows forcefully on a stormy day; they are unable [to keep] from what they earned a [single] thing. That is what is extreme error.
interpretation: This verse compares the futility of the actions of those who reject faith in Allah to ashes blown away by strong winds on a stormy day. Just as the ashes are scattered and lost, rendering them useless, the disbelievers' good deeds are nullified because of their lack of faith, leaving them with nothing of value in the Hereafter. Their disbelief is described as "extreme error" because it ultimately leads to the complete loss of any benefit from their worldly actions, emphasizing the gravity of rejecting faith in Allah.
orig: مثل الذين كفروا بربهم أعمالهم كرماد اشتدت به الريح في يوم عاصف لا يقدرون مما كسبوا على شيء ذلك هو الضلال البعيد

translation: Do you not see that Allah created the heavens and the earth in truth? If He wills, He can do away with you and bring forth a new creation.
interpretation: This verse reminds us of Allah's omnipotence and His ability to create and destroy as He wills. It emphasizes that the creation of the universe is not a mere accident or without purpose, but rather a manifestation of Allah's wisdom and truth. The verse also serves as a warning to humanity that our existence is dependent on Allah's will, and that He can easily replace us with a new creation if He so desires. This should inspire humility and gratitude towards our Creator, as well as a sense of responsibility to fulfill our purpose and obey His commands.
orig: ألم تر أن الله خلق السماوات والأرض بالحق إن يشأ يذهبكم ويأت بخلق جديد

translation: And that is not difficult for Allah.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the omnipotence and infinite power of Allah. It conveys the idea that nothing is beyond His capabilities or too difficult for Him to accomplish. Whether it pertains to the creation of the universe, the resurrection of the dead, or any other matter, Allah has the absolute ability to bring it into being effortlessly. This verse serves as a reminder to humans of Allah's supreme authority and control over all things, inspiring humility, awe, and complete faith in His might.
orig: وما ذلك على الله بعزيز

translation: And they will come forth before Allah all together, and the weak will say to those who were arrogant, "Indeed, we were your followers, so can you avail us anything against the punishment of Allah?" They will say, "If Allah had guided us, we would have guided you. It is all the same for us whether we show intolerance or are patient: there is for us no place of escape."
interpretation: This verse highlights the accountability and regret on the Day of Judgment. The weak, who followed the arrogant in this world, will realize their mistake and seek help from their former leaders. However, the arrogant will express their own helplessness, admitting that they too are facing the consequences of their actions. They will acknowledge that had Allah guided them, they would have guided others as well. This verse emphasizes that on the Day of Judgment, everyone will be held responsible for their own deeds, and no one will be able to escape the punishment or find a way out, regardless of their worldly status or power.
orig: وبرزوا لله جميعا فقال الضعفاء للذين استكبروا إنا كنا لكم تبعا فهل أنتم مغنون عنا من عذاب الله من شيء قالوا لو هدانا الله لهديناكم سواء علينا أجزعنا أم صبرنا ما لنا من محيص

translation: And Satan will say when the matter has been concluded, "Indeed, Allah had promised you the promise of truth. And I promised you, but I betrayed you. But I had no authority over you except that I invited you, and you responded to me. So do not blame me; but blame yourselves. I cannot be called to your aid, nor can you be called to my aid. Indeed, I deny your association of me [with Allah] before. Indeed, for the wrongdoers is a painful punishment."
interpretation: This verse highlights the deception and betrayal of Satan. On the Day of Judgment, when all matters have been settled, Satan will admit that Allah's promise was true, while his own promises were false. He will declare that he had no real power over humans except the ability to invite them to evil, and they chose to follow him of their own free will. Satan will tell his followers not to blame him but to blame themselves for their actions. He will also disassociate himself from their past idolatry and polytheistic practices, emphasizing that he himself rejects the idea of being associated with Allah as a partner or equal. The verse concludes with a warning that wrongdoers will face a severe and painful punishment for their misdeeds and for following Satan's path.
orig: وقال الشيطان لما قضي الأمر إن الله وعدكم وعد الحق ووعدتكم فأخلفتكم وما كان لي عليكم من سلطان إلا أن دعوتكم فاستجبتم لي فلا تلوموني ولوموا أنفسكم ما أنا بمصرخكم وما أنتم بمصرخي إني كفرت بما أشركتمون من قبل إن الظالمين لهم عذاب أليم

translation: And those who believed and did righteous deeds will be admitted by Allah to gardens beneath which rivers flow, abiding eternally therein by permission of their Lord; and their greeting therein will be, "Peace!"
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the reward that awaits the righteous believers in the afterlife. It signifies that those who have faith and do good deeds will be granted entry into Paradise, where they will reside eternally by the grace and permission of Allah. In this blessed abode, they will be greeted with the salutation of "Peace" (Salam), indicating the serenity, tranquility, and freedom from all worries and anxieties that they will experience. This verse serves as a motivation for believers to strive in their faith and actions, knowing that their ultimate destination is the eternal bliss of Paradise.
orig: وأدخل الذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات جنات تجري من تحتها الأنهار خالدين فيها بإذن ربهم تحيتهم فيها سلام

translation: Have you not considered how Allah presents an example, [making] a good word like a good tree, whose root is firmly fixed and its branches [high] in the sky?
interpretation: This verse likens a good word to a firmly rooted tree with branches reaching high into the sky. The "good word" represents faith in Allah and righteous deeds. Just as a strong, healthy tree is firmly grounded and bears good fruit, a person with strong faith and good deeds is firmly grounded in their belief and produces beneficial actions that reach towards the heavens. This metaphor emphasizes the importance of having a solid foundation of faith and the far-reaching, positive impact of one's good deeds and words.
orig: ألم تر كيف ضرب الله مثلا كلمة طيبة كشجرة طيبة أصلها ثابت وفرعها في السماء

translation: It produces its fruit all the time, by permission of its Lord. And Allah presents examples for the people that perhaps they will be reminded.
interpretation: This verse is using the metaphor of a tree that consistently bears fruit to illustrate the concept of righteous deeds and their rewards. Just as a healthy tree, with God's permission, provides sustenance perpetually, a person who performs good works and remains conscious of God can expect to receive blessings and recompense from the Divine throughout their lives and in the Hereafter. God provides such examples to encourage people to reflect on spiritual truths and be motivated to lead a virtuous life aligned with His guidance. The verse emphasizes the importance of constancy in faith and the performance of righteous actions.
orig: تؤتي أكلها كل حين بإذن ربها ويضرب الله الأمثال للناس لعلهم يتذكرون

translation: And the example of a bad word is like a bad tree, uprooted from the surface of the earth, not having any stability.
interpretation: This verse draws a parallel between evil words or deeds and a bad tree that has no roots or stability. Just as a tree without roots cannot survive and is easily uprooted, evil words and actions have no foundation or lasting impact. They may appear strong or influential for a time, but ultimately, they will be exposed and destroyed. The verse emphasizes the importance of grounding oneself in goodness and righteousness, as they provide a solid foundation and lead to lasting success and stability in both this life and the hereafter.
orig: ومثل كلمة خبيثة كشجرة خبيثة اجتثت من فوق الأرض ما لها من قرار

translation: Allah keeps firm those who believe, with the firm word, in the life of this world and in the Hereafter. And Allah sends astray the wrongdoers. And Allah does what He wills.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the power and control of Allah over the fate of human beings. It assures the believers that their faith will keep them steadfast and secure, both in this worldly life and in the eternal life of the Hereafter. On the other hand, those who choose to be unjust and wrongdoers will be led astray by Allah, as a consequence of their own actions. Ultimately, the verse affirms the absolute sovereignty of Allah, reminding us that He alone has the power to do as He wills, and His decisions are always wise and just.
orig: يثبت الله الذين آمنوا بالقول الثابت في الحياة الدنيا وفي الآخرة ويضل الله الظالمين ويفعل الله ما يشاء

translation: Have you not seen those who exchanged the favor of Allah for disbelief and settled their people [in] the home of ruin?
interpretation: This verse is a strong condemnation of those who reject Allah's blessings and favors upon them, choosing instead to disbelieve and lead their people astray. By doing so, they condemn themselves and their followers to the "home of ruin" which refers to Hell in the Hereafter. It serves as a warning against ingratitude towards Allah and the severe consequences of leading others away from the truth of Islam. The verse emphasizes that the greatest blessing is faith in Allah, and to reject that blessing by choosing disbelief is the height of foolishness that will lead to destruction and suffering.
orig: ألم تر إلى الذين بدلوا نعمت الله كفرا وأحلوا قومهم دار البوار

translation: They will [enter to] burn in Hell, and wretched is the resting place.
interpretation: This verse serves as a stark warning to those who reject faith and choose to follow the path of evil. It emphasizes the severe consequences that await them in the Hereafter - the torment of Hell. The phrase "wretched is the resting place" underscores the utter misery, despair, and hopelessness that the denizens of Hell will experience eternally. It is a powerful reminder for mankind to be mindful of their actions and to strive for righteousness, as the ultimate destination in the afterlife is determined by one's deeds in this world.
orig: جهنم يصلونها وبئس القرار

translation: And they set up [in opposition] to Allah equals to mislead [people] from His way. Say, "Enjoy yourselves, for indeed, your destination is the Fire."
interpretation: This verse is a stern warning to those who associate partners with Allah or worship other deities besides Him. It highlights the grave consequences of such actions - that those who engage in idolatry and polytheism will ultimately be destined for the Hellfire. The verse emphasizes that the enjoyment and pleasures derived from following false gods is temporary and fleeting, and that the ultimate fate of those who reject Allah's guidance is eternal punishment in the afterlife. It serves as a powerful reminder to mankind to worship Allah alone and to steer clear of all forms of shirk (associating partners with Allah).
orig: وجعلوا لله أندادا ليضلوا عن سبيله قل تمتعوا فإن مصيركم إلى النار

translation: Say to My servants who have believed, that they should establish regular prayers and spend (in charity) out of the sustenance We have given them, secretly and openly, before the coming of a Day in which there will be neither mutual bargaining nor befriending.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of faith and good deeds. It instructs the believers to establish regular prayers and give in charity from what Allah has provided them, both in private and in public. They should do these acts of worship and kindness before the Day of Judgment arrives, when there will be no opportunity for bargaining or friendship to save oneself. This highlights the urgency of doing good and being mindful of the Hereafter, as one's deeds in this life will determine their fate in the eternal life to come.
orig: قل لعبادي الذين آمنوا يقيموا الصلاة وينفقوا مما رزقناهم سرا وعلانية من قبل أن يأتي يوم لا بيع فيه ولا خلال

translation: It is Allah who created the heavens and the earth and sent down rain from the sky and produced thereby some fruits as provision for you and subjected for you the ships to sail through the sea by His command and subjected for you the rivers.
interpretation: This verse highlights Allah's power, creativity, and generosity. It reminds us that Allah is the One who created the vast heavens and the earth we live on. He is the One who sends down rain, which allows vegetation and fruits to grow, providing sustenance for humans. Allah has also made ships and rivers subservient to humans, allowing them to travel and transport goods, which are great blessings and signs of His mercy. The verse encourages reflection on these favors and bounties, instilling gratitude towards Allah and acknowledgment of His lordship and authority over all things.
orig: الله الذي خلق السماوات والأرض وأنزل من السماء ماء فأخرج به من الثمرات رزقا لكم وسخر لكم الفلك لتجري في البحر بأمره وسخر لكم الأنهار

translation: And He has subjected for you the sun and the moon, continuous [in orbit], and subjected for you the night and the day.
interpretation: This verse highlights the immense blessings and favors that Allah has bestowed upon humanity. The sun and moon are described as being "subjected" or "made subservient" to the benefit of mankind, continuously following their ordained paths and cycles. This allows for the establishment of day and night, which are also mentioned as being subjected for our benefit. The alternation of day and night enables us to engage in various activities, rest, and worship. The verse encourages us to reflect upon these celestial bodies and the precise system they follow, recognizing them as signs of Allah's power, wisdom, and mercy. It inspires gratitude for the countless bounties we enjoy and should motivate us to use these blessings in a manner pleasing to Allah.
orig: وسخر لكم الشمس والقمر دائبين وسخر لكم الليل والنهار

translation: And He gave you from all you asked of Him. And if you should count the favor of Allah, you could not enumerate them. Indeed, mankind is [generally] most unjust and ungrateful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the countless blessings and favors that Allah has bestowed upon humanity. Despite receiving so much from Allah, humans often fail to acknowledge and appreciate these blessings. Instead, they are prone to being unjust, both to themselves and others, and ungrateful for what they have been given. The verse serves as a reminder for people to recognize the immense generosity of Allah and to express gratitude for His bounties, as failing to do so is a form of injustice and ingratitude.
orig: وآتاكم من كل ما سألتموه وإن تعدوا نعمت الله لا تحصوها إن الإنسان لظلوم كفار

translation: And [mention] when Abraham said, "My Lord, make this city [Makkah] secure and keep me and my sons away from worshipping idols."
interpretation: This verse shows Abraham's prayer for the city of Makkah to be made a sanctuary of peace and security. It also highlights his plea to Allah to protect him and his progeny from falling into the grave sin of idol-worship. This supplication reflects Abraham's sincerity in faith and his desire to establish a monotheistic tradition, free from the corruption of idolatry. It is a reminder for all believers to seek Allah's protection from polytheism and to strive for establishing a society based on the worship of the One True God.
orig: وإذ قال إبراهيم رب اجعل هذا البلد آمنا واجنبني وبني أن نعبد الأصنام

translation: My Lord, indeed they have led astray many among the people. So whoever follows me - then he is of me; and whoever disobeys me - indeed, You are [yet] Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse highlights the consequences of following or disobeying the guidance sent by Allah through His messengers. Those who follow the prophets and the divine message are considered to be on the right path and belong to the community of believers. However, those who choose to disobey and go astray are not immediately condemned; rather, the verse emphasizes Allah's attributes of forgiveness and mercy, indicating that the door to repentance and redemption is always open for those who sincerely seek it. This interpretation underscores the balance between divine justice and mercy in Islam, and encourages individuals to strive to follow the right path while reassuring them of Allah's compassion for those who err but seek His forgiveness.
orig: رب إنهن أضللن كثيرا من الناس فمن تبعني فإنه مني ومن عصاني فإنك غفور رحيم

translation: Our Lord, I have settled some of my descendants in an uncultivated valley near Your sacred House, our Lord, that they may establish prayer. So make hearts among the people incline toward them and provide for them from the fruits that they might be grateful.
interpretation: This verse is a prayer of Prophet Ibrahim (Abraham) to Allah. The interpretation is that Ibrahim is beseeching Allah to make the hearts of people incline towards his descendants settled in the barren valley of Makkah, near the Sacred House (Kaaba). He prays for their provision and sustenance, both physical and spiritual, so that they may be grateful to Allah for His blessings. This supplication highlights Ibrahim's deep faith and trust in Allah's mercy and providence, even in the face of seemingly unfavorable circumstances. It also emphasizes the importance of establishing prayer and being grateful for Allah's bounties.
orig: ربنا إني أسكنت من ذريتي بواد غير ذي زرع عند بيتك المحرم ربنا ليقيموا الصلاة فاجعل أفئدة من الناس تهوي إليهم وارزقهم من الثمرات لعلهم يشكرون

translation: Our Lord, indeed You know what we conceal and what we declare, and nothing is hidden from Allah on the earth or in the heaven.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the omniscience of Allah, reminding us that He is fully aware of all our actions, thoughts, and intentions, whether we hide them or make them known. It underscores the importance of sincerity and mindfulness in our deeds and words, as nothing escapes Allah's knowledge. The verse also highlights the all-encompassing nature of Allah's knowledge, spanning both the earth and the heavens, reinforcing His complete sovereignty and control over all creation. This understanding should inspire believers to strive for righteousness and be conscious of their actions, knowing that Allah is always watching and will hold them accountable for their deeds.
orig: ربنا إنك تعلم ما نخفي وما نعلن وما يخفى على الله من شيء في الأرض ولا في السماء

translation: Praise be to Allah, Who has granted me in old age Ishmael and Isaac. Indeed, my Lord is the Hearer of supplication.
interpretation: This verse expresses gratitude to Allah for blessing the speaker with two sons, Ishmael and Isaac, despite the speaker's old age. It highlights Allah's power to grant offspring even in advanced years and emphasizes that Allah listens to and answers the supplications of His servants. The verse encourages believers to turn to Allah with their prayers and trust in His ability to fulfill their needs, even in seemingly impossible circumstances. It also serves as a reminder of the importance of expressing gratitude for the blessings bestowed upon us by Allah.
orig: الحمد لله الذي وهب لي على الكبر إسماعيل وإسحاق إن ربي لسميع الدعاء

translation: My Lord, make me an establisher of prayer, and [many] from my descendants. Our Lord, and accept my supplication.
interpretation: In this verse, the speaker is asking Allah to make them steadfast in establishing regular prayer, and to also make their descendants people who establish prayer. They are asking Allah to accept this supplication. This highlights the importance of prayer in Islam, not just for an individual, but also for them to pass on this legacy to their children and future generations. It shows that one of the most important things a believer can ask Allah for is to be able to worship Him consistently through prayer, and for this to continue in their lineage.
orig: رب اجعلني مقيم الصلاة ومن ذريتي ربنا وتقبل دعاء

translation: Our Lord, forgive me and my parents and the believers on the Day of Judgment.
interpretation: This verse is a humble supplication to Allah, seeking His forgiveness not only for oneself but also for one's parents and the entire community of believers. It highlights the importance of seeking Allah's mercy and the significance of the Day of Judgment when all deeds will be accounted for. The verse emphasizes the bond of faith that unites all believers and the collective responsibility to pray for each other's forgiveness. It serves as a reminder to maintain strong family ties, especially with parents, and to always keep the afterlife in mind, striving to lead a righteous life in preparation for the Day of Judgment.
orig: ربنا اغفر لي ولوالدي وللمؤمنين يوم يقوم الحساب

translation: And never think that Allah is unaware of what the wrongdoers do. He only delays them for a Day when eyes will stare [in horror].
interpretation: This verse serves as a stern warning to the wrongdoers and oppressors that Allah is fully aware of their misdeeds, even if they may think otherwise. Although they might escape worldly punishment, Allah will hold them accountable on the Day of Judgment when they will be resurrected and their eyes will stare in horror, realizing the gravity of their actions. This verse emphasizes the concept of divine justice and the ultimate reckoning that awaits the evildoers, reminding believers to refrain from wrongdoing and to have faith in Allah's omniscience and His perfect judgment.
orig: ولا تحسبن الله غافلا عما يعمل الظالمون إنما يؤخرهم ليوم تشخص فيه الأبصار

translation: Their eyes humbled, their heads hung low, their gaze does not return to them, and their hearts are void.
interpretation: This verse describes the state of the disbelievers on the Day of Judgment. They will be utterly humiliated and devastated, with their eyes downcast out of shame and fear. Their heads will be bowed low in submission and defeat. They will be so overwhelmed by the reality of their situation that they will not even be able to lift their gaze. Their hearts will be empty and hollow, devoid of any hope or comfort. This stark imagery conveys the ultimate despair and regret that the disbelievers will experience when faced with the consequences of their actions and their rejection of faith.
orig: مهطعين مقنعي رءوسهم لا يرتد إليهم طرفهم وأفئدتهم هواء

translation: And warn the people of the Day when the punishment will come to them, and those who did wrong will say, "Our Lord, delay us for a short term; we will answer Your call and follow the messengers." [But it will be said], "Had you not sworn, before, that for you there would be no cessation?"
interpretation: This verse is a warning to those who reject faith and do wrong, reminding them of the Day of Judgment when they will face the consequences of their actions. On that day, they will plead for more time to repent and follow the messengers, but it will be too late. The verse also points out that they had previously sworn that they would never change their ways or cease to exist, implying that they had been arrogant and dismissive of the truth. This highlights the importance of heeding the warnings and guidance sent by God through His messengers before it is too late to repent and rectify one's actions.
orig: وأنذر الناس يوم يأتيهم العذاب فيقول الذين ظلموا ربنا أخرنا إلى أجل قريب نجب دعوتك ونتبع الرسل أولم تكونوا أقسمتم من قبل ما لكم من زوال

translation: And you dwelt in the dwellings of those who wronged themselves, and it had become clear to you how We dealt with them. And We presented for you [many] examples.
interpretation: This verse is a reminder to the believers that they have seen the consequences of those who came before them and wronged themselves by rejecting Allah's messages and His messengers. They witnessed how Allah dealt with those past nations, destroying them for their transgressions, and their ruins serve as a visible example and warning. Despite these clear signs and examples, the believers still chose to follow a similar path of disobedience. The verse emphasizes the importance of learning from the mistakes of the past and rectifying one's behavior accordingly, lest they face a similar fate to those who were destroyed before them due to their persistent wrongdoing and rejection of faith.
orig: وسكنتم في مساكن الذين ظلموا أنفسهم وتبين لكم كيف فعلنا بهم وضربنا لكم الأمثال

translation: And they had planned their plan, but with Allah is [recorded] their plan, even if their plan had been [sufficient] to do away with the mountains.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the futility of plotting against Allah's will. It suggests that no matter how clever or powerful the disbelievers' schemes may seem, Allah is fully aware of them and has already recorded them. The verse implies that their plans are ultimately insignificant and powerless against Allah's omnipotence, even if they appear to be as mighty and immovable as mountains. It serves as a reminder to the believers to trust in Allah's protection and not be intimidated by the machinations of those who oppose the truth.
orig: وقد مكروا مكرهم وعند الله مكرهم وإن كان مكرهم لتزول منه الجبال

translation: So do not think that Allah will fail in His promise to His messengers. Indeed, Allah is Exalted in Might and Owner of Retribution.
interpretation: This verse serves as a reminder and warning that Allah always fulfills His promises to His messengers. One should never doubt or think that Allah will fail to keep His word. The verse emphasizes two key attributes of Allah - His Might and His ability to inflict retribution. This implies that Allah has the power to fulfill His promises and the ability to punish those who go against Him or His messengers. It is a call to have complete faith and trust in Allah's promises and to be mindful of the consequences of disobeying or denying Him and His message.
orig: فلا تحسبن الله مخلف وعده رسله إن الله عزيز ذو انتقام

translation: The Day when the earth will be replaced by another earth, and the heavens [as well], and they [i.e., all creatures] will come out before Allah, the One, the Prevailing.
interpretation: This verse refers to the Day of Judgment, when the present world will be replaced by a new earth and heavens. All creatures will be resurrected and brought before Allah, the Almighty, to face the consequences of their deeds in this world. It emphasizes the absolute power and authority of Allah, as He alone will judge and decide the fate of every individual on that Day. The mention of Allah being "the One, the Prevailing" highlights His uniqueness and supremacy over all creation, and that ultimately, everyone will have to submit to His will and judgment.
orig: يوم تبدل الأرض غير الأرض والسماوات وبرزوا لله الواحد القهار

translation: And you will see the criminals that Day bound together in shackles.
interpretation: This verse refers to the Day of Judgment when the sinners and wrongdoers will be shackled and chained together as a form of humiliation and punishment for their evil deeds in this world. It signifies that they will have no escape from the consequences of their actions and will be held accountable before Allah. The shackles are a manifestation of their spiritual state of being imprisoned by their own sins. This imagery serves as a powerful warning for people to avoid the path of criminality and to strive for righteousness in order to be saved from such a fate in the Hereafter.
orig: وترى المجرمين يومئذ مقرنين في الأصفاد

translation: Their garments will be of pitch, and fire will cover their faces.
interpretation: This verse describes the punishment that awaits the disbelievers and wrongdoers in the Hereafter. The "garments of pitch" symbolize the intensity and pain of the punishment, as pitch is a thick, sticky, and flammable substance. Fire covering their faces indicates the severity and encompassing nature of the torment. This imagery conveys the message that those who reject faith and engage in evil deeds will face a terrible fate in the afterlife, experiencing both physical and spiritual anguish. The verse serves as a warning to humanity, urging them to follow the path of righteousness and avoid actions that would lead to such a dreadful outcome.
orig: سرابيلهم من قطران وتغشى وجوههم النار

translation: That Allah may recompense every soul for what it has earned. Indeed, Allah is swift in account.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the ultimate justice and accountability in Allah's judgment. Every soul will be recompensed precisely for what it has earned through its actions and intentions in this worldly life. The mention of Allah's swiftness in account underscores His perfect knowledge of all deeds, His ability to judge them accurately, and the certainty and proximity of the Day of Judgment. It serves as a reminder for individuals to be mindful of their actions, as they will be held accountable for them, and to strive for righteousness with the knowledge that no deed, good or bad, is overlooked by Allah.
orig: ليجزي الله كل نفس ما كسبت إن الله سريع الحساب

translation: This [Qur'an] is a message for humanity so that they may be warned thereby and that they may know that He is but one God and so that those of understanding will be mindful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the Qur'an serves as a universal message and warning to all of humanity. Its purpose is to make people aware of the oneness and uniqueness of God, proclaiming strict monotheism. The verse ends by stating that people of understanding, those who deeply reflect and possess wisdom, will heed this message and be mindful of its profound implications - that they will worship and submit to the One God alone.
orig: هذا بلاغ للناس ولينذروا به وليعلموا أنما هو إله واحد وليذكر أولو الألباب

translation: Alif, Lam, Ra. These are the verses of the Book and a clear Qur'an.
interpretation: This verse is the opening of Surah Al-Hijr. The letters Alif, Lam, Ra are among the disjointed letters that appear at the beginning of several surahs in the Qur'an. The exact meaning of these letters is known only to Allah, but they are believed to be a way of drawing the listener's attention to the divine nature of the Qur'an. The verse then proclaims that what follows are the verses of Allah's Book and a clear Qur'an, indicating the clarity, guidance, and truth contained within the Qur'an. It affirms that the Qur'an is not just any book, but the Book of Allah, revealed as a guide and mercy to mankind.
orig: الر تلك آيات الكتاب وقرآن مبين

translation: Perhaps those who disbelieve will wish that they had been Muslims.
interpretation: This verse suggests that on the Day of Judgment, when the disbelievers witness the rewards granted to the believers, they will regret their choice of disbelief and wish that they had embraced Islam in their worldly life. It implies that the truth of Islam will become evident to all in the Hereafter, and those who rejected it will feel deep remorse for not having followed the right path when they had the chance. The verse serves as a warning to the disbelievers and an encouragement for the believers to remain steadfast in their faith.
orig: ربما يود الذين كفروا لو كانوا مسلمين

translation: Let them eat and enjoy themselves and be diverted by [false] hope, for they are going to know.
interpretation: This verse is a warning to those who are heedless of the consequences of their actions. It suggests that people who are preoccupied with worldly pleasures and false hopes will eventually face the reality of their choices. The verse implies that the pursuit of temporary enjoyment and vain desires can distract people from the truth and lead them astray. It serves as a reminder that the ultimate knowledge and understanding of one's actions will be made clear in the end, and that people should be mindful of their deeds and their implications in the grand scheme of things.
orig: ذرهم يأكلوا ويتمتعوا ويلههم الأمل فسوف يعلمون

translation: And We did not destroy any city except that it had a known decree.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the justice and wisdom of Allah in dealing with past nations. It indicates that Allah never destroyed a nation arbitrarily or without warning. Rather, each nation that was destroyed had been given a fixed term and ample warnings to mend their ways. They were only punished after they had persistently rejected the message and exceeded all bounds in their transgressions. This verse serves as a reminder that the destruction of past nations was a consequence of their own choices and actions, and that Allah's punishment is always just and measured, in accordance with His divine wisdom and decree.
orig: وما أهلكنا من قرية إلا ولها كتاب معلوم

translation: No nation can hasten its term, nor can they delay it.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the predetermined nature of the fate of nations and communities. It asserts that the rise, fall, and ultimate destiny of each nation is preordained by Allah's divine will and cannot be altered or postponed. The verse serves as a reminder that the affairs of nations are ultimately in the hands of Allah, and that humans, despite their efforts, cannot change what has been decreed. It encourages believers to recognize the supremacy of Allah's will and to submit to His divine plan, while striving to live righteously and fulfill their obligations.
orig: ما تسبق من أمة أجلها وما يستأخرون

translation: And they say, "O you upon whom the message has been sent down, indeed you are mad."
interpretation: This verse reflects the disbelief and mockery of the Meccan polytheists towards Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him). They accused him of being possessed or insane because he claimed to receive divine revelation from Allah. This accusation was a common tactic used by the opponents of the prophets to discredit their message and deter people from following them. However, the Qur'an affirms that Prophet Muhammad was not mad, but rather a chosen messenger of Allah, sent to guide humanity to the straight path. The verse also implies that the disbelievers' rejection of the message was not based on reason or evidence, but rather on their arrogance and stubborn adherence to their ancestral beliefs.
orig: وقالوا يا أيها الذي نزل عليه الذكر إنك لمجنون

translation: Why do you not bring us the angels, if you are of the truthful ones?
interpretation: This verse is a challenge posed by the disbelievers to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him), demanding that he bring angels as proof of his prophethood and the truth of his message. It reflects their stubborn refusal to believe in him despite the clear signs and revelations he had already brought. The verse implies that even if the Prophet were to bring angels as they demanded, they would likely still not believe, as their rejection was based on arrogance and not a genuine lack of evidence. It also highlights the fact that the coming of angels is not necessary to prove the truth of the Prophet's message, as the Qur'an itself is sufficient proof for those who sincerely reflect upon it with open hearts and minds.
orig: لو ما تأتينا بالملائكة إن كنت من الصادقين

translation: We do not send down the angels except with the truth, and the disbelievers would not then be reprieved.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that God sends down the angels only with a true and just purpose, such as conveying revelation or carrying out His decrees. It also implies that when the angels descend for the final judgment, the disbelievers will not be given any further respite or opportunity for repentance. The verse underscores the gravity and inevitability of divine justice, suggesting that once God's judgment arrives, there will be no turning back or escape for those who have rejected the truth.
orig: ما ننزل الملائكة إلا بالحق وما كانوا إذا منظرين

translation: Indeed, it is We who sent down the Qur'an and indeed, We will be its guardian.
interpretation: This verse affirms that Allah Himself has taken the responsibility of preserving the Qur'an from any corruption or alteration. It is a divine promise that the Qur'an will remain intact and unchanged throughout the ages, as Allah will protect it from any attempts to distort or modify its content. This preservation is a unique feature of the Qur'an, as no other religious scripture has remained unaltered since its revelation. The verse also implies that memorizing, reciting, and understanding the Qur'an are acts of worship that will be rewarded by Allah, as He has made it easy for believers to preserve and transmit His message.
orig: إنا نحن نزلنا الذكر وإنا له لحافظون

translation: And We had certainly sent [messengers] before you, [O Muhammad], among the sects of the former peoples.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the continuity of Allah's message throughout history. It assures Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) that he is not the first prophet to face opposition and rejection from his people. Many prophets before him, such as Noah, Abraham, Moses, and Jesus, were sent to various nations and communities (referred to as "sects" or "groups") in the past. They all faced similar challenges and hardships while conveying the message of Islam. This verse serves as a reminder that the Prophet's experiences are not unique and that he should remain steadfast in his mission, just as the prophets before him did, trusting in Allah's support and guidance.
orig: ولقد أرسلنا من قبلك في شيع الأولين

translation: And no messenger would come to them except that they ridiculed him.
interpretation: This verse highlights the stubborn nature of those who reject the truth. Whenever a messenger of Allah came to them with guidance and warnings, they responded with mockery and derision. Instead of reflecting on the message and considering its validity, they chose to belittle and ridicule the messenger. This behavior is a sign of arrogance and closed-mindedness, as they were unwilling to humble themselves and accept the truth. It also demonstrates a lack of respect for the divine message and the chosen messengers of Allah. Such an attitude ultimately leads to their own detriment and loss in both this world and the hereafter.
orig: وما يأتيهم من رسول إلا كانوا به يستهزئون

translation: Thus We insert denial into the hearts of the criminals.
interpretation: This verse suggests that Allah allows disbelief and denial to enter into the hearts of those who persistently commit sins and act against His commands. It implies that their continuous engagement in criminal and immoral acts leads to a state where their hearts become hardened and unreceptive to the truth and guidance of Allah. As a consequence of their own evil actions, Allah seals their hearts, making it difficult for them to believe, repent and reform. It is a form of punishment that they bring upon themselves due to their choice of leading a sinful life and rejecting the signs and messages of Allah.
orig: كذلك نسلكه في قلوب المجرمين

translation: They do not believe in it, while there has already occurred the precedent of the former peoples.
interpretation: This verse refers to the disbelievers who reject the message of Islam despite the lessons and precedents set by earlier nations who also disbelieved and were subsequently punished by Allah for their rejection of the truth. It serves as a warning that those who persist in disbelief will face a similar fate to those nations that came before them, and that the Sunnah (way) of Allah in dealing with the disbelievers remains unchanged. The verse also implies that the truth of Islam is not something new, but rather a continuation and confirmation of the messages brought by earlier prophets.
orig: لا يؤمنون به وقد خلت سنة الأولين

translation: And [even] if We opened to them a gate from the heaven and they continued therein to ascend,
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the stubbornness and disbelief of those who reject the truth, even when presented with clear signs and evidence. It suggests that even if God were to open a gate from heaven and allow them to ascend through it, they would still find a way to deny the reality of what they were witnessing. They would attribute it to magic, hallucination, or some other false explanation, rather than accepting it as a sign from God. This highlights the depth of their denial and their unwillingness to embrace the truth, no matter how clear and undeniable it may be.
orig: ولو فتحنا عليهم بابا من السماء فظلوا فيه يعرجون

translation: They would have said, "Our eyes have only been dazzled. Rather, we are a people affected by magic."
interpretation: This verse suggests that if the disbelievers were shown a clear sign or miracle, they would still not believe and would instead attribute it to magic or their own eyes being deceived. It highlights their stubbornness and unwillingness to accept the truth, even when faced with compelling evidence. The interpretation is that no matter how clear the signs of Allah's existence and power may be, those who are determined to disbelieve will find ways to dismiss or explain them away, rather than accepting the message and submitting to Allah.
orig: لقالوا إنما سكرت أبصارنا بل نحن قوم مسحورون

translation: And indeed, We have placed within the heaven great stars and have beautified it for the observers.
interpretation: This verse highlights the majesty and beauty of God's creation in the heavens. The "great stars" or constellations mentioned are not only awe-inspiring to behold, but serve as navigational aids and markers of time. By adorning the night sky with such splendor, God invites us to contemplate His power and artistry. The verse also implies that the stars' positions and arrangements are purposeful, not random. As we observe and appreciate the celestial wonders, we are reminded of God's grand design and our own small place within the vast cosmos. Ultimately, the heavens are presented as a sign for those who look beyond the superficial and reflect deeply on the meaning behind God's creation.
orig: ولقد جعلنا في السماء بروجا وزيناها للناظرين

translation: And We have protected it from every accursed devil.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the divine protection that Allah has bestowed upon the Qur'an, ensuring that it remains free from any corruption or influence of evil forces. The term "accursed devil" refers to Satan and his minions who seek to lead people astray from the path of righteousness. By safeguarding the Qur'an, Allah has guaranteed that its message will remain pure and unchanged, serving as a guiding light for humanity until the end of time. This protection is a testament to the authenticity and reliability of the Qur'an as the final revelation from Allah to mankind.
orig: وحفظناها من كل شيطان رجيم

translation: Except one who steals a hearing and is pursued by a clear burning flame.
interpretation: This verse refers to the devils who try to eavesdrop on the conversations of the angels in the heavens to gain knowledge of the future. However, they are chased away by bright, piercing flames (meteors) that are hurled at them. This is a form of divine protection to prevent the devils from accessing and corrupting the divine knowledge. It also serves as a reminder that no one can access the knowledge of the unseen except what Allah chooses to reveal through His prophets and messengers.
orig: إلا من استرق السمع فأتبعه شهاب مبين

translation: And the earth We have spread out, and have placed therein firm mountains, and caused to grow therein all kinds of things in due balance.
interpretation: This verse highlights Allah's power and wisdom in creating the earth. He has spread it out, making it spacious and suitable for living. The firm mountains placed within it provide stability and balance. Moreover, Allah has caused all kinds of things to grow on the earth in a precisely measured way, emphasizing the perfect balance and order in His creation. This encourages reflection on the signs of Allah's creative ability and the importance of maintaining balance in all aspects of life.
orig: والأرض مددناها وألقينا فيها رواسي وأنبتنا فيها من كل شيء موزون

translation: And We have made for you therein means of living and [provided for] those for whom you are not providers.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's mercy and generosity towards His creation. He has provided us with various means of sustenance and livelihood on Earth, not only for ourselves but also for those who are dependent on us, such as our families and those under our care. It reminds us to be grateful for Allah's blessings and to recognize that ultimately, it is He who sustains and provides for all living beings, even though we may play a role in supporting others. This verse encourages us to be compassionate and mindful of the needs of those who rely on us while acknowledging that Allah is the true provider and sustainer of all.
orig: وجعلنا لكم فيها معايش ومن لستم له برازقين

translation: And there is not a thing but that with Us are its depositories, and We do not send it down except according to a known measure.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that everything in existence, whether tangible or intangible, is under the complete control and authority of Allah. The "depositories" refer to the unlimited treasures and resources that belong to Allah alone. He is the One who determines the measure and proportion of what is sent down or manifested in the world, according to His infinite wisdom and knowledge. This interpretation highlights the concept of divine providence and the belief that nothing happens without the will and permission of Allah, who has preset the quantity and timing of all things in accordance with His perfect plan.
orig: وإن من شيء إلا عندنا خزائنه وما ننزله إلا بقدر معلوم

translation: And We have sent the fertilizing winds and sent down water from the sky and given it to you to drink. And you are not its retainers.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the power and benevolence of Allah in providing sustenance for His creation. The "fertilizing winds" refer to the winds that carry pollen and facilitate plant growth, while the water sent down from the sky is the rain that nourishes the earth and its inhabitants. The verse reminds humanity that these vital resources are gifts from Allah, and that we are not the ones who store or control them. It encourages gratitude and recognition of our dependence on Allah's mercy and provision, as well as the importance of using these resources responsibly as stewards rather than owners.
orig: وأرسلنا الرياح لواقح فأنزلنا من السماء ماء فأسقيناكموه وما أنتم له بخازنين

translation: And indeed, it is We who give life and cause death, and We are the Inheritor.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's absolute power and control over life and death. It affirms that Allah is the One who gives life to His creation and causes them to die according to His will and wisdom. The verse also highlights Allah's attribute as "Al-Warith" (The Inheritor), meaning that after all of His creation perishes, He will remain as the Eternal, to whom all things will return. This attribute underscores Allah's omnipotence and the transient nature of all creation in comparison to His everlasting existence. The verse serves as a reminder for humankind to recognize Allah's sovereignty and to live their lives in accordance with His guidance, knowing that ultimately, all will return to Him.
orig: وإنا لنحن نحيي ونميت ونحن الوارثون

translation: And indeed, We know the first generations of you who had passed away, and indeed, We know the present generations of you [who are alive].
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's comprehensive knowledge that encompasses all of His creation, past and present. He is fully aware of every generation that has come before and every generation that will come after, including their deeds, intentions, and ultimate fate. It serves as a reminder to humanity that nothing is hidden from Allah and that all will be held accountable for their actions in this world.
orig: ولقد علمنا المستقدمين منكم ولقد علمنا المستأخرين

translation: And indeed, your Lord will gather them; indeed, He is Wise and Knowing.
interpretation: This verse affirms that Allah, in His infinite wisdom and knowledge, will gather all of mankind on the Day of Judgment. It serves as a reminder that everyone will be held accountable for their deeds and that no one can escape the ultimate reckoning. The verse also highlights two of Allah's attributes: His wisdom in judging and dealing with His creation, and His all-encompassing knowledge of their actions and intentions. This should inspire believers to strive for righteousness and be mindful of their deeds, knowing that they will eventually return to their Lord.
orig: وإن ربك هو يحشرهم إنه حكيم عليم

translation: And indeed, We created man from sounding clay of altered black smooth mud.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the humble origins of mankind, as God created human beings from a lowly substance - clay that has been altered and shaped. It serves as a reminder for humans to remain humble and recognize their place as creations of God, rather than becoming arrogant or prideful. The verse also highlights the intricate process of human creation, with God carefully fashioning man from a specific type of clay, demonstrating His power, wisdom, and attention to detail in the creation of mankind.
orig: ولقد خلقنا الإنسان من صلصال من حمإ مسنون

translation: And the jinn We created before from scorching fire.
interpretation: This verse indicates that Allah created the jinn before mankind, and that they were created from a special type of fire described as "scorching" or "smokeless". This highlights the different nature and origin of the jinn compared to humans, who were created from clay. It also shows Allah's power and ability to create beings from various elements. The verse reminds us of the unseen world of the jinn, which exists parallel to our own, and the importance of being mindful of their presence and influence.
orig: والجان خلقناه من قبل من نار السموم

translation: And [mention], when your Lord said to the angels, "Indeed, I am going to create a human being from clay of altered black mud."
interpretation: This verse highlights the unique origin and nature of human beings. It shows that Allah created the first human, Adam, from a specific type of clay that was altered and had stagnated. This reflects the special attention and care Allah gave to the creation of humanity. The verse also demonstrates Allah's power and ability to create life from lifeless matter. It serves as a reminder to humans that they have a noble beginning and that they should be humbled by their origin and grateful to their Creator.
orig: وإذ قال ربك للملائكة إني خالق بشرا من صلصال من حمإ مسنون

translation: So when I have proportioned him and breathed into him of My [created] soul, then fall down to him in prostration.
interpretation: This verse is a command from Allah to the angels to prostrate to Adam after Allah had created him and breathed into him the soul that He created. This prostration was not one of worship, but rather a prostration of honor and respect, acknowledging the special status that Allah had bestowed upon Adam. This event also demonstrates the honor and dignity that Allah has given to mankind, as He commanded the angels, noble creatures made from light, to bow down to Adam, a being made from clay. It is a reminder to humans of their noble origin and the great potential and responsibility that comes with being the creatures that Allah has favored above many of His creations.
orig: فإذا سويته ونفخت فيه من روحي فقعوا له ساجدين

translation: So the angels prostrated, all of them entirely,
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute obedience and submission of the angels to Allah's command. When Allah ordered the angels to prostrate before Adam, they all complied without hesitation or exception. This demonstrates their total devotion and lack of arrogance or pride. The verse underscores the importance of humility and obedience to Allah's will, which are essential qualities for believers. It also highlights the elevated status of Adam and, by extension, humanity, as Allah commanded even the angels to bow before him.
orig: فسجد الملائكة كلهم أجمعون

translation: Except Iblees, he refused to be with those who prostrated.
interpretation: This verse refers to the story of Iblees (Satan) who, out of pride and arrogance, disobeyed Allah's command to prostrate before Adam. While all the other angels obeyed and prostrated, Iblees refused, considering himself superior to Adam. This act of defiance and pride led to his expulsion from Paradise and earned him the wrath of Allah. The verse highlights the importance of obedience to Allah's commands and the danger of pride and arrogance in leading one astray from the righteous path.
orig: إلا إبليس أبى أن يكون مع الساجدين

translation: He said, "O Iblees, what is [the matter] with you that you are not with those who prostrate?"
interpretation: In this verse, God is questioning Iblees (Satan) as to why he did not prostrate along with the other angels when commanded to do so. This is in reference to the story of Adam's creation, when God ordered the angels to bow to Adam, and Iblees refused out of pride and arrogance. This verse highlights Iblees' disobedience and defiance of God's command, setting the stage for his role as the tempter and enemy of mankind. It also emphasizes the importance of humility, submission, and obedience to God's will, as opposed to the pride and rebelliousness embodied by Iblees.
orig: قال يا إبليس ما لك ألا تكون مع الساجدين

translation: He said, "I will not prostrate to a human whom You created from sounding clay of altered black smooth mud."
interpretation: This verse refers to the story of Iblis (Satan) refusing to prostrate to Adam when commanded by Allah. Iblis' pride and arrogance led him to disobey Allah's command, as he considered himself superior to Adam, who was created from clay. This verse highlights the dangers of pride and the importance of humility and obedience to Allah's commands, regardless of one's perceived status or superiority. It also demonstrates the consequences of disobedience and the path that led to Iblis being cast out of Paradise and becoming Satan, the sworn enemy of mankind.
orig: قال لم أكن لأسجد لبشر خلقته من صلصال من حمإ مسنون

translation: He said, "Then get out of it, for indeed you are expelled."
interpretation: In this verse, God is commanding Satan to leave Paradise as a consequence of his disobedience and refusal to prostrate before Adam. The use of the word "rajeem" (expelled or accursed) emphasizes the severity of Satan's actions and the resulting punishment of permanent banishment from God's mercy. This verse serves as a reminder to humanity that disobedience to God's commands leads to grave consequences and expulsion from His favor, just as Satan was cast out of Paradise for his prideful defiance.
orig: قال فاخرج منها فإنك رجيم

translation: And indeed, upon you is the curse until the Day of Judgment.
interpretation: This verse is a stern warning and condemnation to those who persistently reject the truth and oppose the message of Islam. It emphasizes that such individuals will bear the burden of Allah's curse and displeasure until the Day of Judgment, when they will face the consequences of their actions. The verse serves as a reminder that the choice to accept or reject guidance has serious and lasting implications, and that those who knowingly turn away from the path of righteousness will face a severe punishment in the Hereafter.
orig: وإن عليك اللعنة إلى يوم الدين

translation: He said, "My Lord, then reprieve me until the Day they are resurrected."
interpretation: In this verse, Satan is asking Allah to grant him respite until the Day of Resurrection. He wants to be allowed to live and continue his mission of misguiding humans until the appointed time when all will be raised from the dead for judgment. This request demonstrates Satan's arrogance and defiance, as he still seeks to oppose Allah's will and lead people astray, even after being condemned for his disobedience. It also highlights the ongoing struggle between good and evil that will persist until the end of time.
orig: قال رب فأنظرني إلى يوم يبعثون

translation: He said, "Then indeed, you are of those reprieved."
interpretation: This verse is a continuation of the dialogue between Allah and Iblis (Satan). After Iblis refused to prostrate before Adam, Allah condemned him. However, Iblis requested a reprieve until the Day of Judgment, and Allah granted his request. This verse confirms that Iblis is among those given respite until the appointed time. It highlights Allah's power over His creation, including Iblis, and shows that even the rebellious are subject to Allah's will and decree. The reprieve given to Iblis is not out of mercy but rather a test for humanity, as Iblis vowed to mislead mankind during this period.
orig: قال فإنك من المنظرين

translation: Until the Day of the time well-known.
interpretation: This verse refers to the Day of Judgment, a time that is known only to Allah. It emphasizes the inevitability and certainty of this event, which will mark the end of the world as we know it and the beginning of the eternal life in the Hereafter. The phrase "time well-known" suggests that the exact timing of this day is predetermined by Allah and will not be revealed until it arrives. This verse serves as a reminder for believers to prepare for this momentous day by leading righteous lives and fulfilling their obligations to Allah and fellow human beings.
orig: إلى يوم الوقت المعلوم

translation: He said: "My Lord, because You have put me in error, I will surely make [disobedience] attractive to them on earth, and I will mislead them all."
interpretation: In this verse, Satan (Iblis) blames God for his own disobedience and vows to lead humanity astray as revenge for being condemned. It shows Satan's arrogance and refusal to take responsibility for his actions, instead shifting the blame to God. The verse highlights the danger of Satan's influence in tempting people towards sin and disobedience to God. It serves as a warning for believers to be aware of Satan's tricks and to seek refuge in God from his whispers and temptations.
orig: قال رب بما أغويتني لأزينن لهم في الأرض ولأغوينهم أجمعين

translation: Except, among them, Your chosen servants.
interpretation: This verse refers to the righteous and sincere servants of Allah who are protected from the influence of Satan. They are the ones who have purified their hearts and actions, and remain steadfast in their devotion to Allah. The "chosen servants" are those who have attained a high level of faith and spiritual purity, making them immune to the temptations and deceptions of Satan. This highlights the importance of sincerity and devotion in one's relationship with Allah, as it is through this that one can attain divine protection and guidance.
orig: إلا عبادك منهم المخلصين

translation: Say, "This is my way; I invite to Allah with insight, I and those who follow me. And exalted is Allah; and I am not of those who associate others with Him."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of inviting others to the path of Allah with clear insight and knowledge. The Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and his followers are called to invite people to Islam based on a deep understanding of the religion, rather than blind imitation. The verse also stresses the significance of pure monotheism, affirming that Allah is exalted and free from any partners or associates. It serves as a reminder for Muslims to follow the example of the Prophet in conveying the message of Islam with wisdom and clarity, while maintaining a strong belief in the oneness of Allah.
orig: قال هذا صراط علي مستقيم

translation: Certainly, as for My servants, you have no authority over them except those who follow you of the deviators.
interpretation: This verse affirms that Satan has no power or influence over the true servants of Allah who are steadfast in their faith and obedience. The only ones who fall under Satan's sway are those who willingly choose to follow him and deviate from the straight path of guidance. It emphasizes the importance of remaining firm in one's faith and resisting the temptations and whispers of Satan. Ultimately, every individual is responsible for their own choices and actions, and cannot blame Satan for their misguidance if they knowingly chose to follow him instead of adhering to Allah's commands.
orig: إن عبادي ليس لك عليهم سلطان إلا من اتبعك من الغاوين

translation: And indeed, Hell is the promised place for them all.
interpretation: This verse serves as a stern warning to those who reject faith and persist in wrongdoing. It emphasizes that Hell is the ultimate destination for all those who choose to disobey God and follow the path of evil. The verse highlights the inescapable nature of divine justice, reminding individuals that their actions in this world have consequences in the afterlife. It is a powerful reminder for believers to stay steadfast in their faith and for those who have strayed to seek repentance before it is too late. The verse also underscores the importance of making the right choices in life, as the consequences of one's actions will determine their eternal fate.
orig: وإن جهنم لموعدهم أجمعين

translation: It has seven gates; for every gate is of them a portion designated.
interpretation: This verse is referring to Hell, which is described as having seven gates or entrances. Each gate is assigned to a specific group of sinners, suggesting that there are different levels or sections of Hell based on the severity and nature of one's sins. This emphasizes the idea that divine justice will be served in the afterlife, with punishment befitting each individual's deeds. The verse also implies that Hell is vast, with ample space to accommodate the multitudes of sinners who will be consigned there for their transgressions.
orig: لها سبعة أبواب لكل باب منهم جزء مقسوم

translation: Indeed, the righteous will be in gardens and springs
interpretation: This verse speaks about the ultimate reward that awaits those who are righteous and God-fearing. "Gardens" here symbolize paradise, a place of eternal bliss, comfort, and peace. The mention of "springs" adds to the imagery of the gardens, indicating the presence of abundant water, which is a symbol of purity, rejuvenation, and life. The righteous are those who follow the path of God, do good deeds, and refrain from evil. As a result of their righteousness, they will be granted the magnificent reward of dwelling in these gardens forever, enjoying the countless blessings and delights that God has prepared for them. This promise serves as a motivation for believers to stay on the path of righteousness and strive for the eternal reward in the hereafter.
orig: إن المتقين في جنات وعيون

translation: Enter it in peace and security.
interpretation: This verse is an assurance from Allah to the believers that they will be granted entry into Paradise, where they will dwell in a state of absolute peace, tranquility, and security. It signifies that all their fears, worries, and hardships of this worldly life will be left behind, and they will forever abide in the blissful gardens of Paradise, free from any form of harm, danger, or distress. This promise of eternal peace and security serves as a reward for their faith, righteous deeds, and perseverance in the path of Allah during their earthly lives.
orig: ادخلوها بسلام آمنين

translation: And We will remove whatever is in their breasts of resentment, [so they will be] brothers, on thrones facing each other.
interpretation: This verse speaks about the state of the believers in Paradise. Allah will remove any traces of resentment, envy, or ill-feelings that they may have harbored in their hearts towards each other in the worldly life. In Paradise, they will be like brothers, sitting on thrones facing each other in a state of peace, love, and harmony. This interpretation highlights the purification of hearts and the establishment of genuine bonds of brotherhood among the believers in the eternal life of Paradise, emphasizing the absence of any negative emotions and the presence of pure, everlasting relationships in the Hereafter.
orig: ونزعنا ما في صدورهم من غل إخوانا على سرر متقابلين

translation: No fatigue will touch them therein, nor from it will they [ever] be removed.
interpretation: This verse speaks about the eternal bliss and comfort that the righteous will experience in Paradise. They will not feel any form of tiredness, exhaustion, or weariness in Paradise. Moreover, they will never be expelled or removed from this state of felicity. This verse emphasizes the everlasting nature of the rewards in the Hereafter for those who have lived a righteous life in this world, in contrast to the temporary and fleeting nature of the pleasures of this worldly life. It serves as an encouragement for believers to strive for the eternal rewards of Paradise through faith and good deeds.
orig: لا يمسهم فيها نصب وما هم منها بمخرجين

translation: Inform My servants that it is I who am the Forgiving, the Merciful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes two of the most important attributes of Allah: His forgiveness and His mercy. It serves as a reminder to the believers that no matter how much they have sinned, they should never lose hope in Allah's mercy and forgiveness. Allah is always ready to forgive those who sincerely repent and turn back to Him. This verse also highlights the importance of conveying this message to others, as the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) is instructed to "inform" Allah's servants of His infinite mercy and forgiveness. It is a message of hope and encouragement for all believers, urging them to seek Allah's forgiveness and strive to be worthy of His mercy.
orig: نبئ عبادي أني أنا الغفور الرحيم

translation: And that My punishment is the painful punishment.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the severity and painfulness of Allah's punishment for those who disobey Him and reject His guidance. It serves as a warning to mankind that they should fear Allah's punishment and strive to follow the right path to avoid facing such torment in the Hereafter. The verse also highlights one of Allah's attributes, which is that He is capable of inflicting severe punishment upon those who deserve it.
orig: وأن عذابي هو العذاب الأليم

translation: And inform them about the guests of Abraham.
interpretation: This verse is referring to the story of Prophet Abraham and the angels who visited him in the form of guests. The purpose of mentioning this story is to remind the listeners of the importance of hospitality, generosity, and trust in Allah's plan. It also highlights the fact that even the most unexpected guests may bring blessings and good news from Allah, as was the case with Abraham's guests who informed him of the upcoming birth of his son, Isaac, despite his old age and his wife's barrenness. This story serves as an example for the believers to always welcome guests and treat them with kindness, as they may be a means of Allah's blessings and mercy.
orig: ونبئهم عن ضيف إبراهيم

translation: When they entered upon him and said, "Peace." He said, "Indeed, we are fearful of you."
interpretation: This verse is referring to the story of Prophet Abraham (peace be upon him) when he was visited by angels in the form of men. When the angels greeted Abraham with "Peace", he felt a sense of fear and unease, possibly because he did not recognize them and was wary of strangers. This shows that even great prophets experienced natural human emotions like fear in uncertain situations. However, the verse also highlights the importance of greeting others with "salam" or peace, which is a fundamental Islamic etiquette that helps establish a sense of trust and goodwill between people.
orig: إذ دخلوا عليه فقالوا سلاما قال إنا منكم وجلون

translation: They said, "Fear not, indeed we give you good tidings of a learned boy."
interpretation: This verse is conveying a message of reassurance and glad tidings. The angels are telling the recipient of this message, likely Prophet Abraham, not to be afraid or worried, as they are bringing him the good news of a son who will be blessed with knowledge and wisdom. This son is believed to be Prophet Isaac. The verse highlights the value and importance of knowledge in Islam, as the child is described as "learned" even before his birth, indicating that he will be endowed with divine knowledge and understanding. It also shows God's favor upon Abraham and his descendants, granting them righteous offspring who will be a source of guidance and blessing for humanity.
orig: قالوا لا توجل إنا نبشرك بغلام عليم

translation: He said, "Do you give me good tidings [of a son] when old age has overtaken me? Then of what [wonder] do you inform?"
interpretation: This verse is a response of Prophet Ibrahim (Abraham) when he was given the glad tidings of a son in his old age by the angels. The rhetorical question posed by Ibrahim expresses his astonishment and disbelief at the news, considering his advanced age. It highlights the miraculous nature of the event, as having a child in one's old age was seen as an impossibility. The verse also emphasizes the power and will of Allah, who can make anything happen, even that which seems impossible to humans. It is a reminder that Allah's plans and blessings can come in the most unexpected ways and times, and one should never lose hope in His mercy and generosity.
orig: قال أبشرتموني على أن مسني الكبر فبم تبشرون

translation: They said, "We have given you good tidings in truth, so do not be of the despairing."
interpretation: This verse is a reminder that one should never lose hope in the mercy and blessings of Allah. Even in the face of adversity or challenges, a believer should remain steadfast and optimistic, trusting in the divine plan. The verse emphasizes the importance of faith and the power of positive thinking, as despair is seen as a lack of trust in Allah's wisdom and beneficence. It encourages individuals to maintain a strong connection with their Creator and to find solace in the knowledge that He is always watching over them, ready to provide guidance and support when needed.
orig: قالوا بشرناك بالحق فلا تكن من القانطين

translation: He said, "And who despairs of the mercy of his Lord except for those astray?"
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of maintaining hope in God's mercy and forgiveness, even in the face of adversity or personal shortcomings. It suggests that only those who have gone astray from the right path would lose hope in God's compassion. The message is to always keep faith in God's ability to forgive and to never despair of His mercy, as this is a sign of being misguided. It encourages believers to continuously strive for self-improvement while trusting in God's love and support throughout their spiritual journey.
orig: قال ومن يقنط من رحمة ربه إلا الضالون

translation: He said, "Then what is your mission, O messengers?"
interpretation: In this verse, the questioner is asking the messengers about the purpose of their mission. It suggests that the messengers have come with a specific goal or objective that they have been sent to fulfill. The question "What is your mission?" implies that the messengers are not there by chance, but have been deliberately sent by a higher authority with a particular task to accomplish. The verse sets the stage for the messengers to explain their divine purpose and the message they have been entrusted to convey to the people.
orig: قال فما خطبكم أيها المرسلون

translation: They said, "Indeed, we have been sent to a people of criminals"
interpretation: This verse suggests that the angels or messengers of God are sent to convey a warning or message to a group of people who are deeply immersed in sin and wrongdoing. The use of the term "criminals" emphasizes the severity and extent of their transgressions. It implies that these people have persistently violated divine laws and moral principles, and their actions have reached a level that warrants divine intervention and admonition. The verse highlights the role of divine messengers as bearers of truth and guides to righteousness, tasked with calling people back to the path of God, even in the face of opposition from those who are steeped in iniquity.
orig: قالوا إنا أرسلنا إلى قوم مجرمين

translation: Except the family of Lot; indeed, We will save them all.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes God's mercy and protection towards the righteous, even amidst widespread punishment. While the people of Lot were generally wicked and faced divine retribution, God made an exception for Lot's family due to their faith and virtuous conduct. It demonstrates that God's justice is tempered with compassion, and that He rewards those who remain steadfast in their belief and good deeds, even if they are a minority. The verse offers hope and reassurance to believers, showing that God will ultimately save and protect the righteous, regardless of the circumstances or the actions of those around them.
orig: إلا آل لوط إنا لمنجوهم أجمعين

translation: Except his wife; We decreed that she is of those who remain behind.
interpretation: This verse refers to the wife of Prophet Lot, who was not among the believers. Allah had decreed that she would be left behind to face the punishment along with the other disbelievers, as she had betrayed her husband and sided with the wrongdoers.
