This highlights that faith and righteousness are personal matters, and even the closest relatives of a prophet can choose to reject the truth. It also emphasizes the justice of Allah, as He does not spare the wrongdoers from punishment, regardless of their relation to the believers.
orig: إلا امرأته قدرنا إنها لمن الغابرين

translation: And when the messengers came to the family of Lot.
interpretation: This verse is referring to the arrival of the angels, sent by Allah as messengers, to the people of Prophet Lot. These angels came in the form of handsome men to test and expose the evil deeds and homosexuality practiced by Lot's people. The arrival of these messengers marks the beginning of the end for the people of Lot, who had persistently rejected Allah's guidance and indulged in abominable acts. It signifies that the time for their punishment and destruction was drawing near, as a consequence of their sinful behavior and defiance of Allah's commands.
orig: فلما جاء آل لوط المرسلون

translation: He said, "Indeed, you are a people unknown."
interpretation: This verse is a response from Prophet Lut (Lot) to the people of Sodom who came to his house seeking to commit immoral acts with his guests. Lut expressed his strong disapproval of their behavior, stating that they were a people who were unknown to him in terms of their conduct and morality. It highlights the fact that their actions were so reprehensible and contrary to the teachings of God that Lut could not even recognize them as people of faith or righteousness. The verse emphasizes the importance of adhering to moral and ethical principles, and the consequences of deviating from the path of virtue.
orig: قال إنكم قوم منكرون

translation: They said, "Rather, we have come to you with that about which they were disputing."
interpretation: This verse is likely referring to a group of people who came to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) with a dispute or disagreement they were having. Instead of resolving the matter themselves, they brought it to the Prophet for his judgment and guidance. This demonstrates the trust and confidence they had in the Prophet's wisdom and authority to settle their differences. It also highlights the role of the Prophet as a leader and arbiter for the Muslim community.
orig: قالوا بل جئناك بما كانوا فيه يمترون

translation: And We have brought you the truth and indeed, We are truthful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the truthfulness and authenticity of the message brought by Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him). It asserts that the Qur'an is the ultimate truth revealed by Allah, and that Allah Himself is testifying to its veracity. The verse serves as a reassurance to the believers that they can have complete faith in the Qur'an and the Prophet's teachings, as they come directly from the Most Truthful, Allah. It also implies that those who reject this truth are in fact rejecting the word of Allah and will be held accountable for their disbelief.
orig: وأتيناك بالحق وإنا لصادقون

translation: So set out with your family during a portion of the night and follow behind them and let not anyone among you look back and continue on to where you are commanded.
interpretation: This verse is a divine command to Prophet Lot (peace be upon him) to leave his town with his believing family members during the night, and not to look back at the destruction that was about to befall the sinful people. It emphasizes the importance of obeying God's commands without hesitation or attachment to the material world, trusting fully in His plan and wisdom. The verse also illustrates God's mercy in saving the righteous while punishing the wicked, and serves as a reminder for believers to always prioritize faith and submission to the Almighty.
orig: فأسر بأهلك بقطع من الليل واتبع أدبارهم ولا يلتفت منكم أحد وامضوا حيث تؤمرون

translation: And We conveyed to him [Lot] that decree: that those [sinners] would be eliminated by early morning.
interpretation: This verse is a warning from Allah to Prophet Lot (peace be upon him) about the impending destruction of his people due to their sinful behavior. Allah had decreed that the wrongdoers among Lot's nation would be completely wiped out and annihilated by the morning as a punishment for their defiance and rejection of Allah's message. It shows the severity and swiftness of Allah's judgment upon those who persist in evil and immorality despite the warnings of His messengers. The verse also serves as a reminder for all people to heed the warnings of divine revelation and to turn away from sin before it is too late and Allah's punishment befalls them.
orig: وقضينا إليه ذلك الأمر أن دابر هؤلاء مقطوع مصبحين

translation: And the people of the city came rejoicing.
interpretation: This verse suggests that the people of the city were excited and happy about something, likely good news or a positive event that they were anticipating. The use of the word "rejoicing" implies a strong sense of joy and celebration among the people. The verse captures a moment of shared happiness and optimism within the community.
orig: وجاء أهل المدينة يستبشرون

translation: He said, "Indeed, these are my guests, so do not embarrass me.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of honoring and protecting one's guests. In Arab culture, hospitality towards guests is highly valued and considered a sacred duty. The host is expected to ensure the comfort, safety, and dignity of their guests. Embarrassing or mistreating guests is seen as a grave violation of social norms and a reflection of poor character. The verse serves as a reminder to uphold the principles of generosity, respect, and hospitality towards those whom one has invited into their home or taken under their care.
orig: قال إن هؤلاء ضيفي فلا تفضحون

translation: And fear Allah and do not disgrace me.
interpretation: This verse is a reminder to be mindful of Allah and to avoid actions that would bring shame or embarrassment to oneself or others. It emphasizes the importance of upholding one's dignity and honor in the sight of Allah. The verse encourages believers to conduct themselves in a manner that is pleasing to Allah, avoiding any behavior that would lead to disgrace or humiliation. It also implies that one should be considerate of others and not engage in actions that would cause them shame or dishonor. Ultimately, the verse highlights the significance of taqwa (God-consciousness) in guiding one's actions and decisions.
orig: واتقوا الله ولا تخزون

translation: They said, "Did we not forbid you from [protecting] the worlds?"
interpretation: This verse is interpreted as the angels questioning Allah's decision to appoint a human (Adam) as a vicegerent on earth, despite their concerns that humans would cause corruption and shed blood. The angels believed that they were more suited for this role as they constantly praised and glorified Allah. However, Allah's response in the following verse affirms His wisdom and knowledge, indicating that He knows what the angels do not know about the potential and purpose of human beings on earth.
orig: قالوا أولم ننهك عن العالمين

translation: He said, "These are my daughters, if you are to do [anything]."
interpretation: This verse is understood by many scholars to be a rhetorical statement by Prophet Lot, not a literal offer of his daughters for marriage or relations. He was appealing to the mob's sense of decency and honor, as in that culture it would be shameful to harm the women under a man's protection. Lot was attempting to dissuade them from their evil intentions by reminding them of proper conduct, not actually presenting his daughters to them. It shows the lengths to which he went to protect his guests from the sinful desires of the mob.
orig: قال هؤلاء بناتي إن كنتم فاعلين

translation: Verily, by your life (O Muhammad), they were wandering blindly in their intoxication.
interpretation: This verse is a strong emphasis on the severity of the disbelievers' misguidance and heedlessness. The phrase "by your life" is a form of oath, indicating the gravity of the matter. The verse suggests that the disbelievers were so deeply immersed in their false beliefs, desires, and worldly pursuits that they became blind to the truth, as if intoxicated. This state of spiritual inebriation prevented them from recognizing the clear signs and guidance that Allah had provided through His Prophet. The verse also implies that this condition of being lost in one's own delusions and failing to see the truth is a form of divine punishment, as it leads to further straying from the right path.
orig: لعمرك إنهم لفي سكرتهم يعمهون

translation: So the shriek seized them at sunrise.
interpretation: This verse refers to a punishment that befell a people who persistently rejected the message of Allah despite repeated warnings. The "shriek" or "blast" that seized them at sunrise is interpreted as a sudden, devastating punishment that destroyed them completely, likely in the form of a natural disaster or a divine intervention. It signifies the ultimate consequence of denying the truth and disobeying Allah's commands, emphasizing that no one can escape Allah's judgment and that His punishment can come swiftly and decisively at any moment, even at the break of dawn when people feel secure and complacent.
orig: فأخذتهم الصيحة مشرقين

translation: So We turned it upside down, and rained upon them stones of baked clay.
interpretation: This verse refers to the punishment that Allah inflicted upon the people of Lut (Lot) for their grave sins and disobedience. Allah destroyed their cities by turning them upside down, causing utter destruction and ruin. Additionally, Allah sent upon them a rain of stones made from baked clay, adding to their torment. This severe punishment serves as a reminder of the consequences of defying Allah's commands and indulging in immoral behavior. It also demonstrates Allah's power over His creation and His ability to inflict retribution on those who persist in wrongdoing.
orig: فجعلنا عاليها سافلها وأمطرنا عليهم حجارة من سجيل

translation: Indeed in that are signs for those who discern.
interpretation: This verse points to the signs of Allah's power and wisdom that are present in the world around us. Those who are perceptive and reflect deeply will be able to recognize these signs and understand their significance. They will see in the creation the handiwork of the Almighty Creator and appreciate His majesty. The verse encourages people to ponder and contemplate, to look beyond the superficial and to discern the deeper truths and meanings behind what they observe in the universe. It is a call to use one's intellect and insight to strengthen faith and attain certainty in the existence and oneness of Allah.
orig: إن في ذلك لآيات للمتوسمين

translation: And indeed, it is on an enduring path.
interpretation: This verse refers to the Qur'an itself, affirming that it is on a path of permanence and timelessness. The Qur'an's message and guidance will endure throughout the ages, remaining unchanged and relevant for all of humanity until the end of time. This is a testament to the divine nature of the Qur'an, as it is protected by Allah from any alteration or corruption. The path of the Qur'an is one that leads to truth, righteousness, and success in both this world and the hereafter for those who follow its teachings sincerely.
orig: وإنها لبسبيل مقيم

translation: Indeed in that is a sign for the believers.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the Qur'an contains clear signs and evidence that it is a revelation from Allah. These signs serve as a means of strengthening the faith of the believers. When they reflect upon the profound wisdom, linguistic miracles, and divine guidance within the Qur'an, it increases their certainty in its divine origin. The verse encourages the believers to ponder over the Qur'an and recognize the numerous proofs that confirm its truth, thereby deepening their conviction and connection with Allah.
orig: إن في ذلك لآية للمؤمنين

translation: And indeed, the companions of the Aykah were [also] wrongdoers.
interpretation: This verse refers to the people of Madyan, who were also known as the companions of the Aykah (the wood or thicket). They were considered wrongdoers because they rejected the message of their prophet, Shu'ayb, and engaged in dishonest business practices, such as cheating in weights and measures. The verse implies that they faced divine punishment for their transgressions, similar to other nations who rejected their prophets. It serves as a warning to those who engage in wrongdoing and emphasizes the importance of heeding the message of the prophets and living a righteous life.
orig: وإن كان أصحاب الأيكة لظالمين

translation: So We took retribution from them, and indeed, both [cities] are on a clear highway.
interpretation: This verse refers to the punishment that Allah inflicted upon the people of the two towns mentioned in the previous verses, who rejected the messengers sent to them. The verse emphasizes that the destruction of these towns serves as a clear sign and warning for those who pass by them on the highway. It is a reminder of the consequences of rejecting Allah's message and the fate that awaits those who persist in disbelief and wrongdoing. The verse also implies that the ruins of these towns will remain as a lasting example and lesson for future generations.
orig: فانتقمنا منهم وإنهما لبإمام مبين

translation: The companions of Al-Hijr denied the messengers.
interpretation: This verse refers to the people of Thamud, who lived in the region of Al-Hijr. They rejected the message brought to them by the prophet Salih, who was sent to guide them to the right path. The Thamud were arrogant and refused to believe in Salih's warnings, instead challenging him to bring about the punishment he threatened them with. As a result of their denial and defiance, Allah destroyed them with a mighty blast, leaving their dwellings abandoned as a reminder to future generations of the consequences of rejecting the truth and the messengers of Allah.
orig: ولقد كذب أصحاب الحجر المرسلين

translation: And We gave them Our signs, but they were turning away from them.
interpretation: This verse suggests that God has provided clear evidence and signs of His existence and power to humanity, but despite this, many people choose to ignore or turn away from these signs. They may be too preoccupied with worldly matters, or simply unwilling to acknowledge the truth. The verse implies that this is a conscious choice on their part, and that they will be held accountable for their decision to reject God's message. It serves as a warning to those who disregard the signs of God, and an encouragement to those who are open to receiving His guidance.
orig: وآتيناهم آياتنا فكانوا عنها معرضين

translation: And they used to carve from the mountains, homes feeling secure.
interpretation: This verse refers to the people of Thamud, who were known for their exceptional skills in carving dwellings out of the mountains. They felt secure and proud of their abilities, thinking that their strong and well-crafted homes would protect them from any calamity. However, their arrogance and disobedience to Allah's messages ultimately led to their destruction, despite their feelings of safety in their mountain homes. This verse serves as a reminder that true security and protection come from obedience to Allah, not from worldly constructions or abilities.
orig: وكانوا ينحتون من الجبال بيوتا آمنين

translation: So the shriek seized them at sunrise.
interpretation: This verse refers to a punishment that befell a group of people who persistently rejected the message of Allah and His prophets. The "shriek" mentioned here is interpreted as a piercing, terrifying sound or blast that came upon them suddenly at sunrise, marking their destruction. It signifies the abrupt and inescapable nature of divine retribution against those who choose to oppose the truth and transgress the bounds set by Allah. The verse serves as a warning to humanity that the consequences of denying faith and indulging in wrongdoing will ultimately lead to a severe and irreversible punishment from Allah.
orig: فأخذتهم الصيحة مصبحين

translation: So there availed them not what they used to earn.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the futility of worldly gains and accomplishments in the face of divine judgment. It suggests that on the Day of Reckoning, the wealth, status, and power that people strived to accumulate in their earthly lives will be of no benefit to them. Their deeds and actions will be the only things that matter, and if they have not lived righteously and in accordance with God's commands, their worldly successes will be rendered meaningless. This verse serves as a reminder to prioritize one's spiritual well-being and to focus on leading a life that is pleasing to God, rather than being preoccupied with material pursuits that ultimately hold no value in the eternal realm.
orig: فما أغنى عنهم ما كانوا يكسبون

translation: And We have not created the heavens and earth and that between them except in truth, and indeed, the Hour is coming; so forgive with gracious forgiveness.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that God created the universe with a profound purpose and meaning, not merely in vain or for sport. It also serves as a reminder that the Day of Judgment is inevitable and will certainly come to pass. In light of this reality, the verse encourages the Prophet Muhammad, and by extension all believers, to be forgiving and gracious towards others, even in the face of hostility or persecution. This "gracious forgiveness" involves pardoning others with kindness and magnanimity, without harboring resentment or bitterness in one's heart. The verse thus promotes a spirit of compassion, mercy, and benevolence, even towards those who may have wronged us, reflecting the highest ideals of Islamic ethics and spirituality.
orig: وما خلقنا السماوات والأرض وما بينهما إلا بالحق وإن الساعة لآتية فاصفح الصفح الجميل

translation: Indeed, your Lord is the Knowing Creator.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes two essential attributes of Allah: His creative power and His infinite knowledge. It reminds us that Allah is the One who brings everything into existence, fashioning all things according to His wisdom and will. Moreover, His creation is not a product of chance or randomness, but a result of His profound knowledge that encompasses all aspects of His creation. This verse encourages believers to reflect upon the marvels of Allah's creation and to recognize His power and knowledge in every facet of their lives, thereby deepening their faith and gratitude towards their Lord.
orig: إن ربك هو الخلاق العليم

translation: And We have certainly given you, [O Muhammad], seven of the often repeated [verses] and the great Qur'an.
interpretation: This verse is referring to the special status and importance of Surah Al-Fatihah, which consists of seven verses that are often repeated in daily prayers. It is considered the greatest surah in the Qur'an. Allah has bestowed this surah upon Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) as a great gift and honor, emphasizing its unique position. The verse also highlights that along with Surah Al-Fatihah, Allah has revealed the entire Qur'an to Muhammad as a guidance and mercy for mankind. This shows the divine origin and significance of both Surah Al-Fatihah and the Qur'an as a whole in the life of believers.
orig: ولقد آتيناك سبعا من المثاني والقرآن العظيم

translation: Do not extend your eyes toward that by which We have given enjoyment to [some] categories of them, and do not grieve over them. And lower your wing to the believers.
interpretation: This verse is advising the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and the believers not to be envious or desirous of the worldly pleasures and luxuries that some disbelievers may enjoy. It reminds us that these temporary enjoyments are fleeting and should not be a source of sadness or distress. Instead, we should focus on humility, gentleness, and compassion towards fellow believers, treating them with kindness and care. The metaphor of lowering one's wing emphasizes the importance of showing empathy, support, and love to the believers, creating a sense of unity and brotherhood within the Muslim community.
orig: لا تمدن عينيك إلى ما متعنا به أزواجا منهم ولا تحزن عليهم واخفض جناحك للمؤمنين

translation: And say, "Indeed, I am the clear warner."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the role of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) as a clear warner to humanity. As a messenger of Allah, his duty is to convey the divine message and warn people of the consequences of rejecting faith and indulging in wrongdoing. The verse underscores the clarity and unambiguity of his warning, leaving no room for doubt or confusion. It also implies that the Prophet's warning comes from a place of concern and compassion for humanity, urging them to heed the message and follow the righteous path to attain salvation in this world and the hereafter.
orig: وقل إني أنا النذير المبين

translation: As We had revealed [scriptures] to those who had divided [revealed scriptures].
interpretation: This verse is referring to the previous nations who were given divine scriptures, but they differed concerning them and divided into sects. They did not preserve the original message and interpret it correctly as it was revealed. Instead, they altered the scriptures to suit their own desires and inclinations. This serves as a warning to the Muslims to avoid falling into the same pattern of sectarianism and division, and to adhere to the Qur'an and the teachings of Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) in order to maintain unity and preserve the authentic message of Islam.
orig: كما أنزلنا على المقتسمين

translation: Those who have made the Qur'an into portions.
interpretation: This verse is criticizing those who have divided the Qur'an into parts, accepting some of it while rejecting other parts to suit their own desires or beliefs. It suggests that the Qur'an should be taken as a whole, with all of its verses and teachings accepted and followed in their entirety. Picking and choosing from the Qur'an according to one's whims is seen as a form of disbelief and a failure to submit to Allah's complete message as revealed in the holy book.
orig: الذين جعلوا القرآن عضين

translation: So by your Lord, We will surely question them all
interpretation: This verse is a strong oath from Allah, swearing by Himself, that on the Day of Judgment, every single person will be questioned about their deeds in this world. It emphasizes the absolute certainty and inevitability of the accountability that all humans will face before their Lord. The verse underscores the gravity and seriousness of the Day of Reckoning, where no one will be left out or excused, and everyone will have to answer for their actions and beliefs. It serves as a reminder for people to be mindful of their conduct in this life, knowing that they will be held responsible for it in the Hereafter.
orig: فوربك لنسألنهم أجمعين

translation: For what they used to do.
interpretation: This verse is referring to the fact that people will be held accountable on the Day of Judgment for their deeds and actions in this worldly life. It implies that nothing will be overlooked or forgotten, and that every person will face the consequences of their choices and behavior, whether good or bad. This verse serves as a reminder for individuals to be mindful of their actions and to strive for righteousness, knowing that they will ultimately be answerable to Allah for how they lived their lives.
orig: عما كانوا يعملون

translation: So proclaim what you are commanded and turn away from the polytheists.
interpretation: This verse is a command to the Prophet Muhammad to openly declare the message of Islam that he has been commanded to convey by Allah, and to disregard the opposition and hostility of the polytheists who reject the message. It is a call to remain steadfast in preaching the truth, even in the face of adversity and persecution. The verse emphasizes the importance of proclaiming the message with courage and conviction, without being deterred or discouraged by the disbelievers. It also highlights the need to turn away from and ignore those who persist in polytheism and refuse to accept the oneness of Allah.
orig: فاصدع بما تؤمر وأعرض عن المشركين

translation: Indeed, We are sufficient for you against the mockers.
interpretation: This verse is a reassurance from Allah to Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) that He will protect him from those who mock and ridicule him and his message. It implies that the Prophet need not worry about the taunts and insults of the disbelievers, as Allah Himself will deal with them and defend His messenger. This verse highlights the divine support and protection granted to the Prophet in the face of adversity and opposition, emphasizing that the ultimate victory belongs to Allah and those who stand firm in faith and righteousness.
orig: إنا كفيناك المستهزئين

translation: Those who set up another god with Allah, they will come to know.
interpretation: This verse serves as a stern warning to those who commit the grave sin of shirk, which is associating partners with Allah or worshipping others besides Him. It emphasizes that those who engage in idolatry or polytheism will eventually face the severe consequences of their actions. They will come to realize the gravity of their mistake and will understand the true power and oneness of Allah. The verse implies that the punishment for shirk will be severe and that the idolaters will regret their wrongdoing when faced with the reality of Allah's judgment.
orig: الذين يجعلون مع الله إلها آخر فسوف يعلمون

translation: And We already know that your breast is constrained by what they say.
interpretation: This verse is addressing the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him), acknowledging that he feels distressed and saddened by the disbelief, rejection, and hurtful words of those who oppose his message. It is a reassurance from Allah that He is aware of the Prophet's emotional state and the difficulties he faces in conveying the message of Islam. The verse serves as a consolation and encouragement to the Prophet to remain patient and steadfast in the face of adversity, knowing that Allah understands his struggles and supports him in his mission.
orig: ولقد نعلم أنك يضيق صدرك بما يقولون

translation: So glorify the praises of your Lord and be of those who prostrate themselves (to Him).
interpretation: This verse is a command to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and, by extension, to all believers to engage in the glorification and praise of Allah, and to be among those who humble themselves before Him in prayer and prostration. It emphasizes the importance of acknowledging Allah's greatness and submitting to Him in worship. By doing so, one aligns oneself with the true purpose of creation and attains spiritual purification and closeness to Allah. This verse highlights the central role of worship and devotion in the life of a believer.
orig: فسبح بحمد ربك وكن من الساجدين

translation: And worship your Lord until there comes to you the certainty [of death].
interpretation: This verse is a command to continue worshipping Allah and obeying His commands until death overtakes us. "The certainty" here refers to death, which is the only thing that is certain in this life. The verse emphasizes the importance of consistent and lifelong devotion to Allah, as we do not know when death will come. It encourages the believers to remain steadfast in their faith and worship, making it a top priority throughout their lives, until they ultimately meet their Lord. This unwavering dedication is key to attaining success and salvation in the Hereafter.
orig: واعبد ربك حتى يأتيك اليقين

translation: The command of Allah has come, so do not seek to hasten it. Exalted is He and high above what they associate with Him.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the inevitability and certainty of Allah's decree. It serves as a reminder to the believers that they should not be impatient or try to rush the fulfillment of Allah's promise, as His plan will unfold according to His divine wisdom and perfect timing. The verse also affirms the absolute transcendence and uniqueness of Allah, stating that He is far above any partners or equals that people may wrongfully attribute to Him. It underscores the importance of having complete trust and submission to Allah's will, knowing that He is in control of all affairs and that His decisions are always just and wise.
orig: أتى أمر الله فلا تستعجلوه سبحانه وتعالى عما يشركون

translation: He sends down the angels, with the inspiration of His command, upon whom He wills of His servants, [telling them], "Warn that there is no deity except Me; so fear Me."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the oneness and uniqueness of Allah, and that He alone deserves to be worshipped and feared. Allah sends down the angels with divine revelation and inspiration to His chosen prophets and messengers, commanding them to warn their people that there is no true deity worthy of worship except Allah. This message serves as a reminder for mankind to be mindful of their actions and to fear Allah by obeying His commands and abstaining from what He has forbidden. The verse also highlights the role of prophets as warners and bearers of glad tidings, conveying Allah's message to guide humanity towards the right path.
orig: ينزل الملائكة بالروح من أمره على من يشاء من عباده أن أنذروا أنه لا إله إلا أنا فاتقون

translation: He created the heavens and earth in truth. High is He above what they associate with Him.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that God created the universe with a profound purpose and meaning, not merely in vain or for sport. It highlights the truth and wisdom behind His creation. The verse also affirms God's transcendence above all the false deities and partners that the polytheists wrongfully attribute to Him. It underscores His uniqueness, stating that He is exalted far above their idolatrous associations. The verse thus serves as a strong rejection of shirk (polytheism) and a call to worship God alone.
orig: خلق السماوات والأرض بالحق تعالى عما يشركون

translation: He created man from a sperm-drop; then at once, he is a clear adversary.
interpretation: This verse highlights the miraculous creation of human beings from a mere drop of fluid, and yet despite this humble beginning, man becomes an open disputant, arguing and challenging his Creator. It points to the rebellious nature of man, who often forgets his origins and purpose, and instead becomes arrogant and contentious. The verse serves as a reminder for humans to remain humble and grateful to their Creator, acknowledging their true nature and the purpose of their existence.
orig: خلق الإنسان من نطفة فإذا هو خصيم مبين

translation: And the cattle, He has created them for you; in them is warmth and [numerous] benefits, and from them you eat.
interpretation: This verse highlights the bounties that Allah has bestowed upon humankind through the creation of cattle. These animals serve multiple purposes that benefit us - they provide us with warmth through their skins and furs, we derive various other benefits from them such as using them for transportation or obtaining milk, and they also serve as a source of food. This verse reminds us to be grateful for the blessings that Allah has provided us through His creation, and to use these resources responsibly and with appreciation.
orig: والأنعام خلقها لكم فيها دفء ومنافع ومنها تأكلون

translation: And for you in them is [their] beauty when you bring them in [for the evening] and when you send them out [to pasture].
interpretation: This verse highlights the beauty and benefits that livestock, such as camels, cattle, and sheep, provide to humans. The animals are a source of aesthetic pleasure when they are brought back home in the evening after grazing, and when they are sent out to pasture in the morning. This implies that these animals not only serve practical purposes but also bring joy and contentment to their owners through their mere presence and the daily routines associated with their care. The verse encourages people to appreciate and be grateful for the blessings and beauty found in the animals that Allah has provided for their benefit.
orig: ولكم فيها جمال حين تريحون وحين تسرحون

translation: And they carry your loads to a land you could not have reached except with difficulty to yourselves. Indeed, your Lord is Kind and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse highlights the mercy and kindness of Allah towards His creation. It points out that Allah has subjected animals to carry the heavy loads of humans to distant lands that they would not have been able to reach without great difficulty. This is a reminder of Allah's favor upon humans and the importance of treating these animals with kindness and not overburdening them beyond their capacity. The verse also emphasizes the idea that Allah is fully aware of the hardships faced by His servants and provides them with the means to overcome those difficulties out of His mercy and kindness.
orig: وتحمل أثقالكم إلى بلد لم تكونوا بالغيه إلا بشق الأنفس إن ربكم لرءوف رحيم

translation: And [He created] the horses, mules and donkeys for you to ride and [as] adornment. And He creates that which you do not know.
interpretation: This verse points to the various modes of transportation that Allah has created for the benefit and convenience of human beings. Horses, mules, and donkeys are mentioned specifically as animals that can be used for riding and as a means of adornment or prestige. The verse also alludes to the fact that Allah creates other means of transportation that were unknown to people at the time of the revelation, hinting at future innovations and technological advancements in the field of transportation. This demonstrates Allah's power, creativity, and His favor upon humanity by providing them with means that facilitate their lives and enable them to traverse distances with ease.
orig: والخيل والبغال والحمير لتركبوها وزينة ويخلق ما لا تعلمون

translation: And upon Allah is the direction of the [right] way, and among the various paths are [some] deviating. And if He willed, He could have guided you all.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that it is Allah who guides people to the straight path, and that there are many paths that deviate from it. The interpretation is that guidance ultimately comes from Allah, and He has the power to guide all of humanity if He so willed. However, Allah has given humans free will to choose their own paths, even though some of those paths may lead astray. It is up to individuals to seek Allah's guidance and follow the straight path that leads to success in this life and the hereafter.
orig: وعلى الله قصد السبيل ومنها جائر ولو شاء لهداكم أجمعين

translation: It is He who sends down rain from the sky; from it is drink and from it is foliage in which you pasture [animals].
interpretation: This verse highlights the immense blessings and mercy of Allah upon His creation. He sends down rain from the sky, which serves multiple purposes essential for life on earth. The rain provides drinking water for humans and animals, sustaining life. Moreover, the rain also nourishes vegetation and trees, providing pastures and grazing areas for livestock. This interpretation emphasizes the interconnectedness of Allah's creation and how He has designed the natural world to support and sustain life. It also reminds us to be grateful for these blessings and recognize the power and benevolence of the Almighty in providing for His creatures.
orig: هو الذي أنزل من السماء ماء لكم منه شراب ومنه شجر فيه تسيمون

translation: He causes to grow for you thereby the crops, olives, palm trees, grapevines, and from all the fruits. Indeed in that is a sign for a people who give thought.
interpretation: This verse points to the signs of Allah's power, mercy and providence in causing all kinds of vegetation and fruits to grow from the earth, providing sustenance for humans. It encourages people to reflect deeply on these signs, which demonstrate Allah's supreme wisdom in His creation. Pondering over how Allah brings forth a wide variety of crops and fruits from the same soil is presented as a proof of His existence and creative power. The verse conveys that those who sincerely contemplate and use their intellect will recognize these as clear indications pointing to the One True God who alone deserves worship.
orig: ينبت لكم به الزرع والزيتون والنخيل والأعناب ومن كل الثمرات إن في ذلك لآية لقوم يتفكرون

translation: And He has subjected for you the night and the day and the sun and the moon, and the stars are subjected by His command. Indeed in that are signs for a people who reason.
interpretation: This verse highlights the immense blessings and favors that Allah has bestowed upon humanity. The alternation of night and day, the sun, the moon, and the stars - all of these are made subservient to us by Allah's command. They follow precise patterns and serve important functions for our benefit, such as providing light, marking the passage of time, and enabling navigation. The fact that these celestial bodies are subjected to Allah's command is a testament to His supreme power and control over the universe. For those who reflect deeply and use their intellect, these are clear signs of Allah's existence, wisdom, and benevolence. The verse encourages us to ponder over these signs and appreciate the Creator who has made them possible for our sustenance and well-being.
orig: وسخر لكم الليل والنهار والشمس والقمر والنجوم مسخرات بأمره إن في ذلك لآيات لقوم يعقلون

translation: And the things on this earth which He has multiplied in varying colours [and qualities]: verily in this is a Sign for men who celebrate the praises of Allah [in gratitude].
interpretation: This verse points to the diverse and colorful creations of Allah on earth as a sign for those who reflect and are grateful. It encourages humans to ponder upon the variety in Allah's creation, such as the different plants, animals, landscapes, and natural phenomena, each with unique colors and qualities. This diversity is presented as a testament to Allah's creative power and wisdom. The verse emphasizes that those who actively remember Allah and celebrate His praises with gratitude will recognize and appreciate these signs, drawing inspiration and faith from the marvels of Allah's creation. It serves as a reminder for humans to be mindful, reflective, and thankful for the blessings and wonders that surround them in the natural world.
orig: وما ذرأ لكم في الأرض مختلفا ألوانه إن في ذلك لآية لقوم يذكرون

translation: And it is He who subjected the sea for you to eat from it tender meat and to extract from it ornaments which you wear. And you see the ships plowing through it, and [He subjected it] that you may seek of His bounty; and perhaps you will be grateful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the blessings and bounties that Allah has bestowed upon humanity through the subjugation of the sea. It highlights the various benefits that we derive from the sea, such as the provision of fresh meat and the extraction of ornaments like pearls and coral. The verse also points to the ships that sail through the sea, facilitating trade and the seeking of Allah's bounty. These blessings are meant to evoke a sense of gratitude within us, reminding us to be thankful for the favors and mercy that Allah has shown us. The verse encourages us to reflect upon the signs of Allah's power and benevolence in the world around us, and to use these blessings in a manner that pleases Him.
orig: وهو الذي سخر البحر لتأكلوا منه لحما طريا وتستخرجوا منه حلية تلبسونها وترى الفلك مواخر فيه ولتبتغوا من فضله ولعلكم تشكرون

translation: And He has cast into the earth firmly set mountains, lest it shift with you, and [made] rivers and roads, that you may be guided.
interpretation: This verse highlights the wisdom and power of Allah in creating the earth with its mountains, rivers, and paths. The mountains serve as stabilizers for the earth's surface, preventing it from shaking or shifting, which could cause great harm to humans. The rivers provide water for life and the paths guide people in their journeys. These natural features are signs of Allah's mercy and care for His creation, designed to help humans navigate the world and find their way both physically and spiritually. The verse encourages reflection on these blessings and the guidance they provide, urging humans to be grateful and to seek Allah's guidance in all aspects of life.
orig: وألقى في الأرض رواسي أن تميد بكم وأنهارا وسبلا لعلكم تهتدون

translation: And landmarks. And by the stars they are [also] guided.
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of natural signs and phenomena that Allah has created to guide humanity. The stars and other celestial bodies serve as navigational aids, helping people determine directions, especially during night travel or sea voyages. These signs point to Allah's wisdom and mercy in providing means of guidance for His creation. Moreover, the verse can also be understood metaphorically, suggesting that just as the stars guide people in the physical world, Allah's revelations and prophets serve as spiritual guides, leading believers towards the right path in their lives.
orig: وعلامات وبالنجم هم يهتدون

translation: Is He then Who creates like one that creates not? Will you not then remember?
interpretation: This verse is a rhetorical question that highlights the vast difference between Allah, the Creator of all things, and His creation. It reminds us to reflect upon the fact that Allah alone has the power to create, while His creations, including humans, cannot create anything from nothing. The question "Will you not then remember?" serves as a wake-up call for those who may have forgotten or neglected to acknowledge Allah's unique attribute as the Creator. It encourages people to use their intellect and reasoning to recognize the signs of Allah's existence and power, and to be grateful for His blessings. The verse also implies that worshipping anyone or anything other than the Creator is illogical and unjustifiable.
orig: أفمن يخلق كمن لا يخلق أفلا تذكرون

translation: And if you should count the favors of Allah, you could not enumerate them. Indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the countless blessings and favors that Allah has bestowed upon humanity. It suggests that no matter how much we try, we can never fully comprehend or appreciate the extent of Allah's generosity and kindness towards us. The verse also highlights two of Allah's important attributes: His forgiveness and mercy. Despite our inability to fully acknowledge and appreciate His blessings, Allah continues to forgive our shortcomings and show us mercy. This verse serves as a reminder for us to be grateful for all that we have been given and to seek Allah's forgiveness and mercy in our lives.
orig: وإن تعدوا نعمة الله لا تحصوها إن الله لغفور رحيم

translation: And Allah knows what you conceal and what you declare.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the omniscience of Allah, reminding us that He is fully aware of both our hidden thoughts and intentions, as well as our outward actions and statements. It serves as a powerful reminder to be mindful of our deeds and to strive for sincerity, knowing that nothing escapes Allah's knowledge. This consciousness of Allah's all-encompassing knowledge should motivate believers to maintain righteousness in all aspects of their lives, whether in public or private, as they will ultimately be held accountable for their actions in the Hereafter.
orig: والله يعلم ما تسرون وما تعلنون

translation: And those they invoke besides Allah create nothing, and they [themselves] are created.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the fundamental difference between Allah, the Creator, and the false deities that people worship. While Allah has the power to create, the idols and false gods that people invoke are themselves created beings, incapable of creating anything. This highlights the futility of worshipping anyone or anything other than Allah, as these false deities are powerless and dependent on Allah for their own existence. The verse serves as a reminder to humanity that Allah alone is worthy of worship and that attributing divine qualities to anyone or anything else is a grave error.
orig: والذين يدعون من دون الله لا يخلقون شيئا وهم يخلقون

translation: They are dead, not alive, and they do not perceive when they will be resurrected.
interpretation: This verse is referring to the disbelievers who have died in a state of disbelief. They are described as being dead, both physically and spiritually, as they have rejected faith. In this state, they have no awareness or consciousness. They do not know or perceive when they will be resurrected by Allah on the Day of Judgment to face the consequences of their actions and disbelief in this world. It highlights the reality of death for those who die without faith, and the lack of realization they have about the inevitability of resurrection and accountability in the Hereafter.
orig: أموات غير أحياء وما يشعرون أيان يبعثون

translation: Your god is One God. But those who do not believe in the Hereafter have hearts that deny the truth, and they are arrogant.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the fundamental Islamic belief in the Oneness of God (tawheed). It points out that despite the clear evidence for monotheism, there are still those who reject belief in the afterlife. Their denial stems from the arrogance in their hearts, which leads them to reject the truth of God's message and prevents them from submitting to Him in humility. The verse implies that belief in the Hereafter goes hand-in-hand with accepting the Oneness of God, while arrogance is a major barrier to faith.
orig: إلهكم إله واحد فالذين لا يؤمنون بالآخرة قلوبهم منكرة وهم مستكبرون

translation: Undoubtedly, Allah knows what they conceal and what they declare. Indeed, He does not like the arrogant.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's omniscience and His dislike for those who are arrogant. Allah is fully aware of both the hidden thoughts and intentions of people, as well as their outward actions and statements. Nothing escapes His knowledge. The verse also highlights that Allah does not love those who are arrogant and consider themselves superior to others. Arrogance is a reprehensible trait that goes against the spirit of humility and submission to Allah. Muslims are encouraged to be humble, recognize their dependence on Allah, and avoid any form of self-conceit or pride. The Qur'an repeatedly condemns arrogance and warns of its consequences in this world and the hereafter.
orig: لا جرم أن الله يعلم ما يسرون وما يعلنون إنه لا يحب المستكبرين

translation: And when it is said to them, "What has your Lord sent down?" They say, "Legends of the former peoples,"
interpretation: This verse is referring to the disbelievers who, when asked about what Allah has revealed, dismiss it as nothing more than ancient fables or legends. They refuse to acknowledge the Qur'an as divine revelation, instead attributing it to mere stories of the past. This highlights their stubborn disbelief and their unwillingness to accept the truth of the message that the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) brought. They are so entrenched in their rejection of faith that they resort to making false claims about the origin and nature of the Qur'an, rather than sincerely reflecting upon its contents and the clear signs within it that point to its divine source.
orig: وإذا قيل لهم ماذا أنزل ربكم قالوا أساطير الأولين

translation: That they may bear their burdens entirely on the Day of Resurrection, and [also] some of the burdens of those whom they misguide without knowledge. Unquestionably, evil is that which they bear.
interpretation: This verse warns that those who misguide others and lead them astray from the truth will bear the full weight of their own sins on the Day of Judgment, as well as a share of the sins of those whom they misled, though the latter will not have their own burden lightened. It emphasizes the gravity and evil of spreading misguidance and corrupting others' faith, as it multiplies one's sins and accountability before God. The verse serves as a stern admonition against leading others away from the straight path and towards wrongdoing, highlighting the severe spiritual consequences in the Hereafter for such actions.
orig: ليحملوا أوزارهم كاملة يوم القيامة ومن أوزار الذين يضلونهم بغير علم ألا ساء ما يزرون

translation: Those before them had already plotted, but Allah came at their building from the foundations, so the roof fell upon them from above them, and the punishment came to them from where they did not perceive.
interpretation: This verse is a warning to those who plot against Islam and the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him). It reminds us that no matter how cleverly the enemies of Islam scheme, Allah is always aware of their plans and will ultimately thwart them. The imagery of a building's foundations being destroyed, causing the roof to collapse on the plotters, symbolizes how their own evil plans will backfire and lead to their downfall. The verse also emphasizes that the punishment for such treachery can come unexpectedly, from sources they never anticipated. It is a powerful reminder of Allah's omniscience and omnipotence, and a warning to those who seek to undermine His message and His messengers.
orig: قد مكر الذين من قبلهم فأتى الله بنيانهم من القواعد فخر عليهم السقف من فوقهم وأتاهم العذاب من حيث لا يشعرون

translation: Then on the Day of Resurrection He will disgrace them and say, "Where are My 'partners' for whose sake you used to oppose [the believers]?" Those who were given knowledge will say, "Indeed disgrace, this Day, and evil are upon the disbelievers" -
interpretation: This verse is a warning to those who associate partners with Allah and oppose His message and believers. On the Day of Judgment, Allah will humiliate the polytheists and challenge them to call upon the false gods they worshipped, exposing their powerlessness. The people of knowledge, likely referring to prophets, angels or righteous believers, will affirm that the disbelievers who rejected Allah's Oneness are deservedly disgraced and condemned on that Day for their disbelief and misdeeds. It emphasizes that worshipping anyone besides Allah leads to ultimate shame and punishment in the Hereafter.
orig: ثم يوم القيامة يخزيهم ويقول أين شركائي الذين كنتم تشاقون فيهم قال الذين أوتوا العلم إن الخزي اليوم والسوء على الكافرين

translation: Those whom the angels take in death [while] wronging themselves, [the angels] will say, "What was your condition?" They will say, "We were oppressed in the land." The angels will say, "Was not the earth of Allah spacious [enough] for you to emigrate therein?" For those, their refuge is Hell - and evil it is as a destination.
interpretation: This verse is addressing those who lived among the disbelievers and did not migrate to Muslim lands due to the oppression they faced, ultimately leading to a state of wronging themselves spiritually. When the angels take their souls at death, they will question their failure to emigrate despite the earth's vastness. These individuals will claim oppression as an excuse, but the angels will assert that they had the opportunity to leave for lands where they could practice their faith freely. As a consequence of their inaction and complacency in the face of religious persecution, their ultimate abode will be Hell - a miserable end as a direct result of their choices in life.
orig: الذين تتوفاهم الملائكة ظالمي أنفسهم فألقوا السلم ما كنا نعمل من سوء بلى إن الله عليم بما كنتم تعملون

translation: So enter the gates of Hell to abide eternally therein, and how wretched is the residence of the arrogant.
interpretation: This verse is a stern warning to those who are arrogant and reject the truth of God's message. It emphasizes that their ultimate destination will be Hell, where they will remain forever as a consequence of their arrogance and disbelief. The verse also implies that arrogance is a grave sin in the eyes of God, as it leads one to deny His signs and teachings. Moreover, it serves as a reminder to the believers to remain humble and submissive to God, as arrogance is a trait that is detested by Him and can lead to one's downfall in both this world and the Hereafter.
orig: فادخلوا أبواب جهنم خالدين فيها فلبئس مثوى المتكبرين

translation: And it will be said to those who feared Allah, "What did your Lord reveal?" They will say, "[That which is] good." For those who do good in this world is good; and the home of the Hereafter is better. And how excellent is the home of the righteous.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the reward that awaits those who are righteous and fear Allah. When they are asked about what Allah has revealed, they respond that it is all good. The verse then affirms that those who do good in this worldly life will be rewarded with goodness, while also emphasizing that the ultimate reward in the Hereafter is even better. It concludes by extoling the excellence of the eternal home that the righteous will enjoy in the Hereafter, which is far superior to anything in this temporary worldly existence. This encourages believers to prioritize the Hereafter by living righteously and fearing Allah in this life.
orig: وقيل للذين اتقوا ماذا أنزل ربكم قالوا خيرا للذين أحسنوا في هذه الدنيا حسنة ولدار الآخرة خير ولنعم دار المتقين

translation: Gardens of perpetual residence; they will enter them with rivers flowing beneath them. They will have therein whatever they wish. Thus does Allah reward the righteous.
interpretation: This verse speaks about the ultimate reward for those who are righteous and God-fearing: they will be granted entry into the eternal Gardens of Paradise. In these gardens, rivers will flow beneath them, symbolizing the abundance of blessings and the tranquility they will experience. The verse also emphasizes that in Paradise, the believers will have whatever they desire, indicating the complete satisfaction and fulfillment of their wishes. This is how Allah rewards those who lead a life of piety and righteousness, always mindful of Him and striving to follow His commands. The verse serves as a powerful motivation for believers to persist in their devotion and good deeds, knowing that an eternal life of bliss awaits them in the Hereafter.
orig: جنات عدن يدخلونها تجري من تحتها الأنهار لهم فيها ما يشاءون كذلك يجزي الله المتقين

translation: Those whom the angels take in death, [being] good and pure; [the angels] will say, "Peace be upon you. Enter Paradise for what you used to do."
interpretation: This verse speaks about the righteous believers who lived a life of goodness and purity. When the angels come to take their souls at the time of death, they will greet them with the words "Peace be upon you" as a sign of respect and honor. The angels will then give them the glad tidings of Paradise which they will enter as a reward for their good deeds and righteous life in this world. This highlights the importance of living a life of faith, goodness, and obedience to Allah in order to attain salvation and eternal bliss in the Hereafter.
orig: الذين تتوفاهم الملائكة طيبين يقولون سلام عليكم ادخلوا الجنة بما كنتم تعملون

translation: Do they await but that the angels should come to them or there comes the command of your Lord? Thus did those do before them. And Allah wronged them not, but they had been wronging themselves.
interpretation: This verse is a warning to those who reject the message of Islam and the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him). It reminds them that just like the previous nations who were destroyed for their disbelief and wrongdoing, they too will face the consequences of their actions. The coming of the angels or the command of Allah refers to the Day of Judgment when everyone will be held accountable for their deeds. The verse emphasizes that Allah does not wrong anyone, but it is the people themselves who wrong their own souls by rejecting the truth and committing sins. It is a call to introspection and repentance before it is too late.
orig: هل ينظرون إلا أن تأتيهم الملائكة أو يأتي أمر ربك كذلك فعل الذين من قبلهم وما ظلمهم الله ولكن كانوا أنفسهم يظلمون

translation: So they were struck by the evil consequences of what they did and were enveloped by what they used to ridicule.
interpretation: This verse warns that those who commit evil deeds and mock the truth will ultimately face the negative repercussions of their actions. They will be afflicted by the very things they used to scorn and dismiss. It emphasizes the universal principle of cause and effect - that one reaps what they sow. The verse also implies that divine justice will catch up with the wrongdoers, and they will not be able to escape the consequences of their misdeeds. It serves as a reminder for people to be mindful of their actions and to refrain from ridiculing or rejecting the truth, as doing so will only lead to their own detriment in the end.
orig: فأصابهم سيئات ما عملوا وحاق بهم ما كانوا به يستهزئون

translation: And those who associate others with Allah say, "If Allah had willed, we would not have worshipped anything other than Him, neither we nor our fathers, nor would we have forbidden anything through other than Him." Thus did those do before them. So is there upon the messengers except [the duty of] clear notification?
interpretation: This verse highlights the flawed logic of the polytheists who argue that their idolatry and religious prohibitions are justified because if Allah disapproved, He would have prevented them from doing so. They fail to understand that Allah has given humans free will to choose their actions, and that their ancestors followed the same misguided thinking. The verse emphasizes that the role of the prophets is to deliver the clear message of monotheism, and it is up to individuals to accept or reject that message based on their free will. Ultimately, people will be held accountable for their choices, and cannot blame Allah or the prophets for their misguidance.
orig: وقال الذين أشركوا لو شاء الله ما عبدنا من دونه من شيء نحن ولا آباؤنا ولا حرمنا من دونه من شيء كذلك فعل الذين من قبلهم فهل على الرسل إلا البلاغ المبين

translation: And We certainly sent into every nation a messenger, [saying], "Worship Allah and avoid Taghut." And among them were those whom Allah guided, and among them were those upon whom error was [deservedly] decreed. So proceed through the earth and observe how was the end of the deniers.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the universality of Allah's message throughout human history. Every nation received a prophet or messenger calling them to the worship of the One True God and to shun false objects of worship. However, the people's response differed - some were rightly guided by Allah, while others persisted in misguidance and disbelief. The verse invites one to travel and reflect on the ultimate fate of those who rejected the truth of Divine Oneness, indicating that their end was one of loss and destruction. It is a warning for people of all times to heed the call of monotheism and not follow the footsteps of those who earned Allah's punishment for their denial.
orig: ولقد بعثنا في كل أمة رسولا أن اعبدوا الله واجتنبوا الطاغوت فمنهم من هدى الله ومنهم من حقت عليه الضلالة فسيروا في الأرض فانظروا كيف كان عاقبة المكذبين

translation: If you are keen on guiding them, then indeed Allah does not guide those who are astray, and there is no helper for them.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that guidance is ultimately in the hands of Allah. Even if someone, such as the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him), is eager to guide people to the right path, it is Allah who decides whom to guide and whom to leave astray. Those whom Allah leaves astray will have no helpers or supporters, as no one can guide them against Allah's will. This highlights the importance of seeking guidance from Allah and relying on His mercy and wisdom, rather than depending solely on human efforts in guiding others.
orig: إن تحرص على هداهم فإن الله لا يهدي من يضل وما لهم من ناصرين

translation: And they swear by Allah their strongest oaths [that] Allah will not resurrect one who dies. But yes - [it is] a true promise [binding] upon Him, but most of the people do not know.
interpretation: This verse highlights the disbelief of those who deny the resurrection, swearing by Allah that He will not bring the dead back to life. However, Allah affirms that the resurrection is a true promise that He has made, emphasizing His power and ability to do so. The verse also points out the ignorance of most people who fail to recognize this truth, despite the clear evidence and promises given by Allah in the Qur'an. It serves as a reminder for believers to have faith in Allah's promise of the Day of Judgment and the resurrection, even if others around them may doubt or deny it.
orig: وأقسموا بالله جهد أيمانهم لا يبعث الله من يموت بلى وعدا عليه حقا ولكن أكثر الناس لا يعلمون

translation: That He may make clear to them [the truth of] that wherein they differ and that those who have disbelieved may know that they were liars.
interpretation: This verse indicates that one of the purposes of divine revelation is to clarify the matters in which people have disagreements, so that the truth becomes evident. It also serves as a proof against the disbelievers, exposing that they were following falsehood and lies in their beliefs and actions, contrary to the truth revealed by Allah. The Qur'an guides to the truth and resolves disputes, while making it clear that those who reject it were simply following deception.
orig: ليبين لهم الذي يختلفون فيه وليعلم الذين كفروا أنهم كانوا كاذبين

translation: Indeed, Our word to a thing when We intend it is but that We say to it, "Be," and it is.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute power and authority of Allah over His creation. When Allah wills something to happen, He merely says "Be" and it comes into existence. This demonstrates the ease with which Allah creates and the immediacy of His command. It also highlights the concept of Allah's omnipotence and His control over all things in the universe. The verse serves as a reminder to humans of their own weakness and dependence on Allah, and encourages them to submit to His will and trust in His wisdom.
orig: إنما قولنا لشيء إذا أردناه أن نقول له كن فيكون

translation: And those who emigrated for [the cause of] Allah after they had been wronged - We will surely settle them in this world in a good place; but the reward of the Hereafter is greater, if only they could know.
interpretation: This verse speaks about the rewards that await those who leave their homes and migrate for the sake of Allah, after being persecuted and oppressed. It promises them a good settlement in this worldly life, but emphasizes that the reward of the Hereafter is far greater, if they only knew. This interpretation highlights the importance of sacrificing for one's faith and the immense rewards that God has in store for those who remain steadfast in the face of hardships and persecution. It encourages believers to prioritize the eternal life over the temporary comforts of this world.
orig: والذين هاجروا في الله من بعد ما ظلموا لنبوئنهم في الدنيا حسنة ولأجر الآخرة أكبر لو كانوا يعلمون

translation: Those who are patient and upon their Lord they rely.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of patience and complete reliance on Allah in the face of adversity. It suggests that true believers are those who remain steadfast and unwavering in their faith, even during difficult times, and who put their trust in Allah's plan and wisdom. They understand that Allah is the ultimate source of strength and support, and that by relying on Him, they will be able to overcome any obstacle or hardship. This verse encourages Muslims to cultivate the virtues of patience and trust in Allah, as these are essential qualities for spiritual growth and success in both this life and the hereafter.
orig: الذين صبروا وعلى ربهم يتوكلون

translation: And We sent not before you, [O Muhammad], except men to whom We revealed [the message], so ask the people of the message if you do not know.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that all the prophets and messengers sent by Allah before Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) were human beings, not angels or any other creatures. They received divine revelation from Allah to guide their people. If one is unsure or lacks knowledge about the history of previous prophets or the message they brought, Allah instructs them to ask those who possess knowledge, particularly the People of the Book (Jews and Christians) who had received earlier scriptures. This highlights the importance of seeking knowledge from reliable sources and acknowledging the continuity of Allah's message throughout human history.
orig: وما أرسلنا من قبلك إلا رجالا نوحي إليهم فاسألوا أهل الذكر إن كنتم لا تعلمون

translation: With clear proofs and written ordinances. And We have revealed to you the message that you may make clear to the people what was sent down to them and that they might give thought.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the role of Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) as a messenger who received divine revelation in order to clarify the message to humanity. The Qur'an was revealed with clear evidence and written ordinances to guide people towards the truth. The Prophet's duty was to convey and explain the revelation so that people could understand its meaning, reflect upon its wisdom, and apply its teachings in their lives. This verse highlights the importance of contemplation and intellectual engagement with the Qur'an, encouraging people to ponder over its verses and derive lessons that can benefit them in this world and the hereafter.
orig: بالبينات والزبر وأنزلنا إليك الذكر لتبين للناس ما نزل إليهم ولعلهم يتفكرون

translation: Then, do those who have planned evil deeds feel secure that Allah will not cause the earth to swallow them or that the punishment will not come upon them from where they do not perceive?
interpretation: This verse is a warning to those who plot evil and engage in wicked schemes. It reminds them that they are not beyond the reach of Allah's punishment, which can come upon them suddenly and unexpectedly, either by the earth swallowing them up or through other means they cannot foresee. The verse implies that no one should feel secure in their evil plans, as Allah's retribution can strike at any moment, catching the evildoers off guard. It serves as a powerful reminder of Allah's omnipotence and the ultimate futility of trying to oppose His will or evade His justice.
orig: أفأمن الذين مكروا السيئات أن يخسف الله بهم الأرض أو يأتيهم العذاب من حيث لا يشعرون

translation: Or that He may seize them in the midst of their going to and fro (in their livelihood), so that there be no escape for them (from Allah's punishment)?
interpretation: This verse warns that Allah has the power to seize the disbelievers during their daily activities and business, leaving them no escape from His punishment. It emphasizes that no matter how occupied or distracted they may be in worldly pursuits, they cannot evade Allah's grasp or outrun His decree. This serves as a reminder of Allah's omnipotence and a warning for people to be mindful of their actions, knowing that they can be held accountable at any moment.
orig: أو يأخذهم في تقلبهم فما هم بمعجزين

translation: Or that He may seize them with gradual wasting? But indeed, your Lord is Kind and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse highlights the mercy and kindness of Allah towards His creation, even when they deserve punishment. Allah may seize the wrongdoers gradually, giving them time to repent and turn back to Him. This shows that Allah's door of forgiveness is always open, and He is ever ready to accept the repentance of His servants. The verse also serves as a reminder that no matter how much we sin, we should never lose hope in Allah's mercy and forgiveness. It encourages us to constantly seek His forgiveness and strive to improve ourselves, knowing that He is "Ra'oof" (Kind) and "Raheem" (Merciful).
orig: أو يأخذهم على تخوف فإن ربكم لرءوف رحيم

translation: Have they not considered what things Allah has created? Their shadows incline to the right and to the left, prostrating to Allah, while they are humble.
interpretation: This verse is a reminder for people to reflect upon the natural world around them and recognize the signs of Allah's power and creation. The shadows of all things, whether living or inanimate, are constantly shifting from right to left as the sun moves across the sky. This is a metaphor for how all of creation submits to Allah's will, prostrating before Him in humility and obedience. It encourages humans to also humble themselves before their Creator and acknowledge His supremacy over all things. By observing the natural world, one can find evidence of Allah's existence and wisdom, which should inspire faith and submission to His will.
orig: أولم يروا إلى ما خلق الله من شيء يتفيأ ظلاله عن اليمين والشمائل سجدا لله وهم داخرون

translation: And to Allah prostrates whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth of creatures, and the angels [as well], and they are not arrogant.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the complete submission and obedience of all creation to Allah, the Almighty. It highlights that every living being in the heavens and on earth, including animals and angels, prostrates to Allah in humility and worship. The angels, despite their high status, do not display any arrogance or pride; instead, they humble themselves before their Lord. This verse serves as a reminder for humans to follow suit and submit to Allah with sincerity and humility, recognizing His supreme authority and power over all creation.
orig: ولله يسجد ما في السماوات وما في الأرض من دابة والملائكة وهم لا يستكبرون

translation: They fear their Lord above them, and they do what they are commanded.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of having a strong sense of taqwa, or consciousness and fear of Allah. Those who truly believe in Allah and the Day of Judgment are always mindful that He is watching over them, and this awareness motivates them to obey His commands and refrain from what He has prohibited. They submit themselves completely to the will of Allah, knowing that He is above them in power and authority. The verse also highlights the significance of obedience in Islam. True believers not only have faith in their hearts but also demonstrate it through their actions, following Allah's orders without hesitation or reservation.
orig: يخافون ربهم من فوقهم ويفعلون ما يؤمرون

translation: And Allah has said, "Do not take for yourselves two deities. He is but one God, so fear only Me."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the fundamental concept of monotheism in Islam. It clearly states that there is only one true God, Allah, and that worshipping any other deity alongside Him is strictly forbidden. The verse also highlights the importance of having a deep reverence and fear of Allah, as He is the only one worthy of worship and submission. It serves as a reminder for believers to direct all their devotion and obedience solely towards Allah and to avoid associating partners with Him in any form of worship or belief.
orig: وقال الله لا تتخذوا إلهين اثنين إنما هو إله واحد فإياي فارهبون

translation: And to Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and the earth, and to Him is [due] worship constantly. Then is it other than Allah that you fear?
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute sovereignty and ownership of Allah over all that exists in the heavens and the earth. It also highlights the obligation of mankind to worship Him alone, as He is the only One deserving of worship. The rhetorical question at the end of the verse serves as a reminder and admonishment to those who fear anything or anyone other than Allah, implying that such fear is misplaced and irrational, as Allah is the Supreme Being who controls all aspects of existence.
orig: وله ما في السماوات والأرض وله الدين واصبا أفغير الله تتقون

translation: And whatever of blessings and good things you have, it is from Allah. Then, when harm touches you, unto Him you cry aloud for help.
interpretation: This verse reminds us that all the blessings and favors we enjoy in life come from Allah alone. It is a call to acknowledge and appreciate the countless bounties bestowed upon us by our Creator. However, the verse also points out the tendency of human beings to turn to Allah only when faced with difficulties and hardships. It highlights the inconsistency in human behavior, where people often forget to thank and remember Allah during times of ease and prosperity, but immediately cry out to Him for help when touched by adversity. This verse encourages us to maintain a constant connection with Allah, expressing gratitude in good times and seeking His aid in times of distress, with the understanding that He is the ultimate source of all blessings and the only One who can alleviate our sufferings.
orig: وما بكم من نعمة فمن الله ثم إذا مسكم الضر فإليه تجأرون

translation: Then when He removes the affliction from you, behold, a group among you associates partners with their Lord.
interpretation: This verse highlights the fickle nature of some people's faith. When they are in distress, they turn to Allah for help, but as soon as the affliction is removed, they revert to their old ways of associating partners with Allah. It shows their lack of gratitude and the weakness of their belief, as they fail to recognize that it is Allah alone who has the power to alleviate their suffering. The verse serves as a reminder to remain steadfast in faith and to attribute all blessings and relief from hardships to Allah alone, without associating any partners with Him.
orig: ثم إذا كشف الضر عنكم إذا فريق منكم بربهم يشركون

translation: So that they will deny what We have granted them. Then enjoy yourselves, for you are going to know.
interpretation: This verse is a warning to those who reject God's blessings and favors upon them. It suggests that those who deny God's gifts and indulge in worldly pleasures will soon come to realize the consequences of their actions. The phrase "for you are going to know" implies that they will face the reality of their choices in the afterlife, where they will be held accountable for their deeds. It serves as a reminder that the temporary enjoyment of this world should not distract one from the ultimate purpose of life, which is to worship God and follow His guidance.
orig: ليكفروا بما آتيناهم فتمتعوا فسوف تعلمون

translation: And they assign to what they do not know a portion of that which We have provided them. By Allah, you will surely be questioned about what you used to invent.
interpretation: This verse is a strong condemnation of those who attribute a share of what Allah has provided them to false deities or idols that they have no knowledge of. It emphasizes that Allah alone is the provider and that assigning any portion of His provisions to others is a form of fabrication and falsehood. The verse also serves as a warning that people will be held accountable on the Day of Judgment for these false attributions and inventions they used to make in this world, associating partners with Allah without any basis in truth or knowledge.
orig: ويجعلون لما لا يعلمون نصيبا مما رزقناهم تالله لتسألن عما كنتم تفترون

translation: And they attribute daughters to Allah, glory be to Him, while they have what they desire!
interpretation: This verse criticizes the pre-Islamic Arab practice of attributing daughters to Allah while they themselves desired sons. It highlights the contradiction and injustice in their thinking, as they ascribed to Allah what they considered inferior (daughters) while keeping what they preferred (sons) for themselves. The verse emphasizes that Allah is far above such false attributions and that both sons and daughters are created by Him according to His wisdom and plan. It also implies that one should be content with whatever child Allah grants them, without showing preference or discrimination based on gender.
orig: ويجعلون لله البنات سبحانه ولهم ما يشتهون

translation: And when one of them is informed of [the birth of] a female, his face becomes dark, and he suppresses grief.
interpretation: This verse highlights the negative attitude some people had towards the birth of a daughter in pre-Islamic Arabia. The verse describes the reaction of a man who has just been told that his wife has given birth to a girl. His face darkens with disappointment and he is filled with sorrow, which he tries to hide. This reaction reflects the low status of women in that society and the preference for male children. The Qur'an condemns this attitude and emphasizes the equal worth of both genders in the sight of Allah.
orig: وإذا بشر أحدهم بالأنثى ظل وجهه مسودا وهو كظيم

translation: He hides himself from the people because of the ill of which he has been informed. Should he keep it in humiliation or bury it in the ground? Unquestionably, evil is what they decide.
interpretation: This verse is referring to the pre-Islamic practice of burying infant daughters alive out of shame or fear of poverty. The father, upon hearing the news of a daughter's birth, would hide from people out of embarrassment and decide whether to keep the baby girl in humiliation or bury her in the ground. The Qur'an strongly condemns this evil practice and the mindset behind it, emphasizing that the decision to kill innocent children is truly abhorrent and morally reprehensible in the sight of God.
orig: يتوارى من القوم من سوء ما بشر به أيمسكه على هون أم يدسه في التراب ألا ساء ما يحكمون

translation: For those who do not believe in the Hereafter is the description of evil; and for Allah is the highest attribute. And He is the Exalted in Might, the Wise.
interpretation: This verse highlights the contrast between the disbelievers and Allah. Those who reject faith in the afterlife are associated with evil and negative qualities. On the other hand, Allah possesses the most sublime attributes, emphasizing His superiority, might, and wisdom. The interpretation suggests that while the disbelievers are mired in evil and base characteristics, Allah represents the epitome of goodness, power, and wisdom. It serves as a reminder for believers to strive towards emulating the divine attributes rather than falling into the ways of the disbelievers.
orig: للذين لا يؤمنون بالآخرة مثل السوء ولله المثل الأعلى وهو العزيز الحكيم

translation: And if Allah were to impose blame on the people for their wrongdoing, He would not have left upon the earth any creature, but He defers them for a specified term. And when their term has come, they will not remain behind an hour, nor will they precede [it].
interpretation: This verse highlights Allah's mercy and forbearance towards His creation. Despite the wrongdoings and sins committed by people, Allah does not immediately punish them. Instead, He gives them respite until a predetermined time, allowing them the opportunity to repent and mend their ways. The verse also emphasizes the inevitability of death and the Day of Judgment. When the appointed time arrives, no one can delay it or advance it even by a single hour.
