This serves as a reminder for people to be mindful of their actions and to make the most of the time they have been granted in this world, for they will ultimately be held accountable for their deeds.
orig: ولو يؤاخذ الله الناس بظلمهم ما ترك عليها من دابة ولكن يؤخرهم إلى أجل مسمى فإذا جاء أجلهم لا يستأخرون ساعة ولا يستقدمون

translation: And they assign to Allah what they dislike, and their tongues assert the lie that they will have the best [from Him]. Assuredly, they will have the Fire, and they will be [therein] neglected.
interpretation: This verse is criticizing the hypocrisy and false beliefs of the polytheists. They attribute to Allah qualities and offspring that they themselves would dislike, such as daughters, while claiming that they will have the best outcome in the Hereafter. However, Allah emphatically refutes this notion, affirming that their destination is undoubtedly the Fire, where they will be abandoned and forgotten as a consequence of their disbelief and lies against Allah. This highlights the severity of attributing false characteristics to Allah and the ultimate fate of those who engage in such practices.
orig: ويجعلون لله ما يكرهون وتصف ألسنتهم الكذب أن لهم الحسنى لا جرم أن لهم النار وأنهم مفرطون

translation: By Allah, We have surely sent [messengers] to nations before you, but Satan made their deeds attractive to them. So he is their ally today, and they will have a painful punishment.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the role of Satan in leading people astray by making their evil deeds appear attractive to them. It serves as a warning that those who follow Satan's path will face severe consequences in the form of a painful punishment in the Hereafter. The verse also highlights the importance of seeking guidance from Allah and His messengers to avoid falling into Satan's traps and to stay on the righteous path. It reminds believers to be vigilant against the deceptions of Satan and to constantly seek Allah's protection and guidance.
orig: تالله لقد أرسلنا إلى أمم من قبلك فزين لهم الشيطان أعمالهم فهو وليهم اليوم ولهم عذاب أليم

translation: And We have not revealed to you the Book, [O Muhammad], except for you to make clear to them that wherein they have differed and as guidance and mercy for a people who believe.
interpretation: The purpose of revealing the Qur'an to Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) is to clarify the matters in which people have differed, such as the nature of God, the purpose of life, and the path to salvation. The Qur'an serves as a guide and a mercy for those who sincerely believe in its message and strive to follow its teachings. It is a source of guidance that leads believers to the straight path and helps them navigate through the challenges and uncertainties of life. The Qur'an is also a mercy from God, as it provides comfort, hope, and spiritual nourishment for those who seek His guidance and forgiveness.
orig: وما أنزلنا عليك الكتاب إلا لتبين لهم الذي اختلفوا فيه وهدى ورحمة لقوم يؤمنون

translation: And Allah has sent down rain from the sky and given life thereby to the earth after its lifelessness. Indeed in that is a sign for a people who listen.
interpretation: This verse highlights the power and mercy of Allah in reviving the dead earth by sending down rain from the sky. It serves as a reminder for those who are willing to listen and reflect upon the signs of Allah's existence and His ability to resurrect life after death. The revival of the earth after its lifelessness is a metaphor for the resurrection of the dead on the Day of Judgment, emphasizing that Allah has the power to bring back life to those who have died. This verse encourages believers to pay attention to the signs around them and to contemplate on the wonders of Allah's creation, strengthening their faith and belief in the Hereafter.
orig: والله أنزل من السماء ماء فأحيا به الأرض بعد موتها إن في ذلك لآية لقوم يسمعون

translation: And indeed, for you in grazing livestock is a lesson. We give you drink from what is in their bellies - between excretion and blood - pure milk, palatable to drinkers.
interpretation: This verse points to the miraculous nature of milk production in livestock. From what the animals consume, which includes their waste matter, Allah causes their bodies to produce pure, wholesome milk that is palatable and beneficial for human consumption. This is a sign of Allah's creative power, wisdom and mercy, that He has made such a process to provide sustenance for mankind. It is one of the many natural phenomena that should prompt humans to reflect on Allah's favors upon them and be grateful for His provisions.
orig: وإن لكم في الأنعام لعبرة نسقيكم مما في بطونه من بين فرث ودم لبنا خالصا سائغا للشاربين

translation: And from the fruits of the palm trees and grapevines you take intoxicant and good provision. Indeed in that is a sign for a people who reason.
interpretation: This verse highlights that God has provided us with the bounties of dates and grapes, from which we can derive both intoxicating substances as well as wholesome, lawful provisions. The ability to make this distinction and to benefit from God's gifts in a good way is a sign of intelligence and reason that God has bestowed upon humans. It reminds us to use our intellect to choose the path of righteousness, avoiding what is harmful and prohibited while enjoying the lawful blessings that God has created for our benefit.
orig: ومن ثمرات النخيل والأعناب تتخذون منه سكرا ورزقا حسنا إن في ذلك لآية لقوم يعقلون

translation: And your Lord inspired to the bee, "Take for yourself among the mountains, houses, and among the trees and [in] that which they construct.
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine guidance and wisdom bestowed upon the bees by Allah. It shows how Allah has inspired them with the instinct to build their hives in the mountains, trees, and man-made structures. This points to the intricate balance and harmony in nature, where even small creatures like bees have a significant role to play in the ecosystem. The verse also implies that humans can learn from the bees' diligence, organization, and the way they utilize natural resources for their survival and benefit.
orig: وأوحى ربك إلى النحل أن اتخذي من الجبال بيوتا ومن الشجر ومما يعرشون

translation: Then eat from all the fruits and follow the ways of your Lord laid down [for you]. There emerges from their bellies a drink, varying in colors, in which there is healing for people. Indeed in that is a sign for a people who give thought.
interpretation: This verse is a reminder of the incredible bounty and wisdom of Allah in His creation. The bees are inspired by Allah to seek out a variety of flowers and fruits, and from this produce honey in different hues, each with its own unique medicinal properties that bring healing to mankind. This intricate process points to the existence of a higher power and encourages reflection and contemplation on the signs of Allah and the perfection of His creation. It is a call to ponder deeply on the blessings we have been granted and to be grateful for them.
orig: ثم كلي من كل الثمرات فاسلكي سبل ربك ذللا يخرج من بطونها شراب مختلف ألوانه فيه شفاء للناس إن في ذلك لآية لقوم يتفكرون

translation: And Allah created you; then He will take you in death. And among you is he who is reversed to the most decrepit [old] age so that he will not know, after [having had] knowledge, a thing. Indeed, Allah is Knowing and Competent.
interpretation: This verse reminds us of the power and knowledge of Allah. He is the One who created us and will eventually take our lives. Some people may live to old age and experience a decline in their mental faculties, forgetting the knowledge they once possessed. This highlights the temporary nature of worldly knowledge and abilities, which can deteriorate with time. However, Allah's knowledge is perfect and eternal. He is fully aware of all things and has the power to control life and death. This verse encourages humility and recognition of our limitations, while emphasizing the greatness and wisdom of Allah.
orig: والله خلقكم ثم يتوفاكم ومنكم من يرد إلى أرذل العمر لكي لا يعلم بعد علم شيئا إن الله عليم قدير

translation: And Allah has favored some of you over others in provision. But those who were favored would not hand over their provision to those whom their right hands possess so they would be equal to them therein. Then is it the favor of Allah they reject?
interpretation: This verse highlights the fact that God has granted some people more sustenance and provisions than others, yet those who have been favored do not share their wealth with those under their care or responsibility, such as servants or slaves, to the extent of making them equal. The rhetorical question at the end implies that despite this disparity, people still deny and reject the favors and blessings that God has bestowed upon them, rather than being grateful and sharing with others.
orig: والله فضل بعضكم على بعض في الرزق فما الذين فضلوا برادي رزقهم على ما ملكت أيمانهم فهم فيه سواء أفبنعمة الله يجحدون

translation: And Allah has made for you from yourselves mates and has made for you from your mates sons and grandchildren and has provided for you from the good things. Then in falsehood do they believe and in the favor of Allah they disbelieve?
interpretation: This verse highlights the blessings that Allah has bestowed upon humanity. It emphasizes that Allah has created spouses for us from our own kind, allowing us to find comfort, love, and companionship in our partners. Moreover, through these unions, Allah grants us the gift of children and grandchildren, which bring joy and purpose to our lives. Additionally, Allah provides us with sustenance and the good things in life. Despite these evident blessings, the verse questions how some people can still believe in falsehood and deny the favors of Allah. It suggests that to disbelieve in Allah's blessings is a form of ingratitude and a failure to recognize the true source of all that is good in our lives.
orig: والله جعل لكم من أنفسكم أزواجا وجعل لكم من أزواجكم بنين وحفدة ورزقكم من الطيبات أفبالباطل يؤمنون وبنعمت الله هم يكفرون

translation: And they worship besides Allah that which does not possess for them [the power of] provision from the heavens and the earth at all, and [in fact], they are unable.
interpretation: This verse criticizes the foolishness and futility of worshipping false deities besides Allah. These false objects of worship have no power to provide any sustenance or benefit, neither from the heavens nor the earth. They are completely powerless and incapable, unable to help their worshippers in any way. Worshipping such powerless entities is irrational and misguided, when only Allah has the power to provide and assist His creation. The verse emphasizes that all provision and power belongs to Allah alone, so He should be the only One worshipped.
orig: ويعبدون من دون الله ما لا يملك لهم رزقا من السماوات والأرض شيئا ولا يستطيعون

translation: So do not assert similarities to Allah. Indeed, Allah knows and you do not know.
interpretation: This verse is a clear warning against making comparisons or asserting similarities between Allah and His creation. It emphasizes the fundamental Islamic belief in the absolute uniqueness and transcendence of Allah. Human beings, with their limited knowledge and understanding, cannot comprehend the true nature of Allah. Therefore, they should refrain from making any analogies or comparisons that might lead to anthropomorphizing Allah or reducing Him to the level of His creation. The verse reminds us that Allah alone possesses perfect and infinite knowledge, while human knowledge is limited and imperfect. It is an admonition to submit to Allah's wisdom and to avoid speculation or assumptions about His divine attributes based on our own limited understanding.
orig: فلا تضربوا لله الأمثال إن الله يعلم وأنتم لا تعلمون

translation: Allah sets forth the Parable (of two men: one) a slave under the dominion of another; He has no power of any sort; and (the other) a man on whom We have bestowed goodly favours from Ourselves, and he spends thereof (freely), privately and publicly: are the two equal? (By no means;) praise be to Allah. But most of them understand not.
interpretation: This verse highlights the vast difference between those who are enslaved by their desires and have no control over their actions, and those who have been blessed with God's guidance and are able to spend their wealth in His cause, both privately and publicly. It emphasizes that these two types of people are not equal in the sight of Allah, and that true praise and gratitude belong to Him alone. However, most people fail to recognize this truth and do not understand the significance of being guided by Allah and using His blessings in a righteous manner.
orig: ضرب الله مثلا عبدا مملوكا لا يقدر على شيء ومن رزقناه منا رزقا حسنا فهو ينفق منه سرا وجهرا هل يستوون الحمد لله بل أكثرهم لا يعلمون

translation: And Allah presents an example of two men, one of them dumb and unable to do a thing, and he is a burden to his master; wherever he directs him, he brings no good. Is he equal to him who commands justice, and is on a straight path?
interpretation: This verse highlights the contrast between two types of people: one who is incapable of doing anything good and is a burden to others, and another who actively promotes justice and follows the right path. The former, represented by the "dumb" man, lacks the ability to benefit himself or others, while the latter, who "commands justice," is on the straight path and brings goodness to society. The rhetorical question at the end emphasizes that these two individuals are not equal in the sight of Allah, as the one who upholds justice and follows the right path is far superior. This parable encourages believers to strive for righteousness and to be active in promoting good, rather than being passive or burdensome to others.
orig: وضرب الله مثلا رجلين أحدهما أبكم لا يقدر على شيء وهو كل على مولاه أينما يوجهه لا يأت بخير هل يستوي هو ومن يأمر بالعدل وهو على صراط مستقيم

translation: And to Allah belongs the unseen [aspects] of the heavens and the earth. And the command of the Hour is not but as a glance of the eye or even nearer. Indeed, Allah is over all things competent.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the omnipotence and omniscience of Allah. It reminds us that the knowledge of the unseen, including the timing of the Day of Judgment (the Hour), belongs exclusively to Allah. The verse also highlights the swiftness with which the Hour will arrive, comparing it to the blink of an eye or even faster. This serves as a reminder for humans to be always prepared for the Day of Judgment, as it can come at any moment without warning. The verse concludes by reaffirming Allah's power and control over all things, emphasizing that He is capable of bringing about the Hour and everything else in existence.
orig: ولله غيب السماوات والأرض وما أمر الساعة إلا كلمح البصر أو هو أقرب إن الله على كل شيء قدير

translation: And Allah has extracted you from the wombs of your mothers not knowing a thing, and He made for you hearing and vision and intellect that perhaps you would be grateful.
interpretation: This verse highlights the miraculous nature of human birth and development, reminding us that we come into this world as helpless infants, knowing nothing. It is through Allah's grace and mercy that He has bestowed upon us the faculties of hearing, sight, and understanding, which enable us to learn, grow, and navigate the world around us. The verse encourages us to be grateful for these precious gifts and to use them in a manner that pleases Allah, recognizing that our abilities are not of our own making but are blessings from our Creator. It also implies that we should continually strive to increase our knowledge and understanding, using the faculties Allah has given us to seek truth and wisdom throughout our lives.
orig: والله أخرجكم من بطون أمهاتكم لا تعلمون شيئا وجعل لكم السمع والأبصار والأفئدة لعلكم تشكرون

translation: Do they not see the birds controlled in the atmosphere of the sky? None holds them up except Allah. Indeed in that are signs for a people who believe.
interpretation: This verse draws our attention to the marvels of Allah's creation, specifically the birds that fly effortlessly in the sky. It reminds us that it is only by Allah's power and will that these creatures are able to soar and remain aloft. The flight of birds is presented as a sign of Allah's existence, omnipotence, and supreme control over the universe. It is an invitation for people to reflect upon this phenomenon and strengthen their faith in the One who created and sustains all living beings. The verse emphasizes that such wonders are apparent to those who sincerely believe and are willing to contemplate the signs of their Lord in the world around them.
orig: ألم يروا إلى الطير مسخرات في جو السماء ما يمسكهن إلا الله إن في ذلك لآيات لقوم يؤمنون

translation: And Allah has made for you from your homes a place of rest and made for you from the hides of the animals tents which you find light on your day of travel and your day of encampment; and from their wool, fur and hair is furnishing and enjoyment for a time.
interpretation: This verse highlights the blessings and provisions that Allah has bestowed upon humanity. It emphasizes that Allah has not only provided us with permanent homes for shelter and rest, but also with temporary dwellings in the form of tents made from animal hides, which are easy to transport and set up during our journeys and encampments. Furthermore, Allah has granted us the benefits of using the wool, fur, and hair of these animals for furnishing our homes and deriving enjoyment from them for a period of time. This interpretation underscores the idea that Allah's bounties are all-encompassing, catering to both our permanent and temporary needs, and that we should be grateful for the various ways in which He has facilitated our lives on earth.
orig: والله جعل لكم من بيوتكم سكنا وجعل لكم من جلود الأنعام بيوتا تستخفونها يوم ظعنكم ويوم إقامتكم ومن أصوافها وأوبارها وأشعارها أثاثا ومتاعا إلى حين

translation: And Allah has made for you, from that which He has created, shadows and has made for you from the mountains, shelters and has made for you garments which protect you from the heat and garments which protect you from your [enemy in] battle. Thus does He complete His favor upon you that you might submit [to Him].
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's benevolence and care for His creation. It highlights how Allah has provided various means of protection and comfort for humans, such as shade from the sun, shelter in the mountains, and clothing to shield against heat and during battle. These provisions are a testament to Allah's favor upon humanity, encouraging them to submit to His will and be grateful for His blessings. The verse also implies that recognizing and appreciating these divine gifts should lead one to surrender to Allah and follow His guidance.
orig: والله جعل لكم مما خلق ظلالا وجعل لكم من الجبال أكنانا وجعل لكم سرابيل تقيكم الحر وسرابيل تقيكم بأسكم كذلك يتم نعمته عليكم لعلكم تسلمون

translation: But if they turn away, [O Muhammad] - then only upon you is [responsibility for] clear notification.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the role of Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) as a messenger whose duty is to convey the message of Islam clearly to the people. If they choose to reject the message after it has been clearly conveyed to them, then the Prophet is not responsible for their choice or actions. His responsibility is only to deliver the message in a clear manner, and the rest is up to the individuals to accept or reject it based on their own free will. This highlights the concept of individual responsibility in Islam, where each person is accountable for their own decisions and actions.
orig: فإن تولوا فإنما عليك البلاغ المبين

translation: They recognize the favor of Allah; then they deny it. And most of them are disbelievers.
interpretation: This verse highlights the ingratitude and disbelief of those who, despite recognizing the blessings and favors bestowed upon them by Allah, choose to deny and reject His grace. It suggests that many people are aware of the divine blessings in their lives, such as health, sustenance, and various abilities, yet they fail to acknowledge and appreciate these gifts. Instead, they attribute their blessings to other factors or take them for granted, thus displaying ingratitude and disbelief in Allah's benevolence. The verse emphasizes that a majority of people fall into this category of disbelievers, indicating the prevalence of ingratitude and lack of faith among humankind.
orig: يعرفون نعمت الله ثم ينكرونها وأكثرهم الكافرون

translation: And [warn of] the Day when We will resurrect among every nation a witness [i.e., their prophet]. Then it will not be permitted to the disbelievers [to apologize or make excuses], nor will they be asked to appease [Allah].
interpretation: This verse speaks about the Day of Judgment, when Allah will raise a witness from every nation to testify against their own people. The witness will be the prophet or messenger that Allah sent to guide them during their worldly life. On that day, the disbelievers who rejected the message and the warnings of their prophets will not be allowed to make excuses or seek forgiveness. They will not be given a chance to appease Allah or make amends for their sins and disbelief. This highlights the severity and finality of the judgment, emphasizing the importance of believing in Allah's message and following the guidance of His prophets during one's lifetime, as there will be no opportunity for redemption on the Day of Judgment for those who disbelieved.
orig: ويوم نبعث من كل أمة شهيدا ثم لا يؤذن للذين كفروا ولا هم يستعتبون

translation: And when those who did wrong see the punishment, it will not be lightened for them, nor will they be reprieved.
interpretation: This verse warns that on the Day of Judgment, when the wrongdoers and sinners face the consequences of their actions, there will be no relief or respite from the punishment decreed by Allah. They will have to endure the full weight of the penalty for their misdeeds, with no possibility of it being reduced or postponed. It emphasizes the severity and inevitability of divine justice, and serves as a reminder for people to be mindful of their actions in this world, as they will be held accountable in the Hereafter where no intercession or second chances will be granted to the evildoers.
orig: وإذا رأى الذين ظلموا العذاب فلا يخفف عنهم ولا هم ينظرون

translation: And when those who associated others with Allah see their 'partners' they will say, "Our Lord, these are our partners whom we used to invoke besides You." But they will throw at them the statement, "Indeed, you are liars!"
interpretation: This verse is referring to the Day of Judgment when the polytheists will face the reality of their false beliefs. They will see that the idols or beings they used to worship besides Allah are of no help to them. In a desperate attempt to shift blame, they will point to these false gods and claim that they misled them. However, these very 'partners' will refute their claim and declare that the polytheists are liars. This highlights the futility of worshipping anyone or anything besides Allah, and that ultimately, each soul is responsible for its own faith and actions. It also emphasizes Allah's Oneness and the severity of the sin of shirk (associating partners with Allah).
orig: وإذا رأى الذين أشركوا شركاءهم قالوا ربنا هؤلاء شركاؤنا الذين كنا ندعو من دونك فألقوا إليهم القول إنكم لكاذبون

translation: And they will offer submission to Allah on that Day, and lost from them is what they used to invent.
interpretation: This verse refers to the Day of Judgment when all people will submit completely to Allah, realizing the truth of His message and the falsehood of their previous beliefs. The false gods and idols that they used to worship and invoke besides Allah will be of no avail to them. They will recognize that the fabrications and lies they attributed to Allah were baseless and misguided. On that day, they will have no choice but to surrender to Allah's judgment and authority, facing the consequences of their actions and beliefs in this worldly life.
orig: وألقوا إلى الله يومئذ السلم وضل عنهم ما كانوا يفترون

translation: Those who disbelieved and averted [others] from the way of Allah - We will increase them in punishment over [their] punishment for what corruption they were causing.
interpretation: This verse warns that those who reject faith in Allah and actively hinder others from following His path will face severe consequences in the Hereafter. Their punishment will be multiplied beyond the normal retribution for their own disbelief, because they also engaged in spreading corruption and leading others astray. It emphasizes the gravity of not only disbelieving oneself, but also working to prevent others from embracing the truth of Islam. Such people will bear the burden of their own misguidance along with the sins of those they misled, resulting in an intensified punishment for their destructive actions in this world.
orig: الذين كفروا وصدوا عن سبيل الله زدناهم عذابا فوق العذاب بما كانوا يفسدون

translation: And [mention] the Day when We will resurrect among every nation a witness over them from themselves. And We will bring you, [O Muhammad], as a witness over your nation. And We have sent down to you the Book as clarification for all things and as guidance and mercy and good tidings for the Muslims.
interpretation: This verse highlights the role of prophets as witnesses over their nations on the Day of Judgment. Each prophet will testify regarding their respective nations and their response to the divine message. Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) will serve as a witness over his nation. The Qur'an, which was revealed to him, serves as a comprehensive source of guidance, clarifying all matters pertaining to faith, worship, and way of life. It is a means of attaining God's mercy and a bearer of glad tidings for those who submit to God's will and follow the teachings of Islam.
orig: ويوم نبعث في كل أمة شهيدا عليهم من أنفسهم وجئنا بك شهيدا على هؤلاء ونزلنا عليك الكتاب تبيانا لكل شيء وهدى ورحمة وبشرى للمسلمين

translation: Indeed, Allah orders justice and good conduct and giving to relatives and forbids immorality and bad conduct and oppression. He admonishes you that perhaps you will be reminded.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of upholding justice, engaging in virtuous deeds, and showing kindness to one's relatives. It serves as a reminder that Allah commands us to abstain from all forms of indecency, wickedness, and transgression. The mention of Allah's admonishment at the end of the verse indicates that by reflecting upon these injunctions, we may be more mindful of our actions and strive to align ourselves with the divine guidance. Ultimately, this verse encapsulates the core ethical principles that should govern our behavior and interactions with others, both in our personal lives and within society at large.
orig: إن الله يأمر بالعدل والإحسان وإيتاء ذي القربى وينهى عن الفحشاء والمنكر والبغي يعظكم لعلكم تذكرون

translation: And fulfill the covenant of Allah when you have taken it, [O believers], and do not break oaths after their confirmation while you have made Allah, over you, a witness. Indeed, Allah knows what you do.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of keeping promises and fulfilling covenants, especially those made in the name of Allah. It reminds believers that Allah is a witness to their oaths and agreements, and that He is aware of all their actions. The verse warns against breaking promises after confirming them, as it is a grave sin and a violation of trust. It encourages Muslims to be true to their word and to maintain the highest standards of integrity and honesty in their dealings with others, as this is pleasing to Allah and a sign of true faith.
orig: وأوفوا بعهد الله إذا عاهدتم ولا تنقضوا الأيمان بعد توكيدها وقد جعلتم الله عليكم كفيلا إن الله يعلم ما تفعلون

translation: And do not be like she who untwisted her spun thread after it was strong [by] taking your oaths as [means of] deceit between you because one community is more plentiful [in number or wealth] than another community. Allah only tries you thereby. And He will surely make clear to you on the Day of Resurrection that over which you used to differ.
interpretation: This verse cautions against breaking promises and treaties, comparing it to a woman who painstakingly spins thread and then untwists it, rendering her effort futile. It admonishes against using oaths as a means of deception for worldly gain or due to feelings of superiority over others. Allah reminds that He tests people through such situations and that the ultimate consequences of one's choices and disputes will be made clear on the Day of Judgment. The verse emphasizes the importance of honoring commitments, maintaining integrity, and recognizing that all communities are equal before Allah, regardless of their power or prosperity.
orig: ولا تكونوا كالتي نقضت غزلها من بعد قوة أنكاثا تتخذون أيمانكم دخلا بينكم أن تكون أمة هي أربى من أمة إنما يبلوكم الله به وليبينن لكم يوم القيامة ما كنتم فيه تختلفون

translation: And if Allah had willed, He could have made you [of] one religion, but He lets go astray whom He wills and guides whom He wills. And you will surely be questioned about what you used to do.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the concept of free will and individual responsibility in Islam. Allah, in His infinite wisdom, has given humans the freedom to choose their own path, whether it leads to guidance or misguidance. He could have easily created all of humanity to follow a single religion, but instead, He has allowed diversity in belief and practice. However, this freedom of choice comes with the responsibility of facing the consequences of one's actions. On the Day of Judgment, every individual will be questioned about their deeds and the choices they made in their worldly life. This verse serves as a reminder for Muslims to be mindful of their actions and to strive to follow the path of righteousness, as they will be held accountable for their decisions in the Hereafter.
orig: ولو شاء الله لجعلكم أمة واحدة ولكن يضل من يشاء ويهدي من يشاء ولتسألن عما كنتم تعملون

translation: And do not take your oaths as [means of] deceit between you, lest a foot slip after it was [once] firm and you would taste evil [in this world] for what [people] you diverted from the way of Allah, and you would have [in the Hereafter] a great punishment.
interpretation: This verse warns against using oaths as a means of deception or betrayal. It cautions that doing so may lead to a person's downfall, even if they were previously on firm footing. The verse emphasizes that those who use their oaths to mislead others from the path of Allah will face severe consequences, both in this world and in the Hereafter. It serves as a reminder to be truthful and sincere in one's oaths and not to use them as a tool for personal gain at the expense of others or in defiance of Allah's guidance.
orig: ولا تتخذوا أيمانكم دخلا بينكم فتزل قدم بعد ثبوتها وتذوقوا السوء بما صددتم عن سبيل الله ولكم عذاب عظيم

translation: And do not exchange the covenant of Allah for a small price. Indeed, what is with Allah is best for you, if only you could know.
interpretation: This verse warns against compromising one's faith and principles for worldly gains or temporary benefits. It emphasizes that what Allah has in store for the believers in the Hereafter is far superior and more valuable than anything this world can offer. The verse encourages Muslims to remain steadfast in their commitment to Allah's commands and to prioritize their relationship with Him over any material temptations or short-term advantages. It reminds us that true success and happiness lie in adhering to Allah's guidance and striving for His pleasure, even if it means sacrificing some worldly comforts or facing challenges along the way. Ultimately, the rewards that await the faithful in the Hereafter will make all their efforts and sacrifices worthwhile.
orig: ولا تشتروا بعهد الله ثمنا قليلا إنما عند الله هو خير لكم إن كنتم تعلمون

translation: Whatever you have will end, but what Allah has is lasting. And We will surely give those who were patient their reward according to the best of what they used to do.
interpretation: This verse reminds us that the material possessions and worldly pleasures we have are temporary and will eventually perish, while the rewards and blessings that Allah has in store for the believers are eternal. It encourages patience and perseverance in the face of hardships and trials, with the promise that those who remain steadfast will be rewarded by Allah in the best possible manner, according to their good deeds and actions. This interpretation highlights the importance of focusing on the eternal rather than the temporary, and striving to please Allah through our actions and conduct.
orig: ما عندكم ينفد وما عند الله باق ولنجزين الذين صبروا أجرهم بأحسن ما كانوا يعملون

translation: Whoever does righteousness, whether male or female, while he is a believer - We will surely cause him to live a good life, and We will surely give them their reward [in the Hereafter] according to the best of what they used to do.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of faith and good deeds, regardless of one's gender. It promises that those who believe in Allah and do righteous deeds will be granted a good life in this world and will be rewarded in the Hereafter according to the best of their actions. This interpretation highlights the equality between men and women in Islam, as both are judged by their faith and actions, not their gender. It also encourages believers to strive for excellence in their deeds, as they will be rewarded based on the quality of their actions.
orig: من عمل صالحا من ذكر أو أنثى وهو مؤمن فلنحيينه حياة طيبة ولنجزينهم أجرهم بأحسن ما كانوا يعملون

translation: So when you recite the Qur'an, [first] seek refuge in Allah from Satan, the expelled [from His mercy].
interpretation: This verse instructs the believer to seek protection in Allah from the whisperings and temptations of Satan before reciting the Qur'an. It emphasizes the importance of being mindful of the devil's influence and striving to approach the Qur'an with a pure heart and sincere intentions. By seeking refuge in Allah, one acknowledges His supreme power and authority, and seeks His guidance and protection from going astray due to the deceptions of Satan. This act of seeking refuge is a means of spiritual fortification and preparation to receive the divine message of the Qur'an with humility, reverence, and a receptive state of mind.
orig: فإذا قرأت القرآن فاستعذ بالله من الشيطان الرجيم

translation: Indeed, there is for him no authority over those who have believed and rely upon their Lord.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Satan has no power or influence over the true believers who put their complete trust in Allah. Those who have strong faith and reliance on their Lord are protected from the whispers and temptations of Satan. It highlights the importance of having unwavering belief and depending on Allah's guidance and support to shield oneself from evil influences. The verse reassures the believers that by staying steadfast in their faith and relying on Allah, they will remain safe from Satan's deceptions and authority.
orig: إنه ليس له سلطان على الذين آمنوا وعلى ربهم يتوكلون

translation: His authority is only over those who take him as an ally and those who through him associate others with Allah.
interpretation: This verse indicates that Satan's influence and power are limited to those who willingly follow him and make him their ally, turning away from the guidance of Allah. It also suggests that those who associate partners with Allah, committing shirk, are more susceptible to falling under the sway of Satan. However, Satan has no real authority over the true believers who seek refuge in Allah and adhere to His guidance. The verse emphasizes the importance of staying firm in one's faith and avoiding any form of association with Satan or polytheistic practices in order to be protected from his influence.
orig: إنما سلطانه على الذين يتولونه والذين هم به مشركون

translation: And when We substitute a verse in place of a verse - and Allah is most knowing of what He sends down - they say, "You, [O Muhammad], are but an inventor [of lies]." But most of them do not know.
interpretation: This verse addresses the accusation made by the disbelievers that the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) was fabricating the Qur'an. They claimed that whenever a verse was revealed that contradicted their desires or beliefs, the Prophet would replace it with another verse to suit his own purposes. However, Allah refutes this accusation by affirming that He alone is the source of the Qur'an and that He reveals it according to His divine wisdom. The substitution of verses is not a contradiction or an abrogation, but rather a part of Allah's plan to gradually reveal His message in a way that is most suitable for the guidance of humanity. The majority of the disbelievers, however, lack the knowledge and understanding to recognize the truth of the Qur'an and the prophethood of Muhammad (peace be upon him).
orig: وإذا بدلنا آية مكان آية والله أعلم بما ينزل قالوا إنما أنت مفتر بل أكثرهم لا يعلمون

translation: Say, "The Holy Spirit has brought it down from your Lord in truth to make firm those who believe and as guidance and good tidings to the Muslims."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the Qur'an is a divine revelation brought down by the Holy Spirit (Angel Gabriel) from God to Prophet Muhammad. Its purpose is to strengthen the faith of the believers, provide them with guidance, and give them glad tidings of God's mercy and rewards. The verse also affirms that the Qur'an is the ultimate truth and that it comes from the Lord of the universe, dispelling any doubts about its authenticity or divine origin. It serves as a source of spiritual nourishment, direction, and hope for those who submit themselves to God's will and follow the teachings of Islam.
orig: قل نزله روح القدس من ربك بالحق ليثبت الذين آمنوا وهدى وبشرى للمسلمين

translation: And We certainly know that they say, "It is only a human being who teaches the Prophet." The tongue of the one they refer to is foreign, and this Qur'an is [in] a clear Arabic language.
interpretation: This verse is a response to those who claimed that Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) was being taught the Qur'an by a foreign man. Allah refutes this accusation by pointing out that the language of the person they refer to is not Arabic, while the Qur'an is revealed in clear and eloquent Arabic. This proves that the Qur'an could not have been taught by a foreigner, but rather it is a divine revelation from Allah. The verse emphasizes the purity and clarity of the Arabic language used in the Qur'an, which is a testament to its divine origin.
orig: ولقد نعلم أنهم يقولون إنما يعلمه بشر لسان الذي يلحدون إليه أعجمي وهذا لسان عربي مبين

translation: Indeed, those who do not believe in the signs of Allah - Allah does not guide them, and for them is a painful punishment.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that those who reject the clear signs and proofs sent by Allah will not receive His guidance. They have chosen to turn away from the truth, and as a result, they will face a severe and painful punishment in the Hereafter. It serves as a warning to those who deny the message of Islam and the evidence that supports it, urging them to reflect upon the consequences of their disbelief and to turn towards faith and righteousness before it is too late.
orig: إن الذين لا يؤمنون بآيات الله لا يهديهم الله ولهم عذاب أليم

translation: Only they forge the lie who do not believe in Allah's communications, and these are the liars.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that those who reject Allah's signs and revelations are the ones who fabricate lies and falsehoods. They are characterized as the true liars because they knowingly deny the truth and invent deceptions to lead others astray from the path of righteousness. The verse implies that believers in Allah and His messages would not engage in such dishonest behavior, as their faith guides them towards honesty and integrity. It serves as a warning against those who deliberately spread misinformation and highlights the importance of believing in and upholding the truth revealed by Allah.
orig: إنما يفتري الكذب الذين لا يؤمنون بآيات الله وأولئك هم الكاذبون

translation: Whoever disbelieves in Allah after his belief... except for one who is forced [to renounce his religion] while his heart is secure in faith. But those who [willingly] open their breasts to disbelief, upon them is wrath from Allah, and for them is a great punishment.
interpretation: This verse indicates that a person who renounces their faith in Islam after having believed, except under compulsion while their heart remains firm in faith, will face the anger and severe punishment of Allah. However, those who willingly embrace disbelief wholeheartedly and reject Islam without coercion will incur an even greater punishment and wrath from Allah. It emphasizes the gravity of apostatizing and abandoning one's faith in Islam, showing it is a major sin warranting severe consequences in the Hereafter, unless done under duress while still believing in one's heart.
orig: من كفر بالله من بعد إيمانه إلا من أكره وقلبه مطمئن بالإيمان ولكن من شرح بالكفر صدرا فعليهم غضب من الله ولهم عذاب عظيم

translation: That is because they preferred the worldly life over the Hereafter, and because Allah does not guide the disbelieving people.
interpretation: This verse highlights the fundamental reason behind the disbelievers' actions and attitudes - their preference for the temporary pleasures and gains of this worldly life over the eternal rewards of the Hereafter. It suggests that their lack of faith and short-sightedness lead them to prioritize the fleeting comforts of this world, neglecting the more significant and lasting consequences of their choices in the afterlife. The verse also emphasizes that Allah does not guide those who choose to reject faith and remain in a state of disbelief, as they have willfully turned away from His guidance and mercy. This interpretation underscores the importance of having a strong faith and keeping the Hereafter in mind when making decisions and living one's life, as it is the ultimate goal for believers.
orig: ذلك بأنهم استحبوا الحياة الدنيا على الآخرة وأن الله لا يهدي القوم الكافرين

translation: Those are the ones over whose hearts, hearing, and vision Allah has sealed, and it is they who are the heedless.
interpretation: This verse refers to those individuals whose hearts have been sealed by Allah due to their persistent disbelief and rejection of the truth. As a result, their spiritual faculties of perception - namely, their hearts, ears, and eyes - have been rendered dysfunctional. They are unable to comprehend or accept the divine message, as they have become heedless and unmindful of Allah's signs and warnings. This state of heedlessness is a consequence of their own choices and actions, as they have consistently turned away from the path of guidance and righteousness. The sealing of their hearts, hearing, and vision is a metaphorical description of their spiritual condition, emphasizing the severity of their disconnection from divine truth.
orig: أولئك الذين طبع الله على قلوبهم وسمعهم وأبصارهم وأولئك هم الغافلون

translation: Without doubt, in the Hereafter they will be the losers.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the ultimate fate of those who reject faith and do evil deeds. It asserts that, despite any worldly gains or temporary success they may enjoy in this life, they will be the ones who suffer the greatest loss in the Hereafter. Their loss will be eternal, as they will be deprived of God's mercy, forgiveness, and the everlasting bliss of Paradise. The verse serves as a reminder that the ultimate success or failure of a person is not determined by their worldly status, but by their faith, righteousness, and obedience to God's commands. It encourages believers to prioritize their spiritual well-being over worldly pursuits and to strive for success in the Hereafter.
orig: لا جرم أنهم في الآخرة هم الخاسرون

translation: Then, indeed your Lord, to those who emigrated after they had been compelled [to renounce their religion] and thereafter fought [for the cause of Allah] and were patient - indeed, your Lord, after that, is Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse highlights Allah's forgiveness and mercy towards those who faced persecution and hardships for their faith. It refers to the early Muslims who were tortured and forced to renounce Islam in Mecca, but later emigrated to Medina. Despite the trials they faced, they remained steadfast in their faith, fought in the way of Allah, and persevered patiently. Allah reassures them that after all they have endured, He is Forgiving and Merciful. This interpretation emphasizes the importance of patience, perseverance and staying true to one's beliefs in the face of adversity. It offers hope and comfort to those who are struggling, letting them know that Allah's mercy and forgiveness await those who strive in His cause and remain steadfast.
orig: ثم إن ربك للذين هاجروا من بعد ما فتنوا ثم جاهدوا وصبروا إن ربك من بعدها لغفور رحيم

translation: The Day when every soul will come pleading for itself, and every soul will be fully compensated for what it did, and they will not be wronged.
interpretation: This verse speaks about the Day of Judgment when every soul will be held accountable for their deeds. Each person will be solely concerned with their own fate, attempting to defend their actions and plead their case before Allah. The verse emphasizes the concept of individual responsibility and divine justice. No soul will bear the burden of another, and everyone will receive the full recompense for their actions, whether good or bad. Allah, being the Most Just, will ensure that no one is treated unfairly or wronged in any way. This verse serves as a reminder for believers to be mindful of their actions in this world, as they will have consequences in the Hereafter.
orig: يوم تأتي كل نفس تجادل عن نفسها وتوفى كل نفس ما عملت وهم لا يظلمون

translation: And Allah presents an example: a city which was safe and secure, its provision coming to it in abundance from every location, but it denied the favors of Allah. So Allah made it taste the envelopment of hunger and fear for what they had been doing.
interpretation: This verse serves as a warning and reminder that Allah's blessings and favors should never be taken for granted. It illustrates the consequences of ingratitude and disbelief through the example of a city that enjoyed safety, security, and abundance. However, when its inhabitants turned away from acknowledging and appreciating Allah's blessings, they were afflicted with hunger and fear as a result of their actions. This verse emphasizes the importance of gratitude, faith, and righteous deeds, as failing to recognize and appreciate the blessings bestowed by Allah can lead to their removal and replacement with hardship and suffering.
orig: وضرب الله مثلا قرية كانت آمنة مطمئنة يأتيها رزقها رغدا من كل مكان فكفرت بأنعم الله فأذاقها الله لباس الجوع والخوف بما كانوا يصنعون

translation: And certainly a messenger from among themselves came to them, but they denied him, so the punishment seized them while they were wrongdoers.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the consequences of rejecting the messengers sent by Allah. It highlights that even when a messenger was sent from among the people themselves, they still denied him and refused to believe in his message. As a result of their disbelief and wrongdoing, Allah's punishment seized them. This serves as a warning to all people that denying the truth and persisting in wrongdoing will ultimately lead to severe consequences in this world and the hereafter. It also underscores the importance of recognizing and accepting the messengers sent by Allah, as they are guides to the straight path and a means of attaining His mercy and forgiveness.
orig: ولقد جاءهم رسول منهم فكذبوه فأخذهم العذاب وهم ظالمون

translation: So eat of what Allah has provided for you [which is] lawful and good. And be grateful for the favor of Allah, if it is [indeed] Him that you worship.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of consuming what is lawful and good from the sustenance that Allah has provided. It reminds believers to be grateful for Allah's blessings and favors, as gratitude is a fundamental aspect of true worship. The verse implies that the consumption of halal and wholesome food is not only permissible but also an act of obedience and worship to Allah. It also suggests that one should avoid what is unlawful or harmful, as this would be a sign of ingratitude and disobedience to the Almighty. Ultimately, the verse encourages believers to lead a life of consciousness, gratitude, and submission to Allah in all aspects, including their dietary choices.
orig: فكلوا مما رزقكم الله حلالا طيبا واشكروا نعمت الله إن كنتم إياه تعبدون

translation: He has only forbidden to you dead animals, blood, the flesh of swine, and that which has been dedicated to other than Allah. But whoever is forced [by necessity], neither desiring [it] nor transgressing [its limit], there is no sin upon him. Indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse clarifies the dietary restrictions in Islam. It specifies that Muslims are prohibited from consuming carrion (animals that died without being slaughtered in the Islamic manner), blood, pork, and any animal dedicated to other than Allah. However, if someone is in a dire situation and consumes these forbidden items out of necessity to survive, without transgressing the limits or desiring it, then Allah will forgive them as He is the Most Forgiving and Merciful. This highlights the compassion and understanding embedded within the Islamic law, which takes into account the various circumstances people may face while still maintaining the general principles and guidelines.
orig: إنما حرم عليكم الميتة والدم ولحم الخنزير وما أهل لغير الله به فمن اضطر غير باغ ولا عاد فإن الله غفور رحيم

translation: And do not say about what your tongues assert of untruth, "This is lawful and this is unlawful," to invent falsehood about Allah. Indeed, those who invent falsehood about Allah will not succeed.
interpretation: This verse is a stern warning against falsely attributing things as lawful or prohibited without any basis from Allah. It condemns those who invent lies about God's law to suit their own whims and desires. Such people deliberately fabricate falsehood and spread misinformation about what Allah has made permissible or forbidden. The verse makes it clear that this is a grievous sin and that those who engage in this kind of deception will never attain success or salvation. It emphasizes the gravity of inventing religious rulings and trying to pass them off as coming from Allah. This verse establishes the important principle that the authority to declare things lawful or unlawful rests with Allah alone, and that humans must submit to His laws without alteration.
orig: ولا تقولوا لما تصف ألسنتكم الكذب هذا حلال وهذا حرام لتفتروا على الله الكذب إن الذين يفترون على الله الكذب لا يفلحون

translation: A little enjoyment, then they will have a painful punishment.
interpretation: This verse warns that the fleeting pleasures and temporary gains of this worldly life are insignificant compared to the severe and painful punishment that awaits those who indulge in them while neglecting their duties to Allah. It emphasizes the importance of prioritizing one's relationship with Allah and the Hereafter over the short-lived temptations of this world. The verse serves as a reminder that the ultimate consequences of one's actions will be faced in the afterlife, and that the wise believer should focus on what is truly meaningful and lasting.
orig: متاع قليل ولهم عذاب أليم

translation: And to those who are Jews We have prohibited what We related to you before. And We did not wrong them [thereby], but they were wronging themselves.
interpretation: This verse refers to the dietary restrictions that were imposed on the Jews in the Torah, such as the prohibition of certain animals like camels and rabbits, as mentioned in an earlier verse (6:146). The verse emphasizes that these prohibitions were not meant to oppress the Jews or wrong them in any way. Rather, it was the result of their own actions and disobedience to Allah's commands. They had brought these restrictions upon themselves through their sinful behavior and deviation from the straight path. The verse implies that had they been righteous and obedient, they would not have been burdened with such prohibitions.
orig: وعلى الذين هادوا حرمنا ما قصصنا عليك من قبل وما ظلمناهم ولكن كانوا أنفسهم يظلمون

translation: Then indeed your Lord, to those who have done wrong out of ignorance and then repent after that and correct themselves - indeed, your Lord, thereafter, is Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse highlights Allah's infinite mercy and forgiveness. It reassures those who have committed sins out of ignorance that if they sincerely repent, mend their ways, and strive to do good, Allah will forgive them. It emphasizes that no matter how grave a person's sins might be, the door to repentance is always open. Allah's forgiveness knows no bounds, and He is ever ready to embrace those who turn back to Him with sincere remorse and a firm resolve to follow the path of righteousness. This verse instills hope in the hearts of believers, encouraging them to never despair of Allah's mercy and to always seek His forgiveness.
orig: ثم إن ربك للذين عملوا السوء بجهالة ثم تابوا من بعد ذلك وأصلحوا إن ربك من بعدها لغفور رحيم

translation: Indeed, Abraham was a [comprehensive] leader, devoutly obedient to Allah, inclining toward truth, and he was not of those who associate others with Allah.
interpretation: This verse highlights the exemplary character of Prophet Abraham. He is described as an "ummah" which signifies that he combined in himself all the virtuous qualities that make an ideal leader and nation. He was obedient to God's commands, led his life according to the true monotheistic faith, and completely shunned polytheism and idolatry. The verse presents Abraham as a role model for believers to emulate - his unwavering devotion to the One God, his commitment to the truth, and his leadership in guiding people to the straight path. It reminds us that the path Abraham followed is the one that leads to success and earns the pleasure of Allah.
orig: إن إبراهيم كان أمة قانتا لله حنيفا ولم يك من المشركين

translation: Grateful for His favors, He chose him and guided him to a straight path.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of gratitude towards Allah for the blessings and guidance He bestows upon His chosen servants. It suggests that being grateful is a key reason why Allah selects certain individuals and guides them to the right path. The straight path mentioned here refers to the way of life that is pleasing to Allah and leads to success in this world and the hereafter. The verse implies that those who are appreciative of Allah's favors and follow His guidance will be among the blessed ones who are close to Him.
orig: شاكرا لأنعمه اجتباه وهداه إلى صراط مستقيم

translation: And We gave him good in this world, and indeed in the Hereafter he will be among the righteous.
interpretation: This verse indicates that Allah blessed the person mentioned with goodness and prosperity in this worldly life, which could include wealth, health, knowledge, and other blessings. Moreover, it affirms that in the Hereafter, this person will be among the righteous servants of Allah who will attain His pleasure and be admitted into Paradise. This suggests that the person lived a life of faith, righteousness, and obedience to Allah, which earned him both worldly and heavenly rewards from his Lord.
orig: وآتيناه في الدنيا حسنة وإنه في الآخرة لمن الصالحين

translation: Then We revealed to you [O Muhammad] to follow the religion of Abraham, inclining to truth, and he was not of those who associate others with Allah.
interpretation: This verse is a divine command to Prophet Muhammad to follow the pure monotheistic faith of Prophet Abraham, who shunned all forms of idolatry and polytheism. It emphasizes the continuity of the core message of Islam with the original teachings of Abraham, based on the belief in the Oneness of God. The verse also affirms that Abraham was not among those who ascribed partners to Allah, underlining the importance of strict monotheism in the Islamic faith. It serves as a reminder for Muslims to adhere to the pure, unadulterated teachings of Abraham and to avoid the practices of those who deviate from the path of worshipping the One True God.
orig: ثم أوحينا إليك أن اتبع ملة إبراهيم حنيفا وما كان من المشركين

translation: The Sabbath was only appointed for those who differed over it. And indeed, your Lord will judge between them on the Day of Resurrection concerning that over which they used to differ.
interpretation: This verse suggests that the Sabbath was prescribed specifically for the Jews who disagreed about its observance. It implies that there were differences of opinion among them regarding the Sabbath and its regulations. The verse then affirms that God will judge between them on the Day of Judgment concerning these differences. This could mean that those who observed the Sabbath properly will be rewarded, while those who did not will be held accountable. It also indicates that such differences will be resolved by God's ultimate judgment in the Hereafter, emphasizing His authority and wisdom in settling disputes that arose among people.
orig: إنما جعل السبت على الذين اختلفوا فيه وإن ربك ليحكم بينهم يوم القيامة فيما كانوا فيه يختلفون

translation: Invite to the way of your Lord with wisdom and good instruction, and argue with them in a way that is best. Indeed, your Lord is most knowing of who has strayed from His way, and He is most knowing of who is [rightly] guided.
interpretation: This verse provides guidance on how to invite others to the path of Islam. It instructs Muslims to use wisdom, kindness, and the best manner of speech when calling others to the faith. Arguing should be done in the most gracious way possible. Ultimately, it is Allah who knows best who is astray and who is rightly guided. The verse emphasizes using gentle persuasion over harsh argumentation or compulsion in matters of faith.
orig: ادع إلى سبيل ربك بالحكمة والموعظة الحسنة وجادلهم بالتي هي أحسن إن ربك هو أعلم بمن ضل عن سبيله وهو أعلم بالمهتدين

translation: And if you punish [an enemy, O believers], punish with an equivalent of that with which you were harmed. But if you are patient - it is better for those who are patient.
interpretation: This verse encourages Muslims to respond to aggression with a measured and proportionate response, while also emphasizing that patience and forgiveness are superior qualities. It suggests that while retaliation is permitted, it should not exceed the harm that was originally inflicted. However, the verse also highlights that choosing patience and forbearance over revenge is the more virtuous path and will ultimately lead to a better outcome for those who are able to exercise restraint in the face of provocation. This interpretation promotes the Islamic values of justice, mercy, and self-control, even in difficult circumstances.
orig: وإن عاقبتم فعاقبوا بمثل ما عوقبتم به ولئن صبرتم لهو خير للصابرين

translation: And be patient, [O Muhammad], and your patience is not but through Allah. And do not grieve over them and do not be in distress over what they conspire.
interpretation: This verse is a reminder to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and to all believers to remain patient in the face of adversity and opposition. It emphasizes that true patience comes only through reliance on Allah and not through one's own strength. The verse also advises against being saddened or distressed by the plots and schemes of the disbelievers, as Allah is fully aware of their actions and will deal with them accordingly. It encourages the believers to put their trust in Allah and remain steadfast in their faith, knowing that He will support and guide them through any difficulties they may face.
orig: واصبر وما صبرك إلا بالله ولا تحزن عليهم ولا تك في ضيق مما يمكرون

translation: Indeed, Allah is with those who fear Him and those who are doers of good.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah is always with those who are righteous and do good deeds. It serves as a reminder and encouragement for believers to be mindful of Allah and strive to live a life of piety and virtue. Those who fear Allah and act in accordance with His guidance can take comfort in knowing that He is with them, supporting and guiding them through life's challenges. The verse also highlights the importance of not only having faith but also translating that faith into action through good deeds and moral conduct. Ultimately, it conveys the message that the path to earning Allah's pleasure and support lies in leading a life of righteousness and beneficence.
orig: إن الله مع الذين اتقوا والذين هم محسنون

translation: Exalted is He who took His Servant by night from al-Masjid al-Haram to al-Masjid al-Aqsa, whose surroundings We have blessed, to show him of Our signs. Indeed, He is the Hearing, the Seeing.
interpretation: This verse refers to the miraculous night journey of Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) from Mecca to Jerusalem, known as Al-Isra' wal-Mi'raj. It emphasizes Allah's power and ability to make His servant travel vast distances in a short span of time, defying the conventional laws of physics. The verse also highlights the holiness and blessings of the area surrounding Al-Aqsa Mosque in Jerusalem. This journey was a divine revelation, showing Prophet Muhammad some of Allah's signs and wonders, affirming that Allah is All-Hearing and All-Seeing, aware of all things. The night journey stands as a testament to the Prophet's truthfulness and the authenticity of his message, as well as a significant event in Islamic history that strengthened the Prophet's faith and resolve.
orig: سبحان الذي أسرى بعبده ليلا من المسجد الحرام إلى المسجد الأقصى الذي باركنا حوله لنريه من آياتنا إنه هو السميع البصير

translation: And We gave Moses the Scripture and made it a guidance for the Children of Israel that you not take other than Me as Disposer of affairs.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the Torah, which was revealed to Prophet Moses, was meant to be a source of guidance for the Children of Israel. It served as a divine message to direct them towards the right path. The key point highlighted here is that they should rely solely on Allah as their Guardian and Protector, and not seek anyone else for this purpose. It stresses the importance of complete trust in Allah alone and not associating partners with Him or seeking protection from others besides Him.
orig: وآتينا موسى الكتاب وجعلناه هدى لبني إسرائيل ألا تتخذوا من دوني وكيلا

translation: Descendants of those We carried [in the ship] with Noah. Indeed, he was a grateful servant.
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of gratitude and faithfulness, as exemplified by Prophet Noah. It suggests that the descendants of those who were saved with Noah in the ark were blessed because of Noah's unwavering devotion and thankfulness to Allah, despite the immense challenges he faced. The verse serves as a reminder for believers to emulate Noah's qualities of gratitude and steadfastness in their own lives, as these virtues are highly valued by Allah and can lead to His favors and blessings being bestowed upon them and their descendants.
orig: ذرية من حملنا مع نوح إنه كان عبدا شكورا

translation: And We decreed for the Children of Israel in the Scripture that indeed you would do mischief on the earth twice and you will become tyrants and extremely arrogant!
interpretation: This verse is a warning to the Children of Israel, as mentioned in their scripture, that they would cause corruption on the earth twice and would become arrogant and tyrannical in their behavior. It suggests that this is a result of their disobedience to Allah's commands and their straying from the right path. The verse implies that there will be consequences for their actions, and that Allah is aware of their misdeeds. It serves as a reminder for them to mend their ways and return to righteousness, or else face the repercussions of their transgressions.
orig: وقضينا إلى بني إسرائيل في الكتاب لتفسدن في الأرض مرتين ولتعلن علوا كبيرا

translation: Then when the first of the two warnings came to pass, We sent against you Our servants given to terrible warfare. They entered the very inmost parts of your homes. And it was a warning (completely) fulfilled.
interpretation: This verse refers to the divine punishment that befell the Children of Israel due to their disobedience and transgression. Allah sent against them a powerful enemy that invaded their homes and lands, causing destruction and suffering. This was the fulfillment of Allah's warning and a reminder of the consequences of turning away from His guidance. It emphasizes that Allah's promise of retribution for the wrongdoers is inevitable and that His punishment can be severe. The verse also implicitly warns believers to be mindful of Allah's commands and to avoid the mistakes of previous nations who earned Allah's wrath due to their persistent sinfulness.
orig: فإذا جاء وعد أولاهما بعثنا عليكم عبادا لنا أولي بأس شديد فجاسوا خلال الديار وكان وعدا مفعولا

translation: Then We gave you back the turn [of victory] over them and We reinforced you with wealth and sons and made you more numerous in manpower.
interpretation: This verse refers to the favor of Allah upon the Children of Israel after they had suffered defeat and humiliation. Allah granted them victory over their enemies, blessed them with wealth, offspring, and increased their numbers and strength. It signifies the cyclical nature of divine intervention in human affairs, where Allah may test people with hardship and then grant them relief and prosperity as a means of trial and mercy. The verse also emphasizes the importance of recognizing Allah's blessings and remaining grateful and obedient to Him in times of ease and difficulty.
orig: ثم رددنا لكم الكرة عليهم وأمددناكم بأموال وبنين وجعلناكم أكثر نفيرا

translation: If you do good, you do good for yourselves, and if you do evil, [you do it] to yourselves. Then when the final promise came, [We sent your enemies] to sadden your faces and to enter the temple in Jerusalem, as they entered it the first time, and to destroy what they had taken over with [total] destruction.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the concept of personal responsibility and accountability for one's actions. It suggests that the consequences of our deeds, whether good or bad, ultimately fall upon ourselves. The verse also alludes to the recurring pattern of divine retribution against those who transgress and oppress others, as exemplified by the destruction of the Temple in Jerusalem. It serves as a reminder that wrongdoing and injustice will eventually lead to one's own downfall and that the ultimate judgment lies with God.
orig: إن أحسنتم أحسنتم لأنفسكم وإن أسأتم فلها فإذا جاء وعد الآخرة ليسوءوا وجوهكم وليدخلوا المسجد كما دخلوه أول مرة وليتبروا ما علوا تتبيرا

translation: It may be that your Lord will have mercy upon you, but if you return [to sin], We will return [to punishment]. And We have made Hell, for the disbelievers, a prison-bed.
interpretation: This verse conveys a message of both hope and warning. It suggests that Allah is merciful and may forgive those who have sinned if they repent and mend their ways. However, it also serves as a stern warning that if people return to their sinful behavior after being forgiven, then Allah will also revert to punishing them. The verse emphasizes that Hell has been prepared as a final abode and severe punishment for those who persistently disbelieve and reject the truth, likening it to a prison-bed that will confine them eternally. It highlights the justice of Allah in dealing with those who are rebellious and ungrateful, while also offering hope for those who seek His forgiveness and mercy.
orig: عسى ربكم أن يرحمكم وإن عدتم عدنا وجعلنا جهنم للكافرين حصيرا

translation: Indeed, this Qur'an guides to that which is most suitable and gives good tidings to the believers who do righteous deeds that they will have a great reward.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the Qur'an is a guide for humanity, leading them to the most righteous and virtuous path in life. It also brings glad tidings and hope to the believers who perform good deeds, assuring them that they will be rewarded generously by Allah in the Hereafter. This interpretation highlights the Qur'an's role as a source of guidance and motivation for believers to lead a life of righteousness and piety, with the promise of a great reward awaiting them in the afterlife.
orig: إن هذا القرآن يهدي للتي هي أقوم ويبشر المؤمنين الذين يعملون الصالحات أن لهم أجرا كبيرا

translation: And for those who do not believe in the Hereafter, We have prepared for them a painful punishment.
interpretation: This verse serves as a stern warning to those who reject belief in the afterlife. It emphasizes that there are severe and painful consequences for denying the existence of the Hereafter, where individuals will be held accountable for their deeds in this worldly life. The "painful punishment" mentioned here alludes to the torment of Hell that awaits those who refuse to accept the truth of resurrection and divine judgment. This interpretation highlights the gravity of disbelief and the importance of having faith in the Hereafter to avoid the agonizing fate that God has prepared for the deniers.
orig: وأن الذين لا يؤمنون بالآخرة أعتدنا لهم عذابا أليما

translation: Man prays for evil as he prays for good, and man is ever hasty.
interpretation: This verse highlights the impatient and impulsive nature of human beings. People often make hasty prayers and wishes without fully considering the consequences, sometimes even praying for things that may harm them in the long run. They are just as quick to pray for evil as they are to pray for good, due to their shortsightedness and lack of wisdom. The verse reminds us to be careful and thoughtful in our supplications, and to trust in Allah's plan rather than our own limited understanding. It also emphasizes the importance of patience and perseverance, as opposed to the human tendency towards haste and impulsiveness.
orig: ويدع الإنسان بالشر دعاءه بالخير وكان الإنسان عجولا

translation: And We have made the night and the day two signs, and We erased the sign of the night and made the sign of the day visible that you may seek bounty from your Lord and may know the number of years and the account [of time]. And everything We have set out in detail.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the divine wisdom behind the alternation of night and day. The night, with its darkness, provides a time for rest and tranquility, while the day, with its light, enables people to engage in various activities and seek sustenance. The mention of "erasing the sign of the night" could symbolize the transition from darkness to light, which is essential for the continuation of life on Earth. Moreover, the verse highlights the importance of understanding the passage of time through the cycle of day and night, as it helps humans keep track of years and maintain accurate records. The final statement, "And everything We have set out in detail," underscores the perfection and purposefulness of God's creation, where every aspect of the universe is meticulously designed and interconnected.
orig: وجعلنا الليل والنهار آيتين فمحونا آية الليل وجعلنا آية النهار مبصرة لتبتغوا فضلا من ربكم ولتعلموا عدد السنين والحساب وكل شيء فصلناه تفصيلا

translation: And [for] every person We have imposed his fate upon his neck, and We will produce for him on the Day of Resurrection a record which he will encounter spread open.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the concept of individual responsibility and accountability. Each person's deeds, whether good or bad, are tied to them like a collar around their neck, and they will be held accountable for these deeds on the Day of Judgment. The record mentioned in the verse refers to the book of deeds, which will be presented to each individual, revealing all their actions throughout their life. This serves as a reminder that everyone will face the consequences of their choices and that no one can escape the ultimate judgment of their deeds. It encourages people to be mindful of their actions and to strive for righteousness, knowing that they will be held responsible for their decisions in this life.
orig: وكل إنسان ألزمناه طائره في عنقه ونخرج له يوم القيامة كتابا يلقاه منشورا

translation: Read your record. Sufficient is yourself against you this Day as accountant.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes personal responsibility on the Day of Judgment. Each individual will be presented with the record of their deeds, and they will have to account for their own actions. No excuses or intercession will be accepted. The verse implies that we should be mindful of our deeds in this life, as we will have to face the consequences of our choices in the Hereafter. It is a reminder to live righteously and be prepared to take full responsibility for our actions when we stand before Allah for judgment.
orig: اقرأ كتابك كفى بنفسك اليوم عليك حسيبا

translation: Whoever is guided is only guided for [the benefit of] his soul. And whoever errs only errs against it. And no bearer of burdens will bear the burden of another. And never would We punish until We sent a messenger.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes individual responsibility and divine justice. It states that each person is accountable for their own spiritual guidance or misguidance, and that no one will bear the burden of another's sins. Moreover, it highlights God's mercy and fairness, as He would never punish people without first sending a messenger to warn and guide them. This underscores the importance of the prophetic mission in conveying divine messages and providing clear guidance to humanity.
orig: من اهتدى فإنما يهتدي لنفسه ومن ضل فإنما يضل عليها ولا تزر وازرة وزر أخرى وما كنا معذبين حتى نبعث رسولا

translation: And when We intend to destroy a city, We command its affluent but they defiantly disobey therein; so the word comes into effect upon it, and We destroy it with [complete] destruction.
interpretation: This verse speaks to a pattern in the destruction of past civilizations. When a society becomes corrupt, especially amongst its leadership and elite, and they become ungrateful for God's blessings and heedless of His guidance, then God's decree becomes justified against them. They bring destruction upon themselves through their own sinful behavior and defiance of divine laws. It is a warning that affluence and power should not lead to transgression and that the fate of past destroyed nations can befall others who follow the same path of corruption. It encourages gratitude, humility, and obedience to God to avoid such a fate.
orig: وإذا أردنا أن نهلك قرية أمرنا مترفيها ففسقوا فيها فحق عليها القول فدمرناها تدميرا

translation: And how many generations have We destroyed after Noah. And sufficient is your Lord, concerning the sins of His servants, as Acquainted and Seeing.
interpretation: This verse serves as a reminder of Allah's power and knowledge. It points out that many generations and civilizations were destroyed by Allah after the time of Prophet Noah due to their sins and disobedience. It emphasizes that Allah is fully aware of the sins committed by His servants and sees all their actions. The verse implies that people should be mindful of their deeds, as Allah has the power to punish those who persist in wrongdoing, just as He destroyed past nations. It also underscores the importance of heeding the warnings of prophets and messengers sent by Allah to guide humanity.
orig: وكم أهلكنا من القرون من بعد نوح وكفى بربك بذنوب عباده خبيرا بصيرا

translation: Whoever desires the immediate, We hasten for him therein what We will for whom We intend. Then We have made for him Hell, which he will [enter to] burn, censured and banished.
interpretation: This verse is a warning to those who are focused solely on the pleasures and gains of this worldly life, while neglecting the Hereafter. It states that if someone desires only the immediate benefits of this world, Allah may grant them some of what they desire, according to His will. However, their ultimate destination will be Hell, where they will burn as a consequence of their choices. They will be blamed, humiliated, and cast out from Allah's mercy due to their shortsightedness and failure to prioritize their eternal life over temporary gratification. This interpretation highlights the importance of maintaining a balance between seeking the good of this world and preparing for the Hereafter, as an excessive focus on worldly pursuits at the expense of one's spiritual well-being can lead to dire consequences in the afterlife.
orig: من كان يريد العاجلة عجلنا له فيها ما نشاء لمن نريد ثم جعلنا له جهنم يصلاها مذموما مدحورا

translation: And whoever desires the Hereafter and strives for it as he ought to strive and he is a believer - it is those whose striving is ever appreciated [by Allah].
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that those who sincerely believe in Allah and the Hereafter, and put in the necessary effort to achieve success in the afterlife, will have their striving appreciated and rewarded by Allah. It highlights the importance of having a strong faith coupled with righteous deeds and actions. The verse also implies that merely desiring the Hereafter is not enough; one must actively work towards attaining it by following Allah's guidance and living a life pleasing to Him. Those who do so will find their efforts acknowledged and valued by Allah, and they will be granted the eternal rewards of Paradise.
orig: ومن أراد الآخرة وسعى لها سعيها وهو مؤمن فأولئك كان سعيهم مشكورا

translation: To each [category] We extend - to these and to those - from the gift of your Lord. And never has the gift of your Lord been restricted.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the generosity and boundlessness of Allah's provision. It assures that Allah bestows His gifts and blessings upon all His creatures, without discrimination or restriction. The verse implies that no one should feel entitled to Allah's favors or think that they have been deprived of His mercy. It also serves as a reminder that all blessings come from Allah alone and that humans should be grateful for whatever they have been given, whether it seems abundant or scarce. Ultimately, the verse encourages believers to trust in Allah's wisdom and to be content with what He has decreed for them.
orig: كلا نمد هؤلاء وهؤلاء من عطاء ربك وما كان عطاء ربك محظورا

translation: See how We have favored some of them over others, and the Hereafter has greater ranks and greater favors.
