interpretation: This verse points to the varying degrees of blessings and favors that Allah has bestowed upon His creation in this worldly life. Some individuals are granted more wealth, status, or abilities than others. However, the verse emphasizes that the differences and rankings in the Hereafter are of far greater significance and magnitude. The rewards and elevated positions in Paradise that the righteous believers will attain are infinitely superior to any worldly favors or distinctions. This serves as a reminder for believers to prioritize striving for success in the eternal life to come, rather than being preoccupied with worldly pursuits and temporary advantages.
orig: انظر كيف فضلنا بعضهم على بعض وللآخرة أكبر درجات وأكبر تفضيلا

translation: Do not set up any other god alongside Allah, lest you end up condemned, abandoned.
interpretation: This verse is a clear warning against associating partners with Allah or worshipping any other deity besides Him. It emphasizes the grave consequences of committing shirk (polytheism) - that one will be condemned by Allah and abandoned, left with no support or help. Worshipping Allah alone is a fundamental tenet of Islam, and ascribing divinity to anyone or anything else is considered the greatest sin that will not be forgiven if one dies in that state. The verse urges the believers to direct all their worship and devotion to Allah alone in order to avoid a miserable fate in this world and the Hereafter.
orig: لا تجعل مع الله إلها آخر فتقعد مذموما مخذولا

translation: And your Lord has decreed that you not worship except Him, and to parents, good treatment. Whether one or both of them reach old age [while] with you, say not to them [so much as], "uff," and do not repel them but speak to them a noble word.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of worshipping Allah alone and being dutiful to one's parents. It instructs us to treat our parents with utmost kindness and respect, especially when they reach old age and become dependent on us. We should never express displeasure or irritation towards them, even by saying "uff" (a word indicating annoyance). Instead, we should always speak to them gently and nobly, showing them love, care, and gratitude for their lifelong sacrifices. This verse highlights the high status of parents in Islam and the obligation of children to care for them, as this is a commandment directly from Allah.
orig: وقضى ربك ألا تعبدوا إلا إياه وبالوالدين إحسانا إما يبلغن عندك الكبر أحدهما أو كلاهما فلا تقل لهما أف ولا تنهرهما وقل لهما قولا كريما

translation: And lower to them the wing of humility out of mercy and say, "My Lord, have mercy upon them as they brought me up [when I was] small."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of showing utmost respect, kindness, and humility towards one's parents. It encourages us to treat them with gentleness and to always keep in mind the sacrifices they made in raising us from childhood. The metaphor of lowering "the wing of humility" signifies the act of showing complete submission and reverence to our parents out of love and gratitude. Furthermore, the verse instructs us to pray for Allah's mercy and blessings upon them, acknowledging their efforts in nurturing and caring for us when we were young and vulnerable. This highlights the immense status of parents in Islam and the obligation of children to honor and care for them, especially in their old age.
orig: واخفض لهما جناح الذل من الرحمة وقل رب ارحمهما كما ربياني صغيرا

translation: Your Lord knows best what is in your minds. If you are righteous, then indeed He is ever, to the often returning [to Him], Forgiving.
interpretation: This verse highlights the omniscience of Allah, who is fully aware of the innermost thoughts and intentions of human beings. It also emphasizes the importance of being righteous and constantly turning to Allah in repentance. The verse assures that for those who sincerely return to Him and seek His forgiveness, Allah is ever-forgiving and merciful. It encourages believers to maintain a strong connection with their Lord, to strive for righteousness, and to have faith in His boundless forgiveness for those who turn to Him with sincere repentance.
orig: ربكم أعلم بما في نفوسكم إن تكونوا صالحين فإنه كان للأوابين غفورا

translation: And give the relative his right, and [also] the poor and the traveler, and do not spend wastefully.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of fulfilling the rights of others, especially those who are in need. It specifically mentions giving relatives their due rights, which may include financial support, kind treatment, and maintaining family ties. The verse also instructs Muslims to care for the poor and assist travelers who are in need. At the same time, it warns against extravagance and wasting resources, promoting a balanced approach to spending wealth. The underlying message is to prioritize social responsibility and generosity while exercising moderation and wisdom in managing one's resources.
orig: وآت ذا القربى حقه والمسكين وابن السبيل ولا تبذر تبذيرا

translation: Indeed, the wasteful are brothers of the devils, and ever has Satan been to his Lord ungrateful.
interpretation: This verse warns against extravagance and wastefulness, stating that those who are wasteful in their spending and consumption are like brothers to the devils. It implies that Satan himself is ungrateful to God, and those who squander and waste are following his example of ingratitude. The verse encourages moderation, gratitude and mindful use of the resources that God has provided, rather than excessive and unnecessary spending which is likened to the behavior of the devils.
orig: إن المبذرين كانوا إخوان الشياطين وكان الشيطان لربه كفورا

translation: And if you [must] turn away from them [expectantly] seeking mercy from your Lord which you expect, then speak to them a gentle word.
interpretation: This verse advises Muslims to be kind and gentle in their speech, even when they are unable to help others due to their own constraints or limitations. It encourages them to express their inability politely, without being harsh or rude, while still hoping for God's mercy and blessings that may enable them to assist others in the future. This highlights the importance of maintaining good character, manners, and positive relationships with people, even in difficult circumstances.
orig: وإما تعرضن عنهم ابتغاء رحمة من ربك ترجوها فقل لهم قولا ميسورا

translation: And do not keep your hand chained to your neck or extend it completely, lest you sit blamed and deprived.
interpretation: This verse advises moderation and balance in spending. One should neither be miserly, keeping their hands "chained to their neck", nor spend extravagantly "extending it completely". The consequences of either extreme are blame and deprivation. Islam encourages the middle path, spending wisely and in moderation, neither hoarding wealth nor squandering it. This balanced approach to finances is conducive to both individual and societal well-being.
orig: ولا تجعل يدك مغلولة إلى عنقك ولا تبسطها كل البسط فتقعد ملوما محسورا

translation: Indeed, your Lord extends provision for whom He wills and restricts [it]. Indeed He is ever, concerning His servants, Acquainted and Seeing.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah is the One who controls the provision and sustenance of all His creation. He gives abundantly to some and limits the provision of others according to His wisdom and knowledge. This highlights the importance of trusting in Allah's plan and decree, as He is fully aware of the needs and circumstances of each individual. It also serves as a reminder to be content with what Allah has provided and to seek His pleasure in both times of ease and hardship, knowing that He is always watching over His servants and knows what is best for them.
orig: إن ربك يبسط الرزق لمن يشاء ويقدر إنه كان بعباده خبيرا بصيرا

translation: And do not kill your children for fear of poverty. We provide for them and for you. Indeed, their killing is ever a great sin.
interpretation: This verse is a clear prohibition against infanticide, which was a practice in pre-Islamic Arabia due to poverty and fear of shame. It emphasizes that Allah is the provider for all, and that killing innocent children is a major sin. The verse highlights the value and sanctity of human life, and the trust one should have in Allah's provision, regardless of one's circumstances. It also underscores the gravity of taking a life unjustly, as it is considered among the greatest of sins in Islam.
orig: ولا تقتلوا أولادكم خشية إملاق نحن نرزقهم وإياكم إن قتلهم كان خطئا كبيرا

translation: And do not approach unlawful sexual intercourse. Indeed, it is ever an immorality and is evil as a way.
interpretation: This verse is a clear prohibition of engaging in any form of unlawful sexual relations or acts that may lead to it. It emphasizes that adultery and fornication are not only immoral and sinful but also detrimental to one's spiritual well-being and societal health. The verse describes such actions as "fahishah" (an immorality) and "saa'a sabeela" (an evil path), indicating the severity of the sin and its negative consequences in this world and the hereafter. The verse also implies that one should stay away from anything that may lead to or facilitate such illicit acts, such as inappropriate interactions, provocative behavior, or consuming content that promotes promiscuity. Instead, Muslims are encouraged to maintain chastity, modesty, and respect in their relationships, and to seek intimacy only within the bounds of marriage, which is considered a sacred bond in Islam.
orig: ولا تقربوا الزنا إنه كان فاحشة وساء سبيلا

translation: And do not kill the soul which Allah has forbidden, except by right. And whoever is killed unjustly - We have given his heir authority, but let him not exceed limits in [the matter of] taking life. Indeed, he has been supported [by the law].
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the sanctity of human life and the prohibition of taking it unjustly. It grants the legal heir of someone killed unjustly the right to seek justice or compensation, but warns against exceeding the limits and taking the law into one's own hands through excessive retribution. The verse affirms that the aggrieved party is supported by the law in seeking justice through the proper channels and authorities, rather than vigilantism. It strikes a balance between the right to justice and avoiding the escalation of violence and bloodshed.
orig: ولا تقتلوا النفس التي حرم الله إلا بالحق ومن قتل مظلوما فقد جعلنا لوليه سلطانا فلا يسرف في القتل إنه كان منصورا

translation: And do not approach the property of the orphan except in the best manner until he reaches maturity. And fulfill [every] commitment. Indeed, the commitment is ever [that about which one will be] questioned.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of protecting the rights and property of orphans. It instructs believers to handle the wealth of orphans with utmost care and honesty until they reach the age of maturity and can manage their own affairs. Additionally, it stresses the significance of fulfilling promises and commitments, as one will be held accountable for them in the Hereafter. This verse promotes a sense of responsibility, trustworthiness, and justice in dealing with the vulnerable members of society and in honoring one's obligations.
orig: ولا تقربوا مال اليتيم إلا بالتي هي أحسن حتى يبلغ أشده وأوفوا بالعهد إن العهد كان مسئولا

translation: And give full measure when you measure, and weigh with an even balance. That is the best way and best in result.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of honesty and fairness in business dealings, particularly in measuring and weighing goods. It instructs believers to give full measure when selling products and to use accurate scales when weighing items. This is considered the best practice not only because it is morally right but also because it leads to the best outcomes in both this world and the hereafter. Honesty and integrity in commerce are essential values in Islam, as they promote trust, social harmony, and blessings from Allah. The verse implies that cheating or shortchanging others will lead to negative consequences and displeasure from God.
orig: وأوفوا الكيل إذا كلتم وزنوا بالقسطاس المستقيم ذلك خير وأحسن تأويلا

translation: And do not pursue that of which you have no knowledge. Indeed, the hearing, the sight and the heart - about all those [one] will be questioned.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of seeking knowledge and avoiding baseless assumptions or actions. It warns against following hearsay, speculation, or blind imitation without proper understanding. The verse reminds us that we will be held accountable for how we use our faculties of hearing, sight, and intellect. It encourages critical thinking, seeking evidence, and making informed decisions based on sound knowledge. The message is to be mindful and responsible in our pursuit of information and to use our God-given abilities wisely, as we will be answerable for them in the Hereafter.
orig: ولا تقف ما ليس لك به علم إن السمع والبصر والفؤاد كل أولئك كان عنه مسئولا

translation: And do not walk upon the earth exultantly. Indeed, you will never tear the earth [apart], and you will never reach the mountains in height.
interpretation: This verse is a reminder for humans to be humble and not arrogant. It emphasizes that no matter how powerful or important we may feel, we are still insignificant in comparison to the vastness of the earth and the mountains. Walking with pride and arrogance is discouraged, as it reflects a lack of humility and understanding of our place in the grand scheme of creation. The verse encourages us to adopt a more modest and grounded approach to life, recognizing our limitations and the immense power of Allah's creation surrounding us.
orig: ولا تمش في الأرض مرحا إنك لن تخرق الأرض ولن تبلغ الجبال طولا

translation: All that, the evil of it, is hateful in the sight of your Lord.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that all the aforementioned evil deeds and sins are greatly disliked and detested by Allah. It serves as a strong warning and reminder to humans to abstain from such actions, as they invite Allah's displeasure and anger. The verse underscores the gravity of engaging in these prohibited acts and highlights the importance of leading a righteous life in accordance with Allah's commands. It also implies that one should be mindful of their actions and strive to avoid anything that earns the hatred of their Lord, as it ultimately leads to negative consequences in this world and the hereafter.
orig: كل ذلك كان سيئه عند ربك مكروها

translation: That is from what your Lord has revealed to you, [O Muhammad], of wisdom. And, [O mankind], do not make [as equal] with Allah another deity, lest you be thrown into Hell, blamed and banished.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of monotheism in Islam. It warns against the grave sin of shirk, which is associating partners with Allah or worshipping other deities alongside Him. The verse states that this wisdom comes directly from Allah to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and serves as a reminder to all of mankind. It cautions that those who commit shirk will be condemned to Hell, facing blame and banishment from Allah's mercy. This highlights the severity of the sin and the consequences of deviating from the core Islamic belief in the oneness of Allah.
orig: ذلك مما أوحى إليك ربك من الحكمة ولا تجعل مع الله إلها آخر فتلقى في جهنم ملوما مدحورا

translation: Has your Lord then chosen sons for you and taken from among the angels daughters? Indeed, you say a grave saying.
interpretation: This verse is questioning the belief of some people who attribute daughters to Allah while they prefer sons for themselves. It is highlighting the absurdity and gravity of such a claim, as it goes against the perfection and transcendence of Allah. The verse implies that attributing offspring to Allah, whether sons or daughters, is a serious transgression and a baseless assertion that has no foundation in truth. It emphasizes the importance of maintaining a pure and correct belief in the oneness and uniqueness of Allah, free from any form of anthropomorphism or ascribing to Him attributes that do not befit His majesty.
orig: أفأصفاكم ربكم بالبنين واتخذ من الملائكة إناثا إنكم لتقولون قولا عظيما

translation: And indeed, We have explained [in detail] in this Qur'an that they may be reminded, but it does not increase them except in aversion.
interpretation: This verse suggests that despite God's efforts to explain the teachings and guidance of the Qur'an in various ways to serve as a reminder for humanity, many people only become more averse and distant from its message. It implies that the problem lies not in any lack of clarity in the Qur'an itself, but rather in the hearts and attitudes of those who turn away from it out of arrogance, stubbornness or attachment to worldly desires. The Qur'an is meant to soften hearts and provide a remembrance of God, but those who are determined to reject it will only find their aversion increased the more they are reminded.
orig: ولقد صرفنا في هذا القرآن ليذكروا وما يزيدهم إلا نفورا

translation: Say, "If there had been with Him [other] gods, as they say, then they [each] would have sought to the Owner of the Throne a way."
interpretation: This verse challenges the polytheistic belief that there are multiple gods besides Allah. It argues that if there were truly other gods, they would have sought to compete with Allah for supremacy and control over the Throne, which symbolizes ultimate power and authority. The fact that no such attempt has been made proves the falsehood of polytheism and affirms the absolute oneness and sovereignty of Allah. The verse emphasizes that Allah alone is the Lord of the Throne, with no rivals or partners.
orig: قل لو كان معه آلهة كما يقولون إذا لابتغوا إلى ذي العرش سبيلا

translation: Exalted is He and high above what they say by great sublimity.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute transcendence and perfection of Allah, exalting Him far above any false attributions, descriptions or partners that people may ascribe to Him out of ignorance or disbelief. It affirms His uniqueness, superiority and sublimity over all of His creation. The verse serves as a reminder for believers to venerate and glorify Allah alone, and to negate any notion that does not befit His majesty and perfection. It is a declaration of His immeasurable greatness and a rejection of the way some people may speak of Him in a manner that does not align with His divine attributes and unity.
orig: سبحانه وتعالى عما يقولون علوا كبيرا

translation: The seven heavens and the earth and whatever is in them exalt Him. And there is not a thing except that it exalts [Allah] by His praise, but you do not understand their [way of] exalting. Indeed, He is ever Forbearing and Forgiving.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that all of Allah's creation, from the vast heavens to the earth and everything within them, constantly glorifies and praises Him in a manner befitting His majesty. Even though we may not comprehend how these creations exalt Him, it is an ongoing process that reflects His deserving of all praise. The verse concludes by highlighting two of Allah's attributes: His forbearance and forgiveness towards His servants, despite their shortcomings in fully recognizing and appreciating His glory and magnificence. It serves as a reminder for humankind to strive in acknowledging and exalting Allah, while seeking His forgiveness for any lapses in doing so.
orig: تسبح له السماوات السبع والأرض ومن فيهن وإن من شيء إلا يسبح بحمده ولكن لا تفقهون تسبيحهم إنه كان حليما غفورا

translation: And when you recite the Qur'an, We put between you and those who do not believe in the Hereafter a concealed partition.
interpretation: This verse refers to the spiritual veil that exists between the believers and the disbelievers. When the Qur'an is recited, Allah creates an unseen barrier that prevents the disbelievers from understanding and accepting its message. This partition is a result of their lack of faith in the Hereafter and their rejection of the truth. It symbolizes the separation between those guided by the light of the Qur'an and those who remain in spiritual darkness due to their disbelief. The concealed nature of this partition indicates that the disbelievers are unaware of their own spiritual blindness and the reality of the divine message.
orig: وإذا قرأت القرآن جعلنا بينك وبين الذين لا يؤمنون بالآخرة حجابا مستورا

translation: And We have placed over their hearts coverings, lest they understand it, and in their ears deafness. And when you mention your Lord alone in the Qur'an, they turn back in aversion.
interpretation: This verse refers to the disbelievers who reject the message of Islam. Allah has placed a barrier over their hearts and ears, making them unable to comprehend or accept the truth of the Qur'an. When Allah is mentioned alone, without any partners or associates, they turn away in disgust and aversion. This is because they are deeply entrenched in their polytheistic beliefs and cannot bear to hear the concept of Allah's oneness and uniqueness. Their spiritual blindness and deafness prevent them from recognizing the truth and embracing the guidance of the Qur'an.
orig: وجعلنا على قلوبهم أكنة أن يفقهوه وفي آذانهم وقرا وإذا ذكرت ربك في القرآن وحده ولوا على أدبارهم نفورا

translation: We are most knowing of how they listen to it when they listen to you and when they are in private conversation, when the wrongdoers say, "You follow not but a man affected by magic."
interpretation: This verse is addressing the Prophet Muhammad, telling him that Allah is fully aware of how the disbelievers and wrongdoers secretly listen to the Qur'an and the Prophet's teachings, while outwardly rejecting and mocking it. In their private conversations, they dismiss the Prophet as a man bewitched or possessed by magic, refusing to acknowledge the truth of his message. The interpretation is that despite their outward denial and ridicule, the disbelievers are inwardly affected by the power of the Qur'an and the Prophet's teachings, but their arrogance and stubbornness prevent them from openly accepting the truth. Allah reassures the Prophet that He knows the reality of their behavior and inner thoughts, even as they try to deceive themselves and others.
orig: نحن أعلم بما يستمعون به إذ يستمعون إليك وإذ هم نجوى إذ يقول الظالمون إن تتبعون إلا رجلا مسحورا

translation: See how they strike similitudes for you, and go astray, and cannot find a way!
interpretation: This verse is a rebuke to the disbelievers who tried to discredit the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) by making false comparisons and analogies. They compared him to poets, soothsayers, and madmen in an attempt to undermine his message. However, their comparisons were baseless and only served to expose their own ignorance and stubbornness. The verse emphasizes that by resorting to such tactics, they have strayed far from the truth and cannot find the right path to understanding and accepting the divine message. It highlights the futility of their efforts to oppose the truth of Islam through irrational arguments and false analogies.
orig: انظر كيف ضربوا لك الأمثال فضلوا فلا يستطيعون سبيلا

translation: And they say, "When we are bones and crumbled particles, will we [truly] be resurrected as a new creation?"
interpretation: This verse is addressing the skepticism and disbelief of those who deny the resurrection. They question how it is possible for them to be brought back to life as a new creation after their bodies have decomposed into bones and dust. The verse implies that God, who created them in the first place, is certainly capable of recreating them and bringing them back to life, even after their physical bodies have disintegrated. It highlights the power and ability of God to resurrect the dead, despite the doubts and objections raised by the disbelievers.
orig: وقالوا أإذا كنا عظاما ورفاتا أإنا لمبعوثون خلقا جديدا

translation: Say, "Be you stones or iron"
interpretation: This verse is challenging the disbelievers, saying that even if they were to become as hard as stones or iron in their resistance to the truth of Islam, it would not avail them anything before the power and will of Allah. It emphasizes that no matter how stubborn or unyielding they may be, they cannot escape the judgment of Allah or prevent His message from prevailing. The verse also implies that the hearts of the disbelievers have become hardened and unreceptive to faith, spiritually resembling lifeless materials like stone and iron.
orig: قل كونوا حجارة أو حديدا

translation: Or [they will say], "[We are] a creation greater than that in your breasts." Then they will say, "Who will restore us?" Say, "He who brought you forth the first time." Then they will nod their heads toward you and say, "When is that?" Say, "Perhaps it will be soon -
interpretation: This verse is addressing the skepticism and disbelief of those who deny the resurrection. They question how their scattered remains could be brought back to life, considering it an impossibility. In response, God instructs the Prophet to remind them that the One who created them initially from nothing has the power to resurrect them. The nodding of their heads suggests their mocking attitude towards the idea of resurrection. The verse concludes with the assertion that the Day of Judgment may be closer than they imagine, emphasizing the reality and imminence of accountability before God.
orig: أو خلقا مما يكبر في صدوركم فسيقولون من يعيدنا قل الذي فطركم أول مرة فسينغضون إليك رءوسهم ويقولون متى هو قل عسى أن يكون قريبا

translation: The Day He will call you and you will respond with His praise, and you will think that you had not remained [in the world] except for a little.
interpretation: This verse refers to the Day of Resurrection, when Allah will call upon all of humanity to rise from their graves. The people will respond immediately, praising Allah and realizing the brevity of their worldly life in comparison to the eternal hereafter. It serves as a reminder for believers to focus on the eternal life rather than being distracted by the temporary pleasures of this world, as the time spent on Earth will seem insignificant on the Day of Judgment.
orig: يوم يدعوكم فتستجيبون بحمده وتظنون إن لبثتم إلا قليلا

translation: And tell My servants to say that which is best. Indeed, Satan induces [dissension] among them. Indeed Satan is ever, to mankind, a clear enemy.
interpretation: This verse instructs the believers to speak in the best manner possible, as this can help prevent the influence of Satan in causing disputes and ill feelings between people. It reminds us that Satan is an open enemy to mankind, always seeking to sow discord and lead people astray. By speaking with kindness, wisdom and graciousness, even in the face of provocation or disagreement, Muslims can help maintain unity and resist Satan's attempts to divide them. This verse emphasizes the importance of good communication and positive interaction in preserving the bonds of brotherhood and repelling the schemes of the devil.
orig: وقل لعبادي يقولوا التي هي أحسن إن الشيطان ينزغ بينهم إن الشيطان كان للإنسان عدوا مبينا

translation: Your Lord knows you best. If He wills, He will have mercy upon you; and if He wills, He will punish you. We have not sent you [O Muhammad] over them as a guardian.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute power and authority of Allah over His creation. It is He alone who decides whether to bestow His mercy or inflict punishment upon individuals based on His divine wisdom and justice. The Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) is reminded that his role is not to act as a guardian or guarantor for people's actions and ultimate fate. Rather, his duty is to convey the message of Islam and guide people to the right path, while the final judgment rests with Allah. This verse underscores the importance of recognizing Allah's sovereignty and submitting to His will, as He alone knows what is best for His servants.
orig: ربكم أعلم بكم إن يشأ يرحمكم أو إن يشأ يعذبكم وما أرسلناك عليهم وكيلا

translation: And your Lord is most knowing of whoever is in the heavens and the earth. And We have made some of the prophets exceed others [in various ways], and to David We gave the book [of Psalms].
interpretation: This verse highlights the omniscience of Allah, who has complete knowledge of all beings in the heavens and the earth. It also indicates that Allah has favored some prophets over others, bestowing upon them unique qualities, abilities, or divine revelations. The verse specifically mentions the prophet David (Dawud), to whom Allah granted the Zabur (Psalms). This suggests that while all prophets are chosen and guided by Allah, they are not all equal in their roles, their miracles, or the revelations they received. The mention of David and the Psalms also serves as a reminder of the continuity of Allah's message and the shared spiritual heritage among the Abrahamic faiths.
orig: وربك أعلم بمن في السماوات والأرض ولقد فضلنا بعض النبيين على بعض وآتينا داوود زبورا

translation: Say, "Invoke those you claim [as deities] besides Him, for they do not possess [the ability] to remove adversity from you or [to] change [your condition]."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute power and authority of Allah, stating that no one besides Him has the ability to alleviate hardships or change one's circumstances. It challenges those who invoke other deities or seek help from anyone other than Allah, making it clear that such actions are futile. The verse serves as a reminder for believers to put their trust solely in Allah and to turn to Him alone for assistance and guidance, as He is the only One capable of removing difficulties and granting relief.
orig: قل ادعوا الذين زعمتم من دونه فلا يملكون كشف الضر عنكم ولا تحويلا

translation: Those whom they call upon seek means of access to their Lord, [striving as to] which of them would be nearest, and they hope for His mercy and fear His punishment. Indeed, the punishment of your Lord is ever feared.
interpretation: This verse highlights the concept of intercession in Islam. It states that even those beings that people call upon besides Allah, such as angels or prophets, are themselves seeking means to get closer to Allah. They hope for His mercy and fear His punishment, acknowledging His supreme power and authority. The verse emphasizes that no one can grant benefit or cause harm except by Allah's permission. It also serves as a reminder to humans that if even those exalted beings stand in awe and reverence of Allah and seek His closeness, then human beings should be even more devoted to worshipping Him alone and seeking His pleasure, knowing that His punishment is to be feared.
orig: أولئك الذين يدعون يبتغون إلى ربهم الوسيلة أيهم أقرب ويرجون رحمته ويخافون عذابه إن عذاب ربك كان محذورا

translation: There is not a city but that We will destroy it before the Day of Resurrection or punish it with a severe punishment. That has ever been in the Register inscribed.
interpretation: This verse is a stern warning from Allah to the disbelievers and wrongdoers. It emphasizes the inevitability of divine retribution for those who persist in their disbelief and transgression. Allah declares that every city that rejects His message and opposes His messengers will face destruction or severe punishment before the Day of Judgment. This decree is already written in the Preserved Tablet (al-Lawh al-Mahfūẓ). The verse serves as a reminder of Allah's ultimate power and justice, and encourages people to embrace faith and righteousness before it is too late. It also consoles the believers, assuring them that the oppression and injustice they face will not go unpunished, and that Allah's promise of judgment is certain.
orig: وإن من قرية إلا نحن مهلكوها قبل يوم القيامة أو معذبوها عذابا شديدا كان ذلك في الكتاب مسطورا

translation: And nothing has prevented Us from sending signs except that the former peoples denied them. And We gave Thamud the she-camel as a visible sign, but they wronged her. And We send not the signs except as a warning.
interpretation: This verse highlights that Allah has the power to send clear signs and miracles to guide people, but He refrains from doing so excessively because previous nations rejected and disbelieved in them despite their clarity. The example given is of the people of Thamud, who were sent a miraculous she-camel as a sign, yet they still wronged it and faced the consequences of their actions. The purpose of sending such signs is not to force belief, but rather to serve as a warning and reminder for people to reflect and believe in Allah's message. Ultimately, it is up to individuals to choose faith or disbelief, and Allah's signs serve as a mercy and guidance for those who are open to accepting the truth.
orig: وما منعنا أن نرسل بالآيات إلا أن كذب بها الأولون وآتينا ثمود الناقة مبصرة فظلموا بها وما نرسل بالآيات إلا تخويفا

translation: And [remember, O Muhammad], when We told you, "Indeed, your Lord has encompassed the people." And We did not make the sight which We showed you except as a trial for the people, as was the accursed tree [mentioned] in the Qur'an. And We threaten them, but it increases them not except in great transgression.
interpretation: This verse is a reminder to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) that Allah has full knowledge and control over all people. The vision mentioned in the verse, which was shown to the Prophet, and the accursed tree (believed by many scholars to refer to Zaqqum, a tree that grows in Hell) are both described as a test for people. Despite Allah's warnings and threats, these only increase the transgressors in their disobedience and rebellion against Allah, as they refuse to heed the signs and admonitions, and persist in their wrongdoing.
orig: وإذ قلنا لك إن ربك أحاط بالناس وما جعلنا الرؤيا التي أريناك إلا فتنة للناس والشجرة الملعونة في القرآن ونخوفهم فما يزيدهم إلا طغيانا كبيرا

translation: And [mention] when We said to the angels, "Prostrate before Adam"; so they prostrated, except for Iblees. He said, "Should I prostrate to one You created from clay?"
interpretation: This verse highlights the superiority of Adam over the angels, as Allah commanded them to prostrate before him. It also showcases the arrogance and disobedience of Iblees (Satan), who refused to follow Allah's command, questioning His wisdom in creating Adam from clay. Iblees' pride and sense of self-superiority led to his downfall and expulsion from Paradise. The verse serves as a reminder for humans to be humble, obedient, and submissive to Allah's will, and to avoid the path of arrogance and disobedience that Iblees followed.
orig: وإذ قلنا للملائكة اسجدوا لآدم فسجدوا إلا إبليس قال أأسجد لمن خلقت طينا

translation: He said, "Do You see this one whom You have honored above me? If You delay me until the Day of Resurrection, I will surely destroy his descendants, except for a few."
interpretation: This verse is spoken by Satan (Iblis) in response to God honoring Adam over him. Satan, out of pride and arrogance, vows to mislead and corrupt the descendants of Adam until the Day of Judgment, except for a small group of righteous individuals. It highlights the enmity between Satan and humanity, and his determination to lead people astray from the straight path. The verse also implies that while Satan will try to misguide many, there will always be a group of faithful believers who will resist his temptations and remain steadfast in their obedience to God.
orig: قال أرأيتك هذا الذي كرمت علي لئن أخرتن إلى يوم القيامة لأحتنكن ذريته إلا قليلا

translation: [Allah] said, "Go, for whoever of them follows you, indeed Hell will be the recompense of [all of] you - an ample recompense."
interpretation: This verse is a warning from Allah to Satan and his followers. It emphasizes that those who follow the path of Satan and disobey Allah will face the severe punishment of Hell as a consequence of their actions. The phrase "an ample recompense" underscores the gravity and completeness of the punishment, suggesting that it will be a fitting retribution for their sins and that there will be no escape or reduction in its severity. The verse serves as a reminder to humans to be cautious of Satan's temptations and to strive to follow the path of righteousness to avoid the fate of eternal damnation.
orig: قال اذهب فمن تبعك منهم فإن جهنم جزاؤكم جزاء موفورا

translation: And incite [to senselessness] whoever you can among them with your voice and assault them with your horses and foot soldiers and become a partner in their wealth and their children and promise them." But Satan does not promise them except delusion.
interpretation: This verse is interpreted as a warning against the deceptive tactics of Satan. It suggests that Satan will use various means to lead people astray, such as tempting them with wealth, children, and empty promises. The mention of "horses and foot soldiers" is seen as a metaphor for the different ways in which Satan attacks and influences people. The verse emphasizes that ultimately, Satan's promises are nothing but delusions and that believers should be cautious and resist his temptations. It serves as a reminder to stay steadfast in faith and not be swayed by worldly desires or false promises.
orig: واستفزز من استطعت منهم بصوتك وأجلب عليهم بخيلك ورجلك وشاركهم في الأموال والأولاد وعدهم وما يعدهم الشيطان إلا غرورا

translation: Indeed, over My [believing] servants there is for you no authority. And sufficient is your Lord as Disposer of affairs.
interpretation: This verse asserts that Satan has no power or influence over the true servants of Allah who are steadfast in their faith and devotion. It emphasizes that Allah alone is sufficient as a Guardian and Protector for His servants, and He will defend them against the temptations and deceptions of Satan. The verse serves as a reassurance to the believers that as long as they remain sincere in their worship and obedience to Allah, they will be under His protection and Satan will have no authority over them.
orig: إن عبادي ليس لك عليهم سلطان وكفى بربك وكيلا

translation: It is your Lord who drives the ship for you through the sea, that you may seek of His bounty. Indeed, He is ever, to you, Merciful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's mercy and kindness towards His servants. It is He who enables people to sail ships across the vast oceans, making it possible for them to travel great distances, conduct trade, and seek His bounties in the form of livelihood and provision. This verse also points to the fact that Allah has subjected the sea and ships to the benefit of human beings, which is a sign of His immense mercy. It encourages people to be grateful for Allah's blessings and to seek His bounties through lawful means, while acknowledging that all blessings come from Him alone.
orig: ربكم الذي يزجي لكم الفلك في البحر لتبتغوا من فضله إنه كان بكم رحيما

translation: And when adversity touches you upon the sea, lost are [all] those you invoke except for Him. But when He delivers you to the land, you turn away [from Him]. And ever is man ungrateful.
interpretation: This verse highlights the fickleness of human nature and the tendency to turn to God only in times of hardship. When people are in distress, such as when they face difficulties at sea, they often call upon God for help, forgetting all other deities or sources of support. However, once God rescues them and brings them safely to land, they turn away from Him and forget their reliance on His mercy. This behavior demonstrates the inherent ingratitude of human beings, who fail to acknowledge and appreciate God's blessings and guidance in both good times and bad. The verse serves as a reminder for people to remain steadfast in their faith and gratitude towards God, regardless of the circumstances they face in life.
orig: وإذا مسكم الضر في البحر ضل من تدعون إلا إياه فلما نجاكم إلى البر أعرضتم وكان الإنسان كفورا

translation: Do you then feel secure that He will not cause a part of the land to swallow you up, or that He will not send against you a violent sandstorm? Then, you shall find no Wakil (guardian one to guard you from the torment).
interpretation: This verse is a reminder that Allah has power over all things and can inflict punishment upon those who disbelieve or disobey Him. It emphasizes the helplessness of humans before Allah's might, as no one can protect them from His wrath if He decides to send calamities or disasters their way. The verse serves as a warning for people to be mindful of their actions and to submit to Allah's will, seeking His protection and guidance rather than relying on their own strength or worldly allies. It highlights the importance of having faith, humility, and consciousness of Allah in order to be saved from His punishment in this world and the hereafter.
orig: أفأمنتم أن يخسف بكم جانب البر أو يرسل عليكم حاصبا ثم لا تجدوا لكم وكيلا

translation: Do you feel secure that He will not send you back into it another time and send upon you a hurricane of wind and drown you for what you denied? Then you would not find for yourselves against Us an avenger.
interpretation: This verse is a warning to those who disbelieve in Allah's power and deny His favors. It reminds them that just as Allah has saved them from the perils of the sea before, He can easily send them back into it and drown them with a powerful wind as a punishment for their ingratitude and disbelief. The verse emphasizes that no one can protect them from Allah's wrath or seek vengeance on their behalf if they face His punishment. It is a reminder to be grateful for Allah's blessings and to have faith in His power and authority over all things.
orig: أم أمنتم أن يعيدكم فيه تارة أخرى فيرسل عليكم قاصفا من الريح فيغرقكم بما كفرتم ثم لا تجدوا لكم علينا به تبيعا

translation: And We have certainly honored the children of Adam and carried them on the land and sea and provided for them of the good things and preferred them over much of what We have created, with [definite] preference.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the special status and honor that God has bestowed upon human beings. It highlights the favors and blessings that God has granted humans, such as the ability to travel on land and sea, the provision of sustenance and good things, and the superiority of humans over many other creatures. This special status comes with a responsibility for humans to be grateful to God and to use their God-given abilities and blessings in a righteous manner, in accordance with God's guidance. The verse serves as a reminder of the need for humans to acknowledge and appreciate the many blessings and favors that God has bestowed upon them.
orig: ولقد كرمنا بني آدم وحملناهم في البر والبحر ورزقناهم من الطيبات وفضلناهم على كثير ممن خلقنا تفضيلا

translation: The Day We will call forth every people with their leader. Then whoever is given his record in his right hand - those will read their records, and injustice will not be done to them, [even] as much as a thread [inside a date seed].
interpretation: This verse refers to the Day of Judgment when every person will be called forth with their leader or the one they followed in this world. Those who receive their book of deeds in their right hand will be the successful ones who will read their records with happiness and will not be wronged in the least. This emphasizes the importance of following righteous leaders and doing good deeds in this life, as it will determine one's fate on the Day of Judgment. It also highlights Allah's ultimate justice, as no one will be treated unfairly, not even by an amount as small as a thread inside a date seed.
orig: يوم ندعو كل أناس بإمامهم فمن أوتي كتابه بيمينه فأولئك يقرءون كتابهم ولا يظلمون فتيلا

translation: And whoever is blind in this [life] will be blind in the Hereafter and more astray in way.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of spiritual insight and guidance in this worldly life. Those who are "blind" to the truth and fail to recognize and follow the guidance of Allah in this life will find themselves in an even worse state of spiritual blindness and misguidance in the Hereafter. They will have strayed far from the straight path that leads to salvation and eternal bliss. The verse serves as a warning to mankind to open their hearts and minds to the truth, to seek Allah's guidance, and to live righteously in this world so that they may be among the successful in the next life.
orig: ومن كان في هذه أعمى فهو في الآخرة أعمى وأضل سبيلا

translation: And indeed, they were about to tempt you away from that which We revealed to you in order to [make] you invent about Us something else; and then they would have taken you as a friend.
interpretation: This verse is a warning to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) that the disbelievers were trying to tempt him away from the revelation that Allah had sent down to him. They wanted him to compromise with them and make changes to the message to suit their desires. If he had done so, they would have taken him as a close friend and ally. However, Allah is reminding the Prophet to stay firm on the truth and not be swayed by their attempts to lead him astray. This highlights the importance of remaining steadfast in one's faith and not compromising on the teachings of Islam, even in the face of pressure or temptation from others.
orig: وإن كادوا ليفتنونك عن الذي أوحينا إليك لتفتري علينا غيره وإذا لاتخذوك خليلا

translation: And if We had not strengthened you, you would have almost inclined to them a little.
interpretation: This verse is a reminder from Allah to Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) that if it were not for Allah's guidance and support, even the Prophet himself might have been tempted to compromise with the disbelievers and those who opposed his message. It emphasizes the importance of remaining steadfast in one's faith and the need for divine assistance to overcome the challenges and temptations that one may face in conveying the truth. The verse also highlights the fact that no one, not even the prophets, is immune to human weaknesses and that it is only through Allah's grace and protection that one can remain on the straight path.
orig: ولولا أن ثبتناك لقد كدت تركن إليهم شيئا قليلا

translation: Then We would have made you taste double [punishment in] life and double [after] death. Then you would not find for yourself against Us a helper.
interpretation: This verse is a stern warning to those who oppose Allah and His messenger. It emphasizes the absolute power and authority of Allah over His creation. If Allah were to punish someone, He could do so in this life and the next, and no one would be able to help or protect them from His wrath. It is a reminder that we should fear Allah and seek His pleasure, for He alone has the power to determine our fate in this world and the hereafter. The verse also highlights the importance of having Allah as our helper and protector, for without His aid, we are truly helpless.
orig: إذا لأذقناك ضعف الحياة وضعف الممات ثم لا تجد لك علينا نصيرا

translation: And indeed, they were about to drive you from the land to evict you therefrom. And then [when they do], they will not remain [there] after you, except for a little.
interpretation: This verse is a warning to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) that his enemies were plotting to expel him from Mecca, his hometown. It also serves as a reminder that even if they succeeded in driving him out, they would not be able to enjoy their victory for long, as they would soon face the consequences of their actions. The verse highlights the temporary nature of worldly power and the ultimate triumph of truth and righteousness over falsehood and oppression. It encourages the believers to remain steadfast in the face of adversity, knowing that God's support is with them and that the wrongdoers will ultimately be defeated.
orig: وإن كادوا ليستفزونك من الأرض ليخرجوك منها وإذا لا يلبثون خلافك إلا قليلا

translation: The way of those We had sent before you of Our messengers. And you will not find in Our way any alteration.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the continuity and consistency of Allah's message throughout history. The prophets and messengers sent by Allah before Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) followed the same fundamental teachings and principles. The verse reassures the Prophet that the message he is conveying is not new or different from what was revealed to the previous prophets. It also highlights the immutability of Allah's way (sunnah), indicating that His laws and decrees are unchanging and eternal. This verse serves as a reminder that the core message of Islam, such as the belief in one God and the importance of righteousness, has remained the same across all divinely revealed religions.
orig: سنة من قد أرسلنا قبلك من رسلنا ولا تجد لسنتنا تحويلا

translation: Establish prayer at the decline of the sun [from its meridian] until the darkness of the night and [also] the Qur'an of dawn. Indeed, the recitation of dawn is ever witnessed.
interpretation: This verse is instructing the believers to establish and maintain the five obligatory prayers throughout the day, starting from the time when the sun begins to decline from its zenith (Dhuhr prayer) until the darkness of the night sets in (Isha prayer). It places special emphasis on the dawn prayer (Fajr), stating that it is witnessed by the angels. This highlights the importance and virtues of the Fajr prayer. The verse encourages Muslims to be steadfast in observing their prayers at their designated times, as it is a fundamental pillar of Islam and a means of maintaining a strong connection with Allah.
orig: أقم الصلاة لدلوك الشمس إلى غسق الليل وقرآن الفجر إن قرآن الفجر كان مشهودا

translation: And from [part of] the night, pray with it as additional [worship] for you; it is expected that your Lord will resurrect you to a praised station.
interpretation: This verse encourages the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) to engage in extra voluntary prayers at night, known as Tahajjud. It suggests that by dedicating a portion of the night to additional worship, the Prophet may be elevated by Allah to a highly praised and honored position (Maqam Mahmud). This can be interpreted as a spiritual station of intercession, where the Prophet will have the privilege of interceding on behalf of his followers on the Day of Judgment. The verse emphasizes the importance and value of performing voluntary prayers and seeking closeness to Allah during the quiet hours of the night.
orig: ومن الليل فتهجد به نافلة لك عسى أن يبعثك ربك مقاما محمودا

translation: And say, "My Lord, cause me to enter a sound entrance and to exit a sound exit and grant me from Yourself a supporting authority."
interpretation: This verse is a prayer for guidance and support from Allah. The believer is asking Allah to grant them a righteous and dignified way of entering into any situation or place, and to exit from it in the same manner. They are also seeking Allah's help and authority to support them in their endeavors. This prayer reflects the believer's reliance on Allah's guidance and assistance in all aspects of life, and their desire to conduct themselves with integrity and righteousness at all times.
orig: وقل رب أدخلني مدخل صدق وأخرجني مخرج صدق واجعل لي من لدنك سلطانا نصيرا

translation: And say, "Truth has come, and falsehood has departed. Indeed is falsehood, [by nature], ever bound to depart."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the ultimate triumph of truth over falsehood. It asserts that when the truth arrives, falsehood inevitably vanishes, as it is in the very nature of falsehood to be temporary and fleeting. The verse encourages believers to have faith in the power of truth and to trust that, in the end, it will always prevail over deception and lies. It serves as a reminder that no matter how strong or pervasive falsehood may seem, it is inherently weak and destined to disappear when confronted with the light of truth.
orig: وقل جاء الحق وزهق الباطل إن الباطل كان زهوقا

translation: And We send down of the Qur'an that which is healing and mercy for the believers, but it does not increase the wrongdoers except in loss.
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine nature of the Qur'an and its dual effect on people. For the believers, the Qur'an serves as a source of spiritual healing and mercy, providing guidance, comfort, and solace. It helps them navigate through life's challenges and find inner peace. However, for those who are unjust and reject its message, the Qur'an only increases their loss and misery. This is because they choose to turn away from its wisdom and continue in their wrongdoing, which ultimately leads to their own detriment in this world and the hereafter. The verse emphasizes the importance of faith and righteousness in benefiting from the Qur'an's blessings.
orig: وننزل من القرآن ما هو شفاء ورحمة للمؤمنين ولا يزيد الظالمين إلا خسارا

translation: And when We bestow favor upon man, he turns away and distances himself; but when evil touches him, he is ever despairing.
interpretation: This verse highlights the fickle nature of human beings. When God blesses them with favors and bounties, they often become ungrateful and turn away from Him, forgetting that it is He who has bestowed these blessings upon them. They become arrogant and distance themselves from God, thinking that they are self-sufficient and do not need His help. However, when faced with difficulties or hardships, they quickly lose hope and become despaired, forgetting that God is the One who can alleviate their suffering. This verse serves as a reminder for humans to remain grateful to God in times of ease and to turn to Him for help and support during hardships, maintaining a consistent and unwavering faith in His mercy and wisdom.
orig: وإذا أنعمنا على الإنسان أعرض ونأى بجانبه وإذا مسه الشر كان يئوسا

translation: Say, "Each works according to his manner, but your Lord is most knowing of who is best guided in way."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that people act according to their own dispositions and inclinations. However, it is Allah who ultimately knows which path is the most rightly guided. It serves as a reminder that while we may judge others based on their actions and beliefs, true judgment belongs to Allah alone. The verse encourages introspection and humility, acknowledging that we cannot always determine who is on the right path. Instead, we should focus on our own spiritual journey and strive to follow the guidance provided by Allah to the best of our abilities.
orig: قل كل يعمل على شاكلته فربكم أعلم بمن هو أهدى سبيلا

translation: And they ask you, [O Muhammad], about the soul. Say, "The soul is of the affair of my Lord. And mankind have not been given of knowledge except a little."
interpretation: This verse indicates that the true nature and essence of the soul (al-ruh) is a matter that belongs to the realm of God's knowledge alone. Human beings have been granted only a limited amount of knowledge by God, and the soul is a matter that is beyond the grasp of human understanding. The verse emphasizes that there are limits to human knowledge and that one should not delve into matters that have not been made clear by divine revelation. It encourages humility and acceptance that certain aspects of existence, such as the soul, are known only to God.
orig: ويسألونك عن الروح قل الروح من أمر ربي وما أوتيتم من العلم إلا قليلا

translation: And if We willed, We could surely take away that which We have revealed to you. Then you would not find for yourself concerning it an advocate against Us.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute power and control of Allah over the revelation given to Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him). It states that if Allah so willed, He could easily withdraw the revelation from the Prophet, leaving him without divine guidance and support. This highlights the fact that the Qur'an is not the Prophet's own creation, but rather a gift from Allah that can be taken back at any time. The verse also underscores the Prophet's complete dependence on Allah and his role as a mere recipient and conveyer of the divine message. It serves as a reminder to the Prophet and the believers to always remain humble and grateful for the blessing of revelation and to never take it for granted.
orig: ولئن شئنا لنذهبن بالذي أوحينا إليك ثم لا تجد لك به علينا وكيلا

translation: Except for the mercy from your Lord. Indeed, His favor upon you has ever been great.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the immense favor and mercy that Allah has bestowed upon the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him). It suggests that if it were not for Allah's mercy and grace, the Prophet would not have been able to achieve the great heights of spiritual and moral excellence that he did. The verse also implies that the Prophet's success and achievements are ultimately due to Allah's favor and support, rather than his own abilities or efforts alone. This interpretation highlights the importance of recognizing and being grateful for the blessings and guidance that Allah provides to His servants.
orig: إلا رحمة من ربك إن فضله كان عليك كبيرا

translation: Say, "If mankind and the jinn gathered in order to produce the like of this Qur'an, they could not produce the like of it, even if they were to each other assistants."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the miraculous nature and inimitability of the Qur'an. It challenges all of mankind and jinn (spiritual beings), even if they were to work together and assist one another, to produce something equivalent to the Qur'an in terms of its linguistic beauty, profound wisdom, and divine guidance. The verse asserts that the Qur'an is a unique and unparalleled revelation from Allah, and its superiority cannot be matched by any human or spiritual creation. This serves as a testament to the Qur'an's divine origin and its status as the ultimate source of guidance for humanity.
orig: قل لئن اجتمعت الإنس والجن على أن يأتوا بمثل هذا القرآن لا يأتون بمثله ولو كان بعضهم لبعض ظهيرا

translation: And indeed We have put forth for men, in this Quran every kind of similitude, but most men refuse aught but disbelief.
interpretation: This verse highlights the Quran's use of various examples, parables, and analogies to convey its message effectively to humanity. Despite Allah's efforts to make the Quran's teachings clear and relatable, many people still choose to reject faith and resort to disbelief. This suggests that the problem lies not in the clarity of the message but in the stubborn nature of human beings who refuse to accept the truth, even when it is presented to them in the most compelling manner. The verse also implies that the responsibility for accepting or rejecting faith ultimately lies with the individual, as Allah has provided sufficient guidance through the Quran.
orig: ولقد صرفنا للناس في هذا القرآن من كل مثل فأبى أكثر الناس إلا كفورا

translation: And they say, "We will not believe you until you break open for us from the ground a spring."
interpretation: This verse is a response to the disbelievers who demanded that the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) perform miracles to prove his prophethood. They asked him to bring forth a spring from the ground, thinking that this would be an impossible task. The verse highlights their stubbornness and refusal to believe in the message of Islam, even when presented with clear signs and evidence. It also shows that faith is not dependent on witnessing miracles, but rather on understanding and accepting the truth through reason and revelation.
orig: وقالوا لن نؤمن لك حتى تفجر لنا من الأرض ينبوعا

translation: Or you have a garden of date palms and grapes, and cause rivers to gush forth in their midst abundantly.
interpretation: This verse is challenging the disbelievers who demand miracles from the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him). It suggests that even if they were given the miracle of having lush gardens with abundant date palms, grapes, and flowing rivers, they would still not believe. The verse implies that their disbelief is not due to a lack of evidence, but rather due to their stubborn refusal to accept the truth. It also highlights the fact that the ultimate power to create such wonders belongs to Allah alone, and no human being, not even a prophet, can produce them at will. The verse serves as a reminder that true faith is not contingent upon witnessing miracles, but rather on recognizing the signs of Allah's power and wisdom in the world around us.
orig: أو تكون لك جنة من نخيل وعنب فتفجر الأنهار خلالها تفجيرا

translation: Or you cause the sky to fall upon us in fragments as you have claimed, or you bring Allah and the angels before [us]
interpretation: This verse is a challenge to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) from the disbelievers who refused to accept his message. They demanded that he perform impossible miracles to prove his prophethood, such as causing the sky to fall upon them or bringing Allah and the angels before them. The verse highlights their stubborn disbelief and their unwillingness to accept the truth, even if they were presented with clear signs and evidence. It also emphasizes the fact that the Prophet's role was to convey the message, not to perform miracles on demand. Ultimately, it is up to each individual to open their heart to the truth and accept the guidance of Allah.
orig: أو تسقط السماء كما زعمت علينا كسفا أو تأتي بالله والملائكة قبيلا

translation: "Or you have a house of gold or you ascend into the sky. And [even then], we will not believe in your ascension until you bring down to us a book we may read." Say, "Exalted is my Lord! Was I ever but a human messenger?"
interpretation: This verse is addressing the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and the demands made by the disbelievers for him to prove his prophethood. They asked for material miracles, such as a house made of gold or for him to ascend to the heavens and bring back a physical book for them to read. However, the Prophet is instructed to respond with humility, acknowledging that he is only a human messenger and that the ultimate glory belongs to Allah alone. This highlights the fact that the Prophet's role was to convey the message, not to perform supernatural feats on demand. The verse emphasizes the humanity of the Prophet and the supremacy of Allah, while also exposing the stubborn and unreasonable nature of the disbelievers' demands.
orig: أو يكون لك بيت من زخرف أو ترقى في السماء ولن نؤمن لرقيك حتى تنزل علينا كتابا نقرؤه قل سبحان ربي هل كنت إلا بشرا رسولا

translation: And what prevented the people from believing when guidance came to them except that they said, "Has Allah sent a human messenger?"
interpretation: This verse questions the disbelief of people who rejected the prophethood of Muhammad (peace be upon him) on the basis that he was a human being. It implies that their rejection stemmed from their preconceived notion that a messenger of God could not be a mere human, and that this bias prevented them from accepting the divine guidance that the Prophet brought. The verse suggests that there is no valid reason to reject a prophet simply because he is human, as Allah has the power and wisdom to choose whomever He wills as His messenger, regardless of their human status.
orig: وما منع الناس أن يؤمنوا إذ جاءهم الهدى إلا أن قالوا أبعث الله بشرا رسولا

translation: Say, "If there were upon the earth angels walking securely, We would have sent down to them from the heaven an angel [as a] messenger."
interpretation: This verse implies that since the inhabitants of the earth are human beings and not angels, it is befitting that God sends a human messenger to guide them rather than an angel. The verse suggests that the nature of the messenger should correspond to the nature of those being addressed. If the earth were inhabited by angels, then it would be appropriate for God to send an angel as a messenger to them. However, since human beings populate the earth, God has sent human messengers to deliver His message in a way that is relatable and understandable to mankind.
orig: قل لو كان في الأرض ملائكة يمشون مطمئنين لنزلنا عليهم من السماء ملكا رسولا

translation: Say, "Sufficient is Allah as Witness between me and you. Indeed He is ever, concerning His servants, Acquainted and Seeing."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah is the ultimate witness and judge between the Prophet Muhammad and those who reject his message. It reminds us that Allah is fully aware of the actions and intentions of His servants, and that He sees and knows everything. The verse implies that the truth of the Prophet's message will be made clear by Allah Himself, and that those who reject it will be held accountable before Him. It is a powerful statement of Allah's omniscience and justice, and a warning to those who oppose the Prophet and the message of Islam.
orig: قل كفى بالله شهيدا بيني وبينكم إنه كان بعباده خبيرا بصيرا

translation: And whoever Allah guides - he is the [rightly] guided; and whoever He sends astray - you will never find for them protectors besides Him. And We will gather them on the Day of Resurrection [fallen] on their faces - blind, dumb and deaf. Their refuge is Hell; every time it subsides We increase them in blazing fire.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that ultimate guidance and misguidance are in the hands of Allah alone. Those whom Allah guides are truly guided, while those He leaves astray will have no protectors or helpers besides Him. On the Day of Judgment, the misguided will be resurrected in a humiliating state - blind, unable to speak or hear. Their eternal abode will be Hell, where the torment will continuously increase whenever the flames subside. This interpretation highlights the importance of seeking Allah's guidance and the severe consequences of being misguided, which include a disgraceful resurrection and unending punishment in the Hereafter.
orig: ومن يهد الله فهو المهتد ومن يضلل فلن تجد لهم أولياء من دونه ونحشرهم يوم القيامة على وجوههم عميا وبكما وصما مأواهم جهنم كلما خبت زدناهم سعيرا

translation: That is their recompense because they disbelieved in Our verses and said, "When we are bones and crumbled particles, will we [truly] be resurrected as a new creation?"
interpretation: This verse is a warning to those who reject the signs and messages of Allah and deny the possibility of resurrection and the afterlife. It emphasizes that their disbelief and mockery of the concept of being brought back to life after death will lead to severe consequences in the hereafter. The verse implies that the deniers fail to recognize the power and ability of Allah to create and recreate life, and that their skepticism stems from a lack of faith and understanding of the divine wisdom behind the creation of the universe and the purpose of human existence. As a result, they will face the recompense for their disbelief and arrogance in the form of punishment in the afterlife.
orig: ذلك جزاؤهم بأنهم كفروا بآياتنا وقالوا أإذا كنا عظاما ورفاتا أإنا لمبعوثون خلقا جديدا

translation: Do they not see that Allah, who created the heavens and earth, is [the one] Able to create the likes of them? And He has appointed for them a term, about which there is no doubt. But the wrongdoers refuse [anything] except disbelief.
interpretation: This verse points to the immense power and ability of Allah, the Creator of the heavens and the earth. If Allah can create such vast and complex entities, then surely He is more than capable of recreating human beings after their death for the Day of Judgment. Allah has also decreed a fixed term for each person's life and for the coming of the Day of Judgment, which is inevitable and certain. However, despite these clear signs and evidences, the wrongdoers and disbelievers persist in their ingratitude and rejection of faith. They refuse to acknowledge Allah's power, authority and the reality of the afterlife, thus doing injustice to their own souls. The verse emphasizes the stubborn and arrogant nature of disbelief in the face of overwhelming proofs of Allah's existence and abilities.
orig: أولم يروا أن الله الذي خلق السماوات والأرض قادر على أن يخلق مثلهم وجعل لهم أجلا لا ريب فيه فأبى الظالمون إلا كفورا

translation: Say, "If you possessed the depositories of the mercy of my Lord, then you would withhold out of fear of spending." And ever has man been stingy.
interpretation: This verse highlights the innate stinginess and greed of human beings. Even if people were given access to the vast treasures of God's mercy and blessings, they would still hesitate to spend freely out of fear of depleting their resources. This tendency to hoard wealth and be miserly is a common human trait. The verse implies that true generosity and trust in God's providence are qualities that people should strive for, as God's bounty is limitless. It serves as a reminder to overcome the inclination towards greed and to be more charitable, trusting in God's mercy and provision.
orig: قل لو أنتم تملكون خزائن رحمة ربي إذا لأمسكتم خشية الإنفاق وكان الإنسان قتورا

translation: And We had certainly given Moses nine evident signs, so ask the Children of Israel [about] when he came to them and Pharaoh said to him, "Indeed I think, O Moses, that you are affected by magic."
interpretation: This verse highlights the confrontation between Moses and Pharaoh, where despite Moses presenting nine clear miracles as evidence of his prophethood, Pharaoh arrogantly dismissed them as mere magic. This interpretation emphasizes the stubbornness and pride of those in power who refuse to acknowledge the truth, even when faced with overwhelming evidence. It also underscores the importance of faith and perseverance in the face of opposition and disbelief, as exemplified by Moses' unwavering commitment to his divine mission.
orig: ولقد آتينا موسى تسع آيات بينات فاسأل بني إسرائيل إذ جاءهم فقال له فرعون إني لأظنك يا موسى مسحورا

translation: He said, "You have already known that none has sent down these [signs] except the Lord of the heavens and the earth as evidence, and indeed, O Pharaoh, I think that you are destroyed."
interpretation: The verse conveys Moses' firm belief and confidence in the message he was sent with by Allah. He challenges Pharaoh, stating that Pharaoh already knows deep inside that these signs and miracles could only come from the Lord of the heavens and earth as clear proofs of Moses' prophethood. Moses then expresses his conviction that due to Pharaoh's arrogance and denial of the truth, he is doomed to destruction and loss in this life and the Hereafter. It highlights the consequences of rejecting the clear signs of Allah and opposing His messengers.
orig: قال لقد علمت ما أنزل هؤلاء إلا رب السماوات والأرض بصائر وإني لأظنك يا فرعون مثبورا

translation: So he intended to scare them from the land, but We drowned him and those with him all together.
interpretation: This verse is referring to Pharaoh, who wanted to expel Moses and the Children of Israel from Egypt through intimidation and oppression. However, Allah punished Pharaoh for his tyranny and arrogance by drowning him and his army in the sea when they pursued Moses and his people. This demonstrates Allah's power over the oppressors and His support for the oppressed believers. It also serves as a warning to those who reject the truth and persist in wrongdoing, that their end will be destruction and loss in this world and the Hereafter.
orig: فأراد أن يستفزهم من الأرض فأغرقناه ومن معه جميعا

translation: And We said to the Children of Israel after Pharaoh, "Dwell in the land, and when there comes the promise of the Hereafter, We will bring you forth in [one] gathering."
interpretation: This verse is a promise from Allah to the Children of Israel, granting them the right to dwell in the Holy Land after their deliverance from Pharaoh's oppression. It also serves as a reminder that when the Day of Judgment arrives, all people will be gathered together before Allah to face the consequences of their deeds. The verse emphasizes the temporary nature of this worldly life and the importance of preparing for the eternal life in the Hereafter by following Allah's guidance and living righteously.
orig: وقلنا من بعده لبني إسرائيل اسكنوا الأرض فإذا جاء وعد الآخرة جئنا بكم لفيفا

translation: And with the truth We have sent it down (i.e. the Quran), and with the truth it has descended. And We have not sent you (O Muhammad) except as a bearer of glad tidings (of Paradise for those who follow your Message of Islamic Monotheism), and a warner (against Hell for those who refuse to follow your Message of Islamic Monotheism).
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the truthfulness and authenticity of the Quran, as it was sent down by Allah with the truth and it descended with the truth. The role of Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) is also highlighted as a messenger of Allah, whose primary duty is to convey the message of Islam, giving glad tidings of Paradise to those who believe and follow the teachings of Islam, and warning those who reject the message of the consequences of their disbelief, which is the punishment of Hell. The verse underscores the importance of the Quran as a divine revelation and the role of the Prophet in delivering its message to humanity.
orig: وبالحق أنزلناه وبالحق نزل وما أرسلناك إلا مبشرا ونذيرا

translation: And [it is] a Qur'an which We have divided [into parts], in order that you might recite it to men at intervals. And We have revealed it by stages.
interpretation: This verse highlights the gradual revelation of the Qur'an to Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) over a period of 23 years. The Qur'an was not revealed all at once but in stages, allowing the Prophet and his followers to absorb, understand, and implement its teachings gradually. This method of revelation also facilitated the memorization and recitation of the Qur'an, as it was easier to learn and remember smaller portions at a time. The verse emphasizes that the Qur'an is meant to be recited to people at intervals, indicating the importance of its regular recitation and study for spiritual growth and guidance.
orig: وقرآنا فرقناه لتقرأه على الناس على مكث ونزلناه تنزيلا

translation: Say, "Believe in it or do not believe. Indeed, those who were given knowledge before it - when it is recited to them, they fall upon their faces in prostration."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the power and truth of the Qur'an, suggesting that those who possess true knowledge and understanding, particularly those who were given divine knowledge before the revelation of the Qur'an, such as the learned among the People of the Book, readily recognize its authenticity and submit to its message when they hear it recited. Their act of prostration demonstrates their humility, reverence, and acknowledgment of the Qur'an as the word of Allah. The verse also implies that belief in the Qur'an is not dependent on the acceptance or rejection of others, as the truth of its message is self-evident to those with sincere hearts and open minds.
orig: قل آمنوا به أو لا تؤمنوا إن الذين أوتوا العلم من قبله إذا يتلى عليهم يخرون للأذقان سجدا

translation: And they say, "Exalted is our Lord! Indeed, the promise of our Lord has been fulfilled."
interpretation: This verse reflects the believers' acknowledgment and praise of Allah's fulfillment of His promise. It signifies that when the believers witness the realization of Allah's promise, such as the coming of the Day of Judgment or the rewards in Paradise, they will glorify and exalt Him, recognizing His truthfulness and the inevitability of His promise. This verse emphasizes the believers' unwavering faith in Allah's words and their gratitude towards Him for keeping His promise, which strengthens their trust in Him and their hope for the ultimate reward in the Hereafter.
orig: ويقولون سبحان ربنا إن كان وعد ربنا لمفعولا

translation: And they fall upon their faces weeping, and it increases them in humble submission.
interpretation: This verse describes the emotional and spiritual state of the true believers when they hear the words of Allah. They are so moved and humbled by the truth and beauty of the Qur'an that they fall to the ground in prostration, weeping tears of awe, love, and gratitude. This experience of profound reverence and submission to Allah deepens their faith and increases their devotion. It shows that the more they comprehend and internalize the divine message, the more they are inspired to worship and obey their Lord with utmost sincerity and humility.
orig: ويخرون للأذقان يبكون ويزيدهم خشوعا

translation: Say, "Call upon Allah or call upon the Most Merciful. Whichever [name] you call - to Him belong the best names." And do not recite [too] loudly in your prayer or [too] quietly but seek between that an [intermediate] way.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the oneness and unity of God, regardless of the name by which He is invoked. It encourages the believers to call upon Him by any of His beautiful names, as they all refer to the same Supreme Being. Additionally, the verse provides guidance on the manner of prayer, instructing the believers to find a balance between loud and quiet recitation, suggesting that one should pray with humility and sincerity, without drawing attention to oneself or disturbing others. This moderate approach in worship reflects the overall balanced nature of Islam, which discourages extremism in all aspects of life.
orig: قل ادعوا الله أو ادعوا الرحمن أيا ما تدعوا فله الأسماء الحسنى ولا تجهر بصلاتك ولا تخافت بها وابتغ بين ذلك سبيلا

translation: And say, "[All] praise is [due] to Allah, who has not taken a son and has had no partner in [His] dominion and has no [need of a] protector out of weakness; and glorify Him with [great] glorification."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute oneness and uniqueness of Allah. It negates the idea of Allah having a son or partner, affirming His complete sovereignty and power. The verse also highlights Allah's self-sufficiency, indicating that He does not need any protector or helper due to weakness. It concludes by commanding the believers to glorify Allah and magnify Him, acknowledging His perfection and supremacy. This interpretation underscores the Islamic belief in the absolute unity of Allah and His transcendence above all human attributes and limitations.
orig: وقل الحمد لله الذي لم يتخذ ولدا ولم يكن له شريك في الملك ولم يكن له ولي من الذل وكبره تكبيرا

translation: [All] praise is [due] to Allah, who has sent down upon His Servant the Book and has not made therein any deviance.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the Qur'an, revealed to Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him), is a perfect and straightforward book without any contradictions or deviations from the truth. It is a reminder that all praise and gratitude should be directed towards Allah for bestowing this divine guidance upon humanity, which serves as a clear path to righteousness and salvation. The verse also affirms the infallibility and trustworthiness of the Prophet as the recipient and conveyer of Allah's message.
orig: الحمد لله الذي أنزل على عبده الكتاب ولم يجعل له عوجا

translation: That it may give admonition of a severe punishment from Him, and that it may give the believers who do righteous deeds the glad tidings that they shall have a goodly reward.
