interpretation: This verse emphasizes the dual purpose of the Qur'an: to warn those who reject its message of a severe punishment from Allah, and to give glad tidings to the believers who do righteous deeds that they will be rewarded with Paradise. It serves as a reminder that our actions in this world have consequences in the Hereafter, and encourages us to strive for righteousness and obedience to Allah in order to attain His pleasure and the ultimate reward of Paradise.
orig: قيما لينذر بأسا شديدا من لدنه ويبشر المؤمنين الذين يعملون الصالحات أن لهم أجرا حسنا

translation: Abiding therein forever.
interpretation: This verse refers to the eternal fate of those who attain Paradise. It emphasizes that the believers who enter Paradise will remain there permanently, enjoying its endless blessings and delights. The term "abiding" (ماكثين) signifies a state of permanence and stability, indicating that there will be no end to their stay in Paradise. This promise of eternal bliss serves as a motivation for the believers to strive in the path of righteousness and to seek the pleasure of Allah, knowing that their ultimate reward will be an everlasting life of happiness and contentment in the Gardens of Paradise.
orig: ماكثين فيه أبدا

translation: And to warn those who say, "Allah has taken a son"
interpretation: This verse serves as a stern warning to those who falsely attribute a son to Allah, which is a grave sin in Islam. It emphasizes the absolute oneness and uniqueness of Allah, rejecting any notion of Him having offspring or partners. The Qur'an repeatedly stresses that Allah is self-sufficient, eternal, and has no need for a family. Claiming that Allah has a son is considered a major deviation from the core Islamic belief in the unity of God (tawheed) and is tantamount to polytheism (shirk). The verse aims to correct this serious misconception and remind people of Allah's true nature.
orig: وينذر الذين قالوا اتخذ الله ولدا

translation: They have no knowledge of it, nor had their fathers. Grave is the word that comes out of their mouths; they speak not except a lie.
interpretation: This verse criticizes those who make claims about religious matters without having any authentic knowledge or evidence to support their assertions. It suggests that such people, and even their ancestors before them, lack genuine understanding and are merely following conjecture or inherited false notions. The verse emphasizes the seriousness of uttering baseless statements about God or religious truths, considering it a grave sin. It asserts that their words are nothing but lies and fabrications, without any foundation in divine revelation or reason. The verse warns against speaking about religious affairs without proper knowledge and highlights the importance of seeking truth from authentic sources.
orig: ما لهم به من علم ولا لآبائهم كبرت كلمة تخرج من أفواههم إن يقولون إلا كذبا

translation: Then perhaps you would kill yourself through grief over them, [O Muhammad], if they do not believe in this message, [and] out of sorrow.
interpretation: This verse is addressing the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him), consoling him and telling him not to grieve himself to death over the disbelievers who reject the message of Islam. It conveys that the Prophet should not be so distressed and saddened by their disbelief and rejection that it consumes him and destroys his well-being. The verse highlights the deep concern and care that the Prophet had for his people, wanting them to believe and be guided, to the point that their rejection greatly grieved him. However, Allah is telling him to not let it reach the extent of ruining his own health and life. It shows the Prophet's immense compassion, while reassuring him that he has fulfilled his duty of conveying the message, and their choice to believe or not is not his responsibility to bear.
orig: فلعلك باخع نفسك على آثارهم إن لم يؤمنوا بهذا الحديث أسفا

translation: Indeed, We have made that which is on the earth adornment for it that We may test them [as to] which of them is best in deed.
interpretation: This verse suggests that the beauty and bounties of the earth are a test for humanity. God has adorned the world with blessings and attractions to see how people will respond - whether they will be grateful and use these gifts righteously, or become distracted and ungrateful. It is a reminder that the true purpose of our worldly life is not merely to enjoy its fleeting pleasures, but to strive for good deeds and God's pleasure. The best among people are those who maintain a focus on the eternal, even amidst the glitter of the temporal, using the gifts of this life for noble ends. Ultimately, it is the purity of our intentions and actions that will distinguish us in God's eyes, not the extent of our worldly possessions or indulgences.
orig: إنا جعلنا ما على الأرض زينة لها لنبلوهم أيهم أحسن عملا

translation: And indeed, We will make that which is upon it [as] a barren ground.
interpretation: This verse is referring to the Day of Judgment, when Allah will transform the earth into a flat, lifeless, and barren plain, devoid of any vegetation, landmarks, or signs of life. It serves as a reminder that all the worldly possessions, achievements, and adornments that people strive for in this life are ultimately temporary and will be reduced to nothing. The verse encourages believers to focus on the eternal life in the Hereafter rather than being distracted by the fleeting nature of this world.
orig: وإنا لجاعلون ما عليها صعيدا جرزا

translation: Or have you thought that the companions of the cave and the inscription were, among Our signs, a wonder?
interpretation: This verse is drawing the reader's attention to the story of the companions of the cave, suggesting that while their story is indeed wondrous and extraordinary, it is but one of the many signs and marvels of Allah's creation. It implies that one should not be astonished by this particular story as if it were the only amazing sign, because Allah's power and ability to create wonders is infinite and not limited to this one incident. The verse invites reflection on the vast array of Allah's signs in the universe, of which the story of the companions of the cave is just one example, albeit a remarkable one.
orig: أم حسبت أن أصحاب الكهف والرقيم كانوا من آياتنا عجبا

translation: When the youths took refuge in the cave, they said, "Our Lord! Grant us mercy from Yourself, and facilitate for us our affair rightly."
interpretation: This verse refers to the story of the "People of the Cave" or "Seven Sleepers". The interpretation is that when the young believers were facing persecution for their faith, they sought refuge in a cave and prayed to Allah for His mercy and guidance. They put their complete trust in Allah to help them through their difficult situation and guide them to the right course of action. This highlights the importance of turning to Allah in times of hardship, seeking His mercy and guidance, and having faith that He will provide a way out of any difficulty.
orig: إذ أوى الفتية إلى الكهف فقالوا ربنا آتنا من لدنك رحمة وهيئ لنا من أمرنا رشدا

translation: So We cast [a cover of sleep] over their ears within the cave for a number of years.
interpretation: This verse is referring to the story of the People of the Cave (Ashab al-Kahf). According to the Qur'anic narrative, these were a group of young believers who fled persecution and took refuge in a cave. As a means of protecting them, Allah caused them to fall into a deep sleep for a long period of time, rendering them oblivious to the passage of time. This divine intervention allowed them to emerge from the cave much later, unharmed and unaged, as a sign of Allah's power and mercy towards those who remain steadfast in their faith despite facing oppression and hardship.
orig: فضربنا على آذانهم في الكهف سنين عددا

translation: Then We awakened them that We might show which of the two factions was most precise in calculating what [extent] they had remained in time.
interpretation: This verse is referring to the story of the People of the Cave (Ashab al-Kahf). After Allah caused the youths to sleep in the cave for many years, He then awakened them in order to demonstrate His power and to show which group of people was better at estimating the length of time they had stayed in the cave. The verse highlights that there was a difference of opinion about how long they had slept, with some being more accurate in their estimation than others. Ultimately, it was a test from Allah to demonstrate who had stronger faith and trust in His plan, even in the face of an extraordinary and inexplicable situation like sleeping for hundreds of years. The verse emphasizes Allah's control over time and His ability to resurrect and bring back to life.
orig: ثم بعثناهم لنعلم أي الحزبين أحصى لما لبثوا أمدا

translation: We relate to you, [O Muhammad], their story in truth. Indeed, they were youths who believed in their Lord, and We increased them in guidance.
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of faith and belief in Allah, especially during one's youth. It suggests that when young people sincerely believe in God and follow His guidance, He will increase them in their faith and understanding of the truth. This divine guidance and support will help them remain steadfast on the right path, even in the face of challenges or adversities. The verse emphasizes the value of having a strong connection with Allah from an early age, as it can lay the foundation for a life of righteousness and spiritual growth.
orig: نحن نقص عليك نبأهم بالحق إنهم فتية آمنوا بربهم وزدناهم هدى

translation: And We made their hearts firm and strong when they stood up and said: "Our Lord is the Lord of the heavens and the earth, never shall we call upon any ilah (god) other than Him; if we did, we should indeed have uttered an enormity in disbelief.
interpretation: This verse speaks about the unwavering faith and conviction of a group of believers, likely referring to the companions of the cave mentioned in Surah Al-Kahf. Despite the pressures and challenges they faced, they remained steadfast in their belief in the oneness of Allah, refusing to worship any other deity. The verse emphasizes the importance of having a strong faith and the courage to stand up for one's beliefs, even in the face of adversity. It also highlights the gravity of committing shirk (associating partners with Allah), describing it as an "enormity in disbelief." The firm resolve of these believers serves as an example for all Muslims to follow, encouraging them to remain steadfast in their faith and to never compromise their belief in the oneness of Allah.
orig: وربطنا على قلوبهم إذ قاموا فقالوا ربنا رب السماوات والأرض لن ندعو من دونه إلها لقد قلنا إذا شططا

translation: These, our people, have taken gods besides Him. Why do they not bring for [worship of] them a clear authority? And who is more unjust than one who invents about Allah a lie?
interpretation: This verse is a condemnation of those who worship false gods and idols instead of Allah. It suggests that there is no legitimate reason or justification for worshipping these false deities. To invent lies about Allah by claiming that these idols should be worshipped is considered the height of injustice and wrongdoing. The implication is that Allah alone is worthy of worship, and attributing divine status to anything else based on falsehoods is a grave sin.
orig: هؤلاء قومنا اتخذوا من دونه آلهة لولا يأتون عليهم بسلطان بين فمن أظلم ممن افترى على الله كذبا

translation: And when you have withdrawn from them and that which they worship other than Allah, retreat to the cave. Your Lord will spread out for you of His mercy and will prepare for you from your affair facility.
interpretation: This verse is advising believers to seek refuge in Allah and withdraw from those who worship others besides Him. It promises that if they do so, Allah will bestow His mercy upon them and make their affairs easy. The "cave" mentioned could be interpreted metaphorically as a place of spiritual retreat and connection with Allah, away from worldly distractions and false worship. By putting their trust in Allah alone, believers will be granted divine support and provisions to facilitate their path.
orig: وإذ اعتزلتموهم وما يعبدون إلا الله فأووا إلى الكهف ينشر لكم ربكم من رحمته ويهيئ لكم من أمركم مرفقا

translation: And you would have seen the sun when it rose, inclining away from their cave on the right, and when it set, passing away from them on the left, while they were [laying] within an open space thereof. That was from the signs of Allah. He whom Allah guides is the [rightly] guided, but he whom He leaves astray - never will you find for him a protecting guide.
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine protection and guidance that Allah bestows upon those He chooses. The positioning of the sun in relation to the cave where the companions of the cave were sleeping demonstrates Allah's power over the natural world and His ability to shield His servants from harm. The verse emphasizes that true guidance comes only from Allah, and those whom He guides are on the right path. Conversely, those whom Allah leaves astray will not find anyone to guide them aright, as ultimate guidance is solely in His hands. This serves as a reminder for believers to seek Allah's guidance and protection in all aspects of their lives.
orig: وترى الشمس إذا طلعت تزاور عن كهفهم ذات اليمين وإذا غربت تقرضهم ذات الشمال وهم في فجوة منه ذلك من آيات الله من يهد الله فهو المهتد ومن يضلل فلن تجد له وليا مرشدا

translation: And you would think them awake, while they were asleep. And We turned them to the right and to the left, while their dog stretched his forelegs at the entrance. If you had looked at them, you would have turned from them in flight and been filled by them with terror.
interpretation: This verse is describing the story of the people of the cave, who were a group of believers that fled persecution and took refuge in a cave. Allah caused them to sleep for a long time, and protected them during their sleep. The verse emphasizes the power and protection of Allah, as He kept them safe and made them appear as if they were awake, while they were actually in a deep sleep. Their dog, who was guarding the entrance of the cave, is also mentioned as a sign of Allah's protection. The verse also highlights the fear and awe that one would feel if they saw this scene, as it is a manifestation of Allah's might and power.
orig: وتحسبهم أيقاظا وهم رقود ونقلبهم ذات اليمين وذات الشمال وكلبهم باسط ذراعيه بالوصيد لو اطلعت عليهم لوليت منهم فرارا ولملئت منهم رعبا

translation: And similarly, We awakened them that they might question one another. Said a speaker from among them, "How long have you remained [here]?" They said, "We have remained a day or part of a day." They said, "Your Lord is most knowing of how long you remained. So send one of you with this silver coin of yours to the city and let him look to which is the best of food and bring you provision from it and let him be cautious. And let no one be aware of you.
interpretation: This verse is referring to the story of the People of the Cave (Ashab al-Kahf). It highlights the wisdom and power of Allah in putting them to sleep for a long period of time and then waking them up. The verse emphasizes the importance of relying on Allah's knowledge and wisdom, as the people of the cave themselves were unsure of how long they had slept. It also teaches the importance of caution and discretion when in a vulnerable position, as they were instructed to send one of their members to the city carefully and discreetly to acquire provisions. Overall, this verse serves as a reminder of Allah's control over all affairs and the importance of putting one's trust in Him.
orig: وكذلك بعثناهم ليتساءلوا بينهم قال قائل منهم كم لبثتم قالوا لبثنا يوما أو بعض يوم قالوا ربكم أعلم بما لبثتم فابعثوا أحدكم بورقكم هذه إلى المدينة فلينظر أيها أزكى طعاما فليأتكم برزق منه وليتلطف ولا يشعرن بكم أحدا

translation: Indeed, if they come to know of you, they will stone you or return you to their religion. And never would you succeed, then - ever.
interpretation: This verse warns the believers of the grave consequences they would face if their enemies were to gain the upper hand over them. It suggests that the disbelievers would not hesitate to persecute the Muslims, either by physically assaulting them (stoning) or by forcing them to abandon their faith and revert to the religion of their ancestors. The verse emphasizes that succumbing to such pressure would lead to eternal failure and loss in the Hereafter, as apostasy is an unforgivable sin if one dies in that state. Thus, it serves as a reminder for the believers to remain steadfast in their faith, even in the face of severe opposition and threats, and to trust in Allah's protection and guidance.
orig: إنهم إن يظهروا عليكم يرجموكم أو يعيدوكم في ملتهم ولن تفلحوا إذا أبدا

translation: And similarly, We caused them to be found that they [who found them] would know that the promise of Allah is truth and that of the Hour there is no doubt. [That was] when they disputed among themselves about their affair and [then] said, "Construct over them a structure. Their Lord is most knowing about them." Said those who prevailed in the matter, "We will surely take [for ourselves] over them a masjid."
interpretation: This verse is highlighting the story of the People of the Cave (Ashab al-Kahf), who were a group of young believers who took refuge in a cave to escape persecution. Allah caused them to sleep for a long period of time and then made them to be discovered by the people of a later generation. The purpose of this was to demonstrate that Allah's promise of resurrection and the coming of the Hour (Day of Judgment) is true and there should be no doubt about it. The people who discovered them argued about what to do with them, with some suggesting to build a structure over them. But those who prevailed in the end decided to build a place of worship (masjid) at the site to commemorate their faith and as a reminder of the truth of the Hereafter.
orig: وكذلك أعثرنا عليهم ليعلموا أن وعد الله حق وأن الساعة لا ريب فيها إذ يتنازعون بينهم أمرهم فقالوا ابنوا عليهم بنيانا ربهم أعلم بهم قال الذين غلبوا على أمرهم لنتخذن عليهم مسجدا

translation: They will say there were three, the fourth of them being their dog; and they will say there were five, the sixth of them being their dog - guessing at the unseen; and they will say there were seven, and the eighth of them was their dog. Say, "My Lord is most knowing of their number. None knows them except a few. So do not argue about them except with an obvious argument and do not inquire about them among [the speculators] from anyone."
interpretation: This verse is referring to the story of the People of the Cave, a group of young believers who took refuge in a cave to escape religious persecution. The exact number of the people is not known, and the verse mentions the various speculations people made about their number, ranging from three to seven, with their dog being counted as an additional member. The verse emphasizes that the true knowledge of their number rests with Allah alone, and that arguing about it is futile. It also discourages seeking information about the People of the Cave from those who speculate without knowledge. The message is to focus on the lessons and wisdom from the story, rather than indulging in unnecessary debates about the details that Allah has chosen not to reveal.
orig: سيقولون ثلاثة رابعهم كلبهم ويقولون خمسة سادسهم كلبهم رجما بالغيب ويقولون سبعة وثامنهم كلبهم قل ربي أعلم بعدتهم ما يعلمهم إلا قليل فلا تمار فيهم إلا مراء ظاهرا ولا تستفت فيهم منهم أحدا

translation: And never say of anything, "Indeed, I will do that tomorrow,"
interpretation: This verse reminds us that we should not be arrogant or overconfident about our plans for the future. It emphasizes the importance of acknowledging Allah's will and recognizing that ultimately, He is in control of all things. We should always say "InshaAllah" (God willing) when speaking about our future intentions, as a way of submitting to Allah's decree and recognizing that our plans may not always come to fruition without His permission. This verse encourages humility, mindfulness, and a constant awareness of our dependence on Allah in all aspects of life.
orig: ولا تقولن لشيء إني فاعل ذلك غدا

translation: Except as Allah wills. And remember your Lord when you forget [it] and say, "Perhaps my Lord will guide me to what is nearer than this to right conduct."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of remembering Allah and seeking His guidance, especially in moments of forgetfulness or weakness. It encourages the believer to turn to Allah for direction and support, acknowledging that He alone can guide us to the most righteous path. The verse also highlights the concept of divine will and the believer's submission to it, recognizing that ultimately, everything happens by the will of Allah. It serves as a reminder to constantly strive for self-improvement and to rely on Allah's guidance in all aspects of life.
orig: إلا أن يشاء الله واذكر ربك إذا نسيت وقل عسى أن يهدين ربي لأقرب من هذا رشدا

translation: And they remained in their cave for three hundred years and increased by nine.
interpretation: This verse refers to the story of the People of the Cave (known as "The Seven Sleepers" in some traditions), who were a group of young believers that fled persecution and took refuge in a cave, where Allah caused them to sleep for a long period of time. The exact duration of their stay is mentioned here as 309 years (300 solar years which equal 309 lunar years). This long period emphasizes Allah's power over life and death, and how He can easily resurrect people even after a long time. It also highlights the relativity of time; what seemed like a short nap to the People of the Cave was actually centuries. This story encourages believers to have faith in Allah's protection and in the Day of Resurrection.
orig: ولبثوا في كهفهم ثلاث مائة سنين وازدادوا تسعا

translation: Say, "Allah is most knowing of how long they remained. He has [knowledge of] the unseen [aspects] of the heavens and the earth. How Seeing is He and how Hearing! They have not besides Him any protector, and He shares not His legislation with anyone."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's complete knowledge and power over all things. It asserts that only Allah knows the duration of time that has passed or will pass, as He alone has knowledge of the unseen in the heavens and earth. The verse also highlights Allah's perfect sight and hearing, implying that nothing escapes His awareness. Furthermore, it states that no one besides Allah can provide protection or guidance to humans, and that Allah does not share His authority or judgment with anyone. This interpretation underscores the fundamental Islamic belief in Allah's oneness, omniscience, and sovereignty.
orig: قل الله أعلم بما لبثوا له غيب السماوات والأرض أبصر به وأسمع ما لهم من دونه من ولي ولا يشرك في حكمه أحدا

translation: And recite what has been revealed to you of the Book of your Lord. There is no changer of His words, and never will you find in other than Him a refuge.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the immutability and permanence of Allah's words and message in the Qur'an. It instructs the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and, by extension, all believers to recite and adhere to the divine revelation, as it remains unchanged and unaltered. The verse also highlights the fact that only Allah can provide true protection and refuge, and that seeking help or support from anyone or anything else is futile. This interpretation underscores the importance of relying solely on Allah and His guidance, as provided in the Qur'an, and serves as a reminder of His power and sovereignty over all things.
orig: واتل ما أوحي إليك من كتاب ربك لا مبدل لكلماته ولن تجد من دونه ملتحدا

translation: And keep yourself patient [by being] with those who call upon their Lord in the morning and the evening, seeking His countenance. And let not your eyes pass beyond them, desiring adornments of the worldly life, and do not obey one whose heart We have made heedless of Our remembrance and who follows his desire and whose affair is ever [in] neglect.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of keeping company with righteous people who constantly remember Allah and seek His pleasure, rather than being distracted by the temporary allures of this worldly life. It warns against following those who are heedless of Allah's remembrance and have succumbed to their desires, as their affairs are in a state of neglect and loss. The verse encourages the Prophet (ﷺ) and the believers to remain patient and steadfast in the company of the righteous, focusing on the eternal rewards of the Hereafter rather than the fleeting pleasures of this world.
orig: واصبر نفسك مع الذين يدعون ربهم بالغداة والعشي يريدون وجهه ولا تعد عيناك عنهم تريد زينة الحياة الدنيا ولا تطع من أغفلنا قلبه عن ذكرنا واتبع هواه وكان أمره فرطا

translation: And say, "The truth is from your Lord, so whoever wills - let him believe; and whoever wills - let him disbelieve." Indeed, We have prepared for the wrongdoers a fire whose walls will surround them. And if they call for relief, they will be relieved with water like murky oil, which scalds [their] faces. Wretched is the drink, and evil is the resting place.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the freedom of choice that Allah has granted to human beings. They can choose to believe in the truth that comes from Allah or reject it. However, those who reject the truth and wrong themselves will face severe consequences in the form of Hell-fire. The verse graphically describes the punishment of Hell, where the disbelievers will be surrounded by flames and given boiling water to drink that will scald their faces. This highlights the severity and permanence of the punishment for those who reject Allah's message. The verse serves as a strong warning to those who disbelieve, urging them to make the right choice and accept the truth before it is too late.
orig: وقل الحق من ربكم فمن شاء فليؤمن ومن شاء فليكفر إنا أعتدنا للظالمين نارا أحاط بهم سرادقها وإن يستغيثوا يغاثوا بماء كالمهل يشوي الوجوه بئس الشراب وساءت مرتفقا

translation: Indeed, those who believe and do righteous deeds - indeed, We will not allow to be lost the reward of any who did well in deeds.
interpretation: This verse assures believers that Allah will not let their good deeds go to waste. Those who have faith and do righteous actions can be certain that Allah will reward them for their efforts. It emphasizes the importance of both belief and good deeds, showing that they are inextricably linked. The verse also highlights Allah's justice and mercy, as He promises not to neglect the reward of anyone who does well, no matter how small their deeds may seem. This serves as an encouragement for believers to persist in doing good, knowing that their efforts will be recognized and rewarded by Allah.
orig: إن الذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات إنا لا نضيع أجر من أحسن عملا

translation: Those will have gardens of perpetual residence; beneath them rivers will flow. They will be adorned therein with bracelets of gold and will wear green garments of fine silk and brocade, reclining therein on adorned couches. Excellent is the reward, and good is the resting place.
interpretation: This verse describes the eternal reward that awaits the righteous believers in Paradise. It paints a vivid picture of the luxuries and comforts they will enjoy, such as wearing fine garments, being adorned with gold bracelets, and reclining on beautiful couches in lush gardens with flowing rivers. The verse emphasizes that this is an excellent reward from Allah and a wonderful place of rest and repose for those who have lived a life of faith and good deeds. It serves as a reminder and motivation for believers to strive for this ultimate goal in the Hereafter.
orig: أولئك لهم جنات عدن تجري من تحتهم الأنهار يحلون فيها من أساور من ذهب ويلبسون ثيابا خضرا من سندس وإستبرق متكئين فيها على الأرائك نعم الثواب وحسنت مرتفقا

translation: And present to them an example of two men: We granted to one of them two gardens of grapevines, and We bordered them with palm trees and placed between them [fields of] crops.
interpretation: This verse presents a parable to illustrate the contrast between a grateful believer and an ungrateful disbeliever. The two gardens of grapevines symbolize the blessings and bounties that Allah bestows upon His servants. The palm trees and crops surrounding the gardens represent the additional favors and provisions that complement the main blessings. The parable suggests that the believer recognizes these blessings as gifts from Allah and expresses gratitude, while the disbeliever fails to acknowledge the true source of these favors and becomes arrogant and ungrateful. The verse emphasizes the importance of recognizing and appreciating the blessings that Allah grants us in this life, and the consequences of either gratitude or ingratitude in the Hereafter.
orig: واضرب لهم مثلا رجلين جعلنا لأحدهما جنتين من أعناب وحففناهما بنخل وجعلنا بينهما زرعا

translation: Each of the two gardens brought forth its produce, and did not fall short thereof in anything. And We caused a river to gush forth in their midst.
interpretation: This verse speaks to the abundance and prosperity that Allah bestows upon those who are righteous and follow His path. The two gardens mentioned here are metaphors for the blessings and bounties, both material and spiritual, that Allah grants to the believers. The fact that each garden yielded its fruits without fail and that a river flowed between them signifies the constancy and continuity of Allah's favors. It also suggests that when we align our lives with Allah's will and obey His commands, He will provide for us from sources we could never imagine and remove any barriers that hinder our progress. The gushing river can be seen as a symbol of the knowledge, wisdom, and guidance that Allah causes to spring forth in the hearts of the believers, nourishing their souls and helping them grow in faith and righteousness.
orig: كلتا الجنتين آتت أكلها ولم تظلم منه شيئا وفجرنا خلالهما نهرا

translation: And he had fruit, so he said to his companion while he was conversing with him, "I am greater than you in wealth and mightier in [numbers of] men."
interpretation: This verse is a reminder that worldly possessions and status are temporary and can lead to arrogance and a false sense of superiority over others. The person in the verse boasts about his wealth and the number of people under his command, thinking that these things make him better than his companion. However, true worth is not measured by material possessions or social status, but by one's faith, good deeds, and humility before God. The verse serves as a warning against letting worldly success and power lead to pride and a lack of gratitude towards the One who bestowed these blessings.
orig: وكان له ثمر فقال لصاحبه وهو يحاوره أنا أكثر منك مالا وأعز نفرا

translation: And he entered his garden while he was unjust to himself. He said, "I do not think that this will perish - ever."
interpretation: This verse is a warning against arrogance and self-delusion. The man, blinded by his wealth and status, enters his garden feeling invincible, believing that his prosperity will last forever. He fails to acknowledge that all blessings come from Allah and can be taken away at any moment. His statement "I do not think that this will perish - ever" reflects his lack of humility and gratitude towards his Creator. It serves as a reminder for believers to always remain humble, grateful, and mindful that everything in this world is temporary, and that ultimate success lies in the hereafter through obedience to Allah.
orig: ودخل جنته وهو ظالم لنفسه قال ما أظن أن تبيد هذه أبدا

translation: And I do not think the Hour will occur. And even if I should be brought back to my Lord, I will surely find better than this as a return.
interpretation: This verse reflects the disbelief and arrogance of those who deny the Day of Judgment and the Hereafter. They assume that even if there were an afterlife, they would be entitled to a better fate than what they have in this world. This mindset stems from their lack of faith in Allah's justice and their failure to recognize the temporary nature of worldly pleasures. The verse serves as a warning against such misguided thinking and emphasizes the importance of believing in and preparing for the inevitable reality of the Day of Judgment.
orig: وما أظن الساعة قائمة ولئن رددت إلى ربي لأجدن خيرا منها منقلبا

translation: His companion said to him while he was conversing with him, "Have you disbelieved in He who created you from dust and then from a sperm-drop and then proportioned you [as] a man?"
interpretation: This verse is a reminder of the power and wisdom of Allah in creating human beings. It emphasizes that Allah created us from a humble beginning, starting with dust, then a sperm-drop, and finally shaping us into our human form. The companion in the verse is questioning the disbelief of the person he is conversing with, despite the clear signs of Allah's creation in his own existence. This serves as a powerful reminder for all of us to reflect on our own origins and the immense favor of Allah in granting us life and guiding us to faith. It encourages humility, gratitude, and a deeper connection with our Creator.
orig: قال له صاحبه وهو يحاوره أكفرت بالذي خلقك من تراب ثم من نطفة ثم سواك رجلا

translation: But for me, Allah is my Lord, and I do not associate anyone with my Lord.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of pure monotheism in Islam. The speaker affirms that Allah alone is their Lord and that they do not ascribe any partners or equals to Him. It is a declaration of complete devotion and submission to the oneness of Allah, rejecting any form of polytheism or idolatry. This unwavering belief in the unity of Allah is the foundation of the Islamic faith, and it is incumbent upon every Muslim to uphold this principle in their worship and daily lives.
orig: لكنا هو الله ربي ولا أشرك بربي أحدا

translation: And why did you, when you entered your garden, not say, 'What Allah willed [has occurred]; there is no power except in Allah'? Although you see me less than you in wealth and children.
interpretation: This verse is a reminder that all blessings and possessions come from Allah alone. When one is blessed with wealth, success, or any other favors, they should acknowledge that it is solely by the will and power of Allah. Saying "What Allah willed has occurred" is an expression of humility, gratitude, and submission to the Almighty. It serves as a protection against arrogance and self-admiration, which can lead to one's downfall. The verse also emphasizes that true power and strength belong to Allah alone, and that worldly possessions such as wealth and children should not be a source of pride or a means to look down upon others who may have less. Instead, one should remain humble and grateful for whatever Allah has bestowed upon them.
orig: ولولا إذ دخلت جنتك قلت ما شاء الله لا قوة إلا بالله إن ترن أنا أقل منك مالا وولدا

translation: It may be that my Lord will give me [something] better than your garden and will send upon it a calamity from the sky, and it will become a smooth, dusty ground,
interpretation: This verse can be interpreted as a reminder that everything in this world is temporary and can be taken away in an instant. It emphasizes the power and control of Allah over all things, and suggests that one should not become too attached to worldly possessions or status. The verse implies that even the most beautiful and prosperous gardens can be reduced to barren, lifeless land if Allah wills it. It serves as a warning against arrogance and a call to humility and gratitude for the blessings we have been given, while recognizing that they are ultimately fleeting and dependent on Allah's mercy.
orig: فعسى ربي أن يؤتين خيرا من جنتك ويرسل عليها حسبانا من السماء فتصبح صعيدا زلقا

translation: Or its water sinks [into the earth], so you would never be able to seek it.
interpretation: This verse is a reminder of the transient nature of worldly blessings and the ultimate dependence on Allah. It suggests that even if one has access to abundant resources, such as water, these blessings can easily disappear or become inaccessible. The sinking of water into the earth symbolizes the loss of a vital resource, emphasizing the helplessness of humans in the face of such events. The verse implies that one should not become overly attached to worldly possessions or take them for granted, as they can be taken away at any moment by Allah's will. Instead, one should focus on building a strong spiritual connection with Allah and seeking His guidance and mercy, which are the only true and lasting sources of sustenance and support.
orig: أو يصبح ماؤها غورا فلن تستطيع له طلبا

translation: And his fruits were encompassed [by ruin], so he began to turn his hands about [in dismay] over what he had spent on it, while it had collapsed upon its trellises, and said, "Oh, I wish I had not associated with my Lord anyone."
interpretation: This verse is a reminder that all the wealth and possessions we accumulate in this world are temporary and can be taken away from us at any moment. The man in the verse had invested heavily in his garden, but it was all destroyed in an instant. In his despair, he realizes his mistake of associating partners with Allah and wishes he had been a true believer. It emphasizes the importance of putting our trust in Allah alone and not being distracted by worldly pursuits that can lead us astray from the path of righteousness. Ultimately, it is only our faith and good deeds that will benefit us in the Hereafter.
orig: وأحيط بثمره فأصبح يقلب كفيه على ما أنفق فيها وهي خاوية على عروشها ويقول يا ليتني لم أشرك بربي أحدا

translation: And he had no company to help him other than Allah, nor could he defend himself.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the ultimate helplessness and vulnerability of human beings without the support and guidance of Allah. It suggests that no matter how powerful or influential a person may seem, they are ultimately dependent on Allah's will and cannot succeed or protect themselves without His aid. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of humility, submission, and reliance on Allah, as even the mightiest of individuals are powerless without Him.
orig: ولم تكن له فئة ينصرونه من دون الله وما كان منتصرا

translation: There, the [true] authority is [completely] for Allah, the Truth. He is best in reward and best in outcome.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that ultimate authority and judgment belong solely to Allah, who is the absolute Truth. It reminds believers that seeking Allah's pleasure and striving for His cause will lead to the best rewards in this life and the hereafter. The verse encourages Muslims to prioritize their actions and decisions based on what pleases Allah, rather than worldly gains or temporary benefits, as Allah's judgment and rewards are far superior and everlasting compared to the fleeting nature of this world.
orig: هنالك الولاية لله الحق هو خير ثوابا وخير عقبا

translation: And present to them the example of the life of this world, [its being] like rain which We send down from the sky, and the vegetation of the earth mingles with it and [then] it becomes dry remnants, scattered by the winds. And Allah is ever, over all things, Perfect in Ability.
interpretation: This verse is a reminder of the fleeting nature of worldly life. It compares the life of this world to vegetation that grows after rainfall, only to wither away and be scattered by the winds. This symbolizes how the pleasures and attachments of this world are temporary and will ultimately fade away. The verse emphasizes that Allah has power over all things, including the transient nature of worldly life. It serves as a reminder for believers to focus on the eternal life of the hereafter rather than being consumed by the fleeting nature of this world.
orig: واضرب لهم مثل الحياة الدنيا كماء أنزلناه من السماء فاختلط به نبات الأرض فأصبح هشيما تذروه الرياح وكان الله على كل شيء مقتدرا

translation: Wealth and children are [but] adornment of the worldly life. But the enduring good deeds are better to your Lord for reward and better for [one's] hope.
interpretation: This verse reminds us that worldly possessions and offspring, while desirable, are ultimately fleeting adornments of this temporary life. True and lasting value lies in good deeds that are pleasing to Allah. These righteous actions, such as prayer, charity, and kindness, bring us closer to our Lord and give us hope for His eternal rewards in the Hereafter. The verse encourages believers to prioritize their spiritual well-being over material pursuits, as the former has far greater significance in the grand scheme of existence.
orig: المال والبنون زينة الحياة الدنيا والباقيات الصالحات خير عند ربك ثوابا وخير أملا

translation: And [warn of] the Day when We will remove the mountains and you will see the earth prominent, and We will gather them and not leave behind from them anyone.
interpretation: This verse is referring to the Day of Judgment, when the world as we know it will be utterly transformed. The mountains, which seem so permanent and immovable, will be swept away, and the earth will be laid bare, with nothing to hide or obscure. All of humanity, from the first to the last, will be gathered together, and not a single soul will be left behind or forgotten. It is a reminder of the awesome power of God and the inevitability of the final reckoning that all will face. The verse emphasizes the completeness and comprehensiveness of the gathering, highlighting that absolutely no one will be exempt from standing before God for judgment on that immense and momentous Day.
orig: ويوم نسير الجبال وترى الأرض بارزة وحشرناهم فلم نغادر منهم أحدا

translation: And they will be presented before your Lord in rows, [and He will say], "You have certainly come to Us just as We created you the first time. But you claimed that We would never make for you an appointment."
interpretation: This verse refers to the Day of Judgment when all of humanity will be brought before Allah (SWT) in rows. Allah will remind them that they have returned to Him in the same state as when He first created them, with nothing of the worldly possessions they had acquired. This is a rebuke to those who denied the resurrection and the appointed time when they would be held accountable for their deeds. It serves as a reminder that the life of this world is temporary and that our ultimate return is to Allah, who will judge us based on our faith and actions.
orig: وعرضوا على ربك صفا لقد جئتمونا كما خلقناكم أول مرة بل زعمتم ألن نجعل لكم موعدا

translation: And the record [of deeds] will be placed [open], and you will see the criminals fearful of that within it, and they will say, "Oh, woe to us! What is this book that leaves nothing small or great except that it has enumerated it?" And they will find what they did present [before them]. And your Lord does not wrong anyone.
interpretation: This verse speaks about the Day of Judgment when the record of every person's deeds will be presented before them. The criminals, upon seeing their record, will be shocked and fearful because the record is comprehensive and leaves out nothing, big or small. They will regret their actions and realize the gravity of their situation. The verse emphasizes the concept of individual accountability and divine justice. It highlights that on the Day of Judgment, everyone will find their deeds presented before them, and God Almighty will not wrong anyone. This serves as a reminder for people to be mindful of their actions in this world, as they will be held accountable for them in the Hereafter.
orig: ووضع الكتاب فترى المجرمين مشفقين مما فيه ويقولون يا ويلتنا مال هذا الكتاب لا يغادر صغيرة ولا كبيرة إلا أحصاها ووجدوا ما عملوا حاضرا ولا يظلم ربك أحدا

translation: And [mention] when We said to the angels, "Prostrate to Adam," and they prostrated, except for Iblees. He was of the jinn and departed from the command of his Lord. Then will you take him and his descendants as allies other than Me while they are enemies to you? Wretched it is for the wrongdoers as an exchange.
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of obedience to Allah and the consequences of disobedience. Iblees' refusal to prostrate to Adam, despite Allah's command, demonstrates arrogance and rebellion. The verse warns against taking Iblees and his descendants (i.e., the devils) as allies instead of Allah, emphasizing that they are our enemies. It also underscores the foolishness of those who choose to follow the path of Iblees, as they are ultimately wronging themselves by exchanging the guidance and protection of Allah for the deception of His enemies.
orig: وإذ قلنا للملائكة اسجدوا لآدم فسجدوا إلا إبليس كان من الجن ففسق عن أمر ربه أفتتخذونه وذريته أولياء من دوني وهم لكم عدو بئس للظالمين بدلا

translation: I did not make them witness to the creation of the heavens and the earth or to the creation of themselves, and I would not have taken the misguiders as assistants.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah alone is the Creator of the heavens and the earth, and that He did not seek the assistance or witness of any of His creation in the process. It also affirms that Allah would never appoint those who misguide others as His helpers or supporters. The verse underscores Allah's omnipotence, self-sufficiency, and wisdom in creating and managing the universe independently, without relying on anyone, especially those who lead others astray from the right path.
orig: ما أشهدتهم خلق السماوات والأرض ولا خلق أنفسهم وما كنت متخذ المضلين عضدا

translation: And [warn of] the Day when He will say, "Call 'upon' those you claimed to be My partners," and they will invoke them, but they will not respond to them. And We will put between them [a valley of] destruction.
interpretation: This verse is a warning about the Day of Judgment, when Allah will challenge the disbelievers to call upon the false deities they associated with Him. The idols and false gods will be unable to respond or help them in any way. Allah emphasizes the complete separation and estrangement between the disbelievers and their supposed partners, symbolized by the "valley of destruction" placed between them. This interpretation highlights the futility of worshipping anyone or anything besides Allah and the severe consequences of doing so on the Day of Judgment.
orig: ويوم يقول نادوا شركائي الذين زعمتم فدعوهم فلم يستجيبوا لهم وجعلنا بينهم موبقا

translation: And the criminals will see the Fire and will be certain that they are to fall into it. And they will not find from it a way elsewhere.
interpretation: This verse speaks to the fate of those who have committed grave sins and rejected faith in God. When they are confronted with the reality of Hell on the Day of Judgment, they will realize with certainty that this is their destined abode as a consequence of their actions. The description of them not finding "a way elsewhere" emphasizes the finality and inescapability of God's judgment. It serves as a severe warning to all of mankind that we must be conscious of God and strive to live righteously, or else we will face this terrifying end with no possibility of reprieve or redirection. The verse instills a sense of urgency to repent and align ourselves with God's path before it is too late.
orig: ورأى المجرمون النار فظنوا أنهم مواقعوها ولم يجدوا عنها مصرفا

translation: And indeed We have put forth for men, in this Quran every kind of similitude, but man is, in most things, contentious.
interpretation: This verse highlights the Qur'an's use of various examples, parables, and analogies to convey its message effectively to humanity. Despite God's efforts to make the Qur'an's teachings clear and relatable, human beings often engage in unnecessary arguments and disputes. This tendency to be contentious and argumentative is a common human trait that hinders their ability to grasp and accept the truth. The verse serves as a reminder for people to approach the Qur'an with an open mind and heart, focusing on understanding its wisdom rather than engaging in fruitless debates.
orig: ولقد صرفنا في هذا القرآن للناس من كل مثل وكان الإنسان أكثر شيء جدلا

translation: And nothing has prevented the people from believing when guidance came to them and from asking forgiveness of their Lord except that there [must] befall them the [accustomed] precedent of the former peoples or that the punishment should come [directly] before them.
interpretation: This verse highlights the stubborn nature of those who reject faith despite receiving clear guidance. It suggests that people often refuse to believe and seek forgiveness from Allah due to their expectation that they will face the same fate as earlier nations who were punished for their disbelief, or because they are waiting to witness the punishment with their own eyes before believing. This attitude reflects a lack of sincerity and a failure to recognize the truth when it is presented to them, as they prioritize their own desires and preconceptions over the clear signs and warnings sent by Allah.
orig: وما منع الناس أن يؤمنوا إذ جاءهم الهدى ويستغفروا ربهم إلا أن تأتيهم سنة الأولين أو يأتيهم العذاب قبلا

translation: And We send not the Messengers except as bearers of good news and warners. And those who disbelieve dispute with falsehood in order to refute the truth thereby. And they take My signs and what they are warned of in mockery.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the role of the prophets and messengers as conveying both good news and warnings to humanity. However, those who reject faith resort to false arguments and deception in an attempt to undermine the truth. They mock and ridicule the divine revelations and the warnings they receive, failing to take them seriously. This behavior reflects their arrogance and their unwillingness to accept the guidance provided by God through His messengers.
orig: وما نرسل المرسلين إلا مبشرين ومنذرين ويجادل الذين كفروا بالباطل ليدحضوا به الحق واتخذوا آياتي وما أنذروا هزوا

translation: And who is more unjust than one who is reminded of the verses of his Lord but turns away from them and forgets what his hands have put forth? Indeed, We have placed over their hearts coverings, lest they understand it, and in their ears deafness. And if you invite them to guidance - they will never be guided, then - ever.
interpretation: This verse highlights the severity of turning away from Allah's guidance after being reminded of it. Those who reject the truth and persist in disbelief, despite the clear signs and reminders, are considered the most unjust. As a consequence of their choice, Allah places a barrier over their hearts and deafness in their ears, making it difficult for them to understand and accept the truth. Even if they are invited to the right path, their persistent denial will prevent them from being guided. This emphasizes the importance of being receptive to divine guidance and the consequences of turning away from it.
orig: ومن أظلم ممن ذكر بآيات ربه فأعرض عنها ونسي ما قدمت يداه إنا جعلنا على قلوبهم أكنة أن يفقهوه وفي آذانهم وقرا وإن تدعهم إلى الهدى فلن يهتدوا إذا أبدا

translation: And your Lord is the Forgiving, the possessor of mercy. If He were to impose blame upon them for what they earned, He would have hastened for them the punishment. Rather, for them is an appointment from which they will never find an escape.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's infinite mercy and forgiveness towards His creation. Despite the sins and shortcomings of human beings, Allah does not punish them immediately for their misdeeds. Instead, out of His compassion, He gives them respite and opportunities to repent and mend their ways. However, this verse also serves as a warning that there will come a time when people will face the consequences of their actions, and on that promised Day of Judgment, they will have no refuge or escape from Allah's justice. The verse encourages introspection and turning to Allah in repentance while the door of mercy is still open.
orig: وربك الغفور ذو الرحمة لو يؤاخذهم بما كسبوا لعجل لهم العذاب بل لهم موعد لن يجدوا من دونه موئلا

translation: And those cities - We destroyed them when they wronged, and We made for their destruction an appointed time.
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine justice and retribution that befalls those who engage in wrongdoing and oppression. It emphasizes that Allah has set a predetermined time for the destruction of such unjust societies, indicating that their punishment is not arbitrary but rather a consequence of their own actions. The verse serves as a warning to individuals and communities to abstain from transgression and to uphold justice, as the ultimate fate of the wrongdoers is inevitable destruction at the appointed time decreed by Allah.
orig: وتلك القرى أهلكناهم لما ظلموا وجعلنا لمهلكهم موعدا

translation: And [mention] when Moses said to his servant, "I will not cease [traveling] until I reach the junction of the two seas or continue for a long period."
interpretation: This verse is interpreted as a metaphor for the spiritual journey and the quest for knowledge. Moses represents the seeker of truth who is determined to reach his goal, even if it means traveling to the farthest reaches of the world or spending a long time in pursuit of it. The "junction of the two seas" symbolizes the meeting point between the worldly knowledge and divine wisdom. It is a reminder that the path to enlightenment requires patience, perseverance, and a willingness to go beyond one's comfort zone.
orig: وإذ قال موسى لفتاه لا أبرح حتى أبلغ مجمع البحرين أو أمضي حقبا

translation: But when they reached the junction between them, they forgot their fish, and it took its course into the sea, slipping away.
interpretation: This verse is interpreted as a lesson in mindfulness and the consequences of forgetting one's responsibilities. The two companions, believed to be Moses and his servant, forgot about the fish they were carrying, which symbolizes their divine mission. The fish's escape into the sea represents how easily one can lose sight of their purpose when they become unmindful or distracted. It serves as a reminder to remain vigilant and focused on one's spiritual journey and the tasks entrusted to them by God, lest they stray from the righteous path.
orig: فلما بلغا مجمع بينهما نسيا حوتهما فاتخذ سبيله في البحر سربا

translation: So when they had passed beyond it, [Moses] said to his boy, "Bring us our morning meal. We have certainly suffered in this, our journey, [much] fatigue."
interpretation: This verse is interpreted as a reminder that even prophets and righteous people face difficulties and hardships during their journeys and missions. Moses, despite being a prophet, experienced fatigue and hunger during his travels. It teaches us that facing challenges is a natural part of life and that we should turn to Allah for help and support during these times. The verse also highlights the importance of having patience and perseverance in the face of adversity, as it is through these trials that we grow and become closer to Allah.
orig: فلما جاوزا قال لفتاه آتنا غداءنا لقد لقينا من سفرنا هذا نصبا

translation: He said, "Did you see when we retired to the rock? Indeed, I forgot [there] the fish. And none made me forget it except Satan - that I should mention it. And it took its course into the sea amazingly".
interpretation: This verse is interpreted as a reminder that even the most righteous and knowledgeable people, such as prophets, can forget or make mistakes due to the whisperings and distractions of Satan. It emphasizes the importance of remaining vigilant and mindful of Allah's remembrance at all times, and not allowing oneself to be misled by the devil's temptations. The verse also highlights the miraculous nature of the fish's journey, which serves as a sign of Allah's power and control over all things in the universe.
orig: قال أرأيت إذ أوينا إلى الصخرة فإني نسيت الحوت وما أنسانيه إلا الشيطان أن أذكره واتخذ سبيله في البحر عجبا

translation: He said, "That is what we were seeking." So they returned, following their footprints.
interpretation: This verse is referring to the story of Moses and his servant, who were on a journey to find the meeting place of the two seas. They had forgotten the fish they were carrying, which had miraculously come back to life and swam away. When Moses' servant remembered this, they retraced their steps to find where the fish had gone, knowing that this was a sign of the location they were seeking. The verse emphasizes the importance of paying attention to divine signs and guidance, even in unexpected forms. It also shows the value of retracing one's steps when one has lost the way, both literally and spiritually, in order to find the right path again.
orig: قال ذلك ما كنا نبغ فارتدا على آثارهما قصصا

translation: And they found a servant from among Our servants to whom we had given mercy from us and had taught him from [direct] knowledge.
interpretation: This verse is referring to Al-Khidr, a righteous servant of Allah who was blessed with special wisdom and knowledge from God, above what is given to ordinary people. The "mercy" given to him could refer to prophethood or spiritual insight. Moses sought him out to learn from his God-given knowledge and wisdom that was beyond Moses' own understanding at that time. It shows that there are those who are granted special divine knowledge by God's grace and mercy.
orig: فوجدا عبدا من عبادنا آتيناه رحمة من عندنا وعلمناه من لدنا علما

translation: Moses said to him, "May I follow you on [the condition] that you teach me from what you have been taught of sound judgement?"
interpretation: This verse is about the encounter between Prophet Moses and a wise man, who is believed to be Al-Khidr. Moses, despite being a prophet himself, shows humility and the desire to learn from someone more knowledgeable. It teaches us that seeking knowledge is a virtuous act, and one should always be open to learning from others, regardless of their status or position. The verse also highlights the importance of having sound judgment and wisdom, which can be acquired through learning from those who possess it. It encourages us to seek guidance from the knowledgeable and wise individuals in our pursuit of righteousness and truth.
orig: قال له موسى هل أتبعك على أن تعلمن مما علمت رشدا

translation: He said, "Indeed, with me you will never be able to have patience."
interpretation: This verse is a reminder that patience is a virtue that requires effort and discipline to maintain, especially in the face of challenges or when dealing with those who have more knowledge or wisdom than ourselves. It suggests that we should be humble and willing to learn from others, even if their ways may be difficult for us to understand or accept at first. Ultimately, the verse encourages us to cultivate patience and perseverance in our spiritual journey, trusting in the guidance of those who are more experienced and knowledgeable than ourselves.
orig: قال إنك لن تستطيع معي صبرا

translation: And how can you have patience for what you do not encompass in knowledge?
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of having knowledge and understanding before making judgments or decisions. It suggests that one cannot truly be patient or endure something without fully comprehending its nature and implications. The verse implies that it is essential to seek knowledge and strive to gain a deep understanding of matters before forming opinions or taking actions. It highlights the value of education, research, and thorough investigation in order to make well-informed choices and exhibit proper patience and perseverance in the face of challenges or uncertainties.
orig: وكيف تصبر على ما لم تحط به خبرا

translation: He said, "You will find me, if Allah wills, patient and I shall not disobey you in [any] order."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of patience and obedience to righteous figures and those in authority. The speaker, believed to be Moses, expresses his willingness to follow the commands of his companion, believed to be Al-Khidr, as long as it is in accordance with the will of Allah. This highlights the significance of submitting to divine guidance and wisdom, even if one may not fully comprehend the reasons behind certain actions or instructions. The verse also underscores the value of humility and the recognition that ultimate knowledge and understanding belong to Allah alone.
orig: قال ستجدني إن شاء الله صابرا ولا أعصي لك أمرا

translation: He said, "Then if you follow me, do not ask me about anything until I make to you about it mention."
interpretation: This verse is part of the story of Prophet Moses and Al-Khidr in Surah Al-Kahf. It emphasizes the importance of patience, trust, and respect for those with greater knowledge or wisdom. Al-Khidr, who possesses divine knowledge, sets a condition for Moses to follow him: that Moses must not question any of Al-Khidr's actions until Al-Khidr himself explains them. This teaches us to have faith in the wisdom of those more knowledgeable than ourselves, even if their actions seem unconventional or difficult to understand at first. It also highlights the value of humility in the pursuit of knowledge, recognizing that we may not always grasp the full picture and should trust in the guidance of those more enlightened.
orig: قال فإن اتبعتني فلا تسألني عن شيء حتى أحدث لك منه ذكرا

translation: So they both proceeded: until, when they were in the boat, he scuttled it. Said Moses: "Hast thou scuttled it in order to drown those in it? Truly a strange thing hast thou done!"
interpretation: This verse is about the story of Prophet Moses and Al-Khidr. The interpretation is that sometimes things that seem bad or harmful on the surface may have a greater wisdom behind them that we cannot immediately perceive. Al-Khidr, having been granted divine knowledge by God, understood the hidden wisdom behind damaging the boat, even though to Moses it seemed like a terrible act that would cause people to drown. It teaches us to have faith that God's plan is ultimately good and wise, even if we can't always understand it from our limited human perspective.
orig: فانطلقا حتى إذا ركبا في السفينة خرقها قال أخرقتها لتغرق أهلها لقد جئت شيئا إمرا

translation: He said, "Did I not tell you that you would not be able to have patience with me?"
interpretation: This verse is a reminder from a wise teacher to his student about the importance of patience and trust in the face of seemingly incomprehensible events. The teacher is emphasizing that true understanding requires faith and perseverance, even when the reasons behind certain actions or occurrences are not immediately clear. It is a lesson in humility, urging the student to recognize the limits of their own knowledge and to submit to the greater wisdom of the teacher. Ultimately, this verse encourages the cultivation of patience and the willingness to learn from those who possess deeper insight and understanding.
orig: قال ألم أقل إنك لن تستطيع معي صبرا

translation: He said, "Do not blame me for what I forgot and do not cover me in my matter with hardship."
interpretation: This verse is a plea for forgiveness and understanding. The speaker is asking not to be held accountable for what they have forgotten, and not to be burdened with excessive hardship in their affairs. It reflects the Islamic principle of showing compassion and leniency towards others, recognizing that humans are forgetful and imperfect by nature. The verse encourages a gentle and forgiving approach in dealing with people's shortcomings, rather than being harsh or imposing undue difficulty upon them.
orig: قال لا تؤاخذني بما نسيت ولا ترهقني من أمري عسرا

translation: So they both proceeded, until when they met a boy, he killed him. [Musa] said, "Have you killed a pure soul for other than [having killed] a soul? You have certainly done a deplorable thing."
interpretation: This verse is interpreted as a test of faith and trust in Allah's wisdom. The killing of an innocent child seems unjust and wrong from a human perspective, but the verse suggests that there may be a greater divine wisdom behind such actions that humans cannot fully comprehend. It emphasizes the importance of having faith in Allah's plan even when faced with seemingly inexplicable or difficult circumstances. The verse also highlights the contrast between human judgment based on limited knowledge and Allah's infinite wisdom and knowledge of all things, seen and unseen.
orig: فانطلقا حتى إذا لقيا غلاما فقتله قال أقتلت نفسا زكية بغير نفس لقد جئت شيئا نكرا

translation: He said, "Did I not tell you that you would not be able to have patience with me?"
interpretation: This verse is a reminder from a wise teacher to his student about the importance of patience and trust in the face of seemingly inexplicable events. The teacher is emphasizing that true understanding requires faith and perseverance, even when the reasons behind certain actions or occurrences are not immediately clear. It is a lesson in humility, urging the student to recognize the limits of human knowledge and to submit to the greater wisdom of the divine plan. The verse suggests that the path to enlightenment often involves trials and challenges that test one's commitment and resolve, and that only through unwavering dedication can one hope to attain the highest levels of spiritual insight and growth.
orig: قال ألم أقل لك إنك لن تستطيع معي صبرا

translation: He said, "If I should ask you about anything after this, then do not keep me as a companion. You have obtained from me an excuse."
interpretation: This verse is emphasizing the importance of trust and clear communication in a relationship or companionship. The speaker is setting a boundary and giving a final warning that if the listener asks about anything further, it will be grounds for ending their companionship. The speaker asserts that they have already given sufficient excuse or explanation, and any further questioning would cross a line. This highlights the need for respecting boundaries, being satisfied with explanations given, and not pushing a relationship past a point of broken trust.
orig: قال إن سألتك عن شيء بعدها فلا تصاحبني قد بلغت من لدني عذرا

translation: So they set out, until when they came to the people of a town, they asked its people for food, but they refused to offer them hospitality. And they found therein a wall about to collapse, so he restored it. [Moses] said, "If you wished, you could have taken for it a payment."
interpretation: This verse is part of the story of Moses and Al-Khidr, where Al-Khidr's actions seem to contradict common sense or justice. In this case, after being refused hospitality by the people of the town, Al-Khidr repairs a wall that was about to collapse. Moses questions this act, saying that Al-Khidr could have demanded payment for his work. The deeper meaning is that sometimes, acts of kindness and charity should be done without expecting reward, even towards those who have wronged you. It also suggests that there may be wisdom behind events that seem unfair or illogical from a limited human perspective.
orig: فانطلقا حتى إذا أتيا أهل قرية استطعما أهلها فأبوا أن يضيفوهما فوجدا فيها جدارا يريد أن ينقض فأقامه قال لو شئت لاتخذت عليه أجرا

translation: He said, "This is parting between me and you. I will inform you of the interpretation of that about which you could not have patience."
interpretation: This verse marks the end of the journey and the parting of ways between Prophet Moses and Al-Khidr. Al-Khidr, having been granted divine knowledge and wisdom, promises to explain to Moses the true meaning and wisdom behind the seemingly strange and incomprehensible events that Moses witnessed. It highlights the importance of having patience, trust in God's plan, and the realization that there is often a deeper wisdom and purpose behind events that may initially seem troubling or confusing to our limited human understanding. The verse emphasizes the value of seeking knowledge and guidance from those who are divinely inspired, even if their actions may sometimes appear unconventional or difficult to comprehend.
orig: قال هذا فراق بيني وبينك سأنبئك بتأويل ما لم تستطع عليه صبرا

translation: As for the ship, it belonged to poor people working at sea. So I intended to cause defect in it as there was after them a king who seized every [good] ship by force.
interpretation: This verse is referring to the story of Prophet Musa (Moses) and Al-Khidr. Al-Khidr, who was given special knowledge by Allah, damaged the ship that belonged to poor people. The interpretation is that Al-Khidr did this seemingly bad deed of damaging the ship in order to save it from being seized by an unjust king who was known for forcefully taking every good ship he came across. So, while it appeared to be a harmful action, Al-Khidr's intention was to protect the poor people's means of livelihood from greater harm. This teaches us that sometimes, what appears to be a misfortune may actually be a blessing in disguise from Allah to prevent a greater calamity.
orig: أما السفينة فكانت لمساكين يعملون في البحر فأردت أن أعيبها وكان وراءهم ملك يأخذ كل سفينة غصبا

translation: And as for the boy, his parents were believers, and we feared that he would overburden them by transgression and disbelief.
interpretation: This verse is referring to the story of Khidr and Moses, where Khidr killed a young boy. The interpretation is that the boy's parents were righteous believers, but there was a fear that as the boy grew older, he would become rebellious and lead his parents into transgression and disbelief through his actions. Therefore, the boy's death was decreed to prevent this from happening and to save the parents from being led astray by their love for their son. It highlights the concept of divine wisdom and that God may allow seemingly bad things to happen for a greater good or to prevent a greater evil.
orig: وأما الغلام فكان أبواه مؤمنين فخشينا أن يرهقهما طغيانا وكفرا

translation: So we intended that their Lord should substitute for them one better than him in purity and nearer to mercy.
interpretation: This verse is referring to the story of Moses and Al-Khidr, where Al-Khidr killed a young boy. The interpretation is that although the act seemed cruel and unjustified, there was divine wisdom behind it. Allah knew that the boy would grow up to be a disbeliever who would overburden his pious parents with his transgression and disbelief. By his death, Allah intended to replace him with a child who would be better in purity and righteousness, and who would be a source of mercy and comfort to his parents, being dutiful and bringing them happiness in this world and the next. It shows that there can be hidden wisdom in events that seem tragic on the surface.
orig: فأردنا أن يبدلهما ربهما خيرا منه زكاة وأقرب رحما

translation: And as for the wall, it belonged to two orphan boys in the city, and there was beneath it a treasure for them, and their father had been righteous. So your Lord intended that they reach maturity and extract their treasure, as a mercy from your Lord. And I did it not of my own accord. That is the interpretation of that about which you could not have patience.
interpretation: This verse highlights the wisdom and mercy of Allah in His actions, even if they may seem incomprehensible to us at first. The wall that was rebuilt was protecting a treasure belonging to two orphan boys, which Allah wanted them to have when they grew older. This act of kindness was done out of mercy for the orphans, as their father had been a righteous man. The verse also emphasizes the importance of patience and trust in Allah's plan, as we may not always understand the reasons behind certain events in our lives. Ultimately, it is a reminder that Allah's wisdom and mercy are infinite, and that we should submit to His will with faith and patience.
orig: وأما الجدار فكان لغلامين يتيمين في المدينة وكان تحته كنز لهما وكان أبوهما صالحا فأراد ربك أن يبلغا أشدهما ويستخرجا كنزهما رحمة من ربك وما فعلته عن أمري ذلك تأويل ما لم تسطع عليه صبرا

translation: And they ask you about Dhul-Qarnayn. Say, "I will recite to you a mention of him."
interpretation: In this verse, Allah instructs Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) on how to respond when asked about the story of Dhul-Qarnayn. Rather than providing a direct answer, the Prophet is told to recite the upcoming verses, which will serve as a reminder and a lesson about this historical figure. This approach highlights the importance of seeking knowledge through divine revelation and reflects the Qur'an's role as a source of guidance and wisdom for humanity.
orig: ويسألونك عن ذي القرنين قل سأتلو عليكم منه ذكرا

translation: Indeed, We established him upon the earth, and We gave him to everything a way.
interpretation: This verse highlights the power and authority that Allah bestowed upon a certain individual, likely referring to a prophet or a great leader. By establishing them on earth, Allah granted them a strong foothold and influence over their surroundings. Moreover, Allah provided them with the means and resources to achieve their goals, opening doors and pathways to success in various aspects of life. This divine support and empowerment allowed them to fulfill their mission and make a significant impact in the world. The verse emphasizes the idea that when Allah chooses someone for a special purpose, He ensures that they have the necessary tools and opportunities to carry out their responsibilities effectively.
orig: إنا مكنا له في الأرض وآتيناه من كل شيء سببا

translation: Then he followed a way.
interpretation: This verse is referring to Dhul-Qarnayn, a righteous ruler mentioned in the Qur'an. "Then he followed a way" means that after completing one task or reaching one destination, Dhul-Qarnayn continued his journey and pursued another path or goal. It indicates that he was determined, focused and kept striving in the way of Allah, utilizing the knowledge and resources that Allah had blessed him with. The verse emphasizes the importance of continuous effort and steadfastness in pursuing noble objectives and fulfilling one's mission in life.
orig: فأتبع سببا

translation: Until, when he reached the setting of the sun, he found it [as if] setting in a spring of dark mud, and he found near it a people. We [i.e., Allah] said, "O Dhul-Qarnayn, either you punish [them] or else adopt among them [a way of] goodness."
interpretation: This verse is interpreted as a metaphorical description of Dhul-Qarnayn's journey to the west, where he encountered a people living near a murky spring. The "setting of the sun" is not to be taken literally; rather, it symbolizes the limits of human knowledge and experience. The choice given to Dhul-Qarnayn by Allah, to either punish or treat these people with kindness, is seen as a test of his character and leadership. The verse emphasizes the importance of justice and compassion in dealing with others, even those who may be different or unfamiliar.
orig: حتى إذا بلغ مغرب الشمس وجدها تغرب في عين حمئة ووجد عندها قوما قلنا يا ذا القرنين إما أن تعذب وإما أن تتخذ فيهم حسنا

translation: He said, "As for him who wrongs, we will punish him. Then he will be returned to his Lord, and He will punish him with a terrible punishment."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the severity of Allah's punishment for those who commit injustice and wrongdoing. It serves as a warning that even if wrongdoers may escape punishment in this world, they will ultimately face the consequences of their actions in the Hereafter, where Allah will subject them to a severe and terrible punishment. The repetition of the word "punish" highlights the gravity of the consequences and the importance of refraining from oppression and injustice. This interpretation underscores the Islamic belief in divine justice and the accountability of all individuals before Allah in the afterlife.
orig: قال أما من ظلم فسوف نعذبه ثم يرد إلى ربه فيعذبه عذابا نكرا

translation: But as for he who believed and did righteousness, he will have the best reward, and we will speak to him from our command with ease.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of faith and good deeds in Islam. Those who sincerely believe in Allah and perform righteous actions will be rewarded with the best reward in the Hereafter, which is Paradise. Additionally, Allah will make things easy for the believers in this world and the next, speaking to them with gentleness and kindness. This verse encourages Muslims to strive for faith and righteousness, knowing that their efforts will be appreciated and rewarded by Allah, both in this life and in the eternal life to come.
orig: وأما من آمن وعمل صالحا فله جزاء الحسنى وسنقول له من أمرنا يسرا

translation: Then he followed a way.
interpretation: In this verse, Allah is referring to Dhul-Qarnayn, a great ruler mentioned in the Qur'an. The verse indicates that after reaching a certain point in his journey and conquests, Dhul-Qarnayn then followed a particular path or course of action. This could be interpreted as him continuing his mission of establishing justice and spreading monotheism, as he was known to be a righteous ruler. It suggests that he had a clear purpose and methodology that he adhered to. The verse emphasizes the importance of having a direction and goal in one's efforts and journeys in life, and pursuing it with determination.
orig: ثم أتبع سببا

translation: Until, when he reached the rising of the sun, he found it rising on a people for whom We had not made against it any shield.
interpretation: This verse refers to Dhul-Qarnayn's journey towards the east, where he reached the place of the rising sun. He found that the sun was rising upon a people for whom Allah had not provided any shelter or protection against it. This could imply that these people were living a very primitive life, without the means or knowledge to protect themselves from the harsh sun. It may also suggest that they were unaware of or not worshipping Allah, as they lacked the blessing of His protection that comes with faith and righteousness. The verse highlights Dhul-Qarnayn's vast travels and the diversity of people and civilizations he encountered, while also pointing to Allah's power and wisdom in creating different conditions and tests for different peoples.
orig: حتى إذا بلغ مطلع الشمس وجدها تطلع على قوم لم نجعل لهم من دونها سترا

translation: And We have encompassed whatever he has [of knowledge] in Our knowledge.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the all-encompassing knowledge of Allah. It suggests that whatever knowledge or understanding a person may possess, it is ultimately insignificant in comparison to the infinite wisdom and knowledge of the Almighty. It serves as a reminder for humans to remain humble and recognize the limitations of their own knowledge, as Allah is the One who has complete awareness and comprehension of all things, both seen and unseen.
orig: كذلك وقد أحطنا بما لديه خبرا

translation: Then he followed a way.
interpretation: This verse refers to Dhul-Qarnayn, a righteous ruler mentioned in the Qur'an.
