After being granted power and means by Allah, he traveled and followed a path that led him to various places and nations. The verse indicates that he used his power and resources to explore, learn, and spread justice and goodness in the lands he visited, following the way of Allah. It symbolizes using one's God-given abilities and opportunities for noble pursuits and beneficial actions in accordance with divine guidance.
orig: ثم أتبع سببا

translation: Until, when he reached [a pass] between two mountains, he found beside them a people who could hardly understand [his] speech.
interpretation: This verse is referring to Dhul-Qarnayn, a righteous ruler mentioned in the Qur'an. When he reached a pass between two mountains, he encountered a group of people who spoke a language that was difficult for him to understand. This highlights the diversity of languages and peoples that existed even in ancient times. It also shows that despite the differences in language and culture, Dhul-Qarnayn was able to communicate and interact with them, perhaps demonstrating patience, wisdom and good leadership in navigating this challenge. The verse reminds us of the importance of striving to understand and cooperate with others, even when there are linguistic or cultural barriers.
orig: حتى إذا بلغ بين السدين وجد من دونهما قوما لا يكادون يفقهون قولا

translation: They said, "O Dhul-Qarnayn, indeed Gog and Magog are [great] corrupters in the land. So may we assign for you an expenditure that you might make between us and them a barrier?"
interpretation: This verse is referring to a conversation between a righteous ruler or king, known as Dhul-Qarnayn, and a people who were suffering at the hands of the tribes of Gog and Magog. The people beseeched Dhul-Qarnayn to build a barrier between them and the destructive tribes in exchange for payment. The verse highlights the wisdom and power of Dhul-Qarnayn, who was a divinely guided leader tasked with protecting the weak and oppressed. It also demonstrates the importance of seeking help and protection from righteous authorities against evil and corruption in society.
orig: قالوا يا ذا القرنين إن يأجوج ومأجوج مفسدون في الأرض فهل نجعل لك خرجا على أن تجعل بيننا وبينهم سدا

translation: He said, "That in which my Lord has established me is better [than what you offer], but assist me with strength; I will make between you and them a dam."
interpretation: In this verse, Dhul-Qarnayn is responding to the people who sought his help against Gog and Magog. He acknowledges that the power and resources bestowed upon him by Allah are superior to any material compensation they could offer. Instead of accepting their tribute, Dhul-Qarnayn asks for their physical assistance in constructing a barrier between them and the troublesome nation. This demonstrates his wisdom, as he recognizes that the true solution lies in utilizing the strength and unity of the people, rather than relying on wealth or personal gain. The verse highlights the importance of collaboration, resourcefulness, and seeking practical solutions to protect oneself and others from harm.
orig: قال ما مكني فيه ربي خير فأعينوني بقوة أجعل بينكم وبينهم ردما

translation: Bring me sheets of iron. Until, when he had leveled [them] between the two mountain walls, he said, "Blow [with bellows]," until when he had made it [like] fire, he said, "Bring me, that I may pour over it molten copper."
interpretation: This verse is referring to the story of Dhul-Qarnayn, a righteous ruler mentioned in the Qur'an. It describes how he built a barrier between two mountains to protect people from the attacks of Gog and Magog. The interpretation is that with determination, planning, and the right resources, one can overcome great challenges and protect others from harm. It also symbolizes the importance of using our skills and knowledge for the benefit of society.
orig: آتوني زبر الحديد حتى إذا ساوى بين الصدفين قال انفخوا حتى إذا جعله نارا قال آتوني أفرغ عليه قطرا

translation: And they were unable to pass over it, nor were they able [to effect] in it any penetration.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the impenetrability and strength of the barrier that Dhul-Qarnayn constructed between the people and Gog and Magog. It suggests that the barrier was so formidable that no one could scale it or breach it in any way. This can be interpreted as a metaphor for God's protection and the power of faith to shield believers from evil and corruption. It also highlights the temporary nature of worldly constructions, as even the mightiest of barriers will eventually perish, while God's word and decree are eternal.
orig: فما اسطاعوا أن يظهروه وما استطاعوا له نقبا

translation: He said, "This is a mercy from my Lord; but when the promise of my Lord comes, He will make it level, and ever is the promise of my Lord true."
interpretation: This verse speaks about a great blessing or favor that Allah has bestowed, but it also serves as a reminder that all of Allah's blessings and creations in this world are temporary. When the appointed time arrives, Allah will destroy or level whatever it is, as His promise is always true. This highlights the fleeting nature of the world and encourages humans to focus on the eternal life of the Hereafter rather than being distracted by temporary worldly pleasures or attachments.
orig: قال هذا رحمة من ربي فإذا جاء وعد ربي جعله دكاء وكان وعد ربي حقا

translation: And We shall leave them, on that day, to surge like waves on one another, and the Trumpet will be blown, and We shall gather them all together.
interpretation: This verse refers to the Day of Judgment when all of humanity will be resurrected and gathered together before Allah. The people will be in a state of confusion and chaos, likened to waves crashing against each other. The blowing of the Trumpet signifies the beginning of the judgment, where everyone will be held accountable for their deeds in this world. It emphasizes the power and authority of Allah in gathering all of His creation for the final reckoning, and serves as a reminder for mankind to be mindful of their actions in this life as they will have consequences in the Hereafter.
orig: وتركنا بعضهم يومئذ يموج في بعض ونفخ في الصور فجمعناهم جمعا

translation: And on that Day We will present Hell to the Disbelievers, on display
interpretation: This verse is a stark warning to those who reject faith in God. It conveys that on the Day of Judgment, Hell will be brought forth and displayed vividly before the disbelievers. They will witness the terrible reality of the punishment that awaits those who turned away from God's guidance in the worldly life. The verse emphasizes the severity and inevitability of the consequences of disbelief. It serves as a powerful reminder for people to sincerely embrace faith and righteousness before it is too late, for on that Day, there will be no escape from God's ultimate justice.
orig: وعرضنا جهنم يومئذ للكافرين عرضا

translation: Those whose eyes had been under a cover from My remembrance, and they were unable to hear.
interpretation: This verse refers to those who are heedless of Allah's message and reminders. They have chosen to ignore the truth and have become blind and deaf to the guidance of Allah. Their spiritual senses are covered, preventing them from perceiving and understanding the signs of Allah in the world around them and in the divine revelation. They are unable to hear the message of truth and benefit from it due to their own choice of turning away from Allah's remembrance. This state of heedlessness and spiritual insensitivity is a result of their own actions and decisions, as they have voluntarily chosen to close their eyes and ears to the truth.
orig: الذين كانت أعينهم في غطاء عن ذكري وكانوا لا يستطيعون سمعا

translation: Do the disbelievers think that they can take My servants as allies besides Me? Indeed, We have prepared Hell as a lodging for the disbelievers.
interpretation: This verse is a stern warning to those who reject faith in God and take others as protectors or allies instead of Him. It conveys that such people are deluded if they think they can find true support and guidance from anyone other than God. As a consequence of their disbelief and misplaced reliance, God has prepared Hell as their final abode in the afterlife. The verse emphasizes the gravity of shirk (associating partners with God) and underscores that no one can provide the protection, support and guidance that God alone can provide. It is a reminder for humans to direct their worship and trust towards God alone.
orig: أفحسب الذين كفروا أن يتخذوا عبادي من دوني أولياء إنا أعتدنا جهنم للكافرين نزلا

translation: Say, "Shall we inform you of the greatest losers in deeds?"
interpretation: This verse is a rhetorical question, asking if the listeners want to know about those who will face the greatest loss and whose deeds will be rendered worthless on the Day of Judgment. It serves as a warning and an invitation to reflect on one's actions and intentions, emphasizing that the ultimate loss is not in worldly matters but in one's standing with Allah. The verse implies that there are people who may think they are doing good deeds, but due to their wrong intentions or lack of faith, their deeds will not be accepted by Allah and will result in significant loss in the Hereafter.
orig: قل هل ننبئكم بالأخسرين أعمالا

translation: Those whose efforts have been wasted in this life while they thought that they were acquiring good by their deeds.
interpretation: This verse refers to those who may have worked hard in this worldly life, but their efforts were misguided and not in accordance with the teachings of Islam. They believed that they were doing good deeds and would be rewarded, but in reality, their actions were futile because they were not based on true faith and submission to Allah. It highlights the importance of ensuring that our intentions and actions align with what pleases Allah, rather than simply following our own desires or what society deems as good.
orig: الذين ضل سعيهم في الحياة الدنيا وهم يحسبون أنهم يحسنون صنعا

translation: Those who disbelieved in the signs of their Lord and in the meeting with Him, their deeds have become worthless, so We will not give them any weight on the Day of Resurrection.
interpretation: This verse refers to the disbelievers who rejected the signs and messages sent by Allah and denied the reality of the Day of Judgment when they will meet their Lord. As a result of their disbelief, all their seemingly good deeds and actions in this worldly life will be rendered void and worthless on the Day of Resurrection. Allah will not give any consideration or value to their deeds because they lacked true faith and sincerity. This emphasizes the importance of belief in Allah and the Hereafter, without which all actions, no matter how righteous they may appear, will carry no weight in the eyes of Allah.
orig: أولئك الذين كفروا بآيات ربهم ولقائه فحبطت أعمالهم فلا نقيم لهم يوم القيامة وزنا

translation: That is their recompense - Hell - for what they denied and [because] they took My signs and My messengers in ridicule.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the severe punishment that awaits those who reject God's signs and messengers. Their recompense is Hell, a direct consequence of their disbelief and their mockery of the divine message. It serves as a warning to those who turn away from the truth and treat God's revelations and prophets with contempt. The verse highlights the gravity of denying the Almighty and the importance of treating His signs and messengers with respect and reverence. It also underscores the concept of divine justice, where every action has its consequences, and those who choose to disbelieve and ridicule will face the ultimate punishment in the afterlife.
orig: ذلك جزاؤهم جهنم بما كفروا واتخذوا آياتي ورسلي هزوا

translation: Indeed, those who have believed and done righteous deeds will have the Gardens of Paradise as a lodging,
interpretation: This verse highlights the immense reward that awaits those who have true faith in Allah and couple that faith with good deeds. It emphasizes that Paradise, with its unimaginable beauty and pleasures, will be the eternal abode for the righteous believers. The use of the word "nuzulan" (lodging) indicates that Paradise will be a welcoming gift and a hospitable accommodation that Allah has prepared for His devoted servants. This promise serves as a great motivation for believers to persist in their faith and strive to do good in this world, knowing that their ultimate destination is the blissful gardens of Paradise.
orig: إن الذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات كانت لهم جنات الفردوس نزلا

translation: Abiding eternally therein. They will not desire from it any transfer.
interpretation: This verse speaks about the eternal bliss and contentment of the inhabitants of Paradise. They will be so satisfied and pleased with their abode in Paradise that they will have no desire to leave or change their situation. This highlights the perfection and completeness of the rewards in Paradise, where the believers will find ultimate peace, happiness, and fulfillment, never feeling any sense of boredom, dissatisfaction, or longing for something else. It emphasizes the everlasting nature of Paradise and the unwavering joy experienced by those who are granted entry into it by Allah's mercy and grace.
orig: خالدين فيها لا يبغون عنها حولا

translation: Say, "If the sea were ink for [writing] the words of my Lord, the sea would be exhausted before the words of my Lord were exhausted, even if We brought the like of it as a supplement."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the infinite nature of Allah's knowledge and wisdom. It suggests that even if the entire ocean were turned into ink, it would be insufficient to write down all of Allah's words. The metaphor of the sea as ink conveys the idea that Allah's knowledge is so vast and inexhaustible that it cannot be contained or fully comprehended by human beings. Even if another ocean of the same size were added, it would still not be enough to capture the entirety of Allah's words. This verse serves as a reminder of the limitless nature of Allah's attributes and the humility with which humans should approach the pursuit of knowledge and understanding of the divine.
orig: قل لو كان البحر مدادا لكلمات ربي لنفد البحر قبل أن تنفد كلمات ربي ولو جئنا بمثله مددا

translation: Say, "I am only a man like you, to whom has been revealed that your god is one God. So whoever would hope for the meeting with his Lord - let him do righteous work and not associate in the worship of his Lord anyone."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the humanity of Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and that he is not divine, but rather a messenger who receives revelation from the one true God. It calls upon those who desire to meet their Lord to perform good deeds sincerely for His sake alone, without associating partners with Him or worshipping anyone else besides Him. This highlights the importance of pure monotheism (tawheed) and righteous actions in attaining salvation and closeness to Allah in the Hereafter.
orig: قل إنما أنا بشر مثلكم يوحى إلي أنما إلهكم إله واحد فمن كان يرجو لقاء ربه فليعمل عملا صالحا ولا يشرك بعبادة ربه أحدا

translation: Kaf, Ha, Ya, 'Ayn, Sad.
interpretation: This verse consists of disjointed letters, the meaning of which is not entirely clear. Some scholars believe that these letters represent a secret code or a challenge to the doubters of the Qur'an's divine origin, as if to say that even with these seemingly random letters, the Qur'an is a masterpiece of language and meaning that cannot be replicated by human beings. Others interpret these letters as abbreviations for certain phrases or attributes of Allah, or as a way to draw the listener's attention to the importance of the message that follows. Ultimately, the true meaning of these letters is known only to Allah, and their presence in the Qur'an serves as a reminder of the limitless depth and mystery of Allah's word.
orig: كهيعص

translation: A mention of the mercy of your Lord to His servant Zechariah.
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of remembering and acknowledging God's mercy and blessings upon His servants. It specifically mentions the story of Prophet Zechariah, who was blessed with a son, John (Yahya), despite his old age and his wife's barrenness. This serves as a reminder that God's mercy and power know no bounds, and He can grant His servants whatever He wills, even in seemingly impossible situations. The verse encourages believers to always have faith in God's mercy and to turn to Him in prayer and supplication, just as Zechariah did.
orig: ذكر رحمت ربك عبده زكريا

translation: When he called upon his Lord a private supplication.
interpretation: This verse refers to the prophet Zakariya (Zechariah) when he secretly called upon Allah, beseeching Him to bless him with a righteous child in his old age. It highlights the sincerity and humility of Zakariya's supplication, as he turned to Allah in private, away from the eyes of people, expressing his innermost desires and hopes. This teaches us the importance of having a personal, intimate relationship with Allah and making heartfelt, sincere du'a (supplication) to Him in both our moments of ease and hardship.
orig: إذ نادى ربه نداء خفيا

translation: He said, "My Lord, indeed my bones have weakened, and my head has filled with white, and never have I been in my supplication to You, my Lord, unhappy.
interpretation: This verse reflects the humility and devotion of Prophet Zakariya (PBUH) as he acknowledges his old age and physical weakness, yet remains steadfast in his faith and continues to supplicate to Allah without despair or dissatisfaction. It highlights the importance of maintaining a strong spiritual connection with Allah, even in the face of life's challenges and the passage of time. The verse encourages believers to persistently turn to Allah in prayer, trusting in His wisdom and mercy, and finding contentment in their relationship with Him regardless of their circumstances.
orig: قال رب إني وهن العظم مني واشتعل الرأس شيبا ولم أكن بدعائك رب شقيا

translation: And indeed, I fear the successors after me, and my wife has been barren, so give me from Yourself an heir
interpretation: In this verse, the speaker, who is believed to be the Prophet Zakariya (Zechariah), expresses his concern about the future of his mission and his people after his death. He fears that those who come after him may not be able to carry on his work and may lead the people astray. Additionally, he mentions that his wife is barren, which means that he does not have a natural heir to succeed him. In light of these circumstances, he turns to Allah in prayer and supplication, asking Him to grant him a child who will be able to continue his mission and guide the people to the right path. This verse highlights the importance of having righteous successors and the role of supplication in seeking Allah's help and support in achieving one's goals.
orig: وإني خفت الموالي من ورائي وكانت امرأتي عاقرا فهب لي من لدنك وليا

translation: Who shall inherit me and inherit from the family of Jacob. And make him, my Lord, pleasing [to You].
interpretation: This verse is a prayer of Prophet Zakariya (Zechariah) asking Allah to grant him a righteous son who will continue the legacy of prophethood in the family of Prophet Ya'qub (Jacob). He asks Allah to make this child pleasing to Him, indicating his desire for the child to be obedient, God-fearing, and a source of goodness. This prayer highlights the importance of righteous offspring who will carry on the mission of guiding people to the path of Allah and the significance of seeking Allah's pleasure in all aspects of life.
orig: يرثني ويرث من آل يعقوب واجعله رب رضيا

translation: O Zakariya! Indeed, We give you good tidings of a boy whose name will be John. We have not assigned to any before [this] name.
interpretation: This verse is a divine message to Prophet Zakariya, announcing the glad tidings of a son named Yahya (John). The name Yahya is unique, as Allah states that no one before him was given this name. This signifies the special status and role of Prophet Yahya. The verse also highlights the power and mercy of Allah in granting a child to Zakariya, despite his old age and his wife's barrenness. It demonstrates that nothing is impossible for Allah and that He can bestow His blessings upon whomever He wills.
orig: يا زكريا إنا نبشرك بغلام اسمه يحيى لم نجعل له من قبل سميا

translation: He said, "My Lord, how will I have a boy when my wife has been barren and I have reached extreme old age?"
interpretation: This verse reflects Zakariya's astonishment and wonder at the news of being granted a son despite his old age and his wife's barrenness. It highlights the power and might of Allah, who is capable of creating life and granting offspring even in seemingly impossible circumstances. The verse also demonstrates Zakariya's humility and recognition of his own limitations, as he questions how this miracle could come about. It serves as a reminder to believers that nothing is impossible for Allah, and that His plans and wisdom are beyond human comprehension.
orig: قال رب أنى يكون لي غلام وكانت امرأتي عاقرا وقد بلغت من الكبر عتيا

translation: He said, "Thus [it will be]; your Lord says, 'It is easy for Me, and I have already created you before, while you were nothing.' "
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the omnipotence and creative power of Allah. It reminds us that Allah created us from nothing, and that bringing us back to life after death is easy for Him. The verse also highlights our humble origins and the fact that we were once non-existent, which should inspire gratitude and humility towards our Creator. It encourages us to have faith in Allah's ability to resurrect us and to trust in His divine plan, even if we cannot fully comprehend it.
orig: قال كذلك قال ربك هو علي هين وقد خلقتك من قبل ولم تك شيئا

translation: He said, "My Lord, make for me a sign." He Said, "Your sign is that you will not [be able to] speak to the people for three nights, [being] sound."
interpretation: This verse is a response to the prophet Zechariah's prayer for a sign that would confirm the glad tidings of a son, despite his old age and his wife's barrenness. Allah grants him the sign of not being able to speak for three nights, while being physically sound and healthy. This temporary loss of speech serves as a reminder of Allah's power and a test of Zechariah's faith and patience. It also symbolizes the importance of silent contemplation and spiritual reflection in one's relationship with Allah. The verse highlights the fact that Allah can manifest His signs and miracles in various ways, and that believers should trust in His wisdom and submit to His will, even when faced with seemingly impossible circumstances.
orig: قال رب اجعل لي آية قال آيتك ألا تكلم الناس ثلاث ليال سويا

translation: So he came out to his people from the prayer chamber and signaled to them to exalt [Allah] in the morning and afternoon.
interpretation: This verse is referring to Prophet Zakariya (Zechariah). After being blessed with a son, Yahya (John), in his old age, Zakariya came out from his prayer chamber to his people and signaled to them to praise and glorify Allah in the morning and evening. This gesture was to express gratitude to Allah for granting him a child despite his advanced years and his wife's barrenness. It emphasizes the importance of being thankful to Allah and exalting Him for His blessings and mercy at all times, particularly in the morning and afternoon, which are times of transition in the day.
orig: فخرج على قومه من المحراب فأوحى إليهم أن سبحوا بكرة وعشيا

translation: O John, take the Scripture with determination. And We gave him judgement [while yet] a boy.
interpretation: This verse is addressing John the Baptist (Yahya in Arabic), who was a prophet and contemporary of Jesus. It highlights that John was given wisdom, knowledge, and the ability to make sound judgments even at a very young age. This suggests that he was blessed with divine inspiration and guidance from an early stage in his life, allowing him to fulfill his role as a prophet and guide people to the right path. The verse emphasizes the importance of holding firmly to the scripture and divine teachings, as they provide the necessary wisdom and guidance to navigate through life's challenges.
orig: يا يحيى خذ الكتاب بقوة وآتيناه الحكم صبيا

translation: And tenderness from Us and purity, and he was fearing of Allah.
interpretation: This verse refers to Prophet Yahya (John the Baptist), highlighting the special qualities bestowed upon him by Allah. The "tenderness" mentioned here signifies the compassion, kindness, and mercy that Allah granted him. "Purity" indicates his righteousness, chastity, and being free from sins. The verse also emphasizes that Yahya was a pious individual who constantly feared Allah, which means he was always conscious of Allah, obeying His commands and refraining from His prohibitions out of reverence and love for Him. These qualities made Yahya an exemplary figure and a role model for believers.
orig: وحنانا من لدنا وزكاة وكان تقيا

translation: And dutiful to his parents, and he was not a disobedient tyrant.
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of being kind and obedient to one's parents. It emphasizes that a righteous person is not only devoted to God but also treats their parents with respect and kindness. The verse implies that being undutiful or disobedient to parents is a form of tyranny and oppression, which is strongly condemned in Islam. It serves as a reminder for Muslims to always honor and care for their parents, as this is considered a fundamental duty and a means of attaining God's pleasure.
orig: وبرا بوالديه ولم يكن جبارا عصيا

translation: And peace be upon him the day he was born and the day he dies and the day he is raised alive.
interpretation: This verse conveys a prayer for peace and blessings upon a prophet, likely referring to Jesus (Isa) based on the context of the surrounding verses. It highlights three significant moments in his life: his birth, his death, and his resurrection. The verse emphasizes the importance of these events and invokes God's peace and protection over the prophet throughout his existence, from the beginning of his life until his resurrection. This interpretation underscores the reverence and respect accorded to the prophets in Islamic tradition, acknowledging their unique status and the divine support they receive.
orig: وسلام عليه يوم ولد ويوم يموت ويوم يبعث حيا

translation: And mention in the Book [the story of] Mary, when she withdrew from her family to a place toward the east.
interpretation: This verse is referring to Mary, the mother of Jesus, and her devotion to God. By withdrawing from her family to a place in the east, Mary sought solitude to worship God and reflect upon her faith. This action demonstrates her strong commitment to spirituality and her desire to connect with the divine. The verse highlights the importance of dedicating time and space for spiritual practices and seeking a closer relationship with God, even if it means temporarily distancing oneself from worldly affairs and loved ones.
orig: واذكر في الكتاب مريم إذ انتبذت من أهلها مكانا شرقيا

translation: And she took, in seclusion from them, a screen. Then We sent to her Our Angel, and he represented himself to her as a well-proportioned man.
interpretation: This verse refers to the story of Mary, the mother of Jesus. It indicates that she secluded herself from her people, seeking solitude for worship and devotion to God. During this time, God sent the Angel Gabriel to her, who appeared before her in the form of a perfect man. This was to allay her fears and facilitate communication of the divine message that she would miraculously conceive Jesus, a great prophet. The verse highlights Mary's piety, God's favor upon her, and the miraculous nature of Jesus' birth, which occurred without a father by God's power and command.
orig: فاتخذت من دونهم حجابا فأرسلنا إليها روحنا فتمثل لها بشرا سويا

translation: She said, "Indeed, I seek refuge in the Most Merciful from you, if you should be fearing of Allah."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of seeking protection from Allah against any form of harm or evil, especially from those who do not have taqwa (consciousness of Allah). The woman mentioned in the verse, believed to be Mary, seeks refuge in Allah from the person approaching her, indicating that if he truly fears Allah, he would refrain from any inappropriate behavior. This highlights the significance of taqwa in guiding one's actions and the power of seeking Allah's protection in the face of potential danger or temptation.
orig: قالت إني أعوذ بالرحمن منك إن كنت تقيا

translation: He said, "I am only the messenger of your Lord to give you [news of] a pure boy."
interpretation: This verse is a part of the story of Mary, the mother of Jesus. The angel Gabriel appears to Mary and informs her that she will have a pure and righteous son, despite being a virgin. The verse emphasizes that this miraculous event is not of Gabriel's own doing, but rather he is merely a messenger conveying the will of God. It highlights the divine nature of Jesus' conception and birth, as well as the idea that God has the power to bring about miracles and events that may seem impossible to humans. The use of the term "pure boy" also underscores the sinless and virtuous nature of Jesus, setting him apart from ordinary human beings.
orig: قال إنما أنا رسول ربك لأهب لك غلاما زكيا

translation: She said, "How can I have a boy while no man has touched me and I have not been unchaste?"
interpretation: This verse is about Mary's reaction when she was told that she would have a child, despite being a virgin. Her response reflects her purity and righteousness, as she expresses her astonishment at the idea of having a child without being touched by a man or engaging in any unchaste behavior. This verse highlights Mary's unwavering faith and submission to God's will, even in the face of seemingly impossible circumstances. It also emphasizes the miraculous nature of Jesus' birth and his unique status as a prophet born to a virgin mother.
orig: قالت أنى يكون لي غلام ولم يمسسني بشر ولم أك بغيا

translation: He said, "Thus [it will be]; your Lord says, 'It is easy for Me, and We will make him a sign to the people and a mercy from Us. And it is a matter [already] decreed.' "
interpretation: This verse is a response to Mary's astonishment at the news of her immaculate conception. The verse emphasizes that God's power is infinite and that nothing is impossible for Him. The birth of Jesus, despite Mary being a virgin, is a sign of God's omnipotence and mercy to humanity. It also highlights that this event was predestined and decreed by God, reflecting His ultimate wisdom and control over all affairs. The verse serves as a reminder to have faith in God's plan and to trust in His wisdom, even when faced with seemingly impossible circumstances.
orig: قال كذلك قال ربك هو علي هين ولنجعله آية للناس ورحمة منا وكان أمرا مقضيا

translation: So she conceived him, and she withdrew with him to a remote place.
interpretation: This verse refers to Mary, the mother of Jesus, who withdrew to a secluded place after conceiving Jesus miraculously. The interpretation is that Mary sought solitude and privacy during her pregnancy to avoid any potential social stigma or gossip, as she was not married. Her withdrawal to a remote location highlights her piety, devotion, and trust in God's plan for her and her child, Jesus. It also emphasizes the miraculous nature of Jesus' conception and birth, which was unlike any other human being.
orig: فحملته فانتبذت به مكانا قصيا

translation: And the pains of childbirth drove her to the trunk of a palm tree. She said, "Oh, I wish I had died before this and was in oblivion, forgotten."
interpretation: This verse speaks to the immense difficulty and pain that Mary experienced during childbirth. Alone and without support, the agony drove her to seek comfort by leaning on a palm tree. In her suffering, she cried out, wishing that she had died before this event so as to avoid the anguish and to be forgotten rather than face the social stigma and challenges that lay ahead of her as an unmarried mother. It highlights the very human emotions and struggles that Mary faced, even as a chosen and righteous woman, and invokes a sense of empathy and understanding for her plight.
orig: فأجاءها المخاض إلى جذع النخلة قالت يا ليتني مت قبل هذا وكنت نسيا منسيا

translation: So he called her from below her, "Do not grieve; your Lord has provided beneath you a stream.
interpretation: This verse is a message of comfort and reassurance from God to Mary. It shows that even in moments of great difficulty and hardship, God provides support and relief to His servants. The stream beneath Mary symbolizes the sustenance and providence that God bestows upon those who trust in Him and remain steadfast. It is a reminder that God never abandons His faithful servants, and that He always provides a way out of hardship and distress. The verse encourages believers to have faith in God's plan and to turn to Him for comfort and guidance during challenging times.
orig: فناداها من تحتها ألا تحزني قد جعل ربك تحتك سريا

translation: And shake toward you the trunk of the palm tree; it will drop upon you ripe, fresh dates.
interpretation: This verse is a reminder of God's mercy and provision. It shows that even in difficult times, God provides sustenance and comfort to those who trust in Him. The verse also symbolizes that with effort and reliance on God, one can overcome hardships and reap the rewards of perseverance. The palm tree represents a source of nourishment and shade, both physical and spiritual. Shaking the tree to obtain the dates is a metaphor for the active effort needed to receive God's blessings and bounties.
orig: وهزي إليك بجذع النخلة تساقط عليك رطبا جنيا

translation: So eat and drink and be contented. And if you see from among humanity anyone, say, 'Indeed, I have vowed to the Most Merciful abstention, so I will not speak today to [any] man.'
interpretation: This verse is instructing Mary, the mother of Jesus, on what to do after she has given birth to him. She is told to eat, drink, and be at peace. If any human approaches her, she is to indicate that she has taken a vow of silence (as a spiritual devotion) to the Most Merciful (one of the names of God), and thus she will not speak to anyone that day. This vow of silence serves to protect her from having to respond to any questions or accusations regarding the birth of her child, since she was known to be unmarried. It places her under God's protection at a time of great vulnerability.
orig: فكلي واشربي وقري عينا فإما ترين من البشر أحدا فقولي إني نذرت للرحمن صوما فلن أكلم اليوم إنسيا

translation: Then she brought him to her people, carrying him. They said, "O Mary, you have certainly done a thing unprecedented.
interpretation: This verse is referring to the reaction of Mary's people when she returned to them carrying her newborn son, Jesus. They were shocked and astonished, accusing her of doing something unheard of and scandalous, as she was known to be a chaste and pious woman. The verse highlights the extraordinary nature of Jesus' birth and the initial disbelief and judgment that Mary faced from her community. It also sets the stage for the subsequent verses, where Jesus miraculously speaks in defense of his mother's innocence and proclaims his prophethood.
orig: فأتت به قومها تحمله قالوا يا مريم لقد جئت شيئا فريا

translation: O sister of Aaron, your father was not a man of evil, nor was your mother unchaste.
interpretation: This verse is addressing Mary, the mother of Jesus, and defending her honor and chastity. By referring to her as "sister of Aaron", it is connecting her to a righteous family and lineage. The verse asserts that Mary's father was not an evil man and her mother was not unchaste, thus refuting any accusations or slander made against Mary or her family. It is a strong defense of Mary's character and virtue, emphasizing her purity and righteousness, despite the extraordinary circumstances of her pregnancy with Jesus.
orig: يا أخت هارون ما كان أبوك امرأ سوء وما كانت أمك بغيا

translation: Then she pointed to him. They said, "How can we speak to one who is in the cradle a child?"
interpretation: This verse is referring to the miraculous event when Mary, the mother of Jesus, was accused of adultery after giving birth to Jesus. When her people saw the baby, they questioned how she could have had a child without being married. In response, Mary pointed to the infant Jesus, indicating that they should ask him. The people were astonished, wondering how they could speak to a mere infant in the cradle. This verse highlights the miraculous nature of Jesus, who was able to speak and defend his mother even as a newborn, demonstrating his divine wisdom and status as a prophet chosen by God.
orig: فأشارت إليه قالوا كيف نكلم من كان في المهد صبيا

translation: He said, "Indeed, I am the servant of Allah. He has given me the Scripture and made me a prophet."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the humility and servitude of Jesus (peace be upon him) to Allah. Despite his miraculous birth and the honor of being chosen as a prophet, Jesus affirms that he is ultimately a servant of Allah, who has bestowed upon him the revelation (the Scripture) and the status of prophethood. This interpretation highlights the importance of recognizing one's subservience to Allah, even for those who are granted special favors or elevated positions. It also counters the notion of Jesus being divine or the son of God, as he himself acknowledges his role as a servant and prophet of Allah.
orig: قال إني عبد الله آتاني الكتاب وجعلني نبيا

translation: And He has made me blessed wherever I am and has enjoined upon me prayer and zakah as long as I remain alive
interpretation: This verse speaks to the special status and role of Jesus. Wherever he went, he was a source of blessings and goodness for the people around him. God also instructed him to establish prayer and give charity throughout his life, emphasizing the importance of spiritual devotion and caring for the needy. This indicates that Jesus was not just a recipient of God's blessings, but had the responsibility to worship God and serve humanity. The fact that these were lifelong commandments underscore the consistency of his mission and message. It also suggests that blessings flow through living in accordance with God's will.
orig: وجعلني مباركا أين ما كنت وأوصاني بالصلاة والزكاة ما دمت حيا

translation: And dutiful to my mother, and He has not made me a wretched tyrant.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of being kind and obedient to one's mother. It also suggests that being a tyrant or oppressor is a wretched and miserable state, and that God's grace and guidance saves one from such a fate. The verse implies that a truly blessed and righteous person is one who treats his parents, especially his mother, with love, respect and dutifulness. Obeying and honoring one's mother is thus linked with being saved from arrogance, cruelty and wickedness in this verse.
orig: وبرا بوالدتي ولم يجعلني جبارا شقيا

translation: And peace be upon me the day I was born and the day I will die and the day I am raised alive.
interpretation: This verse conveys the idea that the Prophet Jesus (peace be upon him) was blessed and protected by Allah throughout his life, from his birth until his death and eventual resurrection on the Day of Judgment. It emphasizes the continuity of Allah's favor upon him and highlights the significant stages of his existence. The verse also serves as a reminder to all believers that true peace and security come from submitting to Allah's will and seeking His protection throughout one's life and in the Hereafter.
orig: والسلام علي يوم ولدت ويوم أموت ويوم أبعث حيا

translation: That is Jesus, the son of Mary - the word of truth about which they are in dispute.
interpretation: This verse affirms the truth about Jesus, that he is the son of Mary and a prophet of God. It points out that despite this truth, people still dispute and differ in their beliefs about him. Some consider him divine or the son of God, while others reject him entirely. The Qur'an asserts that he was a human prophet and messenger, not divine himself, and that the truth about his nature is clear despite the doubts and disputes that surround him. The verse emphasizes the importance of accepting the Qur'anic account as the accurate truth about Jesus.
orig: ذلك عيسى ابن مريم قول الحق الذي فيه يمترون

translation: It is not [befitting] for Allah to take a son; exalted is He! When He decrees an affair, He only says to it, "Be," and it is.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute oneness and uniqueness of Allah, rejecting the notion that He could have a son or offspring. It asserts that such a concept is beneath His divine majesty and perfection. When Allah wills something to happen, He merely commands it to "Be" and it comes into existence, highlighting His omnipotence and supreme authority over all creation. The verse affirms that Allah is self-sufficient and does not require any partners, associates, or offspring, as He is the sole creator and sustainer of the universe.
orig: ما كان لله أن يتخذ من ولد سبحانه إذا قضى أمرا فإنما يقول له كن فيكون

translation: And indeed, Allah is my Lord and your Lord, so worship Him. This is a straight path.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the oneness of Allah and the importance of worshipping Him alone. It reminds us that Allah is the Lord and Creator of all, and that submitting to His will and following His straight path is the way to success and salvation. The straight path refers to Islam, the religion of monotheism and complete submission to Allah. By sincerely worshipping Allah alone and obeying His commands, one can hope to attain His pleasure and be granted eternal paradise in the Hereafter.
orig: وإن الله ربي وربكم فاعبدوه هذا صراط مستقيم

translation: Then the sects differed [i.e., separated] among them, so woe to those who disbelieved from the sight of a tremendous Day.
interpretation: This verse warns of the consequences of disbelief and rejecting the truth. It alludes to the fact that people will be divided into different groups based on their beliefs and actions in this world. Those who rejected faith and denied the signs of Allah will face a severe punishment on the Day of Judgment, which is described as a "tremendous Day". The word "woe" emphasizes the severity and inevitability of the punishment that awaits the disbelievers when they witness the horrors of that Day and realize the error of their ways. This serves as a reminder for people to carefully consider their choices and to follow the path of truth and righteousness to avoid such a fate.
orig: فاختلف الأحزاب من بينهم فويل للذين كفروا من مشهد يوم عظيم

translation: You will see them and hear them on the Day they come to Us, but today the wrongdoers are clearly astray.
interpretation: This verse is a stark reminder of the Day of Judgment, when all of humanity will stand before Allah. On that day, the truth will be clear and the wrongdoers will realize their misguidance. However, in this worldly life, those who choose to wrong themselves and others are in manifest error, unable to see the truth despite the signs and guidance provided by Allah. It is a warning to be mindful of our actions and to strive for righteousness, for the ultimate accounting will take place in the Hereafter, where the consequences of our deeds will become evident.
orig: أسمع بهم وأبصر يوم يأتوننا لكن الظالمون اليوم في ضلال مبين

translation: And warn them, [O Muhammad], of the Day of Regret, when the matter will be concluded; and [yet], they are in [a state of] heedlessness, and they do not believe.
interpretation: This verse is a reminder to mankind about the Day of Judgment, also known as the Day of Regret. It is a warning to those who are heedless and do not believe in the message of Islam. On that day, all matters will be concluded, and it will be too late for those who did not heed the warning and lived their lives in a state of heedlessness. The verse emphasizes the importance of being mindful of one's actions in this life, as they will have consequences in the Hereafter. It is a call to believe in the message of Islam and to live one's life in accordance with its teachings, so as to avoid regret on the Day of Judgment.
orig: وأنذرهم يوم الحسرة إذ قضي الأمر وهم في غفلة وهم لا يؤمنون

translation: Indeed, it is We who will inherit the earth and whoever is on it, and to Us they will be returned.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the ultimate ownership and authority of Allah over the earth and all its inhabitants. It reminds us that no matter how much power, wealth, or influence people may possess in this world, it is all temporary and will eventually return to Allah. The verse also implies the inevitability of death and the Day of Judgment, when all souls will be brought back to Allah to face the consequences of their deeds. It serves as a powerful reminder for humankind to focus on their relationship with Allah and to live their lives in accordance with His guidance, as everything in this world is fleeting and the only thing that truly matters is one's standing with Allah in the Hereafter.
orig: إنا نحن نرث الأرض ومن عليها وإلينا يرجعون

translation: And mention in the Book [the story of] Abraham. Indeed, he was a man of truth and a prophet.
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance and status of Prophet Abraham (peace be upon him) in Islam. By describing him as "Siddiq" (a man of truth), it emphasizes his unwavering commitment to honesty, integrity, and upholding the truth in all aspects of his life. The verse also confirms his prophethood, indicating that he was chosen by Allah to receive divine revelation and guide his people to the straight path. As a prophet and a man of truth, Abraham serves as an exemplary role model for all believers, demonstrating the virtues of sincerity, steadfastness, and complete submission to the will of Allah.
orig: واذكر في الكتاب إبراهيم إنه كان صديقا نبيا

translation: When he said to his father, "O my father, why do you worship that which does not hear and does not see and will not benefit you at all?"
interpretation: This verse is addressing the importance of worshipping the One True God, Allah, and not false idols or deities that have no power or ability to benefit or harm. It emphasizes using reason and logic to recognize that only Allah is worthy of worship, as He is the All-Hearing, All-Seeing, and the only One who can truly benefit or harm us. The verse encourages us to advise others, even our own family members, to abandon the worship of false gods and to turn to the worship of Allah alone.
orig: إذ قال لأبيه يا أبت لم تعبد ما لا يسمع ولا يبصر ولا يغني عنك شيئا

translation: O my father, indeed there has come to me of knowledge that which has not come to you, so follow me; I will guide you to an even path.
interpretation: In this verse, the son is respectfully addressing his father, acknowledging that he has received knowledge and guidance that his father does not possess. He invites his father to follow him on the straight path, which represents the path of righteousness and truth. This verse highlights the importance of seeking and following divine guidance, even if it means going against the beliefs or practices of one's family or society. It also emphasizes the value of humility and openness to learning from others, regardless of their age or status.
orig: يا أبت إني قد جاءني من العلم ما لم يأتك فاتبعني أهدك صراطا سويا

translation: O my father, do not worship Satan. Indeed Satan has ever been, to the Most Merciful, disobedient.
interpretation: In this verse, a righteous son is advising his father not to worship Satan or obey his temptations and whispers. He reminds his father that Satan is the one who rebelled against Allah, the Most Merciful, and disobeyed His commands out of pride and arrogance. The son is appealing to his father's conscience to abandon the path of Satan and submit to the will of Allah instead. This highlights the importance of giving sincere advice to one's family members, especially parents, to follow the straight path and reject the deceptions of Satan.
orig: يا أبت لا تعبد الشيطان إن الشيطان كان للرحمن عصيا

translation: O my father, indeed I fear that there will touch you a punishment from the Most Merciful so you would be to Satan a companion [in Hellfire].
interpretation: In this verse, the prophet Abraham is pleading with his father to abandon the worship of idols and to submit to the one true God, Allah. Abraham expresses his deep concern that if his father persists in idol worship, he will incur the wrath and punishment of Allah, the Most Merciful. As a consequence of this punishment, his father would become a companion of Satan in the Hellfire. This verse highlights the importance of worshipping Allah alone and the grave consequences of associating partners with Him. It also demonstrates Abraham's love for his father and his desire to save him from the terrible fate of the disbelievers, even as his father rejects his message.
orig: يا أبت إني أخاف أن يمسك عذاب من الرحمن فتكون للشيطان وليا

translation: He said, "Do you reject my gods, O Abraham? If you do not desist, I will surely stone you, so leave me for a long time."
interpretation: This verse shows the confrontation between Prophet Abraham and his people who worshipped idols. The speaker, likely Abraham's father or a leader of his community, is angry and threatens Abraham with stoning and banishment for rejecting their gods and criticizing their idol worship. It reflects the strong opposition Abraham faced in calling people to monotheism and the courage he displayed in holding firm to his beliefs despite the dangers. The verse captures the tension between following the truth versus blindly adhering to ancestral traditions, and the sacrifices that may be required in standing up for one's faith.
orig: قال أراغب أنت عن آلهتي يا إبراهيم لئن لم تنته لأرجمنك واهجرني مليا

translation: He said, "Peace be upon you. I will ask forgiveness for you from my Lord. Indeed, He is ever gracious to me."
interpretation: This verse shows the importance of seeking forgiveness and maintaining good relationships with family members. The speaker, believed to be Prophet Ibrahim (Abraham), is bidding farewell to a family member, possibly his father or uncle, with a greeting of peace. Despite their differences in belief, Ibrahim still cares for his relative and promises to pray for God's forgiveness on his behalf. This demonstrates Ibrahim's compassion, humility, and faith in God's mercy. It also emphasizes the value of keeping familial ties and showing kindness even towards those who may not share the same beliefs or values.
orig: قال سلام عليك سأستغفر لك ربي إنه كان بي حفيا

translation: And I will withdraw from you and what you call upon besides Allah, and I will call upon my Lord. Perhaps I will not be, by calling to my Lord, unhappy.
interpretation: This verse shows the importance of turning away from false deities and focusing solely on worshipping Allah. The speaker, believed to be Prophet Ibrahim, declares his intention to distance himself from those who worship others besides Allah and instead devote himself completely to calling upon his Lord. He expresses hope that by sincerely supplicating to Allah alone, he will find contentment and avoid the misery that comes from associating partners with God. This highlights the concept of pure monotheism (tawheed) and the need to abandon all forms of idolatry or polytheism in order to attain true happiness and success in both this life and the hereafter.
orig: وأعتزلكم وما تدعون من دون الله وأدعو ربي عسى ألا أكون بدعاء ربي شقيا

translation: So when he had withdrawn from them and that which they were worshipping other than Allah, We gave him Isaac and Jacob, and each [of them] We made a prophet.
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of staying away from false deities and remaining steadfast in the worship of Allah alone. When Prophet Ibrahim (Abraham) withdrew from his people and their idolatrous practices, Allah rewarded him by blessing him with two righteous sons, Isaac and Jacob, both of whom were made prophets. This shows that when a person dedicates himself sincerely to Allah and turns away from all forms of polytheism, Allah grants him blessings and guides his offspring to the right path as well. It also emphasizes the significance of raising children with strong faith and moral values, as they can become the torchbearers of the divine message for future generations.
orig: فلما اعتزلهم وما يعبدون من دون الله وهبنا له إسحاق ويعقوب وكلا جعلنا نبيا

translation: And We granted them of Our mercy, and We made for them a reputation of high honour.
interpretation: In this verse, Allah is bestowing His favors upon certain individuals. He grants them His special mercy, which could refer to both spiritual and worldly blessings. Additionally, Allah elevates their status and reputation among people, making them highly respected and honored. This "lisan sidq" or "reputation of high honour" indicates that they are known for their truthfulness, righteousness, and noble character. Such individuals are held in high esteem by society due to their virtuous qualities and conduct. This verse emphasizes that when Allah chooses to bless someone, He not only grants them internal peace and tranquility but also elevates their social standing and makes them respected leaders or role models within their communities.
orig: ووهبنا لهم من رحمتنا وجعلنا لهم لسان صدق عليا

translation: And mention in the Book, Moses. Indeed, he was chosen, and he was a messenger and a prophet.
interpretation: This verse highlights the special status of Moses as a prophet chosen by Allah. He was not only a messenger who received divine revelation, but also a prophet who was sent to guide his people. The verse emphasizes his sincerity, devotion and complete submission to the will of Allah. It reminds us that Moses was among the elite of Allah's messengers, and his life story serves as an example for believers to emulate in their own spiritual journeys of faith and obedience to Allah.
orig: واذكر في الكتاب موسى إنه كان مخلصا وكان رسولا نبيا

translation: And We called him from the right side of the mount, and We brought him near in communion.
interpretation: This verse refers to the special status and closeness that Allah granted to Prophet Moses (peace be upon him). Allah called Moses from the right side of Mount Sinai, which is considered a blessed and sacred place, and brought him near to Himself to speak with him directly. This event highlights the unique relationship between Allah and Moses, as Allah chose him to be His prophet and messenger and honored him with direct communication. It signifies the importance of Moses' prophetic mission and the guidance he received from Allah to lead the Children of Israel. The verse emphasizes the spiritual elevation and privileged position of Moses in the sight of Allah.
orig: وناديناه من جانب الطور الأيمن وقربناه نجيا

translation: And We granted him, out of Our mercy, his brother Aaron as a prophet.
interpretation: This verse highlights the mercy and grace of Allah towards His prophets. Allah not only blessed Moses with prophethood but also granted him the companionship and support of his brother Aaron, who was also made a prophet. This shows that Allah provides help and guidance to His chosen servants in various ways, including through family members who share the same mission. It also emphasizes the importance of having righteous and supportive companions on the path of faith and in the face of challenges.
orig: ووهبنا له من رحمتنا أخاه هارون نبيا

translation: And mention in the Book, Ishmael. Indeed, he was true to his promise, and he was a messenger and a prophet.
interpretation: This verse highlights the noble character of Prophet Ishmael (peace be upon him), who was known for his truthfulness and for fulfilling his promises. It also affirms his status as a messenger and prophet of Allah, chosen to convey His message to humanity. The mention of Ishmael's truthfulness and commitment to keeping his word serves as an example for believers to emulate, emphasizing the importance of honesty and reliability in one's dealings with others and in fulfilling one's obligations to Allah.
orig: واذكر في الكتاب إسماعيل إنه كان صادق الوعد وكان رسولا نبيا

translation: He used to enjoin his people to prayer and zakah, and he was pleasing to his Lord.
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of enjoining others, especially one's family, to pray and give zakah (obligatory charity). It also emphasizes the significance of being pleasing to Allah through one's actions and conduct. The verse suggests that a person who encourages others to fulfill their religious obligations and maintains a righteous character will be favored by Allah and will attain His pleasure. This serves as a reminder for believers to not only focus on their own spiritual growth but also to guide and support others in their religious duties, ultimately seeking the satisfaction and approval of their Lord.
orig: وكان يأمر أهله بالصلاة والزكاة وكان عند ربه مرضيا

translation: And mention in the Book, Idrees. Indeed, he was a man of truth and a prophet.
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance and status of Prophet Idrees (Enoch) in Islamic tradition. By mentioning him in the Qur'an, Allah emphasizes that Idrees was a truthful man and a prophet, indicating his high moral character and his role in conveying Allah's message to his people. The verse serves as a reminder for Muslims to learn from the example of Prophet Idrees and to strive for truthfulness and righteousness in their own lives.
orig: واذكر في الكتاب إدريس إنه كان صديقا نبيا

translation: And We raised him to a high station.
interpretation: This verse refers to the Prophet Idris (Enoch), who was mentioned in the previous verse. Allah honored him by elevating his status and granting him a lofty position among the righteous. This high station could refer to his spiritual rank, his physical ascension to the heavens, or both. It signifies that Allah rewards His devoted servants and prophets by raising their status and granting them special privileges and nearness to Him. The verse encourages believers to follow the example of Prophet Idris in righteousness and devotion to Allah, with the promise of being elevated to a higher state of spiritual purity and closeness to the Divine.
orig: ورفعناه مكانا عليا

translation: Those were the ones upon whom Allah bestowed favor from among the prophets of the descendants of Adam and of those We carried [in the ship] with Noah, and of the descendants of Abraham and Israel, and of those whom We guided and chose. When the verses of the Most Merciful were recited to them, they fell in prostration and weeping.
interpretation: This verse highlights the special status and honor bestowed upon the prophets chosen by Allah. They were the recipients of divine favor and guidance, descending from the lineages of esteemed figures like Adam, Noah, Abraham, and Israel. The prophets' deep devotion and reverence for Allah is exemplified by their response to the recitation of the Qur'an - falling into heartfelt prostration and weeping, signifying their complete submission, humility, and emotional connection to the words of their Lord. This verse serves as a reminder for believers to emulate the prophets' sincerity and to be moved by the profound impact of Allah's revelations.
orig: أولئك الذين أنعم الله عليهم من النبيين من ذرية آدم وممن حملنا مع نوح ومن ذرية إبراهيم وإسرائيل وممن هدينا واجتبينا إذا تتلى عليهم آيات الرحمن خروا سجدا وبكيا

translation: But there came after them successors who neglected prayer and pursued desires; so they are going to meet evil -
interpretation: This verse warns about the consequences of neglecting one's religious duties and pursuing worldly desires instead. It suggests that those who come after a righteous generation and fail to uphold the same values and practices will face spiritual loss and punishment in the afterlife. The "evil" mentioned could refer to the negative outcomes in this world, such as corruption and moral decay, as well as the ultimate punishment of Hell in the hereafter for those who consistently deviate from the straight path. The verse emphasizes the importance of maintaining regular prayer and resisting temptations in order to avoid such a fate.
orig: فخلف من بعدهم خلف أضاعوا الصلاة واتبعوا الشهوات فسوف يلقون غيا

translation: Except for those who repent, believe, and do righteous deeds. For them will be an entrance into Paradise, and they will not be wronged at all.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of sincere repentance, true faith, and righteous actions. It offers hope and reassurance to those who have strayed from the right path, indicating that it is never too late to turn back to Allah and seek His forgiveness. The verse promises that those who sincerely repent, embrace faith, and perform good deeds will be granted entry into Paradise without any injustice or diminution of their rewards. It highlights the mercy and forgiveness of Allah, showing that He is always ready to accept the repentance of His servants, regardless of their past sins, as long as they turn to Him with sincerity and strive to lead a righteous life.
orig: إلا من تاب وآمن وعمل صالحا فأولئك يدخلون الجنة ولا يظلمون شيئا

translation: Gardens of perpetual residence which the Most Merciful has promised His servants in the unseen. Indeed, His promise has ever been coming.
interpretation: This verse refers to the eternal gardens of Paradise that Allah, the Most Merciful, has promised to His righteous servants, even though they have not seen it yet. This promise of Allah is certain to be fulfilled, as Allah always keeps His promises. The mention of "the unseen" emphasizes the fact that the believers have faith in the unseen aspects of the afterlife, trusting in Allah's promise without having witnessed it with their own eyes. The verse serves as an encouragement and reassurance to the believers, reminding them that their faith and good deeds will be rewarded with the eternal bliss of Paradise.
orig: جنات عدن التي وعد الرحمن عباده بالغيب إنه كان وعده مأتيا

translation: No vain discourse will they hear therein, nor anything but salutations of Peace: And they will have therein their sustenance, morning and evening.
interpretation: This verse speaks about the blessings and rewards that await the righteous believers in Paradise. It emphasizes that in Paradise, they will not hear any vain, useless, or sinful speech, but only words of peace and tranquility. This creates an atmosphere of serenity and positivity. Additionally, the verse mentions that the inhabitants of Paradise will receive their provisions at all times, morning and evening, without any interruption or difficulty. This signifies the continuous blessings and ease that they will experience in the afterlife as a reward for their faith and good deeds in this world.
orig: لا يسمعون فيها لغوا إلا سلاما ولهم رزقهم فيها بكرة وعشيا

translation: That is Paradise, which We give as inheritance to those of Our servants who were fearing of Allah.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Paradise is the ultimate reward for those who live a life of righteousness and piety. It is an inheritance, a gift from Allah to His devoted servants who have spent their lives in obedience and submission to His will. The verse highlights the importance of taqwa, the consciousness and fear of Allah, as the key characteristic of those who will be granted this immense blessing. It serves as a reminder and motivation for believers to strive for piety in all aspects of their lives, knowing that their ultimate destination and reward is the eternal bliss of Paradise.
orig: تلك الجنة التي نورث من عبادنا من كان تقيا

translation: And we do not descend except by the command of your Lord. To Him belongs what is before us and what is behind us and what is in between. And never is your Lord forgetful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute obedience and submission of the angels to Allah's commands. They only descend to earth and carry out tasks by His order. Everything in the past, present, and future belongs to Him and is under His control. The verse also highlights Allah's perfect knowledge and awareness, affirming that He never forgets or overlooks anything. It serves as a reminder of Allah's omnipotence, omniscience, and all-encompassing authority over all matters in the universe.
orig: وما نتنزل إلا بأمر ربك له ما بين أيدينا وما خلفنا وما بين ذلك وما كان ربك نسيا

translation: Lord of the heavens and the earth and whatever is between them - so worship Him and have patience for His worship. Do you know of any similarity to Him?
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute uniqueness and oneness of Allah, the Lord and Creator of the entire universe. It calls upon the believers to direct their worship solely to Him and to persevere in His worship with patience and dedication. The rhetorical question at the end of the verse, "Do you know of any similarity to Him?", underscores the fact that there is nothing and no one comparable to Allah in His divine attributes and perfection. It serves as a reminder to humans that Allah alone deserves our worship and that we should not associate any partners with Him or attribute any similarities to Him.
orig: رب السماوات والأرض وما بينهما فاعبده واصطبر لعبادته هل تعلم له سميا

translation: And man says, "When I am dead, am I going to be brought forth alive?"
interpretation: This verse is questioning the skepticism and disbelief of those who deny the resurrection and afterlife. It highlights the limited perspective of human beings, who may find it difficult to comprehend or accept the concept of being brought back to life after death. The rhetorical question posed in this verse serves as a reminder that the power of Allah is beyond human understanding and that the resurrection and judgment in the Hereafter are an integral part of Islamic faith. It encourages believers to have faith in Allah's promise and to live their lives with the awareness that they will be held accountable for their deeds in the afterlife.
orig: ويقول الإنسان أإذا ما مت لسوف أخرج حيا

translation: Does man not remember that We created him before, while he was nothing?
interpretation: This verse is a reminder to mankind that Allah created them from nothing, and that they should be humble and grateful for their existence. It emphasizes the power and mercy of Allah in bringing humans into being, even though they were previously non-existent. The verse also implies that since Allah created humans, He has the ability to resurrect them after death for the Day of Judgment. It serves as a call to recognize one's origins and to submit to the will of the Creator.
orig: أولا يذكر الإنسان أنا خلقناه من قبل ولم يك شيئا

translation: So by your Lord, We will surely gather them and the devils; then We will bring them to be present around Hell upon their knees.
interpretation: This verse is a strong oath from Allah, swearing by Himself, that on the Day of Judgment, He will gather all the disbelievers and the devils who misled them, and bring them together to be present around Hell, humiliated and on their knees. It emphasizes Allah's power and control over all beings, and serves as a severe warning to those who reject faith and follow the path of Satan, that their ultimate end will be in the punishment of Hell, in a state of disgrace and submission. The verse aims to instill fear and encourage people to abandon falsehood and embrace the truth of Islam.
orig: فوربك لنحشرنهم والشياطين ثم لنحضرنهم حول جهنم جثيا

translation: Then We will surely drag out from every sect those of them who were worst in obstinate rebellion against the Most Merciful.
interpretation: This verse warns that on the Day of Judgment, God will separate from each group or sect those individuals who were most rebellious and defiant against Him. It suggests that even within religious or ideological groups, there will be varying degrees of disobedience to God, and the worst offenders from each will be singled out for punishment. The verse emphasizes God's ultimate justice and that no one who persistently rebels against His mercy and guidance will escape accountability, regardless of their claimed affiliation or identity.
orig: ثم لننزعن من كل شيعة أيهم أشد على الرحمن عتيا

translation: Then indeed, We are most knowing of those who are most worthy of burning therein.
interpretation: In this verse, Allah is asserting His knowledge and power over the ultimate fate of mankind. He knows best who deserves the punishment of the Hellfire due to their disbelief, transgressions, and rejection of His messages. It serves as a warning to those who persist in their wrongdoings, reminding them that Allah is fully aware of their actions and will judge them accordingly in the Hereafter. The verse also implies that no one can escape Allah's justice and that He will determine the appropriate consequences for each individual based on their deeds and intentions.
orig: ثم لنحن أعلم بالذين هم أولى بها صليا

translation: And there is none of you except he will come to it. This is upon your Lord an inevitability decreed.
interpretation: This verse refers to the fact that every soul will pass over Hell on the Day of Judgment. It is a destined and unavoidable event decreed by Allah. However, this does not mean that every person will enter Hell. The righteous believers will be saved and pass over it safely, while the disbelievers and sinners will fall into it. This verse serves as a reminder of the reality of the Hereafter and the consequences of one's deeds in this life. It encourages individuals to strive for righteousness and be mindful of their ultimate fate.
orig: وإن منكم إلا واردها كان على ربك حتما مقضيا

translation: Then We will save those who feared Allah and leave the wrongdoers within it, on their knees.
interpretation: This verse speaks about the Day of Judgment, when Allah will distinguish between the righteous and the wrongdoers. Those who were mindful of Allah and followed His guidance in this worldly life will be saved from the punishment of Hell. They will be granted salvation and admitted into Paradise by the mercy of Allah. As for the wrongdoers and the disbelievers who rejected Allah's signs and transgressed against His limits, they will be left humiliated in the Fire of Hell, on their knees in a state of despair and regret. This verse emphasizes the importance of righteousness and mindfulness of Allah in this life, and that ultimately, everyone will face the consequences of their deeds in the Hereafter, either earning salvation or facing destruction.
orig: ثم ننجي الذين اتقوا ونذر الظالمين فيها جثيا

translation: And when Our clear verses are recited to them, those who disbelieve say to those who believe, "Which of [our] two groups is best in position and best in association?"
interpretation: This verse is referring to the attitude of the disbelievers towards the believers when they hear the clear verses of the Qur'an. Instead of reflecting on the truth and guidance contained in these verses, the disbelievers try to belittle the believers by claiming that their own group is superior in status and has better gatherings or associations. It shows their arrogance and lack of humility in the face of divine revelation. They are more concerned with worldly status and social gatherings than with the truth and the eternal consequences of their choices. The verse highlights the misplaced priorities and flawed thinking of those who reject faith in favor of temporary worldly gains.
orig: وإذا تتلى عليهم آياتنا بينات قال الذين كفروا للذين آمنوا أي الفريقين خير مقاما وأحسن نديا

translation: And how many a generation before them did We destroy who were better in possessions and [outward] appearance?
interpretation: This verse serves as a reminder that worldly possessions and outward appearances are ultimately fleeting and meaningless in the face of God's judgment. It emphasizes that even those nations or generations who may have seemed superior in wealth and power were not spared from destruction when they incurred the wrath of Allah due to their transgressions and disobedience. The verse implies that material success and grandeur should not lead to arrogance or a false sense of invincibility, as all will face the consequences of their deeds in the Hereafter. It encourages humility, righteousness, and a focus on spiritual growth rather than temporary worldly gains.
orig: وكم أهلكنا قبلهم من قرن هم أحسن أثاثا ورئيا

translation: Say, "Whoever is in error - let the Most Merciful extend for him an extension [in wealth and time] until, when they see that which they were promised - either punishment [in this world] or the Hour [of resurrection] - they will come to know who is worst in position and weaker in soldiers."
interpretation: This verse is a warning to those who persist in disbelief and error. It states that God, out of His mercy, may grant them respite and allow them to enjoy the pleasures of this world for a time. However, when the promised punishment or the Day of Judgment arrives, they will realize their grave mistake and understand that their position is the worst imaginable, and their forces are utterly weak and powerless compared to God's might. The verse emphasizes the severity of the consequences awaiting those who choose to remain in error, despite God's gracious offer of guidance and mercy.
orig: قل من كان في الضلالة فليمدد له الرحمن مدا حتى إذا رأوا ما يوعدون إما العذاب وإما الساعة فسيعلمون من هو شر مكانا وأضعف جندا

translation: And Allah increases those who were guided, in guidance, and the enduring good deeds are better to your Lord for reward and better for recourse.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah grants further guidance to those who are already on the right path. It also highlights the importance of performing good deeds that have a lasting impact, as they are considered the best in the sight of Allah in terms of reward and ultimate return. The verse encourages believers to continuously seek Allah's guidance and engage in righteous actions that will benefit them both in this world and in the Hereafter.
orig: ويزيد الله الذين اهتدوا هدى والباقيات الصالحات خير عند ربك ثوابا وخير مردا

translation: Then, have you seen he who disbelieved in Our verses and said, "I will surely be given wealth and children [in the next life]"?
interpretation: This verse is a rhetorical question that highlights the arrogance and delusion of those who reject God's signs and revelations, yet still believe that they will be granted wealth and offspring in the Hereafter. It emphasizes the futility of such thinking, as the disbelievers have no basis for their assumptions and are not guaranteed anything in the afterlife. The verse serves as a warning against the false sense of entitlement and the lack of gratitude towards God's blessings, reminding believers to remain humble and steadfast in their faith.
orig: أفرأيت الذي كفر بآياتنا وقال لأوتين مالا وولدا

translation: Did he look into the unseen, or has he taken a covenant with the Most Merciful?
interpretation: This verse questions whether someone has access to the knowledge of the unseen or has made a special pact with Allah. It implies that no one can claim to have such knowledge or a special relationship with Allah unless He Himself has granted it. The verse emphasizes that the knowledge of the unseen belongs only to Allah and that no one can make claims about it without His permission. It serves as a reminder to be humble and not to make false claims about having access to divine knowledge or a special status with Allah.
orig: أطلع الغيب أم اتخذ عند الرحمن عهدا

translation: No! We will record what he says and extend for him from the punishment extensively.
interpretation: This verse is a stern warning to those who reject the truth and persist in their disbelief. Allah declares that He will record every word they utter against the truth, and as a consequence, He will increase their punishment in the Hereafter. It emphasizes the severity of rejecting Allah's message and the grave consequences that await those who do so. The verse also implies that the more one rebels against the truth, the greater their punishment will be, as Allah will extend it extensively. This serves as a reminder for mankind to be mindful of their words and actions, and to embrace the truth before it is too late.
orig: كلا سنكتب ما يقول ونمد له من العذاب مدا

translation: And We will inherit from him what he says, and he will come to Us alone.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that ultimately, all of a person's worldly possessions and claims will be left behind, and they will face Allah alone on the Day of Judgment. It serves as a reminder that one should focus on their deeds and relationship with Allah, rather than being preoccupied with worldly matters and empty claims, as these will be of no benefit in the Hereafter when each individual will be held accountable for their actions.
orig: ونرثه ما يقول ويأتينا فردا

translation: And they have taken besides Allah [false] deities that they would be for them [a source of] honor.
interpretation: This verse criticizes those who worship false gods or idols, believing that these deities will grant them power, strength, and honor. However, the Qur'an emphasizes that true honor and power come only from Allah, the One True God. By relying on false deities, these people are deluding themselves and straying from the path of righteousness. The verse serves as a reminder that one should put their faith and trust in Allah alone, as He is the only source of genuine strength and honor in this world and the hereafter.
orig: واتخذوا من دون الله آلهة ليكونوا لهم عزا

translation: No! They will deny their worship of them and will be against them opponents.
interpretation: This verse warns that those who worship false deities and idols will ultimately face the reality that these objects of worship will not help them. On the Day of Judgment, the worshippers will deny having worshipped these false gods, but it will be too late. The very idols they worshipped will turn against them, unable to offer any assistance or intercession on their behalf before Allah. It highlights the futility of worshipping anything other than Allah and the severe consequences of polytheism and idolatry in the Hereafter.
orig: كلا سيكفرون بعبادتهم ويكونون عليهم ضدا

translation: Did you not see that We have sent the devils upon the disbelievers, inciting them [to evil] with [constant] incitement?
interpretation: This verse is indicating that Allah has allowed the devils and evil forces to influence and tempt the disbelievers, urging them strongly towards sin, disbelief and evil deeds. It suggests that those who reject faith are more susceptible to the whisperings and provocations of the devils. The devils act to constantly incite and provoke the disbelievers, aiming to lead them further astray. This highlights the spiritual battle between good and evil, with the devils working to misguide mankind, while Allah guides whom He wills to the straight path.
