It also underscores the importance of seeking refuge in Allah from the influences of the devils and shayateen.
orig: ألم تر أنا أرسلنا الشياطين على الكافرين تؤزهم أزا

translation: So be not in haste against them, for We only count out to them a (limited) number (of days).
interpretation: This verse is a reminder to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and the believers not to be impatient or hasty in seeking punishment for the disbelievers. It emphasizes that Allah has granted the disbelievers a limited time in this world, and He is counting down their days. The verse implies that the disbelievers will face the consequences of their actions in the Hereafter, and their ultimate fate is with Allah. It encourages patience and trust in Allah's plan, knowing that He will hold the disbelievers accountable for their deeds in due time.
orig: فلا تعجل عليهم إنما نعد لهم عدا

translation: The Day We will gather the righteous to the Most Merciful in a delegation
interpretation: This verse refers to the Day of Judgment when the righteous believers who feared Allah and followed His commands will be honored and gathered together as a delegation before Allah, the Most Merciful. This signifies their special status and the reward of being in the presence of their Lord. The term "wafd" used here denotes a group of people sent for a noble cause, indicating the great honor bestowed upon the pious. This gathering highlights the mercy and grace of Allah towards His righteous servants, distinguishing them from the disbelievers and sinners.
orig: يوم نحشر المتقين إلى الرحمن وفدا

translation: And We will drive the criminals to Hell in thirst.
interpretation: This verse is a warning to those who reject God's message and persist in wrongdoing. It emphasizes that on the Day of Judgment, the criminals and sinners will be driven to Hell, suffering from extreme thirst as a consequence of their evil deeds. The use of the word "وردا" (wirdan) implies that they will be herded like thirsty animals, highlighting their desperation and helplessness. This interpretation serves as a reminder of the severe punishment awaiting those who choose to disobey God and commit injustices in this world, encouraging individuals to seek righteousness and repentance.
orig: ونسوق المجرمين إلى جهنم وردا

translation: None will have [power of] intercession except he who has taken from the Most Merciful a covenant.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that on the Day of Judgment, no one will have the power to intercede on behalf of others except those who have been granted permission by Allah, the Most Merciful. This permission is referred to as a "covenant" or a special agreement between the intercessor and Allah. It suggests that intercession is not a right that anyone can claim, but rather a privilege granted by Allah to those He chooses, such as prophets, righteous individuals, and martyrs. The verse also implies that those seeking intercession should strive to establish a strong connection with Allah and seek His pleasure through righteous deeds and sincere worship.
orig: لا يملكون الشفاعة إلا من اتخذ عند الرحمن عهدا

translation: And they say, "The Most Merciful has taken [for Himself] a son."
interpretation: This verse is a response to those who falsely claim that Allah has taken a son or offspring. It is a rejection of such a notion, as it goes against the fundamental Islamic belief in the oneness and uniqueness of Allah. The Qur'an repeatedly emphasizes that Allah is One, without partners or offspring, and that He is far above having any family or relatives. Attributing a son to Allah is considered a grave sin and a form of polytheism, as it implies that Allah is in need of or similar to His creation. The verse affirms that Allah, the Most Merciful, is self-sufficient and independent of all His creation, and that the concept of Him having a son is an invention and a falsehood.
orig: وقالوا اتخذ الرحمن ولدا

translation: Indeed, you have come with something monstrous.
interpretation: This verse is expressing shock and disbelief at the gravity or audacity of an act committed or a claim made. It suggests that what has been done or said is so outrageous, unheard of, or abominable that it is almost beyond comprehension. The use of the word "iddan" emphasizes the enormity and monstrosity of the matter being referred to.
orig: لقد جئتم شيئا إدا

translation: The heavens almost break apart therefrom, and the earth splits asunder, and the mountains collapse in devastation.
interpretation: This verse conveys the immense power and majesty of Allah's words and actions. It suggests that the revelation of Allah's message or the occurrence of major events by His will are so momentous that they can have a profound impact on the entire universe. The heavens, earth, and mountains - some of the mightiest creations - are described as being on the verge of breaking apart, splitting, or collapsing, indicating that nothing is too great to be immune from being shaken to its core by Allah's decree. The imagery also alludes to the awe-inspiring nature of Allah's words and the overwhelming reaction of His creation, highlighting the importance of receiving His message with utmost reverence, humility and obedience.
orig: تكاد السماوات يتفطرن منه وتنشق الأرض وتخر الجبال هدا

translation: That they attribute to the Most Merciful a son.
interpretation: This verse criticizes the belief of attributing offspring to Allah, such as the notion that Allah has a son. It emphasizes the fundamental Islamic concept of Allah's oneness and uniqueness (tawheed). Ascribing divine sonship to anyone is considered a grave error and deviation from the pure monotheistic message of Islam. The "Most Merciful" (ar-Rahman) refers to one of Allah's names, highlighting His infinite mercy and compassion. So the idea of Allah having a child is presented as incompatible with His sublime attributes and absolute self-sufficiency.
orig: أن دعوا للرحمن ولدا

translation: It is not befitting for the Most Merciful to take a son.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the fundamental Islamic belief in the absolute oneness and uniqueness of Allah. It categorically denies the notion that Allah has offspring or children, which was a common belief among the pagan Arabs and some other religious groups at the time of the Prophet Muhammad. The verse asserts that it is not fitting or appropriate for the Most Merciful (ar-Rahman), one of the names of Allah, to have a child. This is because having offspring implies a need or deficiency, which is not befitting for the Self-Sufficient and Perfect nature of Allah. The verse affirms the Islamic concept of Tawheed (monotheism) and rejects any form of anthropomorphism or likening Allah to His creation.
orig: وما ينبغي للرحمن أن يتخذ ولدا

translation: There is none in the heavens and earth but that he comes to the Most Merciful as a servant.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute sovereignty and lordship of Allah over all of His creation. Every being in the heavens and the earth, whether angel, jinn, human, or any other creature, is a servant of Allah and is subject to His will and command. They are all in need of Him, dependent upon Him, and will ultimately return to Him. It highlights the complete submission and servitude that all creatures owe to their Creator and Lord. At the same time, it underscores the infinite mercy, generosity and benevolence of Allah, who is ar-Rahman (the Most Merciful), towards His servants and creation.
orig: إن كل من في السماوات والأرض إلا آتي الرحمن عبدا

translation: He has enumerated them and counted them a [full] counting.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's omniscience and His precise knowledge of all things. It suggests that Allah has a perfect record of every single being, having counted and enumerated them all individually. This interpretation highlights the concept of Allah's all-encompassing knowledge and His awareness of every detail in His creation, reinforcing the idea that nothing escapes His attention and that all creatures are accounted for by Him.
orig: لقد أحصاهم وعدهم عدا

translation: And all of them are coming to Him on the Day of Resurrection alone.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the individual accountability of each person on the Day of Judgment. No one will be able to rely on others or hide behind them. Each person will stand alone before Allah and be held responsible for their own deeds, intentions, and beliefs. This highlights the importance of living a righteous life and being mindful of one's actions, as ultimately, we will face the consequences of our choices in the Hereafter, without anyone to support or defend us except our own good deeds and Allah's mercy.
orig: وكلهم آتيه يوم القيامة فردا

translation: Indeed, those who have believed and done righteous deeds - the Most Merciful will appoint for them affection.
interpretation: This verse indicates that those who have true faith and couple it with good deeds will be granted a special status by Allah. Allah, the Most Merciful, will place love and affection for them in the hearts of others. This means that the righteous believers will be beloved and respected by the people around them due to their virtuous conduct and sincerity. It is a reward from Allah that He blesses them with cordial relationships and makes them well-liked in society. This special favor is a fruit of their faith and righteousness, emphasizing the importance of combining belief with good actions to earn Allah's pleasure and grace in this world and the Hereafter.
orig: إن الذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات سيجعل لهم الرحمن ودا

translation: And We have certainly made the Qur'an easy in your tongue, [O Muhammad], that you may give good tidings thereby to the righteous and warn thereby a hostile people.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah has made the Qur'an easy to understand and recite in the Arabic language, which was the native tongue of Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him). The purpose of this is twofold: firstly, to enable the Prophet to give glad tidings of Paradise and Allah's pleasure to those who are righteous and follow the guidance of the Qur'an; and secondly, to warn the hostile and stubborn disbelievers of the consequences of their rejection and the punishment that awaits them in the Hereafter. The ease of the Qur'an's language and style serves to make its message clear and accessible to all, so that they may reflect upon it and be guided to the right path.
orig: فإنما يسرناه بلسانك لتبشر به المتقين وتنذر به قوما لدا

translation: And how many generations have We destroyed before them? Do you perceive from them anyone or hear from them a sound?
interpretation: This verse serves as a reminder of the fate that befell previous nations who rejected the message of Allah and His prophets. It emphasizes the complete destruction and obliteration of these civilizations, highlighting that no trace or remnant of them remains. The rhetorical questions "Do you perceive from them anyone or hear from them a sound?" force the reader to reflect on the absolute nature of their annihilation. This verse aims to warn those who oppose the truth and persist in disbelief, reminding them that they too could face a similar fate if they do not heed the warnings and signs sent by Allah.
orig: وكم أهلكنا قبلهم من قرن هل تحس منهم من أحد أو تسمع لهم ركزا

translation: Ta-Ha.
interpretation: This verse consists of two Arabic letters, Ta and Ha. Many chapters of the Qur'an begin with such mysterious letter combinations, known as the "Muqatta'at" or "disjoined letters". The exact meaning and purpose of these letters is unknown, and there are various interpretations among scholars. Some believe that these letters have a mystical significance known only to Allah, while others suggest that they may serve as a way to attract the attention of the listener or reader, or as a sign of the divine origin of the Qur'an. Ultimately, the true meaning behind these letters remains one of the many mysteries of the Qur'an that encourages contemplation and humility before the infinite wisdom of Allah.
orig: طه

translation: We have not sent down to you the Qur'an that you be distressed
interpretation: This verse is a reassurance from Allah to Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) that the revelation of the Qur'an is not meant to cause him hardship or distress. Rather, it is a guidance and a mercy for him and for all of mankind. The Qur'an is not a burden, but a blessing that brings peace, comfort, and enlightenment to those who follow its teachings. This verse highlights Allah's compassion and care for His Prophet and serves as a reminder that the path of Islam, while challenging at times, ultimately leads to contentment and success in this life and the hereafter.
orig: ما أنزلنا عليك القرآن لتشقى

translation: But [it is] only a reminder for those who fear [Allah].
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the Qur'an serves as a powerful reminder and admonition for those who have a sense of reverence and fear towards Allah. It is meant to guide and benefit those who are conscious of Allah and seek to follow His guidance. The Qur'an is not merely a book of stories or historical accounts, but a source of wisdom, guidance, and spiritual enlightenment for those who approach it with a sincere heart and a desire to draw closer to their Creator. Those who fear Allah will find in the Qur'an a treasure trove of knowledge and a means of purifying their souls.
orig: إلا تذكرة لمن يخشى

translation: A revelation from He who created the earth and highest heavens.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the Qur'an is a divine revelation from Allah, the Creator of the entire universe, including the earth and the highest heavens. It highlights the supreme authority and power of Allah as the originator of all creation. By attributing the Qur'an to the Creator Himself, the verse establishes the authenticity, importance, and sublime nature of the Qur'anic message. It implies that the teachings and guidance contained within the Qur'an come directly from the One who has complete knowledge and wisdom over all things, making it a book of utmost significance for humanity to follow and obey.
orig: تنزيلا ممن خلق الأرض والسماوات العلى

translation: The Most Merciful [who is] above the Throne established.
interpretation: This verse affirms that Allah, the Most Merciful, has risen above His Throne in a manner befitting His Majesty. It emphasizes Allah's transcendence and sovereignty over all of His creation. The "establishment" on the Throne indicates Allah's power, authority and control over the universe. However, the exact nature of this "establishment" is unknown to us. It is essential to affirm this attribute of Allah without trying to interpret it in a way that likens Allah to His creation, as Allah is unlike anything in His creation. The verse encourages humility and submission before the Majestic Creator who reigns supreme over all things.
orig: الرحمن على العرش استوى

translation: To Him belongs what is in the heavens and what is on the earth and what is between them and what is under the soil.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute sovereignty and dominion of Allah over all of creation. Everything in the universe, whether in the heavens above, on the earth we inhabit, in the space between them, or even beneath the depths of the soil, belongs to Him alone. It highlights His complete ownership, power, and authority over all things, seen and unseen. This understanding should instill humility, reverence, and submission to Allah in the hearts of believers, recognizing that nothing exists or happens without His knowledge and permission.
orig: له ما في السماوات وما في الأرض وما بينهما وما تحت الثرى

translation: And if you speak aloud - then indeed, He knows the secret and what is [even] more hidden.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the all-encompassing knowledge of Allah. It states that whether one speaks openly or keeps their thoughts hidden, Allah is fully aware of it all. He knows the secrets within people's hearts and even what is more concealed than that. This verse serves as a reminder for believers to be mindful of their intentions and actions, as nothing escapes the knowledge of Allah. It encourages sincerity and discourages hypocrisy, as Allah is well-aware of what lies in the depths of our souls.
orig: وإن تجهر بالقول فإنه يعلم السر وأخفى

translation: Allah - there is no deity except Him. To Him belong the best names.
interpretation: This verse affirms the fundamental Islamic belief in the oneness and uniqueness of God (Allah). It states that there is no other being worthy of worship except Allah alone. The verse also indicates that Allah possesses the most beautiful names and attributes, which reflect His perfection, majesty, and grace. These names, such as ar-Rahman (the Most Merciful), al-Hakeem (the All-Wise), and al-Qadeer (the All-Powerful), help believers understand and connect with Allah's divine qualities. By recognizing and invoking these names, Muslims can strengthen their faith, seek guidance, and find comfort in their relationship with the Almighty.
orig: الله لا إله إلا هو له الأسماء الحسنى

translation: And has the story of Moses reached you?
interpretation: This verse is a rhetorical question that serves as an introduction to the story of Prophet Moses (peace be upon him) which is narrated in the following verses. It is meant to draw the listener's attention to the importance and significance of the upcoming story, and to encourage them to reflect upon its lessons and wisdom. The story of Moses is one of the most frequently mentioned stories in the Qur'an, highlighting his role as a great prophet and messenger of God, and his struggles against the tyranny and oppression of Pharaoh.
orig: وهل أتاك حديث موسى

translation: When he saw a fire and said to his family, "Stay here; indeed, I have perceived a fire; perhaps I can bring you a torch or find at the fire some guidance."
interpretation: This verse is referring to the story of Prophet Moses when he saw a fire on the side of Mount Tur and told his family to wait while he went to investigate it, hoping to either bring back a burning torch to give them light and warmth or to find someone there who could guide him to the right path. This event marks the beginning of Moses' prophethood, as it was at this fire that Allah spoke to him directly and commissioned him with the task of going to Pharaoh and leading the Children of Israel out of Egypt. The verse emphasizes the importance of seeking guidance and knowledge, even in unexpected places or circumstances.
orig: إذ رأى نارا فقال لأهله امكثوا إني آنست نارا لعلي آتيكم منها بقبس أو أجد على النار هدى

translation: But when he came to it, he was called, "O Moses,
interpretation: This verse is referring to when Moses approached the burning bush and heard the voice of Allah calling out to him directly. The interpretation is that this was a pivotal moment in Moses' life, where he was chosen by Allah for a special purpose and mission. It marks the beginning of his prophethood and his role as a messenger to Pharaoh and the Israelites. The direct call from Allah signifies the importance and magnitude of the task that Moses was about to undertake, and highlights his status as a chosen prophet of God.
orig: فلما أتاها نودي يا موسى

translation: Indeed, I am your Lord, so remove your sandals. Indeed, you are in the sacred valley of Tuwa.
interpretation: This verse is a command from Allah to Prophet Moses (peace be upon him) to show reverence and humility in the sacred valley of Tuwa. The removal of sandals symbolizes the act of leaving behind worldly attachments and approaching the divine presence with utmost respect and submission. It signifies the importance of recognizing the sanctity of the place where one is receiving divine revelation and the need to purify oneself, both physically and spiritually, before entering into a direct dialogue with the Almighty.
orig: إني أنا ربك فاخلع نعليك إنك بالواد المقدس طوى

translation: And I have chosen you, so listen to what is revealed [to you].
interpretation: This verse is a direct address from Allah to Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him), affirming that He has chosen him for the noble task of receiving divine revelation and conveying it to mankind. It is a reminder to the Prophet to pay full attention to the message being revealed to him, as it is of utmost importance for the guidance of humanity. The verse emphasizes the special status of Prophet Muhammad as the chosen recipient of Allah's words and highlights his responsibility to carefully listen, understand, and follow the divine instructions. It also serves as a lesson for all believers to be attentive and obedient when it comes to the teachings of the Qur'an and the Prophet's example.
orig: وأنا اخترتك فاستمع لما يوحى

translation: Indeed, I am Allah. There is no deity except Me, so worship Me and establish prayer for My remembrance.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the oneness and uniqueness of Allah, asserting that He alone is worthy of worship. It serves as a reminder for believers to direct their devotion and prayers solely to Allah, as a means of remembering and connecting with Him. The establishment of prayer is highlighted as a fundamental act of worship and a way to keep Allah's remembrance alive in one's heart and daily life. This interpretation underscores the importance of monotheism and the centrality of prayer in maintaining a strong spiritual bond with the Creator.
orig: إنني أنا الله لا إله إلا أنا فاعبدني وأقم الصلاة لذكري

translation: Indeed, the Hour is coming - I almost conceal it - so that every soul may be recompensed according to that for which it strives.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the inevitability and nearness of the Day of Judgment, which Allah has kept hidden from human knowledge. The purpose of concealing the exact time is to encourage people to strive in doing good deeds consistently throughout their lives, as every soul will be rewarded or punished based on their actions and intentions. It serves as a reminder for believers to always be mindful of their deeds and to live righteously, knowing that the Hour could come at any moment and that they will be held accountable for their actions in this world.
orig: إن الساعة آتية أكاد أخفيها لتجزى كل نفس بما تسعى

translation: So do not let one who does not believe in it and follows his own desire turn you away from it, lest you perish.
interpretation: This verse is a warning against being swayed by those who reject faith and follow their own whims and desires. It cautions that allowing oneself to be influenced by such people can lead one astray from the path of truth and righteousness, ultimately resulting in spiritual ruin and destruction. The Qur'an emphasizes the importance of remaining steadfast in faith and not succumbing to the temptations or persuasions of those who have turned away from divine guidance. It is a reminder to hold fast to one's beliefs and convictions, even in the face of opposition or pressure from others who may seek to lead one astray.
orig: فلا يصدنك عنها من لا يؤمن بها واتبع هواه فتردى

translation: And what is that in your right hand, O Moses?
interpretation: This verse is from the story of Moses when Allah spoke to him directly. Allah asks Moses about what he is holding in his right hand, which is his staff. The question serves to draw Moses' attention to the staff and to prepare him for the miracles that Allah would manifest through it. It also emphasizes Allah's complete knowledge and awareness of all things, even what is in Moses' hand. The verse prompts reflection on the power and wisdom of Allah and how He can use ordinary objects for extraordinary purposes in supporting His prophets and guiding humanity.
orig: وما تلك بيمينك يا موسى

translation: He said, "It is my staff; I lean upon it, and I bring down leaves for my sheep, and I have other uses for it."
interpretation: This verse is a powerful reminder of the importance of resourcefulness and finding multiple uses for the tools and gifts that Allah has bestowed upon us. The staff of Moses was not just a simple walking stick, but a multi-purpose tool that he used in various ways to benefit himself and his flock. Similarly, each of us has been given unique talents, skills, and resources that we can employ in diverse ways to bring benefit to ourselves and others in accordance with Allah's will. The verse encourages us to think creatively about how we can make the most of what we have been given and to use our blessings in a way that is pleasing to Allah.
orig: قال هي عصاي أتوكأ عليها وأهش بها على غنمي ولي فيها مآرب أخرى

translation: He said, "Throw it down, O Moses."
interpretation: This verse is a command from Allah to Prophet Moses to throw down his staff. The staff was a symbol of Moses' prophethood and a tool that Allah had blessed with miraculous powers. By asking Moses to throw it down, Allah was demonstrating His power and control over all things, even the seemingly ordinary objects like a staff. It also served as a test of Moses' faith and obedience to Allah's commands. The act of throwing down the staff and witnessing its transformation into a serpent was a powerful sign of Allah's might and a confirmation of Moses' divine mission as a prophet.
orig: قال ألقها يا موسى

translation: Then he threw it down, and thereupon it was a snake, moving swiftly.
interpretation: This verse is referring to the miracle of Moses' staff turning into a snake. The interpretation is that God has the power to transform ordinary objects into extraordinary things, and to imbue His prophets with miraculous abilities as a sign of their prophethood and a means of convincing others of the truth of their message. It also symbolizes how God can bring the "dead" to life, as the inanimate staff became a living creature. The swiftness of the snake's movement can be interpreted as representing the speed and decisiveness with which God's will and plan is enacted.
orig: فألقاها فإذا هي حية تسعى

translation: He said, "Take it and do not fear. We will return it to its former state."
interpretation: This verse is a reference to the story of Moses and his staff. God is reassuring Moses that he should not be afraid to take hold of his staff, even after it had been transformed into a serpent. God promises that He will restore the staff to its original form. This verse symbolizes the power and authority that God can bestow upon His chosen servants, and the importance of trusting in His plan even in the face of seemingly impossible or frightening circumstances. It also demonstrates God's ability to transform and restore things to their original state, highlighting His ultimate control over all creation.
orig: قال خذها ولا تخف سنعيدها سيرتها الأولى

translation: And draw your hand to your side; it will come out white without disease - another sign,
interpretation: This verse refers to one of the miracles given to Prophet Moses (peace be upon him) as a sign of his prophethood. God commanded Moses to put his hand under his arm and when he drew it out, it appeared shining white and radiant, without any disease or imperfection. This was a divine miracle serving as proof of Moses' prophethood and a means to strengthen his faith and resolve in the face of the challenges of his mission. It symbolizes purity, righteousness and being chosen by God for a sacred purpose. The miracle of the white hand was a compelling sign for the people to witness God's power and affirm the truth of Moses' message.
orig: واضمم يدك إلى جناحك تخرج بيضاء من غير سوء آية أخرى

translation: We will show you of Our greater signs.
interpretation: This verse indicates that Allah will reveal to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) some of His most magnificent and awe-inspiring signs. These signs serve as evidence of Allah's power, wisdom, and the truth of the Prophet's message. The "greater signs" could refer to the profound verses of the Qur'an, the miracles performed by the Prophet, or the various wonders of creation that testify to Allah's existence and omnipotence. By witnessing these signs, the believers' faith will be strengthened, and they will be reminded of Allah's greatness and the importance of submitting to His will.
orig: لنريك من آياتنا الكبرى

translation: Go to Pharaoh. Indeed, he has transgressed.
interpretation: This verse is a command from Allah to Prophet Moses to go to Pharaoh and confront him about his arrogance and transgression. It shows that it is the duty of the prophets and believers to stand up against tyranny and oppression, even in the face of powerful rulers. The verse also implies that Pharaoh's transgression had reached a point where divine intervention was necessary to bring him to account and protect the oppressed. It demonstrates Allah's concern for justice and His willingness to support His messengers in their mission to guide people to the right path.
orig: اذهب إلى فرعون إنه طغى

translation: My Lord, expand for me my breast [with assurance]
interpretation: This verse is a prayer asking Allah to expand one's heart and mind, granting tranquility, peace, and the ability to face life's challenges with patience and wisdom. It is a plea for Allah to remove anxiety, stress, and constriction from one's chest, allowing the heart to be filled with faith, contentment, and spiritual enlightenment. By making this supplication, the believer seeks Allah's support to remain steadfast on the right path and to be able to fulfill their responsibilities with ease and confidence.
orig: قال رب اشرح لي صدري

translation: And ease my task for me
interpretation: This verse is a prayer to Allah to make one's affairs and tasks easy and manageable. It is a recognition that ultimately, success and ease in any endeavor comes from Allah's grace and mercy. The supplicant is asking Allah to remove any hardships or difficulties that may arise in their path, and to grant them the strength, wisdom, and means to accomplish their goals with ease. This prayer reflects the believer's complete trust and reliance on Allah in all matters of life.
orig: ويسر لي أمري

translation: And remove the impediment from my speech
interpretation: This verse is a prayer to Allah to grant the supplicant eloquence and clarity of speech, so that they may effectively convey the message of Islam. It is a recognition that the ability to communicate well is a blessing from Allah, and that any limitations or hindrances in one's speech can be removed through sincere supplication to Him. The verse emphasizes the importance of effective communication in spreading the teachings of Islam and inviting others to the path of righteousness.
orig: واحلل عقدة من لساني

translation: That they may understand my speech.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of clear communication and conveying the message in a way that the audience can comprehend. It suggests that the speaker, likely a prophet or messenger of God, is striving to make their words intelligible and accessible to their listeners. The verse implies that understanding the divine message is crucial for the spiritual growth and guidance of individuals and the community as a whole. It also highlights the responsibility of religious leaders and teachers to articulate their teachings effectively, tailoring their language and approach to the level of understanding of their followers.
orig: يفقهوا قولي

translation: And appoint for me a minister from my family
interpretation: This verse is a request from Prophet Moses to Allah, asking Him to appoint his brother Aaron as his assistant and supporter in his mission. It highlights the importance of having a trustworthy and reliable person, especially from one's own family, to help in carrying out important responsibilities and facing challenges. The verse also shows the humility of Prophet Moses in seeking divine help and acknowledging the need for support in fulfilling his prophetic duties.
orig: واجعل لي وزيرا من أهلي

translation: Aaron, my brother
interpretation: This verse is addressing Aaron, the brother of Moses, who was also a prophet. It shows the close relationship between the two prophets and highlights the importance of brotherhood and family ties in Islam. The verse also implies that Aaron played a significant role in supporting Moses in his mission to guide the Children of Israel and deliver God's message to them.
orig: هارون أخي

translation: And strengthen through him my back
interpretation: This verse is a prayer asking Allah to provide support and strength through another person, likely a close companion or helper. It conveys the idea that having a righteous and reliable person to assist one can provide both physical and moral support, making it easier to bear life's burdens and fulfill one's responsibilities. The metaphorical reference to strengthening one's back suggests standing firm, feeling empowered, and being readily equipped to face challenges with the aid of a trusted ally.
orig: اشدد به أزري

translation: And let him share in my task
interpretation: This verse is a continuation of Prophet Moses' prayer to Allah, in which he asks Allah to appoint his brother Aaron as his helper and supporter in his prophetic mission. Moses recognizes the immense responsibility of conveying Allah's message to Pharaoh and his people, and seeks divine assistance by requesting that Aaron share in this task. This highlights the importance of seeking help and support from righteous companions in fulfilling one's religious duties and responsibilities. It also emphasizes the value of collaboration and teamwork in achieving noble goals and facing challenges on the path of faith.
orig: وأشركه في أمري

translation: That we may glorify You much
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of glorifying and praising Allah abundantly. It reminds the believers that one of the main purposes of their existence is to constantly remember and exalt Allah, expressing gratitude for His blessings and acknowledging His greatness. The verse encourages Muslims to engage in frequent remembrance of Allah, not just through ritual acts of worship, but also by infusing their daily lives with a sense of God-consciousness and appreciation for His favors. It highlights that glorifying Allah should be a central focus and a primary goal for every believer, as it helps strengthen their spiritual connection with Him and attain His pleasure.
orig: كي نسبحك كثيرا

translation: And remember you much
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of remembering Allah frequently. It encourages the believer to engage in constant remembrance of Allah, which can be done through various means such as reciting His names, supplicating to Him, and reflecting upon His signs in creation. Remembering Allah much is a means of attaining peace and tranquility in the heart, as well as gaining Allah's love and pleasure. It serves as a reminder to the believer to always keep Allah at the forefront of their thoughts and actions, and to never forget Him in the midst of the distractions and temptations of this worldly life.
orig: ونذكرك كثيرا

translation: Indeed, You are of us ever Seeing.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's attribute of being All-Seeing (Al-Baseer). It means that Allah is constantly aware of and observing His creation. Nothing escapes His sight or knowledge, whether it is apparent or hidden. This attribute instills a sense of taqwa (God-consciousness) in the believer, knowing that Allah is always watching their actions, intentions, and innermost thoughts. It encourages the believer to be mindful, sincere, and strive for good deeds, while being wary of sins and disobedience, as Allah is witness to everything they do.
orig: إنك كنت بنا بصيرا

translation: He said, "You have been granted your request, O Moses."
interpretation: This verse is a response from Allah to Prophet Moses's prayer or request. It shows that Allah listens to the sincere supplications of His servants and grants them what they ask for, especially when it is something beneficial for their spiritual growth and for fulfilling their role as prophets and messengers of God. It is an assurance to Moses that Allah has accepted his prayer and will support him in his mission to guide the Children of Israel and face the challenges posed by Pharaoh and his people.
orig: قال قد أوتيت سؤلك يا موسى

translation: And We had already conferred favor upon you another time.
interpretation: This verse is reminding the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) of the favors that Allah has bestowed upon him throughout his life. It implies that Allah has been continuously supporting, guiding, and blessing the Prophet, not just once, but multiple times. This could be referring to various instances in the Prophet's life where he received divine help and guidance, such as during his childhood, his early adulthood, and his prophethood. The verse serves as a reminder of Allah's constant love, care, and protection for the Prophet, emphasizing the special bond between them and the unique status of Muhammad as the chosen final messenger of Allah.
orig: ولقد مننا عليك مرة أخرى

translation: When We inspired in your mother that which is inspired,
interpretation: This verse is referring to the divine inspiration given to the mother of Prophet Moses. Allah inspired her with the idea to place her infant son in a chest and cast it into the river Nile, in order to protect him from being killed by Pharaoh's soldiers who were ordered to slay all newborn boys. This inspiration was a form of divine revelation and guidance to save Moses' life and set in motion the events that would lead to his prophethood and the liberation of the Children of Israel from Pharaoh's tyranny. It demonstrates Allah's power to inspire and guide His chosen servants, and His ability to protect and support those who have faith in Him even in the most difficult of circumstances.
orig: إذ أوحينا إلى أمك ما يوحى

translation: Place him into the chest and cast it into the river. The river will throw it onto the bank, and he will be taken in by [someone who is] an enemy to Me and an enemy to him. And I bestowed upon you [My] affection that you would be brought up under My eye.
interpretation: This verse is referring to the story of Moses, where Allah commanded his mother to place him in a chest and cast it into the river Nile. Allah assured her that He would protect Moses and return him to her, and that he would be brought up under Allah's care and protection, despite being found by Pharaoh, who was an enemy to Allah and Moses. This verse demonstrates Allah's power and control over all affairs, and His ability to protect and guide His chosen servants, even in the face of great adversity.
orig: أن اقذفيه في التابوت فاقذفيه في اليم فليلقه اليم بالساحل يأخذه عدو لي وعدو له وألقيت عليك محبة مني ولتصنع على عيني

translation: When your sister went and said, "Shall I direct you to someone who will take care of him?" So We returned you to your mother that she might be content and not grieve. And you killed someone, but We saved you from retaliation and tried you with a [severe] trial. And you remained [some] years among the people of Madyan. Then you came [here] at the decreed time, O Moses.
interpretation: This verse highlights significant events in the life of Prophet Moses (peace be upon him). It shows how Allah protected and guided him through various challenges, such as being saved from Pharaoh's decree of killing male infants, being returned to his mother's care, being forgiven for accidentally killing a man, and spending time among the people of Madyan. These experiences were part of Allah's plan to prepare Moses for his role as a prophet and to demonstrate His power and mercy in shaping the destiny of His chosen servants. The verse emphasizes that Moses' arrival at this point in his life was predetermined by Allah's decree, indicating that everything happens according to His divine will and wisdom.
orig: إذ تمشي أختك فتقول هل أدلكم على من يكفله فرجعناك إلى أمك كي تقر عينها ولا تحزن وقتلت نفسا فنجيناك من الغم وفتناك فتونا فلبثت سنين في أهل مدين ثم جئت على قدر يا موسى

translation: And I have chosen you for Myself.
interpretation: This verse is interpreted to mean that Allah has specifically chosen and favored the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) for His divine purpose and message. It signifies the special status and relationship that the Prophet has with Allah, as he was selected and prepared by Allah Himself to be the final messenger and recipient of divine revelation. This choosing by Allah reflects the Prophet's unique qualities, virtues, and his role in conveying the message of Islam to humanity.
orig: واصطنعتك لنفسي

translation: Go, you and your brother, with My signs and do not slacken in My remembrance.
interpretation: This verse is a command from Allah to Moses and his brother Aaron to go forth with His signs and miracles, and to constantly remember Him and not neglect His remembrance. It emphasizes the importance of remaining steadfast in faith and keeping Allah's remembrance alive in one's heart and actions, even in the face of adversity or while engaged in the active pursuit of one's mission. The verse also highlights the power of divine support and how Allah empowers His chosen servants with signs and miracles to fulfill their prophetic roles and overcome the challenges they face from those who oppose them.
orig: اذهب أنت وأخوك بآياتي ولا تنيا في ذكري

translation: Go, both of you, to Pharaoh. Indeed, he has transgressed.
interpretation: This verse is a command from Allah to Moses and his brother Aaron to confront Pharaoh, the ruler of Egypt, who had become arrogant and oppressive. It emphasizes the importance of standing up against tyranny and injustice, even in the face of a powerful ruler. The verse also implies that Moses and Aaron were chosen by Allah for this mission because of their faith, courage, and wisdom. It teaches us that we should not fear confronting oppressors when we are on the side of truth and justice, and that Allah will support those who strive in His cause with sincerity and determination.
orig: اذهبا إلى فرعون إنه طغى

translation: And speak to him with gentle speech that perhaps he may be reminded or fear [Allah].
interpretation: This verse instructs Prophet Moses and his brother Aaron to speak gently and kindly to Pharaoh when conveying Allah's message, even though Pharaoh was known for his arrogance and tyranny. The gentle approach is encouraged with the hope that Pharaoh might reflect upon the message, mend his ways, and develop a sense of reverence and fear of Allah due to the softness of speech. It highlights the importance of using wisdom, kindness, and good communication skills when reaching out to others about faith, as a harsh or confrontational method is less likely to be well-received or create a positive change in the person.
orig: فقولا له قولا لينا لعله يتذكر أو يخشى

translation: They said, "Our Lord, indeed we are afraid that he will hasten [punishment] against us or that he will transgress."
interpretation: This verse reflects the fear and apprehension felt by Moses and Aaron as they were tasked with confronting Pharaoh. They were worried that Pharaoh, known for his arrogance and tyranny, would react harshly and punish them severely for challenging his authority. The verse highlights their reliance on God's protection and guidance in the face of a powerful and oppressive ruler. It demonstrates the importance of having faith and trust in God, even in the most daunting of circumstances. The prophets' fear also shows their human nature and the immense pressure they were under, emphasizing the significance of their steadfastness and courage in fulfilling their divine mission.
orig: قالا ربنا إننا نخاف أن يفرط علينا أو أن يطغى

translation: He said, "Fear not. Indeed, I am with you both; I hear and I see."
interpretation: This verse is a reassurance from Allah to two of His prophets, emphasizing that they should not fear anyone or anything because Allah is with them, hearing their prayers and seeing their actions. It highlights the concept of Allah's omnipresence and His support for His chosen messengers. The verse instills a sense of comfort, courage, and confidence in the believers, knowing that Allah is always watching over them and guiding them through their struggles and challenges.
orig: قال لا تخافا إنني معكما أسمع وأرى

translation: So go you both to him, and say: 'Verily, we are Messengers of your Lord, so let the Children of Israel go with us, and torment them not; indeed, we have come to you with a sign from your Lord! And peace will be upon him who follows the guidance!'
interpretation: This verse is a divine command to Moses and Aaron to go to Pharaoh and deliver the message that they are prophets sent by God. They are instructed to demand the release of the Children of Israel from Pharaoh's oppression and torment. The verse emphasizes that Moses and Aaron have come with a clear sign from God to validate their prophethood and message. It also conveys a promise of peace and security for those who follow the guidance brought by the prophets, indicating that following divine guidance leads to a path of peace and well-being.
orig: فأتياه فقولا إنا رسولا ربك فأرسل معنا بني إسرائيل ولا تعذبهم قد جئناك بآية من ربك والسلام على من اتبع الهدى

translation: Indeed, it has been revealed to Us that the punishment will be upon whoever denies and turns away.
interpretation: This verse serves as a stern warning to those who reject the truth of Islam and turn away from the path of Allah. It emphasizes that divine revelation has made it clear that those who persist in denying the message of Islam and refuse to submit to Allah will face severe consequences in the form of punishment in the Hereafter. The verse highlights the gravity of disbelief and the importance of accepting the truth and following the guidance provided by Allah through His messengers. It is a reminder that one's choices and actions in this life will determine one's fate in the eternal life to come.
orig: إنا قد أوحي إلينا أن العذاب على من كذب وتولى

translation: He said, "Then who is your Lord, O Moses?"
interpretation: In this verse, Pharaoh is questioning Moses about the identity of his Lord. It shows Pharaoh's arrogance and disbelief in the existence of a supreme deity other than himself. The question is posed in a challenging manner, as if to say that Pharaoh does not recognize any authority higher than his own. This verse sets the stage for Moses to declare his faith in the one true God and to challenge Pharaoh's claim of divinity. It highlights the confrontation between the truth of monotheism and the falsehood of Pharaoh's self-proclaimed godhood.
orig: قال فمن ربكما يا موسى

translation: Our Lord is He Who gave to each thing its form and nature, then guided it aright.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's role as the Creator and His guidance for all of creation. It implies that everything in the universe has been created with a specific purpose and design, and that Allah has provided guidance for each of His creations to fulfill its purpose. This guidance can be seen in the natural instincts and innate characteristics that Allah has bestowed upon every living being, allowing them to function and thrive in their respective environments. For human beings, this guidance comes in the form of divine revelation through prophets and scriptures, which help guide them towards the path of righteousness and success in both this world and the hereafter.
orig: قال ربنا الذي أعطى كل شيء خلقه ثم هدى

translation: He said, "Then what is the case of the former generations?"
interpretation: This verse is a question posed by someone, likely a disbeliever, to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him). The questioner is asking about the fate of the previous generations who lived before the advent of Islam and the message brought by the Prophet. The implication seems to be that if Islam is the true religion, then what will happen to all those people in the past who did not follow it or have access to its teachings? This verse sets the stage for the Islamic perspective on the issue of divine justice and the accountability of people throughout history based on the knowledge and means that were available to them in their own times.
orig: قال فما بال القرون الأولى

translation: He said, "Its knowledge is with my Lord in a Record. My Lord neither errs nor forgets."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the omniscience and infallibility of Allah. It asserts that the knowledge of all things, including the Hour (Day of Judgment), is with Him in a divine Record or Book. Allah is free from any error, forgetfulness, or imperfection. The verse highlights the contrast between the limitless knowledge of Allah and the limited knowledge of His creation. It serves as a reminder for humans to trust in Allah's wisdom and to acknowledge that there are matters beyond their comprehension that only Allah knows.
orig: قال علمها عند ربي في كتاب لا يضل ربي ولا ينسى

translation: Who has made for you the earth a bed [spread out] and has made for you upon it roads and has sent down rain from the sky and thereby We have brought forth [many] species of diverse plants.
interpretation: This verse highlights Allah's benevolence and power in creating the earth as a suitable habitat for human beings. The phrase "made for you the earth a bed" suggests that Allah has designed the earth to be a comfortable place for humans to live and thrive. The mention of roads indicates that Allah has provided means for people to travel and explore His creation. The verse also emphasizes Allah's role in the water cycle, as He sends down rain from the sky, which allows for the growth and diversity of plant life. This serves as a reminder of Allah's ability to bring forth life and sustain it through His divine providence.
orig: الذي جعل لكم الأرض مهدا وسلك لكم فيها سبلا وأنزل من السماء ماء فأخرجنا به أزواجا من نبات شتى

translation: Eat [therefrom] and pasture your livestock. Indeed in that are signs for those of intelligence.
interpretation: This verse is an invitation for humans to benefit from the provisions that Allah has created on earth, such as vegetation and water, both for their own sustenance and for their livestock. It encourages people to reflect upon these signs of Allah's mercy, power and wisdom in nature, which serve as evidence for those who have insight and understanding. The verse implies that by pondering over these favors and blessings, one can strengthen their faith and draw closer to Allah, recognizing Him as the source of all provisions and the One worthy of worship and gratitude.
orig: كلوا وارعوا أنعامكم إن في ذلك لآيات لأولي النهى

translation: From the earth We created you, and into it We will return you, and from it We will extract you another time.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the intimate connection between human beings and the earth. It reminds us that we were created from the very elements found within the earth, and that upon death, our physical bodies will return to it through burial and decomposition. However, the verse also points to the belief in resurrection, stating that we will be brought forth from the earth once more on the Day of Judgment. This interpretation highlights the cyclical nature of life and death, the temporary nature of our worldly existence, and the ultimate return to our Creator for judgment and the afterlife.
orig: منها خلقناكم وفيها نعيدكم ومنها نخرجكم تارة أخرى

translation: And We had certainly shown him [i.e., Pharaoh] Our signs - all of them - but he denied and refused.
interpretation: This verse is referring to the story of Prophet Moses and Pharaoh. Despite God showing Pharaoh numerous signs and miracles as evidence of Moses' prophethood and the truth of his message, Pharaoh arrogantly denied them and refused to believe. It demonstrates Pharaoh's stubborn disbelief and his choice to reject the clear proofs presented to him. The verse emphasizes that God gave Pharaoh every opportunity to believe, yet he persisted in his denial and opposition to the truth out of pride and heedlessness. It serves as a warning and reminder that even when faced with overwhelming evidence, some people will still choose disbelief due to their own arrogance and attachment to worldly power.
orig: ولقد أريناه آياتنا كلها فكذب وأبى

translation: They said, "Have you come to us to drive us out of our land with your magic, O Moses?"
interpretation: This verse reveals the stubborn and arrogant attitude of Pharaoh and his people towards Moses. They accused Moses of using magic to try to drive them out of their own land, rather than acknowledging the signs and miracles that Moses brought as proof of his prophethood. This accusation demonstrates their unwillingness to accept the truth and submit to the message that Moses brought from Allah. It also shows how those in power often resist change and cling to their false beliefs and ways, even in the face of clear evidence to the contrary.
orig: قال أجئتنا لتخرجنا من أرضنا بسحرك يا موسى

translation: Then we will surely bring you magic like it, so make between us and you an appointment, which we will not fail to keep [and] neither will you, [in] a place assigned.
interpretation: This verse is a challenge from the magicians of Pharaoh's court to Moses, after he had shown them signs of his prophethood. They were not willing to believe in his message despite witnessing his miracles. Instead, they arrogantly claimed that they could produce magic similar to his signs. They challenged Moses to set an appointed time and place where both sides would meet and demonstrate their abilities, without fail. This shows the stubbornness and pride of those who oppose the truth, even when faced with clear evidence. Rather than humbly accepting the signs of God, they resort to challenging and denying them.
orig: فلنأتينك بسحر مثله فاجعل بيننا وبينك موعدا لا نخلفه نحن ولا أنت مكانا سوى

translation: He said, "Your appointment is on the day of the festival when the people assemble at mid-morning."
interpretation: This verse refers to the challenge between Moses and the magicians of Pharaoh's court. Pharaoh sets the time and place for this public contest - the day of the festival at mid-morning, when all the people will be gathered to witness the event. The choice of this specific time and occasion shows Pharaoh's arrogance and his desire to make a spectacle out of the confrontation, as he is confident that his magicians will easily overcome Moses. It also sets the stage for God's great signs to be displayed before the maximum number of people, so that they may witness His power and the truth of Moses' message, and so that Pharaoh's scheme may be utterly defeated in front of his subjects.
orig: قال موعدكم يوم الزينة وأن يحشر الناس ضحى

translation: So Pharaoh turned away, put together his plan, and then came [to Moses].
interpretation: This verse shows the arrogance and defiance of Pharaoh in the face of Moses' message and miracles. Despite witnessing clear signs, Pharaoh refused to acknowledge the truth and instead turned away to plot against Moses. He gathered his forces and advisors to devise a scheme to discredit or defeat Moses, rather than humbling himself and accepting the message. This highlights the stubborn nature of those in power who are unwilling to relinquish their authority, even in the face of overwhelming evidence. It also demonstrates the patience and perseverance required of prophets and believers in the face of opposition and hostility from those who reject the truth.
orig: فتولى فرعون فجمع كيده ثم أتى

translation: Moses said to them, "Woe to you! Do not invent falsehood against Allah or He will exterminate you with a punishment; and he has failed who invents [such falsehood]."
interpretation: This verse is a stern warning against attributing lies to Allah or falsely claiming things about Him. Moses admonishes his people not to invent falsehoods about Allah, as doing so will bring His punishment and wrath upon them leading to their destruction. Inventing lies about Allah is presented as a path to utter failure and ruin. The verse emphasizes the gravity of this sin and aims to deter people from engaging in it by highlighting the severe consequences. It is an exhortation to be truthful about Allah and not spread misinformation or lies about Him and His teachings.
orig: قال لهم موسى ويلكم لا تفتروا على الله كذبا فيسحتكم بعذاب وقد خاب من افترى

translation: Then they disputed between themselves about their affair and concealed their private conversation.
interpretation: This verse refers to a group of people who were in disagreement about a certain matter. Instead of openly discussing and resolving the issue, they chose to have secret conversations and private discussions amongst themselves. This behavior of concealing their true thoughts and intentions behind closed doors suggests a lack of transparency, trust, and sincerity within the group. It highlights the negative consequences of not addressing conflicts or differences of opinion openly and honestly, as it can lead to further division, misunderstandings, and a breakdown in communication and cooperation.
orig: فتنازعوا أمرهم بينهم وأسروا النجوى

translation: They said, "Indeed, these are two magicians who want to drive you out of your land with their magic and do away with your most exemplary way [of life]."
interpretation: This verse refers to the accusations made by Pharaoh and his people against Moses and Aaron, claiming that they were magicians who aimed to disrupt the established order and way of life in Egypt. The interpretation is that those in power often view those who challenge the status quo as a threat, even when the challengers are divinely inspired prophets. It highlights the tendency of those in authority to discredit and undermine the message of truth by labeling it as sorcery or deception, in order to maintain their own power and influence over the people.
orig: قالوا إن هذان لساحران يريدان أن يخرجاكم من أرضكم بسحرهما ويذهبا بطريقتكم المثلى

translation: So resolve upon your plan and then come [forward] in line. And he has succeeded today who overcomes.
interpretation: This verse is a challenge to the disbelievers who oppose the message of Islam. It tells them to gather their forces and come up with their best plan to defeat the truth, and then to array themselves in ranks against the believers. However, it also asserts that despite their efforts, only those who stand firm upon the truth and rise above falsehood will be the ultimate victors. It is a reminder that the scheming of the disbelievers is futile before the power of Allah, and that success lies in aligning oneself with the divine will.
orig: فأجمعوا كيدكم ثم ائتوا صفا وقد أفلح اليوم من استعلى

translation: They said, "O Moses, either you throw [your staff], or we will be the first to throw [our magic]."
interpretation: This verse is from the story of Moses and the magicians of Pharaoh. The magicians challenge Moses to either throw his staff first or let them begin the contest. They are confident in their magic and believe they can defeat Moses. However, this challenge also shows their arrogance and disbelief in the power of Allah. The verse sets the stage for the miraculous event where Moses' staff, by Allah's will, transforms into a serpent and devours the illusions created by the magicians, proving the superiority of Allah's power over any form of magic or deception.
orig: قالوا يا موسى إما أن تلقي وإما أن نكون أول من ألقى

translation: He said: "Nay, throw ye first!" Then behold their ropes and their rods - so it seemed to him on account of their magic - began to be in lively motion!
interpretation: This verse is referring to the confrontation between Moses and the magicians of Pharaoh's court. When challenged to show their skills, the magicians cast down their ropes and staffs, which through their magic, appeared to Moses as if they were moving serpents. This illusion was so convincing that even Moses felt a sense of fear within himself at that moment. The verse highlights the power of deception and how it can shake the faith of even the most resolute believers. It serves as a reminder that we must remain steadfast in our belief in God, even when faced with seemingly convincing illusions or challenges to our faith.
orig: قال بل ألقوا فإذا حبالهم وعصيهم يخيل إليه من سحرهم أنها تسعى

translation: And Moses felt in himself apprehension
interpretation: This verse captures the human side of Moses, one of the greatest prophets in Islam. Despite his strong faith and close relationship with God, Moses still experiences fear and anxiety when faced with a challenging situation. It shows that even the most righteous individuals are not immune to human emotions and weaknesses. The verse reminds us that it is natural to feel apprehensive or afraid at times, but we should strive to overcome these feelings through trust in God and reliance on His guidance and support. It also highlights the importance of recognizing and acknowledging our own limitations and seeking help from God in times of difficulty.
orig: فأوجس في نفسه خيفة موسى

translation: We said, "Fear not, for you are the superior one."
interpretation: This verse is reassuring the Prophet Moses (peace be upon him) that he should not fear the magicians or their magic, as Allah has granted him superiority over them. It emphasizes the power and support of Allah for His prophets and believers, even in the face of seemingly formidable challenges or opponents. The verse encourages the believer to have faith and confidence in Allah's help and not to be intimidated by the apparent strength of those who oppose the truth.
orig: قلنا لا تخف إنك أنت الأعلى

translation: And throw what is in your right hand; it will swallow up what they have crafted. What they have crafted is but the trick of a magician, and the magician will not succeed wherever he is.
interpretation: This verse can be interpreted as a reminder that the truth will always prevail over falsehood and deception. The magicians' tricks, no matter how impressive they may seem, are ultimately futile and will be exposed by the power of truth. It also suggests that those who engage in deception and trickery will not find lasting success, as their actions will eventually catch up with them. The verse encourages believers to have faith in the ultimate triumph of truth and to stand firm against those who seek to mislead or deceive.
orig: وألق ما في يمينك تلقف ما صنعوا إنما صنعوا كيد ساحر ولا يفلح الساحر حيث أتى

translation: So the magicians fell down in prostration, saying, "We believe in the Lord of Aaron and Moses."
interpretation: This verse illustrates the profound impact that Moses' miracle had on the magicians. Despite being skilled in their craft, they immediately recognized the superior power of God when confronted with a genuine miracle. By prostrating and declaring their belief in the Lord of Moses and Aaron, the magicians demonstrated humility, submission, and a willingness to abandon their previous beliefs in the face of divine truth. This act of faith highlights the transformative nature of witnessing God's signs and the importance of acknowledging the supremacy of the Almighty, even for those who were once opposed to His message.
orig: فألقي السحرة سجدا قالوا آمنا برب هارون وموسى

translation: He said, "You believed him before I gave you permission. Indeed, he is your leader who has taught you magic. So I will surely cut off your hands and your feet on opposite sides, and I will crucify you on the trunks of palm trees, and you will surely know which of us is more severe in [giving] punishment and more enduring."
interpretation: This verse is a threat from Pharaoh to the magicians who believed in Moses. Pharaoh accuses Moses of being their master who taught them magic, and threatens to cut off their hands and feet on opposite sides and crucify them on palm trunks as punishment for their belief. He asserts that this will make them realize that his punishment is more severe and lasting than anything Moses could do. It shows Pharaoh's arrogance, cruelty and his desperation to maintain control and suppress the truth of Moses' message at any cost.
orig: قال آمنتم له قبل أن آذن لكم إنه لكبيركم الذي علمكم السحر فلأقطعن أيديكم وأرجلكم من خلاف ولأصلبنكم في جذوع النخل ولتعلمن أينا أشد عذابا وأبقى

translation: They said, "Never will we prefer you over what has come to us of clear proofs and [over] He who created us. So decree whatever you are to decree. You can only decree for this worldly life."
interpretation: This verse highlights the steadfastness and conviction of the believers in the face of opposition and threats from those in power. They declare that they will never prioritize the ruler's demands over the clear signs and proofs that have come to them from God, their Creator. The believers recognize that the ruler's authority is limited to this temporary worldly life, and they are willing to face any consequences in this world for the sake of their faith. This demonstrates their deep trust in God and their willingness to sacrifice for the sake of truth and righteousness.
orig: قالوا لن نؤثرك على ما جاءنا من البينات والذي فطرنا فاقض ما أنت قاض إنما تقضي هذه الحياة الدنيا

translation: We have believed in our Lord that He may forgive us our sins and what you compelled us [to do] of magic. And Allah is better and more enduring.
interpretation: This verse speaks to the power of sincere faith and repentance. Despite being compelled to practice magic, which is considered a grave sin in Islam, the believers turn to Allah seeking His forgiveness. They acknowledge their wrongdoings and place their trust in Allah's mercy and grace. The verse emphasizes that Allah's forgiveness and eternal reward are far superior to any temporary worldly gains or pressures. It encourages believers to turn to Allah in repentance, no matter the magnitude of their sins, with the assurance that Allah's forgiveness and blessings are boundless for those who sincerely seek Him.
orig: إنا آمنا بربنا ليغفر لنا خطايانا وما أكرهتنا عليه من السحر والله خير وأبقى

translation: Indeed, whoever comes to his Lord as a criminal - then indeed, for him is Hell; he will neither die therein nor live.
interpretation: This verse is a stern warning to those who commit sins and crimes, and then come before Allah on the Day of Judgment without repenting and seeking forgiveness. It emphasizes that such individuals will be condemned to Hell, where they will suffer eternally, neither dying to find relief nor truly living a meaningful life. This interpretation highlights the severity of the punishment that awaits the unrepentant sinners and serves as a reminder for people to mend their ways, seek Allah's forgiveness, and lead a righteous life to avoid this dreadful fate in the Hereafter.
orig: إنه من يأت ربه مجرما فإن له جهنم لا يموت فيها ولا يحيى

translation: But whoever comes to Him as a believer having done righteous deeds - for those will be the highest degrees [in position].
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of faith and good deeds in attaining the highest ranks in the sight of Allah. Those who come to Him with sincere belief and have performed righteous actions throughout their lives will be granted the loftiest positions in Paradise. This interpretation highlights the significance of combining faith with good works, as both are essential for achieving the ultimate reward from Allah. It serves as an encouragement for believers to strive for excellence in their spiritual and moral conduct, knowing that their efforts will be duly recognized and rewarded in the Hereafter.
orig: ومن يأته مؤمنا قد عمل الصالحات فأولئك لهم الدرجات العلى

translation: Gardens of Eden, beneath which rivers flow, they will abide therein forever, and that is the reward of the one who purifies himself.
interpretation: This verse speaks about the ultimate reward for those who purify themselves spiritually and lead a righteous life. It describes the eternal bliss of Paradise, represented by the Gardens of Eden, where rivers flow beneath the lush greenery. The phrase "they will abide therein forever" emphasizes the everlasting nature of this reward, indicating that the believers will enjoy the blessings of Paradise for all eternity. The verse concludes by stating that this is the recompense for those who purify themselves, suggesting that spiritual purification and righteousness are the key to attaining this sublime reward from Allah. It serves as a reminder and motivation for believers to strive for inner purity and lead a life of goodness and piety.
orig: جنات عدن تجري من تحتها الأنهار خالدين فيها وذلك جزاء من تزكى

translation: And We had inspired to Moses, "Travel by night with My servants and strike for them a dry path through the sea; you will not fear being overtaken [by Pharaoh] nor be afraid [of drowning]."
interpretation: This verse is a reminder of God's power and mercy towards His servants. It shows that God can provide a way out of difficult situations for those who trust in Him and follow His guidance. The verse also highlights the importance of having faith and courage in the face of adversity, as exemplified by Moses who led his people to safety despite the seemingly impossible odds. It teaches us to rely on God's help and protection, even in the most challenging circumstances.
orig: ولقد أوحينا إلى موسى أن أسر بعبادي فاضرب لهم طريقا في البحر يبسا لا تخاف دركا ولا تخشى

translation: Then Pharaoh pursued them with his soldiers, and there covered them from the sea that which covered them.
interpretation: This verse refers to the story of Prophet Moses and the Israelites' escape from Egypt. As they fled, Pharaoh and his army chased after them. However, God commanded Moses to strike the sea with his staff, causing it to split and allowing the Israelites to cross safely. When Pharaoh and his soldiers attempted to follow, the sea closed in on them, drowning them all. This event demonstrates God's power and protection over His believers, as well as the consequences faced by those who oppose His will and oppress others. It serves as a reminder to have faith in God's plan and to stand firm in the face of adversity.
orig: فأتبعهم فرعون بجنوده فغشيهم من اليم ما غشيهم

translation: And Pharaoh led his people astray and did not guide [them].
interpretation: This verse highlights the role of leaders in misguiding their followers. Pharaoh, with his arrogance and tyranny, led his people away from the path of truth and righteousness. Instead of guiding them towards God and His message, he actively misled them, causing them to reject faith and follow him in his wrongdoing. The verse serves as a warning against blindly following misguided leaders and emphasizes the importance of discernment and adherence to divine guidance rather than human authority.
orig: وأضل فرعون قومه وما هدى

translation: O Children of Israel! We delivered you from your enemy, and We made a covenant with you on the right side of Mount (Sinai), and We sent down to you Al-Manna and quails,
interpretation: This verse is a reminder to the Children of Israel of the favors that Allah bestowed upon them. It highlights how Allah saved them from their enemy, the Egyptians, and made a covenant with them on the right side of Mount Sinai. This covenant likely refers to the commandments and laws given to Moses. Additionally, Allah provided them with sustenance in the form of Al-Manna, a sweet substance, and quails, a type of bird. These favors demonstrate Allah's care and mercy towards the Children of Israel, despite their past transgressions. The verse serves as an admonition for them to be grateful and obedient to Allah's commands.
orig: يا بني إسرائيل قد أنجيناكم من عدوكم وواعدناكم جانب الطور الأيمن ونزلنا عليكم المن والسلوى

translation: Eat from the good things which We have provided for you and do not transgress in it, lest My anger should descend upon you. And he upon whom My anger descends has certainly fallen.
interpretation: This verse is a reminder for people to be grateful for the blessings and sustenance that Allah has provided them with. It encourages them to consume what is lawful and good, and warns against transgressing the boundaries set by Allah in pursuit of worldly desires. The verse emphasizes that those who incur Allah's anger by disobeying His commands and indulging in excesses will face severe consequences and will be in a state of loss and ruin. It highlights the importance of moderation, gratitude, and obedience to Allah in all aspects of life, including the consumption of food and other bounties bestowed upon humans by their Creator.
orig: كلوا من طيبات ما رزقناكم ولا تطغوا فيه فيحل عليكم غضبي ومن يحلل عليه غضبي فقد هوى

translation: And indeed, I am the Perpetual Forgiver of whoever repents and believes and does righteousness and then continues in guidance.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the boundless mercy and forgiveness of Allah towards those who sincerely repent from their sins, embrace true faith, perform good deeds, and remain steadfast on the path of guidance. It highlights that no matter how grave one's past mistakes might have been, the door to forgiveness is always open for those who turn back to Allah with a contrite heart and a firm resolve to mend their ways. The verse serves as a powerful reminder of Allah's infinite compassion and a source of hope for all those seeking redemption and spiritual purification.
orig: وإني لغفار لمن تاب وآمن وعمل صالحا ثم اهتدى

translation: And what made you hasten from your people, O Moses?
interpretation: This verse is addressing Prophet Moses (peace be upon him) and questioning him about why he hastened to meet Allah, leaving his people behind. It suggests that Moses was so eager to receive revelation and guidance from Allah that he rushed ahead of his people to the appointed meeting place. This demonstrates Moses' strong faith, dedication, and longing to be close to his Lord. It also highlights the importance of balancing individual spiritual pursuits with the responsibility of guiding and leading one's community.
orig: وما أعجلك عن قومك يا موسى

translation: He said, "There the people are following in my footsteps, and I have hastened to You, my Lord, that You be pleased."
interpretation: In this verse, Moses is explaining to Allah why he has come ahead of his people. He states that the people are following behind him on the path, but he has hastened ahead to meet Allah sooner, seeking His pleasure and approval. This shows Moses' eagerness and devotion to Allah, as he is not content to merely follow the pace of his people, but rushes forward to be in Allah's presence as soon as possible. It reflects his deep desire to please his Lord and be close to Him.
orig: قال هم أولاء على أثري وعجلت إليك رب لترضى

translation: He said, "But indeed, We have tried your people after you [departed], and the Samiri has led them astray."
interpretation: This verse refers to the incident when Moses left his people for forty days to receive the Torah from Allah. In his absence, a man named Samiri misled the people by creating a golden calf for them to worship. The verse highlights the weakness of faith among the Israelites and their susceptibility to idolatry. It also emphasizes the importance of having strong leadership and guidance to keep the community on the right path. The incident serves as a reminder for all believers to remain steadfast in their faith and to be cautious of those who try to lead them astray from the worship of the One True God.
orig: قال فإنا قد فتنا قومك من بعدك وأضلهم السامري

translation: So Moses returned to his people, angry and grieved. He said, "O my people, did your Lord not make you a good promise? Then, was the time [of its fulfillment] too long for you, or did you wish that wrath from your Lord should descend upon you, so you broke your promise [of obedience] to me?"
interpretation: This verse highlights Moses' disappointment and anger towards his people for breaking their promise to worship Allah alone and follow His commandments during his absence. It suggests that the people may have grown impatient waiting for Moses' return or deliberately chose to disobey Allah, knowing it would invite His wrath upon them. The verse emphasizes the importance of keeping one's promises, especially those made to Allah or His messengers, and the consequences of breaking such promises. It also shows Moses' concern for his people's spiritual well-being and his role as a prophet in guiding them back to the right path.
orig: فرجع موسى إلى قومه غضبان أسفا قال يا قوم ألم يعدكم ربكم وعدا حسنا أفطال عليكم العهد أم أردتم أن يحل عليكم غضب من ربكم فأخلفتم موعدي

translation: They said, "We did not break our promise to you by our will, but we were made to carry burdens from the ornaments of the people, so we threw them [into the fire], and thus did the Samiri throw."
interpretation: This verse refers to the incident where the Israelites, in Moses' absence, were led astray by the Samiri who made a golden calf for them to worship. When Moses returned and questioned them, they tried to justify their actions by claiming that they were influenced by the Samiri and the weight of the Egyptians' ornaments they carried, which they threw into the fire to create the idol. This highlights the human tendency to shift blame and make excuses for one's wrongdoings, rather than taking responsibility and seeking forgiveness. It also demonstrates the importance of having strong faith and resisting temptations that lead one astray from the path of righteousness.
orig: قالوا ما أخلفنا موعدك بملكنا ولكنا حملنا أوزارا من زينة القوم فقذفناها فكذلك ألقى السامري

translation: Then he extracted for them a calf - an image having a lowing sound - and they said, "This is your god and the god of Moses, but he forgot."
interpretation: This verse refers to the story of the Israelites worshipping a golden calf in the absence of Moses. It suggests that people can be easily misled into idolatry and false worship when their faith is weak and their leader is away. The verse also implies that such idolatry is a form of forgetfulness or heedlessness of the true God. It serves as a warning against being tempted by worldly allures and straying from the path of monotheism, emphasizing the importance of strong faith and adherence to divine guidance to avoid falling into the sin of idolatry.
orig: فأخرج لهم عجلا جسدا له خوار فقالوا هذا إلهكم وإله موسى فنسي

translation: Do they not see that it does not return to them any speech and does not possess for them [the power of] harm or benefit?
interpretation: This verse is pointing out the futility and irrationality of worshipping idols or false gods. It asks the rhetorical question of whether the idol worshippers do not realize that their idols are incapable of responding to them or providing them any benefit or harm. The implication is that it is foolish to worship or put one's trust in inanimate objects or imaginary beings that have no power or agency. True divinity belongs only to Allah, who is All-Hearing, All-Knowing and All-Powerful. Worshipping anything else is misguided and ultimately fruitless.
orig: أفلا يرون ألا يرجع إليهم قولا ولا يملك لهم ضرا ولا نفعا

translation: And Aaron had already told them before [the return of Moses], "O my people, you are only being tested by it, and indeed, your Lord is the Most Merciful, so follow me and obey my order."
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of following the guidance of the prophets and messengers sent by Allah.
