Aaron, in the absence of Moses, reminds the people that their worship of the golden calf is a test from Allah and that they should not be swayed by it. He emphasizes that their true Lord is the Most Merciful and that they should follow his teachings and obey his commands. The verse also underscores the role of the prophets as guides and leaders who strive to keep their people on the right path, even in the face of challenges and tests from Allah.
orig: ولقد قال لهم هارون من قبل يا قوم إنما فتنتم به وإن ربكم الرحمن فاتبعوني وأطيعوا أمري

translation: They said, "We will never cease being devoted to the calf until Moses returns to us."
interpretation: This verse shows the stubborn nature of the Israelites who, despite witnessing God's signs and miracles, turned to idol worship in Moses' absence. It highlights their weak faith and the ease with which they were misled by their desires and temptations. The verse also emphasizes the importance of having strong, righteous leaders who can guide people and keep them on the right path, as the Israelites quickly went astray without Moses' presence and guidance. It serves as a warning to believers to remain steadfast in their faith and to be cautious of falling into idol worship or other forms of disobedience to God, even in the absence of their religious leaders.
orig: قالوا لن نبرح عليه عاكفين حتى يرجع إلينا موسى

translation: He said, "O Aaron, what prevented you, when you saw them going astray,
interpretation: In this verse, Allah is questioning Aaron (Harun) about why he did not stop the people from going astray and worshipping the golden calf when Moses (Musa) was away receiving the Torah. It highlights the responsibility of religious leaders and those in authority to guide and prevent their followers from falling into misguidance and sin. The verse emphasizes the importance of taking action against wrongdoing and not remaining silent or passive in the face of deviation from the straight path of Allah's guidance.
orig: قال يا هارون ما منعك إذ رأيتهم ضلوا

translation: "Then will you not follow me? Have you then disobeyed my order?"
interpretation: This verse is a rebuke from Allah to someone who has disobeyed His command and refused to follow the guidance of His messenger. It emphasizes the importance of obedience to Allah and His messengers, and implies that disobedience is a grave sin that will lead to serious consequences. The rhetorical question "Then will you not follow me?" serves as a strong admonishment and a call to rectify one's behavior and submit to the will of Allah.
orig: ألا تتبعن أفعصيت أمري

translation: He said, "O son of my mother, do not seize [me] by my beard or by my head. Indeed, I feared that you would say, 'You caused division among the Children of Israel, and you did not observe [or await] my word.' "
interpretation: This verse is addressing the importance of maintaining unity and avoiding division among the believers. It emphasizes the significance of respecting and obeying the commands of the prophets and leaders appointed by Allah. The verse also highlights the fear of being held accountable for causing disunity and not following the instructions of those in authority. It serves as a reminder to the believers to strive for unity, obedience, and the preservation of the community's cohesion.
orig: قال يا ابن أم لا تأخذ بلحيتي ولا برأسي إني خشيت أن تقول فرقت بين بني إسرائيل ولم ترقب قولي

translation: He said, "And what is your case, O Samiri?"
interpretation: In this verse, Allah is questioning Samiri about his reason for leading the people astray by creating the golden calf for worship. It shows that Allah holds individuals accountable for their actions and misguidance of others. The verse serves as a reminder that we will all be questioned about our deeds and intentions, emphasizing the importance of staying on the right path and not being a source of misguidance for others. It also highlights the significance of sincerity in worship and not associating partners with Allah.
orig: قال فما خطبك يا سامري

translation: He said, "I saw what they did not see, so I took a handful [of dust] from the track of the messenger and threw it, and thus did my soul entice me."
interpretation: This verse is referring to the story of the Samiri, who led the Israelites astray by creating a golden calf for them to worship while Moses was away on Mount Sinai. The Samiri is saying that he saw an opportunity that the others did not see, and he took some dust from the hoofprints of the horse of the Angel Gabriel, who had come as a messenger. He threw this dust onto the molten gold, and it formed into a calf that made a lowing sound, which the Israelites then began to worship. The Samiri is admitting that his own soul enticed him to do this misleading act, implying that it was his own evil inclinations and desires that led him astray, rather than any outside force or the influence of Satan.
orig: قال بصرت بما لم يبصروا به فقبضت قبضة من أثر الرسول فنبذتها وكذلك سولت لي نفسي

translation: He said, "Then go, and indeed, it is for you [that] throughout life none will touch you. And indeed, you have an appointment [in the Hereafter] you will not fail to keep. And look at your 'god' to which you remained devoted. We will surely burn it and blow it [i.e., its ashes] into the sea with a blast."
interpretation: This verse is a warning to those who worship false gods and idols. It emphasizes the futility of devoting oneself to anything other than Allah, as these false objects of worship will ultimately be destroyed and reduced to nothing. The verse also highlights the inevitability of the Day of Judgment, where everyone will be held accountable for their actions and beliefs. It serves as a reminder to focus on worshipping Allah alone and to avoid being distracted by temporary worldly attachments that will not benefit us in the Hereafter.
orig: قال فاذهب فإن لك في الحياة أن تقول لا مساس وإن لك موعدا لن تخلفه وانظر إلى إلهك الذي ظلت عليه عاكفا لنحرقنه ثم لننسفنه في اليم نسفا

translation: Your god is only Allah, there is no deity except Him. He encompasses all things in knowledge.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the oneness and uniqueness of Allah as the only true God worthy of worship. It highlights His all-encompassing knowledge, indicating that nothing escapes His awareness and understanding. The verse serves as a reminder for believers to direct their faith, devotion, and reliance solely towards Allah, acknowledging His supreme authority and wisdom over all matters in the universe.
orig: إنما إلهكم الله الذي لا إله إلا هو وسع كل شيء علما

translation: Thus We relate to you, [O Muhammad], from the news of what has preceded. And We have certainly given you from Us the Qur'an.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah is revealing stories of the past prophets and their nations to Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) through the Qur'an. The Qur'an serves as a reminder and a guidance for him and his followers. It is a special gift from Allah to Muhammad, providing him with knowledge and wisdom that will benefit him in his mission as the final messenger to humanity. The stories of the past serve as lessons and examples for the believers to learn from and apply in their own lives.
orig: كذلك نقص عليك من أنباء ما قد سبق وقد آتيناك من لدنا ذكرا

translation: But whoever turns away from it - then indeed, he will bear on the Day of Resurrection a burden,
interpretation: This verse warns that those who turn away from the Qur'an and its teachings will bear a heavy burden of sin on the Day of Judgment. They will be held accountable for their rejection of divine guidance and will face the consequences of their actions. The "burden" mentioned symbolizes the weight of their transgressions and the spiritual toll it will take on them in the Hereafter. It emphasizes the gravity of turning away from the truth and the importance of adhering to the Qur'an's message for one's own salvation.
orig: من أعرض عنه فإنه يحمل يوم القيامة وزرا

translation: Abiding eternally therein. And wretched is it for them on the Day of Resurrection as a load.
interpretation: This verse warns that those who reject faith and do evil deeds will bear the terrible consequences of their actions on the Day of Judgment. The "load" they will carry on that day refers to the heavy burden of their sins and misdeeds. It emphasizes the gravity and permanence of the punishment they will face in the Hereafter for their wrongdoings and disobedience to Allah in this worldly life. The verse serves as a strong reminder for people to be mindful of their actions and to strive for righteousness.
orig: خالدين فيه وساء لهم يوم القيامة حملا

translation: The Day the Horn will be blown, and We will gather the criminals, that Day, blue-eyed.
interpretation: This verse refers to the Day of Judgment when the Horn will be blown to signal the resurrection of the dead. The criminals, meaning the disbelievers and sinners, will be gathered with their eyes strained and their faces blue with fear and horror, realizing the consequences of their actions in this world. The blue color of their eyes is interpreted as a sign of extreme terror and anguish, as they face the reality of the Hereafter and the punishment that awaits them for their wrongdoings. This verse serves as a reminder of the ultimate accountability and the severity of the consequences for those who reject faith and engage in evil deeds.
orig: يوم ينفخ في الصور ونحشر المجرمين يومئذ زرقا

translation: They will whisper among themselves, "You remained not but ten [days in the world]."
interpretation: This verse refers to the Day of Judgment when the disbelievers will be resurrected and realize the brevity of their worldly life. They will whisper among themselves in shock, stating that their entire earthly existence felt like a mere ten days compared to the eternal consequences they now face. This serves as a reminder for mankind to not be deceived by the fleeting nature of this world and to instead focus on preparing for the Hereafter through faith and righteous deeds, as the perception of time will drastically differ in the afterlife.
orig: يتخافتون بينهم إن لبثتم إلا عشرا

translation: We know best what they say when the best of them in manner [i.e., wisdom or speech] says, "You remained not but one day."
interpretation: This verse is referring to the Day of Judgment, when the disbelievers will realize the brevity of their life in this world compared to the eternal afterlife. Even those among them who were most wise and eloquent in speech will acknowledge that their time on earth felt like a mere day. It emphasizes how people's perception of time will drastically change when faced with the realities of the Hereafter, and they will regret not having used their limited time in the world to prepare for eternity by following God's guidance.
orig: نحن أعلم بما يقولون إذ يقول أمثلهم طريقة إن لبثتم إلا يوما

translation: And they ask you about the mountains, so say, "My Lord will blow them away with a blast."
interpretation: This verse is referring to the Day of Judgment when Allah will destroy the mountains, reducing them to scattered dust. It emphasizes the immense power of Allah and the momentous events that will unfold on that day. The verse also serves as a reminder of the transient nature of this world and the importance of preparing for the eternal life to come by living righteously and in obedience to Allah's commands. It encourages believers to focus on their spiritual growth rather than being attached to the temporary and illusory aspects of this worldly life.
orig: ويسألونك عن الجبال فقل ينسفها ربي نسفا

translation: And He leaves it a level plain.
interpretation: This verse is referring to the power and might of Allah, who is capable of transforming the earth into a flat and barren plain, devoid of any vegetation or irregularities. It emphasizes the idea that all of creation is subject to Allah's will and that He has the ability to alter the very nature of the world as He sees fit. The verse serves as a reminder of the temporary nature of this world and the ultimate authority of Allah over all things.
orig: فيذرها قاعا صفصفا

translation: In it you will see neither crookedness nor curve.
interpretation: This verse is referring to the perfection and flawlessness of Paradise. It suggests that in Paradise, everything will be perfectly straight and even, without any imperfections or irregularities. This can be understood both literally, in terms of the physical landscape and architecture of Paradise, and metaphorically, in terms of the moral and spiritual rectitude of its inhabitants. The verse emphasizes the idea that Paradise is a place of ultimate perfection and harmony, where everything is as it should be, and where there is no room for any kind of deviation or imperfection. This serves to highlight the reward that awaits the righteous in the afterlife, and to encourage believers to strive for righteousness and perfection in this life.
orig: لا ترى فيها عوجا ولا أمتا

translation: That Day, they will follow [the call of] the Caller [with] no deviation therefrom, and [all] voices will be stilled before the Most Merciful, so you will not hear except a whisper [of footsteps].
interpretation: This verse refers to the Day of Judgment when all of humanity will be resurrected and will obediently answer the call of the Caller, who is Allah or an angel appointed by Him. They will follow the Caller without turning away or deviating from the path. On that momentous day, all voices will be humbled and silenced in submission to the Most Merciful, Allah. The only sound that will be heard is the whispering or the soft sound of footsteps as people proceed towards their final destination, emphasizing the gravity and solemnity of the occasion. This verse underscores the absolute authority and power of Allah on the Day of Judgment and the complete submission of all beings before Him.
orig: يومئذ يتبعون الداعي لا عوج له وخشعت الأصوات للرحمن فلا تسمع إلا همسا

translation: On that Day, no intercession will benefit except [that of] one to whom the Most Merciful has given permission and has accepted his word.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute authority and sovereignty of Allah on the Day of Judgment. It states that on that day, no one will be able to intercede or plead on behalf of another person, except those whom Allah has granted permission to do so, and whose words and deeds Allah is pleased with. This highlights the importance of living a righteous life and seeking Allah's pleasure in this world, as it will be the only way to attain His mercy and forgiveness in the Hereafter. The verse also serves as a reminder that ultimately, it is only Allah's judgment and decision that will matter on that Day, and no one else will have the power to influence the outcome.
orig: يومئذ لا تنفع الشفاعة إلا من أذن له الرحمن ورضي له قولا

translation: He knows what is [presently] before them and what will be after them, but they do not encompass it in knowledge.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the limitless knowledge of Allah, who is aware of everything that has happened in the past and everything that will happen in the future. It also highlights the limited knowledge of human beings, who can never fully comprehend the vastness of Allah's wisdom and understanding. The verse reminds believers to trust in Allah's plan and to recognize that their own knowledge and perception are inherently limited compared to the all-encompassing knowledge of the Creator.
orig: يعلم ما بين أيديهم وما خلفهم ولا يحيطون به علما

translation: And [all] faces will be humbled before the Ever-Living, the Sustainer of existence. And he will have failed who carries injustice.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the ultimate submission and humility of all beings before Allah, the Ever-Living and Self-Sustaining. On the Day of Judgment, everyone will bow down before Him, realizing His supreme authority. Those who have lived their lives with injustice and wrongdoing will face the consequences of their actions, as they will have failed in the sight of Allah. It serves as a reminder that we should strive to live righteously and avoid oppressing others, as we will be held accountable for our deeds in the Hereafter. Ultimately, it is only through humility, obedience, and justice that one can attain success and salvation in the eyes of Allah.
orig: وعنت الوجوه للحي القيوم وقد خاب من حمل ظلما

translation: And whoever does righteous deeds while he is a believer - he will neither fear injustice nor deprivation.
interpretation: This verse assures believers that if they do good deeds with sincere faith, they need not worry about being treated unjustly or being deprived of the rewards for their actions. It emphasizes that Allah is just and will ensure that everyone receives what they deserve based on their deeds and intentions. This promise provides comfort and motivation for the believers to persist in righteousness, knowing that their efforts will not be in vain and that they will be fairly compensated in this life and the hereafter.
orig: ومن يعمل من الصالحات وهو مؤمن فلا يخاف ظلما ولا هضما

translation: And thus We have sent it down as an Arabic Qur'an and have diversified therein the warnings that perhaps they will avoid [sin] or it would cause them remembrance.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the divine nature of the Qur'an, which has been revealed in the Arabic language. The purpose of the Qur'an's revelation is to provide warnings and reminders to humanity, with the hope that they will take heed and avoid sinful actions. The diversification of warnings throughout the Qur'an serves to reinforce its message and increase the likelihood that people will be mindful of their actions and remember Allah's guidance. This verse highlights the Qur'an's role as a source of guidance and a means of encouraging righteousness among believers.
orig: وكذلك أنزلناه قرآنا عربيا وصرفنا فيه من الوعيد لعلهم يتقون أو يحدث لهم ذكرا

translation: So high [above all] is Allah, the Sovereign, the Truth. And, [O Muhammad], do not hasten with [recitation of] the Qur'an before its revelation is completed to you, and say, "My Lord, increase me in knowledge."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the supreme authority and truthfulness of Allah, while instructing Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) to be patient in receiving the revelation of the Qur'an. It also serves as a reminder for the Prophet and all believers to continuously seek an increase in knowledge from Allah. This highlights the importance of patience, humility, and the pursuit of knowledge in the life of a Muslim, as these qualities are essential for spiritual growth and understanding the divine message of the Qur'an.
orig: فتعالى الله الملك الحق ولا تعجل بالقرآن من قبل أن يقضى إليك وحيه وقل رب زدني علما

translation: And We had already taken a promise from Adam before, but he forgot; and We found not in him determination.
interpretation: This verse highlights the weakness of human nature and the importance of resolve and determination in fulfilling one's commitments to Allah. Adam, despite being directly created by Allah and given the honor of being the first human, forgot his covenant with Allah when he was tempted by Shaytan to eat from the forbidden tree. This demonstrates that even the most noble of creation can fall into error and disobedience if they lack strong willpower and the resolve to resist temptation. The verse serves as a reminder to all believers to strive for steadfastness in their faith and to be mindful of the promises they make to Allah, as it is through unwavering determination and adherence to Allah's commands that one can hope to attain success in this life and the Hereafter.
orig: ولقد عهدنا إلى آدم من قبل فنسي ولم نجد له عزما

translation: And [mention] when We said to the angels, "Prostrate before Adam"; so they prostrated, except for Iblees. He refused
interpretation: This verse highlights the superiority of Adam (and by extension, humanity) over the angels, as God commanded the angels to bow down to Adam. All the angels obeyed, except for Iblees (Satan), who refused out of pride and arrogance. This act of disobedience led to Iblees being cast out of Paradise and becoming the sworn enemy of mankind, always trying to lead them astray from the path of righteousness. The verse serves as a reminder for humans to be humble, obedient to God's commands, and wary of the temptations and whispers of Satan.
orig: وإذ قلنا للملائكة اسجدوا لآدم فسجدوا إلا إبليس أبى

translation: Then We said, "O Adam, indeed this is an enemy to you and to your wife. Then let him not get you both out of Paradise, so you would suffer.
interpretation: This verse is a warning from Allah to Adam and Eve about the danger posed by Satan. Allah is cautioning them not to listen to Satan's deceptions, as he is their sworn enemy whose goal is to lead them astray and cause them to be expelled from Paradise. The interpretation is that we must be vigilant against the temptations and tricks of Satan, who seeks to exploit our weaknesses and lead us into sin and disobedience to Allah. We should seek refuge in Allah from Satan's evil and strive to follow the righteous path to avoid the fate of being cast out of Allah's favor and into a state of suffering and misery.
orig: فقلنا يا آدم إن هذا عدو لك ولزوجك فلا يخرجنكما من الجنة فتشقى

translation: Indeed, it is [promised] for you not to be hungry therein or be unclothed.
interpretation: This verse is a promise from Allah to the believers that in Paradise, they will never experience hunger or lack of clothing. It emphasizes the complete contentment and satisfaction that the inhabitants of Paradise will enjoy, free from any form of physical discomfort or deprivation. This promise serves as a reminder of the immense rewards that await those who strive to please Allah in this worldly life, and it motivates the believers to remain steadfast in their faith and good deeds.
orig: إن لك ألا تجوع فيها ولا تعرى

translation: And you will not suffer thirst therein or be exposed to the sun.
interpretation: This verse is referring to the blessings and comforts that will be granted to the believers in Paradise. In Paradise, they will not experience any form of discomfort or hardship, such as thirst or exposure to the harsh sun. This is a metaphor indicating that all their needs will be taken care of and they will live in complete ease and pleasure. It signifies the perfection and completeness of the rewards that Allah has prepared for His righteous servants in the eternal life to come.
orig: وأنك لا تظمأ فيها ولا تضحى

translation: Then Satan whispered to him; he said, "O Adam, shall I direct you to the tree of eternity and possession that will not deteriorate?"
interpretation: This verse illustrates the cunning nature of Satan, who seeks to deceive and mislead mankind. Satan whispers to Adam, tempting him with the promise of immortality and eternal possessions if he eats from the forbidden tree. It highlights the deceptive tactics employed by Satan to lure humans away from the path of obedience to Allah. The verse serves as a warning to believers to be vigilant against the whispers and temptations of Satan, who constantly tries to exploit human weaknesses and desires. It emphasizes the importance of seeking refuge in Allah and adhering to His guidance to protect oneself from falling into Satan's traps.
orig: فوسوس إليه الشيطان قال يا آدم هل أدلك على شجرة الخلد وملك لا يبلى

translation: Then they both ate of it, so their private parts became apparent to them, and they began to fasten over themselves from the leaves of Paradise. And Adam disobeyed his Lord and erred.
interpretation: This verse is referring to the story of Adam and Eve in Paradise. The interpretation is that Adam and Eve ate from the forbidden tree after being deceived by Satan. As a result, their nakedness was exposed to them and they tried to cover themselves with the leaves of Paradise. This verse highlights the disobedience of Adam to Allah's command not to eat from that tree, and shows that even Paradise can be a place of temptation and sin. It teaches us the importance of obeying Allah's commands and being mindful of the traps of Satan.
orig: فأكلا منها فبدت لهما سوآتهما وطفقا يخصفان عليهما من ورق الجنة وعصى آدم ربه فغوى

translation: Then his Lord chose him, and turned to him in forgiveness, and guided him.
interpretation: This verse highlights the mercy and guidance of Allah towards those who turn to Him in repentance. It suggests that even if one has strayed or made mistakes, Allah is always ready to forgive and guide those who sincerely seek His forgiveness and guidance. The verse emphasizes the importance of tawbah (repentance) and the fact that Allah's door of mercy is always open for those who turn to Him with a sincere heart. It also implies that being chosen by Allah and receiving His guidance is a great blessing and honor, and that one should strive to be among those who are recipients of Allah's special favor and guidance.
orig: ثم اجتباه ربه فتاب عليه وهدى

translation: He said, "Descend from Paradise - all, [your descendants] being enemies to one another. And if there should come to you guidance from Me - then whoever follows My guidance will neither go astray [in the world] nor suffer [in the Hereafter]."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the consequences of following or rejecting divine guidance. It suggests that after the fall from Paradise, humanity will face conflicts and enmity among themselves. However, God promises that He will provide guidance to mankind. Those who choose to follow this guidance will be protected from going astray in this world and from suffering in the Hereafter. The verse implies that obedience to God's guidance is the key to living a righteous life and attaining salvation, while rejecting it leads to misguidance and suffering. It also highlights the importance of unity and the need to overcome differences by adhering to the divine message.
orig: قال اهبطا منها جميعا بعضكم لبعض عدو فإما يأتينكم مني هدى فمن اتبع هداي فلا يضل ولا يشقى

translation: And whoever turns away from My remembrance - indeed, he will have a depressed life, and We will gather him on the Day of Resurrection blind.
interpretation: This verse is a stern warning from Allah to those who turn away from His remembrance and guidance. It emphasizes that those who choose to ignore Allah's message and live their lives without regard for His commands will face severe consequences, both in this world and the Hereafter. In this world, they will lead a life of misery, depression, and hardship, devoid of true happiness and contentment. This is because true peace and satisfaction can only be found in the remembrance of Allah and obedience to His will. In the Hereafter, they will be resurrected blind, unable to see the truth and the path to salvation, as a result of their spiritual blindness in this world. This verse serves as a powerful reminder for believers to constantly engage in the remembrance of Allah and to strive to live their lives in accordance with His guidance, in order to attain success and happiness in both this world and the next.
orig: ومن أعرض عن ذكري فإن له معيشة ضنكا ونحشره يوم القيامة أعمى

translation: He will say, "My Lord, why have you raised me blind while I was [once] seeing?"
interpretation: This verse is referring to the Day of Judgment when those who were blind to the truth in this worldly life will be resurrected blind in the Hereafter. They will question Allah as to why they have been raised as such, despite having the faculty of sight in the world. It signifies that their spiritual blindness and failure to recognize and follow the truth will manifest as literal blindness in the afterlife. They had the means to see and acknowledge the signs of Allah, but they chose to remain blind to them. As a result, they will face the consequences of their choice in the Hereafter by being resurrected without sight, symbolizing their spiritual state.
orig: قال رب لم حشرتني أعمى وقد كنت بصيرا

translation: Thus did Our signs come to you, but you forgot them; and thus will you this Day be forgotten.
interpretation: This verse is a stern warning to those who ignore or forget the signs and messages of Allah. It emphasizes that just as they neglected and failed to heed the signs sent to them in this worldly life, they will be neglected and forgotten by Allah on the Day of Judgment. It highlights the grave consequences of turning away from divine guidance and the importance of being mindful and attentive to the signs and reminders sent by Allah. Those who are heedless and ungrateful will face the ultimate loss and abandonment in the Hereafter.
orig: قال كذلك أتتك آياتنا فنسيتها وكذلك اليوم تنسى

translation: And thus do We recompense him who transgresses beyond bounds and believes not in the Ayat (proofs, evidences, verses, lessons, signs, revelations, etc.) of his Lord, and the torment of the Hereafter is far more severe and more lasting.
interpretation: This verse warns that those who exceed the limits set by Allah and reject His signs will face severe and lasting punishment in the Hereafter. It emphasizes the gravity of disbelief and the importance of faith. The punishment of the Hereafter is portrayed as being far worse and more enduring than any hardship or suffering experienced in this worldly life. This serves as a strong reminder for individuals to stay within the boundaries of what Allah has ordained and to believe in His messages, as the consequences of transgression and rejection are severe and eternal.
orig: وكذلك نجزي من أسرف ولم يؤمن بآيات ربه ولعذاب الآخرة أشد وأبقى

translation: Does it not then direct them aright how many of the generations In whose dwelling-places they (themselves) do walk about did We destroy before them? Verily, in that are Signs indeed for men endued with understanding.
interpretation: This verse is a reminder to the people that they should take heed from the fate of previous nations who were destroyed by Allah due to their disobedience and rejection of His messages. The fact that the present generation walks amidst the ruins of those destroyed nations should serve as a clear sign and lesson for people of understanding to realize the consequences of going against Allah's commands. It is an invitation to ponder and reflect on the power and might of Allah, and submit to Him alone, so as to avoid a similar dire fate.
orig: أفلم يهد لهم كم أهلكنا قبلهم من القرون يمشون في مساكنهم إن في ذلك لآيات لأولي النهى

translation: And if not for a word that preceded from your Lord, it would have been an obligation [due immediately], and [there would have been] a specified term [for its fulfillment].
interpretation: This verse suggests that if it were not for Allah's prior decree or promise, the punishment for the disbelievers would have been immediate and inevitable. However, Allah has set a specific appointed term for the fulfillment of His judgment, granting respite to humanity. This interpretation highlights Allah's mercy in allowing time for repentance and the opportunity to embrace faith before the arrival of the predetermined moment of reckoning.
orig: ولولا كلمة سبقت من ربك لكان لزاما وأجل مسمى

translation: So be patient over what they say and exalt [Allah] with praise of your Lord before the rising of the sun and before its setting; and during periods of the night [also] exalt [Him] and at the ends of the day that you may be satisfied.
interpretation: This verse is a reminder to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) to remain patient in the face of the disbelief and hostility of his opponents, and to seek comfort and strength in the remembrance of Allah. The verse encourages the Prophet to engage in constant praise and glorification of Allah, particularly at specific times of the day: before sunrise, before sunset, during the night, and at the beginning and end of each day. By doing so, the Prophet is assured that he will find contentment and satisfaction, despite the challenges he faces in conveying the message of Islam. This interpretation emphasizes the importance of maintaining a strong spiritual connection with Allah, especially during times of hardship or adversity, and highlights the role of prayer and remembrance in providing solace and guidance to the believer.
orig: فاصبر على ما يقولون وسبح بحمد ربك قبل طلوع الشمس وقبل غروبها ومن آناء الليل فسبح وأطراف النهار لعلك ترضى

translation: And do not extend your eyes toward that by which We have given enjoyment to [some] categories of them, [its being but] the splendor of worldly life by which We test them. And the provision of your Lord is better and more enduring.
interpretation: This verse reminds us not to be envious of the worldly possessions and luxuries that others may enjoy. These temporary pleasures are merely a test from Allah to see how people will respond. Instead, we should focus on the eternal rewards and provisions that come from Allah, which are far superior and lasting compared to the fleeting nature of this world. True contentment and success lie in seeking Allah's pleasure and striving for the Hereafter.
orig: ولا تمدن عينيك إلى ما متعنا به أزواجا منهم زهرة الحياة الدنيا لنفتنهم فيه ورزق ربك خير وأبقى

translation: And enjoin prayer upon your family [and people] and be steadfast therein. We ask you not for provision; We provide for you, and the [best] outcome is for [those of] righteousness.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of establishing regular prayer and being consistent in its observance. As the head of the household, one should encourage their family to pray and lead by example in maintaining this practice. The verse also highlights that one should not be concerned about their sustenance, as Allah is the ultimate provider. Instead, one should focus on leading a righteous life, as the best outcome in both this world and the hereafter is reserved for those who are mindful of Allah and follow His guidance.
orig: وأمر أهلك بالصلاة واصطبر عليها لا نسألك رزقا نحن نرزقك والعاقبة للتقوى

translation: And they say, "Why does he not bring us a sign from his Lord?" Has there not come to them evidence of what was in the former scriptures?
interpretation: This verse is addressing the skepticism and disbelief of those who demand a miraculous sign from the Prophet Muhammad to prove his prophethood. It points out that the evidence for the truth of his message is already present in the earlier scriptures, such as the Torah and the Gospel, which contain prophecies and indications of his coming. The Qur'an suggests that the disbelievers are ignoring or rejecting this evidence out of stubbornness, rather than genuinely seeking the truth. The implication is that no additional sign should be necessary if one sincerely reflects upon the consistency between Muhammad's message and the teachings of the previous prophets.
orig: وقالوا لولا يأتينا بآية من ربه أولم تأتهم بينة ما في الصحف الأولى

translation: And if We had destroyed them with a punishment before him, they would have said, "Our Lord, why did You not send to us a messenger so we could have followed Your verses before we were humiliated and disgraced?"
interpretation: This verse highlights the wisdom and mercy of Allah in sending messengers and revelations to mankind before punishing them for their transgressions. It suggests that if Allah had punished people without first sending them guidance, they would have complained and argued that they were not given a fair chance to follow the right path. By sending prophets and revelations, Allah removes any excuse or argument people may have for not believing and obeying Him. The verse also emphasizes the importance of following Allah's guidance to avoid humiliation and disgrace in this world and the Hereafter.
orig: ولو أنا أهلكناهم بعذاب من قبله لقالوا ربنا لولا أرسلت إلينا رسولا فنتبع آياتك من قبل أن نذل ونخزى

translation: Say, "Each [of us] is waiting; so wait. For you will know who are the companions of the even path and who is guided."
interpretation: This verse is a challenge to those who oppose the message of Islam and the Prophet Muhammad. It tells them to wait and see the ultimate outcome, for in the end, it will become clear who is on the right path and who is rightly guided. The "companions of the even path" refers to those who follow the straight way of Islam, while those who are "guided" are those who have been blessed with divine guidance and are following the truth. The verse implies that while the opponents of Islam may have power and influence in this world, ultimately it is those who follow the straight path who will be successful in the Hereafter.
orig: قل كل متربص فتربصوا فستعلمون من أصحاب الصراط السوي ومن اهتدى

translation: The people's account has drawn near, and they, in heedlessness, are turning away.
interpretation: This verse is a warning to humanity that the Day of Judgment is approaching, and yet many people remain oblivious and neglectful of this reality. They are preoccupied with worldly matters and have turned away from remembering Allah and preparing for the Hereafter. The verse serves as a reminder for people to wake up from their spiritual slumber, reflect on the purpose of their existence, and mend their ways before it is too late. It emphasizes the importance of being mindful of one's actions and their consequences in the afterlife, rather than being distracted by the temporary pleasures and pursuits of this world.
orig: اقترب للناس حسابهم وهم في غفلة معرضون

translation: No mention comes to them anew from their Lord except that they listen to it while they are at play.
interpretation: This verse is criticizing the attitude of the disbelievers towards the revelation of the Qur'an. Whenever a new verse or chapter of the Qur'an is revealed to them from Allah, they do not pay serious attention to it or reflect deeply on its meanings and lessons. Instead, they listen to it superficially while being distracted and engaged in frivolous activities and amusements. They treat the profound message of the Qur'an, which is meant to guide them, as mere entertainment or background noise, without letting it penetrate their hearts and reform their lives. This demonstrates their lack of sincerity, reverence and receptiveness to divine guidance.
orig: ما يأتيهم من ذكر من ربهم محدث إلا استمعوه وهم يلعبون

translation: Their hearts are distracted, and those who do wrong conceal their private conversation, [saying], "Is this [Prophet] except a human being like you? So would you approach magic while you are aware [of it]?"
interpretation: This verse is referring to the disbelievers who reject the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and his message. Their hearts are heedless and distracted from the truth, and they secretly plot against the Prophet, questioning his humanity and accusing him of practicing magic or sorcery. They fail to recognize that the Prophet is a human being chosen by Allah to convey His message, and that the Qur'an is a divine revelation, not magic. The verse highlights their stubborn refusal to accept the truth despite their awareness of the Prophet's sincerity and the clear proofs of his prophethood.
orig: لاهية قلوبهم وأسروا النجوى الذين ظلموا هل هذا إلا بشر مثلكم أفتأتون السحر وأنتم تبصرون

translation: My Lord knows whatever is said throughout the heaven and earth, and He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the all-encompassing knowledge and awareness of Allah. It affirms that Allah has complete knowledge of everything that is said or happens in the heavens and the earth. Nothing escapes His attention, whether it is spoken openly or secretly. The verse also highlights two of Allah's attributes: As-Sami' (the All-Hearing) and Al-'Aleem (the All-Knowing). These attributes underscore that Allah perceives and hears everything, and He possesses the perfect knowledge of all things, including the intentions and thoughts behind every word uttered by His creation. This understanding should instill a sense of consciousness and mindfulness in the believers, knowing that Allah is always aware of their actions and words, and that they will be held accountable for them.
orig: قال ربي يعلم القول في السماء والأرض وهو السميع العليم

translation: But they say, "[The revelation is but] a mixture of false dreams; rather, he has invented it; rather, he is a poet. So let him bring us a sign just as the previous [messengers] were sent [with miracles]."
interpretation: This verse reflects the disbelief and skepticism of the opponents of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him). They dismissed the Qur'an as a mere collection of muddled dreams or a fabrication by the Prophet himself, whom they accused of being just a poet. They challenged him to produce a miraculous sign to prove his prophethood, similar to the miracles performed by earlier prophets. This demand for a sign demonstrates their obstinacy and unwillingness to accept the truth, as they set conditions for belief based on their own desires rather than openness to divine guidance.
orig: بل قالوا أضغاث أحلام بل افتراه بل هو شاعر فليأتنا بآية كما أرسل الأولون

translation: No city which We destroyed before them had believed. So will they believe?
interpretation: This verse points to the stubbornness and disbelief of past nations who rejected the messages of Allah's prophets despite the clear signs and warnings they received. It suggests that the disbelievers of Mecca, to whom the Prophet Muhammad was sent, are similarly unlikely to believe since they are following the same pattern of denying the truth. The rhetorical question "So will they believe?" emphasizes the expectation that, like those before them, most of the Meccans will persist in their disbelief, as it is the nature of those who have hardened their hearts against divine guidance. It serves as a warning and a reminder of the consequences of rejecting faith, while affirming that the ultimate judgment rests with Allah.
orig: ما آمنت قبلهم من قرية أهلكناها أفهم يؤمنون

translation: And We sent not before you, [O Muhammad], except men to whom We revealed [the message], so ask the people of the message if you do not know.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that all the prophets and messengers sent by Allah before Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) were human beings who received divine revelation. It instructs those who have doubts or questions about the message to seek knowledge from the people of the message, meaning those who have knowledge of the previous scriptures and prophets. This highlights the importance of seeking knowledge from reliable sources and the continuity of the divine message throughout human history.
orig: وما أرسلنا قبلك إلا رجالا نوحي إليهم فاسألوا أهل الذكر إن كنتم لا تعلمون

translation: And We did not make them [i.e., the prophets] bodies not eating food, nor were they immortal.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the humanity of the prophets and messengers. They were not supernatural beings, but rather mortals who had physical needs like eating food. They were also subject to death, as they were not granted immortality. This highlights that the prophets, despite their lofty status and receiving divine revelation, were still human beings with human limitations. It underscores the idea that their extraordinary qualities were due to Allah's favor upon them, not because they possessed inherent superhuman abilities. The verse also implies that their role was to convey the message and be an example to others, not to be worshipped or regarded as divine themselves.
orig: وما جعلناهم جسدا لا يأكلون الطعام وما كانوا خالدين

translation: Then We fulfilled for them the promise, and We saved them and whom We willed and destroyed the transgressors.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's justice and His power over all things. It shows that Allah always fulfills His promises to the believers who are steadfast in their faith and do righteous deeds. He saves them from harm and destruction, along with whomever He wills, while destroying the transgressors who exceed the limits set by Him and disobey His commands. This serves as a reminder for us to stay on the right path, have faith in Allah's promises, and avoid transgression in order to be among those who are saved and not those who are destroyed.
orig: ثم صدقناهم الوعد فأنجيناهم ومن نشاء وأهلكنا المسرفين

translation: We have sent down to you a Book in which is your mention. Then will you not reason?
interpretation: This verse is a reminder from Allah to mankind that He has sent down the Qur'an as a guide and a reminder for them. The Qur'an contains the history of previous nations, the stories of the Prophets, and the teachings that mankind needs to follow in order to attain success in this life and the Hereafter. The verse also serves as a call to mankind to use their intellect and reason to reflect upon the Qur'an and its teachings, rather than blindly following their desires or the ways of their forefathers. It is a reminder that the Qur'an is not just a book to be recited, but a book to be understood and acted upon.
orig: لقد أنزلنا إليكم كتابا فيه ذكركم أفلا تعقلون

translation: And how many a city We destroyed that was unjust, and We produced after it another people.
interpretation: This verse highlights the consequences of injustice and oppression. It suggests that when a society becomes unjust and oppressive, it ultimately leads to its own destruction. Allah, in His wisdom and justice, destroys such communities and replaces them with others who may be more righteous and just. This serves as a warning to all societies to uphold justice and avoid oppression, as it can lead to their downfall. It also emphasizes the idea that no society, no matter how powerful or established, is immune to Allah's judgment if they persist in wrongdoing.
orig: وكم قصمنا من قرية كانت ظالمة وأنشأنا بعدها قوما آخرين

translation: Then, when they perceived Our punishment, at once they fled from it.
interpretation: This verse is referring to the disbelievers who, upon realizing the punishment of Allah is coming upon them, try to flee from it. However, it is too late for them to escape as they had persistently denied the truth and warnings from Allah and His messengers. It shows that when the punishment of Allah befalls the wrongdoers, there is no escape from it. The verse emphasizes the severity and inevitability of Allah's punishment for those who reject His messages and persist in disbelief and wrongdoing.
orig: فلما أحسوا بأسنا إذا هم منها يركضون

translation: Do not run away and return to where you were indulged in luxury and to your homes, so that you may be questioned.
interpretation: This verse is a warning to those who have been blessed with wealth and luxury in this world. It reminds them that they should not flee from their responsibilities and the questioning that will come on the Day of Judgment. They will be held accountable for how they used their blessings and whether they were grateful to Allah and used their wealth in His cause. The verse emphasizes that the luxuries and comforts of this world are temporary, and that ultimately, everyone will have to face the consequences of their actions before Allah. It is a call to reflect on one's life and to use one's blessings in a way that pleases Allah, rather than being distracted by the fleeting pleasures of this world.
orig: لا تركضوا وارجعوا إلى ما أترفتم فيه ومساكنكم لعلكم تسألون

translation: They will say, "O woe to us! Indeed, we were wrongdoers."
interpretation: This verse is referring to the Day of Judgment when the wrongdoers and disbelievers will realize their grave error in denying the truth and rejecting faith in Allah. They will express their deep regret and remorse, acknowledging that they were indeed unjust to themselves by choosing the path of disobedience and transgression. The phrase "O woe to us" (يا ويلنا) expresses their anguish, despair, and self-blame upon recognizing the consequences of their actions. It highlights the severity of their realization that they had wasted their lives in pursuit of falsehood and now face the dire repercussions of their choices. This verse serves as a powerful reminder for individuals to reflect upon their deeds and to strive for righteousness before it is too late, as on that Day, regret and remorse will be of no avail.
orig: قالوا يا ويلنا إنا كنا ظالمين

translation: And that cry of theirs ceased not, till We made them as a field that is mown, as ashes silent and quenched.
interpretation: This verse is referring to the fate of those who persistently rejected the truth and opposed the messengers of Allah. Despite being warned repeatedly, they continued in their disbelief and wrongdoing until Allah's punishment descended upon them, causing their complete destruction. Their cries and pleas ceased as they were made like a field that has been harvested, lifeless and still. It symbolizes the silencing of their arrogance and the futility of their resistance against Allah's will. The verse serves as a reminder that those who choose the path of denial and transgression will ultimately face the severe consequences of their choices, becoming a mere remnant of what they once were.
orig: فما زالت تلك دعواهم حتى جعلناهم حصيدا خامدين

translation: And We did not create the heaven and the earth and that between them in play.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah did not create the universe and everything within it without a profound purpose or meaning. The creation of the heavens and the earth, and all that exists between them, is not a mere act of play or amusement for Allah. Instead, it reflects His infinite wisdom, power, and divine plan. The verse implies that every aspect of creation has a significant purpose and is designed to serve a higher goal, even if human beings may not always comprehend the full extent of that purpose. It encourages believers to contemplate the signs of Allah's creation and to recognize the seriousness and intentionality behind the existence of the universe.
orig: وما خلقنا السماء والأرض وما بينهما لاعبين

translation: If We had intended to take a diversion, We would have taken it from [what is] with Us - if We were to do so.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that if Allah had desired to have a form of amusement or diversion, He would have chosen it from what is with Him, i.e., from His own creation, rather than from the false objects of worship that the polytheists have taken besides Him. It affirms that Allah is far above such human attributes and desires, and that He does not engage in vain or trivial activities. The verse also implies that the very notion of Allah "taking a diversion" is hypothetical and contrary to His divine nature, as indicated by the phrase "if We were to do so."
orig: لو أردنا أن نتخذ لهوا لاتخذناه من لدنا إن كنا فاعلين

translation: Nay, We hurl the truth against falsehood, and it destroys it, and behold, it vanishes. And woe to you for what you describe.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the ultimate triumph of truth over falsehood. It suggests that when the truth is presented with clarity and force, it has the power to shatter and obliterate falsehood completely. The verse also serves as a warning to those who persist in describing false beliefs or attributing false qualities to Allah, indicating that they will face severe consequences and divine retribution for their actions. It highlights the importance of upholding the truth and rejecting falsehood in all aspects of life.
orig: بل نقذف بالحق على الباطل فيدمغه فإذا هو زاهق ولكم الويل مما تصفون

translation: To Him belongs whoever is in the heavens and the earth. And those near Him are not prevented by arrogance from His worship, nor do they tire.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute sovereignty and lordship of Allah over all creation. Every being in the heavens and earth belongs to Him alone. Even the angels and those closest to Allah do not disdain worshipping Him out of pride or arrogance. They worship Him tirelessly and continuously, never feeling exhausted or weary in carrying out their devotion and servitude to their Lord. It underscores the importance of humility, submission and steadfastness in worship for all of Allah's creatures.
orig: وله من في السماوات والأرض ومن عنده لا يستكبرون عن عبادته ولا يستحسرون

translation: They glorify [Him] by night and by day; they do not slacken.
interpretation: This verse refers to the angels who are in constant worship and glorification of Allah, without ever tiring or slacking in their devotion. It emphasizes the unwavering dedication and obedience of the angels to Allah. The verse also serves as a reminder for believers to strive for consistency in their own worship and remembrance of Allah, taking inspiration from the tireless devotion of the angels.
orig: يسبحون الليل والنهار لا يفترون

translation: Or have they taken gods from the earth who resurrect [the dead]?
interpretation: This verse questions the belief in false deities or idols that are worshipped by some people. It challenges the notion that these man-made gods have any power or ability to resurrect the dead. The Qur'an emphasizes that only Allah has the power to give life and cause death, and that worshipping anyone or anything besides Him is futile and misguided. The verse implies that believing in false gods is irrational, as they are incapable of creating, sustaining, or resurrecting life, which are attributes that belong solely to Allah, the One True God.
orig: أم اتخذوا آلهة من الأرض هم ينشرون

translation: If there were, in the heavens and the earth, other gods besides Allah, there would have been confusion in both! but glory to Allah, the Lord of the Throne: (High is He) above what they attribute to Him!
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the concept of Tawhid (monotheism) in Islam. It argues that if there were multiple gods, as polytheists believe, then there would be chaos and confusion in the heavens and the earth due to the competing wills and authorities of these gods. However, the fact that the universe operates in a harmonious and orderly manner is evidence that there is only one God, Allah, who is in full control. The verse glorifies Allah as the Lord of the Throne, which symbolizes His supreme authority and sovereignty, and declares Him to be far above the false attributes and partners that polytheists ascribe to Him.
orig: لو كان فيهما آلهة إلا الله لفسدتا فسبحان الله رب العرش عما يصفون

translation: He is not questioned about what He does, but they will be questioned.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute sovereignty and power of Allah. He is not accountable to anyone for His actions and decisions, as He has supreme authority over all things. On the other hand, human beings will be held responsible and questioned about their deeds on the Day of Judgment. This highlights the contrast between the limitless power of the Creator and the accountability of His creation. It serves as a reminder for humans to be mindful of their actions, as they will have to answer for them in the Hereafter.
orig: لا يسأل عما يفعل وهم يسألون

translation: Or have they taken gods besides Him? Say, [O Muhammad], "Produce your proof. This [Qur'an] is the message for those with me and the message of those before me." But most of them do not know the truth, so they are turning away.
interpretation: This verse challenges the polytheists who have taken other deities besides Allah. It demands that they bring forth evidence and proof to support their claim of the existence of these false gods. The Qur'an is mentioned as a reminder and a message, not only for the people of Prophet Muhammad's time but also for those who came before them, indicating the continuity of the divine message. However, the verse points out that most people do not recognize or acknowledge the truth, and as a result, they turn away from the guidance provided by Allah. This highlights the human tendency to ignore or reject the truth, often due to ignorance, stubbornness, or attachment to misguided beliefs.
orig: أم اتخذوا من دونه آلهة قل هاتوا برهانكم هذا ذكر من معي وذكر من قبلي بل أكثرهم لا يعلمون الحق فهم معرضون

translation: And We sent not before you any messenger except that We revealed to him that, "There is no deity except Me, so worship Me."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the fundamental message that has been conveyed by all the prophets and messengers sent by Allah throughout history. The core of this message is the belief in the oneness of Allah (tawheed) and the commandment to worship Him alone. It highlights that the call to monotheism and the rejection of all forms of polytheism and idolatry has been the common thread binding all divine revelations. The verse also serves as a reminder to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) that his message is not new, but rather a continuation of the same message that was delivered by all the prophets before him, reinforcing the unity and consistency of the divine message across time and nations.
orig: وما أرسلنا من قبلك من رسول إلا نوحي إليه أنه لا إله إلا أنا فاعبدون

translation: And they say, "The Most Merciful has taken [for Himself] a son." Exalted is He! Rather, they are [but] honored servants.
interpretation: This verse refutes the false claim made by some people that Allah has taken a son. It emphasizes the absolute perfection and transcendence of Allah, declaring that He is far above having any offspring. Instead, those whom people may mistakenly consider as Allah's children, such as angels or prophets, are in reality His honored servants. They are created beings who submit to Allah's will and carry out His commands with utmost obedience and devotion. This verse affirms the fundamental Islamic belief in the oneness of Allah and rejects any form of association or partnership with Him.
orig: وقالوا اتخذ الرحمن ولدا سبحانه بل عباد مكرمون

translation: They do not precede Him in speech, and they act by His command.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute obedience and submission of the angels to Allah. The angels do not speak or act before Allah commands them to do so. They are His faithful servants who carry out His orders without question or hesitation. This verse highlights the supreme authority of Allah over all of His creation, including the angels, and underscores the importance of complete obedience and devotion to Him.
orig: لا يسبقونه بالقول وهم بأمره يعملون

translation: He knows what is [presently] before them and what will be after them, and they cannot intercede except on behalf of one whom He approves. And they, from fear of Him, are apprehensive.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute knowledge and power of Allah. He is aware of everything, past, present, and future, and no one can intercede on behalf of another without His permission. Even those closest to Him, such as the angels, fear Him and are in awe of His majesty. It reminds us that we should always be mindful of Allah and strive to earn His pleasure, as only those whom He approves will be granted intercession on the Day of Judgment.
orig: يعلم ما بين أيديهم وما خلفهم ولا يشفعون إلا لمن ارتضى وهم من خشيته مشفقون

translation: And whoever of them says, "Indeed, I am a god besides Him" - that one We will recompense with Hell. Thus do We recompense the wrongdoers.
interpretation: This verse is a stern warning to those who claim divinity or associate partners with Allah. It emphasizes the grave sin of shirk (polytheism) and the severe punishment that awaits those who commit it. The interpretation is that anyone who arrogantly claims to be a god besides Allah or deserves to be worshipped will be condemned to Hell as a just recompense for their wrongdoing and transgression against the Oneness of Allah. This highlights the severity of associating partners with Allah and serves as a reminder to humanity to worship Allah alone and avoid falling into the sin of shirk.
orig: ومن يقل منهم إني إله من دونه فذلك نجزيه جهنم كذلك نجزي الظالمين

translation: Have those who disbelieved not considered that the heavens and the earth were a joined entity, and We separated them and made from water every living thing? Then will they not believe?
interpretation: This verse is a reminder to those who reject faith in Allah to reflect upon the signs of His creation and power. It points to the fact that the universe began as a single entity before Allah separated the heavens and the earth, and that water is the source of all life. The verse is asking the disbelievers to ponder over these signs and recognize the existence and oneness of the Creator. It is an invitation for them to believe in Allah and submit to His will, as the signs of His creation and power are clear and undeniable for those who reflect deeply.
orig: أولم ير الذين كفروا أن السماوات والأرض كانتا رتقا ففتقناهما وجعلنا من الماء كل شيء حي أفلا يؤمنون

translation: And We have placed on the earth firmly set mountains, lest it should shift with them, and We made therein [mountain] passes [as] roads that they might be guided.
interpretation: This verse highlights the wisdom and power of Allah in creating the earth and its features. The mountains are described as "firmly set" and serve the purpose of stabilizing the earth, preventing it from shaking or shifting. This stability is essential for the inhabitants of the earth to live and thrive. Additionally, Allah has created mountain passes and roads, which serve as pathways for people to travel and navigate through the landscape. These natural features are seen as a guidance and a means for people to find their way, both physically and spiritually. The verse emphasizes the purposeful design behind the creation of the earth and its features, all of which are signs of Allah's power, wisdom, and mercy towards His creation.
orig: وجعلنا في الأرض رواسي أن تميد بهم وجعلنا فيها فجاجا سبلا لعلهم يهتدون

translation: And We have made the sky a protected ceiling, but they, from its signs, are turning away.
interpretation: This verse points to the divine creation and protection of the sky, which serves as a secure canopy over the earth. Despite the clear signs and evidence of Allah's power and wisdom in the creation of the heavens, many people choose to ignore or turn away from these indications. They fail to reflect upon and appreciate the marvels of the universe, remaining heedless of the messages and lessons that can be derived from observing the sky and contemplating its purpose. This attitude of disregard and indifference towards the signs of Allah in the heavens is a form of ingratitude and a failure to acknowledge His boundless creativity and benevolence.
orig: وجعلنا السماء سقفا محفوظا وهم عن آياتها معرضون

translation: And it is He who created the night and the day and the sun and the moon; all [heavenly bodies] in an orbit are swimming.
interpretation: This verse highlights Allah's power and control over the universe. He created the alternation of night and day, and the sun and moon, which follow precise orbits according to His decree. The phrase "all in an orbit are swimming" suggests that these celestial bodies are continuously moving in their designated paths, like swimmers in a vast cosmic ocean. This conveys the sense of harmony, balance, and order in Allah's creation. The verse invites us to reflect on these signs and marvel at the Creator's wisdom and might. It also implies that just as the heavenly bodies submit to Allah's laws, we too should strive to align our lives with His guidance and purpose.
orig: وهو الذي خلق الليل والنهار والشمس والقمر كل في فلك يسبحون

translation: And We did not grant to any man before you eternity [on earth]; so if you die - would they be eternal?
interpretation: This verse reminds us of the fleeting nature of this worldly life and that no one, not even the prophets, can escape death. It is a powerful reminder of our own mortality and the importance of focusing on the eternal life of the Hereafter rather than becoming attached to the temporary pleasures of this world. The verse also highlights the unique status of Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) as the final messenger, while emphasizing that even he, like all humans, will taste death. Ultimately, it is a call to reflect on the purpose of our existence and to strive for righteousness in preparation for the Day of Judgment.
orig: وما جعلنا لبشر من قبلك الخلد أفإن مت فهم الخالدون

translation: Every soul will taste death. And We test you with evil and with good as trial; and to Us you will be returned.
interpretation: This verse reminds us of the inevitability of death and that our time on earth is a test. God tests us with both good and bad experiences to see how we respond and to help us grow spiritually. Ultimately, we will all return to God after death for judgment. This should motivate us to make the most of our limited time, remain patient through difficulties, stay humble and grateful during blessings, and keep our focus on pleasing God and attaining a good eternal outcome, rather than getting absorbed in temporary worldly matters.
orig: كل نفس ذائقة الموت ونبلوكم بالشر والخير فتنة وإلينا ترجعون

translation: And when those who disbelieve see you, they take you not except in ridicule, [saying], "Is this the one who mentions your gods [in criticism]?" And they are, at the mention of the Most Merciful, disbelievers.
interpretation: This verse highlights the attitude of the disbelievers towards the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and the message he conveyed. They mocked and ridiculed him, questioning his credibility and the validity of his criticism of their false deities. Moreover, it emphasizes their disbelief and rejection of the concept of Allah's mercy and compassion, denying the very existence of the Most Merciful. This interpretation suggests that the disbelievers' arrogance and attachment to their false beliefs blinded them from recognizing the truth and accepting the guidance brought by the Prophet, leading them to resort to mockery and derision instead of engaging in meaningful discourse.
orig: وإذا رآك الذين كفروا إن يتخذونك إلا هزوا أهذا الذي يذكر آلهتكم وهم بذكر الرحمن هم كافرون

translation: Man was created of haste. I will show you My signs, so do not impatiently urge Me.
interpretation: This verse points to the hasty and impatient nature of human beings. They often desire immediate results and are unwilling to wait for God's plan to unfold. However, God reminds us that He will reveal His signs and wonders in due time, according to His wisdom. We should not try to rush or pressure Him, but rather trust in His timing and have faith that He will guide us and show us the right path. Patience and trust in God's plan are essential qualities for believers to cultivate.
orig: خلق الإنسان من عجل سأريكم آياتي فلا تستعجلون

translation: And they say, "When is this promise, if you should be truthful?"
interpretation: This verse is a challenge from the disbelievers to the Prophet Muhammad and the believers, questioning the truth of the Day of Judgment and the fulfillment of God's promise. They are essentially saying, "If you are truthful in your claim about the Day of Judgment, then tell us when it will happen." This question is asked in a mocking and disbelieving tone, as they do not believe in the reality of the Hereafter. The verse highlights the skepticism and denial of the disbelievers regarding the divine message and their demand for proof or a specific time for the promised event to occur. It serves as a reminder for the believers to remain steadfast in their faith despite the challenges and doubts posed by others.
orig: ويقولون متى هذا الوعد إن كنتم صادقين

translation: If only those who disbelieved knew [that] when they will not be able to ward off the Fire from their faces or from their backs, nor will they be helped...
interpretation: This verse is a warning to the disbelievers that on the Day of Judgment, they will face the torment of the Fire and will not be able to protect themselves from it or find any help. It emphasizes the severity and inevitability of the punishment for those who reject faith in Allah. The mention of faces and backs suggests that the Fire will engulf them from all sides, leaving no escape. It also implies that their worldly power, wealth or status will be of no avail on that Day, as no one will be able to help them against Allah's judgment. The verse serves as a reminder for people to reflect on the consequences of disbelief and to embrace faith before it is too late.
orig: لو يعلم الذين كفروا حين لا يكفون عن وجوههم النار ولا عن ظهورهم ولا هم ينصرون

translation: Nay, it (the Hour) will come upon them suddenly and bewilder them, and they will not be able to avert it, nor will they be reprieved.
interpretation: This verse speaks about the sudden arrival of the Day of Judgment, which will catch people off guard and leave them in a state of shock and confusion. They will be unable to prevent its coming or delay it, and they will not be given any respite or additional time to make amends for their past deeds. This interpretation highlights the importance of being prepared for the Day of Judgment at all times, as it can come unexpectedly without any prior warning. It also emphasizes the finality of that day, as there will be no opportunity for people to change their fate once it arrives.
orig: بل تأتيهم بغتة فتبهتهم فلا يستطيعون ردها ولا هم ينظرون

translation: And already were messengers ridiculed before you, but those who mocked them were enveloped by what they used to ridicule.
interpretation: This verse serves as a reminder and consolation to Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) that he is not the first prophet to face ridicule and mockery from his people. Many prophets before him were also mocked and belittled by their communities. However, the verse also carries a warning to those who engage in such mockery, stating that the very thing they ridiculed will come back to encompass them. It implies that the truth they denied and made fun of will ultimately be their undoing, and they will face the consequences of their actions. This interpretation highlights the importance of respecting the message and the messengers sent by Allah, as those who arrogantly reject and mock them will eventually face the reality they denied.
orig: ولقد استهزئ برسل من قبلك فحاق بالذين سخروا منهم ما كانوا به يستهزئون

translation: Say, "Who can protect you at night or by day from the Most Merciful?" But they are, from the remembrance of their Lord, turning away.
interpretation: This verse is a reminder that Allah is the only one who can protect us at all times, whether it be during the night or day. It emphasizes the importance of remembering Allah and not turning away from His remembrance. The verse implies that those who turn away from the remembrance of their Lord are depriving themselves of His protection and mercy. It is a call to humanity to turn towards Allah and seek His protection and guidance at all times.
orig: قل من يكلؤكم بالليل والنهار من الرحمن بل هم عن ذكر ربهم معرضون

translation: Or have they gods that defend them from Us? They are not able to help themselves, nor can they be protected from Us.
interpretation: This verse questions the belief in false gods and idols, emphasizing their inability to provide protection or assistance to their worshippers. It highlights the fact that these false deities are powerless and cannot even defend themselves, let alone offer any support to those who seek their help. The verse implies that only Allah, the One True God, possesses the power to protect and aid His creation, and that relying on anyone or anything else is futile. It serves as a reminder to humanity to put their trust in Allah alone and not to be misled by the false promises of man-made idols or deities.
orig: أم لهم آلهة تمنعهم من دوننا لا يستطيعون نصر أنفسهم ولا هم منا يصحبون

translation: Rather, We have provided enjoyment for these [disbelievers] and their fathers until life was prolonged for them. Then do they not see that We set upon the land, reducing it from its borders? So is it they who will overcome?
interpretation: This verse points to the fact that the disbelievers have been given the comforts and luxuries of this worldly life, which has made them heedless of the Hereafter. They and their forefathers have been enjoying these worldly pleasures for so long that they think it will last forever. However, they fail to realize that Allah is gradually reducing the land from its edges, which could be a metaphor for the diminishing of their power and dominion, or a literal reference to the earth's eventual destruction. The question at the end challenges their assumption of invincibility and suggests that it is Allah who is in control and will ultimately prevail, not them.
orig: بل متعنا هؤلاء وآباءهم حتى طال عليهم العمر أفلا يرون أنا نأتي الأرض ننقصها من أطرافها أفهم الغالبون

translation: Say, "I only warn you by revelation." But the deaf do not hear the call when they are warned.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes that the Prophet Muhammad's role is to convey the divine revelation and warn people about the consequences of their actions. However, those who are spiritually "deaf" and unwilling to listen to the truth will not heed the warning, even when they are admonished. This verse highlights the importance of being receptive to the message of Islam and the need for individuals to take responsibility for their own spiritual growth and actions, as the Prophet can only deliver the message, but it is up to each person to accept and act upon it.
orig: قل إنما أنذركم بالوحي ولا يسمع الصم الدعاء إذا ما ينذرون

translation: And if even a whiff of your Lord's punishment touched them, they would surely cry, "Woe to us! We have truly been wrongdoers!"
interpretation: This verse is a warning to those who persist in wrongdoing and disbelief. It emphasizes that even a small taste of Allah's punishment would make the wrongdoers realize the error of their ways and the gravity of their sins. They would then lament their fate and acknowledge that they had indeed been unjust to themselves by rejecting faith and committing evil deeds. The verse underscores the severity of divine retribution and the inevitability of facing the consequences of one's actions in the Hereafter. It serves as a reminder for people to mend their ways, seek forgiveness, and embrace righteousness before it is too late.
orig: ولئن مستهم نفحة من عذاب ربك ليقولن يا ويلنا إنا كنا ظالمين

translation: And We place the scales of justice for the Day of Resurrection, so no soul will be treated unjustly at all. And if there is [even] the weight of a mustard seed, We will bring it forth. And sufficient are We as accountant.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute justice of God on the Day of Judgment. It assures that every deed, no matter how small or seemingly insignificant, will be accounted for. The mention of the "mustard seed" illustrates that even the tiniest of actions will not be overlooked. The verse also affirms that God is sufficient as the ultimate reckoner, implying His perfect knowledge and fairness in judging all matters. It serves as a reminder for individuals to be conscious of their actions, as nothing escapes divine accountability.
orig: ونضع الموازين القسط ليوم القيامة فلا تظلم نفس شيئا وإن كان مثقال حبة من خردل أتينا بها وكفى بنا حاسبين

translation: And We had certainly given Moses and Aaron the criterion and a light and a reminder for the righteous.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of divine guidance and revelation. The "criterion" refers to the Torah, which was given to Moses and Aaron as a means of distinguishing between right and wrong. The "light" symbolizes the guidance and clarity that the Torah provides, illuminating the path to righteousness. The "reminder" serves as a constant admonition for those who are mindful of God, encouraging them to stay on the right path. This verse highlights the significance of prophetic teachings and their role in guiding believers towards a life of piety and righteousness.
orig: ولقد آتينا موسى وهارون الفرقان وضياء وذكرا للمتقين

translation: Those who fear their Lord in the unseen, and they are apprehensive of the Hour.
interpretation: This verse speaks about the true believers who have a deep reverence and fear of Allah, even when they are not in public view. They are constantly mindful of the Day of Judgment ("the Hour") and are anxious about their standing before Allah on that day. This fear and apprehension motivates them to lead righteous lives, follow Allah's commands, and refrain from sins. They are aware that Allah is always watching them, and this consciousness keeps them on the straight path. The verse emphasizes the importance of having a strong faith and being mindful of one's actions, even in private, as Allah is All-Seeing and All-Knowing.
orig: الذين يخشون ربهم بالغيب وهم من الساعة مشفقون

translation: And this is a blessed message which We have sent down. Will you then reject it?
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the divine nature of the Qur'an, describing it as a blessed message sent down by Allah. The rhetorical question "Will you then reject it?" serves as a reminder to the believers to accept and follow the guidance contained within the Qur'an, as rejecting it would be an act of disbelief and ingratitude towards Allah's mercy and guidance. The verse encourages believers to embrace the Qur'an wholeheartedly and to live their lives according to its teachings.
orig: وهذا ذكر مبارك أنزلناه أفأنتم له منكرون

translation: And We had certainly given Abraham his sound judgement before, and We were of him well-Knowing.
interpretation: This verse highlights the special status of Prophet Abraham (peace be upon him). It indicates that Allah had granted Abraham wisdom, understanding and sound judgement from an early age. The verse also affirms Allah's complete knowledge of Abraham's inner state, his sincerity, and his potential as a great Prophet and leader. It suggests that Allah chose Abraham and guided him based on His prior knowledge of Abraham's righteousness and suitability for the momentous tasks and trials that lay ahead of him in conveying the message of monotheism.
orig: ولقد آتينا إبراهيم رشده من قبل وكنا به عالمين

translation: When he said to his father and his people, "What are these statues to which you are devoted?"
interpretation: This verse is a rhetorical question that Abraham (Ibrahim) posed to his father and his people, challenging their practice of idol worship. He was essentially asking them to reflect on the meaninglessness and futility of worshipping man-made statues that have no power or ability to benefit or harm. Abraham's question aimed to make them contemplate the irrationality of their belief system and to guide them towards the worship of the One True God (Allah). It highlights the role of prophets in calling people away from polytheism and towards monotheism.
orig: إذ قال لأبيه وقومه ما هذه التماثيل التي أنتم لها عاكفون

translation: They said, "We found our fathers worshipping them."
interpretation: This verse is highlighting the tendency of people to blindly follow the religious practices and beliefs of their ancestors without questioning their validity or reasoning. It suggests that many people adopt a certain faith or engage in certain rituals simply because it is what their forefathers did, rather than out of personal conviction or understanding. The Qur'an is critical of this attitude and encourages people to use their intellect to reflect on their beliefs and practices, and to follow the truth based on reason and divine guidance, not just inherited tradition.
orig: قالوا وجدنا آباءنا لها عابدين
