translation: He said, "Verily, you and your fathers have been in manifest error."
interpretation: This verse is a rebuke to those who persist in following the misguided beliefs and practices of their forefathers, despite the clear guidance that has come to them through the prophets and messengers. It emphasizes that blindly adhering to ancestral traditions is not an excuse for rejecting the truth. The verse implies that one must use reason and discernment to recognize and follow the straight path, even if it means breaking away from the erroneous ways of one's predecessors. It is a call to take personal responsibility for one's faith and actions, rather than simply inheriting and perpetuating the mistakes of the past.
orig: قال لقد كنتم أنتم وآباؤكم في ضلال مبين

translation: They said, "Have you come to us with the truth, or are you of those who jest?"
interpretation: This verse is questioning the seriousness and sincerity of the message being conveyed. The people are asking whether the message is truly from God or if it is merely a jest or a form of amusement. It reflects the skepticism and doubt that people may have when confronted with a divine message, wondering if it is genuine or just a form of play or entertainment from the one delivering it. The verse highlights the importance of delivering the truth with conviction and seriousness, so that it may be received with the gravity it deserves.
orig: قالوا أجئتنا بالحق أم أنت من اللاعبين

translation: Rather, your Lord is the Lord of the heavens and the earth who created them, and I am, to that, of the witnesses.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that it is Allah alone who is the true Lord and Creator of the heavens and the earth. The speaker, likely a prophet or messenger, affirms that they bear witness to this fundamental truth. It highlights the importance of recognizing Allah's sovereignty and power over all of creation, as opposed to worshipping false deities or attributing lordship to anyone or anything else. The verse serves as a reminder for humanity to direct their worship, obedience, and reverence to the One who brought the universe into existence.
orig: قال بل ربكم رب السماوات والأرض الذي فطرهن وأنا على ذلكم من الشاهدين

translation: And [I swear] by Allah, I will surely plan against your idols after you have turned and gone away.
interpretation: This verse shows the resolve of Prophet Ibrahim (Abraham) to destroy the idols that his people worshipped, as he recognized them to be false gods. It demonstrates his strong faith in the one true God and his willingness to stand up against the prevalent polytheistic beliefs of his time, even if it meant going against his own family and community. Ibrahim's intention to carry out this plan while the people were away also indicates his desire to make a clear statement against idolatry without causing direct confrontation or harm to anyone.
orig: وتالله لأكيدن أصنامكم بعد أن تولوا مدبرين

translation: So he broke them into pieces, except a large one among them, that they might return to it [and question].
interpretation: This verse is referring to the story of Prophet Ibrahim (Abraham) when he destroyed the idols that his people worshipped, leaving only the biggest one intact. He did this to make them realize the futility of idol worship and to encourage them to turn towards the worship of the one true God. The act of destroying the idols was a symbolic gesture to demonstrate the powerlessness of these false deities and to challenge the people to reflect on their beliefs. By leaving the biggest idol unharmed, Prophet Ibrahim was setting the stage for a confrontation where he could expose the irrationality of their idolatrous practices and call them towards monotheism.
orig: فجعلهم جذاذا إلا كبيرا لهم لعلهم إليه يرجعون

translation: They said, "Who has done this to our gods? Indeed, he is of the wrongdoers."
interpretation: This verse is referring to the story of Prophet Abraham (peace be upon him) when he destroyed the idols that his people worshipped. The people, upon seeing their destroyed idols, were enraged and accused the person responsible of being a wrongdoer and a transgressor. They failed to realize that their idolatry was the real wrongdoing and that Abraham was trying to guide them to the truth of worshipping the One True God. This highlights the human tendency to cling to false beliefs and to oppose those who try to rectify them, even accusing them of wrongdoing. It also shows the courage of the prophets in standing up for the truth despite the opposition and accusations they faced from their people.
orig: قالوا من فعل هذا بآلهتنا إنه لمن الظالمين

translation: They said, "We heard a young man mentioning them, who is called Abraham."
interpretation: This verse refers to the people who opposed Prophet Abraham and his message of monotheism. They heard about Abraham's preaching against their idolatry and polytheistic beliefs. The verse highlights that even at a young age, Abraham had the courage and wisdom to challenge the prevailing religious norms of his society and call people towards the worship of the One True God. It also implies that Abraham's message was beginning to gain attention and spread among the people, causing concern among the opponents of his message.
orig: قالوا سمعنا فتى يذكرهم يقال له إبراهيم

translation: They said, "Then bring him before the eyes of the people that they may testify."
interpretation: This verse is referring to a challenge posed by the disbelievers to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him). They demanded that he bring forth a miracle or sign to prove his prophethood in front of the people, so that they could witness it and testify to its authenticity. The disbelievers were essentially setting a condition for believing in the Prophet's message - that he must perform a public miracle. This highlights their stubbornness and refusal to accept the truth, as they were not content with the clear proofs and signs already provided to them. It also shows their insincerity, as even if a miracle were shown, they likely would have found some other excuse to reject faith.
orig: قالوا فأتوا به على أعين الناس لعلهم يشهدون

translation: They said, "Are you the one who did this to our gods, O Abraham?"
interpretation: This verse is questioning Abraham's actions against the idols that his people worshipped. The tone suggests that they are angry and accusing him of destroying or defacing their gods. It reflects the conflict between Abraham's monotheistic beliefs and the polytheistic practices of his community. The verse sets the stage for Abraham's response and his attempt to guide them towards the worship of the One True God.
orig: قالوا أأنت فعلت هذا بآلهتنا يا إبراهيم

translation: He said, "Rather, this - the largest of them - did it, so ask them, if they should [be able to] speak."
interpretation: This verse is from the story of Prophet Ibrahim (Abraham) when he destroyed the idols of his people. When confronted about the destruction, Ibrahim cleverly pointed to the largest idol, suggesting that it was responsible for the act. He challenged his people to ask the idols themselves about what happened, knowing full well that they could not speak. This was a powerful demonstration of the futility of worshipping false gods and a testament to Ibrahim's unwavering faith in the one true God. The verse highlights the absurdity of idolatry and the importance of using reason and logic to arrive at the truth.
orig: قال بل فعله كبيرهم هذا فاسألوهم إن كانوا ينطقون

translation: Then they returned to themselves and said, "Indeed, you yourselves are the wrongdoers."
interpretation: This verse is referring to a moment of realization and self-reflection. The people in question had previously been accusing others of wrongdoing, but upon introspection, they came to the understanding that they themselves were the ones guilty of wrongdoing and injustice. This highlights the importance of looking inward and holding oneself accountable before pointing fingers at others. It is a reminder to be humble, self-aware, and willing to admit one's own faults and shortcomings, rather than projecting blame onto others. This moment of self-realization is a crucial step towards repentance, self-improvement, and ultimately, seeking forgiveness from Allah.
orig: فرجعوا إلى أنفسهم فقالوا إنكم أنتم الظالمون

translation: Then they reversed themselves, [saying], "You have already known that these do not speak!"
interpretation: This verse is referring to the story of Prophet Abraham when he confronted his people about their idol worship. After breaking the idols except for the largest one, his people questioned him. Abraham then pointed to the largest idol, suggesting that it had done the destruction. At this point, the people reversed their stance, admitting that they knew the idols could not speak, as mentioned in this verse. This highlights the irrationality of idol worship and the way people can delude themselves into believing in false gods, even when faced with clear evidence against it. The verse emphasizes the importance of using reason and logic in matters of faith and worship.
orig: ثم نكسوا على رءوسهم لقد علمت ما هؤلاء ينطقون

translation: He said, "So do you worship besides Allah that which does not benefit you at all nor harm you?"
interpretation: This verse is a rebuke to those who worship false deities and idols instead of Allah. It points out the futility and irrationality of worshipping entities that have no power to benefit or harm, and that are ultimately powerless. The rhetorical question serves to make the addressees reflect on the error of their ways and the baselessness of their beliefs. It is an invitation to abandon false worship and to turn to the One True God who alone deserves worship and devotion.
orig: قال أفتعبدون من دون الله ما لا ينفعكم شيئا ولا يضركم

translation: Fie upon you and upon that which you worship besides Allah! Do you not then understand?
interpretation: This verse is a strong rebuke to those who worship anything other than Allah. It expresses disgust and disapproval towards such people and the false objects of worship they venerate. The rhetorical question at the end challenges them to use their intellect and reason to recognize the falsehood of their idolatry and polytheism. It implies that if they truly understood, they would realize that worshipping anything besides the One True God is irrational and wrong.
orig: أف لكم ولما تعبدون من دون الله أفلا تعقلون

translation: They said, "Burn him and support your gods, if you are to act."
interpretation: This verse refers to the story of Prophet Abraham (peace be upon him) when he was confronted by his people for rejecting their idols and calling them to worship the One True God. In response to his message, they decided to punish him by burning him alive. This highlights the depth of their ignorance, stubbornness, and attachment to their false deities. Instead of reflecting upon Abraham's logical arguments against idol worship, they resorted to violence and cruelty to suppress the truth. The verse also emphasizes the importance of standing firm in one's faith, even in the face of severe opposition and threats, as exemplified by Prophet Abraham's unwavering commitment to monotheism.
orig: قالوا حرقوه وانصروا آلهتكم إن كنتم فاعلين

translation: We said, "O fire, be coolness and safety upon Abraham."
interpretation: This verse demonstrates God's power and mercy towards His prophets and righteous servants. When Abraham was thrown into the fire by the disbelievers, God commanded the fire to become cool and safe for him, miraculously protecting Abraham from harm. This event serves as a reminder that God is always in control and can protect His faithful servants even in the most dire circumstances. It also highlights the unwavering faith and trust that Abraham had in God, as he remained steadfast in his belief despite the threat of being burned alive. The verse encourages believers to have a similar level of trust in God's plan and protection.
orig: قلنا يا نار كوني بردا وسلاما على إبراهيم

translation: And they intended a plot [against him], but We made them the greatest losers.
interpretation: This verse highlights the futility of plotting against the prophets and the believers. Those who scheme against God's chosen ones will ultimately fail and suffer the consequences of their actions. It serves as a reminder that no matter how cleverly the enemies of faith may plan, Allah's will shall prevail, and those who oppose His message will be the ones to face loss and humiliation in this world and the Hereafter. The verse emphasizes the power and wisdom of Allah in protecting His servants and foiling the plots of the wrongdoers.
orig: وأرادوا به كيدا فجعلناهم الأخسرين

translation: And We delivered him and Lot to the land which We had blessed for the worlds.
interpretation: This verse refers to the Prophet Abraham and his nephew Lot, who were saved by Allah from the disbelieving people and were guided to the blessed land, which is interpreted by many scholars to be the region of Syria and Palestine. This land was blessed by Allah for all of mankind, as it became the birthplace of many prophets and the site of important religious events. The verse emphasizes Allah's favor upon Abraham and Lot, and highlights the significance of this blessed land in the history of divine revelation and human guidance.
orig: ونجيناه ولوطا إلى الأرض التي باركنا فيها للعالمين

translation: And We bestowed upon him Isaac and Jacob in addition, and all [of them] We made righteous.
interpretation: This verse highlights the immense blessings and favors that Allah bestowed upon Prophet Abraham (peace be upon him). Not only did Allah grant him a son, Isaac, despite his old age, but He also blessed him with a grandson, Jacob, as an additional gift. The use of the word "naafilah" (translated as "in addition") emphasizes the extraordinary nature of this blessing, as it was beyond what Abraham had initially been promised. Moreover, Allah made all of them - Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob - righteous individuals who were guided to the straight path and were role models for their communities. This verse serves as a reminder of Allah's limitless generosity and the importance of being grateful for His blessings in our lives.
orig: ووهبنا له إسحاق ويعقوب نافلة وكلا جعلنا صالحين

translation: And We made them leaders guiding by Our command. And We inspired to them the doing of good deeds, establishment of prayer, and giving of zakah; and they were worshippers of Us.
interpretation: This verse highlights the qualities and responsibilities of the righteous leaders chosen by Allah. These leaders guide others according to Allah's command, having been inspired to perform good deeds, establish regular prayer, and give zakah (obligatory charity). The verse emphasizes that these leaders are devoted worshippers of Allah, indicating that their leadership is rooted in their strong faith and submission to the will of Allah. It suggests that true leadership in Islam is not just about worldly power, but about setting a righteous example and guiding others towards the path of Allah through one's actions and devotion.
orig: وجعلناهم أئمة يهدون بأمرنا وأوحينا إليهم فعل الخيرات وإقام الصلاة وإيتاء الزكاة وكانوا لنا عابدين

translation: And to Lot We gave judgement and knowledge, and We saved him from the city that was committing wicked deeds. Indeed, they were a people of evil, defiantly disobedient.
interpretation: This verse highlights the wisdom and knowledge bestowed upon Prophet Lot by Allah, as well as His divine intervention in saving Lot from the wicked city. The interpretation suggests that the people of Lot's city were engaged in immoral and sinful practices, defying Allah's commandments. Their actions were so abhorrent that they were characterized as "people of evil" and "defiantly disobedient." The verse emphasizes the importance of adhering to Allah's guidance and the consequences of straying from the righteous path. It also demonstrates Allah's mercy in protecting and rescuing His chosen servants, such as Lot, from the corruption and punishment that befell the disobedient people.
orig: ولوطا آتيناه حكما وعلما ونجيناه من القرية التي كانت تعمل الخبائث إنهم كانوا قوم سوء فاسقين

translation: And We admitted him into Our mercy. Indeed, he was of the righteous.
interpretation: This verse speaks about the infinite mercy and grace of Allah towards His righteous servants. It indicates that those who lead a life of righteousness and obedience to Allah will be granted His special mercy and favor, both in this world and the Hereafter. Being admitted into Allah's mercy is the ultimate success and triumph one can achieve. The verse emphasizes that righteousness is the key to attaining this great blessing and reward from Allah. It encourages the believers to strive in doing good and staying away from sins to be among those whom Allah chooses to shower His mercy upon.
orig: وأدخلناه في رحمتنا إنه من الصالحين

translation: And [mention] Noah, when he called out before, and We responded to him and saved him and his family from the great distress.
interpretation: This verse is a reminder of Allah's mercy and power. It shows that when a believer calls out to Allah with sincerity, even in times of great distress, Allah will respond and provide relief. Noah faced a tremendous trial, but his faith in Allah remained strong. As a result, Allah saved him and his family from the great flood that destroyed his people. This demonstrates that the believers who remain steadfast will ultimately triumph, even against seemingly insurmountable odds, by the grace and mercy of Allah.
orig: ونوحا إذ نادى من قبل فاستجبنا له فنجيناه وأهله من الكرب العظيم

translation: And We helped him against the people who denied Our signs. Indeed, they were an evil people, so We drowned them all.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the power and support of Allah for His prophets and believers against those who reject His messages and signs. It also highlights the consequences of denying the truth and being an evil people, which ultimately leads to their destruction, as exemplified by the drowning of the disbelievers. The verse serves as a reminder that Allah's justice will prevail, and those who oppose His guidance will face the consequences of their actions in this world and the hereafter.
orig: ونصرناه من القوم الذين كذبوا بآياتنا إنهم كانوا قوم سوء فأغرقناهم أجمعين

translation: And [mention] David and Solomon, when they judged concerning the field - when the sheep of a people overran it [at night], and We were witness to their judgement.
interpretation: This verse highlights the wisdom and justice of the Prophets David and Solomon in their judgment regarding a case where sheep had grazed in a field at night without the owner's permission. It emphasizes that God was witnessing their judgment, indicating the importance of fairness and righteousness in resolving disputes. The verse also serves as a reminder for those in positions of authority to exercise their judgment with wisdom, impartiality, and mindfulness of God's presence.
orig: وداوود وسليمان إذ يحكمان في الحرث إذ نفشت فيه غنم القوم وكنا لحكمهم شاهدين

translation: Then We gave understanding of the case to Solomon, and to each [of them] We gave judgement and knowledge. And We subjected the mountains to exalt [Us], along with David and [also] the birds. And We were doing [that].
interpretation: This verse highlights the wisdom and knowledge bestowed upon both David and Solomon by Allah. It emphasizes that Allah granted Solomon the understanding to judge rightly in a particular case. Moreover, it underscores Allah's power and control over His creation, as He subjected the mountains and birds to praise Him along with David. This signifies that all of creation is in a state of worship and submission to Allah, and that He has the ability to subjugate them as He wills. The verse also affirms that Allah is constantly in action, directing His creation according to His wisdom and knowledge.
orig: ففهمناها سليمان وكلا آتينا حكما وعلما وسخرنا مع داوود الجبال يسبحن والطير وكنا فاعلين

translation: And We taught him the fashioning of coats of armor to protect you from your [enemy in] battle. So will you then be grateful?
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine wisdom and benevolence in teaching Prophet David (peace be upon him) the skill of making armor, which serves as a means of protection for believers during times of war or conflict. It is a reminder of God's favor upon humanity in providing them with knowledge and means to defend themselves against their enemies. The verse concludes with a rhetorical question, urging people to express gratitude for this blessing and to acknowledge the countless bounties that God has bestowed upon them. It emphasizes the importance of recognizing and appreciating the divine gifts and using them in a manner that pleases God.
orig: وعلمناه صنعة لبوس لكم لتحصنكم من بأسكم فهل أنتم شاكرون

translation: And to Solomon [We subjected] the wind, blowing forcefully, proceeding by his command toward the land which We had blessed. And We are ever, of all things, Knowing.
interpretation: This verse highlights the power and authority that Allah bestowed upon Prophet Solomon. The wind was made subservient to him, blowing strongly and swiftly, carrying out his commands and directing it towards the blessed land, which could refer to the region of Sham (Syria, Palestine, Lebanon, and Jordan). This divine gift demonstrates Solomon's unique status and the special favors he enjoyed from Allah. The verse also emphasizes Allah's all-encompassing knowledge, signifying that He is fully aware of everything, including the forces of nature and the actions of His servants.
orig: ولسليمان الريح عاصفة تجري بأمره إلى الأرض التي باركنا فيها وكنا بكل شيء عالمين

translation: And of the devils were those who dived for him and did work other than that. And We were of them a guardian.
interpretation: This verse refers to the subjugation of the jinn to Prophet Solomon. Some of the jinn were made to dive into the sea to retrieve pearls and other precious items for Solomon, while others were made to perform various tasks and skilled labor for him. However, God was watching over them, ensuring they did not overstep their bounds or cause harm, and that they fulfilled only what Solomon commanded them to do in service to him. It demonstrates God's power over all His creation and how He granted Solomon authority over the jinn.
orig: ومن الشياطين من يغوصون له ويعملون عملا دون ذلك وكنا لهم حافظين

translation: And [mention] Job, when he called to his Lord, "Indeed, adversity has touched me, and you are the Most Merciful of the merciful."
interpretation: This verse is a reminder of the story of Prophet Ayyub (Job) and his unwavering faith in Allah despite the immense hardships he faced. It teaches us that even in the darkest of times, we should turn to Allah with sincere supplication, acknowledging our weakness and His infinite mercy. Prophet Ayyub's example demonstrates the importance of patience, perseverance, and complete trust in Allah's plan. It encourages believers to seek comfort and relief through prayer, knowing that Allah is the Most Merciful and will respond to the sincere invocations of His servants.
orig: وأيوب إذ نادى ربه أني مسني الضر وأنت أرحم الراحمين

translation: So We responded to him and removed what afflicted him of adversity. And We gave him [back] his family and the like thereof with them as mercy from Us and a reminder for the worshippers [of Allah].
interpretation: This verse highlights the mercy and grace of Allah towards His devoted servants. When a person turns to Allah with sincere supplication during times of hardship, Allah responds by alleviating their suffering and granting them relief. The verse also indicates that Allah may not only remove the affliction but also bestow additional blessings and rewards upon His servant, as exemplified by restoring the family of the supplicant and even increasing them in number. This serves as a reminder for all worshippers that turning to Allah with sincerity and devotion during both ease and adversity is the key to attaining His mercy and favors.
orig: فاستجبنا له فكشفنا ما به من ضر وآتيناه أهله ومثلهم معهم رحمة من عندنا وذكرى للعابدين

translation: And Ishmael and Idrees and Dhul-Kifl; all were of the patient.
interpretation: This verse highlights the virtue of patience by mentioning three prophets who exemplified this quality: Ishmael, Idrees, and Dhul-Kifl. It emphasizes that patience is a characteristic of the righteous and is essential in facing the trials and challenges of life. The prophets mentioned serve as role models for believers, demonstrating how to remain steadfast in faith and persevere through hardships with unwavering trust in Allah's plan. The verse encourages Muslims to cultivate patience in their own lives, as it is a means of attaining Allah's pleasure and success in both this world and the hereafter.
orig: وإسماعيل وإدريس وذا الكفل كل من الصابرين

translation: And We admitted them into Our mercy. Indeed, they were of the righteous.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that those who are righteous and follow the path of Allah will be granted His mercy and blessings. Being admitted into Allah's mercy is a great honor and a reward for their good deeds and unwavering faith. It signifies that they will be protected, guided, and favored by Allah in this world and the hereafter. The verse also implies that righteousness is a key factor in attaining Allah's mercy and that one should strive to be among the righteous through sincere worship, good moral character, and obedience to Allah's commands.
orig: وأدخلناهم في رحمتنا إنهم من الصالحين

translation: And [mention] the man of the fish, when he went off in anger and thought that We would not decree [anything] upon him. And he called out within the darknesses, "There is no deity except You; exalted are You. Indeed, I have been of the wrongdoers."
interpretation: This verse refers to the Prophet Yunus (Jonah) and his story of being swallowed by a whale. The interpretation is that even in the darkest and most difficult times, one should never lose hope in Allah's mercy and should turn to Him in repentance and supplication. Yunus realized his mistake of leaving his people without Allah's permission and acknowledged his wrongdoing. His sincere supplication from the belly of the whale, admitting his weakness and Allah's greatness, is an example for all believers to humble themselves before Allah and seek His forgiveness, no matter how desperate their situation may seem.
orig: وذا النون إذ ذهب مغاضبا فظن أن لن نقدر عليه فنادى في الظلمات أن لا إله إلا أنت سبحانك إني كنت من الظالمين

translation: So We responded to him and saved him from the distress. And thus do We save the believers.
interpretation: This verse highlights the mercy and grace of Allah towards His believing servants. When they call upon Him sincerely, especially in times of hardship and distress, He responds to their supplications and delivers them from their difficulties. This serves as a reassurance to the believers that Allah is always there for them, ready to help and support them through their trials and tribulations. It also emphasizes the importance of having strong faith and trust in Allah, as it is this unwavering belief that allows the believers to turn to Him in their time of need and experience His saving grace.
orig: فاستجبنا له ونجيناه من الغم وكذلك ننجي المؤمنين

translation: And [mention] Zechariah, when he called to his Lord, "My Lord, do not leave me alone [with no heir], while you are the best of inheritors."
interpretation: This verse is a reminder of the importance of supplication and reliance on Allah. Zechariah, a prophet of Allah, feared that he would die without an heir to carry on his legacy and the propagation of the message. He turned to Allah in sincere supplication, acknowledging His power and wisdom in all affairs. The verse emphasizes that Allah is the best of inheritors, meaning that everything ultimately returns to Him and He is the one who will preserve and protect what is dear to us. It encourages believers to turn to Allah in times of need and to trust in His plan, knowing that He will never abandon His servants who call upon Him with sincerity and faith.
orig: وزكريا إذ نادى ربه رب لا تذرني فردا وأنت خير الوارثين

translation: So We responded to him, and We granted to him John, and amended for him his wife. Indeed, they used to hasten to good deeds and supplicate Us in hope and fear, and they were to Us humbly submissive.
interpretation: This verse highlights the virtues and noble qualities of Prophet Zakariya and his family. They were quick to perform good deeds, showing their eagerness and enthusiasm in obeying Allah. They called upon Allah with a balance of hope and fear - hoping for His mercy and fearing His punishment. This demonstrates their strong faith and sincere devotion. Additionally, they were humble and submissive before Allah, displaying true humility and servitude. As a reward for these great qualities, Allah blessed Prophet Zakariya with a righteous son, Yahya (John), despite his old age and his wife's barrenness, and made his wife fertile. This shows that Allah answers the sincere supplications of His devoted servants and blesses them in ways they may have never expected.
orig: فاستجبنا له ووهبنا له يحيى وأصلحنا له زوجه إنهم كانوا يسارعون في الخيرات ويدعوننا رغبا ورهبا وكانوا لنا خاشعين

translation: And [mention] the one who guarded her chastity, so We blew into her [garment] through Our angel [Gabriel], and We made her and her son a sign for the worlds.
interpretation: This verse refers to Mary, the mother of Jesus. It highlights her purity and chastity, as she protected herself from any form of immorality. As a reward for her righteousness, Allah sent the angel Gabriel to blow into her garment, miraculously conceiving Jesus without a father. The birth of Jesus to the virgin Mary was a remarkable sign of Allah's power and a miracle for all of humanity to witness. This event demonstrates that Allah can create life in any manner He chooses and is not bound by the natural laws of conception. The story of Mary and Jesus serves as an example for all people to have faith in Allah's omnipotence and to trust in His divine plan, even when it may seem impossible or beyond comprehension.
orig: والتي أحصنت فرجها فنفخنا فيها من روحنا وجعلناها وابنها آية للعالمين

translation: Indeed this, your religion, is one religion, and I am your Lord, so worship Me.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the unity and universality of the true religion, which is submission to the One God. It reminds us that all the prophets and messengers came with the same fundamental message: to worship Allah alone and to follow His guidance. The verse also highlights the direct relationship between the Creator and His creation, as He addresses humanity saying, "I am your Lord." This establishes the basis for the worship and obedience that mankind owes to Allah. The unity of religion is a recurring theme in the Qur'an, and this verse succinctly captures the essence of that message, calling upon all people to recognize and submit to the Lordship of Allah.
orig: إن هذه أمتكم أمة واحدة وأنا ربكم فاعبدون

translation: But they have broken their religion among them into sects, each group rejoicing in what is with it [i.e., its beliefs].
interpretation: This verse speaks to the division and fragmentation that has occurred within religion, where people have split into various sects and groups, each holding firmly to their own beliefs and practices. Rather than maintaining unity and cohesion, they have allowed their differences to create separation and discord. The verse suggests that this is not the right way, as ultimately all will return to Allah (God) and be accountable for their actions and choices. It serves as a reminder for the believers to strive for unity based on the core principles of faith, rather than becoming divided over minor differences or innovations.
orig: وتقطعوا أمرهم بينهم كل إلينا راجعون

translation: So whoever does righteous deeds while he is a believer - no denial will there be for his effort, and indeed We, of it, are recorders.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of faith and good deeds in Islam. It assures believers that their righteous actions will not go unnoticed or unrewarded by Allah. The phrase "no denial will there be for his effort" means that Allah will fully acknowledge and appreciate the good deeds of those who believe in Him. Moreover, the verse states that Allah is recording the righteous deeds of the believers, which implies that every good action, no matter how small, is documented and will be rewarded accordingly in the Hereafter. This serves as an encouragement for Muslims to persistently do good and have faith in Allah's recognition and justice.
orig: فمن يعمل من الصالحات وهو مؤمن فلا كفران لسعيه وإنا له كاتبون

translation: And it is forbidden for a town which We have destroyed that they will not return.
interpretation: This verse conveys the idea that once Allah has decreed the destruction of a town or community due to their persistent wrongdoing and rejection of His messages, there is no possibility for them to return to their former state or be given another chance. It emphasizes the finality of Allah's judgment and the consequences of repeatedly ignoring His guidance and warnings. The verse also serves as a reminder to people that they should heed the signs and lessons from the past, and not follow in the footsteps of those who were destroyed for their disobedience and transgression.
orig: وحرام على قرية أهلكناها أنهم لا يرجعون

translation: Until when [the dam of] Gog and Magog has been opened and they, from every elevation, descend
interpretation: This verse refers to one of the signs of the Day of Judgment. Gog and Magog, two tribes that were contained behind a barrier, will be let loose and they will surge forth from every hill and elevation, wreaking havoc on earth. Their release will be a major tribulation and a sign that the end of times is near. It serves as a reminder for humanity to be righteous and prepared for the Day of Reckoning, as these events are inevitable and will come to pass according to God's decree.
orig: حتى إذا فتحت يأجوج ومأجوج وهم من كل حدب ينسلون

translation: And the true promise has approached; then behold, the eyes of those who disbelieved will be staring [in horror, while they say], "O woe to us; we had been unmindful of this; rather, we were wrongdoers."
interpretation: This verse is referring to the Day of Judgment, when the disbelievers will face the reality of their actions. Their eyes will be fixed in horror as they realize the consequences of their disbelief and wrongdoing. They will express regret and admit their heedlessness and injustice. This interpretation highlights the shock, fear, and remorse the disbelievers will experience upon facing the truth they had denied and the punishment they will receive for their actions in this world.
orig: واقترب الوعد الحق فإذا هي شاخصة أبصار الذين كفروا يا ويلنا قد كنا في غفلة من هذا بل كنا ظالمين

translation: Indeed, you [disbelievers] and what you worship other than Allah are the firewood of Hell. You will be coming to [enter] it.
interpretation: This verse is a stern warning to those who worship false deities and idols instead of Allah. It emphasizes that these false objects of worship have no power or ability to save their worshippers from the punishment of Hell. The disbelievers and their false gods will all be cast into the Hellfire as its fuel, highlighting the severe consequence of associating partners with Allah and rejecting His oneness. This interpretation underscores the gravity of polytheism and the importance of worshipping Allah alone to avoid the torment of Hell.
orig: إنكم وما تعبدون من دون الله حصب جهنم أنتم لها واردون

translation: If these were gods, they would not have entered it, and all of them will abide therein eternally.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the concept of monotheism in Islam and refutes the idea of polytheism or associating partners with Allah. It suggests that if the deities worshipped by polytheists were truly gods, they would not have entered Hell, as gods should be perfect and free from any punishment. The fact that these alleged gods will abide in Hell eternally proves that they are not divine and have no power or authority. This interpretation highlights the Islamic belief in the oneness of Allah and the falsehood of worshipping any entity besides Him.
orig: لو كان هؤلاء آلهة ما وردوها وكل فيها خالدون

translation: For them therein is sighing, and they therein will not hear.
interpretation: This verse describes the fate of the disbelievers in Hell. The "sighing" represents their anguish and suffering. The statement that "they therein will not hear" indicates that they will be so overwhelmed by their painful punishment that they will not be able to hear or comprehend anything else. It suggests a state of complete distress and hopelessness where the only thing they are aware of is their ongoing torment. This emphasizes the severity and totality of the punishment in Hell for those who rejected faith.
orig: لهم فيها زفير وهم فيها لا يسمعون

translation: Indeed, those for whom the best [reward] has preceded from Us - they are from it far removed.
interpretation: This verse refers to the righteous believers who have earned Allah's favor through their good deeds and faith. They are promised the best reward in the Hereafter, which is Paradise. The verse emphasizes that these blessed individuals will be kept far away from the torments of Hell, as they have already secured their place in Heaven due to their righteousness and the mercy of Allah. It serves as a reassurance to the believers that their efforts will be rewarded and that they will be protected from the punishment of the Hellfire if they remain steadfast in their faith and good actions.
orig: إن الذين سبقت لهم منا الحسنى أولئك عنها مبعدون

translation: They will not hear its sound, while they abide eternally in what their souls desire.
interpretation: In Paradise, the righteous believers will be so immersed in the pleasures and delights that their souls desire, that they will not even hear the slightest whisper of the Hellfire. This verse emphasizes the complete peace, tranquility, and protection that the inhabitants of Paradise will experience, being forever shielded from any discomfort or distress. It also highlights the fulfillment and contentment they will find, as they eternally abide in a state of ultimate bliss and satisfaction, where all their desires are met in the most perfect way possible, in accordance with what pleases Allah.
orig: لا يسمعون حسيسها وهم في ما اشتهت أنفسهم خالدون

translation: The greatest terror will not grieve them, and the angels will meet them, [saying], "This is your Day which you have been promised."
interpretation: This verse refers to the state of the righteous believers on the Day of Judgment. They will not be affected by the great terror that will seize the hearts of others on that day. Instead, they will be met by angels who will give them glad tidings and reassure them that this is the day they have been promised - the day of reward for their good deeds and faith. The verse highlights the peace and tranquility that the believers will experience on a day that will be full of fear and distress for others, emphasizing the importance of faith and righteousness in attaining salvation and divine favor in the Hereafter.
orig: لا يحزنهم الفزع الأكبر وتتلقاهم الملائكة هذا يومكم الذي كنتم توعدون

translation: The Day when We will fold the heaven like the folding of a [written] sheet for the records. As We began the first creation, We will repeat it. [That is] a promise binding upon Us. Indeed, We will do it.
interpretation: This verse is referring to the Day of Judgment, when the current universe will be brought to an end and a new creation will take its place. Just as Allah created the universe the first time, He has the power to recreate it anew. The folding of the heavens like a scroll symbolizes the ease with which Allah can roll up the old universe and replace it. This is a promise that Allah has made and He will certainly fulfill it, as He is capable of all things. The verse emphasizes Allah's omnipotence and the inevitability of the Day of Judgment, urging humans to be mindful of that Day and to prepare for it through righteous deeds.
orig: يوم نطوي السماء كطي السجل للكتب كما بدأنا أول خلق نعيده وعدا علينا إنا كنا فاعلين

translation: And indeed, We have written in the Zabur after the Reminder that the earth shall be inherited by My righteous servants.
interpretation: This verse conveys the promise of Allah that the righteous believers who follow His guidance and do good deeds will ultimately inherit the earth. It suggests that even though the wicked may seem to have the upper hand in this world, it is the pious servants of Allah who will triumph in the end and be granted authority and dominion over the earth. This inheritance could be in the form of political power, spiritual influence, or the establishment of a just and virtuous society. The verse serves as a reassurance to the believers and a warning to the wrongdoers that the ultimate outcome rests with Allah, who will reward His faithful servants and punish those who reject His message.
orig: ولقد كتبنا في الزبور من بعد الذكر أن الأرض يرثها عبادي الصالحون

translation: Indeed, in this [Qur'an] is notification for a worshipping people.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the Qur'an serves as a profound reminder and admonition for those who are sincerely devoted to worshipping Allah. It suggests that the teachings, guidance, and wisdom contained within the Qur'an are particularly beneficial for individuals who have submitted themselves to the will of Allah and strive to live righteously. The Qur'an acts as a means of spiritual enlightenment, providing direction and inspiration for those who seek to strengthen their connection with their Creator through worship and obedience. Thus, the verse highlights the significance of the Qur'an as a source of divine communication specifically tailored for the believers who dedicate themselves to the worship of Allah.
orig: إن في هذا لبلاغا لقوم عابدين

translation: And We have not sent you, [O Muhammad], except as a mercy to the worlds.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the universal nature of Prophet Muhammad's message. He was not sent just for a specific group or nation, but as a mercy and blessing for all of humanity. His teachings and example are meant to guide people towards righteousness, compassion, and the worship of the One True God. The Prophet's mission is to bring mercy, peace, and healing to a world filled with strife and suffering. This underscores the all-encompassing and benevolent nature of Islam, which seeks to benefit all of mankind.
orig: وما أرسلناك إلا رحمة للعالمين

translation: Say, "It is only revealed to me that your god is but one God; so will you be Muslims [in submission to Him]?"
interpretation: This verse is a clear call to monotheism, the belief in the oneness of God. The Prophet Muhammad is instructed to convey the message that there is only one true God worthy of worship and submission. It serves as an invitation to the people to embrace Islam and submit themselves wholly to the will of the one true God. The verse emphasizes that the core message revealed to the Prophet is the unity of God, and it challenges the audience to respond positively to this message by becoming Muslims, those who surrender themselves to God in obedience and worship.
orig: قل إنما يوحى إلي أنما إلهكم إله واحد فهل أنتم مسلمون

translation: And if they turn away, then say, "I have announced to you upon equal terms. And I do not know whether what you are promised is near or far."
interpretation: This verse is a warning to those who reject the message of Islam. The Prophet is instructed to tell them that he has conveyed the message to them clearly and equally, without any ambiguity or hidden agenda. He has fulfilled his duty as a messenger, and now it is up to them to accept or reject the message. The Prophet is also reminded that he does not know when the promised punishment or reward will come, whether it is near or far in the future. This emphasizes the idea that the ultimate judgment and consequences are in the hands of Allah, and that the Prophet's role is only to deliver the message and leave the outcome to Allah.
orig: فإن تولوا فقل آذنتكم على سواء وإن أدري أقريب أم بعيد ما توعدون

translation: He knows what is said openly and He knows what you conceal.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the all-encompassing knowledge of Allah. It reminds us that nothing is hidden from Him, whether it is the words we speak openly or the thoughts and intentions we keep concealed within our hearts. It is a call for us to be mindful of our actions and intentions, as Allah is fully aware of everything we do or think. This verse encourages us to strive for sincerity and purity in our deeds and intentions, as ultimately, Allah knows the true nature of our actions, even if we may hide them from others.
orig: إنه يعلم الجهر من القول ويعلم ما تكتمون

translation: And I do not know; perhaps it is a trial for you and enjoyment for a time.
interpretation: This verse suggests that the worldly life and its pleasures may be a test for mankind, to see whether they will be grateful to Allah and obey His commands, or be diverted by these temporary enjoyments. It implies that one should not be deceived by the fleeting nature of worldly delights, as they are ultimately a means of trial. Rather, one should focus on the eternal life of the Hereafter and strive to please Allah. The verse also indicates that Allah, in His wisdom, may grant people temporary enjoyment as a means of testing their faith and resolve.
orig: وإن أدري لعله فتنة لكم ومتاع إلى حين

translation: He said, "My Lord, judge [between us] in truth. And our Lord is the Most Merciful, the one whose help is sought against that which you describe."
interpretation: This verse is a prayer for God's just judgment and an affirmation of His mercy. It emphasizes the believer's trust in God's wisdom and justice, seeking His aid against false accusations or descriptions. The verse highlights the importance of relying on God's guidance and support when faced with adversity or conflicts, acknowledging that ultimate judgment belongs to Him alone.
orig: قال رب احكم بالحق وربنا الرحمن المستعان على ما تصفون

translation: O mankind, fear your Lord. Indeed, the convulsion of the [final] Hour is a terrible thing.
interpretation: This verse is a reminder and warning to all of humanity to be mindful of God and to fear Him, because the Day of Judgment will be a tremendously dreadful event. It emphasizes the severity and intensity of the final Hour, describing the convulsion and upheaval that will occur on that Day. The verse aims to instill a sense of awe and reverence for God in people's hearts, motivating them to lead righteous lives and be prepared for the ultimate reckoning. It underscores the importance of taqwa (God-consciousness) in the life of a believer, as it is the key to attaining salvation and success in the Hereafter.
orig: يا أيها الناس اتقوا ربكم إن زلزلة الساعة شيء عظيم

translation: The Day you see it every nursing mother will be distracted from that [child] she was nursing, and every pregnant woman will abort her pregnancy, and you will see the people [appearing] intoxicated while they are not intoxicated; but the punishment of Allah is severe.
interpretation: This verse is describing the immense terror and upheaval that will occur on the Day of Judgment. It will be so overwhelming that even the most basic human instincts, like a mother's care for her child, will be forgotten. People will be in a state of shock and confusion, appearing as if drunk, though they are not. This is because Allah's punishment is so severe that it will shake people to their core, making them lose all sense of normalcy. The verse emphasizes the gravity of that Day and the importance of being mindful of one's deeds in this life, as they will have consequences in the Hereafter.
orig: يوم ترونها تذهل كل مرضعة عما أرضعت وتضع كل ذات حمل حملها وترى الناس سكارى وما هم بسكارى ولكن عذاب الله شديد

translation: And of the people is he who disputes about Allah without knowledge and follows every rebellious devil.
interpretation: This verse is referring to those who argue about Allah and His existence, attributes, or teachings without having proper knowledge or understanding. They are misguided and follow the whispers and temptations of the rebellious devils, who lead them astray from the straight path. Such people are arrogant and stubborn in their ignorance, refusing to accept the truth even when it is presented to them clearly. They are more concerned with their own desires and opinions than with seeking the guidance of Allah and His Messenger. This verse serves as a warning to those who engage in such futile disputes and a reminder to seek knowledge from reliable sources and to follow the guidance of Allah and His Messenger.
orig: ومن الناس من يجادل في الله بغير علم ويتبع كل شيطان مريد

translation: It has been decreed for every person that whoever takes him as an ally - he will misguide him and will lead him to the punishment of the Blaze.
interpretation: This verse warns against taking those who misguide as allies or protectors. Whoever follows and obeys such people will be led astray from the straight path and guided towards the torment of Hell. It emphasizes the importance of choosing righteous companions and leaders who will guide one towards the pleasure of Allah rather than towards misguidance and punishment in the Hereafter.
orig: كتب عليه أنه من تولاه فأنه يضله ويهديه إلى عذاب السعير

translation: O People, if you should be in doubt about the Resurrection, then [consider that] indeed, We created you from dust, then from a sperm-drop, then from a clinging clot, and then from a lump of flesh, formed and unformed - that We may show you. And We settle in the wombs whom We will for a specified term, then We bring you out as a child, and then [We develop you] that you may reach your [time of] maturity. And among you is he who is taken in [early] death, and among you is he who is returned to the most decrepit [old] age so that he knows, after [once having] knowledge, nothing. And you see the earth barren, but when We send down upon it rain, it quivers and swells and grows [something] of every beautiful kind.
interpretation: This verse reminds us of God's power and the reality of resurrection. It highlights the stages of human development from conception to death, illustrating God's ability to create and recreate life. The analogy of the barren earth coming to life with rain emphasizes that just as God can revive the dead earth, He can resurrect the dead. This encourages believers to have faith in the resurrection and the afterlife, knowing that God, who created them once, can easily restore them to life again. The verse also points to the signs in creation that testify to God's power and the truth of resurrection.
orig: يا أيها الناس إن كنتم في ريب من البعث فإنا خلقناكم من تراب ثم من نطفة ثم من علقة ثم من مضغة مخلقة وغير مخلقة لنبين لكم ونقر في الأرحام ما نشاء إلى أجل مسمى ثم نخرجكم طفلا ثم لتبلغوا أشدكم ومنكم من يتوفى ومنكم من يرد إلى أرذل العمر لكيلا يعلم من بعد علم شيئا وترى الأرض هامدة فإذا أنزلنا عليها الماء اهتزت وربت وأنبتت من كل زوج بهيج

translation: That is because Allah is the Truth and because He gives life to the dead and because He is over all things competent.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute power and authority of Allah. It affirms that Allah is the ultimate reality and truth, and that everything else is subordinate to Him. The verse also highlights Allah's ability to give life to the dead, which is a testament to His omnipotence. The interpretation is that Allah's power extends over all things, and that He has the ability to bring the dead back to life, which is a fundamental belief in Islamic theology. This verse serves as a reminder to Muslims of Allah's supremacy and the importance of submitting to His will.
orig: ذلك بأن الله هو الحق وأنه يحيي الموتى وأنه على كل شيء قدير

translation: And [that] the Hour is coming - no doubt about it - and that Allah will resurrect those in the graves.
interpretation: This verse affirms the absolute certainty of two fundamental Islamic beliefs: the inevitability of the Day of Judgment (the Hour) and the resurrection of the dead. It emphasizes that there should be no doubt whatsoever about these events taking place as promised by Allah. The verse serves as a reminder for believers to live righteously and be ever mindful of the afterlife, as each person will be held accountable for their deeds when raised from their graves on the Day of Judgment. It also highlights Allah's supreme power and ability to bring the dead back to life, reinforcing His sovereignty over all creation.
orig: وأن الساعة آتية لا ريب فيها وأن الله يبعث من في القبور

translation: And among the people is he who disputes about Allah without knowledge or guidance or an enlightening book [from Him].
interpretation: This verse is criticizing those who argue about Allah and matters of faith without having proper knowledge, divine guidance, or a scripture that provides clear evidence for their claims. Such people engage in baseless disputes out of ignorance or stubbornness, rather than sincerely seeking the truth. They follow their own whims and conjectures instead of relying on authentic sources of knowledge like revelation. The verse implies that valid arguments about Allah should be based on sound knowledge, divine guidance, and the light of scriptures revealed by Him. Arguing without these is blameworthy and leads people astray.
orig: ومن الناس من يجادل في الله بغير علم ولا هدى ولا كتاب منير

translation: Bending his neck [in arrogance] to mislead [people] from the way of Allah. For him in the world is disgrace, and We will make him taste on the Day of Resurrection the punishment of the Burning Fire.
interpretation: This verse warns against arrogance and pride that leads people astray from the path of Allah. Those who engage in such behavior will face humiliation in this world and the torment of the blazing Fire in the Hereafter. It emphasizes the consequences of using one's position or influence to misguide others and highlights the importance of humility and submission to Allah's guidance. The mention of the "Burning Fire" underscores the severity of the punishment awaiting those who persist in leading others away from the truth.
orig: ثاني عطفه ليضل عن سبيل الله له في الدنيا خزي ونذيقه يوم القيامة عذاب الحريق

translation: That is for what your hands have put forth and because Allah is not ever unjust to [His] servants.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the concept of individual responsibility and divine justice in Islam. It suggests that whatever befalls a person is a result of their own actions and choices ("what your hands have put forth"). At the same time, it affirms that Allah is never unjust or unfair to His servants. He does not punish people without reason or cause them undue suffering. Rather, the consequences faced by individuals are a direct result of their own deeds, as Allah is infinitely just and equitable in His treatment of humanity. This verse serves as a reminder for believers to be mindful of their actions and to trust in the perfect justice of Allah.
orig: ذلك بما قدمت يداك وأن الله ليس بظلام للعبيد

translation: And among the people is he who worships Allah on an edge. If he is touched by good, he is reassured by it; but if he is struck by trial, he turns on his face [to the other direction]. He has lost [this] world and the Hereafter. That is what is the manifest loss.
interpretation: This verse refers to those people whose faith is weak and superficial. They worship God only when things are going well for them, but when faced with trials and difficulties, they turn away from faith and revert to disbelief. Such people are spiritually unstable and fickle. Their loss is twofold - they neither gain anything worthwhile in this world due to their lack of sincerity and commitment, nor do they attain success in the Hereafter because of their lack of true faith. This is indeed a manifest and evident loss, as they have squandered the opportunity of both worlds due to their spiritual fickleness.
orig: ومن الناس من يعبد الله على حرف فإن أصابه خير اطمأن به وإن أصابته فتنة انقلب على وجهه خسر الدنيا والآخرة ذلك هو الخسران المبين

translation: He invokes besides Allah that which neither harms him nor benefits him. That is what is the far straying.
interpretation: This verse is criticizing those who worship false gods or idols instead of Allah. It points out the futility and irrationality of invoking entities that can neither harm nor benefit a person in any way. Doing so is described as being in a state of "far straying" - meaning that the person is utterly misguided and distant from the truth of monotheism. The implication is that only Allah is worthy of worship, since only He has the power to truly benefit or harm, and that directing worship to anything else is a grave error that leads one far astray from the straight path.
orig: يدعو من دون الله ما لا يضره وما لا ينفعه ذلك هو الضلال البعيد

translation: He invokes [instead of Allah] that which can neither harm him nor benefit him. That is what is the extreme error.
interpretation: This verse criticizes those who call upon false deities or beings other than Allah for help or support. It points out the futility and misguidance in seeking aid from those who can neither harm nor benefit, as all power and control belongs to Allah alone. Invoking anyone else is considered to be in grave error and contrary to the principle of Tawheed (the Oneness of Allah). The verse emphasizes that Allah is the only true protector and ally, and relying on false objects of worship leads one far astray from the path of guidance and truth.
orig: يدعو لمن ضره أقرب من نفعه لبئس المولى ولبئس العشير

translation: Indeed, Allah will admit those who believe and do righteous deeds to gardens beneath which rivers flow. Indeed, Allah does what He intends.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the power and authority of Allah. It assures the believers that if they have faith and do good deeds, Allah will certainly reward them with Paradise, where they will enjoy eternal bliss. The flowing of rivers beneath the gardens of Paradise is a metaphor for the abundance of blessings and delights that await the righteous. The verse also underscores the idea that Allah's will is absolute and that He can do whatever He pleases. This serves as a reminder to humans that they should submit to Allah's will and strive to earn His pleasure through faith and righteous actions.
orig: إن الله يدخل الذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات جنات تجري من تحتها الأنهار إن الله يفعل ما يريد

translation: Whoever thinks that Allah will not support him in this world and the Hereafter - let him extend a rope to the ceiling and cut [himself] off, and let him see if his effort will remove that which enrages [him].
interpretation: This verse is a warning to those who doubt Allah's support and help. It tells them metaphorically to go ahead and hang themselves if they think that Allah will not aid His servant. The verse challenges the doubters, saying that even if they were to end their own lives in despair, it would not change the reality that Allah does indeed support the believers. It emphasizes having complete trust and reliance on Allah, knowing that He is sufficient as a helper and protector for those who have faith in Him.
orig: من كان يظن أن لن ينصره الله في الدنيا والآخرة فليمدد بسبب إلى السماء ثم ليقطع فلينظر هل يذهبن كيده ما يغيظ

translation: And thus have We sent it down as clear verses. And indeed, Allah guides whom He intends.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the Qur'an has been revealed with clear and unambiguous signs, indicating its divine origin. It also highlights the concept of divine guidance, stating that Allah guides those whom He chooses to guide. This suggests that while the Qur'an provides clear guidance, ultimately, it is Allah who grants individuals the ability to understand and follow its teachings. The verse implies that guidance is a gift from Allah, bestowed upon those He intends to guide, and that the clarity of the Qur'anic message is a testament to Allah's wisdom and mercy in providing a path to righteousness for humanity.
orig: وكذلك أنزلناه آيات بينات وأن الله يهدي من يريد

translation: Indeed, those who believed and those who were Jews or Sabeans or Christians or Magians [before Prophet Muhammad] and those who associated with Allah - Allah will judge between them on the Day of Resurrection. Indeed Allah is, over all things, Witness.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that on the Day of Judgment, God will judge between people of different faiths - the Muslims, Jews, Sabeans, Christians, Magians (Zoroastrians), and the polytheists. It underscores the idea that God is aware of everyone's beliefs and actions, and He will judge each individual based on their deeds and the truth of their faith. The verse implies that what matters is one's sincere belief and good deeds, rather than mere labels or affiliations. It also suggests that God's judgment is ultimately fair and based on His all-encompassing knowledge, emphasizing His role as the ultimate Witness over all things.
orig: إن الذين آمنوا والذين هادوا والصابئين والنصارى والمجوس والذين أشركوا إن الله يفصل بينهم يوم القيامة إن الله على كل شيء شهيد

translation: Do you not see that to Allah prostrates whoever is in the heavens and whoever is on the earth and the sun, the moon, the stars, the mountains, the trees, the moving creatures and many of the people? But upon many the punishment has been justified. And he whom Allah humiliates - for him there is no bestower of honor. Indeed, Allah does what He wills.
interpretation: This verse highlights the absolute power and authority of Allah over His creation. It states that all beings in the heavens and earth, whether living or non-living, prostrate to Allah in submission and obedience. This includes celestial bodies like the sun, moon, and stars, as well as natural phenomena such as mountains and trees. Even animals and many people prostrate to Allah. However, there are also many people who have earned Allah's punishment due to their disobedience and rejection of faith. The verse emphasizes that whomever Allah humiliates and disgraces, no one can grant them honor, as Allah does whatever He wills according to His wisdom and justice. This serves as a reminder for humans to humble themselves before the Almighty and strive to earn His pleasure through faith and righteousness.
orig: ألم تر أن الله يسجد له من في السماوات ومن في الأرض والشمس والقمر والنجوم والجبال والشجر والدواب وكثير من الناس وكثير حق عليه العذاب ومن يهن الله فما له من مكرم إن الله يفعل ما يشاء

translation: These are two adversaries who have disputed about their Lord. But those who disbelieved will have cut out for them garments of fire. Poured upon their heads will be scalding water.
interpretation: This verse speaks about the fate of the disbelievers on the Day of Judgment. It depicts a scene where two groups, the believers and the disbelievers, are in dispute about their faith in Allah. As a consequence of their disbelief, those who rejected the truth will be punished by having garments of fire cut out for them, and scalding water will be poured over their heads. This interpretation highlights the severe punishment that awaits those who deny the existence or unity of Allah and reject the message of His prophets. It serves as a warning for mankind to embrace faith and righteousness before it is too late.
orig: هذان خصمان اختصموا في ربهم فالذين كفروا قطعت لهم ثياب من نار يصب من فوق رءوسهم الحميم

translation: With it will melt that which is within their bellies and [their] skins.
interpretation: This verse refers to the punishment that awaits the disbelievers in Hell. The intense heat of the Hellfire will cause their internal organs and skin to melt, indicating the severity and pain of the torment. It serves as a grave warning to those who reject faith, emphasizing the consequences of their actions in the Hereafter. The verse aims to instill fear and encourage people to embrace belief and righteousness to avoid such a dreadful fate.
orig: يصهر به ما في بطونهم والجلود

translation: And for them are hooked rods of iron.
interpretation: This verse refers to one of the punishments that await the disbelievers and wrongdoers in Hell. The "hooked rods of iron" are understood to be a means of torture, used by the angels of Hell to strike and punish the sinners. This fearsome imagery serves as a severe warning and reminder of the grave consequences of rejecting faith and indulging in evil deeds. It emphasizes the absolute justice of God, and that those who knowingly choose the path of disobedience will face a terrifying recompense in the Hereafter.
orig: ولهم مقامع من حديد

translation: Every time they want to get out of it from anguish, they will be returned to it, and [it will be said], "Taste the punishment of the Burning Fire!"
interpretation: This verse is referring to the punishment of the disbelievers in Hell. Whenever they try to escape from the anguish and torment of the Fire, they will be pushed back into it by the angels and it will be said to them, "Taste the punishment of the burning Fire!" This emphasizes the severity and endlessness of the punishment, as there will be no respite or escape for them. It also serves as a warning to those who reject faith, urging them to believe and do righteous deeds in order to avoid this terrible fate.
orig: كلما أرادوا أن يخرجوا منها من غم أعيدوا فيها وذوقوا عذاب الحريق

translation: Indeed, Allah will admit those who believe and do righteous deeds to gardens beneath which rivers flow. They will be adorned therein with bracelets of gold and pearl, and their garments therein will be silk.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the great reward that Allah has prepared for the believers who do good deeds in this world. It describes the eternal bliss of Paradise, where the faithful will enjoy luxuries beyond imagination. The mention of gold, pearls, and silk symbolizes the ultimate beauty, purity, and comfort that the inhabitants of Paradise will experience. This promise serves as an encouragement for believers to remain steadfast in their faith and to continuously strive for righteousness, knowing that their efforts will be handsomely rewarded in the Hereafter.
orig: إن الله يدخل الذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات جنات تجري من تحتها الأنهار يحلون فيها من أساور من ذهب ولؤلؤا ولباسهم فيها حرير

translation: And they are guided to the good of the speech and they are guided to the path of the Praiseworthy.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that those who are rightly guided by Allah are directed towards virtuous and righteous speech. They are inspired to speak in a manner that is good, beneficial, and pleasing to Allah. Moreover, they are guided to the straight path that leads to the Almighty, the One who is worthy of all praise. This path is the way of Islam, submission to Allah's will, and adherence to His commands. The verse signifies that true guidance encompasses both one's words and actions, aligning them with what is beloved and praised by Allah.
orig: وهدوا إلى الطيب من القول وهدوا إلى صراط الحميد

translation: Indeed, those who disbelieve and hinder [people] from the way of Allah and [from] al-Masjid al-Haram, which We made for the people - equal are the resident therein and one from outside; and [also] whoever intends [a deed] therein of deviation [in religion] or wrongdoing - We will make him taste of a painful punishment.
interpretation: This verse warns those who reject faith and prevent others from following the path of Allah and accessing the Sacred Mosque (al-Masjid al-Haram) in Makkah. It emphasizes that the Sacred Mosque is open to all people, whether they reside there or come from outside. The verse also cautions that anyone who seeks to commit sacrilege or wrongdoing in the Sacred Mosque will face severe punishment from Allah. This highlights the sanctity and importance of the Sacred Mosque and the severity of the consequences for those who violate its sanctity or hinder others from worshipping there.
orig: إن الذين كفروا ويصدون عن سبيل الله والمسجد الحرام الذي جعلناه للناس سواء العاكف فيه والباد ومن يرد فيه بإلحاد بظلم نذقه من عذاب أليم

translation: And [mention] when We designated for Abraham the site of the House, [saying], "Do not associate anything with Me and purify My House for those who perform Tawaf and those who stand [in prayer] and those who bow and prostrate."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of monotheism and the sanctity of the Ka'bah. It reminds us that the Ka'bah was established by Prophet Abraham as a place of worship dedicated solely to Allah, free from any form of idolatry or polytheism. The command to purify the House of Allah is not only physical but also spiritual, requiring the worshippers to maintain a pure intention and devotion to Allah alone. This verse also highlights the significance of the various acts of worship performed at the Ka'bah, such as Tawaf (circumambulation), standing in prayer, bowing, and prostration, which are all expressions of submission and humility before Allah.
orig: وإذ بوأنا لإبراهيم مكان البيت أن لا تشرك بي شيئا وطهر بيتي للطائفين والقائمين والركع السجود

translation: And proclaim to the people the Hajj [pilgrimage]; they will come to you on foot and on every lean camel; they will come from every distant pass.
interpretation: This verse is a divine command to Prophet Ibrahim (Abraham) to announce the pilgrimage to the Sacred House (Ka'bah) in Makkah. It signifies that people from all over the world, from every corner of the earth, will come to perform Hajj, the annual pilgrimage. They will come on foot and on lean camels, symbolizing their dedication and devotion to this spiritual journey. The verse emphasizes the universal nature of the pilgrimage, as it calls upon people from all walks of life, from near and far, to answer the call of Hajj and gather in one place for the sole purpose of worshipping Allah. It also highlights the spiritual significance of Hajj as a means of attaining closeness to Allah and seeking His forgiveness and mercy.
orig: وأذن في الناس بالحج يأتوك رجالا وعلى كل ضامر يأتين من كل فج عميق

translation: That they may witness benefits for themselves and mention the name of Allah on known days over what He has provided for them of [sacrificial] animals. So eat of them and feed the miserable and poor.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of performing the pilgrimage (Hajj) and the sacrificial rites associated with it. The "benefits" mentioned refer to both spiritual and worldly advantages gained from the pilgrimage, such as increased faith, forgiveness of sins, and strengthening of social bonds among Muslims. The verse also highlights the significance of mentioning Allah's name during the specified days of sacrifice and the act of sharing the meat from the sacrificed animals with those in need, particularly the poor and destitute. This practice promotes a sense of unity, compassion, and social responsibility within the Muslim community.
orig: ليشهدوا منافع لهم ويذكروا اسم الله في أيام معلومات على ما رزقهم من بهيمة الأنعام فكلوا منها وأطعموا البائس الفقير

translation: Then let them end their untidiness and fulfill their vows and perform Tawaf around the ancient House.
interpretation: This verse is referring to the rites of Hajj, the annual pilgrimage to Mecca. After the pilgrims complete their ritual acts and end their state of dishevelment from the journey, they are instructed to fulfill any vows or promises they have made to Allah. The verse then commands them to circumambulate the Ka'bah, the ancient cube-shaped structure at the heart of the Sacred Mosque, as a key ritual of Hajj. This Tawaf, or circling, around the "ancient House" - built by Abraham and his son Ishmael according to Islamic tradition - symbolizes the unity and centrality of the worship of the One God. It is an integral part of the Hajj rites that connects the pilgrims with the long spiritual history of monotheism.
orig: ثم ليقضوا تفثهم وليوفوا نذورهم وليطوفوا بالبيت العتيق

translation: That [has been commanded], and whoever honors the sacred ordinances of Allah - it is best for him in the sight of his Lord. And permitted to you are the grazing livestock, except what is recited to you. So avoid the uncleanliness of idols and avoid false statement,
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of respecting and upholding the sacred rites and ordinances decreed by Allah. It suggests that honoring these ordinances is highly virtuous and will be rewarded by Allah. The verse also clarifies that livestock are permissible for consumption, except for those categories which have been specifically prohibited and mentioned in the Qur'an. It instructs believers to shun the impurity associated with idolatry and to refrain from making false statements or testifying falsely. The overall message is to adhere to Allah's commands, maintain purity in faith and actions, and to be truthful in one's speech.
orig: ذلك ومن يعظم حرمات الله فهو خير له عند ربه وأحلت لكم الأنعام إلا ما يتلى عليكم فاجتنبوا الرجس من الأوثان واجتنبوا قول الزور

translation: Inclining [only] to Allah, not associating [anything] with Him. And he who associates with Allah - it is as though he had fallen from the sky and was snatched by the birds or the wind carried him down into a remote place.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of pure monotheism and the grave consequences of associating partners with Allah (shirk). It compares the one who commits shirk to someone who falls from the sky, completely helpless and vulnerable, either being snatched away by birds or carried by the wind to a distant, desolate place. This metaphor illustrates the spiritual destruction and loss of guidance that results from associating others with Allah in worship or attributing divine characteristics to anyone or anything other than Him. It serves as a strong warning against shirk and highlights the significance of maintaining sincere devotion and submission to Allah alone.
orig: حنفاء لله غير مشركين به ومن يشرك بالله فكأنما خر من السماء فتخطفه الطير أو تهوي به الريح في مكان سحيق

translation: That [is so]. And whoever honors the symbols of Allah - indeed, it is from the piety of hearts.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of respecting and honoring the sacred rites and symbols associated with Allah and His worship. It suggests that showing reverence to these symbols, such as the rituals of Hajj or the sanctity of the Ka'bah, is a reflection of the righteousness and devotion within one's heart. The act of honoring these symbols externally is an indication of the sincerity, submission, and love for Allah that resides internally. Thus, the verse encourages believers to approach these sacred elements with utmost respect and dedication, as it is a means of nurturing and strengthening the piety and God-consciousness within their hearts.
orig: ذلك ومن يعظم شعائر الله فإنها من تقوى القلوب

translation: And you have benefits in them for a specified term; then their place of sacrifice is at the ancient House.
interpretation: This verse refers to the sacrificial animals that are offered during the Hajj pilgrimage. These animals, such as camels, cows, and sheep, are brought to the sacred precinct of Mecca, where they are sacrificed as an act of worship and devotion to Allah. The verse highlights that these animals provide benefits to the pilgrims, such as being a source of food and provision, until the specified time of sacrifice. The "ancient House" refers to the Kaaba, the sacred structure at the heart of the Grand Mosque in Mecca, which serves as the focal point of the Hajj pilgrimage and the direction of prayer for Muslims worldwide. The act of sacrificing these animals near the Kaaba symbolizes the ultimate submission and dedication to Allah, following the footsteps of Prophet Ibrahim (Abraham) who was willing to sacrifice his son as an act of obedience to Allah's command.
orig: لكم فيها منافع إلى أجل مسمى ثم محلها إلى البيت العتيق

translation: And for every nation We have appointed a rite [of sacrifice] that they may mention the name of Allah over what He has provided for them of [sacrificial] animals. For your god is one God, so to Him submit. And, [O Muhammad], give good tidings to the humble [before their Lord]
interpretation: This verse highlights the universality of the concept of sacrifice in various religious traditions. It emphasizes that the ultimate purpose of these sacrificial rites is to remember and invoke the name of Allah, acknowledging His provision and blessings. The verse also stresses the core belief in the oneness of God (tawheed) and the importance of submitting to Him alone. It concludes with a message of glad tidings to those who humble themselves before their Lord, indicating that humility and submission to the One God are the key to attaining divine favor and salvation.
orig: ولكل أمة جعلنا منسكا ليذكروا اسم الله على ما رزقهم من بهيمة الأنعام فإلهكم إله واحد فله أسلموا وبشر المخبتين

translation: Those whose hearts tremble when Allah is mentioned, and those who are patient with whatever afflicts them, and those who establish prayer, and who spend from what We have provided for them.
interpretation: This verse describes the qualities of the righteous believers. When Allah is mentioned, their hearts are filled with awe and reverence, indicating their deep faith and consciousness of Allah. They display patience and perseverance in the face of trials and difficulties, trusting in Allah's plan. They are diligent in establishing prayer, which demonstrates their commitment to worshipping Allah and maintaining a connection with Him. Lastly, they are generous in spending from the provisions that Allah has granted them, showing their gratitude and willingness to help others in need. These characteristics highlight the believers' sincerity, devotion, and righteousness in their relationship with Allah and their conduct in life.
orig: الذين إذا ذكر الله وجلت قلوبهم والصابرين على ما أصابهم والمقيمي الصلاة ومما رزقناهم ينفقون

translation: And the camels and cattle, We have appointed them for you as among the symbols of Allah; for you therein is good. So mention the name of Allah upon them when lined up [for sacrifice]; and when they are [lifeless] on their sides, then eat from them and feed the needy and the beggar. Thus have We subjected them to you that you may be grateful.
interpretation: This verse highlights the significance of sacrificing animals, particularly camels and cattle, as a symbol of devotion to Allah. It emphasizes the importance of invoking Allah's name while sacrificing these animals and the virtue of sharing the meat with those in need, such as the poor and the beggars. The act of sacrifice is portrayed as a means of expressing gratitude to Allah for subjecting these animals to the benefit of humankind. The verse encourages believers to recognize the blessings bestowed upon them by Allah and to show their appreciation through acts of worship and charity.
