orig: والبدن جعلناها لكم من شعائر الله لكم فيها خير فاذكروا اسم الله عليها صواف فإذا وجبت جنوبها فكلوا منها وأطعموا القانع والمعتر كذلك سخرناها لكم لعلكم تشكرون

translation: It is not their meat nor their blood that reaches Allah, but it is piety from you that reaches Him. Thus have We made them subject to you that you may magnify Allah for His Guidance to you. And give glad tidings to the good-doers.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the essence of sacrifice is not in the flesh or blood of the animal, but rather in the devotion, obedience, and righteousness of the person making the offering. Allah has subjected these animals to humans so that they may express their gratitude to Him for guiding them to the right path. The physical act of sacrifice is merely a means to demonstrate one's submission to Allah's will and to glorify Him. The verse also encourages people to do good deeds, as Allah gives glad tidings to those who strive to be righteous and perform acts of kindness.
orig: لن ينال الله لحومها ولا دماؤها ولكن يناله التقوى منكم كذلك سخرها لكم لتكبروا الله على ما هداكم وبشر المحسنين

translation: Indeed, Allah defends those who have believed. Indeed, Allah does not like everyone treacherous and ungrateful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah protects and supports those who sincerely believe in Him and follow His guidance. It also highlights two qualities that Allah dislikes: treachery (betrayal and deception) and ungratefulness (denying Allah's blessings and favors). The verse serves as a reminder for the believers to remain steadfast in their faith, knowing that Allah is on their side, while also warning against the vices of treachery and ingratitude, which are displeasing to Allah.
orig: إن الله يدافع عن الذين آمنوا إن الله لا يحب كل خوان كفور

translation: Permission [to fight] has been given to those who are being fought, because they were wronged. And indeed, Allah is competent to give them victory.
interpretation: This verse establishes the principle of permissibility of fighting in self-defense for those who have been wronged and oppressed. It assures the believers that Allah has the power to grant them victory against their oppressors. The verse implies that fighting is only allowed in response to aggression and persecution, not as a means of imposing faith or spreading the religion by force. It emphasizes that the cause must be just and the intention pure for those who fight in the way of Allah, seeking to end oppression and establish justice.
orig: أذن للذين يقاتلون بأنهم ظلموا وإن الله على نصرهم لقدير

translation: Those who have been expelled from their homes without right - only because they say, "Our Lord is Allah." And were it not that Allah checks the people, some by means of others, there would have been demolished monasteries, churches, synagogues, and mosques in which the name of Allah is much mentioned. And Allah will surely support those who support Him. Indeed, Allah is Powerful and Exalted in Might.
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of religious freedom and the right of people to worship God as they choose. It condemns the forced expulsion of people from their homes simply because of their faith, emphasizing that the only reason for their persecution is their belief in Allah. The verse also underscores the divine wisdom in allowing people to defend themselves and their places of worship against aggression, as this prevents the destruction of monasteries, churches, synagogues, and mosques where Allah's name is celebrated. Moreover, it assures believers that Allah will aid and support those who stand up for His cause, as He is the Ultimate Source of strength and power.
orig: الذين أخرجوا من ديارهم بغير حق إلا أن يقولوا ربنا الله ولولا دفع الله الناس بعضهم ببعض لهدمت صوامع وبيع وصلوات ومساجد يذكر فيها اسم الله كثيرا ولينصرن الله من ينصره إن الله لقوي عزيز

translation: [And they are] those who, if We give them authority in the land, establish prayer and give zakah and enjoin what is right and forbid what is wrong. And to Allah belongs the outcome of [all] matters.
interpretation: This verse highlights the characteristics and responsibilities of righteous leaders and believers. When given positions of authority and power, they prioritize the establishment of prayer, which represents their spiritual connection with Allah. They also fulfill the obligation of giving zakah, demonstrating their commitment to social welfare and economic justice. Moreover, they actively promote good and forbid evil, striving to create a society based on Islamic values and ethics. The verse concludes by emphasizing that the ultimate outcome of all affairs rests with Allah, reminding believers to trust in His wisdom and decree while carrying out their duties with sincerity and dedication.
orig: الذين إن مكناهم في الأرض أقاموا الصلاة وآتوا الزكاة وأمروا بالمعروف ونهوا عن المنكر ولله عاقبة الأمور

translation: And if they deny you, [O Muhammad], so did the people of Noah and 'Aad and Thamud deny [their prophets] before them.
interpretation: This verse is a consolation to Prophet Muhammad, reminding him that even if his people reject his message, he is not the first prophet to face such rejection. The people of Noah, 'Aad, and Thamud, who were ancient nations mentioned in the Qur'an, also denied their prophets. This implies that the rejection of the truth by some people is not a new phenomenon and should not discourage the Prophet or the believers from continuing to convey the message of Islam. It also serves as a warning to those who reject the message, as the mentioned nations faced severe consequences for their denial of the truth.
orig: وإن يكذبوك فقد كذبت قبلهم قوم نوح وعاد وثمود

translation: And the people of Abraham and the people of Lot
interpretation: This verse refers to the nations of the Prophets Abraham and Lot, who were sent by Allah to guide their people to the right path. Despite the Prophets' efforts, their people rejected the message and continued in their disbelief and wrongdoing. This ultimately led to their destruction as a punishment from Allah. The verse serves as a reminder that those who reject the truth and persist in their disobedience will face severe consequences in this world and the Hereafter. It also highlights the importance of following the guidance of the Prophets and adhering to the teachings of Islam to attain success and salvation.
orig: وقوم إبراهيم وقوم لوط

translation: And the companions of Madyan, and Moses was denied, but I granted respite to the disbelievers; then I seized them, and how [terrible] was My reproach.
interpretation: This verse is a warning to those who reject the message of Allah and His messengers. It mentions the people of Madyan, who were sent the prophet Shu'aib, and how they denied him. It also mentions Moses, who was denied by Pharaoh and his people. Allah granted these disbelievers respite, allowing them time to repent and mend their ways. However, when they persisted in their disbelief and transgression, Allah seized them with a terrible punishment. The verse emphasizes the severity of Allah's reproach and punishment for those who reject His signs and messengers, reminding us that while Allah is patient and merciful, He is also just and will hold the disbelievers accountable for their actions in the end.
orig: وأصحاب مدين وكذب موسى فأمليت للكافرين ثم أخذتهم فكيف كان نكير

translation: And how many a city did We destroy while it was committing wrong - so it is [now] fallen into ruin - and [how many] an abandoned well and [how many] a lofty palace.
interpretation: This verse is a reminder of the consequences of wrongdoing and injustice. It points out that many cities and civilizations in the past were destroyed by Allah due to their persistent wrongdoing and transgression. Their destruction is evident from their ruins, abandoned wells, and once lofty palaces. This serves as a warning to people that they should not engage in wrongdoing and injustice, as it can lead to their downfall and destruction, just like the cities mentioned in the verse. The verse also highlights the power and authority of Allah, who can destroy even the mightiest of cities if He wills, as a punishment for their sins.
orig: فكأين من قرية أهلكناها وهي ظالمة فهي خاوية على عروشها وبئر معطلة وقصر مشيد

translation: Have they not traveled through the land, having hearts by which to reason and ears by which to hear? For indeed, it is not eyes that are blinded, but blinded are the hearts which are within the breasts.
interpretation: This verse is a call to reflect upon the signs of Allah's creation and to use one's intellect and senses to recognize the truth. It suggests that the real blindness is not the physical inability to see, but rather the spiritual and intellectual blindness that results from a hardened heart. The verse implies that those who reject the truth do so not because of a lack of evidence, but because of their own stubborn refusal to accept it. It is a reminder that true understanding and faith come from an open and receptive heart, not just from external sensory perception.
orig: أفلم يسيروا في الأرض فتكون لهم قلوب يعقلون بها أو آذان يسمعون بها فإنها لا تعمى الأبصار ولكن تعمى القلوب التي في الصدور

translation: They ask you to hasten the punishment. But Allah will never fail in His promise. And indeed, a day with your Lord is like a thousand years of those which you count.
interpretation: This verse is a reminder that Allah's timing is different from human perception. While people may be impatient and desire immediate results or consequences, Allah's plan unfolds according to His wisdom and divine timeline. The verse emphasizes that Allah will never break His promise, whether it pertains to rewarding the righteous or punishing the wrongdoers. It also highlights the relativity of time, suggesting that what may seem like a long period to humans is insignificant in the grand scheme of Allah's eternal plan. The verse encourages believers to trust in Allah's timing, remain patient, and have faith that He will fulfill His promises in due course.
orig: ويستعجلونك بالعذاب ولن يخلف الله وعده وإن يوما عند ربك كألف سنة مما تعدون

translation: And how many a city did I give respite while it was committing wrong. Then I seized it, and to Me is the [final] destination.
interpretation: This verse is a warning to those who persist in wrongdoing and oppression, thinking that Allah's delay in punishment means they can escape the consequences of their actions. It emphasizes that Allah may grant respite and time for people to mend their ways, but ultimately, He will hold them accountable for their deeds. The verse also underscores the absolute power and authority of Allah, reminding us that all things and all beings will eventually return to Him for judgment. It serves as a reminder for individuals and nations to be mindful of their actions and to turn to Allah in repentance before it is too late.
orig: وكأين من قرية أمليت لها وهي ظالمة ثم أخذتها وإلي المصير

translation: Say, "O people, I am only a clear warner to you."
interpretation: In this verse, Allah commands Prophet Muhammad to openly declare and warn all of humanity that he is a messenger sent by Allah to caution them about the consequences of rejecting the truth and the message he has brought. As a "clear warner", his duty is to plainly convey the revelations and guidance he has received, making the reality of the Divine message and the Day of Judgment evident, so that people may reflect and choose the right path. This emphasizes the universal nature of the Prophet's mission and the importance of his role in delivering Allah's message to mankind.
orig: قل يا أيها الناس إنما أنا لكم نذير مبين

translation: So those who have believed and done righteous deeds - for them is forgiveness and noble provision.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of faith and good deeds in Islam. Those who sincerely believe in Allah and perform righteous actions will be rewarded with Allah's forgiveness for their sins and a noble provision in the Hereafter, which refers to Paradise. It highlights the mercy and generosity of Allah towards His faithful servants who strive to live according to His teachings. The verse encourages believers to remain steadfast in their faith and to continuously engage in good deeds, knowing that their efforts will be acknowledged and rewarded by Allah in the afterlife.
orig: فالذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات لهم مغفرة ورزق كريم

translation: But those who strive against Our verses [seeking] to cause failure - those are the companions of Hellfire.
interpretation: This verse warns that those who actively oppose and seek to undermine Allah's revelations and signs will face severe consequences in the Hereafter. They exert effort in trying to disprove, discredit, or obstruct the message of Islam. As a result of their arrogant and stubborn rejection of the truth, they will be among the inhabitants of Hell. It emphasizes that deliberately working against Allah's religion is a grave sin that leads to the worst outcome in the afterlife.
orig: والذين سعوا في آياتنا معاجزين أولئك أصحاب الجحيم

translation: And We did not send before you any messenger or prophet except that when he spoke [or recited], Satan threw into it [some misunderstanding]. But Allah abolishes that which Satan throws in; then Allah makes precise His verses. And Allah is Knowing and Wise.
interpretation: This verse highlights the fact that even prophets and messengers are not immune to the whispers and interference of Satan. However, Allah ultimately nullifies any falsehood or misunderstanding that Satan tries to cast into their recitation or speech. Allah then firmly establishes His verses, ensuring that the divine message remains pure and intact. This demonstrates Allah's wisdom and knowledge in protecting His revelation from corruption, even when Satan attempts to create confusion or doubt. It also serves as a reminder that one should always seek clarity and guidance from Allah and not be misled by the whisperings of Satan.
orig: وما أرسلنا من قبلك من رسول ولا نبي إلا إذا تمنى ألقى الشيطان في أمنيته فينسخ الله ما يلقي الشيطان ثم يحكم الله آياته والله عليم حكيم

translation: That He may make what is thrown in by Satan a trial for those in whose hearts is a disease and whose hearts are hardened. And certainly, the wrongdoers are in an extreme opposition.
interpretation: This verse suggests that God allows Satan to whisper doubts and temptations in order to test those whose faith is weak or whose hearts are hardened by sin. It is a trial that exposes the inner state of people's hearts. Those who are truly righteous will resist these temptations and remain steadfast, while those who are inwardly diseased or sinful will be led astray by them. The verse also emphasizes that those who persistently wrong themselves and others are in a state of extreme opposition to God's guidance, as their hearts have grown hard and resistant to the truth.
orig: ليجعل ما يلقي الشيطان فتنة للذين في قلوبهم مرض والقاسية قلوبهم وإن الظالمين لفي شقاق بعيد

translation: And [that] those who have been given knowledge may know that it is the truth from your Lord and [therefore] believe in it, and their hearts humbly submit to it. And indeed is Allah the Guide of those who have believed to a straight path.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of knowledge in recognizing the truth that comes from Allah. Those who are blessed with knowledge and understanding will realize that the Qur'an is indeed the truth from their Lord. As a result, they will believe in it sincerely, and their hearts will submit humbly to its teachings. The verse also affirms that Allah guides the believers to the straight path, which is the path of righteousness and salvation. It implies that true faith is not just a matter of blind acceptance, but rather a result of knowledge, understanding, and humble submission to the truth revealed by Allah.
orig: وليعلم الذين أوتوا العلم أنه الحق من ربك فيؤمنوا به فتخبت له قلوبهم وإن الله لهاد الذين آمنوا إلى صراط مستقيم

translation: And those who disbelieve will not cease to be in doubt of it until the Hour comes upon them unexpectedly or there comes to them the punishment of a barren Day.
interpretation: This verse warns that the disbelievers will continue to doubt the truth of the Qur'an and the message of Islam until they are suddenly faced with the reality of the Day of Judgment or a severe punishment from Allah. The "barren Day" refers to a day of great distress and anguish, where no good deeds will be accepted and no intercession will be allowed. It emphasizes the importance of faith and the consequences of rejecting the truth, as the disbelievers will ultimately face the consequences of their choices when it is too late to repent or change their ways.
orig: ولا يزال الذين كفروا في مرية منه حتى تأتيهم الساعة بغتة أو يأتيهم عذاب يوم عقيم

translation: That Day, the dominion will be for Allah; He will judge between them. So those who believed and did righteous deeds will be in the Gardens of Pleasure.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that on the Day of Judgment, Allah will have complete authority and will judge all people based on their faith and deeds. Those who believed in Allah and performed good deeds will be rewarded with Paradise, where they will experience eternal bliss and pleasure. This interpretation highlights the importance of faith and righteous actions in determining one's fate in the Hereafter, and serves as a reminder for believers to strive for excellence in their spiritual and moral conduct.
orig: الملك يومئذ لله يحكم بينهم فالذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات في جنات النعيم

translation: But those who disbelieved and denied Our signs - for them will be a humiliating punishment.
interpretation: This verse warns that those who reject faith in God and refuse to acknowledge His signs and revelations will face a degrading and shameful punishment in the Hereafter. It emphasizes that denying the truth of God's message has severe consequences, as it is an act of arrogance and ingratitude. The "humiliating punishment" points to the fact that these disbelievers will be exposed and disgraced for their rejection of God in front of all of creation on the Day of Judgment. This interpretation highlights the gravity of disbelief and the justice of God in punishing those who willfully deny Him despite the signs and guidance He has provided.
orig: والذين كفروا وكذبوا بآياتنا فأولئك لهم عذاب مهين

translation: And those who emigrated for the cause of Allah and then were killed or died - Allah will surely provide for them a good provision. And indeed, it is Allah who is the best of providers.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the great reward and honor that awaits those who make sacrifices for the sake of Allah, such as leaving their homes and families to spread the message of Islam or defend the Muslim community. Even if they lose their lives in the process, Allah promises to provide for them generously in the Hereafter. This highlights Allah's attribute as the Ultimate Provider, who never fails to justly compensate His devoted servants. The verse encourages believers to prioritize their faith over worldly comforts, trusting that Allah will always take care of their needs and reward their sacrifices immensely in the afterlife.
orig: والذين هاجروا في سبيل الله ثم قتلوا أو ماتوا ليرزقنهم الله رزقا حسنا وإن الله لهو خير الرازقين

translation: That He may admit them to an entrance with which they will be pleased, and indeed, Allah is Knowing and Forbearing.
interpretation: This verse highlights the mercy and grace of Allah towards His faithful servants. It indicates that Allah will grant them entry into Paradise through a gate that will please them immensely. This special entrance is a reward for their righteous deeds and unwavering faith. The verse also emphasizes two important attributes of Allah: His knowledge and forbearance. Allah is all-knowing, fully aware of His servants' actions, intentions, and struggles. He is also forbearing, patient, and forgiving towards those who sincerely repent and strive to follow His path. This verse brings comfort and hope to the believers, assuring them that their efforts will be recognized and rewarded by their merciful and compassionate Lord.
orig: ليدخلنهم مدخلا يرضونه وإن الله لعليم حليم

translation: That [is so]. And whoever responds [to injustice] with the equivalent of that with which he was harmed and then is tyrannized - Allah will surely aid him. Indeed, Allah is Pardoning and Forgiving.
interpretation: This verse affirms the right to respond to injustice and oppression in an equivalent manner, without transgressing the limits. It assures believers that if they are further wronged after responding justly, Allah will come to their aid and support them against their oppressors. The verse concludes by emphasizing Allah's attributes of forgiveness and pardoning, indicating that while responding to injustice is permitted, the higher virtue is to forgive when possible. It encourages believers to strike a balance between justice and mercy in their dealings with others.
orig: ذلك ومن عاقب بمثل ما عوقب به ثم بغي عليه لينصرنه الله إن الله لعفو غفور

translation: That is because Allah causes the night to enter the day and causes the day to enter the night and because Allah is Hearing and Seeing.
interpretation: This verse highlights the omnipotence and omniscience of Allah. The alternation of day and night is a sign of Allah's power over the universe. He is the one who causes the night to gradually turn into day and the day to turn into night, in a continuous cycle. This is a reminder for humans to reflect on the precision and regularity of Allah's creation. Moreover, Allah is All-Hearing and All-Seeing, which means that He is aware of everything that happens in the universe, including the deeds and intentions of His creatures. This verse encourages believers to be mindful of Allah's presence and to strive to do good deeds, knowing that nothing escapes His knowledge and that He will hold them accountable for their actions.
orig: ذلك بأن الله يولج الليل في النهار ويولج النهار في الليل وأن الله سميع بصير

translation: That is because Allah is the Truth, and that which they call upon other than Him is falsehood, and because Allah is the Most High, the Grand.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the fundamental Islamic belief in the oneness and supremacy of Allah. It asserts that Allah is the ultimate truth and reality, while all other objects of worship or devotion are false and baseless. The verse also highlights two of Allah's key attributes: His exaltedness and greatness. This serves as a reminder to humans that Allah is far above all of His creation and that nothing can ever be equal to or rival Him. The verse encourages believers to put their complete trust and faith in Allah alone, as He is the only true source of guidance, support, and salvation.
orig: ذلك بأن الله هو الحق وأن ما يدعون من دونه هو الباطل وأن الله هو العلي الكبير

translation: Do you not see that Allah sends down rain from the sky and the earth becomes green? Indeed, Allah is Subtle and Acquainted.
interpretation: This verse highlights Allah's power and wisdom in creating and sustaining life on Earth. The rain that Allah sends down from the sky is a miraculous blessing that transforms the barren land into a lush, green landscape teeming with life. This process demonstrates Allah's gentleness and subtlety in providing for His creation, as well as His intimate knowledge of the intricate workings of the natural world. The verse serves as a reminder for humans to reflect upon the signs of Allah's existence and to be grateful for the countless blessings He bestows upon us, even in the seemingly simple act of sending down rain to revitalize the Earth.
orig: ألم تر أن الله أنزل من السماء ماء فتصبح الأرض مخضرة إن الله لطيف خبير

translation: To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth. And indeed, Allah is the Free of need, the Praiseworthy.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's sovereignty and ownership over all of creation. Everything in the heavens and the earth belongs to Him alone. It also highlights two of His divine attributes: His self-sufficiency (Al-Ghani), meaning He is free from any need or dependency on His creation, and His being worthy of all praise (Al-Hamid). This reminds us to direct our worship, gratitude, and reliance towards Him alone, recognizing that He is the ultimate possessor and controller of all things, while being praiseworthy in all His actions and decrees.
orig: له ما في السماوات وما في الأرض وإن الله لهو الغني الحميد

translation: Do you not see that Allah has subjected to you whatever is on the earth and the ships which run through the sea by His command? And He restrains the sky from falling upon the earth, unless by His permission. Indeed Allah, to the people, is Kind and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse reminds us of Allah's immense power and control over the universe. He has made everything on earth subservient to mankind for our benefit. The ships that sail the seas do so only by His command. He keeps the sky from falling upon the earth, which would destroy everything, except by His will. This demonstrates Allah's kindness and mercy towards humanity, providing us with all we need to live and protecting us from harm, even though we may not always acknowledge or appreciate it. It encourages us to be grateful for Allah's blessings and recognize His dominion over all creation.
orig: ألم تر أن الله سخر لكم ما في الأرض والفلك تجري في البحر بأمره ويمسك السماء أن تقع على الأرض إلا بإذنه إن الله بالناس لرءوف رحيم

translation: And it is He who gave you life; then He causes you to die and then will [again] give you life. Indeed, mankind is ungrateful.
interpretation: This verse reminds us of the power and mercy of Allah. He is the One who has given us life, and He is the One who will cause us to die at the appointed time. But even more than that, He will resurrect us after death and give us a new, eternal life in the Hereafter. Despite these immense blessings and clear signs of Allah's ability, mankind is often ungrateful. We take the gift of life for granted and fail to appreciate the opportunity it provides us to worship and draw closer to our Creator. The verse is a wake-up call to recognize Allah's favors upon us and to strive to be among the grateful servants, rather than the ungrateful ones who will regret their heedlessness on the Day of Judgment.
orig: وهو الذي أحياكم ثم يميتكم ثم يحييكم إن الإنسان لكفور

translation: For every nation We have appointed rites which they perform. So, [O Muhammad], let them not dispute with you over the matter but invite them to your Lord. Indeed, you are upon straight guidance.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that every community has its own religious rites and practices, which they should adhere to. It instructs Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) not to engage in arguments with those who dispute the validity of Islamic practices. Instead, he should continue inviting people to the path of Allah, as he is on the right guidance. The verse highlights the importance of focusing on one's own spiritual journey and not being distracted by the criticism or disagreements of others, while still conveying the message of Islam with wisdom and patience.
orig: لكل أمة جعلنا منسكا هم ناسكوه فلا ينازعنك في الأمر وادع إلى ربك إنك لعلى هدى مستقيم

translation: And if they argue with you, say, "Allah is most knowing of what you do."
interpretation: This verse instructs the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) on how to respond to those who argue or debate with him regarding religious matters. It emphasizes that ultimately, Allah is the One who knows the true intentions and actions of people, even if they try to conceal them or present them in a certain way. The Prophet is advised to remind them of Allah's all-encompassing knowledge, which should serve as a warning for them to be sincere in their intentions and deeds, as nothing escapes His sight. It also implies that arguing or debating excessively is futile, as the final judgment rests with Allah, who will hold everyone accountable for their actions.
orig: وإن جادلوك فقل الله أعلم بما تعملون

translation: Allah will judge between you on the Day of Resurrection concerning that over which you used to differ.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that all disputes and differences that arise between people in this worldly life will ultimately be judged and resolved by Allah on the Day of Judgment. It serves as a reminder that humans should not become too attached to their own opinions and disagreements, as the final truth and justice will be established by Allah in the Hereafter. The verse encourages humility, open-mindedness, and a focus on pleasing Allah rather than insisting on one's own views in matters of faith.
orig: الله يحكم بينكم يوم القيامة فيما كنتم فيه تختلفون

translation: Do you not know that Allah knows what is in the heaven and earth? Indeed, that is in a Record. Indeed that, for Allah, is easy.
interpretation: This verse reminds us of Allah's infinite knowledge and power. It emphasizes that nothing is hidden from Him, whether it is in the heavens or on the earth. All things are recorded in a divine record, and it is effortless for Allah to have such comprehensive knowledge. This should instill in believers a sense of awe and consciousness that Allah is always aware of their actions, thoughts, and intentions. It encourages them to strive for righteousness and refrain from wrongdoing, knowing that nothing escapes Allah's knowledge and that they will be held accountable for their deeds.
orig: ألم تعلم أن الله يعلم ما في السماء والأرض إن ذلك في كتاب إن ذلك على الله يسير

translation: And they worship other than Allah that which He has not sent down authority for, and that which they have no knowledge of. And there will not be for the wrongdoers any helper.
interpretation: This verse criticizes those who worship false deities and idols instead of Allah, without any divine authority or proof to justify their worship. It suggests that such people are following baseless traditions or their own whims rather than authentic divine guidance. The verse warns that those who engage in such wrongdoing and idolatry will have no helper or supporter to save them from Allah's punishment in the Hereafter. It emphasizes the gravity of ascribing partners to Allah and worshipping others besides Him, as it is a form of oppression against one's own soul and a violation of the fundamental right of Allah to be worshipped exclusively.
orig: ويعبدون من دون الله ما لم ينزل به سلطانا وما ليس لهم به علم وما للظالمين من نصير

translation: And when Our verses are recited to them as clear evidences, you recognize in the faces of those who disbelieve denial. They are almost on the verge of assaulting those who recite to them Our verses. Say, "Then shall I inform you of [what is] worse than that? [It is] the Fire which Allah has promised those who disbelieve, and wretched is the destination."
interpretation: This verse highlights the intense hostility and resentment that the disbelievers harbor towards the clear revelations of Allah. Their faces reveal their deep aversion and denial of the truth when they hear the Qur'anic verses being recited to them. Their animosity is so severe that they are on the verge of physically attacking the believers who convey Allah's message. However, Allah instructs the Prophet (peace be upon him) to warn them of a fate far worse than their current state of denial—the Fire of Hell, which Allah has promised to those who persistently disbelieve. This interpretation emphasizes the gravity of rejecting Allah's signs and the ultimate consequence of choosing disbelief over faith.
orig: وإذا تتلى عليهم آياتنا بينات تعرف في وجوه الذين كفروا المنكر يكادون يسطون بالذين يتلون عليهم آياتنا قل أفأنبئكم بشر من ذلكم النار وعدها الله الذين كفروا وبئس المصير

translation: O people, an example is presented, so listen to it. Indeed, those you invoke besides Allah will never create [as much as] a fly, even if they gathered together for that purpose. And if the fly should steal away from them a [tiny] thing, they could not recover it from him. Weak are the pursuer and pursued.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the powerlessness of false gods and idols that people worship besides Allah. It presents a vivid example that even if all these false gods were to come together, they would not be able to create something as insignificant as a fly. Moreover, if a fly were to take something away from them, they would be incapable of retrieving it. This highlights the weakness and helplessness of both the false gods and those who pursue them for help or intercession. The verse aims to make people realize the futility of worshipping anyone or anything besides Allah, who is the only true Creator and Supreme Power.
orig: يا أيها الناس ضرب مثل فاستمعوا له إن الذين تدعون من دون الله لن يخلقوا ذبابا ولو اجتمعوا له وإن يسلبهم الذباب شيئا لا يستنقذوه منه ضعف الطالب والمطلوب

translation: They have not appraised Allah with true appraisal. Indeed, Allah is Powerful and Exalted in Might.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the immense power and might of Allah, which humans often fail to comprehend or appreciate fully. It suggests that people tend to underestimate the true extent of Allah's capabilities and strength. The verse serves as a reminder for believers to recognize and acknowledge the absolute supremacy and omnipotence of Allah, as He is far beyond human understanding and imagination. It encourages humility and submission to Allah's will, as He is the ultimate authority and has control over all things in the universe.
orig: ما قدروا الله حق قدره إن الله لقوي عزيز

translation: Allah chooses from the angels messengers and from the people. Indeed, Allah is Hearing and Seeing.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's absolute authority and wisdom in selecting His messengers, both from among the angels and human beings. He chooses those who are most suitable for conveying His message and fulfilling His purpose. The mention of Allah being "Hearing and Seeing" underscores His omniscience and perfect awareness of all things, including the qualities and abilities of His chosen messengers. It also implies that Allah is fully aware of the actions and intentions of those to whom the message is delivered, and He will hold them accountable for their response to the truth.
orig: الله يصطفي من الملائكة رسلا ومن الناس إن الله سميع بصير

translation: He knows what is [presently] before them and what will be after them. And to Allah will be returned [all] matters.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the omniscience of Allah, who has knowledge of all things, past, present, and future. It also reminds us that ultimately, all affairs and matters will be returned to Allah for judgment and final decision. This highlights the importance of being mindful of our actions and intentions, as we will be held accountable for them in the end. The verse encourages believers to trust in Allah's wisdom and submit to His will, knowing that He is aware of all things and that all matters will eventually return to Him.
orig: يعلم ما بين أيديهم وما خلفهم وإلى الله ترجع الأمور

translation: O you who have believed, bow and prostrate and worship your Lord and do good - that you may succeed.
interpretation: This verse is a call to the believers to engage in acts of worship and righteousness. Bowing and prostrating are two essential components of the Muslim prayer, representing submission and humility before Allah. Worshipping Allah involves not only the ritual acts of prayer but also living one's life in accordance with His commands and guidance. Doing good encompasses all acts of kindness, charity, and service to others. The verse emphasizes that by consistently engaging in these acts of worship and righteousness, believers may attain success and felicity both in this world and in the Hereafter. It is a reminder that true success lies in living a life dedicated to pleasing Allah and benefiting His creation.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا اركعوا واسجدوا واعبدوا ربكم وافعلوا الخير لعلكم تفلحون

translation: And strive for Allah with the striving due to Him. He has chosen you and has not placed upon you in the religion any difficulty. [It is] the religion of your father, Abraham. Allah named you "Muslims" before [in former scriptures] and in this [revelation] that the Messenger may be a witness over you and you may be witnesses over the people. So establish prayer and give zakah and hold fast to Allah. He is your protector; and excellent is the protector, and excellent is the helper.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of striving in the way of Allah with sincere dedication and effort. It reminds believers that Allah has chosen them and has not burdened them with hardship in religion, as it is the same religion followed by Prophet Abraham. The verse also highlights the role of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) as a witness over the believers, and the believers' role as witnesses over humanity. It encourages Muslims to establish prayer, give charity, and hold fast to Allah, who is their protector and helper. The verse underscores the significance of remaining steadfast in faith and fulfilling one's religious obligations with devotion and sincerity.
orig: وجاهدوا في الله حق جهاده هو اجتباكم وما جعل عليكم في الدين من حرج ملة أبيكم إبراهيم هو سماكم المسلمين من قبل وفي هذا ليكون الرسول شهيدا عليكم وتكونوا شهداء على الناس فأقيموا الصلاة وآتوا الزكاة واعتصموا بالله هو مولاكم فنعم المولى ونعم النصير

translation: Certainly will the believers have succeeded:
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that true believers who possess sincere faith and perform righteous deeds will attain success, felicity, and salvation in this world and the Hereafter. It serves as a reassurance and glad tidings to those who strive to uphold their faith and live according to the teachings of Islam, indicating that their efforts will be rewarded with the ultimate triumph of entering Paradise and earning Allah's pleasure. The verse sets the tone for the subsequent verses, which outline the qualities and characteristics of the successful believers.
orig: قد أفلح المؤمنون

translation: Those who are humble in their prayers
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of humility and concentration during prayer. Those who are truly devoted to Allah are those who approach prayer with a sense of reverence, humility, and full attentiveness. They are not distracted by worldly matters, but instead focus their hearts and minds entirely on connecting with their Creator. This humble attitude reflects their deep faith and sincerity. The verse suggests that the quality of one's prayer is not judged by outward appearances or eloquent recitation, but by the inner state of the heart and the level of spiritual engagement. Humility in prayer is a sign of true submission to Allah's will.
orig: الذين هم في صلاتهم خاشعون

translation: And those who turn away from ill speech
interpretation: This verse praises those who avoid engaging in or listening to vain, useless, or inappropriate speech. They turn away from conversations or situations that involve gossip, slander, obscenity, or anything that displeases Allah. Instead, they focus on what is beneficial and good. This demonstrates their consciousness of Allah, their self-discipline, and their commitment to purifying their hearts and tongues. It is a characteristic of the believers who are mindful of their actions and strive to please Allah in all aspects of their lives.
orig: والذين هم عن اللغو معرضون

translation: And those who are doers of zakah
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of giving zakah, which is a mandatory charity in Islam. It refers to those who actively fulfill this obligation and give a portion of their wealth to those in need. The verse suggests that giving zakah is a key characteristic of the righteous believers. It highlights the significance of social responsibility and the redistribution of wealth in Islamic society. By giving zakah, believers purify their wealth, support the less fortunate, and demonstrate their obedience to Allah's commands. The verse implies that those who consistently give zakah are among the successful and pious servants of Allah.
orig: والذين هم للزكاة فاعلون

translation: And those who guard their private parts
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of chastity and modesty in Islam. It refers to those believers who protect their sexual desires and refrain from any unlawful sexual activity outside of marriage. They guard their private parts from being exposed or engaged in sinful acts. This is a sign of their righteousness, self-control, and obedience to Allah's commands. Guarding one's chastity is essential for maintaining the purity of the soul and the well-being of society. It is a virtue that is highly valued in Islam and is a characteristic of true believers who seek to please Allah and follow His guidance in all aspects of their lives.
orig: والذين هم لفروجهم حافظون

translation: Except with their wives or those ˹bondwomen˺ in their possession, for then they are free from blame,
interpretation: This verse establishes the boundaries of sexual relations in Islam. It states that sexual relations are only permissible within the confines of marriage or with women who are legally owned as concubines or slaves (a practice that was prevalent in the past but is no longer applicable). Outside of these two scenarios, any sexual activity is considered sinful and blameworthy. This verse emphasizes the importance of maintaining chastity and limiting sexual relations to what is lawful in Islam. It also implies that within marriage or legal ownership, consensual sexual relations are permissible and not a cause for blame or sin.
orig: إلا على أزواجهم أو ما ملكت أيمانهم فإنهم غير ملومين

translation: But whoever seeks beyond that, then those are the transgressors.
interpretation: This verse is emphasizing the importance of staying within the boundaries and limits set by Allah. Those who seek to go beyond what has been permitted or prescribed are considered transgressors. They have overstepped the limits and have disobeyed Allah's commands. The verse serves as a warning against exceeding the boundaries of what is lawful and permissible, as doing so would be an act of transgression and would incur Allah's displeasure and punishment. Muslims should strive to stay within the limits of what Allah has allowed and avoid falling into transgression.
orig: فمن ابتغى وراء ذلك فأولئك هم العادون

translation: And those who are faithful to their trusts and their covenant
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of being trustworthy and fulfilling one's obligations. It highlights that the righteous believers are those who faithfully uphold the trusts and responsibilities placed upon them, whether it pertains to the rights of Allah or the rights of other people. They are reliable in keeping their promises, honoring their contracts, and maintaining the confidentiality of what has been entrusted to them. This trait of being trustworthy and true to one's word is a fundamental characteristic of the believers and is highly valued in Islam.
orig: والذين هم لأماناتهم وعهدهم راعون

translation: And those who carefully maintain their prayers.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of being diligent and consistent in performing the obligatory prayers. It highlights that the righteous believers are those who guard their prayers, perform them on time, and do so with sincerity and devotion. They prioritize their prayers and do not allow worldly matters to distract them from this fundamental pillar of Islam. The verse suggests that maintaining prayers is a key characteristic of the believers and a sign of their faith and submission to Allah.
orig: والذين هم على صلواتهم يحافظون

translation: Those are the inheritors
interpretation: This verse refers to the righteous believers who will inherit Paradise in the Hereafter. They are the ones who have fulfilled their duties towards Allah and followed His commandments. As a result of their faith and good deeds, they will be granted the ultimate reward of eternal bliss in the Gardens of Paradise, where they will dwell forever as the inheritors of the greatest blessing from their Lord. This inheritance signifies their success and triumph in the life to come, as they will be among the fortunate ones who will enjoy the proximity and pleasure of Allah.
orig: أولئك هم الوارثون

translation: Those who inherit Paradise, they will abide therein eternally.
interpretation: This verse speaks about the ultimate reward for the righteous believers - inheriting Paradise and dwelling there forever. It emphasizes the eternal nature of the reward, indicating that once a person enters Paradise, they will never leave it or experience death again. The verse gives hope and encouragement to the believers to strive for this ultimate goal and not be distracted by the temporary pleasures of this worldly life. It also highlights the mercy and generosity of Allah in granting such an immense and everlasting reward to His faithful servants.
orig: الذين يرثون الفردوس هم فيها خالدون

translation: And indeed, We created man from an extract of clay.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the humble origins of mankind. It reminds us that despite our achievements and abilities, we were created from a lowly substance - clay. This should instill humility and prevent arrogance or self-aggrandizement. It also points to the creative power of God, who fashioned the marvel of the human being starting from such a simple material. The verse encourages introspection about our nature, our purpose, and our relationship with our Creator.
orig: ولقد خلقنا الإنسان من سلالة من طين

translation: Then We placed him as a sperm-drop in a firm lodging.
interpretation: This verse refers to the early stages of human development, where God places the fertilized egg (the sperm-drop) in the womb of the mother. The "firm lodging" mentioned here is the womb, which provides a safe and nurturing environment for the developing embryo. This interpretation highlights the intricate process of human creation and the care taken by God in ensuring the proper development of the fetus in the mother's womb, emphasizing the miraculous nature of human life and the power and wisdom of the Creator.
orig: ثم جعلناه نطفة في قرار مكين

translation: Then We made the sperm-drop into a clinging clot, and We made the clot into a lump [of flesh], and We made [from] the lump, bones, and We covered the bones with flesh; then We developed him into another creation. So blessed is Allah, the best of creators.
interpretation: This verse describes the miraculous process of human development in the womb, showing Allah's power and wisdom in creating life. It emphasizes that after the initial stages of the embryo's growth from a sperm-drop to a clinging clot and a lump of flesh, Allah fashions bones and covers them with flesh, bringing forth a new creation. This transformation is a testament to Allah's supreme creative ability, making Him the best of all creators. The verse invites reflection on the miracle of human life and encourages gratitude towards Allah for His blessings and the perfection of His creation.
orig: ثم خلقنا النطفة علقة فخلقنا العلقة مضغة فخلقنا المضغة عظاما فكسونا العظام لحما ثم أنشأناه خلقا آخر فتبارك الله أحسن الخالقين

translation: Then indeed, after that you will surely die.
interpretation: This verse is a reminder of the inevitability of death. It emphasizes that regardless of one's actions or beliefs in this worldly life, every soul will eventually taste death. This serves as a wake-up call for humans to reflect on their purpose and to strive for righteousness before it is too late. The verse also implies the existence of an afterlife, as death is mentioned as a transition rather than an end. It encourages believers to focus on the eternal life to come and to use their limited time in this world wisely in preparation for the Day of Judgment.
orig: ثم إنكم بعد ذلك لميتون

translation: Then indeed you, on the Day of Resurrection, will be resurrected.
interpretation: This verse affirms the Islamic belief in the resurrection of the dead on the Day of Judgment. It emphasizes that after death, all humans will be brought back to life by Allah to face the consequences of their deeds in this world. The verse serves as a reminder for believers to lead a righteous life, knowing that they will be held accountable for their actions in the Hereafter. It also provides hope and consolation to those who face hardships and injustices in this world, assuring them that ultimate justice will be served in the afterlife.
orig: ثم إنكم يوم القيامة تبعثون

translation: And indeed, We have created above you seven layered heavens, and never have We been of [Our] creation unaware.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's omniscience and His role as the Creator of the universe. The "seven layered heavens" refer to the vastness and complexity of the cosmos, highlighting the intricate design and order in Allah's creation. The verse also asserts that Allah is not oblivious to His creation; rather, He is constantly aware of and attentive to every aspect of it. This interpretation underscores the idea that the universe is not a product of chance but a deliberate and purposeful creation by an all-knowing, all-powerful Creator who continues to oversee and maintain His creation.
orig: ولقد خلقنا فوقكم سبع طرائق وما كنا عن الخلق غافلين

translation: And We have sent down rain from the sky in a measured amount and settled it in the earth. And indeed, We are Able to take it away.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's power and control over the natural world. He sends down rain in precise, measured quantities according to His wisdom and knowledge of what the earth needs. This rain allows vegetation to grow and sustains life. But just as easily as Allah gives this blessing, He can also take it away if He wills. This serves as a reminder for humankind to be grateful for the bounties Allah provides and to recognize that He can withhold them at any time. It also points to the temporary nature of the life of this world and encourages us to place our ultimate reliance on Allah alone.
orig: وأنزلنا من السماء ماء بقدر فأسكناه في الأرض وإنا على ذهاب به لقادرون

translation: And We have brought forth for you thereby gardens of palm trees and grapevines; you have therein abundant fruits, and from them you eat.
interpretation: This verse highlights God's bounty and grace upon humankind. He has caused gardens of date-palms and grapevines to grow, providing people with abundant fruit as a means of sustenance. It is a reminder for humans to be grateful for the provisions bestowed upon them by their Creator. The gardens and fruits mentioned are a symbol of God's favor and a sign of His power to bring forth life and provide for His creation. The verse encourages contemplation on these blessings and should inspire thankfulness to the One who grants them.
orig: فأنشأنا لكم به جنات من نخيل وأعناب لكم فيها فواكه كثيرة ومنها تأكلون

translation: And a tree that grows from Mount Sinai which produces oil and a condiment for those who eat.
interpretation: This verse is referring to the olive tree, which is native to the region around Mount Sinai. The olive tree is a symbol of blessings, prosperity, and peace in the Qur'an. The oil produced by the olive tree has many beneficial uses, both as a food and as a source of light. The "condiment" mentioned in the verse is likely referring to the olive fruit itself, which can be eaten as a food. The fact that the olive tree is specifically mentioned as growing from Mount Sinai is significant, as Mount Sinai is the place where Moses received revelation from Allah. Thus, the olive tree is a reminder of Allah's blessings and the importance of revelation in guiding humanity.
orig: وشجرة تخرج من طور سيناء تنبت بالدهن وصبغ للآكلين

translation: And indeed, for you in the cattle is a lesson. We give you drink from what is in their bellies, and for you in them are numerous benefits, and from them you eat.
interpretation: This verse highlights the blessings and benefits that Allah has bestowed upon mankind through cattle. It reminds us to reflect upon the miraculous nature of these creatures, which provide us with sustenance in the form of milk, meat, and other resources. The verse also emphasizes the importance of gratitude and acknowledging the numerous ways in which Allah has provided for our needs. It encourages us to contemplate the intricate systems and processes within the creation, such as the production of milk in the bellies of cattle, as signs of Allah's power and mercy. By recognizing these blessings, we are encouraged to develop a deeper appreciation for Allah's favors and to use these resources responsibly and with gratitude.
orig: وإن لكم في الأنعام لعبرة نسقيكم مما في بطونها ولكم فيها منافع كثيرة ومنها تأكلون

translation: And upon the ships you are carried.
interpretation: This verse is a reminder of Allah's favor upon humanity, as He has subjugated the means of transportation for our benefit, including the ships that sail across the seas and oceans. It encourages us to reflect on the blessings we often take for granted and to be grateful for the ease and convenience that Allah has provided us in our journeys. The verse also alludes to the idea that just as we are carried by ships, we are ultimately dependent on Allah's support and guidance in all aspects of our lives.
orig: وعليها وعلى الفلك تحملون

translation: And indeed, We sent Noah to his people, and he said, "O my people, worship Allah; you have no deity other than Him. Then will you not fear Him?"
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of worshipping Allah alone and abandoning all false deities. It serves as a reminder that Allah is the only true God worthy of worship and that fearing Him and obeying His commands is essential for attaining salvation. The verse also highlights the role of prophets, such as Noah, in conveying this message to their people and guiding them towards the path of righteousness. It implies that those who reject this message and continue to worship false gods will face the consequences of their actions in the Hereafter.
orig: ولقد أرسلنا نوحا إلى قومه فقال يا قوم اعبدوا الله ما لكم من إله غيره أفلا تتقون

translation: But the eminent ones who disbelieved among his people said, "This is not but a man like yourselves who wishes to take precedence over you. And if Allah had willed [to send a messenger], He would have sent down angels. We have not heard of this among our forefathers."
interpretation: This verse reflects the skepticism and disbelief of the leaders among Prophet Noah's people. They rejected his message, arguing that he was just an ordinary human being like them, and accused him of seeking superiority over them. They reasoned that if God truly wanted to send a messenger, He would have sent angels instead. They also claimed that this message was unheard of among their ancestors, suggesting that it went against their traditional beliefs. This interpretation highlights the common arguments used by those who oppose divine messages, such as questioning the messenger's authority, expecting supernatural signs, and adhering to ancestral traditions rather than considering the truth of the message itself.
orig: فقال الملأ الذين كفروا من قومه ما هذا إلا بشر مثلكم يريد أن يتفضل عليكم ولو شاء الله لأنزل ملائكة ما سمعنا بهذا في آبائنا الأولين

translation: He is not but a man possessed with madness, so wait for him for a time.
interpretation: This verse suggests that the disbelievers accused the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) of being possessed by madness or insanity, rather than accepting his message as divine revelation. They are advised to observe him for a period of time, implying that his consistency, wisdom, and noble character would become evident, disproving their accusations. It highlights the patience and resilience required of the Prophet in facing such opposition and continuing to convey the message of Islam despite the challenges.
orig: إن هو إلا رجل به جنة فتربصوا به حتى حين

translation: He said, "My Lord, support me because they deny me."
interpretation: In this verse, the prophet is seeking Allah's help and support against those who reject his message and deny him. It shows the prophet's complete reliance and trust in Allah in the face of adversity and opposition. The prophet turns to Allah alone for aid, knowing that only He can provide the necessary assistance and strength to overcome the challenges posed by the disbelievers. This verse highlights the importance of turning to Allah in times of difficulty and trusting in His support and guidance.
orig: قال رب انصرني بما كذبون

translation: So We inspired him (saying): "Construct the ship under Our Eyes and under Our Revelation (guidance). Then, when Our Command comes, and the oven gushes forth water, take on board of each kind two (male and female), and your family, except those thereof against whom the Word has already gone forth. And address Me not in favour of those who have done wrong. Verily, they are to be drowned.
interpretation: This verse is a command from Allah to Prophet Noah to build an ark under divine guidance and supervision. It also instructs Noah to take on board pairs of every animal species and his family members, except those who were destined to be drowned due to their wrongdoings and disbelief. The verse emphasizes the importance of following divine instructions and the consequences of disobedience and wrongdoing. It also highlights the concept of divine retribution and the ultimate fate of those who reject faith and engage in evil deeds.
orig: فأوحينا إليه أن اصنع الفلك بأعيننا ووحينا فإذا جاء أمرنا وفار التنور فاسلك فيها من كل زوجين اثنين وأهلك إلا من سبق عليه القول منهم ولا تخاطبني في الذين ظلموا إنهم مغرقون

translation: And when you and those with you have boarded the ship, then say, "[All] praise is [due] to Allah, who has saved us from the wrongdoing people."
interpretation: This verse is a reminder to be grateful to Allah for His protection and deliverance from difficult situations or oppressive people. It encourages the believer to acknowledge and praise Allah's favor and mercy, especially after being saved from danger or hardship. The verse also implies that one should attribute success and safety to Allah alone, recognizing that it is through His grace and help that we overcome challenges. Gratitude is a key theme, highlighting the importance of thanking Allah for His blessings and interventions in our lives.
orig: فإذا استويت أنت ومن معك على الفلك فقل الحمد لله الذي نجانا من القوم الظالمين

translation: And say, "My Lord, let me land at a blessed landing place, and You are the best to accommodate [us]."
interpretation: This verse is a prayer for guidance and blessings from Allah. It teaches us to seek Allah's help in all our endeavors and to trust in His wisdom and mercy. The "blessed landing place" can be interpreted as a metaphor for a successful outcome or a favorable situation in life. By asking Allah to be the one to "accommodate" us, we acknowledge that He is the ultimate provider and sustainer, and that all good things come from Him. This verse encourages humility, gratitude, and reliance on Allah in all aspects of our lives.
orig: وقل رب أنزلني منزلا مباركا وأنت خير المنزلين

translation: Indeed in that are signs, and indeed, We are testing [Our servants].
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the events and phenomena mentioned in the preceding verses are clear signs of Allah's power, wisdom, and control over His creation. It also highlights that Allah tests His servants through various means, such as blessings, hardships, and trials, to assess their faith, patience, and gratitude. The verse serves as a reminder for believers to recognize the signs of Allah in the world around them and to remain steadfast in their faith, knowing that they will be tested throughout their lives. It encourages introspection and the understanding that the challenges faced in life are ultimately a means of spiritual growth and a way to attain closeness to Allah.
orig: إن في ذلك لآيات وإن كنا لمبتلين

translation: Then We produced after them another generation.
interpretation: This verse refers to the continuous cycle of creation and destruction of nations and civilizations. It emphasizes that after Allah destroys a nation due to its transgressions and disbelief, He replaces them with another generation of people. This new generation is given a chance to learn from the mistakes of the previous ones and to follow the right path. The verse serves as a reminder of Allah's supreme power over His creation and the consequences of disobeying His commands. It also highlights the importance of learning from history and striving to be among the righteous servants of Allah to avoid a similar fate.
orig: ثم أنشأنا من بعدهم قرنا آخرين

translation: So We sent among them a messenger from themselves, [saying], "Worship Allah; you have no deity other than Him. Then will you not fear Him?"
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of worshipping Allah alone and fearing Him. It shows that Allah sends messengers from among the people themselves to guide them to the right path. The messenger's role is to remind people that there is no god worthy of worship except Allah and that they should fear Him and obey His commands. The verse also implies that those who reject the message and continue to worship false deities lack understanding and fail to recognize the consequences of their actions in the Hereafter.
orig: فأرسلنا فيهم رسولا منهم أن اعبدوا الله ما لكم من إله غيره أفلا تتقون

translation: And the eminent among his people who disbelieved and denied the meeting of the Hereafter while We had given them luxury in the worldly life said, "This is not but a man like yourselves. He eats of that from which you eat and drinks of what you drink."
interpretation: This verse highlights the arrogance and disbelief of the wealthy and influential members of society who reject the message of the Prophet and the concept of the Hereafter. They view the Prophet as a mere mortal, no different from themselves, and fail to recognize his divine mission. Their attachment to worldly pleasures and luxuries has blinded them to the truth, causing them to deny the existence of an afterlife where they will be held accountable for their actions. The verse emphasizes the importance of humility, faith, and the realization that worldly status and affluence are temporary and should not hinder one's belief in the divine message and the Hereafter.
orig: وقال الملأ من قومه الذين كفروا وكذبوا بلقاء الآخرة وأترفناهم في الحياة الدنيا ما هذا إلا بشر مثلكم يأكل مما تأكلون منه ويشرب مما تشربون

translation: And if you obey a human being like yourselves, then you will surely be losers.
interpretation: This verse warns against following the commands or desires of other human beings instead of the guidance of Allah. It emphasizes that obeying someone who is just like you, with the same weaknesses and limitations, will only lead to loss and failure in this life and the hereafter. The implication is that true success lies in submitting to Allah alone and adhering to His commands as revealed in the Qur'an and taught by His Prophet (peace be upon him). Blindly following other people, no matter their status or authority, at the expense of one's faith and obedience to Allah is a path to spiritual ruin.
orig: ولئن أطعتم بشرا مثلكم إنكم إذا لخاسرون

translation: Does he promise you that when you have died and become dust and bones that you will be brought forth [once more]?
interpretation: This verse is questioning the belief in resurrection after death. It suggests that it seems implausible or unlikely for humans to be brought back to life after they have died and their bodies have decomposed into dust and bones. The tone expresses skepticism towards the idea of being resurrected and restored from such a state of complete physical deterioration. It prompts reflection on the power of God to recreate and bring forth life again even after the body has completely disintegrated, which is a central tenet of belief in the Hereafter in Islam.
orig: أيعدكم أنكم إذا متم وكنتم ترابا وعظاما أنكم مخرجون

translation: How far, how far is that which you are promised!
interpretation: This verse is expressing the idea that the Day of Judgment and the promises of the Hereafter are very distant and far off from the present reality. It conveys a sense of the immense gap between the current worldly life and the eventual consequences and outcomes that have been foretold to occur in the afterlife. The repetition of "how far" emphasizes the vast distance and remoteness of these future events, suggesting that they may seem almost unimaginable or unbelievable from the limited human perspective in the present.
orig: هيهات هيهات لما توعدون

translation: It is not but our worldly life - we die and live, but we will not be resurrected.
interpretation: This verse reflects the belief of those who deny the afterlife and resurrection. They think that this worldly life is all there is, and that death is the ultimate end. They believe in the cycle of life and death in this world, but reject the idea of being brought back to life after death for judgment. This mindset is a reflection of a materialistic worldview that fails to acknowledge the existence of a higher power and the accountability of humans in the Hereafter.
orig: إن هي إلا حياتنا الدنيا نموت ونحيا وما نحن بمبعوثين

translation: He is not but a man who has invented a lie about Allah, and we will not believe him.
interpretation: This verse is referring to those who reject the message of Islam and accuse the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) of fabricating lies about Allah. It emphasizes that the Prophet is only a human being who has been chosen by Allah to convey His message, and that he is not making up falsehoods. The verse also expresses the firm conviction of the believers in not accepting such accusations and remaining steadfast in their faith.
orig: إن هو إلا رجل افترى على الله كذبا وما نحن له بمؤمنين

translation: He said, "My Lord, support me because they have denied me."
interpretation: In this verse, the prophet is calling upon Allah for help and support against those who have rejected his message and denied him. It shows the prophet's complete reliance and trust in Allah in the face of adversity and opposition. The verse highlights the importance of turning to Allah for aid when facing difficulties, especially when it comes to matters of faith and conveying the divine message. It also demonstrates the prophet's perseverance and determination to continue his mission despite the challenges and denials he faced from his people.
orig: قال رب انصرني بما كذبون

translation: He said: "In a little while they will surely become regretful."
interpretation: This verse is a warning from Allah that those who reject His message and oppose His messenger will soon come to regret their actions. It implies that the consequences of their disbelief and disobedience will catch up with them, and they will feel remorse for not having followed the truth when they had the chance. The phrase "in a little while" suggests that their regret is inevitable and will afflict them sooner rather than later. It is a reminder that the time to repent and turn to Allah is now, before it is too late and one has to face the outcome of their choices in this life and the Hereafter.
orig: قال عما قليل ليصبحن نادمين

translation: So the shriek seized them in truth, and We made them as rubbish of dead leaves. So away with the wrongdoing people.
interpretation: This verse is a warning and a reminder of the consequences of rejecting the truth and being unjust. It shows that those who persist in wrongdoing and deny the messages of God will ultimately face a terrible fate. The "shriek" represents a sudden and overwhelming punishment that will seize them as a result of their misdeeds. They will be reduced to worthless remnants, like scattered, decaying leaves. The verse emphasizes God's justice and the inevitability of consequences for evil actions. It also contains a prayer for the removal and distancing of those who are cruel and unjust, expressing the desire to be disassociated from wrongdoers and their ultimate end.
orig: فأخذتهم الصيحة بالحق فجعلناهم غثاء فبعدا للقوم الظالمين

translation: Then We produced after them other generations.
interpretation: This verse points to the continuous cycle of creation and the rise and fall of civilizations throughout human history. It indicates that after the destruction or decline of one group of people, Allah brings forth new generations to populate the earth. This serves as a reminder of the transient nature of worldly existence and the ultimate power and control of Allah over His creation. It also implies that no matter how powerful or advanced a civilization may become, it will eventually be succeeded by others in accordance with the divine plan.
orig: ثم أنشأنا من بعدهم قرونا آخرين

translation: No nation can hasten its term, nor can they delay it.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the idea of divine predestination and the ultimate power of Allah over the affairs of nations and civilizations. It suggests that every nation has a fixed lifespan or term (ajal) decreed by Allah, and that this term cannot be hastened or delayed by any means. The rise and fall of nations, as well as their ultimate fate, are determined by Allah's will and wisdom, and human beings have no control over these matters. This verse serves as a reminder for people to submit to Allah's will, to make the most of their given time, and to realize that the destiny of nations lies in the hands of the Almighty.
orig: ما تسبق من أمة أجلها وما يستأخرون

translation: Then We sent Our messengers in succession. Every time there came to a nation their messenger, they denied him, so We made them follow one another [to destruction], and We made them narrations. So away with a people who do not believe.
interpretation: This verse highlights the pattern of nations rejecting the messengers sent to them by Allah. Despite the clear signs and warnings brought by the messengers, these nations persisted in their disbelief and denial. As a consequence of their obstinacy, Allah caused these nations to be destroyed one after another, making their stories a lesson and a warning for future generations. The verse emphasizes that such a fate awaits those who choose not to believe in the divine message and the messengers sent by Allah. It serves as a reminder of the importance of faith and the consequences of rejecting the truth.
orig: ثم أرسلنا رسلنا تترى كل ما جاء أمة رسولها كذبوه فأتبعنا بعضهم بعضا وجعلناهم أحاديث فبعدا لقوم لا يؤمنون

translation: Then We sent Moses and his brother Aaron with Our signs and a clear authority,
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine mission of Moses and his brother Aaron, who were sent by God to guide the people and establish His message on earth. The "signs" mentioned here refer to the miracles and proofs that God bestowed upon them to validate their prophethood and convince others of the truth they brought. The "clear authority" points to the compelling evidence and arguments they presented, leaving no room for doubt about the authenticity of their message. This verse emphasizes the importance of prophethood in delivering God's guidance to humanity and the role of divine signs in supporting the prophets' mission.
orig: ثم أرسلنا موسى وأخاه هارون بآياتنا وسلطان مبين

translation: To Pharaoh and his establishment, but they were arrogant and were a haughty people.
interpretation: This verse highlights the arrogance and pride of Pharaoh and his people when they were confronted with the message of Allah delivered by Moses. Despite the clear signs and evidence presented to them, they refused to humble themselves and submit to the truth. Their haughtiness and self-importance prevented them from accepting the guidance of Allah. This serves as a warning to all of us to guard against arrogance and to always remain humble before our Creator, no matter our status or position in this worldly life. Arrogance is a destructive trait that can lead to our downfall both in this life and the hereafter.
orig: إلى فرعون وملئه فاستكبروا وكانوا قوما عالين

translation: But they said, "Should we believe two men like ourselves, while their people are servants to us?"
interpretation: This verse reflects the arrogance and pride of the disbelievers who rejected the message of the prophets sent to them. They considered themselves superior to the prophets and their followers, as they saw them as mere servants or slaves. The disbelievers used their perceived social status and power as a justification to reject the divine message, rather than evaluating its truth based on its merits. This highlights the importance of humility and open-mindedness when seeking the truth, and not allowing one's ego or social position to cloud their judgment.
orig: فقالوا أنؤمن لبشرين مثلنا وقومهما لنا عابدون

translation: But they denied them both, so they were of those who were destroyed.
interpretation: This verse warns of the consequences of denying and rejecting the messages and warnings sent by Allah through His prophets. Those who persist in disbelief and refuse to heed the signs and guidance provided to them will ultimately face destruction and ruin, both in this world and in the Hereafter. It emphasizes the importance of faith, obedience, and heeding the call of the prophets to avoid being among the lost and destroyed ones.
orig: فكذبوهما فكانوا من المهلكين

translation: And We had certainly given Moses the Scripture that perhaps they would be guided.
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine wisdom behind revealing the Torah to Prophet Moses. The purpose was to provide guidance to the Children of Israel, so that they may find the right path in life and follow God's commandments. It implies that the Scripture is a means of guidance, a light that shows the way to righteousness and helps people avoid misguidance and error. The verse also suggests that it is ultimately up to individuals to make use of this guidance and choose the path of faith and obedience to God.
orig: ولقد آتينا موسى الكتاب لعلهم يهتدون

translation: And We made the son of Mary and his mother a sign and sheltered them within a high ground having level [areas] and flowing water.
interpretation: This verse highlights the miraculous birth and life of Jesus and his mother Mary as a sign of God's power and mercy. God protected and provided for them, giving them refuge in a place of comfort and abundance. This can be interpreted as a metaphor for the spiritual sanctuary and blessings that God provides for His righteous servants. It also emphasizes the special status of Jesus and Mary in Islam as chosen and honored individuals, while affirming that Jesus is not divine but a human prophet born miraculously to a virtuous mother.
orig: وجعلنا ابن مريم وأمه آية وآويناهما إلى ربوة ذات قرار ومعين

translation: O messengers, eat from the good foods and work righteousness. Indeed, I, of what you do, am Knowing.
interpretation: This verse is a reminder to the messengers of Allah to partake in what is lawful and pure, both in terms of food and deeds. It emphasizes the importance of righteous actions and that Allah is fully aware of all that they do. The verse encourages the messengers to lead by example, consuming wholesome things and engaging in good works, as this aligns with their role as guides for mankind. It also serves as a reassurance that their efforts are acknowledged by Allah, who possesses infinite knowledge of their actions and intentions.
orig: يا أيها الرسل كلوا من الطيبات واعملوا صالحا إني بما تعملون عليم

translation: And indeed this, your religion, is one religion, and I am your Lord, so fear Me.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the unity and universality of the true religion, which is submission to the One God. It reminds believers that they all belong to a single spiritual community, regardless of their diverse backgrounds or nationalities. The verse also stresses the importance of having consciousness of God (taqwa) and being mindful of one's actions and intentions, as God is the ultimate authority and judge. It serves as a call for unity among believers based on their shared faith and devotion to the Almighty.
orig: وإن هذه أمتكم أمة واحدة وأنا ربكم فاتقون

translation: But they have broken their religion among them into sects, each group rejoicing in what it has.
interpretation: This verse is referring to the divisions and disagreements that have arisen within religion, leading to the formation of various sects or groups. Each group is pleased and content with their own beliefs and practices, feeling that they are the ones who are correct. This fragmentation of religion into competing sects is seen as a negative development, as it goes against the idea of unity and cohesion within the faith. The verse suggests that people have allowed their differences to divide them, rather than focusing on what unites them under the banner of their shared religion. It is a reminder to strive for unity and avoid the pitfalls of sectarianism and factionalism within religious communities.
orig: فتقطعوا أمرهم بينهم زبرا كل حزب بما لديهم فرحون

translation: So leave them in their confusion for a time.
interpretation: This verse is a command from Allah to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) to leave the disbelievers and those who reject the truth in their state of confusion, misguidance, and heedlessness until a later time that Allah has decreed. It implies that the Prophet should not be disheartened by their rejection and should continue his mission of conveying the message, knowing that Allah will deal with them in due time according to His wisdom and justice. It also serves as a reminder to the believers to focus on their own faith and actions, and not be overly concerned with those who persist in disbelief.
orig: فذرهم في غمرتهم حتى حين

translation: Do they think that what We extend to them of wealth and children
interpretation: This verse is questioning the belief of those who think that the wealth and children that Allah has bestowed upon them are signs of His favor and approval of their actions. The Qur'an is pointing out that these worldly blessings are not necessarily indicative of Allah's pleasure or a reward for righteousness. Rather, they may be a test or a means of leading one further astray if not used properly in accordance with Allah's guidance. The verse reminds us not to be deluded by material prosperity, but to focus on our spiritual state and whether we are using Allah's blessings to draw closer to Him or not.
orig: أيحسبون أنما نمدهم به من مال وبنين

translation: We hasten to them in good things? Rather, they do not perceive.
interpretation: This verse suggests that God bestows blessings and good things upon people, even though they may not realize or appreciate it. It implies that God's grace and generosity are constant, but human beings often fail to perceive or acknowledge the divine favors in their lives due to their lack of spiritual awareness or gratitude.
