translation: Allah is the Light of the heavens and the earth. The example of His light is like a niche within which is a lamp, the lamp is within glass, the glass as if it were a pearly [white] star lit from [the oil of] a blessed olive tree, neither of the east nor of the west, whose oil would almost glow even if untouched by fire. Light upon light. Allah guides to His light whom He wills. And Allah presents examples for the people, and Allah is Knowing of all things.
interpretation: This verse symbolically describes Allah's divine guidance and enlightenment. The light of Allah is compared to a lamp in a niche, shining brightly like a star, fueled by the pure oil of a blessed olive tree. This light is self-sustaining, glowing even without being lit by fire. It represents the purity and clarity of Allah's guidance, which can lead individuals out of darkness and into the light of faith and righteousness. The verse emphasizes that Allah guides whom He wills to this light, as He has supreme knowledge and wisdom. The metaphor of light upon light underscores the idea that Allah's guidance is layered and profound, illuminating the hearts and minds of those who seek it sincerely.
orig: الله نور السماوات والأرض مثل نوره كمشكاة فيها مصباح المصباح في زجاجة الزجاجة كأنها كوكب دري يوقد من شجرة مباركة زيتونة لا شرقية ولا غربية يكاد زيتها يضيء ولو لم تمسسه نار نور على نور يهدي الله لنوره من يشاء ويضرب الله الأمثال للناس والله بكل شيء عليم

translation: In houses which Allah has ordered to be raised and that His name be mentioned therein; exalting Him within them in the morning and the evenings.
interpretation: This verse refers to the mosques, the houses of worship that Allah has commanded to be built and maintained, where His name is celebrated and invoked. In these sacred spaces, the believers engage in praising and glorifying Allah, especially in the morning and evening hours. The verse emphasizes the importance of establishing and preserving places dedicated to the remembrance of Allah, where individuals can connect with their Creator and find spiritual solace. It highlights the significance of consistent devotion and the value of starting and ending one's day with the remembrance of Allah in His houses of worship.
orig: في بيوت أذن الله أن ترفع ويذكر فيها اسمه يسبح له فيها بالغدو والآصال

translation: Men whom neither commerce nor sale distracts from the remembrance of Allah and performance of prayer and giving of zakah. They fear a Day in which the hearts and eyes will [fearfully] turn about
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of remaining steadfast in faith and worship even while engaging in worldly pursuits like trade and commerce. It praises those believers who are not distracted from remembering Allah, establishing prayer, and giving charity despite their business preoccupations. They are ever-mindful of the Day of Judgment when hearts will be overturned in fear and eyes will be horrified at the recompense for their deeds. The verse encourages prioritizing one's religious obligations and maintaining consciousness of Allah over getting absorbed in the temporary affairs of this world.
orig: رجال لا تلهيهم تجارة ولا بيع عن ذكر الله وإقام الصلاة وإيتاء الزكاة يخافون يوما تتقلب فيه القلوب والأبصار

translation: That Allah may reward them [according to] the best of what they did and increase them from His bounty. And Allah gives provision to whom He wills without account.
interpretation: This verse highlights the immense generosity and mercy of Allah towards His servants. It conveys that Allah, in His infinite grace, not only rewards the righteous for their good deeds, but He multiplies their rewards and blesses them with even more from His boundless favors. This interpretation emphasizes that Allah's provision and blessings are not constrained by worldly measures or limitations; rather, He bestows His bounties upon whomever He wills, without any restriction or account. The verse serves as a reminder of Allah's limitless capacity to give and encourages believers to strive for righteousness with the assurance that their efforts will be acknowledged and abundantly rewarded by their Most Gracious Lord.
orig: ليجزيهم الله أحسن ما عملوا ويزيدهم من فضله والله يرزق من يشاء بغير حساب

translation: But those who disbelieved - their deeds are like a mirage in a lowland which a thirsty one thinks is water until, when he comes to it, he finds it is nothing but finds Allah before Him, and He will pay him in full his due; and Allah is swift in account.
interpretation: This verse compares the deeds of the disbelievers to a mirage in a desert. Just as a thirsty person in the desert might see a mirage and think it is water, only to find nothing when he reaches it, the disbelievers' good deeds are ultimately worthless because they were not done in faith. They will find that their deeds will not save them on the Day of Judgment when they stand before Allah. Instead, they will find Allah's justice and He will swiftly hold them accountable for their disbelief and sins. The verse emphasizes the importance of faith and the ultimate futility of good deeds done without belief in Allah.
orig: والذين كفروا أعمالهم كسراب بقيعة يحسبه الظمآن ماء حتى إذا جاءه لم يجده شيئا ووجد الله عنده فوفاه حسابه والله سريع الحساب

translation: Or [they are] like darknesses within an unfathomable sea which is covered by waves, upon which are waves, over which are clouds - darknesses, some of them upon others. When one puts out his hand [therein], he can hardly see it. And he to whom Allah has not granted light - for him there is no light.
interpretation: This verse uses a powerful metaphor to describe the depths of disbelief and ignorance. The "darknesses" represent layers of spiritual blindness, while the "unfathomable sea" symbolizes the vastness and complexity of life's trials. The waves upon waves depict the relentless challenges and doubts that can overwhelm a person. The clouds further obscure any glimmer of truth or guidance. In this state of complete darkness, one is utterly lost, unable to even see their own hand before them. It conveys the hopelessness and confusion of those who lack faith and divine guidance. The final line affirms that only Allah can grant the light of guidance and without it, one remains in spiritual darkness, no matter their worldly knowledge or status.
orig: أو كظلمات في بحر لجي يغشاه موج من فوقه موج من فوقه سحاب ظلمات بعضها فوق بعض إذا أخرج يده لم يكد يراها ومن لم يجعل الله له نورا فما له من نور

translation: Do you not see that Allah is exalted by whomever is within the heavens and the earth and [by] the birds with wings spread [in flight]? Each [of them] has known his [means of] prayer and exalting [Him], and Allah is Knowing of what they do.
interpretation: This verse highlights the fact that all of Allah's creation, whether in the heavens or on earth, glorifies Him in their own unique ways. The birds in flight, with their wings spread out, are also engaged in the remembrance and exaltation of Allah. Each creature has its own distinct method of prayer and glorification, which Allah is fully aware of. This serves as a reminder for humans to recognize the signs of Allah's magnificence in the world around them and to join in the universal praise and submission to the Almighty Creator.
orig: ألم تر أن الله يسبح له من في السماوات والأرض والطير صافات كل قد علم صلاته وتسبيحه والله عليم بما يفعلون

translation: And to Allah belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth, and to Allah is the final return.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute sovereignty and power of Allah over all of creation. It reminds us that everything in the heavens and the earth belongs to Him alone, and that all things will ultimately return to Him. This serves as a powerful reminder for believers to submit to Allah's will, seek His pleasure, and strive for success in the eternal life to come, rather than being consumed by the temporary distractions of this worldly life. It also highlights the importance of accountability, as we will all be held responsible for our actions when we return to Allah on the Day of Judgment.
orig: ولله ملك السماوات والأرض وإلى الله المصير

translation: Do you not see that Allah drives clouds? Then He brings them together, then He makes them into a mass, and you see the rain emerge from within it. And He sends down from the sky, mountains [of clouds] within which is hail, and He strikes with it whom He wills and averts it from whom He wills. The flash of its lightening almost takes away the eyesight.
interpretation: This verse is a reminder of Allah's power and control over the natural world. It describes the process of cloud formation and precipitation, highlighting how Allah drives the clouds, brings them together, and causes rain and hail to fall from them. The verse also emphasizes the power of lightning, which is so bright that it can almost take away one's eyesight. This display of natural phenomena serves as a sign of Allah's omnipotence and a reminder for humans to marvel at His creation and submit to His will.
orig: ألم تر أن الله يزجي سحابا ثم يؤلف بينه ثم يجعله ركاما فترى الودق يخرج من خلاله وينزل من السماء من جبال فيها من برد فيصيب به من يشاء ويصرفه عن من يشاء يكاد سنا برقه يذهب بالأبصار

translation: Allah alternates the night and the day. Indeed in that is a lesson for those who have perception.
interpretation: This verse reminds us of Allah's power and control over the universe. The alternation of night and day is a sign of His wisdom and a lesson for those who reflect deeply. It encourages us to ponder upon the creation and appreciate the perfect balance and harmony in nature. The verse also implies that just as Allah brings about change in the physical world, He can bring about change in our lives and circumstances. It is a message of hope and a call to be mindful of Allah's signs in the universe.
orig: يقلب الله الليل والنهار إن في ذلك لعبرة لأولي الأبصار

translation: Allah has created every [living] creature from water. And of them are those that move on their bellies, and of them are those that walk on two legs, and of them are those that walk on four. Allah creates what He wills. Indeed, Allah is over all things competent.
interpretation: This verse points to the creative power and wisdom of Allah, who has created all living beings from water, which is essential for life. It also highlights the diversity of Allah's creation, with creatures that move in different ways - some on their bellies like snakes, some on two legs like birds and humans, and some on four like most mammals. The verse emphasizes that Allah creates whatever He wills, and has the power to do all things, demonstrating His absolute sovereignty and omnipotence. It encourages reflection on the wonders of Allah's creation and acknowledging His greatness.
orig: والله خلق كل دابة من ماء فمنهم من يمشي على بطنه ومنهم من يمشي على رجلين ومنهم من يمشي على أربع يخلق الله ما يشاء إن الله على كل شيء قدير

translation: We have sent down clear revelations, and Allah guides whom He wills to a straight path.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the Qur'an contains clear and unambiguous guidance for humanity. However, it is ultimately Allah who guides individuals to the right path according to His divine wisdom and will. The verse implies that while the Qur'an provides the necessary guidance, it is up to each individual to open their heart to its message and seek Allah's guidance sincerely. It also highlights the concept of divine will and predestination in Islam, acknowledging that Allah has the power to guide or misguide individuals based on His infinite knowledge and wisdom.
orig: لقد أنزلنا آيات مبينات والله يهدي من يشاء إلى صراط مستقيم

translation: And they say, "We have believed in Allah and in the Messenger, and we obey"; then a party of them turns away after that, and those are not believers.
interpretation: This verse is criticizing the hypocrites who outwardly profess belief in Allah and His Messenger, and claim to be obedient, but then turn away from following the teachings and commands of Islam. Their actions belie their words, proving that their faith is not sincere. True believers are consistent in their obedience to Allah and His Messenger, whereas the hypocrites' behavior reveals the hollowness of their claims to faith. The Qur'an is exposing their contradictory nature and making it clear that such individuals cannot be considered real believers due to the discrepancy between their statements and their actual conduct.
orig: ويقولون آمنا بالله وبالرسول وأطعنا ثم يتولى فريق منهم من بعد ذلك وما أولئك بالمؤمنين

translation: And when they are called to [the words of] Allah and His Messenger to judge between them, at once a party of them turns aside [in refusal].
interpretation: This verse highlights the hypocrisy of some people who claim to believe in Allah and His Messenger, but when they are called to submit to the judgment of Allah and His Messenger in their disputes, a group of them turns away in refusal. They only want to follow the judgment of Allah and His Messenger when it suits their desires and interests. This behavior is a clear sign of weak faith and lack of sincerity in their claim of belief. True believers submit to the judgment of Allah and His Messenger in all matters, whether it is in their favor or against them, as a sign of their complete trust and obedience to Allah.
orig: وإذا دعوا إلى الله ورسوله ليحكم بينهم إذا فريق منهم معرضون

translation: And if the truth is in their favor, they come to him in prompt obedience.
interpretation: This verse highlights the hypocritical nature of some people. When the truth aligns with their personal interests or desires, they readily accept it and even hasten to comply with it enthusiastically. However, when the truth goes against their wishes or exposes their wrongdoings, they are reluctant to acknowledge it and may even oppose it vehemently. The verse implies that true believers should embrace the truth consistently, regardless of whether it suits their inclinations or not, as submitting to the truth is a sign of sincere faith and righteousness.
orig: وإن يكن لهم الحق يأتوا إليه مذعنين

translation: Is there a disease in their hearts? Or do they doubt or fear that Allah and His Messenger will deal unjustly with them? Rather, it is they who are the wrongdoers.
interpretation: This verse suggests that those who harbor doubts or fears about Allah and His Messenger's justice are themselves afflicted with a spiritual disease or are engaged in wrongdoing. It implies that questioning the fairness of divine judgment or the Prophet's decisions is a sign of an unhealthy heart and a lack of true faith. The verse asserts that Allah and His Messenger are always just, and it is the doubters who are in the wrong due to their misgivings and mistrust. This highlights the importance of having unwavering faith and trust in Allah and His chosen messenger.
orig: أفي قلوبهم مرض أم ارتابوا أم يخافون أن يحيف الله عليهم ورسوله بل أولئك هم الظالمون

translation: The only statement of the [true] believers when they are called to Allah and His Messenger to judge between them is that they say, "We hear and we obey." And those are the successful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of obedience and submission to Allah and His Messenger. When true believers are called to accept the judgment of Allah and His Prophet, their immediate response is to say, "We hear and we obey." They do not argue, question, or hesitate in their compliance. This unconditional obedience to divine authority is a hallmark of sincere faith. Those who exhibit such readiness to accept Allah's decree and the Prophet's decision are described as the successful ones, indicating that their attitude will lead them to prosperity both in this world and in the Hereafter. The verse underscores that true success lies in aligning oneself with the will of Allah and following the guidance of His Messenger wholeheartedly.
orig: إنما كان قول المؤمنين إذا دعوا إلى الله ورسوله ليحكم بينهم أن يقولوا سمعنا وأطعنا وأولئك هم المفلحون

translation: And whoever obeys Allah and His Messenger and fears Allah and is conscious of Him - it is those who are the attainers.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of complete obedience to Allah and His Messenger, Muhammad (peace be upon him). It also highlights the significance of having a deep reverence for Allah and being mindful of one's actions and their consequences. Those who embody these qualities - obedience, fear of Allah, and righteousness - are the ones who will ultimately attain success and triumph in both this world and the Hereafter. The verse serves as a reminder that true success lies in aligning oneself with the commandments of Allah and following the guidance of His Messenger, while cultivating a heart that is filled with awe and consciousness of the Almighty.
orig: ومن يطع الله ورسوله ويخش الله ويتقه فأولئك هم الفائزون

translation: And they swear by Allah their strongest oaths that if you ordered them, they would go forth [in Allah's cause]. Say, "Do not swear. [Such] obedience is known. Indeed, Allah is Acquainted with that which you do."
interpretation: This verse is addressing the hypocrites who outwardly claimed to be believers but inwardly harbored doubts and ill intentions. They would swear strongly that if the Prophet commanded them to go forth and fight, they would readily obey. However, Allah instructs the Prophet to tell them not to make such false oaths, because their true obedience and sincerity is already known to Allah. Mere words and oaths do not prove faith; rather it is one's actions and intentions that Allah is fully aware of. The lesson is that we cannot deceive Allah with empty promises and verbal commitments - He knows what is in our hearts and will judge us based on our actual deeds and intentions, not mere claims of loyalty and obedience.
orig: وأقسموا بالله جهد أيمانهم لئن أمرتهم ليخرجن قل لا تقسموا طاعة معروفة إن الله خبير بما تعملون

translation: Say, "Obey Allah and obey the Messenger; but if you turn away - then upon him is only that [duty] with which he has been charged, and upon you is that with which you have been charged. And if you obey him, you will be [rightly] guided. And there is not upon the Messenger except the [responsibility for] clear notification."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of obedience to Allah and His Messenger. It makes it clear that the Prophet's responsibility is to convey the message, while the people's responsibility is to follow and obey the guidance. If they turn away from the message, the Prophet is not accountable for their actions; he has fulfilled his duty of delivering the clear message. However, if the people obey the Prophet, they will be rightly guided. The verse underscores the distinct roles and responsibilities of the Prophet and his followers in regards to the divine message.
orig: قل أطيعوا الله وأطيعوا الرسول فإن تولوا فإنما عليه ما حمل وعليكم ما حملتم وإن تطيعوه تهتدوا وما على الرسول إلا البلاغ المبين

translation: Allah has promised those who have believed among you and done righteous deeds that He will surely grant them succession [to authority] upon the earth just as He granted it to those before them and that He will surely establish for them [therein] their religion which He has preferred for them and that He will surely substitute for them, after their fear, security, [for] they worship Me, not associating anything with Me. But whoever disbelieves after that - then those are the defiantly disobedient.
interpretation: This verse contains a promise from Allah to the righteous believers that He will grant them authority and leadership on earth, just as He did for the righteous people before them. Allah will firmly establish the religion of Islam which He has chosen for them. He will remove their state of fear and insecurity, granting them peace and stability instead, as long as they worship Allah alone without associating partners with Him. Whoever rejects faith after this promise, they are the rebellious transgressors who have gone outside the obedience of Allah.
orig: وعد الله الذين آمنوا منكم وعملوا الصالحات ليستخلفنهم في الأرض كما استخلف الذين من قبلهم وليمكنن لهم دينهم الذي ارتضى لهم وليبدلنهم من بعد خوفهم أمنا يعبدونني لا يشركون بي شيئا ومن كفر بعد ذلك فأولئك هم الفاسقون

translation: And establish prayer and give zakah and obey the Messenger that you may receive mercy.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of three key aspects of Islamic faith and practice: establishing regular prayer (salah), giving obligatory charity (zakah), and obeying the teachings and example of Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him). By fulfilling these essential duties, Muslims may hope to attain Allah's mercy, forgiveness, and blessings in this life and the hereafter. The verse highlights the interconnectedness of one's relationship with Allah (through prayer), one's social responsibility towards the less fortunate (through zakah), and one's adherence to the prophetic guidance (through obedience to the Messenger). Together, these form the foundation of a believer's spiritual growth and the key to earning divine mercy and compassion.
orig: وأقيموا الصلاة وآتوا الزكاة وأطيعوا الرسول لعلكم ترحمون

translation: Never think that the disbelievers are able to escape in the land. Their abode will be the Fire - and how wretched the destination.
interpretation: This verse serves as a stern warning to those who reject faith in Allah and His message. It emphasizes that no matter how much power, influence, or resources the disbelievers may possess in this worldly life, they will never be able to escape Allah's judgment and punishment. Their ultimate abode will be the Fire of Hell, which is described as the worst possible destination one could face in the Hereafter. This interpretation highlights the consequences of disbelief and the importance of accepting the truth and submitting to Allah's will to avoid such a terrible fate.
orig: لا تحسبن الذين كفروا معجزين في الأرض ومأواهم النار ولبئس المصير

translation: O you who have believed, let those whom your right hands possess and those who have not [yet] reached puberty among you ask permission of you [before entering] at three times: before the dawn prayer and when you put aside your clothing [for rest] at noon and after the night prayer. [These are] three times of privacy for you. There is no blame upon you nor upon them beyond these [periods], for they continually circulate among you - some of you, among others. Thus does Allah make clear to you the verses; and Allah is Knowing and Wise.
interpretation: This verse provides guidelines for maintaining privacy and modesty within the household. It instructs that servants and children who have not reached puberty should seek permission before entering private areas during three specific times of the day: before the dawn prayer, during the afternoon rest period, and after the night prayer. These are times when individuals may be in a state of undress or engaged in private matters. Outside of these designated times, there is no blame on either the servants, children, or the household members for moving freely within the house. This verse emphasizes the importance of respecting personal boundaries and privacy while also acknowledging the practical realities of living together in a household. It reflects Allah's wisdom in providing clear guidance for maintaining a harmonious and modest living environment.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا ليستأذنكم الذين ملكت أيمانكم والذين لم يبلغوا الحلم منكم ثلاث مرات من قبل صلاة الفجر وحين تضعون ثيابكم من الظهيرة ومن بعد صلاة العشاء ثلاث عورات لكم ليس عليكم ولا عليهم جناح بعدهن طوافون عليكم بعضكم على بعض كذلك يبين الله لكم الآيات والله عليم حكيم

translation: And when the children among you reach puberty, let them ask permission [at all times] as those before them have done. Thus does Allah make clear to you His verses; and Allah is Knowing and Wise.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of seeking permission and maintaining privacy, especially as children reach the age of puberty. It teaches that once children attain maturity, they should follow the same etiquette of seeking permission before entering private spaces as adults do. This practice helps to foster a sense of respect, modesty, and personal boundaries within the family and the larger community. The verse also highlights Allah's wisdom in providing clear guidance through His revelations, which are designed to promote a harmonious and morally upright society.
orig: وإذا بلغ الأطفال منكم الحلم فليستأذنوا كما استأذن الذين من قبلهم كذلك يبين الله لكم آياته والله عليم حكيم

translation: And women of post-menstrual age who have no desire for marriage - there is no blame upon them for putting aside their outer garments [but] not displaying adornment. But to modestly refrain [from that] is better for them. And Allah is Hearing and Knowing.
interpretation: This verse indicates that elderly women who have passed the age of marriage and no longer have sexual desires are allowed to relax their dress code to some extent, such as not wearing a head cover or outer garment, provided they do not do so with the intention of displaying their beauty and attracting attention. However, the verse emphasizes that it is still better and more virtuous for them to refrain from this relaxation and maintain their modesty in dress and behavior. This reflects Islam's general encouragement of modesty for all believers. The verse ends by affirming that Allah hears and knows all things, including the intentions behind people's actions, so one should be mindful of Him in all circumstances.
orig: والقواعد من النساء اللاتي لا يرجون نكاحا فليس عليهن جناح أن يضعن ثيابهن غير متبرجات بزينة وأن يستعففن خير لهن والله سميع عليم

translation: There is no blame upon the blind nor any blame upon the lame nor any blame upon the sick nor upon yourselves if you eat from your [own] houses or the houses of your fathers or the houses of your mothers or the houses of your brothers or the houses of your sisters or the houses of your father's brothers or the houses of your father's sisters or the houses of your mother's brothers or the houses of your mother's sisters or [from houses] whose keys you possess or [from the house] of your friend. There is no blame upon you whether you eat together or separately. But when you enter houses, give greetings of peace upon each other - a greeting from Allah, blessed and good. Thus does Allah make clear to you the verses [of ordinance] that you may understand.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that there is no sin or blame on those who are blind, lame, sick, or on anyone for eating in the houses of their close relatives or friends, or houses they have the keys to. It encourages a sense of community, trust, and sharing among people, especially with those who may have disabilities or illnesses that make it difficult for them to provide for themselves. The verse also promotes the Islamic etiquette of greeting each other with peace when entering homes, describing it as a blessed and good greeting from Allah Himself. Overall, this passage highlights the importance of social bonds, empathy, and courtesy in Islamic teachings, with the aim of fostering understanding and harmony in society.
orig: ليس على الأعمى حرج ولا على الأعرج حرج ولا على المريض حرج ولا على أنفسكم أن تأكلوا من بيوتكم أو بيوت آبائكم أو بيوت أمهاتكم أو بيوت إخوانكم أو بيوت أخواتكم أو بيوت أعمامكم أو بيوت عماتكم أو بيوت أخوالكم أو بيوت خالاتكم أو ما ملكتم مفاتحه أو صديقكم ليس عليكم جناح أن تأكلوا جميعا أو أشتاتا فإذا دخلتم بيوتا فسلموا على أنفسكم تحية من عند الله مباركة طيبة كذلك يبين الله لكم الآيات لعلكم تعقلون

translation: The believers are only those who believe in Allah and His Messenger and, when they are with him for a collective matter, they do not leave until they have asked his permission. Indeed, those who ask your permission, [O Muhammad] - those are the ones who believe in Allah and His Messenger. So when they ask your permission for something of their affairs, then give permission to whom you will among them and ask forgiveness for them of Allah. Indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of seeking permission from the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) before leaving a gathering or attending to personal matters. It highlights the respect and obedience that true believers should have towards the Prophet and the significance of collective affairs and unity within the Muslim community. The verse also encourages the Prophet to grant permission when appropriate and to seek Allah's forgiveness for the believers, reminding us of Allah's forgiving and merciful nature towards those who sincerely believe in Him and His Messenger.
orig: إنما المؤمنون الذين آمنوا بالله ورسوله وإذا كانوا معه على أمر جامع لم يذهبوا حتى يستأذنوه إن الذين يستأذنونك أولئك الذين يؤمنون بالله ورسوله فإذا استأذنوك لبعض شأنهم فأذن لمن شئت منهم واستغفر لهم الله إن الله غفور رحيم

translation: Do not make [your] calling of the Messenger among yourselves as the call of one of you to another. Already Allah knows those of you who slip away, concealed by others. So let those beware who dissent from the Prophet's order, lest fitnah strike them or a painful punishment.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of showing utmost respect and reverence to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him). It warns against treating the Prophet like any ordinary person and highlights the distinction between addressing him and addressing others. The verse also cautions those who disobey the Prophet's commands or try to avoid their responsibilities, stating that they may face trials and tribulations (fitnah) or a severe punishment from Allah for their actions. This serves as a reminder for believers to hold the Prophet in high regard, follow his teachings sincerely, and not take their religious obligations lightly.
orig: لا تجعلوا دعاء الرسول بينكم كدعاء بعضكم بعضا قد يعلم الله الذين يتسللون منكم لواذا فليحذر الذين يخالفون عن أمره أن تصيبهم فتنة أو يصيبهم عذاب أليم

translation: Unquestionably, to Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and earth. Already He knows that upon which you [stand] and [knows] the Day when they will be returned to Him and He will inform them of what they have done. And Allah is Knowing of all things.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's complete knowledge and sovereignty over all things in existence. It asserts that Allah is fully aware of people's deeds, intentions and the state they are in. On the Day of Judgment, all will be returned to Him and He will make them understand the full implications of their actions in this world. Nothing is hidden from Allah, and He has perfect knowledge of everything, including what is apparent and what is hidden in people's hearts. This should inspire believers to be ever conscious of Allah and strive for righteousness.
orig: ألا إن لله ما في السماوات والأرض قد يعلم ما أنتم عليه ويوم يرجعون إليه فينبئهم بما عملوا والله بكل شيء عليم

translation: Blessed is He who sent down the Criterion upon His Servant that he may be to the worlds a warner.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the significance and divine origin of the Qur'an, which is referred to as the Furqan or the Criterion. It is a blessing from Allah that He has revealed this scripture to His servant, Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him), so that he may serve as a warner to all of mankind. The Qur'an acts as a criterion, distinguishing between truth and falsehood, guiding people to the right path. The verse also highlights the universal nature of the Prophet's message, as he was sent as a messenger to the entire world, not just to a specific community or region.
orig: تبارك الذي نزل الفرقان على عبده ليكون للعالمين نذيرا

translation: He to whom belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth and who has not taken a son and has not had a partner in dominion and has created each thing and determined it with [precise] determination.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute sovereignty and oneness of Allah. He is the sole owner and ruler of the heavens and the earth, and He has no offspring or partners sharing in His dominion. It also highlights Allah's role as the Creator of everything, and that He has precisely determined and measured all things according to His wisdom and knowledge. This interpretation underscores the importance of recognizing Allah's unity, power, and control over all creation, and serves as a reminder for humans to submit to His will and worship Him alone.
orig: الذي له ملك السماوات والأرض ولم يتخذ ولدا ولم يكن له شريك في الملك وخلق كل شيء فقدره تقديرا

translation: And they have taken besides Him gods which create nothing, while they are created, and possess not for themselves any harm or benefit and possess not [power to cause] death or life or resurrection.
interpretation: This verse criticizes the polytheists who worship idols and false deities besides Allah. These false gods are powerless and cannot create anything, while they themselves are created by others. They have no ability to bring harm or benefit to themselves, let alone to those who worship them. Furthermore, these idols have no control over life and death, nor can they resurrect anyone. The verse emphasizes the complete powerlessness and futility of worshipping anyone or anything besides Allah, as all power and authority belong to Him alone.
orig: واتخذوا من دونه آلهة لا يخلقون شيئا وهم يخلقون ولا يملكون لأنفسهم ضرا ولا نفعا ولا يملكون موتا ولا حياة ولا نشورا

translation: And those who disbelieve say, "This [Qur'an] is not except a falsehood he invented, and another people assisted him in it." But they have committed an injustice and a lie.
interpretation: This verse is addressing the accusations made by the disbelievers against Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him). They claimed that the Qur'an was not a divine revelation, but rather a fabrication invented by the Prophet himself, with the help of other people. The verse refutes this claim and states that by making such accusations, the disbelievers have committed a great injustice and a lie. It affirms that the Qur'an is indeed the word of Allah, revealed to the Prophet, and not a product of human invention. The verse highlights the stubbornness and disbelief of those who reject the truth, even when it is clear and evident.
orig: وقال الذين كفروا إن هذا إلا إفك افتراه وأعانه عليه قوم آخرون فقد جاءوا ظلما وزورا

translation: And they say, "Legends of the former peoples which he has written down, and they are dictated to him morning and afternoon."
interpretation: This verse is referring to the accusations made by the disbelievers against the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him). They claimed that the Qur'an was not a divine revelation, but rather a collection of ancient legends and stories that the Prophet had learned from others and had written down. They further claimed that he was being taught these stories by someone else on a regular basis, morning and evening. This interpretation highlights the skepticism and disbelief of the Prophet's opponents, who sought to discredit the divine origin of the Qur'an by attributing it to human sources and fabrication. It also reflects their unwillingness to accept the truth of the Prophet's message despite the clear evidence of its divine nature.
orig: وقالوا أساطير الأولين اكتتبها فهي تملى عليه بكرة وأصيلا

translation: Say, [O Muhammad], "It has been revealed by He who knows [every] secret within the heavens and the earth. Indeed, He is ever Forgiving and Merciful."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the omniscience of Allah, who has revealed the Qur'an to Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him). It highlights that Allah is aware of all secrets in the heavens and the earth, indicating His complete knowledge and wisdom. The verse also underscores two of Allah's essential attributes: His forgiveness and mercy. This interpretation suggests that although Allah is all-knowing and aware of every deed, He is also ever ready to forgive those who repent and seek His mercy. It serves as a reminder for believers to turn to Allah for forgiveness and to trust in His infinite wisdom and knowledge.
orig: قل أنزله الذي يعلم السر في السماوات والأرض إنه كان غفورا رحيما

translation: And they say, "What is this messenger that eats food and walks in the markets? Why was there not sent down to him an angel so he would be with him as a warner?"
interpretation: This verse reflects the skepticism and disbelief of the Meccan pagans towards Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him). They found it strange that a prophet would engage in ordinary human activities like eating and walking in the markets. They expected a prophet to be accompanied by an angel as proof of his divine mission. This shows their lack of understanding of the nature of prophethood and their demand for supernatural signs to believe. The verse implies that a prophet is a human being chosen by God to convey His message, not a superhuman figure exempt from human needs and activities.
orig: وقالوا مال هذا الرسول يأكل الطعام ويمشي في الأسواق لولا أنزل إليه ملك فيكون معه نذيرا

translation: Or that he should have a treasure thrown to him, or should have a garden from which he may eat. And the wrongdoers say, "You follow not but a man affected by magic."
interpretation: The disbelievers are making unreasonable demands of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him), suggesting that he should have wealth or gardens miraculously given to him to prove his prophethood. They are not content with the clear proofs and guidance he has brought. Instead, they dismiss him as a man bewitched or deluded by magic. This highlights their stubborn refusal to accept the truth, as they resort to making excuses and setting impossible conditions to avoid believing in the message of Islam. It shows their spiritual blindness and attachment to worldly desires, unable to recognize the true value of divine revelation.
orig: أو يلقى إليه كنز أو تكون له جنة يأكل منها وقال الظالمون إن تتبعون إلا رجلا مسحورا

translation: See how they strike similitudes for you, and have gone astray, and cannot find a way.
interpretation: This verse is a rebuke to those who reject the message of Islam and the prophethood of Muhammad (peace be upon him). It points out how they invent false analogies and comparisons to discredit the truth, but in doing so, they only lead themselves further astray from the right path. Their arguments are baseless and their reasoning is flawed, leaving them unable to find the way to guidance and salvation. The verse emphasizes that their rejection is not based on any sound logic or evidence, but rather on their own misguided notions and stubborn refusal to accept the clear signs of Allah.
orig: انظر كيف ضربوا لك الأمثال فضلوا فلا يستطيعون سبيلا

translation: Blessed is He who, if He willed, could have made for you [something] better than that - gardens beneath which rivers flow - and could make for you palaces.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute power and sovereignty of Allah. It reminds us that if Allah wills, He can bestow upon us blessings far greater than what we can imagine, such as gardens with flowing rivers and magnificent palaces. It highlights the idea that everything in this world and the hereafter is ultimately under Allah's control and that He can grant us whatever He desires. The verse also implies that we should be grateful for whatever Allah has given us, as it is only by His will and mercy that we have been blessed with the things we possess in this life.
orig: تبارك الذي إن شاء جعل لك خيرا من ذلك جنات تجري من تحتها الأنهار ويجعل لك قصورا

translation: But they have denied the Hour, and We have prepared for those who deny the Hour a Blaze.
interpretation: This verse is a stern warning to those who reject the concept of the Day of Judgment (referred to as "the Hour"). It emphasizes that denying the inevitable accountability for one's deeds is a grave sin. God has prepared a severe punishment, described as a blazing Fire, for those who persist in denying the reality of the Day of Judgment. This interpretation highlights the importance of believing in the afterlife and the consequences of one's actions, as it is a fundamental aspect of Islamic faith. The verse serves as a reminder for individuals to be mindful of their choices and to live righteously in preparation for the eventual reckoning.
orig: بل كذبوا بالساعة وأعتدنا لمن كذب بالساعة سعيرا

translation: When it sees them from a distant place, they will hear its fury and roaring.
interpretation: This verse is referring to the torments of Hell that await the disbelievers in the Hereafter. It describes how even from a distance, the inhabitants of Hell will be able to hear the raging and roaring of the Hellfire. This serves as a vivid warning and reminder of the severe punishment that awaits those who reject faith and indulge in sin. The verse aims to instill fear and encourage people to mend their ways and follow the path of righteousness to avoid such a dreadful fate.
orig: إذا رأتهم من مكان بعيد سمعوا لها تغيظا وزفيرا

translation: And when they are thrown into a narrow place therein bound in chains, they will cry out thereupon for destruction.
interpretation: This verse is describing the fate of the disbelievers in Hell. When they are cast into the narrow confines of Hell, bound in chains, they will cry out in anguish and despair, wishing for complete destruction to escape their torment. It emphasizes the severity and hopelessness of their punishment in the Hereafter as a consequence of their disbelief and evil deeds in this world. The verse serves as a stark warning to those who reject faith, urging them to mend their ways before it is too late.
orig: وإذا ألقوا منها مكانا ضيقا مقرنين دعوا هنالك ثبورا

translation: Do not cry out today for one destruction, but cry out for much destruction.
interpretation: This verse is a warning to the disbelievers and wrongdoers on the Day of Judgment. It emphasizes the severity and multitude of the punishments they will face as a consequence of their actions in this world. The verse tells them not to cry out for a single instance of destruction or ruin, but rather to cry out for repeated and numerous destructions, indicating the continuous and overwhelming nature of their suffering in the Hereafter. This serves as a reminder for people to be mindful of their deeds and to turn towards righteousness before it is too late.
orig: لا تدعوا اليوم ثبورا واحدا وادعوا ثبورا كثيرا

translation: Say, "Is that better or the Garden of Eternity which is promised to the righteous? It will be for them a reward and destination."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the superiority of the eternal Paradise promised to the righteous believers over the fleeting pleasures of this worldly life. It serves as a reminder that the ultimate goal and reward for those who lead a life of piety and righteousness is the everlasting bliss of the Garden of Eternity. The verse encourages believers to focus on the hereafter and strive for this ultimate destination, rather than being distracted by the temporary enjoyments of this world. It highlights the importance of making choices and living a life that aligns with the path of righteousness, as it will lead to the greatest reward of all: an eternal abode in Paradise.
orig: قل أذلك خير أم جنة الخلد التي وعد المتقون كانت لهم جزاء ومصيرا

translation: They will have whatever they wish therein, abiding eternally. It is ever a promise binding upon your Lord.
interpretation: This verse speaks to the eternal reward that awaits the righteous believers in Paradise. It emphasizes that they will have all that their hearts desire, without any limitations or restrictions, and that this state of bliss will be everlasting. The verse also underscores the certainty of Allah's promise, indicating that it is a binding covenant that He has taken upon Himself to fulfill. This serves as a powerful motivation for the believers to persevere in faith and good deeds, knowing that their ultimate reward is guaranteed by the One whose promise never fails.
orig: لهم فيها ما يشاءون خالدين كان على ربك وعدا مسئولا

translation: And the Day when He will gather them and that which they worship besides Allah and will say, "Was it you who misled these, My servants, or did they [themselves] stray from the way?"
interpretation: This verse is referring to the Day of Judgment when Allah will gather all the people along with the false deities they used to worship. Allah will then question these false gods, asking them if they were the ones who misled His servants or if the people went astray on their own. The interpretation is that the false deities will not be able to claim any power of misguidance, as it was the people who chose to deviate from the right path of their own accord. It emphasizes that everyone is responsible for their own actions and beliefs, and that false gods have no real power or influence over people's choices. The verse also highlights Allah's authority and His role as the ultimate judge on the Day of Reckoning.
orig: ويوم يحشرهم وما يعبدون من دون الله فيقول أأنتم أضللتم عبادي هؤلاء أم هم ضلوا السبيل

translation: They will say, "Exalted are You! It was not for us to take besides You any allies. But You provided comforts for them and their fathers until they forgot the message and became a people ruined."
interpretation: This verse reflects the realization of those who took false deities as protectors besides Allah. On the Day of Judgment, they will acknowledge Allah's perfection and admit that it was wrong for them to take others as allies instead of Him. They will recognize that the comforts and luxuries that Allah provided for them and their ancestors in worldly life diverted them from remembering Him and following His guidance. As a result, they became a people spiritually ruined and lost. This highlights the importance of remaining steadfast in faith, gratitude, and remembrance of Allah, despite the distractions and temptations of worldly life, to avoid such a fate in the Hereafter.
orig: قالوا سبحانك ما كان ينبغي لنا أن نتخذ من دونك من أولياء ولكن متعتهم وآباءهم حتى نسوا الذكر وكانوا قوما بورا

translation: For they have denied you in what you say, so you will not be able to avert [punishment] or [find] help. And whoever commits injustice among you - We will make him taste a great punishment.
interpretation: This verse is a stern warning to those who reject the message of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him). It emphasizes that those who deny the truth will face severe consequences for their actions. They will be unable to escape the punishment that awaits them, nor will they find any help or support. The verse also highlights the concept of divine justice, stating that anyone who commits injustice will taste a great punishment. This serves as a reminder that all individuals are accountable for their deeds and will face the consequences of their choices in the Hereafter. The verse encourages believers to stay firm in their faith and to avoid any form of injustice or wrongdoing.
orig: فقد كذبوكم بما تقولون فما تستطيعون صرفا ولا نصرا ومن يظلم منكم نذقه عذابا كبيرا

translation: And We did not send before you, [O Muhammad], any of the messengers except that they ate food and walked in the markets. And We have made some of you [people] as trial for others - will you have patience? And ever is your Lord, Seeing.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the human nature of the prophets and messengers, showing that they were not divine beings but ordinary humans who ate, drank, and engaged in daily activities just like everyone else. It also highlights that God tests people through one another, putting some in positions of power or privilege over others to see how they will respond and whether they will remain patient and steadfast in their faith. The verse ends with a reminder that God is always watching and aware of people's actions and reactions.
orig: وما أرسلنا قبلك من المرسلين إلا إنهم ليأكلون الطعام ويمشون في الأسواق وجعلنا بعضكم لبعض فتنة أتصبرون وكان ربك بصيرا

translation: And those who do not expect the meeting with Us say, "Why were not angels sent down to us, or [why] do we [not] see our Lord?" They have certainly become arrogant within themselves and [become] insolent with great insolence.
interpretation: This verse is a rebuke to those who reject the message of Islam and demand to see physical proof of Allah's existence or His angels. Their demand stems from their arrogance and their refusal to accept the truth of the message that has been conveyed to them through the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him). They are not content with the clear signs and proofs that Allah has provided in the Qur'an and in the natural world around them. Instead, they make unreasonable demands for direct physical evidence of Allah's existence, such as demanding to see Him or His angels with their own eyes. This attitude reflects their insolence and their lack of humility before their Creator. The verse makes it clear that such demands are not acceptable and that those who make them have transgressed the proper bounds of behavior towards Allah.
orig: وقال الذين لا يرجون لقاءنا لولا أنزل علينا الملائكة أو نرى ربنا لقد استكبروا في أنفسهم وعتوا عتوا كبيرا

translation: The Day they see the angels - no good tidings will there be that Day for the criminals, and [the angels] will say, "Prevented and inaccessible."
interpretation: This verse refers to the Day of Judgment when the criminals will see the angels, but there will be no good news or comfort for them. The angels will declare that Paradise is "prevented and inaccessible" to these sinners. It signifies that on that Day, the wrongdoers will face the consequences of their actions and will be denied entry into Paradise due to their sins and disbelief. This serves as a warning for mankind to avoid evil deeds and to live righteously according to God's commands in order to be among those who receive glad tidings and are granted access to Paradise on the Day of Judgment.
orig: يوم يرون الملائكة لا بشرى يومئذ للمجرمين ويقولون حجرا محجورا

translation: And We will proceed to whatever deeds they did, and We will make them as scattered dust.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the ultimate insignificance of deeds that are not done for the sake of Allah. On the Day of Judgment, Allah will show that any actions done for worldly gain, fame, or other vain purposes will be rendered worthless, scattered like dust in the wind. It serves as a reminder for believers to purify their intentions and perform righteous deeds solely for Allah's pleasure, as those are the only ones that will carry weight and be rewarded in the Hereafter.
orig: وقدمنا إلى ما عملوا من عمل فجعلناه هباء منثورا

translation: The companions of Paradise, that Day, are [in] a better settlement and better resting place.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the great reward and blissful destination that awaits the righteous believers in the Hereafter. On the Day of Judgment, those who have earned Paradise through their faith and good deeds will find themselves in a far superior abode compared to the fleeting comforts of this worldly life. In Paradise, they will experience ultimate peace, joy, and tranquility in a perfect environment designed for eternal happiness. The verse also implies that the delights and pleasures of Paradise are beyond human comprehension, surpassing anything one can imagine or experience in this world.
orig: أصحاب الجنة يومئذ خير مستقرا وأحسن مقيلا

translation: And [remember] the Day when the sky will split open with [emerging] clouds, and the angels will be sent down in successive descent.
interpretation: This verse refers to the Day of Judgment, when the sky will be torn apart and the angels will descend in ranks. It signifies the magnitude and awe-inspiring nature of that day, as the natural order of the universe will be disrupted. The descent of the angels in succession emphasizes the solemnity and importance of the occasion, as they will come to carry out Allah's commands and gather the people for judgment. This verse serves as a reminder of the inevitability of that day and the need for humans to prepare for it by leading righteous lives and fulfilling their obligations to Allah.
orig: ويوم تشقق السماء بالغمام ونزل الملائكة تنزيلا

translation: The sovereignty on that Day will be the true (sovereignty), belonging to the Most Merciful (Allah), and it will be a difficult Day for the disbelievers.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that on the Day of Judgment, the ultimate and true authority will belong solely to Allah, the Most Merciful. It suggests that those who rejected faith in Allah will face great difficulty on that Day, as they will have to confront the reality of Allah's supreme power and their own helplessness. The verse implies that the disbelievers will face the consequences of their actions and will find no escape or support, as Allah's judgment will be final and just. It serves as a reminder for people to submit to Allah's will and seek His mercy before it is too late.
orig: الملك يومئذ الحق للرحمن وكان يوما على الكافرين عسيرا

translation: And the Day the wrongdoer will bite on his hands [in regret] he will say, "Oh, I wish I had taken with the Messenger a way."
interpretation: This verse is a powerful reminder of the regret and remorse that those who reject the message of Islam will feel on the Day of Judgment. The wrongdoer will bite his hands in anguish, wishing that he had followed the path of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and embraced the truth of Islam. It highlights the importance of making the right choices in this life, as the consequences of our actions will be felt in the Hereafter. The verse also emphasizes the role of the Prophet as a guide and example for humanity, showing us the way to salvation and success in both this world and the next.
orig: ويوم يعض الظالم على يديه يقول يا ليتني اتخذت مع الرسول سبيلا

translation: Oh, woe to me! I wish I had not taken that person as a friend!
interpretation: This verse is expressing deep regret over having taken a certain person as a close friend or companion. It implies that this friendship led the speaker astray or caused them harm in some way. The use of "woe to me" conveys a strong sense of sorrow and self-reproach over this mistake in judgment. The verse serves as a warning about being cautious in choosing friends and the significant influence that close companions can have on one's life and spiritual well-being.
orig: يا ويلتى ليتني لم أتخذ فلانا خليلا

translation: He led me away from the remembrance after it had come to me. And ever is Satan, to man, a deserter.
interpretation: This verse is referring to how Satan misguides and deceives humans, leading them astray from the path of God and His remembrance (the Qur'an and faith) after they have received guidance. It emphasizes that Satan is always a betrayer and abandoner of mankind, luring them towards sin and disbelief and then deserting them, leaving them to face the consequences of their actions alone. The verse serves as a warning to be vigilant against Satan's tricks and to hold fast to God's guidance and remembrance, as Satan's goal is to lead people away from the truth and into misguidance and loss.
orig: لقد أضلني عن الذكر بعد إذ جاءني وكان الشيطان للإنسان خذولا

translation: And the Messenger has said, "O my Lord, indeed my people have taken this Qur'an as [a thing] abandoned."
interpretation: This verse conveys the Prophet's deep concern and sorrow over his people's neglect and abandonment of the Qur'an. Despite the Qur'an being a divine revelation and guidance for mankind, many of the Prophet's contemporaries turned away from it, failing to recognize its value and importance in their lives. The Prophet's words express his heartfelt plea to Allah, seeking help and support in the face of his people's disregard for the sacred scripture. This verse serves as a reminder for all believers to hold fast to the Qur'an, to study and implement its teachings, and to never allow it to be neglected or abandoned in their lives.
orig: وقال الرسول يا رب إن قومي اتخذوا هذا القرآن مهجورا

translation: And thus have We made for every prophet an enemy from among the criminals. But sufficient is your Lord as a guide and a helper.
interpretation: This verse highlights the fact that every prophet faced opposition and enmity from the wrongdoers and criminals of their time. However, it also emphasizes that Allah is sufficient as a guide and helper for His prophets and believers, providing them with support, guidance, and protection against their enemies. This interpretation suggests that the believers should not be disheartened by the presence of adversaries, as Allah's help and guidance will always be there for those who sincerely follow His path and trust in His wisdom.
orig: وكذلك جعلنا لكل نبي عدوا من المجرمين وكفى بربك هاديا ونصيرا

translation: And those who disbelieve say, "Why was the Qur'an not revealed to him all at once?" Thus [it is] that We may strengthen thereby your heart. And We have spaced it distinctly.
interpretation: This verse addresses the objections raised by the disbelievers regarding the gradual revelation of the Qur'an to Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him). They questioned why the entire Qur'an was not revealed all at once. Allah responds by stating that the gradual revelation was to strengthen the Prophet's heart and resolve, allowing him to absorb and understand the message more effectively. The verse also emphasizes that the Qur'an was revealed in a well-arranged and distinct manner, making it easier for the believers to comprehend and memorize. This interpretation highlights the wisdom behind the gradual revelation of the Qur'an and its role in supporting the Prophet's mission and facilitating the understanding of its message for the believers.
orig: وقال الذين كفروا لولا نزل عليه القرآن جملة واحدة كذلك لنثبت به فؤادك ورتلناه ترتيلا

translation: And they do not come to you with an example [i.e., argument] except that We bring you the truth and the best explanation.
interpretation: This verse assures Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) that whenever the disbelievers come to him with arguments or questions to challenge his message, Allah will provide him with the truth and the best explanation to counter their claims. It emphasizes that the Qur'an is the ultimate truth and that no argument or example brought forth by the disbelievers can stand against it. The verse also highlights the fact that Allah supports His messenger by providing him with the best answers and explanations, ensuring that the truth will always prevail over falsehood.
orig: ولا يأتونك بمثل إلا جئناك بالحق وأحسن تفسيرا

translation: Those who will be gathered on their faces to Hell - those are the worst in position and farthest astray in [their] way.
interpretation: This verse refers to the disbelievers who will be resurrected on the Day of Judgment and will be driven to Hell on their faces. Their position in the Hereafter will be the worst, as they will be humiliated and disgraced. They are described as being the "farthest astray" because, in this world, they deviated from the straight path of guidance and followed their own desires and the whispers of Satan. As a result, they will be far removed from Allah's mercy and will face the consequences of their disbelief and wrongdoings in the depths of Hell.
orig: الذين يحشرون على وجوههم إلى جهنم أولئك شر مكانا وأضل سبيلا

translation: And indeed, We gave Moses the Scripture and made his brother Aaron with him as an assistant.
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of having support and assistance in fulfilling a divine mission. God provided Moses with the Torah as a guide and also appointed his brother Aaron as his helper and minister. This shows that even great prophets like Moses needed support and collaboration to carry out their responsibilities effectively. It also emphasizes the value of family bonds and how they can be utilized for a greater purpose in serving God and guiding people towards righteousness.
orig: ولقد آتينا موسى الكتاب وجعلنا معه أخاه هارون وزيرا

translation: Then We said: "Go both of you to the people who have rejected Our signs." Then We destroyed them with utter destruction.
interpretation: This verse serves as a warning to those who reject the signs and messages of Allah. It shows that Allah sends His messengers to guide people to the right path, but if they persist in their disbelief and rejection, they will face severe consequences and destruction. The verse emphasizes the importance of heeding the warnings and accepting the truth brought by the messengers of Allah, as those who refuse to do so will ultimately face a terrible fate. It also highlights the power and authority of Allah in dealing with those who oppose Him and His messengers.
orig: فقلنا اذهبا إلى القوم الذين كذبوا بآياتنا فدمرناهم تدميرا

translation: And the people of Noah - when they denied the messengers, We drowned them, and We made them for mankind a sign. And We have prepared for the wrongdoers a painful punishment.
interpretation: This verse serves as a stark warning to those who reject the messages and guidance sent by Allah through His prophets. The people of Noah faced severe consequences for their disbelief and defiance, as they were drowned by a great flood. Their fate stands as a clear sign and reminder for all of mankind, demonstrating the gravity of denying the truth and the inevitability of divine justice. The verse also emphasizes that those who persist in wrongdoing and oppression will ultimately face a painful punishment in the Hereafter, highlighting the importance of heeding the warnings and following the path of righteousness.
orig: وقوم نوح لما كذبوا الرسل أغرقناهم وجعلناهم للناس آية وأعتدنا للظالمين عذابا أليما

translation: And [We destroyed] 'Aad and Thamud and the companions of the well and many generations between them.
interpretation: This verse is a reminder of Allah's power and the consequences of disobedience. It mentions ancient nations that were destroyed by Allah due to their rejection of His messengers and their persistence in wrongdoing. 'Aad and Thamud were powerful nations that were destroyed by severe winds and earthquakes respectively, while the "companions of the well" (ashab ar-rass) were a people who threw their prophet into a well. The verse also alludes to many other generations in between these mentioned nations who were also destroyed for their transgressions. It serves as a warning to mankind that no matter how strong or numerous a nation may be, it is not immune to Allah's punishment if it persists in disobedience and rejection of His message. The verse implores us to learn from the fate of these past nations and to strive for righteousness and obedience to Allah.
orig: وعادا وثمود وأصحاب الرس وقرونا بين ذلك كثيرا

translation: And for each [prophet] We presented examples [as warnings], and each [of them] We destroyed with [total] destruction.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah has sent many prophets before Prophet Muhammad, and each of them was given examples and warnings to convey to their people. However, when their respective nations persisted in disbelief and rejection, Allah destroyed them completely. This serves as a reminder that those who continue to reject the message of Islam and the warnings given by the Prophet Muhammad will face a similar fate of destruction in this world and the hereafter. It is a call to heed the examples of the past and embrace the truth before it is too late.
orig: وكلا ضربنا له الأمثال وكلا تبرنا تتبيرا

translation: And indeed they passed by the town which was showered with a bad rain. Did they not see it? Nay! But they used not to expect any resurrection.
interpretation: This verse is a reminder of the consequences of disbelief and rejection of Allah's messages. The people mentioned in the verse passed by the ruins of a town that was destroyed by a terrible rain, likely as a punishment for their sins. Despite seeing the clear signs of destruction, they failed to take heed and continued in their disbelief. They did not believe in the resurrection and the afterlife, where they would be held accountable for their deeds. This lack of belief in the hereafter led them to persist in their wrongdoings without fear of consequences. The verse serves as a warning to those who ignore the signs of Allah and fail to believe in the Day of Judgment.
orig: ولقد أتوا على القرية التي أمطرت مطر السوء أفلم يكونوا يرونها بل كانوا لا يرجون نشورا

translation: And when they see you, they take you not except in ridicule, [saying], "Is this the one whom Allah has sent as a messenger?"
interpretation: This verse reflects the disbelief and mockery of the pagans towards Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him). They ridiculed him and found it hard to accept that Allah had chosen him as a messenger. This highlights their arrogance and inability to recognize the truth, as they judged the Prophet based on their own limited understanding rather than the wisdom of Allah. It also demonstrates the patience and perseverance required of the Prophet in the face of such adversity and rejection, as he continued to convey the message despite the ridicule and opposition he faced.
orig: وإذا رأوك إن يتخذونك إلا هزوا أهذا الذي بعث الله رسولا

translation: He would have almost misled us from our gods had we not been steadfast in [worship of] them. But they are going to know, when they see the punishment, who is more astray in [his] way.
interpretation: This verse is a warning to those who try to lead others astray from the worship of Allah. It emphasizes the importance of remaining steadfast in faith, even in the face of temptation or pressure to abandon one's beliefs. The verse also serves as a reminder that those who mislead others will ultimately face the consequences of their actions on the Day of Judgment, when they will realize the error of their ways and the severity of their punishment. It highlights the idea that the path of truth and righteousness, as ordained by Allah, is the only way to salvation, and that deviating from it will lead to eternal regret and suffering.
orig: إن كاد ليضلنا عن آلهتنا لولا أن صبرنا عليها وسوف يعلمون حين يرون العذاب من أضل سبيلا

translation: Have you seen he who has taken as his god his [own] desire, and Allah has sent him astray due to knowledge and has set a seal upon his hearing and his heart and put over his vision a veil? So who will guide him after Allah? Then will you not be reminded?
interpretation: This verse is a stern warning against following one's own desires and whims instead of the guidance of Allah. It suggests that those who prioritize their own desires over Allah's commands have essentially taken their desires as a false god. As a result, Allah leaves such individuals astray, sealing their hearing and hearts from the truth, and veiling their vision. The verse emphasizes that once Allah has decreed such misguidance on someone due to their choice to follow their desires, no one else can guide them back to the straight path. It concludes with a reminder for us to heed this warning and not fall into the same trap of worshipping our own desires over the worship and obedience of Allah.
orig: أرأيت من اتخذ إلهه هواه أفأنت تكون عليه وكيلا

translation: Or do you think that most of them hear or reason? They are not except like livestock. Rather, they are [even] more astray in [their] way.
interpretation: This verse is a rhetorical question that highlights the lack of understanding and reasoning among those who reject the message of Islam. It compares such people to livestock, suggesting that they are even more misguided than animals. The implication is that animals, at least, follow their God-given instincts, while those who reject divine guidance have strayed from their natural disposition and are lost in their own waywardness. The verse emphasizes the importance of using one's intellect and reasoning faculties to understand and accept the truth, rather than blindly following one's desires or the misguided ways of others.
orig: أم تحسب أن أكثرهم يسمعون أو يعقلون إن هم إلا كالأنعام بل هم أضل سبيلا

translation: Have you not considered your Lord - how He extends the shadow, and if He willed, He could have made it stationary? Then We made the sun for it an indication.
interpretation: This verse is a reminder of Allah's power and wisdom in creating the universe. The extension of the shadow is a sign of His mercy, as it provides comfort and relief from the heat of the sun. If Allah willed, He could have made the shadow permanent, but instead, He made the sun an indicator of the shadow's presence and absence. This serves as a reminder that everything in the universe is under Allah's control and that He has a purpose for everything He creates. It also encourages us to reflect on the signs of Allah's creation and to be grateful for His blessings.
orig: ألم تر إلى ربك كيف مد الظل ولو شاء لجعله ساكنا ثم جعلنا الشمس عليه دليلا

translation: Then We drew it [i.e., the sun] towards Us with an easy drawing.
interpretation: This verse is referring to the eventual fate of the sun. Allah states that He will draw the sun towards Himself with ease, indicating the effortless nature of His power and control over the universe. It alludes to the end of the world, when the current order will be dismantled and the sun will be extinguished or drawn back as a sign of the approaching Day of Judgment. This verse serves as a reminder of Allah's absolute authority and the transient nature of the world, encouraging humans to be mindful of their ultimate return to their Creator.
orig: ثم قبضناه إلينا قبضا يسيرا

translation: And it is He who has made the night for you as clothing and sleep for rest and has made the day a resurrection.
interpretation: In this verse, Allah reminds us of His great blessings and mercy upon mankind. He has created the night as a covering, like a garment that envelops us, providing tranquility and a time for rest. Sleep is described as a means of repose, allowing our bodies and minds to rejuvenate. In contrast, the day is made for us to rise up and engage in our daily activities, seeking sustenance and fulfilling our responsibilities. This natural cycle of night and day is a sign of Allah's wisdom and perfect design, facilitating balance and harmony in our lives. It encourages us to be grateful for these divine gifts and to utilize our time meaningfully, remembering that each new day is an opportunity for spiritual resurrection and striving in the path of righteousness.
orig: وهو الذي جعل لكم الليل لباسا والنوم سباتا وجعل النهار نشورا

translation: And it is He who sends the winds as good tidings before His mercy, and We send down from the sky pure water.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's power and mercy. The winds are sent as a sign of His coming blessings and mercy, giving hope and glad tidings to people. The pure water sent down from the sky is a manifestation of His mercy and a means of purification and life. It symbolizes both physical and spiritual cleansing and rejuvenation. The verse reminds us to be grateful for these gifts and to recognize them as coming from Allah alone.
orig: وهو الذي أرسل الرياح بشرا بين يدي رحمته وأنزلنا من السماء ماء طهورا

translation: That We may give life thereby to a dead land, and We give to drink thereof many cattle and men that We had created.
interpretation: This verse highlights the life-giving power of water, which is a blessing from Allah. It emphasizes that water is essential for the sustenance of all living beings, including both animals and humans. The verse also points to the fact that it is Allah who creates and sustains life on earth by providing water, even to lands that seem barren and lifeless. This serves as a reminder of Allah's omnipotence and His ability to bring forth life from what appears to be dead. Moreover, the verse underscores the importance of water conservation and gratitude for this precious resource, as it is a divine gift that enables the survival of countless creatures.
orig: لنحيي به بلدة ميتا ونسقيه مما خلقنا أنعاما وأناسي كثيرا

translation: And We have certainly diversified [the contents] among them that they might be reminded, but most of the people refuse [anything] except disbelief.
interpretation: This verse suggests that God has provided ample signs, warnings, and reminders to humanity through His revelation, so that they may reflect upon them and be guided to the right path. However, despite these clear signs and messages, the majority of people persist in disbelief and ingratitude. They refuse to acknowledge the truth and instead choose to remain in a state of denial and rejection of God's guidance. This highlights the stubborn nature of human beings who, even when presented with clear evidence, often prefer to follow their own desires and inclinations rather than submit to the will of their Creator.
orig: ولقد صرفناه بينهم ليذكروا فأبى أكثر الناس إلا كفورا

translation: And if We had willed, We could have sent into every city a warner.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's power and wisdom in sending messengers and warners to humanity. It implies that Allah could have easily sent a prophet to every single town or community if He so desired. However, in His infinite wisdom, He chose to send messengers to specific nations at specific times, according to His divine plan. This verse also serves as a reminder that the message of Islam is universal and applicable to all people, regardless of their location or time period. It is the responsibility of those who have received the message to convey it to others and invite them to the path of righteousness.
orig: ولو شئنا لبعثنا في كل قرية نذيرا

translation: So do not obey the disbelievers, and strive against them with the Qur'an a great striving.
interpretation: This verse instructs the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and the believers not to yield to the pressure and opposition of the disbelievers. Instead, they are commanded to exert great effort in conveying the message of the Qur'an and striving against the disbelievers by means of the Qur'an's teachings, wisdom, and arguments. The "great striving" implies a dedicated, unwavering commitment to upholding the truth of Islam and countering the false beliefs and practices of the disbelievers through peaceful dialogue, logical reasoning, and virtuous conduct, while remaining patient in the face of their hostility and persecution.
orig: فلا تطع الكافرين وجاهدهم به جهادا كبيرا

translation: And it is He who has released [simultaneously] the two seas, one fresh and sweet and one salty and bitter, and He placed between them a barrier and prohibiting partition.
interpretation: This verse speaks to the power and wisdom of Allah in creating the natural world. The "two seas" refer to bodies of fresh and salt water, which Allah has caused to flow near each other without mixing due to His design. This is a metaphor for how Allah separates and maintains the order of all things in creation, according to His will. The barrier between the two seas is symbolic of the divine laws and limits that Allah has set in the natural world and in the lives of human beings. Nothing happens except by His permission, and He alone has power to change the nature of what He has created. The verse thus emphasizes Allah's absolute sovereignty, the perfection of His creation, and the importance of recognizing the boundaries He has ordained.
orig: وهو الذي مرج البحرين هذا عذب فرات وهذا ملح أجاج وجعل بينهما برزخا وحجرا محجورا

translation: And it is He who has created from water a human being and made him [a relative by] lineage and marriage. And ever is your Lord competent [concerning creation].
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the power and ability of Allah in creating human beings from a seemingly simple substance, water. It also highlights the importance of family relationships and the institution of marriage, which Allah has established for the continuation and stability of human society. The verse reminds us that Allah is the One who has created these intricate systems and relationships, and He is fully capable of managing and sustaining His creation. It encourages us to reflect on the wisdom and mercy of Allah in His creation and to be grateful for the blessings He has bestowed upon us, including the gift of family and the bond of marriage.
orig: وهو الذي خلق من الماء بشرا فجعله نسبا وصهرا وكان ربك قديرا

translation: And they worship other than Allah that which neither benefits them nor harms them, and the disbeliever is ever, against his Lord, an assistant [to Satan].
interpretation: This verse criticizes those who worship false idols and deities instead of Allah. These false objects of worship have no power to benefit or harm anyone. By engaging in this idolatry and polytheism, the disbelievers are in fact assisting Satan against Allah, even though Allah is their true Lord and Creator. It highlights the foolishness and ingratitude of worshipping anything other than Allah.
orig: ويعبدون من دون الله ما لا ينفعهم ولا يضرهم وكان الكافر على ربه ظهيرا

translation: And We have not sent you, [O Muhammad], except as a bringer of good tidings and a warner.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the role of Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) as a messenger of Allah. His primary duties were to convey the message of Islam, giving glad tidings of Paradise to those who believe and do righteous deeds, and warning those who disbelieve and engage in evil actions of the consequences of their choices. The Prophet's mission was not to force people to accept Islam, but rather to deliver the message clearly and leave the choice to them, while guiding them towards the path of righteousness.
orig: وما أرسلناك إلا مبشرا ونذيرا

translation: Say, "I do not ask you for any reward for this, except that whoever wills may take a path to his Lord."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) did not seek any worldly gain or reward for conveying the message of Islam. His sole intention was to guide people towards the path of righteousness and to help them establish a connection with their Lord. The Prophet's selfless dedication to his mission serves as an example for all believers to follow, reminding them that their ultimate goal should be to seek the pleasure of Allah and to strive towards spiritual growth and nearness to Him, rather than pursuing worldly benefits or recognition.
orig: قل ما أسألكم عليه من أجر إلا من شاء أن يتخذ إلى ربه سبيلا

translation: And put your trust in the Ever-Living who does not die, and exalt [Allah] with His praise. And sufficient is He to be, with the sins of His servants, Acquainted.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of putting one's trust in Allah, who is the Ever-Living and does not die. It encourages the believer to praise and exalt Allah, acknowledging His perfection and supremacy. The verse also highlights Allah's omniscience, as He is fully aware of the sins committed by His servants. It serves as a reminder to the believer to turn to Allah in repentance and seek His forgiveness, while trusting in His guidance and support throughout one's life.
orig: وتوكل على الحي الذي لا يموت وسبح بحمده وكفى به بذنوب عباده خبيرا

translation: Who created the heavens and earth and what is between them in six days and then established Himself above the Throne - the Most Merciful, so ask about Him one well informed.
