interpretation: This verse is emphasizing the absolute power and authority of Allah. It poses a rhetorical question, asking if anyone besides Allah has the ability to help or support either the listener or even themselves. The implied answer is no - only Allah has the power to truly help or grant victory. It conveys the idea that relying on anyone or anything besides Allah is futile, as all power and control ultimately lies with Him alone. The verse encourages complete reliance and trust in Allah above all else.
orig: من دون الله هل ينصرونكم أو ينتصرون

translation: So they will be overturned into it, they and the deviators
interpretation: This verse refers to the fate of the disbelievers and those who have gone astray from the path of Allah on the Day of Judgment. They will be thrown face-first into the Hellfire along with the devils who misled them in the worldly life. It emphasizes the severe punishment that awaits those who reject faith and follow falsehood, highlighting the gravity of their actions and the justice of Allah in recompensing them. The imagery of being overturned into the Fire evokes a sense of humiliation, helplessness, and regret for the choices they made that led them to this outcome.
orig: فكبكبوا فيها هم والغاوون

translation: And the soldiers of Iblees, all together.
interpretation: This verse refers to the forces of evil and temptation that are led by Satan (Iblees). It suggests that these forces are united in their purpose to lead people astray from the path of righteousness. The mention of "soldiers" implies that there is a spiritual battle or struggle between good and evil, with Satan commanding an army of demons and evil influences. The verse serves as a warning to believers to be vigilant against the tactics and deceptions of Satan and his allies, who are constantly working to undermine faith and morality.
orig: وجنود إبليس أجمعون

translation: They will say while they dispute therein,
interpretation: This verse refers to the people in Hell who will be arguing and disputing with each other. They will be blaming one another for their fate and regretting their actions in the worldly life that led them to this punishment. This highlights the severity of the punishment in Hell and the hopelessness of its inhabitants. It also serves as a warning to people to be mindful of their actions and to follow the right path to avoid such a fate in the Hereafter.
orig: قالوا وهم فيها يختصمون

translation: By Allah, we were indeed in manifest error
interpretation: This verse is an admission of the disbelievers on the Day of Judgment that they were clearly misguided and in error during their worldly life by rejecting Allah's messages and revelations. It highlights the regret they will feel for not following the right path when the truth becomes evident to them in the Hereafter. The verse emphasizes the importance of faith and submission to Allah in this life to avoid such regret and punishment in the next.
orig: تالله إن كنا لفي ضلال مبين

translation: When We equate you with the Lord of the worlds.
interpretation: This verse is a rhetorical question that God poses to humanity, reminding them of the great honor and privilege that He has bestowed upon them by creating them in the best of forms and favoring them over much of His creation. It is a reminder for humans not to be arrogant or ungrateful, but to humble themselves before their Creator and acknowledge His greatness and superiority over all things. The verse also implies that associating partners with God or claiming to be equal to Him is a grave sin and a sign of ingratitude towards the One who created us and granted us countless blessings.
orig: إذ نسويكم برب العالمين

translation: And no one misled us except the criminals.
interpretation: This verse suggests that those who have gone astray and followed the wrong path have been misled by the criminals, the wrongdoers, and the sinners. It implies that the responsibility for being misguided lies with those who engage in criminal and sinful acts, as they lead others away from the straight path through their bad influence and example. The verse serves as a reminder to be cautious of following those who engage in wrongdoing, as they can lead one astray from the path of righteousness.
orig: وما أضلنا إلا المجرمون

translation: So now we have no intercessors.
interpretation: This verse suggests that on the Day of Judgment, no one will be able to intercede or plead on behalf of the sinners. They will have to face the consequences of their actions alone, without anyone to speak in their favor or seek forgiveness for them from Allah. It emphasizes the individual responsibility and accountability for one's deeds, and that ultimately, each person will have to answer for their own actions without relying on anyone else to save them from Allah's judgment.
orig: فما لنا من شافعين

translation: And no intimate friend
interpretation: This verse suggests that in the end, a person will have no close friend or companion to help them or stand by their side. It emphasizes the ultimate loneliness and helplessness one may face, especially in the context of the Day of Judgment or in times of great difficulty. The verse reminds us that our true reliance should be on Allah alone, as even our closest friends may not be there for us in our time of greatest need.
orig: ولا صديق حميم

translation: If only we had another chance, we would be among the believers.
interpretation: This verse conveys the deep regret and remorse felt by those who rejected faith in this life when they are faced with the realities of the Hereafter. It highlights the finality of death and the lost opportunity for redemption once one passes from this world. The verse serves as a warning to those who disbelieve, emphasizing that they should seize the opportunity to embrace faith before it is too late, as there are no second chances after death. It is a reminder to all of us about the importance of making the right choices in this life, as they will determine our eternal fate in the next.
orig: فلو أن لنا كرة فنكون من المؤمنين

translation: Indeed in that is a sign, but most of them were not to be believers.
interpretation: This verse points to the fact that even though there are clear signs and evidence of Allah's existence and power in the world around us, many people still choose not to believe. It suggests that disbelief is often a matter of choice and willful rejection of the truth, rather than a lack of evidence. The verse also implies that true faith is not something that can be forced or coerced, but is ultimately a matter of individual conviction and submission to God's will.
orig: إن في ذلك لآية وما كان أكثرهم مؤمنين

translation: And indeed, your Lord is the Exalted in Might, the Merciful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes two important attributes of Allah: His power and His mercy. The word "Al-Azeez" signifies that Allah is Almighty, All-Powerful, and none can overcome Him. At the same time, He is "Ar-Raheem", the Most Merciful, showing immense compassion and kindness to His creation. This verse serves as a reminder for believers to have faith in Allah's power to help and support them, while also having hope in His mercy and forgiveness. It encourages us to turn to Him in both good times and difficult times, seeking His aid and mercy, knowing that He is capable of all things and His mercy encompasses all.
orig: وإن ربك لهو العزيز الرحيم

translation: The people of Noah denied the messengers.
interpretation: This verse refers to the story of Prophet Noah and his people. The people of Noah rejected Noah's message and refused to believe in the one true God. They denied not only Noah but all the messengers sent by God. This denial and rejection of the truth is a common theme in the Qur'an, with many nations throughout history refusing to heed the warnings of their prophets. The verse emphasizes the stubbornness and arrogance of those who turn away from divine guidance, and serves as a warning to all people to have faith and follow the path of righteousness.
orig: كذبت قوم نوح المرسلين

translation: When their brother Noah said to them, "Will you not fear Allah?"
interpretation: In this verse, Noah, who is referred to as the brother of his people, is calling upon them to have taqwa, which is the fear of Allah that inspires righteousness and piety. He is reminding them of their obligation to worship Allah alone and to live their lives in accordance with His commands. This call to taqwa is a central theme in the Islamic concept of prophethood, as all prophets were sent to guide their people to the straight path and to warn them of the consequences of disobedience to Allah. The verse highlights the importance of heeding the call of the prophets and the need for people to constantly examine their actions and intentions in light of their faith.
orig: إذ قال لهم أخوهم نوح ألا تتقون

translation: Indeed, I am to you a trustworthy messenger.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of trust and honesty in the role of a messenger or prophet. The speaker, likely a prophet, is assuring his audience that he is a reliable and truthful conveyer of the divine message. This highlights the significance of having faith in the integrity of God's chosen messengers, as they are responsible for guiding people to the right path. The verse also implies that the messenger's trustworthiness is a crucial aspect of his mission, as it enables people to have confidence in the message he delivers and follow his guidance without doubt or hesitation.
orig: إني لكم رسول أمين

translation: So fear Allah and obey me.
interpretation: This verse is a call to righteousness and submission to Allah. It reminds believers to have consciousness (taqwa) of Allah, which means to be ever mindful of Him, to fear His displeasure, and to hope for His mercy. Along with this, the verse commands obedience to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him), as obeying him is tantamount to obeying Allah. Taqwa and obedience are two essential qualities of true faith. This concise verse encapsulates the core of the Islamic way of life - to live with mindfulness of the Divine and to follow the guidance brought by the Prophet (peace be upon him). It is an exhortation to stay on the Straight Path through God-consciousness and prophetic example.
orig: فاتقوا الله وأطيعون

translation: And I do not ask you for it any payment. My payment is only from the Lord of the worlds.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the prophet is not seeking any worldly gain or compensation for conveying the message of Islam. His sole purpose is to fulfill the duty entrusted to him by Allah, the Lord of all creation. The prophet's reward and recompense lies solely with God, not with the people he is sent to guide. This highlights the sincerity and selflessness of the prophet's mission, as he is not motivated by any personal or material gain, but rather by his obedience and devotion to Allah.
orig: وما أسألكم عليه من أجر إن أجري إلا على رب العالمين

translation: So fear Allah and obey me.
interpretation: This verse is a call to the believers to have consciousness of Allah (taqwa) and to obey His messenger. It emphasizes the importance of submission to the will of Allah and following the guidance and teachings of His prophet. Taqwa is a central concept in Islam, referring to being mindful of Allah, fearing His displeasure, and striving to do what pleases Him. Obedience to the messenger is linked with obedience to Allah Himself, as the prophet conveys Allah's message and his sunnah is a manifestation of Quranic teachings. This verse reminds us that the path to success and salvation lies in having taqwa and aligning our actions with the guidance of Allah and His messenger.
orig: فاتقوا الله وأطيعون

translation: They said, "Should we believe you while the lowest [class of people] follow you?"
interpretation: This verse reflects the arrogance and pride of the elite who rejected the message of the prophets. They looked down upon the followers of the prophets, considering them to be from the lowest class of society, and therefore unworthy of being followed. The elite believed that their social status and wealth made them superior and that they should not follow the same religion as the poor and weak. This attitude stems from their lack of understanding of the true value of faith and the equality of all people before God. The verse highlights the importance of humility and the rejection of social hierarchy in matters of faith.
orig: قالوا أنؤمن لك واتبعك الأرذلون

translation: He said, "And what knowledge have I of what they used to do?"
interpretation: This verse is a declaration of Prophet Muhammad's (peace be upon him) lack of knowledge about the deeds and actions of the previous nations. It emphasizes that the Prophet had no way of knowing what happened in the past except through divine revelation from Allah. This highlights the fact that the Qur'an is not a product of the Prophet's own knowledge or imagination, but rather a direct revelation from God. It also serves as a reminder that the Prophet, despite his elevated status, was still a human being with limited knowledge and that all knowledge ultimately belongs to Allah.
orig: قال وما علمي بما كانوا يعملون

translation: Indeed, their account is only upon my Lord, if you could perceive.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that ultimately, it is Allah alone who will hold people accountable for their deeds and intentions. The phrase "if you could perceive" suggests that this reality may not be apparent to everyone, but those with spiritual insight and understanding recognize that we are all answerable to our Lord. It is a reminder to focus on our own actions and relationship with Allah, rather than being overly concerned with judging or condemning others, as their ultimate reckoning is with Him alone.
orig: إن حسابهم إلا على ربي لو تشعرون

translation: And I am not the one to drive away the believers.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) was not sent to turn away or reject those who believe in Allah's message. As a messenger of God, his duty was to invite people to faith, not to push away the sincere believers. It highlights the inclusive nature of Islam, indicating that the Prophet's mission was to embrace and guide all those who accepted the truth, regardless of their social status or background. The verse also serves as a reminder to the believers to be welcoming and accommodating towards fellow believers, creating a sense of unity and brotherhood within the Muslim community.
orig: وما أنا بطارد المؤمنين

translation: I am only a clear warner.
interpretation: The role of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) is to serve as a clear warner to humanity. His duty is to convey the message of Islam plainly and unambiguously, making people aware of the consequences of their actions in this world and the Hereafter. He is not responsible for forcing people to accept the message or for their ultimate fate. His mission is simply to deliver the warning with utmost clarity, so that no one has an excuse on the Day of Judgment that they were not informed or reminded of the truth.
orig: إن أنا إلا نذير مبين

translation: They said, "If you do not desist, O Noah, you will surely be of those who are stoned."
interpretation: This verse shows the hostility and stubbornness of Noah's people towards his message. They threatened him with stoning, which was a severe punishment, if he did not stop preaching his faith in one God. It reflects their deep-rooted attachment to their polytheistic beliefs and their unwillingness to listen to the truth that Noah was conveying to them. The verse also highlights the great patience and perseverance of Prophet Noah in the face of such strong opposition and threats, as he continued his mission with steadfastness, trusting in God's support and protection.
orig: قالوا لئن لم تنته يا نوح لتكونن من المرجومين

translation: He said, "My Lord, indeed my people have denied me."
interpretation: In this verse, a prophet (likely Noah) is expressing his frustration and sadness to Allah that despite his best efforts to guide his people to the right path, they have rejected his message and denied him. This highlights the challenges faced by prophets in conveying the divine message to their communities, and the disappointment they feel when their efforts are met with disbelief and opposition. It also emphasizes the importance of patience and perseverance in the face of adversity, and the need to turn to Allah for support and guidance during difficult times.
orig: قال رب إن قومي كذبون

translation: So judge between me and them with decisive judgement and save me and those with me of the believers.
interpretation: This verse is a prayer of Prophet Moses, asking Allah to judge between him and his opponents, and to grant him and his believing followers salvation and deliverance from their oppressors. It reflects the believer's trust in Allah's justice and power to save the righteous from harm, even in the face of powerful enemies. The verse also highlights the importance of solidarity among believers in the face of adversity, as Moses prays not just for himself but for all those who believed with him.
orig: فافتح بيني وبينهم فتحا ونجني ومن معي من المؤمنين

translation: So We saved him and those with him in the laden ship.
interpretation: This verse refers to the story of Prophet Noah (peace be upon him). It indicates that Allah saved Noah and the believers who followed him by instructing them to board the ark, which was filled with pairs of living creatures. This event demonstrates Allah's mercy and power in protecting His faithful servants from calamity, while punishing the disbelievers who rejected Noah's message. The verse emphasizes the importance of faith and obedience to Allah, as it is the key to salvation in both this world and the hereafter.
orig: فأنجيناه ومن معه في الفلك المشحون

translation: Then afterwards We drowned the others.
interpretation: This verse refers to the story of Prophet Moses and the Israelites. After Allah saved the believers by parting the sea and allowing them to cross safely, He caused the pursuing army of Pharaoh to be drowned as the waters closed in on them. This demonstrates Allah's power over all things and His ability to save the righteous and destroy the wicked. It serves as a reminder that no matter how powerful or numerous the enemies of faith may seem, ultimately Allah's will shall prevail and those who reject His messages will face the consequences of their choices in this life and the Hereafter.
orig: ثم أغرقنا بعد الباقين

translation: Indeed in that is a sign, but most of them were not to be believers.
interpretation: This verse points to the fact that even though there are clear signs and evidence of Allah's existence and power in the world around us, many people still choose not to believe. It suggests that disbelief is often a matter of choice and willful rejection of the truth, rather than a lack of evidence. The verse also implies that true faith is not something that can be forced or coerced, but is ultimately a matter of individual conviction and submission to God's will.
orig: إن في ذلك لآية وما كان أكثرهم مؤمنين

translation: And indeed, your Lord is the Exalted in Might, the Merciful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes two important attributes of Allah: His power and His mercy. "Al-Aziz" (the Exalted in Might) signifies that Allah is supremely powerful, and no one can overcome or defeat Him. At the same time, He is "Ar-Raheem" (the Merciful), which means that despite His immense power, Allah treats His creation with kindness, care, and compassion. The juxtaposition of these two attributes highlights the perfect balance in Allah's nature. It serves as a reminder for believers to have hope in Allah's mercy while also being in awe of His power and majesty. This verse encourages Muslims to turn to Allah for help and guidance, knowing that He is capable of all things and that His mercy encompasses all.
orig: وإن ربك لهو العزيز الرحيم

translation: The people of 'Aad denied the messengers.
interpretation: This verse refers to the ancient Arabian tribe of 'Aad who rejected the warnings and message brought to them by the prophets sent by Allah. It highlights the arrogance and disbelief of the people, as they refused to acknowledge the truth despite clear signs and admonitions from the messengers. The denial of the messengers is equated to denying Allah Himself, as the messengers were sent by Him to guide humanity. This verse serves as a reminder of the consequences of rejecting divine guidance and the importance of heeding the call of the prophets.
orig: كذبت عاد المرسلين

translation: When their brother Hud said to them, "Will you not fear Allah?"
interpretation: This verse is a reminder from the prophet Hud to his people, the 'Ad, to be mindful of Allah and to fear Him. It is a call to righteousness, to abandon their wrongdoings and to submit to the will of Allah. Hud is appealing to their conscience, urging them to recognize the error of their ways and to turn back to the path of truth. The rhetorical question "Will you not fear Allah?" is a powerful admonition, emphasizing the importance of having taqwa, or God-consciousness, which is the foundation of faith and the key to salvation. It implies that by neglecting their duty to Allah, they are inviting His displeasure and risking severe consequences in this life and the hereafter.
orig: إذ قال لهم أخوهم هود ألا تتقون

translation: Indeed, I am to you a trustworthy messenger.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the trustworthiness and reliability of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) as a messenger of Allah. It assures the audience that he is a honest and dependable conveyor of the divine message, and that they can have full confidence in the truth and authenticity of the revelations he brings. The verse underscores the Prophet's integrity and his unwavering commitment to faithfully delivering Allah's words without any alteration or personal interest.
orig: إني لكم رسول أمين

translation: So fear Allah and obey me.
interpretation: This verse is a call to the believers to have taqwa (God-consciousness) and to obey the commands of Allah as conveyed by His messenger. It emphasizes the importance of submitting to the will of Allah and following the guidance provided by the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him). Having taqwa and obedience are essential qualities of true faith and are necessary for attaining success and salvation in this world and the Hereafter. The verse also implies that disobeying Allah and His messenger leads to negative consequences and loss. Therefore, the believers should strive to cultivate taqwa and obedience in their hearts and actions.
orig: فاتقوا الله وأطيعون

translation: And I do not ask you for it any payment. My payment is only from the Lord of the worlds.
interpretation: The prophet is emphasizing that he does not seek any worldly reward or compensation for conveying the message of Islam. His only desire is to please Allah and fulfill the duty with which he has been entrusted. This highlights the sincerity and selflessness that should characterize the preaching of faith, which is done for the sake of God alone, not for any material gain or personal benefit in this life. The prophet's ultimate reward is with Allah, the Lord of all creation, in the Hereafter.
orig: وما أسألكم عليه من أجر إن أجري إلا على رب العالمين

translation: Do you construct on every elevation a sign, amusing yourselves,
interpretation: This verse is criticizing those who build monuments or structures in prominent places out of vanity and for worldly purposes, rather than for the sake of God. The "signs" they construct are meaningless because they serve no higher purpose and are only for show or amusement. It suggests that one should be humble and make good use of resources, not waste them on ostentatious displays that don't benefit society or honor the divine. The verse reminds us to check our intentions and not get caught up in ego-driven pursuits that distract from what truly matters in life.
orig: أتبنون بكل ريع آية تعبثون

translation: And you take for yourselves palaces and fortresses that you might abide eternally?
interpretation: This verse is criticizing the people who build grand structures and fortresses with the intention of living forever, as if they can escape death. It is a reminder that no matter how much worldly power and wealth one accumulates, it is all temporary and fleeting. The Qur'an emphasizes that true eternal life is in the hereafter, and that one should focus on good deeds and righteousness rather than material pursuits. The verse encourages humility and the realization that all humans are mortal and will eventually face judgment before Allah.
orig: وتتخذون مصانع لعلكم تخلدون

translation: And when you strike, you strike as tyrants.
interpretation: This verse is a condemnation of those who use excessive force and act in a tyrannical manner when they have power over others. It suggests that such people, when they seize upon others, do so in an oppressive and merciless way, like despots who have no regard for justice or human life. The implication is that this kind of behavior is unacceptable and blameworthy in the sight of God. The verse calls on believers to act with justice, restraint and mercy, even when they have the upper hand, and not to succumb to the temptation of abusing their power in the manner of oppressive tyrants.
orig: وإذا بطشتم بطشتم جبارين

translation: So fear Allah and obey me.
interpretation: This verse is a call to righteousness and submission to Allah. It reminds believers to have consciousness (taqwa) of Allah, which means to be ever mindful of Him, to fear His displeasure, and to hope for His mercy. Along with this awareness, the verse commands obedience to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) as Allah's Messenger. Obeying the Prophet is tantamount to obeying Allah Himself. So the core message is that one should align their life with the teachings of Islam out of love, reverence and fear of Allah, submitting to His will as conveyed through the example and instructions of His chosen Prophet. It encapsulates the heart of being a Muslim - God-consciousness combined with adherence to the prophetic way.
orig: فاتقوا الله وأطيعون

translation: And fear the One who provided you with what you know.
interpretation: This verse is a reminder for people to be mindful and fearful of Allah, who has bestowed upon them various blessings and knowledge. It emphasizes the importance of acknowledging the source of one's abilities and resources, and being grateful to the Almighty. The verse also implies that with knowledge comes responsibility; as humans are equipped with understanding and awareness, they should use it to make righteous decisions and avoid transgressing the boundaries set by Allah. Ultimately, the verse encourages individuals to lead a life of piety, gratitude, and obedience to the One who has provided them with everything they know and possess.
orig: واتقوا الذي أمدكم بما تعلمون

translation: He will provide for you with cattle and children
interpretation: This verse is a promise from Allah to provide sustenance and blessings in the form of livestock and offspring to those who are righteous and follow His path. Cattle represent wealth and provision, as they can be used for food, clothing, transportation, and trade. Children are a gift that bring joy, purpose, and continuation of one's lineage and legacy. The mention of both cattle and children together emphasizes the comprehensive nature of Allah's provision, covering both material and emotional needs. It is a reminder to be grateful for these blessings and to use them in a way that pleases Allah.
orig: أمدكم بأنعام وبنين

translation: And gardens and springs
interpretation: This verse is referring to the rewards that await the righteous believers in Paradise. The "gardens" mentioned are the lush, beautiful gardens of Paradise, filled with delights beyond imagination. The "springs" are the flowing springs of pure, delicious water in Paradise. These gardens and springs are a symbolic representation of the peace, comfort, and eternal bliss that the believers will experience in the afterlife as a reward for their faith and good deeds in this world. It is a reminder that the ultimate goal is to strive for the eternal Paradise in the Hereafter, rather than being solely focused on the temporary pleasures of this worldly life.
orig: وجنات وعيون

translation: Indeed, I fear for you the punishment of a tremendous Day.
interpretation: This verse conveys a dire warning from a prophet or messenger to their people. The prophet expresses deep concern and fear that if the people continue in their wrongdoing and rejection of divine guidance, they will face severe consequences on a momentous Day of Judgment. It emphasizes the gravity of the people's choices and actions in this world, as they will be held accountable in the Hereafter. The verse aims to shake the people's conscience, urging them to change their ways and turn to God's path before it is too late, so that they may be saved from a terrible fate in the afterlife.
orig: إني أخاف عليكم عذاب يوم عظيم

translation: They said, "It is all the same to us whether you advise or are not of the advisors."
interpretation: This verse is referring to the disbelievers who are so stubborn in their disbelief that they are not willing to listen to any advice or warning from the prophets and messengers sent by Allah. They are saying that it makes no difference to them whether someone tries to advise them or not, as they have already made up their minds to reject the message and persist in their wrongdoing. It reflects the depth of their arrogance and their unwillingness to consider the truth, even when it is presented to them clearly. They have sealed their own fate by choosing to turn away from divine guidance.
orig: قالوا سواء علينا أوعظت أم لم تكن من الواعظين

translation: This is not but the tradition of the former peoples.
interpretation: This verse suggests that the disbelievers are rejecting the message of Islam, claiming that it is nothing new or unique, but merely a repetition of the beliefs and practices of previous generations. They are dismissing the Prophet's teachings as a mere imitation of ancient traditions, rather than a divine revelation. The Qur'an refutes this notion by emphasizing that the message of Islam is a continuation and confirmation of the eternal truth revealed to all prophets throughout history, while also bringing new guidance and wisdom relevant to the current time and context.
orig: إن هذا إلا خلق الأولين

translation: And We will not punish.
interpretation: This verse conveys that Allah, in His infinite mercy and justice, does not punish people without first sending them guidance and warnings through His messengers. It emphasizes the idea that Allah gives humans the opportunity to follow the right path and that punishment only comes after clear warnings have been given and ignored. This highlights Allah's attribute of being Just (Al-'Adl) and not subjecting His creation to punishment without giving them a chance to reform and seek forgiveness.
orig: وما نحن بمعذبين

translation: And they denied him, so We destroyed them. Indeed in that is a sign, but most of them were not to be believers.
interpretation: This verse serves as a warning and reminder that those who reject the truth and the messengers of Allah will face severe consequences. The destruction of the disbelievers mentioned in this verse is a sign of Allah's power and a lesson for future generations. However, despite such clear signs, the majority of people still choose not to believe in the message and follow the path of righteousness. This highlights the stubborn nature of human beings and their tendency to ignore divine guidance, even when presented with clear evidence.
orig: فكذبوه فأهلكناهم إن في ذلك لآية وما كان أكثرهم مؤمنين

translation: And indeed, your Lord is the Exalted in Might, the Merciful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes two important attributes of Allah: His power and His mercy. The phrase "Exalted in Might" (Al-Azeez) signifies that Allah is all-powerful, omnipotent, and has the ability to do whatever He wills. No one can overcome or defeat Him. At the same time, He is also "the Merciful" (Ar-Raheem), indicating that along with His might, Allah is exceedingly merciful and compassionate towards His creation. He provides for them, guides them, and forgives their sins when they repent sincerely. The juxtaposition of these two attributes highlights the balance between Allah's power and His mercy, reminding believers that while they should revere and fear Allah's might, they can also find comfort in His boundless mercy and love.
orig: وإن ربك لهو العزيز الرحيم

translation: Thamud denied the messengers.
interpretation: This verse is referring to the people of Thamud, an ancient civilization that rejected the message brought to them by their prophet, Salih. The Thamud were a prosperous people, but they were arrogant and refused to believe in the oneness of God and the message of their prophet. As a result, they were ultimately destroyed by a divine punishment. This verse serves as a warning to those who reject the truth and the messengers of God, reminding us of the consequences of denying the divine message and the importance of heeding the call of the prophets.
orig: كذبت ثمود المرسلين

translation: When their brother Salih said to them, "Will you not fear Allah?"
interpretation: This verse is a reminder from Prophet Salih to his people, the Thamud, to be mindful of Allah and obey His commands. It emphasizes the importance of taqwa (God-consciousness) and the role of prophets in guiding their communities towards righteousness. The verse also implies that the Thamud were not heeding the warnings and guidance provided by their prophet, highlighting their disobedience and the potential consequences they may face as a result of their actions. It serves as a warning to all believers to fear Allah, follow the guidance of His messengers, and avoid the fate of those who reject divine guidance.
orig: إذ قال لهم أخوهم صالح ألا تتقون

translation: Indeed, I am to you a trustworthy messenger.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the honesty and trustworthiness of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) in conveying the message of Islam. As a messenger of Allah, he was reliable and sincere in delivering the divine revelation without any alteration or concealment. The verse assures the audience that they can have full faith in the Prophet's words and actions, as he was a man of integrity chosen by Allah to guide humanity to the straight path. It highlights the importance of trust in the relationship between the Prophet and his followers, as well as the significance of honesty and reliability in conveying the truth.
orig: إني لكم رسول أمين

translation: So fear Allah and obey me.
interpretation: This verse is a call to the believers to have consciousness of Allah (taqwa) and to obey His messenger. It emphasizes the importance of submission to the will of Allah and following the guidance and teachings of His prophet. Taqwa, often translated as "fear of Allah", actually encompasses a wider meaning of being ever-mindful of Allah, having reverence for Him, and being in a state of obedience to His commands and avoidance of His prohibitions. The verse links taqwa with obedience to the messenger, indicating that true piety and righteousness lies in adhering to the path shown by the prophet, as he is the one who conveys the message of Allah to humanity. It is an injunction for the believers to align their intentions and actions with the pleasure of Allah and to follow the example of the prophet in all aspects of life.
orig: فاتقوا الله وأطيعون

translation: And I do not ask you for it any payment. My payment is only from the Lord of the worlds.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes that the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) did not seek any worldly reward or compensation for conveying the message of Islam. His sole motivation was to please Allah, the Lord of all creation, and he looked to Him alone for his ultimate reward in the Hereafter. This demonstrates the Prophet's sincerity, selflessness, and complete trust in Allah's promise of recompense for his efforts in guiding humanity to the path of righteousness.
orig: وما أسألكم عليه من أجر إن أجري إلا على رب العالمين

translation: Do you feel secure in that which is here?
interpretation: This verse is a reminder that the material possessions and comforts of this worldly life are fleeting and temporary. It calls into question the false sense of security that people may derive from their wealth, status, or earthly attachments. The verse implores the reader to reflect on the transient nature of the world and not to be deluded by its illusory sense of permanence or safety. It suggests that true security and peace can only be found through faith in God and by placing one's trust in Him, rather than in the ephemeral trappings of the material realm.
orig: أتتركون في ما هاهنا آمنين

translation: In gardens and springs
interpretation: This verse refers to the eternal abode of the righteous believers in Paradise. The "gardens" mentioned here are the lush, beautiful gardens of Paradise, filled with delightful amenities and breathtaking scenery. The "springs" allude to the abundant flowing water in Paradise, which symbolizes purity, refreshment, and the endless blessings bestowed upon the inhabitants of Paradise by Allah. This verse serves as a reminder and motivation for believers to strive for righteousness in this world, so that they may attain the everlasting bliss of dwelling in the gardens and by the springs of Paradise in the Hereafter.
orig: في جنات وعيون

translation: And [fields of] crops and palm trees with softened fruit clusters [hanging] low.
interpretation: This verse is drawing attention to the beauty and bounty of Allah's creation. The mention of crops and palm trees with ripe, low-hanging fruit clusters ready for harvest is a reminder of Allah's favor upon mankind in providing sustenance and the means of life. It also points to the perfect design in nature, where these plants are created in a way to facilitate easy gathering of the fruits by humans. The verse invokes a sense of gratitude for the blessings and provisions bestowed by the Creator.
orig: وزروع ونخل طلعها هضيم

translation: And you carve out of the mountains, homes, with great skill.
interpretation: This verse highlights the ingenuity and craftsmanship of humans in utilizing natural resources, such as mountains, to create dwellings and structures. It points to the God-given ability of humans to shape their environment and construct impressive buildings and homes, even in challenging terrain like mountains. The verse also implies that such skill and mastery over the environment is a blessing from God, and should be used responsibly and with gratitude.
orig: وتنحتون من الجبال بيوتا فارهين

translation: So fear Allah and obey me.
interpretation: This verse is a command from Allah to mankind to have consciousness and fear of Him, and to obey His messenger. It emphasizes the importance of submission to Allah and following the guidance and teachings brought by His prophet. Taqwa, or fear of Allah, is a central concept in Islam that motivates believers to stay away from sin and to strive for righteousness. Obedience to the messenger is also critical, as he conveys the message and instructions of Allah. The verse reminds us that true success lies in aligning our will with the will of our Creator and abiding by His commandments.
orig: فاتقوا الله وأطيعون

translation: And do not obey the command of the transgressors,
interpretation: This verse warns believers against following the orders or desires of those who are extravagant and wasteful in their actions and behavior. "Al-musrifeen" refers to those who exceed the limits set by Allah, indulging in excesses and committing sins without regard for divine guidance. The Qur'an instructs us not to obey such individuals as they will lead us astray from the straight path of righteousness and moderation. Instead, we should adhere to Allah's commands and the teachings of His Prophet (peace be upon him), using our reason and conscience to discern right from wrong. Obeying the transgressors ultimately leads to corruption and spiritual ruin.
orig: ولا تطيعوا أمر المسرفين

translation: Those who spread corruption on earth and do not amend [their ways]
interpretation: This verse is referring to those individuals who actively engage in spreading mischief, chaos, and corruption in society, without making any efforts to rectify their behavior or make amends. They are people who cause harm and damage to others and the environment, without any regard for the consequences of their actions. The Qur'an strongly condemns such behavior and warns of severe punishment for those who persist in spreading corruption and fail to reform themselves.
orig: الذين يفسدون في الأرض ولا يصلحون

translation: They said, "You are only of those affected by magic."
interpretation: The disbelievers are accusing the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) of being under the influence of magic or sorcery. They are dismissing his message and claiming that he is not a true prophet, but rather someone who has been bewitched or enchanted. This accusation is baseless and reflects their stubborn refusal to accept the truth of Islam despite the clear signs and evidence presented to them. It shows their arrogance and their desire to cling to their false beliefs rather than submit to the will of Allah.
orig: قالوا إنما أنت من المسحرين

translation: You are not but a man like us, so bring a sign, if you should be of the truthful.
interpretation: This verse is challenging the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him), saying that he is just a human being like everyone else, and demanding that he produce a miracle or sign to prove his claim of being a messenger of God. It reflects the skepticism and disbelief of those who opposed the Prophet's message, and their unwillingness to accept him without tangible evidence of his divine appointment. The verse implies that if Muhammad were truly a prophet, he should be able to perform supernatural feats as proof of his status. This demand for a sign is a recurring theme in the Qur'an, as many of the Prophet's contemporaries refused to believe in him without witnessing miracles. However, the Qur'an asserts that the Prophet's greatest miracle is the Qur'an itself, and that true faith does not require physical signs but rather stems from an open heart and mind receptive to the truth of God's message.
orig: ما أنت إلا بشر مثلنا فأت بآية إن كنت من الصادقين

translation: He said, "This is a she-camel; she has a [time of] drink, and you have a [time of] drink, [each] on a known day."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of sharing resources fairly and equitably. The she-camel is a symbol of God's blessing and provision, and both the camel and the people have a designated time to drink from the water source. This teaches us that we should respect the rights and needs of others, and not monopolize or exploit shared resources. It also highlights the value of setting clear boundaries and agreements to prevent conflict and ensure everyone's needs are met. Ultimately, this verse encourages us to live in harmony with one another and with the natural world, recognizing that we are all interconnected and dependent on God's sustenance.
orig: قال هذه ناقة لها شرب ولكم شرب يوم معلوم

translation: And do not touch it with evil lest you be seized by the punishment of a tremendous Day.
interpretation: This verse serves as a warning to those who might attempt to harm or corrupt the revelations of Allah. It emphasizes the severity of the punishment that awaits those who engage in such actions, likening it to the punishment of a "tremendous Day" which could refer to the Day of Judgment. The verse implies that the Qur'an and its teachings are sacred and should be treated with the utmost respect and reverence. Attempting to alter, distort or malign the word of Allah is a grave sin that will invite His wrath and lead to severe consequences in this world and the Hereafter. The verse thus encourages believers to safeguard the integrity of the Qur'an and to approach it with a pure heart and righteous intentions.
orig: ولا تمسوها بسوء فيأخذكم عذاب يوم عظيم

translation: So they hamstrung her, and then they became regretful.
interpretation: This verse is a warning against disobedience to Allah's commands and the consequences that follow. The people of Thamud, despite being warned by the prophet Salih (peace be upon him), arrogantly decided to defy Allah's sign by killing the she-camel sent as a miracle. As a result of their defiance and cruelty, they were overcome with regret for their actions. However, it was too late, and they had to face the divine punishment for their disobedience. This verse emphasizes the importance of heeding the warnings of Allah's messengers and refraining from transgressing the limits set by Him. It also highlights the fact that regret after committing a sin does not absolve one of the consequences unless it is coupled with sincere repentance and seeking forgiveness from Allah.
orig: فعقروها فأصبحوا نادمين

translation: So the punishment seized them. Indeed in that is a sign, but most of them were not to be believers.
interpretation: This verse serves as a reminder that divine punishment can befall those who reject faith and persist in wrongdoing. The events described are meant to be a clear sign of God's power and justice, yet despite such signs, many people still choose not to believe. It highlights the stubborn nature of disbelief, even in the face of clear evidence. The verse also implies that true faith is not simply a matter of witnessing miracles, but requires a deeper spiritual commitment and openness to divine guidance.
orig: فأخذهم العذاب إن في ذلك لآية وما كان أكثرهم مؤمنين

translation: And indeed, your Lord is the Exalted in Might, the Merciful.
interpretation: This verse affirms two important attributes of Allah: His power and His mercy. "Al-Aziz" (the Exalted in Might) emphasizes Allah's absolute power, strength, and control over all things. He is the One who has the ability to do whatever He wills, and no one can overcome or resist His decree. "Ar-Rahim" (the Merciful) highlights Allah's immense mercy, compassion, and kindness towards His creation. He showers His servants with blessings, forgives their sins, and guides them to the right path. The combination of these two attributes in this verse serves as a reminder for believers to have hope in Allah's mercy while also being in awe of His power and majesty. It encourages them to turn to Him in repentance, seek His forgiveness, and strive to earn His pleasure through righteous deeds, knowing that He is both mighty and merciful.
orig: وإن ربك لهو العزيز الرحيم

translation: The people of Lot denied the messengers.
interpretation: This verse refers to the story of the Prophet Lot and his people. The people of Lot rejected the message of monotheism and the warnings against their immoral practices that Lot conveyed to them. They refused to believe in Lot as a messenger of Allah and in the divine message he brought. This denial and rejection of the messengers is a common theme in the Qur'an, highlighting the stubbornness and arrogance of those who oppose the truth despite clear signs and warnings. The verse emphasizes the gravity of denying Allah's messengers and the consequences that such denial brings in this world and the hereafter.
orig: كذبت قوم لوط المرسلين

translation: When their brother Lot said to them, "Will you not fear Allah?"
interpretation: In this verse, the Prophet Lot (peace be upon him) is addressing his people, urging them to have consciousness of Allah and to abandon their immoral and sinful ways. As their brother and a messenger of Allah, Lot is reminding them of their duty to obey Allah and warning them of the consequences of their actions if they persist in disobedience. The rhetorical question "Will you not fear Allah?" is a powerful appeal to their conscience and an invitation to repent and reform themselves before it is too late. It highlights the importance of taqwa (God-consciousness) as a fundamental principle in Islam and the key to salvation in this world and the hereafter.
orig: إذ قال لهم أخوهم لوط ألا تتقون

translation: Indeed, I am to you a trustworthy messenger.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of trust and honesty in delivering the message of Islam. The Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) is assuring his followers that he is a reliable and truthful messenger, conveying the words of Allah without any alteration or deception. This establishes the credibility of the Prophet and the authenticity of the Qur'anic message he brings. It also sets an example for all Muslims to be trustworthy and honest in their dealings with others, especially when it comes to matters of faith and religious teachings.
orig: إني لكم رسول أمين

translation: So fear Allah and obey me.
interpretation: This verse is a reminder from Allah to mankind to be mindful of Him and to obey His messenger. It emphasizes the importance of having taqwa, which is the consciousness and fear of Allah that leads to righteousness and obedience. By fearing Allah and following the guidance brought by His messenger, one can hope to attain success and salvation in this life and the hereafter. The verse also highlights the role of the prophets as the conveyers of Allah's message and the importance of following their example and teachings.
orig: فاتقوا الله وأطيعون

translation: And I do not ask you for it any payment. My payment is only from the Lord of the worlds.
interpretation: In this verse, the Prophet is telling his people that he does not seek any worldly compensation or reward from them for conveying the message of Islam. He emphasizes that his only reward and motivation comes from Allah, the Lord of all the worlds. This highlights the sincerity and selflessness of the Prophet's mission, as he is not driven by any personal gain but solely by his obedience and devotion to God. It also underscores the universal nature of his message, as the Lord he serves is not just the Lord of a particular people, but the Lord of all creation.
orig: وما أسألكم عليه من أجر إن أجري إلا على رب العالمين

translation: Do you approach males among the worlds
interpretation: This verse is questioning and condemning the act of homosexuality. It is expressing astonishment and disapproval towards those who engage in sexual acts with males instead of females, which is considered the norm and natural way as ordained by God. The verse implies that such behavior goes against the divine order and natural instincts placed in humans by their Creator. It serves as a strong rebuke and prohibition of homosexual practices.
orig: أتأتون الذكران من العالمين

translation: And you leave what your Lord has created for you from your wives? But you are a people transgressing.
interpretation: This verse is criticizing men who engage in homosexual acts instead of fulfilling their natural roles with their wives as God intended. It suggests that homosexual behavior is a transgression against the natural order that God has established for human relationships and procreation. The Qur'an considers homosexual acts to be sinful and a violation of God's law.
orig: وتذرون ما خلق لكم ربكم من أزواجكم بل أنتم قوم عادون

translation: They said, "If you do not desist, O Lot, you will surely be of those evicted."
interpretation: This verse is a warning to Prophet Lot (peace be upon him) from his people, who were engaging in the grave sin of homosexuality. They threatened to expel him from the city if he continued to preach against their immoral behavior. This highlights the stubbornness and arrogance of a people who were so deeply entrenched in their sinful ways that they were willing to reject the guidance of a prophet sent by Allah. It also demonstrates the courage and steadfastness of Prophet Lot in the face of severe opposition and threats, as he continued to convey the message of Allah despite the dangers he faced. The verse serves as a reminder to believers to stand firm in their faith and convictions, even in the face of adversity and persecution from those who oppose the truth.
orig: قالوا لئن لم تنته يا لوط لتكونن من المخرجين

translation: He said, "Indeed, I am, to your deed, of those who detest [it]."
interpretation: This verse conveys a strong sense of disapproval and aversion towards a particular action or deed. The speaker, presumably a righteous figure or prophet, expresses their clear disdain and opposition to the mentioned deed. It highlights the importance of standing against wrongdoing and evil, even if it means going against the majority or popular opinion. The verse emphasizes the value of maintaining one's moral principles and not compromising them for the sake of conformity or acceptance. It encourages individuals to have the courage to voice their disapproval of actions that contradict ethical and religious teachings.
orig: قال إني لعملكم من القالين

translation: My Lord! Save me and my family from what they do.
interpretation: This verse is a prayer of the believer seeking Allah's protection and salvation for themselves and their family from the evil deeds and actions of the wrongdoers. It reflects the believer's trust in Allah as their ultimate protector and savior, and their reliance on Him to shield them from the harm and corruption caused by those who engage in sinful and wicked acts. The supplication also highlights the importance of praying not just for oneself, but for one's loved ones as well, seeking Allah's mercy and guidance for the entire family.
orig: رب نجني وأهلي مما يعملون

translation: So We saved him and all his family.
interpretation: This verse refers to the story of Prophet Lot (Lut) and how Allah saved him and his believing family members from the punishment that befell his people. It emphasizes Allah's mercy and protection towards His righteous servants, even in the face of overwhelming adversity and the sinful actions of those around them. The verse also highlights the importance of remaining steadfast in faith and trusting in Allah's plan, as He will ultimately deliver the believers from harm and grant them salvation in this world and the hereafter.
orig: فنجيناه وأهله أجمعين

translation: Except an old woman among those who remained behind.
interpretation: This verse refers to the wife of Prophet Lot, who was left behind and not saved from the destruction that befell the people of Sodom and Gomorrah due to their sinful ways. The "old woman" mentioned here is an indication that she was a disbeliever who chose to stay with her people rather than follow the guidance of her husband, Prophet Lot. This verse serves as a reminder that even the closest relatives, such as one's spouse, may not be saved from divine punishment if they persist in disbelief and transgression against God's commands.
orig: إلا عجوزا في الغابرين

translation: Then We destroyed the others.
interpretation: This verse refers to the fate of those who rejected the message of Allah and His messengers. After giving them ample warnings and chances to repent, Allah ultimately destroyed those who persisted in disbelief and transgression. It serves as a reminder that while Allah is merciful, He is also just, and those who choose to oppose Him and His guidance will face severe consequences in this world and the Hereafter. The verse also emphasizes Allah's power and control over all things, as He is capable of destroying entire nations when they cross the limits set by Him.
orig: ثم دمرنا الآخرين

translation: And We rained upon them a rain [of stones], and evil was the rain of those who were warned.
interpretation: This verse is a warning to those who reject the message of Allah and His prophets. It refers to the punishment that befell the people of Lut (Lot) who were guilty of gross immorality and refused to heed the warnings of their prophet. Allah sent down a rain of stones upon them, destroying their cities and causing their complete annihilation. The verse emphasizes that the fate of those who are warned but persist in their wrongdoing will be severe and terrible, just as the rain of stones was a dreadful punishment for the people of Lut. It is a reminder for people to take heed of divine warnings and correct their ways before it is too late and they face the consequences of their actions.
orig: وأمطرنا عليهم مطرا فساء مطر المنذرين

translation: Indeed in that is a sign, but most of them were not to be believers.
interpretation: This verse points to the fact that despite the clear signs and evidence of Allah's existence and power, many people still choose not to believe. It suggests that even when faced with undeniable proofs, the majority of mankind will stubbornly persist in disbelief due to their own arrogance, ignorance, or attachment to worldly desires. The verse emphasizes the free will that Allah has granted humans to choose faith or rejection, while highlighting the sad reality that most will fail to embrace the truth. It serves as a reminder for believers to be grateful for their faith and to strive to guide others with wisdom and patience.
orig: إن في ذلك لآية وما كان أكثرهم مؤمنين

translation: And indeed, your Lord is the Exalted in Might, the Merciful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes two essential attributes of Allah: His power and His mercy. "Al-Aziz" (the Exalted in Might) signifies that Allah is supremely powerful, and no one can overcome or resist Him. He has the ability to do whatever He wills, and His decree will always come to pass. At the same time, He is "Ar-Raheem" (the Merciful), which means that despite His immense power, Allah treats His creation with kindness, compassion, and mercy. He provides for them, guides them, and forgives their sins when they repent sincerely. The combination of these two attributes serves as a reminder for believers to have hope in Allah's mercy while also being in awe of His power and majesty. It encourages them to strive for righteousness and to turn to Him in repentance and supplication.
orig: وإن ربك لهو العزيز الرحيم

translation: The companions of the wood denied the messengers.
interpretation: This verse refers to the people of Madyan, who were known as the "companions of the wood" due to their proximity to a dense forest. They rejected the message brought to them by the prophet Shu'ayb, who called upon them to worship Allah alone and to give fair measure in their dealings. The denial of the messengers by the people of Madyan is a recurring theme in the Qur'an, highlighting the stubbornness of those who refuse to accept the truth despite clear signs and warnings. Their story serves as a reminder to believers to remain steadfast in their faith and to heed the guidance of Allah's messengers.
orig: كذب أصحاب الأيكة المرسلين

translation: When Shu'ayb said to them, "Will you not fear Allah?"
interpretation: In this verse, the prophet Shu'ayb is addressing his people, the Midianites, and asking them whether they will not fear Allah and abandon their wrongdoings. This is a call to righteousness, reminding them to be mindful of God and to live according to His teachings. Shu'ayb's question is a way of making them reflect on their actions and the consequences they may face if they do not change their ways and follow the path of God-consciousness (taqwa). It emphasizes the importance of having a healthy fear of Allah, which should serve as a motivation to lead a moral and virtuous life.
orig: إذ قال لهم شعيب ألا تتقون

translation: Indeed, I am to you a trustworthy messenger.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of the Prophet's role as a messenger of Allah. The Prophet is described as being "trustworthy" or "faithful" in his mission to convey the message of Islam to the people. This implies that the Prophet can be trusted to accurately and honestly deliver the revelations he has received from Allah, without any alteration or deception. The verse serves to reassure the believers that they can have complete faith in the Prophet's words and actions, as he is a reliable and sincere guide sent by Allah to lead them on the right path.
orig: إني لكم رسول أمين

translation: So fear Allah and obey me.
interpretation: This verse is a call to the believers to have consciousness of Allah (taqwa) and to obey His messenger. It emphasizes the importance of submission to the will of Allah and following the guidance and teachings of His prophet. Taqwa is a central concept in Islam, referring to being mindful of Allah, fearing His displeasure, and striving to do what is right. Obedience to the messenger is linked with obedience to Allah Himself, as the prophet conveys Allah's message to humanity. This verse thus stresses that true faith requires both an inward attitude of reverence and an outward expression of compliance with divine commands as taught by the prophet.
orig: فاتقوا الله وأطيعون

translation: And I do not ask you for it any payment. My payment is only from the Lord of the worlds.
interpretation: The prophet is not seeking any worldly gain or reward from the people for conveying the message of Islam. His reward comes solely from Allah, the Lord of all creation. This emphasizes the sincerity of the prophet in his mission, as he is not motivated by any personal or material gain, but rather by his obedience and devotion to Allah. It also highlights the universal nature of the message, as it is not limited to any particular people or nation, but is intended for all of humanity, as Allah is the Lord of all the worlds.
orig: وما أسألكم عليه من أجر إن أجري إلا على رب العالمين

translation: Give full measure and do not be among those who cause loss.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of honesty and fairness in business dealings. It commands believers to give full measure when selling goods, without cheating or shortchanging the buyer. This is a matter of integrity and righteousness, as those who engage in fraudulent practices are considered among the losers in the sight of Allah. The verse serves as a reminder that Muslims should conduct their business affairs with the highest ethical standards, ensuring that they do not cause harm or loss to others for their own gain. Honesty in trade is not only a moral obligation but also a means of earning Allah's pleasure and blessings in this world and the hereafter.
orig: أوفوا الكيل ولا تكونوا من المخسرين

translation: And weigh with an even balance.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of fairness, justice, and honesty in all dealings, especially in matters of trade and commerce. The "even balance" is a metaphor for equity and impartiality. It reminds believers to be truthful and accurate in their measurements and transactions, without cheating or exploiting others. This principle extends beyond business dealings to all aspects of life, encouraging individuals to treat others with integrity, respect, and fairness, as this is pleasing to Allah. Upholding justice and balance in society fosters harmony, trust, and the overall well-being of the community.
orig: وزنوا بالقسطاس المستقيم

translation: And do not deprive people of their due and do not commit abuse on earth, spreading corruption.
interpretation: This verse is a commandment from Allah to humans to act with justice and integrity. It warns against withholding from people what they are rightfully owed, whether in terms of wealth, rights, or respect. The verse also forbids causing mischief and corruption on earth through one's actions. It calls for humans to maintain fairness in their dealings and not to disrupt the social order and harmony through wrongdoing and transgression. The message is to establish a society based on equity, honesty and righteousness, shunning exploitation, abuse and corruption.
orig: ولا تبخسوا الناس أشياءهم ولا تعثوا في الأرض مفسدين

translation: And fear the One who created you and the former creation.
interpretation: This verse is a reminder for mankind to be mindful and have consciousness (taqwa) of Allah, the One who created them and all those who came before them. It emphasizes the importance of acknowledging and revering the Creator, and living life in accordance with His guidance and commands. The verse instills a sense of continuity, indicating that just as Allah created previous generations, He has also created the present one. Thus, humans should be humble and recognize their place as creatures before the Almighty Creator, and strive to lead a righteous life out of fear, love and obedience to Him.
orig: واتقوا الذي خلقكم والجبلة الأولين

translation: They said, "You are only of those affected by magic."
interpretation: This verse is referring to the disbelievers who accused the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) of being under the influence of magic or sorcery. They refused to believe that he was a true prophet and messenger of Allah, instead attributing his revelations and teachings to being bewitched or deluded by magic. This accusation was a way for them to dismiss and discredit the Prophet's message, rather than sincerely considering and reflecting upon the truth and wisdom contained within it. The verse highlights the stubborn disbelief and denial of those who opposed the Prophet, despite the clear signs and evidence of his prophethood.
orig: قالوا إنما أنت من المسحرين

translation: You are not but a man like us, and indeed, we think you are among the liars.
interpretation: This verse is addressing the Prophet Muhammad, telling him that he is only a human being like everyone else, and accusing him of being a liar. It reflects the disbelief and skepticism of those who opposed the Prophet's message. The interpretation is that even though the Prophet was chosen by God to deliver His message, to the disbelievers he was seen as just an ordinary man who was falsely claiming to be a prophet. They refused to accept that God would choose a human being to be His messenger, and so they rejected the Prophet's teachings and accused him of lying about his divine mission.
orig: وما أنت إلا بشر مثلنا وإن نظنك لمن الكاذبين

translation: Then cause to fall upon us fragments from the sky, if you should be of the truthful.
interpretation: This verse is a challenge posed by the disbelievers to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him). They demanded that he bring down upon them a piece of the sky as proof of his prophethood and the truth of his message. It reflects their stubbornness, arrogance and refusal to believe despite the clear signs already provided to them. The verse highlights the fact that no matter what miracles or proofs are presented, those who have hardened their hearts against faith will always find an excuse to reject the truth. It also emphasizes that the ultimate decision of punishment or forgiveness rests with Allah alone, and the Prophet's duty is only to convey the message.
orig: فأسقط علينا كسفا من السماء إن كنت من الصادقين

translation: My Lord is most knowing of what you do.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the omniscience of Allah, reminding us that He is fully aware of all our actions, whether good or bad. It serves as a warning to be mindful of our deeds, as nothing escapes His knowledge. The verse also implies that we will be held accountable for our actions in the Hereafter, encouraging believers to strive for righteousness and refrain from wrongdoing. It is a call to self-reflection and a reminder to align our actions with the teachings of Islam, seeking Allah's pleasure in all that we do.
orig: قال ربي أعلم بما تعملون

translation: And they denied him, so the punishment of the day of the black cloud seized them. Indeed, it was the punishment of a terrible day.
interpretation: This verse serves as a warning and reminder that denying the truth and rejecting the messengers of Allah can lead to severe consequences. The people mentioned in this verse faced a terrible punishment in the form of a dark cloud that brought upon them immense suffering. This highlights the gravity of their denial and the magnitude of Allah's punishment for those who persist in disbelief. It emphasizes the importance of heeding the warnings of the prophets and accepting the truth to avoid facing a similar fate in this world or the hereafter.
orig: فكذبوه فأخذهم عذاب يوم الظلة إنه كان عذاب يوم عظيم

translation: Indeed in that is a sign, but most of them were not to be believers.
interpretation: This verse points to the fact that even though there are clear signs and evidence of Allah's existence and power in the world around us, many people still choose not to believe. It suggests that disbelief is often a matter of choice and willful rejection of the truth, rather than a lack of evidence. The verse also implies that true faith is not something that can be forced, but is ultimately a matter of individual choice and submission to Allah's will.
orig: إن في ذلك لآية وما كان أكثرهم مؤمنين

translation: And indeed, your Lord is the Exalted in Might, the Merciful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes two essential attributes of Allah: His power and His mercy. "Al-Aziz" (the Exalted in Might) signifies that Allah is supremely powerful, and no one can overcome or challenge Him. He has the ability to do whatever He wills, and His decree will always come to pass. At the same time, He is "Ar-Raheem" (the Merciful), which means that despite His immense power, Allah treats His creation with kindness, compassion, and forgiveness. He provides for them, guides them, and showers them with His blessings, even though they may not deserve it. The combination of these two attributes serves as a reminder for believers to have both fear and hope in Allah - to recognize His power and submit to Him, while also seeking His mercy and grace.
orig: وإن ربك لهو العزيز الرحيم

translation: And indeed, it is a revelation from the Lord of the worlds.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the divine origin of the Qur'an. It asserts that the Qur'an is not the product of human imagination or creation, but rather a direct revelation from Allah, the Lord and Sustainer of all the worlds. This interpretation highlights the authenticity and authority of the Qur'an as a sacred text, as it comes from the highest possible source, the Creator Himself. It also implies that the message of the Qur'an is universal, intended for all of humanity across all times and places, as Allah is the Lord of all the worlds, not just a specific group or nation.
orig: وإنه لتنزيل رب العالمين

translation: The trustworthy Spirit has brought it down
interpretation: This verse refers to the revelation of the Qur'an to Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) through the angel Gabriel, who is described as the "trustworthy Spirit". It emphasizes the divine origin of the Qur'an and the reliability of the process of its revelation. The verse affirms that the Qur'an is not the product of human imagination or composition, but rather a sacred scripture sent down by God through His trusted angel to guide humanity. It also highlights the integrity and trustworthiness of Gabriel as the messenger chosen by God to convey His words to the Prophet.
orig: نزل به الروح الأمين

translation: Upon your heart, that you may be of the warners.
interpretation: This verse is addressing the Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him, indicating that the Qur'an has been revealed to his heart so that he may become one of those who warn people about the consequences of their actions and guide them to the right path. It emphasizes the role of the Prophet as a messenger chosen by Allah to convey His message and admonish humanity, with the Qur'an serving as the source of guidance and warning that has been bestowed upon his heart.
orig: على قلبك لتكون من المنذرين

translation: In a clear Arabic language.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the Qur'an is revealed in clear, eloquent, and understandable Arabic language. It is a language that the Arabs of that time could easily comprehend and appreciate. The use of "clear" (مبين) indicates that the message of the Qur'an is not ambiguous or obscure, but rather it is plain, evident, and easily intelligible to those who are well-versed in the Arabic language. This clarity of language is a testament to the divine nature of the Qur'an and its intended role as a guide for all mankind.
orig: بلسان عربي مبين

translation: And indeed, it is [mentioned] in the scriptures of former peoples.
interpretation: This verse suggests that the message and teachings found in the Qur'an are not entirely new, but rather a confirmation and continuation of the divine revelations that were sent to earlier prophets and nations. The "scriptures of former peoples" likely refers to sacred texts such as the Torah and the Gospel, which also contained guidance and wisdom from Allah. This verse emphasizes the universality and consistency of Allah's message throughout human history, indicating that the Qur'an is a reminder and reinforcement of the eternal truths that have been conveyed to mankind since the beginning of time.
orig: وإنه لفي زبر الأولين

translation: Is it not a sign to them that the scholars of the Children of Israel know it?
interpretation: This verse points to the fact that the scholars among the Children of Israel, who had knowledge of previous scriptures, recognized the truth of the Qur'an and the prophethood of Muhammad (peace be upon him). Their recognition and acknowledgment of the Qur'an's authenticity should serve as a clear sign and evidence for those who doubt or reject it, as these scholars were well-versed in divine revelations and could discern the true message from falsehood. The verse implies that if the knowledgeable among the Children of Israel confirm the Qur'an, it should be a compelling reason for others to believe in its divine origin and accept Muhammad as a true prophet.
orig: أولم يكن لهم آية أن يعلمه علماء بني إسرائيل

translation: And if We had revealed it to one of the foreigners
interpretation: This verse implies that the Qur'an was revealed in the Arabic language to the Prophet Muhammad, who was an Arab, rather than to a non-Arab. This highlights the wisdom of Allah in revealing the Qur'an in the language of the people to whom the Prophet was sent, so that they could easily understand and relate to its message. It also suggests that the Qur'an's eloquence and inimitability are inherently tied to the Arabic language in which it was originally revealed.
orig: ولو نزلناه على بعض الأعجمين

translation: Then he recited it to them, but they would not believe in it.
interpretation: This verse suggests that even when the truth is presented clearly to some people, they may still refuse to accept it due to their stubbornness, preconceived notions, or lack of faith. It highlights the human tendency to sometimes reject divine guidance even when it is directly conveyed to them. The verse implies that the disbelievers' lack of faith is not due to any shortcoming in the message or its delivery, but rather stems from their own unwillingness to believe and submit to the truth.
orig: فقرأه عليهم ما كانوا به مؤمنين

translation: Thus We have inserted it into the hearts of the criminals.
interpretation: This verse suggests that Allah has caused the disbelievers and wrongdoers to be inherently inclined towards rejecting the truth of the Qur'an and its message. It is as if the denial of faith has been ingrained deep within their hearts, making it difficult for them to accept guidance. This is a consequence of their own choices and actions, as they have persistently refused to believe despite clear signs and warnings. As a result, Allah has sealed their hearts and left them to continue in their misguidance as a form of punishment for their stubbornness and arrogance.
orig: كذلك سلكناه في قلوب المجرمين

translation: They will not believe in it until they see the painful punishment.
interpretation: This verse suggests that some people are so stubborn in their disbelief that they will refuse to accept the truth of God's message until they directly experience His severe punishment in the Hereafter. It implies that for some, mere warnings are not enough to open their hearts to faith. Only the shock of facing the painful consequences of their rejection will make them realize, but by then it will be too late. The verse serves as a warning to not wait until punishment is imminent to believe, but rather to heed the signs and guidance now while there is still opportunity to turn to God's path.
orig: لا يؤمنون به حتى يروا العذاب الأليم

translation: But it will come to them suddenly, while they are unaware.
interpretation: This verse warns that the Day of Judgment or God's punishment will come upon the disbelievers and wrongdoers suddenly, at a time when they least expect it. They will be caught off guard, oblivious to the impending doom, as they had been heedless of the signs and warnings. It emphasizes the element of surprise and the consequences of not being prepared for the inevitable reckoning. The verse serves as a reminder for people to be vigilant, mend their ways, and not be caught in a state of negligence or disbelief when the ultimate reality dawns upon them.
orig: فيأتيهم بغتة وهم لا يشعرون

translation: Then they will say, "Are we to be reprieved?"
interpretation: This verse is referring to the Day of Judgment when the disbelievers will realize the reality of their situation. They will ask if they can be given more time or a second chance to make amends for their past deeds and to embrace faith. However, it will be too late for them at that point, as the time for repentance and good deeds has already passed. This verse serves as a reminder to humanity that we should make the most of our time in this world by believing in God and doing righteous deeds, as there will be no opportunity for reprieve or second chances in the Hereafter.
orig: فيقولوا هل نحن منظرون

translation: Then is it to Our punishment they hasten?
interpretation: This verse is a rhetorical question that highlights the foolishness and arrogance of those who mock or challenge Allah's punishment. It implies that the disbelievers are hastening towards their own destruction by rejecting the truth and the warnings of the prophets. The verse serves as a reminder that Allah's punishment is real and that those who deny it will face the consequences of their actions in the Hereafter. It also emphasizes the importance of believing in Allah and following His guidance before it is too late.
orig: أفبعذابنا يستعجلون

translation: Have you seen if We give them enjoyment for years
interpretation: This verse is a reminder that even if Allah grants the disbelievers worldly pleasures and a long life, it does not mean that they are favored by Him or that they will be saved from punishment in the Hereafter. The temporary enjoyment in this life should not deceive anyone into thinking that they can escape the consequences of their actions, as ultimately everyone will face judgment before Allah. It emphasizes the fleeting nature of worldly pleasures compared to the eternal life of the Hereafter, encouraging believers to focus on righteousness and good deeds rather than being distracted by temporary indulgences.
orig: أفرأيت إن متعناهم سنين

translation: Then there came to them that which they were promised.
