interpretation: This verse is referring to the fulfillment of God's promise to the believers, either in this world or in the Hereafter. It indicates that whatever good or reward God has promised to those who believe and do righteous deeds will certainly come to pass at the appointed time. This promise may be realized in the form of victory, success, or blessings in this worldly life, or it could be the attainment of Paradise and its eternal delights in the afterlife. The verse serves as an assurance and a reminder to the faithful that God's word is always true and that He never fails to deliver on His promises to His servants who strive in His cause with sincerity and perseverance.
orig: ثم جاءهم ما كانوا يوعدون

translation: Of no avail to them was all that they used to enjoy.
interpretation: This verse highlights the fleeting nature of worldly pleasures and possessions. It reminds us that no matter how much we indulge in the luxuries and enjoyments of this life, they will ultimately be of no benefit to us in the Hereafter. The verse implies that we should not become attached to or distracted by the temporary delights of this world, as they will not bring us true contentment or salvation. Instead, we should focus on leading a righteous life and striving for the eternal rewards of the Afterlife, which hold far greater value than any ephemeral worldly gains.
orig: ما أغنى عنهم ما كانوا يمتعون

translation: And We did not destroy any city except that it had warners
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the justice and mercy of Allah. Before destroying a nation or a city due to their persistent disbelief and wrongdoing, Allah always sends messengers and warners to guide them to the right path. These warners, who are usually prophets or righteous individuals, remind the people of their duty to worship Allah alone and follow His commandments. They warn them of the consequences of their sinful actions and urge them to repent and seek forgiveness. Thus, Allah gives every nation a fair chance to mend their ways before He sends down His punishment. This verse also serves as a reminder for people of all times that they should heed the warnings of their prophets and reformers, and not wait until it is too late to turn back to Allah.
orig: وما أهلكنا من قرية إلا لها منذرون

translation: A reminder, and never have We been unjust.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the Qur'an serves as a reminder to humanity, guiding them towards the right path. It also affirms that Allah is never unjust towards His creation. He provides guidance and warnings through His messengers and revelations, giving people the opportunity to follow the truth. Allah's justice is perfect, and He does not wrong anyone. The verse implies that if people face the consequences of their actions, it is not due to Allah's injustice but rather a result of their own choices and deeds.
orig: ذكرى وما كنا ظالمين

translation: It was not the devils who brought it down.
interpretation: This verse is emphasizing that the Qur'an is not the work of evil forces or devils, but rather it is a divine revelation from Allah. It is refuting the accusation made by some of the disbelievers that the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) was being inspired by devils or jinn. The Qur'an asserts its own divine origin and purity, free from any satanic influence or corruption.
orig: وما تنزلت به الشياطين

translation: It is not allowable for them, nor are they able
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute power and authority of Allah over all creation. It conveys that no one has the right or ability to go against His will or decree. Whatever Allah has ordained, no force in the heavens or earth can oppose it. It is a reminder for humankind to submit to Allah's sovereignty and recognize our complete dependence on Him. The verse also implies that those who arrogantly attempt to defy Allah are deluded, as they can never succeed in their defiance or escape the consequences of their disobedience.
orig: وما ينبغي لهم وما يستطيعون

translation: Indeed, they [i.e., the disbelievers] are [to be] removed from [hearing] the hearing.
interpretation: This verse refers to the state of the disbelievers in the Hereafter. They will be prevented from hearing the truth and the guidance that could have saved them from the punishment of Hell. It implies that they had the opportunity to listen to the message of Islam in this world, but they chose to turn away from it. As a result, in the Hereafter, they will be deprived of the ability to hear anything that could bring them comfort or relief from their suffering. This verse serves as a warning to those who reject the truth in this life, highlighting the severe consequences of their choice in the afterlife.
orig: إنهم عن السمع لمعزولون

translation: So do not invoke with Allah another deity and [thus] be among the punished.
interpretation: This verse is a clear warning against associating partners with Allah in worship, which is known as shirk. It emphasizes the grave consequence of committing this major sin, which is being subjected to Allah's punishment in the Hereafter. The verse reminds believers to direct all their worship and invocations solely to Allah, as He alone deserves to be worshipped and called upon. It also highlights the importance of maintaining pure monotheism (tawheed) in one's faith and actions, as this is the foundation of Islam and the key to attaining Allah's pleasure and salvation.
orig: فلا تدع مع الله إلها آخر فتكون من المعذبين

translation: And warn, [O Muhammad], your closest kindred.
interpretation: This verse is instructing Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) to begin his mission of spreading the message of Islam by first warning and inviting his closest relatives and tribesmen to the worship of the One True God, Allah. It emphasizes the importance of starting the call to Islam with those nearest to you, as they are the most deserving of your care and concern. The verse also implies that the Prophet should not expect or seek support from his close relatives simply because of blood ties, but rather should convey the message to them as he would to any other person, and leave the outcome to Allah.
orig: وأنذر عشيرتك الأقربين

translation: And lower your wing to those who follow you of the believers.
interpretation: This verse instructs the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) to be humble, gentle, and compassionate towards his followers who are believers. The metaphor of lowering one's wing symbolizes showing kindness, care, and affection. It emphasizes the importance of treating fellow believers with respect, empathy, and understanding, fostering a sense of unity and brotherhood within the Muslim community. The verse also implies that a leader should not be arrogant or overbearing but should adopt a nurturing and supportive attitude towards those who follow him in faith.
orig: واخفض جناحك لمن اتبعك من المؤمنين

translation: And if they disobey you, say, "Indeed, I am disassociated from what you are doing."
interpretation: This verse is a command to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) to dissociate himself from the actions of those who disobey him and persist in their wrongdoing. It emphasizes the importance of standing firm in one's faith and principles, even in the face of opposition or rejection from others. The Prophet is instructed to clearly state his position and disavowal of their misdeeds, underlining the individual responsibility each person bears for their own choices and actions. This verse also serves as a reminder to all believers to stay true to their beliefs and not be swayed by the disobedience or misconduct of others around them.
orig: فإن عصوك فقل إني بريء مما تعملون

translation: And put your trust in the Almighty, the Most Merciful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of having complete trust and reliance on Allah, who is the Almighty and the Most Merciful. It encourages believers to put their faith in Allah's power, wisdom, and compassion, knowing that He will guide and support them through all challenges and difficulties in life. By surrendering oneself to Allah and relying on His mercy, one can find inner peace, strength, and the ability to overcome any obstacle. This unwavering trust in Allah is a fundamental aspect of Islamic faith and a source of spiritual comfort for believers.
orig: وتوكل على العزيز الرحيم

translation: Who sees you when you arise
interpretation: This verse is referring to Allah's omniscience and omnipresence. It conveys the idea that Allah is always watching over us and is aware of all our actions, even when we are alone and think no one can see us. It serves as a reminder for believers to be mindful of their deeds at all times, as nothing escapes Allah's sight. This consciousness of Allah's presence should motivate individuals to strive for righteousness and refrain from wrongdoing, knowing that they will be held accountable for their choices in this life and the hereafter.
orig: الذي يراك حين تقوم

translation: And your turning about among those who prostrate.
interpretation: This verse refers to Allah's knowledge and awareness of the Prophet Muhammad's (peace be upon him) actions and movements, even in the midst of those who pray and prostrate to Allah. It emphasizes that Allah is constantly watching over and observing His servants, and is fully aware of their deeds and devotion. The verse serves as a reminder for believers to be sincere and mindful in their worship, knowing that Allah witnesses every act of devotion and will reward them accordingly in the Hereafter.
orig: وتقلبك في الساجدين

translation: Indeed, it is He who is the Hearing, the Knowing.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes two fundamental attributes of Allah: His all-encompassing ability to hear everything and His infinite knowledge. It serves as a reminder to believers that Allah is always aware of their actions, thoughts, and intentions. Moreover, it highlights the importance of being mindful of one's deeds and words, as nothing escapes Allah's hearing and knowledge. This verse instills a sense of consciousness and accountability in the hearts of the faithful, encouraging them to strive for righteousness and sincerity in all aspects of their lives.
orig: إنه هو السميع العليم

translation: Shall I inform you upon whom the devils descend?
interpretation: This verse is a rhetorical question from Allah, asking if He should inform us about the type of people that the devils descend upon and whisper to. The implication is that there are certain individuals who are more susceptible to the influence and whisperings of the devils due to their sinful nature and distance from the remembrance of Allah. It serves as a warning for us to be mindful of our actions and to seek refuge in Allah from the whispers of Shaytan.
orig: هل أنبئكم على من تنزل الشياطين

translation: They descend upon every sinful liar.
interpretation: This verse refers to the devils who inspire and whisper evil suggestions to those who are prone to lying and sinning. The "sinful liar" is someone who habitually lies and commits sins without remorse. The verse indicates that such individuals become easy targets for the devils to misguide and lead further astray by planting deceptive thoughts and temptations in their hearts. It serves as a warning that constantly engaging in lying and sinful behavior opens the door for satanic influences and makes one vulnerable to their whisperings, leading a person farther away from truth and righteousness.
orig: تنزل على كل أفاك أثيم

translation: They pass on what is heard, and most of them are liars.
interpretation: This verse is referring to those who spread rumors and false information without verifying its authenticity. They rely on hearsay and pass it on to others, causing the spread of misinformation. The majority of these people are liars, as they do not care about the truth and are only interested in spreading sensational stories or causing mischief. The Qur'an condemns this behavior and emphasizes the importance of verifying information before passing it on to others.
orig: يلقون السمع وأكثرهم كاذبون

translation: And the poets - [only] the deviators follow them;
interpretation: This verse is criticizing those poets who use their talents to misguide people and lead them astray from the right path. It suggests that only those who are themselves misguided and deviant would be attracted to and follow such poets. The implication is that true, righteous poetry should guide people towards what is good and moral, not away from it. Poets have an influence on society, and they must use that position responsibly in line with divine guidance.
orig: والشعراء يتبعهم الغاوون

translation: Do you not see that they roam in every valley?
interpretation: This verse is criticizing poets who use their talents frivolously and without purpose. The "valley" here symbolizes the different topics and themes that poets address in their works. The verse is stating that these poets wander aimlessly in their literary pursuits, moving from one topic to another without any clear direction or higher purpose. It suggests that their poetry is devoid of genuine spiritual or moral value, and that they are merely engaging in vain and unproductive wordplay. The implication is that true poets should use their gifts in the service of God and the truth, rather than wasting them on trivial or even harmful subjects.
orig: ألم تر أنهم في كل واد يهيمون

translation: And they say what they do not do.
interpretation: This verse is criticizing the hypocrites who say good things but do not follow through with their actions. It highlights the importance of honesty and practicing what one preaches. In Islam, it is not enough to simply speak about righteousness and virtue; one must strive to embody those qualities in their daily life and conduct. The Qur'an emphasizes the significance of integrity and the alignment of words and deeds.
orig: وأنهم يقولون ما لا يفعلون

translation: Except those who have believed and done righteous deeds and remembered Allah often and defended [themselves] after they were wronged. And those who have wronged are going to know to what [kind of] return they will be returned.
interpretation: This verse offers hope and a promise of justice to those who have been wronged or oppressed. It states that those who remain steadfast in their faith, do good deeds, and remember Allah frequently will be defended and vindicated by Him. On the other hand, the wrongdoers and oppressors will face the consequences of their actions in the form of a severe punishment in the afterlife. This verse serves as a reminder that justice will ultimately prevail, and the believers should remain patient and persevere in the face of adversity, trusting in Allah's plan and His promise of support for the righteous.
orig: إلا الذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات وذكروا الله كثيرا وانتصروا من بعد ما ظلموا وسيعلم الذين ظلموا أي منقلب ينقلبون

translation: Ta, Seen. These are the verses of the Qur'an and a clear Book.
interpretation: This verse is indicating that the Qur'an is a clear and unambiguous book, providing guidance and wisdom to those who reflect upon its verses. The letters "Ta, Seen" at the beginning are among the "Muqatta'at" (disjoined letters) which appear at the beginning of certain chapters. While their exact meaning is known only to Allah, they are generally understood to be a way of drawing the listener's attention to the divine nature of the Qur'an and its inimitable style. The verse emphasizes that the Qur'an is not just any ordinary book, but a revelation from Allah, clear in its message and guidance for those who approach it with sincerity and reflection.
orig: طس تلك آيات القرآن وكتاب مبين

translation: A guidance and glad tidings for the believers.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the Qur'an serves as a divine guidance and a source of good news for those who have faith in Allah. It provides them with the necessary knowledge, wisdom, and spiritual enlightenment to navigate through life and attain success in both this world and the hereafter. The Qur'an offers glad tidings of Allah's mercy, forgiveness, and the promise of Paradise for those who sincerely believe and follow its teachings. It brings hope, comfort, and reassurance to the hearts of the believers, strengthening their faith and motivating them to lead righteous lives in accordance with Allah's commandments.
orig: هدى وبشرى للمؤمنين

translation: Those who establish prayer and give zakah, and of the Hereafter they are certain [in faith].
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of two key pillars of Islam: establishing regular prayer and giving zakah (obligatory charity). It also highlights the significance of having strong faith and certainty in the Hereafter. Those who fulfill these obligations and maintain unwavering belief in the afterlife are praised in this verse. It suggests that these actions and beliefs are essential characteristics of true believers who seek to please Allah and attain success in both this world and the next.
orig: الذين يقيمون الصلاة ويؤتون الزكاة وهم بالآخرة هم يوقنون

translation: Indeed, those who do not believe in the Hereafter - We have made their deeds pleasing to them, so they wander blindly.
interpretation: This verse highlights the spiritual blindness of those who reject belief in the Hereafter. Because they deny the eternal consequences of their actions, Allah has made their worldly deeds seem attractive to them. They are content with the temporary pleasures and gains of this life, failing to see the ultimate reality. As a result, they wander aimlessly without true guidance, unable to distinguish between what is truly beneficial and what is harmful for their souls. Their lack of faith in the Hereafter veils their hearts from the truth, leading them astray from the straight path.
orig: إن الذين لا يؤمنون بالآخرة زينا لهم أعمالهم فهم يعمهون

translation: Those are the ones for whom there is the worst punishment, and in the Hereafter they are the greatest losers.
interpretation: This verse warns that those who reject faith and do evil deeds will face the most severe punishment from Allah in the Hereafter. They will be the ultimate losers, because they will have lost both this world and the eternal life of the Hereafter. Their loss will be the greatest, as they will have squandered the opportunity to earn Allah's pleasure and Paradise. Instead, they will be condemned to the everlasting torment of Hell as a consequence of their disbelief and sins. This highlights the importance of faith and righteousness in this life to avoid being among the greatest losers in the next.
orig: أولئك الذين لهم سوء العذاب وهم في الآخرة هم الأخسرون

translation: And indeed, you receive the Qur'an from one [who is] Wise and Knowing.
interpretation: This verse affirms that the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) received the Qur'an directly from Allah, the All-Wise and All-Knowing. It emphasizes the divine origin of the Qur'an and the infallibility of its source. The Prophet did not compose the Qur'an himself, but rather it was revealed to him by the One who possesses perfect wisdom and knowledge. This verse serves as a testament to the authenticity and trustworthiness of the Qur'an, as it comes from the highest authority, Allah, who is free from all imperfections and deficiencies.
orig: وإنك لتلقى القرآن من لدن حكيم عليم

translation: When Moses said to his family, "Indeed, I have perceived a fire. I will bring you from there information or will bring you a burning torch that you may warm yourselves."
interpretation: This verse shows the concern and care that Prophet Moses (peace be upon him) had for his family. He was traveling with them in the dark and cold night when he saw a fire in the distance. Instead of just going towards it himself to investigate, his first thought was about his family and how he could bring them the benefits of this fire, either in the form of information or actual warmth and light. This demonstrates his sense of responsibility towards those under his care, and his willingness to take the initiative to help and provide for them even in difficult circumstances. It also shows his resourcefulness and practicality in making the best use of whatever means are available to fulfill his duties. These are admirable qualities for anyone, especially those in positions of leadership and authority over others.
orig: إذ قال موسى لأهله إني آنست نارا سآتيكم منها بخبر أو آتيكم بشهاب قبس لعلكم تصطلون

translation: But when he came to it, he was called from the right side of the valley in a blessed spot - from the tree, "O Moses, indeed I am Allah, Lord of the worlds."
interpretation: This verse is describing the moment when Moses, upon arriving at the blessed location specified by Allah, heard the voice of Allah Himself speaking to him from the direction of a tree. This direct communication from Allah to Moses represents the beginning of Moses' prophethood and his receiving divine revelation. The verse emphasizes Allah's omnipotence and sovereignty as the Lord of all creation, and highlights the extraordinary and miraculous nature of this event, where Allah spoke to a human being directly. This moment marked a significant turning point in Moses' life and his mission as a messenger of Allah to his people.
orig: فلما جاءها نودي أن بورك من في النار ومن حولها وسبحان الله رب العالمين

translation: O Moses, indeed it is I - Allah, the Exalted in Might, the Wise.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the divine power and wisdom of Allah. By directly addressing Moses, it establishes a personal connection between the prophet and his Lord. The use of the divine names "al-Aziz" (the Exalted in Might) and "al-Hakim" (the Wise) highlights Allah's omnipotence and supreme knowledge. It serves as a reminder to Moses, and by extension to all believers, that Allah is the ultimate authority and that His commands and revelations come from a place of unparalleled wisdom. This verse instills a sense of awe, reverence, and trust in Allah's guidance and reinforces the importance of submitting to His will.
orig: يا موسى إنه أنا الله العزيز الحكيم

translation: And [he was told], "Throw down your staff." But when he saw it writhing as if it were a snake, he turned in flight and did not return. [Allah said], "O Moses, fear not. Indeed, in My presence the messengers do not fear."
interpretation: This verse is a reminder that even the greatest of prophets, like Moses, experienced fear and doubt at times. However, Allah reassures Moses that he need not be afraid in His presence, for Allah's messengers are protected and guided by Him. This verse teaches us that we should trust in Allah's plan and have faith in His protection, even in the face of seemingly frightening or overwhelming situations. It also emphasizes the special status of Allah's messengers, who are chosen and supported by Him to deliver His message to humanity.
orig: وألق عصاك فلما رآها تهتز كأنها جان ولى مدبرا ولم يعقب يا موسى لا تخف إني لا يخاف لدي المرسلون

translation: Except for those who have done wrong and then substituted good after evil. Indeed, I am Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the vast mercy and forgiveness of Allah. It indicates that even those who have committed sins and wrongdoings in the past can seek forgiveness by sincerely repenting, mending their ways, and replacing their misdeeds with good actions. Allah's door of forgiveness is always open for those who turn back to Him with a contrite heart, seeking His mercy and pardon. The verse reassures that Allah is Forgiving and Merciful, ready to accept the repentance of His servants, no matter how grave their past sins may have been, as long as they sincerely resolve to change for the better.
orig: إلا من ظلم ثم بدل حسنا بعد سوء فإني غفور رحيم

translation: And put your hand into the opening of your garment [at the breast]; it will come out white without disease. [This is] among the nine signs [you will take] to Pharaoh and his people. Indeed, they have been a people defiantly disobedient.
interpretation: This verse is a command to Moses to perform a miracle as a sign of his prophethood when he goes to Pharaoh and his people to call them to worship Allah alone. The miracle is that if Moses were to put his hand inside his cloak and bring it out, it would appear shining white without any disease or imperfection. This would be one of nine signs given to Moses to prove his divine mission and convince Pharaoh and the Egyptians, who had become corrupt and disobedient to Allah, to believe in his message. The signs serve as clear evidences for the truth, yet Pharaoh and his people arrogantly rejected them due to their rebelliousness and opposition to the truth.
orig: وأدخل يدك في جيبك تخرج بيضاء من غير سوء في تسع آيات إلى فرعون وقومه إنهم كانوا قوما فاسقين

translation: But when there came to them Our visible signs, they said, "This is obvious magic."
interpretation: This verse suggests that when clear evidence and signs of Allah's existence and power were presented to the disbelievers, they stubbornly refused to acknowledge them as divine revelation. Instead, they dismissed these signs as mere magic or trickery, revealing their arrogance and closed-mindedness. The interpretation highlights the tendency of some people to reject the truth even when it is made plainly apparent to them, choosing to remain in a state of denial rather than accepting the message of Islam.
orig: فلما جاءتهم آياتنا مبصرة قالوا هذا سحر مبين

translation: And they rejected them, while their [inner] selves were convinced thereof, out of injustice and haughtiness. So see how was the end of the corrupters.
interpretation: This verse is referring to those who, despite recognizing the truth in their hearts, reject it out of pride and arrogance. They know deep down that the message is true, but their ego and desire for power and status prevent them from accepting it. The verse warns us to be mindful of such behavior and to reflect on the ultimate fate of those who knowingly reject the truth and spread corruption in the land. It reminds us to be humble, sincere, and open to the truth, even if it goes against our personal desires or societal norms. The consequences of rejecting the truth and sowing discord are severe, both in this life and the hereafter.
orig: وجحدوا بها واستيقنتها أنفسهم ظلما وعلوا فانظر كيف كان عاقبة المفسدين

translation: And We had certainly given to David and Solomon knowledge, and they said, "Praise [is due] to Allah, who has favored us over many of His believing servants."
interpretation: This verse highlights the special status and knowledge bestowed upon the prophets David and Solomon by Allah. They acknowledged this favor and praised Allah for elevating them above many other believers. It shows their humility, gratitude and recognition that their gifts and wisdom came from Allah alone. The verse reminds us to be thankful for whatever blessings and abilities Allah has given us, and to use them in His service and in the pursuit of righteousness.
orig: ولقد آتينا داوود وسليمان علما وقالا الحمد لله الذي فضلنا على كثير من عباده المؤمنين

translation: And Solomon inherited David. He said, "O people, we have been taught the language of birds, and we have been given from all things. Indeed, this is evident bounty."
interpretation: This verse highlights the special knowledge and wisdom bestowed upon Prophet Solomon by Allah. Solomon was granted the ability to understand the language of birds, a unique gift that demonstrates his elevated status and the favor he enjoyed from his Lord. The verse also emphasizes that Solomon acknowledged this ability as a blessing from Allah, attributing it to the bounty and grace of God. This serves as a reminder for believers to recognize and appreciate the blessings and abilities they have been granted, understanding that all good things come from Allah alone.
orig: وورث سليمان داوود وقال يا أيها الناس علمنا منطق الطير وأوتينا من كل شيء إن هذا لهو الفضل المبين

translation: And gathered for Solomon his soldiers of the jinn and men and birds, and they were [marching] in rows.
interpretation: This verse refers to the vast army of Prophet Solomon, which consisted not only of human soldiers, but also jinn and birds. The fact that these diverse creatures were all under Solomon's command and marching in disciplined rows demonstrates the great power and authority bestowed upon him by Allah. It also symbolizes the unity and order that can be achieved when all of Allah's creation submits to His will and works together in harmony under righteous leadership.
orig: وحشر لسليمان جنوده من الجن والإنس والطير فهم يوزعون

translation: Until, when they came upon the valley of the ants, an ant said, "O ants, enter your dwellings that you not be crushed by Solomon and his soldiers while they perceive not."
interpretation: This verse is a reminder that even the smallest and seemingly insignificant creatures, like ants, have been given wisdom and understanding by Allah. The ant recognized the danger posed by Solomon's approaching army and warned its fellow ants to seek shelter. It also highlights Solomon's humility, as he was unaware of the ants' presence and the potential harm his army could cause them. This teaches us to be mindful of our actions and their consequences, even if unintentional, and to respect all of Allah's creation, no matter how small or insignificant they may seem.
orig: حتى إذا أتوا على واد النمل قالت نملة يا أيها النمل ادخلوا مساكنكم لا يحطمنكم سليمان وجنوده وهم لا يشعرون

translation: So he smiled, amused at her speech, and said, "My Lord, enable me to be grateful for Your favor which You have bestowed upon me and upon my parents and to do righteousness of which You approve. And admit me by Your mercy into [the ranks of] Your righteous servants."
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of gratitude and righteousness. The person in the verse, upon hearing a certain statement, smiles and turns to Allah in supplication. He asks Allah to enable him to be grateful for the blessings and favors bestowed upon him and his parents. He also prays to Allah to guide him to do righteous deeds that would please Him. Finally, he humbly seeks Allah's mercy to be admitted among the ranks of the righteous servants. This verse emphasizes the significance of recognizing and appreciating Allah's blessings, striving to do good, and seeking Allah's mercy and pleasure.
orig: فتبسم ضاحكا من قولها وقال رب أوزعني أن أشكر نعمتك التي أنعمت علي وعلى والدي وأن أعمل صالحا ترضاه وأدخلني برحمتك في عبادك الصالحين

translation: And he took attendance of the birds and said, "Why do I not see the hoopoe - or is he among the absent?"
interpretation: This verse is interpreted as a lesson in accountability and responsibility. The hoopoe, a bird, was absent from the gathering without excuse or permission. Prophet Solomon (peace be upon him), known for his wisdom, noticed this immediately and questioned the hoopoe's absence. This teaches us that everyone, no matter their position, is accountable for their actions and has a responsibility towards their duties and commitments. It also highlights the importance of attention to detail and not overlooking what may seem to be minor issues, as they could be indicative of larger problems. Leaders especially must be vigilant in ensuring all under their charge are fulfilling their roles.
orig: وتفقد الطير فقال ما لي لا أرى الهدهد أم كان من الغائبين

translation: I will surely punish him with a severe punishment or slaughter him unless he brings me a clear authority.
interpretation: This verse is a warning from Prophet Solomon to the hoopoe bird, who had been absent without permission. It demonstrates the importance of obedience and accountability in Islamic teachings. The "clear authority" mentioned could refer to a valid excuse for the hoopoe's absence or evidence that it had been fulfilling a greater purpose in service of God. The verse emphasizes that there are consequences for disobedience and that justice should be tempered with mercy and the opportunity to provide a defense. It also shows that figures of authority have a responsibility to ensure that those under them are acting rightly and that no one is above the law.
orig: لأعذبنه عذابا شديدا أو لأذبحنه أو ليأتيني بسلطان مبين

translation: But the hoopoe stayed not long and said, "I have encompassed [in knowledge] that which you have not encompassed, and I have come to you from Sheba with certain news."
interpretation: This verse speaks about the hoopoe, a bird that was part of Prophet Solomon's army. The hoopoe had been absent for a while, but upon returning, it claimed to have knowledge that even Solomon did not possess. It had visited the land of Sheba and brought back important information. The hoopoe's statement suggests that sometimes, even those who seem insignificant or lesser in status can have valuable knowledge or insights that others, even those of high rank, might lack. It encourages seeking knowledge from various sources and being open to learning from anyone who has something beneficial to share. The verse also sets the stage for the upcoming story of Solomon's interaction with the Queen of Sheba, which the hoopoe's information initiates.
orig: فمكث غير بعيد فقال أحطت بما لم تحط به وجئتك من سبإ بنبإ يقين

translation: Indeed, I found [there] a woman ruling them, and she has been given of all things, and she has a great throne.
interpretation: This verse refers to the Queen of Sheba, known as Bilqis, who ruled over a prosperous kingdom. The verse emphasizes her power and wealth, as indicated by her possession of "all things" and her "great throne." It suggests that she was a formidable ruler with extensive resources at her disposal. The mention of her throne is significant, as it symbolizes her authority and majesty. The verse sets the stage for the subsequent story of Prophet Solomon's interaction with the Queen of Sheba and her eventual submission to the will of Allah.
orig: إني وجدت امرأة تملكهم وأوتيت من كل شيء ولها عرش عظيم

translation: And I found her and her people prostrating to the sun instead of Allah, and Satan has made their deeds pleasing to them and averted them from [His] way, so they are not guided.
interpretation: This verse is referring to the story of the Queen of Sheba and her people, who were worshipping the sun instead of Allah. It suggests that Satan had deceived them into thinking that their idolatrous practices were acceptable, thus leading them astray from the true path of worshipping Allah alone. The verse implies that when people are misguided by Satan's influence, they become unable to find the right way and remain in a state of disbelief and misguidance. It highlights the importance of staying vigilant against Satan's deceptions and holding fast to the worship of Allah alone.
orig: وجدتها وقومها يسجدون للشمس من دون الله وزين لهم الشيطان أعمالهم فصدهم عن السبيل فهم لا يهتدون

translation: Do they not prostrate to Allah, who brings forth what is hidden within the heavens and the earth and knows what you conceal and what you declare?
interpretation: This verse is a reminder that Allah is the one who brings forth all that is hidden, both in the heavens and on earth. He has knowledge of everything, including what people conceal in their hearts and what they openly declare. It is a call to humble oneself before Allah and submit to Him in prostration, acknowledging His power, knowledge, and authority over all things. The verse emphasizes the importance of recognizing Allah's omniscience and the need for humans to be mindful of their actions and intentions, as nothing is hidden from Him.
orig: ألا يسجدوا لله الذي يخرج الخبء في السماوات والأرض ويعلم ما تخفون وما تعلنون

translation: Allah - there is no deity except Him, Lord of the Great Throne.
interpretation: This verse affirms the central tenet of Islam, which is the oneness and uniqueness of Allah as the only true God worthy of worship. It emphasizes that Allah alone is the Lord and Sovereign of the mighty Throne, which represents His supreme authority and dominion over all of creation. The "Great Throne" symbolizes Allah's majesty, grandeur and control over the entire universe. This verse is a powerful declaration of Islamic monotheism (tawheed) and a rejection of all forms of polytheism or association of partners with Allah.
orig: الله لا إله إلا هو رب العرش العظيم

translation: He said, "We will see whether you were truthful or were of the liars."
interpretation: This verse is a challenge or a warning given by someone in a position of authority to another person who has made a claim or statement. The challenger is expressing doubt about the truthfulness of the claim and is determined to investigate and verify whether the person is being honest or lying. It implies that there will be consequences for lying, and that the truth will eventually come to light. The verse emphasizes the importance of honesty and the gravity of making false statements, especially to those in positions of power or authority.
orig: قال سننظر أصدقت أم كنت من الكاذبين

translation: Take this letter of mine and deliver it to them. Then draw back from them, and see what [answer] they return.
interpretation: This verse is instructing the Prophet or the messenger to deliver a message to a group of people, and then to withdraw and observe their reaction and response from a distance. It emphasizes the importance of conveying the divine message faithfully, without being overly concerned about the immediate response or reaction of the recipients. The messenger's duty is to deliver the message, while the outcome and the people's response is left to God's will and judgment. It also suggests a sense of detachment and trust in God's plan, rather than being emotionally invested in how the message is received.
orig: اذهب بكتابي هذا فألقه إليهم ثم تول عنهم فانظر ماذا يرجعون

translation: She said, "O eminent ones, indeed, to me has been delivered a noble letter."
interpretation: This verse is referring to the Queen of Sheba, Bilqis, who received a letter from Prophet Solomon inviting her and her people to submit to Allah and abandon sun worship. The use of the term "noble letter" indicates the respect and reverence she had for the message, recognizing it as coming from a powerful and important source. Her addressing her ministers and advisors as "eminent ones" shows her political status and the weight of the decision she faced in how to respond to this invitation to monotheism from Solomon. The verse captures a pivotal moment of a leader grappling with a consequential religious and political choice.
orig: قالت يا أيها الملأ إني ألقي إلي كتاب كريم

translation: Indeed, it is from Solomon, and indeed, it reads: 'In the name of Allah, the Entirely Merciful, the Especially Merciful.'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the letter being referred to is from Prophet Solomon, who was known for his wisdom and just rule. The letter begins with the Islamic invocation "In the name of Allah, the Entirely Merciful, the Especially Merciful", indicating that Solomon's reign was guided by his faith in Allah and the principles of Islam. This invocation also sets the tone for the content of the letter, suggesting that it will be based on compassion, mercy and justice in line with the divine attributes of Allah mentioned in the opening line.
orig: إنه من سليمان وإنه بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم

translation: So do not exalt yourselves above me but come to me in submission [as Muslims].
interpretation: This verse is a call to humility and submission to God. It warns against arrogance and pride, reminding us that we should not consider ourselves superior to others or to the message of Islam. Instead, we are encouraged to approach God with humility, recognizing His greatness and our own limitations. The verse emphasizes the importance of surrendering ourselves completely to God, following His guidance and commands without reservation. It is a powerful reminder that true success and salvation lie in aligning our will with the will of our Creator and living our lives in a state of willing submission to Him.
orig: ألا تعلوا علي وأتوني مسلمين

translation: She said, "O eminent ones, advise me in my affair. I would not decide a matter until you witness [for] me."
interpretation: This verse shows the wisdom and leadership qualities of the Queen of Sheba. She seeks the counsel of her advisors before making any important decisions, demonstrating her willingness to listen to different perspectives and make informed choices. This highlights the importance of consultation and considering the views of others in decision-making processes, especially for those in positions of authority. The Queen's approach reflects a collaborative and inclusive leadership style, which can lead to better outcomes and stronger support from those being led.
orig: قالت يا أيها الملأ أفتوني في أمري ما كنت قاطعة أمرا حتى تشهدون

translation: They said, "We are men of great strength and of great military might, but the command is yours, so see what you will command."
interpretation: This verse is addressing the situation where the people of Sheba were consulted by their Queen regarding how to respond to Prophet Solomon's letter inviting them to submit to Allah. The people, who were known for their military strength, expressed their readiness to fight if the Queen commands them to do so. However, they ultimately left the decision to her, recognizing her authority and wisdom to decide the best course of action. This highlights the importance of wise leadership and the willingness of followers to obey their leader's command, while also offering their counsel and support.
orig: قالوا نحن أولو قوة وأولو بأس شديد والأمر إليك فانظري ماذا تأمرين

translation: She said, "Indeed, when kings enter a city, they ruin it and make the honored of its people humbled. And thus do they do."
interpretation: This verse is a warning about the nature of tyrannical rulers and the consequences of their actions. When unjust kings or leaders enter a city or take control of a land, they often bring corruption and destruction. They oppress the people, especially those who were once honored and respected, reducing them to a state of humiliation and disgrace. This interpretation highlights the importance of just and righteous leadership, as opposed to the abuse of power that leads to the ruin of societies. It serves as a reminder for those in positions of authority to rule with fairness and compassion, rather than exploiting their power for personal gain at the expense of their subjects.
orig: قالت إن الملوك إذا دخلوا قرية أفسدوها وجعلوا أعزة أهلها أذلة وكذلك يفعلون

translation: But indeed, I will send to them a gift and see with what [reply] the messengers will return.
interpretation: This verse is referring to the story of the Queen of Sheba and her encounter with Prophet Solomon. The Queen, upon hearing about Solomon's greatness and power, decides to send him gifts as a diplomatic gesture, rather than openly challenging him or submitting to his authority. She wants to test him and see how he will respond to her gifts. This strategy shows her wisdom and caution in dealing with a potentially stronger ruler. It also highlights the importance of diplomacy and tactical maneuvers in political relations. The verse subtly indicates that the reaction of Solomon to these gifts will determine the Queen's next course of action and the future of the relationship between their kingdoms.
orig: وإني مرسلة إليهم بهدية فناظرة بم يرجع المرسلون

translation: But when he came to Solomon, he said, "Do you provide me with wealth? But what Allah has given me is better than what He has given you. Rather, it is you who rejoice in your gift."
interpretation: This verse highlights the wisdom and contentment of Prophet Solomon. When the Queen of Sheba sent him gifts, he was not impressed by the material wealth, recognizing that the blessings and wisdom bestowed upon him by Allah were far superior. Solomon's response emphasizes the importance of valuing spiritual wealth over worldly possessions. It also serves as a reminder that true happiness and satisfaction come from one's relationship with Allah, rather than from material gifts or wealth. Solomon's attitude demonstrates his strong faith and his understanding of the temporary nature of worldly pleasures compared to the eternal rewards of the Hereafter.
orig: فلما جاء سليمان قال أتمدونن بمال فما آتاني الله خير مما آتاكم بل أنتم بهديتكم تفرحون

translation: Return to them, for we will come to them with soldiers that they will be powerless to encounter, and we will expel them from there in humiliation, and they will be debased.
interpretation: This verse is a warning to those who oppose Allah and His messengers. It emphasizes the power and might of Allah, and how He is capable of sending armies that no one can withstand. The interpretation is that those who arrogantly reject the truth and persist in disbelief will face a humiliating defeat and expulsion as a consequence of their actions. It serves as a reminder of the ultimate fate that awaits those who defy Allah's commands and rebel against His authority.
orig: ارجع إليهم فلنأتينهم بجنود لا قبل لهم بها ولنخرجنهم منها أذلة وهم صاغرون

translation: He said, "O assembly [of jinn], which of you will bring me her throne before they come to me in submission?"
interpretation: This verse is interpreted as a challenge posed by Prophet Solomon to the jinn under his command. He asks them who among them can bring the throne of the Queen of Sheba to him before she and her people come to him in submission to Allah. It demonstrates Solomon's authority over the jinn and his desire to impress upon the Queen of Sheba the power of the One True God. The verse also highlights the supernatural abilities of the jinn, who are able to transport the throne over a great distance in a short span of time. Ultimately, it sets the stage for the Queen's eventual acceptance of Solomon's prophethood and her submission to Allah.
orig: قال يا أيها الملأ أيكم يأتيني بعرشها قبل أن يأتوني مسلمين

translation: Said an 'Ifrit (strong one) from the jinns: "I will bring it to you before you rise from your place (council). And verily, I am indeed strong, and trustworthy for such work."
interpretation: This verse shows that not all jinns are evil, and that some of them, despite their immense strength and abilities, can be trustworthy and subservient to the will of Allah. The 'Ifrit's willingness to serve Prophet Solomon and bring him the throne of the Queen of Sheba demonstrates that even powerful beings can humble themselves before the authority of Allah and His chosen servants. It also highlights the importance of trust and reliability in carrying out tasks and fulfilling promises, even for those with extraordinary powers.
orig: قال عفريت من الجن أنا آتيك به قبل أن تقوم من مقامك وإني عليه لقوي أمين

translation: Said one who had knowledge from the Scripture, "I will bring it to you before your glance returns to you." And when [Solomon] saw it placed before him, he said, "This is from the favor of my Lord to test me whether I will be grateful or ungrateful. And whoever is grateful - his gratitude is only for [the benefit of] himself. And whoever is ungrateful - then indeed, my Lord is Free of need and Generous."
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of gratitude and the recognition that all blessings come from Allah. The person with knowledge from the Scripture, believed to be Asif bin Barkhiya, demonstrates the power of faith and knowledge by bringing the throne of the Queen of Sheba to Solomon in an instant. Solomon, upon seeing this, acknowledges that this is a favor from Allah to test his gratitude. He emphasizes that being grateful is beneficial for oneself, as it helps one recognize and appreciate the blessings bestowed by Allah. On the other hand, ingratitude does not harm Allah, as He is self-sufficient and generous, but rather harms the ungrateful person. This verse encourages believers to always be thankful for the blessings in their lives and to remember that everything comes from Allah's favor and mercy.
orig: قال الذي عنده علم من الكتاب أنا آتيك به قبل أن يرتد إليك طرفك فلما رآه مستقرا عنده قال هذا من فضل ربي ليبلوني أأشكر أم أكفر ومن شكر فإنما يشكر لنفسه ومن كفر فإن ربي غني كريم

translation: He said, "Disguise her throne for her that we may see whether she will be guided [to truth] or will be of those who is not guided."
interpretation: This verse is a test of the Queen of Sheba's wisdom and insight. By altering her throne, Solomon aims to determine whether she possesses the discernment to recognize it as her own, despite the changes made to its appearance. This test serves as a means of gauging her spiritual guidance and ability to see beyond superficial alterations. It highlights the importance of inner wisdom and the capacity to perceive the true essence of things, rather than being misled by external modifications. The verse suggests that those who are truly guided by God will have the insight to recognize the truth, even when it is presented in an unfamiliar form.
orig: قال نكروا لها عرشها ننظر أتهتدي أم تكون من الذين لا يهتدون

translation: So when she arrived, it was said [to her], "Is your throne like this?" She said, "[It is] as though it was it." [Solomon said], "And we were given knowledge before her, and we have been Muslims [in submission to Allah].
interpretation: This verse is interpreted as a demonstration of Prophet Solomon's wisdom and power. When the Queen of Sheba arrived, she was asked if her throne resembled the one Solomon had. She acknowledged its similarity, indicating that Solomon had knowledge of her throne before her arrival. This showcases Solomon's divine wisdom and ability. The verse also emphasizes that Solomon and his people were already submitting to Allah before the Queen's arrival, highlighting their strong faith and devotion to monotheism.
orig: فلما جاءت قيل أهكذا عرشك قالت كأنه هو وأوتينا العلم من قبلها وكنا مسلمين

translation: And that which she was worshipping besides Allah had averted her [from submission to Him]. Indeed, she was from a disbelieving people.
interpretation: This verse suggests that the false objects of worship that one devotes themselves to can act as a barrier, preventing them from submitting to the true worship of Allah alone. It implies that her disbelief and idolatry was influenced by her belonging to a people who were engrossed in worshipping false deities instead of Allah. One's social environment and the prevalent religious practices of their community can have a strong sway in shaping their beliefs and leading them away from the straight path, which is the exclusive worship of Allah without any partners.
orig: وصدها ما كانت تعبد من دون الله إنها كانت من قوم كافرين

translation: It was said to her, "Enter the palace." But when she saw it, she thought it was a body of water and uncovered her shins [to wade through]. He said, "Indeed, it is a palace [whose floor is] made smooth with glass." She said, "My Lord, indeed I have wronged myself, and I submit with Solomon to Allah, Lord of the worlds."
interpretation: This verse highlights the power and wisdom of Solomon, who was able to create an illusion that tested the Queen of Sheba's perception and humility. The palace floor, made of smooth glass, appeared to her as a pool of water, causing her to lift her dress and expose her shins. This incident led to her realization of Solomon's superiority and her own limitations, prompting her to submit to Allah alongside Solomon. The verse emphasizes the importance of recognizing one's own faults, submitting to the will of Allah, and acknowledging the wisdom and power of His chosen servants.
orig: قيل لها ادخلي الصرح فلما رأته حسبته لجة وكشفت عن ساقيها قال إنه صرح ممرد من قوارير قالت رب إني ظلمت نفسي وأسلمت مع سليمان لله رب العالمين

translation: And We had certainly sent to Thamud their brother Salih, [saying], "Worship Allah," and at once they were two parties conflicting.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of worshipping Allah alone and avoiding division and conflict. The story of Prophet Salih and his people, Thamud, serves as a reminder that even when a prophet is sent with a clear message to worship Allah, people may still be divided and engage in disputes. It highlights the human tendency towards disagreement and the need for unity in faith and obedience to Allah's message. The verse also implies that rejecting the prophets and their message leads to discord and ultimately, to the downfall of a community, as was the case with the people of Thamud.
orig: ولقد أرسلنا إلى ثمود أخاهم صالحا أن اعبدوا الله فإذا هم فريقان يختصمون

translation: He said, "O my people, why are you impatient for evil instead of good? Why do you not seek forgiveness of Allah that you may receive mercy?"
interpretation: This verse is a call to repentance and seeking Allah's forgiveness. The speaker is admonishing his people for hastening towards evil deeds and wrongdoing, rather than being eager to do good. He reminds them that they should seek Allah's forgiveness sincerely, so that Allah may have mercy on them and guide them to the right path. The verse emphasizes the importance of turning to Allah in repentance and seeking His mercy, as this is the way to attain success and salvation in this life and the hereafter.
orig: قال يا قوم لم تستعجلون بالسيئة قبل الحسنة لولا تستغفرون الله لعلكم ترحمون

translation: They said, "We consider you a bad omen, you and those with you." He said, "Your omen is with Allah. Rather, you are a people being tested."
interpretation: This verse is addressing the disbelievers who attributed their misfortunes and calamities to the presence of the Prophet and his followers. They considered them as a bad omen and blamed them for the difficulties they faced. However, the Prophet responded by stating that their fate and destiny is determined by Allah alone, and that the difficulties they face are a test from Him. The verse emphasizes that people should not be superstitious or attribute their circumstances to omens, but rather understand that all events occur by the will of Allah as a means of testing and trial for mankind.
orig: قالوا اطيرنا بك وبمن معك قال طائركم عند الله بل أنتم قوم تفتنون

translation: And there were in the city nine men who made mischief in the land and did not reform.
interpretation: This verse is referring to a group of nine individuals in the city who were actively causing corruption and harm, and not making any effort to rectify their behavior or improve the situation. It highlights the negative impact that even a small group of people can have on society when they engage in destructive actions and fail to fulfill their responsibilities towards others. The Qur'an is condemning this type of behavior and emphasizing the importance of striving for righteousness and positive reform within the community.
orig: وكان في المدينة تسعة رهط يفسدون في الأرض ولا يصلحون

translation: They said, "Take a mutual oath by Allah that we will kill him by night, him and his family. Then we will say to his executor, 'We did not witness the destruction of his family, and indeed, we are truthful.'"
interpretation: This verse is referring to a plot by a group of people who conspire to kill a man and his family at night, and then claim to his heir or guardian that they had no knowledge of what happened to them. They plan to swear by Allah that they are telling the truth, even though they are actually lying and are responsible for the murders. This highlights the depths of their treachery and willingness to commit such a heinous act, while also showing their audacity in attempting to cover it up with false oaths.
orig: قالوا تقاسموا بالله لنبيتنه وأهله ثم لنقولن لوليه ما شهدنا مهلك أهله وإنا لصادقون

translation: And they planned a plan, and We planned a plan, while they perceived not.
interpretation: This verse speaks to the futility of plotting against God's will. The disbelievers schemed against the Prophet and the message of Islam, thinking they could outsmart the divine plan. However, God is the best of planners, and His plan will always supersede the machinations of men. The verse implies that while the enemies of faith may think themselves clever, they are ultimately unaware of and powerless before God's superior wisdom and strategy. It is a reminder that no human plot can ever thwart what God has decreed, and that the faithful should remain steadfast, trusting in His plan even in the face of apparent setbacks or opposition.
orig: ومكروا مكرا ومكرنا مكرا وهم لا يشعرون

translation: So look how was the end of their plot! Indeed, We destroyed them and their people, all together.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the ultimate fate of those who scheme and plot against the truth. It serves as a warning that no matter how clever or powerful the enemies of faith may seem, their plots will ultimately fail and lead to their own destruction. The verse highlights God's power and justice in dealing with those who oppose His message and His messengers. It also serves as a reminder to the believers to trust in God's plan and not be discouraged by the apparent success of the wrongdoers, for their end will be utter ruin and loss, both in this world and in the Hereafter.
orig: فانظر كيف كان عاقبة مكرهم أنا دمرناهم وقومهم أجمعين

translation: So those are their houses, desolate because of the wrong they had done. Indeed in that is a sign for people who know.
interpretation: This verse points to the consequences of wrongdoing and injustice. It suggests that the desolation and ruin of the homes of the wrongdoers serve as a clear sign and lesson for those who reflect and seek knowledge. The verse implies that the ultimate fate of those who engage in oppression and transgression is destruction and loss, and that their end serves as a warning and admonition for others. It highlights the importance of justice, righteousness, and avoiding oppression, as the consequences of such actions are severe and long-lasting. The verse encourages people to learn from the mistakes of others and to take heed of the signs that Allah presents in the world around them.
orig: فتلك بيوتهم خاوية بما ظلموا إن في ذلك لآية لقوم يعلمون

translation: And We saved those who believed and used to fear Allah.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah saves and protects those who have true faith and live their lives in accordance with that faith, fearing Allah and being mindful of Him in all their actions. It implies that even in times of great difficulty or trials, those who remain steadfast in their belief and piety will ultimately be saved by Allah's mercy and grace, while those who reject faith or transgress against Allah's commands will face the consequences of their choices. The verse encourages believers to cultivate taqwa (God-consciousness) as a means of attaining salvation and success in this life and the hereafter.
orig: وأنجينا الذين آمنوا وكانوا يتقون

translation: And [mention] Lot, when he said to his people, "Do you commit immorality while you are seeing?"
interpretation: This verse is a strong condemnation of the immoral acts being committed by the people of Lot, specifically homosexuality. The rhetorical question "Do you commit immorality while you are seeing?" implies that they are fully aware of the depravity and unnaturalness of their actions, yet they persist in them anyway. It suggests that engaging in such acts goes against the innate human understanding of right and wrong that God has instilled in mankind. The verse emphasizes the gravity of the sin and the people's culpability in knowingly committing it despite the ability to recognize its immorality.
orig: ولوطا إذ قال لقومه أتأتون الفاحشة وأنتم تبصرون

translation: Do you approach men with desire instead of women? Rather, you are a people behaving ignorantly.
interpretation: This verse is a strong condemnation of homosexual behavior, describing it as an act of ignorance and a deviation from the natural order established by God. It suggests that engaging in same-sex relations is a result of not understanding or accepting the proper roles and functions of men and women as ordained by God. The verse implies that heterosexual relationships between men and women are the only acceptable form of intimate relations sanctioned in Islam.
orig: أئنكم لتأتون الرجال شهوة من دون النساء بل أنتم قوم تجهلون

translation: But the answer of his people was not except that they said, "Evict the family of Lot from your city. Indeed, they are people who keep themselves pure."
interpretation: This verse highlights the arrogance and moral depravity of the people of Sodom. Instead of heeding the warnings of Prophet Lot (peace be upon him) and abandoning their sinful ways, they mocked him and his family for their righteousness. They viewed the purity and chastity of Lot's family as a threat to their own corrupt lifestyle. As a result, they sought to expel them from the city, revealing their deep-rooted rejection of divine guidance and their persistence in transgression. This response demonstrates how those who are steeped in sin often react with hostility and derision towards those who call them to the path of righteousness.
orig: فما كان جواب قومه إلا أن قالوا أخرجوا آل لوط من قريتكم إنهم أناس يتطهرون

translation: So We saved him and his family, except for his wife; We destined her to be of those who remained behind.
interpretation: This verse highlights the mercy and justice of Allah. He saved the Prophet Lut (Lot) and his believing family members from the punishment that befell his people due to their grave sins. However, Allah did not save Lut's wife as she was not a believer and sided with the wrongdoers. This shows that faith and righteousness are the criteria for salvation, not mere family ties. It also emphasizes that everyone is responsible for their own choices and actions, and will face the consequences accordingly in this life and the hereafter.
orig: فأنجيناه وأهله إلا امرأته قدرناها من الغابرين

translation: And We rained upon them a rain [of stones], and evil was the rain of those who were warned.
interpretation: This verse is a warning to those who reject the message of Allah and His prophets. It refers to the punishment that befell the people of Lut (Lot) who were guilty of practicing homosexuality and other immoral acts. Allah sent down a rain of stones upon them as a form of destruction, which serves as a reminder of the severe consequences of disobedience to Allah's commands. The verse emphasizes that those who are warned of the consequences of their sinful actions, yet persist in their wrongdoings, will face a terrible fate, symbolized by the "evil rain" that destroyed the people of Lut. It is a reminder for all people to heed the warnings of Allah and to follow the righteous path to avoid a similar punishment.
orig: وأمطرنا عليهم مطرا فساء مطر المنذرين

translation: Say, "[All] praise is [due] to Allah, and peace upon His servants whom He has chosen. Is Allah better or what they associate with Him?"
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of praising Allah alone and rejecting the worship of any other entity besides Him. It highlights the superiority of Allah over any false deities or idols that people may associate with Him. The verse also conveys a message of peace and blessings upon those servants of Allah whom He has chosen, indicating that true believers who submit to Allah's will and follow His guidance will be rewarded with divine favor and tranquility. It serves as a reminder for people to direct their worship, gratitude, and reverence towards Allah alone, as He is the only One worthy of such devotion.
orig: قل الحمد لله وسلام على عباده الذين اصطفى آلله خير أما يشركون

translation: Is He [not best] who created the heavens and the earth and sent down for you rain from the sky, causing to grow thereby gardens of joyful beauty which you could not [otherwise] have grown the trees thereof? Is there a deity with Allah? [No], but they are a people who ascribe equals [to Him].
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the power and uniqueness of Allah as the Creator and Sustainer of the universe. It challenges the notion of associating partners with Him by highlighting His ability to create the heavens and the earth, and to send down rain that causes gardens of incredible beauty to grow - something that humans could never accomplish on their own. The rhetorical question "Is there a deity with Allah?" is meant to underscore the absurdity of attributing divine qualities to anyone or anything other than Him. The verse concludes by characterizing those who ascribe equals to Allah as misguided and irrational.
orig: أمن خلق السماوات والأرض وأنزل لكم من السماء ماء فأنبتنا به حدائق ذات بهجة ما كان لكم أن تنبتوا شجرها أإله مع الله بل هم قوم يعدلون

translation: Is He [not best] who made the earth a stable ground and placed within it rivers and made for it firmly set mountains and placed between the two seas a barrier? Is there a deity with Allah? [No], but most of them do not know.
interpretation: This verse points to the power and wisdom of Allah in creating the earth with its perfect balance and intricate systems. It highlights how Allah has made the earth stable and habitable for humans, with rivers flowing through it, mountains firmly rooted to provide stability, and natural barriers between bodies of water. The rhetorical question "Is there a deity with Allah?" emphasizes that these wonders of creation could only be the work of the One True God. Despite these clear signs, the verse suggests that most people fail to recognize and acknowledge Allah's sovereignty and uniqueness, remaining ignorant of the truth.
orig: أمن جعل الأرض قرارا وجعل خلالها أنهارا وجعل لها رواسي وجعل بين البحرين حاجزا أإله مع الله بل أكثرهم لا يعلمون

translation: Is He [not best] who responds to the desperate one when he calls upon Him and removes evil and makes you inheritors of the earth? Is there a deity with Allah? Little do you remember.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's unique power and mercy. It reminds us that Allah alone answers the prayers of those in dire need, relieves their distress, and grants them success and authority on earth. The rhetorical question "Is there a deity with Allah?" stresses His oneness and supremacy. The final admonition, "Little do you remember," is a wake-up call for humans to reflect more on Allah's countless blessings and favor upon them, instead of being heedless or ungrateful. It motivates believers to turn to Allah with sincerity, especially in times of hardship, trusting that He will respond and provide relief.
orig: أمن يجيب المضطر إذا دعاه ويكشف السوء ويجعلكم خلفاء الأرض أإله مع الله قليلا ما تذكرون

translation: Is He [not best] who guides you through the darknesses of the land and sea and who sends the winds as good tidings before His mercy? Is there a deity with Allah? High is Allah above whatever they associate with Him.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the power and uniqueness of Allah. It poses a rhetorical question, asking if there is any other deity who can guide humanity through the difficulties and perils of life, symbolized by the "darknesses of the land and sea". It also mentions Allah's mercy and grace, as represented by the winds that bring good tidings and relief. The verse asserts that Allah is far above any partners or equals that people may attribute to Him, highlighting His supremacy and the foolishness of those who associate others with Him in worship or devotion.
orig: أمن يهديكم في ظلمات البر والبحر ومن يرسل الرياح بشرا بين يدي رحمته أإله مع الله تعالى الله عما يشركون

translation: Is He [not best] who begins creation and then repeats it and who provides for you from the heaven and earth? Is there a deity with Allah? Say, "Produce your proof, if you should be truthful."
interpretation: This verse challenges those who associate partners with Allah to provide evidence for their beliefs. It asserts that Allah alone is the One who originates creation and will resurrect it, and He is the sole provider of sustenance from the heavens and the earth. The verse emphasizes the concept of tawheed (oneness of Allah) and demands proof from those who claim there are other deities besides Him. It serves as a powerful reminder that faith in Allah should be based on clear evidence and not mere speculation or blind following of ancestral traditions. The verse also highlights Allah's power, creativity, and all-encompassing provision for His creation.
orig: أمن يبدأ الخلق ثم يعيده ومن يرزقكم من السماء والأرض أإله مع الله قل هاتوا برهانكم إن كنتم صادقين

translation: Say, "None in the heavens and earth knows the unseen except Allah, and they do not perceive when they will be resurrected."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that knowledge of the unseen, particularly the timing of the Day of Resurrection, belongs exclusively to Allah. No one in the heavens or on earth, including angels, jinn, and humans, possesses this knowledge. It serves as a reminder for humans to focus on their actions in this life, as they cannot predict or know when the Day of Judgment will occur. The verse also highlights the importance of submitting to Allah's will and trusting in His divine plan, as He alone holds the knowledge of the unseen and the ultimate fate of all creation.
orig: قل لا يعلم من في السماوات والأرض الغيب إلا الله وما يشعرون أيان يبعثون

translation: Nay, their knowledge of the Hereafter is slight and hasty. Nay, they are in doubt concerning it. Nay, they are blind thereunto.
interpretation: This verse highlights the limited and flawed understanding of those who reject the concept of the Hereafter. It suggests that their knowledge is superficial and based on hasty assumptions rather than deep reflection or genuine insight. The repetition of "Nay" emphasizes the gravity of their misconceptions. The verse further states that they are not only doubtful about the Hereafter but are entirely blind to its reality, indicating a complete lack of spiritual awareness and understanding. This blindness prevents them from recognizing the truth and significance of the afterlife, leading them to live their lives without proper guidance or purpose.
orig: بل ادارك علمهم في الآخرة بل هم في شك منها بل هم منها عمون

translation: And those who disbelieve say, "When we have become dust as well as our forefathers, will we indeed be brought out [of the graves]?"
interpretation: This verse reflects the skepticism and disbelief of those who reject the concept of resurrection and afterlife. They find it hard to believe that after their bodies have decomposed and turned to dust, they will be brought back to life and held accountable for their deeds. This skepticism stems from their limited understanding of God's power and their attachment to the material world. The verse highlights the importance of faith in the unseen and the need to trust in God's wisdom and ability to resurrect the dead, as it is a fundamental belief in Islam.
orig: وقال الذين كفروا أإذا كنا ترابا وآباؤنا أئنا لمخرجون

translation: We have been promised this, we and our forefathers before. This is not but legends of the former peoples.
interpretation: This verse reflects the skepticism and disbelief of those who reject the message of the Qur'an and the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him). They dismiss the warnings of divine judgment and the promise of resurrection as mere legends or myths passed down from previous generations. It suggests that they are unwilling to open their hearts to the truth and instead cling to the familiar beliefs and traditions of their ancestors. The verse highlights the human tendency to resist change and to find comfort in the status quo, even when confronted with a message that challenges their worldview and calls them to a higher purpose.
orig: لقد وعدنا هذا نحن وآباؤنا من قبل إن هذا إلا أساطير الأولين

translation: Say, "Travel through the land and observe how was the end of the criminals."
interpretation: This verse is a call to reflect on the fate of past nations who rejected the message of Allah and committed crimes and sins. It encourages people to travel the earth and observe the ruins and remains of those who were destroyed by Allah's punishment due to their disobedience and wrongdoing. The verse implies that the end of the criminals is always destruction and loss, both in this world and the Hereafter. It serves as a warning to those who follow in the footsteps of the criminals and a reminder of Allah's justice and power. The verse also highlights the importance of learning from history and taking heed of the lessons and admonitions found in the stories of past nations mentioned in the Qur'an.
orig: قل سيروا في الأرض فانظروا كيف كان عاقبة المجرمين

translation: And grieve not over them or be in distress from what they conspire.
interpretation: This verse is a reminder from Allah to Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) not to feel saddened or distressed by the plots and conspiracies of the disbelievers against him and the message of Islam. It is a reassurance that Allah is aware of their schemes and will protect His Prophet and the believers from their harm. The verse encourages the Prophet to remain steadfast in his faith and mission, and to trust in Allah's plan and support, despite the challenges and opposition he faces. It emphasizes the importance of patience, perseverance, and reliance on Allah in the face of adversity.
orig: ولا تحزن عليهم ولا تكن في ضيق مما يمكرون

translation: And they say, "When is this promise, if you should be truthful?"
interpretation: This verse is a challenge from the disbelievers to the believers, questioning the timing of the fulfillment of God's promise. The disbelievers are skeptical and doubtful about the reality of the Day of Judgment and the afterlife that the believers have faith in. They demand to know when this promised event will occur, as if to prove the truthfulness of the believers' claims. The verse highlights the contrast between the certainty of faith held by the believers and the cynicism and disbelief of those who reject the divine message. It also underscores the human tendency to seek immediate gratification and proof, rather than having patience and trust in God's plan and timing.
orig: ويقولون متى هذا الوعد إن كنتم صادقين

translation: Say, "Perhaps that which you are impatient for has already drawn near to you."
interpretation: This verse is a warning to those who are impatient for Allah's punishment or judgment to come upon others. It reminds them that what they wish for may be closer than they think, and that they should be careful what they wish for. The verse implies that one should not be hasty in seeking Allah's punishment on others, as it may come back to affect them as well. Instead, one should focus on their own actions and strive to be righteous, rather than concerning themselves with the fate of others. The verse encourages patience, humility, and trust in Allah's wisdom and timing.
orig: قل عسى أن يكون ردف لكم بعض الذي تستعجلون

translation: And indeed, your Lord is full of bounty to the people, but most of them do not show gratitude.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the immense generosity and grace that Allah bestows upon humanity, providing them with countless blessings and favors. However, it also points out the unfortunate reality that the majority of people fail to acknowledge and appreciate these blessings. They take them for granted and do not express their gratitude to Allah for His kindness and mercy. This lack of gratitude is a sign of heedlessness and ingratitude, which can lead to negative consequences in both this world and the hereafter. The verse serves as a reminder for believers to constantly recognize and appreciate the bounties of their Lord and to express their thankfulness through worship, obedience, and good deeds.
orig: وإن ربك لذو فضل على الناس ولكن أكثرهم لا يشكرون

translation: And indeed, your Lord knows what their breasts conceal and what they declare.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's omniscience and His complete knowledge of all things, whether hidden in the hearts of people or openly declared. It serves as a reminder that nothing can be concealed from Allah, and that He is fully aware of the innermost thoughts, intentions, and secrets of His creation. This understanding should motivate believers to purify their hearts, maintain sincerity in their actions, and be mindful of their thoughts and deeds, as they are all known to Allah.
orig: وإن ربك ليعلم ما تكن صدورهم وما يعلنون

translation: And there is nothing concealed within the heaven and the earth except that it is in a clear Register.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the concept of divine omniscience, stating that nothing in the heavens or earth is hidden from Allah. Everything is recorded in a "clear Register" or "clear Book", referring to Allah's perfect knowledge and the divine records that encompass all things. It highlights the idea that nothing escapes Allah's awareness, whether it is apparent or concealed, and that all things are meticulously accounted for in His divine records. This verse serves as a reminder of Allah's all-encompassing knowledge and the ultimate accountability of all things before Him.
orig: وما من غائبة في السماء والأرض إلا في كتاب مبين

translation: Indeed, this Qur'an relates to the Children of Israel most of that over which they disagree.
interpretation: The Qur'an serves as a source of guidance and clarification for the Children of Israel, addressing many of the religious matters and historical events about which they have differing opinions. It provides them with the truth regarding these issues, resolving their disagreements and offering them a clear understanding of their own history and the teachings of their prophets. The Qur'an aims to guide them towards the right path and unite them under the true message of Islam.
orig: إن هذا القرآن يقص على بني إسرائيل أكثر الذي هم فيه يختلفون

translation: And indeed, it is guidance and mercy for the believers.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the Qur'an serves as a source of guidance and mercy for those who have faith in Allah. It directs believers towards the right path, helping them navigate through life's challenges and uncertainties. The Qur'an's teachings and wisdom act as a compassionate guide, providing solace, comfort, and spiritual nourishment to the hearts of the faithful. By following its guidance and embracing its mercy, believers can attain inner peace, contentment, and a deeper connection with their Creator.
orig: وإنه لهدى ورحمة للمؤمنين

translation: Indeed, your Lord will judge between them by His [wise] judgement. And He is the Exalted in Might, the Knowing.
interpretation: This verse assures that Allah, in His infinite wisdom and power, will ultimately judge between people regarding their differences and disputes. It emphasizes that we should put our trust in Allah's judgement, as He is the All-Mighty and All-Knowing. His decisions are based on perfect knowledge and wisdom, unlike human judgements which can be biased or flawed. As believers, we should find comfort in knowing that justice will prevail in the end, even if it may not seem apparent in this worldly life. The verse encourages us to be patient and have faith in Allah's plan, knowing that He will hold everyone accountable for their deeds and resolve all matters with His perfect understanding and fairness.
orig: إن ربك يقضي بينهم بحكمه وهو العزيز العليم

translation: So rely upon Allah; indeed, you are upon the clear truth.
