interpretation: This verse encourages the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and the believers to put their complete trust in Allah, knowing that they are following the path of truth and righteousness. It emphasizes the importance of having unwavering faith in Allah's support and guidance, especially in the face of challenges or opposition. By relying on Allah, one can find strength, comfort, and reassurance in the knowledge that they are adhering to the clear and unambiguous truth of Islam.
orig: فتوكل على الله إنك على الحق المبين

translation: Indeed, you cannot make the dead hear, nor can you make the deaf hear the call when they have turned their backs retreating.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the idea that guidance ultimately comes from Allah, and that the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) cannot force anyone to accept the message of Islam. Those who have turned away from the truth and are not open to listening are compared to the dead and the deaf, who cannot perceive or respond to any call. It highlights the importance of free will and the individual's choice to accept or reject the divine message. The Prophet's role is to convey the message clearly, but the response and acceptance lie with each person, as Allah alone can guide hearts towards the truth.
orig: إنك لا تسمع الموتى ولا تسمع الصم الدعاء إذا ولوا مدبرين

translation: And you cannot guide the blind away from their error. You can only make hear those who believe in Our verses so they are Muslims.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) cannot force anyone to accept Islam or guide those who are spiritually "blind" due to their persistent disbelief. He can only convey the message to those who are willing to believe in Allah's revelations and submit to Him. It is ultimately up to each individual to open their heart to the truth and embrace faith, as guidance comes from Allah alone. The Prophet's role is to deliver the message clearly, but he has no control over who will accept it and who will not.
orig: وما أنت بهادي العمي عن ضلالتهم إن تسمع إلا من يؤمن بآياتنا فهم مسلمون

translation: And when the word befalls them, We will bring forth for them a creature from the earth speaking to them, [saying] that the people were, of Our verses, not certain [in faith].
interpretation: This verse refers to one of the signs of the Day of Judgment. When Allah's decree comes to pass, He will bring forth a beast from the earth that will speak to the people, admonishing them that they did not have true faith and conviction in Allah's signs and revelations. This extraordinary event will be a clear indication that the Day of Judgment is near, and it serves as a warning to humanity that they should have believed in Allah's messages when they had the chance. The appearance of this beast will be a supernatural occurrence, demonstrating Allah's power and the truth of His warnings to mankind.
orig: وإذا وقع القول عليهم أخرجنا لهم دابة من الأرض تكلمهم أن الناس كانوا بآياتنا لا يوقنون

translation: And the Day We will gather from every nation a company of those who deny Our signs, and they will be [driven] in rows.
interpretation: This verse is referring to the Day of Judgment, when Allah will gather a group from every nation who rejected His signs and messages. They will be driven in rows, indicating that they will be organized and controlled, unable to escape their fate. The interpretation is that denying Allah's signs and revelations is a grave sin that will lead to severe consequences on the Day of Judgment. It serves as a warning to those who reject faith and a reminder of the importance of believing in and following Allah's guidance.
orig: ويوم نحشر من كل أمة فوجا ممن يكذب بآياتنا فهم يوزعون

translation: Until, when they come [before their Lord], He will say, "Did you deny My signs while you encompassed them not in knowledge, or what [was it that] you were doing?"
interpretation: This verse is a stern warning from Allah to those who reject His signs and revelations without having any knowledge or understanding of them. It highlights the arrogance and ignorance of the disbelievers who deny the truth without any basis or evidence. On the Day of Judgment, Allah will question them about their actions and their reasons for rejecting His messages. This verse serves as a reminder for people to seek knowledge and understanding before making judgments or rejecting the truth, as they will be held accountable for their actions and beliefs in the Hereafter.
orig: حتى إذا جاءوا قال أكذبتم بآياتي ولم تحيطوا بها علما أماذا كنتم تعملون

translation: And the word [of judgement] will fall upon them for the wrong they did, and they will not speak.
interpretation: This verse refers to the Day of Judgment when the wrongdoers will be condemned for their actions. They will be rendered speechless, unable to defend themselves or make excuses for their misdeeds. It emphasizes the concept of accountability and divine justice, where everyone will face the consequences of their deeds. The verse also implies that the time for repentance and rectification is in this worldly life, before it is too late and one must answer for their transgressions in the Hereafter.
orig: ووقع القول عليهم بما ظلموا فهم لا ينطقون

translation: Do they not see that We made the night that they may rest therein and the day giving sight? Indeed in that are signs for a people who believe.
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine wisdom behind the creation of night and day. The night is meant for rest and tranquility, allowing people to recharge and find peace. The day, on the other hand, is designed for work, activity, and the pursuit of one's livelihood. The alternation of night and day is a sign of Allah's power, mercy, and perfect design of the universe. It serves as a reminder for those who believe, encouraging them to reflect upon the wonders of creation and strengthen their faith in the Creator. The verse emphasizes that these signs are apparent to those who are willing to believe and open their hearts to the truth.
orig: ألم يروا أنا جعلنا الليل ليسكنوا فيه والنهار مبصرا إن في ذلك لآيات لقوم يؤمنون

translation: And the Day the Horn will be blown, and whoever is in the heavens and whoever is on the earth will be terrified except whom Allah wills. And all will come to Him humbled.
interpretation: This verse refers to the Day of Judgment when the trumpet will be blown, causing terror and fear in all creatures in the heavens and the earth, except those whom Allah wills to spare. It emphasizes the absolute power and authority of Allah over His creation. The verse also highlights the inevitability of all beings returning to Allah in a state of humility and submission, regardless of their status or power in this worldly life. It serves as a reminder for mankind to remain humble and mindful of their ultimate return to their Creator.
orig: ويوم ينفخ في الصور ففزع من في السماوات ومن في الأرض إلا من شاء الله وكل أتوه داخرين

translation: And you see the mountains, thinking them rigid, while they will pass as the passing of clouds. [It is] the work of Allah, who perfected all things. Indeed, He is Acquainted with that which you do.
interpretation: This verse highlights the power and perfection of Allah's creation. The mountains, which appear solid and unmoving to the human eye, are in fact in constant motion, just like the passing clouds. This is a reminder that Allah has created everything with precise detail and purpose, and that nothing in the universe is truly stationary or permanent. The verse also emphasizes that Allah is fully aware of all our actions and deeds, encouraging us to be mindful of our behavior and to strive for righteousness in all aspects of our lives.
orig: وترى الجبال تحسبها جامدة وهي تمر مر السحاب صنع الله الذي أتقن كل شيء إنه خبير بما تفعلون

translation: Whoever comes [on the Day of Judgement] with a good deed will have better than it, and they, from the terror of that Day, will be safe.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the immense value of doing good deeds in this worldly life. It promises that whoever does a single good deed will be rewarded with something far better than the deed itself on the Day of Judgment. Moreover, those who come with good deeds will be granted safety and security from the overwhelming terror of that Day, when everyone will be held accountable for their actions. This highlights the importance of striving to do righteous acts, even if they may seem small, as they can lead to immense rewards and divine protection in the Hereafter.
orig: من جاء بالحسنة فله خير منها وهم من فزع يومئذ آمنون

translation: And whoever comes [on the Day of Judgement] with an evil deed - their faces will be overturned into the Fire, [and it will be said], "Are you recompensed except for what you used to do?"
interpretation: This verse warns that those who commit evil deeds in this life will face severe consequences on the Day of Judgment. Their faces will be cast into the Fire of Hell as a punishment for their actions. The rhetorical question at the end emphasizes the justice of this recompense, as people will receive what they deserve based on their deeds in this world. It serves as a reminder for individuals to be mindful of their actions and to strive for righteousness, knowing that they will be held accountable in the Hereafter.
orig: ومن جاء بالسيئة فكبت وجوههم في النار هل تجزون إلا ما كنتم تعملون

translation: I have only been commanded to worship the Lord of this city, who has made it sacred and to whom belongs all things. And I am commanded to be of the Muslims.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of worshipping Allah alone, who is the Lord and Creator of the sacred city of Makkah. It reminds us that everything in existence belongs to Him and that we should submit ourselves completely to His will. The verse also highlights the significance of being among those who surrender themselves to Allah, i.e., the Muslims, and following His commands with sincerity and devotion. It encourages us to dedicate our lives to the worship of the One True God and to strive to be among His faithful servants.
orig: إنما أمرت أن أعبد رب هذه البلدة الذي حرمها وله كل شيء وأمرت أن أكون من المسلمين

translation: And to recite the Qur'an. So whoever is guided is only guided for [the benefit of] his soul. And whoever strays - say, "I am only of the warners."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the role of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) as a messenger whose duty is to convey the message of the Qur'an to mankind. It highlights that the ultimate responsibility for accepting guidance or going astray lies with each individual. The Prophet's task is to warn people of the consequences of their actions, but he cannot force anyone to follow the right path. This interpretation underscores the importance of free will and personal accountability in the Islamic faith, as each person will be held responsible for their own spiritual choices and actions in the Hereafter.
orig: وأن أتلو القرآن فمن اهتدى فإنما يهتدي لنفسه ومن ضل فقل إنما أنا من المنذرين

translation: And say, "[All] praise is [due] to Allah. He will show you His signs, and you will recognize them. And your Lord is not unaware of what you do."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of recognizing and acknowledging the signs of Allah's power and wisdom in the world around us. It reminds us to be grateful to Allah for His blessings and guidance, as He will continue to reveal His signs to those who seek them with an open heart and mind. The verse also serves as a warning that Allah is fully aware of our actions and intentions, and that we will be held accountable for them. It encourages us to strive for righteousness and to live our lives in accordance with Allah's teachings, knowing that He is always watching over us and guiding us towards the right path.
orig: وقل الحمد لله سيريكم آياته فتعرفونها وما ربك بغافل عما تعملون

translation: Ta, Seen, Meem.
interpretation: These are among the "Muqatta'at", the disjointed letters that appear at the beginning of some surahs in the Qur'an. The precise meaning of these letters is unknown, though there are various theories. One common view is that they represent a mystical communication between Allah and the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him), the full meaning of which is known only to Allah. Another perspective is that they serve to attract the attention of the listener and remind them that the Qur'an is a divine revelation, not ordinary speech. Ultimately, the meaning of these letters is part of the unseen knowledge that belongs to Allah alone.
orig: طسم

translation: These are the verses of the clear Book.
interpretation: This verse is emphasizing the clarity and unambiguity of the Qur'an. It affirms that the verses of the Qur'an are clear signs and evidence of its divine origin. The Qur'an is described as a "clear Book" because its teachings, guidance, and messages are presented in a lucid and comprehensible manner, making it accessible to all people regardless of their background or level of knowledge. The clarity of the Qur'an leaves no room for doubt about its authenticity as the word of Allah.
orig: تلك آيات الكتاب المبين

translation: We recite to you from the story of Moses and Pharaoh in truth for a people who believe.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of conveying the true and accurate account of the story of Moses and Pharaoh to the believers. It highlights that the Qur'an is the source of this authentic narration, which is being recited to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and, by extension, to all believers. The mention of "a people who believe" indicates that this story is particularly relevant and beneficial for those who have faith, as they will appreciate its lessons and derive guidance from it. It also suggests that the believers are the ones who will truly understand and accept the truth of this account, as opposed to those who reject faith and may dismiss or distort such narratives.
orig: نتلو عليك من نبإ موسى وفرعون بالحق لقوم يؤمنون

translation: Indeed, Pharaoh exalted himself in the land and made its people into factions, oppressing a sector among them, slaughtering their [newborn] sons and keeping their females alive. Indeed, he was of the corrupters.
interpretation: This verse highlights the tyrannical rule of Pharaoh, who divided his people into groups and oppressed a particular group among them. He sought to weaken them by killing their male children and sparing their females, likely to prevent any potential uprising against his rule. This act of oppression and corruption demonstrates Pharaoh's evil nature and his abuse of power. The verse implies that such actions go against the principles of justice and righteousness, and that those who engage in such oppression are considered among the corrupters in the sight of Allah.
orig: إن فرعون علا في الأرض وجعل أهلها شيعا يستضعف طائفة منهم يذبح أبناءهم ويستحيي نساءهم إنه كان من المفسدين

translation: And We wanted to confer favor upon those who were oppressed in the land and make them leaders and make them inheritors.
interpretation: This verse indicates that Allah's will and plan is to elevate those who have been oppressed and persecuted, and to ultimately make them the leaders and inheritors of the land. It suggests that Allah supports the weak and downtrodden, and will grant them victory and authority in the end, as a favor and blessing upon them. This conveys a message of hope and empowerment to those facing oppression and hardship, that their suffering is seen by Allah and will be rewarded and rectified in time according to His wisdom and justice.
orig: ونريد أن نمن على الذين استضعفوا في الأرض ونجعلهم أئمة ونجعلهم الوارثين

translation: And We establish them in the land and show Pharaoh and Haman and their soldiers through them that which they had feared.
interpretation: This verse speaks about how Allah grants power and authority to the believers in the land, even in the face of opposition from mighty rulers like Pharaoh and Haman. It shows that Allah can turn the tables on the oppressors and make what they feared (i.e., losing power to the believers) come to pass. The verse demonstrates Allah's support for His righteous servants and His ability to bring about outcomes that the tyrants and wrongdoers dread, thereby reassuring the believers and warning the oppressors about the consequences of their misdeeds.
orig: ونمكن لهم في الأرض ونري فرعون وهامان وجنودهما منهم ما كانوا يحذرون

translation: And We inspired the mother of Moses, saying: Suckle him and, when thou fearest for him, then cast him into the river and fear not nor grieve. Lo! We shall bring him back unto thee and shall make him (one) of Our messengers.
interpretation: This verse is a reassurance to the mother of Moses from Allah. It shows that even in the face of great danger and fear, putting one's trust in Allah's plan and following divine inspiration can lead to a positive outcome. The mother's faith and obedience, despite her natural worries as a parent, are rewarded with the promise that her child will not only be saved, but will have an exalted status as a messenger of God. It illustrates the theme that submitting to God's will, even in difficult circumstances, ultimately leads to the best result.
orig: وأوحينا إلى أم موسى أن أرضعيه فإذا خفت عليه فألقيه في اليم ولا تخافي ولا تحزني إنا رادوه إليك وجاعلوه من المرسلين

translation: And the family of Pharaoh picked him up [out of the river] so that he would become to them an enemy and a [cause of] grief. Indeed, Pharaoh and Haman and their soldiers were deliberate sinners.
interpretation: This verse suggests that the discovery of Moses by Pharaoh's family was not a coincidence, but rather a part of Allah's plan. Despite being raised in Pharaoh's household, Moses was destined to become an adversary to Pharaoh and his oppressive regime. The verse also emphasizes the sinful nature of Pharaoh, Haman, and their followers, implying that their actions were intentional and not merely misguided. This highlights the importance of recognizing and opposing tyranny and injustice, even when it comes from those in positions of power and authority.
orig: فالتقطه آل فرعون ليكون لهم عدوا وحزنا إن فرعون وهامان وجنودهما كانوا خاطئين

translation: And the wife of Pharaoh said, "[He will be] a comfort of the eye for me and for you. Do not kill him; perhaps he may benefit us, or we may adopt him as a son." And they perceived not.
interpretation: This verse shows the wisdom and compassion of Pharaoh's wife, who recognized the potential in the infant Moses and wanted to spare his life. She saw that he could be a source of joy and comfort for her and her husband, and even suggested adopting him as their own son. This highlights the value of seeing the good in others and giving them a chance, even if they come from a different background. It also demonstrates the power of maternal instinct and the ability of women to influence their husbands for the better. However, the verse ends with a note of irony, as Pharaoh's household was unaware of the future role Moses would play in challenging Pharaoh's tyranny and leading the Israelites to freedom.
orig: وقالت امرأت فرعون قرت عين لي ولك لا تقتلوه عسى أن ينفعنا أو نتخذه ولدا وهم لا يشعرون

translation: And the heart of Moses' mother became empty [of all else]. She was about to disclose [the matter concerning] him had We not bound fast her heart that she would be of the believers.
interpretation: This verse highlights the unwavering faith and trust in Allah that was instilled in the heart of Moses' mother. Despite the overwhelming fear and anxiety she felt when she had to cast her infant son into the river, Allah strengthened her heart and kept her composed, preventing her from revealing the truth about her son. This divine intervention allowed her to remain steadfast in her belief, trusting that Allah would protect and guide Moses according to His plan. The verse emphasizes the importance of having a strong connection with Allah and relying on Him during times of hardship and uncertainty.
orig: وأصبح فؤاد أم موسى فارغا إن كادت لتبدي به لولا أن ربطنا على قلبها لتكون من المؤمنين

translation: And she said to his sister, "Follow him." So she watched him from a distance, and they did not perceive.
interpretation: This verse is referring to the story of Prophet Moses (peace be upon him) when he was an infant. Moses' mother put him in a basket and placed it in the river Nile to protect him from being killed by Pharaoh's decree. She instructed her daughter, Moses' sister, to follow the basket and keep an eye on him from a distance without anyone noticing. This shows the wisdom, faith, and trust in Allah's plan that Moses' mother and sister possessed. It also demonstrates the importance of taking necessary precautions while relying on Allah's protection and guidance.
orig: وقالت لأخته قصيه فبصرت به عن جنب وهم لا يشعرون

translation: And We had prevented from him [all] wet nurses before, so she said, "Shall I direct you to a household that will be responsible for him for you while they are to him [for his upbringing] sincere?"
interpretation: This verse is referring to the story of Prophet Moses. When he was an infant, Allah prevented him from accepting any wet nurse other than his own mother. This was a divine plan to reunite Moses with his mother, who was hired by Pharaoh's wife to nurse him, unaware that she was actually his real mother. The verse highlights the sincerity and care with which Moses' mother and family raised him, despite the challenging circumstances. It shows Allah's power in orchestrating events and protecting His chosen servants, even in the most unlikely situations.
orig: وحرمنا عليه المراضع من قبل فقالت هل أدلكم على أهل بيت يكفلونه لكم وهم له ناصحون

translation: So We restored him to his mother that she might be content and not grieve and that she would know that the promise of Allah is true. But most of the people do not know.
interpretation: This verse highlights the mercy and wisdom of Allah in returning Prophet Moses to his mother after he was cast into the river. It shows that Allah's plan and promise will always come to pass, even if it seems unlikely or impossible to humans. The return of Moses to his mother was a source of comfort and reassurance for her, and a sign of Allah's power and control over all affairs. However, the verse also points out that most people do not recognize or appreciate the signs and promises of Allah, and lack faith in His wisdom and plan.
orig: فرددناه إلى أمه كي تقر عينها ولا تحزن ولتعلم أن وعد الله حق ولكن أكثرهم لا يعلمون

translation: And when he reached his maturity and became fully grown, We gave him wisdom and knowledge. And thus do We reward the doers of good.
interpretation: This verse is referring to Prophet Moses (peace be upon him) and how Allah blessed him with wisdom and knowledge when he reached the age of maturity. It emphasizes that Allah rewards those who do good deeds and live righteously by granting them knowledge, wisdom and understanding as they grow older. This divine favor is a result of their sincere faith, God-consciousness and virtuous actions in accordance with Allah's commands. The verse encourages believers to persist in doing good throughout their lives, with the assurance that Allah will bless them with the gifts of wisdom and insight as a reward for their righteousness.
orig: ولما بلغ أشده واستوى آتيناه حكما وعلما وكذلك نجزي المحسنين

translation: And he entered the city at a time of inattention by its people and found therein two men fighting: one from his faction and one from his enemy. And the one from his faction called for help to him against the one from his enemy, so Moses struck him and [unintentionally] killed him. [Moses] said, "This is from the work of Satan. Indeed, he is a manifest, misleading enemy."
interpretation: This verse sheds light on the human nature of prophets, as it portrays Moses in a moment of haste and unintended consequences. It demonstrates that even the most righteous individuals can make mistakes or act impulsively. However, what distinguishes them is their ability to recognize their errors, seek forgiveness, and learn from their experiences. The verse also highlights the deceptive nature of Satan, who seeks to mislead and incite discord among people. It serves as a reminder for believers to be mindful of their actions and to seek refuge in God from the influences of Satan.
orig: ودخل المدينة على حين غفلة من أهلها فوجد فيها رجلين يقتتلان هذا من شيعته وهذا من عدوه فاستغاثه الذي من شيعته على الذي من عدوه فوكزه موسى فقضى عليه قال هذا من عمل الشيطان إنه عدو مضل مبين

translation: He said, "My Lord, indeed I have wronged myself, so forgive me," and He forgave him. Indeed, He is the Forgiving, the Merciful.
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of recognizing one's mistakes, sincerely repenting, and seeking forgiveness from Allah. It emphasizes Allah's infinite mercy and forgiveness towards those who turn to Him in genuine repentance. The verse also serves as a reminder that no matter how great one's sins may be, Allah's forgiveness is greater, and He is always ready to forgive those who sincerely seek His pardon. This encourages believers to maintain a strong connection with Allah, constantly seek His forgiveness, and strive to improve themselves spiritually.
orig: قال رب إني ظلمت نفسي فاغفر لي فغفر له إنه هو الغفور الرحيم

translation: He said, "My Lord, for the favor You bestowed upon me, I will never be an assistant to the criminals."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of staying away from evil and wrongdoing, even if one has received blessings and favors from Allah. The speaker, believed to be Moses, acknowledges the blessings bestowed upon him by Allah and resolves never to support or assist those who engage in criminal or sinful activities. It highlights the principle that a believer should always strive to be on the side of righteousness and justice, regardless of their personal circumstances or the favors they have received. This interpretation underscores the Islamic values of integrity, moral uprightness, and the active rejection of evil and corruption in society.
orig: قال رب بما أنعمت علي فلن أكون ظهيرا للمجرمين

translation: And he became inside the city fearful and anticipating [exposure], when suddenly the one who sought his help the previous day cried out to him [once again]. Moses said to him, "Indeed, you are an evident, [persistent] deviator."
interpretation: This verse is a continuation of the story of Moses in Egypt. After killing an Egyptian, Moses became fearful of being exposed and punished for his actions. When the same Israelite who had sought his help the day before called out to him again, Moses rebuked him, recognizing that this man was a persistent troublemaker who would likely draw unwanted attention to Moses. This verse highlights Moses' realization that his actions had put him in a precarious position and that he needed to be cautious in his interactions with others to avoid further complications.
orig: فأصبح في المدينة خائفا يترقب فإذا الذي استنصره بالأمس يستصرخه قال له موسى إنك لغوي مبين

translation: And when he wanted to strike the one who was an enemy to both of them, he said, "O Moses, do you intend to kill me as you killed someone yesterday? You only want to be a tyrant in the land and do not want to be of the amenders."
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of justice and the dangers of abusing power. The person confronting Moses accuses him of wanting to be a tyrant by using violence to solve problems, rather than seeking to make peace and rectify the situation. It serves as a reminder that even those in positions of authority must be mindful of their actions and strive to be just and fair in their dealings with others. The verse emphasizes that true righteousness lies in working towards reconciliation and betterment of society, not in exerting force and control over others.
orig: فلما أن أراد أن يبطش بالذي هو عدو لهما قال يا موسى أتريد أن تقتلني كما قتلت نفسا بالأمس إن تريد إلا أن تكون جبارا في الأرض وما تريد أن تكون من المصلحين

translation: And there came a man running from the farthest end of the city. He said, "O Moses! Verily, the chiefs are taking counsel together about you, to kill you, so escape. Truly, I am one of your well-wishers."
interpretation: This verse is referring to an incident from the life of Prophet Moses. A man, who was a believer from the people of Pharaoh, came running from the far end of the city to warn Moses that the chiefs of Pharaoh's court were plotting to kill him. The man advised Moses to leave the city immediately in order to save his life. This demonstrates the believer's sincerity, courage and concern for the safety of Moses, despite the risk to his own life in going against Pharaoh. It also shows how God protects His prophets and righteous servants through various means, sometimes even through unexpected sources. The verse emphasizes the importance of well-wishing and helping others, especially those who are striving in God's cause, even in the face of danger and opposition.
orig: وجاء رجل من أقصى المدينة يسعى قال يا موسى إن الملأ يأتمرون بك ليقتلوك فاخرج إني لك من الناصحين

translation: So he left it, fearful and anticipating [apprehension]. He said, "My Lord, save me from the wrongdoing people."
interpretation: This verse is referring to Prophet Moses (peace be upon him) when he fled Egypt after accidentally killing an Egyptian. It shows his complete reliance and trust in Allah even in a state of fear and danger. Moses prays to Allah to protect him from the oppressors who would seek to harm him for his act, recognizing that only Allah can provide true safety and security. It demonstrates the importance of turning to Allah in times of hardship and having faith that He will answer the sincere supplications of the believers.
orig: فخرج منها خائفا يترقب قال رب نجني من القوم الظالمين

translation: And when he directed himself toward Madyan, he said, "Perhaps my Lord will guide me to the sound way."
interpretation: This verse is referring to Prophet Moses (peace be upon him) as he fled Egypt and headed towards the city of Madyan. Despite the uncertainty and challenges that lay ahead, Moses expressed his trust and reliance upon Allah to guide him on the right path. It demonstrates the importance of having faith and turning to Allah for guidance during difficult times or when facing major life decisions. The verse emphasizes that ultimately, it is Allah who can direct us to the most suitable way forward and help us navigate through the challenges we encounter on our journeys.
orig: ولما توجه تلقاء مدين قال عسى ربي أن يهديني سواء السبيل

translation: And when he came to the water of Madyan, he found there a crowd of people watering [their flocks], and he found aside from them two women driving back [their flocks]. He said, "What is your circumstance?" They said, "We do not water until the shepherds dispatch [their flocks]; and our father is an old man."
interpretation: This verse highlights the chivalry and kindness of Moses (peace be upon him) towards the two women who were unable to water their flocks due to the crowd of male shepherds. It also showcases the women's modesty and their respect for their elderly father. The verse emphasizes the importance of helping those in need and standing up against injustice or unfair treatment, even if it means going against societal norms. It teaches us to be proactive in assisting others, especially the vulnerable, and to do so with compassion and respect.
orig: ولما ورد ماء مدين وجد عليه أمة من الناس يسقون ووجد من دونهم امرأتين تذودان قال ما خطبكما قالتا لا نسقي حتى يصدر الرعاء وأبونا شيخ كبير

translation: So he watered [their flocks] for them; then he went back to the shade and said, "My Lord, indeed I am, for whatever good You would send down to me, in need."
interpretation: This verse is interpreted as a reminder of the importance of humility and reliance on God. Even after performing a good deed, such as helping others in need, one should not feel proud or self-sufficient. Instead, one should acknowledge that all blessings come from God and that we are always in need of His mercy and provision. The verse encourages believers to turn to God in supplication, recognizing their own limitations and dependence on Him for all good things in life.
orig: فسقى لهما ثم تولى إلى الظل فقال رب إني لما أنزلت إلي من خير فقير

translation: Then one of the two women came to him walking with shyness. She said, "Indeed, my father invites you that he may reward you for having watered for us." So when he came to him and related to him the story, he said, "Fear not. You have escaped from the wrongdoing people."
interpretation: This verse shows the importance of kindness and helping others, even if they are strangers. The two women were grateful for Moses' help in watering their flocks, and their father wanted to reward him for his good deed. It also demonstrates the virtue of hospitality and welcoming guests. Additionally, the verse highlights the idea of divine protection and refuge, as Moses was assured that he had escaped from the oppressive people who were pursuing him. This story encourages believers to have faith in God's plan and to trust that He will protect and guide them through difficult times.
orig: فجاءته إحداهما تمشي على استحياء قالت إن أبي يدعوك ليجزيك أجر ما سقيت لنا فلما جاءه وقص عليه القصص قال لا تخف نجوت من القوم الظالمين

translation: One of the women said, "O my father, hire him. Indeed, the best one you can hire is the strong and the trustworthy."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of hiring individuals based on their strength of character and trustworthiness, rather than other superficial qualities. The woman in the story recognizes that these traits are essential for a reliable and effective employee. This advice is applicable not only in business dealings but also in all aspects of life, as surrounding oneself with people of integrity and strength can lead to success and positive outcomes. The verse also highlights the wisdom and insight that can come from unexpected sources, as it is the daughter who offers this valuable advice to her father.
orig: قالت إحداهما يا أبت استأجره إن خير من استأجرت القوي الأمين

translation: He said, "Indeed, I wish to wed you one of these, my two daughters, on [the condition] that you serve me for eight years; but if you complete ten, it will be [as a favor] from you. And I do not wish to put you in difficulty. You will find me, if Allah wills, from among the righteous."
interpretation: This verse is about a marriage proposal made by Prophet Shu'aib to Prophet Moses. Shu'aib offers one of his two daughters in marriage to Moses on the condition that Moses serves him for eight years, with an option to extend it to ten years if Moses wishes. Shu'aib emphasizes that he does not want to burden Moses with this condition and assures him that he will find him to be among the righteous, Allah willing. This verse demonstrates the importance of setting clear terms and conditions in marriage contracts and the value of serving others as a means of earning trust and building relationships.
orig: قال إني أريد أن أنكحك إحدى ابنتي هاتين على أن تأجرني ثماني حجج فإن أتممت عشرا فمن عندك وما أريد أن أشق عليك ستجدني إن شاء الله من الصالحين

translation: He said, "That is between me and you. Whichever term I fulfill, there will be no injustice to me, and Allah, over what we say, is Witness."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of fulfilling contracts and agreements. It teaches that when two parties make an agreement, they should both honor their part of the deal. Whichever party fulfills their obligation, they will not be wronged or treated unjustly. The verse also reminds us that God is a witness over all our dealings and contracts. This should motivate the believers to be truthful and just in their interactions, knowing that God is watching and will hold them accountable. It promotes integrity, trustworthiness and the fulfillment of promises in interpersonal dealings.
orig: قال ذلك بيني وبينك أيما الأجلين قضيت فلا عدوان علي والله على ما نقول وكيل

translation: And when Moses had completed the term and was traveling with his family, he perceived from the direction of the mount a fire. He said to his family, "Stay here; indeed, I have perceived a fire. Perhaps I will bring you from there [some] information or burning wood from the fire that you may warm yourselves."
interpretation: This verse signifies a turning point in the life of Moses, as he embarks on a new journey after fulfilling his commitment. The fire he sees from afar symbolizes divine guidance and revelation that he is about to receive. Moses' concern for his family's well-being and his initiative to seek out the source of the fire demonstrate his leadership qualities and his readiness for the prophetic mission that awaits him. The verse also highlights the human need for warmth and comfort, both physical and spiritual, which God provides through His guidance and mercy.
orig: فلما قضى موسى الأجل وسار بأهله آنس من جانب الطور نارا قال لأهله امكثوا إني آنست نارا لعلي آتيكم منها بخبر أو جذوة من النار لعلكم تصطلون

translation: But when he came to it, he was called from the right side of the valley in a blessed spot - from the tree, "O Moses, indeed I am Allah, Lord of the worlds."
interpretation: This verse is describing the moment when Moses, upon arriving at the blessed spot in the valley, was directly addressed by Allah from the burning bush. This miraculous event marked the beginning of Moses' prophethood and his divine mission to free the Children of Israel from the tyranny of Pharaoh. The verse emphasizes the direct communication between Allah and Moses, establishing Moses' status as a chosen prophet and messenger of God. It also highlights the sacred nature of the location where this event took place, which is referred to as a "blessed spot" in the valley.
orig: فلما أتاها نودي من شاطئ الواد الأيمن في البقعة المباركة من الشجرة أن يا موسى إني أنا الله رب العالمين

translation: And [he was told], "Throw down your staff." But when he saw it writhing as if it were a snake, he turned in flight and did not return. [Allah said], "O Moses, approach and fear not. Indeed, you are of the secure.
interpretation: This verse is a powerful reminder of the importance of trusting in Allah's plan, even when faced with seemingly frightening or inexplicable circumstances. When Moses sees his staff transformed into a writhing serpent, his instinctive reaction is to flee in terror. However, Allah reassures him that he has nothing to fear, and that he is under divine protection. This teaches us that even when we are confronted with trials or challenges that shake our faith, we must remember to place our trust in Allah's wisdom and mercy. By approaching these difficulties with courage and submission to Allah's will, we can overcome our fears and emerge stronger in our faith.
orig: وأن ألق عصاك فلما رآها تهتز كأنها جان ولى مدبرا ولم يعقب يا موسى أقبل ولا تخف إنك من الآمنين

translation: Insert your hand into your bosom; it will come out white, without disease. And draw in your arm close to you [as prevention] from fear. Those are two proofs from your Lord to Pharaoh and his establishment. Indeed, they have been a people defiantly disobedient.
interpretation: This verse refers to the miracles given to Moses as signs of his prophethood when he was sent to Pharaoh. The first sign was that when Moses put his hand inside his cloak and brought it out, it shone with a bright light, symbolizing purity and divine guidance. The second sign was for Moses to draw his hand close to himself to dispel fear, symbolizing God's protection and reassurance. These miracles served as clear proofs from God to Pharaoh and his people of Moses' divine mission, despite them being a disobedient and rebellious nation that rejected the message.
orig: اسلك يدك في جيبك تخرج بيضاء من غير سوء واضمم إليك جناحك من الرهب فذانك برهانان من ربك إلى فرعون وملئه إنهم كانوا قوما فاسقين

translation: He said, "My Lord, indeed I have killed from among them a man, and I fear they will kill me."
interpretation: In this verse, Moses is expressing his fear and concern to Allah after he had accidentally killed an Egyptian man while trying to defend one of his own people. He is worried that the Egyptians will retaliate and kill him in return for this act. This verse highlights the human emotions and vulnerabilities of even great prophets like Moses, and shows how they turned to Allah for help and guidance during difficult times. It also emphasizes the gravity of taking a life, even unintentionally, and the consequences that can follow such actions.
orig: قال رب إني قتلت منهم نفسا فأخاف أن يقتلون

translation: And my brother Aaron is more eloquent than me in speech, so send him with me as a helper to support me. Indeed, I fear that they will deny me.
interpretation: In this verse, Moses is asking Allah to send his brother Aaron with him to confront Pharaoh and his people. Moses recognizes that Aaron is more eloquent in speech than he is, and thus would serve as a valuable support in conveying the message. This request highlights the importance of having a strong and reliable companion when facing a daunting task or challenge. It also shows the humility of Moses in acknowledging his own limitations and seeking help from others who may be better suited for certain aspects of the mission. The verse emphasizes the value of collaboration, mutual support, and the pooling of individual strengths to achieve a common goal in the face of adversity.
orig: وأخي هارون هو أفصح مني لسانا فأرسله معي ردءا يصدقني إني أخاف أن يكذبون

translation: He said, "We will strengthen your arm through your brother and grant you both authority so they will not reach you. By Our signs, you and those who follow you will be the predominant."
interpretation: This verse is a promise from Allah to Moses and his brother Aaron, assuring them of divine support and protection in their mission to confront Pharaoh and deliver the message of Allah. The verse emphasizes that with the help of Allah's signs and miracles, Moses, Aaron, and their followers will be victorious over their adversaries, despite the power and influence of Pharaoh and his people. This interpretation highlights the importance of trusting in Allah's plan and relying on His guidance and support, even in the face of seemingly insurmountable challenges.
orig: قال سنشد عضدك بأخيك ونجعل لكما سلطانا فلا يصلون إليكما بآياتنا أنتما ومن اتبعكما الغالبون

translation: But when Moses came to them with Our clear signs, they said, "This is nothing but invented magic, and we have not heard of this [religion] among our forefathers."
interpretation: This verse highlights the stubborn disbelief of the people to whom Moses was sent. Despite Moses presenting them with clear signs and miracles from God, they dismissed his message as mere magic and deception. They claimed that the message Moses brought was something new and unfamiliar, not practiced by their ancestors. This shows their attachment to the traditions and beliefs of their forefathers, even if it meant rejecting the truth. It demonstrates the difficulty prophets faced in conveying God's message to people who were deeply entrenched in their ways and resistant to change.
orig: فلما جاءهم موسى بآياتنا بينات قالوا ما هذا إلا سحر مفترى وما سمعنا بهذا في آبائنا الأولين

translation: And Moses said, "My Lord is most knowing of who has come with guidance from Him and to whom will be succession in the home. Indeed, wrongdoers do not succeed."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that ultimate knowledge and judgment belong to Allah alone. Moses, despite being a prophet, acknowledges that it is Allah who knows best who is truly guided and who will ultimately attain success in the eternal home of the Hereafter. The verse also underscores the fate of the wrongdoers and oppressors, stating that they will never achieve true success or prosperity, neither in this world nor in the next, because success is only for those who follow Allah's guidance and adhere to righteousness.
orig: وقال موسى ربي أعلم بمن جاء بالهدى من عنده ومن تكون له عاقبة الدار إنه لا يفلح الظالمون

translation: And Pharaoh said, "O eminent ones, I have not known you to have a god other than me. Then ignite for me, O Haman, [a fire] upon the clay and make for me a tower that I may look at the God of Moses. And indeed, I do think he is among the liars."
interpretation: This verse shows the arrogance and disbelief of Pharaoh, who claimed divinity for himself and denied the existence of the one true God. He ordered his minister Haman to build a high tower, possibly as a way to "reach" the God of Moses and prove Moses was lying. It demonstrates the depths of denial the disbelievers can sink to, refusing to acknowledge God even when confronted with clear signs and miracles from a prophet like Moses. The verse is a warning for people not to be misled by worldly power and their own egos into denying the truth of God's existence and sovereignty.
orig: وقال فرعون يا أيها الملأ ما علمت لكم من إله غيري فأوقد لي يا هامان على الطين فاجعل لي صرحا لعلي أطلع إلى إله موسى وإني لأظنه من الكاذبين

translation: And he and his soldiers were arrogant in the land without right, and they thought that they would not return to Us.
interpretation: This verse is referring to the arrogance and pride of a ruler and his army, who oppressed and tyrannized people on earth without any justification. They were deluded by their power and thought they would not be held accountable or returned to Allah for judgment in the Hereafter. It reflects the false sense of invincibility that tyrants often have, not realizing that ultimately everyone will face God and be called to account for their deeds, no matter how powerful they were in this worldly life. The verse condemns such arrogance and serves as a reminder that no one can escape divine justice.
orig: واستكبر هو وجنوده في الأرض بغير الحق وظنوا أنهم إلينا لا يرجعون

translation: So We seized him and his hosts, and We threw them into the sea. So see how was the end of the wrongdoers.
interpretation: This verse serves as a warning and reminder of the consequences of oppression and wrongdoing. It illustrates that no matter how powerful or influential a person may be, if they engage in unjust and tyrannical behavior, they will ultimately face the wrath of Allah. The fate of Pharaoh and his army, being cast into the sea, demonstrates that the punishment for those who transgress against Allah's laws and oppress others will be severe. It encourages believers to reflect upon the ultimate fate of the wrongdoers and to strive for justice and righteousness in their own lives.
orig: فأخذناه وجنوده فنبذناهم في اليم فانظر كيف كان عاقبة الظالمين

translation: And We made them leaders inviting to the Fire, and on the Day of Resurrection they will not be helped.
interpretation: This verse refers to those who lead others astray and invite them towards evil and the path to Hell. These leaders of misguidance and sin will face the consequences of their actions on the Day of Judgment, when they will be helpless and will not receive any support or assistance from anyone. It serves as a warning that those who misguide others and spread corruption will ultimately be held accountable by Allah for their deeds, and will have no escape or aid on the Day of Reckoning.
orig: وجعلناهم أئمة يدعون إلى النار ويوم القيامة لا ينصرون

translation: And We caused a curse to follow them in this world, and on the Day of Resurrection they will be among the despised.
interpretation: This verse highlights the consequences faced by those who reject faith and oppose the message of Allah. They are not only disgraced and humiliated in this worldly life, but their punishment extends to the Hereafter as well. On the Day of Judgment, they will find themselves among the despised and rejected, far removed from Allah's mercy. This interpretation emphasizes that one's actions and choices in this life have far-reaching implications, both in this world and the next, and that opposing divine guidance leads to a most wretched fate.
orig: وأتبعناهم في هذه الدنيا لعنة ويوم القيامة هم من المقبوحين

translation: And We had certainly given Moses the Scripture, after We had destroyed the former generations, as enlightenment for the people and guidance and mercy that they might be reminded.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance and purpose of divine revelation. The Scripture given to Moses, which is the Torah, was sent after the destruction of earlier generations who had rejected the truth. The Torah served as a source of enlightenment, guidance, and mercy for the people of Moses' time. It was meant to remind them of Allah's teachings, help them distinguish right from wrong, and guide them towards the path of righteousness. The verse implies that the Qur'an, revealed to Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him), serves a similar purpose for humanity - to enlighten, guide, and remind people of Allah's message, so that they may reflect upon it and follow the right path.
orig: ولقد آتينا موسى الكتاب من بعد ما أهلكنا القرون الأولى بصائر للناس وهدى ورحمة لعلهم يتذكرون

translation: And you were not on the western side when We decreed to Moses the command, and you were not among the witnesses.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Prophet Muhammad was not present at the time when Allah decreed His commandment to Prophet Moses on the western side of the Mount Sinai. It affirms that Muhammad did not witness the events of Moses' life and the revelation given to him directly. Rather, the knowledge Muhammad received about Moses came through divine revelation from Allah. This verse serves as a proof of Muhammad's prophethood, as he could not have known these details of Moses' life except through revelation from Allah.
orig: وما كنت بجانب الغربي إذ قضينا إلى موسى الأمر وما كنت من الشاهدين

translation: But We produced [many] generations [after Moses], and prolonged was their duration. And you were not a resident among the people of Madyan, reciting to them Our verses, but We were senders [of this message].
interpretation: This verse points to the fact that many generations passed between the time of Moses and the time of Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon them both. It also emphasizes that Prophet Muhammad was not present among the people of Madyan (Midian) to whom Prophet Shu'ayb was sent, reciting Allah's verses to them. Rather, it was Allah Who sent down the revelation to Prophet Muhammad, making him one of the messengers. This highlights the divine nature of the Qur'anic message and its continuity with the teachings of the previous prophets, despite the long passage of time and the Prophet's absence from the earlier nations.
orig: ولكنا أنشأنا قرونا فتطاول عليهم العمر وما كنت ثاويا في أهل مدين تتلو عليهم آياتنا ولكنا كنا مرسلين

translation: And you were not at the side of the mount when We called out, but [were sent] as a mercy from your Lord to warn a people to whom no warner had come before you that perhaps they will be reminded.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) was not present at Mount Sinai when Allah spoke to Moses directly. Instead, Muhammad's prophethood and message are a mercy from Allah to warn people who had not received a messenger before him. The verse suggests that by sending Muhammad as a prophet, Allah gives these people an opportunity to be reminded of the truth and to follow the right path, as they had no one to guide them previously. It highlights Muhammad's role as a messenger sent by Allah's mercy to guide and warn people, even though he was not a witness to the events at Mount Sinai.
orig: وما كنت بجانب الطور إذ نادينا ولكن رحمة من ربك لتنذر قوما ما أتاهم من نذير من قبلك لعلهم يتذكرون

translation: And if not that a disaster should strike them for what their hands put forth [of sins] and they would say, "Our Lord, why did You not send us a messenger so we could have followed Your verses and been among the believers?"
interpretation: This verse highlights the human tendency to seek guidance and a messenger from God only after facing the consequences of their own misdeeds. It suggests that people often blame God for not sending them a messenger to guide them, rather than taking responsibility for their own actions and seeking guidance proactively. The verse implies that God sends messengers and revelations as a mercy, but it is up to individuals to follow the guidance and become believers before calamity strikes them as a result of their sins.
orig: ولولا أن تصيبهم مصيبة بما قدمت أيديهم فيقولوا ربنا لولا أرسلت إلينا رسولا فنتبع آياتك ونكون من المؤمنين

translation: But when the truth came to them from Us, they said, "Why was he not given like that which was given to Moses?" Did they not disbelieve in that which was given to Moses before? They said, "[They are but] two works of magic supporting each other, and indeed we are, in both, disbelievers."
interpretation: This verse highlights the stubborn disbelief of those who rejected the message brought by Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him), despite recognizing its truth. They demanded that he be given miracles similar to those given to Prophet Moses, forgetting that they had already rejected Moses' miracles before. They accused both prophets of practicing magic and supporting each other's claims, declaring their disbelief in both. This shows their deep-rooted resistance to the truth and their willingness to find excuses to justify their disbelief, even when faced with clear signs and evidence from God.
orig: فلما جاءهم الحق من عندنا قالوا لولا أوتي مثل ما أوتي موسى أولم يكفروا بما أوتي موسى من قبل قالوا سحران تظاهرا وقالوا إنا بكل كافرون

translation: Say, "Then bring a scripture from Allah which is more guiding than either of them that I may follow it, if you should be truthful."
interpretation: This verse challenges those who reject the Qur'an and the previous scriptures to produce a book from Allah that is more guiding than them. It implies that the Qur'an is the most guiding book and that no one can produce something superior to it in terms of guidance. The demand to bring forth a better scripture is a way of proving the divine origin of the Qur'an and the truth of the Prophet Muhammad's message. It emphasizes that if the disbelievers are honest in their claims, they should be able to bring a more guiding book, which is an impossible task, thus establishing the superiority and authenticity of the Qur'an.
orig: قل فأتوا بكتاب من عند الله هو أهدى منهما أتبعه إن كنتم صادقين

translation: But if they do not respond to you, then know that they only follow their [own] desires. And who is more astray than one who follows his desire without guidance from Allah? Indeed, Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of following divine guidance rather than one's own desires or whims. It suggests that those who do not respond to the message of Islam are merely following their own misguided inclinations without any true guidance from Allah. The verse also asserts that Allah does not guide those who persist in wrongdoing and choose to follow their own desires instead of the truth. It highlights the dangers of being led astray by one's own ego and the necessity of submitting to Allah's guidance to stay on the right path.
orig: فإن لم يستجيبوا لك فاعلم أنما يتبعون أهواءهم ومن أضل ممن اتبع هواه بغير هدى من الله إن الله لا يهدي القوم الظالمين

translation: And We have certainly conveyed to them the Qur'an that they might be reminded.
interpretation: In this verse, Allah emphasizes that He has sent down the Qur'an to mankind as a reminder and a guidance. The phrase "conveyed to them" indicates that the message of the Qur'an has been clearly communicated and made accessible to all people. The purpose of this revelation is to encourage people to reflect upon its teachings, take heed of its warnings, and follow its guidance. The verse suggests that by pondering over the Qur'an and implementing its principles, one can attain a state of heightened awareness, consciousness, and remembrance of Allah. It serves as a call to humanity to be mindful of their actions and to live a life in accordance with the divine message.
orig: ولقد وصلنا لهم القول لعلهم يتذكرون

translation: Those to whom We have given the Book before it, they believe in it.
interpretation: This verse refers to the righteous among the People of the Book, namely the Jews and Christians, who recognized the truth of the Qur'an and the prophethood of Muhammad (peace be upon him) when they encountered his message. Despite the differences between their scriptures and the Qur'an, they were able to see the common thread of divine revelation and monotheism that runs through all of them. Their belief in the Qur'an is a testament to their sincerity and their willingness to follow the truth, even if it meant acknowledging the validity of a new prophet and a new scripture. This verse highlights the fact that the Qur'an is not a completely new or alien message, but rather a continuation and confirmation of the earlier revelations sent by God to humanity.
orig: الذين آتيناهم الكتاب من قبله هم به يؤمنون

translation: And when it is recited to them, they say, "We have believed in it; indeed, it is the truth from our Lord. Indeed, we were, [even] before it, Muslims [submitting to Allah].
interpretation: This verse speaks about the true believers who, when they hear the Qur'an being recited, immediately recognize it as the truth from their Lord. They declare their belief in it without any hesitation or doubt. The verse also emphasizes that these believers were already in a state of submission to Allah even before the revelation of the Qur'an. This indicates that their hearts were receptive to the truth and they were ready to accept the message of Islam. The verse highlights the importance of having an open and sincere heart that is ready to accept the truth when it comes from Allah, and the significance of recognizing and submitting to the truth without delay or hesitation.
orig: وإذا يتلى عليهم قالوا آمنا به إنه الحق من ربنا إنا كنا من قبله مسلمين

translation: Those will be given their reward twice for what they patiently endured and [because] they avert evil through good, and from what We have provided them they spend.
interpretation: This verse is referring to the righteous believers who will be rewarded twice for their patience and perseverance in the face of adversity. They respond to evil and harm with goodness and kindness, rather than retaliating in kind. They are also generous in spending from the provisions that Allah has granted them, giving in charity and helping others. Because of these noble qualities and actions, Allah will multiply their rewards and blessings in this life and the Hereafter.
orig: أولئك يؤتون أجرهم مرتين بما صبروا ويدرءون بالحسنة السيئة ومما رزقناهم ينفقون

translation: And when they hear ill speech, they turn away from it and say, "For us are our deeds, and for you are your deeds. Peace will be upon you; we seek not the ignorant."
interpretation: This verse encourages Muslims to avoid engaging with those who speak ill or ignorantly. It promotes the idea of focusing on one's own actions and deeds, rather than getting involved in fruitless arguments or debates with those who are not open to reason or understanding. The verse emphasizes the importance of maintaining peace and not seeking out or engaging with the ignorant or foolish. It teaches Muslims to be mindful of their own conduct and to strive for righteousness in their own lives, rather than being preoccupied with the misdeeds of others.
orig: وإذا سمعوا اللغو أعرضوا عنه وقالوا لنا أعمالنا ولكم أعمالكم سلام عليكم لا نبتغي الجاهلين

translation: Indeed, [O Muhammad], you do not guide whom you like, but Allah guides whom He wills. And He is most knowing of the [rightly] guided.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that guidance ultimately comes from Allah, not from any human being, even the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him). It is a reminder that the Prophet's role is to convey the message and invite people to the truth, but it is Allah who guides people's hearts to accept or reject that message. The verse also highlights Allah's omniscience, as He alone knows who will be guided and who will not. This understanding should instill humility in believers and prevent them from judging others based on their apparent faith or lack thereof, as the inner reality of a person's guidance is known only to Allah.
orig: إنك لا تهدي من أحببت ولكن الله يهدي من يشاء وهو أعلم بالمهتدين

translation: And they say, "If we were to follow the guidance with you, we would be swept from our land." Have we not established for them a safe sanctuary to which are brought the fruits of all things as provision from Us? But most of them do not know.
interpretation: This verse is addressing the excuses made by the disbelievers for not following the guidance brought by the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him). They claimed that if they were to accept Islam, they would be driven out of their land by their enemies. However, Allah reminds them that He has already provided them with a safe sanctuary in Mecca, where they are protected and to which fruits and provisions from all over are brought as a blessing from Him. Despite this, most of them fail to recognize and appreciate the favors and security that Allah has bestowed upon them. The interpretation highlights their ingratitude and the weakness of their arguments against following the truth.
orig: وقالوا إن نتبع الهدى معك نتخطف من أرضنا أولم نمكن لهم حرما آمنا يجبى إليه ثمرات كل شيء رزقا من لدنا ولكن أكثرهم لا يعلمون

translation: And how many a city did We destroy that was insolent in its [way of] living, and those are their dwellings which have not been inhabited after them except briefly. And it is We who were the inheritors.
interpretation: This verse is a reminder of the fate that befell previous nations who were ungrateful for Allah's blessings and indulged in a life of luxury and excess. Despite their power and wealth, Allah destroyed them for their arrogance and disobedience. Their once thriving cities and grand dwellings lay in ruins, uninhabited except for a short while. This serves as a warning that all power and dominion ultimately belong to Allah, and those who are ungrateful and rebellious will face a severe punishment. It is a call for humility, gratitude, and obedience to Allah's commands, lest we face a similar fate as those before us.
orig: وكم أهلكنا من قرية بطرت معيشتها فتلك مساكنهم لم تسكن من بعدهم إلا قليلا وكنا نحن الوارثين

translation: And never would your Lord destroy the cities until He sends to their mother a messenger reciting to them Our verses. And We would not destroy the cities except while their people were wrongdoers.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's justice and mercy. He does not destroy a people without first sending them a messenger to warn them and give them a chance to repent and follow the right path. The destruction only comes after they have persistently committed wrong and rejected the signs and guidance of Allah. It shows that Allah always gives people a fair opportunity to be guided before any punishment. At the same time, it establishes that when a nation becomes corrupt and oppressive, ignoring all warnings, then Allah's punishment becomes justified. The verse highlights the importance of heeding the messengers and revelations sent by Allah to reform ourselves.
orig: وما كان ربك مهلك القرى حتى يبعث في أمها رسولا يتلو عليهم آياتنا وما كنا مهلكي القرى إلا وأهلها ظالمون

translation: And whatever you have been given is but [for] enjoyment of the worldly life and its adornment. But what is with Allah is better and more lasting; so will you not use reason?
interpretation: This verse reminds us that all the material possessions and pleasures of this world are temporary and fleeting. They are merely for our enjoyment and adornment in this short worldly life. However, what Allah has prepared for the believers in the eternal life of the Hereafter is far superior and everlasting. The verse encourages us to use our intellect and reason to recognize the true value of our deeds and prioritize the eternal rewards of the Hereafter over the temporary delights of this world. It is a call to focus on our relationship with Allah and strive for His pleasure, rather than being distracted by the ephemeral nature of worldly possessions and desires.
orig: وما أوتيتم من شيء فمتاع الحياة الدنيا وزينتها وما عند الله خير وأبقى أفلا تعقلون

translation: Is he whom We have promised a good promise which he will obtain like he whom We provided enjoyment of worldly life [but] then he is, on the Day of Resurrection, among those presented [for punishment in Hell]?
interpretation: This verse highlights the stark contrast between those who believe in Allah's promise of Paradise and strive righteously in this life, versus those who are only concerned with the temporary pleasures of this world while neglecting the Hereafter. It emphasizes that the ultimate fate of these two groups will be vastly different on the Day of Judgment. The believers who trusted in Allah's good promise will attain eternal bliss, while those who were deceived by worldly enjoyments will face the severe consequences of their heedlessness and will be among those brought forth for punishment in Hell. This serves as a powerful reminder for mankind to prioritize their eternal fate over the fleeting delights of this life.
orig: أفمن وعدناه وعدا حسنا فهو لاقيه كمن متعناه متاع الحياة الدنيا ثم هو يوم القيامة من المحضرين

translation: And the Day He will call them and say, "Where are My 'partners' whom you used to claim?"
interpretation: This verse is a stern warning from Allah to those who associate partners with Him. On the Day of Judgment, Allah will confront the polytheists and demand to know where are the false gods they used to worship alongside Him. It is a rhetorical question, as these alleged partners will be nowhere to be found and unable to help their worshippers. The verse emphasizes the gravity of the sin of shirk (associating partners with Allah) and the severe consequences the polytheists will face for this grievous offense. It is a reminder that only Allah deserves worship and that relying on anyone or anything else is futile.
orig: ويوم يناديهم فيقول أين شركائي الذين كنتم تزعمون

translation: Those upon whom the word has come into effect will say, "Our Lord, these are the ones we led to error. We led them to error just as we were in error. We declare our disassociation [from them] to You. They did not used to worship us."
interpretation: This verse is referring to the leaders who misled others on the Day of Judgment. They will confess that they were the ones who led others astray, just as they themselves were astray. They will try to disassociate themselves from those they misled, declaring to Allah that these people did not truly worship them, but rather followed their misguidance. It shows that on the Day of Judgment, no one will be able to help another, and everyone will be held accountable for their own actions and beliefs. The leaders will not be able to bear the burden of those they misled.
orig: قال الذين حق عليهم القول ربنا هؤلاء الذين أغوينا أغويناهم كما غوينا تبرأنا إليك ما كانوا إيانا يعبدون

translation: And it will be said, "Call upon your 'partners' [whom you associated with Allah]." So they will call upon them, but they will not respond to them. And they will see the punishment; if only they had followed guidance!
interpretation: This verse highlights the helplessness and regret of those who associated partners with Allah on the Day of Judgment. When they are asked to call upon their false deities for help, they will realize that these "partners" cannot respond or provide any assistance. The polytheists will then face the severe punishment for their wrongdoings and will wish that they had followed the true guidance of Allah in their worldly lives. This interpretation emphasizes the importance of worshipping Allah alone and the consequences of associating partners with Him, as it will ultimately lead to disappointment and regret in the Hereafter.
orig: وقيل ادعوا شركاءكم فدعوهم فلم يستجيبوا لهم ورأوا العذاب لو أنهم كانوا يهتدون

translation: And [warn of] the Day when He will call them and say, "What did you answer the messengers?"
interpretation: This verse is a reminder of the Day of Judgment when Allah will question the people about their response to the messengers He sent to guide them. It emphasizes the importance of heeding the call of the prophets and following the guidance they brought from Allah. The verse implies that people will be held accountable for their actions and their acceptance or rejection of the divine message. It serves as a warning to those who ignore or oppose the teachings of the prophets, as they will have to answer for their choices on the Day of Reckoning. The verse also highlights the significance of the role of the messengers as conveyors of Allah's message and the gravity of the responsibility placed upon those who receive it.
orig: ويوم يناديهم فيقول ماذا أجبتم المرسلين

translation: That Day, the news will be obscured to them, so they will not ask one another.
interpretation: On the Day of Judgment, the disbelievers will be so overwhelmed and confused by the events unfolding before them that they will not even be able to ask one another about what is happening. This verse emphasizes the severity and shock of that Day, when all truths will be laid bare, and those who rejected faith will face the consequences of their choices. It serves as a reminder for people to reflect on their actions in this life and to strive for righteousness before it is too late.
orig: فعميت عليهم الأنباء يومئذ فهم لا يتساءلون

translation: But as for him who repents, believes, and does righteous deeds, it is expected that he will be among the successful.
interpretation: This verse conveys a message of hope and encouragement for those who have strayed from the right path. It suggests that no matter how far one may have gone astray, there is always a chance for redemption through sincere repentance, genuine faith, and righteous actions. By turning back to God, believing in His message, and doing good deeds, one can hope to attain success and salvation in this life and the hereafter. This interpretation highlights the merciful and forgiving nature of God, who is always ready to accept the repentance of His servants and guide them towards the path of righteousness.
orig: فأما من تاب وآمن وعمل صالحا فعسى أن يكون من المفلحين

translation: And your Lord creates what He wills and chooses; not for them was the choice. Exalted is Allah and high above what they associate with Him.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute power and authority of Allah in His creation and decision-making. It asserts that Allah alone has the right to create and choose as He wills, and that human beings have no say or choice in the matter. The verse also affirms the transcendence and uniqueness of Allah, declaring Him to be far above any partners or equals that people may associate with Him. This interpretation highlights the fundamental Islamic belief in the oneness and supremacy of Allah, and the importance of submitting to His will and wisdom.
orig: وربك يخلق ما يشاء ويختار ما كان لهم الخيرة سبحان الله وتعالى عما يشركون

translation: And your Lord knows what their breasts conceal and what they declare.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the omniscience of Allah, reminding us that He is fully aware of both the hidden thoughts and feelings within our hearts, as well as our outward actions and words. It serves as a powerful reminder to be mindful of our intentions and deeds, knowing that nothing escapes His knowledge. This consciousness of Allah's all-encompassing awareness should motivate us to purify our hearts, refine our character, and strive for sincerity in our worship and dealings with others.
orig: وربك يعلم ما تكن صدورهم وما يعلنون

translation: And He is Allah; there is no deity except Him. To Him is [due all] praise in the first [life] and the Hereafter. And His is the [final] decision, and to Him you will be returned.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the oneness and supremacy of Allah, stating that He alone is worthy of worship and praise. It highlights that all praise belongs to Him in this world and the next, indicating His eternal glory and perfection. The verse also affirms that Allah has the ultimate judgment and authority over all matters, and that all of humanity will return to Him in the Hereafter to face the consequences of their deeds. This interpretation underscores the importance of recognizing Allah's sovereignty and living one's life in accordance with His guidance, knowing that we will be held accountable for our actions in the afterlife.
orig: وهو الله لا إله إلا هو له الحمد في الأولى والآخرة وله الحكم وإليه ترجعون

translation: Say, "Have you considered: if Allah should make for you the night continuous until the Day of Resurrection, what deity other than Allah could bring you light? Then will you not hear?"
interpretation: This verse is a reminder of Allah's power and control over the universe. It asks the reader to consider a hypothetical situation where Allah makes the night perpetual until the Day of Judgment. In such a scenario, no other deity or power could bring light to dispel the darkness. The verse challenges the disbelievers to acknowledge that Allah alone has the ability to control the cycle of day and night and that no other being deserves to be worshipped besides Him. It also serves as an admonition to those who fail to recognize and appreciate Allah's signs and blessings, urging them to listen attentively to the message of the Qur'an and reflect upon its teachings.
orig: قل أرأيتم إن جعل الله عليكم الليل سرمدا إلى يوم القيامة من إله غير الله يأتيكم بضياء أفلا تسمعون

translation: Say, "Have you considered: if Allah should make for you the day continuous until the Day of Resurrection, what deity other than Allah could bring you a night in which you may rest? Then will you not see?"
interpretation: This verse is a reminder of Allah's power and control over the universe. It asks the reader to consider a hypothetical situation where Allah makes the day continuous until the Day of Judgment, without any night for rest. The verse emphasizes that no other deity besides Allah has the ability to bring forth night or change the natural order of things. It is a call to recognize Allah's sovereignty and to be grateful for the blessings of day and night, which are essential for our well-being and survival. The verse also implies that those who fail to acknowledge Allah's signs and worship others besides Him are spiritually blind and lack true insight.
orig: قل أرأيتم إن جعل الله عليكم النهار سرمدا إلى يوم القيامة من إله غير الله يأتيكم بليل تسكنون فيه أفلا تبصرون

translation: And out of His mercy He has made for you the night and the day, that you may rest therein and [by day] seek from His bounty, and [that] perhaps you will be grateful.
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine wisdom and mercy behind the alternation of night and day. The night is a time for rest and tranquility, allowing humans and other creatures to rejuvenate and recharge. The day, on the other hand, is a time for seeking sustenance and engaging in various activities. This natural cycle is a manifestation of Allah's mercy and a reminder for humans to be grateful for His blessings. It emphasizes the importance of striking a balance between work and rest, and encourages individuals to appreciate and make the most of the opportunities provided by both night and day. Ultimately, this verse prompts reflection on the perfection of Allah's creation and the countless blessings He bestows upon His creatures, inspiring gratitude and devotion towards Him.
orig: ومن رحمته جعل لكم الليل والنهار لتسكنوا فيه ولتبتغوا من فضله ولعلكم تشكرون

translation: And the Day He will call them and say, "Where are My 'partners' which you used to claim?"
interpretation: This verse is a stern warning to those who associate partners with Allah, reminding them that on the Day of Judgment, Allah will question them about their false claims of divinity for anyone or anything besides Him. It emphasizes the gravity of the sin of shirk (polytheism) and the accountability that awaits those who engage in it. The verse also highlights the fact that those false gods or idols will be of no help to their worshippers on that Day, exposing the futility of their beliefs and actions. It serves as a powerful reminder for believers to maintain pure monotheism and avoid ascribing partners to Allah in any form.
orig: ويوم يناديهم فيقول أين شركائي الذين كنتم تزعمون

translation: And We will draw forth from every nation a witness and say, "Produce your proof," and they will know that the truth belongs to Allah, and lost from them is that which they used to invent.
interpretation: This verse speaks about the Day of Judgment when Allah will call forth a witness from every nation to testify against their people. Allah will challenge the disbelievers to produce evidence for their false beliefs and actions, but they will realize that the ultimate truth belongs to Allah alone. They will recognize the falsehood of the lies and fabrications they used to associate with Allah, and these inventions will vanish, leaving them with no support or argument. This verse emphasizes the importance of faith in Allah and the consequences of rejecting the truth, especially on the Day of Judgment when all deeds will be laid bare, and the reality of Allah's sovereignty will be undeniable.
orig: ونزعنا من كل أمة شهيدا فقلنا هاتوا برهانكم فعلموا أن الحق لله وضل عنهم ما كانوا يفترون

translation: Indeed, Qarun was from the people of Moses, but he tyrannized them. And We gave him of treasures whose keys would burden a band of strong men; thereupon his people said to him, "Do not exult. Indeed, Allah does not like the exultant."
interpretation: This verse is a warning against arrogance and the love of wealth. Qarun was blessed with immense wealth, but instead of being grateful and using it for good, he became proud and oppressed his own people. His people advised him not to be arrogant, reminding him that Allah does not love those who are boastful and exultant over the blessings they have received. The verse emphasizes the importance of humility, gratitude, and using one's blessings in the way of Allah, rather than letting them lead to pride and transgression.
orig: إن قارون كان من قوم موسى فبغى عليهم وآتيناه من الكنوز ما إن مفاتحه لتنوء بالعصبة أولي القوة إذ قال له قومه لا تفرح إن الله لا يحب الفرحين

translation: And seek, through that which Allah has given you, the home of the Hereafter; and [yet], do not forget your share of the world. And do good as Allah has done good to you. And desire not corruption in the land. Indeed, Allah does not like corrupters.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of maintaining a balance between seeking the rewards of the Hereafter and enjoying the blessings of this worldly life. It encourages Muslims to use the bounties and provisions that Allah has bestowed upon them to seek His pleasure and the ultimate goal of attaining Paradise in the Hereafter. However, it also reminds them not to neglect their share of lawful enjoyment and benefits in this world.
