The verse urges Muslims to do good deeds and be kind to others, just as Allah has been kind and generous to them. It also warns against spreading corruption and mischief on earth, as Allah does not love those who cause disorder and harm in society. Overall, this verse promotes a balanced and moderate approach to life, where one strives for success in both this world and the Hereafter while maintaining righteousness and goodness.
orig: وابتغ فيما آتاك الله الدار الآخرة ولا تنس نصيبك من الدنيا وأحسن كما أحسن الله إليك ولا تبغ الفساد في الأرض إن الله لا يحب المفسدين

translation: He said, "I was only given it because of knowledge I have." Did he not know that Allah had destroyed before him of generations those who were greater than him in power and greater in accumulation [of wealth]? But the criminals, about their sins, will not be asked.
interpretation: This verse highlights the arrogance and ignorance of those who attribute their wealth and success solely to their own knowledge and abilities, while failing to acknowledge that everything is ultimately from Allah. It serves as a reminder that even the most powerful and wealthy individuals are not immune to Allah's punishment if they engage in sinful behavior. The verse also emphasizes that on the Day of Judgment, the criminals will not be asked about their sins, indicating that their guilt is already established and that they will face the consequences of their actions without any excuses or negotiations.
orig: قال إنما أوتيته على علم عندي أولم يعلم أن الله قد أهلك من قبله من القرون من هو أشد منه قوة وأكثر جمعا ولا يسأل عن ذنوبهم المجرمون

translation: So he went forth before his people in his adornment. Those who desired the worldly life said, "Oh, would that we had like what was given to Qarun. Indeed, he is one of great fortune."
interpretation: This verse is a commentary on the human tendency to be dazzled by worldly wealth and status. When Qarun went out amongst his people decked in his finery, those who were focused on the material world wished that they could have what he had, seeing his riches as the ultimate success. This highlights the short-sightedness of valuing ephemeral worldly gains over lasting spiritual wealth. It's a reminder to keep our priorities and perspective aligned with higher truths, rather than being seduced by fleeting glitter. True fortune lies not in accumulating worldly treasures, but in living righteously and nurturing the soul.
orig: فخرج على قومه في زينته قال الذين يريدون الحياة الدنيا يا ليت لنا مثل ما أوتي قارون إنه لذو حظ عظيم

translation: But those who had been given knowledge said, "Woe to you! The reward of Allah is better for he who believes and does righteousness. And none are granted it except the patient."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of faith and good deeds over worldly gains. Those who possess true knowledge and wisdom understand that the ultimate reward from Allah is far superior to any temporary benefits or pleasures in this life. They remind others that the path to this reward is through sincere belief and righteous actions, which require patience and perseverance. The verse also suggests that those who are patient in the face of challenges and temptations, while remaining steadfast in their faith, are the ones who will be granted the best reward from Allah in the Hereafter.
orig: وقال الذين أوتوا العلم ويلكم ثواب الله خير لمن آمن وعمل صالحا ولا يلقاها إلا الصابرون

translation: Then We caused the earth to swallow him and his home. And there was for him no company to aid him other than Allah, nor was he of those who [could] defend themselves.
interpretation: This verse is a warning to those who are arrogant and ungrateful for Allah's blessings. It refers to the story of Qarun, who was given great wealth by Allah but became proud and rebellious. As a punishment, Allah caused the earth to swallow him and his dwelling, showing that no matter how wealthy or powerful one may be in this world, it is nothing compared to the power of Allah. It also emphasizes that in the end, no one can help or defend us except Allah, and we should humble ourselves before Him and be grateful for His favors.
orig: فخسفنا به وبداره الأرض فما كان له من فئة ينصرونه من دون الله وما كان من المنتصرين

translation: And those who had wished for his position the previous day began to say, "Oh, how Allah extends provision to whom He wills of His servants and restricts it. If not that Allah had conferred favor on us, He would have caused the earth to swallow us. Oh, how the disbelievers do not succeed!"
interpretation: This verse highlights the fickleness of human nature and the tendency to envy others' good fortune. When people see someone prospering, they may wish to be in their place. However, when that person's fortune changes, those same people are quick to recognize that it is Allah who gives and takes away provision as He wills. They realize that if not for Allah's favor upon them, they too could have faced a similar fate. The verse also emphasizes that ultimately, the disbelievers who do not recognize Allah's power and mercy will not succeed in the end.
orig: وأصبح الذين تمنوا مكانه بالأمس يقولون ويكأن الله يبسط الرزق لمن يشاء من عباده ويقدر لولا أن من الله علينا لخسف بنا ويكأنه لا يفلح الكافرون

translation: That home of the Hereafter We assign to those who do not desire exaltedness upon the earth or corruption. And the [best] outcome is for the righteous.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the ultimate reward of the Hereafter is reserved for those who are humble, righteous, and do not seek to cause mischief or corruption on earth. It highlights the importance of living a life focused on pleasing Allah, rather than pursuing worldly power, status, or wealth at the expense of moral integrity. The verse also assures that the best outcome and success in both this life and the next belongs to those who are mindful of Allah and strive to live righteously.
orig: تلك الدار الآخرة نجعلها للذين لا يريدون علوا في الأرض ولا فسادا والعاقبة للمتقين

translation: Whoever comes [on the Day of Judgement] with a good deed will have better than it; and whoever comes with an evil deed - then those who did evil deeds will not be recompensed except [as much as] what they used to do.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the concept of divine justice and individual accountability on the Day of Judgment. Those who perform good deeds will be rewarded with something even better, highlighting God's generosity and mercy. On the other hand, those who engage in evil actions will face the consequences of their deeds, receiving a punishment commensurate with their actions. This interpretation underscores the importance of one's choices and actions in this life, as they will determine one's fate in the Hereafter. It encourages individuals to strive for righteousness and refrain from wrongdoing, knowing that God will judge everyone fairly based on their deeds.
orig: من جاء بالحسنة فله خير منها ومن جاء بالسيئة فلا يجزى الذين عملوا السيئات إلا ما كانوا يعملون

translation: Indeed, [O Muhammad], He who imposed upon you the Qur'an will take you back to a place of return. Say, "My Lord is most knowing of who brings guidance and who is in clear error."
interpretation: This verse assures Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) that Allah, Who has entrusted him with the Qur'an and its message, will surely bring him back to his place of return, meaning Makkah, after his migration to Madinah. It also emphasizes that Allah alone knows best who is rightly guided and who is in manifest error. The Prophet is instructed to put his trust in Allah's knowledge and wisdom, as He is the ultimate judge of people's faith and actions. This interpretation highlights the theme of divine providence and the assurance given to the Prophet during his challenging mission.
orig: إن الذي فرض عليك القرآن لرادك إلى معاد قل ربي أعلم من جاء بالهدى ومن هو في ضلال مبين

translation: And you were not expecting that the Book would be conveyed to you, but [it is] a mercy from your Lord. So do not be an assistant to the disbelievers.
interpretation: This verse highlights the unexpected and miraculous nature of the revelation of the Qur'an to Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him). It emphasizes that the revelation was not something he anticipated or sought, but rather a mercy and blessing from Allah. The verse also instructs the Prophet not to support or aid the disbelievers in their opposition to the message of Islam. This interpretation underscores the divine origin of the Qur'an and the Prophet's role as a recipient and conveyer of Allah's message, rather than someone who actively sought or invented it. It also stresses the importance of remaining steadfast in faith and not aligning with those who reject the truth.
orig: وما كنت ترجو أن يلقى إليك الكتاب إلا رحمة من ربك فلا تكونن ظهيرا للكافرين

translation: And let them not turn you away from the verses of Allah after they have been revealed to you. And invite [people] to your Lord and do not be of those who associate others with Allah.
interpretation: This verse is a reminder to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and to all believers to remain steadfast in their faith and not be swayed by the disbelievers who try to turn them away from the revelations of Allah. It emphasizes the importance of inviting others to the path of Allah and remaining monotheistic in one's belief, avoiding any form of shirk (associating partners with Allah). The verse encourages the believers to stay committed to their faith and to actively call others to the truth, even in the face of opposition or discouragement from those who reject the message of Islam.
orig: ولا يصدنك عن آيات الله بعد إذ أنزلت إليك وادع إلى ربك ولا تكونن من المشركين

translation: And do not invoke with Allah another deity. There is no deity except Him. Everything will be destroyed except His Face. His is the judgement, and to Him you will be returned.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the fundamental principle of Islam, which is the oneness of Allah (tawhid). It warns against associating partners with Allah or invoking any other deity besides Him. The verse also reminds us that everything in this world is temporary and will perish, except the Face of Allah, which represents His Eternal Essence. It affirms that Allah alone holds the ultimate judgement and that all of mankind will return to Him for accountability on the Day of Resurrection. This verse encourages believers to direct their worship, devotion, and reliance solely towards Allah, seeking His guidance and mercy, while recognizing the fleeting nature of worldly pursuits and the importance of preparing for the eternal life in the Hereafter.
orig: ولا تدع مع الله إلها آخر لا إله إلا هو كل شيء هالك إلا وجهه له الحكم وإليه ترجعون

translation: Alif, Lam, Meem.
interpretation: These disjointed letters are one of the miracles of the Qur'an, and none but Allah (Alone) knows their meanings. They may represent a challenge to those who doubt the divine origin of the Qur'an, as if to say that this book, composed of the same letters as those with which the Arabs were familiar, cannot be duplicated or imitated by human beings. Some scholars interpret these letters as symbolizing Allah's divine attributes or serving as an oath by which Allah swears to the veracity of His book. Ultimately, their true meaning remains known only to Allah.
orig: الم

translation: Do the people think that they will be left to say, "We believe" and they will not be tried?
interpretation: This verse suggests that true faith is not merely a verbal proclamation, but it must be tested and proven through trials and difficulties. It is not enough for people to simply say "We believe" without their faith being put to the test. God will examine the sincerity and strength of their faith through various challenges and hardships. This interpretation highlights that genuine belief requires patience, perseverance, and steadfastness in the face of adversity. It also implies that God will distinguish between those who have true faith and those who merely make a superficial claim of belief.
orig: أحسب الناس أن يتركوا أن يقولوا آمنا وهم لا يفتنون

translation: And We have already tested those before them, and Allah will surely make evident those who are truthful, and He will surely make evident the liars.
interpretation: This verse is a reminder that Allah has tested the people of the past, just as He tests people in the present. The purpose of these tests is to distinguish between those who are truthful in their faith and those who are merely paying lip service or are outright liars. Allah knows what is in the hearts of people and will make it clear who is sincere and who is not. This verse serves as a warning to be mindful of one's intentions and actions, as ultimately, the truth will be made manifest by Allah.
orig: ولقد فتنا الذين من قبلهم فليعلمن الله الذين صدقوا وليعلمن الكاذبين

translation: Or do those who commit evils think they can outrun Us? Evil is what they judge.
interpretation: This verse is a stern warning to those who engage in evil deeds and think they can escape God's justice. It suggests that no matter how clever or powerful they may think they are, they will never be able to outrun or outsmart God. The verse implies that such people have poor judgment and their thinking is flawed. It serves as a reminder that God is aware of all actions and will hold everyone accountable, so one should be mindful and strive to do good rather than evil.
orig: أم حسب الذين يعملون السيئات أن يسبقونا ساء ما يحكمون

translation: Whoever hopes for the meeting with Allah - indeed, the term decreed by Allah will come. And He is the Hearing, the Knowing.
interpretation: This verse reminds believers that the ultimate meeting with Allah is inevitable, and that everyone will face the consequences of their deeds on the Day of Judgment. It encourages people to live their lives with the consciousness that they will be held accountable for their actions and to strive for righteousness. The verse also emphasizes Allah's attributes of being All-Hearing and All-Knowing, which implies that He is aware of all our intentions, thoughts, and deeds, and will judge us accordingly. This should serve as a motivation for believers to lead a life pleasing to Allah and to always have hope in His mercy and forgiveness.
orig: من كان يرجو لقاء الله فإن أجل الله لآت وهو السميع العليم

translation: And whoever strives only strives for [the benefit of] himself. Indeed, Allah is free from need of the worlds.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the ultimate beneficiary of one's spiritual struggle and efforts is oneself. When a person strives to purify their soul, resist temptations, and follow the path of righteousness, they are ultimately doing so for their own spiritual growth and salvation. Allah, being self-sufficient and independent of His creation, does not gain or lose anything from an individual's actions. Therefore, the struggle for self-improvement and obedience to Allah is a personal journey that benefits the individual, while Allah remains free from any need or reliance on His creation.
orig: ومن جاهد فإنما يجاهد لنفسه إن الله لغني عن العالمين

translation: And those who believe and do righteous deeds, We will surely remove from them their misdeeds and will surely reward them according to the best of what they used to do.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of faith and good deeds in attaining salvation and reward from Allah. It assures the believers that if they have faith and do righteous acts, Allah will forgive their sins and reward them in the best possible manner for their good deeds. This interpretation highlights the mercy and justice of Allah, as He promises to not only forgive the sins of the believers but also to reward them abundantly for their righteousness. It serves as an encouragement for the believers to persist in their faith and good works, knowing that their efforts will not go in vain and that they will be recompensed with the highest reward from their Lord.
orig: والذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات لنكفرن عنهم سيئاتهم ولنجزينهم أحسن الذي كانوا يعملون

translation: And We have enjoined upon man goodness to parents. But if they endeavor to make you associate with Me that of which you have no knowledge, do not obey them. To Me is your return, and I will inform you about what you used to do.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of being kind and respectful to one's parents, as it is a commandment from Allah. However, it also sets a limit to this obedience - if one's parents try to persuade one to associate partners with Allah or worship others besides Him, then one should not obey them in that matter. The verse reminds us that ultimately, we will all return to Allah and He will inform us of our deeds, both good and bad. This highlights the importance of staying true to the path of Tawhid (oneness of Allah) and not letting anyone, even one's parents, lead us astray from worshipping Allah alone.
orig: ووصينا الإنسان بوالديه حسنا وإن جاهداك لتشرك بي ما ليس لك به علم فلا تطعهما إلي مرجعكم فأنبئكم بما كنتم تعملون

translation: And those who believe and do righteous deeds, We will surely admit them among the righteous [into Paradise].
interpretation: This verse promises that those who have faith in Allah and do good deeds will be granted entry into Paradise, where they will be in the company of the righteous. It emphasizes the importance of both belief and action in attaining salvation. The verse motivates believers to persist in their faith and good works, knowing that their ultimate reward is the eternal bliss of Paradise, where they will be united with the pious and the righteous. It also underscores Allah's mercy and justice in rewarding those who strive to follow His path.
orig: والذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات لندخلنهم في الصالحين

translation: And of the people are some who say, "We believe in Allah," but when one [of them] is harmed for [the cause of] Allah, they consider the trial of the people as [if it were] the punishment of Allah. But if victory comes from your Lord, they say, "Indeed, We were with you." Is not Allah most knowing of what is within the breasts of all creatures?
interpretation: This verse highlights the hypocrisy of some people who claim to believe in Allah, but their faith is superficial and weak. When faced with hardships or persecution for their belief, they equate the trials from people to the punishment from Allah, showing their lack of understanding and commitment. However, when victory and ease come, they quickly change their stance and claim to have always been with the believers. The verse emphasizes that Allah is fully aware of what lies within the hearts of all people, and He knows the true nature of their faith and intentions.
orig: ومن الناس من يقول آمنا بالله فإذا أوذي في الله جعل فتنة الناس كعذاب الله ولئن جاء نصر من ربك ليقولن إنا كنا معكم أوليس الله بأعلم بما في صدور العالمين

translation: And Allah will surely make evident those who believe, and He will surely make evident the hypocrites.
interpretation: This verse highlights that Allah has the ability to distinguish between true believers and hypocrites. It serves as a warning that one's inner beliefs and intentions cannot be hidden from Allah. The Almighty will make it clear who are the sincere believers, whose faith is reflected in their actions and words, and who are the hypocrites, those who outwardly profess belief but harbor disbelief and ill intentions in their hearts. This knowledge of Allah is perfect and all-encompassing, and on the Day of Judgment, the true nature of every individual will be laid bare before Him.
orig: وليعلمن الله الذين آمنوا وليعلمن المنافقين

translation: And those who disbelieve say to those who believe, "Follow our way, and we will carry your sins." But they will not carry anything of their sins. Indeed, they are liars.
interpretation: This verse is a warning against being misled by the false promises of the disbelievers. They try to entice the believers to abandon their faith by claiming that they will bear the burden of their sins. However, this is a deception, as no soul can bear the sins of another. Everyone is accountable for their own deeds. The disbelievers are lying when they make such claims, as they have no power to absolve anyone of their sins. This highlights the importance of remaining steadfast in faith and not being swayed by the temptations and false assurances of those who seek to lead believers astray.
orig: وقال الذين كفروا للذين آمنوا اتبعوا سبيلنا ولنحمل خطاياكم وما هم بحاملين من خطاياهم من شيء إنهم لكاذبون

translation: And they will surely carry their [own] burdens and [other] burdens along with their burdens, and they will surely be questioned on the Day of Resurrection about what they used to invent.
interpretation: This verse warns that those who invent lies and falsehoods about Allah and His religion will not only bear the burden of their own sins on the Day of Judgment, but they will also carry the additional burden of having misled others with their lies. They will be held accountable and questioned about the fabrications they used to spread in this world, facing the severe consequences of their actions in the Hereafter. It emphasizes the gravity of leading others astray through religious innovations and false teachings.
orig: وليحملن أثقالهم وأثقالا مع أثقالهم وليسألن يوم القيامة عما كانوا يفترون

translation: And We certainly sent Noah to his people, and he remained among them a thousand years minus fifty years, and the flood seized them while they were wrongdoers.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the patience and perseverance of Prophet Noah in his mission to guide his people to the right path. Despite preaching for an extremely long period of 950 years, his people remained obstinate and refused to believe in his message. As a result, they were ultimately punished by Allah through the great flood that drowned the wrongdoers. The verse also highlights the consequences of rejecting the truth and persisting in wrongdoing, as the people of Noah faced a severe punishment for their actions. It serves as a reminder for believers to remain steadfast in their faith and to continue inviting others to the path of righteousness, even in the face of adversity and rejection.
orig: ولقد أرسلنا نوحا إلى قومه فلبث فيهم ألف سنة إلا خمسين عاما فأخذهم الطوفان وهم ظالمون

translation: So We saved him and the companions of the ship, and We made it a sign for the worlds.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the power and mercy of Allah in saving Prophet Noah and his followers from the great flood that destroyed the disbelievers. The ark that Noah built under Allah's guidance became a symbol of salvation and a reminder for all generations to come. It serves as a sign of Allah's existence, His ability to protect the righteous, and the consequences of rejecting faith. The story of Noah's ark is meant to inspire believers to trust in Allah's plan and to warn disbelievers of the consequences of their actions.
orig: فأنجيناه وأصحاب السفينة وجعلناها آية للعالمين

translation: And [mention] when Abraham said to his people, "Worship Allah and fear Him. That is best for you, if you should know."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of worshipping Allah alone and being mindful of Him. Abraham, as a prophet and messenger, advises his people to direct their worship and devotion solely to Allah, the One True God. He reminds them that fearing Allah, which means being conscious of Him and avoiding disobedience to His commands, is in their best interest if they truly comprehend the significance of faith. This interpretation highlights the central message of Islam, which is the worship of Allah alone and the avoidance of all forms of idolatry or polytheism. It also underscores the role of prophets in guiding their communities towards the path of righteousness and the benefits of heeding their advice.
orig: وإبراهيم إذ قال لقومه اعبدوا الله واتقوه ذلكم خير لكم إن كنتم تعلمون

translation: You only worship idols besides Allah, and you produce falsehood. Indeed, those you worship besides Allah do not possess for you [the power of] provision. So seek from Allah provision and worship Him and be grateful to Him. To Him you will be returned.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the futility of worshipping false idols and deities other than Allah. It points out that these idols are mere fabrications and have no power to provide sustenance or fulfill the needs of their worshippers. Instead, one should turn to Allah alone, the true source of all provision, and worship Him with gratitude. The verse also reminds us of the inevitable return to Allah, highlighting the importance of staying on the right path and dedicating our worship exclusively to Him.
orig: إنما تعبدون من دون الله أوثانا وتخلقون إفكا إن الذين تعبدون من دون الله لا يملكون لكم رزقا فابتغوا عند الله الرزق واعبدوه واشكروا له إليه ترجعون

translation: And if you deny the truth, so did nations before you. And the Messenger's duty is only to convey the message clearly.
interpretation: This verse serves as a reminder that the Prophet Muhammad's role is to deliver the message of Islam clearly and faithfully, and that he is not responsible for whether people accept or reject it. It also points out that rejection of the truth is not a new phenomenon, as previous nations also denied the messages of their prophets. Ultimately, each individual is accountable for their own beliefs and actions, and the Prophet's duty is fulfilled by conveying the message, regardless of how it is received.
orig: وإن تكذبوا فقد كذب أمم من قبلكم وما على الرسول إلا البلاغ المبين

translation: Do they not see how Allah begins creation and then repeats it? Indeed that, for Allah, is easy.
interpretation: This verse is a reminder of Allah's power and ability to create and resurrect. It encourages people to reflect on the natural world around them and recognize the signs of Allah's creative power. Just as Allah originates the creation of all things, He is also fully capable of bringing them back to life after death. This should instill a sense of awe and recognition of Allah's greatness. It also emphasizes that for an All-Powerful God, resurrecting the dead is easy and effortless. The verse prompts introspection for deniers of resurrection to reconsider their views in light of the wonders of Allah's creation that they witness.
orig: أولم يروا كيف يبدئ الله الخلق ثم يعيده إن ذلك على الله يسير

translation: Say, "Travel through the land and observe how He began creation. Then Allah will produce the final creation. Indeed Allah, over all things, is competent."
interpretation: This verse invites people to reflect upon the signs of Allah's creation that are evident in the world around us. By pondering the intricate beauty and perfect design in nature, one can appreciate Allah's power and creative ability. The verse then points to the fact that just as Allah initiated the first creation, He is also fully capable of bringing about the next creation, i.e., the resurrection of the dead and the final judgment. This should inspire humans to be mindful of their ultimate accountability before their Creator, and to live righteously in preparation for the Hereafter. The verse emphasizes Allah's omnipotence and absolute control over all things, reassuring believers that He has the power to fulfill His promises and bring about the ultimate destiny that He has decreed for His creation.
orig: قل سيروا في الأرض فانظروا كيف بدأ الخلق ثم الله ينشئ النشأة الآخرة إن الله على كل شيء قدير

translation: He punishes whom He wills and shows mercy to whom He wills, and to Him you will be returned.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute power and authority of Allah over His creation. He alone has the right to punish or show mercy to whomever He chooses, based on His infinite wisdom and justice. It also reminds us that ultimately, all of humanity will return to Allah on the Day of Judgment to face the consequences of their actions in this world. This should inspire believers to strive for righteousness and seek Allah's mercy, while also serving as a warning to those who reject faith and persist in wrongdoing.
orig: يعذب من يشاء ويرحم من يشاء وإليه تقلبون

translation: And you cannot escape from Allah in the earth or in the heaven, and you have neither a protector nor a helper besides Allah.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute power and authority of Allah over all of His creation. It reminds us that no matter where we are, whether on earth or in the heavens, we cannot escape from His reach or evade His judgment. It also highlights our complete dependence on Allah, as we have no true protector or helper besides Him. This verse encourages believers to turn to Allah alone for support, guidance, and salvation, recognizing that He is the only One who can truly help us in both this life and the Hereafter.
orig: وما أنتم بمعجزين في الأرض ولا في السماء وما لكم من دون الله من ولي ولا نصير

translation: And those who disbelieved in the signs of Allah and in the meeting with Him, they have despaired of My mercy, and they will have a painful punishment.
interpretation: This verse warns those who reject the signs and evidence of Allah's existence and deny the Day of Judgment, that they have lost all hope of receiving Allah's mercy and forgiveness. As a result of their disbelief, they will face a severe and agonizing punishment in the Hereafter. It emphasizes the grave consequences of denying the truth and turning away from the path of righteousness, as it leads to eternal despair and suffering. The verse serves as a reminder for people to acknowledge Allah's signs, believe in the inevitability of the Day of Judgment, and strive for His mercy and grace through faith and good deeds.
orig: والذين كفروا بآيات الله ولقائه أولئك يئسوا من رحمتي وأولئك لهم عذاب أليم

translation: But the only answer of his people was that they said, "Kill him or burn him." But Allah saved him from the fire. Indeed in that are signs for a people who believe.
interpretation: This verse highlights the unwavering faith and trust in Allah exhibited by Prophet Ibrahim (Abraham) when faced with the threat of death by his own people. Despite their attempts to kill or burn him, Allah protected Ibrahim from harm, demonstrating His power and mercy towards those who believe in Him. This incident serves as a reminder for the believers to remain steadfast in their faith, even in the face of adversity, knowing that Allah will always protect and support those who sincerely believe in Him and follow His guidance.
orig: فما كان جواب قومه إلا أن قالوا اقتلوه أو حرقوه فأنجاه الله من النار إن في ذلك لآيات لقوم يؤمنون

translation: And he said, "You have only taken, other than Allah, idols as [a bond of] affection among you in worldly life; then on the Day of Resurrection you will deny one another and curse one another, and your refuge will be the Fire, and you will not have any helpers."
interpretation: This verse highlights the futility and deception of worshipping false idols and forming alliances based on worldly affections rather than faith in Allah. It warns that on the Day of Judgment, these superficial bonds will disintegrate, and those who followed false idols will turn against each other, denying and cursing one another. Their ultimate fate will be the Fire of Hell, and they will have no helpers or saviors. The verse emphasizes the importance of sincere faith in Allah and the consequences of deviating from the path of true worship.
orig: وقال إنما اتخذتم من دون الله أوثانا مودة بينكم في الحياة الدنيا ثم يوم القيامة يكفر بعضكم ببعض ويلعن بعضكم بعضا ومأواكم النار وما لكم من ناصرين

translation: And Lot believed him. [Abraham] said, "Indeed, I will emigrate to [the service of] my Lord. Indeed, He is the Exalted in Might, the Wise."
interpretation: This verse speaks about the unwavering faith and trust that Prophet Lot had in Prophet Abraham's message and mission. When Abraham declared his intention to leave his homeland and migrate to a place where he could freely worship Allah and spread His message, Lot believed in him and decided to join him on this journey. Abraham's statement, "Indeed, I will emigrate to [the service of] my Lord," demonstrates his complete submission and dedication to Allah, acknowledging that his migration is not just a physical journey but a spiritual one as well. He recognizes Allah as the Exalted in Might and the Wise, which implies that Abraham's decision to migrate is guided by divine wisdom and that Allah will support and protect him throughout his mission. This verse highlights the importance of having faith, following the footsteps of the prophets, and being willing to make sacrifices for the sake of one's belief in Allah.
orig: فآمن له لوط وقال إني مهاجر إلى ربي إنه هو العزيز الحكيم

translation: And We bestowed upon him Isaac and Jacob, and We placed prophethood and scripture among his descendants. And We gave him his reward in this world, and indeed, he is among the righteous in the Hereafter.
interpretation: This verse highlights the blessings and favors bestowed upon Prophet Abraham (peace be upon him) by Allah. Not only was he granted righteous sons in Isaac and Jacob, but prophethood and divine scriptures were also placed among his descendants, indicating a continuation of divine guidance through his lineage. Moreover, Allah rewarded Abraham in this worldly life, potentially through his reputation, influence, and the respect he earned from people. The verse also affirms that in the Hereafter, Abraham will be among the righteous who will be granted the highest ranks in Paradise due to his unwavering faith, sincerity, and dedication to Allah's cause. This verse serves as a reminder for believers to follow in the footsteps of Abraham, aspiring to be among the righteous both in this world and the next.
orig: ووهبنا له إسحاق ويعقوب وجعلنا في ذريته النبوة والكتاب وآتيناه أجره في الدنيا وإنه في الآخرة لمن الصالحين

translation: And [mention] Lot, when he said to his people, "Indeed, you commit such immorality as no one has preceded you with from among the worlds."
interpretation: This verse is a strong condemnation of the immoral acts practiced by the people of Lot, specifically referring to homosexuality. The verse emphasizes the gravity and uniqueness of their sins, stating that no other people before them had committed such acts. It serves as a reminder that engaging in such immorality is a severe transgression against the natural order established by Allah and a deviation from the righteous path. The mention of Lot's admonition to his people highlights the role of prophets in guiding their communities towards morality and righteousness, even in the face of strong opposition and rejection.
orig: ولوطا إذ قال لقومه إنكم لتأتون الفاحشة ما سبقكم بها من أحد من العالمين

translation: Do you indeed approach men and cut off the road and commit in your meetings [every] evil?' And the answer of his people was not but they said, 'Bring us the punishment of Allah, if you should be of the truthful.'
interpretation: This verse is a strong condemnation of the sinful acts committed by the people of Prophet Lut (Lot), peace be upon him. It highlights three major sins: homosexuality, highway robbery, and committing indecent acts in public gatherings. Despite Prophet Lut's warnings and advice, they arrogantly challenged him to bring Allah's punishment upon them if he was truthful in his claims. This defiant attitude reflects their deep state of denial, disbelief, and lack of fear of Allah's wrath. The verse serves as a reminder for all people to abstain from such immoral and unlawful practices, and to heed the warnings of Allah's messengers before it is too late.
orig: أئنكم لتأتون الرجال وتقطعون السبيل وتأتون في ناديكم المنكر فما كان جواب قومه إلا أن قالوا ائتنا بعذاب الله إن كنت من الصادقين

translation: He said, "My Lord, support me against the corrupting people."
interpretation: In this verse, the speaker is calling upon Allah for help and support against those who spread corruption and mischief on earth. It reflects the believer's reliance on Allah's aid in the face of evil and oppression. The verse emphasizes the importance of standing up against corruption and seeking divine assistance in this struggle. It also implies that the corrupting people are in opposition to the righteous and their actions are displeasing to Allah.
orig: قال رب انصرني على القوم المفسدين

translation: And when Our messengers came to Abraham with the good tidings, they said, "Indeed, we will destroy the people of that [i.e., Lot's] city. Indeed, its people have been wrongdoers."
interpretation: This verse is a reminder that Allah's punishment will befall those who persist in wrongdoing and transgression. The people of Lot's city were engaged in immoral and sinful acts, disregarding the warnings and guidance sent to them through Prophet Lot. As a result, Allah decreed their destruction as a consequence of their iniquity. This serves as a lesson for all people to abstain from evil deeds and to follow the righteous path, for Allah's judgment will ultimately prevail against the wrongdoers.
orig: ولما جاءت رسلنا إبراهيم بالبشرى قالوا إنا مهلكو أهل هذه القرية إن أهلها كانوا ظالمين

translation: He said, "Indeed, within it is Lot." They said, "We are more knowing of who is within it. We will surely save him and his family, except his wife. She is to be of those who remain behind."
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine protection and salvation that Allah grants to His righteous servants, even in the face of impending destruction. The angels, who were sent to destroy the sinful people of Lot, reassured Prophet Ibrahim that they were well aware of Lot's presence in the city and that they would save him and his family, except for his wife, who had chosen to remain with the disbelievers. This demonstrates that one's faith and righteousness are the determining factors in receiving Allah's mercy and protection, regardless of familial ties or societal pressures. It also emphasizes the importance of aligning oneself with the believers and distancing oneself from the actions and attitudes of the disobedient.
orig: قال إن فيها لوطا قالوا نحن أعلم بمن فيها لننجينه وأهله إلا امرأته كانت من الغابرين

translation: And when Our messengers came to Lot, he was distressed for them and felt for them great discomfort. They said, "Fear not, nor grieve. Indeed, we will save you and your family, except your wife; she is to be of those who remain behind."
interpretation: This verse highlights the mercy and protection of Allah towards His righteous servants. Despite the imminent destruction of the sinful people, Allah sends His angels to rescue Lot and his family, except for his wife who had aligned herself with the wrongdoers. It demonstrates that even in the face of adversity and danger, those who remain faithful to Allah will be saved and protected by His grace. The verse also emphasizes the importance of disassociating oneself from the sinful actions of others, as Lot's wife's fate was sealed due to her association with the wrongdoers, despite her husband's righteousness.
orig: ولما أن جاءت رسلنا لوطا سيء بهم وضاق بهم ذرعا وقالوا لا تخف ولا تحزن إنا منجوك وأهلك إلا امرأتك كانت من الغابرين

translation: Indeed, We will send down upon the people of this city a punishment from the sky because they have been defiantly disobedient.
interpretation: This verse is a warning from Allah to the people of a certain city who have persistently engaged in sinful and disobedient behavior. As a consequence of their actions, Allah declares that He will send down a severe punishment upon them from the sky. This punishment is a manifestation of Allah's justice and a reminder that no one can escape the consequences of their deeds. It serves as a wake-up call for the people to repent and mend their ways before it is too late. The verse also emphasizes the importance of obedience to Allah and the avoidance of sin, as it can lead to devastating consequences in this world and the hereafter.
orig: إنا منزلون على أهل هذه القرية رجزا من السماء بما كانوا يفسقون

translation: And We have certainly left of it a sign as clear evidence for a people who use reason.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah has left clear signs and evidence in His creation that point to His existence, power, and wisdom. These signs are meant for people who use their intellect and reasoning to reflect upon the world around them and draw conclusions about the Creator. The Qur'an encourages people to observe, ponder, and think deeply about the signs in nature, history, and within themselves to strengthen their faith and conviction in Allah's unity and supremacy. Those who sincerely use their God-given faculties of reason and understanding will be able to recognize and appreciate these signs, leading them to a firmer belief in Allah and submission to His will.
orig: ولقد تركنا منها آية بينة لقوم يعقلون

translation: And to [the people of] Madyan [We sent] their brother Shu'ayb, and he said, "O my people, worship Allah and expect the Last Day and do not commit abuse on the earth, spreading corruption."
interpretation: This verse is a reminder to the people of Madyan to worship Allah alone and to believe in the Day of Judgment. It also warns them against spreading corruption and mischief on earth. The verse emphasizes the importance of righteousness and the avoidance of evil deeds. It implies that those who engage in corruption and wrongdoing will face consequences in this world and the Hereafter. The mention of the "Last Day" serves as a motivation for people to lead a virtuous life and to be mindful of their actions, knowing that they will be held accountable before Allah.
orig: وإلى مدين أخاهم شعيبا فقال يا قوم اعبدوا الله وارجوا اليوم الآخر ولا تعثوا في الأرض مفسدين

translation: But they denied him, so the earthquake seized them, and they became within their home [corpses] fallen prone.
interpretation: This verse is a warning to those who reject the message of Allah and His prophets. It tells of a people who denied their prophet and were subsequently punished by Allah with a devastating earthquake that left them lying lifeless in their homes. The verse emphasizes the severity of Allah's punishment for those who reject His guidance and persist in disbelief. It serves as a reminder to all people to heed the call of the prophets and follow the straight path, lest they face a similar fate. The imagery of the people lying prone in their homes highlights the suddenness and totality of the divine retribution, underlining the power and authority of Allah over His creation.
orig: فكذبوه فأخذتهم الرجفة فأصبحوا في دارهم جاثمين

translation: And [We destroyed] 'Aad and Thamud, and it has become clear to you from their [ruined] dwellings. And Satan had made pleasing to them their deeds and averted them from the path, and they were endowed with perception.
interpretation: This verse is a reminder of the fate that befell the ancient tribes of 'Aad and Thamud, who were once powerful and prosperous but were ultimately destroyed by Allah due to their disobedience and rejection of His messengers. The ruins of their dwellings serve as a visible warning to humanity. The verse also highlights the deceptive role of Satan, who makes sinful actions appear attractive to people, leading them astray from the righteous path, even when they possess the ability to discern right from wrong. It emphasizes the importance of remaining vigilant against the temptations of Satan and staying steadfast on the path of guidance, lest one meets a fate similar to that of 'Aad and Thamud.
orig: وعادا وثمود وقد تبين لكم من مساكنهم وزين لهم الشيطان أعمالهم فصدهم عن السبيل وكانوا مستبصرين

translation: And [We destroyed] Qarun and Pharaoh and Haman. And Moses had already come to them with clear evidences, and they were arrogant in the land, but they were not outrunners [of Our punishment].
interpretation: This verse highlights the arrogance and disbelief of three prominent figures who opposed the message of Prophet Moses despite being presented with clear proofs and miracles. Qarun, Pharaoh, and Haman were all destroyed by Allah due to their persistent rejection of the truth and their oppressive behavior. The verse emphasizes that no matter how powerful or influential one may be in this world, they cannot escape Allah's punishment if they choose to rebel against His commands and oppress His servants. It serves as a reminder that ultimate success lies in humility, faith, and righteous deeds, not in worldly power and arrogance.
orig: وقارون وفرعون وهامان ولقد جاءهم موسى بالبينات فاستكبروا في الأرض وما كانوا سابقين

translation: So each [of them] We seized for his sin; and among them were those upon whom We sent a storm of stones, and among them were those who were seized by the blast [from the sky], and among them were those whom We caused the earth to swallow, and among them were those whom We drowned. And Allah would not have wronged them, but it was they who were wronging themselves.
interpretation: This verse highlights the various punishments that Allah inflicted upon past nations who disobeyed His messengers and persisted in their wrongdoings. These punishments were tailored to their specific sins and served as a reminder of Allah's power and justice. However, the verse emphasizes that Allah did not wrong them by sending these punishments; rather, they wronged themselves through their own actions and choices. This interpretation underscores the importance of personal responsibility and the consequences of one's deeds, as well as Allah's fairness in dealing with His creation.
orig: فكلا أخذنا بذنبه فمنهم من أرسلنا عليه حاصبا ومنهم من أخذته الصيحة ومنهم من خسفنا به الأرض ومنهم من أغرقنا وما كان الله ليظلمهم ولكن كانوا أنفسهم يظلمون

translation: The example of those who take allies other than Allah is like that of the spider who takes a home. And indeed, the weakest of homes is the home of the spider, if they only knew.
interpretation: This verse uses the metaphor of a spider's web to illustrate the futility and weakness of relying on anyone or anything other than Allah. Just as a spider's web is flimsy and easily destroyed, those who seek protection, support, or guidance from sources other than Allah will find their sense of security to be illusory and easily shattered. The verse emphasizes that true strength, stability, and protection can only be found by relying on Allah alone. It also suggests that those who ascribe partners to Allah or seek help from false idols are not acting with true knowledge or understanding of reality.
orig: مثل الذين اتخذوا من دون الله أولياء كمثل العنكبوت اتخذت بيتا وإن أوهن البيوت لبيت العنكبوت لو كانوا يعلمون

translation: Indeed, Allah knows whatever thing they invoke besides Him. And He is the Exalted in Might, the Wise.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah has complete knowledge of all the false deities and idols that people worship besides Him. It highlights the futility of invoking anyone or anything other than Allah, as He alone is worthy of worship. The verse also affirms two of Allah's attributes: Al-'Azeez (the Almighty, the All-Powerful) and Al-Hakeem (the All-Wise). It implies that Allah, with His might and wisdom, will deal with those who associate partners with Him or invoke others besides Him, and that He will judge them according to His perfect justice and knowledge.
orig: إن الله يعلم ما يدعون من دونه من شيء وهو العزيز الحكيم

translation: These are the parables We set forth for mankind; but none will understand them except the learned.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the Qur'an contains profound wisdom and knowledge in the form of parables and examples. However, it is only those who possess true knowledge, understanding, and spiritual insight who can grasp the deeper meanings and lessons behind these parables. The "learned" in this context refers to those who have purified their hearts, sought knowledge sincerely, and have been granted wisdom by Allah. They are able to look beyond the literal meanings and comprehend the divine wisdom contained within the Qur'an's verses. This highlights the importance of seeking knowledge, purifying one's intentions, and approaching the Qur'an with a humble and open heart in order to unlock its profound guidance and understanding.
orig: وتلك الأمثال نضربها للناس وما يعقلها إلا العالمون

translation: Allah created the heavens and the earth in truth. Indeed in that is a sign for the believers.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah's creation of the heavens and the earth is purposeful and meaningful, not random or in vain. The intricate design, balance and harmony in the universe is a clear sign and proof for those who believe in Allah's power, wisdom and oneness. Contemplating on the marvels of Allah's creation should strengthen one's faith and remind us that this world has a higher purpose. The universe is a manifestation of Allah's truth, and its very existence is a testament to the reality of the Creator.
orig: خلق الله السماوات والأرض بالحق إن في ذلك لآية للمؤمنين

translation: Recite, [O Muhammad], what has been revealed to you of the Book and establish prayer. Indeed, prayer prohibits immorality and wrongdoing, and the remembrance of Allah is greater. And Allah knows that which you do.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of reciting the Qur'an and establishing regular prayer. It suggests that the act of prayer helps prevent one from engaging in immoral and wrongful deeds, as it serves as a constant reminder of Allah's presence and guidance. Moreover, the verse asserts that remembering Allah is of even greater significance than the prayer itself, highlighting the centrality of Allah's remembrance in a believer's life. The final statement, "And Allah knows that which you do," is a powerful reminder that Allah is fully aware of all our actions, providing a strong incentive to lead a righteous life.
orig: اتل ما أوحي إليك من الكتاب وأقم الصلاة إن الصلاة تنهى عن الفحشاء والمنكر ولذكر الله أكبر والله يعلم ما تصنعون

translation: And do not argue with the People of the Book except in a way that is best, except for those who commit injustice among them, and say, "We believe in that which has been revealed to us and revealed to you. And our God and your God is one; and we are Muslims [in submission] to Him."
interpretation: This verse instructs Muslims to engage in respectful dialogue with the People of the Book (Jews and Christians), using the best manner possible. The only exception is when dealing with those who are unjust or hostile. The verse emphasizes the common ground between Muslims and the People of the Book, namely the belief in one God and the revelation sent down to their respective prophets. It encourages Muslims to affirm their faith while acknowledging the shared monotheistic roots with Jews and Christians, ultimately promoting peaceful coexistence and understanding between the religious communities.
orig: ولا تجادلوا أهل الكتاب إلا بالتي هي أحسن إلا الذين ظلموا منهم وقولوا آمنا بالذي أنزل إلينا وأنزل إليكم وإلهنا وإلهكم واحد ونحن له مسلمون

translation: And thus We have sent down to you the Book. Those to whom We have given the Book believe in it, and among these [people of Makkah] are those who believe in it. And none reject Our verses except the disbelievers.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the divine origin of the Qur'an and its similarity to previous scriptures. It asserts that those who have been given earlier revelations, such as the Jews and Christians, will recognize the truth of the Qur'an and believe in it. Additionally, even among the people of Makkah, there will be some who accept the message despite the general disbelief. The verse concludes by stating that only those who persist in disbelief will reject the clear signs and proofs of Allah's revelation.
orig: وكذلك أنزلنا إليك الكتاب فالذين آتيناهم الكتاب يؤمنون به ومن هؤلاء من يؤمن به وما يجحد بآياتنا إلا الكافرون

translation: And you did not recite before it any scripture, nor did you inscribe one with your right hand. Otherwise the falsifiers would have had [cause for] doubt.
interpretation: This verse is addressing the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him), asserting that he had no prior knowledge of any divine scripture before the revelation of the Qur'an, nor did he know how to read or write. If he had such knowledge or abilities, it would have given the doubters and disbelievers a reason to question the divine origin of the Qur'an and claim that Muhammad (peace be upon him) had authored it himself. However, his lack of prior knowledge and literacy serves as a proof that the Qur'an is indeed a revelation from Allah and not the work of a mere human being.
orig: وما كنت تتلو من قبله من كتاب ولا تخطه بيمينك إذا لارتاب المبطلون

translation: Rather, the Qur'an is distinct verses [preserved] within the breasts of those who have been given knowledge. And none reject Our verses except the wrongdoers.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the Qur'an is not just a written book, but its verses are firmly entrenched in the hearts and minds of those who have been blessed with divine knowledge. The true believers have internalized the message of the Qur'an, and it guides their thoughts and actions. However, those who are unjust and wrongdoers, due to their arrogance and stubbornness, reject the clear signs and verses of Allah, refusing to accept the truth despite its clarity. They choose to follow their own desires and ignore the guidance that Allah has provided through His revelations.
orig: بل هو آيات بينات في صدور الذين أوتوا العلم وما يجحد بآياتنا إلا الظالمون

translation: And they say, "Why are not signs sent down to him from his Lord?" Say, "The signs are only with Allah, and I am only a clear warner."
interpretation: This verse addresses the disbelievers who demand that the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) produce miracles as proof of his prophethood. Allah instructs the Prophet to respond by affirming that the power to produce miracles rests solely with Allah, and that his role is to serve as a clear warner, conveying the message of Islam and cautioning people about the consequences of rejecting faith. The verse emphasizes that the Prophet's duty is to deliver the message, while the ultimate decision to guide or misguide people belongs to Allah alone.
orig: وقالوا لولا أنزل عليه آيات من ربه قل إنما الآيات عند الله وإنما أنا نذير مبين

translation: Is it not sufficient for them that We have sent down to you the Book which is recited to them? Indeed, in that is a mercy and reminder for a people who believe.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the sufficiency and significance of the Qur'an as a divine revelation. It suggests that the Qur'an itself should serve as a clear proof and reminder for those who sincerely believe in its message. The revelation of the Qur'an is described as a mercy and a reminder, indicating that it is a source of guidance, compassion, and spiritual enlightenment for those who have faith. The verse implies that the Qur'an's presence and recitation should be enough to convince the believers of its divine origin and the truth of the Islamic message, without the need for additional signs or miracles.
orig: أولم يكفهم أنا أنزلنا عليك الكتاب يتلى عليهم إن في ذلك لرحمة وذكرى لقوم يؤمنون

translation: Say, "Sufficient is Allah as Witness between me and you. He knows what is in the heavens and earth. And those who have believed in falsehood and disbelieved in Allah - it is those who are the losers."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the sufficiency of Allah as a witness between the Prophet Muhammad and his opponents. It highlights that Allah has complete knowledge of everything in the heavens and the earth, and He is aware of the truth and falsehood. The verse also points out that those who believe in false deities and reject faith in Allah are the ultimate losers, as they have strayed from the path of truth and will face the consequences of their disbelief in the Hereafter. It serves as a reminder that true success lies in believing in Allah and following His guidance, while those who reject Him will ultimately be the losers, regardless of their worldly gains or status.
orig: قل كفى بالله بيني وبينكم شهيدا يعلم ما في السماوات والأرض والذين آمنوا بالباطل وكفروا بالله أولئك هم الخاسرون

translation: And they ask you to hasten the punishment for them. And if not for a specified term, the punishment would have come to them. But it will surely come to them suddenly while they do not perceive.
interpretation: This verse is a warning to the disbelievers who mockingly ask the Prophet to bring about the punishment they have been promised. Allah reassures the Prophet that the punishment will certainly come at the appointed time, decided by divine wisdom. The delay is not due to the punishment being unlikely to happen. Rather, when the time arrives, it will come suddenly, taking the disbelievers by surprise when they least expect it. This highlights the importance of being always mindful of Allah's punishment and not being deceived by the temporary respite given in this worldly life.
orig: ويستعجلونك بالعذاب ولولا أجل مسمى لجاءهم العذاب وليأتينهم بغتة وهم لا يشعرون

translation: They ask you to hasten the punishment, and indeed Hell will encompass the disbelievers.
interpretation: This verse is a warning to those who disbelieve in Allah and His messenger, and mock the idea of divine punishment. It emphasizes that Hell is real and will surely encompass those who reject faith, even if they demand to see the punishment hastened in this world. The verse implies that the disbelievers' arrogance and stubbornness will not change the reality of the Hereafter, where they will face the consequences of their actions. It serves as a reminder for believers to stay steadfast in their faith and for disbelievers to humble themselves and seek Allah's guidance before it is too late.
orig: يستعجلونك بالعذاب وإن جهنم لمحيطة بالكافرين

translation: The Day the punishment will cover them from above them and from below their feet and it is said, "Taste [the result of] what you used to do."
interpretation: This verse refers to the Day of Judgment when the disbelievers will be engulfed by the torment of Hell from all directions as a consequence of their evil deeds. It serves as a stern warning that everyone will face the repercussions of their actions in this world. The phrase "Taste [the result of] what you used to do" emphasizes that the punishment is a direct result of their own choices and misdeeds. It highlights the justice of Allah in recompensing people based on their deeds and the importance of being mindful of our actions in this life, as they will determine our fate in the Hereafter.
orig: يوم يغشاهم العذاب من فوقهم ومن تحت أرجلهم ويقول ذوقوا ما كنتم تعملون

translation: O My servants who have believed, indeed My earth is spacious, so worship only Me.
interpretation: This verse is a reminder from Allah to the believers that if they face persecution or difficulty in freely practicing their faith in one place, they should migrate to another land where they can worship Allah without hindrance. It emphasizes that the earth belongs to Allah and is vast, so believers should seek out a place where they can live and worship in peace, and fulfill their duty of worshipping Allah alone without associating partners with Him. This encourages believers to strive in the cause of their faith and make sacrifices when needed, knowing that Allah's earth is spacious and provides alternatives for them.
orig: يا عبادي الذين آمنوا إن أرضي واسعة فإياي فاعبدون

translation: Every soul will taste death, then to Us you will be returned.
interpretation: This verse reminds us of the inevitability of death and the ultimate return to Allah. It emphasizes that no matter who we are or what we achieve in this worldly life, we will all face death and be held accountable for our deeds in the presence of our Creator. The verse encourages believers to focus on leading a righteous life and preparing for the eternal life in the Hereafter, rather than being overly attached to the fleeting nature of this world. It also offers comfort in the face of loss, reminding us that death is not the end, but rather a transition to our final destination with Allah.
orig: كل نفس ذائقة الموت ثم إلينا ترجعون

translation: And those who believe and do righteous deeds, We will surely assign to them of Paradise [elevated] chambers beneath which rivers flow, wherein they abide eternally. Excellent is the reward of the [righteous] workers.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the great reward that awaits those who have faith and do good deeds. Allah promises to grant them lofty dwellings in Paradise, beneath which rivers flow, as an eternal abode. This signifies the elevated status and honor they will attain in the Hereafter. The mention of rivers flowing beneath their dwellings indicates the abundance of blessings, comfort, and tranquility they will enjoy. The verse concludes by affirming that this reward is the excellent compensation for those who work righteousness in this worldly life, seeking Allah's pleasure and striving in His cause. It motivates believers to persevere in faith and good deeds, knowing that their ultimate reward will be Paradise and its everlasting delights.
orig: والذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات لنبوئنهم من الجنة غرفا تجري من تحتها الأنهار خالدين فيها نعم أجر العاملين

translation: Those who are patient and upon their Lord they rely.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of patience and reliance on Allah. It suggests that those who remain steadfast in the face of challenges and difficulties, while putting their trust in Allah's plan and wisdom, will be rewarded. Patience and tawakkul (reliance on Allah) are key qualities of a believer, as they demonstrate faith and submission to the will of Allah. The verse encourages Muslims to cultivate these qualities in their lives, especially during times of hardship, knowing that Allah will support and guide those who trust in Him.
orig: الذين صبروا وعلى ربهم يتوكلون

translation: And how many a creature carries not its [own] provision. Allah provides for it and for you. And He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing.
interpretation: This verse reminds us that Allah is the ultimate provider for all His creation. Just as He provides for the countless creatures who do not have the means to carry their own provisions, He will also provide for us. We should trust in His wisdom and have faith that He will give us what we need, when we need it. The verse also emphasizes Allah's attributes of being All-Hearing and All-Knowing, implying that He is aware of our needs and circumstances, and will respond to our prayers and supplications.
orig: وكأين من دابة لا تحمل رزقها الله يرزقها وإياكم وهو السميع العليم

translation: And if you asked them, "Who created the heavens and the earth and subjected the sun and the moon?" they would surely say, "Allah." Then how are they deluded?
interpretation: This verse highlights the contradiction between the belief in Allah as the Creator and the actions of those who fail to worship Him alone. Despite acknowledging Allah as the Creator of the universe and the One who has subjected the sun and the moon for the benefit of mankind, they still deviate from the path of true monotheism. The verse implies that this delusion stems from their failure to grasp the logical conclusion of their own belief - that the One who created and controls the universe is the only One worthy of worship and obedience. It is a reminder for mankind to align their actions with their professed beliefs and to submit to the will of the Almighty Creator.
orig: ولئن سألتهم من خلق السماوات والأرض وسخر الشمس والقمر ليقولن الله فأنى يؤفكون

translation: Allah extends provision for whom He wills of His servants and restricts [it] for him. Indeed, Allah is, of all things, Knowing.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's complete control and knowledge over the sustenance and provisions He grants to His servants. He alone decides to whom He will give abundance and whom He will give less, according to His infinite wisdom. This serves as a reminder for humans to be content with what they have been given and to trust in Allah's plan, for He is the All-Knowing and His decisions are based on His perfect knowledge of what is best for each individual. It also encourages people to seek their provisions through lawful means and to rely on Allah's support, rather than being envious of others or resorting to unlawful ways of acquiring wealth.
orig: الله يبسط الرزق لمن يشاء من عباده ويقدر له إن الله بكل شيء عليم

translation: And if you asked them, "Who sends down rain from the sky and gives life thereby to the earth after its lifelessness?" they would surely say, "Allah." Say, "Praise to Allah"; but most of them do not reason.
interpretation: This verse points to the fact that even those who associate partners with Allah or deny Him altogether, when asked about the source of life-giving rain, would instinctively acknowledge that it is Allah who sends it down from the sky. This is because deep down, they recognize the power and magnificence of Allah's creation. However, the verse also highlights the contradiction in their thinking - despite recognizing Allah's hand in such a vital phenomenon, they fail to reason and conclude that Allah alone is worthy of worship. The command to say "Praise to Allah" emphasizes that all gratitude and praise belongs to Him for His countless blessings and mercies, even though most people fail to grasp this truth due to their lack of reasoning and reflection.
orig: ولئن سألتهم من نزل من السماء ماء فأحيا به الأرض من بعد موتها ليقولن الله قل الحمد لله بل أكثرهم لا يعقلون

translation: And this worldly life is not but diversion and amusement. And indeed, the home of the Hereafter - that is the [eternal] life, if only they knew.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the fleeting and ultimately insignificant nature of worldly life in comparison to the eternal life of the Hereafter. It suggests that people are often distracted by the temporary pleasures and amusements of this world, failing to recognize that true, everlasting life is found in the Hereafter. The verse implies that if people had knowledge and understanding of the reality of the Hereafter, they would prioritize their actions and decisions in this life accordingly, focusing on deeds that would benefit them in the eternal life to come rather than being consumed by the transient distractions of this world.
orig: وما هذه الحياة الدنيا إلا لهو ولعب وإن الدار الآخرة لهي الحيوان لو كانوا يعلمون

translation: And when they board a ship, they supplicate Allah, sincere to Him in religion. But when He delivers them to the land, at once they associate others with Him.
interpretation: This verse highlights the fickleness and ingratitude of human nature. In times of danger and distress, such as when aboard a ship in a storm, people turn to Allah with sincere devotion, recognizing His power and beseeching His aid. However, once the danger has passed and they are safe on land, they quickly forget Allah's grace and revert to their old ways of associating partners with Him. This demonstrates the weakness of human faith and the need for constant remembrance and gratitude towards Allah, both in times of hardship and ease. It serves as a reminder for believers to remain steadfast in their devotion and not to be like those who turn to Allah only when in need, but forget Him when they feel secure.
orig: فإذا ركبوا في الفلك دعوا الله مخلصين له الدين فلما نجاهم إلى البر إذا هم يشركون

translation: So that they will deny what We have granted them and they will enjoy themselves. But they are going to know.
interpretation: This verse is a warning to those who reject God's blessings and indulge in worldly pleasures without gratitude. It suggests that such people will eventually face the consequences of their ingratitude and disbelief. They will come to realize the truth and regret their actions, but it will be too late. The verse emphasizes the importance of acknowledging and appreciating the favors bestowed upon us by God, rather than taking them for granted or attributing them to our own abilities. It also implies that temporary enjoyment in this life should not distract us from our ultimate purpose and the inevitability of facing judgment in the Hereafter.
orig: ليكفروا بما آتيناهم وليتمتعوا فسوف يعلمون

translation: Have they not seen that We have made [Makkah] a safe sanctuary, while people are being taken away all around them? Then in falsehood do they believe, and in the favor of Allah they disbelieve?
interpretation: This verse highlights the contrast between the security and peace enjoyed by the people of Makkah, despite the fact that people in the surrounding areas are being attacked and taken away. It suggests that the Makkans should recognize this as a blessing from Allah and a sign of His favor upon them. However, instead of being grateful and believing in Allah, they choose to believe in falsehood and deny Allah's blessings. The verse serves as a reminder for people to acknowledge and appreciate the favors and protection bestowed upon them by Allah, rather than turning towards disbelief and ingratitude.
orig: أولم يروا أنا جعلنا حرما آمنا ويتخطف الناس من حولهم أفبالباطل يؤمنون وبنعمة الله يكفرون

translation: And who is more unjust than one who invents a lie about Allah or denies the truth when it has come to him? Is there not in Hell a residence for the disbelievers?
interpretation: This verse is a stern warning to those who fabricate lies against Allah or reject the truth of His message when it is presented to them. It emphasizes the gravity of these sins and the severe punishment that awaits those who commit them in the Hereafter. The rhetorical question "Is there not in Hell a residence for the disbelievers?" serves as a powerful reminder that Hell is the ultimate destination for those who persist in disbelief and denial of the truth. This verse encourages believers to hold fast to the truth, to be wary of falsehood, and to recognize the consequences of rejecting Allah's guidance.
orig: ومن أظلم ممن افترى على الله كذبا أو كذب بالحق لما جاءه أليس في جهنم مثوى للكافرين

translation: And those who strive in Our cause, We will surely guide them to Our ways. And indeed, Allah is with the doers of good.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that those who sincerely strive and make efforts in the way of Allah, seeking His pleasure and following His guidance, will be guided by Him to the straight path and the ways that lead to success and salvation. It highlights the importance of sincere dedication and perseverance in one's spiritual journey. The verse also affirms that Allah is with those who do good, supporting and helping them in their endeavors. It serves as an encouragement and reassurance for the believers to continue striving in Allah's cause, with the promise of His guidance and support.
orig: والذين جاهدوا فينا لنهدينهم سبلنا وإن الله لمع المحسنين

translation: Alif, Lam, Meem.
interpretation: These disjoined letters are one of the miracles of the Qur'an, and none but Allah (Alone) knows their meanings. They could be an indication of the inimitability of the Qur'an, challenging the Arabs, despite their linguistic mastery, to produce something similar. Some scholars suggest that these letters might be names or abbreviations referring to Allah's attributes or the theme of the surah. Ultimately, their true meaning remains known only to Allah, while we affirm our belief in the wisdom behind their presence in the Qur'an.
orig: الم

translation: The Byzantines have been defeated.
interpretation: This verse refers to the defeat of the Byzantine Empire at the hands of the Persians in the early 7th century. It is believed to have been revealed around the year 615 CE, at a time when the Persians had conquered much of the Byzantine territory. The verse is seen as a prophecy of the eventual Byzantine victory against the Persians, which would come to pass a few years later. The broader message is that the fortunes of nations and empires are in the hands of Allah, and that He has the power to grant victory or defeat as He wills. It also serves as a reminder to the believers to have faith in Allah's plan, even in the face of apparent setbacks or defeats.
orig: غلبت الروم

translation: In the nearer land, and they, after their defeat, will overcome.
interpretation: This verse is referring to the defeat of the Byzantines at the hands of the Persians in the nearer land, which is the region of Syria and Palestine. However, the verse also gives a prophecy that the Byzantines will soon be victorious against the Persians, within a period of a few years. This prophecy was fulfilled as the Byzantines defeated the Persians within the predicted timeframe. The verse is an indication of God's power and knowledge, as He is aware of future events and can reveal them in advance. It also serves as a consolation to the believers, that even if they face temporary setbacks or defeats, ultimately God's promise of victory for the believers will come to pass.
orig: في أدنى الأرض وهم من بعد غلبهم سيغلبون

translation: In a few years. The decision of the matter, before and after [these events] is only with Allah. And on that Day, the believers will rejoice.
interpretation: This verse refers to the ultimate victory and triumph that will be granted to the believers by Allah, even if it takes a few years. It emphasizes that the outcome of all affairs, both before and after any event, is determined solely by Allah's will and decree. The verse also highlights the joy and happiness that the believers will experience on the Day of Judgment when they witness Allah's support and the fulfillment of His promise. It serves as a reminder to the believers to remain patient, steadfast, and trust in Allah's plan, knowing that the final victory belongs to those who have faith in Him.
orig: في بضع سنين لله الأمر من قبل ومن بعد ويومئذ يفرح المؤمنون

translation: By Allah's help He helps whom He wills, and He is the All-Mighty, the Most Merciful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that victory and success come only through the help and support of Allah. He grants victory to whomever He chooses according to His wisdom and mercy. The mention of His attributes "Al-Aziz" (the All-Mighty) and "Ar-Rahim" (the Most Merciful) indicates that while Allah has the power to grant victory, He does so out of His mercy and compassion. It serves as a reminder for believers to seek Allah's assistance and rely upon Him, recognizing that any triumph is ultimately from Him alone.
orig: بنصر الله ينصر من يشاء وهو العزيز الرحيم

translation: The promise of Allah. Allah does not fail in His promise, but most of the people do not know.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute truthfulness and reliability of Allah's promises. It assures believers that whatever Allah has promised will certainly come to pass, as He never breaks His word. However, the verse also points out that most people lack this understanding and fail to grasp the certainty of Allah's promises. This lack of knowledge may lead them to doubt or despair, but the Qur'an reminds us that Allah's word is always true, regardless of people's ignorance or skepticism.
orig: وعد الله لا يخلف الله وعده ولكن أكثر الناس لا يعلمون

translation: They know what is apparent of the worldly life, but they, of the Hereafter, are unaware.
interpretation: This verse highlights the shortsightedness of those who are preoccupied with the superficial aspects of this worldly life, neglecting the eternal consequences of the Hereafter. It suggests that true wisdom lies in recognizing the fleeting nature of this world and focusing on the everlasting realm of the Hereafter. The verse implies that being consumed by worldly pursuits can lead to heedlessness and ignorance of the ultimate reality, which is the accountability and judgment in the afterlife. It serves as a reminder for believers to maintain a balanced perspective, fulfilling their responsibilities in this world while keeping sight of the greater purpose and destination that awaits them in the Hereafter.
orig: يعلمون ظاهرا من الحياة الدنيا وهم عن الآخرة هم غافلون

translation: Do they not contemplate within themselves? Allah has not created the heavens and the earth and what is between them except in truth and for a specified term. And indeed, many of the people, in [the matter of] the meeting with their Lord, are disbelievers.
interpretation: This verse is a call for introspection and reflection upon the creation of the universe. It suggests that if people truly contemplated the nature of the heavens and earth, they would realize that they were not created in vain or without purpose, but rather with truth and for a set period of time. The verse implies that this realization should lead one to acknowledge the inevitable meeting with their Lord (i.e., the Day of Judgment). However, it also points out that despite the signs in the creation, many people still disbelieve in the concept of being held accountable before God. Thus, the verse serves as a reminder for humans to reflect on the purpose of their existence and to prepare for the eventual return to their Creator.
orig: أولم يتفكروا في أنفسهم ما خلق الله السماوات والأرض وما بينهما إلا بالحق وأجل مسمى وإن كثيرا من الناس بلقاء ربهم لكافرون

translation: Have they not traveled through the land and observed how was the end of those before them? They were greater than them in power, and they plowed the earth and built it up more than they have built it up, and their messengers came to them with clear evidences. And Allah would not ever have wronged them, but they were wronging themselves.
interpretation: This verse is a reminder for people to reflect on the fate of previous nations who were mightier and more prosperous than them, yet they were destroyed because of their wrongdoings and rejection of the clear signs brought by their messengers. It emphasizes that Allah did not wrong them, but they wronged themselves through their actions and choices. The verse encourages people to learn from history and not repeat the same mistakes, as the consequences of disbelief and transgression are severe.
orig: أولم يسيروا في الأرض فينظروا كيف كان عاقبة الذين من قبلهم كانوا أشد منهم قوة وأثاروا الأرض وعمروها أكثر مما عمروها وجاءتهم رسلهم بالبينات فما كان الله ليظلمهم ولكن كانوا أنفسهم يظلمون

translation: Then the end of those who did evil was the worst [consequence] because they denied the signs of Allah and used to ridicule them.
interpretation: This verse warns that those who persist in evil deeds and reject Allah's signs and revelations will ultimately face the worst possible fate in the Hereafter. Their denial and mockery of the divine message will lead to their own ruin and loss. It emphasizes that ridiculing or disbelieving in Allah's signs is a grave sin that will incur severe punishment, as it reflects a complete disregard for the truth and a lack of faith. The verse serves as a reminder of the serious consequences of rejecting the guidance sent by Allah and encourages believers to stay steadfast in their faith.
orig: ثم كان عاقبة الذين أساءوا السوأى أن كذبوا بآيات الله وكانوا بها يستهزئون

translation: Allah begins creation; then He will repeat it; then to Him you will be returned.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the power and control of Allah over all of creation.
