It reminds us that Allah is the one who originates creation, and He will also be the one to bring it to an end and resurrect all beings. The verse also highlights our ultimate return to Allah, indicating that we will be accountable for our deeds in this life. It serves as a reminder of the temporary nature of this world and the importance of living in accordance with Allah's guidance, as we will all face judgment in the Hereafter.
orig: الله يبدأ الخلق ثم يعيده ثم إليه ترجعون

translation: And the Day the Hour appears the criminals will be in despair.
interpretation: This verse refers to the Day of Judgment when the Hour of Reckoning will be established. The criminals, those who rejected faith and committed sins, will be in a state of complete despair and hopelessness on that day. They will realize the gravity of their wrongdoings and the consequences they are about to face. The verse emphasizes the stark contrast between the believers who will rejoice in the reward of their good deeds, and the criminals who will be overwhelmed by the weight of their transgressions. It serves as a reminder for humans to be mindful of their actions in this world, for they will be held accountable in the Hereafter.
orig: ويوم تقوم الساعة يبلس المجرمون

translation: And those they associate with Allah will not intercede for them, and they will deny their association.
interpretation: This verse highlights the futility of worshipping false deities or associating partners with Allah. On the Day of Judgment, these false gods or idols will not be able to intercede or help their worshippers in any way. In fact, the worshippers will realize the falsehood of their beliefs and deny their association with these false deities. It emphasizes that only Allah has the power to intercede and that relying on anyone or anything else for salvation is a grave mistake that will lead to disappointment and regret in the Hereafter.
orig: ولم يكن لهم من شركائهم شفعاء وكانوا بشركائهم كافرين

translation: And the Day the Hour appears - that Day they will become separated.
interpretation: This verse refers to the Day of Judgment, when all of humanity will be resurrected and held accountable for their deeds. It emphasizes the stark contrast between the righteous and the wicked on that momentous day. While the believers will rejoice in the reward of Paradise, the disbelievers will face the consequences of their actions and be separated from the righteous, destined for punishment in Hell. This separation underscores the ultimate justice of Allah, as each individual will be recompensed according to their faith and deeds in this world. The verse serves as a powerful reminder for mankind to live righteously and prepare for the inevitable reckoning in the Hereafter.
orig: ويوم تقوم الساعة يومئذ يتفرقون

translation: As for those who believed and did righteous deeds, they will be in a garden [of Paradise], delighted.
interpretation: This verse speaks about the ultimate reward for those who have true faith and do good deeds in this worldly life. It emphasizes that their destination will be the gardens of Paradise, where they will experience joy, happiness, and delight as a result of their righteousness. This interpretation highlights the importance of having a strong belief in God and translating that faith into virtuous actions, as it is the key to attaining the eternal bliss of Paradise in the Hereafter.
orig: فأما الذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات فهم في روضة يحبرون

translation: And as for those who disbelieved and denied Our signs and the meeting of the Hereafter, they will be brought into the punishment [to remain].
interpretation: This verse is a stern warning to those who reject the truth of Islam and deny the signs and revelations of Allah. It emphasizes that those who disbelieve in Allah's messages and refuse to acknowledge the reality of the Day of Judgment will face severe consequences in the form of eternal punishment in the Hereafter. The verse highlights the gravity of disbelief and the importance of faith, reminding individuals that their actions and beliefs in this world will determine their fate in the afterlife. It serves as a powerful reminder for people to reflect upon their choices and to embrace the path of righteousness before it is too late.
orig: وأما الذين كفروا وكذبوا بآياتنا ولقاء الآخرة فأولئك في العذاب محضرون

translation: So exalted is Allah when you reach the evening and when you reach the morning.
interpretation: This verse is a reminder for believers to constantly glorify and praise Allah, acknowledging His perfection and supremacy at all times, particularly during the transitions between day and night. By mentioning these specific times, it emphasizes the importance of remembering Allah throughout the day and night, expressing gratitude for His blessings and seeking His guidance. This consistent remembrance and exaltation of Allah helps Muslims maintain a strong connection with their Creator and cultivates a sense of humility and submission to His will.
orig: فسبحان الله حين تمسون وحين تصبحون

translation: And to Him is [due all] praise throughout the heavens and the earth. And [exalted is He] at night and when you are at noon.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah deserves praise at all times and in all places, whether it is day or night, in the heavens or on the earth. It reminds us that we should constantly be grateful to Him and acknowledge His blessings and favors upon us. The specific mention of "at night and when you are at noon" highlights the importance of remembering and praising Allah during these times, which may represent moments when people are less likely to be mindful of Him due to sleep or preoccupation with worldly affairs. This verse encourages the believers to maintain a constant connection with their Lord through praise and gratitude.
orig: وله الحمد في السماوات والأرض وعشيا وحين تظهرون

translation: He brings forth the living from the dead and brings forth the dead from the living and gives life to the earth after its lifelessness. And thus will you be brought out.
interpretation: This verse speaks to the power and omnipotence of Allah. It highlights His ability to bring forth life from death and death from life, symbolizing His complete control over the cycle of existence. The giving of life to dead earth is a metaphor for resurrection, reminding us that just as Allah can revive the earth, He can also resurrect us after death for judgment. This verse serves as a powerful reminder of Allah's might and our ultimate return to Him, encouraging believers to be mindful of their actions in this temporary worldly life.
orig: يخرج الحي من الميت ويخرج الميت من الحي ويحيي الأرض بعد موتها وكذلك تخرجون

translation: And of His signs is that He created you from dust; then, suddenly you were human beings dispersing [throughout the earth].
interpretation: This verse points to the miraculous nature of human creation and the power of God. It reminds us that we were created from a humble beginning - dust - and yet God has fashioned us into complex, intelligent beings capable of spreading across the earth and building civilizations. This should inspire a sense of wonder at God's creative ability, as well as humility and gratitude for the gift of life. The verse also alludes to the concept of resurrection - just as God first created man from dust, He is able to bring us back to life after death for judgment. Reflecting on our origins and our ultimate destiny should motivate us to live righteously and be mindful of God in our earthly lives.
orig: ومن آياته أن خلقكم من تراب ثم إذا أنتم بشر تنتشرون

translation: And of His signs is that He created for you from yourselves mates that you may find tranquillity in them; and He placed between you affection and mercy. Indeed in that are signs for a people who give thought.
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine wisdom behind the creation of spouses and the institution of marriage. It suggests that the purpose of marriage is not merely physical or sexual, but rather to provide a source of emotional and spiritual comfort, tranquillity, and companionship. The mention of "affection and mercy" between spouses indicates that a successful marriage is built on a foundation of love, compassion, understanding, and mutual support. The verse also invites people to reflect upon and appreciate the signs of Allah's creation and the profound psychological and social benefits of the spousal relationship.
orig: ومن آياته أن خلق لكم من أنفسكم أزواجا لتسكنوا إليها وجعل بينكم مودة ورحمة إن في ذلك لآيات لقوم يتفكرون

translation: And of His signs is the creation of the heavens and the earth, and the diversity of your languages and your colors. Indeed in that are signs for those of knowledge.
interpretation: This verse highlights the immense power and creativity of Allah, as evidenced by the vast and complex creation of the universe. It also points to the diversity of humanity, with our different languages and skin colors, as a further sign of Allah's wisdom and purposeful design. The fact that we are so varied and yet all part of the same human family is a testament to the unity and oneness of our Creator. Those who reflect deeply on these signs with knowledge and insight will recognize them as clear proofs of Allah's existence and attributes.
orig: ومن آياته خلق السماوات والأرض واختلاف ألسنتكم وألوانكم إن في ذلك لآيات للعالمين

translation: And of His signs is your sleep by night and day and your seeking of His bounty. Indeed in that are signs for a people who listen.
interpretation: This verse highlights the power and mercy of Allah. It reminds us that even the natural cycle of sleep and wakefulness, which we often take for granted, is a sign of Allah's perfect design. Our ability to rest and rejuvenate at night, and then seek sustenance and strive during the day, is a blessing from Him. The verse also emphasizes the importance of being attentive and listening to these signs with understanding. Those who reflect deeply will recognize in these patterns the undeniable proofs of Allah's existence, wisdom, and benevolence. They will be filled with gratitude for His provisions and be motivated to use their time and abilities in a way that pleases Him.
orig: ومن آياته منامكم بالليل والنهار وابتغاؤكم من فضله إن في ذلك لآيات لقوم يسمعون

translation: And of His signs is that He shows you the lightning, for fear and for hope, and He sends down rain from the sky and by it gives life to the earth after its lifelessness. Indeed in that are signs for a people who use reason.
interpretation: This verse highlights the power and mercy of Allah. The lightning that we see is both frightening and awe-inspiring, reminding us of Allah's might. At the same time, lightning is often followed by rain, which is a source of hope and life, as it revives the dead earth. This cycle of life and death in nature is one of the signs of Allah's existence and wisdom, but only those who reflect and use their intellect can truly appreciate these signs. The verse encourages us to ponder upon the marvels of Allah's creation and recognize Him through His signs.
orig: ومن آياته يريكم البرق خوفا وطمعا وينزل من السماء ماء فيحيي به الأرض بعد موتها إن في ذلك لآيات لقوم يعقلون

translation: And among His signs is that the heaven and earth remain by His command. Then when He calls you with a [single] call from the earth, immediately you will come forth.
interpretation: This verse points to the omnipotence and absolute authority of Allah over the entire universe. The heavens and the earth, despite their vastness and might, are maintained in their places and functioning according to Allah's decree. It also alludes to the Day of Resurrection when Allah will command the dead to rise from their graves and they will immediately come back to life and emerge from the earth. This demonstrates Allah's power to resurrect the dead and hold people accountable for their deeds, emphasizing the inevitability of the Hereafter. The verse encourages believers to recognize and marvel at Allah's signs in the creation and to be mindful of the Day of Judgment.
orig: ومن آياته أن تقوم السماء والأرض بأمره ثم إذا دعاكم دعوة من الأرض إذا أنتم تخرجون

translation: To Him belongs whoever is in the heavens and the earth. All are devoutly obedient to Him.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute sovereignty and dominion of Allah over all of His creation. It states that every being in the heavens and the earth, whether angels, humans, jinn, or any other creature, belongs to Him alone. They are all under His complete control and authority. The word "qaanitoon" (قانتون) suggests that all these beings are devoutly obedient and submissive to Allah, willingly or unwillingly. It highlights the idea that no one can escape or defy Allah's power and that all are ultimately subject to His will and decree. This reinforces the Islamic belief in the oneness and supremacy of Allah as the sole Creator, Sustainer, and Master of the universe.
orig: وله من في السماوات والأرض كل له قانتون

translation: And it is He who begins creation; then He repeats it, and that is [even] easier for Him. To Him belongs the highest attribute in the heavens and earth. And He is the Exalted in Might, the Wise.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's power and ability to create and recreate with ease. It affirms that Allah alone possesses the most sublime attributes in all of creation. The repetition of creation refers to Allah's ability to resurrect the dead on the Day of Judgment, which is easier for Him than the initial creation. The verse also highlights two of Allah's names and attributes: Al-'Azeez (the Almighty) and Al-Hakeem (the All-Wise), indicating His ultimate power, wisdom, and control over all things in the heavens and the earth.
orig: وهو الذي يبدأ الخلق ثم يعيده وهو أهون عليه وله المثل الأعلى في السماوات والأرض وهو العزيز الحكيم

translation: He sets forth to you a parable from your ownselves: Do you have partners among those whom your right hands possess (i.e. your slaves) to share as equals in the wealth We have bestowed on you? Whom you fear as you fear each other? Thus do We explain the signs in detail to a people who have sense.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the concept of Tawheed (oneness of Allah) by presenting a logical argument. It asks the question: if you do not accept your slaves as partners in your wealth, then how can you accept others as partners with Allah in His creation and sovereignty? Just as you fear your partners in wealth, you should fear Allah alone. This analogy is meant to make people reflect on the illogical nature of shirk (associating partners with Allah) and encourage them to embrace the oneness of Allah wholeheartedly. The verse also highlights that Allah explains His signs in detail for people who use their intellect and reasoning to understand the truth.
orig: ضرب لكم مثلا من أنفسكم هل لكم من ما ملكت أيمانكم من شركاء في ما رزقناكم فأنتم فيه سواء تخافونهم كخيفتكم أنفسكم كذلك نفصل الآيات لقوم يعقلون

translation: But those who do wrong follow their own desires without knowledge. Then who can guide those whom Allah has sent astray? And for them there are no helpers.
interpretation: This verse highlights the consequences of following one's desires and whims without the guidance of divine knowledge. Those who engage in wrongdoing and ignore the truth are led astray by their own desires, and as a result, they lose Allah's guidance. Once Allah has decreed someone to be misguided due to their own actions, no one can guide them back to the right path. They will find no helpers or supporters to save them from the consequences of their misguidance. This emphasizes the importance of seeking knowledge and adhering to divine guidance to avoid being led astray by one's own desires.
orig: بل اتبع الذين ظلموا أهواءهم بغير علم فمن يهدي من أضل الله وما لهم من ناصرين

translation: So direct your face toward the religion, inclining to truth. [Adhere to] the fitrah of Allah upon which He has created [all] people. No change should there be in the creation of Allah. That is the correct religion, but most of the people do not know.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of adhering to the innate, natural disposition (fitrah) that Allah has instilled within all human beings. It suggests that the true religion is in alignment with this fitrah, and that one should remain steadfast on this path. The verse also points out that most people are unaware of this truth, implying the need for guidance and the importance of seeking knowledge to understand and follow the correct religion. It highlights the immutable nature of Allah's creation and the unchanging essence of the true faith.
orig: فأقم وجهك للدين حنيفا فطرت الله التي فطر الناس عليها لا تبديل لخلق الله ذلك الدين القيم ولكن أكثر الناس لا يعلمون

translation: Turning in repentance to Him, and fear Him and establish prayer and do not be of those who associate others with Allah
interpretation: This verse calls upon believers to turn to Allah in sincere repentance, to have consciousness and fear of Him, to establish the obligatory prayers, and to avoid falling into the grave sin of shirk (associating partners with Allah in worship). It emphasizes the importance of maintaining a strong connection with Allah through repentance, righteousness, and upholding the pillars of faith such as prayer. The verse also warns against the danger of committing shirk, which is considered the greatest sin in Islam, as it goes against the fundamental belief in the oneness and uniqueness of Allah.
orig: منيبين إليه واتقوه وأقيموا الصلاة ولا تكونوا من المشركين

translation: Of those who have divided their religion and become sects, every faction rejoicing in what it has.
interpretation: This verse is referring to those who have caused divisions and splits within the religion of Islam, forming into various sects and factions. Each of these groups is pleased and content with their own beliefs and practices, thinking that they alone are on the right path. However, this sectarianism and division is condemned in Islam, which calls for unity among the believers based on the core principles and teachings of the faith as revealed in the Qur'an and taught by the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him). The verse implies that such division and factionism stems from people following their own whims and desires rather than the divine guidance.
orig: من الذين فرقوا دينهم وكانوا شيعا كل حزب بما لديهم فرحون

translation: And when adversity touches the people, they call upon their Lord, turning in repentance to Him. Then when He lets them taste mercy from Him, at once a party of them associate others with their Lord.
interpretation: This verse highlights the fickle nature of human beings. When they are faced with hardships and difficulties, they turn to Allah, seeking His help and mercy. They become humble and repentant, acknowledging their dependence on Him. However, as soon as Allah grants them relief and bestows His blessings upon them, some of them forget their previous state and start associating partners with Allah. They attribute their well-being and success to other factors, such as their own abilities or the influence of false deities, instead of being grateful to Allah alone. This behavior reflects the weakness of faith and the tendency of some individuals to be ungrateful and forgetful of Allah's favors when they are in a state of ease and comfort.
orig: وإذا مس الناس ضر دعوا ربهم منيبين إليه ثم إذا أذاقهم منه رحمة إذا فريق منهم بربهم يشركون

translation: So they may disbelieve in what We have given them. So enjoy yourselves, for you will soon know.
interpretation: This verse is a warning to those who reject the blessings and guidance that Allah has bestowed upon them. It suggests that they are ungrateful and choose to disbelieve, despite the clear signs and favors they have received. The verse tells them to enjoy their temporary worldly life and pleasures, but also warns them that they will soon come to know the consequences of their disbelief and ingratitude. It implies that they will face the reality of their choices in the Hereafter, where they will be held accountable for their actions. The tone is both admonishing and foreboding, urging the disbelievers to reflect on their stance before it is too late.
orig: ليكفروا بما آتيناهم فتمتعوا فسوف تعلمون

translation: Or have We sent down to them an authority, and it speaks of what they were associating with Him?
interpretation: This verse is questioning the validity of the beliefs of those who associate partners with Allah. It asks rhetorically whether Allah has sent down any authority or proof that supports their practice of shirk (associating partners with Allah). The implication is that there is no such authority, and that their beliefs are baseless and false. The verse emphasizes that the Qur'an is the only authority that speaks the truth about Allah and His oneness, and that anything that contradicts it is mere speculation and falsehood.
orig: أم أنزلنا عليهم سلطانا فهو يتكلم بما كانوا به يشركون

translation: And when We let the people taste mercy, they rejoice therein, but if evil afflicts them for what their hands have put forth, immediately they despair.
interpretation: This verse highlights the fickle nature of human beings. When God bestows His mercy and blessings upon them, they become happy and rejoice. However, when they face difficulties or hardships as a result of their own misdeeds and actions, they quickly lose hope and fall into despair. It emphasizes the importance of remaining steadfast in faith and gratitude, both in times of ease and hardship, and not letting one's emotions and reactions be dictated solely by the circumstances they face. It also serves as a reminder that one's own actions have consequences and that people should take responsibility for them instead of losing hope and blaming others or their circumstances.
orig: وإذا أذقنا الناس رحمة فرحوا بها وإن تصبهم سيئة بما قدمت أيديهم إذا هم يقنطون

translation: Do they not see that Allah extends provision for whom He wills and restricts [it]? Indeed in that are signs for a people who believe.
interpretation: This verse is a reminder that Allah is the one who controls the provision and sustenance of all creatures. He gives abundantly to some and limits it for others according to His wisdom and divine will. This is a sign of His power, knowledge, and authority over all things. Those who truly believe should recognize and appreciate these signs, as they demonstrate Allah's sovereignty and the truth of His message. The verse encourages believers to trust in Allah's plan and have faith that He will provide for them, even if it may not be in the way they expect or desire. It also serves as a warning to those who are ungrateful or doubtful, urging them to reflect on the signs of Allah's control over the world and to submit to His will.
orig: أولم يروا أن الله يبسط الرزق لمن يشاء ويقدر إن في ذلك لآيات لقوم يؤمنون

translation: So give the relative his right, as well as the needy and the traveler. That is best for those who desire the pleasure of Allah, and it is they who will be the successful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of fulfilling the rights of others, particularly those who are close to us (relatives), those who are in need (the poor), and those who are traveling or away from home. Giving them what they are entitled to, whether it be financial support, assistance, or kind treatment, is considered one of the best deeds in the sight of Allah. This act of generosity and kindness is a means of seeking Allah's pleasure and attaining success in this world and the Hereafter. The verse implies that true success lies in prioritizing the needs of others and fulfilling our obligations towards them, rather than focusing solely on our own desires and interests.
orig: فآت ذا القربى حقه والمسكين وابن السبيل ذلك خير للذين يريدون وجه الله وأولئك هم المفلحون

translation: That which you give in usury in order that it may increase the wealth of the people does not increase with Allah; but that which you give in charity, seeking the countenance of Allah - it is these who will increase their wealth manifold.
interpretation: This verse highlights the difference between usury (interest) and charity. Usury, which is given with the intention of increasing one's wealth at the expense of others, is not favored by Allah. It may seem to increase wealth in the short term, but it does not lead to any spiritual growth or reward. On the other hand, charity given sincerely for the sake of Allah, without expecting anything in return, is highly valued. Those who give in charity will be rewarded by Allah with an increase in their wealth and blessings, both in this world and in the hereafter. The verse emphasizes the importance of intention and sincerity in one's actions, especially when it comes to financial dealings and helping others.
orig: وما آتيتم من ربا ليربو في أموال الناس فلا يربو عند الله وما آتيتم من زكاة تريدون وجه الله فأولئك هم المضعفون

translation: It is Allah who created you, then provided for you, then will cause you to die, and then will give you life. Are there any of your \"partners\" who does anything of that? Exalted is He and high above what they associate with Him.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the unique power and divinity of Allah. It highlights that Allah alone is responsible for the creation, sustenance, death, and resurrection of human beings. No other being or entity that people may wrongly associate as partners with Allah has any ability to perform these fundamental acts. The verse exalts Allah as being far above and beyond any false associations or partnerships that people may attribute to Him. It is a strong reminder of Allah's oneness and the falsehood of polytheism or idolatry.
orig: الله الذي خلقكم ثم رزقكم ثم يميتكم ثم يحييكم هل من شركائكم من يفعل من ذلكم من شيء سبحانه وتعالى عما يشركون

translation: Corruption has appeared throughout the land and sea by [reason of] what the hands of people have earned so He may let them taste part of [the consequence of] what they have done that perhaps they will return [to righteousness].
interpretation: This verse points to the fact that the corruption, evil and disorder that has spread throughout the world is a result of the misdeeds of human beings. Allah allows people to face some of the consequences of their actions in this world, as a warning and a reminder, so that they may realize the error of their ways and turn back to the path of righteousness and obedience to Allah. It highlights the direct link between human actions and the state of the world, and serves as a call to introspection and repentance.
orig: ظهر الفساد في البر والبحر بما كسبت أيدي الناس ليذيقهم بعض الذي عملوا لعلهم يرجعون

translation: Say, "Travel through the land and observe how was the end of those before. Most of them were associators [of others with Allah].
interpretation: This verse is a call to reflect upon the fate of past nations who rejected the message of monotheism and instead worshipped false gods. By traveling the earth and witnessing the ruins and remains of these civilizations, one can see the consequences of their disbelief and polytheistic practices. It serves as a warning to those who associate partners with Allah, showing that such actions ultimately lead to destruction and downfall. The verse emphasizes the importance of learning from history and avoiding the mistakes of previous generations who turned away from the path of true faith.
orig: قل سيروا في الأرض فانظروا كيف كان عاقبة الذين من قبل كان أكثرهم مشركين

translation: So direct your face toward the correct religion before a Day comes from Allah of which there is no repelling. That Day, they will be divided.
interpretation: This verse is a reminder for believers to remain steadfast in their faith and to follow the straight path of Islam before the Day of Judgment arrives. On that day, there will be no opportunity for repentance or turning back, and people will be divided into two groups: those who followed the truth and those who strayed from it. The verse emphasizes the importance of dedicating oneself to the correct religion and living a righteous life while there is still time, as the Day of Judgment is inevitable and will come suddenly, without any possibility of postponement or reversal by Allah's decree.
orig: فأقم وجهك للدين القيم من قبل أن يأتي يوم لا مرد له من الله يومئذ يصدعون

translation: Whoever disbelieves - upon him is his disbelief; and whoever does righteousness - they are for themselves preparing,
interpretation: This verse emphasizes individual responsibility and accountability. Those who reject faith will bear the consequences of their disbelief, while those who do good deeds are ultimately benefiting themselves by preparing for the Hereafter. It suggests that each person's actions have personal consequences and that righteousness is a means of self-improvement and spiritual preparation for what comes after death.
orig: من كفر فعليه كفره ومن عمل صالحا فلأنفسهم يمهدون

translation: That He may reward those who believe and do righteous deeds out of His bounty. Indeed, He does not like the disbelievers.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of faith and good deeds in attaining Allah's reward and bounty. It suggests that Allah, out of His generosity and grace, will abundantly reward those who sincerely believe in Him and perform righteous actions. The verse also highlights Allah's dislike for those who reject faith and disbelieve in Him, indicating that they will not receive His favor or blessings. It serves as a reminder for believers to remain steadfast in their faith and to continuously strive to do good, while also cautioning against the consequences of disbelief.
orig: ليجزي الذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات من فضله إنه لا يحب الكافرين

translation: And of His signs is that He sends the winds as bringers of good tidings and to let you taste His mercy and so the ships may sail at His command and so you may seek of His bounty, and perhaps you will be grateful.
interpretation: This verse highlights the power and mercy of Allah. The winds that bring good tidings, such as rain clouds, are a sign of His existence and His desire to show mercy to His creation. The verse also points out that it is by Allah's command that ships sail on the seas, allowing people to seek His bounty through trade and travel. These blessings are meant to inspire gratitude in people towards their Lord, encouraging them to appreciate and thank Him for His favors. The verse emphasizes the importance of recognizing and appreciating the signs of Allah's existence, power, and mercy in the natural world around us.
orig: ومن آياته أن يرسل الرياح مبشرات وليذيقكم من رحمته ولتجري الفلك بأمره ولتبتغوا من فضله ولعلكم تشكرون

translation: And indeed, We sent before you [O Muhammad] messengers to their peoples, and they came to them with clear proofs; then We took retribution from those who committed crimes, and it was incumbent upon Us to support the believers.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the consistent pattern in the history of divine revelation. Allah has sent prophets and messengers to various nations in the past, and they came with clear signs and proofs to support their message. However, many people rejected the truth and committed crimes against the messengers and their followers. As a result, Allah punished those who were guilty of such transgressions. At the same time, Allah affirms that it is His duty and responsibility to support and grant victory to the believers who remain steadfast in their faith and follow the guidance of the messengers. This verse serves as a reminder that the ultimate victory belongs to the truth and those who adhere to it, even in the face of opposition and persecution.
orig: ولقد أرسلنا من قبلك رسلا إلى قومهم فجاءوهم بالبينات فانتقمنا من الذين أجرموا وكان حقا علينا نصر المؤمنين

translation: It is Allah who sends the winds, and they stir the clouds and spread them in the sky however He wills, and He makes them fragments so you see the rain emerge from within them. And when He causes it to fall upon whom He wills of His servants, immediately they rejoice.
interpretation: This verse highlights Allah's power and control over the natural world. The winds, clouds, and rain are all under His command, and He directs them as He pleases. The imagery of the clouds being stirred and spread across the sky, then breaking into fragments to release the rain, showcases the intricate design and beauty in Allah's creation. When the rain falls upon those whom Allah chooses, it brings joy and relief, as it is a sign of His mercy and a means of sustenance for His servants. This verse reminds us to appreciate and be grateful for the blessings that Allah bestows upon us through His creation.
orig: الله الذي يرسل الرياح فتثير سحابا فيبسطه في السماء كيف يشاء ويجعله كسفا فترى الودق يخرج من خلاله فإذا أصاب به من يشاء من عباده إذا هم يستبشرون

translation: And indeed before it was sent down upon them, they were in despair.
interpretation: This verse suggests that before the revelation of the Qur'an, the people were in a state of despair and hopelessness. They lacked guidance and were in need of divine intervention. The revelation of the Qur'an brought them hope, purpose, and a clear path to follow. It highlights the transformative power of God's message and how it can uplift individuals and communities from a state of spiritual darkness to one of enlightenment and faith.
orig: وإن كانوا من قبل أن ينزل عليهم من قبله لمبلسين

translation: So observe the effects of the mercy of Allah - how He gives life to the earth after its lifelessness. Indeed, that [same one] will give life to the dead, and He is over all things competent.
interpretation: This verse is a reminder of Allah's power and mercy. It encourages us to reflect on how Allah revives the dead earth with rain and vegetation, and to realize that He has the same ability to resurrect the dead on the Day of Judgment. This should increase our faith in Allah's omnipotence and motivate us to do good deeds in this life, knowing that we will be held accountable in the Hereafter. The verse also highlights the importance of observing and contemplating the signs of Allah in nature, as they serve as evidence of His existence and attributes.
orig: فانظر إلى آثار رحمت الله كيف يحيي الأرض بعد موتها إن ذلك لمحيي الموتى وهو على كل شيء قدير

translation: And if We sent a wind and they saw it turn yellow, they would continue to disbelieve after that.
interpretation: This verse highlights the stubborn nature of the disbelievers. Even if Allah were to send a clear sign, such as a wind that turns their crops and vegetation yellow, indicating a drought or calamity, they would persist in their disbelief. It shows that their rejection of faith is not due to a lack of evidence, but rather a deep-rooted obstinacy and refusal to accept the truth, even when faced with undeniable signs from Allah. This verse serves as a reminder that guidance ultimately comes from Allah, and those who choose to reject it will find excuses to remain in disbelief, no matter how clear the signs may be.
orig: ولئن أرسلنا ريحا فرأوه مصفرا لظلوا من بعده يكفرون

translation: Indeed, you cannot make the dead hear, nor can you make the deaf hear the call when they have turned their backs retreating.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the idea that guidance comes from Allah alone, and that the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) cannot force anyone to believe or accept the message of Islam against their will. Those who have turned away from the truth and rejected the message are likened to the dead who cannot hear or the deaf who cannot perceive the call, implying that their hearts and minds are sealed to the truth. The Prophet's duty is only to convey the message clearly, but he has no power to change the hearts of those who stubbornly refuse to believe, as that is the domain of Allah alone.
orig: فإنك لا تسمع الموتى ولا تسمع الصم الدعاء إذا ولوا مدبرين

translation: And you cannot guide the blind away from their error. You can only make hear those who believe in Our verses so they are Muslims.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) cannot force anyone to accept Islam or guide those who willfully reject the truth. His role is to convey the message of Islam and invite people to faith, but ultimately, it is up to each individual to choose whether to believe or not. The verse also highlights that only those who sincerely believe in Allah's signs and revelations will be receptive to the Prophet's guidance and submit themselves to Allah as Muslims. It underscores the importance of free will and personal responsibility in matters of faith.
orig: وما أنت بهاد العمي عن ضلالتهم إن تسمع إلا من يؤمن بآياتنا فهم مسلمون

translation: Allah is the one who created you from weakness, then made after weakness strength, then made after strength weakness and white hair. He creates what He wills, and He is the Knowing, the Competent.
interpretation: This verse highlights the different stages of human life and the power of Allah in creating and shaping our existence. It reminds us that we start from a state of weakness as infants, then grow into strength in our youth and adulthood, but eventually return to weakness in old age, marked by the appearance of white hair. This cycle of life is a testament to Allah's supreme knowledge and ability to create as He wills. The verse encourages us to reflect on our own mortality and to recognize Allah's omnipotence and wisdom in all aspects of creation. It also serves as a reminder to be humble and grateful for the strength and abilities we possess, knowing that they are ultimately granted by Allah and subject to His will.
orig: الله الذي خلقكم من ضعف ثم جعل من بعد ضعف قوة ثم جعل من بعد قوة ضعفا وشيبة يخلق ما يشاء وهو العليم القدير

translation: And the Day the Hour appears the criminals will swear they had remained but an hour. Thus they were deluded.
interpretation: This verse is referring to the Day of Judgment, when the criminals and disbelievers will realize the gravity of their error in denying the truth of Allah's message. They will swear that their time in this world felt as short as an hour, showing how deluded they were in thinking that their actions would have no consequences in the Hereafter. It highlights the regret and shock they will experience upon being resurrected and held accountable, realizing too late the precious opportunity they squandered in the worldly life to believe and do righteous deeds. The verse emphasizes the distorted perception of time and reality that those who turn away from divine guidance can have, and the ultimate awakening they face in the Afterlife.
orig: ويوم تقوم الساعة يقسم المجرمون ما لبثوا غير ساعة كذلك كانوا يؤفكون

translation: But those who were given knowledge and faith will say, "You remained in the Book of Allah until the Day of Resurrection, and this is the Day of Resurrection, but you did not used to know."
interpretation: This verse highlights the contrast between those who have been given knowledge and faith, and those who have not. The knowledgeable believers understand that the time spent in this worldly life is predetermined by Allah until the Day of Judgment, as recorded in the divine Book (the Preserved Tablet). They recognize that the Day of Resurrection has indeed arrived, as promised by Allah. In contrast, the disbelievers and the ignorant have no understanding of this reality and are taken by surprise when the Day of Judgment comes to pass. The verse emphasizes the importance of seeking knowledge and having faith in Allah's revelations to be prepared for the Hereafter.
orig: وقال الذين أوتوا العلم والإيمان لقد لبثتم في كتاب الله إلى يوم البعث فهذا يوم البعث ولكنكم كنتم لا تعلمون

translation: So that Day, their excuse will not benefit those who wronged, nor will they be asked to appease [Allah].
interpretation: On the Day of Judgment, the excuses and justifications of the wrongdoers and disbelievers will be of no benefit to them. They will not be given the opportunity to make amends or seek forgiveness from Allah, as the time for repentance has passed. This verse emphasizes the finality of judgment and the consequences of one's actions in this life. It serves as a warning to those who persist in wrongdoing and disbelief, reminding them that they will be held accountable for their deeds and that their excuses will hold no weight in the face of divine justice.
orig: فيومئذ لا ينفع الذين ظلموا معذرتهم ولا هم يستعتبون

translation: And indeed We have set forth for mankind, in this Quran every kind of similitude, but if you bring to them any sign or proof, the disbelievers are sure to say (to the believers): "You follow nothing but falsehood, and magic."
interpretation: This verse highlights the stubborn attitude of the disbelievers towards the divine message of the Qur'an. Despite the Qur'an containing numerous examples, parables, and lessons for mankind, the disbelievers refuse to acknowledge its truth. Even when presented with clear signs and proofs, they dismiss them as mere falsehood and magic. This interpretation emphasizes the closed-mindedness of those who reject faith, as they are unwilling to consider the evidence placed before them, instead resorting to baseless accusations against the believers. It serves as a reminder that guidance is ultimately a matter of choice and that those who persist in disbelief will find ways to justify their stance, no matter how compelling the arguments in favor of faith may be.
orig: ولقد ضربنا للناس في هذا القرآن من كل مثل ولئن جئتهم بآية ليقولن الذين كفروا إن أنتم إلا مبطلون

translation: Thus does Allah seal the hearts of those who do not know.
interpretation: This verse suggests that Allah seals the hearts of those who are ignorant or lack knowledge, preventing them from understanding and accepting the truth. It implies that a lack of knowledge and understanding can lead to a hardened heart and a resistance to divine guidance. The sealing of the heart is a consequence of one's own ignorance and unwillingness to learn and embrace the truth. This highlights the importance of seeking knowledge and being open to learning in order to maintain a pure and receptive heart that is guided by Allah's wisdom.
orig: كذلك يطبع الله على قلوب الذين لا يعلمون

translation: So be patient, [O Muhammad]. Indeed, the promise of Allah is truth. And let them not disquiet you who are not certain [in faith].
interpretation: The verse is urging Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) to remain steadfast and patient in the face of opposition and disbelief from those who lack faith and certainty in Allah's promises. It reassures him that Allah's promise of victory and support for the believers is true and will certainly come to pass, even if it may seem delayed. The Prophet is advised not to let the doubts, mockery, or opposition of the disbelievers shake his own conviction or disturb his peace of mind. This interpretation highlights the importance of patience, trust in Allah's plan, and remaining firm in one's faith despite external pressures or challenges.
orig: فاصبر إن وعد الله حق ولا يستخفنك الذين لا يوقنون

translation: Alif, Lam, Meem.
interpretation: These disconnected letters are one of the miracles of the Qur'an, and none but Allah (Alone) knows their meanings. They are used at the beginning of certain surahs as a challenge to the Arabs, who were masters of eloquence and rhetoric, to produce something similar to the Qur'an if they doubted its divine origin. The specific meaning of these letters is unknown, but some scholars have suggested that they may represent the names of Allah or indicate the inimitable nature and divine source of the Qur'anic revelation.
orig: الم

translation: These are the verses of the wise Book.
interpretation: This verse is referring to the Qur'an itself, describing it as a book full of wisdom and guidance. It suggests that the verses contained within the Qur'an are not ordinary, but rather they are profound, insightful, and come from a divine source of wisdom. The use of the word "wise" emphasizes that the Qur'an is not just a collection of rules or stories, but a source of deep understanding and enlightenment for those who reflect upon its messages. It is an invitation for the reader to approach the Qur'an with reverence and to seek the wisdom it offers for living a righteous and meaningful life.
orig: تلك آيات الكتاب الحكيم

translation: A guidance and mercy for the doers of good.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the Qur'an serves as a divine guidance and a source of mercy for those who strive to do good deeds and live righteously. It suggests that by following the teachings of the Qur'an and embodying its principles, one can attain Allah's mercy and be guided towards the path of goodness and virtue. The verse highlights the importance of not only believing in the message of the Qur'an but also actively engaging in acts of kindness, compassion, and righteousness to be among the "doers of good" who are deserving of Allah's guidance and mercy.
orig: هدى ورحمة للمحسنين

translation: Those who establish prayer and give zakah, and they, of the Hereafter, are certain [in faith].
interpretation: This verse speaks about the qualities of the true believers. They are those who establish regular prayer, fulfilling this obligation with sincerity and devotion. They also give the obligatory charity, zakah, recognizing it as a duty and a means of purifying their wealth. Importantly, they have unwavering faith in the Hereafter. They are certain of the Day of Judgment and the eternal life to come, which motivates them to lead a righteous life in this world. This certainty of faith is a defining characteristic of the true believers, guiding their actions and intentions.
orig: الذين يقيمون الصلاة ويؤتون الزكاة وهم بالآخرة هم يوقنون

translation: Those are upon [right] guidance from their Lord, and it is those who are the successful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that true guidance comes only from Allah, and that those who follow this guidance are the ones who will ultimately attain success and prosperity, both in this world and in the Hereafter. The word "muflihun" (successful) implies that they will achieve their goals, overcome challenges, and find contentment and happiness by adhering to the path that Allah has laid out for them in the Qur'an and through the teachings of Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him). This success is not merely material, but also spiritual, as it encompasses the fulfillment of one's purpose in life and the attainment of Allah's pleasure and paradise.
orig: أولئك على هدى من ربهم وأولئك هم المفلحون

translation: And of the people is he who buys the amusement of speech to mislead [others] from the way of Allah without knowledge and who takes it in ridicule. Those will have a humiliating punishment.
interpretation: This verse warns against those who engage in vain and frivolous talk or activities that distract people from the remembrance of Allah and His path. Such people do this out of ignorance and mock the divine message. The Qur'an states that a humiliating punishment awaits those who behave in this manner, as they prioritize worldly amusements over spiritual enlightenment and guidance from Allah. It emphasizes the importance of focusing on one's faith and avoiding distractions that lead people astray from the righteous path.
orig: ومن الناس من يشتري لهو الحديث ليضل عن سبيل الله بغير علم ويتخذها هزوا أولئك لهم عذاب مهين

translation: And when Our verses are recited to him, he turns away arrogantly as if he had not heard them, as if there was deafness in his ears. So give him tidings of a painful punishment.
interpretation: This verse is referring to those who turn away from the message of Allah out of pride and arrogance, even when they hear the clear signs and verses of the Qur'an. They act as if they have not heard them, as if there is a heaviness or deafness in their ears preventing them from understanding and accepting the truth. As a result of their stubborn rejection and turning away, they are promised a severe and painful punishment from Allah in the Hereafter. This emphasizes the severity of rejecting Allah's message and the consequences one will face for such arrogance and denial of the truth.
orig: وإذا تتلى عليه آياتنا ولى مستكبرا كأن لم يسمعها كأن في أذنيه وقرا فبشره بعذاب أليم

translation: Indeed, those who have believed and done righteous deeds will have gardens of pleasure.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the reward that awaits the righteous believers in the Hereafter. Those who have faith in Allah and perform good deeds in accordance with His teachings will be granted the ultimate recompense: the gardens of paradise. These gardens are described as places of eternal bliss, comfort, and delight, where the believers will find all that their souls desire. This promise serves as an encouragement for the believers to remain steadfast in their faith and to continuously strive for righteousness in their actions throughout their worldly lives.
orig: إن الذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات لهم جنات النعيم

translation: Abiding therein eternally. [It is] the promise of Allah [which is] truth. And He is the Exalted in Might, the Wise.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the eternal nature of the reward promised by Allah to the righteous believers in Paradise. It assures the believers that Allah's promise is true and will certainly be fulfilled, as He is the Almighty and the All-Wise. The verse highlights the importance of having faith in Allah's promises and striving to attain His pleasure, knowing that the ultimate reward is an everlasting life in Paradise. It also underscores Allah's attributes of power and wisdom, indicating that He is capable of fulfilling His promises and that His decisions and judgments are based on perfect wisdom.
orig: خالدين فيها وعد الله حقا وهو العزيز الحكيم

translation: He created the heavens without pillars that you see and has cast into the earth firmly set mountains, lest it should shift with you, and dispersed therein from every creature. And We sent down rain from the sky and made grow therein [plants] of every noble kind.
interpretation: This verse highlights the power and wisdom of Allah in creating the universe. The heavens are held up without visible pillars, demonstrating Allah's ability to create and sustain the universe in ways that may be beyond human comprehension. The mountains are firmly set in the earth to provide stability and prevent the earth from shaking or shifting, which is a mercy and protection for humanity. Allah has also dispersed various creatures throughout the earth, showcasing His ability to create and sustain life in all its diversity. The verse also mentions the sending down of rain from the sky, which allows for the growth of plants and vegetation of every noble kind. This emphasizes Allah's role in providing sustenance and the means for life to flourish on earth. Altogether, this verse encourages reflection on the signs of Allah's creation and the blessings He has bestowed upon humanity.
orig: خلق السماوات بغير عمد ترونها وألقى في الأرض رواسي أن تميد بكم وبث فيها من كل دابة وأنزلنا من السماء ماء فأنبتنا فيها من كل زوج كريم

translation: This is the creation of Allah. So show Me what those other than Him have created. Rather, the wrongdoers are in clear error.
interpretation: This verse challenges those who worship others besides Allah to show what their false gods have created, in contrast to the wondrous creation of Allah. It emphasizes that attributing divine powers to anyone other than Allah is a clear error and act of injustice, as only Allah is the Creator and Sustainer of all things. The verse aims to make people reflect on the logical fallacy of polytheism and encourages them to acknowledge the Oneness and Supremacy of Allah as the sole Creator deserving of worship.
orig: هذا خلق الله فأروني ماذا خلق الذين من دونه بل الظالمون في ضلال مبين

translation: And indeed, We bestowed upon Luqman wisdom [and said], "Be grateful to Allah." And whoever is grateful is grateful for [the benefit of] himself. And whoever denies [His favor] - then indeed, Allah is Free of need and Praiseworthy.
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of gratitude and its benefits for the individual. Luqman, a wise man, was granted wisdom by Allah and was advised to be thankful to Him. The verse emphasizes that expressing gratitude to Allah is ultimately beneficial for oneself, as it leads to inner peace, contentment, and spiritual growth. On the other hand, those who deny Allah's favors and refuse to acknowledge His blessings are reminded that Allah is self-sufficient and worthy of all praise, regardless of their attitude. This interpretation underscores the significance of recognizing and appreciating the blessings bestowed upon us by Allah, as it contributes to our personal well-being and strengthens our connection with the Divine.
orig: ولقد آتينا لقمان الحكمة أن اشكر لله ومن يشكر فإنما يشكر لنفسه ومن كفر فإن الله غني حميد

translation: And [mention, O Muhammad], when Luqman said to his son while he was instructing him, "O my son, do not associate [anything] with Allah. Indeed, association [with him] is great injustice."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of monotheism and the grave sin of associating partners with Allah (shirk). Luqman, known for his wisdom, advises his son to avoid the greatest injustice of all - attributing divinity to anyone or anything other than Allah. This instruction highlights the central tenet of Islam, which is the oneness of God (tawheed). It serves as a reminder for believers to direct their worship, devotion, and reliance solely towards Allah and to refrain from ascribing divine attributes or powers to any other being or object. The verse also implies the significant role parents play in guiding their children towards the right path and instilling in them the fundamental principles of faith.
orig: وإذ قال لقمان لابنه وهو يعظه يا بني لا تشرك بالله إن الشرك لظلم عظيم

translation: And We have enjoined upon man [care] for his parents. His mother carried him, [increasing her] in weakness upon weakness, and his weaning is in two years. Be grateful to Me and to your parents; to Me is the [final] destination.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of being kind and respectful to one's parents, especially the mother who endured great hardship and weakness during pregnancy and while nursing the child. It reminds us to be grateful to Allah and to our parents for their sacrifices and to remember that ultimately, we will return to Allah in the Hereafter. This verse encourages us to maintain strong family ties, show gratitude, and recognize the significant role parents play in our lives while keeping in mind our ultimate goal of pleasing Allah.
orig: ووصينا الإنسان بوالديه حملته أمه وهنا على وهن وفصاله في عامين أن اشكر لي ولوالديك إلي المصير

translation: But if they endeavor to make you associate with Me that of which you have no knowledge, do not obey them but accompany them in [this] world with appropriate kindness and follow the way of those who turn back to Me [in repentance]. Then to Me will be your return, and I will inform you about what you used to do.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of monotheism and the rejection of associating partners with Allah, even if one's parents encourage it. It instructs Muslims to treat their parents with kindness and respect in worldly matters, but not to obey them if they call towards polytheism. The verse also reminds believers that their ultimate return is to Allah, who will hold them accountable for their deeds. It encourages following the path of those who sincerely repent and turn back to Allah, seeking His guidance and forgiveness.
orig: وإن جاهداك على أن تشرك بي ما ليس لك به علم فلا تطعهما وصاحبهما في الدنيا معروفا واتبع سبيل من أناب إلي ثم إلي مرجعكم فأنبئكم بما كنتم تعملون

translation: O my son, indeed if it should be the weight of a grain of mustard seed and should be within a rock or [anywhere] in the heavens or in the earth, Allah will bring it forth. Indeed, Allah is Subtle and Acquainted.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the omniscience and omnipotence of Allah. It suggests that no matter how small or insignificant an action or thing may seem, even if it is as tiny as a mustard seed and hidden deep inside a rock or anywhere in the vast heavens or earth, Allah is aware of it and can bring it forth. This highlights the idea that nothing escapes Allah's knowledge and that He has the power to uncover and expose all things. The verse also describes Allah as "Subtle" (Latif), implying His delicate and precise understanding of all matters, and "Acquainted" (Khabir), indicating His comprehensive knowledge of everything, including the most intricate details of His creation. This verse serves as a reminder for believers to be mindful of their actions, as nothing is hidden from Allah, and to trust in His ability to bring forth justice and truth, even in the most seemingly impossible situations.
orig: يا بني إنها إن تك مثقال حبة من خردل فتكن في صخرة أو في السماوات أو في الأرض يأت بها الله إن الله لطيف خبير

translation: O my son, establish prayer, enjoin what is right, forbid what is wrong, and be patient over what befalls you. Indeed, [all] that is of the matters [requiring] determination.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of prayer, promoting good, and forbidding evil. It encourages patience and perseverance in the face of difficulties, considering these qualities as signs of strong resolve and determination. The verse is a form of advice and exhortation, urging the believer to adhere to these righteous actions and noble characteristics, which are essential for spiritual growth and for pleasing Allah. It highlights that facing challenges with patience and remaining steadfast in one's faith are integral parts of a believer's journey and are indicative of a strong will and unwavering commitment to Allah's path.
orig: يا بني أقم الصلاة وأمر بالمعروف وانه عن المنكر واصبر على ما أصابك إن ذلك من عزم الأمور

translation: And do not turn your cheek in contempt toward people or walk through the earth exultantly. Indeed, Allah does not like everyone self-deluded and boastful.
interpretation: This verse is a reminder for Muslims to be humble and modest in their interactions with others. It cautions against arrogance, pride, and looking down upon others with disdain or contempt. The verse also warns against walking with a haughty or boastful attitude, as such behavior is disliked by Allah. Instead, Muslims are encouraged to carry themselves with humility, treating others with respect and kindness, regardless of their social status or position in life. The underlying message is that true believers should embody the qualities of modesty and selflessness, avoiding any form of self-aggrandizement or superiority complex.
orig: ولا تصعر خدك للناس ولا تمش في الأرض مرحا إن الله لا يحب كل مختال فخور

translation: And be moderate in your pace and lower your voice; indeed, the most disagreeable of sounds is the voice of donkeys.
interpretation: This verse instructs Muslims to be humble and modest in their behavior, both in their physical actions and in their speech. Walking with a moderate pace and speaking in a low, gentle voice are signs of humility and self-control. The verse emphasizes this by comparing loud and harsh voices to the braying of donkeys, which is considered to be an unpleasant sound. This encourages Muslims to adopt good manners, to be considerate of others, and to avoid drawing negative attention to themselves through arrogance or loudness in speech and action.
orig: واقصد في مشيك واغضض من صوتك إن أنكر الأصوات لصوت الحمير

translation: Do you not see that Allah has subjected to you whatever is in the heavens and whatever is in the earth and amply bestowed upon you His favors, [both] apparent and unapparent? But of the people is he who disputes about Allah without knowledge or guidance or an enlightening Book [from Him].
interpretation: This verse reminds us of the countless blessings and bounties that Allah has bestowed upon humanity, both in the physical world around us and within ourselves. It encourages reflection on how everything in the heavens and earth has been made subservient to our benefit by Allah's grace. At the same time, the verse criticizes those who argue about Allah and matters of faith without true knowledge, guidance or enlightenment from divine revelation. It suggests that gratitude, humility and seeking authentic religious knowledge are the appropriate responses to Allah's favors, rather than baseless disputes.
orig: ألم تروا أن الله سخر لكم ما في السماوات وما في الأرض وأسبغ عليكم نعمه ظاهرة وباطنة ومن الناس من يجادل في الله بغير علم ولا هدى ولا كتاب منير

translation: And when it is said to them, "Follow what Allah has revealed," they say, "Rather, we will follow that which we found our fathers doing." Even though Satan invites them to the punishment of the Blaze?
interpretation: This verse criticizes the attitude of those who blindly follow the traditions and customs of their forefathers, even if they are misguided and contrary to the teachings of Allah. It highlights the importance of using one's intellect and reasoning to discern between right and wrong, rather than simply adhering to inherited beliefs. The verse warns that such blind imitation can lead one astray and result in severe consequences in the Hereafter, as it is akin to following the invitation of Satan towards the punishment of Hell. It emphasizes the need to follow the divine guidance revealed by Allah, even if it means breaking away from deeply entrenched cultural norms and practices.
orig: وإذا قيل لهم اتبعوا ما أنزل الله قالوا بل نتبع ما وجدنا عليه آباءنا أولو كان الشيطان يدعوهم إلى عذاب السعير

translation: And whoever submits his face to Allah while he is a doer of good - then he has grasped the most trustworthy handhold. And to Allah will be the outcome of [all] matters.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of complete submission to Allah while doing righteous deeds. It assures that whoever sincerely devotes himself to Allah and does good will have a firm handle on his faith, which will serve as a strong support through the challenges of this life. The verse also reminds us that the ultimate outcome of all affairs rests with Allah alone. It encourages the believers to put their trust in Him and seek His pleasure through obedience and virtuous actions, knowing that He will justly decide all matters in the end.
orig: ومن يسلم وجهه إلى الله وهو محسن فقد استمسك بالعروة الوثقى وإلى الله عاقبة الأمور

translation: And whoever disbelieves - let not his disbelief grieve you. To Us is their return, and We will inform them of what they did. Indeed, Allah is Knowing of that within the breasts.
interpretation: This verse is a reminder to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and the believers not to be saddened or disheartened by the disbelief of others. It emphasizes that those who reject faith will ultimately return to Allah, who will inform them of their deeds and hold them accountable. The verse also highlights Allah's omniscience, as He is fully aware of the innermost thoughts and intentions of all individuals. This knowledge serves as a warning to the disbelievers and a reassurance to the believers that no deed, whether good or evil, goes unnoticed by Allah.
orig: ومن كفر فلا يحزنك كفره إلينا مرجعهم فننبئهم بما عملوا إن الله عليم بذات الصدور

translation: We grant them enjoyment for a little; then We will force them to a massive punishment.
interpretation: This verse is a warning to those who reject God's message and indulge in worldly pleasures. It emphasizes the temporary nature of the enjoyment that God grants to the disbelievers in this life, which will be followed by a severe and inescapable punishment in the Hereafter. The verse highlights the consequences of choosing the fleeting pleasures of this world over the eternal rewards of the Hereafter, reminding humans of the importance of faith, righteousness, and submission to God's will.
orig: نمتعهم قليلا ثم نضطرهم إلى عذاب غليظ

translation: If you asked them, "Who created the heavens and earth?" they would surely say, "Allah." Say, "[All] praise is [due] to Allah"; but most of them do not know.
interpretation: This verse points to the innate belief in Allah that is present in all human beings, even those who outwardly reject Him. Despite this inherent recognition of Allah as the Creator, many people fail to fully grasp the implications of this belief and do not live their lives in accordance with it. They may acknowledge Allah's existence and creative power, but they do not truly understand the significance of this reality or express proper gratitude towards Him. The verse emphasizes the importance of not only recognizing Allah as the Creator but also actively praising Him and living in a manner that reflects this understanding.
orig: ولئن سألتهم من خلق السماوات والأرض ليقولن الله قل الحمد لله بل أكثرهم لا يعلمون

translation: To Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth. Indeed, Allah is the Free of need, the Praiseworthy.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that everything in existence belongs to Allah alone. He is the ultimate owner and master of the entire universe. It also highlights two of Allah's beautiful names and attributes: Al-Ghaniyy (The Self-Sufficient) and Al-Hameed (The Praiseworthy). Allah is not in need of anything from His creation, as He is completely self-sufficient. At the same time, He is the only One truly deserving of all praise and gratitude, as all blessings and bounties originate from Him. This verse encourages believers to recognize Allah's sovereignty, to be grateful for His provisions, and to turn to Him alone for all their needs.
orig: لله ما في السماوات والأرض إن الله هو الغني الحميد

translation: And if whatever trees upon the earth were pens and the sea [was ink], replenished thereafter by seven [more] seas, the words of Allah would not be exhausted. Indeed, Allah is Exalted in Might and Wise.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the infinite wisdom and knowledge of Allah. It states that even if all the trees on earth were pens and the ocean was ink, with seven more oceans to replenish it, it would still not be enough to write down all the words of Allah. This is a metaphorical way of expressing that Allah's knowledge and wisdom are boundless and inexhaustible. The verse also affirms that Allah is Almighty and All-Wise, indicating that His words are not mere utterances, but are full of power, purpose, and wisdom. It serves as a reminder for humans to be humble before the vastness of Allah's knowledge and to continuously seek to understand and apply His guidance in their lives.
orig: ولو أنما في الأرض من شجرة أقلام والبحر يمده من بعده سبعة أبحر ما نفدت كلمات الله إن الله عزيز حكيم

translation: He created you not and resurrected you not except as one soul. Indeed, Allah is All-Hearing, All-Seeing.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the unity of humanity and the idea that all human beings are equal in the sight of Allah. It reminds us that we were all created from a single soul, and will be resurrected as such on the Day of Judgment. This underscores the importance of treating each other with respect, compassion and equality, regardless of our superficial differences. The verse also affirms that Allah is aware of all our actions and intentions, both through His divine hearing and sight, encouraging us to be mindful and strive for righteousness in all aspects of our lives.
orig: ما خلقكم ولا بعثكم إلا كنفس واحدة إن الله سميع بصير

translation: Do you not see that Allah causes the night to enter the day and causes the day to enter the night and has subjected the sun and the moon, each running [its course] for a specified term, and that Allah, with whatever you do, is Acquainted?
interpretation: This verse is a reminder of Allah's immense power and control over the universe. The alternation of day and night, and the precise orbits of the sun and moon, are signs of His perfect design and governance. It also emphasizes that Allah is fully aware of all our deeds, both good and bad, and that we will be held accountable for them. This should inspire us to be mindful of our actions and strive to live righteously, knowing that nothing escapes His knowledge and that He will judge us with perfect justice in the Hereafter.
orig: ألم تر أن الله يولج الليل في النهار ويولج النهار في الليل وسخر الشمس والقمر كل يجري إلى أجل مسمى وأن الله بما تعملون خبير

translation: That is because Allah is the Truth, and that which they call upon other than Him is falsehood, and because Allah is the Most High, the Grand.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute truth and supremacy of Allah, while asserting that all other objects of worship are false and futile. It highlights the contrast between the ultimate reality of Allah and the deceptive nature of false deities or idols. The verse also affirms Allah's exalted status and grandeur, reminding believers that He is the only one worthy of worship and that seeking help or guidance from anyone or anything else is meaningless and misguided. It serves as a powerful reminder to maintain unwavering faith in Allah and to avoid the pitfalls of polytheism or idolatry.
orig: ذلك بأن الله هو الحق وأن ما يدعون من دونه الباطل وأن الله هو العلي الكبير

translation: Do you not see that ships sail through the sea by the favor of Allah that He may show you of His signs? Indeed in that are signs for everyone patient and grateful.
interpretation: This verse points to the power and grace of Allah, as evidenced by the ships that sail smoothly through the sea by His command. It is a reminder for us to reflect on the signs of Allah's creation and to be patient and grateful for His blessings. The ability of ships to navigate the vast oceans is a marvel that showcases Allah's engineering and design in the natural world. It should inspire us to be in awe of His might and to express gratitude for the means of transport and trade that He has provided. Moreover, the verse encourages us to adopt the qualities of patience and thankfulness, which are pleasing to Allah. Patience in the face of adversity and gratitude for Allah's favors are hallmarks of a true believer.
orig: ألم تر أن الفلك تجري في البحر بنعمت الله ليريكم من آياته إن في ذلك لآيات لكل صبار شكور

translation: And when waves come over them like canopies, they supplicate Allah, sincere to Him in religion. But when He delivers them to the land, there are [some] of them who are moderate [in faith]. And none rejects Our signs except everyone treacherous and ungrateful.
interpretation: This verse highlights the fickle nature of human faith. In times of great peril, such as when engulfed by waves at sea, people turn sincerely to Allah, beseeching His aid and pledging their devotion. However, once delivered from danger and back on stable land, many of them revert to their old ways, becoming moderate in their faith or even rejecting Allah's signs altogether. Only the truly treacherous and ungrateful would deny Allah's signs after being saved by His mercy. This illustrates the weakness of human resolve and the need for constant remembrance and gratitude towards Allah, both in times of hardship and ease.
orig: وإذا غشيهم موج كالظلل دعوا الله مخلصين له الدين فلما نجاهم إلى البر فمنهم مقتصد وما يجحد بآياتنا إلا كل ختار كفور

translation: O mankind, fear your Lord and fear a Day when no father will avail his son, nor will a son avail his father at all. Indeed, the promise of Allah is truth, so let not the worldly life delude you and be not deceived about Allah by the Deceiver.
interpretation: This verse is a reminder to all of humanity to be mindful of God and the Day of Judgment. It emphasizes that on that day, no person, not even a father or a son, can help or benefit another. It warns against being deluded by the temporary pleasures and distractions of this worldly life, which can lead one away from God. The verse also cautions against being deceived by Satan, who seeks to lead people astray from the path of righteousness. Ultimately, it is a call to live a life of piety, mindful of the ultimate reality of divine judgment.
orig: يا أيها الناس اتقوا ربكم واخشوا يوما لا يجزي والد عن ولده ولا مولود هو جاز عن والده شيئا إن وعد الله حق فلا تغرنكم الحياة الدنيا ولا يغرنكم بالله الغرور

translation: Indeed, Allah has knowledge of the Hour and sends down the rain and knows what is in the wombs. And no soul perceives what it will earn tomorrow, and no soul perceives in what land it will die. Indeed, Allah is Knowing and Acquainted.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute knowledge and power of Allah. It highlights that only Allah knows when the Day of Judgment will occur, controls the rain, and has knowledge of what is in the wombs. It also points out that no person knows what they will earn or where they will die, emphasizing the uncertainty of the future for human beings. The verse concludes by reaffirming Allah's all-encompassing knowledge and awareness of all things, both seen and unseen. This serves as a reminder for humans to submit to Allah's will and trust in His divine wisdom and plan.
orig: إن الله عنده علم الساعة وينزل الغيث ويعلم ما في الأرحام وما تدري نفس ماذا تكسب غدا وما تدري نفس بأي أرض تموت إن الله عليم خبير

translation: Alif, Lam, Meem.
interpretation: These disjointed letters are one of the miracles of the Qur'an, and none but Allah (Alone) knows their meanings. They may represent a challenge to the Arabs, who were masters of eloquence and literary art, to produce a sura like the Qur'an, which begins with these broken letters. Some scholars suggest that these letters might be an oath by Allah or a reference to the divine attributes or names. Ultimately, their true meaning remains known only to Allah, while we are to believe in the Qur'an as a whole, including these mysterious letters.
orig: الم

translation: The revelation of the Book, there is no doubt about it, is from the Lord of the worlds.
interpretation: This verse affirms with certainty that the Qur'an is a divine revelation from Allah, the Lord and Creator of all that exists. It leaves no room for doubt about the authenticity and truth of the Qur'an. The verse establishes that the source of this sacred scripture is not human, but rather it comes directly from the One who has complete knowledge and authority over the entire universe. This emphatic statement serves as a powerful opening to the Qur'an, setting the stage for the guidance and wisdom contained within its pages, which mankind is called upon to accept and follow without reservation.
orig: تنزيل الكتاب لا ريب فيه من رب العالمين

translation: Or do they say, "He invented it"? Rather, it is the truth from your Lord, [O Muhammad], that you may warn a people to whom no warner has come before you [so] perhaps they will be guided.
interpretation: This verse is addressing the accusations made by the disbelievers that the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) had fabricated the Qur'an himself. Allah refutes this claim and affirms that the Qur'an is indeed the truth from Him. The purpose of revealing the Qur'an to the Prophet is so that he may warn the people who had not received a messenger before him, guiding them to the straight path. This highlights the Qur'an's role as a source of guidance for mankind and emphasizes the importance of the Prophet's mission in conveying this message to those who were previously unaware of divine revelation.
orig: أم يقولون افتراه بل هو الحق من ربك لتنذر قوما ما أتاهم من نذير من قبلك لعلهم يهتدون

translation: It is Allah who created the heavens and the earth and what is between them in six days; then He established Himself above the Throne. You have not besides Him any protector or any intercessor; so will you not be reminded?
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the omnipotence and uniqueness of Allah as the sole Creator and Sustainer of the universe. It highlights that He created the heavens, the earth, and everything in between in six days, demonstrating His immense power and control over all creation. The verse then states that Allah "established Himself above the Throne," which symbolizes His supreme authority and sovereignty over the entire universe. It also serves as a reminder to humanity that there is no other protector or intercessor besides Allah, and that we should turn to Him alone for guidance, support, and salvation. The rhetorical question at the end, "so will you not be reminded?" is a powerful call to reflect upon Allah's greatness and to submit to His will, abandoning the worship or reliance upon anyone or anything else.
orig: الله الذي خلق السماوات والأرض وما بينهما في ستة أيام ثم استوى على العرش ما لكم من دونه من ولي ولا شفيع أفلا تتذكرون

translation: He arranges [each] matter from the heaven to the earth; then it will ascend to Him in a Day, the extent of which is a thousand years of those which you count.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the vastness and comprehensive nature of Allah's power and control over the universe. The "matter" refers to Allah's decree and command, which descends from the heavens to the earth, governing all affairs. The ascent of these decrees back to Him in a day equaling a thousand years by human reckoning illustrates the relative nature of time and the immense scale of Allah's authority. It serves as a reminder for humankind to recognize the limitless wisdom and might of the Creator, as His plans unfold across an infinitely greater span of time than we can perceive.
orig: يدبر الأمر من السماء إلى الأرض ثم يعرج إليه في يوم كان مقداره ألف سنة مما تعدون

translation: That is the Knower of the unseen and the witnessed, the Exalted in Might, the Merciful.
interpretation: This verse affirms that Allah alone has complete knowledge of all that is hidden and all that is apparent. He is aware of everything, whether it is concealed from human perception or visible to us. The mention of His attributes "al-Azeez" (the Exalted in Might) and "ar-Raheem" (the Merciful) alongside His knowledge indicates that while Allah is All-Powerful and Supreme, He is also Most Merciful and Compassionate towards His creation. It serves as a reminder for mankind to be conscious of Allah, recognizing that nothing is hidden from Him, and to seek His mercy and grace in all their affairs.
orig: ذلك عالم الغيب والشهادة العزيز الرحيم

translation: Who perfected everything which He created and began the creation of man from clay.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's perfection and His power of creation. It highlights that Allah has created everything in the best possible way, with utmost perfection and without any flaws. The verse also points out that the origin of human creation is from clay, a humble and lowly substance. This serves as a reminder for humans to be humble and recognize their true nature, as they are ultimately created from a simple material by the will and power of Allah. It also underscores the idea that Allah is the One who initiates and controls the process of creation, and that everything in existence is a result of His divine will and design.
orig: الذي أحسن كل شيء خلقه وبدأ خلق الإنسان من طين

translation: Then He made his posterity from an extract of a liquid disdained.
interpretation: This verse refers to the humble origin of human beings.
