God created the progeny of Adam from a seemingly insignificant fluid, emphasizing the miraculous nature of human creation and development. It serves as a reminder for humans to remain humble and recognize their origins, as they started from a liquid that is usually discarded and considered lowly. Despite this modest beginning, God has honored humanity by creating them in the best form and bestowing them with intellect and abilities. The verse encourages introspection on the marvel of human existence and gratitude towards the Creator.
orig: ثم جعل نسله من سلالة من ماء مهين

translation: Then He proportioned him and breathed into him from His [created] soul and made for you hearing and vision and hearts; little are you grateful.
interpretation: This verse points to the special status of human beings in God's creation. After creating the physical form of the human, God breathed into him from His own spirit, endowing humans with a spiritual dimension that sets them apart from other creatures. Furthermore, God has blessed humans with faculties of hearing, sight, and understanding, which are meant to be used in recognizing God's signs and being grateful to Him. However, the verse ends with a reminder that despite these blessings, human beings give little thanks and acknowledgement to their Creator.
orig: ثم سواه ونفخ فيه من روحه وجعل لكم السمع والأبصار والأفئدة قليلا ما تشكرون

translation: And they say, "When we have become lost in the earth, will we indeed be [recreated] in a new creation?" Rather, they are, in [the matter of] the meeting with their Lord, disbelievers.
interpretation: This verse is addressing the disbelief of those who deny the resurrection and the afterlife. They question how it would be possible for them to be recreated and brought back to life after their bodies have decomposed and become part of the earth. However, their skepticism is not based on logical arguments but rather on their disbelief in the very idea of meeting their Lord and being held accountable for their deeds. The verse suggests that their denial stems from their unwillingness to face the consequences of their actions and their lack of faith in God's power and ability to resurrect them.
orig: وقالوا أإذا ضللنا في الأرض أإنا لفي خلق جديد بل هم بلقاء ربهم كافرون

translation: Say, "The angel of death who is entrusted with you will take your soul in death. Then to your Lord you will be returned."
interpretation: This verse reminds us that death is inevitable and that it is the angel of death who is responsible for taking our souls at the appointed time. It emphasizes that after death, we will all return to Allah, our Creator and Sustainer, to face the consequences of our deeds in this world. This verse encourages believers to be mindful of their actions and to strive for righteousness, knowing that they will be held accountable in the Hereafter. It also provides comfort in the face of death, assuring us that it is not the end but rather a transition to the eternal life, where we will be reunited with our Lord.
orig: قل يتوفاكم ملك الموت الذي وكل بكم ثم إلى ربكم ترجعون

translation: And if you could but see when the criminals are hanging their heads before their Lord, [saying], "Our Lord, we have seen and heard, so return us [to the world]; we will work righteousness. Indeed, we are [now] certain."
interpretation: This verse is describing the state of the sinners on the Day of Judgment, when they will be brought before Allah, humbled and regretful. They will plead to Allah to send them back to the worldly life so that they can do righteous deeds and make amends for their past sins. This highlights the realization of the truth and the certainty of faith that will dawn upon them on that day, but it will be too late for them to be given another chance. It serves as a reminder for people to realize the truth and to do good deeds in this life before it is too late.
orig: ولو ترى إذ المجرمون ناكسو رءوسهم عند ربهم ربنا أبصرنا وسمعنا فارجعنا نعمل صالحا إنا موقنون

translation: And if We had willed, We could have given every soul its guidance, but the word from Me will come into effect [that] I will surely fill Hell with jinn and people all together.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the concept of free will in Islam. Although Allah has the power to guide every soul to the right path, He has chosen to grant humans the freedom to choose their own actions and beliefs. However, this freedom comes with the consequence that those who reject Allah's guidance and persist in disbelief and wrongdoing will be consigned to Hell in the afterlife, along with the rebellious jinn. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of making the right choices in life and the ultimate accountability for one's actions before Allah.
orig: ولو شئنا لآتينا كل نفس هداها ولكن حق القول مني لأملأن جهنم من الجنة والناس أجمعين

translation: So taste [the punishment] because you forgot the meeting of this, your Day; indeed, We have [accordingly] forgotten you. And taste the punishment of eternity for what you used to do.
interpretation: This verse is a stern warning to those who rejected faith and lived a life of heedlessness. It conveys that on the Day of Judgment, the disbelievers will be made to taste the severe consequences of their actions. They will be told to suffer the punishment because they forgot or ignored the inevitability of this day during their worldly life. Just as they forgot Allah and their ultimate accountability, Allah will forget them and leave them to face the eternal punishment of Hell as a result of their misdeeds and transgressions in this world. It emphasizes the gravity of neglecting one's spiritual and moral obligations, and the severe repercussions it entails in the Hereafter.
orig: فذوقوا بما نسيتم لقاء يومكم هذا إنا نسيناكم وذوقوا عذاب الخلد بما كنتم تعملون

translation: Only those believe in Our verses who, when they are reminded by them, fall down in prostration and exalt [Allah] with praise of their Lord, and they are not arrogant.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that true believers are those who, when reminded of Allah's signs and verses, humble themselves before Him in complete submission and prostration. They glorify and praise Allah with sincerity and humility, acknowledging His greatness and their own insignificance. These believers do not allow arrogance or pride to prevent them from accepting the truth and worshipping Allah wholeheartedly. The act of prostration symbolizes the highest level of reverence, obedience, and surrender to the Almighty. It signifies that the believers prioritize their relationship with Allah above all else and are ever-ready to respond to His message with utmost devotion and humility.
orig: إنما يؤمن بآياتنا الذين إذا ذكروا بها خروا سجدا وسبحوا بحمد ربهم وهم لا يستكبرون

translation: Their sides forsake their beds, they supplicate their Lord in fear and aspiration, and from what We have provided them, they spend.
interpretation: This verse speaks about the qualities of the righteous believers. They are those who leave the comfort of their beds to pray to Allah with a combination of fear and hope. Fear of His punishment and hope for His mercy and reward. Moreover, they are generous in spending from what Allah has provided them, in charity and for good causes. This demonstrates their strong faith, sincerity, and selflessness.
orig: تتجافى جنوبهم عن المضاجع يدعون ربهم خوفا وطمعا ومما رزقناهم ينفقون

translation: No soul knows what has been hidden for them of comfort for eyes [i.e., satisfaction] as reward for what they used to do.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the unimaginable rewards that await the righteous believers in Paradise. These rewards are so great and beyond human comprehension that no soul can even begin to fathom the bliss and delights that God has prepared for His devoted servants. The phrase "comfort for eyes" suggests that these rewards will bring immense joy, contentment, and satisfaction to the believers, serving as a fitting recompense for their good deeds and unwavering faith during their earthly lives. The verse also implies that the rewards in Paradise will be tailored to each individual's unique desires and aspirations, making the experience all the more gratifying and personal.
orig: فلا تعلم نفس ما أخفي لهم من قرة أعين جزاء بما كانوا يعملون

translation: Is one who is a believer like one who is defiantly disobedient? They are not equal.
interpretation: This verse highlights the fundamental difference between a true believer and a transgressor in the sight of Allah. A believer is one who has faith, submits to Allah's will, and strives to live a righteous life. In contrast, a transgressor openly defies Allah's commands and indulges in sinful acts. The verse emphasizes that these two types of people cannot be considered equal in terms of their spiritual status and the reward or punishment they will receive in the Hereafter. It serves as a reminder for Muslims to strive for faith and righteousness, as it is the key to attaining Allah's pleasure and success in the afterlife.
orig: أفمن كان مؤمنا كمن كان فاسقا لا يستوون

translation: But those who believed and did righteous deeds - for them will be the Gardens of Refuge as accommodation for what they used to do.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the reward that awaits the righteous believers in the Hereafter. Those who have faith in Allah and perform good deeds will be granted the "Gardens of Refuge" (Jannaat al-Ma'wa), which serve as a blessed abode and recompense for their actions in this world. It highlights the direct correlation between one's deeds and their ultimate destiny, encouraging individuals to lead a life of righteousness and obedience to Allah. The verse instills hope and motivation for believers, knowing that their efforts will be acknowledged and generously rewarded in the eternal life to come.
orig: أما الذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات فلهم جنات المأوى نزلا بما كانوا يعملون

translation: But as for those who defiantly disobeyed, their refuge is the Fire. Every time they wish to emerge from it, they will be returned to it while it is said to them, "Taste the punishment of the Fire which you used to deny."
interpretation: This verse speaks about the fate of those who persistently rebel against God and reject His messages. Their ultimate abode will be Hell, and whenever they try to escape from it, they will be forced back into it. The angels will rebuke them, telling them to taste the torment of the Fire as a consequence of their denying it in the worldly life despite the warnings of the prophets. It emphasizes the severity and eternity of the punishment for those who consciously choose to disbelieve and transgress the bounds set by God.
orig: وأما الذين فسقوا فمأواهم النار كلما أرادوا أن يخرجوا منها أعيدوا فيها وقيل لهم ذوقوا عذاب النار الذي كنتم به تكذبون

translation: And we will make them taste the lesser punishment before the greater punishment that perhaps they will return [to righteousness].
interpretation: This verse is a warning from Allah to those who persist in disbelief and wrongdoing. The "lesser punishment" refers to the trials, tribulations, and calamities that befall people in this worldly life as a consequence of their misdeeds and as a reminder for them to repent and turn back to the right path. The "greater punishment" refers to the torment of the Hereafter, which is far more severe and lasting than any punishment in this world. The verse emphasizes Allah's mercy in giving people the opportunity to heed these warnings and correct their ways before it is too late, so that they may be saved from the greater punishment of the Afterlife. It also highlights the idea that the difficulties we face in this life may serve as a wake-up call and a chance for spiritual growth and redemption.
orig: ولنذيقنهم من العذاب الأدنى دون العذاب الأكبر لعلهم يرجعون

translation: And who is more unjust than one who is reminded of the verses of his Lord; then he turns away from them? Indeed, We will take retribution from the criminals.
interpretation: This verse warns that those who are presented with the truth and guidance from Allah through His revelations, yet they arrogantly turn away and reject them, are committing a grave injustice. They are doing wrong to their own souls by denying the opportunity for faith and righteousness. As a consequence of their defiance and criminality, Allah affirms that He will surely hold them accountable and exact retribution upon them in the Hereafter for their willful disobedience and rejection of the truth.
orig: ومن أظلم ممن ذكر بآيات ربه ثم أعرض عنها إنا من المجرمين منتقمون

translation: And We certainly gave Moses the Scripture, so do not be in doubt of his meeting [Us], and We made it a guide for the Children of Israel.
interpretation: This verse affirms that Allah has indeed given Moses the Torah, which served as a guidance for the Children of Israel. The Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) is being reassured not to have any doubts about the divine encounter Moses had with Allah. The Torah was a source of guidance for the Israelites, directing them to the right path. This highlights the continuity of Allah's message and the importance of revealed scriptures in guiding humanity. It also emphasizes the connection between the prophethood of Moses and Muhammad, as both received divine revelations to guide their respective nations.
orig: ولقد آتينا موسى الكتاب فلا تكن في مرية من لقائه وجعلناه هدى لبني إسرائيل

translation: And We made from among them leaders guiding by Our command when they were patient and [when] they were certain of Our signs.
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of patience and unwavering faith in God's signs. Those who possess these qualities are elevated to the status of leaders and guides for their community. They are able to lead others on the right path by virtue of their own steadfastness and conviction in God's message. The verse implies that true leadership in Islam is not based on worldly power or wealth, but on spiritual strength and commitment to God's cause. It also suggests that patience and certainty are essential characteristics for anyone who aspires to be a guide or role model for others in the way of Islam.
orig: وجعلنا منهم أئمة يهدون بأمرنا لما صبروا وكانوا بآياتنا يوقنون

translation: Indeed, your Lord will judge between them on the Day of Resurrection concerning that over which they used to differ.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that on the Day of Judgment, Allah will settle all the differences and disputes that people had in their worldly lives. It serves as a reminder that ultimately, it is Allah who will judge between right and wrong, and His judgment will be final and just. The verse encourages believers to focus on their own actions and beliefs, rather than getting caught up in arguments and disagreements with others, as Allah will eventually make the truth clear and resolve all differences in the Hereafter.
orig: إن ربك هو يفصل بينهم يوم القيامة فيما كانوا فيه يختلفون

translation: Does it not guide them [to see] how many generations We destroyed before them, [as] they walk among their dwellings? Indeed in that are signs; then do they not hear?
interpretation: This verse is a reminder to mankind that they should learn from the fate of previous nations who were destroyed by Allah due to their disobedience and rejection of His messages. The fact that the ruins of these past civilizations still exist and can be seen is a clear sign of Allah's power and a warning to those who refuse to heed His guidance. The verse also implies that people have been given the faculty of hearing, which they should use to listen to and reflect upon the Qur'an and its teachings, rather than remaining deaf to the truth.
orig: أولم يهد لهم كم أهلكنا من قبلهم من القرون يمشون في مساكنهم إن في ذلك لآيات أفلا يسمعون

translation: Have they not seen how We drive the water to the barren land and therewith bring forth crops whereof their cattle and they themselves eat? Can they not then see?
interpretation: This verse is a reminder of Allah's power and mercy. It points out that Allah sends water to the barren land, making it fertile and capable of producing crops that sustain both livestock and people. The rhetorical question at the end is a call for people to reflect on these signs and recognize Allah's blessings. It implies that if they were to contemplate these miracles in nature, they would come to appreciate Allah's omnipotence and graciousness, and would be more inclined to believe in Him and follow His guidance. The verse encourages people to observe and learn from the natural world, as it contains evidence of Allah's existence and attributes.
orig: أولم يروا أنا نسوق الماء إلى الأرض الجرز فنخرج به زرعا تأكل منه أنعامهم وأنفسهم أفلا يبصرون

translation: And they say, "When will this conquest be, if you are truthful?"
interpretation: This verse is addressing the disbelievers who mockingly ask the Prophet Muhammad and the believers about when the promised victory or judgment will come, doubting their truthfulness. It reflects their skepticism and disbelief in the divine promise of God's support and the ultimate triumph of the truth. The verse implies that the disbelievers' questioning stems from their lack of faith and their challenge to the believers to prove the authenticity of their claims. It also serves as a reminder to the believers to remain patient and steadfast in the face of such challenges, trusting in God's plan and timing.
orig: ويقولون متى هذا الفتح إن كنتم صادقين

translation: Say, "On the Day of Conquest no benefit will it be to those who disbelieved their belief or will they be reprieved."
interpretation: This verse highlights the finality of the Day of Judgment, emphasizing that once the ultimate victory of truth over falsehood is established, it will be too late for the disbelievers to benefit from accepting faith at that point. Their previous rejection of the truth will seal their fate, and they will not be granted any respite or second chances. It serves as a reminder that the time to believe and act righteously is in this life, before the arrival of the Day when no excuses or changes of heart will be accepted.
orig: قل يوم الفتح لا ينفع الذين كفروا إيمانهم ولا هم ينظرون

translation: So turn away from them and wait. Indeed, they are waiting.
interpretation: This verse instructs the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) to turn away from the disbelievers who reject his message and to wait patiently for the ultimate outcome. It implies that the disbelievers are also waiting, perhaps for some calamity to befall the Prophet or for him to fail in his mission. However, the verse suggests that the Prophet should remain steadfast in his faith and continue to convey the message of Islam, knowing that the ultimate victory belongs to Allah and those who believe in Him. It is a reminder that the Prophet's duty is to deliver the message, while the outcome is determined by Allah's will.
orig: فأعرض عنهم وانتظر إنهم منتظرون

translation: O Prophet! Fear Allah, and hearken not to the Unbelievers and the Hypocrites: verily Allah is full of Knowledge and Wisdom.
interpretation: This verse is a reminder to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) to remain steadfast in his faith and devotion to Allah, and not to be swayed by the words or actions of those who reject the truth or are hypocritical in their beliefs. It emphasizes the importance of putting one's trust in Allah, who is All-Knowing and Wise, and whose guidance and support are sufficient for the believer. The verse also serves as a warning to all Muslims to be cautious of the influence of those who seek to undermine their faith and to remain firm in their commitment to Allah and His messenger.
orig: يا أيها النبي اتق الله ولا تطع الكافرين والمنافقين إن الله كان عليما حكيما

translation: And follow what is revealed to you from your Lord. Indeed, Allah is ever, with what you do, Acquainted.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of following divine revelation and guidance. It reminds the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and all believers to adhere to the teachings and commandments revealed by Allah through the Qur'an. The verse also highlights Allah's omniscience, indicating that He is fully aware of all our actions and deeds. This serves as a reminder for us to be mindful of our conduct and to strive to act in accordance with Allah's guidance, knowing that He is constantly observing and aware of everything we do. By following the revelation from our Lord, we can stay on the right path and earn His pleasure.
orig: واتبع ما يوحى إليك من ربك إن الله كان بما تعملون خبيرا

translation: And put your trust in Allah, and Allah is sufficient as a Disposer of affairs.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of placing one's complete trust and reliance in Allah. It reminds believers that Allah is the ultimate guardian and protector, and He alone is sufficient to manage and oversee all matters of life. By putting our trust in Him, we acknowledge His power, wisdom, and control over all affairs. This trust should bring peace and tranquility to the heart, knowing that Allah will guide and support those who sincerely rely on Him. The verse encourages believers to let go of their worries and anxieties, and instead, have faith in Allah's plan and His ability to handle all situations in the best possible way.
orig: وتوكل على الله وكفى بالله وكيلا

translation: Allah has not made for a man two hearts in his interior. And He has not made your wives whom you declare unlawful your mothers. And he has not made your adopted sons your [true] sons. That is [merely] your saying by your mouths, but Allah says the truth, and He guides to the [right] way.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the oneness and singularity of the human heart, both physically and spiritually. It rejects the pre-Islamic Arabian custom of zihar, where a man would divorce his wife by declaring her to be like his mother. It also abolishes the practice of adoption as it was known in pre-Islamic times, where an adopted child would take on the family name and have the same rights as a biological child. The verse asserts that Allah speaks the ultimate truth and guides humanity to the right path, while human customs and declarations that contradict divine law are invalid.
orig: ما جعل الله لرجل من قلبين في جوفه وما جعل أزواجكم اللائي تظاهرون منهن أمهاتكم وما جعل أدعياءكم أبناءكم ذلكم قولكم بأفواهكم والله يقول الحق وهو يهدي السبيل

translation: Call them by [the names of] their fathers; it is more just in the sight of Allah. But if you do not know their fathers - then they are [still] your brothers in religion and those entrusted to you. And there is no blame upon you for that in which you have erred but [only for] what your hearts intended. And ever is Allah Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of calling adopted children by the names of their biological fathers, as it is more just and truthful in the sight of Allah. However, if the biological fathers are unknown, the adopted children should be considered as brothers in faith and those entrusted to the care of the adoptive parents. The verse also reassures that there is no blame for unintentional mistakes in this matter, as long as the intentions of the heart are pure. It highlights Allah's forgiveness and mercy towards those who may err unintentionally.
orig: ادعوهم لآبائهم هو أقسط عند الله فإن لم تعلموا آباءهم فإخوانكم في الدين ومواليكم وليس عليكم جناح فيما أخطأتم به ولكن ما تعمدت قلوبكم وكان الله غفورا رحيما

translation: The Prophet is more worthy of the believers than themselves, and his wives are [in the position of] their mothers. And those of [blood] relationship are more entitled [to inheritance] in the decree of Allah than the [other] believers and the emigrants, except that you may do to your close associates a kindness [through bequest]. That was in the Book inscribed.
interpretation: This verse establishes the special status and closeness of Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) to the believers, even more than their own selves. It also elevates the status of his wives as the "Mothers of the Believers." The verse then affirms that blood relatives have higher priority in terms of inheritance and rights than other believers and emigrants, based on the decree of Allah. However, it allows an exception of making a bequest to close friends or allies as an act of kindness. This ruling, as the verse states, is inscribed in the Preserved Book (al-Lawh al-Mahfūẓ).
orig: النبي أولى بالمؤمنين من أنفسهم وأزواجه أمهاتهم وأولو الأرحام بعضهم أولى ببعض في كتاب الله من المؤمنين والمهاجرين إلا أن تفعلوا إلى أوليائكم معروفا كان ذلك في الكتاب مسطورا

translation: And [recall, O Muhammad], when We took from the prophets their covenant and from you and from Noah and Abraham and Moses and Jesus, the son of Mary; and We took from them a solemn covenant.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance and seriousness of the covenant that Allah took from the prophets. It highlights the continuity of the divine message and the unity of the prophets in their mission to guide humanity towards the truth. The mention of specific prophets, such as Noah, Abraham, Moses, and Jesus, alongside Muhammad (peace be upon them all), indicates their high status and the significance of their roles in conveying Allah's message to their respective nations. The "solemn covenant" refers to the heavy responsibility and commitment entrusted to the prophets to deliver the divine revelation faithfully and to lead by example. This covenant serves as a reminder for the prophets and their followers to remain steadfast in their faith and to fulfill their obligations towards Allah and His message.
orig: وإذ أخذنا من النبيين ميثاقهم ومنك ومن نوح وإبراهيم وموسى وعيسى ابن مريم وأخذنا منهم ميثاقا غليظا

translation: That He may question the truthful about their truth. And He has prepared for the disbelievers a painful punishment.
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of truthfulness and the consequences of disbelief. On the Day of Judgment, Allah will question the truthful about their honesty and sincerity in their faith and deeds. This emphasizes the significance of being truthful in all aspects of life, as one will be held accountable for it. In contrast, those who reject faith and choose to disbelieve will face a severe and painful punishment prepared by Allah. The verse serves as a reminder for believers to remain steadfast in their truthfulness and a warning for disbelievers about the impending consequences of their actions.
orig: ليسأل الصادقين عن صدقهم وأعد للكافرين عذابا أليما

translation: O you who have believed, remember the favor of Allah upon you when armies came to [attack] you and We sent upon them a wind and armies [of angels] you did not see. And ever is Allah, of what you do, Seeing.
interpretation: This verse reminds the believers of Allah's favor upon them when they were facing a difficult situation. It refers to the Battle of the Trench, where a coalition of enemies came to attack the Muslims in Madinah. Allah sent a strong wind and an army of angels to help the believers, even though they could not see them. This shows that Allah is always watching over His servants and will help them in times of need, even in ways that they may not perceive. It emphasizes the importance of remembering Allah's blessings and favors, and trusting in His support and protection.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا اذكروا نعمة الله عليكم إذ جاءتكم جنود فأرسلنا عليهم ريحا وجنودا لم تروها وكان الله بما تعملون بصيرا

translation: When they came at you from above you and from below you, and when eyes shifted [in fear], and hearts reached the throats, and you assumed about Allah [various] assumptions.
interpretation: This verse refers to the Battle of the Trench, when the Muslims were besieged by a coalition of enemy forces. The phrase "from above you and from below you" indicates that the enemy attacked from all sides, causing great fear and anxiety among the believers. The shifting of eyes and hearts reaching throats are metaphors for intense fear and panic. The various assumptions about Allah suggest that some people began to doubt and despair, wondering if Allah would help them or abandon them in their time of need. The verse captures the psychological and emotional state of the Muslims during this severe test of their faith, highlighting the challenges they faced and the importance of remaining steadfast and trusting in Allah's plan even in the darkest of times.
orig: إذ جاءوكم من فوقكم ومن أسفل منكم وإذ زاغت الأبصار وبلغت القلوب الحناجر وتظنون بالله الظنونا

translation: There the believers were tried and shaken with a severe shaking.
interpretation: This verse refers to a time of great trial and tribulation that the early Muslim community faced, which severely tested their faith. The "shaking" mentioned could be interpreted metaphorically as the psychological and emotional upheaval they experienced during this difficult period when their beliefs and resolve were challenged. It suggests that true faith is proven and strengthened through trials and hardships, not just in times of ease. The verse emphasizes that even the strongest of believers are not immune to tests and may face periods where their faith is shaken, but those who persevere and hold fast to their beliefs will ultimately emerge stronger. It encourages believers to have patience and fortitude during trying times.
orig: هنالك ابتلي المؤمنون وزلزلوا زلزالا شديدا

translation: And [remember] when the hypocrites and those in whose hearts is disease said, "Allah and His Messenger did not promise us except delusion,"
interpretation: This verse is referring to the hypocrites and those with weak faith who, in times of difficulty or when facing the enemy, would doubt the promises of victory and success that Allah and His Messenger (ﷺ) had given to the believers. They considered these divine promises to be nothing but false hopes and delusions. It highlights their lack of trust in Allah and His Messenger (ﷺ) and exposes the disease of doubt and hypocrisy in their hearts. The verse implies that true believers remain steadfast and have complete trust in Allah's promises, even in the face of adversities, while those with diseased hearts waver and fall into despair and skepticism.
orig: وإذ يقول المنافقون والذين في قلوبهم مرض ما وعدنا الله ورسوله إلا غرورا

translation: And when a party of them said, "O people of Yathrib, there is no stability for you [here], so return [home]." And a faction of them asked permission of the Prophet, saying, "Indeed, our houses are unprotected," while they were not exposed. They did not intend except to flee.
interpretation: This verse is criticizing the hypocrites who tried to discourage the Muslims from defending Medina against the enemy attack. They claimed that Medina was vulnerable and that the Muslims should retreat to safety, using the excuse that their homes were unprotected. However, their real intention was to flee from the battle out of cowardice and lack of faith. The verse exposes their false excuses and highlights their hypocrisy in trying to undermine the Prophet's leadership and the Muslims' resolve in the face of adversity. It teaches us to be wary of those who spread defeatism and to trust in God's plan even in difficult times.
orig: وإذ قالت طائفة منهم يا أهل يثرب لا مقام لكم فارجعوا ويستأذن فريق منهم النبي يقولون إن بيوتنا عورة وما هي بعورة إن يريدون إلا فرارا

translation: And if they had entered upon them from all its [city's] sides and then been asked to cause corruption, they would have done so and hesitated not, except briefly.
interpretation: This verse suggests that if the hypocrites were to gain access to Medina from all directions and were then asked to cause mischief and corruption, they would readily comply without much hesitation. It highlights their inherent inclination towards causing harm and disorder, and their lack of loyalty to the Islamic community. The verse implies that given the opportunity, these hypocrites would not think twice before betraying the Muslims and causing turmoil in the society.
orig: ولو دخلت عليهم من أقطارها ثم سئلوا الفتنة لآتوها وما تلبثوا بها إلا يسيرا

translation: And they had already promised Allah before not to turn their backs and flee. And ever is the promise to Allah [that about which one will be] questioned.
interpretation: This verse is referring to the believers who had made a covenant with Allah to stand firm in battle and not flee from the enemy. It emphasizes the importance of fulfilling one's promises and obligations to Allah, as believers will be held accountable for the covenants they make with Him. The verse serves as a reminder that the commitments and pledges made to Allah are a serious matter and should not be taken lightly or broken, as one will be questioned about them on the Day of Judgment.
orig: ولقد كانوا عاهدوا الله من قبل لا يولون الأدبار وكان عهد الله مسئولا

translation: Say, "Never will fleeing benefit you if you flee from death or killing; and then [if you did], you would not be given enjoyment [of life] except for a little."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the inevitability of death and the futility of trying to escape it. It reminds believers that even if they were to flee from death or being killed, it would not benefit them in the long run, as they would only be granted a short respite in this worldly life. The verse encourages acceptance of one's fate and trust in God's plan, highlighting the temporary nature of our existence and the importance of focusing on the eternal life in the Hereafter rather than clinging to the fleeting pleasures of this world.
orig: قل لن ينفعكم الفرار إن فررتم من الموت أو القتل وإذا لا تمتعون إلا قليلا

translation: Say, "Who is it that can protect you from Allah if He intends for you an ill or intends for you a mercy?" And they will not find for themselves besides Allah any protector or any helper.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute power and authority of Allah over His creation. It challenges those who seek protection or help from anyone or anything besides Allah, reminding them that no one can shield them from Allah's punishment or prevent His mercy from reaching them. It underscores the futility of relying on anyone other than Allah, as He alone is the ultimate source of protection and assistance. The verse encourages believers to put their complete trust in Allah and seek His help and guidance in all matters, knowing that He is the only one who can truly protect and support them.
orig: قل من ذا الذي يعصمكم من الله إن أراد بكم سوءا أو أراد بكم رحمة ولا يجدون لهم من دون الله وليا ولا نصيرا

translation: Allah already knows those who hinder among you and those [hypocrites] who say to their brothers, "Come to us," and do not go to battle, except for a few,
interpretation: This verse is referring to the hypocrites who tried to discourage the Muslims from fighting in the way of Allah. They would tell their fellow Muslims to come and join them in staying behind, away from the battlefield, except for a few who would go to maintain appearances. Allah is aware of who these hypocrites are and their attempts to hinder the Muslims' efforts. It highlights how Allah has knowledge of people's true intentions and actions, even if they try to hide or deceive others.
orig: قد يعلم الله المعوقين منكم والقائلين لإخوانهم هلم إلينا ولا يأتون البأس إلا قليلا

translation: Being miserly towards you; but when fear comes, you see them looking at you, their eyes revolving like one being overcome by death. But when fear departs, they lash you with sharp tongues, miserly towards [doing] any good. Those have not believed, so Allah has rendered their deeds worthless, and ever is that, for Allah, easy.
interpretation: This verse describes the hypocrites who are miserly and reluctant to spend in the way of Allah. When faced with danger or fear, they are cowardly and their eyes roll in fear as if they are facing death. However, when the danger passes, they become bold and criticize the believers harshly, and remain miserly towards doing any good deeds. Due to their hypocrisy and lack of true faith, Allah nullifies their deeds, rendering them worthless. This emphasizes that Allah is fully aware of their actions and can easily make their efforts fruitless as a consequence of their insincerity.
orig: أشحة عليكم فإذا جاء الخوف رأيتهم ينظرون إليك تدور أعينهم كالذي يغشى عليه من الموت فإذا ذهب الخوف سلقوكم بألسنة حداد أشحة على الخير أولئك لم يؤمنوا فأحبط الله أعمالهم وكان ذلك على الله يسيرا

translation: They think that the confederates have not [yet] withdrawn. And if the confederates should come [again], they would wish they were in the desert among the bedouins, inquiring [from afar] about your news. And if they should be among you, they would not fight except for a little.
interpretation: This verse is referring to the hypocrites who, during the Battle of the Trench, were hoping that the confederate armies would defeat the Muslims. They were so cowardly that even if they were present with the Muslims, they would barely participate in the fighting. The verse exposes their weak faith and their desire to be far away from the conflict, among the Bedouins in the desert, inquiring about the news of the battle from a safe distance. It highlights their lack of commitment to defending Islam and supporting the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and the Muslim community in times of hardship and danger.
orig: يحسبون الأحزاب لم يذهبوا وإن يأت الأحزاب يودوا لو أنهم بادون في الأعراب يسألون عن أنبائكم ولو كانوا فيكم ما قاتلوا إلا قليلا

translation: There has certainly been for you in the Messenger of Allah an excellent pattern for anyone whose hope is in Allah and the Last Day and [who] remembers Allah often.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) is the best role model for believers to follow. His life, character, and teachings serve as an excellent example for those who have faith in Allah and the Day of Judgment, and who constantly remember Allah in their lives. Muslims should strive to emulate the Prophet's virtues, such as his compassion, integrity, devotion to Allah, and selflessness, in order to lead a righteous life and attain success in this world and the hereafter.
orig: لقد كان لكم في رسول الله أسوة حسنة لمن كان يرجو الله واليوم الآخر وذكر الله كثيرا

translation: And when the believers saw the confederates, they said, "This is what Allah and His Messenger had promised us, and Allah and His Messenger spoke the truth." And it only increased them in faith and acceptance.
interpretation: This verse refers to the Battle of the Trench, when a coalition of Arab and Jewish tribes laid siege to Medina. The Muslims were greatly outnumbered, but they remained steadfast in their faith. When they saw the enemy alliance, rather than being discouraged, they were reminded of God's promise that they would face hardships and that He would support them. Seeing the prophecy fulfilled increased their faith and their submission to God's will. It demonstrates that true believers meet challenges with increased devotion and trust in God's plan, not with despair.
orig: ولما رأى المؤمنون الأحزاب قالوا هذا ما وعدنا الله ورسوله وصدق الله ورسوله وما زادهم إلا إيمانا وتسليما

translation: Among the believers are men true to what they promised Allah. Among them is he who has fulfilled his vow [to the death], and among them is he who awaits [his chance]. And they did not alter [the terms of their commitment] by any alteration -
interpretation: This verse speaks about the unwavering commitment and steadfastness of true believers. They are the ones who fulfill the promises they make to Allah, even if it costs them their lives. Some of them have already attained martyrdom, while others are still waiting for their opportunity to prove their devotion. What distinguishes them is their consistency and reliability - they do not change their stance or go back on their word, no matter what the circumstances. This verse praises those who demonstrate such a high level of faith and dedication to Allah's cause.
orig: من المؤمنين رجال صدقوا ما عاهدوا الله عليه فمنهم من قضى نحبه ومنهم من ينتظر وما بدلوا تبديلا

translation: That Allah may reward the truthful for their truth and punish the hypocrites if He wills or accept their repentance. Indeed, Allah is ever Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse highlights the ultimate justice of Allah. He will reward those who are truthful and sincere in their faith and deeds. As for the hypocrites who outwardly profess belief but harbor disbelief in their hearts, Allah may punish them if He wills, as their hypocrisy is a grave sin. However, the door to repentance is always open. If the hypocrites sincerely repent and mend their ways, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful, and He may accept their repentance. This shows that Allah's justice is tempered with His mercy, and He gives everyone the opportunity to turn back to Him and seek forgiveness, even those who have been insincere in their faith.
orig: ليجزي الله الصادقين بصدقهم ويعذب المنافقين إن شاء أو يتوب عليهم إن الله كان غفورا رحيما

translation: And Allah turned back the disbelievers for all their fury; no advantage did they gain. And Allah sufficed for the believers in the fighting. And Allah is Ever All-Strong, All-Mighty.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the power and strength of Allah in protecting the believers and thwarting the plans of the disbelievers. Despite their rage and efforts, the disbelievers were unable to achieve any good or benefit, and Allah spared the believers from having to engage in battle. This highlights the idea that no matter how much the enemies of Islam may try, they will never be able to overcome the will and support of Allah for His faithful servants. The verse also serves as a reminder to the believers to trust in Allah's protection and have faith in His ability to defend them against any adversity or opposition.
orig: ورد الله الذين كفروا بغيظهم لم ينالوا خيرا وكفى الله المؤمنين القتال وكان الله قويا عزيزا

translation: And He brought down those who supported them among the People of the Scripture from their fortresses and cast terror into their hearts [so that] a party you killed, and you took captive a party.
interpretation: This verse refers to the Battle of the Trench (Al-Ahzab), where the Muslims were besieged by a confederacy of pagan Arab and Jewish tribes. The "People of the Scripture" mentioned here are the Jewish tribe of Banu Qurayza, who initially had a peace treaty with the Muslims but violated it by secretly collaborating with the enemy. After the siege was lifted and the confederate army dispersed, the Muslims laid siege to the fortresses of Banu Qurayza. The verse indicates that Allah cast terror into the hearts of Banu Qurayza, leading to their surrender. As a consequence of their treachery, the men of Banu Qurayza were executed, while the women and children were taken as captives, following the judgment of Sa'd ibn Mu'adh, who was appointed as an arbiter by mutual agreement. This incident serves as a warning against betraying treaties and allying with the enemies of Islam.
orig: وأنزل الذين ظاهروهم من أهل الكتاب من صياصيهم وقذف في قلوبهم الرعب فريقا تقتلون وتأسرون فريقا

translation: And He caused you to inherit their land and their homes and their properties and a land which you have not trodden. And ever is Allah, over all things, competent.
interpretation: This verse highlights the power and authority of Allah in granting victory and bounties to the believers. It refers to the conquest of Mecca, where the Muslims inherited the lands, homes, and wealth of their former enemies. The mention of "a land which you have not trodden" suggests that Allah's favor extends beyond what they have already acquired, hinting at future conquests and the spread of Islam. The verse emphasizes that Allah has the ability to bestow such blessings and victories upon His servants, as He is all-powerful and competent over everything. It serves as a reminder for the believers to be grateful for Allah's favors and to trust in His plan and support.
orig: وأورثكم أرضهم وديارهم وأموالهم وأرضا لم تطئوها وكان الله على كل شيء قديرا

translation: O Prophet, say to your wives: If you should desire the worldly life and its adornment, then come, I will provide for you and give you a gracious release.
interpretation: This verse is addressing the wives of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him). It is giving them a choice between the worldly life with its temporary adornments and the eternal life of the Hereafter. If they desire the worldly life, the Prophet is instructed to provide for them and then release them from the marriage in a kind manner. This verse highlights the importance of prioritizing the Hereafter over the temporary pleasures of this world. It also emphasizes the compassionate and gracious manner in which the Prophet treated his wives, even in the event of a separation.
orig: يا أيها النبي قل لأزواجك إن كنتن تردن الحياة الدنيا وزينتها فتعالين أمتعكن وأسرحكن سراحا جميلا

translation: But if you desire Allah and His Messenger and the home of the Hereafter, then indeed, Allah has prepared for the doers of good among you a great reward.
interpretation: This verse is addressing the wives of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him), giving them a choice between the worldly life and its adornments or seeking the pleasure of Allah, His Messenger, and the reward of the Hereafter. It emphasizes that those who choose the latter and do good deeds will be granted a tremendous reward by Allah. The interpretation is that the believers should prioritize their devotion to Allah and His Messenger over worldly desires and pleasures, as the ultimate goal is to attain the best reward in the Hereafter through righteousness and good deeds in this life.
orig: وإن كنتن تردن الله ورسوله والدار الآخرة فإن الله أعد للمحسنات منكن أجرا عظيما

translation: O wives of the Prophet, whoever of you should commit a clear immorality - for her the punishment would be doubled two fold, and ever is that, for Allah, easy.
interpretation: This verse is a stern warning specifically addressed to the wives of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him). It emphasizes the great responsibility and high status they hold. As the wives of the Prophet, they are expected to be role models of righteousness and morality for the entire Muslim community. The verse states that if any of them were to commit a clear and evident immorality, then their punishment would be doubled compared to ordinary women. This is because of their close association with the Prophet and the honor of being part of his household. The doubling of the punishment highlights the severity and gravity of them falling into sin, given their position. However, the verse ends by affirming that such a punishment, while severe, is easy for Allah to carry out. This serves as a reminder of Allah's power and ability to enforce justice, even for those held in high regard.
orig: يا نساء النبي من يأت منكن بفاحشة مبينة يضاعف لها العذاب ضعفين وكان ذلك على الله يسيرا

translation: And whoever of you devoutly obeys Allah and His Messenger and does righteousness - We will give her her reward twice; and We have prepared for her a noble provision.
interpretation: This verse promises a great reward for the women who are obedient to Allah and His Messenger and do good deeds. Their reward will be doubled, indicating the immense value of their faith and righteous actions. Additionally, Allah has prepared for them a noble provision in the Hereafter, emphasizing the generosity and benevolence of Allah towards His faithful servants. This verse encourages women to strive for righteousness and obedience, knowing that their efforts will be greatly appreciated and rewarded by Allah in this life and the next.
orig: ومن يقنت منكن لله ورسوله وتعمل صالحا نؤتها أجرها مرتين وأعتدنا لها رزقا كريما

translation: O wives of the Prophet, you are not like anyone among women. If you fear Allah, then do not be soft in speech [to men], lest he in whose heart is disease should covet, but speak with appropriate speech.
interpretation: This verse is addressing the wives of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him), reminding them of their unique status and the responsibility that comes with it. As the wives of the Prophet, they are held to a higher standard of behavior and conduct than other women. The verse instructs them to be mindful of their speech and not to speak in a soft or alluring manner that might attract the attention of men with ill intentions or desires. Instead, they are advised to speak in a dignified and appropriate manner that does not invite any wrongful thoughts or actions. This verse emphasizes the importance of modesty, propriety, and caution in the behavior and speech of Muslim women, especially those in positions of influence or public visibility.
orig: يا نساء النبي لستن كأحد من النساء إن اتقيتن فلا تخضعن بالقول فيطمع الذي في قلبه مرض وقلن قولا معروفا

translation: And abide in your houses and do not display yourselves as [was] the display of the former times of ignorance. And establish prayer and give zakah and obey Allah and His Messenger. Allah intends only to remove from you the impurity [of sin], O people of the [Prophet's] household, and to purify you with [extensive] purification.
interpretation: This verse instructs the wives of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) to remain in their homes, avoid displaying their beauty and adornments as women did in the pre-Islamic era, establish regular prayer, give obligatory charity (zakah), and obey Allah and His Messenger. It emphasizes that Allah's intention is to keep the Prophet's household pure and free from sins and to grant them extensive purification. This signifies the special status and spiritual purity of the Prophet's family (Ahl al-Bayt) and serves as a reminder for them to uphold the highest standards of righteousness and be role models for the Muslim community.
orig: وقرن في بيوتكن ولا تبرجن تبرج الجاهلية الأولى وأقمن الصلاة وآتين الزكاة وأطعن الله ورسوله إنما يريد الله ليذهب عنكم الرجس أهل البيت ويطهركم تطهيرا

translation: And remember what is recited in your houses of the verses of Allah and wisdom. Indeed, Allah is ever Subtle and Acquainted.
interpretation: This verse is addressing the wives of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him), reminding them to pay attention to and reflect upon the revelations and wisdom that are recited in their homes. It emphasizes the importance of learning and internalizing the teachings of the Qur'an and the Prophet's guidance. The verse also highlights two attributes of Allah: His subtlety (Latif), meaning that He is gentle, kind, and aware of the finest details, and His being Acquainted (Khabir), meaning that He is well-informed about all matters, including the actions and intentions of His servants. This serves as a reminder that Allah is always watching over us and is aware of our deeds, so we should strive to live according to His guidance and wisdom.
orig: واذكرن ما يتلى في بيوتكن من آيات الله والحكمة إن الله كان لطيفا خبيرا

translation: Indeed, the Muslim men and Muslim women, the believing men and believing women, the obedient men and obedient women, the truthful men and truthful women, the patient men and patient women, the humble men and humble women, the charitable men and charitable women, the fasting men and fasting women, the men who guard their private parts and the women who do so, and the men who remember Allah often and the women who do so - for them Allah has prepared forgiveness and a great reward.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the equality of men and women in Islam, and that both genders will be rewarded for their faith, good deeds, and righteousness. It lists several praiseworthy characteristics, such as being faithful, obedient to Allah, truthful, patient, humble, charitable, chaste, and mindful of Allah, indicating that these traits are valued and encouraged in Islam for both men and women. The verse concludes by stating that those who embody these qualities will be granted Allah's forgiveness and a significant reward in the afterlife, emphasizing the importance of striving for these attributes and the spiritual benefits they bring.
orig: إن المسلمين والمسلمات والمؤمنين والمؤمنات والقانتين والقانتات والصادقين والصادقات والصابرين والصابرات والخاشعين والخاشعات والمتصدقين والمتصدقات والصائمين والصائمات والحافظين فروجهم والحافظات والذاكرين الله كثيرا والذاكرات أعد الله لهم مغفرة وأجرا عظيما

translation: It is not for a believing man or a believing woman, when Allah and His Messenger have decided a matter, that they should [thereafter] have any choice about their affair. And whoever disobeys Allah and His Messenger has certainly strayed into clear error.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of obedience to Allah and His Messenger. Once a decision has been made by them, the believers have no choice but to follow it without question. It is a reminder that the wisdom and authority of Allah and His Messenger supersede individual opinions and preferences. Disobeying or going against their decision is considered a clear and serious deviation from the right path. The verse underscores the principle of submission to divine decree and the prophetic authority in Islamic faith.
orig: وما كان لمؤمن ولا مؤمنة إذا قضى الله ورسوله أمرا أن يكون لهم الخيرة من أمرهم ومن يعص الله ورسوله فقد ضل ضلالا مبينا

translation: And [remember, O Muhammad], when you said to the one on whom Allah bestowed favor and you bestowed favor, "Keep your wife and fear Allah," while you concealed within yourself that which Allah is to disclose. And you feared the people, while Allah has more right that you fear Him. So when Zayd had no longer any need for her, We married her to you in order that there not be upon the believers any discomfort concerning the wives of their adopted sons when they no longer have need of them. And ever is the command of Allah accomplished.
interpretation: This verse is addressing the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) regarding his marriage to Zaynab bint Jahsh, who was previously married to the Prophet's adopted son, Zayd bin Harithah. The verse highlights that the Prophet concealed his feelings for Zaynab out of fear of people's opinions, despite Allah's knowledge of what was in his heart. Once Zayd divorced Zaynab, Allah commanded the Prophet to marry her to establish the principle that adoption does not create a permanent barrier to marriage. This marriage was decreed by Allah to show that adopted sons are not considered the same as biological sons in Islam, and there is no sin in marrying the former wives of adopted sons once they have been divorced. The verse emphasizes that Allah's command will always come to pass, regardless of people's opinions or societal norms.
orig: وإذ تقول للذي أنعم الله عليه وأنعمت عليه أمسك عليك زوجك واتق الله وتخفي في نفسك ما الله مبديه وتخشى الناس والله أحق أن تخشاه فلما قضى زيد منها وطرا زوجناكها لكي لا يكون على المؤمنين حرج في أزواج أدعيائهم إذا قضوا منهن وطرا وكان أمر الله مفعولا

translation: There is no blame upon the Prophet for that which Allah has ordained for him. [That is] the way of Allah with those [prophets] who have passed on before. And ever is the command of Allah a destiny decreed.
interpretation: This verse affirms that Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) is not to be blamed for following the commandments and revelations given to him by Allah. It is a divine decree and a continuation of Allah's way of dealing with His prophets and messengers throughout history. The verse emphasizes that Allah's command is predetermined and inevitable, and that the Prophet's actions are in line with the divine will. It serves as a reassurance to the Prophet and the believers, indicating that they should not feel any guilt or hesitation in obeying Allah's ordinances, as it is a part of the divine plan.
orig: ما كان على النبي من حرج فيما فرض الله له سنة الله في الذين خلوا من قبل وكان أمر الله قدرا مقدورا

translation: Those [messengers] who convey the messages of Allah and fear Him and do not fear anyone but Allah. And sufficient is Allah as Accountant.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the qualities of true messengers of Allah. They are those who faithfully deliver Allah's messages to the people, without alteration or concealment, fearing only Allah and no one else. They are not intimidated by anyone's power or influence, nor do they seek to please anyone at the expense of their duty to Allah. They know that Allah is sufficient as a Reckoner, keeping account of all deeds, and that He alone can reward or punish. This unwavering loyalty, sincerity, and reliance on Allah are the hallmarks of His true messengers.
orig: الذين يبلغون رسالات الله ويخشونه ولا يخشون أحدا إلا الله وكفى بالله حسيبا

translation: Muhammad is not the father of [any] one of your men, but [he is] the Messenger of Allah and last of the prophets. And ever is Allah, of all things, Knowing.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) was not like any other man or father figure to the believers. Rather, he was the final messenger sent by Allah to humanity, chosen to deliver His message and guidance. The verse also highlights Allah's omniscience, affirming that He has complete knowledge of all things, including the role and status of Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) as the seal of the prophets.
orig: ما كان محمد أبا أحد من رجالكم ولكن رسول الله وخاتم النبيين وكان الله بكل شيء عليما

translation: O you who have believed, remember Allah with much remembrance.
interpretation: This verse is a reminder for the believers to constantly remember and invoke Allah in their daily lives. It emphasizes the importance of maintaining a strong spiritual connection with Allah through frequent remembrance and supplication. By engaging in the remembrance of Allah, believers can attain inner peace, tranquility, and guidance in their lives. It is a means of strengthening one's faith, seeking Allah's pleasure, and remaining conscious of His presence at all times. The verse encourages believers to make the remembrance of Allah a consistent and integral part of their lives, as it brings immense benefits both in this world and in the hereafter.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا اذكروا الله ذكرا كثيرا

translation: And glorify Him morning and evening.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of remembering Allah and glorifying Him consistently throughout the day, specifically in the morning and evening. It encourages believers to make praising and exalting Allah a regular part of their daily routine, as this helps to maintain a strong connection with Him and keeps one mindful of His presence and blessings. By glorifying Allah in the early and later parts of the day, Muslims express their gratitude, devotion, and submission to their Lord, seeking His pleasure and guidance in all their affairs.
orig: وسبحوه بكرة وأصيلا

translation: It is He who confers blessing upon you, and His angels [ask Him to do so] that He may bring you out from darknesses into the light. And ever is He, to the believers, Merciful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's mercy and care for the believers. The act of Allah sending His blessings upon the believers, along with the angels praying for them, demonstrates His immense love and concern for their well-being. The ultimate goal of this divine blessing and prayer is to guide the believers out of the darkness of ignorance, disbelief, and sin, and into the light of faith, guidance, and righteousness. The verse concludes by reaffirming Allah's attribute of being ever Merciful to the believers, which underscores the depth and continuity of His compassion and grace towards those who have faith in Him.
orig: هو الذي يصلي عليكم وملائكته ليخرجكم من الظلمات إلى النور وكان بالمؤمنين رحيما

translation: Their greeting on the Day they meet Him will be, "Peace." And He has prepared for them a noble reward.
interpretation: This verse refers to the greeting that the righteous believers will receive from Allah on the Day of Judgment. "Peace" here means safety, security, and freedom from all fears and sorrows. This is a special greeting from Allah to His devoted servants, indicating His pleasure with them. The "noble reward" mentioned in the verse signifies the eternal bliss of Paradise that Allah has prepared for those who believed in Him and did good deeds in this world. This reward is a manifestation of Allah's infinite grace and generosity towards His faithful servants. The verse emphasizes the immense value and honor of this reward, which is far beyond human imagination and encompasses both spiritual and physical delights that will never end.
orig: تحيتهم يوم يلقونه سلام وأعد لهم أجرا كريما

translation: O Prophet, indeed We have sent you as a witness and a bringer of good tidings and a warner.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the important roles that the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) was sent to fulfill. As a witness, he testifies to the truth of the message he brought and the realities of the Day of Judgment. As a bearer of good news, he conveys the promise of Paradise and God's pleasure for those who believe and do righteous deeds. As a warner, he cautions people about the consequences of disbelief and sin, urging them to turn to God in repentance and obedience. These roles highlight the Prophet's responsibility in guiding humanity towards the path of salvation and his significance as the final messenger of God.
orig: يا أيها النبي إنا أرسلناك شاهدا ومبشرا ونذيرا

translation: And one who invites to Allah by His permission, and an illuminating lamp.
interpretation: This verse refers to Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) as someone who invites people towards Allah with His permission, guidance and authority. He is described metaphorically as an "illuminating lamp" because through his teachings, actions and example, he removes the darkness of ignorance, disbelief and misguidance, and lights the path to faith, righteousness and truth. Just as a radiant lamp dispels darkness and enables people to see clearly, the Prophet's message and mission serve to enlighten hearts and minds towards the worship of the One True God and adherence to His straight path.
orig: وداعيا إلى الله بإذنه وسراجا منيرا

translation: And give good tidings to the believers that they will have from Allah great bounty.
interpretation: This verse is a promise from Allah to the believers that they will be rewarded abundantly for their faith and good deeds. The "great bounty" mentioned could refer to Allah's forgiveness, mercy, and the ultimate reward of Paradise in the Hereafter. It is meant to encourage and motivate the believers to remain steadfast in their faith, knowing that their efforts will not go unnoticed or unrewarded by Allah. This verse highlights Allah's generosity and kindness towards His faithful servants, assuring them that their commitment to Islam will be greatly compensated both in this world and the next.
orig: وبشر المؤمنين بأن لهم من الله فضلا كبيرا

translation: And do not obey the disbelievers and the hypocrites but do not harm them, and put your trust in Allah. And sufficient is Allah as Disposer of affairs.
interpretation: This verse instructs the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and the believers not to follow or comply with the demands of the disbelievers and hypocrites who oppose Islam. It advises them to disregard the insults, mockery, and harm caused by these groups and to remain patient in the face of their hostility. The verse emphasizes the importance of putting one's trust in Allah alone, as He is sufficient as a Guardian and Protector for the believers. It highlights the need for Muslims to rely on Allah's support and guidance, rather than seeking the approval or assistance of those who reject faith or harbor ill intentions towards Islam.
orig: ولا تطع الكافرين والمنافقين ودع أذاهم وتوكل على الله وكفى بالله وكيلا

translation: O you who have believed, when you marry believing women and then divorce them before you have touched them, then there is not for you any waiting period to count concerning them. So provide for them and give them a gracious release.
interpretation: This verse provides guidance on the issue of divorce before consummation of marriage. If a man marries a believing woman but divorces her before having sexual relations, then there is no prescribed waiting period (iddah) for the woman before she can remarry. In such a case, the husband should still provide some material support or compensation (mut'ah) to the divorced wife, and should release her from the marriage in a kind and gracious manner without any ill feelings or resentment. This highlights the importance of treating women with respect and dignity even in the process of divorce.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا إذا نكحتم المؤمنات ثم طلقتموهن من قبل أن تمسوهن فما لكم عليهن من عدة تعتدونها فمتعوهن وسرحوهن سراحا جميلا

translation: O Prophet, indeed We have made lawful to you your wives to whom you have given their due compensation and those your right hand possesses from what Allah has returned to you [of captives] and the daughters of your paternal uncles and the daughters of your paternal aunts and the daughters of your maternal uncles and the daughters of your maternal aunts who emigrated with you and a believing woman if she gives herself to the Prophet [and] if the Prophet wishes to marry her, [this is] only for you, excluding the [other] believers. We certainly know what We have made obligatory upon them concerning their wives and those their right hands possess, [but this is for you] in order that there will be upon you no discomfort. And ever is Allah Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse highlights the special privileges and permissions granted to Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) in terms of marriage. It allowed him to marry a wider range of women, including his cousins and those who had emigrated with him, as well as women who gifted themselves to him in marriage. This was a unique allowance for the Prophet, not extended to other believers. The verse emphasizes that these permissions were given to ease any discomfort or difficulty for the Prophet in his personal life, reflecting Allah's mercy and forgiveness towards him.
orig: يا أيها النبي إنا أحللنا لك أزواجك اللاتي آتيت أجورهن وما ملكت يمينك مما أفاء الله عليك وبنات عمك وبنات عماتك وبنات خالك وبنات خالاتك اللاتي هاجرن معك وامرأة مؤمنة إن وهبت نفسها للنبي إن أراد النبي أن يستنكحها خالصة لك من دون المؤمنين قد علمنا ما فرضنا عليهم في أزواجهم وما ملكت أيمانهم لكيلا يكون عليك حرج وكان الله غفورا رحيما

translation: You, [O Muhammad], may put aside whom you will of them or take to yourself whom you will. And any that you desire of those [wives] from whom you had [temporarily] separated - there is no blame upon you [in returning her]. That is more suitable that they should be content and not grieve and that they should be satisfied with what you have given them - all of them. And Allah knows what is in your hearts. And ever is Allah Knowing and Forbearing.
interpretation: This verse grants the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) the special privilege of being able to allocate his time and attention among his wives as he sees fit, without being blamed for favoring some over others. It acknowledges the emotional needs of his wives, stating that this arrangement is best for keeping them content and free from grief or jealousy. The verse emphasizes that Allah knows the innermost feelings in people's hearts, and He is All-Knowing and Forbearing. This indicates that the Prophet's marital relations were guided by divine wisdom and not personal whims.
orig: ترجي من تشاء منهن وتؤوي إليك من تشاء ومن ابتغيت ممن عزلت فلا جناح عليك ذلك أدنى أن تقر أعينهن ولا يحزن ويرضين بما آتيتهن كلهن والله يعلم ما في قلوبكم وكان الله عليما حليما

translation: It is not lawful for you (to marry other) women after this, nor to change them for other wives even though their beauty attracts you, except those (captives or slaves) whom your right hand possesses. And Allah is Ever a Watcher over all things.
interpretation: This verse establishes a restriction specifically for the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him), prohibiting him from marrying any additional women after the revelation of this verse, even if he found them attractive. The only exception to this rule was regarding female captives or slaves obtained through war or other legitimate means, as permitted by Islamic law. This injunction served to limit the Prophet's marriages and to prevent any further additions to his household. It also emphasizes that Allah is constantly observing and aware of all things, ensuring that His commands are followed and that the limits He has set are not transgressed.
orig: لا يحل لك النساء من بعد ولا أن تبدل بهن من أزواج ولو أعجبك حسنهن إلا ما ملكت يمينك وكان الله على كل شيء رقيبا

translation: O you who have believed, do not enter the houses of the Prophet except when you are permitted for a meal, without awaiting its readiness. But when you are invited, then enter; and when you have eaten, disperse without seeking to remain for conversation. Indeed, that [behavior] was troubling the Prophet, and he is shy of [dismissing] you. But Allah is not shy of the truth. And when you ask [his wives] for something, ask them from behind a partition. That is purer for your hearts and their hearts. And it is not [conceivable or lawful] for you to harm the Messenger of Allah or to marry his wives after him, ever. Indeed, that would be in the sight of Allah an enormity.
interpretation: This verse establishes important etiquette and boundaries in social interactions with the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and his household. It prohibits entering the Prophet's houses without permission and lingering unnecessarily after meals. It institutes the use of a barrier (hijab) when addressing his wives and forbids causing any harm or discomfort to the Prophet. The verse also permanently prohibits marrying the Prophet's widows after his passing, out of respect for him and his unique status. These injunctions aim to maintain purity, modesty and reverence in the believers' conduct towards the Prophet and his family, recognizing his lofty position and the importance of avoiding any behavior that may disturb or offend him.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا لا تدخلوا بيوت النبي إلا أن يؤذن لكم إلى طعام غير ناظرين إناه ولكن إذا دعيتم فادخلوا فإذا طعمتم فانتشروا ولا مستأنسين لحديث إن ذلكم كان يؤذي النبي فيستحيي منكم والله لا يستحيي من الحق وإذا سألتموهن متاعا فاسألوهن من وراء حجاب ذلكم أطهر لقلوبكم وقلوبهن وما كان لكم أن تؤذوا رسول الله ولا أن تنكحوا أزواجه من بعده أبدا إن ذلكم كان عند الله عظيما

translation: Whether you reveal anything or conceal it, Allah is Ever All-Knower of everything.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the all-encompassing knowledge of Allah. It reminds us that nothing can be hidden from Him, whether it is our outward actions or our innermost thoughts and intentions. Allah is fully aware of everything we do or think, at all times. This realization should motivate us to be mindful of our deeds and strive for sincerity, knowing that Allah sees and knows all. It also serves as a comforting reminder that Allah understands our struggles and secrets, and that we can turn to Him with our concerns and prayers, for He is the All-Knowing.
orig: إن تبدوا شيئا أو تخفوه فإن الله كان بكل شيء عليما

translation: There is no blame upon them [i.e., women] concerning their fathers or their sons or their brothers or their brothers' sons or their sisters' sons or their women or those their right hands possess [i.e., slaves]. And fear Allah. Indeed Allah is ever, over all things, a Witness.
interpretation: This verse affirms that Muslim women are permitted to appear before certain male relatives without their outer garments or hijab. These relatives include fathers, sons, brothers, nephews (sons of brothers or sisters), other women, and their female slaves. The verse ends by reminding believers to be mindful of Allah, as He is always watching over everything. It underscores the idea that even in the presence of close relatives, propriety and modesty in behavior and dress should be maintained out of consciousness of Allah.
orig: لا جناح عليهن في آبائهن ولا أبنائهن ولا إخوانهن ولا أبناء إخوانهن ولا أبناء أخواتهن ولا نسائهن ولا ما ملكت أيمانهن واتقين الله إن الله كان على كل شيء شهيدا

translation: Indeed, Allah confers blessing upon the Prophet, and His angels [ask Him to do so]. O you who have believed, ask [ Allah to confer] blessing upon him and ask [ Allah to grant him] peace.
interpretation: This verse highlights the elevated status of Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) in the sight of Allah. It encourages the believers to send their blessings and salutations upon the Prophet, indicating that this act is highly rewarded and beloved to Allah. The verse also shows the unity between Allah and His angels in honoring and blessing the Prophet, emphasizing his importance and the respect that should be accorded to him by the believers. It serves as a reminder for Muslims to constantly remember and praise the Prophet, seeking Allah's blessings and peace upon him.
orig: إن الله وملائكته يصلون على النبي يا أيها الذين آمنوا صلوا عليه وسلموا تسليما

translation: Indeed, those who abuse Allah and His Messenger - Allah has cursed them in this world and the Hereafter and prepared for them a humiliating punishment.
interpretation: This verse is a stern warning to those who verbally abuse, mock, or disrespect Allah and His Messenger Muhammad (peace be upon him). It emphasizes that such a grave sin will incur Allah's wrath and condemnation both in this worldly life and in the Hereafter. Those who commit this offence are distanced from Allah's mercy and will face a disgraceful and humiliating punishment in the afterlife as recompense for their insolence towards the Creator and His chosen Prophet. The verse underscores the severity of this matter and serves as a deterrent for anyone who may dare to engage in such a reprehensible act.
orig: إن الذين يؤذون الله ورسوله لعنهم الله في الدنيا والآخرة وأعد لهم عذابا مهينا

translation: And those who harm believing men and believing women for [something] other than what they have earned have certainly born upon themselves a slander and manifest sin.
interpretation: This verse is a strong condemnation of those who falsely accuse or malign believing men and women without any justification. It emphasizes that spreading lies, rumors or false allegations against innocent believers is a grave sin that incurs the wrath of Allah. Slandering others unjustly is described as a "manifest sin", indicating that it is a clear and major transgression in Islam. The verse serves as a deterrent for engaging in such behavior and as a protection for the honor and reputation of the believers.
orig: والذين يؤذون المؤمنين والمؤمنات بغير ما اكتسبوا فقد احتملوا بهتانا وإثما مبينا

translation: O Prophet, tell your wives and your daughters and the women of the believers to bring down over themselves [part] of their outer garments. That is more suitable that they will be known and not be abused. And ever is Allah Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse instructs Muslim women to dress modestly by wearing outer garments that cover their bodies. The purpose is so that they will be recognized as believing women and not be harassed or molested. It shows that Islam values the dignity and protection of women. At the same time, Allah's attributes of forgiveness and mercy are emphasized, indicating that He excuses mistakes if one has good intentions and strives to follow the guidance.
orig: يا أيها النبي قل لأزواجك وبناتك ونساء المؤمنين يدنين عليهن من جلابيبهن ذلك أدنى أن يعرفن فلا يؤذين وكان الله غفورا رحيما

translation: If the hypocrites and those in whose hearts is disease and those who spread rumors in al-Madinah do not cease, We will surely incite you against them; then they will not remain your neighbors therein except for a little.
interpretation: This verse is a stern warning from Allah to the hypocrites, those with spiritual diseases in their hearts, and those who spread rumors to cause instability in Madinah. Allah tells the Prophet that if they do not desist from their evil behavior, He will command the Prophet to expel them from the city, driving them out so that they will no longer be able to live there as his neighbors, except for a short period of time. It shows that those who persistently undermine the Muslim community and spread corruption will not be tolerated indefinitely and will face serious consequences for their actions.
orig: لئن لم ينته المنافقون والذين في قلوبهم مرض والمرجفون في المدينة لنغرينك بهم ثم لا يجاورونك فيها إلا قليلا

translation: Accursed, wherever they are found, they are seized and slain mercilessly.
interpretation: This verse refers to the punishment that awaits those who oppose Allah and His Messenger. It emphasizes that wherever they may be, they will face the consequences of their actions. The verse indicates that they will be seized and killed without mercy, highlighting the severity of their punishment. It serves as a warning to those who choose to defy the teachings of Islam and persist in their wrongdoing. The verse also implies that there will be no escape or refuge for these individuals, as they will be pursued and punished wherever they are found.
orig: ملعونين أينما ثقفوا أخذوا وقتلوا تقتيلا

translation: This has been the way of Allah with those who passed on before. And you will not find in the way of Allah any change.
interpretation: This verse highlights the immutable nature of Allah's laws and decrees. It emphasizes that Allah's way of dealing with His creation, including the consequences of their actions and the ultimate judgment, remains consistent and unchanging throughout history. Just as past nations faced the repercussions of their deeds according to Allah's laws, the same will apply to present and future generations. This verse serves as a reminder that Allah's justice, mercy, and wisdom are eternal and that humans should strive to align themselves with His unchanging principles.
orig: سنة الله في الذين خلوا من قبل ولن تجد لسنة الله تبديلا

translation: People ask you concerning the Hour. Say, "The knowledge of it is only with Allah. And what may make you perceive? Perhaps the Hour is near."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the knowledge of when the Day of Judgment will occur is known only to Allah. The Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) is instructed to inform people that he does not possess this knowledge, and that it is possible that the Hour is close at hand. This serves as a reminder for people to be mindful of their actions and to always be prepared for the Day of Judgment, as it can come at any time without prior notice. The verse also highlights the importance of putting one's trust in Allah and accepting that certain matters, such as the timing of the Hour, are beyond human knowledge and control.
orig: يسألك الناس عن الساعة قل إنما علمها عند الله وما يدريك لعل الساعة تكون قريبا

translation: Indeed, Allah has cursed the disbelievers and prepared for them a Blaze.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the severe punishment that awaits those who reject faith in God. The "curse" of God upon the disbelievers refers to them being cast far away from His mercy. The "Blaze" is one of the names of Hell, indicating the intensity of the punishment there, likened to a raging fire.
