It conveys the gravity of disbelief and the ultimate consequence for those who choose that path. The verse serves as a strong warning to humanity about the importance of faith and the dire result of rejecting God's message and guidance.
orig: إن الله لعن الكافرين وأعد لهم سعيرا

translation: Abiding therein forever, they will not find any protector or helper.
interpretation: This verse speaks about the fate of those who reject Allah's guidance and persist in disbelief. It emphasizes the eternal nature of their punishment in the Hereafter, where they will abide in Hell forever, without any hope of escape or relief. The verse also highlights their complete helplessness and isolation in that state, as they will have no protector or helper to turn to for support or intercession. This serves as a severe warning to those who choose to turn away from the path of truth and righteousness, reminding them of the grave consequences of their actions in the afterlife.
orig: خالدين فيها أبدا لا يجدون وليا ولا نصيرا

translation: The Day their faces will be turned about in the Fire, they will say, "How we wish we had obeyed Allah and obeyed the Messenger."
interpretation: This verse is a stark reminder of the consequences of disobedience to Allah and His Messenger. It depicts the terrible regret and anguish that the disbelievers will experience on the Day of Judgment when they are faced with the reality of their actions. Their faces will be constantly turned in the blazing Fire as a punishment for their rejection of faith, and in that state of suffering, they will desperately wish that they had followed the guidance of Allah and His Messenger during their worldly life. This interpretation highlights the importance of heeding the divine message and submitting to the will of Allah before it is too late, as the regret in the Hereafter will be of no avail. It serves as a powerful warning to humanity to embrace the path of righteousness and obedience to escape the painful fate of those who turn away from the truth.
orig: يوم تقلب وجوههم في النار يقولون يا ليتنا أطعنا الله وأطعنا الرسولا

translation: And they will say, "Our Lord, indeed we obeyed our masters and our dignitaries, and they led us astray from the [right] way."
interpretation: This verse speaks to the regret that those who followed misguided leaders will feel on the Day of Judgment. It highlights the human tendency to sometimes blindly follow authority figures, even when they lead us away from the righteous path. The verse serves as a warning against such blind following, and emphasizes the importance of each individual taking responsibility for discerning truth from falsehood and following the guidance of God rather than the whims of men. Ultimately, each soul is accountable for its own choices and actions, and saying "we only followed our leaders" will not be an adequate excuse when standing before God.
orig: وقالوا ربنا إنا أطعنا سادتنا وكبراءنا فأضلونا السبيلا

translation: Our Lord, give them double the punishment and curse them with a great curse.
interpretation: This verse is a supplication to Allah to punish the disbelievers and those who reject His message with twice the punishment that they deserve, and to curse them greatly. It reflects the severity of their wrongdoing and the consequences they will face in the Hereafter for their disbelief and opposition to the truth. The verse emphasizes the gravity of rejecting faith and the ultimate justice that will be served by Allah.
orig: ربنا آتهم ضعفين من العذاب والعنهم لعنا كبيرا

translation: O you who have believed, do not be like those who abused Moses; then Allah cleared him of what they said. And he, in the sight of Allah, was distinguished.
interpretation: This verse serves as a reminder to the believers not to engage in slandering or speaking ill of others, especially the prophets and righteous individuals. It refers to an incident where some people falsely accused Moses (peace be upon him) of wrongdoing, but Allah exonerated him and affirmed his honorable status. The verse emphasizes the importance of refraining from causing harm to others through words and accusations, as it can lead to divine displeasure. It also highlights the virtuous position of Moses in the sight of Allah, despite the false allegations made against him. Believers should strive to emulate the prophets in their righteousness and trust that Allah will defend those who are unjustly accused or slandered.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا لا تكونوا كالذين آذوا موسى فبرأه الله مما قالوا وكان عند الله وجيها

translation: O you who have believed, fear Allah and speak words of appropriate justice.
interpretation: This verse is calling upon the believers to have consciousness and fear of Allah in all their actions and words. It encourages them to be truthful, just and righteous in their speech, avoiding anything that is inappropriate, false or misleading. Speaking with justice and honesty is a sign of true faith and a means of attaining closeness to Allah. The verse emphasizes the importance of integrity and good character in the life of a believer.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا اتقوا الله وقولوا قولا سديدا

translation: He will [then] amend your deeds for you and forgive you your sins. And whoever obeys Allah and His Messenger has certainly attained a great attainment.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance and benefits of obeying Allah and His Messenger. It promises that for those who are obedient, Allah will rectify their deeds, meaning that He will accept their good actions and multiply their rewards. Additionally, Allah will forgive their sins, which is a tremendous blessing and a means of attaining salvation in the Hereafter. The verse concludes by stating that whoever obeys Allah and His Messenger has achieved a great success and a tremendous victory. This highlights that true success lies in earning Allah's pleasure and following the guidance of His Prophet, which leads to happiness in this world and the next.
orig: يصلح لكم أعمالكم ويغفر لكم ذنوبكم ومن يطع الله ورسوله فقد فاز فوزا عظيما

translation: Indeed, we offered the Trust to the heavens and the earth and the mountains, but they declined to bear it and feared it; but man [undertook to] bear it. Indeed, he was unjust and ignorant.
interpretation: This verse highlights the unique position of human beings in the universe. The "Trust" mentioned here is generally understood to be free will and the responsibility that comes with it. The heavens, earth, and mountains, despite their vastness and strength, refused to bear this responsibility out of fear of the consequences. However, human beings, despite being comparatively weak and prone to mistakes, accepted this Trust. The verse points out that this decision was born out of ignorance and injustice on the part of human beings, as they often misuse their free will and fail to fulfill the responsibilities that come with it. This interpretation emphasizes the importance of using our God-given free will wisely and being mindful of our actions and their consequences in this world and the hereafter.
orig: إنا عرضنا الأمانة على السماوات والأرض والجبال فأبين أن يحملنها وأشفقن منها وحملها الإنسان إنه كان ظلوما جهولا

translation: That Allah may punish the hypocrite men and hypocrite women and the polytheist men and polytheist women and that Allah may accept repentance from the believing men and believing women. And ever is Allah Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the ultimate fate of those who are insincere in their faith (the hypocrites) and those who associate partners with Allah (the polytheists). Allah will punish them for their transgressions. In contrast, Allah offers forgiveness and mercy to the true believers who sincerely repent for their sins. This highlights Allah's attributes of being Forgiving (Ghafoor) and Merciful (Raheem) to those who turn back to Him in genuine repentance, while holding the hypocrites and polytheists accountable for their misdeeds. It serves as both a warning and a promise - a warning to those who persist in hypocrisy and polytheism, and a promise of forgiveness to sincere believers.
orig: ليعذب الله المنافقين والمنافقات والمشركين والمشركات ويتوب الله على المؤمنين والمؤمنات وكان الله غفورا رحيما

translation: All praise is due to Allah, to whom belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is in the earth, and to Him belongs [all] praise in the Hereafter. And He is the Wise, the Acquainted.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that all praise and gratitude belong to Allah alone, as He is the Creator and Owner of everything in the universe, both in this world and in the Hereafter. It also highlights two of His divine attributes: His wisdom (al-Hakeem) and His all-encompassing knowledge (al-Khabeer). This reminds believers that Allah is the One who deserves to be praised and acknowledged for His countless blessings, and that He is the ultimate source of guidance and knowledge in all matters of life.
orig: الحمد لله الذي له ما في السماوات وما في الأرض وله الحمد في الآخرة وهو الحكيم الخبير

translation: He knows what enters the earth and what comes out of it, and what descends from the sky and what ascends therein. And He is the Most Merciful, the Oft-Forgiving.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's all-encompassing knowledge and His complete awareness of everything that happens in the universe. It highlights that Allah knows everything that enters the earth, such as rain, seeds, and the dead, and what comes out of it, like plants, springs, and the resurrected. He also knows what descends from the sky, such as angels, divine decrees, and provisions, and what ascends to it, like angels, righteous deeds, and supplications. Despite His complete knowledge of all our actions and deeds, Allah is still Most Merciful and Oft-Forgiving, providing us with countless blessings and opportunities to seek His forgiveness and attain His pleasure. This verse serves as a reminder for us to be mindful of Allah's presence and knowledge in every aspect of our lives, and to strive in performing good deeds while seeking His mercy and forgiveness.
orig: يعلم ما يلج في الأرض وما يخرج منها وما ينزل من السماء وما يعرج فيها وهو الرحيم الغفور

translation: But the disbelievers say, "The Hour will not come to us." Say, "Yes, by my Lord, it will surely come to you. [Allah is] the Knower of the unseen." Not absent from Him is an atom's weight within the heavens or within the earth or [what is] smaller than that or greater, except that it is in a clear register.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the certainty of the Day of Judgment and the all-encompassing knowledge of Allah. The disbelievers deny the coming of the Hour, but Allah affirms through His Prophet that it will undoubtedly occur. Allah's knowledge is perfect and complete, extending to the smallest and largest of things in the heavens and the earth. Everything is recorded in a clear register, indicating that all deeds, whether good or bad, are accounted for and will be brought forth on the Day of Judgment. This verse serves as a reminder for mankind to be mindful of their actions and to prepare for the inevitable meeting with their Lord.
orig: وقال الذين كفروا لا تأتينا الساعة قل بلى وربي لتأتينكم عالم الغيب لا يعزب عنه مثقال ذرة في السماوات ولا في الأرض ولا أصغر من ذلك ولا أكبر إلا في كتاب مبين

translation: That He may reward those who believe and do righteous deeds. Those will have forgiveness and noble provision.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of faith and good deeds in attaining Allah's forgiveness and blessings. It suggests that those who sincerely believe in Allah and strive to live a righteous life, performing good actions and fulfilling their obligations, will be rewarded with Allah's mercy, forgiveness for their shortcomings, and a generous provision in this life and the hereafter. This interpretation highlights the direct connection between one's faith, actions, and the divine rewards promised by Allah to His faithful servants.
orig: ليجزي الذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات أولئك لهم مغفرة ورزق كريم

translation: But those who strive against Our verses [seeking] to cause failure - for them will be a painful punishment of foul nature.
interpretation: This verse is a stern warning to those who actively oppose and seek to undermine the message and signs of Allah. It emphasizes that those who arrogantly strive to discredit or defeat Allah's revelations and religion will face a severe and agonizing punishment in the Hereafter. Their efforts to cause the failure of Islam are futile, and they will ultimately taste the consequences of their stubborn disbelief and hostility towards the truth. The "painful punishment of foul nature" highlights the severity and abhorrence of the penalty they will suffer for their deliberate rejection of faith.
orig: والذين سعوا في آياتنا معاجزين أولئك لهم عذاب من رجز أليم

translation: And those who have been given knowledge see that what is revealed to you from your Lord is the truth, and it guides to the path of the Exalted in Might, the Praiseworthy.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that those who possess true knowledge and understanding recognize that the revelation given to Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) from Allah is the ultimate truth. They acknowledge that the Qur'an guides humanity towards the straight path leading to Allah, the Almighty and the Praiseworthy. It highlights the importance of seeking and valuing knowledge, as it enables one to discern the truth and follow the guidance provided by Allah through His revelation. Those endowed with wisdom and insight can appreciate the divine nature of the Qur'an and its role in directing mankind towards righteousness and the path of Allah's pleasure.
orig: ويرى الذين أوتوا العلم الذي أنزل إليك من ربك هو الحق ويهدي إلى صراط العزيز الحميد

translation: And those who disbelieve say, "Shall we direct you to a man who will inform you [that] when you have disintegrated in complete disintegration, you will [then] be [recreated] in a new creation?"
interpretation: This verse is referring to the disbelievers who mock the idea of resurrection and the afterlife. They sarcastically ask if they should direct the believers to someone who will tell them that even after their bodies have completely decomposed and disintegrated, they will be brought back to life and recreated anew. This highlights their skepticism and disbelief in the concept of life after death and the Day of Judgment. The Qur'an is affirming that despite their mockery, the resurrection and recreation of humans is indeed a reality that will occur by the power and will of Allah.
orig: وقال الذين كفروا هل ندلكم على رجل ينبئكم إذا مزقتم كل ممزق إنكم لفي خلق جديد

translation: Has he invented about Allah a lie or is there in him madness? Rather, they who do not believe in the Hereafter will be in the punishment and [are in] extreme error.
interpretation: This verse questions the credibility of those who reject the message of Islam and the concept of the Hereafter. It suggests that such individuals are either deliberately inventing lies about Allah or are suffering from a form of insanity. The verse asserts that those who do not believe in the Hereafter will face severe punishment and are in a state of extreme misguidance. This interpretation highlights the gravity of rejecting faith and the consequences that await those who choose to disbelieve in the afterlife, emphasizing the importance of belief in the Hereafter as a fundamental aspect of Islamic faith.
orig: أفترى على الله كذبا أم به جنة بل الذين لا يؤمنون بالآخرة في العذاب والضلال البعيد

translation: Do they not look at what is before them and what is behind them of the heaven and earth? If We will, We could cause the earth to swallow them or [could] let fall upon them fragments from the sky. Indeed in that is a sign for every servant turning back [to Allah].
interpretation: This verse is a reminder for mankind to reflect upon the signs of Allah's power and might that surround them in the heavens and the earth. It suggests that if Allah willed, He could easily destroy them by causing the earth to swallow them or by sending down pieces of the sky upon them. This should serve as a powerful sign for those who are willing to turn back to Allah in repentance and submission. The verse emphasizes the complete control and authority that Allah has over His creation, and encourages people to humble themselves before Him and turn to Him in worship and obedience.
orig: أفلم يروا إلى ما بين أيديهم وما خلفهم من السماء والأرض إن نشأ نخسف بهم الأرض أو نسقط عليهم كسفا من السماء إن في ذلك لآية لكل عبد منيب

translation: And We certainly gave David from Us bounty. [We said], "O mountains, repeat [Our] praises with him, and the birds [as well]." And We made pliable for him iron.
interpretation: This verse highlights the special favors and blessings that Allah bestowed upon Prophet David (Dawud). Allah granted him the unique ability to communicate with the mountains and birds, which would join him in praising and glorifying Allah. This symbolizes the harmony between David and nature, as well as his deep devotion to Allah. Additionally, Allah made iron pliable for David, enabling him to shape it according to his will. This could be interpreted as a metaphor for the strength, resilience, and malleability that Allah granted David in his role as a prophet and leader. It also suggests that Allah provided David with the necessary tools and resources to fulfill his divine mission and serve his people effectively.
orig: ولقد آتينا داوود منا فضلا يا جبال أوبي معه والطير وألنا له الحديد

translation: Make full coats of mail and calculate [precisely] the links, and work [all of you] righteousness. Indeed I, of what you do, am Seeing.
interpretation: This verse is instructing the addressees, likely metalworkers or armorers, to construct high-quality and well-fitted coats of chainmail armor. The command to "calculate the links" suggests that careful attention to detail and proportion is necessary in the production process. More broadly, the verse is enjoining righteous conduct and reminding that God is fully aware of all human deeds. It connects the physical crafting of armor with the spiritual forging of one's moral character, emphasizing that all actions should be done with excellence and mindfulness of divine oversight.
orig: أن اعمل سابغات وقدر في السرد واعملوا صالحا إني بما تعملون بصير

translation: And to Solomon [We subjected] the wind - its morning [journey was that of] a month - and its afternoon [journey was that of] a month, and We made flow for him a spring of [liquid] copper. And among the jinn were those who worked for him by the permission of his Lord. And whoever deviated among them from Our command - We will make him taste of the punishment of the Blaze.
interpretation: This verse highlights the blessings and favors bestowed upon Prophet Solomon by Allah. The wind was made subservient to him, enabling him to travel vast distances in a short span of time. This could be interpreted as a metaphor for the power and authority granted to Solomon to govern his kingdom efficiently. The flowing of molten copper could symbolize the abundance of resources and wealth in his realm. The mention of jinn working under his command with Allah's permission indicates that Solomon had authority over supernatural beings, but this power was still subject to divine will. The verse also serves as a warning that disobedience to Allah's commands, even by those with great power, will result in severe punishment in the Hereafter.
orig: ولسليمان الريح غدوها شهر ورواحها شهر وأسلنا له عين القطر ومن الجن من يعمل بين يديه بإذن ربه ومن يزغ منهم عن أمرنا نذقه من عذاب السعير

translation: They made for him what he willed of elevated chambers, statues, bowls like reservoirs, and stationary kettles. [We said], "Work, O family of David, in gratitude." And few of My servants are grateful.
interpretation: This verse highlights the special skills and craftsmanship that Allah bestowed upon Prophet David and his family. They were able to create magnificent structures, statues, and other objects as a blessing from Allah. However, Allah reminds them that these abilities should be used with gratitude and in service of Him. The verse also emphasizes that true gratitude is rare among people, and that only a few of Allah's servants are truly grateful for His blessings. It serves as a reminder for all believers to use their talents and blessings in a manner pleasing to Allah and to always be grateful for what He has provided.
orig: يعملون له ما يشاء من محاريب وتماثيل وجفان كالجواب وقدور راسيات اعملوا آل داوود شكرا وقليل من عبادي الشكور

translation: Then when We decreed death for him [Solomon], nothing indicated to them [i.e., the jinn] his death except a creature of the earth eating his staff. But when he fell, it became clear to the jinn that if they had known the unseen, they would not have remained in humiliating punishment.
interpretation: This verse highlights the limited knowledge of the jinn, despite their supernatural abilities. Even though they were under the command of Prophet Solomon, they were unaware of his death until his staff was eaten away by a termite, causing his body to collapse. This incident made it clear to the jinn that if they truly possessed knowledge of the unseen, they would not have continued to serve Solomon and endure humiliating punishment. The verse emphasizes that only Allah has knowledge of the unseen, and that all creatures, including the jinn, are limited in their knowledge and abilities.
orig: فلما قضينا عليه الموت ما دلهم على موته إلا دابة الأرض تأكل منسأته فلما خر تبينت الجن أن لو كانوا يعلمون الغيب ما لبثوا في العذاب المهين

translation: There was for [the tribe of] Saba' in their dwelling place a sign: two [fields of] gardens on the right and on the left. [They were told], "Eat from the provisions of your Lord and be grateful to Him. A good land [have you], and a forgiving Lord."
interpretation: This verse highlights the blessings that Allah had bestowed upon the people of Saba' (Sheba). They were given two flourishing gardens, one on each side, as a sign of Allah's favors upon them. The verse emphasizes the importance of gratitude and thankfulness for the sustenance and provisions given by Allah. It also points out that they were living in a good and prosperous land, while having a forgiving and merciful Lord. The verse serves as a reminder for people to always acknowledge and appreciate the blessings and bounties given to them by Allah, and to express gratitude through obedience and righteousness.
orig: لقد كان لسبإ في مسكنهم آية جنتان عن يمين وشمال كلوا من رزق ربكم واشكروا له بلدة طيبة ورب غفور

translation: But they turned away [refusing], so We sent upon them the flood of the dam, and We replaced their two [fields of] gardens with gardens of bitter fruit, tamarisks and something of sparse lote trees.
interpretation: This verse is a warning and a reminder of the consequences of ingratitude and turning away from Allah's blessings. The people mentioned in the verse were blessed with two beautiful gardens, but they turned away from the path of righteousness. As a result, Allah sent upon them a devastating flood that destroyed their gardens and replaced them with gardens of bitter fruit, tamarisks, and a few lote trees. This serves as a lesson that when people are ungrateful for the blessings bestowed upon them and turn away from the right path, they will face the consequences of their actions in this world and the hereafter. It emphasizes the importance of being grateful for the blessings we have and staying steadfast in our faith and obedience to Allah.
orig: فأعرضوا فأرسلنا عليهم سيل العرم وبدلناهم بجنتيهم جنتين ذواتي أكل خمط وأثل وشيء من سدر قليل

translation: Thus We recompensed them for their disbelief. And We only give such a recompense to the ungrateful disbelievers.
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine justice in punishing those who reject faith and show ingratitude towards God's blessings and signs. It emphasizes that the punishment meted out to the disbelievers is a direct consequence of their own actions and choices. The rhetorical question at the end of the verse, "And do We thus recompense except the ungrateful disbelievers?", underscores the fact that such a fate is reserved only for those who persistently deny the truth and refuse to acknowledge God's favors. It serves as a warning to humanity that disbelief and ingratitude will ultimately lead to severe consequences in the Hereafter, while also reassuring the believers that God's justice will prevail and the wrongdoers will be held accountable for their deeds.
orig: ذلك جزيناهم بما كفروا وهل نجازي إلا الكفور

translation: And We placed between them and the towns which We had blessed, towns easy to be seen, and We made the stages (of journey) between them easy (saying): "Travel in them safely both by night and day."
interpretation: This verse highlights Allah's favor upon a certain group of people by blessing their lands with prosperity and security. He made their towns prominent and well-known, and facilitated easy and safe travel between them, both during the day and night. This allowed them to engage in trade, foster relationships, and spread the message of Islam without fear of danger or hardship during their journeys. It is a reminder of Allah's mercy and the importance of gratitude for the blessings and security that He bestows upon us.
orig: وجعلنا بينهم وبين القرى التي باركنا فيها قرى ظاهرة وقدرنا فيها السير سيروا فيها ليالي وأياما آمنين

translation: But they said, "Our Lord, lengthen the distance between our journeys," and wronged themselves, so We made them narrations and dispersed them in total dispersion. Indeed in that are signs for everyone patient and grateful.
interpretation: This verse is a warning against ingratitude and disobedience to Allah. The people mentioned in the verse were blessed with ease and comfort in their journeys, but instead of being grateful, they asked Allah to make their journeys more difficult. As a result of their ingratitude and wrongdoing, Allah caused them to become mere stories of the past and scattered them, destroying their unity and strength. The verse emphasizes that there are lessons to be learned from their fate for those who are patient in adversity and grateful for Allah's blessings. It serves as a reminder to be appreciative of God's favors and to avoid arrogance and disobedience, lest we suffer a similar fate.
orig: فقالوا ربنا باعد بين أسفارنا وظلموا أنفسهم فجعلناهم أحاديث ومزقناهم كل ممزق إن في ذلك لآيات لكل صبار شكور

translation: And Iblees had already confirmed his assumption about them and they followed him, except for a party of believers.
interpretation: This verse indicates that Satan's assumption about most of mankind turned out to be true - that he would be able to lead them astray from the straight path of Allah. Most people followed Satan's temptations and went against Allah's commands, except for a group of true believers who remained steadfast in their faith and did not succumb to Satan's influence. This shows the power of Satan's deception over most of humanity, but also highlights that with sincere faith and devotion to Allah, one can resist and overcome the lures of Satan. It is a reminder for believers to always be vigilant against Satan's plots and to hold fast to their faith.
orig: ولقد صدق عليهم إبليس ظنه فاتبعوه إلا فريقا من المؤمنين

translation: And he had over them no authority except [it was decreed] that We might make evident who believes in the Hereafter from who is thereof in doubt. And your Lord, over all things, is Guardian.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Satan has no real power or authority over human beings, except what God allows him as a test of faith. The purpose behind this divine plan is to distinguish the true believers, who have unwavering faith in the Hereafter, from those who harbor doubts about it. It also highlights the fact that God is the ultimate Guardian and Protector, watching over all His creation and fully aware of their actions and beliefs. The verse serves as a reminder for humans to strengthen their faith and resist the temptations of Satan, while trusting in God's wisdom and protection.
orig: وما كان له عليهم من سلطان إلا لنعلم من يؤمن بالآخرة ممن هو منها في شك وربك على كل شيء حفيظ

translation: Say, "Invoke those you claim [as deities] besides Allah." They do not possess an atom's weight [of ability] in the heavens or on the earth, and they do not have therein any partnership [with Him], nor is there for Him from among them any assistant.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute oneness and power of Allah, stating that those whom people invoke besides Him have no power or ownership whatsoever in the heavens or on earth. They are not partners with Allah in His dominion, nor can they assist Him in any way. It serves as a reminder to humanity that worshipping anyone or anything other than Allah is futile and misguided, as He alone is the All-Powerful and Supreme Being worthy of worship and devotion.
orig: قل ادعوا الذين زعمتم من دون الله لا يملكون مثقال ذرة في السماوات ولا في الأرض وما لهم فيهما من شرك وما له منهم من ظهير

translation: And intercession does not benefit with Him except for one whom He permits. [And those wait] until, when terror is removed from their hearts, they will say [to one another], "What has your Lord said?" They will say, "The truth." And He is the Most High, the Grand.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that on the Day of Judgment, intercession will only be granted by Allah's permission to those whom He allows. It also depicts a scene where the terror and fear in the hearts of people will be removed, and they will ask each other about what Allah has decreed. The response will be that Allah has spoken the truth, affirming His justice and wisdom. The verse concludes by asserting Allah's supremacy and greatness, reminding believers of His ultimate authority and the importance of submitting to His will.
orig: ولا تنفع الشفاعة عنده إلا لمن أذن له حتى إذا فزع عن قلوبهم قالوا ماذا قال ربكم قالوا الحق وهو العلي الكبير

translation: Say, "Who provides for you from the heavens and the earth?" Say, "Allah. And indeed, we or you are either upon guidance or in clear error."
interpretation: This verse challenges those who deny Allah's existence and His role as the sole provider and sustainer of all creation. It emphasizes that there can only be two positions: either one acknowledges Allah's guidance and lives accordingly, or they are in manifest error by denying Him and attributing their provisions to other sources. The verse also highlights the contrast between the believers and the disbelievers, with the former being upon clear guidance while the latter are in a state of misguidance. It serves as a reminder for humans to reflect on the source of their sustenance and to acknowledge Allah as the ultimate provider, leading them to the path of guidance and righteousness.
orig: قل من يرزقكم من السماوات والأرض قل الله وإنا أو إياكم لعلى هدى أو في ضلال مبين

translation: Say, "You will not be asked about what we committed, nor will we be asked about what you do."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the individual responsibility of each person for their own actions. It suggests that on the Day of Judgment, no one will be questioned or held accountable for the sins or misdeeds of others. Each person will only be answerable for their own deeds and choices. This highlights the Qur'anic principle of personal accountability, where every soul bears the burden of its own actions and cannot shift that burden to someone else. It also implies that one should focus on rectifying their own conduct rather than worrying about or judging the actions of others, as ultimately, each individual will face the consequences of their own behavior.
orig: قل لا تسألون عما أجرمنا ولا نسأل عما تعملون

translation: Say, "Our Lord will bring us together; then He will judge between us in truth. And He is the Knowing Judge."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the ultimate authority and wisdom of Allah in resolving disputes and differences among people. It reminds us that, in the end, it is Allah who will gather all of humanity and judge between them with perfect knowledge and justice. The verse also highlights two of Allah's attributes: Al-Fattah (the Opener, the One who judges and decides) and Al-Aleem (the All-Knowing). It encourages believers to trust in Allah's judgment and have faith that He will resolve all matters fairly, as He possesses complete knowledge of every situation and intention. This verse promotes patience, trust in Allah, and the acceptance of His divine wisdom in all affairs.
orig: قل يجمع بيننا ربنا ثم يفتح بيننا بالحق وهو الفتاح العليم

translation: Say, "Show me those whom you have attached to Him as partners. No! Rather, He [alone] is Allah, the Exalted in Might, the Wise."
interpretation: This verse challenges the polytheists who associate partners with Allah. It asks them to present evidence for their claims of divine partners, but then asserts that no such evidence can be produced because Allah alone is the Almighty and All-Wise. The verse emphasizes the fundamental Islamic belief in the oneness and uniqueness of Allah, rejecting any notion of partners or equals to Him. It highlights Allah's attributes of power and wisdom, implying that it is contrary to divine wisdom to have partners or rivals. The verse serves as a powerful refutation of polytheism and a call to worship Allah alone.
orig: قل أروني الذين ألحقتم به شركاء كلا بل هو الله العزيز الحكيم

translation: And We have not sent you, [O Muhammad], except as a bringer of good tidings and a warner to all mankind, but most of the people do not know.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the universality of Prophet Muhammad's message. He was sent as a messenger to all of humanity, not just to a specific group or nation. His role was to bring good news of God's mercy and reward for those who follow the right path, and to warn people of the consequences of disobedience and disbelief. However, the verse also acknowledges that despite the clarity of the message, many people will still not understand or accept it due to their ignorance, stubbornness, or preoccupation with worldly matters. This highlights the importance of continually striving to spread the message and invite people to the truth, even in the face of rejection or apathy.
orig: وما أرسلناك إلا كافة للناس بشيرا ونذيرا ولكن أكثر الناس لا يعلمون

translation: And they say, "When is this promise, if you should be truthful?"
interpretation: This verse is a challenge posed by the disbelievers and skeptics who doubt the reality of the Day of Judgment and the afterlife promised by Allah and His messengers. They mockingly ask the believers when this promised event will occur, as if to suggest that it is merely a baseless claim or a delusion. The verse implies that these doubters consider themselves to be the ones who are truthful and rational, while viewing the believers as misguided or deceptive. It reflects the arrogance and cynicism of those who reject divine revelation and the concept of accountability before God. The Qur'an often cites such rhetoric from the deniers of faith to underscore their spiritual blindness and the weakness of their arguments in the face of the compelling evidence for the truth of Islam and the inevitability of the Day of Judgment.
orig: ويقولون متى هذا الوعد إن كنتم صادقين

translation: Say, "For you is the appointment of a Day [when] you will not remain behind an hour, nor will you precede [it]."
interpretation: This verse is a reminder that there will come a day when all of humanity will be held accountable for their deeds, and that this day is fixed and cannot be changed or avoided. It emphasizes the inevitability and finality of the Day of Judgment. The interpretation is that every soul will face the consequences of their actions on that day, and no one will be able to delay or hasten its arrival. It serves as a warning to be mindful of one's actions in this life, as they will determine one's fate in the hereafter.
orig: قل لكم ميعاد يوم لا تستأخرون عنه ساعة ولا تستقدمون

translation: And those who disbelieved say, "We will never believe in this Qur'an nor in that before it." But if you could see when the wrongdoers are made to stand before their Lord, refuting each other's words... Those who were oppressed will say to those who were arrogant, "If not for you, we would have been believers."
interpretation: This verse highlights the arrogance and stubbornness of the disbelievers, who refuse to accept the truth of the Qur'an and the revelations that came before it. On the Day of Judgment, when they are made to stand before Allah, they will blame each other for their disbelief. The oppressed followers will blame their arrogant leaders, claiming that if it were not for their influence, they would have believed in the truth. This emphasizes the importance of taking responsibility for one's own faith and actions, and not being swayed by the influence of others who may lead us astray from the path of righteousness.
orig: وقال الذين كفروا لن نؤمن بهذا القرآن ولا بالذي بين يديه ولو ترى إذ الظالمون موقوفون عند ربهم يرجع بعضهم إلى بعض القول يقول الذين استضعفوا للذين استكبروا لولا أنتم لكنا مؤمنين

translation: Those who were arrogant will say to those who were oppressed, "Did we avert you from guidance after it had come to you? Rather, you were criminals."
interpretation: This verse highlights the arrogance and denial of the disbelievers on the Day of Judgment. When confronted by those they misled and oppressed, the arrogant ones will attempt to shift the blame, claiming that they did not prevent the oppressed from following the truth. Instead, they will accuse the oppressed of being criminals who chose to reject guidance of their own accord. This interpretation emphasizes the importance of personal responsibility and the consequences of one's choices, as well as the tendency of the arrogant to deny their role in leading others astray.
orig: قال الذين استكبروا للذين استضعفوا أنحن صددناكم عن الهدى بعد إذ جاءكم بل كنتم مجرمين

translation: Those who were oppressed will say to those who were arrogant, "Rather, [it was your] conspiracy of night and day when you were ordering us to disbelieve in Allah and attribute to Him equals." But they will [all] confide regret when they see the punishment; and We will put shackles on the necks of those who disbelieved. Will they be recompensed except for what they used to do?
interpretation: This verse highlights the regret and blame-shifting that will occur among the disbelievers on the Day of Judgment. The oppressed followers will blame their arrogant leaders for conspiring and leading them astray from the path of Allah, both day and night. However, when faced with the punishment, both groups will feel remorse for their actions. The shackles around their necks symbolize the consequences of their disbelief and the fact that they will be held accountable for their deeds, receiving the just recompense for what they used to do in this world. This serves as a warning for people to be mindful of their actions and to follow the right path, as they will ultimately be answerable to Allah.
orig: وقال الذين استضعفوا للذين استكبروا بل مكر الليل والنهار إذ تأمروننا أن نكفر بالله ونجعل له أندادا وأسروا الندامة لما رأوا العذاب وجعلنا الأغلال في أعناق الذين كفروا هل يجزون إلا ما كانوا يعملون

translation: And We did not send into a city any warner except that its affluent said, "Indeed we, in that with which you were sent, are disbelievers."
interpretation: This verse suggests that whenever God sent a prophet or messenger to warn a community, the wealthy and privileged members of that society arrogantly rejected the divine message. They were too attached to their worldly status and comforts to heed the call to righteousness and reform their ways. The affluent are often the most resistant to spiritual guidance because they feel self-sufficient and see no need for God or religion. Their rejection of the prophets is rooted in materialism, pride and stubborn disbelief. The verse highlights a recurring theme in human history - that the elites and establishment of a community are usually the main opponents and obstacles to religious truth and social justice when proclaimed by God's messengers.
orig: وما أرسلنا في قرية من نذير إلا قال مترفوها إنا بما أرسلتم به كافرون

translation: And they said, "We have more wealth and children, and we are not to be punished."
interpretation: This verse is referring to the disbelievers who were arrogant and boastful about their worldly possessions and offspring. They believed that their wealth and large families were signs of God's favor upon them, and that they would not be punished in the Hereafter. This misguided notion stems from their lack of faith and understanding of the true purpose of life. The Qur'an refutes this idea by emphasizing that worldly blessings are not necessarily indicative of God's pleasure, and that everyone will be held accountable for their deeds on the Day of Judgment, regardless of their material status in this life. The verse serves as a reminder for believers not to be deceived by temporary worldly gains and to focus on leading a righteous life to attain success in the Hereafter.
orig: وقالوا نحن أكثر أموالا وأولادا وما نحن بمعذبين

translation: Say, "Indeed, my Lord extends provision for whom He wills and restricts [it], but most of the people do not know."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah is the one who controls the provision and sustenance of all creatures. He gives abundantly to some and limits the provision for others according to His wisdom and divine will. However, most people fail to recognize or acknowledge this truth. They may attribute their wealth or poverty to their own efforts or circumstances, rather than understanding that everything is ultimately in Allah's hands. This verse reminds us to have faith in Allah's wisdom and to be content with what He has decreed for us, knowing that He is the All-Knowing and All-Wise.
orig: قل إن ربي يبسط الرزق لمن يشاء ويقدر ولكن أكثر الناس لا يعلمون

translation: And it is not your wealth or your children that bring you nearer to Us in position, but it is [by being] one who has believed and done righteousness. For them there will be the double reward for what they did, and they will be in the upper chambers [of Paradise], safe [and secure].
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that worldly possessions and offspring do not bring a person closer to Allah or earn them a higher status in His sight. Rather, it is sincere faith and righteous deeds that truly matter. Those who believe and do good will be rewarded in multiples for their actions and will reside in the lofty dwellings of Paradise, where they will be safe and secure from any harm or distress. This highlights the importance of focusing on one's spiritual growth and moral conduct, rather than being preoccupied with materialistic pursuits or pride in one's children.
orig: وما أموالكم ولا أولادكم بالتي تقربكم عندنا زلفى إلا من آمن وعمل صالحا فأولئك لهم جزاء الضعف بما عملوا وهم في الغرفات آمنون

translation: But those who strive against Our verses [seeking] to cause failure - those will be brought into the punishment [to remain].
interpretation: This verse is a stern warning to those who actively oppose and seek to undermine the message and signs of Allah. Those who arrogantly strive to discredit or defeat the Qur'an and the proofs of Allah's power will face severe punishment in the Hereafter. They will be brought forth and made to endure the torment as a consequence of their defiant disbelief and hostility towards the truth. It emphasizes that opposing the Qur'an is futile and will only lead to suffering divine retribution, as Allah's word and message will ultimately prevail.
orig: والذين يسعون في آياتنا معاجزين أولئك في العذاب محضرون

translation: Say, "Indeed, my Lord extends provision for whom He wills of His servants and restricts [it] for him. But whatever thing you spend [in His cause] - He will compensate it; and He is the best of providers."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah is the ultimate provider and sustainer. It assures believers that whatever they spend in the way of Allah, whether it be wealth, time, or effort, will be compensated by Him in this world or in the Hereafter. It encourages generosity and selflessness, reminding us that Allah is the best of providers and will never let His servants down. The verse also highlights the concept of divine will, stating that Allah gives provision to whom He wills and restricts it from others according to His wisdom and knowledge. This reinforces the idea of complete trust and reliance on Allah in all matters of life.
orig: قل إن ربي يبسط الرزق لمن يشاء من عباده ويقدر له وما أنفقتم من شيء فهو يخلفه وهو خير الرازقين

translation: And [mention] the Day when He will gather them all together; then He will say to the angels, "Did these [people] used to worship you?"
interpretation: This verse is referring to the Day of Judgment when Allah will gather all of mankind and question the angels about those who used to worship them instead of Allah. It is a reminder that worshipping anyone or anything besides Allah is a grave sin and that ultimately, everyone will be held accountable for their deeds and beliefs. The verse also highlights the fact that the angels, who are often worshipped by some people, are themselves subservient to Allah and will testify against those who wrongly worshipped them.
orig: ويوم يحشرهم جميعا ثم يقول للملائكة أهؤلاء إياكم كانوا يعبدون

translation: They will say, "Exalted are You! You, [O Allah], are our benefactor not them. Rather, they used to worship the jinn; most of them were believers in them."
interpretation: This verse refers to the Day of Judgment when the disbelievers who worshipped false gods and idols will realize their error. They will acknowledge that Allah alone is their true benefactor and that the false gods they worshipped were of no benefit to them. The verse also reveals that many of these disbelievers were actually worshipping the jinn, who had misled them into idolatry and polytheism. This highlights the deceptive nature of the jinn and their ability to lead people astray from the path of true monotheism and worship of Allah alone.
orig: قالوا سبحانك أنت ولينا من دونهم بل كانوا يعبدون الجن أكثرهم بهم مؤمنون

translation: So Today no soul will have power [to do] anything for another soul; and the command, that Day, will be [entirely] with Allah.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the ultimate justice and accountability that will take place on the Day of Judgment. It highlights that on that day, no one will have the power to benefit or harm another person, regardless of their worldly status or relationships. Everyone will be held accountable for their own deeds, and the ultimate decision will rest with Allah alone. The verse also serves as a warning to those who have wronged others, telling them to taste the punishment of the Fire which they used to deny. It is a reminder that the consequences of one's actions in this world will be faced in the Hereafter, and that the ultimate justice will be served by Allah, the All-Knowing and All-Wise.
orig: فاليوم لا يملك بعضكم لبعض نفعا ولا ضرا ونقول للذين ظلموا ذوقوا عذاب النار التي كنتم بها تكذبون

translation: And when Our clear verses are recited to them, they say, "This is not but a man who wishes to avert you from that which your fathers were worshipping." And they say, "This is not except a lie invented." And those who disbelieve say of the truth when it has come to them, "This is not but obvious magic."
interpretation: This verse points to the stubborn disbelief of those who reject the truth of the Qur'an and the message of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him). When they hear the clear verses of the Qur'an, instead of reflecting on their meaning and accepting the truth, they dismiss it as the words of a mere man trying to turn them away from the false beliefs and practices of their ancestors. They accuse the Prophet of inventing lies and label the Qur'an as obvious magic. This highlights their arrogance, closed-mindedness, and unwillingness to accept the truth even when it is clearly presented to them. It shows the depths of their spiritual blindness and attachment to the misguided ways of their forefathers.
orig: وإذا تتلى عليهم آياتنا بينات قالوا ما هذا إلا رجل يريد أن يصدكم عما كان يعبد آباؤكم وقالوا ما هذا إلا إفك مفترى وقال الذين كفروا للحق لما جاءهم إن هذا إلا سحر مبين

translation: And We had not given them any books which they could study, and We had not sent to them before you, [O Muhammad], any warner.
interpretation: This verse highlights the fact that the people to whom Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) was sent had not received any divine books or messengers before him. They were not given any scriptures to study and follow, nor were they warned by any prophet or messenger prior to Muhammad (peace be upon him). This emphasizes the importance and necessity of Muhammad's mission, as he was sent to guide a people who had been left without divine guidance for a long period of time. It also implies that these people would be held accountable for their actions and beliefs only after they had received the message of Islam through Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him), as they had no previous knowledge or warning of the divine message.
orig: وما آتيناهم من كتب يدرسونها وما أرسلنا إليهم قبلك من نذير

translation: Those before them denied, and the people of Makkah have not attained a tenth of what We had given them (of strength and power). Yet they denied My Messengers. Then how (terrible) was My rejection (of them)!
interpretation: This verse is a warning to the disbelievers of Makkah, reminding them of the fate of previous nations who rejected Allah's messengers. Despite being given greater strength and resources than the people of Makkah, those earlier nations still denied the truth and were ultimately destroyed by Allah's punishment. The verse emphasizes the severity of Allah's rejection and the consequences of denying His messengers, implying that the disbelievers of Makkah will face a similar fate if they persist in their disbelief. It serves as a reminder that no matter how powerful or wealthy a nation may be, it is not immune to Allah's judgment if it turns away from His guidance.
orig: وكذب الذين من قبلهم وما بلغوا معشار ما آتيناهم فكذبوا رسلي فكيف كان نكير

translation: Say, "I only advise you of one [thing] - that you stand for Allah, [seeking truth] in pairs and individually, and then give thought." There is not in your companion any madness. He is only a warner to you before a severe punishment.
interpretation: This verse is a call to reflect deeply and sincerely on the message of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him). It urges people to rise above blind following and mob mentality, and instead to ponder individually and in small groups, seeking the truth for the sake of God alone. The verse emphasizes that Prophet Muhammad is not a madman as his detractors claimed, but rather a warner sent by God to alert people of the severe consequences in the Hereafter for those who reject the truth and persist in wrongdoing. It is an invitation to use one's God-given intellect to recognize the veracity of the Prophet's message before it's too late and punishment befalls the deniers.
orig: قل إنما أعظكم بواحدة أن تقوموا لله مثنى وفرادى ثم تتفكروا ما بصاحبكم من جنة إن هو إلا نذير لكم بين يدي عذاب شديد

translation: Say, "Whatever payment I might have asked of you is yours. My payment is only from Allah, and He is, over all things, Witness."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) did not seek any worldly gain or payment from the people for conveying the message of Islam. He made it clear that his reward and compensation come only from Allah, and that Allah is a witness to all things, including the sincerity of the Prophet's intentions and actions. This interpretation highlights the selflessness and devotion of the Prophet in his mission to guide humanity towards the path of righteousness, seeking only the pleasure and reward of Allah.
orig: قل ما سألتكم من أجر فهو لكم إن أجري إلا على الله وهو على كل شيء شهيد

translation: Say, "Indeed, my Lord projects the truth. Knower of the unseen."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the omniscience and omnipotence of Allah. It asserts that Allah is the ultimate source of truth and that He reveals it to His chosen messengers. The phrase "projects the truth" suggests that Allah actively sends down the truth, which can be understood as divine revelation or guidance. Moreover, Allah is described as the "Knower of the unseen," indicating His complete knowledge of all that is hidden from human perception, including the past, present, and future, as well as the innermost thoughts and intentions of His creation. This verse serves as a reminder for believers to trust in Allah's wisdom and to seek His guidance in all aspects of life.
orig: قل إن ربي يقذف بالحق علام الغيوب

translation: Say, "The truth has come, and falsehood can neither begin [anything] nor repeat [it]."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the ultimate triumph of truth over falsehood. It asserts that when the truth arrives, falsehood cannot initiate anything new or even repeat its previous deceptions. The arrival of truth, which can be understood as the message of Islam or the revelation of the Qur'an, renders falsehood powerless and ineffective. This interpretation highlights the idea that the truth, once established, cannot be overshadowed or undermined by false beliefs, practices, or ideologies. It provides reassurance to believers that adherence to the truth will ultimately lead to success and that falsehood, despite its temporary allure, is destined to fade away.
orig: قل جاء الحق وما يبدئ الباطل وما يعيد

translation: Say, "If I have gone astray, I stray only to my own loss. And if I am guided, it is by what my Lord reveals to me. Indeed, He is All-Hearing, All-Near."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the individual responsibility of each person for their own spiritual path. If one goes astray, they alone bear the consequences. However, if one is guided, it is only through Allah's revelation and guidance. The verse also highlights two important attributes of Allah: He is All-Hearing, meaning He is aware of all our prayers and needs, and He is All-Near, signifying His closeness and accessibility to those who seek His guidance. This verse encourages introspection and seeking Allah's guidance while reminding us of His omnipresence and readiness to help those who turn to Him.
orig: قل إن ضللت فإنما أضل على نفسي وإن اهتديت فبما يوحي إلي ربي إنه سميع قريب

translation: And if you could but see when they are terrified, but there is no escape, and they will be seized from a place nearby.
interpretation: This verse is referring to the Day of Judgment when the disbelievers will be seized and punished. They will be in a state of terror and there will be no escape for them from Allah's punishment. The phrase "from a place nearby" could mean that the punishment is very close and there is no way to avoid it. It also suggests that the disbelievers will be taken by surprise, as they were not expecting the punishment to come so suddenly and from so close. This verse serves as a warning to those who reject faith, reminding them that on the Day of Judgment, there will be no escape from the consequences of their actions.
orig: ولو ترى إذ فزعوا فلا فوت وأخذوا من مكان قريب

translation: And they say, "We have believed in it," but how can they reach [it] from a place far away?
interpretation: This verse is referring to the hypocrites who claim to believe in Islam and the Qur'an, but their actions and inner beliefs are far from true faith. The phrase "from a place far away" symbolizes the great distance between their outward claim of belief and their actual spiritual state. It suggests that their faith is superficial and insincere, as they are unable to grasp the true essence and meaning of the message due to their insincerity and the corruption in their hearts. The verse implies that mere verbal affirmation of faith is not enough, and that true belief requires inner conviction, sincerity, and consistency between one's words and actions.
orig: وقالوا آمنا به وأنى لهم التناوش من مكان بعيد

translation: And they had already disbelieved in it before and would assault the unseen from a distant place.
interpretation: This verse refers to the disbelievers who rejected the truth of the Qur'an and the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) even before they had fully understood or considered its message. They made baseless accusations and attacked the unseen realm of divine revelation from a position of ignorance and prejudice, without any genuine knowledge or understanding. This highlights the stubborn and irrational nature of their disbelief, as they were not open to sincerely reflecting upon the Qur'an's teachings and instead resorted to making wild and unfounded claims against it from a distance, without engaging with its actual content or the clear proofs and signs that pointed to its divine origin.
orig: وقد كفروا به من قبل ويقذفون بالغيب من مكان بعيد

translation: And a barrier will be placed between them and what they desire, as was done with their kind before. Indeed, they were in disquieting doubt.
interpretation: This verse speaks about the fate of the disbelievers in the Hereafter. It conveys that a barrier will be placed between them and what they desire, meaning they will be prevented from attaining their wishes and pleasures. This punishment is similar to what befell earlier disbelieving nations. The verse also suggests that these disbelievers were engulfed in deeply unsettling doubts about the truth of the message and the reality of the Hereafter during their worldly lives. Their skepticism and rejection of faith ultimately lead to their unfortunate destiny in the afterlife, where they will be deprived of their desires and face the consequences of their disbelief.
orig: وحيل بينهم وبين ما يشتهون كما فعل بأشياعهم من قبل إنهم كانوا في شك مريب

translation: All praise is due to Allah, Creator of the heavens and the earth, [who] made the angels messengers having wings, two or three or four. He increases in creation what He wills. Indeed, Allah is over all things competent.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's power and sovereignty over all creation. It highlights that Allah is the sole Creator of the heavens and the earth, and everything within them. The mention of angels having varying numbers of wings symbolizes the diversity and complexity in Allah's creation. The verse also affirms that Allah can increase His creation in any way He wills, reflecting His absolute power and control over the universe. It concludes by asserting that Allah is capable of all things, reminding us of His omnipotence and the vastness of His abilities. This verse instills a sense of awe and reverence for Allah's magnificence and encourages humility and submission to His will.
orig: الحمد لله فاطر السماوات والأرض جاعل الملائكة رسلا أولي أجنحة مثنى وثلاث ورباع يزيد في الخلق ما يشاء إن الله على كل شيء قدير

translation: Whatever mercy Allah opens for the people, none can withhold it; and whatever He withholds, none can release it thereafter. And He is the Exalted in Might, the Wise.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's absolute control and power over His mercy and blessings. It states that when Allah decides to bestow His mercy upon people, no one can prevent or stop it from reaching them. Conversely, if Allah decides to withhold His mercy, no one can release or grant it to people after Him. This highlights the fact that Allah is the ultimate source of all mercy and blessings, and He alone has the power to give or withhold them according to His wisdom and judgment. The verse also affirms two of Allah's attributes: Al-Azeez (the Exalted in Might) and Al-Hakeem (the Wise), indicating that His decisions and actions are based on His perfect wisdom and unparalleled might.
orig: ما يفتح الله للناس من رحمة فلا ممسك لها وما يمسك فلا مرسل له من بعده وهو العزيز الحكيم

translation: O mankind, remember the favor of Allah upon you. Is there any creator other than Allah who provides for you from the heaven and earth? There is no deity except Him, so how are you deluded?
interpretation: This verse is a reminder to humanity to be grateful for the blessings and favors bestowed upon them by Allah. It emphasizes that Allah is the sole creator and sustainer of the universe, providing for all of His creation from the heavens and the earth. The verse questions the existence of any other deity worthy of worship besides Allah, as He alone possesses the power to create and provide. It also admonishes those who are deluded by false beliefs or ingratitude, urging them to recognize and appreciate the bounties of their Lord. This verse underscores the importance of monotheism and gratitude in the Islamic faith.
orig: يا أيها الناس اذكروا نعمت الله عليكم هل من خالق غير الله يرزقكم من السماء والأرض لا إله إلا هو فأنى تؤفكون

translation: And if they deny you, [O Muhammad], so were messengers denied before you. And to Allah are returned [all] matters.
interpretation: This verse is a consolation to Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him), reminding him that he is not the first prophet to face rejection and denial from his people. Many prophets before him, such as Noah, Abraham, Moses, and Jesus, faced similar challenges and opposition from their communities. The verse emphasizes that the ultimate outcome of all affairs, including the fate of those who reject the message, rests with Allah. It encourages the Prophet to remain steadfast in his mission and trust in Allah's plan, knowing that the truth will ultimately prevail, and that the deniers will be held accountable for their actions in the Hereafter.
orig: وإن يكذبوك فقد كذبت رسل من قبلك وإلى الله ترجع الأمور

translation: O mankind, indeed the promise of Allah is truth, so let not the worldly life delude you and be not deceived about Allah by the Deceiver.
interpretation: This verse is a reminder and warning to all of humanity that the promise of Allah - resurrection, judgment, and the eternal life of the Hereafter - is absolutely true and will come to pass. Therefore, one should not be deluded and distracted by the temporary and fleeting nature of the worldly life and its pleasures, causing them to forget or disregard their ultimate purpose and destination. Additionally, one should be cautious not to fall prey to the deceptions and temptations of Satan, who constantly tries to lead people astray from the path of Allah and righteousness. The verse emphasizes the importance of maintaining focus on one's spiritual goals, remaining steadfast in faith, and not being misled by worldly distractions or the deceits of the Devil.
orig: يا أيها الناس إن وعد الله حق فلا تغرنكم الحياة الدنيا ولا يغرنكم بالله الغرور

translation: Indeed, Satan is an enemy to you; so take him as an enemy. He only invites his party to be among the companions of the Blaze.
interpretation: This verse warns believers that Satan is their clear enemy, who constantly tries to lead them astray from the righteous path. It emphasizes the importance of recognizing Satan's enmity and being vigilant against his temptations and whispers. The verse also highlights the ultimate fate of those who follow Satan and his party - they will be among the companions of the Blazing Fire in Hell. This serves as a strong reminder for believers to stay away from Satan's path and to strive for righteousness and obedience to Allah in order to attain salvation and avoid the severe punishment of the Hereafter.
orig: إن الشيطان لكم عدو فاتخذوه عدوا إنما يدعو حزبه ليكونوا من أصحاب السعير

translation: Those who disbelieve will have a severe punishment, and those who believe and do righteous deeds will have forgiveness and great reward.
interpretation: This verse highlights the fundamental difference in the ultimate fate of those who reject faith in God and those who sincerely believe and act righteously. It emphasizes that disbelievers will face a severe punishment in the Hereafter for their ingratitude and denial of the truth. In contrast, those who combine genuine faith with good deeds will be granted God's forgiveness for their shortcomings and will be rewarded generously in the Hereafter. This interpretation underscores the importance of faith and righteous actions in attaining salvation and God's pleasure, while warning against the grave consequences of disbelief.
orig: الذين كفروا لهم عذاب شديد والذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات لهم مغفرة وأجر كبير

translation: Then is one to whom the evil of his deed has been made attractive so he considers it good [like one rightly guided]? For indeed, Allah sends astray whom He wills and guides whom He wills. So do not let yourself perish over them in regret. Indeed, Allah is Knowing of what they do.
interpretation: This verse highlights that people can be deceived by their own evil actions, seeing them as good due to their distorted perception. It emphasizes that guidance and misguidance are ultimately in Allah's hands. The Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) is consoled and advised not to grieve excessively over those who persist in wrongdoing and disbelief, as Allah is fully aware of their actions and will deal with them accordingly in the Hereafter. The verse underscores the importance of seeking Allah's guidance and not being misled by the apparent attractiveness of sinful deeds.
orig: أفمن زين له سوء عمله فرآه حسنا فإن الله يضل من يشاء ويهدي من يشاء فلا تذهب نفسك عليهم حسرات إن الله عليم بما يصنعون

translation: And it is Allah who sends the winds, and they stir the clouds, and We drive them to a dead land and give life thereby to the earth after its lifelessness. Thus is the resurrection.
interpretation: This verse is a reminder of Allah's power and ability to bring life from death. Just as Allah sends the winds to stir up clouds and bring rain to a barren land, giving it new life, He is also capable of resurrecting the dead on the Day of Judgment. This metaphor emphasizes the idea that just as the dead earth can be revived by rain, our bodies will be revived and resurrected by Allah's power. It is a message of hope and a call to believe in the afterlife and the accountability for our deeds in this world.
orig: والله الذي أرسل الرياح فتثير سحابا فسقناه إلى بلد ميت فأحيينا به الأرض بعد موتها كذلك النشور

translation: Whoever desires honor [through power] - then to Allah belongs all honor. To Him ascends good speech, and righteous work raises it. But they who plot evil deeds will have a severe punishment, and the plotting of those - it will perish.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that true honor and power belong to Allah alone. Good words and righteous deeds are what elevate a person's status in the sight of Allah. On the other hand, those who plot evil will face severe consequences, and their schemes will ultimately fail. It serves as a reminder that seeking honor through worldly means is futile, and that one should instead focus on pleasing Allah through virtuous speech and actions.
orig: من كان يريد العزة فلله العزة جميعا إليه يصعد الكلم الطيب والعمل الصالح يرفعه والذين يمكرون السيئات لهم عذاب شديد ومكر أولئك هو يبور

translation: And Allah created you from dust, then from a sperm-drop; then He made you mates. And no female conceives nor does she give birth except with His knowledge. And no aged person is granted [additional] life nor is his lifespan lessened but that it is in a register. Indeed, that for Allah is easy.
interpretation: This verse highlights Allah's power and knowledge over the creation and life cycle of human beings. It emphasizes that every stage of human existence, from conception to birth to aging and death, occurs only by the will and knowledge of Allah. The verse also affirms that the lifespan of each individual is predetermined and recorded in a divine register, and that altering or extending one's life is entirely within Allah's control and is easy for Him. This serves as a reminder for humans to recognize their own limitations and to submit to the supreme authority and wisdom of their Creator.
orig: والله خلقكم من تراب ثم من نطفة ثم جعلكم أزواجا وما تحمل من أنثى ولا تضع إلا بعلمه وما يعمر من معمر ولا ينقص من عمره إلا في كتاب إن ذلك على الله يسير

translation: And not alike are the two seas [i.e., bodies of water]. One is fresh and sweet, palatable for drinking, and one is salty and bitter. And from each you eat tender meat and extract ornaments which you wear, and you see the ships plowing through [them] that you might seek of His bounty; and perhaps you will be grateful.
interpretation: This verse highlights the power and wisdom of Allah in creating different types of water bodies, each with its unique characteristics and benefits for mankind. It reminds us to be grateful for the blessings that Allah has bestowed upon us, such as the provision of fresh water for drinking and the abundance of seafood and pearls from the oceans. The mention of ships plowing through the seas also points to the opportunities for trade and commerce that Allah has made possible through His bounty. Ultimately, the verse encourages us to reflect on these signs and express gratitude to Allah for His favors.
orig: وما يستوي البحران هذا عذب فرات سائغ شرابه وهذا ملح أجاج ومن كل تأكلون لحما طريا وتستخرجون حلية تلبسونها وترى الفلك فيه مواخر لتبتغوا من فضله ولعلكم تشكرون

translation: He causes the night to enter the day, and He causes the day to enter the night and has subjected the sun and the moon - each running [its course] for a specified term. That is Allah, your Lord; to Him belongs sovereignty. And those whom you invoke other than Him do not possess [as much as] the membrane of a date seed.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's absolute power and control over the universe. The alternation of night and day, and the precise movements of the sun and moon, are all under His command. These celestial bodies follow a predetermined course set by Allah until a specified time. The verse also affirms that Allah alone is the true sovereign and owner of all things. In contrast, the false deities that people invoke besides Him have no power or possession, not even something as insignificant as the thin membrane covering a date seed. This highlights the futility of worshipping anyone or anything other than Allah, as they are powerless and do not deserve any form of devotion or attribution of divinity.
orig: يولج الليل في النهار ويولج النهار في الليل وسخر الشمس والقمر كل يجري لأجل مسمى ذلكم الله ربكم له الملك والذين تدعون من دونه ما يملكون من قطمير

translation: If you invoke them, they do not hear your supplication; and if they heard, they would not respond to you. And on the Day of Resurrection they will deny your association. And none can inform you like [one] Acquainted [with all matters].
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the futility of worshipping false deities or idols. These false gods are unable to hear the supplications of their worshippers, and even if they could hear, they would be incapable of responding or providing any assistance. On the Day of Judgment, these false deities will disassociate themselves from their worshippers, denying any claim of partnership with Allah. The verse concludes by stating that no one can inform mankind about the reality of this matter better than Allah Himself, who is the All-Knowing and All-Aware.
orig: إن تدعوهم لا يسمعوا دعاءكم ولو سمعوا ما استجابوا لكم ويوم القيامة يكفرون بشرككم ولا ينبئك مثل خبير

translation: O mankind, you are those in need of Allah, while Allah is the Free of need, the Praiseworthy.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the fundamental relationship between God and human beings. It reminds us that we are all inherently dependent on God for our existence, sustenance, and well-being. No matter how self-sufficient or powerful we may feel, we ultimately rely on God's grace and mercy. On the other hand, God is completely self-sufficient and free from any need or dependency. He is the One who provides for His creation and is worthy of all praise. This verse encourages humility and gratitude towards God, recognizing our own limitations and His infinite power and generosity.
orig: يا أيها الناس أنتم الفقراء إلى الله والله هو الغني الحميد

translation: If He wills, He can do away with you and bring forth a new creation.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute power and authority of Allah over His creation. It reminds us that our existence is entirely dependent on His will. If He so desires, He can easily eliminate us and replace us with a new creation. This highlights the temporary and fragile nature of our lives in this world, and encourages us to be humble, grateful, and obedient to our Creator. It also warns against arrogance and the false belief that we are self-sufficient or immortal. Ultimately, this verse is a call to submit to Allah's will and recognize His supreme control over all things.
orig: إن يشأ يذهبكم ويأت بخلق جديد

translation: And that is not difficult for Allah.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the omnipotence and boundless power of Allah. It conveys the idea that nothing is beyond His capabilities or too difficult for Him to accomplish. Whether it pertains to the creation of the universe, the resurrection of the dead, or any other matter, Allah has the absolute ability to bring it into being effortlessly. This verse serves as a reminder to humans of Allah's supreme authority and control over all things, encouraging believers to put their trust in His will and recognize His limitless might.
orig: وما ذلك على الله بعزيز

translation: And no bearer of burdens will bear the burden of another. And if a heavily laden soul calls [another] to [carry some of] its load, nothing of it will be carried, even if he should be a close relative. You can only warn those who fear their Lord unseen and have established prayer. And whoever purifies himself only purifies himself for [the benefit of] his soul. And to Allah is the [final] destination.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the concept of individual responsibility in Islam. Each person is accountable for their own actions and will bear the consequences of their deeds. No one can carry the burden of another's sins, even if they are closely related. The only people who will heed the warning and benefit from it are those who fear Allah without seeing Him and establish prayer. Purifying oneself from sin is ultimately for one's own benefit, as everyone will return to Allah for judgment in the end.
orig: ولا تزر وازرة وزر أخرى وإن تدع مثقلة إلى حملها لا يحمل منه شيء ولو كان ذا قربى إنما تنذر الذين يخشون ربهم بالغيب وأقاموا الصلاة ومن تزكى فإنما يتزكى لنفسه وإلى الله المصير

translation: Not equal are the blind and the seeing.
interpretation: This verse is drawing a contrast between those who are spiritually blind, unable to perceive the truth and guidance of Allah, and those who have spiritual insight and can see the right path. It emphasizes that there is a clear distinction between those who are guided by faith and those who are lost in disbelief. The "blind" here symbolizes those who are ignorant of divine revelation and fail to recognize the signs of Allah's existence and unity, while the "seeing" represents those who have embraced the truth of Islam and live their lives according to Allah's commandments. The verse implies that the two groups are not equal in the sight of Allah and will face different consequences in the Hereafter based on their spiritual status.
orig: وما يستوي الأعمى والبصير

translation: Nor the darkness, nor the light.
interpretation: This verse is drawing a contrast between darkness and light, which are often used metaphorically in the Qur'an to represent evil and good, disbelief and faith, or ignorance and knowledge. The verse emphasizes that Allah is the creator of both darkness and light, and that both are under His control and serve His purposes. It reminds us that just as we cannot equate darkness with light, we cannot equate falsehood with truth, or evil with good. Rather, we must strive to follow the light of Allah's guidance and avoid the darkness of ignorance and disbelief.
orig: ولا الظلمات ولا النور

translation: Neither the shade nor the heat
interpretation: This verse is likely referring to the idea that in the afterlife, the righteous will be protected from both the scorching heat of the sun and the bitter cold of the shade. It emphasizes that in Paradise, believers will experience perfect comfort, without any of the hardships or unpleasant extremes of temperature that are experienced in this worldly life. The verse serves as a reminder of the rewards that await those who follow the path of righteousness and strive to please Allah in this life.
orig: ولا الظل ولا الحرور

translation: And not equal are the living and the dead. Indeed, Allah causes to hear whom He wills, but you cannot make hear those in the graves.
interpretation: This verse highlights the fundamental difference between those who are spiritually alive and receptive to God's message, and those who are spiritually dead and unable to benefit from divine guidance. It emphasizes that it is Allah who grants the ability to truly hear and understand His words, and that no one, not even the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him), can make those who are spiritually dead in their graves (i.e., those who have died in a state of disbelief or heedlessness) hear or benefit from the truth. This serves as a reminder that guidance is ultimately in the hands of Allah and that the role of the Prophet and believers is to convey the message, while the response and acceptance of that message is up to each individual soul, based on Allah's will and their own choices.
orig: وما يستوي الأحياء ولا الأموات إن الله يسمع من يشاء وما أنت بمسمع من في القبور

translation: You are not but a warner.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the Prophet Muhammad's role is to serve as a warner to humanity, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the importance of following the right path. He is not responsible for guiding people or forcing them to believe, as that is ultimately in the hands of Allah. The Prophet's duty is to convey the message clearly and to advise people to be mindful of their deeds, while the choice to accept or reject the message lies with each individual.
orig: إن أنت إلا نذير

translation: Indeed, We have sent you with the truth as a bringer of good tidings and a warner. And there was no nation but that there had passed within it a warner.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the universality of Allah's message and the role of prophets throughout human history. The Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) was sent as a messenger to convey the truth, bringing glad tidings to those who believe and follow the right path, and warning those who reject the message of the consequences of their actions. The verse also states that every nation in the past had received a warner, a prophet or messenger, to guide them to the straight path. This highlights the mercy and justice of Allah, as He has never left humanity without guidance. It also serves as a reminder that the message of Islam is not new, but rather a continuation and culmination of the messages sent to previous prophets.
