orig: إنا أرسلناك بالحق بشيرا ونذيرا وإن من أمة إلا خلا فيها نذير

translation: And if they deny you, [O Muhammad], so were messengers denied before you. They came with clear proofs and written ordinances and the enlightening Scripture.
interpretation: This verse is a consolation to Prophet Muhammad, reminding him that even if his people reject his message, he is not alone in facing such rejection. Many prophets before him, such as Noah, Abraham, Moses, and Jesus, were also denied by their people, despite coming with clear signs, scriptures, and enlightenment from Allah. The verse encourages the Prophet to remain steadfast in conveying the message, as the ultimate fate of those who reject it rests with Allah. It also serves as a reminder to the believers that facing opposition and rejection is a natural part of the prophetic mission, and they should not be disheartened by it, but rather remain firm in their faith and continue to follow the guidance of the Prophet.
orig: وإن يكذبوك فقد كذب الذين من قبلهم جاءتهم رسلهم بالبينات وبالزبر وبالكتاب المنير

translation: Then I seized the ones who disbelieved, and how [terrible] was My reproach.
interpretation: This verse is a stern warning from Allah to those who reject His message and persist in disbelief. It emphasizes the severity and terribleness of Allah's punishment for those who choose to disbelieve, despite the clear signs and warnings sent to them. The verse implies that the disbelievers were first given respite and time to mend their ways, but when they failed to do so, Allah seized them with a mighty punishment. The rhetorical question "and how [terrible] was My reproach" serves to underscore the gravity and intensity of Allah's wrath towards the disbelievers, and acts as a reminder to all of the consequences of rejecting faith.
orig: ثم أخذت الذين كفروا فكيف كان نكير

translation: Do you not see that Allah sends down rain from the sky, and We produce thereby fruits of varying colors? And in the mountains are tracts, white and red of varying shades and [some] extremely black.
interpretation: This verse is a reminder of Allah's power and creativity. The rain that Allah sends down from the sky is a source of life and sustenance for all living things on earth. It causes the growth of fruits of various colors, each with its own unique taste and nutritional value. Similarly, the mountains are adorned with different colored tracts, ranging from white to red to black. These variations in color and shade are a testament to Allah's artistic mastery and attention to detail in His creation. The verse encourages us to reflect on the beauty and diversity of nature, and to appreciate the countless blessings that Allah has bestowed upon us. It also serves as a reminder that just as Allah can create such a vast array of colors and shades in fruits and mountains, He can also create diversity among human beings, each with their own unique qualities and characteristics.
orig: ألم تر أن الله أنزل من السماء ماء فأخرجنا به ثمرات مختلفا ألوانها ومن الجبال جدد بيض وحمر مختلف ألوانها وغرابيب سود

translation: And among people and moving creatures and grazing livestock are various colors similarly. Only those fear Allah, from among His servants, who have knowledge. Indeed, Allah is Exalted in Might and Forgiving.
interpretation: This verse highlights that it is those who have true knowledge and understanding who fear Allah the most. They recognize the signs of Allah's power and creativity in the diversity of His creation, in the varying colors and forms of people, animals and livestock. The scholars and learned ones humbly submit to Allah out of profound reverence, knowing His Might and Greatness. At the same time, they pin their hopes on His forgiveness and mercy. Thus, knowledge strengthens faith and increases one in piety and righteous conduct. The more one comprehends about Allah, the more one is in awe of Him and fears disobeying Him.
orig: ومن الناس والدواب والأنعام مختلف ألوانه كذلك إنما يخشى الله من عباده العلماء إن الله عزيز غفور

translation: Indeed, those who recite the Book of Allah and establish prayer and spend [in His cause] out of what We have provided them, secretly and publicly, [can] expect a profit that will never perish
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of reciting the Qur'an, establishing regular prayer, and spending in charity both privately and publicly. It emphasizes that those who engage in these righteous deeds with sincerity and consistency can expect a reward from Allah that will never diminish or fade away. The "profit that will never perish" refers to the eternal rewards and blessings in the Hereafter, which are far superior to any temporary worldly gains. This interpretation underscores the significance of these fundamental acts of worship and their role in securing a believer's success and happiness in both this life and the next.
orig: إن الذين يتلون كتاب الله وأقاموا الصلاة وأنفقوا مما رزقناهم سرا وعلانية يرجون تجارة لن تبور

translation: That He may give them in full their rewards and increase for them of His bounty. Indeed, He is Forgiving and Appreciative.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's generosity and mercy towards His servants. He not only grants them the full reward for their good deeds but also increases it out of His boundless grace. This highlights the immense value of doing righteous acts, as even a small deed can lead to a significant reward from Allah. Moreover, the mention of Allah's attributes of forgiveness and appreciation underscores His readiness to pardon His servants' shortcomings and acknowledge their efforts, further motivating them to strive in His cause. The verse thus serves as a powerful reminder of Allah's infinite kindness and the importance of seeking His pleasure through continuous good deeds.
orig: ليوفيهم أجورهم ويزيدهم من فضله إنه غفور شكور

translation: And that which We have revealed to you of the Book is the truth, confirming what was before it. Indeed, Allah, of His servants, is Acquainted and Seeing.
interpretation: This verse affirms the authenticity and truthfulness of the Qur'an revealed to Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him). It asserts that the Qur'an confirms and supports the divine messages that came before it, such as the Torah and the Gospel. The verse also emphasizes Allah's omniscience and all-seeing nature, indicating that He is fully aware of His servants' actions, intentions, and beliefs. This interpretation highlights the Qur'an's role as a continuation and validation of the previous revelations while underscoring Allah's complete knowledge and insight concerning His creation.
orig: والذي أوحينا إليك من الكتاب هو الحق مصدقا لما بين يديه إن الله بعباده لخبير بصير

translation: Then We gave the Book as an inheritance to those We have chosen from among Our servants. Some of them wrong themselves, some follow a middle course, and some are foremost in good deeds by Allah's Leave. That is the greatest bounty.
interpretation: This verse highlights the different categories of people in relation to their faith and deeds. After revealing the divine message through the prophets, Allah has chosen certain individuals among His servants to inherit the Book, i.e., to preserve, follow, and convey its teachings. However, these chosen people are not all alike in their adherence to the Book's guidance. Some of them wrong themselves by neglecting their duties or committing sins, while others follow a moderate path, fulfilling their obligations without going above and beyond. The third group, however, is foremost in performing good deeds and acts of devotion, striving to excel in virtue by Allah's permission and grace. This last group is the most praiseworthy, as they have attained the greatest bounty from Allah by utilizing the Book's guidance to the fullest extent.
orig: ثم أورثنا الكتاب الذين اصطفينا من عبادنا فمنهم ظالم لنفسه ومنهم مقتصد ومنهم سابق بالخيرات بإذن الله ذلك هو الفضل الكبير

translation: Gardens of perpetual residence; they will enter them wearing [bracelets of] gold and pearls, and their garments therein will be silk.
interpretation: This verse refers to the rewards that await the righteous believers in Paradise. The "Gardens of perpetual residence" denote that they will abide there eternally, never having to leave. The mention of gold bracelets, pearls, and silk garments symbolizes the luxuries and pleasures they will enjoy in the Hereafter as a reward for their faith and good deeds in this world. These are not mere worldly adornments, but represent the ultimate bliss and satisfaction that the believers will experience in the presence of Allah, free from any imperfections or negative aspects associated with the fleeting nature of worldly luxuries.
orig: جنات عدن يدخلونها يحلون فيها من أساور من ذهب ولؤلؤا ولباسهم فيها حرير

translation: And they will say, "Praise be to Allah, who has removed from us [all] sorrow. Indeed, our Lord is Forgiving and Appreciative.
interpretation: This verse speaks about the people of Paradise and their gratitude towards Allah. They praise Him for removing all their sorrows and worries, acknowledging that He is the One who forgives their sins and appreciates their good deeds. It shows the immense relief and joy they feel in the eternal bliss of Paradise, realizing that all their earthly struggles and hardships have been lifted by the mercy of their Lord. The verse emphasizes Allah's attributes of forgiveness and appreciation, indicating that He not only pardons His servants' shortcomings but also rewards them abundantly for their righteousness.
orig: وقالوا الحمد لله الذي أذهب عنا الحزن إن ربنا لغفور شكور

translation: Who, out of His Bounty, has settled us in a Home that abides forever, where no toil touches us, nor yet weariness affects us.
interpretation: This verse speaks of the eternal bliss and comfort that the righteous will experience in Paradise. It emphasizes that this is a gift from Allah's grace and bounty, not something earned through their own efforts. In this abode of permanence, the believers will be free from all forms of fatigue, hardship, and weariness that are part of the human condition in this worldly life. It points to the perfection and completeness of the joy and peace that the inhabitants of Paradise will experience eternally, as a reward for their faith and good deeds.
orig: الذي أحلنا دار المقامة من فضله لا يمسنا فيها نصب ولا يمسنا فيها لغوب

translation: And for those who disbelieve will be the fire of Hell. [Death] is not decreed for them so they may die, nor will its torment be lightened for them. Thus do we recompense every ungrateful one.
interpretation: This verse speaks about the punishment that awaits disbelievers in the Hereafter. Those who reject faith will be consigned to the Fire of Hell, where they will neither be granted death to be relieved of the torment, nor will the punishment be lightened for them. This is how Allah will requite every ungrateful soul who denied His signs and revelations in this world. The verse emphasizes the severity and eternality of the punishment, as a consequence of the disbelievers' ingratitude and rejection of the truth.
orig: والذين كفروا لهم نار جهنم لا يقضى عليهم فيموتوا ولا يخفف عنهم من عذابها كذلك نجزي كل كفور

translation: And they will cry therein, "Our Lord, remove us; we will do righteousness - other than what we were doing!" But did We not grant you life enough for whoever would remember therein to remember, and the warner had come to you? So taste [the punishment], for there is not for the wrongdoers any helper.
interpretation: This verse is a stark reminder of the consequences of rejecting the truth and the messengers sent by Allah. The people in Hell will plead for another chance to do good deeds, but it will be too late. Allah reminds them that they were given ample time in their worldly life to heed the warnings and follow the right path. The verse emphasizes the importance of making the most of the time we have in this world to do good and avoid wrongdoing, for once death comes, there will be no more chances. It also highlights the justice of Allah, as He does not punish anyone without first sending them clear warnings through His messengers. The verse ends with a severe warning to the wrongdoers that they will have no helpers or saviors in the Hereafter, and they will taste the consequences of their actions.
orig: وهم يصطرخون فيها ربنا أخرجنا نعمل صالحا غير الذي كنا نعمل أولم نعمركم ما يتذكر فيه من تذكر وجاءكم النذير فذوقوا فما للظالمين من نصير

translation: Indeed, Allah is the Knower of the unseen of the heavens and the earth. Indeed, He is Knowing of that within the breasts.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the all-encompassing knowledge of Allah. He is not only aware of what is apparent in the heavens and the earth, but also knows the innermost secrets hidden within the hearts of people. It highlights that nothing is concealed from Allah, be it the vast expanse of the universe or the intimate thoughts and intentions of individuals. This understanding should instill a sense of consciousness and sincerity in believers, as they realize that Allah is fully aware of their actions, intentions, and innermost feelings, even if they may be hidden from others.
orig: إن الله عالم غيب السماوات والأرض إنه عليم بذات الصدور

translation: It is He who has made you successors upon the earth. And whoever disbelieves - upon him will be [the consequence of] his disbelief. And the disbelief of the disbelievers does not increase them in the sight of their Lord except in hatred; and the disbelief of the disbelievers does not increase them except in loss.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the responsibility that comes with being God's vicegerents on earth. Those who reject faith and disbelieve will bear the consequences of their own actions. Their disbelief only increases God's displeasure with them and leads them to further loss and ruin, both in this world and the next. The repetition of the phrase "the disbelief of the disbelievers" underscores the severity and gravity of rejecting faith in God. Ultimately, disbelief is a losing proposition that harms none but the disbelievers themselves.
orig: هو الذي جعلكم خلائف في الأرض فمن كفر فعليه كفره ولا يزيد الكافرين كفرهم عند ربهم إلا مقتا ولا يزيد الكافرين كفرهم إلا خسارا

translation: Say, "Have you considered your partners whom you invoke besides Allah? Show me what they have created from the earth, or have they partnership [with Him] in the heavens? Or have We given them a book so they are [standing] on evidence therefrom? [No], rather, the wrongdoers do not promise each other except delusion."
interpretation: This verse challenges the idolaters to reflect upon the powerlessness and ineffectuality of their false gods. It asks them to consider whether these idols have created anything on earth or have any share in the creation of the heavens. It also questions whether these idolaters have received any divine scripture that validates their idolatrous beliefs and practices. The verse asserts that they have no such evidence and that the promises made by the wrongdoers to each other are nothing but delusion and deception. It emphasizes that only Allah is the true Creator and that worshipping others besides Him is baseless and futile.
orig: قل أرأيتم شركاءكم الذين تدعون من دون الله أروني ماذا خلقوا من الأرض أم لهم شرك في السماوات أم آتيناهم كتابا فهم على بينت منه بل إن يعد الظالمون بعضهم بعضا إلا غرورا

translation: Indeed, Allah holds the heavens and the earth, lest they cease. And if they should cease, no one could hold them [in place] after Him. Indeed, He is Forbearing and Forgiving.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the immense power and control of Allah over the universe. He alone sustains the heavens and the earth, preventing them from falling out of balance or collapsing. If Allah were to withdraw His support, no one else could possibly maintain the order and stability of the cosmos. This verse also highlights two of Allah's attributes: His forbearance (hilm) and forgiveness (ghafoor). Despite the sins and disobedience of His creatures, Allah continues to maintain the universe and show mercy to His creation. This should inspire gratitude and awe in the hearts of believers, knowing that their existence depends entirely on the will and power of their Creator.
orig: إن الله يمسك السماوات والأرض أن تزولا ولئن زالتا إن أمسكهما من أحد من بعده إنه كان حليما غفورا

translation: And they swore by Allah their strongest oaths that if a warner came to them, they would be more guided than [any] one of the [previous] nations. But when a warner came to them, it did not increase them except in aversion.
interpretation: This verse highlights the hypocrisy and arrogance of those who rejected the message of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him). Despite their earlier claims that they would follow the guidance if a warner came to them, when the Prophet actually arrived with the message of Islam, they turned away in aversion and rejection. This demonstrates that their earlier oaths were insincere and that their hearts were hardened against the truth. It serves as a warning to all people to be sincere in their search for guidance and to humble themselves before the truth when it comes to them, rather than arrogantly rejecting it out of pride or stubbornness.
orig: وأقسموا بالله جهد أيمانهم لئن جاءهم نذير ليكونن أهدى من إحدى الأمم فلما جاءهم نذير ما زادهم إلا نفورا

translation: In arrogance in the land and plotting of evil; but the evil plot does not encompass except its own people. Then do they await except the way of the former peoples? But you will never find in the way of Allah any change, and you will never find in the way of Allah any alteration.
interpretation: This verse warns against arrogance and evil plotting, stating that such plots will only backfire on those who devise them. It reminds us that the fate of those who engage in such behavior will be the same as that of previous nations who were punished for their misdeeds. The verse emphasizes the immutability of Allah's laws and the consequences of going against them, suggesting that no one can escape the divine justice and that the only way to avoid such a fate is to adhere to the righteous path ordained by Allah.
orig: استكبارا في الأرض ومكر السيئ ولا يحيق المكر السيئ إلا بأهله فهل ينظرون إلا سنت الأولين فلن تجد لسنت الله تبديلا ولن تجد لسنت الله تحويلا

translation: Have they not traveled through the land and observed how was the end of those before them, and they were greater than them in power? But Allah is not to be caused failure by anything in the heavens or on the earth. Indeed, He is ever Knowing and Competent.
interpretation: This verse is a reminder for people to reflect on the fate of previous nations who, despite their greater strength and power, were ultimately destroyed by Allah due to their disobedience and wrongdoings. It emphasizes that nothing in the universe can overpower or defeat Allah, as He possesses infinite knowledge and ability. The verse encourages individuals to learn from history and recognize the consequences of going against Allah's teachings, serving as a warning to stay on the righteous path and submit to the will of the Almighty.
orig: أولم يسيروا في الأرض فينظروا كيف كان عاقبة الذين من قبلهم وكانوا أشد منهم قوة وما كان الله ليعجزه من شيء في السماوات ولا في الأرض إنه كان عليما قديرا

translation: And if Allah were to impose blame on the people for what they have earned, He would not leave upon the earth any creature. But He defers them for a specified term. And when their time comes, then indeed Allah has ever been, of His servants, Seeing.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's mercy and forbearance towards His creation. If He were to punish people immediately for their misdeeds, no living being would survive on earth. However, in His infinite wisdom, He gives respite to people until an appointed time. This allows them the opportunity to repent and mend their ways. The verse also underscores Allah's omniscience; He is fully aware of all the deeds of His servants and will hold them accountable at the appropriate time. It serves as a reminder for humans to be conscious of their actions and to seek forgiveness before their time runs out.
orig: ولو يؤاخذ الله الناس بما كسبوا ما ترك على ظهرها من دابة ولكن يؤخرهم إلى أجل مسمى فإذا جاء أجلهم فإن الله كان بعباده بصيرا

translation: Ya Seen.
interpretation: This verse consists of two Arabic letters, "Ya" and "Seen". There are various interpretations regarding the meaning and significance of these disjoined letters. One interpretation is that they are among the "Muqatta'at", or mysterious letters, found at the beginning of several chapters in the Qur'an. The exact meaning of these letters is known only to Allah, but they are believed to carry deep spiritual significance and serve as a reminder of the divine origin of the Qur'an. Some scholars suggest that these letters also draw attention to the importance of the chapter and invite the reader to reflect deeply upon its content.
orig: يس

translation: By the Qur'an, full of wisdom.
interpretation: This verse is an oath by Allah swearing by the Qur'an, which is full of wisdom, guidance, and profound insights. It emphasizes the greatness, nobility and inimitable nature of the Qur'an. The Qur'an is described as "Al-Hakeem" which means wise, judicious and full of wisdom in its content, message, laws and teachings. This highlights that the Qur'an is not just a book, but divine revelation from the All-Wise, containing what is best for humanity's wellbeing and success in this life and the next.
orig: والقرآن الحكيم

translation: Indeed, you are one of the messengers.
interpretation: This verse affirms the prophethood of Muhammad (peace be upon him), assuring him that he is truly one of the messengers sent by Allah to guide humanity. It serves as a confirmation of his divine mission and a reassurance that he is following the path of the previous prophets who were chosen by Allah to convey His message. This verse also implies that Muhammad (peace be upon him) possesses the qualities and characteristics of a true messenger, such as sincerity, trustworthiness, and devotion to delivering Allah's message to the people.
orig: إنك لمن المرسلين

translation: On a straight path.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of staying on the righteous path that leads to Allah's pleasure and paradise. It is a reminder for believers to remain steadfast in their faith, follow the teachings of Islam, and avoid deviating from the straight path. The verse encourages Muslims to lead a life guided by the principles of the Qur'an and the example set by Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him), as this is the only way to attain success and salvation in this world and the hereafter.
orig: على صراط مستقيم

translation: A revelation from the Exalted in Might, the Merciful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the Qur'an is a revelation from Allah, who is described as the Exalted in Might and the Merciful. The use of these two attributes highlights Allah's power and authority, as well as His compassion and mercy towards His creation. It serves as a reminder to the believers that the Qur'an is a divine message that should be respected, contemplated, and followed, as it comes from the One who is both Almighty and Merciful.
orig: تنزيل العزيز الرحيم

translation: That you may warn a people whose forefathers were not warned, so they are unaware.
interpretation: The purpose of the revelation of the Qur'an and the mission of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) is to warn and remind people who have become heedless of the message of God due to the long period of time that has passed since the previous prophets. Their ancestors were not warned, and as a result, the current generation has become negligent and unaware of the truth. This verse emphasizes the importance of the prophetic mission in awakening people's hearts and minds to the reality of their existence and the purpose of their life, which is to worship God and follow His guidance. It also highlights the mercy of God in sending a new messenger to guide humanity back to the straight path.
orig: لتنذر قوما ما أنذر آباؤهم فهم غافلون

translation: Already the word has come into effect upon most of them, so they do not believe.
interpretation: This verse suggests that Allah has already decreed that the majority of people will not believe in His message, despite the clear signs and warnings sent to them. It implies that their disbelief is a result of their own choices and actions, and that Allah's word and judgment have already been established concerning their fate. The verse highlights the idea of divine predestination and the consequences of rejecting faith.
orig: لقد حق القول على أكثرهم فهم لا يؤمنون

translation: Indeed, We have put shackles on their necks, and they are to their chins, so they are with heads [kept] aloft.
interpretation: This verse is a metaphorical description of the state of the disbelievers. The "shackles" around their necks symbolize their stubbornness, arrogance, and refusal to bow down to the truth of Allah's message. These shackles keep their heads raised high in defiance, preventing them from humbling themselves and accepting faith. It signifies that their own pride and obstinacy have become like chains that keep them trapped in disbelief, making it difficult for them to see the truth or submit to Allah's will. The imagery conveys the idea that the disbelievers are prisoners of their own ego and are unable to lower their heads in humility and acceptance of the divine message.
orig: إنا جعلنا في أعناقهم أغلالا فهي إلى الأذقان فهم مقمحون

translation: And We have put a barrier before them, and a barrier behind them, and We have covered them up, so that they cannot see.
interpretation: This verse speaks about the spiritual state of those who persistently reject the truth. The barriers before and behind them symbolize their inability to see the truth due to their arrogance, ignorance, and blind following of their desires. Allah has "covered them up" means that due to their own choices and actions, they have lost the ability to perceive and understand the truth. They are trapped in their own spiritual blindness, unable to see the signs of Allah's existence and guidance all around them. This verse serves as a warning to those who turn away from the path of righteousness and a reminder for believers to always strive for humility, knowledge, and submission to Allah's will.
orig: وجعلنا من بين أيديهم سدا ومن خلفهم سدا فأغشيناهم فهم لا يبصرون

translation: And it is the same for them whether you warn them or do not warn them - they will not believe.
interpretation: This verse suggests that there are some people who are so deeply entrenched in their disbelief that no matter how much they are warned or advised, they will not change their ways and come to faith. It implies that the Prophet's duty is to convey the message, but he should not feel disheartened if some people still refuse to believe, as that is a matter of their own choice and willingness. The verse highlights the reality that faith is a matter of the heart and that external factors like warnings can only go so far in influencing someone's inner convictions.
orig: وسواء عليهم أأنذرتهم أم لم تنذرهم لا يؤمنون

translation: You can only warn one who follows the message and fears the Most Merciful unseen. So give him good tidings of forgiveness and noble reward.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the Prophet's warning and message can only benefit those who sincerely follow the Qur'an and fear Allah without seeing Him. These are the people who will receive Allah's forgiveness and a generous reward in the Hereafter. It implies that the Qur'an's guidance is only effective for those who approach it with humility, submission and consciousness of Allah, even though they cannot perceive Him directly. The verse encourages the believers to remain steadfast in their faith and good deeds, seeking Allah's pleasure, with the promise of His mercy and bountiful recompense.
orig: إنما تنذر من اتبع الذكر وخشي الرحمن بالغيب فبشره بمغفرة وأجر كريم

translation: Indeed, it is We who bring the dead to life and record what they have put forth and what they left behind, and all things We have enumerated in a clear register.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the power and knowledge of Allah. It affirms that Allah has the ability to resurrect the dead and bring them back to life. It also states that Allah keeps a precise record of all the deeds, both good and bad, that a person has done in their life, as well as the impact and legacy they leave behind. The verse indicates that nothing is hidden from Allah and that all things are recorded in a clear register, which can be interpreted as referring to the preservation of deeds for the Day of Judgment. This verse serves as a reminder for individuals to be mindful of their actions and to strive for good deeds, knowing that Allah is constantly aware and keeping account of everything they do.
orig: إنا نحن نحيي الموتى ونكتب ما قدموا وآثارهم وكل شيء أحصيناه في إمام مبين

translation: And present to them an example: the people of the city, when the messengers came to it.
interpretation: This verse is an instruction to the Prophet Muhammad to give an example or parable to his audience about the people of a certain city who rejected the messengers that came to them. The purpose of this example is likely to illustrate the consequences of rejecting the message of God and His messengers, and to warn the audience against making the same mistake. The interpretation could be that those who reject the truth and the guidance sent by God through His messengers will face negative consequences and punishment, just like the people of that city did when they rejected the messengers. It emphasizes the importance of heeding the message and following the guidance of the messengers sent by God.
orig: واضرب لهم مثلا أصحاب القرية إذ جاءها المرسلون

translation: When We sent to them two but they denied them, so We strengthened them with a third, and they said, "Indeed, we are messengers to you."
interpretation: This verse refers to the story of the people of Antioch, to whom Allah sent two messengers to guide them to the right path. However, the people rejected and belied these messengers. So, Allah supported the two messengers with a third one to strengthen their cause and to serve as further proof of their truthfulness. The three messengers then proclaimed to the people that they were indeed sent by Allah to convey His message. This highlights the importance of conveying the divine message with persistence and resilience, even in the face of rejection and opposition. It also shows Allah's support for His messengers and the ultimate triumph of truth over falsehood.
orig: إذ أرسلنا إليهم اثنين فكذبوهما فعززنا بثالث فقالوا إنا إليكم مرسلون

translation: They said, "You are not but human beings like us, and the Most Merciful has not revealed a thing. You are only telling lies."
interpretation: This verse conveys the disbelief and rejection of the divine message by those who oppose the prophets and messengers. They argue that the prophets are mere human beings like themselves, and that God has not actually revealed anything to them. They accuse the prophets of lying and fabricating the message they preach. This attitude stems from their arrogance, ignorance, and attachment to their own ways and desires. They fail to recognize the signs of divine revelation and the exceptional character and wisdom of the prophets. The verse highlights the challenges faced by the prophets in conveying the truth to those who are stubbornly opposed to it.
orig: قالوا ما أنتم إلا بشر مثلنا وما أنزل الرحمن من شيء إن أنتم إلا تكذبون

translation: They said, "Our Lord knows that we are surely messengers to you,
interpretation: This verse conveys the sincerity and conviction of the messengers sent by Allah to deliver His message to the people. They affirm that Allah Himself bears witness to the truth of their mission, and that they have been appointed by Him to guide and enlighten those to whom they have been sent. The messengers emphasize their role as intermediaries, stressing that their duty is only to convey the divine message, and that the ultimate knowledge and judgment rest with Allah alone. This declaration serves as a testament to their unwavering faith, their submission to Allah's will, and their commitment to fulfilling the sacred trust placed upon them as His chosen emissaries.
orig: قالوا ربنا يعلم إنا إليكم لمرسلون

translation: And our duty is only to convey the clear Message.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the role of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and the believers is to clearly convey the message of Islam to others. They are not responsible for whether people accept or reject the message, as that is ultimately a matter of individual choice and God's will. The duty of the believers is to communicate the teachings of Islam with clarity and to be an example of righteousness, but the outcome of their efforts is in God's hands. This verse highlights the importance of conveying the message without coercion or compulsion, and trusting in God's plan and wisdom.
orig: وما علينا إلا البلاغ المبين

translation: They said, "Indeed, we consider you a bad omen. If you do not desist, we will surely stone you, and there will surely touch you, from us, a painful punishment."
interpretation: This verse is a warning from the people to the messengers who were sent to them. The people saw the messengers as a bad omen, believing that their presence would bring misfortune. They threatened the messengers with stoning and painful punishment if they did not cease their mission. This highlights the stubbornness and disbelief of the people, as they rejected the message of the messengers and resorted to threats and violence instead of listening and reflecting upon the truth that was being conveyed to them.
orig: قالوا إنا تطيرنا بكم لئن لم تنتهوا لنرجمنكم وليمسنكم منا عذاب أليم

translation: They said, "Your omen is with yourselves. Is it because you were reminded? Rather, you are a transgressing people."
interpretation: This verse is a response to the people who attributed their misfortunes to bad omens associated with the presence of the messengers among them. The interpretation is that the real cause of their misfortune is not any external omen, but their own actions and transgressions. They are being reminded through the messengers to correct their ways, but instead of heeding the reminder, they are blaming and rejecting the messengers. The verse emphasizes that it is their own excesses and wrongdoings that are the source of their problems, not the presence of the messengers who have come to guide them.
orig: قالوا طائركم معكم أئن ذكرتم بل أنتم قوم مسرفون

translation: And there came from the farthest end of the city a man, running. He said, "O my people, follow the messengers."
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of heeding the call of the messengers of God, even if it comes from an unexpected source. The man who came running from the outskirts of the city, urging his people to follow the messengers, represents those individuals who recognize the truth and are eager to share it with others, regardless of their social status or position. It emphasizes that the message of God's guidance can come from anyone, and that we should be open to receiving it, no matter who the messenger may be. The verse also underscores the urgency of responding to the call of faith, as the man came running, implying the need to act swiftly in embracing the truth and following the path of righteousness.
orig: وجاء من أقصى المدينة رجل يسعى قال يا قوم اتبعوا المرسلين

translation: Follow those who do not ask of you [any] payment, and they are [rightly] guided.
interpretation: This verse encourages people to follow the guidance of those who are not seeking any worldly gain or reward for their teachings. It suggests that the true and sincere guides are those who do not ask for any payment or compensation in return for their guidance. They are the ones who are on the right path themselves and can lead others to the truth. This highlights the importance of seeking knowledge and guidance from sincere and righteous individuals who are not motivated by material gains, but rather by their desire to please Allah and benefit others.
orig: اتبعوا من لا يسألكم أجرا وهم مهتدون

translation: And why should I not worship He who created me and to whom you will be returned?
interpretation: This verse is a rhetorical question that emphasizes the logical necessity and obligation of worshipping Allah alone. It implies that since Allah is the One who created human beings and to Him is their ultimate return in the Hereafter, it only makes sense to direct all worship and devotion to Him alone. Worshipping anyone or anything else would be irrational and ungrateful, as no other being has the power to create or the right to be worshipped. The verse also serves as a reminder of the inevitability of being returned to Allah for judgment, encouraging the listener to consider their devotional life and relationship with their Creator.
orig: وما لي لا أعبد الذي فطرني وإليه ترجعون

translation: Should I take other than Him [false] deities [while], if the Most Merciful intends for me some adversity, their intercession will not avail me at all, nor can they save me?
interpretation: This verse is a rhetorical question that highlights the futility of worshipping false deities instead of Allah. It emphasizes that these false gods have no power to intercede or save one from harm if the Most Merciful (Allah) wills it. The verse implies that only Allah has the ultimate power and control over all affairs, and that relying on anyone or anything else for protection or salvation is misguided and ineffective. It serves as a reminder to put one's faith and trust solely in Allah, as He alone can provide true guidance, support, and deliverance in times of adversity.
orig: أأتخذ من دونه آلهة إن يردن الرحمن بضر لا تغن عني شفاعتهم شيئا ولا ينقذون

translation: Indeed, I am in clear error
interpretation: This verse is an acknowledgement of one's own misguidance and being lost. It is a realization that without the guidance of Allah, a person is in manifest error and straying far from the straight path. It highlights the importance of recognizing one's own shortcomings and the need for divine guidance to stay on the right course in life. This admission of being in clear error is a sign of humility and self-awareness, which are essential qualities for a believer seeking Allah's guidance and mercy.
orig: إني إذا لفي ضلال مبين

translation: Indeed, I have believed in your Lord, so listen to me.
interpretation: This verse is a declaration of faith by a believer, who is calling upon others to listen to his message and follow his example of believing in the one true Lord. It emphasizes the importance of proclaiming one's faith openly and inviting others to embrace the truth. The believer is confident in his faith and wants others to experience the same spiritual fulfillment and guidance that comes from believing in and submitting to the Lord. This verse encourages believers to be bold in their faith, to share it with others, and to stand firm in their conviction even in the face of opposition or disbelief from those around them.
orig: إني آمنت بربكم فاسمعون

translation: It will be said, "Enter Paradise." He will say, "I wish my people could know"
interpretation: This verse speaks about the immense joy and gratitude a believer will experience upon being granted entry into Paradise. The believer's first thought is not about himself, but rather about his people and his desire for them to know the truth of Allah's promise and the reality of the Hereafter. It reflects the believer's deep concern for others and his wish that they, too, could experience the bliss of Paradise. This highlights the importance of conveying the message of Islam to others and striving to guide them to the straight path, so that they may also attain salvation and eternal happiness in the Hereafter.
orig: قيل ادخل الجنة قال يا ليت قومي يعلمون

translation: For my Lord has forgiven me and made me of the honored ones.
interpretation: This verse suggests that Allah has not only forgiven the speaker of their sins, but also elevated their status and made them among those who are honored and respected. It implies that forgiveness from Allah is not just about absolving one of wrongdoings, but also about being granted a higher rank and dignity. The verse conveys a sense of gratitude and recognition of Allah's immense favor and mercy in both forgiving and honoring His servant.
orig: بما غفر لي ربي وجعلني من المكرمين

translation: And We did not send down upon his people after him any soldiers from the heaven, nor would We have done so.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that God did not send any heavenly forces or armies to support or punish the people of the Prophet after him. It implies that the divine message and guidance had already been completed through the Prophet, and there was no need for further divine intervention or punishment. The verse also suggests that God does not typically intervene directly in human affairs by sending armies from heaven, as this is not His way of dealing with His creation. Instead, people are expected to follow the guidance already provided and face the consequences of their actions in this world and the hereafter.
orig: وما أنزلنا على قومه من بعده من جند من السماء وما كنا منزلين

translation: It will be but one shout, and at once they will be extinguished.
interpretation: This verse is referring to the Day of Judgment, when a single powerful blast will mark the end of this world. It signifies that when Allah wills for it to happen, it will be extremely swift, and the life of this world will be extinguished in an instant. The verse emphasizes the suddenness and decisiveness with which the current order will be terminated by Allah's command. It is a reminder of the transient nature of worldly existence and the inevitable coming of the Hereafter, encouraging believers to be always mindful of the Day of Reckoning and to live their lives in preparation for it.
orig: إن كانت إلا صيحة واحدة فإذا هم خامدون

translation: Alas for the servants! There comes not a messenger to them but they mock him.
interpretation: This verse expresses Allah's disappointment and sorrow over the attitude of those who reject and mock His messengers. It highlights the arrogance and ignorance of people who, instead of heeding the guidance brought by the prophets, choose to ridicule and belittle them. The verse also implies that this has been a recurring pattern throughout history, with many nations rejecting the messengers sent to them. It serves as a warning to mankind not to follow in the footsteps of those who mocked the prophets, as they will face the consequences of their actions in the Hereafter.
orig: يا حسرة على العباد ما يأتيهم من رسول إلا كانوا به يستهزئون

translation: Have they not considered how many generations We destroyed before them - that they to them will not return?
interpretation: This verse is a reminder to humanity that Allah has destroyed many past civilizations and generations who rejected the truth and were ungrateful for His blessings. It emphasizes the finality of death and that those who have passed away will not return to this world. The verse also serves as a warning to the disbelievers that they too may face a similar fate if they do not heed the message of Islam and submit to Allah's will. It encourages introspection and reflection on the lessons that can be learned from the fate of past nations.
orig: ألم يروا كم أهلكنا قبلهم من القرون أنهم إليهم لا يرجعون

translation: And indeed, all of them will be brought present before Us.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the concept of accountability and resurrection in Islam. It affirms that every single person will be brought before Allah (God) on the Day of Judgment to face the consequences of their deeds in this worldly life. No one will be left out or forgotten; all will be held responsible for their actions, good or bad. This serves as a reminder for believers to be mindful of their conduct and strive to lead righteous lives, knowing that they will ultimately answer to their Creator.
orig: وإن كل لما جميع لدينا محضرون

translation: And a sign for them is the dead earth. We have brought it to life and brought forth from it grain, and from it they eat.
interpretation: This verse is a reminder of Allah's power and mercy. It points to the miracle of life and growth that Allah brings forth from the seemingly lifeless earth. Just as Allah can resurrect the dead earth and make it fertile, He can also resurrect the dead on the Day of Judgment. The verse also emphasizes Allah's provision for mankind through the food that grows from the earth. It is a call to gratitude and recognition of Allah's blessings, and a sign of His ability to restore life where there appears to be none, both in this world and the next.
orig: وآية لهم الأرض الميتة أحييناها وأخرجنا منها حبا فمنه يأكلون

translation: And We placed therein gardens of palm trees and grapevines and caused to burst forth therefrom some springs.
interpretation: This verse highlights Allah's power and generosity in creating a beautiful and bountiful earth for humanity. The mention of palm trees, grapevines, and springs suggests that Allah has provided us with a variety of fruits and sources of water, which are essential for our sustenance and enjoyment. The burst forth of springs also implies a sense of abundance and ease in accessing these resources. This verse serves as a reminder for us to be grateful for the blessings that Allah has bestowed upon us and to appreciate the natural world that He has created. It encourages us to be mindful of our responsibility as stewards of the earth and to use its resources wisely and sustainably.
orig: وجعلنا فيها جنات من نخيل وأعناب وفجرنا فيها من العيون

translation: That they may eat of His fruit. And their hands have not produced it, so will they not be grateful?
interpretation: This verse is a reminder of Allah's blessings and favors upon mankind. It emphasizes that the fruits and produce that people consume are not the result of their own efforts, but rather a gift from Allah. The verse encourages gratitude and acknowledgment of Allah's benevolence, as it is He who has provided sustenance for His creation. It also implies that since these bounties come from Allah, people should not be arrogant or take credit for them, but rather express their thankfulness to the One who has bestowed them with such provisions.
orig: ليأكلوا من ثمره وما عملته أيديهم أفلا يشكرون

translation: Glory be to Him Who created all the pairs of that which the earth produces, as well as their own (human) kind and of that which they do not know.
interpretation: This verse points to the infinite power and wisdom of Allah, Who has created all things in pairs, whether they are plants, animals, or human beings. It also suggests that there are many things in the universe that humans do not yet know or understand, but which Allah has created in His wisdom. The verse invites us to reflect on the wonders of Allah's creation and to glorify Him for His boundless creativity and knowledge. It reminds us that the world is full of signs of Allah's existence and power, and that we should be humble before His greatness and seek to understand His creation with a spirit of reverence and awe.
orig: سبحان الذي خلق الأزواج كلها مما تنبت الأرض ومن أنفسهم ومما لا يعلمون

translation: And a sign for them is the night. We remove from it [the light of] day, so they are [left] in darkness.
interpretation: This verse is a reminder of Allah's power and control over the universe. The alternation of night and day is a sign of His wisdom and mercy. The sudden transition from light to darkness is a metaphor for the human condition - we are dependent on Allah's guidance and grace to navigate through life. Without His light, we are lost in the darkness of ignorance and sin. The verse also implies that just as Allah can bring forth light from darkness, He can guide those who are lost and bring them into the light of faith. It is a call to reflect on the signs of Allah's creation and to turn to Him in gratitude and submission.
orig: وآية لهم الليل نسلخ منه النهار فإذا هم مظلمون

translation: And the sun runs [on course] toward its stopping point. That is the determination of the Exalted in Might, the Knowing.
interpretation: This verse alludes to the precise and ordained motion of the sun, which follows a specific course determined by Allah, the Almighty and All-Knowing. It emphasizes the divine power and wisdom behind the intricate workings of the universe, reminding us that every celestial body moves according to His plan. The verse encourages contemplation on the magnificence of Allah's creation and the perfect order He has established in the cosmos. It also serves as a reminder of the temporary nature of this world, as even the mighty sun has a designated end point, symbolizing the inevitable conclusion of all things in accordance with Allah's will.
orig: والشمس تجري لمستقر لها ذلك تقدير العزيز العليم

translation: And the moon - We have determined for it phases, until it returns [appearing] like the old date stalk.
interpretation: This verse is a reminder of Allah's power and control over the universe. The phases of the moon, from a thin crescent to a full moon and back again, are a sign of Allah's precise measurement and decree. Just as a date stalk withers and curves into a crescent shape as it ages, the moon's appearance follows a similar pattern, showcasing the perfection of Allah's creation. This verse encourages reflection on the natural world and recognition of the Creator's might and wisdom behind its intricate design.
orig: والقمر قدرناه منازل حتى عاد كالعرجون القديم

translation: It is not allowable for the sun to reach the moon, nor does the night overtake the day, but each, in an orbit, is swimming.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the perfect order and balance in the universe created by Allah. The sun and the moon follow their own ordained paths and orbits, never catching up with each other. Similarly, the night and day cycle is also precisely determined, with neither overstepping its limits. Each celestial body "swims" or moves in its own orbit, following the laws set by Allah. This verse emphasizes the harmony, regularity, and precision in Allah's creation, reflecting His infinite wisdom and power. It invites us to ponder over these signs and appreciate the magnificent design in the universe.
orig: لا الشمس ينبغي لها أن تدرك القمر ولا الليل سابق النهار وكل في فلك يسبحون

translation: And a sign for them is that We carried their descendants in the laden ship.
interpretation: This verse is a reminder of Allah's power and mercy. It refers to the story of Prophet Noah (peace be upon him) and the Ark, which was a sign of Allah's protection for the believers. The verse emphasizes that Allah saved not only Noah and the believers of his time but also their descendants, ensuring the continuity of faith and righteousness among future generations. It is a testament to Allah's promise that He will always support and protect those who believe in Him and follow His guidance, even in the face of great adversity. The "laden ship" symbolizes the safety and security provided by faith in Allah, which can carry believers through the storms of life towards salvation and success in this world and the Hereafter.
orig: وآية لهم أنا حملنا ذريتهم في الفلك المشحون

translation: And We have created for them the likes of which they ride.
interpretation: This verse suggests that Allah has created various means of transportation for human beings, similar to what they already use, such as animals like horses and camels. It implies that Allah provides humanity with the necessary resources and means to facilitate their journeys and make their lives easier. This can be interpreted as a sign of Allah's mercy and generosity towards His creation, as He ensures that they have access to suitable modes of transportation according to their needs and the time they live in.
orig: وخلقنا لهم من مثله ما يركبون

translation: And if We willed, We could drown them; then no one responding to a cry would there be for them, nor would they be saved.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute power and control of Allah over His creation. It reminds us that our lives and fates are entirely in His hands. If He wills, He can easily destroy us, and there would be no one to save us or respond to our cries for help. This should instill in us a sense of humility, submission, and gratitude towards our Creator. It also serves as a warning against arrogance and the belief that we are self-sufficient or invincible. Ultimately, our salvation and well-being depend on Allah's mercy and grace, and we should constantly strive to seek His protection and guidance.
orig: وإن نشأ نغرقهم فلا صريخ لهم ولا هم ينقذون

translation: Except as a mercy from Us and provision for a time.
interpretation: This verse suggests that whatever blessings or respite people enjoy in this worldly life is only due to the mercy of Allah and is limited to a finite period of time. It serves as a reminder that the pleasures and comforts of this temporary existence are ultimately fleeting, and that one should be grateful to Allah for His mercy in granting them. The verse also implies that people should use the time and provisions Allah has mercifully given them to do good deeds and prepare for the eternal life to come, rather than becoming attached to the transient nature of this world.
orig: إلا رحمة منا ومتاعا إلى حين

translation: And when it is said to them, "Fear what is before you and what is behind you, so that you may receive mercy."
interpretation: This verse is a reminder for people to be mindful of their actions and their consequences, both in this life and in the Hereafter. "What is before you" refers to the present and the future, while "what is behind you" refers to the past. By being conscious of Allah and following His guidance in all aspects of life, one can hope to attain His mercy and forgiveness. This verse emphasizes the importance of taqwa (God-consciousness) and the need to constantly evaluate one's deeds and intentions, seeking to please Allah and avoid His displeasure. It encourages believers to lead a life of righteousness, knowing that they will be held accountable for their actions and that the ultimate goal is to earn Allah's mercy and grace.
orig: وإذا قيل لهم اتقوا ما بين أيديكم وما خلفكم لعلكم ترحمون

translation: And no sign comes to them from the signs of their Lord except that they are from it turning away.
interpretation: This verse highlights the stubborn nature of the disbelievers who, despite being presented with numerous signs and proofs of Allah's existence and power, choose to ignore and turn away from them. It suggests that their hearts are sealed and their minds are closed, preventing them from acknowledging the truth. The repetition of this behavior indicates a deep-rooted arrogance and a refusal to submit to the will of Allah, even when confronted with clear evidence. This verse serves as a warning to believers not to fall into the same pattern of denying or disregarding the signs of Allah in their own lives.
orig: وما تأتيهم من آية من آيات ربهم إلا كانوا عنها معرضين

translation: And when it is said to them, "Spend from that which Allah has provided for you," those who disbelieve say to those who believe, "Should we feed one whom, if Allah had willed, He would have fed? You are not but in clear error."
interpretation: This verse highlights the attitude of the disbelievers towards charity and their lack of faith in Allah's wisdom and power. They question the believers' act of giving, arguing that if Allah willed, He would have directly provided for those in need without human intervention. This interpretation suggests that the disbelievers fail to understand the importance of human responsibility and the role of charity in fulfilling Allah's commandments. It also emphasizes their arrogance in questioning Allah's will and their dismissal of the believers' actions as misguided, revealing their own lack of understanding and faith.
orig: وإذا قيل لهم أنفقوا مما رزقكم الله قال الذين كفروا للذين آمنوا أنطعم من لو يشاء الله أطعمه إن أنتم إلا في ضلال مبين

translation: And they say, "When is this promise, if you should be truthful?"
interpretation: This verse is a challenge posed by the disbelievers and skeptics who doubt the promise of resurrection and the Day of Judgment. They ask the believers and the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) to specify when this promised event will occur, as if to prove the truthfulness of their claim. The question is asked in a mocking and disbelieving tone, suggesting that they consider the promise of the hereafter to be false or unlikely. The verse highlights the skepticism and lack of faith among those who reject the divine message, as they demand tangible proof or a specific time for the fulfillment of God's promise. It also emphasizes the importance of having faith and trust in God's plan, even if the exact timing remains unknown to human beings.
orig: ويقولون متى هذا الوعد إن كنتم صادقين

translation: They await not but one Saihah [shout (i.e. the blowing of the Trumpet by the angel Israfil)] which will seize them while they are disputing!
interpretation: This verse refers to the sudden and inevitable coming of the Day of Judgment. The disbelievers are heedlessly arguing and disputing in this world, oblivious to the fact that a single, mighty blast from the Trumpet of the angel Israfil will seize them and bring about the end of this world. It highlights the need for people to be always mindful of the Hereafter and to prepare for it through righteous deeds, rather than being caught up in worldly disputes and arguments that ultimately hold no meaning in the face of the Day of Judgment. The verse emphasizes the suddenness and finality with which the Hour will arrive, leaving no opportunity for repentance or escape for those who had been heedless.
orig: ما ينظرون إلا صيحة واحدة تأخذهم وهم يخصمون

translation: Then they will not be able to make a bequest, nor will they return to their family.
interpretation: This verse refers to the Day of Judgment, when the disbelievers will face the consequences of their actions. They will be in such a state of shock and despair that they will not be able to leave any last wishes or instructions (توصية) for their loved ones. Moreover, they will not be able to return to their families to bid farewell or seek forgiveness. This emphasizes the finality of death and the gravity of the Day of Judgment, urging people to repent and live righteously while they still have the chance in this worldly life.
orig: فلا يستطيعون توصية ولا إلى أهلهم يرجعون

translation: And the Horn will be blown, and at once from the graves to their Lord they will hasten.
interpretation: This verse refers to the Day of Resurrection, when the trumpet will be blown and the dead will rise from their graves and rush towards Allah for judgment. It emphasizes the suddenness and inevitability of the event, and how all souls will be brought before their Lord to face the consequences of their deeds in this world. The verse serves as a reminder of the ultimate accountability that awaits every human being, encouraging them to lead righteous lives in preparation for that decisive moment.
orig: ونفخ في الصور فإذا هم من الأجداث إلى ربهم ينسلون

translation: They will say, "O woe to us! Who has raised us up from our sleeping place?" [The reply will be], "This is what the Most Merciful had promised, and the messengers told the truth."
interpretation: This verse is referring to the Day of Resurrection, when the dead will be brought back to life from their graves. Upon realizing this, they will cry out in shock and distress, "O woe to us! Who has raised us up from our sleeping place?" This emphasizes the suddenness and overwhelming nature of the resurrection. The response to their cry, "This is what the Most Merciful had promised, and the messengers told the truth," affirms that this event is the fulfillment of Allah's promise, which was conveyed by His messengers. It validates the truthfulness of the prophets and the reality of the Day of Judgment, which they had warned about during their lifetimes. This verse serves as a reminder of the inevitability of resurrection and the importance of heeding the warnings of the messengers in preparation for that Day.
orig: قالوا يا ويلنا من بعثنا من مرقدنا هذا ما وعد الرحمن وصدق المرسلون

translation: It will be but one shout, and at once they will all be brought before Us.
interpretation: This verse is referring to the Day of Judgment, when Allah will resurrect all of humanity with a single mighty blast of the trumpet. It emphasizes the power and inevitability of the final hour, that in just one moment, every soul who has ever lived will be brought forth and made to stand before their Lord for judgment. The verse underscores the suddenness of that awesome event and that there will be no escape or delay when Allah commands it to occur. It is a reminder for mankind to be ever mindful of that day and to strive in righteousness in preparation for it.
orig: إن كانت إلا صيحة واحدة فإذا هم جميع لدينا محضرون

translation: So today no soul will be wronged at all, and you will not be recompensed except for what you used to do.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute justice of God on the Day of Judgment. No one will be treated unjustly or wronged in the slightest way. Every person will be recompensed precisely based on their deeds in this worldly life. Good deeds will be rewarded, while evil deeds will incur punishment. This highlights the importance of being mindful of one's actions, as they will determine one's ultimate fate in the Hereafter. It also underscores God's perfect fairness and wisdom in judging His creation, as He is the Most Just and All-Knowing.
orig: فاليوم لا تظلم نفس شيئا ولا تجزون إلا ما كنتم تعملون

translation: Indeed the companions of Paradise, that Day, will be amused in [joyful] occupation -
interpretation: This verse is referring to the eternal bliss and joy that the righteous believers will experience in Paradise on the Day of Judgment. They will be engaged in delightful activities that will keep them happily occupied, such as enjoying the magnificent bounties of Paradise, socializing with other believers, and basking in the pleasure of Allah's company. The verse emphasizes that unlike the temporary and often stressful preoccupations of this worldly life, the "occupation" of the people of Paradise will be purely focused on joy, peace, and spiritual fulfillment in the presence of their Lord. It is a reminder for the believers to strive for this eternal reward through faith and good deeds.
orig: إن أصحاب الجنة اليوم في شغل فاكهون

translation: They and their spouses - in shade, reclining on adorned couches.
interpretation: This verse refers to the believers in Paradise, who will be reclining on adorned couches or thrones in the shade along with their spouses. It symbolizes the ultimate comfort, luxury, and tranquility that the righteous will enjoy in the eternal gardens of Paradise as a reward for their faith and good deeds in this world. The mention of spouses indicates that the believers will be joined with their righteous partners in the Hereafter, adding to their happiness and contentment.
orig: هم وأزواجهم في ظلال على الأرائك متكئون

translation: In it they will have fruits, and they will have whatever they ask for.
interpretation: This verse refers to the blessings and rewards that the righteous will enjoy in Paradise. They will have an abundance of delicious fruits and will be granted whatever they desire. This signifies the complete satisfaction and contentment that the believers will experience in the afterlife, as a result of their faith and good deeds in this world. It also highlights the generosity and benevolence of Allah, who will fulfill all the wishes of His faithful servants in Paradise.
orig: لهم فيها فاكهة ولهم ما يدعون

translation: Peace, a word from a Merciful Lord.
interpretation: This verse conveys a profound message of divine mercy and grace. The word "Peace" (Salam) is not merely a greeting, but a blessing and a promise from Allah, the Most Merciful. It signifies the ultimate peace and tranquility that can only be found through faith and submission to the will of Allah. This peace is a gift from the Almighty, bestowed upon those who seek His guidance and strive to live according to His commandments. It is a reminder that true peace and contentment can only be achieved by fostering a deep connection with the Creator and seeking His mercy and forgiveness.
orig: سلام قولا من رب رحيم

translation: But stand apart today, you criminals!
interpretation: This verse is a stern warning to the criminals and sinners on the Day of Judgment. God is commanding them to separate themselves from the righteous believers. It emphasizes the clear distinction that will be made between those who followed the right path and those who deviated from it. The criminals will be singled out and made to face the consequences of their actions, while the believers will be rewarded for their faith and good deeds. This verse serves as a reminder that ultimately, everyone will be held accountable for their choices in this life, and that justice will be served in the Hereafter.
orig: وامتازوا اليوم أيها المجرمون

translation: Did I not enjoin upon you, O children of Adam, that you not worship Satan - [for] indeed, he is to you a clear enemy?
interpretation: This verse is a stern reminder and warning from Allah to all of mankind. Allah is reminding us that He has already commanded us not to follow or worship Satan, because Satan is our clear and open enemy. Satan's goal is to misguide us and lead us astray from the straight path of Islam. He wants us to disobey Allah and fall into sin and disbelief. Allah has made it clear that we should not obey Satan or follow his temptations and whispers. Rather, we must be steadfast in obeying Allah alone and resisting the tricks of Satan. This requires full consciousness of Allah, seeking refuge in Him, and adhering firmly to His guidance and the teachings of His Prophet (peace be upon him). The path of Satan only leads to loss and regret in this life and the Hereafter.
orig: ألم أعهد إليكم يا بني آدم أن لا تعبدوا الشيطان إنه لكم عدو مبين

translation: And worship Me. This is the straight path.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of worshipping Allah alone, as it is the only path that leads to success and salvation. It reminds us that our ultimate purpose in life is to submit to the will of our Creator and to direct all our acts of worship solely to Him. Following this straight path, which involves sincere devotion and obedience to Allah, will guide us towards righteousness and help us attain His pleasure in this world and the hereafter.
orig: وأن اعبدوني هذا صراط مستقيم

translation: And he had already led astray from among you much of creation, so did you not use reason?
interpretation: This verse is a rebuke to those who followed Satan and his temptations, despite the signs and warnings from Allah. It implies that Allah has given humans the faculty of reason and intellect to distinguish between right and wrong, truth and falsehood. However, many people fail to use this gift and instead follow their desires or the whispers of Satan, leading them astray from the straight path. The verse is a reminder for people to reflect and use their God-given intelligence to see through the deceptions of Satan and adhere to the guidance of Allah.
orig: ولقد أضل منكم جبلا كثيرا أفلم تكونوا تعقلون

translation: This is the Hell which you were promised.
interpretation: This verse serves as a stark reminder to those who denied the truth and the warnings of the prophets. It emphasizes that the Hell that was described to them is now a reality that they must face as a consequence of their actions and disbelief. The verse also implies that the people had been given ample warning and opportunity to mend their ways, but they chose to persist in their wrongdoing. It underscores the importance of heeding the divine message and living a righteous life to avoid the punishment of Hell in the afterlife.
orig: هذه جهنم التي كنتم توعدون

translation: Burn therein today for what you used to deny.
interpretation: This verse is a warning to the disbelievers that they will face the consequences of their actions in the Hereafter. They will be punished in the Fire of Hell for their rejection of the truth and their disbelief in Allah and His messengers. The verse emphasizes the justice of Allah, as people will be recompensed according to their deeds. It serves as a reminder for mankind to be mindful of their actions in this world, as they will be held accountable for them in the next life. The verse also highlights the severity and permanence of the punishment in Hell, as the disbelievers will be told to "burn therein today" for their past transgressions.
orig: اصلوها اليوم بما كنتم تكفرون

translation: That Day, We will seal over their mouths, and their hands will speak to Us, and their feet will testify about what they used to earn.
interpretation: This verse speaks about the Day of Judgment when the disbelievers will be unable to speak in their defense. Instead, their own limbs will testify against them, providing irrefutable evidence of their misdeeds. It emphasizes the concept of ultimate justice, where no one will be able to hide their actions or intentions from Allah. The sealing of mouths symbolizes the silencing of false excuses, while the speaking of hands and feet represents the undeniable proof of one's deeds. This verse serves as a powerful reminder for believers to be mindful of their actions, as they will be held accountable for everything they do in this life.
orig: اليوم نختم على أفواههم وتكلمنا أيديهم وتشهد أرجلهم بما كانوا يكسبون

translation: And if We willed, We could have obliterated their eyes, and they would race to [find] the path, and how could they see?
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's absolute power and control over His creation. It suggests that if Allah wanted, He could easily take away the sight of those who disbelieve or disobey Him, leaving them to grope blindly for guidance. This serves as a reminder that the ability to see and perceive is a blessing from Allah, and that one should be grateful for this gift and use it to follow the straight path of faith and righteousness. The verse also implies that without Allah's guidance and mercy, humans would be lost and unable to find their way, both physically and spiritually. It is a warning against taking one's blessings for granted and a call to humble oneself before the Almighty.
orig: ولو نشاء لطمسنا على أعينهم فاستبقوا الصراط فأنى يبصرون

translation: And if We willed, We could have deformed them, [paralyzing them] in their places so they would not be able to proceed, nor could they return.
interpretation: This verse is a reminder of Allah's ultimate power and control over His creation. If He so willed, He could easily paralyze the wrongdoers in their tracks, rendering them unable to move forward or turn back. It serves as a warning that no one can escape Allah's judgment or punishment if He decides to inflict it upon them. The verse also implies that it is only by Allah's mercy and permission that people are able to move about freely and go about their lives. Ultimately, it emphasizes the importance of being mindful of Allah and striving to stay on the right path, as He has the power to stop us in our tracks at any moment if He so chooses.
orig: ولو نشاء لمسخناهم على مكانتهم فما استطاعوا مضيا ولا يرجعون

translation: And he to whom We grant long life, We reverse in creation; so will they not understand?
interpretation: This verse highlights the natural process of aging, where those who are granted long lives eventually experience a decline in their physical and mental faculties. It serves as a reminder of the temporary nature of worldly life and the inevitable changes that come with advanced age. The verse encourages people to reflect upon this reality and understand the wisdom behind it, urging them to make the most of their abilities while they can and to focus on spiritual growth and good deeds rather than being overly attached to the fleeting nature of youth and vitality.
orig: ومن نعمره ننكسه في الخلق أفلا يعقلون

translation: And We have not taught him poetry, nor is it befitting for him. It is nothing but a reminder and a clear Qur'an.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) was not taught poetry by Allah, nor was it appropriate for him to compose poetry. The Qur'an is not a work of poetry, but rather a reminder to mankind and a clear revelation from Allah. The Prophet's role was to convey the divine message, not to create artistic expressions. This verse also implies that the Qur'an's eloquence and beauty are inherent in its divine nature, not the result of human poetic skill.
orig: وما علمناه الشعر وما ينبغي له إن هو إلا ذكر وقرآن مبين

translation: That it may give admonition to any (who are) alive, and that the charge may be proved against those who reject (Truth).
interpretation: The purpose of the Qur'an is to serve as a warning and reminder to those whose hearts are alive and receptive to the truth, so that they may be guided and reform themselves. At the same time, it establishes the proof against the disbelievers who willfully reject the message despite its clarity, so that they will have no excuse on the Day of Judgment for their denial and can be justly held accountable for their actions.
orig: لينذر من كان حيا ويحق القول على الكافرين

translation: Do they not see that We have created for them from what Our hands have made, grazing livestock, and [then] they are their owners?
interpretation: This verse is a reminder of Allah's power and generosity towards mankind. It points out that Allah has created livestock, such as cattle, sheep, and camels, for the benefit of human beings. These animals are a gift from Allah, created by His own hands, and He has made humans their owners and masters. This means that humans have been granted the right to use these animals for their own purposes, such as for food, clothing, transportation, and other benefits. The verse encourages people to reflect on this blessing and to be grateful to Allah for His provisions. It also implies that since these animals are a gift from Allah, humans have a responsibility to treat them with kindness and respect, and not to abuse or exploit them. The verse is a call to recognize Allah's bounty and to use it in a way that is pleasing to Him.
orig: أولم يروا أنا خلقنا لهم مما عملت أيدينا أنعاما فهم لها مالكون

translation: And We have subdued them for them, so some of them they ride, and some of them they eat.
interpretation: This verse highlights the blessings and favors that Allah has bestowed upon humanity. He has made animals subservient and useful to humans, providing them with means of transportation and a source of food. It emphasizes the idea that Allah has created these creatures for the benefit of mankind, and we should be grateful for His provisions. The verse also implies that humans have a responsibility to treat these animals with kindness and respect, as they are a gift from Allah. It serves as a reminder of the interconnectedness between humans and the natural world, and the importance of maintaining a balanced and sustainable relationship with the creatures that share our planet.
orig: وذللناها لهم فمنها ركوبهم ومنها يأكلون

translation: And for them therein are [other] benefits and drinks, so will they not be grateful?
interpretation: This verse reminds us of the countless blessings that Allah has bestowed upon us, such as the various benefits and sustenance we derive from His creation. It encourages us to reflect upon these favors and express our gratitude to the Almighty. Gratitude is a fundamental aspect of faith, as it acknowledges Allah's benevolence and mercy towards His servants. By being thankful for what we have been given, we not only please our Lord but also cultivate a sense of contentment and humility in our hearts. The verse also serves as a gentle admonition to those who fail to recognize and appreciate the divine blessings in their lives, urging them to open their eyes and be grateful for all that Allah has provided them with.
orig: ولهم فيها منافع ومشارب أفلا يشكرون

translation: And they have taken besides Allah [false] deities that perhaps they would be helped.
interpretation: This verse is criticizing the polytheistic practice of worshipping false gods and idols in the hope of receiving their aid and support. It suggests that such deities are powerless and unable to provide any real assistance to those who venerate them. The implication is that only Allah, the one true God, has the power to help and that relying on false gods is futile. It emphasizes the folly of polytheism and serves as a call to worship Allah alone.
orig: واتخذوا من دون الله آلهة لعلهم ينصرون

translation: They are unable to help them, and they [themselves] are soldiers brought to them.
interpretation: This verse is referring to the false gods and idols that the disbelievers worship. Despite the disbelievers' belief that these false deities will help them, in reality, they are powerless and cannot provide any assistance. Moreover, these very idols that they worship will be brought forth as witnesses against them on the Day of Judgment, testifying to their disbelief and serving as evidence of their wrongdoing. The verse emphasizes the futility of worshipping anyone or anything besides Allah, as these false objects of worship have no power to benefit or harm, and will ultimately be a source of regret and humiliation for their worshippers in the Hereafter.
orig: لا يستطيعون نصرهم وهم لهم جند محضرون

translation: So let not their speech grieve you. Indeed, We know what they conceal and what they declare.
interpretation: This verse is a reassurance to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) from Allah. It tells him not to be saddened or affected by the hurtful words, mockery or rejection of the disbelievers, for Allah has full knowledge of both their outward actions and inward intentions. He knows the animosity, plots and disbelief they hide in their hearts, as well as what they openly proclaim with their tongues. This is a reminder that Allah is aware of everything and that He will deal with the disbelievers' actions in the appropriate manner in this world and the next. It is a consolation to the Prophet to remain patient, continue conveying the message, and trust in Allah's plan, wisdom and support, without being discouraged by people's negative reactions.
orig: فلا يحزنك قولهم إنا نعلم ما يسرون وما يعلنون

translation: Does man not consider that We created him from a [mere] sperm-drop - then at once he is a clear adversary?
interpretation: This verse is a reminder to mankind of their humble origins and their audacity in challenging and denying Allah despite this fact. It highlights the power and ability of Allah to create man from a mere drop of fluid, emphasizing the miraculous nature of human creation.
