The verse also points out the ungrateful nature of man, who, despite being created from such a lowly substance, becomes an open adversary to Allah, arguing against His signs and revelations. It serves as a call for man to reflect upon his origins and his relationship with his Creator, and to humble himself before the One who brought him into existence from nothingness.
orig: أولم ير الإنسان أنا خلقناه من نطفة فإذا هو خصيم مبين

translation: And he presents for Us an example and forgets his [own] creation. He says, "Who will give life to bones while they are disintegrated?"
interpretation: This verse is referring to those who doubt the possibility of resurrection and the afterlife. They question how God can bring the dead back to life after their bodies have decomposed into bones. However, they forget that God created them from nothing in the first place. The verse implies that if God has the power to create life from nothing, then surely He has the power to resurrect the dead. It is a reminder that God's power and abilities are beyond human comprehension and that doubting His capabilities is a result of human forgetfulness and limited understanding.
orig: وضرب لنا مثلا ونسي خلقه قال من يحيي العظام وهي رميم

translation: Say, "He will give them life who produced them the first time; and He is, of all creation, Knowing."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the power and knowledge of Allah in His ability to resurrect the dead just as He created them the first time. It highlights that Allah has complete knowledge of every single creation and is fully aware of how to restore life to them after death. The verse serves as a reminder of Allah's omnipotence and omniscience, and encourages believers to have faith in the reality of the Day of Resurrection.
orig: قل يحييها الذي أنشأها أول مرة وهو بكل خلق عليم

translation: He who made for you from the green tree, fire, and then from it you ignite.
interpretation: This verse alludes to the power and wisdom of Allah in creating things that may seem contradictory or impossible, such as extracting fire from a green tree. It is a reminder that Allah has the ability to bring forth the opposite of things and make the impossible possible. The verse also points to the blessings that Allah has bestowed upon humanity, providing them with the means to create fire, which is essential for cooking, warmth, and light. It encourages reflection on the signs of Allah's creation and the ways in which He has provided for His creatures, even through means that may seem unlikely or paradoxical.
orig: الذي جعل لكم من الشجر الأخضر نارا فإذا أنتم منه توقدون

translation: Is not He Who created the heavens and the earth able to create the like of them? Yea, indeed! for He is the Creator Supreme, of skill and knowledge (infinite)!
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the omnipotence and infinite creative power of Allah. It poses a rhetorical question, asking if the One who created the vast heavens and earth is not capable of recreating human beings in the afterlife. The answer is a resounding "Yes" as Allah is the Supreme Creator possessing boundless skill and knowledge. This verse serves as a reminder for mankind that resurrection and the afterlife are easily within the power of Allah, the Almighty Creator of the universe.
orig: أوليس الذي خلق السماوات والأرض بقادر على أن يخلق مثلهم بلى وهو الخلاق العليم

translation: His command is only when He intends a thing that He says to it, "Be," and it is.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the omnipotence and absolute power of Allah. It conveys that when Allah wills something to happen, He merely commands it to "Be" and it comes into existence. This highlights the idea that Allah's will is not constrained by the laws of nature or any other limitations; rather, His command is sufficient to bring anything into being. The verse also implies the effortlessness with which Allah creates and the immediacy of His creations' response to His command. It underscores the complete submission of all creation to Allah's will and His supreme authority over all things.
orig: إنما أمره إذا أراد شيئا أن يقول له كن فيكون

translation: So exalted is He in whose hand is the realm of all things, and to Him you will be returned.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute sovereignty and power of Allah over all things in existence. It reminds us that everything is under His control and dominion, and that ultimately, all of mankind will return to Him for judgment in the Hereafter. It is a call to recognize and submit to the supreme authority of Allah, and to live our lives with the awareness that we will be held accountable for our deeds when we stand before Him on the Day of Judgment. The verse encourages humility, reverence, and obedience to Allah, knowing that our ultimate fate rests in His hands.
orig: فسبحان الذي بيده ملكوت كل شيء وإليه ترجعون

translation: By those [angels] lined up in rows
interpretation: This verse is referring to the angels who are standing in rows, ready to carry out Allah's commands. It emphasizes the discipline, obedience, and devotion of the angels to Allah. The angels are lined up in perfect rows, which symbolizes their unwavering commitment to serving Allah and executing His orders without hesitation. This verse serves as a reminder to the believers to strive for similar discipline and devotion in their worship and obedience to Allah.
orig: والصافات صفا

translation: By those [angels] who drive [the clouds]
interpretation: This verse is referring to the angels who drive the clouds and bring about rain by the command of Allah. It is a reminder of Allah's power and control over the natural world, and how He provides sustenance for His creation through the rain. The verse also alludes to the idea that just as the angels obey Allah's commands without question, so too should humans submit to His will and follow His guidance. It is a call to recognize Allah's sovereignty and to live in accordance with His teachings.
orig: فالزاجرات زجرا

translation: By those who recite the Reminder
interpretation: This verse is referring to the angels who recite the Qur'an and convey its message to mankind. It emphasizes the importance of the Qur'an as a reminder and guidance for humanity, and the role of the angels in communicating this divine revelation. The verse also implies that the Qur'an should be frequently recited and remembered by believers, as it is a source of spiritual enlightenment and moral guidance.
orig: فالتاليات ذكرا

translation: Indeed, your God is One.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the fundamental concept of monotheism in Islam, which is the belief in the oneness and uniqueness of God. It affirms that there is only one true God worthy of worship, and that He has no partners, associates, or equals. This belief is the foundation of the Islamic faith and is essential for a person to be considered a Muslim. The verse also implies that all other deities or objects of worship are false and that dedicating one's devotion to anything or anyone other than the One true God is a form of polytheism, which is strictly prohibited in Islam.
orig: إن إلهكم لواحد

translation: Lord of the heavens and the earth and whatever is between them and Lord of the sunrises.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute sovereignty and lordship of Allah over all of creation. He is the Lord and Sustainer of the heavens, the earth, and everything in between them. The specific mention of "sunrises" (in plural form) alludes to the fact that the sun rises from different points on the horizon throughout the year, and Allah is the Lord of all these points of sunrise. It is a reminder for mankind to recognize and submit to the One True God who has ultimate power and control over the entire universe.
orig: رب السماوات والأرض وما بينهما ورب المشارق

translation: Indeed, We have adorned the nearest heaven with an adornment of stars.
interpretation: This verse highlights the beauty and majesty of God's creation. The "nearest heaven" refers to the sky that we can see from Earth, which God has decorated with the breathtaking beauty of the stars. This serves as a reminder of God's power and creativity, and encourages us to appreciate and reflect on the wonders of the universe. The stars not only serve as a magnificent sight, but also as a navigational tool for travelers and a way to determine time and seasons. This adornment is a sign of God's mercy and a means for humans to ponder upon His greatness.
orig: إنا زينا السماء الدنيا بزينة الكواكب

translation: And as a guard against every rebellious devil.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's protection and guardianship over the Qur'an, ensuring that it remains free from any corruption or influence of the devils who seek to lead people astray. It highlights the divine preservation of the Qur'an, safeguarding its integrity and authenticity throughout time. This protection extends to guarding the believers against the whisperings and temptations of the rebellious devils, providing them with spiritual security and guidance as they engage with the Qur'an.
orig: وحفظا من كل شيطان مارد

translation: They cannot listen to the exalted assembly and are pelted from every side.
interpretation: This verse refers to the devils who try to eavesdrop on the discussions of the angels in the heavens. They are prevented from doing so by being pelted with shooting stars from every direction. It signifies that the revelations and divine secrets are protected from the interference of evil forces. The "exalted assembly" likely refers to the gathering of angels in the higher realms. The pelting of the devils with stars symbolizes driving them away and guarding the sanctity of divine communications.
orig: لا يسمعون إلى الملإ الأعلى ويقذفون من كل جانب

translation: Repelled [from the mercy of Allah], and for them is a perpetual punishment.
interpretation: This verse speaks about the fate of those who reject Allah's guidance and persist in disbelief. They will be cast away from Allah's mercy and subjected to a never-ending punishment in the Hereafter. The word "واصب" emphasizes the continuous and unrelenting nature of this punishment, indicating that there will be no relief or respite for those who have earned Allah's wrath through their actions in this world. It serves as a stern warning for mankind to heed the message of Islam and strive for righteousness before it is too late.
orig: دحورا ولهم عذاب واصب

translation: Except one who snatches [some words] by theft, but they are pursued by a burning flame, piercing [in brightness].
interpretation: This verse refers to the devils who try to eavesdrop on the conversations of the angels in the heavens to gain knowledge of the future. However, they are chased away by bright, piercing flames (meteors) that prevent them from listening or pose a punishment for their attempt. It highlights the divine protection over the revelation and the unseen knowledge, ensuring that no evil forces can access or tamper with it without facing consequences.
orig: إلا من خطف الخطفة فأتبعه شهاب ثاقب

translation: Then ask them whether they are a stronger creation or those [others] We have created. Indeed, We created them from sticky clay.
interpretation: This verse is a reminder of God's power and the weakness of human beings in comparison. It challenges those who deny the resurrection and God's ability to recreate life after death. The verse implies that if God can create human beings from a humble material like clay, then surely He is capable of bringing them back to life after death. It emphasizes the supreme power and wisdom of God, while exposing the arrogance and shortsightedness of those who question or deny His abilities. The verse encourages humility, faith, and recognition of our total dependence on God.
orig: فاستفتهم أهم أشد خلقا أم من خلقنا إنا خلقناهم من طين لازب

translation: But you wonder, while they mock,
interpretation: This verse highlights the contrast between the reaction of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and the disbelievers to the message of Islam. The Prophet is amazed at their rejection of the truth, while they respond with ridicule and mockery. This interpretation suggests that the disbelievers are unable to comprehend the profound wisdom and guidance contained within the Qur'an, and instead resort to derision as a means of dismissing its message. It also emphasizes the patience and perseverance of the Prophet in the face of such opposition, as he remains steadfast in his faith and continues to marvel at the revelation he has received, despite the negative reactions of those around him.
orig: بل عجبت ويسخرون

translation: And when they are reminded, they do not remember.
interpretation: This verse is referring to those who are heedless and do not take heed of the reminders and warnings that come to them. Even when they are reminded of Allah and His messages, they do not pay attention or take them to heart. They remain forgetful and neglectful, not remembering the purpose of their existence or the consequences of their actions. This state of heedlessness is a major barrier to faith and righteousness, as it prevents people from reflecting on the signs of Allah and responding to His call.
orig: وإذا ذكروا لا يذكرون

translation: And when they see a sign, they ridicule.
interpretation: This verse is referring to the disbelievers who, when they are presented with clear signs and evidence of Allah's existence and power, they respond with mockery and derision instead of taking them seriously and reflecting upon them. It highlights their arrogance and closed-mindedness in the face of the truth. They are so engrossed in their worldly life and desires that they fail to recognize and appreciate the signs of Allah all around them, and instead resort to ridiculing them out of ignorance and stubbornness.
orig: وإذا رأوا آية يستسخرون

translation: And they said, "This is nothing but obvious magic."
interpretation: This verse refers to the disbelievers who, upon witnessing the clear signs and miracles of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him), dismissed them as mere magic or sorcery. They refused to acknowledge the divine nature of the Qur'an and the prophethood of Muhammad, attributing his teachings to magic rather than accepting them as the truth from Allah. This interpretation highlights the stubborn nature of those who reject faith, even when presented with compelling evidence, and their tendency to find alternative explanations that align with their preconceived notions and desires.
orig: وقالوا إن هذا إلا سحر مبين

translation: When we have died and become dust and bones, are we indeed to be resurrected?
interpretation: This verse is questioning the idea of resurrection after death, when the body has decomposed into dust and bones. It reflects the skepticism or disbelief of some people regarding the concept of being brought back to life after death for judgment by Allah. The rhetorical question implies doubt about the possibility or likelihood of such an event actually occurring. It suggests that for some, the idea of being resurrected in the Hereafter after one's body has disintegrated seems far-fetched or implausible from a human worldview, hence the incredulous tone of the question.
orig: أإذا متنا وكنا ترابا وعظاما أإنا لمبعوثون

translation: Or our forefathers of old?
interpretation: This verse is questioning the belief in following the traditions and practices of one's ancestors without critical examination. It suggests that people should not blindly adhere to the ways of their forefathers, but rather use their own reason and judgment to determine what is right and true. The Qur'an encourages individuals to think for themselves and not simply accept inherited beliefs or customs without reflection.
orig: أوآباؤنا الأولون

translation: Say, "Yes, and you will be humbled."
interpretation: This verse is a warning to those who reject the message of Islam and the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him). It emphasizes that even if they deny the truth now, a day will come when they will have to acknowledge it, but it will be too late and they will find themselves humiliated and debased before Allah. This interpretation highlights the consequences of rejecting the truth and the importance of accepting the message of Islam before it is too late.
orig: قل نعم وأنتم داخرون

translation: Then it will only be a single shout, and at once they will be observing.
interpretation: This verse is referring to the Day of Judgment. It suggests that the onset of the Day of Judgment will be sudden and swift, marked by a single mighty blast. After this shout or blast, all of mankind will be instantly resurrected and will find themselves facing the reality of the Hereafter, observing the events unfolding before them. The verse emphasizes the idea that the transition from this worldly life to the eternal life of the Hereafter will be extraordinarily rapid, leaving no time for preparation or escape. It serves as a reminder for people to be always mindful of the inevitability of death and the Day of Judgment, and to live their lives accordingly in obedience and submission to Allah.
orig: فإنما هي زجرة واحدة فإذا هم ينظرون

translation: And they will say, "O woe to us! This is the Day of Recompense."
interpretation: This verse is referring to the Day of Judgment, when people will realize the consequences of their actions in this world. The phrase "O woe to us" expresses their deep regret and sorrow upon understanding the gravity of their situation. It emphasizes the concept of accountability, as everyone will be held responsible for their deeds and will face the ultimate justice on that day. The verse serves as a reminder for people to be mindful of their actions in this life, as they will have a profound impact on their fate in the hereafter.
orig: وقالوا يا ويلنا هذا يوم الدين

translation: That is the Day of Judgement which you used to deny.
interpretation: This verse is a stark reminder to those who rejected the reality of the Day of Judgement during their worldly lives. It emphasizes that the Day they were warned about and denied is now upon them, and they can no longer escape facing the consequences of their actions and beliefs. The verse implies a sense of regret and realization for the deniers, as the truth they refused to acknowledge is now undeniable. It also serves as a warning to believers to remain steadfast in their faith and to prepare for this inevitable event through righteous deeds and obedience to Allah's commands.
orig: هذا يوم الفصل الذي كنتم به تكذبون

translation: Gather those who did wrong, their kinds, and what they used to worship
interpretation: This verse is referring to the Day of Judgment, when the wrongdoers will be gathered together with those who were similar to them in their actions and beliefs, as well as the false deities or idols that they used to worship instead of Allah. It emphasizes the severity of their punishment, as they will be confronted with the very things they placed their faith in besides Allah. The gathering of the wrongdoers with their "kinds" or associates also suggests that they will share in each other's punishment, as they supported and encouraged one another in their wrongdoing and disbelief in this world.
orig: احشروا الذين ظلموا وأزواجهم وما كانوا يعبدون

translation: Other than Allah, so guide them to the path of Hell.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that those who follow guides other than Allah are misguided and will be led astray to the path of Hell. It implies that Allah is the only true guide and that following any other path or ideology will ultimately lead to damnation and suffering in the Hereafter. The verse serves as a warning to believers to stay steadfast in their faith and to avoid being swayed by false guides or temptations that lead away from Allah's straight path.
orig: من دون الله فاهدوهم إلى صراط الجحيم

translation: But stop them; indeed, they are to be questioned.
interpretation: This verse is referring to the Day of Judgment when the disbelievers will be stopped and held accountable for their actions in this world. They will be questioned about their deeds, their beliefs, and their rejection of the truth that was brought to them by the prophets. This questioning will expose their guilt and the justice of Allah's judgment upon them. It serves as a reminder to all people that we will be held responsible for our choices and actions in this life, and that we should strive to live righteously and follow the guidance of Allah to avoid a terrible fate in the Hereafter.
orig: وقفوهم إنهم مسئولون

translation: What is [the matter] with you that you do not aid...
interpretation: This verse is questioning why the addressees are not coming to the aid and support of someone or some cause. It is rebuking them for their lack of willingness to help and assist in a time of need. The verse is criticizing their inaction and apathy, and urging them to step up and provide the necessary support and aid to those who require it. It highlights the importance of solidarity, cooperation and coming to the aid of others, especially in difficult times.
orig: ما لكم لا تناصرون

translation: But they, today, are in surrender.
interpretation: This verse suggests that on the Day of Judgment, the disbelievers who once opposed the message of Islam will find themselves in a state of complete submission and surrender to Allah's will. They will realize the truth and the consequences of their actions, but it will be too late for them to change their fate. The verse emphasizes the finality of judgment and the ultimate submission of all beings to Allah's authority.
orig: بل هم اليوم مستسلمون

translation: And they will approach one another, inquiring of each other.
interpretation: This verse refers to the Day of Judgment when people will turn to each other, asking about their deeds and the reasons behind their fate. It signifies the realization of the consequences of one's actions in the worldly life and the curiosity about how others fared. This inquiry among people highlights the importance of being mindful of one's conduct, as everyone will be held accountable for their deeds on that Day. It also emphasizes the significance of maintaining good relationships with others, as people will be interested in knowing about each other's outcomes in the Hereafter.
orig: وأقبل بعضهم على بعض يتساءلون

translation: They will say, "Indeed, you used to come at us from the right."
interpretation: This verse is interpreted to mean that on the Day of Judgment, the disbelievers will blame the believers for misleading them and preventing them from following the truth. The phrase "from the right" is understood to mean that the believers approached the disbelievers with the truth and tried to guide them to the right path, but the disbelievers refused to listen and follow. It shows the regret and blame-shifting of the disbelievers when faced with the consequences of their actions and their rejection of the message brought to them by the believers during their worldly lives.
orig: قالوا إنكم كنتم تأتوننا عن اليمين

translation: They said, "Rather, you were not believers."
interpretation: In this verse, the disbelievers are being rebuked by the believers in the Hereafter. The believers are telling the disbelievers that their claim of faith in this world was false and insincere. They never truly believed in Allah and His messengers, and their actions and intentions contradicted any outward proclamation of faith they might have made. This highlights the importance of sincerity and consistency in faith, and that mere lip service is not enough to be considered a true believer in the sight of Allah.
orig: قالوا بل لم تكونوا مؤمنين

translation: And we had no authority over you, but you were a transgressing people.
interpretation: This verse is addressing the disbelievers on the Day of Judgment. The leaders or the followed will declare that they did not have any power or authority over their followers to compel them to disbelief or transgression. Rather, it was the people themselves who willfully chose to exceed the limits set by Allah and indulge in sins and disobedience. The verse emphasizes personal responsibility and accountability for one's actions and choices. It negates the argument of the sinners that they were merely following their leaders or were under their influence, thus asserting that every soul is answerable for its own deeds.
orig: وما كان لنا عليكم من سلطان بل كنتم قوما طاغين

translation: So the word of our Lord has come into effect upon us: Indeed, we will taste [punishment].
interpretation: This verse conveys the realization and admission by the sinners in the Hereafter that they are deservedly facing the consequences of their actions. They acknowledge that Allah's warning of punishment for their wrongdoings has come true, and they are now experiencing the "taste" of that punishment. It highlights the concept of divine justice, emphasizing that no one can escape the consequences of their deeds and that Allah's words and promises will inevitably come to pass. The verse also serves as a reminder for believers to be mindful of their actions in this world, as they will be held accountable in the Hereafter.
orig: فحق علينا قول ربنا إنا لذائقون

translation: So we led you astray; indeed, we were ourselves astray.
interpretation: This verse suggests that those who lead others astray are themselves misguided and astray from the right path. It implies that the blind cannot lead the blind, and that those who are themselves misguided cannot provide proper guidance to others. The verse also highlights the concept of personal responsibility, as those who follow misguided leaders will still be held accountable for their own actions and choices. Ultimately, it emphasizes the importance of seeking guidance from the divine source and not being swayed by those who are themselves far from the truth.
orig: فأغويناكم إنا كنا غاوين

translation: For indeed they, that Day, will be sharing in the punishment.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the severity and universality of the punishment that will befall the disbelievers on the Day of Judgment. It suggests that all those who rejected faith and acted wrongfully will face the consequences together, sharing in the torment and suffering. The use of the word "sharing" implies that the punishment will be experienced collectively, highlighting the idea that no one will be exempt or able to escape the divine retribution for their actions in this world. This interpretation underscores the Qur'an's repeated warnings about the importance of faith, righteousness, and being mindful of the Day of Judgment.
orig: فإنهم يومئذ في العذاب مشتركون

translation: Indeed, thus do We deal with the criminals.
interpretation: This verse highlights the justice and fairness of Allah in dealing with those who commit crimes and sins. It serves as a warning to wrongdoers that they will face the consequences of their actions in accordance with divine law. The use of "We" emphasizes Allah's power and authority in executing judgment. The verse also implies that this is a consistent and established way in which Allah deals with criminals, indicating that no one can escape His justice. It serves as a reminder for believers to stay on the right path and for sinners to repent before facing the consequences of their deeds.
orig: إنا كذلك نفعل بالمجرمين

translation: Indeed, they, when it was said to them, "There is no deity but Allah," were arrogant.
interpretation: This verse highlights the arrogance and pride of the disbelievers who, when reminded of the fundamental truth that there is no god worthy of worship except Allah, respond with disdain and rejection. It underscores their unwillingness to submit to the oneness of Allah and their persistence in associating partners with Him. The verse implies that acknowledging the unity of Allah requires humility and the abandonment of one's ego, which the disbelievers are unwilling to do due to their self-importance and attachment to false deities.
orig: إنهم كانوا إذا قيل لهم لا إله إلا الله يستكبرون

translation: And they say, "Are we to leave our gods for a mad poet?"
interpretation: This verse reflects the disbelief and stubbornness of the polytheists who rejected the message of Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him). They were so attached to their false deities that they could not fathom the idea of abandoning them for the worship of the One True God, Allah. They dismissed the Prophet as a mere poet who had gone insane, refusing to acknowledge the divine truth of his message. This highlights the arrogance and closed-mindedness of those who cling to false beliefs, even when presented with clear evidence of the truth.
orig: ويقولون أئنا لتاركو آلهتنا لشاعر مجنون

translation: Rather, he came with the truth and confirmed the [previous] messengers.
interpretation: This verse affirms that Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him, came with the truth from Allah and confirmed the message of the messengers who came before him. It emphasizes the continuity and consistency of the divine message throughout history, and that Muhammad's prophethood is a continuation and culmination of the previous prophetic missions. The verse also implies that the Qur'an, revealed to Muhammad, is the ultimate truth that validates and supports the teachings of the earlier prophets and scriptures.
orig: بل جاء بالحق وصدق المرسلين

translation: Indeed, you will be tasters of the painful punishment.
interpretation: This verse is a stern warning from Allah to the disbelievers and wrongdoers. It emphasizes that they will certainly face a severe and agonizing punishment in the Hereafter as a consequence of their rejection of faith and persistence in evil deeds. The use of the word "tasters" suggests that they will directly experience and suffer the torment. It serves as a reminder of the gravity of their actions and the inescapable justice of Allah. The verse aims to instill fear in the hearts of the disobedient and encourage them to repent and follow the right path before it is too late.
orig: إنكم لذائقو العذاب الأليم

translation: And you are not recompensed except for what you used to do.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the principle of individual responsibility and the concept of divine justice in Islam. It suggests that on the Day of Judgment, each person will be held accountable for their deeds and actions in this worldly life. The recompense or reward one receives in the Hereafter will be based solely on their own conduct, good or bad, and not on factors like wealth, status, or lineage. This interpretation highlights the importance of leading a righteous life and being mindful of one's actions, as they will have consequences in the afterlife according to God's justice.
orig: وما تجزون إلا ما كنتم تعملون

translation: Except the chosen servants of Allah.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that only the sincere and devoted servants of Allah, who are steadfast in their faith and righteous deeds, will be saved from the temptations and deceptions of Satan. These chosen servants have purified their hearts and intentions, seeking only to please Allah and follow His guidance. They are protected by their unwavering commitment to Allah and their resistance to the whisperings of the devil. This verse serves as a reminder that true salvation lies in being among the sincere and faithful servants of Allah.
orig: إلا عباد الله المخلصين

translation: Those will have a provision determined
interpretation: This verse refers to the believers who will be granted a predetermined provision in Paradise as a reward for their faith and good deeds in this world. The "provision determined" indicates that their sustenance in the Hereafter is guaranteed, abundant, and will never be diminished or interrupted. It is a promise from Allah to His faithful servants, assuring them of a generous and everlasting reward for their dedication and righteousness.
orig: أولئك لهم رزق معلوم

translation: Fruits, and they will be honored.
interpretation: This verse refers to the blessings and rewards that the righteous will receive in Paradise. The mention of fruits suggests that they will have access to an abundance of delightful and nourishing sustenance. The honor bestowed upon them indicates that they will be treated with the utmost respect and dignity, as a reward for their good deeds and devotion to Allah during their worldly life. This verse aims to motivate believers to strive for righteousness, knowing that their efforts will be greatly appreciated and rewarded in the Hereafter.
orig: فواكه وهم مكرمون

translation: In the Gardens of Bliss.
interpretation: This verse refers to the eternal reward that awaits the righteous believers in Paradise. The "Gardens of Bliss" represent the ultimate abode of peace, happiness, and fulfillment, where the faithful will enjoy the countless blessings and delights bestowed upon them by Allah as a recompense for their good deeds and unwavering devotion in this worldly life. It symbolizes the supreme success and the highest aspiration for every believer, to be admitted into these gardens and to experience the unimaginable joy and contentment in the presence of their Lord.
orig: في جنات النعيم

translation: On thrones facing each other.
interpretation: This verse is describing the seating arrangement of the people of Paradise. They will be seated on thrones or couches facing each other, which suggests a sense of intimacy, friendship, and social interaction among the inhabitants of Paradise. The verse paints a picture of a pleasant and comfortable setting where people can enjoy each other's company and engage in meaningful conversations. It highlights the social aspect of Paradise and the joy of being reunited with loved ones and friends in an atmosphere of peace and tranquility.
orig: على سرر متقابلين

translation: There will be passed round to them a cup [of wine] from a flowing spring,
interpretation: In Paradise, the righteous believers will be served cups of pure, delightful wine from a flowing spring. This symbolizes the endless blessings and pleasures that await them as a reward for their faith and good deeds in this worldly life. The flowing spring represents the abundance and continuity of these divine favors, which will never cease or diminish. This verse paints a picture of the unimaginable bliss and satisfaction that the inhabitants of Paradise will experience for eternity.
orig: يطاف عليهم بكأس من معين

translation: White, delicious to the drinkers.
interpretation: This verse is referring to the wine of Paradise, which is described as being white in color and delicious to those who drink it. The verse emphasizes the pleasure and enjoyment that the believers will experience in Paradise, where they will be served with the finest drink that is pure, refreshing, and tasty. This is a reward for their good deeds and righteousness in this world.
orig: بيضاء لذة للشاربين

translation: No bad effect is there in it, nor from it will they be intoxicated.
interpretation: This verse is referring to the wine of Paradise, which is pure and does not cause any intoxication or harmful effects like the wine in this world. The believers will be able to enjoy it without any negative consequences or loss of self-control. This emphasizes the perfection and pleasures of Paradise, where even the drinks are free from the flaws and harms experienced in the worldly life.
orig: لا فيها غول ولا هم عنها ينزفون

translation: And with them will be companions of modest gaze having beautiful eyes.
interpretation: This verse refers to the companions in Paradise, described as having a modest gaze and beautiful eyes. The interpretation is that these companions, often understood as the Hoor al-Ayn (Houris), are pure, chaste, and loyal. Their modest gaze signifies their devotion and faithfulness to their partners in Paradise. The mention of their beautiful eyes is a metaphor for their overall beauty and allure, both inward and outward. These companions serve as a reward for the righteous believers in the afterlife, representing the ultimate companionship and comfort after a life of faith and good deeds.
orig: وعندهم قاصرات الطرف عين

translation: As if they were [delicate] eggs, well-protected.
interpretation: This verse uses the metaphor of well-protected eggs to describe the beauty and purity of the women in Paradise. Just as eggs are delicate and carefully guarded, the women of Paradise are pristine, untouched, and protected from any imperfection or defilement. This metaphor emphasizes their immense value, refinement, and the perfect care and honor they receive in the afterlife as a reward for their righteousness.
orig: كأنهن بيض مكنون

translation: Then they turned to one another, questioning each other.
interpretation: This verse suggests that after a significant event or realization, people turned to each other seeking answers and engaging in dialogue. It implies a sense of confusion, curiosity, or a desire for understanding among the people. The act of questioning one another indicates a need for clarity, explanation, or a shared exploration of the matter at hand. This verse highlights the human tendency to seek knowledge, communicate, and rely on social interaction to make sense of complex situations or profound experiences.
orig: فأقبل بعضهم على بعض يتساءلون

translation: A speaker from among them will say, "Indeed, I had a companion
interpretation: This verse is referring to the Day of Judgment, when the disbelievers will speak about their evil companions who misled them in the worldly life. The speaker is expressing regret and remorse for having followed someone who led them astray from the right path. This highlights the importance of choosing righteous companions and friends who encourage one towards goodness and righteousness, rather than those who incite towards sin and disobedience to Allah. It also emphasizes the individual responsibility each person bears for their own actions and decisions, as on the Day of Judgment, no one will be able to help another or intercede on their behalf except by Allah's permission.
orig: قال قائل منهم إني كان لي قرين

translation: He said, "Do you really believe?"
interpretation: This verse is questioning the sincerity and depth of someone's belief or acceptance of a message. It suggests a sense of doubt or skepticism from the speaker about whether the person being addressed truly believes with conviction, or if their belief is perhaps superficial or insincere. The speaker seems to be looking for reassurance or evidence of genuine faith and commitment from the one being questioned.
orig: يقول أإنك لمن المصدقين

translation: When we have died and become dust and bones, are we indeed to be resurrected?
interpretation: This verse questions the idea of resurrection after death, when the human body has decomposed into dust and bones. It expresses skepticism or doubt about the possibility of being brought back to life and held accountable for one's deeds after the physical body has disintegrated. The verse challenges the concept of life after death and the ultimate divine judgment, reflecting the disbelief or uncertainty of those who raise this question.
orig: أإذا متنا وكنا ترابا وعظاما أإنا لمدينون

translation: He said, "Do you [angels] look in [on the record of deeds]?"
interpretation: This verse is a rhetorical question posed by Allah to the angels, asking if they have access to the records of people's deeds. It implies that only Allah has full knowledge of what people do and what is in their hearts, and that He alone can judge them fairly on the Day of Judgment. The verse reminds us that we should be mindful of our actions and intentions, as they are all recorded and will be presented before Allah for judgment.
orig: قال هل أنتم مطلعون

translation: And he looked and saw him in the midst of the Blazing Fire.
interpretation: This verse refers to the fate of those who reject faith and do evil deeds. The "he" in this verse is generally understood to be an unbeliever who, upon death, will see his final abode in the depths of Hell. It conveys the idea that the unbeliever will directly witness the reality of the punishment that awaits him as a consequence of his actions and disbelief. The verse emphasizes the severity and central location of his punishment within the Blazing Fire of Hell, underscoring the gravity of rejecting faith and the ultimate outcome for those who choose that path.
orig: فاطلع فرآه في سواء الجحيم

translation: He said, "By Allah, you almost ruined me."
interpretation: This verse is a rebuke or an expression of frustration by someone who feels that they were almost led astray or caused to deviate from the right path by the actions or influence of another person. It emphasizes the gravity of the situation and how close the speaker came to being "ruined" in some way, whether spiritually, morally, or otherwise. The invocation of Allah's name ("By Allah") underscores the seriousness and sincerity of the statement, as the speaker calls upon God as a witness to the truth of their words and the intensity of their feelings.
orig: قال تالله إن كدت لتردين

translation: And had it not been for the favor of my Lord, I would have been of those brought [to Hell].
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of God's grace and mercy in guiding and protecting individuals from falling into sin and ultimately being condemned to Hell. It suggests that without God's favor, one would easily succumb to temptations and wrongdoings, leading to dire consequences in the afterlife. The verse serves as a reminder for believers to constantly seek and appreciate God's guidance, as it is only through His favor that one can hope to avoid the fate of those who are brought to Hell due to their transgressions.
orig: ولولا نعمة ربي لكنت من المحضرين

translation: Then, are we not to die
interpretation: This verse is a rhetorical question that emphasizes the inevitability of death. It reminds us that all living beings, including humans, will eventually face death and that there is no escape from this reality. The verse encourages reflection on the temporary nature of worldly life and the importance of preparing for the eternal afterlife through righteous deeds and faith in Allah. It also highlights the power and control of Allah over life and death, as He is the One who determines when each soul will depart from this world.
orig: أفما نحن بميتين

translation: Except our first death, and we will not be punished.
interpretation: This verse suggests that the disbelievers believe that they will only experience death once in this world, and after that they will not be resurrected or punished by Allah in the Hereafter for their disbelief and misdeeds. It reflects their denial of the concept of resurrection and divine accountability. The Qur'an refutes this notion by affirming that there will indeed be a resurrection and judgment, where people will be held accountable for their deeds and beliefs in this worldly life.
orig: إلا موتتنا الأولى وما نحن بمعذبين

translation: Indeed, this is the great attainment.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the immense significance and value of attaining Paradise and earning Allah's pleasure. It suggests that there is no greater success or achievement in the life of a believer than entering Paradise and being saved from the Fire. The word "al-fawz" (attainment, success) is further emphasized with the adjective "al-adheem" (great, tremendous), indicating that this is not just any ordinary success, but the ultimate triumph and fulfillment of the believer's aspirations and struggles in this world. It is a reminder for the believers to keep striving for this noble goal.
orig: إن هذا لهو الفوز العظيم

translation: For the like of this let the workers [on earth] work.
interpretation: This verse encourages people to strive and work hard in this worldly life for the ultimate reward in the Hereafter. It suggests that those who desire the blissful abode of Paradise should direct their efforts towards righteousness and good deeds. The verse motivates believers to dedicate themselves to actions that please Allah, seeking His reward and the eternal delights of the Hereafter, rather than being consumed by temporary worldly gains. It is a reminder that the life of this world is fleeting, and that the true purpose of our existence is to work towards attaining the everlasting joy and contentment in the presence of our Lord.
orig: لمثل هذا فليعمل العاملون

translation: Is that [Paradise] better as accommodation or the tree of Zaqqum?
interpretation: This verse is a rhetorical question that highlights the stark contrast between the bliss of Paradise and the torment of Hell. The tree of Zaqqum, described in the Qur'an as a tree that grows in the depths of Hell, serves as a symbol of the terrible punishment that awaits the disbelievers. Its fruit is described as being like the heads of devils, emphasizing its hideousness and the suffering it brings. By comparing Paradise to this dreadful tree, the verse underscores the vastly different fates that await the righteous and the wicked in the Hereafter, reminding us of the importance of faith and good deeds in this life.
orig: أذلك خير نزلا أم شجرة الزقوم

translation: Indeed, We have made it a trial for the wrongdoers.
interpretation: This verse refers to the tree of Zaqqum, which is mentioned in the previous verses. Allah has made this tree a test and a punishment for the wrongdoers and the disbelievers in the Hereafter. The tree of Zaqqum is described as a tree that springs from the bottom of Hell, and its fruits are like the heads of devils. The wrongdoers will be forced to eat from it, even though it will neither nourish them nor satisfy their hunger. This verse emphasizes that Allah has the power to create whatever He wills, and that He can use His creation to test and punish those who reject His messages and transgress His limits.
orig: إنا جعلناها فتنة للظالمين

translation: Indeed, it is a tree that emerges from the bottom of the Hellfire.
interpretation: This verse is referring to the tree of Zaqqum, a horrifying tree that grows in the depths of Hell. Its mention serves as a warning and reminder of the severe punishment that awaits the disbelievers and sinners in the afterlife. The tree of Zaqqum is described as having fruits that resemble the heads of devils, and its consumption will only increase the torment of those in Hell. This description aims to instill fear in people's hearts and encourage them to avoid sins and disobedience to Allah, seeking instead His mercy and forgiveness to be saved from such a dreadful fate.
orig: إنها شجرة تخرج في أصل الجحيم

translation: Its produce is as if it was heads of the devils.
interpretation: This verse uses a metaphor to describe the terrible appearance and nature of the fruit of the tree of Zaqqum in Hell. The comparison of the fruit to the heads of devils emphasizes its ugliness and repulsiveness, indicating that it is extremely unpleasant and fitting as a punishment for the denizens of Hell. The metaphor also suggests that the tree and its fruit are evil and associated with Satan and his minions. The verse serves as a warning to evildoers about the severe consequences and torments awaiting them in the afterlife if they do not repent and follow the righteous path.
orig: طلعها كأنه رءوس الشياطين

translation: Then indeed, they [the disbelievers] will eat from it [the tree of Zaqqum] and fill their bellies with it.
interpretation: This verse is a warning to the disbelievers about the punishment that awaits them in Hell. The tree of Zaqqum is described as a tree that grows in the depths of Hell, bearing fruits that resemble the heads of devils. The disbelievers will be forced to eat from this tree, filling their bellies with its bitter and disgusting fruits as a form of torment. This punishment is a consequence of their rejection of faith and their arrogance in denying the truth of Allah's message. The verse serves as a reminder of the severe consequences of disbelief and the importance of accepting the guidance of Allah in this life.
orig: فإنهم لآكلون منها فمالئون منها البطون

translation: Moreover, they will have a mixture of boiling water.
interpretation: This verse is referring to the punishment that awaits the disbelievers in the Hereafter. The "mixture of boiling water" is a metaphor for the intense suffering and torment they will experience as a consequence of their rejection of faith and their evil deeds in this world. The scalding liquid symbolizes the severity and pain of the punishment, reflecting the gravity of their sins. This interpretation highlights the Qur'an's warning to humanity about the ultimate consequences of leading a life without belief and righteousness.
orig: ثم إن لهم عليها لشوبا من حميم

translation: Then indeed, their return will be to the Hellfire.
interpretation: This verse serves as a stern warning and reminder that those who reject faith and persist in wrongdoing will ultimately face the consequences of their actions in the Hereafter. It emphasizes that their final destination will be the Hellfire, a place of severe punishment and suffering. The verse aims to instill fear and encourage individuals to reflect upon their deeds and seek repentance before it is too late, as the Hellfire awaits those who deviate from the righteous path and fail to heed the guidance of Allah.
orig: ثم إن مرجعهم لإلى الجحيم

translation: Indeed, they found their fathers astray.
interpretation: This verse is referring to the fact that many people blindly follow the misguided ways and beliefs of their ancestors without questioning them. They simply accept the false traditions and erroneous practices that have been passed down, even though these are leading them astray from the straight path and the truth of Islam. The Qur'an is urging people to critically examine what they have inherited from their forefathers and to abandon those things which are not in line with divine guidance, rather than just imitating them out of blind loyalty or cultural inertia.
orig: إنهم ألفوا آباءهم ضالين

translation: So upon their footsteps they hastened [to follow].
interpretation: This verse refers to the people who followed the messengers sent by God without hesitation or delay. They were eager to follow the guidance and teachings brought by the messengers, and they hastened to do so, following closely in their footsteps. This demonstrates their strong faith, sincerity, and willingness to submit to the truth and embrace the message of God as soon as it reached them.
orig: فهم على آثارهم يهرعون

translation: And indeed, before them, most of the former peoples went astray
interpretation: This verse is a reminder that throughout history, many nations and peoples before the time of Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) had also gone astray from the right path and the guidance of Allah. They rejected the messengers sent to them and followed their own desires and false beliefs instead. This serves as a warning to the people of the present to learn from the mistakes of the past and to follow the straight path of Islam, as revealed in the Qur'an and taught by the Prophet, in order to avoid the same fate as those who went astray before them.
orig: ولقد ضل قبلهم أكثر الأولين

translation: And We had certainly sent among them warners.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah sent messengers and prophets to various nations and communities throughout history to warn them of the consequences of their wrongdoings and to guide them to the right path. These warners were sent to remind people of their purpose in life, which is to worship Allah alone and follow His guidance. The role of these messengers was to convey the divine message clearly and to serve as a reminder for people to mend their ways before it is too late. This verse highlights Allah's mercy and justice, as He does not punish any nation without first sending them a messenger to warn them and give them a chance to repent and reform.
orig: ولقد أرسلنا فيهم منذرين

translation: Then see how was the end of those who were warned
interpretation: This verse is a reminder for people to reflect on the fate of those who were warned by the prophets and messengers in the past, but chose to ignore or reject their warnings. It implies that those who disregarded the divine message faced severe consequences and punishment for their disobedience and wrongdoings. The verse encourages believers to learn from the lessons of history and not to follow in the footsteps of those who were destroyed due to their defiance of God's guidance. It also serves as a warning for those who persist in their disbelief and transgression, reminding them that they, too, will face the consequences of their actions if they do not heed the warnings and embrace the truth.
orig: فانظر كيف كان عاقبة المنذرين

translation: Except the chosen servants of Allah.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that only the sincere and devoted servants of Allah, who are steadfast in their faith and righteous deeds, will be saved from the temptations and deceptions of Satan. These chosen servants have purified their hearts and intentions, seeking only to please Allah and follow His guidance. They are protected by their unwavering commitment to Allah and their resistance to the whisperings of the devil. This verse serves as a reminder that true salvation lies in complete submission to Allah and sincere devotion to His cause.
orig: إلا عباد الله المخلصين

translation: And certainly did Noah call Us, and [We are] the best of responders.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's responsiveness and attentiveness to the sincere prayers and supplications of His servants. When Prophet Noah called upon Allah for help and guidance, Allah responded to him in the best possible manner, providing him with support, protection, and deliverance from the disbelieving people. This verse serves as a reminder to the believers that Allah is always ready to answer the prayers of those who turn to Him with sincerity and faith, and that He is the best of all responders, providing the most suitable and beneficial answers to the needs of His servants.
orig: ولقد نادانا نوح فلنعم المجيبون

translation: And We delivered him and his family from the great distress.
interpretation: This verse refers to the story of Prophet Noah (peace be upon him). It indicates that after the great flood that destroyed the disbelievers, Allah saved Noah and his family, as well as the believers who followed him, from the immense hardship and suffering they endured. It demonstrates Allah's mercy and protection towards His righteous servants who remain steadfast in faith and obedience, even in the face of severe trials and challenges. The verse also serves as a reminder that no matter how difficult our circumstances may be, if we turn to Allah and trust in Him, He will deliver us from hardship and grant us relief and salvation, just as He did for Noah and his family.
orig: ونجيناه وأهله من الكرب العظيم

translation: And We made his offspring the survivors.
interpretation: This verse refers to the Prophet Noah (peace be upon him) and his descendants after the Great Flood. It indicates that Allah saved Noah and his followers on the Ark, while the disbelievers were drowned. After the flood, only Noah's offspring remained to repopulate the earth. This shows Allah's favor upon Noah and his righteous descendants, as He chose them to be the survivors and the progenitors of future generations of humanity. It also demonstrates that the righteous will ultimately prevail, while those who reject Allah's message will perish.
orig: وجعلنا ذريته هم الباقين

translation: And We left for him [favorable mention] among later generations:
interpretation: This verse refers to the legacy and reputation of Prophet Solomon (peace be upon him). It indicates that due to Solomon's righteousness, wisdom, and devotion to Allah, he was blessed with a lasting positive remembrance among the generations after him. His story and example serve as an inspiration and model for those who came later, leaving a profound impact on human history. The verse emphasizes the importance of leading a virtuous life and striving for Allah's pleasure, as it can lead to a positive lasting legacy that endures long after one's worldly life comes to an end.
orig: وتركنا عليه في الآخرين

translation: Peace be upon Noah among the worlds.
interpretation: This verse conveys a greeting of peace upon the prophet Noah (Nuh) and acknowledges his high status among all nations and peoples across the worlds. It signifies that Noah is not only honored and respected by Muslims but is also recognized as a great prophet by all of humanity. The verse emphasizes the universal message of Islam and its reverence for all the prophets sent by Allah throughout history to guide mankind.
orig: سلام على نوح في العالمين

translation: Indeed, We thus reward the doers of good.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah rewards those who do good deeds and live righteously. It serves as an encouragement and promise to the believers that their good actions will not go unnoticed or unrewarded by Allah. The use of "We" in this verse refers to Allah Himself, indicating His direct involvement in recognizing and recompensing the righteous. This interpretation highlights the importance of striving to do good in one's life, as it will lead to blessings and rewards from Allah in this world and the Hereafter.
orig: إنا كذلك نجزي المحسنين

translation: Indeed, he was of Our believing servants.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the person being referred to was a true believer and a devoted servant of Allah. It highlights the importance of faith and submission to God's will. The use of the pronoun "Our" indicates the special status and closeness of this individual to Allah. It suggests that through his strong belief and righteous deeds, he attained a high rank among the believers and earned Allah's pleasure and recognition.
orig: إنه من عبادنا المؤمنين

translation: Then We drowned the others.
interpretation: This verse refers to the fate of those who rejected the message of Allah and opposed His prophets. After saving the believers who followed the prophets, Allah caused the disbelievers to drown as a punishment for their defiance and wrongdoing. It serves as a reminder that those who persist in disbelief and rebellion against Allah will ultimately face a severe consequence for their actions, while those who have faith and follow the guidance of the prophets will be saved by Allah's mercy.
orig: ثم أغرقنا الآخرين

translation: And indeed, among his followers was Abraham.
interpretation: This verse highlights the fact that Prophet Abraham was a follower of the same monotheistic message that was later preached by Prophet Muhammad. It establishes a connection between the two prophets and emphasizes the continuity of the divine message throughout history. The verse suggests that Abraham was a part of the same spiritual tradition and followed the teachings of submission to the One God, which is the essence of Islam. This interpretation underscores the unity of the prophetic mission and the universal nature of the Islamic faith.
orig: وإن من شيعته لإبراهيم

translation: When he came to his Lord with a sound heart.
interpretation: This verse refers to the prophet Abraham, who came to Allah with a pure and unblemished heart, free from any form of idolatry or polytheism. It emphasizes the importance of having a sincere and devoted heart when approaching God, without any trace of doubt or insincerity. The "sound heart" is one that is entirely focused on worshipping and submitting to the One true God alone, with complete trust and reliance on Him. It is a heart that is not tainted by worldly desires or attachments, but rather seeks only the pleasure and nearness of Allah.
orig: إذ جاء ربه بقلب سليم

translation: When he said to his father and his people, "What do you worship?"
interpretation: This verse is questioning the idolatrous practices of Prophet Ibrahim's (Abraham's) father and his community. It highlights Ibrahim's role in challenging the false beliefs and polytheistic practices prevalent in his society. The verse suggests that Ibrahim, guided by divine wisdom, sought to make his people reflect on the futility of worshipping idols and encouraged them to direct their worship solely to the One True God. It marks the beginning of Ibrahim's mission to spread the message of monotheism and reject the worship of false deities.
orig: إذ قال لأبيه وقومه ماذا تعبدون

translation: Is it falsehood [as] gods other than Allah you desire?
interpretation: This verse is questioning the desire of some people to worship false gods and idols instead of the one true God, Allah. It suggests that seeking divinity or objects of worship other than Allah is misguided and amounts to following falsehood. The rhetorical question drives home the point that it is irrational and wrong to turn away from worshipping Allah alone in favor of powerless false deities that are undeserving of worship. It emphasizes the importance of monotheism and avoiding polytheistic practices or the deification of anything besides Allah.
orig: أئفكا آلهة دون الله تريدون

translation: Then what do you think about the Lord of the worlds?
interpretation: This verse is a rhetorical question that encourages reflection on the nature and attributes of Allah, the Lord of all creation. It prompts the reader to consider the immense power, wisdom, and authority of the One who created and sustains the entire universe. The question implies that given the magnificence of Allah's creation, one should hold Him in the highest regard, with utmost reverence, awe, and submission. It also suggests that doubting or disregarding the Lord of the worlds would be irrational and foolish, as His existence and supremacy are evident through His creation.
orig: فما ظنكم برب العالمين

translation: And he cast a glance at the stars.
interpretation: This verse is referring to Prophet Abraham (peace be upon him) when he looked towards the heavens, seeking guidance and pondering upon the creation of Allah. It signifies the importance of reflecting upon the signs of Allah in the universe, such as the stars, to strengthen one's faith and attain a deeper understanding of the Creator's magnificence and power. The act of looking at the stars symbolizes the contemplation and intellectual pursuit that is encouraged in Islam, as it leads to a greater appreciation of Allah's wisdom and the realization of one's purpose in life.
orig: فنظر نظرة في النجوم

translation: So he said, "Indeed, I am [about to be] ill."
interpretation: In this verse, Prophet Ibrahim (Abraham) feigns illness to avoid participating in the idolatrous practices of his people. This clever response allows him to withdraw from their activities without directly confronting them or revealing his true intentions. It demonstrates his wisdom and tactical approach in dealing with a challenging situation where openly expressing his beliefs could lead to conflict or persecution. By saying he is ill, Ibrahim finds a way to remain true to his faith while avoiding immediate confrontation with the idolaters.
orig: فقال إني سقيم

translation: So they turned away from him, departing.
interpretation: This verse is referring to the disbelievers who, when faced with the truth of the message brought by the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him), turned away from him and his message in aversion and rejection. They chose to persist in their disbelief and willfully turned their backs on the guidance that was offered to them, departing from the presence of the Prophet and the opportunity to embrace faith. This turning away is a manifestation of their arrogance, stubbornness, and refusal to accept the truth, even when it is clearly presented to them.
orig: فتولوا عنه مدبرين

translation: Then he turned to their gods and said, "Do you not eat?"
interpretation: In this verse, Abraham (peace be upon him) is challenging the idols worshipped by his people. By asking the rhetorical question "Do you not eat?", he is highlighting the absurdity of worshipping inanimate objects that are incapable of performing basic functions like eating. This verse demonstrates Abraham's logical approach in conveying the message of monotheism and rejecting idol worship. It also shows his courage in confronting the false beliefs of his community, even at the risk of facing their wrath. The verse emphasizes the importance of using reason and critical thinking when it comes to matters of faith and the necessity of rejecting false deities in favor of worshipping the One True God.
orig: فراغ إلى آلهتهم فقال ألا تأكلون

translation: What is [the matter] with you [that] you do not speak?
interpretation: This verse is questioning why the people being addressed are remaining silent and not speaking up. It suggests that there is an expectation or need for them to say something, but they are failing to do so. The verse conveys a sense of rebuke or admonishment towards their silence, implying that their lack of speech is inappropriate or unwarranted given the circumstances. It is a rhetorical question designed to prompt them to reflect on and justify their muteness.
orig: ما لكم لا تنطقون

translation: Then strike them with your right hand.
interpretation: This verse is likely referring to a metaphorical striking, not a literal physical one. The "right hand" in Islamic tradition often symbolizes strength, authority and decisive action. So the meaning may be to confront and deal firmly with wrongdoers or opponents, to act against them with power and resolution in support of truth and justice. The Qur'an generally encourages responding to hostility with what is better, so this verse should be understood in light of the overall Qur'anic ethics of justice tempered with mercy, not as a carte blanche for violence. The specific circumstances and nature of the "striking" would need to be interpreted carefully within the Qur'an's wider moral framework.
orig: فراغ عليهم ضربا باليمين

translation: So they came to him, hastening.
interpretation: This verse describes the eagerness and swiftness with which the people responded to the call or command mentioned in the preceding verse. The word "yaziffūn" conveys a sense of brisk walking or even running, indicating their immediate compliance and fervor in answering the summons. It suggests a willingness and enthusiasm on their part to present themselves before the one who called them, without hesitation or delay. The verse paints a vivid picture of a group of people hurrying towards a central figure or authority, ready to hear and obey.
orig: فأقبلوا إليه يزفون

translation: He said, "Do you worship that which you [yourselves] carve?"
interpretation: This verse is a rhetorical question posed by the Prophet Abraham to his people, challenging their practice of idol worship. The interpretation is that it is illogical and foolish to worship idols that they themselves have carved and created with their own hands. It highlights the absurdity of worshipping false deities that have no power or ability, as they are merely inanimate objects crafted by human beings. The verse emphasizes the importance of worshipping the One True God, who is the Creator of all things, rather than the creations of man.
orig: قال أتعبدون ما تنحتون

translation: And Allah created you and that which you do.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah is the Creator of human beings and all their actions. It implies that while humans have free will to choose their actions, ultimately it is Allah who has created them with this ability. Therefore, humans are accountable to Allah for their deeds. The verse also suggests that Allah has knowledge of all that humans do, as He is their Creator. It serves as a reminder for humans to be mindful of their actions and to strive to do good, as they will be held responsible for their choices in front of their Creator.
orig: والله خلقكم وما تعملون

translation: They said, "Build for him a furnace and throw him into the blazing fire."
interpretation: This verse refers to the story of Prophet Abraham (Ibrahim) and his people. The interpretation is that the disbelievers, unable to defeat Abraham's arguments in support of monotheism, resorted to violence and decided to punish him by throwing him into a furnace. This highlights the cruelty and intolerance of those who oppose the truth, and their willingness to use force when they fail to counter the arguments of the believers. It also demonstrates Abraham's unwavering faith and trust in God, as he was ready to face even death for the sake of his beliefs.
orig: قالوا ابنوا له بنيانا فألقوه في الجحيم

translation: So they intended a plot against him, but We made them the lowest.
interpretation: This verse highlights the ultimate fate of those who scheme and plot against the righteous servants of Allah. Despite their best efforts to undermine and harm the believers, Allah turns the tables on them and causes their plans to backfire. The schemers end up in a state of humiliation and disgrace, becoming the lowest of the low in both this world and the Hereafter. It serves as a reminder that no matter how cunningly the enemies of faith may plan, Allah is always in control and will protect His chosen ones, ensuring that truth and justice prevail in the end.
orig: فأرادوا به كيدا فجعلناهم الأسفلين

translation: And he said, "Indeed, I am going to my Lord; He will guide me."
interpretation: This verse reflects the unwavering faith and trust that Prophet Ibrahim (Abraham) had in Allah. Despite facing challenges and opposition, he remained steadfast in his belief that Allah would guide him on the right path. It demonstrates the importance of having complete reliance on Allah's guidance, especially during difficult times. The verse also highlights the concept of turning to Allah for direction and support, acknowledging that He is the ultimate source of guidance in a believer's life.
orig: وقال إني ذاهب إلى ربي سيهدين

translation: My Lord! Grant me [a child] from among the righteous.
interpretation: In this verse, the supplicant is beseeching Allah to bless them with a righteous child. This heartfelt prayer reflects the deep yearning of a believer for offspring who will be a source of goodness, piety, and a means of attaining closeness to Allah. It underscores the importance of seeking not just any child, but one who will grow up to be a righteous servant of Allah, following the straight path and embodying noble qualities. The supplicant recognizes that a child is a precious gift and trust from Allah, and they aspire to raise their child in a manner pleasing to Him. This prayer also serves as a reminder for all believers to seek Allah's guidance in their journey of parenthood and to strive to nurture their children's faith and character.
orig: رب هب لي من الصالحين

translation: So We gave him good tidings of a forbearing boy.
interpretation: This verse is interpreted as a reference to the glad tidings given to Prophet Abraham (peace be upon him) about the birth of his son, Isaac. The description of the boy as "forbearing" (haleem) indicates that he would grow up to be a patient, wise and gentle person, embodying noble qualities. It signifies the blessing of a righteous child who would be a source of comfort and joy to his parents. The glad tidings given to Abraham also serve as a reward for his unwavering faith, obedience and trust in Allah.
orig: فبشرناه بغلام حليم

translation: And when he reached with him [the age of] exertion, he said, "O my son, indeed I have seen in a dream that I [must] sacrifice you, so see what you think." He said, "O my father, do as you are commanded. You will find me, if Allah wills, of the steadfast."
interpretation: This verse illustrates the ultimate devotion and submission to Allah's will. Abraham, in obedience to Allah's command, was ready to sacrifice his beloved son. Ishmael's response demonstrates his unwavering faith and willingness to surrender to Allah's decree. It highlights the importance of complete trust in Allah, even in the face of great personal sacrifice. The verse also emphasizes the significance of patience and steadfastness in the face of trials and tribulations, as Ishmael assures his father that he will find him among the steadfast, Allah willing.
orig: فلما بلغ معه السعي قال يا بني إني أرى في المنام أني أذبحك فانظر ماذا ترى قال يا أبت افعل ما تؤمر ستجدني إن شاء الله من الصابرين

translation: And when they had both submitted and he put him down upon his forehead,
interpretation: This verse refers to the ultimate test of faith that Prophet Ibrahim (Abraham) faced when Allah commanded him to sacrifice his beloved son, Ismail (Ishmael). Both father and son submitted completely to Allah's will. The verse captures the pivotal moment when Ibrahim had laid down Ismail ready to be sacrificed, in an act of pure obedience and submission to Allah. It symbolizes the epitome of faith, trust and surrender to the will of Allah, even in the face of losing what one loves most. This event is commemorated by Muslims each year during Eid al-Adha.
orig: فلما أسلما وتله للجبين

translation: And We called out to him, "O Abraham,
interpretation: This verse is a part of the story of Prophet Abraham (peace be upon him) when he was about to sacrifice his son, Ishmael, in obedience to Allah's command. At the critical moment, Allah called out to Abraham to stop him from sacrificing his son, as it was only a test of his faith and submission to Allah's will. The calling out to Abraham by name signifies the intimate relationship between Allah and His chosen servants, and how Allah communicates with them directly in times of need. It also shows Allah's mercy and compassion towards His servants, as He intervened to prevent the sacrifice from taking place, replacing Ishmael with a ram instead.
orig: وناديناه أن يا إبراهيم

translation: You have fulfilled the vision. Indeed, We thus reward the doers of good.
interpretation: This verse is a confirmation from Allah that the vision or dream that was seen has come true. It is also a reminder that Allah rewards those who do good deeds and fulfill their obligations. The verse emphasizes the importance of being among the "muhsineen" or the doers of good, as they are the ones who will be rewarded by Allah for their righteousness and sincerity. It encourages the believers to strive for excellence in their faith and actions, knowing that Allah will compensate them for their efforts in this life and the Hereafter.
orig: قد صدقت الرؤيا إنا كذلك نجزي المحسنين

translation: Indeed, this is the clear trial.
interpretation: This verse is referring to the trials and tribulations that humans face in this world. It suggests that the hardships and challenges we encounter are a clear test from Allah to see how we will respond and whether we will remain steadfast in our faith. The trials serve as a means of purification and a way for us to grow spiritually. It is through these difficulties that our true character and commitment to Allah are revealed. The verse reminds us to view the trials of life as an opportunity to prove our devotion and to seek Allah's pleasure, rather than becoming discouraged or losing hope.
orig: إن هذا لهو البلاء المبين

translation: And We ransomed him with a great sacrifice.
interpretation: This verse refers to the story of Prophet Ibrahim (Abraham) and his son Ismail (Ishmael). Allah commanded Ibrahim to sacrifice his beloved son as a test of his faith and submission to Allah's will. As Ibrahim was about to carry out the command, Allah replaced Ismail with a ram to be sacrificed instead. This event is commemorated by Muslims during the Eid al-Adha festival. The "great sacrifice" mentioned in the verse symbolizes the ultimate act of obedience and devotion to Allah, and serves as an example for all believers to prioritize their faith and submission to the Almighty above all else, even their most cherished possessions or loved ones.
orig: وفديناه بذبح عظيم

translation: And We left for him [favorable mention] among later generations:
interpretation: This verse refers to the legacy and lasting impact of a righteous person, in this case Prophet Solomon, who is mentioned in the preceding verses. It indicates that due to Solomon's faith, wisdom, and good deeds, Allah has preserved his honorable reputation and made him an example to be remembered and praised by subsequent generations until the end of time. This enduring positive remembrance among later generations is a gift and reward from Allah for those who lead a virtuous life in His service.
orig: وتركنا عليه في الآخرين

translation: Peace be upon Abraham
interpretation: This verse is a salutation of peace upon the Prophet Abraham (Ibrahim), one of the most important figures in the Abrahamic religions. It signifies the high status and respect accorded to Abraham in Islam for his unwavering faith, dedication to monotheism, and his role as a leader and father of many prophets. The invocation of peace upon him is a form of prayer and a reminder for Muslims to follow his example of submission to the One God and to spread the message of peace and righteousness in the world.
orig: سلام على إبراهيم

translation: Thus do We reward the doers of good.
interpretation: This verse highlights the concept of divine reward in Islam. It emphasizes that Allah rewards those who do good deeds and live righteously. The use of the plural "We" indicates that it is Allah Himself who grants these rewards, and that He does so in a manner befitting His majesty and generosity. The verse serves as an encouragement and motivation for believers to strive towards goodness, knowing that their efforts will be recognized and celebrated by their Creator. It is a reminder that the ultimate goal of a believer's actions should be to please Allah and earn His rewards, both in this life and in the Hereafter.
orig: كذلك نجزي المحسنين

translation: Indeed, he was of Our believing servants.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the person being referred to was a true believer and a devoted servant of Allah. It highlights the importance of faith and submission to God's will. The use of the pronoun "Our" indicates the special status and closeness of this individual to Allah. It also implies that being a sincere believer and servant of God is a highly praiseworthy quality that is valued and recognized by Allah Himself.
orig: إنه من عبادنا المؤمنين

translation: And We gave him the good news of Isaac, a prophet from among the righteous.
interpretation: This verse conveys the glad tidings given to Prophet Abraham (peace be upon him) by Allah's angels that he would be blessed with a son, Isaac, who would grow up to be a righteous prophet. This news came to Abraham in his old age, which made it even more joyous and miraculous. The verse emphasizes the high status of Prophet Isaac as a chosen prophet of Allah, who would be among the righteous servants of God. It also highlights the importance of righteousness and the blessings that come with it, both in this world and the hereafter.
orig: وبشرناه بإسحاق نبيا من الصالحين

translation: And We blessed him and Isaac. And among their descendants is the doer of good and the clearly unjust to himself.
interpretation: This verse indicates that among the descendants of Abraham and Isaac, there will be those who do righteous deeds and follow the straight path, but there will also be those who wrong themselves by rejecting faith and committing sins.
