The example of Prophet Ayyub teaches us to remain patient and faithful during life's challenges, trusting in Allah's wisdom and mercy.
orig: وخذ بيدك ضغثا فاضرب به ولا تحنث إنا وجدناه صابرا نعم العبد إنه أواب

translation: And remember Our servants, Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, those of strength and [religious] vision.
interpretation: This verse is reminding the believers to remember and reflect upon the lives of the great Prophets Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. These Prophets were blessed with both outer strength and inner vision. "Strength" here could refer to their physical strength and abilities, as well as their strength of faith and character. The "vision" refers to their spiritual insight and wisdom, their ability to see beyond the material world and understand the divine truths. By mentioning these qualities, the verse is encouraging believers to cultivate a balance of outer and inner strength, to be people of action as well as contemplation and spiritual awareness. The Prophets are held up as examples for believers to learn from and emulate in their own lives.
orig: واذكر عبادنا إبراهيم وإسحاق ويعقوب أولي الأيدي والأبصار

translation: Indeed, We chose them for an exclusive quality: remembrance of the Hereafter.
interpretation: This verse highlights that Allah has chosen certain individuals and purified them due to a special characteristic they possess, which is their constant remembrance of the Hereafter. These chosen people are mindful of the eternal life that awaits them after death, and this awareness guides their actions and keeps them on the righteous path. Their focus on the Hereafter sets them apart from others who may be distracted by the temporary pleasures of this worldly life. By singling out this quality, Allah emphasizes the importance of keeping the Hereafter in mind and living one's life in preparation for it.
orig: إنا أخلصناهم بخالصة ذكرى الدار

translation: And indeed, they are to Us among the chosen and outstanding.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that certain individuals, likely referring to prophets or righteous people, hold a special status in the sight of Allah. They are carefully selected and chosen by Him due to their exceptional qualities, virtues, and devotion. Allah has favored them and elevated their rank among humanity. Being chosen by Allah is a tremendous honor and blessing, indicating their purity, sincerity, and commitment to faith. These individuals serve as role models and guides for others to follow on the path of righteousness.
orig: وإنهم عندنا لمن المصطفين الأخيار

translation: And mention Ishmael and Elisha and Dhul-Kifl; and all are among the best.
interpretation: This verse highlights three prophets of Allah - Ishmael, Elisha, and Dhul-Kifl - and praises them as being among the best of Allah's servants. It reminds us to remember and honor these great individuals who exemplified righteousness, patience, and devotion to Allah. By mentioning them alongside each other, the Qur'an emphasizes that all prophets and righteous individuals, regardless of their time or place, share the common qualities of faith, virtue and being chosen by Allah for their roles. The verse encourages believers to look up to them as role models and to strive to emulate their noble characteristics in our own lives.
orig: واذكر إسماعيل واليسع وذا الكفل وكل من الأخيار

translation: This is a reminder. Indeed, for the righteous is a good place of return.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the Qur'an serves as a reminder and a guide for those who are mindful of Allah and seek to live righteously. It assures the believers that their ultimate destination is a blessed and beautiful place of return, which is Paradise. This interpretation highlights the importance of heeding the message of the Qur'an and striving to be among the righteous, as they will be rewarded with the best of outcomes in the Hereafter.
orig: هذا ذكر وإن للمتقين لحسن مآب

translation: Gardens of perpetual residence; the gates will be opened for them.
interpretation: This verse refers to the eternal reward of Paradise that awaits the righteous believers in the Hereafter. The "Gardens of perpetual residence" denote the everlasting nature of Paradise, where the believers will reside forever. The phrase "the gates will be opened for them" signifies that the believers will be warmly welcomed into Paradise, and that they will have unrestricted access to all of its bounties and delights. This verse serves as a reminder and motivation for the believers to strive for righteousness in this world, knowing that their ultimate reward will be the eternal bliss of Paradise in the Hereafter.
orig: جنات عدن مفتحة لهم الأبواب

translation: Reclining therein, they will call for abundant fruit and drink.
interpretation: In Paradise, the believers will recline on comfortable furnishings and will be able to request and enjoy an abundance of fruits and drinks as they please. This verse emphasizes the luxurious and pleasurable nature of Paradise, where all the desires of the righteous will be fulfilled. The mention of reclining also suggests a state of relaxation, peace, and satisfaction that the dwellers of Paradise will experience eternally as a reward for their faith and good deeds in this world.
orig: متكئين فيها يدعون فيها بفاكهة كثيرة وشراب

translation: And with them will be companions of modest gaze, of equal age.
interpretation: This verse refers to the companions that the righteous will have in Paradise. These companions are described as having a "modest gaze", indicating their purity, chastity, and lack of lustful inclinations. The mention of them being "of equal age" suggests that they will be perfectly suited to their companions, being of similar physical and mental maturity. This is a blessing and reward for the righteous in the afterlife, symbolizing the perfection and harmony that will exist in Paradise. The verse emphasizes the contrast between the pure relationships in Paradise and the often imbalanced or impure relationships that may exist in the worldly life.
orig: وعندهم قاصرات الطرف أتراب

translation: That is what you were promised for the Day of Account.
interpretation: This verse serves as a reminder to humanity that the Day of Judgment, which has been promised by Allah, will indeed come to pass. It emphasizes the inevitability of being held accountable for one's deeds in this world. The verse implies that the events and consequences of the Day of Account have been clearly communicated to mankind through divine revelation, leaving no room for excuses or ignorance. It is a call to be mindful of one's actions and to strive for righteousness in preparation for the ultimate reckoning before Allah.
orig: هذا ما توعدون ليوم الحساب

translation: Indeed, this is Our provision; for it there is no depletion.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the infinite and inexhaustible nature of the blessings and provisions that Allah bestows upon His servants in Paradise. It serves as a reminder that, unlike the temporary and limited resources of this worldly life, the rewards and bounties in the Hereafter are eternal and will never diminish or come to an end. This knowledge should inspire believers to strive for Paradise and seek Allah's pleasure, knowing that their efforts will be rewarded with an everlasting and abundant provision.
orig: إن هذا لرزقنا ما له من نفاد

translation: Indeed, for the transgressors is an evil place of return
interpretation: This verse warns that those who transgress the limits set by Allah and reject His guidance will have a terrible abode in the Hereafter. The "evil place of return" refers to Hell, where the transgressors will face the consequences of their actions and suffer eternal punishment. It emphasizes the severity of the punishment that awaits those who choose to rebel against Allah and persist in their wrongdoing, reminding us of the importance of staying on the right path and avoiding transgression in our lives.
orig: هذا وإن للطاغين لشر مآب

translation: They will [enter to] burn in Hell, and wretched is the resting place.
interpretation: This verse serves as a stern warning to those who reject faith and choose to disobey Allah. It emphasizes the severe consequence of their actions - being condemned to the eternal torment of Hell. The phrase "wretched is the resting place" underscores the utter misery, despair, and regret that the denizens of Hell will experience forever. It is a reminder for believers to stay steadfast on the righteous path and for the disbelievers to repent and amend their ways before it is too late, as the punishment of Hell is the worst possible fate one can face in the Hereafter.
orig: جهنم يصلونها فبئس المهاد

translation: So let them taste it - scalding water and [foul] purulence.
interpretation: This verse is referring to the punishment that awaits the disbelievers in Hell. The "scalding water and [foul] purulence" are among the terrible torments they will face as a consequence of their rejection of God's message and their evil deeds in this world. It serves as a severe warning to all of the horrific fate that awaits those who turn away from God's guidance and persist in wrongdoing. The graphic imagery of the boiling water and disgusting discharge emphasizes the physical and psychological anguish of this eternal punishment, which is the ultimate outcome for those who fail to believe and live righteously.
orig: هذا فليذوقوه حميم وغساق

translation: And of others, in pairs of various kinds.
interpretation: This verse points to the vast diversity and variety in Allah's creation. It suggests that Allah has created all living beings in pairs, male and female, and in a wide array of shapes, colors, and forms. This diversity is a sign of Allah's infinite creative power and wisdom. It also emphasizes the importance of pairs and the complementary nature of creation, where each creature has its mate or counterpart. The verse invites us to reflect on the wonders of Allah's creation and appreciate the beauty and balance in the natural world.
orig: وآخر من شكله أزواج

translation: This is a company bursting in with you, not welcome to them. Indeed, they will [enter to] burn in the Fire.
interpretation: This verse is referring to the companions of the disbelievers who will be thrown into Hell along with them on the Day of Judgment. It emphasizes that they are not welcome in the Hereafter and will face the punishment of burning in the Fire as a consequence of their disbelief and evil deeds in this world. The verse also implies that the disbelievers will be gathered together with their companions in the Hellfire, sharing the same fate and torment.
orig: هذا فوج مقتحم معكم لا مرحبا بهم إنهم صالو النار

translation: They said, "Nay, you are not welcome! You brought this upon us, so what an evil abode!"
interpretation: This verse is a response from the people of Hell to those who led them astray in the worldly life. They are expressing their anger and resentment towards their misguiders, telling them that they are not welcome in Hell and blaming them for bringing this terrible fate upon them. The phrase "what an evil abode" emphasizes the severity and wretchedness of their final destination as a consequence of following false guides and rejecting the truth in the world.
orig: قالوا بل أنتم لا مرحبا بكم أنتم قدمتموه لنا فبئس القرار

translation: They will say, "Our Lord, whoever brought this upon us - increase for him double punishment in the Fire."
interpretation: This verse speaks about the people in Hell who will blame each other for their fate. They will ask Allah to double the punishment of those who misled them and caused them to end up in Hell. It shows the regret and resentment the denizens of Hell will feel towards each other. They will realize the error of following false leaders and ideologies in this world that led them astray from the straight path. The verse highlights the severe consequences of leading others away from the truth and the divine retribution that awaits those who misguide people in religious matters.
orig: قالوا ربنا من قدم لنا هذا فزده عذابا ضعفا في النار

translation: And they will say, "What is [the matter] with us that we do not see men whom we used to count among the bad ones?
interpretation: This verse refers to the Day of Judgment when the disbelievers will be surprised to find that some of those they considered to be evil or wicked in this world are not present with them in Hell. It suggests that their judgments and perceptions in this world were flawed and that the true nature of people's deeds and character will be revealed in the Hereafter. It also implies that those who were looked down upon or marginalized in this world due to their righteousness will be elevated and honored by Allah in the next life.
orig: وقالوا ما لنا لا نرى رجالا كنا نعدهم من الأشرار

translation: Did We take them in mockery, or have [our] eyes turned away from them?
interpretation: This verse is a rhetorical question that suggests two possible reasons for the disbelievers' failure to recognize the truth: either God has made them the object of mockery and ridicule due to their persistent disbelief, or they have become so misguided that they are unable to perceive the signs of God's existence and power that are evident to those who reflect deeply. It implies that their spiritual blindness is a consequence of their own choices and actions, and that they have brought upon themselves the state of being mocked or disregarded by God.
orig: أتخذناهم سخريا أم زاغت عنهم الأبصار

translation: Indeed, that is the truth - the quarreling of the people of the Fire.
interpretation: This verse affirms that the arguments and disputes among the people of Hell mentioned in the preceding verses are absolutely true and real. It emphasizes the severity of their punishment and the reality of their fate. The quarreling highlights their regret, blame, and anguish as they face the consequences of their actions and their failure to follow the right path during their worldly life. This serves as a warning to mankind to avoid such an end by heeding God's message and living righteously.
orig: إن ذلك لحق تخاصم أهل النار

translation: Say, "I am only a warner, and there is no deity except Allah, the One, the Prevailing."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the core message of Islam, which is the oneness and supremacy of Allah. The Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) is instructed to declare that he is only a warner, whose role is to remind people of the truth and guide them towards the right path. The verse also affirms that there is no god worthy of worship except Allah, who is unique in His divinity and has absolute power and control over all things. This highlights the importance of submitting to Allah alone and rejecting any form of polytheism or association of partners with Him. It is a call to embrace the pure monotheistic faith and acknowledge Allah's sovereignty over the entire universe.
orig: قل إنما أنا منذر وما من إله إلا الله الواحد القهار

translation: Lord of the heavens and the earth and whatever is between them, the Exalted in Might, the Perpetual Forgiver.
interpretation: This verse affirms that Allah is the Lord and Creator of the heavens, the earth, and everything in between them. He is Exalted in Might, meaning that He is supremely powerful and no one can overcome Him. At the same time, He is the Perpetual Forgiver, always ready to forgive the sins of those who repent and turn to Him. It emphasizes both Allah's absolute power and authority over the entire universe, as well as His infinite mercy and readiness to forgive. This encourages the believers to have hope in Allah's forgiveness while also being in awe of His might and majesty.
orig: رب السماوات والأرض وما بينهما العزيز الغفار

translation: Say, "It is great news"
interpretation: This verse is emphasizing the importance and magnitude of the message that the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) is conveying to mankind. The "great news" refers to the revelation of the Qur'an and the teachings of Islam, which are of utmost significance for the guidance and salvation of humanity. The verse is urging the Prophet to boldly proclaim this message, as it is not something trivial or ordinary, but rather a matter of great consequence that deserves the attention and consideration of all people.
orig: قل هو نبأ عظيم

translation: You are turning away from it
interpretation: This verse is addressing humanity, pointing out that they are heedless and turning away from the message of the Qur'an and the guidance it provides. It suggests that people are distracted by worldly pursuits and are not paying attention to the spiritual truths and divine wisdom contained within the Qur'an. The verse serves as a reminder and a warning to individuals to reflect upon the Qur'an and its teachings, rather than ignoring or disregarding them, as doing so will have consequences in this life and the hereafter.
orig: أنتم عنه معرضون

translation: I had no knowledge of the exalted assembly [of angels] when they were disputing [the matter of Adam's creation].
interpretation: This verse highlights the limited knowledge of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and that he had no access to the unseen realm or the discussions of the angels. It emphasizes that divine revelation was the source of his knowledge about such matters, not any personal insight or experience. The verse also alludes to the story of Adam's creation and the discourse that took place among the angels regarding Allah's decision to create and place a human being on earth as a vicegerent. Overall, it underscores the Prophet's role as a messenger who received revelation, while affirming that ultimate knowledge belongs only to Allah.
orig: ما كان لي من علم بالملإ الأعلى إذ يختصمون

translation: It is not revealed to me except that I am a clear warner.
interpretation: The role of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) is to convey the message of Islam clearly and to warn people of the consequences of rejecting it. He does not possess any supernatural powers or knowledge beyond what is revealed to him by God. His mission is to serve as a warner, delivering the divine message to humanity in a clear and unambiguous manner, so that people may understand and follow the right path. The verse emphasizes the Prophet's role as a messenger and not as someone who can perform miracles or know the unseen on his own accord.
orig: إن يوحى إلي إلا أنما أنا نذير مبين

translation: When your Lord said to the angels, "Indeed, I am going to create a human being from clay."
interpretation: This verse refers to the creation of Adam, the first human being. It emphasizes that God has the power to create life from lifeless matter, such as clay. The mention of God informing the angels about His plan to create Adam indicates the special status of human beings and the significance of their creation. It also highlights the concept of God's omnipotence and His role as the Creator of all things. The verse sets the stage for the story of Adam's creation and his role as the father of humanity.
orig: إذ قال ربك للملائكة إني خالق بشرا من طين

translation: So when I have proportioned him and breathed into him of My [created] soul, then fall down to him in prostration.
interpretation: This verse is a command from Allah to the angels to prostrate before Adam after Allah had created him and breathed into him the soul that Allah created. This prostration was a sign of honor and respect for Adam, not an act of worship. It demonstrates the high status that Allah bestowed upon Adam and, by extension, humanity. The verse also highlights the divine origin of the human soul, which Allah created and breathed into Adam. This distinguishes human beings from other creatures and emphasizes their spiritual nature and connection to the divine.
orig: فإذا سويته ونفخت فيه من روحي فقعوا له ساجدين

translation: So the angels prostrated, all of them entirely,
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the complete obedience and submission of the angels to Allah's command. When Allah ordered the angels to prostrate before Adam, they all did so without hesitation or exception. This demonstrates their total compliance with Allah's will and their lack of arrogance or defiance. The verse underscores the importance of humility, obedience, and unity in faith and worship, as exemplified by the angels' collective act of prostration.
orig: فسجد الملائكة كلهم أجمعون

translation: Except Iblees; he was arrogant and became one of the disbelievers.
interpretation: This verse highlights the arrogance and disobedience of Iblees (Satan), who refused to prostrate before Adam when commanded by Allah. His pride and sense of superiority led him to rebel against Allah's command, thus becoming one of the disbelievers. This verse serves as a warning to humanity about the dangers of arrogance and the importance of submitting to Allah's will, as even a being as close to Allah as Iblees can fall from grace due to pride and disobedience.
orig: إلا إبليس استكبر وكان من الكافرين

translation: He said, "O Iblees, what prevented you from prostrating to that which I created with My hands? Were you arrogant [then], or were you [already] among the haughty?"
interpretation: This verse is a rebuke from Allah to Iblees (Satan) for his disobedience and refusal to prostrate to Adam, whom Allah created with His own hands. It highlights Iblees' arrogance and pride, which led him to consider himself superior to Adam and disobey Allah's command. The verse implies that Iblees' defiance stems from his pre-existing haughtiness and that his arrogance prevented him from submitting to Allah's will, even though Allah had directly created Adam. This incident serves as a warning against allowing pride and self-importance to come between oneself and obedience to Allah.
orig: قال يا إبليس ما منعك أن تسجد لما خلقت بيدي أستكبرت أم كنت من العالين

translation: He said, "I am better than him. You created me from fire and created him from clay."
interpretation: This verse refers to the story of Iblis (Satan) refusing to prostrate before Adam when commanded by Allah. Iblis' pride and arrogance led him to believe that he was superior to Adam because he was created from fire, whereas Adam was created from clay. This verse highlights the sin of pride and the importance of humility and obedience to Allah's commands, regardless of one's perceived status or origin. It also emphasizes that the true measure of superiority in Allah's sight is not based on physical composition, but rather on piety and righteousness.
orig: قال أنا خير منه خلقتني من نار وخلقته من طين

translation: He said, 'Then get out of it, for indeed you are expelled.'
interpretation: This verse is a command from Allah to Satan, expelling him from Paradise due to his disobedience and refusal to prostrate before Adam. It emphasizes that arrogance and pride lead to being distanced from the mercy and blessings of Allah. The use of the word "rajeem" (expelled or accursed) indicates that Satan is now permanently removed from Allah's grace and is condemned for his rebellious actions. This serves as a warning to humanity not to follow in Satan's footsteps by letting arrogance and disobedience come between them and their Creator.
orig: قال فاخرج منها فإنك رجيم

translation: And indeed, upon you is My curse until the Day of Judgment.
interpretation: This verse is a stern warning from Allah to those who disobey Him and incur His wrath. The curse of Allah is not a trivial matter; it implies being cut off from His mercy, blessings, and guidance. The mention of "until the Day of Judgment" emphasizes the severity and duration of this punishment, which will last until the final reckoning when all souls will be judged for their deeds. It serves as a reminder for individuals to be mindful of their actions and to strive for righteousness to avoid facing the consequences of Allah's curse in this life and the hereafter.
orig: وإن عليك لعنتي إلى يوم الدين

translation: He said, "My Lord, then reprieve me until the Day they are resurrected."
interpretation: This verse is a plea from Iblis (Satan) to Allah, asking for a reprieve until the Day of Resurrection. Iblis, out of pride and arrogance, disobeyed Allah's command to prostrate before Adam. As a result, Allah expelled him from Paradise. However, Iblis requested a delay in his ultimate punishment until the Day of Judgment. This request demonstrates Iblis' defiance and his determination to lead humanity astray until the end of time. The verse highlights the ongoing struggle between good and evil, with Iblis representing the forces of temptation and disobedience, while Allah's guidance and mercy offer a path to salvation for those who follow His commands.
orig: قال رب فأنظرني إلى يوم يبعثون

translation: He said: "Then surely you are of the respited ones."
interpretation: This verse is from Surah Al-A'raf (7:15). It refers to the conversation between Allah and Iblis (Satan) after the latter refused to prostrate before Adam. Allah declares that although Iblis is granted respite until the Day of Judgment, he is still considered among those who are rebuked and cast out from His mercy due to his disobedience and arrogance. This also serves as a warning to humanity that following the path of Iblis and giving in to pride and rebellion against Allah's commands will lead to the same fate of being distanced from Allah's grace, even if the punishment is delayed until the Hereafter.
orig: قال فإنك من المنظرين

translation: Until the Day of the time well-known.
interpretation: This verse refers to the Day of Resurrection, a time that is known only to Allah. It emphasizes the inevitability and certainty of the Day of Judgment, when all souls will be raised from their graves to face the consequences of their deeds in this world. The phrase "time well-known" suggests that this event has been predetermined by Allah and will occur at its appointed time, which is unknown to anyone except Him. This verse serves as a reminder for believers to prepare for this momentous day by leading righteous lives and fulfilling their obligations to Allah and His creation.
orig: إلى يوم الوقت المعلوم

translation: He said, "By Your might, I will surely mislead them all,"
interpretation: In this verse, Satan (Iblis) is addressing Allah, swearing by His might that he will deceive and lead astray all of humanity. This statement reflects Satan's arrogance and defiance against Allah's command to prostrate before Adam. It also highlights the ongoing struggle between good and evil, as Satan vows to use his influence to misguide people from the righteous path. The verse serves as a warning to believers to be vigilant against Satan's temptations and to seek refuge in Allah's guidance and protection.
orig: قال فبعزتك لأغوينهم أجمعين

translation: Except, among them, Your chosen servants.
interpretation: This verse highlights the concept of God's chosen servants who are sincere in their devotion and faith. These individuals are an exception to those who may be led astray by Satan's temptations and deceptions. The "mukhlasin" or the chosen ones, are those who have purified their intentions, actions, and worship solely for the sake of God. They are steadfast in their obedience and submission to the Almighty, seeking only His pleasure and nearness. This verse emphasizes that even when the majority may deviate, there will always remain a group of true believers who are protected by their sincerity and unwavering commitment to God.
orig: إلا عبادك منهم المخلصين

translation: So the truth [I say], and the truth I say.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of speaking the truth and being honest in one's speech. It is a reminder that the truth should always be upheld and spoken, even if it may be difficult or unpopular. The repetition of "the truth" highlights its significance and the need to adhere to it consistently. As a believer, one should strive to be truthful in all aspects of life, as it is a fundamental Islamic value and a sign of righteousness.
orig: قال فالحق والحق أقول

translation: I will surely fill Hell with you and those of them that follow you, all together.
interpretation: This verse is a stern warning from Allah to Iblis (Satan) and his followers. It emphasizes the severity of the punishment that awaits those who disobey Allah and follow the path of evil. The interpretation is that Hell will be filled with Satan and all those who were misled by him, highlighting the consequences of rejecting faith and succumbing to temptation. It serves as a reminder for mankind to stay on the righteous path and resist the whispers of Satan, as the ultimate fate of the disobedient is the eternal torment of Hell.
orig: لأملأن جهنم منك وممن تبعك منهم أجمعين

translation: Say, "I do not ask you for any reward for it, nor am I of those who pretend."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the sincerity of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) in conveying the message of Islam. He is not seeking any worldly gain or reward for his efforts, nor is he pretending to be something he is not. The Prophet's sole motivation is to fulfill his divine mission and guide humanity to the truth, without any personal agenda or desire for recognition. This verse highlights the purity of his intentions and the authenticity of his prophethood.
orig: قل ما أسألكم عليه من أجر وما أنا من المتكلفين

translation: It is but a reminder to the worlds.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the Qur'an is a universal message and a reminder for all of humanity, not just for a specific group or nation. It serves as a guidance and admonition for everyone, regardless of their background or status, inviting them to reflect upon its teachings and to follow the path of righteousness. The Qur'an is a timeless message that transcends the boundaries of time and place, relevant for all generations until the end of time.
orig: إن هو إلا ذكر للعالمين

translation: And you will surely know [the truth of] its information after a time.
interpretation: This verse is a warning and a reminder that the truth of the Qur'an's message and the consequences of rejecting it will become clear to the disbelievers in due time. It implies that even if they do not believe now, a time will come when they will realize the reality of the Qur'an's teachings and the consequences of their actions. This verse encourages believers to remain steadfast in their faith, knowing that the ultimate truth will be revealed, while also serving as a warning to those who deny the message that they will eventually face the repercussions of their choice.
orig: ولتعلمن نبأه بعد حين

translation: The revelation of the Book is from Allah, the Exalted in Might, the Wise.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the Qur'an is a divine revelation from Allah, who is described as the Exalted in Might and the Wise. It affirms that the source of the Qur'an is Allah Himself, and not the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) or any other human being. The attributes of Allah mentioned here, "Al-Aziz" (the Exalted in Might) and "Al-Hakeem" (the Wise), underscore His power, wisdom, and authority in revealing this sacred book as a guidance for mankind. The verse sets the tone for the entire Qur'an, establishing its divine origin and the importance of accepting its teachings as the ultimate truth from the All-Knowing Creator.
orig: تنزيل الكتاب من الله العزيز الحكيم

translation: Indeed, We have sent down to you the Book (the Quran) in truth. So worship Allah, [being] sincere to Him in religion.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of worshipping Allah with sincerity and devotion. It reminds us that the Qur'an has been revealed as a guide for humanity, and that we should dedicate our lives to serving Allah alone, without associating partners with Him or seeking the approval of others. The verse also highlights the significance of the Qur'an as a source of truth and guidance, and encourages us to turn to it for direction in our lives. Ultimately, this verse serves as a call to purify our intentions and to live our lives in accordance with the teachings of Islam, seeking only the pleasure of Allah.
orig: إنا أنزلنا إليك الكتاب بالحق فاعبد الله مخلصا له الدين

translation: Unquestionably, for Allah is the pure religion. And those who take protectors besides Him [say], "We only worship them that they may bring us nearer to Allah in position." Indeed, Allah will judge between them concerning that over which they differ. Indeed, Allah does not guide he who is a liar and [confirmed] disbeliever.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that true devotion and worship belong to Allah alone. Those who worship others besides Allah, claiming that these false deities will bring them closer to Him, are misguided. Allah will ultimately judge between the believers and the disbelievers regarding their differences. The verse also asserts that Allah does not guide those who persistently lie and disbelieve in Him, indicating that their actions will lead them astray and deprive them of divine guidance. It serves as a reminder to direct one's faith, obedience, and worship solely to Allah and to avoid the futile worship of false deities or intermediaries.
orig: ألا لله الدين الخالص والذين اتخذوا من دونه أولياء ما نعبدهم إلا ليقربونا إلى الله زلفى إن الله يحكم بينهم في ما هم فيه يختلفون إن الله لا يهدي من هو كاذب كفار

translation: If Allah had intended to take a son, He could have chosen from what He creates whatever He willed. Exalted is He; He is Allah, the One, the Prevailing.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute oneness and sovereignty of Allah. It refutes the notion that Allah has a son or offspring, which is a belief held by some other religions. The verse asserts that if Allah had wanted to take a son, He could have easily chosen anyone or anything from His creation. However, Allah is exalted above such needs and associations. He is the One and Only God, the Almighty, who has no partners or equals. This interpretation highlights the Islamic belief in the unity of Allah and rejects any form of polytheism or the attribution of divine qualities to anyone or anything other than Allah.
orig: لو أراد الله أن يتخذ ولدا لاصطفى مما يخلق ما يشاء سبحانه هو الله الواحد القهار

translation: He created the heavens and earth in truth. He wraps the night over the day and wraps the day over the night and has subjected the sun and the moon, each running [its course] for a specified term. Unquestionably, He is the Exalted in Might, the Perpetual Forgiver.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's power and wisdom in creating the universe with a precise system and balance. The alternation of night and day, and the orbits of the sun and moon, all operate according to Allah's decree for a set period of time. This points to Allah's might and control over all things. At the same time, He is merciful and forgiving to His servants, despite their shortcomings and sins. The verse invites reflection on Allah's creation and encourages humans to seek His forgiveness and live righteously in accordance with the divine laws governing the cosmos.
orig: خلق السماوات والأرض بالحق يكور الليل على النهار ويكور النهار على الليل وسخر الشمس والقمر كل يجري لأجل مسمى ألا هو العزيز الغفار

translation: He created you from one soul. Then He made from it its mate, and He produced for you from the grazing livestock eight mates. He creates you in the wombs of your mothers, creation after creation, within three darknesses. That is Allah, your Lord; to Him belongs dominion. There is no deity except Him, so how are you averted?
interpretation: This verse highlights the power and unity of Allah in the process of creation. It emphasizes that all of humanity originated from a single soul, and that Allah created mates and offspring in pairs. The verse also describes the development of the human embryo through various stages in the womb, enveloped in three layers of darkness, which could refer to the abdominal wall, uterine wall, and the amniotic sac. This complex and miraculous process of creation is attributed to Allah alone, who is the sole creator and ruler of the universe. The verse ends with a rhetorical question, urging people to contemplate the signs of Allah's creation and to turn away from worshipping any other entity besides Him.
orig: خلقكم من نفس واحدة ثم جعل منها زوجها وأنزل لكم من الأنعام ثمانية أزواج يخلقكم في بطون أمهاتكم خلقا من بعد خلق في ظلمات ثلاث ذلكم الله ربكم له الملك لا إله إلا هو فأنى تصرفون

translation: If you disbelieve - indeed, Allah is Free from need of you. And He does not approve for His servants disbelief. And if you are grateful, He approves it for you; and no bearer of burdens will bear the burden of another. Then to your Lord is your return, and He will inform you about what you used to do. Indeed, He is Knowing of that within the breasts.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah is self-sufficient and not in need of human worship or belief. However, He desires for His servants to have faith and show gratitude, as it benefits them in this life and the hereafter. Each individual is responsible for their own actions and will not bear the burden of another's sins. Ultimately, all will return to Allah, who has full knowledge of what is hidden in the hearts, and He will inform them of their deeds and hold them accountable accordingly.
orig: إن تكفروا فإن الله غني عنكم ولا يرضى لعباده الكفر وإن تشكروا يرضه لكم ولا تزر وازرة وزر أخرى ثم إلى ربكم مرجعكم فينبئكم بما كنتم تعملون إنه عليم بذات الصدور

translation: And when affliction touches man, he calls upon his Lord, turning to Him [alone]; then when He bestows on him a favor from Himself, he forgets Him whom he called upon before, and he attributes to Allah equals to mislead [people] from His way. Say, "Enjoy your disbelief for a little; indeed, you are of the companions of the Fire."
interpretation: This verse highlights the fickle nature of human beings. When faced with hardship, they turn to Allah for help, but when blessed with favors, they forget Him and attribute partners to Him. This behavior is a form of ingratitude and disbelief, leading people astray from the right path. The verse warns those who engage in such practices that their enjoyment of disbelief will be short-lived, and they will ultimately be among the inhabitants of Hell. It emphasizes the importance of remaining steadfast in faith and gratitude towards Allah, both in times of hardship and ease.
orig: وإذا مس الإنسان ضر دعا ربه منيبا إليه ثم إذا خوله نعمة منه نسي ما كان يدعو إليه من قبل وجعل لله أندادا ليضل عن سبيله قل تمتع بكفرك قليلا إنك من أصحاب النار

translation: Is one who is devoutly obedient during periods of the night, prostrating and standing [in prayer], fearing the Hereafter and hoping for the mercy of his Lord, [like one who does not]? Say, "Are those who know equal to those who do not know?" Only they will remember [who are] people of understanding.
interpretation: This verse highlights the distinction between those who are mindful of God and those who are not. The devout believers who spend their nights in worship, fearing God's judgment and hoping for His mercy, are contrasted with those who are heedless. The rhetorical question emphasizes that those endowed with knowledge and understanding are not equal to the ignorant. It is the people of reason and insight who truly take heed of such comparisons and are prompted to reflect and be mindful of their Creator. The verse encourages introspection and the pursuit of spiritual knowledge and wisdom.
orig: أمن هو قانت آناء الليل ساجدا وقائما يحذر الآخرة ويرجو رحمة ربه قل هل يستوي الذين يعلمون والذين لا يعلمون إنما يتذكر أولو الألباب

translation: Say, "O My servants who have believed, fear your Lord. For those who do good in this world is good, and the earth of Allah is spacious. Indeed, the patient will be given their reward without account."
interpretation: This verse encourages the believers to have consciousness of Allah (taqwa) and promises them good both in this world and the Hereafter. It reminds that Allah's earth is vast, suggesting that one can always find a place to practice Islam freely. The verse especially highlights the virtue of patience, emphasizing that those who remain steadfast will be rewarded immensely in the Hereafter, without their deeds being questioned or their rewards being limited. It motivates the believers to persevere through hardships and trials for the sake of Allah, with the assurance of generous recompense awaiting them.
orig: قل يا عباد الذين آمنوا اتقوا ربكم للذين أحسنوا في هذه الدنيا حسنة وأرض الله واسعة إنما يوفى الصابرون أجرهم بغير حساب

translation: Say, "Indeed, I have been commanded to worship Allah, [being] sincere to Him in religion."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of worshipping Allah alone with sincerity and devotion. It is a command to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) to declare that he has been instructed to dedicate his worship exclusively to Allah, without associating any partners with Him. This sincere devotion to Allah is the essence of true religion and the path to salvation. It requires one to submit wholeheartedly to Allah's will, obey His commands, and purify their intentions solely for His sake, without any ulterior motives or desires for worldly gain. By doing so, a believer can attain the pleasure of Allah and success in both this life and the hereafter.
orig: قل إني أمرت أن أعبد الله مخلصا له الدين

translation: And I have been commanded to be the first of those who submit [to Allah].
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of being among the first to embrace Islam and submit to the will of Allah. It suggests that the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) was not only instructed to convey the message of Islam but also to lead by example in accepting and following the teachings of the religion. The verse implies that submitting to Allah and being a true Muslim requires promptness, eagerness, and dedication in accepting and implementing the commandments of Allah without hesitation or delay. It also highlights the significance of setting a precedent for others to follow in the path of Islam.
orig: وأمرت لأن أكون أول المسلمين

translation: Say, "Indeed I fear, if I should disobey my Lord, the punishment of a tremendous Day."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of obedience to Allah and the fear of His punishment on the Day of Judgment. It serves as a reminder for the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and all believers to remain steadfast in their faith and to avoid disobeying Allah's commands. The verse highlights the magnitude of the consequences one would face for defying Allah, describing it as the "punishment of a tremendous Day." This interpretation underscores the significance of submitting to Allah's will and the gravity of the afterlife, encouraging believers to lead a righteous life and to be mindful of their actions in this world.
orig: قل إني أخاف إن عصيت ربي عذاب يوم عظيم

translation: Say, "It is Allah I worship, sincere to Him in my religion,
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of worshipping Allah alone with sincerity and devotion. It instructs the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) to declare that he worships only Allah, dedicating his religion and worship exclusively to Him. This highlights the fundamental principle of Islam, which is the oneness of Allah (tawheed) and the rejection of all forms of polytheism or worship of anyone or anything besides Him. It also stresses the significance of having pure intentions and being sincere in one's faith and religious practices, as sincerity is a key factor in the acceptance of one's deeds by Allah.
orig: قل الله أعبد مخلصا له ديني

translation: So worship what you will besides Him. Say, "Indeed, the losers are the ones who will lose themselves and their families on the Day of Resurrection. Unquestionably, that is the manifest loss."
interpretation: This verse is a stern warning to those who choose to worship others besides Allah. It emphasizes that those who engage in idolatry and polytheism will face the ultimate loss on the Day of Judgment. They will not only lose themselves but also their loved ones, as they will be separated from them in the Hereafter. The verse highlights the gravity of this loss by stating that it is the most evident and undeniable loss one can ever experience. It serves as a reminder for believers to stay steadfast in their worship of Allah alone and to avoid falling into the trap of worshipping false deities, as doing so will lead to eternal regret and despair.
orig: فاعبدوا ما شئتم من دونه قل إن الخاسرين الذين خسروا أنفسهم وأهليهم يوم القيامة ألا ذلك هو الخسران المبين

translation: They will have canopies of fire above them and below them. By this Allah threatens His servants. O My servants, then fear Me.
interpretation: This verse is a stern warning from Allah to His servants, vividly describing the terrible fate that awaits those who disobey Him. The "canopies of fire" above and below symbolize the all-encompassing nature of the punishment in Hell, leaving no escape or relief for the sinners. Allah uses this frightening imagery to strike fear into the hearts of His servants, urging them to be mindful of Him and obey His commands. The verse concludes with a direct address, "O My servants", followed by the command "then fear Me". This drives home the message that the only way to avoid this dreadful fate is through having taqwa - consciousness and fear of Allah that compels one to obey Him and refrain from sin. It is a powerful reminder for mankind to live righteously and be ever-conscious of their ultimate accountability to their Creator.
orig: لهم من فوقهم ظلل من النار ومن تحتهم ظلل ذلك يخوف الله به عباده يا عباد فاتقون

translation: But those who have avoided Taghut, lest they worship it, and turned back to Allah - for them are good tidings. So give good tidings to My servants.
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of shunning false deities and turning to Allah alone. "Taghut" refers to anything that is worshipped or obeyed besides Allah, such as idols, desires, or worldly powers. Those who resist the temptation to worship false gods and instead direct their devotion and obedience to Allah will be rewarded with glad tidings in this life and the Hereafter. The verse emphasizes the significance of sincere servitude to Allah and the blessings that await those who remain steadfast in their faith and avoid the pitfalls of polytheism and disobedience. As a believer, one should strive to be among the servants of Allah who receive these glad tidings by maintaining a strong connection with Him and resisting the allure of false deities.
orig: والذين اجتنبوا الطاغوت أن يعبدوها وأنابوا إلى الله لهم البشرى فبشر عباد

translation: Those who listen to the Word, and follow the best of it. Those are they whom Allah has guided, and those are men of understanding.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of not only listening to the teachings of the Qur'an, but also actively following the best of its guidance. Those who do so are considered to be the ones whom Allah has guided and blessed with true understanding and wisdom. It implies that simply hearing the words is not enough - one must strive to discern the best meaning and put it into practice in their lives. The "Word" refers to the Qur'an and its divine message. "Men of understanding" are those who deeply reflect on the wisdom of the Qur'an and use their intellect to grasp its profound meanings, rather than following it blindly or superficially. Ultimately, this verse is a call to thoughtful contemplation and application of Quranic teachings.
orig: الذين يستمعون القول فيتبعون أحسنه أولئك الذين هداهم الله وأولئك هم أولو الألباب

translation: Then, is one who has deserved the decree of punishment [to be guided]? Then, can you save one who is in the Fire?
interpretation: This verse is a rhetorical question that highlights the fate of those who have earned God's punishment due to their actions and choices. It implies that once someone has incurred the decree of divine retribution, no one can save them from the torment of the Fire (Hell). The verse serves as a reminder that each individual is ultimately responsible for their own spiritual destiny, and that even the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) cannot intercede on behalf of those who have persistently rejected faith and righteousness. It emphasizes the gravity of the consequences of one's decisions in this life, and the inability of anyone to rescue those condemned to the Fire in the Hereafter.
orig: أفمن حق عليه كلمة العذاب أفأنت تنقذ من في النار

translation: But those who have feared their Lord will have chambers, above them chambers built high, beneath which rivers flow. [This is] the promise of Allah. Allah does not fail in [His] promise.
interpretation: This verse speaks about the reward that awaits the righteous believers in the Hereafter. Those who have lived their lives in obedience and reverence to Allah will be granted lofty dwellings in Paradise, described as chambers built one above the other. Beneath these chambers, rivers will flow, adding to the beauty and serenity of their abode. This is a promise from Allah Himself, and Allah never fails to fulfill His promises. The verse emphasizes the importance of leading a God-conscious life and serves as an encouragement for believers to strive for righteousness, knowing that their ultimate reward is Paradise, where they will enjoy eternal bliss and comfort in the presence of their Lord.
orig: لكن الذين اتقوا ربهم لهم غرف من فوقها غرف مبنية تجري من تحتها الأنهار وعد الله لا يخلف الله الميعاد

translation: Do you not see that Allah sends down rain from the sky and makes it flow as springs [and rivers] in the earth; then He produces thereby crops of varying colors; then they dry and you see them turned yellow; then He makes them [scattered] debris. Indeed in that is a reminder for those of understanding.
interpretation: This verse is a reminder of Allah's power and the transient nature of this world. It highlights the cycle of life, from the rain that brings forth vegetation to the eventual decay and death of all living things. The changing colors of the crops symbolize the different stages of life, from vibrant youth to the yellowing of old age and finally to the scattered debris of death. This is a powerful message for those who reflect deeply, urging them to remember the temporary nature of this world and to focus on the eternal life to come. It is a call to be mindful of our actions and to live our lives in accordance with Allah's guidance, knowing that all things will eventually come to an end and we will be held accountable for our deeds.
orig: ألم تر أن الله أنزل من السماء ماء فسلكه ينابيع في الأرض ثم يخرج به زرعا مختلفا ألوانه ثم يهيج فتراه مصفرا ثم يجعله حطاما إن في ذلك لذكرى لأولي الألباب

translation: So is one whose breast Allah has expanded to [accept] Islam and he is upon a light from his Lord [like one whose heart rejects it]? Then woe to those whose hearts are hardened against the remembrance of Allah. Those are in manifest error.
interpretation: This verse highlights the contrast between those whose hearts are open to the guidance of Islam and those whose hearts are hardened against the remembrance of Allah. Those who accept Islam and follow the light of guidance from their Lord are in a state of spiritual enlightenment and contentment. On the other hand, those whose hearts are hardened and resist the message of Islam are in a state of manifest error and misguidance. The verse serves as a warning to those who turn away from the remembrance of Allah and reject His guidance, emphasizing the dire consequences of such a choice.
orig: أفمن شرح الله صدره للإسلام فهو على نور من ربه فويل للقاسية قلوبهم من ذكر الله أولئك في ضلال مبين

translation: Allah has sent down the best statement: a consistent Book wherein is reiteration. The skins shiver therefrom of those who fear their Lord; then their skins and their hearts relax at the remembrance of Allah. That is the guidance of Allah by which He guides whom He wills. And one whom Allah leaves astray - for him there is no guide.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the power and beauty of the Qur'an as the best form of speech revealed by Allah. Its consistency and repetition of themes serve to remind and impact the hearts of the believers, causing them to feel a profound sense of awe and reverence for their Lord. The physical response of their skin shivering and then relaxing, along with the softening of their hearts, illustrates the deep spiritual influence of Allah's words upon those who fear Him. The verse also highlights that the Qur'an is a source of guidance, but only for those whom Allah chooses to guide. Those who are left astray by Allah cannot be guided by anyone else, emphasizing His ultimate control and authority over the guidance of mankind.
orig: الله نزل أحسن الحديث كتابا متشابها مثاني تقشعر منه جلود الذين يخشون ربهم ثم تلين جلودهم وقلوبهم إلى ذكر الله ذلك هدى الله يهدي به من يشاء ومن يضلل الله فما له من هاد

translation: Is he who has to guard his face from the evil of the punishment on the Day of Resurrection [like one secure from it]? And it will be said to the wrongdoers, "Taste what you used to earn."
interpretation: This verse is a warning to the wrongdoers and those who reject faith. It contrasts the fate of the disbelievers, who will have to shield their faces from the severity of the punishment on Judgment Day, with the implied state of the righteous believers who will be secure from such torment. The rhetorical question emphasizes that no one would want to be in the position of having to protect themselves from God's punishment. The verse concludes with the wrongdoers being rebuked and told to "taste" the consequences of their evil deeds and rejection of truth, emphasizing the justice of God in punishing them for what they have earned through their own actions.
orig: أفمن يتقي بوجهه سوء العذاب يوم القيامة وقيل للظالمين ذوقوا ما كنتم تكسبون

translation: Those before them denied, and so the punishment came upon them from where they did not perceive.
interpretation: This verse is a warning to those who reject the message of Islam and the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him). It reminds us that previous nations also denied the truth brought by their prophets, and as a result, they were afflicted with divine punishment that came upon them suddenly and from directions they did not expect. The verse implies that the deniers of truth in the present time will also face similar consequences if they persist in their disbelief and rejection of God's message. It serves as a reminder for people to reflect upon the lessons from past nations and to embrace the truth before it is too late, as the punishment of God can come swiftly and unexpectedly to those who continue to deny and oppose His message.
orig: كذب الذين من قبلهم فأتاهم العذاب من حيث لا يشعرون

translation: So Allah made them taste disgrace in worldly life. But the punishment of the Hereafter is greater, if they only knew.
interpretation: This verse is a warning to those who reject faith and oppose the message of Islam. It emphasizes that while they may face humiliation and disgrace in this worldly life as a consequence of their actions, the punishment that awaits them in the Hereafter is far greater and more severe. The verse implies that if they truly understood the gravity of their situation and the consequences of their choices, they would realize the importance of faith and righteous deeds. It serves as a reminder that the ultimate accountability lies in the afterlife, and that the temporary pleasures or gains of this world pale in comparison to the eternal consequences of one's actions.
orig: فأذاقهم الله الخزي في الحياة الدنيا ولعذاب الآخرة أكبر لو كانوا يعلمون

translation: And indeed We have put forth for men, in this Quran every kind of similitude in order that they may remember.
interpretation: This verse highlights the Qur'an's use of parables, analogies, and examples drawn from various aspects of life to convey its message effectively. The purpose of these similitudes is to make the teachings of the Qur'an more relatable, understandable, and memorable for people. By presenting the divine message in a way that resonates with human experiences and observations, Allah encourages people to reflect upon the Qur'an's wisdom, internalize its lessons, and apply them in their lives. The verse emphasizes the Qur'an's universality and its ability to address the diverse needs and understanding of all people, regardless of their background or era.
orig: ولقد ضربنا للناس في هذا القرآن من كل مثل لعلهم يتذكرون

translation: An Arabic Quran, without any crookedness, so that they may become righteous.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the Qur'an is revealed in clear, straightforward Arabic language, free from any distortion or ambiguity. Its purpose is to guide people towards righteousness and piety. The Qur'an's clarity and directness in conveying its message is intended to make it easily understandable and accessible to those who seek guidance, enabling them to follow the straight path and avoid deviating from it. By adhering to the teachings of the Qur'an, one can cultivate taqwa, or consciousness of Allah, which is the key to attaining righteousness and success in this life and the hereafter.
orig: قرآنا عربيا غير ذي عوج لعلهم يتقون

translation: Allah presents an example: a slave owned by quarreling partners and another belonging exclusively to one man - are they equal in comparison? Praise be to Allah! But most of them do not know.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the concept of monotheism (Tawheed) using a metaphor. The man owned by multiple quarreling partners represents the one who worships multiple deities or follows multiple belief systems, leading to confusion and internal conflict. In contrast, the man belonging exclusively to one master represents the believer who worships Allah alone, leading to inner peace and harmony. The verse emphasizes that these two states are not equal, with the latter being superior. It also suggests that most people fail to recognize this truth and the importance of dedicating oneself to the worship of the One True God.
orig: ضرب الله مثلا رجلا فيه شركاء متشاكسون ورجلا سلما لرجل هل يستويان مثلا الحمد لله بل أكثرهم لا يعلمون

translation: Indeed, you are to die, and indeed, they are to die as well.
interpretation: This verse is a reminder of the inevitable reality of death. It emphasizes that no one, not even the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him), is exempt from this fate. The verse serves as a powerful reminder for all of humanity to reflect on the temporary nature of this worldly life and to strive for righteousness and good deeds, as we will all face the consequences of our actions in the Hereafter. It encourages humility, as death is the great equalizer, and it motivates believers to make the most of their limited time on Earth by living a life pleasing to Allah.
orig: إنك ميت وإنهم ميتون

translation: Then, on the Day of Resurrection, you will be disputing before your Lord.
interpretation: This verse is a reminder that on the Day of Judgment, people will present their disputes and arguments before Allah. It implies that all the differences, conflicts, and disagreements that exist among people in this worldly life will be brought forth on that day, and Allah will judge between them with perfect justice. This verse serves as a warning for people to be mindful of their actions and to strive for reconciliation and righteousness in this life, as they will be held accountable for their deeds in the Hereafter.
orig: ثم إنكم يوم القيامة عند ربكم تختصمون

translation: So who is more unjust than one who lies about Allah and denies the truth when it has come to him? Is there not in Hell a residence for the disbelievers?
interpretation: This verse is a rhetorical question that emphasizes the severity of the sin of lying about Allah and rejecting the truth of His message when it is presented. It suggests that there can be no greater injustice than to attribute falsehood to Allah or to deny the truth that comes from Him. The verse then answers its own question by affirming that those who disbelieve and reject the truth will have their eternal dwelling in Hell as a consequence of their actions. It serves as a strong warning against denying Allah's truth and a reminder of the ultimate fate that awaits those who persist in disbelief.
orig: فمن أظلم ممن كذب على الله وكذب بالصدق إذ جاءه أليس في جهنم مثوى للكافرين

translation: And the one who has brought the truth and [they who] believed in it - those are the righteous.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of truthfulness and belief in the truth. Those who bring the truth, such as the prophets and messengers, and those who sincerely believe in and follow that truth are considered among the righteous and God-fearing individuals. It highlights that true righteousness lies in accepting and adhering to the truth that comes from God, rather than mere claims or outward actions. The verse also implies that believing in and following the truth requires courage and sincerity, as it may face opposition or challenges from others who reject it.
orig: والذي جاء بالصدق وصدق به أولئك هم المتقون

translation: They will have whatever they wish with their Lord. That is the reward of the doers of good.
interpretation: This verse speaks to the immense rewards that await the righteous believers in Paradise. It emphasizes that those who lived their lives in accordance with God's commands and did good deeds will be granted their heart's desires in the afterlife. The verse underscores that such blessings are not mere wishes, but a recompense from God Himself for the believers' righteousness. It motivates the faithful to persist in virtue, knowing that their ultimate reward will be the fulfillment of their souls' deepest longings in the gardens of eternal bliss. The verse encapsulates God's infinite generosity towards those who excel in faith and good works.
orig: لهم ما يشاءون عند ربهم ذلك جزاء المحسنين

translation: That Allah may remove from them the worst of what they did and reward them their due for the best of what they used to do.
interpretation: This verse conveys the immense mercy and forgiveness of Allah towards His servants. It indicates that Allah, in His infinite grace, is willing to overlook the worst of a person's deeds and instead reward them according to the best of their actions. This highlights the importance of repentance, seeking forgiveness, and striving to do good deeds consistently. It also serves as a reminder that one should never despair of Allah's mercy, no matter how grave their sins may seem, for Allah's forgiveness encompasses all. The verse encourages believers to turn to Allah with sincere repentance and to have hope in His boundless compassion and generosity in rewarding righteousness.
orig: ليكفر الله عنهم أسوأ الذي عملوا ويجزيهم أجرهم بأحسن الذي كانوا يعملون

translation: Is not Allah sufficient for His Servant [Prophet Muhammad]? And [yet], they threaten you with those [they worship] other than Him. And whoever Allah leaves astray - for him there is no guide.
interpretation: This verse assures Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) that Allah is sufficient for him as a protector and supporter, despite the threats and intimidation from the disbelievers who worship other deities. It emphasizes that those who Allah allows to go astray due to their choice to reject His guidance will have no one to guide them, as Allah alone is the ultimate source of guidance. The verse serves as a comfort and reassurance to the Prophet and the believers, highlighting the power and sufficiency of Allah in the face of opposition and challenges from those who associate partners with Him.
orig: أليس الله بكاف عبده ويخوفونك بالذين من دونه ومن يضلل الله فما له من هاد

translation: And whoever Allah guides - for him there is no misleader. Is not Allah Exalted in Might and Owner of Retribution?
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's power and control over the guidance of individuals. It asserts that when Allah guides someone, no one can lead them astray. The rhetorical question at the end of the verse serves as a reminder of Allah's might and His ability to exact retribution on those who oppose Him or lead others away from His path. It underscores the idea that Allah's will is supreme and that He has the power to both guide individuals and punish those who work against His guidance. The verse encourages believers to trust in Allah's guidance and to be mindful of His power and justice.
orig: ومن يهد الله فما له من مضل أليس الله بعزيز ذي انتقام

translation: And if you asked them, "Who created the heavens and the earth?" they would surely say, "Allah." Say, "Then have you considered what you invoke besides Allah? If Allah intended me harm, are they removers of His harm; or if He intended me mercy, are they withholders of His mercy?" Say, "Sufficient for me is Allah; upon Him [alone] rely the [wise] reliers."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute power and sovereignty of Allah. Even the polytheists acknowledge that Allah is the Creator of the heavens and earth, yet they still invoke other deities besides Him. The Prophet is instructed to challenge their logic by asking if these false gods can remove any harm or withhold any mercy that Allah intends for him. The verse affirms that Allah alone is sufficient for the believers and that they should put their complete trust in Him. It highlights the futility of seeking help or protection from anyone other than Allah, as no one has the power to influence His will or decisions. The wise believers are those who rely solely upon Allah, recognizing His complete control over all affairs and submitting to His decree.
orig: ولئن سألتهم من خلق السماوات والأرض ليقولن الله قل أفرأيتم ما تدعون من دون الله إن أرادني الله بضر هل هن كاشفات ضره أو أرادني برحمة هل هن ممسكات رحمته قل حسبي الله عليه يتوكل المتوكلون

translation: Say, "O my people, work according to your position; [for] indeed, I am working. And you are going to know"
interpretation: This verse is a warning to the disbelievers who reject the message of Islam. It tells them to continue in their ways and that the Prophet (peace be upon him) will continue in his. The verse implies that the ultimate consequences of each party's actions will become apparent in due time, and the disbelievers will come to know the error of their ways and the truth of the Prophet's message. It conveys a sense of confidence on the part of the Prophet in the face of opposition and rejection, and a warning to the disbelievers that their choices will have consequences in this life and the next.
orig: قل يا قوم اعملوا على مكانتكم إني عامل فسوف تعلمون

translation: He will be afflicted by a disgracing torment, and a lasting punishment will descend upon him.
interpretation: This verse warns of the severe consequences that await those who reject faith and persist in wrongdoing. The "disgracing torment" refers to the humiliation and shame that the sinner will experience in this world and the Hereafter as a result of their misdeeds. The "lasting punishment" emphasizes the unending nature of the torment in the afterlife, serving as a stark reminder of the gravity of turning away from God's guidance. The verse aims to inspire introspection and repentance, urging individuals to align their actions with divine teachings to avoid such a fate.
orig: من يأتيه عذاب يخزيه ويحل عليه عذاب مقيم

translation: Indeed, We have sent down to you the Book for the people in truth. So whoever is guided - it is for [the benefit of] his soul; and whoever goes astray only goes astray to its detriment. And you are not a manager over them.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the Qur'an has been revealed as a guidance for all of humanity. It is a reminder that each individual is responsible for their own spiritual path and the consequences of their choices. The Prophet's role is to convey the message, not to force people to believe or be held accountable for their decisions. Ultimately, each soul will bear the responsibility for its own actions and whether it chooses to be guided by the truth of the Qur'an or to go astray. The verse highlights the importance of free will and individual accountability in the journey of faith.
orig: إنا أنزلنا عليك الكتاب للناس بالحق فمن اهتدى فلنفسه ومن ضل فإنما يضل عليها وما أنت عليهم بوكيل

translation: Allah takes the souls at the time of their death, and those that do not die [He takes] during their sleep. Then He keeps those for which He has decreed death and releases the others for a specified term. Indeed in that are signs for a people who give thought.
interpretation: This verse speaks to the power and control of Allah over life and death. It emphasizes that Allah is the one who takes the souls of people, both at the time of their physical death and during their sleep. Those whose time has come are kept with Him, while the others are sent back until their appointed time. This is a reminder for people to reflect on the temporary nature of this life and the inevitability of death, and to turn to Allah in remembrance and obedience. It also highlights the concept of divine decree and predestination, as Allah has already determined the time of death for each soul. The verse encourages people to ponder over these signs and to live their lives with the awareness that they will ultimately return to their Creator.
orig: الله يتوفى الأنفس حين موتها والتي لم تمت في منامها فيمسك التي قضى عليها الموت ويرسل الأخرى إلى أجل مسمى إن في ذلك لآيات لقوم يتفكرون

translation: Or have they taken intercessors besides Allah? Say, "Even though they do not possess [power over] anything, nor do they reason?"
interpretation: This verse questions the logic of those who take intercessors besides Allah. It points out the futility of such an action, as these supposed intercessors have no power or ability to reason. The rhetorical question serves to highlight the irrationality of worshipping or seeking help from anyone other than Allah, who alone holds power over all things. It emphasizes that only Allah is worthy of worship and that relying on anyone else for intercession or help is misguided and baseless.
orig: أم اتخذوا من دون الله شفعاء قل أولو كانوا لا يملكون شيئا ولا يعقلون

translation: Say, "To Allah belongs [the right to allow] intercession entirely. To Him belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth. Then to Him you will be returned."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the power of intercession belongs solely to Allah. He is the ultimate authority over the heavens and the earth, and all will return to Him for judgment. It serves as a reminder that no one can intercede on behalf of another except by Allah's permission, highlighting His supreme sovereignty and the importance of directing all worship and supplication towards Him alone. The verse also points to the inevitability of the Day of Judgment, when all souls will be brought before Allah to face the consequences of their deeds in this world.
orig: قل لله الشفاعة جميعا له ملك السماوات والأرض ثم إليه ترجعون

translation: And when Allah is mentioned alone, the hearts of those who do not believe in the Hereafter shrink with aversion, but when those [worshipped] other than Him are mentioned, immediately they rejoice.
interpretation: This verse highlights the stark contrast between the believers and the disbelievers. When Allah is mentioned alone, without associating any partners with Him, the hearts of those who reject the concept of the Hereafter are filled with disgust and aversion. They find no comfort or joy in the remembrance of Allah. However, when the false deities or idols that they worship besides Allah are mentioned, they become elated and rejoice. This shows the misguided nature of their beliefs and their attachment to false gods. It emphasizes the importance of pure monotheism and the need to worship Allah alone, without associating any partners with Him.
orig: وإذا ذكر الله وحده اشمأزت قلوب الذين لا يؤمنون بالآخرة وإذا ذكر الذين من دونه إذا هم يستبشرون

translation: Say, "O Allah, Creator of the heavens and the earth, Knower of the unseen and the witnessed, You will judge between your servants concerning that over which they used to differ."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute authority and sovereignty of Allah as the Creator and Supreme Judge. It highlights that Allah alone possesses the knowledge of the unseen and the seen, and He will ultimately judge between people regarding their differences and disputes on the Day of Judgment. The verse serves as a reminder for believers to turn to Allah for guidance and resolution, acknowledging His omniscience and supreme authority in all matters. It also implies that people should strive to resolve their conflicts and differences in accordance with Allah's teachings and commandments, as they will be held accountable for their actions in the Hereafter.
orig: قل اللهم فاطر السماوات والأرض عالم الغيب والشهادة أنت تحكم بين عبادك في ما كانوا فيه يختلفون

translation: And if those who did wrong had all that is in the earth entirely and the like of it with it, they would [attempt to] ransom themselves thereby from the worst of the punishment on the Day of Resurrection. And there will appear to them from Allah that which they had not taken into account.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the severity and inescapability of Allah's punishment for the wrongdoers on the Day of Judgment. Even if they possessed all the wealth in the world and more, it would not be enough to ransom themselves from the terrible consequences of their actions. The verse also suggests that the punishment will be something unexpected and beyond their imagination, as "there will appear to them from Allah that which they had not taken into account." This serves as a powerful warning for people to be mindful of their deeds and to seek forgiveness before it is too late.
orig: ولو أن للذين ظلموا ما في الأرض جميعا ومثله معه لافتدوا به من سوء العذاب يوم القيامة وبدا لهم من الله ما لم يكونوا يحتسبون

translation: And the evil consequences of what they earned will appear to them, and they will be enveloped by what they used to ridicule.
interpretation: This verse warns that the disbelievers and wrongdoers will face the negative repercussions of their actions and will be surrounded by the very things they used to mock and dismiss. It emphasizes the idea of divine justice, where people will be held accountable for their deeds and will experience the consequences of their choices in this world and the Hereafter. The verse also implies that the disbelievers' arrogance and derision towards the truth will ultimately lead to their own suffering and humiliation when the reality of their actions becomes apparent to them.
orig: وبدا لهم سيئات ما كسبوا وحاق بهم ما كانوا به يستهزئون

translation: When affliction touches man, he calls on Us, then when We bestow on him a favor from Us, he says, "I have only been given it because of [my] knowledge." Rather, it is a trial, but most of them do not know.
interpretation: This verse highlights the fickle nature of human beings. When faced with hardship, they turn to Allah for help and guidance. However, when Allah grants them favors and blessings, they attribute their success to their own knowledge and abilities, rather than acknowledging the true source of their blessings. This attitude is a form of ingratitude and a failure to recognize the trials and tests that Allah puts before us. The verse serves as a reminder that all blessings come from Allah, and that we should remain humble and grateful, even in times of prosperity. It also emphasizes the importance of seeking knowledge and understanding, as true knowledge leads to the recognition of Allah's power and the realization that all things are ultimately a test from Him.
orig: فإذا مس الإنسان ضر دعانا ثم إذا خولناه نعمة منا قال إنما أوتيته على علم بل هي فتنة ولكن أكثرهم لا يعلمون

translation: Those before them had already said it, but they were not availed by what they used to earn.
interpretation: This verse is a reminder that those who reject the message of Islam and the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) are not the first to do so. Previous nations also rejected their prophets and the message they brought, but their worldly gains and achievements did not protect them from the consequences of their disbelief and disobedience to Allah. This serves as a warning that no matter how much wealth, power, or status one may accumulate in this life, it will ultimately be of no benefit if one does not have faith and does not follow the guidance of Allah. The only path to success and salvation is through sincere belief and righteous deeds.
orig: قد قالها الذين من قبلهم فما أغنى عنهم ما كانوا يكسبون

translation: And the evil consequences of what they earned struck them. And those who have wronged of these [people] will be afflicted by the evil consequences of what they earned; and they will not cause failure.
interpretation: This verse warns that those who engage in evil deeds and wrongdoing will face the negative repercussions of their actions. It emphasizes the concept of divine justice, where individuals are held accountable for their choices and will experience the consequences of their misdeeds. The verse also suggests that no one can escape or prevent the consequences of their actions, as they are bound to face the results of what they have earned. It serves as a reminder for people to be mindful of their deeds and to refrain from wrongdoing, as the consequences will inevitably catch up with them.
orig: فأصابهم سيئات ما كسبوا والذين ظلموا من هؤلاء سيصيبهم سيئات ما كسبوا وما هم بمعجزين

translation: Do they not know that Allah extends provision for whom He wills and restricts [it]? Indeed in that are signs for a people who believe.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's absolute control over the distribution of sustenance and provisions among His creation. He alone has the power to grant abundance to whomever He wills and to limit it for others according to His infinite wisdom. The varying levels of provision among people serve as a test of faith, reminding believers to be content with what they have been given and to trust in Allah's plan. The verse also points to the fact that the distribution of wealth is not random or unjust, but rather a purposeful decision by Allah. Those who have faith will recognize these variations as signs of Allah's power and wisdom, using them as opportunities for reflection and gratitude rather than envy or resentment. Ultimately, the verse encourages believers to place their trust in Allah's providence and to remain steadfast in their faith, knowing that He is the All-Wise and All-Knowing.
orig: أولم يعلموا أن الله يبسط الرزق لمن يشاء ويقدر إن في ذلك لآيات لقوم يؤمنون

translation: Say, "O My servants who have transgressed against themselves [by sinning], do not despair of the mercy of Allah. Indeed, Allah forgives all sins. Indeed, it is He who is the Forgiving, the Merciful."
interpretation: This verse is a powerful reminder of Allah's infinite mercy and forgiveness. It encourages those who have sinned and transgressed against themselves to never lose hope in Allah's mercy. No matter how great the sin, Allah is willing to forgive those who sincerely repent and turn back to Him. This verse emphasizes that Allah's forgiveness knows no bounds, and that He is the ultimate source of mercy and compassion.
