It serves as a comforting message for those who may feel burdened by their past mistakes, reassuring them that the door to repentance and forgiveness is always open.
orig: قل يا عبادي الذين أسرفوا على أنفسهم لا تقنطوا من رحمة الله إن الله يغفر الذنوب جميعا إنه هو الغفور الرحيم

translation: And turn in repentance to your Lord and submit to Him before the punishment comes upon you; then you will not be helped.
interpretation: This verse is a reminder for people to turn back to Allah in sincere repentance and completely submit to Him before it's too late and the punishment descends upon them. Once the punishment arrives, there will be no one to help or support them. It emphasizes the importance of seeking forgiveness and aligning one's life with the teachings of Islam before facing the consequences in the Hereafter. The verse urges individuals to prioritize their spiritual well-being and relationship with Allah above all else.
orig: وأنيبوا إلى ربكم وأسلموا له من قبل أن يأتيكم العذاب ثم لا تنصرون

translation: And follow the best of what was revealed to you from your Lord before the punishment comes upon you suddenly while you do not perceive.
interpretation: This verse is a reminder for people to adhere to the teachings and guidance revealed in the Qur'an before it is too late. It emphasizes the importance of following the best and most virtuous aspects of the revelation, as it comes directly from Allah. The verse also warns that divine punishment can come suddenly and unexpectedly, catching people off guard while they are unaware or heedless. It implies that by following the Qur'an's teachings, one can protect themselves from such punishment and attain Allah's mercy and forgiveness.
orig: واتبعوا أحسن ما أنزل إليكم من ربكم من قبل أن يأتيكم العذاب بغتة وأنتم لا تشعرون

translation: Lest a soul should say, "Oh, [how great is] my regret over what I neglected in regard to Allah and that I was among the mockers."
interpretation: This verse is a warning and reminder for people not to neglect their duties towards Allah and mock His signs or religion. It emphasizes the regret one would feel on the Day of Judgment for not fulfilling their obligations to Allah and for taking His messages lightly or in jest during their worldly life. The verse encourages believers to be mindful of their actions, to obey Allah's commands, and to refrain from ridiculing or undermining matters related to faith, as doing so would lead to immense regret and loss in the Hereafter.
orig: أن تقول نفس يا حسرتا على ما فرطت في جنب الله وإن كنت لمن الساخرين

translation: Or you would say, "If only Allah had guided me, I would have been among the righteous."
interpretation: This verse suggests that on the Day of Judgment, those who rejected faith and guidance from Allah will regret their choices and wish that they had followed the path of righteousness. They will realize the error of their ways and long for the guidance they ignored in their worldly life. It highlights the importance of heeding divine guidance and living a life of piety and righteousness to avoid such regrets in the afterlife. The verse also emphasizes Allah's role as the ultimate guide and the one who can lead people to the straight path if they sincerely seek His guidance.
orig: أو تقول لو أن الله هداني لكنت من المتقين

translation: Or [lest] it say when it sees the punishment, "If only I had another turn so I could be among the doers of good."
interpretation: This verse is a warning to those who reject faith and do evil deeds. When they face the punishment of Hell on the Day of Judgment, they will wish for another chance to return to the world and do righteous deeds. However, it will be too late, as they had already been given ample opportunities in their worldly life to believe and do good, but they squandered them. This highlights the importance of making the most of the present life to earn God's pleasure before death takes us and we have no more chances left. It also emphasizes the severity and permanence of the punishment of Hell, which will make the disbelievers deeply regret their choices and wish desperately for another chance that will never come.
orig: أو تقول حين ترى العذاب لو أن لي كرة فأكون من المحسنين

translation: Yes, indeed My signs came to you, but you denied them and were arrogant and became of the disbelievers.
interpretation: This verse is a stern rebuke and reminder from Allah to those who rejected His signs and messages that came to them through His prophets and messengers. It highlights the arrogance and pride that led them to disbelief, as they considered themselves too great to humble themselves and submit to Allah's guidance. The consequence of such persistent denial and arrogance is that they became counted among the disbelievers, those who have gone astray from the straight path and earned Allah's anger and punishment in the Hereafter. It serves as a warning to all of mankind to be receptive to divine guidance and to avoid the pitfalls of arrogance and disbelief that lead to doom and loss in this world and the next.
orig: بلى قد جاءتك آياتي فكذبت بها واستكبرت وكنت من الكافرين

translation: And on the Day of Resurrection you will see those who lied about Allah [with] their faces blackened. Is there not in Hell a residence for the arrogant?
interpretation: This verse is a stern warning to those who attribute false statements to Allah or reject His signs. On the Day of Judgment, their faces will be darkened, signifying their shame, humiliation, and the gravity of their sin. The rhetorical question at the end emphasizes that Hell is indeed the appropriate abode for those who arrogantly refuse to accept the truth and persist in their lies and disbelief. It serves as a reminder that one's actions and beliefs in this life have consequences in the Hereafter, and that the ultimate fate of the arrogant disbelievers is the punishment of Hell.
orig: ويوم القيامة ترى الذين كذبوا على الله وجوههم مسودة أليس في جهنم مثوى للمتكبرين

translation: And Allah will deliver those who feared Him to their place of salvation; no evil will touch them, nor will they grieve.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that those who are mindful of Allah and live righteously will be saved from harm and suffering in the Hereafter. Allah will protect them and grant them success, ensuring that they will not be afflicted by any evil or distress. The verse highlights the importance of having taqwa (God-consciousness) and the rewards that come with it. It serves as a reminder for believers to strive for righteousness in this world, as it will lead to their ultimate salvation and protection from any form of grief or sorrow in the eternal life to come.
orig: وينجي الله الذين اتقوا بمفازتهم لا يمسهم السوء ولا هم يحزنون

translation: Allah is the Creator of all things, and He is, over all things, Disposer of affairs.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute power and authority of Allah over all of His creation. It affirms that Allah is the sole Creator of everything that exists, and that He is the ultimate Disposer of all affairs. This means that nothing happens in the universe without His knowledge, permission, and control. It also implies that all creatures are dependent on Allah for their existence and sustenance, and that they should submit to His will and seek His guidance in all matters of life. This verse is a powerful reminder of Allah's omnipotence and sovereignty, and it encourages believers to put their trust in Him and seek His help and protection at all times.
orig: الله خالق كل شيء وهو على كل شيء وكيل

translation: To Him belong the keys of the heavens and the earth. And those who disbelieve in the signs of Allah - it is they who are the losers.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah holds absolute control and authority over the entire universe. The keys symbolize His power and dominion. Those who reject Allah's signs and messages are described as the ultimate losers because they fail to recognize and submit to the truth, depriving themselves of His guidance and mercy. The verse implies that true success lies in believing in Allah and following His path, while disbelief leads to spiritual loss and failure in both this world and the hereafter.
orig: له مقاليد السماوات والأرض والذين كفروا بآيات الله أولئك هم الخاسرون

translation: Say, "Is it other than Allah that you order me to worship, O ignorant ones?"
interpretation: This verse is a strong rebuke to those who call upon others to worship anyone or anything besides Allah. It emphasizes the ignorance and foolishness of such people, as they fail to recognize that worship and devotion should be directed solely to the One True God, Allah. The Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) is instructed to firmly reject any calls to worship false deities or idols, and to proclaim his unwavering commitment to the worship of Allah alone. This verse serves as a reminder to all believers to remain steadfast in their faith and to reject any form of polytheism or idolatry, no matter how persuasive or influential those who promote such practices may be.
orig: قل أفغير الله تأمروني أعبد أيها الجاهلون

translation: And it was already revealed to you and to those before you that if you should associate [anything] with Allah, your work would surely become worthless, and you would surely be among the losers.
interpretation: This verse is a stern warning against associating partners with Allah (shirk). It emphasizes that even if one has done many good deeds, if they commit shirk, all their deeds will be rendered null and void, and they will be among the losers in the Hereafter. This highlights the gravity of shirk and the importance of maintaining pure monotheism (tawheed). It also serves as a reminder that no matter how righteous a person may be, they must always guard against falling into shirk, as it can negate all their efforts and lead to eternal loss.
orig: ولقد أوحي إليك وإلى الذين من قبلك لئن أشركت ليحبطن عملك ولتكونن من الخاسرين

translation: Rather, worship [only] Allah and be among the grateful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of worshipping Allah alone and being grateful for His blessings. It reminds us that our ultimate purpose in life is to submit to the will of Allah and express gratitude for all that He has bestowed upon us. By dedicating ourselves to the worship of Allah and acknowledging His favors, we can attain true contentment and fulfillment in both this world and the hereafter. The verse also implies that gratitude is a key characteristic of a believer, as it demonstrates our recognition of Allah's mercy and kindness towards us.
orig: بل الله فاعبد وكن من الشاكرين

translation: They have not appraised Allah with true appraisal, while the earth entirely will be [within] His grip on the Day of Resurrection, and the heavens will be folded in His right hand. Exalted is He and high above what they associate with Him.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the immense power and greatness of Allah, which humans often fail to truly comprehend or appreciate. It depicts a vivid image of the Day of Judgment, where the entire earth will be held in Allah's grip, and the vast heavens will be folded up in His right hand. This metaphorical description illustrates Allah's absolute control and dominion over all of creation. The verse also affirms Allah's transcendence and superiority above any partners or equals that people may wrongfully attribute to Him, highlighting the grave error of polytheism or idolatry. It serves as a powerful reminder for humans to acknowledge and revere Allah's unparalleled might and sovereignty.
orig: وما قدروا الله حق قدره والأرض جميعا قبضته يوم القيامة والسماوات مطويات بيمينه سبحانه وتعالى عما يشركون

translation: And the Horn will be blown, and whoever is in the heavens and whoever is on the earth will fall dead except whom Allah wills. Then it will be blown again, and at once they will be standing, looking on.
interpretation: This verse speaks about the Day of Judgment, when the trumpet will be blown twice. The first blow will cause all creatures in the heavens and the earth to die, except those whom Allah wills to spare. This signifies the end of the world as we know it. The second blow will bring the dead back to life, and they will rise from their graves, standing and waiting for the judgment to begin. This verse emphasizes the power and authority of Allah over all of His creation, and the inevitability of the Day of Judgment, where every soul will be held accountable for their deeds in this world.
orig: ونفخ في الصور فصعق من في السماوات ومن في الأرض إلا من شاء الله ثم نفخ فيه أخرى فإذا هم قيام ينظرون

translation: And the earth will shine with the light of its Lord, and the record [of deeds] will be placed, and the prophets and the witnesses will be brought, and it will be judged between them in truth, and they will not be wronged.
interpretation: This verse refers to the Day of Judgment when the earth will be illuminated by the light of Allah's presence. The book of deeds will be presented, and the prophets and witnesses will be brought forth to testify. The judgment will be carried out with perfect justice, and no one will be treated unfairly. It emphasizes the idea that on the Day of Judgment, all will be held accountable for their actions, and the ultimate truth will be revealed. It serves as a reminder for believers to lead righteous lives, knowing that they will face the consequences of their deeds in the presence of Allah.
orig: وأشرقت الأرض بنور ربها ووضع الكتاب وجيء بالنبيين والشهداء وقضي بينهم بالحق وهم لا يظلمون

translation: And every soul will be fully compensated for what it did, and He is most knowing of what they do.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the perfect justice of Allah on the Day of Judgment. Each person will be recompensed in full for their deeds, good or evil, as Allah is completely aware of everything that people do in this worldly life. Nothing escapes His knowledge, and He will ensure that everyone receives what they deserve based on their actions, intentions, and the consequences of their deeds. This verse serves as a reminder for people to be mindful of their actions and to strive for righteousness, knowing that they will be held accountable before Allah.
orig: ووفيت كل نفس ما عملت وهو أعلم بما يفعلون

translation: And those who disbelieved will be driven to Hell in groups until, when they reach it, its gates are opened and its keepers will say, "Did there not come to you messengers from yourselves, reciting to you the verses of your Lord and warning you of the meeting of this Day of yours?" They will say, "Yes, but the word of punishment has come into effect upon the disbelievers."
interpretation: This verse describes the fate of the disbelievers on the Day of Judgment. They will be driven to Hell in groups, and upon reaching it, they will find its gates open and its keepers ready to receive them. The keepers will then rebuke the disbelievers, asking if they had not been warned by messengers from among themselves who recited God's verses to them and warned them of this very Day. The disbelievers will acknowledge that they were indeed warned, but they will also admit that the decree of punishment has been justly carried out against them due to their rejection of faith. This interpretation highlights the consequences of disbelief and the importance of heeding the warnings conveyed by God's messengers.
orig: وسيق الذين كفروا إلى جهنم زمرا حتى إذا جاءوها فتحت أبوابها وقال لهم خزنتها ألم يأتكم رسل منكم يتلون عليكم آيات ربكم وينذرونكم لقاء يومكم هذا قالوا بلى ولكن حقت كلمة العذاب على الكافرين

translation: It will be said, "Enter the gates of Hell to abide eternally therein, and wretched is the residence of the arrogant."
interpretation: This verse is a stern warning to those who are arrogant and reject the truth of God's message. It emphasizes that the ultimate fate of such people will be to enter the gates of Hell, where they will remain forever. The verse highlights the terrible consequences of arrogance and pride, which lead one away from the path of righteousness and towards eternal punishment. It serves as a reminder to all believers to cultivate humility and submission to God, as these are the qualities that will lead to success in this life and the hereafter. The verse also underscores the justice of God, as those who are arrogant and reject His message will face the consequences of their actions in the form of an abode in Hell, which is described as a wretched and miserable place, in stark contrast to the blissful abode of Paradise that awaits the righteous.
orig: قيل ادخلوا أبواب جهنم خالدين فيها فبئس مثوى المتكبرين

translation: And those who feared their Lord will be led to Paradise in groups until, when they reach it while its gates have been opened and its keepers say, "Peace be upon you; you have become pure; so enter it to abide eternally therein,"
interpretation: This verse describes the ultimate reward for those who lived their lives in obedience and reverence to Allah. They will be led to Paradise in honored groups, finding its gates wide open in welcome. The keepers of Paradise will greet them with the salutation of "Peace be upon you", affirming that they have been purified of all sins and imperfections. They will be invited to enter Paradise, not as temporary guests, but as eternal dwellers. This emphasizes the everlasting nature of the reward, in contrast to the fleeting nature of this worldly life. The verse instills hope and motivation for believers to persevere in faith and righteousness.
orig: وسيق الذين اتقوا ربهم إلى الجنة زمرا حتى إذا جاءوها وفتحت أبوابها وقال لهم خزنتها سلام عليكم طبتم فادخلوها خالدين

translation: And they will say, "All praise is due to Allah, who has fulfilled for us His promise and made us inherit the earth, settling in Paradise wherever we please." How excellent is the reward of the [righteous] workers!
interpretation: This verse speaks to the ultimate reward and satisfaction of the righteous believers in the Hereafter. They will praise Allah for fulfilling His promise of granting them Paradise, where they will have the freedom to settle wherever they desire. This emphasizes that their good deeds and righteousness in this world will be compensated with the most excellent reward conceivable in the afterlife - Paradise. It motivates believers to continue striving in Allah's cause, knowing that their efforts will never go to waste and that they will be granted the ultimate abode of peace and pleasure, precisely as Allah has promised.
orig: وقالوا الحمد لله الذي صدقنا وعده وأورثنا الأرض نتبوأ من الجنة حيث نشاء فنعم أجر العاملين

translation: And you will see the angels surrounding the Throne, exalting [Allah] with praise of their Lord. And it will be judged between them in truth, and it will be said, "[All] praise is [due] to Allah, Lord of the worlds."
interpretation: This verse depicts a powerful scene from the Day of Judgment, where the angels are seen encircling the Throne of Allah, glorifying Him with praises. It signifies that on that day, all matters will be judged with perfect justice and truth, leaving no room for doubt or ambiguity. The final statement, "All praise is due to Allah, Lord of the worlds," is a declaration of Allah's supreme authority and sovereignty over all creation. It emphasizes that ultimately, all praise and gratitude belong to Him alone, as He is the One who has created and sustained the entire universe. This verse serves as a reminder for believers to strive for justice and righteousness in this world, knowing that they will be held accountable for their deeds in the presence of Allah on the Day of Judgment.
orig: وترى الملائكة حافين من حول العرش يسبحون بحمد ربهم وقضي بينهم بالحق وقيل الحمد لله رب العالمين

translation: Ha, Meem.
interpretation: This verse consists of two Arabic letters, "Ha" and "Meem". Many chapters of the Qur'an begin with such mysterious letters, known as "Al-Muqatta'at" or "The Disjoined Letters". The exact meaning and purpose of these letters is not explicitly mentioned in the Qur'an or Hadith. Scholars have proposed various interpretations, such as them being a way to draw attention to the divine nature of the Qur'an, or as a challenge to those who doubt the Qur'an's authenticity to produce something similar. Ultimately, the true meaning of these letters is known only to Allah, and they serve as a reminder of the Qur'an's miraculous nature and the limitless wisdom of its Creator.
orig: حم

translation: The revelation of the Book is from Allah, the Exalted in Might, the Wise.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the Qur'an is a divine revelation from Allah, who is described as the Exalted in Might and the Wise. It affirms that the source of the Qur'an is Allah Himself, and not the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) or any other human being. The attributes of Allah mentioned here, "Al-Aziz" (the Exalted in Might) and "Al-Alim" (the All-Knowing), underscore His power and knowledge, indicating that the Qur'an is a manifestation of His wisdom and authority. This verse sets the stage for the revelations that follow, establishing the divine origin and authenticity of the Qur'an.
orig: تنزيل الكتاب من الله العزيز العليم

translation: The Forgiver of sin, the Accepter of repentance, the Severe in punishment, the Bestower of favours. There is no god but He, to Him is the final return.
interpretation: This verse highlights some of the key attributes of Allah. He is the one who forgives sins when people sincerely repent and turn back to Him. At the same time, He is severe in punishing those who persist in wrongdoing and transgression. He is the source of all blessings and favors bestowed on His creation. The verse affirms the fundamental Islamic belief in the oneness of Allah and that He alone is worthy of worship. It also reminds us that everyone will ultimately return to Allah in the Hereafter to be held accountable for their deeds. This should motivate the believer to be conscious of Allah, seek His forgiveness, and strive to do good in this worldly life.
orig: غافر الذنب وقابل التوب شديد العقاب ذي الطول لا إله إلا هو إليه المصير

translation: None dispute in the signs of Allah except those who disbelieve, so be not deceived by their [uninhibited] movement throughout the land.
interpretation: This verse warns believers not to be misled by the apparent worldly success and prosperity of the disbelievers who reject and argue against Allah's signs and revelations. Their freedom to travel and engage in worldly activities should not be taken as a sign of Allah's approval or their ultimate success in the Hereafter. Rather, it is a temporary respite and a test. Believers should remain steadfast in their faith and not be swayed by the disbelievers' worldly positions or arguments against the truth of Islam. Ultimately, the disbelievers' rejection will lead to their loss in the Hereafter, while the believers' faith and righteousness will be rewarded with eternal success in Paradise.
orig: ما يجادل في آيات الله إلا الذين كفروا فلا يغررك تقلبهم في البلاد

translation: The people of Noah denied before them, and the [disbelieving] factions after them, and every nation intended [a plot] for their messenger to seize him, and they disputed by [using] falsehood to [attempt to] invalidate thereby the truth. So I seized them, and how [terrible] was My penalty.
interpretation: This verse highlights the recurring pattern of disbelieving nations throughout history who rejected the messengers sent to them by Allah. They not only denied the message but also plotted against the messengers, trying to seize them and silence their call to the truth. These nations engaged in false arguments and deception to discredit the clear proofs and signs brought by the messengers. As a result of their persistent disbelief and hostility, Allah inflicted upon them severe punishment, emphasizing the gravity of rejecting the truth and opposing the messengers of Allah. The verse serves as a warning to those who follow a similar path of denying the truth and plotting against the messengers, reminding them of the severe consequences that await those who persist in disbelief.
orig: كذبت قبلهم قوم نوح والأحزاب من بعدهم وهمت كل أمة برسولهم ليأخذوه وجادلوا بالباطل ليدحضوا به الحق فأخذتهم فكيف كان عقاب

translation: And thus the word of your Lord has come into effect upon those who disbelieved that they are companions of the Fire.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the fate of those who reject faith in Allah and His messages. It affirms that Allah's decree and judgment have been established against the disbelievers, sealing their destiny as the inhabitants of Hell in the afterlife. The "word" of Allah refers to His divine will, decree, and promise, which will inevitably come to pass. This verse serves as a stern warning to those who choose to disbelieve, highlighting the severe consequences of their actions and the ultimate justice of Allah.
orig: وكذلك حقت كلمت ربك على الذين كفروا أنهم أصحاب النار

translation: Those who carry the Throne and those around it exalt [Allah] with praise of their Lord and believe in Him and ask forgiveness for those who have believed, [saying], "Our Lord, You have encompassed all things in mercy and knowledge, so forgive those who have repented and followed Your way and protect them from the punishment of Hellfire."
interpretation: This verse speaks about the angels who carry the Throne of Allah and those who surround it. They are engaged in glorifying Allah, praising Him, and seeking forgiveness for the believers. The angels acknowledge Allah's infinite mercy and knowledge, which encompasses all things. They pray to Allah to forgive those who have repented sincerely and followed the path that He has ordained. Furthermore, they beseech Allah to save the believers from the torment of Hell. This verse highlights the importance of repentance, following the right path, and the vastness of Allah's mercy and knowledge.
orig: الذين يحملون العرش ومن حوله يسبحون بحمد ربهم ويؤمنون به ويستغفرون للذين آمنوا ربنا وسعت كل شيء رحمة وعلما فاغفر للذين تابوا واتبعوا سبيلك وقهم عذاب الجحيم

translation: Our Lord! And admit them to gardens of perpetual residence which You have promised them and whoever was righteous among their fathers, their spouses and their offspring. Indeed, it is You who is the Exalted in Might, the Wise.
interpretation: This verse is a supplication to Allah, asking Him to admit the righteous believers into Paradise (Jannah) which He has promised them. The supplication also includes a request for the admission of the righteous among their ancestors, spouses, and offspring. This highlights the importance of righteousness and its impact on one's family and loved ones. The verse concludes by acknowledging Allah's power and wisdom, emphasizing that He alone can fulfill this promise and reward the righteous in the hereafter. It also serves as a reminder for believers to strive for righteousness, not only for themselves but also for the sake of their families, with the hope of being united with them in Paradise.
orig: ربنا وأدخلهم جنات عدن التي وعدتهم ومن صلح من آبائهم وأزواجهم وذرياتهم إنك أنت العزيز الحكيم

translation: And protect them from the evil [consequences of their deeds]. And he whom You protect from evil consequences that Day - You will have given him mercy. And that is the great attainment.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of seeking Allah's protection from the evil consequences of one's actions, especially on the Day of Judgment. It suggests that being saved from the punishment of one's misdeeds on that crucial Day is a sign of Allah's immense mercy and a tremendous success. This interpretation highlights the significance of striving to avoid sinful acts and seeking forgiveness, as the ultimate goal is to attain Allah's mercy and be among those who are protected from the grievous consequences of their wrongdoings in the Hereafter. Achieving this protection is considered the greatest triumph one can aspire to.
orig: وقهم السيئات ومن تق السيئات يومئذ فقد رحمته وذلك هو الفوز العظيم

translation: Indeed, those who disbelieve are called to the hatred of Allah [which is] greater than your hatred of yourselves [now] when you are called to faith and you disbelieve [in it].
interpretation: This verse highlights the severity of disbelief in Allah. It suggests that the hatred Allah has towards those who reject faith is even greater than the disbelievers' own self-hatred when they are called to believe but refuse. This emphasizes the gravity of rejecting Allah's message and the consequences that come with it. The verse also implies that deep down, the disbelievers recognize the truth of the message, which is why they hate themselves for rejecting it when called to faith.
orig: إن الذين كفروا ينادون لمقت الله أكبر من مقتكم أنفسكم إذ تدعون إلى الإيمان فتكفرون

translation: They will say, "Our Lord, You made us lifeless twice and gave us life twice, and we have confessed our sins. So is there to an exit any way?"
interpretation: This verse refers to the two deaths and two lives that human beings experience according to Islamic belief. The first death is the state of non-existence before birth, and the second death is the physical death that every human being experiences. The first life is the life in this world, and the second life is the life in the Hereafter after resurrection. The people referred to in this verse acknowledge their sins and wrongdoings, and they ask if there is any way out of the punishment of the Hellfire. This highlights the importance of seeking forgiveness and repenting to Allah in this life before it is too late, as there will be no opportunity for redemption or escape from the consequences of one's actions in the Hereafter.
orig: قالوا ربنا أمتنا اثنتين وأحييتنا اثنتين فاعترفنا بذنوبنا فهل إلى خروج من سبيل

translation: That is because, when Allah was invoked alone, you disbelieved; but if others were associated with Him, you believed. So the judgement is with Allah, the Most High, the Grand.
interpretation: This verse highlights the fundamental error of polytheism. When people are called to worship Allah alone, they reject this message. However, if other deities are associated with Allah, they readily believe in them. This irrational behavior stems from their misguided beliefs and lack of understanding of the true nature of Allah. The verse emphasizes that the ultimate judgment and authority belong to Allah alone, who is the Most High and the Grand. It serves as a reminder that associating partners with Allah is a grave sin and that true faith lies in worshipping Him alone, without any partners or intermediaries.
orig: ذلكم بأنه إذا دعي الله وحده كفرتم وإن يشرك به تؤمنوا فالحكم لله العلي الكبير

translation: It is He who shows you His signs and sends down to you from the sky, provision. But none will remember except he who turns back [in repentance].
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that it is Allah alone who bestows upon humanity the signs and evidence of His existence, power, and mercy. He provides sustenance, both physical and spiritual, from the heavens. However, only those who sincerely turn to Him with a repentant heart and an open mind will truly benefit from these blessings and recognize the significance of His signs. It suggests that divine guidance and provision are available to all, but it is up to each individual to embrace them through reflection, gratitude, and turning to Allah in submission and repentance.
orig: هو الذي يريكم آياته وينزل لكم من السماء رزقا وما يتذكر إلا من ينيب

translation: So invoke Allah, [being] sincere to Him in religion, although the disbelievers dislike it.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of worshipping Allah with sincerity and devotion, even in the face of opposition from those who reject faith. It reminds believers to remain steadfast in their commitment to Allah and to call upon Him with pure intentions, regardless of the opinions or reactions of others. The verse highlights the central role of sincerity (ikhlas) in one's relationship with Allah, as it is the essence of true faith and the key to earning His pleasure and acceptance. It also implies that the disapproval or dislike of disbelievers should not deter or discourage believers from their devotion to Allah, as His approval is what ultimately matters.
orig: فادعوا الله مخلصين له الدين ولو كره الكافرون

translation: Exalted in Rank, Owner of the Throne; He places the inspiration of His command upon whom He wills from among His servants to warn of the Day of Meeting.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's absolute power and authority. He is exalted above all creation and is the master of the mighty Throne. Out of His wisdom and will, He selects certain individuals among His servants to receive divine revelation and inspiration, appointing them as messengers and prophets. The purpose of this revelation is to warn mankind about the inevitable Day of Judgment, when all souls will meet their Lord and be held accountable for their deeds in this world. It is a reminder for humans to be mindful of their actions and to prepare for that great Day by following the guidance sent through Allah's chosen messengers.
orig: رفيع الدرجات ذو العرش يلقي الروح من أمره على من يشاء من عباده لينذر يوم التلاق

translation: The Day they come forth, nothing concerning them will be concealed from Allah. To whom belongs [all] sovereignty this Day? To Allah, the One, the Prevailing.
interpretation: This verse refers to the Day of Judgment when all human beings will be resurrected and will stand before Allah, fully exposed, with nothing hidden from Him. On that day, it will be clear that all sovereignty, power, and authority belong to Allah alone, the One who subdues all and prevails over all things. It emphasizes Allah's absolute dominion and the fact that on the Day of Reckoning, everyone will realize and submit to His supreme authority, and all false claims of power will be rendered void. The verse underscores the importance of acknowledging Allah's sovereignty in this life before the arrival of that inevitable Day.
orig: يوم هم بارزون لا يخفى على الله منهم شيء لمن الملك اليوم لله الواحد القهار

translation: This Day every soul will be recompensed for what it has earned. No injustice today! Indeed, Allah is swift in account.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the concept of divine justice on the Day of Judgment. Each individual will be held accountable for their deeds and will be rewarded or punished accordingly. There will be no injustice or unfairness on that day, as Allah is swift in settling accounts. This serves as a reminder for believers to be mindful of their actions in this world, as they will have consequences in the hereafter. It also highlights Allah's attribute of being swift in reckoning, indicating that no deed, good or bad, will be overlooked or forgotten on the Day of Judgment.
orig: اليوم تجزى كل نفس بما كسبت لا ظلم اليوم إن الله سريع الحساب

translation: And warn them, [O Muhammad], of the Approaching Day, when hearts are at the throats, filled [with distress]. For the wrongdoers there will be no devoted friend and no intercessor [who is] obeyed.
interpretation: This verse is a reminder of the Day of Judgment, when people will be in a state of intense fear and anxiety, with their hearts feeling as if they are stuck in their throats due to the overwhelming distress. It emphasizes that on this day, the wrongdoers and sinners will have no close friend or intercessor who can plead on their behalf and be listened to by Allah. This highlights the importance of leading a righteous life and seeking forgiveness for one's sins before it is too late, as on the Day of Judgment, no one will be able to help the wrongdoers escape the consequences of their actions.
orig: وأنذرهم يوم الآزفة إذ القلوب لدى الحناجر كاظمين ما للظالمين من حميم ولا شفيع يطاع

translation: He knows the deceit of the eyes and what the breasts conceal.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the all-encompassing knowledge of Allah. He is aware of even the smallest and most hidden of things, such as the deceptive glances of the eyes and the secrets hidden within the hearts of people. It serves as a reminder that nothing can be concealed from Allah, and that He has knowledge of all things, including our innermost thoughts and intentions. This should inspire believers to be sincere in their faith and actions, knowing that Allah is always watching and aware of what is in their hearts.
orig: يعلم خائنة الأعين وما تخفي الصدور

translation: And Allah judges with truth, while those they invoke besides Him judge not with anything. Indeed, Allah - He is the Hearing, the Seeing.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah alone is the ultimate judge and that His judgment is always based on truth and justice. It contrasts Allah's perfect judgment with the inability of false deities to judge or make decisions. The verse also highlights two of Allah's attributes: He is the All-Hearing, aware of everything that is said, and the All-Seeing, aware of everything that happens. This interpretation underscores the importance of putting one's trust in Allah's judgment and not relying on false deities or worldly authorities who lack the wisdom and perfect attributes of Allah.
orig: والله يقضي بالحق والذين يدعون من دونه لا يقضون بشيء إن الله هو السميع البصير

translation: Have they not traveled through the land and observed how was the end of those before them? They were greater than them in power and in impression on the land, but Allah seized them for their sins, and they had not from Allah any protector.
interpretation: This verse serves as a reminder and warning to those who reject faith and persist in wrongdoing. It encourages people to reflect on the fate of past civilizations that were mightier and more advanced than them, yet were ultimately destroyed due to their sins and disobedience to Allah. The verse emphasizes that no matter how powerful or influential a person or society may be, they are not immune to the consequences of their actions and will face divine retribution if they do not mend their ways. It also highlights the idea that there is no protector or savior other than Allah, and that one cannot escape His judgment and punishment for their misdeeds.
orig: أولم يسيروا في الأرض فينظروا كيف كان عاقبة الذين كانوا من قبلهم كانوا هم أشد منهم قوة وآثارا في الأرض فأخذهم الله بذنوبهم وما كان لهم من الله من واق

translation: That was because their messengers were coming to them with clear proofs, but they disbelieved, so Allah seized them. Indeed, He is Powerful and severe in punishment.
interpretation: This verse indicates that the reason for the punishment and destruction of past nations was their rejection of the clear proofs and signs brought to them by their prophets. They chose to disbelieve despite the evidence, so Allah seized them with a mighty punishment. The verse emphasizes Allah's power and His severity in punishing those who reject the truth after it has been made clear to them. It serves as a warning to people not to follow the same path of denying the messages and signs sent by Allah through His messengers, as doing so will result in severe consequences.
orig: ذلك بأنهم كانت تأتيهم رسلهم بالبينات فكفروا فأخذهم الله إنه قوي شديد العقاب

translation: And indeed, We sent Moses with Our signs and a clear authority
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the divine mission of Prophet Moses, who was sent by Allah with clear signs and undeniable proofs of his prophethood. The "clear authority" mentioned in the verse refers to the compelling evidence and miracles that Moses was granted to support his message and establish his authority as a prophet. This interpretation highlights the importance of divine support for prophets in their mission to guide humanity and deliver Allah's message.
orig: ولقد أرسلنا موسى بآياتنا وسلطان مبين

translation: To Pharaoh, Haman, and Korah; but they said, "[He is] a magician and a liar."
interpretation: This verse refers to the disbelieving response of Pharaoh, Haman, and Korah when Allah sent Moses to them with clear signs and miracles. Instead of accepting the truth, they arrogantly rejected Moses, accusing him of being a lying magician who was only performing tricks to deceive them. This highlights the stubborn attitude of those in power who are often blinded by their own arrogance and fail to recognize the truth even when it is presented to them clearly. It serves as a warning to believers not to be like those who reject the signs of Allah due to their pride and disbelief.
orig: إلى فرعون وهامان وقارون فقالوا ساحر كذاب

translation: And when he brought them the truth from Us, they said, "Kill the sons of those who have believed with him and keep their women alive." But the plan of the disbelievers is not except in error.
interpretation: This verse highlights the cruelty and desperation of the disbelievers when faced with the truth. Instead of accepting the message brought to them, they resort to violence and oppression, targeting the families of the believers. They seek to kill the sons and enslave the women, hoping to weaken the resolve of the faithful. However, their evil plots are ultimately futile and misguided, as they are destined to fail in the face of divine truth. The verse serves as a reminder that those who oppose the truth will always be in a state of loss and misguidance, while the believers remain steadfast in their faith, even in the face of persecution.
orig: فلما جاءهم بالحق من عندنا قالوا اقتلوا أبناء الذين آمنوا معه واستحيوا نساءهم وما كيد الكافرين إلا في ضلال

translation: And Pharaoh said, "Let me kill Moses and let him call upon his Lord. Indeed, I fear that he will change your religion or that he will cause corruption in the land."
interpretation: This verse shows the arrogance and tyranny of Pharaoh, who sees Moses as a threat to his power and the established religion of his people. Pharaoh fears that Moses will lead the people away from their current beliefs and practices, or cause rebellion and chaos in the land. It reflects the common tactic of oppressive rulers to paint reformers and prophets as dangerous agitators who will disrupt society, in order to justify their persecution and maintain their own authority. The verse also highlights Moses' reliance on God in the face of danger, as Pharaoh mockingly suggests that Moses can call upon his Lord for help, implying the powerlessness of God against Pharaoh's might.
orig: وقال فرعون ذروني أقتل موسى وليدع ربه إني أخاف أن يبدل دينكم أو أن يظهر في الأرض الفساد

translation: And Moses said, "Indeed, I have sought refuge in my Lord and your Lord from every arrogant one who does not believe in the Day of Account."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of humility and belief in the Day of Judgment. Moses seeks protection from those who are arrogant and do not believe in being held accountable for their actions on the Day of Reckoning. It serves as a reminder that ultimate justice will be served by Allah, and that one should strive to be humble and mindful of their deeds, knowing that they will be answerable for them in the Hereafter. The verse also highlights the significance of having faith in the existence of the Day of Judgment, which is a fundamental aspect of Islamic belief.
orig: وقال موسى إني عذت بربي وربكم من كل متكبر لا يؤمن بيوم الحساب

translation: And a believing man from the family of Pharaoh who concealed his faith said, "Do you kill a man [merely] because he says, 'My Lord is Allah' while he has brought you clear proofs from your Lord? And if he should be lying, then upon him is [the consequence of] his lie; but if he should be truthful, there will strike you some of what he promises you. Indeed, Allah does not guide one who is a transgressor and a liar.
interpretation: This verse highlights the courage and wisdom of a believer from Pharaoh's own family, who spoke out against the injustice of persecuting someone solely for their faith in Allah. He argues that if the man is lying, then he will bear the consequences of his own falsehood, but if he is truthful, then the people will suffer the punishment he warns them about. The believer emphasizes that Allah does not guide those who are transgressors and liars, implying that Pharaoh and his supporters are the ones in the wrong for their oppression and disbelief, not the man they seek to punish for his faith.
orig: وقال رجل مؤمن من آل فرعون يكتم إيمانه أتقتلون رجلا أن يقول ربي الله وقد جاءكم بالبينات من ربكم وإن يك كاذبا فعليه كذبه وإن يك صادقا يصبكم بعض الذي يعدكم إن الله لا يهدي من هو مسرف كذاب

translation: O my people, sovereignty is yours today, [your being] dominant in the land. But who would protect us from the punishment of Allah if it came to us?" Pharaoh said, "I do not show you except what I see, and I do not guide you except to the way of right conduct."
interpretation: This verse highlights the arrogance and delusion of Pharaoh, who believes that his worldly power and dominance can protect him and his people from Allah's punishment. Despite his claims of guiding his people to the right path, his words reveal his own limited understanding and lack of true guidance. The verse serves as a reminder that no matter how powerful or influential one may seem in this world, ultimately, it is only Allah who can provide protection and guidance to the straight path. It also emphasizes the importance of seeking guidance from divine sources rather than relying solely on human judgment, which can be flawed and misguided.
orig: يا قوم لكم الملك اليوم ظاهرين في الأرض فمن ينصرنا من بأس الله إن جاءنا قال فرعون ما أريكم إلا ما أرى وما أهديكم إلا سبيل الرشاد

translation: And the believer said, "O my people, indeed I fear for you [a fate] like the day of the companies -
interpretation: This verse is a warning from a believer to his people, expressing his fear that they may face a fate similar to that of previous nations who rejected God's messengers. The "day of the companies" refers to the destruction that befell those past nations who opposed the prophets sent to them. The believer is urging his people to heed the message and avoid the same disastrous consequences. This highlights the importance of learning from history and not repeating the mistakes of those who came before. It also emphasizes the role of sincere advisors within a community who strive to guide others to the right path out of genuine concern for their well-being in this life and the hereafter.
orig: وقال الذي آمن يا قوم إني أخاف عليكم مثل يوم الأحزاب

translation: Like the way of the people of Noah and 'Aad and Thamud and those after them. And Allah does not intend injustice to [His] servants.
interpretation: This verse is a reminder that the fate of those who reject Allah's message and persist in wrongdoing will be similar to that of previous nations, such as the people of Noah, 'Aad, and Thamud. These ancient communities were destroyed due to their disobedience and defiance of Allah's guidance. The verse emphasizes that Allah does not wish to be unjust to His servants; rather, it is their own actions and choices that lead to their downfall. This serves as a warning to those who may be following a similar path of disbelief and transgression, urging them to reflect upon the consequences of their actions and to turn back to Allah in repentance before it is too late.
orig: مثل دأب قوم نوح وعاد وثمود والذين من بعدهم وما الله يريد ظلما للعباد

translation: And O my people, indeed I fear for you the Day of Calling Out
interpretation: In this verse, the prophet is warning his people about the Day of Judgment, also known as the Day of Calling Out. It is called such because on that day, people will call out to each other in distress and regret, but it will be of no benefit. The prophet is expressing his deep concern and fear for his people, that if they do not heed his warning and change their ways, they will face a severe reckoning on that terrible Day. This verse serves as a reminder for all believers to be mindful of their actions in this life, and to strive for righteousness so that they may be saved from the punishment of the Hereafter.
orig: ويا قوم إني أخاف عليكم يوم التناد

translation: The Day you will turn your backs fleeing; there is not for you from Allah any protector. And whoever Allah leaves astray - there is not for him any guide.
interpretation: This verse is referring to the Day of Judgment, when people will flee in terror, realizing that there is no escape from Allah's judgment. It emphasizes that on that day, no one can protect or save a person from Allah's punishment. Furthermore, it highlights that those whom Allah has left to stray from the right path in this world will have no guide to lead them to salvation in the Hereafter. It serves as a reminder of the consequences of turning away from Allah's guidance in this life.
orig: يوم تولون مدبرين ما لكم من الله من عاصم ومن يضلل الله فما له من هاد

translation: And Joseph had already come to you before with clear proofs, but you remained in doubt about what he brought to you, until when he died, you said, "Never will Allah send a messenger after him." Thus does Allah leave astray he who is a transgressor and skeptic.
interpretation: This verse highlights the stubborn disbelief of those who rejected the prophets despite clear evidence. Even after Joseph came with clear proofs, they remained doubtful until his death, claiming that no messenger would come after him. This shows their arrogance and skepticism. As a result, Allah leaves such transgressors and doubters astray, withholding His guidance from those who persistently reject the truth brought by His messengers. It emphasizes that doubting the clear signs of Allah and His messengers leads people away from the straight path.
orig: ولقد جاءكم يوسف من قبل بالبينات فما زلتم في شك مما جاءكم به حتى إذا هلك قلتم لن يبعث الله من بعده رسولا كذلك يضل الله من هو مسرف مرتاب

translation: Those who dispute concerning the signs of Allah without an authority having come to them - great is hatred [of them] in the sight of Allah and in the sight of those who have believed. Thus does Allah seal over every heart [belonging to] an arrogant tyrant.
interpretation: This verse is a strong condemnation of those who argue against the clear signs and revelations of Allah without any valid authority or proof. Such argumentative behavior is detestable in the sight of Allah and the believers. The verse emphasizes that Allah seals the hearts of the arrogant and tyrannical individuals who engage in such futile disputes, making them unable to accept the truth. It serves as a warning against arrogance and the rejection of divine guidance, highlighting the severe spiritual consequences of such actions.
orig: الذين يجادلون في آيات الله بغير سلطان أتاهم كبر مقتا عند الله وعند الذين آمنوا كذلك يطبع الله على كل قلب متكبر جبار

translation: And Pharaoh said, "O Haman, construct for me a tower that I might reach the ways -
interpretation: This verse shows the arrogance and pride of Pharaoh, who believed himself to be a god and wanted to build a tower to reach the heavens and challenge the authority of the true God. It demonstrates how those in power can become deluded by their own greatness and forget their place as mere human beings under the sovereignty of Allah. The verse serves as a warning against such hubris and a reminder to remain humble before the Almighty.
orig: وقال فرعون يا هامان ابن لي صرحا لعلي أبلغ الأسباب

translation: The means of access to the heavens, so that I may look at the God of Moses; but indeed, I think he is a liar." And thus was made attractive to Pharaoh the evil of his deed, and he was averted from the [right] way. And the plan of Pharaoh was not except in ruin.
interpretation: This verse highlights the arrogance and disbelief of Pharaoh, who sought to challenge the authority of God and His messenger, Moses. Pharaoh's demand to ascend to the heavens and look upon the God of Moses reflects his egotistical belief that he himself was a divine being. His accusation that Moses was a liar further emphasizes his rejection of the truth. The verse also points out that Pharaoh's evil actions and his turning away from the right path were made attractive to him, suggesting that his own pride and stubbornness blinded him to the reality of his situation. Ultimately, the verse concludes by stating that Pharaoh's schemes and plans would only lead to his own destruction and ruin, serving as a warning to those who would follow in his footsteps and reject the message of God.
orig: أسباب السماوات فأطلع إلى إله موسى وإني لأظنه كاذبا وكذلك زين لفرعون سوء عمله وصد عن السبيل وما كيد فرعون إلا في تباب

translation: And the one who believed said, "O my people, follow me; I will guide you to the way of right conduct."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of following the guidance of those who are righteous and believe in Allah. The believer invites his people to follow him on the path of truth and righteousness, which ultimately leads to success in this life and the hereafter. It highlights the role of a faithful individual in guiding others towards the right path and encourages people to seek and follow the advice of those who have strong faith and knowledge.
orig: وقال الذي آمن يا قوم اتبعون أهدكم سبيل الرشاد

translation: O my people, this worldly life is only [temporary] enjoyment, and indeed, the Hereafter - that is the home of [permanent] settlement.
interpretation: This verse reminds us that the life of this world is fleeting and temporary, filled with distractions and pleasures that will ultimately fade away. In contrast, the afterlife is our true eternal home where we will find permanent settlement and recompense for our deeds. It encourages believers to focus on the Hereafter rather than being consumed by the ephemeral nature of worldly enjoyments, as investing in one's spiritual well-being and righteousness will lead to everlasting rewards in the life to come. The verse emphasizes the importance of maintaining a proper perspective regarding the transient nature of this world compared to the eternal significance of the Hereafter.
orig: يا قوم إنما هذه الحياة الدنيا متاع وإن الآخرة هي دار القرار

translation: Whoever does an evil deed will not be recompensed except by the like thereof; but whoever does righteousness, whether male or female, while he is a believer - those will enter Paradise, being given provision therein without account.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the justice and mercy of Allah. Those who commit evil deeds will only be punished to the extent of their wrongdoing, without any excess. However, those who do good deeds, whether male or female, while believing in Allah and His message, will be rewarded with Paradise, where they will be provided for abundantly without any limit or account. This highlights the immense generosity and grace of Allah towards His believing servants, and encourages people to strive for righteousness and faith, regardless of their gender.
orig: من عمل سيئة فلا يجزى إلا مثلها ومن عمل صالحا من ذكر أو أنثى وهو مؤمن فأولئك يدخلون الجنة يرزقون فيها بغير حساب

translation: And O my people! How is it that I call you to salvation while you call me to the Fire?
interpretation: The verse highlights the contrast between the righteous and the misguided. The speaker is perplexed by the fact that while he invites his people towards salvation and the path of righteousness, they instead beckon him towards the Fire, symbolizing sin, disbelief, and ultimately, Hell. It emphasizes the importance of heeding the call to faith and virtue, rather than succumbing to the temptations and influences that lead one astray from the straight path. The verse also underscores the responsibility of those who possess knowledge and wisdom to guide others towards the truth, even in the face of opposition and resistance.
orig: ويا قوم ما لي أدعوكم إلى النجاة وتدعونني إلى النار

translation: You invite me to disbelieve in Allah and associate with Him that of which I have no knowledge, and I invite you to the Exalted in Might, the Perpetual Forgiver.
interpretation: This verse highlights the contrast between the invitation to disbelief and polytheism, and the invitation to believe in Allah, the Almighty and Oft-Forgiving. It emphasizes that associating partners with Allah is done without knowledge or proof, while belief in Allah's power and forgiveness is the path of wisdom and guidance. The verse encourages the listener to turn away from false deities and instead turn towards the One true God who is capable of forgiving all sins and transgressions.
orig: تدعونني لأكفر بالله وأشرك به ما ليس لي به علم وأنا أدعوكم إلى العزيز الغفار

translation: There is no doubt that what you invite me to has no claim in this world or in the Hereafter, and that our return is to Allah, and that the transgressors are the companions of the Fire.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the futility of following false deities or ideologies that have no basis in truth. It reminds us that ultimately, we will all return to Allah and be held accountable for our actions. Those who transgress the boundaries set by Allah and indulge in excesses will be the inhabitants of the Fire in the Hereafter. The verse urges us to be mindful of our choices and to align ourselves with the path of righteousness, as defined by Allah's guidance, in order to attain success in both this world and the next.
orig: لا جرم أنما تدعونني إليه ليس له دعوة في الدنيا ولا في الآخرة وأن مردنا إلى الله وأن المسرفين هم أصحاب النار

translation: And you will remember what I [now] say to you, and I entrust my affair to Allah. Indeed, Allah is Seeing of [His] servants.
interpretation: This verse is a reminder that the truth will eventually become clear, and that those who reject it will come to realize their mistake. It encourages the believer to have trust in Allah and to leave their affairs in His hands, knowing that He is aware of everything that His servants do. It is a call to patience and perseverance in the face of opposition and difficulty, with the assurance that Allah will ultimately support and vindicate those who are sincere in their faith.
orig: فستذكرون ما أقول لكم وأفوض أمري إلى الله إن الله بصير بالعباد

translation: So Allah protected him from the evils they plotted, and the people of Pharaoh were enveloped by the worst of punishment.
interpretation: This verse highlights the power and justice of Allah. It shows that Allah protects His righteous servants from the plots and schemes of the wrongdoers, while the evildoers themselves are ultimately afflicted with severe punishment for their misdeeds. The verse specifically mentions the people of Pharaoh, who were known for their oppression, arrogance, and rejection of Allah's messages. Despite their power and influence, they could not escape Allah's retribution. This serves as a reminder that no matter how mighty or cunning the enemies of truth may seem, Allah's will always prevails, and those who oppose Him will face the consequences of their actions in this world and the Hereafter.
orig: فوقاه الله سيئات ما مكروا وحاق بآل فرعون سوء العذاب

translation: The Fire, they are exposed to it morning and evening. And the Day the Hour appears [it will be said], "Make the people of Pharaoh enter the severest punishment."
interpretation: This verse speaks about the punishment that awaits the people of Pharaoh in the Hereafter. They will be exposed to the Fire of Hell every morning and evening, indicating the constancy and severity of their torment. On the Day of Judgment, when the final Hour arrives, they will be commanded to enter the severest form of punishment due to their arrogance, tyranny, and rejection of Allah's signs and messengers during their worldly life. This interpretation highlights the gravity of their sins and the justice of Allah in recompensing evildoers with the most severe consequences in the eternal life to come.
orig: النار يعرضون عليها غدوا وعشيا ويوم تقوم الساعة أدخلوا آل فرعون أشد العذاب

translation: And when they will dispute in the Fire, and the weak will say to those who had been arrogant, "Indeed, we were [only] your followers, so will you relieve us of a share of the Fire?"
interpretation: This verse speaks about the Day of Judgment when the people will be disputing in Hell. The weak, who followed the arrogant leaders in this world, will plead to those leaders to relieve them of a portion of the punishment of the Fire. They will argue that they were only following the lead of the arrogant ones, so they should bear some responsibility and share in the punishment. However, this plea will be of no avail, as each soul will be held accountable for its own deeds. The leaders will not be able to help their followers on that Day, nor will anyone be able to help another. This highlights the individual responsibility of each person and the justice of Allah in holding everyone accountable for their own actions, regardless of their status or position in this worldly life.
orig: وإذ يتحاجون في النار فيقول الضعفاء للذين استكبروا إنا كنا لكم تبعا فهل أنتم مغنون عنا نصيبا من النار

translation: Those who were arrogant said, "Indeed, all of us are in it. Indeed, Allah has judged between the servants."
interpretation: This verse points to the realization of the arrogant disbelievers in the Hereafter that their arrogance and rejection of faith was futile. When they are thrown into the Hellfire, they will finally acknowledge that Allah's judgment is just and that no one can escape His decree. It emphasizes the absolute authority and justice of Allah in deciding the fate of His servants based on their deeds and beliefs in this world. The arrogant will be humbled, realizing too late the error of their ways, while the righteous believers will be vindicated and rewarded for their faith and good deeds.
orig: قال الذين استكبروا إنا كل فيها إن الله قد حكم بين العباد

translation: And those in the Fire will say to the keepers of Hell, "Pray to your Lord to lighten for us a day from the punishment."
interpretation: This verse portrays the desperation and anguish of those condemned to the Fire of Hell. In their torment, they plead with the guardians of Hell to intercede on their behalf, begging for even a single day's respite from the unrelenting punishment. This highlights the severity and eternality of the consequences faced by those who reject God's guidance in this life. The verse serves as a stark warning to humanity, urging them to follow the righteous path to avoid such a terrible fate in the Hereafter. It also emphasizes the absolute justice of God, as even the pleas of the condemned will not sway His decree once the Day of Judgment has passed.
orig: وقال الذين في النار لخزنة جهنم ادعوا ربكم يخفف عنا يوما من العذاب

translation: They will say, "Did there not come to you your messengers with clear proofs?" They will say, "Yes." They will reply, "Then supplicate [yourselves], but the supplication of the disbelievers is not except in error."
interpretation: This verse highlights the fate of the disbelievers on the Day of Judgment. When confronted with the reality of their actions, they will acknowledge that messengers had indeed come to them with clear proofs and guidance from Allah. However, despite this admission, they will be told to supplicate and call upon Allah themselves, knowing that their prayers will be in vain and will not be answered. This emphasizes the idea that once the Day of Judgment arrives, it will be too late for the disbelievers to repent or seek forgiveness, as they had ample opportunities to do so during their worldly life but chose to reject the truth. The verse serves as a reminder for individuals to embrace faith and righteousness before it is too late.
orig: قالوا أولم تك تأتيكم رسلكم بالبينات قالوا بلى قالوا فادعوا وما دعاء الكافرين إلا في ضلال

translation: Indeed, We will support Our messengers and those who believe during the life of this world and on the Day when the witnesses will stand -
interpretation: This verse is a promise from Allah that He will grant victory and support to His messengers and the believers, not only in this worldly life but also on the Day of Judgment when witnesses will testify. It emphasizes the unwavering commitment of Allah to aid those who are on the path of truth and righteousness, giving them strength and assurance in the face of adversities and challenges. The verse instills hope and confidence in the hearts of the believers, knowing that they have the ultimate support and backing of their Lord, both in this temporary world and in the eternal Hereafter when all deeds will be accounted for.
orig: إنا لننصر رسلنا والذين آمنوا في الحياة الدنيا ويوم يقوم الأشهاد

translation: The Day when their excuse will not benefit the wrongdoers, and they will have the curse, and they will have the worst home.
interpretation: This verse speaks about the Day of Judgment, when the excuses and justifications of the wrongdoers and oppressors will be of no benefit to them. They will face the curse of Allah and be condemned to the worst abode, which is Hell. It serves as a warning to those who commit injustice and oppression in this world, reminding them that they will be held accountable for their deeds and will face severe consequences in the Hereafter if they do not repent and mend their ways.
orig: يوم لا ينفع الظالمين معذرتهم ولهم اللعنة ولهم سوء الدار

translation: And We had certainly given Moses the guidance and caused the Children of Israel to inherit the Scripture
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the special status and favor that God bestowed upon the Children of Israel. God provided them with divine guidance through the prophet Moses, who was given the Torah. The scripture was then passed down as an inheritance to subsequent generations of Israelites. This inheritance of sacred knowledge and law was meant to guide them on the right path and help them maintain their covenant with God. The verse serves as a reminder of the spiritual legacy and responsibility entrusted to the Israelites.
orig: ولقد آتينا موسى الهدى وأورثنا بني إسرائيل الكتاب

translation: A guidance and a reminder for people of understanding.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the Qur'an serves as a guide and a reminder for those who possess wisdom, insight, and the ability to reflect deeply upon its teachings. "People of understanding" refers to individuals who use their intellect to contemplate the signs of Allah and the profound meanings within the Qur'anic verses. They are the ones who can truly benefit from the guidance and reminders contained in the Qur'an, as they actively seek to understand and apply its teachings in their lives. The verse suggests that the Qur'an is not merely a book to be recited, but a source of guidance and enlightenment for those who approach it with an open heart and a thoughtful mind.
orig: هدى وذكرى لأولي الألباب

translation: So be patient, [O Muhammad]. Indeed, the promise of Allah is truth. And ask forgiveness for your sin and exalt [Allah] with praise of your Lord in the evening and the morning.
interpretation: This verse is a reminder to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and all believers to remain patient and steadfast in the face of adversity and challenges, knowing that Allah's promise of victory and success is true and will come to pass. It also emphasizes the importance of seeking forgiveness for one's sins and constantly praising and glorifying Allah, particularly in the evening and morning, as a means of maintaining a strong connection with Him and attaining inner peace and tranquility. The verse underscores the significance of patience, repentance, and devotion in the life of a believer.
orig: فاصبر إن وعد الله حق واستغفر لذنبك وسبح بحمد ربك بالعشي والإبكار

translation: Indeed, those who dispute concerning the signs of Allah without an authority having come to them - there is not within their breasts except pride, [the extent of] which they cannot reach. So seek refuge in Allah. Indeed, it is He who is the Hearing, the Seeing.
interpretation: This verse is addressing those who argue against the clear signs and proofs of Allah without any valid authority or evidence to support their claims. Their rejection of the truth stems from arrogance and pride within their hearts, which prevents them from accepting the message. However, their pride is futile and will not help them attain their goals or prevail over the truth. The believer is advised to seek protection in Allah from such arrogant people and their false arguments, trusting that Allah is All-Hearing and All-Seeing, fully aware of their intentions and actions. Ultimately, the truth will prevail, and the prideful disbelievers will face the consequences of their rejection.
orig: إن الذين يجادلون في آيات الله بغير سلطان أتاهم إن في صدورهم إلا كبر ما هم ببالغيه فاستعذ بالله إنه هو السميع البصير

translation: The creation of the heavens and the earth is greater than the creation of mankind, but most of mankind do not know.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the immense power and wisdom of Allah in creating the vast universe, which is far more complex and magnificent than the creation of human beings. It suggests that most people fail to recognize or appreciate the true scale and significance of Allah's creation. The verse implies that if humans were to reflect deeply on the wonders of the heavens and the earth, they would better understand the greatness of their Creator and develop a stronger faith and reverence for Him. It also serves as a reminder of human limitations in knowledge and understanding compared to the infinite wisdom of Allah.
orig: لخلق السماوات والأرض أكبر من خلق الناس ولكن أكثر الناس لا يعلمون

translation: Not equal are the blind and the seeing, nor are those who believe and do righteous deeds and the evildoer. Little do you remember.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the stark contrast between those who have faith and do good deeds, and those who reject the truth and engage in wrongdoing. It compares the believers to those who have sight, and the disbelievers to those who are blind. The analogy suggests that just as a blind person cannot perceive the world around them, those who lack faith are unable to discern the truth and the right path. The verse also implies that the believers who do righteous deeds will be rewarded, while the evildoers will face consequences for their actions. However, it notes that people often fail to reflect on this reality and take heed of the warning.
orig: وما يستوي الأعمى والبصير والذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات ولا المسيء قليلا ما تتذكرون

translation: Indeed, the Hour is coming - no doubt about it - but most of the people do not believe.
interpretation: This verse is a reminder that the Day of Judgment, or the "Hour", is an inevitable reality that will come to pass, even though most people do not have faith in its occurrence. It emphasizes the certainty of the Hour and implies that disbelief in it does not negate its reality. The verse serves as a warning to humanity that they should prepare for the Day of Judgment by having faith and doing righteous deeds, as it is a matter of when, not if, it will happen. It also highlights the human tendency to deny or disregard matters of the unseen, such as the afterlife, despite the Qur'an's clear assertions about their certainty.
orig: إن الساعة لآتية لا ريب فيها ولكن أكثر الناس لا يؤمنون

translation: And your Lord says, "Call upon Me; I will respond to you." Indeed, those who disdain My worship will enter Hell [rendered] contemptible.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of supplicating to Allah and seeking His help and guidance. It is a reminder that Allah is always ready to answer the prayers of His servants who call upon Him with sincerity and humility. On the other hand, those who are too proud to worship Allah and submit to His will, will be humiliated and disgraced when they enter Hell as a punishment for their arrogance and disobedience. This verse encourages believers to constantly turn to Allah in prayer and to never let their ego or pride prevent them from worshipping Him and seeking His mercy and forgiveness.
orig: وقال ربكم ادعوني أستجب لكم إن الذين يستكبرون عن عبادتي سيدخلون جهنم داخرين

translation: It is Allah who made for you the night that you may rest therein and the day giving sight. Indeed, Allah is full of bounty to the people, but most of the people are not grateful.
interpretation: This verse highlights the immense blessings and mercy that Allah has bestowed upon humanity. He has created the night as a time for rest and tranquility, allowing people to recharge and find peace. On the other hand, He has made the day bright and full of light, enabling people to see clearly and go about their daily activities. These alternating periods of night and day are a manifestation of Allah's boundless grace and generosity towards His creation. However, despite the abundance of His favors, most people fail to acknowledge and appreciate them. They take these blessings for granted and do not express their gratitude to Allah. This lack of thankfulness is a reminder for us to constantly reflect upon the countless bounties in our lives and to turn to Allah in sincere appreciation and worship.
orig: الله الذي جعل لكم الليل لتسكنوا فيه والنهار مبصرا إن الله لذو فضل على الناس ولكن أكثر الناس لا يشكرون

translation: That is Allah, your Lord, Creator of all things; there is no deity except Him, so how are you deluded?
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the fundamental concept of Tawheed (Islamic monotheism) and the Oneness of Allah. It affirms that Allah is the sole Creator of everything in existence and that there is no true deity worthy of worship except Him. The verse then questions how people can be misled or deceived into worshipping false deities or attributing partners to Allah despite this clear truth. It serves as a reminder for believers to stay steadfast in their faith and to reject any form of polytheism or idolatry, as it contradicts the very essence of Islam's monotheistic message.
orig: ذلكم الله ربكم خالق كل شيء لا إله إلا هو فأنى تؤفكون

translation: Thus were deluded those who were wont to reject the signs of Allah.
interpretation: This verse is referring to those who persistently denied and rejected the clear signs and proofs of Allah's existence and power that were shown to them. As a result of their stubborn disbelief, Allah allowed them to be misled and deceived by falsehood, turning away from the truth. It illustrates that those who knowingly reject divine guidance and persist in disbelief will ultimately be led further astray from the straight path, as a consequence of their own choices. The verse serves as a warning that rejecting faith in Allah and His signs leads one to misguidance and loss in this world and the Hereafter.
orig: كذلك يؤفك الذين كانوا بآيات الله يجحدون

translation: It is Allah who made for you the earth a place of settlement and the sky a ceiling and formed you and perfected your forms and provided you with good things. That is Allah, your Lord; then blessed is Allah, Lord of the worlds.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's power, creativity and generosity towards mankind. It reminds us that Allah has provided us with all the necessary means for our survival and well-being on this earth - a stable place to live, a protective sky above us, our own intricate forms and features, and numerous good provisions to sustain us. Contemplating over these immense blessings and favors should increase us in gratitude towards our Lord and make us recognize His greatness. The verse ends by exalting Allah, affirming that abundant blessings and perfection belong to Him alone, as He is the Lord and Cherisher of all the worlds. It inspires a sense of awe at Allah's power and benevolence.
orig: الله الذي جعل لكم الأرض قرارا والسماء بناء وصوركم فأحسن صوركم ورزقكم من الطيبات ذلكم الله ربكم فتبارك الله رب العالمين

translation: He is the Ever-Living; there is no deity except Him, so call upon Him, [being] sincere to Him in religion. [All] praise is [due] to Allah, Lord of the worlds.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the Oneness and Uniqueness of Allah, the Ever-Living, the Eternal. It calls upon believers to worship Him alone with sincere devotion, turning to Him in all matters of life. It also reminds us that all praise and gratitude belong to Allah, the Lord and Sustainer of all the worlds. This highlights the importance of sincerity in faith and the recognition of Allah's supreme lordship over the entire universe.
orig: هو الحي لا إله إلا هو فادعوه مخلصين له الدين الحمد لله رب العالمين

translation: Say, "Indeed, I have been forbidden to worship those you invoke besides Allah once the clear proofs have come to me from my Lord, and I have been commanded to submit to the Lord of the worlds."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of worshipping Allah alone and rejecting the worship of any other beings or entities. It highlights that once a person receives clear guidance and evidence from Allah, they are obligated to submit completely to Him and abandon the worship of false deities. The verse also underscores the concept of Tawheed (Islamic monotheism) and the necessity of dedicating all acts of worship solely to the Creator and Sustainer of the universe, Allah. It serves as a reminder for believers to remain steadfast in their faith and not be swayed by the misguided practices or beliefs of others who may invoke or worship entities other than Allah.
orig: قل إني نهيت أن أعبد الذين تدعون من دون الله لما جاءني البينات من ربي وأمرت أن أسلم لرب العالمين

translation: It is He who created you from dust, then from a sperm-drop, then from a clinging clot; then He brings you out as a child; then [He develops you] that you reach your [time of] maturity, then [further] that you become elders. And among you is he who is taken in death before [that], so that you reach a specified term; and perhaps you will use reason.
interpretation: This verse highlights the various stages of human development, from the humble beginnings of dust and a drop of fluid, to the formation of a clinging clot, and then the emergence of a child. It emphasizes the power and wisdom of Allah in guiding humans through these stages until they reach maturity and old age. The verse also acknowledges that death can occur at any stage of life, reminding us of the fragility of our existence and the importance of using our intellect to reflect on the purpose of our lives and our ultimate return to our Creator.
orig: هو الذي خلقكم من تراب ثم من نطفة ثم من علقة ثم يخرجكم طفلا ثم لتبلغوا أشدكم ثم لتكونوا شيوخا ومنكم من يتوفى من قبل ولتبلغوا أجلا مسمى ولعلكم تعقلون

translation: It is He who gives life and causes death. And when He decrees a matter, He only says to it, "Be," and it is.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute power and sovereignty of Allah over all creation. He alone has the power to give life and cause death, and His command is sufficient to bring anything into existence. When He decrees a matter, it comes to pass without delay or difficulty. This highlights the importance of submitting to Allah's will and recognizing His supreme authority over all aspects of life and death. It also serves as a reminder that everything in the universe exists and occurs by His command, and that nothing can happen without His permission.
orig: هو الذي يحيي ويميت فإذا قضى أمرا فإنما يقول له كن فيكون

translation: Have you not considered those who dispute concerning the signs of Allah - how are they averted?
