interpretation: This verse is addressing the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him), drawing his attention to those who argue against and reject the clear signs and proofs of Allah's existence, power, and revelation. The rhetorical question "Have you not considered" is meant to emphasize the strange and irrational behavior of these individuals who, despite being presented with clear evidence, turn away from the truth. The verse implies that their rejection is not based on sound reasoning or sincere seeking of the truth but rather on their own desires, arrogance, or blind following of their forefathers' traditions. It also serves as a warning to the believers not to be like those who dispute Allah's signs and are thus led astray from the straight path.
orig: ألم تر إلى الذين يجادلون في آيات الله أنى يصرفون

translation: Those who denied the Book and that with which We sent Our messengers - they are going to know.
interpretation: This verse serves as a stern warning to those who reject the divine message and the prophets who convey it. It implies that those who deny the truth will eventually face the consequences of their disbelief and will come to realize their grave error. The verse suggests that the deniers will be confronted with the reality of their actions in the afterlife, where they will face the judgment of Allah. It emphasizes the importance of faith and the acceptance of the divine message, as those who reject it will ultimately face the repercussions of their choice.
orig: الذين كذبوا بالكتاب وبما أرسلنا به رسلنا فسوف يعلمون

translation: When the shackles are around their necks and the chains; they will be dragged
interpretation: This verse is describing the fate of the disbelievers and sinners in the Hereafter. The shackles and chains mentioned symbolize the punishment and humiliation they will face as a consequence of their actions and disbelief in this world. The verse paints a vivid and terrifying picture of them being dragged by these shackles and chains, emphasizing the severity and inescapability of the torment that awaits them. It serves as a powerful warning and reminder for people to mend their ways, have faith, and do righteous deeds to avoid such a dreadful outcome in the afterlife.
orig: إذ الأغلال في أعناقهم والسلاسل يسحبون

translation: In the Blazing Fire, then they will be burned.
interpretation: This verse is referring to the punishment that awaits the disbelievers and wrongdoers in the Hereafter. They will be thrown into the scorching depths of the Blazing Fire, where they will suffer the agony of being burned. This verse serves as a severe warning to those who reject faith and persist in evil deeds, highlighting the gravity of the consequences they will face in the afterlife. It is a reminder for individuals to be mindful of their actions and to strive for righteousness in this world to avoid such a terrible fate.
orig: في الحميم ثم في النار يسجرون

translation: Then it will be said to them, "Where are those you used to associate [with Him in worship]?"
interpretation: This verse is referring to the Day of Judgment when the disbelievers will be questioned about the false gods they used to worship alongside Allah. It is a rhetorical question meant to highlight the futility and falsehood of their idolatry. On that day, their false gods will be unable to help them or respond on their behalf, exposing the disbelievers' error in worshipping them. The verse emphasizes that only Allah is worthy of worship and that associating partners with Him is a grave sin that will be punished in the Hereafter.
orig: ثم قيل لهم أين ما كنتم تشركون

translation: Other than Allah they said, "They have departed from us," rather, we did not invoke anything before. Thus does Allah put astray the disbelievers.
interpretation: This verse highlights the fate of those who worship false deities instead of Allah. On the Day of Judgment, these false gods will abandon their worshippers, revealing that they were never truly worthy of worship. The idolaters will realize that their devotion was misplaced and that their deities were powerless. This realization comes too late, as Allah has already decreed that those who reject Him and follow false gods will be led astray and face the consequences of their disbelief. The verse emphasizes the importance of worshipping Allah alone and the futility of placing one's faith in anything or anyone else.
orig: من دون الله قالوا ضلوا عنا بل لم نكن ندعو من قبل شيئا كذلك يضل الله الكافرين

translation: That is because you used to exult upon the earth without right and because you used to behave insolently.
interpretation: This verse is a stern warning and admonition to those who are arrogant and exult in their worldly possessions and status without any regard for truth, justice or humility before Allah. It points to the fact that such people are deluded by their own hubris and fail to recognize that everything they have is from Allah alone. Their insolent and ungrateful behavior will lead to severe consequences in the Hereafter when they will be recompensed for their deeds. The verse reminds us to be humble, grateful and mindful of Allah at all times instead of being intoxicated by ephemeral worldly pleasures and power.
orig: ذلكم بما كنتم تفرحون في الأرض بغير الحق وبما كنتم تمرحون

translation: Enter the gates of Hell to abide eternally therein, and wretched is the residence of the arrogant.
interpretation: This verse serves as a stern warning to those who are arrogant and reject the truth of God's message. It emphasizes that the ultimate fate of those who persist in their arrogance and disbelief is eternal damnation in Hell. The mention of "gates" suggests that there are different levels or sections of Hell, each corresponding to the severity of one's sins. The verse also highlights the contrast between the miserable abode of Hell and the blissful residence of the righteous in Paradise. It reminds us to humble ourselves before God, submit to His will, and follow the path of righteousness to avoid the grievous consequences of arrogance and disbelief in the afterlife.
orig: ادخلوا أبواب جهنم خالدين فيها فبئس مثوى المتكبرين

translation: So be patient, [O Muhammad]. Indeed, the promise of Allah is truth. And whether We show you some of what We have promised them or We take you in death, it is to Us they will be returned.
interpretation: This verse is a reminder to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) to remain patient and steadfast in the face of adversity and opposition from those who reject his message. It assures him that Allah's promise of victory and success for the believers is true and will certainly come to pass, whether in this life or the next. The verse also emphasizes the ultimate return of all people to Allah, regardless of their beliefs or actions in this world. It serves as a source of comfort and encouragement for the Prophet and the believers, urging them to persevere in their faith and trust in Allah's plan, knowing that the final outcome is in His hands.
orig: فاصبر إن وعد الله حق فإما نرينك بعض الذي نعدهم أو نتوفينك فإلينا يرجعون

translation: And indeed, We have sent messengers before you, among them are those [whose stories] We have related to you, and among them are those [whose stories] We have not related to you. And it was not for any messenger to bring a sign [or verse] except by permission of Allah. So when the command of Allah comes, it will be concluded in truth, and the falsifiers will thereupon lose [all].
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah has sent numerous messengers before Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him), some of whose stories have been narrated in the Qur'an while others have not. It also highlights that no messenger can bring forth a miracle or a sign without Allah's permission. When Allah's command comes on the Day of Judgment, the truth will be established, and those who followed falsehood will be the losers. This verse serves as a reminder that the ultimate power and authority belong to Allah, and all messengers are merely His servants, delivering His message to mankind.
orig: ولقد أرسلنا رسلا من قبلك منهم من قصصنا عليك ومنهم من لم نقصص عليك وما كان لرسول أن يأتي بآية إلا بإذن الله فإذا جاء أمر الله قضي بالحق وخسر هنالك المبطلون

translation: It is Allah who made for you the grazing animals upon which you ride, and from them you eat.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's benevolence and providence towards humankind. He has created livestock animals and made them subservient to humans, providing multiple benefits. Not only do these animals serve as a means of transportation, allowing people to travel and carry goods, but they also provide sustenance in the form of meat and milk. This highlights the divine wisdom in creating a balanced ecosystem where different creatures serve specific purposes and contribute to the overall well-being of humans. It is a reminder for people to be grateful for Allah's blessings and to use these resources responsibly and with compassion.
orig: الله الذي جعل لكم الأنعام لتركبوا منها ومنها تأكلون

translation: And for you in them are benefits and that you may reach upon them a need which is in your breasts; and upon them and upon ships you are carried.
interpretation: This verse highlights the various benefits and uses that Allah has provided for humans through His creation. The animals mentioned, such as camels, serve as means of transportation, allowing people to reach their destinations and fulfill their needs. They can carry heavy loads and traverse difficult terrains, easing the burden of travel. Additionally, the verse mentions that humans are also carried upon ships, indicating the blessing of sea travel and the ability to transport goods and people across vast distances. These means of transportation are a sign of Allah's favor and provision for His creation, facilitating movement, commerce, and the fulfillment of various needs and desires that arise within the hearts of human beings.
orig: ولكم فيها منافع ولتبلغوا عليها حاجة في صدوركم وعليها وعلى الفلك تحملون

translation: And He shows you His signs. So which of the signs of Allah do you deny?
interpretation: This verse is a reminder to humanity to reflect upon the countless signs and blessings that Allah has bestowed upon them. It challenges individuals to consider which of these signs they would dare to deny or ignore. The interpretation is that Allah's existence, power, and mercy are evident in the world around us, from the intricate design of the universe to the beauty of nature and the miracles of life itself. By acknowledging and appreciating these signs, one can strengthen their faith and connection with the Creator. The verse also serves as a warning against ingratitude and disbelief, as denying the signs of Allah is a grave sin that leads to spiritual darkness and distance from His grace.
orig: ويريكم آياته فأي آيات الله تنكرون

translation: Have they not traveled through the land and observed how was the end of those before them? They were more numerous than themselves and greater in strength and in impression on the land, but they were not availed by what they used to earn.
interpretation: This verse is a reminder for people to reflect on the fate of previous nations who were mightier and more prosperous than them, yet their power and wealth did not save them from Allah's punishment when they disobeyed Him and rejected His messages. It emphasizes that worldly gains and material success are temporary and ultimately meaningless if one does not follow the righteous path. The verse encourages people to learn from history and not be deluded by their own strength or achievements, but rather to humble themselves before Allah and strive for His pleasure.
orig: أفلم يسيروا في الأرض فينظروا كيف كان عاقبة الذين من قبلهم كانوا أكثر منهم وأشد قوة وآثارا في الأرض فما أغنى عنهم ما كانوا يكسبون

translation: Then when their messengers came to them with clear proofs, they rejoiced in the knowledge they [already] had. And they were enveloped by what they used to ridicule.
interpretation: This verse is referring to the people who rejected the messengers of Allah despite being given clear proofs and evidence of their truthfulness. Instead of accepting the message, they were arrogant and took pride in their own limited knowledge, thinking they knew better than the messengers. They mocked and ridiculed the warnings of punishment that the messengers brought. However, the very punishment that they used to make fun of ended up encompassing them, showing the consequences of their arrogance and disbelief in the face of clear truth from Allah.
orig: فلما جاءتهم رسلهم بالبينات فرحوا بما عندهم من العلم وحاق بهم ما كانوا به يستهزئون

translation: But when they saw Our punishment, they said, "We believe in Allah Alone and reject (all) that we used to associate with Him as (His) partners."
interpretation: This verse is referring to the disbelievers who, upon witnessing the punishment of Allah, suddenly profess belief in Him alone and reject their previous idolatry and polytheism. It highlights the human tendency to turn to God in times of hardship and desperation, even if one had previously denied Him. However, the implication is that this last-minute profession of faith, driven by fear of punishment rather than sincere conviction, is unlikely to be accepted by Allah. True faith requires consistency and steadfastness, both in times of ease and adversity. The verse emphasizes the importance of sincere, unwavering belief in the oneness of Allah and the rejection of all forms of idolatry, rather than a superficial declaration of faith under duress.
orig: فلما رأوا بأسنا قالوا آمنا بالله وحده وكفرنا بما كنا به مشركين

translation: But their faith did not avail them when they saw Our punishment. [It is] the established way of Allah which has preceded among His servants. And the disbelievers thereupon lost [all].
interpretation: This verse highlights the fate of those who reject faith in Allah until it is too late. When Allah's punishment comes upon them and they witness it with their own eyes, their sudden profession of faith at that point will be of no benefit to them. This is the established way of Allah that has been decreed for those who persist in disbelief. They will realize their error and loss, but it will be too late for repentance to be accepted. The verse emphasizes the importance of having faith and submitting to Allah before the coming of death and judgement, after which the fate of disbelievers is sealed in eternal loss.
orig: فلم يك ينفعهم إيمانهم لما رأوا بأسنا سنت الله التي قد خلت في عباده وخسر هنالك الكافرون

translation: Ha, Meem.
interpretation: This verse consists of two Arabic letters, Ha and Meem. Many chapters in the Qur'an begin with such mysterious letter combinations, known as Al-Muqatta'at or "the disjoined letters". The exact meaning and purpose of these letters are not explicitly mentioned in the Qur'an or Hadith. Islamic scholars have proposed various interpretations, such as them being symbols of divine secrets, attention-grabbing devices, or indications of the Qur'an's inimitability. Ultimately, the true meaning of these letters is considered to be known only to Allah, reflecting the concept that some aspects of the Qur'an remain mysterious and beyond human comprehension.
orig: حم

translation: A revelation from the Entirely Merciful, the Especially Merciful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the Qur'an is a divine revelation sent down by Allah, who is characterized by His all-encompassing mercy and His special mercy towards the believers. It highlights the divine origin of the Qur'an and the infinite mercy and compassion of Allah towards His creation. The repetition of the attributes "Entirely Merciful" and "Especially Merciful" underscores the immense significance of Allah's mercy in the context of revealing the Qur'an as a guidance for mankind.
orig: تنزيل من الرحمن الرحيم

translation: A Book whose verses have been detailed, an Arabic Qur'an for a people who know
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the Qur'an is a book whose verses have been explained in detail, making it clear and easy to understand. It is revealed in the Arabic language for people who have knowledge and understanding, so that they may comprehend its meanings and benefit from its guidance. The Qur'an is not a book of ambiguity or confusion, but rather a book of clarity and wisdom for those who reflect upon its verses and seek to live by its teachings.
orig: كتاب فصلت آياته قرآنا عربيا لقوم يعلمون

translation: As a bringer of good tidings and a warner, but most of them turn away, so they do not hear.
interpretation: This verse highlights the role of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) as both a bearer of good news and a warner to humanity. Despite his efforts to convey the message of Islam, many people chose to ignore his teachings and turn away from the truth. They metaphorically "do not hear" the message, meaning they refuse to listen, understand, and accept the guidance provided by the Prophet. This verse emphasizes the free will of human beings to either accept or reject the divine message, while also expressing the disappointment and frustration felt by the Prophet when his sincere efforts to guide people towards righteousness were met with indifference and rejection.
orig: بشيرا ونذيرا فأعرض أكثرهم فهم لا يسمعون

translation: And they say, "Our hearts are within coverings from that to which you invite us, and in our ears is deafness, and between us and you is a partition, so work; indeed, we are working."
interpretation: This verse refers to the disbelievers who reject the message of Islam despite the clear proofs and evidence presented to them. They claim that their hearts are covered, preventing them from understanding or accepting the truth, and that there is a barrier between them and the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him). They are determined to persist in their disbelief and continue their worldly pursuits, disregarding the call to faith. It highlights the stubbornness and arrogance of those who choose to remain in a state of spiritual ignorance, even when the path of guidance is made clear to them.
orig: وقالوا قلوبنا في أكنة مما تدعونا إليه وفي آذاننا وقر ومن بيننا وبينك حجاب فاعمل إننا عاملون

translation: Say, "I am only a man like you, to whom has been revealed that your god is one God. So take a straight course to Him and seek His forgiveness." And woe to those who associate others with Allah -
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the humanity of Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and that he is not divine, but a messenger who receives revelation from the one true God. It calls upon people to direct their worship and obedience solely to Allah, seeking His forgiveness and avoiding the grave sin of associating partners with Him (shirk). The verse warns that those who commit shirk and refuse to follow the straight path to Allah will face severe consequences in the Hereafter.
orig: قل إنما أنا بشر مثلكم يوحى إلي أنما إلهكم إله واحد فاستقيموا إليه واستغفروه وويل للمشركين

translation: Those who do not give zakah and they, in the Hereafter, they are disbelievers.
interpretation: This verse is emphasizing the importance of giving zakah, which is a mandatory charity in Islam. It suggests that those who do not fulfill this obligation and do not believe in the Hereafter are considered disbelievers. The verse highlights the connection between one's actions in this world, particularly in regards to fulfilling religious duties like giving zakah, and one's faith and belief in the afterlife. It implies that true belief necessitates adherence to the commandments of Allah, and failure to do so is a sign of disbelief.
orig: الذين لا يؤتون الزكاة وهم بالآخرة هم كافرون

translation: Indeed, those who believe and do righteous deeds will have a reward uninterrupted.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that those who have true faith in Allah and couple that faith with good deeds and righteous actions will be granted an immense reward from Allah that will never end or be cut off. It points to the great value Allah places on faith and good works. The "uninterrupted reward" signifies Paradise, which the believers will enjoy eternally without any fear of it ending or being taken away from them. This promise from Allah serves as a great encouragement and motivation for the believers to persist in faith and righteousness.
orig: إن الذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات لهم أجر غير ممنون

translation: Say, "Do you indeed disbelieve in He who created the earth in two days and attribute to Him equals? That is the Lord of the worlds."
interpretation: This verse is a rhetorical question that challenges those who disbelieve in Allah and associate partners with Him. It emphasizes the power and uniqueness of Allah as the sole Creator of the earth, which He created in just two days. By attributing equals to Him, the disbelievers are committing a grave error and denying the truth of Allah's lordship over all creation. The verse serves as a reminder of Allah's omnipotence and the need to worship Him alone, without ascribing partners to Him. It also highlights the absurdity of disbelief in the face of such clear signs of Allah's existence and creative power.
orig: قل أئنكم لتكفرون بالذي خلق الأرض في يومين وتجعلون له أندادا ذلك رب العالمين

translation: And He placed on the earth firmly set mountains over its surface, and He blessed it and determined therein its [creatures'] sustenance in four days without distinction - for [the information] of those who ask.
interpretation: This verse highlights Allah's power and wisdom in creating the earth and all that it contains. The mention of mountains suggests that they play a crucial role in stabilizing the earth's surface. Allah's blessing of the earth and His determination of sustenance for all creatures in four days emphasizes His benevolence and perfect planning. The phrase "for those who ask" indicates that this information is readily available to those who seek knowledge and reflect upon the signs of Allah's creation. It invites humans to contemplate the earth's wonders and appreciate the divine wisdom behind them.
orig: وجعل فيها رواسي من فوقها وبارك فيها وقدر فيها أقواتها في أربعة أيام سواء للسائلين

translation: Then He directed Himself to the heaven while it was smoke and said to it and to the earth, "Come [into being], willingly or by compulsion." They said, "We have come willingly."
interpretation: This verse signifies Allah's supreme power and authority over His creation. It illustrates that when Allah decreed for the heavens and the earth to come into existence, they had no choice but to obey His command, whether willingly or unwillingly. The phrase "while it was smoke" refers to the initial state of the universe, which modern science describes as a nebulous, gaseous mass. The verse also emphasizes the complete submission of all creation to Allah's will, as the heavens and earth responded, "We have come willingly," demonstrating their total obedience to their Creator. This highlights the importance of humankind, as the pinnacle of Allah's creation, to willingly submit to His commands and worship Him alone.
orig: ثم استوى إلى السماء وهي دخان فقال لها وللأرض ائتيا طوعا أو كرها قالتا أتينا طائعين

translation: Then He completed and finished from their creation as seven heavens in two Days and He assigned to each heaven its duty and command. And We adorned the nearest (lowest) heaven with lamps (stars) to be an adornment as well as to guard. Such is the Decree of Him the Exalted in Might, the All-Knower.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's power and wisdom in creating the seven heavens in just two days, assigning each its specific purpose and laws. The adornment of the lowest heaven with stars serves both as a beautiful display and a means of protection. This precise and purposeful design is a testament to Allah's might and all-encompassing knowledge, highlighting that everything in the universe is created with a specific function and role according to His divine plan.
orig: فقضاهن سبع سماوات في يومين وأوحى في كل سماء أمرها وزينا السماء الدنيا بمصابيح وحفظا ذلك تقدير العزيز العليم

translation: But if they turn away, then say, "I have warned you of a thunderbolt like the thunderbolt [that struck] 'Aad and Thamud."
interpretation: This verse is a warning to those who reject the message of Islam. It reminds them of the fate of the ancient tribes of 'Aad and Thamud, who were destroyed by a thunderbolt from Allah as a punishment for their disbelief and disobedience. The verse emphasizes the severity of Allah's punishment and the consequences of rejecting His message. It serves as a reminder to the disbelievers that they too may face a similar fate if they persist in their disbelief and do not heed the warning of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him). The verse also highlights the importance of accepting the message of Islam and submitting to Allah's will in order to avoid His wrath and punishment.
orig: فإن أعرضوا فقل أنذرتكم صاعقة مثل صاعقة عاد وثمود

translation: When the messengers came to them from before them and behind them, [saying], "Do not worship except Allah," they said, "If our Lord had willed, He would have sent down the angels, so indeed we, in that with which you have been sent, are disbelievers."
interpretation: This verse highlights the stubborn disbelief of certain people when faced with the clear message brought by the prophets and messengers of Allah. Despite the messengers coming to them from all directions, urging them to worship Allah alone, they arrogantly rejected the message, claiming that if Allah truly wanted to guide them, He would have sent angels as messengers instead of human beings. This interpretation emphasizes the depth of their disbelief and their willingness to make excuses to avoid submitting to the truth, even when it is presented to them clearly and repeatedly by the messengers of Allah.
orig: إذ جاءتهم الرسل من بين أيديهم ومن خلفهم ألا تعبدوا إلا الله قالوا لو شاء ربنا لأنزل ملائكة فإنا بما أرسلتم به كافرون

translation: As for 'Aad, they were arrogant upon the earth without right and said, "Who is greater than us in strength?" Did they not consider that Allah who created them was greater than them in strength? But they were rejecting Our signs.
interpretation: This verse highlights the arrogance and pride of the people of 'Aad, who believed that their strength and power made them superior to others. They failed to recognize that their strength was nothing compared to the might of Allah, their Creator. Despite witnessing the signs and evidence of Allah's power, they continued to reject and deny them. This arrogance and denial of truth ultimately led to their downfall and destruction. The verse serves as a reminder for mankind to humble themselves before the Almighty and acknowledge His supremacy, rather than being deluded by their own perceived strength and abilities.
orig: فأما عاد فاستكبروا في الأرض بغير الحق وقالوا من أشد منا قوة أولم يروا أن الله الذي خلقهم هو أشد منهم قوة وكانوا بآياتنا يجحدون

translation: So We sent upon them a screaming wind during days of misfortune to make them taste the punishment of disgrace in the worldly life; but the punishment of the Hereafter is more disgracing, and they will not be helped.
interpretation: This verse speaks about how Allah punished a group of people who rejected His message by sending upon them a fierce, screaming wind during a period of misfortune and calamity. The purpose was to give them a taste of humiliation and disgrace in this worldly life. However, the verse warns that the punishment of the Hereafter will be even more shameful and degrading, and they will have no one to help or support them against it. This highlights the severity of rejecting Allah's guidance and the ultimate consequences in store for disbelievers in the afterlife.
orig: فأرسلنا عليهم ريحا صرصرا في أيام نحسات لنذيقهم عذاب الخزي في الحياة الدنيا ولعذاب الآخرة أخزى وهم لا ينصرون

translation: And as for Thamud, We guided them, but they preferred blindness over guidance, so the thunderbolt of humiliating punishment seized them for what they used to earn.
interpretation: This verse is a warning to those who reject divine guidance in favor of their own desires and worldly pursuits. The people of Thamud were given clear signs and guidance from Allah, but they chose to ignore it and continue in their wrongdoing. As a result, they were struck with a severe and humiliating punishment for their actions. This serves as a reminder that the consequences of rejecting Allah's guidance and persisting in sin can be severe, both in this life and in the hereafter. It is a call to submit to the will of Allah and follow the path of righteousness, even when it may be difficult or unpopular, in order to attain success and avoid the fate of those who were destroyed for their disobedience.
orig: وأما ثمود فهديناهم فاستحبوا العمى على الهدى فأخذتهم صاعقة العذاب الهون بما كانوا يكسبون

translation: And We saved those who believed and used to fear Allah.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah will ultimately save and protect those who have true faith and live their lives in accordance with that faith, fearing Allah and following His guidance. It implies that even in times of great difficulty or when facing oppression from disbelievers, the believers who remain steadfast will be delivered to safety by Allah due to their taqwa (God-consciousness). This serves as a reassurance and promise of Allah's support for the righteous.
orig: ونجينا الذين آمنوا وكانوا يتقون

translation: And the Day when the enemies of Allah will be gathered to the Fire, they will be [driven] in rows.
interpretation: This verse refers to the Day of Judgment when those who opposed Allah and His message will be driven to the Hellfire in groups. It signifies the ultimate consequence of rejecting faith and choosing to be an enemy of the truth. The verse emphasizes the severity of the punishment and the regret the disbelievers will face for their actions and decisions in this world. It serves as a warning for people to mend their ways, submit to Allah, and follow the righteous path to avoid this dreadful fate in the Hereafter.
orig: ويوم يحشر أعداء الله إلى النار فهم يوزعون

translation: Until, when they reach it, their hearing and their eyes and their skins will testify against them of what they used to do.
interpretation: This verse refers to the Day of Judgment when the disbelievers will be confronted with the reality of their actions. Their own faculties - their hearing, sight, and even their skins - will bear witness against them, testifying to the sins they committed in their worldly life. It highlights the inescapable nature of divine justice. No matter how much one tries to hide or deny their misdeeds, on that day, the truth will be laid bare. It serves as a powerful reminder of the importance of righteousness and the consequences of our choices. It also underscores God's omniscience - nothing is hidden from Him, and we will be held accountable for our deeds.
orig: حتى إذا ما جاءوها شهد عليهم سمعهم وأبصارهم وجلودهم بما كانوا يعملون

translation: And they will say to their skins, "Why have you testified against us?" They will say, "We were made to speak by Allah, who has made everything speak; and He created you the first time, and to Him you are returned."
interpretation: This verse highlights the concept of ultimate accountability before Allah. On the Day of Judgment, even one's own body parts will testify against them for the deeds they committed in this world. It emphasizes that nothing is hidden from Allah, as He has the power to make everything speak and bear witness. The verse also points to the fact that Allah is the One who created human beings in the first place and that everyone will return to Him for judgment. It serves as a reminder for people to be mindful of their actions in this life, as they will be held accountable for them in the Hereafter.
orig: وقالوا لجلودهم لم شهدتم علينا قالوا أنطقنا الله الذي أنطق كل شيء وهو خلقكم أول مرة وإليه ترجعون

translation: And you were not covering yourselves, lest your hearing testify against you or your sight or your skins, but you assumed that Allah does not know much of what you do.
interpretation: This verse is a reminder that nothing can be hidden from Allah, even if we try to conceal our actions from others. It emphasizes the all-encompassing knowledge of Allah, and that He is aware of everything we do, even if we think we can keep it a secret. The verse also highlights the fact that on the Day of Judgment, our own bodies - our hearing, sight, and skin - will testify against us, revealing the truth about our deeds. This should serve as a warning to be mindful of our actions and to strive for righteousness, knowing that Allah is always watching and will hold us accountable for what we do.
orig: وما كنتم تستترون أن يشهد عليكم سمعكم ولا أبصاركم ولا جلودكم ولكن ظننتم أن الله لا يعلم كثيرا مما تعملون

translation: And that was your assumption which you assumed about your Lord. It has brought you to ruin, and you have become among the losers.
interpretation: This verse is addressing the disbelievers who held wrong assumptions about Allah. They thought that Allah would not resurrect them or hold them accountable for their deeds. These false assumptions led them astray and caused their ultimate loss and ruin in the Hereafter. The verse emphasizes the gravity of having incorrect beliefs about Allah and the severe consequences that result from such assumptions. It serves as a warning to people to correct their faith and to believe in Allah's power, justice, and the reality of the Day of Judgment.
orig: وذلكم ظنكم الذي ظننتم بربكم أرداكم فأصبحتم من الخاسرين

translation: And if they are patient, the Fire will be a residence for them; and if they ask to appease [Allah], they are not of those who will be allowed to appease.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the hopeless situation of the disbelievers in the Hereafter. If they bear the torment of Hell patiently, it will still be their permanent abode. And if they seek to appease Allah and be relieved from the punishment, their plea will be rejected. They will not be given another chance or be allowed to make amends. This highlights the severity and finality of the consequences of disbelief and rejection of Allah's message in this world.
orig: فإن يصبروا فالنار مثوى لهم وإن يستعتبوا فما هم من المعتبين

translation: And We appointed for them companions who made attractive to them what was before them and what was behind them, and the word has come into effect upon them among nations which had passed on before them of jinn and men. Indeed, they [all] were losers.
interpretation: This verse suggests that those who reject faith and follow evil are influenced by companions who make their past and present misdeeds seem attractive. These companions could be interpreted as evil influences, whether human or jinn (unseen beings), that lead people astray. The fate of such individuals is sealed, as they join the ranks of previous nations who were also led astray and ultimately faced loss and failure in both this world and the hereafter due to their rejection of truth and indulgence in sin. It emphasizes the importance of choosing one's company wisely and being cautious of negative influences that can lead to spiritual ruin.
orig: وقيضنا لهم قرناء فزينوا لهم ما بين أيديهم وما خلفهم وحق عليهم القول في أمم قد خلت من قبلهم من الجن والإنس إنهم كانوا خاسرين

translation: And those who disbelieve say, "Do not listen to this Qur'an and speak noisily during [the recitation of] it that perhaps you will overcome."
interpretation: This verse refers to the attempts of the disbelievers to prevent people from listening to the Qur'an. They would make noise and create distractions when the Qur'an was being recited, hoping to drown out its message and discourage people from paying attention to it. This behavior reflects their deep-seated aversion to the truth and their desire to maintain their power and influence over others. The verse serves as a warning to the believers not to be swayed by such tactics and to remain steadfast in their faith and commitment to the Qur'an, even in the face of opposition and hostility from those who reject its message.
orig: وقال الذين كفروا لا تسمعوا لهذا القرآن والغوا فيه لعلكم تغلبون

translation: So We will surely cause those who disbelieve to taste a severe punishment, and We will surely recompense them for the worst of what they had been doing.
interpretation: This verse is a stern warning to those who reject faith in Allah and His message. It emphasizes that disbelievers will face severe consequences for their actions in this world and the Hereafter. Allah will make them taste a painful punishment and will recompense them based on the worst of their deeds. This highlights the gravity of disbelief and the importance of faith and righteous actions. The verse serves as a reminder for believers to stay steadfast in their faith and for disbelievers to repent and turn to Allah before it is too late.
orig: فلنذيقن الذين كفروا عذابا شديدا ولنجزينهم أسوأ الذي كانوا يعملون

translation: That is the recompense of the enemies of Allah: the Fire. For them therein is the eternal home, a recompense for what they used to deny of Our verses.
interpretation: This verse speaks to the ultimate fate of those who reject Allah's signs and teachings - the Fire of Hell, where they will abide eternally. It is a just recompense for their willful denial and disbelief, as they consciously chose to turn away from the truth of Allah's revelation. The "eternal home" emphasizes the permanence and inescapability of this punishment. This stark warning serves as a reminder to humanity of the grave consequences of denying faith, while affirming Allah's ultimate justice in dealing with those who knowingly oppose Him.
orig: ذلك جزاء أعداء الله النار لهم فيها دار الخلد جزاء بما كانوا بآياتنا يجحدون

translation: And those who disbelieved will [then] say, "Our Lord, show us those who misled us of the jinn and men [so] we may put them under our feet that they will be among the lowest."
interpretation: This verse speaks to the regret and resentment the disbelievers will feel on the Day of Judgment. They will plead with Allah to reveal to them those among the jinn and humans who led them astray, so that they may trample them underfoot and make them the lowest of the low. It reflects the human tendency to blame others for one's own misdeeds and the desire for revenge. However, in reality, each soul is responsible for its own faith and actions. The verse serves as a warning against following those who invite to disbelief and misguidance, as their end will be humiliation and punishment in the Hereafter.
orig: وقال الذين كفروا ربنا أرنا اللذين أضلانا من الجن والإنس نجعلهما تحت أقدامنا ليكونا من الأسفلين

translation: Indeed, those who have said, "Our Lord is Allah" and then remained on a right course - the angels will descend upon them, [saying], "Do not fear and do not grieve but receive good tidings of Paradise, which you were promised.
interpretation: This verse is a reassurance and glad tidings for the believers who remain steadfast in their faith. It emphasizes that those who acknowledge Allah as their Lord and stay committed to the right path will be rewarded with Paradise. The angels will descend upon them, comforting them and dispelling their fears and sorrows. This verse highlights the importance of unwavering faith and righteousness, as it is the key to attaining the ultimate reward of Paradise in the Hereafter. It serves as a source of hope and motivation for the believers to persevere in their devotion to Allah, knowing that their efforts will be recognized and celebrated by the angels and Allah Himself.
orig: إن الذين قالوا ربنا الله ثم استقاموا تتنزل عليهم الملائكة ألا تخافوا ولا تحزنوا وأبشروا بالجنة التي كنتم توعدون

translation: We [angels] were your allies in worldly life and [are so] in the Hereafter. And you will have therein whatever your souls desire, and you will have therein whatever you request [or wish]
interpretation: This verse is a reassurance to the righteous believers that the angels are their protectors and supporters not only in this worldly life, but also in the eternal life of the Hereafter. It emphasizes that in Paradise, the believers will have all that their souls could wish for or request. This signifies the perfect contentment, satisfaction and bliss that the people of Paradise will experience, as a reward for their faith and good deeds in the worldly life. The verse underscores God's boundless generosity and the comprehensive nature of His rewards to His faithful servants in the afterlife.
orig: نحن أولياؤكم في الحياة الدنيا وفي الآخرة ولكم فيها ما تشتهي أنفسكم ولكم فيها ما تدعون

translation: It is sent down by the Forgiving, the Merciful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the Qur'an is a revelation from Allah, who is characterized by His infinite forgiveness and mercy. It serves as a reminder that the Qur'an is not a human creation, but rather a divine gift bestowed upon humanity by the Most Forgiving and Most Merciful. This attribute of Allah's forgiveness and mercy is reflected throughout the Qur'an, as it guides people towards righteousness and offers them the opportunity to seek repentance and attain salvation. The verse also implies that the Qur'an itself is a manifestation of Allah's forgiveness and mercy, as it provides guidance and light to those who sincerely seek to follow the right path.
orig: نزلا من غفور رحيم

translation: And who is better in speech than one who invites to Allah and does righteousness and says, "Indeed, I am of the Muslims."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance and virtue of inviting others to the path of Allah through good speech and righteous deeds. The one who combines these qualities - calling people to faith, performing good actions, and openly identifying as a Muslim - is considered among the best in the sight of Allah. It highlights the significance of aligning one's words and actions in the service of God and being a positive example and guide for others. The verse encourages Muslims to actively share the message of Islam with wisdom and kindness while striving to embody its teachings in their own lives.
orig: ومن أحسن قولا ممن دعا إلى الله وعمل صالحا وقال إنني من المسلمين

translation: Good and evil deeds are not equal. Repel evil with what is better; then you will see that one who was once your enemy has become your dearest friend.
interpretation: This verse encourages Muslims to respond to wrongdoing and hostility with kindness, patience, and forgiveness. It suggests that by treating others with compassion and understanding, even those who were once enemies can become close friends. The message is that one should strive to overcome negativity and animosity by taking the moral high ground and responding with what is best. This high standard of behavior reflects the virtues of mercy and clemency promoted in Islam. By acting with grace and benevolence, hearts can be softened and relationships transformed in a positive way.
orig: ولا تستوي الحسنة ولا السيئة ادفع بالتي هي أحسن فإذا الذي بينك وبينه عداوة كأنه ولي حميم

translation: But none is granted it except those who are patient, and none is granted it except one having a great portion [of good].
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of patience and perseverance in attaining great rewards and blessings from Allah. It suggests that only those who consistently display patience and steadfastness in the face of challenges and hardships will be granted the tremendous fortune of Allah's favor and grace. The verse implies that patience is a key virtue that distinguishes the true believers and that the greatest rewards are reserved for those who remain patient and steadfast in their faith and good deeds, seeking Allah's pleasure above all else. It encourages believers to cultivate patience and to trust in Allah's plan, knowing that their patience will ultimately be rewarded with immense blessings and success in this life and the hereafter.
orig: وما يلقاها إلا الذين صبروا وما يلقاها إلا ذو حظ عظيم

translation: And if an evil suggestion comes to you from Satan, then seek refuge in Allah. Indeed, He is the Hearing, the Knowing.
interpretation: This verse reminds us that whenever we feel tempted or misguided by the whisperings of Satan, we should immediately turn to Allah and seek His protection. By seeking refuge in Allah, we acknowledge His power and authority over all things, including the plots of Satan. Allah is the All-Hearing, so He hears our pleas for help, and He is the All-Knowing, so He knows what is best for us and how to guide us away from the path of evil. This verse emphasizes the importance of maintaining a strong connection with Allah and relying on Him for guidance and support in the face of temptation and adversity.
orig: وإما ينزغنك من الشيطان نزغ فاستعذ بالله إنه هو السميع العليم

translation: And of His signs are the night and day and the sun and moon. Do not prostrate to the sun or to the moon, but prostate to Allah, who created them, if it should be Him that you worship.
interpretation: This verse reminds us that the natural phenomena we observe, such as the alternation of night and day and the sun and moon, are all signs of Allah's power and creation. We should not worship or prostrate to these created entities, but rather direct our worship and submission solely to Allah, the One who brought them into existence. This verse emphasizes the importance of pure monotheism and avoiding any form of idolatry or associating partners with Allah in worship, as our devotion should be exclusively for Him if we claim to be His true servants.
orig: ومن آياته الليل والنهار والشمس والقمر لا تسجدوا للشمس ولا للقمر واسجدوا لله الذي خلقهن إن كنتم إياه تعبدون

translation: But if they are arrogant - then those who are near your Lord exalt Him by night and by day, and they do not become weary.
interpretation: This verse highlights the contrast between the arrogance of those who reject God's message and the devotion of the angels who constantly worship and glorify Him. The angels, who are close to God, tirelessly praise and exalt Him day and night without ever growing weary or bored. This serves as a reminder that true devotion to God is characterized by humility, submission, and unwavering commitment. It also emphasizes the importance of perseverance in worship and the need to avoid arrogance and pride, which can lead one astray from the path of righteousness.
orig: فإن استكبروا فالذين عند ربك يسبحون له بالليل والنهار وهم لا يسأمون

translation: And among His signs is that you see the earth barren, but when We send down upon it rain, it quivers and swells. Indeed, He who has given it life is the Giver of Life to the dead. Indeed, He is over all things competent.
interpretation: This verse is a reminder of Allah's power and ability to bring life from death. Just as He can revive the barren earth with rain, making it green and fertile, He can also resurrect the dead. This is a sign of His omnipotence and a testament to the truth of the Day of Judgment when all will be brought back to life. The verse encourages believers to reflect on the wonders of Allah's creation and to have faith in His promise of resurrection and the Hereafter. It also emphasizes that Allah has power over all things and can do whatever He wills, so we should trust in Him and submit to His commands.
orig: ومن آياته أنك ترى الأرض خاشعة فإذا أنزلنا عليها الماء اهتزت وربت إن الذي أحياها لمحيي الموتى إنه على كل شيء قدير

translation: Indeed, those who inject deviation into Our verses are not concealed from Us. So, is he who is cast into the Fire better or he who comes secured on the Day of Resurrection? Do whatever you will; indeed, He is Seeing of what you do.
interpretation: This verse serves as a stern warning to those who distort or misinterpret the verses of the Qur'an. It emphasizes that God is fully aware of their actions and that they cannot hide from His knowledge. The verse poses a rhetorical question, comparing the fate of those who will be punished in the Fire of Hell with those who will come safely on the Day of Judgment. It implies that the latter group, those who follow the Qur'an's teachings faithfully, are far better in the sight of God. The verse concludes by reminding people that they are free to choose their actions, but God is always observing and will hold them accountable for their deeds. This interpretation highlights the importance of sincerity in faith and the consequences of deliberately misrepresenting or deviating from the divine message of the Qur'an.
orig: إن الذين يلحدون في آياتنا لا يخفون علينا أفمن يلقى في النار خير أم من يأتي آمنا يوم القيامة اعملوا ما شئتم إنه بما تعملون بصير

translation: Indeed, those who disbelieve in the message when it comes to them... And indeed, it is a mighty Book.
interpretation: This verse is referring to the Qur'an itself, describing it as a mighty and powerful book. It also speaks about those who reject and disbelieve in the Qur'an when it is presented to them. The interpretation is that the Qur'an is a noble and unassailable scripture, protected by Allah from corruption or change. Despite its clear truth, there will still be those who arrogantly refuse to believe in it due to their own stubborn disbelief. However, their rejection does not detract from the Qur'an's power and authority as the final revelation from Allah to mankind.
orig: إن الذين كفروا بالذكر لما جاءهم وإنه لكتاب عزيز

translation: No falsehood can approach it from before or behind it. [It is] a revelation from a [Lord who is] Wise and Praiseworthy.
interpretation: This verse affirms the divine protection of the Qur'an from any form of alteration or corruption. It asserts that the Qur'an is free from falsehood and cannot be approached by it from any direction, whether past, present, or future. This is because the Qur'an is a revelation from Allah, the All-Wise and Praiseworthy, Who has taken it upon Himself to preserve it. The verse emphasizes the authenticity and trustworthiness of the Qur'an as a source of guidance for mankind, as it remains unchanged and uncorrupted since its revelation to Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him).
orig: لا يأتيه الباطل من بين يديه ولا من خلفه تنزيل من حكيم حميد

translation: Nothing is said to you, [O Muhammad], except what was already said to the messengers before you. Indeed, your Lord is a possessor of forgiveness and a possessor of painful penalty.
interpretation: This verse is a reminder to Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) that he is not facing anything new in terms of the challenges and opposition from his people. The previous prophets and messengers faced similar trials and difficulties in conveying the message of God to their nations. However, the verse also emphasizes two important attributes of God: His forgiveness and His punishment. On one hand, God is Oft-Forgiving to those who repent and seek His mercy. On the other hand, He is severe in punishment for those who persist in disbelief and rejection of His messages, despite the clear signs and warnings. This duality serves as both a comfort and a warning - a comfort for the believers who may face hardships in the path of God, and a warning for the disbelievers of the consequences of their choices.
orig: ما يقال لك إلا ما قد قيل للرسل من قبلك إن ربك لذو مغفرة وذو عقاب أليم

translation: And if We had made it a non-Arabic Qur'an, they would have said, "Why are its verses not explained in detail [in our language]? Is it a foreign [recitation] and an Arab [messenger]?" Say, "It is, for those who believe, a guidance and cure." And those who do not believe - in their ears is deafness, and it is upon them blindness. Those are being called from a distant place.
interpretation: This verse addresses the hypothetical objection of the disbelievers who might have questioned the revelation of the Qur'an in Arabic. It asserts that even if the Qur'an were revealed in a foreign language, they would still not believe and would find other excuses to reject it. The verse emphasizes that for the believers, the Qur'an serves as a guide and a source of spiritual healing, regardless of its language. However, for those who choose not to believe, the message of the Qur'an falls on deaf ears, and they are unable to comprehend its truth, as if they are being called from a distant place, unable to hear or understand the call.
orig: ولو جعلناه قرآنا أعجميا لقالوا لولا فصلت آياته أأعجمي وعربي قل هو للذين آمنوا هدى وشفاء والذين لا يؤمنون في آذانهم وقر وهو عليهم عمى أولئك ينادون من مكان بعيد

translation: And We had certainly given Moses the Scripture, but it came under disagreement. And if not for a word that preceded from your Lord, it would have been concluded between them. And indeed they are, concerning the Qur'an, in disquieting doubt.
interpretation: This verse highlights the fact that even though God sent down revelation to Moses in the form of scripture, people still disagreed about it and had doubts. This shows the tendency of human beings to differ and dispute, even when divine guidance is given to them. The verse also indicates that if it were not for God's prior decree, He would have judged between the disputing parties regarding the truth. However, God in His wisdom allows people free will to either accept the guidance or remain in doubt. The verse subtly warns that those who choose to reject the truth of revelation will remain in an unsettled state of uncertainty and skepticism.
orig: ولقد آتينا موسى الكتاب فاختلف فيه ولولا كلمة سبقت من ربك لقضي بينهم وإنهم لفي شك منه مريب

translation: Whoever does righteousness - it is for his [own] soul; and whoever does evil [does so] against it. And your Lord is not ever unjust to [His] servants.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the concept of individual responsibility in Islam. Every person is accountable for their own actions, whether good or bad. Righteous deeds benefit one's own soul, while evil deeds only harm oneself. It also highlights God's perfect justice - He does not wrong any of His servants, and everyone will be recompensed fairly for what they have done. This encourages believers to strive for righteousness and refrain from evil, knowing that they alone bear the consequences of their choices.
orig: من عمل صالحا فلنفسه ومن أساء فعليها وما ربك بظلام للعبيد

translation: To Him is referred the knowledge of the Hour. And fruits do not emerge from their coverings nor does a female conceive or give birth except by His knowledge. And the Day He will call to them, "Where are My 'partners'?" they will say, "We announce to You that there is no witness among us."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah alone has the knowledge of the Hour, the time of the Day of Judgment. It also highlights that every event in the universe, from the emergence of fruits from their coverings to the conception and birth of a child, happens only by the knowledge and will of Allah. On the Day of Judgment, when Allah questions the polytheists about their false deities, they will realize and admit that none of their so-called partners can bear witness or provide any support, affirming the absolute oneness and sovereignty of Allah.
orig: إليه يرد علم الساعة وما تخرج من ثمرات من أكمامها وما تحمل من أنثى ولا تضع إلا بعلمه ويوم يناديهم أين شركائي قالوا آذناك ما منا من شهيد

translation: And lost from them will be those they were invoking before, and they will be certain that they have no place of escape.
interpretation: This verse is referring to the Day of Judgment, when the false gods and idols that the disbelievers used to invoke will be of no help to them. They will realize that there is no escape from Allah's punishment and that they have no one to turn to for help or intercession. It is a stark reminder of the consequences of rejecting faith in Allah and the inevitability of facing the truth on the Day of Reckoning. The verse emphasizes the futility of relying on anyone or anything other than Allah and the importance of sincere faith and righteous deeds in this life.
orig: وضل عنهم ما كانوا يدعون من قبل وظنوا ما لهم من محيص

translation: Man does not tire of supplication for good [things], but if evil touches him, he is hopeless and despairing.
interpretation: This verse highlights the fickle nature of human beings. When things are going well, people are eager to pray and ask Allah for blessings and good things in life. However, when faced with difficulties or evil, many lose hope quickly and fall into despair, forgetting to turn to Allah for help and guidance. It serves as a reminder to remain steadfast in faith and continue supplicating to Allah in both good times and bad, trusting in His wisdom and mercy, and not losing hope when facing challenges or hardships.
orig: لا يسأم الإنسان من دعاء الخير وإن مسه الشر فيئوس قنوط

translation: And if We give him a taste of mercy from Us after an adversity which has touched him, he will surely say, "This is [due] to me, and I do not think the Hour will occur; and [even] if I should be returned to my Lord, indeed, for me there will be with Him the best." But We will surely inform those who disbelieved about what they did, and We will surely make them taste a massive punishment.
interpretation: This verse highlights the arrogance and ingratitude of some people. When God blesses them with ease and comfort after a period of hardship, they attribute it to their own abilities and worth, rather than acknowledging God's mercy. They even doubt the coming of the Day of Judgment. They assume that if there is an afterlife, they would still be entitled to God's favor due to their self-perceived status. However, God makes it clear that those who disbelieve and are ungrateful will be held accountable for their deeds and will face severe punishment in the Hereafter. This serves as a warning for people to be humble, grateful, and mindful of God's blessings and the inevitability of the Day of Judgment.
orig: ولئن أذقناه رحمة منا من بعد ضراء مسته ليقولن هذا لي وما أظن الساعة قائمة ولئن رجعت إلى ربي إن لي عنده للحسنى فلننبئن الذين كفروا بما عملوا ولنذيقنهم من عذاب غليظ

translation: And when We bestow favor upon man, he turns away and distances himself; but when evil touches him, then he has recourse to long supplications.
interpretation: This verse highlights the fickle nature of human beings. When God blesses them with favors and comforts, they often become arrogant and turn away from Him, forgetting to be grateful. However, when faced with difficulties or calamities, they quickly turn back to God, making lengthy and fervent supplications, seeking His help and mercy. This demonstrates the weakness of human nature and the importance of remaining steadfast in faith and gratitude, both in times of ease and hardship. It serves as a reminder for believers to consistently turn to God in all circumstances, acknowledging His blessings and seeking His guidance and support.
orig: وإذا أنعمنا على الإنسان أعرض ونأى بجانبه وإذا مسه الشر فذو دعاء عريض

translation: Say, "Have you considered: if the Qur'an is from Allah and you disbelieved in it, who would be more astray than one who is in extreme dissension?"
interpretation: This verse is a powerful warning to those who reject the divine origin of the Qur'an. It challenges them to consider the consequences of their disbelief, suggesting that if the Qur'an is truly from Allah, then rejecting it would be the ultimate misguidance and would lead one far astray from the truth. The verse emphasizes the gravity of denying the Qur'an's divine source and implies that such rejection stems from deep-rooted dissension and opposition to the truth. It serves as a reminder for people to carefully examine the Qur'an and its message, as turning away from it, if it is indeed from Allah, would be the most severe form of misguidance.
orig: قل أرأيتم إن كان من عند الله ثم كفرتم به من أضل ممن هو في شقاق بعيد

translation: We will show them Our signs in the horizons and within themselves until it becomes clear to them that it is the truth. But is it not sufficient concerning your Lord that He is, over all things, a Witness?
interpretation: This verse points to the fact that Allah's signs and proofs of His existence, power, and wisdom are evident both in the vast expanse of the universe and within the human soul itself. These signs are so numerous and clear that eventually, even the disbelievers will have to acknowledge the truth of Allah's message. The verse also emphasizes that Allah is a witness over everything, implying that He is aware of all our actions and intentions, and that this alone should be sufficient for us to believe in Him and follow His guidance. It encourages us to reflect upon the world around us and within ourselves, as doing so will inevitably lead to a stronger faith and a deeper understanding of Allah's presence in our lives.
orig: سنريهم آياتنا في الآفاق وفي أنفسهم حتى يتبين لهم أنه الحق أولم يكف بربك أنه على كل شيء شهيد

translation: Unquestionably, they are in doubt about the meeting with their Lord. Unquestionably He is, of all things, encompassing.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that despite the clear signs and evidence, there are still those who doubt that they will meet their Lord on the Day of Judgment. They are uncertain about the reality of the afterlife and the accountability for their deeds. However, Allah affirms that He encompasses everything in His knowledge and power. Nothing escapes His awareness, and He will bring all matters to light on the Day of Reckoning. This serves as a reminder for believers to remain steadfast in their faith and for the doubters to reflect upon the inevitable encounter with their Creator.
orig: ألا إنهم في مرية من لقاء ربهم ألا إنه بكل شيء محيط

translation: Ha, Meem.
interpretation: This verse consists of two Arabic letters, Ha and Meem. Many chapters in the Qur'an begin with such mysterious letter combinations, known as Al-Muqatta'at (the Disjoined Letters). The exact meaning and purpose of these letters are not explicitly mentioned in the Qur'an or Hadith. Scholars have proposed various interpretations, such as them being symbols of divine secrets, attention-grabbers, or abbreviations for certain phrases. Ultimately, the true meaning of these letters is known only to Allah, and they serve as a reminder of the Qur'an's divine nature and the limitations of human understanding.
orig: حم

translation: 'Ain Sin Qaf.
interpretation: This verse consists of disjointed letters, the meaning of which is known only to Allah. Such letters appear at the beginning of several surahs in the Qur'an. While their exact meaning is not known, they are believed to serve as a way to attract the attention of the listener or reader, and to indicate that what follows is divine revelation from Allah. The letters may also have some mystical significance that is beyond human understanding. Ultimately, the meaning of these letters is part of the unseen knowledge that belongs to Allah alone.
orig: عسق

translation: Thus He reveals to you and to those before you - Allah, the Exalted in Might, the Wise.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the continuity of divine revelation throughout human history. It asserts that the message being revealed to Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) is the same as that which was revealed to the prophets before him, such as Abraham, Moses, and Jesus. This highlights the unity and consistency of God's message across time and reinforces the idea that Islam is not a new religion but a continuation and culmination of the same spiritual truth that has been conveyed by all the prophets. The verse also underscores two key attributes of God: His power (Al-'Azeez) and His wisdom (Al-Hakeem), indicating that the revelation is coming from a source of ultimate authority and knowledge.
orig: كذلك يوحي إليك وإلى الذين من قبلك الله العزيز الحكيم

translation: To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth, and He is the Most High, the Most Great.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute sovereignty and ownership of Allah over everything in the universe. It affirms that all things in the heavens and the earth belong to Him alone, and no one else has any share in this ownership. The verse also highlights two of Allah's sublime attributes: He is the Most High, indicating His exaltedness and supremacy above all of His creation, and He is the Most Great, signifying His infinite greatness and majesty that surpasses human comprehension. This verse serves as a reminder for believers to recognize and submit to Allah's ultimate authority and to humble themselves before His grandeur.
orig: له ما في السماوات وما في الأرض وهو العلي العظيم

translation: The heavens almost break apart from above them, and the angels exalt [Allah] with praise of their Lord and ask forgiveness for those on the earth. Unquestionably, it is Allah who is the Forgiving, the Merciful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the immense power and grandeur of Allah, to the extent that even the vast heavens are barely able to contain it. The angels, in their reverence and devotion, constantly praise Allah and seek forgiveness on behalf of humanity. This highlights Allah's infinite mercy and readiness to forgive those who seek His forgiveness, despite the enormity of His power and the comparatively small and insignificant nature of human beings. It serves as a reminder for humans to humble themselves before Allah, recognize His greatness, and seek His mercy and forgiveness.
orig: تكاد السماوات يتفطرن من فوقهن والملائكة يسبحون بحمد ربهم ويستغفرون لمن في الأرض ألا إن الله هو الغفور الرحيم

translation: And those who take as allies other than Him - Allah is [yet] Guardian over them; and you, [O Muhammad], are not over them a manager.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that those who take protectors or allies other than Allah are still under His guardianship and control. It also clarifies that Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) is not responsible for managing or overseeing those who choose to follow false deities or protectors. His role is to convey the message of Islam, but he has no power to force people to believe or control their actions. Ultimately, Allah is the Guardian and Overseer of all His creation, regardless of their beliefs or allegiances.
orig: والذين اتخذوا من دونه أولياء الله حفيظ عليهم وما أنت عليهم بوكيل

translation: And thus We have revealed to you an Arabic Qur'an that you may warn the Mother of Cities [Makkah] and those around it and warn of the Day of Assembly, about which there is no doubt. A party will be in Paradise and a party in the Blaze.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the universality and authority of the Qur'an as a divine revelation sent to Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) in the Arabic language. The primary purpose of this revelation is to warn the people of Makkah and its surroundings about the Day of Judgment, which is an inevitable reality. On that day, humanity will be divided into two groups: those who will enter Paradise as a reward for their faith and righteous deeds, and those who will be condemned to the Blazing Fire of Hell as a consequence of their disbelief and sins. The verse also establishes Makkah as the spiritual center of Islam, being the "Mother of Cities" and the location of the sacred Ka'bah.
orig: وكذلك أوحينا إليك قرآنا عربيا لتنذر أم القرى ومن حولها وتنذر يوم الجمع لا ريب فيه فريق في الجنة وفريق في السعير

translation: And if Allah willed, He could have made them [of] one religion, but He admits whom He wills into His mercy. And the wrongdoers have not any protector or helper.
interpretation: This verse highlights the concept of divine will and guidance in Islam. It suggests that while Allah could have created all of humanity as a single nation following one religion, He has instead chosen to guide whom He wills to the path of Islam and His mercy. Those who reject this guidance and choose to be wrongdoers will find themselves without any protector or helper, emphasizing the importance of submitting to Allah's will and following the guidance provided through His messengers and revelations. The verse also implies that the diversity of religions and beliefs among humans is part of Allah's greater plan and wisdom.
orig: ولو شاء الله لجعلهم أمة واحدة ولكن يدخل من يشاء في رحمته والظالمون ما لهم من ولي ولا نصير

translation: Or have they taken allies besides Him? But Allah - He is the [true] ally, and He gives life to the dead, and He is over all things competent.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute power and authority of Allah. It questions those who seek protection or support from anyone other than Allah, reminding them that Allah alone is the true protector and ally. The verse asserts that Allah has the power to give life to the dead, demonstrating His control over life and death. It also states that Allah is competent over all things, suggesting that He has the ability to do anything and that nothing is beyond His reach or power. The interpretation of this verse is that believers should put their trust and faith in Allah alone, as He is the only one who can truly protect and support them, and He has the ultimate power and control over all aspects of existence.
orig: أم اتخذوا من دونه أولياء فالله هو الولي وهو يحيي الموتى وهو على كل شيء قدير

translation: And in anything over which you disagree - its ruling is [to be referred] to Allah. [Say], "That is Allah, my Lord; upon Him I have relied, and to Him I turn back."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of referring all matters of disagreement back to Allah and His divine law. It reminds believers that ultimately, it is Allah who has the final say and authority over all things. The verse encourages complete trust and reliance upon Allah, seeking His guidance and turning to Him in repentance. It highlights the believer's submission to Allah's will and recognition of His sovereignty, particularly in times of dispute or differing opinions. By turning to Allah's judgment, one can find resolution and unity in faith.
orig: وما اختلفتم فيه من شيء فحكمه إلى الله ذلكم الله ربي عليه توكلت وإليه أنيب

translation: The Originator of the heavens and the earth. He has made for you from yourselves, mates, and among the cattle, mates; He multiplies you thereby. There is nothing like unto Him, and He is the Hearing, the Seeing.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's power and uniqueness as the Creator of the universe. It highlights that Allah has created pairs, both among humans and animals, to facilitate procreation and the continuation of life. The verse also stresses that there is nothing comparable to Allah in His attributes and essence. He is the All-Hearing and All-Seeing, which means that He is aware of all things, including the needs and actions of His creatures. This interpretation underscores the importance of recognizing Allah's sovereignty and uniqueness, while also appreciating His provisions and the systems He has put in place for the sustenance and growth of life on earth.
orig: فاطر السماوات والأرض جعل لكم من أنفسكم أزواجا ومن الأنعام أزواجا يذرؤكم فيه ليس كمثله شيء وهو السميع البصير

translation: To Him belong the keys of the heavens and the earth. He extends provision for whom He wills and restricts [it]. Indeed, He is, of all things, Knowing.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's absolute control and authority over the entire universe. He alone possesses the keys to the treasures of the heavens and the earth, which symbolize His power and dominion. Allah, in His infinite wisdom, gives sustenance and provisions to whomever He chooses, and He can also withhold or limit it according to His will. This highlights the fact that all blessings and bounties come from Allah, and He distributes them based on His divine knowledge and wisdom. The verse also underscores Allah's omniscience, affirming that He has complete knowledge of all things, including the needs and circumstances of His creatures. This understanding should instill humility, gratitude, and reliance upon Allah in the hearts of believers, knowing that their sustenance and well-being are ultimately in His hands.
orig: له مقاليد السماوات والأرض يبسط الرزق لمن يشاء ويقدر إنه بكل شيء عليم

translation: He has ordained for you of religion what He enjoined upon Noah and that which We have revealed to you, [O Muhammad], and what We enjoined upon Abraham and Moses and Jesus - to establish the religion and not be divided therein. Difficult for those who associate others with Allah is that to which you invite them. Allah chooses for Himself whom He wills and guides to Himself whoever turns back [to Him].
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the unity and continuity of the divine message throughout history. It states that the core principles of faith, such as monotheism and the establishment of religion, have been consistently enjoined upon all prophets, including Noah, Abraham, Moses, Jesus, and Muhammad. The verse also acknowledges the difficulty faced by those who associate partners with Allah in accepting this message of pure monotheism. It affirms that Allah guides those who sincerely turn to Him and chooses for Himself whom He wills, emphasizing His sovereignty and the importance of submitting to His will.
orig: شرع لكم من الدين ما وصى به نوحا والذي أوحينا إليك وما وصينا به إبراهيم وموسى وعيسى أن أقيموا الدين ولا تتفرقوا فيه كبر على المشركين ما تدعوهم إليه الله يجتبي إليه من يشاء ويهدي إليه من ينيب

translation: And they did not become divided until after knowledge had come to them - out of jealous animosity between themselves. And if not for a word that preceded from your Lord [postponing the penalty] until a specified time, it would have been concluded between them. And indeed, those who were granted inheritance of the Scripture after them are, concerning it, in disquieting doubt.
interpretation: This verse suggests that religious differences and sectarianism arose among people even after they received divine knowledge, out of mutual envy and rivalry. It implies that such divisions are not based on the truth of the message itself, but on human weaknesses and worldly motives. The verse also indicates that if it were not for God's predetermined decree to allow people respite until a set time, He would have already passed judgment between the disputing factions. Furthermore, it alludes to the fact that even those who inherited the Scripture after the original recipients have doubts and uncertainties about it, showing the persistence of human confusion in matters of faith despite access to revelation.
orig: وما تفرقوا إلا من بعد ما جاءهم العلم بغيا بينهم ولولا كلمة سبقت من ربك إلى أجل مسمى لقضي بينهم وإن الذين أورثوا الكتاب من بعدهم لفي شك منه مريب

translation: So to that [religion of Allah] invite, [O Muhammad], and remain on a right course as you are commanded and do not follow their inclinations but say, "I have believed in what Allah has revealed of the Qur'an, and I have been commanded to do justice among you. Allah is our Lord and your Lord. For us are our deeds, and for you your deeds. There is no [need for] argument between us and you. Allah will bring us together, and to Him is the [final] destination."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of remaining steadfast in one's faith and not being swayed by the desires or beliefs of others. The Prophet Muhammad is instructed to invite people to the religion of Islam and to remain on the right path, as commanded by Allah. He is told to declare his belief in the revelation of the Qur'an and to act with justice and fairness towards all people, regardless of their beliefs. The verse also highlights the concept of individual responsibility, stating that each person is accountable for their own actions and deeds. It concludes with the idea that ultimately, it is Allah who will bring all people together and judge them in the afterlife.
orig: فلذلك فادع واستقم كما أمرت ولا تتبع أهواءهم وقل آمنت بما أنزل الله من كتاب وأمرت لأعدل بينكم الله ربنا وربكم لنا أعمالنا ولكم أعمالكم لا حجة بيننا وبينكم الله يجمع بيننا وإليه المصير

translation: And those who argue concerning Allah after He has been responded to, their argument is invalid with their Lord, and upon them is [His] wrath, and for them is a severe punishment.
interpretation: This verse is referring to those who continue to argue against the truth of Allah's message even after it has been clearly conveyed to them and they have no valid argument against it. Their stubborn rejection and disputation is futile and baseless in the sight of Allah. As a result, they have earned Allah's anger and will face a severe punishment in the Hereafter for their obstinacy and refusal to accept the truth.
orig: والذين يحاجون في الله من بعد ما استجيب له حجتهم داحضة عند ربهم وعليهم غضب ولهم عذاب شديد

translation: It is Allah who has sent down the Book in truth and [also] the balance. And what will make you perceive? Perhaps the Hour is near.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that it is Allah who has revealed the Qur'an with truth and justice. The mention of the "balance" alongside the Book suggests that the Qur'an provides a standard of justice and guidance for mankind. The verse also reminds us that the Day of Judgment, or "the Hour", may be closer than we think. This serves as a warning for humans to be mindful of their actions and to follow the guidance provided in the Qur'an, as they will be held accountable for their deeds on the Day of Judgment, which could come at any moment without warning.
orig: الله الذي أنزل الكتاب بالحق والميزان وما يدريك لعل الساعة قريب

translation: Those who do not believe in it are impatient for it, but those who believe are fearful of it and know that it is the truth. Unquestionably, those who dispute concerning the Hour are in extreme error.
interpretation: This verse speaks to the contrasting attitudes between believers and disbelievers regarding the Day of Judgment (referred to as "the Hour"). The disbelievers are impatient for it to come, likely because they do not truly believe it will happen or fail to grasp its gravity. In contrast, the believers have a reverent fear of that Day, recognizing it as an inevitable reality. They understand the magnitude of the accounting that will take place and therefore strive to prepare for it through righteous deeds. The verse concludes by emphasizing that those who argue or doubt the coming of the Day of Judgment are in serious error and far astray from the truth. It serves as a warning to those who reject or question the reality of the afterlife, affirming that it is an absolute certainty that should be anticipated with a combination of hope and fear.
orig: يستعجل بها الذين لا يؤمنون بها والذين آمنوا مشفقون منها ويعلمون أنها الحق ألا إن الذين يمارون في الساعة لفي ضلال بعيد

translation: Allah is Subtle with His servants; He gives provisions to whom He wills. And He is the Powerful, the Almighty.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's kindness and benevolence towards His creation. He provides sustenance to whomever He chooses, in accordance with His infinite wisdom and mercy. It also highlights two of His divine attributes: "Al-Qawiyy" (the Powerful) and "Al-'Azeez" (the Almighty), indicating that Allah has the ultimate power and strength to bestow blessings upon His servants as He wills. The verse serves as a reminder for believers to trust in Allah's plan and have faith in His ability to provide for them, even in times of hardship or uncertainty.
orig: الله لطيف بعباده يرزق من يشاء وهو القوي العزيز
