translation: Whoever desires the harvest of the Hereafter - We increase for him in his harvest. And whoever desires the harvest of this world - We give him thereof, but there is not for him in the Hereafter any share.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of having the right intentions and priorities in life. Those who focus on the eternal rewards of the Hereafter and live their lives accordingly will be granted an increased share of blessings and goodness in their spiritual harvest. On the other hand, those who prioritize worldly gains and neglect their spiritual obligations may attain some temporary benefits in this life, but they will have no share of the eternal rewards in the Hereafter. It reminds believers to align their intentions and actions with seeking Allah's pleasure and the everlasting success of the Hereafter, rather than being solely consumed by the fleeting pursuits of this world.
orig: من كان يريد حرث الآخرة نزد له في حرثه ومن كان يريد حرث الدنيا نؤته منها وما له في الآخرة من نصيب

translation: Or have they partners who have ordained for them a religion to which Allah has not consented? But if not for the decisive word, it would have been concluded between them. And indeed, the wrongdoers will have a painful punishment.
interpretation: This verse questions whether the disbelievers have taken other deities besides Allah who have legislated for them a religion that Allah has not permitted. It suggests that if it were not for Allah's predetermined decree to delay the final judgment until the Day of Resurrection, He would have already passed judgment between the believers and the disbelievers. The verse affirms that those who wrong themselves by associating partners with Allah and following a false religion will face a severe and painful punishment in the Hereafter for their disbelief and disobedience to Allah's commands.
orig: أم لهم شركاء شرعوا لهم من الدين ما لم يأذن به الله ولولا كلمة الفصل لقضي بينهم وإن الظالمين لهم عذاب أليم

translation: You will see the wrongdoers fearful for what they have earned, and it will [certainly] befall them. And those who have believed and done righteous deeds will be in the flowering meadows of the gardens; they will have whatever they wish with their Lord. That is what is the great bounty.
interpretation: This verse highlights the stark contrast between the fate of the wrongdoers and the believers on the Day of Judgment. The wrongdoers will be in a state of fear and anxiety due to their misdeeds, knowing that the consequences of their actions will soon befall them. On the other hand, the believers who have done righteous deeds will be in a state of bliss and contentment in the gardens of Paradise. They will have whatever they desire from their Lord, indicating the immense blessings and rewards that await them. This verse emphasizes the importance of faith and righteous actions, as they lead to the ultimate success and the great bounty in the Hereafter.
orig: ترى الظالمين مشفقين مما كسبوا وهو واقع بهم والذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات في روضات الجنات لهم ما يشاءون عند ربهم ذلك هو الفضل الكبير

translation: It is that of which Allah gives good tidings to His servants who believe and do righteous deeds. Say, [O Muhammad], "I do not ask you for this message any payment [but] only good will through kinship." And whoever commits a good deed - We will increase for him good therein. Indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Appreciative.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) did not seek any worldly gain or payment for conveying the message of Islam. His only request was for people to show love and kindness towards his family and relatives. The verse also highlights the immense rewards that Allah has promised for those who believe and do good deeds. It encourages people to perform righteous actions, as Allah will multiply the rewards for each good deed. The verse concludes by affirming Allah's attributes of forgiveness and appreciation, reminding us that He is ever ready to forgive our sins and appreciates even the smallest acts of goodness from His servants.
orig: ذلك الذي يبشر الله عباده الذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات قل لا أسألكم عليه أجرا إلا المودة في القربى ومن يقترف حسنة نزد له فيها حسنا إن الله غفور شكور

translation: Or do they say, "He has invented about Allah a lie"? But if Allah willed, He could seal over your heart. And Allah eliminates falsehood and establishes the truth by His words. Indeed, He is Knowing of that within the breasts.
interpretation: This verse addresses the accusation made by the disbelievers that the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) had fabricated lies about Allah. It asserts that if Allah had willed, He could have sealed the Prophet's heart, preventing him from receiving divine revelation. However, Allah's will is to eliminate falsehood and establish the truth through His words and revelations. The verse emphasizes that Allah is fully aware of what lies within the hearts of people, their intentions, and their innermost thoughts. It serves as a reminder that Allah's knowledge encompasses all things and that He will always support and protect the truth while eradicating falsehood.
orig: أم يقولون افترى على الله كذبا فإن يشإ الله يختم على قلبك ويمح الله الباطل ويحق الحق بكلماته إنه عليم بذات الصدور

translation: And it is He who accepts repentance from His servants and pardons misdeeds, and He knows what you do.
interpretation: This verse highlights Allah's infinite mercy and forgiveness. It emphasizes that Allah is always ready to accept sincere repentance from His servants, no matter how grave their sins may be. He not only forgives their misdeeds but also erases the consequences of those sins. The verse also reminds us that Allah is all-knowing and is fully aware of our actions, intentions, and inner thoughts. This should motivate us to constantly strive for self-improvement, seek Allah's forgiveness, and be mindful of our deeds, knowing that nothing escapes His knowledge.
orig: وهو الذي يقبل التوبة عن عباده ويعفو عن السيئات ويعلم ما تفعلون

translation: And He answers [the supplication of] those who have believed and done righteous deeds and increases [for] them from His bounty. But the disbelievers will have a severe punishment.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of faith and good deeds in attaining Allah's favor and blessings. Those who sincerely believe in Allah and perform righteous actions will have their prayers answered and will be granted an increase in Allah's bounty and generosity. On the other hand, those who reject faith and disbelieve in Allah will face severe punishment in the Hereafter. This verse serves as an encouragement for believers to remain steadfast in their faith and to continuously strive for righteousness, while also serving as a warning for disbelievers about the consequences of their actions.
orig: ويستجيب الذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات ويزيدهم من فضله والكافرون لهم عذاب شديد

translation: And if Allah were to extend the provision for His servants, they would surely rebel in the earth; but He sends down in due measure as He wills. Indeed, He is All-Aware and All-Seeing of His servants.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah, in His infinite wisdom, provides for His servants in a measured and controlled way. If He were to grant them an overabundance of wealth and provisions, it would lead to transgression and rebellion on earth. Humans, if left unchecked, may become arrogant and forget their purpose and servitude to Allah. Therefore, Allah sends down sustenance in due measure, according to His will and knowledge of what is best for each individual. This underscores Allah's perfect awareness and insight into the needs, capacities, and tendencies of His servants. It is a reminder for humans to trust in Allah's wisdom and be content with what He provides, knowing that He is All-Aware and All-Seeing of their circumstances and what is ultimately best for them in this life and the hereafter.
orig: ولو بسط الله الرزق لعباده لبغوا في الأرض ولكن ينزل بقدر ما يشاء إنه بعباده خبير بصير

translation: And it is He who sends down the rain after they had despaired and spreads His mercy. And He is the Protector, the Praiseworthy.
interpretation: This verse highlights Allah's infinite mercy and power. Even when people lose hope and think there is no chance of rain, Allah can send down rain and revive the earth, spreading His blessings and mercy. This reminds us to never despair of Allah's mercy, for He is our Protector and Guardian who is worthy of all praise. It encourages having faith and trust in Allah's plan and timing, knowing that He can bring relief and grace even in seemingly hopeless situations. The verse emphasizes Allah's attributes of being the Protector who looks after His creation, and the Praiseworthy who is deserving of gratitude and praise for all His favors and blessings.
orig: وهو الذي ينزل الغيث من بعد ما قنطوا وينشر رحمته وهو الولي الحميد

translation: And of His signs is the creation of the heavens and the earth and what He has dispersed throughout them of creatures. And He, for gathering them when He wills, is competent.
interpretation: This verse reminds us of Allah's immense power and wisdom in creating the vast universe and all the living beings within it. It emphasizes that the existence of such a diverse and intricate creation is a clear sign of Allah's existence and His ability to do as He wills. The verse also points out that just as Allah has the power to create and disperse these creatures throughout the heavens and the earth, He is equally capable of gathering them all together at a time of His choosing, such as on the Day of Judgment. This serves as a reminder for humans to be mindful of their actions and to recognize Allah's absolute authority and control over all things.
orig: ومن آياته خلق السماوات والأرض وما بث فيهما من دابة وهو على جمعهم إذا يشاء قدير

translation: And whatever misfortune befalls you, it is because of what your hands have earned. And He pardons much.
interpretation: This verse conveys that the difficulties and trials people face in life are often the result of their own actions and misdeeds. It emphasizes the concept of personal responsibility, suggesting that individuals must be accountable for the consequences of their choices. However, the verse also highlights God's immense mercy and forgiveness, indicating that He overlooks and pardons many of our transgressions. This interpretation encourages introspection, repentance, and seeking forgiveness while acknowledging God's compassion and willingness to forgive those who sincerely turn to Him.
orig: وما أصابكم من مصيبة فبما كسبت أيديكم ويعفو عن كثير

translation: And you will not cause failure [to Allah] upon the earth. And you have not besides Allah any protector or helper.
interpretation: This verse reminds us that no matter how powerful or influential we may think we are, we can never overcome or defeat Allah's will on earth. We are ultimately dependent on Him and have no true protector or helper besides Him. It emphasizes the complete sovereignty of Allah and the futility of thinking that we can act independently of His will or escape the consequences of our actions. The verse encourages humility, submission to Allah, and recognition that our success lies in aligning ourselves with His guidance and seeking His support and protection.
orig: وما أنتم بمعجزين في الأرض وما لكم من دون الله من ولي ولا نصير

translation: And among His signs are the ships in the sea, like mountains.
interpretation: This verse draws our attention to the majestic ships that sail the seas, comparing them to mountains in their grandeur and size. It is a reminder of Allah's power and creativity, as these massive vessels are able to navigate the vast oceans by His command and grace. The verse also suggests that the ability to build and sail ships is a blessing and a sign of Allah's favor upon humankind, enabling them to traverse great distances, engage in trade, and explore the world. Moreover, the stability and strength of the ships amidst the unpredictable and sometimes treacherous conditions of the sea is a metaphor for the believer's steadfastness and reliance upon Allah in the face of life's challenges and uncertainties.
orig: ومن آياته الجوار في البحر كالأعلام

translation: If He willed, He could still the wind, and they would remain motionless on its surface. Indeed in that are signs for everyone patient and grateful.
interpretation: This verse points to the power and control of Allah over His creation. The wind, which propels the ships across the sea, is under His command. If He so willed, He could cause the wind to become still, leaving the ships motionless on the surface of the water. This is a reminder for those who are patient in times of difficulty and grateful for Allah's blessings. It encourages us to recognize and appreciate the signs of Allah's power and mercy in the world around us, and to respond with patience and gratitude in all circumstances.
orig: إن يشأ يسكن الريح فيظللن رواكد على ظهره إن في ذلك لآيات لكل صبار شكور

translation: Or that He may destroy them for what they have earned; and He pardons much.
interpretation: This verse highlights the power and mercy of Allah. It suggests that Allah has the ability to destroy people for their misdeeds and sins, as they have earned such punishment through their actions. However, the verse also emphasizes Allah's immense capacity for forgiveness, stating that He pardons much. This interpretation underscores the balance between divine justice and mercy in Islamic theology. It serves as a reminder that while our actions have consequences, Allah's forgiveness is vast for those who seek it sincerely. The verse encourages introspection, repentance, and the pursuit of Allah's mercy, while acknowledging that ultimate judgment lies with Him alone.
orig: أو يوبقهن بما كسبوا ويعف عن كثير

translation: And those who dispute Our verses know that there is no place of refuge for them.
interpretation: This verse is a stern warning to those who argue against or reject the clear signs and revelations of Allah. It emphasizes that they will ultimately have no escape or refuge from the consequences of their disbelief and defiance. They will face the inescapable judgment of Allah, and there will be no place to hide or seek protection from His punishment. This highlights the gravity of rejecting Allah's message and the importance of accepting and submitting to His guidance while one has the opportunity in this life.
orig: ويعلم الذين يجادلون في آياتنا ما لهم من محيص

translation: So whatever you have been given is but [for] enjoyment of the worldly life, but what is with Allah is better and more lasting for those who have believed and upon their Lord rely.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the temporary and fleeting nature of worldly possessions and pleasures, contrasting them with the eternal rewards that Allah has prepared for the believers in the Hereafter. It encourages the believers to focus on their relationship with Allah and to trust in Him, rather than being distracted by the allure of worldly gains. The verse reminds us that the ultimate satisfaction and happiness lie in seeking Allah's pleasure and striving for His rewards, which are far superior to anything this world can offer.
orig: فما أوتيتم من شيء فمتاع الحياة الدنيا وما عند الله خير وأبقى للذين آمنوا وعلى ربهم يتوكلون

translation: And those who avoid the major sins and immoralities, and when they are angry, they forgive.
interpretation: This verse highlights the virtuous qualities of the believers who stay away from major sins and shameful deeds. It also emphasizes the importance of forgiveness, especially when one is angry or wronged by others. The ability to forgive despite anger is a sign of strength, self-control, and spiritual maturity. This verse encourages Muslims to cultivate the habit of forgiveness and to control their anger, as these are essential characteristics of the righteous believers who seek Allah's pleasure and reward in the Hereafter.
orig: والذين يجتنبون كبائر الإثم والفواحش وإذا ما غضبوا هم يغفرون

translation: And those who have responded to their lord and established prayer and whose affair is [determined by] consultation among themselves, and from what We have provided them, they spend.
interpretation: This verse highlights some of the key characteristics of the believers. They are those who respond to Allah's call and establish regular prayer, demonstrating their devotion and submission to Him. Moreover, they conduct their affairs through mutual consultation, indicating the importance of seeking advice, considering different perspectives, and reaching decisions collectively. This promotes unity, wisdom, and justice within the community. Additionally, the believers are generous with the provisions that Allah has granted them, willing to spend in His cause and help those in need. This reflects their gratitude, selflessness, and concern for the welfare of others. Ultimately, this verse emphasizes that true believers are those who maintain a strong connection with Allah, foster a spirit of cooperation and consultation, and are actively engaged in acts of goodness and charity.
orig: والذين استجابوا لربهم وأقاموا الصلاة وأمرهم شورى بينهم ومما رزقناهم ينفقون

translation: And those who, when tyranny strikes them, they defend themselves.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the right of people to resist oppression and injustice. It suggests that it is praiseworthy to stand up against tyranny and defend one's rights and dignity. The Qur'an does not condone passivity in the face of oppression, but rather encourages believers to take action to protect themselves and fight against injustice in a righteous manner. This verse highlights the importance of courage, self-respect, and the active pursuit of justice in Islamic teachings.
orig: والذين إذا أصابهم البغي هم ينتصرون

translation: The recompense for an injury is an injury equal thereto (in degree): but if a person forgives and makes reconciliation, his reward is due from Allah: for (Allah) loveth not those who do wrong.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the principle of justice and equality in retaliation, stating that the punishment for a wrong should be proportionate to the offense committed. However, it also encourages forgiveness and reconciliation, stating that those who choose to forgive and make peace will be rewarded by Allah. The verse ends with a reminder that Allah does not love those who transgress the limits and commit injustice, highlighting the importance of maintaining balance and fairness in all dealings.
orig: وجزاء سيئة سيئة مثلها فمن عفا وأصلح فأجره على الله إنه لا يحب الظالمين

translation: And those who defend themselves after they were wronged - there is no blame on them.
interpretation: This verse affirms the right of the oppressed to seek justice and defend themselves against their oppressors. It indicates that those who have been wronged are not to be blamed or held accountable for taking action to protect their rights and dignity. The Qur'an upholds the principle of justice and allows the wronged party to take necessary measures to rectify the injustice they have suffered, as long as they do not transgress the limits set by Allah. This verse emphasizes the importance of standing up against oppression and tyranny, and seeking to establish fairness and equity in society.
orig: ولمن انتصر بعد ظلمه فأولئك ما عليهم من سبيل

translation: The cause [for blame] is only upon those who wrong the people and tyrannize upon the earth without right. Those will have a painful punishment.
interpretation: This verse is a warning to those who oppress others and spread corruption on earth without any justification. It emphasizes that such people, who violate the rights of others and cause harm and injustice, will face a severe and painful punishment from Allah in the Hereafter. The verse highlights the gravity of the sin of oppression and tyranny, and serves as a reminder for people to be just, compassionate, and mindful of the rights of others in order to avoid incurring Allah's wrath and punishment.
orig: إنما السبيل على الذين يظلمون الناس ويبغون في الأرض بغير الحق أولئك لهم عذاب أليم

translation: And whoever is patient and forgives - indeed, that is of the matters [requiring] determination.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of patience and forgiveness in the face of adversity or wrongdoing. It suggests that exercising these qualities requires strong willpower and resolve, as they are not always easy to practice. The verse implies that those who are able to remain patient and forgiving, even in difficult circumstances, demonstrate a commendable level of determination and strength of character. It encourages believers to strive for these virtues, as they are considered among the most praiseworthy and noble qualities in Islamic teachings.
orig: ولمن صبر وغفر إن ذلك لمن عزم الأمور

translation: And whoever Allah leaves astray - for him there is no protector beyond Him. And you will see the wrongdoers, when they see the punishment, saying, "Is there for return [to the former world] any way?"
interpretation: This verse highlights the fate of those who have gone astray and earned Allah's displeasure. It emphasizes that once Allah has decreed someone to be misguided, no one can guide them or protect them from the consequences of their actions. The verse also depicts the despair and hopelessness of the wrongdoers when they face the punishment in the Hereafter. They will wish for a second chance to return to the world and make amends, but it will be too late. This serves as a reminder for mankind to stay on the right path and seek Allah's guidance before it is too late, as there will be no opportunity for redemption once the punishment is witnessed.
orig: ومن يضلل الله فما له من ولي من بعده وترى الظالمين لما رأوا العذاب يقولون هل إلى مرد من سبيل

translation: And you will see them being exposed to it [i.e., the Fire], humbled from humiliation, looking with [a] stolen glance. And those who had believed will say, "Indeed, the [true] losers are the ones who lost themselves and their families on the Day of Resurrection. Unquestionably, the wrongdoers are in an enduring punishment."
interpretation: This verse describes the fate of the disbelievers on the Day of Judgment. They will be brought before the Fire, humbled and disgraced, looking at it furtively in fear. The believers will then realize that the true losers are those who have lost themselves and their families due to their disbelief and wrongdoings. The verse emphasizes that the wrongdoers will suffer an everlasting punishment in the Hereafter as a consequence of their actions in this world.
orig: وتراهم يعرضون عليها خاشعين من الذل ينظرون من طرف خفي وقال الذين آمنوا إن الخاسرين الذين خسروا أنفسهم وأهليهم يوم القيامة ألا إن الظالمين في عذاب مقيم

translation: And they had no allies to help them other than Allah. And whoever Allah leaves astray - for him there is no way.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the complete power and control of Allah over all affairs. It states that those whom Allah has left astray and misguided have no protectors or helpers besides Him. No one can guide them or show them the right path if Allah Himself has decreed for them to be misguided. It highlights the concept of divine decree (qadar) in Islam, where everything happens by the will and permission of Allah. The verse also serves as a warning to those who turn away from Allah's guidance, that they will have no escape or means of salvation except through returning to Allah and seeking His mercy and guidance.
orig: وما كان لهم من أولياء ينصرونهم من دون الله ومن يضلل الله فما له من سبيل

translation: Respond to your Lord before a Day comes from Allah of which there is no repelling. No refuge will you have that day, nor for you will there be any denial.
interpretation: This verse is a call to mankind to turn to Allah and respond to His message before it is too late. It warns that a Day will come when there will be no turning back, no refuge, and no denial of the truth. It emphasizes the urgency and importance of heeding Allah's call and following His guidance in this life, before the Day of Judgment arrives. The verse reminds us that on that Day, there will be no escape from the consequences of our actions and no opportunity for excuses or denials. It is a powerful reminder of the fleeting nature of this world and the eternal significance of the Hereafter.
orig: استجيبوا لربكم من قبل أن يأتي يوم لا مرد له من الله ما لكم من ملجإ يومئذ وما لكم من نكير

translation: But if they turn away, We have not sent you as a guardian over them. Your duty is only to convey the message. And indeed, when We let man taste mercy from Us, he rejoices in it; but if evil befalls them for what their hands have put forth, then indeed, man is ungrateful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the Prophet's role is to deliver the message of Islam, not to force people to accept it. It also highlights the fickle nature of human beings, who are quick to rejoice in God's blessings but turn ungrateful when faced with adversity, failing to recognize that their own actions may have contributed to their misfortune. The verse serves as a reminder to be steadfast in faith and to trust in God's plan, even in the face of rejection or hardship.
orig: فإن أعرضوا فما أرسلناك عليهم حفيظا إن عليك إلا البلاغ وإنا إذا أذقنا الإنسان منا رحمة فرح بها وإن تصبهم سيئة بما قدمت أيديهم فإن الإنسان كفور

translation: To Allah belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth; He creates what he wills. He gives to whom He wills female [children], and He gives to whom He wills males.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's absolute power and sovereignty over the entire universe. It affirms that Allah alone has the authority to create and grant offspring according to His divine will and wisdom. He bestows daughters or sons upon whomever He chooses, and this is a matter of His divine prerogative. The verse underscores the belief that the gender of a child is determined by Allah's decree and not by human preference or intervention. It serves as a reminder for believers to accept Allah's will with contentment and gratitude, recognizing that every child, regardless of gender, is a precious gift from Allah.
orig: لله ملك السماوات والأرض يخلق ما يشاء يهب لمن يشاء إناثا ويهب لمن يشاء الذكور

translation: Or He marries them [in the wombs], males and females, and He renders whom He wills barren. Indeed, He is Knowing and Competent.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's power and knowledge in determining the outcome of human reproduction. He alone decides whether a couple will have male or female children, or whether they will remain childless. This highlights the fact that everything happens according to His will and wisdom, and that He has the ability to grant or withhold offspring as He sees fit. It also serves as a reminder to humans that they have no control over such matters and should submit to Allah's decree, trusting in His knowledge and power.
orig: أو يزوجهم ذكرانا وإناثا ويجعل من يشاء عقيما إنه عليم قدير

translation: And it is not for any human being that Allah should speak to him except by revelation or from behind a partition or that He sends a messenger to reveal, by His permission, what He wills. Indeed, He is Most High and Wise.
interpretation: This verse establishes the fundamental principle that Allah does not speak directly to human beings. Rather, Allah communicates His message through three main methods: 1) Direct revelation to the heart and mind of the recipient, as was the case with the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) when receiving the Qur'an, 2) Speaking from behind a veil or barrier, as Allah spoke to Moses, or 3) Sending an angel messenger, such as Gabriel, to convey Allah's words to His chosen prophets and messengers who then deliver the divine message to humanity. This highlights Allah's transcendence and the special status of those selected to receive divine revelation, emphasizing that it is by Allah's will and permission alone. The verse also affirms Allah's wisdom in choosing these methods of communication, which suit the lofty nature of the divine message and the limited capacity of human beings to receive it directly.
orig: وما كان لبشر أن يكلمه الله إلا وحيا أو من وراء حجاب أو يرسل رسولا فيوحي بإذنه ما يشاء إنه علي حكيم

translation: And thus We have sent to you (O Muhammad) Ruhan (an Inspiration, and a Mercy) of Our Command. You knew not what is the Book, nor what is Faith? But We have made it (this Quran) a light wherewith We guide whosoever of Our slaves We will. And verily, you (O Muhammad) are indeed guiding (mankind) to the Straight Path (i.e. Allah's religion of Islamic Monotheism).
interpretation: This verse highlights that the Quran was revealed to Prophet Muhammad as a divine inspiration and mercy from Allah. Prior to this revelation, the Prophet had no knowledge of the divine scriptures or the true essence of faith. However, Allah made the Quran a guiding light through which He guides whomever He wills among His servants to the straight path of Islam. The verse also affirms that Prophet Muhammad, through the Quranic message, is undoubtedly guiding humanity towards the right way that pleases Allah.
orig: وكذلك أوحينا إليك روحا من أمرنا ما كنت تدري ما الكتاب ولا الإيمان ولكن جعلناه نورا نهدي به من نشاء من عبادنا وإنك لتهدي إلى صراط مستقيم

translation: The path of Allah, to whom belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth. Unquestionably, to Allah do [all] matters evolve.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that everything in the universe belongs to Allah and follows His ordained path or way (siraat). It reminds us that all affairs and matters ultimately return to Allah, the Supreme Controller and Master of all things. It underscores the idea of Allah's ownership, authority and the ultimate destination of all creation being towards Him. The verse encourages the believer to align their own path and actions with the "siraat" of Allah, as that is the only path of success, leading to Him.
orig: صراط الله الذي له ما في السماوات وما في الأرض ألا إلى الله تصير الأمور

translation: Ha, Meem.
interpretation: This verse consists of two Arabic letters, "Ha" and "Meem". Such combinations of letters are known as "Al-Muqatta'at" or "The Disjoined Letters", and they appear at the beginning of several chapters in the Qur'an. The exact meaning and purpose of these letters are not explicitly mentioned in the Qur'an or Hadith. Many scholars believe that these letters hold a divine secret known only to Allah, while others have attempted to interpret their significance. One interpretation is that these letters serve as a reminder of the miraculous nature of the Qur'an and its inimitability, as it challenges the Arabs, known for their mastery of the language, to produce something similar to the Qur'an using the same letters and language.
orig: حم

translation: By the clear Book.
interpretation: This verse is an oath taken by Allah swearing by the clear Qur'an, which is described as "clear" because its verses are clear in their meaning and guidance. The fact that Allah swears by the Qur'an is an indication of its great status and the truth it contains. It affirms that the Qur'an is the ultimate source of guidance for humanity, providing clear evidence and arguments for the Oneness of Allah and the truthfulness of His message conveyed through Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him). The Qur'an is a light that removes doubts and establishes certainty in the hearts of the believers.
orig: والكتاب المبين

translation: Indeed, We have made it an Arabic Quran so that you may understand.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah has revealed the Qur'an in the Arabic language to make it comprehensible for the Arabs, who were the initial recipients of the divine message. The use of the Arabic language facilitates understanding the Qur'an's teachings, as it is the language spoken by the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and his people. By revealing the Qur'an in Arabic, Allah has made it easier for people to grasp its meaning, reflect upon its content, and apply its guidance in their lives. This verse also implies that the Qur'an's message is universal and can be understood by people of all times and places, provided they make an effort to comprehend its teachings.
orig: إنا جعلناه قرآنا عربيا لعلكم تعقلون

translation: And indeed it is, in the Mother of the Book with Us, exalted and full of wisdom.
interpretation: This verse refers to the Qur'an itself, affirming that its original source, the "Mother of the Book" (Umm al-Kitab), is with Allah. This source is described as "exalted" ('Aliy), meaning it holds a high and noble status, and "full of wisdom" (Hakeem), meaning that its contents are full of wisdom and truth. This verse emphasizes the divine nature of the Qur'an, its preservation with Allah, and its status as a source of guidance and wisdom for humanity.
orig: وإنه في أم الكتاب لدينا لعلي حكيم

translation: Then should We turn away the message from you because you are a transgressing people?
interpretation: This verse is a rhetorical question from Allah, asking if He should withhold His guidance and revelation from mankind because of their excessive sins and transgressions. It implies that Allah's mercy and guidance continue to be offered despite the wrongdoings of people. The verse also serves as a warning that if people persist in their disobedience and ingratitude, they may be deprived of divine guidance. It encourages introspection and repentance, reminding humans of the consequences of their actions while emphasizing Allah's forbearance and willingness to guide those who seek His path.
orig: أفنضرب عنكم الذكر صفحا أن كنتم قوما مسرفين

translation: And how many a prophet We sent among the former peoples.
interpretation: This verse highlights the fact that Allah has sent numerous prophets to guide humanity throughout history, even before the time of Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him). It serves as a reminder that the message of Islam is not new, but rather a continuation and culmination of the teachings of all the prophets who came before. The verse also implies that just as earlier nations were held accountable for their response to the prophets sent to them, people in the present will also be held responsible for how they receive and follow the final prophet and his message. It emphasizes the universality and continuity of Allah's guidance to mankind.
orig: وكم أرسلنا من نبي في الأولين

translation: And no messenger would come to them except that they ridiculed him.
interpretation: This verse highlights the stubborn and arrogant nature of those who reject the divine message brought by the prophets. Despite the clear signs and wisdom conveyed by the messengers, the disbelievers mock and ridicule them, refusing to acknowledge the truth. This behavior is a recurring pattern throughout history, showing the persistence of human pride and the difficulty in accepting guidance that challenges one's existing beliefs and way of life. The verse serves as a reminder that the prophets faced significant challenges and opposition in delivering God's message, and that the rejection of faith often stems from deep-seated psychological and social factors rather than a lack of evidence or reasoning.
orig: وما يأتيهم من نبي إلا كانوا به يستهزئون

translation: So We destroyed [those] stronger than them in power, and the example of the former peoples has preceded.
interpretation: This verse serves as a reminder that no matter how powerful or mighty a nation or people may seem, they are not invincible. Allah has the power to destroy even the strongest of civilizations, just as He has done with those who came before. It is a warning to not be arrogant or believe oneself to be above the consequences of one's actions, for the fate of previous nations serves as a lesson for those who come after. Ultimately, it is a call to humility and recognition of Allah's supreme power and authority over all of creation.
orig: فأهلكنا أشد منهم بطشا ومضى مثل الأولين

translation: If you ask them who created the heavens and the earth, they will surely say: "The All-Mighty, the All-Knowing created them."
interpretation: This verse points to the innate belief in a Supreme Creator that is ingrained in human nature, even among those who outwardly reject faith. Despite their disbelief, when directly questioned about the origin of the universe, they instinctively acknowledge that it must have been created by a Being of immense power and knowledge. This highlights the inherent contradiction in denying God while simultaneously recognizing the signs of His existence and attributes manifest in the creation. The verse serves as a reminder that deep down, every soul has the capacity to recognize and submit to its Creator, and that disbelief often stems from arrogance, stubbornness, or worldly distractions rather than a genuine lack of awareness of God's presence.
orig: ولئن سألتهم من خلق السماوات والأرض ليقولن خلقهن العزيز العليم

translation: The One Who has made for you the earth a bed, and made for you in it paths, so that you may be guided.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's benevolence and mercy towards His creation. He has prepared the earth for human habitation, making it a comfortable place to live and providing pathways for people to travel and explore. The paths mentioned can be understood both literally, as roads and trails, and metaphorically, as the guidance provided by Allah through His messengers and revelations. The verse encourages people to reflect upon these blessings and to seek Allah's guidance in their lives, so that they may stay on the right path and attain success in this world and the hereafter.
orig: الذي جعل لكم الأرض مهدا وجعل لكم فيها سبلا لعلكم تهتدون

translation: And who sends down rain from the sky in measured amounts, and We revive thereby a dead land - thus will you be brought forth -
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's power and control over the natural world. The rain that falls from the sky is not random or arbitrary, but is sent down in precise quantities according to Allah's will. This rain has the power to bring life to dead and barren land, causing plants to grow and the earth to become green and fertile once again. The revival of dead land through rain is used as an analogy for the resurrection of human beings on the Day of Judgment. Just as Allah can bring dead land back to life, He can also bring human beings back to life after death for the final reckoning. This verse is a reminder of Allah's ultimate power over life and death, and the inevitability of the resurrection and judgment in the Hereafter.
orig: والذي نزل من السماء ماء بقدر فأنشرنا به بلدة ميتا كذلك تخرجون

translation: And who created all the pairs, and made for you of the ships and the cattle on which you ride
interpretation: This verse points to the creative power and wisdom of Allah, who has created all things in pairs, such as male and female, positive and negative, light and darkness, etc. It also highlights Allah's favor upon humanity by providing them with means of transportation, both on water (ships) and land (cattle). These blessings demonstrate Allah's care and provision for His creation, enabling them to traverse distances and carry out their affairs with ease. The verse invites reflection on the signs of Allah's creation and encourages gratitude for His countless bounties.
orig: والذي خلق الأزواج كلها وجعل لكم من الفلك والأنعام ما تركبون

translation: That you may sit firmly on their backs, and then may remember the Favor of your Lord when you sit firmly on them, and say: "Glory to Him who has subjected this to us, and we could never have [subdued it] ourselves."
interpretation: This verse is a reminder for us to be grateful for the blessings that Allah has bestowed upon us, such as the ability to tame and use animals for transportation. It encourages us to acknowledge and remember Allah's favor upon us whenever we ride on the backs of these animals, recognizing that it is only by His grace and power that we are able to subdue them for our benefit. The verse also emphasizes the importance of humility and acknowledging our own limitations, as we could never have achieved this on our own without Allah's help and guidance.
orig: لتستووا على ظهوره ثم تذكروا نعمة ربكم إذا استويتم عليه وتقولوا سبحان الذي سخر لنا هذا وما كنا له مقرنين

translation: And indeed to our Lord we will return.
interpretation: This verse reminds us that our ultimate destination is back to Allah, our Creator. It emphasizes the temporary nature of this worldly life and that we will all face the reality of death and return to our Lord for judgment. This realization should inspire us to live righteously, fulfill our purpose, and prepare for the eternal life in the Hereafter. It also brings comfort during trials and hardships, knowing that this world is not our final abode and that our struggles will come to an end as we return to Allah's mercy and justice.
orig: وإنا إلى ربنا لمنقلبون

translation: And they have attributed to Him a portion of His servants. Indeed, man is clearly ungrateful.
interpretation: This verse is a criticism of those who associate partners with Allah or attribute divine qualities to His creation. It highlights the ingratitude of human beings who, despite being created by Allah and sustained by His blessings, still ascribe divinity to others. The verse emphasizes the clear nature of this ingratitude, as it is an open and obvious form of disbelief. It serves as a reminder for people to acknowledge the oneness of Allah and to be grateful for His favors, rather than attributing His qualities or worship to anyone or anything else.
orig: وجعلوا له من عباده جزءا إن الإنسان لكفور مبين

translation: Or has He taken daughters out of what He has created, and chosen sons for you?
interpretation: This verse is questioning the belief of some people who attributed daughters to Allah while desiring sons for themselves. It highlights the contradiction and injustice in such thinking. The rhetorical question implies that Allah does not have offspring, and that assigning daughters to Him while preferring sons for oneself is baseless and irrational. It challenges the notion of attributing human characteristics or family relations to the Divine, emphasizing His transcendence beyond such limitations or preferences.
orig: أم اتخذ مما يخلق بنات وأصفاكم بالبنين

translation: And when one of them is given good tidings of that which he attributes to the Most Merciful in comparison, his face becomes dark, and he suppresses grief.
interpretation: This verse is referring to the pagan Arabs who would attribute daughters to Allah, while considering it a disgrace to have daughters themselves. When one of them was given the news of the birth of a daughter, his face would darken with gloom and he would be filled with suppressed anger and grief, considering it a humiliation. This highlights their hypocrisy in attributing to Allah what they disliked for themselves, and their ingratitude for Allah's blessings and gifts, be it a son or a daughter. It also emphasizes the need for treating sons and daughters with equal love and care, as they are all blessings from Allah.
orig: وإذا بشر أحدهم بما ضرب للرحمن مثلا ظل وجهه مسودا وهو كظيم

translation: Is one brought up in ornaments, and who in dispute cannot make himself clear,
interpretation: This verse is questioning the notion of attributing daughters to Allah. It points out the absurdity of the idea by highlighting that in the society of that time, daughters were seen as a liability and a source of shame, being brought up in adornments and unable to eloquently express themselves in disputes. The rhetorical question implies that it would be illogical and unbefitting to ascribe such a child to Allah, emphasizing the pure transcendence of the Divine.
orig: أومن ينشأ في الحلية وهو في الخصام غير مبين

translation: And they have made the angels, who are servants of the Most Merciful, females. Did they witness their creation? Their testimony will be recorded, and they will be questioned.
interpretation: This verse criticizes the pre-Islamic Arab belief that angels were females and daughters of Allah. It questions whether those who hold this belief witnessed the creation of the angels to make such a claim. The verse emphasizes that the angels are servants of Allah, not His offspring. It also warns that those who make this false claim will be held accountable for their testimony on the Day of Judgment, when they will be questioned about the basis of their belief. This highlights the importance of basing one's beliefs on divine revelation and not on mere speculation or cultural traditions.
orig: وجعلوا الملائكة الذين هم عباد الرحمن إناثا أشهدوا خلقهم ستكتب شهادتهم ويسألون

translation: And they said, "If the Most Merciful had willed, we would not have worshipped them." They have of that no knowledge. They are not but falsifying.
interpretation: This verse is addressing the polytheists who justified their worship of idols by claiming that if Allah had not approved of their idolatry, He would have prevented them from worshipping these false gods. However, their claim is baseless and stems from ignorance. They have no proof or knowledge to support their assertion. In reality, they are merely making false assumptions and lying to themselves and others to validate their misguided beliefs and practices. The verse highlights the fact that people often try to rationalize their wrongdoings by attributing them to the will of Allah, without any evidence or genuine understanding of His message.
orig: وقالوا لو شاء الرحمن ما عبدناهم ما لهم بذلك من علم إن هم إلا يخرصون

translation: Or have We given them a book before it to which they are holding fast?
interpretation: This verse is questioning whether those who reject the Qur'an have any divine scripture from before that they can refer to as justification for their disbelief. It implies that they do not have any such book and are merely following their own whims and desires rather than divine guidance. The verse suggests that the Qur'an is the only authentic divine scripture and that clinging to it is the path of truth and righteousness.
orig: أم آتيناهم كتابا من قبله فهم به مستمسكون

translation: But they say, "Indeed, we found our fathers upon a religion, and we are in their footsteps [rightly] guided."
interpretation: This verse is highlighting the tendency of people to blindly follow the traditions and beliefs of their ancestors without questioning their validity or correctness. They assume that since their forefathers followed a certain way, it must be the right path. This attitude hinders critical thinking, progress, and the ability to discern truth from falsehood. The Qur'an encourages people to use their intellect, reflect upon the signs of Allah, and embrace the truth, even if it means breaking away from the ways of their ancestors when those ways are misguided or based on ignorance.
orig: بل قالوا إنا وجدنا آباءنا على أمة وإنا على آثارهم مهتدون

translation: And similarly, We did not send before you any warner into a city except that its affluent said, "Indeed, we found our fathers upon a religion, and we are, in their footsteps, following."
interpretation: This verse highlights a common pattern of resistance to divine guidance throughout history. Whenever a prophet or messenger was sent to a community to warn them and call them to the right path, the wealthy and influential members of that society would often reject the message, citing their attachment to the traditions and beliefs of their ancestors. They were content to blindly follow the ways of their forefathers, even if those ways were misguided or contrary to the truth brought by the prophet. This attitude of stubbornness and adherence to ancestral customs, despite the clear evidence provided by the messengers, is a major obstacle to accepting divine revelation and reforming one's beliefs and actions accordingly.
orig: وكذلك ما أرسلنا من قبلك في قرية من نذير إلا قال مترفوها إنا وجدنا آباءنا على أمة وإنا على آثارهم مقتدون

translation: They said, "Even if we brought you better guidance than what you found your forefathers following?" They said, "Indeed we, in that with which you were sent, are disbelievers."
interpretation: This verse illustrates the stubborn attitude of those who reject the message of Islam despite its clear guidance. They are so attached to the traditions and beliefs of their ancestors that they are unwilling to consider any alternative, even if it is demonstrably better. This blind following of tradition is a major obstacle to accepting the truth. The verse also highlights the fact that the disbelievers are not rejecting the message out of ignorance, but rather out of a conscious choice to disbelieve, as they clearly state "Indeed we, in that with which you were sent, are disbelievers."
orig: قال أولو جئتكم بأهدى مما وجدتم عليه آباءكم قالوا إنا بما أرسلتم به كافرون

translation: So We took retribution from them; then see how was the end of the deniers.
interpretation: This verse is a warning to those who reject the message of Allah and His prophets. It emphasizes that Allah will punish those who persistently deny the truth, and their fate will be a lesson for others. The verse implies that the consequences of denying the truth are severe and that one should reflect upon the destiny of past nations who rejected the divine message. It serves as a reminder that the ultimate outcome of those who choose to disbelieve will be one of loss and regret, both in this world and in the hereafter.
orig: فانتقمنا منهم فانظر كيف كان عاقبة المكذبين

translation: And [mention] when Abraham said to his father and his people, "Indeed, I am disassociated from that which you worship,
interpretation: This verse highlights Abraham's strong conviction in monotheism and his rejection of the idolatry practiced by his father and his community. It demonstrates his unwavering commitment to worshipping Allah alone, even if it meant going against the beliefs of his loved ones and society. Abraham's statement serves as a powerful example of standing firm in one's faith and not compromising on the fundamental principle of worshipping the One True God, regardless of the pressures or influences from others.
orig: وإذ قال إبراهيم لأبيه وقومه إنني براء مما تعبدون

translation: Except for He who created me; and indeed, He will guide me.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the believer's complete trust and reliance on Allah's guidance. It conveys the idea that since Allah is the One who created us, He alone can guide us to the right path in life. The verse implies that we should not seek guidance from anyone or anything else, as only our Creator truly knows what is best for us and can lead us to success in this world and the hereafter. It is a reminder to always turn to Allah for direction and support, acknowledging His wisdom and mercy in all aspects of our lives.
orig: إلا الذي فطرني فإنه سيهدين

translation: And He made it a word enduring in his posterity, so that they may return.
interpretation: This verse refers to the enduring legacy of faith and monotheism that was established through the progeny of Prophet Abraham. The "word" here signifies the testament of faith, "La ilaha illa Allah" (There is no god but Allah), which was passed down through generations of prophets and believers. The verse emphasizes that this legacy of pure monotheism was preserved in Abraham's descendants, serving as a reminder and an invitation for people to turn back to the path of righteousness and submit to the One True God. It highlights the importance of transmitting the message of Islam from one generation to the next, ensuring the continuity and preservation of faith.
orig: وجعلها كلمة باقية في عقبه لعلهم يرجعون

translation: Rather, you provided enjoyment for these [people] and their fathers until there came to them the truth and a clear Messenger.
interpretation: This verse is a rebuke to those who have been distracted by worldly pleasures and have neglected the truth of Islam. It suggests that God has allowed them to enjoy the temporary delights of this life, along with their ancestors, until the arrival of the Qur'an and Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) with a clear message of guidance. The verse implies that now that the truth has come, there is no excuse for continuing to indulge in worldly distractions at the expense of one's faith and obedience to God. It is a call to prioritize the eternal realities over fleeting enjoyments.
orig: بل متعت هؤلاء وآباءهم حتى جاءهم الحق ورسول مبين

translation: And when the truth came to them, they said, "This is magic, and indeed we are, in it, disbelievers."
interpretation: This verse is referring to the disbelievers who, when presented with the truth of Islam and the message of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him), rejected it outright and accused it of being mere magic or sorcery. They refused to accept the clear signs and proofs that were brought to them, instead choosing to remain in disbelief and denial. This highlights the stubborn nature of those who are determined to reject the truth, even when it is made plain to them. It also serves as a warning to those who may be inclined to dismiss the message of Islam without giving it proper consideration or reflection.
orig: ولما جاءهم الحق قالوا هذا سحر وإنا به كافرون

translation: And they say, "Why was this Qur'an not sent down upon a great man from [one of] the two cities?"
interpretation: This verse reflects the attitude of the disbelievers who questioned why the Qur'an was revealed to Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) instead of someone they considered more prominent or influential from the two major cities of Makkah and Taif. They believed that a person's status, wealth, or influence should have been the criteria for prophethood. However, Allah chooses His messengers based on their spiritual qualities, piety, and suitability for the task, regardless of their social standing or material possessions. This verse highlights the flawed thinking of those who judge others by worldly standards rather than by their faith, character, and devotion to Allah.
orig: وقالوا لولا نزل هذا القرآن على رجل من القريتين عظيم

translation: Is it they who would portion out the Mercy of your Lord? It is We Who portion out between them their livelihood in this world, and We raised some of them above others in ranks, so that some may employ others in their work. But the Mercy of your Lord is better than the (wealth) which they amass.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that it is Allah alone who determines the provisions and status of individuals in this worldly life. He has created a system where people differ in their ranks and positions, enabling some to employ others and benefit from their services. However, the true wealth and success lies in attaining Allah's mercy, which is far superior to any material possessions one may accumulate in this temporary world. The verse reminds us to focus on seeking Allah's pleasure and mercy rather than being preoccupied with worldly pursuits and comparisons with others.
orig: أهم يقسمون رحمت ربك نحن قسمنا بينهم معيشتهم في الحياة الدنيا ورفعنا بعضهم فوق بعض درجات ليتخذ بعضهم بعضا سخريا ورحمت ربك خير مما يجمعون

translation: And if it were not that the people would become one community [of disbelievers], We would have made for those who disbelieve in the Most Merciful - for their houses - ceilings and stairways of silver upon which to mount.
interpretation: This verse points to the fact that Allah could have easily granted the disbelievers luxuries and wealth in this worldly life, such as houses with silver ceilings and stairways. However, He chose not to do so, because that would make all of mankind inclined towards disbelief, being deceived by the temporary glitter of this world. Allah's wisdom is to distinguish the believers who are seeking His pleasure from those who are only after worldly gain, even if it means disbelieving in Him. The verse emphasizes that faith should be based on sincere conviction, not influenced by materialistic temptations.
orig: ولولا أن يكون الناس أمة واحدة لجعلنا لمن يكفر بالرحمن لبيوتهم سقفا من فضة ومعارج عليها يظهرون

translation: And for their houses [they make] doors and couches [of silver] upon which they recline
interpretation: This verse is describing the luxurious and extravagant lifestyle of those who have been blessed with wealth and prosperity in this world. The mention of doors and couches made of silver symbolizes their indulgence in worldly pleasures and their attachment to material possessions. It serves as a reminder that such luxuries are temporary and should not distract one from remembering Allah and striving for success in the eternal life of the Hereafter. The verse implicitly warns against becoming preoccupied with worldly comforts at the expense of one's spiritual well-being and encourages maintaining a balanced perspective on the true purpose of life.
orig: ولبيوتهم أبوابا وسررا عليها يتكئون

translation: And gold adornment. But all that is not but the enjoyment of worldly life. And the Hereafter with your Lord is for the righteous.
interpretation: This verse reminds us that the luxuries and adornments of this worldly life, such as gold and other material possessions, are temporary and fleeting. They provide enjoyment and pleasure in this life, but they have no lasting value in the eternal perspective. The true and everlasting reward lies with Allah in the Hereafter, which is reserved for those who are righteous and God-fearing. It emphasizes the importance of prioritizing our spiritual well-being and seeking the pleasure of Allah over the temporary attractions of this world.
orig: وزخرفا وإن كل ذلك لما متاع الحياة الدنيا والآخرة عند ربك للمتقين

translation: And whoever is blinded from remembrance of the Most Merciful - We appoint for him a devil, and he is to him a companion.
interpretation: This verse warns that those who turn away from the remembrance of Allah and become heedless of His message will be afflicted with the companionship of a devil. The devil appointed to such a person will become their constant companion, leading them further astray from the path of righteousness. This highlights the importance of maintaining a strong connection with Allah through remembrance, supplication, and adherence to His guidance. Failing to do so leaves one vulnerable to the influence of Satanic forces that aim to misguide and corrupt. The verse serves as a reminder for believers to be vigilant in their remembrance of Allah and to seek His protection from the whispers and temptations of the devil.
orig: ومن يعش عن ذكر الرحمن نقيض له شيطانا فهو له قرين

translation: And indeed, they [the devils] avert them from the way [of guidance] while they think that they are [rightly] guided.
interpretation: This verse is referring to the deceptive nature of the devils who mislead people away from the straight path of Islam. They do this by making falsehood appear attractive and appealing, causing people to think that they are following the right way when in reality they have strayed far from it. The devils exploit people's weaknesses, desires, and ignorance to lead them astray, all the while making them believe that they are on the path of guidance. This highlights the importance of seeking knowledge, using reason, and being cautious of temptations and deceptions that can lead one away from the truth.
orig: وإنهم ليصدونهم عن السبيل ويحسبون أنهم مهتدون

translation: Until, when he comes to Us, he says [to his companion], "Oh, I wish there was between me and you the distance between the east and the west - how wretched a companion."
interpretation: This verse is referring to the Day of Judgment when the disbelievers will face the consequences of their actions. The person being referred to here is the one who was misguided by his companion in the worldly life. On the Day of Judgment, he will wish that there was a great distance between him and his companion who misled him, as vast as the distance between the east and the west. He will express his regret and sorrow for having such a wretched companion who led him astray from the right path. This verse emphasizes the importance of choosing righteous companions in this life who will guide us towards good deeds and help us stay on the straight path, as they will be questioned about their influence on the Day of Judgment.
orig: حتى إذا جاءنا قال يا ليت بيني وبينك بعد المشرقين فبئس القرين

translation: And it will not benefit you today, since you did wrong, that you are [all] sharing in the punishment.
interpretation: This verse is a stark reminder that on the Day of Judgment, when the wrongdoers face the consequences of their actions, sharing in the punishment will not bring them any benefit or relief. It emphasizes the individual responsibility for one's deeds and the inevitability of divine justice. The verse implies that those who committed wrongs and injustices in this world will face the full weight of their actions in the Hereafter, regardless of whether others are also being punished for similar transgressions. It serves as a warning against oppression and wrongdoing, urging individuals to be mindful of their actions and to seek forgiveness and redemption before it is too late.
orig: ولن ينفعكم اليوم إذ ظلمتم أنكم في العذاب مشتركون

translation: Then can you make the deaf hear or guide the blind or he who is in clear error?
interpretation: This verse is a rhetorical question, emphasizing that guidance ultimately comes from Allah alone. The Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) cannot force anyone to accept the message of Islam, especially those who are spiritually "deaf" or "blind" due to their persistent disbelief and rejection of the truth. It is a reminder that the Prophet's role is to convey the message clearly, but the responsibility of accepting it lies with each individual. The verse also implies that those who persistently reject the truth are in manifest error, as they fail to recognize the signs and guidance provided by Allah.
orig: أفأنت تسمع الصم أو تهدي العمي ومن كان في ضلال مبين

translation: And if We take you away [in death], indeed, We will take retribution upon them.
interpretation: This verse is a warning and a promise from Allah to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) that even if he were to die or be killed, Allah would still take vengeance upon those who opposed and persecuted him and his followers. It emphasizes the idea that the ultimate victory belongs to Allah and those who are on His path, regardless of the challenges and hardships they may face in this world. The verse also serves as a comfort to the believers, reminding them that Allah will always support and protect His cause, and that the oppressors and wrongdoers will face the consequences of their actions in the Hereafter.
orig: فإما نذهبن بك فإنا منهم منتقمون

translation: Or [if We will], We can show you that which We have promised them, for indeed, We are over them Perfect in Ability.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's omnipotence and His ability to fulfill His promises. It suggests that Allah can easily show the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) the punishment that has been promised to the disbelievers, as a way of reassuring him that Allah's threats are not empty. The verse also implies that Allah has complete control over the disbelievers and can subject them to His will and punishment at any time He chooses. It is a reminder that no one can escape Allah's judgment and that His power is absolute.
orig: أو نرينك الذي وعدناهم فإنا عليهم مقتدرون

translation: So adhere to that which is revealed to you. Indeed, you are on a straight path.
interpretation: This verse is a reminder to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and all believers to hold fast to the Qur'an and its teachings. It emphasizes the importance of staying committed to the divine revelation, as it is the straight path that leads to success in this world and the hereafter. The verse encourages the believers to remain steadfast in their faith, despite the challenges and obstacles they may face, and to trust in the guidance provided by the Qur'an. It also serves as an assurance that following the Qur'an will lead to a life of righteousness and a direct connection with Allah.
orig: فاستمسك بالذي أوحي إليك إنك على صراط مستقيم

translation: And indeed, it is a reminder for you and your people, and you will be questioned.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance and significance of the Qur'an as a reminder and a source of guidance for the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and his people, the Arabs. It also serves as a warning that they will be held accountable and questioned about their faith, deeds, and adherence to the message of the Qur'an on the Day of Judgment. This verse encourages believers to study, reflect upon, and live by the teachings of the Qur'an, as it is a means of attaining success and salvation in this world and the hereafter.
orig: وإنه لذكر لك ولقومك وسوف تسألون

translation: And ask those We sent before you of Our messengers; did We appoint gods to be worshipped besides the Most Merciful?
interpretation: This verse is a rhetorical question, challenging the notion of worshipping any deity other than Allah, the Most Merciful. It implies that none of the previous prophets and messengers, who were sent by Allah, ever preached the worship of other gods. The message conveyed is that the worship should be directed solely to Allah, as He is the only true God worthy of worship. This verse reaffirms the fundamental principle of Islamic monotheism (Tawheed) and rejects the concept of polytheism or associating partners with Allah in worship.
orig: واسأل من أرسلنا من قبلك من رسلنا أجعلنا من دون الرحمن آلهة يعبدون

translation: And indeed, We sent Moses with Our signs to Pharaoh and his establishment, and he said, "Indeed, I am the messenger of the Lord of the worlds."
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine mission of Prophet Moses, who was sent by God to convey His message to Pharaoh and his people. Moses declared himself as a messenger of the Lord of the worlds, emphasizing the universality and supremacy of God's authority. The mention of "Our signs" indicates that Moses was given miracles and clear proofs to support his claim and to convince Pharaoh and his followers of the truth of his message. This verse serves as a reminder that God sends prophets and messengers to guide humanity towards the right path and to establish His worship and obedience on earth.
orig: ولقد أرسلنا موسى بآياتنا إلى فرعون وملئه فقال إني رسول رب العالمين

translation: But when he came to them with Our signs, at once they laughed at them.
interpretation: This verse is referring to the reaction of the disbelievers when a prophet or messenger came to them with clear signs and proofs from Allah. Instead of reflecting on these signs and recognizing their truth, they arrogantly mocked and laughed at them. This shows their ignorance, closed-mindedness, and lack of respect for the divine message. They were so engrossed in their false beliefs and worldly pursuits that they could not open their hearts to the guidance that was sent to them. This kind of response is typical of those who reject faith due to their pride and attachment to their own misguided ways.
orig: فلما جاءهم بآياتنا إذا هم منها يضحكون

translation: And We showed them not a sign except that it was greater than its sister, and We seized them with affliction that perhaps they might return [to faith].
interpretation: This verse highlights Allah's mercy and His desire for people to turn back to Him in repentance. Despite sending clear signs and warnings, people often persist in disbelief. The verse indicates that Allah gradually increases the severity of His signs and punishments, giving people multiple opportunities to recognize the truth and mend their ways. The ultimate goal is not to destroy them, but to encourage them to return to the path of faith and righteousness. It serves as a reminder that Allah's door of forgiveness is always open for those who sincerely seek to return to Him.
orig: وما نريهم من آية إلا هي أكبر من أختها وأخذناهم بالعذاب لعلهم يرجعون

translation: And they said, "O you magician, invoke for us your Lord by what He has promised you. Indeed, we will be guided."
interpretation: This verse is referring to the disbelievers who mockingly called the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) a magician. They challenged him to invoke Allah and bring about the punishment that he had warned them about, claiming that they would then believe and be guided. However, their statement was insincere and merely a way to ridicule the Prophet. It shows their arrogance and stubbornness in refusing to accept the truth despite clear signs and warnings. The verse highlights the defiant attitude of those who oppose the message of Islam and their attempts to discredit the Prophet through taunts and challenges.
orig: وقالوا يا أيه الساحر ادع لنا ربك بما عهد عندك إننا لمهتدون

translation: But when We removed the torment from them, behold! They broke their covenant.
interpretation: This verse points to the fickleness and ingratitude of human nature. Even when God relieves people from hardships and trials, they often quickly forget His mercy and revert to their old ways of disobedience and breaking their promises to Him. It highlights how people tend to turn to God in times of difficulty, but when ease comes, they become heedless and ungrateful. The verse serves as a reminder for humans to remain steadfast in faith and thankfulness to God both in times of hardship and ease, and to fulfill the covenants they make with Him.
orig: فلما كشفنا عنهم العذاب إذا هم ينكثون

translation: And Pharaoh called out among his people; he said, "O my people, does not the kingdom of Egypt belong to me, and these rivers flowing beneath me; then do you not see?"
interpretation: In this verse, Pharaoh is boasting about his power and authority over the land of Egypt and its resources, particularly the Nile river. He is trying to convince his people that he is the supreme ruler and that they should not question his authority or follow anyone else, such as Moses. This verse highlights Pharaoh's arrogance and his belief that his worldly possessions and status make him superior to others, while in reality, true power and authority belong only to Allah. It serves as a reminder for believers not to be deceived by worldly temptations and to always remember that Allah is the ultimate authority.
orig: ونادى فرعون في قومه قال يا قوم أليس لي ملك مصر وهذه الأنهار تجري من تحتي أفلا تبصرون

translation: Am I not better than this one who is insignificant and hardly makes himself clear?
interpretation: This verse is showing the arrogance and pride of the Pharaoh, who considered himself superior to Moses due to his power, wealth and eloquence. He belittled Moses as someone insignificant and lacking in clear speech. It reflects the Pharaoh's egotism and his disdain for the message and prophethood of Moses. The Pharaoh was deluded by his worldly status into thinking he was better than the prophet and messenger of Allah, which is a sign of great arrogance and disbelief.
orig: أم أنا خير من هذا الذي هو مهين ولا يكاد يبين

translation: Why has he not been given bracelets of gold or come with the angels as companions?
interpretation: This verse reflects the skepticism and disbelief of the people towards the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him). They questioned why he was not adorned with gold bracelets or accompanied by angels, which they believed would be signs of a true prophet. This demand for material wealth and supernatural companions as proof of prophethood demonstrates their lack of understanding of the true nature of divine revelation and the role of a prophet. It also highlights their attachment to worldly status and their inability to recognize the spiritual essence of the Prophet's message.
orig: فلولا ألقي عليه أسورة من ذهب أو جاء معه الملائكة مقترنين

translation: So he bluffed his people, and they obeyed him. Indeed, they were a people defiantly disobedient.
interpretation: This verse is referring to a leader who misled his people through deception and false promises. Instead of guiding them to the right path, he made fools out of them, exploiting their willingness to follow him blindly. The people are also to blame, as they were already inclined towards disobedience and transgression. They allowed themselves to be easily swayed by their leader's trickery because it aligned with their own corrupt desires. The verse highlights the dangers of both arrogant leadership and the lack of discernment among the masses. It serves as a warning against following others blindly and stresses the importance of using reason and adhering to divine guidance to avoid being led astray.
orig: فاستخف قومه فأطاعوه إنهم كانوا قوما فاسقين

translation: So when they provoked Our wrath, We took retribution from them and drowned them all.
interpretation: This verse speaks to the consequences of persistently defying and angering Allah. When the people mentioned crossed all limits and provoked Allah's wrath through their misdeeds, Allah exacted retribution upon them by drowning them all as punishment. It demonstrates that while Allah is oft-forgiving and merciful, there are still severe consequences for those who continuously transgress and fail to heed warnings. The verse serves as a reminder that one cannot forever escape divine justice for wrongdoings and that Allah's punishment, when it comes, is thorough and decisive against the unrepentant.
orig: فلما آسفونا انتقمنا منهم فأغرقناهم أجمعين

translation: And We made them a precedent and an example for the later generations.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah made the fate of the disbelievers who rejected His message a lesson and a warning for those who come after them. Their destruction serves as a precedent, showing the consequences of denying the truth and opposing the Messengers of Allah. It is an example that should be heeded by subsequent generations, reminding them to follow the right path and avoid the mistakes of those who were punished for their disobedience and disbelief. The verse underscores the importance of learning from history and taking admonition from the examples set by past nations.
orig: فجعلناهم سلفا ومثلا للآخرين

translation: And when the son of Mary was presented as an example, immediately your people laughed aloud.
interpretation: This verse is referring to the reaction of the disbelievers when Jesus, the son of Mary, was mentioned as an example of Allah's power and ability to create. Instead of reflecting on the miraculous nature of Jesus' birth and the significance of his prophethood, the disbelievers mocked and laughed at the mention of him. This reaction stems from their arrogance, ignorance, and refusal to accept the truth. It highlights their lack of understanding and appreciation for the signs and messages that Allah has sent through His prophets. The verse serves as a reminder to the believers to be mindful of the examples and lessons presented in the Qur'an, and to approach them with respect, contemplation, and an open heart.
orig: ولما ضرب ابن مريم مثلا إذا قومك منه يصدون

translation: And they said, "Are our gods better, or is he?" They did not present it [i.e., the comparison] to you except for [mere] argument. But, [in fact], they are a people prone to dispute.
interpretation: This verse is a response to the polytheists who tried to compare their false gods with Allah. They did not make this comparison sincerely, but only to argue and dispute with the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him). The verse points out that their argument is baseless and stems from their argumentative nature, rather than a genuine desire for truth. It highlights the stubborn and contentious attitude of those who oppose the message of Islam, even when faced with clear evidence of Allah's superiority and uniqueness.
orig: وقالوا أآلهتنا خير أم هو ما ضربوه لك إلا جدلا بل هم قوم خصمون

translation: He was not but a servant upon whom We bestowed favor, and We made him an example for the Children of Israel.
interpretation: This verse refers to a prophet or a righteous person whom Allah blessed with His favors and made him a role model for the Children of Israel. It emphasizes that this person, despite his high status, was still a servant of Allah and not divine himself. The verse reminds us that the prophets and the righteous are examples to be followed, but they are not to be worshipped or elevated to the status of Allah. It also highlights Allah's grace upon the Children of Israel by sending them a guide to follow.
orig: إن هو إلا عبد أنعمنا عليه وجعلناه مثلا لبني إسرائيل

translation: And if We willed, We could have made [instead of you] angels on the earth succeeding [one another].
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute power and authority of Allah over His creation. It suggests that Allah could have easily created angels to inhabit the earth instead of human beings, but He chose to create humans and entrust them with the responsibility of being His vicegerents on earth. This highlights the special status and purpose that Allah has given to mankind. It also implies that humans should be grateful for the opportunity to live on earth and strive to fulfill their God-given role, rather than taking their existence for granted or becoming arrogant. The verse serves as a reminder of Allah's omnipotence and the fact that everything happens by His will and wisdom.
orig: ولو نشاء لجعلنا منكم ملائكة في الأرض يخلفون

translation: And indeed, it is knowledge of the Hour, so have no doubt about it and follow Me. This is a straight path.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the Qur'an is a source of knowledge about the Day of Judgment (the Hour). It serves as a reminder for believers to have unwavering faith in its inevitability and to follow the straight path laid out by Allah and His Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him). The verse urges Muslims to trust in the divine guidance provided by the Qur'an and to adhere to its teachings without doubt or hesitation, as this is the only way to attain success in this life and the hereafter.
orig: وإنه لعلم للساعة فلا تمترن بها واتبعون هذا صراط مستقيم

translation: And do not let Satan avert you. Indeed, he is to you a clear enemy.
interpretation: This verse warns believers not to be deceived or misled by Satan, who is described as a clear enemy to mankind. Satan's goal is to lead people astray from the path of righteousness and into sin and disobedience to Allah. The verse emphasizes the importance of being vigilant and steadfast in one's faith, resisting the temptations and whispers of Satan. It serves as a reminder that Satan is not a friend or well-wisher, but rather an avowed enemy whose sole purpose is to lead people away from Allah's guidance and mercy. Therefore, Muslims should seek refuge in Allah from Satan's influence and strive to follow the straight path.
orig: ولا يصدنكم الشيطان إنه لكم عدو مبين

translation: And when Jesus came with clear proofs, he said, "I have come to you with wisdom and to make clear to you some of that over which you differ, so fear Allah and obey me."
interpretation: This verse highlights the role of Prophet Jesus as a messenger of Allah who came with clear evidence and wisdom to guide people towards the right path.
