He clarified some of the matters over which people differed, indicating that there were disagreements and confusion among people regarding certain religious issues. Jesus emphasized the importance of having consciousness (taqwa) of Allah and obeying His commands as conveyed through the prophets. This interpretation suggests that following the guidance brought by the prophets, including Jesus, is essential for resolving differences and attaining righteousness.
orig: ولما جاء عيسى بالبينات قال قد جئتكم بالحكمة ولأبين لكم بعض الذي تختلفون فيه فاتقوا الله وأطيعون

translation: Indeed, Allah is my Lord and your Lord, so worship Him. This is a straight path.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the oneness of Allah and the importance of worshipping Him alone. It reminds us that Allah is the Lord and Creator of all, and that following His guidance and worshipping Him is the straight path that leads to success in this life and the hereafter. The verse also implies that straying from this path of monotheism and devotion to Allah will lead one astray. It is a clear call to submit to Allah alone and follow the way of Islam.
orig: إن الله هو ربي وربكم فاعبدوه هذا صراط مستقيم

translation: Then the factions differed among them. So woe to those who did wrong from the punishment of a painful Day.
interpretation: This verse warns about the consequences of disagreement and disunity among people, especially in matters of faith. Those who deviate from the truth and engage in wrongdoing will face a severe punishment on the Day of Judgment. It emphasizes the importance of staying united upon the correct path and avoiding actions that lead to discord and injustice, as they will result in painful consequences in the Hereafter.
orig: فاختلف الأحزاب من بينهم فويل للذين ظلموا من عذاب يوم أليم

translation: Do they await except for the Hour to come upon them suddenly while they perceive not?
interpretation: This verse is a warning to those who reject the message of Islam and the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him). It suggests that the Day of Judgment, referred to as "the Hour", will come suddenly and unexpectedly, catching the disbelievers off guard. They are heedless and unaware of the impending doom that awaits them due to their lack of faith and righteous deeds. The verse implies that it is essential for individuals to be prepared for the Day of Judgment by believing in Allah, following His guidance, and performing good actions, as the arrival of "the Hour" is inevitable and can occur at any moment without prior notice.
orig: هل ينظرون إلا الساعة أن تأتيهم بغتة وهم لا يشعرون

translation: Close friends, that Day, will be enemies to each other, except for the righteous.
interpretation: This verse highlights the dramatic shift in relationships that will occur on the Day of Judgment. Even the closest of friends will turn against each other due to the intensity and gravity of the situation. The only exception to this will be the righteous, those who have lived their lives in accordance with God's commands and have maintained their integrity. Their friendships will endure because they are based on a shared devotion to God rather than worldly interests. This verse serves as a reminder that ultimately, our relationship with God is the most important, and that we should strive to be among the righteous whose bonds will remain strong even in the face of the most challenging circumstances.
orig: الأخلاء يومئذ بعضهم لبعض عدو إلا المتقين

translation: O servants, no fear will be upon you today, nor will you grieve.
interpretation: This verse is a reassurance from Allah to His righteous servants on the Day of Judgment. It indicates that those who believed in Him, followed His guidance, and did good deeds will have nothing to fear on that momentous day. They will be protected from the horrors and difficulties that others will face. Moreover, they will not grieve or feel sorrow for any worldly losses or missed opportunities, as they will be content with what Allah has prepared for them in Paradise. This verse highlights the importance of faith and righteous deeds in securing a peaceful and blessed outcome in the Hereafter.
orig: يا عباد لا خوف عليكم اليوم ولا أنتم تحزنون

translation: Those who believed in Our verses and were Muslims.
interpretation: This verse refers to the true believers who have complete faith in the Qur'an and the signs of Allah's existence and power that are mentioned throughout it. They not only profess their belief verbally, but also demonstrate it through their actions by submitting to Allah's will and following His commandments. The verse emphasizes that these are the people who will be rewarded by Allah for their sincere faith and righteousness. It implies that mere verbal profession of faith is not enough; one must live according to the teachings of Islam and embody the qualities of a true Muslim, such as humility, obedience, and devotion to Allah.
orig: الذين آمنوا بآياتنا وكانوا مسلمين

translation: Enter Paradise, you and your spouses, in happiness.
interpretation: This verse is a promise from Allah to the righteous believers that they will enter Paradise along with their spouses in a state of joy, delight, and honor. It emphasizes the importance of righteousness and the reward that awaits those who follow the path of Islam. The mention of spouses entering Paradise together also highlights the significance of marriage and the strong bond between husband and wife in Islam, indicating that this relationship extends beyond worldly life and into the hereafter, where they will share in the blessings and happiness of Paradise together.
orig: ادخلوا الجنة أنتم وأزواجكم تحبرون

translation: Circulated among them will be plates and vessels of gold. And therein is whatever the souls desire and [what] delights the eyes, and you will abide therein eternally.
interpretation: This verse speaks of the eternal bliss that awaits the righteous in Paradise. The mention of gold plates and vessels signifies the luxurious and magnificent nature of Paradise. The verse also emphasizes that in Paradise, the believers will have everything their souls desire and that which brings joy to their eyes. This includes not only material pleasures but also spiritual fulfillment and contentment. The verse ends with the promise of eternity, indicating that this state of ultimate happiness will last forever, without any fear of it coming to an end or being taken away. This serves as a powerful motivation for believers to strive for righteousness in this world, knowing that their ultimate reward lies in the eternal delights of Paradise.
orig: يطاف عليهم بصحاف من ذهب وأكواب وفيها ما تشتهيه الأنفس وتلذ الأعين وأنتم فيها خالدون

translation: And that is Paradise which you have been made to inherit for what you used to do.
interpretation: This verse speaks about the ultimate reward for the righteous believers - inheriting Paradise as a result of their good deeds and obedience to Allah during their worldly life. It emphasizes that entering Paradise is not arbitrary, but rather a consequence of one's actions and conduct in this world. The verse motivates and encourages believers to persevere in doing good and following the straight path, knowing that their efforts will be rewarded with the eternal bliss of Paradise in the Hereafter. It instills hope and serves as a reminder that the temporary struggles and sacrifices of this life are worth the everlasting joy that awaits the faithful in the Gardens of Paradise.
orig: وتلك الجنة التي أورثتموها بما كنتم تعملون

translation: In it you have much fruit from which you eat.
interpretation: This verse is referring to the bounties and blessings that Allah has provided for mankind in this world. The "it" in this verse is referring to the earth or the gardens of the earth. Allah is reminding us that He has provided an abundance of fruit for our sustenance and enjoyment. The verse is encouraging gratitude for the provisions that Allah has given us, and to recognize that it is through His mercy and generosity that we have access to such a variety of nourishing and delicious fruits. It also implies that we should partake of these fruits in moderation and not be wasteful or ungrateful for them.
orig: لكم فيها فاكهة كثيرة منها تأكلون

translation: Indeed, the criminals will be in the punishment of Hell, abiding eternally.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the severe and eternal punishment that awaits those who persistently commit grave sins and reject faith in Allah. It serves as a powerful warning to humanity that the consequences of leading a sinful life, without seeking repentance and Allah's mercy, will be the everlasting torment of Hell. The verse aims to instill a sense of fear and consciousness in the hearts of believers, encouraging them to stay on the righteous path and avoid actions that would lead to such a dreadful fate. It also highlights the concept of divine justice, as the criminals who transgress against Allah's laws and harm others will face the ultimate retribution in the Hereafter.
orig: إن المجرمين في عذاب جهنم خالدون

translation: It will not be allowed to subside for them, and they, therein, are in despair.
interpretation: This verse speaks about the state of the disbelievers in Hell. The punishment and torment will be constant and unrelenting, without any respite or relief. The people condemned to Hell will be in a state of complete despair and hopelessness, realizing the permanence of their suffering as a consequence of their rejection of faith and righteous deeds in the worldly life. It serves as a severe warning for mankind to adopt the path of submission to Allah and to live according to His guidance in order to avoid this grievous fate in the Hereafter.
orig: لا يفتر عنهم وهم فيه مبلسون

translation: And We did not wrong them, but they were the wrongdoers.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah is just and does not wrong anyone. The people mentioned in this verse were not wronged by Allah, but rather they were the ones who committed wrongdoings and injustices. They brought punishment upon themselves through their own actions and choices. It highlights the principle that everyone is responsible for their own deeds and will face the consequences accordingly. Allah's judgment is always fair and based on the actions of individuals.
orig: وما ظلمناهم ولكن كانوا هم الظالمين

translation: And they will call, "O Malik, let your Lord put an end to us!" He will say, "Indeed, you will remain."
interpretation: This verse speaks about the people in Hell who, out of desperation and anguish, will call out to the angel Malik, the keeper of Hell, pleading with him to ask Allah to put an end to their suffering by destroying them completely. However, Malik will respond that they are doomed to remain in Hell for eternity, as a consequence of their disbelief and wrongdoings in their worldly life. This highlights the severity and permanence of the punishment in Hell, and serves as a warning to humanity to strive for faith and righteousness to avoid such a fate.
orig: ونادوا يا مالك ليقض علينا ربك قال إنكم ماكثون

translation: We have certainly brought you the truth, but most of you, to the truth, are averse.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the message brought by the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) is the ultimate truth from Allah. However, it also points out the tragic reality that despite the clear truth being conveyed, the majority of people are averse to accepting it. They reject the truth due to their attachment to their desires, traditions, or worldly inclinations. It highlights the innate stubbornness of human beings in accepting divine guidance, even when it is presented with clear proofs and evidence. The verse serves as a reminder for believers to be grateful for being guided to the truth and to have patience in facing the rejection and opposition of those who turn away from it.
orig: لقد جئناكم بالحق ولكن أكثركم للحق كارهون

translation: Or have they devised [some] affair? But indeed, We are devising [a plan].
interpretation: This verse is a warning to those who plot against Islam and the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him). It suggests that while the disbelievers may be making their own plans against the Muslims, Allah is also devising a plan which will ultimately overcome the schemes of the disbelievers. It conveys that no matter what strategies or plots the enemies of Islam contrive, they cannot outsmart or defeat the will and plan of Allah. The verse emphasizes Allah's power, wisdom and control over all affairs, and serves as a reassurance to believers to have faith and trust in Allah's plan even in the face of adversity or the machinations of the enemies of Islam.
orig: أم أبرموا أمرا فإنا مبرمون

translation: Or do they think that We do not hear their secrets and their private conversations? Yes, [We do], and Our messengers are with them recording.
interpretation: This verse is a reminder that Allah is all-knowing and all-aware of everything, including the secrets and private conversations of people. It emphasizes that nothing is hidden from Allah, and that He has assigned angels to record the deeds and words of individuals. This serves as a warning to those who might think that they can conceal their wrongdoings or evil intentions from Allah, and encourages people to be mindful of their actions and words at all times, knowing that they will be held accountable for them in the Hereafter.
orig: أم يحسبون أنا لا نسمع سرهم ونجواهم بلى ورسلنا لديهم يكتبون

translation: Say, "If the Most Merciful had a son, then I would be the first of [his] worshippers."
interpretation: This verse challenges the notion that God has a son or offspring. It asserts that even if it were true that the Most Merciful (ar-Rahman, one of the names of God in Islam) had a son, Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) would be the first to worship and submit to him. However, the implication is that since God does not have a son, there is no need for such worship. The verse emphasizes the Islamic belief in the absolute oneness and uniqueness of God, rejecting any ideas of divine offspring or partners associated with Him. It is a clear refutation of the Christian belief in Jesus as the son of God.
orig: قل إن كان للرحمن ولد فأنا أول العابدين

translation: Exalted is the Lord of the heavens and the earth, the Lord of the Throne, above what they describe.
interpretation: This verse affirms the transcendence and perfection of Allah, who is far above any descriptions or attributes that His creation may try to ascribe to Him. It emphasizes that Allah is the Lord and Creator of the entire universe, including the heavens, the earth, and the mighty Throne. The verse also implies that no one can truly comprehend or describe the greatness and majesty of Allah, as He is beyond human understanding and imagination. It serves as a reminder for believers to glorify and exalt Allah, acknowledging His supremacy and uniqueness.
orig: سبحان رب السماوات والأرض رب العرش عما يصفون

translation: So leave them to converse vainly and amuse themselves until they meet their Day which they are promised.
interpretation: This verse is a warning to those who reject the message of Islam and are engrossed in worldly pursuits. It instructs the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) to leave such people to their idle talk and amusement until they face the Day of Judgment, which they have been promised. On that day, they will realize the consequences of their actions and the truth of what they were warned about. This verse emphasizes the temporary nature of this world and the importance of focusing on the eternal life to come. It also highlights the patience and perseverance required by believers in the face of rejection and mockery from those who oppose the truth.
orig: فذرهم يخوضوا ويلعبوا حتى يلاقوا يومهم الذي يوعدون

translation: And it is He who is God in the heaven and God on the earth. And He is the Wise, the Knowing.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the oneness and uniqueness of Allah, stating that He is the only true God worshipped in the heavens and on the earth. It affirms His sovereignty over all creation and that He alone deserves worship. The verse also highlights two of Allah's attributes: His wisdom and His knowledge. He is the All-Wise, whose every decree and action is perfect and full of wisdom, and the All-Knowing, whose knowledge encompasses all things in the heavens and the earth, both seen and unseen. This verse is a reminder for believers to direct their worship and devotion to Allah alone, seeking His guidance and submitting to His will.
orig: وهو الذي في السماء إله وفي الأرض إله وهو الحكيم العليم

translation: And blessed is He to whom belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth and whatever is between them and with whom is knowledge of the Hour and to whom you will be returned.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute sovereignty and dominion of Allah over the entire universe. It highlights that Allah alone possesses the knowledge of the Day of Judgment (the Hour), which is known only to Him. The verse also reminds us that all of humanity will ultimately return to Allah for judgment and accountability. It serves as a powerful reminder of Allah's supreme authority and the inevitability of facing Him in the Hereafter, encouraging believers to lead righteous lives and remain mindful of their ultimate destiny.
orig: وتبارك الذي له ملك السماوات والأرض وما بينهما وعنده علم الساعة وإليه ترجعون

translation: And those they invoke besides Him do not possess [power of] intercession; but only those who testify to the truth [can benefit], and they know.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that no one has the power of intercession with Allah except those who bear witness to the truth and have knowledge of it. It suggests that mere invocation of others besides Allah is futile, as they do not possess the ability to intercede. Only those who have affirmed the truth of Allah's message and have acted upon it with knowledge and sincerity will be able to benefit from intercession on the Day of Judgment. This highlights the importance of faith, righteous deeds, and adherence to the truth in Islam.
orig: ولا يملك الذين يدعون من دونه الشفاعة إلا من شهد بالحق وهم يعلمون

translation: If you asked them who created them, they would surely say, "Allah". So how are they deluded?
interpretation: This verse points to the inherent belief in Allah that all humans possess, even if they outwardly deny it or associate partners with Him. It suggests that deep down, everyone acknowledges Allah as their Creator, but many are led astray from this natural belief by various factors such as their desires, societal influences, or lack of reflection. The verse implies that if people were to sincerely reflect upon their own existence and the world around them, they would inevitably conclude that Allah is the One who created them and everything else. However, they are deluded and turn away from this truth, following false beliefs and ideologies instead. This highlights the importance of sincere reflection, contemplation, and staying true to one's innate belief in Allah, without being swayed by external influences or desires.
orig: ولئن سألتهم من خلقهم ليقولن الله فأنى يؤفكون

translation: And he said, "O my Lord, indeed these are a people who do not believe."
interpretation: In this verse, the prophet is expressing his frustration and sadness to Allah about the disbelief and stubbornness of his people. Despite his tireless efforts to guide them to the right path, they persist in their rejection of faith. The prophet recognizes that only Allah can ultimately guide people's hearts, so he turns to Him in supplication, seeking help and support in the face of this challenge. This highlights the importance of patience, perseverance, and reliance on Allah when facing difficulties in conveying the message of Islam.
orig: وقيله يا رب إن هؤلاء قوم لا يؤمنون

translation: So turn away from them and say, "Peace." They will come to know.
interpretation: This verse advises the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and the believers to disregard the mockery and opposition of the disbelievers and to respond with a greeting of peace. It implies that the truth will eventually become clear to them, either in this world or in the Hereafter, and they will realize the consequences of their actions. The verse promotes patience, forbearance, and taking the high road in the face of adversity, while having faith that God will ultimately establish justice and make the truth prevail.
orig: فاصفح عنهم وقل سلام فسوف يعلمون

translation: Ha, Meem.
interpretation: This verse consists of two Arabic letters, Ha and Meem. Many chapters in the Qur'an begin with such letter combinations, known as Al-Muqatta'at (the Disjoined Letters). The exact meaning and purpose of these letters are not explicitly mentioned in the Qur'an or Hadith. Scholars have proposed various interpretations, such as them being symbols of divine secrets, abbreviations for certain phrases or names, or a way to draw the listener's attention to the message that follows. Ultimately, the true meaning of these letters is known only to Allah, and believers are encouraged to reflect upon them as part of the Qur'an's miraculous nature and profound wisdom.
orig: حم

translation: By the clear Book.
interpretation: This verse is an oath taken by Allah, swearing by the clear Qur'an. The Qur'an is described as "clear" because its meanings, teachings, and guidance are evident and unambiguous for those who reflect upon it sincerely. The oath signifies the great importance and sublime nature of the Qur'an, emphasizing that it is a book of truth, guidance, and wisdom from Allah.
orig: والكتاب المبين

translation: Indeed, We sent it down during a blessed night. Indeed, We were to warn [mankind].
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the significance and sacredness of the night in which the Qur'an was revealed. It suggests that the revelation of the Qur'an on this blessed night is a sign of Allah's mercy and guidance to humanity. The verse also highlights the role of the Qur'an as a warning to mankind, reminding them of their obligations towards Allah and the consequences of their actions. It implies that the Qur'an serves as a clear message and a reminder for people to follow the right path and avoid wrongdoings.
orig: إنا أنزلناه في ليلة مباركة إنا كنا منذرين

translation: Therein [that night] every wise matter is made distinct,
interpretation: This verse refers to the Night of Decree (Laylat al-Qadr), which is a special night in the month of Ramadan. On this night, Allah decrees every matter of ordainment for the coming year, such as life and death, sustenance, and other affairs. It is a night of great wisdom and blessing, where the angels descend and carry out Allah's decrees. This night emphasizes the importance of divine wisdom and the predetermined nature of all events in the universe, as decreed by Allah in His infinite knowledge and wisdom.
orig: فيها يفرق كل أمر حكيم

translation: As a command from Us. Indeed, We were to send [a messenger].
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that sending messengers and revealing divine messages is a command from Allah Himself. It highlights the fact that Allah, in His infinite wisdom and mercy, has taken it upon Himself to guide humanity through His chosen messengers. The verse also implies that sending messengers is a predetermined plan of Allah, and it is not a mere coincidence or an afterthought. The use of the word "Indeed" (إنا) adds emphasis and certainty to the statement, leaving no doubt about Allah's intention and commitment to guiding mankind through His messengers.
orig: أمرا من عندنا إنا كنا مرسلين

translation: As a mercy from your Lord. Indeed, He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the blessings and guidance given to humanity are a manifestation of Allah's infinite mercy. It reminds us that Allah is All-Hearing, meaning that He hears our prayers and supplications, and All-Knowing, indicating that He is aware of our needs, desires, and the innermost secrets of our hearts. This verse encourages believers to turn to Allah with sincerity, knowing that He will respond to their prayers and guide them towards the right path. It also highlights the importance of recognizing and appreciating the mercy of Allah in our lives.
orig: رحمة من ربك إنه هو السميع العليم

translation: Lord of the heavens and the earth and whatever is between them, if you [truly] are certain.
interpretation: This verse affirms that Allah is the supreme creator and sustainer of the entire universe, including the heavens, the earth, and everything in between. It challenges the reader to have firm conviction in this truth, emphasizing that if one is truly certain of Allah's existence and power, they should acknowledge Him as the sole Lord and master of all creation. The verse implies that recognizing Allah's lordship over the cosmos is a natural consequence of having strong faith and certainty in Him.
orig: رب السماوات والأرض وما بينهما إن كنتم موقنين

translation: There is no deity except Him; He gives life and causes death. [He is] your Lord and the Lord of your first forefathers.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute oneness and uniqueness of Allah, affirming that He alone is worthy of worship. It highlights His power over life and death, a fundamental aspect of His divine authority. The mention of Him being the Lord of both the addressees and their ancestors implies that Allah's lordship and right to be worshipped is eternal and unchanging, not limited to a specific time or generation. This interpretation underscores the importance of recognizing Allah's sovereignty and submitting to Him alone, as He is the ultimate source of life, death, and all existence.
orig: لا إله إلا هو يحيي ويميت ربكم ورب آبائكم الأولين

translation: But they are in doubt, amusing themselves.
interpretation: This verse suggests that the disbelievers are not sincere in their doubts about the truth of Islam. Rather, they are merely entertaining these doubts as a form of amusement or distraction, without truly seeking to understand or engage with the message of the Qur'an. They are playing with their doubts, rather than genuinely grappling with the questions of faith and belief. This attitude is seen as a form of heedlessness and lack of seriousness in the face of the profound spiritual truths being conveyed by the Qur'an.
orig: بل هم في شك يلعبون

translation: Then watch for the Day when the sky will bring a visible smoke.
interpretation: This verse is warning of a future event, likely near the end of times or on the Day of Judgment, when the sky will be filled with a clearly visible smoke. This smoke could be literal, or it may be symbolic of the great upheavals and calamities that will befall the world in the end days. It is a sign for humanity to be watchful and prepared, as this smoke heralds the coming of a time of reckoning and judgment. The verse urges the believers to be ever mindful of that Day and to live righteously in anticipation of it.
orig: فارتقب يوم تأتي السماء بدخان مبين

translation: It will cover the people. This is a painful punishment.
interpretation: This verse warns of a terrible punishment that will envelop all of mankind. It suggests that this punishment will be inescapable and cause great suffering to those who experience it. The use of the word "yaghsha" (cover or envelop) emphasizes the all-encompassing nature of this retribution. The verse serves as a stark admonition to humanity, urging them to be mindful of their actions and to strive for righteousness to avoid such a harrowing fate in the Hereafter. It is a reminder of Allah's ultimate justice and the severity of the consequences for those who reject His guidance and persist in wrongdoing.
orig: يغشى الناس هذا عذاب أليم

translation: Our Lord, remove the torment from us; indeed, we are believers.
interpretation: This verse is a plea to Allah from those who are suffering torment, acknowledging their belief and requesting relief from their affliction. It demonstrates the human tendency to turn to God in times of hardship and suffering, seeking His mercy and alleviation of their difficulties. The verse also highlights the power of faith and the believer's trust in Allah's ability to remove their torment, emphasizing the importance of maintaining belief even in the face of adversity. It serves as a reminder that Allah is the ultimate source of relief and comfort for those who sincerely believe in Him and seek His help.
orig: ربنا اكشف عنا العذاب إنا مؤمنون

translation: How will there be for them a reminder [at that time]? And there had come to them a clear Messenger.
interpretation: This verse questions how the disbelievers can be reminded of the truth on the Day of Judgment when they had already been sent a clear messenger, Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him), who conveyed the message of Islam to them in this world. It implies that they had the opportunity to heed the reminder and follow the guidance during their lifetime, but they chose to ignore and reject it. Therefore, on the Day of Judgment, when the consequences of their actions become apparent, it will be too late for them to be reminded and guided, as they had already been given sufficient opportunity and warning through the clear messenger sent to them.
orig: أنى لهم الذكرى وقد جاءهم رسول مبين

translation: Then they turned away from him and said, "[He is] a taught madman."
interpretation: This verse is referring to the disbelievers who rejected the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and his message. They turned away from him, not willing to listen to or accept the truth he brought. Instead, they dismissed him as a madman who had been taught by others to recite the Qur'an. This accusation was baseless, as the Prophet was known for his integrity and truthfulness even before his prophethood. The disbelievers' reaction stems from their arrogance and unwillingness to humble themselves before the truth, preferring to cling to their false beliefs and ways. The verse highlights the common response of those who oppose the truth when faced with clear evidence - they resort to insults and false accusations rather than engaging sincerely with the message.
orig: ثم تولوا عنه وقالوا معلم مجنون

translation: Indeed, We will remove the torment for a little. Indeed, you [disbelievers] will return [to disbelief].
interpretation: This verse warns the disbelievers that even if Allah grants them a temporary respite from punishment, they will likely revert to their disbelief and sinful ways. It highlights the ingratitude and stubbornness of those who reject faith, emphasizing that they fail to learn from the warnings and opportunities for redemption provided by Allah. The verse also implies that the ultimate consequences of persistent disbelief will be severe and inescapable, as the temporary removal of torment is not a sign of acceptance or forgiveness from Allah, but rather a test and a chance for the disbelievers to mend their ways.
orig: إنا كاشفو العذاب قليلا إنكم عائدون

translation: The Day We will strike with the greatest assault, indeed, We will take retribution.
interpretation: This verse warns of the Day of Judgment when Allah will seize the wrongdoers with a mighty onslaught and exact vengeance upon them for their misdeeds. It emphasizes the severity and decisiveness of Allah's punishment on that momentous day. The "greatest assault" signifies that there will be no escape or respite for the evildoers, and Allah's justice will be served fully and completely. It is a reminder for mankind to be mindful of their actions in this world, for they will face the consequences in the Hereafter.
orig: يوم نبطش البطشة الكبرى إنا منتقمون

translation: And We had already tried before them the people of Pharaoh, and there came to them a noble messenger,
interpretation: This verse is a reminder that Allah had tested the people of Pharaoh before the Quraysh, and He sent them a noble messenger, Moses, to guide them to the right path. However, they rejected him and faced the consequences of their disobedience. The interpretation is that the disbelievers of Mecca are being warned that they too will face a similar fate if they continue to reject the message of Prophet Muhammad, just as the people of Pharaoh did with Moses. It emphasizes the importance of heeding the call of the prophets and the consequences of rejecting their message.
orig: ولقد فتنا قبلهم قوم فرعون وجاءهم رسول كريم

translation: That; "Deliver to the servants of Allah [the message] that indeed, I am to you a trustworthy messenger."
interpretation: This verse is a command from Allah to His prophets and messengers to convey His message to mankind faithfully and truthfully. The messenger is emphasizing that he is trustworthy and honest in delivering the divine revelation without any alteration or concealment. It highlights the important responsibility of the prophets in communicating Allah's words as they were revealed, and that people can trust the message being delivered to them.
orig: أن أدوا إلي عباد الله إني لكم رسول أمين

translation: And [saying], "Do not exalt yourselves above Allah. Indeed, I have come to you with clear authority."
interpretation: This verse is a reminder for people not to be arrogant or consider themselves superior to Allah. It emphasizes the importance of humility and submission to the will of Allah. The verse also highlights the role of the prophets, who come with clear proofs and authority from Allah to guide people towards the right path. It implies that one should not let their ego or pride come in the way of accepting the truth and following the guidance of the prophets.
orig: وأن لا تعلوا على الله إني آتيكم بسلطان مبين

translation: And indeed, I seek refuge in my Lord and your Lord, lest you stone me.
interpretation: In this verse, the prophet is expressing his complete trust and reliance on Allah for protection against those who oppose and threaten him. He is affirming that Allah is not only his Lord but the Lord of all mankind, including his enemies. The act of seeking refuge is a sign of humility, submission and faith in Allah's power and mercy. The verse also implies that those who reject the message and resort to violence are in fact going against their own Lord and Creator. It serves as a reminder that ultimately, everyone will have to answer to Allah for their deeds.
orig: وإني عذت بربي وربكم أن ترجمون

translation: And if you do not believe me, then leave me alone.
interpretation: This verse is a command from Allah to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) to tell the disbelievers that if they do not believe in his message, they should simply leave him alone and not interfere with his mission. It emphasizes the principle of religious freedom and non-compulsion in Islam. The Prophet's duty is to convey the message, but he cannot force anyone to accept it. Those who choose not to believe should not harass or persecute the believers, but rather should respect their choice and leave them to practice their faith in peace.
orig: وإن لم تؤمنوا لي فاعتزلون

translation: So he called upon his Lord that these were a criminal people.
interpretation: In this verse, the prophet is calling upon Allah and informing Him that the people he is dealing with are criminals who are stubbornly rejecting the truth and committing sins. It reflects the prophet's frustration and his seeking of support and guidance from Allah in the face of a defiant and wicked people. The prophet recognizes that only Allah can judge and deal with those who persist in wrongdoing and disbelief despite the clear signs and warnings given to them.
orig: فدعا ربه أن هؤلاء قوم مجرمون

translation: So set out with My servants by night. Indeed, you will be pursued.
interpretation: This verse is a divine command to Prophet Moses to lead the Children of Israel out of Egypt during the night, as they will be pursued by Pharaoh and his army. It emphasizes the importance of trusting in God's plan and guidance, even in the face of adversity and danger. The verse also highlights the concept of divine intervention and protection for those who follow God's commands and have faith in His wisdom.
orig: فأسر بعبادي ليلا إنكم متبعون

translation: And leave the sea in stillness. Indeed, they are an army to be drowned.
interpretation: This verse is a command from Allah to Prophet Moses to leave the sea as it is, calm and still, after it had parted for the Children of Israel to cross. Allah assures Moses that the pursuing army of Pharaoh will be drowned in the sea as a punishment for their transgression and disbelief. It demonstrates Allah's power over His creation and His ability to protect His believing servants while destroying their enemies. The verse also serves as a reminder that those who oppose Allah and His messengers will face severe consequences in this world and the Hereafter.
orig: واترك البحر رهوا إنهم جند مغرقون

translation: How much they left behind of gardens and springs
interpretation: This verse is a reminder of the fleeting nature of worldly possessions and the ultimate fate that awaits all humans. It suggests that no matter how much wealth, power, or luxury one accumulates in this life, it will all be left behind when death arrives. The mention of "gardens and springs" symbolizes the material comforts and pleasures that people often pursue and become attached to. However, the verse implies that these things are temporary and insignificant in the grand scheme of existence. It serves as a call for reflection on the true purpose of life and the importance of focusing on spiritual matters rather than being consumed by worldly desires. The verse encourages humility, detachment from material possessions, and the realization that the only thing one can take to the afterlife is their deeds and relationship with God.
orig: كم تركوا من جنات وعيون

translation: And [various] crops and noble sites.
interpretation: This verse refers to the blessings that Allah has bestowed upon mankind, including the variety of crops and vegetation that grow on earth, as well as noble and honored places of worship, such as mosques and other sacred sites. It is a reminder of Allah's generosity and the abundance of His provisions, which should inspire gratitude and devotion in the hearts of believers.
orig: وزروع ومقام كريم

translation: And [in] ease were they amused
interpretation: This verse refers to the people who were given blessings and bounties by Allah, but instead of being grateful, they became distracted and amused by these worldly pleasures. They indulged in the luxuries and comforts of this life, forgetting their purpose and their duty to worship and obey Allah. This is a warning to all of us not to be deceived by the temporary attractions of this world, but to stay focused on our ultimate goal of pleasing Allah and attaining success in the Hereafter.
orig: ونعمة كانوا فيها فاكهين

translation: Thus We caused another people to inherit it.
interpretation: This verse refers to the fact that when a nation or civilization turns away from God's guidance and becomes corrupt, God may cause their downfall and allow another people to take their place and inherit their land and resources. It is a reminder that no nation or power lasts forever, and that ultimately all dominion belongs to God, who grants it to whom He wills. The verse encourages reflection on the lessons of history and the consequences of turning away from divine guidance.
orig: كذلك وأورثناها قوما آخرين

translation: So the heaven and earth wept not for them, nor were they reprieved.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the insignificance and worthlessness of the disbelievers in the sight of Allah. Their deaths were so inconsequential that even the heavens and earth did not weep for them, nor was their punishment delayed. It highlights the severity of their state and the gravity of their disbelief, that the universe itself did not mourn their loss or show them any mercy. The verse serves as a stark warning to those who reject faith, that their end will be one of ignominy and that they will face the consequences of their actions without respite.
orig: فما بكت عليهم السماء والأرض وما كانوا منظرين

translation: And We certainly saved the Children of Israel from the humiliating torment,
interpretation: This verse refers to how Allah saved the Children of Israel, i.e. the Jews, from the oppressive and humiliating persecution they faced at the hands of Pharaoh in Egypt. It is a reminder of Allah's favor upon them in rescuing them from tyranny and subjugation through His prophets Moses and Aaron. The deliverance of the Israelites is a major recurring theme in the Qur'an, emphasizing Allah's power to save the oppressed and punish the transgressors. It also serves as a lesson that the believers who remain steadfast in faith will ultimately be aided by Allah, even against the mightiest oppressors.
orig: ولقد نجينا بني إسرائيل من العذاب المهين

translation: From Pharaoh. Indeed, he was a haughty one among the transgressors.
interpretation: This verse refers to the arrogant and tyrannical nature of Pharaoh, who was a transgressor and exceeded all bounds in his oppression and disbelief. His haughtiness and pride led him to reject the signs of Allah and oppose His messengers, ultimately leading to his downfall and destruction. The verse serves as a warning to those who follow in the footsteps of Pharaoh, reminding them that arrogance and transgression will only lead to ruin in this world and the Hereafter.
orig: من فرعون إنه كان عاليا من المسرفين

translation: And We have certainly chosen them by knowledge over [all] the worlds.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah has specifically chosen and favored certain individuals or nations over others based on His divine knowledge and wisdom. It implies that this choice is not arbitrary but rather a deliberate selection by Allah, who knows the true nature and potential of His creation. The verse suggests that those chosen by Allah have unique qualities, abilities, or roles that set them apart from the rest of humanity. This choice could refer to prophets, messengers, or other righteous individuals whom Allah has selected to guide and benefit mankind.
orig: ولقد اخترناهم على علم على العالمين

translation: And We gave them of the signs that in which there was a clear trial.
interpretation: This verse suggests that Allah has given people clear signs and evidence of His existence and power, but these signs also serve as a test or trial for mankind. The signs are meant to make people reflect and acknowledge the truth, but they can also be a means of distinguishing between those who are grateful and obedient to Allah and those who are ungrateful and rebellious. The verse implies that the response to these divine signs, whether it is acceptance or rejection, will have consequences in this life and the hereafter, and that is the "clear trial" mentioned. It is a reminder for people to carefully consider the signs Allah has placed before them and to respond appropriately with faith and righteousness.
orig: وآتيناهم من الآيات ما فيه بلاء مبين

translation: Indeed, these [people] are saying
interpretation: This verse is addressing the disbelievers who make false claims and spread lies about Allah and His message. It emphasizes that their statements are baseless and untrue, and that they are merely speaking out of their own desires and ignorance, without any evidence or proof to support their claims. The verse serves as a warning to the believers not to be swayed by the empty words of the disbelievers, and to remain steadfast in their faith and trust in Allah.
orig: إن هؤلاء ليقولون

translation: It is but our first [i.e., only] death, and we will not be resurrected.
interpretation: This verse reflects the belief of those who deny the resurrection and the afterlife. They argue that death is the end of existence and that there is no coming back to life after it. It represents a materialistic worldview that rejects the idea of accountability and divine justice in the hereafter. The Qur'an refutes this notion and affirms the reality of resurrection and the final judgment, where every soul will be held responsible for its deeds in this world.
orig: إن هي إلا موتتنا الأولى وما نحن بمنشرين

translation: Then bring [back] our forefathers, if you should be truthful.
interpretation: This verse is a challenge posed by the disbelievers to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and the believers. They are essentially saying, "If you claim that there will be resurrection and judgement in the Hereafter, then prove it by bringing our ancestors back to life." It reflects their skepticism and denial of the concept of life after death. The Qur'an often mentions such arguments put forth by those who reject the divine message, highlighting their flawed reasoning and lack of faith. The demand to bring back their forefathers is an impossible task, as resurrection is an event that will occur by Allah's will on the Day of Judgement. This verse emphasizes the disbelievers' stubbornness and their unwillingness to accept the truth despite clear signs and warnings.
orig: فأتوا بآبائنا إن كنتم صادقين

translation: Are they better or the people of Tubba and those before them? We destroyed them, [for] indeed, they were criminals.
interpretation: This verse is a rhetorical question that emphasizes the fate of the disbelievers who came before the people of the Prophet Muhammad's time. It suggests that the people of Tubba and those before them, who were destroyed by Allah due to their criminal and sinful behavior, serve as a warning and example for those who continue to reject the message of Islam. The verse implies that no matter how powerful or numerous the disbelievers may seem, they will ultimately face the same fate as those who were destroyed before them if they persist in their wrongdoing and rejection of faith.
orig: أهم خير أم قوم تبع والذين من قبلهم أهلكناهم إنهم كانوا مجرمين

translation: And We did not create the heavens and earth and that between them in play.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah did not create the universe and everything in it without a profound purpose or meaning. The creation of the heavens and the earth, and all that exists between them, is not a mere act of play or amusement for Allah. Instead, it is a deliberate and purposeful creation, reflecting His wisdom, power, and divine plan. This interpretation suggests that humans should contemplate the purpose of their existence and recognize the seriousness and significance of life, rather than viewing it as a meaningless or frivolous endeavor. It encourages individuals to live their lives with a sense of responsibility, purpose, and consciousness of Allah's creation and its ultimate objectives.
orig: وما خلقنا السماوات والأرض وما بينهما لاعبين

translation: We did not create them except in truth, but most of them do not know.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that God created the heavens and the earth, and everything within them, with a profound purpose and in accordance with the ultimate truth. It suggests that there is a deeper meaning and wisdom behind the creation that many people fail to recognize or understand. The verse implies that if people were to reflect upon the intricacy, balance, and beauty of the universe, they would realize that it could not have come into existence without the will and wisdom of a Supreme Creator. However, most people remain unaware of this truth due to their lack of reflection, knowledge, or spiritual insight.
orig: ما خلقناهما إلا بالحق ولكن أكثرهم لا يعلمون

translation: Indeed, the Day of Judgement is the appointed time for all of them.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the inevitability and universality of the Day of Judgement. It is a reminder that all individuals will be held accountable for their deeds on a specific, predetermined day. The phrase "appointed time" underscores the precision and definiteness of this event, leaving no room for doubt or escape. The verse serves as a warning to humanity that they should be mindful of their actions in this world, as they will have consequences in the Hereafter. It also highlights the concept of divine justice, as everyone will be judged fairly based on their deeds, and no one will be exempt from this ultimate reckoning.
orig: إن يوم الفصل ميقاتهم أجمعين

translation: The Day when no relation will avail a relation at all, nor will they be helped.
interpretation: This verse refers to the Day of Judgment, when no person, regardless of their worldly status or relationships, will be able to help another. On that day, each individual will be held accountable for their own deeds and actions, and no intercession or assistance from others will be accepted. This emphasizes the importance of leading a righteous life and being responsible for one's own spiritual growth, as ultimately, everyone will face the consequences of their actions alone before Allah.
orig: يوم لا يغني مولى عن مولى شيئا ولا هم ينصرون

translation: Except for those on whom Allah has mercy. Indeed, He is the Exalted in Might, the Merciful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of Allah's mercy and forgiveness. It suggests that only those who receive Allah's mercy will be saved from punishment or difficulty. The verse also highlights two of Allah's attributes: His power (Al-'Azeez) and His mercy (Ar-Raheem). This implies that while Allah has the power to punish, He is also merciful and willing to forgive those who seek His forgiveness and strive to follow His path. It serves as a reminder for believers to constantly seek Allah's mercy and guidance in their lives.
orig: إلا من رحم الله إنه هو العزيز الرحيم

translation: Indeed, the tree of Zaqqum
interpretation: The tree of Zaqqum is mentioned in the Qur'an as a tree that grows in the depths of Hell. Its fruits are extremely bitter and repulsive. The mention of this tree is used as a warning and a reminder of the severe punishment that awaits the disbelievers and sinners in the Hereafter. It symbolizes the ultimate suffering, disgrace, and humiliation that they will face as a consequence of their actions and their rejection of faith in this world. The reference to this tree serves to instill fear in the hearts of those who refuse to believe and follow the straight path, urging them to repent and turn back to Allah before it is too late.
orig: إن شجرت الزقوم

translation: The food of the sinful
interpretation: This verse is referring to the food that will be given to the sinners in Hell. It is described as a food that is disgusting and repulsive, befitting their evil deeds and rejection of faith. The "food of the sinful" symbolizes the consequences and punishment that await those who turn away from God's guidance and persist in their wrongdoing. It serves as a stark reminder of the ultimate fate of the evildoers in the Hereafter.
orig: طعام الأثيم

translation: Like murky oil, boiling in the bellies.
interpretation: This verse is describing the painful punishment that awaits the disbelievers in Hell. The boiling liquid that will be forced down their throats and into their bellies is compared to murky, thick oil that scalds and burns. This interpretation highlights the severity and agony of the torment, as the consistency and temperature of this liquid is meant to inflict immense suffering. It serves as a grave warning to those who reject faith, emphasizing the consequences of their actions in the afterlife.
orig: كالمهل يغلي في البطون

translation: Like the boiling of scalding water.
interpretation: This verse uses a vivid metaphor to describe an intensely painful and agonizing situation or punishment, likening it to being submerged in boiling, scalding water. It emphasizes the severity and unrelenting nature of the torment, creating a powerful image of suffering and distress. The verse serves as a warning and reminder of the consequences of wrongdoing and the importance of righteousness to avoid such a fate.
orig: كغلي الحميم

translation: Seize him and drag him into the midst of the Blazing Fire!
interpretation: This verse is a warning to the disbelievers and wrongdoers. It depicts their fate in the Hereafter, where they will be seized by the angels and dragged forcefully into the depths of Hell. The phrase "midst of the Blazing Fire" emphasizes the severity and intensity of the punishment that awaits them. This verse serves as a reminder of the consequences of rejecting faith and indulging in sin, urging individuals to mend their ways and seek God's forgiveness before it is too late.
orig: خذوه فاعتلوه إلى سواء الجحيم

translation: Then pour over his head from the torment of scalding water.
interpretation: This verse refers to the punishment that awaits the disbelievers and wrongdoers in the Hereafter. The scalding water poured over their heads is a manifestation of the severe torment they will face as a consequence of their actions and their rejection of the truth in this worldly life. It serves as a reminder for mankind to be mindful of their deeds and to strive for righteousness, as the ultimate recompense for one's choices will be faced in the afterlife.
orig: ثم صبوا فوق رأسه من عذاب الحميم

translation: Taste! Indeed, you [considered yourself] the mighty, the noble!
interpretation: This verse is a stern rebuke to those who are arrogant and consider themselves to be mighty and noble in this world. It warns them that they will face the consequences of their actions in the Hereafter, where their worldly status and power will be of no avail. The verse emphasizes that true might and nobility belong only to Allah, and those who are haughty and proud will be humbled and disgraced. It serves as a reminder for people to be humble, recognize their own weakness and need for Allah's mercy, and to live their lives in submission to Him rather than being deluded by their own sense of self-importance.
orig: ذق إنك أنت العزيز الكريم

translation: Indeed, this is what you used to dispute.
interpretation: This verse is a rebuke to the disbelievers who denied the reality of the Day of Judgment and the Hereafter. It emphasizes that the very thing they used to mock and dismiss as impossible is now unfolding before their eyes. The verse serves as a reminder that the warnings and promises mentioned in the Qur'an and by the prophets were true all along, and that the disbelievers' skepticism and denial were unfounded. It highlights the regret and remorse they will feel for not having believed and prepared for this inevitable reality during their worldly lives.
orig: إن هذا ما كنتم به تمترون

translation: Indeed, the righteous will be in a secure place.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the ultimate reward for those who lead a righteous life, following the teachings of Islam and maintaining a strong connection with Allah. The "secure place" mentioned here is generally understood to be Paradise or Heaven, where the righteous will find eternal peace, comfort, and happiness. This interpretation highlights the importance of living a life guided by Islamic principles, as it will lead to a blessed afterlife free from the hardships and trials of this worldly existence. The verse serves as a reminder and motivation for believers to strive for righteousness in all aspects of their lives.
orig: إن المتقين في مقام أمين

translation: In gardens and springs
interpretation: This verse is referring to the eternal bliss and rewards that await the righteous believers in Paradise. The "gardens" mentioned here are the lush, beautiful gardens of Paradise, filled with delights beyond imagination. The "springs" are the clear, flowing springs of pure water that run through these gardens, providing refreshment and tranquility. This verse is a reminder of the ultimate goal for believers, encouraging them to strive for righteousness in this life to attain these everlasting rewards in the Hereafter.
orig: في جنات وعيون

translation: They will wear [garments of] fine silk and brocade, facing each other.
interpretation: This verse describes the attire of the inhabitants of Paradise. The people of Paradise will be dressed in the finest clothing made of silk and brocade, indicating their high status and the luxury they will enjoy. The mention of them "facing each other" suggests a sense of social harmony, unity, and the joy of being in the company of righteous companions. This verse portrays the reward of the believers in the afterlife, emphasizing the beauty, comfort, and delight they will experience as a result of their faith and good deeds in this world.
orig: يلبسون من سندس وإستبرق متقابلين

translation: And We will marry them to fair ones with large, [beautiful] eyes.
interpretation: This verse refers to one of the rewards that the righteous believers will receive in Paradise. Allah will bless them with spouses who possess great beauty, indicated by the description of their eyes being "large" and "beautiful". The term "ḥūr ʿīn" has been interpreted to mean fair-skinned companions with a deep contrast between the whiteness of their eyes and the blackness of their pupils. This reward of a beautiful spouse is a gift of Allah to the believers in the eternal life of the Hereafter, reflective of their faith and good deeds in the worldly life.
orig: كذلك وزوجناهم بحور عين

translation: They will call therein for every [kind of] fruit - safe and secure.
interpretation: In Paradise, the believers will have access to all kinds of fruits without any fear or danger. They will be able to enjoy these blessings in a state of complete peace and security, without worrying about anything harming them or causing them distress. This verse highlights the abundance, variety, and safety of the provisions in Paradise, emphasizing the eternal bliss and comfort that the righteous will experience as a reward for their faith and good deeds in this world.
orig: يدعون فيها بكل فاكهة آمنين

translation: They will not taste death therein except the first death, and He will have protected them from the punishment of Hellfire.
interpretation: This verse refers to the believers in Paradise, who will not experience death again after their first death in the worldly life. Allah will protect them from the torment of Hell, granting them eternal life in bliss and safety. It emphasizes the mercy and reward that Allah bestows upon the righteous, shielding them from any further suffering or pain in the Hereafter. The verse brings comfort and hope to the believers, assuring them of the everlasting peace and protection they will enjoy in Paradise as a result of their faith and good deeds in this life.
orig: لا يذوقون فيها الموت إلا الموتة الأولى ووقاهم عذاب الجحيم

translation: As a favor from your Lord. That is the great attainment.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the ultimate success and triumph in the Hereafter is a favor and blessing from Allah. It is not something that can be earned solely through one's own efforts, but rather it is a gift from the Almighty bestowed upon those whom He chooses. Attaining Allah's pleasure, forgiveness, and the reward of Paradise is the greatest achievement one can aspire for, and it is only possible by His grace and mercy. This realization should instill humility, gratitude, and a deeper sense of reliance on Allah in the hearts of the believers.
orig: فضلا من ربك ذلك هو الفوز العظيم

translation: And We have certainly made the Qur'an easy in your tongue that they might be reminded.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah has made the Qur'an easy to understand and recite in the Arabic language, which was the native tongue of Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and his people. The purpose of this is so that the people may reflect upon its teachings, take heed of its guidance, and be reminded of their purpose in life and their ultimate return to Allah. By making the Qur'an accessible and comprehensible, Allah shows His mercy and desire for humanity to be guided to the straight path.
orig: فإنما يسرناه بلسانك لعلهم يتذكرون

translation: So watch; indeed, they are watching [as well].
interpretation: This verse is a warning and a reminder that just as the disbelievers are watching and waiting for the downfall of the Prophet and the believers, the believers should also be vigilant and watchful. They should not let their guard down, but rather should be prepared for any challenges or plots against them. At the same time, it is a reassurance that Allah is aware of the schemes of the enemies and will protect and support the believers. The verse emphasizes the importance of patience, perseverance, and trust in Allah's plan in the face of adversity.
orig: فارتقب إنهم مرتقبون

translation: Ha, Meem.
interpretation: This verse consists of two Arabic letters, "Ha" and "Meem". Many chapters of the Qur'an begin with such letter combinations, known as "Al-Muqatta'at" or "The Disjoined Letters". The exact meaning and purpose of these letters is not explicitly mentioned in the Qur'an or Hadith. Scholars have proposed various interpretations, such as them being symbols of divine secrets, attention-grabbers for the listener, or abbreviations for certain phrases or names of Allah. Ultimately, the true meaning is known only to Allah, and the letters serve as a reminder of the miraculous nature and divine origin of the Qur'an.
orig: حم

translation: The revelation of the Book is from Allah, the Exalted in Might, the Wise.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the Qur'an is a divine revelation from Allah, who is described as "Al-Aziz" (the Exalted in Might) and "Al-Hakim" (the Wise). It highlights the supreme power and wisdom of Allah, indicating that the Qur'an is not a product of human creation but rather a guidance sent down by the Almighty. The mention of these attributes of Allah reinforces the authenticity and authority of the Qur'an as a sacred scripture.
orig: تنزيل الكتاب من الله العزيز الحكيم

translation: Indeed, in the heavens and earth are signs for the believers.
interpretation: This verse points to the countless signs and wonders in the universe that testify to the existence, power, and wisdom of Allah. The intricate design, perfect balance, and magnificent beauty found in the heavens and the earth serve as undeniable proofs for those who have faith. These signs invite believers to reflect upon the creation and strengthen their belief in the Creator. The verse encourages the faithful to ponder over the universe, as it can deepen their spiritual connection with Allah and reinforce their conviction in His oneness and supremacy.
orig: إن في السماوات والأرض لآيات للمؤمنين

translation: And in the creation of yourselves and what He disperses of moving creatures are signs for people who are certain [in faith].
interpretation: This verse points to the signs of Allah's existence, power, and wisdom that can be found in the creation of human beings and in the various animals that Allah has scattered throughout the earth. These signs serve as proof and evidence for those who have certainty in their faith. They reflect on these signs and see in them the handiwork of the Creator, increasing their conviction in Allah's oneness and strengthening their belief. The intricate design and perfect balance found in the human body and in the diverse animal kingdom testify to Allah's supreme knowledge and ability, leaving no doubt for those with unwavering faith.
orig: وفي خلقكم وما يبث من دابة آيات لقوم يوقنون

translation: And [in] the alternation of night and day and [in] what Allah sends down from the sky of provision and gives life thereby to the earth after its lifelessness and [in His] directing of the winds are signs for a people who reason.
interpretation: This verse points to the signs of Allah's power and wisdom that are evident in the natural world. The alternation of night and day, the rain that brings life to the earth, and the movement of the winds are all indications of a higher power at work. These signs are meant for people who use their intellect and reason to reflect upon the world around them and recognize the existence and majesty of the Creator. The verse encourages humans to ponder and appreciate the intricate balance and design in the universe, which should lead them to acknowledge and worship the One who created it all.
orig: واختلاف الليل والنهار وما أنزل الله من السماء من رزق فأحيا به الأرض بعد موتها وتصريف الرياح آيات لقوم يعقلون

translation: These are the verses of Allah which We recite to you in truth. Then in what statement after Allah and His verses will they believe?
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the divine nature of the Qur'an and its verses, affirming that they are revealed by Allah to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) with absolute truth. It challenges those who reject the Qur'an to consider what other message or statement they would believe in if they do not accept the words of Allah and His clear signs. The verse implies that there is no higher truth or more authentic source of guidance than the Qur'an, as it comes directly from the Creator Himself. It serves as a reminder for people to reflect upon the authenticity and superiority of Allah's words over any other discourse or belief system.
orig: تلك آيات الله نتلوها عليك بالحق فبأي حديث بعد الله وآياته يؤمنون

translation: Woe to every sinful liar.
interpretation: This verse is a stern warning and condemnation of those who habitually lie and commit sins. "Woe" here signifies impending punishment and misery that awaits such individuals. The terms "sinful" and "liar" highlight that these people not only lie profusely but also engage in various sinful activities. It emphasizes that dishonesty and sinfulness often go hand-in-hand. The verse serves as a reminder that Allah disapproves of lying and sinning, and those who indulge in such behavior will face severe consequences in this world and the Hereafter unless they repent and reform themselves.
orig: ويل لكل أفاك أثيم

translation: He hears the verses of Allah recited to him, then persists arrogantly as if he had not heard them. So give him tidings of a painful punishment.
interpretation: This verse is a warning to those who hear the words of Allah, but persist in their arrogance and disbelief, acting as if they have not heard the truth. It suggests that those who stubbornly refuse to accept the message of Islam, despite being exposed to its teachings, will face a severe punishment in the Hereafter. The verse emphasizes the importance of humility, open-mindedness, and willingness to accept the truth when it is presented, rather than allowing pride and ego to blind one to the reality of Allah's message.
orig: يسمع آيات الله تتلى عليه ثم يصر مستكبرا كأن لم يسمعها فبشره بعذاب أليم

translation: And when he learns something of Our verses, he takes them in ridicule. Those will have a humiliating punishment.
interpretation: This verse is a stern warning to those who mock and ridicule the verses and signs of Allah when they come to know of them. Instead of pondering over their meanings and taking guidance from them, they make fun of them out of arrogance and ignorance. Allah declares that such people will face a humiliating punishment in the Hereafter as a recompense for their disbelief and derision of His revelations. It highlights the severity of ridiculing the Qur'an and the need to approach it with utmost respect and reverence.
orig: وإذا علم من آياتنا شيئا اتخذها هزوا أولئك لهم عذاب مهين

translation: Before them is Hell, and what they had earned will not avail them at all nor what they had taken besides Allah as allies. And they will have a great punishment.
interpretation: This verse warns that those who reject faith and do evil deeds will face the punishment of Hell in the Hereafter. All their worldly gains, possessions, and the false gods or idols they relied upon besides Allah will be of no benefit to them. They will suffer a severe torment as a consequence of their disbelief and misdeeds. It emphasizes that only faith in Allah and righteous actions can save one from the Fire and earn His pleasure and reward in the eternal life to come.
orig: من ورائهم جهنم ولا يغني عنهم ما كسبوا شيئا ولا ما اتخذوا من دون الله أولياء ولهم عذاب عظيم

translation: It is guidance. And those who disbelieve in the signs of their Lord will have a painful punishment of foul nature.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the Qur'an serves as a guide for humanity. However, those who reject its teachings and the signs of Allah will face severe consequences in the form of a painful and terrible punishment in the Hereafter. The interpretation highlights the importance of faith and the consequences of denying the truth revealed by Allah in the Qur'an.
orig: هذا هدى والذين كفروا بآيات ربهم لهم عذاب من رجز أليم

translation: It is Allah who subjected to you the sea so that ships may sail upon it by His command and that you may seek of His bounty; and perhaps you will be grateful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the power and benevolence of Allah, who has made the seas and oceans navigable for mankind. It is by His command that ships are able to sail smoothly on the water, allowing people to travel, trade, and benefit from the resources that the sea provides. These blessings are a reminder for humans to be grateful to Allah for His favors and bounties. The verse encourages people to appreciate and acknowledge the gifts that Allah has bestowed upon them, as gratitude is a fundamental aspect of faith in Islam. It also highlights the idea that everything in the universe is under Allah's control and subject to His will.
orig: الله الذي سخر لكم البحر لتجري الفلك فيه بأمره ولتبتغوا من فضله ولعلكم تشكرون

translation: And He has subjected to you whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth - all from Him. Indeed in that are signs for a people who give thought.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the idea that everything in the universe has been created by Allah and subjected to the benefit of mankind. It is a reminder for people to reflect upon the countless blessings and signs of Allah's existence, power, and mercy. The verse encourages humans to use their intellect and contemplate the purpose behind the creation of the universe and their own existence. By recognizing these signs and utilizing the resources provided by Allah in a responsible manner, one can attain a deeper understanding of the Creator and live a life of gratitude and submission to His will.
orig: وسخر لكم ما في السماوات وما في الأرض جميعا منه إن في ذلك لآيات لقوم يتفكرون

translation: Say to those who have believed that they [should] forgive those who expect not the days of Allah so that He may recompense a people for what they used to earn.
interpretation: This verse encourages the believers to forgive those who do not believe in the Day of Judgment or the power of Allah. The reason for this is so that Allah can judge and recompense people based on their deeds and actions in this world, without the believers taking matters into their own hands or holding grudges. It promotes patience, mercy and leaving the ultimate judgment to Allah alone.
orig: قل للذين آمنوا يغفروا للذين لا يرجون أيام الله ليجزي قوما بما كانوا يكسبون

translation: Whoever does righteousness - it is for his [own] soul; and whoever does evil [does so] against it. Then to your Lord you will be returned.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the concept of individual responsibility in Islam. Each person is accountable for their own actions, whether good or bad. Righteous deeds benefit one's own soul, while evil deeds harm it. Ultimately, everyone will return to Allah on the Day of Judgment to face the consequences of their deeds in this world. This verse serves as a reminder for individuals to strive for righteousness and refrain from evil, as they will be held responsible for their choices and actions in the Hereafter.
orig: من عمل صالحا فلنفسه ومن أساء فعليها ثم إلى ربكم ترجعون

translation: And We did certainly give the Children of Israel the Scripture and judgement and prophethood, and We provided them with good things and preferred them over the worlds.
interpretation: This verse highlights the special status and blessings bestowed upon the Children of Israel (Bani Israil) by Allah. They were granted divine scriptures for guidance, wisdom to judge between right and wrong, and were honored with many prophets among them. Allah also provided them with lawful, good provisions and favored them over other nations during their time. This underscores the importance of gratitude for Allah's blessings and the responsibility that comes with being granted such favors, which should be met with faith and righteous deeds.
orig: ولقد آتينا بني إسرائيل الكتاب والحكم والنبوة ورزقناهم من الطيبات وفضلناهم على العالمين

translation: And We had given them clear proofs of the matter, but they did not differ except after knowledge had come to them, out of jealous animosity between themselves. Indeed, your Lord will judge between them on the Day of Resurrection concerning that over which they used to differ.
interpretation: This verse highlights the fact that even after receiving clear signs and proofs from Allah, people still differed and disputed due to their own envy, jealousy, and selfish desires. It suggests that the pursuit of worldly gains and ego can lead people astray, causing them to reject the truth even when it is evident. The verse also emphasizes the ultimate justice of Allah, reminding us that He will judge between the differing parties on the Day of Judgment, resolving their disputes and holding them accountable for their actions and beliefs in this world. It serves as a warning against letting our own biases and desires cloud our judgment and a reminder to stay steadfast on the path of truth and righteousness.
orig: وآتيناهم بينات من الأمر فما اختلفوا إلا من بعد ما جاءهم العلم بغيا بينهم إن ربك يقضي بينهم يوم القيامة فيما كانوا فيه يختلفون

translation: Then We put you, [O Muhammad], on an ordained way concerning the matter [of religion]; so follow it and do not follow the inclinations of those who do not know.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of following the divine law and guidance revealed to Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) through the Qur'an and his Sunnah. It instructs the Prophet to adhere to the straight path ordained by Allah and not to be swayed by the desires, opinions, or whims of those who lack true knowledge and understanding of the divine message. The verse highlights the significance of staying committed to the teachings of Islam and resisting the temptation to deviate from the ordained way, even if it means going against the inclinations of others who may not have the same level of faith or understanding.
orig: ثم جعلناك على شريعة من الأمر فاتبعها ولا تتبع أهواء الذين لا يعلمون

translation: Indeed, they will not avail you against Allah at all. And indeed, the wrongdoers are allies of one another; but Allah is the protector of the righteous.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that those who engage in wrongdoing and injustice cannot protect or benefit each other against Allah's judgment and punishment. Their alliances and mutual support are ultimately futile in the face of divine justice. In contrast, Allah is the true protector and ally of those who are righteous and mindful of Him. The verse highlights the importance of aligning oneself with righteousness and piety, as it is only through this that one can attain Allah's protection and support. It also serves as a warning against associating with or relying on those who engage in wrongdoing, as their alliance will prove useless in the ultimate reckoning.
orig: إنهم لن يغنوا عنك من الله شيئا وإن الظالمين بعضهم أولياء بعض والله ولي المتقين

translation: These are insights for the people, and guidance and mercy for a people who are certain [in faith].
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the Qur'an provides clear evidence, guidance, and mercy for those who have strong faith and conviction in Allah. The teachings and lessons within the Qur'an serve as a source of enlightenment, directing believers towards the right path. Moreover, the Qur'an is a manifestation of Allah's mercy, offering solace and comfort to those who firmly believe in its message. The verse highlights that the benefits of the Qur'an are reserved for those who approach it with certainty and unwavering faith, as they are the ones who truly appreciate and internalize its wisdom.
orig: هذا بصائر للناس وهدى ورحمة لقوم يوقنون

translation: Or do those who commit evils think that We will make them like those who have believed and done righteous deeds - [make them] equal in their life and their death? Evil is that which they judge.
interpretation: This verse is a rhetorical question that highlights the flawed thinking of those who commit evil deeds. They mistakenly believe that Allah will treat them the same as those who have faith and do good deeds, both in this life and in the Hereafter. The verse emphasizes that it is a grave misjudgment to assume that the evildoers and the righteous will have the same fate. It implies that the evildoers will face the consequences of their actions and will be distinguished from the believers who will be rewarded for their righteousness. The verse serves as a warning to those who persist in wrongdoing, reminding them that their actions will not go unaccounted for and that divine justice will prevail.
orig: أم حسب الذين اجترحوا السيئات أن نجعلهم كالذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات سواء محياهم ومماتهم ساء ما يحكمون

translation: And Allah created the heavens and the earth in truth and so that every soul may be recompensed for what it has earned, and they will not be wronged.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the purpose and justice behind Allah's creation of the universe. The heavens and earth were created with truth and wisdom, not merely in vain or for sport. Moreover, every soul will be fairly judged and recompensed for its deeds, good or evil, without any injustice. No one will be wronged or treated unfairly by Allah. This highlights the importance of doing righteous deeds and avoiding sins, as each person is ultimately accountable to their Creator for how they lived their life. It also underscores Allah's perfect justice and that the Day of Judgment will rectify all wrongs and inequities that may have occurred in the worldly life.
orig: وخلق الله السماوات والأرض بالحق ولتجزى كل نفس بما كسبت وهم لا يظلمون

translation: Have you seen he who has taken as his god his [own] desire, and Allah has sent him astray due to knowledge and has set a seal upon his hearing and his heart and put over his vision a veil? So who will guide him after Allah? Then will you not be reminded?
interpretation: This verse is a warning against following one's own desires and whims instead of the guidance of Allah. It suggests that those who prioritize their own desires over the teachings of Islam have been led astray by Allah Himself, as a consequence of their own actions and choices. Their senses and faculties of understanding have been sealed, making them unable to perceive the truth. The verse emphasizes that once someone has reached this state of being misguided by Allah, no one else can guide them back to the right path. It serves as a reminder for believers to be mindful of their actions and to prioritize obedience to Allah over their own desires.
orig: أفرأيت من اتخذ إلهه هواه وأضله الله على علم وختم على سمعه وقلبه وجعل على بصره غشاوة فمن يهديه من بعد الله أفلا تذكرون
