translation: And they say, "There is not but our worldly life; we die and live, and nothing destroys us except time." And they have of that no knowledge; they are only assuming.
interpretation: This verse is a critique of those who reject the concept of an afterlife and divine accountability. They believe that life is limited to this worldly existence, where people are born, live, and die, and that the passage of time is the only thing that ultimately destroys them. However, the verse points out that they have no real knowledge or evidence to support this belief; it is merely an assumption on their part. This highlights the importance of faith and the acknowledgment of a higher power and purpose beyond the confines of this temporary world. The verse implies that those who hold such a view are short-sighted and fail to recognize the deeper spiritual realities that exist beyond the physical realm.
orig: وقالوا ما هي إلا حياتنا الدنيا نموت ونحيا وما يهلكنا إلا الدهر وما لهم بذلك من علم إن هم إلا يظنون

translation: And when Our clear verses are recited to them, their argument is no other than that they say, "Bring [back] our forefathers, if you should be truthful."
interpretation: This verse is addressing the disbelievers who, when presented with clear evidence and signs of Allah's truth, resort to a flawed argument. Instead of reflecting on the message, they demand that their deceased ancestors be brought back to life, as if that would prove the truthfulness of the message. It highlights their stubbornness and irrational thinking, as they are unable to accept the truth even when it is clearly presented to them. They cling to their ancestral ways and traditions, refusing to acknowledge the validity of the Qur'anic message. This response demonstrates their lack of sincerity in seeking the truth and their determination to remain in disbelief.
orig: وإذا تتلى عليهم آياتنا بينات ما كان حجتهم إلا أن قالوا ائتوا بآبائنا إن كنتم صادقين

translation: Say, "Allah gives you life, then causes you to die, then He will assemble you for the Day of Resurrection, about which there is no doubt, but most of the people do not know."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the power and control of Allah over life and death. It reminds us that Allah is the one who grants us life, and He is also the one who will cause us to die at the appointed time. The verse also affirms the certainty of the Day of Resurrection, when all humans will be gathered before Allah for judgment. Despite the clarity of this message, the verse points out that most people remain ignorant of this truth, either due to their lack of faith or their preoccupation with worldly affairs. It serves as a wake-up call for mankind to recognize Allah's sovereignty and to prepare for the inevitable Day of Reckoning by leading a righteous life in accordance with His guidance.
orig: قل الله يحييكم ثم يميتكم ثم يجمعكم إلى يوم القيامة لا ريب فيه ولكن أكثر الناس لا يعلمون

translation: And to Allah belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth. And the Day the Hour appears - that Day the falsifiers will lose.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute sovereignty and ownership of Allah over the entire universe, including the heavens and the earth. It also highlights the consequences that await those who reject the truth and follow falsehood on the Day of Judgment. When the appointed Hour arrives, and the world as we know it comes to an end, those who have been deluded by their own false beliefs and have denied the signs of Allah will face the ultimate loss. They will realize the gravity of their mistake, but it will be too late for them to make amends. This verse serves as a reminder for believers to stay steadfast in their faith and for those who have strayed to turn back to the path of righteousness before it is too late.
orig: ولله ملك السماوات والأرض ويوم تقوم الساعة يومئذ يخسر المبطلون

translation: And you will see every nation kneeling [from fear]. Every nation will be called to its record [and will be told], "Today you are being recompensed for what you used to do."
interpretation: This verse speaks about the Day of Judgment, when all nations will be held accountable for their deeds. Each nation will be brought before Allah and presented with a record of their actions in this world. They will be in a state of fear and submission, kneeling before their Lord. The verse emphasizes the concept of individual and collective responsibility, as every person and every nation will face the consequences of their choices and actions. It serves as a reminder that we should be mindful of our deeds in this life, as they will determine our fate in the Hereafter. The verse also highlights the justice of Allah, as He will recompense each individual and nation according to their deeds, without any injustice or favoritism.
orig: وترى كل أمة جاثية كل أمة تدعى إلى كتابها اليوم تجزون ما كنتم تعملون

translation: This, Our record, speaks about you in truth. Indeed, We were having transcribed whatever you used to do.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of one's deeds and actions in this worldly life. It states that Allah has assigned angels to record every deed performed by an individual, both good and bad. This record will be presented on the Day of Judgment as irrefutable evidence of one's conduct in this world. It serves as a reminder that every action, no matter how small or insignificant it may seem, is being recorded and will be accounted for in the Hereafter. Therefore, one should strive to perform righteous deeds and refrain from sinful actions, as they will ultimately determine one's fate in the eternal life to come.
orig: هذا كتابنا ينطق عليكم بالحق إنا كنا نستنسخ ما كنتم تعملون

translation: As for those who believed and did righteous deeds, their Lord will admit them into His mercy. That is the clear attainment.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the reward that awaits the believers who have faith and do good deeds in accordance with that faith. Allah, in His infinite mercy and grace, will admit these righteous believers into Paradise (Jannah). Attaining Allah's mercy, forgiveness and the bliss of Paradise is described as the supreme success and the ultimate triumph one can achieve in the Hereafter. It signifies the fulfillment of the true purpose of life and the realization of the believer's deepest hopes and aspirations. The verse underscores the importance of combining faith with righteous actions, as both are essential for attaining salvation and earning Allah's pleasure and mercy.
orig: فأما الذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات فيدخلهم ربهم في رحمته ذلك هو الفوز المبين

translation: But as for those who disbelieved, [the decree will say], "Were not Our verses recited to you, but you were arrogant and became a people of criminals?"
interpretation: This verse is a stern warning to those who rejected the message of Islam despite having heard the verses of the Quran recited to them. It suggests that their disbelief was not due to ignorance, but rather a result of their arrogance and criminal nature. The rhetorical question "Were not Our verses recited to you?" emphasizes that they had ample opportunity to embrace the truth, but chose to turn away from it. The verse implies that on the Day of Judgment, the disbelievers will be confronted with their deliberate rejection of God's signs and will have no excuse for their actions. It serves as a reminder that one's response to the divine message in this life will have consequences in the Hereafter.
orig: وأما الذين كفروا أفلم تكن آياتي تتلى عليكم فاستكبرتم وكنتم قوما مجرمين

translation: And when it is said, "Indeed, the promise of Allah is truth and the Hour [is coming] - no doubt about it," you say, "We know not what is the Hour. We assume only assumption, and we are not convinced."
interpretation: This verse is addressing the disbelievers who, when reminded of Allah's promise of the Day of Judgment and the Hour, express their doubts and uncertainties. They claim that they have no sure knowledge about the Hour and that their opinions are based merely on conjecture and assumption, not on any firm conviction. This highlights their lack of faith and their reluctance to accept the reality of the Hereafter, as they prefer to remain in a state of denial and skepticism rather than acknowledging the truth of Allah's message and preparing for the inevitable reckoning.
orig: وإذا قيل إن وعد الله حق والساعة لا ريب فيها قلتم ما ندري ما الساعة إن نظن إلا ظنا وما نحن بمستيقنين

translation: And the evil consequences of what they did will appear to them, and they will be enveloped by what they used to ridicule.
interpretation: This verse warns that those who commit evil deeds and mock the truth will ultimately face the negative repercussions of their actions. The very things they ridiculed and dismissed will come back to haunt them, and they will be unable to escape the consequences. It emphasizes the idea that everyone is accountable for their choices and that divine justice will prevail, even if it is not immediately apparent. The verse serves as a reminder to be mindful of one's actions and to take the message of Islam seriously, rather than treating it with derision or contempt.
orig: وبدا لهم سيئات ما عملوا وحاق بهم ما كانوا به يستهزئون

translation: And it will be said, "Today We will forget you as you forgot the meeting of this Day of yours, and your refuge is the Fire, and for you there are no helpers."
interpretation: This verse is a stern warning to those who reject faith and forget the Day of Judgment. It emphasizes that on that Day, they will be abandoned by Allah, just as they had abandoned His remembrance in their worldly life. They will find no refuge except in the Fire of Hell, and there will be no one to help or support them. This interpretation highlights the severe consequences of neglecting one's spiritual obligations and turning away from the truth, as well as the ultimate justice that will be served on the Day of Reckoning.
orig: وقيل اليوم ننساكم كما نسيتم لقاء يومكم هذا ومأواكم النار وما لكم من ناصرين

translation: That is because you took the verses of Allah in ridicule, and worldly life deluded you. So that Day, they will not be removed from it, nor will they be asked to appease [Allah].
interpretation: This verse is a stern warning to those who mock and ridicule the signs and verses of Allah, and are deluded by the temporary pleasures of this worldly life. On the Day of Judgment, they will face the consequences of their actions and will not be able to escape the punishment of the Hellfire. They will not be given another chance to repent or appease Allah, as the time for that has passed. This highlights the importance of taking the Qur'an and its teachings seriously, and not being distracted by the fleeting nature of this world at the expense of one's eternal fate in the Hereafter.
orig: ذلكم بأنكم اتخذتم آيات الله هزوا وغرتكم الحياة الدنيا فاليوم لا يخرجون منها ولا هم يستعتبون

translation: Then praise be to Allah, Lord of the heavens and Lord of the earth, Lord of the worlds.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that all praise and gratitude belong to Allah alone, as He is the Lord and Creator of the heavens, the earth, and all the worlds. It highlights His absolute sovereignty and dominion over the entire universe. By acknowledging Allah as the Lord of all worlds, it underscores the belief in His unique divinity and the obligation of all creation to submit to Him in worship and obedience. This verse serves as a powerful reminder for believers to direct their praise and thankfulness towards Allah, recognizing His boundless mercy, wisdom, and power in creating and sustaining the universe.
orig: فلله الحمد رب السماوات ورب الأرض رب العالمين

translation: And to Him belongs [all] grandeur within the heavens and the earth, and He is the Exalted in Might, the Wise.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah alone possesses true greatness and majesty in the entire universe. His grandeur is evident in the vastness and perfection of the heavens and the earth. The mention of His attributes "al-'Azeez" (the Exalted in Might) and "al-Hakeem" (the Wise) further accentuates His supreme power and wisdom. It serves as a reminder for humankind to humble themselves before the Almighty, recognizing His absolute authority and wisdom in all affairs. Believers should strive to glorify Him and submit to His will, as He alone is deserving of all praise and reverence.
orig: وله الكبرياء في السماوات والأرض وهو العزيز الحكيم

translation: Ha, Meem.
interpretation: These disjoined letters "Ha" and "Meem" are among the miracles of the Qur'an, and none but Allah (Alone) knows their meanings. They indicate the unique inimitability of the Qur'an's language and style, challenging mankind to produce anything similar if they claim the Qur'an is not from Allah. These letters also draw the attention of the listener and invite reflection upon the profound message that follows.
orig: حم

translation: The revelation of the Book is from Allah, the Exalted in Might, the Wise.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the Qur'an is a divine revelation from Allah, who is described as "Al-Aziz" (the Exalted in Might) and "Al-Hakim" (the Wise). It highlights the supreme power and wisdom of Allah, indicating that the contents of the Qur'an are not from human origin but rather from the All-Knowing Creator. The verse establishes the authority and authenticity of the Qur'an as a guidance for mankind, as it comes from the ultimate source of wisdom and power.
orig: تنزيل الكتاب من الله العزيز الحكيم

translation: We did not create the heavens and earth and what is between them except in truth and [for] a specified term. But those who disbelieve, from that of which they are warned, are turning away.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that God created the universe with a divine purpose and for a fixed period of time. It implies that the creation is not without meaning or in vain, but rather it is based on truth and wisdom. The verse also points out that despite the clear signs and warnings, the disbelievers choose to ignore and turn away from the message, heedless of the consequences. It suggests that their denial and disregard for the truth will not change the reality of God's creation and purpose.
orig: ما خلقنا السماوات والأرض وما بينهما إلا بالحق وأجل مسمى والذين كفروا عما أنذروا معرضون

translation: Say, "Have you considered that which you invoke besides Allah? Show me what they have created of the earth; or did they have partnership in [creation of] the heavens? Bring me a scripture [revealed] before this or a [remaining] trace of knowledge, if you should be truthful."
interpretation: This verse challenges those who worship other than Allah to provide evidence that their objects of worship have created anything on earth or have any share in the creation of the heavens. It demands that they produce an earlier scripture or any remnant of knowledge that supports their polytheistic beliefs. The implication is that they cannot do so, as there is no valid evidence for worshipping anyone or anything besides Allah, the sole Creator and Sustainer of the universe. This verse emphasizes the fundamental Islamic principle of Tawheed (monotheism) and the logical inconsistency of polytheism.
orig: قل أرأيتم ما تدعون من دون الله أروني ماذا خلقوا من الأرض أم لهم شرك في السماوات ائتوني بكتاب من قبل هذا أو أثارة من علم إن كنتم صادقين

translation: And who is more astray than he who invokes besides Allah those who will not respond to him until the Day of Resurrection, and they, of their invocation, are unaware.
interpretation: This verse highlights the futility and misguidance of those who invoke or worship entities other than Allah. It emphasizes that these false deities or idols are unable to respond to the supplications of their worshippers, not only in this life but even until the Day of Judgment. The verse also points out the heedlessness of these worshippers, as they are unaware that their invocations are in vain and that their false gods are entirely oblivious to their prayers and pleas. This interpretation underscores the importance of directing one's worship and devotion solely to Allah, the only true God worthy of worship, who alone can hear and respond to the supplications of His servants.
orig: ومن أضل ممن يدعو من دون الله من لا يستجيب له إلى يوم القيامة وهم عن دعائهم غافلون

translation: And when the people are gathered [on the Day of Judgement], they [false deities] will be enemies to them, and they will be deniers of their worship.
interpretation: This verse speaks about the Day of Judgment when all the people will be gathered before Allah. On that day, the false deities that people used to worship will become their enemies and will disown their worshippers. The idols and false gods will declare that they had no knowledge of the worship that was being done to them. This highlights the futility of worshipping anyone or anything other than Allah. It also emphasizes the fact that on the Day of Judgment, no one will be able to help another, and each individual will be accountable for their own deeds. The false deities will not be able to intercede or provide any benefit to their worshippers, leaving them in a state of loss and regret for their misdirected worship in the worldly life.
orig: وإذا حشر الناس كانوا لهم أعداء وكانوا بعبادتهم كافرين

translation: And when Our clear verses are recited to them, those who disbelieve say of the truth when it has come to them, "This is obvious magic."
interpretation: This verse is referring to the disbelievers who, when confronted with the clear and evident signs and verses of Allah in the Qur'an, dismiss it as mere magic or sorcery rather than acknowledging it as the truth from their Lord. It highlights their stubborn refusal to accept the message despite its clarity, and their attempts to discredit it by attributing it to magic. This is a reflection of their deep-rooted disbelief and their unwillingness to submit to the truth of Allah's revelation.
orig: وإذا تتلى عليهم آياتنا بينات قال الذين كفروا للحق لما جاءهم هذا سحر مبين

translation: Or do they say, "He has invented it"? Say, "If I have invented it, you do not possess for me [the power of protection] from Allah at all. He is most knowing of that in which you are involved. Sufficient is He as Witness between me and you, and He is the Forgiving the Merciful."
interpretation: This verse is addressing the accusations made by the disbelievers that the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) had fabricated the Qur'an himself. Allah instructs the Prophet to respond by saying that if he had indeed invented it, then they would have no power to protect him from Allah's punishment, as Allah is fully aware of what they are saying and doing. The verse emphasizes that Allah is sufficient as a witness between the Prophet and his accusers, and that He is Forgiving and Merciful to those who repent and believe in Him. The interpretation is that the Qur'an is a divine revelation and not the product of human invention, and that those who reject it will be held accountable by Allah, while those who accept it and follow its guidance will be forgiven and shown mercy.
orig: أم يقولون افتراه قل إن افتريته فلا تملكون لي من الله شيئا هو أعلم بما تفيضون فيه كفى به شهيدا بيني وبينكم وهو الغفور الرحيم

translation: Say, "I am not something original among the messengers, nor do I know what will be done with me or with you. I only follow that which is revealed to me, and I am not but a clear warner."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the humanity and humility of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him). He is instructed to inform people that he is not unique among the prophets and messengers sent by Allah. Like them, he does not possess knowledge of the unseen or the future, including what will happen to him or his followers. His role is to faithfully convey the divine message revealed to him and warn people of the consequences of rejecting it. This highlights the Prophet's submission to Allah and his role as a messenger, not a divine being with extraordinary powers.
orig: قل ما كنت بدعا من الرسل وما أدري ما يفعل بي ولا بكم إن أتبع إلا ما يوحى إلي وما أنا إلا نذير مبين

translation: Say, "Have you considered: if the Qur'an was from Allah, and you disbelieved in it while a witness from the Children of Israel has testified to something similar and believed while you were arrogant...?" Indeed, Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people.
interpretation: This verse challenges the disbelievers to consider the possibility that the Qur'an is indeed from Allah, despite their rejection of it. It points out that even a witness from the Children of Israel, who would be familiar with previous scriptures, has recognized the truth of the Qur'an and believed in it. The verse implies that the disbelievers' rejection stems from their arrogance rather than any lack of evidence. It concludes with a warning that Allah does not guide those who persist in wrongdoing and reject the truth out of pride and stubbornness. The verse highlights the importance of humility and openness to the truth, rather than allowing one's ego and preconceptions to blind them to the signs of Allah's guidance.
orig: قل أرأيتم إن كان من عند الله وكفرتم به وشهد شاهد من بني إسرائيل على مثله فآمن واستكبرتم إن الله لا يهدي القوم الظالمين

translation: And those who disbelieve say of those who believe, "If it had [truly] been good, they would not have preceded us to it." And when they are not guided by it, they will say, "This is an ancient falsehood."
interpretation: This verse highlights the arrogance and stubbornness of the disbelievers. They claim that if the message of Islam were truly good, they would have been the first to embrace it. Their pride prevents them from accepting the truth, even when it is clear. Instead of acknowledging their own shortcomings, they dismiss the message as an old lie, refusing to be guided by it. This attitude reflects their deep-rooted resistance to the truth and their unwillingness to humble themselves before the guidance of Allah.
orig: وقال الذين كفروا للذين آمنوا لو كان خيرا ما سبقونا إليه وإذ لم يهتدوا به فسيقولون هذا إفك قديم

translation: And before it was the Book of Moses to lead and as a mercy. And this is a Book confirming it in an Arabic tongue to warn those who have wronged and as good tidings to the doers of good.
interpretation: This verse highlights the continuity and consistency of the divine message across different prophets and scriptures. It affirms that the Qur'an, revealed in Arabic, serves as a confirmation of the earlier revelations, particularly the Torah given to Moses. The Qur'an's role is twofold: it serves as a warning to those who have strayed from the righteous path and indulged in wrongdoing, urging them to mend their ways and turn to God in repentance. Simultaneously, it brings glad tidings to those who do good deeds and lead a virtuous life, assuring them of God's pleasure and rewards in this world and the hereafter. The verse emphasizes the universality of the Qur'anic message, as it is conveyed in clear Arabic language, making it accessible and comprehensible to the people it was initially addressed to, while also bearing a message that transcends time and speaks to all of humanity.
orig: ومن قبله كتاب موسى إماما ورحمة وهذا كتاب مصدق لسانا عربيا لينذر الذين ظلموا وبشرى للمحسنين

translation: Indeed, those who have said, "Our Lord is Allah" and then remained on a right course - there will be no fear concerning them, nor will they grieve.
interpretation: This verse is a reassurance and a promise from Allah to those who have unwavering faith and remain steadfast in their belief and righteous deeds. It emphasizes that those who acknowledge Allah as their Lord and stay committed to the right path will be free from fear and grief in the Hereafter. They will not fear the consequences of their actions or grieve over what they may have lost in this worldly life. Instead, they will find comfort, peace, and happiness in the eternal life of the Hereafter, knowing that they have earned Allah's pleasure and mercy through their faith and good deeds.
orig: إن الذين قالوا ربنا الله ثم استقاموا فلا خوف عليهم ولا هم يحزنون

translation: Those are the companions of Paradise, abiding eternally therein as reward for what they used to do.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that those who have lived righteously and followed the teachings of Islam will be granted eternal residence in Paradise as a reward for their good deeds and actions in this worldly life. It highlights the direct correlation between one's conduct in this life and their ultimate fate in the Hereafter, stressing the importance of leading a virtuous life in accordance with Islamic principles to attain the everlasting bliss of Paradise.
orig: أولئك أصحاب الجنة خالدين فيها جزاء بما كانوا يعملون

translation: And We have enjoined upon man, to his parents, good treatment. His mother carried him with hardship and gave birth to him with hardship, and his gestation and weaning [period] is thirty months. [He grows] until, when he reaches maturity and reaches [the age of] forty years, he says, "My Lord, enable me to be grateful for Your favor which You have bestowed upon me and upon my parents and to work righteousness of which You will approve and make righteous for me my offspring. Indeed, I have repented to You, and indeed, I am of the Muslims."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of being kind and respectful to one's parents, recognizing the hardships and sacrifices they endured in raising their child. It also highlights the significance of reaching the age of forty, a time when one becomes more reflective and appreciative of God's blessings. The verse encourages individuals to express gratitude to Allah for His favors, both upon themselves and their parents, and to strive for righteousness in their actions and in their offspring. It concludes with the importance of repentance and submission to Allah as a Muslim.
orig: ووصينا الإنسان بوالديه إحسانا حملته أمه كرها ووضعته كرها وحمله وفصاله ثلاثون شهرا حتى إذا بلغ أشده وبلغ أربعين سنة قال رب أوزعني أن أشكر نعمتك التي أنعمت علي وعلى والدي وأن أعمل صالحا ترضاه وأصلح لي في ذريتي إني تبت إليك وإني من المسلمين

translation: Those are the ones from whom We will accept the best of what they did and overlook their misdeeds, [their being] among the companions of Paradise. [That is] the promise of truth which they had been promised.
interpretation: This verse speaks about the righteous believers whose good deeds Allah will accept and whose sins He will forgive. They are promised Paradise as a reward for their faith and good works. This is a true promise from Allah that will certainly be fulfilled, giving the believers hope and encouragement to persist in righteousness. It shows Allah's mercy and generosity in accepting the best of their deeds while overlooking their shortcomings. The verse emphasizes that Paradise is attained through both Allah's grace and the individual's sincere efforts in faith and good works.
orig: أولئك الذين نتقبل عنهم أحسن ما عملوا ونتجاوز عن سيئاتهم في أصحاب الجنة وعد الصدق الذي كانوا يوعدون

translation: And the one who says to his parents, "Uff to you; do you promise me that I will be brought forth [from the earth] when generations before me have already passed on [into oblivion]?" while they call to Allah for help [and to their son], "Woe to you! Believe! Indeed, the promise of Allah is truth." But he says, "This is not but legends of the former people."
interpretation: This verse is a stern warning to those who are ungrateful and disrespectful towards their parents. It describes a person who dismisses the idea of resurrection and afterlife, despite his parents' pleas to believe in Allah's promise. The person arrogantly rejects their advice, considering the concept of resurrection as mere legends of the past. This highlights the importance of treating one's parents with utmost respect and gratitude, as well as having faith in Allah's promises, even if they seem impossible or beyond our comprehension. The verse also emphasizes that disbelief and ingratitude towards one's parents are grave sins that can lead to severe consequences in the hereafter.
orig: والذي قال لوالديه أف لكما أتعدانني أن أخرج وقد خلت القرون من قبلي وهما يستغيثان الله ويلك آمن إن وعد الله حق فيقول ما هذا إلا أساطير الأولين

translation: Those are the ones upon whom the word has come into effect, [who will be] among nations which had passed on before them of jinn and men. Indeed, they [all] were losers.
interpretation: This verse speaks about those individuals who have been destined for Hell due to their disbelief and evil deeds. The "word" refers to Allah's decree that such people will face the consequences of their actions. These condemned souls belong to past nations of both jinn (spirits) and men who lived before the time of Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him). The verse emphasizes that all those who reject faith and choose to engage in sin are ultimately losers in both this world and the Hereafter, as they have failed to fulfill the purpose of their existence and will face the eternal punishment of Hell.
orig: أولئك الذين حق عليهم القول في أمم قد خلت من قبلهم من الجن والإنس إنهم كانوا خاسرين

translation: And for all there are degrees for what they have done, and [it is] so that He may fully compensate them for their deeds, and they will not be wronged.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the concept of divine justice in Islam. It asserts that every individual will be assigned a rank or status in the Hereafter based on their deeds and actions in this worldly life. God will ensure that each person is fully recompensed for their good or bad deeds, without any injustice or oppression. This interpretation highlights the importance of personal responsibility and accountability in Islam, as well as the belief in the ultimate fairness and justice of God's judgment. It serves as a reminder for believers to strive for righteousness and good deeds, knowing that their efforts will be duly rewarded in the afterlife.
orig: ولكل درجات مما عملوا وليوفيهم أعمالهم وهم لا يظلمون

translation: And the Day those who disbelieved are exposed to the Fire [it will be said], "You exhausted your pleasures during your worldly life and enjoyed them, so this Day you will be awarded the punishment of [extreme] humiliation because you were arrogant upon the earth without right and because you were defiantly disobedient."
interpretation: This verse is a stern warning to those who reject faith and indulge in worldly pleasures without regard for the Hereafter. It emphasizes that the disbelievers will face the consequences of their arrogance and disobedience on the Day of Judgment. They will be exposed to the Fire and will receive the punishment of extreme humiliation as a recompense for their wrongdoings. The verse serves as a reminder that the temporary pleasures of this world should not be prioritized over one's faith and obedience to Allah, as the ultimate accountability lies in the Hereafter.
orig: ويوم يعرض الذين كفروا على النار أذهبتم طيباتكم في حياتكم الدنيا واستمتعتم بها فاليوم تجزون عذاب الهون بما كنتم تستكبرون في الأرض بغير الحق وبما كنتم تفسقون

translation: And mention, [O Muhammad], the brother of 'Aad, when he warned his people in the [region of] al-Ahqaf - and warners had already passed on before him and after him - [saying], "Do not worship except Allah. Indeed, I fear for you the punishment of a terrible day."
interpretation: This verse is a reminder to the Prophet Muhammad to mention the story of the prophet Hud, who was sent to the people of 'Aad. Hud warned his people, who lived in the region of al-Ahqaf, to worship none but Allah alone, just as other warners before and after him had done. He feared that if they continued in their polytheism and rejection of the message, they would suffer a severe punishment on a tremendous day, the Day of Judgment. The verse emphasizes the importance and continuity of the prophetic message throughout history, calling people to monotheism and warning them of the consequences of disobedience to Allah.
orig: واذكر أخا عاد إذ أنذر قومه بالأحقاف وقد خلت النذر من بين يديه ومن خلفه ألا تعبدوا إلا الله إني أخاف عليكم عذاب يوم عظيم

translation: They said, "Have you come to delude us away from our gods? Then bring us what you promise us, if you should be of the truthful."
interpretation: This verse reflects the skepticism and defiance of the disbelievers towards the message of the Prophet. They accuse him of trying to lead them astray from their traditional beliefs and challenge him to bring about the punishment he warns them of if he is truthful in his claim. It shows their stubbornness in clinging to their false deities and their unwillingness to accept the truth, demanding immediate proof instead of reflecting on the signs and wisdom in the Prophet's teachings. The verse highlights the difficulty faced by the prophets in conveying the message to those who are deeply entrenched in their misguided ways.
orig: قالوا أجئتنا لتأفكنا عن آلهتنا فأتنا بما تعدنا إن كنت من الصادقين

translation: He said, "Knowledge is only with Allah, and I convey to you what I was sent with, but I see you are a people behaving ignorantly."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that true knowledge and wisdom belong to Allah alone. The messenger, in this case Moses, acknowledges that he is merely conveying the message entrusted to him by Allah. He observes that the people he is addressing are acting in ignorance, possibly by rejecting the divine message or by attributing knowledge and power to beings other than Allah. This highlights the importance of humility, recognizing human limitations in knowledge, and the need to seek guidance from Allah and His messengers to overcome ignorance and attain true understanding.
orig: قال إنما العلم عند الله وأبلغكم ما أرسلت به ولكني أراكم قوما تجهلون

translation: But when they saw it as a cloud approaching their valleys, they said, "This is a cloud bringing us rain." Rather, it is that for which you were impatient: a wind, within it a painful punishment.
interpretation: This verse is a warning to those who are hasty in seeking punishment or disbelieving in God's signs. The people mentioned saw the approaching cloud and assumed it would bring them rain and relief, but instead it brought a severe wind carrying a painful punishment. This highlights the consequences of impatience and the importance of having faith and trust in God's plan, even if it may not align with one's immediate desires or expectations. It also emphasizes that what may appear as a blessing or relief can actually be a form of divine retribution for those who persist in disbelief and wrongdoing.
orig: فلما رأوه عارضا مستقبل أوديتهم قالوا هذا عارض ممطرنا بل هو ما استعجلتم به ريح فيها عذاب أليم

translation: It destroyed everything by the command of its Lord, so they became such that nothing could be seen except their dwellings. Thus do We recompense the criminal people.
interpretation: This verse serves as a warning and a reminder of the ultimate fate of those who persist in wrongdoing and reject the signs and guidance of Allah. It emphasizes that when the punishment of Allah befalls a nation due to their sins and transgressions, it is so complete and devastating that nothing remains except the ruins of their dwellings, serving as a testament to their destruction. This interpretation highlights the idea of divine justice, where the evildoers are recompensed for their deeds, and their end serves as a lesson for others to take heed and mend their ways before it is too late.
orig: تدمر كل شيء بأمر ربها فأصبحوا لا يرى إلا مساكنهم كذلك نجزي القوم المجرمين

translation: And We had certainly established them in such as We have not established you, and We made for them hearing and vision and hearts. But their hearing and vision and hearts availed them not from anything [of the punishment] when they were [continually] rejecting the signs of Allah; and they were enveloped by what they used to ridicule.
interpretation: This verse is a reminder that even if people are given great power, wealth, and faculties like hearing, sight, and intellect, none of it will be of any benefit if they persist in denying and mocking the signs and revelations of Allah. The people referred to had been given all these blessings, but because they arrogantly rejected faith, they were eventually overtaken by the very punishment they used to scoff at. It emphasizes that the real success and protection comes from belief, obedience to Allah, and heeding His warnings - not from worldly strengths that are temporary and can be taken away at any time if one turns away from divine guidance.
orig: ولقد مكناهم فيما إن مكناكم فيه وجعلنا لهم سمعا وأبصارا وأفئدة فما أغنى عنهم سمعهم ولا أبصارهم ولا أفئدتهم من شيء إذ كانوا يجحدون بآيات الله وحاق بهم ما كانوا به يستهزئون

translation: And We have already destroyed what surrounds you of [those] cities, and We have diversified the signs [or verses] that perhaps they might return [to faith].
interpretation: This verse is a reminder from Allah that He has destroyed many nations and civilizations before as a consequence of their disbelief and rejection of His messages. The ruins of these destroyed cities served as a visible sign and warning to the people of Mecca and surrounding areas. Allah varied and repeated His signs, revelations, and warnings so that people might recognize the truth, repent from their wrongdoings, and return to the path of righteousness and belief in Him. It emphasizes the importance of learning from history and heeding the signs and warnings sent by Allah to avoid a similar fate of destruction.
orig: ولقد أهلكنا ما حولكم من القرى وصرفنا الآيات لعلهم يرجعون

translation: Then why did those they took besides Allah as deities by way of approach [to Him] not aid them? But they had strayed from them. And that was their falsehood and what they were inventing.
interpretation: This verse is questioning the logic of those who worship idols and false gods instead of Allah. It points out that these false deities were of no help to their worshippers in their time of need, exposing the futility and deception of idolatry. The idols that they invented and worshipped were nothing but lies and fabrications that led them astray from the truth of worshipping the one true God, Allah. It highlights how their false beliefs and practices were baseless and could not provide them any real benefit or support.
orig: فلولا نصرهم الذين اتخذوا من دون الله قربانا آلهة بل ضلوا عنهم وذلك إفكهم وما كانوا يفترون

translation: And [mention, O Muhammad], when We directed to you a few of the jinn, listening to the Qur'an. And when they attended it, they said, "Listen quietly." And when it was concluded, they went back to their people as warners.
interpretation: This verse indicates that Allah directed a group of jinn to listen to the Qur'an being recited by Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ). Upon hearing it, they were so moved that they called upon each other to listen attentively. After the recitation was over, they returned to their fellow jinn to warn them of the consequences of disbelief and to convey the message of Islam. This highlights the universal nature of the Qur'an's message, which is meant not only for humans but for jinn as well. It also demonstrates the power and impact of the Qur'an on those who sincerely listen to and reflect upon its verses.
orig: وإذ صرفنا إليك نفرا من الجن يستمعون القرآن فلما حضروه قالوا أنصتوا فلما قضي ولوا إلى قومهم منذرين

translation: They said, "O our people, indeed we have heard a [recited] Book revealed after Moses confirming what was before it which guides to the truth and to a straight path.
interpretation: This verse speaks about a group of people who have heard of a scripture that was revealed after the time of Moses, which confirms the teachings that came before it. This scripture is described as guiding towards the truth and the straight path. The interpretation is that this verse is likely referring to the Qur'an, which Muslims believe was revealed after the time of Moses and confirms the divine messages that preceded it, such as the Torah. The Qur'an is seen as a guide for humanity, leading them towards the truth of monotheism and righteousness, and away from falsehood and sin.
orig: قالوا يا قومنا إنا سمعنا كتابا أنزل من بعد موسى مصدقا لما بين يديه يهدي إلى الحق وإلى طريق مستقيم

translation: O our people, respond to the Messenger of Allah and believe in him; He will forgive for you your sins and protect you from a painful punishment.
interpretation: This verse is a call to the people to accept the message of Islam and follow the teachings of Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him). It promises forgiveness of sins and protection from the torment of Hell for those who heed this call and sincerely believe in Allah and His Messenger. The verse emphasizes the importance and urgency of responding positively to the invitation of faith, as it is the path to salvation and success in this life and the Hereafter. It reminds us that the opportunity to repent and turn to Allah is available, and encourages us to seize it before it is too late.
orig: يا قومنا أجيبوا داعي الله وآمنوا به يغفر لكم من ذنوبكم ويجركم من عذاب أليم

translation: And whoever does not respond to the Caller of Allah will not cause failure [to Him] upon earth, and he will not have besides Him any protectors. Those are in manifest error.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that those who reject Allah's call and guidance are in clear misguidance. They cannot escape from Allah's power and authority on earth, nor do they have any protectors besides Him who can save them from the consequences of their disbelief. Their rejection of the truth will not harm or affect Allah in any way, as He is Self-Sufficient and Independent of His creation. The verse serves as a warning to those who turn away from Allah's message, reminding them of their vulnerability and the error of their ways.
orig: ومن لا يجب داعي الله فليس بمعجز في الأرض وليس له من دونه أولياء أولئك في ضلال مبين

translation: Do they not see that Allah, who created the heavens and earth and did not tire from creating them, is able to give life to the dead? Yes, indeed! He is over all things competent.
interpretation: This verse is a powerful reminder of Allah's omnipotence and His ability to resurrect the dead. It encourages people to reflect on the marvel of Allah's creation of the vast heavens and earth, which He created without any fatigue. The argument presented is that if Allah can effortlessly create such immense and complex entities, then surely He is more than capable of bringing the dead back to life. The verse affirms with certainty that Allah has power over all things, including resurrection, emphasizing His absolute authority and dominion. It serves as a call to humankind to recognize and submit to Allah's supreme power and to have faith in the reality of the Day of Judgment, when all souls will be brought back to life to face the consequences of their deeds.
orig: أولم يروا أن الله الذي خلق السماوات والأرض ولم يعي بخلقهن بقادر على أن يحيي الموتى بلى إنه على كل شيء قدير

translation: And the Day those who disbelieved are exposed to the Fire [it will be said], "Is this not the truth?" They will say, "Yes, by our Lord." He will say, "Then taste the punishment because you used to disbelieve."
interpretation: This verse speaks of the fate of the disbelievers on the Day of Judgment. When they are confronted with the reality of the Fire of Hell, they will be asked if this punishment is not indeed the truth that they denied in their worldly life. They will have no choice but to acknowledge it, admitting their Lord's truth and justice. As a consequence of their disbelief and rejection of the truth, God will command them to taste the torment of the Fire. This verse serves as a severe warning for those who reject faith, emphasizing that denying God's signs and revelations will lead to a painful punishment in the Hereafter.
orig: ويوم يعرض الذين كفروا على النار أليس هذا بالحق قالوا بلى وربنا قال فذوقوا العذاب بما كنتم تكفرون

translation: So be patient, [O Muhammad], as were those of determination among the messengers and do not be impatient for them. It will be - on the Day they see that which they are promised - as though they had not remained [in the world] except an hour of a day. [This is] notification. And will [any] be destroyed except the defiantly disobedient people?
interpretation: This verse encourages the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) to remain steadfast and patient in the face of adversity and opposition, just as the previous prophets of strong will did. On the Day of Judgment, when the disbelievers face the consequences of their actions, their time on earth will seem fleeting, as if it were only an hour of a day. This verse serves as a warning and reminder that ultimately, only those who persistently rebel against God's guidance will be destroyed. It emphasizes the importance of patience, faith, and obedience to God's message, even in the face of hardships and challenges.
orig: فاصبر كما صبر أولو العزم من الرسل ولا تستعجل لهم كأنهم يوم يرون ما يوعدون لم يلبثوا إلا ساعة من نهار بلاغ فهل يهلك إلا القوم الفاسقون

translation: Those who disbelieve and avert [people] from the way of Allah - He will waste their deeds.
interpretation: This verse warns that those who reject faith in Allah and actively try to prevent others from following His path will ultimately have their good deeds rendered worthless by Allah. It emphasizes that disbelief and working against the cause of Allah leads to the futility and loss of any virtuous actions one may have done, as they are not based on true faith and sincerity towards Allah. The verse highlights the gravity of not only disbelieving, but also obstructing others from the truth, and that such people will face the severe consequence of having their deeds nullified in the Hereafter.
orig: الذين كفروا وصدوا عن سبيل الله أضل أعمالهم

translation: And those who have believed and done righteous deeds and believed in what was revealed to Muhammad, and it is the truth from their Lord, He will remove from them their misdeeds and amend their condition.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that those who have true faith, which is demonstrated through righteous actions and belief in the divine revelation sent to Prophet Muhammad, will be forgiven for their past sins. Allah will erase their misdeeds and rectify their spiritual state. This highlights the importance of coupling faith with good deeds, and the mercy of Allah towards those who sincerely believe and strive to follow the teachings revealed to the final prophet. It offers hope and motivation to the believers that their efforts will be rewarded with purification and spiritual improvement in the sight of Allah.
orig: والذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات وآمنوا بما نزل على محمد وهو الحق من ربهم كفر عنهم سيئاتهم وأصلح بالهم

translation: That is because those who disbelieve follow falsehood, and those who believe follow the truth from their Lord. Thus does Allah present to the people their comparisons.
interpretation: This verse highlights the fundamental difference between those who reject faith and those who accept it. The disbelievers are misguided, following falsehood and deception, while the believers adhere to the truth that comes from Allah. The verse emphasizes that Allah presents these comparisons and examples to humanity so that they may reflect upon the consequences of their choices and actions. It serves as a reminder that following the path of truth leads to righteousness and divine guidance, whereas following falsehood leads to misguidance and straying from the right path. The verse encourages introspection and urges individuals to align themselves with the truth that comes from their Lord.
orig: ذلك بأن الذين كفروا اتبعوا الباطل وأن الذين آمنوا اتبعوا الحق من ربهم كذلك يضرب الله للناس أمثالهم

translation: So when you meet those who disbelieve [in battle], strike [their] necks until, when you have inflicted slaughter upon them, then secure their bonds, and either [confer] favor afterwards or ransom [them] until the war lays down its burdens. That [is the command]. And if Allah had willed, He could have taken vengeance upon them [Himself], but [He ordered armed struggle] to test some of you by means of others. And those who are killed in the cause of Allah - never will He waste their deeds.
interpretation: This verse is providing guidance to Muslims on how to conduct themselves during times of war and battle against those who disbelieve and oppose Islam. It instructs Muslims to fight fiercely and decisively against the enemy until they are thoroughly subdued. At that point, Muslims have the option to either show mercy and release the prisoners, or to ransom them until the conflict is over. The verse also notes that God could easily defeat the enemies Himself if He so willed, but He commands the Muslims to fight in order to test and strengthen their faith. Finally, it reassures those who are killed in battle for the cause of Allah that their sacrifices and good deeds will not be forgotten or go to waste, and they will be justly rewarded by God.
orig: فإذا لقيتم الذين كفروا فضرب الرقاب حتى إذا أثخنتموهم فشدوا الوثاق فإما منا بعد وإما فداء حتى تضع الحرب أوزارها ذلك ولو يشاء الله لانتصر منهم ولكن ليبلو بعضكم ببعض والذين قتلوا في سبيل الله فلن يضل أعمالهم

translation: He will guide them and improve their condition.
interpretation: This verse suggests that Allah will provide guidance to those who seek it and will improve their spiritual and mental well-being. It implies that by following the path of righteousness and submitting to Allah's will, one can attain inner peace, contentment, and a sense of purpose in life. The verse offers hope and reassurance to believers, indicating that Allah is merciful and will support those who strive to live according to His teachings.
orig: سيهديهم ويصلح بالهم

translation: And admit them to Paradise, which He has made known to them.
interpretation: In this verse, Allah promises the believers that He will admit them into Paradise, a place of eternal bliss and comfort. The phrase "which He has made known to them" suggests that Allah has already given the believers a glimpse or knowledge of what Paradise entails, through descriptions in the Qur'an and the teachings of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him). This prior knowledge of Paradise acts as a motivator for the believers to strive in Allah's cause and remain steadfast in their faith, knowing that their ultimate goal is to attain this eternal reward that Allah has prepared for them.
orig: ويدخلهم الجنة عرفها لهم

translation: O you who have believed, if you support Allah, He will support you and plant firmly your feet.
interpretation: This verse is a promise from Allah to the believers that if they support His cause and strive in His way, He will grant them His aid and support, making them firm and steadfast. It emphasizes the reciprocal nature of the relationship between Allah and the believers - as they stand by Him, He will stand by them and strengthen their resolve in the face of challenges and adversities. This divine assurance is meant to encourage and motivate the believers to remain committed to their faith and to actively work towards upholding the values and teachings of Islam, with the knowledge that Allah will be their helper and protector.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا إن تنصروا الله ينصركم ويثبت أقدامكم

translation: But those who disbelieve - for them is misery, and He will waste their deeds.
interpretation: This verse warns that those who reject faith in Allah will face a miserable fate in this world and the Hereafter. Their good deeds will be rendered worthless because they were not done for the sake of Allah or in accordance with His guidance. Without faith, even seemingly righteous actions have no value in Allah's sight and will not benefit a person in the afterlife. The verse emphasizes the gravity of disbelief and how it leads to ultimate loss and despair.
orig: والذين كفروا فتعسا لهم وأضل أعمالهم

translation: That is because they disliked what Allah revealed, so He rendered their deeds worthless.
interpretation: This verse points to the fact that the disbelievers rejected and opposed the revelation sent down by Allah, which was the truth. As a result of their aversion and hostility towards the divine message, Allah made all their actions and good deeds futile and void of any reward, because they lacked the essential component of faith and submission to Allah's will. It emphasizes that no matter how righteous one's deeds may appear externally, if they are not built upon the foundation of belief in Allah and acceptance of His guidance, they will carry no weight or value in the sight of Allah.
orig: ذلك بأنهم كرهوا ما أنزل الله فأحبط أعمالهم

translation: Have they not traveled through the land and observed how was the end of those before them? Allah destroyed [everything] over them, and for the disbelievers is something comparable.
interpretation: This verse is a reminder for people to reflect on the fate of past civilizations that were destroyed by Allah due to their disbelief and wrongdoings. It encourages people to travel and observe the ruins of these civilizations, and to take heed of the lessons that can be learned from their destruction. The verse also serves as a warning to those who choose to disbelieve in Allah, that they may face a similar fate if they do not change their ways and follow the path of righteousness. It emphasizes the power and judgment of Allah, and the consequences of going against His commands.
orig: أفلم يسيروا في الأرض فينظروا كيف كان عاقبة الذين من قبلهم دمر الله عليهم وللكافرين أمثالها

translation: That is because Allah is the protector of those who have believed and because the disbelievers have no protector.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the stark contrast between the believers and the disbelievers in terms of their relationship with Allah. It asserts that Allah is the guardian, protector, and supporter of those who have faith in Him and follow His guidance. On the other hand, it highlights that the disbelievers have no such protector or ally, as they have rejected Allah and His message. This interpretation underscores the importance of faith and the consequences of disbelief, reminding believers of the privilege and security they enjoy under Allah's guardianship, while warning disbelievers of their vulnerability and lack of support in the face of divine judgment.
orig: ذلك بأن الله مولى الذين آمنوا وأن الكافرين لا مولى لهم

translation: Indeed, Allah will admit those who believe and do righteous deeds to gardens beneath which rivers flow, but those who disbelieve enjoy themselves and eat as grazing livestock eat, and the Fire will be a residence for them.
interpretation: This verse highlights the stark contrast between the ultimate fate of the believers and the disbelievers. Those who have faith and do good deeds will be rewarded by Allah with Paradise, where they will enjoy eternal bliss in gardens with flowing rivers. On the other hand, the disbelievers are only concerned with worldly pleasures and satisfying their desires, living like cattle without any higher purpose. They indulge in temporary enjoyments, but their final abode will be the Fire of Hell. This interpretation emphasizes the importance of faith and righteousness in attaining salvation and the consequences of rejecting faith and leading a hedonistic life.
orig: إن الله يدخل الذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات جنات تجري من تحتها الأنهار والذين كفروا يتمتعون ويأكلون كما تأكل الأنعام والنار مثوى لهم

translation: And how many a city was stronger than your city [Makkah] which drove you out? We destroyed them; and there was no helper for them.
interpretation: This verse is a reminder to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and his followers that even though they were driven out of Makkah by its powerful inhabitants, Allah has the power to destroy even stronger cities and civilizations. It emphasizes that no matter how strong or powerful a nation or people may seem, they are not invincible and can be brought down by Allah's will. The verse also implies that those who oppose the message of Islam and persecute the believers will face the consequences of their actions, and there will be no one to help or save them from Allah's punishment.
orig: وكأين من قرية هي أشد قوة من قريتك التي أخرجتك أهلكناهم فلا ناصر لهم

translation: Then is he who is on clear evidence from his Lord like him for whom his evil deed has been beautified and they follow their [own] desires?
interpretation: This verse highlights the contrast between those who are guided by clear evidence from Allah and those who are misled by their own desires and the allure of their evil deeds. Those with clear evidence have a strong foundation of faith and are less likely to be swayed by temptations or self-interest. On the other hand, those who follow their desires and are attracted to the superficial beauty of their misdeeds are more prone to straying from the right path. The verse reminds us to be mindful of our intentions and actions, seeking to align ourselves with divine guidance rather than being misled by our own whims and short-sighted desires.
orig: أفمن كان على بينة من ربه كمن زين له سوء عمله واتبعوا أهواءهم

translation: The example of Paradise, which the righteous have been promised, is [that] beneath it rivers flow. Its fruit is lasting, and its shade. That is the consequence for the righteous, and the consequence for the disbelievers is the Fire.
interpretation: This verse describes the eternal reward that awaits the righteous believers in Paradise. It emphasizes the stark contrast between the blissful fate of those who are mindful of God, and the severe punishment that awaits the disbelievers in Hell. Paradise is depicted as a place of abundant flowing rivers, perpetual fruits, and comforting shade - a perfect abode of peace and fulfillment, and the ultimate manifestation of God's mercy and grace for those who lived righteously. The disbelievers, on the other hand, will suffer the torment of the Fire as a direct consequence of their rejection of faith and good deeds. The verse serves as both an invitation and warning, encouraging mankind to strive for righteousness to attain Paradise, and to avoid the path of disbelief that leads to the agonizing punishment of Hell.
orig: مثل الجنة التي وعد المتقون فيها أنهار من ماء غير آسن وأنهار من لبن لم يتغير طعمه وأنهار من خمر لذة للشاربين وأنهار من عسل مصفى ولهم فيها من كل الثمرات ومغفرة من ربهم كمن هو خالد في النار وسقوا ماء حميما فقطع أمعاءهم

translation: And among them are those who listen to you, until when they depart from you, they say to those who were given knowledge, "What has he said just now?" Those are the ones over whose hearts Allah has sealed, and they have followed their [own] desires.
interpretation: This verse refers to the hypocrites who pretend to listen attentively to the Prophet's teachings, but in reality, they do not internalize or understand the message. After leaving the Prophet's presence, they mockingly ask the knowledgeable believers about what was just said, revealing their true lack of interest and comprehension. Allah has sealed their hearts due to their insincerity and hypocrisy, and they prioritize following their own whims and desires over the guidance of Islam. This highlights the importance of genuine intentions and openness in seeking and applying religious knowledge.
orig: ومنهم من يستمع إليك حتى إذا خرجوا من عندك قالوا للذين أوتوا العلم ماذا قال آنفا أولئك الذين طبع الله على قلوبهم واتبعوا أهواءهم

translation: And those who are guided - He increases them in guidance and gives them their righteousness.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that those who are already on the right path and seek guidance from Allah, He will increase them in guidance and bless them with righteousness (taqwa). Taqwa is the quality of being mindful of Allah, fearing Him, and thus leading a life of obedience and submission to His commands. Allah rewards those who strive to follow His guidance by granting them more guidance and instilling in their hearts the quality of taqwa, which helps them stay on the straight path and protects them from deviating. This verse encourages believers to continuously seek Allah's guidance and strive to increase in righteousness.
orig: والذين اهتدوا زادهم هدى وآتاهم تقواهم

translation: Do they then wait for anything other than the Hour, that it should come upon them suddenly? But some of its portents have already come, and when it is on them, how can they benefit then by their reminder?
interpretation: This verse is a warning to those who reject the truth and the signs of Allah. It reminds them that the Hour, meaning the Day of Judgment, will come suddenly and unexpectedly. Some of the signs of its approach have already appeared, yet they continue to ignore them. When the Hour does arrive, it will be too late for them to benefit from the reminders and warnings they were given. They will have lost their chance for repentance and salvation. This verse emphasizes the importance of heeding the signs and preparing for the Day of Judgment before it is too late.
orig: فهل ينظرون إلا الساعة أن تأتيهم بغتة فقد جاء أشراطها فأنى لهم إذا جاءتهم ذكراهم

translation: So know, [O Muhammad], that there is no deity except Allah and ask forgiveness for your sin and for the believing men and believing women. And Allah knows of your movement and your resting place.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the fundamental principle of Islam, which is the oneness of Allah (Tawheed). It commands Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) to have firm conviction in this belief and to seek forgiveness for his own sins and the sins of the believing men and women. The verse also reminds us that Allah is all-knowing, aware of our every action and movement, as well as our resting place, both in this world and the hereafter. This knowledge should inspire us to be mindful of our deeds and to constantly seek Allah's forgiveness and guidance.
orig: فاعلم أنه لا إله إلا الله واستغفر لذنبك وللمؤمنين والمؤمنات والله يعلم متقلبكم ومثواكم

translation: Those who believe say, "Why has a surah not been sent down?" But when a precise surah is revealed and fighting is mentioned therein, you see those in whose hearts is hypocrisy looking at you with a look of one overcome by death. And more appropriate for them [would have been]
interpretation: This verse is addressing the hypocrites who questioned why a surah was not revealed, but when a clear surah was revealed that mentioned fighting, their true nature was exposed. They looked at the Prophet with fear and aversion, as if they were facing death. This reaction showed that their faith was weak and that they were not willing to make sacrifices for the cause of Islam. The verse suggests that it would have been better for them to have been sincere and obedient rather than hypocritical and reluctant to fight for their faith.
orig: ويقول الذين آمنوا لولا نزلت سورة فإذا أنزلت سورة محكمة وذكر فيها القتال رأيت الذين في قلوبهم مرض ينظرون إليك نظر المغشي عليه من الموت فأولى لهم

translation: Obedience and good words. And when the matter [of fighting] was determined, if they had been true to Allah, it would have been better for them.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of obedience to Allah and speaking in a good manner. It suggests that when a decision has been made, especially regarding matters like fighting in the cause of Allah, it is best for the believers to be sincere and faithful to Allah. Being true to one's commitment and devotion to Allah, even in difficult situations, is ultimately better for an individual than going back on one's word or hesitating in fulfilling one's duty. The verse implies that loyalty and sincerity to Allah lead to the best outcomes, even if the path may seem challenging at the time.
orig: طاعة وقول معروف فإذا عزم الأمر فلو صدقوا الله لكان خيرا لهم

translation: So would you perhaps, if you turned away, cause corruption on earth and sever your [ties of] relationship?
interpretation: This verse is a warning to those who turn away from the path of Allah and His messenger. It suggests that such people are likely to spread corruption and mischief on earth, and sever their ties of kinship. Cutting off family relations is considered a major sin in Islam. The verse implies that faith and righteousness should lead to maintaining good relations, especially with one's relatives, and spreading peace and goodness on earth. Turning away from Allah's guidance, on the other hand, results in the opposite - spreading corruption and cutting off the ties of kinship that Allah has commanded to maintain.
orig: فهل عسيتم إن توليتم أن تفسدوا في الأرض وتقطعوا أرحامكم

translation: Those are the ones whom Allah has cursed, so He deafened them and blinded their vision.
interpretation: This verse refers to those who have earned Allah's anger and punishment due to their persistent disbelief, disobedience, and rejection of the truth. As a result of their actions, Allah has sealed their hearts, making them spiritually deaf and blind. They are unable to hear the guidance or see the signs that would lead them to the right path. This metaphorical deafness and blindness is a consequence of their own choices and a form of divine retribution for their continuous transgression against Allah's commands. It serves as a warning to believers to be mindful of their actions and to strive for obedience and righteousness to avoid incurring Allah's wrath.
orig: أولئك الذين لعنهم الله فأصمهم وأعمى أبصارهم

translation: Then do they not reflect upon the Qur'an, or are there locks upon [their] hearts?
interpretation: This verse is a call to reflect deeply on the meanings and teachings of the Qur'an. It suggests that those who fail to ponder over the Qur'an and take heed of its message do so because their hearts are sealed, preventing them from understanding and accepting the truth. The metaphor of locks on hearts denotes a state of spiritual insensitivity and an unwillingness to open one's mind and heart to the guidance of Allah. The verse urges people to approach the Qur'an with an open mind, contemplating its verses and striving to understand its wisdom, rather than turning away from it due to arrogance, prejudice, or worldly distractions. Ultimately, it is a reminder that the Qur'an is a source of guidance and enlightenment for those who sincerely seek to understand and apply its teachings in their lives.
orig: أفلا يتدبرون القرآن أم على قلوب أقفالها

translation: Indeed, those who reverted back [to disbelief] after guidance had become clear to them - Satan enticed them and prolonged hope for them.
interpretation: This verse is referring to those who had embraced Islam but then turned back to disbelief and abandoned their faith. It suggests that this reversion happened because Satan tempted them with worldly desires and false promises, leading them astray from the clear guidance of Islam that they had previously recognized and accepted. The verse implies that Satan exploited their weaknesses and vulnerabilities, and made the path of disbelief seem more appealing to them by giving them false hopes of gaining some temporary benefit in this world. It serves as a warning to the believers to be steadfast in their faith and to beware of the deceptions of Satan that could lead one away from the straight path.
orig: إن الذين ارتدوا على أدبارهم من بعد ما تبين لهم الهدى الشيطان سول لهم وأملى لهم

translation: That is because they said to those who disliked what Allah sent down, "We will obey you in part of the matter." And Allah knows what they conceal.
interpretation: This verse is addressing the hypocrites who secretly allied with the disbelievers against the Muslims. They told the disbelievers that they would obey them in some matters, likely referring to opposing the Prophet Muhammad and the message of Islam. However, Allah is fully aware of what they hide in their hearts and their secret plots, even if they outwardly pretend to be believers. This highlights the importance of sincerity and not harboring ill intentions or allying with those who oppose the truth, as nothing is hidden from Allah's knowledge.
orig: ذلك بأنهم قالوا للذين كرهوا ما نزل الله سنطيعكم في بعض الأمر والله يعلم إسرارهم

translation: Then how [will it be] when the angels take them in death, striking their faces and their backs?
interpretation: This verse is a warning to those who reject faith and do evil deeds. It depicts the terrible fate that awaits them at the time of death, when the angels come to take their souls. The striking of their faces and backs symbolizes the humiliation, pain, and punishment they will face for their wrongdoings. It emphasizes the severity of the consequences for those who choose to disobey Allah and turn away from the path of righteousness. The verse serves as a reminder to all believers to stay steadfast in their faith and to avoid actions that would lead to such a dreadful end.
orig: فكيف إذا توفتهم الملائكة يضربون وجوههم وأدبارهم

translation: That is because they followed what angered Allah and disliked [what earns] His pleasure, so He rendered worthless their deeds.
interpretation: This verse highlights the consequences of going against Allah's commands and desires. When people persistently follow what displeases Allah and avoid what pleases Him, their actions become void and meaningless in His sight. It emphasizes the importance of aligning one's intentions and deeds with the will of Allah to attain success and reward. The verse serves as a warning against disobedience and a reminder to strive for Allah's pleasure in all aspects of life.
orig: ذلك بأنهم اتبعوا ما أسخط الله وكرهوا رضوانه فأحبط أعمالهم

translation: Or do those in whose hearts is disease think that Allah would never expose their [feelings of] hatred?
interpretation: This verse is addressing those who harbor ill feelings and hatred in their hearts towards Islam and the Muslims. They may think that they can keep their malice hidden, but Allah exposes what is in their hearts. It suggests that the inner intentions and feelings cannot be concealed from Allah, and that He will bring forth what is within people, whether good or evil. The "disease" in their hearts refers to their hypocrisy, doubts, and animosity towards the truth. The verse serves as a warning to such individuals that their true nature will be made manifest, and that they cannot escape the consequences of their ill intentions and actions, even if they try to keep them secret.
orig: أم حسب الذين في قلوبهم مرض أن لن يخرج الله أضغانهم

translation: And if We willed, We could show them to you, and you would know them by their mark; but you will surely know them by the tone of [their] speech. And Allah knows your deeds.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah has the power to expose the hypocrites and make their true nature known to the believers. Even though the hypocrites may outwardly appear to be part of the Muslim community, their speech and actions will ultimately betray their insincerity. The "tone of their speech" refers to the subtle hints, inconsistencies, and contradictions in their words that reveal their true intentions. The verse also serves as a reminder that Allah is fully aware of all deeds, both good and bad, and that people will be held accountable for their actions in the Hereafter. It encourages Muslims to be vigilant, to discern between true believers and hypocrites, and to focus on purifying their own intentions and actions, as Allah knows what is in their hearts.
orig: ولو نشاء لأريناكهم فلعرفتهم بسيماهم ولتعرفنهم في لحن القول والله يعلم أعمالكم

translation: And We will surely test you until We make evident those who strive among you [for the cause of Allah] and the patient, and We will test your affairs.
interpretation: This verse is a reminder that Allah will test the believers in various ways to distinguish those who are truly sincere and steadfast in their faith from those who are not. The tests may come in the form of hardships, trials, and difficulties, which will reveal the true nature and strength of a person's faith. Those who remain patient and persevere through these tests, striving in the cause of Allah, will be evident to Allah. The verse also indicates that Allah will test and expose the true nature of people's deeds and intentions, whether good or bad. This emphasizes the importance of sincerity and consistency in one's faith and actions, as Allah is aware of all that we do and will judge us accordingly.
orig: ولنبلونكم حتى نعلم المجاهدين منكم والصابرين ونبلو أخباركم

translation: Indeed, those who disbelieve and avert [people] from the way of Allah and oppose the Messenger after guidance has become clear to them - never will they harm Allah at all, and He will render worthless their deeds.
interpretation: This verse is a stern warning to those who reject faith, actively hinder others from following the path of God, and oppose the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) even after the truth has been made evident to them. It emphasizes that their actions, while causing difficulties for the believers, will ultimately be futile and will not harm God in the least. Moreover, because of their obstinate disbelief and hostility towards the divine message, all their good deeds will be rendered void and they will not benefit from them in the Hereafter. This highlights the gravity of rejecting the truth and actively working against it, as it leads to the nullification of one's good works and invites severe consequences in the afterlife.
orig: إن الذين كفروا وصدوا عن سبيل الله وشاقوا الرسول من بعد ما تبين لهم الهدى لن يضروا الله شيئا وسيحبط أعمالهم

translation: O you who have believed, obey Allah and obey the Messenger and do not invalidate your deeds.
interpretation: This verse is a reminder to the believers that obedience to Allah and His Messenger is essential for their good deeds to be accepted. It emphasizes that disobedience or neglecting the commands of Allah and His Prophet can render one's righteous actions worthless. The verse underscores the importance of sincerity, submission and adherence to the Qur'an and Sunnah in order for our efforts and worship to be rewarded by Allah. It warns against letting our good works go to waste through sins, insincerity or innovations that contradict divine guidance.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا أطيعوا الله وأطيعوا الرسول ولا تبطلوا أعمالكم

translation: Indeed, those who disbelieve and avert [people] from the way of Allah and then die while they are disbelievers - never will Allah forgive them.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the severity of disbelief and actively hindering others from the path of Allah. It states that those who engage in such actions and die without repenting will never be forgiven by Allah. This highlights the importance of faith and the consequences of persistently rejecting Allah's guidance until death. It serves as a warning to those who oppose Islam and discourage others from embracing it, reminding them that such actions can lead to eternal damnation if they do not seek forgiveness and change their ways before their time comes to an end.
orig: إن الذين كفروا وصدوا عن سبيل الله ثم ماتوا وهم كفار فلن يغفر الله لهم

translation: So do not weaken and call for peace while you are superior; and Allah is with you and will never deprive you of [the reward of] your deeds.
interpretation: This verse encourages the believers to remain steadfast and not lose heart or seek a truce when they have the upper hand in a conflict. It reassures them that Allah is on their side and will not let their efforts and sacrifices go to waste. The verse emphasizes the importance of staying strong in faith and continuing to strive in the path of Allah, trusting that He will support the believers and reward them for their good deeds. It serves as a reminder to the Muslims to maintain their resolve and not compromise their principles or beliefs, even in the face of challenges or pressure to seek peace prematurely.
orig: فلا تهنوا وتدعوا إلى السلم وأنتم الأعلون والله معكم ولن يتركم أعمالكم

translation: The life of this world is only play and amusement. But if you believe and fear Allah, He will give you your rewards and will not ask you for your wealth.
interpretation: This verse reminds us that the life of this world is temporary and ultimately insignificant compared to the eternal life of the Hereafter. It encourages believers to focus on their faith and righteousness, rather than being distracted by worldly pleasures and pursuits. Allah promises to reward those who believe and live in accordance with His guidance, emphasizing that true success lies in earning His pleasure rather than amassing wealth or indulging in fleeting enjoyments. The verse also highlights Allah's generosity, as He grants rewards to the faithful without demanding their wealth in return.
orig: إنما الحياة الدنيا لعب ولهو وإن تؤمنوا وتتقوا يؤتكم أجوركم ولا يسألكم أموالكم

translation: If He were to ask you for it [i.e., all your wealth] and press you, you would withhold [out of greed], and He would expose your unwillingness.
interpretation: This verse is a warning against greed and miserliness. It suggests that if Allah were to demand from people all of their wealth, they would be reluctant to give it up, exposing their inner greed and unwillingness to part with their possessions. This highlights the human tendency to hoard wealth and the difficulty in overcoming attachment to worldly belongings, even when called upon by Allah. The verse serves as a reminder to be generous and willing to sacrifice for the sake of Allah, rather than allowing greed to control one's actions and corrupt the heart.
orig: إن يسألكموها فيحفكم تبخلوا ويخرج أضغانكم

translation: Behold! You are those who are called to spend in the cause of Allah, yet among you are some who are niggardly. And whoever is niggardly, it is only at the expense of his own self. But Allah is Rich (Free of all needs), and you (mankind) are poor. And if you turn away (from Islam and the obedience to Allah), He will exchange you for some other people and they will not be your likes.
interpretation: This verse is admonishing the believers who are reluctant to spend in the way of Allah despite being called upon to do so. It warns that being miserly only harms one's own soul, for Allah is self-sufficient and not in need of anyone's charity, whereas human beings are inherently needy and dependent on Allah. The verse also cautions that if people turn away from the path of faith and obedience to Allah, He can easily replace them with others who will be better than them in fulfilling their duties and obligations. This highlights the importance of sincerity, generosity and submission to Allah's commands.
orig: ها أنتم هؤلاء تدعون لتنفقوا في سبيل الله فمنكم من يبخل ومن يبخل فإنما يبخل عن نفسه والله الغني وأنتم الفقراء وإن تتولوا يستبدل قوما غيركم ثم لا يكونوا أمثالكم

translation: Indeed, We have given you, [O Muhammad], a clear conquest.
interpretation: This verse refers to the Treaty of Hudaybiyyah, which was a significant victory for the Muslims despite initial appearances. The "clear conquest" mentioned here is not a military victory, but rather a diplomatic and spiritual one. The treaty allowed for a period of peace, during which the message of Islam spread rapidly and many people entered the faith. It also paved the way for the eventual conquest of Makkah.
