The verse reassures the Prophet (ﷺ) that even though the treaty seemed unfavorable at first, it was ultimately a great triumph given by Allah, as it led to the rapid spread and eventual dominance of Islam in the region.
orig: إنا فتحنا لك فتحا مبينا

translation: That Allah may forgive for you what preceded of your sin and what will follow and complete His favor upon you and guide you to a straight path.
interpretation: This verse is a reassurance to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) that Allah will forgive all of his past and future shortcomings, and will continue to bless him with His favors and guidance. It emphasizes the completeness of Allah's forgiveness and the perfection of His blessings upon the Prophet. The "straight path" mentioned refers to the path of Islam, which is the way of submission to Allah's will and adherence to His commands. This verse highlights the special status of the Prophet and the immense mercy and grace that Allah bestows upon him.
orig: ليغفر لك الله ما تقدم من ذنبك وما تأخر ويتم نعمته عليك ويهديك صراطا مستقيما

translation: And Allah will give you a mighty victory.
interpretation: This verse is a promise from Allah to the believers that He will grant them a decisive and honorable victory over their enemies. It is an assurance of divine support and a reminder that the ultimate triumph belongs to those who stand firm in their faith and trust in Allah's plan. The verse encourages the believers to remain steadfast in the face of adversity, knowing that Allah's help will come at the appointed time, leading them to a glorious victory that will strengthen their position and solidify their faith.
orig: وينصرك الله نصرا عزيزا

translation: It is He who sent down tranquility into the hearts of the believers that they would increase in faith along with their [present] faith. And to Allah belong the soldiers of the heavens and the earth, and ever is Allah Knowing and Wise.
interpretation: This verse highlights the spiritual support and comfort that Allah grants to the believers, strengthening their faith and resolve. It emphasizes that the inner peace and tranquility experienced by the believers is a divine gift from Allah. The mention of Allah's soldiers in the heavens and the earth is a reminder of His omnipotence and control over all forces in the universe. The verse also affirms Allah's infinite knowledge and wisdom, indicating that His support for the believers is based on His deep understanding of their needs and what is best for them in both spiritual and worldly matters.
orig: هو الذي أنزل السكينة في قلوب المؤمنين ليزدادوا إيمانا مع إيمانهم ولله جنود السماوات والأرض وكان الله عليما حكيما

translation: That He may admit the believing men and the believing women to gardens beneath which rivers flow to abide therein eternally and remove from them their misdeeds - and ever is that, in the sight of Allah, a great attainment.
interpretation: This verse speaks to the ultimate reward that awaits the faithful believers, both men and women, in the Hereafter. It emphasizes that through their sincere faith and good deeds, they will be granted entry into Paradise, where they will enjoy eternal bliss in gardens with flowing rivers. Moreover, Allah will forgive and absolve them of their sins and shortcomings, which in itself is a tremendous triumph and a testament to His infinite mercy and grace. The verse underscores that attaining this state of felicity and redemption is the greatest possible achievement one can aspire to, and it is only possible by seeking the pleasure of Allah and striving in His cause.
orig: ليدخل المؤمنين والمؤمنات جنات تجري من تحتها الأنهار خالدين فيها ويكفر عنهم سيئاتهم وكان ذلك عند الله فوزا عظيما

translation: And He will punish the hypocrite men and hypocrite women and the polytheist men and polytheist women - those who assume about Allah an assumption of evil nature. Upon them is a misfortune of evil nature; and Allah has become angry with them and has cursed them and prepared for them Hell, and evil it is as a destination.
interpretation: This verse warns of the severe punishment that awaits those who are hypocrites and polytheists, and who harbor evil thoughts and assumptions about Allah. It emphasizes that they will face a terrible fate, incurring Allah's anger, being cursed by Him, and being consigned to the eternal punishment of Hell. The verse underscores the gravity of hypocrisy and polytheism, depicting them as sins that lead to the worst possible outcome in the Hereafter. It serves as a strong reminder for believers to be sincere in faith and to attribute only good to Allah.
orig: ويعذب المنافقين والمنافقات والمشركين والمشركات الظانين بالله ظن السوء عليهم دائرة السوء وغضب الله عليهم ولعنهم وأعد لهم جهنم وساءت مصيرا

translation: And to Allah belong the soldiers of the heavens and the earth. And ever is Allah Exalted in Might and Wise.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute power and wisdom of Allah. It conveys that all the forces in the universe, whether in the heavens or on the earth, are under His command and control. The term "soldiers" metaphorically refers to all the creatures and entities that serve Allah's will and purpose. The verse also highlights two of Allah's attributes: His might (Al-'Azeez), which signifies His absolute power and strength, and His wisdom (Al-Hakeem), which denotes His perfect knowledge and judgment in all affairs. This serves as a reminder for believers to trust in Allah's power, submit to His will, and seek guidance from His wisdom in all aspects of life.
orig: ولله جنود السماوات والأرض وكان الله عزيزا حكيما

translation: Indeed, We have sent you as a witness and a bringer of good tidings and a warner.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the role of Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) as a messenger of Allah. He was sent not only to convey the message of Islam but also to serve as a witness to the truth of the message, to bring glad tidings of Allah's mercy and reward to those who believe and follow the straight path, and to warn those who reject the message of the consequences of their disbelief. The verse highlights the comprehensive nature of the Prophet's mission, which encompasses all aspects of human life and serves as a guide for individuals and societies alike.
orig: إنا أرسلناك شاهدا ومبشرا ونذيرا

translation: That you [people] may believe in Allah and His Messenger and honor him and respect the Prophet and exalt Allah morning and afternoon.
interpretation: This verse calls upon the believers to have complete faith in Allah and His Messenger, Muhammad (peace be upon him). It encourages them to honor, respect, and support the Prophet in his mission of spreading the message of Islam. The believers are also urged to glorify and praise Allah consistently, both in the morning and the afternoon, as a means of strengthening their connection with Him and expressing gratitude for His blessings. This verse emphasizes the importance of unwavering faith, reverence for the Prophet, and the continuous remembrance of Allah in the daily lives of Muslims.
orig: لتؤمنوا بالله ورسوله وتعزروه وتوقروه وتسبحوه بكرة وأصيلا

translation: Indeed, those who pledge allegiance to you, [O Muhammad] - they are actually pledging allegiance to Allah. The hand of Allah is over their hands. So he who breaks his word only breaks it to the detriment of himself. And he who fulfills that which he has promised Allah - He will give him a great reward.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the significance of the pledge of allegiance (bay'ah) made to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him). It clarifies that by pledging allegiance to the Prophet, the believers are actually pledging their loyalty to Allah Himself. The phrase "The hand of Allah is over their hands" symbolizes the divine support and blessing in this act. The verse then warns against breaking this pledge, stating that doing so will only harm oneself. On the other hand, those who remain true to their covenant with Allah and fulfill their obligations will be granted a tremendous reward by Him. This interpretation highlights the spiritual dimension of the pledge, the importance of remaining steadfast in one's commitment, and the promise of divine recompense for faithfulness.
orig: إن الذين يبايعونك إنما يبايعون الله يد الله فوق أيديهم فمن نكث فإنما ينكث على نفسه ومن أوفى بما عاهد عليه الله فسيؤتيه أجرا عظيما

translation: Those who remained behind of the bedouins will say to you, "Our properties and our families occupied us, so ask forgiveness for us." They say with their tongues what is not within their hearts. Say, "Then who could prevent Allah at all if He intended for you harm or intended for you benefit? Rather, ever is Allah, with what you do, Acquainted."
interpretation: This verse is addressing the hypocrites who made excuses for not joining the Prophet (peace be upon him) in the expedition of Tabuk. They claimed that their wealth and families kept them preoccupied, and asked the Prophet to seek forgiveness for them. However, their words did not match what was in their hearts. The verse emphasizes that nothing can protect one from Allah's punishment or prevent His blessings. It also affirms that Allah is fully aware of people's actions and intentions, and will hold them accountable accordingly. The verse serves as a warning against hypocrisy and a reminder of Allah's omniscience and ultimate control over all affairs.
orig: سيقول لك المخلفون من الأعراب شغلتنا أموالنا وأهلونا فاستغفر لنا يقولون بألسنتهم ما ليس في قلوبهم قل فمن يملك لكم من الله شيئا إن أراد بكم ضرا أو أراد بكم نفعا بل كان الله بما تعملون خبيرا

translation: But you thought that the Messenger and the believers would never return to their families, ever, and that was made pleasing in your hearts. And you assumed an assumption of evil and became a people ruined.
interpretation: This verse is addressing the hypocrites who, during the Battle of the Trench, spread rumors that the Prophet Muhammad and the believers would be defeated and would never return to their families in Medina. The verse points out that these hypocrites had evil assumptions about Allah's support for the believers and the Prophet's mission. They assumed the worst outcome, revealing the corruption in their hearts. As a result of their evil assumptions and lack of faith, they became a ruined people, destined for loss in this world and the Hereafter. The verse emphasizes the importance of having faith and trust in Allah's plan, and the dangers of allowing doubts and ill assumptions to penetrate one's heart.
orig: بل ظننتم أن لن ينقلب الرسول والمؤمنون إلى أهليهم أبدا وزين ذلك في قلوبكم وظننتم ظن السوء وكنتم قوما بورا

translation: And whoever has not believed in Allah and His Messenger - then indeed, We have prepared for the disbelievers a Blaze.
interpretation: This verse serves as a stern warning to those who reject faith in Allah and His Messenger. It emphasizes that disbelief and rejection of the divine message will lead to severe consequences in the afterlife. The "Blaze" mentioned here refers to the intense punishment of Hellfire that awaits those who choose to disbelieve. This interpretation highlights the gravity of denying the truth and the importance of accepting faith in Allah and following His Messenger to attain salvation and avoid the terrible fate of the disbelievers in the Hereafter.
orig: ومن لم يؤمن بالله ورسوله فإنا أعتدنا للكافرين سعيرا

translation: And to Allah belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth. He forgives whom He wills and punishes whom He wills. And ever is Allah Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's absolute sovereignty and authority over the entire universe. It affirms that Allah alone has the power to forgive sins or punish individuals according to His divine wisdom and justice. The mention of Allah's attributes of forgiveness and mercy at the end of the verse underscores the idea that while Allah may punish those who deserve it, He is also ever ready to forgive those who sincerely repent and seek His mercy. This verse encourages believers to turn to Allah for forgiveness and to have hope in His infinite mercy, while at the same time recognizing His power and authority to judge and punish as He sees fit.
orig: ولله ملك السماوات والأرض يغفر لمن يشاء ويعذب من يشاء وكان الله غفورا رحيما

translation: Those who remained behind will say when you set out toward the war booty to take it, "Let us follow you." They wish to change the words of Allah. Say, "Never will you follow us. Thus did Allah say before." So they will say, "Rather, you envy us." But [in fact] they were not understanding except a little.
interpretation: This verse is addressing the hypocrites who stayed behind from the battle of Hunayn, seeking to share in the spoils of war without participating in the fight. It highlights their selfish motives and desire to change Allah's decree, which had already been established regarding their non-participation. The Prophet Muhammad is instructed to firmly deny their request, exposing their envy and lack of understanding of the true nature of faith and sacrifice in the path of Allah. This verse serves as a reminder that true believers are those who are willing to strive and make sacrifices for the sake of Allah, not those who seek worldly gains without effort.
orig: سيقول المخلفون إذا انطلقتم إلى مغانم لتأخذوها ذرونا نتبعكم يريدون أن يبدلوا كلام الله قل لن تتبعونا كذلكم قال الله من قبل فسيقولون بل تحسدوننا بل كانوا لا يفقهون إلا قليلا

translation: Say to those who remained behind of the Bedouins, "You will be called to [face] a people of great military might; you may fight them, or they will submit. So if you obey, Allah will give you a good reward; but if you turn away as you turned away before, He will punish you with a painful punishment."
interpretation: This verse is a warning to the Bedouins who failed to join the Muslims in their expeditions and jihad. It informs them that they will soon be called upon to fight against a formidable enemy, and they will have to either fight or the enemy will submit to Islam. If they obey this call and participate in the fight, Allah will reward them graciously. However, if they turn away and refuse to join the fight as they did before, Allah will inflict upon them a severe punishment. This verse emphasizes the importance and obligation of jihad in Islam, and warns against the consequences of neglecting this duty.
orig: قل للمخلفين من الأعراب ستدعون إلى قوم أولي بأس شديد تقاتلونهم أو يسلمون فإن تطيعوا يؤتكم الله أجرا حسنا وإن تتولوا كما توليتم من قبل يعذبكم عذابا أليما

translation: There is no blame upon the blind nor any blame upon the lame nor any blame upon the sick. And whoever obeys Allah and His Messenger - He will admit him to gardens beneath which rivers flow; but whoever turns away - He will punish him with a painful punishment.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that physical limitations or sickness do not prevent a person from being a faithful servant of Allah. Those with disabilities are not to be blamed or looked down upon. What matters most is one's obedience and submission to Allah and His Messenger. Those who are obedient, despite any hardships or limitations, will be greatly rewarded with Paradise in the Hereafter. However, those who turn away from Allah's path and are disobedient will face severe punishment. The verse encourages all believers to strive in obeying Allah to the best of their abilities, regardless of their circumstances.
orig: ليس على الأعمى حرج ولا على الأعرج حرج ولا على المريض حرج ومن يطع الله ورسوله يدخله جنات تجري من تحتها الأنهار ومن يتول يعذبه عذابا أليما

translation: Certainly was Allah pleased with the believers when they pledged allegiance to you, [O Muhammad], under the tree, and He knew what was in their hearts, so He sent down tranquillity upon them and rewarded them with an imminent conquest.
interpretation: This verse refers to the pledge of allegiance known as Bay'at ar-Ridwan, which took place under a tree in Hudaybiyyah. The believers demonstrated their unwavering loyalty and commitment to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) despite facing a challenging situation. Allah was pleased with their sincerity and faith, knowing the purity of their intentions within their hearts. As a result, He bestowed upon them tranquillity and inner peace, strengthening their resolve. Additionally, Allah rewarded their devotion with a near victory, referring to the conquest of Makkah that followed shortly after the Treaty of Hudaybiyyah. This verse highlights the importance of sincere allegiance to the Prophet and the rewards that come with it, both in terms of spiritual contentment and worldly triumphs.
orig: لقد رضي الله عن المؤمنين إذ يبايعونك تحت الشجرة فعلم ما في قلوبهم فأنزل السكينة عليهم وأثابهم فتحا قريبا

translation: And abundant spoils that they will take. And ever is Allah Exalted in Might and Wise.
interpretation: This verse refers to the promise of Allah to the believers that they will be victorious over their enemies and will gain a large amount of war booty. It emphasizes that this victory and reward is from Allah, who is Mighty and Wise. The spoils of war are seen as a blessing and a sign of Allah's favor upon the believers. The verse also implies that the believers should trust in Allah's plan and wisdom, even if it may not be immediately apparent. Ultimately, Allah's decree will come to pass, and the believers will be rewarded for their faith and sacrifices in His cause.
orig: ومغانم كثيرة يأخذونها وكان الله عزيزا حكيما

translation: Allah has promised you much booty that you will take [in the future] and has hastened for you this [victory] and withheld the hands of people from you - that it may be a sign for the believers and [that] He may guide you to a straight path.
interpretation: This verse is a reminder of Allah's promise to the believers that they will attain great rewards and victories in the future, both in this world and the hereafter. The immediate victory and booty mentioned here is a sign of Allah's favor upon the believers and a confirmation that they are on the right path. It also serves as a lesson that the believers should trust in Allah's plan and remain steadfast in their faith, knowing that Allah will fulfill His promises to them in due time. The verse also emphasizes that Allah's protection and guidance are always with the believers, keeping them safe from the harm of their enemies and leading them towards success and righteousness.
orig: وعدكم الله مغانم كثيرة تأخذونها فعجل لكم هذه وكف أيدي الناس عنكم ولتكون آية للمؤمنين ويهديكم صراطا مستقيما

translation: And [there are] others over which you have not yet had power, but Allah has encompassed them. And ever is Allah, over all things, competent.
interpretation: This verse refers to future victories and conquests that the Muslims will achieve by the grace of Allah. It emphasizes that even though the Muslims may not have the means or ability to overcome certain challenges at present, Allah has already encompassed those challenges and will grant the Muslims victory over them in due time. The verse serves as a reminder of Allah's power, control, and support for the believers, encouraging them to have faith and persevere in the face of difficulties, knowing that Allah's help will come and that He is capable of all things.
orig: وأخرى لم تقدروا عليها قد أحاط الله بها وكان الله على كل شيء قديرا

translation: And if those who disbelieve had fought you, they would have turned their backs [in flight]. Then they would not find a protector or a helper.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the power and support of Allah for the believers. It suggests that if the disbelievers were to engage in battle with the Muslims, they would be defeated and would flee, finding no one to protect or help them. This highlights the idea that those who oppose Allah and His message will ultimately face failure and loss, while those who have faith and stand firm will be granted victory and divine assistance. It serves as a reminder to the believers to remain steadfast in their faith, trusting in Allah's promise of support and success against their enemies.
orig: ولو قاتلكم الذين كفروا لولوا الأدبار ثم لا يجدون وليا ولا نصيرا

translation: Such has been the way of Allah that has passed before, and you will never find any change in the way of Allah.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the unchanging nature of Allah's laws and decrees. It asserts that Allah's way of dealing with His creation, including the consequences of people's actions and the ultimate fate of believers and disbelievers, has always been the same throughout history. The verse also implies that no one can alter or escape from these divine laws, as they are eternal and immutable. This serves as a reminder for people to submit to Allah's will and to live their lives according to His guidance, as His laws and decrees are just, wise, and perfect.
orig: سنة الله التي قد خلت من قبل ولن تجد لسنة الله تبديلا

translation: And it is He who withheld their hands from you and your hands from them within [the area of] Makkah after He caused you to overcome them. And ever is Allah of what you do, Seeing.
interpretation: This verse refers to the Treaty of Hudaybiyyah, where Allah prevented a battle between the Muslims and the Meccans, even though the Muslims had the upper hand. It shows Allah's power in controlling the situation and His awareness of all that transpires. The treaty, though seemingly unfavorable to the Muslims at the time, proved to be a great victory, demonstrating Allah's wisdom and foresight in managing the affairs of the believers. It teaches trust in Allah's plan, even if it doesn't align with our immediate desires or expectations.
orig: وهو الذي كف أيديهم عنكم وأيديكم عنهم ببطن مكة من بعد أن أظفركم عليهم وكان الله بما تعملون بصيرا

translation: They are the ones who disbelieved and obstructed you from al-Masjid al-Haram while the offering was prevented from reaching its place of sacrifice. And if not for believing men and believing women whom you did not know - that you might trample them and there would befall you because of them dishonor without [your] knowledge - [you would have been permitted to enter Makkah]. [This was so] that Allah might admit to His mercy whom He willed. If they had been apart [from them], We would have punished those who disbelieved among them with painful punishment.
interpretation: This verse highlights God's wisdom and mercy in preventing the Muslims from entering Makkah to complete their pilgrimage. Though the disbelievers had unjustly barred the Muslims from the Sacred Mosque, God knew that had the Muslims forcibly entered, they may have unintentionally harmed some of the believing men and women still living in Makkah unknown to the Muslims. This could have brought the Muslims dishonor, so God mercifully kept them back. The verse also implies that had the believers been clearly distinguishable and separate from the disbelievers, God would have allowed the Muslims to punish the wrongdoers among the pagans of Makkah for obstructing their worship. Overall, it shows God's knowledge, wisdom, and mercy in orchestrating events.
orig: هم الذين كفروا وصدوكم عن المسجد الحرام والهدي معكوفا أن يبلغ محله ولولا رجال مؤمنون ونساء مؤمنات لم تعلموهم أن تطئوهم فتصيبكم منهم معرة بغير علم ليدخل الله في رحمته من يشاء لو تزيلوا لعذبنا الذين كفروا منهم عذابا أليما

translation: When those who disbelieved had put into their hearts chauvinism - the chauvinism of the time of ignorance. But Allah sent down His tranquillity upon His Messenger and upon the believers and imposed upon them the word of righteousness, and they were more deserving of it and worthy of it. And ever is Allah, of all things, Knowing.
interpretation: This verse highlights the contrast between the arrogance and pride of the disbelievers and the tranquility and righteousness bestowed upon the Prophet Muhammad and the believers by Allah. It emphasizes that even when faced with the ignorant and misguided attitudes of those who reject faith, the believers remain steadfast in their devotion to Allah and are rewarded with inner peace and a higher moral standard. The verse also serves as a reminder that Allah is all-knowing and aware of the intentions and actions of all individuals, and that He will ultimately support those who follow the path of righteousness.
orig: إذ جعل الذين كفروا في قلوبهم الحمية حمية الجاهلية فأنزل الله سكينته على رسوله وعلى المؤمنين وألزمهم كلمة التقوى وكانوا أحق بها وأهلها وكان الله بكل شيء عليما

translation: Indeed, Allah has fulfilled the vision for His Messenger in truth. You will surely enter al-Masjid al-Haram, if Allah wills, in safety, with your heads shaved and [hair] shortened, not fearing [anyone]. He knew what you did not know and has arranged before that a conquest near at hand.
interpretation: This verse is a reassurance from Allah to the Prophet Muhammad and the believers that the vision the Prophet had of entering Makkah and performing Umrah (minor pilgrimage) would come true, despite the obstacles and opposition they faced from the Quraysh. It was a promise of a near victory, which was fulfilled in the form of the Treaty of Hudaybiyyah. This treaty, although seemingly unfavorable to the Muslims at the time, proved to be a great victory as it paved the way for the peaceful conquest of Makkah. The verse emphasizes the importance of trusting in Allah's plan and having faith in His promises, even in the face of adversity. It also highlights the wisdom and knowledge of Allah, who knows what we do not and arranges matters in ways that may not be immediately apparent to us.
orig: لقد صدق الله رسوله الرؤيا بالحق لتدخلن المسجد الحرام إن شاء الله آمنين محلقين رءوسكم ومقصرين لا تخافون فعلم ما لم تعلموا فجعل من دون ذلك فتحا قريبا

translation: It is He who sent His Messenger with guidance and the religion of truth to manifest it over all religion. And sufficient is Allah as Witness.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that it is Allah who sent Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) with the true guidance and the religion of Islam, with the ultimate aim of making it prevail over all other religions. The verse also affirms that Allah Himself is sufficient as a witness to the truth of Islam and the mission of Prophet Muhammad. It underscores the divine origin and superiority of Islam, as well as Allah's support for His Messenger in spreading the message of truth. The interpretation highlights the universal nature of Islam and its destined triumph, with Allah's aid and testimony.
orig: هو الذي أرسل رسوله بالهدى ودين الحق ليظهره على الدين كله وكفى بالله شهيدا

translation: Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah; and those with him are forceful against the disbelievers, merciful among themselves. You see them bowing and prostrating [in prayer], seeking bounty from Allah and [His] pleasure. Their mark is on their faces from the trace of prostration. That is their description in the Torah. And their description in the Gospel is as a plant which produces its offshoots and strengthens them so they grow firm and stand upon their stalks, delighting the sowers - so that Allah may enrage by them the disbelievers. Allah has promised those who believe and do righteous deeds among them forgiveness and a great reward.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the strong bond of brotherhood and unity among the believers who follow Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him). They are described as being firm and determined in their faith, while showing compassion and mercy towards each other. The physical act of prayer, particularly bowing and prostration, is highlighted as a means of seeking Allah's bounty and pleasure. The mark of prostration on their faces symbolizes their devotion and sincerity in worship. The verse also draws a comparison between the believers and a plant that grows and becomes strong, standing firmly on its stalks. This metaphor suggests that the believers' faith and unity will continue to grow and become stronger over time. Ultimately, the verse conveys a message of hope and promise, assuring the believers that their righteous deeds will be rewarded with forgiveness and a great reward from Allah.
orig: محمد رسول الله والذين معه أشداء على الكفار رحماء بينهم تراهم ركعا سجدا يبتغون فضلا من الله ورضوانا سيماهم في وجوههم من أثر السجود ذلك مثلهم في التوراة ومثلهم في الإنجيل كزرع أخرج شطأه فآزره فاستغلظ فاستوى على سوقه يعجب الزراع ليغيظ بهم الكفار وعد الله الذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات منهم مغفرة وأجرا عظيما

translation: O you who have believed, do not put [yourselves] before Allah and His Messenger but fear Allah. Indeed, Allah is Hearing and Knowing.
interpretation: This verse is a reminder to the believers to show proper respect and etiquette towards Allah and His Messenger (ﷺ). It warns against putting oneself ahead of them in any matter, whether in speech or action. The phrase "between the hands" is an Arabic idiom indicating closeness in time or space. So the meaning is that one should not rush to decide a matter or act before receiving guidance and direction from Allah and His Messenger. Instead, the believers are instructed to have consciousness (taqwa) of Allah, recognizing that He is All-Hearing and All-Knowing, aware of all that we say and do. This consciousness should instill in the believer a sense of reverence, obedience and carefulness not to overstep the proper bounds in religious matters.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا لا تقدموا بين يدي الله ورسوله واتقوا الله إن الله سميع عليم

translation: O you who have believed, do not raise your voices above the voice of the Prophet or be loud to him in speech like the loudness of some of you to others, lest your deeds become worthless while you perceive not.
interpretation: This verse is a reminder for the believers to show utmost respect to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him). It warns against raising one's voice above the Prophet's voice or speaking to him in a loud or harsh manner, as one would speak to their peers. Such disrespectful behavior could lead to the nullification of one's good deeds without even realizing it. This verse emphasizes the importance of maintaining proper etiquette and reverence when interacting with the Prophet, as his status is far above that of ordinary human beings. It also highlights the gravity of one's actions and how they can impact the acceptance of their deeds in the sight of Allah.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا لا ترفعوا أصواتكم فوق صوت النبي ولا تجهروا له بالقول كجهر بعضكم لبعض أن تحبط أعمالكم وأنتم لا تشعرون

translation: Indeed, those who lower their voices before the Messenger of Allah - they are the ones whose hearts Allah has tested for righteousness. For them is forgiveness and great reward.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of showing respect and reverence to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him). Those who speak softly and humbly in his presence demonstrate their piety and righteousness. Allah has tested and purified their hearts, making them worthy of His forgiveness and a great reward in the Hereafter. This verse encourages believers to adopt a respectful and modest attitude when interacting with the Prophet and to cultivate a strong sense of taqwa (God-consciousness) in their hearts.
orig: إن الذين يغضون أصواتهم عند رسول الله أولئك الذين امتحن الله قلوبهم للتقوى لهم مغفرة وأجر عظيم

translation: Indeed, those who call you, [O Muhammad], from behind the chambers - most of them do not use reason.
interpretation: This verse is criticizing the behavior of some people who would call out to the Prophet Muhammad from behind his private chambers rather than coming to speak to him properly and respectfully. It suggests that such an action shows a lack of understanding, etiquette and reason on their part. The verse implies that the Prophet deserves to be treated with utmost respect and dignity, and that it is inappropriate to disturb him or call out to him in this rude manner, especially at his private quarters. It emphasizes having good manners and using wisdom and reason in one's conduct, particularly in dealing with the Prophet.
orig: إن الذين ينادونك من وراء الحجرات أكثرهم لا يعقلون

translation: And if they had been patient until you [Muhammad] came out to them, it would have been better for them. And Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of patience and respect towards the Prophet Muhammad. It suggests that if the companions had waited patiently for the Prophet to come out and address them, instead of acting hastily or impatiently, it would have been better for their spiritual growth and development. The verse also reminds us of Allah's attributes of forgiveness and mercy, indicating that even if the companions made a mistake in their impatience, Allah is always ready to forgive those who sincerely repent and seek His mercy. This highlights the significance of cultivating patience, respect, and trust in Allah and His Messenger in our lives as believers.
orig: ولو أنهم صبروا حتى تخرج إليهم لكان خيرا لهم والله غفور رحيم

translation: O you who have believed, if there comes to you a disobedient one with information, investigate, lest you harm a people out of ignorance and become, over what you have done, regretful.
interpretation: This verse cautions believers against acting hastily on information provided by an unreliable source. It advises them to verify the authenticity of the news before taking any action, as acting without proper investigation may lead to harming innocent people and causing regret later. The Qur'an emphasizes the importance of seeking truth, avoiding rumors, and making informed decisions based on verified facts. This principle is crucial in maintaining social harmony, preventing the spread of misinformation, and upholding justice in society.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا إن جاءكم فاسق بنبإ فتبينوا أن تصيبوا قوما بجهالة فتصبحوا على ما فعلتم نادمين

translation: And know that among you is the Messenger of Allah. If he were to obey you in much of the matter, you would be in difficulty, but Allah has endeared to you the faith and has made it pleasing in your hearts and has made hateful to you disbelief, defiance and disobedience. Those are the [rightly] guided.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of following the guidance of Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) over one's own desires and opinions. It points out that the Prophet's judgement and decisions come from divine wisdom, so going against them would lead to difficulty and misguidance. The verse also highlights that true faith is a blessing and gift from Allah, as He has made belief beloved to the hearts of the believers and made disbelief, sin and disobedience hateful to them. Those who have been granted this blessing of faith and adherence to the Prophet's teachings are considered the rightly guided ones.
orig: واعلموا أن فيكم رسول الله لو يطيعكم في كثير من الأمر لعنتم ولكن الله حبب إليكم الإيمان وزينه في قلوبكم وكره إليكم الكفر والفسوق والعصيان أولئك هم الراشدون

translation: As a bounty from Allah and a favor. And Allah is Knowing and Wise.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the blessings and favors bestowed upon individuals are solely from Allah's grace and generosity. It highlights that Allah grants these blessings to whomever He wills, based on His infinite knowledge and wisdom. The verse serves as a reminder for believers to be grateful for the bounties they receive and to acknowledge that these favors are not earned through their own efforts alone, but rather are a result of Allah's mercy and kindness. It also underscores the importance of recognizing Allah's omniscience and wisdom in all matters, trusting that His decisions and provisions are ultimately for the benefit of His creation.
orig: فضلا من الله ونعمة والله عليم حكيم

translation: And if two factions among the believers should fight, then make settlement between the two. But if one of them oppresses the other, then fight against the one that oppresses until it returns to the ordinance of Allah. And if it returns, then make settlement between them in justice and act justly. Indeed, Allah loves those who act justly.
interpretation: This verse provides guidance on resolving conflicts between believers. If two groups of believers fight each other, efforts should be made to reconcile them fairly. However, if one group transgresses against the other and refuses to cease hostilities, then the Muslims should collectively fight against the aggressing party until they agree to return to the commands of Allah. Once the aggressing party ceases hostilities, reconciliation should again be attempted with justice, as Allah loves those who embody justice in their dealings. The verse emphasizes the importance of striving for peace and justice in the Muslim community.
orig: وإن طائفتان من المؤمنين اقتتلوا فأصلحوا بينهما فإن بغت إحداهما على الأخرى فقاتلوا التي تبغي حتى تفيء إلى أمر الله فإن فاءت فأصلحوا بينهما بالعدل وأقسطوا إن الله يحب المقسطين

translation: The believers are but brothers, so make settlement between your brothers. And fear Allah that you may receive mercy.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the strong bond of brotherhood and unity among believers in Islam. It instructs Muslims to strive for reconciliation and peace whenever disputes or conflicts arise between fellow believers. The verse also reminds Muslims to be mindful of Allah and to act with righteousness and piety, as this will lead to receiving Allah's mercy and blessings. It highlights the importance of maintaining harmony, solidarity, and mutual support within the Muslim community, treating each other with compassion, understanding, and forgiveness. The verse encourages Muslims to prioritize resolving differences and restoring relationships, as this is essential for the overall well-being and strength of the Muslim community.
orig: إنما المؤمنون إخوة فأصلحوا بين أخويكم واتقوا الله لعلكم ترحمون

translation: O you who have believed, let not a people ridicule [another] people; perhaps they may be better than them; nor let women ridicule [other] women; perhaps they may be better than them. And do not insult one another and do not call each other by [offensive] nicknames. Wretched is the name of disobedience after [one's] faith. And whoever does not repent - then it is those who are the wrongdoers.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of respecting others and avoiding mockery, ridicule, and offensive name-calling. It reminds believers that those they mock or look down upon may be better than them in the eyes of Allah. The Qur'an condemns such behavior as a sign of disobedience and wrongdoing, urging individuals to repent from these actions. This verse promotes humility, kindness, and the avoidance of causing harm or offense to others within the Muslim community and beyond.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا لا يسخر قوم من قوم عسى أن يكونوا خيرا منهم ولا نساء من نساء عسى أن يكن خيرا منهن ولا تلمزوا أنفسكم ولا تنابزوا بالألقاب بئس الاسم الفسوق بعد الإيمان ومن لم يتب فأولئك هم الظالمون

translation: O you who have believed, avoid much [negative] assumption. Indeed, some assumption is sin. And do not spy or backbite each other. Would one of you like to eat the flesh of his brother when dead? You would detest it. And fear Allah; indeed, Allah is Accepting of repentance and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse cautions believers against engaging in excessive negative assumptions, as some assumptions can lead to sinful behavior. It also warns against spying on others and backbiting, which is likened to eating the flesh of one's dead brother - something that would naturally be detested. The verse encourages believers to be mindful of Allah and to seek His forgiveness, reminding them that Allah is Accepting of repentance and Merciful to those who turn to Him in sincere repentance.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا اجتنبوا كثيرا من الظن إن بعض الظن إثم ولا تجسسوا ولا يغتب بعضكم بعضا أيحب أحدكم أن يأكل لحم أخيه ميتا فكرهتموه واتقوا الله إن الله تواب رحيم

translation: O mankind, indeed We have created you from male and female and made you peoples and tribes that you may know one another. Indeed, the most noble of you in the sight of Allah is the most righteous of you. Indeed, Allah is Knowing and Acquainted.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the fundamental equality of all human beings in the eyes of Allah, regardless of their race, ethnicity, or social status. It underscores that the true measure of a person's worth is not their lineage or worldly position, but rather their righteousness and piety. The verse encourages people to transcend superficial differences and to recognize the common humanity that binds us all together. It also highlights the importance of getting to know one another and fostering understanding and cooperation among diverse peoples and tribes. Ultimately, the verse reminds us that Allah is all-knowing and fully aware of our deeds and intentions, and that He will judge us based on our righteousness and devotion to Him.
orig: يا أيها الناس إنا خلقناكم من ذكر وأنثى وجعلناكم شعوبا وقبائل لتعارفوا إن أكرمكم عند الله أتقاكم إن الله عليم خبير

translation: The Bedouins say, "We have believed." Say, "You have not [yet] believed; but say [instead], 'We have submitted,' for faith has not yet entered your hearts. And if you obey Allah and His Messenger, He will not deprive you from your deeds of anything. Indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful."
interpretation: This verse highlights the difference between true faith (iman) and mere outward submission (islam). The Bedouins claimed to have faith, but the Qur'an clarifies that true faith is not just a verbal declaration, but a deep conviction in the heart that is reflected through actions and obedience to Allah and His Messenger. The verse emphasizes that Allah does not diminish the reward of good deeds for those who sincerely submit to Him, and that He is Forgiving and Merciful to those who strive to follow His path, even if their faith is not yet perfect.
orig: قالت الأعراب آمنا قل لم تؤمنوا ولكن قولوا أسلمنا ولما يدخل الإيمان في قلوبكم وإن تطيعوا الله ورسوله لا يلتكم من أعمالكم شيئا إن الله غفور رحيم

translation: The believers are only those who have believed in Allah and His Messenger and then doubt not but strive with their properties and their lives in the cause of Allah. It is those who are the truthful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that true believers are those who not only profess faith in Allah and His Messenger but also demonstrate their commitment through unwavering conviction and sacrificing their wealth and lives in the path of Allah. It suggests that mere verbal proclamation of faith is insufficient; rather, it must be accompanied by sincere dedication and tangible actions in supporting the cause of Islam. The verse also implies that those who exhibit such qualities are the ones who are truthful in their claim of faith, as their actions validate their words.
orig: إنما المؤمنون الذين آمنوا بالله ورسوله ثم لم يرتابوا وجاهدوا بأموالهم وأنفسهم في سبيل الله أولئك هم الصادقون

translation: Say, "Do you acquaint Allah with your religion while Allah knows whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth, and Allah is Knowing of all things?"
interpretation: This verse is a reminder that Allah is all-knowing and aware of everything in the heavens and the earth, including the true nature of one's faith and intentions. It suggests that it is futile to try to deceive Allah or present a false image of one's religiosity, as He knows the innermost secrets of the heart. The verse emphasizes the importance of sincerity and genuine devotion in one's religious practice, rather than mere outward displays or claims of piety. It encourages believers to cultivate a deep, authentic connection with Allah, recognizing that He is the ultimate judge of one's actions and intentions.
orig: قل أتعلمون الله بدينكم والله يعلم ما في السماوات وما في الأرض والله بكل شيء عليم

translation: They consider it a favor to you that they have accepted Islam. Say, "Do not consider your Islam a favor to me. Rather, Allah has conferred favor upon you that He has guided you to the faith, if you should be truthful."
interpretation: This verse is addressing the attitude of some people who felt that they were doing the Prophet Muhammad a favor by accepting Islam. Allah is telling the Prophet to respond to them by saying that their acceptance of Islam is not a favor to him, but rather it is a favor from Allah to them that He has guided them to the true faith. The verse emphasizes that guidance to faith is a blessing and favor from Allah, not something that anyone can claim credit for. It also implies that true faith requires sincerity and humility, not a sense of superiority or self-righteousness.
orig: يمنون عليك أن أسلموا قل لا تمنوا علي إسلامكم بل الله يمن عليكم أن هداكم للإيمان إن كنتم صادقين

translation: Indeed, Allah knows the unseen [aspects] of the heavens and the earth. And Allah is Seeing of what you do.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the omniscience and omnipresence of Allah. It reminds us that Allah has complete knowledge of everything, including the unseen and hidden aspects of the heavens and the earth. Nothing escapes His knowledge, and He is fully aware of all our actions, intentions, and deeds. This verse encourages believers to be mindful of their actions and to strive for righteousness, knowing that Allah is constantly watching over them and will hold them accountable for their deeds. It also serves as a source of comfort, knowing that Allah is aware of our struggles and will reward us for our good deeds, even if they are not apparent to others.
orig: إن الله يعلم غيب السماوات والأرض والله بصير بما تعملون

translation: Qaf. By the honored Qur'an.
interpretation: This verse is an oath taken by Allah, swearing by the letter Qaf and by the Qur'an, which is described as being honorable and glorious. The letter Qaf could represent various meanings, such as referring to the Qur'an itself, or to Allah's power and ability (Qudrah). By swearing by the Qur'an, Allah emphasizes its importance, its truthfulness, and its role as a guidance for mankind. This oath serves to affirm the significance of the message that follows in the subsequent verses of the chapter.
orig: ق والقرآن المجيد

translation: But they wonder that there has come to them a warner from among themselves, and the disbelievers say, "This is an amazing thing."
interpretation: The verse expresses the disbelievers' astonishment and skepticism towards the concept of prophethood. They find it strange and incredible that a human being from among their own people would be chosen by God to deliver His message and warn them of the consequences of their actions. This reaction stems from their arrogance, ignorance, and attachment to their ancestral beliefs. They fail to recognize that God selects prophets based on their moral character, wisdom, and ability to convey the divine message effectively, regardless of their social status or lineage. The disbelievers' dismissive attitude towards the prophet is a recurring theme in the Qur'an, highlighting the challenges faced by those who are tasked with guiding humanity to the path of righteousness.
orig: بل عجبوا أن جاءهم منذر منهم فقال الكافرون هذا شيء عجيب

translation: When we have died and become dust, [we will] return [to life]? That is a distant return.
interpretation: This verse questions the idea of resurrection after death, expressing skepticism that humans can be brought back to life after their bodies have decomposed into dust. It suggests that the concept of returning to life after death is far-fetched and difficult to believe. The verse reflects the doubts and disbelief of those who deny the possibility of an afterlife and the accountability for one's actions in this world.
orig: أإذا متنا وكنا ترابا ذلك رجع بعيد

translation: We know well what the earth diminishes of them, and with Us is a Book that preserves.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's omniscience and the fact that nothing is hidden from Him. He is fully aware of what happens to the bodies of the deceased as they decompose in the earth. The "Book that preserves" refers to the divine record that meticulously keeps track of every detail, including what becomes of each person after their death. This verse serves as a reminder that Allah has complete knowledge of all things, even what may seem to be lost or forgotten by people. It also points to the existence of a perfect, preserved divine record that will be used on the Day of Judgment when all deeds are accounted for.
orig: قد علمنا ما تنقص الأرض منهم وعندنا كتاب حفيظ

translation: But they have denied the truth when it came to them, so they are in a confused condition.
interpretation: This verse suggests that when the truth, likely referring to the message of Islam, was presented to the disbelievers, they rejected it outright. As a result of their denial, they find themselves in a state of confusion and inner turmoil. They are unable to accept the truth due to their arrogance, stubbornness, and attachment to their old ways and beliefs. The denial of clear signs and guidance leaves them in a state of spiritual and mental disarray, as they struggle with the cognitive dissonance of rejecting what deep down they may recognize as the truth. This confused state is a consequence of their own choice to turn away from divine guidance.
orig: بل كذبوا بالحق لما جاءهم فهم في أمر مريج

translation: Have they not looked at the heaven above them, how We have made it and adorned it, and there are no flaws in it?
interpretation: This verse is a reminder for mankind to reflect upon the perfection and beauty of the heavens above them. It encourages people to ponder on the flawless creation of Allah and appreciate His power and wisdom. The verse implies that the sky is a sign of Allah's existence and His ability to create something so vast and magnificent without any imperfections. It also suggests that if Allah can create such a perfect and beautiful sky, then He is certainly capable of creating and managing all other aspects of the universe, including human life and destiny. The verse invites people to contemplate the wonders of creation and strengthen their faith in the Creator.
orig: أفلم ينظروا إلى السماء فوقهم كيف بنيناها وزيناها وما لها من فروج

translation: And the earth We have spread out, and set therein mountains standing firm, and produced therein every kind of beautiful growth (in pairs).
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's power and creativity in creating the earth and all its wonders. The spreading out of the earth refers to the vast expanse of land that has been made suitable for human habitation. The mountains serve as stabilizers for the earth's surface, preventing it from shaking or shifting. The mention of "every kind of beautiful growth in pairs" highlights the diversity and beauty of the vegetation that Allah has caused to grow on the earth. It also alludes to the fact that all living things are created in pairs, which is a sign of Allah's perfect design and balance in the universe. This verse encourages reflection on the marvels of Allah's creation and should inspire gratitude and awe in the believer.
orig: والأرض مددناها وألقينا فيها رواسي وأنبتنا فيها من كل زوج بهيج

translation: An insight and a reminder for every servant who turns [to Allah]
interpretation: This verse serves as a reminder and a means of enlightenment for those who sincerely turn to Allah in repentance and obedience. It indicates that the Qur'an is not merely a book of guidance, but also a source of deep spiritual insights for those who reflect upon its verses with a humble and devoted heart. The word "munib" (one who turns) emphasizes the importance of turning away from disobedience and heedlessness, and turning towards Allah with sincerity and submission. This verse encourages the believers to approach the Qur'an with an open heart and mind, seeking to gain valuable insights and reminders that will help them grow closer to their Lord.
orig: تبصرة وذكرى لكل عبد منيب

translation: And We have sent down blessed rain from the sky and made grow thereby gardens and grain from the harvest.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the power and mercy of Allah in providing sustenance for His creation. The blessed rain sent down from the sky is a symbol of Allah's grace and generosity, as it enables the growth of lush gardens and bountiful harvests. This interpretation highlights the importance of recognizing and appreciating the divine blessings that sustain life on Earth, and encourages gratitude towards the Creator for His provisions. It also serves as a reminder of the delicate balance and interconnectedness of the natural world, with the rain playing a crucial role in the cycle of life and the flourishing of vegetation.
orig: ونزلنا من السماء ماء مباركا فأنبتنا به جنات وحب الحصيد

translation: And lofty date-palms with ranged clusters,
interpretation: This verse draws our attention to the beauty and perfection in Allah's creation. The tall, majestic date-palms with their clusters of fruit arranged in a precise and orderly manner are a sign of Allah's creative power and wisdom. It reminds us to reflect upon the natural world around us and appreciate the intricate design and purpose behind every creation. The mention of date-palms also highlights their significance as a blessed fruit and a symbol of prosperity and abundance in the Islamic tradition. This verse encourages us to be mindful of Allah's favors and bounties, and to express gratitude for His provisions in our lives.
orig: والنخل باسقات لها طلع نضيد

translation: As provision for the servants, and We have given life thereby to a dead land. Thus is the resurrection.
interpretation: This verse highlights the power and mercy of Allah in providing sustenance for His creation. The rain that He sends down from the sky not only serves as a means of nourishment for humans and animals but also has the ability to revive dead land, causing vegetation to grow and flourish. This process of bringing life to what was once barren and lifeless is likened to the concept of resurrection, where Allah will raise the dead from their graves on the Day of Judgment. It serves as a reminder that just as Allah can bring dead land back to life, He has the power to resurrect humans after death for the purpose of judgment and either reward or punishment in the eternal Hereafter.
orig: رزقا للعباد وأحيينا به بلدة ميتا كذلك الخروج

translation: The people of Noah denied before them, and [the people of] Ar-Rass and Thamud.
interpretation: This verse is a reminder that disbelief and rejection of Allah's messengers is not unique to the people being addressed in the Quran. It mentions previous nations who also denied the truth, specifically the people of Prophet Noah, the people of Ar-Rass (who are less well-known), and the people of Thamud (to whom Prophet Salih was sent). The implication is that those who reject the message of Islam will face consequences just as these earlier disbelieving nations did when they rejected their prophets and brought Allah's punishment upon themselves. It serves as a warning to heed the lessons of history and not be arrogant in the face of divine revelation.
orig: كذبت قبلهم قوم نوح وأصحاب الرس وثمود

translation: And 'Aad and Pharaoh and the brothers of Lot.
interpretation: This verse is referring to ancient nations that were destroyed by Allah due to their persistent disbelief and transgression. The people of 'Aad, Pharaoh and his people, and the people of Lot (Sodom) were all given warnings through prophets to mend their ways, but they arrogantly rejected the message and continued in their sinful behavior. As a result, Allah sent down severe punishments upon them as a consequence of their actions and as a lesson for future generations. The verse serves as a reminder that no matter how powerful or numerous a nation may be, if they turn away from Allah's guidance and persist in wrongdoing, they will ultimately face destruction.
orig: وعاد وفرعون وإخوان لوط

translation: And the companions of the wood and the people of Tubba'. All denied the messengers, so My threat was justly fulfilled.
interpretation: This verse refers to the people of Madyan, who were known as the "companions of the wood" due to their proximity to a dense forest. It also mentions the people of Tubba', an ancient Yemeni king. Both these nations rejected the messengers sent to them by Allah, just like many other nations before them. As a result, Allah's warning and punishment became inevitable for them due to their persistent disbelief and opposition to the truth. This verse serves as a reminder that denying Allah's messengers and their message leads to severe consequences and the fulfillment of Allah's warning of punishment in this world and the hereafter.
orig: وأصحاب الأيكة وقوم تبع كل كذب الرسل فحق وعيد

translation: Were We then tired with the first creation? Nay, they are in confused doubt about a new creation.
interpretation: This verse is addressing the disbelievers who doubt the possibility of resurrection and a new creation after death. It rhetorically asks if Allah was tired or exhausted by the first act of creation, implying that He certainly was not. The verse asserts that the disbelievers are simply in a state of confusion and uncertainty about the concept of a new creation and life after death. It emphasizes Allah's omnipotence and ability to resurrect and recreate, just as He created the first time without any fatigue. The verse challenges the skepticism and lack of faith of those who deny the Hereafter.
orig: أفعيينا بالخلق الأول بل هم في لبس من خلق جديد

translation: And indeed We have created man, and We know what his ownself whispers to him. And We are nearer to him than his jugular vein (by Our Knowledge).
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the intimate knowledge and closeness of Allah to every human being. It highlights that Allah is fully aware of even the most private thoughts and inner dialogues that a person has within themselves. The reference to being nearer than the jugular vein is a powerful metaphor, as this vein is one of the closest and most vital vessels to a person's heart and mind. The verse serves as a reminder that nothing is hidden from Allah, and that He is always watching over and aware of His creation. It encourages introspection and mindfulness of one's thoughts and actions, knowing that Allah is ever-present and all-knowing.
orig: ولقد خلقنا الإنسان ونعلم ما توسوس به نفسه ونحن أقرب إليه من حبل الوريد

translation: When the two receivers receive, seated on the right and on the left.
interpretation: This verse refers to the two angels assigned to every person, recording their good and bad deeds. One sits on the right, recording good deeds, while the other sits on the left, recording sins. This serves as a reminder that all our actions are witnessed and will be accounted for on the Day of Judgment, encouraging believers to be mindful and strive for righteousness.
orig: إذ يتلقى المتلقيان عن اليمين وعن الشمال قعيد

translation: Man does not utter any word except that with him is an observer prepared [to record].
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the concept of individual accountability. It reminds us that every word we speak is recorded by the ever-watchful angels appointed by Allah. This serves as a powerful reminder to be mindful of our speech, as we will be held responsible for what we say on the Day of Judgment. It encourages believers to speak truthfully, kindly, and justly, while avoiding vain talk, slander, and hurtful words. The verse instills a sense of Taqwa (God-consciousness) in the hearts of the believers, urging them to purify their intentions and carefully consider the impact of their words, as nothing escapes the knowledge of Allah and His appointed angels.
orig: ما يلفظ من قول إلا لديه رقيب عتيد

translation: And the intoxication of death will bring the truth; that is what you were trying to avoid.
interpretation: This verse reminds us that death is an inevitable reality that we cannot escape. The "intoxication of death" refers to the overwhelming and disorienting nature of the experience of dying. It brings with it the ultimate truth that we must all face: the reality of our mortality and the judgment that awaits us in the Hereafter. The verse also implies that many people try to avoid thinking about or facing this truth during their lives, distracting themselves with worldly pursuits. However, at the moment of death, this truth can no longer be avoided or denied. The verse encourages us to confront the reality of death and live our lives in preparation for this unavoidable event, rather than trying to flee from it.
orig: وجاءت سكرة الموت بالحق ذلك ما كنت منه تحيد

translation: And the Trumpet will be blown. That is the Day of the threat.
interpretation: This verse refers to the Day of Judgment, when the Trumpet will be blown to signal the resurrection of the dead and the commencement of the final reckoning. It emphasizes the gravity and the inevitability of this event, which has been repeatedly warned about throughout the Qur'an. The blowing of the Trumpet instills a sense of awe and fear, as it marks the end of the world as we know it and the beginning of the eternal afterlife. The verse serves as a reminder for believers to be mindful of their actions in this life, as they will be held accountable for them on that Day.
orig: ونفخ في الصور ذلك يوم الوعيد

translation: And every soul will come, with it a driver and a witness.
interpretation: This verse refers to the Day of Judgment when every soul will be accompanied by two angels: one who drove or guided the person during their earthly life (the driver) and the other who recorded their deeds (the witness). These angels will testify about the person's actions and intentions during their life, providing evidence for God's judgment. It emphasizes the idea that everyone is accountable for their deeds and will face the consequences in the afterlife based on the record kept by the witnessing angel. The verse serves as a reminder for people to be mindful of their actions and to strive for righteousness, knowing that nothing escapes God's knowledge and that ultimate justice will be served on the Day of Judgment.
orig: وجاءت كل نفس معها سائق وشهيد

translation: You were certainly in unmindfulness of this, and We have removed from you your cover, so your sight, this Day, is sharp.
interpretation: This verse is addressing the disbelievers on the Day of Judgment. It suggests that in this worldly life, they were heedless and unmindful of the reality of the Hereafter, as if there was a veil or cover over their perception. But on the Day of Judgment, Allah will remove this cover, making their vision crystal clear, and then they will realize the truth with certainty. It will be too late for repentance then. The verse warns us not to be unmindful of the Hereafter in the life of this world, when we still have the opportunity to work righteousness for it.
orig: لقد كنت في غفلة من هذا فكشفنا عنك غطاءك فبصرك اليوم حديد

translation: And his companion will say, "This is what is with me, prepared."
interpretation: The verse is referring to the record of a person's deeds, which will be presented by their accompanying angel on the Day of Judgment. The angel will declare that this record is ready and available as evidence of the person's actions throughout their life. This interpretation highlights the Islamic belief in individual accountability, where every person will be held responsible for their deeds and will face the consequences in the Hereafter based on the record kept by the angels assigned to them.
orig: وقال قرينه هذا ما لدي عتيد

translation: Throw into Hell every stubborn disbeliever.
interpretation: This verse is a command from Allah to the angels to cast into Hell every obstinate disbeliever who persistently denied the truth and refused to accept the message of Islam. It emphasizes the severe punishment that awaits those who reject faith and remain defiant in their disbelief, despite the clear signs and warnings sent by Allah. The verse also highlights the justice of Allah in dealing with those who choose to disbelieve, as they will face the consequences of their actions in the Hereafter. It serves as a warning to all individuals to embrace faith and submit to the will of Allah before it is too late.
orig: ألقيا في جهنم كل كفار عنيد

translation: Hindering good, transgressing, and suspicious.
interpretation: This verse is referring to a person who actively prevents others from doing good deeds, consistently transgresses the limits set by Allah, and whose actions and intentions are suspicious and doubtful. Such a person is considered blameworthy in the sight of Allah due to their negative traits and behavior which go against the teachings of Islam.
orig: مناع للخير معتد مريب

translation: Whoever sets up another god beside Allah, then both of you throw him into the severe punishment.
interpretation: This verse is a stern warning against the grave sin of shirk, or associating partners with Allah in worship. It emphasizes the severity of the punishment that awaits those who commit this transgression. The use of the dual pronoun "both of you" could be understood as referring to the angels who carry out Allah's command to cast the idolaters into Hell. It serves as a reminder that worshipping anyone or anything besides Allah is the greatest injustice and will lead to a painful fate in the Hereafter. The verse also highlights the absolute authority and oneness of Allah, making it clear that He alone deserves to be worshipped and that setting up rivals to Him is a grievous offense that warrants severe retribution.
orig: الذي جعل مع الله إلها آخر فألقياه في العذاب الشديد

translation: His [devil] companion will say, "Our Lord, I did not make him transgress, but he [himself] was in extreme error."
interpretation: This verse is referring to the Day of Judgment when the sinful human will blame his devil companion for leading him astray. However, the devil will respond by saying that he did not force the human to transgress or commit sins, but rather the human himself was deeply misguided and chose to follow the path of error out of his own free will. This highlights the Islamic concept that every individual is responsible for their own actions and will be held accountable for their deeds, and that blaming others for one's own misdeeds is futile in front of God's judgment.
orig: قال قرينه ربنا ما أطغيته ولكن كان في ضلال بعيد

translation: He said, "Do not quarrel in my presence, while I had already presented to you the warning."
interpretation: This verse is a stern warning from Allah to those who dispute and argue about the truth after it has been made clear to them. Allah is telling them that they have no excuse for their behavior, as He has already sent them messengers and revelations to guide them to the right path. The verse emphasizes the importance of submitting to Allah's will and accepting His guidance, rather than engaging in futile arguments and disputes. It also serves as a reminder that on the Day of Judgment, there will be no opportunity for argument or debate, and everyone will be held accountable for their actions in this life.
orig: قال لا تختصموا لدي وقد قدمت إليكم بالوعيد

translation: The word will not be changed with Me, and never will I be unjust to [My] servants.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the immutability of Allah's word and His justice towards His servants. It assures that Allah will not go back on His promises or decrees, and that He will always treat His creation with fairness and equity. The verse highlights the reliability and trustworthiness of Allah, as He is not one to break His word or act unjustly. It serves as a reminder to the believers that they can have complete faith in Allah's promises and that they will be judged solely on the basis of their deeds, without any discrimination or prejudice.
orig: ما يبدل القول لدي وما أنا بظلام للعبيد

translation: On the Day We will say to Hell, "Have you been filled?" and it will say, "Are there some more?"
interpretation: This verse refers to the vastness and insatiable nature of Hell on the Day of Judgment. It suggests that Hell will never be full, no matter how many sinners are thrown into it. The rhetorical question "Are there some more?" emphasizes the idea that Hell is always ready to receive more of those who have earned God's punishment through their actions in this world. This verse serves as a powerful warning to humanity about the consequences of straying from the righteous path and indulging in sin.
orig: يوم نقول لجهنم هل امتلأت وتقول هل من مزيد

translation: And Paradise will be brought near to the righteous, not far
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the reward that awaits the righteous and God-fearing believers in the Hereafter. Paradise will be brought close to them, making it easily accessible as a result of their faith, good deeds, and obedience to Allah throughout their worldly lives. The proximity of Paradise to the righteous signifies the ease and comfort with which they will enter it, in contrast to the difficult path that awaits the sinners and disbelievers. This closeness also symbolizes the special status and honor bestowed upon the pious, as their destination is near to Allah's mercy and pleasure.
orig: وأزلفت الجنة للمتقين غير بعيد

translation: That is what you are promised - for every returner [to Allah], keeper [of His covenant]
interpretation: This verse is referring to the rewards that await the righteous believers in the Hereafter. Those who constantly turn to Allah in repentance, obedience and worship, and who fulfill the obligations and responsibilities entrusted to them by Allah, are promised these great rewards in Paradise. It emphasizes that Allah's promise of reward is certain for those who are mindful of Him and devoted to following His path with sincerity and consistency.
orig: هذا ما توعدون لكل أواب حفيظ

translation: Who feared the Most Merciful unseen and came with a heart returning [in repentance].
interpretation: This verse speaks about those who fear Allah and worship Him sincerely, even when they are alone and no one can see them except Allah. They have a heart that is humble, repentant and turns to Allah in submission and obedience. Such people will be honored and rewarded by Allah on the Day of Judgment for their sincerity and devotion, even if their deeds were hidden from the eyes of people in this world. It emphasizes the importance of having consciousness of Allah (taqwa) and purifying one's intentions solely for His pleasure.
orig: من خشي الرحمن بالغيب وجاء بقلب منيب

translation: Enter it in peace. That is the Day of Eternity.
interpretation: This verse refers to the righteous believers entering Paradise on the Day of Judgment. They will be welcomed with the greeting of peace, signifying that they have attained eternal safety and security. The phrase "Day of Eternity" emphasizes that this is a permanent state of bliss and immortality, free from any fear of death or end. It is a reminder to the believers that their ultimate goal should be to strive for this everlasting peace and happiness in the Hereafter through faith and good deeds in this worldly life.
orig: ادخلوها بسلام ذلك يوم الخلود

translation: They will have whatever they wish therein, and with Us is more.
interpretation: In Paradise, the believers will have everything they desire, and even beyond that, Allah has prepared for them more than they can imagine or wish for. This verse emphasizes the boundless generosity and blessings that Allah will bestow upon the believers in the Hereafter, indicating that their happiness and satisfaction will be complete and everlasting, and that the rewards of Paradise will exceed their expectations and desires.
orig: لهم ما يشاءون فيها ولدينا مزيد

translation: And how many a generation before them did We destroy who were greater than them in [striking] power and had explored throughout the lands. Is there any place of escape?
interpretation: This verse is a reminder of the fate that befell previous nations who were mightier and more advanced than the people being addressed. Despite their power and dominance, they were ultimately destroyed by Allah due to their disobedience and transgression. The rhetorical question at the end emphasizes that there is no escape from Allah's punishment and justice, no matter how strong or influential a nation may seem. It serves as a warning to the current generation not to follow in the footsteps of those who were destroyed before them, and to turn to Allah in repentance and obedience.
orig: وكم أهلكنا قبلهم من قرن هم أشد منهم بطشا فنقبوا في البلاد هل من محيص

translation: Indeed in that is a reminder for whoever has a heart or who listens while he is present [in mind].
interpretation: This verse is a reminder for those who are willing to reflect and ponder upon the signs of Allah. It calls upon people to open their hearts and minds to the truth, to listen attentively with presence of mind, and to witness the manifestations of Allah's power and wisdom in the universe. The verse emphasizes the importance of being receptive to divine guidance and using one's intellect and spiritual faculties to comprehend the deeper meanings behind Allah's creation and revelation. It is a call to awaken one's conscience and to be mindful of the purpose of life, which is to worship Allah and follow His path.
orig: إن في ذلك لذكرى لمن كان له قلب أو ألقى السمع وهو شهيد

translation: And We did certainly create the heavens and earth and what is between them in six days, and there touched Us no weariness.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's omnipotence and that the creation of the vast universe was effortless for Him. The "six days" mentioned are not like the days we know, but rather six stages or periods. This also refutes the notion attributed to God in the Bible of "resting" on the seventh day after completing creation. Allah is far above any human weakness like weariness or needing rest. The verse underscores that Allah's creative power and energy are infinite and unaffected by the magnitude of His creation.
orig: ولقد خلقنا السماوات والأرض وما بينهما في ستة أيام وما مسنا من لغوب

translation: So be patient over what they say and exalt [Allah] with praise of your Lord before the rising of the sun and before its setting.
interpretation: This verse advises the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) to remain patient in the face of the disbelievers' accusations and mockery, and to continue praising and glorifying Allah at the appointed times of prayer, specifically before sunrise and sunset. It emphasizes the importance of steadfastness, patience, and maintaining a strong connection with Allah through regular worship and remembrance, even in the face of adversity or opposition. The verse also serves as a reminder to all believers to remain committed to their faith and to seek solace and strength through prayer and devotion to Allah.
orig: فاصبر على ما يقولون وسبح بحمد ربك قبل طلوع الشمس وقبل الغروب

translation: And exalt [Allah] with praise of your Lord in the night and after prostration.
interpretation: This verse encourages the believers to engage in the remembrance and glorification of Allah during the night, particularly after performing the prescribed prayers that involve prostration. It emphasizes the importance of dedicating oneself to the worship and praise of Allah beyond the obligatory prayers, especially during the quiet and tranquil hours of the night. This additional act of devotion and submission to Allah is a means of attaining spiritual purification, closeness to Him, and earning His pleasure and rewards. It also serves as a reminder for the believers to consistently maintain a connection with their Lord and to seek His guidance and mercy at all times.
orig: ومن الليل فسبحه وأدبار السجود

translation: And listen on the Day when the Caller will call out from a place that is near -
interpretation: This verse refers to the Day of Judgment when the angel Israfil will blow the trumpet, signaling the beginning of the Day of Resurrection. The sound of the trumpet will be so powerful that it will be heard from a very close distance, indicating the imminence and inevitability of the event. It serves as a reminder to mankind that the Day of Judgment is real and that everyone will be held accountable for their deeds in this world. The verse emphasizes the importance of being prepared for that Day by leading a righteous life in accordance with God's commandments.
orig: واستمع يوم يناد المناد من مكان قريب

translation: The Day they will hear the Blast in truth: that will be the Day of Resurrection.
interpretation: This verse refers to the Day of Judgment, when the trumpet will be blown and all the dead will be resurrected from their graves to face the reckoning of their deeds. It emphasizes the reality and inevitability of that Day, which will mark the end of this world and the beginning of the eternal life in the Hereafter. The "Blast" mentioned here is the second blowing of the trumpet, which will signal the start of the resurrection and gathering of all souls before Allah for judgment. This verse serves as a reminder to mankind that they will all be held accountable for their actions in this life, and should therefore strive to live righteously and prepare for that crucial Day.
orig: يوم يسمعون الصيحة بالحق ذلك يوم الخروج

translation: Indeed, it is We who give life and cause death, and to Us is the final return.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute power and authority of Allah over life and death. It reminds us that Allah is the One who grants life and takes it away, and that ultimately, all of creation will return to Him for judgment. This verse encourages believers to recognize the temporary nature of worldly life and to focus on the eternal life of the Hereafter by living righteously and seeking Allah's pleasure. It also serves as a comforting reminder that death is not the end, but rather a transition to the next stage of existence where we will face the consequences of our deeds in this world.
orig: إنا نحن نحيي ونميت وإلينا المصير

translation: The Day the earth breaks away from them [and they emerge] rapidly; that is a gathering easy for Us.
interpretation: This verse refers to the Day of Resurrection, when the dead will be raised from their graves and will emerge rapidly from the earth. The verse emphasizes the ease with which Allah will gather all of humanity for judgment, highlighting His power and control over all things. It serves as a reminder to humans that they will be held accountable for their deeds and that the Day of Resurrection is inevitable. The rapid emergence from the graves also symbolizes the urgency and suddenness of the event, giving humans no time to prepare or escape from facing the consequences of their actions in this world.
orig: يوم تشقق الأرض عنهم سراعا ذلك حشر علينا يسير

translation: We are most knowing of what they say, and you are not over them a tyrant. But remind by the Qur'an whoever fears My threat.
interpretation: This verse is a reminder that Allah knows best what people say, whether good or bad. The Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) is told not to force people to believe, as he is not a tyrant over them. Rather, his duty is to remind and warn people by reciting the Qur'an, especially those who fear Allah's warning and punishment in the Hereafter. The Qur'an is thus a means of guidance and a reminder for those who are open to its message and heedful of Allah's warnings, not a means of compulsion or tyranny.
