orig: نحن أعلم بما يقولون وما أنت عليهم بجبار فذكر بالقرآن من يخاف وعيد

translation: By the winds that scatter dust
interpretation: This verse is referring to the winds that blow and scatter dust particles in the air. It is an oath taken by Allah, swearing by one of His creations to emphasize the importance and truth of the message that follows in the subsequent verses. The winds are a sign of Allah's power and control over the universe, and how He can use them to bring about changes on the earth. Some scholars interpret the "winds that scatter" as a metaphor for the angels who carry out Allah's commands and scatter His mercy and blessings upon the earth. Overall, this verse serves as a reminder of Allah's omnipotence and the need for humans to recognize and submit to His will.
orig: والذاريات ذروا

translation: And [by] the clouds carrying a load [of water]
interpretation: This verse is referring to the clouds that carry rain, which is a great blessing and mercy from Allah. The clouds are like vessels that transport water from one place to another, providing sustenance for the earth and its inhabitants. This is a sign of Allah's power and wisdom, as He has created a perfect system for the distribution of water on earth. The verse reminds us to be grateful for the blessings of rain and the abundance it brings, and to recognize the might and generosity of our Creator.
orig: فالحاملات وقرا

translation: By the [ships] sailing with ease
interpretation: This verse is referring to the ships that sail smoothly and effortlessly through the water, guided by Allah's command. It is a reminder of Allah's power and control over all things, including the forces of nature that allow these ships to navigate the seas. The ease with which the ships sail is a sign of Allah's mercy and favor upon humankind, as He has made it possible for us to travel and trade across great distances by water. This verse encourages us to reflect on the blessings that Allah has bestowed upon us and to be grateful for His provisions.
orig: فالجاريات يسرا

translation: By those [angels] who arrange [God's] commands
interpretation: This verse is interpreted as referring to the angels who carry out God's commands and arrange the affairs of the universe according to His will. It emphasizes the important role that angels play in executing the divine decrees and maintaining the order and harmony in God's creation. The verse is also seen as an oath, where God swears by these angels to underscore the significance and truth of the message that follows in the subsequent verses of the chapter.
orig: فالمقسمات أمرا

translation: Indeed, what you are promised is true.
interpretation: This verse affirms the certainty and truthfulness of God's promises, particularly those related to the Day of Judgment, Paradise, and Hell. It serves as a reminder to believers that they should have unwavering faith in God's words and promises, as they will undoubtedly come to pass. The verse also implies that one should live their life in accordance with these promises, striving to attain the reward of Paradise and avoiding the punishment of Hell by following God's commands and guidance.
orig: إنما توعدون لصادق

translation: And indeed, the Judgment is about to occur.
interpretation: This verse is a stark reminder that the Day of Judgment is an inevitable reality that will come to pass. It emphasizes the certainty and imminence of this event, urging believers to be mindful of their actions and to prepare for the ultimate reckoning. The verse underscores the importance of living a righteous life in accordance with God's guidance, as every deed will be accounted for on that fateful day. It serves as a wake-up call for those who may be heedless or doubtful of the Hereafter, reminding them that the consequences of their choices in this world will determine their eternal fate in the next.
orig: وإن الدين لواقع

translation: By the sky full of paths
interpretation: This verse is referring to the sky and its intricate, interconnected patterns that resemble a woven fabric or a well-constructed edifice. It is an oath by Allah, drawing attention to the marvels of His creation. The "paths" mentioned could allude to the orbits of celestial bodies, the layers of the atmosphere, or the invisible pathways that angels and divine decrees traverse. This verse invites us to ponder upon the perfection, beauty, and order in the heavens above, all of which point to the existence, power, and wisdom of the Creator.
orig: والسماء ذات الحبك

translation: Indeed, you are in differing statement.
interpretation: This verse points to the fact that people have varying opinions and beliefs about God and the divine message. It suggests that there is a lack of unity and consensus among people when it comes to matters of faith. The Qur'an acknowledges this reality of human differences in thought and belief, and it serves as a prelude to asserting that only those whom God guides will find the right path amidst the differing views and opinions. It implies that without divine guidance, people will remain in a state of disagreement and divergence concerning the ultimate truths.
orig: إنكم لفي قول مختلف

translation: Averted from it [i.e., the Fire] will be he who was the most righteous.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that those who are the most righteous and pious in this world will be saved from the punishment of the Hellfire in the Hereafter. It implies that one's actions and deeds in this life will determine their fate in the afterlife. The verse encourages people to strive for righteousness and to avoid sin and disobedience to Allah, as this will ultimately lead to salvation and protection from the torment of the Fire.
orig: يؤفك عنه من أفك

translation: The liars have been killed.
interpretation: This verse is likely referring to the ultimate fate of those who deliberately spread falsehoods and misinformation. In the Islamic worldview, lying and deception are considered major sins. The Qur'an warns that those who engage in such behavior will face severe consequences, both in this world and the next. The verse suggests that the liars will eventually be exposed and punished for their actions, emphasizing the importance of honesty and truthfulness in one's conduct. It serves as a reminder that while lies may provide temporary benefits, they ultimately lead to ruin and divine retribution.
orig: قتل الخراصون

translation: Those who are in heedless pursuit of worldly pleasures
interpretation: This verse is referring to those people who are engrossed in the temporary pleasures and distractions of this worldly life, neglecting their spiritual duties and heedless of the ultimate reality of the Hereafter. They are in a state of ghafla (heedlessness), pursuing their desires and whims without reflecting on the purpose of their existence or the consequences of their actions. This verse serves as a reminder for believers to avoid falling into this state of heedlessness and to remain mindful of Allah and the Day of Judgment, prioritizing their spiritual well-being over worldly temptations.
orig: الذين هم في غمرة ساهون

translation: They ask, "When is the Day of Recompense?"
interpretation: This verse is referring to the disbelievers who mockingly question the believers about when the Day of Judgment will occur. They do not believe in the Hereafter and the accountability for their deeds. The "Day of Recompense" or "Day of Judgment" is the day when all souls will be judged by Allah for their actions in this worldly life. It is a reminder for mankind that this life is temporary and that we will all face the consequences of our deeds in the eternal life of the Hereafter. The verse serves as a warning for those who deny the Day of Judgment to reflect upon their actions and to turn towards the path of righteousness before it is too late.
orig: يسألون أيان يوم الدين

translation: The Day they will be tormented over the Fire.
interpretation: This verse refers to the Day of Judgment when the disbelievers and wrongdoers will face the consequences of their actions. They will be exposed to the Fire of Hell as a form of punishment and torment for their rejection of faith and their sinful deeds in this worldly life. The verse emphasizes the severity and the inevitability of the punishment that awaits those who deviate from the right path and do not follow the guidance of Allah. It serves as a warning and a reminder for people to be mindful of their actions and to strive for righteousness before it is too late.
orig: يوم هم على النار يفتنون

translation: Taste [the consequence of] your trial. This is what you were asking to be hastened.
interpretation: This verse is a stern warning to those who disbelieved and mocked the warnings of divine punishment. It suggests that the disbelievers will face the consequences of their actions and their rejection of faith. They had arrogantly demanded that the threatened punishment come to pass, not believing it would happen. Now, as they face the reality of the punishment, they are told to "taste" the result of the trial they brought upon themselves through their disbelief and haste in seeking to challenge God. It emphasizes the severity and inescapability of the punishment that awaits those who reject God's messages and warnings.
orig: ذوقوا فتنتكم هذا الذي كنتم به تستعجلون

translation: Indeed, the righteous will be in gardens and springs.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the great reward that awaits those who are righteous and live their lives in accordance with God's commands. The "gardens" mentioned here refer to Paradise, a place of eternal bliss, beauty, and comfort. The "springs" signify the abundance of pure, refreshing water in Paradise, which is a symbol of the endless blessings and provisions that the righteous will enjoy in the afterlife. This verse serves as a reminder and motivation for believers to strive for righteousness in this world, knowing that their ultimate reward will be the unimaginable delights of Paradise in the Hereafter.
orig: إن المتقين في جنات وعيون

translation: Accepting what their Lord has given them. Indeed, they were before that doers of good.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of gratitude and righteousness. Those who accept Allah's blessings with gratitude and were doers of good before receiving these blessings are praised in this verse. It suggests that their righteous deeds in the past have made them deserving of Allah's favors and rewards in the present. The verse encourages believers to constantly strive for goodness and righteousness, as it will lead to Allah's acceptance and blessings in this life and the hereafter.
orig: آخذين ما آتاهم ربهم إنهم كانوا قبل ذلك محسنين

translation: They used to sleep but little of the night.
interpretation: This verse refers to the righteous believers who would spend much of the night in prayer and worship, taking only a small portion of the night for sleep. It highlights their devotion and sincerity in their faith, as they prioritized their spiritual connection with Allah over worldly comforts and rest. This characteristic of minimizing sleep for the sake of worship is praised as a sign of true believers who are mindful of the Hereafter and strive to make the most of their limited time in this world by dedicating it to the remembrance and obedience of Allah.
orig: كانوا قليلا من الليل ما يهجعون

translation: And in the hours before dawn they would ask forgiveness
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance and virtue of seeking Allah's forgiveness during the early hours of the morning, before dawn. It suggests that the righteous believers make it a habit to wake up during this blessed time to engage in prayer, supplication, and seeking forgiveness for their sins. This act demonstrates their sincerity, devotion, and humility before Allah. Seeking forgiveness during the peaceful and quiet hours of the night, when worldly distractions are minimal, allows for greater concentration and spiritual connection with the Creator. It is a time when prayers are more likely to be accepted and when one can attain greater peace and tranquility in their heart and soul.
orig: وبالأسحار هم يستغفرون

translation: And in their wealth there is a right for the beggar and the deprived.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of giving charity and helping those in need. It reminds us that a portion of our wealth belongs to those who are less fortunate, such as beggars and the deprived. As Muslims, we have a responsibility to share our blessings with others and to support those who are struggling financially. This verse encourages us to be generous and compassionate, and to recognize that our wealth is ultimately a trust from Allah that we should use to benefit society as a whole.
orig: وفي أموالهم حق للسائل والمحروم

translation: And on the earth are signs for the certain [in faith]
interpretation: This verse points to the various signs and indications in the natural world that testify to the existence, power, and wisdom of Allah. These signs, such as the perfect order and balance in the universe, the intricate design of living beings, and the provision of sustenance for all creatures, serve as proof for those who have certainty in their faith. The verse encourages people to reflect upon these signs and strengthen their belief in the Creator. It also implies that those who are truly certain in their faith will readily recognize and appreciate these signs, while those who lack certainty may overlook or dismiss them.
orig: وفي الأرض آيات للموقنين

translation: And in yourselves. Then will you not see?
interpretation: This verse is a call for introspection and self-reflection. It reminds us that the signs of Allah's existence and power are not only present in the external world but also within our own selves. The human body, with its complex systems and intricate design, is a testament to the Creator's wisdom and omnipotence. The verse encourages us to ponder upon our own creation, the physical and spiritual aspects of our being, and recognize the undeniable proof of Allah's presence within us. By reflecting on the marvels of our own existence, we can strengthen our faith and develop a deeper connection with our Creator.
orig: وفي أنفسكم أفلا تبصرون

translation: And in the heaven is your provision and whatever you are promised.
interpretation: This verse reminds us that our sustenance and all the blessings we have been promised in this world and the Hereafter come from Allah, the Most High. It emphasizes that Allah is the ultimate provider and that we should put our trust in Him for all our needs. The verse also alludes to the fact that the rewards promised to the believers in the afterlife are as real and certain as the provisions we receive in this worldly life. It encourages us to focus on our spiritual growth and to strive for the eternal blessings that await the righteous in Paradise.
orig: وفي السماء رزقكم وما توعدون

translation: Then by the Lord of the heaven and earth, indeed, it is truth, just as [sure as] it is that you are speaking.
interpretation: In this verse, Allah swears by the heaven and the earth, emphasizing the absolute truth and certainty of His message and the inevitability of the Day of Judgment. Just as one is certain about their own ability to speak, one should be equally certain about the truth of Allah's words and promises. This powerful oath serves as a reminder for believers to have unwavering faith in the Qur'an and its teachings, as they are the ultimate truth from the Creator of the universe.
orig: فورب السماء والأرض إنه لحق مثل ما أنكم تنطقون

translation: Has there reached you the story of the honored guests of Abraham?
interpretation: This verse is a rhetorical question, drawing the listener's attention to the story of Prophet Abraham and his honored guests, who were angels in human form. The verse emphasizes the importance and significance of this event, which demonstrates Abraham's exemplary hospitality, generosity, and faith in God. It also highlights the divine message and support that Abraham received through these guests, who brought him glad tidings of a son despite his old age. This story serves as a reminder for believers to emulate Abraham's virtues and to trust in God's plan and blessings, even in seemingly impossible situations.
orig: هل أتاك حديث ضيف إبراهيم المكرمين

translation: When they entered upon him and said, "Peace." He said, "Peace, [you are] a people unknown."
interpretation: This verse is referring to the story of Prophet Abraham (peace be upon him) when he was visited by angels in the form of men. When they greeted him with "Peace", Abraham replied with "Peace" as well, but he felt that these visitors were unfamiliar to him. This shows the importance of greeting others with "Salam" (peace) in Islam, even if they are strangers. It also highlights Abraham's caution and wisdom in dealing with unknown individuals, while still showing them hospitality as guests.
orig: إذ دخلوا عليه فقالوا سلاما قال سلام قوم منكرون

translation: And he went to his family and brought a fat [roasted] calf.
interpretation: This verse is referring to the story of Prophet Ibrahim (Abraham) when he was visited by angels in the form of guests. As a gracious host, Ibrahim went to his family and brought back a roasted calf to serve his guests, displaying his generosity and hospitality. This act of kindness and warmth towards guests is highly valued in Islamic tradition and is seen as a righteous deed. The verse emphasizes the importance of showing hospitality and being welcoming to others, even to strangers.
orig: فراغ إلى أهله فجاء بعجل سمين

translation: So he brought it near them; he said, "Will you not eat?"
interpretation: In this verse, Abraham presents the food he has prepared to his guests, who are actually angels in disguise. His question "Will you not eat?" reflects the traditional Arab hospitality and generosity, where guests are expected to accept the host's offer of food. The deeper meaning could be an invitation to partake in the spiritual sustenance and blessings that God provides. It also shows Abraham's humility and eagerness to serve, even when hosting beings as exalted as angels.
orig: فقربه إليهم قال ألا تأكلون

translation: And he felt from them apprehension. They said, "Fear not," and gave him good tidings of a learned boy.
interpretation: This verse is referring to the story of Prophet Ibrahim (Abraham) when he was visited by angels in the form of guests. Ibrahim felt a sense of fear or apprehension towards them, as he did not know who they were. However, the angels reassured him, telling him not to be afraid, and gave him the good news of a son who would be born to him, who would be knowledgeable and wise. This son is believed to be Prophet Ishaq (Isaac). The interpretation is that even in moments of uncertainty or fear, there can be blessings and good tidings from Allah. It also highlights the importance of knowledge and wisdom, as the son being foretold is described as "learned".
orig: فأوجس منهم خيفة قالوا لا تخف وبشروه بغلام عليم

translation: And his wife approached with a cry and struck her face and said, "[I am] a barren old woman!"
interpretation: This verse is describing the reaction of Abraham's wife, Sarah, upon hearing the news that she would bear a child in her old age. Her response of crying out and striking her face demonstrates her shock and disbelief at this seemingly impossible news, as she had been barren throughout her life. Her exclamation of being a "barren old woman" further emphasizes her astonishment, as she had long accepted her inability to have children, especially at her advanced age. This reaction highlights the miraculous nature of the announcement and the power of God to bring about the seemingly impossible.
orig: فأقبلت امرأته في صرة فصكت وجهها وقالت عجوز عقيم

translation: They said, "Thus has your Lord said. Indeed, He is the Wise, the Knowing."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the wisdom and knowledge of Allah. When the angels convey a message or a decree from Allah, they affirm that it is from the All-Wise and All-Knowing. This highlights the fact that Allah's decisions and commands are based on His infinite wisdom and knowledge, and that He is aware of all things, including the past, present, and future, as well as what is apparent and what is hidden. It also serves as a reminder for believers to trust in Allah's wisdom and submit to His will, knowing that He always does what is best for His creation.
orig: قالوا كذلك قال ربك إنه هو الحكيم العليم

translation: He said, "Then what is your mission, O messengers?"
interpretation: In this verse, the addressee (likely a figure of authority) is questioning a group of messengers about the purpose of their visit or the message they have come to convey. The inquiry "Then what is your mission?" suggests that the addressee is seeking to understand the reason behind the messengers' presence and the nature of the task or objective they have been sent to accomplish. The use of the term "O messengers" indicates that the addressee recognizes or acknowledges their status as individuals bearing a message or representing a higher authority. This verse sets the stage for the messengers to deliver their message or explain their purpose, highlighting the importance of their mission and the significance of the interaction between the questioner and the messengers.
orig: قال فما خطبكم أيها المرسلون

translation: They said, "Indeed, we have been sent to a people of criminals"
interpretation: This verse is likely referring to the angels sent to the people of Lot to warn them of their impending destruction due to their sinful behavior. The interpretation is that when a society becomes engrossed in major sins and immorality, Allah may send messengers or signs to warn them to repent and reform before divine punishment befalls them. It is a reminder that no nation is immune from Allah's judgment if they persist in evil and reject the guidance sent to them.
orig: قالوا إنا أرسلنا إلى قوم مجرمين

translation: That We may send upon them stones of clay
interpretation: This verse refers to the punishment that Allah inflicted upon the People of the Elephant who attempted to destroy the Ka'bah. Allah sent birds that pelted them with stones of baked clay, destroying the army. It demonstrates Allah's power to protect His House and punish those who seek to profane it or harm the believers. The verse also serves as a warning to anyone who might attempt to attack or destroy the sacred symbols and places of Islam, as they will face severe divine retribution.
orig: لنرسل عليهم حجارة من طين

translation: Marked in the presence of your Lord for the transgressors.
interpretation: This verse warns that those who transgress the limits set by Allah and indulge in excessive and extravagant behavior are marked or identified in Allah's presence. Their deeds are recorded, and they will be held accountable for their actions on the Day of Judgment. It serves as a reminder that Allah is aware of the transgressors and their actions, and they will face the consequences of their extravagance and disobedience.
orig: مسومة عند ربك للمسرفين

translation: So We brought out whoever was in the cities of the believers.
interpretation: This verse speaks to the idea that God will protect and save the believers from punishment or destruction, even if they are in the midst of a disbelieving society. It shows that God's mercy and care extends to all those who have faith, and that He will ultimately deliver them from harm or oppression. The verse also implies that the believers may be few in number compared to the disbelievers around them, but that this does not diminish their worth or God's love for them. Ultimately, it is a reassurance to the believers that God is aware of their situation and will save them in times of hardship or danger.
orig: فأخرجنا من كان فيها من المؤمنين

translation: But We found not there any household of the Muslims except one [single] house.
interpretation: This verse suggests that at the time and place being referred to, there was only a single household or family of Muslims present. It implies that the Muslim population in that area was very small or nearly non-existent, with the exception of one solitary Muslim home. The verse highlights the scarcity or rarity of Muslims in that particular location during the period being discussed.
orig: فما وجدنا فيها غير بيت من المسلمين

translation: And We left therein a sign for those who fear the painful punishment.
interpretation: This verse indicates that Allah has left a clear sign or evidence in the story or the place mentioned previously, which serves as a reminder and a warning for those who fear the painful punishment in the Hereafter. This sign is meant to encourage people to reflect upon the consequences of their actions and to live righteously in accordance with Allah's guidance, so that they may avoid the severe punishment that awaits the wrongdoers in the afterlife. The verse emphasizes the importance of being mindful of the Hereafter and living a life that pleases Allah.
orig: وتركنا فيها آية للذين يخافون العذاب الأليم

translation: And in Moses, when We sent him to Pharaoh with a clear authority.
interpretation: This verse refers to the story of Prophet Moses, who was sent by Allah to Pharaoh with clear signs and miracles as proof of his prophethood. The "clear authority" mentioned in the verse indicates the compelling evidence and strong arguments that Moses presented to Pharaoh to establish the truth of his message and to call him towards the worship of the One True God. It also signifies the divine support and power that Allah bestowed upon Moses to confront the tyranny and disbelief of Pharaoh and his people. The verse emphasizes the importance of conveying the message of Islam with clarity, wisdom, and authority, following the example of Prophet Moses.
orig: وفي موسى إذ أرسلناه إلى فرعون بسلطان مبين

translation: But he turned away with his supporters and said, "[He is] a magician or a madman."
interpretation: This verse is referring to the disbelievers who rejected the message of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him). When they heard his teachings and saw the signs of his prophethood, they turned away in arrogance and pride, dismissing him as a mere magician or a madman. They refused to accept the truth out of their own stubborn resistance, preferring to cling to their false beliefs and worldly interests. The verse highlights the common reaction of those who are deeply entrenched in their ways and unwilling to open their hearts to divine guidance, even when confronted with clear evidence.
orig: فتولى بركنه وقال ساحر أو مجنون

translation: So We seized him and his soldiers, and We threw them into the sea, and he was blameworthy.
interpretation: This verse is a warning to those who oppose God and His messengers. It refers to the story of Pharaoh, who rejected the message of Moses and oppressed the Children of Israel. As a result, God punished Pharaoh and his army by drowning them in the sea. The verse emphasizes that Pharaoh was "maliim" (blameworthy) for his actions and his fate serves as a reminder that those who defy God's will and oppress others will ultimately face the consequences of their deeds.
orig: فأخذناه وجنوده فنبذناهم في اليم وهو مليم

translation: And in 'Aad [there is a sign], when We sent against them the barren wind.
interpretation: This verse refers to the story of the people of 'Aad, an ancient Arabian tribe. As a punishment for their disbelief and arrogance, Allah sent upon them a devastating wind that destroyed everything in its path. The term "barren wind" emphasizes its destructive nature, as it brought no benefit or mercy, only ruin. This serves as a reminder that Allah's punishment can come in various forms and that no one is beyond His reach when they persist in wrongdoing and reject His guidance. It is a warning to heed the lessons of history and to humble oneself before the power and authority of the Almighty.
orig: وفي عاد إذ أرسلنا عليهم الريح العقيم

translation: It spares nothing that it comes upon, but makes it like disintegrated ruins.
interpretation: This verse is referring to the overwhelming and destructive power of the Day of Judgment. When it arrives, it will spare nothing and leave everything in a state of complete ruin and disintegration, like decayed bones or debris. It emphasizes the all-encompassing nature of the Day of Judgment and how it will completely transform and destroy the world as we know it, leaving nothing untouched. This serves as a reminder of the ultimate fate that awaits all of creation and the importance of being prepared for that inevitable day.
orig: ما تذر من شيء أتت عليه إلا جعلته كالرميم

translation: And [We had sent] to Thamud their brother Salih, [saying], "Worship Allah," but at once they were two parties conflicting.
interpretation: This verse refers to the story of the prophet Salih and his people, the Thamud. Salih was sent by Allah to guide the Thamud to the right path and to worship Allah alone. However, the Thamud were divided into two groups - those who believed in Salih's message and those who rejected it. The interpretation is that when a prophet or messenger is sent by Allah to a people, they often become divided into believers and disbelievers. This highlights the human tendency to differ and dispute, even when presented with clear guidance from Allah. It also emphasizes the importance of unity and following the path of truth, as opposed to creating divisions based on personal desires or interests.
orig: وفي ثمود إذ قيل لهم تمتعوا حتى حين

translation: But they turned away from the command of their Lord, so the thunderbolt seized them while they were looking on.
interpretation: This verse is a warning to those who disobey Allah's commands. It shows that defiance of Allah's orders can lead to severe consequences, such as being struck by a thunderbolt. The punishment is swift and comes while they are witnessing it, emphasizing the immediacy of Allah's retribution against the disobedient. It serves as a reminder for believers to stay steadfast in their faith and obedience to Allah, as those who arrogantly turn away from His path will face grave repercussions in this life and the hereafter.
orig: فعتوا عن أمر ربهم فأخذتهم الصاعقة وهم ينظرون

translation: So they were not able to rise up, nor could they help themselves.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the complete helplessness and powerlessness of those who reject Allah's message and oppose His will. Despite their arrogance and defiance, they will be brought low and rendered utterly incapable of resisting Allah's judgment or defending themselves against His punishment. It serves as a warning to those who persist in disbelief and rebellion, reminding them that ultimately, no one can stand against the power and authority of the Almighty Creator.
orig: فما استطاعوا من قيام وما كانوا منتصرين

translation: And the people of Noah before; indeed they were a defiantly disobedient people.
interpretation: This verse refers to the people of Prophet Noah, who lived long before the time of the Qur'an's revelation. It states that they were a corrupt and sinful people who persistently disobeyed Allah's commands and rejected the message brought to them by Noah. The verse implies that their defiant disobedience was the reason for their ultimate destruction through the Great Flood. It serves as a warning to later generations not to follow in their footsteps, but to heed the call of Allah's messengers and live righteously.
orig: وقوم نوح من قبل إنهم كانوا قوما فاسقين

translation: And the heaven, We constructed it with strength, and indeed We are [its] expander.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the power and majesty of Allah in His creation of the heavens. The use of the word "strength" or "power" (aydin) implies that the creation of the heavens is a testament to Allah's immense capabilities and that He has built it with a firm foundation. The second part of the verse, stating that Allah is the expander of the heavens, alludes to the vastness of the universe and Allah's ability to extend and spread out His creation continuously. It also suggests that the universe is not static but is ever-expanding, which is in line with modern scientific discoveries about the expanding nature of the universe. This verse invites humans to reflect on the magnificence of Allah's creation and to acknowledge His boundless power and wisdom in designing and maintaining the heavens.
orig: والسماء بنيناها بأيد وإنا لموسعون

translation: And the earth We have spread out, and excellent is the preparer.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's power and creativity in designing and creating the earth. The earth has been spread out and made suitable for human habitation, with its vast expanses, mountains, valleys, and resources that sustain life. The use of the word "Maahidoon" (preparer) suggests that the earth has been meticulously prepared and equipped to support the needs of its inhabitants. This verse encourages reflection on the divine wisdom behind the earth's creation and instills a sense of gratitude towards the Creator for providing such a well-designed and hospitable planet for humanity to live upon.
orig: والأرض فرشناها فنعم الماهدون

translation: And of all things We created two mates, that perhaps you may remember.
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine wisdom behind the creation of all things in pairs. It invites humans to reflect upon the purposeful duality that exists in the universe, such as male and female, day and night, and positive and negative charges. By contemplating these pairs, one can appreciate the delicate balance and complementary nature of God's creation. This realization should inspire gratitude and serve as a reminder of God's power, wisdom, and the inherent order in the universe. Ultimately, this verse encourages people to be mindful of their Creator and to live in harmony with the natural pairs and balance that exist in all aspects of life.
orig: ومن كل شيء خلقنا زوجين لعلكم تذكرون

translation: So flee to Allah. Indeed, I am to you from Him a clear warner.
interpretation: This verse is a clear call to turn to Allah and seek His protection and guidance. It emphasizes the importance of fleeing from all that displeases Allah and running towards His mercy and forgiveness. The Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) is instructed to warn people that he is a clear warner from Allah, urging them to heed his message and follow the path of righteousness. It highlights the urgency of turning to Allah in repentance and submission before it is too late, as there will come a Day of Judgment when all will be held accountable for their deeds. The verse serves as a reminder for believers to prioritize their relationship with Allah above all else and to strive towards earning His pleasure and avoiding His wrath.
orig: ففروا إلى الله إني لكم منه نذير مبين

translation: And do not set up with Allah another deity. Indeed, I am to you from Him a clear warner.
interpretation: This verse is a clear warning against the grave sin of associating partners with Allah (shirk). It emphasizes the importance of worshipping Allah alone and not ascribing divine attributes or powers to anyone or anything else. The Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) is instructed to convey this message as a "clear warner," highlighting the severity and consequences of committing shirk. This interpretation underscores the fundamental Islamic belief in the oneness of Allah (tawheed) and the necessity of directing all worship and devotion solely to Him.
orig: ولا تجعلوا مع الله إلها آخر إني لكم منه نذير مبين

translation: Similarly, no messenger came to those before them except that they said, "[He is] a magician or a madman."
interpretation: This verse highlights the stubborn disbelief and rejection that previous nations showed towards the messengers sent to them by Allah. Instead of accepting the clear proofs and guidance brought by these messengers, the disbelievers would dismiss them as mere magicians or madmen. This pattern of denial and accusation demonstrates the arrogance and closed-mindedness of those who refuse to acknowledge the truth, even when it is presented to them clearly. The verse also serves as a consolation to Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him), reminding him that he is not alone in facing such opposition and that the prophets before him encountered similar challenges in delivering Allah's message to their people.
orig: كذلك ما أتى الذين من قبلهم من رسول إلا قالوا ساحر أو مجنون

translation: Did they exhort each other to it? Rather, they are a transgressing people.
interpretation: This verse suggests that the disbelievers did not advise one another to follow the truth or believe in the message brought by the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him). Instead, they collectively chose to persist in their transgression and defiance of God's commands. The rhetorical question implies that their disbelief and rejection of the truth was not due to a lack of mutual encouragement towards righteousness, but rather a result of their own rebellious nature and their desire to overstep the limits set by God. The verse emphasizes that they are a people who have exceeded all bounds in their disobedience and have become utterly misguided.
orig: أتواصوا به بل هم قوم طاغون

translation: So turn away from them, and you are not to be blamed.
interpretation: This verse is advising the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) to turn away from those who reject his message and persist in disbelief. It reassures him that he is not to be blamed or held accountable for their choice to reject faith, as he has fulfilled his duty of conveying the message of Islam to them. The responsibility now lies with the disbelievers for their decision. The Prophet is instructed to focus his efforts on those who are open to guidance and receptive to the truth, without being disheartened by those who stubbornly oppose it.
orig: فتول عنهم فما أنت بملوم

translation: And remind, for indeed, the reminder benefits the believers.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance and benefits of reminding the believers about Allah's message and teachings. It suggests that even though the believers have faith, they still need to be constantly reminded of their religious duties and the rewards that await them in the Hereafter. The act of reminding serves as a means of strengthening their faith, keeping them steadfast on the right path, and helping them avoid distractions or deviations. Moreover, this verse implies that those who are receptive to such reminders and take heed of them are the ones who will truly benefit from the guidance provided in the Qur'an.
orig: وذكر فإن الذكرى تنفع المؤمنين

translation: And I did not create the jinn and mankind except to worship Me.
interpretation: The ultimate purpose of the creation of jinn and mankind is to worship Allah alone. This verse emphasizes that the primary reason for our existence is to acknowledge and submit to the Oneness of Allah, dedicating our lives to His worship and obedience. It reminds us that our worldly pursuits and desires should be secondary to our devotion to Allah, as fulfilling this purpose is the key to achieving success and contentment in both this life and the Hereafter.
orig: وما خلقت الجن والإنس إلا ليعبدون

translation: I do not want from them any provision, nor do I want them to feed Me.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the fact that Allah is not in need of anything from His creation. He does not require sustenance or nourishment from them, as He is the One who provides for all. It highlights Allah's absolute independence and self-sufficiency, while also reminding humans that their acts of worship and obedience are for their own benefit and not because Allah needs them in any way. This verse encourages humans to be sincere in their worship, seeking only Allah's pleasure and not expecting any worldly gain or reciprocity from Him.
orig: ما أريد منهم من رزق وما أريد أن يطعمون

translation: Indeed, it is Allah who is the [continual] Provider, the firm possessor of strength.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah is the sole provider and sustainer of all creation. He possesses immense strength and power, and His provisions are constant and unwavering. It serves as a reminder for believers to rely on Allah for their needs and to trust in His ability to provide for them, even in times of hardship or uncertainty. The verse also highlights one of the divine attributes of Allah, "Al-Razzaq" (the Provider), which underscores His role as the source of all sustenance, both physical and spiritual.
orig: إن الله هو الرزاق ذو القوة المتين

translation: Indeed, those who have wronged will have a share [of punishment] like the share of their companions, so let them not be impatient.
interpretation: This verse warns the wrongdoers that they will face a punishment similar to that which befell previous nations who also transgressed. It cautions them against hastening the coming of that punishment out of arrogance or disbelief, for it will surely come to pass at its appointed time. The verse implies that the fate of past nations serves as a lesson and reminder for those in the present. It emphasizes the universality and inevitability of divine justice, and encourages introspection and repentance before it is too late.
orig: فإن للذين ظلموا ذنوبا مثل ذنوب أصحابهم فلا يستعجلون

translation: So woe to those who disbelieve from their Day which they are promised.
interpretation: This verse is a stern warning to those who reject faith in God and the Day of Judgment. The phrase "woe to those" (فويل للذين) emphasizes the severity of the punishment that awaits the disbelievers on the Day they are promised, which refers to the Day of Resurrection. It implies that they will face a terrible fate as a consequence of their disbelief and their failure to heed the warnings sent by God through His messengers. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of faith and the gravity of denying the truth of God's message.
orig: فويل للذين كفروا من يومهم الذي يوعدون

translation: By the Mount
interpretation: In this verse, Allah swears by "the Mount" which refers to Mount Sinai where Prophet Moses received divine revelation. The act of swearing by this sacred place emphasizes the importance and gravity of the message that follows in the subsequent verses. It also serves as a reminder of the significant events that took place on Mount Sinai, such as the communication between Allah and Moses, and the giving of the Ten Commandments. By invoking this location, the verse draws attention to the continuity of divine revelation throughout history and the pivotal role of prophets in conveying Allah's message to humanity.
orig: والطور

translation: And by the Book inscribed.
interpretation: This verse is referring to the Qur'an itself, which is described as a "Book inscribed". This emphasizes the divine nature and preservation of the Qur'an. It is a book that has been written down and recorded, safeguarded from alteration or corruption. The use of the term "inscribed" also alludes to the permanence and immutability of the Qur'anic message. It is a reminder that the Qur'an is not just any ordinary book, but a sacred scripture whose every word is divinely ordained and protected by Allah.
orig: وكتاب مسطور

translation: In parchment spread out
interpretation: This verse is referring to the Qur'an itself, which is written on pages of parchment that are spread out. It emphasizes the physical nature of the Qur'an as a tangible scripture, while also alluding to its wide dissemination and accessibility to people. The spread-out parchment symbolizes the vastness and expansiveness of the Qur'an's message and its potential to reach all of humanity.
orig: في رق منشور

translation: And by the much-frequented House
interpretation: The "much-frequented House" refers to the Ka'bah in Mecca, which is the holiest site in Islam. It is believed to have been built by the Prophet Ibrahim and his son Ismail as a house of worship dedicated to the one true God. The Ka'bah is the direction towards which all Muslims face when performing their prayers, and it is also the focal point of the annual Hajj pilgrimage. The verse emphasizes the sanctity and importance of the Ka'bah as a symbol of monotheism and unity among believers.
orig: والبيت المعمور

translation: And by the raised canopy [of heaven]
interpretation: This verse is referring to the sky or the heavens above us, which Allah has raised high without any pillars or support that we can see. It is a sign of Allah's immense power and creative ability that He has created this vast, lofty canopy above us. The verse invites us to reflect on the wonders of Allah's creation and to be in awe of His majesty. It reminds us that just as the heavens are elevated high above us by Allah's power, similarly Allah is exalted high above His creation in His attributes and is not similar to any of His creation.
orig: والسقف المرفوع

translation: And by the sea filled with fire,
interpretation: This verse is an oath by Allah swearing by the sea that will be set ablaze on the Day of Judgment. It could symbolize the vastness and intensity of the events on that momentous day. The sea "filled with fire" paints a vivid and terrifying picture of the end of times, showing Allah's ultimate power over His creation. This oath serves to emphasize the gravity and certainty of the divine message that follows in the subsequent verses of the chapter.
orig: والبحر المسجور

translation: Indeed, the punishment of your Lord will surely take place.
interpretation: This verse is a stern warning from Allah that His punishment is inevitable for those who persist in disbelief and wrongdoing. It emphasizes the certainty and inescapability of divine retribution. The verse serves as a reminder for humans to be mindful of their actions and to turn to Allah in repentance before it is too late, for when the punishment arrives, there will be no escape from it. It is a call to reflect on one's deeds and to strive for righteousness in this life before facing the consequences in the Hereafter.
orig: إن عذاب ربك لواقع

translation: There is no repeller for it.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the inevitability and irresistible nature of God's decree or punishment when it comes. It suggests that when God decides to send down His judgment or retribution, no one can prevent, avert, or push it back. It highlights the absolute power and authority of God over all affairs and the ultimate submission of all things to His will. The verse implies that humans should be mindful of their actions and strive to follow the right path to avoid facing the unstoppable consequences of divine justice.
orig: ما له من دافع

translation: On the Day the heaven will sway with circular motion
interpretation: This verse is referring to the Day of Judgment, when the universe as we know it will be in a state of upheaval and destruction. The swaying and circular motion of the heavens depicts the severity of the events that will unfold. It symbolizes the tremendous changes and instability that will occur on that Day, as the existing order is dismantled. This conveys the immense power and authority of Allah over His creation, and serves as a reminder of the temporary nature of this world and the importance of preparing for the eternal Hereafter.
orig: يوم تمور السماء مورا

translation: And the mountains will move away with [definite] movement.
interpretation: This verse is referring to the Day of Judgment, when the mountains, which seem so firm and immovable in this world, will be set in motion and will move away. This is a sign of the tremendous upheaval and change that will occur on that Day. The verse is emphasizing the power of Allah and the reality of the Day of Judgment, when all of creation will be transformed and nothing will remain as it was in this world. It is a reminder to humanity that everything in this life is temporary and that we will all face the consequences of our deeds in the Hereafter.
orig: وتسير الجبال سيرا

translation: Then woe, that Day, to the deniers.
interpretation: This verse is a stern warning to those who reject the truth of the Day of Judgment. "Woe" here signifies a severe punishment and suffering that awaits those who persistently deny the reality of the Hereafter, despite clear signs and warnings. It emphasizes the gravity of their disbelief and the consequences they will face on that Day for their rejection of faith. The repetition of this warning throughout the chapter underscores the importance of belief in the Day of Judgment as a fundamental tenet of Islam, and the dire fate that awaits those who refuse to acknowledge it.
orig: فويل يومئذ للمكذبين

translation: Those who are engrossed in vain discourse
interpretation: This verse is referring to those who are preoccupied with futile and frivolous activities, wasting their time in idle talk and play. Instead of focusing on the remembrance of Allah and fulfilling their religious obligations, they indulge in meaningless pursuits. It is a reminder for believers to be mindful of how they spend their time and to prioritize their spiritual growth and righteous deeds over temporary amusements and distractions.
orig: الذين هم في خوض يلعبون

translation: The Day they are thrust toward the Fire of Hell with a [violent] thrust,
interpretation: This verse is referring to the Day of Judgment, when the disbelievers and sinners will be forcefully driven into the Fire of Hell as a punishment for their actions in this world. The use of the word "thrust" emphasizes the severity and violence of this punishment, indicating that they will have no choice or control over their fate. It serves as a stark warning and reminder to humanity about the consequences of rejecting faith and indulging in sin, urging them to mend their ways before it is too late.
orig: يوم يدعون إلى نار جهنم دعا

translation: This is the Fire which you used to deny.
interpretation: This verse is a stern warning and admonition to the disbelievers who denied the existence of Hellfire during their worldly life. It emphasizes that the Hellfire they face in the Hereafter is the very same one they used to reject and mock, despite the warnings from the prophets and messengers. The verse highlights the reality of the consequences of disbelief and the regret the deniers will feel when faced with the punishment they arrogantly dismissed. It serves as a reminder to all of the importance of faith, righteousness, and heeding the divine message before it is too late.
orig: هذه النار التي كنتم بها تكذبون

translation: Then is this magic, or do you not see?
interpretation: This verse is challenging the disbelievers who deny the truth of the Qur'an and attribute it to magic. It asks them rhetorically if what they are witnessing - the profound and miraculous nature of the Qur'an - is mere magic, or if they are simply blind to the truth and unable to perceive it for what it really is: a divine revelation from Allah. The implication is that the Qur'an is so powerful and convincing in its message that to dismiss it as magic is irrational, and that only those who lack insight and spiritual perception would fail to recognize it as the word of God.
orig: أفسحر هذا أم أنتم لا تبصرون

translation: Burn therein; then whether you are patient of it or impatient of it, it is all the same to you. You are only being recompensed [for] what you used to do.
interpretation: This verse is addressing the people of Hell, telling them that whether they bear the torment of the Fire with patience or not, it will make no difference to their situation. They will be punished in accordance with their deeds in the worldly life. It emphasizes the justice of Allah in dealing with His creation, as He only punishes people for the sins and evil they committed, and their reaction to the punishment does not change what they deserve. It also highlights the severity and eternity of the punishment in Hell, as being patient or impatient will not lighten it or change its duration.
orig: اصلوها فاصبروا أو لا تصبروا سواء عليكم إنما تجزون ما كنتم تعملون

translation: Indeed, the righteous will be in gardens and pleasure,
interpretation: This verse speaks about the ultimate reward for those who are righteous and live their lives in accordance with God's commands. "Gardens" here symbolize Paradise, a place of eternal bliss, beauty, and comfort. "Pleasure" denotes the various delights and joys that the righteous will experience in Paradise, both physical and spiritual. This includes not only the absence of any pain, sorrow, or discomfort, but also the presence of all that brings happiness, peace, and satisfaction to the soul. The verse emphasizes that this reward is certain and definite ("indeed") for those who qualify as "the righteous" through their faith, good deeds, and moral character in this worldly life.
orig: إن المتقين في جنات ونعيم

translation: Enjoying what their Lord has given them, and their Lord protected them from the punishment of Hellfire.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the blessings and rewards that the righteous will enjoy in Paradise. They will delight in the gifts bestowed upon them by Allah, which may include various pleasures and delights. Moreover, their Lord will have saved them from the severe torment of Hell, granting them protection and safety from the consequences of their sins. This highlights the mercy and generosity of Allah towards those who follow His path and obey His commands, as He not only rewards them with immense blessings but also spares them from the painful punishment of the Hereafter.
orig: فاكهين بما آتاهم ربهم ووقاهم ربهم عذاب الجحيم

translation: Eat and drink at ease for that which you have sent forth (good deeds) in days past!
interpretation: This verse is addressing the people of Paradise, telling them to enjoy the food and drink that is provided for them as a reward for their good deeds in their worldly life. It emphasizes the idea that the actions we take in this life have consequences in the afterlife, and that those who do good will be rewarded with ease and comfort in Paradise. The verse encourages believers to focus on doing good deeds, as they will be the basis for their eternal reward in the Hereafter.
orig: كلوا واشربوا هنيئا بما كنتم تعملون

translation: Reclining on lined up couches, and We will marry them to fair women with large, [beautiful] eyes.
interpretation: This verse speaks about the rewards that await the righteous believers in Paradise. The "lined up couches" symbolize comfort, luxury, and a high status that will be granted to them. The mention of being married to "fair women with large, beautiful eyes" is a metaphor indicating that the believers will have pure, beautiful spouses in Paradise. These spouses are described as having eyes that are large and lustrous, which was considered a mark of beauty in Arabic culture. The verse aims to convey the idea that Paradise will be a place of ultimate physical and spiritual fulfillment, where the believers will enjoy eternal blessings and delights as a reward for their faith and good deeds in this worldly life.
orig: متكئين على سرر مصفوفة وزوجناهم بحور عين

translation: And those who believed and whose descendants followed them in faith - We will join with them their descendants, and We will not deprive them of anything of their deeds. Every person, for what he earned, is retained.
interpretation: This verse highlights the mercy and justice of Allah. It shows that the righteous believers and their offspring who follow them in faith will be united together in Paradise. This is a great blessing and reward from Allah, showing His kindness to the believers and their families. At the same time, Allah emphasizes individual responsibility - each person will be held accountable for their own deeds and will reap what they have sown. No one will bear the burden of another or be deprived of the rewards of their own good works. This motivates us to have faith and do good, knowing that our efforts will not be lost, while also reminding us that we cannot rely on anyone else's deeds for our own salvation.
orig: والذين آمنوا واتبعتهم ذريتهم بإيمان ألحقنا بهم ذريتهم وما ألتناهم من عملهم من شيء كل امرئ بما كسب رهين

translation: And We will provide them with fruit and meat from whatever they desire.
interpretation: This verse is a promise from Allah to the believers in Paradise. It indicates that they will have an abundance of fruits and meats that they desire, without any restrictions or limitations. This is a reward for their faith, good deeds, and patience in this worldly life. The verse emphasizes the generosity and benevolence of Allah towards His faithful servants in the eternal life of bliss and satisfaction, where they will have everything they wish for as a manifestation of Allah's mercy and grace.
orig: وأمددناهم بفاكهة ولحم مما يشتهون

translation: Therein they will pass to one another a cup [of wine] wherein there is no ill speech or sin.
interpretation: This verse describes the blissful state of the righteous in Paradise. The cup being passed around is filled with pure wine that does not lead to any vain talk or sinful behavior. It symbolizes the spiritual purity and joy experienced by the believers in the afterlife, where they will be free from all worldly vices and temptations. The absence of ill speech and sin highlights the perfect harmony and peace that will prevail among the dwellers of Paradise, as they engage in virtuous and uplifting conversations while enjoying the delights bestowed upon them by Allah.
orig: يتنازعون فيها كأسا لا لغو فيها ولا تأثيم

translation: And there will circulate among them [servant] boys [especially] for them, as if they were pearls well-protected.
interpretation: This verse describes one of the rewards that the righteous believers will enjoy in Paradise. They will be served by young boys who are exclusively devoted to their service. These boys are described as being exceptionally beautiful, pure, and precious, like well-preserved pearls. This metaphor emphasizes their beauty, innocence, and the great value placed on them in Paradise. The presence of these servants is a manifestation of the honor, luxury, and comfort that the believers will experience as a reward for their faith and good deeds in this world.
orig: ويطوف عليهم غلمان لهم كأنهم لؤلؤ مكنون

translation: And they will approach one another, inquiring of each other.
interpretation: This verse refers to the Day of Judgment when people will turn to each other, asking about their deeds and the reasons behind their fate. It signifies the realization of the consequences of one's actions in the worldly life and the curiosity about how others fared. This inquiry among people highlights the importance of being mindful of one's conduct, as everyone will be held accountable for their deeds on that Day. It also emphasizes the significance of maintaining good relations with others, as people will be interested in knowing about each other's outcomes in the Hereafter.
orig: وأقبل بعضهم على بعض يتساءلون

translation: They will say, "Indeed, we were previously among our people fearful [of displeasing Allah].
interpretation: This verse speaks about the state of the righteous people in the Hereafter. They will acknowledge that during their worldly life, they lived among their families and communities in a state of fear and consciousness of Allah. They were always mindful of displeasing Him through sins and disobedience. This constant state of being fearful of Allah and seeking to please Him through good deeds is what led them to attain His mercy and reward in the afterlife. It highlights the importance of having Taqwa - consciousness and fear of Allah - in order to stay on the right path and attain success in this world and the next.
orig: قالوا إنا كنا قبل في أهلنا مشفقين

translation: But Allah conferred favor upon us and protected us from the punishment of the Scorching Fire.
interpretation: This verse expresses gratitude to Allah for His mercy and protection. It acknowledges that it is only through Allah's favor and grace that one can be saved from the severe punishment of Hell, described here as the "Scorching Fire". This interpretation highlights the importance of recognizing Allah's blessings and seeking His protection from the consequences of one's sins and wrongdoings in the afterlife. It emphasizes the need for humility and reliance on Allah's mercy, as ultimately, it is only through His favor that one can attain salvation and be shielded from the torment of Hell.
orig: فمن الله علينا ووقانا عذاب السموم

translation: Indeed, we used to call upon Him before. Indeed, it is He who is the Beneficent, the Merciful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of consistently turning to Allah in supplication and remembrance, both in times of ease and hardship. It highlights that Allah has always been and will always be the source of all goodness, kindness, and mercy. The verse serves as a reminder for believers to maintain a strong connection with their Lord, acknowledging His benevolence and compassion towards His creation. It encourages individuals to seek Allah's guidance, support, and forgiveness throughout their lives, with the assurance that He will respond to their sincere invocations with love and mercy.
orig: إنا كنا من قبل ندعوه إنه هو البر الرحيم

translation: So remind, [O Muhammad]; you are not, by the favor of your Lord, a soothsayer or a madman.
interpretation: This verse is reassuring Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) that he is not a soothsayer or a madman, as his opponents accused him of being. Rather, he is a prophet and a messenger of Allah, and the revelations he receives are a favor and blessing from his Lord. The verse encourages him to continue his mission of reminding people of Allah's message, despite the accusations and opposition he faces. It emphasizes that his role is to deliver the message, and that he is not responsible for people's choices to accept or reject it.
orig: فذكر فما أنت بنعمت ربك بكاهن ولا مجنون

translation: Or do they say, "[He is] a poet for whom we await a misfortune of time?"
interpretation: This verse is a response to those who reject the Prophet Muhammad's message and accuse him of being a mere poet. The disbelievers are essentially saying that they are waiting for some calamity or misfortune to befall the Prophet, proving that he is not a true messenger of Allah. The Qur'an refutes this notion, affirming that the Prophet's words are divinely inspired and not the product of poetic imagination. It also implies that those who wish ill upon the Prophet will themselves face the consequences of their disbelief and opposition to the truth.
orig: أم يقولون شاعر نتربص به ريب المنون

translation: Say, "Wait, for indeed I am, with you, among those who wait."
interpretation: This verse is a warning to those who oppose the message of Islam and the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him). It tells them to wait and see what will happen, as the believers are also waiting patiently for the ultimate outcome. The verse implies that the truth will eventually prevail and the opponents will face the consequences of their actions. It is a reminder to have faith in God's plan and to remain steadfast in the face of adversity, knowing that the final victory belongs to the believers.
orig: قل تربصوا فإني معكم من المتربصين

translation: Or do their minds command them this [i.e., to tell lies about Allah], or are they a transgressing people?
interpretation: This verse questions whether the disbelievers are being driven by their own misguided thoughts and desires to reject the truth and fabricate lies about Allah, or if they are simply a people who have crossed all boundaries of righteousness and are steeped in transgression and rebellion against Allah. It suggests that their behavior is either a result of their own corrupt minds and desires, or a reflection of their inherently rebellious and disobedient nature. The verse implies that there is no justification for their rejection of the truth and their slanderous lies against Allah, and that they will be held accountable for their actions.
orig: أم تأمرهم أحلامهم بهذا أم هم قوم طاغون

translation: Or do they say, "He has made it up"? Rather, they do not believe.
interpretation: This verse is addressing the disbelievers who accuse the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) of fabricating the Qur'an. It refutes their claim by stating that the real reason for their rejection is not any flaw in the Qur'an, but rather their lack of faith. They are not willing to believe in the divine message, so they resort to making false accusations against the Prophet. The verse implies that if they were sincere seekers of truth, they would recognize the Qur'an as the word of Allah and embrace its teachings. Their stubborn refusal to believe is rooted in their arrogance and attachment to their old ways, not in any legitimate criticism of the Qur'an itself.
orig: أم يقولون تقوله بل لا يؤمنون

translation: Then let them produce a discourse like it, if they are truthful.
interpretation: This verse challenges those who doubt the divine origin of the Qur'an to produce a discourse that matches its eloquence, wisdom, and profound message. It implies that the Qur'an is inimitable and could not have been produced by any human being, as it is a miracle from Allah. The verse emphasizes that if the doubters are truthful in their claim that the Qur'an is not from Allah, then they should be able to create something similar to it. However, the Qur'an's unique style, structure, and content are beyond human capability, serving as a testament to its divine source.
orig: فليأتوا بحديث مثله إن كانوا صادقين

translation: Or were they created by nothing, or were they the creators [of themselves]?
interpretation: This verse poses a rhetorical question to make people reflect on the fact that they could not have come into existence without a Creator. It challenges the notion that humans came into being without any cause or that they created themselves, both of which are logically impossible. The implied answer is that Allah is the only One who could have created human beings and everything else in existence. This verse encourages people to acknowledge their Creator and to submit to Him in gratitude and worship.
orig: أم خلقوا من غير شيء أم هم الخالقون

translation: Or did they create the heavens and the earth? Rather, they are not certain.
interpretation: This verse questions the belief of those who deny Allah's existence and creative power. It challenges them by asking if they themselves created the vast heavens and the earth, which is an impossibility for any human being. The verse implies that if they cannot create such magnificent entities, then how can they doubt the existence of the One who did create them? The verse ends by stating that despite this clear evidence, they still lack certainty in their hearts about Allah's existence and His role as the Creator of all things. This highlights the stubbornness and arrogance of those who reject faith in Allah, even when faced with undeniable signs of His power and majesty in the creation around them.
orig: أم خلقوا السماوات والأرض بل لا يوقنون

translation: Or do they have the depositories of your Lord, or are they the controllers?
interpretation: This verse questions whether the disbelievers have access to the treasures of Allah's knowledge and power, or if they have the authority to control and manage the affairs of the universe. It highlights the fact that only Allah possesses such power and knowledge, and that the disbelievers are deluding themselves if they think they have any control over the workings of the world. The verse emphasizes the complete sovereignty and omnipotence of Allah, while exposing the weakness and ignorance of those who reject His authority.
orig: أم عندهم خزائن ربك أم هم المصيطرون

translation: Or have they a stairway [into the heaven] upon which they listen? Then let their listener produce a clear authority.
interpretation: This verse is challenging the disbelievers who claim to have access to divine knowledge or revelation. It asks rhetorically whether they have a stairway or ladder to climb up into heaven and eavesdrop on the conversations of the angels to gain this supposed knowledge. If they make such a claim, then the Qur'an demands they bring clear proof and authority to support it. The implication is that their claims are baseless and they have no such proof, thus exposing the falsehood of their assertions to have divine knowledge that contradicts the message brought by Prophet Muhammad (pbuh). It emphasizes that divine revelation only comes through the proper channels that God has established, not through illicit means claimed by those who oppose the truth.
orig: أم لهم سلم يستمعون فيه فليأت مستمعهم بسلطان مبين

translation: Or has He taken daughters for Himself and chosen sons for you?
interpretation: This verse is questioning the belief of the pagan Arabs who attributed daughters to Allah while considering it a disgrace to have daughters themselves. It highlights the contradiction and irrationality in their thinking. The verse implies that attributing children to Allah is blasphemous, and that the preference for sons over daughters is baseless and unjust. It challenges the prevailing notions of gender bias and emphasizes the equality of all human beings before Allah.
orig: أم له البنات ولكم البنون

translation: Or do you ask them for a payment, so they are burdened with a load of debt?
interpretation: This verse is questioning whether the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) is asking the people for any payment or reward for conveying the message of Islam to them. It suggests that if he were to do so, it would be a burden on them, like a heavy debt. However, the implication is that the Prophet is not asking for any worldly gain, but rather he is fulfilling his duty to convey the message of Allah purely for the sake of guiding humanity. This emphasizes the sincerity of the Prophet's mission and the fact that he is not motivated by any personal gain or desire for wealth or status.
orig: أم تسألهم أجرا فهم من مغرم مثقلون

translation: Or do they have [knowledge of] the unseen, so they write [it] down?
interpretation: This verse is questioning those who claim to have knowledge of the unseen or the future. It suggests that if they truly had such knowledge, they would be able to write it down and record it. The implication is that no one except Allah has knowledge of the unseen, and those who claim otherwise are merely making baseless assertions. It emphasizes the unique and exclusive nature of Allah's knowledge and the futility of anyone claiming to possess such knowledge independently of Him.
orig: أم عندهم الغيب فهم يكتبون

translation: Or do they intend a plot? But those who disbelieve - they are the object of a plot.
interpretation: This verse warns the disbelievers that their plots and schemes against Islam and the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) will ultimately fail and backfire on them. It implies that Allah is aware of their conspiracies and will protect His religion and His messenger. The verse also suggests that the disbelievers are deluded in thinking that they can outsmart or outmaneuver Allah, as it is they who are actually being plotted against by Allah in ways they cannot perceive. Ultimately, their plans will come to nothing and they will face the consequences of their actions in this world and the Hereafter.
orig: أم يريدون كيدا فالذين كفروا هم المكيدون

translation: Or have they a deity other than Allah? Exalted is Allah above whatever they associate with Him.
interpretation: This verse is a rhetorical question that highlights the concept of Tawheed (monotheism) in Islam. It challenges the idea of worshipping any deity besides Allah, emphasizing that Allah is far above and free from any partners or equals that people may associate with Him. The verse implies that it is irrational and baseless to worship anyone or anything other than the One True God, Allah. It serves as a reminder for believers to direct all their worship and devotion to Allah alone and to reject any form of polytheism or idolatry.
orig: أم لهم إله غير الله سبحان الله عما يشركون

translation: And if they were to see a fragment from the sky falling, they would say, "[It is merely] clouds heaped up."
interpretation: This verse is referring to the stubbornness and willful blindness of the disbelievers. Even if they were to witness a clear sign or miracle, such as a piece of the sky falling down, they would dismiss it and attribute it to something ordinary like clouds piled up on top of each other. They are so entrenched in their disbelief that they refuse to acknowledge any evidence that contradicts their views, no matter how extraordinary or undeniable it may be. It highlights their irrational denial and determination to reject the truth of God's messages and signs.
orig: وإن يروا كسفا من السماء ساقطا يقولوا سحاب مركوم

translation: So leave them until they meet their Day in which they will be struck insensible.
interpretation: This verse is a warning to the disbelievers who reject the message of Islam. It tells the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) to leave them alone and not to worry about their disbelief, for they will face the consequences of their actions on the Day of Judgment. On that day, they will be struck with a deafening blast that will render them unconscious and powerless. This interpretation emphasizes the inevitability of divine justice and the ultimate fate of those who choose to deny the truth of God's message.
orig: فذرهم حتى يلاقوا يومهم الذي فيه يصعقون

translation: The Day when their scheming will not avail them at all, nor will they be helped.
interpretation: This verse refers to the Day of Judgment when all the plots, plans, and schemes of the disbelievers will be of no use to them. They will not be able to escape the consequences of their actions, and no one will be there to help or support them. It emphasizes the futility of their scheming in this world and the ultimate justice that will be served in the Hereafter, where everyone will be held accountable for their deeds.
orig: يوم لا يغني عنهم كيدهم شيئا ولا هم ينصرون

translation: And indeed, for those who do wrong is a punishment before that, but most of them do not know.
interpretation: This verse serves as a warning to the wrongdoers and the unjust. It states that even before the ultimate punishment in the Hereafter, those who commit injustice and transgress the limits set by Allah will face consequences and punishment in this worldly life. However, most of these wrongdoers are unaware of this fact or choose to ignore it, continuing in their unjust ways without realizing the impending consequences of their actions. This verse encourages people to be mindful of their deeds and to refrain from wrongdoing, as Allah's punishment can befall them in this world as well, even before the final judgment in the Hereafter.
orig: وإن للذين ظلموا عذابا دون ذلك ولكن أكثرهم لا يعلمون

translation: And be patient for the decision of your Lord, for indeed, you are in Our eyes. And exalt [Allah] with praise of your Lord when you arise.
interpretation: This verse is a reminder to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and all believers to remain patient and steadfast in the face of adversity and challenges, knowing that they are under the watchful care and protection of Allah. It encourages them to have faith in Allah's plan and timing, and to trust that He will guide them through any difficulties. The verse also emphasizes the importance of praising and glorifying Allah at all times, especially upon waking or rising from sleep. This act of remembrance and gratitude helps to strengthen one's connection with Allah and maintain a positive mindset throughout the day. Ultimately, the verse highlights the value of patience, trust in Allah, and constant remembrance and praise of Him in navigating the ups and downs of life.
orig: واصبر لحكم ربك فإنك بأعيننا وسبح بحمد ربك حين تقوم

translation: And in a part of the night, exalt Him and after [the setting of] the stars.
interpretation: This verse encourages the believers to engage in worship and glorification of Allah during the night, particularly in the later part of the night after the stars have set. This is a time of solitude and tranquility, where one can focus on their spiritual connection with the Creator. The act of exalting Allah and engaging in His remembrance during these quiet moments is highly rewarding and helps strengthen one's faith and devotion. It also serves as a means of seeking forgiveness and purifying one's soul from the sins and distractions of the day.
orig: ومن الليل فسبحه وإدبار النجوم

translation: By the star when it descends,
interpretation: This verse is an oath taken by Allah, swearing by the star when it sets or descends. It could refer to any star or celestial body that appears to fall or descend, emphasizing the certainty and importance of the revelation that follows. The descending star symbolizes the divine knowledge and guidance sent down from the heavens through the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him). It also alludes to the transient nature of worldly life compared to the eternal truth and wisdom of Allah's message.
orig: والنجم إذا هوى

translation: Your companion [Muhammad] has not strayed, nor has he erred,
interpretation: This verse affirms that Prophet Muhammad, who is referred to as the companion, has not deviated from the right path or the truth in conveying the divine message. It emphasizes that he is guided by Allah and does not speak or act based on his own desires or whims. The verse serves as a testament to the Prophet's integrity, trustworthiness, and his unwavering commitment to delivering Allah's revelation to humanity without any alteration or error.
orig: ما ضل صاحبكم وما غوى

translation: Nor does he speak from [his own] inclination.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) does not speak or convey the message of Islam based on his own desires, whims, or personal inclinations. Rather, his words and teachings come from divine revelation, inspired and guided by Allah. This highlights the authenticity and trustworthiness of the Prophet's message, as it is not tainted by human bias or self-interest, but instead represents the pure and unadulterated word of God.
orig: وما ينطق عن الهوى

translation: It is not but a revelation revealed,
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the Qur'an is a divine revelation from Allah to Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him). It is not something that the Prophet invented or composed on his own, but rather it is a message that was revealed to him by Allah through the angel Gabriel. This interpretation highlights the divine origin and authenticity of the Qur'an, affirming that it is the direct word of Allah and not the product of human imagination or creation.
orig: إن هو إلا وحي يوحى

translation: Taught by one Mighty in Power.
interpretation: This verse refers to the fact that the Qur'an was taught to Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) by the angel Gabriel, who is described as being mighty in power. This emphasizes the divine origin and authority of the Qur'anic revelation, as it was not the product of human intellect or imagination, but rather a direct communication from God through His powerful angelic messenger.
