The verse also highlights the trustworthiness and reliability of the transmission process, as the Qur'an was faithfully conveyed by a being of immense strength and capability appointed by God Himself.
orig: علمه شديد القوى

translation: Possessor of Power, so He established Himself.
interpretation: This verse affirms Allah's attribute of having ultimate power and authority. It also emphasizes that Allah has established Himself above His creation on the Throne in a manner befitting His Majesty, without the "how" of it being known to us. This establishes Allah's sovereignty over all things and His being distinct from and above His creation.
orig: ذو مرة فاستوى

translation: And he was at the highest horizon.
interpretation: This verse is referring to the Prophet Muhammad's ascension to the highest point in the heavens during his miraculous night journey (Isra and Mi'raj). It signifies his elevated status and closeness to Allah, as he reached a point where no other human being had ever been before. The "highest horizon" symbolizes the pinnacle of spiritual attainment and the ultimate nearness to the Divine presence that the Prophet experienced during this extraordinary event.
orig: وهو بالأفق الأعلى

translation: Then he approached and descended
interpretation: This verse is referring to the Prophet Muhammad's miraculous journey known as the Isra and Mi'raj, where he ascended to the heavens and came close to Allah. The verse describes how the Prophet drew near to Allah and then descended back to earth. It symbolizes the intimate connection and communication between the Prophet and Allah, highlighting the spiritual significance of this extraordinary event in Islamic history. The verse also emphasizes the Prophet's unique status and his role as a messenger chosen by Allah to receive divine revelations.
orig: ثم دنا فتدلى

translation: And he was at a distance of two bow lengths or nearer.
interpretation: This verse is referring to the Prophet Muhammad's miraculous journey to the heavens, known as Al-Isra' wal-Mi'raj (the Night Journey and Ascension). During this journey, the Prophet came very close to Allah, metaphorically described as being at a distance of two bow lengths or even nearer. This symbolizes the intimate spiritual connection and closeness the Prophet experienced with Allah during this extraordinary event, highlighting his unique status and the special relationship he had with the Divine. It emphasizes the profound spiritual experience and the highest honor bestowed upon Prophet Muhammad by Allah.
orig: فكان قاب قوسين أو أدنى

translation: And He revealed to His servant what He revealed.
interpretation: This verse refers to the miraculous event of the Prophet Muhammad's ascension to heaven (Mi'raj), where Allah directly communicated with him and revealed profound truths and commandments. It emphasizes the special status of Muhammad as Allah's chosen servant and messenger, and highlights the direct and intimate nature of divine revelation. The repetition of "what He revealed" underscores the extraordinary and ineffable nature of this communication, which is beyond human comprehension. This verse affirms Muhammad's prophethood and the authenticity of the message he received from Allah.
orig: فأوحى إلى عبده ما أوحى

translation: The heart did not lie about what it saw.
interpretation: This verse affirms the truthfulness and reliability of Prophet Muhammad's vision and experience during his ascension to heaven (Mi'raj). It emphasizes that his heart, symbolizing his inner perception and understanding, did not deceive him or make false claims about what he witnessed during this miraculous journey. The verse serves as a testament to the authenticity of the Prophet's spiritual encounter and the divine revelations he received.
orig: ما كذب الفؤاد ما رأى

translation: So do you dispute with him over what he saw?
interpretation: This verse is questioning those who doubt or argue against the Prophet Muhammad's (peace be upon him) vision and experience during his ascension to heaven (Mi'raj). It implies that the Prophet's account of what he witnessed should not be contested, as it was a divine revelation and a true experience. The verse suggests that it is not appropriate for anyone to dispute or challenge the Prophet's direct encounter with the divine, emphasizing the authenticity and significance of his spiritual journey.
orig: أفتمارونه على ما يرى

translation: And he certainly saw him in another descent
interpretation: This verse refers to another occasion when Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) saw the angel Gabriel in his true form. This event, known as the "second vision", occurred during the Prophet's ascension to heaven (Mi'raj). The verse confirms that the Prophet had multiple encounters with Gabriel, emphasizing the authenticity of the revelation and the Prophet's direct connection with the divine. It also serves as a testament to the Prophet's unique status and the special favor bestowed upon him by Allah.
orig: ولقد رآه نزلة أخرى

translation: By the Lote Tree of the Utmost Boundary -
interpretation: The "Lote Tree of the Utmost Boundary" (Sidrat al-Muntaha) symbolizes the furthest limit of spiritual knowledge and closeness to Allah that any created being can attain. It represents the highest point that even the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) reached during his miraculous Night Journey and Ascension. Beyond this point, no one except Allah has knowledge of what lies further. This verse emphasizes that there are limits and boundaries to the spiritual realm and human understanding that only Allah can surpass. It also highlights the special status of Prophet Muhammad in attaining the closest possible proximity to the Divine Presence.
orig: عند سدرة المنتهى

translation: Near it is the Garden of Refuge -
interpretation: This verse refers to the highest level of Paradise, known as Jannah al-Ma'wa or the Garden of Refuge. It is a place of eternal peace and comfort, reserved for those who have attained the highest level of righteousness and closeness to Allah. The verse suggests that this Garden is situated near the Lote Tree of the Utmost Boundary (Sidrat al-Muntaha), which marks the end of the seventh heaven and the limit of what any creation can know about Allah's realm. Reaching this exalted abode is the ultimate goal and aspiration for the believers.
orig: عندها جنة المأوى

translation: When there covered the lote tree that which covered [it].
interpretation: This verse is referring to the miraculous event of the Prophet Muhammad's ascension to heaven (Mi'raj). The "lote tree" mentioned here is believed to be the "Sidrat al-Muntaha" or the farthest boundary in the seventh heaven, which marks the end of the created universe. The verse indicates that this tree was covered or enveloped by an immense, indescribable light or by a great number of angels. This covering symbolizes the magnificence and mystery of the divine realm that is beyond human comprehension. It also emphasizes the extraordinary nature of the Prophet's spiritual journey and his encounter with the divine presence at the highest point in the heavens.
orig: إذ يغشى السدرة ما يغشى

translation: The sight [of the Prophet] did not swerve, nor did it transgress [its limit].
interpretation: This verse affirms that during his miraculous journey to the heavens (Mi'raj), Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) remained steadfast in his vision and did not allow his sight to stray or go beyond what was divinely permitted. It emphasizes his unwavering commitment to the path of truth and his complete submission to the will of Allah. The verse also serves as a testament to the Prophet's integrity and trustworthiness, as he faithfully conveyed the divine message without any alteration or transgression.
orig: ما زاغ البصر وما طغى

translation: He has already seen some of the greatest Signs of his Lord.
interpretation: This verse refers to the Prophet Muhammad's miraculous night journey and ascension to heaven (Isra and Mi'raj), where he witnessed incredible signs of Allah's power and magnificence. This experience was a testament to Muhammad's prophethood and a confirmation of his divine message. It strengthened his faith and resolve, preparing him for the challenges he would face in spreading Islam. The verse emphasizes that the signs the Prophet saw were of the greatest magnitude, indicating the immense significance of this event in his spiritual journey and the history of Islam.
orig: لقد رأى من آيات ربه الكبرى

translation: So have you considered al-Lat and al-'Uzza?
interpretation: This verse is questioning the validity and power of the pagan idols al-Lat and al-'Uzza that were worshipped by the Arabs before Islam. It challenges the belief in these false deities, implying that they are not worthy of worship and have no real authority or influence. The rhetorical question serves to make the listeners reflect on the baselessness of their idolatrous practices and consider the truth of monotheism in worshipping the one true God, Allah.
orig: أفرأيتم اللات والعزى

translation: And Manat, the third - the other one.
interpretation: This verse refers to one of the three main idols that were worshipped by the pagan Arabs before the advent of Islam, alongside Al-Lat and Al-Uzza. Manat was considered the goddess of fate and destiny. The mention of these idols in the Qur'an serves to condemn idolatry and polytheistic practices, emphasizing that there is no deity worthy of worship except the One True God, Allah. It highlights the misguided beliefs of attributing divine powers to created beings or inanimate objects, which is in stark contrast to the Islamic principle of pure monotheism (tawhid).
orig: ومناة الثالثة الأخرى

translation: Is the male for you and for Him the female?
interpretation: This verse questions the belief of attributing daughters to Allah while desiring sons for themselves. It criticizes the hypocrisy and illogical thinking of those who ascribe to Allah what they dislike for themselves, as having daughters was seen as less desirable in their society. The verse highlights the inconsistency and flawed nature of such beliefs, emphasizing that Allah is far above their false assumptions and attributions.
orig: ألكم الذكر وله الأنثى

translation: That, then, is an unjust division.
interpretation: This verse is criticizing the polytheists who ascribed daughters to Allah while preferring sons for themselves. It emphasizes that such an attribution and division is extremely unjust and unfair, as it implies that they are assigning to Allah what they consider to be inferior (daughters), while keeping the preferred for themselves (sons). This highlights their flawed thinking and the baselessness of their beliefs in attributing offspring to Allah.
orig: تلك إذا قسمة ضيزى

translation: They are not but [mere] names you have named them - you and your forefathers - for which Allah has sent down no authority. They follow not except assumption and what [their] souls desire, and there has already come to them from their Lord guidance.
interpretation: This verse is a criticism of the polytheistic practice of naming and worshipping false deities that have no basis in divine revelation. It asserts that these names are mere human inventions, passed down through generations, without any legitimate authority from Allah. The polytheists are following their own whims, desires, and assumptions, despite the fact that Allah has already provided them with guidance through His messengers and revelations. This highlights the importance of adhering to divine guidance and not being misled by baseless traditions or personal inclinations in matters of faith and worship.
orig: إن هي إلا أسماء سميتموها أنتم وآباؤكم ما أنزل الله بها من سلطان إن يتبعون إلا الظن وما تهوى الأنفس ولقد جاءهم من ربهم الهدى

translation: Or shall man have what he wishes?
interpretation: This verse is questioning the notion that humans can simply wish for something and attain it without putting in the necessary effort or seeking the will of Allah. It suggests that mere wishful thinking is not enough to achieve one's desires and goals. Rather, one must strive and work towards them while aligning their actions with the teachings of Islam and seeking the pleasure of Allah. Ultimately, it is Allah who decides what each person will or will not have, not their own whims and desires.
orig: أم للإنسان ما تمنى

translation: To Allah belongs the Hereafter and the first [life].
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that both the afterlife and the present world belong to Allah alone. It is a reminder that Allah is the ultimate owner and controller of all things, from the beginning of creation to the eternal life after death. It implies that humans should focus on pleasing Allah in both this world and the next, as He is the One who holds power over all aspects of existence. The verse also suggests that the fleeting nature of the worldly life should not distract believers from their ultimate goal of attaining success in the Hereafter, which is the eternal abode.
orig: فلله الآخرة والأولى

translation: And there are many angels in the heavens whose intercession will not avail at all except after Allah has permitted [it] for whom He wills and approves.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute sovereignty and authority of Allah. It states that even the angels, who are highly revered creatures, cannot intercede on behalf of anyone without Allah's permission. Their intercession is not automatic or inherent, but rather depends on Allah's will and approval. This highlights the fact that all power and decision-making ultimately belong to Allah alone. It also serves as a reminder to humans that they should not seek intercession from anyone other than Allah or place their trust and hope in anyone besides Him. The verse underscores the importance of directing all worship, supplication, and reliance towards Allah alone.
orig: وكم من ملك في السماوات لا تغني شفاعتهم شيئا إلا من بعد أن يأذن الله لمن يشاء ويرضى

translation: Indeed, those who do not believe in the Hereafter name the angels female names.
interpretation: This verse criticizes the pre-Islamic Arab practice of referring to angels as daughters of Allah. It highlights the ignorance and disbelief of those who attribute female characteristics to the angels, which is seen as a form of polytheism. The Qur'an emphasizes that angels are genderless beings created by Allah to worship and serve Him. Assigning them feminine names is considered a misguided belief held by those who reject the concept of the Hereafter and the true nature of Allah's creation.
orig: إن الذين لا يؤمنون بالآخرة ليسمون الملائكة تسمية الأنثى

translation: And they have no knowledge of it. They follow nothing but conjecture, and indeed conjecture avails nothing against the truth.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that those who reject faith and follow their own desires have no real knowledge or evidence to support their beliefs. They rely solely on conjecture and speculation, which are baseless and futile in the face of divine truth. The Qur'an asserts that conjecture, no matter how strong or prevalent, cannot substitute for the absolute truth that comes from Allah. This serves as a reminder for believers to ground their faith in the revealed knowledge of the Qur'an and Sunnah, rather than falling prey to the whims and assumptions of those who are misguided.
orig: وما لهم به من علم إن يتبعون إلا الظن وإن الظن لا يغني من الحق شيئا

translation: So turn away from he who turns away from Our remembrance and desires not except the worldly life.
interpretation: This verse instructs the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and the believers to turn away from those who reject the message of Islam and are only concerned with the fleeting pleasures and gains of this worldly life. Such people have no interest in the remembrance of Allah or the eternal life of the Hereafter. The verse implies that engaging with those who persistently turn away from the truth is futile, and believers should focus their efforts on those who are open to guidance and spiritual growth. It also highlights the importance of prioritizing the eternal life over the temporary attractions of this world.
orig: فأعرض عن من تولى عن ذكرنا ولم يرد إلا الحياة الدنيا

translation: That is their sum of knowledge. Indeed, your Lord is most knowing of who has strayed from His way, and He is most knowing of who is [rightly] guided.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the limitedness of human knowledge compared to God's infinite knowledge. It asserts that God alone knows the true spiritual state of each individual - who is misguided and who is rightly guided. Humans can only judge based on outward actions, but God knows the secrets of the hearts. The verse reminds us to be humble about our own knowledge and judgments, and to put our ultimate trust in God's wisdom and guidance. It also implies that we should not be quick to condemn others, as their inner reality may be different from what we perceive.
orig: ذلك مبلغهم من العلم إن ربك هو أعلم بمن ضل عن سبيله وهو أعلم بمن اهتدى

translation: And to Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is in the earth - that He may recompense those who do evil with [the penalty of] what they have done and recompense those who do good with the best [reward] -
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute ownership and sovereignty of Allah over everything in the universe. It conveys that Allah, being the ultimate owner, has the power and right to judge and recompense people according to their deeds. Those who engage in evil actions will be punished in proportion to their wrongdoings, while those who do good will be rewarded with the finest reward, which is Paradise. This interpretation highlights the concept of divine justice and accountability, encouraging individuals to be mindful of their actions and strive for righteousness.
orig: ولله ما في السماوات وما في الأرض ليجزي الذين أساءوا بما عملوا ويجزي الذين أحسنوا بالحسنى

translation: Those who avoid the major sins and immoralities, only [committing] slight ones. Indeed, your Lord is vast in forgiveness. He was most knowing of you when He produced you from the earth and when you were fetuses in the wombs of your mothers. So do not claim yourselves to be pure; He is most knowing of who fears Him.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's vast forgiveness and knowledge of human beings. It encourages people to avoid major sins and shameful acts, acknowledging that minor sins are somewhat inevitable. However, one should not be arrogant or consider themselves pure, as Allah alone knows the true level of righteousness and piety of each individual. The verse also highlights Allah's omniscience, as He has been aware of each person since their creation from earth and development in the womb. Ultimately, it is a reminder to strive for humility, God-consciousness, and reliance on Allah's mercy rather than one's own perceived virtue.
orig: الذين يجتنبون كبائر الإثم والفواحش إلا اللمم إن ربك واسع المغفرة هو أعلم بكم إذ أنشأكم من الأرض وإذ أنتم أجنة في بطون أمهاتكم فلا تزكوا أنفسكم هو أعلم بمن اتقى

translation: Have you seen the one who turned away
interpretation: This verse is referring to those who turn away from the truth and the guidance of Allah. It is a rhetorical question that serves as a rebuke and a warning to those who reject faith and choose to follow their own desires instead of submitting to the will of Allah. The verse implies that such people are misguided and will face the consequences of their actions in the Hereafter. It is a reminder for believers to stay steadfast in their faith and not be swayed by the distractions and temptations of this world.
orig: أفرأيت الذي تولى

translation: So he gave a little and then stopped.
interpretation: This verse is criticizing those who are miserly and only give a little in charity before stopping. It suggests that such people are not truly generous or committed to helping others. The use of the word "akda" implies that their giving is grudging and reluctant, and they quickly become tired of it. The verse encourages Muslims to be consistently generous and to give freely without holding back, rather than making only token contributions. It emphasizes the importance of sincerity and wholeheartedness in acts of charity and kindness towards others.
orig: وأعطى قليلا وأكدى

translation: Does he have knowledge of the unseen, so he sees?
interpretation: This verse questions whether someone claims to have knowledge of the unseen realm (al-ghayb), which is known only to Allah. It implies that no one can claim to possess such knowledge or the ability to perceive the unseen, as this is a divine attribute belonging solely to Allah. The verse serves as a reminder that human beings are limited in their knowledge and should not make claims about matters that are beyond their understanding or perception.
orig: أعنده علم الغيب فهو يرى

translation: Or has he not been informed of what is in the scriptures of Moses?
interpretation: This verse is questioning whether the person being addressed has knowledge of the teachings and revelations contained within the scriptures revealed to Prophet Moses (peace be upon him). It suggests that the wisdom and guidance found in these earlier revelations should be known and heeded, as they come from the same divine source. The verse emphasizes the continuity of God's message throughout time and the importance of being aware of and learning from the teachings of previous prophets and scriptures.
orig: أم لم ينبأ بما في صحف موسى

translation: And [mention] Abraham, who fulfilled [his obligations].
interpretation: This verse refers to Prophet Abraham (peace be upon him) as one who fulfilled all the commands and obligations that Allah had placed upon him. He was steadfast in his devotion to Allah, unwavering in his faith, and fully committed to carrying out Allah's will, even when it meant great personal sacrifice. Abraham's obedience and submission to Allah is held up as an example for all believers to aspire to. The verse emphasizes the importance of being faithful to one's covenant with Allah and striving to live up to the responsibilities and duties of faith.
orig: وإبراهيم الذي وفى

translation: That no bearer of burdens will bear the burden of another.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the concept of individual responsibility in Islam. Each person is accountable for their own actions and will bear the consequences of their deeds. No one can carry the burden of another's sins or be held responsible for their wrongdoings. This highlights the importance of personal accountability and the need for each individual to strive for righteousness in their own lives, as they will face the ultimate judgment based on their own actions and intentions.
orig: ألا تزر وازرة وزر أخرى

translation: And that there is not for man except that [good] for which he strives
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of individual effort and responsibility. It states that a person will only be rewarded for the good deeds they themselves have strived for and earned through their own actions. It highlights the concept of personal accountability, as no one can rely on the good deeds of others or expect unearned rewards. The verse encourages people to actively work towards righteousness and not be passive in their faith, as ultimately, each individual is responsible for their own spiritual growth and will be judged accordingly by God based on their own efforts and intentions.
orig: وأن ليس للإنسان إلا ما سعى

translation: And that his effort will be seen.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of individual responsibility and accountability. It affirms that every person's deeds and efforts, whether good or bad, will be made manifest before Allah and will be justly recompensed. No action, however small, goes unnoticed or unrecorded. This motivates the believer to strive for righteousness, knowing that their striving is acknowledged by Allah and will be appropriately rewarded in this life and the Hereafter. It serves as a reminder that ultimately, we are answerable for our own actions and decisions.
orig: وأن سعيه سوف يرى

translation: Then He will give them the fullest recompense
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that on the Day of Judgment, Allah will give people the complete and just recompense for their deeds in this world. It highlights the concept of divine justice, where everyone will be rewarded or punished fairly and fully, with nothing left unaccounted for. The use of the word "al-awfa" (fullest, most complete) stresses that the recompense will be thorough and comprehensive, reflecting every single deed, big or small. This motivates believers to do good and refrain from evil, knowing that ultimately, God's perfect justice will prevail and each person will receive what they truly deserve based on their actions in this life.
orig: ثم يجزاه الجزاء الأوفى

translation: And that to your Lord is the finality.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that all things ultimately return to Allah, and that He is the final destination and the ultimate goal. It reminds us that no matter what we do or achieve in this life, our ultimate purpose and end is with Allah. It encourages us to focus on pleasing Him and seeking His pleasure, rather than getting caught up in worldly pursuits that will eventually come to an end. The verse also highlights Allah's power and control over all things, as everything will eventually come back to Him.
orig: وأن إلى ربك المنتهى

translation: And that it is He who makes [one] laugh and weep
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah is the One who controls human emotions, such as joy and sorrow. It reminds us that both laughter and tears are ultimately in His hands, and that we should attribute these feelings to His will and wisdom. This understanding helps believers maintain a balanced perspective in times of happiness and sadness, acknowledging that all circumstances are part of Allah's divine plan for our lives.
orig: وأنه هو أضحك وأبكى

translation: And that it is He who causes death and gives life
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute power and control of Allah over life and death. It affirms that Allah alone has the ability to take life away and to grant it, highlighting His sovereignty and omnipotence. The verse serves as a reminder to humans that their existence and fate are ultimately in the hands of their Creator, and that they should submit to His will and guidance. It also implies the concept of resurrection and the afterlife, as Allah has the power to bring the dead back to life.
orig: وأنه هو أمات وأحيا

translation: And that He created the two mates - the male and the female
interpretation: This verse points to the divine wisdom in Allah's creation of all living beings in pairs, male and female. This duality is necessary for procreation and the continuance of life. It also highlights the complementary nature of the two genders, each with its unique physical and psychological characteristics that enable them to fulfill their respective roles. The mention of this fundamental reality encourages reflection on the signs of Allah's power and purposeful design in the universe.
orig: وأنه خلق الزوجين الذكر والأنثى

translation: From a sperm-drop when it is emitted.
interpretation: This verse refers to the humble origin of human life, which begins with a mere drop of fluid. It emphasizes the miraculous nature of human development, as this seemingly insignificant fluid contains the potential for a complete human being. The verse also alludes to the fact that the creation of life is an intentional act of God, as the sperm is emitted with a specific purpose and destiny. This serves as a reminder for humans to reflect on their origins and the power of God in creating and sustaining life.
orig: من نطفة إذا تمنى

translation: And upon Him is the next creation.
interpretation: This verse refers to the fact that Allah is responsible for the resurrection and the creation of life after death. It affirms that just as Allah created us in this world, He has the power to recreate us anew in the Hereafter. This is a fundamental belief in Islam, that there will be a Day of Judgment where all souls will be resurrected and held accountable for their deeds in this world. The verse emphasizes Allah's omnipotence and His ability to bring about the next life, reminding believers of the inevitability of the Hereafter and the importance of leading a righteous life in preparation for it.
orig: وأن عليه النشأة الأخرى

translation: And that it is He who enriches and suffices
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that it is Allah alone who provides sustenance, wealth, and contentment to His creation. He is the ultimate source of all provisions, both material and spiritual. It reminds believers to turn to Allah for their needs and to be grateful for His blessings, as He is the One who can truly enrich and satisfy the hearts of those who put their trust in Him. This verse encourages humans to seek fulfillment and contentment through their connection with Allah rather than relying solely on worldly possessions or achievements.
orig: وأنه هو أغنى وأقنى

translation: And that He is the Lord of Sirius.
interpretation: This verse affirms that Allah is the Lord and Creator of the star Sirius, which was worshipped by some pagan Arabs. It emphasizes Allah's power and sovereignty over all of His creation, even the celestial bodies that people may mistakenly venerate or ascribe divinity to. The mention of this specific star serves as an example to assert that Allah alone is worthy of worship, and that no part of His creation, no matter how magnificent it may appear, shares in His divine attributes or deserves to be worshipped alongside Him.
orig: وأنه هو رب الشعرى

translation: And that He destroyed the former 'Aad
interpretation: This verse refers to the destruction of the ancient people of 'Aad, who were a powerful and prosperous nation but became arrogant and rejected the message of their prophet, Hud. As a result, Allah punished them with a severe wind that devastated their land and destroyed them utterly. The verse serves as a reminder of the consequences of disobedience to Allah and the fate that awaits those who persist in disbelief and rebellion against His commands. It also highlights Allah's supreme power over His creation and His ability to bring about the downfall of even the mightiest of nations when they incur His wrath.
orig: وأنه أهلك عادا الأولى

translation: And the Thamud, He spared none
interpretation: This verse refers to the ancient tribe of Thamud, who were punished by Allah for their disobedience and rejection of His message. The phrase "He spared none" indicates the completeness and severity of their destruction, highlighting the consequences of turning away from God's guidance. It serves as a warning to future generations not to follow in the footsteps of the Thamud and to heed the signs and warnings sent by Allah through His prophets.
orig: وثمود فما أبقى

translation: And the people of Noah before them. Indeed, they were more unjust and more tyrannical.
interpretation: This verse refers to the people of Prophet Noah, who lived before the time of the Prophet Muhammad. It states that they were even more unjust and tyrannical than the disbelievers of Mecca who opposed the Prophet Muhammad. The people of Noah rejected the message of monotheism and the warning of punishment that Noah conveyed to them. They persisted in their disbelief, injustice, and transgression, leading to their destruction by the Great Flood. This verse serves as a reminder that those who reject the truth and persist in wrongdoing will face severe consequences, just as the people of Noah did.
orig: وقوم نوح من قبل إنهم كانوا هم أظلم وأطغى

translation: And He destroyed the overturned cities [of Sodom and Gomorrah]
interpretation: This verse refers to the destruction of the ancient cities of Sodom and Gomorrah, which were overturned by Allah as a punishment for their people's grave sins and defiance of His messages. The verse serves as a reminder of the consequences of disobedience to Allah and the fate that awaits those who persist in wrongdoing and reject the guidance of His messengers. It also emphasizes Allah's power and ability to destroy even the mightiest of human civilizations when they stray from the path of righteousness.
orig: والمؤتفكة أهوى

translation: And there covered her what covered [her].
interpretation: This verse is referring to the miraculous conception of Jesus by Mary. The phrase "what covered her" is interpreted by many scholars to mean that God's power and decree overshadowed Mary, causing her to conceive Jesus without a father. It emphasizes the divine and miraculous nature of Jesus' birth, as it was not through the normal means of human reproduction, but through the direct intervention and will of God.
orig: فغشاها ما غشى

translation: Then which of the favors of your Lord do you doubt?
interpretation: This verse is a rhetorical question that challenges the reader to consider the countless blessings and favors bestowed upon them by Allah. It implies that, in light of all the divine gifts and mercies evident in one's life and in the world around them, it would be unreasonable and ungrateful to doubt or deny Allah's benevolence. The verse prompts introspection and encourages the recognition and appreciation of the many ways in which Allah provides for and sustains His creation. It serves as a reminder to have faith, gratitude, and trust in Allah's wisdom and generosity, rather than questioning or doubting His favors.
orig: فبأي آلاء ربك تتمارى

translation: This is a warner, from among the warners of old.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the continuity of the divine message throughout human history. The Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) is not bringing a new message, but rather, he is a warner among many warners who came before him, such as Noah, Abraham, Moses, and Jesus. They all brought the same fundamental message: to worship the One True God and to follow His guidance. This verse also implies that just as the previous nations were held accountable for their response to the warners, so too will the people of Muhammad's time and future generations be held accountable for their response to his message.
orig: هذا نذير من النذر الأولى

translation: The Approaching Day has approached.
interpretation: This verse is referring to the Day of Judgment, which is drawing near. It emphasizes the inevitability and closeness of the final day of reckoning when all souls will be held accountable for their deeds in this world. The repetition of the word "approaching" (azifat/azifah) underscores the urgency and certainty of this event. It serves as a reminder for believers to be mindful of their actions and to prepare for the Hereafter, as the arrival of Judgment Day is assured and could come at any moment.
orig: أزفت الآزفة

translation: There is no remover of it besides Allah.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute power and authority of Allah. It conveys that when Allah decrees something, whether it be a blessing or a trial, no one else has the ability to change, alter, or remove it except Allah Himself. It highlights the complete reliance and submission that believers should have towards Allah, recognizing that He alone has the ultimate control over all affairs. The verse encourages trust in Allah's wisdom and acceptance of His will, knowing that He is the only one who can alleviate difficulties or change circumstances according to His divine plan.
orig: ليس لها من دون الله كاشفة

translation: Then at this statement do you wonder?
interpretation: This verse is questioning the amazement or surprise of the disbelievers at the message of Islam. It implies that there is no reason for them to be astonished by the truth of the Qur'an and the Prophet's teachings, as they are clear signs from Allah. The verse suggests that rather than wondering at the message, they should reflect on its meaning and accept its guidance.
orig: أفمن هذا الحديث تعجبون

translation: And you laugh and do not weep
interpretation: This verse is a reminder that people often engage in frivolous pursuits and laughter, while neglecting the more important matters that should bring them to tears, such as the remembrance of Allah, the fleeting nature of this world, and the reality of the Hereafter. It is a call to reflect on one's priorities and to cultivate a sense of reverence and humility before the Almighty, recognizing the gravity of our actions and their consequences in the eternal life to come.
orig: وتضحكون ولا تبكون

translation: While you were heedless.
interpretation: This verse is addressing the disbelievers, pointing out that they were heedless and inattentive to the signs and warnings from Allah. They were engrossed in worldly pursuits and pleasures, neglecting their spiritual duties and the reality of the Hereafter. The verse implies that this heedlessness is a reason for their disbelief and a cause for their ultimate loss and regret. It serves as a reminder for all people to be mindful and attentive to Allah's message and to live their lives with consciousness of Him and the Day of Judgment.
orig: وأنتم سامدون

translation: So prostrate to Allah and worship [Him].
interpretation: This verse is a command to submit completely to Allah and worship Him alone. Prostration is the ultimate physical act of submission, humility and reverence before Allah. By prostrating and worshipping Allah exclusively, one affirms His Oneness and supremacy, and frees oneself from servitude to anything or anyone else. It is a call to direct all acts of worship, obedience and devotion to Allah alone, as He is the only One worthy of worship. This is the essence of Islam - total submission to the will of Allah and sincere worship dedicated to Him alone, without any partners or intermediaries.
orig: فاسجدوا لله واعبدوا

translation: The Hour has come near, and the moon has split [in two].
interpretation: This verse is referring to one of the signs of the approaching Day of Judgment. The splitting of the moon was a miracle performed by Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) as a sign to the disbelievers who challenged him to show proof of his prophethood. It signifies that the end of time is drawing near and that people should be prepared for the coming of the Day of Reckoning by believing in Allah and following His messenger. The splitting of the moon also demonstrates Allah's power over His creation and the truth of Muhammad's message.
orig: اقتربت الساعة وانشق القمر

translation: And if they see a sign, they turn away and say, "[This is] continuing magic."
interpretation: This verse refers to the disbelievers who, when presented with clear signs and evidence of the truth of Islam, stubbornly reject them and dismiss them as mere magic or sorcery. They turn away from the signs, refusing to reflect upon them or consider their implications. Instead, they attribute the signs to "continuing magic," suggesting that the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) is a persistent magician who constantly deceives people with his sorcery. This interpretation highlights the arrogance and obstinacy of those who reject the truth, even when faced with compelling proofs. It demonstrates their unwillingness to open their hearts and minds to the message of Islam, preferring to remain in a state of denial and disbelief.
orig: وإن يروا آية يعرضوا ويقولوا سحر مستمر

translation: And they denied and followed their inclinations. But for every matter is a [time of] settlement.
interpretation: This verse highlights the human tendency to reject the truth and instead follow their own desires and whims. It suggests that people often choose to deny the signs and messages of Allah, preferring to pursue their own selfish interests and inclinations. However, the verse also emphasizes that every matter, whether good or bad, will ultimately reach its appointed conclusion or "settlement." This implies that all actions and choices will have consequences, and that everyone will be held accountable for their deeds in the end. It serves as a reminder that the temporary pleasures and distractions of this world should not lead one astray from the path of truth and righteousness, as the ultimate outcome of every matter is predetermined by Allah's will and justice.
orig: وكذبوا واتبعوا أهواءهم وكل أمر مستقر

translation: And there has already come to them of information that in which there is deterrence -
interpretation: This verse is a reminder that the disbelievers have been given ample warnings and information through the prophets and revelations that should have deterred them from their disbelief and wrongdoing. The "information" refers to the stories of past nations who were punished for rejecting the truth, as well as the clear signs and proofs of Allah's existence and power. Despite these deterrents, they persist in their disbelief out of arrogance and stubbornness. The verse serves as a warning that they have no excuse for their actions and will face the consequences in the Hereafter if they do not change their ways and heed the warnings that have come to them.
orig: ولقد جاءهم من الأنباء ما فيه مزدجر

translation: Wisdom [which is] penetrating. But warning does not avail [them].
interpretation: This verse suggests that even the most profound wisdom and insightful teachings may not be effective in guiding those who are determined to reject the truth. The Qur'an, with its deep wisdom, serves as a warning to humanity, but for some individuals, no amount of warning or admonition will make a difference in their attitude or behavior. They have chosen to ignore the signs and messages that Allah has sent through His prophets and revelations, and thus, they fail to benefit from the guidance that is readily available to them. It is a reminder that the ultimate responsibility lies with each individual to open their hearts and minds to the truth and to heed the warnings that Allah has provided through His wisdom.
orig: حكمة بالغة فما تغن النذر

translation: So turn away from them on the Day the Caller will call them to something unpleasant.
interpretation: This verse is referring to the Day of Judgment, when the caller (angel) will summon all people to the place of reckoning. It will be a difficult and unpleasant day for the disbelievers, as they will face the consequences of their actions and be called to account for their deeds. The Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) is being instructed to turn away from those who reject the message of Islam, as their fate on that Day will be sealed and there will be no more opportunity for them to repent or believe. It serves as a reminder of the severity and finality of the Day of Judgment, and the importance of believing and doing good deeds in this life before it is too late.
orig: فتول عنهم يوم يدع الداع إلى شيء نكر

translation: Their eyes humbled, they will emerge from the graves as if they were locusts spreading
interpretation: This verse describes the state of people on the Day of Resurrection. They will come out of their graves in a state of humility and fear, with their eyes downcast. The emergence of people from their graves in large numbers is likened to the swarming of locusts, emphasizing the vastness of the scene. This imagery conveys the overwhelming nature of that day and the realization of people about the consequences of their deeds. It serves as a reminder for humans to be mindful of their actions in this life, as they will be held accountable in the Hereafter.
orig: خشعا أبصارهم يخرجون من الأجداث كأنهم جراد منتشر

translation: Racing ahead to the Caller. The disbelievers will say, "This is a difficult Day."
interpretation: This verse refers to the Day of Judgment when all of humanity will be rushing towards the call of Allah. The disbelievers, upon realizing the reality of this day, will remark on its severity and difficulty. They will recognize, with despair, the consequences of their denial and the gravity of their situation. The verse emphasizes the stark contrast between the believers who heeded the call of truth in this world and the disbelievers who turned away from it, ultimately facing the harshness of the Day of Reckoning.
orig: مهطعين إلى الداع يقول الكافرون هذا يوم عسر

translation: The people of Noah denied before them, and they denied Our servant and said, "A madman," and he was repelled harshly.
interpretation: This verse refers to the story of Prophet Noah and his people who rejected his message and accused him of being insane. It highlights the common pattern of disbelievers throughout history who deny God's messengers and treat them with contempt and hostility. The verse emphasizes that Noah's people not only rejected him but also actively sought to suppress his message through intimidation and repulsion. This serves as a reminder to the Prophet Muhammad and the believers that facing opposition and accusations is a trial that many prophets before him had to endure, and they should remain steadfast in their faith despite the challenges they face from the disbelievers.
orig: كذبت قبلهم قوم نوح فكذبوا عبدنا وقالوا مجنون وازدجر

translation: So he called upon his Lord, "Indeed, I am overpowered, so help."
interpretation: This verse is a plea for help from a believer who feels overwhelmed and overpowered by the challenges and difficulties they face. They turn to Allah, their Lord, in sincere supplication, acknowledging their weakness and inability to overcome their struggles alone. The believer humbles themselves before Allah, seeking His aid and support in their time of need. This verse emphasizes the importance of turning to Allah in times of hardship, recognizing that true strength and victory come from Him alone. It also highlights the believer's complete trust and reliance upon Allah, knowing that He is the only One who can truly help and grant them relief from their difficulties.
orig: فدعا ربه أني مغلوب فانتصر

translation: Then We opened the gates of the sky with pouring water.
interpretation: This verse is referring to the story of Prophet Noah (peace be upon him) and the Great Flood. It indicates that Allah caused the sky to rain down torrentially, with water gushing forth in abundance. The opening of the "gates of heaven" is a metaphor for the onset of the heavy, incessant downpour that led to the flooding of the entire earth. This was a divine punishment inflicted upon Noah's people for their persistent disbelief and rejection of his message. The verse emphasizes Allah's supreme power over the forces of nature and His ability to use them to carry out His divine will and judgment.
orig: ففتحنا أبواب السماء بماء منهمر

translation: And We caused the earth to burst with springs, and the waters met for a matter already predestined.
interpretation: This verse speaks to the power and wisdom of Allah in His creation. It suggests that the natural world, with its springs and waters, operates according to a divine plan that has been predetermined by Allah. The meeting of the waters is not a random occurrence, but rather a purposeful event that reflects the intricate design of the universe. This interpretation emphasizes the belief in Allah's sovereignty and the idea that everything in creation is subject to His will and decree. It invites reflection on the beauty and order of the natural world as signs of Allah's existence and wisdom.
orig: وفجرنا الأرض عيونا فالتقى الماء على أمر قد قدر

translation: And We carried him on a [construction of] planks and nails
interpretation: This verse is referring to the story of Prophet Noah (peace be upon him) and the ark he built to save the believers from the great flood. The "planks and nails" mentioned here symbolize the sturdy construction of the ark, which was built according to Allah's instructions. The verse emphasizes the importance of following divine guidance and trusting in Allah's protection during times of hardship and adversity. It also highlights the concept of salvation through faith and righteous deeds, as only those who believed in Noah and followed his teachings were saved from the flood.
orig: وحملناه على ذات ألواح ودسر

translation: It sailed under Our observation as reward for he who had been denied.
interpretation: This verse refers to the Ark of Noah, which was built and sailed under the watchful eyes of Allah as a reward for Noah, who was rejected and opposed by his people for his faith and message. The verse emphasizes Allah's protection and favor upon His chosen servants who remain steadfast in the face of adversity and rejection, and highlights the ultimate triumph of faith over disbelief.
orig: تجري بأعيننا جزاء لمن كان كفر

translation: And We have certainly left it as a sign, so is there any who will remember?
interpretation: This verse is a reminder from Allah that He has left signs and lessons for mankind to reflect upon and learn from. The pronoun "it" in this verse could refer to a past nation or event that was destroyed by Allah as a punishment for their disobedience and wrongdoing. The verse is asking if there is anyone who will take heed of these signs and remember the lessons they contain, so as to avoid a similar fate. It is an invitation for people to use their intellect and reason to recognize the truth and to follow the right path, rather than being heedless and ignoring the signs and warnings that Allah has provided.
orig: ولقد تركناها آية فهل من مدكر

translation: Then how [terrible] was My punishment and warning.
interpretation: This verse is a stern warning from Allah, emphasizing the severity and terrible nature of His punishment for those who disbelieve and disobey Him. It implies that the disbelievers and the wicked should take heed of the warnings and the examples of divine retribution mentioned in the Qur'an and reflect upon the consequences of incurring Allah's wrath. The verse also suggests that Allah's punishment is not to be taken lightly, and that His warnings should be heeded by all, as the consequences of ignoring them are severe and inescapable.
orig: فكيف كان عذابي ونذر

translation: And We have certainly made the Qur'an easy for remembrance, so is there any who will remember?
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah has made the Qur'an easy to understand, memorize, and reflect upon. It serves as an invitation and encouragement for people to engage with the Qur'an, to remember its teachings, and to take heed of its guidance. The rhetorical question "so is there any who will remember?" is a powerful reminder that it is the responsibility of each individual to make the effort to study, contemplate, and internalize the messages of the Qur'an. The verse implies that there are no excuses for neglecting the Qur'an since Allah has made it accessible and comprehensible for all. It is a call to action, urging believers to actively engage with the divine revelation and allow it to transform their lives.
orig: ولقد يسرنا القرآن للذكر فهل من مدكر

translation: The 'Aad denied; and how [severe] were My punishment and warning.
interpretation: This verse is a warning to those who deny the message of God and His prophets. It refers to the ancient people of 'Aad who were destroyed by a severe punishment from God because of their persistent disbelief and defiance. The rhetorical question "how [severe] were My punishment and warning" emphasizes the gravity of the consequences that await those who reject divine guidance. It serves as a reminder that denying the truth does not change its reality, and that the ultimate result of such denial is a severe punishment from God. The verse urges people to learn from the example of past nations and to heed the warnings of God's messengers before it is too late.
orig: كذبت عاد فكيف كان عذابي ونذر

translation: Indeed, We sent upon them a screaming wind on a day of continuous misfortune.
interpretation: This verse is a warning and a reminder of Allah's power and ability to punish those who disobey Him. The "screaming wind" mentioned in the verse is likely a reference to a severe and destructive wind that Allah sent as a punishment to a particular group of people who had rejected His messages and warnings. The fact that this wind came on a day of "continuous misfortune" emphasizes the severity and duration of the punishment, suggesting that the people had no respite from the calamity. This verse serves as a cautionary tale for all of mankind, reminding us of the consequences of turning away from Allah's guidance and the importance of heeding His warnings and following His path.
orig: إنا أرسلنا عليهم ريحا صرصرا في يوم نحس مستمر

translation: Plucking out men as if they were uprooted palm-tree trunks.
interpretation: This verse is describing the Day of Judgment, when the angels will pluck out the souls of the disbelievers from their bodies with great force, just as an uprooted palm tree is violently pulled out from the earth. It emphasizes the severity and harshness of the punishment that awaits those who reject faith in God. The imagery of an uprooted palm tree highlights the complete destruction and displacement of the disbelievers' souls from their bodies, signifying a painful and irreversible extraction as they face the consequences of their actions in the Hereafter.
orig: تنزع الناس كأنهم أعجاز نخل منقعر

translation: Then how [terrible] was My punishment and warning.
interpretation: This verse serves as a stern warning and reminder of the severity of Allah's punishment for those who reject His messages and warnings. It implies that the consequences of disbelieving and disobeying Allah are extremely dire, and that one should take heed of the examples of past nations who were destroyed for their defiance. The verse also highlights the importance and urgency of heeding the warnings sent by Allah through His messengers, as ignoring them will lead to a terrible fate in this world and the Hereafter.
orig: فكيف كان عذابي ونذر

translation: And We have certainly made the Qur'an easy for remembrance, so is there any who will remember?
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah has made the Qur'an easy to understand, memorize, and reflect upon. It serves as an invitation and encouragement for people to engage with the Qur'an, to study its meanings, and to take heed of its lessons and guidance. The question "so is there any who will remember?" is a rhetorical one, urging people to actively engage with the Qur'an and benefit from its wisdom, as Allah has made it accessible and comprehensible for all. It also implies that despite the Qur'an's clarity and accessibility, it is up to individuals to choose whether they will take advantage of this opportunity to learn and grow spiritually.
orig: ولقد يسرنا القرآن للذكر فهل من مدكر

translation: Thamud denied the warning.
interpretation: This verse refers to the people of Thamud, an ancient Arabian tribe, who rejected the warnings and messages sent to them by Allah through His prophet, Salih. They were arrogant and refused to believe in the oneness of Allah and the prophethood of Salih. The denial of the divine warning by the people of Thamud is a reminder for all people to heed the signs and messages sent by Allah and to follow the righteous path, or else face the consequences of their disbelief and disobedience, just as the Thamud faced destruction for their denial.
orig: كذبت ثمود بالنذر

translation: And they said, "Is it one human being among us that we should follow? Indeed, we would then be in error and madness."
interpretation: This verse reveals the arrogance and disbelief of those who reject the message of Allah's prophets and messengers. They consider it beneath them to follow the guidance of a single human being from among themselves, viewing such a prospect as a form of misguidance and insanity. Their pride and sense of superiority prevent them from accepting the truth, as they cannot fathom the idea that a mere mortal could be chosen by Allah to convey His message. This attitude stems from their lack of understanding of Allah's wisdom in selecting prophets and their inability to recognize the signs of divine revelation in the teachings of these chosen individuals.
orig: فقالوا أبشرا منا واحدا نتبعه إنا إذا لفي ضلال وسعر

translation: Has the message been sent down upon him from among us? Rather, he is an insolent liar.
interpretation: This verse questions the legitimacy of the Prophet Muhammad's claim to prophethood. The disbelievers are expressing their doubt and disbelief, suggesting that Muhammad is not worthy of receiving divine revelation. They accuse him of being an insolent liar who has fabricated the message himself. This interpretation highlights the resistance and opposition faced by the Prophet in delivering the message of Islam, as well as the arrogance and stubbornness of those who rejected his prophethood without fair consideration of the evidence and signs that supported his claim.
orig: أألقي الذكر عليه من بيننا بل هو كذاب أشر

translation: They will know tomorrow who is the most wicked liar.
interpretation: This verse serves as a stern warning and reminder that the truth will eventually come to light, and those who have been deceitful and wicked will be exposed. It emphasizes the idea that one cannot escape the consequences of their actions and that justice will ultimately prevail. The verse also implies that God is all-knowing and will hold people accountable for their deeds, particularly those who have been dishonest and have caused harm to others. It encourages individuals to be truthful and righteous, as the consequences of their actions will be revealed in due time.
orig: سيعلمون غدا من الكذاب الأشر

translation: Indeed, We are sending the she-camel as a trial for them, so watch them and be patient.
interpretation: This verse is a warning to the people of Thamud, who demanded a miracle from their prophet Salih as proof of his prophethood. Allah sent them a miraculous she-camel as a test of their faith, commanding them to allow her to graze freely and not harm her. The verse instructs Prophet Salih to observe their reaction and remain patient in the face of their defiance. It highlights the importance of patience and trust in Allah's plan when faced with the disbelief and opposition of others, as well as the consequences of rejecting divine signs and miracles sent as a mercy and guidance from Allah.
orig: إنا مرسلو الناقة فتنة لهم فارتقبهم واصطبر

translation: And inform them that the water is shared between them, each drink attended [by turn].
interpretation: This verse is emphasizing the importance of equitable distribution of resources, in this case water. It suggests that water should be shared fairly among people, with each person getting their turn to drink. This could be interpreted as a broader message about social justice and ensuring that everyone has access to the necessities of life. It also implies the need for proper management and conservation of vital resources like water, so that they can be sustainably shared by the community. The verse promotes the values of fairness, equality, and responsible stewardship over God's gifts to mankind.
orig: ونبئهم أن الماء قسمة بينهم كل شرب محتضر

translation: Then they called their companion, so he took [a sword] and slaughtered [her].
interpretation: This verse is referring to the story of the people of Thamud, who were asked by their prophet Salih to leave alone the she-camel sent by Allah as a sign. However, they disobeyed and one of their companions took a sword and hamstrung the camel, leading to their destruction. The interpretation is that disobedience to Allah's commands and harming what He has decreed as sacred will lead to severe punishment and doom. It highlights the importance of respecting divine signs and submitting to God's will.
orig: فنادوا صاحبهم فتعاطى فعقر

translation: Then how [terrible] was My punishment and warning.
interpretation: This verse serves as a stern warning and reminder of the severity of Allah's punishment for those who reject His messages and warnings. It implies that the disbelievers and wrongdoers who ignored the signs and admonitions will face a terrifying fate in the form of Allah's retribution. The verse also underscores the importance of heeding the warnings sent by Allah through His prophets and messengers, as failing to do so will result in grave consequences in this world and the Hereafter. It is an invitation for people to reflect upon the past nations who were destroyed due to their disobedience and learn from their mistakes before it is too late.
orig: فكيف كان عذابي ونذر

translation: Indeed, We sent upon them one shout, and they became like the dry twig fragments of an [animal] pen.
interpretation: This verse is a warning to those who reject the message of Allah and His prophets. The "one shout" refers to a sudden, overwhelming punishment that Allah sends upon the disbelievers, which utterly destroys them, leaving them like broken and crumbled twigs in an animal pen. It emphasizes the power and decisiveness of Allah's judgment against those who persist in disbelief and rebellion against His commands. The verse also serves as a reminder to the believers of the consequences of rejecting faith, urging them to remain steadfast in their belief and obedience to Allah.
orig: إنا أرسلنا عليهم صيحة واحدة فكانوا كهشيم المحتظر

translation: And We have certainly made the Qur'an easy for remembrance, so is there any who will remember?
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah has made the Qur'an easy to understand, memorize, and reflect upon for those who seek guidance and remembrance. It serves as an invitation and encouragement for people to engage with the Qur'an, ponder its meanings, and take lessons from its teachings. The rhetorical question "so is there any who will remember?" is a powerful reminder that the opportunity to benefit from the Qur'an is available to all, but it is up to each individual to make the choice to embrace its message and apply its wisdom in their lives.
orig: ولقد يسرنا القرآن للذكر فهل من مدكر

translation: The people of Lot denied the warnings.
interpretation: This verse refers to the people of Prophet Lot, who lived in the cities of Sodom and Gomorrah. They were known for their immorality, homosexuality, and rejection of Lot's message. Despite Lot's repeated warnings about the consequences of their actions, they refused to believe him and change their ways. This denial of the divine warnings ultimately led to their destruction, as God sent down a severe punishment upon them. The verse emphasizes the importance of heeding the warnings of God's messengers and the consequences of rejecting divine guidance.
orig: كذبت قوم لوط بالنذر

translation: Indeed, We sent upon them a storm of stones, except the family of Lot - We saved them before dawn
interpretation: This verse refers to the punishment that Allah inflicted upon the people of Lot for their immoral and sinful behavior. Allah sent a storm of stones to destroy them, but saved Lot and his family before dawn as a mercy to them for their righteousness. This verse serves as a reminder of Allah's power and His ability to punish those who disobey Him, while also showing His mercy to those who follow His guidance. It emphasizes the importance of leading a moral and virtuous life, and the consequences of straying from the right path.
orig: إنا أرسلنا عليهم حاصبا إلا آل لوط نجيناهم بسحر

translation: As a favor from Us. Thus do We reward those who are grateful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of gratitude in Islam. It suggests that Allah bestows His blessings and favors upon those who are thankful for what they have been given. Gratitude is seen as a key virtue that leads to further blessings and rewards from Allah. The verse implies that by expressing sincere appreciation for the bounties and mercies received, one can attain more of Allah's grace and kindness. It serves as a reminder to acknowledge and appreciate the divine favors in one's life, as this is a means of attracting more goodness and blessings from the Almighty.
orig: نعمة من عندنا كذلك نجزي من شكر

translation: And We had already warned them of Our assault, but they disputed the warning.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the stubborn nature of the disbelievers who, despite being warned of God's impending punishment, chose to ignore and even argue against these warnings. It highlights their arrogance and refusal to heed the signs and messages sent by God through His prophets. The verse implies that the disbelievers have no excuse for their behavior, as they were given ample warning and opportunity to repent and follow the right path. Their dismissal of the warnings is seen as a direct challenge to God's authority and a justification for the severe punishment that awaits them.
orig: ولقد أنذرهم بطشتنا فتماروا بالنذر

translation: And they had demanded from him his guests, but We obliterated their eyes, [saying], "Taste My punishment and warning."
interpretation: This verse refers to the story of Prophet Lot and his people. The people of Sodom demanded that Lot hand over his guests, who were actually angels in disguise, so that they could commit their abominable acts with them. As a punishment for their sinful intentions and defiance of Lot's warnings, Allah blinded them, rendering them unable to see. The verse emphasizes that they should taste the punishment and heed the warning of Allah for their wicked behavior. It serves as a reminder that those who engage in immoral acts and defy the messages of the prophets will face severe consequences in this world and the Hereafter.
orig: ولقد راودوه عن ضيفه فطمسنا أعينهم فذوقوا عذابي ونذر

translation: And indeed, there came upon them by morning an abiding punishment.
interpretation: This verse refers to a punishment that befell a certain group of people who had persistently rejected the truth and the warnings of their prophet. The punishment is described as "abiding" or "settled in place", indicating its severity and permanence. It came upon them suddenly in the morning, when they were unprepared. This verse serves as a reminder of the consequences of rejecting divine guidance and the reality of divine retribution in this world, as well as the Hereafter for those who persist in wrongdoing without repentance.
orig: ولقد صبحهم بكرة عذاب مستقر

translation: So taste My punishment and My warnings.
interpretation: This verse is a stern warning from Allah to those who reject His messages and disobey His commands. It emphasizes that the disbelievers will face the severe consequences of their actions in the form of Allah's punishment and the fulfillment of His warnings. The verse implies that the time for repentance has passed, and now the disbelievers must face the reality of the consequences they were warned about. It serves as a reminder to all people to heed Allah's warnings and submit to His will before it is too late.
orig: فذوقوا عذابي ونذر

translation: And We have certainly made the Qur'an easy for remembrance, so is there any who will remember?
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah has made the Qur'an easy to understand, memorize, and reflect upon. It serves as an invitation and encouragement for people to engage with the Qur'an, to study its meanings, and to take heed of its lessons and guidance. The rhetorical question "so is there any who will remember?" is a call to action, urging individuals to actively seek the wisdom and reminders contained within the Qur'an, and to apply them in their lives. It suggests that the Qur'an's accessibility is a divine gift, and it is up to each person to make the most of this opportunity for spiritual growth and enlightenment.
orig: ولقد يسرنا القرآن للذكر فهل من مدكر

translation: And there came to the people of Pharaoh warners.
interpretation: This verse refers to the prophets and messengers, such as Moses, who were sent by Allah to warn the people of Pharaoh about the consequences of their disbelief and tyranny. Despite the clear signs and warnings brought by these messengers, the people of Pharaoh arrogantly rejected the truth and persisted in their wrongdoing. This verse serves as a reminder that those who reject the guidance of Allah and oppress others will ultimately face the consequences of their actions, both in this world and in the Hereafter.
orig: ولقد جاء آل فرعون النذر

translation: They denied Our signs, all of them, so We seized them with the seizure of one Exalted in Might and Perfect in Ability.
interpretation: This verse is a warning to those who reject the signs and messages of Allah. It emphasizes that denying even one of Allah's signs is equivalent to denying all of them, as they come from the same source. The consequence of such denial is that Allah will seize the disbelievers with His might and power, and no one can escape His punishment. This interpretation highlights the importance of believing in all of Allah's signs and revelations, as well as the severity of the punishment for those who reject them.
orig: كذبوا بآياتنا كلها فأخذناهم أخذ عزيز مقتدر

translation: Are your disbelievers better than those [former ones], or have you [been granted] immunity in the divine scriptures?
interpretation: This verse is questioning the disbelievers, asking if they think they are somehow better or superior to the disbelievers of past nations who were destroyed for their disbelief. It also asks if they have been granted some special exemption or immunity from punishment in the divine scriptures, implying that they have not. The underlying message is that these disbelievers are no different than those of the past, and they too will face consequences for their rejection of faith unless they change their ways and believe.
orig: أكفاركم خير من أولئكم أم لكم براءة في الزبر

translation: Or do they say, "We are an assembly supporting [each other]?"
interpretation: This verse is questioning the belief of the disbelievers that their large numbers and unity can protect them against Allah's punishment. It suggests that they are deluded in thinking that their mutual support and strength in numbers can save them from the consequences of their rejection of faith. The Qur'an emphasizes that no matter how powerful or numerous the disbelievers may seem, they are ultimately powerless before Allah's will and decree. Their assembly and alliance will be of no avail on the Day of Judgment when each soul will stand alone before its Creator. The verse serves as a warning against the arrogance and false sense of security that comes with relying on worldly power and support, while neglecting one's relationship with Allah.
orig: أم يقولون نحن جميع منتصر

translation: Their assembly will be defeated, and they will turn their backs [in retreat].
interpretation: This verse is referring to the enemies of Islam and the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him). It is foretelling that despite their apparent strength and numbers, they will ultimately face defeat at the hands of the Muslims. The phrase "turn their backs" is an idiomatic expression indicating that they will flee from the battlefield in retreat. This verse served as a reassurance to the early Muslim community that no matter how powerful and intimidating their foes seemed, Allah would grant them victory as long as they remained steadfast in their faith. It conveys a message of hope and divine support for those who strive in the path of Allah against oppression and disbelief.
orig: سيهزم الجمع ويولون الدبر

translation: But the Hour is their appointment [for due punishment], and the Hour is more disastrous and more bitter.
interpretation: This verse is a warning to those who reject the message of Islam and the reality of the Day of Judgment. It emphasizes that the appointed time for their ultimate reckoning is the Hour, referring to the Day of Resurrection. The verse stresses that this Hour will be far more catastrophic and bitter than any hardship or punishment they may face in this worldly life. It serves as a reminder that the disbelievers' denial and mockery of the Day of Judgment will only lead them to a severe and painful consequence in the Hereafter, and that they should heed the warning and embrace faith before it is too late.
orig: بل الساعة موعدهم والساعة أدهى وأمر

translation: Indeed, the criminals are in error and madness.
interpretation: This verse suggests that those who commit sins and reject the truth are lost in a state of delusion and insanity. Their actions and beliefs are not based on reason or guidance, but rather on their own misguided desires and passions. They are so deeply entrenched in their wrongdoing that they cannot see the error of their ways, and thus they continue to stray further from the path of righteousness. This verse serves as a warning to those who persist in their sinful behavior, reminding them of the grave consequences that await them if they do not repent and turn back to Allah.
orig: إن المجرمين في ضلال وسعر

translation: The Day they will be dragged in the Fire on their faces [it will be said], "Taste the touch of Saqar."
interpretation: This verse is a stark warning about the punishment that awaits those who reject faith and do evil deeds. On the Day of Judgment, they will be humiliated by being dragged face-first into the blazing Fire of Hell. The verse emphasizes the physical and psychological torment they will endure as they are forced to "taste" the scorching touch of Saqar, one of the names of Hell. This degrading punishment serves as a manifestation of divine justice against those who knowingly and persistently transgressed in the worldly life. The graphic imagery aims to instill fear in the believers, motivating them to stay on the righteous path and avoid the terrible fate of the disbelievers.
orig: يوم يسحبون في النار على وجوههم ذوقوا مس سقر

translation: Indeed, all things We created with predestination.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the concept of divine destiny in Islam. It asserts that everything in the universe, from the smallest atom to the largest celestial body, has been created by Allah according to His predetermined plan. This predestination encompasses all aspects of life, including the actions and fate of human beings. The verse implies that nothing happens by chance or accident; rather, it is all part of God's grand design. This belief in divine predestination is a fundamental tenet of Islamic faith, and it encourages Muslims to trust in Allah's wisdom and submit to His will, knowing that He has a greater purpose behind every event and circumstance in their lives.
orig: إنا كل شيء خلقناه بقدر

translation: And Our command is but one, like a glance of the eye.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the omnipotence and swiftness of Allah's command. When Allah decrees something, it happens instantaneously, without any delay or hesitation. It is as quick as the blink of an eye, highlighting the absolute power and authority of Allah over all creation. This also serves as a reminder to humans that when Allah decides to bring about the Day of Judgment or any other event, it will happen in a mere instant, and we should always be prepared for it.
orig: وما أمرنا إلا واحدة كلمح بالبصر

translation: And We have already destroyed your kinds, so is there any who will remember?
interpretation: This verse is a reminder from Allah that He has destroyed previous nations who rejected His messages and warnings, just as He can destroy those who reject the message of Islam. It is a call to reflect upon the fate of those who came before and to take heed of their example. The verse emphasizes the importance of remembering the lessons of history and the consequences of denying the truth. It serves as a warning to those who persist in disbelief and a reminder to believers to remain steadfast in their faith.
orig: ولقد أهلكنا أشياعكم فهل من مدكر

translation: And all that they did is in the written records.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the concept of divine record-keeping in Islam. It suggests that all deeds, whether good or bad, are meticulously recorded by Allah or His angels. These written records will serve as the basis for judgment on the Day of Reckoning. The verse implies that humans should be mindful of their actions, as nothing escapes Allah's knowledge and everything will be accounted for. It serves as a reminder for believers to strive for righteousness and refrain from wrongdoing, as the consequences of their actions will be preserved in the divine records.
orig: وكل شيء فعلوه في الزبر

translation: And every small and great thing is inscribed.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the comprehensive nature of God's knowledge and record-keeping. It suggests that all deeds, whether they seem insignificant or monumental to us, are meticulously noted and will be accounted for. This serves as a reminder for individuals to be mindful of their actions, as nothing escapes God's awareness. It also highlights the importance of striving to do good and avoiding wrongdoing, as every choice we make carries weight and will be considered on the Day of Judgment.
orig: وكل صغير وكبير مستطر

translation: Indeed, the righteous will be in gardens and rivers
interpretation: This verse speaks about the ultimate reward for those who are righteous and lead a life of piety and obedience to Allah. "Gardens" refer to the gardens of Paradise, a place of eternal bliss, beauty, and comfort. The mention of "rivers" flowing in these gardens adds to the imagery of the perfect, idyllic environment that awaits the believers in the afterlife. This promise of Paradise serves as a motivation for the righteous to continue on the path of righteousness and a source of hope for the struggles and trials they may face in this worldly life.
orig: إن المتقين في جنات ونهر

translation: In the seat of honor with a Sovereign, Perfect in Ability.
interpretation: This verse refers to the highest status and honor that will be granted to the righteous believers in Paradise. They will be seated in a place of truth and sincerity, in close proximity to Allah, the Almighty, who is the Sovereign and the Most Powerful. This nearness to Allah signifies the ultimate reward and blessing for those who lived a life of faith and righteousness. It is a metaphor for the spiritual closeness, blessings, and favors that the believers will enjoy in the presence of their Lord in the eternal abode of Paradise.
orig: في مقعد صدق عند مليك مقتدر

translation: The Most Gracious
interpretation: This verse, consisting of just one word, is the first verse of Surah Ar-Rahman (Chapter 55). It refers to one of the names and attributes of Allah, "Ar-Rahman", which means "The Most Gracious" or "The Most Merciful". This name emphasizes Allah's immense mercy, compassion, and grace that He bestows upon all of His creation. It sets the tone for the rest of the surah, which goes on to describe the countless blessings and favors that Allah has provided for humanity and the rest of creation, highlighting His infinite mercy and love.
orig: الرحمن

translation: The knowledge of the Qur'an
interpretation: This phrase refers to the deep understanding and comprehension of the meanings, teachings, and wisdom contained within the Qur'an. It encompasses the study of the language, context, and implications of the verses, as well as the ability to apply the Qur'anic principles to one's life and derive guidance from its message. Seeking knowledge of the Qur'an is considered a noble pursuit for Muslims, as it allows them to strengthen their faith, gain closeness to Allah, and live according to the divine guidance revealed in this sacred text.
