orig: علم القرآن

translation: He created man
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the power and wisdom of Allah in creating human beings. It reminds us that our existence is not by chance or accident, but rather a deliberate act of creation by the Almighty. The verse also implies the special status and honor given to human beings as the crown of Allah's creation, endowed with intellect, free will, and the capacity to know and worship Him. As such, it is incumbent upon us to be grateful for the gift of life and to use our abilities in a manner pleasing to our Creator.
orig: خلق الإنسان

translation: He taught him the clear expression.
interpretation: This verse refers to Allah's gift of speech and eloquence to human beings. "Al-Bayan" encompasses the ability to express oneself clearly, to articulate thoughts and ideas effectively, and to communicate meaningfully with others. It is through divine teaching that humans have been endowed with the faculties of language, reasoning, and rhetoric. This verse emphasizes the immense value and power of clear expression as a blessing from Allah that distinguishes human beings and enables them to convey their inner thoughts, engage in intellectual discourse, and spread knowledge.
orig: علمه البيان

translation: The sun and the moon [move] by precise calculation,
interpretation: This verse points to the precise and orderly movement of the sun and the moon, which follow a predetermined course set by Allah. It highlights the perfection and accuracy in Allah's creation and the laws governing the universe. The regularity and predictability of their motions serve as signs of Allah's power, wisdom, and meticulous planning. This verse encourages contemplation on these celestial bodies and recognizing them as evidence of Allah's existence and supremacy over all creation.
orig: الشمس والقمر بحسبان

translation: And the stars and the trees prostrate.
interpretation: This verse is a reminder of the ultimate submission and obedience of all creation to Allah. Even the stars in the sky and the trees on earth, despite their majesty and might, humble themselves and bow down in prostration to their Creator. It is a call for humans to reflect on the humility of these grand objects and to submit to God's will with sincerity and devotion. The verse emphasizes that everything in existence recognizes the sovereignty of Allah and worships Him in their own way, and that humans should strive to do the same through their prayers and righteous deeds.
orig: والنجم والشجر يسجدان

translation: And the heaven He raised and imposed the balance
interpretation: This verse is referring to the fact that Allah has created the universe with perfect balance and order. The "heaven" here refers to the sky or the universe as a whole, which Allah has raised up high above us. The "balance" refers to the equilibrium and harmony that exists in all of Allah's creation. This balance is evident in the precise movements of the planets and stars, the cycle of life and death, and the intricate ecosystems that exist on Earth. The verse reminds us of Allah's power and wisdom in creating and maintaining this balance, and encourages us to strive for balance and moderation in our own lives, in accordance with Allah's will.
orig: والسماء رفعها ووضع الميزان

translation: So do not transgress within the balance.
interpretation: This verse is a reminder from Allah to maintain justice and fairness in all our dealings. It emphasizes the importance of upholding equity and balance, and not allowing ourselves to be swayed by our desires or biases. The "balance" can be interpreted as the universal principles of justice and morality that Allah has ordained for humanity. Transgressing these boundaries leads to corruption, oppression, and societal discord. As believers, we are called to be steadfast in adhering to these divine standards, even in the face of temptation or pressure to do otherwise. By heeding this commandment, we contribute to the establishment of a just and harmonious world in accordance with Allah's will.
orig: ألا تطغوا في الميزان

translation: And establish weight with justice and do not make deficient the balance.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of fairness and honesty in all dealings, particularly in matters of trade and commerce. It commands believers to maintain accurate weights and measures, and not to cheat others by giving them less than what they are due. The establishment of justice in weights and measures is a fundamental principle of Islamic economic ethics. This verse also has a broader spiritual meaning, urging individuals to maintain balance and equity in all aspects of their lives, and to avoid transgressing the limits set by Allah. It serves as a reminder that ultimately, everyone will be held accountable for their deeds on the Day of Judgment, and that the scales of justice will be established with perfect accuracy and fairness by the Almighty.
orig: وأقيموا الوزن بالقسط ولا تخسروا الميزان

translation: And the earth, He laid [out] for the creatures.
interpretation: In this verse, Allah is emphasizing that He has created the earth and made it suitable for all living creatures, including humans, animals, and plants. The earth has been designed and prepared by Allah with all the necessary resources and conditions to support and sustain life. This highlights Allah's mercy, wisdom, and power in creating a perfect balance and harmony in the universe for the benefit of His creation. It also reminds humans of their responsibility to be grateful for these blessings and to use them wisely and sustainably, without causing corruption or destruction on earth.
orig: والأرض وضعها للأنام

translation: In it are fruit and palm trees having sheaths [of dates].
interpretation: This verse is describing the bounties and blessings that Allah has provided in Paradise (Jannah). The mention of fruit and date-bearing palm trees with their sheaths or coverings emphasizes the perfection, abundance, and eternal nature of provisions in Paradise. It signifies that the believers will have access to delightful sustenance without any effort or hardship. The sheathed palm trees also symbolize the modesty and purity that will be maintained even in Paradise. This verse aims to motivate believers to strive for righteousness in this life by giving them a glimpse of the eternal rewards awaiting them in the Hereafter.
orig: فيها فاكهة والنخل ذات الأكمام

translation: And grain having husks and scented plants.
interpretation: This verse is highlighting the beauty and diversity of Allah's creation. The mention of grain with husks, such as wheat and barley, and fragrant plants like herbs and flowers, draws attention to the incredible variety in the plant kingdom. It encourages reflection on how Allah has designed plants to serve different purposes, providing both sustenance and aesthetic pleasure to humans. The verse invites us to appreciate the intricate details and wonders in nature as signs of Allah's creative power and benevolence.
orig: والحب ذو العصف والريحان

translation: Then which of the favors of your Lord will you deny?
interpretation: This verse is a rhetorical question that appears multiple times in Surah Ar-Rahman (Chapter 55) of the Qur'an. It serves as a reminder for humans and jinn to acknowledge and appreciate the countless blessings and favors bestowed upon them by Allah. The repetition of this verse throughout the chapter emphasizes the importance of gratitude and the need to recognize the magnitude of Allah's generosity. It encourages introspection and reflection on the various bounties provided by the Creator, such as the creation of the universe, the sustenance of life, and the guidance through divine revelation. By posing this question repeatedly, the Qur'an challenges the reader to consider the immense favors of Allah and to be grateful for them, rather than denying or taking them for granted.
orig: فبأي آلاء ربكما تكذبان

translation: He created man from clay like [that of] pottery.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the humble origin of mankind, as God created human beings from a lowly substance like clay, which is molded and shaped like pottery. It serves as a reminder for humans to remain humble and recognize their place as creations of God, rather than becoming arrogant or considering themselves superior to others. The comparison to pottery also highlights the delicate and fragile nature of human life, as we are ultimately dependent on God's will and subject to His power, just as pottery is shaped by the potter's hands.
orig: خلق الإنسان من صلصال كالفخار

translation: And He created the jinn from a smokeless flame of fire.
interpretation: This verse refers to the creation of the jinn, another form of intelligent life created by Allah. They are described as being created from a "smokeless flame of fire", indicating their incorporeal nature, as opposed to humans who are created from clay. This highlights the diversity in Allah's creation and the existence of beings beyond the physical realm that we can perceive. It also serves as a reminder that there are unseen forces at play in the universe, and that humans are not the only conscious entities accountable to Allah.
orig: وخلق الجان من مارج من نار

translation: Then which of the favors of your Lord will you deny?
interpretation: This verse is a rhetorical question that is repeated many times throughout Surah Ar-Rahman. It serves as a reminder to humanity and the jinn of the countless blessings and favors that Allah has bestowed upon them, both in this world and in the Hereafter. The repetition of this verse emphasizes the importance of acknowledging and appreciating Allah's blessings, and it encourages the listeners to reflect on the various ways in which they have benefited from His generosity. The verse also implies that denying or failing to recognize Allah's favors is an act of ingratitude and that one should always be thankful for the blessings they have received from their Lord.
orig: فبأي آلاء ربكما تكذبان

translation: Lord of the two Easts and Lord of the two Wests.
interpretation: This verse refers to Allah's power and dominion over the entire universe. The "two Easts" and "two Wests" could symbolize the rising and setting points of the sun at the summer and winter solstices, encompassing the whole world. It signifies that Allah is the Lord of all directions and all regions of the earth, and everything is under His control and sovereignty. This verse emphasizes Allah's omnipotence and His role as the Master and Sustainer of all creation.
orig: رب المشرقين ورب المغربين

translation: Then which of the favors of your Lord will you deny?
interpretation: This verse is a rhetorical question that is repeated throughout Surah Ar-Rahman (Chapter 55) in the Qur'an. It serves as a reminder to humanity and the jinn of the countless blessings and favors that Allah has bestowed upon them. The repetition of this question emphasizes the importance of acknowledging and appreciating the divine favors, such as the creation of the heavens and earth, the alternation of day and night, the provision of sustenance, and the guidance through revelation. It encourages introspection and gratitude towards the Creator, urging the reader to recognize and be thankful for the innumerable bounties they enjoy in this life, which are all due to Allah's mercy and generosity. The verse also implies that denying or failing to appreciate these favors is an act of ingratitude and heedlessness towards the Almighty.
orig: فبأي آلاء ربكما تكذبان

translation: He released the two seas, meeting [side by side];
interpretation: This verse refers to the power and wisdom of Allah in creating the natural world. The "two seas" mentioned here are interpreted by many scholars to refer to the salt water of the oceans and the fresh water of rivers. Allah allows these two types of water bodies to exist side by side, meeting at estuaries and coastal zones, yet miraculously they do not mix and overwhelm one another. This is seen as a sign of Allah's design and control over creation. The verse invites reflection on the delicate natural balance and order that Allah has established on earth.
orig: مرج البحرين يلتقيان

translation: Between them is a barrier which they do not transgress.
interpretation: This verse is referring to the two bodies of water, salt and fresh, that God has placed side by side. Despite their proximity, they do not mix or transgress into each other due to the barrier that God has placed between them. This barrier is both a physical and a metaphorical one, representing God's power in maintaining the balance and separation in His creation. It also symbolizes the boundaries and limits that God has set in various aspects of life which should not be overstepped by humans. The verse reminds us to respect and marvel at the divine order in nature and apply the same principle of respecting boundaries in our own lives.
orig: بينهما برزخ لا يبغيان

translation: Then which of the favors of your Lord will you deny?
interpretation: This verse is a rhetorical question that appears multiple times in Surah Ar-Rahman. It serves as a reminder to humans and jinn about the countless blessings and favors bestowed upon them by Allah. The repetition of this question emphasizes the importance of acknowledging and appreciating these favors, and it encourages gratitude towards the Almighty. It also implies that denying or failing to recognize these blessings is an act of ingratitude and ungratefulness towards the Creator, who has provided us with everything we need to sustain our lives and achieve success in this world and the hereafter.
orig: فبأي آلاء ربكما تكذبان

translation: From both of them emerge pearl and coral.
interpretation: This verse refers to the two bodies of water, fresh and salt, that Allah has created and allowed to meet. Yet, they do not mix due to a barrier between them. From these two bodies of water, Allah brings forth precious jewels like pearls and coral. This is a sign of Allah's creative power and a blessing that He has bestowed upon mankind. The verse reminds us to reflect on the wonders of Allah's creation and to be grateful for the bounties He has provided us from the depths of the sea.
orig: يخرج منهما اللؤلؤ والمرجان

translation: Then which of the favors of your Lord will you deny?
interpretation: This verse is a rhetorical question that is repeated many times throughout Surah Ar-Rahman. It serves as a reminder to humanity and the jinn of the countless blessings and favors that Allah has bestowed upon them. The repetition of this question emphasizes the importance of acknowledging and being grateful for these blessings, as it is human nature to often take them for granted or forget about them. The verse encourages introspection and reflection upon the various bounties that Allah has provided, both in this world and in the promise of Paradise in the Hereafter, prompting the listener to recognize and appreciate the immense generosity and mercy of their Lord.
orig: فبأي آلاء ربكما تكذبان

translation: And to Him belong the ships [with sails] elevated in the sea like mountains.
interpretation: This verse is drawing our attention to the greatness and power of Allah by reminding us of the ships that sail the seas. These ships, described as being as tall as mountains with their sails elevated high, are a marvel of Allah's creation. They are a means that Allah has subjugated for human benefit, allowing transport and trade across the vast oceans. The imagery of the ships like mountains emphasizes their immense size and strength, which is only possible by the will and power of Allah who has made the natural laws that govern buoyancy, wind currents, etc. Reflecting on these ships should increase us in faith and gratitude to Allah.
orig: وله الجوار المنشآت في البحر كالأعلام

translation: Then which of the favors of your Lord will you deny?
interpretation: This verse is a rhetorical question that is repeated many times throughout Surah Ar-Rahman. It serves as a reminder to humanity and the jinn of the countless blessings and favors that Allah has bestowed upon them, both in this world and in the Hereafter. The repetition of this verse emphasizes the importance of acknowledging and appreciating Allah's blessings, and it encourages us to be grateful for everything that He has provided us with. It also implies that denying or failing to recognize these favors is a sign of ingratitude and heedlessness. This verse is a powerful reminder for us to constantly reflect on the many blessings in our lives and to express our gratitude to Allah for His generosity and mercy.
orig: فبأي آلاء ربكما تكذبان

translation: Everyone upon it [i.e., the earth] will perish.
interpretation: This verse reminds us of the fleeting nature of this worldly life and that every soul shall taste death. It emphasizes that no matter how much we may be attached to this world, ultimately everything and everyone on this earth is transient and will pass away. The only thing that remains is Allah, the Eternal. This verse encourages believers to focus on the eternal life of the Hereafter rather than being consumed by the temporary pleasures and distractions of this world. It is a powerful reminder to prioritize our relationship with Allah and to live our lives in accordance with His guidance, as that is what will ultimately matter when we face Him on the Day of Judgment.
orig: كل من عليها فان

translation: And there will remain the Face of your Lord, Owner of Majesty and Honor.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the eternal nature of Allah, the Almighty. It asserts that while everything in this world is temporary and will eventually perish, Allah's existence is everlasting. His divine attributes, such as His Majesty and Honor, will forever remain. This verse serves as a reminder for believers to focus on the eternal aspects of existence, rather than being distracted by the fleeting nature of worldly pursuits. It encourages humans to strive for the pleasure of Allah, as He is the only constant in a constantly changing world.
orig: ويبقى وجه ربك ذو الجلال والإكرام

translation: Then which of the favors of your Lord will you deny?
interpretation: This verse is a rhetorical question that is repeated throughout Surah Ar-Rahman. It encourages introspection and serves as a call to abandon ingratitude and disbelief, instead embracing faith and thankfulness for all that Allah has provided, both in this world and the promise of Paradise in the hereafter. The verse also highlights the fact that despite the abundance of blessings, human beings often take them for granted or even deny them outright, and this rhetorical question is a strong admonition against such ungratefulness.
orig: فبأي آلاء ربكما تكذبان

translation: Reclining on green cushions and beautiful fine carpets.
interpretation: This verse is describing the luxurious and comfortable setting that the righteous will enjoy in Paradise. The mention of "green cushions" and "beautiful fine carpets" paints a picture of an opulent and pleasant environment. Green is a color associated with tranquility, freshness and nature. The fine carpets add to the sense of luxury and reward that the believers will experience in the Hereafter. This verse aims to motivate people to strive for righteousness by giving them a glimpse of the wonderful abode that awaits them, in contrast to the punishment that the sinners will face. It shows that God will honor the faithful with the best of provisions in the eternal life to come.
orig: متكئين على رفرف خضر وعبقري حسان

translation: Then which of the favors of your Lord will you deny?
interpretation: This verse is a rhetorical question that is repeated many times throughout Surah Ar-Rahman. It serves as a reminder to humanity and the jinn of the countless blessings and favors that Allah has bestowed upon them. It encourages reflection on the various gifts mentioned in the preceding verses, such as the creation of the heavens and earth, the perfect balance in nature, and the provisions that sustain life. The repetition of this question emphasizes the importance of acknowledging and appreciating Allah's benevolence, rather than denying or taking it for granted. It is a call to be grateful for the innumerable bounties that the Creator has granted to His creation, and to recognize that everything we have is from Him alone.
orig: فبأي آلاء ربكما تكذبان

translation: Blessed is the name of your Lord, Owner of Majesty and Honor.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the greatness and perfection of Allah's name and attributes. It calls upon mankind to glorify and praise Him, recognizing His absolute majesty and boundless generosity. The verse serves as a reminder that all blessings and bounties originate from Allah alone, and that He is worthy of our utmost reverence and gratitude. It encourages believers to constantly remember and exalt His holy name, acknowledging His sovereignty over all creation and His infinite wisdom in all affairs.
orig: تبارك اسم ربك ذي الجلال والإكرام

translation: When the Occurrence occurs
interpretation: This verse is referring to the Day of Judgment, a momentous event that will mark the end of this world and the beginning of the eternal afterlife. The "Occurrence" is one of the names of the Day of Judgment, indicating its inevitability and the gravity of what will transpire on that day. This opening verse of Surah Al-Waqi'ah sets the stage for the rest of the chapter which goes on to describe the events of the Day of Judgment in vivid detail, including the division of humanity into three groups and their respective fates in the Hereafter based on their deeds in this life. The sudden opening with this impactful statement serves to capture the audience's attention and remind them of the importance of preparing for that inevitable Day.
orig: إذا وقعت الواقعة

translation: There is none to deny its occurrence.
interpretation: This verse is referring to the Day of Judgment, emphasizing that it is an inevitable reality that no one can deny or escape from. It serves as a reminder to humanity that they will be held accountable for their deeds in this world and should strive to live righteously in preparation for that momentous event. The verse underscores the absolute certainty and truthfulness of Allah's promise concerning the Day of Reckoning.
orig: ليس لوقعتها كاذبة

translation: It lowers [some] and raises [others]
interpretation: This verse refers to the vicissitudes of life and the changing fortunes of people. It suggests that God has the power to bring down the mighty and elevate the humble according to His will. The verse reminds us of the fleeting nature of worldly status and success, and encourages humility and reliance on God's grace rather than on one's own achievements or position in society. It also implies that the ultimate judgment of a person's worth lies with God, who sees beyond outward appearances and knows the true nature of each soul.
orig: خافضة رافعة

translation: When the earth is shaken with its [final] earthquake
interpretation: This verse is referring to the end of times, when the earth will be shaken violently in a massive earthquake, signaling the beginning of the Day of Judgment. It emphasizes the tremendous power and might of Allah, and serves as a reminder to humanity that this world is temporary and that we will all face the ultimate reckoning for our deeds. The shaking of the earth is a sign of the complete upheaval and destruction of the current world order, making way for the eternal afterlife. It is a wake-up call for people to reflect on their lives and actions, and to strive for righteousness before it is too late.
orig: إذا رجت الأرض رجا

translation: And the mountains will be crumbled with a [single] blow,
interpretation: This verse speaks about the Day of Judgment when the mountains, despite their firmness and strength, will be completely pulverized and scattered like dust with a single powerful blast. It emphasizes the immense power and might of Allah, and how even the most colossal and unshakable creations will be reduced to nothing on that fateful day. The verse serves as a reminder of the inevitability of the Day of Judgment and the ultimate fate that awaits all of Allah's creation, urging believers to be mindful of their actions and to prepare for the Hereafter.
orig: وبست الجبال بسا

translation: And becomes dust dispersing.
interpretation: This verse refers to the ultimate fate of all worldly things and pursuits. No matter how grand or significant they may seem in this life, in the end, everything will perish and turn to scattered dust. It is a reminder of the fleeting nature of the material world and encourages believers to focus on the eternal spiritual realm instead of being distracted by temporary worldly gains. The verse emphasizes the importance of living a righteous life and prioritizing one's relationship with Allah, as that is the only thing that will matter in the end when all else has turned to dust.
orig: فكانت هباء منبثا

translation: And you will be [divided into] three kinds:
interpretation: This verse indicates that on the Day of Judgment, people will be divided into three distinct groups based on their deeds and faith in this worldly life. The categorization of people into these three groups highlights the importance of one's actions and beliefs, as they will determine one's fate in the Hereafter. It serves as a reminder for individuals to strive for righteousness and to be among those who will be granted the highest rewards in Paradise.
orig: وكنتم أزواجا ثلاثة

translation: So those on the right - what are those on the right?
interpretation: This verse is referring to the people who will be given their records in their right hands on the Day of Judgment, indicating that they are the righteous and blessed ones who will enter Paradise. The repetition of the phrase "those on the right" emphasizes their high status and the great reward that awaits them for their good deeds and faith in this world. It is a reminder for believers to strive to be among those on the right by living a life of righteousness and obedience to Allah.
orig: فأصحاب الميمنة ما أصحاب الميمنة

translation: And the companions of the left - what are the companions of the left?
interpretation: This verse is referring to the people who will be on the left side of Allah on the Day of Judgment, meaning those who are condemned and will enter Hell. They are called "the companions of the left" or "the people of misfortune" because they will face a terrible fate due to their disbelief, sins, and disobedience to Allah during their worldly lives. The repetition of the phrase emphasizes the severity and horror of their situation, and serves as a warning to all people to strive for righteousness and be among those on the right side, the people of Paradise.
orig: وأصحاب المشأمة ما أصحاب المشأمة

translation: And the foremost, the foremost.
interpretation: This verse refers to those who are foremost in faith, good deeds, and closeness to Allah. They are the ones who have surpassed others in their devotion and obedience to Allah, and as a result, they will be among the closest to Him in Paradise. This verse emphasizes the importance of striving to be among the foremost believers, as they will be granted the highest ranks and rewards in the Hereafter. It encourages Muslims to compete with one another in righteousness and to excel in their worship and service to Allah.
orig: والسابقون السابقون

translation: Those are the ones brought near [to Allah].
interpretation: This verse refers to the righteous believers who have attained the highest ranks in Paradise due to their strong faith, good deeds, and devotion to Allah. They are granted the special privilege of being in close proximity to Allah, enjoying His pleasure and blessings. This nearness to Allah is not in a physical sense, but rather a spiritual closeness and a high status in the Hereafter, which is the ultimate goal and aspiration of every true believer.
orig: أولئك المقربون

translation: In the Gardens of Bliss.
interpretation: This verse refers to the ultimate reward for the righteous believers in the Hereafter. The "Gardens of Bliss" or "Gardens of Delight" (Jannat an-Na'eem) represent the highest level of Paradise, where the faithful servants of Allah will enjoy eternal peace, happiness, and pleasure. It symbolizes the spiritual and physical delights that await those who have lived a life of obedience, good deeds, and devotion to Allah. The verse emphasizes the incomparable beauty, serenity, and joy that the believers will experience in these gardens as a reward for their faith and righteousness in this worldly life.
orig: في جنات النعيم

translation: A group of the former people
interpretation: This verse refers to a group or party of people from earlier generations or civilizations. It suggests that the Qur'an is drawing attention to the fate or example of these people from the past, possibly as a lesson or warning for the current listeners. The specific identity of this group is not mentioned in this short verse, but it is likely elaborated upon in the surrounding context. The use of the word "ثلة" (translated as "group") implies a smaller subset or selection from a larger population of "the former people".
orig: ثلة من الأولين

translation: And few from the later peoples.
interpretation: This verse suggests that only a small number of people from later generations will follow the righteous path and be among the successful ones in the Hereafter. It implies that as time passes, fewer and fewer people will adhere to the teachings of Islam and remain steadfast in their faith. This could be due to the increasing distractions, temptations, and challenges that people face in later times, making it more difficult for them to stay committed to their religious beliefs and practices.
orig: وقليل من الآخرين

translation: On adorned couches [of gold and precious stones].
interpretation: This verse refers to the couches or thrones in Paradise that the righteous believers will recline upon. These couches are described as being "mawdoona", which means they are adorned, decorated, and elevated. This suggests that the couches will be beautiful, luxurious, and befitting of the high status and honor that will be bestowed upon the inhabitants of Paradise. The verse paints a picture of comfort, elegance, and reward for those who have earned Allah's pleasure through faith and good deeds in this worldly life.
orig: على سرر موضونة

translation: Reclining on them, facing each other.
interpretation: This verse is describing the state of the believers in Paradise. They will be reclining on couches or thrones, facing each other in a pleasant and intimate setting. This posture symbolizes the comfort, peace, and companionship they will enjoy in the eternal bliss of the Hereafter. The verse emphasizes the social aspect of Paradise, where the righteous will be in the company of their loved ones and fellow believers, engaging in delightful conversations and strengthening their bonds of friendship and love in the presence of Allah's grace and mercy.
orig: متكئين عليها متقابلين

translation: There will circulate among them young boys made eternal
interpretation: This verse is referring to the eternal bliss and pleasures that the righteous will enjoy in Paradise. The "young boys made eternal" are the servants in Paradise who will attend to the needs and desires of the inhabitants. They are described as eternally youthful, indicating that they will not age or lose their beauty and vigor. This is a metaphor for the timeless nature of Paradise, where everything remains perfect and unchanging. The presence of these eternal servants is a reward for the righteous deeds of the believers and a symbol of their honored status in the Hereafter.
orig: يطوف عليهم ولدان مخلدون

translation: With cups and pitchers and a glass from a flowing spring.
interpretation: This verse is describing the vessels from which the righteous will drink in Paradise. The mention of cups, pitchers, and glasses suggests an abundance of pure, refreshing drink that will be served to them. The flowing spring indicates a continuous supply of this blessed beverage, symbolizing the never-ending bliss and bounties that the inhabitants of Paradise will enjoy. This imagery conveys the idea of luxury, satisfaction, and the fulfillment of all desires in the eternal abode of the hereafter, as a reward for the righteous deeds performed in this worldly life.
orig: بأكواب وأباريق وكأس من معين

translation: No headache will they have therefrom, nor will they be intoxicated.
interpretation: This verse refers to the state of the believers in Paradise. They will drink from the rivers of wine, but unlike the wine of this world, it will not cause them any headaches or intoxication. This emphasizes the purity and perfection of the blessings in Paradise, which are free from any negative consequences or drawbacks that are associated with worldly pleasures. The believers will be able to enjoy the delights of Paradise without any fear of harm or impairment to their faculties.
orig: لا يصدعون عنها ولا ينزفون

translation: And fruit of what they may choose.
interpretation: This verse refers to the blessings and rewards that the righteous will enjoy in Paradise. Among these delights are fruits of their choosing, indicating that they will have access to an abundance and variety of fruits according to their desires. This highlights the generosity and benevolence of Allah in rewarding those who have lived a life of faith and righteousness. The verse also implies that the fruits in Paradise will be of a superior quality and taste compared to those in this worldly life, emphasizing the perfection and excellence of the eternal abode prepared for the believers.
orig: وفاكهة مما يتخيرون

translation: And the meat of fowls that they desire.
interpretation: This verse is referring to one of the delights that the righteous will enjoy in Paradise. The "meat of fowls" mentioned here symbolizes the finest and choicest of foods that will be available to the believers in the afterlife. It signifies that all their desires and cravings will be fulfilled in the most perfect manner. The verse emphasizes the boundless generosity and benevolence of Allah towards those who have earned His pleasure through their faith and good deeds in this worldly life. It serves as a motivation for the believers to strive harder in Allah's way, knowing that their ultimate reward will be the unimaginable bliss of Paradise, where all their wishes will be granted.
orig: ولحم طير مما يشتهون

translation: And [for them are] fair women with large, [beautiful] eyes,
interpretation: This verse is describing one of the rewards in Paradise (Jannah) for the righteous believers. "Hoor Ein" refers to the beautiful companions with captivating eyes who will be the spouses of the believers in the afterlife. Their beauty is unparalleled and pure. The mention of these companions is to emphasize the ultimate bliss, tranquility, and joy that the righteous will experience in Paradise as a reward for their faith and good deeds in this worldly life.
orig: وحور عين

translation: Like well-protected pearls
interpretation: This verse likens righteous women to precious pearls that are carefully guarded and protected from anything that may taint their purity and beauty. It signifies that virtuous believing women are highly valued and should be honored, respected and protected by the believing men in their lives, whether fathers, husbands, brothers or sons. The verse emphasizes the importance of modesty, chastity and righteousness as the noblest qualities for a woman to embody.
orig: كأمثال اللؤلؤ المكنون

translation: A reward for what they used to do.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the concept of divine justice in Islam. It indicates that people will be recompensed in the Hereafter based on their deeds and actions in this worldly life. Those who performed good deeds with sincerity and in accordance with God's commands will be rewarded generously, while those who engaged in evil and disobedience will face the consequences of their actions. This verse serves as a reminder for individuals to be mindful of their conduct and to strive for righteousness, knowing that ultimately, everyone will be held accountable before God and will receive what they deserve based on their own choices and behaviors.
orig: جزاء بما كانوا يعملون

translation: No vain discourse will they hear therein, nor any sinful speech.
interpretation: In Paradise, the believers will not hear any vain, useless, or sinful speech. This verse emphasizes the purity and sanctity of Paradise, where all discourse will be meaningful, virtuous, and free from any form of sin or evil. It highlights the fact that Paradise is a place of peace, tranquility, and spiritual upliftment, where the believers will be protected from any kind of harmful or inappropriate speech that could taint their eternal bliss.
orig: لا يسمعون فيها لغوا ولا تأثيما

translation: Except a saying: "Peace, peace."
interpretation: This verse refers to the greeting that the righteous will receive in Paradise. Instead of any vain or harmful speech, they will be met with the greeting of "Peace" from all sides. This represents the tranquility, security, and goodwill that will prevail in that blessed abode. It signifies that they will be safe from any form of distress, hardship, or conflict. The repetition of "Peace" emphasizes the completeness and abundance of peace in Paradise, which is the ultimate goal and reward for the believers who lived righteously in this world.
orig: إلا قيلا سلاما سلاما

translation: And the companions of the right - what are the companions of the right?
interpretation: This verse is referring to the righteous believers who will be given their records of deeds in their right hands on the Day of Judgment. They are called the "companions of the right" because receiving the record in the right hand signifies that they will enter Paradise due to their good deeds and obedience to Allah during their worldly life. The repetition of the phrase "what are the companions of the right?" serves to emphasize their honored and distinguished position on that Day, and to draw attention to the great rewards that await them in the Hereafter as a result of their righteousness.
orig: وأصحاب اليمين ما أصحاب اليمين

translation: Among lote trees with thorns removed
interpretation: This verse refers to one of the delights that the righteous will enjoy in Paradise. The "lote trees" mentioned here are a type of tree that bears fruit, but unlike the lote trees of this world, the ones in Paradise will have their thorns removed, making them easier and more pleasant to enjoy. This small detail highlights the perfection and ease of everything in Paradise, where even the trees are made more beautiful and accessible for the pleasure of its inhabitants. It symbolizes how all imperfections and difficulties will be removed in the next life for those who have earned Allah's favor through their faith and good deeds.
orig: في سدر مخضود

translation: And [banana] trees layered [with fruit]
interpretation: This verse is describing the bounties and blessings that will be present in Paradise. The mention of "layered banana trees" suggests that there will be an abundance of fruit in Paradise, stacked and arranged in a beautiful and plentiful manner. This imagery conveys the idea of the perfection and never-ending provision of delights that the righteous will enjoy in the Hereafter as a reward for their faith and good deeds in this world. It is a reminder of the generosity and mercy of Allah towards His deserving servants in the eternal life to come.
orig: وطلح منضود

translation: And extended shade
interpretation: This verse is referring to the shade that will be provided to the righteous believers in Paradise. It is described as being "extended" or "spread out", indicating its vastness and abundance. This shade is a blessing and a comfort, protecting the inhabitants of Paradise from any heat or discomfort. It is a symbol of the perfect peace, tranquility, and ease that the believers will enjoy in the eternal gardens of the Hereafter, as a reward for their faith and good deeds in this worldly life.
orig: وظل ممدود

translation: And water poured forth
interpretation: This verse is referring to the abundance of blessings and provisions that Allah has bestowed upon His creation. The "water poured forth" is a metaphor for the plentiful sustenance, both physical and spiritual, that Allah provides. It symbolizes the life-giving nature of water and how it is essential for the existence and flourishing of all living beings. The verse reminds us to be grateful for the blessings that Allah has given us and to recognize His generosity and mercy in providing for our needs.
orig: وماء مسكوب

translation: And abundant fruit
interpretation: This verse is referring to the blessings and rewards that will be bestowed upon the righteous believers in Paradise. Among these rewards is an abundance of various fruits that they will be able to enjoy eternally. The mention of "abundant fruit" highlights the generosity and limitlessness of God's provision in the afterlife, as the inhabitants of Paradise will have access to a never-ending supply of delicious fruits. This serves as a reminder of the importance of striving for righteousness in this life, as the ultimate reward for doing so is the attainment of Paradise and its countless blessings, including the abundant fruit mentioned in this verse.
orig: وفاكهة كثيرة

translation: Neither cut off [from future hope] nor forbidden [from mercy]
interpretation: This verse is conveying a message of hope and optimism. It suggests that no matter how difficult or hopeless a situation may seem, one should never lose hope or feel that they are beyond God's mercy and forgiveness. The doors of repentance and divine grace are always open. It encourages perseverance and faith even in the darkest of times, knowing that God's mercy and blessings are boundless. The verse serves as a reminder to never despair or feel cut off from God's love and compassion.
orig: لا مقطوعة ولا ممنوعة

translation: And [upon] beds raised high.
interpretation: This verse refers to the elevated beds or couches that will be provided to the righteous believers in Paradise. These beds are described as being raised high, indicating their honor, comfort, and luxury. The verse suggests that the inhabitants of Paradise will enjoy a state of ease, rest, and delight, reclining on these magnificent furnishings as a reward for their faith and good deeds in this world. The raised beds symbolize the lofty status and dignity that the believers will attain in the eternal life of the Hereafter.
orig: وفرش مرفوعة

translation: Indeed, We have produced them in a [new] creation
interpretation: In this verse, Allah is referring to the women of Paradise, who will be created anew, free from the imperfections and flaws of their worldly existence. They will be made in a perfect form, with beauty and youth that will never fade. This is a reminder of the power and ability of Allah to create and recreate as He wills, and a promise of the eternal bliss that awaits the righteous in the Hereafter.
orig: إنا أنشأناهن إنشاء

translation: And We have made them virgins
interpretation: In this verse, Allah is describing the pure and untouched nature of the companions in Paradise. The word "abkaar" (virgins) signifies that they will be restored to a state of purity and innocence, free from any previous worldly experiences or relationships. This emphasizes the perfection and beauty of Paradise, where everything is created anew and flawless for the believers to enjoy eternally. It also highlights the importance of maintaining purity and chastity in this world, as it will be rewarded with the ultimate purity and companionship in the Hereafter.
orig: فجعلناهن أبكارا

translation: Companions of equal age
interpretation: This verse is referring to the companions that the righteous will have in Paradise. The term "atraban" indicates that these companions will be of similar age to one another. This suggests that the relationships and interactions between the dwellers of Paradise will be harmonious and free of any generational gaps or differences that may cause friction or misunderstanding. It is a blessing from Allah that the believers will have the company of those who are well-matched to them and with whom they can enjoy eternal happiness and peace.
orig: عربا أترابا

translation: For the companions of the right.
interpretation: This verse refers to the righteous believers who will be granted Paradise on the Day of Judgment. They are called "the companions of the right" because they will receive their records of deeds in their right hands, signifying their good deeds and righteousness. These individuals have followed the path of truth, obeyed Allah's commands, and will be rewarded with eternal bliss in the Hereafter.
orig: لأصحاب اليمين

translation: A company of the former peoples
interpretation: This verse refers to a group or party of people from earlier nations or generations who have passed away. It suggests that the Quran contains stories and lessons from the lives of those who came before, and that reflecting on their experiences can provide guidance and wisdom for the present. The verse may also serve as a reminder of the transient nature of worldly life and the inevitability of death, encouraging believers to focus on righteousness and good deeds while they still have the opportunity.
orig: ثلة من الأولين

translation: And a group of others
interpretation: This verse is referring to a group or party of people who are distinct from those mentioned previously. It suggests that in addition to the main subject or group being discussed, there is another subset or faction that is also relevant to the matter at hand. The use of the word "uthla" (group or party) implies that these "others" share some common characteristics or purpose. Without further context about the preceding verses, it is difficult to ascertain the exact identity or role of this particular group. However, the verse clearly indicates that they are separate from the primary subject, while still having some connection or relevance to the overall discussion.
orig: وثلة من الآخرين

translation: And the companions of the left - what are the companions of the left?
interpretation: This verse is referring to the people who will be on the left side of Allah on the Day of Judgment, which is a metaphor for those who will be condemned to Hell. The repetition of the phrase "companions of the left" is used for emphasis and to draw attention to their terrible fate. It implies that these people lived their lives in a way that earned them this punishment, such as rejecting faith, indulging in sin, and oppressing others. The verse serves as a warning to all people to be mindful of their actions and to strive for righteousness, so that they may be among the "companions of the right" who will be granted Paradise.
orig: وأصحاب الشمال ما أصحاب الشمال

translation: In a scorching wind and scalding water
interpretation: This verse is describing the punishment that awaits the disbelievers in Hell. They will be subjected to extreme heat in the form of a scorching wind and scalding water. This torment is a result of their rejection of God's message and their evil deeds in this world. The verse serves as a warning to all of mankind to follow the straight path and avoid the fate of the disbelievers.
orig: في سموم وحميم

translation: And a shade of Yahmum
interpretation: This verse is referring to the shade that will be provided to the righteous in Paradise. "Yahmum" is a type of tree in Paradise that will provide a cool and pleasant shade for those who are granted entry into it. This shade is a reward for their good deeds and righteousness in this world. It symbolizes the comfort, peace, and tranquility that the believers will experience in the eternal abode of the Hereafter, in contrast to the hardships and difficulties they faced in the world.
orig: وظل من يحموم

translation: No cold and no generous
interpretation: This phrase is likely an idiom or figure of speech rather than a Qur'anic verse. It seems to express that someone or something is neither refreshing (cold) nor noble/generous in character. More context would be needed to interpret the intended meaning fully.
orig: لا بارد ولا كريم

translation: Indeed, they were before that living in luxury.
interpretation: This verse suggests that those being referred to had previously been living a life of extravagance, indulgence, and self-gratification. The use of the word "mutrafin" implies that they were immersed in worldly pleasures and had become accustomed to a luxurious lifestyle. This statement could be seen as a criticism of their past behavior, indicating that their excessive indulgence in material comforts had led them astray from the path of righteousness. It serves as a reminder that a life focused solely on worldly pleasures can have negative consequences and that one should strive for balance and moderation in their pursuits.
orig: إنهم كانوا قبل ذلك مترفين

translation: And they persisted in great sin.
interpretation: This verse is referring to the stubborn persistence of some people in committing major sins and disobeying Allah, despite knowing that what they are doing is wrong. It highlights the human tendency to sometimes willfully engage in sinful behavior out of arrogance, pride or giving in to lowly desires, even after receiving guidance and reminders. The verse serves as a warning against such a mindset and emphasizes the importance of humility, repentance and making efforts to avoid falling into grave sins.
orig: وكانوا يصرون على الحنث العظيم

translation: And they say, "When we have died and become dust and bones, are we indeed to be resurrected?"
interpretation: This verse is questioning the idea of resurrection after death. It reflects the skepticism and disbelief of those who deny the possibility of life after death. They cannot comprehend how their scattered remains could be brought back to life after they have decomposed into dust and bones. This incredulity towards resurrection stems from a lack of faith and understanding of God's power and ability to restore life to the dead. The verse highlights the limitation of human perception in grasping the reality of the afterlife and the need for faith in God's promise of resurrection and judgment.
orig: وكانوا يقولون أئذا متنا وكنا ترابا وعظاما أإنا لمبعوثون

translation: Or our forefathers [before us]?
interpretation: This verse is questioning the belief in blindly following the traditions and practices of one's ancestors without critical examination. It suggests that people should not simply accept the beliefs and ways of their forefathers without reflecting on their validity and alignment with divine guidance. The Qur'an encourages individuals to use their intellect, reason, and the guidance provided by revelation to discern truth from falsehood, rather than unquestioningly adhering to inherited customs or beliefs.
orig: أوآباؤنا الأولون

translation: Say, "Indeed, the former and the later peoples"
interpretation: This verse is referring to the fact that all of mankind, from the earliest generations to the last, will be gathered together by Allah on the Day of Judgment. It emphasizes the universality and inevitability of the final reckoning, where every soul will be held accountable for their deeds in this world. The verse serves as a reminder for people to be mindful of their actions and to strive for righteousness, knowing that they will ultimately face the consequences in the Hereafter.
orig: قل إن الأولين والآخرين

translation: To be gathered together for the appointment of a known Day.
interpretation: This verse is referring to the Day of Judgment, when all of humanity will be resurrected and gathered before Allah to be held accountable for their deeds in this worldly life. It is a "known Day" because Allah has already decreed when it will occur, though that knowledge is with Him alone. This verse serves as a reminder to mankind that there will come a time when we will have to answer for how we lived our lives, and that we should strive to live righteously and in accordance with Allah's commands in preparation for that inevitable Day.
orig: لمجموعون إلى ميقات يوم معلوم

translation: Moreover, indeed you, O you the ones astray, the deniers.
interpretation: This verse is addressing the disbelievers who have strayed from the right path and rejected the truth. It emphasizes their state of being misguided and their active denial of the divine message. The use of the word "moreover" (ثم) and the emphatic "indeed you" (إنكم) serves to stress the gravity of their condition and the consequences that await them as a result of their conscious choice to disbelieve. It is a stern admonition and a reminder that their actions will not go unaccounted for.
orig: ثم إنكم أيها الضالون المكذبون

translation: Eaters of the tree of Zaqqum
interpretation: This verse refers to the punishment of the sinners in Hell, where they will be forced to eat from the tree of Zaqqum. The tree of Zaqqum is described in the Qur'an as a tree that grows in the bottom of Hell, with fruits that resemble the heads of devils. Eating from this tree will be a painful and humiliating experience for the sinners, as it will neither nourish them nor satisfy their hunger. This punishment serves as a reminder of the consequences of rejecting God's message and indulging in sin during one's worldly life.
orig: لآكلون من شجر من زقوم

translation: And fill their bellies with it.
interpretation: This verse is likely referring to the punishment that awaits the disbelievers in Hell. The "it" being referred to is probably the fruit of the tree of Zaqqum, which is described in the Qur'an as a food for the sinners in Hell (see 37:62-66). The verse suggests that the bellies of the inhabitants of Hell will be filled with this terrible food as a form of torment and punishment for their disbelief and evil deeds in this world. It emphasizes the severity and abhorrence of the punishment that awaits those who reject God's message.
orig: فمالئون منها البطون

translation: And they will drink with it scalding water.
interpretation: This verse refers to the punishment that awaits the disbelievers in the Hereafter. They will be forced to drink extremely hot water as a form of torment. This scalding water will intensify their suffering and pain. It symbolizes the severity and horror of the consequences they will face for rejecting faith and indulging in evil deeds during their worldly life. The verse serves as a strong warning and reminder for people to be mindful of their actions and to embrace the path of righteousness.
orig: فشاربون عليه من الحميم

translation: And they will drink as the thirsty camels drink
interpretation: This verse is referring to the people in Hell who will drink boiling water like thirsty camels. The metaphor of drinking like camels emphasizes the desperation and intensity of their thirst due to the severity of the punishment they are facing. It paints a vivid picture of their suffering and the consequences of their wrongdoing in this life. The verse serves as a strong warning for people to avoid sinful deeds that could lead to such a fate in the Hereafter.
orig: فشاربون شرب الهيم

translation: That is their accommodation on the Day of Judgement.
interpretation: This verse refers to the fate of the disbelievers and wrongdoers on the Day of Judgement. The "accommodation" mentioned here is Hell, where they will abide as a consequence of their actions and disbelief in this world. It emphasizes the concept of divine justice, where everyone will be held accountable for their deeds and will be rewarded or punished accordingly in the Hereafter. The verse serves as a warning to those who reject faith and engage in sinful acts, reminding them of the severe consequences that await them if they do not repent and follow the righteous path.
orig: هذا نزلهم يوم الدين

translation: It is We Who created you; why then do you not accept the truth?
interpretation: This verse is a reminder from Allah to humanity that He is the One who created them, and therefore, they should believe in Him and accept the truth of His message. It is a call to reflect on the fact that our existence is not by chance, but rather by the will and power of the Almighty Creator. The verse implies that since Allah has created us, it is only logical and righteous that we acknowledge Him as our Lord and submit to His guidance. It is an invitation to ponder upon the signs of Allah's creation within ourselves and in the universe around us, which should lead us to affirm His existence and accept the truth of the message He has sent through His prophets.
orig: نحن خلقناكم فلولا تصدقون

translation: Have you then considered what you emit?
interpretation: This verse is asking mankind to reflect upon the miracle of human reproduction. It draws attention to the fact that the fluid that creates human life originates from within ourselves, yet we have no control over the intricate process that transforms this fluid into a new living being. The verse invites us to ponder the power and wisdom of Allah in designing this incredible system, and to appreciate the sanctity and significance of the act that leads to procreation. It reminds us that life is a sacred gift from Allah, and that we should approach the matter of intimacy and reproduction with a sense of responsibility, reverence and gratitude to the Creator.
orig: أفرأيتم ما تمنون

translation: Is it you who create it, or are We the Creator?
interpretation: This verse is a rhetorical question that emphasizes the power and supremacy of Allah as the sole Creator. It challenges the notion that humans or any other entity can create life or have control over the creation process. The verse implies that it is Allah alone who possesses the ability to create and give life, and that this power is far beyond the capabilities of any human being. It serves as a reminder for people to acknowledge and submit to the ultimate creative authority of Allah.
orig: أأنتم تخلقونه أم نحن الخالقون

translation: We have decreed death among you, and We are not to be outdone
interpretation: This verse reminds us of the inevitability of death, which is a decree from Allah that no one can escape or overcome. It emphasizes Allah's power and control over life and death, and that He has predetermined the time of death for every soul. The verse also implies that no matter how much we try to avoid or delay death, we cannot outdo Allah's decree. This should serve as a reminder for us to live our lives in accordance with Allah's teachings, as we will all face the reality of death and be held accountable for our deeds in the Hereafter.
orig: نحن قدرنا بينكم الموت وما نحن بمسبوقين

translation: That We will change your likenesses and create you in that [form] which you do not know.
interpretation: This verse alludes to the concept of resurrection in Islam, where Allah has the power to recreate human beings in a new form that is unknown to them. It emphasizes the idea that the human form and likeness are not permanent, and that Allah can transform and resurrect people in a manner that is beyond their current knowledge and understanding. This interpretation highlights the absolute power and control of Allah over His creation, and serves as a reminder of the inevitability of the afterlife and the Day of Judgment.
orig: على أن نبدل أمثالكم وننشئكم في ما لا تعلمون

translation: And you have already known the first creation, so will you not remember?
interpretation: This verse is a reminder to mankind that they have already witnessed the marvel of their own creation from nothing, yet they still doubt Allah's ability to resurrect them after death. It is an appeal to human intellect and reason, urging people to reflect on the origin of their existence. If Allah can create human beings from a mere drop of fluid, then surely He has the power to bring them back to life after death for the Day of Judgment. The verse encourages people to be mindful of this truth and to live their lives with the understanding that they will one day return to their Creator to be held accountable for their deeds.
orig: ولقد علمتم النشأة الأولى فلولا تذكرون

translation: Have you seen what you sow?
interpretation: This verse is asking us to reflect on the process of growing crops. It reminds us that while we may plant the seeds and tend to the land, it is ultimately Allah who causes the plants to grow and bear fruit. The verse encourages us to recognize Allah's power and providence in sustaining us through agriculture. It also implies that just as we cannot control the outcome of what we plant, we cannot control the ultimate outcome of our actions in life. We should do our best, but put our trust in Allah for the results.
orig: أفرأيتم ما تحرثون

translation: Is it you who makes it grow, or are We the grower?
interpretation: This verse is a reminder that it is Allah who causes the crops to grow, not human beings. While humans may plant the seeds and tend to the crops, it is ultimately through Allah's power and will that the plants are able to sprout, grow, and bear fruit. This verse encourages humility and recognition of our dependence on Allah for even the most basic necessities of life, such as food. It also implies that we should be grateful to Allah for His blessings and provisions, rather than attributing success solely to our own efforts.
orig: أأنتم تزرعونه أم نحن الزارعون

translation: If We willed, We could have made it [vegetation] debris, and you would remain in wonder,
interpretation: This verse is a reminder of Allah's power and control over all things. It emphasizes that the growth and sustenance of vegetation is solely by Allah's will and mercy. If He wished, He could easily destroy the crops and leave people in a state of shock and amazement at the sudden loss. This serves as a lesson for humanity to recognize and appreciate the blessings and provisions bestowed upon them by Allah, and to remain humble and grateful, knowing that everything they have is ultimately from Him and can be taken away if He so wills.
orig: لو نشاء لجعلناه حطاما فظلتم تفكهون

translation: Indeed, we are ruined.
interpretation: This verse conveys a sense of despair and hopelessness, as if the speaker and those with them are facing an overwhelming calamity or loss that has left them feeling utterly defeated and ruined. It suggests that they are burdened by a great debt or penalty that they cannot overcome, leaving them in a state of anguish and distress. The verse captures the human experience of hitting rock bottom and feeling as though there is no way out of their misfortune, emphasizing the depth of their suffering and the weight of the consequences they face.
orig: إنا لمغرمون

translation: Nay, but we are deprived.
interpretation: This verse suggests that humans often feel a sense of deprivation or loss, perhaps due to their own actions or the circumstances of life. It implies that we may blame external factors for our misfortunes, saying "Nay" to personal responsibility. However, the verse also hints that this feeling of deprivation is a matter of perspective - we are not truly deprived, but rather choosing to view our situation negatively. It prompts introspection about the root causes of our perceived lack and encourages shifting our mindset from one of victimhood to one of empowerment and gratitude for what we do have.
orig: بل نحن محرومون

translation: Have you considered the water that you drink?
interpretation: This verse draws our attention to the blessing of water, a vital necessity for life. It invites us to reflect upon the source and provision of this essential resource. The rhetorical question implies that water is a divine gift that we often take for granted. It reminds us to be mindful and grateful for the sustenance Allah has provided us through water, without which life would be impossible. This verse encourages contemplation on the signs of Allah's creation and benevolence in our everyday lives.
orig: أفرأيتم الماء الذي تشربون

translation: Is it you who sent it down from the clouds, or are We the sender?
interpretation: This verse is a rhetorical question that emphasizes Allah's power and control over the natural world. It reminds humans that they are not the ones who bring down the life-giving rain from the clouds, but rather it is Allah who does so. The verse implies that humans should be grateful for the blessings that Allah bestows upon them, such as the rain that nourishes the earth and sustains life. It also serves as a reminder of human beings' dependence on Allah and their ultimate lack of control over the forces of nature.
orig: أأنتم أنزلتموه من المزن أم نحن المنزلون

translation: If We willed, We could make it bitter, so why are you not grateful?
interpretation: This verse is a reminder of Allah's power and control over all things. He has the ability to make the water that sustains life bitter and undrinkable, yet He chooses to provide us with sweet, fresh water instead. This is a great blessing that we often take for granted. The verse is a call to recognize this blessing and express gratitude to Allah for His provision. It emphasizes the importance of thankfulness and appreciation for the bounties that Allah bestows upon us, even in the small things that we may overlook. The verse encourages us to reflect on the many blessings in our lives and to turn to Allah in gratitude and worship.
orig: لو نشاء جعلناه أجاجا فلولا تشكرون

translation: Then have you seen the fire that you ignite?
interpretation: This verse is a reminder of Allah's power and generosity. It prompts us to reflect on the blessing of fire, which we often take for granted. Fire is a source of light, warmth, and energy that enables us to cook food, illuminate our homes, and power our industries. Yet, we cannot create fire ourselves; it is Allah who has granted us the ability to ignite it and benefit from it. This verse encourages us to be grateful for Allah's favors and to recognize His sovereignty over all things. It also implies that just as Allah has control over the physical fire, He has control over the spiritual fire of Hell. Therefore, we should be mindful of our actions and strive to earn His pleasure, so that we may be saved from the Fire in the Hereafter.
orig: أفرأيتم النار التي تورون

translation: Is it you who produced its tree, or are We the producer?
interpretation: This verse is a rhetorical question that emphasizes Allah's power and control over His creation. It reminds us that it is Allah who creates and sustains all life, including the trees that provide us with numerous benefits. The question is meant to make us reflect on our own limitations and recognize Allah's supreme authority as the Creator and Sustainer of the universe. It encourages humility and gratitude towards Allah for His countless blessings and provisions.
orig: أأنتم أنشأتم شجرتها أم نحن المنشئون

translation: We have made it a reminder and a provision for the travelers.
interpretation: This verse refers to the she-camel that was sent as a sign to the people of Thamud. Allah made this camel a reminder of His power and a test for the people, to see if they would obey His command to leave her alone and not harm her. The camel was also a provision, a means of sustenance, for the travelers in that barren land, as she could provide them with milk. The verse emphasizes Allah's wisdom in creating signs and tests for people, both to remind them of His presence and power, and to provide for their needs, even in challenging environments.
orig: نحن جعلناها تذكرة ومتاعا للمقوين

translation: So glorify the Name of your Lord, the Most Great.
interpretation: This verse is a command to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and all believers to glorify and praise Allah, acknowledging His greatness and supremacy. It emphasizes the importance of remembering Allah and exalting Him above all else. By glorifying Allah's name, one recognizes His majesty, power, and perfection, while also expressing gratitude for His countless blessings. This act of glorification serves as a means of drawing closer to Allah and attaining inner peace and tranquility. It is a reminder to humans that, despite their worldly pursuits and concerns, they should always prioritize their connection with their Lord and Creator.
orig: فسبح باسم ربك العظيم

translation: But nay! I swear by the setting of the stars
interpretation: In this verse, Allah swears by the positions of the stars, emphasizing the importance and gravity of what is to follow. The stars hold a significant place in the vastness of the universe, and their precise positions and movements are a testament to Allah's power and wisdom. By swearing by the stars, Allah draws attention to the profound nature of the revelation that is about to be mentioned, indicating that it is a matter of utmost importance and should be taken seriously by the believers. This oath serves as a prelude to the divine message, underscoring its authenticity and the truthfulness of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) as the recipient of this revelation.
orig: فلا أقسم بمواقع النجوم

translation: And indeed, it is an oath - if you could know - [most] great.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the immense significance and gravity of the oath being taken. It suggests that if humans truly understood the magnitude and implications of this oath, they would recognize its paramount importance. The phrase "if you could know" implies that human understanding is limited and cannot fully grasp the profound nature of this oath. The verse underscores the idea that the matter at hand is of utmost seriousness and consequence, even if its true extent lies beyond human comprehension.
orig: وإنه لقسم لو تعلمون عظيم

translation: Indeed, it is a noble Qur'an.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the exalted and noble status of the Qur'an. It is a divine revelation from Allah, free from any imperfections or falsehood. The Qur'an is a book of guidance, wisdom, and spiritual enlightenment for all of humanity. Its teachings are timeless and universal, addressing the needs of individuals and societies across all ages. The nobility of the Qur'an lies in its ability to transform hearts, uplift souls, and guide people towards righteousness and closeness to Allah. It is a source of mercy, healing, and salvation for those who believe in its message and strive to live by its principles.
orig: إنه لقرآن كريم

translation: In a Book well-guarded.
interpretation: This verse refers to the Qur'an being protected and preserved in the "Preserved Tablet" (al-Lawh al-Mahfūẓ) in heaven, safeguarded from any alteration, distortion, or corruption. It emphasizes the divine origin and the authentic nature of the Qur'an, as it remains unchanged since its revelation to Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him). The verse also implies that the Qur'an is not accessible to everyone, but only to those who are pure and sincere in their intentions to understand and follow its teachings.
orig: في كتاب مكنون

translation: None touch it except the purified.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the sanctity and purity of the Qur'an. It suggests that only those who are spiritually pure and have purified themselves through righteousness and good deeds are worthy of touching and engaging with the sacred scripture. It serves as a reminder for believers to approach the Qur'an with reverence, respect, and a clean heart and mind. The verse also implies that the Qur'an is protected from any form of corruption or alteration, as it is safeguarded by Allah and can only be accessed by those who are deemed worthy and pure.
orig: لا يمسه إلا المطهرون

translation: A revelation from the Lord of the worlds.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the Qur'an is not a human invention, but a divine revelation from Allah, the Creator and Sustainer of all that exists. It affirms the divine origin and authority of the Qur'an, which serves as a guidance for all mankind. The phrase "Lord of the worlds" highlights Allah's sovereignty and His role as the Master and Provider for all creation, encompassing both the physical and spiritual realms.
orig: تنزيل من رب العالمين

translation: Then is it to this statement that you are deluded?
interpretation: This verse is questioning and criticizing those who are deluded by false statements or narratives, instead of adhering to the truth and guidance provided by God. It suggests that being swayed or deceived by baseless talk is a form of heedlessness and a failure to use reason and discernment. The Qur'an repeatedly emphasizes the importance of seeking truth, reflecting deeply, and avoiding blind following of misguided ideas or people. This verse prompts introspection - are we carefully analyzing what we hear and believe, or are we being intellectually lazy and uncritically accepting false ideas that delude us from reality and divine guidance?
orig: أفبهذا الحديث أنتم مدهنون

translation: And you make your provision that you deny.
interpretation: This verse is criticizing those who are ungrateful to Allah despite His blessings and provisions upon them. Instead of acknowledging Allah's favors and being thankful, they make it their habit to constantly deny and reject the truth. They have taken their ingratitude and disbelief as their "provision" rather than the actual sustenance provided to them by Allah. It highlights the wrongdoing of those who knowingly persist in denying Allah's signs and blessings.
orig: وتجعلون رزقكم أنكم تكذبون

translation: Then why, when the soul at death reaches the throat
interpretation: This verse is a reminder of the inevitability of death and the moment when the soul reaches the throat, signifying the end of life. It is a call for introspection and reflection on one's actions and deeds before it is too late. The verse implies that at the time of death, one will realize the truth and the consequences of their actions, but it will be too late to make amends or change the course of their fate. It emphasizes the importance of living a righteous life and being mindful of one's actions, as death can come at any moment without warning. The verse also highlights the helplessness of man at the time of death, as no one can prevent or delay the soul from leaving the body when the appointed time arrives.
orig: فلولا إذا بلغت الحلقوم

translation: And you will be looking on.
interpretation: This verse is referring to the Day of Judgment when people will witness the consequences of their deeds. It implies that on that day, people will be mere spectators, unable to change their fate or the outcome of their actions. They will helplessly watch as the reality of their lives unfolds before them. This verse serves as a reminder for people to be mindful of their actions in this world, as they will be held accountable for them in the Hereafter.
orig: وأنتم حينئذ تنظرون

translation: And We are nearer to him than you, but you do not see.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the closeness of Allah to His creation, particularly to human beings. It reminds us that Allah is always near, watching over us and aware of our actions, thoughts, and feelings, even though we cannot perceive His presence with our physical senses. This nearness is not in terms of physical proximity, but rather in terms of His knowledge, power, and control over all things. The verse also suggests that people often forget or fail to recognize Allah's closeness, which is why they engage in actions that displease Him or neglect their duties towards Him. It serves as a reminder for people to be mindful of Allah's presence and to strive to maintain a strong connection with Him through faith, obedience, and remembrance.
orig: ونحن أقرب إليه منكم ولكن لا تبصرون

translation: Why not, if you are not to be judged?
interpretation: This verse is questioning the disbelievers who reject the concept of accountability in the Hereafter. It asks them why they do not fear the consequences of their actions if they truly believe they will not be held accountable or judged by Allah for their deeds. The implication is that deep down, they know that they will indeed face judgment, but they choose to deny it out of arrogance or desire to follow their own whims without restriction. It is a powerful reminder that everyone will ultimately answer for their choices and actions in this life.
orig: فلولا إن كنتم غير مدينين

translation: Bring it back, if you are truthful.
interpretation: This verse is challenging those who deny the resurrection and the afterlife. It is asking them to bring back life to the dead, if they are truthful in their claim that there is no resurrection. The verse implies that only Allah has the power to give and restore life, and that denying the resurrection is tantamount to denying Allah's power and wisdom. It is a powerful reminder of the inevitability of death and the reality of the afterlife, and a call to faith and submission to Allah's will.
orig: ترجعونها إن كنتم صادقين

translation: And if he was of those brought near [to Allah],
interpretation: This verse refers to the fate of the righteous believers on the Day of Judgment. Those who are "brought near" to Allah are the highest in rank among the believers due to their strong faith, righteous deeds, and devotion to Allah throughout their lives. They will be granted the special privilege of being close to Allah and enjoying His pleasure and rewards in Paradise. This nearness to Allah is the ultimate aspiration and goal of every true believer, and it reflects the immense honor and blessings that Allah will bestow upon His most faithful servants in the Hereafter.
orig: فأما إن كان من المقربين

translation: So [they will be] among gardens and springs
interpretation: This verse is referring to the reward that awaits the righteous believers in the Hereafter. They will be admitted into gardens of Paradise, where they will enjoy eternal bliss and delight. The mention of "springs" suggests that these gardens will be lush, verdant, and filled with flowing water, adding to the beauty and serenity of the environment. This is a stark contrast to the punishment that awaits the disbelievers, emphasizing the importance of faith and righteousness in this life to attain the ultimate reward in the next.
orig: فروح وريحان وجنت نعيم

translation: And if he was of the companions of the right,
interpretation: This verse refers to the fate of the righteous believers on the Day of Judgment. Those who are "the companions of the right" are the ones who will receive their records of deeds in their right hands, signifying their good deeds and righteousness in this world. They will be granted ease, comfort, and the pleasure of Allah in the Hereafter as a reward for their faith and good actions. This highlights the importance of striving to be among the righteous in this life to attain success and happiness in the eternal life to come.
orig: وأما إن كان من أصحاب اليمين

translation: So peace will be upon you from the companions of the right.
interpretation: This verse refers to the believers who will be granted Paradise on the Day of Judgment. They are called the "companions of the right" because they will receive their records of deeds in their right hands, signifying their righteousness and good deeds.
