Allah is assuring them that they will be greeted with peace and tranquility in Paradise, free from any fear, grief, or hardship. It is a reminder of the ultimate reward that awaits those who follow the straight path and live their lives in obedience to Allah's commands.
orig: فسلام لك من أصحاب اليمين

translation: But if he was of the deniers [who were] astray,
interpretation: This verse refers to the fate of those who reject faith and are misguided. They are the ones who deny the truth of God's message and wander far from the straight path. The verse implies that such individuals will face a different outcome in the Hereafter compared to the righteous believers. It serves as a warning that denying the truth and straying from divine guidance leads to grave consequences in the afterlife. The verse emphasizes the importance of faith and staying on the right path to attain salvation and avoid the fate of the deniers and the misguided.
orig: وأما إن كان من المكذبين الضالين

translation: So he will be poured upon with scalding water.
interpretation: This verse is referring to the punishment that awaits the disbelievers in the Hereafter. The scalding water mentioned here is one of the forms of torment that they will face in Hell. It signifies the severity and painfulness of the punishment, as the boiling water will be poured over their heads, causing immense suffering and agony. This verse serves as a warning to those who reject faith and do not follow the path of righteousness, reminding them of the consequences of their actions in the afterlife.
orig: فنزل من حميم

translation: And the burning of Hell.
interpretation: This verse refers to the punishment that awaits the disbelievers and sinners in the Hereafter. The "burning of Hell" emphasizes the severity and intensity of the torment that they will face as a consequence of their actions and their rejection of faith. It serves as a warning to mankind to be mindful of their deeds and to strive for righteousness in this world, so as to avoid the painful fate of the Hellfire in the next.
orig: وتصلية جحيم

translation: Indeed, this is the true certainty.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute truth and certainty of the Qur'an and its message. It asserts that the revelations contained within the Qur'an are not mere speculation or conjecture, but rather they represent the ultimate and unquestionable reality. The verse aims to remove any doubts or skepticism regarding the authenticity and veracity of the Qur'anic teachings, affirming that they are the embodiment of divine truth. It serves as a powerful reminder to believers to have unwavering faith in the Qur'an and its guidance, as it is the true and certain path to salvation and righteousness.
orig: إن هذا لهو حق اليقين

translation: So glorify the name of your Lord, the Magnificent.
interpretation: This verse is a command to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and, by extension, to all believers to glorify and praise Allah, acknowledging His greatness and magnificence. It emphasizes the importance of remembering Allah and exalting Him above all else. By glorifying Allah's name, one recognizes His supreme attributes and perfection, while also expressing gratitude for His countless blessings. This act of glorification serves as a means of strengthening one's faith, humility, and connection with the Almighty. It is a reminder to focus on the worship and remembrance of Allah, which should be the central focus of a believer's life.
orig: فسبح باسم ربك العظيم

translation: Whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth exalts Allah, and He is the Exalted in Might, the Wise.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that all of creation, whether in the heavens or on earth, glorifies and praises Allah. It points to the complete submission and recognition of Allah's majesty by everything in existence. The mention of Allah's attributes of being "Exalted in Might" and "Wise" highlights His supreme power and knowledge over all things. It serves as a reminder for humans to join the rest of creation in acknowledging and exalting Allah, recognizing His wisdom in all affairs and might above everything else.
orig: سبح لله ما في السماوات والأرض وهو العزيز الحكيم

translation: To Him belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth. He gives life and causes death, and He is over all things competent.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute sovereignty and power of Allah over all of creation. It affirms that Allah alone is the ultimate owner and ruler of the heavens and the earth, and everything within them. He has the power to give life and cause death, demonstrating His complete control over the cycle of existence. The verse also highlights Allah's omnipotence, stating that He is capable of all things and has the ability to do whatever He wills. This serves as a reminder to humanity that Allah is the Supreme Being, and we should submit to His will and recognize His authority in all aspects of our lives.
orig: له ملك السماوات والأرض يحيي ويميت وهو على كل شيء قدير

translation: He is the First and the Last, the Ascendant and the Intimate, and He is, of all things, Knowing.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the all-encompassing nature of Allah. He is the First, existing before all creation, and the Last, remaining after all creation perishes. He is the Ascendant, above and beyond His creation, and the Intimate, closer to us than our own selves. The verse affirms that Allah's knowledge is complete and perfect, spanning all things in existence. It highlights His eternal and infinite attributes, His transcendence and immanence, and the all-pervading quality of His knowledge, reminding us of His omnipresence and omniscience.
orig: هو الأول والآخر والظاهر والباطن وهو بكل شيء عليم

translation: It is He who created the heavens and the earth in six days and then established Himself above the Throne. He knows what penetrates into the earth and what emerges from it and what descends from the heaven and what ascends therein; and He is with you wherever you are. And Allah, of what you do, is Seeing.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's omniscience and omnipresence. He is aware of all that happens in the universe, from the smallest details within the earth to the vast occurrences in the heavens. Moreover, Allah is always with His creation, observing their deeds and actions. This interpretation highlights the importance of being mindful of Allah's presence and the fact that He is constantly watching over us, which should motivate believers to perform righteous deeds and refrain from wrongdoing.
orig: هو الذي خلق السماوات والأرض في ستة أيام ثم استوى على العرش يعلم ما يلج في الأرض وما يخرج منها وما ينزل من السماء وما يعرج فيها وهو معكم أين ما كنتم والله بما تعملون بصير

translation: To Him belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth, and to Allah are returned [all] matters.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's absolute sovereignty and control over the entire universe. It reminds us that everything in existence belongs to Him alone, and that all affairs and matters ultimately return to Him for judgment and decision. This highlights the importance of recognizing Allah's supreme authority and submitting to His will, as we will all be accountable to Him in the end. It also serves as a source of comfort and reassurance for believers, knowing that no matter what challenges or difficulties they face, Allah is in control and will ensure justice prevails.
orig: له ملك السماوات والأرض وإلى الله ترجع الأمور

translation: He causes the night to enter the day and causes the day to enter the night, and he is Knowing of that within the breasts.
interpretation: This verse speaks to Allah's power and control over the universe. The alternation of night and day is a sign of His omnipotence. The phrase "causes the night to enter the day and causes the day to enter the night" refers to the gradual lengthening and shortening of the days and nights throughout the year, which is a precise system that Allah has put in place. The verse ends by affirming that Allah has full knowledge of what is in people's hearts and minds. Nothing is hidden from Him, and He is aware of all our thoughts, feelings, and intentions, whether good or bad. This should motivate us to purify our hearts and be mindful of Allah at all times.
orig: يولج الليل في النهار ويولج النهار في الليل وهو عليم بذات الصدور

translation: Believe in Allah and His Messenger and spend out of that in which He has made you successors. For those who have believed among you and spent, there will be a great reward.
interpretation: This verse encourages believers to have faith in Allah and His Messenger, and to spend from the wealth and resources that Allah has entrusted them with in His cause. It reminds us that we are mere trustees of the blessings Allah has given us in this world. Those who sincerely believe and generously spend from their wealth for the sake of Allah will be rewarded abundantly in the Hereafter. It emphasizes the importance of faith coupled with righteous actions and spending in charity, indicating that true believers are those who not only profess their faith, but also demonstrate it through their deeds and by using their God-given resources in a manner pleasing to Him.
orig: آمنوا بالله ورسوله وأنفقوا مما جعلكم مستخلفين فيه فالذين آمنوا منكم وأنفقوا لهم أجر كبير

translation: And why do you not believe in Allah while the Messenger invites you to believe in your Lord and He has taken your covenant, if you should [truly] be believers?
interpretation: This verse is questioning the disbelievers as to why they do not believe in Allah and His Messenger, when the Messenger is inviting them to faith in their Lord. It reminds them that Allah has already taken a covenant from them to believe, if they are truly believers as they claim. The implication is that true believers would readily accept the invitation to faith from Allah's Messenger, and that rejecting this invitation is a sign of ingratitude and disbelief, a violation of the covenant one has with their Lord. It is a powerful reminder of the obligation to have faith and the consequences of rejecting the call to belief.
orig: وما لكم لا تؤمنون بالله والرسول يدعوكم لتؤمنوا بربكم وقد أخذ ميثاقكم إن كنتم مؤمنين

translation: It is He who sends down upon His Servant [Muhammad] verses of clear evidence that He may bring you out from darknesses into the light. And indeed, Allah is to you Kind and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's mercy and kindness towards humanity. He sends clear revelations through His Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) to guide people out of the darkness of ignorance, disbelief, and sin, and into the light of faith, knowledge, and righteousness. The verse also highlights the role of the Prophet as a recipient and conveyor of divine messages, serving as a means for people's spiritual enlightenment and salvation. Moreover, it underscores Allah's attributes of kindness (Ra'uf) and mercifulness (Rahim), indicating His compassion and care for His servants, as He provides them with the necessary guidance to attain success in this world and the Hereafter.
orig: هو الذي ينزل على عبده آيات بينات ليخرجكم من الظلمات إلى النور وإن الله بكم لرءوف رحيم

translation: And why do you not spend in the cause of Allah while to Allah belongs the heritage of the heavens and the earth? Not equal among you are those who spent before the conquest [of Makkah] and fought [and those who did so after it]. Those are greater in degree than they who spent afterwards and fought. But to all Allah has promised the best [reward]. And Allah, with what you do, is Acquainted.
interpretation: This verse encourages believers to spend their wealth in the way of Allah, reminding them that everything in the heavens and the earth belongs to Him. It highlights the superior status of those who spent and fought for Islam before the conquest of Makkah, compared to those who did so afterwards. However, it also emphasizes that Allah has promised the best reward to all who spend and strive in His cause, regardless of when they did so. The verse underscores the importance of sincerity and sacrifice in the path of Allah, and reassures believers that He is fully aware of their actions and will reward them accordingly.
orig: وما لكم ألا تنفقوا في سبيل الله ولله ميراث السماوات والأرض لا يستوي منكم من أنفق من قبل الفتح وقاتل أولئك أعظم درجة من الذين أنفقوا من بعد وقاتلوا وكلا وعد الله الحسنى والله بما تعملون خبير

translation: Who is it that would loan Allah a goodly loan so He may multiply it for him many times over? And it is Allah who withholds and grants abundance, and to Him you will be returned.
interpretation: This verse encourages Muslims to spend in the way of Allah, with the promise that Allah will multiply their good deeds and reward them generously in the Hereafter. It emphasizes that whatever wealth we have is from Allah, and that by giving in His cause, we are not losing anything, but rather investing for our own eternal benefit. The "goodly loan" refers to sincere charity given for the sake of Allah alone, without any show or ulterior motives. The verse also reminds us that ultimately, all things return to Allah, and it is to Him that we will be accountable for how we used the blessings He bestowed upon us in this temporary worldly life.
orig: من ذا الذي يقرض الله قرضا حسنا فيضاعفه له وله أجر كريم

translation: On the Day you see the believing men and believing women, their light proceeding before them and on their right, [it will be said], "Your good tidings today are [of] gardens beneath which rivers flow, wherein you will abide eternally." That is what is the great attainment.
interpretation: This verse describes the rewards that await the righteous believers on the Day of Judgment. It emphasizes that their faith and good deeds in this world will be manifested as a guiding light that will lead them to Paradise. The mention of "gardens beneath which rivers flow" symbolizes the eternal bliss, comfort, and abundance that the believers will enjoy in the Hereafter as a result of their devotion to Allah. The verse concludes by affirming that attaining this everlasting reward is the ultimate success and the greatest achievement one can hope for, superseding any worldly gains or pleasures.
orig: يوم ترى المؤمنين والمؤمنات يسعى نورهم بين أيديهم وبأيمانهم بشراكم اليوم جنات تجري من تحتها الأنهار خالدين فيها ذلك هو الفوز العظيم

translation: On the Day the hypocrite men and hypocrite women will say to those who believed, "Wait for us that we may acquire some of your light." It will be said, "Go back behind you and seek light." And a wall will be placed between them with a door, its interior containing mercy, but on the outside of it is torment.
interpretation: This verse is referring to the Day of Judgment, when the hypocrites who pretended to be believers in this world will seek to benefit from the light of the true believers. However, they will be told to go back and find their own light, which they will not be able to do. A barrier will then be placed between the two groups, with the believers experiencing God's mercy on one side, while the hypocrites face His punishment on the other. This highlights the ultimate fate of those who are insincere in their faith and the importance of being true believers in this life.
orig: يوم يقول المنافقون والمنافقات للذين آمنوا انظرونا نقتبس من نوركم قيل ارجعوا وراءكم فالتمسوا نورا فضرب بينهم بسور له باب باطنه فيه الرحمة وظاهره من قبله العذاب

translation: They will call to them, "Were we not with you?" They will say, "Yes, but you afflicted yourselves and awaited [misfortune for us] and doubted, and wishful thinking deluded you until there came the command of Allah. And the Deceiver deceived you concerning Allah.
interpretation: This verse is referring to the Day of Judgment, when the hypocrites will call out to the believers, claiming that they were with them in the worldly life. However, the believers will respond by pointing out that the hypocrites had, in fact, deceived themselves by not being true in their faith. They had harbored doubts, waited for misfortune to befall the believers, and allowed themselves to be deluded by false hopes and desires until the decree of Allah came to pass. The "Deceiver" mentioned in this verse is Satan, who had misled the hypocrites by making them think that they could escape the consequences of their actions and that they would not be held accountable by Allah.
orig: ينادونهم ألم نكن معكم قالوا بلى ولكنكم فتنتم أنفسكم وتربصتم وارتبتم وغرتكم الأماني حتى جاء أمر الله وغركم بالله الغرور

translation: So today no ransom will be taken from you, nor from those who disbelieved. Your refuge is the Fire. It is your master, and wretched is the destination.
interpretation: This verse is a warning to the disbelievers on the Day of Judgment. It emphasizes that on that day, no amount of ransom or compensation will be accepted from them to save them from the punishment of Hell. Their ultimate abode will be the Fire, which will be their master and companion. This destination is described as the worst possible outcome, highlighting the severity and permanence of the punishment for those who rejected faith in this world. The verse serves as a reminder of the consequences of disbelief and the importance of accepting the truth before it is too late.
orig: فاليوم لا يؤخذ منكم فدية ولا من الذين كفروا مأواكم النار هي مولاكم وبئس المصير

translation: Has the time not come for those who have believed that their hearts should become humbly submissive at the remembrance of Allah and what has come down of the truth? And let them not be like those who were given the Scripture before, and a long period passed over them, so their hearts hardened; and many of them are defiantly disobedient.
interpretation: This verse is a reminder and a warning to the believers not to become complacent and heedless like the previous nations who were given divine scriptures. Despite receiving guidance, they allowed their hearts to become hardened over time due to their prolonged neglect of Allah's remembrance and the truth that was revealed to them. As a result, many of them became disobedient and strayed from the right path. The verse urges the believers to maintain a state of humility, submission, and consciousness of Allah, so that their hearts remain soft and receptive to the truth, and they do not fall into the same state of heedlessness and disobedience as the previous nations.
orig: ألم يأن للذين آمنوا أن تخشع قلوبهم لذكر الله وما نزل من الحق ولا يكونوا كالذين أوتوا الكتاب من قبل فطال عليهم الأمد فقست قلوبهم وكثير منهم فاسقون

translation: Know that Allah gives life to the earth after its death. We have made clear to you the signs that you might reason.
interpretation: This verse is a reminder of Allah's power and ability to bring life back to what was once dead. Just as Allah can resurrect the dead earth by sending down rain and causing vegetation to grow, He can also resurrect the dead on the Day of Judgment. The signs of Allah's power and might are all around us in nature, and by reflecting upon them, we can strengthen our faith and increase our understanding of His greatness. This verse encourages us to use our intellect and reason to recognize these signs and appreciate the wonder of Allah's creation.
orig: اعلموا أن الله يحيي الأرض بعد موتها قد بينا لكم الآيات لعلكم تعقلون

translation: Indeed, the men who practice charity and the women who practice charity and [they who] have loaned Allah a goodly loan - it will be multiplied for them, and they will have a noble reward.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of giving in charity and lending to Allah, which means giving for the sake of Allah without expecting worldly gains. It promises that those who sincerely give in charity and lend to Allah will have their rewards multiplied manifold by Allah's grace. The "goodly loan" mentioned here refers to spending one's wealth in the way of Allah with pure intentions. The verse also makes no distinction between men and women in their rewards for charitable giving, highlighting the equality of the genders in attaining Allah's blessings through righteous deeds. Ultimately, the verse encourages selfless generosity and promises a noble reward in the Hereafter for those who spend in Allah's cause.
orig: إن المصدقين والمصدقات وأقرضوا الله قرضا حسنا يضاعف لهم ولهم أجر كريم

translation: And those who have believed in Allah and His messengers - those are [in the ranks of] the supporters of truth and the martyrs in the sight of their Lord. For them is their reward and their light. But those who have disbelieved and denied Our verses - those are the companions of Hellfire.
interpretation: This verse highlights the great reward and honor that awaits those who sincerely believe in Allah and His messengers. They are considered the truthful ones and the martyrs, holding a high rank in Allah's sight. They will be granted their full reward in the Hereafter and will be enveloped in divine light. In contrast, those who reject faith and deny Allah's revelations will be the dwellers of the Hellfire, emphasizing the severe consequence of disbelief. This verse encourages faith, righteousness, and staying on the straight path to attain salvation and the pleasure of Allah.
orig: والذين آمنوا بالله ورسله أولئك هم الصديقون والشهداء عند ربهم لهم أجرهم ونورهم والذين كفروا وكذبوا بآياتنا أولئك أصحاب الجحيم

translation: Know that the life of this world is only play and amusement, pomp and mutual boasting among you, and rivalry in respect of wealth and children. (It is) as the likeness of vegetation after rain, thereof the growth is pleasing to the tiller; afterwards it dries up and you see it turning yellow; then it becomes straw. But in the Hereafter (there is) a severe torment (for the disbelievers), and (there is) Forgiveness from Allah and (His) Good Pleasure (for the believers). And the life of this world is only a deceiving enjoyment.
interpretation: This verse reminds us of the fleeting and ultimately insignificant nature of worldly life. It compares the temporary allure and distractions of this world, such as play, amusement, luxury, boasting, and competition in wealth and children, to the short-lived cycle of vegetation after rainfall. Just as the crops sprout, look appealing for a while, and then wither away into mere straw, the pursuits and attachments of this world are eventually rendered worthless. The verse warns of severe punishment in the Hereafter for those who are deceived by worldly life, while promising forgiveness and pleasure from Allah for the believers. It emphasizes that the life of this world is nothing but a deceptive enjoyment, urging us to focus on our eternal destination rather than temporary worldly gains.
orig: اعلموا أنما الحياة الدنيا لعب ولهو وزينة وتفاخر بينكم وتكاثر في الأموال والأولاد كمثل غيث أعجب الكفار نباته ثم يهيج فتراه مصفرا ثم يكون حطاما وفي الآخرة عذاب شديد ومغفرة من الله ورضوان وما الحياة الدنيا إلا متاع الغرور

translation: Race toward forgiveness from your Lord and a Garden whose width is like the width of the heavens and earth, prepared for those who believed in Allah and His messengers. That is the bounty of Allah which He gives to whom He wills, and Allah is the possessor of great bounty.
interpretation: This verse encourages believers to hasten towards seeking forgiveness from Allah and striving for Paradise, which is described as being as vast as the heavens and the earth. This immense reward has been prepared for those who have faith in Allah and His messengers. The verse emphasizes that attaining this reward is a great blessing and bounty from Allah, which He bestows upon whomever He wills. It also highlights Allah's infinite generosity and mercy towards His believing servants, motivating them to increase their faith and good deeds.
orig: سابقوا إلى مغفرة من ربكم وجنة عرضها كعرض السماء والأرض أعدت للذين آمنوا بالله ورسله ذلك فضل الله يؤتيه من يشاء والله ذو الفضل العظيم

translation: No disaster strikes upon the earth or among yourselves except that it is in a register before We bring it into being - indeed that, for Allah, is easy.
interpretation: This verse conveys the idea of divine predestination in Islam. It asserts that all calamities and afflictions, whether affecting the world at large or individuals, are preordained and written in a divine record before they occur. This concept emphasizes Allah's omniscience and sovereignty over all affairs. The verse also suggests that such predestination is effortless for Allah, highlighting His power and control over the universe. It serves as a reminder to believers that hardships are ultimately part of God's greater plan, encouraging patience, trust, and submission to the divine will.
orig: ما أصاب من مصيبة في الأرض ولا في أنفسكم إلا في كتاب من قبل أن نبرأها إن ذلك على الله يسير

translation: In order that you not despair over what has eluded you and not exult [in pride] over what He has given you. And Allah does not like everyone self-deluded and boastful.
interpretation: This verse is a reminder for believers to maintain a balanced perspective in life. We should not be overly saddened by what we have lost or missed out on, nor should we become arrogant and boastful about our achievements and blessings. True contentment comes from accepting Allah's decree and remaining humble in all circumstances. The verse also highlights that Allah dislikes those who are self-deluded and boastful, as these traits are indicative of ingratitude and a lack of faith. Instead, we should strive to be grateful for what we have been given and remain steadfast in the face of adversity, trusting in Allah's plan for us.
orig: لكيلا تأسوا على ما فاتكم ولا تفرحوا بما آتاكم والله لا يحب كل مختال فخور

translation: Those who are stingy and enjoin upon [other] people stinginess. And whoever turns away - then indeed, Allah is the Free of need, the Praiseworthy.
interpretation: This verse is a warning against stinginess and miserliness. It condemns those who are not only miserly themselves but also encourage others to be stingy. The verse reminds us that if someone turns away from the path of generosity and kindness, it does not affect Allah in any way, for He is self-sufficient and worthy of all praise. The verse emphasizes the importance of being generous and charitable, and discourages the attitude of withholding wealth and resources from those in need. It highlights that such behavior is displeasing to Allah, who is the ultimate source of all bounties and blessings.
orig: الذين يبخلون ويأمرون الناس بالبخل ومن يتول فإن الله هو الغني الحميد

translation: We have already sent Our messengers with clear evidences and sent down with them the Scripture and the balance that the people may maintain [their affairs] in justice. And We sent down iron, wherein is great military might and benefits for the people, and so that Allah may make evident those who support Him and His messengers unseen. Indeed, Allah is Powerful and Exalted in Might.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of justice and the role of divine guidance in establishing it. Allah has sent messengers with clear proofs and revelations to guide humanity towards righteousness. The "balance" mentioned refers to the principles of justice and fairness that should govern human affairs. The verse also highlights the significance of iron, which symbolizes strength, both in terms of military might and the benefits it provides to people in their daily lives. Ultimately, Allah tests and distinguishes those who sincerely support Him and His messengers, even without seeing them directly. This demonstrates Allah's power and might in guiding and aiding the believers.
orig: لقد أرسلنا رسلنا بالبينات وأنزلنا معهم الكتاب والميزان ليقوم الناس بالقسط وأنزلنا الحديد فيه بأس شديد ومنافع للناس وليعلم الله من ينصره ورسله بالغيب إن الله قوي عزيز

translation: And indeed, We sent Noah and Abraham and We placed in their descendants prophethood and scripture; and among them is he who is guided, but many of them are defiantly disobedient.
interpretation: This verse highlights the continuity of Allah's message and the important role of prophethood in guiding humanity. The descendants of Noah and Abraham were blessed with the honor of prophethood and divine scriptures, indicating the significance of their lineage in the history of faith. However, the verse also acknowledges that while some of their descendants followed the right path, many others deviated and became disobedient to Allah's commands. This serves as a reminder that being a descendant of a prophet does not guarantee righteousness, and that each individual is responsible for their own actions and choices. The verse emphasizes the importance of staying on the straight path and avoiding transgression, regardless of one's lineage or background.
orig: ولقد أرسلنا نوحا وإبراهيم وجعلنا في ذريتهما النبوة والكتاب فمنهم مهتد وكثير منهم فاسقون

translation: Then We sent following their footsteps Our messengers and followed [them] with Jesus, the son of Mary, and gave him the Gospel. And We placed in the hearts of those who followed him compassion and mercy and monasticism, which they innovated; We did not prescribe it for them except [that they did so] seeking the approval of Allah. But they did not observe it with due observance. So We gave the ones who believed among them their reward, but many of them are defiantly disobedient.
interpretation: This verse highlights the continuity of God's message through various prophets, with a specific focus on Jesus and his followers. It suggests that the true essence of religious devotion lies in seeking God's pleasure rather than adhering to self-imposed practices. The verse also acknowledges that while some of Jesus' followers were sincere in their faith and were rewarded accordingly, others strayed from the righteous path. This interpretation emphasizes the importance of sincere devotion and the pursuit of God's approval, rather than mere adherence to outward religious practices.
orig: ثم قفينا على آثارهم برسلنا وقفينا بعيسى ابن مريم وآتيناه الإنجيل وجعلنا في قلوب الذين اتبعوه رأفة ورحمة ورهبانية ابتدعوها ما كتبناها عليهم إلا ابتغاء رضوان الله فما رعوها حق رعايتها فآتينا الذين آمنوا منهم أجرهم وكثير منهم فاسقون

translation: O you who have believed, fear Allah and believe in His Messenger; He will [then] give you a double portion of His mercy and make for you a light by which you will walk and forgive you; and Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse is calling upon the believers to have consciousness of Allah (taqwa) and to believe in His Messenger Muhammad (peace be upon him). Allah promises that those who do so will be granted a double share of His mercy. Additionally, Allah will provide them with a light by which they can walk, meaning guidance to navigate through life. Furthermore, Allah will forgive their sins, emphasizing His attributes of forgiveness and mercy to those who are mindful of Him and follow His Messenger. This verse highlights the importance of faith, obedience to Allah, and adherence to the teachings of Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) in attaining Allah's blessings, guidance, and forgiveness.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا اتقوا الله وآمنوا برسوله يؤتكم كفلين من رحمته ويجعل لكم نورا تمشون به ويغفر لكم والله غفور رحيم

translation: So that the People of the Book may know that they have no power over anything of the bounty of Allah, and that [all] bounty is in the hand of Allah; He gives it to whom He wills. And Allah is the possessor of great bounty.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that all blessings and favors come from Allah alone, and no one has any power or control over them. It serves as a reminder to the People of the Book (Jews and Christians) that they should not feel entitled to Allah's bounty or think that they have a monopoly over His favors. The verse highlights the absolute sovereignty of Allah in granting His blessings to whomever He chooses, and that He alone is the possessor of infinite grace and generosity. It encourages humility and gratitude towards Allah, recognizing that all good things come from Him and that no one can claim to have earned or deserved His favors.
orig: لئلا يعلم أهل الكتاب ألا يقدرون على شيء من فضل الله وأن الفضل بيد الله يؤتيه من يشاء والله ذو الفضل العظيم

translation: Allah has indeed heard the words of the woman who pleads with you concerning her husband and complains to Allah. And Allah hears your dialogue. Surely Allah is All-Hearing, All-Seeing.
interpretation: This verse is addressing a specific incident where a woman came to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) to complain about her husband and seek divine intervention. The interpretation is that Allah is aware of all our conversations, pleas and supplications. Nothing escapes His knowledge, whether it is done in public or private. The verse emphasizes two key attributes of Allah - As-Sami' (the All-Hearing) and Al-Baseer (the All-Seeing). It reassures the believers that Allah listens to their prayers and is fully aware of their circumstances. They can turn to Him with their worries and concerns, knowing that He will respond in the way that is best for them in this life and the next.
orig: قد سمع الله قول التي تجادلك في زوجها وتشتكي إلى الله والله يسمع تحاوركما إن الله سميع بصير

translation: Those who pronounce zihar among you [to separate] from their wives - they are not [consequently] their mothers. Their mothers are none but those who gave birth to them. And indeed, they are saying an objectionable statement and a falsehood. But indeed, Allah is Pardoning and Forgiving.
interpretation: This verse addresses the pre-Islamic practice of zihar, where a man would say to his wife, "You are to me like the back of my mother," thereby prohibiting himself from intimate relations with her. The verse clarifies that this statement does not actually make the wife like the man's mother, as his true mother is only the woman who gave birth to him. It emphasizes that such statements are objectionable and false. However, the verse concludes by affirming that Allah is Pardoning and Forgiving, suggesting that even though this practice is wrong, Allah's mercy and forgiveness are available for those who repent and correct their behavior.
orig: الذين يظاهرون منكم من نسائهم ما هن أمهاتهم إن أمهاتهم إلا اللائي ولدنهم وإنهم ليقولون منكرا من القول وزورا وإن الله لعفو غفور

translation: And those who pronounce zhihar from their wives and then [wish to] go back on what they said - then [there must be] the freeing of a slave before they touch one another. That is what you are admonished thereby; and Allah is Acquainted with what you do.
interpretation: This verse addresses the pre-Islamic practice of zhihar, where a man would say to his wife, "You are to me like the back of my mother." This was considered a form of divorce. However, if the man wished to retract his statement and return to his wife, he would have to free a slave as expiation before resuming marital relations. This served as a deterrent to using such statements lightly and thoughtlessly. The verse emphasizes that Allah is fully aware of people's actions and intentions, encouraging them to be mindful and conscientious in their behavior and treatment of others, especially their spouses.
orig: والذين يظاهرون من نسائهم ثم يعودون لما قالوا فتحرير رقبة من قبل أن يتماسا ذلكم توعظون به والله بما تعملون خبير

translation: But whoever cannot find [a slave] - then a fast for two months consecutively before they touch one another; and he who is unable - then the feeding of sixty poor persons. That is for you to believe [completely] in Allah and His Messenger; and those are the limits [set by] Allah. And for the disbelievers is a painful punishment.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of adhering to Allah's laws and the consequences of disobedience. It outlines the options for expiation if one cannot free a slave: fasting for two consecutive months before engaging in intimacy, or feeding sixty needy individuals. These acts demonstrate complete faith in Allah and His Messenger. The mention of painful punishment for disbelievers serves as a reminder that Allah's boundaries must be respected, and that those who reject His guidance will face severe consequences in the Hereafter.
orig: فمن لم يجد فصيام شهرين متتابعين من قبل أن يتماسا فمن لم يستطع فإطعام ستين مسكينا ذلك لتؤمنوا بالله ورسوله وتلك حدود الله وللكافرين عذاب أليم

translation: Indeed, those who oppose Allah and His Messenger are abased as those before them were abased. And We have certainly sent down verses of clear evidence. And for the disbelievers is a humiliating punishment.
interpretation: This verse warns those who oppose and challenge Allah and His Messenger (Muhammad) that they will face disgrace and humiliation, just as those who opposed the truth in the past were disgraced. Allah emphasizes that He has revealed clear signs and evidence of the truth, leaving no excuse for disbelief. Those who persist in their disbelief and rejection of the truth will face a degrading punishment in the Hereafter, which will be a source of shame and humiliation for them. This interpretation highlights the consequences of opposing the divine message and the importance of accepting the clear evidence that Allah has provided through His revelations.
orig: إن الذين يحادون الله ورسوله كبتوا كما كبت الذين من قبلهم وقد أنزلنا آيات بينات وللكافرين عذاب مهين

translation: The Day when Allah will resurrect them all and inform them of what they did. Allah had enumerated it, while they forgot it; and Allah is, over all things, Witness.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the concept of the Day of Judgment, when Allah will resurrect all humans and make them fully aware of their deeds in this worldly life. It highlights Allah's omniscience, as He has recorded every action, even those that people have forgotten. The verse also stresses Allah's attribute as the Witness over everything, implying that no deed, whether good or bad, is hidden from Him. This serves as a reminder for believers to be mindful of their actions, as they will be held accountable for them in the Hereafter.
orig: يوم يبعثهم الله جميعا فينبئهم بما عملوا أحصاه الله ونسوه والله على كل شيء شهيد

translation: Have you not considered that Allah knows what is in the heavens and what is on the earth? There is in no private conversation three but that He is the fourth of them, nor are there five but that He is the sixth of them - and no less than that and no more except that He is with them [in knowledge] wherever they are. Then He will inform them of what they did, on the Day of Resurrection. Indeed Allah is, of all things, Knowing.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the omniscience and omnipresence of Allah. It reminds us that Allah is aware of everything that happens in the heavens and on earth, even the most private conversations between individuals. Whether it is a conversation between three, five, or any number of people, Allah is always present with them, having complete knowledge of their discussions and actions. The verse also serves as a warning that on the Day of Judgment, Allah will inform every individual of their deeds, as He is All-Knowing of everything. This encourages believers to be mindful of their actions and words, even in private, as nothing escapes Allah's knowledge.
orig: ألم تر أن الله يعلم ما في السماوات وما في الأرض ما يكون من نجوى ثلاثة إلا هو رابعهم ولا خمسة إلا هو سادسهم ولا أدنى من ذلك ولا أكثر إلا هو معهم أين ما كانوا ثم ينبئهم بما عملوا يوم القيامة إن الله بكل شيء عليم

translation: Have you not considered those who were forbidden from private conversation, then they return to that which they were forbidden and converse among themselves about sin and aggression and disobedience to the Messenger? And when they come to you, they greet you with that [word] by which Allah does not greet you and say among themselves, "Why does Allah not punish us for what we say?" Sufficient for them is Hell, which they will [enter to] burn, and wretched is the destination.
interpretation: This verse is a warning to those who engage in secret conversations and plotting against the Prophet and the Muslim community. Despite being forbidden from such behavior, they persist in it, discussing sinful and aggressive acts. When they come to the Prophet, they greet him insincerely, in a manner not approved by Allah. They arrogantly question why Allah does not punish them for their words and actions. The verse states that Hell is sufficient punishment for them, emphasizing the severity of their wrongdoing and the consequences they will face in the Hereafter. It serves as a reminder to the believers to refrain from such behavior and to be sincere in their dealings with the Prophet and the Muslim community.
orig: ألم تر إلى الذين نهوا عن النجوى ثم يعودون لما نهوا عنه ويتناجون بالإثم والعدوان ومعصيت الرسول وإذا جاءوك حيوك بما لم يحيك به الله ويقولون في أنفسهم لولا يعذبنا الله بما نقول حسبهم جهنم يصلونها فبئس المصير

translation: O you who have believed, when you converse privately, do not converse about sin and aggression and disobedience to the Messenger but converse about righteousness and piety. And fear Allah, to whom you will be gathered.
interpretation: This verse is advising the believers to be mindful of their private conversations and to avoid discussing matters that are sinful, aggressive, or disobedient to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him). Instead, they should focus their private discussions on matters of righteousness, piety, and goodness. The verse also reminds the believers to have taqwa (consciousness) of Allah, recognizing that they will all be gathered before Him on the Day of Judgment and held accountable for their deeds and words. It emphasizes the importance of using our speech in a way that is pleasing to Allah and beneficial to others, even in private settings where we may feel less inhibited. Ultimately, this verse encourages us to align our private conduct with our public persona as believers, striving for consistency in our character and actions.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا إذا تناجيتم فلا تتناجوا بالإثم والعدوان ومعصيت الرسول وتناجوا بالبر والتقوى واتقوا الله الذي إليه تحشرون

translation: Private conversations are only [inspired] by Satan to grieve those who have believed, but he will not harm them at all except by permission of Allah. And upon Allah let the believers rely.
interpretation: This verse warns believers that secret conversations and whispers that aim to cause harm or grief to others are inspired by Satan. However, it also reassures them that Satan cannot harm them without Allah's permission. The verse emphasizes the importance of putting one's trust in Allah and relying on Him alone, especially in the face of adversity or ill intentions from others. It encourages believers to remain steadfast in their faith and not be swayed or discouraged by the plots or schemes of those who wish them harm, knowing that ultimately, everything happens by Allah's will and that He is sufficient as a protector and guardian for those who believe in Him.
orig: إنما النجوى من الشيطان ليحزن الذين آمنوا وليس بضارهم شيئا إلا بإذن الله وعلى الله فليتوكل المؤمنون

translation: O you who have believed, when you are told, "Space yourselves" in assemblies, then make space; Allah will make space for you. And when you are told, "Arise," then arise; Allah will raise those who have believed among you and those who were given knowledge, by degrees. And Allah is Acquainted with what you do.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of humility, respect, and the pursuit of knowledge in Islam. When gathered in assemblies or meetings, Muslims are encouraged to make space for others, symbolizing the need to be considerate and accommodating. The verse also instructs believers to rise when called upon, which can be interpreted as a call to action and readiness to serve the community. Furthermore, Allah promises to elevate the status of those who have faith and those who seek knowledge, highlighting the significance of education and spiritual growth in a Muslim's life. This verse reminds Muslims that their actions and intentions are known to Allah, encouraging them to act with sincerity and righteousness in all aspects of life.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا إذا قيل لكم تفسحوا في المجالس فافسحوا يفسح الله لكم وإذا قيل انشزوا فانشزوا يرفع الله الذين آمنوا منكم والذين أوتوا العلم درجات والله بما تعملون خبير

translation: O you who have believed, when you [wish to] privately consult the Messenger, present before your consultation a charity. That is better for you and purer. But if you find not [the means] - then indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse is teaching the believers the etiquette of privately consulting with the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him). It instructs them to give charity before having a private conversation with him. The wisdom behind this is that it purifies the intention of the person seeking counsel, as they are willing to make a financial sacrifice for the sake of gaining guidance and knowledge. It also serves as a means of supporting the poor and needy. However, Allah acknowledges that some people may not have the means to give charity, and reassures them that He is Forgiving and Merciful, and will not hold them accountable if they are unable to do so. This demonstrates Allah's compassion and understanding of the varied circumstances of His servants.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا إذا ناجيتم الرسول فقدموا بين يدي نجواكم صدقة ذلك خير لكم وأطهر فإن لم تجدوا فإن الله غفور رحيم

translation: Is it that you are afraid of spending in charity before your private consultation? If then you do not do it and Allah has forgiven you, then establish prayer and give zakah and obey Allah and His Messenger. And Allah is Aware of what you do.
interpretation: This verse is addressing the believers who were hesitant to give charity before consulting privately with the Prophet. It suggests that if they failed to do so, they should not despair, as Allah has forgiven them. However, they are reminded to fulfill their religious obligations such as prayer, giving zakah, and obeying Allah and His Messenger. The verse emphasizes that Allah is fully aware of all their actions, both good and bad, and they should strive to please Him through their deeds.
orig: أأشفقتم أن تقدموا بين يدي نجواكم صدقات فإذ لم تفعلوا وتاب الله عليكم فأقيموا الصلاة وآتوا الزكاة وأطيعوا الله ورسوله والله خبير بما تعملون

translation: Have you not seen those who turn in friendship to a people upon whom is Allah's Wrath? They are neither of you nor of them, and they swear to falsehood while they know.
interpretation: This verse is criticizing the hypocrites who outwardly claim to be Muslims but secretly maintain alliances with the enemies of Islam, in this case the Jews, upon whom Allah's anger descended due to their rejection of His messages and Prophets. These hypocrites are not truly part of the Muslim community nor the Jewish community, but they straddle between the two, swearing false oaths of loyalty while being fully aware of their own deceit. It highlights their duplicitous nature and the severity of allying with those who have earned Allah's displeasure.
orig: ألم تر إلى الذين تولوا قوما غضب الله عليهم ما هم منكم ولا منهم ويحلفون على الكذب وهم يعلمون

translation: Allah has prepared for them a severe punishment. Indeed, it was evil that they used to do.
interpretation: This verse warns that those who persist in evil deeds and reject the truth will face severe consequences in the Hereafter. Allah has prepared a painful punishment for them because of their misdeeds and transgressions in this worldly life. It emphasizes that evil actions will not go unpunished and that divine justice will ultimately prevail. The verse serves as a strong reminder for individuals to be mindful of their conduct and to abstain from wrongdoing.
orig: أعد الله لهم عذابا شديدا إنهم ساء ما كانوا يعملون

translation: They have made their oaths a screen (for their misdeeds): thus they obstruct (men) from the Path of Allah: therefore shall they have a humiliating Penalty.
interpretation: This verse refers to the hypocrites who swear false oaths to deceive others and hinder them from the path of Allah. They use their oaths as a cover to conceal their true intentions and misdeeds. By doing so, they create obstacles that prevent people from following the right path and guidance of Allah. As a consequence of their deceit and obstruction, they will face a humiliating punishment in the Hereafter. This highlights the severity of using oaths falsely and deliberately leading others astray from the truth.
orig: اتخذوا أيمانهم جنة فصدوا عن سبيل الله فلهم عذاب مهين

translation: Their wealth and their children will not avail them against Allah at all. Those are the companions of the Fire; they will abide therein eternally.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the ultimate worthlessness of worldly possessions and progeny in the face of Allah's judgment. Those who have rejected faith and instead put their trust in fleeting worldly gains will find that nothing can protect them from the consequences of their disbelief. Their eternal abode will be the Fire of Hell, where they will remain forever. This interpretation highlights the importance of prioritizing one's relationship with Allah over all else, as even the most valued worldly attachments cannot secure salvation in the Hereafter.
orig: لن تغني عنهم أموالهم ولا أولادهم من الله شيئا أولئك أصحاب النار هم فيها خالدون

translation: On the Day when Allah will resurrect them all, they will swear to Him as they swear to you, thinking that they are upon something. Unquestionably, it is they who are the liars.
interpretation: This verse refers to the hypocrites who outwardly profess faith but inwardly harbor disbelief. On the Day of Judgment, they will swear to Allah that they were believers just as they used to falsely swear to the Muslims in this world. They deceive themselves, thinking that their false oaths and pretenses will benefit them. However, Allah emphatically declares that they are indeed the liars. Their duplicity and false oaths will be of no avail on the Day when all secrets will be laid bare, and they will face the consequences of their hypocrisy and deception.
orig: يوم يبعثهم الله جميعا فيحلفون له كما يحلفون لكم ويحسبون أنهم على شيء ألا إنهم هم الكاذبون

translation: Satan has overcome them and made them forget the remembrance of Allah. Those are the party of Satan. Unquestionably, the party of Satan - they will be the losers.
interpretation: This verse warns that those who succumb to the temptations and whispers of Satan, allowing him to lead them astray from the remembrance of Allah, have essentially joined the party of Satan. They have been deceived and overcome by his evil influence. As a result, they will ultimately be among the losers in both this world and the Hereafter, because they have turned away from the path of guidance and righteousness that comes from keeping Allah in their hearts and minds. It emphasizes the grave spiritual consequences of forgetting Allah and following the footsteps of Satan.
orig: استحوذ عليهم الشيطان فأنساهم ذكر الله أولئك حزب الشيطان ألا إن حزب الشيطان هم الخاسرون

translation: Indeed, those who oppose Allah and His Messenger - those will be among the most humiliated.
interpretation: This verse warns that those who actively work against Allah and His Messenger Muhammad (peace be upon him) will be among the lowest of the low, utterly disgraced and humiliated in this world and the Hereafter. It emphasizes the severity of opposing the divine message and the ignominy that awaits those who defiantly challenge God's authority and the guidance brought by His Prophet. The fate of such opponents is utter humiliation and abasement as a consequence of their arrogant rejection of truth.
orig: إن الذين يحادون الله ورسوله أولئك في الأذلين

translation: Allah has written, "I will surely overcome, I and My messengers." Indeed, Allah is Powerful and Exalted in Might.
interpretation: This verse asserts the ultimate victory and triumph of Allah's cause and His messengers over all opposition and challenges. It emphasizes the invincibility of Allah's power and might, indicating that no force can overcome His will and decree. The verse instills confidence and hope in the believers, assuring them that despite the challenges and hardships they may face in supporting Allah's cause, the final outcome will be in their favor. It encourages them to remain steadfast in their faith and to persevere in the face of adversity, knowing that Allah's support and victory is with them.
orig: كتب الله لأغلبن أنا ورسلي إن الله قوي عزيز

translation: You will not find a people who believe in Allah and the Last Day having affection for those who oppose Allah and His Messenger, even if they were their fathers or their sons or their brothers or their kindred. Those - He has decreed within their hearts faith and supported them with spirit from Him. And We will admit them to gardens beneath which rivers flow, wherein they abide eternally. Allah is pleased with them, and they are pleased with Him - those are the party of Allah. Unquestionably, the party of Allah - they are the successful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of loyalty to Allah and His Messenger above all else, even family ties. True believers cannot have love or affection for those who oppose Allah and His Prophet, regardless of their relationship. Allah has strengthened the faith of these believers in their hearts and will reward them with Paradise for their unwavering devotion. They are considered the party of Allah, the successful ones who have earned His pleasure. The verse highlights that one's allegiance should be to Allah first and foremost, superseding all other loyalties.
orig: لا تجد قوما يؤمنون بالله واليوم الآخر يوادون من حاد الله ورسوله ولو كانوا آباءهم أو أبناءهم أو إخوانهم أو عشيرتهم أولئك كتب في قلوبهم الإيمان وأيدهم بروح منه ويدخلهم جنات تجري من تحتها الأنهار خالدين فيها رضي الله عنهم ورضوا عنه أولئك حزب الله ألا إن حزب الله هم المفلحون

translation: Whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth exalts Allah, and He is the Exalted in Might, the Wise.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute sovereignty and supremacy of Allah over all creation. Everything in the universe, whether in the heavens or on earth, glorifies and praises Him. This exaltation is a testament to His might and wisdom, which are unparalleled. It serves as a reminder for humans to acknowledge His greatness and submit to His will, as all of creation inherently recognizes and worships Him. The verse also highlights that Allah's power and wisdom are not limited to any realm, but encompass the entire universe.
orig: سبح لله ما في السماوات وما في الأرض وهو العزيز الحكيم

translation: It is He who expelled the ones who disbelieved among the People of the Scripture from their homes at the first gathering. You did not think they would leave, and they thought that their fortresses would protect them from Allah; but [the decree of] Allah came upon them from where they had not expected, and He cast terror into their hearts [so] they destroyed their houses by their [own] hands and the hands of the believers. So take warning, O people of vision.
interpretation: This verse refers to the expulsion of the Jewish tribe of Banu Nadir from Medina. Despite their fortifications and presumed security, Allah's decree came upon them unexpectedly, instilling fear in their hearts. As a result, they were forced to dismantle their own homes, with the help of the Muslims. This event serves as a lesson for those who have insight and understanding, demonstrating Allah's power and the consequences of disbelief and betrayal. It highlights the importance of faith, loyalty, and the realization that no worldly strength or security can withstand Allah's will.
orig: هو الذي أخرج الذين كفروا من أهل الكتاب من ديارهم لأول الحشر ما ظننتم أن يخرجوا وظنوا أنهم مانعتهم حصونهم من الله فأتاهم الله من حيث لم يحتسبوا وقذف في قلوبهم الرعب يخربون بيوتهم بأيديهم وأيدي المؤمنين فاعتبروا يا أولي الأبصار

translation: And if Allah had not decreed for them evacuation, He would have punished them in this world, and for them in the Hereafter is the punishment of the Fire.
interpretation: This verse suggests that if it were not for Allah's decree allowing the Jews to be expelled from Medina, He would have punished them in this worldly life for their treachery and opposition to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him). However, they will still face the punishment of the Hellfire in the Hereafter for their actions. This highlights the gravity of their offenses and the justice of Allah in dealing with those who oppose His messengers and religion, giving them respite in this life but ultimately holding them accountable in the next.
orig: ولولا أن كتب الله عليهم الجلاء لعذبهم في الدنيا ولهم في الآخرة عذاب النار

translation: That is because they opposed Allah and His Messenger. And whoever opposes Allah - then indeed, Allah is severe in penalty.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the severe consequences of opposing or defying Allah and His Messenger. It suggests that those who choose to challenge or resist the will of Allah and the teachings of His Prophet will face a harsh punishment from Allah Himself. The interpretation underscores the importance of obedience, submission, and alignment with the divine message in order to avoid incurring Allah's displeasure and the resulting penalties in this life and the hereafter. It serves as a strong warning against knowingly contradicting or acting against the commandments of Allah and the guidance provided through His Messenger.
orig: ذلك بأنهم شاقوا الله ورسوله ومن يشاق الله فإن الله شديد العقاب

translation: Whatever you have cut down of [their] palm trees or left standing on their trunks - it was by permission of Allah and so He would disgrace the defiantly disobedient.
interpretation: This verse refers to the incident during the Battle of Banu Nadir, when the Muslims cut down some of the palm trees belonging to the Jewish tribe. The verse explains that this action was permitted by Allah in order to weaken and disgrace those who were disobedient and opposed to the message of Islam. It highlights the idea that whatever happens, whether good or bad from a worldly perspective, occurs by the will and permission of Allah for a greater purpose, such as exposing the wrongdoers and giving victory to the believers.
orig: ما قطعتم من لينة أو تركتموها قائمة على أصولها فبإذن الله وليخزي الفاسقين

translation: And what Allah restored to His Messenger from them - you did not spur for it [in an expedition] any horses or camels, but Allah gives His messengers power over whom He wills, and Allah is over all things competent.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the victory and spoils of war obtained by the Muslims were not due to their own military strength or efforts, but rather due to Allah's favor and support. It underscores the idea that success comes from Allah's help and not mere human endeavors. The verse also highlights the authority and power that Allah grants to His messengers over whomever He wills, demonstrating His absolute control and might over all affairs. It serves as a reminder to the believers to put their trust in Allah and recognize that He alone is the source of all victories and blessings.
orig: وما أفاء الله على رسوله منهم فما أوجفتم عليه من خيل ولا ركاب ولكن الله يسلط رسله على من يشاء والله على كل شيء قدير

translation: What Allah has bestowed upon His Messenger from the people of the towns belongs to Allah, and to the Messenger, and to the near of kin, and to the orphans, and to the needy, and to the wayfarer, so that it may not circulate between the rich among you. And whatever the Messenger gives you, take it, and whatever he forbids you from, abstain from it, and fear Allah. Indeed, Allah is severe in punishment.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the fair distribution of war spoils and resources, ensuring that wealth does not remain concentrated among the rich. It highlights the importance of obeying the Prophet's commands and prohibitions, as he guides the believers according to Allah's will. The verse also stresses the importance of having consciousness (taqwa) of Allah and fearing His punishment for disobedience. It underscores the concept of social and economic justice in Islam, where the needs of the poor, orphans, and travelers are taken into consideration, and the authority of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) in guiding the Muslim community is affirmed.
orig: ما أفاء الله على رسوله من أهل القرى فلله وللرسول ولذي القربى واليتامى والمساكين وابن السبيل كي لا يكون دولة بين الأغنياء منكم وما آتاكم الرسول فخذوه وما نهاكم عنه فانتهوا واتقوا الله إن الله شديد العقاب

translation: For the poor emigrants who were expelled from their homes and their properties, seeking bounty from Allah and [His] approval and supporting Allah and His Messenger, [there is also a share]. Those are the truthful.
interpretation: This verse highlights the virtues and sincerity of the poor emigrants who were forced to leave their homes and possessions behind for the sake of their faith. They sought Allah's favor and pleasure, and they supported His cause and His Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him). Despite their hardships and sacrifices, they remained steadfast in their belief and loyalty. The verse emphasizes that these individuals are the epitome of truthfulness and deserve a share in the distribution of resources. It serves as a reminder of the importance of sacrificing for one's faith and the rewards that await those who remain sincere and devoted to Allah's path.
orig: للفقراء المهاجرين الذين أخرجوا من ديارهم وأموالهم يبتغون فضلا من الله ورضوانا وينصرون الله ورسوله أولئك هم الصادقون

translation: And those who had settled in the homeland and [had abided] in faith before them love those who emigrated to them, and do not find in their breasts any want for what these [emigrants] have been given, but give them preference over their own selves, even though they be in privation. And whoever is saved from the niggardliness of his own soul - it is they who are the successful.
interpretation: This verse highlights the virtuous qualities of the Ansar, the residents of Madinah who welcomed and supported the Muhajirun, the emigrants from Makkah. Despite their own needs and limited resources, the Ansar selflessly gave preference to the Muhajirun, sharing their possessions and ensuring their well-being. This act of generosity and sacrifice demonstrates the true essence of brotherhood and solidarity among the early Muslim community. The verse emphasizes that those who overcome their inner desires and selfishness, prioritizing the needs of others, are the ones who will attain true success and salvation in the sight of Allah.
orig: والذين تبوءوا الدار والإيمان من قبلهم يحبون من هاجر إليهم ولا يجدون في صدورهم حاجة مما أوتوا ويؤثرون على أنفسهم ولو كان بهم خصاصة ومن يوق شح نفسه فأولئك هم المفلحون

translation: And those who came after them say, "Our Lord, forgive us and our brothers who preceded us in faith and put not in our hearts [any] resentment toward those who have believed. Our Lord, indeed You are Kind and Merciful."
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of unity, compassion, and forgiveness among believers. Those who come later should pray for the forgiveness of their fellow believers who preceded them in faith, and they should harbor no ill feelings or resentment towards them. Instead, they should seek Allah's mercy and kindness for themselves and their brothers and sisters in faith. This verse emphasizes the need for a strong, cohesive Muslim community that supports one another and seeks each other's well-being, both in this world and in the hereafter.
orig: والذين جاءوا من بعدهم يقولون ربنا اغفر لنا ولإخواننا الذين سبقونا بالإيمان ولا تجعل في قلوبنا غلا للذين آمنوا ربنا إنك رءوف رحيم

translation: Have you not considered those who practice hypocrisy, saying to their brothers who have disbelieved among the People of the Scripture, "If you are expelled, we will surely leave with you, and we will not obey, in regard to you, anyone - ever; and if you are fought, we will surely aid you." But Allah testifies that they are liars.
interpretation: This verse is referring to the hypocrites who pretended to be Muslims but secretly supported the disbelievers. They made false promises to their allies among the People of the Book (Jews and Christians), assuring them that if they were expelled from Medina, the hypocrites would leave with them and never obey the Muslims. They also claimed that if the disbelievers were attacked, the hypocrites would come to their aid. However, Allah exposes their lies and affirms that they are insincere in their promises, as they are only concerned with their own interests and self-preservation.
orig: ألم تر إلى الذين نافقوا يقولون لإخوانهم الذين كفروا من أهل الكتاب لئن أخرجتم لنخرجن معكم ولا نطيع فيكم أحدا أبدا وإن قوتلتم لننصرنكم والله يشهد إنهم لكاذبون

translation: If they are expelled, they will not go out with them, and if they are fought, they will not aid them. And [even] if they should aid them, they will surely turn their backs; then [thereafter] they will not be aided.
interpretation: This verse is referring to the hypocrites who claimed to be allies of the Muslims but were secretly plotting against them. Allah is saying that even if these hypocrites were expelled from Medina along with the Jews, they would not actually go with them or help them. And even if they did try to help them, they would quickly turn their backs and flee, and then they would not be helped by anyone. This highlights the cowardice and disloyalty of the hypocrites, and shows that their supposed alliance with the enemies of Islam is meaningless and insincere.
orig: لئن أخرجوا لا يخرجون معهم ولئن قوتلوا لا ينصرونهم ولئن نصروهم ليولن الأدبار ثم لا ينصرون

translation: Indeed, you [believers] are more fearful within their breasts than Allah. That is because they are a people who do not understand.
interpretation: This verse suggests that the disbelievers fear the believers more than they fear Allah. Their lack of understanding and faith in Allah causes them to have misplaced fear. They are more concerned with worldly threats than the consequences of disobeying Allah. It highlights the ignorance and misguided priorities of those who reject faith, as they fail to grasp the true power and authority of Allah. The believers, on the other hand, have a proper understanding of Allah's might and therefore fear Him above all else.
orig: لأنتم أشد رهبة في صدورهم من الله ذلك بأنهم قوم لا يفقهون

translation: They will not fight you all except within fortified cities or from behind walls. Their violence among themselves is severe. You think they are together, but their hearts are diverse. That is because they are a people who do not reason.
interpretation: This verse suggests that the enemies of the Muslims are cowardly and disunited. They only dare to fight from behind the safety of fortified walls and cities. Though they may appear united in their opposition to Islam, in reality their hearts are divided and they have serious internal conflicts. The root cause of their behavior is said to be their lack of reason and understanding. They fail to grasp the truth of Islam due to an inability or unwillingness to think deeply and sincerely about it.
orig: لا يقاتلونكم جميعا إلا في قرى محصنة أو من وراء جدر بأسهم بينهم شديد تحسبهم جميعا وقلوبهم شتى ذلك بأنهم قوم لا يعقلون

translation: Just like those shortly before them: they tasted the evil consequence of their affair, and they will have a painful punishment.
interpretation: This verse serves as a warning and reminder to those who reject the message of Islam and the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him). It compares their fate to that of previous nations who also denied their prophets and faced the consequences of their actions. The "painful punishment" mentioned refers to the torment that awaits the disbelievers in the Hereafter as a result of their rejection of faith and persistence in wrongdoing. The verse emphasizes the severity and certainty of divine retribution for those who choose to oppose God's guidance and cling to disbelief.
orig: كمثل الذين من قبلهم قريبا ذاقوا وبال أمرهم ولهم عذاب أليم

translation: Like the example of Satan when he says to man, "Disbelieve." But when he disbelieves, he says, "Indeed, I am disassociated from you. Indeed, I fear Allah, Lord of the worlds."
interpretation: This verse is a warning against following the temptations of Satan. It illustrates how Satan lures people into disbelief and sin, but then abandons them once they have succumbed to his influence. The verse emphasizes that even Satan himself fears the consequences of disobeying Allah, the Lord of all creation. It serves as a reminder to believers to be steadfast in their faith and not be swayed by the deceptions of Satan, who is ultimately a false friend and will leave his followers to face the consequences of their actions alone.
orig: كمثل الشيطان إذ قال للإنسان اكفر فلما كفر قال إني بريء منك إني أخاف الله رب العالمين

translation: So the end of both of them was that they will be in the Fire, abiding eternally therein. And that is the recompense of the wrongdoers.
interpretation: This verse serves as a stern warning and reminder of the severe consequences that await those who choose the path of wrongdoing and injustice. It emphasizes that the ultimate fate of the wrongdoers is eternal punishment in the Hellfire, where they will remain forever, without any hope of escape or relief. This interpretation highlights the gravity of committing injustice and the importance of leading a righteous life in accordance with God's guidance to avoid such a terrible outcome in the Hereafter.
orig: فكان عاقبتهما أنهما في النار خالدين فيها وذلك جزاء الظالمين

translation: O you who have believed, fear Allah. And let every soul look to what it has put forth for tomorrow - and fear Allah. Indeed, Allah is Acquainted with what you do.
interpretation: This verse is a reminder for believers to be mindful of Allah and to consider their actions in this life, as they will have consequences in the Hereafter. It emphasizes the importance of leading a righteous life and being aware that Allah is fully aware of all our deeds. The verse encourages introspection and self-evaluation, urging believers to reflect on their actions and strive to do good deeds that will benefit them in the afterlife. It also highlights the concept of taqwa (God-consciousness) and the need to maintain it consistently throughout one's life.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا اتقوا الله ولتنظر نفس ما قدمت لغد واتقوا الله إن الله خبير بما تعملون

translation: And be not like those who forgot Allah, so He made them forget themselves. Those are the defiantly disobedient.
interpretation: This verse warns against heedlessness and neglecting one's relationship with Allah. Those who forget Allah and become consumed by worldly pursuits will lose sight of their own spiritual well-being and purpose in life. As a result, they will fall into a state of disobedience and transgression. The verse emphasizes the importance of maintaining a strong connection with Allah and being mindful of Him in all aspects of life. Forgetting Allah leads to forgetting one's own true nature and purpose, ultimately leading to a state of moral corruption and spiritual loss.
orig: ولا تكونوا كالذين نسوا الله فأنساهم أنفسهم أولئك هم الفاسقون

translation: Not equal are the companions of the Fire and the companions of Paradise. The companions of Paradise - they are the attainers [of success].
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the stark contrast between the ultimate fate of those who reject faith and those who embrace it. The "companions of the Fire" refers to those who have earned God's punishment in Hell through their disbelief and evil deeds, while the "companions of Paradise" are the believers who have earned God's pleasure and reward through their faith and righteousness. The verse makes clear that these two groups are not at all equal in God's sight. The companions of Paradise are declared the true winners and achievers of success, highlighting that attaining Paradise is the ultimate triumph one can aspire to. It reminds us that our beliefs, choices and actions in this life have eternal consequences.
orig: لا يستوي أصحاب النار وأصحاب الجنة أصحاب الجنة هم الفائزون

translation: If We had sent down this Qur'an upon a mountain, you would have seen it humbled and coming apart from fear of Allah. And these examples We present to the people that perhaps they will give thought.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the power and majesty of the Qur'an. It suggests that even an inanimate object as mighty and solid as a mountain would be humbled and shattered by the awe-inspiring words of Allah. The Qur'an's message is so profound and impactful that it can move the hardest of hearts and the most unyielding of substances. Allah presents such vivid imagery to make people reflect deeply on the significance of His revelation and to inspire them to approach the Qur'an with reverence, humility, and a sincere desire to understand and apply its teachings in their lives.
orig: لو أنزلنا هذا القرآن على جبل لرأيته خاشعا متصدعا من خشية الله وتلك الأمثال نضربها للناس لعلهم يتفكرون

translation: He is Allah, other than whom there is no deity, Knower of the unseen and the witnessed. He is the Entirely Merciful, the Especially Merciful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the oneness and uniqueness of Allah, affirming that He alone is worthy of worship. It highlights two of His essential attributes: His omniscience, as He has knowledge of both the unseen and the seen realms, and His infinite mercy, which encompasses all of His creation. This verse serves as a reminder for believers to direct their worship and devotion solely to Allah, trusting in His all-encompassing knowledge and seeking His mercy in all aspects of their lives.
orig: هو الله الذي لا إله إلا هو عالم الغيب والشهادة هو الرحمن الرحيم

translation: He is Allah, other than whom there is no deity, the Sovereign, the Pure, the Perfection, the Bestower of Faith, the Overseer, the Exalted in Might, the Compeller, the Superior. Exalted is Allah above whatever they associate with Him.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute oneness and supremacy of Allah. It highlights His unique attributes as the only true God worthy of worship. He is the Sovereign ruler, completely pure and perfect, the source of peace and security, the one who bestows faith, the overseer of all things, the possessor of ultimate might and power, and the one who is superior above all else. The verse ends by declaring that Allah is exalted above any partners or equals that people may wrongfully attribute to Him. It serves as a powerful reminder of Allah's unparalleled greatness and the importance of worshipping Him alone.
orig: هو الله الذي لا إله إلا هو الملك القدوس السلام المؤمن المهيمن العزيز الجبار المتكبر سبحان الله عما يشركون

translation: He is Allah, the Creator, the Initiator, the Fashioner; to Him belong the most beautiful names. Whatever is in the heavens and earth is exalting Him. And He is the Exalted in Might, the Wise.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the unique attributes and powers of Allah as the sole Creator and Fashioner of the universe. It highlights that everything in existence glorifies and praises Him. The mention of His beautiful names invites contemplation on His divine qualities. The verse also affirms Allah's wisdom and might, indicating that His creation and governance of the universe are based on perfect knowledge and power. It encourages believers to recognize, praise, and submit to Allah's supreme authority and majesty.
orig: هو الله الخالق البارئ المصور له الأسماء الحسنى يسبح له ما في السماوات والأرض وهو العزيز الحكيم

translation: O you who have believed, do not take My enemies and your enemies as allies, extending to them affection while they have disbelieved in what came to you of the truth, having driven out the Prophet and yourselves [only] because you believe in Allah, your Lord. If you have come out for jihad in My cause and seeking means to My approval, [take them not as friends]. You confide to them affection, but I am most knowing of what you have concealed and what you have declared. And whoever does it among you has certainly strayed from the soundness of the way.
interpretation: This verse is a warning to the believers not to take the disbelievers as allies or friends, even if they show affection towards them. It emphasizes that the disbelievers are the enemies of Allah and the believers, as they have rejected the truth and driven out the Prophet and the believers from their homes simply because of their faith in Allah. The verse also points out the inconsistency in the behavior of those who claim to strive in the way of Allah and seek His pleasure, yet secretly maintain friendly relations with His enemies. It reminds them that Allah is fully aware of their hidden and apparent actions, and that such behavior is a clear deviation from the right path.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا لا تتخذوا عدوي وعدوكم أولياء تلقون إليهم بالمودة وقد كفروا بما جاءكم من الحق يخرجون الرسول وإياكم أن تؤمنوا بالله ربكم إن كنتم خرجتم جهادا في سبيلي وابتغاء مرضاتي تسرون إليهم بالمودة وأنا أعلم بما أخفيتم وما أعلنتم ومن يفعله منكم فقد ضل سواء السبيل

translation: If they gain dominance over you, they would be to you as enemies and extend against you their hands and their tongues with evil, and they wish you would disbelieve.
interpretation: This verse warns the believers that if the disbelievers were to gain the upper hand over them, they would treat them with open hostility and enmity. They would not only physically attack the believers with their hands, but also verbally assault them with harsh words and slander, using their tongues to speak evil against them. The ultimate wish of the disbelievers is for the believers to abandon their faith and revert to disbelief. This highlights the depth of their animosity and the danger they pose to the believers, emphasizing the need for caution and steadfastness in faith.
orig: إن يثقفوكم يكونوا لكم أعداء ويبسطوا إليكم أيديهم وألسنتهم بالسوء وودوا لو تكفرون

translation: Your family ties and your children will not benefit you on the Day of Resurrection. He will judge between you, and Allah is All-Seeing of what you do.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that on the Day of Judgment, worldly relationships and ties will not be of any benefit or significance. Family connections and offspring, which are often a source of pride and attachment in this life, will not hold any weight or offer any advantage in the Hereafter. The verse highlights that on that Day, each individual will be judged solely based on their own deeds and actions, and Allah, being All-Seeing, is fully aware of what every person has done. It serves as a reminder to prioritize one's relationship with Allah and focus on righteous actions, rather than relying on worldly connections or lineage for salvation.
orig: لن تنفعكم أرحامكم ولا أولادكم يوم القيامة يفصل بينكم والله بما تعملون بصير

translation: There has already been for you an excellent pattern in Abraham and those with him, when they said to their people, "Indeed, we are disassociated from you and from whatever you worship other than Allah.
