We have denied you, and there has appeared between us and you animosity and hatred forever until you believe in Allah alone" except for the saying of Abraham to his father, "I will surely ask forgiveness for you, but I have not [power to do] for you anything against Allah. Our Lord, upon You we have relied, and to You we have returned, and to You is the destination."
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of staying true to one's faith and disassociating from those who worship false deities. Abraham and his followers set an excellent example by declaring their disbelief in their people's idols and their complete devotion to Allah alone. This stance led to animosity between them and their polytheistic community. However, Abraham's promise to seek forgiveness for his father shows that one should still maintain compassion and hope for the guidance of their loved ones, while acknowledging that ultimate power and judgment belong to Allah. The verse emphasizes the significance of relying on Allah, turning to Him in repentance, and recognizing that our final return is to Him.
orig: قد كانت لكم أسوة حسنة في إبراهيم والذين معه إذ قالوا لقومهم إنا برآء منكم ومما تعبدون من دون الله كفرنا بكم وبدا بيننا وبينكم العداوة والبغضاء أبدا حتى تؤمنوا بالله وحده إلا قول إبراهيم لأبيه لأستغفرن لك وما أملك لك من الله من شيء ربنا عليك توكلنا وإليك أنبنا وإليك المصير

translation: Our Lord, do not make us a trial for those who disbelieve, and forgive us. Our Lord, indeed You are the Exalted in Might, the Wise.
interpretation: This verse is a humble prayer and plea to Allah, asking Him to protect the believers from becoming a source of misguidance or trial for the disbelievers. It is a supplication to not let the disbelievers see any weakness, vulnerability, or flaws in the believers that may cause them to feel justified in their disbelief or to ridicule the faith. Additionally, the verse includes a request for Allah's forgiveness, recognizing that only He has the power to forgive and that He is the Exalted in Might and the Wise, whose wisdom and decisions are perfect and unquestionable.
orig: ربنا لا تجعلنا فتنة للذين كفروا واغفر لنا ربنا إنك أنت العزيز الحكيم

translation: There has certainly been for you in them an excellent pattern for anyone whose hope is in Allah and the Last Day. And whoever turns away - then indeed, Allah is the Free of need, the Praiseworthy.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the believers should look up to and follow the example of the prophets and righteous individuals who came before them. They embodied the best of qualities and conduct, especially in their devotion to Allah and focus on the Hereafter. For those who seek Allah's pleasure and reward in the afterlife, emulating these role models is key. However, those who turn away from this guidance and choose a different path should know that Allah is not in need of them or their worship. He is self-sufficient, worthy of all praise, and not affected by their choices. The verse encourages following the righteous examples of the past while also affirming Allah's independence and perfection.
orig: لقد كان لكم فيهم أسوة حسنة لمن كان يرجو الله واليوم الآخر ومن يتول فإن الله هو الغني الحميد

translation: Perhaps Allah will put, between you and those to whom you have been enemies among them, affection. And Allah is competent, and Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse conveys a message of hope and reconciliation. It suggests that even if there has been enmity between Muslims and others, Allah has the power to transform that hostility into love and affection. The verse encourages Muslims to be open to the possibility of reconciliation, even with those they have considered enemies. It emphasizes Allah's power to bring about change in people's hearts and relationships, and it highlights His attributes of forgiveness and mercy. The verse implies that Muslims should not hold on to bitterness or resentment, but rather trust in Allah's plan and be ready to embrace peace and friendship when the opportunity arises.
orig: عسى الله أن يجعل بينكم وبين الذين عاديتم منهم مودة والله قدير والله غفور رحيم

translation: Allah does not forbid you from those who do not fight you because of religion and do not expel you from your homes - from being righteous toward them and acting justly toward them. Indeed, Allah loves those who act justly.
interpretation: This verse encourages Muslims to treat non-Muslims who are peaceful and do not oppose them with kindness, fairness, and justice. It emphasizes that Allah loves those who are just and equitable in their dealings with others, regardless of their faith. The Qur'an promotes peaceful coexistence and good relations with people of different beliefs, as long as they do not actively fight against or persecute Muslims. This verse highlights the importance of tolerance, compassion, and upholding justice in interpersonal relationships, even with those who do not share the same religious beliefs.
orig: لا ينهاكم الله عن الذين لم يقاتلوكم في الدين ولم يخرجوكم من دياركم أن تبروهم وتقسطوا إليهم إن الله يحب المقسطين

translation: Allah only forbids you from those who fight you because of religion and expel you from your homes and aid in your expulsion - [forbids] that you make allies of them. And whoever makes allies of them, then it is those who are the wrongdoers.
interpretation: This verse is emphasizing that Muslims should not take as allies or protectors those who actively fight against them, persecute them, and drive them out of their homes on account of their faith. Doing so would be considered an act of injustice and wrongdoing. The Qur'an is drawing a clear distinction between those non-Muslims who are peaceful and those who are hostile and aggressive towards the Muslim community. Allying with the latter group is prohibited, as it would be aiding oppression. However, this verse does not preclude having positive relations with non-Muslims in general, as long as they are not fighting against or oppressing the Muslims.
orig: إنما ينهاكم الله عن الذين قاتلوكم في الدين وأخرجوكم من دياركم وظاهروا على إخراجكم أن تولوهم ومن يتولهم فأولئك هم الظالمون

translation: O you who have believed, when the believing women come to you as emigrants, examine them. Allah is most knowing as to their faith. And if you know them to be believers, then do not return them to the disbelievers; they are not lawful [wives] for them, nor are they lawful [husbands] for them. But give them [the disbelievers] what they have spent. And there is no blame upon you if you marry them when you have given them their due compensation. And hold not to marriage bonds with disbelieving women, but ask for what you have spent and let them [the disbelievers] ask for what they have spent. That is the judgement of Allah; He judges between you. And Allah is Knowing and Wise.
interpretation: This verse provides guidance on how to deal with believing women who emigrate from disbelieving societies to join the Muslim community. It instructs the believers to examine the sincerity of their faith, and if they are found to be true believers, they should not be returned to the disbelievers as they are no longer permissible for them in marriage. The believers are allowed to marry these women, provided they give them their due dowries. It also instructs the believers to sever ties with disbelieving women, but to ask for the return of any wealth spent on them, and to let the disbelievers do the same. This is the judgment of Allah, who is All-Knowing and All-Wise in His rulings and decrees.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا إذا جاءكم المؤمنات مهاجرات فامتحنوهن الله أعلم بإيمانهن فإن علمتموهن مؤمنات فلا ترجعوهن إلى الكفار لا هن حل لهم ولا هم يحلون لهن وآتوهم ما أنفقوا ولا جناح عليكم أن تنكحوهن إذا آتيتموهن أجورهن ولا تمسكوا بعصم الكوافر واسألوا ما أنفقتم وليسألوا ما أنفقوا ذلكم حكم الله يحكم بينكم والله عليم حكيم

translation: And if you have lost any of your wives to the disbelievers, and you have subsequently overcome them, then give those whose wives have gone the equivalent of what they had spent. And fear Allah in whom you believe.
interpretation: This verse provides guidance on how to handle a situation where a Muslim man's wife has left him and joined the disbelievers. If the Muslims later triumph over those disbelievers, the man whose wife had left him is to be compensated for his loss from the spoils of war, being given the equivalent of the dowry he had originally paid for her. This ruling demonstrates Islam's concern for fairness and ensuring that believers are not left suffering losses due to the actions of hostile parties. At the same time, the verse ends by enjoining taqwa (mindfulness of Allah), emphasizing that Muslims should always act righteously and justly in all affairs, seeking Allah's pleasure above worldly considerations.
orig: وإن فاتكم شيء من أزواجكم إلى الكفار فعاقبتم فآتوا الذين ذهبت أزواجهم مثل ما أنفقوا واتقوا الله الذي أنتم به مؤمنون

translation: O Prophet! When believing women come to you pledging to you that they will not associate anything with Allah, nor will they steal, nor will they commit unlawful sexual intercourse, nor will they kill their children, nor will they bring forth a slander they have invented between their arms and legs, nor will they disobey you in what is right - then accept their pledge and ask forgiveness for them of Allah. Indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse establishes the conditions and requirements for women who wish to pledge their allegiance to the Prophet Muhammad and join the Muslim community. It emphasizes the importance of monotheism, moral integrity, and obedience to the Prophet's teachings. The verse also highlights Allah's forgiveness and mercy towards those who sincerely repent and seek His forgiveness.
orig: يا أيها النبي إذا جاءك المؤمنات يبايعنك على أن لا يشركن بالله شيئا ولا يسرقن ولا يزنين ولا يقتلن أولادهن ولا يأتين ببهتان يفترينه بين أيديهن وأرجلهن ولا يعصينك في معروف فبايعهن واستغفر لهن الله إن الله غفور رحيم

translation: O you who have believed, do not take as allies a people with whom Allah has become angry. They have despaired of [reward in] the Hereafter just as the disbelievers have despaired of [meeting] the inhabitants of the graves.
interpretation: This verse is a warning to the believers not to take as allies or friends those who have earned Allah's anger and wrath due to their disbelief and transgressions. These people have lost all hope in the rewards of the Hereafter, just as the disbelievers have lost hope in the resurrection of those buried in the graves. The verse emphasizes the importance of choosing one's allies and friends wisely, as associating with the wrong group can lead to spiritual ruin and the loss of Allah's favor in this world and the next.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا لا تتولوا قوما غضب الله عليهم قد يئسوا من الآخرة كما يئس الكفار من أصحاب القبور

translation: Whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth exalts Allah, and He is the Exalted in Might, the Wise.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute sovereignty and power of Allah over all creation. Everything in the universe, whether in the heavens or on earth, glorifies and praises Him. The mention of His attributes "the Exalted in Might" and "the Wise" further underscores His omnipotence and supreme wisdom in governing all affairs. It serves as a reminder for humans to humble themselves before the Almighty and recognize His greatness in every aspect of existence.
orig: سبح لله ما في السماوات وما في الأرض وهو العزيز الحكيم

translation: O you who have believed, why do you say what you do not do?
interpretation: This verse is a reminder to the believers to be sincere in their words and actions. It emphasizes the importance of honesty and integrity in one's conduct. The Qur'an is admonishing those who profess faith but fail to live up to its standards, highlighting the discrepancy between their claims and their deeds. It serves as a warning against hypocrisy and encourages Muslims to align their behavior with their beliefs, practicing what they preach. The verse underscores the significance of being truthful and consistent, as mere words without corresponding actions are of little value in the sight of Allah.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا لم تقولون ما لا تفعلون

translation: Most hateful it is with Allah that you say that which you do not do.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of honesty and integrity in speech and action. It is considered a grave sin in the sight of Allah to say something but not follow through with it or act upon it. This applies to all aspects of life, including making promises, taking oaths, or claiming to possess certain qualities or beliefs. The Qur'an teaches that one's words and deeds should be consistent, as this is a sign of sincerity and righteousness. Hypocrisy and false claims are strongly condemned, as they demonstrate a lack of faith and a disconnect between one's inner beliefs and outward actions. This verse serves as a reminder for believers to be mindful of their words and to strive for truthfulness and reliability in all their affairs.
orig: كبر مقتا عند الله أن تقولوا ما لا تفعلون

translation: Indeed, Allah loves those who fight in His cause in a row as though they are a [single] structure joined firmly.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of unity, discipline, and steadfastness among the believers, especially when they are fighting for the cause of Allah. It compares the Muslims who fight in the way of Allah to a solid, well-built structure that cannot be easily broken or penetrated. This metaphor suggests that when the believers stand together, united in their faith and purpose, they become an unshakable force capable of facing any challenge or adversity. The verse also implies that Allah's love and support are with those who demonstrate such unity and commitment in defending His cause and the Muslim community.
orig: إن الله يحب الذين يقاتلون في سبيله صفا كأنهم بنيان مرصوص

translation: And [mention] when Moses said to his people, "O my people, why do you harm me while you certainly know that I am the messenger of Allah to you?" And when they deviated, Allah caused their hearts to deviate. And Allah does not guide the defiantly disobedient people.
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of staying on the right path and not deviating from it. When the people of Moses started to harm and trouble him despite knowing that he was Allah's messenger, Allah caused their hearts to deviate as a consequence of their actions. It shows that Allah does not guide those who deliberately and persistently engage in disobedience and corruption. The verse serves as a warning to stick to the straight path and not be led astray by one's desires or the influences of others, as it can lead to Allah withdrawing His guidance and letting people's hearts deviate.
orig: وإذ قال موسى لقومه يا قوم لم تؤذونني وقد تعلمون أني رسول الله إليكم فلما زاغوا أزاغ الله قلوبهم والله لا يهدي القوم الفاسقين

translation: And [mention] when Jesus, the son of Mary, said, "O children of Israel, indeed I am the messenger of Allah to you confirming what came before me of the Torah and bringing good tidings of a messenger to come after me, whose name is Ahmad." But when he came to them with clear evidences, they said, "This is obvious magic."
interpretation: This verse can be interpreted as a prophecy of the coming of Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him). Jesus, as a messenger of Allah, informed the Children of Israel about the advent of a future prophet named Ahmad, which is another name for Muhammad. However, when Prophet Muhammad came with clear proofs and evidences of his prophethood, the people rejected him and accused him of practicing magic. This highlights the tendency of people to deny the truth even when it is presented to them clearly, and underscores the importance of faith and submission to Allah's message despite the opposition and rejection one may face.
orig: وإذ قال عيسى ابن مريم يا بني إسرائيل إني رسول الله إليكم مصدقا لما بين يدي من التوراة ومبشرا برسول يأتي من بعدي اسمه أحمد فلما جاءهم بالبينات قالوا هذا سحر مبين

translation: And who is more unjust than one who invents about Allah untruth while he is being invited to Islam. And Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people.
interpretation: This verse condemns those who fabricate lies against Allah, especially when they are being called to the truth of Islam. It emphasizes the severity of this sin by stating that there is no one more unjust than a person who does this. The verse also affirms that Allah does not guide those who persist in wrongdoing and choose to remain misguided, as they have willfully rejected the truth after it has been made clear to them. This highlights the importance of sincerity and honesty in one's faith and the grave consequences of deliberately inventing falsehoods about Allah and His religion.
orig: ومن أظلم ممن افترى على الله الكذب وهو يدعى إلى الإسلام والله لا يهدي القوم الظالمين

translation: They want to extinguish the light of Allah with their mouths, but Allah will perfect His light, although the disbelievers dislike it.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the futility of the efforts of those who oppose Allah and His message. Despite their attempts to undermine or extinguish the light of Islam through their words and actions, Allah will ensure that His light prevails and reaches its perfection, regardless of the aversion and disapproval of the disbelievers. It highlights the invincibility of Allah's plan and the ultimate triumph of His religion, even in the face of adversity and opposition from those who reject faith.
orig: يريدون ليطفئوا نور الله بأفواههم والله متم نوره ولو كره الكافرون

translation: It is He who sent His Messenger with guidance and the religion of truth to manifest it over all religion, although those who associate others with Allah dislike it.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the supremacy and ultimate victory of Islam over all other religions, despite the opposition and dislike of those who associate partners with Allah. It asserts that Allah has sent His Messenger, Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him), with the true guidance and the religion of truth, which will prevail and become dominant over all other belief systems. This interpretation highlights the divine support for Islam and its inevitable triumph, regardless of the resistance and aversion of the polytheists and disbelievers.
orig: هو الذي أرسل رسوله بالهدى ودين الحق ليظهره على الدين كله ولو كره المشركون

translation: O you who have believed, shall I guide you to a transaction that will save you from a painful punishment?
interpretation: This verse is calling upon the believers to engage in a trade that will ultimately save them from the painful punishment of Hell. The "trade" being referred to here is the exchange of the temporary pleasures of this world for the eternal bliss of the Hereafter, by living a life of faith, obedience to Allah, and good deeds. It's an invitation to prioritize one's relationship with Allah and the life to come over the fleeting temptations of the present world. The verse emphasizes that this is the most beneficial transaction one can make, as it guarantees salvation from the agonizing torment of the Afterlife.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا هل أدلكم على تجارة تنجيكم من عذاب أليم

translation: You believe in Allah and His Messenger and strive in the cause of Allah with your wealth and your lives. That is best for you, if you only knew.
interpretation: This verse is encouraging the believers to have complete faith in Allah and His Messenger, and to be willing to make sacrifices in the path of Allah, both with their wealth and their lives. It emphasizes that this is the best course of action for them, even if they may not fully realize it. The verse implies that striving in Allah's cause, through faith and selfless sacrifice, is the key to attaining the highest good and success, both in this world and the Hereafter. It is a call to prioritize one's spiritual obligations and the service of Allah's cause above worldly concerns and attachments.
orig: تؤمنون بالله ورسوله وتجاهدون في سبيل الله بأموالكم وأنفسكم ذلكم خير لكم إن كنتم تعلمون

translation: He will forgive for you your sins and admit you to gardens beneath which rivers flow and pleasant dwellings in gardens of perpetual residence. That is the great attainment.
interpretation: This verse is a promise from Allah to the believers that if they sincerely repent and follow His guidance, He will forgive their sins and grant them entry into Paradise. The "gardens beneath which rivers flow" and "pleasant dwellings" are descriptions of the eternal bliss and comfort that await the righteous in the Hereafter. This is considered the ultimate success and triumph, as it represents salvation from the punishment of Hell and the attainment of Allah's pleasure and rewards. The verse emphasizes the importance of faith, good deeds, and seeking Allah's forgiveness in order to reach this great achievement.
orig: يغفر لكم ذنوبكم ويدخلكم جنات تجري من تحتها الأنهار ومساكن طيبة في جنات عدن ذلك الفوز العظيم

translation: And [you will obtain] another [favor] that you love - victory from Allah and an imminent conquest; and give good tidings to the believers.
interpretation: This verse is a promise from Allah to the believers that they will be granted victory and conquest in the near future, in addition to other favors that they love. It is meant to encourage and motivate the believers to remain steadfast in their faith and to continue striving in the path of Allah, knowing that His support and help are always with them. The verse also emphasizes the importance of giving good news and glad tidings to the believers, as this helps to strengthen their resolve and increase their hope and trust in Allah's promises.
orig: وأخرى تحبونها نصر من الله وفتح قريب وبشر المؤمنين

translation: O you who have believed, be supporters of Allah, as when Jesus, the son of Mary, said to the disciples, "Who are my supporters for Allah?" The disciples said, "We are supporters of Allah." And a faction of the Children of Israel believed and a faction disbelieved. So We supported those who believed against their enemy, and they became dominant.
interpretation: This verse calls upon the believers to be steadfast supporters and helpers of Allah's cause, just as the disciples of Jesus were when he asked them who would stand by him in support of Allah. The disciples readily responded that they were the supporters of Allah. The verse then mentions that some among the Children of Israel believed in the message of Jesus while others rejected it. However, Allah aided and strengthened those who believed, making them victorious over their enemies. This interpretation highlights the importance of being firm in faith, standing up for the truth, and trusting in Allah's support and victory for the believers, even in the face of opposition and challenges.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا كونوا أنصار الله كما قال عيسى ابن مريم للحواريين من أنصاري إلى الله قال الحواريون نحن أنصار الله فآمنت طائفة من بني إسرائيل وكفرت طائفة فأيدنا الذين آمنوا على عدوهم فأصبحوا ظاهرين

translation: Whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth exalts Allah, the Sovereign, the Pure, the Exalted in Might, the Wise.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that all of creation, whether in the heavens or on earth, glorifies and praises Allah. It highlights several of Allah's attributes: His sovereignty over all things, His perfection and freedom from any deficiency or impurity, His might and power, and His wisdom in all that He decrees. It serves as a reminder for humans to join the rest of creation in recognizing Allah's greatness and to submit to Him as the One deserving of all praise and worship.
orig: يسبح لله ما في السماوات وما في الأرض الملك القدوس العزيز الحكيم

translation: It is He who has sent among the unlettered a Messenger from themselves reciting to them His verses and purifying them and teaching them the Book and wisdom - although they were before in clear error.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of the Prophet Muhammad's mission to the Arabs, who were mostly illiterate at the time. The verse highlights that the Prophet was sent to recite God's verses to them, purify their souls, and teach them the Qur'an and wisdom. This suggests that the Prophet's role was not merely to convey a message but also to spiritually and intellectually uplift his people, guiding them out of the state of ignorance and error they were in before his advent. The verse underscores the transformative power of the Prophet's teachings in bringing about a profound change in the lives of the Arabs.
orig: هو الذي بعث في الأميين رسولا منهم يتلو عليهم آياته ويزكيهم ويعلمهم الكتاب والحكمة وإن كانوا من قبل لفي ضلال مبين

translation: And [there are] others of them who have not yet joined them. And He is the Exalted in Might, the Wise.
interpretation: This verse refers to those who had not yet embraced Islam at the time of its revelation, but would do so in the future. It is a promise from Allah that Islam will continue to grow and spread, and that more people will join the ranks of the believers over time. The verse also emphasizes Allah's power and wisdom in guiding people to the truth, as He is the one who ultimately controls the hearts and minds of individuals. It serves as a reminder to the early Muslims that their community will continue to expand and flourish, and that they should have faith in Allah's plan.
orig: وآخرين منهم لما يلحقوا بهم وهو العزيز الحكيم

translation: That is the bounty of Allah, which He gives to whom He wills, and Allah is the possessor of great bounty.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that all blessings, favors, and bounties come from Allah alone. He bestows His grace and mercy upon whomever He chooses, according to His infinite wisdom and knowledge. It is a reminder that the gifts we receive in this world, whether they be material or spiritual, are ultimately from Allah. The verse also highlights the immense generosity and kindness of Allah, as He is described as the possessor of great bounty, indicating that His giving knows no bounds. This should inspire gratitude and humility in the hearts of believers, recognizing that everything they have is a result of Allah's favor upon them.
orig: ذلك فضل الله يؤتيه من يشاء والله ذو الفضل العظيم

translation: The example of those who were entrusted with the Torah and then did not take it on is like that of a donkey who carries volumes [of books]. Wretched is the example of the people who deny the signs of Allah. And Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people.
interpretation: This verse is criticizing the Jews who were given the Torah but failed to follow its teachings and implement them in their lives. They are compared to a donkey carrying a load of books, symbolizing that while they possess the scripture, they do not understand or benefit from its wisdom. It highlights the importance of not just having sacred knowledge, but acting upon it sincerely. Those who reject Allah's messages and signs are considered wrongdoers, and Allah does not guide such unjust people to the right path.
orig: مثل الذين حملوا التوراة ثم لم يحملوها كمثل الحمار يحمل أسفارا بئس مثل القوم الذين كذبوا بآيات الله والله لا يهدي القوم الظالمين

translation: Say, "O you who are Jews, if you claim that you are allies of Allah, excluding the [other] people, then wish for death, if you should be truthful."
interpretation: This verse is challenging the Jews who claimed to have a special status with Allah above other people. It tells the Prophet Muhammad to say to them that if they sincerely believe they are the chosen allies of Allah, then they should wish for death to hasten their meeting with Him. The implication is that their reluctance to do so betrays their lack of conviction in their claimed status and reveals that they know deep down that their claim is false. It suggests that their claim of being Allah's chosen people is insincere and motivated by worldly considerations rather than true faith and devotion to Allah.
orig: قل يا أيها الذين هادوا إن زعمتم أنكم أولياء لله من دون الناس فتمنوا الموت إن كنتم صادقين

translation: And they will never wish for it, because of what their hands have put forth. And Allah is Knowing of the wrongdoers.
interpretation: This verse highlights the regret and despair that the wrongdoers will feel in the Hereafter due to their misdeeds and sins in this worldly life. They will never wish to return to the world, as they know that their actions have already sealed their fate. The verse also emphasizes Allah's omniscience, as He is fully aware of those who commit injustice and transgress His boundaries. It serves as a warning to humans to be mindful of their actions and to refrain from wrongdoing, as they will be held accountable for their deeds in the afterlife.
orig: ولا يتمنونه أبدا بما قدمت أيديهم والله عليم بالظالمين

translation: Say, "Indeed, the death from which you flee - indeed, it will meet you. Then you will be returned to the Knower of the unseen and the witnessed, and He will inform you about what you used to do."
interpretation: This verse reminds us that death is inevitable and inescapable. No matter how much we try to avoid it or run away from it, it will eventually catch up to us. The verse also emphasizes the concept of accountability in the afterlife. After death, we will be returned to Allah, who has knowledge of both the unseen and the seen. He will then inform us about our deeds in this world and hold us accountable for them. This serves as a reminder for us to be mindful of our actions and to strive to do good deeds, as they will ultimately determine our fate in the hereafter.
orig: قل إن الموت الذي تفرون منه فإنه ملاقيكم ثم تردون إلى عالم الغيب والشهادة فينبئكم بما كنتم تعملون

translation: O you who have believed, when [the adhan] is called for the prayer on the day of Jumu'ah [Friday], then proceed to the remembrance of Allah and leave trade. That is better for you, if you only knew.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of attending the Friday prayer (Jumu'ah) and putting aside worldly matters, such as business transactions, when the call to prayer is made. It reminds the believers that remembering Allah and fulfilling religious obligations should take precedence over material pursuits, as this is ultimately more beneficial for them in both this world and the hereafter. The verse also implies that true success and knowledge lie in prioritizing one's spiritual well-being over temporary worldly gains.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا إذا نودي للصلاة من يوم الجمعة فاسعوا إلى ذكر الله وذروا البيع ذلكم خير لكم إن كنتم تعلمون

translation: And when the prayer has been concluded, disperse within the land and seek from the bounty of Allah, and remember Allah often that you may succeed.
interpretation: This verse encourages Muslims to actively engage in worldly pursuits and seek sustenance after fulfilling their spiritual obligations. It emphasizes the importance of maintaining a balance between worship and work, reminding believers that success in both this life and the hereafter can be achieved by remembering Allah frequently while going about their daily activities. The verse also highlights the concept of tawakkul, which is to put one's trust in Allah's providence while striving to earn a living through lawful means. It serves as a reminder that Muslims should not neglect their religious duties in the pursuit of worldly gains, but rather integrate their faith into all aspects of life.
orig: فإذا قضيت الصلاة فانتشروا في الأرض وابتغوا من فضل الله واذكروا الله كثيرا لعلكم تفلحون

translation: And when they see a transaction or entertainment, [O Muhammad], they rush to it and leave you standing. Say, "What is with Allah is better than entertainment and than a transaction, and Allah is the best of providers."
interpretation: This verse is a reminder that the pursuit of worldly pleasures and material gains should not distract believers from their devotion to Allah. It emphasizes that what Allah has in store for the faithful is far superior to any temporary enjoyment or financial gain. The verse also highlights the importance of prioritizing one's relationship with Allah over worldly affairs, as He is the ultimate provider and sustainer of all things. It serves as a warning against becoming consumed by the distractions of this world at the expense of one's spiritual well-being and connection to Allah.
orig: وإذا رأوا تجارة أو لهوا انفضوا إليها وتركوك قائما قل ما عند الله خير من اللهو ومن التجارة والله خير الرازقين

translation: When the hypocrites come to you, [O Muhammad], they say, "We testify that you are the Messenger of Allah." And Allah knows that you are His Messenger, and Allah testifies that the hypocrites are liars.
interpretation: This verse is referring to the hypocrites who outwardly professed their belief in Islam and the Prophet Muhammad, but inwardly harbored disbelief and ill intentions. Their outward proclamation of faith was insincere and merely a facade to protect themselves and their interests. Allah affirms that Muhammad is truly His Messenger, but also exposes the hypocrisy of those who falsely claim to believe in him. The verse serves as a warning to the hypocrites that their true nature is known to Allah and that they will be held accountable for their dishonesty and deception.
orig: إذا جاءك المنافقون قالوا نشهد إنك لرسول الله والله يعلم إنك لرسوله والله يشهد إن المنافقين لكاذبون

translation: They have made their oaths a screen (for their misdeeds): thus they obstruct (men) from the Path of Allah: truly evil are their deeds.
interpretation: This verse is criticizing the hypocrites who outwardly swear oaths of loyalty and belief, but use these false oaths as a cover to hide their true evil intentions and actions. Their oaths are a shield to protect them while they scheme to turn people away from the path of God and truth. The verse emphasizes how wicked their behavior is, to use an oath - something meant to be sacred - for such deceitful and obstructive purposes against faith.
orig: اتخذوا أيمانهم جنة فصدوا عن سبيل الله إنهم ساء ما كانوا يعملون

translation: That is because they believed, and then they disbelieved; so their hearts were sealed over, and they do not understand.
interpretation: This verse refers to the hypocrites who outwardly professed belief in Islam but inwardly harbored disbelief. As a result of their vacillation and insincerity, Allah has caused their hearts to be sealed, making them unable to comprehend the truth or gain guidance. Their lack of understanding is a direct consequence of their choice to reject faith after having accepted it, and their hearts have been made impervious to the light of truth due to their hypocrisy and duplicity.
orig: ذلك بأنهم آمنوا ثم كفروا فطبع على قلوبهم فهم لا يفقهون

translation: And when you see them, their forms please you, and if they speak, you listen to their speech. [They are] as if they were pieces of wood propped up - they think that every shout is against them. They are the enemy, so beware of them. May Allah destroy them; how are they deluded?
interpretation: This verse is referring to the hypocrites who outwardly appear impressive and eloquent, but inwardly they are devoid of faith and substance, like propped up pieces of wood. They are paranoid and assume that every outcry or shout is directed against them, as they are constantly fearful due to their guilty conscience. The verse warns the believers to be cautious of the hypocrites, as they are the enemy within the community. The verse ends with a prayer for their destruction, expressing disapproval of their deceptive behavior and marveling at how they are deluded and led astray from the truth.
orig: وإذا رأيتهم تعجبك أجسامهم وإن يقولوا تسمع لقولهم كأنهم خشب مسندة يحسبون كل صيحة عليهم هم العدو فاحذرهم قاتلهم الله أنى يؤفكون

translation: And when it is said to them, "Come, the Messenger of Allah will ask forgiveness for you," they turn their heads aside, and you see them turning away while they are arrogant.
interpretation: This verse highlights the arrogance and stubbornness of the disbelievers who refuse to accept the Prophet's invitation to seek forgiveness from Allah. Despite being offered the opportunity to be forgiven through the intercession of the Prophet, they proudly turn away, showing their disdain for the message of Islam. This behavior demonstrates their deep-rooted arrogance and their unwillingness to humble themselves before Allah and His Messenger. It serves as a reminder to believers to always remain humble and receptive to the guidance and mercy offered by Allah through His chosen messengers.
orig: وإذا قيل لهم تعالوا يستغفر لكم رسول الله لووا رءوسهم ورأيتهم يصدون وهم مستكبرون

translation: It is the same for them whether you ask forgiveness for them or do not ask forgiveness for them; never will Allah forgive them. Indeed, Allah does not guide the defiantly disobedient people.
interpretation: This verse suggests that there are some people who have gone so far astray in their disobedience and rejection of God's guidance that even the Prophet's prayers for their forgiveness will not be accepted by God. It indicates that forgiveness is not guaranteed simply by someone else seeking it on one's behalf. Rather, true repentance and correction of one's conduct is necessary to receive God's pardon and mercy. The verse also affirms that God does not compel or "guide" those who willfully choose the path of corruption and disobedience - they have to sincerely seek guidance themselves. Ultimately, each individual is responsible for their own spiritual destiny based on their choices and actions.
orig: سواء عليهم أستغفرت لهم أم لم تستغفر لهم لن يغفر الله لهم إن الله لا يهدي القوم الفاسقين

translation: They are the ones who say, "Do not spend on those who are with the Messenger of Allah until they disband." And to Allah belongs the depositories of the heavens and the earth, but the hypocrites do not understand.
interpretation: This verse is referring to the hypocrites who tried to undermine the Prophet Muhammad's mission by discouraging people from financially supporting him and his followers. They hoped that by cutting off support, the Prophet's companions would desert him. However, the verse asserts that all wealth and resources ultimately belong to Allah, and He is the one who provides for His servants. The hypocrites' lack of understanding of this spiritual reality exposes their ignorance and weak faith. The verse implies that true believers should trust in Allah's provision and continue to support the cause of Islam, regardless of the challenges or opposition they may face.
orig: هم الذين يقولون لا تنفقوا على من عند رسول الله حتى ينفضوا ولله خزائن السماوات والأرض ولكن المنافقين لا يفقهون

translation: They say, "If we return to Medina, the more honored [for power] will surely expel therefrom the more humble." And to Allah belongs [all] honor, and to His Messenger, and to the believers, but the hypocrites do not know.
interpretation: This verse highlights the arrogance and hypocrisy of some individuals who believed that they held power and influence over others in Medina. They boasted that if they were to return to the city, they would expel those whom they considered inferior or weaker. However, the verse affirms that true honor and power belong to Allah, His Messenger, and the believers. It emphasizes that the hypocrites, who make such false claims and fail to recognize the supremacy of Allah and the strength of faith, are ignorant of the reality that all might and glory are in the hands of Allah alone.
orig: يقولون لئن رجعنا إلى المدينة ليخرجن الأعز منها الأذل ولله العزة ولرسوله وللمؤمنين ولكن المنافقين لا يعلمون

translation: O you who have believed, let not your wealth and your children divert you from remembrance of Allah. And whoever does that - then those are the losers.
interpretation: This verse is a reminder to believers not to let worldly possessions and family distract them from remembering and worshipping Allah. It emphasizes that those who prioritize material things and neglect their spiritual duties will ultimately be the losers in the Hereafter. The verse encourages Muslims to maintain a balance between their worldly responsibilities and their obligation to remember and obey Allah, as neglecting one's faith leads to spiritual loss and failure in the eyes of Allah.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا لا تلهكم أموالكم ولا أولادكم عن ذكر الله ومن يفعل ذلك فأولئك هم الخاسرون

translation: And spend [in the way of Allah] from what We have provided you before death approaches one of you and he says, "My Lord, if only You would delay me for a brief term so I would give charity and be among the righteous."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of spending in charity and doing good deeds before it's too late. It reminds us that death can come unexpectedly, and we should not postpone our obligations to Allah and our fellow human beings. The verse also highlights the regret that one may feel at the time of death for not having done enough good in their life. It serves as a warning to use our wealth and resources wisely in the path of righteousness while we still have the opportunity, rather than waiting until it's too late and facing the consequences in the afterlife.
orig: وأنفقوا من ما رزقناكم من قبل أن يأتي أحدكم الموت فيقول رب لولا أخرتني إلى أجل قريب فأصدق وأكن من الصالحين

translation: And never will Allah delay a soul when its time has come. And Allah is Acquainted with what you do.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the inevitability of death and the predetermined time that Allah has set for each soul. It serves as a reminder that no matter how much we may wish to prolong our lives or delay the inevitable, when our time comes, there will be no postponing it. The verse also highlights Allah's omniscience, indicating that He is fully aware of all our actions and deeds. This knowledge should motivate believers to lead righteous lives, as they will be held accountable for their choices and actions in the Hereafter. The verse encourages introspection and the realization that our time on Earth is limited, urging us to make the most of our lives by fulfilling our purpose and living in accordance with Allah's guidance.
orig: ولن يؤخر الله نفسا إذا جاء أجلها والله خبير بما تعملون

translation: Whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth exalts Allah, and He is the Exalted in Might, the Wise.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute sovereignty and power of Allah over all creation. Everything in the heavens and the earth glorifies Him and is under His dominion. He alone deserves all praise and gratitude. The mention of His might and wisdom underscores that His power is coupled with perfect knowledge and judgment. It serves as a reminder for humans to humble themselves before the Almighty, recognizing His greatness in all aspects of existence.
orig: يسبح لله ما في السماوات وما في الأرض له الملك وله الحمد وهو على كل شيء قدير

translation: It is He who created you; and among you is the disbeliever, and among you is the believer. And Allah, of what you do, is Seeing.
interpretation: This verse highlights the fact that Allah is the Creator of all human beings, regardless of their beliefs. He has given humans the free will to choose their path - whether to believe or disbelieve. It also emphasizes that Allah is fully aware of all our actions and intentions. This serves as a reminder for us to be mindful of our deeds, as we will be held accountable for them. The verse encourages introspection and the conscious choice to follow the path of faith and righteousness, while recognizing that ultimately, it is Allah who guides whom He wills.
orig: هو الذي خلقكم فمنكم كافر ومنكم مؤمن والله بما تعملون بصير

translation: He created the heavens and earth in truth and formed you and perfected your forms; and to Him is the [final] destination.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah created the universe with a profound purpose and meaning, not merely in vain or for sport. It also highlights Allah's power and creativity in fashioning human beings in the best of forms and shapes. Furthermore, it reminds us that our ultimate return and the final destination is to Allah alone for judgment. This should inspire us to live righteously and be mindful of our actions in this temporary worldly life, as we will be held accountable in the eternal Hereafter.
orig: خلق السماوات والأرض بالحق وصوركم فأحسن صوركم وإليه المصير

translation: He knows what is in the heavens and earth and knows what you conceal and what you declare. And Allah is Knowing of that within the breasts.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the all-encompassing knowledge of Allah. He is aware of everything in the universe, both in the physical realm of the heavens and earth, as well as the inner realm of people's hearts and minds. Allah knows what people hide and what they reveal, indicating that nothing can be concealed from Him. The verse concludes by affirming that Allah has intimate knowledge of people's innermost thoughts, feelings, and intentions ("that within the breasts"). This highlights the importance of sincerity and purity of heart, as Allah judges people not only by their outward actions but also by what lies within their hearts.
orig: يعلم ما في السماوات والأرض ويعلم ما تسرون وما تعلنون والله عليم بذات الصدور

translation: Has there not reached you the news of those who disbelieved before? So they tasted the bad consequence of their affair, and they will have a painful punishment.
interpretation: This verse serves as a warning to those who reject faith in Allah and His messengers. It reminds them of the fate of previous nations who disbelieved and faced the consequences of their actions in this world and the Hereafter. The "painful punishment" mentioned refers to the torment that awaits the disbelievers in the afterlife as a result of their rejection of the truth and their persistence in wrongdoing. This verse emphasizes the importance of learning from the mistakes of the past and choosing the path of faith and righteousness to avoid a similar fate.
orig: ألم يأتكم نبأ الذين كفروا من قبل فذاقوا وبال أمرهم ولهم عذاب أليم

translation: That is because their messengers used to come to them with clear proofs, but they said, "Shall human beings guide us?" So they disbelieved and turned away. And Allah dispensed [with them]; and Allah is Free of need and Praiseworthy.
interpretation: This verse suggests that the disbelievers rejected the guidance brought by the messengers of Allah out of arrogance and pride. They could not accept the idea of mere human beings guiding them, despite the clear proofs and evidence the messengers presented. As a result, they chose to disbelieve and turn away from the truth. However, Allah is not in need of their belief or obedience. He is self-sufficient and worthy of all praise, regardless of whether people accept His guidance or not. The verse implies that rejecting the truth does not harm Allah in any way, but rather, it is the disbelievers who suffer the consequences of their choice.
orig: ذلك بأنه كانت تأتيهم رسلهم بالبينات فقالوا أبشر يهدوننا فكفروا وتولوا واستغنى الله والله غني حميد

translation: Those who disbelieve claim that they will not be resurrected. Say, "Yes, by my Lord, you will surely be resurrected; then you will surely be informed of what you did. And that, for Allah, is easy."
interpretation: This verse affirms the reality of resurrection and the Day of Judgment. It refutes the claim of the disbelievers who deny that they will be brought back to life after death. Allah commands the Prophet to respond to them with certainty, swearing by His Lord, that they will indeed be resurrected and then informed of all their deeds in this world. This verse emphasizes the power and ability of Allah, for whom resurrecting the dead is easy, and it serves as a warning to those who reject faith that they will face the consequences of their actions in the Hereafter.
orig: زعم الذين كفروا أن لن يبعثوا قل بلى وربي لتبعثن ثم لتنبؤن بما عملتم وذلك على الله يسير

translation: So believe in Allah and His Messenger and the Light which We have sent down. And Allah is All-Aware of what you do.
interpretation: This verse is a call to faith, urging people to believe in Allah, His Messenger Muhammad (peace be upon him), and the divine revelation (the Qur'an) that Allah has sent down as a guide and a light for humanity. The verse emphasizes that Allah is fully aware of all our actions and deeds, both good and bad. This awareness should motivate believers to be mindful of their conduct, strive to follow the guidance provided by Allah and His Messenger, and lead a righteous life in accordance with the teachings of Islam. The mention of Allah's all-encompassing knowledge also serves as a reminder that everyone will be held accountable for their actions in the Hereafter.
orig: فآمنوا بالله ورسوله والنور الذي أنزلنا والله بما تعملون خبير

translation: The Day when He will gather you for the Day of Assembly - that is the Day of Deprivation. And whoever believes in Allah and does righteousness - He will remove from him his misdeeds and admit him to gardens beneath which rivers flow, wherein they will abide forever. That is the great attainment.
interpretation: This verse highlights the significance of the Day of Judgment, referred to as the "Day of Assembly" or "Day of Deprivation". It emphasizes that those who have true faith in Allah and perform righteous deeds will be forgiven for their sins and granted entry into Paradise, where they will dwell eternally. This is described as the ultimate success and the greatest achievement one can attain. The verse serves as a reminder for believers to strive for righteousness and maintain their faith, as it will lead to immense rewards in the Hereafter.
orig: يوم يجمعكم ليوم الجمع ذلك يوم التغابن ومن يؤمن بالله ويعمل صالحا يكفر عنه سيئاته ويدخله جنات تجري من تحتها الأنهار خالدين فيها أبدا ذلك الفوز العظيم

translation: But those who disbelieved and denied Our signs - those are the companions of the Fire, abiding eternally therein; and wretched is the destination.
interpretation: This verse serves as a stern warning to those who reject faith in Allah and deny the truth of His revelations. It emphasizes that such individuals will face the severe consequence of being condemned to the eternal torment of Hell. The phrase "companions of the Fire" underscores the permanence of their suffering, as they will forever remain in the blazing flames of Hell as a result of their disbelief and rejection of divine guidance. The verse concludes by describing Hell as a "wretched" destination, highlighting the immense anguish and despair that awaits those who turn away from the path of righteousness and deny the signs of Allah.
orig: والذين كفروا وكذبوا بآياتنا أولئك أصحاب النار خالدين فيها وبئس المصير

translation: No disaster strikes except by permission of Allah. And whoever believes in Allah - He will guide his heart. And Allah is Knowing of all things.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the concept of divine decree and predestination in Islam. It asserts that no calamity or misfortune befalls a person except by the will and permission of Allah. However, for those who have true faith and belief in Allah, He will guide their hearts to patience, perseverance, and acceptance of His decree. This guidance helps the believer to cope with and overcome the challenges they face. The verse also highlights Allah's omniscience, affirming that He has knowledge of all things, including the wisdom behind the trials and tribulations that people encounter in life.
orig: ما أصاب من مصيبة إلا بإذن الله ومن يؤمن بالله يهد قلبه والله بكل شيء عليم

translation: And obey Allah and obey the Messenger; but if you turn away - then upon Our Messenger is only [the duty of] clear notification.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of obeying Allah and His Messenger, Muhammad (peace be upon him). It reminds believers that their primary duty is to follow the commands of Allah and the teachings of the Prophet. However, if they choose to turn away from this obedience, they should know that the Messenger's responsibility is only to convey the message clearly. He is not accountable for their actions or choices. The Messenger's duty is to communicate the divine message with clarity, and once he has done so, the responsibility lies with the individuals to accept and follow the guidance or bear the consequences of their disobedience.
orig: وأطيعوا الله وأطيعوا الرسول فإن توليتم فإنما على رسولنا البلاغ المبين

translation: Allah - there is no deity except Him. And upon Allah let the believers rely.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the core Islamic belief in the oneness and uniqueness of Allah as the only true God worthy of worship. It stresses that believers should put their complete trust, reliance and dependence in Allah alone for all their affairs. Trusting in Allah's wisdom, power and mercy is a key aspect of faith that brings inner peace and strength to face life's challenges, knowing that the ultimate authority and control belongs to Allah.
orig: الله لا إله إلا هو وعلى الله فليتوكل المؤمنون

translation: O you who have believed, indeed, among your spouses and your children are enemies to you, so beware of them. But if you pardon and overlook and forgive - then indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse is a warning to believers that sometimes their spouses and children can be a source of spiritual distraction or even opposition, pulling them away from the path of Allah. They may encourage worldly pursuits over religious devotion. However, the verse advises to treat them with patience, forgiveness and overlooking of their faults. This is because Allah Himself is Forgiving and Merciful to those who show such noble qualities. The verse encourages prioritizing one's relationship with Allah, while also maintaining ties of kinship with wisdom and compassion.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا إن من أزواجكم وأولادكم عدوا لكم فاحذروهم وإن تعفوا وتصفحوا وتغفروا فإن الله غفور رحيم

translation: Your wealth and your children are but a trial, and Allah has with Him a great reward.
interpretation: This verse reminds us that our worldly possessions and relationships, such as wealth and children, can be a source of temptation and distraction from our ultimate purpose of worshipping and obeying Allah. We should not become overly attached to these temporary things, as they are merely a test of our faith and priorities. Instead, we should focus on earning the pleasure of Allah and striving for the great reward that He has promised in the Hereafter to those who remain steadfast in their devotion to Him. The verse encourages believers to maintain a balanced perspective, recognizing the fleeting nature of worldly blessings and keeping their sights set on the eternal rewards of the Hereafter.
orig: إنما أموالكم وأولادكم فتنة والله عنده أجر عظيم

translation: So fear Allah as much as you are able and listen and obey and spend [in the way of Allah]; it is better for your selves. And whoever is protected from the stinginess of his soul - it is those who will be the successful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of having taqwa (God-consciousness) to the best of one's ability. It encourages believers to listen to and obey Allah's commands, and to spend in His cause, as this is ultimately beneficial for their own souls. The verse also highlights the significance of overcoming miserliness and greed, stating that those who protect themselves from such negative traits will be among the successful in both this world and the Hereafter. It serves as a reminder that true success lies in submission to Allah and generosity towards others.
orig: فاتقوا الله ما استطعتم واسمعوا وأطيعوا وأنفقوا خيرا لأنفسكم ومن يوق شح نفسه فأولئك هم المفلحون

translation: If you loan Allah a goodly loan, He will multiply it for you and forgive you. And Allah is Most Appreciative and Forbearing.
interpretation: This verse encourages Muslims to spend their wealth in the way of Allah, such as giving in charity. It promises that whatever one spends for Allah's sake with sincere intentions, Allah will multiply the rewards many times over. It also assures forgiveness of sins as an additional reward. The verse ends by emphasizing two attributes of Allah - that He is Most Appreciative (Shakoor) of the good deeds of His servants, and that He is Forbearing (Haleem), not rushing to punish them for their mistakes. This encourages the believers to hasten in doing good, and not to despair when they fall short, but to keep turning back to Allah in repentance.
orig: إن تقرضوا الله قرضا حسنا يضاعفه لكم ويغفر لكم والله شكور حليم

translation: Knower of the unseen and the witnessed, the Exalted in Might, the Wise.
interpretation: This verse refers to two of Allah's attributes - His knowledge and His wisdom. "Knower of the unseen and the witnessed" means that Allah has knowledge of all things, whether they are apparent to His creation or hidden from them. Nothing escapes His knowledge in the heavens or the earth. "The Exalted in Might" refers to Allah's power, grandeur and supremacy over all things. "The Wise" means that Allah is All-Wise in His creation, commandments and decree. He has placed everything in its proper place according to His wisdom. The verse emphasizes that Allah alone possesses the totality and perfection of these attributes.
orig: عالم الغيب والشهادة العزيز الحكيم

translation: O Prophet, when you [Muslims] divorce women, divorce them for [the commencement of] their waiting period and keep count of the waiting period, and fear Allah, your Lord. Do not turn them out of their [husbands'] houses, nor should they [themselves] leave [during that period] unless they are committing a clear immorality. And those are the limits [set by] Allah. And whoever transgresses the limits of Allah has certainly wronged himself. You know not; perhaps Allah will bring about after that a [different] matter.
interpretation: This verse provides guidance on the proper way to divorce women in Islam. It emphasizes the importance of timing the divorce to coincide with the beginning of the woman's waiting period ('iddah), during which she remains in her husband's house and cannot remarry. This waiting period serves to ensure that the woman is not pregnant and allows for the possibility of reconciliation. The verse also warns against transgressing the limits set by Allah in the divorce process, as doing so is considered a form of self-oppression. It concludes with a reminder that even after divorce, Allah may bring about a change in circumstances, possibly leading to a reconciliation between the couple.
orig: يا أيها النبي إذا طلقتم النساء فطلقوهن لعدتهن وأحصوا العدة واتقوا الله ربكم لا تخرجوهن من بيوتهن ولا يخرجن إلا أن يأتين بفاحشة مبينة وتلك حدود الله ومن يتعد حدود الله فقد ظلم نفسه لا تدري لعل الله يحدث بعد ذلك أمرا

translation: And when they have [nearly] fulfilled their term, either retain them according to acceptable terms or part with them according to acceptable terms. And bring to witness two just men from among you and establish the testimony for [the acceptance of] Allah. That is instructed to whoever should believe in Allah and the Last day. And whoever fears Allah - He will make for him a way out.
interpretation: This verse provides guidance on how to handle the end of a woman's waiting period after divorce. It instructs men to either reconcile with their wives on equitable terms or to release them with kindness once the waiting period is over. It also emphasizes the importance of having witnesses present for either decision, as a means of upholding justice and accountability before Allah. The verse ends with a reminder that those who are mindful of Allah and follow His guidance will be granted relief and a way out of their difficulties, emphasizing the spiritual benefits of adhering to Quranic principles in personal affairs.
orig: فإذا بلغن أجلهن فأمسكوهن بمعروف أو فارقوهن بمعروف وأشهدوا ذوي عدل منكم وأقيموا الشهادة لله ذلكم يوعظ به من كان يؤمن بالله واليوم الآخر ومن يتق الله يجعل له مخرجا

translation: And He provides for him from where he does not expect. And whoever relies upon Allah - then He is sufficient for him. Indeed, Allah will accomplish His purpose. Allah has already set for everything a [decreed] extent.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of putting one's trust in Allah (tawakkul). It assures believers that if they sincerely rely on Allah, He will provide for them from sources they may not anticipate. The verse also highlights the concept of divine decree (qadar), stating that Allah has predetermined the measure and extent of all things. This encourages believers to have faith in Allah's plan and wisdom, knowing that He will fulfill His will and purpose in their lives, even if the means are not immediately apparent to them. Tawakkul, in this context, is not just a passive acceptance of fate but an active trust in Allah's guidance and provision, coupled with the believer's own effort and striving in Allah's cause.
orig: ويرزقه من حيث لا يحتسب ومن يتوكل على الله فهو حسبه إن الله بالغ أمره قد جعل الله لكل شيء قدرا

translation: And those who no longer expect menstruation among your women - if you doubt, then their period is three months, and [also for] those who have not menstruated. And for those who are pregnant, their term is until they give birth. And whoever fears Allah - He will make for him of his matter ease.
interpretation: This verse provides guidance on the waiting period (iddah) for divorced women in various circumstances. For older women who have ceased menstruating and for those who have not yet begun menstruating, the waiting period is three months if there is any doubt about their status. For pregnant women, the waiting period lasts until they deliver their child. The verse emphasizes that for those who are mindful of Allah and follow His commandments, He will ease their affairs and grant them relief during this challenging time. It highlights the importance of patience, faith, and trust in Allah's plan during the difficult process of divorce and separation.
orig: واللائي يئسن من المحيض من نسائكم إن ارتبتم فعدتهن ثلاثة أشهر واللائي لم يحضن وأولات الأحمال أجلهن أن يضعن حملهن ومن يتق الله يجعل له من أمره يسرا

translation: That is the command of Allah which He has sent down to you; and whoever fears Allah, He will remove his misdeeds from him and will enlarge his reward.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of fearing Allah and obeying His commands. It promises that those who have taqwa (God-consciousness) and follow the divine injunctions will be rewarded by Allah in two ways: their sins will be forgiven, and they will be granted a great reward in the Hereafter. This interpretation highlights the spiritual benefits of leading a righteous life and staying mindful of Allah's presence and guidance. It encourages believers to strive for taqwa, as it purifies one's soul and leads to ultimate success and happiness in the afterlife.
orig: ذلك أمر الله أنزله إليكم ومن يتق الله يكفر عنه سيئاته ويعظم له أجرا

translation: Lodge them [in a section] of where you dwell out of your means and do not harm them in order to oppress them. And if they should be pregnant, then spend on them until they give birth. And if they breastfeed for you, then give them their payment and confer among yourselves in the acceptable way; but if you are in discord, then there may breastfeed for the father another woman.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of treating divorced women with kindness and respect, especially during their waiting period. Men are obligated to provide for their basic needs, such as housing and financial support, without causing them any harm or distress. If the woman is pregnant, the man must continue to support her until she gives birth. If she chooses to breastfeed the child, she should be fairly compensated for her time and effort. If the parents cannot come to an agreement regarding the child's care, they may seek a wet nurse to breastfeed the child. This verse highlights the Islamic principles of compassion, justice, and the protection of women's rights during and after divorce.
orig: أسكنوهن من حيث سكنتم من وجدكم ولا تضاروهن لتضيقوا عليهن وإن كن أولات حمل فأنفقوا عليهن حتى يضعن حملهن فإن أرضعن لكم فآتوهن أجورهن وأتمروا بينكم بمعروف وإن تعاسرتم فسترضع له أخرى

translation: Let a man of wealth spend from his wealth, and he whose provision is restricted - let him spend from what Allah has given him. Allah does not charge a soul except [according to] what He has given it. Allah will bring about, after hardship, ease.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of spending in the way of Allah according to one's means. Those who are wealthy should give generously from their abundance, while those with limited resources should still give what they can from what Allah has provided them. The verse reassures believers that Allah does not burden anyone beyond their capacity and that after every hardship, He will bring ease and relief. It encourages people to have faith in Allah's plan and to trust that He will provide for them, even in difficult times. The verse also highlights the value of generosity and the idea that one's wealth ultimately belongs to Allah, and should be used in a way that pleases Him.
orig: لينفق ذو سعة من سعته ومن قدر عليه رزقه فلينفق مما آتاه الله لا يكلف الله نفسا إلا ما آتاها سيجعل الله بعد عسر يسرا

translation: And how many a city was insolent toward the command of its Lord and His messengers, so We took it to severe account and punished it with a terrible punishment.
interpretation: This verse serves as a stern warning to those who arrogantly defy the commands of Allah and reject the guidance brought by His messengers. It reminds us that throughout history, many nations and communities who were defiant and rebellious against divine law faced severe consequences for their actions. The phrase "terrible punishment" emphasizes the gravity and intensity of the retribution they faced for their insolence. The verse implies that Allah's punishment is just and that those who persistently disobey and reject the truth will ultimately face the consequences of their choices. It encourages believers to remain humble, obedient, and mindful of Allah's commands to avoid a similar fate.
orig: وكأين من قرية عتت عن أمر ربها ورسله فحاسبناها حسابا شديدا وعذبناها عذابا نكرا

translation: So it tasted the evil consequence of its affair, and the outcome of its affair was loss.
interpretation: This verse serves as a warning and reminder that those who engage in evil deeds and disobey God will ultimately face the negative consequences of their actions. The "it" in this verse refers to a nation or group of people who turned away from the path of righteousness. By using the metaphor of "tasting" the evil consequence, the Qur'an emphasizes the direct and tangible nature of the punishment that awaits the wrongdoers. The final outcome and destination of their evil conduct is loss and ruin, both in this world and in the hereafter. This verse encourages individuals and societies to be mindful of their actions and to strive for goodness and piety, as the consequences of one's choices will eventually catch up with them.
orig: فذاقت وبال أمرها وكان عاقبة أمرها خسرا

translation: Allah has prepared for them a severe punishment, so fear Allah, O you of understanding who have believed. Allah has sent down to you a reminder.
interpretation: This verse is a stern warning to the believers to be mindful of Allah and to fear His punishment. It emphasizes that Allah has prepared a severe torment for those who disobey Him and reject His message. The verse specifically addresses those who possess understanding and have faith, urging them to heed the reminder that Allah has sent down. This reminder likely refers to the Qur'an itself, which serves as a guidance and admonition for mankind. The verse underscores the importance of taqwa (God-consciousness) and the need to live one's life in accordance with Allah's commands in order to avoid His wrath and attain His pleasure in the Hereafter.
orig: أعد الله لهم عذابا شديدا فاتقوا الله يا أولي الألباب الذين آمنوا قد أنزل الله إليكم ذكرا

translation: A Messenger reciting to you the clear verses of Allah that He may bring out those who believe and do righteous deeds from darknesses into the light. And whoever believes in Allah and does righteousness - He will admit him into gardens beneath which rivers flow to abide therein forever. Allah will have perfected for him a provision.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the role of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) in conveying the clear message of Islam, which guides believers from the darkness of disbelief and ignorance to the light of faith and knowledge. It promises that those who sincerely believe in Allah and perform righteous deeds will be rewarded with eternal Paradise, where they will enjoy the blessings of Allah forever. This highlights the importance of faith and good actions in attaining salvation and the perfect provision that Allah has prepared for the believers in the Hereafter.
orig: رسولا يتلو عليكم آيات الله مبينات ليخرج الذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات من الظلمات إلى النور ومن يؤمن بالله ويعمل صالحا يدخله جنات تجري من تحتها الأنهار خالدين فيها أبدا قد أحسن الله له رزقا

translation: It is Allah who has created seven heavens and of the earth, the like of them. [His] command descends among them so you may know that Allah is over all things competent and that Allah has encompassed all things in knowledge.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the omnipotence and omniscience of Allah. The creation of the seven heavens and earths, and the descent of Allah's command between them, serves as a testament to His power and control over all things. It also highlights that Allah's knowledge encompasses everything, and nothing is hidden from Him. The verse encourages believers to recognize and appreciate the vastness and perfection of Allah's creation, as well as to submit to His will and guidance, knowing that He is all-powerful and all-knowing.
orig: الله الذي خلق سبع سماوات ومن الأرض مثلهن يتنزل الأمر بينهن لتعلموا أن الله على كل شيء قدير وأن الله قد أحاط بكل شيء علما

translation: O Prophet, why do you prohibit [yourself from] what Allah has made lawful for you, seeking the approval of your wives? And Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse is addressing the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and gently admonishing him for prohibiting himself something that Allah had made permissible, out of a desire to please his wives. It reminds the Prophet that Allah is Forgiving and Merciful, implying that he need not be so strict upon himself. The verse highlights the importance of following divine law over human preferences. It also reflects the Qur'an's intimate conversational style in places, directly addressing the Prophet. Overall, the verse emphasizes the supremacy of Allah's law while recognizing the human weaknesses and desires that sometimes lead people, even prophets, to deviate from it in small ways.
orig: يا أيها النبي لم تحرم ما أحل الله لك تبتغي مرضات أزواجك والله غفور رحيم

translation: Allah has already ordained for you the dissolution of your oaths. And Allah is your protector, and He is the Knowing, the Wise.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of keeping one's oaths and the gravity of breaking them. However, it also acknowledges that there may be circumstances where dissolving an oath becomes necessary. In such cases, Allah has provided a way out through the expiation of oaths. The verse reminds believers that Allah is their ultimate protector and guide, and He possesses the wisdom and knowledge to legislate what is best for them. It underscores the idea that while oaths should be taken seriously, there is also room for flexibility and forgiveness when warranted, as determined by Allah's infinite wisdom.
orig: قد فرض الله لكم تحلة أيمانكم والله مولاكم وهو العليم الحكيم

translation: And [remember] when the Prophet confided to one of his wives a statement; and when she informed [another] of it and Allah showed it to him, he made known part of it and ignored a part. And when he informed her about it, she said, "Who told you this?" He said, "I was informed by the Knowing, the Acquainted."
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of maintaining trust and confidentiality in marital relationships. It also demonstrates that Allah is all-knowing and aware of even the most private conversations and actions. The Prophet's response to his wife's question emphasizes that he receives divine knowledge and guidance from Allah, who is the ultimate source of wisdom and understanding. This incident serves as a reminder for believers to be mindful of their words and actions, as nothing remains hidden from Allah's knowledge.
orig: وإذ أسر النبي إلى بعض أزواجه حديثا فلما نبأت به وأظهره الله عليه عرف بعضه وأعرض عن بعض فلما نبأها به قالت من أنبأك هذا قال نبأني العليم الخبير

translation: If you two [wives] repent to Allah, [it is best], for your hearts have deviated. But if you cooperate against him - then indeed Allah is his protector, and Gabriel and the righteous of the believers and the angels, moreover, are [his] assistants.
interpretation: This verse is addressing the Prophet's wives, warning them that if they conspire against the Prophet, they will face the wrath of Allah. It emphasizes that Allah is the protector and supporter of the Prophet, along with the angel Gabriel, the righteous believers, and the angels. This interpretation highlights the importance of loyalty and obedience to the Prophet, as well as the consequences of going against him. It also underscores the divine support and protection that the Prophet enjoys from Allah and his allies.
orig: إن تتوبا إلى الله فقد صغت قلوبكما وإن تظاهرا عليه فإن الله هو مولاه وجبريل وصالح المؤمنين والملائكة بعد ذلك ظهير

translation: It may be if he divorced you [all] that his Lord would substitute for him wives better than you - submitting [to Allah], believing, devoutly obedient, repentant, worshipping, and traveling - [ones] previously married and virgins.
interpretation: This verse indicates that if a husband divorces his wives, Allah may replace them with better wives who possess noble qualities. These qualities include being submissive to Allah, having strong faith, being devoutly obedient, repentant for their sins, dedicated to worship, and willing to travel for the sake of Allah. The verse also mentions that these potential new wives could be either previously married or virgins. This serves as a reminder that the marital relationship should be based on piety and righteousness, and that Allah can provide better spouses to those who seek His pleasure.
orig: عسى ربه إن طلقكن أن يبدله أزواجا خيرا منكن مسلمات مؤمنات قانتات تائبات عابدات سائحات ثيبات وأبكارا

translation: O you who have believed, protect yourselves and your families from a Fire whose fuel is people and stones, over which are [appointed] angels, harsh and severe; they do not disobey Allah in what He commands them but do what they are commanded.
interpretation: This verse is a reminder for believers to protect themselves and their families from the punishment of Hell. It emphasizes the importance of obedience to Allah and following His commands. The angels appointed over Hell are described as harsh and severe, indicating the severity of the punishment. They obey Allah's commands without question, highlighting the importance of submission to Allah's will. The verse serves as a warning for believers to be mindful of their actions and to strive to protect themselves and their loved ones from the Fire by adhering to Allah's guidance and living a righteous life.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا قوا أنفسكم وأهليكم نارا وقودها الناس والحجارة عليها ملائكة غلاظ شداد لا يعصون الله ما أمرهم ويفعلون ما يؤمرون

translation: O you who have disbelieved, make no excuses that Day. You will only be recompensed for what you used to do.
interpretation: This verse is a stern warning to the disbelievers that on the Day of Judgment, their excuses and justifications for their actions will be of no avail. They will face the consequences of their deeds and will be held accountable for their disbelief and transgressions. It emphasizes the finality of that Day, where no plea or argument can change the outcome. The verse also highlights the justice of Allah, as every person will be recompensed precisely for what they have done, with no favoritism or exception. It serves as a reminder to the disbelievers that their ultimate fate rests on their actions in this world, and that they should heed the message before it is too late.
orig: يا أيها الذين كفروا لا تعتذروا اليوم إنما تجزون ما كنتم تعملون

translation: O you who have believed, repent to Allah with sincere repentance. Perhaps your Lord will remove from you your misdeeds and admit you into gardens beneath which rivers flow [on] the Day when Allah will not disgrace the Prophet and those who believed with him. Their light will proceed before them and on their right; they will say, "Our Lord, perfect for us our light and forgive us. Indeed, You are over all things competent."
interpretation: This verse is a call to sincere repentance and turning back to Allah. It encourages the believers to seek forgiveness for their sins with the hope that Allah will erase their misdeeds and grant them entry into Paradise on the Day of Judgment. On that day, the Prophet and the believers will not be disgraced; rather, they will be honored with a special light that will guide them. They will supplicate to Allah to perfect their light and forgive them, acknowledging His power and ability over all things. This verse emphasizes the importance of repentance, the rewards of sincere faith, and the believers' reliance on Allah's mercy and forgiveness.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا توبوا إلى الله توبة نصوحا عسى ربكم أن يكفر عنكم سيئاتكم ويدخلكم جنات تجري من تحتها الأنهار يوم لا يخزي الله النبي والذين آمنوا معه نورهم يسعى بين أيديهم وبأيمانهم يقولون ربنا أتمم لنا نورنا واغفر لنا إنك على كل شيء قدير

translation: O Prophet! Strive against the disbelievers and the hypocrites, and be stern with them. Hell will be their home, a hapless journey's end.
interpretation: This verse instructs the Prophet Muhammad to firmly oppose and struggle against those who reject faith in God (the disbelievers) as well as those who outwardly profess Islam while concealing disbelief in their hearts (the hypocrites). The Prophet is told to be harsh and uncompromising with them in upholding the truth. It warns that such people will face the severe punishment of Hell as the ultimate destination for their evil and deception. The verse emphasizes the importance of the Prophet staying strong in conveying the message of Islam and not yielding to the plots and pressures of its opponents.
orig: يا أيها النبي جاهد الكفار والمنافقين واغلظ عليهم ومأواهم جهنم وبئس المصير

translation: Allah presents an example of those who disbelieved: the wife of Noah and the wife of Lot. They were under two of Our righteous servants but betrayed them, so those prophets did not avail them from Allah at all, and it was said, "Enter the Fire with those who enter."
