interpretation: This verse highlights the individual responsibility of each person for their own faith and actions, regardless of their close association with righteous individuals. The wives of the prophets Noah and Lot, despite being married to such pious men, chose to disbelieve and betray their husbands. As a result, their husbands' righteousness could not protect them from the consequences of their own disbelief and they were condemned to the Fire. This serves as a reminder that one's ultimate fate depends on their own choices and actions, and that even close proximity to the righteous does not guarantee salvation if an individual persists in disbelief and wrongdoing.
orig: ضرب الله مثلا للذين كفروا امرأت نوح وامرأت لوط كانتا تحت عبدين من عبادنا صالحين فخانتاهما فلم يغنيا عنهما من الله شيئا وقيل ادخلا النار مع الداخلين

translation: And Allah presents an example of those who believed: the wife of Pharaoh, when she said, "My Lord, build for me near You a house in Paradise and save me from Pharaoh and his deeds and save me from the wrongdoing people."
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of faith and reliance on Allah, even in the face of oppression and adversity. Asiya, the wife of Pharaoh, is presented as an exemplary believer who sought refuge in Allah and asked for His protection and salvation, despite being married to a tyrannical and oppressive ruler. Her unwavering faith in the face of hardship serves as an inspiration for all believers to trust in Allah's plan and seek His help, no matter how difficult their circumstances may be. The verse also emphasizes the significance of seeking a home in Paradise, which should be the ultimate goal of every believer, surpassing all worldly desires and attachments.
orig: وضرب الله مثلا للذين آمنوا امرأت فرعون إذ قالت رب ابن لي عندك بيتا في الجنة ونجني من فرعون وعمله ونجني من القوم الظالمين

translation: And [mention] Mary, the daughter of 'Imran, who guarded her chastity, so We blew into [her garment] through Our angel, and she believed in the words of her Lord and His scriptures and was of the devoutly obedient.
interpretation: This verse highlights the virtue and piety of Mary, the mother of Jesus. Despite the immense honor of being chosen to miraculously conceive Jesus through God's command, she remained humble, chaste, and devoutly obedient to God. Mary's unwavering faith in God's words and scriptures, even in the face of such an extraordinary event, sets an example for all believers to trust in God's plan and remain steadfast in their faith no matter the circumstances. Her story emphasizes the importance of purity, submission to God's will, and the power of divine intervention in the lives of His chosen servants.
orig: ومريم ابنت عمران التي أحصنت فرجها فنفخنا فيه من روحنا وصدقت بكلمات ربها وكتبه وكانت من القانتين

translation: Blessed is He in Whose Hand is the dominion, and He is Able to do all things.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the supreme power and authority of Allah. It affirms that all dominion and sovereignty belong to Him alone. He is the One Who has the ultimate control over the entire universe and everything within it. The verse also highlights Allah's omnipotence, stating that He has the ability to do all things without any limitations. It serves as a reminder for believers to submit to Allah's will and to trust in His wisdom and power in all aspects of their lives.
orig: تبارك الذي بيده الملك وهو على كل شيء قدير

translation: Who created death and life to test you [as to] which of you is best in deed - and He is the Exalted in Might, the Forgiving.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that God created the cycle of life and death as a test for humanity, to see who among them will do the best deeds and live righteously. It reminds us that our actions in this temporary world have consequences and that we will be judged based on how we lived our lives. At the same time, it highlights two key attributes of God - His power and might (Al-Aziz) as well as His forgiveness and mercy (Al-Ghafur). This suggests that while God will judge us, He is also ready to forgive those who sincerely repent and strive to do good. Ultimately, the verse encourages introspection and motivates the believer to make the most of the limited time they have in this world by living ethically and seeking God's pleasure.
orig: الذي خلق الموت والحياة ليبلوكم أيكم أحسن عملا وهو العزيز الغفور

translation: The One Who created seven heavens in layers. You do not see in the creation of the Most Merciful any inconsistency. So return [your] vision [to the sky]; do you see any breaks?
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the perfection and flawlessness of Allah's creation. The seven heavens are created in perfect harmony and balance, without any discrepancies or inconsistencies. When one looks at the sky and reflects upon the creation, they will not find any faults, cracks, or breaks. This is a testament to the supreme power and wisdom of the Creator, who has fashioned the universe with utmost precision and care. The verse invites humans to contemplate the marvels of Allah's creation and appreciate the beauty and order that exists in the heavens above.
orig: الذي خلق سبع سماوات طباقا ما ترى في خلق الرحمن من تفاوت فارجع البصر هل ترى من فطور

translation: Then return [your] vision twice again. [Your] vision will return to you humbled while it is fatigued.
interpretation: This verse is referring to the vastness and perfection of Allah's creation. No matter how much one looks and tries to find flaws or imperfections in the creation, they will fail to do so, and their eyes will become tired and strained from the effort. It emphasizes that everything Allah has created is perfect and without any defects or flaws. The repeated looking and failing to find faults is a sign of the perfection of Allah's creation and the inability of humans to encompass or fully comprehend it. It serves as a reminder for humans to humble themselves before the greatness and perfection of Allah's work.
orig: ثم ارجع البصر كرتين ينقلب إليك البصر خاسئا وهو حسير

translation: And indeed We have adorned the nearest heaven with lamps, and We have made such lamps (as) missiles to drive away the Shayatin (devils), and have prepared for them the torment of the blazing Fire.
interpretation: This verse highlights the power and wisdom of Allah in His creation. The "lamps" mentioned here are interpreted as stars that illuminate the night sky. Not only do they serve as adornment and a source of light, but they also serve as a means of protection against the devils. The shooting stars that we observe are actually these "missiles" driving away the evil forces. This verse also serves as a warning to those who follow the path of Satan, reminding them of the severe punishment that awaits them in the form of the blazing Fire of Hell. It emphasizes the consequences of straying from the right path and the importance of seeking refuge in Allah from the whispers and temptations of the devils.
orig: ولقد زينا السماء الدنيا بمصابيح وجعلناها رجوما للشياطين وأعتدنا لهم عذاب السعير

translation: And for those who disbelieved in their Lord is the punishment of Hell, and wretched is the destination.
interpretation: This verse serves as a stern warning to those who reject faith in Allah and deny His existence or unity. It emphasizes that disbelief and ingratitude towards one's Creator will lead to severe consequences in the afterlife, namely the punishment of Hell. The verse describes Hell as a terrible destination, highlighting the gravity of choosing to disbelieve. It implies that faith and righteousness are essential for salvation and that rejecting the truth will result in an undesirable fate. The verse aims to encourage people to embrace belief in Allah and avoid the path of disbelief to escape the torment of Hell and attain a blessed eternal life instead.
orig: وللذين كفروا بربهم عذاب جهنم وبئس المصير

translation: When they are thrown into it, they will hear from it a [dreadful] inhaling while it boils up.
interpretation: This verse describes the terrible fate of those condemned to Hell. When they are cast into the blazing fire, they will hear the horrifying sound of the flames roaring and the inferno itself seeming to breathe in deeply, as if eager to consume them. This vivid imagery emphasizes the unimaginable suffering and anguish that awaits the denizens of Hell, conveying a sense of the fire's intensity and the overwhelming terror experienced by those subjected to its torments. The verse serves as a powerful warning to humanity, urging them to heed God's message and strive for righteousness to avoid such a dreadful outcome in the afterlife.
orig: إذا ألقوا فيها سمعوا لها شهيقا وهي تفور

translation: It almost bursts with rage. Every time a group is cast into it, its keepers will ask them, "Did there not come to you a warner?"
interpretation: This verse describes the intense anger and fury of Hell towards its inhabitants. Whenever a new group of sinners is thrown into Hell, the guardians of Hell mockingly ask them if they were not warned by messengers about the consequences of their actions. This question is rhetorical, emphasizing that the denizens of Hell have no excuse, for they were indeed warned by prophets and messengers, yet they chose to reject the truth and persist in their wrongdoing. The verse underscores the severity of the punishment and the regret the sinners will experience for not heeding the warnings that could have saved them from this terrible fate.
orig: تكاد تميز من الغيظ كلما ألقي فيها فوج سألهم خزنتها ألم يأتكم نذير

translation: They will say, "Yes, a warner had come to us, but we denied and said, 'Allah has not sent down anything. You are not but in great error.' "
interpretation: This verse is a warning to those who reject the message of Allah and His messengers. It depicts the regret and admission of the disbelievers on the Day of Judgment when they will confess that they had indeed received warners, but they arrogantly denied them and accused them of being in great error. This highlights the gravity of rejecting divine guidance and the consequences one will face in the Hereafter for such disbelief. It serves as a reminder for people to heed the warnings of the prophets and to follow the path of righteousness before it is too late.
orig: قالوا بلى قد جاءنا نذير فكذبنا وقلنا ما نزل الله من شيء إن أنتم إلا في ضلال كبير

translation: And they will say, "If only we had been listening or reasoning, we would not be among the companions of the Blaze."
interpretation: This verse is a reminder that those who end up in Hell will regret their actions and wish they had used their faculties of hearing and reasoning to follow the right path in life. It emphasizes the importance of listening to the truth and using our intellect to discern right from wrong. The verse also implies that those who are destined for Hell had the capacity to listen and reason, but chose not to use these faculties properly. Ultimately, it is a warning for people to be mindful and to make the most of the gifts of hearing and reasoning that Allah has bestowed upon them in order to avoid the fate of the companions of the Blaze.
orig: وقالوا لو كنا نسمع أو نعقل ما كنا في أصحاب السعير

translation: Then they will confess their sin, so away with the companions of the Blaze.
interpretation: This verse warns that on the Day of Judgment, the sinners will finally acknowledge their wrongdoings and sins, but it will be too late for them. They will be condemned to the blazing fire of Hell as a consequence of their actions. The phrase "so away with the companions of the Blaze" emphasizes the severity of their punishment and their complete removal from God's mercy. It serves as a reminder for believers to avoid sin and to seek repentance while they still have the opportunity in this life.
orig: فاعترفوا بذنبهم فسحقا لأصحاب السعير

translation: Indeed, those who fear their Lord unseen will have forgiveness and great reward.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of having a sincere and unwavering faith in Allah, even when one is not in the public eye. It highlights the concept of "Taqwa" or the fear of Allah, which is a fundamental aspect of Islamic faith. Those who maintain this level of consciousness and reverence for Allah, even in private moments, are promised forgiveness for their sins and a great reward in the Hereafter. This interpretation underscores the significance of having a strong, internalized faith that is not dependent on external factors or recognition from others, but rather stems from a deep, personal connection with Allah.
orig: إن الذين يخشون ربهم بالغيب لهم مغفرة وأجر كبير

translation: And whether you conceal your speech or publicize it, indeed, He is Knowing of that within the breasts.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the all-encompassing knowledge of Allah. It reminds us that whether we express our thoughts and intentions openly or keep them hidden within our hearts, Allah is fully aware of them. It underscores the idea that we cannot conceal anything from Allah, as He knows the innermost secrets of our hearts. This verse encourages us to be mindful of our thoughts and intentions, and to strive for sincerity and purity in our actions, as Allah is always watching and aware of what lies within us.
orig: وأسروا قولكم أو اجهروا به إنه عليم بذات الصدور

translation: Does He who created not know, while He is the Subtle, the Acquainted?
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the all-encompassing knowledge of Allah, the Creator. It rhetorically asks how the One who created everything could possibly be unaware of His creation. Allah's knowledge is perfect and complete, extending to the most subtle and minute details. He is "Al-Lateef", the Subtle One, aware of the finest and most intricate aspects of His creation. He is also "Al-Khabeer", the Acquainted, possessing intimate knowledge of all things. This verse serves as a powerful reminder of Allah's omniscience and the impossibility of anything being hidden from Him.
orig: ألا يعلم من خلق وهو اللطيف الخبير

translation: It is He who made the earth tame for you - so walk among its slopes and eat of His provision - and to Him is the resurrection.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes God's benevolence and power over creation. He has made the earth subservient and manageable for human beings, enabling them to traverse its paths and benefit from its provisions. It encourages people to freely explore the earth, utilize its resources responsibly, and be grateful for God's sustenance. The verse ends with a reminder that all will return to God for the final judgment, prompting individuals to be mindful of their actions and purpose on earth. It highlights the balance of enjoying worldly provisions while maintaining consciousness of the eventual return to the divine.
orig: هو الذي جعل لكم الأرض ذلولا فامشوا في مناكبها وكلوا من رزقه وإليه النشور

translation: Do you feel secure that He who [holds authority] in the heaven would not cause the earth to swallow you and suddenly it would sway?
interpretation: This verse is a reminder that Allah has ultimate power and control over all things. It asks if people feel safe and secure, thinking that the One in the Heavens cannot cause the earth to swallow them up and shake violently. It serves as a warning not to become complacent or arrogant, forgetting Allah's might and ability to bring about sudden calamity or destruction. The verse encourages humility, mindfulness of Allah, and recognition that all stability and security are dependent on His will and mercy.
orig: أأمنتم من في السماء أن يخسف بكم الأرض فإذا هي تمور

translation: Do you feel secure that He who [holds authority] in the heaven would not send against you a storm of stones? Then you would know how [severe] was My warning.
interpretation: This verse is a stern warning to those who reject God's message and feel secure in their disbelief. It reminds them that God, who is above them in the heavens, has the power to send down a devastating punishment like a storm of stones. The rhetorical question implies that no one should feel safe from God's wrath if they choose to deny Him. The verse emphasizes that if such a calamity were to befall them, they would realize the gravity of the warning they had ignored. It serves as a wake-up call to reflect on one's spiritual state and turn to God in repentance before it is too late.
orig: أم أمنتم من في السماء أن يرسل عليكم حاصبا فستعلمون كيف نذير

translation: And indeed, those before them had denied, and how [terrible] was My reproach.
interpretation: This verse is a reminder that previous nations had also rejected the messages and warnings sent to them by Allah through His prophets. As a result, they faced the severe consequences of Allah's punishment and wrath. The phrase "how [terrible] was My reproach" emphasizes the gravity and intensity of the divine retribution that befell those who persisted in their disbelief and transgression. It serves as a warning to the current generation not to follow in the footsteps of their predecessors and to heed the call of faith and righteousness before it is too late.
orig: ولقد كذب الذين من قبلهم فكيف كان نكير

translation: Do they not see the birds above them with wings outspread and [sometimes] folded in? None holds them [aloft] except the Most Merciful. Indeed He is, of all things, Seeing.
interpretation: This verse draws our attention to the wonders of Allah's creation, specifically the birds soaring in the sky. It reminds us that it is only by Allah's power and mercy that these creatures are able to fly and remain aloft. The verse encourages us to reflect on the signs of Allah's existence and His complete control over the universe. It also emphasizes Allah's attribute of being All-Seeing, implying that He is fully aware of His creation and their actions. This realization should instill a sense of awe and humility in believers, as they recognize the greatness of their Lord and their own insignificance in comparison.
orig: أولم يروا إلى الطير فوقهم صافات ويقبضن ما يمسكهن إلا الرحمن إنه بكل شيء بصير

translation: Or who is it that could be an army for you to aid you other than the Most Merciful? The disbelievers are not but in delusion.
interpretation: This verse is a rhetorical question that highlights the delusion of the disbelievers who think they have support and protection apart from Allah. It emphasizes that no one can provide real help or be a true ally except for the Most Merciful. The verse implies that relying on anyone or anything other than Allah is futile and a manifestation of the disbelievers' deception. It serves as a reminder for the believers to put their complete trust only in Allah and not be misled by the false sense of security that the disbelievers find in worldly alliances and support systems.
orig: أمن هذا الذي هو جند لكم ينصركم من دون الرحمن إن الكافرون إلا في غرور

translation: Who is it that would provide for you if He withheld His provision? But they have persisted in insolence and aversion.
interpretation: This verse is a reminder that it is Allah alone who provides sustenance to all of His creation. No one else has the power to provide or withhold provision. Despite this clear reality, many people persist in their arrogance and turn away from acknowledging and being grateful to their Lord for His favors upon them. They fail to recognize that if Allah were to withhold His blessings and provision, no one would be able to replace Him as the source of all sustenance. The verse emphasizes the importance of humility, gratitude and turning to Allah for all of one's needs, rather than being deluded by a false sense of self-sufficiency and independence from Him.
orig: أمن هذا الذي يرزقكم إن أمسك رزقه بل لجوا في عتو ونفور

translation: Then is one who walks fallen on his face better guided or one who walks erect on a straight path?
interpretation: This verse is drawing a contrast between those who are misguided and those who are rightly guided. One who "walks fallen on his face" symbolizes someone who is spiritually blind, stumbling through life without true guidance. They are contrasted with one who "walks erect on a straight path" - someone who follows God's guidance and lives righteously. The message is that it is far better to follow the straight path of God's guidance than to stumble blindly through life. Guidance from God allows one to walk through life with clarity and purpose.
orig: أفمن يمشي مكبا على وجهه أهدى أمن يمشي سويا على صراط مستقيم

translation: Say, "It is He who has produced you and made for you hearing and vision and hearts; little are you grateful."
interpretation: This verse reminds us that it is Allah who has created us and bestowed upon us the faculties of hearing, sight, and understanding. These are precious gifts that allow us to perceive and comprehend the world around us. However, despite the immense value of these blessings, many people fail to express sufficient gratitude to their Creator. The verse subtly admonishes mankind for their lack of thankfulness and encourages them to reflect upon the bounties they have been granted. It emphasizes the importance of acknowledging and appreciating the favors of Allah, as gratitude is a fundamental aspect of faith and a means of drawing closer to Him.
orig: قل هو الذي أنشأكم وجعل لكم السمع والأبصار والأفئدة قليلا ما تشكرون

translation: Say, "It is He who has multiplied you throughout the earth, and to Him you will be gathered."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that it is Allah who has created human beings and spread them across the earth. It also reminds us that, ultimately, all of humanity will be gathered before Allah on the Day of Judgment to be held accountable for their deeds in this world. This serves as a reminder for people to be mindful of their actions and to live their lives in accordance with Allah's guidance, as they will have to answer for their choices in the Hereafter.
orig: قل هو الذي ذرأكم في الأرض وإليه تحشرون

translation: And they say, "When is this promise, if you should be truthful?"
interpretation: This verse is a rhetorical question posed by the disbelievers and skeptics who doubt the reality of the Day of Judgment and the fulfillment of God's promise. They challenge the Prophet and the believers, asking them when the promised Day will come to pass, as if to mock their belief and expose it as false. The tone of the question implies disbelief and derision, suggesting that the promise of judgment is nothing but a baseless claim. The verse highlights the skeptical attitude of those who reject faith and the message of the Prophets, and their unwillingness to believe in the unseen realities of the Hereafter.
orig: ويقولون متى هذا الوعد إن كنتم صادقين

translation: Say, "The knowledge is only with Allah, and I am only a clear warner."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that true knowledge and wisdom belong to Allah alone. The role of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) is to serve as a clear warner, conveying the message of Islam to mankind. He does not possess knowledge of the unseen or the future, as that lies solely with Allah. This verse encourages humility and recognition of human limitations, while affirming the absolute knowledge and power of Allah.
orig: قل إنما العلم عند الله وإنما أنا نذير مبين

translation: And when they saw it approaching, the faces of those who disbelieved turned bad, and it was said, "This is that for which you used to call."
interpretation: This verse refers to the Day of Judgment when the disbelievers will face the consequences of their actions. When they see the punishment approaching, their faces will be filled with fear and despair. They will realize that what they used to mock and deny is actually true, and now they have to face the reality of it. This verse serves as a warning to those who reject faith and reminds them that they will be held accountable for their deeds in the Hereafter.
orig: فلما رأوه زلفة سيئت وجوه الذين كفروا وقيل هذا الذي كنتم به تدعون

translation: Say, "Have you considered: if Allah should cause my death and those with me or have mercy upon us, then who can protect the disbelievers from a painful punishment?"
interpretation: This verse is a reminder that ultimately, it is only Allah who has the power over life and death, and the fate of all individuals. It emphasizes that even if the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and his followers were to perish or be shown mercy, the disbelievers would still face the consequences of their actions in the form of a painful punishment. The verse underscores the idea that no one can escape Allah's judgment and that the only path to salvation is through faith and righteousness. It serves as a warning to those who reject the message of Islam and persist in their disbelief.
orig: قل أرأيتم إن أهلكني الله ومن معي أو رحمنا فمن يجير الكافرين من عذاب أليم

translation: Say, "He is the Most Merciful; we have believed in Him, and upon Him we have relied. And you will [come to] know who it is that is in clear error."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of having complete faith and trust in Allah, the Most Merciful. It encourages believers to declare their belief in Him and to rely solely upon Him for guidance and support. The verse also serves as a warning to those who reject faith in Allah, suggesting that they will eventually come to realize their clear error and misguidance. It highlights the contrast between the believers who are on the right path and the disbelievers who are in manifest error, emphasizing the consequences of one's choice to either believe or reject faith in Allah.
orig: قل هو الرحمن آمنا به وعليه توكلنا فستعلمون من هو في ضلال مبين

translation: Say, "Have you considered: if your water was to become sunken [into the earth], then who could bring you flowing water?"
interpretation: This verse is a reminder of Allah's power and the fragility of human existence. It prompts reflection on the fact that the water we depend on for survival is ultimately under Allah's control. If He wills, He can cause our water sources to vanish, leaving us in desperate need. The verse implies that no one besides Allah can provide us with the life-giving water we require. It is a call to recognize our complete dependence on Allah's mercy and provision, and to be grateful for the blessings we enjoy, never taking them for granted. The verse encourages humility, reverence for Allah's might, and awareness that He alone sustains us moment by moment.
orig: قل أرأيتم إن أصبح ماؤكم غورا فمن يأتيكم بماء معين

translation: Nun. By the pen and what they inscribe,
interpretation: This verse is interpreted as an oath by Allah, swearing by the pen and what is written with it. It highlights the importance of writing and knowledge in Islam. The pen symbolizes the means by which knowledge is recorded and preserved, while "what they inscribe" refers to the various forms of writing, such as scriptures, books of knowledge, and records of deeds. This verse emphasizes that writing and knowledge are sacred and have a high status in Islam, as Allah has sworn by them. It also serves as a reminder for humans to value and pursue knowledge, as it is through writing that divine revelations and human experiences are recorded and passed down through generations.
orig: ن والقلم وما يسطرون

translation: You are not, by the grace of your Lord, a madman.
interpretation: This verse is a reassurance to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) that he is not insane or possessed, as his opponents claimed. It affirms that his prophethood and the revelations he received are a blessing and a favor from Allah, and not a sign of madness. The verse emphasizes that the Prophet's sound mind and wisdom are evident in his teachings and actions, which reflect divine guidance rather than insanity. It serves as a comfort to the Prophet and a reminder to his followers that Allah's support and protection are with him, despite the accusations and challenges he faced.
orig: ما أنت بنعمة ربك بمجنون

translation: And indeed, for you is a reward uninterrupted.
interpretation: This verse is a promise from Allah to Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) that he will be granted a great and endless reward in the Hereafter for his efforts in conveying the message of Islam and guiding people to the right path. The reward is described as "uninterrupted" or "unfailing", emphasizing its continuity and permanence. This verse serves as an assurance to the Prophet (peace be upon him) and a motivation for him to persevere in his mission, knowing that his striving will not go unappreciated or unrewarded by Allah.
orig: وإن لك لأجرا غير ممنون

translation: And indeed, you are of a great moral character.
interpretation: This verse is a testament to the exceptional character and morality of Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him). It highlights that he possessed a sublime and noble character, which was a reflection of his deep faith and connection with Allah. The Prophet's exemplary behavior, compassion, integrity, and righteousness were unparalleled, setting a standard for all of humanity to aspire to. This verse serves as a reminder for Muslims to strive to emulate the Prophet's moral character in their own lives, as his conduct was a manifestation of the Qur'an's teachings and a guide for attaining nearness to Allah.
orig: وإنك لعلى خلق عظيم

translation: And you will see and they will see
interpretation: This verse alludes to the fact that on the Day of Judgment, the truth will become clear to everyone. The Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) will see the reality of those who opposed him, and they too will realize the error of their ways. It is a reminder that ultimately, all will be held accountable for their deeds and the truth will be laid bare before all.
orig: فستبصر ويبصرون

translation: Then which of you is the deluded one?
interpretation: This verse is questioning which of the people addressed is deluded or deceived. It implies that someone among them is misguided or has been led astray by false beliefs or temptations, but leaves open the question of who specifically that may be. The verse prompts introspection for the listeners to examine themselves and consider if they may be the ones who are deluded, rather than pointing fingers at others. It emphasizes the importance of guarding against self-delusion and being honest in evaluating one's own spiritual state and beliefs.
orig: بأييكم المفتون

translation: Indeed, your Lord is most knowing of who has gone astray from His way, and He is most knowing of the [rightly] guided.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's omniscience and perfect knowledge. He alone knows the true spiritual state of every individual, whether they are misguided or rightly guided. It is a reminder that we cannot judge others based on outward appearances, as only Allah knows what is in the hearts. The verse also implies that guidance comes from Allah alone, and that those who are rightly guided are so by His grace and mercy. As human beings, we should strive to stay on the straight path, seeking Allah's guidance, while recognizing that He is the ultimate judge of who is truly guided and who is astray.
orig: إن ربك هو أعلم بمن ضل عن سبيله وهو أعلم بالمهتدين

translation: So do not obey the deniers.
interpretation: This verse is a clear instruction from Allah to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and, by extension, to all believers. It warns against following or yielding to the pressure of those who reject the truth of Islam and the message of the Qur'an. The "deniers" mentioned here could refer to the pagan Meccans who opposed the Prophet, or to anyone who rejects the truth of Allah's revelation. The verse emphasizes the importance of remaining steadfast in one's faith and not compromising one's beliefs in the face of opposition or criticism from non-believers. It encourages believers to stay true to their convictions and to trust in Allah's guidance, even in the face of adversity.
orig: فلا تطع المكذبين

translation: They wish that you would soften [in your position], so they would soften [toward you].
interpretation: This verse is addressing the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and the believers, indicating that the disbelievers and hypocrites wish that the Prophet and the believers would compromise their principles and beliefs in order to appease them. They desire that the Muslims would be lenient and accommodating towards their false beliefs and practices, so that they, in turn, could be more accepting of Islam. However, the verse implies that the Prophet and the believers should remain firm in their faith and not yield to the pressure of compromising their values and principles for the sake of pleasing others or gaining their approval. It emphasizes the importance of standing strong in one's belief and not succumbing to the desires of those who oppose the truth.
orig: ودوا لو تدهن فيدهنون

translation: And do not obey every worthless habitual swearer
interpretation: This verse is a warning against following or obeying individuals who are known for their excessive swearing and insincere oaths. Such people are often described as worthless and dishonorable, as their words carry little weight or credibility due to their habitual swearing. The Qur'an encourages believers to be cautious of those who engage in this behavior, as they may lead others astray with their empty promises and false commitments. Instead, one should rely on those who are trustworthy, sincere, and whose actions align with their words. The verse emphasizes the importance of surrounding oneself with righteous companions and avoiding the influence of those who lack integrity and moral character.
orig: ولا تطع كل حلاف مهين

translation: A slanderer, going about with calumnies
interpretation: This verse refers to a person who habitually engages in backbiting and spreading malicious rumors about others. Such a person is condemned for their behavior, which causes discord and harms the fabric of society. The Qur'an emphasizes the importance of speaking truthfully, avoiding gossip, and protecting the honor and reputation of others. Engaging in slander and calumny is considered a major sin that believers should abstain from in order to maintain the purity of their hearts and the integrity of their communities.
orig: هماز مشاء بنميم

translation: Hinderer of good, transgressor, sinful,
interpretation: This verse refers to a person who actively prevents others from doing good deeds, habitually transgresses the limits set by Allah, and engages in sinful behavior. Such an individual not only fails to do good himself but also tries to obstruct others from the path of righteousness. The verse condemns this type of behavior and implies that it is a grave sin to hinder others from performing virtuous acts, as it goes against the teachings of Islam which encourage believers to enjoin what is right and forbid what is wrong.
orig: مناع للخير معتد أثيم

translation: Moreover, he was of illegitimate birth.
interpretation: This verse is referring to a person who, in addition to his other negative qualities mentioned in the preceding verses, was born out of wedlock. In the cultural context of the time, this was considered a shameful and disgraceful circumstance. The verse is highlighting that this individual not only possessed an evil character but also had a dishonorable background. It emphasizes that such a person's wickedness is deeply rooted and that their very origin is tainted. This verse serves as a severe condemnation of the person in question, indicating that their moral corruption is fundamental to their being.
orig: عتل بعد ذلك زنيم

translation: That he should have wealth and children.
interpretation: This verse is referring to the fleeting nature of worldly possessions and offspring. It suggests that even if a person is blessed with abundant wealth and many children, these things are ultimately temporary and cannot provide true fulfillment or salvation in the Hereafter. The Qur'an often reminds believers not to be deluded by the allure of worldly gains, but rather to focus on cultivating faith, good deeds, and God-consciousness, which are the only things that will matter in the eternal life to come. The verse serves as a caution against becoming overly attached to or proud of one's material blessings and lineage, as these do not determine a person's ultimate fate or worth in the sight of God.
orig: أن كان ذا مال وبنين

translation: When Our verses are recited to him, he says, "Legends of the former peoples."
interpretation: This verse is referring to the disbelievers who, when they hear the verses of the Qur'an, dismiss them as mere legends or fables of the ancient people. They refuse to acknowledge the divine origin and truth of the Qur'an, and instead attribute it to human fabrication. This attitude stems from their arrogance, ignorance, and unwillingness to accept the message of Islam. The verse highlights the stubborn denial of the disbelievers and their tendency to reject the clear signs and revelations of Allah without any valid reason or proof.
orig: إذا تتلى عليه آياتنا قال أساطير الأولين

translation: We will brand him upon the snout.
interpretation: This verse is interpreted as a warning to those who reject the truth and persist in their wrongdoing. The "branding upon the snout" is seen as a metaphor for the humiliation and disgrace that the sinners will face in the Hereafter as a consequence of their actions. It emphasizes that their misdeeds will be exposed, and they will bear the mark of their sins. This interpretation serves as a reminder for people to be mindful of their conduct in this world, as it will have implications in the afterlife.
orig: سنسمه على الخرطوم

translation: Indeed, We have tried them as We tried the companions of the garden, when they swore to cut its fruit in the [early] morning
interpretation: This verse is referring to a story about a group of people who owned a garden and made an oath to harvest its fruits early in the morning without giving anything to the poor. Allah tested them by destroying the garden, teaching them a lesson about greed and not being charitable. It serves as a reminder that Allah tests people in various ways, and that one should be grateful for the blessings they have and share with those less fortunate, rather than being stingy and greedy. The story also emphasizes the importance of keeping one's promises and oaths, as the companions of the garden failed to do so and faced the consequences.
orig: إنا بلوناهم كما بلونا أصحاب الجنة إذ أقسموا ليصرمنها مصبحين

translation: And they do not make an exception.
interpretation: This verse is referring to the fact that the disbelievers do not make any exceptions in their disbelief. They reject all of Allah's signs and revelations, without considering the possibility that some of them may be true. This unwavering stubbornness and refusal to even entertain the idea of faith is a sign of their arrogance and closed-mindedness. The verse serves as a warning to believers not to fall into the same trap of blind rejection, but rather to approach matters of faith with humility, open-mindedness, and a willingness to consider the evidence before them.
orig: ولا يستثنون

translation: Then there came upon it [i.e., the garden] an affliction from your Lord while they were asleep.
interpretation: This verse is referring to a parable mentioned in the Qur'an about a group of people who owned a garden and became arrogant due to their wealth and possessions. As a result, Allah sent down a punishment upon their garden while they were asleep, destroying it completely. The interpretation is that one should never become proud or ungrateful due to the blessings and bounties given by Allah, as He can easily take them away at any moment. It serves as a reminder for humans to always remain humble and grateful to their Lord, acknowledging that all blessings come from Him alone.
orig: فطاف عليها طائف من ربك وهم نائمون

translation: So it became like a garden after harvest.
interpretation: This verse uses a powerful metaphor to describe the utter destruction and desolation that befalls those who are ungrateful and reject God's blessings. Just as a lush garden is reduced to mere stalks and stubble after the harvest, leaving no trace of its former beauty and abundance, the lives and possessions of the ungrateful are wiped out when God's punishment descends upon them. It is a stark reminder of the fleeting nature of worldly things and the importance of gratitude and faith in the face of God's power and judgment.
orig: فأصبحت كالصريم

translation: But they called out to one another in the morning,
interpretation: This verse is referring to the owners of a garden who had plotted to deprive the poor of their share of the harvest by gathering the fruits early in the morning without giving anything in charity. The use of the word "called out" suggests that they were reminding each other of their plan and encouraging one another to carry it out. The fact that this was done "in the morning" implies that they wanted to execute their scheme secretly before anyone else would notice. This passage highlights the greed and lack of compassion of the wealthy landowners, who were willing to go to great lengths to avoid sharing their wealth with the less fortunate.
orig: فتنادوا مصبحين

translation: That [you may] go early to your crop if you would cut [the fruit].
interpretation: This verse is encouraging the believers to be proactive and diligent in their work and daily tasks. It suggests that if one wants to reap the benefits and fruits of their labor, they should start their day early and attend to their responsibilities with determination and consistency. The metaphor of going early to one's crop to harvest the fruits can be applied to various aspects of life, signifying the importance of seizing opportunities, being productive, and putting in the necessary effort to achieve one's goals. It also implies that procrastination and laziness can lead to missed opportunities and a lack of success or growth.
orig: أن اغدوا على حرثكم إن كنتم صارمين

translation: So they proceeded, conversing in secret
interpretation: This verse is referring to a group of people who went off together, speaking privately amongst themselves in hushed tones. It suggests they were discussing something confidential or sensitive that they did not want others to overhear. The use of the word "yatakhafatun" implies a sense of secrecy and discretion in their conversation. This could be interpreted as the group plotting or conspiring together, or simply having a private discussion about a delicate matter. The verse captures a moment of human interaction and the dynamics of private communication within a group.
orig: فانطلقوا وهم يتخافتون

translation: No poor person shall enter it today upon you [i.e., in Jannah].
interpretation: This verse is interpreted to mean that on the Day of Judgment, those who were poor and needy in this worldly life will be prevented from entering Paradise alongside the wealthy and privileged. It highlights the stark contrast between the fate of those who had means and those who did not, emphasizing the importance of caring for the less fortunate and the consequences of neglecting this duty in the Hereafter. The verse serves as a reminder to Muslims to be mindful of the plight of the poor and to strive for social justice and compassion in their communities.
orig: أن لا يدخلنها اليوم عليكم مسكين

translation: And they became, by [their] power, those of great capability.
interpretation: This verse refers to a group of people who, through their strength and capabilities, rose to a position of power and influence. It suggests that they were able to achieve great things and exert their will due to the power and means at their disposal. The verse highlights the idea that with power comes the ability to shape one's circumstances and attain lofty goals, but it also carries an implicit warning about the potential for abuse and the importance of using power responsibly.
orig: وغدوا على حرد قادرين

translation: But when they saw it, they said, "Indeed, we are lost;"
interpretation: This verse is referring to the reaction of the brothers of Joseph when they saw the missing cup in their belongings, which had been secretly placed there by Joseph's servants. Upon seeing it, they immediately realized the gravity of the situation and the trouble they were in. They exclaimed that they were lost and doomed, knowing that they would be accused of theft and face severe consequences. This highlights their sense of despair and hopelessness in the face of what seemed like an impossible situation to explain or escape from.
orig: فلما رأوها قالوا إنا لضالون

translation: Nay, but we are deprived!
interpretation: This verse suggests that humans often feel a sense of deprivation or loss, perhaps due to being denied something they desire or feel entitled to. It could be interpreted as a reminder that in the grand scheme of God's creation and plan, humans are not always granted what they want, and must accept that some things are withheld or taken away by God. The verse may serve as a call for humility, gratitude, and acceptance of God's will, even in the face of perceived deprivation.
orig: بل نحن محرومون

translation: The most moderate of them said, "Did I not tell you, 'Why do you not exalt [Allah]?' "
interpretation: This verse is a reminder of the importance of remembering and glorifying Allah in all situations. The wise companion among the group pointed out the error of the others in not exalting Allah, emphasizing the need to maintain a strong connection with God and acknowledge His greatness. It highlights the role of those who are mindful of Allah in guiding others towards righteousness and the significance of heeding the advice of the wise and pious individuals in our lives.
orig: قال أوسطهم ألم أقل لكم لولا تسبحون

translation: They said, "Exalted is our Lord! Indeed, we were wrongdoers."
interpretation: This verse reflects the realization and acknowledgement of one's sins and wrongdoings. It emphasizes the importance of humility and repentance before Allah. By saying "Exalted is our Lord", they are acknowledging Allah's greatness and their own insignificance in comparison. The phrase "Indeed, we were wrongdoers" is an admission of their past mistakes and a plea for forgiveness. This verse teaches us that recognizing our faults, turning to Allah in repentance, and seeking His forgiveness are essential steps in attaining spiritual growth and purification of the soul.
orig: قالوا سبحان ربنا إنا كنا ظالمين

translation: Then they approached one another, blaming each other.
interpretation: This verse refers to the mutual recrimination and blame-shifting among the dwellers of Hell. It indicates that when faced with the consequences of their actions and the reality of their eternal punishment, they will turn against each other, trying to assign blame and fault for their predicament. This highlights the human tendency to avoid personal responsibility and seek scapegoats in times of distress, even though they all share culpability for their choices and actions in life that led them to this fate. It also emphasizes the breakdown of relationships and unity among the sinners in Hell, as opposed to the camaraderie and solidarity among the righteous in Paradise.
orig: فأقبل بعضهم على بعض يتلاومون

translation: They will say, "O woe to us! Indeed, we were transgressors."
interpretation: This verse describes the realization and regret expressed by the disbelievers and wrongdoers on the Day of Judgment. They will acknowledge their transgression and disobedience to Allah, recognizing that they had exceeded the limits set by Him. The phrase "O woe to us" indicates their deep sorrow, regret, and despair over their past actions, as they face the consequences of their sins. This moment of clarity comes too late, as they cannot return to the world to rectify their mistakes, emphasizing the importance of seeking forgiveness and living righteously during one's lifetime.
orig: قالوا يا ويلنا إنا كنا طاغين

translation: Perhaps our Lord will substitute for us [one] better than it. Indeed, we are toward our Lord desirous.
interpretation: This verse reflects the attitude of true believers who, when faced with loss or hardship, turn to Allah with hope and optimism. They trust that whatever Allah decrees for them is ultimately good, even if it appears difficult at first. The believers recognize that everything in this world is temporary, and they seek the eternal rewards of the Hereafter. They find comfort in the knowledge that Allah can replace what they have lost with something better, either in this world or in the next. This positive outlook stems from their deep faith and sincere desire to please their Lord, as they constantly long for His mercy, forgiveness, and blessings.
orig: عسى ربنا أن يبدلنا خيرا منها إنا إلى ربنا راغبون

translation: Thus is the punishment [in this world]. And the punishment of the Hereafter is greater, if they only knew.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the severity of the punishment in the Hereafter compared to the punishment in this worldly life. It serves as a warning to those who disbelieve or transgress against Allah's commands, reminding them that while they may face consequences in this life, the ultimate punishment in the Hereafter will be far greater and more severe. The verse also implies that if people truly understood the magnitude of the punishment awaiting them in the Hereafter, they would strive to avoid it by following the right path and obeying Allah's guidance.
orig: كذلك العذاب ولعذاب الآخرة أكبر لو كانوا يعلمون

translation: Indeed, for the righteous with their Lord are the Gardens of Pleasure.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the great reward that awaits those who are righteous and God-fearing in this life. It promises them "Gardens of Pleasure" or Paradise in the presence of their Lord in the Hereafter. This signifies the ultimate bliss, felicity and delight that the pious will experience eternally as recompense for their faith, good deeds and perseverance in the path of God. It motivates the believers to strive for righteousness with the knowledge that God has prepared for them an immense and everlasting reward that surpasses anything in this worldly life.
orig: إن للمتقين عند ربهم جنات النعيم

translation: Then will We treat the Muslims like the criminals?
interpretation: This verse is questioning the notion of equating the righteous believers with the sinful transgressors in the eyes of Allah. It implies that it would be unjust for God to consider those who submit to Him and follow His path as being equal to those who reject faith and commit evil deeds. The rhetorical question emphasizes that the two groups are not at all alike in merit and thus will not be treated the same in the Hereafter, as the believers will be rewarded with Paradise while the criminals will be punished in Hell. It highlights God's perfect justice in differentiating between the good and the wicked based on their faith and actions.
orig: أفنجعل المسلمين كالمجرمين

translation: What is [the matter] with you? How do you judge?
interpretation: This verse is questioning the basis and reasoning behind people's judgments and decisions. It implies that their way of thinking and judging matters is flawed or misguided. The verse is a form of criticism or rebuke, suggesting that people need to reassess how they form opinions and make choices. It calls on individuals to deeply reflect on their thought processes and the foundations of their beliefs, as there seems to be something amiss in their current approach that warrants this critical questioning from Allah.
orig: ما لكم كيف تحكمون

translation: Or do you have a book in which you learn?
interpretation: This verse is questioning the disbelievers who reject the message of Islam. It asks them if they have a divine book from which they learn and derive their beliefs, implying that their rejection of the Qur'an and the Prophet's teachings is baseless and not founded on any authentic scripture. The verse challenges them to produce a book of divine origin that supports their views if they claim to have one. It highlights the fact that the Qur'an is the only authentic divine scripture that should be followed and that the disbelievers have no valid reason to reject its message.
orig: أم لكم كتاب فيه تدرسون

translation: Indeed, for you therein is whatever you choose.
interpretation: This verse suggests that in Paradise, the believers will have the freedom to choose whatever they desire, and that all their wishes and preferences will be fulfilled. It implies that Paradise is a place of ultimate satisfaction, where the inhabitants will have access to an abundance of blessings and delights, tailored to their individual tastes and inclinations. The verse emphasizes the concept of free will and the absence of any limitations or restrictions in the afterlife for those who have earned Allah's pleasure through their faith and righteous deeds in this world.
orig: إن لكم فيه لما تخيرون

translation: Or have you received oaths binding on Us until the Day of Resurrection that you will have whatever you decide?
interpretation: This verse is a rhetorical question addressed to those who claim that they will have whatever they desire in the Hereafter. It emphasizes that no one has any binding oaths or promises from Allah that guarantee them whatever they wish for on the Day of Judgment. The verse implies that such claims are baseless and that people will be judged based on their deeds and faith, not their whims or desires. It serves as a reminder that ultimate judgment and decision belong to Allah alone, and that humans should focus on leading righteous lives rather than making presumptuous claims about their fate in the Hereafter.
orig: أم لكم أيمان علينا بالغة إلى يوم القيامة إن لكم لما تحكمون

translation: Ask them which of them will be the guarantor for that.
interpretation: This verse is challenging the disbelievers who deny the resurrection and the afterlife. It is asking them to produce someone who can guarantee or take responsibility for their claim that there will be no resurrection or judgment. The implication is that none of them can do so, as they have no evidence or authority to back up their denial of the hereafter. The verse emphasizes the lack of any logical or evidentiary basis for rejecting the Islamic doctrine of resurrection and accountability before God.
orig: سلهم أيهم بذلك زعيم

translation: Or do they have partners? Then let them bring their partners if they are truthful.
interpretation: This verse is challenging the polytheists who associate partners with Allah. It is asking them to bring forth their alleged partners if they are truthful in their claim. The verse implies that these alleged partners do not exist and that the polytheists are lying. It emphasizes the fact that Allah alone deserves worship and that associating partners with Him is a grave sin. The verse serves as a powerful reminder to the polytheists to abandon their false beliefs and to submit to the one true God.
orig: أم لهم شركاء فليأتوا بشركائهم إن كانوا صادقين

translation: The Day the shin will be uncovered and they are invited to prostration but the disbelievers will not be able
interpretation: This verse refers to the Day of Judgment when the intensity and severity of the situation will be so great that "the shin will be uncovered". This is an idiomatic expression in Arabic indicating a tremendously difficult situation. On that Day, the disbelievers will be called to prostrate before Allah, but they will be unable to do so, even though they were physically able to in the worldly life when they arrogantly refused. This signifies that it will be too late for them on that Day and they will face the consequences of their disbelief and rejection of faith. It serves as a strong warning to humanity to submit to Allah before it is too late.
orig: يوم يكشف عن ساق ويدعون إلى السجود فلا يستطيعون

translation: Their eyes humbled, humiliation will cover them. And they used to be invited to prostration while they were sound.
interpretation: This verse is referring to the state of the disbelievers on the Day of Judgment. Their eyes will be downcast out of shame and humiliation will overwhelm them. This is because in their worldly life, they were called to worship Allah alone and to prostrate to Him, at a time when they were safe and secure, but they refused to do so out of arrogance and disbelief. Now, on the Day of Reckoning, they will face the consequences of their actions, and will be covered with disgrace and humiliation for having rejected the truth that was conveyed to them.
orig: خاشعة أبصارهم ترهقهم ذلة وقد كانوا يدعون إلى السجود وهم سالمون

translation: Then leave Me alone with such as reject this Message: by degrees shall We punish them from directions they perceive not.
interpretation: This verse is a stern warning to those who reject the message of the Qur'an. It emphasizes that God will deal with the deniers Himself, and the Prophet should not be overly concerned about them. The phrase "leave Me alone" shows that God will personally take charge of their fate. The verse also points to a gradual and subtle punishment that will befall the deniers, coming from directions and in ways they do not perceive or expect. This indicates that their punishment will not necessarily be a sudden or overt calamity, but a slow and cumulative process that will ultimately lead to their downfall. The verse underscores the seriousness of rejecting divine revelation and the inevitability of consequences for those who persist in disbelief.
orig: فذرني ومن يكذب بهذا الحديث سنستدرجهم من حيث لا يعلمون

translation: And I will give them respite. Indeed, My plan is firm.
interpretation: This verse is a warning from Allah to those who disbelieve and reject His signs. Allah is giving them time and allowing them to enjoy their lives for a while, but this respite is part of His wise plan. Allah's plan is firm, meaning it is strong, well-designed, and cannot be overturned or thwarted. The disbelievers may think they are getting away with their actions, but in reality, they are only being led further astray and will ultimately face the consequences of their choices. This verse emphasizes the power and wisdom of Allah, and serves as a reminder that no one can escape His judgment or outmaneuver His plans.
orig: وأملي لهم إن كيدي متين

translation: Or do you ask them for a payment, so they are burdened with a load of debt?
interpretation: This verse questions whether the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) was asking his people for any payment or reward for conveying the message of Islam to them. It suggests that if he were to do so, it would be a burden on them, like a heavy debt. However, the Prophet did not ask for any worldly gain in exchange for his teachings. This emphasizes the sincerity of his message and that he was not motivated by any personal benefit, but rather by a genuine desire to guide people to the truth of Islam solely for the sake of Allah.
orig: أم تسألهم أجرا فهم من مغرم مثقلون

translation: Or do they have [knowledge of] the unseen, so they write [it] down?
interpretation: This verse is questioning whether the disbelievers who reject the Prophet's message have access to the knowledge of the unseen, which is known only to Allah. It suggests that if they did possess such knowledge, they would be able to write it down and produce their own scripture. The rhetorical question implies that they do not have this knowledge, and therefore their rejection of the Qur'an and the Prophet is baseless. It emphasizes that only Allah has knowledge of the unseen, and the Qur'an is a revelation from Him, not something fabricated by the Prophet or anyone else.
orig: أم عندهم الغيب فهم يكتبون

translation: So be patient for the decision of your Lord and do not be like the companion of the fish when he called out while he was distressed.
interpretation: This verse is advising the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and the believers to remain patient and steadfast in the face of adversity and trials, and to trust in Allah's plan and decree. It warns against being like Prophet Yunus (Jonah), who grew impatient and left his people without Allah's permission, and found himself in the belly of a whale, calling out to Allah in distress. The verse emphasizes the importance of patience, perseverance, and complete reliance on Allah during difficult times, knowing that Allah's help and relief will come at the appropriate time He has decreed.
orig: فاصبر لحكم ربك ولا تكن كصاحب الحوت إذ نادى وهو مكظوم

translation: Had it not been for a favor from his Lord, he would have been thrown onto the naked shore while he was censured.
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of God's mercy and favor upon His servants. Without God's grace, even the most righteous individuals, such as Prophet Yunus (Jonah), would face difficulties and trials in life. The verse implies that when one is faced with hardships, it is essential to turn to God and seek His forgiveness and mercy. It also serves as a reminder that no matter how dire one's circumstances may seem, God's intervention can change the situation for the better. Ultimately, the verse emphasizes the significance of maintaining a strong connection with God and relying on His support and guidance throughout life's challenges.
orig: لولا أن تداركه نعمة من ربه لنبذ بالعراء وهو مذموم

translation: So his Lord chose him and made him among the righteous.
interpretation: This verse indicates that Allah has chosen the individual mentioned and elevated him to the ranks of the righteous due to his faith, good deeds, and sincerity. It shows Allah's favor upon those who strive in His cause and live according to His guidance. Being chosen by Allah is a great honor and blessing, and it is a result of one's efforts in seeking Allah's pleasure and living a life of righteousness. The verse emphasizes that ultimately, it is Allah who guides and grants success to whomever He wills among His servants.
orig: فاجتباه ربه فجعله من الصالحين

translation: And indeed, those who disbelieve would almost make you slip with their eyes when they hear the message, and they say, "Indeed, he is mad."
interpretation: This verse refers to the intense hostility and malice that the disbelievers had towards the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him). Their hatred was so intense that they would almost cause the Prophet to slip or make a mistake with their piercing looks when they heard him reciting the Qur'an. They were frustrated and angered by the message, to the point of slandering the Prophet by calling him insane. This highlights the unwavering stance of the disbelievers against the truth, and their willingness to resort to various means to undermine the message and the messenger, even if it meant making false accusations against the Prophet's sanity.
orig: وإن يكاد الذين كفروا ليزلقونك بأبصارهم لما سمعوا الذكر ويقولون إنه لمجنون

translation: And it is not except a reminder to the worlds.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the Qur'an is a universal message and a reminder for all of humanity, not limited to a specific group or nation. It serves as a guidance and admonition for everyone, regardless of their background or status, inviting them to reflect upon its teachings and follow the path of righteousness. The Qur'an is a timeless message that addresses the fundamental aspects of human life and provides a framework for living a purposeful and fulfilling existence in accordance with the will of Allah.
orig: وما هو إلا ذكر للعالمين

translation: The Inevitable Reality
interpretation: Surah Al-Haaqqa, or "The Inevitable Reality", refers to the Day of Judgment, which is an unavoidable and certain event that will come to pass. The name emphasizes the absolute truth and certainty of this momentous occasion, where all individuals will be held accountable for their deeds in this world. It serves as a reminder for believers to lead righteous lives and prepare for the ultimate reckoning, as the consequences of one's actions will be inescapable on that day.
orig: الحاقة

translation: What is the Inevitable Reality?
interpretation: This verse is asking about the true nature and meaning of the Day of Judgment, also known as the Inevitable Reality or the Sure Reality (al-Haqqa). It is a rhetorical question that draws the listener's attention to the momentous events of that Day. The interpretation is that this Day is an inescapable and unavoidable event that will come to pass, when all souls will be held accountable for their deeds. It emphasizes the gravity and certainty of the Day of Judgment in the Islamic belief system.
orig: ما الحاقة

translation: And what can make you know what the Inevitable Reality is?
interpretation: The verse is emphasizing the immense and unimaginable nature of the Day of Judgment, also known as the Inevitable Reality or the Sure Reality (Al-Haaqqa). It suggests that the human mind cannot fully comprehend or grasp the true essence and magnitude of that Day. This rhetorical question serves to draw the listener's attention to the importance and seriousness of the Day of Judgment, encouraging them to reflect upon its significance and to prepare for it through righteous deeds and unwavering faith in Allah.
orig: وما أدراك ما الحاقة

translation: Thamud and 'Aad denied the Striking Calamity.
interpretation: This verse is referring to the ancient tribes of Thamud and 'Aad, who were punished by Allah for their disbelief and rejection of His messengers. The "Striking Calamity" mentioned here is likely referring to the Day of Judgment or the final destruction that befell these tribes. The verse serves as a warning to those who deny the truth and reject the signs and warnings sent by Allah, reminding them of the fate that befell previous nations who did the same. It emphasizes the importance of belief and submission to Allah to avoid a similar punishment in this life and the hereafter.
orig: كذبت ثمود وعاد بالقارعة

translation: As for Thamud, they were destroyed by the overwhelming [blast].
interpretation: This verse refers to the ancient tribe of Thamud, who were punished by Allah for their disobedience and rejection of His message. The "overwhelming blast" mentioned in the verse is interpreted as a powerful sound or a devastating event that destroyed the people of Thamud. It serves as a reminder that those who persist in disbelief and transgression will face the consequences of their actions in this world and the Hereafter. The verse emphasizes the importance of heeding Allah's warnings and following the guidance of His messengers to avoid a similar fate.
orig: فأما ثمود فأهلكوا بالطاغية

translation: And as for 'Aad, they were destroyed by a furious wind, exceedingly violent.
interpretation: This verse refers to the ancient people of 'Aad, who were punished by Allah for their disobedience and rejection of His message. The "furious wind" mentioned here was likely a devastating hurricane or tornado that completely destroyed their civilization. The verse emphasizes the severity and overwhelming power of this wind, describing it as "exceedingly violent." This serves as a reminder that no matter how powerful or advanced a society may be, it is ultimately at the mercy of Allah's will and judgment. The fate of 'Aad is a warning to all people to heed the signs and messages sent by Allah, and to submit to His guidance before it is too late.
orig: وأما عاد فأهلكوا بريح صرصر عاتية

translation: He imposed it upon them for seven nights and eight days in succession, so you would see the people therein fallen as if they were hollow trunks of palm trees.
interpretation: This verse refers to the punishment that Allah inflicted upon the people of 'Aad, who were a powerful and prosperous nation but rejected the message of Prophet Hud (peace be upon him). Allah sent upon them a severe windstorm that lasted for seven nights and eight days continuously, uprooting them and leaving them like hollow trunks of palm trees. This interpretation highlights the severity and duration of the punishment, emphasizing that no matter how strong or established a nation may be, they are not immune to Allah's punishment if they persist in disbelief and rejection of His messages. It also serves as a reminder for people to humble themselves before Allah and to heed the warnings of His prophets.
orig: سخرها عليهم سبع ليال وثمانية أيام حسوما فترى القوم فيها صرعى كأنهم أعجاز نخل خاوية

translation: So do you see for them any remainder?
interpretation: This verse is questioning whether there is anything left or remaining of the disbelievers and their legacies after Allah has destroyed them for their rejection and disbelief. It suggests that they have been completely wiped out and eliminated, with no trace or remnant of them surviving. The verse emphasizes the complete and utter destruction that befalls those who oppose Allah and reject His messages and prophets.
orig: فهل ترى لهم من باقية

translation: And there came Pharaoh and those before him and the overturned cities with sin.
interpretation: This verse refers to the punishment that befell Pharaoh and the previous nations who rejected Allah's messengers and committed grave sins. The "overturned cities" is believed to be a reference to the people of Prophet Lut (Lot) who practiced homosexuality and were destroyed by Allah as a result of their transgressions. The verse emphasizes that those who persist in sin and reject divine guidance will face severe consequences in this world and the Hereafter, serving as a warning to humanity to follow the straight path and avoid the fate of the destroyed nations.
orig: وجاء فرعون ومن قبله والمؤتفكات بالخاطئة

translation: But they disobeyed the messenger of their Lord, so He seized them with a devastating seizure.
interpretation: This verse warns of the consequences of disobeying Allah's messengers. When people reject the guidance sent to them through prophets, they invite Allah's punishment upon themselves. The "devastating seizure" mentioned here could refer to a calamity or disaster that destroys the disobedient people as a result of their defiance. It emphasizes that going against the commandments conveyed by the messengers leads to severe repercussions, signifying Allah's displeasure and wrath towards those who knowingly rebel against His instructions. The verse serves as a reminder for believers to heed the messages of prophets and stay on the right path to avoid facing a similar fate.
orig: فعصوا رسول ربهم فأخذهم أخذة رابية

translation: Indeed, when the water overflowed, We carried you in the sailing ship.
interpretation: This verse refers to the story of Prophet Noah (peace be upon him) and the Great Flood. It reminds humanity that when the floodwaters rose as a punishment for the disbelievers, Allah saved the believers by commanding Noah to build an ark. The verse emphasizes Allah's power over His creation and His ability to protect the righteous from calamities. It also serves as a warning to those who reject the message of the prophets, highlighting the consequences of disobedience to Allah's commands. The ark symbolizes the safety and security that can be found in following the guidance of Allah and His messengers.
orig: إنا لما طغى الماء حملناكم في الجارية

translation: That We might make it a reminder for you, and the retaining ear might retain it.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of the Qur'an as a reminder for mankind. The phrase "the retaining ear" suggests that those who listen attentively and sincerely to the Qur'an will internalize its message and benefit from its guidance. It is a call to reflect deeply upon the verses and to allow the teachings to penetrate one's heart and mind, leading to a transformative spiritual experience. The Qur'an serves as a constant reminder of Allah's presence, His mercy, and the purpose of human existence, helping believers stay on the straight path.
orig: لنجعلها لكم تذكرة وتعيها أذن واعية

translation: Then, when the Trumpet is blown with a single blast,
interpretation: This verse is referring to the Day of Judgment, when the Trumpet will be blown to signal the resurrection of the dead and the beginning of the final reckoning. The single blast emphasizes the suddenness and enormity of this event, which will mark the end of the world as we know it and the commencement of the afterlife. It is a reminder to humanity that this life is temporary and that we will all be held accountable for our deeds in the Hereafter. The verse underscores the importance of leading a righteous life and being prepared for the inevitable moment when we will face our Creator and the consequences of our actions in this world.
orig: فإذا نفخ في الصور نفخة واحدة

translation: And the earth and the mountains are lifted and leveled with one blow.
interpretation: This verse refers to the cataclysmic events of the Day of Judgment, when the earth and mountains will be utterly destroyed and flattened in a single devastating blow. It symbolizes the complete transformation and upheaval of the world as we know it, marking the end of the present order and the beginning of the eternal afterlife. The verse emphasizes the immense power and authority of God, who can effortlessly annihilate even the mightiest of His creations, and serves as a reminder of the inevitability and gravity of the final reckoning that all souls must face.
orig: وحملت الأرض والجبال فدكتا دكة واحدة

translation: Then on that Day the Event will occur.
interpretation: This verse is referring to the Day of Judgment, a central theme in Islamic eschatology. It emphasizes the inevitability and gravity of this event. The "Event" (al-Waqi'ah) is one of the names given to the Day of Judgment in the Qur'an. It signifies the momentous occasion when all of humanity will be resurrected and held accountable for their deeds in this world. The use of the word "then" (fa) at the beginning of the verse underscores the sequence of events leading up to Judgment Day and its definitive occurrence at the destined time decreed by Allah. This verse serves as a reminder to believers about the ultimate reality that awaits them, encouraging them to lead righteous lives in preparation for that decisive Day.
orig: فيومئذ وقعت الواقعة

translation: And the heaven will split [open], and that Day, it will be frail.
interpretation: This verse refers to the Day of Judgment when the sky will be torn apart and will be fragile, losing its strength and stability. It symbolizes the immense upheaval and destruction that will occur on that day, highlighting the magnitude and significance of the event. The splitting of the sky also represents the exposure of all that was hidden and the revelation of the ultimate truth. It serves as a reminder of the temporary nature of this world and the inevitability of facing the consequences of one's actions in the Hereafter.
orig: وانشقت السماء فهي يومئذ واهية

translation: And the angels will be on its sides, and eight will, that Day, bear the Throne of your Lord above them.
interpretation: This verse refers to the Day of Judgment when eight angels will carry the Throne of Allah above them. This symbolizes the majesty and power of Allah on that momentous day. The number eight may represent the eight directions or the eight angels who are closest to Allah. The verse emphasizes that on the Day of Judgment, Allah's sovereignty and authority will be fully manifest, and all of creation will submit to His will. It is a reminder for believers to be mindful of that day and to strive for righteousness in this life.
orig: والملك على أرجائها ويحمل عرش ربك فوقهم يومئذ ثمانية

translation: That Day, you will be exhibited [for judgement]; not hidden among you is anything concealed.
interpretation: On the Day of Judgment, all of our deeds, both good and bad, will be laid bare before Allah. Nothing will remain hidden, and we will be held accountable for everything we have done in this life. This verse serves as a reminder that we should be mindful of our actions and strive to live righteously, as ultimately, we will have to answer for all that we have done.
orig: يومئذ تعرضون لا تخفى منكم خافية

translation: Then as for he who is given his record in his right hand, he will say, "Here, read my record!"
interpretation: This verse refers to the believers who will receive their records of deeds in their right hands on the Day of Judgment. They will be proud and eager to have their records read out, knowing that they contain their good deeds. This symbolizes their confidence and happiness at having lived righteously in accordance with God's commands. Receiving the record in the right hand signifies success, salvation, and entry into Paradise as a reward for their faith and good deeds in this world.
orig: فأما من أوتي كتابه بيمينه فيقول هاؤم اقرءوا كتابيه

translation: Indeed, I was certain that I would be meeting my account [i.e., my reckoning].
interpretation: This verse conveys the believer's unwavering faith and certainty that they will face the reckoning of their deeds on the Day of Judgment. It emphasizes the importance of being mindful of one's actions in this world, knowing that every deed will be accounted for in the Hereafter. The verse serves as a reminder for individuals to strive for righteousness and to prepare themselves for the inevitable meeting with their Lord, where they will be held responsible for their choices and actions in this life.
orig: إني ظننت أني ملاق حسابيه

translation: So he will be in a pleasant life -
interpretation: This verse refers to the blissful state of the believers in Paradise. Those who lived a righteous life and followed the teachings of Islam will be rewarded with a life of contentment and satisfaction in the Hereafter. They will be pleased with their condition, enjoying the countless bounties and delights that Allah has prepared for them. This "pleasant life" is the ultimate goal and aspiration of every believer, and it serves as a motivation to persist in doing good deeds and avoiding sins during our worldly existence.
orig: فهو في عيشة راضية

translation: In a high garden.
interpretation: This verse refers to the elevated status and lofty position of the righteous believers in Paradise. The "high garden" symbolizes the exalted spiritual rank and the closeness to Allah that the pious servants will attain in the Hereafter as a reward for their faith and good deeds in this worldly life. It indicates that they will be granted a special place in the highest levels of Paradise, enjoying the ultimate bliss, serenity, and proximity to their Lord.
orig: في جنة عالية

translation: Its [fruit] to be picked hanging near.
interpretation: This verse is describing the fruits of Paradise, indicating that they will be within easy reach of its inhabitants. The phrase "qutufuha daniyah" suggests that the branches of the trees in Paradise will bend low, bringing their fruits close to those who desire to pick them. This imagery conveys the idea of the perfect accessibility and abundance of blessings in Paradise, where the believers will have everything they desire within their grasp, without any hardship or difficulty in obtaining it. It is a metaphor for the ease and comfort that the righteous will enjoy in the Hereafter as a reward for their faith and good deeds in this life.
orig: قطوفها دانية

translation: Eat and drink at ease for that which you have sent forth (good deeds) in days past!
