interpretation: This verse is addressing the righteous people in Paradise, inviting them to enjoy the delights and pleasures therein as a reward for the good deeds they had performed in their worldly life. It emphasizes the concept that the good actions one does in this temporary world will yield everlasting benefits in the Hereafter. The verse encourages believers to focus on doing good and reminds them that their efforts will not go unappreciated by Allah. It also highlights the contrast between the temporary nature of this world and the eternal bliss awaiting the righteous in Paradise.
orig: كلوا واشربوا هنيئا بما أسلفتم في الأيام الخالية

translation: But as for he who is given his record in his left hand, he will say, "Oh, I wish I had not been given my record"
interpretation: This verse refers to the Day of Judgment when people will be given the record of their deeds. Those who receive their record in their left hand will be the sinners who will express regret and wish that they had never been given their record of sins. This is because receiving the record in the left hand signifies that they will be condemned to Hell for their evil deeds. It reflects the despair and hopelessness they will feel upon realizing the consequences of their actions when it is too late to repent or make amends.
orig: وأما من أوتي كتابه بشماله فيقول يا ليتني لم أوت كتابيه

translation: But I do not know what my account is.
interpretation: This verse conveys the profound uncertainty and apprehension one feels about the unknown nature of the reckoning they will face on the Day of Judgment. It underscores the gravity of that day, where every soul will be held accountable for their deeds, yet they remain unaware of what that accounting will entail or what the outcome will be. This fear of the unknown adds to the overall sense of trepidation and emphasizes the importance of striving for good in this worldly life, in hopes of a favorable judgment in the next.
orig: ولم أدر ما حسابيه

translation: Oh, would that it had been the decisive one.
interpretation: This verse expresses a deep sense of longing and desire for the Day of Judgment, the "decisive one", to arrive. It reflects the believer's yearning for the ultimate resolution and justice that will be established on that day, when all deeds will be accounted for and the truth will be made clear. The verse conveys a feeling of impatience and eagerness for the arrival of that decisive moment, perhaps due to the challenges, trials, and injustices faced in this worldly life. It is a heartfelt plea for the final reckoning and the establishment of divine justice.
orig: يا ليتها كانت القاضية

translation: Of no avail will be to him his wealth
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the ultimate worthlessness of worldly riches and possessions in the afterlife. It conveys that on the Day of Judgment, an individual's wealth and material gains will be of no benefit or use in attaining salvation or escaping punishment. The verse serves as a reminder for humans to focus on good deeds, righteousness, and faith, rather than being preoccupied with amassing temporal wealth, as it holds no value or merit in the eyes of God when one's eternal fate is being determined.
orig: ما أغنى عني ماليه

translation: My power has departed from me.
interpretation: This verse is expressing a sense of loss and despair, as if the speaker's authority, influence or strength has suddenly vanished or been taken away from them. It conveys a feeling of helplessness, that whatever power or control they once had is now gone, leaving them weakened and vulnerable. The verse captures the anguish of someone who has been stripped of their might and stature.
orig: هلك عني سلطانيه

translation: Seize him and shackle him.
interpretation: This verse is likely referring to the punishment of the disbelievers and wrongdoers in the Hereafter. The command to "seize him and shackle him" indicates that they will be forcibly taken and bound, possibly before being cast into the Hellfire as mentioned in other verses. It emphasizes the severity and inevitability of the punishment that awaits those who reject faith and do evil deeds. The shackling could also symbolize the restriction and confinement that the denizens of Hell will suffer for eternity as a consequence of their actions in this world.
orig: خذوه فغلوه

translation: Then they will burn him in the Hellfire.
interpretation: This verse is a stark warning about the severe punishment that awaits those who reject faith and do evil deeds. The "Hellfire" mentioned here refers to the eternal abode of suffering and torment in the Hereafter, where sinners will be subjected to burning and other forms of unimaginable pain as a consequence of their actions in this world. The verse emphasizes the gravity of turning away from God's guidance and the importance of leading a righteous life to avoid such a terrible fate in the afterlife.
orig: ثم الجحيم صلوه

translation: Then in a chain whose length is seventy cubits, insert him.
interpretation: This verse is referring to the punishment of those who reject faith and persist in evil deeds. The "chain" mentioned here symbolizes the shackles of their own sins and misdeeds that will bind them in the afterlife. The length of seventy cubits emphasizes the severity and enormity of their punishment. It signifies that they will be completely trapped and immobilized by the consequences of their own actions, with no possibility of escape or respite. This verse serves as a stern warning to those who knowingly choose the path of transgression and reminds us of the ultimate accountability we all face for our deeds in this world.
orig: ثم في سلسلة ذرعها سبعون ذراعا فاسلكوه

translation: Indeed, he did not believe in Allah, the Almighty.
interpretation: This verse is referring to a person who lacks faith and belief in Allah, the Supreme Being. It emphasizes the gravity of disbelief, as Allah is described as "Al-Azeem" which means "The Almighty" or "The Magnificent". Disbelieving in Allah is considered a major sin in Islam, as faith in the oneness of God is the core principle of the religion. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of having unwavering faith in Allah and the consequences of rejecting His existence and supremacy.
orig: إنه كان لا يؤمن بالله العظيم

translation: And does not encourage the feeding of the poor.
interpretation: This verse is a criticism of those who are miserly and do not care for the needy. It emphasizes the importance of not only feeding the poor oneself, but also encouraging others to do so. The Qur'an places great importance on social welfare and taking care of the less fortunate members of society. Neglecting this duty or discouraging others from fulfilling it is seen as a serious moral failing. The verse implies that true righteousness and piety require active concern and practical steps to alleviate poverty and hunger.
orig: ولا يحض على طعام المسكين

translation: But he has not here this Day any devoted friend
interpretation: This verse suggests that on the Day of Judgment, the wrongdoers and disbelievers will find themselves alone without any close friends or helpers. Despite the relationships and bonds they may have had in this worldly life, those will be of no avail on that crucial Day. They will face the consequences of their actions individually, with no one to support them or intercede on their behalf before God. It emphasizes the importance of building a strong relationship with God and doing good deeds, as that is what will ultimately matter and benefit a person in the Hereafter.
orig: فليس له اليوم هاهنا حميم

translation: No food will there be for them but from Ghislin.
interpretation: This verse refers to the punishment of the disbelievers in Hell. "Ghislin" is a foul discharge from the bodies of the people of Hell, indicating that they will have no nourishment except this disgusting substance. It emphasizes the severity and repulsiveness of their penalty in the afterlife for rejecting faith in Allah. The verse serves as a stark warning of the consequences of disbelief and a reminder to embrace the path of righteousness to avoid such a dreadful fate.
orig: ولا طعام إلا من غسلين

translation: None will eat it except the sinners.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that only those who have transgressed and committed sins will partake in the consumption of the forbidden fruit of Zaqqum in Hell. It serves as a warning to those who engage in wrongdoing and highlights the consequences of their actions in the afterlife. The verse implies that the righteous and pious individuals will be spared from this punishment, as they have adhered to the path of righteousness and refrained from sinful behavior.
orig: لا يأكله إلا الخاطئون

translation: So I swear by what you see
interpretation: In this verse, Allah swears by the visible world that we perceive with our senses. This is to emphasize the truth and importance of what follows in the Qur'an. By drawing attention to the wonders of His creation that we can observe, Allah is reminding us of His power, wisdom, and the reality of His existence. The verse encourages reflection on the signs of Allah in the universe, which can strengthen faith and serve as evidence for the truth of His message in the Qur'an.
orig: فلا أقسم بما تبصرون

translation: And that which you do not perceive.
interpretation: This verse reminds us that there are many things in the universe that are beyond our perception and understanding. It encourages humility and the recognition that human knowledge is limited. The verse implies that there are realities and dimensions of existence that we cannot grasp with our senses or intellect, and that the true nature of the universe is known only to Allah. It is a call to acknowledge the vastness and complexity of Allah's creation, and to submit to His wisdom and power even in matters that we cannot comprehend.
orig: وما لا تبصرون

translation: It is the word of a noble Messenger.
interpretation: This verse affirms that the Qur'an is the word of a noble Messenger, referring to the Angel Gabriel who conveyed the divine revelation to Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him). It emphasizes the trustworthiness and high status of the angelic intermediary who delivered God's message to humanity. The verse underscores the divine origin and authenticity of the Qur'anic revelation, as it comes from a reliable and honored source in the heavenly realm.
orig: إنه لقول رسول كريم

translation: And it is not the word of a poet; little do you believe.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the Qur'an is not the work of a mere poet, as some of the disbelievers claimed. It is a divine revelation from Allah, and its wisdom and eloquence far surpass human poetry. The verse also implies that the disbelievers have little faith in the truth of the Qur'an, despite its clear signs and proofs. They are unwilling to accept it as the word of Allah, and instead seek to attribute it to human sources. However, the Qur'an challenges them to produce something similar if they truly believe it is the work of a poet, which they are unable to do.
orig: وما هو بقول شاعر قليلا ما تؤمنون

translation: Nor is it the word of a soothsayer, little do you remember.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the Qur'an is not the word of a mere soothsayer or fortune-teller, whose predictions are often baseless and rarely come true. It serves as a reminder to the people who doubt the divine origin of the Qur'an, urging them to reflect upon the profound wisdom and guidance contained within its verses. The phrase "little do you remember" suggests that people often forget or fail to recognize the true nature of the Qur'an, and should therefore strive to approach it with an open heart and mind, seeking to understand its message and apply its teachings in their lives.
orig: ولا بقول كاهن قليلا ما تذكرون

translation: A revelation from the Lord of the worlds.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the Qur'an is a divine revelation sent down by Allah, the Lord and Creator of all the worlds. It affirms the divine origin and authority of the Qur'an, establishing that it is not the work of Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) or any human being, but rather a direct communication from the Almighty Himself. This verse sets the foundation for the belief in the Qur'an as the ultimate source of guidance for humanity, as it comes from the One who has created and sustains the entire universe.
orig: تنزيل من رب العالمين

translation: And if he had made up about Us some [false] sayings,
interpretation: This verse is a stern warning to anyone who might attribute false statements to Allah or fabricate lies about Him. It emphasizes the gravity of such an action and the severe consequences that would befall someone who engages in this type of behavior. The verse implies that Allah is aware of all that is said and done, and that He will not tolerate any form of deception or falsehood, especially when it comes to His divine message and teachings. It serves as a reminder to be truthful and sincere in one's faith and to refrain from any form of dishonesty or manipulation when it comes to religious matters.
orig: ولو تقول علينا بعض الأقاويل

translation: We would have seized him by the right hand
interpretation: This verse is a warning to those who oppose or reject the message of Allah. It emphasizes Allah's power and control over all things. If He had willed, He could have easily seized the wrongdoer or punished them severely for their disobedience and arrogance. The "right hand" here symbolizes strength, authority, and the ability to subdue. It implies that no one can escape Allah's grasp or punishment if He decides to inflict it upon them. The verse serves as a reminder for people to be mindful of their actions and to submit to Allah's will, as He has the ultimate power and control over all affairs.
orig: لأخذنا منه باليمين

translation: Then We would have cut from him the aorta.
interpretation: This verse is a warning from Allah to those who oppose His messengers and reject His message. It emphasizes Allah's power and control over life and death. The "aorta" mentioned here is the main artery that carries blood from the heart to the rest of the body. Cutting it would result in immediate death. The verse implies that if Allah willed, He could easily take the life of those who defy Him, but He gives them respite and opportunities to repent and mend their ways. It also serves as a reminder to the believers that their lives are in Allah's hands and they should always strive to please Him and follow His guidance.
orig: ثم لقطعنا منه الوتين

translation: And there is none of you that can prevent Us from punishing him.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute power and authority of Allah over His creation. No one can stand in the way or prevent Allah from carrying out His will and decree. It serves as a reminder to humans that they are ultimately helpless before Allah and subject to His judgment and punishment if He so wills. The verse aims to instill a sense of humility, submission and taqwa (God-consciousness) in the believers, recognizing that their fate lies in Allah's hands alone.
orig: فما منكم من أحد عنه حاجزين

translation: And indeed, it is a reminder for the righteous.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the Qur'an serves as a powerful reminder and source of guidance for those who are mindful of Allah and strive to live righteously. It suggests that the righteous individuals will greatly benefit from the teachings and wisdom contained within the Qur'an, as it will help them stay on the straight path and maintain their God-consciousness. The verse implies that the Qur'an is not merely a book, but a divine reminder that has the power to transform the hearts and lives of those who approach it with sincere piety and devotion.
orig: وإنه لتذكرة للمتقين

translation: And indeed, We know that among you are those who deny.
interpretation: This verse is a warning from Allah that He is fully aware that there are those among the people who reject the message of Islam and the prophethood of Muhammad (peace be upon him). It serves as a reminder that no matter how much the deniers try to hide their disbelief, Allah knows what is in their hearts and will hold them accountable for their rejection of the truth. The verse also implies that the believers should not be disheartened by the presence of deniers, as this is something that Allah has already foretold and is a part of His divine plan.
orig: وإنا لنعلم أن منكم مكذبين

translation: And indeed, it [i.e., the Qur'an] is a cause of regret upon the disbelievers.
interpretation: The Qur'an serves as a source of profound regret and remorse for those who reject its message and deny the truth of Islam. They will realize, especially in the Hereafter, the grave error they made in not believing in the Qur'an and following its guidance. The disbelievers will feel immense sorrow and anguish for having turned away from the path of righteousness and for not heeding the warnings conveyed through the Qur'an. This verse emphasizes the consequences of disbelief and the ultimate regret that awaits those who choose to reject the divine message.
orig: وإنه لحسرة على الكافرين

translation: And indeed, it is the truth of certainty.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute truth and certainty of the Qur'an and its message. It asserts that there is no doubt or ambiguity in the divine revelation, and that believers can have complete faith and conviction in its teachings. The phrase "truth of certainty" (haqq al-yaqin) denotes the highest level of certainty, indicating that the Qur'an is not merely a probable truth, but an unequivocal and indisputable reality. This verse serves as a powerful affirmation of the Qur'an's authenticity and its status as the ultimate source of guidance for humanity.
orig: وإنه لحق اليقين

translation: So glorify the Name of your Lord, the Most Great.
interpretation: This verse is a command to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and all believers to glorify and praise Allah, the Most Great, by His beautiful names and sublime attributes. It reminds us to constantly remember and exalt Allah, acknowledging His greatness, majesty, and perfection in all aspects. By engaging in the remembrance of Allah and glorifying Him, we purify our hearts, strengthen our faith, and draw closer to Him. This verse emphasizes the importance of making the praise and glorification of Allah a central part of our lives, as it helps us maintain a strong connection with our Creator and keeps us grounded in humility and submission to His will.
orig: فسبح باسم ربك العظيم

translation: A questioner asked about a punishment bound to happen.
interpretation: This verse refers to an unbeliever who mockingly asked the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) about the punishment that Allah has promised the disbelievers in the Hereafter. The verse affirms that this punishment is inevitable and will certainly occur to those who reject faith in Allah and His messengers. It serves as a warning to those who doubt or deny the reality of divine retribution, emphasizing that the Day of Judgment and the consequences of one's deeds are an inescapable reality that every soul will face.
orig: سأل سائل بعذاب واقع

translation: For the disbelievers, there is no preventer [of Allah's punishment].
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that nothing can stop Allah's punishment from befalling those who reject faith and choose disbelief. It serves as a warning that the disbelievers will face the consequences of their actions and that no one can protect them from Allah's judgment. The verse implies the absolute power and authority of Allah over all His creation and the inevitability of divine justice.
orig: للكافرين ليس له دافع

translation: From Allah, Owner of the Ways of Ascent.
interpretation: This verse refers to Allah as the One who is Exalted above all creation. The "Ways of Ascent" signify the paths by which the angels and the believers' deeds ascend to Allah. It emphasizes Allah's Majesty, Grandeur, and Supremacy over all things. The verse reminds us that Allah is far above His creation, yet He is near to His servants through His Knowledge, Hearing, and Seeing. It encourages the believers to send their good deeds and prayers up to Allah through these ways of ascent, seeking His Pleasure and Nearness.
orig: من الله ذي المعارج

translation: The angels and the Spirit will ascend to Him during a Day the extent of which is fifty thousand years.
interpretation: This verse is referring to the Day of Judgment, indicating its immense length and gravity. The ascension of the angels and the Spirit (believed by many to refer to Angel Gabriel) to God on such a long "Day" emphasizes the vastness and timelessness of the divine realm compared to our earthly experience of time. It also alludes to the momentous events and the deliverance of judgment that will take place on that Day, the duration of which is known only to God. The mention of fifty thousand years could be literal or metaphorical to express an unimaginably long period, reminding humans of the eternal consequences of their actions in this temporary worldly life.
orig: تعرج الملائكة والروح إليه في يوم كان مقداره خمسين ألف سنة

translation: So be patient with gracious patience.
interpretation: This verse encourages the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and the believers to remain patient in the face of adversity and hardship. "Gracious patience" refers to a type of patience that is beautiful, dignified, and free from complaint or despair. It is a patience that stems from trust in Allah's plan and the recognition that all affairs are ultimately in His hands. The verse reminds us that in times of difficulty, we should turn to Allah with patience and perseverance, knowing that He will provide relief and guidance in due time. It is a call to maintain composure, steadfastness, and faith, even when faced with trials and tribulations.
orig: فاصبر صبرا جميلا

translation: Indeed, they see it [as] distant,
interpretation: This verse is referring to the disbelievers who view the Day of Judgment as something far off and unlikely to happen. They do not believe in the reality of the Hereafter and the accountability for their deeds. They see it as a distant event that will never come to pass, and thus they continue in their disbelief and transgression. The verse highlights the shortsightedness and delusion of those who reject the truth of the Day of Judgment, despite the clear signs and warnings given to them.
orig: إنهم يرونه بعيدا

translation: And We see it [as] near.
interpretation: This verse is referring to the Day of Judgment, which Allah sees as near, even if it may seem distant to human beings. It emphasizes the idea that time is relative and that the coming of the Day of Judgment is inevitable, as it is part of Allah's divine plan. The verse serves as a reminder for believers to be mindful of their actions and to prepare for the Day of Reckoning, as it can arrive at any moment, even if human perception may suggest otherwise.
orig: ونراه قريبا

translation: The Day the sky will be like murky oil,
interpretation: This verse is referring to the Day of Judgment, when the world as we know it will come to an end. The sky being like "murky oil" is a vivid metaphor indicating that the heavens will be in a state of turmoil and chaos. It suggests that the usual order and stability of the sky will be completely disrupted, reflecting the gravity and momentousness of that Day. The choice of the word "murky" to describe the oil emphasizes the unsettling and ominous nature of the events that will unfold. This description of the sky serves to underscore the complete upheaval and transformation that will occur on the Day of Reckoning, as the universe itself will bear witness to God's ultimate judgment of humanity.
orig: يوم تكون السماء كالمهل

translation: And the mountains will be like wool
interpretation: This verse is using a metaphor to describe the state of the mountains on the Day of Judgment. Just as wool is light, fluffy, and easily blown about by the wind, the mountains, despite their current strength and firmness, will be reduced to a similar state - light, crumbling, and scattered by the cataclysmic events of that Day. It emphasizes the complete upheaval and transformation that will occur, where even the mightiest and most solid of structures will not remain unaltered. The imagery conveys the power and momentousness of the Day of Reckoning, and the complete dissolution of the world as we know it in the face of God's judgment.
orig: وتكون الجبال كالعهن

translation: And no friend will ask [anything of] a friend,
interpretation: On the Day of Judgment, people will be so consumed with their own fate that even close friends will not ask about each other's condition. The bonds and relationships of this world will be rendered insignificant, as each individual will be solely concerned with their own reckoning before Allah. This verse emphasizes the severity and gravity of that Day, where everyone will stand alone to face the consequences of their deeds, without the support or inquiry of their loved ones.
orig: ولا يسأل حميم حميما

translation: They will see them. The criminal will wish that he could be ransomed from the punishment of that Day by his children
interpretation: This verse highlights the severity and inescapability of the punishment on the Day of Judgment. The criminals will be so desperate to avoid the torment that they would be willing to sacrifice even their own children as ransom. However, this verse implies that no ransom will be accepted, and everyone will face the consequences of their deeds. It emphasizes the importance of leading a righteous life and the ultimate accountability for one's actions in the Hereafter.
orig: يبصرونهم يود المجرم لو يفتدي من عذاب يومئذ ببنيه

translation: And his companion and his brother
interpretation: This verse is referring to the close relationships that one has in this world, such as a spouse or a sibling. It serves as a reminder that even these intimate bonds will be of no avail on the Day of Judgment, and that each soul will be held accountable for its own deeds. The verse emphasizes the individual nature of divine reckoning and the importance of focusing on one's own spiritual growth and righteousness, rather than relying on the merits or intercession of others, even those closest to us.
orig: وصاحبته وأخيه

translation: And his relatives who shelter him
interpretation: This verse refers to the importance of family ties and the responsibility of relatives to support and protect each other. It emphasizes the duty of family members to provide shelter, care, and assistance to their kin, especially in times of need or hardship. The verse highlights the value of strong familial bonds and the Islamic principle of maintaining good relations with one's relatives.
orig: وفصيلته التي تؤويه

translation: And whoever is on the earth entirely [so] then He saves him
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute power and control of Allah over all of His creation. It suggests that every single being on Earth is ultimately dependent on Allah for their salvation and well-being. No matter how powerful or self-sufficient someone may seem, in the end, it is only through Allah's mercy and will that they can be saved from harm or difficulty. This serves as a reminder for humankind to always turn to Allah and seek His protection and guidance, recognizing that He alone has the ability to provide true safety and security.
orig: ومن في الأرض جميعا ثم ينجيه

translation: No! Indeed, it is the Flame [of Hell],
interpretation: This verse is a stern warning about the severity of Hell-fire. The Arabic word "ladhaa" refers to the intense, blazing flames of Hell that will engulf the sinners. It emphasizes that Hell is not a mere figment of imagination or a metaphorical concept, but a real, tangible destination for those who reject faith and indulge in evil. The verse serves as a wake-up call for humans to mend their ways, seek forgiveness, and strive for righteousness to avoid this dreadful fate in the Hereafter.
orig: كلا إنها لظى

translation: Extracting the contents of the marrow bones.
interpretation: This phrase is referring to the Hellfire, which is so intense that it burns through the flesh and reaches deep into the bones to extract the marrow. It emphasizes the severity and thoroughness of the punishment in Hell for those who have earned it through their evil deeds and rejection of God's message. The graphic imagery serves as a powerful warning to encourage righteousness and obedience to Allah in this life.
orig: نزاعة للشوى

translation: You call the one who turned away and went away.
interpretation: This verse is addressing the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him), telling him that he is calling to the message of Islam even those who have turned away from it and rejected it. It is a reminder that the Prophet's duty is to convey the message, regardless of how people respond to it. The verse encourages perseverance in inviting others to the path of guidance, even in the face of rejection and opposition. It emphasizes the importance of not giving up on anyone, and continuing to reach out with the truth, leaving the ultimate outcome to Allah.
orig: تدعو من أدبر وتولى

translation: And collected [wealth] and hoarded.
interpretation: This verse is criticizing those who greedily accumulate wealth and possessions, hoarding them without spending in charity or using them for good. It suggests that merely gathering material riches is not praiseworthy, but rather wealth should be used in a way that is pleasing to Allah, such as helping the needy. Hoarding wealth without fulfilling one's obligations is seen as a blameworthy trait that stems from worldly attachment and miserliness rather than faith and righteousness.
orig: وجمع فأوعى

translation: Indeed, mankind was created anxious:
interpretation: This verse highlights a fundamental aspect of human nature - that humans are inherently prone to anxiety, impatience, and complaining. It suggests that when faced with difficulties or lack of resources, humans tend to become fearful and ungrateful. This anxiety is seen as an innate characteristic that humans are created with, emphasizing the weakness in human nature and the need for spiritual guidance and discipline to overcome these tendencies. The verse serves as a reminder for humans to be conscious of this predisposition and strive to cultivate patience, gratitude, and trust in God's plan, even in the face of adversity.
orig: إن الإنسان خلق هلوعا

translation: When evil touches him, he is full of lament.
interpretation: This verse suggests that when a person is afflicted with hardship or calamity, they may become impatient, anxious and full of complaints. Rather than being steadfast and turning to Allah in times of difficulty, they become despondent and lose hope. It is a reminder for believers to remain patient and have faith in Allah's plan, knowing that after every hardship comes ease. One should turn to Allah in supplication and seek His help and guidance during challenging times.
orig: إذا مسه الشر جزوعا

translation: And when good touches him, withholding [of it]
interpretation: This verse is referring to the nature of some people who, when blessed with wealth or good fortune, become stingy and withhold their blessings from others. They do not share their prosperity or use it for good causes, but rather keep it selfishly for themselves. This behavior is considered blameworthy in Islam, as Muslims are encouraged to be generous and to share their blessings with others, especially those in need. The verse highlights the negative trait of miserliness and the importance of being charitable and grateful for God's blessings.
orig: وإذا مسه الخير منوعا

translation: Except those who pray
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of prayer in Islam. Those who consistently observe their prayers and maintain a strong connection with Allah through worship will be among the successful ones in the Hereafter. Prayer is a fundamental pillar of Islam that helps individuals develop piety, humility, and righteousness. It serves as a reminder of one's purpose in life and helps to protect against sinful actions. Thus, those who establish prayer and fulfill this obligation sincerely will be exempt from the negative consequences mentioned in the previous verses, such as being among the negligent or facing difficulties in the afterlife.
orig: إلا المصلين

translation: Those who are constant in their prayer
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of being consistent and steadfast in performing the obligatory prayers. It suggests that those who maintain their prayers with devotion and regularity are among the successful believers. Prayers serve as a means to remember Allah, express gratitude, and seek guidance. By being "constant" in prayer, one demonstrates discipline, commitment, and submission to Allah's commands. This verse implies that maintaining regular prayer is a key characteristic of the righteous and a fundamental aspect of Islamic faith.
orig: الذين هم على صلاتهم دائمون

translation: And those in whose wealth there is a known right
interpretation: This verse refers to the obligation of giving a portion of one's wealth to those in need, such as the poor, the needy, and those who ask for help. It emphasizes the importance of recognizing the rights of others in one's wealth and the duty to share it with those less fortunate. The "known right" implies a fixed, predetermined portion that should be given, such as the obligatory alms (Zakat) in Islam. This verse encourages believers to be generous, compassionate, and socially responsible by acknowledging the rights of others in their wealth and actively seeking to fulfill those rights.
orig: والذين في أموالهم حق معلوم

translation: For the petitioner and the deprived.
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of giving charity to those in need. "The petitioner" refers to those who actively seek help, while "the deprived" refers to those who are in need but may not ask for assistance. The Qur'an encourages Muslims to be mindful of both groups and to provide support and aid to them. This verse emphasizes the Islamic principle of social responsibility and the duty to care for the less fortunate members of society.
orig: للسائل والمحروم

translation: And those who believe in the Day of Judgment.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of belief in the Day of Judgment, which is a fundamental tenet of Islamic faith. Believing in the Day of Judgment means acknowledging that every individual will be held accountable for their deeds in this world and will be rewarded or punished accordingly in the Hereafter. This belief serves as a powerful motivation for Muslims to lead righteous lives, as they know that their actions have consequences beyond this temporary worldly existence. It encourages them to strive for good, avoid evil, and maintain a strong connection with their Creator, as they prepare for the ultimate reckoning on the Day of Judgment.
orig: والذين يصدقون بيوم الدين

translation: And those who are fearful of the punishment of their Lord
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of having a healthy fear and reverence for Allah. Those who are truly mindful of Allah are always conscious of the consequences of their actions, knowing that they will be held accountable for their deeds in the Hereafter. They strive to avoid sin and disobedience, and they constantly seek Allah's forgiveness and mercy. This fear is not a paralyzing or despair-inducing fear, but rather a motivating force that drives them to be better Muslims and to live righteously. It is a sign of true faith and submission to Allah.
orig: والذين هم من عذاب ربهم مشفقون

translation: Indeed, the punishment of their Lord is not that from which one is safe.
interpretation: This verse serves as a stern warning to humanity that no one should feel secure or complacent against the punishment of Allah. It emphasizes the severity and inescapable nature of divine retribution for those who transgress the bounds set by Allah and persist in their wrongdoings. The verse aims to instill a sense of fear, caution, and mindfulness in the hearts of believers, reminding them to constantly strive for righteousness and avoid actions that may incur Allah's wrath. It underscores the absolute justice of Allah and the inevitability of facing the consequences of one's deeds in the Hereafter.
orig: إن عذاب ربهم غير مأمون

translation: And those who guard their chastity
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of maintaining sexual purity and chastity. It refers to those who protect their private parts from engaging in any unlawful sexual acts, whether it be fornication, adultery, or other immoral behaviors. They guard their chastity by lowering their gaze, avoiding temptations, and preserving their modesty. This verse highlights the virtue of self-control and the need to channel sexual desires only within the bounds of marriage as ordained by Allah. It is a reminder for believers to maintain their dignity, honor, and purity in their sexual conduct.
orig: والذين هم لفروجهم حافظون

translation: Except with their wives or those their right hands possess, for then they are not to be blamed.
interpretation: This verse outlines the boundaries of sexual relations in Islam. It states that sexual intimacy is only permissible within the confines of marriage or with female slaves that a man rightfully possesses. In these cases, men are not to be blamed or considered sinful for engaging in such relations. This verse reflects the idea that sexuality should be regulated and confined to specific, lawful contexts. It also alludes to the historical reality of slavery and concubinage, which was prevalent in 7th-century Arabian society when the Qur'an was revealed. However, it's important to note that Islam encouraged the freeing of slaves and greatly restricted the practice compared to pre-Islamic times.
orig: إلا على أزواجهم أو ما ملكت أيمانهم فإنهم غير ملومين

translation: But whoever seeks beyond that, then those are the transgressors.
interpretation: This verse warns against exceeding the limits set by Allah in seeking intimate relations. It implies that those who transgress beyond what is permissible, such as engaging in extramarital affairs or deviant sexual practices, are considered transgressors who have violated the boundaries of Allah's law. The verse emphasizes the importance of maintaining chastity and adhering to the guidelines of lawful intimate relations within the confines of marriage. Transgressing these limits is a serious sin that incurs Allah's displeasure and punishment.
orig: فمن ابتغى وراء ذلك فأولئك هم العادون

translation: And those who are faithful to their trusts and their covenant
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of being trustworthy and fulfilling one's obligations. It highlights that the righteous believers are those who uphold their responsibilities, whether it be in the form of trusts given to them by others or covenants they have made with Allah or with people. They are diligent in safeguarding what has been entrusted to them and are true to their word, fulfilling their promises and agreements. This verse stresses the significance of integrity, reliability, and honesty in the character of a believer.
orig: والذين هم لأماناتهم وعهدهم راعون

translation: And those who stand firm in their testimonies
interpretation: This verse refers to the believers who are truthful and steadfast in their testimonies and uphold justice. They do not conceal the truth or give false testimony, even if it goes against their own interests or the interests of those close to them. They are unwavering in their commitment to honesty and integrity, and they fulfill their duty to bear witness to the truth, as enjoined by Allah. This is a praiseworthy quality that is essential for maintaining justice and upholding the rights of others in society.
orig: والذين هم بشهاداتهم قائمون

translation: And those who carefully maintain their prayers.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of being consistent and punctual in performing the obligatory prayers. Those who "carefully maintain their prayers" are the ones who perform them on time, with proper focus, humility, and devotion. They make prayer a priority in their lives and do not allow other matters to distract them from this fundamental pillar of Islam. Maintaining prayers is a sign of true faith and submission to Allah, as it demonstrates discipline, obedience, and mindfulness of one's connection with the Creator. The verse implies that those who are diligent in their prayers will be among the successful ones in this world and the Hereafter.
orig: والذين هم على صلاتهم يحافظون

translation: Those will be in gardens, honored.
interpretation: This verse speaks about the reward of the righteous believers in the Hereafter. Those who lived their lives in accordance with God's commands and followed the path of righteousness will be honored and rewarded with the eternal bliss of Paradise. In these gardens of Paradise, they will be treated with utmost respect, dignity, and honor as a recompense for their good deeds and unwavering faith in this world. This verse serves as a reminder and motivation for believers to strive for righteousness in order to attain this great reward of being among the honored ones in the gardens of Paradise.
orig: أولئك في جنات مكرمون

translation: So those who disbelieved turn their heads toward you, hastening.
interpretation: This verse is referring to the disbelievers who, upon hearing the message of Islam, turn their heads towards the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) in haste and confusion. They are rushing to reject the message without giving it proper consideration or thought. The use of the word "hastening" implies that they are quick to dismiss the truth and are not willing to reflect on the message with an open mind and heart. It suggests a state of close-mindedness and an unwillingness to engage with the divine revelation. The verse highlights the stubborn attitude of the disbelievers and their resistance to the truth, even when it is presented to them clearly.
orig: فمال الذين كفروا قبلك مهطعين

translation: On the right and on the left, in two groups.
interpretation: This verse is referring to the people on the Day of Judgment, who will be divided into two groups: those on the right, who are the blessed and righteous believers, and those on the left, who are the condemned disbelievers and sinners. The term "'izīn" (عزين) denotes that these two groups will be distinct and separate from each other, emphasizing the stark contrast between their ultimate fates based on their beliefs and deeds in this worldly life.
orig: عن اليمين وعن الشمال عزين

translation: Does every person among them aspire to enter a Garden of Pleasure?
interpretation: This verse is questioning the aspirations and expectations of those who reject faith and do evil deeds. It suggests that they are deluded in thinking that they will be admitted into Paradise despite their actions and lack of belief. The rhetorical question implies that it is unreasonable and foolish for them to hold such hopes, as Paradise is reserved for those who believe and do righteous deeds. The verse serves as a wake-up call and admonition, urging people to realign their aspirations with the reality of God's judgment and the requirements for attaining His pleasure and reward.
orig: أيطمع كل امرئ منهم أن يدخل جنة نعيم

translation: No! Indeed, We have created them from that which they know.
interpretation: This verse is a reminder that Allah has created human beings from a substance that they are familiar with, which is the sperm. It emphasizes the idea that Allah has complete knowledge and power over His creation, and that humans should not be arrogant or dismissive of His signs and warnings. The verse also implies that since Allah created humans, He knows what is best for them and has the right to command and prohibit as He wills. Humans, on the other hand, have limited knowledge and should submit to Allah's guidance and wisdom.
orig: كلا إنا خلقناهم مما يعلمون

translation: But nay! I swear by the Lord of the Easts and the Wests that indeed We are able
interpretation: In this verse, Allah swears by Himself as the Lord of the places of sunrise and sunset, emphasizing His absolute power and ability over all things. It serves as a reminder to humanity that Allah's might and control extends over the entire universe, and that He is fully capable of accomplishing whatever He wills, including the resurrection of the dead and holding people accountable for their deeds on the Day of Judgment. The verse aims to instill a sense of awe, reverence, and humility in believers, urging them to recognize Allah's sovereignty and submit to His will.
orig: فلا أقسم برب المشارق والمغارب إنا لقادرون

translation: That We will change them and bring in their place a better people? And We are not to be outdone.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's power and control over His creation. It suggests that if the current people disobey or displease Him, He has the ability to replace them with others who are better and more obedient. The verse also asserts that nothing can prevent Allah from carrying out His will or hinder His plans. It serves as a warning to humanity that they should strive to follow the right path, as Allah can easily replace them if they fail to do so. Ultimately, it highlights the supremacy and omnipotence of Allah.
orig: على أن نبدل خيرا منهم وما نحن بمسبوقين

translation: So leave them to converse vainly and amuse themselves until they meet their Day which they are promised.
interpretation: This verse is a warning to those who reject the message of Islam and the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him). It instructs the Prophet to leave such people to their idle talk and amusement, as they will eventually face the Day of Judgment that they have been promised. The verse implies that engaging with those who persistently deny the truth is futile, and that their ultimate fate is already sealed. It also serves as a reminder to believers to focus on their own spiritual growth and not be distracted by the disbelief and mockery of others, as everyone will be held accountable for their actions on the Day of Reckoning.
orig: فذرهم يخوضوا ويلعبوا حتى يلاقوا يومهم الذي يوعدون

translation: The Day they will emerge from the graves rapidly as if they were, toward an erected idol, hastening.
interpretation: This verse refers to the Day of Resurrection when the dead will rise from their graves in haste, as if they are rushing towards a goal or destination that they were always striving for in their worldly lives. The use of the word "nusub" (erected idol) suggests that in their worldly lives, they were driven by false goals, materialistic aims and misguided objectives that they pursued single-mindedly, while neglecting their spiritual purpose. On the Day of Judgment, they will realize the futility and deception of their worldly pursuits, and will frantically rush towards their ultimate fate, as decreed by Allah. The verse serves as a powerful reminder of the fleeting nature of this world and the importance of leading a righteous life with the correct intentions and goals, in preparation for the eternal Hereafter.
orig: يوم يخرجون من الأجداث سراعا كأنهم إلى نصب يوفضون

translation: Their eyes humbled, humiliation will cover them. That is the Day which they were promised.
interpretation: This verse speaks about the state of the disbelievers on the Day of Judgment. Their eyes will be downcast out of shame and humiliation will envelop them completely. This is because they had been forewarned about this Day but they disregarded the warning and continued in their ways of disbelief and transgression. Now, on this momentous Day, they will face the consequences of their actions. The humbling of their eyes and the shroud of disgrace covering them signifies their utter helplessness, regret and despair on realizing the gravity of their mistakes, while it is too late to repent or make amends.
orig: خاشعة أبصارهم ترهقهم ذلة ذلك اليوم الذي كانوا يوعدون

translation: Indeed, We sent Noah to his people, [saying], "Warn your people before there comes to them a painful punishment."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of warning people about the consequences of their wrongdoings. God sent Prophet Noah to his people to warn them of the impending punishment if they continued to disbelieve and commit sins. It highlights the role of prophets as messengers of God, sent to guide people towards righteousness and save them from Divine retribution. The verse also implies that God gives people ample opportunities to repent and mend their ways before He sends down His punishment, which can be severe and painful for those who persist in their disobedience.
orig: إنا أرسلنا نوحا إلى قومه أن أنذر قومك من قبل أن يأتيهم عذاب أليم

translation: He said, "O my people, indeed I am to you a clear warner."
interpretation: In this verse, a prophet or messenger of God is addressing his people, warning them in clear terms about the consequences of their actions and the importance of following the right path. As a warner, his role is to convey the divine message and guide his people towards righteousness, cautioning them against incurring God's wrath through their misdeeds. The use of the phrase "clear warner" emphasizes the unmistakable nature of his warning and the urgency of heeding his advice to avoid the fate that befalls those who persist in their wrongdoings and disbelief.
orig: قال يا قوم إني لكم نذير مبين

translation: Worship Allah, fear Him, and obey me.
interpretation: This verse is a call to humanity from a prophet or messenger of God to worship Allah alone, to have consciousness and reverence for Him, and to follow the teachings and guidance brought by the prophet. It emphasizes the importance of monotheism, piety, and submission to the will of Allah as conveyed through His chosen messenger. The verse also highlights the role of prophets as guides and examples for mankind to follow in order to attain righteousness and earn Allah's pleasure.
orig: أن اعبدوا الله واتقوه وأطيعون

translation: He will forgive you of your sins and delay you for a specified term. Indeed, when the time [of death] appointed by Allah comes, it will not be delayed, if you only knew.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of seeking forgiveness from Allah and not delaying repentance. It reminds us that our time on earth is limited and that death will come at the appointed time, which cannot be postponed. The verse encourages us to seek Allah's forgiveness while we still have the opportunity, as delaying repentance may lead to missing the chance altogether. It also highlights the fact that Allah is All-Knowing and that we should be mindful of our actions and their consequences in the Hereafter.
orig: يغفر لكم من ذنوبكم ويؤخركم إلى أجل مسمى إن أجل الله إذا جاء لا يؤخر لو كنتم تعلمون

translation: He said, "My Lord, indeed I invited my people [to truth] night and day."
interpretation: In this verse, the prophet Noah is expressing his deep concern and sadness to Allah about his people's persistent disbelief. Despite his tireless efforts in calling them to the path of truth and righteousness both night and day, they remained obstinate in their ways. This highlights Noah's unwavering dedication to his prophetic mission, as well as the tremendous patience and perseverance he exhibited in the face of his people's resistance. It also underscores the importance of persistence and steadfastness in conveying the message of Islam, even in the face of adversity and rejection.
orig: قال رب إني دعوت قومي ليلا ونهارا

translation: But my invitation only increased their flight [from the truth].
interpretation: The more the Prophet called his people to the truth of Islam, the more they turned away and fled from it. They became more stubborn and persistent in their disbelief and rejection of the message, rather than being receptive to it. This shows the depth of their aversion to the truth and their determination to cling to their false beliefs and ways, despite the clear proofs and sincere efforts of the Prophet to guide them.
orig: فلم يزدهم دعائي إلا فرارا

translation: And indeed, every time I invited them that You may forgive them, they put their fingers in their ears, covered themselves with their garments, persisted, and were arrogant with [great] arrogance.
interpretation: This verse highlights the stubborn and arrogant nature of those who reject the message of Allah. Despite the repeated invitations to seek forgiveness, they actively choose to ignore the truth by symbolically blocking their ears and covering themselves, indicating their unwillingness to listen or change. They persist in their disbelief and display great arrogance, showing the depth of their resistance to the guidance offered to them. This behavior demonstrates the hardness of their hearts and their determination to remain in a state of denial, even when presented with the opportunity for divine forgiveness.
orig: وإني كلما دعوتهم لتغفر لهم جعلوا أصابعهم في آذانهم واستغشوا ثيابهم وأصروا واستكبروا استكبارا

translation: Then indeed, I invited them publicly.
interpretation: In this verse, the speaker, likely a prophet or messenger of God, is declaring that they have openly and publicly invited the people to the message of Islam. The use of the word "jaharan" emphasizes that this invitation was done openly and loudly, without any secrecy or hiding. This demonstrates the confidence and conviction of the speaker in their mission to spread the word of God and guide people to the right path. It also serves as a testament to their bravery in the face of potential opposition or persecution for openly preaching their faith.
orig: ثم إني دعوتهم جهارا

translation: Then indeed, I announced to them and confided to them secretly,
interpretation: This verse refers to Prophet Noah's efforts in preaching to his people. He made public declarations, inviting them to believe in Allah's message. He also reached out to them privately, having intimate conversations to persuade them to abandon their misguided ways. It emphasizes Noah's patience and determination in guiding his community, using various methods of communication to help them see the truth. The verse underscores the importance of persistence and employing wisdom in conveying the divine message to others.
orig: ثم إني أعلنت لهم وأسررت لهم إسرارا

translation: So I said, 'Ask forgiveness of your Lord. Indeed, He is ever a Perpetual Forgiver.'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance and power of seeking forgiveness from Allah. The speaker, likely a prophet or messenger, is urging his people to turn to Allah in repentance and seek His forgiveness. The description of Allah as "Ghaffara" (a Perpetual Forgiver) highlights His infinite mercy and willingness to forgive those who sincerely repent, no matter how numerous or grave their sins may be. It serves as a reminder that the door to repentance is always open, and that Allah's forgiveness knows no bounds for those who turn to Him with sincerity and humility.
orig: فقلت استغفروا ربكم إنه كان غفارا

translation: He will send [rain from] the sky upon you in [continuing] showers
interpretation: This verse is a promise from Allah to the believers that if they are righteous and obedient, He will bless them with abundant rain and prosperity. The word "midrar" suggests copious and continuous rainfall. This metaphorically represents the blessings and bounties, both material and spiritual, that Allah will shower upon those who follow His path. It is an encouragement for the believers to stay firm in their faith and do good deeds, with the assurance that Allah will reward them generously in this world and the Hereafter.
orig: يرسل السماء عليكم مدرارا

translation: And He will provide you with wealth and children, and He will make for you gardens, and make for you rivers.
interpretation: This verse highlights the blessings and rewards that Allah bestows upon those who believe in Him and follow His path. The mention of wealth and children signifies both material and emotional fulfillment, indicating that Allah provides for the believers' worldly needs and blesses them with the joy of family. The gardens and rivers are symbolic of the beauty, serenity, and abundance that Allah grants to His faithful servants, both in this life and in the Hereafter. This verse serves as a reminder of Allah's generosity and mercy, encouraging believers to remain steadfast in their faith and to trust in His providence.
orig: ويمددكم بأموال وبنين ويجعل لكم جنات ويجعل لكم أنهارا

translation: What is [the matter] with you that you do not attribute to Allah [due] grandeur
interpretation: The verse is questioning why people do not show proper reverence and respect to Allah, despite His greatness and power. It implies that humans should acknowledge Allah's majesty and have a sense of awe and veneration towards Him. The verse suggests that failing to attribute due grandeur to Allah is a shortcoming on the part of human beings, who should recognize His superiority and submit to His will with humility and reverence.
orig: ما لكم لا ترجون لله وقارا

translation: And He has created you in stages.
interpretation: This verse refers to the gradual development of the human being, both physically and spiritually. It alludes to the various stages of human embryonic development, from a drop of fluid to a clinging clot, to a lump of flesh, and then the formation of bones and muscles. Beyond the physical, it also points to the spiritual and intellectual evolution of the human soul through different phases of life, from infancy to adulthood and even beyond death, in the eternal life of the hereafter. It is a reminder of God's creative power and wisdom in fashioning the human being in such a meticulous and progressive manner.
orig: وقد خلقكم أطوارا

translation: Do you not see how Allah has created seven heavens in layers?
interpretation: This verse draws our attention to the wondrous creation of Allah in the heavens. The seven heavens, arranged in layers one above the other, demonstrate Allah's immense power and perfect design. It invites us to ponder upon the vastness and precision of the universe, recognizing the supreme wisdom behind its creation. The verse encourages mankind to reflect on these signs and appreciate the magnificence of Allah's handiwork, which can strengthen our faith and remind us of His greatness. It also highlights the harmony and order in the cosmos, as each layer of heaven has its own purpose and function within the grand scheme of creation.
orig: ألم تروا كيف خلق الله سبع سماوات طباقا

translation: And made the moon therein a [reflected] light and made the sun a burning lamp.
interpretation: In this verse, Allah is highlighting two of His great creations that benefit mankind - the moon and the sun. He has made the moon a source of reflected light that illuminates the night, while the sun is described as a burning lamp that provides immense heat and light during the day. This verse points to the perfect balance and harmony in Allah's creation, where the moon and sun serve specific purposes and operate according to His divine plan. It also reminds us of Allah's power, wisdom, and mercy in creating such magnificent celestial bodies for our benefit, guiding us through the darkness of the night and providing us with warmth and energy during the day.
orig: وجعل القمر فيهن نورا وجعل الشمس سراجا

translation: And Allah has caused you to grow from the earth a [progressive] growth.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the power and wisdom of Allah in creating human beings. It alludes to the fact that humans are created from the very elements found in the earth, and that their growth and development is a gradual process, much like the growth of a plant. This interpretation highlights the intimate connection between humans and the earth, and suggests that our physical and spiritual growth is guided by Allah's divine plan. It also implies that, just as plants are nurtured by the earth, we too are sustained and nourished by Allah's grace and provisions throughout our lives.
orig: والله أنبتكم من الأرض نباتا

translation: Then He will return you into it and extract you [another] extraction.
interpretation: This verse refers to the cycle of life and death ordained by Allah. It means that after creating humans from the earth, Allah will cause them to die and return their bodies to the earth. Then, on the Day of Resurrection, He will bring them forth from the earth once again, resurrecting them for judgment. This emphasizes Allah's power over life and death and the inevitability of the afterlife, encouraging believers to be mindful of their actions in this life as they will be held accountable in the next.
orig: ثم يعيدكم فيها ويخرجكم إخراجا

translation: And Allah has made for you the earth a spreading [surface].
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's benevolence and mercy towards His creation. He has spread out the earth and made it suitable for human habitation, providing a stable platform upon which we can live, build, and travel. It is a reminder of Allah's power and wisdom in designing the earth to perfectly suit our needs, and it encourages us to be grateful for this immense blessing. The verse also implies that we should use the earth responsibly and not abuse or exploit it, as it is a gift entrusted to us by our Creator.
orig: والله جعل لكم الأرض بساطا

translation: That you may go about therein in wide roads.
interpretation: This verse suggests that Allah has made the earth vast and spacious, with many paths and roads that people can traverse easily. It implies that the earth has been made suitable for human habitation and travel, allowing people to journey far and wide, explore new lands, and connect with one another. The "wide roads" mentioned could be interpreted both literally, as physical pathways, and metaphorically, as the various opportunities and avenues that life presents. Ultimately, this verse points to the bounty and mercy of Allah in creating a world that facilitates human activity and progress.
orig: لتسلكوا منها سبلا فجاجا

translation: Noah said, "My Lord, indeed they have disobeyed me and followed him whose wealth and children will not increase him except in loss."
interpretation: This verse highlights the frustration and disappointment of Prophet Noah (peace be upon him) with his people who refused to heed his warnings and instead followed those who were wealthy and powerful, but ultimately misguided. Noah complains to Allah that despite his tireless efforts to guide his people, they persisted in their disobedience and were swayed by the temporary allure of worldly gain and status. However, Noah recognizes that such pursuits are ultimately futile and will only lead to loss and ruin in the Hereafter. The verse underscores the importance of following divine guidance and not being deceived by the fleeting nature of worldly success and influence.
orig: قال نوح رب إنهم عصوني واتبعوا من لم يزده ماله وولده إلا خسارا

translation: And they planned a great plan.
interpretation: This verse refers to the plots and schemes of the disbelievers against the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and the message of Islam. It highlights the fact that the enemies of Islam are constantly plotting and planning to undermine and destroy the religion, but their plans are ultimately futile because Allah is the best of planners and He will always protect His religion and His believers. The verse serves as a reminder to the believers to remain steadfast in their faith and to trust in Allah's plan, even in the face of adversity and opposition.
orig: ومكروا مكرا كبارا

translation: And they said, 'Do not leave your gods and do not leave Wadd or Suwa' or Yaghuth and Ya'uq and Nasr.'
interpretation: This verse refers to the idols that were worshipped by the people of Noah. It shows their stubbornness and attachment to their false gods, even when faced with the truth of monotheism preached by Noah. The interpretation is that people can become so entrenched in their misguided beliefs and practices that they are unable to see the truth even when it is presented to them clearly. They cling to their false idols and refuse to abandon them, leading to their own destruction. The verse serves as a warning against following false beliefs and idols, and highlights the importance of embracing the truth and worshipping the One true God.
orig: وقالوا لا تذرن آلهتكم ولا تذرن ودا ولا سواعا ولا يغوث ويعوق ونسرا

translation: And they have misled many. And do not increase the wrongdoers except in error.
interpretation: This verse is a warning against those who lead others astray and commit injustice. It suggests that such people have already misguided many, and asks God not to let their misguidance and wrongdoing increase further. The implication is that those who persistently engage in misleading others and oppression only stray further from truth and righteousness. It serves as a reminder of the grave spiritual consequences of leading people away from God's path and indulging in injustice and tyranny.
orig: وقد أضلوا كثيرا ولا تزد الظالمين إلا ضلالا

translation: Because of their sins they were drowned and put into the Fire, and they found not for themselves besides Allah [any] helpers.
interpretation: This verse is a warning to those who persist in sin and disbelief. It indicates that due to their numerous transgressions and rejection of Allah's guidance, they will face a severe punishment in both this world and the Hereafter. The drowning mentioned could be a literal reference to a past nation or a metaphorical description of being overwhelmed by sin. Being put into the Fire signifies their ultimate fate in Hell as a consequence of their actions. Moreover, the verse emphasizes that on the Day of Judgment, no one will be able to help or protect them from Allah's justice, as they had failed to seek His assistance and mercy during their worldly life. This should serve as a reminder for individuals to repent, follow the righteous path, and seek Allah's help and forgiveness before it is too late.
orig: مما خطيئاتهم أغرقوا فأدخلوا نارا فلم يجدوا لهم من دون الله أنصارا

translation: And Noah said, "My Lord, do not leave upon the earth from among the disbelievers an inhabitant.
interpretation: In this verse, Prophet Noah prays to Allah to destroy all the disbelievers on earth who rejected his message and opposed him. This came after Noah had spent a long time preaching to his people, warning them of Allah's punishment if they continued in their disbelief and wrongdoing, but they persisted in their ways. Noah's prayer reflects his frustration and despair with his people's stubbornness and his desire for Allah to cleanse the earth of their corruption and disbelief. It also demonstrates Noah's complete trust and reliance on Allah to judge and deal with the disbelievers in His infinite wisdom and justice.
orig: وقال نوح رب لا تذر على الأرض من الكافرين ديارا

translation: If You leave them, they will lead Your servants astray and will beget none but wicked disbelievers.
interpretation: This verse is a warning from Allah that if the disbelievers are left unchecked, they will mislead the believers and lead them astray from the straight path. The offspring of such disbelievers will also be wicked and ungrateful, as they will be raised in an environment of disbelief and sin. It emphasizes the importance of protecting the believers from the influence of the disbelievers and the need to counter their efforts to spread corruption and disbelief in society.
orig: إنك إن تذرهم يضلوا عبادك ولا يلدوا إلا فاجرا كفارا

translation: My Lord, forgive me and my parents and whoever enters my house a believer and the believing men and believing women. And do not increase the wrongdoers except in destruction.
interpretation: This verse is a prayer for forgiveness and mercy. The speaker is asking Allah to forgive them, their parents, and all believing men and women who enter their home. It emphasizes the importance of forgiveness and the believer's duty to pray for the forgiveness of their fellow Muslims. The verse ends with a plea to Allah to bring about the destruction of the wrongdoers and oppressors, highlighting the ultimate fate that awaits those who persist in their wrongdoing and rejection of faith.
orig: رب اغفر لي ولوالدي ولمن دخل بيتي مؤمنا وللمؤمنين والمؤمنات ولا تزد الظالمين إلا تبارا

translation: Say, [O Muhammad], "It has been revealed to me that a group of the jinn listened and said, 'Indeed, we have heard an amazing Qur'an.
interpretation: This verse indicates that the message of the Qur'an is not limited to humans, but even the jinn, who are unseen beings created from fire, have listened to it and found it to be amazing and extraordinary. This suggests the universal appeal and profound impact of the Qur'an, as it can touch the hearts and minds of beings beyond the realm of humans. The jinn's acknowledgment of the Qur'an's remarkable nature serves as a testament to its divine origin and its ability to guide and inspire all of Allah's creation.
orig: قل أوحي إلي أنه استمع نفر من الجن فقالوا إنا سمعنا قرآنا عجبا

translation: It guides to the right course, and we have believed in it. And we will never associate anyone with our Lord.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of believing in the divine guidance provided by Allah and following the right path. It also highlights the fundamental principle of Islam, which is the oneness of Allah and the rejection of associating any partners with Him. The believers affirm their faith in the guidance and declare their unwavering commitment to monotheism, refusing to attribute any equals or partners to Allah. This interpretation underscores the significance of true faith and the necessity of maintaining a pure, unadulterated belief in the unity of God.
orig: يهدي إلى الرشد فآمنا به ولن نشرك بربنا أحدا

translation: And [it is] that our Lord, the Exalted, in His glory, has not taken a companion nor a child.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the fundamental Islamic belief in the absolute oneness and uniqueness of Allah. It negates the notion that Allah has a partner, spouse, or offspring, which is a common belief in some other religions. The verse affirms that Allah is self-sufficient, independent, and free from any need or resemblance to His creation. It reinforces the concept of Tawheed (monotheism) and rejects any form of shirk (associating partners with Allah) or attributing human characteristics to Him. The interpretation highlights the importance of maintaining a pure and unadulterated faith in the unity of Allah.
orig: وأنه تعالى جد ربنا ما اتخذ صاحبة ولا ولدا

translation: And that the foolish among us used to utter extravagant lies about Allah.
interpretation: This verse is referring to the false and exaggerated claims that some foolish people used to make about Allah, such as attributing sons or daughters to Him or claiming that He has partners or equals. The Qur'an firmly rejects such blasphemous statements and emphasizes that Allah is One, without any partners or offspring. The verse implies that making such outrageous claims about Allah is a sign of foolishness and lack of understanding of His true nature and attributes.
orig: وأنه كان يقول سفيهنا على الله شططا

translation: And we had thought that mankind and the jinn would never speak about Allah a lie.
interpretation: This verse conveys the idea that both humans and jinn, despite their differences, were expected to be truthful about God and not attribute false statements to Him. It suggests a sense of surprise or disappointment that some among them would resort to lying about God, as it goes against the inherent expectation of honesty and reverence towards the Divine. The verse implies the gravity of such an act, as speaking falsehoods about God is considered a major transgression in Islamic belief.
orig: وأنا ظننا أن لن تقول الإنس والجن على الله كذبا

translation: And there were men from mankind who sought refuge in men from the jinn, so they [only] increased them in burden.
interpretation: This verse is referring to the pre-Islamic practice of some Arabs who would seek protection from the jinn by invoking them or seeking refuge in them. However, by doing so, they only increased their own fear, anxiety, and misery. The jinn would take advantage of their weakness and ignorance, and would further misguide them away from the truth of Allah's message. This practice is condemned in Islam, as one should only seek refuge and protection in Allah alone, and not in any of His creation, as they themselves are in need of Allah's mercy and guidance. Seeking help from the jinn opens the door for misguidance and oppression.
orig: وأنه كان رجال من الإنس يعوذون برجال من الجن فزادوهم رهقا

translation: And they thought, as you thought, that Allah would never send anyone [as a messenger].
interpretation: This verse refers to the disbelievers who, like the people being addressed, assumed that Allah would not send any messenger to guide humanity. It highlights the arrogance and ignorance of those who reject the concept of prophethood and divine revelation. The verse implies that such an assumption is baseless and that Allah, in His wisdom, chooses to send messengers to guide people towards the right path. It serves as a reminder that the denial of prophethood is a common trait among those who reject the truth, and that believers should not be swayed by such misconceptions.
orig: وأنهم ظنوا كما ظننتم أن لن يبعث الله أحدا

translation: And we have sought to reach the heaven; but found it filled with stern guards and flaming fires.
interpretation: This verse suggests that the jinn, in their attempt to eavesdrop on the heavenly assembly and gain knowledge of the unseen, found the heavens heavily guarded by stern angels and flaming meteors. It implies that after the advent of Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him), the jinn were prevented from accessing the divine secrets that they used to overhear previously. The "stern guards" refer to the angels, while the "flaming fires" allude to the shooting stars used to drive away the jinn. This verse emphasizes the divine protection of the revelation and the unseen knowledge, making it inaccessible to the jinn and affirming the supreme authority of Allah over all realms.
orig: وأنا لمسنا السماء فوجدناها ملئت حرسا شديدا وشهبا

translation: And we used to sit therein in positions for hearing, but whoever listens now will find a burning flaming fire lying in wait for him.
interpretation: This verse refers to the jinn who used to eavesdrop on the heavenly assembly to gain knowledge of the unseen. However, after the advent of Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him), they were prevented from doing so by the shooting stars that were set as guards. The verse indicates that anyone among the jinn who tries to listen to the divine secrets now will be met with a severe punishment in the form of a piercing flame. This highlights the divine protection of the revelation and the unseen knowledge from any interference or tampering.
orig: وأنا كنا نقعد منها مقاعد للسمع فمن يستمع الآن يجد له شهابا رصدا

translation: And we do not know whether evil is intended for those on earth or whether their Lord intends for them a right course.
interpretation: This verse reflects the limited knowledge and understanding of human beings regarding the divine wisdom behind the events and circumstances that unfold in the world. It acknowledges that people cannot fully comprehend whether seemingly bad or good situations are ultimately intended for their benefit or detriment, as only Allah possesses the complete knowledge of the consequences and outcomes of all affairs. The verse emphasizes the importance of having faith and trust in Allah's plan, recognizing that His wisdom surpasses human perception and that He ultimately desires what is best for His creation.
orig: وأنا لا ندري أشر أريد بمن في الأرض أم أراد بهم ربهم رشدا

translation: And among us are the righteous, and among us are [others] not so; we were [of] divided ways.
interpretation: This verse suggests that among the believers, there are those who are righteous and pious, adhering strictly to the teachings of Islam and living a life of virtue. However, there are also those who fall short of this standard, not reaching the same level of righteousness. The verse acknowledges the diversity within the Muslim community, indicating that people have taken different paths and have varying levels of commitment to their faith. It serves as a reminder that not all believers are at the same spiritual level and that there is room for improvement and growth in one's religious devotion.
orig: وأنا منا الصالحون ومنا دون ذلك كنا طرائق قددا

translation: And we thought that we could not escape Allah in the earth, nor could we escape Him by flight.
interpretation: This verse highlights the realization of the jinn that they cannot evade or escape Allah's power and authority, whether by remaining on earth or attempting to flee from it. It emphasizes the all-encompassing nature of Allah's dominion and the futility of trying to hide or run away from His will. The verse serves as a reminder to all creatures, including humans, that submitting to Allah and seeking His mercy is the only path to salvation, as there is no place or means by which one can escape His judgment and authority.
orig: وأنا ظننا أن لن نعجز الله في الأرض ولن نعجزه هربا

translation: And indeed, when we heard the guidance [i.e., the Qur'an], we believed in it. And whoever believes in his Lord will not fear deprivation or burden.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of faith and belief in Allah. When one truly believes in Allah and follows the guidance of the Qur'an, they will have no fear of being deprived of Allah's blessings or being burdened with hardships. True faith instills a sense of security and trust in Allah's plan, knowing that whatever happens is ultimately for the best. The verse encourages believers to put their complete trust in Allah and to have confidence that their faith will protect them from any harm or loss, both in this world and in the hereafter.
orig: وأنا لما سمعنا الهدى آمنا به فمن يؤمن بربه فلا يخاف بخسا ولا رهقا

translation: And among us are Muslims [in submission to Allah] and among us are the unjust. And whoever has become Muslim - those have sought out the right course.
interpretation: This verse highlights the fact that within the Muslim community, there are those who are truly submitting to Allah and following the right path, while there are also those who are unjust and not adhering to the teachings of Islam. It emphasizes the importance of sincerely embracing Islam and seeking the guidance of Allah, as those who do so are considered to be on the right course towards salvation and success in both this life and the hereafter. The verse serves as a reminder for Muslims to strive for righteousness and to be cautious of falling into injustice or disobedience to Allah.
orig: وأنا منا المسلمون ومنا القاسطون فمن أسلم فأولئك تحروا رشدا

translation: And as for the deviators, they will be firewood for Hell.
