interpretation: This verse warns that those who deviate from the straight path and the teachings of Islam will face severe consequences in the Hereafter. They will be used as fuel for the Fire of Hell, emphasizing the gravity of their actions and the punishment that awaits them. It serves as a reminder for believers to stay steadfast in their faith and to avoid straying from the right course, as the ultimate fate of the deviators is eternal suffering in the blazing flames of Hell.
orig: وأما القاسطون فكانوا لجهنم حطبا

translation: If they had remained straight on the Path, We would have given them abundant water to drink
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of staying steadfast on the straight path of Islam. It suggests that if people adhere to the teachings and guidance provided by Allah, they will be blessed with abundant spiritual sustenance and blessings, symbolized by the metaphorical "abundant water". The verse implies that deviating from the straight path leads to spiritual deprivation and loss of divine favors. It serves as an encouragement for believers to remain committed to their faith and to follow the righteous way, as it will lead to spiritual prosperity and the attainment of Allah's blessings in this life and the hereafter.
orig: وأن لو استقاموا على الطريقة لأسقيناهم ماء غدقا

translation: So We may test them thereby. And whoever turns away from the remembrance of his Lord He will put into arduous punishment.
interpretation: This verse warns that those who turn away from the remembrance of Allah and His guidance will face a severe and ever-increasing punishment in the Hereafter. It emphasizes the importance of staying connected to Allah through remembrance, obedience, and following His commandments. The verse also suggests that the blessings and bounties given to humans in this world are a test to see who will be grateful and remain steadfast in faith, and who will become heedless and turn away from the path of righteousness. Ultimately, those who persistently ignore Allah's messages and fail to live by His guidance will find themselves in a state of perpetual torment and hardship in the Afterlife.
orig: لنفتنهم فيه ومن يعرض عن ذكر ربه يسلكه عذابا صعدا

translation: And the places of worship are for Allah, so do not invoke anyone along with Allah.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of dedicating worship solely to Allah and not associating any partners with Him. It serves as a reminder that mosques and other places of worship are sacred spaces meant for the remembrance and worship of Allah alone. Muslims should not invoke or pray to anyone else alongside Allah, as it goes against the fundamental principle of Islamic monotheism (tawheed). This verse encourages sincerity in faith and the avoidance of any form of idolatry or polytheism, even within the walls of a mosque.
orig: وأن المساجد لله فلا تدعوا مع الله أحدا

translation: And when the servant of Allah stood up in prayer to Him, they crowded on him, almost stifling him.
interpretation: This verse refers to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and the early Muslims who faced intense opposition and hostility from the polytheists of Mecca when they began to worship Allah alone and reject idolatry. The verse indicates that when the Prophet stood up to pray and call upon Allah, the disbelievers would gather around him in a hostile manner, crowding him and trying to discourage or intimidate him from his worship. This reflects the severe challenges and persecution faced by the early Muslim community in their struggle to establish monotheism and the worship of Allah alone.
orig: وأنه لما قام عبد الله يدعوه كادوا يكونون عليه لبدا

translation: Say, "I only invoke my Lord and do not associate anyone with Him."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of pure monotheism in Islam. The Prophet Muhammad is instructed to declare that he worships Allah alone and does not associate any partners with Him. This is a fundamental principle of Islamic belief, known as Tawheed, which rejects the idea of polytheism or the worship of anyone or anything besides Allah. The verse also implies that invoking others besides Allah is a form of shirk (associating partners with Allah), which is considered a grave sin in Islam. Muslims are encouraged to direct all their worship, supplications, and devotion to Allah alone, seeking His guidance and assistance in all matters of life.
orig: قل إنما أدعو ربي ولا أشرك به أحدا

translation: Say, "Indeed, I do not possess for you [the power of] harm or right direction."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the fact that the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) does not have the power to bring harm or benefit to anyone, nor can he guide anyone to the right path. It is a reminder that ultimate power and guidance belong to Allah alone. The Prophet's role is only to convey the message and serve as an example for others to follow. It also highlights the importance of seeking guidance directly from Allah through prayer, supplication, and reflecting upon the Qur'an, rather than relying solely on intermediaries or religious figures.
orig: قل إني لا أملك لكم ضرا ولا رشدا

translation: Say, "Indeed, there is no one who can protect me from Allah, nor can I find any refuge apart from Him."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute power and authority of Allah. It conveys the message that no one can provide protection or shelter from Allah's judgment and that seeking refuge in anything or anyone other than Him is futile. It highlights the importance of complete submission to Allah and reliance on Him alone, as He is the only true source of security and guidance. The verse also implies that one should fear Allah and be mindful of their actions, as there will be no escape from the consequences decreed by Him.
orig: قل إني لن يجيرني من الله أحد ولن أجد من دونه ملتحدا

translation: But [their duty is] only to convey [the message] from Allah and His messages. And whoever disobeys Allah and His Messenger - then indeed, for him is the fire of Hell; they will abide therein forever.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the role of the messengers as conveyers of Allah's message and warnings. Their duty is only to deliver the divine revelation, and it is up to the people to accept or reject it. Those who choose to disobey Allah and His Messenger will face the severe consequence of eternal punishment in the Hellfire. The verse serves as a stern warning to those who reject the message and persist in their disobedience, highlighting the gravity of their choice and the ultimate fate that awaits them in the Hereafter.
orig: إلا بلاغا من الله ورسالاته ومن يعص الله ورسوله فإن له نار جهنم خالدين فيها أبدا

translation: Until, when they see that which they are promised, then they will know who is weaker in helpers and less in number.
interpretation: This verse is a warning to the disbelievers who reject God's message and His prophets. It states that when the Day of Judgment arrives and they witness the fulfillment of God's promise of punishment, they will realize how weak and few in number their helpers and supporters truly are. They will understand the futility of relying on anyone or anything other than God. The verse emphasizes the powerlessness of the disbelievers in the face of God's might and justice on that fateful day when no one can escape His judgment. It serves as a reminder for people to put their faith and trust in God alone.
orig: حتى إذا رأوا ما يوعدون فسيعلمون من أضعف ناصرا وأقل عددا

translation: Say, "I do not know if what you are promised is near or if my Lord will grant for it an [extended] period."
interpretation: This verse conveys the idea that even the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) did not have knowledge of when the Day of Judgment would occur. It emphasizes that the timing of this event is known only to Allah. The verse instructs the Prophet to inform people that he does not know whether the promised Day of Judgment is near or if Allah has set for it a distant time. This highlights the principle that the knowledge of the unseen, including the timing of the Day of Judgment, belongs exclusively to Allah. It serves as a reminder for believers to focus on preparing for that Day through righteous deeds, rather than speculating about its exact timing.
orig: قل إن أدري أقريب ما توعدون أم يجعل له ربي أمدا

translation: He is the Knower of the unseen, and He does not disclose His unseen to anyone,
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute knowledge of Allah, particularly regarding the unseen realm (al-ghayb). It asserts that Allah alone possesses complete knowledge of the unseen, and He does not reveal this knowledge to anyone in its entirety. The unseen encompasses various aspects, such as the future, the inner thoughts and intentions of people, and the metaphysical realities that are beyond human perception. The verse highlights the exclusivity of Allah's knowledge and the fact that no one can access it without His permission. It serves as a reminder for believers to trust in Allah's wisdom and to acknowledge the limitations of human understanding when it comes to the mysteries of the unseen world.
orig: عالم الغيب فلا يظهر على غيبه أحدا

translation: Except for the messenger He has approved, for he will have angels before him and behind him, watching over him,
interpretation: This verse indicates that Allah protects His chosen messengers by assigning angels to guard them from both front and back. These angels act as a divine security detail, ensuring that the messenger can carry out their mission without interference or harm. This special protection is a sign of Allah's favor and approval towards the messenger, emphasizing their elevated status and the importance of the message they carry. It also serves as a reminder that the words and actions of these chosen individuals are safeguarded by Allah, lending them an added level of credibility and authority.
orig: إلا من ارتضى من رسول فإنه يسلك من بين يديه ومن خلفه رصدا

translation: That he may know that they have conveyed the messages of their Lord; and He has encompassed whatever is with them and has enumerated all things in number.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of conveying the message of Allah faithfully and completely. It assures that Allah is fully aware of everything that the messengers do and say, and that He keeps a precise record of all things. The verse implies that the messengers will be held accountable for their mission, and that they should strive to fulfill it to the best of their abilities, knowing that Allah is watching over them and will judge them based on their deeds. It also serves as a reminder to all believers to be mindful of their actions and to strive to please Allah in all aspects of their lives.
orig: ليعلم أن قد أبلغوا رسالات ربهم وأحاط بما لديهم وأحصى كل شيء عددا

translation: O you who wraps himself [in clothing],
interpretation: This verse is addressing the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him), who used to wrap himself in a garment during worship or when receiving revelation. It could be interpreted as a gentle and affectionate way of calling upon the Prophet, showing Allah's love and care for him. The verse serves as an introduction to the subsequent verses which instruct the Prophet regarding prayer, recitation of the Qur'an, and being patient in the face of adversity. It highlights the special status of the Prophet as the recipient of divine revelation and guidance.
orig: يا أيها المزمل

translation: Stand [in prayer] during the night, except for a little -
interpretation: This verse is encouraging the believers to spend a significant portion of the night in prayer and devotion to Allah. The night prayer, known as Tahajjud, is a highly recommended voluntary act of worship that brings one closer to Allah and helps in spiritual purification. The verse indicates that one should stand in prayer for most of the night, except for a small portion, which can be used for rest and sleep. This dedication to nightly worship demonstrates sincerity, commitment, and the willingness to sacrifice comfort for the sake of seeking Allah's pleasure and guidance.
orig: قم الليل إلا قليلا

translation: Half of it, or lessen from it a little.
interpretation: This verse is giving permission to reduce the amount of night prayer from half of the night to a little less than that, according to one's capacity and circumstances. It shows Allah's mercy and consideration for the believers, recognizing that praying for half the night every night may be difficult to sustain. The verse encourages consistency and doing what is manageable in the long term, rather than taking on more than one can handle and then giving up completely.
orig: نصفه أو انقص منه قليلا

translation: Or add to it, and recite the Qur'an with measured recitation.
interpretation: This verse instructs the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and the believers to recite the Qur'an slowly, carefully, and with proper pronunciation and intonation. The measured recitation allows for deeper reflection on the meanings of the verses and helps in memorizing the Qur'an. It also emphasizes the importance of dedicating time to the Qur'an and increasing one's engagement with it. The verse encourages believers to make the recitation of the Qur'an a regular practice and to strive for improvement in the quality of their recitation.
orig: أو زد عليه ورتل القرآن ترتيلا

translation: Indeed, We will cast upon you a heavy word.
interpretation: This verse is addressing the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him), informing him that Allah will reveal to him a weighty and significant message, which is the Qur'an. The word "heavy" here symbolizes the profound responsibility and the great importance of the revelation that the Prophet will receive. It indicates that the message is not merely words, but a substantial and impactful revelation that carries immense wisdom, guidance, and obligations. The verse also implies that the Prophet will need to bear the burden of conveying this message to humanity, facing challenges and opposition in the process. However, it is a task that Allah has chosen him for, and He will support him in fulfilling this momentous duty.
orig: إنا سنلقي عليك قولا ثقيلا

translation: Indeed, the night prayer is more effective and more suitable for recitation.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance and value of praying at night, particularly the voluntary night prayers known as Tahajjud. It suggests that praying during the night, when there are fewer distractions and one can focus more intently on their connection with Allah, is more impactful and meaningful than prayers during the day. The tranquility and stillness of the night allows for greater concentration, devotion, and sincerity in one's supplications and recitation of the Qur'an. The verse encourages believers to make an effort to wake up and engage in this highly rewarding spiritual practice, even if it requires sacrificing some sleep. It highlights that the words spoken in night prayers are more precise, aligned with righteousness, and carry more weight in the sight of Allah.
orig: إن ناشئة الليل هي أشد وطئا وأقوم قيلا

translation: Verily, you have by day prolonged occupation.
interpretation: This verse is addressing Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him), reminding him that he has many duties and responsibilities to attend to during the day, such as conveying the message of Islam, leading the believers, and managing the affairs of the community. The phrase "prolonged occupation" suggests that these tasks require significant time and effort. The verse implies that the Prophet should dedicate himself to these important duties during the day, while reserving the night for spiritual devotion and seeking nearness to Allah through prayer and meditation. It emphasizes the importance of balancing worldly obligations with spiritual pursuits and allocating time wisely to fulfill both aspects of life.
orig: إن لك في النهار سبحا طويلا

translation: And remember the name of your Lord and devote yourself to Him with [complete] devotion.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of remembering Allah and dedicating oneself to Him completely. It encourages the believer to constantly invoke Allah's name and engage in His remembrance (dhikr) with sincerity and devotion. The word "tabattul" implies detaching oneself from worldly distractions and focusing solely on worshipping and connecting with Allah. This verse highlights the significance of having a strong spiritual connection with Allah and making Him the central focus of one's life, thoughts, and actions. It serves as a reminder to prioritize one's relationship with Allah above all else and to strive for complete submission and devotion to Him.
orig: واذكر اسم ربك وتبتل إليه تبتيلا

translation: Lord of the East and the West; there is no deity except Him, so take Him as Disposer of [your] affairs.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute oneness and uniqueness of Allah, who is the Lord and Sustainer of the entire universe, from the East to the West. It affirms that there is no god worthy of worship except Him alone. Therefore, one should put their complete trust in Allah and rely upon Him in all their affairs, making Him the ultimate guardian and disposer of their matters. This highlights the importance of Tawheed (belief in the oneness of Allah) and Tawakkul (reliance on Allah) in a believer's life.
orig: رب المشرق والمغرب لا إله إلا هو فاتخذه وكيلا

translation: And be patient over what they say, and avoid them with gracious avoidance.
interpretation: This verse advises the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and the believers to remain patient in the face of the hurtful words and actions of the disbelievers. It encourages them to respond with dignity and grace, avoiding confrontation and hostility. The "gracious avoidance" mentioned in the verse suggests that Muslims should distance themselves from those who mock or insult their faith, but to do so in a manner that is not rude or aggressive. This patient and peaceful response is seen as a sign of strength and faith, reflecting the believer's trust in Allah's plan and their commitment to following the path of righteousness, even in the face of adversity.
orig: واصبر على ما يقولون واهجرهم هجرا جميلا

translation: And leave Me alone with the deniers, those of ease and plenty, and allow them respite a little.
interpretation: This verse is a warning to those who reject the message of Islam despite being blessed with wealth and comfort in this worldly life. Allah is telling the Prophet to leave these deniers to Him, as He will deal with them accordingly. The verse implies that their wealth and ease should not deceive them into thinking they can escape the consequences of their disbelief. They are only being granted a short respite, and will soon face the recompense for their ingratitude and denial of the truth. It serves as a reminder that worldly blessings are temporary, and one's ultimate fate depends on their faith and deeds.
orig: وذرني والمكذبين أولي النعمة ومهلهم قليلا

translation: Indeed, We have shackles and a blazing Fire.
interpretation: This verse serves as a stern warning to those who reject God's message and persist in wrongdoing. The "shackles" symbolize the spiritual bondage and suffering that the disbelievers will face in the Hereafter as a consequence of their actions. The "blazing Fire" refers to the torment of Hell, emphasizing the severe punishment awaiting those who turn away from the path of righteousness. The verse aims to instill fear and encourage people to reflect upon their deeds, seeking to guide them towards repentance and obedience to God before it is too late.
orig: إن لدينا أنكالا وجحيما

translation: And food that chokes and a painful punishment.
interpretation: This verse warns of the severe consequences that await those who reject faith and persist in wrongdoing. The "food that chokes" symbolizes the anguish and regret they will experience in the Hereafter for their misdeeds. The "painful punishment" emphasizes the intense suffering they will endure as a result of earning God's wrath through their disobedience and transgression. It serves as a powerful reminder for people to be mindful of their actions in this life, as they will be held accountable in the next.
orig: وطعاما ذا غصة وعذابا أليما

translation: On the Day when the earth and the mountains will shake, and the mountains will become a heap of pouring sand.
interpretation: This verse is referring to the Day of Judgment, when the world as we know it will come to an end. The shaking of the earth and mountains symbolizes the massive upheaval and destruction that will take place. The mountains, which are usually seen as symbols of stability and permanence, will be reduced to mere piles of sand, showing that nothing in this world is truly lasting or secure. This imagery is meant to convey the awesome power of Allah and the momentous nature of the Day of Judgment, when all of humanity will be called to account for their deeds in this life. It is a reminder for people to be mindful of their actions and to strive for righteousness, as the consequences of our choices in this world will be made manifest on that Day.
orig: يوم ترجف الأرض والجبال وكانت الجبال كثيبا مهيلا

translation: Indeed, We have sent to you a Messenger as a witness upon you just as We sent to Pharaoh a messenger.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance and authority of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) as a messenger of Allah, drawing a parallel between him and Moses, who was sent to Pharaoh. Just as Moses was sent to guide Pharaoh and his people, Muhammad was sent as a witness and guide for all of humanity. This comparison also serves as a warning to those who reject the message of Islam, reminding them of the fate that befell Pharaoh and his people when they refused to accept the truth brought by Moses. The verse underscores the universality of Muhammad's message and the gravity of the choice faced by those to whom it is conveyed.
orig: إنا أرسلنا إليكم رسولا شاهدا عليكم كما أرسلنا إلى فرعون رسولا

translation: But Pharaoh disobeyed the messenger, so We seized him with a ruinous seizure.
interpretation: This verse is a warning to those who reject the message of Allah and His messengers. Pharaoh, despite being shown clear signs and miracles, arrogantly refused to believe in the message brought by Moses. As a result, Allah punished him severely in this world and the Hereafter. The "ruinous seizure" refers to the drowning of Pharaoh and his army in the Red Sea as they pursued Moses and the Children of Israel. This verse emphasizes that no one, not even the most powerful rulers, can escape the consequences of disobeying Allah and rejecting His guidance. It serves as a reminder for all of mankind to humble themselves before the Almighty and follow the path of righteousness as shown by His prophets and messengers.
orig: فعصى فرعون الرسول فأخذناه أخذا وبيلا

translation: Then how will you guard yourselves, if you disbelieve, on a Day that will make the children white-haired?
interpretation: This verse is a stark warning to those who reject faith in Allah. It speaks of the Day of Judgment, which will be so terrifying that even children will turn gray-haired from its horror. The rhetorical question "Then how will you guard yourselves" implies that there will be no escape or protection for the disbelievers on that Day. They will face the full consequences of their denial and ingratitude. The shocking imagery of children turned aged drives home the severity and inescapability of divine justice. It is a powerful reminder to have faith, be grateful to Allah, and live righteously to avoid such a dreadful fate in the Hereafter.
orig: فكيف تتقون إن كفرتم يوما يجعل الولدان شيبا

translation: The sky will break apart therefrom; His promise is ever fulfilled.
interpretation: This verse speaks about the Day of Judgment, when the sky will be torn apart, signifying the magnitude and gravity of that event. The phrase "His promise is ever fulfilled" emphasizes the certainty and inevitability of Allah's promise concerning the Day of Judgment. It serves as a reminder to humanity that the Day of Reckoning is a reality that will come to pass, as Allah has decreed, and that everyone will be held accountable for their deeds in this world. The verse underscores the importance of leading a righteous life and being mindful of one's actions, as the consequences in the Hereafter are inescapable.
orig: السماء منفطر به كان وعده مفعولا

translation: Indeed, this is a reminder, so whoever wills may take to his Lord a way.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the Qur'an serves as a reminder and a guide for those who seek to draw closer to Allah. It highlights the concept of free will, indicating that individuals have the choice to either accept the message and follow the path leading to their Lord or to reject it. The verse encourages people to make a conscious decision to embrace the Qur'anic teachings and embark on a spiritual journey towards Allah, seeking His pleasure and guidance. It underscores the importance of personal responsibility and the active role one must play in their own spiritual growth and development.
orig: إن هذه تذكرة فمن شاء اتخذ إلى ربه سبيلا

translation: Indeed, your Lord knows, [O Muhammad], that you stand [in prayer] almost two thirds of the night or half of it or a third of it, and [so do] a group of those with you. And Allah determines [the extent of] the night and the day. He has known that you [Muslims] will not be able to do it and has turned to you in forgiveness, so recite what is easy [for you] of the Qur'an. He has known that there will be among you those who are ill and others traveling throughout the land seeking [something] of the bounty of Allah and others fighting for the cause of Allah. So recite what is easy from it and establish prayer and give zakah and loan Allah a goodly loan. And whatever good you put forward for yourselves - you will find it with Allah. It is better and greater in reward. And seek forgiveness of Allah. Indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's omniscience and understanding of the varying circumstances and abilities of His servants. It encourages the believers to pray and recite the Qur'an according to their capacity, acknowledging that some may be unable to pray for long hours due to illness, travel, or engagement in jihad. The verse also urges Muslims to give charity and do good deeds, with the promise that they will find their rewards with Allah, who is the most generous and forgiving. This interpretation highlights the importance of striving in worship and good deeds while maintaining a balance based on one's individual situation, as well as the boundless mercy and forgiveness of Allah towards His servants.
orig: إن ربك يعلم أنك تقوم أدنى من ثلثي الليل ونصفه وثلثه وطائفة من الذين معك والله يقدر الليل والنهار علم أن لن تحصوه فتاب عليكم فاقرءوا ما تيسر من القرآن علم أن سيكون منكم مرضى وآخرون يضربون في الأرض يبتغون من فضل الله وآخرون يقاتلون في سبيل الله فاقرءوا ما تيسر منه وأقيموا الصلاة وآتوا الزكاة وأقرضوا الله قرضا حسنا وما تقدموا لأنفسكم من خير تجدوه عند الله هو خيرا وأعظم أجرا واستغفروا الله إن الله غفور رحيم

translation: O you who covers himself [with a garment],
interpretation: This verse is addressing the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him), who is being called upon by Allah. The word "muddathir" refers to one who covers himself with a garment or blanket, which the Prophet used to do when he received revelation. The verse serves as a direct call to the Prophet to rise to his duty of conveying the message of Islam and warning people, even as he faces challenges and opposition in doing so. It signifies the beginning of his public ministry and the tremendous responsibility placed upon him by Allah.
orig: يا أيها المدثر

translation: So arise and warn.
interpretation: This verse is a command from Allah to Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) to stand up and warn the people about the consequences of their wrongdoings and to convey the message of Islam to them. It emphasizes the importance of the Prophet's role as a warner and a messenger, whose duty is to guide people towards the right path and save them from the punishment of the Hereafter. The verse also implies that the Prophet should be active, determined, and tireless in his mission, as the task of warning and conveying the message requires great effort and dedication.
orig: قم فأنذر

translation: And your Lord (Allah) magnify!
interpretation: This verse is a command to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and all believers to glorify, exalt, and magnify Allah. It serves as a reminder to recognize His greatness and superiority over all things. By magnifying Allah, one acknowledges His infinite power, wisdom, and mercy. This act of glorification should be reflected in our thoughts, words, and deeds, as we strive to live in accordance with His guidance and express our gratitude for His countless blessings. Magnifying Allah also helps us maintain perspective, humility, and reverence in our lives, as we submit to His will and seek His pleasure.
orig: وربك فكبر

translation: And your garments purify.
interpretation: This verse is a reminder to maintain both physical and spiritual purity. It encourages believers to keep their clothes clean and free from impurities, which is a reflection of one's inner state. More importantly, it emphasizes the purification of the soul, meaning that one should strive to cleanse their heart and mind from evil thoughts, intentions, and actions. By maintaining purity in both the external and internal sense, a believer can attain closeness to Allah and earn His pleasure. This verse highlights the importance of taharah (purity) in Islam, which extends beyond mere physical cleanliness to encompass the purification of the soul and the cultivation of righteous character.
orig: وثيابك فطهر

translation: And uncleanliness do shun
interpretation: In this verse, Allah commands the believers to stay away from all forms of impurities and uncleanliness, both physical and spiritual. This includes staying away from shirk (associating partners with Allah), immorality, evil deeds, and anything that is displeasing to Allah. The verse emphasizes the importance of maintaining purity and cleanliness in one's life, as it is a fundamental aspect of the Islamic faith. By shunning uncleanliness, the believers can attain closeness to Allah and earn His pleasure.
orig: والرجز فاهجر

translation: And do not confer favor to acquire more.
interpretation: This verse cautions against doing favors for others with the ulterior motive of expecting greater favors or rewards in return. It emphasizes the importance of sincere intentions when helping others, rather than using acts of kindness as a means to gain personal benefit. The Qur'an encourages selflessness and discourages actions driven by greed or the desire for self-aggrandizement. Believers should give and help others solely for the sake of Allah, without anticipating any worldly gain or recognition.
orig: ولا تمنن تستكثر

translation: So be patient for the sake of your Lord.
interpretation: This verse is a command from Allah to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) to remain patient and steadfast in the face of adversity and opposition. It reminds him that his patience is for the sake of Allah and that Allah will support and reward him for his perseverance. The verse encourages the Prophet to endure the challenges and hardships of his mission with patience and trust in Allah, knowing that ultimate victory and success come from Him. It is a lesson for all believers to remain patient and steadfast in their faith and to trust in Allah's plan, even in the face of difficulties and trials.
orig: ولربك فاصبر

translation: Then when the Trumpet is blown
interpretation: This verse refers to the Day of Judgment, when the Trumpet will be blown to signal the resurrection of the dead and the beginning of the final reckoning. It emphasizes the suddenness and inevitability of this event, which will mark the end of the world as we know it and the commencement of the eternal afterlife. The blowing of the Trumpet is a central theme in Islamic eschatology, and serves as a powerful reminder of the fleeting nature of worldly existence and the importance of preparing for the Hereafter through righteous deeds and unwavering faith in God.
orig: فإذا نقر في الناقور

translation: That Day will be a difficult day.
interpretation: This verse is referring to the Day of Judgment, emphasizing that it will be an extremely challenging and arduous day for those who have strayed from the right path and disobeyed Allah's commands. It serves as a reminder for people to be mindful of their actions in this world, as they will have to face the consequences on that formidable Day. The difficulty of that Day is beyond human comprehension, and it will be a time of great distress and anguish for the sinners.
orig: فذلك يومئذ يوم عسير

translation: Not easy for the disbelievers.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the path of disbelief and rejection of God's message is not an easy one. It suggests that those who choose to disbelieve will face difficulties, challenges, and ultimately, consequences for their choice. The verse implies that following the guidance of Allah and accepting His message is the easier and more rewarding path, while rejecting it leads to hardship and difficulty in this life and the hereafter.
orig: على الكافرين غير يسير

translation: Leave Me and the one I created alone
interpretation: This verse is a stern warning from Allah to those who oppose His messenger and the message he brings. It emphasizes the power and authority of Allah as the sole Creator and Sustainer of all beings. The verse also highlights the special status of Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) as the one chosen and created by Allah for a unique purpose. It serves as a reminder that no one can stand against the will of Allah or harm those whom He protects. Ultimately, this verse conveys the message that the disbelievers should abandon their hostility towards the Prophet and submit to the will of Allah before it is too late.
orig: ذرني ومن خلقت وحيدا

translation: And I have granted him extensive wealth
interpretation: This verse suggests that Allah has bestowed abundant wealth and resources upon an individual. The "extensive wealth" could refer to not just monetary riches, but also other forms of provision and blessings that have been granted continuously or in large quantities by Allah to sustain and support the person. It is a reminder that all wealth and bounties ultimately come from Allah's favor and generosity, and should be acknowledged as such with gratitude rather than be a cause for arrogance or ingratitude to Allah.
orig: وجعلت له مالا ممدودا

translation: And sons as witnesses.
interpretation: This verse is referring to the blessings that Allah bestows upon His servants in Paradise. The "sons as witnesses" could be interpreted as the children of the believers who will testify to their parents' faith and righteousness on the Day of Judgment. It signifies that in Paradise, the believers will be reunited with their offspring who died in a state of innocence or faith, and they will be a source of joy and pride for their parents as witnesses to their good deeds and belief in the Hereafter.
orig: وبنين شهودا

translation: And I spread out for him a fitting place.
interpretation: The verse suggests that God has prepared and made easy the way for the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and his mission. It implies that God has provided the necessary means, support, and guidance to facilitate the Prophet's efforts in conveying the message of Islam. The "fitting place" could refer to the physical, social, and spiritual environment that was made conducive for the Prophet to carry out his divine task of spreading the truth and enlightening humanity.
orig: ومهدت له تمهيدا

translation: Then he desires that I should add more.
interpretation: This verse is referring to the insatiable nature of human beings, who are never satisfied with what they have been given by Allah. Even when Allah blesses them with abundance, they still desire more and are not content with His favors upon them. It highlights the greed and ingratitude that can consume people, causing them to constantly seek more rather than being thankful for what they already have from Allah's bounty.
orig: ثم يطمع أن أزيد

translation: Nay! He has been stubborn to Our verses.
interpretation: This verse is referring to those who persistently and arrogantly reject the signs and revelations of Allah, despite their clarity and truth. It emphasizes that their disbelief is not due to a lack of understanding or evidence, but rather a result of their stubborn refusal to accept the message out of pride and obstinacy. Such individuals are blameworthy for their deliberate rejection of divine guidance, as they have chosen to turn away from the truth that has been made manifest to them through Allah's verses.
orig: كلا إنه كان لآياتنا عنيدا

translation: I will impose upon him a hard ascent.
interpretation: This verse is a warning from Allah that those who reject His signs and turn away from the truth will face a difficult and arduous journey in the Hereafter. The "hard ascent" refers to the challenges and tribulations that the disbelievers will encounter as they are held accountable for their actions and face the consequences of their choices. It serves as a reminder that the path of disbelief and disobedience to Allah leads to hardship and suffering, both in this life and the next.
orig: سأرهقه صعودا

translation: Indeed, he thought and deliberated.
interpretation: This verse is referring to the human faculty of reasoning and contemplation. It suggests that the person in question engaged in deep thought and carefully considered a matter before reaching a conclusion or making a decision. The ability to think, ponder, and deliberate is seen as a unique and valuable trait bestowed upon human beings by Allah. It emphasizes the importance of using one's intellect and wisdom in navigating the challenges and choices of life, rather than acting impulsively or without proper reflection.
orig: إنه فكر وقدر

translation: So he killed, how he plotted!
interpretation: This verse is a condemnation of those who plot and scheme to harm others or oppose the message of Islam. It suggests that those who engage in such evil plotting will ultimately face the consequences of their actions, and that their schemes will be exposed and thwarted by Allah. The repetition of "how he plotted" emphasizes the severity and deviousness of the plotting. Overall, it serves as a warning against engaging in malicious schemes and a reminder of the ultimate fate that awaits those who do so.
orig: فقتل كيف قدر

translation: Then he thought and plotted.
interpretation: This verse is referring to the disbeliever who denies the truth of the Qur'an and the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him). The disbeliever thinks deeply and plots against the message of Islam, trying to find ways to discredit or undermine it. However, his plotting is in vain, as the truth of Islam will always prevail. The verse serves as a warning to those who seek to oppose the message of Islam, reminding them that their efforts will ultimately be futile in the face of God's will.
orig: ثم قتل كيف قدر

translation: Then he looked
interpretation: This short verse is open to interpretation, but it likely refers to Allah observing His creation. It could imply that after creating the universe, Allah then looked upon what He had made, signifying His attentiveness and care for the world. The act of Allah "looking" may metaphorically mean His omniscience - that He perceives and knows all things. It may also allude to Allah's judgement, that He watches over the deeds of mankind and will hold them accountable. Ultimately, it is a reminder that Allah is ever-watchful and nothing escapes His sight.
orig: ثم نظر

translation: Then he frowned and scowled.
interpretation: This verse is referring to the Prophet Muhammad's reaction when he was approached by a blind man while he was engaged in conversation with some influential leaders of Quraysh. The Prophet's frown and scowl indicate his initial annoyance at being interrupted. However, the following verses rebuke this reaction, reminding the Prophet and all believers to treat everyone with respect and kindness, regardless of their social status or physical abilities. It emphasizes the importance of humility, equality, and attentiveness to those seeking guidance, as they may be more sincere and receptive to the message of Islam than those with worldly power and influence.
orig: ثم عبس وبسر

translation: Then he turned his back and was haughty.
interpretation: This verse is referring to someone who, after being presented with the truth or guidance, arrogantly turns away and rejects it out of pride and self-importance. It highlights the negative qualities of arrogance and haughtiness, which can prevent a person from accepting the truth and following the right path. The act of turning one's back symbolizes a deliberate and contemptuous rejection of the message or advice given to them. This behavior is condemned in Islam, as it shows a lack of humility and a refusal to submit to Allah's guidance.
orig: ثم أدبر واستكبر

translation: Then he said, "This is nothing but magic, [which] influences."
interpretation: The interpretation of this verse is that the person being referred to, likely a disbeliever, is dismissing the signs or miracles presented to him as mere magic or sorcery that has an effect on people. He refuses to acknowledge them as divine signs from Allah, instead attributing them to worldly trickery or illusion. This reflects the stubborn attitude of those who reject faith even when confronted with clear evidence, choosing to explain it away rather than accept the truth of Allah's message and the prophethood of His messenger.
orig: فقال إن هذا إلا سحر يؤثر

translation: This is not but the word of a human being.
interpretation: This verse suggests that the Qur'an is being dismissed by some as merely the words of a mortal man, rather than divine revelation from Allah. It implies that the disbelievers are rejecting the prophethood of Muhammad (peace be upon him) and the divine origin of the message he conveyed. The Qur'an refutes this notion and asserts that it is indeed the word of Allah, not a fabrication or product of human imagination.
orig: إن هذا إلا قول البشر

translation: I will drive him into Saqar.
interpretation: In this verse, Allah is warning the disbelievers and those who reject His signs that He will punish them by casting them into the blazing Fire of Hell, which is also referred to as "Saqar". This is a severe warning to those who persist in their disbelief and do not heed the call to faith and righteousness. It emphasizes the severity and inevitability of Allah's punishment for those who choose to reject Him and His guidance.
orig: سأصليه سقر

translation: And what can make you know what Saqar is?
interpretation: This verse is a rhetorical question, emphasizing the severity and unimaginable nature of Saqar, which is one of the names of Hell. It suggests that the true nature of this punishment is beyond human comprehension. The verse serves as a warning to those who disbelieve and a reminder of the consequences of rejecting faith and doing evil deeds. It encourages people to reflect on the gravity of the afterlife and to strive for righteousness in this world to avoid the torment of Saqar in the hereafter.
orig: وما أدراك ما سقر

translation: It spares not (any sinner), nor does it leave (anything unburnt)!
interpretation: This verse refers to the intense and all-consuming nature of the Hellfire. It emphasizes that the Hellfire will not spare any sinner who deserves punishment, nor will it leave anything unburnt or unconsumed. The verse conveys the severity and comprehensiveness of the punishment in Hell, highlighting the importance of seeking God's mercy and forgiveness to avoid such a fate. It serves as a powerful reminder for believers to strive for righteousness and repentance in this world.
orig: لا تبقي ولا تذر

translation: A tablet for mankind
interpretation: This short phrase refers to the Qur'an itself, which is described as a guiding tablet or scripture for all of humanity. It emphasizes the universality of the Qur'an's message, indicating that its teachings and wisdom are meant to benefit and guide people of all nations and backgrounds. The use of "tablet" symbolizes the Qur'an as a written record of divine revelation and instruction that serves to illuminate the path of righteousness for mankind to follow.
orig: لواحة للبشر

translation: Over it are nineteen [angels].
interpretation: This verse refers to the nineteen angels who are appointed as guardians over Hell. Their role is to oversee the punishment of the sinners and to ensure that the torment is carried out as decreed by Allah. The number nineteen is significant, as it represents a specific group of angels assigned to this task, and it also serves as a reminder of the severity and certainty of the punishment in Hell for those who reject Allah's message and guidance.
orig: عليها تسعة عشر

translation: And We have not made the keepers of the Fire except angels. And We have not made their number except as a trial for those who disbelieve - that those who were given the Scripture will be convinced and those who have believed will increase in faith and those who were given the Scripture and the believers will not doubt and that those in whose hearts is hypocrisy and the disbelievers will say, "What does Allah intend by this as an example?" Thus does Allah leave astray whom He wills and guides whom He wills. And none knows the soldiers of your Lord except Him. And mention of the Fire is not but a reminder to humanity.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the number and nature of the angels guarding Hell is known only to Allah and serves as a test of faith. Those with pure hearts will find their faith strengthened, while doubters and disbelievers will question Allah's wisdom. The verse affirms that Allah alone decides whom to guide or leave astray. Ultimately, the mention of Hell is intended as a powerful reminder for all of humanity to be mindful of their actions and to strive for righteousness.
orig: وما جعلنا أصحاب النار إلا ملائكة وما جعلنا عدتهم إلا فتنة للذين كفروا ليستيقن الذين أوتوا الكتاب ويزداد الذين آمنوا إيمانا ولا يرتاب الذين أوتوا الكتاب والمؤمنون وليقول الذين في قلوبهم مرض والكافرون ماذا أراد الله بهذا مثلا كذلك يضل الله من يشاء ويهدي من يشاء وما يعلم جنود ربك إلا هو وما هي إلا ذكرى للبشر

translation: Nay, by the moon!
interpretation: This verse is an oath taken by Allah, swearing by the moon. Oaths in the Qur'an are used to emphasize the importance and gravity of what follows. The moon is invoked to testify to the truth of the message, as it is one of the great signs of Allah's power and creative ability in the universe. Swearing by the moon also alludes to the changing phases of the moon, which symbolize the passing of time and the ultimate return of all things to their Creator. The verse serves to underscore the seriousness of the divine message and the consequences of denying it.
orig: كلا والقمر

translation: And by the night when it departs,
interpretation: This verse is referring to the night as it comes to an end and gives way to the morning. It is an oath by Allah, swearing by the night and its departure, which is a sign of His power and control over the universe. The night is a time of rest and tranquility, and its departure signifies the start of a new day and the renewal of life. This verse reminds us of the cyclical nature of time and the constant change and transition in the world around us, all of which are under the control of Allah.
orig: والليل إذ أدبر

translation: And [by] the morning when it brightens,
interpretation: This verse is an oath by Allah, swearing by the morning when it becomes bright and clear. It signifies the transition from darkness to light, both literally and metaphorically. The brightening of the morning symbolizes the revelation of truth, guidance, and enlightenment after periods of ignorance or confusion. It also represents the victory of good over evil, as the light of the morning dispels the darkness of the night. This oath emphasizes the importance and significance of the message that follows, drawing attention to the power and wisdom of Allah in His creation and the signs He provides for humanity to reflect upon.
orig: والصبح إذا أسفر

translation: Indeed, it is of the greatest [afflictions].
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the gravity and enormity of the matter being discussed. It suggests that the subject at hand is one of the most severe trials, calamities, or sins that one may face. The use of the word "indeed" (إنها) and the superlative form "the greatest" (الكبر) underscore the seriousness and magnitude of the issue, urging the listener or reader to pay close attention and recognize its significance in the context of their spiritual life and moral responsibilities.
orig: إنها لإحدى الكبر

translation: As a warner to mankind
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the role of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) as a messenger sent by Allah to warn humanity about the consequences of their actions and to guide them towards the right path. It highlights the universal nature of his message, which is intended for all of mankind, regardless of their race, ethnicity, or social status. The Prophet's warning serves as a reminder for people to be mindful of their deeds and to strive for righteousness in this world, as they will be held accountable for their actions in the Hereafter.
orig: نذيرا للبشر

translation: For whoever wills among you to proceed or stay behind.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the concept of free will in Islam. It suggests that each individual has the choice to either move forward in their spiritual journey and do good deeds, or to lag behind and engage in wrongdoing. Ultimately, the decision lies with the individual, and they will be held accountable for their choices. The verse serves as a reminder that humans have been granted the gift of free will, and it is up to them to use it wisely and in accordance with God's guidance.
orig: لمن شاء منكم أن يتقدم أو يتأخر

translation: Every soul, for what it has earned, will be retained
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the concept of individual responsibility in Islam. Each soul is held accountable for its own deeds and will be either rewarded or punished based on what it has earned through its actions in this world. No one can bear the burden of another's sins or escape the consequences of their own choices. This highlights the importance of striving to do good and avoiding wrongdoing, as ultimately, every person will face the results of their own conduct on the Day of Judgment. It serves as a reminder to be mindful of one's actions and to live a life pleasing to Allah.
orig: كل نفس بما كسبت رهينة

translation: Except the companions of the right,
interpretation: This verse refers to the righteous believers who will be spared from the torments of Hell on the Day of Judgment. They are called "the companions of the right" because they will receive their records of deeds in their right hands, signifying their good actions and faith. These individuals have lived their lives according to the teachings of Islam, fulfilling their obligations, and abstaining from major sins. As a result, they will be granted the mercy and forgiveness of Allah and will enter Paradise. This verse serves as a reminder for Muslims to strive to be among the "companions of the right" by leading a righteous life and following the path of Islam.
orig: إلا أصحاب اليمين

translation: In gardens, they will ask one another
interpretation: This verse refers to the people of Paradise who will be engaged in pleasant conversations with each other. They will be in a state of bliss and tranquility, enjoying the company of their fellow believers in the beautiful gardens of Paradise. The verse suggests that the relationships and interactions between the inhabitants of Paradise will be characterized by harmony, friendship, and a genuine interest in each other's well-being. This emphasizes the social aspect of Paradise, where believers will find joy not only in the physical pleasures and comforts but also in the meaningful connections they will have with others who share their faith and righteousness.
orig: في جنات يتساءلون

translation: About the criminals
interpretation: This short verse is likely referring to the fate of the sinners and disbelievers on the Day of Judgment. It suggests that they will be questioned about their deeds and will have to answer for their transgressions. The verse serves as a reminder that everyone will be held accountable before Allah for their actions in this world, and the criminals who rejected faith and did evil will face severe consequences in the Hereafter. It emphasizes the importance of righteousness and avoiding sin.
orig: عن المجرمين

translation: What led you into Saqar?
interpretation: This verse is asking the people in Hell what led them to this terrible fate. The implication is that their own evil deeds and rejection of truth during their worldly lives has brought them to the blazing Fire of Saqar (one of the names of Hell). It serves as a reminder that our actions in this life have consequences in the Hereafter, and that we will be held accountable. The verse prods us to reflect on our conduct and beliefs, and to strive for righteousness to avoid the punishment of Hell.
orig: ما سلككم في سقر

translation: They will say, "We were not of those who prayed,"
interpretation: This verse suggests that on the Day of Judgment, the disbelievers will confess that they were not among those who performed the obligatory prayers during their worldly life. Prayer is one of the most important pillars of Islam, and neglecting it is a grave sin. The verse implies that failing to establish regular prayer is a characteristic of the disbelievers and a cause for their ultimate doom in the Hereafter. It highlights the significance of prayer in the life of a Muslim and its role in attaining salvation.
orig: قالوا لم نك من المصلين

translation: And we used not to feed the poor.
interpretation: This verse is a reminder of the importance of caring for the less fortunate and the consequences of neglecting this duty. It implies that those who fail to feed the poor and needy will be held accountable for their actions in the Hereafter. The verse emphasizes the significance of social responsibility and the obligation of those who are blessed with wealth and resources to share with those in need. It serves as a warning against selfishness and encourages believers to cultivate compassion and generosity towards the underprivileged members of society.
orig: ولم نك نطعم المسكين

translation: And we used to indulge in vain discourse with those who indulge [in it].
interpretation: This verse is a confession of the disbelievers in the Hereafter, admitting that they used to engage in idle and frivolous talk with others who did the same. They would mock and ridicule the idea of resurrection and the Day of Judgment. It shows how heedless and negligent they were in the worldly life, wasting their time in vain pursuits instead of reflecting on the truth and preparing for the eternal life to come. The verse implies the importance of using our time wisely, avoiding useless speech and activities, and focusing on what is beneficial for our spiritual growth and salvation in the Hereafter.
orig: وكنا نخوض مع الخائضين

translation: And we used to deny the Day of Judgment.
interpretation: This verse is a confession from the people in Hell, admitting that during their worldly life, they used to reject the concept of the Day of Judgment. They did not believe in being held accountable for their deeds or in the existence of an afterlife. This disbelief led them to live a life of sin and disobedience to Allah, ultimately resulting in their punishment in the Hereafter. The verse serves as a reminder for believers to affirm their faith in the Day of Judgment and to live their lives accordingly, knowing that they will be held responsible for their actions in the presence of Allah.
orig: وكنا نكذب بيوم الدين

translation: Until there came to us [the death] of certainty.
interpretation: This verse is referring to the inevitable reality of death that every soul will face. The "certainty" mentioned here is death itself, which is the only thing that is certain in this life. The verse serves as a reminder that no matter how much we may try to avoid or delay it, death will eventually come to each and every one of us. It is a call to reflect on the temporary nature of this worldly life and to strive for what is eternal in the Hereafter by leading a righteous life and doing good deeds.
orig: حتى أتانا اليقين

translation: So the intercession of intercessors will not benefit them.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the futility of seeking intercession from anyone other than Allah on the Day of Judgment. It suggests that no one, not even the prophets or angels, will have the power to intercede on behalf of sinners without Allah's permission. The verse implies that people should focus on their own deeds and righteousness, as they will be held accountable for their actions and will not be able to rely on anyone else to save them from the consequences of their sins. It serves as a reminder to put one's faith and trust in Allah alone and to strive for good deeds in this life.
orig: فما تنفعهم شفاعة الشافعين

translation: So what is [the matter] with them that they are, from the reminder, turning away
interpretation: This verse is questioning why people are turning away from the Qur'an's message and reminders. It implies that there is no valid reason for them to do so, and that they should be heeding the Qur'an's guidance and warnings rather than disregarding them. The verse suggests that turning away from divine revelation is an irrational and blameworthy act, since the Qur'an contains important truths and admonitions for humanity's benefit.
orig: فما لهم عن التذكرة معرضين

translation: As if they were frightened donkeys
interpretation: This verse uses a simile to describe the state of the disbelievers on the Day of Judgment. It compares them to wild donkeys that are fleeing in panic from a perceived threat or predator. The interpretation is that the disbelievers will be in a state of extreme fear, confusion, and desperation on that Day, running aimlessly without any sense of direction or purpose, just like frightened donkeys. This emphasizes the severity of the consequences they will face for their rejection of faith and the message of Islam.
orig: كأنهم حمر مستنفرة

translation: Fleeing from a lion?
interpretation: This verse is using a metaphor to describe someone fleeing from something frightening or powerful, like prey running away from a fierce lion. It could be interpreted as referring to people who try to flee from God's judgment or punishment due to their sins and transgressions. The "lion" symbolizes God's power and authority, which sinners attempt to escape out of fear, but ultimately cannot evade God's reckoning. It serves as a warning that one cannot outrun the consequences of their actions or hide from divine justice.
orig: فرت من قسورة

translation: Rather, every person among them desires to be given scriptures spread out.
interpretation: This verse suggests that the disbelievers are not content with the revelation given to Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him). Instead, each one of them arrogantly desires to receive their own individual revelation directly from Allah, in the form of "scriptures spread out" before them. They are not willing to accept the Qur'an as the final and complete message from Allah to humanity, revealed through His chosen messenger. This highlights their stubborn refusal to acknowledge the truth, as they demand special treatment and personalized revelations to satisfy their ego and pride, rather than submitting to the universal message of Islam.
orig: بل يريد كل امرئ منهم أن يؤتى صحفا منشرة

translation: Nay, but they do not fear the Hereafter.
interpretation: This verse is a rebuke to those who deny the reality of the Hereafter and the Day of Judgment. It suggests that their disbelief and wrongdoing stem from a lack of fear and consciousness of the consequences they will face in the next life. The verse implies that if they truly feared God and the accounting of their deeds in the Hereafter, they would amend their ways and live righteously. It is a reminder that belief in the Afterlife is essential for leading a morally upright life and that denying it can lead to heedlessness and sin.
orig: كلا بل لا يخافون الآخرة

translation: Nay, indeed it is an admonition.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the Qur'an serves as a powerful reminder and admonition for humanity. It is not merely a book of stories or historical accounts, but a divine message that aims to guide people towards righteousness and away from wrongdoing. The Qur'an encourages self-reflection, repentance, and the adoption of virtuous conduct in one's life. It reminds individuals of their purpose, their accountability to Allah, and the consequences of their actions in this world and the hereafter. By describing the Qur'an as an admonition, this verse underscores its role as a source of guidance, warning, and spiritual awakening for those who approach it with an open heart and a willingness to learn and reform themselves.
orig: كلا إنه تذكرة

translation: So whoever wills may remember it.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of free will and individual responsibility in remembering and reflecting upon the Qur'an. It suggests that the choice to engage with the divine message and to benefit from its guidance ultimately lies with each person. The verse serves as an invitation and a reminder that the Qur'an is available for those who sincerely desire to study, understand, and apply its teachings in their lives, but it is not forced upon anyone. It highlights the significance of personal volition and the active role one must play in their own spiritual growth and development.
orig: فمن شاء ذكره

translation: And they will not remember except what Allah wills. He is worthy of fear and adequate for [granting] forgiveness.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that remembrance of Allah and turning to Him in repentance is only possible through His divine will and grace. It is Allah alone who guides individuals to the path of righteousness and grants them the ability to engage in His remembrance. The verse also highlights two important attributes of Allah: He is the One deserving of being feared and revered due to His power and majesty, and He is also the source of forgiveness for those who sincerely repent and seek His mercy. This encourages believers to maintain a balance between having hope in Allah's forgiveness while also fearing the consequences of disobeying Him.
orig: وما يذكرون إلا أن يشاء الله هو أهل التقوى وأهل المغفرة

translation: I swear by the Day of Resurrection
interpretation: In this verse, Allah swears by the Day of Resurrection, emphasizing its great importance and the certainty of its occurrence. The Day of Resurrection is when all souls will be brought back to life to face judgment for their deeds in this world. By swearing by this momentous event, Allah draws attention to the significance of belief in the Hereafter and the consequences of one's actions. This oath serves as a reminder for humans to be mindful of their conduct in this life, as they will be held accountable on that Day. It also highlights the power and authority of Allah, who alone has the ability to bring about such a tremendous event and determine the fate of all creatures.
orig: لا أقسم بيوم القيامة

translation: And I swear by the self-reproaching soul.
interpretation: This verse is emphasizing the importance of the human conscience and its ability to self-reflect and recognize one's own faults and shortcomings. The "self-reproaching soul" refers to the inner voice within each person that holds them accountable for their actions and guides them towards righteousness. By swearing by this self-reproaching soul, Allah is highlighting its significance as a moral compass and a means of spiritual purification. It serves as a reminder for individuals to constantly examine their deeds and strive for self-improvement, as the soul that is aware of its own imperfections and seeks to rectify them is highly valued in Islam.
orig: ولا أقسم بالنفس اللوامة

translation: Does man think that We will not assemble his bones?
interpretation: This verse is a rhetorical question that highlights the power and ability of Allah to resurrect the dead. It implies that some people doubt or deny the concept of resurrection, thinking that Allah cannot reassemble their scattered bones after death and decay. However, the verse affirms that Allah, who created man from nothing, is certainly capable of gathering the bones and recreating the body for the Day of Judgment. It serves as a reminder of Allah's omnipotence and the inevitability of the afterlife, encouraging believers to have faith in the divine promise of resurrection and accountability.
orig: أيحسب الإنسان ألن نجمع عظامه

translation: Yes, [We are] Able to proportion his fingertips.
interpretation: This verse affirms Allah's power and ability to resurrect human beings in their complete form, down to the minute details of their fingerprints. It emphasizes that Allah, who created human beings in the first place, is undoubtedly capable of recreating them after death for the purpose of judgment. The mention of fingerprints, a unique human feature, serves as a reminder of Allah's creative power and the individuality of each human being, which will be maintained even after resurrection.
orig: بلى قادرين على أن نسوي بنانه

translation: But man desires to continue in sin.
interpretation: This verse is referring to the innate tendency of human beings to persist in wrongdoing and disobedience, even when they are aware of the consequences. It highlights the human inclination towards instant gratification and the desire to indulge in worldly pleasures without considering the long-term spiritual impact. The verse suggests that man, by his very nature, is prone to transgressing the boundaries set by Allah and engaging in sinful behavior, unless he consciously strives to resist those temptations and submit to the will of Allah. It serves as a reminder for individuals to be vigilant against their base desires and to continuously seek Allah's guidance and forgiveness.
orig: بل يريد الإنسان ليفجر أمامه

translation: He asks, "When is the Day of Resurrection?"
interpretation: This verse is questioning when the Day of Judgment will occur. It reflects the human curiosity and perhaps anxiety about the timing of this momentous event in Islamic belief. The Day of Resurrection is when all souls will be raised to face God's judgment and be held accountable for their deeds in this worldly life. However, the exact timing is known only to God. This verse reminds the believer to always be mindful of that Day and to strive to live righteously, as it could come at any time without warning. It emphasizes the importance of being ever ready to face one's ultimate destiny.
orig: يسأل أيان يوم القيامة

translation: And when sight is dazzled
interpretation: This verse is referring to the Day of Judgment, when people will be so overwhelmed and awed by the events unfolding that their vision will be "dazzled" or "blinded." It suggests that the magnitude of that Day will be beyond human comprehension and that people will be in a state of shock and disorientation. The dazzling of the sight symbolizes the inability of humans to fully grasp or process the reality of the Day of Reckoning when all souls will be held accountable for their deeds in this worldly life.
orig: فإذا برق البصر

translation: And the moon is split.
interpretation: This verse refers to one of the miracles performed by Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) where he split the moon into two parts by pointing at it with his finger. It was a sign of his prophethood and a warning to the disbelievers who challenged him to show a miracle. The splitting of the moon also symbolizes the power and authority of Allah over His creation and serves as a reminder of the coming Day of Judgment when the natural order will be disrupted and the universe will be destroyed.
orig: وخسف القمر

translation: And the sun and the moon are brought together
interpretation: This verse is referring to the Day of Judgment, when the natural order of the universe will be disrupted and the sun and moon will be joined together, signifying the end of time as we know it. It is a reminder of the ultimate power and authority of Allah over His creation, and that all things will come to an end according to His will. The joining of the sun and moon also symbolizes the removal of all distinctions and barriers, as everything will be laid bare before Allah for judgment. It is a call for humans to reflect on their actions and to live righteously in preparation for that inevitable day.
orig: وجمع الشمس والقمر

translation: On that Day man will say, "Where is the [place of] escape?"
interpretation: This verse refers to the Day of Judgment when people will realize the gravity of their situation and seek to escape the consequences of their actions. However, there will be no escape or refuge from the divine justice on that day. It emphasizes the inevitability of accountability and the importance of leading a righteous life in this world, as there will be no opportunity to rectify one's deeds or seek forgiveness once the Day of Judgment commences. The verse serves as a reminder for humans to be mindful of their actions and to strive for good deeds, as they will ultimately be held accountable for them.
orig: يقول الإنسان يومئذ أين المفر

translation: No! There is no refuge.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that on the Day of Judgment, there will be no escape or refuge from the consequences of one's actions. It serves as a reminder that everyone will be held accountable for their deeds and that there will be no place to hide or seek protection from the divine justice. The verse encourages individuals to be mindful of their actions and to strive for righteousness, as ultimately, they will have to face the repercussions of their choices.
orig: كلا لا وزر

translation: To your Lord, that Day, is the [place of] permanence.
interpretation: This verse reminds us that on the Day of Judgment, our ultimate destination and permanent abode will be with Allah. It emphasizes that the worldly life is temporary, and our focus should be on our eternal life in the Hereafter. The verse encourages believers to prioritize their relationship with Allah and to strive for His pleasure, as He is the only true source of stability and security. It also serves as a warning to those who disregard their spiritual obligations, reminding them that they will have to face the consequences of their actions in the presence of their Lord.
orig: إلى ربك يومئذ المستقر

translation: On that Day, man will be informed of what he sent ahead and kept back.
interpretation: This verse refers to the Day of Judgment when each person will be confronted with their deeds, both good and bad, that they have done in their worldly life. It emphasizes the concept of individual accountability, as every person will be informed about what they have sent forth for their life in the Hereafter through their actions and what they have left behind or neglected. This verse serves as a reminder for humans to be mindful of their actions and to focus on doing good deeds, as they will have consequences in the afterlife.
orig: ينبأ الإنسان يومئذ بما قدم وأخر

translation: Rather, man, against himself, will be a witness
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that on the Day of Judgment, every individual will be a witness against themselves. Their own actions, intentions, and deeds will testify against them, even if they try to make excuses or deny their wrongdoings. This highlights the importance of being mindful of one's actions in this life, as ultimately, each person will be held accountable for their own choices and behavior. It serves as a reminder that one cannot escape the consequences of their actions and that the ultimate witness and judge is Allah, who knows all that is hidden and apparent.
orig: بل الإنسان على نفسه بصيرة

translation: Even if he offers his excuses
interpretation: This verse suggests that even if someone presents excuses or justifications for their wrongdoings, it does not absolve them of responsibility or consequence. It implies that God is aware of the true intentions behind people's actions, and that attempting to make excuses for one's misdeeds will not change the ultimate judgment or outcome. The verse emphasizes the importance of sincerity, accountability, and taking responsibility for one's choices and actions, rather than trying to evade or justify them.
orig: ولو ألقى معاذيره

translation: Move not your tongue with it, [O Muhammad], to hasten with recitation of the Qur'an.
interpretation: This verse is addressing the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him), instructing him not to rush or hasten in reciting the Qur'an. It suggests that the Prophet should not try to repeat the words of the revelation immediately as they are being revealed to him by the angel Gabriel. Instead, he should listen attentively and allow the revelation to be completed before reciting it. This interpretation emphasizes the importance of patience, concentration, and allowing the divine message to be fully conveyed without interruption or haste. It also implies that the Prophet should trust in Allah's plan for the revelation and its preservation, rather than feeling the need to rush or hurry the process.
orig: لا تحرك به لسانك لتعجل به

translation: Indeed, upon Us is its collection [in your heart] and [to make possible] its recitation.
interpretation: This verse assures Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) that Allah Himself will ensure the preservation and compilation of the Qur'an, as well as enabling the Prophet to recite it correctly. It emphasizes the divine responsibility in safeguarding the Qur'an's integrity and facilitating its memorization and recitation for the Prophet and the believers. This verse highlights the Qur'an's divine origin and the guarantee of its protection by Allah throughout time.
orig: إن علينا جمعه وقرآنه

translation: So when We have recited it [through Gabriel], then follow its recitation.
interpretation: This verse instructs Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and the believers to listen attentively when the Qur'an is being recited, and to follow its teachings and commandments. It emphasizes the importance of not only hearing the Qur'an but also understanding and implementing its guidance in one's life. The verse also highlights the divine nature of the Qur'an, as it is Allah Himself who recites it through the angel Gabriel to the Prophet. Therefore, the believers should treat the Qur'an with utmost respect and reverence, and strive to apply its teachings in their daily lives.
orig: فإذا قرأناه فاتبع قرآنه

translation: Then upon Us is its clarification.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that it is Allah's responsibility to explain and clarify the meanings and teachings of the Qur'an. It is a promise from Allah that He will ensure the Qur'an's message is made clear and understandable to humanity. This interpretation highlights the divine nature of the Qur'an and Allah's role in guiding people through its revelation and subsequent elucidation by trusted scholars and religious authorities. It also implies that humans should seek guidance in understanding the Qur'an from reliable sources that align with Allah's intended message.
orig: ثم إن علينا بيانه

translation: No! But you love the immediate,
interpretation: This verse is a criticism of those who are preoccupied with the fleeting pleasures and gains of this worldly life, while neglecting the eternal life of the Hereafter. It suggests that humans have a tendency to prioritize immediate gratification over long-term spiritual well-being. The verse serves as a reminder to Muslims to focus on the eternal rewards of the afterlife rather than being distracted by temporary worldly desires. It encourages believers to resist the temptations of instant gratification and to cultivate patience, self-discipline, and a strong connection with God in order to attain success in both this life and the next.
orig: كلا بل تحبون العاجلة

translation: And you neglect the Hereafter.
interpretation: This verse is a reminder and admonition to humanity that they should not be preoccupied solely with the fleeting pleasures and pursuits of this worldly life while neglecting the eternal life of the Hereafter. It emphasizes the importance of keeping the ultimate goal in mind and living a balanced life, fulfilling one's duties and obligations towards God and preparing for the Day of Judgment. The verse implies that focusing only on worldly matters at the expense of one's spiritual well-being and the life to come is a grave mistake that will lead to regret and loss in the Hereafter.
orig: وتذرون الآخرة

translation: Faces on that Day will be radiant,
interpretation: This verse is referring to the Day of Judgment. The faces of the righteous believers will be glowing with joy and radiance on that day because of the blessings and rewards they will receive from Allah for their good deeds and faith in this world. Their faces will reflect the inner peace, contentment, and happiness they feel in anticipation of entering Paradise. This radiance symbolizes the spiritual light and purity of their souls as a result of living a life pleasing to Allah.
orig: وجوه يومئذ ناضرة

translation: Looking at their Lord.
interpretation: This verse refers to the believers in Paradise who will be blessed with the ultimate reward of seeing Allah directly. It signifies the height of spiritual attainment and the culmination of the believer's journey. The verse emphasizes that the greatest joy in Paradise will be beholding the countenance of Allah, which will bring the believers immense pleasure, peace, and contentment. This direct vision of Allah is a special favor granted only to the righteous believers and is the fulfillment of their ultimate desire and aspiration.
orig: إلى ربها ناظرة

translation: And [some] faces, that Day, will be contorted,
interpretation: This verse refers to the Day of Judgment when some people will have faces that are gloomy, sad, and filled with regret. Their faces will reflect the misery and despair they feel as a result of their sinful actions and disobedience to Allah during their worldly life. The contorted faces symbolize the anguish and hopelessness of those who have earned Allah's displeasure and punishment due to their wrongdoings. It serves as a reminder for believers to strive for righteousness and obedience to Allah in order to avoid such a fate on the Day of Reckoning.
orig: ووجوه يومئذ باسرة

translation: You think that he would do with it poverty
