interpretation: This verse is likely referring to the idea that some people may believe that giving in charity or spending for the sake of Allah will lead to poverty or financial hardship. However, the Qur'an refutes this notion and encourages believers to give generously, assuring them that Allah will provide for them and that their charitable deeds will be rewarded both in this world and in the hereafter. The verse emphasizes the importance of trusting in Allah's provision and not letting the fear of poverty hinder one's willingness to help others and spend in the way of Allah.
orig: تظن أن يفعل بها فاقرة

translation: No! When the soul reaches the collar bones
interpretation: This verse is referring to the moment of death, when the soul reaches the collar bones as it departs from the body. It is a reminder that at this critical juncture, worldly matters and disbelief will be of no avail. The emphatic "No!" at the beginning of the verse serves to negate any notion that one can escape death or that anything other than one's deeds and faith will matter at that time. It underscores the gravity and inevitability of this event, urging individuals to reflect on their mortality and to live their lives in preparation for this ultimate reality.
orig: كلا إذا بلغت التراقي

translation: And it will be said, "Who will cure [him]?"
interpretation: This verse is a rhetorical question, implying that no one will be able to cure or save the disbelievers from the punishment of Hell on the Day of Judgment. It emphasizes the hopelessness and despair of those who rejected faith in Allah and His messengers, as they will realize that no one can rescue them from the consequences of their actions and disbelief. The verse also serves as a reminder for believers to stay on the right path and seek Allah's mercy and forgiveness in this life before it is too late.
orig: وقيل من راق

translation: And he was certain that it was the parting.
interpretation: This verse alludes to a profound realization or a deeply unsettling feeling that a significant separation or departure is imminent and inevitable. It suggests that the person in question has come to the stark conclusion that the parting of ways, either in a literal or metaphorical sense, is unavoidable and that the relationship or connection is coming to an end. The use of the word "ظن" (zanna) implies a strong sense of certainty and conviction about this impending separation, highlighting the emotional gravity and finality of the situation.
orig: وظن أنه الفراق

translation: And the leg is wound about the leg.
interpretation: This verse is referring to the Day of Judgment, when the intensity and difficulty of the situation will be so severe that a person's legs will be intertwined due to fear, anxiety and distress. It symbolizes the helplessness and desperation one will feel on that day, unable to flee or find comfort. The winding of one leg over the other represents the complete loss of control and power, submitting to the will of Allah for the final reckoning of deeds in this world. It is a reminder for believers to be mindful of their actions and to strive for good, as the ultimate consequences will be faced in the Hereafter.
orig: والتفت الساق بالساق

translation: To your Lord, that Day, will be the [final] destination.
interpretation: This verse is emphasizing that on the Day of Judgment, all humans will be brought before Allah for the final reckoning. It serves as a reminder that our ultimate destination and return is to our Creator, and we will be held accountable for our deeds in this world. The verse implies that there is no escape from facing the consequences of our actions and that we should live our lives with the awareness that we will eventually stand before Allah. It encourages introspection, righteousness, and the pursuit of Allah's pleasure, as that is what will ultimately matter on that fateful Day.
orig: إلى ربك يومئذ المساق

translation: So he neither believed nor prayed.
interpretation: This verse refers to the disbeliever who neither affirms the truth of the divine message nor performs the prayer, which is one of the most important pillars of Islam. It highlights the importance of both faith and righteous deeds in the life of a believer. Merely claiming to believe without acting upon the teachings and commandments of Islam is not sufficient. The verse emphasizes that true faith must be accompanied by sincere worship and obedience to Allah's commands.
orig: فلا صدق ولا صلى

translation: But he denied and turned away.
interpretation: This verse is referring to those who reject the truth of the message brought by the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) despite its clarity and evidence. They turn away from it out of arrogance, stubbornness, and following their own desires rather than submitting to the will of Allah. It is a warning that denying the truth and turning away from guidance will lead to serious consequences in this life and the Hereafter.
orig: ولكن كذب وتولى

translation: Then he went to his family, walking proudly [in an arrogant manner].
interpretation: This verse is referring to the arrogant and haughty manner in which a disbeliever or a wicked person walks and carries himself, particularly after rejecting the truth or committing evil deeds. It highlights the pride and self-conceit that consumes such individuals, leading them to behave in a vain and boastful way. The verse serves as a reminder for believers to avoid such behavior and to always remain humble and modest in their conduct, regardless of their accomplishments or status in society.
orig: ثم ذهب إلى أهله يتمطى

translation: Woe to you, and woe!
interpretation: This verse is a strong warning and admonition to those who reject the truth and persist in disbelief and wrongdoing. The repetition of the word "woe" emphasizes the severity of the consequences that await such individuals in the Hereafter. It serves as a wake-up call for them to repent and mend their ways before it is too late, as they will have to face the full weight of divine justice for their actions. The verse also implies that the opportunity for repentance and forgiveness is still available, but time is running out, so one must seize the chance before it passes.
orig: أولى لك فأولى

translation: Then, woe to you, and woe!
interpretation: This verse is a strong warning and admonition to those who reject the truth and persist in disbelief and wrongdoing. The repetition of "woe" emphasizes the severity of the consequences that await them in the Hereafter. It implies that they will face a series of misfortunes, disasters, and punishments for their actions. The verse serves as a wake-up call, urging individuals to reflect upon their choices and the ultimate outcome of their deeds, encouraging them to repent and turn towards the path of righteousness before it is too late.
orig: ثم أولى لك فأولى

translation: Does man think that he will be left neglected?
interpretation: This verse is a reminder to humanity that we will not be left without purpose or accountability. It suggests that every human being will be held responsible for their actions and decisions in this life, and that we will all face the consequences of our choices in the Hereafter. The verse implies that God has created us with a specific purpose and that He is constantly watching over us, aware of everything we do. It serves as a wake-up call for those who may be heedless or negligent in their spiritual obligations, urging them to be mindful of their actions and to live a life pleasing to God.
orig: أيحسب الإنسان أن يترك سدى

translation: Was he not a Nutfah (mixed male and female discharge of semen) poured forth?
interpretation: This verse is reminding mankind of their humble origin. Every human being starts as a drop of semen, a seemingly insignificant fluid. Yet from this fluid, by the power and will of Allah, a full human being is formed and given life. The verse thus invites reflection on the wonder of human creation and the power of Allah in fashioning man from such a small beginning. It also serves as a reminder for humans not to be arrogant or proud, as they all share this lowly origin, and that their existence and growth is only by the grace and power of their Creator.
orig: ألم يك نطفة من مني يمنى

translation: Then he was a clinging clot, and [Allah] created [his form] and proportioned [him]
interpretation: This verse refers to the stages of human development in the womb. After the initial stage of being a drop of fluid, the embryo becomes a clinging clot ('alaqah). At this stage, Allah creates the basic form and features of the human body and proportions it, making it symmetrical and balanced. This points to the incredible precision and design in the creation of human beings, and how Allah fashions each individual in the womb according to His will and wisdom.
orig: ثم كان علقة فخلق فسوى

translation: And made from it the two mates, the male and the female.
interpretation: This verse points to the divine wisdom and power in creating the two genders, male and female, from a single source or origin. It suggests that there is a deep harmony, complementarity and equality between the two sexes, as they have been fashioned from the same essence by God. The duality and pairing of male and female is portrayed as a fundamental part of God's design and plan for creation and for the continuation of human life. The verse invites reflection on the profound mystery and beauty of gender and sexuality as a gift from God.
orig: فجعل منه الزوجين الذكر والأنثى

translation: Is He not able to give life to the dead?
interpretation: This verse is a rhetorical question that emphasizes God's power and ability to resurrect the dead. It implies that if God can create life in the first place, then surely He is capable of bringing the dead back to life on the Day of Judgment. The verse encourages believers to have faith in God's omnipotence and in the reality of the afterlife, where all souls will be held accountable for their deeds in this world. It also serves as a reminder that death is not the end, but rather a transition to the eternal life to come.
orig: أليس ذلك بقادر على أن يحيي الموتى

translation: Has there [not] come upon man a period of time when he was not a thing [even] mentioned?
interpretation: This verse is a reminder to mankind that there was a time before their existence when they were not even mentioned or known. It highlights the insignificance of man in the grand scheme of things and serves as a reminder of man's humble origins. The verse encourages humility and gratitude towards the Creator who brought man into existence from a state of nothingness. It also implies that just as man came into being by Allah's will, he can also be returned to a state of non-existence, emphasizing the temporary nature of worldly life and the importance of striving for the eternal life of the Hereafter.
orig: هل أتى على الإنسان حين من الدهر لم يكن شيئا مذكورا

translation: Indeed, We created man from a sperm-drop mixture that We may test him; and We made him hearing and seeing.
interpretation: This verse highlights the purpose and wisdom behind the creation of human beings. God created humans from a humble beginning, a mere drop of fluid, in order to test them throughout their lives. The tests and trials faced by humans serve to reveal their true nature and the strength of their faith. God has equipped humans with the faculties of hearing and sight, which are not only physical senses but also represent the ability to understand, learn, and discern right from wrong. These gifts come with the responsibility of using them wisely and in accordance with God's guidance. The verse emphasizes the importance of recognizing one's origin, appreciating the blessings bestowed by God, and striving to fulfill the purpose of one's existence by passing the tests of life with faith and righteousness.
orig: إنا خلقنا الإنسان من نطفة أمشاج نبتليه فجعلناه سميعا بصيرا

translation: Indeed, We guided him to the way, be he grateful or be he ungrateful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the free will that God has granted to human beings. God has shown humanity the right path and given them the choice to either be grateful and follow His guidance, or to be ungrateful and reject it. It is up to each individual to decide which path they will take - the path of gratitude and submission to God, or the path of ingratitude and rejection of His message. Ultimately, we are responsible for our own choices and will face the consequences of those choices in the Hereafter.
orig: إنا هديناه السبيل إما شاكرا وإما كفورا

translation: Indeed, We have prepared for the disbelievers chains and shackles and a blaze.
interpretation: This verse serves as a stern warning to those who reject faith in Allah and His message. It emphasizes that the disbelievers will face severe punishment in the Hereafter for their defiance and ingratitude. The mention of chains, shackles, and a blazing fire symbolizes the physical and mental anguish they will endure as a consequence of their actions. This interpretation highlights the gravity of disbelief and the importance of embracing faith and righteousness to avoid such a fate. It also underscores Allah's justice in dealing with those who willfully reject His guidance and persist in their wrongdoing.
orig: إنا أعتدنا للكافرين سلاسل وأغلالا وسعيرا

translation: Indeed, the righteous will drink from a cup [of wine] whose mixture is of Kafur,
interpretation: This verse speaks about the reward of the righteous believers in Paradise. They will be given a special drink mixed with Kafur, which is a fragrant substance that has cooling and soothing properties. This drink is a symbol of the pure and refreshing bliss that the righteous will enjoy in the afterlife as a reward for their good deeds and devotion to Allah in this world. It signifies that their thirst will be quenched and they will find ultimate satisfaction and peace in the presence of their Lord.
orig: إن الأبرار يشربون من كأس كان مزاجها كافورا

translation: A spring from which the servants of Allah drink, making it gush forth abundantly.
interpretation: This verse refers to a special spring in Paradise, which the righteous believers will have access to. They will be able to drink from it and direct its flow as they wish, highlighting the honor and privilege that will be granted to them in the afterlife. The verse emphasizes the reward of those who are faithful to Allah and live according to His teachings. It also symbolizes the abundance of blessings and the fulfillment of desires that the believers will experience in Paradise as a result of their righteousness and devotion to Allah in this worldly life.
orig: عينا يشرب بها عباد الله يفجرونها تفجيرا

translation: They [are those who] fulfill [their] vows and fear a Day whose evil will be widespread.
interpretation: This verse speaks about the qualities of the righteous believers. They are the ones who fulfill the vows and promises they make to Allah, showing their sincerity and commitment to their faith. They also fear the Day of Judgment, which is described as a Day whose evil will be widespread. This fear motivates them to do good deeds and avoid sins, knowing that they will be held accountable for their actions on that great Day. The verse emphasizes the importance of being faithful to one's commitments and maintaining consciousness of Allah and the Hereafter.
orig: يوفون بالنذر ويخافون يوما كان شره مستطيرا

translation: And they give food in spite of love for it to the needy, the orphan, and the captive,
interpretation: This verse highlights the selflessness and generosity of those who, despite their own love for food and their own needs, prioritize feeding the poor, orphans, and prisoners. It emphasizes the importance of putting others before oneself and showing compassion towards the less fortunate, even in times of personal hardship. The act of giving food to those in need is portrayed as a noble and righteous deed, reflecting the high moral character of the believers who engage in such acts of kindness and charity.
orig: ويطعمون الطعام على حبه مسكينا ويتيما وأسيرا

translation: We feed you only for the sake of Allah. We desire from you neither reward nor thanks.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of doing good deeds solely for the sake of Allah, without expecting any worldly reward or even gratitude from others. It highlights the purity of intention that should drive a believer's actions, seeking only the pleasure of Allah and His reward in the Hereafter. This selfless attitude is a key characteristic of true faith and sincerity in worship, as it demonstrates a person's willingness to serve others and make sacrifices without any ulterior motives or desire for recognition.
orig: إنما نطعمكم لوجه الله لا نريد منكم جزاء ولا شكورا

translation: Indeed, we fear from our Lord a Day austere and distressful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of being mindful of the Day of Judgment, which is described as a day that will be difficult and distressing for those who have not lived righteously. It serves as a reminder for believers to fear Allah and strive to do good deeds in this world, as they will be held accountable for their actions on that Day. The verse encourages Muslims to lead a life of piety and righteousness, seeking Allah's pleasure and mercy, in order to be saved from the hardships of the Day of Judgment.
orig: إنا نخاف من ربنا يوما عبوسا قمطريرا

translation: So Allah will protect them from the evil of that Day and give them radiance and happiness.
interpretation: This verse speaks about the rewards that await the righteous believers on the Day of Judgment. Allah, in His infinite mercy, will shield them from the horrors and difficulties of that Day. Instead, He will bless them with radiant faces, glowing with the light of faith and good deeds. Their hearts will be filled with pure joy and contentment, knowing that they have earned Allah's pleasure and are among the successful ones. This verse serves as a reminder for the believers to persevere in their faith and good actions, seeking the ultimate reward of Allah's protection and happiness in the Hereafter.
orig: فوقاهم الله شر ذلك اليوم ولقاهم نضرة وسرورا

translation: And will reward them for what they patiently endured [with] a garden [in Paradise] and silk [garments].
interpretation: This verse speaks about the reward that Allah has prepared for those who remain steadfast and patient in the face of difficulties and trials in this world. Their patience and perseverance will be rewarded with the eternal bliss of Paradise, where they will enjoy its gardens and be clothed in garments of silk. This highlights the immense value of patience in Islam and encourages believers to remain firm in their faith, knowing that their struggles will be worth it in the end when they are granted the ultimate reward of Paradise.
orig: وجزاهم بما صبروا جنة وحريرا

translation: Reclining therein on adorned couches, they will not see therein [burning] sun or [freezing] cold.
interpretation: This verse describes the comfort and ease that the righteous will enjoy in Paradise. They will recline on beautifully decorated couches, indicating a state of rest and relaxation. The mention of not seeing the sun or experiencing extreme cold suggests that the climate in Paradise will be perfect and temperate, neither too hot nor too cold. This is a blessing from Allah, as the inhabitants of Paradise will be protected from any form of discomfort or hardship. The verse emphasizes the idea that Paradise is a place of ultimate pleasure and satisfaction, where believers will be rewarded for their faith and good deeds in this world.
orig: متكئين فيها على الأرائك لا يرون فيها شمسا ولا زمهريرا

translation: And near above them are its shades, and its [fruit] to be picked will be lowered in compliance.
interpretation: This verse describes the blissful state of the righteous in Paradise. The shade of the trees in Paradise will be within easy reach, providing comfort and coolness to the inhabitants. The branches of the trees will be lowered, making it effortless for the righteous to pluck the fruits they desire. This symbolizes the ease, abundance, and perfect servitude that will be granted to the believers in the Hereafter as a reward for their faith and good deeds in this world. It emphasizes the concept that Paradise is a place of ultimate pleasure, tranquility, and fulfillment, where all desires will be satisfied without any hardship or struggle.
orig: ودانية عليهم ظلالها وذللت قطوفها تذليلا

translation: And there will be circulated among them vessels of silver and cups having been [created] clear [as glass],
interpretation: In Paradise, the righteous will be served drinks in vessels made of silver and cups as transparent as glass. This verse emphasizes the exquisite beauty and refined luxury that the believers will enjoy in the Hereafter as a reward for their faith and good deeds in this world. The mention of silver and crystal-clear cups symbolizes purity, perfection, and the unimaginable delights that await the inhabitants of Paradise, far beyond the material pleasures of this worldly life.
orig: ويطاف عليهم بآنية من فضة وأكواب كانت قواريرا

translation: Vessels of silver which they have determined [according to] measure.
interpretation: This verse refers to the vessels of Paradise, which will be made of pure silver, carefully crafted to perfection. The mention of silver vessels indicates the immense value, beauty, and purity of what the believers will be given in Paradise. The fact that these vessels are "determined according to measure" suggests that everything in Paradise will be precisely tailored to the desires and preferences of its inhabitants, giving them the utmost satisfaction and pleasure. It also implies that the blessings of Paradise are not haphazard or random but are meticulously prepared and bestowed upon the believers as a reward for their faith and righteousness in this world.
orig: قوارير من فضة قدروها تقديرا

translation: And they will be given to drink a cup [of wine] whose mixture is of ginger
interpretation: This verse is describing one of the rewards that the righteous will receive in Paradise. The cup of wine mixed with ginger is symbolic of the exquisite pleasures and delights that await them. Ginger was considered a luxury in the ancient world, so its mention here emphasizes the specialness and rarity of what the believers will experience in the afterlife. The ginger may also hint at the drink's soothing and invigorating properties, representing the perfect refreshment and bliss that the people of Paradise will enjoy eternally as a reward for their faith and good deeds in this worldly life.
orig: ويسقون فيها كأسا كان مزاجها زنجبيلا

translation: A spring therein [in Paradise] called Salsabeel.
interpretation: This verse refers to one of the springs in Paradise, named Salsabeel. The name itself carries a beautiful meaning, suggesting that the water from this spring flows gently and is delightfully palatable. This interpretation highlights the concept of the perfect bliss and delights that await the righteous in the Hereafter. The mention of such a specific name for a spring in Paradise indicates that it possesses unique and exceptional qualities, emphasizing the magnificence and beauty that God has prepared for His faithful servants in the eternal life to come.
orig: عينا فيها تسمى سلسبيلا

translation: And there will circulate among them young boys made eternal. When you see them, you would think them [as beautiful as] scattered pearls.
interpretation: This verse describes one of the rewards that the righteous will enjoy in Paradise. They will be served by immortal young boys who are so beautiful that they resemble scattered pearls. This metaphor emphasizes their purity, beauty, and the perfection of their service. These attendants will circulate among the believers, fulfilling their every need and desire, adding to the overall atmosphere of luxury, comfort, and bliss in Paradise. This verse aims to motivate believers to strive for righteousness in this life, so that they may attain such eternal rewards in the Hereafter.
orig: ويطوف عليهم ولدان مخلدون إذا رأيتهم حسبتهم لؤلؤا منثورا

translation: And when you look there [in Paradise], you will see pleasure and great dominion.
interpretation: This verse is describing the immense rewards and blessings that await the believers in Paradise. When they look around them, they will see all that their hearts desire - pleasures beyond imagination and a vast kingdom that belongs to them. This is a reminder of the great honor and favor that Allah will bestow upon His righteous servants in the Hereafter, as a reward for their faith and good deeds in this world. It encourages the believers to strive for Paradise and to remain steadfast on the path of righteousness.
orig: وإذا رأيت ثم رأيت نعيما وملكا كبيرا

translation: Upon them will be green garments of fine silk and heavy brocade, and they will be adorned with bracelets of silver, and their Lord will give them a purifying drink.
interpretation: This verse describes the attire and adornments of the inhabitants of Paradise. The green garments of fine silk and heavy brocade symbolize luxury, comfort, and honor bestowed upon them by Allah. The silver bracelets are a further indication of their elevated status. The "purifying drink" given to them by their Lord represents spiritual purity and freedom from any form of imperfection or sin. It signifies the ultimate reward for their righteous deeds and unwavering faith during their earthly life. The verse emphasizes the boundless generosity and mercy of Allah towards His faithful servants in the eternal life of the Hereafter.
orig: عاليهم ثياب سندس خضر وإستبرق وحلوا أساور من فضة وسقاهم ربهم شرابا طهورا

translation: Indeed, this is your reward, and your effort has been appreciated.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the reward given to the believers in the Hereafter is a recompense for their good deeds and efforts in this world. It highlights the idea that God acknowledges and appreciates the strivings of His servants who follow the righteous path. The verse also implies that the reward in Paradise is not merely a gift, but something that is earned through one's actions and dedication to God's cause. It serves as an encouragement for believers to continue their efforts in doing good, knowing that their striving will not go unnoticed or unrewarded by their Lord.
orig: إن هذا كان لكم جزاء وكان سعيكم مشكورا

translation: Indeed, it is We who have sent down to you, [O Muhammad], the Qur'an progressively.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the Qur'an was revealed to Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) gradually over a period of 23 years by Allah Himself. This progressive revelation allowed the Prophet and his followers to learn, understand, and implement the teachings of the Qur'an in their lives step by step. It also served as a means of strengthening their faith and providing them with guidance and support during the various challenges they faced. The verse also highlights the divine nature of the Qur'an, as it is Allah who has sent it down, ensuring its authenticity and protection from any form of alteration or corruption.
orig: إنا نحن نزلنا عليك القرآن تنزيلا

translation: So be patient for the decision of your Lord and do not obey from among them a sinner or ungrateful disbeliever.
interpretation: This verse is advising the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and the believers to remain steadfast and patient in the face of opposition and hostility from the disbelievers and wrongdoers. It urges them not to give in to the pressure or temptation to follow the ways of those who are sinful or ungrateful to Allah. Rather, they should hold firmly to their faith, trusting in Allah's plan and judgment, and not compromise their beliefs or values no matter how difficult the circumstances may be. This requires strong willpower, conviction, and reliance on Allah to resist the influences of those who seek to lead them astray from the straight path.
orig: فاصبر لحكم ربك ولا تطع منهم آثما أو كفورا

translation: And remember the name of your Lord morning and evening.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of remembering Allah and mentioning His name consistently throughout the day, particularly in the morning and evening. It encourages the believer to engage in constant remembrance and supplication, keeping Allah at the forefront of their thoughts and actions. By doing so, one strengthens their connection with Allah, attains peace and tranquility, and remains mindful of their purpose in life. This remembrance can take the form of dhikr (verbal remembrance), prayer, or reflecting upon Allah's names and attributes. Consistency in this practice is key to spiritual growth and maintaining a strong relationship with the Creator.
orig: واذكر اسم ربك بكرة وأصيلا

translation: And during the night, prostrate to Him and exalt [in praise of] Him a long [part of the] night.
interpretation: This verse instructs the believers to dedicate a significant portion of the night to worshipping Allah through prayer and glorification. It emphasizes the importance of utilizing the quiet and peaceful hours of the night to strengthen one's spiritual connection with Allah. By prostrating and engaging in prolonged praise and remembrance of Him, one can attain greater closeness to Allah and seek His pleasure. This night worship serves as a means of purification for the soul, helping the believer to detach from worldly distractions and focus on their ultimate purpose of serving and submitting to Allah.
orig: ومن الليل فاسجد له وسبحه ليلا طويلا

translation: Indeed, these [disbelievers] love the immediate and leave behind them a grave Day.
interpretation: This verse is a reminder that those who reject faith and the message of Islam are often preoccupied with worldly pleasures and short-term gains. They neglect the consequences of their actions and the weight of the Day of Judgment that awaits them in the Hereafter. It emphasizes the importance of having a long-term perspective, keeping the Afterlife in mind, and not being distracted by fleeting desires and temptations of this world. The verse warns against the attitude of those who disregard their ultimate accountability before Allah and the gravity of the Day of Reckoning.
orig: إن هؤلاء يحبون العاجلة ويذرون وراءهم يوما ثقيلا

translation: We have created them and strengthened their forms, and when We will, We can replace them with others like them with [complete] replacement.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's power and control over His creation. He has not only created human beings, but has also perfected their physical forms and capabilities. However, this verse also serves as a reminder that if Allah wills, He can easily replace them with others, signifying that no one is indispensable or irreplaceable. It encourages humility and submission to Allah's will, recognizing that He alone has the ultimate authority and power over all things. This verse also implies that humans should be grateful for the abilities and strengths that Allah has granted them, using them in a manner that pleases Him, for He can take them away and replace them whenever He chooses.
orig: نحن خلقناهم وشددنا أسرهم وإذا شئنا بدلنا أمثالهم تبديلا

translation: Indeed, this is a reminder, so whoever wills may take to his Lord a way.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the role of the Qur'an as a reminder and a guide for those who seek to draw closer to Allah. It highlights the concept of free will, indicating that individuals have the choice to either accept the message of the Qur'an and follow the path leading to their Lord or to reject it. The verse encourages people to make a conscious decision to embrace the teachings of the Qur'an and to strive in the way of Allah, seeking His pleasure and nearness. It serves as a call to action, urging individuals to take the initiative in their spiritual journey and to actively seek the path that leads to their Creator.
orig: إن هذه تذكرة فمن شاء اتخذ إلى ربه سبيلا

translation: And you do not will except that Allah wills. Indeed, Allah is ever Knowing and Wise.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the ultimate power and authority of Allah over all things. It reminds us that our own will and desires are subject to the will of Allah, and that nothing happens without His permission and decree. The verse also highlights two of Allah's attributes: His perfect knowledge and wisdom. This means that whatever Allah wills is based on His complete knowledge of all things and His infinite wisdom, even if we may not always understand the reasons behind what happens in our lives. As believers, we should strive to align our own will with the will of Allah and trust in His plan for us, knowing that He is the All-Knowing and All-Wise.
orig: وما تشاءون إلا أن يشاء الله إن الله كان عليما حكيما

translation: He admits whom He wills into His mercy; but the wrongdoers - He has prepared for them a painful punishment.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the ultimate power and authority of Allah in determining the fate of individuals in the Hereafter. It highlights His infinite mercy, which He bestows upon whomever He chooses, guiding them to the path of righteousness and granting them entry into Paradise. Simultaneously, the verse serves as a stern warning to the wrongdoers, those who persistently engage in sinful acts and transgress the boundaries set by Allah. For them, Allah has prepared a severe and painful punishment in the Afterlife as a consequence of their actions. This interpretation underscores the importance of striving to be among those whom Allah favors with His mercy, while also reminding believers to avoid wrongdoing and to seek forgiveness for their sins.
orig: يدخل من يشاء في رحمته والظالمين أعد لهم عذابا أليما

translation: By those [winds] sent forth in gusts
interpretation: This verse is referring to the winds that Allah sends as a mercy, to drive the clouds, pollinate trees, and bring rain to revive dead lands. It is an oath that emphasizes the power and wisdom behind these winds, and how they are a sign of Allah's existence and control over the universe. The verse reminds us to reflect on these natural phenomena and appreciate the blessings that Allah bestows upon us through them.
orig: والمرسلات عرفا

translation: By the [winds] that blow violently
interpretation: This verse is interpreted as an oath by Allah swearing by the strong winds that blow fiercely. The winds are a sign of Allah's power and control over the forces of nature. They can be both beneficial, such as bringing rain and assisting in pollination, and destructive, causing storms and devastation. The mention of violent winds could also symbolize the trials and tribulations that people face in life, which test their faith and resilience. Ultimately, this verse reminds us of Allah's supremacy and the importance of submitting to His will, even in the face of adversity.
orig: فالعاصفات عصفا

translation: By those [winds] that scatter far and wide
interpretation: This verse is referring to the winds that Allah sends forth to spread His mercy and blessings throughout the earth. The winds carry rain clouds, pollinate plants, and perform many other vital functions in nature. This verse is a reminder of Allah's power and wisdom in creating and sustaining the natural world. It encourages believers to reflect on the signs of Allah's creation and to be grateful for His countless blessings. The scattering of the winds also symbolizes the spread of Allah's message and guidance to all corners of the world.
orig: والناشرات نشرا

translation: By those [angels] who extract with force
interpretation: This verse refers to the angels who are tasked with extracting the souls of the deceased from their bodies. The use of the word "farqan" (translated as "force") indicates that this process is not always gentle or easy, but rather can be difficult and even painful for some souls. This extraction of the soul marks the transition from the temporary life of this world to the eternal life of the hereafter, and serves as a reminder of the inevitability of death and the importance of preparing for the afterlife through righteous deeds and faith in God.
orig: فالفارقات فرقا

translation: By those [winds] scattering [dust] dispersing
interpretation: This verse is referring to the winds that blow and scatter dust and debris across the earth. It is a reminder of the power and might of Allah, who controls the forces of nature. The winds are a sign of Allah's ability to create and destroy, and to bring about change in the world. This verse is also a reminder that just as the winds can scatter and disperse, so too can Allah scatter and disperse those who oppose Him and His message. It is a warning to those who reject the truth and a reminder to the believers to remain steadfast in their faith.
orig: فالملقيات ذكرا

translation: an excuse or a warning
interpretation: This verse is highlighting the two main purposes of the Quran and the prophets that were sent by Allah. They serve as either an excuse, meaning a clear proof and explanation of the truth so that people have no justification for rejecting it, or as a warning of the consequences of disbelief and wrongdoing. The Quran and the prophets give mankind the opportunity to embrace guidance while cautioning them of the fate that awaits those who persist in misguidance. It establishes Allah's justice in holding people accountable, as they were given ample opportunity to follow the right path.
orig: عذرا أو نذرا

translation: Indeed, what you are promised is going to happen.
interpretation: This verse is a strong affirmation from Allah that the Day of Judgment and the events that have been promised to humanity, such as resurrection, accounting of deeds, and the ultimate reward of Paradise or punishment of Hell, are inevitable and will certainly occur. It is a reminder for believers to have faith in Allah's promises and to prepare for the Hereafter by doing good deeds and abstaining from sins, as they will be held accountable for their actions in this world.
orig: إنما توعدون لواقع

translation: So when the stars are obliterated
interpretation: This verse is referring to the Day of Judgment, when the natural order of the universe will be disrupted and the stars will lose their light and be extinguished. It is one of the signs of the impending arrival of the Day of Resurrection, highlighting the momentous and cataclysmic events that will unfold. The obliteration of the stars symbolizes the end of the world as we know it and the ushering in of a new reality where all souls will be held accountable for their deeds. It serves as a reminder of the temporary nature of this worldly existence and the importance of preparing for the eternal life to come by living righteously and in submission to God's will.
orig: فإذا النجوم طمست

translation: And when the sky is split open
interpretation: This verse refers to the Day of Judgment when the sky will be torn apart, unveiling the unseen realm and the divine presence. It signifies the end of the world as we know it and the beginning of the eternal afterlife. The splitting of the sky is a sign of the immense power and authority of Allah over His creation. It also indicates that all secrets will be laid bare and every person will face the consequences of their deeds. This event will mark the transition from the temporary life of this world to the everlasting reality of the hereafter.
orig: وإذا السماء فرجت

translation: And when the mountains are blown away
interpretation: This verse refers to the Day of Judgment when the mountains, which seem so firm and immovable in this world, will be utterly destroyed and scattered like dust. It signifies the tremendous upheaval and destruction that will occur on that Day, showing Allah's supreme power and the transient nature of this world. The blowing away of the mountains also symbolizes the removal of all barriers and distinctions, as everyone will stand equal before Allah for judgment based solely on their deeds and faith.
orig: وإذا الجبال نسفت

translation: And when the messengers are brought at the appointed time.
interpretation: This verse refers to the Day of Judgment when all the messengers will be brought together at their appointed time to bear witness for or against their nations. It signifies that the messengers will be questioned about their deliverance of the divine message to their people and how their people responded to it. This verse emphasizes the importance and inevitability of the Day of Judgment and the accountability of both the messengers and their nations before Allah.
orig: وإذا الرسل أقتت

translation: For what Day are these [signs] deferred?
interpretation: This verse is questioning for what purpose and until when the signs of Allah's power and the coming of the Day of Judgment are being postponed. It suggests that there is an appointed time when these signs will be manifest and the truth will be clear to all, and it is not for humans to know or decide when that time is. Rather, it is a reminder to be mindful and prepared for that inevitable Day which Allah has set.
orig: لأي يوم أجلت

translation: For the Day of Judgement.
interpretation: This verse refers to the Day of Judgement, also known as the Day of Resurrection or the Last Day, when all souls will be held accountable for their deeds in this worldly life. It emphasizes the importance and inevitability of this day, reminding believers to prepare for it by leading righteous lives and fulfilling their obligations to Allah. The mention of the Day of Judgement in this concise manner serves as a powerful reminder of the ultimate purpose of human existence and the consequences of one's actions.
orig: ليوم الفصل

translation: And what can make you know what is the Day of Judgement?
interpretation: This verse is emphasizing the momentous and unimaginable nature of the Day of Judgement. It suggests that no one can truly comprehend or fathom the gravity and significance of that Day, except Allah. It is a Day when all souls will be held accountable for their deeds, and the ultimate fate of each individual will be decided. The verse aims to instill a sense of awe, reverence and mindfulness about the inevitability of divine justice and the consequences of one's actions in this life.
orig: وما أدراك ما يوم الفصل

translation: Woe, that Day, to the deniers.
interpretation: This verse serves as a stern warning to those who reject the truth of Islam and the Day of Judgment. "That Day" refers to the Day of Resurrection, when all souls will be held accountable for their deeds in this world. The "deniers" are those who refuse to believe in Allah, His messengers, and the divine message they brought. The word "woe" emphasizes the severity of the punishment and suffering that awaits these deniers on that fateful day. It implies that they will face a dreadful fate as a consequence of their disbelief and their choice to reject the guidance provided by Allah. This verse is a reminder for all of humanity to reflect upon their actions and beliefs, and to strive for righteousness before it is too late.
orig: ويل يومئذ للمكذبين

translation: Did We not destroy the former peoples?
interpretation: This verse is a rhetorical question from Allah, reminding mankind that He has the power to destroy those who reject His message, just as He destroyed the disbelieving nations of the past. It serves as a warning to those who oppose the truth and persist in their disbelief, emphasizing that they will face a similar fate if they do not change their ways and submit to Allah's will. The verse also highlights the consistency of Allah's dealings with humanity throughout history, as He punishes the wrongdoers and rewards the righteous.
orig: ألم نهلك الأولين

translation: Then We shall follow them up with those of later times.
interpretation: This verse refers to the punishment that awaits the disbelievers and wrongdoers in the Hereafter. After mentioning the fate of earlier nations who rejected the truth, Allah declares that those of later generations who follow the same path of disbelief and transgression will also face the consequences of their actions. It serves as a warning that no one can escape divine justice and that everyone will be held accountable for their deeds, regardless of when they lived in this world. The verse emphasizes the universality and timelessness of Allah's message and the importance of heeding it to avoid a grievous fate in the afterlife.
orig: ثم نتبعهم الآخرين

translation: Thus do We deal with the criminals.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah punishes the criminals and wrongdoers in a manner that is befitting their crimes. It serves as a warning to those who engage in sinful activities and transgress the limits set by Allah. The verse also highlights the concept of divine justice, indicating that no one can escape the consequences of their evil deeds and that Allah will deal with them accordingly in this world and the Hereafter.
orig: كذلك نفعل بالمجرمين

translation: Woe, that Day, to the deniers.
interpretation: This verse serves as a stern warning and admonition to those who reject the truth and deny the Day of Judgment. It emphasizes that on that fateful day, those who have persistently denied the signs of Allah and the reality of the Hereafter will face severe consequences and eternal regret. The repetition of this verse throughout the surah underscores the gravity of their misguidance and the inevitability of their fate. It is a reminder for all of humanity to reflect upon their beliefs and actions in this world, as they will be held accountable in the next.
orig: ويل يومئذ للمكذبين

translation: Did We not create you from a liquid disdained?
interpretation: This verse is reminding human beings of their humble origins. It emphasizes that God created humans from a seemingly insignificant fluid, which is often seen as something despicable or of little value. The rhetorical question serves to highlight the miraculous nature of human creation and to remind humans that, despite their lofty status and achievements, they originated from a lowly substance. This verse encourages humility, gratitude towards the Creator, and recognition of the marvel of human development from a mere drop of fluid into a complex being. It also implies that since God has the power to create from something so simple, He also has the power to resurrect and hold humans accountable for their deeds.
orig: ألم نخلقكم من ماء مهين

translation: And We placed him in a firm resting place.
interpretation: This verse refers to the miraculous conception and birth of Prophet Jesus (peace be upon him). After mentioning the conception of Jesus by his mother Mary, Allah states that He placed Jesus in the womb of his mother, which is described as a "firm resting place". The womb provides security, protection, and nourishment for the developing fetus. This points to the special care and attention given by Allah to Jesus and his mother during the pregnancy and birth, as a sign of His power and favor upon them. It also highlights the sanctity of the womb as a secure place designed by Allah for the development of human life.
orig: فجعلناه في قرار مكين

translation: For a known period.
interpretation: This verse is referring to the idea that everything in this world, including our lives and provisions, are predetermined by Allah for a set period of time that is known only to Him. It reminds us that our time on Earth is limited and that we should make the most of it by living righteously and fulfilling our purpose before the appointed time arrives. The verse encourages us to recognize the temporary nature of worldly life and to focus on what is truly important - our relationship with Allah and our ultimate fate in the Hereafter.
orig: إلى قدر معلوم

translation: So We determined, and how excellent are We to determine.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's power and ability to decree and determine all matters in the universe. It highlights that Allah's determination and planning is perfect, wise and carried out in the best possible way. The use of the word "We" in reference to Allah denotes His majesty and grandeur. The verse also serves as a reminder to humans that Allah is in full control, and His decrees and decisions are unquestionable and final, as He is the Best of Planners.
orig: فقدرنا فنعم القادرون

translation: Woe, that Day, to the deniers.
interpretation: This verse is a stern warning to those who reject the truth and deny the Day of Judgment. "Woe" here signifies a severe punishment and suffering that awaits the deniers on that Day. It emphasizes the gravity of their disbelief and the consequences they will face for their rejection of faith. The repetition of this warning throughout the chapter underscores the importance of belief and the severity of the punishment for those who persist in their denial despite clear signs and warnings.
orig: ويل يومئذ للمكذبين

translation: Have We not made the earth a receptacle
interpretation: In this verse, Allah reminds us of His immense power and mercy by pointing out that He has made the earth a suitable place for living beings. The word "kifaatan" can mean a receptacle, container, or resting place. This implies that the earth has been designed to accommodate and sustain life, providing all the necessary elements for survival, such as water, air, and food. It also serves as a temporary abode for humans until the Day of Judgment, emphasizing the transient nature of worldly life and the importance of preparing for the eternal hereafter. This verse encourages reflection on Allah's blessings and should inspire gratitude and obedience to Him.
orig: ألم نجعل الأرض كفاتا

translation: Alive and dead
interpretation: This verse is referring to the power of Allah over life and death. It emphasizes that Allah has the ability to give life and take it away, and that all living beings will eventually face death. The verse serves as a reminder of the temporary nature of worldly life and the importance of being mindful of the afterlife. It encourages believers to focus on doing good deeds and seeking Allah's pleasure, as ultimately, it is Allah who determines one's fate in both this life and the hereafter.
orig: أحياء وأمواتا

translation: And We placed therein lofty, firmly set mountains and have given you to drink sweet water.
interpretation: This verse highlights Allah's power and mercy in creating the earth with its majestic mountains that are firmly rooted, providing stability and beauty to the landscape. It also emphasizes His benevolence in providing humanity with clean, fresh water to sustain life. The verse serves as a reminder for humans to be grateful for these blessings and to recognize the greatness of the Creator who has designed the earth with such intricate balance and purpose.
orig: وجعلنا فيها رواسي شامخات وأسقيناكم ماء فراتا

translation: Woe, that Day, to the deniers.
interpretation: This verse is a stern warning to those who reject the truth and deny the Day of Judgment. "Woe" here signifies a severe punishment and suffering that awaits the deniers on that Day. It emphasizes the gravity of their disbelief and the consequences they will face for their rejection of faith. The repetition of this verse throughout Surah Al-Mursalat serves as a reminder of the fate that awaits those who persistently deny the truth, despite the clear signs and warnings sent by Allah. It is a call for introspection and repentance before it is too late.
orig: ويل يومئذ للمكذبين

translation: Proceed to that which you used to deny.
interpretation: This verse is a stern warning to the disbelievers on the Day of Judgment. It conveys that they will be asked to face the reality of the Hereafter which they used to deny and reject in their worldly life. They will be powerless to avoid the consequences of their disbelief and will have to confront the punishment that awaits them. It emphasizes that there will be no escape from Divine justice and that everyone will be held accountable for their deeds. The verse serves as a reminder to mankind to reflect on the reality of the Afterlife and to live righteously in preparation for that inevitable event.
orig: انطلقوا إلى ما كنتم به تكذبون

translation: Proceed to a shade having three branches.
interpretation: This verse is likely referring to the shade provided by a tree or plant with three branches or parts. It could be interpreted as an instruction to seek refuge, rest, or comfort in a place that offers protection from the heat of the sun. The three branches may symbolize completeness, balance, or the divine nature of the shade being offered. It suggests that one should seek out a place of respite and renewal when needed, and that such a place may be found in nature or in the shelter provided by God's creation.
orig: انطلقوا إلى ظل ذي ثلاث شعب

translation: No shade, nor availing against the flame.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the severity and inescapability of the punishment in Hell. It suggests that there will be no respite or protection from the scorching flames of the Fire. The shade, which normally provides comfort and relief from heat, will be absent, indicating the all-encompassing nature of the torment. Moreover, nothing will be able to shield or protect the inhabitants of Hell from the burning flames. This interpretation highlights the hopelessness and despair of those condemned to such a fate, as they will find no means of alleviation or escape from the unrelenting punishment.
orig: لا ظليل ولا يغني من اللهب

translation: It throws sparks [as huge] as a fortress
interpretation: This verse is describing the intense and powerful nature of the sparks that are thrown from the Hellfire. The sparks are so large and mighty that they are compared to fortresses or castles in their size and strength. This imagery conveys the severity and terror of the punishment that awaits those who are condemned to Hell, and serves as a warning to humanity to strive for righteousness and avoid evil deeds that would lead to such a fate. The verse emphasizes the unimaginable scale and intensity of the torments of Hell.
orig: إنها ترمي بشرر كالقصر

translation: As if they were hollow trunks of palm trees.
interpretation: This verse uses a vivid metaphor to describe the state of the disbelievers on the Day of Judgment. It compares them to hollow, lifeless palm trunks, emphasizing their spiritual emptiness and lack of substance. The imagery suggests that despite their outward appearance or worldly status, those who reject faith are devoid of any real meaning, purpose, or inner strength. They will stand before God as mere shells, stripped of the false trappings they relied upon in this life. The verse serves as a powerful reminder of the ultimate insignificance and fragility of those who turn away from divine guidance.
orig: كأنه جمالت صفر

translation: Woe, that Day, to the deniers.
interpretation: This verse is a stern warning to those who reject the truth of the Day of Judgment. "Woe" here signifies a severe punishment and suffering that awaits those who deny the reality of the Hereafter. The repetition of this phrase in Surah Al-Mursalat emphasizes the gravity of their denial and the consequences they will face on that Day. It serves as a reminder for mankind to believe in the Divine message and prepare for the inevitable reckoning, as disbelief will lead to a dreadful fate in the Afterlife.
orig: ويل يومئذ للمكذبين

translation: That is a Day they will not speak.
interpretation: This verse refers to the Day of Judgment when people will be held accountable for their deeds. On that day, they will be unable to speak or offer any excuses for their wrongdoings. It emphasizes the gravity and finality of the ultimate reckoning, where individuals will face the consequences of their actions in this world. The silence mentioned in the verse highlights the helplessness and realization of the truth that will dawn upon the sinners when they stand before Allah for judgment.
orig: هذا يوم لا ينطقون

translation: And they will not be permitted to make excuses.
interpretation: This verse refers to the Day of Judgment when the disbelievers will not be given the opportunity to offer any excuses for their actions. They will be silenced and will have to face the consequences of their deeds without being able to justify themselves. It emphasizes the finality of the judgment and the inability of the sinners to escape from the divine justice on that day. The verse also implies that the time for repentance and seeking forgiveness is in this worldly life, and once the Day of Judgment arrives, it will be too late for excuses or apologies.
orig: ولا يؤذن لهم فيعتذرون

translation: Woe, that Day, to the deniers.
interpretation: This verse serves as a stern warning and admonition to those who reject the truth and deny the Day of Judgment. It emphasizes that on that momentous Day, those who persistently denied the signs of Allah and the reality of the Hereafter will face severe consequences and regret. The repetition of this verse throughout the surah underscores the gravity of their denial and the inevitability of their fate. It is a reminder for all of humanity to reflect upon their beliefs and actions in this world, as they will be held accountable in the next.
orig: ويل يومئذ للمكذبين

translation: This is the Day of Judgement; We will have assembled you and those [who lived] before.
interpretation: This verse refers to the Day of Judgment when all of humanity, from the first to the last, will be gathered together by Allah to be judged for their deeds in this worldly life. It emphasizes the inevitability and significance of this event, reminding believers that they will be held accountable for their actions and that they should strive to live righteously in preparation for this momentous day. The verse also highlights Allah's power and ability to resurrect and assemble all of creation, regardless of the time that has passed since their death.
orig: هذا يوم الفصل جمعناكم والأولين

translation: Now, if you have a plan, then carry it out against me.
interpretation: This verse is a bold challenge from the Prophet to his opponents who are plotting against him. It conveys an attitude of fearlessness and confidence in God's protection. The underlying message is that no matter what schemes or plans the enemies devise, they cannot harm the Prophet or stop the message of Islam, for he is under God's care. It reflects the strong faith and reliance on God that believers should have in the face of adversity or threats from those who oppose the truth.
orig: فإن كان لكم كيد فكيدون

translation: Woe, that Day, to the deniers.
interpretation: This verse is a stern warning to those who reject the truth and deny the Day of Judgment. "Woe" here signifies a severe punishment and suffering that awaits the deniers on that fateful Day. It emphasizes the gravity of their disbelief and the consequences they will face for their rejection of faith. The repetition of this warning throughout the chapter underscores the importance of belief and the severity of the punishment for those who persist in their denial despite clear signs and warnings.
orig: ويل يومئذ للمكذبين

translation: Indeed, the righteous will be among shades and springs.
interpretation: This verse speaks about the reward that awaits the righteous and God-fearing individuals in the afterlife. They will find themselves in a state of eternal bliss, surrounded by pleasant shades and refreshing springs. This imagery symbolizes the peace, comfort, and tranquility that the righteous will experience in Paradise as a result of their faith and good deeds in this worldly life. It serves as a reminder and motivation for believers to strive for righteousness and piety, knowing that their efforts will be rewarded with an everlasting abode of happiness and contentment in the Hereafter.
orig: إن المتقين في ظلال وعيون

translation: And fruit of what they desire.
interpretation: This verse is referring to the blessings and rewards that will be granted to the righteous believers in Paradise. Among these rewards are fruits that they desire and wish for. This highlights the idea that in Paradise, the believers will have all that their souls desire and yearn for, without any limitations or restrictions. It is a place of ultimate satisfaction, contentment, and fulfillment of all pure wishes and aspirations. The mention of fruit specifically could also symbolize the sweetness, freshness, and abundance of the bounties in Paradise.
orig: وفواكه مما يشتهون

translation: Eat and drink at ease for that which you have sent forth (good deeds) in days past!
interpretation: This verse is addressing the righteous believers in Paradise, inviting them to enjoy the delights that await them as a reward for their good deeds performed in their worldly life. It emphasizes the concept that the actions we perform in this life have consequences in the Hereafter. The verse encourages believers to focus on performing good deeds, as these will ultimately lead to their contentment and happiness in the eternal life of Paradise. It also serves as a reminder that the pleasures of Paradise are far superior to those of this world and that the believers' ultimate goal should be to attain these everlasting rewards through their faith and righteous actions.
orig: كلوا واشربوا هنيئا بما كنتم تعملون

translation: Indeed, We thus reward the doers of good.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah rewards those who do good deeds and live righteously. It serves as an encouragement and promise to the believers that their good actions will not go unnoticed or unrewarded by Allah. The use of "We" in this verse refers to Allah Himself, indicating the greatness and significance of the reward that comes from Him. It also highlights the concept of divine justice, as Allah ensures that everyone receives what they deserve based on their deeds. This verse motivates individuals to strive for excellence in their moral conduct and to persistently do good, knowing that Allah will acknowledge and reward their efforts in this life and the Hereafter.
orig: إنا كذلك نجزي المحسنين

translation: Woe, that Day, to the deniers.
interpretation: This verse serves as a stern warning and admonition to those who reject the truth and deny the Day of Judgment. It emphasizes that on that fateful day, those who have persistently denied the signs of Allah and the reality of the Hereafter will face severe consequences and regret. The repetition of this phrase throughout the surah underscores the gravity of their wrongdoing and the certainty of their impending doom. It is a reminder for all people to reflect upon their actions and beliefs, and to embrace the path of faith and righteousness before it is too late.
orig: ويل يومئذ للمكذبين

translation: Eat and enjoy yourselves for a little; indeed, you are criminals.
interpretation: This verse is a stern warning to those who indulge in worldly pleasures while neglecting their spiritual duties and committing sins. It suggests that the enjoyment of such people is temporary and fleeting, and that they will ultimately face the consequences of their actions. The use of the word "criminals" emphasizes the gravity of their wrongdoing and the inevitability of divine justice. This verse serves as a reminder for believers to prioritize their faith and righteousness over material pursuits and to be mindful of the Day of Judgment.
orig: كلوا وتمتعوا قليلا إنكم مجرمون

translation: Woe, that Day, to the deniers.
interpretation: This verse is a stern warning to those who reject the truth and deny the Day of Judgment. "Woe" here signifies a severe threat and a grievous punishment that awaits the deniers on that momentous Day. It emphasizes the gravity of their disbelief and the consequences they will face for their stubborn rejection of faith. The repetition of this warning throughout the chapter underscores the seriousness of the matter and serves as a wake-up call for those who persist in their denial, urging them to reflect upon their actions and the inevitable outcome that awaits them if they do not change their ways.
orig: ويل يومئذ للمكذبين

translation: And when it is said to them, "Bow [in prayer]," they do not bow.
interpretation: This verse is criticizing the hypocrites or disbelievers who, when called upon to humble themselves before Allah in prayer and bow down in submission, they arrogantly refuse to do so. It highlights their stubbornness, pride and lack of faith. They are unwilling to submit to Allah's commands and show humility in worship. The verse points to the importance of sincere prayer and obedience to Allah, and condemns those who reject His call out of arrogance or disbelief.
orig: وإذا قيل لهم اركعوا لا يركعون

translation: Woe, that Day, to the deniers.
interpretation: This verse is a stern warning to those who reject the truth of Islam and the Day of Judgment. "That Day" refers to the Day of Resurrection, when all souls will be held accountable for their deeds in this world. The "deniers" are those who refuse to believe in Allah, His messengers, and the divine message they brought. The repetition of this verse throughout Surah Al-Mursalat emphasizes the severity of the punishment awaiting those who persist in their disbelief and denial of the truth. It serves as a reminder for mankind to heed the warnings, follow the righteous path, and prepare for the ultimate reckoning in the Hereafter, or face the dire consequences of their rejection.
orig: ويل يومئذ للمكذبين

translation: Then in what statement after it [i.e., the Qur'an] will they believe?
interpretation: This verse is a rhetorical question that emphasizes the supreme authority and truth of the Qur'an. It implies that if people do not believe in the Qur'an, which is the ultimate truth from Allah, then there is no other message or statement that they will believe in. The verse suggests that the Qur'an is the final and most complete revelation from Allah, and that there is no other source of guidance that can supersede it. It is a powerful reminder to humanity to recognize the Qur'an as the ultimate source of truth and to submit to its teachings.
orig: فبأي حديث بعده يؤمنون

translation: About what are they asking one another?
interpretation: This verse is questioning what people are preoccupied with and discussing amongst themselves. It suggests that rather than busying themselves with trivial matters or idle gossip, people should turn their attention to more important spiritual concerns. The verse prompts introspection about one's priorities and how one is spending their time and mental energy. It is a reminder to focus on what truly matters in life from the perspective of faith and the afterlife, rather than getting caught up in worldly distractions or frivolous debates.
orig: عم يتساءلون

translation: About the Great News -
interpretation: This verse is referring to the Day of Judgment, which is described as "The Great News" because it is the most important event that will occur, and it is the news that all of creation will be informed about. It is called great because of the monumental events that will take place on that day, such as the resurrection of the dead, the gathering of all people, the reckoning of deeds, and the final abode of Paradise or Hell. This news is so great that it overshadows all other news and events, and it is the ultimate concern of every soul since it determines their eternal fate.
orig: عن النبإ العظيم

translation: That in which they differ
interpretation: This verse refers to the differences and disagreements among people regarding various matters of faith and religion. It suggests that there are many issues and topics about which people hold divergent views and opinions, leading to disputes and debates. The Qur'an acknowledges the reality of these differences existing among humankind, but also emphasizes that ultimate truth and guidance comes from Allah alone. It is a reminder that despite the disagreements and varying interpretations, one should turn to the Qur'an and authentic teachings of Islam to seek clarity and resolution on matters of faith.
orig: الذي هم فيه مختلفون

translation: No! They will come to know.
interpretation: This verse serves as a stern warning to those who reject the truth and persist in their disbelief. It implies that while they may be heedless or dismissive of the consequences now, a time will come when they will face the reality of their actions and gain a clear understanding of the gravity of their choices. This realization will dawn upon them either in this world or in the Hereafter, and they will come to comprehend the enormity of their mistake in denying the truth. The repetition of the phrase "They will come to know" emphasizes the certainty and inevitability of this outcome, leaving no doubt about the fate that awaits those who refuse to believe.
orig: كلا سيعلمون

translation: Then they will surely come to know.
interpretation: This verse serves as a stern warning and reminder that those who reject the truth and persist in their wrongdoing will eventually face the consequences of their actions. They will come to realize the gravity of their mistakes and the reality of the Hereafter when it is too late. It emphasizes the inevitability of divine justice and the importance of heeding the guidance provided by Allah before it is too late. The repetition of the phrase "will surely come to know" adds emphasis to the certainty and severity of the impending realization.
orig: ثم كلا سيعلمون

translation: Have We not made the earth a resting place?
interpretation: In this verse, Allah reminds us of His immense power and benevolence. He has created the Earth as a perfect abode for humans, providing us with a stable and comfortable place to live, grow, and thrive. The Earth is likened to a "mihad" or a resting place, emphasizing its suitability for sustaining life. This verse encourages us to reflect upon Allah's blessings and be grateful for the bounties He has bestowed upon us, such as the Earth itself, which serves as a nurturing cradle for humanity. It also highlights the importance of being responsible stewards of the Earth, preserving and protecting it as a sacred trust from our Creator.
orig: ألم نجعل الأرض مهادا

translation: And the mountains as pegs?
interpretation: The verse likens mountains to pegs or stakes that hold down the earth. This metaphor suggests that mountains play a crucial role in stabilizing the earth's surface and preventing it from shaking or shifting. It points to the wisdom and power of Allah in creating these massive structures that serve an essential purpose in maintaining the balance and stability of the planet. The verse invites reflection on the intricate design and purposefulness in Allah's creation, encouraging humans to appreciate and marvel at the natural world around them.
orig: والجبال أوتادا

translation: And We have created you in pairs.
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine wisdom behind the creation of human beings in pairs, male and female. It emphasizes the complementary nature of the two genders and the importance of the institution of marriage in Islam. The creation of humans in pairs is a sign of Allah's mercy and a means for humans to find tranquility, love, and compassion in their spouses. This verse also serves as a reminder that all humans, regardless of their gender, are equal in the sight of Allah and that they should treat each other with respect and kindness.
orig: وخلقناكم أزواجا

translation: And We have made your sleep [a means for] rest
interpretation: In this verse, Allah reminds us of one of His great blessings upon mankind - the gift of sleep. Sleep is described as a means of rest, indicating its restorative and rejuvenating properties. It is during sleep that our bodies and minds are able to relax, heal, and prepare for the challenges of the coming day. This verse encourages us to appreciate and make the most of the time we have been granted for sleep, recognizing it as a mercy from our Creator. It also implies that we should maintain a balanced approach to sleep, not neglecting our responsibilities but also ensuring we get sufficient rest to function at our best. Ultimately, this verse highlights the wisdom and care Allah has placed in the design of our daily cycle and the blessings we often take for granted.
orig: وجعلنا نومكم سباتا

translation: And We have made the night as a covering (through its darkness),
interpretation: In this verse, Allah compares the night to a garment or covering. Just as a garment covers and conceals the body, the darkness of night covers the world. This metaphor suggests that night provides comfort, rest, and privacy. It is a time when people can retreat from the busyness and exposure of the day, finding solace in the night's embrace. The night serves as a natural cycle for rest and rejuvenation, a divine blessing that enables humans and other creatures to renew their energy and prepare for the activities of the coming day.
orig: وجعلنا الليل لباسا

translation: And We have made the day for livelihood.
interpretation: In this verse, Allah emphasizes the importance of the day as a time for work, earning a living, and engaging in various activities. The day is a blessing from Allah, providing opportunities for humans to strive, learn, and fulfill their responsibilities. This interpretation highlights the significance of utilizing the daylight hours productively and gratefully, recognizing it as a divine gift to support one's livelihood and contribute to the betterment of oneself and society.
orig: وجعلنا النهار معاشا

translation: And We have built above you seven strong [heavens]
interpretation: This verse is referring to the creation of the seven heavens by Allah. The word "shidad" used to describe the heavens implies that they are strong, firmly constructed, and indestructible. This verse is a reminder of Allah's power and ability to create such vast and magnificent structures. It also highlights the perfection and precision in Allah's creation, as the heavens are built with strength and stability. The verse invites us to reflect on the grandeur of Allah's creation and to appreciate His immense power and wisdom.
orig: وبنينا فوقكم سبعا شدادا

translation: And We have made [therein] a burning lamp
interpretation: In this verse, Allah is referring to the sun as a "burning lamp" (sirajan wahhajan). This metaphor emphasizes the sun's immense heat and its role in providing light to the world. The verse points to Allah's power and wisdom in creating the sun, which is essential for the existence and sustenance of life on Earth. It also serves as a reminder for humans to reflect upon and appreciate the natural phenomena that Allah has created and set in motion for our benefit.
orig: وجعلنا سراجا وهاجا

translation: And We have sent down, from the rain clouds, pouring water
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the power and mercy of Allah in providing sustenance for His creation. The "pouring water" mentioned here refers to the heavy rains that come from the clouds, which Allah sends down to revive the earth and provide water for all living beings. This is a reminder of Allah's ability to bring forth life and abundance from what appears to be lifeless. It also highlights the importance of water as a fundamental blessing that sustains all life on earth, and therefore, it should be valued and used wisely as a gift from Allah. The verse encourages humans to reflect on the natural phenomena around them as signs of Allah's existence, power, and benevolence.
orig: وأنزلنا من المعصرات ماء ثجاجا

translation: That We may produce therewith grain and vegetation
interpretation: This verse is referring to the power and mercy of Allah in providing sustenance for His creation. The interpretation is that Allah sends down rain from the sky to cause the growth of crops and vegetation from the earth, which then provides food for humans and animals. It highlights Allah's ability to bring forth life and provision from the seemingly lifeless earth. The verse is a reminder for humans to reflect on and be grateful for the blessings and bounties that Allah bestows upon them, and to recognize His power, wisdom and mercy in sustaining all living beings.
orig: لنخرج به حبا ونباتا

translation: And gardens of thick foliage.
interpretation: This verse refers to the gardens of Paradise, which are described as having dense, interwoven foliage. The word "alfaafaa" conveys the idea of lush, abundant greenery that provides shade and beauty. This description of Paradise serves as a reminder of the reward that awaits the righteous in the Hereafter, and encourages believers to strive for righteousness in this life in order to attain these eternal gardens of bliss.
orig: وجنات ألفافا

translation: Indeed, the Day of Judgement is an appointed time.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the inevitability and certainty of the Day of Judgement. It is a fixed appointment that cannot be delayed or avoided. The use of the word "miqat" (appointed time) underscores the precision and definiteness of this event. It serves as a reminder to humanity that they will be held accountable for their deeds and that the ultimate justice will be served on that day. The verse encourages believers to prepare for this momentous occasion by leading righteous lives and seeking Allah's forgiveness.
orig: إن يوم الفصل كان ميقاتا

translation: The Day the Horn will be blown, and you will come forth in multitudes
interpretation: This verse refers to the Day of Judgment when the trumpet will be blown, signaling the resurrection of the dead. All of humanity will rise from their graves and come forth in crowds to face the reckoning of their deeds. It emphasizes the magnitude and universality of this event, as every soul will be brought back to life to stand before Allah for judgment. The imagery of people coming in multitudes highlights the vast scale of resurrection and the overwhelming nature of that momentous day.
orig: يوم ينفخ في الصور فتأتون أفواجا

translation: And the heaven is opened and becomes gates.
interpretation: This verse refers to the Day of Judgment when the barriers between the heavens and the earth will be removed. The gates of heaven will be opened, signifying that the righteous believers will be granted admission into Paradise. It symbolizes the end of the worldly life and the beginning of the eternal afterlife, where people will face the consequences of their deeds. The opening of the heavenly gates also indicates the magnitude and glory of that Day, as it will be a momentous event witnessed by all of creation.
orig: وفتحت السماء فكانت أبوابا

translation: And the mountains will be moved and will be [but] a mirage.
interpretation: This verse is describing the Day of Judgment, when the world as we know it will come to an end. The mountains, which seem so solid and permanent in this life, will be made to move and will ultimately disappear like a mirage. This imagery conveys the idea that everything in this world is transient and illusory, and that the only true reality is Allah and the eternal life of the Hereafter. It reminds us not to be deceived by the apparent stability and durability of the physical world, but to focus on our spiritual lives and our relationship with Allah.
orig: وسيرت الجبال فكانت سرابا

translation: Indeed, Hell has been lying in wait
