interpretation: This verse warns that Hell is always watchful and ready to receive those who have earned it through their evil deeds and disbelief. It emphasizes the reality and severity of Hell as a punishment for the wicked. The use of the word "mirsaadaa" (lying in wait) personifies Hell as an entity that is vigilantly observing and anticipating the arrival of its inhabitants, ready to ensnare and punish them for their transgressions. This serves as a reminder for people to be mindful of their actions and to strive for righteousness to avoid this dreadful fate.
orig: إن جهنم كانت مرصادا

translation: A place of return for the transgressors.
interpretation: This verse refers to Hell as the ultimate destination and abode for those who transgress against the boundaries set by Allah, reject His guidance, and persist in their wrongdoings and disbelief. It serves as a warning that the transgressors will face the consequences of their actions in the Hereafter, where they will be consigned to the eternal punishment of Hell, a place of suffering and despair, as a result of their defiance and rebellion against Allah's commands.
orig: للطاغين مآبا

translation: Abiding therein for ages.
interpretation: This verse refers to the people who will abide in Hell for a very long time, described as "ages" or "aeons". It emphasizes the severity and duration of the punishment in Hell for those who have earned it through their actions and disbelief in this world. The use of the word "ahqab" (ages) indicates that their stay in Hell will feel endless and that there will be no respite or escape from its torment until Allah wills it.
orig: لابثين فيها أحقابا

translation: They will not taste therein [any] coolness or drink
interpretation: This verse refers to the punishment of the disbelievers in Hell. In the scorching heat of Hell, the disbelievers will not find any relief or respite from the torment. They will not have access to any means of cooling themselves, nor will they be given any drink to quench their thirst. This deprivation of coolness and drink emphasizes the severity and endlessness of the punishment in Hell, where the disbelievers will suffer without any comfort or mercy. It serves as a warning to those who reject faith and do not follow the path of righteousness, highlighting the consequences of their actions in the afterlife.
orig: لا يذوقون فيها بردا ولا شرابا

translation: Except boiling water and dirty wound discharges.
interpretation: This verse refers to the punishment that awaits the disbelievers in Hell. Instead of pure and refreshing water, they will only have access to boiling water that scalds their throats and faces, as well as filthy discharges from the wounds of the inhabitants of Hell. This interpretation highlights the severity and abhorrence of the punishment, emphasizing that the disbelievers will be deprived of any form of relief or comfort in the afterlife. It serves as a warning to those who reject faith and a reminder of the consequences of one's actions in this world.
orig: إلا حميما وغساقا

translation: A fitting recompense.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the concept of divine justice in Islam. It suggests that everyone will be rewarded or punished in the afterlife according to their deeds and actions in this world. Those who do good will be rewarded with good, while those who do evil will face the consequences of their actions. It is a reminder that God is just and fair, and that ultimately, we are all accountable for our choices and behavior in this life.
orig: جزاء وفاقا

translation: Indeed, they were not expecting an account.
interpretation: This verse suggests that the disbelievers lived their lives without any regard for the consequences of their actions. They did not believe that they would be held accountable by Allah for their deeds on the Day of Judgment. They lived as if there was no afterlife, no divine reckoning, and no ultimate justice. This lack of belief in accountability led them to transgress the bounds set by Allah and indulge in sins and disobedience without any fear of retribution. The verse implies that such an attitude is foolish and misguided, as every soul will indeed face the consequences of its actions in the Hereafter.
orig: إنهم كانوا لا يرجون حسابا

translation: And they denied Our signs with [emphatic] denial.
interpretation: This verse refers to those who persistently and emphatically reject the clear signs and proofs sent by Allah to guide humanity. They not only disbelieve in these divine revelations but also go to great lengths to deny their truth and validity. This emphatic denial stems from their arrogance, stubbornness, and unwillingness to submit to Allah's guidance. As a result of their strong rejection of the truth, they will face severe consequences in the Hereafter for their disbelief and for leading others astray.
orig: وكذبوا بآياتنا كذابا

translation: And all things We have enumerated in a clear register.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that everything in existence is accounted for and recorded by Allah in a clear register or book. It implies that nothing escapes Allah's knowledge and that He keeps precise records of all things, including the deeds of human beings. This verse serves as a reminder for humans to be mindful of their actions, as everything they do is being recorded and will be presented to them on the Day of Judgment. It also highlights Allah's omniscience and His perfect ability to keep track of every detail in the universe.
orig: وكل شيء أحصيناه كتابا

translation: So taste [the penalty], and never will We increase you except in torment.
interpretation: This verse is a stern warning to the disbelievers and those who reject God's message. It emphasizes that they will face severe punishment in the Hereafter for their actions and that their torment will only increase with time. The verse implies that once they "taste" the consequences of their disbelief, there will be no respite or mercy, only an escalation in their suffering. This serves as a reminder for individuals to be mindful of their choices and actions in this life, as they will have a direct bearing on their fate in the afterlife according to Islamic beliefs.
orig: فذوقوا فلن نزيدكم إلا عذابا

translation: Indeed, for the righteous is attainment
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that those who are righteous and God-fearing will ultimately achieve success, salvation, and a blissful end in the Hereafter. "Mafaza" can be interpreted as a place of safety, triumph, and felicity. The verse implies that by staying on the path of righteousness, believers will escape punishment and attain the reward of Paradise. It serves as a promise and motivation for the faithful to persist in their devotion and good deeds, knowing that their efforts will be rewarded with the ultimate success in the afterlife.
orig: إن للمتقين مفازا

translation: Gardens and grapevines
interpretation: This verse mentions two of the blessings that Allah bestows upon His servants in this world and in Paradise. Gardens and grapevines are a source of sustenance, beauty, and enjoyment. They symbolize the bounty and generosity of Allah towards His creation. The verse reminds us to be grateful for these blessings and to use them in a way that pleases Allah. It also points to the perfection and magnificence of Allah's creation, as He is the One who creates and sustains these gardens and grapevines.
orig: حدائق وأعنابا

translation: And full-breasted [companions] of equal age
interpretation: This verse refers to the companions of Paradise, describing them as youthful and attractive. The mention of "full-breasted" and "equal age" suggests that these companions will be in the prime of their beauty and vitality, and that they will be well-matched to their partners. This imagery conveys the idea of Paradise as a place of ultimate pleasure and fulfillment, where believers will be granted all that they desire in the company of pure and beautiful companions.
orig: وكواعب أترابا

translation: And a full cup [of wine]
interpretation: The mention of a full cup in this verse is symbolic of the bountiful blessings and rewards that await the righteous believers in Paradise. It represents the complete and overflowing satisfaction, joy, and pleasure that they will experience in the afterlife as a result of their faith and good deeds in this world. The cup being "full" emphasizes the abundance and never-ending nature of these divine favors bestowed upon them by Allah.
orig: وكأسا دهاقا

translation: No vain discourse will they hear therein, nor any falsehood.
interpretation: In Paradise, the believers will not hear any vain, useless, or frivolous speech, nor will they hear any lies or falsehood. This emphasizes the purity and sanctity of Paradise, where all speech will be truthful, meaningful, and beneficial. It also highlights the stark contrast between the environment of Paradise and the worldly life, where people often engage in idle talk, gossip, and dishonesty. The absence of such negative speech in Paradise indicates the perfection and righteousness of its inhabitants, who will be rewarded with an eternal abode free from any form of evil or wrongdoing.
orig: لا يسمعون فيها لغوا ولا كذابا

translation: A reward from your Lord, a sufficient gift.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the ultimate reward that believers seek is from Allah alone. It is a gift that is sufficient and fulfilling, not because of its quantity or worldly value, but because it comes from the Most Generous and Appreciative. The word "hisaaban" suggests that this reward will be given in full measure, without any shortcoming or withholding. It points to the satisfaction and contentment that the believers will find in Allah's gifts in the Hereafter, which will be far superior to any pleasures or rewards of this temporary worldly life.
orig: جزاء من ربك عطاء حسابا

translation: Lord of the heavens and the earth and whatever is between them, the Most Merciful. They do not possess [the right] to address Him.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute sovereignty and lordship of Allah over the entire universe, including the heavens, the earth, and everything in between. It also highlights His attribute of being the Most Merciful (Ar-Rahman). The verse further states that no one has the right or authority to speak to Allah or make any demands of Him, as He is the Supreme Being and all creation is subservient to Him. This underscores the importance of humility and submission before Allah, acknowledging His greatness and our complete dependence on His mercy and grace.
orig: رب السماوات والأرض وما بينهما الرحمن لا يملكون منه خطابا

translation: The Day that Ar-Ruh [Jibrael (Gabriel) or another angel] and the angels will stand forth in rows, they will not speak except him whom the Most Beneficent (Allah) allows, and he will speak what is right.
interpretation: This verse refers to the Day of Judgment when all of creation will stand before Allah. Even the angels, including Jibreel (Gabriel), will stand in rows, silent and awaiting Allah's command. None will dare to speak unless permitted by Allah, and those given permission will only speak the truth. This conveys the gravity, solemnity and magnitude of that Day, when all souls will be held accountable before their Creator. It emphasizes Allah's ultimate power and authority, and the importance of speaking only what is righteous and true.
orig: يوم يقوم الروح والملائكة صفا لا يتكلمون إلا من أذن له الرحمن وقال صوابا

translation: That is the True Day; so whoever wills may take to his Lord a [way of] return.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the reality and inevitability of the Day of Judgment, reminding people that it is a true event that will surely come to pass. It also highlights the concept of free will, indicating that each individual has the choice to seek a path that leads back to Allah (God) by following His guidance and doing righteous deeds. The verse implies that one should strive to make the best use of the opportunities in this life to earn Allah's pleasure and prepare for the eternal life in the Hereafter, where every soul will be held accountable for their actions.
orig: ذلك اليوم الحق فمن شاء اتخذ إلى ربه مآبا

translation: Indeed, We have warned you of a near punishment on the Day when a man will observe what his hands have put forth and the disbeliever will say, "Oh, I wish that I were dust!"
interpretation: This verse is a stark reminder of the Day of Judgment, when every individual will face the consequences of their actions in this world. The "near punishment" refers to the imminence and inevitability of this event. On that day, people will witness the results of their deeds, both good and bad, as if they are laid bare before them. The disbeliever, upon realizing the gravity of their mistake in rejecting faith, will wish they were reduced to mere dust, expressing deep regret and despair. This verse emphasizes the importance of faith, righteous deeds, and being mindful of the accountability we all face in the Hereafter.
orig: إنا أنذرناكم عذابا قريبا يوم ينظر المرء ما قدمت يداه ويقول الكافر يا ليتني كنت ترابا

translation: By those [angels] who extract with violence
interpretation: This verse is referring to the angels who pull out the souls of the disbelievers at the time of death. The word "gharqan" (translated as "with violence") indicates that the angels will extract these souls forcefully and violently, reflecting the difficult nature of death for those who rejected faith in God. This imagery sets the tone for the following verses which describe the Day of Judgment and the fate that awaits the deniers of truth.
orig: والنازعات غرقا

translation: And those who pull out, pulling out
interpretation: This verse is referring to the angels who pull out the souls of the disbelievers at the time of death. They do so with force and violence, as a punishment for their rejection of faith and their evil deeds in this world. It emphasizes the severity and harshness that the disbelievers will face in the Hereafter as a consequence of their actions.
orig: والناشطات نشطا

translation: By those [angels] who glide along [on errands of mercy]
interpretation: This verse is referring to the angels who traverse the heavens and the earth, carrying out Allah's commands and decrees. They are described as "gliding" or "swimming" (sabhan) through the vast expanse of the universe, indicating their swift and effortless movement as they fulfill their duties. This interpretation highlights the existence of angels as noble creatures who serve as intermediaries between Allah and His creation, executing His will and bringing mercy and blessings to those whom He favors.
orig: والسابحات سبحا

translation: And those [angels] who race each other in a race
interpretation: This verse refers to the angels who compete with one another in carrying out Allah's commands and decrees. They race to fulfill His orders and implement His will in the universe. It emphasizes the eagerness and swiftness of the angels in obeying Allah and executing their assigned tasks. The angels' dedication and promptness in serving Allah is an example for believers to emulate in their own worship and obedience to Him.
orig: فالسابقات سبقا

translation: By those [angels] who arrange [each] matter,
interpretation: This verse refers to the angels who are entrusted by Allah with managing and arranging the affairs of the universe according to His divine will and wisdom. They carry out His commands faithfully and efficiently, ensuring the smooth functioning and order of all creation. This highlights the meticulous planning and organization that goes into the running of the cosmos, under the supreme authority of Allah. It also emphasizes the important role played by the angels as obedient servants and executors of the divine decree.
orig: فالمدبرات أمرا

translation: The Day the earth will convulse
interpretation: This verse is referring to the Day of Judgment, when a great earthquake or convulsion will shake the earth. It signifies the tremendous upheaval and terror of that day, as the world as we know it comes to an end. The convulsion of the earth is one of the signs of the approaching Judgment, emphasizing the magnitude and inescapability of this event. It serves as a reminder for humans to be mindful of their actions and to prepare for the ultimate reckoning before Allah.
orig: يوم ترجف الراجفة

translation: There comes after it the subsequent [one].
interpretation: This verse is referring to the Day of Judgment, indicating that there will be a second blowing of the trumpet that will follow the first one. The first blow will cause all creatures to die, and the second blow will bring them back to life to face judgment before Allah. This emphasizes the certainty and inevitability of the Day of Resurrection and the accountability for one's deeds in this world.
orig: تتبعها الرادفة

translation: Hearts on that Day will be pounding.
interpretation: This verse is referring to the Day of Judgment, when people's hearts will be filled with intense fear and anxiety due to the uncertainty of their fate. The pounding of the hearts symbolizes the extreme distress and terror people will experience as they face the consequences of their deeds in this world. It serves as a reminder for believers to be mindful of their actions and to strive for righteousness, as they will be held accountable for everything they have done when they stand before Allah on that fateful Day.
orig: قلوب يومئذ واجفة

translation: Their eyes downcast.
interpretation: This verse refers to the state of the disbelievers on the Day of Judgment. Their eyes will be downcast out of shame, humiliation, and regret for their actions in the worldly life. They will realize the truth and the consequences of their disbelief and sins, but it will be too late for them to repent or change their fate. The downcast eyes symbolize their submission, helplessness, and despair in front of Allah's justice and punishment.
orig: أبصارها خاشعة

translation: They say, "Will we indeed be returned to [our] former state [of life]?"
interpretation: This verse questions the disbelief of those who deny the resurrection and the afterlife. They express their doubt and skepticism about the possibility of being brought back to life after death, considering it impossible to return to their former state of existence. The rhetorical question implies their rejection of the concept of resurrection, as they find it hard to believe that they will be revived after their bodies have decomposed in the grave. This verse highlights the lack of faith and the limited perspective of those who deny the power and wisdom of Allah in restoring life after death.
orig: يقولون أإنا لمردودون في الحافرة

translation: Even when we have become decayed bones?
interpretation: This verse is questioning the idea of resurrection after death, when the human body has decomposed into bones. It expresses skepticism or doubt about the possibility of being brought back to life after the physical body has completely decayed. The verse reflects the disbelief of those who find it hard to accept the concept of life after death and physical resurrection, considering the state of the human remains after a long time in the grave.
orig: أإذا كنا عظاما نخرة

translation: They said, "That would then be a losing return."
interpretation: This verse is referring to the disbelievers' reaction to the idea of resurrection after death. They are saying that if they were to be brought back to life after death, it would be a "losing return" for them, meaning that it would not be in their favor or to their benefit. They see resurrection as something undesirable and disadvantageous, as they do not believe in the afterlife and divine judgment. The verse captures their skepticism and rejection of the concept of life after death.
orig: قالوا تلك إذا كرة خاسرة

translation: Then it will only be a single shout,
interpretation: This verse is referring to the Day of Judgment, indicating that it will be initiated by a single, powerful blast from the Trumpet of the Angel Israfil. This emphasizes the suddenness and inevitability of the event, as it will happen in an instant, without any prior warning or opportunity for preparation. The verse also implies the immense power and authority of Allah, as He is able to bring about such a momentous event with a single command. This serves as a reminder to humanity that they should always be mindful of their actions and ready to face the consequences on the Day of Judgment.
orig: فإنما هي زجرة واحدة

translation: And suddenly they will be [alert] upon the earth's surface.
interpretation: This verse refers to the Day of Resurrection, when the dead will be brought back to life and will find themselves on the surface of the earth, fully conscious and aware. It emphasizes the suddenness and inevitability of this event, as well as the state of alertness and realization that people will experience upon being resurrected. The verse serves as a reminder of the reality of the afterlife and the accountability that all individuals will face for their deeds in this world.
orig: فإذا هم بالساهرة

translation: Has there come to you the story of Moses?
interpretation: This verse is an introduction to the story of Prophet Moses, which is narrated in the following verses. It serves as a rhetorical question to draw the attention of the listener or reader to the importance and significance of the story that is about to be told. The verse implies that the story of Moses contains valuable lessons and wisdom that are worthy of reflection and contemplation.
orig: هل أتاك حديث موسى

translation: When his Lord called him in the sacred valley of Tuwa.
interpretation: This verse refers to the moment when Allah called upon Prophet Moses (peace be upon him) in the sacred valley of Tuwa. It highlights the special spiritual status of this location where Allah chose to communicate directly with Moses. The fact that Allah initiated this conversation emphasizes His divine power and authority, while also signifying the importance of the message He was about to convey to Moses. This event marks the beginning of Moses' prophethood and his mission to guide the Children of Israel out of oppression in Egypt. It demonstrates Allah's direct intervention in human affairs to support His chosen messengers and establish justice on earth.
orig: إذ ناداه ربه بالواد المقدس طوى

translation: Go to Pharaoh. Indeed, he has transgressed.
interpretation: This verse is a command from Allah to Moses to go to Pharaoh and confront him about his arrogance and oppression. It shows that it is the duty of the prophets and believers to stand up against tyranny and injustice, even in the face of powerful rulers. The verse also implies that Pharaoh's transgression and abuse of power had reached such a level that divine intervention was necessary to put an end to it. It is a reminder that ultimately, all oppressors will be held accountable before Allah for their actions.
orig: اذهب إلى فرعون إنه طغى

translation: So say, "[O Muhammad], are you willing to purify yourself,"
interpretation: This verse is an invitation from Allah to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) to ask the disbelievers if they are willing to purify themselves spiritually by accepting Islam and following its teachings. It implies that the path to spiritual purification and righteousness is through belief in Allah and obedience to His commandments. The verse encourages the Prophet to continue his mission of inviting people to the way of Allah, even in the face of opposition and rejection from the disbelievers.
orig: فقل هل لك إلى أن تزكى

translation: And guide you to your Lord so you may fear [Him].
interpretation: The purpose of divine guidance is to lead one to the path of righteousness and God-consciousness. The ultimate goal is to develop a profound reverence and awe for Allah, which will motivate the individual to obey His commands and refrain from what He has prohibited. This verse emphasizes that the role of the prophets and messengers is to direct people towards their Creator, so that they may establish a strong connection with Him and live their lives in accordance with His will, driven by a deep sense of love, respect and fear of displeasing Him.
orig: وأهديك إلى ربك فتخشى

translation: Then He showed him the greatest sign.
interpretation: In this verse, Allah is referring to the miraculous journey of Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) known as Isra and Mi'raj, where he was taken from Mecca to Jerusalem and then ascended to the heavens. During this journey, Allah showed Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) many of His wondrous signs and miracles, the greatest of which was the direct communication between Allah and His servant. This event demonstrated Allah's immense power and the special status of Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) as His chosen messenger. It served as a powerful confirmation of his prophethood and a source of reassurance for him in the face of the challenges and adversities he faced in conveying Allah's message to mankind.
orig: فأراه الآية الكبرى

translation: But he denied and disobeyed.
interpretation: This verse is referring to the disbelief and disobedience of those who reject the message of Islam despite clear signs and guidance from Allah. It highlights the arrogance and stubbornness of those who choose to go against divine commandments, even when the truth is made evident to them. The verse serves as a warning that denying the truth and disobeying Allah's laws will lead to grave consequences in this life and the hereafter.
orig: فكذب وعصى

translation: Then he turned his back, striving [against Allah].
interpretation: This verse refers to a person who, after receiving guidance and knowledge from Allah, turns away from it and actively works against the message of Islam. It highlights the attitude of arrogance and defiance some people adopt when faced with the truth, choosing to strive against it rather than embrace it. The verse serves as a warning against such behavior and emphasizes the importance of humility and submission to Allah's guidance.
orig: ثم أدبر يسعى

translation: Then he gathered [his people] and called out
interpretation: This verse is referring to Pharaoh, who gathered his people and proclaimed his power and greatness over them. It shows his arrogance and pride, as he tried to assert his authority and make his people believe that he was their supreme lord. This action of gathering and calling out to his people demonstrates Pharaoh's tyrannical nature and his desire to maintain control over his subjects, even in the face of the clear signs and warnings sent by Allah through Moses.
orig: فحشر فنادى

translation: And he said, "I am your Lord, Most High."
interpretation: This verse refers to the arrogant claim made by Pharaoh, who considered himself to be the supreme lord over his people, rejecting the existence and authority of Allah. It highlights the extreme level of pride and self-delusion that can lead a person to believe they are superior to everyone, even God Himself. The verse serves as a warning against such arrogance and reminds believers to humble themselves before the one true Lord, Allah, and submit to His will alone.
orig: فقال أنا ربكم الأعلى

translation: So Allah seized him in exemplary punishment for the last and the first [transgression].
interpretation: This verse refers to the punishment that Allah inflicted upon Pharaoh for his arrogance and defiance of Allah's commands. The "last and the first transgression" refers to Pharaoh's persistence in his wrongdoing and his refusal to believe in Allah despite the clear signs and warnings he received. The verse emphasizes that Allah's punishment is severe and that no one can escape His justice, even if they are powerful and influential like Pharaoh was. It serves as a reminder to all people to humble themselves before Allah and to obey His commands, lest they face a similar fate.
orig: فأخذه الله نكال الآخرة والأولى

translation: Indeed in that is a lesson for those who fear [Allah].
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the stories and examples mentioned in the Qur'an serve as important lessons and reminders for those who have reverence and fear of Allah. It suggests that individuals who are mindful of Allah and seek to obey Him can derive wisdom, guidance, and admonition from the Qur'anic narratives. The verse implies that reflecting upon these lessons with a heart that fears Allah can lead to spiritual growth, increased faith, and a deeper understanding of the consequences of one's actions in this world and the hereafter.
orig: إن في ذلك لعبرة لمن يخشى

translation: Are you a more difficult creation or is the heaven? Allah constructed it.
interpretation: This verse is a rhetorical question that prompts reflection on the immense power and creativity of Allah. It suggests that the creation of the vast heavens is a far greater feat than the creation of human beings, yet humans sometimes behave arrogantly as if they are the most important creation. The verse reminds us of our relative insignificance in the grand scheme of Allah's creation and encourages humility before the Almighty. It also highlights the perfection and purposefulness in the construction of the heavens, inspiring awe at Allah's design of the universe.
orig: أأنتم أشد خلقا أم السماء بناها

translation: And raised its ceiling and proportioned it.
interpretation: This verse refers to the creation of the sky or heavens by Allah. The interpretation is that after creating the heavens, Allah raised them high above the earth like a canopy or ceiling. He made the sky well-proportioned and perfect in its structure and appearance, without any flaws or irregularities. This points to Allah's great power, precise design and order in the universe that He has created, and the harmony between the heavens and the earth.
orig: رفع سمكها فسواها

translation: And He makes dark its night and brings out its day.
interpretation: This verse refers to Allah's power and control over the universe. He is the One who alternates between night and day, making the night dark and bringing out the brightness of the day. It is a reminder of Allah's omnipotence and His ability to control all aspects of creation according to His will. The cycle of night and day is a sign of Allah's perfect design and a manifestation of His mercy towards His creatures, providing them with a time for rest and a time for work and activity. This verse encourages believers to reflect on the wonders of Allah's creation and to be grateful for His blessings.
orig: وأغطش ليلها وأخرج ضحاها

translation: And after that He spread the earth.
interpretation: This verse refers to the process of making the earth suitable for life after its initial creation. "Daha" in Arabic means to spread out or expand. It points to Allah's power and wisdom in making the earth a perfect place for His creatures to live, with its vast expanses, diverse landscapes, and delicate balance of resources. This verse invites us to reflect on the earth's beauty and intricacy, and to be grateful for the blessings that Allah has bestowed upon us through His creation.
orig: والأرض بعد ذلك دحاها

translation: He brought forth from it its water and its pasture
interpretation: This verse is referring to Allah's power and ability to bring forth sustenance and provisions from the earth. The "water" mentioned here can be interpreted as the life-giving rains that allow vegetation to grow, while the "pasture" refers to the resulting produce and greenery that provides food for grazing animals. This highlights Allah's mercy and wisdom in creating a system where the earth is made fertile and productive, sustaining His creation. It also serves as a reminder for humans to be grateful for these blessings and bounties provided by Allah.
orig: أخرج منها ماءها ومرعاها

translation: And the mountains, He set them firmly
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the power and wisdom of Allah in creating the mountains and setting them firmly on the earth. The mountains serve important purposes, such as stabilizing the earth's crust, providing habitats for various creatures, and acting as water reservoirs. Their presence is a testament to Allah's careful design and planning in creating a balanced and sustainable environment for life to thrive. The verse also reminds us of the immense strength and stability of the mountains, which can be seen as a metaphor for the unwavering faith and steadfastness that believers should strive for in their lives.
orig: والجبال أرساها

translation: As a provision for you and your livestock.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the bounty and mercy of Allah in providing sustenance and resources for both humans and their livestock. It reminds us that the provisions we enjoy in this world, such as food, water, and other necessities, are ultimately from Allah. He has created and sustains the earth and all its inhabitants. This should inspire gratitude and recognition of our dependence on Allah's grace. The verse also highlights the interconnectedness between humans and animals, as we share in the provisions of the earth. It encourages responsible stewardship and care for the creatures under our charge, acknowledging them as part of Allah's creation.
orig: متاعا لكم ولأنعامكم

translation: But when the greatest Overwhelming Calamity comes
interpretation: This verse is referring to the Day of Judgment, which is described as the "greatest Overwhelming Calamity". It suggests that this event will be of such immense magnitude and significance that it will overshadow all other calamities or disasters that have occurred in the world. The use of the word "Taamah" (Overwhelming Calamity) emphasizes the severity and inescapable nature of this event. It serves as a reminder to humanity that they will ultimately be held accountable for their deeds and that the Day of Judgment is an inevitable reality that everyone will have to face. The verse aims to instill a sense of awe, fear, and consciousness of God in the hearts of believers, urging them to prepare for that great day by leading righteous lives.
orig: فإذا جاءت الطامة الكبرى

translation: The Day when man will remember that for which he strove
interpretation: This verse refers to the Day of Judgment when every person will be confronted with their deeds, both good and bad, that they strove for in their worldly life. It serves as a reminder that our actions in this temporary world have consequences in the eternal Hereafter. On that Day, people will realize the true worth of their striving and will regret any time wasted or spent in disobedience to Allah. This verse encourages introspection and self-evaluation, urging us to be mindful of our actions and to strive in what pleases Allah and benefits us in the Hereafter, rather than being distracted by fleeting worldly pursuits that will be of no avail on the Day of Reckoning.
orig: يوم يتذكر الإنسان ما سعى

translation: And the Hellfire will be brought forth for [all] those who see -
interpretation: This verse is a stark reminder of the reality of the Hellfire and the consequences of one's actions in this world. The Hellfire will be made visible and brought close to the people on the Day of Judgment. It emphasizes that the Hellfire is not an abstract concept, but a real destination for those who have earned it through their sinful deeds and rejection of faith. Seeing the Hellfire with one's own eyes will be a terrifying and regretful moment for the sinners, as they will realize the gravity of their mistakes and the justice of Allah's punishment. This verse serves as a warning for people to be mindful of their actions and to strive for righteousness in order to avoid this dreadful fate.
orig: وبرزت الجحيم لمن يرى

translation: Then as for he who transgressed
interpretation: This verse refers to those who rebel against God and exceed the limits set by Him. It suggests that those who are arrogant, disobedient, and reject faith will face consequences for their actions. The verse serves as a warning against transgressing the boundaries of what God has ordained and emphasizes the importance of humility, obedience and staying within the limits of divine law.
orig: فأما من طغى

translation: But you prefer the worldly life,
interpretation: This verse is a reminder that many people prioritize the temporary pleasures and comforts of this worldly life over the eternal rewards of the Hereafter. It is a call to reflect on one's priorities and to strive for what is truly meaningful and lasting. The verse suggests that focusing solely on worldly gains is shortsighted, as the life of this world is fleeting compared to the everlasting life after death. It encourages believers to orient their lives around pleasing Allah and working for the Hereafter, rather than being consumed by material pursuits and immediate gratification in this temporary existence.
orig: وآثر الحياة الدنيا

translation: Indeed, Hell is the [final] refuge.
interpretation: This verse serves as a stern warning to those who reject faith and persist in wrongdoing. It emphasizes that their ultimate destination will be Hell, a place of eternal punishment and suffering. The verse highlights the consequences of one's actions and choices in this life, reminding individuals of the importance of faith, righteousness, and repentance. It also underscores the reality of divine justice, as those who transgress against God's laws and guidance will face the repercussions of their deeds in the afterlife.
orig: فإن الجحيم هي المأوى

translation: But as for he who feared the position of his Lord and prevented the soul from [unlawful] inclination,
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of having consciousness and fear of Allah, and the need to control one's desires and inclinations that may lead to sin. Those who are mindful of their standing before Allah on the Day of Judgment, and curb their soul's vain desires for the sake of Allah, are the ones who will attain success and salvation in the Hereafter. It highlights the value of self-restraint, piety, and submission to the will of Allah over the temporary and fleeting pleasures of this worldly life.
orig: وأما من خاف مقام ربه ونهى النفس عن الهوى

translation: Then indeed, Paradise will be [his] refuge.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that those who strive to purify their souls and resist their base desires will be rewarded with Paradise as their ultimate destination and eternal abode. It serves as a reminder that the temporary pleasures of this world are fleeting, and that one should focus on leading a righteous life to attain the everlasting bliss of Paradise in the Hereafter. The verse encourages believers to prioritize their spiritual well-being over worldly temptations, knowing that their efforts will be rewarded with the supreme comfort and peace of Paradise.
orig: فإن الجنة هي المأوى

translation: They ask you about the Hour (i.e., the Day of Resurrection): "When will be its appointed time?"
interpretation: This verse is referring to the curiosity and questioning of people about the exact time of the Day of Judgment. The interpretation is that only Allah knows the precise time of this event, and it is not for anyone else, including the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him), to know or reveal this information. The verse emphasizes the importance of focusing on one's spiritual preparation and good deeds rather than being preoccupied with the specific timing of the Day of Judgment, as it will come to pass at the appointed time decreed by Allah, and no one can hasten or delay it.
orig: يسألونك عن الساعة أيان مرساها

translation: What are you [concerned] with the mention of it (i.e., the Hour)?
interpretation: This verse is questioning why someone would be so preoccupied with the mention or discussion of the Hour (i.e., the Day of Judgment). It suggests that excessive speculation or obsession over the timing and details of the Hour is unproductive and misguided. Rather than being consumed with curiosity about the Hour, one should focus on living righteously and preparing for its inevitability through good deeds and obedience to God. Ultimately, the knowledge of the Hour's exact timing is with God alone.
orig: فيم أنت من ذكراها

translation: To your Lord is the final destination.
interpretation: This verse reminds us that our ultimate goal and the end of our journey in this life is to return to Allah, our Creator. It emphasizes that everything in this world is temporary and that our final destination is the Hereafter, where we will stand before our Lord and be held accountable for our deeds. This verse encourages believers to focus on their relationship with Allah and to strive to please Him in all aspects of their lives, knowing that He is the only One who can grant us eternal happiness and success in the Hereafter.
orig: إلى ربك منتهاها

translation: You are only a warner for those who fear it.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the Prophet Muhammad's role is to serve as a warner and reminder to those who have a sense of awe and reverence towards God and the Day of Judgment. His duty is to convey the message and guide those who are receptive to it, but he cannot force anyone to believe or change their ways. Ultimately, it is up to each individual to choose whether to heed the warning and embrace the path of righteousness out of their own free will and fear of God.
orig: إنما أنت منذر من يخشاها

translation: On the Day they see it, [it will be] as if they had not remained [in the world] except for an afternoon or a morning thereof.
interpretation: This verse is emphasizing the fleeting nature of this worldly life. When people are resurrected on the Day of Judgment and look back at their time on earth, it will seem to them as if they had lived for only a very short period of time, like a mere afternoon or morning. This is because the afterlife is eternal, and in comparison, the entire span of one's worldly life will appear insignificant and brief. The verse serves as a reminder for humans not to become engrossed in the temporary pleasures of this world, but rather to focus on preparing for the eternal life to come by living righteously and performing good deeds.
orig: كأنهم يوم يرونها لم يلبثوا إلا عشية أو ضحاها

translation: He frowned and turned away
interpretation: This verse is a gentle reprimand to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) for momentarily turning away from a blind man who had come to seek knowledge, in order to attend to some influential leaders of Quraysh. It reminds us that in the sight of Allah, a person's spiritual sincerity and yearning is more important than their worldly status or influence. We should give our full attention to anyone who comes to us seeking guidance about Islam, regardless of their social standing. The verse emphasizes the importance of humility, empathy and treating all people with equal respect in our interactions, especially when imparting religious knowledge and advice.
orig: عبس وتولى

translation: When the blind man came to him
interpretation: This verse is referring to an incident when a blind man, Abdullah ibn Umm Maktum, came to the Prophet Muhammad seeking guidance while the Prophet was in the midst of a conversation with some influential leaders of Quraysh. The verse gently admonishes the Prophet for frowning and turning away from the blind man, as it was his duty to attend to the needs of all individuals, regardless of their social status. It emphasizes the importance of treating all people with equal respect and giving priority to those seeking spiritual guidance and knowledge, even if they are from a lower social class or have a disability. The verse highlights the Islamic principles of equality, compassion, and the significance of attending to the needs of the marginalized members of society.
orig: أن جاءه الأعمى

translation: And what can make you know that he might purify himself
interpretation: This verse is a reminder that one should not judge others based on their outward appearance or status. It suggests that even those who may seem lowly or unimportant could potentially purify themselves spiritually and become righteous believers. The verse encourages humility and warns against making assumptions about people's inner states or spiritual potential. It emphasizes that only Allah truly knows what lies within someone's heart and their capacity for growth and goodness.
orig: وما يدريك لعله يزكى

translation: Or he may take heed and the reminder may benefit him.
interpretation: This verse suggests that the Qur'an serves as a reminder and admonition for those who are willing to listen and reflect upon its teachings. It implies that by paying attention to the message of the Qur'an and taking it to heart, one can derive great benefit and guidance from it. The verse encourages people to be open-minded and receptive to the wisdom contained within the Qur'an, as it has the power to positively transform their lives if they allow it to penetrate their hearts and minds.
orig: أو يذكر فتنفعه الذكرى

translation: But as for he who thinks himself without need,
interpretation: This verse is referring to those who are arrogant and think they are self-sufficient, not needing God's guidance or mercy. It suggests that such people, due to their pride and feeling of being above needing divine direction, turn away from the truth and from humbling themselves before their Lord. The implication is that this attitude leads one astray and is spiritually harmful, causing one to reject faith and revelation out of a misplaced sense of self-reliance and autonomy.
orig: أما من استغنى

translation: So you, [O Muhammad], direct yourself to him.
interpretation: This verse is addressing the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him), instructing him to devote himself fully to the one who approached him with a sincere desire to learn and understand the message of Islam. It emphasizes the importance of giving attention and guidance to those who genuinely seek knowledge and truth, even if they are initially hesitant or unsure. The Prophet is being told to make himself available to this individual, to answer their questions, and to provide them with the guidance they need to embrace the faith wholeheartedly.
orig: فأنت له تصدى

translation: And it is not upon you [O Muhammad] whether they purify themselves or not.
interpretation: This verse is addressing the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him), telling him that he is not responsible for whether people purify their souls and become righteous or not. His duty is only to convey the message of Islam and guide people to the right path. It is up to each individual to choose whether to accept this guidance and work on purifying themselves spiritually. The ultimate fate of their souls is not the Prophet's burden to bear, as he has fulfilled his responsibility by delivering the message. This highlights the Islamic principle of individual accountability, where each person is answerable for their own spiritual growth and actions.
orig: وما عليك ألا يزكى

translation: As for the one who came to you running
interpretation: This verse is referring to a sincere seeker of knowledge and guidance who comes to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) with eagerness and enthusiasm to learn about Islam. It highlights the importance of giving attention and priority to those who are genuinely interested in learning about the religion, even if they are from a lower social status or are not as influential as others. The verse emphasizes the value of humility and the significance of catering to the spiritual needs of individuals who are yearning for divine guidance, regardless of their worldly position or circumstances.
orig: وأما من جاءك يسعى

translation: And he fears [Allah]
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of having a sense of reverence and fear towards Allah. It suggests that a true believer is one who is constantly mindful of Allah and fears displeasing Him through disobedience or neglect. This fear is not a paralyzing terror, but rather a profound respect and awe that motivates the believer to strive for righteousness and avoid sin. It is a recognition of Allah's immense power and a desire to submit to His will out of love and devotion. Having this sense of "khushoo"" or reverent fear is seen as a key characteristic of the believers and a means of drawing closer to Allah.
orig: وهو يخشى

translation: But you, [O Muhammad], from it [i.e., the Hereafter] are distracted.
interpretation: This verse is a gentle reprimand to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) for being distracted by worldly matters and not focusing enough on the Hereafter. It serves as a reminder that the ultimate goal of a believer should be to prepare for the life to come, and not to get too absorbed in the temporary affairs of this world. The verse encourages the Prophet, and by extension, all Muslims, to prioritize their spiritual well-being and to keep the Hereafter at the forefront of their thoughts and actions.
orig: فأنت عنه تلهى

translation: Nay, it is surely a reminder.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the Qur'an is not just an ordinary book, but a profound reminder for humanity. It serves as a powerful admonition, guiding people towards the path of righteousness and reminding them of their ultimate purpose in life. The Qur'an is a divine message that awakens the hearts and minds of those who reflect upon its verses, urging them to contemplate the signs of Allah's creation and to live a life of submission to His will. As a reminder, the Qur'an encourages individuals to constantly seek spiritual growth, maintain a strong connection with their Creator, and strive for the betterment of themselves and society as a whole.
orig: كلا إنها تذكرة

translation: So whoever wills may remember it.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of free will and individual responsibility in remembering and reflecting upon the Qur'an and its teachings. It suggests that the choice to engage with the divine message and to internalize its lessons is ultimately up to each person. The verse implies that while guidance is available to all, it is the individual's prerogative to actively seek and embrace it. This highlights the Qur'an's view that faith and righteousness cannot be forced upon someone, but rather must be willingly and sincerely pursued by each believer.
orig: فمن شاء ذكره

translation: In honored scriptures
interpretation: This verse refers to the divine revelations and scriptures that are held in high esteem and are considered sacred by believers. The use of the word "honored" emphasizes the reverence and respect accorded to these religious texts, which are believed to contain the words and guidance of God. The verse suggests that these scriptures are not ordinary writings, but are distinguished and exalted due to their divine origin and the wisdom they impart to humanity.
orig: في صحف مكرمة

translation: Exalted and purified
interpretation: This verse is referring to the pages or records of deeds that are honored, elevated in status, and kept pure from any alteration or distortion. It signifies that the deeds of people are meticulously recorded and preserved by the noble angels appointed by Allah. These records will be presented on the Day of Judgment as an accurate and untainted account of each person's actions in this world, forming the basis for their final judgment and ultimate fate in the Hereafter.
orig: مرفوعة مطهرة

translation: By the hands of messenger-angels,
interpretation: This verse is referring to the noble angels who are entrusted by Allah to convey His messages and carry out His commands. They are described as "safarah" which means scribes or messengers, indicating their role in faithfully delivering Allah's revelations. The mention of their hands symbolizes their power, ability and readiness to fulfill the tasks assigned to them by Allah. It highlights the lofty status and trustworthiness of these angels in the divine scheme.
orig: بأيدي سفرة

translation: Noble and dutiful.
interpretation: This verse is describing the angels as being noble and dutiful in their service to Allah. They are obedient to His commands and carry out their duties with honor and dignity. The angels are pure beings created from light who worship Allah and act as intermediaries between Him and His creation. They are not prone to sin or disobedience like humans and jinn. This verse highlights their lofty status and the important role they play in the unseen spiritual realm.
orig: كرام بررة

translation: Man has killed, how ungrateful he is!
interpretation: This verse is expressing the idea that mankind has a tendency towards violence and killing, and that this is a sign of his ingratitude and ungratefulness towards God. It suggests that the act of taking a life is a grave sin and a rejection of the blessings and mercy that God has bestowed upon humanity. The verse is a reminder of the sanctity of life and the need for humans to show gratitude and respect for the gift of existence that God has given them, rather than engaging in acts of destruction and violence.
orig: قتل الإنسان ما أكفره

translation: From what thing did He create him?
interpretation: This verse is asking a rhetorical question about the origin of man's creation. It is meant to make the reader reflect on the fact that God created human beings from a seemingly insignificant substance, emphasizing His power and the miraculous nature of creation. The verse encourages humility and gratitude towards the Creator, reminding us of our humble beginnings and complete dependence on God. It also highlights the common origin shared by all human beings, which should serve as a basis for unity and equality among people, as we are all created by the same God from the same lowly substance.
orig: من أي شيء خلقه

translation: From a sperm-drop He created him and destined for him;
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the power and wisdom of Allah in creating human beings from a humble beginning, a mere drop of fluid. It also highlights the concept of divine decree or predestination (qadar), implying that Allah has determined the course of each person's life from the very start of their existence. This serves as a reminder for humans to be humble and recognize the immense power and knowledge of their Creator, who has fashioned them from something seemingly insignificant and has already ordained their path in life.
orig: من نطفة خلقه فقدره

translation: Then He makes the way easy for him.
interpretation: This verse refers to how Allah eases the path for those who strive in His cause and follow His guidance. It suggests that when a person sincerely seeks to please Allah and live according to His commands, Allah will remove the obstacles and difficulties from their path, making it easier for them to achieve success and reach their goals in this life and the Hereafter. It is a reminder of Allah's mercy and support for His faithful servants.
orig: ثم السبيل يسره

translation: Then He caused him to die and put him in his grave.
interpretation: This verse speaks to the power and control of Allah over human life and death. It reminds us that after creating us and giving us life, Allah also has the power to cause our death at any time He wills. The mention of the grave emphasizes the finality of death and that we will all eventually return to Allah. It is a call to reflect on the temporary nature of this worldly life and to strive in doing good deeds and worshipping Allah before death overtakes us. The verse also highlights Allah's ability to resurrect us from the grave for the final judgement, affirming the reality of the afterlife.
orig: ثم أماته فأقبره

translation: Then when He wills, He will resurrect him.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's power and control over life and death. It conveys that after a person's death, Allah has the ability to resurrect them whenever He chooses, demonstrating His supreme authority over all creation. This serves as a reminder to humans that their ultimate fate rests in Allah's hands and that they will be accountable for their deeds in the Hereafter when they are brought back to life by His will.
orig: ثم إذا شاء أنشره

translation: No! He has not yet accomplished what He commanded him.
interpretation: This verse is a reminder that man has not yet fulfilled the purpose for which God created him. It suggests that man has a duty and responsibility towards God, and that he will be held accountable for his actions and whether he lived up to what God commanded him to do. The verse implies that man should strive to obey God's commands and fulfill his purpose in this life, rather than being neglectful or disobedient. It is a call to be mindful of one's ultimate destiny and to live righteously in accordance with God's will.
orig: كلا لما يقض ما أمره

translation: Then let mankind look at his food
interpretation: This verse is a reminder for mankind to reflect upon and appreciate the food that Allah has provided for them. It encourages people to think about the origins and sources of their sustenance, and to recognize the blessings and bounties that Allah has bestowed upon them. By contemplating the food we eat, we can develop a deeper sense of gratitude and humility towards our Creator. This verse also implies that we should be mindful of what we consume, ensuring that it is halal (permissible) and obtained through ethical means. Ultimately, this reflection on our food should lead us to acknowledge Allah's power, wisdom, and mercy in sustaining all living beings.
orig: فلينظر الإنسان إلى طعامه

translation: Indeed, We have poured the water in abundance.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the abundance and bounty that Allah has provided in the form of water, which is essential for all life on earth. It reminds us of the immense blessing of water and how it is a vital resource that should be valued and not taken for granted. The verse also points to the power and control of Allah over the natural world, as He is the One who sends down the rain and causes the rivers to flow. It encourages gratitude and mindfulness of the countless blessings that Allah has bestowed upon us.
orig: أنا صببنا الماء صبا

translation: Then We split the earth, splitting [it with sprouts].
interpretation: This verse is referring to the power and mercy of Allah in causing the earth to split open and allow plants to grow forth from it. It is a reminder of the miraculous process of life and growth that Allah facilitates, and how He provides sustenance for His creation through the earth. The splitting of the earth can also symbolize the emergence of truth and guidance, as the Qur'an has been sent down to mankind to guide them on the right path. The verse encourages reflection on the signs of Allah's creation and the importance of recognizing His blessings and mercy in all aspects of life.
orig: ثم شققنا الأرض شقا

translation: And We caused to grow therein grains
interpretation: This verse highlights Allah's power and mercy in causing various grains to grow from the earth, providing sustenance for His creation. It reminds us of the blessings and bounties that Allah bestows upon us, and encourages gratitude for His provisions. The growth of grains also symbolizes the potential for spiritual growth and development within each individual, as we nurture the seeds of faith and righteousness in our hearts through obedience to Allah and adherence to His guidance.
orig: فأنبتنا فيها حبا

translation: And grapes and herbage
interpretation: This verse is referring to the bounties that Allah has provided for His creation. Grapes are a delicious fruit that grow in bunches, and are a source of nutrition and enjoyment for people. Herbage refers to the various green plants and vegetation that grow on the earth, which serve as food for grazing animals and add beauty to the landscape. The mention of these natural blessings is a reminder for humans to be grateful to Allah for His provisions and to use them in a way that pleases Him. It also points to the perfect design and balance in Allah's creation, where everything has a purpose and is interconnected in the grand scheme of life.
orig: وعنبا وقضبا

translation: And olives and palm trees
interpretation: This verse mentions olives and palm trees as examples of the bounties and blessings that Allah has provided for mankind. Olives and palm trees are both highly beneficial plants, providing food, oil, and other resources. The mention of these specific plants could also symbolize the diversity and abundance of provisions that Allah has created on earth for the benefit of His creation. It reminds us to be grateful for the numerous blessings and sustenance that Allah has bestowed upon us, and to recognize His wisdom and generosity in creating such a wide variety of useful plants and resources for our use and enjoyment.
orig: وزيتونا ونخلا

translation: And gardens of dense foliage.
interpretation: This verse is referring to the gardens of Paradise, which are described as having dense, lush foliage. The use of the word "ghulban" implies that the vegetation will be so thick and abundant that it will be difficult to penetrate or see through. This description emphasizes the beauty, richness, and perfection of the gardens in Paradise, which will be far superior to any gardens or landscapes found in this worldly life. The verse invites believers to strive for these eternal gardens through faith and righteous deeds.
orig: وحدائق غلبا

translation: And fruit and grass,
interpretation: This verse is highlighting the bounties and blessings that Allah has provided for His creation. "Fruit" represents the various delicious and nourishing fruits that grow from the earth, while "grass" or fodder represents the vegetation that supports grazing animals and livestock. These provisions demonstrate Allah's mercy, generosity, and care for all living beings, both humans and animals alike. It is a reminder for us to be grateful for the sustenance Allah has given us and to recognize His power and wisdom in creating a balanced ecosystem where all creatures' needs are met.
orig: وفاكهة وأبا

translation: As a provision for you and your livestock.
interpretation: This verse highlights that Allah has created the earth and its resources as a means of sustenance and benefit for human beings and their livestock. It emphasizes the divine wisdom behind the creation, where everything has been designed to support and facilitate the life of humans and the animals they depend upon. The verse reminds us to be grateful for these provisions and to use them responsibly, acknowledging them as a gift from the Almighty to fulfill our needs in this world.
orig: متاعا لكم ولأنعامكم

translation: Then when the Deafening Blast comes
interpretation: This verse is referring to the Day of Judgment, when a deafening sound will herald the beginning of the end. It is a warning to mankind that the ultimate reckoning is inevitable and that we must prepare for it by living righteous lives and fulfilling our obligations to Allah. The "Deafening Blast" is a sign of the immense power and magnitude of that event, showing that it will be unlike anything we have experienced in this worldly life. It serves as a reminder to focus on our spiritual growth and not be distracted by the temporary pleasures of this world.
orig: فإذا جاءت الصاخة

translation: The Day a man will flee from his brother
interpretation: This verse refers to the Day of Judgment, when people will be so consumed with their own fate that they will forsake even their closest family ties. It emphasizes the severity and intensity of that day, where the only concern will be one's own salvation. The fleeing from family members symbolizes the ultimate disruption of social bonds and the singular focus on facing God's judgment alone. It is a reminder that in the end, we are accountable as individuals and cannot rely on anyone else to save us from the consequences of our deeds.
orig: يوم يفر المرء من أخيه

translation: And his mother and his father
interpretation: This verse is emphasizing the importance of one's parents and the respect and gratitude that should be shown towards them. In Islam, being dutiful to one's parents is considered one of the most important obligations and is often mentioned alongside worshipping Allah alone. This verse serves as a reminder of the immense sacrifices and love that parents provide, and the need to reciprocate that love and care, especially as they grow older. Obeying and honoring one's parents is a means of attaining Allah's pleasure and blessings in this life and the hereafter.
orig: وأمه وأبيه

translation: And his wife and his children.
interpretation: This verse is emphasizing the importance of family ties and the strong bond between a man, his wife, and his children. It highlights the significance of maintaining good relations with one's immediate family members and treating them with kindness, love, and respect. The verse also implies that a person's responsibility extends beyond just himself, but also to his family, whom he should care for and protect.
orig: وصاحبته وبنيه

translation: Every man that Day will have enough to make him careless of others.
interpretation: This verse is referring to the Day of Judgment, when each person will be solely concerned with their own fate and standing before Allah. They will be so preoccupied with their own situation that they will have no time or attention for others, even their closest loved ones. It emphasizes the individual nature of the ultimate accountability before God, where everyone will face the consequences of their deeds alone, and no one can help or intercede for another. It is a reminder to focus on one's own spiritual state and conduct in this life, as that is what will matter in the end.
orig: لكل امرئ منهم يومئذ شأن يغنيه

translation: Faces on that Day will be bright,
interpretation: This verse refers to the faces of the believers on the Day of Judgment. Their faces will be radiant, shining with joy and happiness, reflecting the inner peace and contentment they feel. This is because they lived their lives in accordance with God's commands, performing good deeds and avoiding sin. As a result, they will be among the successful ones in the Hereafter, enjoying the rewards and blessings of Paradise. The bright and radiant faces symbolize the spiritual purity and success that the believers will attain through their faith and righteousness.
orig: وجوه يومئذ مسفرة

translation: Laughing, rejoicing
interpretation: This phrase is not a complete Qur'anic verse, but rather a description of a state or emotion. It depicts a person who is laughing and feeling happy or optimistic. In the context of the Qur'an, such phrases are often used to describe the faces of the believers on the Day of Judgment, when they will be rejoicing in the reward and mercy bestowed upon them by Allah. The believer's face will be "laughing and rejoicing" because of the joy and contentment they experience when they realize the great reward that awaits them in Paradise as a result of their faith and good deeds in this worldly life.
orig: ضاحكة مستبشرة

translation: And [some] faces, that Day, will have upon them dust.
interpretation: This verse refers to the Day of Judgment when some people will have faces covered with dust, indicating their humiliation and despair due to their sins and disbelief in this world. The dust on their faces symbolizes the darkness and gloom they will experience as a result of their actions. It serves as a reminder that one's deeds in this life will have consequences in the Hereafter, and that those who reject faith and do evil will face a grim fate on the Day of Reckoning.
orig: ووجوه يومئذ عليها غبرة

translation: Darkness covers it.
interpretation: This verse is referring to the Day of Judgment, when the faces of the disbelievers will be covered in darkness and gloom due to their sins and disbelief. It symbolizes the hopelessness, despair, and regret they will experience for not having followed the right path during their worldly life. The darkness on their faces will be a manifestation of the darkness in their hearts and souls, reflecting their spiritual state. This interpretation highlights the consequences of rejecting faith and the importance of living righteously to avoid such a fate in the Hereafter.
orig: ترهقها قترة

translation: Those are the disbelievers, the wicked ones.
interpretation: This verse is referring to those who reject faith in Allah and His messages, and instead follow their own desires and commit evil deeds. They are described as "disbelievers" because they knowingly deny the truth, and "wicked" because their actions are morally corrupt and sinful. The verse emphasizes that such people have strayed far from the path of righteousness and have earned Allah's displeasure and punishment in the Hereafter.
orig: أولئك هم الكفرة الفجرة

translation: When the sun is wrapped up [in darkness]
interpretation: This verse refers to one of the events that will take place on the Day of Judgment. The sun, which is a source of light and energy for the world, will be darkened and lose its light. This could symbolize the end of the world as we know it and the beginning of a new realm. It also reminds us that even the most powerful and seemingly permanent objects in the universe, like the sun, will one day come to an end and be subjected to Allah's power and will. This verse encourages believers to reflect on the temporary nature of this world and to focus on preparing for the eternal life to come.
orig: إذا الشمس كورت

translation: And when the stars fall, losing their luster,
interpretation: This verse refers to the Day of Judgment, when the natural order of the universe will be disrupted. The falling and dimming of the stars symbolize the dramatic events that will unfold during this time. It signifies that the world as we know it will come to an end, and all creation will be held accountable before Allah. This verse serves as a reminder of the temporary nature of this world and the importance of preparing for the eternal life to come by living righteously and fulfilling our obligations to Allah.
orig: وإذا النجوم انكدرت

translation: And when the mountains are moved
interpretation: This verse refers to the Day of Judgment when the natural order will be overturned. The mountains, which seem so solid and immovable in this life, will be set in motion and flattened. This conveys the overwhelming power of Allah and the momentous, transformative events that will occur on that Day. It is a reminder of the temporary, fleeting nature of the world and a warning for mankind to be mindful of the Hereafter and to live righteously in preparation for the judgment to come.
orig: وإذا الجبال سيرت

translation: And when the full-term she-camels are neglected,
interpretation: This verse refers to the Day of Judgment, when the world will be turned upside down and people will be held accountable for their deeds. The mention of neglected she-camels, which were highly valued in Arab society, symbolizes the complete disregard for worldly possessions and status on that day. It signifies that all material things that were once cherished will lose their significance, and only one's faith and good deeds will matter in the face of divine judgment. This verse serves as a reminder for humans to prioritize their spiritual well-being over temporary worldly gains.
orig: وإذا العشار عطلت

translation: And when the wild beasts are gathered together
interpretation: This verse refers to the Day of Judgment when all creatures, including wild animals, will be resurrected and gathered together before Allah. It signifies that even the animals will face the consequences of their actions in this world, and that Allah's justice encompasses all of His creation. The gathering of the wild beasts also symbolizes the end of the natural order as we know it and the beginning of a new reality where all creatures will be held accountable for their deeds. This verse serves as a reminder for humans to be mindful of their actions and to treat all of Allah's creation, including animals, with respect and compassion.
orig: وإذا الوحوش حشرت

translation: And when the seas are set on fire,
interpretation: This verse refers to one of the events that will take place on the Day of Judgment. The seas being "set on fire" is a metaphorical description indicating that the oceans will boil over, evaporate or otherwise be destroyed in a cataclysmic event. It signifies the complete transformation and upheaval of the earth's natural order as we know it, as part of the end of the world and the commencement of the afterlife. The image of the seas burning conveys the enormity and intensity of the changes that will occur on that momentous Day, emphasizing Allah's supreme power over His creation.
orig: وإذا البحار سجرت

translation: And when the souls are paired
interpretation: This verse refers to the Day of Judgment when souls will be paired with their deeds and the bodies they belonged to in this worldly life. It signifies that every soul shall be held accountable for its actions and will be justly recompensed. The pairing of souls also alludes to the idea that each person will be confronted with the reality of their beliefs, intentions, and actions, and the ultimate fate of their soul shall be decided based on Divine justice.
orig: وإذا النفوس زوجت

translation: And when the girl [who was] buried alive is asked
interpretation: This verse refers to the pre-Islamic practice of burying newborn girls alive, which was considered a great sin. On the Day of Judgment, these innocent girls will be asked for what crime they were killed, highlighting the gravity and injustice of this act. The verse serves as a strong condemnation of female infanticide and emphasizes the value and sanctity of every human life, regardless of gender. It also implies that those who committed this heinous crime will be held accountable and will have to answer for their actions in the Hereafter.
orig: وإذا الموءودة سئلت

translation: For what sin was it killed?
interpretation: This verse is questioning the reason behind the killing of an innocent soul, emphasizing the gravity and injustice of taking a life without a valid reason. It implies that killing an innocent person is a grave sin and that the perpetrator will be held accountable before Allah for this heinous act. The verse encourages people to respect and value human life, and to refrain from unjustly taking it away.
orig: بأي ذنب قتلت

translation: And when the pages are spread [i.e., made public].
interpretation: This verse refers to the Day of Judgment when the records of deeds of every individual will be laid open. All the actions, good or bad, done in this worldly life will be made known on the Day of Reckoning. Nothing will remain hidden, and every person will be confronted with their own record. This verse serves as a reminder for humans to be mindful of their actions in this life, as they will be held accountable for them in the Hereafter. It encourages righteousness and discourages wrongdoing, as the consequences of one's actions will be made manifest on that Day.
orig: وإذا الصحف نشرت

translation: And when the sky is stripped away
interpretation: This verse refers to the Day of Judgment when the sky will be torn apart and stripped away, revealing the ultimate reality and the presence of Allah. It signifies that all the veils and barriers that concealed the truth in this world will be removed, and everything will be laid bare before Allah. The stripping away of the sky is a metaphor for the complete exposure and revelation of all deeds, intentions, and secrets. It is a reminder that on the Day of Judgment, nothing will remain hidden, and every soul will be held accountable for its actions in this world.
orig: وإذا السماء كشطت

translation: And when the Hellfire is set ablaze
interpretation: This verse refers to the Day of Judgment when the Hellfire will be ignited and intensified for those who have earned it through their evil deeds and disbelief in this world. It serves as a warning to humanity that the consequences of their actions in this life will be faced in the Hereafter, and that the punishment of the Hellfire is severe and everlasting for those who have been condemned to it. The verse also implies that the Hellfire is not constantly burning, but will be set ablaze on the Day of Judgment for the purpose of punishing the sinners. This emphasizes the gravity and finality of the Day of Reckoning.
orig: وإذا الجحيم سعرت

translation: And when Paradise is brought near
interpretation: This verse refers to the Day of Judgment when Paradise will be brought close to the righteous believers as a reward for their good deeds and obedience to Allah. It signifies that the ultimate goal and aspiration of the believers will be within reach. The nearness of Paradise is a metaphor indicating that the believers will soon be admitted into it and will be able to enjoy its blessings and delights eternally. This verse serves as a reminder and motivation for the believers to continue striving in Allah's path and to remain steadfast in faith, knowing that their ultimate destination is the blissful nearness of Paradise in the Hereafter.
orig: وإذا الجنة أزلفت

translation: Every soul will know what it has brought.
interpretation: This verse refers to the Day of Judgment when every person will become fully aware of their deeds, both good and bad, that they have sent forth in their worldly life. They will realize the consequences of their actions and the ultimate fate that awaits them based on what they have earned through their conduct. It serves as a reminder for individuals to be mindful of their choices and actions in this life, as they will be held accountable for them in the Hereafter.
orig: علمت نفس ما أحضرت

translation: So I swear by the retreating stars -
interpretation: In this verse, Allah swears by the "retreating stars", which are understood to be the planets that appear to move backwards (retrograde) periodically in the night sky from the perspective of the earth. This is a powerful oath by Allah, drawing attention to His immense power and control over the celestial bodies and the precise laws of the universe that He has set in motion. It is a reminder for mankind to marvel at Allah's creation and recognize Him as the One Creator and Sustainer of all existence.
orig: فلا أقسم بالخنس

translation: By the runners, the women who withdraw,
interpretation: This verse is referring to the stars that traverse the sky at night, likening their movement to that of a group of women who are hastening to fulfill their duties. The stars are described as "al-kunnas", which means they withdraw or recede during the day and become visible at night. This is a reminder of Allah's power and control over the universe, as He has set the stars in motion according to His divine plan. The verse invites us to reflect on the beauty and precision of Allah's creation, and to recognize His greatness and majesty.
orig: الجوار الكنس

translation: And by the night when it darkens,
interpretation: This verse is an oath by the night when it becomes very dark, quiet and still. It refers to the depth of night, a time when people usually sleep and rest. The darkness and stillness of night is a sign of Allah's power and control over the universe. It also serves as a reminder for humans to reflect on their deeds during the day and seek forgiveness for their shortcomings before the night ends and a new day begins.
