This verse emphasizes the divine design and intricacy involved in the human reproductive process, highlighting that God has created human beings with a remarkable system for procreation.
orig: يخرج من بين الصلب والترائب

translation: Indeed, He is Able to bring him back [to life].
interpretation: This verse affirms Allah's power and ability to resurrect the dead on the Day of Judgment. It emphasizes that just as Allah created human beings in the first place, He is certainly capable of bringing them back to life after death for the purpose of judgment and recompense. This verse serves as a reminder of the inevitability of the afterlife and encourages believers to live their lives in accordance with the teachings of Islam, knowing that they will be held accountable for their deeds in the Hereafter.
orig: إنه على رجعه لقادر

translation: The Day when secrets will be disclosed.
interpretation: This verse refers to the Day of Judgment when all the secrets of people will be exposed and brought to light. Nothing will remain hidden on that day. All the deeds, intentions, and thoughts that were concealed in worldly life will be made manifest before Allah. It serves as a reminder for believers to be mindful of their actions and intentions, knowing that ultimately everything will be unveiled and accounted for in front of their Lord.
orig: يوم تبلى السرائر

translation: For he has no power or helper.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the complete powerlessness and helplessness of those who reject faith in Allah. Without Allah's support and guidance, no one has any real strength or assistance to rely upon. It serves as a reminder that ultimately, we are all dependent on Allah and that true power and help can only come from Him. Those who turn away from Allah's path will find themselves alone and without any reliable ally or protector in this world or the Hereafter.
orig: فما له من قوة ولا ناصر

translation: By the sky which returns [rain]
interpretation: This verse is referring to the water cycle, where water evaporates from the Earth's surface, condenses in the sky to form clouds, and then returns back to Earth as rain. It is a sign of Allah's power and wisdom in creating a self-sustaining system that supports life on our planet. The verse invites us to reflect on this natural phenomenon and appreciate the delicate balance that Allah has established in His creation.
orig: والسماء ذات الرجع

translation: By the Earth that cracks open,
interpretation: This verse is referring to the Earth's ability to split and crack, allowing for the growth of vegetation. It is a reminder of Allah's power and ability to create life and sustain it. The cracking of the Earth can also symbolize the emergence of truth and the removal of falsehood, as well as the resurrection of the dead on the Day of Judgment when the Earth will split open and the dead will rise from their graves. This verse emphasizes the importance of acknowledging Allah's signs in nature and reflecting on His creation.
orig: والأرض ذات الصدع

translation: Indeed, it is a decisive statement,
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the clear and unambiguous nature of the Qur'an. It affirms that the Qur'an is a decisive statement, leaving no room for doubt or confusion. The Qur'an provides guidance and clarity, distinguishing truth from falsehood. It is a definitive message from Allah, delivered with precision and wisdom, serving as a criterion for mankind to follow. The verse highlights the authority and significance of the Qur'an as a divine revelation that resolves matters decisively.
orig: إنه لقول فصل

translation: And it is not a joke.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the seriousness and gravity of the matter being discussed. It suggests that the subject at hand, likely referring to the Qur'an or the Day of Judgment, should not be taken lightly or dismissed as mere jest. The verse serves as a reminder to approach such matters with utmost sincerity, reverence, and understanding of their profound significance in the context of Islamic faith.
orig: وما هو بالهزل

translation: Indeed, they are plotting a plot.
interpretation: This verse is a warning from Allah that the disbelievers are constantly plotting and scheming against Islam and the Muslims. They are always trying to find ways to undermine the religion and create doubts in the hearts of the believers. However, their plots will ultimately fail because Allah is the best of planners and He will protect His religion and His faithful servants. The verse reminds us to be aware of the enemies of Islam and to remain steadfast in our faith, trusting in Allah's plan and wisdom.
orig: إنهم يكيدون كيدا

translation: And plot (your) plotting.
interpretation: This verse is a challenge to the disbelievers who plot against Islam and the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him). It tells them to go ahead and scheme all they want, but ultimately their plots will fail and God's plan will prevail. It conveys that no matter how cunningly they plan, they cannot outsmart God or prevent His will from being realized. The verse also serves as a reassurance to believers to not be discouraged by the machinations of those who oppose them and their faith, as the ultimate victory belongs to God and those who are on His path.
orig: وأكيد كيدا

translation: So allow time for the disbelievers. Leave them awhile.
interpretation: This verse is a warning to the disbelievers, telling the Prophet Muhammad to give them respite and allow them time to reflect and repent. It suggests that the disbelievers should not be immediately punished or condemned, but rather given an opportunity to change their ways and embrace the truth of Islam. The use of the word "ruwayda" (meaning "a little while") indicates that this period of respite is temporary and that ultimately, the disbelievers will have to face the consequences of their actions if they persist in their disbelief. It is a reminder of Allah's mercy and patience, as well as a call for the believers to exercise restraint and not rush to judge others.
orig: فمهل الكافرين أمهلهم رويدا

translation: Exalt the name of your Lord, the Most High,
interpretation: This verse is a command to glorify and praise Allah, the Most High, by remembering His name and attributes. It reminds us to recognize His greatness and superiority over all creation. By exalting Allah's name, we acknowledge His power, wisdom, and perfection. This act of glorification should be done sincerely and consistently, as it helps us maintain a strong connection with our Creator and cultivate humility and reverence in our hearts. Remembering Allah's name and exalting Him is a fundamental aspect of Islamic spirituality and a means of attaining inner peace and contentment.
orig: سبح اسم ربك الأعلى

translation: Who created and proportioned
interpretation: This verse refers to Allah, the Creator, who not only brought everything into existence but also fashioned and balanced His creation with perfect proportion and harmony. It emphasizes Allah's power, wisdom, and the purposeful design in the universe. The verse invites us to reflect on the perfection and intricate balance in the world around us, recognizing it as a sign of Allah's creative might and His role as the Fashioner of all things.
orig: الذي خلق فسوى

translation: And Who has measured [all things] and then guided [them]
interpretation: This verse refers to Allah's attribute of providing guidance and direction to His creation. It implies that Allah has not only created everything in the universe but has also determined their purpose and guided them towards fulfilling it. This guidance includes the instincts and natural patterns that Allah has placed within living beings, as well as the revelation and messages sent through prophets to guide humanity. The verse emphasizes Allah's wisdom, knowledge, and care in measuring and directing all affairs in the creation according to His divine plan.
orig: والذي قدر فهدى

translation: And [it is He] who causes grazing pastures to grow
interpretation: This verse highlights Allah's power and generosity in causing vegetation to grow on the earth, providing sustenance for grazing animals. It is a reminder of Allah's mercy and His ability to bring forth life and nourishment even from the seemingly lifeless earth. The growth of pastures is a sign of Allah's creative power and a means by which He sustains His creatures. This verse encourages gratitude for the blessings that Allah bestows upon His creation and prompts reflection on the intricate balance and harmony in the natural world.
orig: والذي أخرج المرعى

translation: And He made it as black stubble.
interpretation: This verse is referring to the aftermath of the destruction that Allah can bring upon the disbelievers. The term "ghuthaa" refers to the debris or rubbish left behind after plants have been cut down and left to dry and wither away. "Ahwaa" means black and dark in color. So the verse paints a vivid picture of how Allah can reduce what was once green and thriving to mere blackened remnants and stubble, symbolizing the fate that awaits those who reject faith and persist in wrongdoing. It is a reminder of Allah's ultimate power over all things.
orig: فجعله غثاء أحوى

translation: We will make you recite, [O Muhammad], and you will not forget,
interpretation: This verse is a promise from Allah to Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) that He will reveal the Qur'an to him and make him recite it, and that the Prophet will not forget what has been revealed to him. This is a reassurance to the Prophet that the preservation of the Qur'an is not his responsibility, but rather it is Allah who will protect and preserve it. This verse also highlights the divine nature of the Qur'an and the infallibility of the Prophet's memory in conveying the message accurately.
orig: سنقرئك فلا تنسى

translation: Except what Allah wills. Indeed, He knows what is declared and what is hidden.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute knowledge and power of Allah. It affirms that nothing happens in the universe without His will and permission. Moreover, it highlights that Allah is aware of everything, whether it is apparent or concealed from human perception. This includes people's actions, intentions, and even their innermost thoughts. The verse serves as a reminder for believers to be mindful of Allah's omniscience and to strive for righteousness in all aspects of their lives, knowing that nothing escapes His knowledge.
orig: إلا ما شاء الله إنه يعلم الجهر وما يخفى

translation: And We will ease you toward ease.
interpretation: This verse is a promise from Allah to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and to all believers that He will make their path easy and will guide them towards goodness and righteousness. It is a reminder that even in the face of difficulties and challenges, Allah will provide a way out and will make things easier for those who strive in His cause. The verse encourages the believers to remain steadfast in their faith and to trust in Allah's plan, knowing that He will always support and assist them in their journey towards success and salvation.
orig: ونيسرك لليسرى

translation: So remind, if the reminder should benefit;
interpretation: This verse encourages the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and by extension, all believers, to continue reminding people about the message of Islam and the teachings of the Qur'an, as long as there is benefit in doing so. The reminder serves as a means of guiding people towards the right path and helping them remember their purpose in life. However, the verse also implies that if the reminder does not benefit or falls on deaf ears, then one should not persist in trying to convince those who are unwilling to listen or change their ways. The decision to accept or reject the message ultimately lies with the individual, and the believer's duty is to convey the message with wisdom and compassion.
orig: فذكر إن نفعت الذكرى

translation: He who fears [Allah] will be reminded.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that only those who have a sense of awe and reverence for Allah will truly benefit from the reminders and guidance provided in the Qur'an. It suggests that a person must have a certain level of God-consciousness and humility to internalize the messages and admonitions contained within the divine revelation. Without this foundational fear of Allah, the individual may hear the words but fail to absorb their deeper meanings and implications for their life. Thus, the verse highlights the importance of cultivating taqwa, or a profound awareness of Allah's presence and power, as a prerequisite for spiritual growth and receptivity to Qur'anic teachings.
orig: سيذكر من يخشى

translation: But the most wretched will avoid it -
interpretation: This verse refers to the people who will avoid the blazing Fire of Hell on the Day of Judgment. The "most wretched" are those who rejected faith, disbelieved in Allah and lived a life of sin and disobedience. They did not heed the warnings and continued in their evil ways. As a result, they will be far removed from Allah's mercy and will not be able to enter Paradise. Instead, they will face the severe punishment of the Hellfire, which they earned through their own misdeeds and rejection of the truth.
orig: ويتجنبها الأشقى

translation: The one who will burn in the greatest Fire,
interpretation: This verse refers to those who will face the severest punishment in the Hereafter, which is the burning in the great Fire of Hell. It implies that there are varying degrees of punishment in the afterlife, and the greatest Fire is reserved for those who committed the gravest sins and rejected faith in God. The verse serves as a warning to mankind about the consequences of disbelief and wrongdoing, urging them to follow the righteous path to avoid such a terrible fate.
orig: الذي يصلى النار الكبرى

translation: Then he will neither die therein nor live.
interpretation: This verse refers to the fate of those who are condemned to Hell. It suggests that the punishment of Hell is eternal and that there will be no escape or relief from it. The damned will not be granted the mercy of death, which would end their suffering, but nor will they be truly alive, in the sense of enjoying any of the pleasures or comforts of life. Instead, they will be trapped in a state of endless torment, neither fully dead nor fully alive. This stark image conveys the severity and hopelessness of the punishment that awaits those who have earned God's condemnation through their actions in this life.
orig: ثم لا يموت فيها ولا يحيى

translation: Certainly will the believers have succeeded: They who are during their prayer humbly submissive.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of purifying one's soul and being humble and submissive in prayer. It suggests that true success and spiritual fulfillment can be attained by those who strive for inner purity and approach prayer with a sense of humility and reverence. The verse implies that merely going through the motions of worship is not enough; rather, one must engage in sincere self-purification and cultivate a deep connection with God through humble and focused prayer. Ultimately, those who embody these qualities are the ones who will attain true success and contentment in both this life and the hereafter.
orig: قد أفلح من تزكى

translation: And he remembered the name of his Lord and prayed.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of remembering Allah and establishing prayer. It suggests that when one is mindful of Allah and invokes His name, it should be followed by the act of prayer. Prayer is a means of connecting with the divine and expressing gratitude, submission, and seeking guidance. The verse implies that the remembrance of Allah and the performance of prayer are essential aspects of a believer's spiritual life, bringing them closer to their Lord and attaining inner peace and contentment.
orig: وذكر اسم ربه فصلى

translation: But you prefer the worldly life,
interpretation: This verse is a reminder that humans often prioritize the temporary pleasures and comforts of this worldly life over the eternal rewards of the Hereafter. It suggests that people are inclined to focus on the immediate gratification of their desires, neglecting their spiritual obligations and the consequences of their actions in the afterlife. The verse encourages believers to reflect on their priorities and to strive for balance, ensuring that they do not become entirely consumed by worldly pursuits at the expense of their faith and moral responsibilities.
orig: بل تؤثرون الحياة الدنيا

translation: And the Hereafter is better and more lasting.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance and superiority of the eternal life in the Hereafter compared to the temporary and fleeting nature of the worldly life. It reminds believers that striving for success and rewards in the afterlife should be their ultimate goal, as the Hereafter offers everlasting peace, happiness, and closeness to Allah. The verse encourages Muslims to prioritize their actions and decisions based on what will benefit them in the life to come, rather than being solely focused on the short-lived pleasures and gains of this world.
orig: والآخرة خير وأبقى

translation: Indeed, this is in the former scriptures.
interpretation: This verse affirms that the message and teachings of the Qur'an are not new, but rather a continuation and confirmation of the divine revelations that came before it, such as the scriptures of Abraham and Moses. It emphasizes the consistency and universality of God's message throughout human history, and that the Qur'an is a reminder and reinforcement of the eternal truths and guidance contained in the earlier scriptures.
orig: إن هذا لفي الصحف الأولى

translation: The scriptures of Abraham and Moses.
interpretation: This verse is referring to the sacred scriptures that were revealed to the prophets Abraham and Moses before the revelation of the Qur'an to Prophet Muhammad. These scriptures, such as the Torah given to Moses, contained divine guidance and teachings for their respective nations. The mention of these earlier prophets and their scriptures in the Qur'an serves to emphasize the continuity of God's message throughout history and the unity of the core teachings across different revelations. It also affirms that Muhammad's message is not a novelty, but rather a confirmation and culmination of the same eternal truth that was conveyed by the earlier prophets.
orig: صحف إبراهيم وموسى

translation: Has there come to you the report of the Overwhelming [event]?
interpretation: This verse is a rhetorical question, asking if the listener has heard about the overwhelming event, referring to the Day of Judgment. It serves as a reminder and a warning to reflect upon the inevitable reckoning that every soul will face. The verse aims to capture the attention of the audience and encourage them to contemplate the consequences of their actions in this life, as they will be held accountable on that momentous day. It emphasizes the importance of being prepared for the Hereafter and living a life in accordance with God's guidance.
orig: هل أتاك حديث الغاشية

translation: Faces on that Day will be humbled.
interpretation: This verse refers to the Day of Judgment when people will be held accountable for their deeds. The faces of those who lived a life of disobedience to Allah will be humbled and downcast, reflecting their shame, regret, and fear of the consequences they are about to face. It serves as a reminder that everyone will have to answer for their actions and that the ultimate humiliation awaits those who turned away from the path of righteousness. The verse encourages introspection and the pursuit of a life pleasing to Allah to avoid such a fate on the Day of Reckoning.
orig: وجوه يومئذ خاشعة

translation: 'Amilatun Nasibatun
interpretation: This phrase refers to a particle in Arabic grammar that causes the following noun or pronoun to be in the accusative case (nasb). It is a grammatical term used to describe the function of certain words or particles that affect the case ending of the subsequent word. The presence of an "'amilatun nasibatun" changes the grammatical state of the word that follows it, requiring it to be in the accusative case.
orig: عاملة ناصبة

translation: He will burn in a Flaming Fire.
interpretation: This verse serves as a severe warning to those who reject faith and choose to disobey Allah. It emphasizes the grave consequences of such actions, stating that the disbelievers will be subjected to the torment of the blazing Hellfire in the Hereafter. The "Flaming Fire" mentioned here refers to the intense punishment that awaits those who turn away from the truth and persist in their wrongdoings. This interpretation highlights the importance of faith, righteousness, and submission to Allah's will to avoid the painful destiny of the Hellfire and attain salvation in the afterlife.
orig: تصلى نارا حامية

translation: They will be given to drink from a flowing spring.
interpretation: This verse refers to the righteous believers in Paradise who will be rewarded with pure, ever-flowing water from a spring as a blessing for their good deeds and faith in this world. The spring is described as "aaniyah", indicating its continuous flow and abundance, symbolizing the never-ending blessings and bounties that the believers will enjoy in the eternal life of the Hereafter. This reward signifies the ultimate satisfaction, purity, and refreshment that the believers will experience in Paradise, in contrast to the temporary and often tainted pleasures of this worldly life.
orig: تسقى من عين آنية

translation: No food will there be for them except from a bitter, thorny plant
interpretation: This verse refers to the food of the people in Hell. The only food available to them will be a thorny, bitter, and foul-smelling plant known as "dari'". This plant is so vile and disgusting that even starving animals would avoid eating it. The verse emphasizes the severity of the punishment in Hell, where not even basic sustenance will provide any comfort or relief to the sinners. It serves as a warning to mankind to avoid actions that lead to such a fate and to strive for righteousness in order to attain Paradise, where bountiful and delightful provisions await the believers.
orig: ليس لهم طعام إلا من ضريع

translation: It neither nourishes nor avails against hunger.
interpretation: This verse is often interpreted metaphorically to mean that something is useless or futile. It suggests that the thing being referred to provides no real sustenance, benefit or fulfillment, just as food that does not nourish or satisfy hunger is pointless. The implication is that one should not waste time or effort on fruitless endeavors that do not enrich the soul or bring one closer to God. Instead, a person should focus on that which is truly nourishing spiritually and which helps ward off the hunger of the soul.
orig: لا يسمن ولا يغني من جوع

translation: Faces, that Day, will be radiant,
interpretation: This verse refers to the faces of the believers on the Day of Judgment. Their faces will be radiant, shining with happiness and joy, reflecting the inner peace and contentment they feel. This is because they lived their lives in accordance with Allah's commands, seeking His pleasure and striving to do good deeds. As a result, they will be among the successful ones in the Hereafter, enjoying the bliss of Paradise. The radiance on their faces symbolizes the light of faith and the beauty of their souls, which will be manifested outwardly on that great Day.
orig: وجوه يومئذ ناعمة

translation: With her effort, satisfied.
interpretation: This verse suggests that one should strive and put in effort in a manner that leaves them content and satisfied with what they have done. It implies that the level of satisfaction with one's actions is linked to the amount of effort and hard work they put in. Contentment comes from knowing that one has done their best and given their all in pursuing their goals or fulfilling their responsibilities.
orig: لسعيها راضية

translation: In a high garden.
interpretation: This verse is referring to the lofty status and elevated ranks of Paradise that the righteous believers will attain in the Hereafter. The "high garden" symbolizes the ultimate spiritual bliss, peace, and closeness to Allah that the faithful servants will experience as a reward for their good deeds and obedience in this worldly life. It indicates that Paradise is not just a physical place of pleasure, but also a state of profound spiritual joy and contentment in the presence of the Almighty.
orig: في جنة عالية

translation: No evil speech will they hear therein
interpretation: This verse refers to the blessed state of the believers in Paradise. It indicates that in Paradise, the believers will not hear any vain, frivolous, or sinful speech. The atmosphere will be pure, serene, and free from anything that causes distress or offends the senses. This is a great blessing and reward for the righteous who guarded their tongues and avoided vain talk in their worldly life. It signifies the perfect peace and tranquility that the inhabitants of Paradise will experience, in a realm where only good and pleasant things exist.
orig: لا تسمع فيها لاغية

translation: In both of them are two springs, flowing freely.
interpretation: This verse is describing the two gardens of Paradise promised to the righteous believers. The mention of "two springs, flowing freely" indicates the abundant blessings and bounties that will be available to the inhabitants of these gardens. The ever-flowing springs symbolize the endless provision of refreshment, sustenance, and delight for those who have earned their place in Paradise through their faith and good deeds in this worldly life. It is a reminder of the rewards awaiting those who strive to please Allah and follow His guidance.
orig: فيها عين جارية

translation: Within it are [thrones or beds] raised high.
interpretation: This verse is describing one of the features of Paradise (Jannah). The "thrones or beds raised high" symbolize the honor, comfort, and luxury that will be bestowed upon the believers in the afterlife. These thrones or beds are elevated, indicating the high status and rank of those who will occupy them. The verse emphasizes that Paradise is a place of ultimate reward, where the faithful will be treated with the utmost respect and will enjoy the finest amenities as a result of their righteousness and good deeds in this world.
orig: فيها سرر مرفوعة

translation: And cups put in place.
interpretation: This verse is referring to the cups of wine that will be readily available for the believers in Paradise. The cups are described as being "put in place", indicating that they are prepared and easily accessible for the believers to drink from and enjoy. This is a symbol of the luxury, comfort, and ease that the believers will experience in the afterlife as a reward for their faith and good deeds in this world.
orig: وأكواب موضوعة

translation: And we have made the sky a protected ceiling
interpretation: This verse refers to the protective nature of the Earth's atmosphere. The sky acts as a shield, protecting life on Earth from harmful radiation and meteors. It is a sign of Allah's power and mercy that He has created this "protected ceiling" to make life possible on our planet. The verse reminds us to be grateful for the many ways in which Allah has provided for us and made our existence possible through His creative power.
orig: ونمارق مصفوفة

translation: And [upon] carpets spread around.
interpretation: This verse is describing the luxurious and comfortable furnishings that will be provided in Paradise. The "carpets spread around" indicate that the inhabitants of Paradise will have access to the finest and most beautiful carpets and rugs, adding to the overall atmosphere of comfort and indulgence. This is a reward for the righteous who have lived their lives in accordance with God's teachings and have earned their place in Paradise.
orig: وزرابي مبثوثة

translation: Do they not look at the camels, how they are created?
interpretation: This verse invites people to reflect upon the creation of camels as a sign of God's power and wisdom. Camels are uniquely adapted to survive in harsh desert environments, with their ability to store water, withstand extreme temperatures, and carry heavy loads. Their creation testifies to the intricate design and purpose in God's creation. By pondering over the camels, one can appreciate the magnitude of God's creative power and be humbled by the realization that such a magnificent creature is but one of countless signs pointing to the existence and greatness of the Creator. This reflection should inspire faith, gratitude, and reverence for God Almighty.
orig: أفلا ينظرون إلى الإبل كيف خلقت

translation: And [look] at the sky, how it has been raised high
interpretation: This verse directs our attention to the sky and how it has been elevated without any visible pillars or support. It is an invitation to ponder upon the immense power and wisdom of Allah, who has created this vast and magnificent universe. The verse encourages us to reflect on the perfection and precision with which the sky has been constructed, and to appreciate the beauty and harmony that exists in Allah's creation. It also reminds us of our own insignificance in comparison to the grandeur of the universe, and humbles us before the might and majesty of our Creator.
orig: وإلى السماء كيف رفعت

translation: And at the mountains, how they are erected?
interpretation: This verse draws our attention to the majestic creation of mountains by Allah. Mountains are erected firmly and stand tall on the earth's surface, providing stability and balance to the earth's crust. They are a testament to Allah's immense power and wisdom in creating such massive structures that serve multiple purposes, such as being a source of water, habitat for various creatures, and a means of protection and shelter for humans. The verse invites us to reflect on the creation of mountains and appreciate the divine design behind their existence, which is a sign of Allah's greatness and mercy towards His creation.
orig: وإلى الجبال كيف نصبت

translation: And at the earth, how it has been spread out?
interpretation: This verse draws our attention to the earth and how it has been made flat and spread out, making it suitable for human habitation. It invites us to reflect upon the divine wisdom behind the creation of the earth in this manner, allowing for the growth of vegetation, the construction of dwellings, and the ease of travel. The verse reminds us of Allah's power, creativity, and benevolence in designing the earth to perfectly suit the needs of His creation, encouraging gratitude and mindfulness of His blessings in our daily lives.
orig: وإلى الأرض كيف سطحت

translation: So remind, [O Muhammad]; you are only a reminder.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the role of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) as a messenger and a reminder to the people. His duty is to convey the message of Islam and remind people of their obligations towards Allah. However, he is not responsible for forcing people to accept the message or for their ultimate fate. The verse implies that the Prophet's task is to deliver the message clearly and to the best of his ability, but the choice to accept or reject it lies with each individual. This highlights the concept of free will in Islam and the idea that each person is accountable for their own actions and decisions.
orig: فذكر إنما أنت مذكر

translation: You are not a controller over them.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and by extension, any person conveying the message of Islam, does not have control or authority over people's hearts and minds. The role of the Prophet and those who follow him is only to deliver the message of Islam clearly, but it is up to each individual to accept or reject that message based on their own free will. The verse highlights the Islamic principle that there is no compulsion in religion and that faith is a matter of personal conviction, not something that can be forced upon others.
orig: لست عليهم بمصيطر

translation: Except for those who turn away and disbelieve.
interpretation: This verse implies that those who deliberately turn away from the truth and reject faith in God will face consequences for their disbelief. It suggests that everyone will be held accountable for their choices and actions, and that turning away from God's message and denying His signs is a grave matter that will not be overlooked. The verse serves as a warning to those who knowingly refuse to believe, indicating that they are excluding themselves from God's mercy and guidance by their own choice.
orig: إلا من تولى وكفر

translation: Then Allah will punish him with the greatest punishment.
interpretation: This verse warns that those who reject faith and persist in wrongdoing will face the severest punishment from Allah in the Hereafter. The "greatest punishment" refers to the everlasting torment of Hell, which is the ultimate consequence for those who turn away from God's guidance and choose the path of disbelief and transgression. It emphasizes the gravity of denying faith and the justice of Allah in holding people accountable for their choices and actions in this life.
orig: فيعذبه الله العذاب الأكبر

translation: Indeed, to Us is their return,
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that all human beings will ultimately return to Allah (God) after their death. It serves as a reminder that we are accountable for our deeds in this world and will face the consequences in the Hereafter. The verse highlights the inevitability of the Day of Judgment and the importance of leading a righteous life in accordance with Allah's guidance. It encourages believers to be mindful of their actions and to strive for good deeds, knowing that they will be held responsible for them when they return to their Creator.
orig: إن إلينا إيابهم

translation: Then indeed, upon Us is their account.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah is ultimately responsible for judging and holding people accountable for their deeds. It is a reminder that no one can escape the reckoning on the Day of Judgment, and that Allah keeps precise records of all our actions. This should motivate believers to be conscious of Allah and strive to do good, knowing that they will have to answer for everything they do in this life. It also provides comfort to those who are wronged or oppressed, knowing that justice will ultimately prevail and the wrongdoers will be held to account by Allah.
orig: ثم إن علينا حسابهم

translation: By the dawn;
interpretation: This verse is an oath taken by Allah, swearing by the dawn. The dawn represents the beginning of a new day and the end of the night. It symbolizes the transition from darkness to light, both literally and metaphorically. The oath by the dawn emphasizes the importance and sacredness of the message that follows in the subsequent verses of the chapter. It also draws attention to the power and majesty of Allah, who brings about the dawn and the alternation of day and night, demonstrating His control over the universe.
orig: والفجر

translation: By the ten nights
interpretation: The "ten nights" mentioned in this verse are widely understood by scholars to refer to the first ten nights of the sacred Islamic month of Dhul-Hijjah. These nights are considered to be among the most blessed and virtuous periods of the year, with the 10th day being Eid al-Adha. Deeds done during this time, such as fasting, prayer, and charity, are believed to carry immense reward. The specific mention of these ten nights in the Qur'an highlights their special status and encourages believers to increase their devotion and good works during this sacred time.
orig: وليال عشر

translation: By the even and the odd,
interpretation: This verse is interpreted by many scholars as an oath by Allah swearing by various creations He has made, both in even and odd numbers. It signifies that everything in the universe, whether even or odd in number, bears witness to Allah's Oneness and His perfect wisdom in creation. It also alludes to the fact that Allah's creations are diverse and perfectly balanced, reflecting His power and divine attributes. The even and the odd could also symbolize the duality and contrast found in Allah's creations, such as night and day, male and female, highlighting the harmony and purposefulness in the universe He has fashioned.
orig: والشفع والوتر

translation: And by the night when it departs,
interpretation: This verse is referring to the night as it moves along and eventually comes to an end, giving way to the light of day. It is an oath that Allah is swearing by, emphasizing the certainty and importance of what follows. The departing of the night symbolizes change and transformation, reminding us that nothing in this world is permanent except Allah. It encourages reflection on the passing nature of time and the need to make the most of our limited time in this world by striving in Allah's cause and seeking His pleasure.
orig: والليل إذا يسر

translation: There is indeed in that an oath for those who possess understanding.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of reflecting upon the signs and wonders of Allah's creation. It suggests that those who possess wisdom, insight, and understanding will recognize the significance of the oaths mentioned in the preceding verses. They will comprehend that these oaths serve as powerful reminders of Allah's omnipotence and the truth of His message. The verse implies that individuals endowed with reason and discernment will be more likely to appreciate the profound meaning behind these oaths and, consequently, strengthen their faith and submission to Allah.
orig: هل في ذلك قسم لذي حجر

translation: Have you not considered how your Lord dealt with 'Aad -
interpretation: This verse is a reminder for mankind to reflect upon the fate of the people of 'Aad, an ancient civilization that was destroyed by Allah due to their arrogance and rejection of His message. It serves as a warning that no matter how powerful or advanced a nation may be, it is not immune to the consequences of turning away from God's guidance. The verse encourages introspection and learning from the lessons of history, emphasizing that ultimate power and authority belong to Allah alone.
orig: ألم تر كيف فعل ربك بعاد

translation: Iram of the pillars
interpretation: This verse is referring to the ancient city of Iram, which was known for its lofty pillars and grand architecture. The people of Iram were very powerful and wealthy, but they became arrogant and disobedient to Allah. As a result, Allah destroyed their city, making it a cautionary tale for those who become too proud and forget their Lord. The verse serves as a reminder that no matter how mighty or prosperous a civilization may be, it can still face destruction if it turns away from the path of righteousness and faith in Allah.
orig: إرم ذات العماد

translation: The like of which was not created in the lands.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the uniqueness and incomparability of God's creation. It suggests that whatever is being referred to, whether it is a specific creation or the entirety of God's creation, is unparalleled and unmatched in all the lands. This interpretation highlights the power, creativity, and mastery of God as the Creator, and encourages reflection on the wonders and marvels that He has brought into existence. It also implies that humans should recognize and appreciate the singular nature of God's handiwork, as there is nothing else like it in the world.
orig: التي لم يخلق مثلها في البلاد

translation: And [We destroyed] Thamud, who carved out the rocks in the valley.
interpretation: This verse refers to the people of Thamud, an ancient Arabian tribe who were known for their skill in carving dwellings out of solid rock in the valley where they lived. Despite their advanced abilities, they rejected the message of Allah's prophet Salih and were ultimately destroyed for their disobedience and arrogance. The verse serves as a reminder that even those with great power and skill are not above the judgment of Allah if they turn away from His guidance and persist in wrongdoing.
orig: وثمود الذين جابوا الصخر بالواد

translation: And Pharaoh, owner of the stakes
interpretation: This verse refers to the Pharaoh of Egypt during the time of Moses. The "stakes" mentioned are interpreted by many scholars to represent the Pharaoh's great power, influence, and the stability of his kingdom. It could also allude to the Pharaoh's use of stakes as a means of torture against those who opposed him, demonstrating his cruelty and oppression. The verse serves as a reminder of the Pharaoh's tyrannical rule and his ultimate fate as a punishment from Allah for his arrogance and disbelief.
orig: وفرعون ذي الأوتاد

translation: Those who tyrannized in the lands
interpretation: This verse refers to those who acted with oppression, injustice and transgression in their lands. They exceeded all bounds in disobedience to Allah and oppressed His servants. It is a warning and condemnation of tyrants and oppressors who abuse their power and spread corruption and evil in the earth, instead of acting with justice and righteousness as Allah commands. Such people will face severe punishment in the Hereafter for their misdeeds and crimes.
orig: الذين طغوا في البلاد

translation: And they made much corruption therein.
interpretation: This verse is referring to people who spread corruption and evil in the land, causing harm and destruction. It implies that they engaged in this behavior excessively and repeatedly. The verse is a condemnation of those who sow discord, engage in wrongdoing, and disrupt the peace and order of society. It serves as a warning against such actions and highlights the negative consequences of corruption on both an individual and societal level.
orig: فأكثروا فيها الفساد

translation: So your Lord poured upon them a scourge of punishment.
interpretation: This verse is a warning to those who reject God's message and persist in wrongdoing. It emphasizes that God has the power to inflict severe punishment on those who defy Him. The "scourge of punishment" represents the various forms of torment and affliction that God can send upon the disobedient, both in this world and in the Hereafter. It serves as a reminder that one cannot escape the consequences of their actions and that ultimately, everyone will be held accountable before God. The verse aims to instill fear and encourage repentance, urging people to mend their ways and submit to God's will before it is too late.
orig: فصب عليهم ربك سوط عذاب

translation: Indeed, your Lord is ever watchful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah is constantly watching over His creation, aware of their actions and intentions. It serves as a reminder to humans that they should be mindful of their deeds, as nothing escapes the attention of their Lord. The use of the word "al-Mirsad" (watchful) implies that Allah is not only observing but also actively monitoring and recording the actions of His servants, ready to hold them accountable for their choices. This verse encourages believers to maintain righteousness and refrain from wrongdoing, knowing that Allah is ever-vigilant and will ultimately judge them based on their deeds.
orig: إن ربك لبالمرصاد

translation: And as for man, when his Lord tries him and [thus] is generous to him and favors him, he says, "My Lord has honored me."
interpretation: This verse highlights the human tendency to attribute success and blessings to one's own abilities or worthiness, rather than recognizing them as gifts from Allah. It suggests that when people are tested with abundance and favor, they often become arrogant and self-centered, believing that they have earned or deserved such blessings through their own merits. This mindset reflects a lack of gratitude and humility, as it fails to acknowledge Allah's grace and mercy in bestowing these blessings upon them. The verse serves as a reminder for people to remain humble and grateful to Allah, even during times of prosperity and success.
orig: فأما الإنسان إذا ما ابتلاه ربه فأكرمه ونعمه فيقول ربي أكرمن

translation: But when He tries him and restricts his provision, he says, "My Lord has humiliated me."
interpretation: This verse is referring to the human tendency to attribute hardship and difficulty to God's will, as a form of humiliation or punishment. It suggests that when God tests an individual by limiting their sustenance or provision, they may feel that God has deliberately chosen to disgrace or humiliate them. This highlights the importance of maintaining faith and trust in God's wisdom and plan, even during times of adversity or hardship. It also serves as a reminder to be grateful for God's blessings and provisions, rather than feeling entitled to them or viewing their absence as a personal slight from God.
orig: وأما إذا ما ابتلاه فقدر عليه رزقه فيقول ربي أهانن

translation: No! But you do not honor the orphan.
interpretation: This verse is a strong rebuke to those who neglect their duty towards orphans. It emphasizes the importance of caring for and honoring orphans in society. Islam places great emphasis on the rights of orphans and the responsibility of the community to protect and provide for them. Neglecting this duty is seen as a serious moral failing. The verse implies that true piety and righteousness are not just about religious rituals, but also about how we treat the most vulnerable members of society, such as orphans. It is a call to show compassion, generosity, and kindness towards those who have lost their parents and are in need of support and care.
orig: كلا بل لا تكرمون اليتيم

translation: Nor do you urge one another to feed the poor.
interpretation: This verse is a reminder and admonition to the believers to be mindful of the less fortunate and to actively encourage and exhort one another to feed the poor and needy. It emphasizes the importance of social responsibility, compassion, and generosity in Islam. The Qur'an repeatedly stresses the significance of taking care of the underprivileged members of society and condemns those who neglect this duty. This verse suggests that it is not enough to merely feed the poor oneself, but one should also inspire and motivate others to do the same, fostering a culture of empathy and solidarity within the community.
orig: ولا تحاضون على طعام المسكين

translation: And you devour inheritance, devouring [it] altogether,
interpretation: This verse is criticizing those who greedily consume the wealth they inherit, without any regard for the rights of others who may be entitled to a share, such as orphans or the needy. It suggests that such people are driven by their own selfish desires and fail to uphold the principles of justice and fairness mandated in Islam when it comes to the distribution of inherited wealth. The emphatic language used ("devouring [it] altogether") underscores the severity and wrongness of this behavior from a Quranic perspective.
orig: وتأكلون التراث أكلا لما

translation: And you love wealth with immense love.
interpretation: This verse is a reminder that humans have a natural inclination to love and desire wealth to a great extent. It points to the materialistic tendencies within people that can sometimes overshadow their spiritual pursuits and moral obligations. The verse encourages reflection on one's relationship with worldly possessions and the importance of maintaining a balanced perspective, recognizing that wealth is a temporary blessing from God that should be used in moderation and for good purposes, rather than being the sole focus of one's life and desires.
orig: وتحبون المال حبا جما

translation: No! When the earth is leveled - pounded and crushed
interpretation: This verse is referring to the Day of Judgment, when the earth will be flattened and destroyed. It emphasizes the complete destruction and transformation of the world as we know it. The repetition of the word "dakka" (pounded, crushed) intensifies the description of the earth's devastating end. This verse serves as a reminder of the inevitable coming of the Day of Judgment and the need for humans to be mindful of their actions and to prepare for the Hereafter by leading righteous lives in accordance with Allah's guidance.
orig: كلا إذا دكت الأرض دكا دكا

translation: And your Lord comes with the angels, rank upon rank.
interpretation: This verse refers to the Day of Judgment when Allah will come to judge His creation, accompanied by the angels who will be lined up in rows. It signifies the grandeur, power, and authority of Allah on that momentous day. The angels' presence in ranks demonstrates their discipline, obedience, and readiness to carry out Allah's commands. This awe-inspiring scene emphasizes the gravity of the situation and the accountability that every soul will face before their Lord. It serves as a reminder for believers to prepare for that day by leading righteous lives and fulfilling their obligations to Allah.
orig: وجاء ربك والملك صفا صفا

translation: And on that Day Hell will be brought [face to face], on that Day man will remember, but what good to him will be the remembrance?
interpretation: This verse is a stark reminder of the consequences of our actions in this world. On the Day of Judgment, Hell will be brought before mankind, and they will realize the gravity of their mistakes and sins. However, at that point, it will be too late for regret or repentance. The remembrance of their wrongdoings will be of no benefit to them, as the time for seeking forgiveness and making amends has passed. This verse emphasizes the importance of being mindful of our actions and their consequences in this life, as we will be held accountable for them in the Hereafter. It is a call to live a righteous life and seek Allah's forgiveness while we still have the opportunity to do so.
orig: وجيء يومئذ بجهنم يومئذ يتذكر الإنسان وأنى له الذكرى

translation: He says, "Oh, I wish I had sent ahead [some good] for my life."
interpretation: This verse is a reminder of the regret that people will feel on the Day of Judgment when they realize that they did not do enough good deeds in their worldly life to prepare for the eternal life in the Hereafter. It emphasizes the importance of using our limited time in this world wisely by performing righteous actions and seeking Allah's pleasure, so that we may have a successful outcome on the Day of Reckoning. The verse also highlights the futility of worldly pursuits and attachments when faced with the reality of death and the Afterlife, urging us to prioritize our spiritual well-being over temporary gains.
orig: يقول يا ليتني قدمت لحياتي

translation: So on that Day, none will punish [as severely] as His punishment,
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the severity and uniqueness of Allah's punishment on the Day of Judgment. It suggests that no one can match the intensity of Allah's chastisement for those who have earned it through their actions and disbelief in this world. The verse serves as a warning to humanity that they should be mindful of their deeds and strive to follow the righteous path to avoid facing such an unparalleled punishment from the Almighty on the Day of Reckoning.
orig: فيومئذ لا يعذب عذابه أحد

translation: And no one can bind [as] His binding.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute power and sovereignty of Allah. It conveys that no one can restrict or limit Allah in any way, and no one can match His ability to control and decree matters in the universe. It highlights the idea that Allah's will and decisions are unbound by anyone or anything, and that He alone has the ultimate authority over all affairs. The verse serves as a reminder for believers to submit to Allah's will and trust in His wisdom, knowing that no force can override or constrain His divine decree.
orig: ولا يوثق وثاقه أحد

translation: O reassured soul,
interpretation: This verse is addressing the soul that has achieved a state of peace and tranquility through its unwavering faith, obedience and remembrance of Allah. It is the soul that is content with Allah's decree, finds serenity in His worship, and has successfully overcome the trials and temptations of worldly life. This "reassured soul" has earned Allah's pleasure and is now being invited to enter Paradise as a reward for its righteousness and perseverance. It signifies the highest spiritual rank a believer can attain.
orig: يا أيتها النفس المطمئنة

translation: Return to your Lord, well-pleased and pleasing [to Him]
interpretation: This verse is referring to the state of the righteous soul at the time of death. It is being called to return to its Lord, Allah, in a state of being pleased with Him and His decree, and also in a state that is pleasing to Him. This is because of the good deeds and obedience the soul has performed in its worldly life. The verse signifies the contentment, happiness and peace the righteous soul experiences when facing its Lord, knowing that it will be rewarded with Paradise for its faith and good deeds. It highlights the importance of living a life pleasing to Allah in preparation for the inevitable return to Him in the Hereafter.
orig: ارجعي إلى ربك راضية مرضية

translation: So enter among My [righteous] servants,
interpretation: This verse is an invitation from Allah to the righteous soul to enter Paradise and join the company of His righteous servants. It signifies that the soul has successfully passed the trials and tribulations of this worldly life and has earned the pleasure of Allah through its faith, good deeds, and obedience. The verse emphasizes the honor and blessing of being among the righteous servants of Allah in the eternal abode of Paradise, where they will enjoy everlasting peace, happiness, and nearness to their Lord. It is a reminder that the ultimate goal of a believer's life is to strive for righteousness and to be counted among the beloved servants of Allah in the Hereafter.
orig: فادخلي في عبادي

translation: And enter My Paradise.
interpretation: This verse is an invitation from Allah to the righteous believers to enter His Paradise as a reward for their good deeds and obedience. It signifies the ultimate success and eternal bliss that awaits those who have followed the path of righteousness and earned Allah's pleasure. The verse encourages believers to strive in this world to attain the everlasting joy and peace of Paradise in the Hereafter.
orig: وادخلي جنتي

translation: I swear by this city (Makkah).
interpretation: In this verse, Allah is taking an oath by the sacred city of Makkah, emphasizing its importance and sanctity. Makkah is a blessed city, chosen by Allah to be the site of His Holy House, the Ka'bah, and the birthplace of Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him). By swearing by Makkah, Allah is drawing attention to the significance of this city in the spiritual and historical context of Islam. The oath signifies that the message and events associated with Makkah, such as the revelation of the Qur'an and the prophethood of Muhammad (peace be upon him), are of utmost importance and truth.
orig: لا أقسم بهذا البلد

translation: And you are free of obligation in this city.
interpretation: This verse is addressing the Prophet Muhammad, telling him that he is not bound by any obligations or restrictions while in the sacred city of Mecca. It implies that he has the freedom to act as he sees fit, without being constrained by the customs or traditions of the people there. This could be seen as a divine sanction for the Prophet to carry out his mission of preaching Islam, even if it goes against the established norms of Meccan society at the time.
orig: وأنت حل بهذا البلد

translation: By the father and that which was born [of him],
interpretation: This verse is interpreted as an oath by Allah swearing by the father, generally understood to be referring to Adam (peace be upon him), and his offspring which includes all of humanity. It emphasizes the special status of Adam as the father of mankind and the progenitor of the human race. The verse also highlights the strong bond and connection between a father and his children, and the importance of recognizing and honoring one's parents and lineage.
orig: ووالد وما ولد

translation: We have certainly created man into hardship.
interpretation: This verse alludes to the fact that human life is filled with trials, tribulations, and difficulties. It suggests that struggle and hardship are an inherent part of the human condition, and that man must strive and persevere through these challenges. The verse can be seen as a reminder to be patient and steadfast in the face of adversity, and to recognize that hardships are a test from God. It also implies that through these struggles, man has the opportunity to grow spiritually and draw closer to God by remaining faithful and trusting in His plan.
orig: لقد خلقنا الإنسان في كبد

translation: Does he think that no one can overcome him?
interpretation: This verse is a rhetorical question that reminds us that no matter how powerful or capable a person may feel, they are ultimately not invincible and are subject to the will and power of Allah. It serves as a warning against arrogance and a reminder to remain humble, recognizing that all power and might belong to Allah alone. The verse implies that those who are deluded by their own power and abilities will face the consequences of their actions and will be held accountable by Allah.
orig: أيحسب أن لن يقدر عليه أحد

translation: Saying, "I have destroyed wealth in abundance,"
interpretation: This verse is referring to a disbeliever who boasts about the wealth he has spent in this worldly life, thinking that it will benefit him in the Hereafter. However, Allah is indicating that no matter how much wealth one spends in this life without faith and good deeds, it will be of no avail on the Day of Judgment. The phrase "destroyed wealth" suggests that he has wasted his wealth on things that will not bring him any good in the Hereafter. It is a reminder for believers to spend their wealth in the way of Allah and not to be attached to the temporary pleasures of this world.
orig: يقول أهلكت مالا لبدا

translation: Does he think that no one sees him?
interpretation: This verse is a rhetorical question that reminds us that Allah is always watching and aware of our actions, even if we think we are alone or that no one can see us. It is a warning against committing sins in secret, thinking that we can escape the sight of Allah. The verse emphasizes the concept of Ihsan, which is to worship Allah as if you see Him, and even though you cannot see Him, know that He sees you at all times. It encourages believers to be mindful of their actions and to strive for righteousness, knowing that Allah is constantly observing and will hold us accountable for our deeds.
orig: أيحسب أن لم يره أحد

translation: Have We not made for him two eyes?
interpretation: In this verse, Allah reminds human beings of the blessings He has bestowed upon them, particularly the gift of sight. The two eyes are mentioned as a representation of the various faculties and senses that Allah has granted humans to perceive and navigate the world around them. This verse encourages gratitude and reflection upon the countless bounties that Allah has provided, emphasizing the importance of using these gifts in a manner pleasing to Him. It also serves as a reminder that these blessings are not self-acquired but are bestowed by the mercy and grace of the Almighty Creator.
orig: ألم نجعل له عينين

translation: And a tongue and two lips.
interpretation: This verse reminds us of the blessings that Allah has bestowed upon us in the form of our ability to speak and communicate. The tongue and lips are essential for speech, which is a unique gift to mankind. It is through language that we can express our thoughts, feelings, and ideas, and connect with others. This verse encourages us to use our speech in a positive manner, to speak the truth, and to use our words to spread goodness and kindness in the world. We should be mindful of the power of our words and use them wisely, as we will be accountable for what we say on the Day of Judgment.
orig: ولسانا وشفتين

translation: And We have guided him to the two ways.
interpretation: This verse refers to the fact that Allah has given human beings the ability to distinguish between right and wrong, good and evil. He has shown them the path of righteousness and the path of sin, and has given them the free will to choose between the two. It is up to each individual to decide which path they will follow in life, but Allah has provided guidance through His revelations and prophets to help people make the right choice and attain success in this world and the Hereafter.
orig: وهديناه النجدين

translation: But he has not broken through the difficult pass.
interpretation: This verse is encouraging people to face and overcome the challenges and difficulties in life. The "difficult pass" is a metaphor for the obstacles and hardships that one encounters on the path to righteousness and success. The verse implies that most people do not have the courage or determination to confront and surmount these challenges. It is urging the believers to be among those who strive against the odds, stay true to their faith, and break through the barriers that stand between them and success in this world and the hereafter.
orig: فلا اقتحم العقبة

translation: And what can make you know what is [breaking through] the difficult pass?
interpretation: This verse is asking the reader a rhetorical question, challenging them to consider the significance and difficulty of the act that is about to be described in the following verses. It is a way of emphasizing the importance and gravity of "breaking through the difficult pass", which is explained in the subsequent verses as freeing a slave or feeding the needy during times of hardship. The verse serves to grab the attention of the reader and make them reflect deeply on the meaning and implications of these righteous deeds that require great sacrifice and effort, but ultimately lead to spiritual triumph and salvation.
orig: وما أدراك ما العقبة

translation: Free a slave
interpretation: This verse is encouraging the freeing of slaves as an act of piety and righteousness. In the context of the time when the Qur'an was revealed, slavery was a common practice. However, Islam encouraged the freeing of slaves and considered it a highly virtuous deed that could expiate sins and bring one closer to God. The verse is a concise but powerful call to end the practice of slavery and to grant freedom to those in bondage. It reflects the Qur'anic emphasis on human dignity, equality, and compassion for the oppressed.
orig: فك رقبة

translation: Or feeding on a day of severe hunger
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of feeding the hungry, especially on a day when hunger is severe and people are in dire need of food. It highlights the virtue of compassion, generosity, and caring for the less fortunate members of society. By mentioning "a day of severe hunger", the verse draws attention to times of hardship and crisis when the need for such acts of kindness is even more crucial. It encourages believers to be proactive in helping others and to prioritize the needs of the hungry and the destitute, even in the face of their own challenges and difficulties.
orig: أو إطعام في يوم ذي مسغبة

translation: An orphan near of kin
interpretation: This verse is emphasizing the importance of taking care of orphans, especially those who are related to us. In Islam, there is a strong emphasis on supporting and caring for the most vulnerable members of society, including orphans. The verse suggests that we have an even greater responsibility towards orphans who are our relatives, as the familial bond creates a stronger obligation to ensure their well-being. This can include providing for their basic needs, offering emotional support, and ensuring they receive a good education and upbringing. The verse serves as a reminder to Muslims to prioritize the care of orphans and to treat them with kindness, compassion, and generosity.
orig: يتيما ذا مقربة

translation: Or the indigent [down] in the dust.
interpretation: This verse is emphasizing the importance of helping and caring for those who are extremely poor and destitute, to the extent that they are in the dust or dirt due to their poverty and lack of means. It encourages Muslims to be charitable and compassionate towards those in dire need, recognizing their suffering and extending a helping hand to alleviate their hardship. The verse serves as a reminder of the social responsibility and the virtues of generosity and kindness towards the less fortunate members of society.
orig: أو مسكينا ذا متربة

translation: Then he was of those who believed and advised one another to patience and advised one another to compassion.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of faith, patience, and compassion. Those who have true faith are not only believers but also encourage and support each other in remaining steadfast during difficult times. They advise one another to be patient in the face of adversity and to show compassion and mercy towards others. This highlights the significance of building a strong, supportive community of believers who uplift and care for one another. The verse suggests that these qualities - faith, patience, and compassion - are interconnected and essential for spiritual growth and success in both this life and the hereafter.
orig: ثم كان من الذين آمنوا وتواصوا بالصبر وتواصوا بالمرحمة

translation: Those are the companions of the right.
interpretation: This verse is referring to the righteous believers who will be honored and blessed on the Day of Judgment. They are called "the companions of the right" because they will receive their records of deeds in their right hands, signifying their good deeds and righteousness. These individuals have followed the straight path, believed in Allah, and performed good deeds in their worldly lives. As a result, they will be granted the highest levels of Paradise and will be in the company of the prophets, the truthful, the martyrs, and the righteous. Their faces will be radiant with joy and happiness as they are welcomed into the eternal bliss of Paradise.
orig: أولئك أصحاب الميمنة

translation: But those who disbelieved in Our signs - they are the companions of the left.
interpretation: This verse refers to the fate of those who reject the signs and messages of Allah. "The companions of the left" is a reference to those who will be on the left side of Allah on the Day of Judgment, which is the side of the condemned and damned. It signifies that those who disbelieve and deny the truth of Allah's revelations will face a severe punishment in the Hereafter. They have chosen the path of misguidance and will suffer the consequences of their disbelief and rebellion against Allah.
orig: والذين كفروا بآياتنا هم أصحاب المشأمة

translation: Over them will be a Fire closed in
interpretation: This verse refers to the punishment that awaits the disbelievers in the Hereafter. The "Fire closed in" represents Hell, which will engulf them from all sides, leaving no escape or relief. It emphasizes the severity and inescapability of the punishment for those who reject faith in Allah and His messages. The verse serves as a warning to humanity about the consequences of disbelief and encourages them to embrace the path of righteousness to avoid this terrible fate.
orig: عليهم نار مؤصدة

translation: By the sun and its brightness
interpretation: This verse is an oath taken by Allah swearing by the sun and its brilliant light that illuminates the earth during the day. It draws attention to the magnificent creation of Allah and His power, reminding us to appreciate and reflect upon the wonders of the universe. The sun is a sign of Allah's mercy, as it provides warmth, energy, and sustenance for all living beings on earth. This oath serves as a prelude to the subsequent verses, which deliver a profound message or wisdom.
orig: والشمس وضحاها

translation: And by the moon as it follows it (the sun),
interpretation: This verse is referring to the moon and how it follows the sun in its orbit. It is a reminder of the perfect order and harmony in the universe, which is a sign of Allah's power and wisdom. The moon's phases and its consistent orbit are a testament to the precision and regularity of Allah's creation. This verse encourages us to reflect on the wonders of the universe and appreciate the magnificence of Allah's handiwork. It also serves as a reminder that just as the moon follows its ordained path, we too should strive to follow the path that Allah has set for us and fulfill our purpose in life.
orig: والقمر إذا تلاها

translation: By the day as it displays it [the sun]
interpretation: This verse is interpreted as an oath by Allah swearing by the day when it illuminates and reveals the beauty of the sun. It signifies the power and magnificence of the day, which is a sign of Allah's creation and a reminder of His omnipotence. The verse also alludes to the fact that the day is a time for work, activity, and the pursuit of one's goals, while the night is meant for rest and reflection. This serves as a reminder for humans to make the most of their time during the day and to be grateful for the blessings of light and clarity that Allah provides.
orig: والنهار إذا جلاها

translation: By the night when it covers her (the sun);
interpretation: This verse is interpreted as an oath by Allah swearing by the night when it envelops the day, covering the light of the sun. It signifies the power and vastness of Allah's creation, where the alternation of night and day is a sign of His wisdom and control over the universe. The night's ability to cover and conceal is seen as a metaphor for the mysteries and secrets that are hidden from human understanding, known only to Allah. It also serves as a reminder of the temporary nature of worldly life, as the night inevitably gives way to the day, just as life gives way to death and the Hereafter.
orig: والليل إذا يغشاها

translation: By the heaven and He Who built it
interpretation: This verse is an oath by Allah swearing by the sky and the One who has built it, i.e., Allah Himself. It draws our attention to the magnificence and perfection of the sky's creation as a sign of Allah's immense power and wisdom. The verse invites us to ponder upon the vastness, beauty and precise order of the heavenly bodies, which bear witness to the existence of the Creator and His attributes of perfection. It also reminds us that the One who has built this amazing sky is surely capable of creating the Hereafter and holding people accountable for their deeds.
orig: والسماء وما بناها

translation: By the Earth and He Who spread it
interpretation: This verse is an oath by Allah, swearing by the Earth and the One who spread it out, flattened it, and made it a suitable place for human beings to live and thrive upon. It draws attention to the power, wisdom and benevolence of the Creator in designing the Earth perfectly for life. The verse invites contemplation on the wonders of Allah's creation and should inspire gratitude and worship towards Him for providing humanity with a perfect abode.
orig: والأرض وما طحاها

translation: By the soul and He who proportioned it
interpretation: This verse is referring to the human soul and how Allah has created it in perfect proportion and balance. It suggests that the soul has been imbued with the innate ability to discern between right and wrong, and that it is up to each individual to nurture and develop their soul in accordance with Allah's guidance. The verse serves as a reminder of the immense responsibility that comes with having a soul, and the importance of striving to keep it pure and aligned with Allah's will. It also highlights the idea that the state of one's soul is ultimately a reflection of their choices and actions in this life.
orig: ونفس وما سواها

translation: And inspired it [with discernment of] its wickedness and its righteousness,
interpretation: This verse suggests that Allah has instilled within each human soul the innate ability to distinguish between right and wrong, good and evil. It implies that every individual has been granted a moral compass or conscience that guides them towards righteousness and away from wickedness. This divine inspiration serves as a fundamental basis for human moral responsibility and accountability. It emphasizes that humans have the free will to choose their actions but are also inherently aware of the moral implications of their choices. Ultimately, this verse highlights the importance of nurturing and following one's conscience in the pursuit of a virtuous life.
orig: فألهمها فجورها وتقواها

translation: He has succeeded who purifies it,
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of purifying one's soul. Those who engage in spiritual purification by doing good deeds, avoiding sins, and remembering Allah will attain success and happiness in this life and the Hereafter. It highlights that true success lies in the purification of the soul, not in worldly gains or materialistic pursuits. The verse encourages believers to focus on their inner spiritual growth and development.
orig: قد أفلح من زكاها

translation: But he has failed who instills it [with corruption].
interpretation: This verse warns that those who corrupt their souls with evil deeds and immorality will ultimately fail and be disappointed in the Hereafter. It emphasizes the importance of keeping one's soul pure and righteous, as succumbing to sinful temptations will lead to spiritual ruin and loss. The verse reminds believers to strive for virtue and guard against the destructive influences that can taint the soul, as the state of one's soul determines their ultimate fate and success or failure in the eyes of Allah.
orig: وقد خاب من دساها

translation: Thamud denied [their prophet] by reason of their transgression,
interpretation: This verse refers to the people of Thamud, an ancient Arabian tribe, who rejected the message and warnings of their prophet due to their arrogance, rebellion, and transgression against God's commands. It highlights how their insolence and defiance led them to deny the truth and persist in their wrongdoings, ultimately leading to their downfall and destruction. The verse serves as a reminder of the consequences of rejecting divine guidance and the importance of humility and obedience to God.
orig: كذبت ثمود بطغواها

translation: When the most wicked of them rose up
interpretation: This verse refers to the people of Thamud, who were a rebellious nation. The "most wicked" among them was a man who brutally hamstrung the she-camel sent by Allah as a sign to them. This action symbolized their utmost defiance and rejection of Allah's message and mercy, leading to their ultimate destruction. It serves as a warning against arrogance, cruelty, and disbelief, highlighting the severe consequences of opposing the will of Allah and harming His creation.
orig: إذ انبعث أشقاها

translation: So the Messenger of Allah said to them, "[It is] the she-camel of Allah and [bar her not from] her drink."
interpretation: This verse is a warning from the Prophet Muhammad to his people not to harm or prevent the she-camel, which was a sign sent by Allah, from drinking water. The interpretation is that one should not interfere with or cause harm to the signs and creatures sent by Allah. It emphasizes showing respect and reverence to what Allah has created or sent as a message. Preventing the she-camel from drinking can be seen as a metaphor for rejecting or opposing the signs of Allah, which would be a grave sin. The verse underscores submission and obedience to the will of Allah.
orig: فقال لهم رسول الله ناقة الله وسقياها

translation: But they denied him and hamstrung her. So their Lord brought down upon them destruction for their sin and made it equal [upon all of them].
interpretation: This verse is a warning to those who reject the messages of Allah's prophets and commit evil deeds. The people of Thamud, to whom the prophet Salih was sent, demanded that he show them a miracle as proof of his prophethood. Allah granted Salih's prayer and a she-camel emerged from a rock as a sign for them. However, instead of believing, they defiantly killed the she-camel. As a consequence of their sin and disbelief, Allah destroyed them all, leaving none alive. This highlights the severity of denying Allah's signs and disobeying His messengers. It also emphasizes Allah's justice in dealing with those who persist in wrongdoing - He punishes them equally, sparing none who were involved in the sin. The verse serves as a reminder for people to heed the warnings of prophets and refrain from transgressing the limits set by Allah.
orig: فكذبوه فعقروها فدمدم عليهم ربهم بذنبهم فسواها

translation: And he does not fear its consequence.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of doing what is right without fearing the consequences. It encourages believers to stand firm in their faith and convictions, even in the face of adversity or opposition. The verse implies that those who act righteously and follow God's path should have trust and reliance on Him, knowing that ultimately, the outcome of their actions is in His hands. It promotes courage, steadfastness, and the willingness to face challenges head-on for the sake of upholding one's beliefs and values.
orig: ولا يخاف عقباها

translation: By the night when it covers
interpretation: This verse is referring to the darkness of night that envelops everything. It could be interpreted as a metaphor for the trials and tribulations that can sometimes overshadow our lives, just as the night covers the day. However, just as the night eventually gives way to the light of dawn, our struggles and challenges will also pass. The verse reminds us to have faith and persevere through difficult times, knowing that relief and light will come, just as surely as the sun rises after the darkness of night. It is a message of hope and resilience in the face of adversity.
orig: والليل إذا يغشى

translation: And by the day when it shines forth
interpretation: This verse is referring to the brightness and clarity of the day when the sun rises and illuminates the earth. It is a reminder of Allah's power and ability to bring light and life to the world after the darkness of the night. The verse encourages reflection on the cyclical nature of day and night, and how it is a sign of Allah's perfect creation and control over the universe. It also serves as a call to make the most of the daylight hours and use them productively in the worship and remembrance of Allah.
orig: والنهار إذا تجلى

translation: And by the creation of the male and the female
interpretation: This verse is referring to the divine creation of human beings in two complementary genders, male and female. It points to the profound wisdom and purpose behind Allah's creation of humans as two distinct yet complementary halves.
