The verse invites reflection on the beauty and balance in Allah's design, and how the two genders are meant to complete each other and fulfill their roles in life according to the divine plan. It also alludes to the procreative function of the two sexes in producing offspring and maintaining the continuity of human life on earth.
orig: وما خلق الذكر والأنثى

translation: Indeed, your efforts are diverse.
interpretation: This verse highlights the fact that people strive for different goals and purposes in life. Some may seek worldly gains, while others pursue spiritual enlightenment or the pleasure of Allah. It reminds us that the efforts and intentions of individuals vary greatly, and ultimately, it is the sincerity and righteousness of one's actions that matter in the sight of Allah. The verse encourages introspection and self-reflection, urging believers to examine their own intentions and strive for what is most pleasing to Allah.
orig: إن سعيكم لشتى

translation: So as for he who gives and fears Allah
interpretation: This verse is referring to the righteous person who gives in charity and is mindful of Allah in all his actions. Such a person spends from his wealth in the way of Allah, seeking His pleasure and fearing His punishment. He is conscious of his duty to Allah and strives to obey Him and refrain from what He has prohibited. This verse highlights the importance of sincere generosity coupled with piety and righteousness. Those who possess these qualities will be among the successful ones in the Hereafter.
orig: فأما من أعطى واتقى

translation: And believed in the best [reward]
interpretation: This verse refers to those who have faith in Allah's promise of the best reward in the Hereafter for those who believe and do righteous deeds. They trust in the "husna" (the best) that Allah has promised them, which includes Paradise and His pleasure. Believing in this promise motivates them to strive for good in this world, knowing that their ultimate goal is the eternal reward of the Hereafter. It reflects the optimism and hopefulness of the believers who are certain that their faith and good deeds will be recompensed with the very best outcome by Allah's grace and mercy.
orig: وصدق بالحسنى

translation: Then We will make it easy for him towards ease.
interpretation: This verse refers to the concept of divine guidance and facilitation. It indicates that Allah will make the path of goodness, righteousness, and obedience easy for those who sincerely seek His pleasure and strive to follow His commands. It is a promise of Allah's support and assistance to the believers, assuring them that if they have the right intention and put in the effort, Allah will help them overcome the challenges and obstacles in their journey towards spiritual purification and success in this world and the Hereafter. This verse encourages the believers to remain steadfast on the path of faith and righteousness, as Allah's help and guidance will always be with them.
orig: فسنيسره لليسرى

translation: But as for he who withheld and considered himself free of need
interpretation: This verse is referring to those who are miserly and refuse to spend their wealth in the way of Allah, thinking that they are self-sufficient and do not need to rely on Him. Such people are deluded by their arrogance and fail to recognize that all blessings come from Allah alone. Their stinginess and ingratitude will lead them astray from the righteous path. The verse serves as a warning against the dangers of greed and self-conceit, urging believers to be generous and humble before their Lord.
orig: وأما من بخل واستغنى

translation: And he denied the best [reward]
interpretation: This verse is referring to those who reject the concept of Paradise and the rewards that Allah has promised for the righteous believers in the Hereafter. They deny the "best" (al-husna), which is the ultimate good - the blissful abode of Paradise that Allah has prepared for His devout servants. Denying this promise stems from a lack of faith and disbelief in the Divine message and revelations. The verse serves as a warning against such rejection and highlights the grave consequences of denying the truth of the Hereafter and the recompense that awaits therein based on one's deeds in this worldly life.
orig: وكذب بالحسنى

translation: We shall ease him to the Difficult Way.
interpretation: This verse warns that those who reject faith and choose evil will find that Allah will make it easy for them to continue in their wayward path that leads to hardship and suffering in this world and the next. It emphasizes that Allah does not compel anyone to believe, but allows people to make their own choices. However, those bad choices will be made easier for them by Allah, ultimately sealing their fate in difficulty and punishment if they don't turn back to the straight path. It's a severe warning against taking the path of disbelief and sin.
orig: فسنيسره للعسرى

translation: And what will his wealth avail him when he goes down (in destruction).
interpretation: This verse is a reminder that worldly possessions and wealth are ultimately of no benefit when a person faces the consequences of their actions in the Hereafter. It emphasizes that on the Day of Judgment, when a person "goes down" or falls into the depths of Hell as a result of their sins and disbelief, their material wealth will be of no use to them. It highlights the temporary nature of worldly riches and the importance of focusing on one's spiritual well-being and good deeds, which are the only things that will truly benefit a person in the afterlife.
orig: وما يغني عنه ماله إذا تردى

translation: Indeed, upon Us is guidance.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that it is Allah's responsibility to guide humanity to the right path. He has taken it upon Himself to provide guidance through His revelations and messengers. It is a reassurance that Allah will not leave mankind without direction and that He will always provide the means for people to find the truth and follow the straight path. However, it is up to individuals to seek out and accept this guidance, as Allah does not force faith upon anyone. The verse also implies that since guidance comes from Allah, one should turn to Him and His revelations for answers and direction in life, rather than relying solely on human wisdom or desires.
orig: إن علينا للهدى

translation: And indeed, to Us belongs the Hereafter and the first [life].
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that both this worldly life and the Hereafter belong to Allah. It reminds us that Allah is the ultimate owner and controller of all things, and that our actions in this life will have consequences in the Hereafter. The verse encourages believers to prioritize the Hereafter over the temporary pleasures of this world, as the Hereafter is eternal and more significant in the grand scheme of things. It also implies that since Allah is the owner of both worlds, He has the power to reward or punish people in the Hereafter based on their deeds in this life.
orig: وإن لنا للآخرة والأولى

translation: So I have warned you of a Fire which is blazing.
interpretation: This verse serves as a powerful warning to humanity about the consequences of rejecting faith and indulging in sin. The "blazing Fire" refers to the torments of Hell that await those who turn away from God's guidance. The verse emphasizes the Prophet's role as a warner, conveying the urgent message that people must mend their ways and submit to God before it is too late. It is a reminder that the choices we make in this life have eternal ramifications, and that we must strive to live righteously to avoid the agonizing punishment of the Hereafter.
orig: فأنذرتكم نارا تلظى

translation: None will burn therein except the most wretched one.
interpretation: This verse refers to the Hellfire, indicating that only the most wretched and miserable individuals will enter it. These are the people who have persistently denied the truth, rejected faith, and committed grave sins without seeking repentance. The "most wretched" are those who have strayed far from God's path and have not heeded the warnings and guidance sent through His messengers. They have chosen to follow their own desires and have been ungrateful for the blessings bestowed upon them. As a result, they will face the severe consequences of their actions in the Hereafter, burning in the Hellfire as a punishment for their transgressions and disbelief.
orig: لا يصلاها إلا الأشقى

translation: Who denied and turned away
interpretation: This verse refers to those who reject the truth of the message brought by the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and turn away from it. They deny the existence of Allah, the prophethood of Muhammad, and the Day of Judgment. Instead of accepting the guidance, they arrogantly turn their backs on it, preferring to follow their own desires and inclinations. This attitude of denial and aversion to the truth is strongly condemned in the Qur'an, as it leads to misguidance and ultimately to perdition in the Hereafter.
orig: الذي كذب وتولى

translation: And the most righteous will be spared from it
interpretation: This verse refers to the righteous believers who will be saved from the Hellfire on the Day of Judgment due to their piety and good deeds. It emphasizes that those who are most conscious of Allah and strive to obey Him will be protected from the punishment of the Hereafter. The verse encourages Muslims to live a life of righteousness and to constantly seek Allah's pleasure through their actions, as this will ultimately lead to their salvation in the next life.
orig: وسيجنبها الأتقى

translation: The one who gives his wealth to purify himself
interpretation: This verse refers to those who spend their wealth in charity and good deeds, seeking to purify their souls and attain righteousness. It highlights the importance of using one's financial resources to help others and support noble causes, as a means of spiritual purification and growth. The act of giving is seen as a way to cleanse oneself from greed, selfishness, and attachment to worldly possessions, while also earning the pleasure and blessings of Allah. The verse emphasizes that true piety and righteousness are not merely about performing rituals or making verbal declarations of faith, but also about translating one's beliefs into practical actions that benefit society and reflect the values of compassion, generosity, and social responsibility.
orig: الذي يؤتي ماله يتزكى

translation: And no one has with him any favor to be rewarded
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that no person has any favor or blessing from Allah that needs to be compensated or rewarded. It highlights the fact that all blessings and bounties are from Allah alone, and He bestows them upon His creation without expecting anything in return. It serves as a reminder for humans to be grateful to Allah for His countless blessings and to recognize that they are not doing Him any favor by worshipping Him or doing good deeds, but rather it is their duty and obligation towards their Creator.
orig: وما لأحد عنده من نعمة تجزى

translation: But only seeking the countenance of his Lord, Most High.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the righteous actions and good deeds of a believer should be done solely for the sake of seeking the pleasure and approval of Allah, the Most High. It highlights the importance of having pure intentions and sincerity in one's worship and actions, rather than being motivated by worldly gains, fame, or recognition. The ultimate goal of a true believer should be to attain the love and satisfaction of Allah, as that is the highest achievement one can aspire for in this life and the Hereafter.
orig: إلا ابتغاء وجه ربه الأعلى

translation: And He will [certainly] be satisfied.
interpretation: This verse refers to the ultimate satisfaction and pleasure that Allah will have with His faithful servants in the Hereafter. It implies that those who strive to please Allah in this worldly life through their faith, good deeds, and obedience will be rewarded with Allah's approval, love, and blessings in the eternal life to come. This divine satisfaction is the highest aspiration and the most significant achievement for a believer, as it signifies the fulfillment of their purpose and the attainment of ultimate success and happiness.
orig: ولسوف يرضى

translation: By the morning brightness
interpretation: This verse is an oath by Allah swearing by the brightness of the morning, emphasizing the importance and sacredness of this time of day. It signifies the light and guidance that comes with the morning, dispelling the darkness of night. The morning brightness symbolizes hope, renewal, and the blessings that Allah bestows upon His creation at the start of each day. This oath serves as a reminder for humans to be grateful for the gift of a new day and to make the most of the opportunities it brings.
orig: والضحى

translation: By the night when it covers with darkness,
interpretation: This verse is an oath taken by Allah swearing by the night when it envelops the world in darkness. It emphasizes the power and vastness of the night, which can be seen as a symbol of the mysteries and unknowns in life. The darkness of the night can also represent the challenges and difficulties that one may face in their journey. However, just as the night eventually gives way to the light of dawn, these challenges can be overcome with faith, perseverance, and the guidance of Allah. The verse serves as a reminder of Allah's power over all things and the temporary nature of the hardships we face in this world.
orig: والليل إذا سجى

translation: Your Lord has not forsaken you, nor has He become displeased.
interpretation: This verse is a reassurance from Allah to Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) that He has not abandoned him or forsaken him, despite the challenges and difficulties he faced in conveying the message of Islam. It emphasizes that Allah's support, guidance, and love for the Prophet remain constant, even during times of hardship or when it may seem that divine help is delayed. This verse serves as a reminder to the believers that Allah's plan is always unfolding, and one should never lose faith or feel despair, as Allah's mercy and support are ever-present.
orig: ما ودعك ربك وما قلى

translation: And the Hereafter is better for you than the first [life].
interpretation: This verse is a reminder that the life of the Hereafter is far superior and more rewarding than the temporary life of this world. It encourages the believer to focus on the eternal rewards of the afterlife rather than being consumed by the fleeting pleasures and distractions of this worldly existence. The verse implies that the efforts and sacrifices made in this life for the sake of Allah will be richly compensated in the Hereafter, making it a much better and more desirable destination for the believer. It is a call to prioritize one's spiritual well-being over worldly gains and to strive for success in the life to come.
orig: وللآخرة خير لك من الأولى

translation: And your Lord is going to give you, and you will be satisfied.
interpretation: This verse is a promise from Allah to Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) that He will grant him abundant blessings and favors, both in this world and in the Hereafter, to the extent that the Prophet will be completely satisfied and content. It signifies the special status of Prophet Muhammad and the immense rewards he will receive for his steadfastness, devotion, and service to Allah. The verse also serves as a reminder to all believers that Allah's rewards and blessings are immeasurable and that true satisfaction and contentment lie in seeking His pleasure and grace.
orig: ولسوف يعطيك ربك فترضى

translation: Did He not find you an orphan and give [you] refuge?
interpretation: This verse is a reminder of God's favor upon the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him). It highlights that God took care of him and protected him when he was a vulnerable orphan child with no parents to look after him. The verse emphasizes God's compassion and mercy towards the Prophet, providing him with shelter, support, and guidance during his time of need. It serves as a lesson for all believers to recognize God's blessings and favors in their own lives, especially during times of hardship and vulnerability.
orig: ألم يجدك يتيما فآوى

translation: And He found you lost and guided [you]
interpretation: This verse is referring to the spiritual guidance that Allah provided to Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him). Before receiving divine revelation, the Prophet was searching for the truth and purpose of life. He felt lost in the midst of the moral decay and polytheistic practices of his society. However, Allah chose him as His final messenger and guided him to the straight path of Islam. Through revelation of the Qur'an and his own wisdom, Allah removed the Prophet from a state of being "lost" to being guided, enlightened and commissioned with the task of spreading the message of Islam. This verse is a reminder to all of us that if we sincerely seek Allah's guidance, He will lead us out of darkness and unto the light of faith and righteousness.
orig: ووجدك ضالا فهدى

translation: And He found you poor and made [you] self-sufficient.
interpretation: This verse refers to the blessings and favors that Allah bestowed upon Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him). Allah found him in a state of poverty and need, but He enriched him both materially and spiritually. This enrichment could refer to the contentment, peace of mind, and spiritual wealth that Allah granted him, as well as the material provisions and support from his companions and followers. It signifies that Allah uplifts those who are in need and blesses them with sufficiency and abundance, both in this world and the hereafter, when they turn to Him with faith and sincerity.
orig: ووجدك عائلا فأغنى

translation: Therefore, as for the orphan, do not oppress [him].
interpretation: This verse is a commandment from Allah to treat orphans with kindness and respect. It emphasizes the importance of showing compassion and care towards those who have lost their parents and are vulnerable in society. The verse warns against oppressing or mistreating orphans in any way, as this is a grave sin in Islam. Instead, Muslims are encouraged to protect the rights of orphans, provide for their needs, and ensure their well-being. This verse highlights the Islamic principle of social justice and the duty of believers to support and uplift the disadvantaged members of their community.
orig: فأما اليتيم فلا تقهر

translation: And as for the petitioner, do not repel [him].
interpretation: This verse is a reminder to treat those who come to us asking for help with kindness and respect. It teaches us not to turn away or rebuke someone in need, even if we are unable to assist them. Instead, we should respond with gentleness and compassion, acknowledging their situation and offering support or directing them to resources if possible. This verse emphasizes the importance of empathy, generosity, and good character in our interactions with others, especially those who are vulnerable or in difficulty.
orig: وأما السائل فلا تنهر

translation: And as for the favor of your Lord, report [it].
interpretation: This verse is a reminder to be grateful for the blessings and favors that Allah has bestowed upon us. It encourages us to acknowledge and speak about the good things in our lives, which are ultimately from Allah. By expressing gratitude and sharing the blessings we have received, we not only show our appreciation to Allah but also inspire others to recognize the favors they have been granted. This verse emphasizes the importance of gratitude and the need to openly express it, as it helps us maintain a positive perspective and strengthens our connection with our Lord.
orig: وأما بنعمة ربك فحدث

translation: Have We not expanded for you your breast?
interpretation: This verse is referring to the spiritual and emotional comfort and strength that Allah granted to Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him). The "expansion of the breast" symbolizes the inner peace, tranquility, and courage that Allah bestowed upon him, enabling him to face the challenges and hardships of conveying the message of Islam. It signifies the divine support and guidance that the Prophet received throughout his mission, providing him with the resilience and determination to fulfill his role as the final messenger of Allah to humanity.
orig: ألم نشرح لك صدرك

translation: And We have removed from you your burden
interpretation: This verse is referring to the lifting of the Prophet Muhammad's (peace be upon him) burdens and difficulties. It signifies that Allah has relieved him of the heavy responsibilities and challenges that came with his mission of spreading the message of Islam. The "burden" can be interpreted as the weight of prophethood, the opposition and persecution he faced, and the personal struggles he endured. By removing this burden, Allah is reassuring the Prophet that He is supporting him, making his task easier, and granting him relief and comfort both spiritually and emotionally. It is a sign of Allah's favor, mercy and care for His chosen Messenger.
orig: ووضعنا عنك وزرك

translation: Which made your back stoop
interpretation: This verse is likely referring to the heavy burden and responsibility that was placed upon the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) in conveying the message of Islam. The "stooping of the back" is a metaphor for the weight and difficulty of this task. It suggests that the challenges and opposition the Prophet faced in spreading the message weighed heavily upon him, like a physical load that bows one down. However, it can also be understood as Allah acknowledging and empathizing with the Prophet's struggles, and in the following verses, Allah reminds that He has elevated the Prophet's renown and will support him, so he need not be burdened or discouraged by the difficulty of his mission.
orig: الذي أنقض ظهرك

translation: And raised high for you your repute.
interpretation: This verse is a reminder of the great honor and status that Allah has bestowed upon Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him). Allah has elevated the Prophet's mention and made his name and message known throughout the world. This is a sign of the Prophet's high rank and the importance of his mission. It also serves as a source of comfort and reassurance for the Prophet, knowing that Allah is supporting him and will continue to spread his message far and wide. The verse encourages believers to follow the Prophet's example and strive to earn Allah's pleasure and recognition.
orig: ورفعنا لك ذكرك

translation: For indeed, with hardship [will be] ease.
interpretation: This verse conveys a message of hope and optimism, reminding believers that even in the face of difficulties and challenges, there is always the promise of relief and ease. It encourages perseverance and trust in God's plan, knowing that after every hardship, there will be a period of comfort and ease. This verse serves as a reassurance to those facing trials, urging them to remain steadfast in their faith and to have patience, for God's help and mercy are always near. It emphasizes the cyclical nature of life, where hardships and ease alternate, and it is through these experiences that one grows and develops spiritually.
orig: فإن مع العسر يسرا

translation: Indeed, with hardship [will be] ease.
interpretation: This verse conveys a message of hope and optimism, assuring believers that after every difficulty or hardship they face, there will be relief and ease. It encourages perseverance and trust in God's plan, knowing that challenging times are temporary and will eventually give way to better circumstances. This verse serves as a reminder to remain patient and steadfast during trials, as God promises to support and guide those who have faith in Him.
orig: إن مع العسر يسرا

translation: So when you have finished [your duties], then stand up [for worship].
interpretation: This verse is encouraging the believer to turn to Allah in worship and supplication after completing their worldly duties and obligations. It reminds us that after we have finished our daily tasks and responsibilities, we should not neglect our spiritual connection with Allah. Instead, we should "stand up" for worship, meaning to devote ourselves wholeheartedly to prayer, remembrance of Allah, and other acts of worship. This verse emphasizes the importance of maintaining a balance between our worldly commitments and our religious devotion, and encourages us to prioritize our relationship with Allah even amidst the busyness of life.
orig: فإذا فرغت فانصب

translation: And to your Lord direct [your] longing.
interpretation: This verse encourages the believer to turn to Allah with all their desires, hopes, and aspirations. It emphasizes that true contentment and fulfillment can only be found by seeking the pleasure of Allah and striving to draw closer to Him. The verse reminds us to make Allah the ultimate focus and goal of our lives, dedicating our actions and intentions solely for His sake. By directing our longing towards Allah, we can find inner peace, guidance, and purpose in both this life and the hereafter.
orig: وإلى ربك فارغب

translation: By the fig and the olive
interpretation: In this verse, Allah swears by the fig and the olive, which are both beneficial fruits that grow in the lands around Jerusalem and the Mediterranean. The fig and olive represent the lands where many prophets were sent, such as Jesus and Muhammad (peace be upon them). By swearing by these fruits, Allah emphasizes the importance and sacredness of these regions where divine revelation was sent down to guide humanity. It also symbolizes the blessings and bounties that Allah has bestowed upon mankind through the sustenance and nourishment provided by these fruits.
orig: والتين والزيتون

translation: And [by] Mount Sinai
interpretation: In this verse, Allah swears by Mount Sinai, the sacred place where Prophet Moses (peace be upon him) received divine revelation and the Ten Commandments. The mention of Mount Sinai is significant as it symbolizes the importance and sanctity of the location where Allah directly communicated with one of His chosen prophets. By swearing by Mount Sinai, Allah emphasizes the truthfulness and gravity of the message that follows, as well as the honor and status bestowed upon Prophet Moses and the revelation he received at this holy site.
orig: وطور سينين

translation: And by this city of security [Makkah]
interpretation: In this verse, Allah swears by the sacred city of Makkah, emphasizing its status as a place of safety and security. This oath highlights the importance and sanctity of Makkah, which is protected by divine decree. The verse serves as a reminder to the believers of the special status of this holy city and the blessings it holds for those who enter it with faith and sincerity. It also implies that the people of Makkah have a responsibility to maintain the sanctity and security of the city, as it is a trust from Allah.
orig: وهذا البلد الأمين

translation: We have certainly created man in the best of stature;
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the special status and honor that God has bestowed upon human beings. God has created humans in the best physical and mental form, endowing them with reason, intellect, and the capacity for moral choices. This interpretation highlights the inherent dignity of all human beings, regardless of their race, ethnicity, or social status. It also implies that humans have a responsibility to live up to this honored status, to use their God-given faculties for good, and to refrain from actions that would debase or disgrace themselves. The "best of stature" includes not just the physical form, but also the spiritual and moral potential that humans possess. This verse is often seen as a reminder for humility and gratitude for the gifts bestowed by God, as well as a call to fulfill the trust placed in humankind as God's stewards on Earth.
orig: لقد خلقنا الإنسان في أحسن تقويم

translation: Then We return him to the lowest of the low.
interpretation: This verse refers to the spiritual decline of those who reject faith and choose to follow their base desires. Despite being created in the best of forms and given the potential for greatness, those who turn away from God's guidance are ultimately reduced to the lowest depths of degradation and despair. It serves as a warning that without faith and righteousness, humans can sink to the level of the lowest creatures, losing their dignity and purpose in life. The verse emphasizes the importance of staying on the right path and the consequences of straying from it.
orig: ثم رددناه أسفل سافلين

translation: Except for those who believe and do righteous deeds, for they will have a reward uninterrupted.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that those who have true faith and back it up with good deeds and righteous actions will be granted an everlasting reward from Allah in the Hereafter. Their reward will be unending and undiminished, unlike the fleeting pleasures of this worldly life. It motivates the believers to persevere in faith and good works, knowing that their ultimate recompense with their Lord will be far greater than anything in this temporary world. The verse also implies that mere belief is not sufficient - it must be coupled with righteous conduct and obedience to Allah's commands to attain His pleasure and the promised reward in the eternal life to come.
orig: إلا الذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات فلهم أجر غير ممنون

translation: Then what can make you deny the Recompense?
interpretation: This verse is a rhetorical question that challenges the disbelievers who deny the Day of Judgment. It implies that after witnessing all the signs and evidence of Allah's power and creation in this world, it is unreasonable for anyone to doubt or reject the concept of the Hereafter, where people will be held accountable for their deeds and recompensed accordingly. The verse serves as a reminder and warning to humanity that the Day of Judgment is inevitable, and that one should prepare for it by living a righteous life and fulfilling their obligations towards Allah and His creation.
orig: فما يكذبك بعد بالدين

translation: Is not Allah the most just of judges?
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the supreme wisdom and justice of Allah in His judgments and decisions. It reminds us that no one can be a better judge than Allah, as He is the Most Wise and the Most Just. This verse encourages believers to trust in Allah's judgments, even if they may not always understand the reasons behind them, because Allah's wisdom and justice are perfect and unquestionable. It also serves as a warning to those who might question or doubt Allah's decisions, reminding them that Allah is the ultimate authority and that His judgments are always fair and just.
orig: أليس الله بأحكم الحاكمين

translation: Read in the name of your Lord who created -
interpretation: This verse is encouraging the believer to seek knowledge and read in the name of Allah, acknowledging that He is the one who has created everything. It emphasizes the importance of education and learning, with the implication that all knowledge comes from Allah. The verse also suggests that one should approach learning and seeking knowledge with humility and reverence for the Creator.
orig: اقرأ باسم ربك الذي خلق

translation: He created man from a clinging substance.
interpretation: This verse is referring to the origin and creation of human beings. The Arabic word "alaq" is often translated as a clinging substance or a blood clot. It signifies the earliest stages of the development of the human embryo, when it is attached to the wall of the uterus. This verse emphasizes the humble and fragile beginnings of human life, reminding us of our origin and the miraculous nature of our creation by Allah. It also highlights the power and knowledge of Allah in creating human beings from such a small and seemingly insignificant substance, guiding its development into a fully formed human being.
orig: خلق الإنسان من علق

translation: Read! And your Lord is the Most Generous.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of seeking knowledge and education. It encourages the believer to read and learn, as it is through knowledge that one can come closer to understanding the greatness and generosity of Allah. The verse also highlights the attribute of Allah's generosity, implying that He bestows knowledge and understanding upon those who seek it sincerely. It serves as a reminder that the pursuit of knowledge is a noble endeavor that is highly valued in Islam, and that Allah rewards those who strive to learn and grow in their understanding of His creation and message.
orig: اقرأ وربك الأكرم

translation: Who taught by the pen
interpretation: This verse refers to Allah, who has taught mankind the use of the pen. It signifies that Allah is the source of all knowledge and has bestowed upon humans the ability to learn, write, and transmit knowledge across generations. The pen symbolizes the importance of literacy, education, and the preservation of knowledge in Islam. It also emphasizes that seeking knowledge is a fundamental duty of every Muslim, as it enables them to better understand and appreciate the wisdom and guidance provided by Allah in the Qur'an and through His prophets.
orig: الذي علم بالقلم

translation: Taught man that which he knew not.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of knowledge and education in Islam. It reminds us that all knowledge ultimately comes from Allah, who has taught human beings what they previously did not know. This can refer to the knowledge and guidance provided in the Qur'an and through the teachings of the Prophets, as well as the innate capacity for learning and discovery that Allah has bestowed upon the human intellect. The verse encourages humans to continually seek knowledge, both religious and worldly, with the understanding that it is a gift and a trust from Allah to be used for good. It also implies that humans should remain humble, recognizing that their knowledge is limited and there is always more to learn from the infinite wisdom of the Creator.
orig: علم الإنسان ما لم يعلم

translation: No! [But] indeed, man transgresses
interpretation: This verse is a warning against the human tendency towards arrogance and transgression. When humans are blessed with wealth, power, or success, they often become prideful and forget their humble origins and their ultimate reliance on Allah. They may begin to believe that they are self-sufficient and no longer need to submit to Allah's will. This verse reminds us that such an attitude is a form of transgression against Allah's boundaries and that we must always strive to remain humble and grateful for His blessings, no matter our station in life. It is a call to resist the temptation of arrogance and to maintain our connection with Allah through obedience and submission to His commands.
orig: كلا إن الإنسان ليطغى

translation: That he considered himself self-sufficient.
interpretation: This verse is criticizing those who, due to their wealth or status, become arrogant and see themselves as not needing God or His guidance. It highlights the danger of self-sufficiency leading to a rejection of divine guidance and a lack of gratitude towards one's Creator. The Qur'an emphasizes that true contentment and success lies in humility, recognition of God's favors, and following the path laid out by Him, rather than in pride and self-reliance.
orig: أن رآه استغنى

translation: Indeed, to your Lord is the return.
interpretation: This verse reminds us that our ultimate destination is back to Allah. No matter what we do in this life, we will eventually return to our Creator to face the consequences of our actions. It is a call to be mindful of our deeds and to strive for righteousness, knowing that we will be held accountable for everything we do. This verse encourages us to live our lives with the awareness that this world is temporary, and that our true home is in the hereafter with our Lord.
orig: إن إلى ربك الرجعى

translation: Have you seen the one who forbids
interpretation: This verse is criticizing those who prevent others from worshipping Allah or following the teachings of Islam. It suggests that such people are arrogant and presumptuous to think they have the authority to forbid others from obeying God. The rhetorical question "Have you seen..." is meant to call attention to the audacity and wrongness of trying to stand between people and the worship of their Lord. It reminds us that no human being has the right to interfere in the relationship between an individual and Allah.
orig: أرأيت الذي ينهى

translation: A slave when he prays
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance and virtue of prayer, especially for a slave or servant of Allah. It suggests that when a person humbles himself before Allah in prayer, sincerely submitting to Him and seeking His pleasure, he attains a noble status and becomes beloved to Allah. Prayer is a means of purification, spiritual elevation, and drawing closer to the Almighty. It also highlights the equality of all humans before Allah, as even a slave can attain a high rank through sincere devotion and prayer.
orig: عبدا إذا صلى

translation: Have you seen if he is upon guidance
interpretation: This verse is questioning whether the person being referred to is following the right path and guidance from Allah. It prompts reflection on whether someone's actions and beliefs align with divine guidance. The implication is that claiming to be rightly guided is not sufficient in itself, but rather one's state needs to be carefully examined to determine if it is truly in accordance with the straight path laid out by Allah's revelation.
orig: أرأيت إن كان على الهدى

translation: Or enjoins righteousness.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of commanding and encouraging others to be righteous, pious, and mindful of God. It suggests that those who actively promote virtue and morality in society are highly regarded in Islam. Enjoining righteousness involves guiding others to follow the path of God, to adhere to His commands, and to refrain from what He has prohibited. This act of enjoining righteousness is seen as a noble deed that benefits not only the individual but also the community as a whole, as it helps to create a society based on Islamic values and principles.
orig: أو أمر بالتقوى

translation: Have you seen if he denies and turns away?
interpretation: This verse is a rhetorical question that draws attention to the attitude of those who reject the truth and turn away from it, despite clear signs and evidence. It implies that such a person is arrogant and misguided, as they choose to deny the truth and turn their back on divine guidance. The verse serves as a warning and reminder that one should be humble and open to the truth, rather than stubbornly denying it out of pride or worldly desires. Ultimately, those who persist in rejecting the truth will face the consequences of their choices in this life and the hereafter.
orig: أرأيت إن كذب وتولى

translation: Does he not know that Allah sees?
interpretation: This verse is a powerful reminder that Allah is always watching and is aware of all our actions, whether good or bad. It serves as a warning to those who may think they can hide their misdeeds from Allah or escape His judgment. At the same time, it is a comforting thought for the righteous, knowing that Allah sees and appreciates their good deeds, even if no one else does. This awareness of Allah's constant presence should motivate us to strive for righteousness and refrain from sin, knowing that we will ultimately be held accountable for all that we do.
orig: ألم يعلم بأن الله يرى

translation: No! If he does not desist, We will surely drag him by the forelock -
interpretation: This verse is a stern warning to those who persist in wrongdoing and opposition to the truth. It emphasizes that if the individual in question does not cease their arrogant and misguided behavior, Allah will seize them by the forelock, signifying their humiliation and disgrace. The forelock is mentioned because it is at the front of the head, and grabbing someone by it is a sign of forcing them to submit. This imagery conveys that no matter how proud or powerful someone may seem, they are ultimately powerless before Allah and will face the consequences of their actions if they do not repent and reform themselves.
orig: كلا لئن لم ينته لنسفعا بالناصية

translation: A lying, sinning forelock.
interpretation: This verse refers to the forehead of a person who persistently lies and sins. The "forelock" is used as a metaphor for the front of the head or the face, which is often associated with a person's character and actions. The description of the forelock as "lying" and "sinning" indicates that this person is deeply immersed in falsehood and transgression, and their very essence is characterized by these negative traits. It serves as a warning against those who are stubbornly and unapologetically engaged in wrongdoing, highlighting the consequences of such behavior in the sight of Allah.
orig: ناصية كاذبة خاطئة

translation: Then let him call his associates;
interpretation: This verse is a challenge to those who deny the truth of the Qur'an and the Prophet Muhammad's message. It dares the disbelievers to call upon their associates, their false gods or supporters, to come to their aid against Allah's punishment. The implication is that no one can help them against Allah's judgment and that their false deities are powerless. It emphasizes the futility of relying on anyone or anything other than Allah and the inevitability of facing the consequences of one's choices and actions in the Hereafter.
orig: فليدع ناديه

translation: We will call the angels of Hell (to deal with them).
interpretation: This verse is a stern warning to those who reject God's message and persist in disbelief and wrongdoing. It emphasizes that on the Day of Judgment, God will summon the fierce and powerful angels of Hell to seize and punish the evildoers. The term "az-Zabaniyah" refers to the stern and strong angels who guard the Hell-fire and carry out God's command to punish the condemned. This verse serves as a reminder of the severe consequences of rejecting faith and indulging in sins, and encourages people to embrace righteousness and obedience to God to avoid such a dreadful fate in the Hereafter.
orig: سندع الزبانية

translation: No! Do not obey him. But prostrate and draw near [to Allah].
interpretation: This verse is a clear command to the believers to not follow or obey those who try to lead them astray from the path of Allah. Instead, they are instructed to humble themselves before Allah through prostration in prayer and to strive to draw closer to Him through obedience and righteousness. It emphasizes the importance of submitting to Allah alone and resisting the temptations and influences that may lead one away from His guidance. The act of prostration is a powerful symbol of humility, surrender and servitude to Allah, while drawing near to Him represents the spiritual journey of the believer to attain nearness and closeness to their Lord through faith and good deeds.
orig: كلا لا تطعه واسجد واقترب

translation: Indeed, We sent it down during the Night of Decree.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the significance and sacredness of the Night of Decree (Laylat al-Qadr), the night in which the Qur'an was first revealed to Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him). It suggests that the revelation of the Qur'an on this night is a testament to its divine origin and its importance as a guide for humanity. The Night of Decree is considered to be one of the most blessed and virtuous nights of the year, and Muslims are encouraged to spend it in prayer, supplication, and reflection upon the Qur'an. The exact date of this night is not specified in the Qur'an, but it is believed to occur during the last ten days of Ramadan, with many scholars identifying it as the 27th night of the month.
orig: إنا أنزلناه في ليلة القدر

translation: And what can make you know what is the Night of Decree?
interpretation: This verse is asking a rhetorical question, emphasizing the greatness and importance of the Night of Decree (Laylat al-Qadr). It suggests that the true significance of this night is beyond human comprehension. The Night of Decree is considered the most important night in the Islamic calendar, as it marks the revelation of the first verses of the Qur'an to Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him). Muslims believe that worship and good deeds performed on this night carry immense rewards and blessings. The exact date of the Night of Decree is not specified in the Qur'an, but it is believed to occur on one of the odd-numbered nights in the last ten days of Ramadan.
orig: وما أدراك ما ليلة القدر

translation: The Night of Decree is better than a thousand months.
interpretation: This verse refers to Laylat al-Qadr, or the Night of Power/Decree, which is considered the holiest night in the Islamic calendar. It is said that worship and good deeds done on this night are worth more than those performed over a thousand months. This underscores the immense spiritual significance and blessings associated with this special night, encouraging believers to devote themselves to prayer, Qur'an recitation, and other acts of worship. It emphasizes that quality and sincerity in worship are more important than quantity, and that there are moments of great divine grace that one should strive to seize.
orig: ليلة القدر خير من ألف شهر

translation: The angels and the Spirit descend therein by permission of their Lord for every matter.
interpretation: This verse refers to the Night of Decree (Laylat al-Qadr), a sacred night in the month of Ramadan. On this night, the angels and the Holy Spirit (Gabriel) descend to the earth with God's permission, carrying out His decrees and bringing blessings and mercy. This night is considered to be better than a thousand months, and it is a time when prayers are answered and destinies are determined. The descent of the angels and the Spirit signifies the immense spiritual importance and blessings of this night, emphasizing the need for believers to engage in worship, prayer, and seeking forgiveness during this special time.
orig: تنزل الملائكة والروح فيها بإذن ربهم من كل أمر

translation: Peace it is until the emergence of dawn.
interpretation: This verse refers to the Night of Decree (Laylat al-Qadr), which is a blessed night during the month of Ramadan. It signifies that throughout this special night, there is an abundance of peace, tranquility, and blessings that last until the break of dawn. This night is considered to be better than a thousand months, and it is a time when the angels and the Spirit (Gabriel) descend to earth with the permission of Allah, carrying His decrees for the coming year. Muslims are encouraged to spend this night in prayer, supplication, and remembrance of Allah to seek His forgiveness and mercy.
orig: سلام هي حتى مطلع الفجر

translation: Those who disbelieved among the People of the Scripture and the polytheists were not to be parted [from misbelief] until there came to them clear evidence -
interpretation: This verse indicates that the disbelievers, whether from the People of the Book (Jews and Christians) or the polytheists, persisted in their disbelief and were not willing to change their ways until they received clear proof and evidence of the truth. It suggests that they were stubborn in their rejection of the message despite the signs and warnings sent to them. The verse implies that clear evidence, in the form of revelation and prophetic teachings, was necessary to break through their resistance and encourage them to embrace the truth of Islam. It highlights the importance of clear proofs and the Qur'an as a means of guiding people to the right path.
orig: لم يكن الذين كفروا من أهل الكتاب والمشركين منفكين حتى تأتيهم البينة

translation: A Messenger from Allah, reciting purified scriptures.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the divine origin and purity of the message brought by the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him). The "purified scriptures" refer to the Qur'an, which is free from any corruption or alteration. The verse highlights the role of the Prophet as a messenger chosen by Allah to convey His words to humanity, and the sacred nature of the Qur'an as a divine revelation that guides people towards righteousness and truth.
orig: رسول من الله يتلو صحفا مطهرة

translation: In it are valuable books.
interpretation: This verse refers to Paradise, indicating that it contains books of great worth and importance. These books likely contain knowledge and wisdom that will be of immense value and benefit to those who reside in Paradise. The verse emphasizes the idea that Paradise is not just a place of physical pleasures and delights, but also a realm where one can attain spiritual and intellectual fulfillment through access to precious and priceless knowledge contained in these "valuable books".
orig: فيها كتب قيمة

translation: And those who were given the Scripture did not become divided until after clear evidence had come to them.
interpretation: This verse is referring to the fact that the People of the Book (Jews and Christians) only became divided and started to differ in their beliefs after clear evidence and truth had already come to them from God through their prophets and scriptures. Despite having received divine guidance, they still ended up in disagreement and sectarianism. This implies that the cause of their division was not a lack of clear proof, but rather their own failings in following the truth that had been made evident to them. It serves as a warning to the believers to hold firmly to the clear guidance that has come to them, lest they too fall into the same trap of division and differing even after the truth has been made manifest.
orig: وما تفرق الذين أوتوا الكتاب إلا من بعد ما جاءتهم البينة

translation: And they were not commanded except to worship Allah, [being] sincere to Him in religion, inclining to truth, and to establish prayer and to give zakah. And that is the correct religion.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the essence of the divine message sent to humanity through the prophets: to worship Allah alone with sincerity, following the path of monotheism (Hanifa). It also highlights the importance of establishing prayer and giving zakah (obligatory charity) as fundamental pillars of the Islamic faith. The verse concludes by asserting that this is the "correct" or "straight" religion, implying that any deviation from these core principles would be considered a divergence from the true path ordained by Allah.
orig: وما أمروا إلا ليعبدوا الله مخلصين له الدين حنفاء ويقيموا الصلاة ويؤتوا الزكاة وذلك دين القيمة

translation: Indeed, those who disbelieve from the People of the Book and the polytheists will be in the Fire of Hell, to stay there forever. They are the worst of creatures.
interpretation: This verse is a stern warning to those who reject the message of Islam, whether they are from the People of the Book (Jews and Christians) or the polytheists. It emphasizes that their ultimate fate will be the eternal punishment of Hell, as a consequence of their disbelief. The verse also makes a strong moral judgment, stating that those who reject the truth and persist in disbelief are the worst of all creatures in the sight of Allah. This highlights the gravity of rejecting the message of Islam and the importance of faith and submission to the One True God.
orig: إن الذين كفروا من أهل الكتاب والمشركين في نار جهنم خالدين فيها أولئك هم شر البرية

translation: Indeed, those who have believed and done righteous deeds - those are the best of creatures.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that true success and the highest status in the sight of Allah belongs to those who combine sincere faith with righteous actions. It is not enough to simply believe; one must demonstrate their faith through good deeds and virtuous conduct. Those who embody this combination of faith and righteousness are considered the best of all creation, as they fulfill the purpose for which they were created and attain the pleasure of their Lord. This interpretation highlights the importance of aligning one's beliefs with their actions and striving to live a life that is pleasing to Allah.
orig: إن الذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات أولئك هم خير البرية

translation: Their reward with their Lord is gardens of perpetual residence beneath which rivers flow, wherein they will abide forever. Allah being pleased with them and they with Him. That is for whoever has feared his Lord.
interpretation: This verse speaks about the ultimate reward for the righteous believers in the Hereafter. It emphasizes that those who fear Allah and live according to His commands will be granted the eternal bliss of Paradise. In these gardens of endless joy, rivers will flow beneath them, signifying the abundance of blessings and the absence of any form of hardship or discomfort. The verse also highlights the mutual pleasure between Allah and His faithful servants. Allah will be pleased with their faith and good deeds, and they will be content with the reward bestowed upon them by their Lord. This profound relationship of love and satisfaction is the result of their sincere devotion and consciousness of Allah throughout their worldly life. Thus, the verse encourages believers to maintain a strong connection with their Creator and strive for His pleasure, knowing that the ultimate reward awaits those who fear Him and follow His path.
orig: جزاؤهم عند ربهم جنات عدن تجري من تحتها الأنهار خالدين فيها أبدا رضي الله عنهم ورضوا عنه ذلك لمن خشي ربه

translation: When the earth is shaken with its [final] earthquake
interpretation: This verse is referring to the tremendous earthquake that will occur on the Day of Judgment. It will be a quake unlike any other, signifying the end of the world as we know it and the beginning of the eternal afterlife. The shaking of the earth is a sign of Allah's immense power and a reminder to humanity that everything in this temporary world will come to an end. It serves as a wake-up call for people to reflect on their deeds and prepare for the ultimate reckoning before their Lord. The verse instills a sense of awe and humility, urging believers to live righteously and be mindful of their actions, as they will have consequences in the Hereafter.
orig: إذا زلزلت الأرض زلزالها

translation: And the earth discharges its burdens
interpretation: This verse refers to the Day of Judgment when the earth will give up all that it contains, including the dead who will be resurrected. It symbolizes the earth relieving itself of the weight of sin and evil that has burdened it throughout human history. The earth will bear witness to the deeds, good and bad, that were committed upon it. This verse serves as a reminder of the inevitability of divine justice and the consequences of our actions in this world, which will ultimately be brought to light on the Day of Reckoning.
orig: وأخرجت الأرض أثقالها

translation: And man says, "What is [wrong] with it?" -
interpretation: This verse is referring to the Day of Judgment, when the earth will quake and man will be in a state of shock and confusion. He will question what is happening to the earth, not understanding the gravity of the situation. It highlights man's ignorance and heedlessness of the consequences of his actions in this world, and his unpreparedness for the realities of the Hereafter. The verse serves as a reminder for humans to reflect on their deeds and to be mindful that they will ultimately be held accountable before Allah.
orig: وقال الإنسان ما لها

translation: That Day, it will report its news
interpretation: On the Day of Judgment, the earth will speak and bear witness to all the deeds, good and evil, that were done upon it by human beings and jinn. It will recount everything that happened on its surface with perfect accuracy, as Allah has commanded it to do so. This verse emphasizes Allah's omniscience and the fact that nothing is hidden from Him. It also serves as a reminder for people to be mindful of their actions, as everything will be accounted for and brought forth as evidence on that fateful Day.
orig: يومئذ تحدث أخبارها

translation: That your Lord inspired it [i.e., the earth].
interpretation: This verse refers to the Day of Judgment when Allah will command the earth to speak and disclose all the deeds, good and evil, that were done on its surface by human beings throughout history. The earth will bear witness to everything that happened on it, and this testimony will be used as evidence for or against people on the Day of Reckoning. This verse emphasizes Allah's omnipotence and His ability to make even inanimate objects, like the earth, speak and testify by His command and inspiration.
orig: بأن ربك أوحى لها

translation: That Day, the people will depart separated [into categories] to be shown [the result of] their deeds.
interpretation: On the Day of Judgment, people will be divided into groups based on their deeds in this worldly life. They will witness the consequences of their actions, whether good or bad. This verse emphasizes the individual accountability and the ultimate justice that will be served by Allah. It serves as a reminder for people to be mindful of their deeds, as they will face the repercussions in the Hereafter.
orig: يومئذ يصدر الناس أشتاتا ليروا أعمالهم

translation: So whoever does an atom's weight of good will see it,
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of doing good deeds, no matter how small they may seem. It suggests that every action, even if it is as tiny as an atom, has significance and will be rewarded by Allah. This encourages believers to strive for righteousness in all aspects of their lives, knowing that no good deed goes unnoticed or unrewarded by God. It also implies that on the Day of Judgment, people will be confronted with the full weight of their deeds, both good and bad, and will be recompensed accordingly.
orig: فمن يعمل مثقال ذرة خيرا يره

translation: And whoever does an atom's weight of evil will see it.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the concept of individual accountability in Islam. It underscores that every deed, no matter how small or seemingly insignificant, will have its consequences. Even an act as minute as an atom's weight of evil will be brought to light and the person will face its repercussions. This interpretation highlights the importance of being mindful of one's actions, as nothing escapes God's knowledge and justice. It serves as a reminder for individuals to strive towards righteousness and refrain from wrongdoing, as they will be held accountable for their choices and actions in this life and the hereafter.
orig: ومن يعمل مثقال ذرة شرا يره

translation: By the racers, panting,
interpretation: This verse is interpreted as referring to the horses that were used in battle during the time of the Prophet Muhammad. The panting of the horses as they race into battle is seen as a symbol of their bravery and loyalty to their riders. The verse is also interpreted metaphorically as referring to the struggles and efforts of the believers in the path of Allah, who strive with sincerity and devotion, just as the horses race with all their might. It emphasizes the importance of exerting oneself fully in the service of Allah and being willing to make sacrifices for the sake of one's faith.
orig: والعاديات ضبحا

translation: And [by] the producers of sparks [when] striking
interpretation: This verse is referring to the horses that were used in battle during the time of the Prophet Muhammad. The sparks mentioned are generated by the horses' hooves striking the ground as they gallop, which is a metaphor for their speed and strength. The verse is part of a passage that describes the bravery and dedication of the Muslim warriors who fought in the cause of Allah, emphasizing their readiness to charge into battle at a moment's notice, even in the early hours of the morning when most people are still asleep. It highlights the sacrifices they made and the importance of their role in defending and spreading Islam.
orig: فالموريات قدحا

translation: By the raiders at dawn,
interpretation: This verse is interpreted as referring to the Muslim warriors who would launch surprise attacks against their enemies at dawn. It highlights the bravery and strategic planning of the early Muslim community in defending themselves and spreading the message of Islam. The verse is seen as a reminder of the sacrifices made by the early Muslims and the importance of being vigilant and proactive in facing challenges and obstacles to the faith.
orig: فالمغيرات صبحا

translation: And they stirred up thereby [clouds of] dust
interpretation: This verse is referring to powerful winds or forces that are so strong that they kick up clouds of dust and debris. It could be interpreted metaphorically as well, suggesting that certain actions or events can stir up trouble or chaos, just as powerful winds stir up dust. The key message is that there are forces or influences in the world, whether natural or figurative, that have the ability to cause upheaval and disruption on a large scale.
orig: فأثرن به نقعا

translation: So the middle prayer, or the best prayer, is the congregational prayer.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance and virtue of praying in congregation. Performing prayers in congregation is considered superior to praying individually because it promotes unity, discipline, and a sense of brotherhood among Muslims. It also helps in fostering a strong Muslim community. The "middle prayer" or "best prayer" referred to in this verse is generally understood to be the congregational prayer, highlighting its significance in Islam.
orig: فوسطن به جمعا

translation: Indeed mankind, to his Lord, is ungrateful.
interpretation: This verse is pointing out the inherent nature of human beings to be ungrateful and unappreciative of the countless blessings and favors bestowed upon them by Allah. Despite all that Allah provides for us in terms of sustenance, guidance, and mercy, many people still turn away from Him and fail to acknowledge and thank Him for these blessings. It is a reminder for us to constantly check ourselves and ensure that we are expressing gratitude to our Lord for all that He has given us, and not taking His favors for granted or being among those described as ungrateful.
orig: إن الإنسان لربه لكنود

translation: And indeed, He is a witness over that.
interpretation: This verse affirms that Allah is a witness over everything that happens in the universe. He is aware of all our actions, thoughts, and intentions. Nothing escapes His knowledge, and He will hold us accountable for our deeds on the Day of Judgment. This should motivate us to be mindful of our conduct and strive to please Him through righteous actions and sincere worship.
orig: وإنه على ذلك لشهيد

translation: And indeed he is, in love of wealth, intense.
interpretation: This verse is referring to the human being's intense love for worldly possessions and wealth. It suggests that this love can become so strong that it consumes a person, making them greedy and miserly. The Qur'an reminds us that an excessive attachment to material wealth can distract us from our spiritual purpose and lead us astray from the path of righteousness. It encourages believers to maintain a balanced perspective, using their wealth in moderation and for good causes, while remembering that true contentment and success lie in seeking Allah's pleasure rather than amassing temporary worldly gains.
orig: وإنه لحب الخير لشديد

translation: Does he not know that when the contents of the graves are scattered
interpretation: This verse is a reminder that on the Day of Judgment, all the dead will be resurrected from their graves and their deeds will be laid bare before Allah. It is a warning to mankind that they should be mindful of their actions in this world, for they will be held accountable for them in the Hereafter. The scattering of the contents of the graves symbolizes the resurrection and the bringing forth of all that was hidden, emphasizing the fact that nothing will remain concealed from Allah on that day. This verse encourages introspection and self-reflection, urging individuals to consider the consequences of their deeds and to strive for righteousness in this life, knowing that the ultimate reckoning awaits them in the afterlife.
orig: أفلا يعلم إذا بعثر ما في القبور

translation: And that which is in the breasts is obtained.
interpretation: This verse alludes to the fact that on the Day of Judgment, all the secrets, intentions, and feelings hidden within people's hearts will be exposed and brought to light. Nothing will remain concealed from Allah, and people will be held accountable for their innermost thoughts and motivations, not just their outward actions. It serves as a reminder for individuals to purify their hearts and be mindful of what they harbor within, as ultimately, Allah has knowledge of all that is hidden in the hearts and will bring it forth for judgment.
orig: وحصل ما في الصدور

translation: Indeed, their Lord with them, that Day, is [fully] Acquainted.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the omniscience of Allah, particularly on the Day of Judgment. It reminds us that on that momentous day, Allah will be fully aware of every deed, intention, and thought of His servants. Nothing escapes His knowledge, and He will judge each individual with perfect justice and fairness based on their actions in this world. The verse instills a sense of accountability and encourages believers to be mindful of their conduct, knowing that their Lord is always watching and will hold them answerable for their choices.
orig: إن ربهم بهم يومئذ لخبير

translation: The Striking Calamity
interpretation: This verse refers to the Day of Judgment, a catastrophic event that will strike the world, causing immense destruction and chaos. It serves as a powerful reminder of the inevitability of divine justice and the consequences of one's actions in this life. The verse emphasizes the importance of leading a righteous life and being prepared for the ultimate reckoning, as the Day of Judgment will be a time of great upheaval and accountability for all of humanity.
orig: القارعة

translation: What is the Striking Calamity?
interpretation: The "Striking Calamity" refers to the Day of Judgment, a catastrophic event that will shake the world and herald the end of times. It is called "Al-Qari'ah" which conveys the sense of a sudden, shocking occurrence that strikes with great force. This verse poses a rhetorical question to draw attention to the momentous nature of this event, emphasizing its inevitability and the need for mankind to be prepared for it by leading righteous lives in accordance with God's guidance.
orig: ما القارعة

translation: And what can make you know what the Striking Calamity is?
interpretation: This verse is asking the question: how can you truly comprehend or understand the reality and severity of the Day of Judgment, referred to here as the "Striking Calamity"? It implies that the events of that Day are so immense and catastrophic that it is beyond normal human understanding. The verse serves as a reminder of the limitations of human knowledge and the importance of having faith in the unseen realities described by Allah in the Qur'an about the end of times and the final judgment.
orig: وما أدراك ما القارعة

translation: The Day when people will be like moths, dispersed.
interpretation: This verse is referring to the Day of Judgment, when all of humanity will be resurrected and will scatter in a state of confusion and terror, like moths that have been disturbed and are flying about erratically. It conveys the sense of chaos, fear, and helplessness that people will experience on that momentous day as they face the consequences of their deeds in this world. The dispersed moths symbolize how people will be separated from their loved ones and will solely be concerned with their own fate, emphasizing the individual nature of the ultimate reckoning before God.
orig: يوم يكون الناس كالفراش المبثوث

translation: And the mountains will be like wool, fluffed up.
interpretation: This verse is describing the end of times, when the world as we know it will be destroyed. The mountains, which are normally seen as symbols of permanence and stability, will be reduced to something as light and insubstantial as carded wool. This metaphor emphasizes the complete transformation and upheaval that will occur on the Day of Judgment. It reminds us that no matter how solid and unshakable the world may seem, ultimately everything in this life is fleeting and will come to an end. The only thing that remains is our deeds and our faith, which we will carry with us into the eternal life of the hereafter.
orig: وتكون الجبال كالعهن المنفوش

translation: Then as for one whose scales are heavy [with good deeds]
interpretation: This verse refers to those whose good deeds outweigh their bad deeds on the Day of Judgment. It suggests that those who have lived a righteous life and performed many good actions will be successful in the Hereafter. The "heavy scales" symbolize the abundance of their virtuous deeds. This verse emphasizes the importance of striving to do good in this world, as it will determine one's fate in the eternal life to come. It serves as an encouragement for believers to focus on performing righteous actions and avoiding sins, knowing that every deed will be weighed and accounted for by Allah.
orig: فأما من ثقلت موازينه

translation: So he will be in a pleasant life.
interpretation: This verse refers to the believer who will be rewarded with a blissful and contented existence in Paradise in the Hereafter. It indicates that those who lived righteously and followed the path of God will find themselves in a state of complete satisfaction, joy, and fulfillment. The "pleasant life" encompasses both the physical comforts and spiritual delights that the believer will experience eternally in the Gardens of Paradise as a result of God's pleasure with their faith and good deeds in the worldly life.
orig: فهو في عيشة راضية

translation: But as for he whose scales are light,
interpretation: This verse refers to those whose good deeds are outweighed by their sins on the Day of Judgment. Their "scales" being light is a metaphor indicating that they lack sufficient good deeds to attain salvation. As a result, they will face the consequences of their wrongdoings and be condemned to Hell. This serves as a warning for individuals to strive for righteousness and perform good deeds throughout their lives, as it will determine their fate in the Hereafter.
orig: وأما من خفت موازينه

translation: His mother is Hawiyah.
interpretation: In this verse, "Hawiyah" refers to the lowest depths of Hell. It suggests that those who reject faith and do evil deeds will be cast into the abyss of Hell, which is personified as a mother embracing the sinner. This metaphor emphasizes the severity and inescapability of the punishment for those who turn away from God's path. It serves as a stark warning of the ultimate consequences of leading a sinful life without repentance and faith.
orig: فأمه هاوية

translation: And what can make you know what it is?
interpretation: This verse is posing a rhetorical question, emphasizing that the true nature and reality of the subject being discussed ("it") is beyond human comprehension. It suggests that the knowledge of "it" is with Allah alone, and that humans have limited understanding of the profound matters being addressed in the Qur'an. The verse prompts reflection on the vastness of Allah's knowledge compared to the limited knowledge of mankind.
orig: وما أدراك ما هيه

translation: A scorching Fire.
interpretation: This verse refers to the intense and severe nature of the Fire of Hell that awaits those who reject faith and do evil deeds. The Arabic word "hamiyah" conveys the meaning of something that is intensely hot and fierce. This description of Hell as a scorching, blazing Fire is meant to instill fear and serve as a warning to those who persist in disbelief and transgression, reminding them of the grave consequences of their choices in the Hereafter.
orig: نار حامية

translation: Competition in [worldly] increase diverts you
interpretation: This verse is a reminder that the pursuit of worldly gains and competing with others for more wealth, status, and power can distract us from our true purpose in life, which is to worship Allah and prepare for the Hereafter. It warns against becoming engrossed in the temporary pleasures and vanities of this world at the expense of our spiritual well-being and our relationship with Allah. The verse encourages us to prioritize our faith and good deeds over the fleeting distractions of this life, as ultimately, it is our deeds and our relationship with Allah that will matter in the Hereafter.
orig: ألهاكم التكاثر

translation: Until you visit the graves
interpretation: This verse is a reminder of the inevitability of death and the importance of being mindful of the afterlife. It suggests that people are often preoccupied with worldly pursuits and pleasures until they are confronted with the reality of death, symbolized by visiting graves. The verse encourages introspection and reflection on one's mortality, urging individuals to prioritize their spiritual well-being and prepare for the hereafter by leading a righteous life in accordance with Islamic teachings. It serves as a wake-up call to focus on what truly matters in the grand scheme of existence, rather than being consumed by fleeting material desires.
orig: حتى زرتم المقابر

translation: No! You will come to know.
interpretation: This verse is a stern warning to those who reject the truth of the Hereafter and the Day of Judgment. It emphasizes that they will eventually come to realize the gravity of their denial and the consequences that await them. The repetition of this warning in the following verse reinforces its severity. It serves as a wake-up call for people to reflect upon their beliefs and actions in this world, as they will be held accountable in the next. The verse implies that the knowledge and certainty of the Hereafter will dawn upon the deniers, but it may be too late for them to change their fate.
orig: كلا سوف تعلمون

translation: Then, no! You are going to know.
interpretation: This verse is a stern warning and admonition to those who reject the truth and persist in disbelief. It emphasizes that they will come to know the consequences of their actions and the reality of what they denied. The repetition of "you are going to know" adds to the severity of the warning, implying that this knowledge will come with certainty and that the disbelievers will face the dire results of their choices in the Hereafter. It serves as a wake-up call for them to reconsider their stance before it is too late.
orig: ثم كلا سوف تعلمون

translation: No! If you only knew with knowledge of certainty.
interpretation: This verse is emphasizing the importance of having certain knowledge and conviction in matters of faith. It suggests that if people truly understood the reality of the afterlife and the consequences of their actions with certainty, they would change their behavior and beliefs. The verse implies that many people lack this level of certain knowledge, and instead rely on conjecture or doubt. It is a call to seek out truth and knowledge, rather than remaining in a state of ignorance or skepticism.
orig: كلا لو تعلمون علم اليقين

translation: You will surely see the Hellfire.
interpretation: This verse serves as a severe warning to those who reject faith and do evil deeds. It emphasizes the reality and inevitability of the Hellfire in the Hereafter for those who choose to disobey Allah and follow their own desires in this worldly life. The verse aims to instill fear and encourage people to mend their ways, seek forgiveness, and strive for righteousness to avoid this terrible fate. It is a reminder that our actions in this life have consequences in the next, and we must be mindful of our choices and deeds.
orig: لترون الجحيم

translation: Then you will surely see it with the eye of certainty.
interpretation: This verse refers to the ultimate reality that will be witnessed by the believers in the Hereafter. "The eye of certainty" denotes a state of absolute conviction and unwavering faith. It suggests that the believers will directly perceive and experience the truth of Allah's promises and the realities of the afterlife, leaving no room for doubt. This direct vision of truth will be a reward for their faith and righteousness in this world. The verse emphasizes the importance of belief and the assurance that the believers will attain a level of certainty that surpasses mere knowledge, as they will witness the truth with their own eyes in the eternal life to come.
orig: ثم لترونها عين اليقين

translation: Then, on that Day, you shall be asked about the delight (you indulged in, in this world)!
interpretation: This verse serves as a reminder that on the Day of Judgment, people will be held accountable for the blessings and delights they enjoyed in this worldly life. It emphasizes the importance of being grateful for the favors bestowed upon us by Allah and using them in a manner that pleases Him. The verse also implies that we should not be distracted by the temporary pleasures of this world, as we will be questioned about how we utilized these blessings and whether we fulfilled our obligations towards Allah and His creation. It encourages believers to maintain a balance between enjoying the lawful pleasures of this life while keeping in mind the ultimate purpose of our existence and the accountability in the Hereafter.
orig: ثم لتسألن يومئذ عن النعيم

translation: By the time,
interpretation: In this verse, Allah swears by "al-Asr", which refers to time, or more specifically, the passage of time. This oath serves to emphasize the importance and gravity of the message that follows in the subsequent verses. It draws attention to the fleeting nature of human life and the urgency to make the most of the limited time we have in this world by engaging in righteous deeds and faith.
orig: والعصر

translation: Indeed, mankind is in loss,
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the general state of loss and misguidance that humanity finds itself in. Without faith, good deeds, and the pursuit of truth, mankind is in a state of spiritual loss and deprivation. The verse serves as a reminder that true success and fulfillment can only be attained through belief in God, righteous actions, and perseverance in the face of challenges. It is a call to reflect on one's life and to strive towards the path of guidance and salvation.
orig: إن الإنسان لفي خسر

translation: Except for those who have believed and done righteous deeds and advised each other to truth and advised each other to patience.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of faith, good deeds, and the virtues of truth and patience. It suggests that those who possess these qualities will be exempt from the loss mentioned in the previous verses of the chapter.
